text:
29th May, 2020
By Robert Mutunga(Mwambua Ngozi)
Ligi nene ya muvila wa maau kuya nthi ya England ikambiia ingi matuku 17/6 na yiithela 1/8 2020. Uu ni kuatinia umbano ula utwaiiwe iyoo ni atongoi ma timu syonthe ila ithaukaa nthini wa ligi isu ya Epl.Mathau ma mbee mkathaukwa ni Aston Villa vs Sheffield United na Manchester City vs Arsenal.
Weekend ya matuku 19 nginya 21, niwo timu syonthe ikethiwa iithauka.Vena mathau 92 ala matialite ni kana ligi isu ithele.Ligi isu yaungamiwe 13/3/2020 itina wa uwau wa corona kumbuka nthi yonthe vala timu ikathaukaa vate mashabiki meulika iwanzani. Mathau asu mesyokethya itina wa mithenya 100.
Kuvikiia vau andu 12 ala ni athauki vamwe na maovisa ma ilavu kivathukanyo nimo maminite ukwatikana na corona itina wa athauki na maovisa 2,752 kuthimwa.
Liverpool nimo matongoetye muungamoni wa ligi isu mekiite utaaniu wa pointi 25 vala timu sya Bournemouth, Aston Villa na Norwich City meuvalukilwa ni ithoka yautheewa ngazi na kuthauka nthini wa championships mwakani usu twathi.

translation:
May 29th, 2020
By Robert Mutunga(Mwambua Ngozi)
The big league of adult men in the country of England has been postponed to June 17th and will end on 1/8 2020. This is due to the pressure that was put in place which is a challenge for all teams but remains within the rules of the current Epl league. The first matches to be played are Aston Villa vs Sheffield United and Manchester City vs Arsenal.
The weekend of the 19th to the 21st, all teams will be seen playing. There remain 92 games to be completed so that the league can end. The current league which started on 13/3/2020 stopped due to the outbreak of corona remembering the whole country closed down and teams played without fans unlike usual. Future matches may be played behind closed doors with 100 people allowed.
Regarding the issue of 12 people who have died and some with severe illnesses, the total number infected with corona is said to be 2,752 confirmed.
Liverpool and their chances of winning the current league are strong with a lead of 25 points while teams like Bournemouth, Aston Villa and Norwich City are likely to be relegated and descend to the championship level as we previously discussed.

text:
9th May 2020
By Robert Mutunga(Mwambua Ngozi)
Ngumbau ya tene ya ithau ya ngundi(Boxing) Mike Tyson nukusyokethya ingi ithauni ya kusangithya ilovia syakutetheesya milati nthini wa muvea wake wa Mike Tyson Foundation. Tyson ula wina ukuu wa myaka 53 avaniiwe kukomana na SONNY Bill Williams na ula wai muthauki wa Boxing myakani ya vau katenange indi kwa ooyu athaukaa Rugby na kilavu kya Toronto Wolfpack.
Kuatiania na mauvoo ala matumiwe mutandaoni wa instagram ni Promoter Brian Amatruda, easya anengie Tyson kimanza kya $1million(Ksh 100 M) ni kana etikile kuthauka na Williams.
Williams na ula wina ukuu wa myaka 34 ni ngumbau ya tene ya musivi wa WBA International Heavyweight champion na asindite mathau make oonthe 7 ala wikitite.
Ona uu wiovo ni kana kuatiania na mauvoo ala matumbithiwe ni ithangu ya SunSport measya Williams ndesya kuthauka atetikilitwe ni kilavu kyake kya Toronto.
Mike Tyson nake ethiitwe aikoota malenyu vandu va myei kauta na kwonanyia ena utonyi wa kusyoka kiwanzani ingi.
Amatruda na ula ukukwata mbau ithau yiu ngalikoni ya ilovia easya yaile kutwaiiwa kiwanzani kya Melbourne Arena nundu kina utonyi wa ulika mashabiki 10,000 kana Princes Park kila kina utonyi wa ulika mashabiki 30,000.
Matuku ma ithau yiu mainatangaaswa kuatiania na uwau wa Covid-19.

translation:
May 9th, 2020
By Robert Mutunga(Mwambua Ngozi)
The former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson has expressed interest in returning to the ring to raise funds for his Mike Tyson Foundation charity. Tyson, who is now 53 years old, has been challenged to fight SONNY Bill Williams, a former boxer who has spent the last few years playing rugby for the Toronto Wolfpack.
According to information shared online on Instagram by promoter Brian Amatruda, he offered Tyson a starting fee of $1 million (Ksh 100M) and believes he can secure a fight with Williams.
Williams, who is also 34 years old, is a former contender for the WBA International Heavyweight championship and has won seven of his fights.
It is said that according to information published by The SunSport newspaper, Williams is likely to accept the challenge due to his contract with the Toronto club.
Mike Tyson has reportedly been training hard lately and is eager to return to the ring.
Amatruda says he has venues ready for the fight, either the Melbourne Arena which can accommodate 10,000 fans, or Princes Park which can hold 30,000 fans.
The dates for the fight are being considered in light of the Covid-19 situation.

text:
Mbanga ya Lelu kumina Dereva umwe na angi 2 muamia Mtito andei Makueni
Ndeleva umwe wa iloli ula wina ukuu wa myaka 37 niwatiwa ni thayu vau kwa vau na mateleva angi 2 makwata maaumisye manene, itina wa mbanga ya lelu ila yakitika usini wa Tsavo kilomita 45 wavituka town ya Mtito andei uendete ngaliko sya Mombasa leluni munene wa Mombasa kuka vaa ilovi.
Mbanga isu yeethiwa umunthi kuikya.
Kommander wa volisi kauntini ya Makueni Jopseh Ole Napeiyan,easya kana, iloli yiu yumite ngaliko sya ilovi yakimana na maloli angi eli na ndeleva usu akwa vau kwa vau na angi eli masembwa sivitalini wa voi kukwata uiiti.
Mwii wa ula watiwa ni thayu wi nyumbani ya kusuvia akwu sivitalini wa Makindu ukunikili iulu wa mbanga isu utwaiiwe.
Kumana na mbanga isu lelu usu wiwetwa ta wavungwa ni ngali ila syeeka mbanga na kwina muatianio munene wa ngali kwa oyu na maovisa ma volisi nimaendee kutata kwathukanisya ngali isu

translation:
The Lelu bus collided with a driver and two others near Mtito Andei in Makueni.
One passenger of the lorry who was 37 years old died on the spot with two other passengers sustaining serious injuries, according to the Lelu bus crew, the accident occurred 45 kilometers from Tsavo while heading towards Mtito Andei town en route to Mombasa during a heavy downpour in Mombasa causing the lorry to overturn.
This bus is said to be completely damaged.
Makueni County Police Commander Joseph Ole Napeiyan stated that the lorry crashed due to the slippery road conditions and collided with another lorry carrying goods and another vehicle which was parked at Voi police station holding evidence.
The driver of the lorry who died on the spot will have his body taken to Makindu mortuary awaiting postmortem examination to determine the cause of this accident.
Currently, this bus is being guarded by police officers but the wreckage and the goods are still scattered around causing a large traffic jam and police officers are working to clear the debris.

Uthinzi wa Mii ya andu 3 ala manakitiwe makwiiye nyumbani yoo Jogoo rd Ilovi
Daktari munene wa silikali wa kwika wia wa uthinzi Johansen Oduor,easya mundu muka na kamwana kake ala maneethiwe me akw'u a nyumbani kwoo Mtaani wa Jogoo Road vaa Ilovi, manatiiwe ni thayu makosa nzeve ya kuveva ya oxygen.

Ukunikili wa vau mbeeni unoonanisye kana, ve yiiko ya makaa yineethiwe utee wa mwii wa mwii wa munduume usu, ula uneethiwe e mukw'u, o na vala volisi nimatwaiisye ukunikili kumanyike uw'o wa ikw'u sya andu asu 3 maneethiwe matiitwe ni thayu.
Asu me 3 manakitiwe iso wakeeli me akw'u nyumbani sya silikali ila syi Jogoo rd vaa Ilovi.

translation:
The smell of three people's bodies was found at home on Jogoo Rd Ilovi.
Senior military doctor investigating the cause of the smell, Johansen Oduor, found a woman and her child who were also found dead in the house on Jogoo Road in Ilovi, suspected of dying due to lack of oxygen.
Dr. Johansen Oduor said yesterday, the cause of the smell of the three bodies, that they were found in a burnt house near Chiromo in Ilovi, where a man who was also found dead in the house appeared to have suffocated from carbon monoxide poisoning.
The investigation of the incident has revealed that there was a charcoal stove used to heat the room of the man, who was found in the house, and police have launched an investigation to identify the owner of the house where the bodies of the three people were found suspected of being killed.
Three bodies were found lying in the room of the house belonging to soldiers along Jogoo rd in Ilovi.

By Robert Mutunga(Mwambua Ngozi)
Ula wai muandiki munene wa ngwatanio ya muvila wa maau kisioni kya Africa ya umiloni wa sua na katikati(CECAFA) Nicholas Musonye, nutangaasie kwitya kivila kya nzama ya FKF nthini wa usakuani munene ula ukite.
Musonye athyumuiie wia nzamani ya CECAFA mweini wa december mwaka muthelu ena mea maitya kivila kya ugavana kaontini ya Kakamega mwakani wa 2022.
Kulika kwa Musonye nthini wa kikungu kiu kya usakuani wa FKF na ula withiitwe uikuiiwa kwa mavinda kauta, ni ukuno munene kwa mweene kivila ula wivo kwa ooyu Nick Mwenda nundu nikutonya uthokoanya mivango yake usakuanini usu nundu Musonye ena utuika mwiingi maunduni ma kuungamia ithau ya muvila wa wa maau kisioni kya East and Central Africa vala unatongoisye vandu Va myaka 21.
Musonye easya osie itambya yiu itina wa ukulwa ni andu vamwe na mivea kivathukanyo ila ituikaa ithau ya soka vaa Kenya ni kana etye kivila kiu ni kana atungiie nguma sya soka vaa Kenya na ila siendee na kwonza.
Atongoi angi ala maminite kuikiithya kuukitia kivila kiu ni vamwe na mweene kivila ula utongoesye nzama isu ivindani yii Nick Mwendwa, mweene kivila wa tene Sam Nyamweya, mweene kivila wa tene wa AFC Leopards Alex Ole Magelo, ula wai gavana wa kaonti ya Vihiga Bishop Moses Akaranga na CEO wa kilavu kya Gor Mahia Lordvick Aduda kati wa angi aingi.

May 16th, 2020
By Robert Mutunga(Mwambua Ngozi)
The former head writer of the Council for East and Central Africa Football Association (CECAFA) Nicholas Musonye, has stated he fears the current state of Kenyan football due to the great chaos that exists.
Musonye resigned from his position at CECAFA in December of last year after fearing the governance issues during the Kakamega County tournament in 2022.
According to Musonye within this issue of the chaos in the Football Federation and the fact that it is being investigated by various parties, it is a big loss for someone like Nick Mwenda who is trying to collect his dues in the federation because Musonye has a lot of experience in supporting the development of sports in the East and Central African region which has benefited people for 21 years.
Musonye said he is ready to work with others and offer solutions but believes the future of Kenyan football is uncertain and whether he can help Kenyan football depends on starting over.
Other leaders who have also expressed their desire to resolve this issue include the person who oversaw the previous federation Nick Mwendwa, former president Sam Nyamweya, former AFC Leopards president Alex Ole Magelo, the governor of Vihiga County Bishop Moses Akaranga and CEO of Gor Mahia club Lordvick Aduda among many others.

text:
MŨSYAĨĨSYA (ĨKASETI YA KWĨMANYĨSYA) Mwei wa 12 2016
Ĩkaseti yĩĩ yĩ na ilungu sya kwĩmanyĩsya sya kwambĩĩa matukũ 30/1/2017 nginya matukũ 26/2/2017.
LIFE STORY
Mawĩa maingĩ ala Denton Hopkinson wĩthĩĩtwe aithũkũma kuma e wa mũika nĩmamũtetheesye kwona ũndũ Yeova wendete andũ ma mĩthemba yonthe.
Nũtonya kũtetheka mũno wasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova wakũthaisye kuma naĩnĩ.
Ĩandĩko ya Alomi kĩlungu kya 8 yĩ na ũtao ũtonya kũũtetheesya ũkwate ĩtuvi yĩla Yeova wathĩte andũ onthe.
Nũsomete makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya ala mela kuma? Sisya ũtonya kũsũngĩa makũlyo meana ata ma kuma Mbivilianĩ.
Mavinda amwe athũkũmi ma Ngai nĩmakwatawa nĩ mawĩmakĩo. Ve maũndũ ana ũtonya kwĩka makaũtetheesya kũkwata "mũuo wa Ngai."
Wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o wa kũnewa ĩtuvi nĩ Yeova ũtũtethasya ata? Aathimie athũkũmi make ma tene ata, na aendeee kwĩka ũu ata ũmũnthĩ?
Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩsiĩĩa ĩla wakuwa naĩ, ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩthuthĩtye Aklĩsto methĩwe me auu. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na nguma ĩsu nzeo?
Syongo ila syaneeneiwe ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya andũ onthe na yĩla ya kwĩmanyĩsya.

translation:
MY STORY (A RECORDING OF EXPERIENCES) December 12, 2016
This recording has interviews about preaching from January 30, 2017, to February 26, 2017.
LIFE STORY
Many years ago, Denton Hopkinson became discouraged because he thought God had abandoned him.
He learned to trust that Jehovah cares for us deeply.
Psalm 89 verse 8 says that Jehovah will always remember his promises.
Have you listened to the My Story recordings lately? Perhaps you can find some helpful ideas, even if you live in Mbiviliani.
Some faithful servants of God have been affected by disappointments. But they found ways to maintain their confidence in "God's name."
How can we stay close to Jehovah so that he continues to comfort us? Are there older brothers who can help us, and should we ask them for advice?
It is important to remember what you have learned, as explained in the Bible, which strengthens Christians. Is there something you can do to strengthen your faith today?
So let us listen to the My Story recordings of others and those about preaching.

Ngewa ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ itonya kũtũtetheesya ata twĩthĩwe na nguma ĩsu? Aklĩsto maĩle kwĩthĩwa na nguma ĩsu nĩkĩ?
Ĩvinda yĩmwe Yeova nĩweemanyĩthisye kwĩ Mose kwa kũmũtavya ĩsyĩtwa yake na nguma syake. Nguma sya mbee ila wamũtavisye syaĩ tei na ũseo, kana ĩnee. Mũndũ wĩ nguma isu ekaa ata, na nĩkĩ waĩlĩte kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa nguma ya ĩnee?
LIFE STORY
David Sinclair aielesya maũndũ mana ũtanĩĩte, na ianda ila waanengwa myakanĩ 61 ĩla wĩthĩĩtwe aithũkũma Mbetheli ya Brooklyn na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aĩkĩĩku.
Mbivilia nĩyo ĩvuku yĩla yĩtetwe mũno kuma yamina kũandĩkwa myaka maana maingĩ mĩvĩtu, o na kau nĩkwĩthĩĩtwe ũalyũku wa ithyomo, ũalyũku wa silikalĩ, na andũ meũvĩnga ĩialyũlwa.
Aingĩ nĩmekĩte moalyũku manene ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsa Ndeto ya Ngai. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũtethye kwa nzĩa ĩsu?
nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ũkũmbaũ, na tũtonya kwĩka ata twĩthĩwe na nguma ĩsu?

translation:
A QUESTION (A CASSETTE FOR DISCUSSION) September 9, 2017
This cassette discusses how to preach from October 23rd to October 26th, November 1st to November 26th, 2017.
However, can we still be zealous even if we are discouraged by some brothers? Why did Christ allow himself to be discouraged by some brothers?
Once, Jehovah reminded Moses about his faithfulness despite discouragement from his people. But those brothers did not discourage him intentionally or knowingly. Does a brother's discouragement always matter, or is it possible to remain zealous despite someone's discouragement?
LIFE STORY
David Sinclair shared many experiences that strengthened him, and at age 61 he was invited to serve at Bethel in Brooklyn with his wife and children.
The Bible is a book that has been used greatly throughout many years, and it has helped people overcome difficulties, sickness, and opposition.
Many have found great strength in preaching God's Word. Can we ever feel that God's Word discourages us?
Why do we get discouraged, and can we remain zealous even when discouraged by others?

ANDŨ methĩawa na mawoni me kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa thayũ na kĩkw'ũ. Amwe maĩkĩĩaa kana mũndũ akw'a, nĩvatonyeka akaendeea kwĩthĩwa e kyũmbe kĩngĩ, kana akaendeea kwĩthĩwa thayũ vandũ vangĩ. Angĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana mũndũ akw'a, asyaawa ĩngĩ na ayĩendeea kwĩthĩwa thayũ. Namo angĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana mũndũ akw'a, ũu wake wĩthĩawa wathela.
Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa na woni wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mawoni asu andũ methĩawa namo kwosana na ũndũ ũeetwe kana kĩthĩo kya kwenyu. Nĩkwĩthĩwa mawoni ĩũlũ wa ũndũ kwĩthĩawa ĩla mũndũ wakw'a me kĩvathũkany'o mũno, ve vandũ tũtonya kũkwata ũw'o ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu?
Kwa myaka maana maingĩ, atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmethĩĩtwe maimanyĩsya kana thayũ wa mũndũ ndũkusaa. Vakuvĩ athaithi ma ndĩni syonthe ila nene maĩkĩĩaa kana thayũ ndũkusaa, na nũendeeaa kwĩkala wĩkalonĩ wa syũmbe sya veva ĩla mũndũ wakw'a. Athaithi asu nĩ ma ndĩni sya Kĩklĩsto, Hindu, Kĩyuti, Aisilamu, na ndĩni ingĩ. Namo andũ ma ndĩni ya Buddha maĩkĩĩaa kana mũndũ akw'a asyaawa ĩngĩ mavinda maingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka, na ũu ũituma ũtonyi wake wa kũsũanĩa wĩthĩwa ũseonĩ mwingĩ kana mũuonĩ mwingĩ. Na kĩu nĩkyo andũ ma ndĩni ya Buddha metaa Nirvana.
Nũndũ wa momanyĩsyo asu, andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmaĩkĩĩaa kana kĩkw'ũ nĩkyo kĩtumaa mũndũ athi wĩkalonĩ ũngĩ. Kwoou, andũ aingĩ monaa kĩkw'ũ kĩ kya vata nũndũ nĩkĩtumaa mũndũ athi kwĩkala thayũ ũngĩ, na monaa kwĩ kwenda kwa Ngai andũ makusae. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu? Wĩkũlw'a ũsome kĩlungu kĩla kĩatĩĩe na nũũkwata ũsũngĩo wa kwendeesya.

Nthini wa ndambuka isu Ruto niumbulile kana ndongoi ya kyama kya ODM Raila Odinga ti mundu wa kuikiika kiuteti kiko kila kinatumia Mudavadi na Wetangula mevatahana kuthukuma nake aiweta kwa yu niwe wina ivuso iseo ya kutongoesya nthi ya kenya itina wa usakuani wa mwai wa 8.

translation:
President William Ruto's bodyguard has been replaced, but there is much competition within the Kenya Kwanza alliance, including Musalia Mudavadi of ANC and Moses Wetangula of Ford Kenya, who were in Muranga county to promote his Bottom Up economic agenda.
Ruto has accused ODM leader Raila Odinga of being someone who cannot be trusted because he always uses Mudavadi and Wetangula to attack him, and he wants them to help him lead the country based on the August 9 election results.

Ona ou wiovo, munduume usu itina wa kutwaaisya kiko kyu, nake niweetonyanga na kavyu okau, indi oovow'a ni enenthi atialitye thayu wa mulungu.
Kwianana na nguusi ya itho ila yaneena na kisese kii ni kana, mututia eendeeye na kwika mutiani wake wa muthya wa kilasi kya form 4 wa KCSE, vala eekomboewe nyumba kwa kavinda ni asyai make sokoni wa Kavasya, nokana ndakavinganiswe ni usi aendeeye na mutiani.

text:
1. Twĩ na ũvoo mwaũ kuma kwa Ngai?
Ngai endaa andũ matanĩe thayũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Oombie nthĩ na syĩndũ syonthe ila syĩ nthĩnĩ wayo nũndũ nĩwendete andũ. O mĩtũkĩ nũkwosa ĩtambya ya kũetee andũ onthe ĩvinda ĩseo. Akavetanga maũndũ ala matumaa andũ mathĩna.
Vaiĩ o na ĩndĩĩ silikalĩ yaatonya kũvetanga kaũ, mowau, kana kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ ve ũvoo mũseo. O mĩtũkĩ, Ngai nũkũvetanga silikalĩ sya andũ na aiũngamya yake. Ala mesumbĩkwa nĩ silikalĩ ĩsu ya Ngai makatanĩa mũuo na ũima wa mwĩĩ.
2. Nĩkĩ ũvoo mũseo nĩ wa vata mũno ũmũnthĩ?
Thĩna ũkathela ĩla Ngai ũkananga andũ athũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Nzevania 2:3) Akeeka ũu ĩndĩĩ? Ndeto ya Ngai nĩyathanie ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala malikĩtye andũ mũisyonĩ ũmũnthĩ. Maũndũ asu maendee kwĩkĩka meonany'a kana ĩvinda ya Ngai ya kwosa ĩtambya nĩthengeeu.
3. Twaĩle kwĩka ata?
Twaĩle kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai kwa kũtũmĩa Mbivilia, Ndeto yake. Mbivilia nĩ ta valũa kuma kwa ĩthe wĩ wendo. Ĩtũtavasya ũndũ tũtonya kũtanĩa thayũ mũseango ũmũnthĩ na ũndũ tũkatanĩa thayũ ũtathela ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩvinda yũkĩte. Nĩ w'o, amwe nĩmatonya kũlea kwendeew'a kwona ũitetheew'a ũelewe nĩ Mbivilia. Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa na ĩvinda yũkĩte ĩseo nĩ ũndũ mũseo vyũ ũtaĩle kũkosa.

translation:
1. How and why should we pray to God?
God cares about people greatly and wants what is best for them. He sees everything and knows all things, but he allows us to choose. And children, God wants us to use our agency to help others and make good choices. He expects us to do good things that will bless people around us.
Truly, it is important to remember that God can help us overcome challenges, difficulties, or temptations. Remember his promise. And children, God helps people through their trials and strengthens them. But those who are troubled by Satan's influence often forget God's love and purpose.
2. Is this promise conditional?
Yes, because God commands people to obey him (2 Nephi 2:3). Does he expect something from us? God's commandments are meant to help us avoid harm and find happiness. Other things may seem appealing or feel good, but following God's guidance will always be better.
3. What can we do then?
We can learn more about God by studying the scriptures, His words. The scriptures are a valuable resource for learning truth. They teach us principles that help us make wise decisions and understand God's plan. So, some may wonder how to know if something is true—to study and ponder the scriptures. It is also helpful to seek understanding and allow the Spirit to guide us in understanding the scriptures.

Weteelete Ndakusaa
Availability: In stock
Quick overview
Kwaatianiya na ngewa ya Mutunga...
Kwaatianiya na ngewa ya Mutunga na Syokau Ivuku yii yaatiiye yila yitawa Mutunga na Ngewa Yake. Yina ngewa ya undu kweethiiwe kuma yila Tito Mutunga wenukiye kwoo Kitui kuma India itina wa myaka mingi andu make matesi vala wii. Yila mooniye ta wooiye athelekelya ta mii ya kyoongowa, asyai make nimamutwaaniye kwianana na syithiyo sya Akamba. Indi Mutunga niwaleile kwosa kiveti kila weethiie asyai make mamutwaaniye. Ameiye akeemanziya kiveti ewe mwene.
Niwatumiye nduu na Loisi Syokau na maina kwendana. Mutunga eethiwa aithukuma ndukani ya Muindi vauKitui, ni kana amanthe mbesa sya kwaka musyi wake, akikwatya muno nokwithiwa esa kutwaa Syokau. Indi Syokau niwamanyanie na Ngandi, mwanaa Muindi vala Mutunga wathukumaa. Nimendaniye kithuumukilo, na meevitha mauma Kitui maenda kutua Kambala, Ukanda. Mutunga eekiye ata atiwa ni Syokau? Ni maundu meva meekikiye itina wa kutaanisya kwa Mutunga na Syokau?
Kati wa mavuku ma Kiikamba, yii niyo yina ngewa ndaasa kumavituka oonthe.

translation:
Let us discuss Ndakusaa
Availability: In stock
Quick overview
Intertwined with the story of Mutunga…
Intertwined with the story of Mutunga and Syokau Ivuku this story tells of a man named Mutunga and His Story. It has a story of a land inherited from his father called Tito Mutunga who originated from Kitui and India for many years and his people were very poor. The story is told to be passed down through generations, and his people remember their connection to the customs of the Akamba. This Mutunga was known to visit every home and his people remembered him. He had a lot of kindness and respect.
I was sent with news by Loisi Syokau and names to match. Mutunga is said to have been born in the lands of Muindi from Kitui, but he traveled far from his homeland, meeting here and being given to Syokau. This Syokau was familiar with Ngandi, a child of Muindi like Mutunga was born. I pondered the mystery, and visited places in Kitui going towards Kambala, Ukanda. Did Mutunga ever marry Syokau? Are these new things I discovered in order to reconcile Mutunga and Syokau?
Among the stories of the Kikamba, this is the story most often told.

translation:
A 66-year-old man was found dead in his house this morning following a suspected poisoning incident in Ngomano area of Mathingau Sublocation, Kinyaata location, Yatta constituency in Machakos county.
The deceased has been identified as Munini, father of Chief of Mathingau Sublocation Michael Mutua Mwinzi who said the cause of death is still being investigated, adding that the body has been taken to Matuu Level 4 Hospital awaiting transfer to Kenyatta National Hospital in Nairobi for postmortem examination.
Mwinzi stated that he received information about his son's death at around 8 am.

MANYĨSYA ŨLA W'O
Ĩkũlyo: Kwĩthĩawa ata ĩla mũndũ wakw'a?
Ĩandĩko: Yoa 11:11-14
Ũw'o: Ĩla mũndũ wakw'a thayũ wake nũthelaa. Kwoou tũyaĩle kũkĩa ala akw'ũ. Yesũ aelekanisye kĩkw'ũ na kũkoma. O tondũ wamũthayũũkisye Lasalo, "akamaamũkya" endwa maitũ ala makwie nĩ kana matanĩe kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩngĩ.—Yovu 14:14.
KATHANGŨ KA KŨTHOKYA ANDŨ ŨMBANONĨ (inv)
Ũndũ ũtonya kwasya: Nĩenda ũkũthokya ũke kwĩthukĩĩsya ũvoo wa andũ onthe umĩte Mbivilianĩ na kũlika nĩ mana. Ũkaumĩw'a Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, vala tũthaithĩaa. [Mũnenge kathangũ ka kũmũthokya ũmbanonĩ, na ũimwony'a saa na vala mwĩĩkĩa ũmbano wa Wakyumwa, na ũimũtavya kyongo kya ũvoo wa andũ onthe.]
Ĩkũlyo: Waathi maũmbanonĩ ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova? [Ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka mwony'e vitio Nĩ Kyaũ Kĩendeeaa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ?]

translation:
A farmer and his accomplice were arrested for illegally harvesting sand.
Two people were arrested, aged 7 years each, both residents of Makindu in Makueni County, found with tools used for illegal sand harvesting in a government forest.
The two were released on bail on December 31, 2019, charged with illegal sand harvesting which damages the environment and leads to soil erosion.
They will appear in court to defend themselves against the charges leveled against them. The case was mentioned before Makindu Senior Resident Magistrate Benson Ireri who ordered them to cooperate with investigations regarding environmental damage caused by the illegal sand harvesting which is a serious offense under Kenyan law.
The case of the two will be heard again on January 28th, 2020, when they will present their defense and continue cooperating with investigations regarding environmental damage caused by the illegal sand harvesting which is a serious offense under Kenyan law, punishable by a hefty fine or imprisonment.
He has 14 days to file an appeal against the sentence.

Ula wai munene wa miao kati kati wa mwaka wa 1963 kuvika 1979 Charles Njonjo niwatiwa ni thayu ena ukuu wa myaka 101kumana na kuwaa pneumonia mauvoo ala maikithwa ni musyi wake.
Njonjo ingi ai minister na kati wa maminista ala maivo Kenya yoosa wiiyathi, niwe etiele thayu.
Mwii wa Njonjo niwavivwa vanduni va vata usu kisioni kya Kariokor vala no andu 25 ma musyi metikilwa kulika kwianana na wendi na mwamulo wake e thayu.
President Uhuru Kenyatta ni kati wa ndongoi ila syatuma ngethi sya ukiakisyo kwa musyi wa mututia na kumuweta kwithiwa ei ngavu nene ya nthi ya Kenya.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The late Charles Njonjo who served as Attorney General from 1963 to 1979 has died at the age of 101 after being diagnosed with pneumonia while at his home.
Njonjo also served as a minister in various ministries during Kenya's independence, and he dedicated his life to public service.
The body of Njonjo will be cremated tomorrow at Kariokor cemetery where about 25 relatives and friends are expected to attend the funeral ceremony.
President Uhuru Kenyatta was among those who sent messages of condolence to the family and praised him for his great contribution to the nation of Kenya.

text:
Ndithya ya Ngie ni thina munene vaa Kenya na nthi Atui
Ngwatanio ya nthi sya UN, niyaumya ukanio muvyu kana,nthi kauta ila syi itheo wa Yalata ya nthi sya Africa,mwaiini usu twathi wa desemba, nitonya kuvithukiwa ni ndithya ya Ngie yivo nthi ya Kenya.
Kiu ni kuatiania na kiiutani kingi kila kikimie nthi mutui ya Somalia naa kila kivulanite na Mbua.
Kuatiani na ukunikili usu, mbua mbingi ila yiendeeye vaa Kenya, yiikwatiwa kuniiya ngu kunyaiika muno kwa ngie isu, naa ila ikwikwatiwa kuma nthi mutui ya Somalia kuthi Ethiopia na kuvika ngaliko ya yiulu ya nthi ya Kenya mwaini usu twathi.
Dr Evelyne Namikoye,ena utuika wa tusamu tuu tuniini twakutamba kuma kimanyishoni kya University ya Kenyatta muviani wa uimi, naa easya nzeve undu yikalile ni amwe ma maundu ala matonya kutuma ikumbo ya keeli ya ngie isu isyoka.
Nake muandiki munene muviani wa uimi profesa Hamadi Boga easya silikali nene kwisila muvia wa uimi, niyikiite mivango myailu kuukitana na ngie isu syavika vaa Kenya.
Kwi muthyani wa kyumwa kivitu, vala minister wa muvia wa Uimi Peter Munya unatangaasie kana,Silikali nene nivathite kimanza kya silingi billion 3 na million ngili 200 sya kuukitana na ndithya sya Ngie.
Munya anawetie kana,silikali niyiyumbanitye yiulu wa vata usu, itina wa maovisaa mena utuika kutaa silikali kana, kati kati wa mwai wa desemba mwakani uu, nthi ya Kenya nitonya kuvithukiwa ni ieeta mbingi sya Ngie kuma nthi ingi.

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mbivilia ndĩwetete ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe ĩũlũ wa kũsisya kana kũsoma maũndũ makonetye ngomany'o, kũtũmanĩa mesengyi ikonetye maũndũ ma ngomany'o nthĩnĩ wa indaneti, kana maũndũ angĩ ma mũthemba ũsu. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye ũtheinĩ ũndũ Ngai wĩw'aa ĩũlũ wa meko ala matonya kũtuma andũ mathi nza wa mũtwaano, kana methĩwa na woni ũtaĩle ĩũlũ wa ngomany'o. Kwoona ũndũ mĩsoa ĩno ya Mbivilia yaĩtye:
"Ũaai mamutha menyu ala me kũũ nthĩ: ũlaalai, na ũvuku, na mĩmeo mĩthũku." (Akolosai 3:5) Vandũ va kũaa mĩmeo mĩthũku, kũsisya kana kũsoma maũndũ makonetye ngomany'o kũkĩlasya mĩmeo ĩsu. Kwĩka ũu kũtumaa mũndũ ethĩwa e mũvuku methonĩ ma Ngai.
"Kĩla mũndũ ũsyaasya mũndũ mũka na kũmwĩw'ĩa mũmeo nĩweka ũlaalai nake ngoonĩ yake." (Mathayo 5:28) Kũsisya mavisa makonetye ũlaalai kũtumaa mũndũ ethĩwa na mesilya mathũku ala matonya kũtuma eka maũndũ mataĩle.
"Ĩndĩ ũlaalai, na ũvuku w'onthe, na wendi, maikawetwe katĩ wenyu." (Aeveso 5:3) Tũyaĩle kũwetanga ĩũlũ wa ngomany'o, kũsisya, kana kũsoma ĩũlũ wasyo nĩ kana twĩtanĩthye.
"Mawĩa ma mwĩĩ nĩ moneku, na nĩmo aa: ũlaalai, ũvuku, . . . na maũndũ angĩ mailyĩ ta asu; kũla kwĩ maũndũ asu nĩmũtaa mbee, o ũndũ namũtaie, kana ala mekaa maũndũ ta asu maikatiĩwa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai." (Akalatia 5:
19- 21) Andũ ala masiasya kana kũsoma maũndũ makonetye ngomany'o, ala matũmanĩaa mesengyi kana kũneenany'a ĩũlũ wa maũndũ makonetye ngomany'o indanetinĩ, ala matũmĩaa simũ kũneenea kana kwĩthukĩĩsya maũndũ mataĩle ĩũlũ wa ngomany'o, na ala matũmanĩaa mesengyi kana mavisa makonetye ngomany'o simũnĩ, Ngai amonaa me avuku. Kwĩka maũndũ asu nĩũtuma twananga vyũ ngwatanĩo yitũ na Ngai.

The Bible teaches us individually to carefully examine or read questionable things, to discern evil things that are contrary to godly principles, or things that promote immorality. "Put to death therefore your earthly members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection." (Colossians 3:5) People who indulge in immoral practices, examining or reading questionable things corrupt their morals. Doing so causes a person to sin against God.
"But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath already committed adultery with her in his heart." (Matthew 5:28) Examining images that incite lust causes a person to sin and lead to terrible consequences that cause them to do wrong things.
"Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them." (Ephesians 5:3) Let us avoid looking at immoral things, examining, or reading such things because we are commanded to do so.
"Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, . . . and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I told you in time past, that they which practice such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God." (Galatians 5: 19-21) Those who examine or read questionable things, those who seek out evil things or become addicted to immoral things online, those who use their time to pursue or glorify wrong things through immorality, and those who seek out evil things intentionally, God sees their wickedness. These things cause us to destroy our relationship with God.

text:
Mutandithya munene Jimmy Wanjigi ula uneekiwe mbini kwi iyoo niwalekwa.
Mwiao wa kumulekya waumwa ni musili wa makoani kotini wa milimani vaa ilovi,Bernard Ochoi,na ula waweta wanjigi aneekiiwe mbini uvathukanu na miao.
Wanjigi ekonananawa na ivityo ya kukwatiania na andu angi 6 kumithya mathangu ma kyati na kwosa kitheka kyeene utee na miao, na vala utuku wa kuamukia umunthi ukomie kiseseni kya volisi kya kamukunji.
Onau wiovo aineena na aandiki ma mauvoo,nuleanile na mavityo aa aiweta kwikiwa mbini kwake kwothootheetwe kiiuteti na muno itina wake kutangaasa akokitia kivila kya upresident nthini wa usakuani munene ukite mweni wa 8 mwakani uu.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Prominent businessman Jimmy Wanjigi was yesterday released on bail after being detained.
The application for his release was made by a lawyer from a law firm based in Nairobi, Bernard Ochoi, and another lawyer representing Wanjigi requested he be released on bail and bond.
Wanjigi is accused of conspiring with six other people to commit offenses related to firearms and possessing ammunition illegally, and allegedly spent the night of December 23rd at the Kamukunji police station.
He denied the charges through his lawyers, claiming the allegations against him were politically motivated and intended to prevent him from vying for the presidency during the upcoming general election scheduled for August next year.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ngai oombie mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka, mamanyanae kĩ-mwĩĩ o nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano ve voka. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:
O na kau Mbivilia nĩvatanĩte mũndũũme aikoma na mũndũũme kana mũndũ mũka kũkoma na mũndũ mũka, ndyaĩtye tũmene andũ asu. Vandũ va ũu, Aklĩsto mathuthĩtw'e 'manenge andũ onthe ndaĩa.'
Mũndũũme ũkomaa na mũndũũme ũngĩ kana mũndũ mũka ũkomaa na mũndũ mũka ũngĩ no ethĩwe asyaiwe na wendi ũsu?
Mbivilia ndĩeleetye andũ ta asu masyaawa me na wendi ũilyĩ ata, ĩndĩ nĩyonanĩtye kana andũ onthe masyaawa me na mwelekelo wa kũleana na mĩao ya Ngai. (Alomi 7:
Aũme ala methĩawa na wendi wa kũkoma na aũme, na aka ala methĩawa na wendi wa kũkoma na aka matonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana mamwendeesye Ngai?
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndũkatongoew'e nĩ mwĩĩ waku. Ũaa wendi w'onthe ũtaĩle wa kũkoma na mũndũ." (Akolosai 3:5, Contemporary English Version) Nĩ kana mũndũ oae wendi mũthũku ũla ũtonya kũtuma eka maũndũ mataĩle, no mũvaka atũmĩe nesa ũtonyi wake wa kũsũanĩa. Ethĩwa ũkeekĩaa maũndũ maseo kĩlĩkonĩ kyaku, nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ũkaeka kwĩthĩwa na wendi mũthũku. (Avilivi 4:8; Yakovo 1:
O namo aũme ala methĩawa na wendi wa kũkoma na aka, kana aka ala methĩawa na wendi wa kũkoma na aũme nĩmokitanaa na wendi ũsu nĩ kana mekale kwosana na myolooto ya Mbivilia. Kwa ngelekany'o, ala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae na mekwona ta matesa kũtwaana kana kũtwawa, kana ala me nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano na ũyĩthĩa ũmwe ndatonya kwĩanĩsya wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ wa ũla ũngĩ, nĩmatataa kũsiĩĩa wendi ũsu o na ĩla matatwa. Nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu, methĩawa matonya kwĩkala me atanu. Kwoou, o namo aũme ala methĩawa na wendi wa kũkoma na aũme, kana aka ala methĩawa na wendi wa kũkoma na aka no makĩlye vinya wendi ũsu ethĩwa nĩmekwenda kũmwendeesya Ngai.

"Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ya ndĩni yĩsĩkĩe mũno. Ĩndĩ nĩ ĩvuku yĩeni na yĩyĩsa kũtethya andũ ma China."—LIN, CHINA.
"Ndiona ũndũ ndonya kũelewa Mbivilia, nao nĩnaemiwe nĩ kũelewa nesa mavuku ma ndĩni ĩla nĩendaa ya Hindu."—AMIT, INDIA.
"Nĩnĩnengete Mbivilia ndaĩa nũndũ nĩ ĩvuku ya tene na yĩthooaw'a mũno. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ndyaaĩsa kwona Mbivilia."—YUMIKO, JAPAN.
Andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmanengete Mbivilia ndaĩa. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, no methĩwe matesĩ kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kana makethĩwa mesĩ o tũmaũndũ tũnini Mbivilianĩ. Ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ kwa andũ aingĩ ma Asia, o na kwa angĩ aingĩ ala mekalaa nthĩ ila Mbivilia ĩkwatĩkanaa laisi.
Ĩndĩ no wĩkũlye, 'Nĩkĩ naĩle kwendeew'a nĩ kũmĩelewa Mbivilia?' Kũmanya kĩla ĩvuku yĩĩ ĩtheu yĩneeneete no kũũtetheesye:
Ũkethĩwa wĩ mũtanu na wĩ mwĩanĩe
Ũkethĩwa ũtonya kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna ma mũsyĩ
Ũkethĩwa ũtonya kũmĩanĩsya na mawĩmakĩo
Ũkethĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na andũ
Ũkethĩwa ũtonya kũtũmĩa mbesa nesa
Kwa ngelekany'o, kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Yoshiko kuma Japan. Nĩwasaanĩaw'a nĩ kĩla Mbivilia ĩneeneaa na avanga kũmĩsoma. Kweethĩiwe ata? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mbivilia nĩndetheesye ngamanya nĩkĩ nĩ thayũ, na ĩkandetheesya ngethĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte." Aendeee kwasya: "Yu nĩthĩawa na ũtanu mbee wa ũndũ nailyĩ ndemanyĩĩtye Mbivilia." Nake Amit, ũla ũwetiwe mbeenĩ nĩwatwie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnaseng'ie mũno nũndũ neethĩie Mbivilia yĩ na ũvoo ũtonya kũtethya kĩla mũndũ."
Mbivilia nĩtetheesye andũ milioni mbingĩ. Wĩona ata ũkamĩsoma na ũyona ũndũ ĩtonya ũkũtethya?

translation:
The wife of noble character who can find? She is worth far more than rubies. Her husband has full confidence in her and lacks nothing of value. She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.
She gets up while it is still night; she provides food for her family and assigns her portion to the servants. She considers a field and buys it; out of her earnings she plants a vineyard. She sets about her work vigorously; her arms are strong for its tasks. She sees that her trading is successful and her lamp does not go out at night. She extends her hand to the poor and opens her arms to the needy. She does not fear snow for her household; for all her household are clothed in linen. She makes coverings for her bed; she has made fine linen and purple cloth. Her husband is known at the city gate when he sits among the elders. She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies belts to the merchants. Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she smiles at the days to come. She speaks with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue. She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat idle bread. Her children arise and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her: "Many women have done wonderful things, but you surpass them all." Charm is deceptive, and beauty is fleeting; but a woman who fears the Lord is to be praised. Give her the reward she deserves, and let her works bring her praise at the city gate.
This verse applies to the virtuous woman
31:13-27
She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands. She is like the merchant ships, bringing goods from afar. She rises while it is still dark and provides provisions for her family. She acquires a field and plants a vineyard. With the strength of her arms she prepares her food. She tests the merchandise and seals a deal. She extends her hand to the poor and opens her arms to the needy. She does not worry about her household's future; she is prepared for harsh winters. She makes quilts and clothes for everyone in her home. She judges whether her business is profitable. Her lamp burns late into the night. She puts her hands to the distaff, and her hands grasp the spindle. She is not afraid of the snow for her family; for they are all clothed in warm garments. This verse applies to the virtuous woman and it has meaning
31:30
Praise her for she deserves it, and let her accomplishments be celebrated throughout the land.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ĩĩ. Yesũ oonanisye kana aatĩĩi make nĩmaĩle kũiitwa ĩla waisye: "
Ala mate awau mati vata wa mũiiti, ĩndĩ no ala awau." (Mathayo 9:12) O na kũtw'ĩka Mbivilia ti ĩvuku ya ũiiti, yĩ na myolooto ĩtonya kũtetheesya ala me na wendi wa kũmwendeesya Ngai.
Makũlyo ala waĩle kwĩkũlya
1. Yo nĩnĩsĩ nesa ũiiti ũla ngũiitwa? Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya twĩke ũkunĩkĩli tũkwate ũvoo w'onthe nesa vandũ va '
kwĩtĩkĩla kĩla ndeto.'—Nthimo 14:15.
2. Nĩnaĩle kũkũlya matakĩtalĩ angĩ woni woo ĩũlũ wa ũiiti ũsu? Kwĩthĩwa na "
wingĩ wa atai" nĩ ũndũ wa vata na mũno mũno ethĩwa ũwaĩte ũwau mũthũku mũno.—Nthimo 15:22.
3. Ũiiti ũsu nũtonya kũtuma nĩtũla mwĩao wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa 'Meko ma Atũmwa 15:20.
4. Ũiiti ũsu nũkonanĩtye na maveva mavuku? Mbivilia nĩleanĩte na "
ũoi." (Akalatia 5:19-21) Nĩ kana ũmanye ethĩwa ũiiti mũna nũkonanĩtye na maveva mavuku ĩkũlye makũlyo aa:

Ũla ũkũkũiita aĩkĩĩaa kana ũwau ũsu wumanĩte na ũoi kana nĩ ngai ithatĩte?
Ve nthembo syĩkumw'a, kana ve syĩthĩo ingĩ ikonetye maveva mavuku ikwĩkwa ũiseũvĩw'a ndawa kana ũimĩnyw'a?

Wũmĩĩsyo wenyu ũmanyĩke nĩ andũ onthe." (Avilivi 4:5) Wũmĩĩsyo ũkaũtetheesya ũatĩĩe "

translation:
The Bible Says
I. Jesus showed mercy, even when people thought he was wrong to associate with sinners, saying:
"Those who are healthy do not need a doctor, but those who are sick do." (Matthew 9:12) And understanding the Bible can help us show compassion like Jesus did and encourage others to turn to God.
Why We Should Show Mercy
1. Why is it important to be merciful? The Bible helps us see things from God's perspective so we can be more understanding of others.—Proverbs 14:15.
2. How can we show practical mercy? Considering "the weight of the matter" is wise and can prevent us from making hasty judgments.—Proverbs 15:22.
3. Being merciful can lead others to appreciate God's standards.—Acts 15:20.
4. Does being merciful mean overlooking serious sin? The Bible does not condone wickedness.—Galatians 5:19-21. But if you wonder whether a certain act is seriously sinful, consider the following:
What should you do if you are unsure about something?
What if you feel inclined to do something that you know is wrong or that violates Bible principles?
Are there times when it might be appropriate to overlook minor offenses rather than risk causing offense or damaging relationships?
5. What can affect our ability to show mercy? The Bible says: "Let your speech always be gracious." (Colossians 4:5) Our speech can either build up or tear down others.—Colossians 1:10; Matthew 5:3.

Ũvoo Mũseo Kuma kwa Ngai!
Kavuku kaa nĩkeũkũtetheesya ũtanĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia. Ĩla ũũsoma Maandĩko asu, sũanĩĩa ũndũ meũsũngĩa makũlyo aa.
Ĩmanyĩsye nĩ kana ũmanye ũvoo mũseo kuma kwa Ngai nĩ kyaũ, nĩkĩ nĩ wa vata, na kĩla waĩle kwĩka.
Ngai e syĩtwa na nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa?
Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũĩkĩĩthya kana Mbivilia nĩ ya w'o?
Ĩmanyĩsye nĩkĩ Yesũ wakwie, wovosyo nĩ kyau na Yesũ aendee kwĩka ata.
Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye nĩkĩ Ngai woombie nthĩ, mathĩna makathela ĩndĩĩ na nũũ ũla ũkekala nthĩnĩ wa Valatiso ĩla yũkĩte.
Kwĩthĩawa ata yĩla twakw'a? Tũkamona ĩngĩ endwa maitũ ala makwie?
Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nũũ, na Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũkeeka ata?
Ũthũku wambĩĩie ata, na nĩkĩ Ngai ũekete ũendee? Mathĩna makathela?
Yeova, Ngai mũtanu, nĩwendaa mĩsyĩ yĩthĩwe na ũtanu. Ĩmanyĩsye wone ũtao wa Mbivilia kwa aume, aka, asyai , na syana..
Kwĩ ndĩni o ĩmwe ya w'o? Sũanĩĩa movano aa atano ma kumanya athaithi maw'o.
Yesu nĩwaeleisye nĩkĩ twĩ na vata wa kũtongoew'a na nĩ myolooto ĩlĩ yĩva ĩla ya vata vyũ.
Ĩmanyĩsye wone Ngai nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya syonthe, twaĩle kũvoya ata, na tũtonya kũmũthengeea Ngai ata.
Ve ĩvinda andũ onthe makeethĩwa na ngwatanĩo nthĩnĩ wa kũmũthaitha Ngai ũla wa w'o weka?
Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye nĩkĩ na ũndũ Aklĩsto ma w'o mombanĩtw'e.
Ũmanyi waku ĩũlũ wa Ngai ũtonya kũtetheesya angĩ ata? Ũtonya kũtanĩa ũnyanya ũilyĩ ata vamwe na Ngai?

Eka twĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa mwanake watangĩĩie thayũ wa mũndũ wasyaanĩw'e na inyia wake. Mũndũ ũsu wasyaanĩw'e na inyia wa mwanake ũsu eetawa mũtũmwa Vaulo. Mwanake ũsu ndawetetwe ĩsyĩtwa yake, ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ nĩweekie ũndũ woonanisye kana ndaĩ na wia. Nũkwenda kũmanya ũndũ weekie?—
Vaulo aĩ mwove ku Yelusaleme. Oovetwe nũndũ wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Andũ amwe nĩmamũmenete Vaulo, na kwoou mavanga mũvango mũthũku. Maisye: 'Ekai tũmũkũlye mũnene wa asikalĩ atũme asikalĩ make mamũtwae Vaulo kotinĩ. Ithyĩ twĩĩvitha nzĩanĩ, na ĩla Vaulo ũkwĩsĩla vau, tũimũaa!'
Mwanake wa mwĩĩtu wasyaanĩw'e na Vaulo nĩweewie ĩũlũ wa mũvango ũsu. Eekie ata? Aendie vala Vaulo woovetwe na amũtavya. Vaulo eew'a ũndũ ũsu oou, nĩwamũtũmie mwanake ũsu athi akamũtavye mũnene wa asikalĩ ĩũlũ wa mũvango ũsu mũthũku. Wĩona waĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa mwanake ũsu kũneena na mũnene wa asikalĩ?— Aiee, nũndũ mũnene ũsu wa asikalĩ aĩ mũndũ wanengetwe ndaĩa. Ĩndĩ, mwanake ũsu ndaĩ na wia, na nĩwaneenie na mũnene ũsu wa asikalĩ.
Mũnene ũsu nĩweesĩ nesa ũndũ waĩle kwĩka. Atũmie asikalĩ vakuvĩ 500 mamũsũvĩe Vaulo! Ameie mamũtwae Vaulo Kaisalea ũtukũ ũsu. Andũ asu athũku nĩmamũaie Vaulo?— Aiee, nĩmaemiwe nĩ kwĩka ũu! Mũvango woo mũthũku watheleile o vau.
Ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na ngewa ĩno?— O naku no wĩthĩwe ũte na wia ta mwanake ũsu. Tũyaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wia ĩla tũũtavya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Ũkaendeea kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Yeova ũteũkĩa?— Weeka ũu, nũtonya kũtangĩĩa thayũ wa mũndũ.

translation:
We have heard about the case of a child who was brought before the council of elders by his father. This man who was brought before the council of his father was named Paul. This child was given a name, and we want to know whether there is something he did wrong or not. Do you want to know what he did?—
Paul went to Jerusalem. He was accused of disturbing the peace of Jesus. Some people opposed Paul, and they stirred up a great commotion. They said: 'Let us kill this evil person who disturbs the peace and stirs up trouble among our people. But let us act quickly, and if Paul escapes from us, we will seize him!'
The child of the person who opposed Paul understood the commotion. Why is that? He went to see Paul because he had been accused. Paul knew about this matter and sent the child to ask the council of elders about the commotion. Do you think this child would dare to speak to the council of elders?— Indeed, this important council of elders is a very powerful person. Therefore, the child was afraid, and he spoke to the important council of elders.
This important elder could not understand what was happening. He sent 500 soldiers to arrest Paul! Fortunately, they did not arrest Paul that night. Did those people seize Paul?— No, they were prevented from doing so! That great commotion ended without success.
Will you be willing to cooperate with us?— Well, you can decide for yourself whether to help this child. Let us continue to preach to people about Jehovah. Will you continue to preach about Jehovah until the end?— Yes, I am willing to start today.

Kavuku keũ ketawa 'The Bible—The Gospel According to Matthew' nĩyaumiw'e Japan. Ke na maũndũ meva? Kaseũviw'e nĩkĩ?

We ũtonya kũsũngĩa ĩkũlyo yĩu ata? Andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana Ngai nĩwĩtĩkĩlanaa na kaũ. Masũanĩaa ũu nũndũ nĩmasomaa Mbivilianĩ kana Ngai nĩweeyĩaĩaa athũkũmi amwe make ma ĩvinda ya tene makokite. Angĩ namo nĩmesĩ kana Mwana wa Ngai, Yesũ, amanyĩisye aatĩĩi make kana nĩmaĩle kwenda amaitha moo. (Mathayo 5:43, 44) Kwoou maasyaa kana ve ĩvinda yavikie woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ waalyũka, na ũmũnthĩ Ngai ndendaa andũ mayũkita.
We wĩona ata? Ngai nĩwĩtĩkĩlanaa na makaũ ala mokitawa ũmũnthĩ? Ethĩwa nĩwĩtĩkĩlanaa namo, nĩ ngalĩko yĩva ũkwataa mbau? Kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu no kũũtetheesye ũkamanya woni waku ĩũlũ wa kaũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, twasye ve kaũ ũendeee vandũ na ũimanya kana Ngai nũkwĩtĩkĩlana na kaũ ũsu, o na nũkũkwata mbau ngalĩko ĩla we mwene wendeeaw'a nĩyo kaũnĩ ũsu, vate nzika no wĩw'e mũyo nũndũ wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana nĩmũũsinda. Nao wĩw'a ata ũkamanya kana Ngai akwete mbau amaitha maku? Vakethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, nĩvatonyeka ũkasũanĩa kũalyũla ũtwi waku.
Ve ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata mũno twaĩle kũũsũanĩa kwa ũliku. Kũmanya woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ no kũtume ũalyũla woni waku ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Ethĩwa wĩ katĩ wa andũ milioni mbingĩ ala maũmĩĩtw'e nĩ makaũ, vate nzika no wendeew'e nĩ kũmanya ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo aa: We Ngai ailyĩ ũndũ andũ amwe maasya kana nĩwendete kaũ na nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa andũ makwatwe nĩ mathĩna ala maumanaa na kaũ? We nũthĩnĩkaa ĩla andũ maendeee na kũvinyĩĩwa mavindanĩ ma kaũ?
No ũseng'e mũno kũmanya kana Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte makũlyo asu kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na woni wa andũ. O na ĩngĩ woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ ndwaalyũka. Ekai twone ũndũ Mbivilia yĩeleetye woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ ĩvindanĩ ya tene na ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ. Ũu nũũtũtetheesya kũmanya woni wake ĩũlũ wa kaũ na tũimanya ethĩwa ĩvinda yũkĩte nĩkũkethĩwa na makaũ.

translation:
Do we really need to keep asking questions? Many people wonder whether God takes sides with someone. They wonder why bad things happen to good people, or why some wicked people seem to prosper. But doesn't the Bible show us that Jehovah cares about everyone? (Matthew 5:43, 44) It says that he makes his sun rise on both the righteous and the unrighteous and sends rain to both the just and the unjust. Doesn't this show that God loves all mankind?
Don't we see that? Does God take sides with anyone at all? If he does so with me, would it be fair? To favor some over others based on their qualities would not demonstrate justice. For example, let us think about how he deals with humans and whether God favors some over others, or whether he shows partiality like we might. If he did, wouldn't that be unfair to those who don't receive such favor, and wouldn't they have reason to complain? So, do you think God shows partiality toward anyone? The elders rightly encourage us to examine our own hearts.
But there is something more important than simply avoiding partiality. Knowing what God thinks and wanting to please him should motivate us to treat others as God treats them. However, millions of people believe that God favors certain ones. They feel that God answers the prayers of some more than others because of their position or circumstances. Do they ask themselves whether Jehovah actually does such a thing, or whether they are influenced by wrong thinking?
So, let us investigate whether the Bible supports the idea that God shows partiality toward individuals. And let us see what God thinks about this matter. Let us examine what the Bible reveals about God's view of fairness and what Jesus taught regarding this. This will help us understand what God thinks and realize that the belief in partiality originates from Satan.

Ndongoi kivathukanyo nisyeendeeye kutuma ngethi sya ukiakisyo kuatiania na kikwu kya ula wa ndongoi ya uthukumi vaa Kenya Dr. Richard Leakey.
Nthini wa utumani wa President Uhuru Kenyatta niumuwetie ta ndongoi yai kithito kusuuvia mawithyululuko na muthukumi weeyumitye iandani kivathukanyo ila wakwaatiiye.
Munini wa president Dr William Ruto otaou niwaamukaathiiya Leakey kwa kila ukuweta ta weyumitye kusuuvia mawiithyululuko na ingi kuikiithya uthukumi museo na utongoi wa wiananu maunduni ma uteti.

translation:
The passing of renowned paleontologist has sent condolences to the family of the late Dr. Richard Leakey, a Kenyan national hero.
During the presidency of Uhuru Kenyatta, I extended my sympathies to the family, recognizing his contribution to archaeological discoveries and economic development, though they were delayed.
President Dr William Ruto's spokesperson stated that Leakey will be remembered for his dedication to archaeological work and his significant role in promoting tourism and cultural heritage.
Leakey passed away at the age of 78, just hours after the death of another prominent figure, retired Attorney General Charles Njonjo.

Kwakũna visa ũtwĩe Kalilii na nĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ. Wauma vaasa wũkĩte Yelusaleme kũtanĩa Mboka ya Malwanda. Mũsyĩ ũsu wa Yelusaleme wusũĩte athaithi angĩ ma Yeova kuma isio syĩ vaasa. O ta athaithi asu angĩ, wĩenda kũmumĩsya Yeova nthembo. Kwoou, ĩtina wa kwosa mbũi yaku, ũyambĩĩa savalĩ wĩsĩle tũsĩlanĩ twĩ andũ aingĩ taoninĩ ĩsu ũendete ĩkalũnĩ. Wavika ĩkalũnĩ, ũyĩthĩa yusĩe andũ mayenda kumya nthembo o taku. Na ĩndĩ andũ ala angĩ mamina kumya nthembo kwa mũthembi, ũivikĩwa umye mbũi yaku. Ndatĩkanĩ ĩsu, ũililikana kana mwana-a-au, ũla ũtonya kwĩthĩwa e o vu andũnĩ ala angĩ kana e taoninĩ ya Yelusaleme, e na ũndũ naku. Veethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, Yesũ nĩ ũeleetye ũndũ waĩle kwĩka. (Soma Mathayo 5:24.) Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana wĩw'ane na mwana-a-au o tondũ Yesũ waisye? Maũndũnĩ ala mawetetwe vaa ĩtheo, ĩkĩa ũvano vala ũkwona ve ũsũngĩo ũla waĩle.

kũneena na mwana-a-au o ĩla ũkwona e na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũthata
kũtata ũlũnge woni wa mwana-a-au ethĩwa wĩona athataa mĩtũkĩ kana o nake no ũvĩtĩtye
kwĩthukĩĩsya nesa ĩla mwana-a-au ũkwĩyĩelesya, na o na ethĩwa ndũnamũelewa nesa, mwĩtye ũekeo kuma ngoonĩ nũndũ eĩw'a avĩtĩw'e kana nũndũ ve ũndũ ũtaĩle wĩkĩkie o na kau ndwĩĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũtuma ũndũ ũsu wĩkĩka
MWANA-A-AU AĨLE . . .
kũtavya ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ ũndũ ũmũvĩtĩsye nĩ kana metĩkĩlane nake ũndũnĩ ũsu

O na kau tũyumasya nthembo sya nyamũ ũthaithinĩ witũ, Yesũ amanyĩisye kyaũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ kwĩthĩwa na mũuo na ana-a-asa kũkonanĩtye na kũmũthaitha Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla wĩtĩkĩlaa?

translation:
Whenever you have a dispute with your brother, settle it with him privately and do not bring it up to Jesus to intervene. Some went from Samaria to Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Tabernacles. The people of Jerusalem were saying about Him that He was a good man because they saw His miracles. But some said, "He deceives the people," while others said, "No, He teaches with authority." So, when someone offends you, try to reconcile with him first so that we can be united with many people like us who go to heaven. By doing heaven, you will show kindness to those who want to know God's purpose. And among those other people who want to know God faithfully, you will find peace. Remember this, if you are angry with your brother, he will be judged by all people, both here and in Jerusalem, and also with you. Consider this, Jesus taught how to resolve matters quickly. (Read Matthew 5:24.) Can you resolve things even if you are upset with your brother or because Jesus intervened? Other matters are forgiven by God, knowing that you have done everything possible to make amends.
TO RESOLVE…
disputes with your brother and see peace and use the opportunity to avoid trouble.
To avoid anger towards your brother, look at his mistakes and do not hold grudges, and always remember that forgiveness is better than holding onto resentment and bitterness.
BROTHER TO RESOLVE…
to forgive everyone and accept whatever offense he has committed against you.
To listen to his reasons carefully, and forgive all other offenses, and strive to forgive him.
To understand whether he regrets speaking to you badly and whether he is sorry and humble, and then help him to turn away from evil deeds or from any wrongdoing and offer guidance.
And let us pray for the sake of our souls, Jesus showed us the importance of dealing with issues promptly and teaching our children to honor God through the way we live.

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ĩĩ, nũndũ ũtethyo ũla mũseo vyũ wumaa kwa "
Ngai, ũla ũkiakiasya, wĩkĩaa vinya, ũvuũũkasya na ũtanĩthasya ala makw'ĩte ngoo."
Ngai atetheeasya ata ala makw'ĩte ngoo?
Nũmanengae vinya. Ngai '
nũkũvuũũkasya na kũũtanĩthya,' ti kwa kũũminĩa thĩna ũla wĩ naw'o ĩndĩ kwa kũsũngĩa mboya syaku ĩla wamũvoya vinya wa kũmĩĩsya. (Avilivi 4:13) No wĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana akasũngĩa mboya syaku nũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye: "
Yeova e vakuvĩ na ala matũlĩkĩte ngoo, na nũtangĩĩaa ala mekwĩlila vevanĩ." (Savuli 34:18) Vate nzika, Yeova no amanye ĩla ũkwenda ũtethyo o na ĩla ũtatonya kũmũtavya mboyanĩ.
—Alomi 8:26, 27.
Kwĩsĩla ngelekany'o sya angĩ. Mũandĩki ũmwe wa Mbivilia avoyie: "
Nĩ thĩnanĩ mũnene nĩngũkwĩkaĩla." Mũandĩki ũũ wa Savuli nĩwakwataa vinya ĩla walilikana kana Ngai nũekeaa. Aisye: "
Ethĩwa we Mwĩaĩi Ngai ũkatala mavĩtyo maitũ, nũũ ũla wĩvonoka? Ĩndĩ we nũtũekeaa, nĩ kana tũkũnenge ndaĩa."
—Savuli 130:1, 3, 4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Nũmanengae wĩkwatyo. O na eka kũtũnenga ũkiakisyo ũmũnthĩ, Ngai nũtwathĩte kana akamina mathĩna ala matumaa tũkw'a ngoo. Ĩla ũkeanĩsya watho ũsu, "
maũndũ ma mbee [ala nĩ vamwe na kũkw'a ngoo] matikalilikanwa, o na matikalika kĩlilikanonĩ."
—Isaia 65:17.
Lilikana: O na kau Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩtĩkĩlĩte kana Ngai no aitetheesye, syo nimanthaa ũiiti ĩla syakw'a ngoo mũno weethĩa nĩsyaĩle kwona ndakĩtalĩ. (Maliko 2:17) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, vaiĩ ũiiti ũla tũtonya kwasya nĩw'o mũseo. Na nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩu, kĩla mũndũ nĩwe waĩle kwĩtw'ĩĩa ũiiti ũla ũkwona waĩle.

translation:
The Book of Proverbs says
Yes, a beautiful saying is worth more than pearls because "
God, who makes things possible, will make you successful and give you honor so that your name will be known."
Does God really help people become famous?
Absolutely. God '
makes them successful and honors them,' not to prove something to us, but to encourage others who may be struggling to trust him. (Proverbs 4:13) So don't be discouraged or stop trying; the book of Proverbs also says: "
Jehovah supports everyone who falls and straightens up those who are bent over." (Psalm 34:18) That is why Jehovah knows what you are going through and what you are able to endure.
—Psalm 8:26, 27.
Consider some examples. One Bible writer said: "
I was very weak, and I almost gave up." This writer of Psalm admitted that he wondered whether God cared. He wrote: "
O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger or discipline me in your fury! Be merciful to me, for I am weak."
—Psalm 130:1, 3, 4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Don't despair. And even when circumstances seem impossible, God can fulfill his purpose. As for the new heavens [and a new earth], they will not be shaken,"
"but everything old will pass away."
—Isaiah 65:17.
Remember: Even though Jehovah's day has not yet come, it is certain that God will act, just as he promised. So let us continue to look forward to it with confidence. (Mark 2:17) In the meantime, let us focus on doing what we can to please him. And with good reason, each person wants to know what pleases him.

President William Ruto na muwandu wa mbee Racheal Ruto nimavika nthi ya Uungelesa mathikoni ma Queen Elizabeth II.
Otaou itina wa mathiko Ruto vamwe na ndongoi ingi sya silikali nimekwithiwa maivika umbanoni wa 77 wa ngwatano ya nthi, UN General Assembly ula utwaiwa kuya New York.
Ruto eweta kana kululumiilya utianya na nthi sya nza nikuukalata mawalyuku vaa Kenya.
Ruto etikilitwe kuvika mathikoni asu eona muka weka oundumwe na ndongoi ingi ithoketwe vala makatumia mbasi kuvika kisioni kya mathiko Westminister Abbey, vala ndongoi kuma nthi ya Russia, Belarus, Myanmar na Korea ya yiulu matathoketwe kuatiania na kwithiwa nthi ii itena mituo miseo.
Ruto eikwatiwa kusyoka vaa Kenya wakana kyumwa twiukwata.

translation:
President William Ruto and his wife Rachel Ruto have attended the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in England.
The Kenyan delegation led by President Ruto and other dignitaries were invited to attend the 77th session of the United Nations General Assembly being held in New York.
Ruto stated that he will strengthen relations with countries to promote development in Kenya.
Ruto was allowed to attend the funeral because he is among the leaders who were given permission to use transport to attend the state funeral at Westminster Abbey, while leaders from Russia, Belarus, Myanmar and North Korea were not allowed to attend and were barred from entering the country.
Ruto was received upon arrival in Kenya by well-wishers.

YEOVA Ngai avevee athani aingĩ Mbivilianĩ kũelesya ĩũlũ wa kũsyawa na wĩa wa Masia nĩ kana atũtetheesye kũmũmanya Mwovosya ũsu wathanĩtwe. Wathani ũsu wa Mbivilia nĩweanĩie ĩũlũ wa Yesũ Klĩsto. Wathani ũsu wĩ maũndũ maingĩ na ũndũ meanĩĩte nĩ ũndũ wa ũsengy'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, sisya wathani ũla wathanĩte ĩũlũ wa kũsyawa na kwĩana kwa Masia.
Mwathani Isaia athanie kana Masia akeethĩwa e wa nzyawa ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti. (Isaia 9:7) Na kwa w'o Yesũ asyaiwe nzyawanĩ ya Ndaviti.
Mika, mwathani ũngĩ wa Ngai athanie kana Yesũ akatw'ĩka mũsumbĩ na akasyaĩwa "Mbethi-leemu ya Evilatha." (Mika 5:2) Yĩla Yesũ wasyaiwe kwaĩ mĩsyĩ ĩlĩ kũya Isilaeli yeetawa Mbethi-leemu. Mũsyĩ ũmwe waĩ vakuvĩ na Nasaleti, na ũla ũngĩ waĩ vakuvĩ na Yelusaleme, ku Yutia. Mũsyĩ wa Mbethi-leemu ũla waĩ vakuvĩ na Yelusaleme, mbeenĩ weetawa Evilatha. Yesũ asyaĩwe mũsyĩ ũsu o tondũ kwathanĩtwe.
Wathani ũngĩ wa Mbivilia wathanĩte kana mwana wa Ngai 'akeetwa kuma Misili.' Yesũ e kana nĩwatwaiwe Misili. Nĩwatũngiwe kuma nthĩ ĩsu ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kya Elote, na kwoou wathani weanĩa.
Ĩthangũnĩ ya 200 ĩvukunĩ yĩĩ maandĩko ala me ĩtheo wa ndeto "Wathani" nĩmonanĩtye maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Masia. Kwamasyaanĩsye na ala me ĩtheo wa ndeto "Kwĩanĩa." Kwĩka ũu nĩkũũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo waku kana Ndeto ya Ngai nĩ ya w'o.
Manya kana maandĩko asu ma wathani maandĩkiwe myaka maana maingĩ mbee wa Yesũ atanasyawa. Yesũ aisye: 'No mũvaka maũndũ onthe meanĩw'e ala maandĩkĩtwe ũndũ wakwa Mĩaonĩ ya Mose, na mavukunĩ ma athani, na ĩvukunĩ ya Savuli.' (Luka 24:44) Wasoma Mbivilianĩ yaku nũkwona kĩla ũndũ wathaniwe ĩũlũ wa Yesũ nĩweanĩie nesa vyũ!

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ngai nĩwĩtĩkĩlasya mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka ma ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o matwaane nũndũ methonĩ make andũ ma ngo syonthe nĩmeanene. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Ngai ti mwendeesya wa andũ . . . , o na ethĩwa nĩ wa mbaĩ yĩva."—Meko ma Atũmwa 10:34, 35, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Kwoona myolooto ĩngĩ ya Mbivilia ĩkonetye mũtwaano na yonanĩtye kana ngo syonthe nĩsianene.
Ngo syonthe syumĩte vandũ vamwe
Andũ onthe maumie kwa mũndũ wa mbee, Atamu, na mũka wake, Eva, ũla Mbivilia ĩmwĩtaa "inyia wa onthe me thayũ." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:20) Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩu, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai "oombie mbaĩ syonthe sya andũ kuma mũndũnĩ ũmwe." (Meko ma Atũmwa 17:26) Kwoou andũ onthe nĩ ta mũsyĩ ũmwe o na ethĩwa nĩ ma ũko wĩva. Ĩndĩ nata ethĩwa vala wĩkalaa ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nimenanĩte, kana ngo imwe syonaa syĩ sya kĩlasi kwĩ ingĩ?
Andũ oĩ 'nĩmataanaa'
O na kau Ngai nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩtye mũndũ kũtwaa mũndũ ũte wa ũko wake, ti andũ onthe monaa ũu waĩle. (Isaia 55:8, 9) Ethĩwa wĩsũanĩa kũtwaa mũndũ wa ũko ũngĩ, nĩwaĩle kũneenea maũndũ aa wĩ na ũsu mũkwenda kũtwaana:
Mũkeekaa ata ĩla mwakwata mathĩna kuma kwa andũ ma ũko, kana ma mũsyĩ waku?
Mũkatetheesya syana syenyu ata iikethĩwe na kĩmena kya mbaĩ?
'Kũtaana' kwa nzĩa ĩno nĩkũtonya kũtetheesya mũtwaano waku ũkaĩla.—Nthimo 13:10; 21:5.

translation:
The Bible teaches
God judges people individually and does not condemn everyone because of the mistakes of others; rather, each person will be judged according to their own deeds—that is, all people are righteous. The Bible says: "God is not partial to persons… and his judgment is based on righteousness."—Acts 10:34, 35, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Many other teachings of the Bible agree with this and show that God is just.
All people are imperfect
All people came from one man, Adam, and his wife, Eve, whom the Bible calls "the ancestor of all mankind." (Genesis 3:20) In addition, the Bible states that God made "every nation of men" from one man. (Acts 17:26) So all people are of one family, and their origin is the same. Wouldn't it be unfair if everyone were condemned because of what some have done, or if some were favored over others?
People are 'accountable'
But God judges each person according to their own actions, not according to those of others. (Isaiah 55:8, 9) His judgment requires each person to be accountable for their own decisions and actions:
Will you blame others for your own mistakes?
Will you allow yourself to be influenced by the wrong desires?
'Accountability' in this sense means taking responsibility for your own actions.—Proverbs 13:10; 21:5.

Ann Kananu Mwenda niwaithwa kithitu kya wia kutwika gavana wa katatu wa county ya Ilovi.

Kananu ethukuma vakuvi na General Mohammed Badi ula utongoesye muvia wa kuthinikia musyi wa Ilovi wa Nairobi Metropolitan services.
Kananu ethiitwe e gavana wa kavinda wa Ilovi kuma mwaka uu waambiiya kuma aavithwa ta munini wa gavana na itambya ya kuavithwa ta gavana yasyiiwa ni ikwani yila yathakiswe ni ula unatwiiye e gavana Mike Mbuvi Sonko vala kyumwani kithelu koti wa yiulu unekisye itheka ikuani yii undu ula umisye lingilia ya kyathi kii kutwaiiwa.
Metho ma Akenya masyaiisye ula ukwolootwa ta munini wa gavana kavindani kaa vatyele myai ikumi unyuvani munene utwaiiwe.

translation:
Ann Kananu Mwenda was sworn in as the third governor of Illovi County.
Kananu was sworn in during an economic downturn while everything was expensive and there were many challenges and she was sworn in at the KICC dome in Illovi city at the COMESA grounds.
Kananu worked with General Mohammed Badi who was transferred from heading the city of Illovi under Nairobi Metropolitan services.
Kananu was appointed governor of Illovi County this year after being nominated as deputy governor and the process of nominating a deputy governor was left to the assembly which had approved the former governor Mike Mbuvi Sonko whose impeachment case is still ongoing causing confusion about this matter.
Kenyan citizens have expressed that the nomination of a deputy governor should be done through a public vote so that people can choose well.

Vulongulamu ya JW Library nĩ vulongulamu ya kombiũta (software application) ĩte ya ũthoosya ĩtonya kũtũmĩwa kumya Mbivilia, mavuku, vitio, na syĩndũ ingĩ simũnĩ, tambuletinĩ, kana kombiũtanĩ.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KUMYA JW LIBRARY INDANETINĨ: Vingũa data nĩ kana wĩthĩe simũ yaku no ĩlike Indanetinĩ, na ĩndĩ ũithi kwa app store simũnĩ yaku, na wavingũa vu, mantha JW Library na ĩndĩ ũyĩkĩa vulongulamu ĩsu simũnĩ. Vulongulamu ĩsu no ĩlike simũnĩ kana tambuletinĩ sya mĩthemba yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Wavingũa Indaneti kana data, vingũa vulongulamu ya JW Library, na ĩndĩ ũinyuva mavuku, vitio, kana o kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩla ũkwenda kumya. Ethĩwa simũ yaku ndĩtonya kũlika indanetinĩ wĩ mũsyĩ kwaku, no ũthi vandũ vangĩ ĩtonya kũlika indaneti ta ũtelinĩ, ndukanĩ, kana Nyũmbanĩ yenyu ya Ũsumbĩ. Wamina kumya ĩvuku nthĩnĩ wa JW Library, vaikethĩawa vata wa kũvingũa Indaneti nĩ kana ũyĩsome. Nũndũ mavinda kwa mavinda JW Library nĩyongelawa syĩndũ nzaũ, nĩ ũseo ũkekalaa ũisisya nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na JW Library ĩla ya mĩtũkĩ.
NĨKĨ WAĨLE KWĨTHĨWA NA JW LIBRARY? Yĩthĩawa ne laisi kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ũtũmĩĩte JW Library, na no ĩkũtetheesye kũvingũa kwa mĩtũkĩ ilungu ila iũneenewa maũmbanonĩ. O na ĩngĩ, JW Library no ĩkũtetheesye ũtavany'anĩ, na mũno mũno ĩla ũũtavany'a wĩ maũndũnĩ maku.

translation:
The JW Library app is a computer (software application) tool used to read the Bible, books, magazines, and other publications such as brochures or applications.
HOW TO READ JW LIBRARY ONLINE: Data is needed, either mobile data or Wi-Fi, and download it from the app store on your device, then open it and search for JW Library and download the application on your device. This application works both on mobile phones or tablets of various brands. Open the JW Library application, and then access books, magazines, or any other publication to read at any time. You can also use your mobile data when you don't have Wi-Fi, and others can use Wi-Fi at school, work, or your own home. To read a book from JW Library, internet access is sometimes required. However, books and magazines from JW Library are downloaded piece by piece, so they take up less space and can be used without an internet connection.
WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS OF USING JW LIBRARY? It helps people to study the Bible using JW Library, and it allows them to find information quickly and easily. Also, JW Library allows offline reading, and often this feature helps people in places where there is no internet.

translation:
It happened once when a hare was very clever at deceiving people.
This Hare was known throughout the land to always outsmart everyone in everything he did.
One day this Hare decided to compete with all animals who boasted about their speed.
Then he said, "Let us race, let us see whether I am slower or faster." The Hare deceived them; he said either five or ten laps would be enough to finish the race.
That is how this story about the Hare began.

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ngai onanĩtye nũtũnengete ndaĩa kwa kũtũnenga ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa vandũ va we mwene kũtũnyuvĩaa kana kũtũamũĩaa maũndũ ala makatũkwataa. Kwoona ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya.
Ngai oombie andũ na mũvw'ano wake. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:26) Kĩvathũkany'o na nyamũ, ila itatongoeaw'a nĩ kĩlĩko, andũ mavw'anene na Mũmbi woo kwa kwĩthĩwa matonya kwonany'a ndaĩa nzeo ta wendo na ũsili wa katĩ. Na, ta Mũmbi witũ twĩthĩawa na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa.
Kwa kĩthimo kĩnene, nithyĩ twĩnyuvĩaa kana nĩtũkwenda twĩtanĩa ĩvinda yitũ yũkĩte. Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya 'tũnyuve thayũ kwa kwĩthukĩĩsya wasya wa Ngai,' na twĩkaa ũu ĩla twaatĩĩa mĩao yake. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 30:19, 20) Keka ti ithyĩ twĩnyuvĩaa maũndũ, ndeto isu syĩthĩwa syĩ sya mana na iyonany'a kana Ngai nde tei. Vandũ va kũtũlasimĩthya twĩke maũndũ ala wendete, Ngai atwĩsũvĩte ũũ: "A! kethĩwa wethukĩĩsye mĩao yakwa! nĩvo ĩndĩ mũuo waku wĩthĩwa wailyĩ ta ũsĩ."—Isaia 48:18.
Kwoou, noithyĩ tũtonya kũtuma tũendeea nesa kana tũendeea naĩ. Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda maũndũ maitũ mathi nesa ũndũnĩ o na wĩva, no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "O ũla kw'oko kwaku kwona wa kwĩka, ĩka na vinya waku."(Mũtavan'ya 9:10) Ĩsyokete ĩkasya atĩĩ: "Mosũanĩo ma ala athingu maelete wingĩnĩ wa syĩndũ."—Nthimo 21:5.
Ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai, nũndũ ũthasyo ũsu nũtumaa tũmwenda na 'ngoo yonthe,' tũte kũlasimĩthw'a.—Mathayo 22:37.
We Ngai nĩwe ũtongoesye kĩla kĩndũ?
Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai nĩwe mwene vinya w'onthe, na kana vinya wake ndũsiĩĩka nĩ mũndũ o na wĩva. (Yovu 37:23; Isaia 40:26) Ĩndĩ Ngai ndatũmĩaa ũkũmũ wake kũtongoesya kĩla kĩndũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai eekie 'kwĩsiĩĩa' kwelekela Mbaviloni ĩla yaĩ mũmaitha wa andũ make. (Isaia 42:14) O ta ĩvindanĩ yĩu, ũmũnthĩ Ngai nĩwũmĩĩasya ala matũmĩaa ũthasyo woo wa kwĩnyuvĩa kũũmĩsya angĩ. Ĩndĩ ndemomĩĩsya tene na tene.—Savuli 37:10, 11.

translation:
The Bible's Counsel
God loves us perfectly and wants what is best for us, to protect us from getting hurt or being misled by false teachings. Truly, the Bible shows its care.
God created humans with personality. (Genesis 1:26) It is pleasant to be with others, but selfishness can cause problems, making people distance themselves from their Creator because of bad associations and lack of good judgment. And, because our Creator loves us, he gives us freedom of choice.
For this reason, we often make wrong choices or act foolishly. The Bible encourages us to 'consider your steps carefully,' and we will succeed if we obey God's laws. (Proverbs 30:19, 20) But if we make mistakes, does that mean God has abandoned us or no longer cares? Those who humbly seek forgiveness find that God is willing to forgive them, saying: "Oh, how I wish you would return and heed my commands, so that things may go well for you—that you may enjoy lasting peace!"—Isaiah 48:18.
So, we should not hesitate to admit our errors or correct our ways. If we act unwisely and suffer consequences, let us learn from our mistakes. The Bible says: "The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of fools to the left." (Ecclesiastes 9:10) It also states: "The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked is deceitful."—Proverbs 21:5.
Freedom of choice allows us to show love to God, and this freedom enables us to please him with 'our whole heart,' proving ourselves obedient.—Matthew 22:37.
Does God Cause All That Happens?
The Bible teaches that God is sovereign over all things, and that his purposes will certainly come about. (Job 37:23; Isaiah 40:26) God uses his power to fulfill his plans. For example, the Bible tells us that God caused 'confusion' to frustrate Babylon the Great, which had mistreated his people. (Isaiah 42:14) However, this does not mean that God directly causes all bad things to happen, but rather that he allows freedom of choice. He patiently endures.—Psalm 37:10, 11.

text:
KWASISYA nthĩ ĩno! Kĩla kĩndũ nthĩnĩ wayo kyanakavĩte ta kĩ! Kwatata kũsisya nyeki na mĩtĩ, malaa na nyamũ syonthe. Nũtonya kũmanya nzou na mĩnyambũ?
Mũũnda ũũ wanakavĩte ũu waumie va? Ekai yu ĩndĩ, twone ũndũ Ngai wamĩseũvisye nthĩ kwondũ witũ
Mbee, Ngai nĩwameisye nyeki nziũ ĩvw'ĩke nthĩ. Na nĩwaseũvisye mĩthemba yonthe ya tũmĩtĩ tũnini na ikuthu o vamwe na itĩ. Syĩndũ ii imeaa mũthanganĩ na kwĩana nĩsyanakavasya nthĩ. Ĩndĩ ti oou wĩ w'oka. Mbingĩ syasyo nitũnengae malĩu me mũyo mũno.
Ĩtina wa ũu Ngai nĩwoombie makũyũ mathambĩae kĩw'ũnĩ na nyũnyi iũlũkae yayayanĩ. Nĩwoombie ngitĩ na mbaka na mbalasi; nyamũ nene na nini. Nĩ nyamũ myaũ syĩkalaa vakuvĩ na mũsyĩ kwenyu? Tyo twaĩlĩtwe nĩkwĩw'a mũyo nĩkwĩthĩwa Ngai nĩwoombie syĩndũ ii syonthe kwondũ witũ?
Ĩtina vyũ, Ngai nĩwaseũvisye kĩsio kĩmwe kya nthĩ kĩthĩwe kĩ kya mwanya mũno. Eetie kĩsio kyu mũũnda wa Eteni. Waĩ mũseo vyũ. Kĩla kĩndũ nthĩnĩ wa w'o kyaĩ kyanake. Na Ngai endaa nthĩ yonthe yĩthĩwe yĩ mbanake o ta mũũnda ũsu waseũvĩtye.
Ĩndĩ kwatata kũsisya ĩngĩ visa wa mũũnda ũũ. We nĩwĩsĩ nĩ kyaũ Ngai woonie kĩte vo? Ekai twone.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:11-25; 2:8, 9.
Makũlyo
- Ngai amĩseũvisye nthĩ ata yĩthĩwe ũtũo witũ?
- Elesya mĩthemba mingĩ ya nyamũ ila Ngai woombie. (Sisya visa.)
- Nĩkĩ mũũnda wa Eteni waĩ wa mwanya mũno?
- Ngai endaa nthĩ yonthe ĩtw'ĩke kyaũ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:11-25.
Ngai oombie kyaũ mũthenya wa katatũ wa wũmbi? (Mwa. 1:12)
Kweekĩkie ata mũthenya wa kana wa wũmbi? (Mwa. 1:16)
Nĩ nyamũ sya mũthemba mwaũ ila Ngai woombie mũthenya wa katano na wa thanthatũ? (Mwa.1:20, 21, 25)
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:8, 9.
Nĩ mĩtĩ myaũ ĩlĩ ya mwanya Ngai wavandie mũũndanĩ ũsu, na yaĩ wonany'o wa kyaũ?

translation:
How wonderful this is! Everything I have seen is good! It's amazing to see earth and trees, fields and all animals. Don't you want to know about heaven and angels?
This world you have created, will it be enough for us? Look here, let's see what God has done for us.
Truly, God has made the earth very beautiful. And He has fulfilled all the hopes of our ancestors and their descendants. This thing that exists is full of joy and peace, it makes me happy. Here, there is no one who can compare. The future seems bright with this life.
The power of this God creates large rivers and flowing springs. He creates strength and blessings; great animals and everything. Is this animal still alive and well with you? So we should praise this life and thank God for doing all this for us?
Indeed, God has given me one small gift, a gift of this precious time. That is the gift of the garden of Eden. Understand this well. Everything I have seen is good. And God remembers all things created and does not forget this world that He has saved.
Here, it's amazing to see more of this world. But are you able to understand what God has done? Let's look.
Philippians 1:11-25; 2:8, 9.
Questions
- Has God saved us from all things created?
- Consider the many hopes of animals, but God provides. (See more.)
- What was the garden of Eden like at that time?
- Will God remember all things He has created?
Additional Questions
- Read Philippians 1:11-25.
What did God promise regarding the salvation of sinners? (Phil. 1:12)
Did He promise salvation to anyone who believes? (Phil. 1:16)
Is the animal of hope yours, but God promised five and six times? (Phil. 1:20, 21, 25)
- Read Philippians 2:8, 9.
What kind of trees were in the garden that God gave to humanity, and how did they show His goodness?

text:
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmeyumasya mamanyĩsye andũ Mbivilia. Ĩla mekwĩmanyĩsya namo nĩmaneeneeaa makũlyo maingĩ, kwa ngelekany'o:
Ngai Nũũ?
We Ngai Nũnthĩnĩkĩaa?
Ndonya kwĩka ata nĩseũvye mũtwaano wakwa?
Ndonya kwĩka ata nĩkale na ũtanu?
Vaa ĩtheo ve mosũngĩo ma makũlyo andũ makothaa kũkũlya ĩũlũ wa mũvango witũ wa kũmanyĩsya andũ.
Twĩkaa ata ĩla tũũmanyĩsya mũndũ Mbivilia? Tũneeneea maũndũ ta "Ngai" kana "mũtwaano" na tũisisya maandĩko me kĩvathũkany'o ala mawetete maũndũ asu. Nĩtũsiasya ũndũ maandĩko asu mosanĩte, na tweeka ũu nĩtũmanyaa kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa kĩu tũũneenea. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu twĩthĩawa twaeka Mbivilia yĩyĩelesye neyo mwene.
Nĩtũtũmĩaa ĩvuku yĩtawa Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? nĩ kana yĩtũtetheesye kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ĩvuku yĩu yĩwetete sanzũ momanyĩsyo maingĩ ala me Mbivilianĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩyĩwetete kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa Ngai, Yesũ, na ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte.
Mũndũ aĩvaa mbesa iana nĩ kana amanyĩw'e Mbivilia? Kũmanyĩw'a nĩ mana, na ndũteeawa ĩvuku yĩla ũũnengwa.
Mũkuaa ĩvinda yĩana ata kwa mũthenya? Andũ aingĩ methĩawa mavangĩte tũmamanyĩsye Mbivilia kwa vakuvĩ ĩsaa kĩla kyumwa. Ĩndĩ ti lasima tũkatũmĩa ĩvinda yĩana ũu. Tũkakua ĩvinda yĩla ũkatũtavya.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩkekĩka ĩla ngakũlya nĩmanyĩw'e Mbivilia? Wakũlya ũmanyĩw'e Mbivilia, ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova akakomanĩa naku vala we ũkwenda na saa ila ũkwenda. Mũtanambĩĩa akamba kwosa ndatĩka nini akwony'e ũndũ twĩmanyĩasya na andũ. Na ĩndĩ wendeew'a, no mũendeesye mũvango wenyu.
Ĩla ngetĩkĩla nĩmanyĩw'e Mbivilia ngeethĩwa natw'ĩka wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova? Aiee. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyendete mũno kũmanyĩsya andũ Mbivilia, ĩndĩ tũyĩsaa kũingĩĩsya mũndũ atw'ĩke ũmwe witũ. Vandũ va kũmũingĩĩsya, tũmonasya na ndaĩa kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya, nũndũ nĩtwĩsĩ kana kĩla mũndũ e na ũthasyo wa kũĩkĩĩa kĩla ũkwenda.—1 Vetelo 3:15.

translation:
The name of Jehovah has been made known to faithful men of the Bible. But to make it known further, we need many more, for this reason:
Who is the true God?
Why is He the true God?
Can you show anyone what your faith involves?
Can you show someone that you have love?
Yes, the truth about important matters needs to be presented to people so they may know our sacred duty of making known God.
Do we then try to make everyone a Bible student? We use the names "God" or "faith" and we leave out scriptures that are difficult, but we simplify matters. We want to present the scripture simply, and we want to make sure that every Bible reader understands the point we are trying to get across. In this way we can help people to appreciate the Bible better.
Should we then use a simplified Bible to help us make it known? Or should we strive to make the Bible known as it is? That simplified version contains much less information than the Bible itself. For example, it does not contain everything that the Bible says about God, Jesus, and other things connected with them.
Does a person who is zealous become a Bible teacher just because he is zealous? Being zealous is good, but training is needed.
Should a person then seek training first? Many people find it hard to teach others about the Bible when they visit homes regularly. It is often best to receive some training first. Then we can seek out opportunities to practice.
What can be done if someone does not understand the Bible? If someone does not understand the Bible, one of Jehovah's Witnesses can come to his home and spend time with him. The publisher will ask questions to find out what the person thinks. And if he wishes, he can continue to study.
But what if I feel inadequate to teach people about the Bible? If you feel inadequate to teach people about the Bible, remember that Jehovah's Witnesses are happy to help anyone who wants to join them. Those who desire to help others, we assist them and encourage them to learn how to share what the Bible teaches, and we also help them to overcome their shyness.—1 Peter 3:15.

text:
AMKENI!
Ĩkũlyo: Andũ aingĩ nĩmendaa kwĩthĩwa na ũima wa mwĩĩ. We wĩona twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩsũvĩane na mowau?
Ĩandĩko: Nth 22:3
Ũndũ ũtonya kwasya: Ĩkaseti yĩĩ ya Amkeni! nĩyĩneeneete maũndũ maseo ala twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana twĩsũvĩane na mowau.
MANYĨSYA ŨLA W'O
Ĩkũlyo: Mo mathĩna ala matũkwataa maetawe nĩ Ngai kana nĩ kĩndũ kĩngĩ?
Ĩandĩko: Yovu 34:10
Ũw'o: Ngai tiwe ũtũeteae mathĩna ala matũkwataa. Vandũ va ũu, mathĩna maumanaa na Ndevili, andũ ala mekaa motwi mathũku, kana mathĩna makethĩwa ĩla mũndũ wĩ vandũ vataĩlĩte ĩvinda yĩla yĩtaĩlĩte. Ngai nũtũtetheeasya mavinda ala twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna. Kwa w'o nũtũsũvĩaa.
NĨKĨ WAĨLE KWĨMANYĨSYA MBIVILIA? (Vitio)

Do you feel overwhelmed sometimes?
Do you worry or experience some form of distress such as anxiety, depression, fear, or panic, and does it make you question whether life is worth living? (Job 14:1, 2) Many people feel this way, and they often hide their feelings from others.—Read Ecclesiastes 2:11.
Do you feel overwhelmed sometimes? What can help us cope when we are struggling is, what makes a person valuable? Many people judge a person's value based on their appearance or abilities, but we are precious in the eyes of our Creator who made us. (Read Psalm 139:14.) And because of this, we are precious to him! Understanding this truth can help us see our own value.
Are we unique?
God created Adam and Eve perfect. They were happy and had a purpose in life, and they lived in beautiful surroundings.—Read Genesis 1:28, 31.
God's standards are different from those of most people. This is why God loves people, and he wants them to live up to his high standards. Many wonder if God will continue to allow imperfect humans to live forever, and if he will uphold his purpose of making the earth a paradise! Consider how important it is to align yourself with God's principles! (Read Psalm 37:29.) Meditate on these thoughts to find comfort in God's standards.
