Amanyiwa 316 ma secondary ala maumite misyini ila mivinyiiye ni ukya kuma kisioni kya Kiasa kila ki Makutano ma Chumvi Ukamba wa Athiriver kaundini ya Masaku nimatetheka ilovia sya bursary sya kimanza Kya silingi million 1.2 kuma kwa muimi umwe kisioni kiu mutumia Stvart Barden ula withiitwe aitwaaisya maundu ma uimi kisioni kwa ivinda yiasa .
Lawrence Ngovi na ula ni munene wa athukumi serikali ya kaundi ya Masaku aineena kyathini kiu kya kunengane bursary isu niwakulya enethi ma ngoo ya ulau na ngwatanio itesya kii serikali uitetheanisye na serikali isu kithitoni kya kutetheesya amanyiwa ala maumite misyini ila yina ukya mwingi kuendeeye na masomo vala ingi waumbula serikali ya kaundi ya Masaku kwisila utongoini wa Gavana Wavinya Ndeti nimaendeeye na kwikia walanio wa kunengane bursary kwi amanyiwa mwakani tuendete .
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The 316 secondary students who excelled in their studies have challenges paying school fees, but hope has emerged through the Kiasa scholarship at Makutano market in Chumvi, Athiriver region, Machakos county; they are benefiting from a Sh1.2 million bursary fund for each student, facilitated by Stvart Barden, whose name is associated with improving education standards in the area.
Lawrence Ngovi, the head of education in the Machakos County government, stated that this initiative aims to address the needs of vulnerable children and strengthen cooperation between the county government and national government in supporting education for bright students facing financial difficulties; he added that the Machakos County government, under Governor Wavinya Ndeti's leadership, will continue to prioritize providing bursaries to deserving students in the coming years.

text:
Kwambĩĩa mwei ũũ, maũmbano ma katĩkatĩ wa kyumwa maikethĩawa na ilungu itatũ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ila ineethĩawa syonanĩtye kĩla tũtonya kwasya ũtavany'anĩ. Vandũ va ũu, Kavuku ka Kwĩmanyĩsya ka Ũmbano kakeethĩawa na kĩlungu kyonanĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwasya kĩ na ĩkũlyo, ĩandĩko, na ĩkũlyo yĩngĩ yonanĩtye kĩla mũkaneenea wasyoka. Kĩla kyumwa vakoonanaw'a vitio ĩmwe yonanĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwasya. Kĩla mũtavany'a no anyuve nĩ ĩvuku yĩva katĩ wa mavuku ala tũtũmĩaa kũmanyĩsya andũ ũkwenda kũtũmĩa na nĩ ĩndĩĩ ũkũyĩtũmĩa. Kwa ngelakany'o, no avange kũyĩtũmĩa ĩla ũkũtavya mũndũ ya mbee kana ĩla ũkũmũsyokea. O na ĩngĩ, kavuku kaitũ kakeethĩawa konanĩtye maũndũ tũtonya kũtũmĩa ilungunĩ ilĩ sya kũsyokea mũndũ ila tũnengetwe. Nzĩa ĩsu ĩkatũtetheesya twĩanĩĩsye nesa kĩeleelo kitũ kya kũmanyĩsya onthe "ala manyuvĩtwe [kana, me na ngoo nzeo kwondũ wa] kwĩthĩwa na thayũ ũtathela."—Meko 13:48.
Ilungu sya Amanyĩw'a: Ethĩwa vayonanĩtw'e ũndũ ũngĩ, amanyĩw'a maĩle kwĩka ũndũ kĩlungu kĩla kyonanĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwasya kyaĩtye.

translation:
Recently, gatherings of sheep were being held by three groups, but they were being scattered because each person was looking out for themselves. The people of this world, the United Nations Organization, is being held by one group looking out for its own interests with power, influence, and much more for each influential person who arises. Every sheep seeks one place looking out for its own interests. Every survivor should be from among the flocks we use to teach people how to go and teach, and it is right to do so. For example, he may want to teach them whether to save a life or to destroy a person. And others, our organization is being held looking out for things we can use to benefit people rather than to destroy them. Let us therefore strengthen ourselves to continue teaching the good news, "but let them be comforted [or, I and my companions toward the direction of] witnessing by means of those who stumble." – Matthew 13:48.
The Groups of Witnesses: They have been shown something; witnesses testify about what each group looks out for its own interests concerning.

text:
"Naendie kũthooa lĩu ĩndĩ neethĩa maithoosya mĩsukuti yĩ yoka. Na thooa wayo wambatĩte kũndũ 10,000 kwĩ ũndũ yatwĩe ĩthooaw'a! Mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe nduka iyaĩ na lĩu o na ũmwe."—Paul, Zimbabwe.
"Mũũme wakwa ambĩtie na ambĩa ethi atakasyoka. Nesaa kũmĩĩsya ũndũ ũsu ata? Nasyo syana syakwa syesaa kwĩka ata?"—Janet, United States.
"Ĩla neew'a wasya wa kĩng'ola nzembaa ngevitha na ndikoma nthĩ mĩsinga ĩendeee na kũlivũka. Ũndũ ũsu weekĩka, moko makwa maendeeaa kũthĩlĩa o na ĩtina wa masaa maingĩ."—Alona , Israel.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ kwĩ mawĩmakĩo maingĩ na nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia yaĩtye kana nĩ "mavinda ma mũisyo." (2 Timotheo 3:1) Andũ aingĩ methĩĩtwe me thĩnanĩ mwingĩ nũndũ wa ũnyivu wa mbesa, mathĩna ma mĩsyĩ, kaũ, mĩimũ, na mĩisyo. O na mathĩna asu me o vo, ve mathĩna angĩ ma mũndũ mwene, kwa ngelekany'o angĩ no mekũlye atĩĩ: 'Wimbu ũũ nĩ naw'o nũtonya kwĩthĩwa ne kanza?' 'Esũkũũa makeanĩa o nthĩ ĩno ĩthũkĩte ũu?'
Ti mawĩmakĩo onthe methĩawa me mathũku. Mavinda angĩ no tũthĩnĩke kana tũkemakĩa ĩla tweteele mũtiani, ĩla tũũneena mbee wa andũ, kana ĩla tũũkũlya wĩa. O na no tũkwatwe nĩ wia nũndũ wa mũisyo ũtonya kũtũkwata na ũu ũituma twĩsũvĩa. Ĩndĩ kwĩmakĩa kũvĩtũkĩte no kũtũũmĩsye. Ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe ũneekiwe katĩ wa andũ aima mbee wa 68,000 ũnoonanisye kana mũndũ eemakĩa o na ethĩwa no vanini, ũu no ũtume akw'a tene. Kwoou ti ũndũ wa kũsengy'a kwĩthĩwa Yesũ akũlilye atĩĩ: "Na nũũ kwenyu ũla ũtonya kwondũ wa kwĩmakĩa kwake kwĩyongeleela ũasa wake mũkono ũmwe?" Kwa w'o kwĩmakĩa kũituma mũndũ ongela ũasa wa thayũ wake. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ wanenganie ũtao ũũ: "Mũikemakĩe." (Mathayo 6:25, 27) Ĩndĩ ũu ũtonyeka ata?
Nzĩa ĩmwe tũtonya kwĩka ũu nĩ kũtũmĩa ũĩ, kũmũĩkĩĩa Ngai vyũ, na kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. O na ethĩwa yu tũi na maũndũ maito matũkwete, no matũkwate ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ekai twone ũndũ kũatĩĩa maũndũ asu kũtetheesye Paul, Janet, na Alona kũmĩanĩsya na mawĩmakĩo.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
"I went to steal a little bit with some friends just for fun. And I stole about 10,000 [currency] to show off! That foolish boy spent it all on beer and one girl."—Paul, Zimbabwe.
"My husband left me and said he won't return. Should I try to understand what happened? And my children, will they ever be okay?"—Janet, United States.
"I used to spend time with bad company and ended up getting involved in crime and suffering. This thing is terrible; two of my friends died because of spending too much time in prison."—Alona, Israel.
Today many people are experiencing great distress, and that is why the Bible rightly calls these "critical times." (2 Timothy 3:1) Many people are troubled by much anxiety, fear, worry, stress, and despair. And others are also facing personal problems, which often lead them to ask themselves: 'Why am I so unhappy?' 'How can I cope with this situation?'
These anxieties are not unique to our time. People in ancient times also struggled with similar concerns, such as how to provide for their families, how to maintain relationships, or how to overcome difficulties. But we are also affected by a deeper problem—the problem of meaninglessness, which causes us to feel empty inside. It is easy to become overwhelmed by life's challenges. One study showed that about 68,000 people commit suicide each year, and many attempts are made due to feelings of hopelessness. That is why Jesus urged his followers: "Stop being anxious over what you will eat or drink." He taught them that focusing on material things can distract us from what truly matters. That is why Jesus gave this advice: "Do not be anxious." (Matthew 6:25, 27) Is that really possible?
One way we can do this is by trusting in God, praying to him, and living according to his standards. And when we face difficult situations, we can remember that we are not alone, and we can find strength in our faith. Let us see how the experiences of Paul, Janet, and Alona can help us deal with our anxieties.

MŨSYAĨĨSYA (ĨKASETI YA KWĨMANYĨSYA) Mwei wa 5 2016
Ĩkaseti yĩĩ yĩ na ilungu sya kwĩmanyĩsya sya kwambĩĩa matukũ 27/06/2016 nginya matukũ 31/07/2016.
Ĩla wathi wĩw'ane na mũndũ mũemanĩtwe, waĩle kũthi wĩ na kĩeleelo kĩva? Nĩ kũsinda ngalali, kana nĩ kũlasimĩthya ũla ũvĩtĩtye etĩkĩle ĩvĩtyo yake, kana nĩ kĩtumi kĩngĩ?
Ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo ana ala me vaa nĩwonanĩtye naaũ ũmũnthĩ meanĩasya wathani wa Yesũ.
Twaĩle kwĩka ata ĩla twakwatwa nĩ ũndũ, na ũyĩthĩa vai mwĩao wa Mbivilia ũwetete ũndũ ũsu ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe?
Ve Ngũsĩ yaekie kũtha kalata, kũnyw'a sikala, kũnyw'a ũkĩ mũno, na kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila nĩ kana ĩvatiswe, ĩndĩ ĩtina wa vau yesa kwĩthĩa ve ũalyũku ũngĩ waĩ vinya mũno kwĩka.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũvĩtwa nĩ ũndũ wĩĩ ũtonya kũtũtethya maũvoonĩ asu?
FROM OUR ARCHIVES
Ũndũ weekiwe mwaka wa 1919 nĩw'o waĩ mwambĩĩo wa wĩa wesie kũtethw'a nthĩ yonthe.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya Aklĩsto mamanye ethĩwa kũnenga athũkũmi ma silikalĩ mũthĩnzĩo kana o kĩndũ kĩnini nĩkwaĩle? Kĩkundi kĩtonya kwonany'a ata nĩkyeew'a mũyo ĩla kyatangaasĩwa kana mũndũ ũnaĩ mũtenge nĩwatũngwa? Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kyatumaa ndia ya Vethesita ĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme yĩkala ta 'yakwaithangw'a'?

translation:
REFLECTION (A TAPE OF REFLECTION) May 5, 2016
This tape has interviews about preaching from June 27, 2016 to July 31, 2016.
But he was alone with a trusted person, did he go with a purpose? Is it to steal sleep, or to strengthen the little strength he has, or is it something else?
The foundation of teachings has always been to show people the way of Jesus.
Did we ever think that when we are afflicted, does the clear word of the Bible explain each thing individually?
Let Ngũsĩ be able to write letters, drink soda, drink good beer, and send medicine to heal whether it is accepted, let them try to see if this small amount is enough.
Is it possible to send us with a small problem to confuse our minds?
FROM OUR ARCHIVES
What happened in 1919 was a time when everyone was told everything.
Is it possible to teach Christians to forget their past mistakes or is there something big that happened? Can a group agree even if they disagree or if someone who disagrees is condemned? Is it possible that this caused the church in Bethlehem and Jerusalem to become known as 'discredited'?

text:
Kambuni wa ukui wa ndeke wa Kenya Airways (KQ) niwavithua kikw'u kya mukuuwa umwe ula endete Mombasa.
Kwisila kwa uvisi wa mikumukanilye wa KQ nikana mukuuwa usu ethiwa na thina wa kuveva yila ei analika ndekeni KQ612 ila ikukuasya kuenda Mombasa saa umwe wiyoo wa matuku 14 mwei wa Kenda.
Nikwaikiithwa kana mukuuwa ei munini wa gavana wa Baringo Charles Kipngok, ula kwaivinda yimwe waungamiiye nzama ya utandithya wa kaawa vsa Kenya KTDA.
Kipngok ni mukuuwa wa katatu kutiwa ni thayu o ndekeni ii nthini wa myei itatu mivitu.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Kenya Airways (KQ) aircraft company has mourned the death of one of its pilots who died in Mombasa.
According to a statement from KQ's communications department, the pilot was identified as Captain Patrick Waithe and was scheduled to fly plane KQ612 to Mombasa at 1 p.m. on October 14th.
It is reported that the deceased was the brother of Baringo Governor Charles Kipngok, who previously served as a director of the Kenya Tea Development Agency (KTDA).
Kipngok is the third family member to die in an accident involving a plane in the last three years.

The smell of livestock, goats, chickens and rabbits has been reported to be very strong in this area near the river in the Masaku County government at a cost of 2 items which cause discomfort and great annoyance to people.

MŨSYAĨĨSYA
Ĩkũlyo: Kwaĩ kwenda kwa Ngai andũ makusae?
Ĩandĩko: Ũvu 21:4
Ũndũ ũtonya kwasya: Ĩkaseti yĩĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya yĩeleetye kĩla Mbivilia ĩwetete ĩũlũ wa thayũ na kĩkw'ũ.
MANYĨSYA ŨLA W'O
Ĩkũlyo: Nĩkĩ ũmũnthĩ andũ mathĩnaa ũu?
Ĩandĩko: 1Yoa 5:19
Ũw'o: Satani, ũla nĩwe Ndevili, nĩwe ũsumbĩkĩte nthĩ.
TWĨKAA ATA ĨLA TŨŨMANYĨSYA MŨNDŨ MBIVILIA?
Ũndũ ũtonya kwasya: Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nimanyĩasya andũ Mbivilia mate kũĩva. Weemanyĩsya Mbivilia no ũsũngĩwe makũlyo ta aa: Nĩkĩ ũmũnthĩ andũ mathĩnaa ũu? Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma mũsyĩ wakwa wĩthĩwa na ũtanu? Vitio ĩno nguvĩ nĩyĩeleetye ũndũ twĩmanyĩasya Mbivilia na andũ. [Mwony'e vitio Twĩkaa Ata Ĩla Tũũmanyĩsya Mũndũ Mbivilia?] Kavuku kaa nĩko tũkatũmĩaa tũyĩmanyĩsya. [Mwony'e kavuku kamwe katĩ wa tũla tũtũmĩaa kwĩmanyĩsya, na vatonyeka ũimwony'a ũndũ twĩmanyĩasya.]

Tũmĩa nzĩa ĩla yonanĩtw'e ngelekany'onĩ ila syĩ vaa ĩũlũ nĩ kana ũandĩke maũndũ maku ma kũtũmĩa ũtavany'anĩ.

translation:

text:
MŨSYAĨĨSYA
Ĩkũlyo: We nũkwona ndeto ii ta ikeanĩa?
Ĩandĩko: Ũvu 21:3, 4
Ũndũ ũtonya kwasya: Ĩkaseti yĩĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya nĩyĩneeneete ũndũ Ngai ũkeanĩsya watho ũsu, na ũndũ tũtonya kũtetheka kumana na ũndũ ũsu.
MŨSYAĨĨSYA (ĩthangũ ya ĩtina)
Ĩkũlyo: Kwasisya ĩkũlyo yĩĩ. [Mũkũlye ĩkũlyo ya mbee na mosũngĩo ala monanĩtw'e kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩ ĩthangũnĩ ya 16.] Ũtonya kũsũngĩa ĩkũlyo yĩu ata?

text:
Ula wai president wa Africa ya Itheo Jacob Zuma niwaalekwa itina wa kumina kyovo kyake vala unoovetwe na ivityo ya kuvuthya koti.
Zuma atwiiwe kyovo kya myei ikumi na itano itina wa kuleana na wendi wa koti aumile mbee wayo kusungia maundu makonetye ulusani.
Itina niweenenganie matuku 7 mwei wa muonza mwaka muvitu vala waambiisye kyovo kyake, kindu kila kyaothootheiye kau mwai kukuusiiwa nthi isu, atii make mayaandamana kuvinga kwikiwa mbini kwake.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Former South African President Jacob Zuma has been ordered to appear in court to face charges related to corruption allegations.
Zuma is facing 15 years in prison for contempt of court after repeatedly failing to comply with court orders, including refusing to testify before a state capture inquiry.
The hearing is scheduled for seven days from the beginning of next month, where he will be asked about each piece of evidence against him, and he says his supporters will march to protect his freedom.

text:
Ukanio muvyu niwaumwa kula kwi ekali ma ward ya Kiteta Kisau na muno ala mathengeanie na mutitu wa katende kumana na kila kiuwetwa ta kwina amwe ma enenthi methiitwe maikwatya mwaki kithekani kiu na kuete ngalama nene na wanangiko .
Aineena na kameme Kaa MCA wa ward isu ya Kiteta Kisau ,ila yii kilio mbunge kya Mbooni Darius Mainga, niwaelesya kana ve mwaki unavuthie mutitu uu wa katende na wavikiia na kuvow'a indi kwi masaani ma mawiyoo muthenyani wa iyoo,mwaki ungi nuvikiie na kwoneka kisioni kiu,na vala wenda onayo silikali ya kaunti ya Makueni uungu wa utongoi wake ngavana Mutula Kilonzo Jnr, undumwe na muvea wa kusuvia mititu Vaa Kenya KENYA FOREST SERVICES kuikiithya kana mivango myailu niyatwaiiwa kusuvia imwe ya mititu kauntini ya Makueni ta nzia imwe ya kuikiithya usuviiku wa mawithyululuko.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The current situation is painful to see the destruction in Ward Kiteta Kisau and this has caused people to gather and discuss the issue of deforestation which is happening everywhere because every piece of land is being cleared for farming and charcoal burning causing a lot of damage and suffering.
Speaking with our reporter Kaa MCA of Ward Kiteta Kisau, but also MP for Mbooni Darius Mainga, said they understand the importance of this forest and have promised to work together to find solutions for future generations, so that the forest can be protected and seen as a resource, and they will continue to push for the county government of Makueni under the leadership of Governor Mutula Kilonzo Jnr, along with the Kenya Forest Service to ensure that illegal logging is stopped and some forests in Makueni County are replanted as a way to protect the environment.

text:
AŨME aa me vaa maendee na kũthũkũmĩthya andũ wĩa na vinya. Kwasisya mũndũ ũya ũnũũvyata ũmwe wa athũkũmi na mũsalisa! Athũkũmi asu nĩ ma mũsyĩ wa Yakovo na metawa Aisilaeli. Na andũ asu meũmathũkũmĩthya na vinya nĩ Amisili. Aisilaeli maĩ ngombo sya Amisili. Kwethĩiwe ũu ata?
Kwa myaka mingĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ mũnene wa Yakovo nĩmekalile Misili na mũuo. Yosevu, ũla waĩ mũndũ wa vata mũno nthĩ ya Misili kũatĩĩa mũsumbĩ Valao, nĩwamasũvĩaa. Ĩndĩ Yosevu nĩwakwie. Na Valao mweũ, ũtendete Aisilaeli, atw'ĩka mũsumbĩ wa nthĩ ya Misili.
Kwoou Valao ũsu mũthũku amatw'ĩkĩthya Aisilaeli ngombo. Na amaiĩa aũngamĩi maĩ onei na mataĩ na tei. Nĩmathũkũmĩthisye Aisilaeli wĩa waĩ na vinya mũno wa kwakĩa Valao ndũa. Ĩndĩ Aisilaeli nĩmaendeeie o na kwingĩva. Na ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩna Amisili makwatwa nĩ w'ĩa nũndũ moonaa Aisilaeli ta matonya kwingĩva mũno na kwĩthĩwa na vinya mwingĩ.
We nĩwĩsĩ Valao eekie ata? Aneenie na iveti ila syateetheasya aka ma Aisilaeli kũsyaa, na asyĩa: 'No nginya mũkowaa kĩla kana ka kavĩsĩ kasyawa.' Ĩndĩ iveti isu syaĩ nzeo, na iyaaũaa twana tũu.
Kwoou ĩndĩ Valao anenga andũ make onthe watho amea: 'Kĩla kana ka kavĩsĩ kasyawa osaai mũkoaa. No twana twa twĩlĩtu tw'oka mwĩekaa twĩkale thayũ.' Ũsu waĩ ũndũ mũthũku mũno kwĩĩaa wĩkwe. Ekai twone ũndũ kamwe ka twana tũu twa tũvĩsĩ kavonokiw'e.
Kuma 1:6-22.
Makũlyo
- Nthĩnĩ wa visa, mũndũ ũũ wĩ na mũsalisa nũũ, na ekũna ũũ?
- Ĩtina wa Yosevu kũkw'a, kweekĩkie ata kwa Aisilaeli?
- Nĩkĩ Amisili makwatiwe nĩ w'ĩa kwondũ wa Aisilaeli?
- Valao ainengie watho mwaũ iveti ila syatetheeasya aka ma Isilaeli kusyaa?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Kuma 1:6-22.
Yeova ambĩĩie kwĩanĩsya ũtianĩo wake na Avalaamu kwa nzĩa yĩva? (Kuma 1:7; Mwa. 12:2; Meko 7:17)
Iveti Aevelania ila syateetheasya aka ma Isilaeli kũsyaa syoonanisye ndaĩa ata kwa ũtheu wa thayũ? (Kuma 1:17; Mwa. 9:6)
Nĩ ĩtuvi yaũ iveti ila syatetheeasya aka ma Isilaeli kũsyaa syanengiwe nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa syĩ ndĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova? (Kuma 1:20, 21; Nth. 19:17)
Satani atatie ata kũsiĩĩa kĩeleelo kya Yeova kĩla kyakonanĩtye na Ũsyao wa Avalaamu ũla wathanĩtwe? (Kuma 1:22; Mt. 2:16)

translation:
They went with peace and blessed the people with gifts. Remember this person who remembers one of the elders and honors him! The elders now are descendants of Jacob and the tribes of Israel. And the people who remember with gifts are Amalekites. Israel came from Amalekites. What happened then?
For many years, the descendants of the great man Jacob lived in Egypt with hardship. Joseph, whose father was a prominent man in Egypt to appease Pharaoh, prospered. But Joseph died, and Pharaoh, who oppressed Israel, established a new ruler over Egypt.
Then Pharaoh arose and began to oppress Israelites greatly. And he made their lives bitter with labor and tears. He remembered Israelites with gifts and hardship because of fearing Pharaoh's power. But Israelites continued on and multiplied. And the end of four hundred thirty years in Egypt were completed when the land groaned under the oppression of Israelites due to much hardship and tears.
But why did Pharaoh harden his heart again? He heard and feared, but refused to let Israelites go, and said, 'Let them not leave until every donkey and ox are gone.' But the fear was useless, and they had many children.
Then Pharaoh commanded his people to kill every male child. He said, 'Every donkey and ox that remains should be killed. Let no sons remain to live.' This was a very cruel decree. Behold we see one thing about those many children being spared.
Exodus 1:6-22.
Questions
- Why does a visitor honor someone with gifts, and what does it mean?
- What effect did Joseph's death have on Israelites?
- Why were Amalekites afflicted because of Israelites?
- What command did Pharaoh give regarding the fear that prevented Israelites from going?
Further Questions
- Read Exodus 1:6-22.
Did Jehovah show his purpose to Abraham through a vision? (Exodus 1:7; Gen. 12:2; Acts 7:17)
Did the Egyptian fear that prevented Israelites from going demonstrate consideration for the future? (Exodus 1:17; Gen. 9:6)
Is it right to fear something that prevents Israelites from going and become indebted to Jehovah? (Exodus 1:20, 21; Prov. 19:17)
Did Satan contribute to distorting Jehovah's purpose concerning everything related to the covenant with Abraham's offspring? (Exodus 1:22; Matt. 2:16)

Aiee. Nĩtũtavanasya nyũmba na nyũmba ĩndĩ tũiĩkĩĩaa atĩ tũkatangĩĩwa nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu. (Aeveso 2:8) Nĩkĩ?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Twasye mũndũ ũmwe mũlau nĩwathanĩte kana mũndũ ũla ũkavika vandũ vana mũthenya mũna nũkũmũnenga mũthĩnzĩo. Ethĩwa nũmũĩkĩĩe mũndũ ũsu tyo ũatĩĩe maũndũ ala ũkũũtavya? Ndũlea kũatĩĩa. O na eka ũu, no kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kũtavya anyanyau na andũ ma mũsyĩ ĩũlũ wa mũvango ũsu nĩ kana o namo matetheke nĩw'o. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o va ndũũnewa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu aĩ nũndũ nĩwathũkũma. Ũsu no mũthĩnzĩo.
O ta ũu, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai nĩwathĩte ala mamwĩw'aa thayũ ũtathela. (Alomi 6:23) Tũtataa tũelesye angĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo witũ nĩ kana ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka o namo mekwata moathimo ala Ngai wathanĩte. Ĩndĩ ithyĩ tũyĩĩkĩĩaa kana ũtangĩĩo ũkwatĩkanaa aĩ nũndũ nĩtwaũthũkũmĩa ĩla tũũtavany'a. (Alomi 1:17; 3:28) Vai mũndũ wĩka ũndũ wĩanene na ũathimo ũsu Ngai ũkanenga andũ. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "
Ti kwondũ wa meko ma ũlũngalu, ala ithyĩ tweekie, ĩndĩ kwĩanana na tei wake nĩwatũtangĩĩe."—Tito 3:5.

translation:
Alas. We will rebuild house after house, and the house we build we will inhabit, so that they may begin to plant vineyards and enjoy their fruit. (Isaiah 2:8) Why?
To illustrate this point: Suppose one skilled man joins forces with another unskilled man, or an unskilled man hires several people to work for him and then praises them excessively. Would you encourage such a person to continue doing wrong? Certainly not. And concerning this, know that it is foolish to associate closely with those who despise the law of your God—even if they offer you gifts. For you and your excessive praise will be destroyed together. You and your praise.
But this, the name of Jehovah has been declared, or God has created everything beautiful for its purpose. (Ecclesiastes 6:23) Let us therefore examine ourselves carefully regarding our attitude, or let us not become complacent, thinking that God approves of our actions. For if we believe that justification is attained through works, we deceive ourselves. (Romans 1:17; 3:28) So a person does something important and attributes his success to his own ability, while God judges people. The Bible states: "
Not by reason of your righteousness, but by reason of His mercy He saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit."—Titus 3:5.

translation:
The meeting of the OKA coalition has several issues to discuss regarding extensive cooperation with many parties, but it will focus on supporting a presidential candidate who can be recognized widely.
This issue is being led by the leader of the Wiper party, Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka, together with the co-leader of Narc Kenya, Martha Karua, Gideon Moi of Kanu, Cyrus Jirongo of UDP.

text:
Kenya ota nthi ingi umunthi niyaatania muthenya wa kana kelitu ula utaniawa kila matuku 11 mwei wa ikumi .
Mwaka uu mautanu asu menengetwe kyongo "Our time is now- Our rights , our future" ualyulo wayo ni "ivinda yitu ni oyu- uw'o witu ni uni witu" wina kielelo kya eitu kusenzya nthi yitu.
kieleelo kinene ni kuvetanga ivathukanyo ila syekiiwe kana kelitu nthi nima nakukamanyithya kana kena utonyi vateusiwa muvai.
Ni muthenya wina uthuthyo kwa andu onthe kunenga aka ndaiya, kumasyiiya na miisyo ta nzaiko, kuvukwa na kau wa misyi ovamwe na kumanenga utonyi kwa kumasomethya na kumavathia mawia na utongoi.
Ta eitu 4/10 kati wa myaka 15-19 nthi nima maikwataa kisomo iisianiwa na kivisi kimwe kati wa ikumi nthi nima, undu ula wendeewe kuthiinikiwa vanene.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Kenya has many challenges including poverty which affects people daily for about 11 days in October .
This year's theme has been named "Our time is now- Our rights , our future" and its slogan is "ivinda yitu ni oyu- uw'o witu ni uni witu" which means a message of unity to build our country.
The main goal is to end child marriage but unfortunately many girls continue to be married off young.
It is a good thing for all people to educate each other, to cooperate with organizations and to avoid being misled by others and to fight against poverty through education and proper guidance.
About 4/10 of those aged 15-19 years old continue to drop out of school and only 1/10 finish, this issue needs to be addressed urgently.

Maovisaa ma volisi musyini wa Masaku nimambiisya ukunikili yiulu wa kiko kimwe vala munduume wa ukuu wa katikati kuma kisioni kya Mukalala kila ki sub-location ya Misakwani Mumbuni location ukamba wa Masaku ukuwetwa wowaa kana kake ka ukuu wa myaka 3 na itina nake eyumya thayu kwa kwisuusya nyumbani yake.
Ayikiithya mauvoo asu chief wa mumbuni location Mathew Mulee niwaweta munduume usu ta waumya thayu kana kau kwa kukatila ngingo na kavyu vala itina wa kutwaiisya kiko kiu kya kinyamu nake wasyoka esuusya nyumbani isu yake.
Kwa oyu maovisaa ma volisi ma Masaku nimavikite kisioni kii kya Mukalala vala maendeeye kuthiana kumanya kila kithwa kyothotheea munduume usu kutwaiisya kiko kiu.
Mii yoo niyooswa ni maovisaa ma volisi yatwawa nyumbani ya kusuvia mii ya akwu ya sivitali wa Machakos level 5.

translation:
The officers who were on patrol in Masaku town have reported an incident where a man from the central ward of Katikati in Mukalala division, every sub-location of Misakwani Mumbuni location in Masaku county, was arrested because he is suspected of being 3 years old and having a mental illness that led him to destroy his house.
According to the officers, Chief of Mumbuni location Mathew Mulee has stated that the man is not well mentally or physically due to drug use and that his condition leads him to destroy things and eventually destroy his own house.
Regarding this incident, the police of Masaku have launched an investigation into the Mukalala division to find out what happened to the man and why he destroyed things.
This information was provided by the police officers who took the man's belongings to the store at Machakos level 5 hospital.

Aiee. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova niĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai oombie syĩndũ syonthe. Ĩndĩ tũyĩĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai oombie nthĩ na mĩthenya thanthatũ, kĩla mũthenya wĩ na masaa 24. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ amwe maĩkĩĩaa kĩu mamanyĩasya maũndũ amwe matosanĩte na Mbivilia. Kwasũanĩa momanyĩsyo aa elĩ:
Ũasa wa ĩla mĩthenya thanthatũ ya wũmbi. Amwe maasya kana mũthenya ũmwe wa wũmbi waĩ na masaa 24. Ĩndĩ mavinda angĩ ĩla Mbivilia yatũmĩa ndeto "mũthenya" nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa ĩiweta ĩvinda o ĩasa.
—Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:4; Savuli 90:4.
Ũkũũ wa nthĩ. Amwe mamanyĩasya kana nthĩ yĩkalĩte o tũkili twĩana ũna twa myaka. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana o na ĩla mĩthenya thanthatũ ya wũmbi ĩtaaĩsa kwambĩĩa, nthĩ na matu syaĩ syoombiwe. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:1) Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩu, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova iileanaa na livoti ila itonya kwĩkwatw'a andũ ma saenzi mawetaa kana nthĩ ĩno nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yĩkalĩte myaka mbilioni mbingĩ mũno.
O na kau ithyĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩtũĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kũmbwa, tũileanaa na maũndũ ma saenzi. Tũĩkĩĩaa kana Mbivilia nĩyĩtĩkĩlanĩte na maũndũ ma saenzi ala maminĩte kũĩkĩĩthw'a kana nĩ ma w'o.

translation:
Alas. The name of Jehovah makes me tremble like God himself in countless ways. We make him tremble like God himself day and night, every day and 24 hours. Why? Because some people study things that contradict the Bible. For example, here's something to consider:
The length of a day is 24 hours. And sometimes one day can be 24 hours. In fact, when the Bible uses the word "day," it doesn't always mean a period of light.
—Ecclesiastes 2:4; Psalm 90:4.
The age of the earth. Some people believe that the earth is very old, perhaps billions of years. But the Bible says that the earth was created in six days, and the earth and everything on it were completed. (Genesis 1:1) Therefore, the name of Jehovah agrees with scientific evidence, but this age of the earth, which is said to be billions of years old, does not agree.
And even though the name of Jehovah makes us tremble, we agree with science. We believe that the Bible agrees with science, because it is accurate and true.

text:
Asomi nĩmethĩawa na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũĩkĩĩa kana Yesũ aĩ kw'o. Yĩineenea maũndũ ala maandĩkiwe nĩ asomi ĩũlũ wa Yesũ na Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa, ĩvuku yĩtawa Encyclopædia Britannica, ya mwaka wa 2002, yaĩtye: "
Maũndũ aa maandĩkiwe nĩ andũ matendeeasya ngalĩ o na ĩmwe monanasya kana o na andũ ala maleaa Ũklĩsto nĩmeesĩ nesa vyũ kana Yesũ aĩ kw'o. Kwa ĩvinda ya mbee, mũthyanĩ wa myaka ya 1700, myakanĩ ya 1800, na mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1900, andũ amwe nĩmaambĩĩie kwasya kana Yesũ ndaĩ kw'o, ĩndĩ mate na itumi mbĩanĩu."
Mwakanĩ wa 2006, ĩvuku yĩtawa Jesus and Archaeology yaisye: "
Ũmũnthĩ vai mũsomi wa w'o wĩthĩawa na nzika kana ve Mũyuti weetawa Yesũ mwana wa Yosevu waĩ kw'o; aingĩ nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana nĩtwĩsĩ maũndũ maingĩ mũno ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala weekie na momanyĩsyo make."
Mbivilia yonanasya kana Yesũ nĩ mũndũ waĩ kw'o. Nĩwetaa masyĩtwa ma mosyaanĩo make na masyĩtwa ma andũ ma mũsyĩ wake. (Mathayo 1:1; 13:55) O na ĩngĩ, nĩwetaa masyĩtwa ma asumbĩ me nguma ala masumbĩkĩte ĩvinda yake. (Luka 3:1, 2) Maũndũ ta asu nĩmatetheeasya asomi kũmanya ũw'o wa maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ.

translation:
Scholars have been challenged by the historical question of whether Jesus existed. It cites sources such as the scholarly work on the life of Jesus and Christ from the perspective of ambassadors, the eighth edition of Encyclopædia Britannica, from 2002, which states: "
The historicity of Jesus is disputed by some scholars, while others accept his existence. Throughout the 18th, 19th, and early 20th centuries, some scholars questioned whether Jesus ever lived, citing lack of evidence."
In 2006, the book Jesus and Archaeology stated: "
Most historians agree that someone named Jesus son of Joseph existed; many believe we know quite a bit about him through the available sources and information."
The Bible questions whether Jesus was a real person. It mentions his family names and the names of his ancestors. (Matthew 1:1; 13:55) And further, it mentions the names of governors who were in power during his time. (Luke 3:1, 2) These details help scholars understand the context of the biblical accounts.

text:
Ndongoi kisioni kya Rift Valley ya yiulu syenda vethiwe na mboya syii mwanya kuatiania na uvithukii na ung'ei wa indo ula wikinyiite muno kisioni kiu.
Ndongoi ii ila syivikite kyathini kya uthaithi wa kutunga muvea kisioni kya Ainabkoi kila kii kauntini ya Uasin Gishu, nimaweta kana uvithukii uu niumatwiikiiye kitung'u na no mboya syii mwanya itonya kuete usungio.
Senator wa Nandi Samson Cherargei easya kana nukwendekethya mwiyao wa kuukitana na umaamai uvitithwe mbungeni nikana avithukii ta asu makoseawa matambya ma kii miyao, aiweta misyi mbingi niityitwe ite kindu itina wa ene kuwawa na indo syoo kutavwa.
Nake minista mwoloote muviani wa malelu na ukui Kipchumba Murkomen easya kana silikali nikuikiithya nikweethiwa na muuw'o mwianiu mbee wa mboya isu kutwaiiwa.
Nake mutetheesya wa vakuvi na muu nthini wa president William Ruto, Farouk Kibet niwaweta no nginya kaunti sya Baringo, West Pokot, Turkana, Elgeyo Marakwet na Samburu ikaetwe vamwe kwa wiwano namakwatianio na mboya iyiendeeya kutuumanya muuw'o kati woo.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Ndorobo community in the Rift Valley region has been displaced by floods which have caused destruction and insecurity, leading to a humanitarian crisis in the area.
This community, however, has appealed to the government to provide assistance to those affected by the floods, and also requested more resources to prevent further suffering.
Nandi Senator Samson Cherargei stated that discussions will be held with the relevant authorities regarding the damage caused by the floods, and he promised to bring a motion to parliament to address the issue, adding that many families have lost everything and need help.
Meanwhile, Infrastructure Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen stated that efforts are underway to restore infrastructure damaged by the recent heavy rains.
Furthermore, President William Ruto's advisor on livestock affairs, Farouk Kibet, has visited several counties including Baringo, West Pokot, Turkana, Elgeyo Marakwet and Samburu to assess the situation and coordinate aid distribution to those affected by the ongoing drought.

Ndeto isu syaneeniwe nĩ kelĩtu ka myaka 13 ĩtina wa kũnengwa kakitĩ ta mũthĩnzĩo. Nake mũndũ mũka ũngĩ wĩkĩte maendeeo maũndũnĩ ma viasala aisye kana kombyũta ĩla wanengiwe nĩ ĩthe e sukulu yaĩ mũthĩnzĩo watumie maũndũ make maseũva. Na mũndũũme wĩla kũtwaana o mĩtũkĩ aisye kana mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũseo vyũ waanengwa waĩ kaati waseũvĩiw'e nĩ kĩveti kyake kwondũ wa mũthenya wa kũtanĩa mwaka woo wa mbee kuma matwaana.
Kĩla mwaka, andũ aingĩ nĩmatũmĩaa ĩvinda yoo na vinya woo maimantha mũthĩnzĩo ũla "mũseo vyũ" manenge anyanyae kana andũ ma mũsyĩ ĩla me na ũndũ wa mwanya mekwĩka. Na andũ aingĩ no mende kwĩw'a ndeto ta ila syaneenwa mwambĩĩonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ. Nao nata ĩũlũ waku? No wende kũnengane kana kũnengwa mũthĩnzĩo ũkwoneka wĩ wa vata?
Ũndũ ũsu no wĩthĩwe wĩ wa kwendeesya mũno nũndũ no ũtanĩthye ũla wanengwa mũthĩnzĩo na ũla waũnengane. O na nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwĩ mũyo kũnengane kwĩ kwosa." (Meko ma Atũmwa 20:35) Kwa w'o, ũtanu ũla mũndũ ũkwataa nũndũ wa kũnengane no wongelekeele ethĩwa ũla wanewa nĩwoonany'a kana nĩwendeew'a nĩ kĩla wanengwa.
Kwoou, ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana mũthĩnzĩo waku ũkũtanĩthye na ũitanĩthya ũla wanenga? Na ethĩwa ndũtonya kũnengane mũthĩnzĩo "mũseo vyũ," ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana mũthĩnzĩo waku wendeesye ũla wanenga?

Ĩĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nitetheeasya andũ ĩla kwaumĩla mĩisyo. Nĩtũtetheeasya Ngũsĩ na andũ ala angĩ mate Ngũsĩ. Ũndũ ũsu wosanĩte na ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akalatia 6:10 "Kwondũ wa ũu, o ũndũ twĩĩthĩwa na ũthei, twĩkei andũ onthe nesa, ĩndĩ mũno ala ma nyũmba ya mũĩkĩĩo." Nĩtũtataa tũkiakisye andũ na tũimatetheesya kĩ-veva nũndũ ũu nĩw'o methĩawa mayenda.—2 Akolintho 1:3, 4.
Ũndũ Mĩvango Yĩkawa
Ĩla mũisyo wakĩtĩka atumĩa ma ikundi kĩsionĩ kĩu nĩmatataa makakũnĩa simũ andũ ala mokaa ũmbanonĩ ikundinĩ isu nĩ kana mamanye kana nasũvĩĩku na nĩ ũtethyo wĩva matonya kwenda. Ĩtina wa ũu, atumĩa nĩmatavasya ovisi wa ũvonge wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũla ũũngamĩe nthĩ yoo ũndũ meethĩa na ũtethyo ũla manengane.
Ethĩwa ikundi sya kĩsio kĩla kĩkwatĩtwe nĩ mũisyo iitonya kwĩanĩsya mavata ma andũ ala makwatĩtwe nĩ mũisyo, Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩyĩkaa mĩvango ya kũnengane syĩndũ ila itonya kwĩthĩwa iyendeka. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwosanĩte na ũndũ Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa matetheanĩasya ĩvindanĩ ya yũa. (1 Akolintho 16:1-4) Ovisi wa ũvonge ũla ũngamĩe nthĩ ĩsu nũnyuvaa Kamitii ya Kũnengane Ũtethyo na ũyonany'a ũndũ maũndũ maĩle kwĩkwa. Nasyo Ngũsĩ kuma isionĩ ingĩ nĩsyumasya ĩvinda yasyo vamwe na malĩ syasyo itetheesye.—Nthimo 17:17.
Vala Mbesa Syumaa
Nzĩa ĩmwe mbesa ila itũmawa movisinĩ ma ũvonge ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itũmĩawa nĩ kũtetheesya andũ ala makwatwa nĩ mĩisyo. (Meko ma Atũmwa 11:27-30; 2 Akolintho 8:13-15) Mbesa sya kũtetheesya andũ ala makwatwa nĩ mũisyo itũmĩawa kũmanenga ũtethyo, iinengawe ala maũngamĩe wĩa ũsu nũndũ methĩawa meyumĩtye na ngenda. Mĩvothi ĩla yumaw'a ĩtũmĩawa nesa.—2 Akolintho 8:20.

Yes, God's name is important and people appreciate when we use it. We honor God and others when we pronounce God's name correctly. When someone asks about our name, we can kindly explain why it is important to us and how it connects us to the Almighty God. In doing so, we can offer to share information about Jehovah's organization and show them how it helps people to learn the truth and live by its principles.
Each congregation has overseers who work hard to care for the spiritual needs of those associated with that congregation, and they are willing to help anyone who wants to know more. Furthermore, overseers encourage experienced brothers to visit congregations to give talks that strengthen faith. (1 Corinthians 16:1-4) These visits build up the brotherhood and provide an opportunity for everyone to benefit from good counsel. At times, funds are needed to assist fellow believers who are affected by disasters. Ũthũku wumaa va?
Andũ nĩmendete kwĩthĩwa me auu, me aĩkĩĩku, na me tei. Ĩndĩ no twĩkũlye, Nĩkĩ kwĩthĩawa na ũtũli wa mĩao, ũng'endu, na ũsili ũte wa katĩ? Ũmũnthĩ nĩtũsomaa kana tũkew'a maũvoo ma kũtelemya. Yo nĩvatonyeka vakethĩwa ve mũndũ ũtumaa andũ meka mothũku?—Soma 1 Yoana 5:19.
We Ngai oombĩte andũ me na wendi wa kwĩka naĩ? Aiee, ĩndĩ amombĩte na kĩtutya kyake, na matonya kwonany'a wendo o take. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:27; Yovu 34:10) O na ĩngĩ, Ngai nĩwanengie andũ ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ĩla asyai maitũ ma mbee mavĩtisye, nĩmaleile mayĩyĩelekany'a na Ngai, na kwoou meethĩwa me ene naĩ. Na ĩndĩ twakwatwa nĩ naĩ nũndũ wa ĩvĩtyo yĩu.—Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 32:4, 5.
W'o ũthũku wĩendeea kwĩthĩwa kw'o tene na tene?

O na kau ũthũku nĩ mwingĩ ũmũnthĩ, Ngai nũwĩtĩkĩlĩtye kwa kavinda nĩ kana kĩla mũndũ one maũndũ ala ũthũku ũetete. (2 Vetelo 3:7-9) Ĩndĩ o mĩtũkĩ nthĩ nĩkusũwa nĩ andũ me na ũtanu na mamwĩw'aa Ngai.—Soma Savuli 37:9-11.

translation:
What is true worship?
People want to be admired for their appearance, their abilities, and what they possess. But we should worship with humility, with a sincere heart, and with faith—is this not better than seeking glory from men?—Read 1 John 5:19.
Does God ask us to understand his ways? Yes, he does so through his spirit and by helping us to appreciate his love. (Proverbs 1:27; Job 34:10) And further, God enables people to benefit from his forgiveness. If they make mistakes, he helps them to correct themselves and to desire to please him. And when we are moved by his holy spirit, we will show appreciation for it.—Read The Law Given to Moses 32:4, 5.
What kind of worship is pleasing to God?
God wants us to live honestly every day. (Psalm 27:11) And he helps us to discern how to deal with difficult situations, so that we can maintain integrity. We can also learn to appreciate God's love in this way.—Read Psalm 32:8.
But sometimes it seems unfair that bad things happen to good people, while wicked people prosper. (2 Peter 3:7-9) However, remember that God is patient and gives everyone an opportunity to change. (Psalm 37:9-11)

Ĩvinda ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ yĩthĩawa no ĩvinda ĩseo ya kũsũanĩa moathimo ala tũkakwata nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo. Ũmwe wa moathimo asu nĩ ũthayũũkyo. Yeova ndavangĩte andũ makusae. Nũndũ wa ũu, kĩkw'ũ nĩ kĩmwe kya syĩndũ ila itũũmĩasya mũno ngoonĩ. (1Ako 15:26) Yesũ nĩwaũmĩie ngoonĩ ĩla woonie amanyĩw'a make me na kyeva nũndũ wa kĩkw'ũ kya Lasalo. (Yoa 11:33-35) Nũndũ Yesũ avw'anene na Ĩthe wake, no twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana o nake Yeova nũũmĩaa mũno ĩla woona twĩ na kyeva. (Yoa 14:7) Yeova e na mea ma kwona ĩvinda yĩla ũkathayũũkya andũ ala makwie yĩ ĩviku, o naitũ nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mea ma kwĩsa kwona ala makwie.—Yovu 14:14, 15.

Andu atatu nimatiwa ni thayu angi kauta mayaasya metho itina wa kunywa nzovi ngune muungu kilioni kya Mbeere ya yiulu kauntini ya Embu.
Ekali ma kisio kiu meweta kana uthoosya wa mbuki sya makavo withiitwe wikiinyiite muno itina wa mivea ila yaile kuukitana nasyo kwithiwa ileelete.
Muyumbe wa kilio mbunge kiu Geoffrey Kiringa niwaumania viasala isu aiweta ena mauvoo kana atandithya asu mena mukwatianio na amwe ma maovisa ma volisi nzeleke, aikulya komanda wa volisi kisioni kiu kwosa matambya ala maile kwa asu na miyao iyaatiiwa.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
People were shocked by the news that a young man committed suicide by drinking poison in Mbeere North constituency in Embu county.
The incident which happened last week has sparked debate on mental health issues among youth, leading to calls for increased awareness campaigns.
Mbeere North MP Geoffrey Kiringa condemned the act, saying he was saddened by the loss of another life, urging parents and teachers to closely monitor children and provide them with guidance, while calling on police commanders to investigate the matter thoroughly and bring those responsible to book.

Maũndũ ala monekete meonany'a kana atavany'a eũ ala mamanyĩaw'a kuma mwambĩĩonĩ kwĩthĩwa na kĩthito na kũtavanasya mate kũeka, mavinda maingĩ methĩawa atavany'a aseo. (Nth 22:6; Avi 3:16) Aa nĩ maũndũ amwe mekwonany'a ũndũ tũtonya kũtetheesya mũmanyĩw'a ethĩwe na mũsingi mũseo ũtavany'anĩ:
Mũmanyĩw'a atw'ĩka mũtavany'a oou, ambĩĩa kũmũmanyĩsya. (km 8/15 1) Mũtetheesye amanye vata wa kwĩthĩawa na mũvango wa kũtavanasya kĩla kyumwa. (Avi 1:10) Neenaa maũndũ maseo ĩũlũ wa andũ ma kĩsio kĩla mũtavanasya. (Avi 4:8) Mũtetheesye atavany'e vamwe na mũsyaĩĩsya wa kĩkundi kyake na atavany'a ala angĩ nĩ kana atetheke kumana na ũmanyi woo.—Nth 1:5; km 10/12 6 ¶3
Mũmanyĩw'a waku avatiswa, ndũkaeke kũmwĩkĩa vinya na kũmũmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũtavany'a, na mũno mũno ethĩwa ndaminĩte kũsoma ĩvuku 'Wendo wa Ngai.'—km 12/13 7
Ĩla wĩ na mũtavany'a mweũ ũtavany'anĩ, tũmĩa nzĩa yĩ laisi. Mũkathe kuma ngoonĩ amina kũtavya mũndũ, na ĩndĩ ũimũtavya maũndũ amwe maseo ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana ethĩwe mũtavany'a mũseango.—km-SW 5/10 7

translation:
These things happened so that the prophecy might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, that all the nations would mock them. (Mt 22:6; Ps 3:16) And these are some things we see happening to show that the time has come to prove our loyalty to God and to avoid being ashamed:
Let us strengthen ourselves to preach, urging people to become loyal. (km 8/15 1) Prove yourself faithful in taking advantage of opportunities to witness and in avoiding shame at all times. If a brother falls, kindly help him up and encourage him to regain his loyalty, and at the same time endeavor to read the book "Love of God."—km 12/13 7
Even if you have a disloyal relative, use tact. Avoid speaking disparagingly about anyone, and do not mention certain things that could cause someone to feel ashamed.—km-SW 5/10 7

text:
Nĩwĩsĩ twĩneenea Ũsumbĩ wĩva?— Twĩneenea Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũkaseũvya nthĩ yĩthĩwe yĩ nzeo. We nũkwenda kũmanya maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ ũsu?—
Kĩla ũsumbĩ nĩwĩthĩawa na mũsumbĩ na ethĩawa asumbĩkĩte andũ ala me nthĩ ĩsu. Nĩwĩsĩ Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nũũ?— Nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto, nake ekalaa ĩtunĩ. O mĩtũkĩ akasumbĩka andũ onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ! Wĩona ta tũkethĩwa na ũtanu ĩla Yesũ wĩsumbĩka nthĩ yonthe?—
Nĩ maũndũ meva wĩenda kwona nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩla ĩkethĩwa ĩseũvĩtw'e ĩkatw'ĩka nzeo
Tũkeethĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno! Nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ andũ maikokita kana mathi kaũnĩ. Andũ onthe makeethĩwa mendene. Vai mũndũ ũkawaa kana kũkw'a. Ala ilalinda makoona nthĩ, ala matew'aa makeew'a, na ala me na maaũ mate na vinya makasemba na kũtũũlĩla. Kũkeethĩwa na lĩu mwingĩ mũno. Nasyo nyamũ iikethĩwa na ũmaitha katĩ wasyo, o na iikethĩwa na ũmaitha na andũ. Andũ ala makwie makathayũũkw'a. Aũme na aka aingĩ ala weemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wamo kavukunĩ kaa ta Leveka, Laavi, Ndaviti, na Eliya o namo makathayũũkw'a! We nũkwenda wĩkomana namo ĩla methayũũkw'a?—
Yeova nũkwendete na endaa wĩthĩwe na ũtanu. Kwoou endeea kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wake na ũikwata mĩao yake. Weeka ũu, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kwĩkala tene na tene nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩla ĩkaseũvw'a yĩthĩwe yĩ nzeo! Ũu nĩw'o ũkwenda?—
SOMA MBIVILIANĨ YAKU
Isaia 2:4; 11:6-9; 25:8; 33:24; 35:5, 6
Yoana 5:28, 29; 17:3

translation:
Are we near the Kingdom?— We are near God's Kingdom. This kingdom will beautify everything perfectly. Do you want to know more about this kingdom?—
Every kingdom has a king and someone appointed to rule over other people like us. Is Jesus Christ the King of God's Kingdom?— Yes, He is, He sat down at the right hand. Oh, how many people will rule over others through this earth! Do you see that we are saved by the life that Jesus gave for us?—
These things are happening so that we can see the world that was made beautiful and make it perfect.
We are saved by much power! The world's foundations tremble and shake. Many people are being saved. Go, someone may fall or stumble. But let them protect their eyes, let them be careful, and those who have ears listen and understand. To be saved by much power. And also, a person is saved either alone or with others. People who were once stumbling are now standing firmly! Remember and those others who were strong like Levia, Levi, David, and Elijah, they too stood firmly! Do you want to join those who stand firmly?—
Jehovah wants you to approach with power. Let him help you to understand his purpose and hold onto his laws. Look, this is what saves you from always being troubled by the world that was ruined perfectly! This is what you need.—

text:
Ula wai mumbunge wa kiliombunge kya Kitui Rural na ungamiite na kyama kya Uda,Charles Mutisya Nyamai,niwakunia kula yake sukuluni wa musingi wa Kanyangi.
Aineena na andiki ma mauvoo,Nyamai niwaumania kiko kila kikitikie kwi amwe ma aatiyi make kya kuumiswa na kuvuwa na ingi umwe wa aatiiyi make aviviswa nyumba utukuni wa kuamukia umunthi,aiweta kila mwenenthi ena haki ya kukwata mbau muteti ula unukwenda.
Mumbunge wa kitui Rural na na ukutetea kivila kii na kyama kya wiper Mboni Mwalika niwakuna kura yake kiseseni kya kukunia kura kya sukulu wa musingi wa mbitini.
Aineena na aandiki ma mauvoo niwaweta kana itina wa usakuani nukwithiwa maithakya ikwani kortini asikatite nzama ya unyuvani na mivaka ya IEBC nundu wa kumanangia ivinda na ingi kumatungia ngalama ya ilovia ila manatumie kwikunia maleve.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Member of Parliament for Kitui Rural and associated with the Uda party, Charles Mutisya Nyamai, was yesterday at his former primary school, Kanyangi Primary School.
Speaking with journalists, Nyamai said he is worried because whenever one of his children is sent home for fees, another of his children is sent home at night to welcome the morning, saying everyone has the right to get a good education.
The MP for Kitui Rural and a staunch supporter of the Wiper party, Mboni Mwalika, cast his vote at the Mbitiini Primary School polling station.
Speaking with journalists, he stated that if the issue of insecurity is not addressed properly it will end up in court and cause problems for the IEBC due to the chaos and much money being used to campaign but not being used to help people.

text:
Maovisaa ikumi ma kambuni wa unyaiikya wa mwaki wa Kenya power nimeuthakwa kotini umunthi kioko kusungia makwani ala masikaatitwe namo ma kulikiliila na kutambaikya uthukumi vamwe na kuvuthiisya wia woo.
Ikumi aa maneekiiwe mbini kwi iyoo na vala makomie kolokoloni wa Muthaiga meteele kuthakwa kotini umunti.
Kii ni kuatiania na kuvaluka kwa mutambo wa unyaaikkya wa mwaki kiseseni kya ilovi – Kiambere kyumwa kithelu undu ula unatumie isio mbingi vaa kenya ikosa mwaki na kuete wasyo wa mamilioni ma ilovia.
Kwii matuku 15 mwei uu mmaovisaa manene muviani usu nimaakulilwe maukulyo ni maovisaa ma isali (DCI) yiulu wa kuvaluka kwa itui inya nene sya unyaiikya wa mwaki.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Ten officials from Kenya Power's procurement department have been arrested in court yesterday following allegations of stealing transformers and conspiring to defraud others and obstructing investigations.
The ten are accused of two counts of conspiracy to commit an offense and damaging property belonging to Muthaiga Estate during their arrest.
This is related to the vandalism and theft of electricity infrastructure - Kiambere dam which has caused significant losses to Kenya due to lack of electricity and loss of millions of shillings.
For the past 15 days this month, major operations have been carried out by detectives from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) leading to the recovery of stolen electricity equipment.

text:
O mĩtũkĩ kamwana ketawa Hugo, ke na myaka ĩkũmi, nĩkanengiwe mũthĩnzĩo wĩsĩkĩe ta Diana Award nĩ kĩkundi kĩmwe kya kũtetheesya andũ kya Britain, nũndũ wa kũtetheesya syana sya sukulu yoo imanye ũndũ itonya kwĩka ĩla syathĩnw'a.
Hugo aisye atĩĩ: "Nanengwa mũthĩnzĩo ũũ nũndũ wa ĩla vitio ya katuni ya Kĩlya Vinya Mũndũ Ũkũthĩnasya Ĩndĩ ũte Kwĩyũkitĩa. Kĩla neemanyĩisye vitionĩ ĩsu nĩkyo kyandetheeisye nambĩĩa kũtavya syana ũndũ itonya kwĩka syathĩnw'a."
Mbee vyũ, Hugo oonisye alimũ make vitio ĩsu. Nĩmendeeiw'e mũno nginya mavanga syana syonthe ikavingũaa Kĩsese kya jw.org. Yu syana mbingĩ ila syĩ na myaka katĩ wa nyanya na ĩkũmi sukulunĩ ĩsu, nitũmĩaa Kĩsese kya jw.org. Syana isu syaasya kana kĩsese kĩu nĩkĩitetheesye kwona ũndũ itonya kwĩka syathĩnw'a, vamwe na kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ta, Ndonya kũkwata anyanya ma w'o ata?
Mĩvango Mĩseo Nĩtetheesye Andũ ma Mũika
Sukulunĩ ĩngĩ yĩ nthĩ ya Britain, kamwana ketawa Elijah, kala ke na myaka nyanya, nĩkathĩnaw'a. Ke na andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmasyaisye vitio ya Kĩlya Vinya Mũndũ Ũkũthĩnasya. Nĩmaneeneie ũndũ Elijah ũtonya kwasya kana kwĩka ĩla wathĩnw'a. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie ethĩwa na ũkũmbaũ wa kũkitana na thĩna ũsu. Ĩvinda yĩmwe, kyumwa kĩla sukulu ũsu waneeneaa ĩũlũ wa kũthĩnw'a, mwalimũ mũnene nĩwoonisye syana syonthe vitio ĩsu.
Vate nzika andũ ma mũika ma nthĩ ya Britain ti mo mathĩnaw'a me oka. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ wĩkĩkaa kĩla vandũ nthĩ yonthe, na vitio ĩno nĩtethetye andũ aingĩ mũno.
Ivie, ũla nĩ kelĩtu ke na myaka ĩkũmi kuma nthĩ ya United States, nĩwakĩaa mwĩĩtu ũmwe masomaa ĩmwe nũndũ nĩwamũthĩnasya. Ĩtina wa kwĩloela vitio ĩno ya Kĩlya Vinya Mũndũ Ũkũthĩnasya, nĩwakwatie ũkũmbaũ wa kũneena na mwĩĩtu ũsu. O na nĩwaneenie na mwalimũ na amũtetheesya. Mwĩĩtu ũsu nĩwamwĩtisye ũekeo, na yu mekalanasya nesa.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyendaa andũ ma mũika maendeee nesa. Nĩtũkũendeea kumya ũtao mũseo wa kũmatetheesya kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna ala mamakwataa ta kũthĩnw'a.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Young Hugo has been honored with a Diana Award by a British youth charity group, for helping his schoolmates cope with difficulties when they lose loved ones.
Hugo said: "I am very happy about this award because of the impact it will have on the children of Kilima Vinya Primary School who are facing challenges. Every encouragement I receive motivates me to continue helping children cope with loss."
Recently, Hugo shared his experience with others. He was interviewed about his efforts on the website jw.org. Many children between the ages of nine and ten at his school use jw.org. These children asked if the website could help them cope with loss, as well as provide practical advice—like, how can we comfort others?
Local Youth Helping Others
At another school in Britain, nine-year-old Elijah was also recognized. He and his friends shared their experiences on the Kilima Vinya Primary School website. It was inspiring to see how Elijah was able to talk about or deal with his own grief. This situation highlighted the importance of connecting with others. One day, when his school had a bereavement, a teacher gathered all the students together to share their feelings.
Many young people in Britain are experiencing similar situations. This is something that affects everyone, and this website helps many people.
Ivy, who is ten years old from the United States, contacted a classmate who was grieving. After finding this Kilima Vinya Primary School website, she felt encouraged to connect with her classmate. She spoke to her teacher and got permission to help. Her classmate appreciated her support, and they talked things over.
Jehovah's Witnesses encourage young people to continue offering such support. We will continue to find ways to help others cope with difficult times like these.

translation:
The incident at Tsavo West National Park involving the cutting down of trees and those cutting down firewood from the forest has caused tension with residents due to the fire that went through the trees cut down for firewood from the Kyulu forest.
Speaking during a meeting with the Thange Ward MCA Eric Katumo and officials from KWS, they agreed to continue working with residents to educate them about the importance of tree planting and conservation, but also warned against cutting down the trees.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mũndũ nde na ũtonyi wa kũete mũuo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, ĩndĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, ũla nĩ silikalĩ ya ĩtunĩ ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto, nĩyo ĩkaete mũuo. Kwoona ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo ũsu mũseo.
Ngai akatuma "
makaũ mathela kũvika kĩtulu kya nthĩ," na kwa nzĩa ĩsu ayĩanĩsya watho wake wa kũete "
mũuo wĩthĩwe kũũ nthĩ andũnĩ ala wendeeaw'a nĩmo."—Savuli 46:9; Luka 2:14.
Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkasumbĩka nthĩ yonthe kuma ĩtunĩ. (Ndanieli 7:14) Nũndũ nĩ silikalĩ ya nthĩ yonthe, ĩkamina kĩmena kya nthĩ, kĩla nĩ ũndũ ũmwe ũtumaa kwĩthĩwa na makaũ.
Yesũ e Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai etawa "
Mũnene wa Mũuo," na akaĩkĩĩthya kana mũuo "
ndũkethĩwa na mũminũkĩlyo."—Isaia 9:6, 7.
Andũ ala mendete kaũ maiketĩkĩlw'a kũlika Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ngai nũndũ '
ngoo ya Yeova nĩmenete ũla wendete ũng'endu.'—Savuli 11:5; Nthimo 2:22.
Ngai nũmanyĩasya ala me ungu wa Ũsumbĩ wake kwĩkala na mũuo. Ĩineenea ũndũ ũsu, Mbivilia yaĩtye: "
Na makatusya mbyũ syoo itw'ĩke maembe ma ng'ombe, na matumo moo tũvyũ twĩ ngoto twa kũsea; mbaĩ ndĩkokĩlĩlya mbaĩ ũvyũ, o na itikemanyĩsya kaũ ĩngĩ."—Isaia 2:3, 4.
Ũmũnthĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova milioni mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ niendeee kũmanyĩw'a nĩ Ngai ũndũ itonya kwĩthĩwa andũ ma mũuo. (Mathayo 5:9) O na kau tumĩte mbaĩnĩ mbingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na twĩkalaa nthĩ mbee wa 230, tũyĩtĩkĩlaa kũkitana na andũ ala angĩ.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova niendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ũndũ itonya kwĩthĩwa na mũuo ũmũnthĩ

translation:
The Bible Reveals
A person who has faith in God's promise of life eternal, through Jesus Christ, can have hope. The Bible reveals how to find this hope.
God sent "
his Word to earth," and through it he shows his purpose for mankind.—Psalm 46:9; Luke 2:14.
God's Kingdom will triumph over all opposition. (Daniel 7:14) But it is also a real government, which is supported by powerful forces.
Jesus, as the representative of God's Kingdom, is called "
the Prince of Peace," and he will ensure that peace prevails.—Isaiah 9:6, 7.
Those who trust in God's Kingdom can be sure that Jehovah's purpose will succeed.—Psalm 11:5; Proverbs 2:22.
God shows all those who love him what his purpose is. The Bible says:
"
And they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks."—Isaiah 2:3, 4.
Today, millions of people around the world are learning about God's purpose for mankind. (Matthew 5:9) And we are using many languages to reach out to people in over 230 lands and territories.
Jehovah's Witnesses continue to teach people about God's purpose.

MWĨKALĨLE WA AKLĨSTO NA WĨA WA KŨTAVANY'A—KAVUKU KA KWĨMANYĨSYA KA ŨMBANO
Mwei wa 1 2016
Ũndũ ũtonya kũnengane ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya o vamwe na mbulosua Ũvoo Mũseo Kuma kwa Ngai! Tũmĩa maũndũ asu na ũyĩandĩka ũndũ ũtonya kwasya ũtũmĩĩte ndeto syaku.
MAŨNDŨ MA VATA KUMA NDETONĨ YA NGAI
Kwakũna visa ũndũ Mũsumbĩ Esekia waĩ na kĩthito kya kũtũngĩĩa ũthaithi wa w'o. Tũmĩa mavisa, mavu, na matukũ ma ĩla maũndũ meekĩkie ala me ĩvukunĩ ya 2 Mavinda 29–30 nĩ kana iũtetheesye.
ĨKĨA KĨTHITO WĨTHIWE MŨTAVANY'A MŨSEO
Nzĩa itano syĩ laisi ũtonya kũtũmĩa kũmanyĩasya mũndũ ũtũmĩĩte mbulosua Ũvoo Mũseo Kuma kwa Ngai!
MWĨKALĨKE WA AKLĨSTO
Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kĩthito na wendo witũ kwondũ wa wĩa mũtheu nthĩnĩ wa nyũmba sitũ sya kũthaithĩa?
MAŨNDŨ MA VATA KUMA NDETONĨ YA NGAI
Kĩlila kwa Mũsumbĩ Manase nĩkwamũtetheeisye mũno. Kwasianĩsya ũndũ ũsumbĩ wake waĩlyĩ atanamba kũtavw'a na amina kũlekw'a kuma Mbaviloni. (2 Mavinda 33–36)
MAŨNDŨ MA VATA KUMA NDETONĨ YA NGAI
Ũndũ maũndũ meekĩkie kwosana na ĩvuku ya Esala 1–5. O na kau kwaĩ isiĩĩi mbingĩ Ayuti nĩmasyokie kuma Mbaviloni, mambĩĩsya ũthaithi wa w'o, na maaka ĩngĩ ĩkalũ.
MAŨNDŨ MA VATA KUMA NDETONĨ YA NGAI
Esala vamwe na ala maendete Yelusaleme maaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, kĩthito kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa w'o, na ũkũmbaũ. Tũmĩa visa na mavu ila syonanĩtw'e iũtetheesye ũkũne visa savalĩ yoo.

Maũndũ atatũ ma kũtũtetheesya ĩla twasyokea mũndũ wendeeiw'e nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia.

Thayũ nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa mwanya. Twonanasya kana nĩtwonaa thayũ wĩ wa vata kwĩanana na ũndũ tũkũũtũmĩa. Twĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũtũmĩe inengo sitũ na ũtonyi witũ kũmũtaĩa Yeova, Mũnengani wa thayũ. (Sav 36:9; Ũvu 4:11) Ĩndĩ mawĩmakĩo ma kĩla mũthenya no matume tũtavĩtya maũndũ ma kĩ-veva mbee. (Mk 4:18, 19) Kĩla ũmwe waitũ no ekũlye-ĩ: 'Nyie nĩnĩmũnengae Yeova kĩla kĩseo vyũ? (Osea 14:2) Wĩa ũla nĩthũkũmaa nũnziĩĩaa kũmũthũkũma Yeova ũndũ vaĩle? Nĩ na mĩvango yĩva ya kĩ-veva? Ndonya kwongeleela ũthũkũmi wakwa ata?' Ethĩwa nũkwona ve vandũ ũtonya kwĩka maendeeo, mũvoye Yeova aũtetheesye na ĩndĩ ũyĩka moalyũku ala maĩle. Vate nzika, kũmũtaĩa Yeova kĩla mũthenya nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma wĩkala wĩ mwĩanĩe na wĩ mũtanu!—Sav 61:8.
ĨLOELEI VITIO YĨ NA KYONGO, TŨMĨA KĨNENGO KYAKU KŨMŨTHŨKŨMA YEOVA, NA ĨNDĨ MŨISŨNGĨA MAKŨLYO AA:
Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ ũte wa ũĩ kũtũmĩa inengo syaku nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩno ya Satani? (1Yoa 2:17)
Nĩ moathimo meva andũ ala manengae Yeova kĩla kĩseo vyũ makwataa?
Ũtonya kũtũmĩa inengo na ũmanyi waku maũndũnĩ ta meva ma ũthũkũmi mũtheu?

translation:
Your strength is perfect in weakness. We are happy when we see our strength being used to do what is right. With Jehovah's help, we can find ways to use our abilities and energy to praise Jehovah, the God of strength. (Ps 36:9; Prov 4:11) Let us always be careful not to become distracted by things that are unimportant. (Mark 4:18, 19) Each one of us should ask himself: "Am I truly praising Jehovah at all times?" (Hosea 14:2) Who will encourage me to praise Jehovah more fully? Do I have important reasons for wanting to please him? And then, work hard to improve your spirituality. Be willing to let Jehovah guide you, and do not be afraid to ask for his help. Remember this, praising Jehovah at all times is something that can make you strong and successful!—Ps 61:8.

Is this something good that you can use to serve Jehovah wholeheartedly? (1 John 2:17)
Are there others who praise Jehovah at all times whom you could imitate?
Can you use your abilities and knowledge to teach people about the truth?

translation:
It was 17 hours on May when Muthemba of the three vehicles became 42 years old and was arrested for possessing vital medicine at Machakos Level 5 Hospital due to injuries sustained from an accident involving three vehicles, but some were obstructing the road and causing congestion, taking people to Kaseve village in Kuma Masaku towards Kitui via Mbanga three vehicles, this vehicle Masaku went to Mbumbuni Makueni.
The suspect is said to be involved in a conspiracy to meet with Mbanga's thieves around Masaku, David Mwongela, who drives the suspect's vehicle or the three vehicles along the road, Kumana and another builder who knows the secrets of Kaseve.
Police report
One police officer from Kuma Police Station in Masii Sub-County, Machakos County, was transferred to Masii Police Station and accused of assaulting the OCS of Kiseese Police Station and stealing Sh71,000, but it was paid through cash bail and she is being held until May when she will appear in court in Kiseese.
The suspect is also accused by Commander of Police Operations in Mwala Sub-County, Ronald Kirui, who drives the suspect's vehicle or the accident vehicle, claiming that the police officer found stolen car parts at his home, but he denies the allegations and will be taken to court to answer the charges.

Ĩkaseti yĩĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya nĩyĩũtũtetheesya kũtũngaa mũvea kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũseo vyũ kuma kwa Ngai.
COVER SUBJECT

THE WATCHTOWER AND ANNOUNCER OF JEHOVAH—A PUBLICATION OF THE WATCH TOWER SOCIETY
May 11 2017
This issue considers the experience of a publisher and shows how his ministry led to an interest in God's Word. We will also discuss why true Christians use their time wisely.
QUESTIONS FROM READERS
Is it wrong to be ambitious? Does our considering the example of Israelites help us to be more zealous in worshiping Jehovah?

Is it wrong if one is motivated by selfish ambition? Continuing to meditate on this, it means thinking about the matter from every angle, and the result is a deep appreciation for it.
QUESTIONS FROM READERS
What does Jonah's story teach us about how Jehovah feels when we disobey him, and what can we learn from our mistakes?
THE WATCHTOWER
Jonah's willingness to preach despite difficulties and what he teaches us about overcoming obstacles, encourages us to make good use of our time in the ministry, and helps us to maintain our zeal.
QUESTIONS FROM READERS
How can we deal with feelings of inadequacy?
QUESTIONS FROM READERS
Why did astute men recognize that the symbolic Babylon represented a world empire, and what lessons can we draw from this? In fact, they saw that its fall was near, and they foretold it. They also encouraged others to get ready.
THE WATCHTOWER

AMKENI!
Ĩkũlyo: We nũkwona andũ ta matonya kũtetheka makekĩa kĩthito nĩ kana maeke mwĩkalĩle mũthũku na mayĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo?
Ĩandĩko: Mũta 7:8a
Ũndũ ũtonya kwasya: Ilungu ii nieleetye myolooto yĩ Mbivilianĩ yonanĩtye ũndũ andũ matonya kũvĩndũa mĩkalĩle yoo na maitetheka.
AMKENI!

translation:
THIS IS GOD'S WILL:
We go to preach the good news, but we stumble. (Acts 3:6) But we should love people and show them kindness, so that they may feel our concern and we can help them. It is important to make a person feel comfortable and to help him understand the importance of the good news, and it is up to us to show him how to live. But let us leave, and let us love the homeowner or visit him to help him understand the good news that we have taught him.
WHAT WE SHOULD DO:
But let us share the good news from house to house, so that everyone may hear the good news and teach the homeowner and encourage him to leave. This good news has been made known throughout the world since ancient times. Or if this is not the case, let it be made known throughout another world so that we can help people understand the Bible and encourage them to leave.
To speak kindly to a kind person, explain whether he wants to speak further with you and teach him the good news that will help him leave. If they refuse, teach them well and see if there is something else we should do.
But if you love him or want to help him and agree with him, then remember to keep your promise.—Mt 5:37.

President Ruto was received in Kampala, Uganda, to attend a national prayer day for the country.

Together with you, Ruto was welcomed with enthusiasm by the President of Uganda, Yoweri Kaguta Museveni, to discuss this important national issue, starting with other issues affecting citizens.

text:
Ruto aneena kii ivindani ya muvinguo wa utandithya sokoni wa Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) umunthi vala waweta atandithya anene na anini medium, small and micro-enterprise (MSME) maile kukonwa aiweta ivinda ni iviku kwa atandithya anini ta athoosya ma mboka na atwai ma mota kutunyaa simuni syoo meteele athoowi kana akuuwa vandu va kutatithya vaati na mayasya mbesa mathauni ma kutatithya (betting).
E vamwe na munini wake Rigathi Gachagua muvinguoni wa soko usu umunthi, Ruto ingi niwaaweta kana ivindani ya mwaka umwe niukuweta ngava 6-10 sya silikali (parastatals) 6 sokoni wa NSE.
Mwenekivila wa NSE Kiprono Kittony nake niwaweta kana soko uu ukonetwe na shares niwiutethya Kenya kukwatiania na nthi ingi kukila kii ukwati aiweta kana soko uu ni wa katano munene ilembetani ya Africa.
Angi meivo ni vamwe na Minista mwoloote muvini wa utandithya Moses Kuria, CEO wa Safaricom Peter Ndegwa, Equity Group CEO James Mwangi na gavana wa Ilovi Johnson Sakaja.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Ruto has launched a plan to improve the operations of companies listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), aiming to enable large, medium, small and micro-enterprise (MSME) sectors to access funds, because accessing funds is difficult for small businesses and it hinders their ability to expand and create jobs, while also preventing people from engaging in harmful activities like betting.
Together with his deputy Rigathi Gachagua during the market opening ceremony, Ruto stated that they aim to list between 6-10 state corporations (parastatals) on the NSE within a year.
NSE Chairman Kiprono Kittony said the market will be improved through shares to attract investment in Kenya and other countries, making the market among the top five largest in Africa.
Among those present were Trade Cabinet Secretary Moses Kuria, Safaricom CEO Peter Ndegwa, Equity Group CEO James Mwangi and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja.

Silikali ya nthi mutui ya Uganda kwisila kwa muvia wa maundu ma nthi sya nza niyaaweta kana vena wiwano na unyanya kati wa nthi ii syeli.
Muvia usu wiiweta kana silikali isu nditumiaa nzia sya mitandao mikumukanilni na nthi ingi kana maunduni ma vata nthi isu na yingi nditumiaa mitandao ta ukusi, itina wa mwanae president wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni, Muhoozi Kainerugaba ula yingi niwe komanda wa ita sya muthangani kumya uneeni mutandaoni uukonya kau vala uwetete Uganda itonya kukua ivinda ya syumwa ili kwosa musyi munene wa Ilovi, ndeto ila syetie ivyuvi yai.
Utumanini wake yingi niuwetete kana president uthyumuiye wia Uhuru Kenyatta ethiwa anaavitie keka nunetisye kivila ivinda ya katatu.
Muhoozi niwanenevwa ndeve kuma komanda na kutwikithywa Geneneral wa ita sya muthangani.
Vau kiokoni kya umunthi, minista mwooloote maunduni ma nthi sya nza Dr Alfred Mutua, niukomanie na Dr Hassan Galiwango, ula niwe High Commissioner wa Uganda vaa Kenya.

translation:
The relationship between the government of Kenya and that of Uganda has deteriorated due to issues of national interests and may lead to tension between the two countries.
This situation could worsen if the government continues to use social media to attack other nations or their leaders, especially using the accounts of President of Uganda Yoweri Museveni's son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is often seen commanding operations on social media which can easily cause problems for Uganda and make it an enemy of regional stability, however this depends on how things unfold.
His main concern is that the current president seems to be supporting former President Uhuru Kenyatta who is accused of trying to destabilize the country for the third time.
Muhoozi is being praised for his command and promotion to General of the military forces.
During a press conference, Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr Alfred Mutua met with Dr Hassan Galiwango, who is the High Commissioner of Uganda to Kenya.

President William Ruto niwakwata mbau kuvithawaa kwa mauvoo meukonya undu mundu ukoovete kusyiiya kuvatwa mikovo ni mivea ingi ya kukovethanya (blacklist).
Kii kithiitwe kiivata aingi myanya ya mawia ovamwe na kukova, aiweta kii nikiikwovosya ta Akenya million 4-5 kuma merino wa 11.
Okavindani kau naw'o kampuni wa mikumukanilye wa Safaricom niwaola usyao wa ngovi ya fuliza kwa 50/100 kwa ngovi ya ilovia syii ithei wa 1,000.
Kii kyaikiithwa ni CEO wa kambuni usu Peter Ndegwa, aiweta kana ngovi ii itethetye Akenya mbee wa million 28 kuma yambiiwa, vala yingi utakaatilawa ilovia sya usyao matuku atatu wakova.

translation:
President William Ruto is currently working on a way to block people who spread false information and rumors, so that those who are caught spreading lies will be added to a large list of blocked individuals (blacklist).
This initiative aims to address the issue of misinformation and fake news, and it is estimated to affect between 4-5 million Kenyans within the next 11 days.
Negotiations are also underway with telecommunications company Safaricom to reduce the Fuliza loan interest rate from 50/100 to a lower rate of 1,000.
This was announced by the CEO of the company, Peter Ndegwa, and he estimates that this reduction will benefit around 28 million Kenyans, while a significant amount of money will be saved through reduced interest rates over three days.

translation:

He met with leaders in Naivasha and discussed matters with Kenyan Kwanza allies; Dr. Ruto easily stated his government's intention is to build on the foundation of leadership left by previous governments and lead Kenya forward.

Recently, I have observed a tendency to politicize issues, defending those who were previously accused of stealing public funds, especially given the recent statements made by Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua about certain individuals involved in corruption scandals.

translation:
Is love conditional at all?
Love is shown by kind words and thoughtful acts, and by forgiving others readily. (Colossians 3:14, 19) Loving people have become more gentle and tender, and they are quick to show mercy because Jehovah showed mercy to his Son.—Read Matthew 3:17.
Our heart reveals our true feelings and intentions. So, show love by being sincere in your dealings and by being considerate of others' needs. (James 1:19) Be willing to listen to others and try to understand their viewpoint.—Read Proverbs 11:11, 15.
It is loving to help someone who has made a mistake.
As a parent, show love by setting good examples. (Ephesians 6:1) Teach them to respect God's standards. Help them to be obedient to their parents, and teach them the importance of discipline. (Proverbs 3:3) Those who imitate God's forgiveness will find that it helps them to remain peaceful.—Read Isaiah 48:18, 19.

Because God shows us kindness through his forgiveness, help your children to show God love through their own forgiveness.—Read The Model Family Worship 6:5-7; Ephesians 4:32; 5:1.

Kwoou no twĩkũlye-ĩ, Andũ amwe ala mavoyaa mekaa ũu nũndũ no kũvoyawa-ĩ, kana kĩeleelo kyoo kya kũvoya kĩthĩawa no kũtetheesya kĩlĩko kĩusye?
Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana mboya nĩyĩanĩasya ũndũ wa vata mũno vyũ eka o kũtetheesya kĩlĩko kĩusye. O na nĩtũmanyĩasya kana mboya nĩsyĩthukĩĩaw'a nesa twavoya maũndũ ala maĩle na kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle. Ndeto isu nĩ sya w'o? Ekai twone ũndũ Mbivilia ĩĩkĩĩthĩtye ũndũ ũsu.

translation:
"I used to hate writing letters. But now I enjoy it, and I even look forward to them. School helps us learn." —Samuel, Kenya.
"We went to school late, but we still managed to finish."—Teresa, Philippines.
"But I still enjoy it. And I enjoy it when I receive a letter from my husband, and I am encouraged by a true Christian."—Magdalene, Ghana.
These experiences of Samuel, Teresa, and Magdalene show how others feel about learning to read, some because of the joy of reading itself, and others because of the practical benefits of being able to read. Some people learn at home, while others learn at school. Still others learn in various ways, but often it takes time and effort to learn to read, and sometimes God blesses the effort, or perhaps others learn quickly, so that millions of people have come to enjoy reading. And indeed, research shows that some people experience great difficulty learning to read.
So why do you read? And what makes you want to read—what motivates you? Are you motivated to read or forced to, and do you ask yourself: 'Is reading really worthwhile?' One writer expressed his opinion in an article by saying that reading 'is like a drug…because a person becomes addicted to it.' And many readers agree with this view, seeing reading as "another form of escape." So let us ask ourselves, do some people become overly engrossed in reading to the point where the benefit of reading becomes like a harmful addiction?
In connection with this, the Bible points out that reading can be misused, becoming like a harmful addiction. And it warns that such addiction may lead us to forget things we once knew and to neglect important matters. What is the answer then? Let us see what the Bible teaches on this issue.

Kipng'ok atiiwe ni thayu e Kiwanzani kya ndekw kya JKIA vaa Ilovi elekeele Mombasa matuku 14 mwei uu vala waendaa umbano wa maumanyisyo kwa magavana na anini moo, itina wa kwithiwa na thina wa kuveva, mbee wa ndeke ya kambuni wa KQ kuuluka.
Gachagua niwakulya enenthi kuima mitituni kwondu wa kuukitana na nzaa na aweta kana thina wa uvungulu wa muuwo kisioni kya Kerio Valley na isio ingi vaa Kenya niwiuthela ivindani ikuvi yukite, aiweta nzama nzau ya maminista nikuwetwa omituki.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The governor of Baringo county's aide, Charles Kipng'ok, is reported missing.
Kipng'ok was last seen on Thursday at the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) departure lounge heading to Mombasa on February 14th this year while going to a workshop for governors and their deputies, according to witnesses and security personnel, before boarding a Kenya Airways plane.
President William Ruto's brother, Rift Valley Regional Commissioner Mohamed Maalim, Governor Benjamin Cheboi, and Economic Planning Minister Simon Chelugui were among those who visited Solian High School students in Eldama Ravine, Baringo.
Gachagua is expected to address residents during his tour to meet communities and leaders and address issues of insecurity in the Kerio Valley region and other parts of Kenya, appealing for peace and unity, and promising to work with ministers to resolve problems.

The Director of Public Prosecutions' (DPP) case is ongoing, but Aisha Jumwa was released on bail due to a lack of evidence regarding the minister's involvement in the shooting and the matter should be mentioned in court for directions.
Jumwa, who is the Member of Parliament for Malindi, through her lawyer Alex Akula, the DPP's office informed Chief Magistrate Martha Mutuku that they have sufficient grounds to charge Aisha with the crime along with eight others, but the matter has been adjourned.
The case will be heard on November 17th this year, pending completion of investigations.

Momanyĩsyo ala me ĩvukunĩ Biblia Inatufundisha [Yĩinamba kumĩthw'a kwa kĩthyomo kya Kĩkamba] mosanĩte na ala me ĩvukunĩ Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya na onthe mavangĩtwe ũndũ ũmwe. Mavuku asu mamanyĩasya ũw'o kwa nzĩa ĩmwe nũndũ ũvoo ũla wĩ vo ũvangĩtwe ũndũ ũmwe. Ĩndĩ ĩvuku Biblia Inatufundisha yĩandĩkĩtwe nĩ kana yĩtetheesye ala mew'aa ne vinya kũelewa ĩvuku Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya. Vandũ va kwĩthĩwa na ũvoo wa kwongeleela, ĩvuku Biblia Inatufundisha yĩ na maelesyo ma mũthya maeleetye kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi ndeto na momanyĩsyo amwe me ĩvukunĩ yĩu. Ilungu sya ĩvuku yĩu iina makũlyo ma kwambĩĩa kana kasandũkũ kala ke na kyongo Ũndũ Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya. Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, mũthyanĩ wa ilungu ve kyongo kyonanĩtye maũndũ ala manene maeleetye ũw'o wa Mbivilia ũla ũneeneetwe kĩlungunĩ kĩu. O tondũ tũnenganae ĩvuku Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya o na ethĩwa tiyo yaĩle kũnenganwe mwei mũna, now'o tũkanenganae ĩvuku Kũtũmanyĩsya. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva tũtonya kũtũmĩa maũndũ ala me ĩvukunĩ yĩu tũyĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na mũndũ?
MAŨNDŨ ALA MANENE: Nzĩa ĩla tũtũmĩaa ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ ya kwamba kũsoma kalungu nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya, na ĩndĩ tũikũlya ĩkũlyo, ĩkeethĩawa yĩ nzeo. Nao nata ethĩwa mũmanyĩw'a ndesĩ nesa kĩthyomo kĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya nakyo kana ndesĩ kũsoma nesa? Ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, no ũvange kũtũmĩa ĩvuku Biblia Inatufundisha. Na ĩndĩ no mũtũmĩe maũndũ ala manene ĩla mũkwĩmanyĩsya, na ũithuthya mũmanyĩw'a ese kũsoma tũlungu ĩvindanĩ yake. Mavinda maingĩ, no mũtũmĩe ndatĩka ta 15 kwĩmanyĩsya ũw'o ũmwe wa Mbivilia. Nũndũ maũndũ ala manene mai na maelesyo maingĩ ala maeleetw'e tũlungunĩ, no nginya mwalimũ eyũmbany'e nesa vyũ, alilikene mavata ma mũmanyĩw'a. Na ethĩwa mwalimũ emanyĩsya atũmĩĩte ũvoo ũla wĩ tũlungunĩ, maũndũ manene no matũmĩwe tamo maũndũ ma kũsyokeleela.
MAELESYO MA MŨTHYA: Maũndũ ala me nthĩnĩ wa maelesyo ma mũthya mavangĩtwe kwosana na ilungu ila maneeneetwe. Mwalimũ no atw'e kũneenea kana o akaema kũneenea maelesyo ma mũthya ala me ĩvukunĩ Biblia Inatufundisha aendeee kwĩmanyĩsya na mũmanyĩw'a.

Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto nĩmaĩle kũatĩĩa Ũtianĩo Mũkũũ vamwe na Ũtianĩo Mweũ?
Mũtũmwa Vaulo, ũla waĩ Mũklĩsto, nĩwaveveewe aandĩka atĩĩ: "Maũndũ o na meva ala mambie kũandĩkwa, nĩmaandĩkiwe nũndũ wa kũtũmanyĩasya." (Alomi 15:4) Kwoou, Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania me na ũvoo wa vata mũno ũtonya kũtũtethya. Maandĩko asu nĩmatũnengete motao matwaĩle na makatũtavya maũndũ meekĩkie tene matonya kũtũtethya. Na ti ũu wĩ w'oka, ve maũndũ angĩ maingĩ.
Maũndũ meekĩkie tene matonya kũtũtethya. Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania nĩmawetete nesa ũndũ syĩndũ syoombiwe na ũndũ mũndũ walikile naĩnĩ. Takethĩwa maandĩko asu mai vo, tũyĩsa kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ta: Twaumie va? Nĩkĩ andũ makusaa? (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:7, 17) O na eka ũu, Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania nĩmawetete ũndũ Yeova Ngai weekanaa na andũ, na andũ asu mailyĩ o taku na maĩ na mathĩna o taku.
—Yakovo 5: 17.
Motao matwaĩle. Ĩvuku ya Nthimo na ya Mũtavan'ya me na motao matakesa kũvĩtwa nĩ ĩvinda. Mavuku asu elĩ me nthĩnĩ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩmatũtavasya ũndũ mĩsyĩ yitũ ĩtonya kwĩkala nesa (Nthimo 15:17), ũndũ tũtonya kũtanĩa wĩa ũla tũtethasya (Nthimo 10:4; Mũtavan'ya 4:6), na ũndũ amũika matonya kwĩka makekalaa me atanu (Mũtavan'ya 11:9–12:1).
O na ĩngĩ, kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ĩla Mĩao ya Mose no kũtũtethye. Mĩao ĩsu yĩ nthĩnĩ wa Torah (ala mavuku atano ma mbee Mbivilianĩ). O na kau Aklĩsto mayovetwe nĩ Mĩao ya Mose, mĩao ĩsu yĩ na maũndũ ma vata matonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkale nesa.

translation:
Indeed, God's Word can help us to understand what is written in the Bible—that is, to make sense of it. (2 Timothy 3:16)
Did Christ ever ask questions to test people or to find out what they thought?
The apostle Paul, a follower of Christ, wrote: "Some things I have written to you in a letter, but I am simplifying them so that you may come to know." (Romans 15:4) Yes, the writings in the Bible can be simplified so that we can understand them better. The scriptures can help us to learn important truths and to deal with difficult situations. And there is much more that they can do.
Important truths that can help us to deal with difficult situations. The writings in the Bible explain why bad things happen and how God feels about them. They also answer questions such as: 'Why do good people suffer?' and 'What will life be like after death?' (Proverbs 2:7, 17) Also, the writings in the Bible show us how Jehovah God cares for people, and how people can please him.
—James 5:17.
Important truths. The book of Proverbs and the book of Ecclesiastes contain many practical lessons. These books are filled with wisdom found in the Bible. For example, they teach us how to avoid being deceived (Proverbs 15:17), how to speak kindly (Proverbs 10:4; Ecclesiastes 4:6), and how to manage our finances wisely (Ecclesiastes 11:9–12:1).
Also, understanding the Law given to Moses helps us to reason. This law includes the first five books of the Bible. And although Christ was not under the Law of Moses, this law contains principles that can help us to live in a way that pleases God.

One passenger on a plane and his companion escaped miraculously with minor injuries after a plane crashed in Wilson Airport, but it emerged that the incident happened during a test flight of the plane belonging to Ilovi Kithekani's animal farm.

Hamdok resigned today after weeks of protests following the October 25 coup that overthrew his government six months ago.
