Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nitanĩaa kũtavya andũ onthe ũvoo mũseo ũla umĩte Mbivilianĩ nũndũ nimwendete Yeova na nĩsyendete andũ. Matavasya andũ onthe, o na ala maminĩte kwasya, "Nyie ndikwendeew'a." (Mathayo 22:37-39) Wendo kwa Ngai nĩw'o ũtũsukumaa tũatĩĩe mwĩao wa kumya "ũkũsĩ" ũla Mwana wake wanenganie. (Meko ma Atũmwa 10:42; 1 Yoana 5:3) Nĩ kana tumye ũkũsĩ ũndũ vaĩle, nĩtũneenaa na andũ ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ o tondũ athani ma Ngai ma tene meekaa. (Yelemia 25:4) Nũndũ nĩtwendete andũ onthe, nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũmatavye ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ o na ala maminĩte kwasya maikwendeew'a.—Mathayo 24:14.
Mavinda maingĩ nĩtwĩthĩaa andũ mekwendeew'a twasyoka nyũmbanĩ ila andũ maisye maikwendeew'a. Ekai twone itumi itatũ sya nĩkĩ vethĩawa ũu:
Andũ nĩmathamaa.
Andũ angĩ ma nyũmba ĩsu nĩmonanasya kwendeew'a.
Andũ nĩmaalyũkaa. Nũndũ wa maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, kana mathĩna ma mũndũ mwene, andũ amwe nĩmesaa kwona vata wa 'kwĩw'a Ndeto ya Ngai' (Mathayo 5:3) O na ala mataaendeew'a nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa maalyũlĩte ngoo o tondũ mũtũmwa Vaulo waalyũkile.—1 Timotheo 1:13.
Ĩndĩ ĩla tũũtavany'a, tũilasimĩthasya andũ methukĩĩsye. (1 Vetelo 3:15) Nĩtwĩthĩawa twĩsĩ kana kĩla mũndũ nĩwe waĩlĩte kwĩyĩkĩa ũtwi wa ũndũ ũkũmũthaitha Ngai.—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 30:19, 20.

translation:
God's love moved him to send his Son to die for us, so we might live through him, and also to preach to people. He feels sorry for people, and he wants them to obey him, saying, "You should love [God]." (Matthew 22:37-39) Love for God motivates us to show obedience to the command that his Son taught. (Acts 10:42; 1 John 5:3) So let us share this good news with others so that they may come to know Jehovah and experience his blessings. (Jeremiah 25:4) And as we preach to people, we will be strengthening our own faith and showing our appreciation for the Kingdom—and others will respond favorably.—Matthew 24:14.
Many people who respond favorably may become inactive, but some will remain faithful. Here are some reasons why:
People are imperfect.
Some in our families may not respond favorably.
People are prejudiced. But despite such difficulties, we continue to make progress, and sometimes individuals see the value of 'associating with God's people' (Matthew 5:3) and then respond favorably because the apostle Paul set an example.—1 Timothy 1:13.
So while we are still able, let us strengthen our brothers. (1 Peter 3:15) We can encourage each one to use his gift in a way that glorifies God.—Proverbs 30:19, 20.

text:
Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia, ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla mavinda angĩ ĩalyũlawa "ĩkanisa" yonanasya kĩkundi kya athaithi ĩndĩ ti vala mombanĩaa.
Kwa ngelekany'o: Ĩla Vaulo waandĩkĩie Aklĩsto ma Lomi valũa, akethisye Akwila na Vilisika na asya: 'Ngethesyai ĩkanisa ĩla yĩ nyũmba kwenyu.' (Alomi 16:5) Vaulo ndatũmanaa akakethew'e mwako. Ĩndĩ atũmanaa akethew'e andũ ala mombanĩaa nyũmbanĩ ĩsu.
Kwoou vandũ va kwĩta mwako ũla tũmbanĩaa ĩkanisa tũwĩtaa "Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ."
Nĩkĩ Mwako Ũsu Wĩtawa "Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova"?
Ĩsyĩtwa yĩu nĩyaĩle nũndũ wa itumi kauta:
Mwako ũsu nĩ nyũmba, kana vandũ va kũmbanĩa.
Tũmbanaa nĩ kana tũmũthaithe Yeova, Ngai ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ, na tũyumya ũkũsĩ ĩũlũ wake.
—Savuli 83:18; Isaia 43:12.
O na ĩngĩ tũmbanaa nĩ kana twĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũla wawetiwe nĩ Yesũ.
—Mathayo 6:9, 10; 24:14; Luka 4:43.
Wĩmũthokye mũno ũke Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ na vala wĩkalaa nĩ kana wĩyonee ũndũ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩkaa maũmbano.
No ũsome maũndũ angĩ ta asu ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 16:19; Akolosai 4:15; na ya Vilemona 2.

translation:
Concerning Priscilla, the Kikuyu church sends greetings to the congregation of believers meeting at her home.
For example: Paul wrote to Christians in Rome, greeting Aquila and Prisca and saying: "Greet the church that meets at their house." (Romans 16:5) Paul sent them as his coworkers. And we send our coworkers to fellow believers meeting in our homes.
Today people who meet in homes call their congregation "House of Worship."
Is Your Home Called "House of Worship of Jehovah's Witnesses"?
Your home can be used for this purpose:
Your home is a place, or people gather together.
We gather to worship Jehovah, the God who was revealed in the Bible, and to learn about His will.
—Psalm 83:18; Isaiah 43:12.
Also, we gather to preach the good news of God's Kingdom, which Jesus foretold.
—Matthew 6:9, 10; 24:14; Luke 4:43.
Consider how your home can become a House of Worship where those visiting feel welcome and can learn about Jehovah's organization.
And read more about this in 1 Corinthians 16:19; Colossians 4:15; and Philemon 2.

Kwasisya kamwana kaa ke visanĩ ũũ. Kailyĩ ta ke na wia na ta keona ta vate mũndũ ũkendete. Wĩona ata? We waaĩw'a ũu?— Mavinda angĩ ithyonthe nĩtwĩw'aa ũu. Mbivilia nĩwetete andũ amwe maĩ anyanyae ma Yeova ala maĩ na wia na moonaa ta vate mũndũ ũmendete. Ũmwe woo nĩ Eliya. Eka twĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wake.
Eliya ekalaa nthĩ ya Isilaeli tene mũno mbee wa Yesũ ate mũsyae. Mũsumbĩ wa nthĩ ĩsu eetawa Aavu na ndamũthaithaa Yeova, Ngai ũla wa w'o. Aavu na mũka wake Yeseveli mathaithaa ngai ya ũvũngũ yeetawa Mbaali. Ũndũ ũsu watumie Aisilaeli aingĩ mambĩĩa kũthaitha ngai ĩsu. Yeseveli aĩ mũthũku mũno na endaa kũaa athaithi onthe ma Yeova, o vamwe na Eliya! Nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ Eliya weekie?—
Eliya nĩwasembie akĩa! Aendie kwĩvitha ngunganĩ, kũndũ kũasa vyũ na kũmũ. Wĩona nĩkĩ weekie ũu?— Nũndũ aĩ na wia. Ĩndĩ ndaaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa na wia. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nĩweesĩ Yeova nũtonya kũmũtetheesya. Yeova nĩwamwonetye Eliya kana e vinya. Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwasũngĩie mboya ya Eliya kwa kũtũma mwaki kuma ĩtunĩ. Ũu wĩonany'a kana ĩvindanĩ yĩu Eliya wakĩĩte, Yeova aĩ atonya kũmũtetheesya.
Ĩla Eliya waĩ ngunganĩ, Yeova nĩwaneenie nake na amũkũlya: 'Wĩĩka ata vaa?' Nake Eliya amũsũngĩa: 'Katĩ wa athaithi maku no inyie nĩ weka ndiele. Vaiĩ mũndũ ũngĩ, na nĩngũkĩa kũawa.' Eliya oonaa athaithi ala angĩ onthe ma Yeova ta mooaiwe. Ĩndĩ Yeova amwĩa: 'Ũu ti w'o. Ve andũ angĩ 7,000 matiele ala manthaithaa. Ndũkethĩwe na wia. Ve wĩa ũngĩ ũtiele ngwenda ũtethye!' Wĩona Eliya ta watanie ĩla weewie ũu?—
Ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na maũndũ ala mamũkwatie Eliya?— Ndwaĩle kwĩw'a wia na kwona ta vate mũndũ ũkwendete. Wĩ na anyanya makwendete na mamwendete Yeova. O na ĩngĩ, Yeova e vinya mwingĩ, na ĩvinda yonthe akaũtetheeasya! Nĩwatana kũmanya kana ve andũ makwendete?—
SOMA MBIVILIANĨ YAKU
1 Asumbĩ 19:3-18
Savuli 145:18
1 Vetelo 5:9

translation:
A young boy was crying bitterly today. He was hurt and he saw someone mistreat another person. Did you see that? This is happening everywhere—violence is increasing. I feel sorry for those people who love Jehovah, because they are also getting hurt and seeing others being mistreated. One of them is Elijah. Let's learn about his story.
Elijah lived in Israel a long time ago during the reign of King Ahab. Ahab's father was named Ahaziah and he worshipped Baal, a false god. Ahab and his wife Jezebel also worshipped a foreign god named Baal. Because of this, the Israelites did many bad things by worshipping false gods. Jezebel was a very wicked woman and she hated anyone who served Jehovah, just like Elijah! What happened to Elijah?—
Elijah was very afraid! He went to hide in a cave, away from everyone and everything. Why was he so afraid?—Because there was trouble. It seemed like everyone was against him. Why? Because he knew that Jehovah could protect him. Jehovah showed Elijah how to find strength. Another story tells about Elijah sending a message to King Ahab using a raven to bring food. This shows that if Elijah trusted in Jehovah, Jehovah could protect him.
But when Elijah was hiding in the cave, Jehovah spoke to him and asked: "What are you doing here?" Elijah replied: "I have been very zealous for you, Lord, but the people have killed your prophets and torn down your altars. I am the only one left, and they are trying to kill me." Elijah had seen many terrible things done by the people of Jehovah. Then Jehovah said to him: "That is not true. There are still 7,000 men in Israel who have not bowed down to Baal. I have reserved them for myself. There are still people who serve me faithfully!" Did Elijah realize how true that was?—
Can you learn something from what happened to Elijah?—Be brave and don't be afraid to stand up for what is right. Love and honor Jehovah and know that Jehovah cares deeply, and will help all those who trust in him! Are you willing to learn more about those who honor Jehovah?—
READ THE BIBLE
1 Kings 19:3-18
Psalm 145:18
1 Peter 5:9

Serikali ya kaundi ya Masaku niyakwata liu wa utethyo muthemba wa mutu na mauta ma kuya kuma kwi ikundi ya County Pension Fund (CPF)
Aineena kavindani kala wathokya itambya yiu kunenganwe kwa liu munini wa Gavana kaundini ya Masaku Francis Mwangangi Kilonzo niwaweta kana liu usu uitha uninyaaikiwa enethi ala avinyiiye muno ninzaa kaundini isu vala ingi wathingiliila kana serikali ya kaundi ya Masaku ungu wa utongoi wa Gavana Wavinya Ndeti nimekuikiithya kana nimekia walanio mwailu wa kunyaaikisye enethi liu ala mekumbilitwe ni nzaa kaundini ya Masaku .
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Machakos County government has taken action regarding the welfare of employees and retirees within the County Pension Fund (CPF).
Residents have expressed concern about the large amount of money Governor Francis Mwangangi Kilonzo of Machakos County possesses, questioning whether this wealth was acquired legitimately, especially given his previous position in the county; they wonder if the Machakos County government under the leadership of Governor Wavinya Ndeti has investigated whether she heard reports of misappropriation of funds which were allegedly embezzled within Machakos County.

text:
Maundu ma ndambuka nimaendeeye kutambaika leluni wa Waiyaki musyini munene wa Ilovi enenthi mayuumania kiko kya uwaani kila kyatwaiiwa ni ovisa wa volisi kwa isyitwa Benson Imbatu utukuni wa kuamukia umunthi,ula wowaa muka wake na andu angi atano na itina ayiatha na kukw'a.
Maovisa ma volisi nimavika kisioni kya Kangemi musyini munene wa Ilovi na kwosa mii muonza wivo wa ovisaa usu na kutwaa andu angi eli kukwata uiiti sivitalini wa Kenyatta kukwata uiiti itina wa maumisye mai ma isasi.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The incidents that have been increasing are now happening along Waiyaki Way in the large forest of Ilovi where many people are experiencing things like theft, and everything stolen is reported to the police by a person named Benson Imbatu during the night of welcoming the month, who was with his wife and five other people when they were attacked and robbed.
The police officers are stationed at the Kangemi police station in the large forest of Ilovi and are investigating this matter thoroughly and arresting other people involved in capturing suspects at the Kenyatta National Hospital while pursuing another group of criminals who possess firearms.

text:
Maovisaa ma volisi kuma kiseseni kya volisi kya Kathonzeni kauntini ya Makueni nimatwaiisye ukunikili kukonya kiko kimwe ya mundume umwe ula utukuni wa kuamkia umunthi woowa mundumuka munyanyae kwa kutemangwa na kivanga kisioni kya Ivinga nzia nduani ya Mavindini vala itina wa kutwaiisya kiko ki nake weyumya thayu kwa nzia sya kwiyita na kakanda
Mii ya andu asu niyoosea ni maovisaa ma volisi ma kathonzweni na yatwawa nyumbani yakusuvia mii ya aku ya sivitali wa Makueni.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The police officers who were on patrol in Kathonzweni ward, Makueni county, have reported receiving information about a certain man who was found dead this morning near a riverbank due to being attacked by poisonous snakes along the Ivinga road towards Mavindini, preventing them from identifying the body properly because of its condition.
Many people are worried about the police in Kathonzweni and they have been taken home to mourn the family of the deceased from Sivitali sub-county of Makueni.

text:
Ula ei minista muviani wa utalii Najib Balala niwaamukaathiiya president William Ruto kwa undu utwaiisye iseso ya kunyuva maminista silikalini yake.
Nthini wa utumani mutandaoni wake wa twitter, Balala niwaatania uthukumi wake silikalini kwa ilungu ya myaka 24 na amuthokya muwandu Peninnah Malonza kwoseleela mwanya usu, aiweta niukumutuiika undu vatonyeka.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Former Tourism Cabinet Secretary Najib Balala has congratulated President William Ruto on his appointment of new cabinet secretaries.
On his official Twitter account, Balala thanked his team for their service over the past 24 years and wished Peninnah Malonza success in her new role, saying he trusts she will deliver as expected.

text:
President William Ruto aineena ivinguani ya mbunge ya13 matuku 29,09, 2022.
President uhuru kenyatta niwaawweta kana siklikali yake ndiivyaiya itheka muvango wa kwailya ilio mbunge (CDF).
Nthini wa kikalo kya mbee kya mbunge ya 13, Ruto niwaaweta kana onakau silikali nimbiinyiiye, ilovia isu niitethasya kukilya miikalile isioni.
Okavindani kau niwaavithua kana silikali yii nzikaiyoni sya kwona mwenenthi niwaitethya kwisila utandithya na kuvatha ilovia sya ukuuni kwisila kwongela muvothi wa mbesa sya ukuuni NSSF.
noo kikaloni kiu vala Ruto waumbua kana ii niyo mbunge ila ayumbe aingi mamisyoka, aikaathiiya wingi wa aka anyuve na kukaathiiya uthasyo wa enenthi itina wa kwithiwwa nowe muvnini wa president unoonekaa ta muvinzani unaatwikie president nake ula unai president aitwika ndongoi ya ulei na onthe kuisania imwe kwa muamba.

translation:
President William Ruto attended a meeting of parliament on September 29, 2022.
President Uhuru Kenyatta was questioned about his development projects during his tenure as a member of parliament (CDF).
During the parliamentary committee meeting, Ruto stated that another force was involved, which is causing problems for many people.
The speaker also said this force is interfering with the welfare of employees and hindering contributions to the NSSF fund.
And in that meeting, Ruto revealed that this is the parliamentarian, but many things have changed, affecting a lot of people and disrupting the peace of the country, so the president's current position seems like an opponent who wants to challenge the president, and he is being called a liar and accused of speaking falsely.

text:
Andu 15 nimatiwa ni thayu kuya nthi ya Congo kumana na uvithukie ula utwaisye kundu kwili kivathukanywo ni maovisa eli ma volisi ala meiamile okavinda kala mendeye kukwata nguthu ya andu ala mena miio ya kau na methitwe mayukita ita sya nthi isu,
vala andu angi 6 nimatiwa na maaaumisye manene na masembwa sivitali yu maendeye kukwata utii.
Maovisa asu ma volisi nimekiwa mbini kusungia maukulyo kukonywa kikwu kya andu asu ovala President wa nthi ya Congo Felix Tshisekedi waweta kana kuete muuo niwo wendi wake.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Fifteen people were killed in an attack in the Democratic Republic of Congo due to the violence that has been happening in several villages which was caused by armed groups who have been attacking homes and causing suffering to people, and some families have lost their loved ones and their heads are filled with sadness about this country.
However, six other people were seriously injured and hospitalized while trying to escape.
The armed groups have been placed under investigation to determine the reasons for the attacks on the population, and the President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Felix Tshisekedi, promised to take action against those responsible.

text:
Mumbunge wa kilio umbunge Kya Machakos Town Caleb Mule niwaweta kana nukuthakya mutalatala mbungeni nene kusukumiiya serikali nikenda kaundi ya Masaku itungwe walanioni wa kaundi ila syikumbilawa ni nzaa na inengawe utethyo wa liu kuma kwi serikali nene na mivia iteya kiiserikali .
Caleb aneena ndeto isu kavindani kala eivikite uthaithini ikanisani ya Katoleki ya St. Joseph Mutituni Ukamba wa Masaku vala wathingiliila kana enethi ma kaundi isu nimailite kunewa uthuthyo wa liu nundu mena nzaa mbingi muno.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Machakos Town Member of Parliament Caleb Mule has stated that he will continue raising issues in parliament to push the government to go to the Masaku county assembly so that the county's budget is approved but he regrets that there is delay and stagnation in the process of development in the government and its agencies.
Caleb said this yesterday while visiting St. Joseph Mutituni Catholic Church in Masaku County saying that counties should start being given development funds quickly because there are many needs in those areas.

text:
Kaunti ya Makueni nikwatie makunia 560 ma mbolea kuma kwi selikali ya kati kutethesya aimi ma kaunti ya Makueni kukwata lato wa mimea yoo ila meuvanda.
Aineena na aandiki ma mauvoo ovisaa munene ula ungamite makumbi ma selikali (cereals Board ) kauntini ya makueni Emily Mbatha niwaumwa wiitano kwi maovisaa ma uimi kauntini ya Makueni kutangasia aimi ala meyiandikithitye kwiyumilya kukwata mbolea isu.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
Makueni County has received 560 bags of fertilizer from the national government to help residents of Makueni County access affordable seeds, especially for maize and beans.
The county director of agriculture, Emily Mbatha, has called on farmers in Makueni County to register quickly so they can benefit from receiving the fertilizer.

text:

Muvothi wa ndawa na mbesa wongelwe kisioni kya Mlolongo

translation:
The MCA for Mlolongo Ward, Daniel Ndwiki, is heading to the Machakos County government to discuss with Governor Wavinya Ndeti about the issue of Mlolongo which has been delayed due to the large amount of infrastructure development happening in the area, especially road construction, to address the issues in the county and promote development, but residents of Mlolongo Ward have complained that they are not being considered when it comes to development in Machakos County.

text:
Matukũ 23, andũ vakuvĩ milioni 12, kana aingĩ kũte asu makoombana kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ vamwe naitũ. Makatetheka mũno nĩ ũvoo ũla ũkethĩwa ũineenea ĩũlũ wa mũthĩnzĩo wa wovosyo ũla Yeova waumisye, na moathimo ala tũkakwata ĩvinda yũkĩte! (Isa 11:6-9; 35:5, 6; 65:21-23; Yoa 3:16) Ĩndĩ ti o mumya wa ũvoo e weka ũkaumya ũkũsĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu wa vata. Ithyonthe tũkeethĩwa na mwanya wa kwĩka ũu kwa kũthokya aeni maitũ. (Alo 15:7) Vaa nĩvonanĩtw'e maũndũ amwe tũtonya kwĩka.
Vandũ va kwĩkala nthĩ na kweteela ũmbano wambĩĩe, thokya aeni na ala mavoie wĩ mũtanu
O na kau no wendeew'e mũno nĩ kũthokya ala wathokisye, ndũkolwe nĩ ala angĩ methĩwa mokie ũmbanonĩ ĩtina wa kũthokw'a nĩ atavany'a ala angĩ. Mathokye mwĩkale ĩmwe na mũitũmĩanĩa Mbivilia na ĩvuku ya mbathi
Ĩtina wa ũvoo, ĩthĩwa vakuvĩ nĩ kana ũmũsũngĩe makũlyo ala ũtonya kũkũlya. Ethĩwa vatiele ndatĩka nini mumaale nĩ kana kĩkundi kĩla kĩatĩĩe kĩlike, ĩka mũvango ũthi kwake mĩthenya mĩvũthũ ĩtina wa ũmbano ũsu. Ethĩwa ndwĩ na namba yake ya simũ kana ndwĩsĩ kwake, no ũmwĩe kana nũkwenda kwĩw'a woni wake ĩũlũ wa ũmbano ũsu, na ũimũkũlya aũnenge namba yake ya simũ kana akwathĩĩe kwake
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
On December 23, about 12 million people, or even more, eagerly look forward to celebrating Christmas together. How happy we are that this good news has spread widely because of Jehovah's loving provision, and may we always cherish this wonderful gift! (Isa 11:6-9; 35:5, 6; 65:21-23; John 3:16) Indeed, this good news is a light that shines brightly and brings hope to all people. Let us continue to be zealous in sharing it with others. (Acts 15:7) So let us discuss some ways we can do so.
Many people enjoy gatherings and festive meals, so reach out to them and show genuine interest.
And remember that being hospitable means welcoming those who have shown hospitality to us, as well as others who may need encouragement. May we all strive to imitate our generous God and share with others generously. Keep associating with Bible students and attending meetings regularly.
In connection with this good news, many people may be wondering where they can find something to eat. Encourage them to inquire at the local congregation to see if help is available, and arrange for someone to visit them and offer assistance. Also, get their phone number and address, and invite them to future meetings at the Kingdom Hall, and then check on them to see if they would like further assistance.

text:
Timotheo aĩ mwanake wendete kũtetheesya andũ. Nĩwaendie kũndũ kwingĩ akatetheesye andũ. Ũu watumie ethĩwa e na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno. Nũkwenda kũmanya ĩũlũ wake?—
Inyia wa Timotheo na ũsũe nĩmamũnyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Yeova
Timotheo eanĩie ndũanĩ yeetawa Lisitela. Ĩla waĩ kana, ũsũe wake Loisi na inyia wake Eunike, nĩmambĩĩie kũmũmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Ĩla weanie, nĩwendaa kũtetheesya andũ mamũmanye Yeova.
Timotheo e o mwanake, Vaulo nĩwamũkũlilye athi vamwe nake makatavany'e isionĩ ingĩ. Timotheo nĩweetĩkĩlile kũthi na Vaulo. Eetĩkĩlile kũthi nũndũ nĩwendaa kũtetheesya andũ.
Timotheo na Vaulo nĩmaendie ndũanĩ ya Thesalonika ĩla yaĩ vandũ veetawa Masetonia. Nĩ kana mavike kũu, maaĩlĩte kũthi na maaũ savalĩ ndaasa mũno, na ĩndĩ mayosa ĩsiwa. Ĩla mavikie kũu, nĩmatetheeisye andũ aingĩ mũno mamũmanye Yeova. Ĩndĩ andũ amwe nĩmeewie woo na menda kũmaũmĩsya. Ũu nĩwatumie Vaulo na Timotheo mauma ndũanĩ ĩsu, na mathi kũtavany'a kũndũ kũngĩ.
Ĩtina wa myei mĩnini, Vaulo nĩwamũkũlilye Timotheo asyoke ĩngĩ ndũanĩ ya Thesalonika nĩ kana akasisye ũndũ ana-a-asa maendee. Yaĩ no nginya Timotheo ethĩwe ate na wia nĩ kana asyoke ndũanĩ ĩsu yaĩ na andũ athũku! Ĩndĩ nĩwasyokie ndũanĩ ĩsu nũndũ nĩwathĩnĩkĩaa ana-a-asa ma kũu. Nĩwaeteie Vaulo ũvoo mũseo kuma kũu Thesalonika. Amwĩie kana ana-a-asa ma kũu maendee nesa vyũ!
Timotheo nĩwathũkũmie na Vaulo myaka mingĩ mũno. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Vaulo nĩwaandĩkie kana Timotheo nĩwe waaĩlĩte vyũ kũtũmwa kũtetheesya ana-a-asa ikundinĩ. Timotheo nĩwe waaĩlĩte nũndũ nĩwamwendete Yeova na akamenda andũ.
Nĩwendete andũ na nĩwendaa kũmatetheesya mamũmanye Yeova?— Ethĩwa wĩ mũndũ wendete andũ na nĩwendaa kũmatetheesya, ũu ũkatuma wĩthĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno o ta Timotheo!

translation:
Timothy was a young man who loved people. He went to many places to teach people. He used strength and much courage. Do you want to know his story?—
The childhood of Timothy and his mother impressed me with the story of Jehovah.
Timothy wrote letters called Letters. But really, his mother Lois and his father Eunice, encouraged him to learn about Jehovah. But he wanted to teach people who knew Jehovah.
Timothy was a young man, Paul took him with some of his companions on many journeys. Timothy liked to be with Paul. He liked to be with him because he wanted to teach people.
Timothy and Paul went to the city of Thessalonica and also to the land of Macedonia. It is true that they had difficulties being with people and sometimes they were very tired, and their bodies were weak. But despite this, they taught many people about Jehovah. Some people believed them and wanted to be comforted. This is what Paul and Timothy did when they traveled to different cities, and they didn't give up going to many places.
Because of great joy, Paul sent Timothy again to Thessalonica and told him to strengthen them in everything he was doing. I am happy that Timothy has returned to us now and with good news! Because he has returned to us because he cares about your well-being. I sent Paul there to comfort you in Thessalonica. Tell him how your faith is doing well!
Timothy spent many years with Paul. One time Paul wrote that Timothy was very willing to go and teach others the good news. Timothy was willing because he loved Jehovah and wanted to help people.
I love people and I want to teach them about Jehovah.— If you are a person who loves people and wants to teach them, then you will be strong and have much courage like Timothy!

Kavindani kaa selikali yeteletwe kutumbithya masyitwa ma amemba ma mbunge ya kaunti ya kitui ikazetini ya selikali nikana kuithwa kithitu kya kwambiiswa uthukumi, mwanya wa spika mbungeni ya kitui nounamelelwa mata ni ndongoi kauta
Kyalo Muli na ula ni umwe ukukitia mwanya usu niwaweta anyuvwa ta spika akakwatania amemba ma mbunge ya kaunti ya kitui na ngavana ni kana kwailya uthukumi mwenenthi isioni sya nduani.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Kavindani sub-county has been requested to investigate allegations against Kitui County Members of Parliament regarding government funds, with the government refusing to be called upon for information on economic matters; the position of Speaker in the Kitui Assembly remains uncertain due to political interference.
Kyalo Muli and others have stated that this position is being sought to allow the Speaker to collaborate with Kitui County Members of Parliament and the Governor, and there are concerns about the misuse of public resources.

text:
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova iyĩendaa kaũnĩ nũndũ wa itumi ii:
Kũmwĩw'a Ngai. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana athũkũmi ma Ngai "makatusya mbyũ syoo itw'ĩke mĩthya ya maembe ma ng'ombe" na kana "[matikemanyĩsya] kaũ ĩngĩ."—Isaia 2:4.
Kũmwĩw'a Yesũ. Yesũ eeie mũtũmwa Vetelo ũũ: "Tũngĩa ũvyũ waku vandũ vaw'o: nũndũ onthe ala makwataa ũvyũ makaanangwa na ũvyũ." (Mathayo 26:52) Kwoou Yesũ oonanisye kana aatĩĩi make maikakua mĩio ya kaũ.
Amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ nĩmaatĩĩaa mwĩao wake wa kwĩthĩwa 'mate ma nthĩ' kwa kũlea kwĩlikya siasanĩ. (Yoana 17:16) Mayĩkaa maandamano maileana na maũndũ ma kaũ o na mailikĩlĩĩlaa ala matw'a kũtw'ĩka asikalĩ ma ita.
Kwenda angĩ. Yesũ eeie amanyĩw'a make ũũ: "Mwĩthĩwe mũkyendana." (Yoana 13:34, 35) Amanyĩw'a asu maĩ mese kũtw'ĩka ana-a-asa ma nthĩ yonthe vate ũmwe ũkũkita na mwana-a-asa ũngĩ kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa.—1 Yoana 3:10-12.
Ngelekany'o ya Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa. Ĩvuku yĩmwe (Encyclopedia of Religion and War) yaĩtye ũũ: "Aatĩĩi ala ma tene vyũ ma Yesũ maleile vyũ kwĩlikya kaũnĩ na itanĩ," nũndũ nĩmeesĩ kwĩka ũu "kũyosanĩte na mwolooto wa wendo ũla Yesũ wamanyĩisye na ũndũ wameaĩe mende amaitha moo." Nake mũsomi ũmwe wa maũndũ ma ndĩni wa Germany wĩtawa Peter Meinhold aisye atĩĩ aiwetea amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ ma tene: "Mũndũ ndaĩ atonya kwĩthĩwa mũsikalĩ na ayĩthĩwa Mũklĩsto ĩvindanĩ yĩmwe."
ŨNDŨ NGŨSĨ ITETHASYA ANDŨ
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩ andũ ma vata ũtũinĩ na iivalaanasya mũuo wa nthĩ ila syĩkalaa. Nĩtũnengete ndaĩa silikalĩ kwosana na mĩao ĩno ya Mbivilia:
"Kĩla mũndũ nĩethĩwe e mwĩwi wa ala me na ũkũmũ."—Alomi 13:1.
"Mũnengei Kaisali syĩndũ sya Kaisali; na Ngai syĩndũ sya Ngai."—Mathayo 22:21.
Kwoou nĩtũatĩĩaa mĩao, tũkaĩva koti, na tũileanaa na mĩvango ya silikalĩ ya kũtetheesya andũ mekale me eanĩe.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The sword of Jehovah goes forth for this purpose:
To rebuke God. The prophets foretold that "the nations will forge their swords into plowshares" and that "[they will] no longer practice war."—Isaiah 2:4.
To rebuke Jesus. Jesus told his apostle Peter: "Put your sword back into its place; for all those who take up the sword will perish by the sword." (Matthew 26:52) Jesus showed by his example that he would not resort to violence.
Jesus' followers imitate his example of being willing to sacrifice themselves rather than use violence. (John 17:16) Let Christians maintain neutrality in political affairs and avoid getting involved in wars.
Show love. Jesus gave this command to his followers: "Love one another." (John 13:34, 35) Christian love moves us to show love to all people, including our brothers and sisters and others.—1 John 3:10-12.
The Example of Early Christians. One reference work (Encyclopedia of Religion and War) states: "The early Christians refused to bear arms, because they considered it incompatible with the teachings of Jesus," adding that this was due to "their understanding of the spirit of Jesus' teaching and their belief in the sanctity of human life." Also, a German religious scholar named Peter Meinhold stated that he appreciated Jesus' stand: "Anyone who wants to be a disciple must also be a pacifist."
WHAT THE BIBLE TEACHES PEOPLE
The Bible teaches people to be loyal and to respect secular authority, while remaining neutral. We can support this by considering these scriptures:
"Let every person be subject to the superior authorities."—Romans 13:1.
"Pay Caesar what Caesar deserves; and pay God what God deserves."—Matthew 22:21.
So let us obey the laws, remain respectful, and cooperate with lawful governmental regulations so that we may live peaceably.

translation:
What makes many people feel inadequate or ashamed before God?
For over 3,000 years ago, one Bible writer expressed this feeling: "I am wonderfully made." (Psalm 139:14) But does such appreciation really help a person when he feels bad about himself? Many people find it hard to believe God truly cares about their imperfections—Read Psalm 139:13-17; Ecclesiastes 3:4.
Our Creator delights in us as individuals and sees our value. (Psalm 36:9) Moreover, He wants to have a relationship with us and enjoys doing so.—Read Isaiah 45:18.
Why do people suffer?
Our lives are often filled with pain and sorrow. Very often this suffering causes people to question God's love. Our Creator desires that humans be happy and does not delight in causing them pain.—Read Proverbs 1:24; 2:7.
People misuse freedom with serious consequences. One reason why there is so much suffering is that people often abuse their free will, ignoring God and rejecting His guidance. Another reason is that imperfection can lead to mistakes and problems, which affect both individuals and others. Indeed, most people realize that human imperfection plays a role in why life is difficult—Read Proverbs 1:27; 2:15-17.

Aiee. Mbivilia yonanasya kana twaĩle kũmũvoya Ngai, syĩtwanĩ ya Yesũ. Yesũ eeie amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "
Inyw'ĩ ĩndĩ voyaai atĩĩ: Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ, syĩtwa yaku yĩtaĩwe." (Mathayo 6:9) O na vai ĩmwe waaĩa amanyĩw'a make mavoyae atheu, alaĩka, kana kĩndũ kĩngĩ eka Ngai.
Yesũ asyokie eea amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "
Nyie ninyie nzĩa, na ninyie w'o, na ninyie thayũ: vai mũndũ wũkaa kwa Asa atesĩle kwakwa." (Yoana 14:6) No Yesũ weka ũtonya kũtw'ĩw'anĩthya na Ngai.—Aevelania 7:25.
Nao nata ngavoya Ngai na ndivoya atheu?
Nthĩnĩ wa ĩla mĩao ĩkũmi, Ngai aĩtye: "
Nyie Yeova Ngai waku nĩ Ngai wĩ kĩwĩu." (Kuma 20:5) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Ngai wĩthĩawa na "kĩwĩu"? Maelesyo ma kwongeleela nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia ya New American Bible maĩtye kana Yeova nĩ Ngai "
wendaa athaithwe e weka." Ngai endaa ũthaithi w'onthe, o na vamwe na mboya, syelekelw'e kwake e weka.—Isaia 48:11.
Nĩtũmũthatasya Ngai ĩla twavoya kĩndũ kĩngĩ, wĩthĩwe nĩ atheu kana alaĩka. Ĩla mũtũmwa Yoana wendaa kũthaitha mũlaĩka, mũlaĩka ũsu nĩwaleile na amwĩa: "
Ndũkeke ũu: nyie nĩ ngombo vamwe naku na vamwe na ana-a-ĩthe maku ala makwataa ũkũsĩ wa Yesũ; thaitha Ngai."—Ũvuan'yo 19:10.

translation:
The Lord's Prayer
Amen. The prayer is pleasing when we learn to praise God, through Jesus. Jesus himself said: "
Pray then like this: 'Our Father who is in heaven, may your name be sanctified.' " (Matthew 6:9) And so you should know his name always, everywhere, or something else to God.
Jesus also himself said: "
I am the way, and the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through me." (John 14:6) So Jesus makes it possible for us to approach God.—Hebrews 7:25.
And how can I praise God and others?
In the tenth commandment, God says: "
You shall have no other gods before me." (Exodus 20:5) Is it because God wants to be called "unique"? Explanations from the New American Bible say that Jehovah is God "
who allows no one else to be equal to him." God allows no equality with anyone, and everyone praises only him.—Isaiah 48:11.
We honor God when we praise someone else, whether it is people or angels. But the apostle John tried to worship an angel, but the angel stopped him and said: "
Take care! Do not do that. I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers who share in the tribulation of Jesus; worship God!"—Revelation 19:10.

translation:
The team of the Azimio La Umoja-One Kenya alliance led by presidential candidate Raila Odinga is preparing to file a petition in court challenging the decision of the Supreme Court dismissing their petition contesting the election results.
Odinga, who campaigned with his team in Meru County yesterday, said they will file the petition today or tomorrow, giving the court five days to hear their case.
He was accompanied by his running mate Martha Karua and former Agriculture Cabinet Secretary Peter Munya.
Odinga intends to go to court to challenge the victory of his rival William Ruto, whose vote count was 50.49 percent but was not declared.
Odinga received 48.85 percent of the votes.

translation:
The head of traffic has today issued directives regarding road safety to all Kenyans, urging caution and responsibility while driving and adhering to traffic laws during this festive season.
Interior Cabinet Secretary Prof Kithure Kindiki and Transport Principal Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen among others have directed increased police patrols and the enforcement of traffic regulations by the National Transport Safety Authority (NTSA).
The ministers have warned against recklessness and emphasized the importance of compliance with the law, including avoiding drunk driving and drug use while operating vehicles.

Uhuru, who is currently serving his second term as President of Kenya, has been recognized for his leadership and commitment to peace, and he will continue to work towards resolving the crisis.

translation:

text:
Munini wa ula unokitiaa kivila kya upresident na tikiti wa Azimio Raila Odinga muwandu Martha Karua easya kana niukuvikya maunyungunyisyo make kukonya usindi wa president munyuve William Ruto kotini wa nthi sya ilembeta ya Avilika ya umiloni wa sua.
Karua easya kana niukuneenanya na koti usu ula wii Arusha nthi ya Tanzania kumanya kana utw'i ula unaumiwe niwaw'o.
Oo kavindani kau Karua niwaweta kana noweteele utw'i mwithianiu kuma kotini wina ukumu vaa Kenya ula ukaumwa itina wa matuku 21 kuma yila koti usu unaanenganie utw'i wa Ruto kwithiwa president wa katano wa Kenya.
Koti wina ukumu vyiu vaa Kenya kwisila kwa musili munene muwandu Martha Koome kwii matuku atano mwei wa kenda niwavitukithisye Dr. William Ruto kwithiwa president wa katano wa Kenya.

translation:
The head of state has filed a petition challenging President-elect William Ruto's victory with his running mate Martha Karua alleging that he is protecting his interests against the new president William Ruto in the Supreme Court of the Republic of South Africa.
Karua alleges that she will be attending court in Arusha, Tanzania to know whether the election was fair to them.
According to Karua's lawyers, they expect the court to issue its ruling within 21 days from today, which will separate Ruto's election as the fifth president of Kenya.
The Kenyan Supreme Court led by Chief Justice Martha Koome has five days next week to swear in Dr. William Ruto as the fifth president of Kenya.

text:
yama kya Jubilee kila kitongoewe ni musumbi ithyumuiye wia Uhuru Kenyatta nikyaete muvuavuano mbungeni itina wakyo kwendekethya myanya imwe ya mbungeni kivathiwe utee na makwatianio ma vau mbeeni ma ngatano ya Azimio la Umoja.
Azimio inendekethetye muyumbe Sabina Chege na munini wake muyumbe wa Suna ya umiloni wa sua Junet Mohammed ta anini ma akuni ma mutalisa, masyitwa ala manengiwe spika Moses Wetangula ni muandiki munene Jeremy Kioni ni angi.
Ayumbe ala mendekethetwe ni Jubilee ni vamwe na muyumbe wa Mbalambala Shurie Abdi Omar ta ndongoi, Samuel Arama (Nakuru Town west)ta mukuni wa mutalisa and Sarah Korere (Laikipia North) ta munini wake, vala muyumbe wa Eldas Adan Kenyan olotetwe ta muandiki.
President Ruto aatangasie muyumbe wa Kikuyu Kimani Ichung'wa ta ndongoi ya aingi mbungeni nake munini wake e muyumbe wa Kilifi North Owen Baya, vala Raila umwoolottete muyumbe wa Ugunja Opiyo Wandayi ta ndongoi ya aingi ungu wa Azimio na munini wake muyumbe wa Kathiani MP Robert Mbui.
Kenya Kwanza imwoolootete muyumbe wa South Mugirango MP Silvanus Osoro ta ndongoi ya aingi mbungeni munini wake e muwakiolishi wa aka kauntini ya Marsabit Naomi Waqo vala Azimio inyuvite muyumbe wa Suna East MP Junet Mohamed ta ta mukuni wa mutalis aitetheeswa ni Sabina Chege.
Kitumini kii spika wa mbunge niwakulya kalani wa mbunge aandike valua kwa ndongoi ya aingi na ya anini mbungeni na yinewa akuni eli ma mutalisa nikana masuanie na kunengane masyitwa kenda ma ayumbe ala makethiw=awa nzamani ya kuthiiniuia maundu mbungeni (HBC)
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Jubilee party's every addition is a puzzle that has troubled President Uhuru Kenyatta, causing chaos among MPs due to their efforts to occupy one of the parliamentary seats reserved for them through consensus within the Azimio la Umoja coalition.
Azimio is proposing Sabina Chege and her brother, Suna East MP Junet Mohammed, for leadership positions, while others claim Speaker Moses Wetangula and prominent writer Jeremy Kioni are also candidates.
The members nominated by Jubilee include Mbalambala MP Shurie Abdi Omar, Samuel Arama (Nakuru Town West), and Sarah Korere (Laikipia North), along with Eldas MP Adan Kenyan, who is being considered as a writer.
President Ruto has appointed Kikuyu MP Kimani Ichung'wa as his majority leader in parliament, alongside Kilifi North MP Owen Baya, while Raila has nominated Ugunja MP Opiyo Wandayi as his majority leader in the Azimio coalition, supported by Kathiani MP Robert Mbui.
Kenya Kwanza has nominated South Mugirango MP Silvanus Osoro as its majority whip in parliament, alongside Marsabit County representative Naomi Waqo, while Azimio is backing Suna East MP Junet Mohamed, whose position is being contested by Sabina Chege.
The speaker of parliament should ensure that the clerk of parliament writes down the names of those nominated for both majority and minority positions in parliament, and that they are presented to the committee on appointments so that the nominations of the proposed members can be finalized to facilitate business in parliament (HBC).

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Kĩla mũndũ e ĩsyĩtwa. Tyo ũndũ waĩle o nake Ngai akethĩwa na ĩsyĩtwa? Kwĩthĩwa na masyĩtwa na kũmatũmĩa nĩ maũndũ ma vata nĩ kana andũ methĩwe anyanya. Vaĩle kwĩthĩwa vailyĩ oou nĩ kana twĩthĩwe anyanya na Ngai.
Ngai aĩtye ũũ: "
Ninyie Yeova, nĩyo syĩtwa yakwa." (Isaia 42:8) O na kau e masyĩtwa maingĩ ma ũnene, ta "
Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe," "
Mwĩaĩi Ngai," na "
Mũmbi," nũthoketye ala onthe mamũthaithaa matũmĩe syĩtwa yake mwene, kwonany'a kana nĩwonaa me ma vata.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 17:1; Meko ma Atũmwa 4:24; 1 Vetelo 4:19.
Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia mbingĩ, ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyonekaa ĩandĩkonĩ ya Kuma 6:3. Mũsoa ũsu waĩtye: "
Nakwa namũmĩlĩle Avalaamu, na Isaka, na Yakovo, nĩ Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe; ĩndĩ na syĩtwa yakwa Yeova ndyaamanyĩka kwoo."
Yeova nĩyo ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩla yĩthĩĩtwe yĩitũmĩka kwa myaka mingĩ kwa kĩthyomo kya Kikamba. O na kau asomi aingĩ mendete kũtũmĩa ĩsyĩtwa "Yahweh," Yeova nĩyo ĩsyĩtwa yĩla yĩsĩkĩe mũno. Kĩlungu kya mbee kya Mbivilia kĩyaandĩkwa na Kĩsũngũ ĩndĩ kyaandĩkiwe na kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania, kĩla kĩsomawa kuma kw'oko kwa aũme. Kĩthyomonĩ kĩu, ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yaĩ na nthoo inya, יהוה. Nthoo isu inya sya Kĩevelania, ila iungamĩe YHWH, syĩtawa Tetragrammaton.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Name Jehovah Is Important
Every person has a name. But why is God's name important and should be known? Knowing and using names is something people value, and often they get upset when their name is misused. His name should be honored, just as we honor God.
God said: "
I am Jehovah, that is my name." (Isaiah 42:8) And although he has many magnificent titles, such as "
God Almighty," "
Creator God," and "
Maker," all creation acknowledges his unique personal name, showing that it is powerful.—Psalm 17:1; Acts 4:24; 1 Peter 4:19.
In many Bible accounts, God's name is closely linked with Exodus 6:3. That verse reads: "
And I have made myself known to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as God Almighty; but as to my name Jehovah, I did not make myself known to them."
Jehovah is the divine name that has been used for centuries in the Kikamba language. And though some scholars prefer to use the name "Yahweh," Jehovah is the name that sounds most familiar. The original manuscripts of the Bible were written in Hebrew, and the name was originally written in Hebrew script, which looks like this: יהוה. These four Hebrew letters represent YHWH, the Tetragrammaton.

Azimio also has its leader Kalonzo Musyoka as a member and Kenneth Marende of the senate, present with Farah Maalim, MP for Dadaab and Otiende Amolo of Rarieda as clerks.

Ĩtina wa myaka yĩana ũndũ mũna, Bebe nĩwaeleisye ũndũ ũsu ĩvukunĩ, na maelesyo make moonany'a kana aĩ o na kyeva.

A certain man named Bebe was the one who received a vision at night and saw in his dreams that he would meet with the end of life.

President William Ruto niwakulya muvia wa useeseyi utumie vinya na ukumu ula unengetwe kuikiithya muuwo niwatuumanw'a kisioni kya Turkana.
Aineenea itina wa ivithukia ila itwaiiwe kuya Turkana ya umiloni wa sua vala andu 11 mevo maovisa nyanya ma volisi, Dr Ruto niwaweta kana silikali yake ndinenga mwanya nzangili indi enenthi nimeekwithiwa na useeseyi wa kwiana.
Okavindani kau niwakulya enenthi kukumbatia nzia ya kwiiyaa ilovia, aiweta kana silikali niikwithiwa imaongelela ukwati.
Niwaweta kana vayii kindu kiisyiiya nzikaiyo syake sya enenthi kuiyaa mbesa sya ukuuni (NSSF).
President aneena ndetoo Ii itina wa uthaithi wa kutunga mivea ula watwaiiwa vomani yake vala wakulya ndongoi sya kii ndini na enenthi kuvoyea muuw'o wa Kenya na ukwati, itina wa ndambuka ya kii wia kuya Ungelesa.
Muwandu wa mbee Racheal Ruto, munini wa president Rigathi Gachagua na muka kati wa ndongoi ingi na athaithi nimeivikite uthaithini usu ula wiitongoewe ni Bishop Mark Kariuki.

translation:
President William Ruto is eating breakfast while using a spoon and fork which have been decorated to welcome him as he arrives at the Turkana airport.
He extended greetings to the people but requested that they move from the Turkana airstrip so that the eleven injured people who were involved in an accident involving police vehicles could be treated, Dr Ruto said his government will ensure security is improved in areas affected by cattle rustling.
Speaking today while addressing the nation via radio, he stated that security has been strengthened to address the issue.
He added that contributors should understand their rights regarding contributions to the National Social Security Fund (NSSF).
The President also announced plans to review laws relating to livestock theft which affect herders and cattle rustlers, laws concerning ownership of property in Kenya and security, laws on cross-border trade with England.
First Lady Rachel Ruto, Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and several other leaders and guests attended the event which was presided over by Bishop Mark Kariuki.

text:
Nĩvatonyeka kũkethĩwa silikalĩ ĩmwe nthĩ yonthe?
Kwasũanĩa ũndũ silikalĩ ĩmwe ĩsumbĩkĩte nthĩ yonthe ĩtonya kũuna andũ. Ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ nĩmathĩnaa kumana na ũkya, kĩvathũkany'o na athwii. Ĩndĩ silikalĩ ya nthĩ yonthe ĩkũelewa mavata ma andũ mayo no ĩtonye kũĩkĩĩthya kana nĩyeanĩsya mavata moo. We wĩona silikalĩ ĩseũvĩte ũu ta ĩetwe nĩ andũ?—Soma Yelemia 10:23.
Silikalĩ ya mũndũ nĩyĩemetwe nĩ kwĩanĩsya mavata me kĩvathũkany'o ma andũ, na mũno mũno ma ala ngya. O na silikalĩ imwe nithĩnasya andũ. (Mũtavan'ya 4:1; 8:9) Ĩndĩ, Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe nĩwathanĩte silikalĩ ĩla ĩkavetanga silikalĩ isu syonthe. Mũsumbĩ wa silikalĩ ya Ngai akasũvĩa andũ nesa vyũ.—Soma Isaia 11:4; Ndanieli 2:44.
Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkeanĩsya maũndũ meva?
Yeova Ngai nũnyuvĩte Mũsumbĩ ũla waĩle kũsumbĩka nthĩ yonthe, nake nĩ Mwana wake Yesũ. (Luka 1:31-33) Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ, nĩwendeeaw'a nĩkũtetheesya andũ. Nũndũ Yesũ nĩ Mũsumbĩ, akaete ngwatanĩo kwa mbaĩ syonthe, na aivetangĩa andũ mathĩna onthe.—Soma Savuli 72:8, 12-14.
Kĩla mũndũ akamwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta Mũsumbĩ? Aiee. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, Yeova nũendeee kũmomĩĩsya. (2 Vetelo 3:9) Nũendeee kũnenga andũ mwanya wa kwĩtĩkĩla kana Yesũ nĩwe Mũsumbĩ. O mĩtũkĩ Yesũ akilyĩ anavetanga andũ athũku, aete mũuo, na aiveta mĩisyo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.—Soma Mika 4:3, 4.

translation:
Am I to be honored with just one scripture throughout my life?
To demonstrate a point, one scripture thoroughly understood can influence people. Many people often struggle with anxiety, becoming frustrated and discouraged. But one scripture throughout life can understand the needs of its people and help to direct or satisfy those needs. So we see one scripture being useful to us and to people—Read Jeremiah 10:23.
A person's scripture is determined by satisfying their own needs and frustrations, and little by little other things come along. And one scripture deceives people. (Philippians 4:1; 8:9) Therefore, Almighty God will provide this scripture which will surpass all other scriptures. The strength of God's scripture will save people greatly.—Read Isaiah 11:4; Daniel 2:44.
What does God's strength accomplish?
Jehovah God has appointed this strength to govern throughout life, and that is his Son Jesus. (Luke 1:31-33) Since Jesus came to earth, he willingly offered himself to benefit people. Because Jesus is the Strength, he reigns justly over all the earth, and delivers people from all distress.—Read Psalm 72:8, 12-14.
Will everyone accept Jesus as the Strength? No. But even so, Jehovah continues to show patience. (2 Peter 3:9) He continues to allow people time to decide whether Jesus is the Strength. However, those who reject Jesus will experience trouble, become foolish, and suffer great destruction throughout life.—Read Micah 4:3, 4.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Aiweta ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala waandĩkie ĩũlũ wa thayũ wa Yesũ, mũtũmwa Yoana aisye: "
Na ũla wonie nĩwe ngũsĩ, na ũkũsĩ wake nĩ wa w'o: nake nĩwĩsĩ kana eneena w'o, nĩ kana nenyu mwĩtĩkĩle."—Yoana 19:35.
Kĩtumi kĩmwe kya kũĩkĩĩa maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo, Maliko, Luka, na Yoana ĩũlũ wa Yesũ nĩ kana maũndũ asu maandĩkiwe ĩla andũ aingĩ ala meyonee maũndũ asu maĩ o thayũ. Andũ amwe maasyaa ĩvuku ya Mathayo yaandĩkiwe o myaka nyanya ĩtina wa Yesũ kũkw'a, na ũsu nĩ ta mwaka wa 41. Asomi angĩ maasyaa yaandĩkiwe ĩtinanga wa vau, ĩndĩ onthe nĩmetĩkĩlanaa kana mavuku onthe ma Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto maandĩkiwe mwaka wa 100 ũte mũviku.
Andũ ala moonie Yesũ e thayũ, moona ayũawa na aithayũũkw'a nĩmatonya kũweta ethĩwa maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe ĩũlũ wake nĩ ma w'o. Vakethĩwa ve ũndũ o na ũmwe wa ũvũngũ ũandĩkĩtwe, nĩmatonya kũumĩlya. Mũsomi ũmwe wĩtawa Professor F. F. Bruce aĩtye ũũ: "
Ũndũ ũmwe woonekaa mũno ĩla atũmwa matavanasya nĩ kana mawetaa mate na nzika maũndũ ala ethukĩĩsya moo meesĩ; mayeekaa o kwasya, 'Ithyĩ twĩ ngũsĩ sya maũndũ asu,' ĩndĩ ĩngĩ nĩmaasyaa, 'o ũndũ inyw'ĩ ene mwĩsĩ' (Meko ma Atũmwa 2:22)."

translation:
The Testimony of an Eyewitness
John, the apostle, wrote about what he saw, and his testimony is reliable. He truthfully testifies so that you may believe. John 19:35 says: "
And the soldier who had seen it testified, and his testimony is true; and he knew that they were lying, so that you also may believe." —John 19:35.
One reason we can be confident in what the Gospels say is that Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John all wrote accounts of Jesus' life and ministry. These accounts, along with other writings, provide a wealth of information about Jesus. Some scholars estimate that the Gospel of Matthew was written about 40 years after Jesus' death, while others place it later, around the year 41. Other Gospels were written decades later, some possibly being compiled from earlier records dating back to the first century C.E., perhaps as early as 100 C.E.
Those who did not know Jesus personally rely on the writings of those who did to learn about him. They trust that the writers recorded events accurately. The fact that there is a consistent account in the four Gospels helps them to have confidence. One scholar, Professor F. F. Bruce, said: "
There is one feature which strikes us as remarkable in the eyewitness reports—it is their sobriety and realism; they record both the successes and failures of Jesus with unflinching honesty, sometimes to the detriment of their own case, and often contain embarrassing details (Acts 2:22)."

text:
Yo no tũĩkĩĩe kana mawatho onthe ma Ngai makeanĩa? Yesũ aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana makeanĩa, na momanyĩsyo make nĩmatetheeisye ala mamwĩthukĩĩsye methĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo. Kwasisya ngelekany'o ĩmwe wanenganie Ũtavany'anĩ wa Kĩĩmanĩ, o tondũ vonanĩtw'e ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo 5:18: "Nũndũ nĩ w'o nĩngũmwĩa, Mũvaka yĩla ĩtu na nthĩ ikavĩta, kũikavĩta kaũandĩko kamwe kana kaũkenyũsyo kamwe mĩaonĩ, mũvaka onthe meanĩw'e."
Nthoo ĩla nini vyũ ya Kĩevelania yĩtawa (yod), na nĩyo ya mbee nthĩnĩ wa Tetragrammaton. Tetragrammaton nĩ nthoo sya ĩsyĩtwa ĩtheu ya Ngai, Yeova. * O vamwe na ndeto na nthoo ila itũmĩĩtwe kũandĩka Mĩao ya Ngai, aandĩki na Avalisi moonaa kaũandĩko kana "kaũkenyũsyo kamwe" ke ka vata mũno.
Yesũ oonanasya kana waĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ĩtu na nthĩ kũvĩta kwĩ o na kaũndũ kala kanini Mĩaonĩ kũlea kwĩanĩa. Ĩndĩ Maandĩko matũĩkĩĩthasya kana matu na nthĩ ĩno twĩkalaa ikekala tene na tene. (Savuli 78:69) Kwoou ndeto isu syoonanasya kana o na kaũndũ kala kanini vyũ ke Mĩaonĩ kakeanĩa.
We Yeova Ngai nĩwonaa tũmaũndũ tũla tũnini mĩaonĩ yake twĩ twa vata? Ĩĩ. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Aisilaeli ma tene manengetwe mwĩao wa kana mayaĩle kũtũla ĩvĩndĩ o na yĩmwe ya katena ka ĩlondu ka Vasaka. (Kuma 12:46) Ũndũ ũsu no woneke wĩ o kaũndũ kanini. Aisilaeli nĩmeesĩ nĩkĩ mataaĩle kũtũla ĩvĩndĩ o na yĩmwe ya katena kau? Noĩthwa mateesĩ. Ĩndĩ Yeova Ngai nĩweesĩ kana kaũndũ kau kaĩ wathani ũla woonanasya kana vai ĩvĩndĩ o na yĩmwe ya Masia yĩkatũlwa ĩla ũkoaĩwa mũtĩnĩ wa mathĩna.—Savuli 34:20; Yoana 19:31-33, 36.
Ndeto ila Yesũ waneenie syĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? No twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana mawatho onthe ma Yeova makeanĩa, nginya o na tũmaũndũ tũla tũnini vyũ. Vai nzika kana nthoo ĩla nini vyũ ya Kĩevelania nĩtonya kũlũlũmĩĩlya mũĩkĩĩo waku!
^ kal. 3 Nthoo ĩla nini vyũ ya Kĩkiliki yĩtawa iota na veonekana yĩthĩawa ĩilyĩ ũndũ ũmwe na nthoo ya Kĩevelania ĩla yĩtawa (yod). Na nũndũ Kĩevelania nĩkyo kyatũmĩiwe kũandĩka Mĩao ya Mose, noĩthwa Yesũ aneeneaa nthoo ya Kĩevelania.

translation:
Don't we build houses so that God may be glorified? Jesus also had a house for glorification, and his teachings have made people wise and have strengthened them with a house. Consider, therefore, one who wants to fulfill the Law of Christ, or because you have read Matthew 5:18: "For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not the smallest letter or the smallest stroke will vanish from the Law until everything is accomplished."
What then is the value of the Hebrew letters (yod), and they are part of the Tetragrammaton. The Tetragrammaton is the name most often used for God, Jehovah. * Some, however, with respect to this name, use it to write God's names, writing in Greek either a "letter" or a "stroke" of it to show reverence.
Jesus explained that something can become invalid by being added to or removed from it, just like an old garment becomes useless when patched with new cloth. The Scriptures show that things remain the same forever and ever. (Psalm 78:69) So let us examine whether something can become invalid by being added to or removed from the value of the names of God.
But does Jehovah God care about small details in his names when we use them? Yes. Consider this: Israelites of old were zealous to carry the Ark of the Covenant, even though some carried it improperly. (Numbers 12:46) This matter was important. Were the Israelites wrong to be zealous to carry the Ark improperly? Not at all. For Jehovah God cares about how he is honored, even regarding small details concerning the Messiah which were fulfilled in the way he was impaled on a tree.—Psalm 34:20; John 19:31-33, 36.
So what did Jesus want to illustrate to them? We are reminded of our love for God and his glory, and also of small details. See how the value of the Hebrew letters is able to illuminate the meaning!
^ par. 3 What is the value of the Coptic letters iota and ve, and they appear to be similar to the Hebrew letters that are valued (yod). And since Hebrew was used to write Moses' Laws, Jesus also used the Hebrew letters.

Silikali ya county ya kitui niyaweta niyinzite masilanga na ndovoi isioni kivathukanio sya county isu ta nzia imwe ya kukitana ma mathina ma kiwu kwa enenthi.
Ndeto ii syaumbulwa ni munini wa gavana countini isu Dr. Wathe Nzau kavindani kala eivikiye kyathini kya kutania muthenya wa kiwu nthi nima , kyathi kila kitwaiiwe kiliouniumbunge kya kitui rural.
Kilungu kya 85% kya enenthi ma kaunti ya kitui,matumiaa kiiw'u kitekitheu na kitonya kumekia muisyoni wa kukwatwa ni mauwau ala maetawe ni kiko.

Nĩkĩ mũka wa Loto wasiisye ĩtina ĩla wakĩĩte kuma ndũanĩ ya Sotomo? Mbivilia ndĩwetete kĩtumi. (Mwa 19:17, 26) Maũndũ ala Yesũ waneeneaa, meonany'a kana nĩvatonyeka mũka wa Loto akethĩwa endeeaw'a nĩ syĩndũ ila watiĩte ĩtina. (Lk 17:31, 32) Tũtonya kwĩvathana na maũndũ meva nĩ kana tũikaeme kũmwendeesya Ngai o tondũ mũka wa Loto weekie? Tũyaĩle kwĩtĩkĩlya kũmantha syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ kwĩthĩwe nekw'o ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ thayũnĩ witũ. (Mt 6:33) Yesũ amanyĩisye kana tũitonya "kũthũkũma Ngai o na ũthwii." (Mt 6:24) Nao nata twamanya kana nĩtwambĩĩe kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yingĩ maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-mwĩĩ kwĩ maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva? No tũmũvoye Yeova atũnenge ũmanyi wa kwona nĩ va twaĩle kwĩka moalyũku, na aitũnenga ũkũmbaũ na vinya wa kwĩka moalyũku asu.
ĨLILIKANY'EI ĨLA VITIO YA ILUNGU ITATŨ YĨ NA KYONGO ILIKANAI MŨKA WA LOTO, NA ĨNDĨ MŨISŨNGĨA MAKŨLYO AA MAATĨĨE:
Wendi wa kwĩthĩwa na mbesa mbingĩ wavĩndũie ata mesilya, ũneeni, na meko ma Gloria?
Maũndũ ala mamũkwatie mũka wa Loto metũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
Kũtũmĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia kwatetheeisye Joe na mũsyĩ wake ata?
Andũ ala Anna wathũkũmaa namo matumie ata aendeea naĩ kĩ-veva?
Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ũkũmbaũ ĩla twaingĩĩw'a twone kũmantha mbesa new'o ũndũ ũla wa vata?
Nĩ kwa nzĩa syĩva Brian na Gloria mambĩĩe ĩngĩ kwosa maũndũ ma kĩ-veva kwa ũito?
Nĩ myolooto yĩva ya Mbivilia woona ĩeleetw'e vitionĩ ĩno?

translation:
Will the man named Loto succeed in hiding his wealth during the time of Sodom? I implore you, remember my plight. (Pr 19:17, 26) Just as Jesus foretold, it seems that the man named Loto will perish unless he flees quickly. (Lu 17:31, 32) Should we be concerned about worldly things, or should we prioritize pleasing God, just as the man named Loto did? Let us strive to seek first the Kingdom and His righteousness, rather than focusing on material possessions and anxieties. (Mt 6:33) Jesus taught us that we must "serve God and no one else." (Mt 6:24) And how can we demonstrate that we truly value spiritual pursuits over materialistic concerns? Let us trust that Jehovah will grant us discernment to recognize what is genuinely important, and He will provide us with strength to make wise decisions.
CONSIDER THE EXAMPLE OF LOT AND HIS FAMILY TO LEARN LESSONS, AND REMEMBER THESE POINTS:
What motivated Lot to try to save his family, including his daughters-in-law, and what happened to them?
What does Lot's example teach us?
Did the Bible's counsel help Joe and his wife escape danger?
Were there any who listened to Anna's warnings and took action?
Can we learn from the distress they experienced and focus on what matters most?
Why did Brian and Gloria feel compelled to share their experiences with others?
Does the Bible offer practical guidance regarding these situations?

President Uhuru Kenyatta niwatongoesya atongoi angi kusisya mwii wa mututuia president wa 3 wa Kenya Mwai Kibaki mawakoni manene ma bunge vaa musyini wa Ilovi.
Mwii uu wa Kibaki yu wiithiwa bungeni isu kwambiiya umunthi nginya muthenyani wa wakatatu nikana kumanenga enenthi ivuso ya kutambuka kuusisya.
Mututia Kibaki anatiiwe ni thayu kwi muthenyani wa Wakatano kyumwani kithelu ena ukuu wa miaka 90, na eikwatiwa kuthikwa muthenyani wa Wanthathatu uu wa matuku 30 musyi kwake kisioni kya Othaya ,countini ya Nyeri.

translation:
President Uhuru Kenyatta has eulogized his predecessor the third president of Kenya Mwai Kibaki during a special parliamentary session in Nairobi's parliament buildings.
This session of Kibaki is being held in parliament today to honor the late leader who served three terms and refused to succumb to pressure to remain in office.
The late Kibaki will be buried on Saturday at his home in Wakatano which he built over 90 years ago, and was received to be buried on Saturday the 30th in his hometown of Othaya, Nyeri county.

translation:

text:
Nthi ya kenya kwi umunthini nikukwatania na nthi ila ingi ikonyoni syonthe sya yonthe kusomethya enethi yiulu wa uwau wi muisyo wa cancer muthenya ula kielelo kithiawa kusomethya enethi nzia sya kwisyiana na uwau usu na kumanenga wikwatyo endwa maitu ala maendeye na kuukitana nawo.
Mwakani uu wa 2022 kielelo ni "Close the Care Gap" kithitoni kya kuete kyenini uwau uu wa cancer na matambya ala mbikaia oyu mosetwe kuukitana uwau usu.
Kwianana na muvea wa uima wa mwii nthi yonthe ni kana uwau wa cancer ivindani yii niwithiitwe muisyo muno na kuwaa ma million ma enethi vala withiawa wi mithemba mbingi.
Ve cancer ya nthakame,ya ivu,ya kikonde,ya itema,ya usyai ila iwaa amwaitu,na ya nondo vala kilungu kya ikw'u sya uwau usu kivikite 27% nthi yonthe.
Ni kumanwa na kii vala serikali ya nthi ya kenya yikiite matambya ala mailite kuikitha ala mawaa uwau usu nimakwata uiti museo kwa kwithiwa amwe mavikiia na kutambuka nthi sya nza kukwata uiiti usu wakosekana vaa nthi ya kenya kindu kila ni ngalama yi yiulu ya uiti.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The country of Kenya, in its entirety, is grappling with illness, but many are suffering silently from all types of diseases, especially the disease of cancer, which has become a serious concern, making it necessary to seek medical attention and connect with those affected.
In the year 2022, the theme is "Close the Care Gap," focusing on reaching out to people with cancer and providing care for them.
Connecting with healthcare providers across the country means that cancer cases are increasing significantly and costing millions of shillings due to increased hope.
There are cancers of the breast, ovaries, cervix, intestines, skin, and others affecting men, and prostate cancer accounts for 27% of all illnesses nationwide.
It is understood that the Kenyan government is implementing measures to provide care, but access to healthcare remains limited due to distance and lack of resources, meaning that many Kenyans struggle to afford quality healthcare.

Ainenea isengeoni ya mbumbanio ya Bomas of Kenya vaa musyini wa ilovi Raila oingi niwathingiliila nthi ya kenya yina ilovia sya kwianana na kunenga enethi maendeo ethiwa muinyu wa ulusani ukokitanwa naw'o aiweta ala alusani serikalini yake makethiawa mayosewa matambya mavyu ma mioa.
Oingi niwatumia ivuso yiu kuvuthiisya munini wa President William Ruto aimuweta ta mundu ukwivanya kwithiwa ena wendi museo kwa nthi ya kenya.

translation:
The leader of the ODM party, Raila Odinga, has sent a message of condolence following the death of his elder brother who was 77 years old, expressing sympathy to Kenyans on the loss of a development visionary but also hoping to seize the opportunity to become the 5th president of Kenya.
He addressed the nation from the Bomas of Kenya grounds where he stated that Kenya needs unity and peace to achieve development for the benefit of citizens, adding that if elected, his government will prioritize addressing issues affecting ordinary people.
He also sent a message encouraging President William Ruto, wishing him well and stating that he has good intentions for the country of Kenya.

Bunge ya Senate umunthi yiikwatiwa kwalania kikalo kya kuneenanisya mbesa ila siutumwa silikalini sya kaunti
Bunge ya Senate umunthi yiikwatiwa kwalania kikalo ki mwanya, kuneenanisya ngusanisyo ila syithiitwe vo, yiulu wa ni nzia yiku yailite kutumiwa kuaania mbesa ila siuthi silikalini sya kaunti.
Kiu ni itina wa amwe ma maseneta kuleana na mutalatala mweu wa kuaania mbesa ila syailite kuthi silikalini sya kaunti, ula ukuatiiya muno utalo wa andu ala me kauntini isu, vandu va unene wa i kaunti.
Ethiwa mutalatala usu mweu nuutumiwa kuaania mbesa isu sya silikali sya kaunti, kaunti 18 nisyikwasya kimanza kya silingi billion 17.
Undu usu nunatumite bunge ya seneti yiemwa ni kuvitukithya mutalatala usu, naa kuselesya uai wa silingi billion 316 na Nusu, mbesa sya mwaka uu ila itumawa ni silikali nene ta kinandu kya kutumiwa ni silikali isu sya Mutiuuko.
Kuatiania na mivango isu myeu, kaunti ila syina ukya mwingi, ivaniiwe ikwate kilungu kya 14% kya mbesa ila ikuaanwa, unene wa kaunti uyiaiwa kilungu 4%, nawo utalo wa andu uyiaiwa kilungu kya 18%.
Uthukumi wa uima wa ene nthi kila kaunti wiithiwa uvathiitwe kilungu kya 20%, namo maundu meukonia uimi maivathiwa kilungu kya 10%.
Kuatiania na Ndongoi ya ala aingi bungeni isu ya seneti Irungu Kangáta,Musumbi Uhuru Kenyatta, nunaumisye mwolooto kana, ngusanisyo isu syailite kuthinikiwa kwa mituki na usungio kuvikiiwa kikaloni kyu ki mwanya kya Umunthi.

translation:
The Senate committee was convened today to discuss the issue of allocating funds, but the distribution was not done at the county level.
The Senate committee was convened today to discuss the criteria for harmonizing allocations, but it was postponed, and there is a way this will be used to allocate funds, but not at the county level.
The challenge is that some senators are responsible for discussing how to allocate funds, but it has not been implemented at the county level; this situation affects the people of those counties, the residents of each county.
However, the discussion about how to allocate funds to the counties, 18 counties were allocated a total of 17 billion shillings.
Wajir County was allocated 2 billion shillings, Marsabit 1 billion and 9 million shillings, Mandera and Garissa counties received 1 billion and 6 million shillings, Tana River 1.5 billion shillings, and Mombasa County also received 1 billion shillings, among other counties.
What was presented to the Senate today was to approve the allocation, or to release 316 billion and half shillings for this year's budget, but it was approved by the national government due to the manner in which it will be used by the Ministry of Finance.
Regarding these figures, counties do not have much capacity, they have been given 14% of the funds they require, the size of the county is allocated 4%, and the population is allocated 18%.
The development of infrastructure in each county is estimated to be allocated 20%, and other services are allocated 10%.
According to various sources within the Senate today, Senator Irungu Kangáta and Musumbi Uhuru Kenyatta have expressed their concerns, and the allocations have not been finalized due to disagreements and objections regarding the criteria for the current committee.

translation:
The Minister for Public Service and Gender Affairs of Kenya, Cecily Kariuki, has today announced her resignation from the position of Governor of Nyandarua County ahead of this year's elections.
Kariuki made this decision in order to focus on other matters and allow others to serve the county.
In two separate announcements regarding the appointment of officials, the Managing Director of the Kenya Broadcasting Corporation (KBC), Bonny Musambi, also announced his resignation from the position of Member of Parliament for Kitui Central Constituency in Kitui County.
The constituency seat was previously held by Frank Kilonzo, who is seeking re-election, while Musambi will now focus on serving the people...

WHO ARE WE AND WHY?
Does the Bible really have the power to change people for the better? Or does it just seem to? The Bible itself says: "All Scripture is inspired by God and beneficial." —2 Timothy 3:16, 17.
This issue of The Watchtower examines some scriptures that can help us understand what the Bible teaches and shows how we can apply what we learn when we read the Bible and teach others.

THE BIBLE CHANGES LIVES
One woman, Yvonne Quarrie, wondered, "Is this possible?" The experience she had proved it was.
IMITATE THEIR FAITH

Mũthenya wa Sila nĩ kyaũ?
Ĩvindanĩ ya tene Ngai atũmĩaa asili kũtangĩĩa andũ make kumana na ũsili ũte wa katĩ. (Asili 2:18) Mbivilia yĩeleetye kana Mũthenya wa Sila nĩ ĩvinda ĩseo yĩla Yeova, Mũsili wa nthĩ yonthe, ũkatangĩĩa andũ kuma maũndũnĩ mate ma ũlũngalu.—Soma Savuli 96:12, 13; Isaia 26:9.
Ngai anyuvĩte Yesũ nĩ kana esilĩla ala me thayũ na ala akw'ũ. (Meko ma Atũmwa 10:42; 17:31) Ve andũ makwie matamwĩsĩ Ngai. Ĩvindanĩ ya Mũthenya wa Sila, Yesũ akathayũũkya andũ asu nĩ kana memanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Ngai na maimwenda.—Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 24:15.
Nĩkĩ Mũthenya wa Sila ũkethĩwa wĩ wa myaka ngili?
Andũ ala makwie makathayũũkw'a ĩvindanĩ ya myaka ngili. (Ũvuan'yo 20:4, 12) Makanengwa ĩvinda nĩ kana mamanyĩw'e kwenda kwa Ngai na kũatĩĩa mĩao yake. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũndũ andũ aingĩ mamanyĩaw'a, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana andũ makasilĩlwa kwĩanana na maũndũ ala makeka ĩtina wa kũthayũũkw'a.—Soma Alomi 6:7.
O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo ũla ũkoka mbee wa ũsumbĩki wa myaka ngili ũtambĩĩe. Mũthenya ũsu now'o wĩtawa mũminũkĩlyo, o tondũ vaeleetw'e ilungunĩ sya mbee sya ĩkaseti yĩĩ. Mũthenya ũsu, Ngai akaananga andũ onthe ala matamũkĩaa na ala athũku. (2 Vetelo 3:7) Kwoou, nĩtwaĩle kwonany'a kana nĩtũmwendete Ngai.—Soma 2 Vetelo 3:9, 13.

translation:
What does Sila's joy mean?
The Bible says that God created people so they could enjoy life and be happy. (Genesis 2:18) However, life has brought challenges, and many people wonder if Sila's joy means that Jehovah, the Creator of everything, wants people to experience true happiness.—Read Psalm 96:12, 13; Isaiah 26:9.
God approved of Jesus because he made both Jews and non-Jews rejoice. (Acts 10:42; 17:31) And many people came to worship God. The joy of Sila meant that Jesus taught people that they should know God's will and obey it.—Read Acts 24:15.
So, is Sila's joy limited to young people?
Many young people have experienced this joy. (Proverbs 20:4, 12) They have learned what it means to please God and live according to his standards. But it is important to remember that many adults also learn, and the Bible shows that people of all ages can find joy in learning how to be happy.—Read Galatians 6:7.
Moreover, the Bible explains that the joy of a righteous life can last throughout our lives, even when we face difficulties. This joy today is often called genuine, because it comes from knowing the truth. This joy, God embraces all people who seek him and trust in him. (2 Peter 3:7) Truly, I want to continue to please God.—Read 2 Peter 3:9, 13.

translation:
The Secretary General of the Central Organization of Trade Unions of Kenya (COTU), Francis Atwoli, is reportedly facing criticism for allegedly recruiting Kenyans to work in various countries in the Gulf and the Middle East, following the circulation of a video online which has sparked controversy.
The controversy revolves around allegations of facilitating travel to the Middle East where individuals claim they face difficult conditions and accuse him of exploiting vulnerable people, promising them good jobs while instead subjecting them to hardship.

Muyumbe wa tene wa Mt Elgon John Serut niwatiwa ni thayu. Andu ma musyi maineena na kisese kimwe kya mauvoo maisye kana Serut atiiwe ni thayu sivitalini munene wa Ilovi.
Michelle, ula ni mwiitu wake, easya kana ithe etiwe itina wa kunyamaawa ni uwau muthuku wa cancer itina wa ivinda yiasa.
Mwaka muvitu, andu ma musyi wa muyumbe usu nimanavikiite kukulya andu mamakwate kwoko kusanga mbesa nundu wa uiiti wake. Thii wa uiiti wake unavikite silingi milioni miongo ili mwaini wa ikumi mwaka muvitu.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The funeral of the late Mount Elgon's John Serut will be held tomorrow. People from his village are mourning together with one sorrowful cry, saying that Serut will be laid to rest peacefully in the large cemetery of Ilovi.
Michelle, who is his daughter, has said that her mother died after battling cancer for a long time.
Last year, people from the village of the deceased were able to help those who were struggling financially to raise funds for his treatment. The cost of his treatment was estimated at ten million shillings over the past ten years.

Mauvoo ala mavikiswe mbungeni meonanya kimanza kya silingi bilion 23 niinatumikie utongoini wa silikali ya president uthyumuiye wia Uhuru Kenyatta vate ngithiiyo ya ayumbe.
muvia wa kinandu wiiweteka kunengane ilovia ii kwa voma ya president na vala inatumikie kuivia kimanza kimwe kya mauta ingi iyaka sivitali wa maovisa ma ita.
Ingi livoti isu yionanya kana ndambuka sya Uhuru na munini wake Ruto inaatumiiye silingi milion 579 ivindani ya myei itatu kwaangiiya unyuvani munene.
Ota ou nikuumbukie kana voma wa president unatumiye silingi bn 1.4 kumbanya mbumbano sya kii uteti mwei umwe mwakani wa muthya wa utongoi wa Uhuru ila na ta silingi milion inya kila muthenya mautanuni vomani usu.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The situation is such that 23 billion shillings have been allocated for the construction of the president's residence, which is being built near Uhuru Kenyatta's farm, causing public outcry.
The tender for this project was awarded through a process involving the president's office and it is said to be used to implement one of the many projects that were previously stalled.
Many voters are questioning whether the expenses incurred by Uhuru and his deputy Ruto amount to 579 million shillings over three years, considering the significant development needs.
It should be remembered that the president's office spent 1.4 billion shillings on renovating a state house just one year during Uhuru's tenure, plus an additional millions of shillings every month for maintenance costs.

text:
Muvia wa kuikiithya wailu wa syindu vaa Kenya KEBS niwakuna muungu uthoosya wa amwe ma mauta ma kuya vaa Kenya.
KEBS yoosa itambya yii kwa kambuni ikumi kwa kila ikuweta kana ndianiisye wailu wa kutuumiika ni andu nundu ti wailu kwa uima wa mwii.
Mivae ya mauta ila kambuni syoo ikuniwe muungu ni vamwe na fresh fry, bahari fresh, fry mate, Sally Fry, Top fry,Rina salit,Fresh fry with garlic na gold and pure olive gold.
Kwisila wa valua kwa ngwatano ya atandithya anini (Retail traders Association of Kenya) nikana muungu uu no wa kavinda kwondu wa kuikiithya kambuni isu nisyaatiiya miyao ya kuikiithya uima museo kwa atumii ma miiyo yoo kumusyiiya mwenenthi na mbanga.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The standardisation marks for products in Kenya from the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) are unique and indicate the quality of Kenyan products.
KEBS uses these marks for ten companies per category depending on who has been certified to be used by many people and not just a few for the life of the product.
Products of quality include companies such as fresh fry, bahari fresh, fry mate, Sally Fry, Top fry, Rina salit, Fresh fry with garlic and gold and pure olive gold.
According to the Retail Traders Association of Kenya, there is a unique mark for each company so that consumers can identify genuine products and avoid being sold substandard goods.

text:
Ni itina wa Koti munene vyu vaa Kenya (Supreme Court) kumya utwi kana vayii ukusi wianiiye kuleana na mausungio ma unyuvani muvitu itina wa asili muonza kwika ukunikili wa maunyungunyisyo ala manaavikitwe ni ngwatanio ya Azimio kotini usu.
Ruto niwaweta niukwianiisya maundu onthe ala silikali yake inaathanite na aweta kana ingi niukukwatiania na president umite Uhuru Kenyatta ovamwe na ngali ya Azimio ila niyo ya ulei.
President Ruto eweta kana nthi ya Kenya ni nthi ya uthasyo na ti nthi ya ngethi sya makwatianio ateo ni makwatianio uthukumini wa mwenenthi.
Ruto eithiwa ayiithwa kithitu kya wia kwii matuku 13 mwei uu na atunga muvea kwa onthe ala manamakwatie mbau na Akenya onthe kuikiithya muuwo mbee na itina wa unyuvani muvitu na athana uthukumi ute kikono na wa maendeeyo.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The fifth president of the Republic of Kenya is Dr. William Samoei Ruto.
He is a judge of the High Court of Kenya (Supreme Court) to hear a case where they challenged his election results, claiming irregularities in the electoral process, but it was dismissed by the Azimio coalition in court yesterday.
Ruto is accused of trying to change things, but his government is said to be working with President Emeritus Uhuru Kenyatta and the Azimio team, but this is untrue.
President Ruto says that Kenya is a country of development and not a country of political conflicts, therefore political stability is essential for citizens.
Ruto has been invited to speak on August 13th this month and give advice to everyone so that Kenyans can live together peacefully and with respect for human rights and promote economic growth and development.

Mbivilia ndyaaminwa na nĩkyo kĩtumi ũtonya kũmĩkwata na kũmĩsoma. Na ĩla wakwata Mbivilia ĩalyũlĩtwe nesa, no wĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana Maandĩko ala ũũsoma vau mayaavĩndũwa, ĩndĩ nĩmo ala maandĩkiwe nĩ aandĩki ma Mbivilia. * Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ ũmũnthĩ tũtonya kũkwata Mbivilia o na kau mavuku ma tene ala maandĩkawa maĩ matonya kwoa, andũ aingĩ maĩ matonya kũmyananga, na angĩ mendaa kũvĩndũa ũvoo ũla wĩ nthĩnĩ? Nĩkĩ Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ya mwanya mũno?
"Yu nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana Mbivilia nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai"
Amanyĩw'a aingĩ ma Mbivilia nĩmetĩkĩlanaa na ndeto ii sya mũtũmwa Vaulo ũla waandĩkie atĩĩ: "Kĩla Ũandĩko nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai." (2 Timotheo 3:16) Maĩkĩĩaa kana Mbivilia yaemie kũminwa nũndũ nĩ Ndeto ya Ngai na kana nĩwe wamĩsũvĩie. Ũla mũndũũme wĩtawa Faizal ũwetetwe mwambĩĩonĩ wa ĩkaseti yĩĩ, nĩwatwie kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli wa maũndũ asu kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Maũndũ ala weemanyĩisye nĩmamũseng'isye mũno. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩwamanyie kana momanyĩsyo maingĩ ala mamanyĩaw'a ndĩninĩ ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto maikwatĩkanaa Mbivilianĩ. O na ĩngĩ, nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ ũndũ Mbivilia yĩeleetye moalyũku ala Ngai ũkeka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Yu nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana Mbivilia nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma mwa Ngai." Aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa Ngai e na vinya wa kũmba ĩtu na nthĩ, kwa w'o no aemwe nĩ kũtũnenga ĩvuku na aiyĩsũvĩa nginya ũmũnthĩ? Tũkasya kana Ngai ndesa kwĩka ũu twĩthĩwa tũivanga kana nde vinya, nake nĩwe Mwene Vinya W'onthe! Nakwa ninyie ũũ nĩ kana nĩvange kana Ngai nde vinya?"—Isaia 40:8.

Mca Sabestian Muli ewetwa kana tawathokaonie na Theophilus Makau me nyumbani imwe ya ndanio ku Tamu Tamu na amukuna amutula kwoko na maeyo 2 atambite kusemba na kwaia muumbini.
Muli anai anekiwa mbini ni volisi sya Kavumbuni ku Kathonzweni muthyani wa kyumwa kithelu itina wa ivinda ila unanengetwe ni volisi kwiyumilya kiseseni kiu yathela indi auma na police bond ya kimanza kya silingi 20,000 nikana ikaoni yii yambiie umunthi uu.
Sabestian Muli anasakuitwe ta mca wa Ward ya Kitise/Kithuki oo mwakani muthelu nthini nthini wa usakuani munini kuatiani na ula wai mca waku kutia kivila kiu.

translation:
The Member of Parliament for Makueni County's Kitise/Kithuki Ward, Sebastian Muli, was arrested and presented in the Makueni court yesterday following allegations of assaulting and causing harm to a trader from the Tamu Tamu market, resulting in injuries lasting 21 days from December of last year.
MCA Sebastian Muli was accused by Theophilus Makau of attacking him at his home in Tamu Tamu and inflicting wounds on his head and body with two knives, leading to severe bleeding.
Muli is currently being held at the Kavumbuni Police Station in Kathonzweni awaiting a hearing next Tuesday, but he has been released on a cash bail of Ksh 20,000 pending further investigation into this matter.
Sebastian Muli is seeking re-election as MCA for the Kitise/Kithuki Ward in the upcoming elections, facing competition from other candidates vying for the position.

Nthini wa kyathi kila kinaatoongoeswe ni President Uhuru Kenyatta na kutwaiiswa ni ita kwianana na kiwango kyake niunengiwe mathiko ma silikali na kukuniwa misinga ikumi na kenda, vala ndongoi na enenthi aingi manaamukumisye kwa kwithiwa okililye ukwati wa nthi ya Kenya,kuete maendeeyo ta malelu vamwe na kisomo kya mana na ingi kwithiwa anai vata na muuwo na ingi mutongoi unaina muungamo wake.

translation:
The third president of the Republic of Kenya, Emilio Stanley Mwai Kibaki, will be laid to rest in his home in Othaya, Nyeri County on Saturday, April 30, 2022.
Kibaki, who was given a state funeral, was 90 years old and is survived by his wife, children and grandchildren, and he will be buried with honors and mourned by the nation.
The national mourning period has been declared by President Uhuru Kenyatta and flags will fly at half-mast for three days, while condolences continue to pour in from across the world recognizing his contribution to the development of Kenya, especially in education and health, and remembering his leadership and dedication to service.
May God comfort his people.

The incident has been confirmed by the Thatha sublocation chief Charles Kingangi who said they are investigating the cause of the incident or whether it is related to the death of the buffalo, adding that the deceased was often seen at night, and this resident is now being sought by detectives together with witnesses.

text:
Minista muviani wa kisomo Prof. George Magoha yu enda misivi ya kwonanya andu maimanyana kii mwii mitandaoni ikunwe muungu vaa Kenya ni silikali yivo kana ila ikooka itina.
Aineena ivindani ya kuviinguuwa kwa mautanu ma kwina mbathi ala matwaiiwe Kisumu, Magoha niwaweta kana ona kau mutandao niwailitye maundu ma kisomo, maweeku maw'o nimaile kumulikwa muno.
Ingi easya kana we ndeumakwa nikuwetwa ta utongotye kwa kithui nundu etetea uni wa nzyawa ila syivo.
Mwakani wa 2020, Magoha niwasukumiite nzama ya maminista vamwe na president mitandao ila yonanasyaa misivi ya waai ikunwe muungu aiweta taikonetwe vanene na ukui wa mavu wa syana sya ukuu munini.
