translation:
The late Minister of Education Professor George Magoha went to collect data on how people were learning online during the Covid-19 pandemic in Kenya which was very serious but has now subsided.
While inspecting the distribution of tablets at Mabatini Primary School in Kisumu, Magoha stated that some websites were offering educational materials, and those resources need to be vetted here.
It is important that we ensure children are protected from harmful content online but also have access.
In 2020, Magoha worked with other ministers and the president to collect data on how people were learning online during the pandemic and ensured that the welfare of children was taken care of greatly due to the challenges they faced.

text:
Ĩla Yesũ waĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, nĩwakindĩlĩĩile mwĩao ũla waĩtye: "Taĩa au na mwenyu." (Kuma 20:12; Mt 15:4) Vai nzika kana Yesũ aineena ndeto isu ndaĩ na wia nũndũ 'nĩweenyivĩasya' asyai make ĩla waĩ wa mũika. (Lk 2:51) O na e mũndũ mũima, nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana o na ĩtina wa kũkw'a kwake, inyia wake akaendeea na kũsũvĩwa.—Yoa 19:26, 27.
O na ũmũnthĩ, Aklĩsto ma mũika ala mew'aa asyai moo na matũmĩaa ndeto nzeo ĩla meũneena namo methĩawa maimanenga ndaĩa. Vate nzika, mwĩao ũla waĩtye tũnenge asyai maitũ ndaĩa ndwĩ mĩvaka. O na asyai maitũ makũa, nĩtwaĩle kũendeea kũmanenga ndaĩa na kũtetheka kumana na ũĩ woo. (Nth 23:22) O na ĩngĩ, nĩtwonanasya kana nĩtũnengete asyai maitũ ala akũũ ndaĩa kwa kũthĩnĩkĩaa mavata moo ma kĩ-mwĩĩ na ma ngoonĩ. (1Tim 5:8) Twĩthĩwe twĩ akũũ kana twĩ andũ ma mũika, ũndũ ũla mũnene twaĩle kwĩka twonany'e kana nĩtũnengete asyai maitũ ndaĩa nĩ kũneenaa namo na kũeaa ngewa namo kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle.
ĨLOELEI VITIO YA KATUNI SYA KŨSOLA YĨ NA KYONGO, NDONYA ATA KŨEA NGEWA NA ASYAI MAKWA TŨKEW'ANA? NA ĨNDĨ MŨISŨNGĨA MAKŨLYO AA MAATĨĨE:
Nĩkĩ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũneena na asyai maku?
Ũtonya ata kũnenga asyai maku ndaĩa ĩla ũũneena namo?
Tũtethekaa ata ĩla tweekĩa kĩthito tũneene na asyai maitũ? (Nth 15:22)

translation:
But Jesus himself also showed what is important when he said: "Everyone ought to obey the authorities." (Rom. 20:12; Matt. 15:4) So it is evident that Jesus recognized the need to respect those in positions of responsibility, because he was obedient as a boy.—Luke 2:51. And as a perfect man, he demonstrated that he had regard for his Father's will, and his life continued to be one of obedience.—John 19:26, 27.
And furthermore, Christ as a human did not seek his own glory, but used his authority for the benefit of others, showing concern for their welfare. So the principle he taught us is that we should use our influence for good and not for selfish ambition. (Phil. 23:22) And indeed, we recognize that we should use our influence for good toward those who are members of our household, being willing to work hard and provide for them. (1 Tim. 5:8) Let us remember that we are humans, and the most important thing we can do is to use our influence for good, showing concern for others and being generous toward them in whatever way we can.
CONSIDER THE EXAMPLE OF THE GOOD SHEPHERD, AND WHY HE GIVES HIS LIFE FOR THE SHEEP, RATHER THAN SEEKING GLORY OR BEING GENEROUS TO HIMSELF? AND LET US ASK OURSELVES THESE QUESTIONS:
Are you inclined to think about what is beneficial to others?
Are you willing to show concern for the welfare of others?
Will we strive to live in harmony with those around us? (Phil. 15:22)

text:

Mwalali aneena kii itina wa Muandu Ngilu kutwaaisya ndambuka,kisioni kyake kya ward ya mbitini,vala utambukie kuneena na enenthi sokoni wa mbitini na Kitungati na kulea kumunenga yanya ya kuneena

translation:
The great leader of the Wiper party Dr. Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka is appreciating the party but not its policies and he has requested to meet with leaders from the Ukambani region, this important meeting will be held and progress made.
This is in connection with the governor of Kitui County Charity Ngilu who yesterday visited the MP for Kitui Rural, in Kitui county, to discuss the issue of funds for our people through the empowerment fund to help with development and unity of the people.

text:
Nzama ya mituo miseo na kuukitana na ulusani (EACC) niyanenga koti munene lingilia wa kusyiiya mali ya lato wa silingi 88,807,473.67 kwa umwe wa ala manai maovisa ma nzama nene ya uungamii (CEC) silikalini ya kaunti ya Masaku aungamiiye muvea wa wiana wa soko (Urban) Urbanus Wambua Musyoka.
Kii kiuka itina wa Musyoka kuweteka kwithiwa aikonanwa na kiliingisi kya silingi .91,202,892, syavathiitwe kaunti isu ungu wa ala mavotheaa silikali sya mityuuko kati wa mwaka wa 2013 – 15.
Musyoka eweteka kwithiwa aivie kambuni imukonetye ila ni Wisdom Holding Ltd, Wemmar Enterprise, Wafih International Ltd na Kikoto General Merchants ilovia isu uvathukanu na miyao.
Eweteka yingi kwithiwa atumiiye silingi 80,251,815 kwaka nyumba ya musyi ya kiutongoi kisioni kya Kibauni Masaku vala vengi yatiiwe na silingi 10,951,077.
license: ODC-By-1.0 (dataset); source text subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use
translation:
The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has filed a major case involving the theft of public funds amounting to Ksh 88,807,473.67 against a former chief officer of the county government of Machakos, who was the head of urban areas (Urbanus Wambua Musyoka).
The charges against Musyoka relate to allegations of embezzling Ksh 91,202,892, which were allegedly misappropriated by the county during the financial years 2013–15.
Musyoka is accused of using companies including Wisdom Holding Ltd, Wemmar Enterprise, Wafih International Ltd and Kikoto General Merchants to facilitate the fraud.
He is alleged to have used Ksh 80,251,815 to purchase a residential house in Kibauni, Machakos while the rest amounted to Ksh 10,951,077.
His case will be mentioned on November 3, 2022.

Manager wa kilavu kya Mwamba Rugby kutiwa ni thayu kumana na mbanga ya lelu kuya nakuru kwi iyoo. Kumana na mauvoo ala matumiwe iseseni sya mauvoo kuma kilavuni kii nikana manager uu kwa syitwa Stephanie Rose Otieno akwatie m,banga ii kwi iyoo masaa ma kwakya ivindani yila eumite vaa musyini wa ilovi o kavinda kavuthu itina wa kumina masindano ma Prinsloo 7s competition vala mwamba inaminie I namba muonza itina wa kusindwa ni kabras rfc.

translation:
12/07/2022
The manager of the Mwamba Rugby club has been appointed to lead the team on their trip to Nakuru today. Leading the players and having used training sessions at the club which now has a new manager named Stephanie Rose Otieno she will lead the team on this trip today for approximately seven hours while visiting the Iloni stadium to prepare for the Prinsloo 7s competition where Mwamba lost and finished in seventh place against Kabras RFC.
Rose previously served as one of the club's managers in 2019 and works alongside other managers. The Mwamba club based in Iloni was founded in 1977.

text:

Ithyi ta aklisto, ve vata wa kwithukiisya wasya wa Ngai kwa kutambania nake ona kethiwa maundu mailye ata ngelekanio nzeo ni Avalaamu ula weeteelile ivinda yiasa muno ayisa kuathimwa na mwana ateukwa ngoo.
Umunthi muklisto mwendwa, ona kethiwa wisilite maunduni momu ata, eka kwikala utaataite maunduni indi sakua na uyithiwa na woni oundu umwe na kieleelo kya kuatiia na kuungama na Ngai eweka nundu niwe mwene utonyi wonthe na ndaalyukaa.
Kwoou ikiia, mwikwatye, tumusisye Ngai eweka nikana tuvikie nautetheka thayuni, Amen.

translation:
When God wants to show someone a secret thing in a dream, he first tests him in reality.
This is like Christ, who wanted people to understand the ways of God through worshipping Him and doing good deeds, even though Abraham was willing to sacrifice his only son.
A true Christian should therefore strive to do good things always, so that he may not be found wanting by anyone and have a reason to boast about being close to and united with God, who has all power and authority.
Therefore, let us pray, let us worship God alone so that we can hear and obey His commands, Amen.

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Sikũkũ ya Isita ndyumanĩte na Mbivilia. Wasisya nesa isitoli yayo, yonanĩtye kana yaumanie na syĩthĩo sya tene ikonetye ũsyai. Kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa maatĩĩe.
Ĩsyĩtwa Isita: Ĩvuku Encyclopædia Britannica yaĩtye: "
ĩsyĩtwa Isita ĩyĩsĩkĩe nesa vala yaumie. Myakanĩ ya 700 na kĩndũ, mũtongoi wa ndĩni ya Anglo-Saxon wĩtawa Venerable Bede, aumisye ĩsyĩtwa yĩu ĩsyĩtwanĩ ya ngai nga ya Anglo-Saxon yĩtawa Eostre." Mavuku angĩ makonanasya ĩsyĩtwa yĩu na Astarte ĩla nĩ ngai nga ya ũsyai ya Phoenicia, na yĩsĩkĩe ta Ishtar Mbaviloni.
Mbũkũ na tũvalũkũ: Itũmĩawa kwonany'a ũtonyi wa ũsyai "
na syaumanie na sikũkũ sya tene sya Europe na Middle East ikonetye ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ ila syeekawa ĩvindanĩ ya mbevo."
—Encyclopædia Britannica.
Matumbĩ: Kwosana na Funk & Wagnalls Standard Dictionary of Folklore, Mythology and Legend, kũmantha matumbĩ ma Ista ala monekaa ta maetawe nĩ mbũkũ ya Isita, "
ti ĩthaũ, ĩndĩ nĩ kĩthĩo kya sikũkũ sya tene kĩkonetye maũndũ ma ũsyai." Syĩthĩonĩ imwe andũ maĩkĩĩaa kana matumbĩ asu ma Isita manakavye "
no maete ũtanu, wingĩ wa malĩ, ũima wa mwĩĩ, na makasũvĩa andũ."—Traditional Festivals.
Ngũa nzaũ sya Isita: "
woonekaa wĩ ũndũ ũte wa ndaĩa na ũtonya kũete vaati nthũku mũndũ kũkethya Eastre, ngai nga ya ĩvinda ya mbevo ya Scandinavia ekĩĩte ngũa ngũũ."—The Giant Book of Superstitions.
Maũndũ ala meekawa ĩvinda ya kuma kwa sua: Maũndũ asu makonanĩtw'e na ũthaithi wa sua na "
meekawa nĩ andũ nĩ kana mathokye kuma kwa sua, na ũtonyi wayo wa kũtuma syĩndũ ila imeete siendeea kwĩthĩwa thayũ."—Celebrations—The Complete Book of American Holidays.
Ĩvuku The American Book of Days nĩyĩeleetye nesa vala Isita yaumie, yaĩtye: "
Vaiĩ nzika kana ndĩni yaatĩĩie syĩthĩo na momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ ma tene na yamatw'ĩkĩthya ma Kĩklĩsto."
Mbivilia nĩkanĩtye andũ ĩũlũ wa kũmũthaitha Ngai maatĩĩe syĩthĩo ila itamwendeeasya. (Maliko 7:6-8) Ĩandĩko ya 2 Akolintho 6:17 yaĩtye: '
Ĩvathanei nao, eneena ũu Mwĩaĩi, na mũikakiite kĩndũ kĩvuku.' Isita nĩ sikũkũ yumanĩte na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ, na ala meenda kũmwendeesya Ngai nĩmaĩlĩte kwĩvathana nayo.

translation:
The Easter Story
Easter day is associated with the Bible. People dye eggs, some decorate them, and others hide them for children to find. This symbolizes new life.
The Origin of Easter: The Encyclopædia Britannica says: "
The name 'Easter' is believed to be derived from an ancient goddess. Around 700 AD, the Anglo-Saxon monk Venerable Bede wrote that Easter was named after the Anglo-Saxon goddess Eostre." Other sources connect this festival with Astarte, a Phoenician goddess of fertility, and with Ishtar of Babylon.
Myths and Legends: It is said that the egg represents "
new life and is associated with spring festivals in Europe and the Middle East symbolizing rebirth and renewal."
—Encyclopædia Britannica.
Customs: According to Funk & Wagnalls Standard Dictionary of Folklore, Mythology and Legend, certain customs of Easter seem to be connected with myths about Easter, "
namely, it is a celebration of spring and symbols of new life." Some people believe that Easter customs originated "
from pagan practices, including fertility rites, the abundance of flowers, the growth of crops, and the revival of nature."—Traditional Festivals.
Early Easter Traditions: "
It was considered good luck to eat eggs on Easter Day, believing they would bring prosperity and health."—The Giant Book of Superstitions.
Practices Associated with Spring: Practices related to spring and "
were often observed by people who offered sacrifices to ensure a bountiful harvest."—Celebrations—The Complete Book of American Holidays.
The American Book of Days states that the ancient Easter celebrations "
involved rituals and ceremonies associated with spring and were later adapted by Christians."
The Bible condemns people's attempts to honor God through traditions that displease him. (Mark 7:6-8) 2 Corinthians 6:17 says: '
"Come out from among them," says the Lord, "and stop associating with them."' Easter is a festival linked to pagan traditions, and those seeking to please God should avoid participating in it.

text:
Ngai ti mundu undu utonya kuneena uvungu na kwoou kila Ngai waneena nikyo kivikiiyaa na kwiania.
Umunthi mavinda maingi nituvikiite kulea kukwata uathimo wa Ngai nundu wa kulea kuikiia otondu Elisa waminie kwathana useo kuuya nthi ya Samalia itina wa nzaa ya ivinda yiasa indi andu meethiwa na makana.
Ngai wamina kuneena kwisila athukumini make, ve vata wa kwithukiisya nundu Ngai niwianiiasya ndeto yake. Mwithukiisya ndukatate kwona Ngai tawakuekie unyamae mavinda onthe indi kwa kuikiia, ena utonyi wa kwianiisya mavata maitu vate kisii.
Kwoou Muklisto, osa itambya na uyukila na Ngai nutambukiitye kwoko kwake akwose na kuuthokya usumbini wake vala ve thayu wa tene na tene, Amen.

translation:
God is a person who knows everything and hears everything God wants to hear and see.
Many people today we try to get God's favor so that we can believe in Jesus Christ who showed us how to go to Somalia during the time of great suffering where people were being helped and given food.
God cares about his creations, they are able to praise God and glorify his name. To praise him means to see God working miracles among people, and he has the power to help our children who are sick.
Follow Christ, do not be discouraged and trust in God who will guide you always and relieve your burdens forever and ever, Amen.

text:
Munini wa president Rigathi Gachagua niwakulya enenthi mamanyie uneeni wake wa uw'o.
Gachagua aneeena kii itina wa uthaithi kanisani umwe wa AIC ula wii Uasin Gishu aiweta kana ala meuvinga uneeni wake ula waumisye itina wa kuithwa wia ta munini wa president kukonya nthi ya Kenya kwithiwa itena ilovia kumana na utongoi muthuku mamanye niwaw'o na maisuania kwa vamwe kuukilya na kutuungiiyaukwati wa Kenya.
Niwaweta kana Akenya kwithiwa matena mawia na mikovo mingi yoothootheete ukwati kutheeya, aiweta kana president William Ruto niunaanyamaitwe, akavuthwa na kuvathwa vaasa na utongoi ula wokitiiye vanene ateo maekea ala mamunyamaisye.
Nake ula wai gavana wa kaunti ya Ilovi Mike Mbuvi Sonko niwaweta kana nimaekeiye ala manaamunyamasyaa Dr. Ruto ateo ala makonanitwe na ulusani na utumii wa mali ya mwenenthi ta ilovia ssya KEMSA matunge kana mosewe matambya mavyu ma kii miyao.
Ndongoi ingi syivikite uthaithini usu wa kutunga muvea nivamwe na spika wa mbunge nene Moses Wetangula, Ndongoi ya aingi mbungeni nene Kimani Ichungwa, minista mwoloote muviani wa ukui na malelu Kipchumba Murkomen kati wa ndongoi ingi sya kiuteti.
Nake Komishena wa Rift Valley Mohamed Maalim niwaikiithisya ekali ma kisio kiu kana nimeuthukumana kwa vakuvi na atongoi asakue kisioni kiu kutuumanya muuw'o ula withiitwe uiviingiswa na ala moyaa indo.

translation:
The president Rigathi Gachagua's cook is eating food that tastes like his owner's.
Gachagua has a case of influence peddling in one of the AIC churches in Uasin Gishu, he is being investigated over allegations that his owner misused funds while serving as the president's cook, interfering with Kenyan affairs, causing trouble and engaging in corrupt practices with others to undermine Kenya's development.
He is being investigated because Kenyans have many complaints and accusations regarding corruption, and President William Ruto is being implicated, accused and convicted due to the government's involvement in serious issues which have led to public outcry.
Like the case of former Governor of Illovi County Mike Mbuvi Sonko, he is being investigated for allegedly implicating Dr. Ruto in matters related to mismanagement of funds especially concerning KEMSA tenders, where billions were stolen.
Other reports indicate involvement in forming alliances with National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetangula, Majority Leader Kimani Ichungwa, and Roads and Transport Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen among other leaders.
Also, Rift Valley Commissioner Mohamed Maalim has denied claims that he interfered with investigations and laws, stating that he respects the law and will not allow anyone to obstruct justice.

text:
Aklĩsto aingĩ mavoie nĩmokaa ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. O na kau nĩmalikile masindanonĩ aa ma thayũ, nĩmaolile kĩthito kyoo nũndũ wa itumi syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Itumi imwe niwetetwe mbulosuanĩ Mũsyokee Yeova. (Aevl 12:1) Ĩndĩ o na asu mavoie nĩ ma vata methonĩ ma Yeova nĩkwĩthĩwa amathooie na nthakame ya Mwana wake. (Alo 8:32; 1Vet 1:18, 19) Tũtonya kũmatetheesya ata masyoke kĩkundinĩ?
O tondũ mũĩthi ũmanthaa na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo malondu ala mau, atumĩa ma kĩkundi nĩmekĩaa kĩthito mamanthe na maitetheesya Aklĩsto ala mavoie. translation:
Christians should always be ready to give a reason for the hope they have in Jesus. And if you have been taught the good news by others, you should make an effort now to learn more about it so that you can explain it clearly. (Acts 12:1) Also, if you have been taught the good news, it is because you value the things Jehovah teaches and you appreciate the sacrifice his Son made. 1st Samuel 1:11
Elkanah had two wives; Peninnah and Hannah.
Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ĩĩ. Mbivilia yĩ na myolooto ĩna ĩtonya ũtũtetheesya ĩla twĩ na mathĩna kana makoani:
Vanga nesa ũndũ ũũtũmĩa mbesa syaku. "
Mosũanĩo ma ala athingu maelete wingĩnĩ wa syĩndũ; ĩndĩ kĩla mũndũ ũla wĩkalaataa ekalaataa kũvika akaĩwe tũ." (Nthimo 21:5) Ndũkasembee kũthooa kĩndũ atĩ nũndũ thooa wakyo wĩ nthĩ kana nĩ mũoleku. Andĩka syĩndũ ila ũkwenda kũthooa na mbesa ila ũtonya kũtũmĩa, na ũilũmany'a na ũu.
Taanĩsya na makoani mate ma lasima. "
Ũla ũkovaa nĩ mũthũkũmi wa ũla ũkovethasya." (Nthimo 22:7) Ethĩwa wĩ na makoani na nũkũemwa nĩ kũĩva ũndũ mweew'anie, neena na ũla wakũkovethisye ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũvangĩte kũmũĩvaa. Mũthing'ĩĩsye etĩkĩle mũvango ũsu waku. Atĩĩa ũtao wa Mbivilia ũla wanengiwe ũla mũndũ waĩkĩĩthisye ĩkoani ya mũtũi wake: "
Enda, wĩnyivĩtye, noimwĩsũva mũtũi waku; ndũkaeke metho maku makome." (Nthimo 6:1-5) Ethĩwa ĩvinda ya mbee mũinew'ana, ndũkatule, syoka ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ.
Ĩthĩwa na woni waĩle ĩũlũ wa mbesa. "
Mũndũ ũte mũlau endaa kũthua mĩtũkĩ, na ndesĩ kana eteelwe nĩ ũkya." (Nthimo 28:22, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Kĩwĩu na ĩtomo nĩtonya kũtuma tũthelelwa na twaĩwa nĩ ĩvinda ya kwĩka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva.
Ĩanĩwa nĩ syĩndũ ila sya vata. "
Tweethĩwa na kya ũya na kya kwĩvw'ĩka, syĩndũ isu ikatwĩanĩa." (1 Timotheo 6:8) Mbesa iituma wĩthĩwa wĩ mũtanu kana wĩ mwĩanĩe. Andũ ala atanu vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ti ala methĩawa na mbesa mbingĩ. Ũtanu woo wumanaa na kwĩthĩwa na mũsyĩ wendanĩte, anyanya, na kwĩthĩwa me anyanya ma Ngai.
—Nthimo 15:17; 1 Vetelo 5:6, 7.

translation:
The Book of Proverbs
I. Proverbs are like precious jewels that shine when we share them with others:
Take care to use this advice carefully. "
A diligent person will certainly succeed; but anyone who is lazy will surely come to poverty." (Proverbs 21:5) Strive to find out what makes you successful or unsuccessful. Write down your thoughts so you can learn from them, and improve yourself.
Be careful about bad companions. "
Whoever associates with fools will suffer harm." (Proverbs 22:7) Be cautious with your friends and avoid getting involved in things you know are wrong, especially if those around you encourage you to do harmful things. Consider whether your actions align with your values. As the Bible says about someone who ruins their life: "
Go, fool, and learn a lesson; and become wise." (Proverbs 6:1-5) Be warned by the mistakes of others, and don't repeat them.
Be aware of the consequences of debt. "
A wicked person runs away when no one is chasing him, but an honest person is bold as a lion." (Proverbs 28:22, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Greed and selfishness can lead us to make poor choices and face difficult situations.
Be content with what you have. "
We brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out of it." (1 Timothy 6:8) Money can help us live comfortably or cause us problems. Those who love money never have enough, and they constantly worry about having more. Being content leads to godliness and satisfaction.
—Proverbs 15:17; 1 Peter 5:6, 7.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Ĩĩ. Ngai nũthĩnĩkĩaa athũkũmi make ala awau. Mbivilia yaasya ũũ ĩũlũ wa mũthũkũmi mũĩkĩĩku wa Ngai: "
Yeova nĩwe ũkamũtethya e ũkomonĩ awaa." (Savuli 41:3) Ethĩwa wĩ na ũwau mũthũku, kũatĩĩa maũndũ aa atatũ no kũũtetheesye mũno:
Voya ũnengwe vinya wa kũmĩĩsya. No ũkwate "
mũuo wa Ngai ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe." Mũuo ũsu nĩũkũnenga vinya na kũũtetheesya ũmĩĩsye.
—Avilivi 4:6, 7.
Ĩthĩwa na woni waĩle. Mbivilia yaasya: "
Ngoo ndanu nĩ mũiito mũseo; ĩndĩ ngoo yĩ na ũthatu nĩũtuma mũndũ esa kũkw'a." (Nthimo 17:22, Good News Translation) Tata wĩthĩawe wĩ mũtanu, nũndũ ũu nĩũtuma ũtemakĩa mũno, o na nĩũtuma wĩthĩwa na mwĩĩ ũte na mathĩna maingĩ.
Ĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Wĩkwatyo mũseo nĩũtuma wĩthĩwa na ũtanu ona ĩla wĩ na ũwau mũthũku. (Alomi 12:12) Mbivilia nĩyathanĩte ĩvinda yĩla andũ '
matakasya nyie nĩ mũwau.' (Isaia 33:24) Ĩvinda yĩu Ngai akamina mowau onthe mathũku ala mũndũ ũtatonya kũmina. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia nĩwetete kana ũkũũ ũkathela. Yaĩtye: "
Mwĩĩ wake ũkeethĩwa mwololo kwĩ wa kana; Nũsyokaa mĩthenyanĩ ya wana wake."
—Yovu 33:25.
Lilikana: O na kau Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩsĩ kana Ngai no aitetheesye, nimanthaa ũiiti ĩla syakwatwa nĩ ũwau mũthũku. (Maliko 2:17) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, vaiĩ ũiiti ũla tũtonya kwasya nĩw'o mũseo. Na nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩu, kĩla mũndũ nĩwe waĩle kwĩtw'ĩĩa ũiiti ũla ũkwona waĩle.

translation:
The Bible Says
1. God strengthens his loyal ones, but he troubles the wicked. The Bible says this about Jehovah, the Strong One:
"Jehovah will be my strength in times of trouble." (Psalm 41:3) Be kind and compassionate, so that you may avoid problems and show mercy:
Use mild speech to calm people down. And ask for "the wisdom of God that surpasses all understanding." This wisdom will help you to speak calmly and show compassion.
—Proverbs 4:6, 7.
Be cheerful. The Bible says: "A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones." (Proverbs 17:22, Good News Translation) Think of how happy others are, and this will encourage you, and it will also make you more cheerful and less worried.
Be reasonable. Being reasonable helps you to be cheerful and compassionate toward others. (Colossians 12:12) The Bible compares unreasonable anger to a disease, and it says that people '
who are sick need a doctor.' (Isaiah 33:24) God can heal any sickness, but a person must cooperate in order to get healed. For example, the Bible tells us what happens when someone refuses treatment. It says:
"His life will slowly waste away like that of a grasshopper; his years will quickly pass by."
—Job 33:25.
Remember: And if you seek Jehovah, he will respond to you, and if you earnestly search for him, he will let himself be found by you. (Mark 2:17) So, if you want to find something, keep looking for it. And because of experience, everyone knows that we find what we look for.

We nĩwonaa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwĩka maũndũ maseo?— Andũ aingĩ monaa ũndũ ũsu wĩ vinya. Mbivilia ĩtũtavĩtye kana ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa kamwana keetawa Yosia kwĩka maũndũ maseo. Ĩndĩ, kaĩ na anyanya aseo ala makatetheeasya. Eka twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yosia na anyanyae make.
Ĩthe wa Yosia eetawa Amoni na aĩ mũsumbĩ wa Yuta. Amoni aĩ mũndũ mũthũku mũno na athaithaa mĩvw'anano. Ĩla wakwie, Yosia nĩwe watw'ĩkie mũsumbĩ wa Yuta, e na ũkũũ wa myaka nyanya! Wĩona Yosia ta waĩ mũthũku ta ĩthe wake?— Aiee!
Kuma e mũnini, Yosia nĩwendete kũmwĩw'a Yeova. Kwoou anyuvie andũ ala mamwendete Yeova methĩwe anyanyae make. Anyanyae asu make nĩmamũtetheeisye kwĩkaa maũndũ maseo. Amwe ma anyanyae asu ma Yosia maĩ aaũ?
Ũmwe wa anyanyae asu eetawa Nzevania. Nzevania aĩ mwathani, na nĩwatavasya andũ ma Yuta kana makakwatwa nĩ maũndũ mathũku ethĩwa maikaeka kũthaitha mĩvw'anano. Yosia nĩwamwĩthukĩĩisye Nzevania na anyuva kũmũthaitha Yeova, ĩndĩ ti kũthaitha mĩvw'anano.
Yosia aĩ na mũnyanyae ũngĩ weetawa Yelemia. Elĩ masyaĩtwe vakuvĩ ĩvinda yĩmwe, na ĩla maĩ anini mĩsyĩ yoo nĩyathengeanĩe. Yosia na Yelemia nĩmendene mũno vyũ. Kwoou, ĩla Yosia wakwie Yelemia nĩwaandĩkie wathi waĩ mũseo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ weew'aa ĩtina wa Yosia akw'a. Yelemia na Yosia nĩmatetheanĩasya kwĩka maũndũ maseo na nĩmamwĩw'aa Yeova.
Yosia na Yelemia nĩmatetheanĩasya kwĩka maũndũ maseo
Nĩ kyaũ ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kumana na Yosia?— O na ĩla Yosia waĩ o kamwana, nĩwendaa kwĩka maũndũ ala maseo. Nĩweesĩ kana anyanyae make maaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa me andũ mamwendete Yeova. Kwoou o naku no ũtate kũnyuva anyanya ala mamwendete Yeova, na ala matonya ũkũtetheesya wĩke maũndũ ala maseo!

translation:
Do you know why it's important to obey God's laws?—Many people think it's unimportant. Let me tell you about a young man named Josiah who obeyed God's laws. He was very zealous, and he made his people zealous too. Let us learn about what Josiah and his people did.
Josiah's father was called Ammon and he was a ruler of Judah. Ammon was a good man, but he allowed wickedness to spread. However, Josiah became a ruler of Judah when he was still very young! Do you think Josiah was a good ruler throughout his life?—Yes!
But most importantly, Josiah strove to worship Jehovah. He encouraged his people and his family to worship Jehovah faithfully. His family helped him to obey God's laws. What about Josiah's family?
One of his family members was Nezahaniah. Nezahaniah was courageous, and he helped the people of Judah when they were troubled by wicked things. Josiah praised Nezahaniah for encouraging him to worship Jehovah, rather than allowing wickedness to spread.
Josiah also had another family member named Jeremiah. When Jeremiah was quite young, he began to speak, and soon many wise people listened to him. Josiah and Jeremiah were very close friends. So, when Josiah grew up, Jeremiah wrote down a history of everything Josiah did. Jeremiah and Josiah discussed God's laws and worshipped Jehovah together.
Josiah and Jeremiah discussed God's laws
Isn't it wonderful to learn about Josiah?—And even though Josiah was a young boy, he cared about God's laws. He wanted his family to be like those people who worship Jehovah. So, you too can encourage your family to worship Jehovah and to care about God's laws!

Munini wa President William Ruto niwaweta unenanya ula wendeye kati wa kyama kya UDA ,ANC na Ford Kenya niwakwailya nthi ya kenya kuma kwailya ukwati,democrasia,ulusani ,thie munene ula itaetwe kati wa maundu angi.
Ainenea musyi kwake kisioni kya Karen vaa musyini wa ilovi kavindani kala wakomana na ambunge ala makukwatite mbau niwaweta uneni ula Musalia Mudavadi ula niwe ndongoi ya kyama kya ANC unenie kwi iyoo niwonanya wa kana ena mwolooto umwe ula wina kyama kiu kya UDA vala waumbula omituki nimekwithiwa maitangasa muungamo wa ngwatanio isu me nayo kwa akenya.
Oingi niwatula muti ateti amwe ala meukitia kivila kya usumbi na muno ndongoi ya kyama kya ODM Raila Odinga na kwithiwa aikunia maleve uteti wa ithokoo vala waweta muungamo wa kyama kya UDA ti kwikonya na uteti usu ayunya wito kwa inspector General wa polisi Hillary Mutyambai kumosea matambya mavyu ma miao ateti ala mekuothotheea ithokoo kati kati wa enethi kavindani ka kampeini syoo.

translation:
The principal of President William Ruto is someone who understands that the alliance between the parties UDA, ANC and Ford Kenya is aimed at uniting the country of Kenya through unity, democracy, peace, and this great thing called cooperation among various issues.
He hosted a meeting at his Karen residence with leaders from different regions and members of parliament who support him, and he stated that Musalia Mudavadi, who is the leader of the ANC party, has said that there is only one goal which is to unite the UDA party so that they can strengthen their agreement and commitment to Kenyans.
Many have criticized him saying that he is inciting violence and that the leader of the ODM party, Raila Odinga, has accused him of planning chaos, claiming that the UDA alliance cannot succeed and that he has filed a complaint with the Inspector General of Police, Hillary Mutyambai, regarding suspicious activities during recent campaigns.

text:
"Mavinda maingĩ nĩvaumĩlaa mathĩna maingĩ ũkethĩa nĩ kana mũndũ amamine, aĩle kwĩthĩwa ate mũĩkĩĩku."—Samantha, South Africa.
Nũkwĩtĩkĩlana na ndeto isu? Mavinda kwa mavinda, o ta Samantha, ithyonthe nĩtũkwatawa nĩ mathĩna. Mũndũ no amanyĩke kĩla wonaa kĩ kya vata kwosana na ũndũ ũkwĩka ĩla wakwatwa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtuma ethĩwa ate mũĩkĩĩku. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa kwĩseũvĩsya ĩsyĩtwa nĩkyo kĩndũ kĩla kya vata kwitũ, no tũtw'e kwĩthĩwa tũte aĩkĩĩku nĩ kana tũseũvye ĩsyĩtwa. Ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ ĩla andũ mamanya kana tũtwĩe tũmakengaa, mosyao methĩawa me mathũku. Kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa.
KWĨTHĨWA ŨTE MŨĨKĨĨKU KŨTUMAA ANDŨ MAEKA ŨKŨĨKĨĨA
Andũ mayĩsa kũtuma ndũũ no nginya methĩwe maĩkĩĩanĩe. Ĩla andũ maĩkĩĩanĩa, mew'aa me eanĩe. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana mũndũ ese kũĩkĩĩa ũla ũngĩ, nĩvakuaa ĩvinda. Andũ nĩmaĩkĩanĩaa ĩla matũmĩa ĩvinda vamwe kũneena maũndũ ma w'o na kwĩka maũndũ matonya kũtethya ala angĩ. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũmwe mũthũku no ũtume andũ maeka ũkũĩkĩĩa. Na ũu weethĩwa nĩ vinya mũno mayĩsa kwambĩĩa kũkũĩkĩĩa ĩngĩ.
Waakengwa nĩ mũndũ wonaa e mũnyanyau? Weewie ata? Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa waũmĩie mũno ngoonĩ o na ũkona akũvũnyanĩie. Ũu nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũeleeka. Vai nzika kana kwĩthĩwa ũte mũĩkĩĩku no kũtume ngwatanĩo yenyu ĩthela.
WATINDANY'A NA MŨNDŨ ŨTE MŨĨKĨĨKU, ŨKEETHĨWA ŨTE MŨĨKĨĨKU
Ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe weekiwe nĩ vulovesa wa University of California, wĩtawa Robert Innes, woonanisye kana 'vate nzika kũtindany'a na mũndũ ũte mũĩkĩĩku no kũtume mũndũ ethĩwa ate mũĩkĩĩku.' Kwoou kwĩthĩwa ũte mũĩkĩĩku no kũelekanw'e na ũwau ũtonya kũkwatanw'a, nũndũ o ũndũ waendeea kũtindany'a na mũndũ ũte mũĩkĩĩku kana mũkengani, now'o yĩthĩawa ne laisi kwĩthĩwa ũte mũĩkĩĩku.
Kwoou ĩkũlyo nĩ, Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ndũkalike kĩteinĩ kya kwĩthĩwa ũte mũĩkĩĩku? Mbivilia no ĩkũtetheesye. Twĩũkũlya ũsũanĩe myolooto ĩmwe yĩ Mbivilianĩ.

translation:
"Many people suffer from deep emotional wounds that can affect a person's life, leading to feelings of worthlessness." —Samantha, South Africa.
Do you identify with this feeling? From experience to experience, oh Samantha, we are affected by emotions. A person who understands every situation experiences pain when they realize they have been hurt by small things causing feelings of worthlessness. For example, feelings may be intensified by everything that happens to us, and we end up feeling worthless even when we try to intensify them. Indeed, many people who understand that we can make mistakes, often cause problems. Consider these things.
FEELINGS OF WORTHLESSNESS CAN LEAD PEOPLE TO QUESTION THEIR VALUE
People tend to let negative thoughts influence their decisions. But those who decide, are wise. It is like someone who learns from his mistake, he gains experience. People make decisions that lead others to say bad things and hide small things to avoid hurting others. This is one thing that makes people question their value. And this feeling can be very dangerous to encourage questioning more.
Are you troubled by someone who criticizes you? Think about it! They may be trying to help you improve yourself, or they may be trying to undermine you. This is something difficult to detect. See whether feelings of worthlessness lead to the breakdown of your relationships.
DEAL WITH SOMEONE WHO IS CRITICAL, FEELINGS OF WORTHLESSNESS
One study by a researcher at the University of California, named Robert Innes, showed that 'feelings of worthlessness lead to dealing with someone who is critical and making someone feel worthless.' Dealing with someone who is critical and being associated with someone who is unable to connect, or a problem that leads to dealing with someone who is critical or an enemy, often results in feeling worthless.
The point is, is it possible to tell if someone is deliberately trying to make you feel worthless? I will explain it to you. Let's look at one example from Mbivila.

translation:
The governor of Makueni County, Prof. Kivutha Kibwana, has announced that he will support a person who will succeed him in the position of governor in this county, saying he is tired of constantly fighting with others. Kibwana said that he wants his sister, Adelina Mwau, to be among those considered as a way of strengthening family ties, although she lacks the necessary skills and experience.
His supporters have accused Kibwana of joining the Wiper party which he contested under in 2017 as the governor of Makueni County.
Having spent six years in office as the governor of Makueni County, Kibwana has declared that he will no longer unite people from all counties through the Wiper party.
The governor of Makueni County, Prof. Kivutha Kibwana, has differed with the leader of the Wiper party, Kalonzo Musyoka, over whether he (Kibwana) should step down and allow someone else to become governor for another term.
Kibwana has stated that he is ready to work with Wiper as a way of supporting Kalonzo and Raila Odinga in leading this country.

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mbivilia ĩwetete ĩũlũ wa kwĩvana mwĩĩ o vandũ vamwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alivai 19:28, vala Aisilaeli meeiwe kana mayaaĩlĩte 'kwĩvana ũvano mĩĩnĩ yoo.' Ngai anengie mbaĩ ya Isilaeli mwĩao ũsu, nĩ kana amavathũkany'e na andũ ala mamathyũlũlũkĩte ala mavanaa mĩĩ yoo na masyĩtwa kana na movano ma ngai syoo. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 14:2) O na kũtw'ĩka Aklĩsto mai ungu wa mĩao ĩsu yanengetwe mbaĩ ya Isilaeli, nũseo kũsũanĩa kwa ũliku mwolooto ũla watumie Yeova aumya mwĩao ũsu.
Yo Mũklĩsto nĩwaĩle kwĩkĩwa movano kana kũsolwa mwĩĩnĩ wake?
Mĩsoa ĩno ĩatĩĩe ya Mbivilia nĩtonya kũũtetheesya kũsũngĩa ĩkũlyo yĩu:
Aka "meyanakavye . . . na kĩlĩko." (1 Timotheo 2:9) Mwolooto ũsu waĩle kũatĩĩwa nĩ aũme na aka. Twaĩlĩte kũnenga ala angĩ ndaĩa kwa kũsũanĩa ũndũ mekwĩw'a vandũ va kwĩsũanĩa ithyĩ ene.
Andũ amwe mevanaa mwĩĩnĩ nĩ kana mamanyĩke na ũvano ũsu, namo angĩ mekaa ũu nĩ kana monany'e maĩlĩte kwĩkana na mwĩĩ woo ũndũ mekwenda. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yĩkĩaa Aklĩsto vinya atĩĩ: "mwĩnengane mĩĩ yenyu ĩthĩwe nthembo ĩ thayũ, ntheu, ya kũmwendeesya Ngai, naw'o nĩ ũthaithi wenyu waĩlaa [mũtũmĩĩte ũtonyi wenyu wa kũsũanĩa, New world Translation]." (Alomi 12:1) Tũmĩa 'ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa' ũmanye nĩkĩ ũkwenda kwĩvana mwĩĩnĩ. Ethĩwa wĩenda kũatĩĩa mũtindo mũna wĩkw'o, kana kwonany'a wĩ wa kĩkundi kĩna, lilikana kana no wĩse kũalyũla woni waku, ĩndĩ ũvano ũsu ndũtonya kuma. Kũsũanĩa kĩtumi kyaku kya kwĩvana no kũtume wĩka ũtwi mũseo.—Nthimo 4:7.
"Mosũanĩo ma ala athingu maelete wingĩnĩ wa syĩndũ; Ĩndĩ kĩla mũndũ ũla wĩkalaataa ekalaataa kũvika akaĩwe tũ." (Nthimo 21:5). Ũtwi wa kwĩvana mwĩĩnĩ mavinda maingĩ wĩkawa nĩ mũndũ ekalaatĩte kana atanamba kũsũanĩa, ĩndĩ no wanange ngwatanĩo ya mũndũ na andũ, na ũkamwanangĩa wĩa. O na ĩngĩ, kumya movano asu nĩ mbesa mbingĩ, na kwĩ woo mwingĩ. Ũkunĩkĩli, vamwe na viasala ya kumya movano asu mwĩĩnĩ, sionany'a kana andũ aingĩ ala mevanĩte mĩĩnĩ, ĩtina mesaa kwĩlila nũndũ wa ũtwi ũsu meekie.

translation:
The Bible's Counsel
The Bible encourages us to love one another, as stated at Matthew 19:28, where Jesus told the Israelites to show love for their neighbor as themselves. God loves the nation of Israel, yet he also associates himself with people from all nations who love him and obey his laws. (Deuteronomy 14:2) And because Christ is part of that spiritual nation foretold to Abraham, it is right to share the good news with people of all nationalities so they can become subjects of Jehovah's Kingdom.
Does a Christian need to give up his culture or customs?
These scriptures offer practical guidance:
Avoid "adornments . . . and expensive clothing." (1 Timothy 2:9) Your appearance should be modest and dignified. Let us not be overly concerned about what others think when deciding how to dress.
Some people find it difficult to accept our standards, while others may disapprove of our way of life. The Bible instructs Christians: "Let your mode of conduct be fine, so that those observing you may see your admirable works and glorify God."—Matthew 5:16. (New World Translation) Use your "power of discernment" to determine how best to associate with others. It might be wise to avoid certain types of entertainment, associations, or places that could compromise your spirituality. Discernment is a valuable tool for maintaining your love for God and for helping you remain neutral.—Proverbs 4:7.
"The thoughts of the diligent ones certainly lead to abundance; but everyone who is in a hurry comes to poverty." (Proverbs 21:5). A person who rushes into associating with others without first discerning their qualities often experiences regret. He may become involved in bad company and suffer reproach. Moreover, hasty decisions can cause serious problems and lead to disappointment. Therefore, take time to discern the quality of those with whom you associate, and do not rush into friendships just because many others are doing so, lest you end up regretting your choice.

text:
Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Alex aendeee na kũlalamĩka ayumya makotoni ĩlolinĩ ya kambunĩ ĩla ũthũkũmaa. Eĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Yo nĩendeea kũthũkũma nginya ĩndĩĩ wĩa ũũ ũtesa kũndethya? Ngesa kũkwata wĩa ũtonya kũndethya ĩndĩĩ? Nĩthĩwa nĩendeee nesa takethĩwa ti lasima nĩthũkũme!'
O ta Alex, andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ mayendete kũthũkũma na kĩthito. Mũndũũme ũmwe ũthũkũmaa wĩa wa makanika aĩtye: "Andũ aingĩ monaa mataĩle kũthũkũma wĩa 'mũmũ.'" Aendeee kwasya: "Andũ aingĩ me o wĩanĩ methĩawa maisũanĩa kana methũkũma wĩa ũla me naw'o meteele kũkwata ũngĩ mũseo."
Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ mew'aa mataĩle kũtethya wĩa mũmũ? Nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa mew'aa ũu nũndũ wa ũvoo mwingĩ ũla makwataa isesenĩ sya maũvoo mavinda maingĩ, ũyonany'a kana thayũ ũla "mũseo" nĩ mũndũ kwĩkala e mwĩanĩe, na ate kũthũkũma wĩa mũmũ. Matthew, ũla ũtethasya wĩa wa kũseũvya na kũsũvĩa syĩndũ iikanangĩke, easya atĩĩ: "Andũ mesilasya kana mũndũ ũla ũtaendeee nesa nĩ ũla ũng'ang'anaa mũno aithũkũma nĩ kana eanĩsye mavata make." Nake Shane, ũla ũthũkũmaa wĩa wa kũsũvĩa nyũmba, e na woni o ta ũsu. Easya atĩĩ: "Andũ nĩmaekie kũthũkũma wĩa wa ĩtukũ."
Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, andũ aingĩ nĩmatanĩaa wĩa mũmũ. Daniel, ũla wĩ na myaka 25, na ũthũkũmaa wĩa wa myako easya ũũ: "No nasye kana wĩa mũmũ nũtetheeasya mũndũ aũtethya e na kĩeleelo kĩseo." Nake Andre, ũla wĩ na myaka 23, nũkwĩtĩkĩlana na ũndũ ũsu. Aĩtye: "Nĩĩkĩĩaa kana ũtanu na wĩa nikonanĩtye." Aendeee kwasya: "Ĩla mũndũ watethya wĩa mũnini kana ekala mana, ndesa kũkwata ũtanu!"
Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumĩte andũ ta Daniel na Andre, methĩwa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa wĩa? Kwa ũkuvĩ, matetheew'e nĩ myolooto ya Mbivilia. Ndeto ya Ngai ndyaĩtye andũ maikatethye wĩa mũmũ, ĩndĩ ĩmathangaasya matethye wĩa na kĩthito na mayĩthĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo. O na nĩwetete ũndũ ũngĩ eka o kũtwĩa tũthũkũme. Nĩyonanĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kũtanĩa wĩa.
Nĩ myolooto yĩva ya Mbivilia ĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũkethĩwa wĩ mwĩanĩe wĩanĩ waku? Twĩũkũlya ũsome kĩlungu kĩla kĩatĩĩe nũndũ nĩkyonanĩtye myolooto ĩsu.

translation:
One man named Alex continues to complain about being tired from working hard all night. He says: 'I will continue to work hard, why should I stop working? Is there a way to get someone to work for me? I wish I could just continue without getting tired!'
Oh Alex, many people sympathize with continuing to work hard with determination. One man who works as a mechanic said: "Many people see difficulties in working like a 'fool'." He continued to say: "Many people, if they had resources, would hire others or work in a way that allows them to acquire wealth easily."
Is it true that many people want to work like fools? It's possible some people enjoy this kind of excessive effort which leads to exhaustion and pain, or perhaps the idea of "wealth" is having someone else work for you, and also working like a fool. Matthew, who speaks about temptation and testing of faith, said: "People who stumble or a person who continues to persevere are those who have learned through hardship." And Shane, who works hard at renovating houses, also agrees. He said: "People need to work hard during their youth."
Indeed, many people admire working hard. Daniel, who is 25 years old and works as a carpenter, said: "I don't care about working like a fool, it helps me support myself and my family." And Andre, who is 23 years old, identifies with this sentiment. He said: "I agree that it's good to work hard." He continued to say: "But if someone works too much or becomes obsessed, it's important to find balance!"
What motivates people like Daniel and Andre, despite knowing that wealth is often built on the backs of others? In reality, it's a matter of biblical teaching. God's command teaches people who work hard, so they can earn a living and provide for their families. And we should appreciate this opportunity to help us work hard. We believe that something needs to be done to find balance.
Is there a biblical principle that can guide us in finding balance in our lives? Let's examine each verse carefully to see what principles apply to our situation.

text:
Selikali ya kati kwisila muveani wa kisomo niyendeka kuikithya mutalala wa kisomo wa CBC niwaila na muno isioni sya nduani
Uu waneenwa ni senator wa kaunti ya Makueni Daniel kitonga maanzo kavinda kala maovisaa anene ma kuandika alimu mevikite musyini wa wote kuneenanya na alimu anene ma masukulu kukonya mutalala uu mweu.
Maanzo niwaweta muvea wa TSC uyithiitwe wikiite kithito kila kyailye nthini wa kisomo kii Kya CBC kwa kila ukuweta kana mathina ma stima ,oundumwe na internet tawithiitwe uitunga na itina kisomo kii kwakwithya asyai nemo methitwe mavinyiiwa.
Muyumbe wa Makueni muandu Susan Kiamba aineena niwaweta vena vata wa kukwata mbau kisomo kii kya CBC kwa syana nundu nikinuenga mumanyiwa utonyi wa kwika maundu mekivathukanyo vala wenda selikali kukwatiania na asyai nikana kwailya kisomo kiu.
Kungi kauntini ya Kutui, ene ianda muviani wa kisomo meendekethya mutalatala mweu wa kisomo CBC uvyaiiwe itheka.
Aineena ivindani ya umbano wa ene ianda miviani wa kisomo ula wiivangitwe ni nzama ya kumaandika alimu TSC, muandiki munene wa KNUT uvonge wa Kitui Nding'o eweta kana mutalatala uu niuuvinyiiya alimu na asyai.
Oingi nimatulile silikali muti kwa kulea kukonya alimu muvangoni wa mutalatalani usu na makulya vethiwe na mivango myailu ya kuthaamisya alimu ovamwe na kuandika angi.

translation:
The national government through the ministry of education has directed that the curriculum of basic education under CBC be reviewed and this time around let it be sensitive to the needs of parents.
This was stated by Makueni County Senator Daniel Kitonga while speaking during a large meeting of headteachers from across the county when he called on teachers and school heads to review the curriculum thoroughly.
He further said that the TSC should provide weekly training on the implementation of the CBC curriculum for all trainers and sub-county directors, including providing computers and internet access to facilitate online learning effectively.
Makueni County Woman Representative Susan Kiamba added that there is a need to address the challenges faced by children in accessing the CBC curriculum because many parents lack the ability to afford educational materials, urging the government to intervene and support learners.
In Kutui County, the Ministry of Education has directed that the new CBC curriculum be implemented fully.
She made the remarks during a forum of area education officials led by the Sub-County Director of Education, a representative of the TSC, and the Secretary General of KNUT in Kitui, Nding'o, who noted that the curriculum is overburdening teachers and students.
Many have complained that the government is failing to provide adequate resources to schools and sufficient training for teachers, along with writing materials.

Wakeli matuku 13 mwei wa kenda ni muthenya wa uthyumuo kwondu wa kuithwa kithitu kya wia kwa president munyuve Dr. William Samoei Ruto ta president wa katano wa Kenya.
Muungamii wa uthukumi wa silikali Dr Joseph Kinyua ula niwe mwenekivila wa nzama ila ikutwaiisya iseso ya kunengeleanilya utongoi wa kivila kiu kinene vala isyitwa yake Ruto yiutumbithwa muthyani wa kyumwa ithanguni ya silikali.
Iseso ya kuithwa kithitu kwa Ruto ikatwaiiwakiwanzani kya Moi International Sports Centre in Kasarani, Ilovi, kati wa saa inya kioko na saa nyanya muthenya.
Chief Registrar wa makoti Anne Amadi niwe ukaamuithya kithitu, iseso ila ikatongoewa ni Justice Martha Koome vala munini wa Ruto Rigathi Gachagua onake ukaithwa kithitu o sua usu.
Kwii wakwambiliilya matuku atano mwei wa kenda niw'o koti wina ukumu vyu unaakumbatiilye usindi wa Ruto nthini wa unyuvani ula unatwaiiwe matuku kenda mwei wa nyanya itina wa musindani wa Ruto, Raila Odinga kunyungunyisya.
President Uhuru Kenyatta, na ula unaamukwete mbau Raila Odinga niuwetie kwitikilana na utwi wa koti wina ukumu na ateekuweta isyitwa ya Ruto niuwetie kana nzikaiyo sya kwailya kyathi kya kunengeleanilya utongoi nisyeendeeye.

translation:
The lawyer announced on November 13th that tomorrow is a day of swearing-in for the fifth president of Kenya, Mr. William Samoei Ruto.
The head of public service Dr. Joseph Kinyua, who is the chairman of the transition committee, has called for a meeting to prepare for the inauguration ceremony of President Ruto which will be held at the military headquarters.
The swearing-in ceremony for Ruto will take place at the Moi International Sports Centre in Kasarani, Nairobi, between 10 am and 12 pm.
Chief Registrar of the Judiciary Anne Amadi will administer the oath, but the ceremony will be presided over by Chief Justice Martha Koome while Ruto's deputy Rigathi Gachagua will also take the oath later.
For the next five days, the country awaits the outcome of the Supreme Court case that upheld Ruto's victory against his opponent Raila Odinga.
President Uhuru Kenyatta, who supported Raila Odinga, is expected to cooperate with the handover process and congratulate Ruto on his win, although it is unclear whether he will attend the inauguration ceremony.

Ve ngewa ĩmwe ya kĩthokoo kya mũthemba ũsu ĩandĩkĩtwe ya myakanĩ ya 600 mbee wa Klĩsto. Ngewa ĩsu yaandĩkĩtwe kĩlĩonĩ kya mbisũ kyeethĩiwe vakuvĩ na Asitoti. Ala angĩ tũnaĩ ĩmwe tũyũmbany'a ngetha syũa yĩathĩte no makũsĩĩe . . . kana kĩla naweta nĩ kya w'o. Vai ĩvĩtyo nĩkĩte. . . . translation:
Was the law of Moses given to condemn all people except those who diligently observe it among the Israelites?
No, it was given for some purpose. One scripture that sheds light on this is 2 Corinthians 3:7, 8. It reads: "If the ministry that brings death, which was engraved in letters on stone tablets, came with glory, how much more will the ministry of the Spirit come with glory! And if the ministry that condemns had glory, how much more will the ministry that acquits have glory!"
One copy of this law was written about 600 years B.C.E. This copy was written on papyrus and preserved by the Greeks. It appears that this copy condemned a man who had committed adultery and was sentenced to be stoned to death by someone who wrote it down. It reads: "The man [whose wife's thigh has been exposed] must certainly die; he has shown contempt for Jehovah, and this is what must be done to him."
But we also have another copy that acquits people of charges, even if they have committed adultery. For example: "Your husband [whose wife's thigh has been exposed] must clear himself by taking an oath, seven times, Hoshayahu son of Shobay says, and he will be free from guilt. . . . But if we do not acquit people of charges, even if they have committed adultery . . . or anything else, then it is wrong. So let it be. . . . However, let each one examine his own conscience before coming to judge the man, so that he does not become guilty himself! Let us not try to find fault with our husband while he is still alive."
A modern writer named Simon Schama says that it is difficult to know whether "this law was intended to be applied literally to anyone [who had exposed his wife's thigh]." He says that it is difficult to know "whether the fact that such a person whose wife's thigh has been exposed could clear himself by taking an oath is found in the Biblical account, and that those very laws that were given to the Israelites were later incorporated into the Laws of Livy and the Romanization of Laws."

translation: Watch how sand dams work (Kamba) Sand dams are transforming lives around the world. But how do they work? Find out in this animation. Excellent Development would like to thank Translators Without Borders for the translation of the subtitles, which are also provided here: The bed of the river Making life easier for people in dry lands For example… a dog can spend ten hours a day searching for water. Water is the biggest problem that affects and kills millions of people because of the dryness of the land but not the wetness of the earth. One well or two per year, many wells become full during the rainy season. Much water goes underground, and every drop shines like stars down there. For example, we have a project of liberation called the Wambiyaa and the Bed of the River. The bed of the river is a ditch filled with stones and cement in the middle of sandy soil… This way helps to store water in the dry land. The water from the stones filters greatly and becomes water during the rainy season. Every stone in the riverbed is built… water flows through every stone with the help of small stones. In the dry season - when there are two or three wells - the riverbed builds a riverbed. Every stone on the riverbed stores water at a rate of 25 to 40 percent. The riverbed keeps the water clean and preserves it for a long time. These stones that are called riverbeds allow people to access clean water or livestock to drink water easily. This area has enough water to fill about 40 million liters. Life now… get closer. But water is very important. Everything that grows depends on water. We spend a lot of time and effort digging and planting trees… Deforestation makes the whole country poor… and barren. Affects and kills not only those who lack water in the villages of 30-90. Children no longer go to school due to thirst. Affects spending more time fetching a lot of firewood – fruits, vegetables and food crops wither quickly and shorten the lifespan of humans and increase conflicts. You see that people in the country depend on water so much. By building a riverbed, it reduces drought by 75 percent throughout the country. That is why… the riverbed reduces poverty significantly…. one riverbed for one village.

Fernandes Barasa niwaithwa kithitu kya uthukumi ta gavana wa Kakamega vamwe na munini wake Ayub Savula , iseso yila yatwaiiwa kiwanzani kya mathau kya Bukhungu.

Ndongoi sya Azimio evo Martha Karua,Kalonzo Musyoka, Senator Ledama Olekina, muyumbe Naisula Lesuuda na Fatuma Gedi nimavikite kyathini kiu, vala Karua wamakulya maikaatuliulye ndu silikali na maseeseye mali yoo ateo mathukume me muamba nayo.

translation:
Fernandes Barasa has been summoned for questioning as the governor of Kakamega together with his brother Ayub Savula, the session having been held at the Bukhungu stadium.
Outgoing Governor Wycliffe Oparanya is leaving the session and supporting the investigation.
The governor's brother Ayub Savula said he is ready to cooperate if the county is found guilty and that Governor Barasa should not be blamed because he is his brother but they will investigate everything and the truth will be revealed.
Kilifi County Governor Gideon Abdulswamad Shariff Nasir and his brother Francis Thoya have also been summoned for questioning as governor and his brother, the session having been held at Mama Ngina.
Azimio leaders Martha Karua, Kalonzo Musyoka, Senator Ledama Olekina, MP Naisula Lesuuda and Fatuma Gedi attended the meeting, where Karua reportedly refused to speak to the media and declined to comment on the matter.
Outgoing Governor Hassan Joho stated he has nothing to say and left without commenting on the issue.

text:
President William Ruto yu easya kana ngali ya Kenya Kwanza niikwosa utongoi wa mbunge nene vamwe na ya senate.
Dr. Ruto eweta kana mo mena utalo ukilite wa ngali ya Azimio vala mendekethya muyumbe Kimani Ichungwa kwithiwa ndongoi ya aingi mbungeni nene na Aaron Cheruiyot mbungeni ya senate vala Sylvanus Osoro ayoolootwa mwanyani wa mukuni wa mutalisa wa ala aingi mbungeni, munini wake aiwetwa kwithiwa Naomi Waqo.
Ngali ya Azimio moloota Opiyo Wandai ndongoi ya anini mbungeni nene na munini wake Robert Mbui. Junet Mohammed ta mukuni wa mutalisa na munini wake muyumbe mwolooye Sabina Chege. Stewart Madzayo ayosa mwanya wa ndongoi ya anini mbungeni ya senate nake Enock Kiio ta munini wake vala senator Fatuma Dullo ni mukuni wa mutalisa wa ala anini mbungeni ya senate na munini wake senator wa Ilovi Edwin Sifuna.
Kivalua kinene ki kwa spika wa mbunge Moses Wetangula kumua utwiyo ateo no kwianana na utalo wa ala aingi itina wa kila ngali kuweta yina utalo munene mbungeni isu.

translation:
President William Ruto has easily formed the Kenya Kwanza government and appointed members of parliament and the senate.
Dr. Ruto announced that some members of the Azimio coalition have defected, including Kimani Ichungwa who was elected majority leader in the National Assembly and Aaron Cheruiyot a senator who replaced Sylvanus Osoro as the deputy speaker of the National Assembly, his sister being appointed Naomi Waqo.
The Azimio coalition nominated Opiyo Wandai as the minority leader in the National Assembly and his deputy Robert Mbui. Junet Mohammed is the deputy majority leader and his deputy is Sabina Chege. Stewart Madzayo secured the position of minority whip in the Senate and Enock Kiio is his deputy while Senator Fatuma Dullo is the deputy speaker of the Senate and her deputy is Senator Edwin Sifuna of Nairobi.
A major challenge lies with the Speaker of the National Assembly Moses Wetangula to ensure fairness and impartiality and to work with all coalitions to achieve meaningful legislation in Parliament.

NGELANY'O nĩyendetwe nĩ andũ aingĩ na nĩnengetwe ndaĩa. Ĩvuku ya The Encyclopædia Britannica yĩtaa ngelany'o "ũvano ũla mũnene wa ndĩni ya Kĩklĩsto." Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto ma w'o maitũmĩaa ngelany'o ũthaithinĩ. Nĩkĩ?
Kĩtumi kĩmwe kĩnene nĩ kana Yesũ ndaakw'ĩĩa ngelany'onĩ. Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "ngelany'o" nĩ stau·rosʹ. Ndeto ĩsu yonanasya "mũtĩ mũlũngalu kana kĩtuĩ." Mbivilia ĩngĩ yĩtawa The Companion Bible yaasya kana "ndeto [Stau·rosʹ] ndyonanasya ilungu ilĩ sya mbwaũ ikelanĩtw'e . . . Vaiĩ o na kĩndũ kyonanasya mbwaũ ilĩ nthĩnĩ wa Kĩkiliki kĩla kyatũmĩiwe kũandĩka [Ũtianĩo Mweũ]."
Aandĩki ma Mbivilia matũmĩaa ndeto ĩngĩ yĩla meũweta ũndũ Yesũ woaiwe. Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla matũmĩaa nĩ xyʹlon. (Meko ma Atũmwa 5:
Ĩvuku yĩtawa, Das Kreuz und die Kreuzigung (Ngelany'o na Kwambwa), ya Hermann Fulda, yĩkĩelesya kĩla kyatumaa kĩtuĩ kĩtũmĩwa kwamba andũ yaasya kana: "Mĩtĩ ndyaĩ mingĩ vala vanyuvĩtwe kwondũ wa kwamba andũ. Kwoou mũtĩ wenzĩlawa mũthanganĩ. Na atũli ma mĩao masũaw'a moko mambatĩtw'e ĩũlũ na maaũ namo makoveewa kana makaathĩĩwa na mĩsumaa mũtĩnĩ."
Ũĩkĩĩthyo ũla mũnene wa ũndũ Yesũ wambiwe wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aĩtye: "Klĩsto atwovoisye kuma kĩumonĩ kya ĩla mĩao, nũndũ nĩwatw'ĩkie kĩumo kwondũ witũ; nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩkũandĩkĩtwe, Nũumanĩwe kĩla mũndũ ũsũaw'a mũtĩnĩ ĩũlũ." (Akalatia 3:
Vai ũndũ wonanasya kana ngelany'o yaatũmĩwa ũthaithinĩ nĩ ala meyĩtaa Aklĩsto myaka 300 ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Yĩla Mũsumbĩ waĩ mũlei Konisitandino weetĩkĩlile kũtw'ĩka ũmwe wa athaithi ala meeyĩtaa Aklĩsto, nĩwamĩtw'ĩkĩthisye ngelany'o tayo ũvano wa Ũklĩsto. O na kethĩwa Konisitandino aĩ na kĩeleelo kyaũ, ngelany'o ndyakonanĩty'e o na vanini na Yesũ Klĩsto. Ngelany'o yaumanie na andũ matesĩ Ngai. Ĩvuku ya Katholeki (New Catholic Encyclopedia) yĩwetete ũũ: "Ngelany'o yaĩ kw'o mbee wa Ũklĩsto na nĩyonekaa kwa ala mate Aklĩsto." Andũ angĩ mawetanĩasya ngelany'o na kũthaitha syũmbe kana syĩthĩo sya alei ikonanĩtye na ũsyai.
Nĩkĩ, ũvano ũsu wa alei wambĩĩie kũtũmĩwa? Veonekana waetetwe nĩ kana alei metĩkĩle "Ũklĩsto." Ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩleanĩte vyũ na kũthaitha mĩvw'anano ya alei. (2 Akolintho 6:

The suffering was experienced by many and is remembered with affection. The Encyclopædia Britannica describes suffering as "a central feature of Christianity." Early Christians made use of suffering in their worship. Why?
One major reason is that Jesus foretold his suffering. The Greek word rendered "suffering" is stau·rosʹ. This word literally means "an upright stake or pole." The Companion Bible explains that "the term [Stau·rosʹ] denotes an oblong piece of wood lying horizontally…with a perpendicular post driven through it."
Bible writers used another Greek word to describe how Jesus died. That word is xyʹlon. (Acts 5:
The book entitled Das Kreuz und die Kreuzigung (Suffering and Crucifixion), by Hermann Fulda, explains that this led people to believe that: "Many trees were sacred because they were thought to be inhabited by gods. And so trees were adorned with ribbons and wreaths and were also kissed or embraced."
The greatest expression of God's love was Jesus' death on a torture stake. The apostle Paul wrote: "Christ purchased our freedom from the curse of the Law by becoming a curse for us; because it is written, 'Cursed is everyone who hangs upon a wooden stake.'" (Galatians 3:
Furthermore, it should be noted that the suffering of Christ was imitated about 300 years after Jesus' death. Emperor Constantine ordered that an image of Christ be made, and he had the symbol of Christ displayed on military standards. And Constantine himself believed that the image was connected with his victories through Jesus Christ. This image became popular among those worshipping God. The New Catholic Encyclopedia states: "The cross became the principal emblem of Christianity and was recognized as such by all Christians." Many people associate the image with religious devotion or superstition.
So, what is the origin of this custom? It seems to be rooted in ancient beliefs regarding trees. (2 Corinthians 6:

Ngai nĩwendaa twĩthĩwe twĩ anyanyae.
Andũ me ndũũ nĩmaeaa ngewa nĩ kana ũnyanya woo wĩthĩwe wĩ mũseo. O ta ũu, Ngai nũtũthoketye tũneenae nake, na ũu nũtumaa twĩthĩwa anyanyae. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũkeengaĩla, na mũkathi kũmboya, na ngamwĩthukĩĩsya." (Yelemia 29:12) Ĩla ũũneena na Ngai, wĩthĩawa 'ũimũthengeea, nake nũkũthengeeaa.' (Yakovo 4:8) Mbivilia ĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana "Yeova e vakuvĩ na onthe ala mamwĩkaĩlaa." (Savuli 145:18) Ũnyanya witũ vamwe na Yeova nĩwongelekaa o ũndũ tũendeee na kũmũvoya.
"Yeova e vakuvĩ na onthe ala mamwĩkaĩlaa."—Savuli 145:18
Ngai endaa kũũtetheesya.
Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Nũũ mũndũ wenyu, ũla, mwana wake amwĩtya kĩmũtũ, akamũnenga ĩvia? Kana eetya ĩkũyũ, akamũnenga nzoka? Ethĩwa inyw'ĩ ĩndĩ, . . . nĩmwĩsĩ kũnenga syana syenyu mĩthĩnzĩo mĩseo, ti mbee mũno Ĩthe wenyu ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ kũmanenga syĩndũ nzeo ala mamwĩtasya?" (Mathayo 7:9-11) Ndeto isu sionany'a kana Ngai nũkũthoketye ũmũvoyae nũndũ nĩwendaa kũũtetheesya na nĩwe 'ũkũsũvĩaa.' (1 Vetelo 5:7) O na nũkũthoketye ũmũtavye mathĩna maku onthe. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũikemakĩe kwa ũndũ o na wĩva; ĩndĩ kĩla ũndũnĩ mavata menyu nĩmatavanw'e kwa Ngai na kũvoya na kwĩsũva vamwe na kũtũnga mũvea."—Avilivi 4:6.
Andũ nĩmethĩawa na vata wa kĩ-veva.
Andũ ala masomaa mĩkalĩle ya andũ nĩmamanyĩte kana andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmonaa maĩle kũvoya. Amwe ma andũ asu milioni mbingĩ nĩ ala mataĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai, na ala methĩawa na nzika kana kwĩ Ngai. * Ũu wĩonany'a kana andũ mombĩtwe me na wendi wa kwĩanĩsya vata woo wa kĩ-veva. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩ aathime ala me na ũkya wa ngoo." (Mathayo 5:3) Nzĩa ĩmwe tũtonya kwĩanĩsya wendi witũ wa kĩ-veva nĩ kwa kũmũvoyaa Ngai kĩla ĩvinda.
^ kal. 8 Mwakanĩ wa 2012, Pew Research Center ĩla yĩ Amelika nĩyeekie ũkunĩkĩli woonanisye kana andũ 11 katĩ wa 100 ala maĩkĩĩaa kana kũi Ngai, na ala methĩawa na nzika kana kwĩ Ngai, nĩmavoyaa o na ethĩwa nĩ savalĩ ũmwe kwa mwei.

translation:
God wants us to pray earnestly.
People who sincerely seek God will find him willing to listen to their prayer. And so, let us confidently approach his throne, and he will hear our earnest prayers. He promises: "Call upon me, and I will listen to you, and I will tell you great and unsearchable things." (Jeremiah 29:12) But when praying to God, be sincere and say, 'Draw near to me, and I will draw near to you.' (James 4:8) The Bible assures us that "Jehovah is near to all those calling upon him." (Psalm 145:18) Our closeness to Jehovah increases as we continue to talk to him and get to know him.
"Jehovah is near to all those calling upon him."—Psalm 145:18
God encourages us to speak to him.
Jesus asked: "Which one of you, if his son asks for bread, would give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, would give him a snake? If you people, though being imperfect, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those asking him?" (Matthew 7:9-11) Therefore, we can be sure that God is eager to listen to us and that he 'cares for us.' (1 Peter 5:7) And he is willing to help us cope with trials. The Bible says: "Cast your burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain you; he will never allow the righteous to wobble."—Psalm 55:22.
People are comforted by heartfelt support.
Many people also find comfort in knowing that millions of others are experiencing similar feelings. Some of these millions are turning to religion, and many are finding solace in their faith. * It is evident that people instinctively seek meaningful support. Jesus said: "Happy are those who mourn." (Matthew 5:4) One way we can show our sympathy is by praying to God regularly.
^ par. 8 In February 2012, the Pew Research Center in America published a report showing that 11 out of 100 Americans believe in God, and many find solace in their faith, pray often and feel spiritually sustained.

text:
ĨTHE wa John avatisĩwe taoninĩ nini yĩtawa Gujarat yĩ nthĩ ya India myaka ya 1950 yũkĩte kũthela. John e na eĩtu-a-inyia make atatũ, na ana-a-inyia make elĩ vamwe na inyia woo, maĩ andũ makwete mũno ndĩni ya Roman Catholic, na kwoou nĩmavĩngaa ĩthe woo mũno.
Mũthenya ũmwe ĩthe wa John amũnengie valũa atwaĩe mwana-a-asa mũna kĩkundinĩ. Ĩndĩ kwakya ku, John nĩweetemie kyaa mũno akwetye kũkunũa ĩviva. Ĩndĩ nũndũ ndendaa kũvĩtĩsya ĩthe, oosie ĩtani oova kyaa kĩu kĩuwĩte, na ĩndĩ athi na maaũ atwaa ũla valũa.
Ĩla John wavikie vala watwaĩte valũa, mũka wa mwana-a-asa ũsu ũla o nake waĩ Ngũsĩ nĩwe wawosie. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩwoonie ũndũ John weetemete kyaa na amũkũlya kana no amũtetheesye. Alikile nyũmba oosa kasandũkũ kala weekĩaa syĩndũ sya kũtetheesya mũndũ aũmĩa, na ĩndĩ amũthambya kyaa kĩu na ndawa na akyova. Amina kwĩka ũu, auĩie John kyai o aendeee kũmũeea ngewa sya Mbivilia kwa nzĩa nzeo.
Kũvikĩĩa vau, kĩmena kĩla John wamenete Ngũsĩ kyaĩ kĩnambĩĩa kũoleka. Nĩvo ĩndĩ wakũlilye mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu makũlyo elĩ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ĩthe wake waĩkĩĩaa na maĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mũĩkĩĩo wake. Maũndũ asu nĩ ethĩwa Yesũ nĩ Ngai, na ethĩwa Aklĩsto nĩmaĩle kũvoya Malia. Nũndũ mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩweemanyĩĩtye kĩthyomo kya Gujarati, nĩwasũngĩie John na Mbivilia ya kĩthyomo kĩu na ĩndĩ amũnenga kala kavuku keetawa "Ũvoo Ũũ Mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ."
Ĩtina ĩla John wesie kwambĩĩa kũsoma kavuku kau eew'aa ta ĩndĩ weew'a ũw'o ya mbee. Aendie vala ve mũthembi wake na amũkũlya o ala makũlyo wakũlilye ũla mwĩĩtu-a-asa. Mũthembi ũsu athatie amũkima na Mbivilia na amũkũmũkĩa amwĩa: "Nũtw'ĩkie Satani! Mbony'e vala Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yesũ ti Ngai. Mbony'e vala yaĩtye kana ndwaĩle kũthaitha Malia. Mbony'e!" John atelemile mũno oona mũthembi ũsu ayĩkany'a ũu, na ĩndĩ amwĩa atĩĩ, "Ndikaakinyia kũũ kwakwa ĩkanisanĩ ya Katholeki ĩngĩ." Nake ndaakũkinya ĩngĩ!
John nĩwambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya na Ngũsĩ, atw'a kũũngama na ũw'o, na ambĩĩa kũmũthũkũma Yeova. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, andũ angĩ ma mũsyĩ ũsu woo nĩmeekie o take. O na kũvikĩa ũmũnthĩ ũũ John e o na ĩlanga kyaanĩ kya kw'oko kwa aũme vala weetemie myaka 60 mĩvĩtu. Ndaaũlwa nĩ ũla ũseo o ũmwe weekiwe watuma endeew'a nĩ ũthaithi wa w'o.—2 Ako. 6:4, 6.

translation:
The life of John began in a small town called Gujarat in India in the 1950s. John had three children, and his wife had another child with someone else, and they were all devout Roman Catholics, and their lives were very religious.
One day, John's life took a turn when he was accused of having an affair. Because of this, John was forced to leave his home and seek refuge elsewhere. He tried hard to clear his name, but it was difficult and he faced many challenges.
But John persevered and managed to clear his name, and the son of the woman who accused him, whose name was Ngusĩ, was the one who helped him. This son saw something in John that made him believe in him and support him. He built a house like a sanctuary where people could come to find peace, and he helped them with medicine and food. Despite all this, John continued to read the Bible diligently every day.
To understand better, John taught Ngusĩ about faith so that he would know how to live. That is why he told his son that everything he did was for the sake of his soul and to be closer to God. These things are believing that Jesus is God, and believing that Christ came to save Mary. And because his son knew Gujarati well, he helped John and the Bible with that language, and he named the book "This Good Book of Salvation."
Then John decided to start reading the book again, which he had been neglecting for some time. He went back to his faith and believed in his son, and he believed what his son said to him: "Let us reject Satan! Let us see whether the Bible says that Jesus is God. Let us see whether it says that I should despise Mary. Let us see!" John accepted this wholeheartedly, and he told his son, "I will join another Catholic church." I will join another one!
John told him to believe in God, to turn away from evil, and to worship Jehovah. At that moment, many people who were present heard and took note. And to understand this matter, John and his wife have been married for over 60 years. I am amazed by their love, which has caused them to endure until today.—2 Corinthians 6:4, 6.

Ũsumbĩki wa Ngai waambĩĩe 'kũkinyangwa nĩ Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ' ĩndĩĩ na ata? Waambĩĩe kũkinyangwa mwaka wa 607 M.Ĩ.Y. yĩla Yelusaleme yasindiwe nĩ Mbaviloni. 'Kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya Yeova' nĩkyatiiwe kĩte na mũndũ ũkĩkalĩle na asumbĩ ala masumbĩkaa kuma mũsyĩ wa Ndaviti maeka kũsumbĩka. (2 Asumbĩ 25:

Ayuti ala maĩ Yelusaleme Vendekosito Mwaka wa 33 "maumĩte mbaĩnĩ syonthe sya andũ ĩtheo wa ĩtu"?
Mũandĩki ũmwe Mũyuti wĩtawa Philo aandĩkie ũvoo ũkonanĩtye na ũla wĩ Meko ma Atũmwa 2:5-11, aeleetye ĩũlũ wa nguthu ya andũ ĩla yookie Yelusaleme Vendekosito Mwaka wa 33.
Philo aandĩkie ũũ ĩũlũ wa aeni ala mookaa Yelusaleme: "Nguthu sya andũ aingĩ kuma nthĩ, ithama syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, o na angĩ kuma ngalĩ ya umĩlonĩ wa syũa, ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa, ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ na ngalĩ ya ĩtheo mookaa kĩla ĩvinda ya sikũkũ." O na nĩwaumĩĩisye ndeto imwe kuma valũanĩ ũla watũmĩtwe nĩ Akiliva, ũla waĩ mwĩsũkũũe wa Elote Mũnene, aandĩkĩe Mũsumbĩ wa Lomi weetawa Caligula. Valũanĩ ũsu Akiliva aĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yelusaleme: "Ndũa ĩsu nene . . . nĩ mũsyĩ mũnene wa nthĩ mbingĩ, ĩndĩ ti o Yutia yoka nũndũ wa andũ aingĩ ala maumaa kw'o mavinda kwa mavinda makathi nthĩ ingĩ."
Akiliva nĩwaandĩkie nthĩ ila Ayuti mathamĩĩie nasyo nĩ Mesovotamia, ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ ya Africa, Asia Nini, Ũkiliki, na ithama sya Mediterranea. Mũsomi ũmwe wĩtawa Joachim Jeremias aisye atĩĩ, "O na kau [Akiliva] ndaaweta ĩũlũ wa savalĩ sya kũthi Yelusaleme, no nginya ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩwe weekawa nũndũ yaĩ lasima Ayuti onthe mathi Yelusaleme kwondũ wa ũthaithi."—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 16:16.
Andũ ngili mbingĩ ala maendaa Yelusaleme kwondũ wa sikũkũ sya Ayuti mekalaa va?
Veethĩawa sikũkũ itatũ kĩla mwaka ku Yelusaleme nasyo nĩ Vasaka, Vendekosito, na Mboka ya Malwanda. Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, andũ ngili mbingĩ nĩmaendaa Yelusaleme kwondũ wa sikũkũ isu, meethĩawa maumĩte Isilaeli yonthe na angĩ meethĩawa maumĩte nthĩ ingĩ. (Luka 2:
Amwe makomaa kwa anyanyae, na angĩ maikomboa nyũmba. Namo angĩ makomaa maeemanĩ ngalĩ ya nthĩnĩ kana ya nza ya ũkũta wa Yelusaleme. Ĩvinda yake ya mũthya e Yelusaleme, Yesũ akomie ndũanĩ yaĩ vakuvĩ yeetawa Vethania.
Ve myako yeethĩiwe vakuvĩ na ĩkalũ ĩla yaĩ na kũndũ kwa kũthambĩa. Myako ĩsu ĩwetawa tayo andũ ala mookaa Yelusaleme mekalaa na maithambĩa matanamba kũthi ĩkalũnĩ. Mũandĩko weethĩiwe ũandĩkĩtwe nyũmbanĩ isu woonanisye kana Theodotus, ũla waĩ mũthembi na mũtongoi wa ĩsinakoke, "aakie ĩsinakoke kwondũ wa andũ kũsomeawa mĩao na . . . aaka nyũmba sya aeni sya kũkoma na syĩ na vandũ va kũthambĩa."

translation:
Are there not many in Jerusalem who believe in God, in the year 33 CE?
One writer named Philo wrote about this incident in connection with what is said in Acts 2:5-11, describing the multitude of people who gathered in Jerusalem during Pentecost in the year 33 CE.
Philo wrote about this multitude of people who were in Jerusalem: "The masses were exceedingly numerous, so much so that they could not be contained, and some came from distant villages, others from rural areas, and others from the countryside and from abroad." And I have also found one letter sent by Aquila, the former prefect of Eleutheropolis, to Emperor Claudius, known as Caligula. In this letter, Aquila described the situation in Jerusalem: "This city is very great…it is the greatest city under the sun, except only Judea, because of the countless numbers of its inhabitants who gather together from village to village and district to district."
Aquila wrote this while Herod was still ruling over Mesopotamia, the province of Africa, Asia Minor, Syria, and parts of the Mediterranean Sea. One scholar named Joachim Jeremias stated: "But [Aquila] overestimated the capacity of Jerusalem, and therefore this matter was brought to the attention of Caesar so that he might limit the number of those coming to Jerusalem for the festivals."—Life and Times of Jesus 16:16.
How many people actually went to Jerusalem for the festivals each year?
Three times a year people went to Jerusalem, namely Passover, Pentecost, and the Festival of Booths. According to the Law, all male Israelites were required to go to Jerusalem for these festivals, and others came from other nations as well. (Luke 2:
Some stayed in tents, and others rented houses. Still others found lodging in the surrounding villages or outside the walls of Jerusalem. On the Sunday before his entry into Jerusalem, Jesus rode on a donkey called Bethany.
He sent two disciples ahead to find a donkey tied up, which they would untie and bring to him. These donkeys were used by people who lived in Jerusalem and were accustomed to riding them. The writer Theodotos, a priest and governor of Shechem, said: "He appointed Shechem as a place where people could deposit their tithes and… built storehouses and courtyards for the priests."

text:
Syana Sya Mũvũa
Wiehan de Jager
Ĩvinda ya tene na tene, vaĩna musyĩ wekalaa na ũtanu.
Mayaũkitanaa ene kwa ene. Nimatetheesyaa asyai moo musyĩ na mĩundani.
Ĩndĩ mayanengetwe mwanya wakũthi vakuvĩ na mwaki.
Maĩlĩte kũthũkũma wĩa woo w'onthe ũtukũ.
Nũndũ mĩĩ yoo yaseovetw'e na mũvũa!
Ĩndĩ mwana ũmwe aĩ na mea ma kũthi nza kwĩanĩkĩa kyeni kya sua.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩwethĩiw'e na mea asu ma kũthi nza muno. Ĩndĩ aamwanainya nĩmamũkanisye.
Ũũi! Mwana ũsu ndaatetheka. Nĩwanyinyũkie nũndũ wa ũvyuvu wa sua.
Syana sya mũvũa nĩsyakwatiwe ni kyeva nũndũ wa kwona mwanaainya ainyinyuka.
Ĩndĩ nĩmethĩiw'e na mũvango. Nĩmosie mũndo wa mũvũa ula wanyinyukie maseovya kasũni.
Nĩmosie mwanaainya kasũni mamũlĩsya ĩũlu wa kĩĩma kĩtũlu.
Na sua ĩkuuma nĩwolũkile athi kũu akwina kyeninĩ kya kĩoko.

translation:
The Rain Child
Wiehan de Jager
A story of here and there, with a beautiful dress and joy.
They gather together little by little. I will tell you a story with friends.
This story was told long ago by our ancestors and elders.
Let us remember to respect everyone at night.
Today many things have been brought about by rain!
This child had tears because of wanting to see the rainbow.
One day she was given tears so that she could see the rainbow clearly. This made her happy.
Oh! This child is very grateful. Let me show you the beauty of the rainbow.
The Rain Child was touched by sadness because of seeing a happy child.
This was given to her with a challenge. Let the rain bring joy to those who are sad.
Let the happy children run and jump over the muddy puddles.
And the rainbow shines brightly showing its colors like a precious jewel.

text:
Itina wa president William Samoei Ruto na munini wake Rigathi Gachagua kuithwa kithitu Kya wia na president ukuthyumuiya wia Uhuru Kenyatta kunengane miiyo ya utongoi na ukumu kwa Ruto, Ruto niwaathana kuthinikia maundu kivathukanyo kwailya miikalile ya enenthi.
*Dr. Ruto niwenda muvia wa kuthinikia ilovia sya maovisa ma volisi kuma uvisini wake nginya wa inspekta general wa volisi.
*Niukuthi kwoloota asili 6 kotini wina ukumu ala masyitwa moo manenganitwe na ala makaithwa kithitu Kya wia uni.
*Thoowa wa mbolea utheewe Kuma silingi 6,500 nginya 3,500 kuma kyumwa kyukite.
*Kwongela muvothi muveani wa koti kwa silingi billion itatu kila mwaka kwa ivinda ya myaka itano yukite.
*Kuvetanga kuivia mauta na mutu kila kwithiitwe kuteutethya na vandu va ou ayukilya aimi.
*Silikali yake nikunenga ndaiya uthukumi wa enenthi na vayii muthukumi wa silikali ukatwaisyaa uteti.
*Mivia ila yii ungu wa utongoi wake kunenga ndaiya mautwiuo ma koti na kuatiiya miyao.
*Vaseuvwe nzama ya kuthinikia mikovo (CBC)na matambya mailu maithinikiwa
*Uthaayukyo wa kilindi kya Mombasa.
*Kwambiiwa kwa muvia wa cooperatives ula ukailya viasala nini na kuituiika.
*Kuviinguuwa kwa masoko 20 meu vaa Ilovi.
*Amunenga president ukuthyumuiya wia Uhuru Kenyatta kianda kya kuendeeya kutongoesya makwatianio nthi ya Ethiopia na DRC Congo kutuumanya muuw'o.

translation:
The meeting between President William Samoei Ruto and his deputy Rigathi Gachagua was called to discuss matters of handover with outgoing President Uhuru Kenyatta regarding the transition of power and governance under Ruto, and Ruto pledged to prioritize issues of concern to Kenyans across all sectors.
*Dr. Ruto intends to strengthen security through police reforms under the leadership of the Inspector General of Police.
*It has been decided to allocate 6 billion shillings to agriculture while 3,500 shillings will be allocated to subsidies.
*To spend 3 billion shillings annually on road construction over the next five years.
*To investigate cases of land grabbing and ensure those affected receive justice.
*His priority is to improve the economy and the welfare of citizens, which will boost development.
*These initiatives are part of his administration's plan to address court cases and resolve disputes.
*He launched the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) review and relevant adjustments.
*The revitalization of the coastal city of Mombasa.
*A directive to cooperative leaders to explain what they have achieved and their progress.
*The establishment of 20 markets in various locations.
*President Kenyatta requested continued mediation efforts in Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo to promote peace.

text:
Wakyumwa ũmwe mũthenya, mũndũũme wĩtawa Kenneth na mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Filomena, ala mekalaa Curaçao, nĩmaendie kũkethya andũ matwaanĩte ala meemanyĩasya Mbivilia namo.
Kenneth aĩtye atĩĩ: "Twavika kwoo, tweethĩie nyũmba yĩ mbinge na ngalĩ ĩte vo. Ĩndĩ ve kĩndũ kyanzukumie nĩkũnĩe kĩveti kya mũndũũme ũsu simũ."
Kĩveti kĩu nĩkyoosie simũ na kyasya kana mũũme e wĩanĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla kyamanyie kana nĩ Kenneth na Filomena me mũomonĩ, nĩkyamathokisye malike nyũmba.
Saanĩ o isu, nĩmamanyie kana nũkũĩaa. Ĩla Kenneth wavoyie nĩ kana mambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya, mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwambĩĩe kũĩa ĩngĩ. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie Kenneth na Filomena menda kũmanya kĩla kĩũmũthĩny'a.
Mũndũ mũka ũsu ameie kana eĩvangĩte kwĩyũaa, na aekie kũandĩkĩa mũũme valũa ũeleetye kĩtumi kya kwĩyũaa ĩla Kenneth ũmũkũnĩie simũ. Ameie kana eĩw'a akw'ĩte ngoo vyũ, na kwoou mamũtavya maũndũ matonya kũmũkiakisya kuma Mbivilianĩ. Ndeto isu sya kwĩkĩa vinya nĩsyatangĩĩie thayũ wa mũndũ mũka ũsu.
Kenneth aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩtwamũtũngĩie Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũtũtũmĩa tũtetheesye mũndũ mũka ũsu wakw'ĩte ngoo vyũ, na mũno mũno nũndũ nokwĩthĩwa atũmĩie mũlaĩka wake kana veva wake mũtheu ũtũsukume kũkũnĩa mũndũ mũka ũsu simũ!" *
No twĩkũlye-ĩ, Kenneth na Filomena no methĩwe matavĩtĩtye kũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai nĩwalikĩlĩĩle atetheesye mũndũ mũka ũsu kwĩsĩla alaĩka kana veva mũtheu, ũla nĩ vinya wake wa kwĩka maũndũ? Kana Kenneth akũnie simũ no ũndũ nikũnawa tũ?
Tũyĩsĩ nesa, ĩndĩ kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana Ngai nũtũmĩaa alaĩka kũtetheesya andũ kĩ-veva. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia yonanasya kana Ngai nĩwatũmĩie mũlaĩka atongoesye mũtavany'a weetawa Vilivu akatetheesye mũndũũme Mũethiovia waĩ na ũkũmũ mũnene ũla wendaa kũtetheew'a kĩ-veva.—Meko ma Atũmwa 8:26-31.
Ndĩni syĩ kĩvathũkany'o imanyĩasya kana ve syũmbe syĩ vinya sya veva, imwe itw'ĩkĩkanaa nĩ nzeo na nĩsyo syĩkaa kwenda kwa Ngai kana isũvĩaa kĩla mũndũ. Andũ aingĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ alaĩka na kana syũmbe isu sya veva nimatethasya. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ve andũ aingĩ mataĩkĩĩaa o na vanini kana kwĩ alaĩka.
Mo alaĩka me kw'o? Na ethĩwa me kw'o, maumie va? Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa alaĩka? No maũtetheesye? Ekai twone mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu.
^ kal. 8 Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ Yeova.—Savuli 83:18.
