translation:
One day in the morning, a man named Kenneth and his wife named Filomena, who were living in Curaçao, decided to visit their relatives and friends in Mbivilia and beyond.
Kenneth said: "We have arrived here, we built a beautiful house with a gate. The only thing that bothers me is to get a gift for my wife."
That gift was very expensive and could cause problems for the family. It seemed like Kenneth and Filomena had agreed, and they started looking for a house.
Just now, I realized that I am dreaming. But Kenneth went ahead and continued searching, while his wife told him to go further. This matter caused Kenneth and Filomena to understand everything clearly.
His wife said she didn't want to die, and she asked him to write a letter to her brother bringing the reason for dying so that Kenneth would understand. She said she was afraid of being beaten, and those things made it difficult to explain to the people of Mbivilia. Today, the reason for crying is because of the words of that woman.
Kenneth said: "Let us pray to Jehovah to help us comfort this woman who is afraid of being beaten, and let Him send His angels or spirits to strengthen her mind and understanding!" *
However, Kenneth and Filomena wondered whether God really cares about comforting that woman, especially considering His ways of doing things? Or did Kenneth simply misunderstand something?
In reality, it is true that God uses angels to comfort people—spirits too. For example, the Bible says that God sent an angel to guide a eunuch named Philip to meet a man from Ethiopia and explain to him the important message. – Acts 8:26-31.
So why do bad things happen to good people, and why do some suffer despite praying to God? Many believe that angels and spirits cause suffering. But is that what the Bible teaches? Often, people blame angels when they don't understand why bad things happen.
What about angels then? And what about their role, really? Does the Bible say how many angels there are? And what do they do? Let's examine some scriptures.
^ par. 8 The Bible identifies God's name as Jehovah.—Psalm 83:18.

text:
Queen Elizabeth II niwathikwa umunthi kuya St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle ula ni muminukilyo wa kyalo kyake kya muthya kila kinaambiiye kisioni kya Westminster Abbey.
Nthi ya Britain niyamunenga ndaiya syake sya muthya Queen Elizabeth II umunthi Wakwambiliilya nthini wa kyathi kila kiivikitwe ni ndongoi kuma ikotoni inya sya nthi na makili ma andu ala metikilitwe kuvika vala Mukumya Malkia ukuthyuumuuwaa.
Ngengele ya kanisa wake ila yina ukuu wa myaka 1,000 niikunie maita 96 mataaniswe na ndatika imwe, wonanyo wa ukuu wake mbee wa misa ya akwu kwambiiya saa itano kioko masaa ma Avilika ya Umiloni wa Sua.
Mwanae mukuu na ula woseleele usumbi King Charles III, ekiite ngua sya ita sya syathi ena ainae atatu maatiiye mboya sya muthya kuma London.
Mei vamwe na mwanae Charles muukuu Prince William, mwanainya Prince Harrykati wa andu ma musyi usu wa kiusumbi.
President William Ruto na muwandu wa mbee Racheal Ruto nimavikie mathikoni asu vamwe na ndngoi ingi mbee wa maana atano ala meithoketwe vala ndongoi kuma nthi ya Russia, Belarus, Myanmar na Korea ya yiulu matathoketwe kuatiania na kwithiwa nthi ii itena mituo miseo.
Ruto niukuvika umbanoni munene wa ngwatano ya nthi UN General Assembly kuya America vamwe na ndongoi ingi 43 sya Kenya na vala meikwaatiwa kuneenea utianya wa Kenya na nthi sya nza na muno wa kiviasala.
Ruto eikwatiwa kusyoka vaa Kenya wakana ukite.

translation:
Queen Elizabeth II was laid to rest at St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle which is near her childhood home where she held her coronation ceremony at Westminster Abbey.
The British nation mourns the passing of their beloved Queen Elizabeth II today as flags fly at half-mast across the country and people gather to pay their final respects to the late Queen.
The tower of her parish church which is 1,000 years old rang 96 chimes representing each year of her life, while the great bell tolled once, signifying the magnitude of her reign as the service began at five o'clock local time during the afternoon hours of Sunday.
Her eldest son and successor King Charles III led the procession of four children from Buckingham Palace to London.
Others including her son Charles' elder son Prince William, younger son Prince Harry were among the crowd of mourners.
President William Ruto and his wife Rachel Ruto attended the funeral alongside other dignitaries from countries including Russia, Belarus, Myanmar and North Korea who were invited to attend despite strained relations with those nations.
Ruto will address the United Nations General Assembly in America along with 43 other representatives from Kenya and discuss issues of concern to Kenya and neighboring countries regarding climate change.
Ruto was received first upon arrival in Kenya yesterday.

text:
Selemeng'e nĩwendete mbaka. Nyũmba kwake kwĩ mbaka mbingĩ.
Selemeng'e ena mbaka ĩmwe nziũ. Mbaka ĩĩ nĩĩsaa nyama mbingĩ.
Selemeng'e ena mbaka ĩmwe nou. Mbaka ĩĩ ĩĩsaa kĩla kĩndũ.
Mbaka yakatatũ nĩsembea kũlĩsa mũtĩ. Mbaka ĩĩ nĩ kwamĩaa mũtĩnĩ.
Selemeng'e nũlĩsaa mũtĩnĩ. Nũkwamaa vamwe na mbaka namba itatũ. Inyaa Selemeng'e nonginya amatetheesye kũtheea kuma mũtini ũsu.
Selemeng'e e mbaka ilĩ ndulu. Sikomaa nza siyota sua mũthenya mũima
Selemeng'e e mbaka itatũ nthangaau. Nikwataa mbĩa ikonĩ ũtukũ.
Selemeng'e e ngitĩ ĩmwe. Syĩtwa yayo nĩ Lilavi. Lilavi nde anyanyae. Ethĩawa amakĩte.
Mbaka sya Selemeng'e syĩyendete Lilavi. Nimũkũaa nyũmba. Lilavi nũsembaa akai.
Selemeng'e amanthaa Lilavi na ayĩ mũete mũsyĩ. Mbaka siyĩwaa mũyo. Ityendaa kwona Lilavi ĩngĩ.
Selemeng'e e mbaka syĩana ata? E mbaka nyanya.
Selemeng'e e ngitĩ syĩana ata? E ngitĩ ĩmwe. Lilavi eva yu?
Wĩna mbaka syĩana mũsyĩ? Wĩna ngitĩ syĩana mũsyĩ?

translation:
The journey was long. His house was very far.
The journey had another distance. The distance contained a lot of meat.
The journey had another place. The place contained everything.
The third journey involved praying to a tree. The distance involved climbing the tree.
The journey involved climbing the tree. He stayed with the journey, number three. Today Selemeng'e remembers the events of climbing that tree.
The journey has a distant land. I don't know what he dreams about at night.
The journey has three locations. He carried water throughout the night.
The journey has one hill. Its name is Lilavi. Lilavi is very beautiful. She has good clothes.
The journey of Selemeng'e ended at Lilavi. He built a house. Lilavi prayed for him.
Selemeng'e loved Lilavi and gave her a gift. The journey didn't have a path. It went to see another Lilavi.
The journey, does it have children? It has a daughter.
The hill, does it have children? It has one hill. Does Lilavi still exist?
Is there another journey? Is there another hill?

text:
ĨVINDA yĩmwe kwaĩ ũmbano wa vata mũno Yelusaleme. Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti oombanĩte na anene me mbee ũsumbĩnĩ, anene ma nyũmba ya ũsumbĩ, na ngũmbaũ syonthe. Onthe nĩmatanie mũno ĩla meewie Ndaviti aimatangaasĩa ũndũ wa mwanya mũno. Amatavisye kana Yeova nĩwanengete mwana wake, Solomoni, wĩa wa kwaka ĩkalũ ĩnene mũno kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa ũla Ngai wa w'o. Mũsumbĩ ũsu wa Isilaeli, ũla ĩvindanĩ yĩu waĩ mũkũũ, nĩwaveveewe amanya ũndũ ĩkalũ yĩu yaĩle kwakwa, na ĩndĩ amũtavya mwana wake, Solomoni. Ndaviti eeie andũ asu woombanĩte namo atĩĩ: "Wĩa nĩ mũnene; nũndũ ĩ nyũmba nene mbanakavye ti kwondũ wa mũndũ, ĩndĩ kwondũ wa Yeova Ngai."—1 Mav. 28:1, 2, 6, 11, 12; 29:1.
Ĩtina wa ũu Ndaviti amakũlilye: "Nũũ ĩndĩ ũla ũnũkwĩnengane na ngoo ya kwenda evathan'ye ũmũnthĩ ethĩwe mũtheu kwa Yeova [kana "amũnenge Yeova mũthĩnzĩo," NWT]?" (1 Mav. 29:5) Keka waĩ vo we wĩthĩwa weekie ata? We nĩwĩthĩwa weeyumisye na ngoo ya kwenda ũkwate kw'oko wĩa ũsu ũnenevete ũu? Aisilaeli nĩmeeyumisye matetheesye o na mateũtindĩa. O na eka ũu, "matanie, nũndũ nĩmanenganie na kwenda kwa ngoo, nũndũ nĩmamumĩsye Yeova makyenda na ngoo mbĩanĩu."—1 Mav. 29:9.
Myaka mingĩ ĩtina wa vau, Yeova nĩwambĩĩisye mũvango ũngĩ mũseango o na kwĩ ĩkalũ yĩu. Nĩwaseũvisye ĩkalũ ĩnene ya kĩ-veva, nayo nĩ mũvango ũla wĩkĩte kwĩsĩla nthembo ĩla Yesũ waumisye nĩ kana andũ matonye kũmũthaitha. (Aevl. 9:11, 12) Yeova aendeee kũtetheesya andũ ata mew'anĩthw'e nake? Amatetheeasya kwĩsĩla wĩa witũ wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a. (Mt. 28:19, 20) Nũndũ wa wĩa ũsu, kĩla mwaka andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmatw'ĩkĩthaw'a amanyĩw'a, na ngili mbingĩ sya asu nĩmavatisawa. O na ĩngĩ kĩla mwaka ikundi maana maingĩ nĩsyambĩĩaw'a.
Nũndũ wa wongeleku ũsu, nĩvethĩĩtwe vata wa kũtumbĩthya mavuku maingangĩ maeleetye Mbivilia, vata wa kwaka na kũtũngĩĩa Nyũmba mbingangĩ sya Ũsumbĩ, na vata wa kũmantha kũndũ kwingangĩ kwa kwĩkĩa maũmbano manene. We nũkwĩtĩkĩla kana wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo nĩ mũnene na wĩ na mosyao maseo?—Mt. 24:14.
Kũmwenda Ngai na mũtũi na kũmanya kana wĩa wa kũtavany'a nĩwaĩle kũtethw'a na mĩtũkĩ nĩkũtumaa andũ ma Ngai 'menengane na ngoo ya kwenda' nĩ kana mamũnenge mũthĩnzĩo wa mĩvothi yoo. Nĩtũtanaa mũno nũndũ wa 'kũmũtaĩa Yeova na syĩndũ sitũ.' O na nĩtũtanaa kwona ũndũ mĩvothi ĩsu twaumya ĩtũmĩawa nesa nĩ kana ĩtetheesye wĩanĩ ũsu mũnene waatethw'a nĩ andũ!—Nth. 3:9.

translation:
One day David gathered together the officials of Israel at Jerusalem. King David stood up and addressed his officials and all the leaders of Israel. Then he encouraged them greatly to build a magnificent temple for the name of the Lord God of Israel. And David made preparations to build this temple, and Solomon his son was appointed to build it. For Jehovah had promised to give him Solomon his son to succeed him on the throne of Israel. The king of Israel, who had gathered them all together, rejoiced greatly, and they appointed Solomon his son to succeed him. David said to all the people who were gathered with him: "I have prospered because my God has exalted me; I have not built a house for myself, but for the Lord God."—1 Chron. 28:1, 2, 6, 11, 12; 29:1.
David asked: "Is there anyone who is willing to volunteer today to go to meet the Lord [or "to seek the favor of the Lord," NWT]?" (1 Chron. 29:5) What motivated those men to offer their service willingly? They were moved by love for God and a desire to support His work. Also, they said, "Let us rejoice and give thanks to the Lord, and let us praise Him for His wonderful works."—1 Chron. 29:9.
Many years later, Jehovah showed Paul a glorious vision. He revealed to him a large and important work that would result in praising Jesus' name among all nations. (Acts 9:11, 12) Will Jehovah continue to use others to accomplish this work? He does so by sending out missionaries to teach people about Him. (Matt. 28:19, 20) As a result, each year millions more learn about God, and many of them become disciples. Moreover, each year a great number of new languages receive translations.
In recent times, we have seen an increase in efforts to distribute literature, build Kingdom Halls, and preach in territories where large gatherings are held. Does this indicate that the time left to finish the work is short and that we need to hurry?—Matt. 24:14.
By supporting God's organization and recognizing the importance of those who preach, we help our brothers "to be zealous in their ministry" and to seek the favor of Jehovah diligently. We will then share in the fulfillment of the prophecy regarding 'making disciples of all nations.' And we will also appreciate how much the preaching work benefits people when they hear the good news!—Prov. 3:9.

Mavia ma kũthia matũmĩawa ata ĩvinda ya tene?
Mavia ma kũthia nĩmatũmĩawa kũthia mũtu wa mĩkate. Vakuvĩ kĩla mũsyĩ, aka kana athũkũmi nĩmatũmĩaa mavia ma kũthia. Ĩvinda ya tene, andũ nĩmamanyĩĩte kwĩw'a wasya wa mavia me kũthia.—Kuma 11:5; Yelemia 25:10.
Mĩsolo na mavisa ma kwasa ma nthĩ ya Egypt nĩmonanĩtye ũndũ mũndũ wathiaa aitũmĩa ĩvia ya kũthia. Ũla ũkũthia ailĩĩlaa kĩla ũkũthia ĩvianĩ ya kũthiĩa, na aitulya ndu mbee wayo na aithia akwete na moko elĩ nthio kana ĩvia ya kũthia. Athiaa kwa kũsukuma nthio mbee na ĩtina nginya akamina kũthia. Kwosana na livoti ĩmwe, nthio yeethĩawa yĩ na kĩlo katĩ wa ilĩ nginya inya. Nthio yaĩ ĩtonya kũaa mũndũ akimĩtwe nayo.—Asili 9:50-54.
Kũthia kwaĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno nthĩnĩ wa mũsyĩ na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilianĩ ve mwĩao wavatanĩte mũndũ ayosa ĩvia ya kũthia yĩthĩwe ngwatĩlĩlyo ayĩsa kũĩvwa kĩla ũtaanĩte. Ĩvuku ya Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 24:6 yaĩtye: "Mũndũ ndakaose ĩvia ya ũthia kana nthio yayo yĩthĩwe ngwatĩlĩlyo; nũndũ ũu nĩ ta kwosa thayũ wa mũndũ wĩthĩwe ngwatĩlĩlyo."
Ndeto "kĩthũinĩ" yonanasya kyaũ?
Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yesũ 'e kĩthũinĩ kya Asa.' (Yoana 1:18) Ndeto isu syonanasya kana Yesũ nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩtwe nĩ Ngai, na nĩ mũnyanyae mũnene mũno wake. O na ĩngĩ, syonanasya kĩthĩo kĩla Ayuti meethĩawa nakyo ĩla me mesanĩ maiya.
Ĩvindanĩ ya Yesũ, Ayuti mekalaa ivĩlanĩ ite vandũ va kwaĩĩa ila syavangawa ithiũũkĩte mesa ya kũĩĩa. Ũla weethĩawa mesanĩ aiya ekalaa atambaaĩtye maaũ, kyongo kĩthengeee mesa, na etw'ĩĩkĩte na kĩkokoa kya kw'oko kwa aka kamũtonĩ. Ekala ũu, weethĩaa no atũmĩe kw'oko kwake kwa aũme. Nũndũ ala meethĩawa mailyĩ mesanĩ ya kũĩĩa meethĩawa meekete na ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwa aka, ĩvuku yĩmwe yaĩtye kana "kyongo kya mũndũ ũmwe kyeethĩawa kĩ vakuvĩ na kĩthũi kya ũla weethĩawa mathengeanĩe, na kĩu nĩkyo kyatumaa awetwa ta 'wĩ kĩthũinĩ' kya mũndũ ũla ũngĩ."
Kwĩkala kĩthũinĩ kya mwene mũsyĩ kana mũndũ ũla ũthokanĩtye mbokanĩ yeethĩawa yĩ ndaĩa nene mũno. Kwoou, ĩvindanĩ ya Vasaka ya mũthya ĩla Yesũ waĩe vamwe na amanyĩw'a make, 'mũmanyĩw'a ũla wendetwe nĩ Yesũ,' ũla nĩ mũtũmwa Yoana, nĩwe waaĩĩe kĩthũinĩ kyake. Na kwoou Yoana aĩ atonya 'kwaĩĩa kĩthũinĩ kya Yesũ' nĩ kana amũkũlye ĩkũlyo.—Yoana 13:

translation:
Will people ever stop being foolish enough to worship idols?
Being foolish is making someone stumble. Every day, some people stumble over foolishness. In ancient times, people knew about the sinfulness of idol worship.—Romans 11:5; Jeremiah 25:10.
The armies and chariots of Egypt were powerless to deliver their nation from idolatry. That is why they stumbled over every stumbling block, and they carried burdens on their shoulders and stumbled while carrying them. They stumbled because they did not trust in God's power. Like a broken footstep, their footing was unstable and slippery. Their feet slipped, and they fell.—Proverbs 9:50-54.
Idolatry is something that weakens a person spiritually and emotionally, and that is why Jehovah has allowed people to stumble over idols so that they may learn a lesson. The book *Reasoning From the Scriptures* page 24:6 says: "Anyone who practices idolatry or makes an image for worship; such a practice does not please God."
What does "foolishness" really mean?
The Bible says that Jesus 'is the foolishness of God.' (1 John 1:18) What this means is that Jesus is unique and different from everyone else, and he is God's beloved Son. Also, it means that everything that the apostles taught was considered foolish by those who did not understand it.
During Jesus' ministry, the apostles went everywhere preaching the good news, but many people rejected their message. They thought it was ridiculous, and they mocked and ridiculed them. However, despite this opposition, they continued to preach, relying on God's strength. And they used what little they had to accomplish their work. For example, they would often travel on foot, using whatever meager resources they could find. But they always trusted in God to provide for them. So, the Bible says that "the foolishness of God is powerful, because what seems foolish to the world is wiser than man's wisdom, and that is why the world through its wisdom did not come to know God."
To be called "foolish" by someone or something can be very painful. However, the apostle Paul, when speaking about Jesus and his companions, said, "We are fools for Christ's sake," and the apostle John was also willing to be called "foolish" for Jesus' sake. And so John boldly declared "to know the foolishness of Jesus" is to love him deeply.—John 13:

Nĩwene aũme aa me visanĩ?— Masyĩtwa moo nĩ Mathayo, Maliko, Luka, Yoana, Vetelo, Yakovo, Yuta, na Vaulo. Aũme aa onthe maĩ thayũ ĩvinda ya Yesũ, na nĩmaandĩkie ĩũlũ wake. Eka twĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wamo.
Nĩ maũndũ meva wĩsĩ ĩũlũ wa aũme aa?
Atatũ katĩ wamo maĩ atũme ala matavanasya na Yesũ. Nĩwĩsĩ asu atatũ maĩ aaũ?— Nĩ Mathayo, Yoana, na Vetelo. Mũtũmwa Mathayo na Yoana nĩmeesĩ Yesũ nesa, na kĩla ũmwe woo nĩwaandĩkie ĩvuku yĩeleetye ĩũlũ wake. O na ĩngĩ mũtũmwa Yoana nĩwaandĩkie ĩvuku yĩtawa Ũvuan'yo. Amina kũandĩka ĩvuku yĩu nĩwasyokie aandĩka Valũa wa Mbee wa Yoana, Valũa wa Kelĩ wa Yoana, na Valũa wa Katatũ wa Yoana. Nake mũtũmwa Vetelo nĩwaandĩkie valũa ilĩ syĩ Mbivilianĩ. Valũa isu nĩ: Valũa wa Mbee wa Vetelo na Valũa wa Kelĩ wa Vetelo. Nthĩnĩ wa valũa wake wa kelĩ, Vetelo nĩwaandĩkie ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla Yeova waneenie e ĩtunĩ na asya ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ: "Ũũ nĩwe Mwana wakwa mwendwa, ũla nendeeaw'a nĩwe."
O namo aũme ala angĩ me vu visanĩ nĩmatũmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa Yesũ nthĩnĩ wa mavuku ala maandĩkie. Ũmwe woo nĩ Maliko. Nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa aĩ vo ĩla Yesũ wakwatiwe, o na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa oonie ũndũ kweethĩiwe. Ũla ũngĩ nĩ Luka. Luka aĩ ndakĩtalĩ na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa atw'ĩkie Mũklĩsto ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ.
Aandĩki ala angĩ wene vu visanĩ masyaanĩw'e na Yesũ, ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩwe waĩ mũkũũ. Nĩwĩsĩ masyĩtwa moo?— Meetawa Yakovo na Yuta. Mwambĩĩonĩ mayamũĩkĩĩaa Yesũ. O na moonaa ta waĩ na ndũũka. Ĩndĩ, ĩtina nĩmesie kũmũĩkĩĩa na matw'ĩka Aklĩsto.
Vaulo nĩwe tũũneenea wa mũthya katĩ wa aandĩki ala me vu visanĩ. Mbee wa atanamba kũtw'ĩka Mũklĩsto, Vaulo eetawa Saulo. Nĩwamenete Aklĩsto na nĩwamathĩnasya mũno. Nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kyatumie Vaulo avĩndũka na kũtw'ĩka Mũklĩsto?— Mũthenya ũmwe e nzĩanĩ, nĩweewie wasya kuma ĩtunĩ ũineena nake. Wasya ũsu waĩ wa Yesũ! Amũkũlilye Vaulo atĩĩ: 'Nĩkĩ ũũmathĩny'a aatĩĩi makwa?' Kuma ĩvinda yĩu Vaulo nĩwavĩndũkie na atw'ĩka Mũklĩsto. Vaulo aandĩkie mavuku 14 nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia, kwambĩĩa ĩvuku ya Alomi kũvika ya Aevelania.
Nĩtũsomaa Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya, kana ti w'o?—Twasoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya nĩtwĩmanyĩasya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. We nũkwenda kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ?—

translation:
Who are the twelve apostles?— They are Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Peter, James, Jude, and Paul. These twelve were sent to preach about Jesus, and they wrote his story. Let us learn their story.
Are there important things about the story of the twelve apostles?
There are three among them who were closest to Jesus. Who are those three?— They are Matthew, John, and Peter. The apostle Matthew and John saw Jesus closely, and each of them wrote a book telling his story. And also the apostle John wrote a book called Revelation. It is said that when he wrote this book, he wrote the Gospel of John, the First Letter of John, and the Second Letter of John. Also the apostle Peter wrote letters concerning repentance. These letters are: the First Letter of Peter and the Second Letter of Peter. After writing his second letter, Peter wrote the story of what Jehovah told him in a vision and how it relates to the story of Jesus: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
And also there are others who were sent to tell the story of Jesus through the books they wrote. One of them is Mark. He recounts what happened when Jesus was arrested, and he recounts what happened afterward. Then there is Luke. Luke was a doctor and he recounts what he heard about Christ's teachings.
These others who were sent to tell the story of Jesus, Jesus is the greatest. Who are they?— They are James and Jude. They believed in Jesus. And they saw him after his resurrection. Because, they witnessed his ascension to heaven.
Paul is another important writer among those who were sent to tell the story. Before he became a believer in Christ, Paul was called Saul. He persecuted Christians and harmed the church. What caused Paul to change and become a believer in Christ?— One day on the road, he had a vision of Jesus. He accepted Jesus as his savior! Paul said: 'What should I do?' After this vision Paul changed and became a believer in Christ. Paul wrote 14 books of the Bible, from the book of Romans to the book of Hebrews.
Let us read the Bible every day, shall we?—When we read the Bible every day we learn many things about the story of Jesus. Do you want to learn more about the story of Jesus?—

Syĩndũ sya tene ila syĩnzawa nthĩ niĩkĩĩthasya maũndũ ala me Mbivilianĩ?
Ũvoo wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Biblical Archaeology Review waisye kana, ve andũ "vakuvĩ 50" mawetetwe Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania, ala syĩndũ sya tene ila syenziwe nthĩ iĩkĩĩthĩtye kana maĩ kw'o. Amwe ma andũ asu nĩ asumbĩ 14 ma Yuta na Isilaeli. Katĩ wa asumbĩ asu mawetetwe ve amwe mesĩkĩe mũno ta Ndaviti na Esekia, o na ve angĩ matawetetwe mũno Mbivilianĩ ta Menaemu na Veka. O na ĩngĩ, ve asumbĩ 5 ma Misili na 19 ma Asuli, Mbaviloni, Moavi, Velisia, na Silia. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ti asumbĩ me oka mawetetwe nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia na mavukunĩ ala maeleasya ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila syĩnzawa nthĩ. O na athembi anene, aandĩki, na andũ angĩ meethĩawa na ũkũmũ nĩmawetetwe.
Ũvoo ũsu wĩonany'a kana "asomi aingĩ nĩmetĩkĩlanaa vyũ" kana andũ asu onthe maĩ kw'o. Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto nĩmawetete andũ angĩ maĩ kw'o, na ve ũĩkĩĩthyo wa ũndũ ũsu umanĩte na syĩndũ ila syĩnzawa nthĩ. Ngelekany'o ya andũ asu nĩ: Elote, Vondio Vilato, Tivelio, Kaiava, na Selikio Vaulo.
Mĩnyambũ yathelile ĩndĩĩ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ila iwetetwe Mbivilianĩ?
O na kau nthĩnĩ wa ĩla yaĩ Nthĩ ya Watho kũiĩ mĩnyambũ ũmũnthĩ, ve Maandĩko ta 150 ala monanasya nesa kana aandĩki ma Mbivilia nĩmeesĩ mĩnyambũ. Kũndũ kwingĩ Mbivilianĩ mĩnyambũ ĩwetetwe kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o, ĩndĩ kwĩ maandĩko amwe monanĩtye andũ makomanie na mĩnyambũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Samusoni, Ndaviti, na Mbenaia, nĩmoowaie mĩnyambũ. Ĩvinda ya tene, mũthemba wa mĩnyambũ yeetawa Asiatic (Panthera leo persica) yeethĩawa nthĩ sya Asia Minor, na Greece nginya Palestine, Syria, Mesovotamia, na northwest India. WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Mwĩĩtu wĩtawa Heather ethĩĩtwe e ndũũ na Mike kwa ĩvinda ya myei ĩlĩ, na esũanĩa kana nũmwĩsĩ nesa vyũ. Maandĩkanĩaa mesengyi kĩla ĩvinda, o na nĩmaneenaa simũnĩ masaa maingĩ, na nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ ya ũla ũngĩ o na atanesa kũkĩweta! Ĩndĩ yu ve ũndũ ũngĩ Mike ũkwenda.
Myei ĩsu ĩlĩ mĩvĩtu, ũndũ ũla mũnene Mike na Heather maaĩka nĩ kũthi makwatene moko na kũkũnana kisi o vanini. Heather ndekwenda kwĩka ũndũ ũvĩtũkĩte maũndũ asu. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ndeenda ndũũ yake na Mike ĩithela nũndũ Mike nũmwendete na atumaa Heather ew'a e mwĩanĩe. Na ti ũu w'oka, Heather esũanĩa kana we na Mike nĩmendanĩte.
Ethĩwa nũvikĩtye myaka ĩla mũndũ wĩthĩawa atonya kũtuma ndũũ, na ũikwatwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũũ wamũkwatie Heather, ũtonya kwĩka ata?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Mũndũ akalĩsa mũtĩnĩ na ayĩyĩkya aũlũke ta kasũni, vethĩwa vailyĩ ata? Vate nzika no aũmĩe. Ũu now'o vatonya kwĩthĩwa vailyĩ mũndũ akalea na ngũlũ mwolooto wa mwĩkalĩle, kwa ngelekany'o, ta mwolooto ũla waĩtye, 'Ĩvathanei na ũlaalai.'—1 Athesalonika 4:3.
Mũndũ atonya kũkwatwa nĩ thĩna mwaũ nũndũ wa kũlea kũatĩĩa mwĩao ũsu? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũla wĩkaa ũlaalai eyĩkaa mwĩĩ wake mwene naĩ." (1 Akolintho 6:18) Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ndeto isu nĩ sya w'o?
Asomi maasyaa kana andũ aingĩ ma mũika ala mamanyanaa kĩ-mwĩĩ matanamba kũtwawa kana kũtwaana nĩmatonya kũkwatwa nĩ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ aa me vaa ĩtheo kana makakwatwa nĩ maingangĩ.
KŨŨMĨA MŨNO NGOONĨ. Andũ aingĩ ma mũika ala mekĩte ũlaalai maasyaa kana ĩtina wa kwĩka ũu nĩmeelilile mũno.
KŨEKA KŨĨKĨĨA ŨLA ŨNGĨ. Ĩtina wa mũndũ kwĩka ũlaalai na ũngĩ, kĩla ũmwe woo ambĩĩa kwĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Ethĩwa eekie ũlaalai na ũngĩ ũũ?'
KŨKW'A NGOO. Eĩtu aingĩ methĩawa mayendeew'a nĩ mũndũũme ũla ũtonya kũmasũvĩa, ĩndĩ ti amatũmĩe naĩ na aimatia. Na aũme aingĩ maasyaa kana ti laisi kwendeew'a nĩ mũndũ mũka ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa makome ĩmwe ĩla mamũkũlya.
Ũndũ ũla wa vata: Weetĩkĩla kwĩka ũlaalai, wĩthĩawa weevũthya mũno kwa kũnengane mũthĩnzĩo wa vata vyũ. (Alomi 1:24) Mwĩĩ waku nĩ wa vata mũno ũkethĩa ti wa kũnenganwe oou!
Onany'a kana nũtw'ĩte vyũ kwĩsiĩĩa kwa 'kwĩvathana na ũlaalai.' (1 Athesalonika 4:3) Na ĩndĩ ethĩwa ũkatwaana kana ũtwawe ĩvinda yũkĩte, ũkakwata mũndũ wa kũmanyanaa nake kĩ-mwĩĩ. Na ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũtanĩa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ ũte na nzika, ũte kwĩlila, na ũte kũkĩa kũkwatwa nĩ maũndũ mathũku ala mavinda maingĩ makwataa andũ ma mũika ala meeka ũlaalai.—Nthimo 7:22, 23; 1 Akolintho 7:3.
WE WĨONA ATA?
Mũndũ ũkwendete vyũ no eke ũndũ ũtonya kũkũũmĩsya ngoonĩ kana mwĩĩ?
Kwa w'o mũndũ ũkwendete no aũtate wĩke ũndũ ũtonya kwananga ngwatanĩo yaku na Ngai?—Aevelania 13:4.

Andũ amwe masũanĩaa kana mũndũ aivoya ethĩawa ayananga saa na mboya syake iyĩthĩawa syĩthukĩĩw'e. O na angĩ nĩmavoyaa, ĩndĩ monaa mboya syoo iteũsũngĩwa. Mũndũ ũmwe ũtaĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai asũanĩie ũndũ Ngai ũtonya kwĩthĩwa ailyĩ, na ũu watuma avoya atĩĩ: "Nĩenda o kwĩw'a kawasya kaku kanini." Ĩndĩ ĩtina esie kwasya kana Ngai "avindisye ki."
Mbivilia ĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana Ngai e vo, na nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya. Ngai atavisye andũ make ndeto ii syĩ Mbivilianĩ: "[Ngai] akakwĩka nesa ũndũ wa wasya wa kĩĩo kyaku; yĩla wĩĩw'a akakũsũngĩa." (Isaia 30:19) O na ve mũsoa ũngĩ Mbivilianĩ waĩtye atĩĩ: "Mboya ya ũla mũlũngalu nĩ ũtanu wake [Ngai]."—Nthimo 15:8.
Yesũ nĩwavoyie Ĩthe wake, "na eethukĩĩw'a."—Aevelania 5:7
O na ĩngĩ Mbivilia yĩ na ngelekany'o sya andũ mavoyie, na mboya syoo syeethukĩĩw'a. Mũsoa ũmwe waĩtye kana Yesũ nĩwamũvoyie "ũla waĩ atonya kũmũtangĩĩa" na "eethukĩĩw'a." (Aevelania 5:7) Ngelekany'o ingĩ sya andũ mavoyie na meethukĩĩw'a syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Ndanieli 9:21 na 2 Mavinda 7:1.
Kwoou, nĩkĩ andũ amwe monaa mboya syoo iteũsũngĩwa? Nĩ kana mboya sitũ isũngĩwe, no nginya tũvoye kwa Ngai ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ, Yeova, * ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kũvoya ngai ingĩ kana aaũmae maitũ. O na ĩngĩ Ngai nĩwendaa tũvoye "kwĩanana na kwenda kwake," na ũu nĩ kwasya kana twaĩle kũvoya maũndũ ala Ngai wĩtĩkĩlĩte. Ngai atũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana twavoya kwosana na kwenda kwake, "nũtwĩw'aa." (1 Yoana 5:14) Kwoou, nĩ kana mboya sitũ syĩthukĩĩw'e nĩtwaĩle kũmũmanya Ngai ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ na tũyĩmanyĩsya kwenda kwake.
Andũ aingĩ maĩkĩaa kana mboya ti o kĩthĩo kya ndĩni tũ, ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya, na aisũngĩa. Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Isaac kuma Kenya, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Navoyie Ngai andetheesye kũelewa Mbivilia. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ mũndũ ũmwe nĩwanthokeie na anenga ũtethyo ũla nendaa." Nake Hilda, kuma Philippines, nĩwendaa kũeka kũnyw'a sikala. Ĩtina wa kũtata kwa ĩvinda yĩana ũna, mũũme wake amwĩie ũũ ĩla woonie kana nũemetwe nĩ kũeka: "Yo tyo ũmũvoye Ngai akaũtetheesya?" Nĩweethukĩĩisye ũtao wa mũũme. Aĩtye: "Naseng'ie mũno ũndũ Ngai wasũngĩie mboya yakwa. Nĩnaekie kwendeew'a nĩ kũnyw'a sikala na naekana nasyo vyũ."
Yo Ngai no ethĩwe endaa kũũtetheesya maũndũnĩ ala ũthĩnĩkĩaa na mosanĩte na kwenda kwake?

translation:
Some people grieve or a person rejoices when they hear news and share it with others. And sometimes those who rejoice, I see them sharing good news. A person does not know whether God will answer their prayer when they pray, and He sends someone to tell them: "Go and tell the great nation." It is important for us to know that God "hears."
I have learned that God hears, and He answers prayers. God has spoken to His people thus in Revelation: "[God] will wipe away tears from every face; then they will be ashamed of their shame." (Isaiah 30:19) And yet some people in Revelation said: "The cry of the poor reaches [God]."—Psalm 15:8.
Jesus wept, "and was heard."—Hebrews 5:7
And also the Bible has examples of people who wept, and their prayers were answered. Someone said that Jesus "prayed earnestly" and "was heard." (Hebrews 5:7) Other examples of people who prayed and were answered are found in Daniel 9:21 and 2 Kings 7:1.
So, why do some people not have their prayers answered? It is because if we do not obey God what is written in the Bible, Jehovah, then we should not expect Him to answer our prayers anymore. And also God wants us to obey "His command," and this means that we should do what God approves. God tells us that if we obey His command, "we shall live." (1 John 5:14) So, if our prayers are not answered it is because we do not know God what is written in the Bible and we do not practice His command.
Many people think that prayer is just something we do, but God hears prayers, and He answers them. One brother named Isaac from Kenya said: "I prayed to God to help me understand the Bible. After much study someone helped me and explained the truth." Also Hilda, from the Philippines, wanted to stop smoking. After praying constantly her husband asked her the question she had been asking herself: "Will you pray to God to help you?" She realized the importance of her husband's words. She said: "I prayed earnestly that God would help me quit smoking. I felt strength to stop smoking and I succeeded."
Why does God sometimes seem not to hear our prayers when we ask for things that worry us and concern us?

Nĩwĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũmew'a asyai maku?— Mavinda amwe ũyĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi. Nĩwĩsĩ kana Yesũ nĩweew'aa Yeova na asyai make?— Ngelekany'o yake nĩtonya ũkũtetheesya ũmew'e asyai maku o na ethĩwa kwĩka ũu ti ũndũ wĩ laisi. Eka twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa twĩ ewi.
Mbee wa kũka kũũ nthĩ, Yesũ ekalaa ĩtunĩ e na Ĩthe wake Yeova. Ĩndĩ ĩla waĩ vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ Yesũ aĩ na asyai meetawa Yosevu na Meli. Nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ Yosevu na Meli matw'ĩkie asyai ma Yesũ?—
Yeova nĩwathamisye thayũ wa Yesũ kuma ĩtunĩ na awĩkĩa ĩvunĩ ya Meli nĩ kana asyawe vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Kĩu kyaĩ kyama! Yesũ ekalile ĩvunĩ ya Meli o ta syana ila ingĩ. Ĩtina wa myei vakuvĩ kenda, Yesũ nĩwasyaiwe. Ũu nĩw'o Meli na mũũme wake Yosevu matw'ĩkie asyai ma Yesũ vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Ĩla Yesũ waĩ na myaka 12, nĩweekie ũndũ ũmwe ũla woonanisye kana nĩwamwendete Ĩthe wake Yeova. Eekie ũndũ ũsu ĩla we na asyai make maendie Yelusaleme kwondũ wa sikũkũ ya Vasaka. Yelusaleme nĩ ndũa yaĩ kũasa mũno. Menũkĩte, Yosevu na Meli nĩmamũmanthie Yesũ aa. Nĩwĩsĩ aĩ va?—
Nĩkĩ Yesũ waĩ ĩkalũnĩ?
Yosevu na Meli nĩmasyokie na mĩtũkĩ Yelusaleme na mamũmantha Yesũ kĩla vandũ, na mayaamwona. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwamatelemilye mũno. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ, mamwĩthĩa ĩkalũnĩ! Nĩwĩsĩ nĩkĩ Yesũ waĩ ĩkalũnĩ?— Nũndũ vu aĩ atonya kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ĩthe wake, Yeova. Nĩwamwendete Yeova na endaa emanyĩsye ũndũ ũtonya kũmũtanĩthya. Ĩla Yesũ weanie atw'ĩka mũndũ mũima, nĩwamwĩw'aa Yeova mavinda onthe. Nĩwamwĩw'aa o na ethĩwa kwĩka ũu waĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya, kana ũtonya kũtuma athĩna. Yesũ nĩwamew'aa asyai make, Yosevu na Meli?— Mbivilia yaĩtye nĩwamew'aa.
Ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na Yesũ?— Nĩwaĩle kũmew'a asyai maku o na ĩla ũte ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩka ũu. Ũkamew'aa asyai maku?—

translation:
How wonderful it is to learn about God's love—to know that He cares for us! Some people wonder how it is possible for God to care for us. Don't we deserve to earn His love? Let us think about what the Bible teaches us about this.
First, let us remember that Jesus lived on earth and pleased Jehovah. The Bible tells us that during his life Jesus had loyal friends named Joseph and Mary. Do you wonder how Joseph and Mary felt when they learned about Jesus?—
Jehovah blessed Jesus with parents who loved him and were willing to help Mary raise him. It was amazing! Jesus grew up helping Mary, but he did not forget his Father. As time went on, Jesus became strong. This is why Joseph and Mary were so proud of Jesus.
When Jesus was 12 years old, something happened that showed he was devoted to his Father, Jehovah. He traveled with his parents to Jerusalem for the Passover celebration. Jerusalem was a busy city. But, Joseph and Mary lost sight of Jesus. Do you wonder where he was?—
Was Jesus worried?
Joseph and Mary searched everywhere in Jerusalem and finally found Jesus among the teachers, and they were relieved. What they heard amazed them. After three days, they found him! Do you wonder what Jesus was doing?— He was listening to the teachers and asking questions, showing his devotion to Jehovah. He loved Jehovah and wanted to learn everything he could about pleasing Him. Although Jesus was still a young boy, he always put Jehovah first. Did Jesus please his parents, Joseph and Mary?— The Bible says that he did.
What can you learn from Jesus?— You can learn to love God and to show that you value His teachings. Do you try to do that?—

SYĨNDŨ syonthe nzeo ila twĩnasyo syumĩte kwa Ngai. We nĩwoombie syũa yĩtũnengae kyeni mũthenya, na mwei na ndata nĩ kenda twĩthĩawe na kyeni kĩnini ũtukũ. Na Ngai nĩwoombie nthĩ tũtũae vo.
Syũa, mwei, ndata na nthĩ tisyo syĩndũ sya mbee kũmbwa nĩ Ngai. We nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kyoombiwe mbee? Mbee Ngai oombie syũmbe ivw'anene nake. Ithyĩ tũitonya kũsyona, o tondũ tũtatonya kũmwona Ngai. Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia syũmbe isu syĩtawa alaĩka. Ngai oombie alaĩka mekalae nake ĩtunĩ.
Mũlaĩka wa mbee ũla Ngai woombie aĩ wa mwanya mũno. We aĩ Mwana wa mbee wa Ngai, na atethasya wĩa vamwe na Ĩthe wake. We atetheeisye Ngai kũmba syĩndũ ila ingĩ syonthe. Nĩwamũtetheeisye kũmba syũa, mwei, ndata o na nthĩ ĩno yaitũ.
Nthĩ yailyĩ ata ĩvinda yĩu? Mwambĩlĩĩlyonĩ vayaĩ ũmwe waĩ atonya kwĩkala ĩũlũ wayo. Vayaĩ kĩndũ o na kĩmwe ate o ũkanga ũmwe mũnene wavw'ĩkĩte nthĩ yonthe. No Ngai endaa andũ matũe ĩ nthĩ. Kwoou nĩwambĩĩie kwalany'a maũndũ kwondũ witũ. We eekie ata?
Mwambĩlĩĩlyonĩ nthĩ nĩyendaa kyeni. Kwoou Ngai nĩwatumie kyeni kya syũa kĩmulĩka nthĩ. Amĩseũvisye nĩ kenda kwĩthĩawe na ũtukũ na mũthenya. Ĩtina wa vau Ngai nĩwatumie nthĩ nyũmũ ĩthambalala ĩũlũ wa ũkanga.
Mbeenĩ vayaĩ kĩndũ o na kĩmwe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Yailyĩ ta visa ũũ ũkwona vaa. Vayaĩ malaa kana mĩtĩ o na nyamũ. O na vayaĩ makũyũ maũkanganĩ. Ngai aĩ na wĩa ũngĩ mwingĩ wa kũmĩtw'ĩkĩthya nthĩ vandũ vaseo va kwĩkalwa nĩ nyamũ na andũ.
Yelemia 10:12; Akolosai 1:15-17; Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:1-10.
Makũlyo
- Syĩndũ ila nzeo syonthe syaumie va, na no ũtonye kũweta imwe?
- Nĩ kyaũ kĩla Ngai wambie kũmba mbee?
- Nĩkĩ mũlaĩka wa mbee waĩ wa mwanya mũno?
- Kwaelesya ũndũ nthĩ yailyĩ mwambĩlĩlyonĩ. (Sisya visa.)
- Ngai ambĩĩie ata kwalany'a nthĩ nĩ kenda yĩkalwe nĩ nyamũ na andũ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Yelemia 10:12.
Nĩ ndaĩa syĩva sya Ngai syonanĩtw'e kwĩsĩla wũmbinĩ wake? (Isa. 40:26; Alo. 11:33)
- Soma Akolosai 1:15-17.
Yesũ aĩ na kĩanda kyaũ nthĩnĩ wa wũmbi, na ũndũ ũsu waĩlĩte ũtuma twĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wake? (Ako. 1:15-17)
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:1-10.
Nthĩ yaumie va? (Mwa. 1:1)
Nĩ ata kweekĩkie mũthenya wa mbee wa wũmbi? (Mwa. 1:3-5)
Kwaelesya ũndũ kweethĩiwe mũthenyanĩ wa kelĩ wa wũmbi. (Mwa. 1:7, 8)

translation:
A story about yesterday, but we remember well before God. And we request a good day today, and evening and tomorrow we will be helped by a great spirit tonight. And God requests that we say so.
Day, evening, tomorrow and spirit are stories told by God. And is it possible everything requested is true? God answers very clearly. Let us strive to hear, so that we may see God. The spirits of the Bible tell stories like this. God answers those who trust him truly.
The angel of truth is the one God sends with a special message. And he is the Son of truth of God, and he shows people the way with his power. He showed God how to love everything. I will show him how to love day, evening, tomorrow and this spirit of ours.
Does this spirit have any strength? Perhaps someone can become their own leader. Someone does something and another does something else, yet they both become one great person who understands everything. But God created many people with this spirit. Tell me what I should do to understand things properly. And is there anything else?
Perhaps the spirit goes somewhere. Tell me God sent a message about this spirit. I felt greatly helped by night and morning. The power of God sent this spirit everywhere, like a large blanket.
People do something and another thing with this spirit. It has been seen that they eat food. They eat meat or vegetables. Or they make mistakes. God has many ways of helping us understand this spirit and people live peacefully with food and others.
Jeremiah 10:12; Colossians 1:15-17; Revelation 1:1-10.
Questions
- This story from yesterday, did it happen, and can you believe it?
- What does God tell you about truth?
- Who is the angel of truth with a special message?
- Explain this spirit which has been talked about. (Think carefully.)
- Does God tell you anything about this spirit being lived with peacefully with food and others?
Further Questions
- Read Jeremiah 10:12.
Is the power of God enough to help us understand his purpose? (Isa. 40:26; Hos. 11:33)
- Read Colossians 1:15-17.
Did Jesus have a beginning of creation, and does this fact cause us to worship him more fully? (Col. 1:15-17)
- Read Revelation 1:1-10.
What was revealed? (Rev. 1:1)
Can we experience the morning of our creation? (Rev. 1:3-5)
Explain what happened in the morning of the first creation. (Rev. 1:7, 8)

text:
Yeova Ngai nĩwe ũtusaa nĩ mwĩkalĩle wĩva waĩle, na nĩ wĩva ũtaĩle. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwaĩtye kana mũtwaano ti ngwatanĩo ya kavinda, ĩndĩ ala matwaana maĩle kwĩkalany'a nginya kĩkw'ũ. (Mt 19:4-6, 9) Nũleanĩte na mĩkalĩle yonthe ĩkonanĩtye na ũlaalai. (1Ako 6:9, 10) O na nũnengete andũ make myolooto ya kũmatongoesya nthĩnĩ wa mĩkĩĩle na kwĩyanakavya ĩla ĩmavathũkanasya na andũ aangĩ.—Kũt 22:5; 1Tim 2:9, 10.
Ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ nĩmaleanĩte na myolooto ya Yeova. (Alo 1:18-32) Monaa maĩle kũatĩĩa kĩla kyendetwe nĩ andũ aingĩ maũndũnĩ ta mĩkĩĩle na kwĩyanakavya na mwĩkalĩle. Aingĩ makumasya mĩkalĩle yoo mĩvuku na matindĩaa kumany'a ala mate mĩtuo mĩthũku tamo.—1Vet 4:3, 4.
Ithyĩ, twĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, nĩtwaĩle kũtetea na ũkũmbaũ myolooto ya Yeova ya mwĩkalĩle. (Alo 12:9) Twaĩle kwĩka ũu ata? Nĩ kwa kũtũmĩa ũĩ tũtavye angĩ kĩla Yeova wĩtĩkĩlĩtye. O na twĩkĩte ũu, no twaĩle kũatĩĩa vyũ myolooto ĩsu thayũnĩ witũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla tũũnyuva kĩla tũkwĩkĩa na ũndũ tũkwĩyanakavya, no twĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Motwi ala ngwĩka maũndũnĩ asu meonany'a nĩatĩĩaa myolooto ya Yeova-ĩ, kana nĩ ĩla ya nthĩ ĩno? Andũ masisya mwĩkĩĩle wakwa na ũndũ ngwĩyanakavya, nĩmambonaa ta nĩ Mũklĩsto ũmũkĩaa Ngai?' Kana ĩla tũũnyuva ivĩndĩ kana sinema sya kwĩloela, no twĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'We Yeova no etĩkĩlane na kĩndũ kĩĩ ngwenda kwĩloela? Nĩ mwĩkalĩle ũilyĩ ata ũũkumw'a kĩvĩndĩnĩ kana sinemanĩ ĩla ngwĩloela? Kĩla ngũnyuva kwĩtanĩthya nakyo nĩkĩtonya kũtuma wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũleana na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku? (Sav 101:3) No kĩluluutĩkye andũ ma mũsyĩ kana o angĩ?'—1Ako 10:31-33.
Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno tũtetee myolooto ya Yeova ya mwĩkalĩle? Nũndũ o mĩtũkĩ Klĩsto Yesũ nũkwananga mbaĩ na aiveta ũthũku w'onthe vyũ. (Esek 9:4-7) No ala mekaa kwenda kwa Ngai makatiwa. (1Yoa 2:15-17) Kwoou ekai tũtetee myolooto ya Yeova ya mwĩkalĩle nĩ kana ala mekwona mwĩkalĩle witũ mũseo mamũkumye Ngai.—1Vet 2:11, 12.
SISYAI VITIO, ĨTHĨWA WĨ MŨNYANYA WA YEOVA—MŨNDŨŨME NA MŨNDŨ MŨKA NĨMO MAĨLE KŨTWAANA, NA ĨNDĨ MŨINEENEA MAKŨLYO AA MAATĨĨE:
Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Yeova thayũnĩ witũ?
Nĩkĩ asyai maĩle kwambĩĩa kũmanyĩsya syana syoo myolooto ya Yeova ya mwĩkalĩle kuma syĩ nini?
Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva amũika na ala akũũ matonya kũtetheesya andũ aangĩ matetheke nĩ wĩkwatyo ũla Ngai ũtũnengete?

translation:
Jehovah God is the One who created us from the beginning, and He created marriage. For this reason, I ask whether a disagreement is not a violation of God's law, damaging the beautiful relationship between husband and wife. (Mt 19:4-6, 9) Be busy with all good works that harmonize with righteousness. (1Co 6:9, 10) And I urge you brothers to conduct yourselves in a way that commends the truth about our ministry and avoids giving outsiders an excuse to speak against us.—Tit 2:5; 1Ti 2:9, 10.
Many people appreciate Jehovah's standards. (Ac 1:18-32) Remember that it is important to imitate the fine example set by others in connection with their ministry and conduct. Many have ruined their lives and brought reproach on themselves because they did not fully investigate matters.—1Pe 4:3, 4.
Truly, we servants of Jehovah want to defend and uphold Jehovah's standard for marriage. (Ac 12:9) Can we do so? Yes, by using discernment in everything we say and do, showing that Jehovah is precious to us. And when we do so, we will be able to support the truth more effectively. For instance, when we come across something questionable in what we read or see, we should ask ourselves: "Is this really in harmony with Jehovah's standards, or is it influenced by this wicked world?" People may question our motives and actions, wondering, 'Are these Christians truly representing God?' Or when we encounter violence in news reports or movies, we should ask ourselves: 'Does Jehovah approve of such things? Is there anything in this entertainment that could corrupt my thinking or lead me astray?' When we examine such matters carefully, we can avoid being influenced by what is morally unclean. (Ps 101:3) And we can continue to please Jehovah.—1Co 10:31-33.
So how can we defend Jehovah's standard for marriage? By following the example of Jesus Christ, who strongly condemned immorality and upheld God's law. (Eze 9:4-7) And by keeping our conduct fine in the eyes of God. (1Jo 2:15-17) We show our zeal for defending Jehovah's standard for marriage when we put spiritual interests first and foremost in our lives.—1Pe 2:11, 12.
QUESTIONS FOR DISCUSSION, A TALK BASED ON THE BIBLE—TO HELP ALL TO REASON THINGS OUT AND TO EXPRESS THEMSELVES CLEARLY:
How can we show that we value Jehovah's standards?
What practical steps can we take to protect ourselves from the influence of Satan's world on our view of Jehovah's standard for marriage?
Why is it important to discern what is acceptable to God and what is not?

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mbivilia ndĩwetete ĩla Yesũ wasyaiwe, o na ndĩwetete kana nĩtwaĩle kũtanĩa kũsyawa kwake. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩandĩkĩtwe nĩ McClintock na Strong yaĩtye: "
Vaiĩ vandũ Mbivilianĩ vaĩtye tũtanĩe Kĩlisimasi, o na ũndũ ũsu ndwonanĩtw'e ũtianĩonĩ mweũ."
Ĩndĩ ũkunĩkĩli wĩonany'a kana Kĩlisimasi yaumanie na syĩthĩo sya ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana nĩtũmũthatasya Ngai yĩla twamũthaitha na nzĩa ũtetĩkĩlĩte.—Kuma 32:5-7.
Vala syĩthĩo ikonetye Kĩlisimasi syaumie
Kũtanĩa mũthenya wa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ: "
Aklĩsto ma mbee mayatanĩaa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ nũndũ moonaa kũtanĩa kũsyawa kwa mũndũ o na wĩva kumanĩte na ũmanyĩsyo wa ndĩni sya ũvũngũ."—The World Book Encyclopedia.
Matukũ 25, Mwei wa 12: Vai vandũ vonanĩtw'e kana Yesũ asyaiwe matukũ asu. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa atongoi ma ndĩni manyuvie mũthenya ũsu nĩ kana wosane na ĩvinda ya mbevo yĩla sikũkũ sya ndĩni sya ũvũngũ syeekawa.
Kũnengane mĩthĩnzĩo, kũĩsanĩa, na kũtana vamwe: Ĩvuku The Encyclopedia Americana yaĩtye: "
Saturnalia, ĩla yaĩ sikũkũ ya Alomi na yeekawa Mwei wa ĩkũmi na ilĩ wĩ katĩkatĩ, nĩyo yaumĩlilye maũndũ maingĩ ala mekawa andũ maitanĩa Kĩlisimasi. Kwa ngelekany'o, maũndũ ta kwĩyũmbanĩsya sikũkũ nene, kũnengane mĩthĩnzĩo, na kwakany'a kendoo syaumanie na sikũkũ ĩno ya Saturnalia." Nayo ĩvuku Encyclopædia Britannica yonanĩtye kana mũthenya ũsu wa Saturnalia "
mawĩa onthe nĩmavungawa."
Mataa ma ĩvinda ya Kĩlisimasi: Ĩvuku The Encyclopedia of Religion, yaĩtye kana mũthenya ũsu andũ ma Europe maanakavasya mĩsyĩ yoo "
na mataa na mĩtĩ ya kĩla mĩthemba" maitanĩa sikũkũ ĩsu, na ĩngĩ meekaa ũu nĩ kana masiĩĩe ndaimoni.
Tũmĩtĩ twĩtawa Mistletoe, na malaa metawa holly: "
Atongoi ma ndĩni maasya kana kamũtĩ ketawa mistletoe kala kekwatĩlaa mĩtĩnĩ ĩngĩ kaĩ katonya kũtũmĩwa maũndũnĩ ma ũwe. Nayo ĩlaa yĩtawa holly yĩla yĩthĩawa yĩ ĩsanzamũku ĩvinda yonthe nĩyathaithawa nũndũ yoonekaa ta ũĩkĩĩthyo wa kana no nginya sua yĩsyoke."—The Encyclopedia Americana.
Mũtĩ wa Kĩlisimasi: "
Andũ ma ndĩni sya ũvũngũ ma Europe ala mathaithaa mĩtĩ nĩmaendeeie na ũthaithi ũsu ĩtina wa kũtw'ĩka Aklĩsto." Ũndũ ũmwe ũla watumie ũthaithi wa mĩtĩ ũendeea nĩ kĩthĩo kya "
kwia mũtĩ wĩtawa Yule mũomonĩ kana nyũmba nthĩnĩ ĩvindanĩ ya sikũkũ ila syeekawa ĩvinda ya mbevo."
—Encyclopædia Britannica.

translation:
The Bible says
The Bible states that Jesus was born, and states also that I failed to celebrate his birth. One book writes by McClintock and Strong says: "
Many people in biblical times celebrated Christmas, and this custom was associated with pagan ceremonies."
Indeed, many associate Christmas with ancient customs from the time of paganism. The Bible states that it dishonors God when we worship him with teachings originating from pagan sources.—Proverbs 32:5-7.
However, some believe Christmas honors
Celebrating the birth of Jesus: "
Christians commemorate the birth of Jesus because they want to celebrate the birth of a person and be reminded of the meaning of the gospel."—The World Book Encyclopedia.
December 25: Many people believe Jesus was born on that day. They choose this date because during those days the Roman festivals were coming to an end and the winter solstice was approaching.
To give gifts, feast, and gather together: A book The Encyclopedia Americana says: "
Saturnalia, which was a festival of the Romans and ended in mid-December, influenced many customs now associated with Christmas. For example, customs such as prolonged feasting, gift-giving, and revelry were common during this festival of Saturnalia." Also, the book Encyclopædia Britannica states that this festival of Saturnalia "
was often riotous."
The origins of Christmas trees: A book The Encyclopedia of Religion says that during this season Europeans decorated their homes with evergreen branches "
and wreaths and trees" to celebrate the season, and others believed this was a way to ward off demons.
The use of mistletoe and holly: "
Ancient peoples believed that mistletoe had magical properties and used it in various rituals. And the plant called holly, which has prickly leaves and red berries, was considered sacred and was brought indoors throughout the winter to symbolize life."—The Encyclopedia Americana.
The Christmas tree: "
People in northern Europe began the custom of bringing trees indoors and decorating them." One reason why the practice of using trees became popular was because of "
the Yule log, a large log burned in the hearth on Christmas Eve."
—Encyclopædia Britannica.

text:
We no wende kũmanya alaĩka naaũ, maumie va, na wĩa ũla matethasya? Vai vandũ vangĩ ũtonya kũkwata mosũngĩo maseo ateo Ndetonĩ ya Ngai mbeveee, Mbivilia. (2 Timotheo 3:16) Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa alaĩka?
O tondũ Ngai nĩ Veva, o namo alaĩka nĩ syũmbe sya veva itonekaa, na iyĩthĩawa na "nyama na mavĩndĩ." Alaĩka ala aĩkĩĩku mekalanasya ĩtunĩ na Ngai.—Luka 24:39; Mathayo 18:10; Yoana 4:24.
Ĩvinda ya tene, ve mavinda alaĩka meekĩaa mĩĩ ya andũ nĩ kana meanĩsye wĩa ũla manengetwe nĩ Ngai kũũ nthĩ, na mamina wĩa woo nĩmaumasya mĩĩ ĩsu.—Asili 6:11-23; 13:15-20.
O na kau alaĩka mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ ta aũme na mavinda onthe maumĩlaa ta aũme, vai mũlaĩka o na ũmwe wĩthĩawa na mwĩĩ wa mũndũũme kana wa mũndũ mũka. Alaĩka maitwaanaa na maisyaa. O na ĩngĩ, alaĩka mayaaũmbwa mekalae kũũ nthĩ me twana tũnini kana andũ aima, na ĩtina maikw'a na maithi ĩtunĩ. Alaĩka moombiwe nĩ Yeova na nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩmetĩte "ana ma Ngai."—Yovu 1:6; Savuli 148:2, 5.
Mbivilia nĩwetete ĩũlũ wa "ithyomo sya andũ na sya alaĩka," na ndeto isu syonanasya kana syũmbe ila syĩ mĩĩ ya veva syĩ kĩthyomo kĩla itũmĩaa. O na kau Ngai nĩwatũmĩaa alaĩka kũneena na andũ, ndetĩkĩlĩtye andũ mamavoye kana mamathaithe.—1 Akolintho 13:1; Ũvuan'yo 22:8, 9.
Kwĩ nguthu mbingĩ mũno vyũ sya alaĩka, o na nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa me mbilioni mbingĩ. *—Ndanieli 7:10; Ũvuan'yo 5:11.
Mbivilia yonanasya kana alaĩka me "ũtonyi vinyanĩ," na ũu nĩ kwasya kana me vinya na ũĩ mwingĩ kwĩ andũ. Alaĩka me ũtonyi wa kũthi na mĩtũkĩ kwĩ kĩndũ o na kĩva mũndũ ũtonya kũsũanĩa.—Savuli 103:20; Ndanieli 9:20-23.
O na kau alaĩka me ũtonyi mwingĩ wa kũsũanĩa na wa kwĩka maũndũ, ve maũndũ amwe matesa kwĩka, o na ve maũndũ amwe matesĩ.—Mathayo 24:36; 1 Vetelo 1:12.
Alaĩka mombĩtwe me na ndaĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na me na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Na kwoou o tondũ andũ mailyĩ, alaĩka no menyuvĩe kwĩka kĩla kĩseo kana kĩla kĩthũku. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana ve alaĩka amwe manyuvie kũleana na Ngai.—Yuta 6.
^ kal. 8 Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩtũmĩĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Ũvuan'yo 5:11 yĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a "ngili ĩkũmi kũndũ ngili ĩkũmi," na kwoou ndeto isu syĩonany'a kana noĩthwa kwĩ alaĩka milioni maana maingĩ kana mbilioni mbingĩ!

translation:
Do we really know what is right and wrong, what is good, and who the righteous ones are? Many people find it hard to accept God's standards, especially when they seem different from those of others—even shocking, like those found in the Bible. (2 Timothy 3:16) Does the Bible truly reveal what is right?
Yes, because God is Truth, what the Bible says is true and reliable, and it exposes "fleshly desires." Those who want to please God will examine their hearts.—Luke 24:39; Matthew 18:10; John 4:24.
However, some people reject Bible principles because they conflict with their own ideas or with what others believe. They may feel that God's standards are too strict. But such thinking can be dangerous.—Genesis 6:11-23; 13:15-20.
And just as some reject the Bible's teachings, so too do some reject angels, believing them to be myths or legends. Some might think of angels as being only symbolic or as representing human qualities. Such beliefs are incorrect. And often, those who reject angels also deny the existence of God and heaven, and they dismiss life after death as foolish. These ones are deceived by Satan, and this is why the Bible calls them "sons of God."—Job 1:6; Psalm 148:2, 5.
The Bible speaks of an "army of heavens" and describes countless numbers of spirits, some of whom are invisible to us. Yet, God uses angels to communicate with humans, helping them during times of trouble or danger.—1 Corinthians 13:1; Revelation 22:8, 9.
In fact, there are billions of angels, and they are powerful creatures. *—Daniel 7:10; Revelation 5:11.
The Bible refers to angels as "powerful spirits," and they have far more ability than humans. Angels who are loyal to God can accomplish things quickly and effectively, while disloyal angels can cause harm.—Psalm 103:20; Daniel 9:20-23.
But even the most powerful angels cannot see the future perfectly, nor can they do everything. Some events take them by surprise.—Matthew 24:36; 1 Peter 1:12.
Angels are moved by our faith and loyalty, and they rejoice when we remain faithful despite difficulties. And although many people do not realize it, angels are always watching over us, ready to help us at any time. The key to receiving angelic help is to maintain a close relationship with God.—Jude 6.
^kal. 8 The Greek manuscript used in the translation of Revelation 5:11 originally read "ten thousand times ten thousand," and some manuscripts say that this represents countless millions or even billions of angels!

text:
Ĩĩ, me kw'o. Maumie va? Lilikana kana Ngai oombie alaĩka me na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ĩvinda ĩnini kuma Atamu na Eva moombwa, ve mũlaĩka watũmĩie naĩ ũthasyo wake wa kwĩnyuvĩa na ambĩĩsya ũlei vaa nthĩ. Mũvango wa mũlaĩka ũsu nĩweanĩie nũndũ nĩwatumie Atamu na Eva maleana na Ngai. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:1-7; Ũvuan'yo 12:9) Mbivilia ndĩwetete nesa vyũ ĩsyĩtwa na kĩanda kya mũlaĩka ũsu e ĩtunĩ atanamba kũleana na Ngai. Ĩndĩ mũlaĩka ũsu amina kũleana na Ngai, eetiwe Satani, kwonany'a "Mũvinganĩsya," na Ndevili, kwonany'a "Mũsukani."—Mathayo 4:8-11.
Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana ũlei ũsu nĩwaendeeie. Ĩvindanĩ ya Noa, ve alaĩka matawetetwe ũtalo woo ala "matiie ũtũo woo ũla wamaĩle" ĩtunĩ, vala Ngai wĩkalaa. Alaĩka asu nĩmookie kũũ nthĩ na meeyosea mĩĩ ya nyama nĩ kana meke ũlaalai, kĩvathũkany'o na ũndũ Ngai wavangĩte kwondũ woo.—Yuta 6; Mwambĩlĩlyo 6:1-4; 1 Vetelo 3:19, 20.
Nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie alaĩka asu athũku? Ĩla Ngai waetie mbua nene nĩ kana athesye nthĩ, alaĩka asu nĩmatiie mĩĩ ya nyama ĩla maĩ nayo na masyoka ĩtunĩ. Ĩndĩ Ngai ndaaĩtĩkĩlya alaĩka asu mataĩ aĩkĩĩku masyokee "ũnene woo ene." Vandũ va ũu, amalikilye "kĩvindunĩ" kingĩ kya kĩ-veva kĩla Mbivilia yĩtaa Talitalo. (Yuta 6; 2 Vetelo 2:4, NWT) Alaĩka asu athũku nĩmanyuvie kũtongoew'a nĩ Satani ũla Ndevili, "mũnene wa ndaimoni," ũla 'wĩyĩalyũlaa mwene ethĩwe ta mũlaĩka wa kyeni.'—Mathayo 12:24; 2 Akolintho 11:14.
Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ũsumbĩ wa Masia wa Ngai nĩ silikalĩ ya ĩtunĩ yambĩĩe kũsumbĩka mwaka wa 1914. * Ũsumbĩ ũsu wambĩĩa kũsumbĩka, Satani na ndaimoni syake nĩmalũngilw'e ĩtunĩ na mekw'a kũũ nthĩ. Maũndũ mathũku ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ vamwe na ũndũ andũ mendete kwĩka ũlaalai meĩkĩĩthya kana Satani na ndaimoni syake me na ũthilĩku mwingĩ na nĩmaendeee kũtongoesya andũ naĩ vyũ.—Ũvuan'yo 12:9-12.
Ĩndĩ ũthũku mwingĩ ũla ũendeee kwongeleka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ wĩonany'a kana ũtongoi mũthũku wa Satani na ndaimoni syake wĩ vakuvĩ kũthela. O mĩtũkĩ syũmbe isu nthũku sya veva ikaanangwa. Ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkamina kũsumbĩka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ kwa myaka 1,000, syũmbe isu nthũku sya veva ikeethĩwa na kamwanya kanini ka kũtata andũ ya mũthya. Ĩtina wa ũu, alaĩka asu athũku makaanangwa tene na tene.—Mathayo 25:41; Ũvuan'yo 20:1-3, 7-10.
^ kal. 6 Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, sisya kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata?, yĩla yumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. O na no ũyĩkwate Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam.

translation:
Yes, I hear you. How are things? Temptation came when God allowed Satan to tempt them with the desire to be like him. A great sin was committed by Adam and Eve, who disobeyed God and hid from Him because of their shame. The purpose of this temptation was to make Adam and Eve turn away from God. (Genesis 3:1-7; Revelation 12:9) Scripture shows that this serpent was influenced by an angel who wanted to oppose God. This angel, who desired to oppose God, is called "the Adversary," which is Satan, and the Devil, which is "the Accuser."—Matthew 4:8-11.
The result of this rebellion is that death has come upon us. In the case of Noah, when people became so wicked that they were said to be "evil in all their dealings," God decided to act. Those people continued to do evil and fill the earth with violence, ignoring God's warning.—Jude 6; Genesis 6:1-4; 1 Peter 3:19, 20.
What caused those ancient people to become so wicked? Because God showed kindness to mankind, those people began to misuse life and practice wickedness and immorality. But God will not allow those people to continue forever doing what is bad.—Jude 6; 2 Peter 2:4, NWT) Those wicked people enjoyed being deceived by Satan the Devil, "the ruler of the demons," who 'misleads the whole inhabited earth.'—Matthew 12:24; 2 Corinthians 11:14.
Scripture reveals that God's Messianic Kingdom began invisibly in heaven in 1914. * With this kingdom beginning, Satan and his demons were thrown down to the earth and started to exert more influence. Difficult times have been increasing on the earth, and since then people have been experiencing greater trials because Satan and his demons have increased their activity and continue to mislead people with lies.—Revelation 12:9-12.
Because much time has passed since then, it is evident that Satan and his demons are desperately trying to hold on. However, God's Kingdom will soon begin ruling over the earth for 1,000 years, and during that time those wicked people will be restrained. After that, those ancient people will be fully eradicated.—Matthew 25:41; Revelation 20:1-3, 7-10.
^ par. 6 What further information about God's Kingdom can you find in the Bible book *Is Scripture Really Inspired by God?*, published by Jehovah's Witnesses? And you can also find information at www.jw.org/kam.

text:
Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ kyaũ?
We no wasye Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩ . . .
• kĩndũ kĩthĩawa ngoonĩ?
• kĩndũ kyaĩle kũeleeka kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o?
• kana nĩ silikalĩ ya ĩtunĩ?
MBIVILIA YAĨTYE ATA?
"Ngai wa ĩtunĩ akaũngamya ũsumbĩ ũtakaanangĩka tene na tene." —Ndanieli 2:44, The Bible in Kikamba, 1974.
'Nĩtũnengetwe mwana mũndũ mũũme; na ũsumbĩko ũkeethĩwa kĩtuonĩ kyake.'—Isaia 9:6.
ŨNDŨ KŨMANYA ŨU KŨTONYA ŨKŨTETHYA
• No kũũtetheesye ũmanye kana kwĩ silikalĩ yĩ na ũlũngalu ĩla ĩtonya kũũtethya we mwene.—Isaia 48:17, 18.
• Ĩngĩ, no kũũtetheesye ũmanye kana nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla yũkĩte kũikethĩwa ũwau, na andũ makeethĩawa na ũtanu.—Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4.
NĨTŨTONYA KŨĨKĨĨA ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE?
Ĩĩ, nũndũ wa itumi ta ilĩ:
• Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkeka. Yesũ amanyĩisye aatĩĩi make mavoyae Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wũke, na kwenda kwake kũyĩkwa kũũ nthĩ. (Mathayo 6:9, 10) Nĩwasyokie oonany'a ũndũ mboya ĩsu ĩkasũngĩwa.
Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ nĩwamanengie lĩu ala maĩ na nzaa, avosya awau, na athayũũkya akw'ũ! (Mathayo 15:29-38; Yoana 11:38-44) Nũndũ Yesũ nĩwe waĩ ethĩwe Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, eekie maũndũ asu nĩ kana onany'e moathimo ala makatanĩwa nĩ andũ ala makethĩwa ungu wa Ũsumbĩ ũsu.—Ũvuan'yo 11:15.
• Maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ meonany'a kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wĩ vakuvĩ. Yesũ athanie kana Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũtambĩte kũete mũuo kũũ nthĩ, kwaĩ kwĩthĩwe makaũ, nzaa, na itetemo sya nthĩ.—Mathayo 24:3, 7.
Maũndũ asu nĩmo me kw'o ũmũnthĩ. Kwoou, no twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkilyĩ kũmina mathĩna asu onthe.
Ethĩwa ndwĩ na Mbivilia, no ũmĩsome nthĩnĩ wa Kĩsese kya www.jw.org/sw (Wavingũa vinyĩĩa vala vaandĩkĩtwe MACHAPISHO, na ũisyoka ũvinyĩĩe BIBLIA)
KWASŨANĨA ĨKŨLYO YĨĨ:
Kũkeethĩwa kũilyĩ ata ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wĩsumbĩka?
Mbivilia nĩsũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu ĩandĩkonĩ ya SAVULI 37:29, na ya ISAIA 65:21-23.
ĨMANYĨSYE MAŨNDŨ ANGĨ VATE NDĨVI
Soma ĩsomo ya 7 nthĩnĩ wa kavuku kaa.
□ Nĩngũmũkũlya mũndũmĩe kavuku kaa.
(Onany'a kĩthyomo kĩla ũkwenda.)
Ĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
□ Nĩngũmũkũlya mũtũme mũndũ kwakwa.
No ũkũlye ũtũmĩwe mũndũ oke kwaku kana umye kavuku kaa nthĩnĩ wa www.jw.org/kam.

translation:
What is God's Kingdom?
We now examine what this Kingdom is…
• Something valuable to people?
• Something that will replace human governments?
• Or just a dream?
DO YOU CARE AT ALL?
"The God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed." —Daniel 2:44, The Bible in Kikamba, 1974.
'For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government will rest on his shoulders.'—Isaiah 9:6.
THIS IMPORTANT MATTER CONCERNS YOU
• Do not let ignorance or fear prevent you from finding out the truth about it.—Isaiah 48:17, 18.
• Rather, find out what the future holds for you and for mankind, and live in harmony.—Proverbs 21:3, 4.
WHY SHOULD WE BE INTERESTED IN THIS IMPORTANT MATTER?
Well, here are some reasons:
• Jesus taught us to pray for God's Kingdom. Jesus showed his followers how to understand God's Kingdom and what it means to them, and his life demonstrated its principles. (Matthew 6:9, 10) He also encouraged them to keep looking forward to it.
But Jesus while on earth performed many miracles, healed the sick, fed the hungry, and raised the dead! (Matthew 15:29-38; John 11:38-44) This shows that Jesus is the one whom God has appointed to establish God's Kingdom, and he will accomplish wonderful things for those who love righteousness.—Revelation 11:15.
• Future events will show that God's Kingdom is real. Jesus foretold signs that would indicate the nearness of the end of this system of things, wars, earthquakes, and famines.—Matthew 24:3, 7.
These things are proof of our time. Therefore, we should be motivated to learn more about God's Kingdom.
To learn more, read the Bible and visit the website at www.jw.org/sw (Look under PUBLICATIONS, then BIBLE)
TO HELP YOU REMEMBER:
What does it mean to have faith that God's Kingdom will succeed?
The Bible answers this question in PSALM 37:29, and in ISAIAH 65:21-23.
LEARN MORE FROM THESE SOURCES
Read lesson 7 from the book.

(Consider what questions you can ask.)
Learn more about the Bible and Jehovah's organization.
□ I will invite someone to the meeting.
You can find help to answer questions or locate a congregation near you at www.jw.org/kam.

text:
Nĩkĩ mũndũ woombiwe?
Nĩkĩ andũ mathĩnaa na makakw'a?
Kũkeethwa kũilyĩ ata ĩvinda yũkĩte?
We Ngai nũnthĩnĩkĩaa?
We waaĩkũlya makũlyo ta asu? Ethĩwa ũu nĩ w'o, ndwĩ weka. Andũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmekũlasya makũlyo ala ma vata thayũnĩ. Yo ve mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu?
Andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmatonya kwasya, "Ĩĩ!" Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nĩmakwatĩte mosũngĩo maseo kuma Mbivilianĩ ma makũlyo moo. No wende kũmanya ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya? No ũtetheke kumana na mũvango wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova * wa kũmanyĩsya andũ Mbivilia vate ndĩvi.
Ũw'o nĩ kana andũ aingĩ methĩawa na mawoni ta aa ĩla makũlw'a mamanyĩw'e Mbivilia: "Nĩngwatene." "Nĩ vinya kũmĩelewa Mbivilia." "Ũndũ ũla ũnemaa nĩ kwĩyumya nĩ kana nĩmanyĩw'e Mbivilia." Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, andũ angĩ nĩmetĩkĩlaa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Amwe moo maĩtye ũũ:
"Nĩnaendie ndĩninĩ ya Katholeki, na nathi ndĩninĩ ila ingĩ sya Kĩklĩsto, o na nĩnaendie ndĩninĩ ya Sikh, na ya Buddha, na nĩnasomie maũndũ ma ndĩni nĩ yunivasĩtĩ. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ndyaakwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala neekũlasya ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Ĩtina, nĩnathokeiwe nĩ mũndũ mũka ũmwe waĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova. Nĩnendeeiw'e nĩ mosũngĩo ala wambonisye kuma Mbivilianĩ na neetĩkĩla kũmanyĩw'a Mbivilia."
—Gill, England.
"Nĩneekũlasya makũlyo maingĩ ĩũlũ wa thayũ, ĩndĩ ndyaaĩanĩwa nĩ mosũngĩo ala nakwatie kuma kwa mwalimũ wa ndĩni ĩla naendaa. Ĩndĩ, mũndũ ũmwe waĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova nĩwasũngĩie makũlyo makwa atũmĩĩte Mbivilia. Ĩla wangũlilye kana nĩngwenda kwĩmanyĩsya mũnango, nĩneetĩkĩlile kuma ngoonĩ."6
—Koffi, Benin.
"Nĩnendaa mũno kũmanya ũndũ kwĩkĩkaa ĩla mũndũ wakw'a. Naĩkĩĩaa kana akw'ũ no maũmĩsye ala me thayũ, ĩndĩ nĩnendaa kũmanya kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya. Kwoou, nambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia vamwe na mũndũũme ũmwe mũnyanyawa waĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova."—José, Brazil.
"Nĩnatataa kũsoma Mbivilia, ĩndĩ ndyaeleawa nĩ kĩla nasomaa. Ĩtina Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyangeleisye nesa mawatho kauta ala me Mbivilianĩ. Nĩnendaa kũmanya kana ve maũndũ angĩ maingĩ naĩ ndonya kwĩmanyĩsya."—Dennize, Mexico.
"Neekũlasya kana Ngai nũnthĩnĩkĩaa. Na kwoou natw'a kũmũvoya Ngai ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyookie nyũmba kwakwa, na neetĩkĩla kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia."—Anju, Nepal.
Maũndũ asu mawetwa metũlilikany'a ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Nĩ aathime ala me na nzaa na waũni wa ũlũngalu." (Mathayo 5:6) Kwoou, andũ mombĩtwe me na wendi wa kũmũmanya Ngai. No Ngai e weka ũtonya kwĩanĩsya wendi ũsu, na ekaa ũu kwĩsĩla Ndeto yake, Mbivilia.
Kwoou, tũmanyĩasya mũndũ Mbivilia ata? Kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kũtonya ũkũtethya ata? Makũlyo asu nĩmeũsũngĩwa kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe.
^ kal. 8 Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ Yeova.

translation:
Am I a person who is being sought?
Are there people who have problems?
Is it possible to be forgiven even a little sin?
Why should I pray to God?
Why do people enjoy food so much? This is how it is, just like that. Many people today are enjoying food without thinking about its source. So, do you also think about where food comes from?
Millions of people respond, "Yes!" Why? Because they have experienced something similar to what happened at Bethphage regarding food. Do you want to know what Bethphage did? Do you want to learn about the purpose of Jehovah's Witnesses in helping people understand the Bible?
This is because many people have questions about what the Bible teaches: "I don't understand it." "It is difficult to comprehend the Bible." "The best thing is to simply believe what others tell me about the Bible." But despite this, many people want to understand the Bible. Some say:
"I went to Catholic churches, and then I tried other Christian churches, and I went to Sikh temples and Buddhist temples, and I studied things at university. But despite all this, I still lacked satisfaction and a true understanding of God. Finally, I was visited by a man from Jehovah's Witnesses. He showed me things from the Bible and helped me to appreciate the Bible."
—Gill, England.
"I used to enjoy life very much, but I became dissatisfied when I realized that my teachers at school were not giving me truthful information. Then, someone from Jehovah's Witnesses helped me to find answers using the Bible. Now, whenever I feel inclined to pursue worldly things, I remember what I learned."6
—Koffi, Benin.
"I wanted to find out the truth about life. I wondered if the beliefs I had been taught were accurate, so I began to investigate what the Bible says. As a result, I started studying the Bible with one of Jehovah's Witnesses."—José, Brazil.
"I found it difficult to read the Bible, but I persevered because I wanted to understand it. Fortunately, Jehovah's Witnesses kindly offered me help to understand the Scriptures. I want to learn more so that I can share it with others."—Dennize, Mexico.
"I used to think that God didn't care about me. But now I realize that God cares about us, as revealed in the Bible. The people I met from Jehovah's Witnesses came to my home, and I appreciated their willingness to study the Bible with me."—Anju, Nepal.
The words Jesus spoke are meaningful to us today: "Happy are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness." (Matthew 5:6) Similarly, many people desire to know God. And God wants to be found, and he has made his Word, the Bible, available to us.
So, how can we come to know the Bible well? How can we make sure our understanding of the Bible is accurate? Let us examine some ways to improve our skills.
^ par. 8 The Bible teaches that God's name is Jehovah.

text:
WE WONAA Mũthenya wa Sila ta kyaũ? Andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana andũ mbilioni mbingĩ makaetwe mbee wa kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya Ngai ũmwe kwa ũmwe. Na kĩla ũmwe aisilĩlwa. Na amwe maitw'ĩĩwa kũthi ĩtunĩ na angĩ ĩianĩ ya mwaki wa tene na tene. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yonanasya ũndũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ũsu ĩũlũ wa Mũthenya wa Sila. Ndeto ya Ngai yonanasya kana mũthenya ũsu ti ĩvinda ya kũtelemya ĩndĩ nĩ ĩvinda ya wĩkwatyo na kũtũnga ũseo kũũ nthĩ.
Nthĩnĩ wa Ũvuan'yo 20:
Yeova Ngai nĩwe Mũsili mũnene vyũ wa andũ onthe. Ĩndĩ nũnenganĩte wĩa wa kũsila. Kwĩanana na Meko ma Atũmwa 17:
Ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo yonanasya kana Mũthenya wa Sila ũkaambĩĩa ĩtina wa walany'o wa Satani kũũ nthĩ kwanangwa kaũnĩ wa Ali-Maketoni. * (Ũvuan'yo 16:
Ĩvinda yĩu ya myaka ngili Yesũ Klĩsto 'akasilĩla ala me thayũ na ala akw'ũ.' (2 Timotheo 4:1) "Ala me thayũ" makeethĩwa ne "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ" yĩla yĩkavonoka Ali-Maketoni. (Ũvuan'yo 7:
Mũtũmwa Yoana oonie woninĩ, "mavuku mavuanw'a," na "ala akw'ũ masilĩlwa na maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe mavukunĩ asu, kwĩanana na meko moo." Mavuku asu maandĩkĩtwe meko ala andũ meekaa matanamba ũkw'a? Tiw'o, nũndũ sila ndũkethĩwa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala andũ meekaa matanakw'a. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya ũu? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Ũla wakwie nũtalĩtwe ta ũte na naĩ." (Alomi 6:7) Kwoou ala methayũũkw'a makeethĩwa mate na naĩ. Kwoou mavuku asu makeethĩwa maandĩkĩtwe motw'ĩo angĩ ma Ngai. Ala mevonoka Ali-Maketoni vamwe na ala methayũũkw'a, no nginya mew'e mĩao ya Ngai na motw'ĩo meũ onthe ala Ngai wĩonany'a ĩvindanĩ ya myaka ngili nĩ kana mekale tene na tene. Kwoou andũ makasilĩlwa kwĩanana na meko moo ĩvindanĩ ya Mũthenya wa Sila.
Mũthenya wa Sila ũkanenga andũ mbilioni mbingĩ mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya na kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Kwoou kũkeethĩwa na wĩa mwingĩ wa kũmanyĩsya. 'Ala matwĩe nthĩ makeemanyĩsya ũlũngalu.' (Isaia 26:9) Ĩndĩ ti onthe meĩthĩwa mayenda kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Isaia 26:10 yaĩtye: 'Ũseo o na woonanw'a kwa ũla mũthũku, ndakemanyĩsya ũlũngalu; e nthĩ ya ũlũngalu akeekaa naĩ, na ndakona ũnene wa Yeova.' Ĩvinda ya Mũthenya wa Sila andũ asu athũku makooawa vate wĩkwatyo ũngĩ.
Mũthenya wa Sila ũithela ala meĩthĩwa me avonoku 'makeethĩwa thayũ' na me eanĩu vyũ. (Ũvuan'yo 20:5) Ĩvinda ya Mũthenya wa Sila andũ onthe makatw'ĩka eanĩu ũndũ mũndũ wa mbee wailye yĩla woombiwe. (1 Akolintho 15:

translation:

text:
1. Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ kyaũ?
Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ silikalĩ ya ĩtunĩ. Ũkavetanga silikalĩ ila ingĩ syonthe na ũkatuma kwenda kwa Ngai kwĩkwa ĩtunĩ na kũũ nthĩ. Nĩ ũvoo mũseo kũmanya kana Ngai akatũmĩa Ũsumbĩ wake kwa nzĩa ĩsu. Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkilyĩ ũneanĩsya wendi wa mũndũ wa kwĩthwa na silikalĩ nzeo. Ũkaete ngwatanĩo katĩ wa andũ onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Ũsumbĩ no nginya wĩthwe na mũsumbĩ. Yeova amũnyuvie Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, ethĩwe Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ Wake.
2. Nĩkĩ Yesũ nĩwe Mũsumbĩ ũla waĩle?
Mwana wa Ngai nĩwe Mũsumbĩ ũla waĩle nũndũ e tei na nũlũmanasya na ũla waĩle. (Yoana 1:14) Ĩngĩ, e vinya mwingĩ ũtoetye kũtetheesya andũ nũndũ akasumbĩka nthĩ e ĩtunĩ. Ĩtina wa kũthayũũkw'a, ambatie ĩtunĩ na ekala kw'okonĩ kwa aũme kwa Yeova, eteele anengwe ũsumbĩ. (Aevelania 10:12, 13) Ĩtina wa ũu, Ngai nĩwamũnengie vinya wa kwambĩĩa kũsumbĩka.
3. Naaũ makasumbĩka vamwe na Yesũ?
Kĩkundi kĩtawa ala "atheu" kĩkasumbĩka vamwe na Yesũ ĩtunĩ. (Ndanieli 7:27) Atheu ma mbee kũnyuvwa maĩ atũmwa aĩkĩĩku ma Yesũ. Yeova no ũendee kũnyuva aũme na aka aĩkĩĩku methĩwe amwe ma asu atheu. Mathayũũkaw'a me na mwĩĩ wa veva o ũndũ ũmwe na Yesũ.
Aala maĩle kũthi ĩtunĩ nĩ meana? Yesũ ametie "ĩĩthya ĩnini." (Luka 12:32) Na onthe makeethĩwa 144,000. Makasumbĩka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ vamwe na Yesũ.
4. Kweethĩiwe ata ĩla Yesũ wambĩĩie kũsumbĩka?
Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wambĩĩie kũsumbĩka 1914. * Ĩtambya ya mbee yĩla Yesũ woosie ambĩĩa kũsumbĩka yaĩ kũmwĩkya Satani na ndaimoni syake kũũ nthĩ. Satani nĩwathilĩkile na ambĩĩa kũete mathĩna ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. (Ũvuan'yo 12:7-10, 12) Kuma ĩvinda yu, mawoo ma andũ nĩmongelekeele vyũ. Makaũ, mayũa, mĩimũ, na ithingitho sya nthĩ nĩ maũndũ amwe me nthĩnĩ wa "wonan'yo" wa kana Ũsũmbĩ ũsu ũkilyĩ kũsumbĩka nthĩ yonthe.
5. Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũendee kwĩka ata?
Kwĩsĩla wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũendeee kũmbany'a ĩkomano ĩnene yĩ na ngwatanĩo kuma mbaĩ syonthe. Andũ auu milioni mbingĩ nĩmenyivĩsye Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũla ũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Yesũ. Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkamasũvĩa ĩla wĩananga walany'o ũũ mũthũku wa maũndũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Kwoou, onthe ala mekwenda moathimo ma Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai maĩle kwĩmanyĩsya kũmwĩnyivĩsya Yesũ.
Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 1,000, Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũkeanĩsya kĩeleelo kya mbee kya Ngai kwa andũ. Nthĩ yonthe ĩkatw'ĩka valatiso. Na ĩtina wa ũu, Yesũ aitũngĩa Ĩthe wake Ũsumbĩ. (1 Akolintho 15:24-26) We ve mũndũ wĩsĩ wenda kũmũtavya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai?

translation:
1. What is God's love?
God's love is a perfect quality. It surpasses all other qualities and motivates people to do good things and to show kindness to others. This is why it is important to know whether God sends his love to us in ways we can understand. God's love often means giving up something valuable to help someone who needs it. It involves showing compassion to all people, regardless of their background.
Love comes from a lover. Jehovah lovingly sent his Son, Jesus Christ, as the expression of his love.
2. Is Jesus the only true Lover?
God's Son is the only true Lover because he is perfect and completely understands our feelings. (John 1:14) However, many people find it difficult to believe that someone would care about them so much. To demonstrate his love, he gave his life and remained loyal to his Father, Jehovah, so that we could receive forgiveness. (Hebrews 10:12, 13) Because of this, God willingly gives us opportunities to show love.
3. Can we show love along with Jesus?
A large group called "the faithful" shows love along with Jesus now. (Daniel 7:27) The faithful ones desire to please Jesus and carry out his will. Jehovah also wants to please his servants and supports them as they imitate Jesus. They work hard to share the good news with others.
Are there others who want to live forever? Jesus has promised "a great crowd." (Luke 12:32) And there are 144,000 chosen ones. Many others will live forever alongside Jesus.
4. How did God allow Satan to test people's loyalty?
God allowed Satan to test people's loyalty in 1914. * This period marked the time when Jesus was given authority to oppose Satan and his demons. Satan has deceived people and caused suffering throughout the earth. (Revelation 12:7-10, 12) In recent times, people have experienced many trials. Wars, famines, earthquakes, and other disasters are signs of "the time of distress" during which God's sovereignty is being challenged.
5. Will God's love ever end?
Besides wanting to save mankind from destruction, God's love motivates him to correct injustice everywhere. Millions of people have learned about God's Kingdom through Jesus. God's Kingdom will accomplish what humans cannot—to solve the world's problems. So, everyone can look forward to living under peaceful conditions ruled by Jesus.
For 1,000 years, this Kingdom will act as a heavenly government over mankind. The entire earth will become a paradise. And eventually, Jesus will hand back his Kingdom to his Father. (1 Corinthians 15:24-26) Is there anyone who would not want to support God's Kingdom?

KWASISYA! ngalawa yĩ thĩnanĩ! Ĩendee na kũtilĩkanga ilungu! We nũkwona andũ asu meeyĩkya kĩw'ũnĩ? Amwe nĩmaminĩte kũthambĩa makaumĩla ũtee wa ũkanga. Ũya nĩ Vaulo wĩ vaya? Ekai twone maũndũ ala methĩĩtwe maimũkwata.
Lilikana, kwa myaka ĩlĩ Vaulo asiĩĩwe Kaisalea e mwovwa. Na ĩndĩ we na ovwa angĩ malikw'a ngalawanĩ na makũsya melekele Lomi. Na yĩla mavĩtĩile vakuvĩ na kĩthama kya Kilete, makomana na kĩuutani kĩnene mũno. Kyauutanie na vinya mũno nginya atwai ma ngalawa maemwa nĩkũmĩtwaa. Na mayaĩ matonya kwona syũa mũthenya kana ndata ũtukũ. Ĩtina vyũ, mĩthenya mingĩ yathela, ala maĩ ngalawanĩ maasya wĩkwatyo wa kũvonoka.
Vaulo ĩndĩ aũngama na asya: 'Vaiĩ ũmwe wenyu wĩasya thayũ wake; ngalawa noyo yĩanangĩka. Nũndũ ũtukũ mũlaĩka wa Ngai nũmbũkĩie na ambĩa: "Ndũkakĩe, Vaulo! No mũvaka ũũngame mbee wa Kaisali, mũsumbĩ wa Alomi. Na Ngai akatangĩĩa onthe ala me ngalawanĩ vamwe naku."'
Ta ũtukũ katĩ mũthenya wa 14 ĩtina wa kĩla kĩuutani kwambĩĩa, atwai ma ngalawa nĩmoonie kana kĩw'ũ nĩkĩendee na kwĩthĩwa kĩte kĩliku! Na nũndũ wa ũkĩa kũkima mavia kĩvindunĩ, matheesya nanga syoo. Ũnĩ ũsu kwakya moona nthĩ nyũmũ. Namo matw'a nĩmatate kũtwaa ngalawa nginya vau.
Yĩla mathengee ũtee wa ũkanga, ngalawa yatina kĩthangathĩ na yalũma. Na ĩndĩ itulumo syambĩĩa kũmyananga, nayo yambĩĩa kũtilĩkanga ilungu. Na mũsikalĩ ũla waũngamĩe asya: 'Inyw'onthe ala mũtonya kũthambĩa ĩyĩkyei ũkanganĩ na mũithambĩa mũvike nthĩ nyũmũ. Nenyu ala mwatiala ĩyĩkyei ĩtina woo, na mũyĩkwatĩla ilungu sya mbwaũ sya ngalawa.' Na ũu nĩw'o meekie. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu andũ 276 ala maĩ ngalawanĩ nĩmavikie nthĩ nyũmũ o nesa, o tondũ mũlaĩka wathanĩte.
Kĩthama kĩu kĩtawa Melita. Andũ ma kũu maĩ aseo mũno, na nĩmathokisye ala maumie ngalawanĩ. Na nzeve yaseũva, Vaulo nĩwalikilw'e ngalawanĩ ĩngĩ na atwawa Lomi.
Meko 27:1-44; 28:1-14.
Makũlyo
- Ngalawa ĩla Vaulo waĩ nthĩnĩ wayo yakwatiwe nĩ kyaũ vakuvĩ na kĩthama kya Kilete?
- Vaulo amatavisye ata ala maĩ nthĩnĩ wa ngalawa ĩsu?
- Ngalawa ĩsu yatilĩkangie ilungu ata?
- Nĩ mawatho maũ mũnene wa asikalĩ wanenganie, na nĩ andũ meana ata maumĩlile nginya nthĩ nyũmũ me aima?
- Kĩthama kĩu mavikie kĩtawa ata, na kweethĩiwe ata kwa Vaulo nzeve yaseũva?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Meko 27:1-44.
Mũĩkĩĩo witũ wa kana Mbivilia ndĩ mavĩtyo ũlũlũmĩĩlaw'a ata twasoma Ngewa ya kyalo kya Vaulo kya ũkanganĩ aendete Lomi? (Meko 27:16-19, 27-32; Lk. 1:3; 2 Tim. 3:16, 17)
- Soma Meko 28:1-14.
Ethĩwa andũ mate etĩkĩli ma kĩthama kya Melita nĩmasukumiwe nĩ ngoo kũmeka "ũseo mũnene" Vaulo na andũ ala waanangĩkĩiwe nĩ ngalawa vamwe namo, Aklĩsto maĩlĩte kũsukumwa monany'e kyaũ na mũno mũno kwa nzĩa yĩva? (Meko 28:1, 2; Aevl. 13:1, 2; 1 Vet. 4:9)

translation:
ALRIGHT! This boat is beautiful! Let's go and celebrate with the whites! Do we see people who understand things properly? Some boast about building houses like those of skilled craftsmen. Is this Paul who went there? Come let us see other things which we have grasped.
Listen, for many years Paul was imprisoned in Caesarea while awaiting trial. And during that time he had many visitors who brought him gifts and praised Lomi. And they told stories to the prisoners about the power of Christ, and great joy filled the place. Because of this joy, many were converted and began to build boats. And some young men saw a vision at night. It happened often, many nights passed, but the boats remained strong and capable of surviving.
Paul then said to them: 'Each of you should repair his own net; the boat will be strengthened. But tonight the angel of God came to me and said: "Fear not, Paul! For you shall go to Rome, a prisoner of Alomi. And God will grant peace to all of us who sail with you."'
That night, around midnight during each watch, the sailors secretly tried to escape by lowering the boat into the sea! But when the officer noticed something suspicious, he prevented them from doing so. He ordered them to remain on board. Now they began to pray earnestly.
When they reached the third day after the storm, they threw overboard everything belonging to the ship. And during that time they continued to celebrate with the whites. And the captain shouted to them: 'Everyone should eat something to strengthen himself for the journey and eat more food for the sake of the boat.' And that is what happened. In total, 276 people on the boat were saved, although the officer had warned them.
The island where they landed was called Malta. The local people showed them much kindness, and they welcomed the sailors. And when it rained, Paul gathered firewood and helped the others start a fire, and they were warmed.
Acts 27:1-44; 28:1-14.
Questions
- What caused Paul to be imprisoned and await trial in Caesarea?
- Did Paul appeal to Caesar while on the boat?
- Was the boat damaged at all?
- What great advice did the sailor give, and who were the men who listened and were saved?
- Where did the island land, and what happened to Paul when it rained?
Further Questions
- Read Acts 27:1-44.
How can we learn from Paul's account of his voyage to Rome? (Acts 27:16-19, 27-32; Luke 1:3; 2 Timothy 3:16, 17)
- Read Acts 28:1-14.
Why were the inhabitants of the island of Malta kind to Paul and those traveling with him, and why did Christians continue to show kindness to others? (Acts 28:1, 2; Hebrews 13:1, 2; 1 Peter 4:9)
