1. Nĩkĩ Ngai woombie nthĩ?
Yeova anengie andũ onthe nthĩ. Nĩyo mũsyĩ witũ. Kwoou, mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka ma mbee, Atamu na Eva, mayaaũmbwa mekale ĩtunĩ nũndũ Ngai aĩ anoomba alaĩka mekalae kũu. (Yovu 38:4, 7) Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, Ngai aiie mũndũ wa mbee nthĩnĩ wa valatiso nzeo yeetawa mũũnda wa Eteni. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:15-17) Yeova nĩwanengie mũndũ ũsu vamwe na nzyawa syake wĩkwatyo wa kũtanĩa thayũ tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Mwambĩlĩlyonĩ, no mũũnda wa Eteni w'oka waĩ valatiso. Mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka ma mbee maaĩle kũsyaana mausũsye nthĩ. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, maĩ makĩlye nthĩ yonthe vinya na kũmĩtw'ĩkĩthya valatiso. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:28) Nthĩ ndĩkaanangwa o na ĩndĩĩ. Ĩkeethĩawa mũsyĩ wa andũ ĩvinda yonthe.
2. Nĩkĩ nthĩ ti valatiso ũmũnthĩ?
Atamu na Eva mayaamwĩw'a Ngai na kwoou Yeova amaumya ũla mũũndanĩ. Valatiso nĩyaaiw'e, na vaiĩ mũndũ waatonya kũmĩtũngĩĩa. Mbivilia yaasya: "Nthĩ nĩnenganĩtwe kw'okonĩ kwa athũku."—Yovu 9:24.
Yeova nũemetwe nĩkwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kyake kya mbee kwa mũndũ? Aiie! Nĩ mwene vinya w'onthe. Ndatonya kũemwa. (Isaia 45:18) Akatuma andũ mekala ũndũ we wendaa mekale.
3. Valatiso ĩkatũngĩĩwa ata?
Valatiso ĩkatũngĩĩwa ĩvinda ya ũsumbĩki wa Yesũ e Mũsumbĩ ũũngamĩtw'e nĩ Ngai. Kaũnĩ wĩtawa Ali–Maketoni, Yesũ akatongoesya alaĩka ma Ngai na kũmananga onthe ala mamũleaa Ngai. Na ĩndĩ Yesũ aimũvingĩa Satani kwa myaka 1,000. Andũ ma Ngai maikanangwa nũndũ Yesũ akamatongoesya na kũmasũvĩa. Makatanĩa thayũ ũtakathela nthĩnĩ wa Valatiso kũũ nthĩ.
4. Mathĩna makathela ĩndĩĩ?
Ngai akaveta ũthũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩndĩĩ? Yesũ nĩwanenganie "wonan'yo" wa kwonany'a mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ. Maũndũ ala mekw'o ũmũnthĩ makaendeea no mamine andũ, namo meonany'a tũtwĩe nthĩnĩ wa "wĩanĩu wa ĩvinda yĩĩ."
Ĩla Yesũ wĩĩthwa asumbĩkĩte nthĩ kwa myaka 1,000 e ĩtunĩ, akavetanga mathĩna onthe. (Isaia 9:6, 7; 11:9) Yesũ akeethĩwa e Mũsumbĩ, na e Mũthembi Mũnene ũla ũkaveta naĩ sya ala mamwendete Ngai. Kwoou, kwĩsĩla Yesũ, Ngai akavetanga mowau, ũkũũ, na kĩkw'ũ.
5. Nũũ ũla ũkekala nthĩnĩ wa Valatiso ĩla yũkĩte?
Andũ ala mamwĩw'aa Ngai makekala Valatisonĩ. (1 Yoana 2:17) Yesũ atũmie aatĩĩi make makamanthe ala auu na maimamanyĩsya ũndũ matonya kwĩka metĩkĩlwe nĩ Ngai. Ũmũnthĩ, Yeova aendee kũmbany'a milioni sya andũ ala meĩkala Valatisonĩ ĩla ĩkethĩwa kũũ nthĩ. (Nzevania 2:3) Nthĩnĩ wa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ sya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, andũ nĩmamanyĩaw'a ũndũ matonya kwĩthĩwa me aũme aseo, iveti nzeo, na asyai aseo. Syana na asyai mathaithaa vamwe na mayĩmanyĩsya ũndũ ũvoo mũseo ũtonya kũmatethya.

translation:
1. Did God create humans?
Jehovah created the heavens and the earth. He is our Creator. In the beginning, man and woman were created perfect, Adam and Eve, they were created beautiful and capable, but they did not obey God's command. (Job 38:4, 7) As a result, God allowed the perfect man to be sent away from his home in Eden. (Genesis 2:15-17) Jehovah loved mankind so much that he made a plan to redeem them time and time again throughout history.
Genesis tells us that the man in Eden was banished. Man and woman began to suffer and experience difficulties. Because of sin, all things became imperfect and people started to die. (Genesis 1:28) The earth became filled with wickedness. It became a place where violence reigned.
2. Why is there suffering?
Adam and Eve disobeyed God, and because of this Jehovah permitted suffering. Suffering is a consequence, and people have the ability to learn from it. The Bible says: "Man is born into trouble."—Job 9:24.
Does Jehovah delight in causing pain to humans? No! He is powerful and just. He can feel sympathy. (Isaiah 45:18) He sends his angels to help those who love him.
3. Will suffering ever end?
Suffering will end when Jesus Christ exercises his authority as King during the Thousand Year Reign appointed by God. A man named Ali–Maketoni, Jesus will restore God's sovereignty and vindicate the name of God. And then Jesus will bind Satan for 1,000 years. God's people will live under Jesus' rule and enjoy peace. Finally, the Kingdom will bring about a world without suffering.
4. What will happen eventually?
Will God make the entire earth a paradise? Jesus promised "newness" for those who love righteousness. All the good things that will come will benefit not only faithful ones, but also those who appreciate the "everlasting covenant."
Yes, Jesus will be given power over the entire earth for 1,000 years, and he will accomplish everything that God purposes. (Isaiah 9:6, 7; 11:9) Jesus will reign from heaven, and the great shepherd will care for his flock. Moreover, through Jesus, God will provide food, security, and peace.
5. Who will inhabit the future Kingdom?
Those who love God will inhabit the Kingdom. (1 John 2:17) Jesus will choose loyal ones to associate with him in heaven and to demonstrate God's purpose. Furthermore, Jehovah will gather millions of those who dwell in the Kingdom that will be on earth. (Revelation 2:3) At the spiritual temples of Jehovah, people learn how to live happily, remain morally clean, and stay spiritually strong. They share this knowledge with others, helping them to understand what they can do to find lasting satisfaction.

Ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka
1. Sũanĩa ĩũlũ maũndũ ala wĩ na ũtonyi wa kwĩka. (2 Akolintho 11:6) O na kau nĩ ũseo kũmanya wĩ o mawonzu maku, wĩ o maũndũ ala ũtonya kwĩka nesa. Kũmanya nguma syaku nzeo nĩkũtonya kũũnenga ũkũmbaũ na kũituma ũvetanga mawoni mataĩle kwĩyelekela na ũyĩeka kwona ta vate mũndũ ũkũũngana naku. Ĩkũlye, 'Nĩ maũndũ mekũ ndonya kwĩka nesa?' Sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa nguma nzeo na ndaĩa nzeo syaku.
2. Endeew'a kuma ngoonĩ nĩ angĩ. Ambĩĩa kwendeew'a no andũ anini. "O ũndũ laisi ta kwenda o kũmanya andũ maendeee ata kana kũmakũlya ĩũlũ wa wĩa woo nĩũkũtetheesya kũmamanya nesa mũnango," ou nĩw'o waĩtye mwanake ũmwe wĩtawa Jorge.
Ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka: Ndũkaneenae tũ na andũ ma ũkũũ waku oka. Andũ amwe maĩ anyanya mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ maĩ na ũkũũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o mũno. Amwe ma anyanya asu nĩ Luthi na Naomi, Ndaviti na Yonathani, na Timotheo na Vaulo. (Luthi 1:16, 17; 1 Samueli 18:1; 1 Akolintho 4:17) Ĩngĩ, lilikana kana ĩla ũkũneena na mũndũ ũngĩ no nginya ũkamwĩthukĩĩsya nake ayĩka o ta ũu. translation:
A speech can be deceiving
1. Let him express himself clearly about what he means, and let his speech be sincere. (2 Corinthians 11:6) And if you don't know how to judge your own motives, how can you tell whether his speech is sincere? Knowing your own heart is key to discerning truth and sending clear messages to others so they can understand and trust you. Ask yourself, 'Are my intentions truly pure?' Examine your own heart and desires carefully.
2. The ability to listen is rare. Speak to listeners, not just people. "The problem with going out and trying to understand people is that you often end up judging them based on your own standards," said a young man named Jorge.
A speech can be deceiving: We need friends who will support us. Some have been greatly helped by fellow Christians in their congregation. Others were Ruth and Naomi, David and Jonathan, and Timothy and Paul. (Ruth 1:16, 17; 1 Samuel 18:1; 1 Corinthians 4:17) Therefore, be careful whom you confide in, lest you offend someone or cause harm. However, there is also a time to speak and a chance to encourage others. People appreciate those who uplift them. So, be wise in your words, knowing when to speak and when to remain silent!
3. Be sympathetic, and love your brothers. (1 Peter 3:8) And always be willing to cooperate with everyone, being considerate and understanding. Listening is a valuable skill. Be eager to hear the feelings of each listener, listening intently and with genuine interest.
A speech can be deceiving: If you speak kindly to others, let your speech always be pleasant and helpful. Speaking tactfully, avoiding harshness, showing consideration, or looking down on others, helps people respond favorably to you. You can make a good impression by speaking in this way, so that others may say: "Your conversation is always seasoned with salt—so that you may know how to answer everyone."—Colossians 4:6.

translation:
"Every request that is made is a theft [or, "begging," NWT]."
Indeed we desire to be satisfied with food, but often we abuse the possessions of our fellow humans. (Proverbs 30:8) Thus it is a bad thing to say "food is insignificant." (Ecclesiastes 7:12) It harms a person and his household when he excessively seeks possessions, forgetting to be grateful for what he has. (Ephesians 4:32) Other people may also become dissatisfied, and I with jealousy will cause myself to misuse possessions.
1 AVOID THESE THINGS
THE QUESTION IS THIS: "Which of you who wants to build a tower does not first sit down and calculate the cost whether he has enough to finish it?" (Luke 14:28) It is wise to consider among yourselves whether you can afford to misuse your possessions. (Amos 3:3) Therefore, carefully examine each time you go out, and see if you have sufficient possessions. (Proverbs 31:16) And if you do not have them, do not acquire debt, because it is better to have no possessions than to be in debt. Be diligent and careful. Do not allow yourself to be drawn into debt.—Proverbs 21:5; 22:7.
WHAT TO CONSIDER:
Before you misuse possessions, consider what you are doing
Before your desires lead you to misuse possessions, set limits on your desires. For example, think about going to visit relatives
2 BE CONTENT WITH WHAT YOU HAVE AND BE SATISFIED
WITH YOUR MEANS
THE QUESTION IS THIS: "Because of this, let everyone put away lying, and speak truth with his neighbor." (Ephesians 4:25) Let us practice honesty in our dealings with others, so that we may not get involved in something wrong.
Therefore, whenever you associate with others, avoid getting involved in things that could cause you trouble and lead to the misuse of your possessions. (Proverbs 13:10) To avoid falling into the trap of misusing your possessions, learn to refuse unreasonable requests from those who exploit you. Do not hesitate to say no to such people. And remember that you are responsible for your own welfare.—1 Timothy 5:8.
WHAT TO CONSIDER:
Refuse possessions, but each of you should be able to use his own resources to help another
Be willing to share your possessions, but only within reasonable limits

NĨ KĨVATHŨKANY'O kyaũ kĩ nthĩnĩ wa visa ũũ? Nĩ andũ ala mevo. Mo nĩ mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka ma mbee. Nũũ wamombie? Nĩ Ngai. We nĩwĩsĩ syĩtwa yake? Nĩ Yeova. Nake ũ mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka meetiwe Atamu na Eva.
Ũũ nĩw'o Yeova Ngai woombie Atamu. Oosie kĩtoo kuma nthĩ na kuma kĩtoonĩ kĩu aseũvya mwĩĩ mwĩanĩu, mwĩĩ wa mũndũ. Na ĩndĩ aveveea manyiũũnĩ ma ũ mũndũ, na Atamu eethĩwa thayũ.
Yeova Ngai nĩwamũnengie Atamu wĩa. Amwĩie atw'ĩĩe nyamũ syonthe sya kĩla mũthemba masyĩtwa. No kwĩthĩwa Atamu asyaaĩsye nyamũ kwa ĩvinda yĩasa nĩ kana ainyuvĩe masyĩtwa ala masyaĩle. Atamu o aendeee na kũtw'ĩĩa nyamũ masyĩtwa nĩwoonie ũndũ mũna. We nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ ũsu waĩ mwaũ?
Nyamũ syonthe syaĩ na atindany'a. Kwaĩ nzou nũme na nzou nga, na mĩnyambũ mĩũme na mĩnyambũ mĩka. No Atamu ndaĩ na ũmwe wa kũtindany'a nake. Kwoou ĩndĩ Yeova amũetee Atamu too mũnene, na aumya wau ĩvavanĩ yake. Yeova nĩwatũmĩie wau ũsu kũmũmbĩa Atamu mũndũ mũka, nake atw'ĩka kĩveti kyake
Atamũ atanie ta kĩ! Kwasũania ũndũ Eva nake watanie kwiwa mũũndanĩ mwanake ekalae vo! Atamu na Eva maĩ matonya kwĩthĩwa na syana na kwĩkalany'a na ũtanu.
Yeova endaa Atamu na Eva matũe tene na tene. We endaa mamĩseũvye nthĩ yonthe na mamyanakavye yĩkale ta mũũnda wa Eteni. Atamu na Eva matanie ta kĩ yĩla masũanĩie ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu! We waĩ wenda kwĩthĩwa na kĩanda kya kwanakavya nthĩ yĩkale ta mũũnda ũsu? Ĩndĩ Atamu na Eva mayaaendeea kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu. Ekai twone kĩtumi nĩ kyaũ.

translation:
Am I bothering you with questions about visas? There are other people around. I am a man and a woman who lives. Who created them? It is God. What is His name? It is Jehovah. He made a man and a woman named Adam and Eve.
This is how Jehovah God created Adam. He gave him life and the ability to live forever, like an animal. And he gave him many gifts as a human being, and Adam was happy.
God loved Adam very much. He showed him everything good on earth, all the beautiful things. But there was one thing Adam could not have—to eat from the tree of knowledge of good and bad, or he would die. Adam continued to enjoy all the beautiful things, but he knew something important. What is this important thing that you know?
Everything was beautiful and perfect. There were lions and tigers, and elephants and giraffes. But Adam wanted something more. So God saw that Adam needed someone equal to him, and He decided to make him a companion. God sent him a woman to be his companion so she could help him fulfill his purpose.
Adam was overjoyed! Because now Eve also had the desire to obey God and to live forever! Adam and Eve were happy to be together and to care for each other.
Jehovah always remembered Adam and Eve. He remembers all living creatures and all those who will live forever in Paradise. Adam and Eve were overjoyed to hear about the future! Will you be happy to live forever in Paradise? Adam and Eve continue to want to live forever. Let us see why.
Psalm 83:18; Genesis 1:26-31; 2:7-25.
Questions
- What does question three of this discussion and question two ask?
- Who created the man who lives and the person you know?
- How did God love Adam greatly?
- Why did God make Adam great?
- Were Adam and Eve ever unhappy, and how did Jehovah remind them?
Further Questions
- Read Psalm 83:18.
The name of God is powerful, and He has strength that cannot be compared to anyone else in all the earth. (Jeremiah 16:21; Daniel 4:17)
- Read Genesis 1:26-31.
Why did God create angels to help his friends and give them a beautiful home? (Genesis 1:26)
Does Jehovah love people very much? (Genesis 1:30)

What happened when Adam wanted to learn more about animals? (Genesis 2:19)
Does Genesis 2:24 teach us about Jehovah's feelings regarding marriage, family, and friendship? (Matthew 19:4-6, 9)

WE WĨTHĨAWA wĩ Mũklĩsto? Ethĩwa wĩ Mũklĩsto, wĩ ũmwe katĩ wa andũ mbee wa mbilioni ilĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ala maasya kana nĩ Aklĩsto. Ũmũnthĩ, kwĩ ndĩni mbingĩ syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto, ĩndĩ syĩthĩawa ĩvathũkene nũndũ wa maũndũ ala kĩla ĩmwe yĩĩkĩĩaa. Kwoou mũĩkĩĩo waku nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na wa ala angĩ maasya kana nĩ Aklĩsto. Yo nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũndũ kũtinda aithĩnĩka nũndũ wa kĩla ũĩkĩĩaa? Ĩĩ, mũndũ nĩwaĩle kũthĩnĩka ethĩwa nũkwenda kũatĩĩa Ũklĩsto wa w'o kwosana na ũndũ wonanĩtw'e Mbivilianĩ.
Aatĩĩi ma tene ma Yesũ Klĩsto nĩmo matw'ĩkie "Aklĩsto." (Meko ma Atũmwa 11:26) Vayaĩ vata wa kũmantha masyĩtwa angĩ ma kũmavathũkany'a nũndũ maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ũmwe. Aklĩsto asu nĩmaatĩĩaa momanyĩsyo ma ũla wambĩĩisye Ũklĩsto, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto mwene. Nao nata ĩũlũ wa ndĩni ĩla ũendaa? Nĩmanyĩasya kĩla Klĩsto wamanyĩasya na kĩla aatĩĩi make ma tene maĩkĩĩaa? Ũtonya kũmanya ata kana kwa w'o nĩyĩkaa ũu? Vai nzĩa ĩngĩ ĩtonya kũũtetheesya ate o kũtũmĩa Mbivilia.
Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwanengete Maandĩko ndaĩa nũndũ nĩweesĩ nĩmo Ndeto ya Ngai. Ndeetĩkĩlanaa na andũ ala maatĩĩaa syĩthĩo sya andũ vandũ va kũatĩĩa momanyĩsyo ma Mbivilia. (Maliko 7:9-13) Vate nzika, maũndũ ala aatĩĩi ma w'o ma Yesũ maĩkĩĩaa maĩle kwosana na kĩla kĩ Mbivilianĩ. Kwoou, kĩla Mũklĩsto aĩle kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: "Mo momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni ĩla nĩendaa nĩmosanĩte na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya?" Nĩ kana ũsũngĩe ĩkũlyo yĩu, sianĩsya kĩla ũĩkĩĩaa na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya.
Yesũ aisye kana ũthaithi witũ kwa Ngai waĩle kwĩthĩwa wosanĩte na ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. (Yoana 4:24; 17:17) O nake mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye kana ũtangĩĩo witũ wumanaa na "kũmanya ũla w'o." (1 Timotheo 2:4) Kwoou, nĩ ũndũ wa vata maũndũ ala tũĩkĩĩaa makethĩwa mosanĩte na ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nũndũ ũndũ ũsu no ũtume tũkwata thayũ kana tũkaũkosa!
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KŨSIANĨSYA MAŨNDŨ ALA TŨĨKĨĨAA NA KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA
Twĩũkũlya ũsome makũlyo aa thanthatũ na ũisisya ũndũ masũngĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ. Soma maandĩko ala monanĩtw'e, na ũisũanĩa kwa ũliku mosũngĩo ala manenganĩtwe. Wamina kwĩka ũu ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Mo momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni ĩla nĩendaa nĩmosanĩte na kĩu Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya?'
Makũlyo asu nĩmatonya kũũtetheesya kũsianĩsya momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni ĩla ũendaa na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya na ũndũ ũsu ũkaũtethya mũno. No wende kũsianĩsya momanyĩsyo angĩ ala ndĩni ĩla ũendaa ĩmanyĩasya na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya? Ngũsĩ sya Yeova no iũtetheesye kũmanya nesa kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya. No ũkũlye ũmwe woo aũmanyĩsye Mbivilia vate ndĩvi. O na no ũvingũe Kĩsese kitũ kya indaneti kya jw.org/kam.

text:
1. Kwĩ ndĩni o ĩmwe ya w'o?
Yesũ amanyĩisye aatĩĩi make ĩũlũ wa ndĩni o ĩmwe ya w'o. Nĩ ta nzĩa elete thayũnĩ ũtathela. Yesũ aisye: "Nĩ avũthũ ala mamyonaa." (Mathayo 7:14) Ngai etĩkĩlaa ũthaithi o ũla wosanĩte na Ndeto yake ya w'o. Athaithi onthe ma w'o makwatanĩtw'e nĩ mũĩkĩĩo o ũmwe.
2. Yesũ aisye ata ĩũlũ wa Aklĩsto ma ũvũngũ?
Yesũ awetie kana athani ma ũvũngũ makavukya Ũklĩsto. Kwa kũsiw'a tũ, monekaa ta athaithi ma w'o. Ndĩni syoo syaasya nĩ sya Kĩklĩsto. Ĩndĩ nũtonya kũmanya kana mo ti Aklĩsto ma w'o. Ata? No ũthaithi wa w'o wĩthĩawa na Aklĩsto ma w'o ala methĩawa na meko na nguma nzeo.
3. Ũtonya kũmanya athaithi ma w'o ata?
Sũanĩĩa movano aa atano:
Athaithi ma w'o nĩmamĩnengete Mbivilia ndaĩa ta Ndeto ya Ngai. Nĩmatataa kwĩkala kwosana na myolooto yayo. Kwoou, ndĩni ya w'o yĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ndĩni ila imanyĩasya momanyĩsyo ma andũ. (Mathayo 15:7-9) Athaithi ma w'o mekalaa kwosana na momanyĩsyo moo.
—Soma Yoana 17:17; 2 Timotheo 3:16, 17.
Aatĩĩi ma w'o ma Yesũ nĩmayĩnengete ndaĩa syĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova. Yesũ nĩwayĩnengie syĩtwa ya Ngai ndaĩa kwa kũyĩmanyĩthya. Nĩwatetheeisye andũ kũmũmanya Ngai na amamanyĩsya kũvoya syĩtwa ya Ngai yĩtaĩwe. (Mathayo 6:9) Ndũanĩ kwenyu, nĩ ndĩni yĩva ĩmanyĩthasya syĩtwa ya Ngai?
—Soma Yoana 17:26; Alomi 10:13, 14.
Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmatavanasya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Yesũ nĩwatũmiwe nĩ Ngai atavany'e ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai now'o wĩkwatyo w'oka wa andũ. Yesũ nĩwaendeeie kũũtavany'a kũvika mũthenya wake wa kũkw'a. (Luka 4:43; 8:1; 23:42, 43) Nĩwawetie kana aatĩĩi make makatavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ ũsu. Mũndũ akoka kũũtavya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, we wona ta wa ndĩni yĩva?
Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ ti ma nthĩ ĩĩ nthũku. Nũtonya kũmamanya nũndũ mayĩlikasya siasanĩ kana ithokoonĩ sya mbaĩ. (Yoana 17:16; 18:36) O na maiatĩĩaa meko na mawoni mathũku ma nthĩ.
—Soma Yakovo 4:4.
Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmendanĩte mũno. Nĩmemanyĩĩtye kuma Ndetonĩ ya Ngai kũmanenga ndaĩa andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe. O na kau mavinda maingĩ ndĩni sya ũvũngũ nĩsyĩlikasya mũno makaũnĩ ma mbaĩ, athaithi ma w'o mayĩkaa ũu. (Mika 4:1-3) Vandũ va ũu, Aklĩsto ma w'o matũmĩaa ĩvinda yoo na malĩ syoo kũtetheesya na kwĩkĩa angĩ vinya.
—Soma Yoana 13:34, 35; 1 Yoana 4:20.
4. Nũtonya kũmanya ndĩni ĩla ya w'o?
Nĩ ndĩni yĩva ĩla momanyĩsyo mayo onthe maumaa Mbivilianĩ, ĩnengae syĩtwa ya Ngai ndaĩa, na ĩtavanasya Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai kana now'o wĩkwatyo w'oka wa andũ? Nĩ ndĩni yĩva yonanasya wendo na ĩtelikasya kaũnĩ? We wĩona ata?

translation:
1. Are you among them?
Jesus showed his followers what people who truly belong to him are like. It's not easy to recognize those who are genuine. Jesus said: "Narrow is the gate and cramped is the road leading to life." (Matthew 7:14) God will help you tell who is really trying to live according to his standards. The qualities of true Christians are similar.
2. Did Jesus teach about false Christians?
Jesus warned that false Christians would appear. For example, look closely at their conduct. Those who don't obey God's laws are not Christ's. It can be difficult to know whether someone is a true Christian. How so? Because their actions often contradict what they say and believe.
3. How can you identify true Christians?
Consider these five points:
True Christians base their lives on the Bible and respect God's standards. They strive to live in harmony with its teachings. Also, their words are consistent with what the Bible teaches and reflect honest thoughts. (Matthew 15:7-9) True Christians live in harmony with those teachings.
—Read John 17:17; 2 Timothy 3:16, 17.
The things Jesus taught honor God's name, Jehovah. Jesus made known God's name and helped others learn it. He taught people how to know God and showed them the importance of sanctifying God's name. (Matthew 6:9) Brothers and sisters, what does it mean to sanctify God's name?
—Read John 17:26; Romans 10:13, 14.
True Christians actively support God's Kingdom. Jesus was sent by God to proclaim this good news. God's Kingdom is the only hope for mankind. Jesus continued proclaiming it until his death. (Luke 4:43; 8:1; 23:42, 43) Ask yourself, 'Do my efforts support God's Kingdom?' What kind of person shows he belongs to God's Kingdom?
The teachings of Jesus are not divisive or exclusive. We should be able to understand them without feeling prejudiced or biased. (John 17:16; 18:36) And they should appeal to our sense of justice and fairness.
—Read James 4:4.
True Christians love one another. They strive to live in harmony with God's standards toward all people. Despite facing many challenges and difficulties, true Christians maintain their unity. (Micah 4:1-3) People everywhere, true Christians use their resources and time to help others and show kindness.
—Read John 13:34, 35; 1 John 4:20.
4. How can we show our love for God?
What is the best way to demonstrate our love for God, to honor His name, and to support God's Kingdom and the hope it offers to mankind? What will motivate us to act kindly and justly? Can you think of ways?

text:
KWASISYA! Aisilaeli maendee na kũinga Ũsĩ wa Yolotani! Nũndũ mbua mbingĩ yuaa ĩvinda yĩu ya mwaka, o ndakĩka nini nthelu ũsĩ wĩĩ musũu vyũ. Ĩndĩ yu vaiĩ kĩw'ũ! Na Aisilaeli maendee na kũinga ũsĩ makinyĩle nthĩ nyũmũ o tondũ meekie kũya Ũkanganĩ Mũtune! Kĩw'ũ kyu kyonthe kyathi va? Ekai twone.
Yĩla ĩvinda ya Aisilaeli yavikie ya kũinga Ũsĩ wa Yolotani, ũũ nĩw'o Yeova weeie Yosua nĩatavye andũ: 'No mũvaka athembi makue ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo na maithi mbee witũ. Na yĩla nyaĩĩ syoo ikakinya nthĩ kĩw'ũnĩ kya Ũsĩ wa Yolotani, kĩw'ũ kĩkavingĩwa.'
Kwoou athembi mookĩlya ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo, na mayĩkua na maenda mbee wa andũ. Yĩla mavikie Yolotani, athembi makinya kĩw'ũnĩ ũtee. Nakyo kĩw'ũ kyasembete na vinya mũno na ũsĩ waĩ mũliku. Ĩndĩ nyaĩĩ syoo syamina kũkinya kĩw'ũ oou, kĩw'ũ kyaũngama! Kyu kyaĩ kyama! Ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya ũsĩ Yeova asiĩĩie kĩw'ũ ta silanga. Kwoou, o mĩtũkĩ ũsĩ wang'ala!
Athembi ala makuĩte ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo mathi nginya ũsĩnĩ katĩ. We nũmene vaa visanĩ? Na maũngamĩte vau, Aisilaeli onthe mainga Ũsĩ wa Yolotani makinyĩle nthĩ nyũmũ!
Yĩla andũ onthe maminie kũinga, Yeova eea Yosua amatavye ũũ aũme me vinya 12: 'Likai ũsĩnĩ nginya vala athembi ala makuĩte ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo maũngamĩte. Osai mavia 12, na mũimakua mũkamaie o vala mwĩkoma ũtukũ ũũ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ, ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte, yĩla syana syenyu ikamũkũlya kĩla mavia asu meonany'a, no nginya mwĩsyĩa kana kĩw'ũ nĩkyaũngamie yĩla ĩsandũkũ ya Yeova ya ũtianĩo yaingie Yolotani. Mavia asu makamũlilikany'a kyama kĩĩ!' Na ĩngĩ Yosua nĩwaũngamisye mavia 12 ũsĩnĩ katĩ vala athembi maũngamĩte.
Na ĩtina vyũ Yosua eea athembi ala makuĩte ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo: 'Ambatai mume Yolotani.' Na mamina kwĩka ũu, ũsĩ wambĩĩa kũvĩtya kĩw'ũ ĩngĩ.
Yosua 3:1-17; 4:1-18.
Makũlyo
- Yeova eekie kyama kĩva nĩ kana Aisilaeli matonye kũinga Ũsĩ wa Yolotani?
- Aisilaeli maĩlĩtwe nĩkwĩka ũndũ mwaũ wa kwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo woo nĩ kana mainge Ũsĩ wa Yolotani?
- Nĩkĩ Yeova weeie Yosua nĩombany'e mavia manene 12 kuma ũsĩnĩ katĩ?
- Kweekĩkie ata athembi mamina kuma Yolotani oou?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Yosua 3:1-17.
O tondũ ngewa ĩno ĩnĩkwonany'a, twaĩlĩtwe nĩkwĩka ata nĩ kana tũkwate ũtethyo na ũathimo wa Yeova? (Yos. 3:13, 15; Nth. 3:5; Yak. 2:22, 26)
Ũsĩ wa Yolotani wailyĩ ata yĩla Aisilaeli maingie mailika Nthĩ ya Watho, na ũndũ ũsu wakumisye syĩtwa ya Yeova ata? (Yos. 3:15; 4:18; Sav. 66:5-7)
- Soma Yosua 4:1-18.
Mavia ala 12 moosiwe kuma Yolotani na maiwa Ngilikali maĩ ma wĩa mwaũ? (Yos. 4:4-7)

translation:
ALAS! The Israelites proceeded to cross the Jordan River! A very large swarm of bees attacked them this year, but what is the reason this time they are so numerous? Go see! And the Israelites proceeded to cross the river to the place where they camped, and because they feared to go to Mount Gilead! Why did everything happen like that? Let us see.
The entire camp of the Israelites was preparing to cross the Jordan River, and then Jehovah commanded Joshua to tell the people: 'Take priests from each tribe and carry the ark of the covenant with you. And if you come across any who oppose you on the way to the Jordan River, that thing will be defeated.'
They took priests carrying the ark of the covenant, and they went ahead of the people. As they approached the Jordan River, the priests stepped forward into the water. Then the waters parted and opened up, and the whole land overflowed. But those who opposed it were unable to step forward, that thing was swept away! Why was it like that! Like a great flood of the river, Jehovah dried up the water for them. Therefore, let us cross the river quickly!
The priests carried the ark of the covenant and walked in the middle of the river. Were there any problems? And when they had passed, the Israelites crossed the Jordan River to the place where they camped!
When all the people had finished crossing, Jehovah said to Joshua to take twelve men from each tribe: 'Go to the middle of the river and take stones from the place where the priests stood. Take one stone from each tribe, and set it up as a memorial in the place where you camp tonight. This is why, the day you cross, the next generation will ask about these stones, and you will tell them that the ark of Jehovah, the covenant, entered the Jordan River. These stones will serve as a sign for you!' And Joshua sent twelve men to the middle of the river to take stones from the place where the priests had passed.
And later Joshua commanded the men who carried the ark of the covenant: 'Go and pass through the Jordan.' And they obeyed him, and the river began to flow back.
Joshua 3:1-17; 4:1-18.
Questions
- Did Jehovah do something special so that the Israelites could cross the Jordan River?
- What lesson can we learn from how the Israelites showed their faith when they crossed the Jordan River?
- Why did Jehovah tell Joshua to choose twelve important men from each tribe to go to the middle of the river?
- What happened when the priests took the ark to the Jordan River?
More Questions
- Read Joshua 3:1-17.
From this account, what can we learn about showing respect for and confidence in Jehovah? (Jos. 3:13, 15; Prov. 3:5; Jas. 2:22, 26)
Did the Jordan River dry up completely when the Israelites crossed, and did this show Jehovah's power? (Jos. 3:15; 4:18; Ps. 66:5-7)
- Read Joshua 4:1-18.
What did the twelve men do when they came to the Jordan River, and what were the stones used for? (Jos. 4:4-7)

text:
KWASISYA kĩla kĩendee kwĩkĩka vaa. Atamu na Eva nĩmeũlũngw'a mũũndanĩ mwanake wa Eteni. We nũũmanya nĩkĩ?
Kĩtumĩ nũndũ nĩmeekie ũndũ mũthũku mũno. Kwoou Yeova nũkũmasilĩla. We nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ mũthũku ũla Atamu na Eva meekie?
Meekie ũndũ Ngai wameĩte maikeke. Ngai ameie nĩmatonya kũya lĩu kuma mĩtĩnĩ ya mũũnda ũsu. Ĩndĩ wa mũtĩ ũmwe Ngai nĩwameie maikaye, nũndũ maya makakw'a. Mũtĩ ũsu waĩ wake e weka. Nĩtwĩsĩ kana kwosa kĩndũ kya mũndũ ũngĩ nĩ ĩvĩtyo, kana tyo twĩsĩ ũu? Yu-ĩ, kweekĩkie ata?
Mũthenya ũmwe Eva e weka mũũndanĩ, nzoka nĩyaneenie nake. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũsu! Yeeie Eva aye matunda ma mũtĩ ũla Ngai wameĩte maikaye. Ĩndĩ yĩla Yeova woombie nzoka ndaainenga ũtonyi wa kũneena. Kwoou veonany'a kana ve mũndũ ũngĩ ũla watumie nzoka ĩneena. We aĩ ũũ?
Ndaĩ Atamu. Kwa kĩtumi kĩu no nginya ethĩwe aĩ ũmwe wa syũmbe ila Yeova woombĩte tene mũno mbee wa kũmba nthĩ. Syũmbe isu nĩ alaĩka, na tũitonya kũmona. Mũlaĩka ũsu aĩ na mĩyono mingĩ. Ambĩĩie kũsũanĩa kana no nginya ethĩwe mũsumbĩ ta Ngai. Na nĩwendaa andũ mamwĩw'ae we vandũ va kũmwĩw'a Yeova. Ũsu nĩwe mũlaĩka ũla watumie nzoka ĩneena.
Mũlaĩka ũsu nĩwamũkengie Eva. Yĩla wamwĩie kana akekala ta Ngai aya ĩtunda, Eva nĩwaĩkĩĩie ũu. Kwoou nĩwaĩye, na Atamu o nake aya. Atamu na Eva nĩmaleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai, na kwa kĩtumi kĩu maasya wĩkalo woo wa mũũnda mwanake.
Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe Ngai akatuma nthĩ yonthe yaĩla ta mũũnda wa Eteni. Ĩtina tũkeemanyĩsya ũndũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa na kĩanda nthĩnĩ wa kũmyaĩlya yĩkale ũu. Ekai ĩndĩ yu twone ũndũ kweethĩiwe ĩũlũ wa Atamu na Eva.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:16, 17; 3:1-13, 24; Ũvuan'yo 12:9.
Makũlyo
- Vaa visanĩ, nĩ kyaũ kĩendee kwĩkĩka kwa Atamu na Eva?
- Yeova amasilĩile nĩkĩ?
- Nzoka yamwĩie Eva ata?
- Nũũ watumie nzoka ĩneena na Eva?
- Nĩkĩ Atamu na Eva maaisye wĩkalo woo wa Valatiso?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:16, 17 na 3:1-13,24.
Ĩkũlyo yĩla nzoka yakũlilye Eva yaetie ata ũvoo ũte waw'o kwelekela Yeova? (Mwa. 3:1-5; 1 Yoa. 5:3)
Nĩkĩ ngelekany'o ya Eva nĩ ũkany'o kwitũ? (Avi. 4:8; Yak. 1:14, 15; 1 Yoa. 2: 16)
Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Atamu na Eva maleile kwĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo ala maumanie na meko moo? (Mwa. 3:12, 13)
Akeluvi ala maiĩtwe wumĩlonĩ wa syũa mũũndanĩ wa Eteni malũlũmĩĩilye ata ũsumbĩ mũnene wa Yeova? (Mwa. 3:24)
- Soma Ũvuan'yo 12:9.
Satani atonyete ata kwasya andũ matie ũsumbĩ wa Ngai? (1 Yoa. 5:19)

translation:
IT happened at every turn to hide itself. Adam and Eve were deceived by their loving son of Satan. Do we know why?
They both did something very bad. May Jehovah forgive them. Why do we think about what Adam and Eve did?
They did what God allowed. God made it possible to live forever among mankind. In one tree God made it forbidden, so they would not take from it. That tree was there for us. Do we understand whether doing something wrong is right, or is it wrong? Yes, let's see!
One day Eve was alone with her husband, the serpent who tempted her. What a terrible thing! Eve ate the fruit from the tree that God had made forbidden. Because of this, Jehovah punished the serpent by taking away its ability to speak. Who do you think used the serpent to tempt people? Is it true?
I am Adam. For this reason I will tell you one of the reasons why Jehovah allowed this to happen, so that we may learn. The reasons are clear, and we can understand. This angel has many eyes. He told me to be careful not to disobey God. And I want people to love him and those who love Jehovah. You are the angel who used the serpent to tempt Eve.
That angel deceived Eve. She believed that she would become like God if she ate the fruit, and Eve did. So she did, and Adam also did. Adam and Eve disobeyed God, and because of this, terrible things happened to their descendants.
One day God sent his spirit to the land of Eden. It is important for us to remember what happened with the first man and woman so that we can avoid making the same mistake. Let us look at how things turned out for Adam and Eve.
Revelation 2:16, 17; 3:1-13, 24; Revelation 12:9.
Questions
- What caused Adam and Eve to hide themselves?
- What did Jehovah allow?
- What did the serpent tell Eve?
- Who used the serpent to tempt Eve?
- Why did Adam and Eve lose the opportunity to live in Paradise?
Further Questions
- Read Revelation 2:16, 17 and 3:1-13,24.
What does the way the serpent tempted Eve teach us about how to resist temptation? (Gen. 3:1-5; 1 John 5:3)
Is Eve's excuse a good one? (Prov. 4:8; James 1:14, 15; 1 John 2: 16)
Why did Adam and Eve experience such bad consequences because of their choice? (Gen. 3:12, 13)
Did the perfect humans living in the garden of Eden realize the seriousness of disobeying Jehovah? (Gen. 3:24)
- Read Revelation 12:9.
Does Satan stop trying to mislead people away from God? (1 John 5:19)

text:
"Mũndũ, ũla ũsyaĩtwe nĩ mũndũ mũka, nĩ wa mĩthenya mĩvũthũ, na ausũĩte thĩna. Nĩwumĩlaa ta ĩlaa, na kũtilwa: nũsembaa ta muunyĩ, na ndekalaa."—Yovu 14:1, 2.
Kuma ĩvinda ya tene andũ nĩmasũanĩaa ũndũ thayũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũseo mayĩkala me na ũima wa mwĩĩ, na me ma mũika tene na tene. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana nĩtũkusaa. Kwoou, ndeto ila Yovu waneenie myaka mbee wa ngili itatũ mĩvĩtu nĩ sya w'o o na ũmũnthĩ.
Kĩla mũndũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩwĩthĩawa na wendi mwingĩ wa kwĩkala tene na tene. Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye kana Ngai nĩwĩkĩĩte wendi wa kwĩkala tene na tene ngoonĩ sitũ, na nĩtwĩthĩawa na mea ma kwona ũndũ ũsu ũianĩa. (Mũtavan'ya 3:11) Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, we wĩona Ngai wĩ wendo ta ũtonya kwĩkĩa wendi ũtakeanĩa ngoonĩ sitũ? Ethĩwa ũsũngĩo waku nĩ aiee, wasũngĩa ũla w'o. Ndeto ya Ngai yĩtĩte kĩkw'ũ mũmaitha na ĩkathana kana 'kĩkaanangwa.'—1 Akolintho 15:26.
Vai nzika kana kĩkw'ũ nĩ mũmaitha. Vaiĩ mũndũ wĩ kĩlĩko kĩseo wendeew'a nĩ kĩkw'ũ. Ĩla vaumĩla mũisyo nĩtũsembaa, tũkevitha, kana tũkakĩĩa vandũ vangĩ. Twawaa nĩtũmanthaa ũndũ tũtonya kũiitwa. O na ĩngĩ, nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya kwĩsiĩanĩa na maũndũ ala matonya kũtuma tũkw'a.
Yo ve ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma tũĩkĩĩa kana mũmaitha ũsu wa tene akaanangwa? Ĩĩ, wĩ vo. Mũmbi witũ, Yeova Ngai, ndaaũmba andũ mekalae myaka mĩnini na ĩtina maikw'a. Kuma mwambĩlĩĩlyonĩ, kĩeleelo kyake kĩyaĩ andũ makusae. Kĩeleelo kyake kyaĩ andũ mekalae ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene, na ndalea kũkĩanĩsya.—Isaia 55:11.
Kwoou, kĩkw'ũ kĩkaanangwa ata? Mũndũ ethĩĩtwe aitata mũno kũsiĩĩa kĩkw'ũ, ĩndĩ nĩwaemiwe. O na kũvika ũmũnthĩ no ũtataa. Andũ ma saenzi nĩmaseũvĩtye ndawa sya kũsiĩĩa na kũiita mowau amwe. O na nĩmasomete ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mĩĩ ya syĩndũ yũmbĩtwe. O na ĩngĩ, andũ kũndũ kwingĩ nĩmekalaa thayũ mũnango mbee wa ũndũ andũ mekalaa myaka 100 mĩvĩtu. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, kĩkw'ũ kĩyaaĩsa kũthela. Andũ "onthe masyokaa ĩngĩ kĩtoonĩ" o tondũ Mbivilia yaĩtye.—Mũtavan'ya 3:20.
Ũndũ wa kũtanĩthya nĩ kana vai vata wa kwĩkwatya ũĩ na ũmanyi wa mũndũ ũtũvetangĩe thĩna ũsu wĩthĩĩtwe vo kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Yeova Ngai nĩwĩkĩte mũvango wa kũtũtangĩĩa kuma kĩkw'ũnĩ, na Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwe ũkatũmĩwa kwĩanĩsya ũndũ ũsu.

translation:
"A person, when he is reproved by someone, it is for minor offenses, and he readily accepts correction. A patient one will endure until calamity comes, and will say: 'I have transgressed, but I will sin no more.'"—Job 14:1, 2.
However, the majority of people quickly become upset over any slight offense, and they get angry because of matters that are insignificant and trivial. Indeed, the matter of getting offended is often foolish. Truly, Job experienced severe suffering for seventy years and more, yet he remained upright.
Every individual who lives forever has a great desire to live forever. Many believe that God allows people to live forever so that they can enjoy life, and they hope to experience good things. (Ecclesiastes 3:11) But if this were true, would you not expect God to allow those who love him to enjoy life? The way God views death is different, and he considers it "sleep."—1 Corinthians 15:26.
So death is simply sleep. When a person dies, he is unaware of anything. But most people want to continue living, to accomplish something, or to help others. They fear what they do not understand. And also, they yearn for things they cannot attain and that prevent them from being happy.
Is there then a reason why we should fear death or think that this endless sleep will be permanent? No, you are right. Our Creator, Jehovah God, purposed mankind to live indefinitely and happily. However, his original purpose has been frustrated. His purpose was for mankind to live forever, and he will fulfill it.—Isaiah 55:11.
Really, can death be undone? Many individuals desire to undo death, but they are powerless. Even scientists have made limited progress in restoring life to those who have died. And yet, they have learned much about the complexity of the human body. Also, many people have lived beyond the age of 100 years. Yet even so, death still approaches. People "keep on dying," as the Bible states.—Ecclesiastes 3:20.
The problem of death is connected with man's desire to be independent and with his knowledge of good and bad. Jehovah God allows humans to experience the consequences of their choices, and Jesus Christ was sent to redeem us from this condition.

text:
WE NĨWĨSĨ mũndũ mũka ũũ wĩ vaa visanĩ? Syĩtwa yake nĩ Leveka. Na mũndũũme ũũ wũkĩte makomane nĩ Isaka. O mĩtũkĩ nũkũtw'ĩka mũka wake. Ũndũ ũsu weekĩkie ata?
Avalaamu ĩthe wa Isaka nĩwendaa mwana wake ethĩwe na mũka mũseo. We ndendaa Isaka atwae ũmwe wa aka ma Kanaani, nũndũ andũ asu mathaithaa ngai sya ũvũngũ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Avalaamu wamwĩtie mũthũkũmi wake na amwĩa: 'Nĩenda ũsyoke kwa andũ ma ũko wakwa ala matũaa Aalani na ũitwaĩa mwana wakwa Isaka mũka kuma kw'o.'
Vate kweteela mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu nĩwoosie ngamĩle ĩkũmi na athi kyalo kĩu kĩasa. Yĩla wavikie vakuvĩ na vala andũ ma ũko wa Avalaamu matwĩe, nĩwaũngamie vakuvĩ na kĩthima. Kwaĩ mawĩoo ĩvinda yĩla aka ma ndũa mookaa kũuta kĩw'ũ kĩthimanĩ kyu. Kwoou mũthũkumi wa Avalaamu amũvoya Yeova ayasya: 'Nĩkwĩthĩwe mwĩĩtu ũla ũkũnenga kĩw'ũ nĩnyw'e, na aisyoka ainenge ngamĩle nĩwe ũla ũnyuvĩte atw'ĩke mũka wa Isaka.'
O mĩtũkĩ Leveka nĩwookie kũuta kĩw'ũ. Yĩla mũthũkũmi ũsu wamwĩtisye kĩw'ũ anyw'e, nĩwamũnengie. Na ĩndĩ nĩwaendie na aete kĩw'ũ kĩtoetye kũnyuwa nĩ ngamĩle isu syaĩ na waũni. Ũsu waĩ wĩa wĩ vinya nũndũ ngamĩle inyusaa kĩw'ũ kingĩ mũno.
Yĩla Leveka waminie kwĩka ũu, mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu nĩwamũkũlilye syĩtwa ya ĩthe wake. Ĩngĩ nĩwamũkũlilye kana nũtonya kũkomela kwoo ũtukũ ũsu. Nake asũngĩa: 'Syĩtwa ya ĩthe wakwa nĩ Mbethũeli, na twĩna ũthei waku wa kwĩkala vamwe naitũ.' Mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu nĩweesĩ kana Mbethũeli aĩ mwana wa Naoli, mwana-a-inyia wa Avalaamu. Kwoou atulya ndu na kũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea kwa kũmũtongoesya kũvika kwa andũ ma ũko wa Avalaamu.
Ũtukũ o ũsu mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu nĩwamũtavisye Mbethũeli na Lavani, mwana-a-inyia wa Leveka, kĩtumi kya kũka kwoo. Elĩ nĩmeetĩkĩlanile kana Leveka no athi nake na kũtwawa nĩ Isaka. Leveka aisye ata ĩla wakũlilw'e? We nĩweetĩkĩlile kũthi. Kwoou o ũnĩ ũsu nĩmatũlile ngamĩle na mambĩĩa kyalo kĩasa kya kũsyoka Kanaani.
Mavikie mawĩoo na Leveka oona mũndũũme aitembea kĩsesinĩ. Mũndũũme ũsu aĩ Isaka. Nake nĩwatanie mũno kũmwona Leveka. Sala inyia wa Isaka aĩ anakw'a myaka ĩtatũ yaĩ mĩthelu, na Isaka aĩ na kyeva nũndũ wa ũndũ ũsu. Ĩndĩ nĩwamwendie Leveka mũno, na eethĩwa na ũtanu ĩngĩ.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:1-67.
Makũlyo
- Mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka aa me visanĩ naaũ?
- Avalaamu eekie ata nĩ kana amũtwaĩe mwana wake mũka na nĩkĩ?
- Mboya ya mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu yasũngĩiwe ata?
- Leveka asũngĩie ata yĩla wakũlilw'e kana nũkwenda kũtwawa nĩ Isaka?
- Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Isaka ethĩwa na ũtanu ĩngĩ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:1-67.
Leveka oonanisye ndaĩa myaũ nzeo yĩla wakomanĩie na mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu kĩthimanĩ? (Mwa. 24:17-20; Nth. 31:17, 31)
Mũvango wa Avalaamu kwoondũ wa Isaka wĩmanenga Aklĩsto ngelekany'o myaũ nzeo ũmũnthĩ? (Mwa. 24:37, 38; 1 Ako. 7:39; 2 Ako. 6:14)
Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩtwe nĩkũmantha ĩvinda ya kũvindĩĩasya kwa ũito o tondũ Isaka weekie? (Mwa. 24:63; Sav. 77:12; Avi. 4:8)

translation:
Do you know anyone who has ever been circumcised? His name is Leveka. And this man's brother is Isaka. Oh children, let us go to his home. Did you hear that?
But Isaka's wife wanted her son to be with a beautiful woman. I want Isaka to take one of the girls from Canaan, so that our people may serve the God of heaven. That is why Abraham sent his servant and told him: 'I want you to go to my relatives and get a wife for my son Isaac.'
The servant of Abraham took ten camels and various gifts and went. He arrived and sat outside the well during the evening when the women of the town came out to draw water, and he prayed. In the evening, one of those girls came to draw water and said to him: 'Let me drink some water.' So Abraham's servant praised the Lord and said: 'Show me favor, so that I may find a wife for Isaac among those who come here to draw water.'
Oh children, Leveka went to draw water. As this girl approached the well to draw water, he met her. And she went and filled her jar with water and carried it. Now you see how the camels drank until they were full. The servant asked about her family.
When Abraham's servant learned her name, it was Rivka. And he inquired about her father and where she lived. Her father said: 'My daughter's name is Rivka, and we have plenty of food and lodging.' The servant bowed down and praised the Lord and said: 'This is the one whom the Lord has chosen to be the wife of Isaac's son.'
Then Rivka went to meet Laban and Leah, the daughters of Bethuel, to discuss the matter. But she did not tell them what had happened until Isaac returned. Rivka didn't say anything until she heard. So today we remember the camels and their journey to Canaan.
Consider also with Leveka, this young man who walked slowly. This young man was Isaac. He wanted to see Leveka again. His mother Sarah died when Isaac was thirty-five years old, and Isaac mourned his mother. Then he went to Leveka, and she became his wife.
Genesis 24:1-67.
Questions
- Does a person need to be beautiful to please God?
- Did Abraham send his servant to find a wife for his son for no reason?
- Was Abraham's servant successful in his mission?
- Did Leveka know why she was being sent to marry Isaac?
- What made Isaac pray and become comforted?
Further Questions
- Read Genesis 24:1-67.
How did Leveka show kindness and hospitality to Abraham's servant? (Gen. 24:17-20; Prov. 31:17, 31)
How does Abraham's concern for Isaac remind Christians of our love for others? (Gen. 24:37, 38; 1 Cor. 7:39; 2 Cor. 6:14)
What can we learn from meditating on the example of Isaac's prayer? (Gen. 24:63; Ps. 77:12; Lam. 4:8)

text:
Ndongoi sya ulei nisyakulwa kunenga silikali nzau ungu wa utongoi wa president William Samoei Ruto yanya iseo ya kuthukuma mwenenthi na kwianiisya mawatho mayo.
Ni ndeto ila syawetwa ni Ambassador Kiema Kilonzo nthini wa valua kwa nyumba sya mauvoo, aisungia uneeni wake ndongoi ya kyama kya Wiper Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka ila unaaneenie kyumwani aivuthiisya utongoi wa Ruto, matuku mavuthu alika kivilani.
Kilonzo niwaweta kana Kalonzo aile ni kukunikila ivindani yila waithiwa silikalini vala uneekunie kithui kuthukuma nayo Kuma mwakani wa 1985 nginya atwikithwa munini wa president mwakani wa 2012 na itina aweta wandani akethiawa mundu wa moko wa president unathyumuiye wiya Uhuru Kenyatta ateo amutula muti kwa kulea kuthinikia kisio kya Ukamba vala maundu ta yua na ujya syikiinyiite vanene.
Ovaluani usu niwamukaathiiya Dr. Ruto kwa kivathia ilembeta ya Ukamba myanya ya maminista ana evo Dr. Alfred Mutua- maundu ma nthi sya nza, Peninah Malonza- utalii na Monicah Juma mutai maunduni ma useeseeyi na kwithiwa anatheeisye thoowa wa mbolea ila ikwithiwa iyailya uimi na kuukitana na nzaa atena kikono kya undu wakwatie kula Kuma kisioni kii.
Kiema niwaweta kana enenthi nimanaasakuiye ndongoi wina muikiiyo kana nikutwaa Kenya mbee vate ivathukanyo, ainyungunyisya utongoi wa Kalonzo ula ukuweta niwa kithui kwa kwithiwa Wiper itaanengane ivuso kwa enenthi isioni imwe kutwaiisya muthungululo, undu ula waimie mwenenthi haki yake ya unyuvi na akathiiya muvea wa Makoti kwa kuungama na u'wo.
Niwaweta kana ivinda ya ngavano na uteti niivititwe ni ivinda aiweta muikiiyo wake kwa Ruto kwailya ukwati wa Kenya kwisila mitalatala wa bottom up economic model.

translation:
The issue of oil has sparked debate about the impact of President William Samoei Ruto's leadership and the reasons for his popularity and strengthening influence.
It is a matter that has been discussed by Ambassador Kiema Kilonzo within the walls of power, who previously served as a spokesperson for Wiper party leader Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka but now seems to support Ruto's leadership, despite past differences.
Kilonzo stated that Kalonzo should focus on addressing issues affecting people rather than dwelling on old grievances dating back to 1985 when he was appointed vice president in 2012 and later claimed that someone like President Uhuru Kenyatta had undermined him, leading to difficulties in uniting the Kamba region because things were done unfairly and openly.
Recently, there have been concerns regarding Dr. Ruto's appointments from the Kamba region, including Dr. Alfred Mutua - water, Peninah Malonza - tourism, and Monica Juma - defense, with accusations that she favors certain individuals while neglecting others and engaging in conflicts over land ownership, causing unrest among the people.
Kiema stated that this situation may be due to internal divisions within the country or a desire to see Kenya progress, criticizing Kalonzo's leadership and suggesting that Wiper will struggle to win elections without a unified approach to achieving development, denying people their right to livelihood and exploiting the resources of Makoti through collusion.
He added that the problem of poverty and hunger can only be solved by addressing the challenges facing Kenyans and implementing the bottom-up economic model.

text:
YESŨ nĩwavoasya awau o aendee na kyalo kyake kũthyũlũlũka nthĩ ĩsu yonthe. Ũvoo wa syama isu nĩwatavaniw'e mĩsyĩnĩ na ndũanĩ syonthe ila syaĩ vakuvĩ. Kwoou andũ mamũetee ala maĩ syonze na ilalinda na ala matatonya kũneena, na awau angĩ aingĩ. Na Yesũ amavosya onthe.
Yu myaka ĩtatũ na kĩndũ nĩ mĩvĩtu kuma yĩla Yoana wavatisie Yesũ. Kwoou Yesũ amea amanyĩw'a make kana o mĩtũkĩ akambata athi Yelusaleme, kũla ũkoaĩwa na ĩndĩ aithayũũkw'a. Ĩndĩ atanamba kũthi Yelusaleme, Yesũ nĩwaendeeie na kũvosya awau.
Mũthenya ũmwe Yesũ nĩwamanyĩasya mũthenya wa Savato. Savato waĩ mũthenya wa kũthũmũa wa Ayuti. Mũndũ mũka ũũ ũkwona vaa ethĩĩtwe e mũwau mũno. Kwa myaka 18 we aendaa akunguutĩtye, na ndaĩ atonya kũũngalala. Kwoou Yesũ amwilĩĩla moko make, na ambĩĩa kũũngalala. Nake avoa!
Ũndũ ũsu nĩwathatisye atongoi ma ndĩni mũno. Na ũmwe woo akũthũkĩa ĩkomano ayasya, 'Kwĩ mĩthenya thanthatũ ĩla twaĩlwe nĩ kũtethya wĩa. Ĩsu nĩyo mĩthenya ya kũka mũvow'e, ĩndĩ ti mũthenya wa Savato!'
Nake Yesũ asũngĩa: 'Inyw'ĩ andũ athũku. Kĩla ũmwe wenyu ndathaasya ĩng'oi yake vala yovetwe mũthenya wa Savato akatwaa kũyĩnyithya? Kwoou mũndũ mũka ũũ mũthĩni, ũtwĩe e mũwau myaka 18, ndaĩlĩte nĩ kũvow'a mũthenya wa Savato?' Ũsũngĩo wa Yesũ watumie andũ asu athũku masonoka.
Ĩtina Yesũ na atũmwa make nĩmaendeeie na kyalo melekele Yelusaleme. Na me nza ya ndũa ya Yeliko, ilalinda ilĩ syaĩ avoyi ma syĩndũ syeew'a kana Yesũ nũvĩtĩte. Kwoou syaneena na wasya mũnene iyasya: 'Yesũ, tũtethye!'
Yesũ nĩweetie aũme asu ilalinda na amakũlya: 'Mwĩenda nĩmwĩke ata?' Namo masya: 'Mwĩaĩi, tũsalukye metho maitũ.' Yesũ akiita metho moo, na vau kwa vau mambĩĩa kwona! We nĩwĩsĩ nĩkĩ Yesũ weekaa syama ii syonthe nzeo? Kĩtumi nũndũ nĩwendete andũ na nĩweendaa mamũĩkĩĩe. Kwoou nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ũ w'o kana yĩla ũkatw'ĩka Mũsumbĩ vaiĩ mũndũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ũkawaa ĩngĩ.
Mathayo 15:30, 31; Luka 13:10-17; Mathayo 20:29-34.
Makũlyo
- Yesũ eekie ata o aendee na kũthi kũũ na kũũ nthĩ ĩsu yonthe?
- Yesũ atavisye atũmwa make ata myaka ĩtatũ ĩtina wa ũvatiso wake?
- Andũ aa me visanĩ naaũ, na Yesũ eĩkana ata na mũndũ mũka ũũ?
- Nĩkĩ ũsũngĩo wa Yesũ kwa ũvinganĩsya wa atongoi ma ndĩni watumie masonoka?
- Yĩla Yesũ na atũmwa make maĩ vakuvĩ na Yeliko, Yesũ amekie ata avoyi elĩ ilalinda?
- Yesũ ekaa syama nĩkĩ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mathayo 15:30, 31.
Yesũ oonanisye ata vinya wa Yeova kwa nzĩa ya ũsengy'a, na ũu waĩlĩte kũtuma twĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala Yeova wathanĩte makonanĩtye na nthĩ nzaũ? (Sav. 37:29; Isa. 33:24)
- Soma Luka 13:10-17.
Nũndũ Yesũ eekie imwe sya syama syake nene vyũ mũthenya wa Savato, ũu wĩonany'a ata ĩũlũ wa ũthyũmũo ũla we ũkaetee andũ ĩvinda ya Ũsumbĩ wake wa Myaka Ngili? (Lk. 13:10-13; Sav. 46:9; Mt. 12:8; Ako. 2:16, 17; Ũvu. 21:1-4)
- Soma Mathayo 20:29-34.
Ũvoo ũũ wĩonany'a ata kana Yesũ ndetalaa ta wĩna wĩa mwingĩ mũno ũndũ ũtatonya kũtethya andũ, na tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na ũndũ ũsu? (Kũt. 15:7; Yak. 2:15, 16; 1 Yoa. 3:17)

translation:
JESUS went around teaching them and his disciples to reveal everything. The day of judgment will come unexpectedly with all kinds of troubles but only for the wicked. Now people who believe this say it is near and it is happening, and they are very afraid. And JESUS was moved deeply.
After three years and some time, John testified about JESUS. Now JESUS knew he would soon be captured and taken to Jerusalem, to suffer greatly and be killed. As he approached Jerusalem, JESUS continued teaching and moving among the people.
One day JESUS healed a man on the Sabbath. The Sabbath was a day of rest for the Jews. This man had been sick for eighteen years and could not stand up straight. Now JESUS looked at him and told him to stand up straight. And he stood up!
This made the synagogue leader angry. He said, "There are six days when work should be done. These are the days for working, not the Sabbath!"
Then JESUS replied, "Hypocrites! Doesn't each of you untie his ox or donkey on the Sabbath to lead it to water? Or wouldn't you pull someone out of a well on the Sabbath?" Jesus began to heal many people, and everyone was amazed.
Then JESUS and his apostles went on to villages around Jerusalem. On the road towards Jericho, a large crowd followed him because they heard he was healing the sick. A blind man sitting by the roadside cried out, "JESUS, have mercy on me!"
JESUS stopped and asked him and the crowd, "What do you want me to do for you?" They said, "Lord, let us see again." JESUS had compassion on them and healed their eyes, and immediately they were able to see! Everyone wondered if JESUS really did all these things himself. But people spread the news about him everywhere. So we can trust him and know that he cares for us, just like he cared for those people. Because we can always rely on him, even when life seems difficult.
Matthew 15:30, 31; Luke 13:10-17; Matthew 20:29-34.
Questions
- Did JESUS go around teaching and revealing everything?
- Did JESUS send his apostles out three years after his baptism?
- Were these people moved by pity, and did JESUS show kindness to this man?
- Does JESUS' ministry demonstrate that God's purpose will succeed?
- When JESUS and his apostles approached Jericho, did JESUS stop and help the people who were waiting?
- What miracle did JESUS perform?
Further Questions
- Read Matthew 15:30, 31.
Did JESUS please Jehovah by showing compassion, and does this remind us that Jehovah wants us to be compassionate toward others? (Ps. 37:29; Isa. 33:24)
- Read Luke 13:10-17.
When JESUS healed a woman on the Sabbath, does this illustrate how his teachings could free people from the bondage of religious tradition? (Lu. 13:10-13; Ps. 46:9; Matt. 12:8; Acts 2:16, 17; Rev. 21:1-4)
- Read Matthew 20:29-34.
Does this account show that JESUS valued humility over power, and can we learn something from this example? (Prov. 15:7; Jas. 2:15, 16; 1 John 3:17)

text:
1. Ve ũvoo mwaũ mũseo ĩũlũ wa ala akw'ũ?
Ĩla Yesũ waendie Vethania, mũsyĩ waĩ vakuvĩ na Yelusaleme, eethĩie mũnyanyae Lasalo aminĩte mĩthenya ĩna kuma akw'a. Yesũ aendie mbũanĩ e na Matha na Meli, eĩtũ-a-inyia ma Lasalo. Ĩtina wa kavinda, andũ aingĩ nĩmookie vau. Kwasũanĩa Matha na Meli maĩ na ũtanu wĩana ata ĩla Yesũ wathayũũkisye Lasalo?
Matha nĩweesĩ ũvoo mũseo ĩũlũ wa akw'ũ. Nĩweesĩ kana Yeova akathayũũkya ala akw'ũ mekale ĩngĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
2. Akw'ũ mailyĩ ata?
Andũ moombiwe kuma kĩtoonĩ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:7; 3:19) Ithyĩ ti maveva me nthĩnĩ wa mĩĩ ya nyama na nthakame. Kwoou ĩla twakw'a, vaiĩ kĩndũ kĩ nthĩnĩ witũ kĩtakusaa. Ĩla twakw'a, w'ongo witũ nũkusaa, na mesilya maitũ mayaa. Kwoou, nũndũ akw'ũ mayĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva, vaiĩ ũndũ Lasalo waaweta wĩthĩwa oonie ĩvinda yĩla waĩ mũkw'ũ.
We Ngai nũthĩnasya andũ mwakinĩ ĩtina wa mamina kũkw'a? Nũndũ Mbivilia yonanasya akw'ũ mayĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva, kũthĩnw'a mwakinĩ nĩ ĩmanyĩsyo ya ũvũngũ yĩla yĩtumaa andũ mailĩĩla Ngai ũndũ ũtekaa. O na yĩsilya ya kũthĩny'a andũ mwakinĩ nĩ ũthatyo kwake.
3. Akw'ũ nĩmatonya kũneena naitũ?
Akw'ũ maitonya kũneena kana kwĩw'a. (Savuli 115:17) Ĩndĩ ve alaĩka amwe athũku, na nĩmatonya kũneena na andũ mayĩtw'a nĩmo andũ ala makwie. (2 Vetelo 2:4) Yeova nũtũvatĩte kũtata kũneena na akw'ũ.
4. Naaũ ala methayũũkw'a?
Andũ milioni mbingĩ ala makwie makathayũũkw'a mekale kũũ nthĩ. O na amwe makwie matamwĩsĩ Ngai na meekaa maũndũ mathũku makathayũũkw'a.
Ala methayũũkw'a makeethĩwa matonya kwĩmanyĩsya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai na mayonany'a kana me na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa Yesũ kwa kũmwĩw'a. (Ũvuan'yo 20:11-13) Ala methayũũkw'a na mayĩka moseo makeethĩwa matonya kũtanĩa thayũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene.
5. Ũthayũũkyo ũtũmanyĩasya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova?
Ngai atumie vethĩwa na wĩkwatyo kwa ala akw'ũ kwa kũmũtũma Mwana wake akw'e kwondũ witũ. Kwoou ũthayũũkyo ũtũmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa wendo wa Yeova na mumo wake. Ĩla akw'ũ methayũũkw'a, nũũ wĩenda kwona mũno vyũ?

translation:
1. Do you know why God allowed this bad thing to happen?
Jesus went to Bethany, near Jerusalem, where Lazarus' sister Martha lived with her sister Mary. Jesus also went there because he heard about Lazarus' death. Many people came to comfort them. While Martha and Mary were talking, they wondered why Jesus had delayed coming.
Martha said, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died." She also believed that God could raise her brother back to life.
2. Why should we trust God?
We often don't understand why things happen. (Proverbs 2:7; 3:19) It seems unfair when good people suffer. But remember that God cares about us deeply. When we trust him, we will find strength. When we trust him, our hope won't be lost, and our future will be bright. So, let us continue to trust God, even when things seem difficult, knowing that Lazarus was raised from the dead to show us what God can do.
Does God cause suffering? The Bible does not say that God causes suffering, but explains that allowing suffering helps people appreciate his love and encourages them to seek him. And teaching people about God is his purpose.
3. How can we speak courageously?
We can speak courageously, even when afraid. (Psalm 115:17) We can pray for help, and we can speak courageously to others who feel the same way. (2 Timothy 2:4) Jehovah gives us the power to speak courageously.
4. Have many people been resurrected?
Millions of faithful people have been resurrected over time. Some who were once unfaithful to God and did wrong things have been resurrected.
Those who are resurrected can demonstrate their gratitude to God by praising him and showing love for Jesus by obeying him. (Revelation 20:11-13) Those who are resurrected and live forever can enjoy life on earth forever.
5. What will resurrection teach us about Jehovah?
God used resurrections and his dealings with those resurrected to send his Son to die for us. This will teach us about Jehovah's love and his purpose. But what if someone you know has died—will they be resurrected?

Itindo nthũkũ nĩsyanangaa mwĩkalĩle mũseo.—1 Ako. 15:33.
Ethĩwa tũikwenda kwananga mwĩkalĩle witũ, tũyaĩle kũtuma ndũũ na ala mekaa mothũku. O na tũyaĩle kũtuma ndũũ na ala meyĩtaa athaithi ma Yeova ĩndĩ matũlaa mĩao yake na ngũlũ. Ngũsĩ ta isu syeeka naĩ ngito na syaema kwĩlila, nĩtũtilaa kĩtindo kitũ nasyo. (Alo. 16:17, 18) Twatuma ndũũ na ala mataatĩĩaa mĩao ya Ngai, no laisi o naitũ tũkambĩĩa kwĩka tamo nĩ kana matwende. Ta kwa ngelekany'o, twatuma ndũũ na ilaalai, no laisi o naitũ tũkalika ũlaalainĩ. Aklĩsto amwe avatise nĩmalikile thĩnanĩ ta ũsu, na amwe moo nĩmatengiwe nũndũ mayaaĩlila. (1 Ako. 5:11-13) Makaema kwĩsa kũmũsyokea Yeova, mesa kũvika vala Vetelo wawetie.—2 Vet. 2:20-22. w15 8/15 4:4-6
Inyw'ĩ mwĩ anyanyawa, ethĩwa nĩmwĩkaa maũndũ ala nĩmwĩaĩaa.—Yoa. 15:14.
Yesũ ndatumaa ndũũ ngamu na kĩla mũndũ. Andũ ta asu waĩ ndũũ namo amanyuvaa katĩ wa andũ ala malũmanĩtye nake na mamũthaithaa Yeova na ngoo yonthe. We ũnyuvaa anyanyau katĩ wa ala mamũthũkũmaa Yeova na ngoo yonthe? Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ waĩlĩte kũtuma ndũũ na andũ ta asu? Wendo wa ana-a-asa no ũkũtetheesye wĩane kĩ-veva. Kwa ngelekany'o, we wĩ mũndũ wa mũika ũkũtata kũmanthĩthya nĩ kyaũ ũkenda kwĩka eana? Wĩ mũndũ mũĩ ethĩwa nũtindanasya na ana-a-asa ala angĩ methĩĩtwe maimũthũkũma Yeova kwa ĩvinda ĩasanga na methĩĩtwe mailũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo kĩkundinĩ! No kwĩthĩwa makomanĩte na maũndũ metu, o na no kwĩthĩwa makwatĩtwe nĩ matatwa mana myaka yonthe ĩla mamũthũkũmĩte Ngai. Kwoou andũ ta asu nĩmatonya kũũtetheesya wĩvangĩĩe ũndũ ũla mũseo vyũ. Kĩtindo kĩseo kya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asu no kĩũtetheesye wĩke motwi maseo na ũiendeea kwĩana kĩ-veva.—Aevl. 5:14. w15 9/15 1:14, 15
Mũsiĩĩei [Ndevili mũlũmĩte] mũĩkĩĩonĩ wenyu.—1 Vet. 5:9.
Meko ma Yesũ na ndeto syake nĩsyatumaa mũĩkĩĩo wa amanyĩw'a make wĩthĩwa wĩ mũlũmu. (Mko. 11:20-24) Nĩtwaĩlĩte kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake nũndũ ĩla tũũtetheesya ala angĩ malũlũmĩlye mũĩkĩĩo woo twĩthĩawa tũilũlũmĩlya ũla witũ. (Nth. 11:25) Kwoou, ĩla ũũtavany'a na ĩla ũũmanyĩsya andũ weta maũndũ ala matũĩkĩĩthasya kana Ngai e kw'o, na kana nĩwĩanĩasya mavata maitũ, na kana Mbivilia nĩ Ndeto yake mbeveee. O na ĩngĩ tetheesya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maku make mũĩkĩĩo woo. Ethĩwa amwe nĩmekwonany'a ta mambĩĩe kũya nzika, kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa nĩmambĩĩe kũnyungunyĩsya ana-a-asa ala manyuvĩtwe matongoesye, ndũkasembee kũtila kĩtindo kyaku namo. Vandũ va ũu tũmĩa ũĩ ũmatetheesye mose matambya ala matonya kũtũngĩĩa mũĩkĩĩo woo. (Yuta 22, 23) Ethĩwa wĩ sukulu na nĩmwambĩĩa kũmanyĩw'a kana syũmbe syeekie kwĩyumĩlya, tetea mũĩkĩĩo waku wĩ na ũkũmbaũ. Na weeka ũu nũtonya kũseng'w'a mũno nĩ woni ũla ala angĩ matonya kwĩthĩwa naw'o. Yeova nũtetheeasya kĩla ũmwe witũ aũngame alũmĩte mũĩkĩĩonĩ. (1 Vet. 5:10) Tweekĩa kĩthito twake mũĩkĩĩo witũ tũikethĩawa tũitethya wĩa wa mana nũndũ mũĩkĩĩo ũtumaa tũkwata moathimo tũtamona vangĩ. w15 9/15 3:20, 21

translation:
Indeed the teaching is delightful to a wise heart.—1 Cor. 15:33.
Let us go on delighting in our Father's teaching, letting it move us to preach and to make disciples. And let us delight in preaching and making disciples of Jehovah among people of all languages and nations. Let us not become lazy or discouraged when we meet opposition, but let us enjoy this work also. (Phil. 16:17, 18) We preach and make disciples of God's Word, and we trust that he will direct our steps. So, brothers, we preach with zeal, and we trust that Jehovah will bless us. A Christian might be afflicted with illness or pain, and some may have problems that cause them distress. (1 Cor. 5:11-13) But they continue to seek Jehovah, and they find comfort in Bible counsel.—2 Tim. 2:20-22. w15 8/15 4:4-6
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.—Prov. 15:14.
Jesus sent me forth with good news to everyone. People who respond to the good news rejoice greatly because of their association with those who love Jehovah and his organization. Do you rejoice greatly because of your association with those who love Jehovah and his organization? What can you do to encourage others? The example of Asaph and his family is instructive. For instance, if you know someone who is struggling to remain faithful, what can you do to help him? A person should always be ready to sympathize with fellow worshipers of Jehovah who are experiencing trials and difficulties. And we should be willing to share our resources with those who need material assistance throughout the year. Many people today are finding it difficult to make ends meet. This example of Asaph and his household shows us how to use our means wisely and to be generous.—Eph. 5:14. w15 9/15 1:14, 15
Be well-trained spiritual men yourselves.—1 Pet. 5:9.
Jesus and his disciples often used illustrations to make their message clear. (Mark 11:20-24) We can imitate their example by using illustrations when we preach and by helping others to understand Bible truth more fully. (Prov. 11:25) So, if you encounter objections or misunderstandings, or if people question God's ways, or if they express doubts about the Bible and its authority, be prepared to use illustrations to help them. Also, be willing to assist fellow worshipers in strengthening their faith. Some may find it hard to apply Bible principles to everyday life; for example, some may struggle to discipline children, so help them to see how Bible principles can be applied. Let us all strive to become skilled in using illustrations to help people appreciate the value of God's Word. (Judg. 22, 23) At school, you might have opportunities to show your classmates that you value Bible principles, and this could lead to interesting conversations. And at times, you may be able to comfort someone who is discouraged. Jehovah helps each of us to become spiritually mature. (1 Pet. 5:10) By regularly exercising our spirituality, we strengthen our faith and increase our ability to endure trials. w15 9/15 3:20, 21

text:
"Ĩvw'ĩkei ngoo . . . ya kwĩw'anĩa tei, wĩnyivyo, ũuu, wũmĩĩsyo."
Mũtwaano wĩthĩawa new'o mwambĩlĩĩlyo wa mũsyĩ, na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake nĩwe waĩle kwĩthĩwa e mũndũ wa vata mũno kwaku. Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana ndũkethĩawa ũimenda na kũmanenga asyai maku ndaĩa. Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwa andũ amwe ma mũsyĩ kwĩtĩkĩla kana ũla ũtwaanĩte nake nĩwe mũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ kwaku. Ĩndĩ myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũkamanya ũndũ waĩle kwĩka nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na mũuo na andũ asu ma mũsyĩ, o ũendeee kũlũlũmĩĩlya ngwatanĩo yaku vamwe na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake na syana syenyu.
1 ĨTHĨWA NA WONI ŨLA WAĨLĨTE ĨŨLŨ WA ANDŨ MENYU MA MŨSYĨ
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Taĩa au na mwenyu." (Aeveso 6:2) O na ethĩwa wĩ na ũkũũ wĩana ata, no nginya ĩvinda yonthe ũmanengae ndaĩa asyai maku. O na ĩngĩ manya kana mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake e na asyai, na nĩwaĩle kũmathĩnĩkĩa. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana 'wendo ndwĩ kĩwĩu,' kwoou ndũkethĩwe na wia, ũisũanĩa kana ngwatanĩo yaku na mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake nĩtonya kwanangwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu.—1 Akolintho 13:4; Akalatia 5:26.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Ti ũseo kũtũmĩa ndeto ta, "Andũ menyu mainengae ndaĩa o na vanini," kana "Inyia waku ndendeeaw'a nongi nĩ maũndũ ala nĩkaa"
Tata wone maũndũ ũndũ mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake ũmonaa
2 TW'A MAŨNDŨ KWA ŨLŨMU ĨLA VE VATA WA KWĨKA ŨU
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Mũndũ mũũme akatia ĩthe na nyinyia, na akalũmany'a na mũka wake: nao makeethĩwa mwĩĩ ũmwe." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:24) Ĩla watwaana kana watwawa, asyai maku nĩmatonya kwĩw'a maĩle ũkũtongoesya maũndũnĩ mana, na nĩvatonyeka makenda kũmwĩyĩaĩa ũndũ mũkwĩka.
We na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake nĩmwaĩle kwĩtĩkĩlana nĩ maũndũ meva asyai mataĩle kũlikĩlĩĩla, na ĩndĩ mũimaelesya maũndũ asu kwa nzĩa nzeo. Nĩmũtonya kũmaelesya kĩla kĩndũ nesa mũteũmony'a kĩvũthya. (Nthimo 15:1) Mweethĩwa na wĩnyivyo, ũuu, na wũmĩĩsyo, mũkeethĩwa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na andũ ma mũsyĩ, na mũiendeea 'kũmĩanĩsya inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo.'—Aeveso 4:2.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Ethĩwa nũũthĩnĩka nĩ ũndũ andũ ma mũsyĩ malikĩlĩĩle mũsyĩ waku, mantha ĩvinda yĩla yaĩlĩte mũneenee ũndũ ũsu wĩ na mũũme waku kana kĩveti kyaku
Ĩw'ana na mũũme waku kana kĩveti kyaku ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũtonya kũthĩnĩkĩa ũndũ ũsu

translation:
"Behold, here is… the time to be intimate, my beloved, yes, I miss you."
This matter is important because of the seriousness of life, and the person who understands this well is the one who wants to be careful with a good person always. It is not right to just rush and make mistakes and regret them later. Be careful about things that happen among some people concerning life so that the person who understands this well does not fall into trouble. According to the teachings of the Bible, it is not good to be ignorant of what is happening or being done by others, or continue deceiving yourself with those who understand it and your children.
1 BE CAREFUL WITH THE ONE WHO UNDERSTANDS LIFE AMONG YOUR PEOPLE
THE BIBLE SAYS: "Associate with the wise." (Proverbs 6:2) And be careful with your behavior at all times and regret nothing later. Also know that the person who understands this is often troubled, and it is good to be patient. The Bible says that 'love is kind,' meaning that your relationship with the person who understands this should not be broken easily.—1 Corinthians 13:4; Galatians 5:26.
THINGS TO AVOID:
Don't say things like, "My people hate me or they are jealous," or "Your words hurt me because of these things"
Consider what the person who understands this sees
2 LET US DISCUSS THINGS IN A WAY THAT HELPS THOSE WHO WANT TO UNDERSTAND THIS
THE BIBLE SAYS: "A capable man marries and has children, and his wife will also be united with him." (Genesis 2:24) But if they quarrel or fight, regret can come, and they may fail to explain things clearly.
Also, the person who understands this is often willing to listen to new ideas and learn, and he tries to understand things from a different perspective. It is possible to understand everything if you ask questions. (Psalm 15:1) Be humble, honest, and sincere, and be patient with others, and try to 'speak kindly to each other with love.'—Ephesians 4:2.
THINGS TO AVOID:
Be careful not to let others control your life, so that you regret the mistakes you have made with your spouse or family
Talk to your spouse or family about what you want to avoid

AKLĨSTO nĩmeĩaĩwe methĩawe maililikana kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto. Ũlilikano ũsu now'o wĩtawa "kyaũya kya wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi." (1 Akolintho 11:
Yesũ Klĩsto ambĩlĩĩilye Ũlilikano ũsu wĩoo wa Vasaka ya Ayuti mwaka wa 33 Ĩ.Y. Vasaka yeethĩawa kĩla mwaka mũthenya wa 14 wa mwei wa Ayuti wĩtawa Nisani. Mwei ũsu wambĩĩa yĩla mwai watisa ĩtina wa kyumwa kya mbee kya Mwei wa 3. Kuma mũthenya ũsu Ayuti matalaa mĩthenya 14 na mũthenya wa Vasaka ũivika. Vasaka yeethĩawa mũthenya ũsu wa 14 syũa yathũa.
Yesũ aĩye Vasaka na atũmwa make, na amina kũmwĩa Yutasi Isikaliote aumaale, ambĩlĩĩlya Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi. Kyaũya kĩu nĩkyo kyambĩĩie kũlilikanawa vandũ va Vasaka. Kwoou kyaĩle kũlilikanawa o ĩmwe kĩla mwaka.
Ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Mathayo yaĩty'e ũũ: "Yesũ oosa kĩmũtũ, akĩathima, na akĩtilanga; na anenga amanyĩw'a, na asya, Osai, mũye; kĩĩ nĩkyo mwĩĩ wakwa. Na oosa kĩkombe, na atũnga mũvea na amanenga, akyasya, Nyw'ai inyw'onthe; nũndũ ĩno nĩyo nthakame yakwa ya ũtianĩo, ĩla ĩĩtĩkw'a kwondũ wa aingĩ kwa ũekeo wa naĩ."
Andũ amwe maĩkĩĩaa Yesũ aalyũlile kĩmũtũ kyatw'ĩka nyama ya mwĩĩ wake na mbinyu yatw'ĩka nthakame yake mwene. Ĩndĩ mwĩĩ wa Yesũ waĩ o mũima yĩla wanenganae kĩmũtũ kĩu. Mo atũmwa ma Yesũ nĩmethĩwa maĩye nyama yake na kũnyw'a nthakame yake? Vaitonyeka nũndũ ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩwa wamatwie malyandũ na mĩao ya Ngai nĩvatanĩte kũya nyama sya mũndũ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 9:
Kwoou kĩmũtũ na mbinyu no ngelekany'o. Kĩmũtũ nĩ ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩ wa Yesũ mwĩanĩu. Yesũ atũmĩie kĩmũtũ kĩla kyatialĩte mamina kũya Vasaka. Kĩmũtũ kĩu kyaseũvĩtw'e kĩte ĩlawa. (Kuma 12:8) Mbivilia ĩtũmĩaa ĩlawa kũyĩelekany'a na naĩ kana wanangĩko. Kwoou kĩmũtũ nĩ ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩ mwĩanĩu wa Yesũ ũla waumisye ta nthembo. Mwĩĩ ũsu ndwaĩ na naĩ.
Mbinyu ndune nĩ ngelekany'o ya nthakame ya Yesũ. Nthakame ĩsu nĩyo yĩtĩkĩlasya na kũlũlũmĩĩlya ũtianĩo mweũ. Yesũ aisye nthakame yake nĩyetĩkiw'e "kwa ũekeo wa naĩ." Nũndũ wa nthakame ĩsu andũ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa me atheu mbee wa metho ma Ngai na kũlika ũtianĩonĩ mweũ vamwe na Yeova. (Aevelania 9:
Naaũ maĩlĩte kũya kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu? Kwĩanana na ũndũ twoona no nginya methĩwe ne o ala me nthĩnĩ wa ũtianĩo mweũ na me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. Veva mũtheu wa Ngai nũmakũsĩaa kana nanyuve kwĩthĩwa me asumbĩ ĩtunĩ. (Alomi 8:
Ala mena wĩkwaty'o wa kwĩkala Valatisonĩ kũũ nthĩ nĩmaĩle kũya kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu? Mo mayĩĩsaa kĩmũtũ kana kũnyw'a mbinyu, ĩndĩ nĩmew'aa mwĩao wa Yesũ wa kwĩthĩwa vo ĩvinda ya kũlilikana Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi, namo nĩmekaa ũu kwa ndaĩa. Kĩla mwaka matukũ 14 mwei wa Nisani ĩtina wa syũa kũthũa, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nililikanaa Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi. O na kau no andũ ngili nini kũũ nthĩ monanasya kana mena wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwa Aklĩsto onthe. Ĩvinda yĩu kĩla mũndũ nũtonya kũsũanĩa kwa ũito ĩũlũ wa wendo mwingĩ wa Yeova Ngai na Yesũ Klĩsto.

translation:
Christ was set aside according to the plan of Christ. This commemoration is now called "the Lord's Memorial." (1 Corinthians 11:
Jesus Christ observed this memorial of his death on Nisan 14, 33 C.E. Nisan 14 always falls on what we call March or April. But on that particular Nisan 14, the Passover was taking place. The Passover was observed on Nisan 14 in the evening.
Jesus went to the Passover with his apostles, and he directed Judas Iscariot to go ahead and prepare the Lord's Memorial. That memorial is what reminds us of the sacrifice of Jesus. It is observed once each year.
The Gospel account by Matthew reads: "While they were reclining, he took a loaf, and after giving thanks, he broke it and gave it to the disciples, saying: 'This represents my body.' And he took a cup, and after offering a prayer, he passed it around to them, saying: 'All of you drink from it, for this represents my blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out in behalf of many for forgiveness of sins.' "
Some may wonder why Jesus used bread to symbolize his body and wine to symbolize his blood. Was there a reason why Jesus chose to use those things to remind his followers of his sacrifice? It seems that those things were commonly associated with God's people. (Matthew 9:
Both the bread and the wine are symbolic. The bread symbolizes Jesus' perfect human body. Jesus instructed his followers to eat the bread to remember his sacrifice. That bread points forward to eternal life. (John 6:8) The Bible uses the expression "eternal life" to mean everlasting life.
The wine is symbolic of Jesus' perfect blood. That blood is what accomplishes our salvation. Jesus said that his blood would be poured out "for forgiveness of sins." By means of that blood, we can have a clean conscience. (Revelation 1:
The wine also represents the new covenant that Jesus inaugurated. That covenant offers us hope for everlasting life. We look forward to living forever under God's Kingdom.
(Luke 22:
But how can eating bread and drinking wine help us to maintain our faith? By regularly remembering Jesus' sacrifice, we show that we appreciate the value of the ransom he paid. And when we meditate on Jehovah's love for us, we will be more motivated to live in harmony with his will. (Romans 8:
What, then, should Christians do regarding partaking of the bread and the wine? Whether you choose to eat the bread and drink the wine depends on your personal relationship with Jesus. If you do so, you are showing that you are one of the spiritual Israelites who are looking ahead to ruling with Christ in heaven, and you are making a public declaration of your loyalty. Every year on Nisan 14, the anniversary of Jesus' death, Jehovah's Witnesses commemorate the Memorial of Christ's death. But even if you do not feel ready to make such a declaration, you can still benefit from attending the Memorial and meditating on the significance of Jesus' sacrifice—it is a valuable opportunity to draw closer to Jehovah God and Jesus Christ.

text:
Vaulo atethekie ata nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa e laiaa wa Lomi?
Mũndũ w'onthe ũla waĩ laiaa wa Lomi nĩwatanĩaa maũndũ mana vandũ vonthe vala ũsumbĩ ũsu wasumbĩkĩte. Kĩla laiaa wa Lomi eethĩawa ungu wa mĩao ya ũsumbĩ ũsu, o na ethĩwa kĩsionĩ kĩla wĩkalaa kĩ mĩao yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ĩla mũndũ wasikatwa, aĩ atonya kwĩtĩkĩla asilĩlwe kwosana na mĩao ya kĩsio kyake, ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, aĩ na ũthasyo wa kwasya asilĩlwe nĩ koti ya Lomi. Nao yĩla mũndũ wasilĩlwa kũawa, aĩ atonya kũmwĩkaĩla mũsumbĩ wa Lomi.
Mũndũ ũmwe waĩ wa siasa weetawa Cicero, na waĩ mũnene ũsumbĩnĩ wa Lomi ũla waĩ thayũ vakuvĩ myaka 2,100 mĩvĩtu aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩ ĩvĩtyo kwova laiaa wa Lomi, nao kũmũkũna nĩ naĩ nene mũno, na kũmũaa no ũndũ ũmwe na kũwaa mũsyai kana mũndũ wa mũsyĩ."
Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwatavanisye mũno kũndũ kw'onthe kũla Ũsumbĩ wa Lomi wasumbĩkĩte. Nĩwatũmĩie ũthasyo ũla waĩ naw'o e laiaa wa Lomi mavinda aa atatũ mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ: (1) Nĩwatavisye mũsili wa makoani wa Vilivi kana nĩmatũlile mĩao kwa kũmũkũna. (2) Ĩla waĩ Yelusaleme, nĩwawetie kana we nĩ Mũlomi nĩ kana maikamũkũne. (3) Nĩweekaĩlile Kaisali nĩ kana akamwĩthukĩĩsye ayĩtetea.—Meko ma Atũmwa 16:37-39; 22:25-28; 25:10-12.
Aĩthi ma ĩvinda ya tene maĩvawa ata?
Yakovo nĩwaĩthisye kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 20 indo sya mũndũ wasyaanĩw'e na inyia, weetawa Lavani. Yakovo athũkũmie myaka 14 nĩ kana anengwe eĩtu elĩ ma Lavani, na kwa myaka ĩngĩ 6 mũsaala wake waĩ indo. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 30:25-33) Ĩvuku yĩtawa Biblical Archaeology Review yaĩtye: "Wĩw'ano wa aĩthi na ala mamaandĩkĩte, ta ũla waĩ vo katĩ wa Lavani na Yakovo waĩ ũndũ weesĩkĩe nĩ aandĩki ma tene na asomi ma Mbivilia."
Syĩndũ sya tene ila syenziwe kũndũ kwĩtawa Nuzi, Larsa, na kũndũ kũngĩ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o nthĩ ya Iraq syaĩ na maandĩko moonanasya wĩw'ano katĩ wa aĩthi na ala mamaandĩkĩte. Ũu wĩonany'a kana ũsu nĩ ũndũ weethĩawa. Meew'anaa kũthũkũma kuma ĩvinda yĩla malondu matilwa wia, kũvika ĩla makatilwa wia ĩngĩ. Aĩthi nĩmeetĩkĩlaa kũsũvĩa indo siana ũndũ mũna, ila syeethĩawa ivangĩtwe kwosana na ũkũũ wasyo na ikonanw'a ethĩwa nĩ nũme kana nĩ nga. Ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe mwene indo aaĩlĩte kwosa tũtena, wia wa malondu, ĩia na mauta, kwosana na ũndũ meew'anĩte. Ila syatiala syeethĩawa syĩ sya mũĩthi.
Ndĩthya yongelekaa kwosana na malondu maka ala mũĩthi wanengetwe. Malondu maka 100 meekwatĩaw'a kũsyaa tũtena 80. Kwoou, mũĩthi nĩwe waaĩlĩte kũĩva ethĩwa malondu asu mainasyaa ũndũ vaĩle, kana veethĩwa wasyo. Ũu watumaa mũĩthi ethĩwa na kĩthito kya kũsũvĩa indo ila waĩthasya.

translation:
Will someone explain to me the laws of Rome?
A person who doesn't know the laws of Rome worries about many things because people always face some kind of trouble. Every law of Rome protects a certain type of trouble, or it prevents something from happening to people. But a judge, he can interpret the law based on his own understanding, and even if he does so wrongly, he has the authority to interpret the law according to Roman customs. And if a person is accused, he can appeal to the judges of Rome.
There was once a man named Cicero, and this great Roman lawyer who lived over 2,100 years ago said: "It is very good to know the laws of Rome, and to respect them greatly, and to live in accordance with one thing and to be either a good or a bad person."
The apostle Paul used this knowledge throughout his ministry to show how the Law of Rome worked. He used his rights under Roman law three times when he was imprisoned in Philippi: (1) He demanded that the local officials of Philippi come and release him. (2) But in Jerusalem, he insisted that he was a Roman citizen and should be tried there. (3) He appealed to Caesar and asked to be defended by him.—Acts 16:37-39; 22:25-28; 25:10-12.
But what about the other cases?
James spent twenty years working for a man named Lavanius, who was a Jewish Christian. James served fourteen years while still living with Lavanius, and for another six years he worked remotely. (Ecclesiastics 30:25-33) A recent issue of Biblical Archaeology Review stated: "Researchers have found that, according to the laws of those days, the agreement between Lavanius and James was legally binding and could be understood by lawyers and Bible scholars."
Similar agreements were made in ancient cities such as Nuzi and Larsa, and in other places in northern Iraq, and they appear in written contracts between people. This shows that what is described is accurate. People often wanted to settle disputes quickly, rather than taking them to court. The parties involved would agree on certain terms, but these agreements were not always considered legally binding unless they were witnessed by others. The amount of money owed each year could vary depending on the type of work done, such as farming, livestock raising, or other services. However, such agreements were not always straightforward.
It seems that debts were often settled through negotiations with creditors. About 100 tablets have been discovered showing that 80 percent of debts were paid. Therefore, lenders usually had some assurance that they would recover their loans, or at least part of them. This helped lenders to continue lending money and investing in businesses.

text:
Maũndũ ala maeleetw'e ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo ĩũlũ wa mbalasi inya na aũme ala makuĩtwe nĩsyo nĩ maũsengy'a mũno, na maeleetw'e nesa ũkethĩa nĩ ta tũmene mayĩkĩka. Mbalasi isu syĩoneka isembete mũno na mavũngũ masyo me na wasya ta wa kĩtundumo! Mbalasi ya mbee nĩ nzaũ, na ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩyo nde na ĩvinda yĩasa kuma atw'ĩkĩthw'a mũsumbĩ. Aatĩĩwe nĩ mbalasi ya langi mũtune, na ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩyo avetangaa mũuo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Nayo mbalasi ya katatũ nĩ nziũ, na ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩyo e na kĩthimi kw'okonĩ kwake, na wasya ũla ũkwĩw'ĩka wĩonany'a kana kwĩ yũa. Mbalasi ya kana nĩ ya langi wa mũkũyũ kana langi mũtuku, na yĩonany'a kana kwĩ mowau na mĩisyo ĩngĩ, na ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩyo ĩsyĩtwa yake nĩ kĩkw'ũ. Mbũa yĩatĩanĩe na mbalasi ĩsu, na andũ aingĩ ala makw'a melika vo!
"Ĩla nasomie kwa ĩvinda ya mbee ĩũlũ wa aũme asu ana makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi, nĩnatelemile. Nasũanĩie kana Mũthenya wa Sila nĩwũkĩte na nũndũ ndyeeyũmbanĩtye, ndiema kwanangwa."
—Crystal.
"Nĩnendeeiw'e nĩ woni ũla ũeleetye ĩũlũ wa aũme ana ala makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi syĩ malangi me kĩvathũkany'o. Nĩnesie kũelewa maũndũ ala me woninĩ ũsu, na namanya kana nĩ ma w'o."
—Ed.
Nĩwĩthĩwa wĩw'aa ũndũ Crystal weewie ĩla wasomie ĩũlũ wa aũme ana ala makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi mawetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo? Kana wĩw'aa ũndũ Ed weew'aa? Wĩthĩwe wĩw'aa ta Crystal, kana wĩw'aa ta Ed, ĩthĩwa wĩsĩ kana woni ũsu wa aũme makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi nĩ ũmwe wa mawoni ala mesĩkĩe nesa ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo, na nĩyo ĩvuku ya mũthya ya Mbivilia. Na we nĩwĩsĩ kana kũelewa woni ũsu no kũũtethye? Kũtonya kũũtethya ata? Ngai nĩwathanĩte kana no ũkwate ũtanu wa w'o wasoma, weemanyĩsya, na weeka kwosana na maũndũ ala me ĩvukunĩ yĩu ya wathani.
O na kau andũ amwe nĩmatelemaa masoma woni ũsu wa aũme ana makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi, woni ũsu ndwaandĩkwa ũtũtelemasye. Ũw'o nĩ kana andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmamanyĩte kana woni ũsu nũlũlũmĩĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo woo, na nũmanengae wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. O naku no ũtetheke o tamo! Twĩũkũlya ũendeee kũsoma ũvoo ũũ.
