translation:
Stories about the beauty of Creation abound, full of wonders and mysteries, and they are told with great skill, and stories are needed to teach what is hidden. Wonders are seen everywhere, and places far and near are filled with amazing things! The first wonder is light, and its name is the one that reveals itself and shines brightly. It is said to be a wonder from heaven above, and its name is the one who brings life to the world. Also, the third wonder is water, and its name is the one that quenches thirst, and places where it flows are known for their coolness. The fourth wonder is the sky, either blue or red, and it is seen both near and far, with many stars, and its name is associated with strength. Animals compete with wonders, and many people also experience miracles!
"I have learned through the brightness of the first wonder, full of mysteries and wonders, I have understood. I have wondered if the Creator of Heaven will reveal more secrets to me, so that I can be enlightened."
—Crystal.
"I am moved by the story of the first wonder, full of mysteries and wonders that make my heart tremble. I want to understand the things that this story tells me, and perhaps it is true."
—Ed.
Will you agree with Crystal when she says she has learned through the brightness of the first wonder, full of mysteries and wonders? Or will you agree with Ed? Will you agree with Crystal, or will you agree with Ed, knowing that this story of the first wonder is one of the stories that are hidden in the traditions of Creation, and it is the foundation of the truth of Mbivilia. And will you also understand this story and share it? To try to share it at all? May God help you to grasp the five aspects of those who read, understand, and live with the things of your own tradition.
And some people have been able to learn this story of the first wonder, this story has been written simply. It is said that millions of people know that this story illuminates their minds, and they find its meaning in the depths of their hearts. Oh, and you too can succeed if you wish! Let us continue to read this together.

NĨWEEKIE ŨTWI MŨSEO
MWĨĨTU-A-ASA ũmwe kuma Poland easya: "Navatisiwe nĩ na myaka 15, na ĩndĩ myei thanthatũ kuma vau natw'ĩka vainia mũtetheesya. Ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe nĩnakũlilye nĩtw'ĩke vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda. Na ĩndĩ ĩla naminie sekondalĩ nĩnakũlilye ngatavany'e kĩsionĩ kĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Ĩvinda yĩu nekalaa na ũsũe wakwa na ndaĩ Ngũsĩ. Na kwoou nĩnendaa mũno ngwate kĩsio kĩ vaasa na mũsyĩ na vaasa na ũsũe wakwa. Ĩndĩ neewie woo mũno ĩla mũsyaĩĩsya witũ wa mũthyũlũlũko wandavisye kana kĩsio kĩla ngũnengwa ndavany'e no kyu kya mũsyĩ! Nĩnatatie mũno ndakamanye ũndũ neewie. Naendie nĩw'ĩte thĩna ngasũanĩe kĩla wandavisye. Nĩvo ĩndĩ natavisye mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũla twanengiwe kĩsio kyu ĩmwe ndeto ii: 'Nĩona ngĩka maũndũ ta Yona. Ĩndĩ ĩtina Yona nĩwesie kũthi Nineva vala watũmĩtwe. Kwoou o nakwa nĩngwĩtĩkĩla kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩĩ nanengwa.'
"Nĩthĩĩtwe nĩ vainia kĩsionĩ kya mũsyĩ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩna, na nĩnonete kana waĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ mũno kwĩka ũndũ neeiwe nĩnĩke. Woni mũthũku ũla naĩ naw'o nĩw'o waĩ thĩna wakwa mũnene. Yu nĩw'aa nĩ mũtanu mũno. O na ve mwei naĩ na amanyĩw'a 24 ma Mbivilia. Na nĩngũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea nũndũ nĩnambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya na ũsũa o na kau tene nĩwambĩngaa."
NĨWOONIE ŨSEO WA KŨTONGOEW'A NĨ NGAI
Ve ĩvinda mũmanyĩw'a ũmwe wa Mbivilia wa nthĩ ya Fiji waĩ na ũtwi mũmũ wa kwĩka. Aĩ no nginya atw'e ethi ũmbanonĩ mũnene kana ethi na mũũme kũlilikana ĩsyawa ya mũndũ ũmwe wa mũsyĩ. Nĩweew'anie na mũũme kana no athi ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Aithi atiie atha mũũme kana auma ũmbanonĩ nũkwĩsa kũmũatĩĩa. Ĩndĩ ĩla waumie ũmbanonĩ eewie ataĩle kwĩlikya ũndũnĩ ũũtuma ethĩwa e mũisyonĩ kĩ-veva, na kwoou anyuva kũlea kũatĩĩa mũũme.
Nake mũũme avika kyathĩnĩ eeie andũ make ma mũsyĩ kana kĩveti nĩkĩmwĩtisye lũũsa kĩthi ũmbanonĩ wa Ngũsĩ na nĩkĩkwĩsa kũmũatĩĩa ũmbano ũsu wathela. Ĩndĩ namo mamũsũngĩie mamwĩa, "Ndwĩsa kũmwona vaa. Ngũsĩ iililikanaa ĩsyawa ya mũndũ!" *
Mũũme nĩweewie mũyo mũno nũndũ kĩveti kyake kyeekie ũtwi kĩtongoew'e nĩ mũĩkĩĩo wakyo na wasya wakyo wa ngoo. Nũndũ mũmanyĩw'a ũsu wa Mbivilia nĩwaendeeie kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku, nĩwesie kũkwata mwanya wa kũtavya mũũme vamwe na andũ angĩ ũvoo mũseo. Kweethĩiwe ata? Mũũme nĩweetĩkĩlile kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na ambĩĩa kũendany'a nake maũmbanonĩ.
^ kal. 7 Sisya "Makũlyo Kuma kwa Asomi Maitũ" ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/12/2001.

translation:
I REMEMBER THE DAYS OF MY YOUTH
A YOUNG MAN FROM POLAND WROTE: "I AM SAD AND I AM 15 YEARS OLD, AND IN THOSE DAYS WE USED TO GO TO CHURCH EVERY SUNDAY. FOR ONE YEAR I TRIED TO GO TO CHURCH EVERY DAY. AND EVEN NOW I SOMETIMES TRY TO FIND PEACE WITH GOD LIKE PEOPLE WHO ARE AFRAID OF JUDGEMENT. THAT DAY WAS DARK AND I PRAYED TO GOD. AND THEN I FELT A GREAT NEED TO CONFESS MY SINS AND TO BE RECONCILED WITH GOD. I HAD A DREAM THAT NIGHT WHICH MADE ME UNDERSTAND EVERYTHING! I WOKE UP FEELING CALM AFTER EVERY PRAYER. THIS IS HOW I EXPERIENCED THE YOUNG MAN'S STORY THAT WE WERE TOLD ABOUT A CERTAIN MATTER: 'I SAW A VISION LIKE JONAH. IN THAT TIME JONAH WENT TO NINEVEH TO WARN THE PEOPLE. TODAY I WANT TO FIND PEACE LIKE HIM.'
"I HAVE BEEN SEARCHING FOR SPIRITUAL PEACE FOR MANY YEARS, AND I REALIZED THAT WHAT I WAS LOOKING FOR WAS ALREADY WITHIN ME. YOU SHOULD KNOW THAT I HAVE A VERY KIND MOTHER. SHE IS THE ONE WHO HELPED ME. AND I HAVE READ THE BIBLE 24 TIMES. AND I THANK JEHOVAH BECAUSE HE HAS HELPED ME TO GET CLOSER TO HIM AND EVEN NOW HE CONTINUES TO GUIDE ME."
I LEARNED A LESSON FROM THIS EXPERIENCE THROUGH PRAYER
ONE OF THE ELDERS IN FIJI SHARED AN EXAMPLE. HE SAID THAT SOME PEOPLE THINK IT IS DIFFICULT TO FORGIVE OTHERS OR TO TREAT THEM WITH RESPECT. HE EXPLAINED THAT IF SOMEONE OFFENDS US, WE SHOULD NOT HOLD A GRUDGE. HE ADDED THAT IF WE DO NOT FORGIVE OTHERS, WE WILL NOT BE ABLE TO RECEIVE FORGIVENESS OURSELVES, AND THEN WE WILL NOT BE ABLE TO APPROACH GOD.
MY MOTHER TOLD ME ABOUT PEOPLE WHO WERE DISAPPOINTED BY THEIR CHILDREN OR SPOUSE AND TRIED TO TAKE REVENGE ON THEM. SHE SAID THAT SUCH ACTIONS ONLY MAKE THINGS WORSE. SHE ALSO ENCOURAGED ME TO SAY, "LET US FORGET THE PAST. LET US START OVER!" *
MY MOTHER EXPLAINED THAT EVERY PERSON HAS FLAWS AND THAT WE SHOULD TRY TO UNDERSTAND EACH OTHER'S FEELINGS AND NEEDS. SHE SAID THAT READING THE BIBLE HELPS US TO DEVELOP LOVE AND COMPASSION FOR OTHERS. DID YOU KNOW THAT MY MOTHER ALWAYS INSISTS ON SHARING THE BIBLE WITH OTHERS AND INVITES THEM TO JOIN HER IN PRAYER?
^ ref. 7 Article "Reasons Why People Need Help," The Watchtower (Swahili) of December 15, 2001.

text:
KWASISYA mũndũ ũũ wĩ kĩw'ũnĩ nthĩnĩ. E thĩnanĩ mũnene mũno, kana ti w'o? Ĩkũyũ yĩĩ yĩkilye kũmũmelya! We nĩwĩsĩ mũndũ ũũ nũũ? Syĩtwa yake nĩ Yona. Ekai twone alikile thĩnanĩ ũnenevete ũu ata.
Yona aĩ mwathani wa Yeova. Ĩvinda yĩte ĩasa ĩtina wa mwathani Elisa kũkw'a Yeova nĩweeie Yona ũũ: 'Enda ndũanĩ nene ya Nineva. Ũthũku wa andũ nĩ mũnene mũno kũu, na nĩngwenda kũneena namo ĩũlũ wa w'o.'
Ĩndĩ Yona ndendaa kũthi. Kwoou alĩsa ngalawa yaendete ngalĩko ĩngĩ eka Nineva. Yeova ndaaendeew'a nĩ kĩko kĩu kya Yona kya kũtoloka. Kwoou Aete kĩuutani kĩnene ũkanganĩ. Kyaĩ na vinya mwingĩ mũno, nakyo kyaĩ vakuvĩ kũthika ngalawa kĩw'ũnĩ. Atwai ma ngalawa nĩmeewie w'ĩa mũno, na meekaĩla ngai syoo imatethye.
Ĩndĩno Yona amea: 'Nyie nĩthaithaa Yeova, Ngai ũla woombie matu na nthĩ. Nakwa ngĩĩte ndikeke ũndũ Yeova ũmbĩie nĩke.' Kwoou atwai asu ma ngalawa mamũkũlya: 'Twĩkwĩka ata nĩ kana ũkanga ũusye?'
Nake Yona amea: 'Mbĩkyai ũkanganĩ, na ũkanga nũkũusya ĩngĩ.' Atwai ma ngalawa mayeendaa kwĩka ũu, ĩndĩ yĩla kĩuutani kyaendeeie na kwingĩva, mamwĩkya Yona ũkanganĩ. Na vau kwa vau kĩuutani kyathela, naw'o ũkanga wausya ĩngĩ.
Yona alika kĩw'ũnĩ, ĩkũyũ yĩĩ ĩnene nĩyamũmelilye. Ĩndĩ ndaakw'a. Yona ekalile mĩthenya ĩtatũ na motukũ atatũ ĩvunĩ ya ĩkũyũ yĩu. Nĩweelilile mũno nũndũ wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Yeova na kũthi Nineva. We nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ weekie?
Yona nĩwavoyie Yeova amũtethye. Na ĩndĩ Yeova atuma ĩkũyũ yĩu yĩmũtavĩka nthĩ nyũmũ. Ĩtina wa ũu Yona nĩwaendie Nineva. Ũndũ ũũ wĩtũmanyĩsya kana nĩ ũndũ wa vata ithyĩ kwĩka maũndũ onthe ala Yeova ũnũkwasya twĩke.
Ĩvuku ya Mbivilia ya Yona.
Makũlyo
- Yona nũũ, na Yeova amwĩie nĩeke ata?
- Yona eekie ata nũndũ ndendaa kũthi kũla Yeova wamwie athi?
- Yona ameie andũ ma ngalawa nĩmeke ata nĩ kana ũkanga ũusye?
- O tondũ we ũtonya kwona vaa visanĩ, kweethĩiwe ata kwa Yona amina kũlika kĩw'ũnĩ nthĩnĩ?
- Yona ekalile ĩvinda yĩana ata ĩvunĩ ya ĩkũyũ yĩu ĩnene, na eekie ata yĩla waĩ vo?
- Yona aendie va ĩtina wa kuma nthĩnĩ wa ĩkũyũ yĩu ĩnene, na ũndũ ũsu wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Yona 1:1-17.
Kwa w'o, Yona aĩ na mawoni maũ ĩũlũ wa wĩa ũla wanengiwe wa kũthi kũtavya Anineva? (Yona 1:2, 3; Nth. 3:7; Mũta. 8:12)
- Soma Yona 2:1, 2, 10.
Ũndũ ũsu wamũkwatie Yona ũtũĩkĩĩthasya ata kana Yeova akasũngĩa mboya sitũ? (Sav. 22:24; 34:6; 1 Yoa. 5:14)
- Soma Yona 3:1-10.
Twĩkĩawa vinya ata nĩkũmanya kana Yeova nĩwaendeeie na kũmũtũmĩa Yona o na kau nĩwaleile kũtethya wĩa ũla wanengetwe mbee? (Sav. 103:14; 1 Vet. 5:10)
Maũndũ ala Yona woonie makonanĩtye na andũ ma Nineva metũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa kũtw'ĩĩa andũ kana nĩmekwĩthukĩĩsya kana maiĩthukĩĩsya kĩsionĩ kĩla tũaĩwe kũtavany'a? (Yona 3:6-9; Mũta. 11:6; Meko 13:48)

translation:
It happened that a man went on a journey. It was a very big city, wasn't it? The Hyksos people were eager to oppress them! Who is this man then? His name is Jonah. Let us see how he went on a very large journey.
Jonah was a servant of Jehovah. He heard a voice from the servant Elijah telling Jehovah to send Jonah saying: 'Go to the great city of Nineveh. The sin of the people is very great there, and I want to speak to them about repentance.'
But Jonah did not want to go. So he found a ship going in the opposite direction towards Nineveh. Jehovah did not approve of Jonah's attempt to flee. Then a great storm arose and raged. There was much wind, and they struggled to steer the ship against it. The sailors were very afraid, and they prayed to their gods.
Then Jonah said: 'I have offended Jehovah, the God who made the sea and the land. Because I disobeyed the command Jehovah gave me.' Then the sailors asked him: 'What should we do so that the storm will subside?'
And Jonah said: 'Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and the storm will calm down because of me.' Then the sailors rowed hard to return to shore, but they could not, because the storm was raging against them. And wave upon wave crashed over the ship, and the storm continued to rage.
Jonah went ashore, and the Hyksos people were very eager to harm him. But he refused. Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the Hyksos fish. He regretted his disobedience to Jehovah and his refusal to go to Nineveh. What lesson does this teach?
Jonah prayed to Jehovah, and Jehovah sent a Hyksos fish to swallow him. After that, Jonah went to Nineveh. This shows us that it is important to obey Jehovah's commands, no matter how difficult they may seem.
The story of Jonah in the Bible.
Questions
- Who is Jonah, and what did Jehovah ask him to do?
- Why did Jonah refuse to go when Jehovah commanded him?
- What did Jonah tell the sailors to do so that the storm would subside?
- How can we learn from Jonah's experience to be obedient to Jehovah?
- Did Jonah spend a long time in the belly of the Hyksos fish, and what did he feel like?
- Why did Jonah go to Nineveh after being released from the belly of the Hyksos fish, and what does this show?
Further Questions
- Read Jonah 1:1-17.
Why was Jonah reluctant to go to Nineveh? (Jonah 1:2, 3; Ps. 3:7; Matt. 8:12)
- Read Jonah 2:1, 2, 10.
What helped Jonah realize that Jehovah had mercy on him? (Ps. 22:24; 34:6; 1 John 5:14)
- Read Jonah 3:1-10.
How does this show that Jehovah is willing to forgive those who repent and turn away from their wickedness? (Ps. 103:14; 1 Pet. 5:10)
What lessons can we learn from Jonah's dealings with the people of Nineveh about reaching out to others, whether they accept our message or reject it? (Jonah 3:6-9; Matt. 11:6; Mark 13:48)

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye ũndũ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana amĩelewe. O na ethĩwa umĩte va, no ũmanye ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nũndũ "
ti mũito mũno kwaku, o na ndwĩ kũasa."—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 30:11.
Maũndũ ala matonya kũũtetheesya ũelewe Mbivilia
Ĩthĩwa na woni waĩle. Mĩtĩkĩle Mbivilia ta Ndeto ya Ngai. Ĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo nũndũ Ngai nũleanĩte na mĩng'athĩlĩlyo. (1 Athesalonika 2:13; Yakovo 4:6) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ndũkaĩkĩĩe kĩla ũndũ ũtamanyĩte ũw'o. Ngai endaa ũtũmĩe '
ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa.'—Alomi 12:1, 2, New World Translation.
Voya ũnengwe ũĩ. Ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 3:5 yaĩtye, "
Ndũkekwatye ũmanyi waku mwene.". Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, endeea '
kũmũvoya Ngai' aũnenge ũĩ wa kũelewa Mbivilia.—Yakovo 1:5.
Mĩsomae kĩla ĩvinda. Ũkatetheka mũnango weemanyĩsya Mbivilia kĩla ĩvinda kũte ĩla wamĩsoma ũitĩĩa.—Yosua 1:8.
Ĩmanyĩsye kyongo kwa kyongo. Nzĩa nzeo ya kwĩmanyĩsya kĩla maandĩko meũmanyĩsya nĩ kũkunĩkĩla kwa ũliku ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa kyongo kĩna kana ũvoo mũna. Ambĩĩa na "
momanyĩsyo ma mbee," na ĩndĩ '
ũithi na mbee ũkavikĩe maũndũ ma ũima.' (Aevelania 6:1, 2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Weeka ũu, ũkeethĩa no ũsyaanĩsye maandĩko, na ũyĩmanyĩsya kana mĩsoa ĩmwe ya Mbivilia nĩyĩeleasya ĩngĩ, o na ĩla yĩ "
vinya kũmanya."—2 Vetelo 3:16.
Kũlya angĩ maũtetheesye. Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya twĩtĩkĩle ũtethyo kuma kwa andũ angĩ ala maeleawa Mbivilia. (Meko ma Atũmwa 8:30, 31) Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩmanyĩasya Mbivilia na andũ vate ndĩvi. O ta Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa, matũmĩaa maandĩko kũtetheesya andũ mamanye yo Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata.—Meko ma Atũmwa 17:2, 3.
Maũndũ ala mate ma lasima kwĩthĩwa namo
Ũĩ mwingĩ kana kĩsomo. Atũmwa ma Yesũ me 12 nĩmaeleetwe maandĩko na nĩmamanyĩasya andũ angĩ o na kau aingĩ mamonaa me andũ "
matamanyĩĩtw'e, na mate na ũmanyi."—Meko ma Atũmwa 4:13.
Mbesa. Nũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia vate ndĩvi. Yesũ eeie atũmwa make atĩĩ: "
Nĩmwosete mana, nenganai mana."—Mathayo 10:8.

translation:
The Bible's Value
The Bible can help a person to find meaning in life and to understand things. And if you read it regularly, you will come to know the wonderful truths found in the Bible—
it is God's inspired Word, and it gives guidance.—Inspired by His Spirit 30:11.
Things that can help you to understand the Bible
Pray to God regularly. Meditate on the Bible, considering it as God's message to you. (1 Thessalonians 2:13; James 4:6) Also, if you encounter something you do not understand, do not hesitate to ask about it. God wants to use his '
gift of understanding.'—Romans 12:1, 2, New World Translation.
Seek wisdom daily. Proverbs 3:5 says, "
Trust in Jehovah with all your heart." For those who do so, God promises to '
give them insight' to understand the Bible.—James 1:5.
Read it every day. Make it a practice to read the Bible every day, taking time to meditate on what you read.—Joshua 1:8.
Compare scripture with scripture. One way to deepen your understanding of each passage is to compare it with other scriptures that say similar things or shed light on the matter. Consider also "
the context," and if a verse seems unclear, look at '
surrounding verses to see what they mean.' (Ecclesiastes 6:1, 2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) In this way, you can examine the scriptures and determine whether some part of the Bible is difficult to understand, or if it is simply "
hard to grasp."—2 Peter 3:16.
Ask questions. The Bible encourages us to ask questions when we do not fully understand something. (Acts 8:30, 31) Jehovah's Witnesses are happy to discuss the Bible with people. And like the apostles of Jesus Christ, they used the scriptures to help people understand its teachings.—Acts 17:2, 3.
Other helpful suggestions
Take notes. The apostles of Jesus were assigned to teach others and to help people learn from the scriptures.—Acts 17:2, 3.
Practice. Be willing to practice explaining the Bible to others. Jesus sent out his apostles and told them to use the scriptures to help people understand the good news.—Matthew 10:8.

text:
1. Mũandĩkĩthya wa Mbivilia nũũ?
Ũvoo mũseo wa kana andũ makekala tene na tene kũũ nthĩ nũandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ. (Savuli 37:29) Mbivilia yĩ na mavuku manini 66. Ngai atũmĩie aũme aĩkĩĩku vakuvĩ 40 kũmaandĩka. Mavuku atano ma mbee maandĩkiwe nĩ Mose kwa ĩvinda ya myaka vakuvĩ 3,500 mĩvĩtu. Ĩvuku ya mũthya yaandĩkiwe nĩ mũtũmwa Yoana myaka mbee wa 1,900 mĩvĩtu. Nĩ mawoni ma ũũ ala aandĩki ma Mbivilia maandĩkie? Ngai atũmĩie veva wake mũtheu kũneena na aandĩki ma Mbivilia. (2 Samueli 23:2) Maandĩkie mawoni ma Ngai, ti mawoni moo ene. Kwoou Yeova nĩwe Mũandĩkĩthya wa Mbivilia.
2. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũĩkĩĩthya kana Mbivilia nĩ ya w'o?
Nĩtwĩsĩ kana Mbivilia yumĩte kwa Ngai nũndũ yathanaa ĩte ũvĩtya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ĩvinda yũkĩte yĩkethĩwa yĩilyĩ. Vaiĩ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ũu. (Yosua 23:14) No Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe ũtonya kũweta ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte ya mũndũ ate ũvĩtya.
Tũtonya kwĩkwatya ĩvuku kuma kwa Ngai yĩthĩwe yĩte maela, na nĩ w'o Mbivilia yĩilyĩ. Mbivilia mbilioni mbingĩ ninyaĩĩkĩtw'e kwa ithyomo maana maingĩ. O na kau nĩ ya tene, nĩyosanĩte na saenzi ya w'o. Ĩngĩ, aandĩki mayo 40 mayaavĩngana. * Vamwe na ũu, kĩla Mbivilia ĩwetete ĩũlũ wa wendo kĩtonya kuma kwa Ngai wa w'o weka, ũla nĩ Ngai wa wendo, na yĩ na vinya wa kũalyũla andũ makaseũva. Maũndũ asu ma w'o maĩkĩĩthasya andũ milioni mbingĩ kana Mbivilia nĩ Ndeto ya Ngai.
3. Mbivilia ĩneenete ĩũlũ wa kyaũ?
Ũndũ ũmwe mũnene Mbivilia ĩwetete nĩ ũvoo mũseo ĩũlũ wa kĩeleelo kya Ngai kĩ wendo kwelekela andũ. Maandĩko nĩmaeleasya ũndũ mwambĩlĩlyonĩ mũndũ waaisye ũathimo wa kwĩkala valatisonĩ kũũ nthĩ na ũndũ valatiso ĩkatũngĩĩwa.
Ĩngĩ, Ndeto ya Ngai yĩ na mĩao, myolooto, na ũtao. O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia yĩ na ngelekany'o sya ũndũ Ngai wĩkanaa na andũ. Ngelekany'o isu itũmanyĩasya ũndũ Ngai ũilyĩ. Kwoou, Mbivilia no ĩkũtetheesye kũmũmanya Ngai. Nĩeleasya ũndũ ũtonya kũtw'ĩka mũnyanyae.
4. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũelewe nĩ Mbivilia?
Kwa kũtũmĩa nzĩa ĩla Yesũ watũmĩie, kavuku kaa nĩkeũkũtetheesya ũelewe nĩ Mbivilia. Nĩwawetaa ĩandĩko yĩmwe ĩtina wa yĩngĩ na aielesya nĩ kana andũ "mamanye Maandĩko."
Nĩ maũndũ manini mendeeasya mũno ta ũvoo mũseo kuma kwa Ngai. Ĩndĩ, andũ amwe maiwosaa ta wa vata, o na angĩ nĩmathataw'a nĩw'o. Ndũkakw'e ngoo. Nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo wa kũtanĩa thayũ ũtathela ĩvinda yũkĩte, no nginya ũmũmanye Ngai.
^ kal. 3 Sisya kavuku Kitabu kwa Ajili ya Watu Wote.

translation:
1. Who is the writer of the Bible?
This question has troubled many people time and again since they began to write the Bible. (Psalm 37:29) The Bible has 66 important books. God used about 40 men to write it. Five of those books were written by Moses over a period of approximately 3,500 years ago. The last book was written by the apostle John about 1,900 years ago. So who actually wrote the books of the Bible? God inspired his servants to write the books of the Bible. (2 Samuel 23:2) These writings are from God, not just from humans. Jehovah is the writer of the Bible.
2. Why can we trust that the Bible is true?
We can be sure that the Bible comes from God because it agrees with what is already known to be true and accurate. No human can say this. (Joshua 23:14) But the Almighty God can know what will happen in the future and accurately foretell it.
We can rely on God's word, which is truthful and reliable, and that is why the Bible is trustworthy. Billions of Bibles have been distributed in many languages. And even though they are old, they agree with modern science. Also, the 40 writers agreed. * Furthermore, every Bible shows that God cares for people and is a loving God, and he has the power to help people overcome difficulties. Many millions of people have found comfort in knowing that the Bible is God's Word.
3. What does the Bible teach us?
One important thing the Bible teaches is that God loves mankind and wants them to live. The scriptures explain how a person can find happiness and meaning in life and how to avoid problems.
Also, God's Word has principles, commands, and laws. And importantly, the Bible tells us what God expects of us. Those standards show us what God is like. Thus, the Bible helps us get to know God. It explains how we can live a meaningful life.
4. How can we understand what the Bible says?
By using the example Jesus gave us, we can learn how to understand what the Bible says. He encouraged people to read the scriptures regularly and to see if they "understand the Scriptures."
These things are very important for getting closer to God. Some people may struggle because of their past, and others may find it difficult. Don't give up. If you are honest and sincere in your desire to learn, you will come to know God.
^ ref. 3 See the book For People of All Nations.

text:
MYAKA mingĩ nĩyavĩtie. Namo ana ma Noa meethĩwa na syana mbingĩ. Syana syoo nĩsyeanie nasyo syeethĩwa na syana syoo mbingĩ. O mĩtũkĩ nĩkweethĩiwe na andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Ũmwe wa andũ aa aĩ nzũkũlũ ya Noa weetawa Nimiloti. Aĩ mũndũ mũthũku wasyĩmaa na kũaa nyamũ na andũ. Na ĩngĩ Nimiloti nĩweetw'ĩkĩthisye mũsumbĩ ĩũlũ wa andũ ala angĩ onthe. Ngai ndaamwenda Nimiloti.
Andũ onthe ĩvinda yĩu maneenaa kĩthyomo o kĩmwe. Nimiloti endaa amekaly'e vandũ vamwe nĩ kana atonye kũmasumbĩka. We nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ weekie? Eeie andũ make ndũa nene na mwako mũtũlu wa mũnyoolo nthĩnĩ waw'o. Kwamasisye vaa visanĩ mayũmba mavali.
Yeova Ngai ndaaendeew'a nĩ mwako ũsu. Ngai endaa andũ manyaĩĩke na kũtũa kĩla vandũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ andũ asu masya: 'Ũkai! Ekai twĩyakĩe ndũa na mwako mũtũlu wa mũnyoolo ũla mũthya waw'o ũtonya kũvika ĩtunĩ. Na tũkeethĩwa na nguma!' Andũ asu mendaa metaĩĩe mo ene vandũ va kũmũtaĩĩa Ngai.
Kwoou ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwatumie andũ asu maeka kwaka mwako ũsu. We nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ weekie ũu? O vau kwa vau nĩwatumie andũ asu mambĩlĩĩlya kũneena ithyomo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, vandũ va kĩthyomo kĩmwe. Ala maakaa mwako ũsu nĩmaekie kũeleanwa. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi ndũa ĩsu yoo yeetiwe Mbaveli, kana Mbaviloni, ũalyũlo wayo nĩ "Kĩthokoany'o."
Andũ asu nĩmambĩĩie kũthama Mbaveli. Ikundi sya andũ ala maneenaa kĩthyomo kĩmwe nĩsyaendie kũtũa vamwe kũndũ kũngĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 10:1, 8-10; 11:1-9.
Makũlyo
- Nimiloti aĩ ũũ, na Ngai amwonaa ata?
- Nthĩnĩ wa visa ũũ nĩkĩ andũ mekũmba mavali?
- Nĩkĩ Yeova ũtaaendeew'a nĩ mwako ũsu?
- Ngai aũngamisye ata wĩa wa mwako ũsu wa mũnyoolo?
- Ndũa ĩsu yeetawa ata, ũalyũlo wa syĩtwa yĩu nĩ mwaũ?
- Kweekĩkie ata ĩtina wa Ngai kũthokoany'a ithyomo syoo?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 10:1, 8-10.
Nimiloti aĩ na mĩkĩle ya mũthemba mwaũ, na ũndũ ũsu wĩna ũkany'o mwaũ kwitũ? (Nth. 3:31)
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 11:1-9.
Kĩeleelo kya mwako ũsu mũtũlu wa mũnyoolo kyaĩ kyaũ, na nĩkĩ wĩa ũsu ũtaĩ ũendeea? (Mwa. 11:4; Nth. 16:18; Yoa. 5:44)

translation:
Many years have passed. Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. These three sons also had many children. And people multiplied and were blessed and increased greatly.
One of Noah's descendants was named Nimrod. He became a mighty hunter and a man powerful among men. Also, Nimrod began to distinguish himself as a leader among men and against God. God favored Nimrod.
All the people moved together to one place and spoke one language. Nimrod led some people to build a city so they would not be scattered. But why did they do this? Because the people were united and wanted glory for themselves. They started building houses and walls.
Jehovah God went down to see what they were doing. God saw that the people were uniting to do something bad. So he said to them: "Look! One language and one power will cause you to do whatever you want. Now go ahead and build your city and tower that reaches the heavens. And let us make a name for ourselves!" The people obeyed and continued to build to honor God.
So God sent people to scatter them from that place. Why did he do this? Because he sent people to confuse their language so they could not understand each other, people who spoke one language. But their city and tower remained standing. This is why it was called Babel, or Babylon, whose name means "Confusion."
The people began to migrate away from Babel. Groups of people who spoke one language went to different parts of the earth.
Genesis 10:1, 8-10; 11:1-9.
Questions
- Who was Nimrod, and how did God view him?
- Why did people start building houses and walls?
- What does Jehovah God care about?
- Has God ever opposed human glory?
- What is the name of our land, and what does its name mean?
- What can we learn from God's confusing of languages?
Further Questions
- Read Genesis 10:1, 8-10.
Nimrod had ambitious plans, and what does this teach us about ambition? (Prov. 3:31)
- Read Genesis 11:1-9.
What lesson can we learn from the account of the tower of Babel, and why is it important? (Matt. 11:4; Prov. 16:18; John 5:44)

text:
Nĩmamanyie ndeto ila mataviw'e.—Nee. 8:12.
Andũ ma Ngai methĩĩtwe maitũmĩa ũtonyi wa kũneena, kana wa kũtũmĩa kĩthyomo, kũmũtaĩa na kũtetheesya angĩ mamanye kwenda kwake. Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ, andũ ma Ngai nĩmatũmĩĩte kĩthyomo kwa nzĩa ya mwanya kũendeesya ũthaithi wa w'o, na nzĩa ĩsu ya mwanya nĩ kũalyũla Mbivilia. Mbivilia ila ialyũlĩtwe nĩ mbingĩ ĩndĩ imwe syĩthĩawa ialyũlĩtwe nesa kwĩ ingĩ. Myakanĩ ya 1940, kamitii yĩtawa New World Bible Translation Committee nĩyatwie kũtũmĩaa myolooto ĩtatũ ya kũalyũla Mbivilia, na myolooto ĩsu yu yĩthĩĩtwe ĩitũmĩwa nĩ aalyũli ma ithyomo mbee wa 130. Myolooto ĩsu nĩ: (1) Kũtaĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai kwa kũyĩtũngĩĩa vala yaĩle Maandĩkonĩ. (Mt. 6:9) (2) Kũalyũla maandĩko ndeto kwa ndeto ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka, ĩndĩ ethĩwa vaitonyeka aalyũli maialyũla ũvoo ũsu kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũeleeka nesa. (3) Kũtũmĩa ndeto ite vinya nĩ kana wĩthĩe mũsomi nũkwendeew'a nĩ kũsoma.—Nee. 8:8. w15 12/15 2:1, 2
Ethĩwa soo ũkavuvwa wasya ũtesĩkĩe, nũũ ũla wĩyũmban'ya kũkita?—1 Ako. 14:8.
Kwasũanĩa kĩla kĩtonya kwĩkĩka ita sya kaũ ikaelya kũvuvĩwa wasya itesĩ! O ta ũu, tũkatw'ĩka tũkaneenaa na nthimo kana tũkaneenaa ta tũũvithany'a kĩla tũũweta, andũ no molanĩlw'e nĩ kĩla tũũmatavya kana makakyosa ũndũ ũngĩ. (1 Ako. 14:9) Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana twaĩle kũtavasya andũ maũndũ tũteũmavuva kana tũteũmasũanĩa nĩ kana tũtw'ĩke atĩ nĩtwatũmĩa ndeto ikũeleeka laisi. Vai mũndũ ũngĩ waamanya kũnyuva ndeto nesa ta Yesũ. Kwasũanĩa ũtavany'a wake ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo kĩlungu kya 5 nginya kya 7. Nthĩnĩ wa ũtavany'a ũsu atũmĩie ndeto nini ĩndĩ syĩ na ũvoo mũito. Ũneeni wake ndwaĩ na ngathĩĩo na ndaatũmĩa ndeto itonya kũlanĩlya ala angĩ kana kũmaũmĩsya. Atũmĩaa ndeto syĩ laisi na ite vinya nĩ kana ilike ngoonĩ sya ala ũkũneena namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩ kana amatetheesye maeke kwĩmakĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩla makaĩsaa, amaeleisye ũndũ Yeova ũĩthasya nyũnyi sya yayaya. Amina ũu amaelekanilye na nyũnyi isu na amakũlya atĩĩ: "Inyw'ĩ mũi vata mũno kwĩ syo?" (Mt. 6:26) Isu ti ndeto nzeo mũno na syĩ laisi vyũ nginya ũkethĩa niũkiita ngoo? w15 12/15 3:13, 14
Wendano wa ana-a-asa nĩwĩkalae.—Aevl. 13:1.
Wendano wa ana-a-asa wĩthĩawa ũilyĩ ata? Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla Vaulo watũmĩie nĩ phi·la·del·phiʹa, na kwa ũkuvĩ ũalyũlo wayo nĩ "kwenda mwana-a-asa." Mũndũ wendete mwana-a-asa ethĩawa atumĩte ndũũ ngamu nake na ethĩawa alũmanĩtye nake o tondũ ũlũmanasya na mũndũ wa mũsyĩ kana mũnyanyae mũnene. (Yoa. 11:36) Kwoou ithyĩ tũyĩkaa kwasya atĩ twĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. Twĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma w'o ki. (Mt. 23:8) Wendano ũla twĩthĩawa naw'o ũeleetw'e nesa vyũ nĩ ndeto ii: "Wendonĩ wa ana-a-asa, ĩthĩwai na wendo mũuu ene kwa ene; ndaĩanĩ, mataĩei ala angĩ mbee." (Alo. 12:10) Wendo ũsu wavulanw'a na ũla wendo ũngĩ wĩthĩawa ũtongoew'e nĩ myolooto ya Ngai (a·gaʹpe), nũtumaa andũ ma Ngai mekalany'a nesa. Kwosana na Aklĩsto ma w'o, ndeto ĩsu yonanasya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa onthe o na ethĩwa nĩ ma mbaĩ yĩva. (Alo. 10:12) Nũndũ no ta tũsyaanĩw'e, Yeova atũmanyĩĩtye kana twaĩlĩte kwendana ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ ta ana-a-asa.—1 Ath. 4:9. w16.01 1:5, 6

translation:
I have rejoiced at your words like one who finds great treasure.—Neh. 8:12.
God's people often use their gifts to preach, or to teach, to help others understand and appreciate what God has purposed for them. For centuries, God's people have used translations of the Scriptures to further his purpose, and another way they have done so is by distributing Bibles. The Bible itself becomes more valuable as time passes and as it continues to reach those who need it. In the 1940's, a committee called the New World Bible Translation Committee was formed to produce new translations of the Bible, and this work is now being carried on by over 130 translators. Their goals are: (1) To honor God's name by using his personal name throughout the Scriptures. (Matt. 6:9) (2) To translate the original texts accurately, making sure that the translators do not inject their own ideas into the translation. (3) To use simple language that can be understood even by those who are not well educated.—Neh. 8:8. w15 12/15 2:1, 2
How does it feel when you find something precious, and then share it with others?—1 Cor. 14:8.
Imagine how thrilled you would be to discover a hidden treasure! Similarly, we delight in sharing the good news with others, whether they are our friends or strangers. (1 Cor. 14:9) We do not want to hoard what we have learned, thinking that we should only share it with a select few. Instead, we want to help others benefit from the truth. But how can we make sure that our presentation is clear and easy to understand? Jesus set an example for us. Consider his sermon recorded in Matthew chapter 5 through chapter 7. His manner of speaking taught us important lessons about effective communication. He spoke simply and directly, avoiding complicated expressions. He used illustrations that people could relate to, and he asked questions that made them think. For instance, he might appeal to their conscience by pointing out how Jehovah feels about certain things. Then he would ask: "Would you really want to disappoint him?" (Matt. 6:26) So, let us strive to speak clearly and simply, asking ourselves, 'Is my message getting across?' w15 12/15 3:13, 14
Brotherly love unites us.—Acts 13:1.
What does brotherly love involve? The Greek word Paul used—philadelphía—literally means "love of brothers." A loving brother shows genuine concern for his spiritual siblings and is eager to help them. (John 11:36) Let us therefore endeavor to show both brotherly love and family affection. We show brotherly love to all our brothers and sisters. (Matt. 23:8) The love we show to one another is evidence that we are disciples of Jesus, and it is expressed in this way: "Let brotherly love continue. Be hospitable to one another." (1 Pet. 4:9) This love is similar to God's selfless love (agape), which motivates God's servants to show kindness to others. Like Christ, we strive to show brotherly love and family affection to everyone, even those who may not appreciate it. (1 John 10:12) And even when we face difficulties, Jehovah knows that we are trying to show love to our brothers and sisters.—1 Thess. 4:9. w16.01 1:5, 6

Mũndũũme wĩtawa Hitoshi athũkũmaa wĩa wa kwĩka masavu ma mbesa ovisinĩ ũmwe wa kũandĩka andũ wĩ nthĩ ya Japan. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Hitoshi na mũnene wake mayĩka masavu ma mbesa, mũnene wake amwĩie aumye livoti ĩte ya w'o. Hitoshi amwĩie kana wasya wake wa ngoo ndwaĩ ũmwĩtĩkĩlya ethĩwe ate mũĩkĩĩku. Nũndũ wa ũu, mũnene wake amwĩa nũkũmũvuta, na kwa w'o nĩwesie kũvutwa.
Myei ĩla yaatĩĩe, Hitoshi nĩwakwie ngoo mũno nũndũ oonaa ta ũtakesa kũkwata wĩa. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Hitoshi wamanthaa wĩa aisye kana ndesa kũtethya wĩa ũtonya kũtuma ethĩwa ate mũĩkĩĩku. Mũndũ ũla wamũkũlasya makũlyo nĩ kana aandĩkwe amwĩie atĩĩ: "Ndyaaĩw'a mũndũ wĩ na woni ta waku!" Andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Hitoshi na anyanyae nĩmamwĩkĩie vinya aendeee kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku, o na kau nĩwambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na nzika. Kwa ngelekany'o, Hitoshi aisye atĩĩ: "Naseng'aa kana ve vata wa kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũĩkĩĩku nũndũ wa maũndũ ala neemanyĩĩtye kuma Mbivilianĩ."
Maũndũ asu mamũkwatie Hitoshi metũlilikany'a kana ti andũ onthe monaa ũĩkĩĩku wĩ wa vata. Andũ amwe masũanĩaa kana kwĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku, na mũno mũno maũndũnĩ ma viasala nĩ ũndũ ũtatethya. Mũndũ mũka ũmwe ũthũkũmaa nthĩ ya South Africa aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩthyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ andũ mate aĩkĩĩku, na ve mavinda amwe andũ asu manzukumaa ũkethĩa nĩ laisi kwĩthĩwa nde mũĩkĩĩku."
Ve maũndũ maingĩ monanasya kana andũ ti aĩkĩĩku, ũmwe wa maũndũ asu nĩ ũvũngũ, na wĩ kĩla vandũ. Myaka yĩana ũna mĩvĩtu, ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe weekiwe nĩ mũsomi wĩtawa Robert S. Feldman wa University of Massachusetts Amherst, woonanisye kana andũ 60 katĩ wa 100 nĩmakenganaa o na ethĩwa nĩ savalĩ ũmwe katĩ wa kĩla ndatĩka ĩkũmi methĩawa maiea ngewa. Feldman aisye atĩĩ: "Ũndũ ũsu waĩ wa kũsengy'a mũno." Aendeee kwasya, "Tũyasũanĩaa kana kũkengana nĩ ũndũ andũ mekaa mate ũkũlya." Nĩ ũndũ wa kũsengy'a mũno kwona andũ aingĩ mamenete kũkengwa ĩndĩ mo nĩmakenganaa!
Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ mendete kũkengana, ũng'ei, na kwĩka maũndũ angĩ mekwonany'a kana ti aĩkĩĩku? Kwĩthĩwa andũ mate aĩkĩĩku kwĩ ũthũku mwaũ? Na ĩkũlyo yĩla ya vata mũno nĩ, Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũikethĩwe tũte aĩkĩĩku?

translation:
The famous writer Hitoshi spent time visiting the homes of people who write novels in Japan. One day, Hitoshi and his wife visited the homes of novelists; his wife told him to buy a ticket for the event. Hitoshi told her that his younger brother was already invited to the event and also attended. Because of this, his wife insisted on going with him, and she ended up being allowed to go along.
Recently, Hitoshi went to visit another home, but he couldn't find anyone to talk to. One day, Hitoshi met people who asked him if he wanted to try writing novels to pass the time and also attend the event. The person who encouraged him said to him: "I will help someone like you succeed!" The people around Hitoshi and his friends advised him to continue attending the event, and some even offered to take him there. However, Hitoshi said: "I wonder if the opportunity to attend the event is only for those who have connections with the Mbiviliani."
Many things happened to Hitoshi, making him realize that not everyone can easily get an invitation. Some people suspect that attending the event is difficult, and often the reasons why are unclear. One person from South Africa said: "We are discriminated against by people at the event, and sometimes others are favored when it comes to getting invitations to the event."
There are many stories about people who don't get invitations, one of which is discrimination, and it happens to everyone. Several years ago, a study conducted by renowned psychologist Robert S. Feldman of the University of Massachusetts Amherst found that approximately 60 out of 100 people lie once in every ten conversations they have. Feldman said: "This is a common phenomenon." He continued, "We suspect that lying is something most people do frequently." It is a common phenomenon indeed that many people tend to lie more often than they admit!
So, if many people tend to lie, what then, and how does this relate to whether or not someone gets an invitation? Does being among those invited depend on luck? And the simple truth is, we only know if we are invited if we actually receive an invitation!

KWASISYA nyũmba ĩno ũndũ yĩany'a andũ. Aa nĩ ana 12 ma Yakovo. Na aĩ o na eĩtu. We nĩwĩsĩ masyĩtwa ma syana imwe? Ekai twĩmanyĩsye masyĩtwa ma amwe moo.
Lea asyaie Leũveni, Simeoni, Livai, na Yuta. Yĩla Lakeli woonie kana ndeũsyaa syana, nĩwamakie mũno vyũ. Kwondũ wa ũu amũnenga Yakovo mũthũkũmi wake wa mwĩĩtu weetawa Mbila, nake Mbila asyaa ana elĩ meetawa Ndani na Navitali. O nake Lea amũnenga Yakovo mũthũkũmi wake wa mwĩĩtu weetawa Nziliva, na Nziliva asyaa Ngati na Aseli. Ĩtina Lea nĩwasyokie asyaa ana angĩ, Isakali na Nzevuluni.
Na ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kũmĩĩsya ĩvinda yĩasa Lakeli nĩwakwatie mwana. Na amwĩta syĩtwa yake Yosevu. Ĩtina tũkeemanyĩsya mũnango ĩũlũ wa Yosevu, nũndũ nĩwesie kũtw'ĩka mũndũ wa vata mũno. Aa nĩmo ana 11 ala Yakovo wasyaĩwe yĩla wekalaa na ĩthe wa Lakeli Lavani.
Na ĩngĩ Yakovo aĩ o na eĩtu, ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩwetete syĩtwa ya ũmwe tũ. Syĩtwa yake eetawa Ndina.
Ĩvinda nĩyavikie yĩla Yakovo watwie kũmũtia Lavani na kũsyoka Kanaani. Kwoou oombany'a andũ ma mũsyĩ wake mũnene na ndĩthya syake nene sya malondu na ng'ombe na ambĩĩa kyalo kĩu kĩasa.
Ĩtina wa Yakovo na andũ ma mũsyĩ wake kũsyoka na kwĩkalanga Kanaani kwa ĩvinda, Lakeli nĩwasyaie mwana ũngĩ. Ũu weethĩiwe me kyalonĩ. Lakeli nĩwaũnyie na vinya na esa o kũkw'a aisyaa. Ĩndĩ kana kanini ka kavĩsĩ kala kasyaiwe kaĩ o kaseo. Yakovo aketie Mbenyamini.
Nĩtũkwenda tũlilikane masyĩtwa ma ana 12 ma Yakovo nũndũ mbaĩ syonthe sya Isilaeli syaumie nthĩnĩ woo. Mbaĩ 12 sya Isilaeli syatw'ĩĩwe masyĩtwa kwĩanana na ana 10 ma Yakovo na ana elĩ ma Yosevu. Isaka ekalile myaka mingĩ ĩtina wa imwana ii kũsyawa, na no mũvaka ethĩwe atanie mũno kwĩthĩwa na esũkũũe aingĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ ekai twone ũndũ kweekĩkie kwa Ndina mwĩsũkũũe wake wa mwĩĩtu.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 29:32-35; 30:1-26; 35:16-19; 37:35.
Makũlyo
- Masyĩtwa ma ana thanthatũ ala Yakovo wasyaie na kĩveti kyake kya mbee Lea nĩ meva?
- Nĩ ana meva elĩ ala Nziliva mũthũkũmi wa mũndũ mũka wa Lea wamũsyaĩe Yakovo?
- Ana elĩ ala Mbila mũthũkũmi wa mũndũ mũka wa Lakeli wamũsyaĩe Yakovo meetawa ata?
- Nĩ ana meva elĩ ala Lakeli wasyaie, ĩndĩ kweekĩkie ata yĩla mwana wa kelĩ wasyaiwe?
- Kwosana na visa, Yakovo ena ana meana, na nĩ kyaũ kyaumie nthĩnĩ woo?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 29:32-35; 30:1-26; na 35:16-19.
Tondũ ũvoo wa ana 12 ma Yakovo ũkwonany'a, mavinda maingĩ imwana sya Aevelania syatw'ĩĩawa masyĩtwa ata?
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 37:35.
O na kũtw'ĩka Ndina nĩwe ũwetetwe nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia, twĩsĩ ata kana Yakovo aĩ na eĩtu aingĩ? (Mwa. 37:34, 35)

translation:
It happened that the house became full of people. And he had 12 sons by Jacob. And they also had daughters. Now, are these the names of the sons, one by one? Let us mention the names of some.
These are Leah's sons, Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah. Then Rachel bore children, but she was barren for a long time. So Jacob loved Rachel more than her sister Leah, and Leah served him instead. And Leah conceived and bore Jacob a son whom she named Bilhah, and Bilhah bore him two daughters named Dinah and Navital. Also Leah conceived and bore Jacob another son whom she named Zilpah, and Zilpah bore Ngati and Azel. Later Leah bore three more sons, Issachar and Nezavuluni.
And indeed, when Rachel saw that she could not conceive, she envied Leah and wished to have a child too. And she called his name Joseph. Later we will learn about Joseph's story, because it is important to know this great man. And he had 11 sons besides Jacob's firstborn son with Rachel, Lavan.
And again Jacob also had daughters, among them Bilhah who gave birth to one daughter. Her name was Dinah.
The matter happened so that Jacob decided to take Lavan and go to Canaan. He went with his people and his large family with flocks of sheep and cattle and many servants to a certain land.
When Jacob and his people arrived and settled in Canaan for a while, Rachel bore another son. This one was highly valued. Rachel died giving birth and did not survive. And when she was almost dead, she said something. Jacob mourned Benjamini.
Let us now review the names of Jacob's 12 sons so that all the tribes of Israel may remember them. The 12 tribes of Israel were named after Jacob's ten sons and Joseph's two sons. Isaac lived many years until his son grew up, and he was blessed with age and many possessions. And we see what happened to Dinah during her father's lifetime.
Genesis 29:32-35; 30:1-26; 35:16-19; 37:35.
Questions
- What are the names of the six sons Jacob had with his wife Leah?
- How many daughters did Zilpah, the handmaid of Leah's husband Jacob, bear?
- What are the names of the two daughters Bilhah, the handmaid of Rachel's husband Jacob, bore?
- How many sons did Rachel bear, and what happened when her first son was born?
- Considering the verses, Jacob had many children, and why are they remembered?
Further Questions
- Read Genesis 29:32-35; 30:1-26; and 35:16-19.
As the story of Jacob's twelve sons unfolds, how many of his sons were given names?
- Read Genesis 37:35.
And to understand God, who is revered in the Bible, do we know whether Jacob had more children? (Gen. 37:34, 35)

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mbivilia ndĩwetete sikũkũ ya Halloween. Ĩndĩ syĩthĩo ila syaatĩĩawa tene andũ maitanĩa sikũkũ ĩsu, vamwe na maũndũ ala andũ mekaa ũmũnthĩ maimĩtanĩa, nĩsyonanĩtye kana sikũkũ ĩsu yumanĩte na momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa andũ akw'ũ, na maveva mavuku.—Sisya kyongo "Wumo wa Halloween na syĩthĩo ila andũ maatĩĩaa maimĩtanĩa."
Mbivilia ĩtũkanĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũikoneke kwaku mũndũ ũla . . . ũkũlasya ala mesene na maveva, kana ũla ũmbasya ithitũ, kana ũla ũkũlasya akw'ũ." (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 18:10-12) Nayo ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 10:20, 21, Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Ndikwenda mwĩthĩwe mũamba na ndaimoni. Mũtitonya kũnyw'a kĩkombe kya Mwĩaĩi, na kĩkombe kya ndaimoni."
Wumo wa Halloween na syĩthĩo ila andũ maatĩaa maimĩtanĩa
Sikũkũ ya Samhain: Kwosana na ĩvuku The World Book Encyclopedia, Halloween yaumanie na "sikũkũ ya ndĩni sya ũvũngũ yĩtawa Samhain ĩla yatanĩawa nĩ mbaĩ ya Celtic myaka mbee wa 2,000 mĩvĩtu." "Mbaĩ ĩsu yaĩkĩĩaa kana ĩvindanĩ ya sikũkũ ĩsu, andũ akw'ũ maĩ matonya kũka kũla kwĩ andũ ala me thayũ." Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana ala akw'ũ "matyĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva." (Mũtavan'ya 9:5) Kwoou maitonya kũka kũla kwĩ andũ ala me thayũ.
Ngũa ila syĩkĩawa ĩvindanĩ ya sikũkũ ya Halloween, na mĩthĩnzĩo ĩngĩ: Kwosana na ĩvuku Halloween
—An American Holiday, An American History, andũ amwe ma mbaĩ ya Celtic meekĩaa ngũa sya ũtelemya nĩ kana maveva mavuku masũanĩe nĩ amwe moo na kwoou maikamaũmĩsye. O na angĩ nĩmanengae maveva asu ngelemende nĩ kana mamatanĩthye. Ĩvindanĩ ya tene nthĩ ya Europe, atongoi ma Katholeki nĩmoosie syĩthĩo sya andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai na meea aatĩĩi moo maendae nyũmba na nyũmba mekĩĩte ngũa sya mũthemba mũna na mayĩtya mĩthĩnzĩo nĩ kana mavoyee ala akw'ũ. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ndĩtĩkĩlĩtye kũvulany'a ũthaithi wa Yeova na syĩthĩo sya ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. —2 Akolintho 6:17.
Maimũ na ũe: Kwa ĩvinda ĩasa, maimũ na ũe syĩthĩĩtwe iikonanw'a na maveva mavuku. (ĩvuku Halloween Trivia) Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte tũleane na maveva mavuku na tũikatanĩe syĩthĩo ikonetye maveva asu.
—Aeveso 6: 12.
Malenge ala matũmĩawa sikũkũnĩ ya Halloween: Ĩvinda ya tene nthĩ ya Britain "avoyi maendaa nyũmba na nyũmba mayĩtya lĩu nĩ kana mavoyee ala akw'ũ." Methĩawa makuĩte ĩkwasĩ ya turnip yĩnzĩtwe maima na makekĩwa kendoo ila syoonanasya thayũ wa mũndũ wĩ tũalanĩ. (Ĩvuku Halloween
—From Pagan Ritual to Party Night) Andũ angĩ maasya kana mataa matũmĩawa kũsiĩĩa maveva mavuku. Myakanĩ ya 1800, nthĩ ya Amelika ya Ĩũlũ, malenge nĩmo matũmĩawa vandũ wa ĩkwasĩ ya turnip nũndũ maĩ maingĩ na maĩ laisi kũtonya maima. Syĩthĩo isu syonanasya mũĩkĩĩo wa kana thayũ ndũkusaa, ve tũalanĩ, na kana andũ no mavoyee ala akw'ũ, ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩleanĩte na maũndũ asu. —Esekieli 18:4.

translation:
The Bible says this:
The Bible is relevant during Halloween. It shows that people used to appease spirits on that day, some with offerings and others by staying away from certain things, fearing that the day might be associated with demonic influence and evil practices.—Read the scripture "The Origin of Halloween and Its Connection With Spiritism."
The Bible warns us saying: "Do not practice divination or sorcery or look for omens…or consult those who manipulate the dead." (Deuteronomy 18:10-12) Also, 1 Corinthians 10:20, 21 states: "What the pagans sacrifice they offer to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to become companions of demons."
The Origin of Halloween and Its Connection With Spiritism
Samhain Day: According to The World Book Encyclopedia, Halloween originated from "an ancient pagan festival called Samhain, which was observed by the Celts over 2,000 years ago." "The Celts believed that on this occasion the boundary between the world of the living and the realm of the dead became blurred." The Bible explains that the dead "are unconscious of anything," and cannot harm anyone. (Ecclesiastes 9:5) So, they cannot bother the living.
However, customs developed around the observance of Halloween, and other festivals: According to the book Halloween
—An American Holiday, An American History, some members of the Celtic tribes practiced forms of fortune-telling and also engaged in mischief. Others imitated demons and dressed up like them. In medieval Europe, Catholic priests sometimes continued the custom of going door-to-door asking for special food in exchange for prayers for the dead. The Bible instructs us to separate ourselves from spiritual wickedness.—2 Corinthians 6:17.
Children and Guising: Traditionally, children and guisers were associated with spirits. (Halloween Trivia) The Bible encourages us to avoid associating with spirit people and to shun practices connected with them.
—Ephesians 6:12.
Costumes Worn on Halloween: In olden times in Britain "people went from house to house begging for food or money." Hollowed turnips were carved with faces and lit candles inside, though they did not resemble human features. (Halloween
—From Pagan Ritual to Party Night) Other people wore costumes to impersonate spirits. During the 1800s, in rural America, costumes often replaced hollowed turnips because pumpkins were larger and easier to carve. Today's costumes often depict frightening creatures, ghosts, and demons, but the Bible condemns such things.—Ezekiel 18:4.

text:
NZA wa mũũnda wa Eteni, Atamu na Eva maĩ na mathĩna maingĩ. Maĩ no mũvaka mathũkũme na vinya nĩ kana makwate lĩu. Vandũ va mĩtĩ yĩ matunda maseo, moonie mĩw'a mingĩ na thangila imeete kĩla vandũ. Ũu nĩ w'o weethĩiwe yĩla Atamu na Eva maleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai na maeka kũtw'ĩka anyanya Make
Na ũndũ ũla mũthũku vyũ, Atamu na Eva nĩmambĩĩie kũkw'a. Lilikana Ngai nĩwamatavĩtye kana makakw'a ethĩwa makaya kuma mũtĩnĩ mũna. Mũthenya o ũla maĩye now'o mambĩlĩĩlye kũkw'a. Matumanĩte ta kĩ kũema kũmwĩw'a Ngai!
Syana syonthe sya Atamu na Eva syasyaiwe ĩtina wa Ngai kũmalũngya kuma mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. Ũu nĩkwasya kana syana isu o nasyo syaĩ no mũvaka ikũe na kũkw'a.
Kethĩwa Atamu na Eva nĩmamwĩwie Yeova, mo na syana syoo methĩwa matanĩie thayũ. Onthe mesaa kwĩkala na ũtanu tene na tene kũũ nthĩ. Vayaĩ ũmwe wesaa kũkũa, kũwaa na kũkw'a.
Ngai endaa andũ matũae na ũtanu tene na tene, na nĩwathanĩte kana mũthenya ũmwe ũu ũkeanĩa. Nthĩ yonthe ĩkethĩwa yĩ mbanake, namo andũ onthe makeethĩwa na mĩĩ mĩseo. Na kĩla mũndũ akeethĩwa mũnyanyae mũseo wa andũ onthe na wa Ngai.
Ĩndĩ Eva ndaaendeea kwĩthĩwa e mũnyanyae wa Ngai. Kwoou ndwaĩ ũndũ mũvũthũ kwake kũsyaa syana. Nĩweethĩawa na woo. Vate nzika kwĩthĩwa ate mwĩwi kwa Yeova nĩkwamũeteie kyeva kingĩ. We ndũĩtĩkĩlana na ũndũ ũsu?
Atamu na Eva maĩ na syana sya imwana na eĩtu. Yĩla mwana woo wa mbee wasyaiwe, mamwĩtie Kaini. Na mwana woo wa kelĩ mamwĩta Aveli. Nata kweekĩkie kwoo? We nĩwĩsĩ?
Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:16-23; 4:1, 2; Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4.

- Kethĩwa Atamu na Eva nĩmamwĩwie Yeova, mwĩkalĩle woo na wa syana syoo wĩthĩwa wailyĩ ata?

Yeova oonanisye ĩnee ata kwa Atamu na Eva mamina kwĩka naĩ? (Mwa. 3:7, 21)

And on that day, Adam and Eve were tempted to steal. But God showed them that they could not steal things from the tree. The reason why their hearts were tempted to steal. Don't let anyone tempt you to disobey God!
All the descendants of Adam and Eve have been condemned to die because of the sin in the Garden of Eden. This is why people today also sin and wrongdoings continue.
Because Adam and Eve disobeyed Jehovah, so did their children and grandchildren afterward. Always remember to be strong and courageous forever. One day you will grow up, mature, and steal.
God loves his people always and forever, and he wants you to remember this one thing. All the earth is beautiful, and people everywhere are blessed. And every person is blessed with good things from others and from God.

text:
Mavuku ma kũkũnzwa ma tene (scrolls) maseũvaw'a ata, na matũmĩawa ata?
Ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Luka yĩneeneete ĩũlũ wa Yesũ aivingũa ĩvuku kana ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa ya mwathani Isaia, na asoma na ayĩkũnza. Nake mwathani Yelemia nĩwakũlilw'e aandĩke ũvoo kuma kwa Ngai mavukunĩ ma kũkũnzwa.—Luka 4:16-20; Yelemia 36:2.
Mavuku makũkũnzwa maseũvaw'a ata? Tũlungu twa ithuma kana makangaa twakwatanaw'a na nguluu tũkatw'ĩka ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa. Yakwatanw'a nĩyakũnzĩĩawa kĩlungunĩ kya mũtĩ, ngalĩko ĩla ĩandĩkĩtwe yĩ nthĩnĩ. Ĩvuku yĩu yeethĩawa yĩandĩkĩtwe kuma ĩũlũ nginya nthĩ, na yĩaanĩtw'e na tũlungu (vertical columns). Ethĩwa ĩvuku yĩu nĩ yĩasa yeethĩawa na mĩtĩ ngalĩ syelĩ ĩla yatũmĩawa nĩ ũla ũkũsoma kũyĩkũnzũa. Ayĩkũnzũaa na kw'oko kũmwe kũla kũngĩ kũendeee na kũkũnza nginya akesa kũkwata vala ũkwendaa kũsoma.
Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩtawa The Anchor Bible Dictionary yaĩtye ũũ: "Ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa yeethĩawa yĩ ĩseo nũndũ yeethĩawa yĩ yĩasa [mavinda maingĩ yeethĩawa yĩ vakuvĩ vuti 33 (mita 10)] ũkethĩa ĩvuku yĩima no yĩandĩkwe kamwanyanĩ kanini." Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Luka yatalĩthaw'a ta yaĩ yĩtonya kwĩanĩa ĩvukunĩ ya kũkũnzwa ya ũasa wa vuti 31 (mita 9.5). Mavinda angĩ ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ na ya ĩtheo ya mavuku asu nĩyeananaw'a, ĩkakũnwa mũsasa, na ĩivakwa langi.
"Athembi anene" ala mawetetwe Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto methĩwa maĩ aaũ?
Kuma ĩla wĩa wa ũthembi wambĩĩie Isilaeli, mũndũũme ũmwe nĩwe weethĩawa e mũthembi mũnene na nĩwekalaa kyeonĩ kĩu nginya ĩla ũkakw'a. (Motalo 35:25) Aluni nĩwe waĩ mũthembi mũnene wa mbee. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, a-a-ĩthe nĩmambĩĩie kũtiĩa mwana woo ũla mũkũũ wĩa ũsu wa kwĩthĩwa mũthembi mũnene. (Kuma 29:9) Aũme ala masyaawa mũvĩanĩ wa Aluni nĩmo meethĩawa me athembi, ĩndĩ no anini moo meethĩwa me athembi anene.
Ĩla Aisilaeli masumbĩkiwe nĩ andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ, asumbĩ ma nthĩ isu manyuvaa athembi ala mekwenda na ĩvindanĩ yĩla mekwenda. Veonekana kana ala manyuvawa methĩwe me athembi anene meethĩawa maumĩte mĩsyĩnĩ ĩla yĩ nguma nzyawanĩ sya Aluni. Ndeto "athembi anene" yonanasya andũ ala maĩ na kyeo katĩ wa ala meethĩawa me athembi. Amwe ma ala maĩ athembi anene maĩ atongoi nyũmbanĩ 24 sya ũthembi; angĩ maumĩte mĩsyĩnĩ ĩla yĩ nguma nyũmbanĩ ila syanyuvawa athembi; na ala angĩ, ta ũmwe weetawa Anasi, maĩ athembi tene na maumw'a.

translation:
What scrolls were available at that time, and how were they made?
The account in Luke chapter 4 shows Jesus reading from a scroll—possibly a scroll of the writings of the prophet Isaiah—and then rolling it up and handing it back. The prophet Jeremiah was also instructed to write God's words on scrolls.—Luke 4:16-20; Jeremiah 36:2.
What kinds of scrolls were available at that time? Scrolls were often made from animal skins or papyrus, which were rolled up to form a scroll. Rolling it up protected the writing, similar to how we protect books today. Such scrolls were usually written on only one side, and the writing was arranged in vertical columns. Often, such a scroll was fastened to wooden rods to make it easier to roll out and read. To read it, one hand would hold the rolled portion while the other hand unrolled it gradually, continuing to unroll and read further along.
One reference work, *The Anchor Bible Dictionary*, states: "Scrolls were commonly about 10 meters [33 feet] long and 28 centimeters [11 inches] high." For example, the Dead Sea Scroll of the Book of Luke is said to be about 9.5 meters [31 feet] long. Other scrolls have been found that are wider and thicker, some being beautifully decorated and encased.
What does the expression "chief priests" refer to in the Christian Greek Scriptures?
In ancient Israel, the chief priest was the most important religious official and served as God's representative. He stood in a prominent position so that he could be seen by the people. (Numbers 35:25) He was the head of the priesthood. The size of the sanctuary, or temple, determined how many assistant priests there were. (2 Chronicles 29:9) Over time, families descended from Aaron came to be those who filled the positions of chief priests, and others who filled the positions of ordinary priests.
When the Israelites were conquered by foreign powers, they often continued to practice their religion, including having chief priests and sanctuaries. It seems that those appointed as chief priests were often chosen because of their political connections with the ruling authorities. The term "chief priests" thus refers to those who held a position of prominence among the priests. Some of these chief priests supervised 24 divisions of priestly service; others oversaw specific duties connected with the temple; and still others, such as Annas, functioned as chief priests even though they were no longer officially holding the office.

text:
1. Kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kũkaũtethya ata?
Vate nzika, momanyĩsyo asu ma mũsingi ma Mbivilia nĩmekĩĩte vinya wendo waku kwa Yeova. No nginya tũendee kwĩkĩa kĩthito ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda wendo ũsu ũendeee kwĩthwa wĩ mũlũmu. (1 Vetelo 2:2) Nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo wa thayũ ũtathela, no nginya ũendee kũmũthengeea Ngai kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto yake.
O ũndũ ũmanyi waku ĩũlũ wa Ngai wongelekeele, now'o mũĩkĩĩo waku wĩendeea kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũlũmu. Mũĩkĩĩo ũkaũtetheesya kũmwendeesya Ngai. (Aevelania 11:1, 6) Ũkatuma wĩlila na ũialyũla mwĩkalo waku wĩthĩwe wĩ mũseo.
2. Ũmanyi waku ĩũlũ wa Ngai ũtonya kũtetheesya angĩ ata?
Vate nzika, ũkendeew'a nĩ kũtavya angĩ maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩĩtye nũndũ ithyonthe nĩtwendeeaw'a nĩ kũtavya angĩ ũvoo mũseo. Waendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ũkamanya ũndũ ũtonya kũmĩtũmĩa kũelesya mũĩkĩĩo waku nthĩnĩ wa Yeova na ũvoo mũseo.
Andũ aingĩ mambĩaa kwa kũtavya anyanyae kana andũ ma mũsyĩ ũvoo mũseo. Ĩthĩwa mũĩ. Vandũ va kũmea ndĩni yoo nĩ ya ũvũngũ, matavye ĩũlũ wa mawatho ma Ngai. Ĩngĩ, lilikana kana mavinda maingĩ andũ mendeeaw'a mũnango nĩ mwĩkalĩle waku mũseo kwĩ kĩla ũũmatavya.
3. Ũtonya kũtanĩa ũnyanya ũilyĩ ata vamwe na Ngai?
Kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai kũkaũtetheesya kwĩana kĩveva. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, no wĩthĩwe na ũnyanya wa mwanya vamwe na Yeova. Kwa w'o, we no wĩthĩwe wake, wĩ ũmwe wa andũ ma mũsyĩ wake.
4. Ũtonya kũendeea kwĩka mandeeo ata?
Nũtonya kwĩka maendeeo ma kĩveva kwa kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai. (Aevelania 5:13, 14) Kũlya ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova akũmanyĩsye Mbivilia aitũmĩa ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? O ũndũ ũkũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai, now'o thayũ waku ũkũendeea kwaĩla.
Ũvoo mũseo umaa kwa Yeova, Ngai mũtanu. No ũmũthengee kwa kũthengeea andũ make. (Aevelania 10:24, 25) Waendeea kwĩthĩwa na kĩthito kya kũmwendeesya Yeova, wĩĩthĩwa ũendee kũtata kũvikĩla thayũ ũla wa w'o, ũla nĩ thayũ wa tene na tene. Kũmũthengeea Ngai nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mũseo vyũ ũtonya kwĩka.

translation:
1.
1. Will continuing to study the Bible ever become tiresome?
Truly, our understanding of the fundamental teachings of the Bible has grown stronger as we have walked with Jehovah. So let us continue to seek wisdom, so that our devotion may endure forever. (1 Peter 2:2) And if you are weighed down by a feeling of inadequacy, continue to confide in God by studying his Word.
Or, if your heart feels sluggish, let your love for God motivate you to seek wisdom. (Hebrews 11:1, 6) This will help you to remain enthusiastic about spiritual matters.
2. Can our appreciation for God's Word ever diminish?
Truly, our privilege is to apply what we learn from the Scriptures to all aspects of our life. As you continue to study the Bible, you will come to know more ways to show your appreciation for Jehovah's loving provision and guidance.
Many people lose their zeal because they focus on their own shortcomings or on the imperfections of others. Don't be like them. Remember that those who serve within God's organization are imperfect, but strive to imitate their faith. Also, do not allow minor disagreements to disrupt your unity.
3. Can we maintain closeness to God despite imperfection?
Studying God's Word can help us to feel closer to him. By doing so, you will strengthen your bond with Jehovah. In this way, you and your family will become part of his family.
4. Can we make progress in our ministry despite difficulties?
We can make real progress in our ministry by continuing to study God's Word. (Hebrews 5:13, 14) Does one of Jehovah's shepherds encourage you to read the Bible and ask yourself, 'How can I use this scripture in my ministry?' Or, if you find it difficult to continue studying God's Word, remember that it is an investment in your future.
That family is precious to Jehovah, the true God. Show your love for them by encouraging others. (Hebrews 10:24, 25) Continue to be motivated by your desire to please Jehovah, and you will remain united with them forever, always. Showing love to God is the most important thing you can do.

Muvea wa kusuvia nyamu sya kithekani wa KWS nuwetie kana nutonya utila utethyo ula methiitwe mainenga imwe sya syana ila syiiviawa fees ila syumitwe misyini ila ituanie na mutitu wausuvia nyamu sya kithekani kya Kyulu,myaki ila ikwataa mutituni uu yaendeea kwananga mutitu usu.
Usu uneeniwe ni amwe ma Maovisaa ma KWS ala meekomanie na enenthi nduani ya Kikunduku_Kibwezi kuneenea undu thina wa mwaki ula ukwataa kiimani kii utonya kuthela ekali ma kisio kiu maitetheanisye na KWS,kuu KWS yiiweta ilovia isu nutonya utilika kutumika kuvosya myaki na utungiia mutitu usu.
Aineena itina wa umbano usu MCA musakue wa Thange Eric Katumo nutulile muti KWS kwenda kuweta ta ekali ma kisio kiu makwatasya myaki mutituni wa Kyulu aiweta nukuendeea ukwatiania na enenthi kusuvia mititu usu aiweta nukuendeea kutwaiisya mbumbano na enenthi kumatavya vata wa kiima kii,ayenda ekali ma kisio kii ala matuanie na kyulu kunewa mwanya kuithya na kutema nyeki ya indo mutituni wa Kyulu undumwe na KWS kuandika amwe ma ekali ma kisio kiu ta athukumi kutetheesya kusuvia mutitu usu.
Enenthi ala meivikite umbanoni usu niamendeeie kuweta kutetheeanisya na KWS kusuvia mutitu wa Kyulu na kuthuima ala matonya itha makwatasya myaki nziakaioni sya kusuvia Kyulu
KWS yiweta ta makee utumia ilovia mbingi kuvosya mwaki wakwata Kyulu nakumia ngalama nene kutungiiya mutitu uu wakwata mwaki ilovia ila meuweta syaile itha iitumika kutetheesya ala matuanie na mutitu uu tanzia ya utui museo na mutitu usu.

translation:
The KWS wildlife conservation area manager has announced that they will soon begin implementing a plan that was previously discussed among stakeholders, but which has been delayed due to fee issues and machinery problems, but it will cooperate with the effort to conserve wildlife in the Kyulu region, however it requires funding to continue this work.
This initiative involves some KWS rangers who have been collaborating with local communities around Kikunduku_Kibwezi to address the issue of illegal logging which threatens the forest, and KWS wants to ensure that this can be used to protect the forest and improve this work.
The Thange MCA Eric Katumo stated that KWS should go ahead and implement the plan to address the illegal logging problem affecting the Kyulu region and continue working with communities to conserve forests, and also continue strengthening cooperation with communities to prevent damage to the hills, going ahead with the plan to address the illegal logging problem and cooperating with Kyulu to create an opportunity to monitor and stop the destruction of trees in the Kyulu region together with KWS to establish some of the plans to effectively conserve the forest.
Communities are welcoming this initiative and are eager to work with KWS to conserve the Kyulu forest and its resources, but they need assurance that they can benefit from protecting the Kyulu forest.
KWS says it needs more resources to protect the Kyulu forest and significant funds to improve this work, but it says it will still work to effectively collaborate with the forest and the community.

text:
MŨISYO ŨLA WAĨ VO: Makangaa na kĩthuma nĩsyo syatũmĩawa mũno nĩ aandĩki ma Mbivilia na ala mesie kũmyumĩĩsya. * (2 Timotheo 4:13) Syĩndũ isu syatũmĩawa kũandĩka Mbivilia syatumie ata yĩthĩwa yĩ mũisyonĩ mũnene wa kwanangĩka?
Makangaa nĩmakũaa laisi, nĩmanangĩkaa mĩtũkĩ na maithela langi. Asomi metawa Richard Parkinson na Stephen Quirke maisye atĩĩ: "Ĩkangaa yoaa mĩtũkĩ na yĩitw'ĩka ndii na yĩyambĩĩa kwĩtĩka ta mũtutu." Mongeleeile kwasya: "Ĩla ĩvuku yĩseũvĩtw'e na makangaa yaiwa yĩ ĩkũnze no yĩmesye mbuka, yĩkoa kana yĩkaĩwa nĩ tũsamũ ta mũthwa." Mavuku amwe ma makangaa mamina kwoneka, malekeilwe sua kana ũthithu na ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie manangĩka na mĩtũkĩ.
Kĩthuma nĩkyo kĩkalaa ĩvinda ĩasa kwĩ ĩkangaa ĩndĩ o nakyo nĩkyanangĩkaa na mĩtũkĩ kyalekelw'a sua, kana ũthithu. * O na nĩkĩĩsawa nĩ tũsamũ. Ĩvuku yĩtawa Everyday Writing in the Graeco-Roman East, ĩyĩelesya ĩũlũ wa mavuku ala maandĩkiwe tene yaĩtye kana "ndyaĩ laisi kwa mavuku ala maandĩkawa tene kwĩkala ĩvinda ĩasa." Kwoou keka mavuku asu nĩmaanangĩkie, tũyĩsa kũkwata ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ.
KĨLA KYATUMIE MBIVILIA ĨTATHELA: Mĩao ya Ayuti yaĩtye kana Asumbĩ onthe maaĩle 'kwĩyumĩĩsya ũandĩko wa mĩao ĩvukunĩ.' Mĩao ĩsu yaĩ ala mavuku atano ma mbee ma Mbivilia. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 17:18) O na aandĩki me na ũtũĩka nĩmaumĩĩisye mavuku maingĩ mũno ma Maandĩko ala maĩ mavukunĩ ma tene, nginya tũivika myakanĩ ya mbee 100 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa weethĩa Maandĩko no makwatĩkane masinakokenĩ onthe ala maĩ Isilaeli na masinakokenĩ ala maĩ Masetonia. (Luka 4:16, 17; Meko ma Atũmwa 17:11) Veethĩiwe ata nginya weethĩa ũmũnthĩ no tũkwate mavuku amwe ma tene ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia?
Mũsomi ũmwe wa Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki wĩtawa Philip W. Comfort aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ayuti nĩmeekĩaa mavuku ma kũkũnzwa mĩtũnginĩ ĩseũvĩtw'e na yũmba nĩ kana mavuku asu masũvĩĩke." Nĩvatonyeka o namo Aklĩsto makethĩwa maatĩĩie nzĩa ĩsu ya kwia mavuku. Na nũndũ wa ũu, mavuku amwe ma tene ala matũmĩkaa kũalyũla Mbivilia nĩmeethĩawa mĩtũnginĩ ĩseũvĩtw'e na yũmba kana mavingĩwe masandũkũnĩ kana makethĩwa ngunganĩ na kũndũ kwaĩ kũmũ vyũ.
ŨNDŨ ŨSU ŨTETHETYE ATA?: Mavuku maingĩ ma tene ala matũmĩawa kũandĩka Mbivilia mevo o na ũmũnthĩ. Amwe ma mavuku asu me na ũkũũ wa myaka mbee wa 2,000. Vai ĩvuku yĩngĩ ya tene yĩ mavuku matonya kũtũmĩwa kũyĩalyũla na makũũ ta asu ma Mbivilia.
^ kal. 3 Makangaa ala maandĩkawa maseũvaw'a kuma makangaanĩ ala mameaa kĩw'ũnĩ. Nakyo kĩthuma kyeethĩawa kyumĩte nyamũnĩ.
^ kal. 5 Kwa ngelekany'o, ũandĩko ũla weekĩiwe saii ĩla Amelika yakwatie wĩyathi (U.S. Declaration of Independence) waandĩkĩtwe kĩthumanĩ. Ĩndĩ yu nĩvathelete myaka ta 250 kuma ũandĩko ũsu waandĩkwa, na ndeto ila syĩ vo iendeee ivutĩkĩte ũkethĩa iyĩsa kũsomeka nesa.

translation:
PEN AND INK: Papyrus and ink were commonly used in ancient times for writing on papyrus and other materials. * (2 Timothy 4:13) Why was papyrus used to write the Bible, even though there were more durable writing materials available?
Papyrus is made from reeds, which grow along rivers and marshes. Scholars Richard Parkinson and Stephen Quirke observe: "Papyrus was an excellent surface for writing on and lent itself to detailed work." They further explain: "The quality of papyrus depended on the skill with which the strips were laid and pressed together, and the best came from plants grown in marshland." Some pieces of papyrus have survived remarkably well, lasting for centuries or even millennia.
Ink was also essential for writing on papyrus, and it was often made from soot or gum. * It was also necessary to be careful. The book Everyday Writing in the Graeco-Roman East explains that many ancient documents were written on papyrus because it was a readily available material. So, despite its limitations, we can appreciate the value of papyrus to the writers of the Bible.
WHAT THE BIBLE SAYS ABOUT WRITING MATERIALS: The people of Egypt commonly referred to their writings as "books" or "rolls." Other materials besides papyrus were also used for writing portions of the Bible. (To Learn More 17:18) And writers could use various styles when writing, sometimes using abbreviations to save space, especially when copying Scripture to make it easier for Jews and Gentiles alike to read. (Luke 4:16, 17; Acts 17:11) Would it surprise you to learn that some ancient writings were deliberately damaged to prevent the Bible from being spread?
One biblical scholar named Philip W. Comfort states: "Scribes often made corrections by scraping away the original writing and then writing over it." This suggests that Christians may have reused old manuscripts. In fact, some ancient texts used to copy the Bible have been found with earlier writings scraped off or overwritten with new text.
IS THIS UNUSUAL?: Many ancient writings that have survived until today were written on perishable materials. Some writings date back nearly 2,000 years. Yet, many ancient writings have been preserved despite being written on fragile materials like papyrus.
^ par. 3 Ancient inks were made from different substances, and some faded over time. But this did not render them useless.
^ par. 5 For example, the American Declaration of Independence was written with iron gall ink. It has now been about 250 years since that document was written, yet much of the ink remains legible and easy to read.

text:
MWOOLOTO WA MBIVILIA: Endeeai "kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene, ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva e na ũndũ na ũngĩ; o tondũ Mwĩaĩi wamũekeie, inyw'ĩ nenyu ĩkaai o ta ũu."—Akolosai 3:13.
Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Mbivilia ĩelekanĩtye naĩ na ĩkoani, nakw'o kũekea kũelekanĩtw'e na kũĩva ĩkoani. (Luka 11:4) Ĩvuku yĩmwe yaĩtye kana Maandĩkonĩ, ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "ekea" yonanasya "kũekea mũndũ kĩndũ wĩĩmũtaĩte ũtakamũandũa ĩngĩ." Kwoou ĩla twavanga kũekea mũndũ ũtũvĩtĩsye, tũyaĩle kũsũanĩa kana ve ũndũ waĩle kwĩka nĩ kana atũĩve nũndũ nĩtwamũekea. Kũekea kũyonanasya kana nĩtũkwĩtĩkĩlana na ũndũ mũthũku, kana nĩtũũvũthĩĩsya ĩkosa yĩla yeekwa. Vandũ va ũu, kwonanasya kana nĩtũekaa kũia ũthũku ngoonĩ o na ethĩwa twĩ na "ũndũ na [mũndũ] ũngĩ."
Ũĩ ũsu no ũtũmĩke ũmũnthĩ? Ithyonthe nĩtũvĩtasya nũndũ twĩ ene naĩ. (Alomi 3:23) Kwoou, twĩthĩawa twatũmĩa ũĩ ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩla twaekea andũ ala angĩ, nũndũ ĩvinda yĩngĩ tũkeethĩwa tũyenda kũekewa. O na ĩngĩ, ĩla twaekea ala angĩ, nĩtũtethekaa. Tũtethekaa ata?
Nithyĩ tũũmĩaa ĩla twaendeea kũthata, twaia ũthũku ngoonĩ, na twalea kũekea. Maũndũ asu no matume twĩkala tũte na ũtanu, na tũyĩkalaa ta twĩ kyovonĩ. O na ĩngĩ, no matume tũkwatwa nĩ mowau mathũku. Ũvoo ũmwe waandĩkiwe nĩ Dr. Yoichi Chida, na mũsomi mũnene (Professor of Psychology) wĩtawa Andrew Steptoe, ĩkasetinĩ ya Journal of the American College of Cardiology, waisye kana, 'Ũkunĩkĩli wa mĩtũkĩ wĩonany'a kana ũwau wa ngoo [coronary heart disease] no ũetwe nĩ kũthata na woo mwingĩ.'
Kwasũanĩa moathimo ala methĩawa vo ĩla twaekeanĩa. Ĩla twaekea ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ, nĩvethĩawa mũuo na ngwatanĩo, na ũu nũsũvĩaa ũnyanya witũ vamwe namo. Na ũndũ ũla wa vata mũno nĩ kana nĩtwonanasya nesa vyũ kana nĩtũatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ya Ngai, ũla ũekeaa vyũ ala mamũvĩtĩsya na meelila, na nĩwendaa o naitũ tũekee vyũ ala matũvĩtĩsya.—Maliko 11:25; Aeveso 4:32; 5:1.

translation:
THE IMPORTANCE OF FORGIVENESS: Continue "forgiving one another, just as Jehovah has forgiven you, so also you should forgive others."—Colossians 3:13.
What does this scripture teach us? Forgiveness is linked to mercy, and forgiving is linked to receiving mercy. (Luke 11:4) One meaning of the Greek word rendered "forgive" conveys the idea of "generously excusing someone something they have done wrong." When we readily forgive someone who has wronged us, we show that we are willing to overlook their offense, or that we do not hold a grudge against them. To forgive means to let go of resentment, or to stop being angry over an injury. In fact, it may mean overlooking a serious wrongdoing, or letting go of the desire for revenge. People do this when they realize that they too have committed wrongs and need forgiveness from God and from others—they understand what it feels like to be forgiven.
How can we cultivate forgiveness? We must put ourselves in their place. (Romans 3:23) So, if we want to apply the principle found in the scriptures regarding forgiving others, we must first recognize our own imperfections. And when we forgive others, we are demonstrating reasonableness. Are we reasonable at all times?
When we find it difficult to forgive, we become stressed, and we risk becoming bitter. Such feelings can make us unhealthy, both emotionally and physically. They can also lead to serious health problems. A study published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology by Dr. Yoichi Chida and Professor of Psychology Andrew Steptoe showed that 'hostility is associated with an increased risk of [coronary heart disease].'
Consider how important it is to forgive others. When we forgive others readily, we experience inner peace and joy, and this benefits our health. Also, doing so may help us avoid stumbling into sin, which could damage our relationship with God, and would prevent us from receiving answers to our prayers.—Mark 11:25; Ephesians 4:32; 5:1.

Nũũlilikana ĩvinda wavalũkile wĩ kana kanini? Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa waũmĩie kw'oko kana mau. Nũlilikene ũndũ inyia waku waũkiakiisye waũmĩa? No kwĩthĩwa athambisye vala vaĩ kĩtau na akwova. O na kau nĩwaĩie, nĩweewie nesa ĩla inyia waku waũtavisye ndeto nzeo na aũkumbatĩa. Waĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi mũno kũkwata ũkiakisyo ĩvindanĩ yĩu waĩ mũnini.
Ĩndĩ o ũndũ tũendeee na kũkũa, now'o maũndũ maendeeaa kwĩthĩwa me momũ. Mathĩna maendeeaa na kwingĩva na ũyĩthĩa nĩ vinya kũkwata ũkiakisyo. Na ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana o na kau asyai maitũ no matũkumbatĩe ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna, nĩ vinya kũmina mathĩna asu. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii.
Ĩla mũndũ wavutwa wĩa, aũmĩaa mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, Julian aĩtye kana ĩla wavutiwe, akwatiwe nĩ kĩmako kingĩ mũno. Eekũlasya-ĩ, 'Ngasũvĩaa andũ makwa ata? Ĩtina wa kũthũkũmana na kambunĩ ĩsu ĩvinda yĩasavĩte ũu, monie ndesa kũmatethya?'
Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa wĩ na kĩmako nũndũ mũtwaano waku nũnaanangĩkie. Mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Raquel aĩtye atĩĩ: "Naĩ na kĩmako kingĩ mũno vyũ ĩla natiiwe nĩ mũemewa myei 18 mĩvĩtu. Neew'aa ngoo yakwa ta ĩtilanĩtw'e ilungu ilĩ." Aendeee na kwasya atĩĩ: "Woo ũla naĩ naw'o waĩ mwingĩ mũno vyũ, o na nĩwatumaa nĩtelema."
O na nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa ũwaĩte mũno na wonaa ũwau ũsu ta ũtesa kũvoa. No vethĩwe ve mavinda wĩw'aa o tondũ Yovu weew'aa ĩla waisye atĩĩ: "Nĩngũthĩtha thayũ wakwa; ndikwenda kwĩkala thayũ ĩndĩ yonthe." (Yovu 7:16) O na nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa wĩw'aa ta mũndũũme wĩtawa Luis, ũla wĩ na myaka 80 na kĩndũ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ve mavinda amwe nĩw'aa naĩle o kũkw'a."
Kana no wĩthĩwe wendaa kũkiakiw'a nũndũ nĩwakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũndũ wendete. Mũndũũme wĩtawa Robert aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩla mwanawa wakw'ĩĩe ndekenĩ ĩla yavalũkile, ya mbee ndyaĩkĩĩaa. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda neewie naũmĩa mũno ngoonĩ. Woo ta ũsu neewie ũelekanĩtw'e Mbivilianĩ na ũvyũ ũkũtonya ngoo."—Luka 2:35.
Robert, Luis, Raquel, na Julian nĩmakwatie ũkiakisyo, o na kau nĩmakwatĩtwe nĩ maũndũ maito mũno. Nĩmakwatie ũkiakisyo kuma kwa Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe, ũla nĩwe ũtonya kũtũkiakisya nesa kwĩ mũndũ o na wĩva. Atũkiakiasya ata? We no aũkiakisye ũndũ wakiakiisye andũ asu twoona?

translation:
Did you experience a dream where you saw someone or something? Did they appear clear or blurry? Did you have a strange feeling about this dream? But perhaps they were just tired and imagining things. And sometimes, we dream of things we deeply desire and embrace them. Don't let a small issue prevent you from understanding your dreams fully.
But how does something grow and develop, and what causes things to happen the way they do? Sometimes things happen because of effort and dedication, which helps us understand. And the ability to learn is like having the opportunity to gain knowledge, and when we acquire knowledge through effort, it helps us overcome challenges. Let's reflect on this carefully.
If a person is troubled, they worry a lot. For example, Julian wondered if she was being watched, and felt burdened by a great responsibility. She asked herself, "Should I trust anyone at all? The desire to connect with another community that seems better than this one makes me want to speak up."
They appeared clear to her with a significant problem that caused her much anxiety. A woman named Raquel said: "I have a great responsibility because I was given 18 talents." She continued, saying: "Oh, I wish I had more responsibility, so I could be useful."
And they appeared clear to her, and she saw the future clearly. But some people see dreams as meaningless. Job once said: "I would rather die than live like this forever." (Job 7:16) And they appeared clear to a man named Luis, who was eighty years old. He said: "Some dreams come true."
Or maybe a dream is interpreted based on what the dreamer already believes. A man named Robert said: "If a child of yours has a vision, remember what they saw, and cherish it. The purpose of the dream is to give you hope. This is how it will be until the day you meet in Mbiviliani and everything becomes clear."—Luke 2:35.
Robert, Luis, Raquel, and Julian embraced the interpretation, and they were comforted by those important things. They embraced the interpretation from Almighty God, who is able to help us interpret visions and dreams. Will he help us? Why don't you ask him to explain the meaning of your dreams?

Leveka aĩ mũndũ mũka wamwendete Yeova. Mũũme wake eetawa Isaka. Isaka o nake nĩwamwendete Yeova. Leveka amanyanie na Isaka ata? Leveka oonanisye ata kana nĩwendaa kũmũtanĩthya Yeova? Eka twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Leveka.
Isaka aĩ mwana wa Avalaamu na Sala. Mo mekalaa nthĩ ya Kanaani na andũ ma Kanaani mayamũthaithaa Yeova. Ĩndĩ, Avalaamu endaa mwana wake atwae mũndũ mũka ũmũthaithaa Yeova. Kwoou, nĩwamũtũmie mũthũkũmi wake akamũmanthĩe Isaka mũka vandũ veetawa Aalani, vala amwe ma andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Avalaamu mekalaa. Nĩvatonyeka mũthũkũmi ũla watũmiwe akethĩwa aĩ Elieseli.
Elieseli aendie Aalani na athũkũmi angĩ ma Avalaamu. Yaĩ savalĩ ndaasa mũno. Maendie na ngamĩle ĩkũmi ikuĩte lĩu na mĩthĩnzĩo. Elieseli esaa kũmanya ata mũndũ mũka ũla ũkũmũnyuvĩa Isaka? Ĩla Elieseli na athũkũmi asu mavikie Aalani, mambie kũũngama kĩthimanĩ nũndũ Elieseli nĩweesĩ kana andũ nĩmekũka kũuta kĩw'ũ. Kwoou amũvoya Yeova ayasya: 'Mwĩĩtu ũla ngũmwĩa anenge kĩw'ũ na ayĩtĩkĩla kũnenga na aisyoka ainenge ngamĩle, ngamanya kana mwĩĩtu ũsu nĩwe ũnyuvĩte.'
Na ĩndĩ mwĩĩtu weetawa Leveka ooka kĩthimanĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Leveka aĩ mwanake mũno. Elieseli amwĩtisye kĩw'ũ, nake Leveka amwĩa: 'Nĩngũũtavĩla kĩw'ũ, na ndisyoka nĩnyithye ngamĩle syaku.' Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũsu! Ngamĩle syĩ na waũni inyusaa kĩw'ũ kingĩ mũno, na kwoou Leveka aaĩle kũsyokanĩsya kĩthimanĩ mavinda maingĩ mũno. Nũmwene vaa visanĩ ũndũ ũendee kũnenga ngamĩle kĩw'ũ na kĩthito?— Elieseli nĩwatanie mũno kwona ũndũ Yeova wasũngĩie mboya yake.
Elieseli nĩwamũnengie Leveka mĩthĩnzĩo mingĩ myanake. Nake Leveka amũthokya Elieseli e na athũkũmi ala angĩ maende kwoo mũsyĩ. Elieseli avika nĩwaeleisye kĩla kyatumie Avalaamu amũtũma ku Aalani na aelesya ũndũ Yeova wasũngĩie mboya yake. Andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Leveka nĩmatanie mũno, na meetĩkĩla Leveka atwawe nĩ Isaka.
Leveka nĩwaendie Kanaani vamwe na Elieseli na atwawa nĩ Isaka
Ĩndĩ wĩona ata: Leveka nĩwendaa kũtwawa nĩ Isaka?— Leveka nĩwamanyie kana Elieseli atũmĩtwe nĩ Yeova. Kwoou, ĩla andũ ma mũsyĩ mamũkũlilye Leveka kana nũkwenda kũthi akatwawe nĩ Isaka, Leveka nĩweetĩkĩlile na asya: 'Ĩĩ nĩngũthi.' Na o vu kwa vu aenda vamwe na Elieseli. Ĩla mavikie Kanaani, Leveka nĩwatwaiwe nĩ Isaka.
Yeova nĩwamũathimie Leveka nũndũ Leveka eekie ũndũ Yeova wendaa. Aathimiwe ata? Ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ, Yesũ nĩwasyaiwe nthĩnĩ wa mũsyĩ wake! O naku Yeova akakũathima weethĩwa ũilyĩ ta Leveka na wamũtanĩthya.

translation:
Leva was a woman who worshiped Jehovah. Her husband's name was Isaac. Isaac also worshiped Jehovah. Did Leva get acquainted with Isaac? Did she think about pleasing Jehovah? Let us examine some things about Leva.
Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah. They lived in the land of Canaan among the Canaanites who worshiped Jehovah. Now, Abraham sent his servant to find a wife for his son, a woman who would worship Jehovah. So he sent his trusted servant and instructed him to find Isaac a wife from among the relatives of Abraham who lived there. The servant took ten camels loaded with gifts. The servant wondered whether he would find a woman who would be kind to Isaac? But the servant and his men arrived at Nahor, and they waited near a well during the evening time. The servant prayed to Jehovah saying: "Show me kindness if I am to succeed, so that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please give me a drink,' and who replies, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too,' may be the one you have chosen."
And just then a woman named Rebecah came out to draw water. She carried a large jar on her shoulder. The servant ran to meet her and said, "Please let me have a drink." She quickly lowered her jar and gave him a drink, and then she offered to water his camels. After the servant had observed her kindness, he thought, 'This is the one Jehovah has chosen.' He gave the woman jewelry and asked about her family. She told him that her father was Bethuel and that she had a brother named Laban.
The servant praised Jehovah and said, "Blessed be Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, who has shown me such kindness!" Then the servant returned to Abraham and reported everything. Laban and Bethuel were happy and agreed to give their daughter to Isaac. So Leva went with the servant and Isaac to Canaan.
Leva traveled to Canaan with the servant and was married to Isaac.
Just think: Leva was willing to marry Isaac—someone she had never met!—But Leva realized that the servant had been sent by Jehovah. Therefore, when her relatives tried to persuade her not to go with Isaac, Leva replied, "I will go." And so she went with the servant. Once they arrived in Canaan, Leva became Isaac's wife.
Jehovah blessed Leva, and she conceived and bore twins. Was she overjoyed? Many years later, Jesus spoke of this event! May Jehovah bless you too and remember you favorably like Leva.

KWASISYA mĩtĩ ĩya mĩasa, malaa manake, na iĩma ndũlu. Vaa tyo vandũ vanake? Kwoona ndaatai ĩya ĩkũya kuma kw'okonĩ kwa kamwana. Na kwasisya mĩnyambũ na ũisisya mbalasi iiya iũngamĩte kĩsesinĩ kĩ vuvĩ. We tyo wendeew'e nĩkwĩkala nthĩnĩ wa nyũmba yĩ vandũ vailyĩ ta vaa?
Ngai eenda wĩĩkala tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ya valatiso. Na ndekwenda we wĩthĩwe na kyalya kana woo o na wĩva ila ithĩnasya andũ ũmũnthĩ. Mbivilia yathaana ũũ kwa ala metũa nthĩnĩ wa valatiso ĩsu nzaũ: 'Ngai akeethĩwa e vamwe nao. Na kĩkw'ũ kĩikethĩwa vo ĩngĩ kana kũĩa kana woo. Maũndũ ma mbee nĩ mavĩtu.'
Yesũ akaĩkĩĩthya kana ũalyũko ũsu mũseo nĩweethĩwa. We nĩwĩsĩ nĩ ĩndĩĩ? Nĩ ĩtina wa Yesũ kũvetanga mothũku onthe na andũ athũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Lilikana, yĩla Yesũ waĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩwavoasya andũ mowau ma mĩthemba yonthe, o na nĩwathayũũkasya andũ. Yesũ eekaa ũu nĩ kana onany'e ũndũ wĩĩthĩwa atonya kwĩka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe yĩla wĩtw'ĩka Mũsumbĩ wa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai.
Kwatata kũsũanĩa kũkeethĩwa kũseũvĩte ta kĩ nthĩnĩ wa valatiso ĩsu nzaũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ! Yesũ, vamwe na amwe ma ala ũnyuvĩte, makeethĩwa masumbĩkĩte ĩtunĩ. Asumbĩ asu makasũvĩa kĩla mũndũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na kũĩkĩĩthya kana e na ũtanu. Ekai twone ũndũ twaĩlĩtwe nĩkwĩka nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na w'o ki kana Ngai akatũnenga thayũ wa tene na tene nthĩnĩ wa valatiso ĩsu nzaũ.
