Because of the trees of deceit, evil people, and a beautiful house. How are those people? Truly I have come to show the way to the child. And because of the spirits and to reveal this thing which has been hidden in secret. Why don't you want to stay in the house where those people were?
God wants to be there forever in the day of salvation. And I will go wherever you go whether good or bad and I will live among people. My friend has gone to look for help in the day of our salvation now saying: 'God is praised by others.' And whatever is praised is good or bad. Things that are small are important.
Jesus showed that if your heart is clean it will be seen. Are you ready today? It is the nature of Jesus to visit everyone and his people in the day of salvation. Therefore, since Jesus is in the day of salvation he heals people from all their hopes and comforts people. Jesus did this so that anyone who believes can enter the entire day of salvation and become a servant of the servant of God.
Hurry up to accept being saved so that it may be in the day of our salvation now in the day of salvation! Jesus, together with others who believe, makes difficult things easy. These difficulties affect everyone in the day of salvation and show them whether they are happy or sad. Let us see what we have learned to know whether we have been given by someone or God will lead us through the day of our salvation now.

- What did the Bible say to those who lived in the world?
- What did Jesus show regarding the hearts of people who seek him?
- Since Jesus is in the day of salvation, did he show anything about becoming a Servant of the Servant of God?
- What things did Jesus and others experience when they suffered that shows how they suffered in the day of salvation today?
Additional Questions
- Read Revelation 5:9, 10.
How can we be given a heart like theirs who suffer in the day of Salvation during the time of the Great Year and make their suffering and prayers acceptable? (Acts 4:20-24; 1 Peter 1:7; 3:8; 5:6-10)
- Read Revelation 14:1-3.
Is the writing of the names of the Father and the name of the Lamb on the foreheads of the 144,000 seen anywhere? (1 Corinthians 3:23; 2 Timothy 2:19; Revelation 3:12)

text:
NDETO isu syaneeniwe nĩ Ndaviti, ũla waĩ wa mbaĩ ya Isilaeli, aikatha mũndũ mũka ũmwe wakomanie nake. Mũndũ mũka ũsu eetawa Avikaili. We Ndaviti amũkathaa nĩkĩ, na tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Avikaili ata?
Ndaviti akomanie na Avikaili ĩvinda yĩla wasembete akĩĩte Mũsumbĩ Saulo. Avikaili atwaĩtwe nĩ mũthwii weetawa Navali, ũla waĩthĩasya indo syake mbingĩ nthĩ yĩ iĩma yaĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya Yuta. Ndaviti vamwe na ala waĩ namo maĩ "ta ũvai" wasũvĩaa aĩthi ma Navali na indo syoo. Me o ngalĩko ĩsu, Ndaviti nĩwesie kũtũma aũme kwa Navali etĩtye 'o kĩla kĩkoneka kw'okonĩ kwake' kya mbaa lĩu. (1 Sam. 25:8, 15, 16) Ndaviti aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩtya ũtethyo kwa Navali wasũanĩa ũndũ we vamwe na andũ make masũvĩĩte malĩ ya Navali.
Ĩndĩ Navali eekie kwosana na ĩsyĩtwa yake, yĩla ũalyũlo wayo nĩ "Mũndũ Mũtumanu" kana "Ndia." Asũngĩie Ndaviti na ngũlũ na alea kũmũtethya. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Ndaviti wathatie na avanga kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya nũndũ wa kĩko kĩu kya ũtumanu Navali weekie. Navali na mũsyĩ wake mayaĩ malea kwona naĩ nũndũ wa ũtumanu wake.—1 Sam. 25:2-13, 21, 22.
Ĩla Avikaili wamanyie kĩla kyeteelye mũsyĩ wake, nĩweenengie vinya na oosa ĩtambya. Nĩwaendie vala ve Ndaviti enyivĩtye mũno amwĩsũva asũanĩe ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova. Nĩwasyokie anenga Ndaviti, ũla nĩwe waĩ atw'ĩke mũsumbĩ ĩtina wa Saulo, lĩu ũmũtoetye vamwe na andũ make. Ndaviti nĩweetĩkĩlile kana Yeova nĩwatũmĩa mũndũ mũka ũsu kũmũsiĩĩa ndakeke ũndũ waĩ ũtonya kũtuma amũvĩtĩsya Ngai. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Ndaviti wamwĩie: "Ũathimwe ũmanyi waku, na ĩthĩwa wĩ mũathime we, ũla ũnziĩĩie ũmũnthĩ ndikethĩwe na ĩvĩtyo ya kwĩtĩkya nthakame."—1 Sam. 25:18, 19, 23-35.
Ũndũ ũmwe wĩ ũtheinĩ tũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩ kana tũyaĩle kũtutya Navali, ũla ũtaaonany'a kana nũkũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa ũseo ũla weekĩtwe. Ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata tũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩ kana tũkesa kwona ta ve ũndũ mũthũku ũkilyĩ kwĩkĩka, nũseo tũkosa ĩtambya tũũsiĩĩe. Tweeka ũu tũkeethĩawa tũyonany'a twĩ na woni ta wa mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli, ũla waisye atĩĩ: "Manyĩsya nyie kwonaa katĩ o na ũmanyi."—Sav. 119:66.
Angĩ no mone ĩla twatũmĩa ũĩ kana kĩlĩko nesa tũyĩka maũndũ. Methĩwe nĩmeũkũtavya na kanyw'a kana maiũtavya, ngoonĩ yoo no methĩwe mayasya o ta Ndaviti: "Ũathimwe ũmanyi waku."

translation:
When David heard about Nabal, a man from the house of Caleb, and about his wife, he sent ten young men to Nabal and said, "This is what David says: 'Peace be to you, and peace to your household, and peace to everything you have.' But Nabal replied rudely to David's messengers, saying, 'Who is David? Who is Jesse's son? There are many rebellious people today who are breaking away from their masters.' So David's men turned back and did not greet Nabal.
David and all his men went to Nabal to ask him for provisions. Nabal had a servant named Abigail, who was very intelligent and beautiful. She told her husband about David's messengers and said, 'David is coming to us asking for food for himself and his men, who have been kind to us. He has never insulted us at any time. But now, Nabal has acted foolishly. Let me go and meet David so I can appease him.' Then she quickly prepared two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, twenty sheep, and a fourth of an ephah of raisins and figs. She loaded them on donkeys and sent them ahead of her servants, saying, 'I will go behind you.' (1 Samuel 25:8, 15, 16) David had been protecting Nabal's flocks and had not stolen anything from him, even though Nabal was a harsh and unpleasant man.
Abigail approached David and greeted him humbly. She said, 'My lord, please forgive my husband's rude behavior. He is a foolish man, but I did not know about this until just now.' David replied to Abigail, 'Praise be to the Lord, the God of Israel, who has sent you to meet me! May you be blessed, and may you remember my kindness.' Abigail then gave him the bread, wine, sheep, and raisins and figs. She said, 'Please accept these gifts for your men.' David said to Abigail, 'May the Lord bless you for bringing me this gift. May your wisdom be known throughout the land!'—1 Samuel 25:2-13, 21, 22.
Abigail also informed her husband about everything that had happened and warned him about the trouble he was in. Nabal listened to her and realized how foolish he had been. The next day, Nabal sent messengers to David with gifts and apologized for his rude behavior. David thanked Abigail for her wisdom and praised God for sending her to prevent him from taking revenge. He said, 'The Lord, the God of Israel, has blessed you for preventing me from shedding blood needlessly.'—1 Samuel 25:18, 19, 23-35.
This experience teaches us that we should always be humble and respectful, even when dealing with difficult people. It also reminds us that we should always seek wisdom and understanding. Let us learn from the example of the psalmist who wrote, 'Teach me good judgment and knowledge.'—Psalm 119:66.
So let us pray that God will give us wisdom and discernment so that we can make right decisions. May we always remember the words of Abigail to David: 'Please accept my gift.'

text:
"Anyanya ala aseo vyũ ĩndĩ matalea kũũthatya"
Andũ ala mũsyaanĩw'e mawetawa ta mo "anyanya ala aseo vyũ, ĩndĩ matalea kũũthatya." Nũmendete, o namo nĩmakwendete, ĩndĩ mavinda amwe ũyĩthĩa nĩ vinya kũmĩanĩsya namo. Helena, ũla wĩ na ũkũũ wa myaka 18, aĩtye atĩĩ, "Mũinawa atindĩaa kũnthatya. Nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũmbĩa kana ũndũ ũtonya kũmbĩka nĩ kana nĩthate."
Mathĩna amwe ma andũ masyaanĩw'e nĩmatonya kũminwa kwa kũea ngewa nesa, na kwĩthukĩanĩsya. Kwa ngelekany'o:
Anake elĩ masyaanĩw'e mekalaa lumunĩ ĩmwe no maemanwe nũndũ wa mũndũ kũlikĩĩla maũndũ ma ũla ũngĩ. Maĩle kwĩka ata? Maĩle kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩthukĩanĩsya na mainengane mwanya ũla kĩla ũmwe ũkwenda. Maĩle kũtũmĩa mwolooto wa Mbivilia ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Luka 6:
Nĩvatonyeka eĩtu elĩ masyaanĩw'e makethĩwa kĩla ũmwe osaa ngũa sya ũla ũngĩ atetĩtye. Maĩle kwĩka ata? Maĩle kũneenea ũndũ ũsu na mayĩkĩanĩa mĩvaka ĩũlũ wa kũtũmĩanĩa syĩndũ. Nĩmaĩle kũtũmĩa mwolooto ũla wĩ nthĩnĩ wa 2 Timotheo 2:
Mathĩna amwe katĩ wa andũ masyaanĩw'e methĩawa me maito, na nĩmatonya kumĩlya maũndũ mathũku. Kwoona ngelekany'o ilĩ syĩ Mbivilianĩ:
Miliamu na Aluni nĩmeew'ĩaa kĩwĩu mwana-a-inyia woo, Mose, na ũu nĩwamaeteie mũisyo mũnene. Soma ngewa ĩsu ĩandĩkonĩ ya Motalo 12:
1- 15. Ĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Ndonya kwĩka ata ndĩkew'ĩe kĩwĩu ala tũsyaanĩw'e?'
Kaini nĩwaekie ũthilĩku wake waingĩva, na ũu watuma esa kũmũaa mwana-a-inyia Aveli. Soma ngewa ĩsu nthĩnĩ wa Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:
1- 12. Ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Ndonya kwĩka ata ngasiĩĩa ũthilĩku wakwa ĩla navĩtĩw'a nĩ ala tũsyaanĩw'e?'
Itumi ilĩ sya kũtũngĩĩa mũuo
O na ethĩwa wĩĩw'a ve vinya ata kũmĩanĩsya na ala mũsyaanĩw'e, ve itumi ilĩ nzeo sya kũtata kwĩka ũu.
Nĩ kwonany'a kana nũendeee kũima. Mwanake ũmwe wĩtawa Alex aĩtye ũũ: "Navu ĩtina eĩtu elĩ ainawa matindĩaa kũnthatya. Ĩndĩ yu ndithataa mĩtũkĩ, na nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye kũmomĩĩsya. No wasye nĩnaimie."
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũla mũmĩĩsya wa kũthata nĩ wa ũmanyi mwingĩ; ĩndĩ ũla wĩ mĩtũkĩ vevanĩ nũnenevasya ũtumanu."
—Nthimo 14:29.
Nĩkũũtetheeasya kũmanya ũndũ ũkekalany'a na andũ ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ethĩwa ndũtonya kũmĩanĩsya na ala mũsyaanĩw'e, ũkatonya kwĩkalany'a ata na ũla wĩtwaana nake, ala mũkathũkũma ĩmwe, ũla ũkakũandĩka, kana o andũ angĩ?
Ũw'o wa maũndũ: Nĩ kana wĩĩkalany'a na andũ nesa ĩvinda yũkĩte, no nginya wĩmanyĩsye kwĩthukĩanĩsya na andũ na kũeleanwa namo, na vai vandũ vangĩ ũtonya kwĩmanyĩĩsya maũndũ asu eka o mũsyĩ kwenyu.
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Kwa ngalĩ ĩla yenyu, ĩthĩwai na mũuo.'
—Alomi 12:18.
We no wende ũtethyo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũtonya kũtũngĩĩa mũuo wĩ na mwĩĩtu kana mwanake mũsyaanĩw'e? Soma kĩlungu kĩĩ, "Kĩla andũ angĩ ma mũika maasya," na ĩndĩ ũisisya ĩthangũ yĩ na makũlyo ma kusũsya yĩla yĩ na kyongo, "Kwĩkalany'a Nesa na Ala Mũsyaanĩw'e."

"Anyone who has nothing should sell what he has and buy a sword."
People who have been shown mercy through the message say like this: "Anyone who has nothing should sell what he has and buy a sword." Truly, I tell you, I came to bring division, not peace. Helena, a girl of 18 years old, said, "My father taught me to hate. It is better to die doing something than to die doing nothing."
Some people who have been shown mercy can be tempted to seek revenge, and to retaliate. For example:
Someone who has been shown mercy might think about harming someone who wronged him. Should we do that? Should we try to retaliate and avenge ourselves on those who hurt us each time? Should we use the story from the Bible found in Luke 6:
31.
Do not ask for anything back from anyone who takes away from you; and from anyone who wants to borrow from you, do not demand it back. Should we do that? Should we understand this thing and practice forgiveness instead of seeking vengeance? Should we use the story which is written in 2 Timothy 2:
24.
Some of those who have been shown mercy are weak, and they can easily fall into sin. See an example from the Bible:
Miriam and Aaron spoke against their brother Moses, and this caused great trouble. Read this story which is written in Numbers 12:
1-15. It says: 'Should we ask why we were shown mercy?'
Cain became very angry with his brother, and this led him to kill his brother Abel. Read this story in Genesis 4:
1-12. It also says, 'Should we ask whether our anger is justified when it leads us to harm others?'
The reason for forgiving others
Even though it is difficult to forgive those who have harmed us, there is a good reason to do so.
I wonder if I should continue speaking. One young man named Alex said this: "I had a dream where my father taught me to hate. I hated many things, and I learned to despise them. But then I woke up."
The Bible says: "A person slow to anger is better than someone strong, and controlling one's temper is evidence of intelligence."
—Proverbs 14:29.
It is helpful to understand how others feel. Sometimes it is hard to get along with others, even with family members, but you may be able to find common ground with them, or perhaps with others?
The importance of relationships: If you try to get along with others, you will learn to cooperate with people and become more understanding, and many people will be willing to teach you new things or share their experiences.
The Bible says: 'Live in peace with everyone.'
—Romans 12:18.
So, what can you do to improve your relationship with someone or a friend who has wronged you? Read the following, "Be kind to everyone," and remember the advice given in the song, "Get Along With Others."

text:
1. Ngai nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya syonthe?
Ngai athoketye andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe mamũthengee mboyanĩ. (Savuli 65:2) Ĩndĩ, ndethukĩĩasya kana kwĩtĩkĩla mboya syonthe. Kwa ngelekany'o, mboya sya mũndũ ũla ũthĩnasya kĩveti kyake no isiĩĩwe. (1 Vetelo 3:7) Ĩngĩ, ĩla Aisilaeli maendeeie kwĩka naĩ, Ngai ndaaĩthukĩĩsya mboya syoo. Vate nzika, mboya nĩ ũndũ wa mwanya. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Ngai nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa mboya sya andũ mekĩte naĩ ngito ethĩwa nĩmeelila.
2. Twaĩle kũvoya ata?
Mboya nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũthaitha, kwoou twaĩle kũmũvoya Mũmbi witũ, Yeova, e weka. (Mathayo 4:10; 6:9) Ĩngĩ, tũi eanĩu, kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũvoya kwĩsĩla syĩtwanĩ ya Yesũ nũndũ akwie kwondũ wa naĩ sitũ. (Yoana 14:6) Yeova ndendaa tũtindĩe kũtũngĩlĩĩla ndeto o imwe ĩla tũũvoya, kana kũsoma mboya mbandĩke. Endaa tũvoye kuma ngoonĩ sitũ.
Mũmbi witũ no atwĩw'e o na twavoya tũvindĩtye. (1 Samueli 1:12, 13) Atũthoketye tũvoyae kĩla ĩvinda. Kwa ngelekany'o, no tũvoye kwakya, wĩoo, mbee wa kũya, na ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ.
3. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto mombanaa vamwe?
Kũmũthengeea Ngai nĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya nũndũ tũtwĩe katĩ wa andũ matamũĩkĩĩa Ngai na mavũthasya watho wake wa kũete mũuo kũũ nthĩ. (2 Timotheo 3:1, 4; 2 Vetelo 3:3, 13) Kwoou, twĩ na vata wa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo na athaithi ala angĩ nĩ kana twĩkĩane vinya.
Kwĩthĩwa twĩ ngwatanĩo na andũ mamwendete Ngai nĩkũtũtetheeasya kũmũthengeea Ngai. Mawũmbano ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova matũnengae myanya mĩseo ya kwĩkĩwa vinya nĩ mũĩkĩĩo wa ala angĩ.
4. Ũtonya kũmũthengeea Ngai ata?
Ũtonya kũmũthengeea Yeova kwa kũsũanĩĩa maũndũ ala weemanyĩsya kuma Ndetonĩ yake. Sũanĩa kĩla ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩsĩla mawĩa make, ũtao wake, na mawatho make. Mboya na kũsũanĩĩa maũndũ kũtũtetheeasya kũelewa kana Ngai e wendo na ũĩ mwingĩ.
Ũndũ ũla ũtonya kũtuma ũmũthengeea Ngai no kũmwĩkwatya, kana kũmũĩkĩĩa. Mũĩkĩĩo nĩ ta kĩndũ kĩ thayũ kĩla kyaĩle kũĩthw'a. No nginya ũendee kũĩthya mũĩkĩĩo waku kwa kũsũanĩĩa kĩla kĩtumĩte wĩthwa na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu.
5. Kũmũthengeea Ngai kũkaũtethya ata?
Yeova nũthĩnĩkĩaa ala mamwendete. No amasũvĩe maikakwatwe nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũlikya mũĩkĩĩo woo na wĩkwatyo woo wa thayũ ũtathela mũisyonĩ. (Savuli 91:1, 2, 7-10) Nũtũkanasya tũikaatĩĩe nzĩa itonya kũmina ũtanu na kwananga ũima witũ wa mwĩĩ. Yeova atũmanyĩasya nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ ya thayũ.

translation:
1. Will God answer all our prayers?
God answers the prayers of righteous people who earnestly seek him. (Psalm 65:2) Therefore, I will continue to pray and never give up. For example, a husband's prayer may be hindered if he mistreats his wife. (1 Peter 3:7) However, when ancient Israel turned away from God, He still answered their prayers. In fact, prayer is a privilege. And even now, God hears the prayers of those who approach Him with faith and sincerity.
2. Should we ever stop praying?
Prayer is one way to worship, so should we ever stop praying to our Creator, Jehovah? (Matthew 4:10; 6:9) Also, we want to please Him, so we should never stop praying according to His will. (John 14:6) Jehovah wants us to keep asking Him for what we need, or to read about Bible accounts of prayer. Let us keep praying regularly.
Our Creator cares about us and listens to our prayers. (1 Samuel 1:12, 13) He encourages us to pray constantly. For instance, we can pray when we wake up, before meals, and when we feel troubled.
3. Is Christ's company desirable?
Serving God is a joy when we associate with others who love God and uphold his standards of conduct. (2 Timothy 3:1, 4; 2 Peter 3:3, 13) So, we benefit from being around faithful brothers and sisters who encourage us spiritually.
Associating with those who serve God helps us to enjoy serving Him. The meetings at Kingdom Halls provide opportunities to find such encouragement.
4. How can you improve your service to God?
You can improve your service to Jehovah by appreciating the things He reveals in His Word. Study each opportunity to learn more about His personality, purpose, and ways. Prayer and studying help us to understand how much God loves us.
The more you learn, the more you will love and appreciate God. Appreciation is a powerful motive that keeps us going. So, strive to cultivate appreciation for everything that Jehovah does and for all the privileges you have.
5. Does serving God bring benefits?
Jehovah cares for those who serve Him. And the blessings we receive are reasons to strengthen our faith and loyalty. (Psalm 91:1, 2, 7-10) We can be confident that we can face trials and maintain our integrity. Jehovah shows us what we need to do to remain courageous.

text:
1. Ũthũku wambĩĩie ata?
Ũthũku wambĩĩie ĩla Satani wakenganie. Mwambĩlĩlyonĩ Satani aĩ mũlaĩka mwĩanĩu, ĩndĩ "ndaaĩkala nthĩnĩ wa w'o." (Yoana 8:44) Nĩweethĩiwe na mea ma kwenda kũthaithwa o na kau Ngai e weka no we waĩle kũthaithwa. Satani akengie mũndũ mũka wa mbee, Eva, na amũsesenga amwĩw'e vandũ va kũmwĩw'a Ngai. Atamu aatĩĩie Eva nthĩnĩ wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai. Ũtwi wa Atamu watumie kwĩthĩwa na mathĩna na kĩkw'ũ.
Ĩla Satani weeie Eva ndakamwĩw'e Ngai, ambĩlĩilye ũlei kwelekela ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai, ayonany'a kana Ngai ti we waĩle kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩ Mũnene Vyũ. O ta Satani, andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmamũleete Ngai kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩ woo. Kwoou, Satani atw'ĩkĩte "mũnene wa nthĩ."
2. W'o wũmbi wa Ngai waĩ na mavĩtyo?
Wĩa w'onthe wa Ngai nĩ mwĩanĩu. Andũ na alaĩka ala Ngai woombie maĩ matonya kũmwĩw'a Ngai kwa wĩanĩu. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 32:4, 5) Ngai atũmbie twĩ na ũthasyo wa kũnyuva kwĩka ũseo kana ũthũku. Ũthasyo ũsu ũtũnengae mwanya wa kwonany'a wendo witũ kwa Ngai.
3. Nĩkĩ Ngai ũekete mathĩna maendee nginya ũmũnthĩ?
Kwa kavinda, Yeova nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũlei kwelekela ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. Nĩkĩ? Nĩ kana onany'e ũsumbĩki o na wĩva ũtaumĩte kwake ndũtonya kũuna andũ. (Mũtavan'ya 7:29; 8:9) Ũndũ ũsu nĩwonekete nesa nthĩnĩ wa myaka 6,000 mĩvĩtu. Asumbĩki ma andũ nĩmaemetwe nĩ kũmina kaũ, ũtũli wa mĩao, ũsili ũte wa katĩ, kana mowau.
Kĩvathũkany'o na ũsumbĩki wa andũ, ũsumbĩki wa Ngai nũmaunaa ala mawĩtĩkĩlaa. (Isaia 48:17, 18) O mĩtũkĩ, Yeova akaananga silikalĩ syonthe sya andũ. Ala manyuvĩte kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Ngai no mo makekala kũũ nthĩ.—Isaia 11:9.
4. Wũmĩĩsyo wa Ngai ũtũnengete mwanya wa kwĩka ata?
Satani aisye vaiĩ mũndũ o na ũmwe ũtonya kũmũthũkũma Yeova nũndũ nũmwendete. No wende kwonany'a kana ũsu nĩ ũneeni wa ũvũngũ? No wĩke ũu! Wũmĩĩsyo wa Ngai ũtũnengae mwanya wa kwonany'a kana twĩenda kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Ngai kana nĩ mũndũ. Mwĩkalo witũ nĩw'o wonanasya kĩla tũnyuvĩte.
5. Tũtonya kũmũnyuva Ngai ata ethĩwe Mũsumbĩ witũ?
No tũmũnyuve Ngai ethĩwe Mũsumbĩ witũ kwa kũmantha na kũatĩĩa ũthaithi wa w'o kwosana na Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia. (Yoana 4:23) No tũlee kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Satani kwa kwĩvathana na siasa na makaũ, o tondũ Yesũ weekie.
Satani atũmĩaa vinya wake kũtuma andũ mona imanyĩo nthũku syĩ nzeo. Ĩla twalea imanyĩo isu, anyanya na andũ amwe maitũ ma mũsyĩ no matũthekee kana kũtũvĩnga. (1 Vetelo 4:3, 4) Kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũtw'a twĩĩka ata. Tũkeethwa twĩ ngwatanĩo na ala mamwendete Ngai? Tũkaatĩĩaa mĩao yake ya ũĩ na wendo? Tweeka ũu, tũkoonany'a kana Satani nĩwakenganie ĩla waisye kana vaiĩ mũndũ ũmwĩw'a Ngai ethĩwa kwĩka ũu kũkamũetee thĩna.
Wendo wa Ngai kwa andũ ũtũĩkĩĩthasya kana akavetanga ũthũku na mathĩna. Andũ ala monanasya nĩmaĩkĩĩte ũndũ ũsu makatanĩa thayũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene.

translation:
1. Are you deceived at all?
You are deceived if Satan misleads you. Satan is a liar and the father of lies, according to "I do not live truthfully with you." (John 8:44) Be convinced by his works of going astray and he is like God who wants you to go astray. Satan misled a perfect man, Eve, and made him disobey God's commandments. He told Eve to disregard obedience to God. The sin of Adam caused suffering and death.
But Satan made Eve believe she was against God, leading her to reject the great kindness of God, questioning whether God truly wanted them to suffer in the Great Kindness. Because of Satan, many people today still mislead God to suffer in His Kindness. Truly, Satan has become "the master of deceit."
2. Why does God allow wickedness?
God's name is holy. People and angels who love God hate wickedness because of their holiness. (Revelation 15:4, 5) God allows us to have freedom of choice, so we can choose good or bad. This freedom gives us an opportunity to show our love for God.
3. Why did God create humans knowing they would sin?
For example, Jehovah showed his great kindness. Why? Because he sees that his kingdom and living among humans will prove his sovereignty. (Proverbs 7:29; 8:9) This matter has been evident for about 6,000 years. Human governments have failed due to corruption, war, poverty, or injustice.
Compared to human governments, God's government is always fair. (Isaiah 48:17, 18) Soon, Jehovah will end all human governments. All those who desire to be ruled by God and live peacefully will survive.—Isaiah 11:9.
4. How does God's justice give us hope?
Satan tries to deceive everyone, making them think they cannot trust Jehovah because he allows suffering. But ask yourself, is this really true? Don't be fooled! God's justice gives us an opportunity to see whether we want to be ruled by God or by humans. Our decision shows what we value.
5. Can we please God despite our imperfections?
We can please God despite our imperfections by learning and applying the truth found in his Word, the Bible. (John 4:23) We avoid being misled by Satan by rejecting false teachings and superstitions, just as Jesus did.
Satan uses lies to mislead people into thinking things that are completely untrue. However, if we learn the truth and discuss it with others, we can strengthen ourselves and help others. (1 Peter 4:3, 4) What can we do to stay firm? Should we associate only with those who love God? Should we imitate their faith and loving-kindness? By doing so, we show that we recognize Satan's deception and that we want to remain loyal to God.
God's love for mankind moves him to forgive mistakes and sins. Those who appreciate this often experience joy again and again.

Ũelesyo wa Ĩvuku Yĩĩ
Ũvoo Mũseo o tondũ ũandĩkĩtwe nĩ Mathayo wĩtavany'a ũvoo kana Yesũ nĩwe Mũtangĩĩi ũla wathanĩtwe, na ũla kwĩsĩla kwake Ngai weanĩisye watho ũla wamathie andũ make nthĩnĩ wa Ũtianĩo Mũkũũ. Ũvoo ũũ Mũseo ndũandĩkĩwe mbaĩ ya Ayuti yĩ yoka, vala nĩvo Yesũ wasyaĩiwe na eanĩa, ĩndĩ ũandĩkĩtwe kwondũ wa andũ ma nthĩ yonthe.
Ĩvuku yĩĩ ya Mathayo yĩandĩkĩtwe yĩatĩanĩw'e nesa. Yambĩlĩĩlye na kũsyawa kwa Yesũ, na yĩkaelesya kũvatiswa na kũtatwa kwake. Kuma vau nĩyĩeleetye wĩa wake wa kũtavany'a, kũmanyĩsya, na kũvosya awau andũnĩ ma Kalilii. Ĩtina wa ũu, ĩvuku yĩĩ nĩyĩwetete ĩũlũ wa kyalo kya Yesũ kya kuma Kalilii na kũthi Yelũsalemu, na maũndũ ala meekĩkie kyumwanĩ kyake kya mũthya kũũ nthĩ. Yĩminũkĩlĩĩlye na kwambwa kwa Yesũ ngelany'onĩ na kũthayũũka kwake.
Ĩvuku yĩĩ yonanĩtye Yesũ ta we mũmanyĩsya ũla mũnene wĩ na ũkũmũ wa kũelesya Mĩao ya Ngai, na ũmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Maũndũ maingĩ ala ũmanyĩĩtye nĩmatũngĩanĩwe kũndũ kũtano: (1) Ũtavany'a wake Kĩĩmanĩ, naw'o nĩ ĩũlũ wa mwĩkalo wa andũ ala ma ũsumbĩ wa ĩtunĩ, mawĩa moo, ĩtuvi yoo na vala melekele (Kĩlungu 5-7). (2) Ũmanyĩsyo wa Yesũ kwa amanyĩw'a make ĩkũmi na elĩ ĩũlũ wa ũthũkũmi woo (Kĩlungu 10). (3) Ngelekany'o syake ĩũlũ wa ũsumbĩ wa ĩtu (Kĩlungu 13). (4) Ũmanyĩsyo ĩũlũ wa mwĩkalo ũla waĩlĩte mũatĩĩi wa Yesũ Klĩsto (Kĩlungu 18). (5) Ũmanyĩsyo ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ na kũka kwa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai (Kĩlungu 24 na 25).
Maũndũ ala me Ĩvukunĩ Yĩĩ
Aaũmae ma Yesũ Klĩsto na kũsyawa kwake 1.1—2.23
Ũthũkũmi wa Yoana Mũvatisi 3.1-12
Kũvatiswa kwa Yesũ na kũtatwa kwake 3.13—4.11
Ũthũkũmi wa Yesũ andũnĩ ma Kalilii 4.12—18.35
Yesũ ayuma Kalilii na kũthi Yelũsalemu 19.1—20.34
Yesũ e vakuvĩ na Yelũsalemu na e nthĩnĩ wayo kyumwanĩ kyake kya mũthya e kũũ nthĩ 21.1—27.66
Kũthayũũka kwa Mwĩai na kũmaumĩlĩĩla amanyĩw'a make 28.1-20

translation:
The Account of Matthew
This book, written by Matthew, who did not witness the events themselves, recounts Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, who fulfilled the prophecies spoken by the prophets of the Old Testament. This account was written in the year forty-three, so that people everywhere would know about Jesus' life, death, and resurrection.
Matthew's first book is written concisely. It begins with the genealogy of Jesus and ends with his ascension and return. Its purpose is to demonstrate his claim to be the Messiah, to convince, and to teach the people of Galilee. In addition, this book tells the story of Jesus' journey from Galilee to Jerusalem, and the miracles he performed during his ministry. It concludes with his crucifixion and resurrection.
This book testifies to Jesus as the great teacher and the fulfillment of the law and the prophets, and reveals the kingdom of God. Many other things it teaches can be divided into five main sections: (1) His Sermon on the Mount, which includes teachings about humility, anger, adultery, oaths, and retaliation (Chapters 5-7). (2) Jesus' sending out of his twelve disciples (Chapter 10). (3) His parables about the kingdom of heaven (Chapter 13). (4) His teaching about the importance of serving others and following Christ (Chapter 18). (5) His teaching about watchfulness and the coming of the kingdom of God (Chapters 24 and 25).
Other Matters in the First Book
The birth of Jesus Christ and his ancestry 1.1—2.23
John the Baptist prepares the way 3.1-12
The baptism and temptation of Jesus 3.13—4.11
Jesus ministers to the Galileans 4.12—18.35
Jesus goes to Jerusalem 19.1—20.34
Jesus suffers in Jerusalem and dies on the cross 21.1—27.66
The resurrection of Jesus and his commissioning of his disciples 28.1-20

text:
MWOOLOTO WA MBIVILIA: "Mũikemakĩe ũndũ wa mathayũ menyu."—Mathayo 6:25.
Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Yesũ aneenie ndeto isu e ũla Ũtavany'anĩ wa Kĩĩmanĩ. Kwosana na ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩeleasya ndeto sya Mbivilia, ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "kwĩmakĩa" yonanasya "thĩna wa ngoo ũla ũkwataa mũndũ eethĩwa e ngya, e na nzaa na akwatwa nĩ mathĩna angĩ ma kĩla mũthenya." Kwĩmakĩa mavinda maingĩ kũetawe nĩ mũndũ kũthĩnĩkĩa mũno maũndũ matonya kwĩsa kwĩkĩka ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ti ũthũku mũndũ kũthĩnĩkĩa ũndũ ũkwĩanĩsya mavata make ma kĩ-mwĩĩ na ma andũ make. (Avilivi 2:20) Ĩndĩ ĩla Yesũ waisye "mũikemakĩe," anengae amanyĩw'a make ũtao wa kana mayaĩlĩte kwĩmakĩa kũvĩtũka kĩasi, nũndũ ĩla mũndũ weemakĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte ethĩawa ate na ũtanu.—Mathayo 6:31, 34.
Ũtao ũsu no ũtũmĩke ũmũnthĩ? Nĩ ũndũ mũseo kũatĩĩa ũtao ũsu wa Yesũ. Nĩkĩ? Mavuku amwe ma kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli monanasya kana ĩla mũndũ weemakĩa mũno, ve kĩlungu kĩna kya mwĩĩ (sympathetic nervous system) kyambĩĩaa kũthũkũma kĩte kũthũmũa na ũu "nũtumaa andũ makwatwa nĩ mowau ta itau sya nda, ũwau wa ngoo, na asthma."
Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana vai vata wa kwĩmakĩa nũndũ kwĩmakĩa kũyĩsa kũtethya mũndũ. Akũlilye atĩĩ: "Nũũ kwenyu ũla ũtonya kwondũ wa kwĩmakĩa kwake kwĩyongeleela ũasa wake mũkono ũmwe?" (Mathayo 6:27) Kwĩmakĩa kũyĩsa kwongela kĩndũ o na kĩmwe thayũnĩ witũ. O na mavinda maingĩ maũndũ mekĩkaa kĩvathũkany'o na ũndũ tũũsũanĩaa. Mũsomi ũmwe aielesya ũndũ ũsu aisye atĩĩ: "Kwĩmakĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte nĩ kwananga saa na mavinda maingĩ maũndũ methĩawa mate mathũku ũndũ tũnasũanĩaa."
Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũeke kwĩmakĩa? Ũndũ wa mbee nĩ kũmwĩkwatya Ngai. Ethĩwa Ngai nũmanthĩaa nyũnyi lĩu na akavw'ĩka malaa, no aemwe nĩ kwĩanĩsya mavata ma andũ ala monaa kũmũthaitha kwĩ kwa vata thayũnĩ woo? (Mathayo 6:25, 26, 28-30) Ũndũ wa kelĩ, ndũkathĩnĩke nũndũ wa ũnĩ. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Mũikemakĩe ĩndĩ ũndũ wa ũnĩ; nũndũ ũnĩ ũkeemakĩa e w'o." We tyo wĩtĩkĩle kana kĩla "mũthenya nĩwĩanĩwe nĩ ũthũku waw'o"?—Mathayo 6:34.
Twaatĩĩa ũtao ũsu wa Yesũ, tũkeesianĩa na mathĩna ala matonya kũtũũmĩsya. O na ĩngĩ tũkeethĩwa na mũuo wa ngoo ũla Mbivilia ĩwĩtĩte "mũuo wa Ngai."—Avilivi 4:6, 7.

translation:
THE WORRY OF LIFE: "Do not be anxious about your life."—Matthew 6:25.
This scripture helps us understand what? Jesus gave this counsel during his Sermon on the Mount. Just as a bird looks for food, the Bible's Greek word translated "to worry" literally means "to be pulled in different directions, being distracted by many concerns." Worrying about too many things can prevent a person from focusing on what is truly important. It is unwise for a person to become preoccupied with material possessions and worldly affairs. (Proverbs 2:20) When Jesus said "Do not worry," he was encouraging his followers to avoid becoming overly concerned about basic necessities, realizing that someone who worries is often neglecting spiritual matters.—Matthew 6:31, 34.
How can we apply this advice? By making a conscious effort to follow Jesus' example. Why? Because studies show that when a person worries, the sympathetic nervous system activates, causing physical reactions such as increased heart rate, rapid breathing, and even triggering conditions like allergies, anxiety, and asthma.
Jesus pointed out that excessive worrying demonstrates a lack of faith. He asked: "Who of you by worrying can add one cubit to his height?" (Matthew 6:27) Worrying does not solve problems; it only adds stress. And many times, our anxieties involve things beyond our control. One researcher explained: "Chronic worry is like spending hours each day preparing for possible disasters that may never happen."
So how can we stop worrying? The key is to trust God. By praying to God regularly and confiding in him, we can also benefit from knowing that he cares about others and will help them during difficult times, won't we?—Matthew 6:25, 26, 28-30. Furthermore, focus on what is important. Jesus said: "Do not be anxious about your life, as to what you will eat or what you will drink; . . . For your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things." But don't you think that means 'don't make any preparations'?—Matthew 6:34.
By following Jesus' example, we can learn to cope with concerns and avoid letting everyday matters overwhelm us. Also, remember that God's spirit, which the Bible calls "God's force," can empower us.—Proverbs 4:6, 7.

Yo ve syĩndũ sya tene syenziwe iĩkĩĩthasya maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ nĩ ma w'o? Mwakanĩ wa 2014, ve ũvoo waĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Biblical Archaeology Review, wakũlĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩ andũ meana me Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania maĩkĩĩthĩtw'e kana maĩ vo kwĩsĩla syĩndũ ila syĩnzawa nthĩ?" Ũsũngĩo woonanisye kana andũ asu "nĩ ta 50!" Ĩndĩ ve mũndũũme ũmwe ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ ũtaĩ ũtalonĩ ũsu, nake nĩ Tatenai. Tatenai aĩ ũũ? Ekai twone maũndũ manini mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ ĩũlũ wake.
Ve ĩvinda Yelusaleme yaĩ ungu wa Ũsumbĩki wa Velisia. Yelusaleme yaĩ kĩsionĩ kĩmwe kĩla andũ ma Velisia makĩtaa Mũingo wa Ũsĩ, kĩla kyaĩ ngalĩko ya ũthũĩlonĩ wa sua ya Euvalati. Ĩtina wa kũsinda Mbaviloni, Velisia nĩyamathaisye Ayuti kuma ũkombonĩ na yametĩkĩlya makatũngĩĩe ĩkalũ ya Yeova yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme. (Esala 1:
Ve masengea maseũvĩtw'e na yũmba (cuneiform tablets) mataanangĩka maandĩkĩtwe ĩsyĩtwa ya Tatenai. Nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa me amwe katĩ wa syĩndũ sya tene ila syaiĩtwe nĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Tatenai. Ĩsengea yĩmwe yonanĩtye kana mũndũ ũmwe wa mũsyĩ ũsu nĩ ũla Tatenai ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Ĩsengea yĩu yĩ na wĩw'ano wa viasala weekiwe mwaka wa 502 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, naw'o waĩ mwaka wa 20 wa kũsumbĩka kwa Ndalio wa 1. Ĩsengea yĩu yonanĩtye kana ngũsĩ ĩla yaĩkĩĩthisye wĩw'ano ũsu yaĩ mũthũkũmi wa "Tattannu, ngavana wa kĩsio kĩla kĩ Mũingo wa Ũsĩ." Ũsu nĩwe Tatenai ũla ũwetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Mbivilia ya Esala.
Tatenai atethasya wĩa mwaũ? Mwakanĩ wa 535 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, Mũsumbĩ Kulusi nĩwavangie isio ila wasumbĩkĩte iaanw'e syĩthĩwe ilungu nene sya nthĩ, na kĩmwe kya isio isu waanisye kyeetawa Mbaviloni na Mũingo wa Ũsĩ. Kĩsio kĩu nĩkyesie kũaanw'a kelĩ, na ngalĩko ĩmwe yeetwa Mũingo wa Ũsĩ. Nthĩ ila syaĩ ungu wa kĩsio kĩu kya Mũingo wa Ũsĩ syaĩ Coele-Syria, Voenike, Samalia, na Yuta, na nĩvatonyeka ikethĩwa syasumbĩkĩtwe kuma Ndamasiku. Tatenai nĩwe waĩ ngavana wa kĩsio kĩu vakuvĩ mwakanĩ wa 520 nginya 502 Klĩsto ate mũsyae.
Ĩla Tatenai waendie Yelusaleme kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli amanye kana kwa w'o Ayuti nĩmaleanĩte na ũsumbĩki wa Velisia, nĩwaeleisye mũsumbĩ Ndalio kana Ayuti measya nĩmanengiwe mwanya wa kũtũngĩĩa ĩkalũ ya Yeova nĩ Kulusi. Ĩla ũkunĩkĩli weekiwe mavukunĩ ma tene ala maĩ nyũmbanĩ ya kĩũsumbĩ, ndeto sya Ayuti syeethĩiwe syĩ sya w'o. (Esala 5:
Ũw'o nĩ kana "Tatenai, ngavana wa mũingo wa ũla Ũsĩ" ndaaĩka maũndũ manene. Ĩndĩ manya kana nũwetetwe Maandĩkonĩ na etĩtwe o ĩsyĩtwa ya ũnene yĩla weetawa. Ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a kana syĩndũ sya tene ila syĩnzawa nthĩ niĩkĩĩthasya kana maũndũ ala Mbivilia ĩeleetye meekĩkie ĩvindanĩ ya tene nĩ ma w'o.

translation:
I ask myself, why were ten things done like this, and why were they recorded about Mbiviliani? In 2014, in an article in Biblical Archaeology Review, they stated: "Are the biblical accounts of the conquest reliable, or are they just legends?" The answer was that there were "about 50!" And there was one person named Mbiviliani who wasn't mentioned, namely Tatenai. Who was Tatenai? Let us look at some important people who were associated with Mbiviliani during his time.
Jerusalem was under the control of the Persian Empire. Jerusalem was a religious center for the Persians, where they worshipped their god, which was located near the province of Euphrates. After conquering Babylon, Persia allowed the Jews to return home and rebuild the temple of Jehovah, which was in Jerusalem. (Ezra 1:
Many inscriptions have been found on clay tablets (cuneiform tablets) mentioning Tatenai. It is possible to find some information about him among these things, but it is written by people from the family of Tatenai. One inscription states that someone from this family was Tatenai who was known as Mbiviliani. This inscription also mentions officials who served around 502 BC and later, even in the 20th year of the reign of Darius I. This inscription states that the official who oversaw them was called "Tattannu, governor of the region beyond the River." He is the Tatenai who is mentioned in the Ezra account of Mbivilia.
What happened to Tatenai then? In 535 BC, King Cyrus conquered the region but appointed governors over it, and one of those regions was named Babylon and Beyond the River. That region stretched far and wide, and another area was called Beyond the River. The lands of Beyond the River included Coele-Syria, Phoenicia, Samaria, and Judea, and they were subject to governors appointed by him. Tatenai was one of those governors from around 520 to 502 BC.
But Tatenai went to Jerusalem to inquire about certain matters, or perhaps he went to Egypt and conspired with the Persians, he informed Governor Darius or Egypt that the Jews had begun rebuilding the temple of Yahweh with Cyrus' permission. But the inquiry concerned the foundations of the temple, and the report from Egypt was unfavorable. (Ezra 5:
He is also known as "Tatenai, governor of Beyond the River" because of important matters. It is said that he was mentioned in the Scriptures and that his name was honored. This matter seems to be related to ten things, but it is difficult to understand what those things are, like the events in Babylonia which have been recorded in detail.

Uu ni kwianana na kaunti komishena wa kitui Mbungai Rioba kavindani kala watongoesya iseso ya kuvingua kwa ikumbi ya mutiani uuiseso ila kyatwaaiwa uvisini kwake musyini wa kitui vala waweta kana mutiani uu niwendeeye na kunyaaikwaa masukuluni kivathunio,aiweta kana vena maovisaa eanu ma kuthingiliila mouw'o masukulu kavindani kala mutiani usu ukwithiwa uendeeye.
Avungwa 15 na ala ni aume nimo mavikiia kwikalila mutiani woo wa KCPE mwaka uu Yielani inene ya kitui,musyini wa kitui
Uu nikwianana na ula ungamiye yiela ii Ibrahim Hassan

translation:
Interior Cabinet Secretary Dr Fred Matiang'i released police officers to thoroughly investigate the leakage of the Kenya Certificate of Primary Education exam papers across the country .
Matiang'i directed Regional Commander Kavindani to oversee the search for a container containing exam papers at Kithimani in Yatta sub-county , Machakos County , saying the investigation will involve both ministers and officials from the government who have been implicated in the leakage of exam papers . He added that he has ordered an investigation into how the exam papers were leaked so that those responsible can be arrested . He said anyone found leaking exam papers will be dealt with severely .
There are 35536 candidates in Makueni County who are sitting for the KCPE exam , and there are 12 examination centers .
Speaking to Makueni County Commissioner Gilbert Kitiyo , he said all measures have been taken to prevent the leakage of the exam papers . I have been informed that security has been beefed up in all parts of Makueni County to ensure the exam papers are safe .
Many irregularities regarding the administration of the KCPE exam in Kitui County have been reported , and some candidates have already been caught cheating during the exam .
This was revealed by Kitui County Commissioner Mbungai Rioba , who said investigations have begun into the theft of exam papers from an office in Kitui town , adding that they have discovered that the exam papers were stolen and sold to schools , and that they have also launched an investigation into how the exam papers were stolen .
Fifteen people , including men , have been arrested for allegedly stealing this year's KCPE exam papers in Kitui Central , Kitui Town .
This was revealed by the head of the center , Ibrahim Hassan

text:
"Ala Ngai ũlũmanĩtye, mũndũ ndakamataan'ye."
Yeova endaa twĩthĩwe 'twendete ũseo [kana, "ũĩkĩĩku," NWT].' (Mika 6:8) Ũĩkĩĩku nĩ wa vata nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano nũndũ weethĩwa ũte vo, mũndũ akeethĩawa na nzika na ũla ũngĩ. Kwoou, nĩ kana ala matwaanĩte methĩwe mendanĩte, no nginya methĩwe maĩkĩanĩe vyũ.
Ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ ala matwaanĩte mayĩĩkĩanĩaa. Nĩ kana wĩthĩwe ũĩkĩanĩe na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake no nginya wĩke maũndũ aa elĩ:
1 KWONA MŨTWAANO WAKU NE KĨNDŨ KYA VATA MŨNO
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: 'Metĩkĩlei maũndũ ala maseo mbee.' (Avilivi 1:10) Mũtwaano waku nĩ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala maseo, kana ma vata vyũ thayũnĩ waku. Kwoou, nĩwaĩle kũwosa kwa ũito.
Yeova endaa wĩthĩwe ũimũsũanĩĩa mũno ũla ũtwaanĩte nake 'mũyĩkalany'a na ũtanu.' (Mũtavan'ya 9:9) Nĩwonanĩtye nesa kana waĩle kwĩthĩwa ũithĩnĩkĩa ũla ũtwaanĩte nake, na ũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũtata kwĩka maũndũ ala matonya kũmũtanĩthya. (1 Akolintho 10:24) Nũseo mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake akamanya kana nũmwonaa e wa vata kwaku.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Ethĩwa nũtwaanĩte kana wĩmũtwae, tata mũno ũtũmĩe ĩvinda yĩanĩtye vamwe na mũũme waku kana kĩveti kyaku, na ndũketĩkĩle kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kĩtume mũteka ũu
Ndũkethĩwe ũisũanĩa ĩũlũ waku o we mwene, ĩndĩ ĩthĩwa ũisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa andũ elĩ, we na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake
2 SŨVĨA NGOO YAKU
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Kĩla mũndũ ũsyaasya mũndũ mũka na kũmwĩw'ĩa mũmeo nĩweka ũlaalai nake ngoonĩ yake." (Mathayo 5:28) Kwoou, ethĩwa mũndũ asũanĩaa maũndũ mathũku, no twasye kana ti mũĩkĩĩku kwa kĩveti kyake kana mũũme wake.
Yeova aĩtye kana nĩwaĩle 'kũsũvĩa ngoo yaku.' (Nthimo 4:23, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language; Yelemia 17:9) Nĩ kana wĩke ũu, no nginya ũsũvĩe metho maku. (Mathayo 5:29, 30) Atĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yovu, ũla watianĩe ũtianĩo na metho make ndakaasisye mũndũ mũka ũngĩ e na wendi mũthũku. (Yovu 31:1) Ndũketĩkĩle o na vanini kũsisya visa kana kũsoma ũvoo ũkonetye ũlaalai. Tw'a vyũ kuma ngoonĩ ndũkese kwĩthĩwa ũyendeew'a nĩ mũndũ ũtatwaanĩte nake.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Eka ala angĩ mamanye nesa kana nũlũmanĩtye vyũ na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake
Endeew'a nĩ kũmanya ũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake ũkwĩw'a, na ũitila ũnyanya o na wĩva ũla ũtonya kũtuma ew'a ate mwĩanĩe

translation:
"God made mankind perfect, a righteous man."
Jehovah commands us to 'practice justice [or, "righteousness," NWT].' (Micah 6:8) Righteousness is doing what is right in God's eyes, a person acting honestly and uprightly. Truly, if we have learned to love, we will also want to show kindness.
Many people have learned to be kind. It is because they have been taught to practice righteousness and to do what is right, and they want to help others:
1 SHOW YOUR LOVE FOR GOD AND WHAT IS RIGHT
IMPORTANT POINT: 'Be zealous for good works.' (Proverbs 1:10) Your love is shown by the good things you do, or by the kindness you show to others. Truly, this pleases God.
Jehovah wants us to understand what is right and to 'be concerned about his name.' (Haggai 9:9) Remember that if you please God, he will notice, and he will strengthen you so that you can continue doing good things. (1 Corinthians 10:24) So a person who loves God will try to please him in everything he does.
POINTS TO REMEMBER:
When you are tempted to do wrong, think about how your actions might affect those around you—your family or friends—and ask yourself whether what you are thinking would please Jehovah.
Examine your own heart carefully, and also examine the hearts of others, and make sure that what you want to do is pleasing to God.
2 USE YOUR STRENGTH WISELY
IMPORTANT POINT: "Every man should look out not only for his own interests, but also for the interests of others." (Matthew 5:28) Truly, when someone has bad thoughts, we should not assume that he is being deliberately unkind to our friend or relative.
Jehovah knows if you are 'using your strength wisely.' (Proverbs 4:23, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language; Jeremiah 17:9) If this is the case, then I encourage you to use your abilities well. (Matthew 5:29, 30) Like Job, who was honest and used his eyes to see what was right instead of looking at a beautiful woman, be careful not to let your eyes wander. (Job 31:1) Ask yourself whether it is wise to look at something inappropriate or read something harmful. We should avoid associating with anyone who does not love Jehovah.
POINTS TO REMEMBER:
Be willing to learn from others and listen to their advice.
Try to understand what is bothering someone, and help them find ways to deal with their problems.

text:
WE WĨONA kyaũ vaa? Ii nĩ ita sya mbalasi nzaũ. Ĩndĩ kwasisya vala syũmĩte. Mbalasi isu isembete syũmĩte ĩtunĩ syĩ ĩũlũ wa mathweo! Kwaw'o ki ĩtunĩ kwĩ mbalasi?
Aiee, ii ti mbalasi sya w'o. Nĩ twĩsĩ ũu nũndũ mbalasi iitonya kũsembela mathweonĩ, kana nitonya? Ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩneenaa ĩũlũ wa mbalasi syĩ ĩtunĩ. We nĩwĩsĩ nĩkĩ?
Kĩtumi nũndũ tene mbalasi nĩsyatũmĩawa mũno kaũnĩ. Kwoou Mbivilia ĩtũtavasya ĩũlũ wa andũ matũlĩte mbalasinĩ matheete kuma ĩtunĩ kwonany'a kana Ngai e na kaũ ũkokita na andũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. We nĩwĩsĩ vala kaũ ũsu ũkokitĩwa ũndũ vetawa? Vetawa Ali-Maketoni. Kaũ ũsu nĩwakũmina ũthũku w'onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Yesũ nĩwe ũkethĩwa atongoetye kaũnĩ ũsu wa Ali-Maketoni. Lilikana kana Yesũ nĩwe Yeova wanyuvie atw'ĩke mũsumbĩ wa silikalĩ Yake. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumĩte Yesũ ekĩa ngovia ya ũsumbĩ. Na ũvyũ ũsu wĩonany'a kana akoaa amaitha ma Ngai onthe. No tũseng'e nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa Ngai akaananga andũ ala athũku onthe?
Kwasisya ĩngĩ Ngewa ya 10. We wĩona kyaũ vau? Kĩw'ũ Kingĩ kĩla kyaminie andũ athũku. Nũũ ũla waetie kĩw'ũ kĩu kingĩ? Nĩ Yeova Ngai. Yu kwasisya ĩngĩ Ngewa ya 15. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkwĩkĩka vau? Ndũa sya Sotomo na Ngomola iendee na kwanangwa na mwaki ũla Yeova watũmie.
Kwavua Ngewa ya 33. Kwasisya kĩla kĩendee na kwĩkĩka kwa mbalasi na makasya ma kaũ ma Amisili. Nũũ ũla watumie kĩw'ũ kĩu kyũka kĩmavw'ĩke? Nĩ Yeova. Eekie ũu nĩ kana avonokye andũ make. Kwasisya Ngewa ya 36 na ya 76. Vau nũkwona kana o na Yeova nĩwaekie andũ make, Isilaeli, manangwe nũndũ wa ũthũku woo.
Kwoou ĩndĩ, tũikasengw'e nĩkwĩthĩwa Yeova akatũma ita syake sya ĩtunĩ nĩ kana amine ũthũku w'onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Kwatata kũsũanĩa ũu ũkoonany'a kyaũ! Kwavĩndũa ĩkalatasi ngalĩko ĩsu ĩngĩ twone.
Ũvuan'yo 16:16; 19:11-16.
Makũlyo
- Nĩkĩ Mbivilia ĩnenaa ĩũlũ wa mbalasi syĩ ĩtunĩ?
- Kaũ wa Ngai vamwe na andũ athũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ wĩtawa ata, na kĩtumi kya kaũ ũsu nĩ kyaũ?
- Tondũ visa ũkwonany'a, Ũla ũkethĩwa atongoetye nthĩnĩ wa kaũ ũsu nũũ, na ekĩĩte ngovia ya ũsumbĩ nĩkĩ, na ũvyũ wake wĩonany'a kyaũ?
- Kwa kũsisya ĩngĩ Ngewa ya 10, 15, na 33, nĩkĩ tũtaĩlĩte nĩ kũseng'a nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa Ngai akaananga andũ athũku?
- Ngewa ya 36 na 76 syĩtwony'a ata kana Ngai akaananga andũ athũku o na ethĩwa maasya nĩmamũthaithaa?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Ũvuan'yo 19:11-16.
Maandĩko monanasya vyũ ata kana Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwe ũtũlĩte mbalasi ĩsu nzaũ? (Ũvu. 1:5; 3:14; 19:11; Isa. 11:4)
Nthakame ĩsu ĩminzangĩw'e ngũanĩ ya Yesũ ya ĩũlũ yĩlũlũmĩĩlya ata kana ũsindi wake vate nzika ũkeanĩa vyũ? (Ũvu. 14:18-20; 19:13; Isa. 63:1-6)
Naaũ matonya kwĩthĩwa me itanĩ isu iatĩĩe Yesũ atũlĩte mbalasi nzaũ? (Ũvu. 12:7; 19:14; Mt. 25:31, 32)

translation:
What shall we see today? This is a story of a very old woman. She tried to refuse many things. The old woman is very kind and has a heart full of blessings! Where does her kindness come from?
Ah, this is not an old woman's story. It is a story about an old woman who can help people with their problems, or can she? I heard from Mbivilia that the story of the old woman is very important. What do you think?
It happens that some old women are respected because of their age. Mbivilia says they bring good news to many people, helping them with their problems and showing God's love to others. What do you think about someone being honored for doing good deeds? Good deeds like Ali-Maketoni. Someone who spends his life serving others.
Jesus is the one who was sent to show us how to live like Ali-Maketoni. Believe it or not, Jesus is the loving Jehovah who gave us His commandments. That is why Jesus came to demonstrate the way of righteousness. And through His sacrifice, He showed all of God's love. So let us pray that we may be able to serve God and help all people?
Read Psalm 10 further. What will we see today? A good king always cares for his people. Who is this good king? It is Jehovah God. Read Psalm 15 further. What is happening today? Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed because of the wickedness that Jehovah saw.
Read Psalm 33. Read about what happened and the destruction of the wicked and the cities of Amisili. Who sends this good message? It is Jehovah. He hears and sees everything that happens to His people. Read Psalms 36 and 76. See how God loves His people, Israel, despite their sins.
Therefore, let us pray that Jehovah may give us strength to fulfill His purpose and bless all people. Let us understand this important matter! Let us read another letter.
Revelation 16:16; 19:11-16.
Questions
- What did Mbivilia say about the importance of the old woman?
- Why do some of God's servants care for people and serve them, and what is the reason for this?
- Because of your understanding, who is worthy to receive the kingdom of God, and what qualities does he possess, and what is his attitude?
- According to Psalms 10, 15, and 33, why should we pray that God may continue to care for His people?
- Do Psalms 36 and 76 show that God cares for people or punishes the wicked?
Further Questions
- Read Revelation 19:11-16.
What scriptures show that Jesus Christ will destroy the wicked? (Rev. 1:5; 3:14; 19:11; Isa. 11:4)
How can Jesus' future victory be seen in the prophecies concerning His reign? (Rev. 14:18-20; 19:13; Isa. 63:1-6)
What lessons can we learn from the fact that Jesus will destroy the wicked? (Rev. 12:7; 19:14; Matt. 25:31, 32)

text:
KWAMASISYE Kaini na Aveli. Elĩ maĩ andũ aima. Kaini aĩ mũĩmi. Aĩmaa lĩu wa mbaa ngetha na matunda vamwe na mboka.
Aveli nake aĩ mũĩthi wa malondu. Nĩwendete kũsũvĩa tũtena twa malondu. Nĩtweanie na twatw'ĩka malondu, na ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kavinda kanini Aveli aĩ na ndĩthya nene ya malondu.
Mũthenya ũmwe Kaini na Aveli nĩmaeteie Ngai mũthĩnzĩo. Kaini aetie mosyao amwe ma ngetha. Nake Aveli aete malondu ala maseo vyũ waĩ namo. Yeova nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ Aveli na mũthĩnzĩo wake. Ĩndĩ ndaaendeew'a nĩ Kaini na mũthĩnzĩo wake. We nĩwĩsĩ nĩkĩ?
Ti kwĩthĩwa mũthĩnzĩo wa Aveli waĩ mũseo kwĩ wa Kaini. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Aveli aĩ mũndũ mũseo. We nĩwamwendete Yeova na mwana-a-inyia. Ĩndĩ Kaini aĩ mũthũku na ndamwendete mwana-a-inyia.
Kwoou Ngai amwĩa Kaini nĩalyũle mĩendele yake. Ĩndĩ alea kwĩw'a. Aĩ na woo mwingĩ nũndũ Ngai nĩwendete Aveli mũnango. Kwoou Kaini amwĩa Aveli, 'Tũthi kĩsesinĩ.' Kũu me oka, Kaini nĩwamũkũnie mwana-a-inyia Aveli. Amũkũnie mũno nginya amũaa. Ũndũ ũsu Kaini weekie waĩ mũthũku mũno.
O na vala Aveli nĩwakwie, o na yu Ngai no ũmũlilikanaa. Aveli aĩ mũndũ mũseo na Yeova ndolawa nĩ mũndũ mũseo. Kwoou mũthenya ũmwe Yeova nũkamũthayũũkya Aveli. Ĩvinda yĩu vaikethĩwa na kĩtumi kya Aveli akw'e ĩngĩ. Akeethĩwa atonya kwĩkala vaa nthĩ tene na tene. Ũkeethĩwa wĩ ũndũ mũseo ta kĩ kũmanyana na andũ mailyĩ ta Aveli!
Ĩndĩ Ngai ndendeeaw'a nĩ andũ mailyĩ ta Kaini. Kwoou ĩtina wa Kaini kũaa mwana-a-inyia, Ngai nĩwamũsilĩile kwa kũmũlũngya athi kũasa vyũ na andũ ala angĩ ma mũsyĩ woo. Yĩla Kaini waendie kwĩkala ngalĩko ĩngĩ ya nthĩ nĩwoosie ũmwe wa eĩtu-a-inyia na atw'ĩka mũka.
Ĩvinda o yĩendee Kaini na mũka nĩmambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na syana. Ana ala angĩ na eĩtu ma Atamu na Eva nĩmatwaanie na o namo meethĩwa na syana. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ nĩkweethĩiwe na andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ekai twĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa amwe moo.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:2-26; 1 Yoana 3:11, 12; Yoana 11:25.
Makũlyo
- Nĩ mawĩa maũ Kaini na Aveli matethasya?
- Kaini na Aveli maeteie Yeova nthembo myaũ?
- Nĩkĩ Yeova wendeeiw'e nĩ nthembo ya Aveli na nĩkĩ ũtaaendeew'a nĩ ya Kaini?
- Kaini aĩ mũndũ wa mũthemba mwaũ na Yeova atatie ata kwenda kũmũalyũla?
- Kaini eekie ata yĩla maĩ oka ena mwana-a-inyia kĩsesinĩ?
- Elesya ũndũ kweekĩkie kwa Kaini amina kũaa mwana-a-inyia?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:2-26.
Yeova aeleisye ata ĩũlũ wa mwelekelo wa mũisyo ũla Kaini waatĩĩe? (Mwa. 4:7)
Kaini oonanisye mwelekelo mwaũ mũthũku wa ngoo yake? (Mwa. 4:9)
Woni wa Yeova nĩ mwaũ ĩũlũ wa kwĩta nthakame ĩte ĩvĩtyo? (Mwa. 4:10; Isa. 26:21)
- Soma 1 Yoana 3: 11, 12.
Nĩkĩ Kaini wathatie mũno na ũndũ ũsu nĩ ũkany'o ata kwitũ ũmũnthĩ? (Mwa. 4:4, 5; Nth. 14:30; 28:22)
Mbivilia yonanasya ata kana o na ethĩwa andũ ala angĩ onthe ma mũsyĩ nĩmeũmũvĩnga Yeova, no tũendeee kwĩlũmya nthĩnĩ wa wĩanĩu witu kwa Ngai? (Sav. 27:10; Mt. 10:21, 22)
- Soma Yoana 11:25.
Nĩ wĩkwatyo mwaũ ũla Yeova ũnengete ala makusaa kwondũ wa ũlũngalu? (Yoa. 5:24)

translation:
The story of Cain and Abel. Once there were two brothers. Cain was a farmer. He harvested crops like maize and fruits with his family.
Abel on the other hand was a shepherd. He liked taking care of sheep. He raised them and they multiplied, and God favored Abel greatly because he had beautiful sheep.
One day Cain and Abel offered sacrifices to God. Cain offered some of his crops. But Abel offered sheep as a sacrifice, and Jehovah was pleased with Abel and his offering. God did not accept Cain and his offering. Why was this so?
It wasn't that Abel's offering was better than Cain's. In fact, Abel was a righteous person. That's why Jehovah accepted him and his firstborn. But Cain was wicked and disliked his brother.
God warned Cain about his wickedness. But he didn't listen. He had much envy because God accepted Abel's offering. So Cain killed Abel, saying, "Let's go to the field." Then Cain struck his brother Abel and killed him. Because of this deed, Cain became a very wicked man.
And behold, Abel was dead, and God was displeased with him. Abel was a righteous man and Jehovah showed favor to him. One day Jehovah came looking for Abel. He searched everywhere and asked about his whereabouts. The blood of your brother cries out to me from the ground!
But God cursed Cain and his descendants. He said, "You will be a wanderer on the earth." And so Cain went away from the presence of Jehovah. He wandered around becoming a restless wanderer.
He went with his wife and they began to build a city. All the other people who were descendants of Adam and Eve also started building cities. From that time onward, cities began to appear on the earth. Let us remember this lesson well.
Genesis 4:2-26; 1 John 3:11, 12; John 11:25.
Questions
- What caused Cain and Abel to quarrel?
- What offerings did Cain and Abel present to Jehovah?
- Why did Jehovah accept Abel's offering and why did he reject Cain's?
- Was Cain a repentant man, and did Jehovah ever try to help him improve?
- Did Cain ever show regret for killing his brother?
- What can we learn from Cain's example?
Further Questions
- Read Genesis 4:2-26.
Did Jehovah overlook Cain's wicked attitude? (Ge. 4:7)
Did Cain offer a sincere sacrifice? (Ge. 4:9)
What does Jehovah want us to understand about the consequences of our actions? (Ge. 4:10; Isa. 26:21)
- Read 1 John 3: 11, 12.
Why did Cain hate his brother and how could such feelings lead to wrongdoing? (Ge. 4:4, 5; Pr. 14:30; 28:22)
Should we be concerned if others seem hostile towards us because of our loyalty to Jehovah, and should we continue to trust in God? (Ps. 27:10; Matt. 10:21, 22)
- Read John 11:25.
What hope does Jehovah give those who mourn the loss of loved ones? (Jo. 5:24)

text:
KĨMWANA kĩtawa Jordan kĩkwete kamasinĩ ka kwasũvya venzoo kailyĩ ta meli. Mũndũ asyaĩtye kamasinĩ kau no asye kai na vata mũnene. Ĩndĩ Jordan akonaa ke ka vata mũno vyũ. Aĩtye ũũ: "Russell, ũla waĩ mũkũũ na waĩ mũnyanya wa mũsyĩ witũ nĩwe wanengie mũthĩnzĩo ũsu ĩla naĩ mũnini." Ĩla Russell wakwie, Jordan nĩwamanyie ũndũ wa vata mũno. Amanyie kana asyai make na ũmae nĩmatethiw'e mũno nĩ Russell na nĩwamakiakiasya mavindanĩ ala me na mathĩna. Jordan ongelete kwasya ũũ: "Yu nũndũ nĩnĩmanyĩte maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Russell, ngoonaa mũthĩnzĩo ũũ mũnini wanengie wĩ wa vata vyũ kwĩ ũndũ nĩnawonaa."
Kwosana na ngelekany'o ĩsu ya Jordan, mũthĩnzĩo no woneke ũte wa vata nĩ andũ angĩ. Ĩndĩ mũndũ ũla wanengwa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu no awone wĩ kĩndũ kya vata mũno vyũ, na kya thooa mũnene mũno. Mbivilia nĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa mũthĩnzĩo wa vata mũno vyũ nthĩnĩ wa ndeto ii syĩsĩkĩe mũno: "Nũndũ Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ, nĩwanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmwĩtĩkĩlaa ndakae, ĩndĩ ethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela."—Yoana 3:16.
Ũsu nĩ mũthĩnzĩo ũtonya kũtuma ũla waũnengwa akwata thayũ ũtathela! Nĩvethĩwa ve mũthĩnzĩo ũngĩ mũnene ta ũsu? O na kau aingĩ no methĩwe matesĩ vata wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu, Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmesĩ nesa kana ũsu nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa "thooa mũnene" kana wa vata mũno. (Savuli 49:8; 1 Vetelo 1:18, 19) Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ Ngai waumisye thayũ wa Mwana wake wĩthĩwe mũthĩnzĩo kwondũ wa andũ?
Mũtũmwa Vaulo nũeleetye nĩkĩ Ngai weekie ũu ndetonĩ ii: "Nũndũ wa mũndũ ũmwe naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ; na kwa ũu kĩkw'ũ kyavikĩa andũ onthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa onthe nĩmeekie naĩ." (Alomi 5:12) Mũndũ wa mbee, Atamu, amũvĩtĩisye Ngai o esĩ na nũndũ wa ũu atw'ĩĩwa kũkw'a. Kwĩsĩla Atamu, ũsyao wake w'onthe nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩkw'ũ.
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ; ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ." (Alomi 6:23) Nĩ kana Ngai ovosye andũ kuma ũkombonĩ wa kĩkw'ũ, atũmie Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, nĩ kana aumye thayũ wake mwĩanĩu kwondũ wa andũ. Kwĩsĩla nthembo ĩsu ya "wovosyo," onthe ala mamũĩkĩĩaa Yesũ Klĩsto makakwata thayũ ũtathela.—Alomi 3:24.
Vaulo aineenea ĩũlũ wa moathimo maingĩ ala Ngai ũnengae athaithi make kwĩsĩla Yesũ Klĩsto, aisye atĩĩ: "Ngai natũngĩwe mũvea kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo wake ũtaweteka." (2 Akolintho 9:15) Wovosyo nĩ mũthĩnzĩo mũseo mũno ũkethĩa tũitonya kũũeleekya nesa. O na kau ve o mĩthĩnzĩo ĩngĩ Ngai ũnengete andũ, nĩkĩ wovosyo nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla wa vata vyũ? Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na mĩthĩnzĩo ĩla ĩngĩ Ngai ũnengete andũ? * Na twaĩle kwona mũthĩnzĩo ũsu ata? Nĩtũũkũthokya ũsome mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu kuma Mbivilianĩ ilungunĩ ilĩ ila iatĩĩe.
^ kal. 8 Yesũ "anenganie thayũ wake kwondũ witũ" na ngenda. (1 Yoana 3:16) Ĩndĩ nũndũ wovosyo waĩ mũvango wa Ngai, ilungu ii syĩneenea mũno mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩanda kya Ngai e we Mũnengani wa nthembo ya wovosyo.

translation:
Jordan's friend was very happy when he heard about his victory over the team. The man appreciated the victory and rejoiced with great joy. Jordan said this about his victory: "Russell, you are big and strong and our father's favorite son, so you deserve this great honor today." But Russell refused, Jordan realized the importance of victory. He understood that his success and growth were due to Russell and he acknowledged all his efforts and struggles. Jordan continued saying: "Because I have learned many things from Russell, this great honor deserves to be yours because of your victories, which I have seen."
Compared to Jordan's generosity, the honor itself seemed small to others. For the person who receives this honor, it means understanding the value of those victories and the greatness of that joy. Truly, I would like to share with you the meaning of that victory, using these simple words: "For God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life."—John 3:16.
This is a great honor that allows the recipient to have eternal life! Are we worthy of such a great honor? Many people believe in the stories of this honor, Christians especially, whether this honor is of "great joy" or of victory. (Psalm 49:8; 1 Peter 1:18, 19) Why did God send his Son's life as an honor to mankind?
The apostle Paul explained why God made this decision: "Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death spread to all men because all sinned." (Romans 5:12) Our first ancestor, Adam, disobeyed God and thus brought sin upon himself. Because of Adam, all his descendants were affected by sin.
The Bible states: "For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is everlasting life through Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23) But since God loved mankind and wanted to save them from the consequences of sin, he sent his Son, Jesus Christ, to give his life as a ransom for mankind. As a result of this "gift," all who exercise faith in Jesus Christ can receive everlasting life.—Romans 3:24.
Paul continued to speak of many blessings God gives those who love him through Jesus Christ, saying: "God has given us the ministry of reconciliation." (2 Corinthians 9:15) The gift is a precious gift that helps us understand what is important. But are there other gifts God gives to mankind, or is this gift the most valuable of all? Is this honor unique among the other gifts God gives to mankind? * And how can we show appreciation for this honor? Let us examine more scriptures found in the Bible to find out.
^ par. 8 Jesus "gives his life for ours" and continues. (1 John 3:16) Because this gift is an expression of God's love, this scripture shows how much God values his creation and why he is the greatest giver of gifts.

text:
Andũ 823 nĩmoombanĩie nthĩnĩ wa Nyũmba ya Maũmbano Manene ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mũsyĩnĩ wa Benin Wathanthatũ wa Ĩtukũ 1, Mwei wa 3, 2014 nĩ kana malilikane ũndũ wa mwanya Nigeria. Kuma mwaka wa 1999, ĩla mũvango wa kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ila syĩ ũkwati mũnini wambĩĩie, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyakĩte Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ 3,000 nthĩ ĩsu.
Maũndũ amwe maneeneiwe ũmbanonĩ ũsu nĩ ũvoo mũkuvĩ ĩũlũ wa wĩa ũla watethiw'e nĩ kana ikundi nthĩ ya Nigeria syĩthĩwe na kũndũ kwa kũthaithĩa kuma myakanĩ ya 1920. Mbeenĩ, mathaithĩaa nyũmbanĩ sya andũ ene na kũndũ kwa kũkomboa. Nyũmba ya mbee ya kũthaithĩa Nigeria ya kũtũmĩwa nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩ syoka yaakĩtwe vakuvĩ mwaka wa 1935 mũsyĩnĩ wa Ilesa. Katĩkatĩ wa mwaka wa 1938 na 1990, ikundi syongelekile vakuvĩ kũndũ 200, kuma ikundi 14 nginya 2,681, na mbingĩ sya ikundi isu vayaĩ laisi kũkwata vandũ va kũmbanĩa. Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ imwe syatũmĩawa nĩ ikundi thanthatũ. Kũndũ kũngĩ, andũ mookaa aingĩ ũkethĩa mayĩanĩa nyũmbanĩ na ũu ũituma angĩ maũngama nza methukĩĩsye maũmbano maũngeme ndĩlĩsyanĩ. Ĩndĩ ikundi mbingĩ syaendeeie kũmbanĩa nyũmbanĩ sya andũ ene na ilasinĩ sya sukulu.
Mwaka wa 1990 ovisi wa ũvonge wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩwambĩĩie kũnengane loni kana mũkovo nĩ kana ũtetheesye ikundi kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ. Kũvikĩa mwaka wa 1997, Kamitii sya Mwako sya Kĩsio syaĩ itetheesye ikundi 105 kwaka kana kũtũngĩĩa nyũmba syoo sya Ũsumbĩ. Katĩkatĩ wa mwaka wa 1997 nginya 1999 nĩkwaakiwe Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ 13. Syathelile kwakwa kwa kĩlungu kya mĩthenya 7 nginya 15.
O na kau nyũmba sya kũmbanĩa nĩsyaendeee kwakwa mĩtũkĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syaendeee kwongeleka Nigeria ũkethĩa iyĩanĩa kũmbanĩa nyũmbanĩ isu. Mwei wa 4, 1998, ovisi wa ũvonge nĩwoonie ve vata wa kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ 1,114 nthĩ ĩsu.
Aineena e ũmbanonĩ ũsu wa mwanya mũsyĩnĩ wa Benin, Don Trost, ũmwe wa Kamitii ya Ovisi wa Ũvonge, eeie ethukĩĩsya atĩĩ: "Waĩ wĩa mũnene mũno! Tweekũlasya, 'Tũkaũtethya ata?'" Kwambĩĩa mwaka wa 1999, ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩyasũngĩiwe ĩla ikundi sya andũ thanthatũ nginya nyanya sya kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ syatetheeisye ikundi kũndũ kw'onthe nthĩ ĩsu ya Nigeria. Iyaka myako ĩte na maũndũ maingĩ, ikundi isu nĩsyakĩte ta nyũmba 17 kĩla mwei kwa kĩlungu kya myaka 14 mĩvĩtu.
Mwana-a-asa Trost amina kũkatha ethukĩĩsya nũndũ wa wĩa ũla wĩanĩĩtw'e, awetie kana ve wĩa mwingĩ ũtiele kũtethw'a. Mwaka wa 2013 nĩkwĩthĩĩtwe na wongeleku wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nthĩ ya Nigeria ta mbee wa 8,000. Mwana-a-asa Trost aisye ĩngĩ atĩĩ: "Nĩ kana wĩthĩe kwĩ nyũmba syĩanĩtye, nĩtũenda kwaka Nyũmba ingĩ sya Ũsumbĩ 100 kĩla mwaka." Mwaka wa 2013 nthĩ ya Nigeria kũnaĩ ngũsĩ 351,000 nthĩnĩ wa ikundi mbee wa 5,700.

translation:
823 brothers and sisters reported their activity from the large Kingdom Hall of Jehovah's Witnesses in Benin on November 1, 2014, which was also linked to Nigeria. Since 1999, they have had the goal of building Kingdom Halls, and so far they have built 3,000 Kingdom Halls themselves.
Some of the reasons why this construction is important is because of the increasing population and because Nigeria has been preaching since the 1920s. In recent years, more people have become interested in freeing themselves. The first Watch Tower Society in Nigeria used by Jehovah's Witnesses was established in Ilesa in 1935. Between 1938 and 1990, the number of publishers increased from 200 to 14, then 2,681, and many of those publishers were able to help others learn about the truth. One Kingdom Hall was used by five congregations. Often, many people would gather at the Kingdom Hall, and this led to larger and more successful meetings. Many congregations continued to preach to people's homes and use school classrooms.
In 1990, the governing body of Jehovah's Witnesses authorized the building of new Kingdom Halls. By 1997, the Building Committee had overseen the construction of 105 Kingdom Halls. Between 1997 and 1999, 13 Kingdom Halls were built. It took between 7 and 15 days to build each hall.
And although there are many places of worship, Jehovah's Witnesses continue to increase in Nigeria, helping more people to learn about the truth. On April 4, 1998, the governing body reported that 1,114 Kingdom Halls had been built.
Don Trost, who served as a member of the Building Committee, said: "What a wonderful work! Will we ever finish?" By 1999, this work had involved over 50,000 volunteers who helped construct Kingdom Halls throughout Nigeria. Despite the challenges, they managed to build an average of 17 halls per month for 14 years.
Mr. Trost recalls wondering what would motivate them to continue, yet many were eager to participate. In 2013, the number of Jehovah's Witnesses in Nigeria reached 8,000. Mr. Trost added: "Even if we visit all the homes, we plan to build 100 more Kingdom Halls each year." In 2013, Nigeria had 351,000 publishers and an average attendance of 5,700.

text:
Ĩvuku yĩtawa Encyclopædia Britannica yĩeleetye kana Isita nĩyo "sikũkũ ĩla nene ya kũlilikana Kũthayũũka kwa Yesũ Klĩsto, ĩla ĩkanisa ya Kĩklĩsto yĩlilikanaa." Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Isita nĩ sikũkũ ya Kĩklĩsto?
Nĩ kana ũmanye ũw'o wa ũndũ nesa, nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli mũseo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu. O ta ũu, nĩ kana tũmanye kana Isita nĩ sikũkũ ya Kĩklĩsto, nĩ ũndũ mũseo kũmanya maũndũ ala makonetye sikũkũ ĩsu.
Ũndũ wa mbee, Yesũ eeie aatĩĩi make malilikanae kĩkw'ũ kyake ĩndĩ ti kũthayũũka kwake. Mũtũmwa Vaulo eetie kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ "Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi."—1 Akolintho 11:20, NWT; Luka 22:19, 20.
Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana kwosana na ĩvuku Britannica, maũndũ maingĩ ala mekawa ĩvinda ya sikũkũ ya Isita "mayĩthĩawa makonetye" ũthayũũkyo wa Yesũ, "ĩndĩ methĩawa maumĩte syĩthĩonĩ sya tene." Kwa ngelekany'o, mbũkũ na matumbĩ nitũmĩawa mũno nthĩ mbingĩ ĩvindanĩ ya sikũkũ ya Isita.
Mũsomi ũmwe wa mavuku ma tene wĩtawa Philippe Walter, aeleetye ũndũ syĩthĩo ta isu syesie kũtw'ĩka kĩlungu kya sikũkũ ya Isita. Aandĩkie kana "ĩvindanĩ yĩla andũ ma ndĩni ite sya Kĩklĩsto mavĩndũawa methĩwe Aklĩsto," waĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi mũno kũlikany'a kũthayũũka kwa Yesũ na sikũkũ yoo ya kũtanĩa "kũthela kwa mbevo, na kwambĩĩa kwa ĩvinda ya ũvyũvu." Walter aendeee na kwasya kana yĩu yaĩ ĩtambya ĩnene ya kũlikya "sikũkũ sya Kĩklĩsto" ndĩninĩ sya andũ ala mataĩ Aklĩsto, na ũu ũituma wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa andũ aingĩ kũvĩndũka matw'ĩke Aklĩsto.
Ũndũ ũsu wa "kũvĩndũa andũ methĩwe Aklĩsto" ndwaaĩkĩka ĩvindanĩ yĩla atũmwa maĩ thayũ, nũndũ maĩ 'asiĩĩi' ma momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ ma andũ ala mataĩ Aklĩsto. (2 Athesalonika 2:7) Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwawetete kana ĩtina wa "kũthi" andũ 'makookĩla, makĩneena ndeto sya ngũlũ, maimakusya amanyĩw'a mamaatĩĩe mo.' (Meko ma Atũmwa 20:29, 30) Vakuvĩ myaka 100 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie kana andũ amwe maĩ manambĩĩa kwasya Aklĩsto. (1 Yoana 2:18, 26) Ũu watumie Aklĩsto mambĩĩa kũatĩĩa syĩthĩo sya andũ ala mataĩ Aklĩsto.
Andũ amwe no mesilye kana kwĩtĩkĩlya syĩthĩo imwe ila syĩkawa sikũkũnĩ ya Isita kũyaĩ kũthũku, nũndũ nĩkwatumie "andũ ala mataĩ Aklĩsto" maelewa ũthayũũkyo wa Yesũ nesa. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Vaulo ndaĩ etĩkĩla ũndũ ũsu. O na kau Vaulo nĩwaendaa kũndũ kwingĩ kwaĩ ungu wa Ũsumbĩ wa Lomi, na kweethĩawa syĩthĩo mbingĩ sya andũ mate Aklĩsto, ndaaĩtĩkĩla o na vanini kũtũmĩa syĩthĩo isu nĩ kana atetheesye andũ mamũelewe Yesũ nesa. Vaulo aumisye ũkany'o ũũ kwa Aklĩsto: "Mũtikovanĩw'e ĩsoki yĩmwe na ala mate etĩkĩli: nũndũ ũlũngalu na ũthũku wĩ mũamba mwaũ? kana kyeni kĩ na mũamba mwaũ na kĩvindu? Kwondũ wa ũu Umai katĩ woo, na mwĩthĩwe mwĩvathanĩte nao, eneena ũu Mwĩaĩi, Na mũikakiite kĩndũ kĩvuku."—2 Akolintho 6:14, 17.
Tweemanyĩsya kyaũ kwa kũneenea maũndũ asu kwa ũkuvĩ? Tweemanyĩsya kana Isita ti sikũkũ ya Kĩklĩsto.
"Mũtikovanĩw'e ĩsoki yĩmwe na ala mate etĩkĩli."—2 Akolintho 6:14

translation:
The book The New Encyclopædia Britannica states that Easter is "the Christian festival celebrating the Resurrection of Jesus Christ, but the church commemorates it." So, is Easter really a Christian festival?
If you understand the origin of this custom, it is an origin that is connected to ancient customs. Otherwise, if we know that Easter is a Christian festival, it is important to know what things have affected this festival.
Furthermore, Jesus himself instituted the Memorial of his death on the night before his impalement. The apostle Paul referred to the Memorial of Jesus' death as "the Lord's evening meal."—1 Corinthians 11:20, NWT; Luke 22:19, 20.
Therefore, according to the Encyclopædia Britannica, many things that are observed during the Easter festival "are connected" to the commemoration of Jesus, "but they have pagan origins." For example, eggs and rabbits are used extensively in the observance of the Easter festival.
One scholar of ancient customs named Philippe Walter stated that some things do not help us understand the meaning of the Easter festival. He writes that "the traditions of pre-Christian peoples were adapted by Christians," so it is difficult to separate the commemoration of Jesus' resurrection from the festival of spring "renewal, and the awakening of nature." Walter goes on to say that a large part of what is celebrated as "the Christian festival" comes from people who were not Christians, and this causes confusion for many people regarding the true meaning of Easter.
This practice of "adapting traditions from non-Christians" has its roots in earlier times, when false religious ideas influenced those who were not Christians. (2 Thessalonians 2:7) The apostle Paul warned about a time when men would be "desperate, grasping for any straw, and easily led astray by false teachings." (Acts 20:29, 30) About 100 years after Christ's death, the apostle John wrote that some people were already abandoning the teaching of Christ. (1 John 2:18, 26) This misled Christ's followers into believing false ideas about those who were not Christians.
Some may feel that adopting certain customs is harmless, especially if they seem to have their origin in ancient times, but this can influence "those who are not Christians" to misunderstand Jesus' message. In fact, Paul himself acknowledged this very thing. He traveled extensively throughout the Roman Empire, and while he preached to many Christians, he also recognized that others needed to understand Jesus' message. Paul used this appeal to Christ: "Do not become unevenly yoked with those who do not believe; for what fellowship does righteousness have with lawlessness? Or what communion does light have with darkness?"—2 Corinthians 6:14, 17.
How can we avoid being influenced by false teachings? How can we ensure that Satan does not deceive us?
"Do not become unevenly yoked with those who do not believe."—2 Corinthians 6:14

text:
"Wendo wa Klĩsto nũũtũthing'ĩĩsya; . . . nĩwamakwĩĩe onthe, nĩ kana ala me thayũ maikethĩwe naw'o ĩngĩ kwondũ woo ene, ĩndĩ no kwondũ wake ũla wakwie na athayũũka ĩngĩ kwondũ woo."—2 Akolintho 5:14, 15.
ĨLA twakwata mũthĩnzĩo mũseo vyũ, nĩtwĩw'aa twaĩle kũtũnga mũvea. Yesũ nĩwoonanisye vata wa ũndũ ũsu ĩtina wa kũvosya ala aũme ĩkũmi maĩ na ũwau wa mangũ ũla ũtaĩ na ndawa ĩvindanĩ yĩu. No ũmwe katĩ wa aũme asu ĩkũmi wasyokie, "aimũkatha Ngai na wasya mũnene." Nĩvo ĩndĩ Yesũ wakũlilye atĩĩ: "Ala mathew'a ti ĩkũmi? ala kenda maĩva?" (Luka 17:12-17) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ? Nĩ laisi kũlwa nĩ maũndũ maseo ala andũ matwĩkĩte!
Vai mũthĩnzĩo ũtonya kũelekanw'a na wovosyo. Nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ wanenganiwe. Kwoou, tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũmũtũngĩaa Ngai mũvea nũndũ wa maũndũ ala ũtwĩkĩte?
Mũmanye Mũnengani wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu. Nthembo ya wovosyo ndĩeteae andũ onthe thayũ ũtathela oou vate ũndũ meanĩĩtye. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ waisye ũũ mboyanĩ yake: 'Na thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto.' (Yoana 17:3) Wĩw'a ata ũkamanya kana ve mũndũũme woovoisye thayũ waku ĩla waĩ mũnini? We tyo wendeew'e nĩ kũmũmanya mũnango na kũmanya nĩkĩ wakwovoisye? Yeova Ngai, ũla watũnengie mũthĩnzĩo wa nthembo ya wovosyo, endaa tũmũmanye na tũyĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ya vakuvĩ nake. Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩĩte vinya na ndeto ii: "Mũthengeei Ngai, nake akamũthengeea inyw'ĩ."—Yakovo 4:8.
Ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ya wovosyo. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa [kana, ũmũĩkĩĩaa] ũ Mwana e na thayũ ũtathela." (Yoana 3:36) Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo? Meko maitũ nĩmo monanasya kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ya wovosyo. (Yakovo 2:17) Nĩ meko mailyĩ ata? Mũthĩnzĩo ũtw'ĩkaa waku ĩla wawosa na kũwĩtĩkĩla. Kwoou no nginya wĩtĩkĩle na ũyĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ya wovosyo. Ũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Ĩmanyĩsye ũndũ Ngai wendaa wĩkale, na ĩndĩ ũyĩka kwosana na kĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya. * Mũvoye Ngai akũekee na aikũnenga wasya mũtheu wa ngoo. Ĩla ũũneena na Ngai, ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana nthembo ya wovosyo ĩkatuma ala methĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wayo methĩwa na mũuo wa tene na tene ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte, mekala mate na mũisyo, na maendeea nesa tene na tene!—Aevelania 11:1.
Endaa ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Yesũ nĩwambĩĩie mũvango wa kũlilikanaa kĩkw'ũ kyake o ĩmwe kwa mwaka. Aineenea ũndũ ũsu awetie ndeto ii: "Ĩkaai ũu ũndũ wa kũndilikana." (Luka 22:19) Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ikalilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ Wakelĩ, Matukũ 11, Mwei wa 4, 2017, sua yathũa. Ũmbano ũsu wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, ũla ũkuaa vakuvĩ ĩsaa yĩmwe, ũkeethĩwa na ũvoo ũkaelesya ũndũ kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kĩtonya kũtũtethya ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ na yĩla yũkĩte. Mwaka mũvĩtu, andũ ta milioni 20 nthĩ yonthe nĩmoombanie kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Nĩtũũkũthokya na ũtanu wĩũka kũmbana naitũ nĩ kana twĩonany'a nĩtũtũngaa mũvea kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu mũnene wa Ngai.

translation:
The love of Christ urges us on;… it convinces us that if One died for all, then all died. And so he died for all in order that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and was raised again.—2 Corinthians 5:14, 15.
BUT if we have heartfelt gratitude, we will be moved to act. Jesus showed the power of this principle when he healed ten lepers, though only one returned to give thanks. And one of those ten became well and said, "Was none found to give glory to God except this foreigner?" So Jesus said: "Were there not ten who were made clean? Where are the other nine?" (Luke 17:12-17) What can we learn from this? It is easy to become preoccupied with our own affairs and forgetful of others!
Have heartfelt gratitude and show appreciation. This is the greatest expression of thankfulness. Truly, should we not always strive to express our gratitude to God for all the good things he does for us?
Understand the importance of this principle. The preaching work helps people everywhere to learn about God's purpose. That is why Jesus used this prayer: 'And this means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent forth.' (John 17:3) Would you want to help someone find out what makes life meaningful? Then get to know Jehovah God, who has given us the privilege of sharing his message, and associate with those who are zealous in proclaiming it. The Bible encourages us with these words: "Draw close to God, and he will draw close to you."—James 4:8.
Have faith in the preaching work. The Bible says: "Whoever puts faith in the Son has everlasting life." (John 3:36) How can we show that we have faith? Our actions demonstrate whether we have genuine faith in the preaching work. (James 2:17) Is this really possible? This principle can move us to take action and put our faith into practice. So let us continue to share good news and encourage others. May we always be willing to support the preaching work! Consider how Noah showed his faith, and remember that when we preach, we may encounter opposition, discouragement, and difficulties, but we must persevere!—Hebrews 11:1.
Attend the Memorial of Jesus' death. Jesus instituted the Memorial of his death once a year. He told his disciples to commemorate this event: "Keep doing this in remembrance of me." (Luke 22:19) Jehovah's Witnesses commemorated the Memorial of Jesus' death on March 11, 2017, which fell on a Saturday. That special occasion to remember Jesus' sacrifice helped millions around the world appreciate what Jesus did for them and strengthened their resolve to remain loyal to Jehovah. In recent years, some 20 million people attended the Memorial of Jesus' death. We are encouraged knowing that we are united with fellow believers worldwide in showing appreciation for God's great love.

text:
"Nyie nasũanĩaa kana kwĩ kũndũ kũtatũ mũndũ ũtonya kũthi akw'a, ĩtunĩ, ĩianĩ ya mwaki, kana tũalanĩ. Nĩneesĩ kana ndyaĩ mũndũ mũthũku mũno ũndũ nĩthi ĩianĩ ya mwaki, na kana ndyaĩ mũseo mũno ũndũ nĩthi ĩtunĩ. Ndyeesĩ nesa kĩla kĩendeeaa tũalanĩ. Na ndyaaona vandũ ĩandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ, ĩndĩ vekaa o kũwetwa nĩ andũ."—Lionel.
"Namanyĩĩtw'e kana andũ onthe maendaa ĩtunĩ ĩtina wa kũkw'a, ĩndĩ ndyaĩ naaĩkĩĩthw'a ũndũ ũsu nesa. Nasũanĩaa kana kĩkw'ũ nĩw'o mũthya wa maũndũ onthe, na vai wĩkwatyo ũngĩ mũndũ wĩthĩawa naw'o akw'a."—Fernando.
We waaĩkũlya makũlyo aa: 'Kwĩthĩawa ata ĩla mũndũ wakw'a? Mo andũ maitũ ala makwie me vandũ maendeee kũthĩnĩa? Yo tũkamona ĩngĩ? Tũtonya ata kũĩkĩĩa ũndũ ũsu?' Kwasisya ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu. Ũndũ wa mbee, ekai twone ũndũ Mbivilia yĩeleetye kĩkw'ũ. Na ĩndĩ tũineenea wĩkwatyo ũla ũeleetw'e Ndetonĩ ya Ngai, Mbivilia.
Ve ũndũ ala akw'ũ matonya kwĩka?
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: 'Nũndũ ala me thayũ mesĩ makakw'a; ĩndĩ ala akw'ũ matyĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva, o na mati na ĩtuvi ĩngĩ; nũndũ kũlilikanwa kwoo nĩkũlaa. O ũla kw'oko kwaku kwona wa kwĩka, ĩka na vinya waku, nũndũ kũti wĩa kana ũsũanĩo, kana ũmanyi, kana ũĩ, Seoli vala ũendete.' *
Ndeto Seoli, kana mbũa nĩ vala akw'ũ methĩawa, ĩndĩ ti vandũ vana maendaa kwĩkala. Ndeto ĩsu ĩtũmĩĩtwe kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o kũelesya ũndũ akw'ũ methĩawa mailyĩ, mate ũndũ mesĩ kana vate ũndũ matonya kwĩka. Mũndũũme mũĩkĩĩku Yovu aĩ na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa Seoli? Nĩwaaisye malĩ yake yonthe na syana syake mũthenya ũmwe, na ĩndĩ akwatwa nĩ mĩimũ mĩthũku mũno mwĩĩnĩ wake w'onthe. Amwĩsũvie Ngai akĩmwĩa atĩĩ: "A! kethĩwa ũkambitha nthĩnĩ wa Seoli, kethĩwa ũkanzũvĩa na kĩmbithĩ." (Yovu 1:13-19; 2:7; 14:13) Ndeto isu syĩonany'a nesa vyũ kana Yovu nĩweesĩ kana Seoli ti ĩia ya mwaki, vandũ vala mathĩna make makaingĩvĩĩa, ĩndĩ avonaa ta vandũ ũkathũmũĩa mathĩna make.
Ve nzĩa ĩngĩ ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya kũmanya ũndũ akw'ũ mailyĩ. No tũsome Mbivilianĩ ũvoo ĩũlũ wa andũ nyanya ala mathayũũkiw'e.—Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Andũ Nyanya Mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ Ala Mathayũũkiw'e."
Vaiĩ ũmwe katĩ wa asu nyanya waaweta kana ĩla waĩ mũkw'ũ, aĩ vandũ vaĩ ũtanu mwingĩ kana vandũ wathĩnĩaw'a. Takethĩwa andũ asu mathayũũkiw'e ve vandũ maĩ maendie ĩtina wa kũkw'a, yo tyo methĩwe matavisye andũ ĩũlũ wa vandũ vau? Na Ngai ndethĩwa aveveeie ũndũ ũsu ũandĩkwe Mbivilianĩ nĩ kana andũ onthe makasomaa? Vai ũndũ ta ũsu tũsomaa Mbivilianĩ. Vate nzika, andũ asu nyanya mayaĩ ũndũ maĩ maweta ĩũlũ wa ĩla maĩ akw'ũ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ vai ũndũ meesĩ, yaĩ ũndũ ũmwe na makomete too mũito vyũ. Mavinda angĩ, Mbivilia nĩtũmĩaa too kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o kũelesya ĩũlũ wa kĩkw'ũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ndaviti na Sitivini 'nĩmakomie' kĩkw'ũnĩ.—Meko ma Atũmwa 7:60; 13:36.
Kwoou, ve wĩkwatyo mwaũ kwondũ wa ala makwie? No maamũke kuma toonĩ wa kĩkw'ũ?
^ kal. 7 Ndeto ya Kĩevelania "Seoli" ĩla ĩtũmĩĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu nĩ "mbũa." Mbivilia ingĩ itũmĩĩte ndeto hell ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu, ĩndĩ ũmanyĩsyo wa kana ve vandũ akw'ũ mathĩnĩaw'a na mwaki ũyosanĩte na Maandĩko.
