translation:
"You people worry about whether a person will be able to steal, cheat, commit adultery, or quarrel. I am surprised if there is a righteous man who does not commit adultery, and I am surprised if there is a wise man who does not cheat. I am very much afraid of quarreling. And I have seen people being judged in Mbiviliani, some being condemned by others."—Lionel.
"I believe that people often go to cheat, and I am surprised that this thing happens so much. I worry about whether cheating is the root of all things, and sometimes someone steals because of cheating."—Fernando.
We ask ourselves questions like: 'Is it possible for anyone not to steal? Why do our people always try to harm each other? Will we ever improve? Can we even understand this matter?' The Mbivilia story shows us the depth of this matter. In the past, we saw what Mbivilia brought about. And now we are experiencing what has been brought upon us by the judgment of God, Mbivilia.
Is there anyone at all who can avoid stealing?
THE MBIVILIA STORY SAYS: 'All the animals that roam around steal; those who have wings fly away, or swim, or hide in caves; the most foolish thing is to remain. Or if you want to see how to steal, look at birds, monkeys, or lizards, Solomon said he learned.' *
Solomon's judgment, or rather, it is said that he did not steal, but it is not people who go to stay. This story is used to explain how to avoid stealing easily, but it is said that some people may still find ways to steal. Job, a wealthy man, had a full understanding of Solomon's wisdom? He lost all his possessions and his children in just one day, and then he was afflicted with terrible sores all over his body. Satan told God: "A! He worships you only because of his blessings, test him and you will see!" (Job 1:13-19; 2:7; 14:13) So today we see that if Job could endure when Solomon did not know the meaning of life, people would also endure their hardships.
In another way, it can help us understand how to avoid hardship. Let us read this story about ancient people who were known.—See the box "Ancient People Mentioned in the Bible."
One of the ancient people who lived in those days, there were many people who knew much more than others. It is not necessary for ancient people to be able to live, so why should we compare ourselves to them? And God has allowed this story to be written in the Bible so that everyone can read it? Why don't we read this story in the Bible. They say that ancient people understood many things from what they saw. Why? Because they always thought about something, and they considered everything carefully. Moreover, the Bible is often used to explain the meaning of life. For example, the Bible says that David and Stephen 'understood' life.—Acts 7:60; 13:36.
So, how can we learn from the lives of others? Should we imitate them?
^ par. 7 The Greek expression "psuche" which is used in the scriptures means "soul." Many Bibles use the expression soul in the scriptures, so you will know whether people have souls and their relationship with the Scriptures.

text:
1. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmũthaitha Ngai?
Ngai wa w'o nĩwe Mũmbi wa syĩndũ syonthe. Ndaĩ na mwambĩlĩlyo na ndakethĩwa na mũminũkĩlyo nongi. (Savuli 90:2) Nĩwe Mwambĩlĩlya wa ũvoo mũseo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. (1 Timotheo 1:11) Nũndũ Ngai nĩwe watũnengie thayũ, no we weka twaĩle kũmũthaitha.
2. Ngai ailyĩ ata?
Nũndũ Ngai nĩ Veva vaiĩ mũndũ waamwona o na ĩndĩĩ, ũu nĩ kwonany'a we ti ũndũ ũmwe na andũ, ala me mwĩĩ wa nyama na nthakame. (Yoana 1:18; 4:24) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩtũtonya kũmanya ũndũ Ngai ũilyĩ kwĩsĩla syĩndũ ila woombie. Kwa ngelekany'o, matunda na malaa ma mĩthemba mingĩ matũtavasya Ngai e wendo na nĩ mũĩ. Ũnene wa nthĩ ũtwonasya ũtonyi wake.
Nĩtũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya mũno ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Ngai ũilyĩ kwa kũsoma Mbivilia. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia nĩtũtavasya kĩla Ngai wendete na kĩla ũmenete, ũndũ wĩkanaa na andũ, na ũndũ wĩkaa ĩla andũ meeka ũseo kana meeka ũthũku.
3. Ngai e syĩtwa?
Yesũ aisye: "Inyw'ĩ ĩndĩ voyaai atĩĩ: Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ, syĩtwa yaku yĩtaĩwe." (Nithyĩ tweeketye ndeto; Mathayo 6:9) Ngai e syĩtwa o yĩmwe, o na kau e masyĩtwa maingĩ ma ũnene. Syĩtwa yĩu yĩtamũkawa kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nthĩnĩ wa kĩla kĩthyomo. Kwa Kĩkamba yĩtamũkawa "Yeova."
Syĩtwa yĩu nĩyumĩtw'e Mbivilianĩ mbingĩ na vandũ vayo vakekĩwa masyĩtwa ma ũnene ta Mwĩaĩi kana Ngai. Ĩndĩ ĩla Mbivilia yaandĩkiwe, syĩtwa yĩu yakwatĩkanaa nthĩnĩ wayo mbee wa mavinda 7,000. Yesũ nĩwamanyĩthisye syĩtwa ya Ngai ĩla wamanyĩasya andũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai.
4. Yeova nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa?
Nĩkwĩthĩwa andũ aingĩ nĩmathĩnaa, ũu nĩkwonany'a kana Yeova nĩ Ngai ũtatũthĩnĩkĩaa? Andũ amwe maasya atũeteae mathĩna nĩ kana atũtate, ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o.
Ngai nĩwonaa andũ me ma vata kwake na nĩkyo kĩtumi ũmanengete ũthasyo wa kũnyuva. Nĩtwaĩle kũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa ũthasyo witũ wa kũnyuva kũmũthũkũma Ngai. (Yosua 24:15) Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ manyuvaa kwĩka angĩ mothũku, na kwondũ wa ũu kũyĩthĩwa na mathĩna maingĩ. Mothũku asu matumaa Yeova ew'a woo.
Yeova nĩ Ngai ũtũthĩnĩkĩaa. Endaa tũtanĩe thayũ. O mĩtũkĩ akamina mathĩna na ayananga ala mamaetae. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ, e na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩtĩkĩlya mathĩna kwa kavinda. Nthĩnĩ wa Ĩsomo ya 8, tũkeemanyĩsya nĩkĩ wĩtĩkĩlĩtye mathĩna methĩwe.
5. Tũtonya kũendeea kũmũthengeea Ngai ata?
Yeova nũtũthoketye tũmũthengeee kwĩsĩla mboyanĩ. Nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ kĩla ũmwe witũ. (Savuli 65:2; 145:18) E wendi wa kũekea. O na ethĩwa mavinda angĩ nĩtũemawa nĩkũmwendeesya, nũmanyaa ĩla tweekĩa kĩthito kya kwĩka ũu. Kwoou o na kau tũi eanĩu, kwa w'o nĩtũtonya kũtanĩa ũnyanya wa vakuvĩ vamwe na Ngai.
Nũndũ Yeova nũtũnengete thayũ, twaĩle kũmwenda mũno kwĩ mũndũ o na wĩva. (Maliko 12:30) O ũndũ ũendeee kwonany'a wendo waku kwa Ngai kwa kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wake na kwĩka ũndũ ũkwenda twĩke, now'o ũkaendeeaa kũmũthengeea ĩvinda yonthe.

translation:
1. How can we come to know God?
God of heaven is the Creator of everything. He is eternal and was not created and will always be. (Psalm 90:2) He is the Revealer of the glorious mystery of the Bible. (1 Timothy 1:11) Therefore God is our teacher, and so we can come to know Him.
2. Does God exist?
Truly God is an invisible Spirit whom no man has seen directly, yet we experience him through his creations and among men, like the body and the soul. (John 1:18; 4:24) Because of this, we learn to understand what God exists beyond things we see. For example, fruits and flowers from many trees show us God's love and he is beautiful. The vastness of space shows us his greatness.
We can learn more about what God exists by reading the Bible. For example, the Bible shows us that God is loving and just, what is right and wrong, how to live among people, and how to live a good life or a bad life.
3. What is God called?
Jesus said: "When you pray, say: 'Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.'" (This is a sample prayer; Matthew 6:9) God is called by one name, but also has many names of majesty. His name will be honored in every creation. In Kikamba it is called "Yeova."
His name is mentioned many times in the Bible and its servants have used majestic names such as Mighty One or God. Where the Bible was written, his name was pronounced with four consonants over 7,000 years ago. Jesus revealed God's name when teaching people about God.
4. Does Jehovah care about us?
Many people wonder, does Jehovah really care about us? Some think that because they suffer, it means that God doesn't care about them, but that is not true.
God cares about people who turn to him and this is why he provides comfort. He wants us to find joy in learning more about him. (Joshua 24:15) Many people give up easily, and because of this they are influenced by wrong beliefs. Let us not make Jehovah feel sorry for us.
Jehovah is a caring God. Let us continue to learn about him. And let us reject false beliefs and embrace the truth. Furthermore, there is a reason to correct wrong beliefs for our benefit. As we saw in Lesson 8, we learned how to correct wrong beliefs.
5. Why should we strive to please God always?
Jehovah encourages us to please him willingly. He is interested in each of us individually. (Psalm 65:2; 145:18) He listens to our prayers. Also, although many things happen to us, we know that we can rely on him. Therefore, we should always try to strengthen our relationship with God.
Because Jehovah cares about us, we want to obey him fully and live according to his will. (Mark 12:30) And to show our love for God, we demonstrate what we have learned from his Word and apply it in our lives, so that we may continue to please him completely.

WE NĨWĨSĨ syĩtwa ya mũndũ ũla waĩ vinya kwĩ ala angĩ onthe? Nĩ mũsili weetawa Samusoni. Yeova nĩwe wanengae Samusoni vinya wake. O na mbee wa Samusoni atanasyawa, Yeova eeie inyia wake ũũ: 'O mĩtũkĩ ũkasyaa mwana. Nake akatongosya nthĩnĩ wa kũtangĩĩa Aisilaeli kuma kwa Avilisiti.'
Avilisiti maĩ andũ athũku matũĩte nthĩ ya Kanaani. Maĩ na aũme aingĩ ma kaũ, na nĩmamathĩnasya Aisilaeli mũno. Ĩvinda yĩmwe, Samusoni aendete kũla Avilisiti mekalaa, mũnyambũ mũnene nĩwookie na kũla ũĩ ũtundumĩte. Ĩndĩ Samusoni ooaa mũnyambũ ũsu na moko mathei. Na ĩngĩ nĩwooaie Avilisiti athũku maana maingĩ.
Ĩtina Samusoni nĩwendanie na mũndũ mũka weetawa Ndelila. Atongoi ma Avilisiti nĩmathanie kana kĩla ũmwe woo akanenga Ndelila ilungu 1,100 sya vetha ethwa akamatavya kĩla kĩtumaa Samusoni ethĩwa na vinya mwingĩ. Ndelila nĩwendaa mbesa isu syonthe. We ndaĩ mũnyanyae wa w'o wa Samusoni, kana wa andũ ma Ngai. Kwoou aendeea na kũkũlya Samusoni kĩla kĩtumaa ethĩwa na vinya mwingĩ ũu.
Ĩtina vyũ, Ndelila nĩwatumie Samusoni amũtavya kĩmbithĩ kya vinya wake ayasya, 'Nzw'ĩĩ yakwa ndyaaenzwa o na ĩndĩĩ. Kuma kũsyawa kwakwa, Ngai anyuvie nĩtw'ĩke mũthũkũmi wake wa mwanya wĩtawa Mũnasili. Nzw'ĩĩ yakwa ĩkenzwa, no nasye vinya wakwa.'
Kwoou ĩndĩ, Ndelila amanya ũu, akomya Samusoni too maũũnĩ make. Na ĩndĩ eeta mũndũ ooka na eenza nzw'ĩĩ yake. Yĩla Samusoni waamũkie eethĩa ndena vinya. Na ĩndĩ Avilisiti mooka na mamũkwata. Na mavũthũanga metho make elĩ, na mamũtw'a ngombo yoo.
Mũthenya ũmwe Avilisiti nĩmavokie mboka nene nĩ kana mathaithe ngai yoo Ndakoni, na maete Samusoni kuma kolokolonĩ nĩ kana mamũthekee. Kũvikĩa ĩvinda yĩu, nzw'ĩĩ yake yaĩ ĩneana ĩngĩ. Na Samusoni eea kĩmwana kĩla kyamũtongoesye kĩmũkwete kw'oko: 'Eka ngwate itũĩ ila iũngamĩtye nyũmba ĩno.' Na ĩndĩ Samusoni avoya Yeova amunenge vinya, na akwata ila itũĩ. Na aneena na wasya mũnene: 'Eka nĩkw'e vamwe na Avilisiti.' Vaĩ na Avilisiti ta 3,000 mbokanĩ ĩsu, na Samusoni asukuma ituĩ isu na vinya wake w'onthe na nyũmba yavalũka na yooaa andũ asu onthe athũku
Asili kĩlungu kya 13 nginya 16.
Makũlyo
- Mũndũ ũla waĩ vinya vyũ kũthonoka andũ onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ eetawa ata, na vinya ũsu wake anengetwe nũũ?
- Ĩvinda yĩmwe, Samusoni eekanie na mũnyambũ ata, tondũ ũtonya kwona vaa visanĩ?
- Nĩ kĩmbithi kyaũ Samusoni ũnũũtavya Ndelila vaa visanĩ, na ũndũ ũsu watumie ata akwatwa nĩ Avilisiti?
- Samusoni amoaie ata amaitha 3,000 Avilisiti mũthenya ũla we wakwie?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Asili 13:1-14.
Manoa na mũka moonanisye ngelekany'o nzeo ata kwa asyai ĩũlũ wa kũea syana syoo? (Asi. 13:8; Sav. 127:3; Aev. 6:4)
- Soma Asili 14:5-9 na 15:9-16
Ngewa ya Samusoni ya kũaa mũnyambũ, kũtw'a makanda meũ, kũtũmĩa ũkambu wa ĩng'oi kũaa aũme 1,000 yĩvuany'a kyaũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ veva Mũtheu wa Yeova ũtethasya wĩa?
Veva mũtheu ũtũtethasya ithyĩ ata ũmũnthĩ? (Asi. 14:6; 15:14; Nzek. 4:6; Meko 4:31)
- Soma Asili 16:18-31.
Samusoni eekiwe ata nĩ itindo nthũku, na tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na ũndũ ũsu? (Asi. 16:18, 19; 1 Ako. 15:33)

translation:
WHO is this man whose strength comes from where, and who judges Israel? His name is called Samson. Jehovah is the one who gave Samson his strength. And when Samson's time came around, Jehovah began to speak to him, saying: "You will become a deliverer to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
The Philistines were fierce people who troubled Israel greatly. They oppressed Israel severely. One day, Samson went down to Timnah and saw a young Philistine woman, and he brought her home, and she became his wife. Later, Samson killed thirty men among the Philistines and took their possessions. He repaid the Philistines for insulting him.
Then Samson went and talked to a woman named Delilah. The Philistines urged her to find out what made Samson so strong, promising each of them eleven hundred pieces of silver if she could discover Samson's secret. Delilah wanted money very much. So she betrayed Samson repeatedly and kept asking him about his strength.
Finally, Delilah pressured Samson to reveal the source of his power, saying: "Tell me your secret, how you got your strength." If you tell me, I will be saved and have great strength."
So, Delilah listened carefully, and she lulled Samson to sleep on her lap. Then she summoned a man to shave off his seven locks of hair. As soon as she did this, his strength left him. And the Philistines captured him.
One day the Philistines gathered a large crowd to offer sacrifices to their god Dagon, and they brought Samson into the temple to mock him. But Samson prayed to Jehovah, and his strength returned. He grasped the two pillars supporting the temple and pushed them apart. The temple collapsed, killing more than three thousand Philistines. Samson also died with them, having killed more Philistines in his death than he had killed during his life.
Judges 16:13-16.
Questions
- What lesson can we learn from Samson's story about associating with bad company? How did his strength leave him?
- Why did Samson confide in Delilah, knowing that she might betray him?
- What motivated Samson to repeatedly give in to Delilah's requests, and why did he eventually allow himself to be captured by the Philistines?
- How did Samson kill three thousand Philistines at the time of his death?
Further Questions
- Read Judges 13:1-14.
How did Manoah and his wife show faith when the angel appeared to them with the promise of a son? (Ju. 13:8; Ps. 127:3; Eph. 6:4)
- Read Judges 14:5-9 and 15:9-16
What does Samson's revenge teach us about controlling our anger and avoiding violence? How does this illustrate the importance of trusting in Jehovah God?
What benefits result from trusting in Jehovah? (Ju. 14:6; 15:14; Prov. 4:6; Mark 4:31)
- Read Judges 16:18-31.
What important principle can we learn from Samson's final mistake, and how can we apply it to our lives? (Ju. 16:18, 19; 1 Cor. 15:33)

MŨISYO ŨLA WAĨ VO: Atongoi aingĩ ma siasa na ma ndĩni maĩ na mũvango wa kũmina Mbivilia vyũ. Mavinda maingĩ matũmĩaa ũkũmũ ũla maĩ naw'o nĩ kana masiĩĩe andũ maikethĩwe na Mbivilia, na maikamyumĩthye kana kũmĩalyũla. Kwasisya ngelekany'o ii ilĩ:
Vakuvĩ mwaka wa 167 Klĩsto atanamba kũsyawa: Mũsumbĩ Antiochus Epiphanes ũla wendaa kũlasimĩthya Ayuti mambĩĩe kũthaitha ndĩni ya Kĩkiliki nĩwaumisye mwĩao nĩ kana kovi syonthe sya Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania ila syaĩ vo syanangwe. Mũsomi ũmwe wa isitoli wĩtawa Heinrich Graetz aisye kana athũkũmi ma mũsumbĩ ũsu "matembũangaa na maivĩvya mavuku ma Mĩao vandũ vonthe vala makomana namo, o na nĩmooaa andũ ala maleanaa na mwĩao ũsu."
Myakanĩ ya katĩ katĩ (Middle Ages): Atongoi amwe ma ndĩni ya Katholeki nĩmathatie mũno ĩla meethĩie alimũ amwe ma ndĩni ĩsu maimanyĩsya kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya vandũ va kũmanyĩsya maũndũ ala makonetye kanisa woo. O na ĩngĩ, ĩla meethĩa mũndũ wĩ na Mbivilia vandũ va kwĩthĩwa e na ĩvuku ya Savuli yĩla yĩandĩkĩtwe na Kĩlatinĩ mamwĩtaa mũlei. O na nzama ĩmwe ya ĩkanisa nĩyaumisye mwĩao na yasya kana aũme moo "mathi makamanthe alei asu na mayĩka ũu na kĩthito, me aĩkĩĩku, na mavinda maingĩ . . . kwa kũmantha mĩsyĩ yonthe na kũndũ kw'onthe kũla andũ matalĩthaw'a ta me na Mbivilia. . . . Mũsyĩ ũla weethĩwa na mũlei waaĩle kwanangwa."
Takeka amaitha ala matendaa Mbivilia nĩmamĩminie, ũvoo ũla wĩ vo wĩthĩwa waaie.
KĨLA KYATUMIE MBIVILIA ĨTAMINWA: Mũsumbĩ Antiochus nĩwavithũkĩie Ayuti ala maĩ Isilaeli, ĩndĩ ve Ayuti angĩ maĩ maendie nthĩ ingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Asomi matalĩthasya kana myakanĩ ya mbee 100 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, Ayuti mbee wa 60 ĩũlũ wa 100 mekalaa nthĩ ingĩ eka Isilaeli. Ayuti nĩmavithaa mavuku ala maandĩkĩtwe Ndeto ya Ngai masinakokenĩ moo na Maandĩko asu nĩmo mesie kũendeea kũtũmĩwa nĩ nzyawa ila syaatĩĩe o vamwe na Aklĩsto.—Meko ma Atũmwa 15:21.
Ivindanĩ yĩu (Middle Ages) andũ ala mendete Mbivilia nĩmaendeeie kũmĩalyũla na kũmyumĩĩsya me na ũkũmbaũ o na kau nĩmathĩnaw'a mũno nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu. O na masinĩ ya kũtumbĩthya mavuku ĩtaaĩsa kũseũvw'a katĩkatĩ wa myaka ya 1400 na 1500, ilungu imwe sya Mbivilia nitonya kwĩthĩwa syaĩ vo kwa ithyomo ta 33! Ĩtina wa ũu, Mbivilia nĩyaalyũlilwe na yatumbĩthw'a kwa kĩwango andũ matasũanĩaa.
ŨNDŨ ŨSU ŨTETHETYE ATA?: O na kau asumbĩ me na vinya na atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmatatie ũndũ matonya mamine Mbivilia, yĩu nĩyo ĩvuku yĩla yĩ na andũ aingĩ na yĩalyũlĩtwe mũno kwĩ mavuku angĩ. Mbivilia nĩtetheesye nthĩ mbingĩ ĩla syĩkũandĩka mĩao ya nthĩ yoo, o na nĩmatetheesye ĩũlũ wa ithyomo ila matũmĩaa, na ĩkaalyũla mĩkalĩle ya andũ milioni mbingĩ.

HISTORY WILL TELL YOU: Stories abound of persecution and suffering with the intention of destroying the Bible. Many attempts have been made to suppress it, and there are those who have persecuted people who believe in the Bible, and they have tried to destroy it completely. Consider this example:
In the year 167 BC, a tyrant named Antiochus Epiphanes attempted to desecrate Jerusalem and defile the Temple with abominations, and he ordered that all copies of the Hebrew Scriptures except those found in his possession be destroyed. A certain historian named Heinrich Graetz said that the actions of this tyrant were "atrocities and acts of barbarism against our people, and he alienated those who were loyal to him."
During the Middle Ages: Some Catholic priests hated the fact that some books were being translated into languages understood by the people so that people could understand things that concerned the church. And others, hating someone who had the Bible, would accuse people of witchcraft and burn them along with the Latin version of the Book of Saul. And another branch of the church ordered that it be proclaimed and declared that "those accursed books should be burned with fire and erased, and their followers, and many...to prevent everyone from learning and understanding everything about the Bible…The book that was burned was considered dangerous."
However, despite all these efforts to destroy the Bible, it has survived, and it continues to exist today.
WHY THE BIBLE WAS PRESERVED: The Syrian Antiochus persecuted the Jews and forbade them from observing Jewish customs, and he went further than previous rulers. Historians estimate that around 100 years after Christ, about 60 out of 100 cities remained in Israel. The Syrians destroyed copies of God's Law and other Scriptures, but some scriptures continued to be used by faithful ones—Acts 15:21.
In those (Middle Ages) times, people who possessed the Bible continued to hide it and cherish it secretly, and often at great risk. And during the period of printing innovation between the years 1400 and 1500, one copy of the Bible sometimes cost as much as 33 oxen! Because of this, the Bible was copied by hand and distributed at a high price to wealthy individuals.
IS THIS STILL TRUE TODAY?: Despite the fact that books and newspapers are readily available today, the Bible remains the most widely circulated book among people, and it has been translated into more languages than any other book. The Bible is published in larger numbers than ever before, and it reaches millions of people worldwide.

Wa mũtĩ wa kũmanyĩthya ũseo na ũthũku, ndũkaye.—Mwa. 2:17.
Andũ aingĩ masoma mwĩao ũla Yeova wanengie Atamu no masye kana nĩwamũvatĩte ũthasyo wa kwĩka kĩla ũkwenda. Mayasya ũu kĩla matamanyaa nĩ kana ve kĩvathũkany'o katĩ wa kwĩthĩwa na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa kĩla ũkwenda kũatĩĩa na ũthasyo wa kũtw'a ũla ũseo na ũthũku. Atamu na Eva maĩ na ũthasyo wa kũnyuva nĩmeũmwĩw'a Ngai kana maimwĩw'a. Ĩndĩ no Yeova e weka waĩle kũtw'a nesa vyũ kĩla kĩseo na kĩla kĩthũku, na "mũtĩ wa kũmanyĩthya ũseo na ũthũku" ũla waĩ mũũndanĩ wa Eteni woonanasya ũkũmũ ũsu wake. (Mwa. 2:9) Kwoou ĩla Yeova wanengie Atamu na Eva mwĩao ũsu, endaa kũmamanyĩsya o nesa kana mamwĩw'a now'o matonya kwĩthĩwa na ũthasyo wa w'o. Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana asyai maitũ ma mbee manyuvie kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai. Ĩndĩ ũtwi ũsu Atamu na Eva meekie nĩwamongeleeile ũthasyo ũla maĩ naw'o? Aiee. Nĩmaaisye ũthasyo wa w'o ũla maĩ naw'o nũndũ wa kũtw'a kwĩkala ũndũ mekwenda. w18.04 5-6 ¶9-12
Thĩnanĩ woo w'onthe nake nĩwathĩnaw'a.—Isa. 63:9.
Ve ũndũ ũngĩ Yeova wĩkaa eka o kũmew'ĩa ĩnee athũkũmi make ala meũthĩnw'a. Nĩwosaa ĩtambya ya kũmatetheesya. Kwa ngelekany'o, yĩla Aisilaeli mathĩnĩaa Misili me ngombo, Yeova nĩwaeleiwe nĩ thĩna woo, na ũu watuma enda kwosa ĩtambya aũmine. Yeova eeie Mose atĩĩ: "Nĩ w'o, nĩnonete thĩna wa andũ makwa . . . , na ngew'a ũkayo woo . . . Nĩnĩsĩ mathĩna moo; nakwa nĩtheete nĩmavonokye mokonĩ ma Amisili." (Kuma 3:7, 8) Yeova nĩwamew'ĩie andũ make ĩnee na kwoou amaumya ũkombonĩ. Myaka mingĩ ĩtina wa vau, Aisilaeli me Nthĩ ya Watho nĩmavithũkĩawa nĩ amaitha. Yeova eekaa ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Nĩweew'ĩaa andũ ma Ĩsilaeli tei nũndũ wa kĩĩo kyoo yĩla maendee kũthĩnw'a na kwĩw'ĩthw'a woo nĩ amaitha moo." Ĩvindanĩ yĩu, Yeova nĩwamew'ĩie andũ make ĩnee na amatetheesya. Atũmie asili mavonokye Aisilaeli kuma kwa amaitha moo.—Asi. 2:16, 18, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language. w19.03 15 ¶4-5
Mũndũ mũka nũtonya kũlwa nĩ kana kake kala kekwonga, ndakew'ĩe tei mwana wa ĩvu yake? ĩĩ, nĩmatonya kũlwa, ĩndĩ ndikolwa nue.—Isa. 49:15.
Mĩao ĩlĩ ya mbee katĩ wa ĩla Mĩao Ĩkũmi yaĩtye kana Aisilaeli maaĩle kũmũthaitha Yeova e weka, na ĩkamakany'a maikathaithe mĩvw'anano. (Kuma 20:3-6) Mĩao ĩsu ndyanenganĩtwe ĩmũtethye Yeova. Ĩndĩ yanenganĩtwe ĩmatethye andũ make. Yĩla mathaitha ngai sya mbai ingĩ, nĩmalikaa thĩnanĩ. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, Yeova nĩwaathimaa andũ make yĩla meethĩwa me aĩkĩĩku kwake na meevathana na kwĩka ala angĩ maũndũ matekwosana na ũsili wa katĩ. (1 Asu. 10:4-9) Yeova ndatonya kũtũlwa mũtĩ yĩla ala maasya nĩ athũkũmi make maema kũatĩĩa myolooto yake, na vandũ va ũu, mayĩũmĩsya andũ make. Ĩndĩ Yeova nũtwendete na nũmanyaa yĩla tweekwa maũndũ matekwosana na ũsili wa katĩ. Ew'aa woo mũno kwĩ o na ũndũ mũndũ mũka wĩw'aa oona mwana wake aithĩna. O na kau ndalikĩlĩĩlaa maũndũ vau kwa vau, ĩvinda yake yavika akamasilĩla eki ma naĩ nũndũ wa maũndũ ala mekaa kwelekela ala angĩ. w19.02 22-22 ¶13-15

translation:
As the tree of knowledge of good and bad was delightful.—Gen. 2:17.
Many people today study their Bible and learn that Jehovah warned Adam and Eve not to eat from it because it would result in death. This is why they understand that disobedience leads to ruin and that disregarding Jehovah's standards brings undesirable consequences. Adam and Eve had the opportunity to live forever if they obeyed God, but they chose to disobey. And so Jehovah allowed them to experience the effects of imperfection on everything, and "the tree of knowledge of good and bad" that was in the garden of Eden came to represent his judgment. (Gen. 2:9) Because Jehovah warned Adam and Eve about this, he showed them consideration and gave them an opportunity to make a choice. The reason for testing them was to demonstrate their love for God. In fact, Adam and Eve proved themselves ungrateful for what He did for them. They rejected His guidance and chose to disobey. w18.04 5-6 ¶9-12
But He was moved by their affliction.—Isa. 63:9.
On occasion, Jehovah allows suffering to teach his faithful servants valuable lessons. It is a time to exercise faith. For example, when the Israelites were in slavery in Egypt, Jehovah took note of their distress, and this motivated him to act in their behalf. Jehovah told Moses: "I have certainly seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry . . . Now go, and I will send you." (Ex. 3:7, 8) Jehovah feels sympathy for his people and responds to their prayers. After many years, the Israelites in the Wilderness were afflicted with plagues. Did Jehovah abandon them? The Bible says: "He delivered them from their affliction." Indeed, Jehovah felt sorry for his people and healed them. He used angels to deliver the Israelites from the plagues.—Acts 2:16, 18, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language. w19.03 15 ¶4-5
Can a mother forget her child, or show no compassion for the son of her womb? Of course not, yet a mother can be heartless.—Isa. 49:15.
Many years ago, during the Ten Plagues, did the Israelites fail to honor Jehovah while he was acting, and did they disregard his mighty acts? (Ex. 20:3-6) Many laws focused on honoring Jehovah. Others focused on benefiting his people. When faced with great difficulties, I want to remain loyal. In harmony with this, Jehovah reminds his people that those who are approved by him are those who are devoted to him and who cooperate with his organization. (1 Chron. 10:4-9) Jehovah is able to support us because his beloved servants value his sovereignty, and he encourages his people. And Jehovah helps us to understand what is involved in remaining devoted to him. Just as a loving father rejoices when his son obeys, so too does Jehovah rejoice when we individually apply what we learn from his Word and continue to demonstrate loyalty. w19.02 22-22 ¶13-15

text:
1. Nĩkĩ Ngai wanyuvie Aisilaeli ma tene methĩwe andũ make?
Ngai anyuvie nzyawa sya Avalaamu na aitw'ĩkĩthya mbaĩ na ainenga mĩao. Mbaĩ ĩsu amĩtie "Isilaeli" na amĩtw'a mũsũvĩi wa ũthaithi wa w'o na ndeto yake. (Savuli 147:19, 20) Kwoou, andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe maĩ matonya kũunĩka kumana na Isilaeli.
Ngai anyuvie Aisilaeli methĩwe ngũsĩ syake. Ũndũ Aisilaeli ma ĩvinda ya tene matwĩe wonanasya ũndũ andũ matonya kũathimĩka maatĩĩa mĩao ya Ngai. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 4:6) Kwoou, kwĩsĩla Aisilaeli andũ angĩ maĩ matonya kũmũmanya Ngai ũla wa w'o.
2. Nĩkĩ Ngai wendaa athũkũmi make ũmũnthĩ methĩwe me ngwatanĩo?
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, Ngai nĩwaleile Isilaeli, na vandũ vayo anyuva kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto. (Mathayo 21:43; 23:37, 38) Ũmũnthĩ, vandũ va Aisilaeli, Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩ mo ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
Yesũ oombanisye aatĩĩi make matavany'e na maitw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a kuma mbaĩ syonthe. (Mathayo 10:7, 11; 24:14; 28:19, 20) Wĩa ũũ ũkilyĩ ũnathela mũminũkĩlyonĩ wa walany'o ũũ wa maũndũ. Yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya mbee Yeova ũmbanĩtye andũ milioni mbingĩ kuma mbaĩ syonthe na kũmaete ũthaithinĩ wa w'o. (Ũvuan'yo 7:9, 10) Aklĩsto ma w'o mombanĩtw'e nĩ kana mekĩane vinya na maitethany'a. Nthĩ yonthe, methĩawa na walany'o ũvw'anene wa momanyĩsyo ma Mbivilia mawũmbanonĩ moo.
3. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ syambĩlĩlye ata?
Myakanĩ ya 1870, kĩkundi kĩnini kya amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩkyambĩĩie kũkunĩkĩla ĩngĩ ũw'o wa Mbivilia ũla waĩ waaie. Nĩkyamanyie Yesũ oombanisye kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto nĩ kana kĩtavany'e, na kwoou kyambĩĩa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ nthĩ yonthe. Mwakanĩ wa 1931 nĩkyambĩĩie kwĩyĩta Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
4. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itongoeaw'a ata?
Ĩvinda ya atũmwa, ikundi sya Kĩklĩsto ila syaĩ nthĩ mbingĩ nĩsyatethekie kumana na nzama ĩla ĩtongoesye nũndũ nĩyamwĩnyivĩsye Yesũ ta we Mũtwe wa kĩkundi. (Meko ma Atũmwa 16:4, 5) O ta ũu ũmũnthĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe nitethekaa kumana na Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye yĩ na atumĩa me na ũmanyi. Nzama ĩsu ĩũngamĩe ovisi sya ũvonge sya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ila syalyũlaa ithyomo, ikakũna kyava, na kũnyaĩĩkya mavuku na syĩndũ ingĩ sya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nthĩnĩ wa ithyomo mbee wa 600. Kwoou, Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye nĩtonya kũtũmĩa Maandĩko kwĩkĩa vinya na kũtongoesya ikundi mbee wa 100,000 nthĩ yonthe. Nthĩnĩ wa kĩla kĩkundi, ve atumĩa, kana asyaĩĩsya, ala nĩ aũme meanĩsye maũndũ mana maĩle kwĩanĩw'a. Aũme asu masũvĩaa ĩĩthya ya Ngai kwa wendo.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syũmbanĩtw'e itavany'e ũvoo mũseo na iitw'ĩkĩthya amanyĩw'a. O ta atũmwa, ithyĩ tũtavanasya nyũmba na nyũmba. (Meko ma Atũmwa 20:20) Ĩngĩ, nĩtwĩyumasya tũmamanyĩsye Mbivilia andũ ala mendete ũw'o kuma ngoonĩ. Ĩndĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ti o kĩkundi tũ. Ithyĩ nĩ mũsyĩ wĩ na Ĩthe wĩ wendo. Ithyĩ twĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa na nĩtũthĩnĩkĩanĩaa. (2 Athesalonika 1:3) Nũndũ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syũmbanĩtw'e vamwe ta kĩkundi nĩ kana imwendeesye Ngai na iitetheesya angĩ, nĩsyo andũ ala atanu vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.

translation:
1. Why did God show favor to Israel among all peoples?
God favored Abraham's offspring and appointed them as a nation and gave them their land. That nation is called "Israel," and it is distinguished as God's chosen people and his property. (Psalm 147:19, 20) Truly, all the nations on earth have a connection with Israel.
God showed favor to Israel because of his covenants. Because Israel broke those covenants repeatedly, the nations were able to defile God's holy name. (Despoiling His Name 4:6) Truly, through Israel other peoples were able to get to know God's God.
2. Why does God allow suffering to come upon his people at times?
As foretold, God turned away from Israel, and other people made up the congregation of Christ. (Matthew 21:43; 23:37, 38) Therefore, the people of Israel, Christ's people, are now a remnant belonging to Jehovah.
Jesus sent out his disciples to preach and to make disciples of people of all the nations. (Matthew 10:7, 11; 24:14; 28:19, 20) In this way, the fulfillment of the prophecy was getting underway. This is why Jehovah has gathered millions of people from all the nations and prepared a spiritual people for himself. (Revelation 7:9, 10) These Christians are united in proclaiming the good news despite opposition. Above all, they rely on the guidance of the Bible and its inspired message.
3. Has the remnant of Jehovah's people ever been organized?
In the 1870's, a large group of Bible students began to investigate ancient prophecies that were being fulfilled. They realized that Jesus had established the Christian congregation, and truly they began to reject the Trinity doctrine. In 1931 they adopted the name Jehovah's Witnesses.
4. Is Jehovah's organization perfect?
As part of the faithful slave, the Christian congregation, but more than ever, has become associated with the organization used by Jesus as Head of the congregation. (Acts 16:4, 5) But because it is imperfect, Jehovah's organization throughout the entire earth is associated with imperfect humans and their mistakes. The organization provides training for elders of Jehovah's Witnesses, but it does not control them, allowing them freedom, and helping them to improve their ability to teach the Bible effectively. Also, the organization can assign Scriptures to study and to research matters affecting the congregation of over 600. Thus, the organization can send out publications to reach nearly 100,000 congregations around the world. In each congregation, the elders, or overseers, use their discernment when dealing with problems. They show love for God and for their brothers.
Jehovah's organization encourages zealous preaching and helps its servants. But like the apostles, we visit homes from house to house. (Acts 20:20) Furthermore, we endeavor to make the Bible known to people who may be interested in the good news. Indeed, Jehovah's organization is not just a group of us. It is God's loving family. We have deep affection for one another and strengthen one another. (2 Thessalonians 1:3) Although Jehovah's organization includes some who are not fully devoted to God and who do not appreciate his standards, they are few in number throughout the earth.

Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Andũ aingĩ monaa ngelany'o ne yo ũvano ũla mũnene wa Aklĩsto. Ĩndĩ, Mbivilia ndĩeleetye mũtĩ ũla Yesũ wooaĩiwe ũndũ wailyĩ, kwoou vai mũndũ wĩsĩ nesa vyũ ũndũ mũtĩ ũsu wailyĩ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Mbivilia nĩĩkĩĩthĩtye kana Yesũ ndaambwa ngelany'onĩ ĩndĩ aathĩĩiwe mũtĩnĩ.
Mbivilia ĩtũmĩaa ndeto ya Kĩkiliki stau·rosʹ ĩla ĩkũweta ĩũlũ wa mũtĩ ũla Yesũ wooaĩiwe. (Mathayo 27:40; Yoana 19:17) O na kau mavinda maingĩ Mbivilia mbingĩ ialyũũlĩte ndeto stau·ros ta "ngelany'o," asomi aingĩ nĩmetĩkĩlanaa kana ndeto ĩsu yonanasya "mũtĩ kana kĩting'ĩ kĩlũngalu kĩnzĩlĩtwe nthĩ." * Ĩvuku yĩtawa A Critical Lexicon and Concordance to the English and Greek New Testament yaĩtye kana ndeto stau·rosʹ "ĩyonanasya ilungu ilĩ sya mbwaũ ikwatanĩtw'e."
Mbivilia nĩtũmĩĩte ndeto ya Kĩkiliki xyʹlon ĩla no ũndũ ũmwe na ndeto stau·rosʹ. (Meko ma Atũmwa 5:30; 1 Vetelo 2:24) Ndeto xyʹlon ĩalyũlĩtwe ta "ũvwaũ," "kĩting'ĩ," kana "mũtĩ." * Mbivilia yĩtawa The Companion Bible yaĩtye ũũ: 'Vaiĩ ndeto o na ĩmwe ya Kĩkiliki nthĩnĩ wa Ũtianĩo Mweũ yonanĩtye ilungu ilĩ sya mũtĩ ikwatanĩtw'e.'
Ngai nĩwendaa andũ matũmĩe ngelany'o ũthaithinĩ?
O na ethĩwa Yesũ ooaĩiwe mũtĩnĩ ũilyĩ ata, maũndũ aa me vaa ĩtheo ma w'o na maandĩko ma Mbivilia nĩmekwonany'a kana tũyaĩle kũtũmĩa ngelany'o ũthaithinĩ.
Ngai ndendeeaw'a nĩ andũ ala matũmĩaa mĩvw'anano ũthaithinĩ vamwe na ala matũmĩaa ngelany'o. Ngai ameie Aisilaeli maikaatũmĩe mũvw'anano wa "kĩndũ o na kĩva" ũthaithinĩ woo. Namo Aklĩsto meĩtwe 'makĩe kũthaitha mĩvw'anano.'
—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 4:15-19; 1 Akolintho 10:14.
Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa mayatũmĩaa ngelany'o ũthaithinĩ. * Atũmwa ma Yesũ nĩmatiĩie Aklĩsto onthe ngelekany'o nzeo kwĩsĩla momanyĩsyo moo.
—2 Athesalonika 2:15.
Kũtũmĩa ngelany'o ũthaithinĩ kwambĩĩiw'e nĩ andũ mathaithaa mĩvw'anano. * Myaka maana maingĩ ĩtina wa Yesũ kũkw'a, makanisa nĩmambĩĩie kwelelũkya momanyĩsyo ala Yesũ wamanyĩasya, na andũ ala mambĩĩie kũthi makanisanĩ asu "nĩmeetĩkĩlilw'e kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ĩla matũmĩaa ũthaithinĩ woo matanatw'ĩka Aklĩsto," mĩvw'anano ĩsu nĩ vamwe na ngelany'o. (The Expanded Vine's Expository Dictionary of New Testament Words) Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ndyaĩtye kana nĩ kenda mũndũ aalyũke ethĩwe Mũklĩsto, no etĩkĩlw'e aendeesye maũndũ ala ũneekaa matosanĩte na Mbivilia ta kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano.
—2 Akolintho 6:17.

translation:
The Biblical Account
Many people view the torture stake as something associated with the death of Christ. In fact, the Bible does not say that Jesus was impaled on a tree, but rather on a torture stake. And because of this, the Bible shows that Jesus was hanged on a pole.
The Bible uses the Greek word stau·rosʹ, meaning "torture stake," to describe what Jesus was impaled on. (Matthew 27:40; John 19:17) However, many translations render the Greek word stau·ros as "cross," leading some to believe that this word refers to a two-beamed structure. *A book titled A Critical Lexicon and Concordance to the English and Greek New Testament states that the word stau·rosʹ "denotes an upright post or stake."
The Bible also uses the Greek word xyʹlon, which is similar to the word stau·rosʹ. (Acts 5:30; 1 Peter 2:24) The word xyʹlon is rendered as "tree," "timber," or "pole." *The Companion Bible says: "It is quite certain that the Greek word xyʹlon never meant a tree, but always a wooden post or stake."
Does God care how people worship?
Even though Jesus died on a pole, the things he taught and what is found in the Scriptures show that we should not worship objects.
God distinguishes between those who practice idolatry and those who worship him. He told the Israelites not to make idols or images to worship. Christ has shown us 'how to hate idolatry.'
—Revelation 4:15-19; 1 Corinthians 10:14.
Christ and his apostles used the torture stake in their ministry. *Jesus' apostles continued to use the torture stake to identify themselves.
—2 Thessalonians 2:15.
Idolatry is often associated with immoral practices. *For many years after Jesus' death, congregations warned against false teachings that encouraged people to engage in idolatry and immorality, and people were warned to separate themselves from such idolaters "who have turned aside to practicing idolatry which defiles Christians," idolatry being linked to immorality. (The Expanded Vine's Expository Dictionary of New Testament Words) The Bible shows that a person who separates himself from wickedness is also separating himself from idolatry.
—2 Corinthians 6:17.

text:
"Mũthaithei ũla wombie ĩtu na nthĩ."—Ũvuan'yo 14:7
Kwĩanana na ũndũ twĩmanyĩĩtye kavukunĩ kaa, nĩtwonete kana Mbivilia yĩ na myolooto ĩtonya ũkũtetheesya vamwe na mũsyĩ waku. Yeova endaa wĩthĩwe na ũtanu. Atwathĩte kana twavĩtya mbee ũthaithi wake, syĩndũ ila ingĩ 'syonthe tũkongeleelwa.' (Mathayo 6:33) Endaa twĩthĩwe twĩ anyanyae make. Tũmĩa mwanya ũla wakwata nĩ kana ũlũlũmĩĩlye ũnyanya waku na Ngai. Ũsu nĩw'o ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩka.—Mathayo 22:37, 38.
1 LŨLŨMĨĨLYAI NGWATANĨO YENYU NA YEOVA
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Ngeethĩwa ĩthe wenyu, na inyw'ĩ mũkeethĩwa ana makwa, aũme na eĩtu, eneena ũu Mwĩaĩi." (2 Akolintho 6:18) Ngai endaa wĩthĩwe wĩ mũnyanyae. Kũvoya nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe mũnyanyae wa Ngai. Yeova atwĩĩte 'tũmũvoyae tũte kũeka.' (1 Athesalonika 5:17) Nĩwĩthĩawa eyũmbanĩtye kũtwĩthukĩĩsya ĩla tũũmũtavya maũndũ ala meũtũthĩny'a ngoonĩ sitũ. (Avilivi 4:6) Ĩla wavoya na andũ ma mũsyĩ waku, nĩmamanyaa kana Ngai nĩ mũnyanyau.
Ũndũ ũngĩ waĩlĩte kwĩka nĩ kũmwĩthukĩĩsya Ngai. Ũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto yake na mavuku ala maeleetye Mbivilia. (Savuli 1:1, 2) Sũanĩĩa mũno kĩla weemanyĩsya. (Savuli 77:11, 12) O na ĩngĩ, nĩ kana tũmwĩthukĩĩsye Ngai, no nginya tũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto tũteũtĩĩa.—Savuli 122:1-4.
Kũneena na andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ nzĩa ĩngĩ ya vata ya kũlũlũmĩĩlya ũnyanya witũ nake. O ũndũ waendeea kwĩka ũu, now'o ũnyanya waku na Yeova ũendeeaa kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũlũmu.—Mathayo 28:19, 20.
ŨNDŨ MŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Manthai ĩvinda ya kũvoya na kũsoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya
Ekai maũndũ ma kĩ-veva methĩwe ne mo mavata vyũ nthĩnĩ wa mũsyĩ wenyu kwĩ maũndũ ma kwĩtanĩthya
2 TANĨAI ŨTHAITHI WA MŨSYĨ
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Mũthengeei Ngai, nake akamũthengeea inyw'ĩ." (Yakovo 4:8) Mwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mĩvango mĩseo ya ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ, na mũimĩatĩĩaa kĩla ĩvinda. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 18:19) Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa na mĩvango kũitoetye. No nginya mũmwĩkwatye Ngai ĩvinda yonthe. Wĩ mũtwe wa mũsyĩ nĩwaĩle kũtetheesya andũ maku methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai. Ũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Ũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũneenaa ĩũlũ wa Ngai "yĩla ũilyĩ nyũmbanĩ yaku, na yĩla ũendaa nzĩanĩ, na yĩla ũkomaa, na yĩla wũkĩlaa." (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 6:6, 7) Tata ũndũ ũtonya wĩke ta Yosua, ũla waisye atĩĩ: "Ũndũ wakwa na nyũmba yakwa, tũkathũkũmaa Yeova."—Yosua 24:15.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Ĩthĩwa na mũvango ũte kũalyũkanga wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ ma mũsyĩ waku. Mũvango ũsu waĩle kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kwĩanĩsya mavata ma kĩla ũmwe wa mũsyĩ

translation:
"Pray constantly."—1 Thessalonians 5:17
By being diligent in our ministry, we show that we value Jehovah and his Kingdom. Jehovah is pleased when we show faith. He wants us to be confident that he will fulfill his purpose for us. Let us always prioritize his interests. We should use the time we have to strengthen our relationship with God. That is how a person shows love for God.—Matthew 22:37, 38.
1 STRENGTHENING YOUR RELATIONSHIP WITH JEHOVAH
WHAT THE BIBLE TEACHES: "Come out from among them, and separate yourselves,' says Jehovah. 'And do not touch what is unclean.'"—2 Corinthians 6:18. God is pleased with those who love him. Showing love for God is one way to please him. Jehovah asks us 'to pray without ceasing.' (1 Thessalonians 5:17) It pleases him to see us depend on him rather than relying on our own understanding. (Proverbs 3:5, 6) When you associate with people who love God, you demonstrate that you love him.
Another way to please God is to meditate on him. You can do this by studying his Word and reflecting on the scriptures. (Psalm 1:1, 2) Remember past acts of deliverance. (Psalm 77:11, 12) Also, when we praise God, we express our appreciation for everything he does for us.—Psalm 122:1-4.
Joining others in proclaiming the good news about Jehovah is another way to deepen our personal relationship with him. And as we continue to do so, our love for Jehovah will grow stronger.—Matthew 28:19, 20.
WHAT YOU CAN DO:
Make time each day to read and study the Bible
Discuss what you learn with family members and friends
2 STRENGTHEN YOUR FAITH
WHAT THE BIBLE TEACHES: "Draw close to God, and he will draw close to you." (James 4:8) Be sincere in your desire to strengthen your faith, and make it a daily practice. (Proverbs 18:19) Be diligent in your worship. And always trust in God completely. As head of the family, you can help your household to remain spiritually strong by encouraging them to have a close relationship with God. Can you do this? You can do this by speaking to your family about what God "requires of you, and what he delights in, and what he expects of you, and what he approves." (Micah 6:6, 7) Like Joshua, decide today: "As for me and my house, we will serve Jehovah."—Joshua 24:15.
WHAT YOU CAN DO:
Be diligent in sharing the Bible with those in your family. This practice will help you to strengthen your faith and encourage everyone in your family

IMWANA ii ilĩ syĩvaa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o mũno, kana tiw'o? We nĩwĩsĩ masyĩtwa masyo? Ũũ mũsyĩmi nĩ Esaũ, na kĩmwana kĩu kĩũĩthya malondu nĩ Yakovo.
Esaũ na Yakovo maĩ imwana mavatha sya Isaka na Leveka. Ĩthe woo Isaka, nĩwendete Esaũ mũno nũndũ aĩ mũsyĩmi mũseo na nĩwaetae lĩu ũkaĩwa nĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ. Ĩndĩ Leveka endete Yakovo mũno vyũ nũndũ aĩ kĩmwana kĩkilu na kĩuu.
Ũmae woo Avalaamu aĩ o thayũ, na notũtate kũsũnĩa ũndũ Yakovo wendeeaw'a nĩkũmwĩthukĩĩsya aineena ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Ĩtina Avalaamu nĩwakwie e na ũkũũ wa myaka 175, namo mavatha asu maĩ na ũkũũ wa myaka 15.
Esaũ e na ũkũũ wa myaka 40 nĩwatwaie iveti ilĩ sya kuma nthĩ ya Kanaani. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie Isaka na Leveka methĩwa na kyeva kingĩ mũno nũndũ iveti isu iyathaithaa Yeova.
Na ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe kweekĩka ũndũ watumie Esaũ amwĩw'ĩa woo mũno mwana-a-inyia wake Yakovo. Ĩvinda nĩyavikie yĩla Isaka waĩ aathime mwana wake ũla mũkũũ. Na nũndũ Esaũ nĩwe waĩ mũkũũ kwĩ Yakovo, Esaũ asũanĩĩa nĩwe ũkũathimwa. Ĩndĩ mbeange Esaũ aĩ anathooesya Yakovo kĩanda kya kwosa ũathimo ũsu. Na ĩngĩ, imwana isu ilĩ iisyawa Ngai nĩwaĩtye kana Yakovo nĩwe ũkosa ũathimo ũsu. Na ũu nĩw'o kweethĩiwe. Isaka aathimie mwana wake Yakovo.
Ĩtina, yĩla Esaũ wamanyie ũvoo ũsu nĩwamũthatĩie Yakovo mũno. Athatie mũno vyũ nginya asya akooaa Yakovo. Yĩla Leveka weewie ũvoo ũsu nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩũũyũ kingĩ. Kwoou ĩndĩ amwĩa mũũme wake Isaka: 'Ũkeethĩwa wĩ ũndũ mũthũku mũno ethĩwa Yakovo o nake akatwaa ũmwe wa aka ma Kanaani.'
Na kwa kĩtumi kĩu Isaka amwĩta Yakovo mwana wake na amwĩa: 'Ndũkatwae mũndũ mũka wa kuma Kanaani. Vandũ va ũu, ũkĩla ũende kwa Mbethũeli ũmae waku, kũũya Aalani. Ũkatwae ũmwe wa eĩtu ma mwana wake Lavani.'
Yakovo nĩwamwĩthukĩĩisye ĩthe wake, na vate kweteela ambĩĩa kyalo kĩasa kya kũthi kwa andũ ma ũko woo ala mekalaa Aalani.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 25:5-11, 20-34; 26:34, 35; 27:1-46; 28:1-5; Aevelania 12:16, 17.
Makũlyo
- Esaũ na Yakovo maĩ aaũ, namo maĩ na kĩvathũkany'o kyaũ?
- Esaũ na Yakovo maĩ na ũkũũ mwaũ yĩla ũmae woo Avalaamu wakwie?
- Esaũ eekie ũndũ mwaũ ũla watumie inyia na ĩthe wake makwatwa nĩ kyeva kingĩ?
- Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Esaũ amũthatĩa mũno mwana-a-inyia Yakovo?
- Isaka amwĩaĩie ata mwana wake Yakovo?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 25:5-11, 20-34.
Yeova athanie ata ĩũlũ wa ana elĩ ma Leveka? (Mwa. 25:23)
Kwaĩ na kĩvathũkany'o kyaũ katĩ wa mwelekelo wa ngoonĩ wa Yakovo na Esaũ ĩũlũ wa ũkithathi? (Mwa. 25:31-34)
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 26:34, 35; 27:1-46; na 28:1-5.
Kũlea kwendeew'a nĩ maũndũ ma kĩveva kwa Esaũ kwoonekie ata ũtheinĩ? (Mwa. 26:34, 35; 27:46)
Isaka amwĩie Yakovo eke ata nĩ kana akwate ũathimo wa Ngai? (Mwa. 28: 1-4)
- Soma Aevelania 12:16, 17.
Ngelekany'o ya Esaũ yoonanisye kyaũ ĩũlũ wa maumĩlĩĩlo ma ala mavũthasya maũndũ matheu?

translation:
This child was born smooth skinned, or wasn't he? Were they wondering about signs? This man is Esau, and his brother who came later is Jacob.
Esau and Jacob were both sons of Isaac and Rebekah. After Isaac grew old, he favored Esau greatly because he loved game and gave him some to eat from among the people. But Rebekah favored Jacob over him because he was the younger son.
In the days of Abraham, there was famine, so they went down to Egypt to seek help because Jacob wanted to be blessed by Jehovah. And Abraham died at the age of 175, and he lived to be 15 years old.
When Esau was 40 years old, he took a wife from among the daughters of Canaan. This displeased Isaac and Rebekah, for they wanted him to take a wife from among their own people, so that the wife would be pleasing to Jehovah.
And on one occasion, while Esau was hungry, he said to Jacob, "Please give me some of that red stew." So he sold his birthright to Jacob for a piece of bread and stew. Later, Esau despised his birthright. And God chose Jacob instead of Esau. And this was His decision. Isaac blessed his son Jacob.
But when Esau learned about this, he hated Jacob greatly. He thought to himself that he would kill Jacob after their father died. And Rebekah heard what Esau planned to do to his brother Jacob. So she sent for Jacob and told him, "Your brother Esau is planning to avenge himself on you. Now go quickly to Haran, to Laban, your mother's brother. Stay with him for a while until your brother's anger subsides. Then I will send someone to bring you back."
So Isaac called Jacob his son and said to him, "Go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take a wife from among his daughters. Go and find a wife from among the daughters of Laban."
Jacob obeyed his father and went to Haran, where he met Rachel at a well in the territory belonging to the people of Shechem.
Genesis 25:5-11, 20-34; 26:34, 35; 27:1-46; 28:1-5; Hebrews 12:16, 17.
Questions
- What did Esau and Jacob both value, and how did they differ?
- How did Esau and Jacob show that they were descendants of Abraham?
- What mistake did Esau make regarding his birthright, and what consequences did he face?
- Why did Esau hate his brother Jacob so much?
- What promise did Isaac make to his son Jacob?
Further Questions
- Read Genesis 25:5-11, 20-34.
What did Jehovah reveal to Rebekah about her twins? (Gen. 25:23)
How did the difference between Jacob and Esau become apparent even before they were born? (Gen. 25:31-34)
- Read Genesis 26:34, 35; 27:1-46; and 28:1-5.
What shows that Esau did not appreciate the importance of his birthright? (Gen. 26:34, 35; 27:46)
What did Isaac tell Jacob, showing that he believed God had chosen him? (Gen. 28:1-4)
- Read Hebrews 12:16, 17.
What does the story of Esau teach us about the dangers of valuing material things too highly?

text:
ASI-ISI! Nĩ kyaũ kyeekĩka vaa? Mwanake ũũ ũkomete vaa nthĩ nĩ mũũmĩu mũno? Kwasisya! Ũmwe wa andũ aa maumaalĩte kuma nyũmba nĩ Vaulo! Nũtonya kwona Timotheo vau o nake? Mwanake ũsu avalũka kuma ndĩlĩsyanĩ?
Ĩĩ, ũu nĩw'o kwamina kwĩkĩka. Vaulo amatavasya ũvoo amanyĩw'a vaa Teloa. Nĩweesĩ kana ndakamona ĩngĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nũndũ aĩ athi na ngalawa ũnĩ ũsu. Kwoou aendeea na kũneena nginya ũtukũ katĩ.
Mwanake ũũ weetawa Eutikusi ekalĩte ndĩlĩsyanĩ, nake akoma too. Na ĩndĩ avalũka kwĩsĩla ndĩlĩsyanĩ, kuma ngolovanĩ ya katatũ nginya nthĩ! Kwoou nũtonya kwona nĩkĩ andũ aa mamakĩte mũno. Andũ asu mookĩlya mwanake ũsu, kaĩ ũndũ masũanĩaa now'o. Aĩ mũkw'ũ!
Yĩla Vaulo woonie kana mwanake nĩ mũkw'ũ, amũmamĩa na amũkũmbatĩlya na moko. Na ĩndĩ asya: 'Mũikamake. Ndena ũndũ!' Na nĩw'o! Nĩ kyama! Vaulo nĩwamũthayũũkya! Na andũ onthe matana.
Na onthe mambata ĩngĩ ngolovanĩ na maya lĩu. Nake Vaulo aendeea na kũneena nginya kwakya. Ĩndĩ nũtonya kwĩthĩwa na w'o kana Eutikusi ndaakoma ĩngĩ! Ĩndĩno Vaulo, Timotheo na ala maendanĩtye namo malĩsa ngalawanĩ. We nĩwĩsĩ maendie va?
Vaulo eethĩiwe amina kyalo kyake kya katatũ kya kũtavany'a, na yu nĩwenũkĩte. Kyalonĩ kĩĩ Vaulo ekalile myaka ĩtatũ ndũanĩ ya Eveso yoka. Kwoou kyalo kĩu kyaĩ kĩasa mũno kũthonoka kĩla kyake kya kelĩ.
Ĩtina wa kuma Teloa, ngalawa nĩyaũngamie Mileto kwa kavinda kanini. Na nũndũ ndũa ya Eveso yaĩ o kĩlomita nini kuma vau, Vaulo atũmana atumĩa ma kĩkundi moke nginya Mileto nĩ kana aneene namo ĩvinda ya mũthya. Ĩtina, ĩvinda ya ngalawa ya kũkũsya yavika, mo meewie kyeva ta kĩ kwona Vaulo aithi!
Ĩtina vyũ ngalawa nĩyookie ĩngĩ Kaisalea. Na Vaulo o ekalĩte vaa nyũmbanĩ ya mũmanyĩw'a Vilivu, mwathani Akavo amũkany'a Vaulo. Na asya kana Vaulo akoovwa avika Yelusaleme. Na kwa w'o, ũu nĩw'o kweethĩiwe. Ĩtina wa kyovo kya myaka ĩlĩ kũu Kaisalea, Vaulo nĩwatwaiwe Lomi akasilĩlwe mbee wa Kaisali, mũsumbĩ wa Alomi. Ekai twone ũndũ kweethĩiwe e kyalonĩ kya kũthi Lomi.
Meko kĩlungu kya 19 nginya 26.
Makũlyo
- Mwanake ũũ ũkomete nthĩ visanĩ nũũ, na eeka ata?
- Vaulo eekie ata eethĩa mwanake nĩ wakw'a
- Vaulo, Timotheo, na ala maendanĩtye vamwe namo maendie va, na kweethĩiwe ata maũngama Melita?
- Nĩ ũkany'o mwaũ mwathani Akavo wanengie Vaulo, na kweethĩiwe ata o tondũ mwathani ũsu waĩtye?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Meko 20:7-38.
Kwĩanana na ndeto sya Vaulo ila iandĩkĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa Meko 20:26, 27, tũtonya kwĩthĩwa "tũtakakũlw'a nthakame ya mũndũ o na wĩva" ata? (Esek. 33:8; Meko 18:6, 7)
Nĩkĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi maĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa "malũmĩtye ndeto ĩla ya kĩthito" yĩla meũmanyĩsya? (Meko 20:17, 29, 30; Tito 1:7-9; 2 Tim. 1:13)
- Soma Meko 26:24-32.
Nũndũ Vaulo aĩ Mũlomi atũmĩie ũndũ ũsu ata kwĩanĩsya wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũla wanengetwe nĩ Yesũ? (Meko 9:15; 16:37, 38; 25:11, 12; 26:32; Lk. 21:12, 13)

translation:
GREETINGS! What news is there? Is this young man well, or is he a believer? Hurry! One of those who visit homes is Paul! Should we go see Timothy with him? Is this young man staying at the inn?
Yes, this is how it happened. Paul requested that we go with him to Thessalonica. Perhaps I will see more beyond the province, if God wills it with me. Let us go ahead and talk tonight.
This young man named Eutychus was staying at the inn, and he was also well. But he wanted to stay at the inn, near the three taverns over there! Let's go see if these people are good. These people received this young man kindly, and they were very happy about it. Oh my!
Then Paul went and embraced the young man and kissed him repeatedly. And then he said: 'Be strong. Don't give up!' And that's it! It is wonderful! Paul encouraged him! And many others were comforted.
And many more gathered at the tavern and ate bread. Then Paul went and talked until dawn. But I should be able to find out whether Eutychus is well! Indeed, Paul, Timothy and the others traveled with ships. Where are you going?
Paul was sent from his homeland of Cilicia, and you know him. He stayed in Ephesus for three years. Now this city is close to Asia, and it is important for the region.
From Thessalonica, the ship sailed to Miletus, a large port. And about ninety kilometers from Ephesus, Paul sent messengers to Miletus to summon the leaders of the churches. From there, the ship that was sailing passed by, so everyone waited to see what Paul would say!
Then the ship stopped at Cos. And Paul stayed in the house of a believer named Julius, whose brother was Jason. And they wanted Paul to go to Jerusalem. And because of this, he was sent. From the province of Asia, after three years, Paul was taken to Rome and imprisoned in Caesar's palace, under the supervision of a Roman official. Everyone knows how he was sent to Rome.
Acts chapter 19 verses 26.
Questions
- What does this passage teach us about perseverance, and how can we apply it?
- What did Paul do when he found out the young man had fallen?
- Where did Paul, Timothy, and the others travel with ships, and what happened at Miletus?
- Did you notice how Jason welcomed Paul, and what happened to the officer who was responsible?
More Questions
- Read Acts 20:7-38.
According to Paul's words recorded in Acts 20:26, 27, can we learn how to "declare ourselves innocent of the blood of all men" ? (Ezek. 33:8; Acts 18:6, 7)
What qualities should those appointed to "oversee in the congregation" possess? (Acts 20:17, 29, 30; Titus 1:7-9; 2 Tim. 1:13)
- Read Acts 26:24-32.
How did Paul use his opportunity to testify to Felix about the hope of salvation offered through Jesus? (Acts 9:15; 16:37, 38; 25:11, 12; 26:32; Luke 21:12, 13)

text:
YEOVA nĩ Ngai mũlau. (Yak. 1:17) Wũmbi wake kuma kũya ĩũlũ ndatanĩ nginya kũũ nthĩ isesinĩ nũmũtaĩaa nũndũ wa ũlau wake.—Sav. 65:12, 13; 147:7, 8; 148:3, 4.
Mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli nĩwendeeiw'e mũno nĩ ũlau wa Mũmbi wake nginya atila wathi akathĩĩe mawĩa make. Kwasoma Savuli ya 104 wone kana o naku ndwĩĩw'a take. Mũandĩki ũsu aisye: "Ngamwinĩa Yeova o yĩla nĩ thayũ: ngaina ngĩkatha Ngai wakwa o yĩla nĩĩkalaa." (Sav. 104:33) We wĩ na wendi ta ũsu?
YEOVA NĨWE NGELEKANY'O ĨLA NZEO VYŨ YA ŨLAU
Yeova endaa twĩthĩwe twĩ alau take. O na nũtũtavĩtye nĩkĩ nũseo twĩthĩwe twĩ alau. Kwoona ũndũ wamũveveee mũtũmwa Vaulo: "Meaĩe ala me na ũthwii wa nthĩ ĩno, maikekathĩĩe, o na maikekwatye ũthwii ũla wanangĩkaa, ĩndĩ mekwatye Ngai, ũla ũtũnengae syĩndũ syonthe na wingĩ, tũtanaw'e nĩsyo; kana mekae nesa, kana methĩwe athwii ma kwĩkaa nesa, methĩwe meyũmbanĩtye kumya syĩndũ syoo, methĩwe me na mũamba wa ngoo na ala angĩ; meyiĩe ene mwambĩlĩlyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte, nĩ kana makwate ũla thayũ wa tene na tene, naw'o nĩ thayũ wa w'o."—1 Tim. 6:17-19.
Ĩla Vaulo waveveewe aandĩkĩa Akolintho valũa wa kelĩ, nĩwoonanisye nesa woni ũla mũndũ waĩle kwĩthĩwa naw'o ĩũlũ wa kũnengane. Aandĩkie ũũ: "Kĩla mũndũ nĩeke o tondũ utw'ĩte ngoonĩ yake: ti kwa kulea kwenda, kana kwa kũingĩĩw'a: nũndũ Ngai endete mũndũ ũnenganae na ũtanu." (2 Ako. 9:7) Amina kũandĩka ũu nĩwawetie ala matethekaa nũndũ wa ũlau. Mbee, nĩ ala manengwa nũndũ methĩawa meanĩw'a mavata moo. Kelĩ, nĩ ala manengane nũndũ nĩmakwataa moathimo maingĩ mũno ma kĩ-veva.—2 Ako. 9:11-14.
Vaulo aminĩĩie kũandĩka kĩlungu kya nyanya na kya kenda kya valũa ũsu wa kelĩ kwa kũweta ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ wonanasya kana Ngai nĩ mũlau. Aisye: "Ngai natũngĩwe mũvea kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo wake ũtaweteka." (2 Ako. 9:15) Mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa Yeova nĩ ta ũtalo w'onthe wa ũseo ũla we mwene wĩkĩte andũ make kwĩsĩla vala ve Yesũ Klĩsto. Nĩ mũnene mũno ũkethĩa vai mũndũ ũelesya nesa vyũ na ndeto ũseo waw'o.
Tũtonya ata kũtũnga mũvea kwondũ wa maũndũ onthe ala Yeova na Mwana wake matũnengete vamwe na ala matwathĩte? Nzĩa ĩmwe nĩ kwa kwĩyumya ũndũ tũtonya tũtũmĩe ĩvinda yitũ, vinya witũ, na syĩndũ ila twĩ nasyo ũthaithinĩ wa Yeova.—1 Mav. 22:14; 29:3-5; Luka 21:1-4.

translation:
JEHOVAH is a God of generosity. (Jas. 1:17) His gifts are perfect, and they come from above, descending from the Father of lights—Ps. 65:12, 13; 147:7, 8; 148:3, 4.
One writer of Psalms greatly appreciated the generosity of his Creator, saying he rejoiced in His works. Read Psalm 104 and see how he expressed himself. That writer said: "May Jehovah rejoice in His work; may He find delight in His creation." (Ps. 104:33) Do you feel the same way?
JEHOVAH IS THE SOURCE OF EVERY GOOD GIFT
Jehovah wants us to appreciate his generosity. And we can show our appreciation by using what He gives us generously. Notice what the apostle Paul said: "Instruct those who are wealthy in this present system of things not to be haughty, nor to put their hope on uncertain riches, but on God, who richly provides us with all things for enjoyment; command them to do good, to be rich in fine works, to be generous and ready to share, storing up a fine reward for themselves as a firm foundation for the future, so that they may lay hold on everlasting life."—1 Tim. 6:17-19.
Indeed, Paul wrote to the Corinthians about this very thing, showing why a person should be modest and not become self-sufficient. He wrote: "A brother must not boast over his superior position; no one should brag, for everything you have comes from God." (2 Cor. 9:7) This principle applies to all Christians regarding material possessions. Often, people misuse what they have. Sometimes, people become self-sufficient and think they have accomplished much on their own.—2 Cor. 9:11-14.
Paul kindly explained the reason for giving liberally and generously to others, so that they might understand how Jehovah views generosity. He said: "God loves a cheerful giver." (2 Cor. 9:15) Jehovah's purpose is to give all humans the opportunity to demonstrate faith in Jesus Christ. It is a great privilege to be able to use what we have to help others.
How can we also show our appreciation for all that Jehovah and his Son have done for us and for those who need help? One way is by using our time, energy, and resources to support Jehovah's work.—1 Tim. 22:14; 29:3-5; Luke 21:1-4.

text:
Ĩthe wa Yosevu aĩ ũũ?
Yosevu, ũla waĩ vundi wa mbwaũ, nĩwe waĩ ĩthe wa Yesũ. Ĩndĩ ĩthe wa Yosevu aĩ ũũ? Katĩ wa aaũmae ma Yesũ ala mawetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Mathayo, ve mũndũũme ũwetetwe wĩtawa Yakovo, nayo ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Luka yaĩtye kana Yosevu aĩ mwana wa "Eli." Nĩkĩ maandĩko asu elĩ me kĩvathũkany'o?—Luka 3:23; Mathayo 1:16.
Ĩvuku ya Mathayo yaĩtye, 'Yakovo asyaa Yosevu.' Mathayo atũmĩie ndeto ya Kĩkiliki kwonany'a nesa kana Yakovo nĩwe waĩ ĩthe wa Yosevu. Mathayo aeleasya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Yosevu, ĩthe wa Yesũ ũla wamũeie, wesie kũsyawa kuma kwa nzyawa ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti nginya ũla kwosana na mĩao waaĩle kũtiĩwa kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya Ndaviti, nake nĩ Yesũ.
Nayo ĩvuku ya Luka yaĩtye kana Yosevu aĩ mwana wa "Eli." Ndeto "mwana wa," no yĩeleeke ta "mũthoni." Ngelekany'o nzeo ya kwonany'a ũndũ ũsu yĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Luka 3:27. Ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu Sealitieli etĩtwe 'mwana wa Neli,' o na kau ĩthe wake ũla wamũsyaie nĩ Yekonia. (1 Mavinda 3:17; Mathayo 1:12) Nĩvatonyeka Sealitieli akethĩwa atwaĩte mwĩĩtu wa Neli, na kwoou ayĩthĩwa aĩ mũthoni wake. O nake Yosevu etĩtwe "mwana" wa Eli nũndũ atwaĩte Meli mwĩĩtu wake. Kwoou Luka aeleetye ũko wa Yesũ "kwondũ wa mwĩĩ," ĩndĩ kwĩsĩla kwa inyia wake, Meli. (Alomi 1:3) Mbivilia nĩeleetye nzyawa kũndũ kwĩlĩ ila syesie kumĩlya Yesũ.
Andũ ĩvindanĩ ya tene matũmĩaa langi wĩva wa kũkundya syĩndũ, na matũmĩaa itambaa sya mũthemba wĩva?
Ĩvindanĩ ya tene, w'ia wa malondu, wa mbũi, na wa ngamĩle nĩwatũmĩawa mũno kũseũvya itambaa sya ngũa nthĩ sya Middle East. Ngũa mbingĩ syaseũvaw'a na w'ia, na nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩwetete malondu, kũtila w'ia, na ngũa iseũvĩtw'e na w'ia mavinda maingĩ. (1 Samueli 25:2; 2 Asumbĩ 3:4; Yovu 31:20) Kamũtĩ keetawa katane (flax) nĩkatũmĩawa kũseũvya ndii sya ngũa, na nĩkavandawa Misili na Isilaeli. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 41:42; Yosua 2:6) Aisilaeli ma ĩvinda ya tene mayavandaa vamba kana waiũ, ĩndĩ Maandĩko nĩmawetete kana vamba nĩwatũmĩawa Velisia. (Esita 1:6) Ngũa sya alili (silk) syaĩ sya thooa mũnene, na atandĩthya masyumasya Far East.
Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩtawa Jesus and His World yaĩtye: "W'ia weethĩawa na malangi me kĩvathũkany'o ta langi mweũ na wa mũthanga [brown], na malangi angĩ maingĩ mavulanĩte." O na ĩngĩ, mavinda maingĩ w'ia weethĩawa wĩ mũkundye langi. Ve langi weethĩawa ũilyĩ ta mũtune (purple), na weethĩawa wĩ wa thooa mũnene mũno. Langi ũsu weethĩawa ũseũvĩtw'e kuma mũthembanĩ mũna wa manyonga (mollusks). Langi ũla watũmĩawa kũkundya syĩndũ waseũvaw'a kuma mĩthemba yĩ kĩvathũkany'o ya mĩtĩ, mĩi, matũ, na tũsamũ tũnini. Syĩndũ isu syaumasya langi syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ta mũtune, yelo, mbuluu, na mwiũ.

translation:
Was Joseph his son?
Joseph, who was legally considered the father of Jesus, is called the father of Jesus in the scriptures. So, was Joseph his father? According to accounts in the Gospel of Matthew and Luke, Jesus' genealogy is traced back to David through Mary, and Luke states that Joseph was the son of "Eli." Does this information cause confusion?—Luke 3:23; Matthew 1:16.
Matthew says, "Jacob begat Joseph." Matthew uses the Greek word for "begat" to indicate that Jacob was the father of Joseph. Matthew explains the reason for Joseph's genealogy—the legal father of Jesus—was to show he was a descendant of King David, so that the fulfillment of the prophecy regarding the kingly line of David could be established, namely, Jesus.
However, Luke states that Joseph was the son of "Eli." The term "son of" can mean "descendant." For further clarification on this matter, see Luke 3:27. This scripture reads that Shealtiel was the "son of Neri," yet his actual father was Jeconiah. (1 Chronicles 3:17; Matthew 1:12) Shealtiel was legally credited as the son of Neri, while actually he was descended from Neri. Similarly, Joseph is referred to as the "son" of Eli because he was descended from Eli. Luke shows Jesus' lineage "through Mary," tracing it back to her ancestor, Heli. (Romans 1:3) The Bible clarifies the ancestry but does not contradict Jesus' origin.
Why do people often find it difficult to understand such matters, and why do they stumble over them?
In ancient times, linen, wool, and cotton were commonly used to make clothing, and they came from the lands of the Middle East. Many fabrics were dyed with colors, and this is why the Bible mentions dyes, coloring materials, and fabrics made with dyes. (1 Samuel 25:2; 2 Kings 3:4; Job 31:20) Flax was also used to make fabric, and it was cultivated in Egypt and Israel. (Proverbs 31:13; Joshua 2:6) Ancient Israelites sometimes traded for purple dye, and the scriptures mention that purple cloth was used in Persia. (Esther 1:6) Silk fabrics were very valuable and originated in the Far East.
One book called Jesus and His World says: "Dyes were made from shellfish—the purple dye coming from snails and the brown dye from oysters—as well as from many other sources." And indeed, many fabrics were dyed with various colors. Purple dye was often expensive, costing a great deal. The source of some dyes was the secretions of sea snails, which were obtained from shells of certain kinds of marine life, such as mussels, clams, snails, and large conch shells. Some of those dyes came from insects, yielding shades of crimson, yellow, blue, and green.

text:
WE NŨŨLILIKANA ũyĩw'a ngewa ya anake aa atatũ? Ĩĩ, aa nĩ anyanyae ma Ndanieli ala maleile kũya lĩu mataaĩlĩtwe nĩkũya. Ambaviloni mametaa Satalaki, Mesaki na Aveti-neko. Ĩndĩ kwasisya yu. Nĩkĩ mateũkumanĩa mũvw'anano ũũ o tondũ andũ ala angĩ onthe mekwĩka? Ekai twone.
We nũũlilikana mĩao ĩla Yeova waandĩkie we mwene yĩtawa Mĩao Ĩkũmi? Ũla wa mbee wayo nĩ: 'Ndũkaathaithe ngai ingĩ o na syĩva ate o nyie.' Anake aa me vaa maatĩĩe mwĩao ũsu, o na kau ti ũndũ ũvũthũ kwĩka ũu.
Nevukatilesa, mũsumbĩ wa Mbaviloni nĩweetie andũ aingĩ anene moke kũnenga ndaĩa mũvw'anano ũũ waũngamĩtye. Nake aĩ anamina kũtavya andũ onthe ũũ: 'Mweew'a wasya wa soo na mbeve, na wa mĩthemba ĩngĩ ya mbeve syĩ mawasya, valũkai nthĩ na kũthaitha mũvw'anano ũũ wa thaavu. Na ũla ũteũvalũka na kũũthaitha nũkwĩkw'a ikonĩ yĩ mwaki mwakanu vau kwa vau.'
Yĩla Nevukatilesa weewie kana Satalaki, Mesaki, na Aveti-neko nĩmalea kũvalũka nthĩ mathaithe, athilĩka mũno. Na atũmana maetwe vala ũĩ. Nake amanenga mwanya ũngĩ wa kũvalũka nthĩ mathaithe. Ĩndĩ anake asu nĩmamũĩkĩĩe Yeova. Namo mamwĩa: 'Ngai witũ ũla tũthũkũmaa nũtonya kũtũtangĩĩa ithyĩ. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa ndetũtangĩĩa, tũikavalũka nthĩ tũthaithe mũvw'anano waku wa thaavu.'
Yĩla weewie ũu, Nevukatilesa athilĩka ĩndĩ vyũ. Vaĩ iko ĩnene o vau vakuvĩ, nake asya: 'Ĩkĩai iko mwaki kũndũ mũonza mbee wa ũndũ yĩkothaa kwĩkĩwa!' Na eea aũme ala me vinya vyũ ma ita syake move Satalaki, Mesaki, na Aveti-neko na maimekya ikonĩ yĩu yĩ mwaki. Iko yĩu yaĩ na mwaki mwingĩ mũno nginya aũme asu me vinya mooawa nĩ itw'ĩki sya w'o. Ĩndĩ kweethĩiwe ata kwa ala anake mamekisye mwakinĩ?
Yĩla Mũsumbĩ wasiisye ikonĩ nthĩnĩ, nĩwakĩie mũno. Na akũlya: 'Tũinekya andũ atatũ me ove ikonĩ yĩĩ yĩ mwaki wakanĩte?'
Namo athũkũmi make masũngĩa: 'Ĩĩ, nĩw'o tweeka.'
Nake asya: 'Ĩndĩ nyie nĩona andũ ana maikinyĩla mwakinĩ. Nĩathasye, na mwaki ndũũmeka ũndũ. Na mũvw'ano wa ũsu wa kana nĩ ta wa ngai.' Nake mũsumbĩ athi vakuvĩ na mũomo wa iko na aneena na wasya mũnene ayasya: 'Satalaki! Mesaki! Aveti-neko! Umaalai mũke kũũ, inyw'ĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai Ũla Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe.'
Na maumaala, kĩla mũndũ oona kana mwaki ndũnameka ũndũ. Nake mũsumbĩ asya: 'Ngai wa Satalaki, Mesaki, na Aveti-neko nataĩwe! Nĩwatũma mũlaĩka wake na amatangĩĩa nũndũ nĩmaleile kũvalũka nthĩ na kũthaitha ngai o na yĩva ateo ngai woo ene.'
Ĩno yo tyo ngelekany'o nzeo ya kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova twaĩlĩtwe nĩkũmĩatĩĩa?
Kuma 20:3; Ndanieli 3:1-30.
Makũlyo
- Nĩ mwĩao wĩva Nevukatilesa mũsumbĩ wa Mbaviloni wanengie andũ?
- Nĩkĩ anyanyae atatũ ma Ndanieli mataakumanĩa mũvw'anano wa thaavu?
- Yĩla Nevukatilesa wanengie Aevelania asu atatũ mwanya ũngĩ wa kũkumana, mo moonanisye ata kana mamwĩkwatĩtye Yeova?
- Nevukatilesa eeie aũme make mekane ata na Satalaki, Mesaki, na Aveti-neko?
- Nevukatilesa oonie kyaũ yĩla wasiisye nthĩnĩ wa iko ĩnene?
- Nĩkĩ mũsumbĩ wataĩĩie Ngai wa Satalaki, Mesaki, na Aveti-neko, namo matũiĩie ngelekany'o myaũ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Ndanieli 3:1-30.
Nĩ mwelekelo mwaũ anake asu Aevelania atatũ moonanisye ũla athũkũmi ma Ngai onthe maĩlĩte kũatĩĩa yĩla ũlũmany'o woo na Ngai watatwa? (Nda. 3:17, 18; Mt. 10:28; Alo. 14:7, 8)
Nĩ ĩsomo yaũ ya vata yĩla Yeova wamanyĩisye Nevukatilesa? (Nda. 3:28, 29; 4:34, 35)

translation:
Did we ever wonder why God allowed those three to be thrown into the fiery furnace? Yes, it was so they could demonstrate their faith in Daniel, just as they had demonstrated their faith before. The Babylonians forced Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. This is what happened.
Did we ever wonder if Jehovah would allow his faithful servants to write down the Ten Commandments? The reason he did so was: "I will show favor to those who love me and keep my commandments." Those three men proved their loyalty to him, and this event showed how strong their faith was.
Unfortunately, the king of Babylon ordered many important people to worship the image, threatening them with death if they refused to obey. He also commanded everyone to say: "When you hear the sound of the horn, flute, harp, and lyre, and all kinds of music, fall down and worship the golden image. But whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into a blazing furnace."
So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were willing to die rather than disobey, and they remained steadfast. They trusted in God completely. And they said: "Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace. But even if he does not, let it be known to you that we will not turn away from serving the true God."
And so it happened, Nebuchadnezzar had them tied up and thrown into the fire. There were so many soldiers around them, and he asked: "Is there anyone who can extinguish this fire?" But they couldn't. Then he saw angels accompanying Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the fire, and their bodies were unharmed. The fire didn't even singe their hair, and their clothes weren't scorched. Did anyone ever question the power of God?
Then the king was amazed and asked: "Didn't we throw three men fully clothed into the fire?"
And they replied: "Yes, we did."
He then said: "I see four men walking freely in the fire, unharmed. The fourth looks like a son of gods!" Then the king called out loudly and said: "Shadrach! Meshach! Abednego! Come here, servants of the Most High God of heaven!"
And they came out, and everyone saw that the fire hadn't harmed them at all. Then the king said: "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel and delivered them from the burning fiery furnace, and who still trusts in him and defies the king's command."
This is how we show our appreciation for Jehovah—by obeying his commands.
Psalm 20:3; Daniel 3:1-30.
Questions
- How did King Nebuchadnezzar test the loyalty of people?
- What lesson did the three young men of Daniel learn about trusting in God?
- Why did King Nebuchadnezzar give Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego another chance, even though he knew they would remain loyal to Jehovah?
- Was Nebuchadnezzar impressed by Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
- What made Nebuchadnezzar realize that the king was powerful?
- Why should we praise the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and what can we learn from their example?
Further Questions
- Read Daniel 3:1-30.
What shows that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were confident that Jehovah could save them from the furnace, even if he didn't? (Dan. 3:17, 18; Matt. 10:28; Acts 14:7, 8)
What does this teach us about what Jehovah expects of us? (Dan. 3:28, 29; 4:34, 35)

text:
DANIEL NA MIRIAM matwaanie Mwei wa 9, 2000, na mathi kwĩkala Barcelona, Spain. Daniel aĩtye: "Ithyĩ twoonaa tũilyĩ o ũndũ aangĩ mekalaa." Aendeee kwasya: "Mũsaala witũ nĩwatũtonyethasya kũya mĩkaawanĩ mĩseo, kũthi kũtembea nthĩ sya mũingo, na kwĩkĩa ngũa sya thooa. O na nĩtwatavanasya tũteũtĩĩa." Ĩndĩ maendeangĩe ve ũndũ weekĩkie.
Me ũmbanonĩ ũmwe mũnene weekiwe 2006, ve ũvoo waumiw'e wakiita Daniel mũno. Ũvoonĩ ũsu nĩvakũlilw'e ĩkũlyo yĩĩ: "Nĩtwĩkĩte kyonthe kĩla tũtonya tũvonokye ala 'matwaĩtwe kĩkw'ũnĩ' makwate nzĩa ĩla ĩelete thayũnĩ ũtathela?" (Nth. 24:11) Ũvoo ũsu nĩwakindĩlĩĩle ũndũ kĩla ũmwe waĩle kwĩthĩwa na kĩthito kya kũtavany'a ũvoo ũla ũtangĩĩaa thayũ. (Meko 20:26, 27) Daniel easya ũũ alilikana ĩvinda yĩu: "Neew'aa Yeova ta ũkũneena nakwa." Ũvoo ũsu nĩwoonanisye ũndũ kwongelanga ĩvinda yĩla tũtũmĩaa ũthũkũminĩ kũtonya kwongelanga ũtanu ũla twĩ naw'o. Daniel nĩweesĩ ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka nũndũ Miriam aĩ anambĩĩa ũvainia na akakwata moathimo maingĩ mũno.
Daniel asyokete akasya, "Kuma vau neewie naĩle kũvindũka vyũ." Na nĩw'o weekie. Aolangile masaa ala wathũkũmaa, oosa ũvainia, na ambĩĩa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũtanu ũla matonya kũkwata manongelanga ũthũkũmi woo na maithamĩĩa kĩsionĩ kĩ na ũnyivu wa atavany'a.
MAWETU ALA MAMBIE KŨKOMANA NAMO, NA ŨATHIMO ŨLA MAKWATIE
Twĩ Mwei wa 5, 2007, Daniel na Miriam nĩmatiie mawĩa moo na mathamĩĩa nthĩ maĩ matembeete ĩvinda yĩngĩ yĩtawa Panama. Kĩsio kĩla maendie kũtavany'a kyaĩ tũthama kauta twa Bocas del Toro Archipelago Ũkanganĩ wa Caribbea. Tũthama tũu twĩkalawa mũno mũno nĩ mbaĩ ya Guaymi. Daniel na Miriam masũanĩaa mbesa ila maĩ nasyo no imekalye myei ta nyanya kũu.
Me kũu matũmĩaa masiwa na isululu. Savalĩ ĩtakamola nĩ ĩla maendie ya mbee na isululu ya maili ta 20 (kĩlomita 32). Makinyie isululu savalĩ ĩsu yonthe maathĩtwe nĩ sua ĩvyũ na mesĩle kũndũ kũvaũũku. Daniel anoie weethĩa eĩw'a ta ũvalũka. Ĩndĩ nĩmatanie nũndũ mĩsyĩ ĩla mesĩlile nĩmathokiw'e nesa nĩ andũ ma mbaĩ ya Guaymi, na mũno mũno ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya ndeto imwe sya kĩthyomo kyoo. O na vatavĩtĩte ĩvinda ĩasa maĩ na amanyĩw'a 23.
Thĩna walikile ĩla matheleilwe. Daniel aĩtye atĩĩ: "Tweew'aa kũĩa twasũanĩa kana yu twaaĩle kũsyoka Spain. Tweew'aa kyeva kingĩ twalilikana amanyĩw'a ala twesaa kũtia." Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa mwei ũmwe nĩmakwatie ũvoo mũseo. Miriam aĩtye: "Twakwatie valũa wa kũtw'ĩka mavainia ma mwanya. Twatanie ta kĩ nũndũ yu twaĩ tũendeee na ũthũkũmi witũ kĩsionĩ kĩu!"
ŨTANU ŨLA MWINGĨ MAKWATĨTE
Twĩ mwaka wa 2015, nũndũ wa moalyũku ala meekiwe ũseũvyonĩ, Daniel na Miriam nĩmakũlilw'e masyokee ũvainia wa kĩla ĩvinda. Meekie ata? Meekĩiwe vinya nĩ ndeto ii syĩ nthĩnĩ wa Savuli 37:5: "Mwiĩe Yeova nzĩa yaku; mũĩkĩĩe we, nake akeeka." Nĩ kana maendeee na ũvainia, nĩmamanthie wĩa ũtonya kũmatetheesya, na ũmũnthĩ me kĩkundinĩ kĩmwe kĩ kĩsionĩ kya Veraguas, Panama.
Daniel aeleetye atĩĩ: "Tũtanauma Spain tũyeesĩ nesa kana nĩtũũtonya kwĩkala tũte na syĩndũ mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ twĩkalaa ũu na tũyonaa kĩndũ kya vata tũkosete." Nĩ kyaũ kĩmanengae ũtanu ũla mwingĩ? Maĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũtetheesya andũ menyivĩtye mamũmanye Yeova nĩw'o ũndũ ũla ũtũeteete ũtanu ũla mwingĩ vyũ!"

translation:
DANIEL AND MIRIAM were married on April 9, 2000, and later moved to Barcelona, Spain. Daniel said: "We realized we needed something more meaningful." He continued: "Our life was becoming too focused on material things, traveling every weekend, and enjoying leisure activities. And we were getting tired." They began to search for something more.
In a large congregation in 2006, they met another Daniel. This brother shared a scripture that deeply touched them: "Are you letting your heart be paralyzed so that you say, 'When will it be?' while you are waiting for it to happen?" (Num. 24:11) That talk reminded them of the need for each one of us to be motivated by a sense of urgency regarding the good news. (Acts 20:26, 27) Daniel added at that time he remembered this thought: "Jehovah is allowing me to live." That talk impressed upon them the importance of using our time wisely to preach the good news now. Daniel felt that this was something that Miriam also understood and she showed great enthusiasm.
Daniel then mentioned, "Come what may, I want to remain faithful." And that is what happened. He worked long hours, maintained his spirituality, and encouraged himself to share the good news with others, despite the challenges and frustrations of being discouraged.
OUR CHALLENGES AND THE STRENGTH WE RECEIVED
On May 5, 2007, Daniel and Miriam got married and with their belongings they moved to a country called Panama. Their desire to serve motivated them to travel to Bocas del Toro Archipelago in the Caribbean Sea. There they settled in a place called Guaymi. Daniel and Miriam spent several months there, and although it was difficult, they enjoyed living among the people.
They used canoes and sailboats. The sailboat journey was about 20 miles (32 kilometers). Throughout the entire voyage, the weather was favorable and the sea was calm. Daniel felt very weak due to exhaustion. But he continued working hard with the help of the Guaymi people, and eventually they managed to build a small house. They also traveled to another island with 23 companions.
Then they faced more difficulties. Daniel said: "We thought we would go and work elsewhere, perhaps even to Spain. We thought we could earn more money and be able to contribute." That plan did not materialize after a month. Miriam said: "We received enough value to sustain us for some time. We were happy to continue our ministry without worrying!"
THE GREAT JOY THEY EXPERIENCED
In 2015, when the local brothers learned of their situation, Daniel and Miriam were given assistance with their living expenses. Was this sufficient? They were reminded of the principle found in Psalm 37:5: "Trust in Jehovah and do good; reside in the land and feed on its abundance." If they continued to trust in Jehovah, they would find ways to meet their needs, and they appreciated the kindness shown by the brothers in Veraguas, Panama.
Daniel explained: "We wanted to return to Spain because we thought we might have more opportunities there. But we realized that we were already comfortable here and saw what we needed to do." So what helped them to experience such great joy? He says: "Helping people learn about Jehovah—that is the greatest joy we can experience!"

text:
Nũsomete nesa makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya ala mela kuma? Ethĩwa nũu, sisya ethĩwa nũtonya kũsũngĩa makũlyo aa maatĩĩe:
Nĩkĩ Yeova weetĩkĩlasya mbaĩ ya Isilaeli ĩthi kaũnĩ?
Yeova nũtwendete. Ĩndĩ ĩla mbaĩ ila syathyũlũlũkĩte Aisilaeli syamavinyĩĩa kana syameka maũndũ mathũku, Ngai nĩweetĩkĩlasya kaũ nĩ kana asũvĩe andũ make. Ngai e weka nĩwe wawetaa ũla waĩle kũkita, na ĩla kaũ ũsu waĩle kũkitwa.—w15 1/11, ĩth. 4-5.
Nĩ maũndũ meva ma vata matonya kũtetheesya asyai mamanyĩsye syana syoo ila sya mũika imũthũkũme Yeova?
Ve vata asyai mende syana syoo na maisyony'a kana nĩmenyivĩtye. O na ĩngĩ nũseo makethĩwa na ũmanyi na maitata maielewe.—w15 15/11, ĩth. 9-11.
Nĩkĩ vovu tiwe wĩthĩawa aendeesye kĩanda kĩla kyaĩ na Vetelo?
Ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 16:17, 18 yĩyonanĩtye kana Vetelo nĩwe wesaa kwĩthĩwa e mũtongoi wa aatĩĩi onthe ma Yesũ. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana Yesũ nĩwe ĩvia ya kĩkotonĩ ya kĩkundi, ĩndĩ ti atĩ Vetelo nĩwe wanengiwe ũtongoi ĩũlũ wakyo. (1 Vet. 2:4-8)—w15 1/12, ĩth. 12-14.
Twaĩle kũsũanĩa maũndũ meva tũtanamba kũneena?
Nĩ kana tũtũmĩe ũĩmĩ witũ nesa, twaĩle (1) kũmanya nĩ ĩndĩĩ twaĩle kũneena (Mũta. 3:7), (2) nĩ ndeto syĩva twaĩle kũtũmĩa (Nth. 12:18), na (3) twĩneena ata (Nth. 25:15).—w15 15/12, ĩth. 19-22.
Aklĩsto maĩle kwĩvetangana na maũndũ amwe meva ala monanasya kana mũndũ ti mũĩkĩĩku?
Aklĩsto ma w'o mayaĩle kũkengana kana kũsukana. O na mayaĩle kũneena maũndũ mate ma w'o me na mũvango wa kwanangĩa mũndũ ũngĩ ĩsyĩtwa, mayaĩle kwĩthĩwa me avenani kana avutani, o na mayaĩle kũya.—wp16.1, ĩth. 5.
"Athembi anene" ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ methĩwa maĩ aaũ?
Ndeto "athembi anene" yonanasya andũ ala maĩ na kyeo katĩ wa ala meethĩawa me athembi. Amwe moo maĩ athembi tene na maumw'a.—wp16.1, ĩth. 10.
Twaĩle kwosa ata Mũklĩsto ũĩsaa kĩmũtũ na akanyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ?
Aklĩsto maikathaa ũndũ vataĩle ala mekũya kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu. O na mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta wa w'o ndendaa kũkathwa ũndũ vataĩle na ndendaa kũtinda aiweta kana we nĩ mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta. (Mt. 23:8-12)—w16.01, ĩth. 23-24.
Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ twasũanĩa ũndũ Avalaamu watw'ĩkie mũnyanyae wa Ngai?
No kwĩthĩwa Avalaamu amanyie Ngai kwĩsĩla vala ve Semu. Kĩngĩ kyatethisye Avalaamu nĩ maũndũ ala weeyonee na metho make mavinda ala Ngai wamũsũvĩie e na andũ make. O naitũ no twĩke oou.—w16.02, ĩth. 9-10.
Naaũ meekĩie ilungu na mĩsoa Mbivilianĩ?
Myakanĩ ya 1200 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto Stephen Langton nĩweekĩie ilungu Mbivilianĩ. Aandĩki amwe ma Kĩyuti mambie kwĩkĩa mĩsoa Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania, na ĩndĩ Robert Estienne eekĩa mĩsoa Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki myakanĩ ya 1501 nginya 1600.—wp16.2, ĩth. 14-15.
Ĩla Satani wamũtataa Yesũ nĩwĩthĩwa amũtwaie ĩkalũnĩ?
Tũyamba kwasya ĩĩ vyũ. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 4:5 na Luka 4:9, Yesũ no ethĩwe eekie kwona woni kana akethĩwa aendie kũũngama vandũ vatũlu ĩkalũnĩ.—w16.03, ĩth. 31-32.
Ũtavany'a witũ ũilyĩ ĩmwe ata?
Ĩmwe yũmbanaa o kavola, na nĩyĩsanzamũkasya syĩndũ, na yĩkaitetheesya iikome. Ĩmwe nĩ ũathimo Ngai ũtũnengete. (Kũt. 33:13) Ũtavany'a wa athũkũmi onthe ma Yeova wĩthĩawa ũilyĩ o ta ĩmwe.—w16.04, ĩth. 4.
