translation:
Let us examine some examples from Musyaisyas, but how? However, my brother, consider how to apply them to real life situations:
Did Jehovah show partiality toward Israel at all?
Jehovah is impartial. If a nation or people were rebellious or did wicked things, God showed partiality against them. God does not want you to be biased when judging, and he hates bias—w15 1/11, pp. 4-5.
What can help young ones to remain loyal to Jehovah despite pressure from their peers?
They need friends who feel the same way and support them. Also, they need to know what is right and why—w15 15/11, pp. 9-11.
Why should we be willing to go to any length to please Jehovah?
The account of Matthew 16:17, 18 shows that Peter was delighted to hear Jesus say that he was the one whom God sent. The Bible shows that Jesus is the foundation of the congregation, so Peter was happy to receive the assignment to expand his ministry. (1 Pet. 2:4-8)—w15 1/12, pp. 12-14.
How can we improve our ability to speak persuasively?
If we use our gift in public speaking, we can (1) know what we want to say (Prov. 3:7), (2) have a clear outline (Prov. 12:18), and (3) practice speaking (Prov. 25:15).—w15 15/12, pp. 19-22.
Can Christians become involved in certain political activities without compromising their neutrality?
Christians may participate in peaceful demonstrations. They may also express their views on matters of public interest, but they should avoid taking sides or becoming emotionally involved, or they may compromise their neutrality—wp16.1, p. 5.
What "great crowd" is mentioned in the Bible, and what hope do they have?
The "great crowd" refers to those who exercise faith in Jehovah and associate with His people. Some of this great crowd will live forever on earth.—wp16.1, p. 10.
Should a Christian feel obligated to associate with someone who has been disfellowshipped, and partake of food or drink with him?
Christians are free to decide whether to associate with a disfellowshipped person and eat or drink with him. However, they should be careful not to let their association lead them to approve of his wrongdoing, or they may compromise their integrity.—w16.01, pp. 23-24.
How did Abraham demonstrate his faith when tested by God?
Abraham showed his faith in God by being willing to sacrifice Isaac, his son. What impressed God about Abraham was the way he acted in harmony with what God asked of him and his love for his fellow humans. And we too can imitate him.—w16.02, pp. 9-10.
Why do some find it difficult to preach the good news?
In 1200 C.E., Archbishop Stephen Langton authorized an English version of the Bible. Later, scholars produced translations of the German Bible, and Robert Estienne produced translations of the Greek Bible between 1501 and 1600.—wp16.2, pp. 14-15.
What tactic did Satan use to try to tempt Jesus?
We will see this in the next article. As Matthew 4:5 and Luke 4:9 show, Jesus was taken to a very high place and offered authority over all the kingdoms of the world in exchange for worshiping Satan.—w16.03, pp. 31-32.
Can you strengthen your faith further?
One way is to pray regularly, to meditate on spiritual things, and to remain active in the ministry. One is the spirit of God that empowers us. (Col. 33:13) Strengthen yourself daily so that Jehovah will give you strength.—w16.04, p. 4.

text:
Mũnene wa nguthu ya asikalĩ 100 ma ita sya Lomi atethasya wĩa mwaũ?
Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto nĩmawetete mũnene wa nguthu ya asikalĩ 100 ma Lomi mavinda kauta. Mũnene wa ita ũla wasyaĩĩsyeYesũ ayũawa aĩ wa kyeo kĩu, o ũndũ ũmwe na Kolinelio ũla waĩ wa mbee katĩ wa Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ kũtw'ĩka Mũklĩsto. O na mũnene ũla waaĩle kũsyaĩĩsya mũtũmwa Vaulo aikũnwa o vamwe na Yuliusi, ũla wamũtwaie Lomi maĩ o anene ma nguthu ya asikalĩ 100.—Maliko 15:39; Meko ma Atũmwa 10:1; 22:25; 27:1.
Mũnene ũsu wa asikalĩ (centurion) eethĩawa aũngamĩe asikalĩ 50 kũvika 100 ala maendaa na maaũ. Wĩa wake waĩ kũmanyĩsya na kũkany'a asikalĩ ala waũngamĩe, kũsisya ũndũ mekĩĩte ngũa na kũsisya mĩio yoo, na kũmeĩaĩa ĩla maendete kaũnĩ.
Kũũngamĩa nguthu ya asikalĩ 100 nĩkyo kyeo kĩla kĩnene mũno mũsikalĩ waĩ atonya kũkwata. Ala makwataa kyeo kĩu nĩ ala meethĩawa mathũkũmĩte wĩa wa ũsikalĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa na me atongoi aseo. Nĩ kana nguthu ya asikalĩ ma Lomi yĩthĩwe ĩtonya kũtethya wĩa nesa na kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle, yaĩ no nginya anene asu ma asikalĩ matethye wĩa woo nesa. Livoti ĩmwe yoonanisye kana anene asu "mavinda maingĩ nĩmo meethĩawa me na ũtũĩka na ũmanyi mwingĩ mũno katĩ wa asikalĩ onthe."
Kĩvathũkany'o kya ioo sya ĩvinda ya tene na sya ũmũnthĩ nĩ kyaũ?
Kĩvathũkany'o na ioo sya ũmũnthĩ, ioo sya ĩvinda ya tene syaseũvaw'a na kyũma kyeethĩawa kĩkũnĩtwe mũsasa kĩkakena vyũ. Nĩvatonyeka ioo isu ikethĩwa syaseũvaw'a na ũthuku, vetha, na thaavu ĩndĩ mũno mũno syaseũvaw'a na bronze. Ioo iwetetwe ĩvinda ya mbee Mbivilianĩ ĩla ĩeema ya Yeova ya kũmbanĩa yaakawa. Ĩeemanĩ yĩu nĩvo vaĩ vandũ va mbee va Aisilaeli va kũthaithĩa. Aka nĩmaumisye ioo sya kwanakavya kĩla kĩndũ kya kũthambĩaa kya ũthuku na ĩtina yakyo. (Kuma 38:8) Nĩvatonyeka ioo isu ikethĩwa syavĩvaw'a nginya ikatweka nĩ kana itũmĩwe wĩanĩ ũsu.
Ioo ila syeethĩiwe kũndũ kũla kwĩnzawa syĩndũ sya tene nthĩ ya Isilaeli, syeethĩiwe syĩ na syĩndũ sya kwĩyanakavya sya aka. Ioo isu syeethĩawa syĩ sya kĩlinge na syĩ na ikwatĩli mbanakavye sya mũtĩ, kyũma, kana iseũvĩtw'e na maeo ma nzou. Ikwatĩli isu syeethĩawa iilyĩ visa wa mũndũ mũka. Ngalĩko ĩla ĩte ngũne mũsasa ndyaanakavaw'a.
Ioo isu sya ĩvinda ya tene iyaetae visa mũtheu ta ioo sya ũmũnthĩ sya ngilasi. Ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a ũw'o wa ndeto sya mũtũmwa Vaulo ĩla waisye atĩĩ: "Ĩvinda yĩĩ twĩona ta kĩsisyonĩ kĩ menyenyi."—1 Akolintho 13:12.

translation:
What about the commander of a hundred soldiers who has a servant whom he loves?
The writings of the Kikuyu Christians show that the commander of a hundred soldiers named Lomi desired to heal him. The commander of that man praised Jesus greatly, realizing that he was his son, or something like Cornelius, whose prayers and alms were remembered by God to bring them to Christ. And that commander also wanted to be healed by the apostle Paul, along with Julius, who sent Lomi messages and had a commander of a hundred soldiers.—Mark 15:39; Acts 10:1; 22:25; 27:1.
This commander (centurion) was accustomed to commanding fifty to one hundred soldiers who went out with him. His servants knew how to command and discipline the soldiers who went out with him, so they could accomplish what was needed and finish their work, and know the way to go.
Commanding a hundred soldiers was a great honor for any soldier to have. Those who held this position were those who had shown themselves to be brave and loyal soldiers for a long time and were trusted by others. It is possible that the commander of Lomi's soldiers was able to help people and, because of his position, was able to help those who needed it, and he did not hesitate to help those soldiers who needed him. One report stated that many commanders "were very courageous and knowledgeable among the soldiers."
What is the connection between this incident and today?
The connection between this incident and today is that just as the incident happened then, so too can courage and loyalty be demonstrated today. We can learn from this incident that courage, bravery, and dedication are always valued. Just as they were honored then with gold, silver, and bronze, we too can be honored today for our service. This event took place near the gate of the Mbivilian tribe, which was part of the camp of Jehovah. The camp was where the Israelites camped. This is what motivated them to make every effort to serve bravely and faithfully. (Exodus 38:8) We can also learn from this incident that we should not be afraid to use our talents.
This event, which took place during the wilderness wanderings of Israel, was meant to inspire them and encourage them. This event showed that courage and loyalty were important, and it encouraged them to continue serving. They were rewarded for their courage and loyalty with gifts such as trees, animals, or precious stones. These gifts were given to show appreciation for their service. However, there was one gift that was more valuable than all the others.
This event involving the tent of meeting is similar to the incident with Paul, who said: "Now we see only a reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face."—1 Corinthians 13:12.

text:
Ithyĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩtwĩsĩkĩe nũndũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Ĩndĩ nĩwĩsĩ kana nĩtwĩthĩawa na mũvango wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ nthĩ yonthe?
Mwakanĩ wa 2014, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mbee wa 8,000,000 nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ 240, kĩla mwei nĩsyeemanyĩisye Mbivilia na andũ vakuvĩ 9,500,000. * Vate nzika, ve nthĩ ta 140 ila syĩ andũ anini mbee wa ala twĩmanyĩasya Mbivilia namo!
Nĩ kana mũvango wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ ũendeee, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syumĩthasya Mbivilia, mavuku, makaseti, na syĩndũ ingĩ syakũtetheesya andũ kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, vakuvĩ mbilioni ĩmwe na nyusu, kwa ithyomo vakuvĩ 700 kĩla mwaka! Mũvango ũsu wa mwanya wa kumĩthya mavuku nũtetheeasya andũ aingĩ makemanyĩsya Mbivilia na kĩthyomo kĩla mekwenda.
MOSŨNGĨO MA MAKŨLYO ALA MAKŨLANGAW'A ĨŨLŨ WA MŨVANGO WITŨ WA KŨMANYĨSYA ANDŨ MBIVILIA
Mũvango ũsu wa kwĩmanyĩsya wĩthĩawa ũilyĩ ata?
Tũnyuvaa masomo me kĩvathũkany'o, na tũimantha Mbivilianĩ mĩsoa ĩla ĩeleetye ĩsomo yĩla twanyuva. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia nĩsũngĩaa makũlyo ta aa: We Ngai nũũ? We Ngai ailyĩ ata? E ĩsyĩtwa? Ekalaa va? Na no tũmũthengeee? Ũndũ ũla wĩ vinya nĩ kũmanya vala tũtonya kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu Mbivilianĩ.
Nĩ kana tũtetheesye andũ kũkwata mosũngĩo, tũtũmĩaa ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? yĩla yĩ na mathangũ 224. * Ĩvuku yĩu yaseũviw'e kwa nzĩa ya mwanya nĩ kana yĩtetheesye andũ kũelewa momanyĩsyo ma mũsingi ma Mbivilia. Ĩvuku yĩu yĩthĩawa na masomo ĩũlũ wa Ngai, Yesũ Klĩsto, mathĩna ala makwataa andũ, ũthayũũkyo, mboya, na maũndũ angĩ maingĩ.
Mũndũ atonya kwĩmanyĩĩsya va, na ĩndĩĩ?
Mũndũ nũtonya kũsakũa saa, na vandũ vala ũkwenda kwĩmanyĩĩsya.
Mũndũ akuaa ndatĩka siana ata kwĩmanyĩsya?
Andũ aingĩ matũmĩaa ĩsaa yĩmwe, kana o mbeange kĩla kyumwa nĩ kana memanyĩsye Mbivilia. Ĩndĩ mũndũ no anyuve ndatĩka ila ũkwenda kwĩmanyĩsya. Tũkeetĩkĩlana na ĩvinda yĩla wanyuva kũtũmĩa. Amwe memanyĩasya kwa ndatĩka 10 kana 15 kĩla kyumwa.
Mũndũ aĩvaa mbesa siana ata nĩ kana amanyĩw'e?
Twĩmanyĩasya na mũndũ vate ndĩvi, na mavuku ala tũtũmĩaa mayĩĩvĩawa. Ũndũ ũsu wosanĩte nesa vyũ na ndeto ii Yesũ watavisye amanyĩw'a make: "Nĩmwosete mana, nenganai mana."—Mathayo 10:8.
Mũndũ akuaa ĩvinda yĩana ata aimina kwĩmanyĩsya?
No ũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kwa ĩvinda yĩla ũkwenda. Ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? yĩthĩawa na masomo 19. No ũnyuve ĩsomo yĩla ũkwenda, kana ũkanyuva kwĩmanyĩsya masomo onthe kwĩanana na ũtonyi waku.
No nginya mũndũ atw'ĩke Ngũsĩ ya Yeova eemanyĩsya?
Aiee. Nĩtũnengete ndaĩa ũthasyo wa kĩla mũndũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa kĩla ũkwenda kũĩkĩĩa. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, andũ ala makwata ũmanyi wa mũsingi wa Mbivilia no meke ũtwi ũla waĩle.
Nĩ va ndonya kũkwata ũvoo mwingangĩ?
Kĩsese kitũ kya jw.org/kam nĩkĩthĩawa na ũvoo wa w'o wa maũndũ ala tũĩkĩĩaa, na maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
Naĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana nĩmanyĩw'e Mbivilia?
Kũlya ũmanyĩw'e Mbivilia Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam.

translation:
We are encouraged by Jehovah's organization to share good news. Would we like to see whether we can associate with more people by means of Bible studies?
In 2014, there were 8,000,000 of Jehovah's Witnesses in some 240 lands, and each month they conducted over 9,500,000 Bible studies. * Imagine how many more people we could help learn about the Bible if each of us had at least 140 studies!
As the work of making disciples continues, Jehovah's organization provides Bibles, publications, videos, and other tools to help people study the Bible—over 1.5 billion items, including 700 tons each year! This provision of literature helps many people to learn about the Bible and to progress spiritually.
QUESTIONS TO HELP YOU IMPROVE YOUR DISCIPLING WORK
Is this disciple-making work satisfying to you?
We review lessons carefully, and we highlight scriptures that support what we learn from the lesson. For example, the Bible answers questions such as: Who is God? Does God care about us? Why is there suffering? What happens when we die? And how can we find meaning in life? By knowing the answers to these important questions found in the Bible, we can help others.
If we want to help people find answers, should we use the publication Make Disciples, page 224? * That publication offers practical suggestions on how to help people understand basic Bible teachings. It discusses topics such as God, Jesus Christ, the Kingdom, morality, hope, and many other things.
Can a person respond favorably, and if so, how?
A person may be busy, and some people may not be available to make disciples.
What if a person seems uninterested?
Many people need time, or perhaps they will be more receptive another time. If a person seems uninterested, don't give up trying to reach them. Let's practice using the material. Some share for 10 or 15 minutes each visit.
What if a person does not seem interested?
We speak to people of all backgrounds, and we use publications that are appealing. This work is similar to the way Jesus sent out his disciples, saying: "Go preach the good news."—Matthew 10:8.
What if a person has little time but wants to learn?
Continue making disciples according to the time he has available. The publication Make Disciples offers 19 lessons. Review the lesson he has available, or review additional lessons based on his interests.
How can we encourage someone to take a stand for Jehovah?
Yes. We should respect the right of each individual to choose freely. However, those who have a basic understanding of Bible truth often appreciate being encouraged.
Is there something I can do to improve my ministry?
The website jw.org/kam provides helpful information and articles about our ministry, as well as information about the organization of Jehovah's Witnesses.
Where can I find more information about the Bible?
For further information about the Bible, go to www.jw.org/kam.

text:
1. Yesũ aumie va?
Kĩvathũkany'o na andũ onthe, Yesũ atwĩe ĩtunĩ e kyũmbe kya veva mbee wa kũsyawa kũũ nthĩ. (Yoana 8:23) Nĩwe woombiwe mbee nĩ Ngai, na nĩwatetheeisye kũmba syĩndũ ila ingĩ syonthe. No we e weka woombiwe nĩ Yeova ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi wĩtĩtwe Mwana wa Ngai "ũla wasyaiwe weka." (Yoana 1:14) Ĩngĩ, Yesũ aĩ Mũneeni wa Ngai, kwoou etawa "ĩla Ndeto."
2. Nĩkĩ Yesũ wookie kũũ nthĩ?
Ngai amũtũmie Mwana wake kũũ nthĩ kwa kũthamya thayũ wake kuma ĩtunĩ na kũũlikya ĩvunĩ ya mwĩĩtu Mũyuti weetawa Meli ũteesĩ mũndũũme. Kwoou, Yesũ ndaĩ na ĩthe wa kĩmũndũ. (Luka 1:30-35) Yesũ ookie kũũ nthĩ nĩ kana (1) amanyĩsye ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai, (2) atũtĩie ngelekany'o ya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai o na ĩla twĩ mathĩnanĩ, na (3) anengane thayũ wake mwĩanĩu wĩthĩwe "wovosyo."
3. Nĩkĩ twĩ na vata wa wovosyo?
Wovosyo nĩ ndĩvi ĩla yumaw'a nĩ kana mũndũ athaw'e ndakoawe. (Kuma 21:29, 30) Kuma mwambĩlĩlyonĩ kĩyaĩ kĩeleelo kya Ngai mũndũ akũe na aikw'a. Twĩsĩ ũu ata? Ngai eeie mũndũ wa mbee, Atamu, ĩla wĩĩka kĩla Mbivilia ĩkĩtaa "naĩ," akakw'a. Kwoou, kethwa Atamu ndaaĩka naĩ, ndethwa aakw'a. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:16, 17; 5:5) Kwosana na Mbivilia, kĩkw'ũ 'kyalikile' kũũ nthĩ kwĩsĩla Atamu. Kwoou, Atamu atiĩa nzyawa syake syonthe naĩ na ĩtuvi ya naĩ, yĩla nĩ kĩkw'ũ. Twĩ na vata wa wovosyo nĩ kana ũtũvetee ĩtuvi yĩu twatiĩwe nĩ Atamu.
Nũũ ũla waĩ atonya kũtũĩvĩa wovosyo wa kũtũthasya kuma kĩkw'ũnĩ? Ĩla twakw'a, twĩthĩawa twaĩvĩa mavĩtyo maitũ ene. Vaiĩ mũndũ ũte mwĩanĩu ũtonya kũĩvĩa mavĩtyo ma mũndũ ũngĩ.
4. Yesũ akwie nĩkĩ?
Kĩvathũkany'o naitũ, Yesũ aĩ mwĩanĩu. Kwoou ndaĩ atonya kũkw'a kwondũ wa naĩ syake nũndũ ndaavĩtya. Ĩndĩ, Yesũ akwie nũndũ wa naĩ sya angĩ. Ngai oonisye andũ wendo mwingĩ vyũ kwa kũmũtũma Mwana wake akw'e kwondũ witũ. Ĩngĩ, Yesũ oonanisye nũtwendete kwa kwĩw'a Ĩthe wake na kũkw'a kwondũ wa naĩ sitũ.
5. Ũmũnthĩ Yesũ aendee kwĩka ata?
Ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ, Yesũ nĩwavoisye awau, athayũũkya akw'ũ, na athũmũsya andũ kuma thĩnanĩ. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu nĩwoonanisye maũndũ ala ũkeka kwondũ wa onthe ala ewi ĩvinda yũkĩte. (Mathayo 15:30, 31; Yoana 5:28) Ĩla Yesũ wakwie, Ngai nĩwamũthayũũkisye na amũnenga mwĩĩ wa veva. (1 Vetelo 3:18) Na ĩndĩ Yesũ ekala kw'okonĩ kwa aũme kwa Ngai eteele nginya Yeova amũnenge ũkũmũ wa kũsumbĩka nthĩ yonthe. (Aevelania 10:12, 13) Ũmũnthĩ Yesũ nũsumbĩkĩte ĩtunĩ e Mũsumbĩ, na aatĩĩi make maendee kũmanyĩthya ũvoo ũsu mũseo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe.
O mĩtũkĩ, Yesũ akatũmĩa ũkũmũ wake e Mũsumbĩ kũveta mathĩna onthe vamwe na ala mamaetae. Onthe ala mamũĩkĩĩa kwa kũmwĩw'a makatanĩa thayũ valatisonĩ kũũ nthĩ.

translation:
1. Did Jesus exist before?
Jesus spoke to the crowds, saying: "I come from above, I am not from this world." (John 8:23) He was sent by God, and he did not hold back anything, but told them everything. But you who are from above are not from above; you are from here below. And that is why you cannot understand what I say." (John 1:14) Indeed, Jesus is God's only-begotten Son, whom he lovingly calls "my beloved Son."
2. How did Jesus come to be?
God sent his Son to earth to demonstrate his love for mankind and to deliver people from the power of death. Therefore, Jesus had a perfect human life. (Luke 1:30-35) Jesus came to be through (1) God transferring his life force, (2) giving him a perfect body so that he could live according to God's will and be a righteous man, and (3) uniting his life with that of "the firstborn."
3. What does being a firstborn mean?
A firstborn is the first child born to a family. (Proverbs 21:29, 30) In ancient times, the firstborn son received special privileges. Is this true today? God allowed Adam, the first man, to disobey, and he became imperfect. So, when Adam disobeyed, he passed on imperfection. (Genesis 2:16, 17; 5:5) Just as Adam passed on imperfection, all humans inherit sin because of Adam. Being a firstborn means inheriting the life that was transferred to Adam.
But can anyone benefit from the transfer of life that would restore us to perfection? If we obey, we can receive benefits from our faith. Everyone needs help from another person.
4. What will Jesus do?
Jesus is perfect. So he can give what he has to others. However, Jesus gave himself to be a ransom for all people. God loved mankind so much that he sent his Son to be a ransom for us. Also, Jesus showed love for us by giving up his life and giving himself to be a ransom for us.
5. Why did Jesus come to earth?
He came to teach people about God's Kingdom, to demonstrate what it means to live according to God's laws, and to comfort people who were suffering. He performed miracles showing God's power and compassion. (Matthew 15:30, 31; John 5:28) But Jesus also died, and God resurrected him and glorified him in heaven. (1 Peter 3:18) And now Jesus sits at God's right hand, waiting until Jehovah appoints the time to gather all things together. (Hebrews 10:12, 13) Jesus completed his work in Heaven, and his accomplishments will continue to bring glory to God throughout eternity.
My brothers, Jesus sends his spirit to Heaven to help all nations and all people. All those who seek him find comfort and peace through him.

text:
1. Nĩkĩ twĩ na vata wa kũtongoew'a?
Mũmbi witũ nĩ mũĩ kwĩ ithyĩ. Nĩ Ĩthe wĩ wendo, kwoou nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa. Ĩngĩ, kĩyaĩ kĩeleelo kyake twĩtongoesye. (Yelemia 10:23) Kwoou, o tondũ syana nini syĩthĩawa na vata wa kũtongoew'a nĩ asyai, ithyonthe twĩ na vata wa kũtongoew'a nĩ Ngai. (Isaia 48:17, 18) Myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩtũnengae ũtongoi, ũla nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai.
Mĩao na myolooto ya Yeova ĩtũmanyĩasya mwĩkalĩle ũla mũseo vyũ ũmũnthĩ na nĩtwonasya ũndũ tũtonya kũkwata moathimo ma ĩvinda yũkĩte matakathela. Nũndũ Ngai nĩwe watũmbie, nĩ ũndũ waĩle kũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa ũtongoi wake wĩ wendo na kũatĩĩa mĩao na myolooto yake twĩ na ũtanu.
2. Myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩ myaũ?
Myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩ ũw'o wa mũsingi. Nayo mĩao nĩtonya kũtũmĩwa kũweta ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe ũndũ twaĩle nĩkwĩka. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 22:8) No nginya tũtũmĩe ũtonyi witũ wa kũtũmĩa kĩlĩko nĩ kana tũelewe ũndũ mwolooto mũna ũũtwĩa twĩke kwosana na ũndũ mũna. (Nthimo 2:10-12) Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana thayũ nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai. Mwolooto ũsu nũtonya kũtũtongoesya ĩla twĩ mũsyĩ, wĩanĩ, kana kyalonĩ. Nũtumaa twĩsũvĩa tũikalike mũisyonĩ kana kũlikya angĩ.
3. Nĩ myolooto ĩlĩ yĩva ĩla ya vata vyũ?
Yesũ nĩwawetie myolooto ĩlĩ ya vata mũno. Wa mbee wonanĩtye kĩeleelo kya thayũ, nakyo nĩ kũmũmanya Ngai, kũmwenda, na kũmũthũkũma kwa ũĩkĩĩku. Mwolooto ũsu nĩwaĩle kũsũanĩĩawa ĩvinda yonthe ĩla tũũtw'a maũndũ. (Nthimo 3:6) Ala maatĩĩaa mwolooto ũsu nĩmethĩawa na ũnyanya na Ngai, ũtanu wa w'o, na thayũ ũtathela.
Mwolooto wa kelĩ nũtonya kũtuma twĩthĩwa na mũamba mũseo na andũ ala angĩ. (1 Akolintho 13:4-7) Ũndũ ũmwe wonanasya kana nĩtũkwataa mwolooto ũsu wa kelĩ nĩ kwĩka andũ o tondũ Ngai ũmekaa.
4. Myolooto ya Mbivilia ĩtũtethasya ata?
Myolooto ya Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ũndũ mũsyĩ ũtonya kũkwatanw'a nĩ wendo. (Akolosai 3:12-14) Ĩngĩ Ndeto ya Ngai nĩsũvĩaa mĩsyĩ kwa kũmanyĩsya mwolooto ũngĩ wa kana mũtwaano nĩ mũvango wa kwĩkala.
Kwa kũatĩĩa momanyĩsyo ma Mbivilia, nĩkũtonya kũtũsũvĩa maũndũnĩ ma kĩmwĩĩ na makonetye kĩlĩko. Kwa ngelekany'o, mavinda maingĩ aandĩkani nĩmendeeaw'a nĩ athũkũmi ala maatĩĩaa myolooto ya Mbivilia ya kwĩthĩwa me na kĩthito na me aĩkĩĩku. (Nthimo 10:4, 26; Aevelania 13:18) Ĩngĩ, Ndeto ya Ngai nĩtũmanyĩasya kwĩanĩawa nĩ syĩndũ ila sya lasima na kwosa ũnyanya witũ na Ngai ta w'o ũndũ wa vata kũthonoka syĩndũ sya kĩmwĩĩ.
Kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩkũtonya kũsũvĩa ũima witũ wa mwĩĩ. (Nthimo 14:30; 22:24, 25) Kwa ngelekany'o, kũatĩĩa mwĩao wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa ũnywi nĩkũtũsũvĩaa tũikakwatwe nĩ mĩisyo na mowau mathũku. (Nthimo 23:20) Yeova nũtwĩtĩkĩlĩtye kũnyw'a mbinyu, ĩndĩ kwa kĩthimo. (Savuli 104:15; 1 Akolintho 6:10) Myolooto ya Ngai ĩtũtethasya kwa kũtũmanyĩsya tũsũvĩe meko na mesilya maitũ. (Savuli 119:97-100) Ĩndĩ, Aklĩsto ma w'o mainengae myolooto ya Ngai ndaĩa atĩ nũndũ nĩmatethasya. Mekaa ũu nĩ kana mamũtaĩe Yeova.

translation:
1. Should we direct our steps?
Our Creator knows what is right. He is a loving God, who cares deeply about us. Therefore, let us harmonize our steps with his will. (Jeremiah 10:23) Indeed, what could be more beneficial than being guided by Jehovah's direction, for Jehovah is God. (Isaiah 48:17, 18) The Bible's counsel helps us to live in harmony with God's standards.
Jehovah's laws and principles teach us how to live in a way that pleases him and help us to make decisions that are in line with his righteous requirements. Because God supports us, we can trust in his loving guidance and appreciate his laws and principles with joy.
2. What are Bible principles?
Bible principles are fundamental truths. They enable us to apply wisdom to everyday situations. (Proverbs 22:8) So we should use our discernment to determine how a principle applies to a specific situation. (Psalm 2:10-12) For example, the Bible teaches that honesty is pleasing to God. This principle can help us to avoid lying, stealing, or cheating. It motivates us to be sincere and honest in all our dealings.
3. What is the most important principle?
Jesus emphasized the most important principle. It is to love God, to cherish him, and to worship him exclusively. This principle enables us to have a good relationship with God throughout our life. (Psalm 3:6) But to practice this principle, we need to cultivate a close bond with God, faith in him, and appreciation for his qualities.
This principle also helps us to show love and kindness to others. (1 Corinthians 13:4-7) One way to demonstrate that we value this principle is to treat people as God treats them.
4. Does the Bible offer practical guidance?
The Bible offers practical guidance on how to live with love. (Colossians 3:12-14) Also, God's law encourages us to develop moral qualities and to apply Bible principles skillfully. For instance, many individuals find comfort in Bible accounts about faithful men and women who demonstrated Bible principles in their lives. (Psalm 10:4, 26; Hebrews 13:18) Furthermore, God's law helps us to avoid harmful influences and to maintain our spiritual health.
Applying Bible principles can help us improve the quality of our life. (Proverbs 14:30; 22:24, 25) For example, obeying God's command to be moderate in eating and drinking can save us from being burdened down with worries and anxieties. (Proverbs 23:20) Jehovah kindly provides wine to gladden our hearts, but in moderation. (Psalm 104:15; 1 Corinthians 6:10) God's wisdom guides us in making wise decisions and avoiding foolish pursuits. (Psalm 119:97-100) Therefore, Christians who appreciate God's law realize its benefits. It truly is a delight to meditate on Jehovah's law.

EKA tũsyoke ĩtina myaka mĩvũthũ mbee wa Esala kũthi Yelusaleme. Molitekai na Esita nĩmo Aisilaeli ala maĩ anene vyũ ũsumbĩnĩ wa Avelisia. Esita aĩ kĩveti kya mũsumbĩ, nake Molitekai, mwana wa mũndũ wasyaanĩw'e na ĩthe wa Esita, nĩwe watĩĩe mũsumbĩ nthĩnĩ wa ũsumbĩki. Ekai twone ũu weethĩiwe ata.
Asyai ma Esita makw'ie e mũnini mũno, na kwoou Molitekai nĩwe wamũeie. Aasuelo, mũsumbĩ wa Velisia, aĩ na nyũmba ya ũsumbĩ ndũanĩ ya Susani, na Molitekai aĩ ũmwe wa athũkũmi make. Mũthenya ũmwe Vasiti, mũka wa mũsumbĩ, nĩwaleile kũmwĩw'a, kwoou mũsumbĩ anyuva mũndũ mũka ũngĩ atw'ĩke mũka wake. We nĩwĩsĩ anyuvie ũũ? Anyuvie Esita mũndũ mũka mwanake.
We nĩwene mũndũ ũũ wĩ na mĩyono andũ meũmũkumanĩa? Ũũ nĩ Amani. Amani aĩ mũndũ mũnene mũno kũu nthĩ ya Velisia. Amani endaa Molitekai, ũũ ũkwona ekalite vaa nthĩ, o nake amũkumanĩe. Ĩndĩ Molitekai alea. We ndoonaa kwaĩlĩte kũkumanĩa mũndũ mũthũku ta ũsu. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie Amani athilĩka mũno. Na ũũ nĩw'o weekie.
Amani nĩwatavisye mũsumbĩ ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa Aisilaeli. We aisye: 'Asu nĩ andũ athũkũ o na mayĩw'aa mĩao yaku. Maĩlĩte kũawa.' Aasuelo ndeesĩ kana mũka wake Esita aĩ Mũisilaeli. Kwoou amwĩthukĩĩsya Amani, na asya mwĩao nũtuw'e, na mũthenya mũna mũnyuve Aisilaeli onthe mayũawa.
Yĩla Molitekai weewie ĩũlũ wa mwĩao ũsu, eew'a woo mũno. Nake atũmana kwa Esita amwĩa: 'No nginya ũmũtavye mũsumbĩ, noimwĩsũva atũtaangĩĩe.' Waĩ ũndũ ũtoosanĩte na mĩao ya Velisia kũthi ũkone mũsumbĩ ate o wĩmũthokye. Ĩndĩ Esita nĩwaendie atemũthokye. Na mũsumbĩ amũkĩlĩlya ndata yake ya thaavu, kwonany'a kana ndeũawa. Esita nĩwathokisye mũsumbĩ na Amani mbokanĩ nene. Na me vau mũsumbĩ akũlya Esita eenda amũnenge kyaũ. Esita amwĩa kana akamũtavya ethĩwa we na Amani makooka mbokanĩ ĩngĩ mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe.
Me mbokanĩ ĩsu Esita nĩwamwĩie mũsumbĩ ũũ: 'Andũ makwa nakwa nĩtũkũawa.' Nake Mũsumbĩ athilĩka na akũlya: 'Nũũ ũsu ũkwenda kwĩka ũndũ ta ũsu?'
Nake Esita asya: 'Ũ mũndũ, nĩ nthũ ĩno, nĩ Amani ũũ mũthũku!'
Yu ĩndĩ mũsumbĩ athilĩka vyũ. Na eeĩaa Amani oawe. Ĩtina wa ũu, mũsumbĩ nĩwamũtwie Molitekai mũndũ wa kelĩ ũsumbĩnĩ. Na ĩndĩ Molitekai aĩkĩĩthya kana mwĩao mweũ nĩwaseũvw'a wa kũmatonyethya Aisilaeli kwĩtetea mũthenya ũla maaĩlĩte kũawa. Na nũndũ Molitekai aĩ mũndũ mũnene ũsumbĩnĩ, andũ aingĩ nĩmamatetheeisye Aisilaeli, namo Aisilaeli mavonokw'a kuma kwa amaitha moo.
Ĩvuku ya Mbivilia ya Esita.
Makũlyo
- Molitekai na Esita naaũ?
- Nĩkĩ Mũsumbĩ Aasuelo wendie kũtwaa kĩveti kĩngĩ, nake anyuvie ũũ?
- Amani nũũ, na nĩ kyaũ kyamũthatĩtye mũno?
- Nĩ mwĩao mwaũ waseũviw'e, na Esita eekie ata akwata ũtũmani kuma kwa Molitekai?
- Kweethĩiwe ata kwa Amani, na kwa Molitekai?
- Aisilaeli matangĩĩiwe ata kuma kwa amaitha moo?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Esita 2:12-18.
Esita oonanisye ata vata wa kwĩthĩwa na "veva wa wĩnyivyo na ũuu"? (Est. 2:15; 1 Vet. 3:1-5)
- Soma Esita 4:1-17.
O tondũ Esita wakwatie mwanya wa kũtetea ũthaithi wa w'o, ithyĩ twĩ na mwanya mwaũ wa kwonany'a kwĩyumya na kwĩkwatany'a na Yeova? (Est. 4:13, 14; Mt. 5:14-16; 24:14)
- Soma Esita 7:1-6.
O tondũ Esita weekie, ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ ma Ngai mekaa ata yĩla meũthĩnw'a? (Est. 7:4; Mt. 10:16-22; 1 Vet. 2:12)

translation:
One day Jesus went up to Jerusalem during the Passover festival. He and his disciples went on to Bethany. Esther was an Israelite woman, and she had a large courtyard belonging to Avelisia. Esther did not have a courtyard, but Molitekai, the son of a man who was honored by Esther, built the courtyard for her. This is what we have heard about it.
It happened that Esther was sitting in the upper room, and they sent Molitekai to go and see her. Asuelo, the courtyard keeper of Velisia, had a house near Susani, and Molitekai was one of his servants. One day Vasiti, the wife of the courtyard keeper, ordered him to bring her, saying the courtyard keeper should send his wife to her. Why would he send her? He sent Esther, his wife.
Who is this man who has connections with influential people? This is Amani. Amani was a very important man in the land of Velisia. Amani visited Molitekai, and he saw how beautiful she was, or he knew her well. Then Molitekai left. Why does it seem difficult to know a good person? Your situation has sent Amani to visit you greatly. And this is what he did.
Amani appointed the courtyard keeper over all the land of Israel. He said, "These are the servants and their families. Go and gather them." Asuelo realized that his wife Esther was an Israelite. So he praised Amani, and he sent his family away, and the next day all the Israelites gathered their families.
Then Molitekai came to his family, and he brought them together. And he sent for Esther and told her, "I will not appoint a courtyard keeper unless you agree to let us rebuild it." But this matter concerned the lands of Velisia, so that the courtyard could be rebuilt, but he refused. And Esther went to refuse him. And the courtyard keeper remembered his past deeds, knowing that he had been rewarded. Esther refused the courtyard keeper and Amani greatly, and they both ate food with Esther, and Esther told him that if he and Amani were to come again another day when he had appointed [someone], she would refuse him.
They both agreed, and Esther said to the courtyard keeper, "My people and I will be gathered." And the Courtyard Keeper replied, "What is your purpose in doing this?"
And Esther said, "This man, this is Amani, a great man!"
So the courtyard keeper thought about it. And he honored Amani. Because of this, the courtyard keeper sent Molitekai, a man who knew the courtyard well. And because Molitekai saw that his family was being used to deceive the Israelites and prevent them from gathering their families, and because Molitekai was a great man in the courtyard, many Israelites trusted him, and the Israelites did not go to the places where they were supposed to go.
The story of Esther's Bible.
Questions
- Did Molitekai and Esther agree?
- Why did the Courtyard Keeper Asuelo want to take another position, and why did he refuse to do so?
- What about Amani, and what made him so important?
- Was his family deceived, and did Esther do anything to send them to Molitekai?
- What happened to Amani, and to Molitekai?
- Were the Israelites deceived to go to those places?
More questions
- Read Esther 2:12-18.
Did Esther ever wonder what it meant to be called "beautiful and graceful"? (Est. 2:15; 1 Chron. 3:1-5)
- Read Esther 4:1-17.
Since Esther took the opportunity to defend her people, how can we use our opportunity to shine brightly and associate with Jehovah? (Est. 4:13, 14; Matt. 5:14-16; 24:14)
- Read Esther 7:1-6.
Since Esther spoke up, does it show that many of God's people will always find a way to speak up? (Est. 7:4; Matt. 10:16-22; 1 Chron. 2:12)

OMĨTHENYA ĩendee na kũvĩta, Yesũ nĩweeyonanisye kwa aatĩĩi make mavinda maingĩ. Ĩvinda yĩmwe amanyĩw'a ta 500 nĩmamwonie. Amaumĩlĩĩla, we nĩwĩsĩ Yesũ aneenie namo ĩũlũ wa kyaũ? Ĩũlũ wa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Yeova atũmie Yesũ kũũ nthĩ kũmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ ũsu. Na nĩwaendeeie na kwĩka ũu o na ĩtina wa kũthayũũkw'a.
We nũũlilikana ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ kyaũ? Ũsumbĩ nĩ silikalĩ ya w'o ya Ngai yĩ ĩtunĩ, na Yesũ nĩwe Ngai ũnyũvĩte ethĩwe mũsumbĩ. O tondũ tũminĩte kwĩmanyĩsya, Yesũ nĩwoonanisye ũndũ ũkethĩwa e mũsumbĩ mũseo kwa kũmanenga lĩu andũ me na nzaa, kũvosya awau, o na kũthayũũkya akw'ũ!
Kwoou yĩla Yesũ wĩsumbĩka ĩtunĩ kwa myaka ngili, nthĩ ĩkeethĩwa ĩilyĩ ata? Nthĩ yonthe ĩkatw'ĩkĩthw'a Valatiso mbanake. Kũikethĩwa ĩngĩ makaũ, ũtũli wa mĩao, ũwau, kana o na kĩkw'ũ. Nĩtwĩsĩ ũu nũndũ Ngai oombie nthĩ yĩthĩwe yĩ Valatiso ya andũ matanĩae. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi mwambĩlĩlyonĩ waseũvisye mũũnda wa Eteni. Na Yesũ akaĩkĩĩthya kana ũndũ Ngai ũnũkwenda wĩkwe nĩweanĩw'a vyũ.
Ĩvinda nĩyavikie ĩndĩ Yesũ asyoke ĩtunĩ. Kwa mĩthenya 40 Yesũ eethĩĩtwe ayĩyonany'a kwa amanyĩw'a make. Kwoou mena w'o ki kana we e thayũ ĩngĩ. Ĩndĩ mbee wa kũmatia amanyĩw'a make Yesũ ameie: 'Ĩkalai Yelusaleme nginya yĩla mũkosa veva mũtheu.' Veva mũtheu nĩ vinya wa Ngai, ũilyĩ ta kĩseve kĩuutanĩte, naw'o ũtetheeasya aatĩĩi make kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Ĩtina vyũ, Yesũ nĩwaisye: 'Mũkatavany'a ĩũlũ wakwa kũvika ilungu syĩ vaasa sya nthĩ.'
Ĩtina wa kwasya ũu, ũndũ wa ũsengy'a nĩweekĩkie. Yesũ nĩwambĩĩie kwambata ĩtunĩ, o tondũ ũkwona vaa. Na ĩtu yamũvw'ĩka aeka kwoneka, na amanyĩw'a mayaamwona ĩngĩ. Yĩla Yesũ waendie ĩtunĩ nĩwambĩlĩĩilye kũsumbĩka aatĩĩi make ala me ĩũlũ wa nthĩ kuma kũu.
1 Akolintho 15:3-8; Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4; Meko 1:1-11.
Makũlyo
- Nĩ amanyĩw'a meana mamwonie Yesũ ĩvinda yĩmwe, nake aneenie namo ĩũlũ wa kyaũ?
- Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ kyaũ, na thayũ ũkeethĩwa ũilyĩ ata ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yĩla Yesũ ũkasumbĩka kwa myaka ngili?
- Yesũ ethĩĩtwe ayumĩlĩla amanyĩw'a make kwa mĩthenya yĩana, ĩndĩ yu nĩ ĩvinda yake ya kwĩka ata?
- Kavinda kanini mbee wa kũtia amanyĩw'a make, Yesũ ameie nĩmeke ata?
- Nĩ kyaũ kĩĩkĩka vaa visanĩ, na Yesũ evithwa ata aeke kwoneka?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma 1 Akolintho 15:3-8.
Nĩkĩ mũtũmwa Vaulo waneenie na ũĩkĩĩku vyũ ĩũlũ wa kũthayũũkw'a kwa Yesũ, naitũ ũmũnthĩ tũtonya kũneena na ũĩkĩĩku ĩũlũ wa maũndũ meva? (1 Ako. 15:4, 7, 8; Isa. 2:2, 3; Mt. 24:14; 2 Tim. 3:1-5)
- Soma Meko 1:1-11.
O tondũ ĩandĩko ya Meko 1:8 yonanĩtye, wĩa wa kũtavany'a wanyaĩĩkie nginya va? (Meko 6:7; 9:31; 11:19-21; Ako. 1:23)

translation:
My heart yearns and trembles, Jesus has reconciled me through his many sacrifices. One sacrifice was worth over 500 lives. But truly, why should I praise Jesus and seek God's kingdom? It is the kingdom of God's righteousness. Jehovah sent Jesus to earth to show me this righteousness. And I will continue to preach this good news with zeal.
How can we experience God's righteousness? Righteousness is God's standard of perfection, and Jesus is the perfect God who fulfilled it. Therefore, when we want to learn, Jesus showed us the way to fulfill this righteousness by forgiving sins, saving people, and perfecting them!
Why did Jesus demonstrate righteousness perfectly for so many years, and what does it mean for us today? All of this was done for the benefit of future generations. To fulfill more purposes, such as life, salvation, or even blessings. We know that God wants this to be inherited by those who believe in the restoration of mankind. This is why he commissioned Moses to write the book of Genesis. And Jesus will accomplish whatever God desires to do through him.
The sacrifice applies to Jesus as soon as it is made. For 40 days Jesus was tempted by his enemies. Why then did he endure more suffering? In order to prove his loyalty to God, Jesus said: "Go to Jerusalem and prepare the way for my coming." Preparing the way is God's command, which is like a decree that directs his sacrifices to align with God's will. Furthermore, Jesus said: "Do not hinder the kingdom until the time comes for its completion."
After this event, the matter of obedience became clear. Jesus commanded them to wait in Galilee, even though they were afraid. And the promise was fulfilled, and his disciples saw more. As Jesus went to Galilee, he reminded them to spread the good news throughout the earth.
1 Corinthians 15:3-8; Acts 21:3, 4; Mark 1:1-11.
Questions
- What did the disciples see when Jesus demonstrated righteousness, and how can we learn from their example?
- What is the significance of God's righteousness, and how does it relate to our inheritance of eternal life through Jesus' perfect demonstration?
- Why did Jesus patiently endure temptation for forty days, and what does this reveal about his commitment to God?
- What message did Jesus convey when he instructed his disciples to prepare the way, and what does it mean for us today?
- What is the importance of waiting for God's timing, and how did Jesus exemplify patience in his ministry?
Further Questions
- Read 1 Corinthians 15:3-8.
How did Paul explain the importance of faith in Jesus' resurrection, and how can we apply this understanding to our lives? (1 Cor. 15:4, 7, 8; Isa. 2:2, 3; Matt. 24:14; 2 Tim. 3:1-5)
- Read Mark 1:1-11.
According to Mark 1:8, what is the meaning of John the Baptist's proclamation, and how does it connect to the arrival of Jesus? (Mark 6:7; 9:31; 11:19-21; Acts 1:23)

text:
Nĩkĩ maũndũ ala Mathayo na Luka maandĩkie ĩũlũ wa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ na myaka yake ya mbee matavw'anene?
Mathayo na Luka mawetete maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ na myaka yake ya mbee kũũ nthĩ nũndũ Mathayo aeleetye mũno maũndũ ala makonetye Yosevu, nake Luka aeleetye mũno maũndũ ala makonetye Meli.
Ĩvuku ya Mathayo yonanĩtye ũndũ Yosevu weekie eewa Meli nĩ mũito, yĩkaelesya ndoto ĩla waotie aitavw'a nĩ mũlaĩka kĩla kĩendeeie Meli aikaatw'ĩka nĩwaitava, na yĩkaweta ĩtambya yĩla woosie atavw'a ũu. (Mt. 1:19-25) Ĩtina wa ũu nĩyĩwetete ndoto ĩla Yosevu waotie mũlaĩka aimwĩa akĩĩe Misili, na yĩkaweta ũndũ wakĩĩie nthĩ ĩsu na andũ make. O na nĩyĩwetete ayĩwa nĩ mũlaĩka ndotonĩ asyoke Isilaeli, yĩkaweta ũndũ wasyokie, na mũthya ũtwi ũla weekie wa kũthamĩĩsya andũ make Nasaleti. (Mt. 2:13, 14, 19-23) Ilungunĩ sya mbee ilĩ sya Mathayo, ĩsyĩtwa ya Yosevu yĩwetetwe mavinda mũonza, ĩndĩ ya Meli yĩwetetwe mavinda o ana.
Nayo ĩvuku ya Luka yĩwetete ĩla Meli wathokeiwe nĩ mũlaĩka Kavilieli, ĩla waendie kwona Elisavethi, na ndeto ila waneenie aimũtaĩa Yeova. (Luka 1:26-56) O na nĩyĩwetete kĩla Simeoni watavisye Meli ĩũlũ wa mathĩna ala maĩ makwate Yesũ. O na Luka nũwetete ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ na asyai make maendie ĩkalũnĩ e wa myaka 12, na akaweta ndeto ila Meli waneenie ĩvinda yĩu ĩndĩ ndawetete ndeto sya Yosevu. Luka ongelete kũweta kana Meli nĩwakiitiwe mũno nĩ maũndũ asu. (Luka 2:19, 34, 35, 48, 51) Ilungunĩ sya mbee ilĩ sya Luka, ĩsyĩtwa ya Meli yĩwetetwe mavinda 12, ĩndĩ ya Yosevu yĩwetetwe mavinda 3 tũ. Kwoou Mathayo aeleetye mũno mũno ĩũlũ wa Yosevu na kĩla weekie, nake Luka aneeneete mũno mũno kĩanda kĩla Meli weanĩisye na maũndũ ala mamũkwatie.
Kĩvathũkany'o kĩngĩ kĩlikĩte nũndũ Mathayo aandĩkie andũ ma ũko wa Yesũ ala maĩ ngalĩko ya Yosevu, nake Luka aandĩkie ala maĩ ngalĩko ya Meli. Mathayo awetie andũ ma ũko wa Yosevu nĩ kana aĩkĩĩthye kana kwosana na mĩao Yesũ nĩwe waaĩle kwĩkalĩla kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya Ndaviti nũndũ aeiwe nĩ Yosevu. Na ũu nĩ w'o nũndũ Yosevu aĩ nzyawa ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti kwĩsĩla vala ve Solomoni, ũla waĩ mwana wa Ndaviti. (Mt. 1:6, 16) Luka nake awetete andũ ma ũko wa Meli nĩ kenda aĩkĩĩthye kana Yesũ aĩ nzyawa ya Ndaviti na kwoou nĩwaaĩle kũtiĩwa kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya Ndaviti "kwondũ wa mwĩĩ." (Alo. 1:3) Na ũu nĩ w'o nũndũ Meli aĩ nzyawa ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti kwĩsĩla vala ve Nathani, ũla waĩ mwana wa Ndaviti. (Luka 3:31) Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ Luka ũtaaweta kana Meli nĩ mwĩĩtu wa Eli aitalany'a andũ ma ũko wa Yesũ? Kĩtumi nũndũ kwosana na mĩao ĩla masyĩtwa ma ũko mũna meũtalanw'a aũme nĩmo makothaa kũwetwa. Kwoou ĩla Luka waandĩkie kana Yosevu nĩ mwana wa Eli, andũ nĩmakwatisye endaa kwasya Yosevu atwaĩte mwĩĩtu wa Eli.—Luka 3:23.
Masyĩtwa ala Mathayo na Luka maandĩkie ma ũko wa Yesũ maĩkĩĩthasya nesa vyũ kana Yesũ nĩwe Masia ũla wathaniwe. O na Avalisi na Asatukai mayaĩ makananĩsya kĩu nũndũ andũ nĩmeesĩ nesa vyũ Yesũ aĩ nzyawa ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti. Ũmũnthĩ, mosyaanĩo asu Mathayo na Luka maandĩkie nĩmatumaa twĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, na nĩmatũĩkĩĩthasya vyũ kana kĩla Ngai ũtwathĩte kĩkeanĩa.

translation:
Is it true that Matthew and Luke wrote about the birth and early years of Jesus with significant differences?
Matthew and Luke present different accounts regarding the birth and early years of Jesus, so much so that Matthew traces his lineage through Joseph, while Luke traces it through Heli.
The story of Matthew tells how Joseph discovered that Mary was pregnant, and he considered divorcing her, but an angel appeared to him in a dream instructing him to marry her because she would give birth to a son. (Mt. 1:19-25) Similarly, Joseph had a dream where an angel warned him to flee to Egypt with Mary and the child to escape Herod, and they remained there until Herod's death. (Mt. 2:13, 14, 19-23) In the longer account found in Matthew, Joseph's genealogy is mentioned first, whereas in Luke, Heli's genealogy is mentioned first.
However, the story of Luke recounts how Mary was visited by the angel Gabriel, who announced to her that she would conceive and bear a son, and she praised God. (Luke 1:26-56) And it also relates how Simeon blessed Mary when she brought the infant Jesus to the temple. Also, Luke describes the incident when Jesus and his parents went to Jerusalem when he was twelve years old, and Mary questioned why he stayed behind, which mirrored Joseph's earlier questioning. Luke adds details about how Mary pondered all these things in her heart. (Luke 2:19, 34, 35, 48, 51) In the longer account found in Luke, Mary's genealogy is listed with twelve ancestors, while Joseph's genealogy is listed with only three generations. Thus, Matthew provides more detail concerning Joseph and his ancestry, while Luke focuses more on Mary and the events surrounding her.
Another difference lies in how Matthew writes about Jesus' lineage through Joseph, and how Luke writes about Jesus' lineage through Mary. Matthew presents Jesus as being descended from David through Joseph, emphasizing that Jesus fulfilled the prophecies regarding the Messiah being a descendant of David. And this is why Joseph is identified as a descendant of King David through Solomon, who was David's son. (Matt. 1:6, 16) But Luke, on the other hand, presents Jesus as being descended from David through Mary, stating that he was considered the son of David "in a certain sense." (Luke 1:3) And this is because Mary is identified as a descendant of King David through Nathan, who was also David's son. (Luke 3:31) So, does Luke imply that Mary was a relative of Eli, tracing Jesus' lineage back through her family tree? The reason is that, according to some accounts, genealogies can be complex and difficult to trace accurately. Therefore, Luke states that Joseph was the son of Eli, which led people to believe that Joseph was related to Eli.—Luke 3:23.
The differing accounts given by Matthew and Luke concerning Jesus' genealogy raise questions about whether they both intended to show that Jesus was the Messiah foretold in the scriptures. However, scholars have observed that people often did not place great importance on precise genealogical details. Thus, the differences in the accounts provided by Matthew and Luke help us understand that God does not require absolute precision in such matters.

text:
WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Ĩla Julia weesisya kĩoonĩ, onaa e mũnou mũno. Atindĩaa kwasya kana eenda kũola kĩlo, o na kau asyai make na anyanyae mamwĩaa nĩ mũtheke mũno.
O mĩtũkĩ, Julia anasũanĩie ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana aole o kĩlo itatũ. Avangĩte kũeka kũya vandũ va mĩthenya yĩana ũna . . .
We keka nue Julia wĩka ata?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
Ti ũthũku kũthĩnĩka ĩũlũ wa wũmbo waku. O na Mbivilia nĩwetete ĩũlũ wa aũme na aka maĩ anake ta Sala, Lakeli, Avikaili, Yosevu, na Ndaviti. O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana mwĩĩtu weetawa Avisaki aĩ "mwanake mũno."—1 Asumbĩ 1:4.
Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ ma mũika nĩmathĩnĩkĩaa mũno vyũ wũmbo woo. Ũndũ ũsu nũtonya kũmaetee mathĩna maingĩ. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii:
Ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe woonanisye kana eĩtu 58 ĩũlũ wa 100 maasya kana me na kĩlo mbingĩ ithonokete, ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũsengy'a nĩ kana no 17 katĩ wa asu maĩ na kĩlo ithonokete.
Naw'o ũkunĩkĩli ũngĩ woonanisye kana aka 45 ĩũlũ wa 100 ala maĩ na kĩlo nini mũno maasya kana maĩ na kĩlo mbingĩ ithonokete!
Andũ amwe ma mũika nĩmawaĩte ũwau wĩtawa anorexia nũndũ wa kwĩvata lĩu kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mayenda kũola kĩlo.
Ethĩwa wĩ na thĩna ũsu wa kwĩvata lĩu nĩ kana ũole kĩlo mantha ũtethyo. No ũtavye mũsyai kana mũndũ mũima ũĩkĩĩe. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũnyanya nĩwendanaa ĩndĩ yonthe; Na mwana-a-ĩthe asyaiwe kwondũ wa kũthĩnũkasya."—Nthimo 17:17.
KĨLA WAĨLE KŨTHĨNĨKĨA MŨNO!
Ũw'o nĩ kana, ũndũ ũla ũtumaa mũndũ ethĩwa e mwanake kana ate mwanake nĩ ũndũ ũilyĩ ngoonĩ. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Avisalomu ũla waĩ mwana wa Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wake:
'Kũtyaĩ ũmwe wa kũtaĩwa mũno ta Avisalomu nũndũ wa mũmbĩle wake. Vatyaĩ kĩema nthĩnĩ wake.'—2 Samueli 14:25.
Ĩndĩ o na anakavĩte ũu, Avisalomu aĩ mũndũ wĩ mĩtũlyo, wendete monene, na nzeleke! Kwoou wasoma Mbivilia ndũmwonaa Avisalomu ta mũndũ waĩ mwanake ĩndĩ ũkwataa visa wa mũndũ ũtaĩ mũĩkĩĩku, mũaani, na waĩ kĩmena kingĩ.
Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩtũnengete ũtao ũũ mũseo:
'Ĩvw'ĩkei mũndũ mweũ.'—Akolosai 3:10.
"Kwĩseũvya kwenyu kũikethĩwe kwĩseũvya kwa ũtheinĩ . . . ; ĩndĩ nĩkwĩthĩwe mũndũ ũla ũtonekaa wa ngoo."—1 Vetelo 3:3, 4.
O na kau ti ũthũku kwenda wĩthĩwe wĩ mwanake, ũndũ ũla wa vata mũno vyũ nĩ ũndũ ũilyĩ ngoonĩ. Kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa nzeo nĩkw'o kũkatuma wĩthĩwa wĩ mũndũ wa kwendeesya, ĩndĩ ti kwĩthĩwa wĩ na vinya kana wĩ mwanake! Mwĩĩtu wĩtawa Phylicia aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwĩthĩwa wĩ mwanake no kwendeesye andũ na mĩtũkĩ, ĩndĩ kĩla makalilikanaa mũno nĩ ũndũ ũilyĩ ngoonĩ na ndaĩa nzeo ila moonie wĩ nasyo."
KWASŨANĨA ŨNDŨ ŨILYĨ
Mavinda maingĩ nĩwĩw'aa ũtekwendeew'a nĩ wũmbo waku?
We waaĩsa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kwĩvaka syĩndũ kana kũnyw'a ndawa nĩ kana wĩthĩwe wĩ mweũ?

Ethĩwa wasũngĩa ĩĩ makũlyonĩ elĩ ma mbee na wakululĩĩla maũndũ mbee wa atatũ ũndũnĩ wa katatũ, manya ũndũ ũũ: Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa ũu wonaa ũilyĩ ti w'o andũ ala angĩ monaa ũilyĩ. Nĩ laisi mũno kwĩka maũndũ ũte na kĩasi nĩ kana wanakave, kana ũkambĩĩa kũthĩnĩkĩa mũno wũmbo waku.—1 Samueli 16:7.

translation:
ARE YOU AFRAID OF DEATH?
Consider this illustration: Sister Julia was very sick, yet she remained calm. She refused to go to the hospital, and she shared her food with needy neighbors—even though she had little herself.
And so, Julia faced death without fear, perhaps because she knew she would live forever…
But how did Julia remain calm?
LET US REASON TOGETHER!
It is good to strengthen our faith. And the Bible tells us about faithful men and women such as Sarah, Rebekah, Abigail, Joseph, and David. And more than that, the Bible speaks of a man named Absalom who was called "a beautiful young man."—1 Samuel 1:4.
Many people today admire these examples of faith. This information can help us to maintain strong faith. Consider this illustration:
One study showed that 58 out of 100 people who were seriously ill and had limited resources refused treatment, while only 17 out of 100 who had ample resources refused treatment.
Also, another study showed that 45 out of 100 poor people with limited resources refused treatment!
Some people develop an eating disorder called anorexia, which causes them to refuse to eat, leading to weight loss.
However, refusing to eat is not the solution. It can lead to serious health problems. A friend may be able to help. The Bible says: "A true companion loves all the time, and is a brother in times of trouble."—Proverbs 17:17.
EVERYONE WANTS TO LIVE FOREVER!
That is why, what makes a person afraid of death or his family members dying is something that affects everyone. Consider the example of Absalom, the son of King David. The Bible describes him like this:
"As for Avisalom, his life was worth ten thousand lives."–2 Samuel 14:25.
Indeed, Avisalom was a handsome, strong, and popular man! If you read the Bible, you will see that Avisalom was a beloved son who had great influence, power, and wealth.
This is why the Bible gives us this advice:
"Become new persons."–Colossians 3:10.
"Your beauty should come from within, from the unchanging character of your heart… so that God will not be displeased with you."–1 Peter 3:3, 4.
So, if you find yourself struggling with fear about death, remember that overcoming such fears is possible. Being modest and avoiding bad company is better than being proud or associating with wrong people! A woman named Phylicia said: "Being around my family and friends helps me cope with difficult situations, because I know they care about me and support me."
CONSIDER THIS
Many young people ask themselves, 'What is the purpose of life?'
Would you be willing to give up something valuable or stop using harmful substances to improve your life?
Think carefully; what really matters to you? (Consider the questions below.)
YES
NO
MAYBE
WHAT REALLY MATTERS TO YOU
TRUTH
LOVE
GOD
Sometimes we judge others based on their appearance, just as Samuel almost did when he went to anoint a king. But remember this: God does not look at the outward appearance, but at the heart.—1 Samuel 16:7.

text:
Aaũmae ma Yesũ
(Lk 3.23-38)
1Ũũ nĩw'o ũatĩanĩo wa masyĩtwa ma aaũmae ma Yesũ Klĩsto, nzyawa ya Ndeviti, ũla nake waĩ nzyawa ya Avalaamu:
2Avalaamu asyaie Isaka, na Isaka asyaa Yakovo, na Yakovo asyaa Yuta na ana-a-ĩthe. 3Yuta asyaie Velesi na Nzela, namo inyia woo aĩ Tamalĩ. Velesi nake asyaie Esiloni, na Esiloni asyaa Lama. 4Lama asyaie Aminatavu, na Aminatavu asyaa Nasoni, na Nasoni asyaa Salimoni. 5Salimoni asyaie Mboasi ũla nyinyia aĩ Laavi, Mboasi nake asyaa Oveti ũla nyinyia aĩ Lũthi. Oveti asyaie Yese, 6Yese nake asyaa Mũsumbĩ Ndeviti.
Ndeviti asyaie Solomoni ũla nyinyia aĩ mũka wa Ulia. 7Solomoni nake asyaie Leovoamu, nake Leovoamu asyaa Aviya. Aviya asyaie Asa, 8nake Asa asyaa Yeosavati. Yeosavati asyaie Yeolamu, nake Yeolamu asyaa Usia. 9Usia asyaie Yothamu, Yothamu asyaa Aasu, na Aasu asyaa Esekia. 10Esekia asyaie Manase, nake Manase asyaa Amoni, na Amoni asyaa Yosia. 11#2Asu 24.14-15; 2Mav 36.10; Yel 27.20 Yosia asyaie Yekonia na ana-a-inyia. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu Ayuti nĩmataviwe matwawa nthĩ ya Mbavilonĩ.
12Ĩtina wa Ayuti kũtavwa na kũtwawa Mbavilonĩ, Yekonia nĩwasyaie Sealitieli, nake Sealitieli asyaa Nzelũvaveli. 13Nzelũvaveli asyaie Aviũti, nake Aviũti asyaa Eliakimu, na Eliakimu asyaa Asoli. 14Asoli asyaie Nzatoki, nake Nzatoki asyaa Akimu, na Akimu asyaa Eliũti. 15Eliũti asyaie Eleasali, nake Eleasali asyaa Mathani, na Mathani asyaa Yakovo. 16Yakovo asyaie Yosevu ũla nĩ mũũme wa Meli, inyia wa Yesũ ũla wĩtawa Klĩsto.#1.16 Klĩsto: Klĩsto nĩ ĩsyĩtwa ya ũla wanyuvĩtwe nĩ Ngai ethĩwe Mwovosya wa andũ. Kwa Kĩevelania nĩ Masia
17Kwoou ve nzyawa ĩkũmi na inya kuma Avalaamu kũvika Ndeviti, na ingĩ ĩkũmi na inya kuma Ndeviti kũvika ĩvinda yĩla Ayuti mataviwe matwawa Mbavilonĩ. O ta ũu ve nzyawa ĩkũmi na inya kuma Ayuti matavwa na kũtwawa Mbavilonĩ, kũka kũvika kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto.
Kũsyawa Kwa Yesũ Klĩsto
(Lk 2.1-7)
Lk 1.27
Kũsyawa kwa Yesũ Klĩsto kwailyĩ ta ũũ: Mwĩĩtu weetawa Meli nĩweevaĩtw'e nĩ mũndũ weetawa Yosevu, ĩndĩ matanamba kũtwaana, eethĩa nĩ mũito kwa vinya wa Veva Mũtheu. 19Ĩndĩ nĩkwĩthĩwa Yosevu aĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu, ndaaenda kwĩkĩĩthya Meli nthoni mbee wa andũ, na kwoou avanga kũmũeka avindĩtye. 20Aendee na kũsũanĩa ũu, mũlaĩka wa Mwĩai nĩwamumĩlĩĩle ndotonĩ amwĩa atĩĩ, "Yosevu, nzyawa ya Ndeviti, ndũkakĩe kũmwosa Meli atw'ĩke mũka waku. Ĩvu yĩla wĩ nayo yumanĩte na ũtonyi wa Veva Mũtheu. 21Akasyaa kavĩsĩ, na ũkaketa Yesũ, nũndũ nĩwe ũkatangĩĩa andũ kuma naĩnĩ syoo."
22Ũu w'onthe weekĩkie nĩ kana wĩanĩsye kĩla kyaneeniwe nĩ Mwĩai kwĩsĩla kwa Mwathani ayasya atĩĩ, 23#Ĩsa 7.14 "Kwa sisyai, mwĩĩtu ũtaamanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ na mũndũ-ũme akaitava na aisyaa kavĩsĩ, na kakeetwa Ĩmanueli," ũalyũlo wayo nĩ, "Ngai e vamwe naitũ."
24Yĩla Yosevu waamũkie nĩwamũtwaie Meli o ũndũ mũlaĩka wamwĩaĩĩte eke. 25#Lk 2.21 Ĩndĩ Yosevu ndaamanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ na Meli mbee wa kũsyaa kavĩsĩ, nake Yosevu aketa Yesũ.

translation:
1
The genealogy of Jesus
(Luke 3:23-38)
1This is the record of the ancestors of Jesus Christ, son of David, descendant of Abraham:
2Abraham was the father of Isaac, and Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers. 3Judah the father of Perez and Zerah, and Zerah the father of Hezron. Hezron the father of Ram, 4Ram the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon the father of Salmon. 5Salmon the father of Boaz, whose mother was Rahab, Boaz the father of Obed, whose mother was Ruth. Obed the father of Jesse, 6Jesse the father of David.
David the father of Solomon, whose mother was Bathsheba. 7Solomon the father of Rehoboam, and Rehoboam the father of Abijah. Abijah the father of Asa, 8whose father was Asa, and Asa the father of Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat the father of Jehoram. 9Jehoram the father of Uzziah, and Uzziah the father of Jotham, and Jotham the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz the father of Hezekiah. 10Hezekiah the father of Manasseh, and Manasseh the father of Ammon, and Ammon the father of Josiah. 11#2Asu 24.14-15; 2Mav 36.10; Yel 27.20 Josiah the father of Jehoiakim and his brothers. At the time of the exile to Babylon.
12After the exile to Babylon, Jehoiakim became the father of Shealtiel, and Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel. 13Zerubbabel the father of Abiud, and Abiud the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim the father of Azor. 14Azor the father of Zadok, and Zadok the father of Achim, and Achim the father of Eliud. 15Eliud the father of Eleazar, and Eleazar the father of Matthan, and Matthan the father of Jacob. 16Jacob the father of Joseph, who was the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus, who is called Christ, was born.#1.16 Christ: Christ is a name given to the one anointed by God, the Messiah. In Greek it is Messiah
17So there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, and fourteen generations from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen generations from the exile to Babylon to the birth of Christ.
The Birth of Jesus Christ
(Luke 2:1-7)
18 #
Luke 1:27
The birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way: While Mary was engaged to Joseph, she became pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19And because Joseph was a righteous man and did not want to expose her to public disgrace, he intended to divorce her quietly. 20But while he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21She will give birth to a son, and you are to give him the name Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins."
22All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: 23#Isaiah 7:14 "Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel"—which means "God with us."
24When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took Mary home as his wife. 25#Luke 2:21 And he had no relations with her until she gave birth to her firstborn son, and he named him Jesus.

text:
YESŨ nĩwathũmũĩte ũtee wa kĩthima kũya Samalia. Amanyĩw'a make maĩ manathi ndũanĩ kũũa lĩu. Mũndũ mũka ũũ Yesũ ũkũneena nake ooka kũuta kĩw'ũ. Na Yesũ emwĩa: 'Nenga kĩw'ũ nĩnyw'e.'
Ũu nĩwaseng'isye mũndũ mũka ũsu mũno. We nĩwĩsĩ nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ Yesũ nĩ Mũyuti nake nĩ Mũsamalia. Ayuti aingĩ mayendete Asamalia. O na mayaneenanasya namo! Ĩndĩ Yesũ endete andũ ma mĩthemba yonthe. Kwoou amwĩa: 'Kethĩwa nĩwĩsĩ ũla ũnũũkwĩa ũmũnenge kĩw'ũ anyw'e, wĩthĩwa wamwĩtya nake ethĩwa akũnenga kĩw'ũ kya thayũ.'
Mũndũ mũka ũsu amwĩa, 'Mwĩaĩi, kĩthima nĩ kĩliku, naku o na ndwĩna ndoo. Kĩw'ũ kyu kya thayũ wĩumya va?'
Nake Yesũ amwĩa: 'Kethĩwa ũkanyw'a kĩw'ũ kya kĩthima kĩĩ ũkeew'a waũnĩ ĩngĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩw'ũ kĩla nĩnenganae nĩkĩtonya kũtuma mũndũ ekala tene na tene.'
Nake mũndũ mũka asya: 'Mwĩaĩi, nenga kĩw'ũ kyu! Na ĩndĩ ndikew'a waũni ĩngĩ. Na ndikethĩwa na vata wa kũka vaa kũtava kĩw'ũ ĩngĩ.'
Mũndũ mũka ũsu asũanĩaa kana Yesũ eneena ĩũlũ wa kĩw'ũ kya w'o. Ĩndĩ we aneenaa ĩũlũ wa ũla w'o kwelekela Ngai na ũsũmbĩ wake. W'o ũsu nĩ ta kĩw'ũ kĩnenganae thayũ. Nũtonya kũnenga mũndũ thayũ ũtathela.
Nayu ĩndĩ Yesũ eea mũndũ mũka ũsu: 'Enda ũkamwĩte mũemeu na ũisyoka.'
Nake asũngĩa: 'Nyie ndi mũũme.'
Na Yesũ amwĩa: 'Waneena w'o. Nũndũ aũme ala waĩ namo nĩ atano, na ũla wĩkalaa nake yu ti mũemeu.'
Mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwaseng'ie nũndũ maũndũ asu onthe maĩ ma w'o. Yesũ amanyie maũndũ asu onthe ata? Amamanyie nũndũ we nĩ Ũla wathanĩtwe na watũmĩtwe nĩ Ngai. Ngai nĩwe wamũmanyĩthasya ũvoo ũsu w'onthe. O kavinda kau amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ masyoka, na maseng'a nũndũ nĩwanenaa na mũndũ mũka Mũsamalia.
Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na ũu w'onthe? Ũu wĩonany'a kana Yesũ e ĩnee kwa andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe. Na now'o o naitũ twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa tũilyĩ. Tũyaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa kana andũ amwe nĩ athũku nũndũ nĩ ma mbaĩ ĩngĩ. Yesũ eenda andũ onthe mamanye w'o ũla ũtongoasya thayũnĩ ũtathela. Na o naitũ nĩtwaĩlĩtwe nĩkwenda kũtetheesya andũ memanyĩsye ũla w'o.
Yoana 4:5-43; 17:3.
Makũlyo
- Nĩkĩ Yesũ wathũmũĩle ũtee wa kĩthima kũya Samalia, nake amwĩie ata mũndũ mũka ũla waĩ vau?
- Ũ mũndũ mũka aseng'iwe nĩ kyaũ, nake Yesũ amwĩie ata, na nĩkĩ?
- Nĩ kĩw'ũ kya mũthemba mwaũ mũndũ mũka ũsu wasũanĩaa takyo Yesũ waneenaa ĩũlũ wakyo, ĩndĩ kwa w'o nĩ kĩw'ũ kĩva Yesũ waneenaa ĩũlũ wakyo?
- Nĩkĩ mũndũ mũka ũsu waseng'ie nũndũ wa maũndũ ala Yesũ weesĩ ĩũlũ wake, nake akwatie ũvoo ũsu ata?
- Nĩ ĩsomo yaũ tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kũmana na Ngewa ya mũndũ mũka ũsu waĩ kĩthimanĩ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Yoana 4:5-43.
Kwa kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ twaĩlĩtwe kwĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ kwelekela andũ ma mbaĩ na ũko ũngĩ? (Yoa. 4:9; 1 Ako. 9:22; 1 Tim. 2:3, 4; Tito 2:11)
Nĩ moseo meva ma kĩveva ala mũndũ ũla watw'ĩka mũmanyĩw'a wa Yesũ ũkwataa? (Yoa. 4:14; Isa. 58:11; 2 Ako. 4:16)
Tũtonya ata kwonany'a weendesyo ta wa mũndũ mũka Mũsamalia, ũla waĩ na mea ma kũtavany'a maũndũ ala weemanyĩisye? (Yoa. 4:7, 28; Mt. 6:33; Lk. 10:40-42)

translation:
JESUS sent him a thief to Somalia. His feet were very sore from walking. A certain man asked Jesus to tell him something. And Jesus said, 'This thing is mine.'
This I have heard about this man. But what is it? Because Jesus his Savior is a Somali. Many saviors go to Somalia. And they rejoice with them! Indeed Jesus went to people of all nations. He said, 'Truly, what you ask is a good question, so listen to me and I will tell you the truth.'
The man said, 'Lord, life is difficult, and also I am very tired. What is this truth you speak of?'
And Jesus said, 'Truly, if you receive the truth of life, you will be able to walk further. For this truth always helps someone to stand firm.'
And the man said, 'Lord, give me this thing! And let me be able to walk further. And help me with the strength to avoid falling from another thing.'
This man was seeking whether Jesus had the power of that thing. For he had the power to please God with his worship. That thing is a truth that lasts forever. It helps someone to stand firm who is weak.
Then indeed Jesus told this man, 'Go, tell the blind and the lame.'
And he went and said, 'I am the blind.'
And Jesus said, 'You have spoken well. Because five of your friends are with you, and the one who stays with you is not blind.'
This man was surprised by all the things he had heard. Did Jesus know all those things? He knew because he is the One appointed and sent by God. God is the one who revealed all this to him. And surely, the feet of Jesus became sore, and he heard about the man from Somalia.
What should we learn from all this? This shows how Jesus cares for all people. And now we also want to be ready to go. We want to seek whether some people are sick and needy. Jesus goes to all people and gives them a lasting solution when they are weak. And now we want to be sent to help people understand that thing.
John 4:5-43; 17:3.
Questions
- When Jesus traveled through Samaria, did he meet anyone who asked him about that thing?
- What did the man ask for, and what did Jesus tell him, and why?
- What is the meaning of the hope of this man who sought Jesus' power, and what is the meaning of Jesus giving him that power?
- Why was this man surprised by all the things Jesus knew about him, and did he receive that revelation?
- What lesson can we learn about relating to the need of this man in Samaria?
Additional Questions
- Read John 4:5-43.
How can we, like Jesus, be motivated to share good news with all people and in many ways? (Jn. 4:9; 1 Cor. 9:22; 1 Tim. 2:3, 4; Tit. 2:11)
What benefits does a person experience when they accept Jesus' message? (Jn. 4:14; Isa. 58:11; 2 Cor. 4:16)
Can we imitate the Samaritan woman's example by being willing to talk about our needs and the things we have learned? (Jn. 4:7, 28; Matt. 6:33; Luke 10:40-42)

text:
KWASISYA malaa na malosi aa meu mathongooete ndatanĩ ĩno, kana mũtĩ. Ĩno nĩ ndata ya Aluni. Malaa na matunda asu meu mathongooie ndatanĩ ya Aluni ũtukũ o ũmwe tũ! Ekai twone kĩtumi nĩkĩ.
Kwa ĩvinda yĩana ũna, Aislaeli methĩĩtwe mayanganga weũnĩ. Andũ amwe mayoonaa Mose ta we waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e mũtongoi, kana Aluni ta we waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e mũthembi mũnene. Kola aĩ ũmwe ũla wasũanĩaa ũu, o na Ndathani, Avilamu na atongoi angĩ ma andũ 250. Aa onthe mookie na meea Mose: 'Nũndũ wa kĩ ũkwĩtũlya ĩũlũ witũ?'
Nake Mose eea Kola na aatĩĩi make: 'Ũnĩ kĩoko mwĩosa itoeesya sya mwaki na mũyĩkĩa ũvani nthĩnĩ wasyo. Na ĩndĩ mũkyũka ĩeemanĩ ya Yeova. Na tũkoona nũũ ũla Yeova wĩnyuva.'
Na mũthenya ũla watĩĩe Kola na aatĩĩi make 250 mooka ĩeemanĩ ya kũmbanĩa. Andũ angĩ aingĩ nĩmookie nĩ kana mamekĩe vinya aũme asu. Yeova aĩ mũthilĩku mũno. Na Mose asya: 'Umai maeemanĩ ma andũ aa athũku, mũikakiite kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kyoo.' Na andũ meew'a na mauma vakuvĩ na maeema ma Kola, Ndathani na Avilamu.
Na ĩndĩ Mose asya: 'Kwondũ wa ũũ mũkamanya ũla Yeova ũnyuvĩte. Nthĩ ĩkathamya na kũmelya andũ aa athũku.'
Na Mose amina kũneena oou, nthĩ yaathamya. Ĩeema ya Kola na syĩndũ syake na Ndathani na Avilamu na ala maĩ vamwe namo mamelw'a nĩ nthĩ, na yamatumisya. Na yĩla andũ meewie ngayaĩ ya asu matheete nthĩ, maneena na wasya mũnene mayasya: 'Tũkĩei! Nthĩ ndĩkatũmelye o naitũ!'
Kola na aatĩĩi make 250 maĩ o vakuvĩ na ĩeema ya kũmbanĩa. Kwoou Yeova aete mwaki, na onthe mavya. Na ĩndĩ Yeova eea Eleasali mwana-a-Aluni ose itoeesya sya mwaki sya aũme asu akw'ũ na akĩimanda itw'ĩke ngunĩko mbũthũ ya kũvw'ĩka kĩthembeo. Ngunĩko ĩsu yaĩ ya kũlilikanasya Aisilaeli kana, vaiĩ mũndũ o na ũmwe eka Aluni na ana make waĩlĩte kũtethya wĩa ta mũthembi wa Yeova.
Ĩndĩ Yeova eendaa kũmanyĩke vyũ kana no Aluni na ana make oka ũnyuvĩte methĩwe athembi. Kwoou eea Mose: 'Ĩa kĩla mũnene wa nyũmba ya Isilaeli aete ndata yake. Na kwondũ wa nyũmba ya Livai, ĩa Aluni aete ndata yake. Na ũkaia kĩla ĩmwe ya ndata isu ĩeemanĩ ya kũmbanĩa ngalĩ ya mbee ya ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo. Na ndata ya mũndũ ũla nĩnyuva ta mũthembi ĩkalaũka malaa.'
Na ũnĩ ũsu kĩoko yĩla Mose wasyaisye, sisya, ndata ya Aluni nĩyalaũkĩte malaa aa na ĩkasyaa malosi aya meu! Kwoou yu we nũkwona nĩkĩ Yeova watumie ndata ya Aluni ĩlaũka malaa?
Motalo 16:1-49; 17:1-11; 26:10.
Makũlyo
- Naaũ mang'endeie ũnene wa Mose na Aluni, na meeie Mose ata?
- Mose atavisye Kola na aatĩĩi make 250 meke ata?
- 3. Mose eeie andũ ata, na kweekĩkie ata amina kũneena oou?
- Nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie Kola na aatĩĩi make 250?
- Eleasali mwana wa Aluni, eekanie ata na itoeesya sya mwaki sya andũ ala makwie, na nĩkĩ?
- Yeova atumie ndata ya Aluni ĩlaũka malaa nĩkĩ? (Sisya visa.)
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Motalo 16:1-49.
Kola na aatĩĩi make meekie ata, na nĩkĩ yĩu yaĩ yĩko ya kũmũng'endea Yeova? (Mot. 16:9, 10, 18; Ali. 10:1, 2; Nth. 11:2)
Nĩ woni mwaũ mũthũku ũla Kola na "anene ma ũmbano" 250 maekie wĩthĩwe ngoonĩ syoo? (Mot. 16:1-3; Nth. 15:33; Isa. 49:7)
- Soma Motalo 17:1-11 na 26:10.
Kũthongooa kwa ndata ya Aluni kwoonanisye kyaũ, na nĩkĩ Yeova waisye nĩyiwe ĩsandũkũnĩ ya ũtianĩo? (Mot. 17:5, 8, 10; Aevl. 9:4)
Nĩ ĩsomo yaũ ya vata tũĩmanyĩsya kumana na wonany'o wa ndata ya Aluni? (Mot. 17:10; Meko 20:28; Avi. 2:14; Aevl. 13:17)

translation:
Yesterday evening and strength of my ancestors since this time, or tree. This is the story of Aluni. Evening and fruits were brought to my ancestors by Aluni one night! Let us see what it means.
For a small child, Israelites remembered their fathers. Some people saw Moses leading them to the mountain, or Aluni leading them to the great temple. There was one man who complained about it, and Nadathani, Abiham and other leaders of 250 people. They went and spoke to Moses: 'What shall we do with our lives?'
Then Moses took Nadathani and told him: 'Go and find firewood and bring a sacrifice from your sheep. And let us seek the favor of the Lord. And we will know when the Lord answers.'
And the day they took Nadathani and his 250 men offered a sacrifice. Many others also offered sacrifices like theirs. The Lord accepted it. And Moses said: 'Tomorrow morning, gather yourselves together and do something good.' And the people obeyed and followed the example of Nadathani, Abiham and Abiham.
And then Moses said: 'Because of this, you will know that the Lord has answered. Today you will be satisfied and full.'
And Moses finished speaking, and they were satisfied. The sacrifice of Nadathani and his family and Nadathani and Abiham and their families were accepted, and it was successful. And the people rejoiced greatly because of the abundance of food, and they spoke with a loud voice saying: 'Let us eat! Today we will be filled and satisfied!'
Nadathani and his 250 men ate from the sacrifice. Then the Lord sent fire, and he consumed the offerings. And when the Lord saw Eleazar son of Aluni offering the sacrifice, he made a law that everyone should offer a sacrifice from their sheep and goats to show respect for the sanctuary. That law remains for the Israelites today, so that no one except Aluni and his children can approach the sanctuary of the Lord.
When the Lord wanted to show his favor to Aluni and his children, he told Moses: 'Every head of the families of Israel shall bring his offering. And concerning the family of Levi, let Aluni bring his offering. And each offering shall be used for the sacrifice, which will be a memorial for the tabernacle. And the offering of anyone who shows disrespect shall be rejected.'
And now see how Moses did, behold, the offering of Aluni was rejected and it caused great strength! So you wonder why the Lord rejected the offering of Aluni?
Numbers 16:1-49; 17:1-11; 26:10.
Questions
- What happened to Moses and Aluni, and what did Moses do?
- Did Moses send Nadathani and his 250 men away?
- 3. Did Moses tell the people something, and what did they say when they finished speaking?
- What happened to Nadathani and his 250 men?
- Eleazar son of Aluni, what did he do and offer the sacrifice of the people, and why?
- Why did the Lord reject the offering of Aluni? (See verse.)
Further Questions
- Read Numbers 16:1-49.
What did Nadathani and his men do, and what kind of thing was this to approach the Lord? (Num. 16:9, 10, 18; Acts 10:1, 2; Prov. 11:2)
- How did Nadathani and his 250 "leaders" come together to rebel? (Num. 16:1-3; Prov. 15:33; Isa. 49:7)
- Read Numbers 17:1-11 and 26:10.
What did the acceptance of Aluni's offering signify, and why did the Lord save it for the tabernacle? (Num. 17:5, 8, 10; Heb. 9:4)
What lesson can we learn from the story of Aluni's offering? (Num. 17:10; Mark 20:28; 1 John 2:14; Heb. 13:17)

text:
Yesũ eekaa ũndũ mwaũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩla wavoasya andũ ala maĩ na mangũ?
Ayuti ma ĩvinda ya tene nĩmakĩĩte ũwau wa mangũ ũla waĩ kw'o ĩvinda yĩu. Ũwau ũsu mũthũku ũtilangaa syaa sya moko na sya maaũ na ũkatuma mũndũ ekala naĩ vyũ. Ũwau wa mangũ ndwaĩ na ndawa. Kwoou andũ ala maĩ na ũwau ũsu nĩmaaĩle kũvetwa vaasa na ala angĩ na maitavasya andũ kana me na ũwau ũsu.—Alivai 13:45, 46.
Atongoi ma ndĩni ya Kĩyuti nĩmaseũvĩtye mĩao yavĩtũkĩte ĩla yaĩ Maandĩkonĩ ĩũlũ wa ũwau ũsu wa mangũ, na ũu watumaa andũ ala me na ũwau ũsu mathĩna mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, amanyĩsya ma mĩao maumĩtye mwĩao ũkwasya kana andũ maĩle kwĩkala ũasa wa vuti 6 kana mita 2 kuma vala ve mũndũ ũwaĩte mangũ. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa kwĩ kĩseve, andũ maaĩle kwĩkala ũasa wa vuti 150 kana mita 45 kuma vala ve mũndũ ũwaĩte mangũ. O na kũtw'ĩka Maandĩko maĩtye kana ala mawaĩte mangũ mekalae "ũtee wa mwako wa maema," ve asomi amwe ma mĩao ya Kĩyuti maeleasya kana ndeto isu syoonanasya kana maaĩle kwĩkala nza wa ndũa ila syaakĩwe ngũta. Kwoou ĩla mũmanyĩsya ũmwe woona mũndũ ũwaĩte mangũ e ndũanĩ ĩsu, amwĩkĩasya mavia na aimwĩa atĩĩ: "Enda kũla waĩle kwĩkala, na ndũkavukye andũ ala angĩ."
Yesũ aĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na amanyĩw'a asu! Vandũ va kũlũngya andũ ala mawaĩte mangũ, Yesũ nĩweethĩawa eyũmbanĩtye kũmakiita na kũmavosya.—Mathayo 8:3.
Nĩ maũndũ meva mũndũ eeka wanengawa valũa wa kũthasya mũtwaano nĩ atongoi ma ndĩni ya Kĩyuti?
Kũthasya mũtwaano nĩ ũndũ waĩ na ngusanĩsyo mũno katĩ wa atongoi ma ndĩni ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa. O na ve ĩvinda Avalisi amwe mamũkũlilye Yesũ ĩkũlyo yĩĩ mayenda kũmũtata: "Nĩkwosana na ĩla mĩao mũndũ kũmũeka mũka kwondũ wa kĩla ũndũ?"—Mathayo 19:3.
Mĩao ya Mose nĩyeetĩkĩlĩtye mũndũũme kũthasya mũtwaano na mũka ethĩwa "nĩwonete ũndũ ũtaĩle kwake." (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 24:1) Ĩvindanĩ ya Yesũ, kwaĩ sukulu ilĩ sya amanyĩsya ma ndĩni ya Kĩyuti ila syamanyĩasya maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa mwĩao ũsu. Sukulu ĩmwe yeetawa Shammai ĩla yeethĩawa na kĩthito kya kũkwata mĩao, yamanyĩasya kana kwosana na mwĩao ũsu kĩtumi kĩla kyaĩ kĩtonya kũtuma andũ mathasya mũtwaano nĩ "ũvuku" kana ũlaalai. Nayo sukulu ĩla ĩngĩ yeetawa Hillel, yamanyĩasya kana mũndũũme aĩ atonya kũthasya mũtwaano ethĩwa nĩwaemanwa na mũka, o na ethĩwa maemanĩwa ũndũ mũnini. Kwosana na ũndũ sukulu ĩsu yamanyĩasya, mũndũũme aĩ atonya kũlũngya kĩveti kyake ethĩwa kyaua lĩu ũte mũyo kana ethĩwa nĩwonie mũndũ mũka ũngĩ mwanake.
Yu ĩndĩ-ĩ, Yesũ asũngĩie ata yĩla ĩkũlyo wakũlilw'e nĩ Avalisi? Amasũngĩie atĩĩ: "O ũla ũkamũeka mũka wake, ate o kwondũ wa ũlaalai, na aitwaa ũngĩ, nũnũũlaalaa: na ũla wĩmũtwaa ũsu ũeketwe nũnũũlaalaa."—Mathayo 19:6, 9.

translation:
Jesus asked them this question: "Who is like a man who digs deep down until he strikes water, and then waters people with it, along with their families?"
They replied that a landowner waits expectantly for the precious crop from the ground. The landowner patiently endures while waiting for the crop to mature and does not let anyone discourage him. A landowner is diligent and careful. So people should wait expectantly for the crop, and this crop will be valuable to refresh others and also to refresh themselves.—Luke 13:45, 46.
The overseers in the congregation are concerned about helping those who have been affected by the crop of landowners, and they want to help people to remain loyal. For example, they may visit homes to encourage individuals to stay away from bad association for six hours or two kilometers from someone who has been disfellowshipped. And if necessary, they may visit homes to encourage individuals to stay away from bad association for 150 hours or 45 kilometers from someone who has been disfellowshipped. But to avoid misinterpreting the Scriptures or causing others to stumble, the overseers must carefully examine whether the visits are truly needed or whether they might cause unnecessary hardship. So if one overseer sees someone who has been disfellowshipped in his territory, he should discreetly approach him and say: "Go home and stay there, and I will look for others."
Jesus showed great concern and compassion! Because he pitied people who were like sheep without a shepherd, Jesus made an earnest effort to teach and comfort them.—Matthew 8:3.
Are there good reasons why a person might feel inclined to compromise his integrity, according to the examples given by the overseers?
Compromising one's integrity is a serious matter that can lead to problems between the overseers and the brothers. Some Pharisees once tried to trick Jesus by asking him: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason whatsoever?"—Matthew 19:3.
Moses' Law allowed a man to divorce his wife if she did something wrong, saying: "He may write her a certificate of dismissal." (Deuteronomy 24:1) However, Jesus, in his teaching, presented a higher standard than what was taught by some Jewish schools of thought. One school called Shammai taught that a man could only divorce his wife if she had committed adultery, believing that allowing a man to divorce his wife for any reason would lead to widespread divorces. Another school called Hillel taught that a man could divorce his wife even if she simply displeased him. According to this view, a man could justify divorcing his wife if she spoiled a meal or if she was not to his liking.
So, how did Jesus respond when questioned by the Pharisees? He said: "Whoever divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery." —Matthew 19:6, 9.

Ĩvinda ĩte ĩasa mũno ĩvĩtu, mavuku maingĩ ala maeleetye mawoni ma andũ ala maasya kũi Ngai nĩmanyaĩĩkĩtw'e. Andũ aingĩ nĩmasomete mavuku asu na ũu ũkatuma maneenea mũno maũndũ ala me mavukunĩ asu. Aineenea ũndũ ũsu, neuroscientist wĩtawa David Eagleman aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Andũ amwe ala masoma mavuku asu matiawa . . . mayĩsilya kana andũ ma saenzi mesĩ kĩla kĩndũ." Ongeleeile kwasya: "Ĩndĩ asomi aseo ma saenzi nĩmetĩkĩlaa mawoni ma andũ ala angĩ, na wĩa woo wendaa kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli nĩ kana mamanye maũndũ meũ."
Kwa myaka mingĩ, andũ ala me kĩnengo kya maũndũ ma saenzi nĩmakwatĩte mosũngĩo maingĩ ma ũsengy'a ma maũndũ masaanĩtye ala methĩĩtwe mayĩkĩa ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa wũmbi. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, amwe nĩmekaa mavĩtyo manene nthĩnĩ wa ũkunĩkĩli woo. Isaac Newton nĩ ũmwe wa andũ ma saenzi ala manengetwe ndaĩa kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Nĩwoonanisye ũndũ gravity ĩkwatĩĩaa syĩndũ ta planets, ndata, na ikundi sya ndata (galaxies) yayayanĩ. Nĩwe wavumbũie nzĩa ya kwĩka masavu yĩtawa calculus, ĩla ĩtũmĩawa maũndũnĩ ma kombiũta, ma saenzi ya nuclear, na syĩndũnĩ ila syĩsĩlaa kĩsevenĩ ta ndeke. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Newton nĩweekie alchemy, ĩla nĩ mũthemba wa saenzi yĩtawa pseudoscience, ĩla mũndũ ũtũmĩaa ũtũĩka wa kũsoma ndata (astrology) na kwĩka syama atũmĩĩte vinya wa Satani nĩ kana avĩndũe syũma ta lead itw'ĩke thaavu.
Myaka mbee wa 1,500 Newton ate mũsyae, mũsomi ũmwe wa ndata waĩ Mũkiliki wĩtawa Ptolemy nĩwoonie ndata mbingĩ atũmĩĩte metho make. Ũtukũ nĩwoonie planets na aĩ na ũtũĩka wa kũsola mavu. Ĩndĩ aĩkĩĩaa kana nthĩ nĩ yo yĩ katĩkatĩ wa syĩndũ syonthe. Mũsomi ũmwe wa syĩndũ ila syĩ yayayanĩ (astrophysicist) wĩtawa Carl Sagan, aandĩkie ũũ ĩũlũ wa Ptolemy: "Ũw'o wa kana andũ maĩkĩĩie woni ũsu wa Ptolemy ũte wa w'o kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 1,500, wĩonany'a nesa kana mũndũ no ethĩwe e mũĩ, ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa ũndũ ũla wĩsĩ ti wa w'o."
Ũmũnthĩ andũ ma saenzi nĩmethĩawa na mawetu ta asu ĩla me wĩanĩ woo. Yo makesa kũelesya nesa vyũ ũndũ nthĩ na yayaya iilyĩ? O na kau nĩ ũndũ mũseo kwĩtĩkĩla kana saenzi nĩyĩkĩte maendeeo na ĩkatuma andũ matetheka, ve vata wa kũmanya kana ve maũndũ ĩtatonya kwĩanĩsya. Mũsomi wa physics wĩtawa Paul Davies aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩ vinya mũno kwĩsa ũkwata ũsũngĩo ũkũelesya nesa ũndũ yayaya ĩilyĩ kwa nzĩa ĩkũeleeka na ĩte kwĩvĩnga." Ndeto isu syĩonany'a kana mũndũ ndesa kũelewa wũmbi vyũ. Kwoou ĩla tweew'a kana saenzi no yĩelesye maũndũ onthe, wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wa vata vyũ tũkalilikana kana ve maũndũ saenzi ĩtesa kũmanya.
Vate nzika, Mbivilia nĩyĩanĩasya mawendi maitũ ũndũ saenzi ĩtesa kwĩka
Mbivilia nĩwetete kana syĩndũ ila syoombiwe nĩ sya ũsengy'a mũno. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Sisya, ii no ndee sya nzĩa syake [Ngai]: Na kaĩ no kĩwe kĩnini twĩw'aa ũndũ wake!" (Yovu 26:14) Ve maũndũ maingĩ mũno matiele andũ matesa kũmamanya kana kũmaelewa. Vate nzika, ndeto ii sya mũtũmwa Vaulo ila waandĩkie myaka vakuvĩ 2,000 nĩ sya w'o: "A! kyũngũ kya ũthwii wa ũĩ na ũmanyi wa Ngai! Motw'ĩo make matamanyĩka, na nzĩa syake itamanthĩka!"—Alomi 11:33.

The brain is an amazing organ, many studies have shown how people react to things and how they relate to God is remarkable. Many people interpret studies differently and this causes misunderstandings about things and different interpretations of studies. Explaining this phenomenon, neuroscientist named David Eagleman writes: "Some people who read studies believe…they can understand everything, even scientists don't know everything." He further explains: "People who study science often misinterpret the reactions of people and in doing so, they end up complicating things or misunderstanding them."
For many years, people in the field of science have held many beliefs about ancient things that were considered superstitious and sometimes led to harmful consequences. Today, some still hold strong views on those beliefs. Isaac Newton was one of the scientists most celebrated for his brilliant mind. He discovered the law of gravity which affects objects like planets, stars, and clusters of stars (galaxies) alike. He invented a mathematical system called calculus, which is used in fields such as computer science, nuclear science, and technologies that allow us to send satellites into space. Despite all this, Newton devoted himself to alchemy, a form of science known as pseudoscience, where people use astrology to predict the future and believe that demons can turn base metals like lead into gold.
About 1,500 years earlier, another astronomer named Ptolemy had described the universe using his own methods. At night he observed planets and stars and tried to understand their movements. He believed that the Earth was at the center of everything. An astrophysicist named Carl Sagan wrote about Ptolemy's theory: "The fact that people accepted Ptolemy's model for over 1,500 years shows how difficult it is to abandon an idea once it has taken root."
However, scientists have made progress and discovered things we did not know before. Why is it so hard to accept new ideas? Perhaps it is because science progresses and causes people to worry, fearing they will lose what they thought they knew. A physicist named Paul Davies said: "It is very tempting to cling to established beliefs when faced with something new and unfamiliar." But sometimes it is necessary to be able to understand different points of view. It seems that we often believe that science has explained everything, but there are still things that science cannot explain.
For example, the Bible explains our origins differently than science does.
The Bible states that nothing happens without God's permission. It says: "This is only the surface of his work, and how little of his vast plan do we see!" (Job 26:14) There are many more things that cause people to question or misunderstand. For instance, this statement from the apostle Paul, written almost 2,000 years ago, says: "Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and how unfathomable his ways!"—Romans 11:33.
