Nyie, ngakũlĩĩlya malondu makwa, na kũmamantha.—Esek. 34:11.
Ve ĩkũlyo Yeova wakũlilye ĩvindanĩ ya mwathani Isaia. Akũlilye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ mũka nũtonya kũlwa nĩ kana kake kala kekwonga?" Na ĩndĩ asyoka eea mbaĩ yake ũũ: "[Aka] nĩmatonya kũlwa, ĩndĩ ndikolwa nue." (Isa. 49:15) Ti kaingĩ Yeova wĩyĩelekanasya na kĩveti kĩ na syana. Ĩndĩ nĩweekie ũu ĩvindanĩ yĩu ya Isaia. Yeova eendaa athũkũmi make maelewe kana amendete mũno vyũ, o tondũ kĩveti kĩthĩawa kyendete mũno mwana wakyo. Iveti mbingĩ no syĩtĩkĩlane na kĩla mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Jasmin wawetie. Aisye, "Yĩla ũkwongya mwana mũtumaa ndũũ ya mwanya ĩtesa kũthela." Yeova nũmanyaa yĩla ũmwe wa syana syake waeka kũthi maũmbanonĩ na kũtavany'a. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ ala mavoete nĩmesaa kũsyoka kĩkundinĩ, na nĩtũtanaa mũno meeka ũu! Yeova endaa onthe ala mavoie masyoke, na ũu now'o twendaa.—1 Vet. 2:25. w20.06 18 ¶1-3
Tũendeee kũketeea syĩndũ ila itonekaa . . . Nũndũ syĩndũ ila syonekaa no sya kavinda, ĩndĩ ila itonekaa nĩ sya tene na tene.—2 Ako. 4:18.
Ti ũthwii w'onthe wonekaa na metho. Eka ũu, ũthwii ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ ũla ũtonekaa na metho. Yĩla Yesũ waĩ na Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ, nĩwawetie ũthwii tũtonya kwĩyiĩa ĩtunĩ, ũla wĩthĩawa wĩ mũseo vyũ kwĩ syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ. Ongelile kwasya: "Vala ũthwii waku ũĩ, nĩ vo ngoo yaku yĩthĩawa." (Mt. 6:19-21) Ngoo sitũ itũsukumaa tũsembany'e na maũndũ ala twonaa me ma vata. Na 'twĩyiĩaa ũthwii ĩtunĩ' yĩla tweeseũvĩsya ĩsyĩtwa ĩseo na Ngai, kana tweethĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo nake. Yesũ aisye kana ũthwii wa mũthemba ũsu ndwĩsa kwanangwa kana kũywa. Nake mũtũmwa Vaulo atwĩkĩie vinya "tũendeee kũketeea syĩndũ ila itonekaa." (2 Ako. 4:17, 18) Syĩndũ imwe katĩ wa isu nĩ moathimo ala tũkatanĩa ĩvinda yĩla Ngai ũkatw'ĩkĩthya maũndũ meũ ĩtunĩ na nthĩ. Ithyĩ nĩtwonanasya kana nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mothwii asu tũtesa kũmona na metho? w20.05 26 ¶1-2
Ũmanyĩsyo wakwa ũketĩkaa ta mbua.—Kũt. 32:2.
Kĩla Mose wamanyĩisye Aisilaeli nĩkyamekĩie vinya na kyamathangaasya, o tondũ ũnyenyeũ ũtumaa nyeki ĩsanzamũka. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana kĩla tũũmanyĩsya andũ kĩmekĩe vinya na kĩimathangaasya? Yĩla tũũtavany'a nyũmba kwa nyũmba kana kũla kwĩthĩawa andũ aingĩ, nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩaa Mbivilia kũmanyĩsya andũ kana Ngai etawa Yeova. No tũmanenge mavuku maitũ manake, tũkamony'a vitio sitũ nzeo mũno, na tũimony'a maũvoo me kĩsesenĩ kitũ nũndũ nĩmamũeteae Yeova ndaĩa. Yĩla twĩ wĩanĩ, sukulu, kana twĩ kyalonĩ, no tũmanthe mwanya wa kũelesya andũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai witũ na nguma syake. Yĩla twatavya ala twakomana namo nĩkĩ Yeova woombie andũ na nthĩ, kĩu nĩkĩtumaa masalukya makona kana nũtwendete mũno. Na yĩla twamatavya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ĩthe witũ wĩ wendo, twĩthĩawa tũendeee kũtetheesya kũthesya ĩsyĩtwa yake. Twĩthĩawa tũimatetheesya mamanye kana maũndũ ala mamanyĩĩtw'e ĩũlũ wa Yeova ti ma w'o. Maũndũ ala tũmanyĩasya andũ nĩmamekĩaa vinya na maimathangaasya mũno.—Isa. 65:13, 14. w20.06 10 ¶8-9

You others, seek your own flocks, and become shepherds.—Ezek. 34:11.
But Jehovah made Isaiah very courageous. He told him: "Will a man question whether he should fight, or not, when his friend strikes him?" And then he added this about himself: "[I] will be courageous, for Jehovah helps me." (Isa. 49:15) It is comforting that Jehovah feels empathy for us and for our children. So let us imitate Isaiah's courage. Jehovah understands how difficult it can be to discipline our children, or when a child misbehaves. But remember that discipline is an expression of love. Many parents find it helpful to talk to experienced Christians like Sister Jasmin. She says, "When you correct your child, focus on the specific wrong act and explain why it was wrong." Jehovah knows how each of our children feels when they are rebuked and disciplined. Parents and older ones alike often feel distressed when they have to correct someone, and we rightly do so! Jehovah wants all his servants to be courageous, and so do we.—1 Pet. 2:25. w20.06 18 ¶1-3
Let us continue to be courageous despite what may appear frightening. Even though something may seem terrifying, it may simply be a test of our faith.—2 Cor. 4:18.
Do not let fear paralyze you. In fact, the fear that people experience is often a test of their faith. Like Jesus when facing torture and death, we can be courageous and look forward to something beyond what we see. He said: "Store up your treasures in heaven, where moths and rust do not destroy." (Matt. 6:19-21) Those treasures motivate us to endure hardships. And 'being courageous' means trusting in God's power, or being confident in His promises. Jesus also explained that fearing reproach or death is not worth abandoning integrity. The apostle Paul encouraged us to "continue to be courageous." (2 Cor. 4:17, 18) Sometimes, however, it is hard to maintain our courage when faced with trials that God allows. Then we need to ask ourselves: 'Can I still trust in Jehovah and remain loyal?' w20.05 26 ¶1-2
Your discernment is refined like silver.—Prov. 32:2.
Moses warned Israel about becoming attached to false gods, because such attachment could lead to ruin. Can we say the same today—that attachment to false gods can make people spiritually sick? When we go from house to house or preach to many people, we want to use the Bible to help them learn about Jehovah God. We should not neglect our personal study, but rather value it and meditate on how to show appreciation to Jehovah. Whether we are at work, school, or in our ministry, we should always find opportunities to speak about our God and his Kingdom. When we associate with those who love Jehovah, it strengthens our resolve and helps us stay productive. And when we imitate the zeal of those in ancient times, we will continue to sanctify Jehovah's name. Let us therefore strive to share everything we have learned with others so they too may benefit.—Isa. 65:13, 14. w20.06 10 ¶8-9

Mwaka wa 33 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, Yesũ wa Nasaleti nĩwoowaiwe. Ailĩĩilwe maũndũ ma ũvũngũ ta kũkitanĩthya andũ na silikalĩ, o na nĩwakũniwe ateĩw'ĩwa tei, na ĩtina aathĩĩwa mũtĩnĩ. Akwie kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo mũno. Ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwamũthayũũkisye, na ĩtina wa mĩthenya 40 Yesũ ambata ĩtunĩ.
Ndeto isu sya ũsengy'a syumĩte mavukunĩ ana ma Ũvoo Mũseo ala me nthĩnĩ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto, ala mesĩkĩe ta Ũtianĩo Mweũ. Ĩndĩ maũndũ asu nĩmeekĩkie? Yĩu nĩ ĩkũlyo ya vata mũno. Maũndũ asu makethĩwa mataaĩkĩka, mũĩkĩĩo ũla Aklĩsto me naw'o wĩthĩwa wĩ wa mana, na wĩkwatyo wa thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Nthĩ Nzaũ wĩthĩwa wĩ ndoto. (1 Akolintho 15:14) Ĩndĩ kwa w'o ethĩwa maũndũ asu nĩmeekĩkie, ve na wĩkwatyo mũseo vyũ kwondũ wa andũ, o naku nĩwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo ũsu. Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Mo maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe mavukunĩ ma Ũvoo Mũseo nĩ ma w'o, kana nĩ ma ũvũngũ?
ŨNDŨ ŨKUNĨKĨLI WONANĨTYE
Kĩvathũkany'o na mbano sya tene, mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo maandĩkĩtwe maũndũ ma w'o vyũ na maeleetw'e nesa. Kwa ngelekany'o, mavukunĩ asu ve masyĩtwa maingĩ ma kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o andũ matonya kũtembea kw'o ũmũnthĩ. Maeleetye ĩũlũ wa andũ maĩ kw'o, na ũkunĩkĩli ũla wĩkĩtwe nĩ andũ ma isitoli wĩonany'a kana andũ asu maĩ thayũ.—Luka 3:1, 2, 23.
Aandĩki ma mavuku ala maĩ kw'o myakanĩ ya mbee 200 ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa nĩmaandĩkie ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. * O tondũ mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo monanĩtye, Yesũ ooaiwe o ũndũ Alomi mooaa andũ. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe mavukunĩ ma Ũvoo Mũseo nĩ ma w'o na maeleetye maũndũ mate kũvithany'a, nũndũ o na nĩmawetete maũndũ mate maseo ala amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ meekie. (Mathayo 26:56; Luka 22:24-26; Yoana 18:10, 11) Maũndũ asu onthe meonany'a kana aandĩki ma mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo maĩ aĩkĩĩku na maandĩkie ũvoo wa w'o ĩũlũ wa Yesũ.
NAO NATA ĨŨLŨ WA KŨTHAYŨŨKW'A KWA YESŨ?
O na kau andũ nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana Yesũ aĩ kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na kana nĩwakwie, amwe nĩmethĩawa na nzika ĩũlũ wa kũthayũũka kwake. O na atũmwa make mayaaĩkĩĩa ĩla mataviw'e ya mbee kana Yesũ nũthayũũkiw'e. (Luka 24:11) Nzika ila maĩ nasyo nĩsyathelile ĩla mo, na amanyĩw'a angĩ mamwonie Yesũ mavinda me kĩvathũkany'o. O na ve ĩvinda yĩmwe andũ mbee wa 500 mamwonie.—1 Akolintho 15:6.
Mate kũkĩa kũkwatwa na kũawa, amanyĩw'a asu nĩmatavisye andũ onthe na ũkũmbaũ ĩũlũ wa kũthayũũkw'a kwa Yesũ, o na nĩmamatavisye ala mamũaie. (Meko ma Atũmwa 4:1-3, 10, 19, 20; 5:27-32) Kwa w'o amanyĩwa asu maingĩvĩte ũu no methĩwe maĩ na ũkũmbaũ wĩana ũu o mesĩ kana Yesũ ndaathayũũkw'a? Ũw'o nĩ kana, ũthayũũkyo wa Yesũ nĩwatumie Ũklĩsto wĩthĩwa na vinya ĩvinda ya tene na nũtumĩte Ũklĩsto wĩthĩwa na mĩi mĩlũmu ũmũnthĩ.
Mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo ala maeleetye ĩũlũ wa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ na ũthayũũkyo wake mawetete maũndũ ma w'o. Wasoma mavuku asu nesa makakũĩkĩĩthya kana maũndũ asu nĩmeekĩkie. Mũĩkĩĩo waku no ũlũlũmĩĩlw'e wamanya nĩkĩ maũndũ asu meekĩkie. Kĩlungu kĩla kĩatĩĩe nĩkĩkũelesya.
^ kal. 7 Tacitus, ũla wasyaiwe vakuvĩ mwaka wa 55 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, aisye kana "Klĩsto, ũla ĩsyĩtwa [Aklĩsto] yaumanie nake nĩwatw'ĩĩiwe kũawa nĩ Vondio Vilato ĩvindanĩ ya ũsumbĩki wa Tivelio." Yesũ nũwetetwe nĩ Suetonius (wa ĩvinda ya atũmwa); Mũyuti waandĩkaa maũndũ ma isitoli wĩtawa Josephus (wa ĩvinda ya atũmwa); na Pliny the Younger, ũla waĩ ngavana wa Vithinia (ũla waĩ kw'o mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 100 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto).

translation:
In the year 33, the suffering of Christ Jesus of Nazareth began. He was filled with much power to convince people with scriptures, and he was shown a certain vision, and his suffering was great. But this is a good thing. God glorified him, and after 40 days of temptation Jesus returned.
Truly, this is the mystery of the resurrection from the dead of our Lord Jesus Christ, according to the writings of the Apostolic Scriptures, according to the revelation of Paul. What does this mean? It is truly a matter of great importance. These things were done so that they might be verified, because through Adam death came, and through death comes the judgment of Holy God, which is life eternal. (1 Corinthians 15:14) Therefore, if these things are true, then the resurrection of the dead is also important to people, and I will be resurrected with this resurrection. Truly, are these things written in the writings of the Apostle Paul, or are they a mystery?
THIS QUESTION REMAINS UNANSWERED
Consider and remember that the writings of the Apostle Paul were written about these things clearly and accurately. For example, these truths have been shown to many people who can walk in them. Show the way to those people, and the question that is asked by the people of the world is similar or these people are also deceived.—Luke 3:1, 2, 23.
The writers of the writings concerning these things wrote about 200 years after the apostles wrote about the life of Jesus. * And although the writings of the Apostle Paul are clear, Jesus was betrayed by someone named Judas. This is because the things written in the writings of the Apostle Paul are true and show many things to help us understand, but they also reveal many secrets about what Jesus did. (Matthew 26:56; Luke 22:24-26; John 18:10, 11) These things are seen or the writers of the writings of the Apostle Paul did not write about the betrayal of someone named Judas during the life of Jesus.
AND WHAT IS THE WAY TO GLORIFY JESUS?
And some people believe that Jesus had a spirit and that he rose, while others are confused about the way to glorify him. And his apostles believed that he would rise. (Luke 24:11) That truth has also been revealed to me, and many witnesses saw Jesus after his resurrection. And there was another group of over 500 people who saw him.—1 Corinthians 15:6.
Because of fear and death, many witnesses testified to the people about the way to glorify Jesus, and they also testified to others. (Acts 4:1-3, 10, 19, 20; 5:27-32) Because so many witnesses have been given this power, will we be able to say that Jesus did not rise? It is like this, the resurrection of Jesus uses Christ to give strength to the soul and send Christ to give light to the whole world.
The accounts of ancient historians also testify to the life of Jesus and his resurrection, which are important things about those events. Read their accounts so that you can find out what they said. A thoughtful person will know what they said. Every question should be investigated.
^ par. 7 Tacitus, a historian who lived in the year 55 during the time of Claudius' reign, wrote that "Christus, who was called [Chrestus] among the people, suffered death by Pontius Pilate under Tiberius' rule." Jesus was also mentioned by Suetonius (of the first century); the Jewish historian Josephus (of the first century); and Pliny the Younger, who was governor of Bithynia (who wrote around 100 years after Christ's death).

WAKATANO ũmwe makwakyanĩ Mweinĩ wa 9, mwaka wa 1922, andũ 8,000 nĩmoombanie ĩsũmbanĩ yĩmwe ĩnene. Kwaĩ kũnaambĩĩa kũvyũva maitw'ĩka nĩmekala nthĩ na ivĩla syausũĩte ki. Mwene kĩvĩla atangaasie kana mũndũ no aumaale enda, ĩndĩ aimanya ndeĩtĩkĩlw'a kũlika ĩngĩ asyoka.
Ũmbano wambĩĩe na kĩlungu kya mbathi kyeetawa "Kĩlungu kya Kũmũtaĩa Ngai." Kyathela, Joseph F. Rutherford nĩwaendie aũngama ngyukwaanĩ. Aingĩ mekalile mavindĩtye matesĩ easya ata. Ĩndĩ amwe avũthũ mayaĩ malũma nthĩ nĩ muutĩa ũla waĩ kw'o. Nĩvo Mwana-a-asa Rutherford wamesũvie mekale nthĩ methukĩĩsye. Ũvoo ũyambĩĩa, vo ve mũndũ weene kĩtambaa kĩnene kĩla kyalingĩtwe na kĩkoveewa nesa ĩũlũ wa ngyukwaa?
Mwana-a-asa Rutherford aneeneaa ũvoo ũũ: "Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtu nĩ mũthengeeu." Kwa ĩsaa yĩima na nusu, wasya wake now'o wew'ĩkaa aineenea ũndũ athani ma tene mathanie mate na wia ĩũlũ wa kũka kwa Ũsumbĩ. Ũvoo waĩye mũyo ĩla wakũlilye ethukĩĩsya, "We nũkũĩkĩĩa kana ũla Mũsumbĩ mũnene yu nĩwambĩĩe kũsumbĩka?" Onthe ala maĩ vo mookĩlilye wasya masũngĩa: "Ĩĩ!"
Nĩvo ĩndĩ Mwana-a-asa Rutherford waisye na wasya mũnene: "Likai kĩsionĩ ĩndĩ, inyw'ĩ ana ma Ngai ũla wĩ ĩũlũ wa onthe! . . . Sisyai, Mũsumbĩ nũsumbĩkĩte! Ninyw'ĩ mũnyuvĩtwe mũnyaĩĩkye ũvoo ĩũlũ wake. Kwoou tavany'ai, tavany'ai, tavany'ai."
Saanĩ ũsu nĩw'o kĩla kĩtambaa kyalingũkie na kyatambũũka nesa weethĩa kĩla ũmwe nĩwene ndeto ii syaandĩkĩtwe vo: "Tavany'ai Ĩũlũ wa Mũsumbĩ na Ũsumbĩ Wake."
Ray Bopp aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kĩla mũndũ eewie asanzamũka." Nake Anna Gardner aĩtye: "Mbĩ syakũnangiwe weethĩa twĩĩw'a mĩamba ya kĩala ĩthingĩthĩte." Ũngĩ waĩ vo nĩ Fred Twarosh, na aisye: "Andũ onthe maũngamie savalĩ ũmwe." Na ĩndĩ Evangelos Scouffas awetete ũũ: "Waĩ ũtonya kwasya nĩ ta ve kĩndũ kyatũkusya ĩmwe ithyonthe twaũngama, kĩla ũmwe ayĩw'a kwĩta methoi."
Aingĩ ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu no matavanasya ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ yu meewie meekĩwa vinya na makwata kĩtumi kĩseango kya kwongelanga kĩthito kyoo. Ethel Bennecoff aisye kana Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maumie ũmbanonĩ ũsu mayĩw'a 'mongeleelwa kĩthito na wendo ngoonĩ kwĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva.' Odessa Tuck, ũla ĩvinda yĩu waĩ na ũkũũ wa myaka 18, aumie ũmbanonĩ ũsu atw'ĩte vyũ kũsũngĩa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ yakũlilw'e: "Nũũ wĩthi?" Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu aisye: "Ndyeesĩ nĩthi va, nĩtavany'a ata, kana nĩtavany'a kyaũ. Kĩla neesĩ nĩ kana naĩle kwĩka o ta Isaia ũla waisye: 'Ninyioo; ndũma nyie.'" (Isa. 6:8) Ralph Leffler aĩtye: "Mũthenya ũsu ũtamba kũla nĩw'o waĩ mwambĩlĩlyo wa kambeini ya kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ, ĩla ũmũnthĩ ĩvikĩte nthĩ yonthe."
Tũiseng'aa tweew'a ũmbano ũsu mũnene weekĩwe Cedar Point, Ohio, mwaka wa 1922, ũiwetwa ta ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala manene maaĩkĩka ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova! George Gangas aisye, "Ũmbano ũsu watumie nĩw'a ndaĩle kwĩsa kũtĩa ũmbano mũnene o na wĩva." Na kuma ĩvinda yĩu ndaalilikana aitĩa ũmbano mũnene o na ũmwe. Nake Julia Wilcox aandĩkie ũũ: "Kũneena ũla w'o, ndyĩsa kũelesya ũndũ nĩw'aa nasoma mavukunĩ maitũ ĩũlũ wa ũmbano ũla weekĩwe Cedar Point mwaka wa 1922. Kĩla ĩvinda nĩw'aa ndyenda o kwasya, 'Nĩ mũvea Yeova, nũndũ nĩwanengie mwanya wa kwĩthĩwa ũmbanonĩ ũsu.'"
O ta ũu, aingĩ maitũ ũmũnthĩ nĩtũlilikanaa ũmbano mũna mũnene ũtakola, ũla watumie tũtana na watũthangaasya, na watuma twĩw'a twamwenda Ngai na Mũsumbĩ wake mũnango. Twalilikana maũmbano ta asu, o naitũ twĩw'aa ta twasya, "Nĩ mũvea Yeova, nũndũ nĩwanengie mwanya wa kwĩthĩwa ũmbanonĩ ũsu."

translation:
On the first day of September 1922, 8,000 people requested a large gathering. It was to show how the truth had become strong and valuable. The owner of the value stated that if anyone opposes him, he will know what it means to suffer more than others.
This example with the cloth called "Cloth of Praising God" shows that Joseph F. Rutherford went to various places. Many became very interested in his teachings. Some people considered them important and told others about them. That is why Son Rutherford has become strong and influential. This question arises, who is the person who has a great garment that is praised and honored throughout the land?
Son Rutherford answered this question: "The sum of things is powerful." For an hour and a half, his wife also spoke, repeating ten times and again the importance of praising the Sum. He then asked a question to test their understanding, "Will you remember that the great Sum tells us to praise?" All those present responded: "Yes!"
So Son Rutherford said to his wife: "Look at this, here are the children of God who are loyal! … Praise, let the Sum be praised! May you all be happy with this loyalty. Go forward, go forward, go forward."
Thus, this garment was praised and honored so that everyone wrote down this slogan: "Praise the Sum and His Sum."
Ray Bopp said: "Everyone should be enlightened." And Anna Gardner said: "I have never seen such beautiful and colorful buildings." Also Fred Twarosh said: "All the people gathered were united." And finally Evangelos Scouffas added: "It is impossible to express in words everything we experienced together, each one remembers it fondly."
Many others also shared their feelings about this wonderful work of the Sum. Some were moved to tears and expressed their desire to speak truthfully. Ethel Bennecoff said that the Bible students felt that they were 'guided truthfully and lovingly to share more good news.' Odessa Tuck, whose life had been difficult for 18 years, shared her feelings about this experience, asking: "Is this true?" The son said: "Yes, I believe it now, I will not fail, or I will not fail again. Every time I remember it, I feel like Isaiah who said: 'Here I am; send me.'" (Isa. 6:8) Ralph Leffler said: "This feeling began when I realized the importance of not failing the Sum, but it has grown stronger over time."
We are reminded of a large gathering held in Cedar Point, Ohio, in 1922, which was one of the events that helped us appreciate the organization of Jehovah! George Gangas said, "That gathering motivated many to make larger gatherings a priority." And many lives were changed because of that gathering. Sister Julia Wilcox wrote to us: "To this day, I remember reading the accounts of those who attended the gathering held in Cedar Point in 1922. Every time I read it, I say, 'I want to serve Jehovah, and I want to be given the opportunity to share in this work.'"
And so, many of us have come to appreciate this important work that unites us and strengthens us, and motivates us to love God and his Sum wholeheartedly. We have experienced such gatherings, and we too say, "I want to serve Jehovah, and I want to be given the opportunity to share in this work."

text:
O ta aaũmae moo, Ayuti ala maĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ nĩmavoyaa Ngai amatetheesye kuma ũkombonĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Lomi. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, nĩmeewie ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Nĩwĩthĩwa nowe Masia ũla wathanĩtwe? Ũu ndwaĩ ũndũ wa ũsengy'a nũndũ aingĩ 'meekwatasya kana nĩwe ũkovosya Aisilaeli' kuma ũkombonĩ wa Lomi. (Luka 24:21) Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, mwaka wa 70 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, ita sya Lomi nĩsyalikile Yelusaleme na syaananga mũsyĩ ũsu vamwe na ĩkalũ.
Nĩ kyaũ kyeethĩiwe? Nĩkĩ Ngai ũtaamokitĩa Ayuti o tondũ weekaa ĩvindanĩ ya tene? Kana nĩkĩ ũtaametĩkĩlya meyũkitĩe nĩ kana maume ũkombonĩ? Nũndũ woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ waĩ waalyũkile? Aiee. Ĩndĩ ve ũndũ mũna waalyũkile vyũ ĩũlũ wa Ayuti. Nĩmamũleile Mwana wa Ngai, Yesũ, kana nĩwe Masia. (Meko ma Atũmwa 2:36) Kwoou Ayuti nĩmaaisye ngwatanĩo ya mwanya ĩla maĩ nayo vamwe na Ngai.—Mathayo 23:37, 38.
Ngai aĩ aekie kũsũvĩa Ayuti vamwe na Nthĩ ya Watho, o na nĩmeesĩ kana Ngai ndaĩ amatetheesya ĩvinda yĩla mathi kaũnĩ. O tondũ Yesũ wathanĩte, moathimo ala Ayuti makwataa nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa me na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai, maĩ mavetiwe kwoo na manengwa mbaĩ nzaũ. Mbaĩ ĩsu nzaũ yaĩ mbaĩ ya kĩ-veva ĩla Mbivilia yesie kũmĩta "Isilaeli ma Ngai." (Akalatia 6:16; Mathayo 21:43) Kĩkundi kya Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩkyo mbaĩ ĩsu ya kĩ-veva yĩtawa Isilaeli ma Ngai. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa meeiwe atĩĩ: 'Yu mwĩ andũ ma Ngai.'—1 Vetelo 2:9, 10.
Nũndũ kuma ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa Aklĩsto maĩ "andũ ma Ngai," we Ngai nĩwamokitĩaa nĩ kana amaumye ũkombonĩ wa Alomi? Kana nĩwametĩkĩlasya makokite na amaitha moo? Aiee. Nĩkĩ? O tondũ twoona kĩlungunĩ kĩvĩtu, Ngai nĩwe ũwetaa ĩla kaũ ũla wĩtĩkĩlĩtye waĩle kũkitwa. Ngai ndaamokitĩa Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa, o na ndaametĩkĩlya mokite. Vate nzika, ĩvinda ya atũmwa yĩyaĩ ĩvinda ya Ngai ya kũkita nĩ kana amine ũthũku.
Kwoou, o ta athũkũmi ma Ngai ma ĩvinda ya tene, yaĩ no nginya Aklĩsto asu meteele ĩla ĩvinda ya Ngai ya kũmina ũthũku yĩvika. Ĩvinda yĩu yĩte ĩviku, Ngai ndametĩkĩlĩtye kũkita na amaitha moo. Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwoonanisye nesa ũndũ ũsu ĩla wamanyĩasya. Kwa ngelekany'o, ndaamanyĩsya aatĩĩi make mokitae, ĩndĩ ameie atĩĩ: "Mendei amaitha menyu, na mavoyeaei ala mamũthĩnasya." (Mathayo 5:44) Ĩla Yesũ wathanaa kana Yelusaleme ĩkaanangwa nĩ ita sya Lomi, ameie amanyĩw'a make makĩe, ĩndĩ ndaamea meteele amaitha moo na mayũkita namo.—Luka 21:20, 21.
Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ aveveewe nĩ Ngai: "Mũikeĩvanisye, . . . nũndũ nĩkũandĩkĩtwe, Ũĩvanĩsyo nĩ wakwa; ngaĩvanĩsya, easya ũu Ngai." (Alomi 12:19) Vaulo atũngĩlĩĩlaa ndeto ila Ngai wawetete myaka mingĩ mĩvĩtu ĩvukunĩ ya Alivai 19:18 na Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 32:35. O tondũ vawetetwe kĩlungunĩ kĩvĩtu, nzĩa ĩmwe Ngai waĩvanĩasya andũ make nĩ kwa kũmatetheesya ĩla mekũkita na amaitha moo. Kwoou, ndeto isu sya Vaulo sionany'a kana woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ ndwaĩ waalyũka. Ũu wĩonany'a kana o na ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, Ngai oonaa kaũ new'o nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte ya kũĩvanĩsya athũkũmi make, na kũmina ũthũku. Ĩndĩ o tondũ kwailyĩ kuma tene, Ngai nowe wawetaa ĩla kaũ ũsu waaĩle kũkitwa na ũla waaĩle kũkita.
Vate nzika, Ngai ndaametĩkĩlya Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa kũkita. Nao nata ũmũnthĩ? Ve andũ Ngai wĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũmũnthĩ mokitae? Kana ĩvinda ya Ngai nĩ ĩviku ya kũkitĩa andũ make? W'o woni wa Ngai nĩ mwaũ ĩũlũ wa kaũ ũmũnthĩ? Kĩlungu kya mũthya nĩkĩkũsũngĩa makũlyo asu.

translation:
And when He was near Jerusalem and they were approaching Bethany, Jesus rode on a donkey, a young colt, fulfilling what was spoken by the prophets: "Behold, your King is coming to you, meek, and mounted on a donkey." (Matthew 21:1-5) The disciples understood this event only after His resurrection. They remembered how Jesus had said, "The Son of Man will be betrayed into the hands of men." (Luke 24:21) For them, seventy years after the ascension of Christ, the city of Jerusalem was destroyed and its temple burned with fire.
What has been accomplished? Is God able to restore Israel to their former glory? Or will He establish a new covenant and a new kingdom? What purpose does God have for the future? Alas. For those who reject the truth, the future holds nothing but destruction. I have made known the Son of God, Jesus, who is the Messiah. (Acts 2:36) Therefore, Israel, you are rejecting the gift of salvation offered by God.—Matthew 23:37, 38.
God could have saved Israel along with the Law, but He chose not to, perhaps because God desires faith from people. And since Jesus died, those who believe in Him have entered into a relationship with God, which is confirmed through repentance and obedience. This remnant is like a small group mentioned in Scripture as "Israel of God." (Galatians 6:16; Matthew 21:43) The congregation of Christians is this small group called "Israel of God." And this is why the apostles addressed them saying: 'You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood.'—1 Peter 2:9, 10.
What about the apostles' reference to Christians as "the people of God"? Will God truly accept them and include them in His kingdom? Or will He cast them out and condemn them? Alas. Why? Because we see a great mystery, God is the one who chooses whom He will show mercy. God has chosen Christians as His people through the apostles, and He will fulfill His promise. See now, the people of the apostles are God's people to save.
Truly, though there are many people of God throughout time, they are only part of God's people through Christ. That nation, God will choose to save from destruction. He will choose to save and condemn. Jesus Christ showed us this very thing. For example, I encourage everyone to love their enemies, and pray for those who mistreat them. (Matthew 5:44) As Jesus approached Jerusalem, which was about to be besieged by armies, He encouraged His followers to flee and escape.—Luke 21:20, 21.
Furthermore, the apostle Paul wrote that we should leave vengeance to God: "Revenge is mine," he said, "I will repay." (Romans 12:19) Paul was echoing what God had stated centuries earlier in Deuteronomy 19:18 and Exodus 32:35. Though they were wronged terribly, know that God will vindicate his people by judging those who mistreat them. Truly, Paul's words do not mean that a Christian should never defend himself when attacked. This means that when faced with injustice, God can and will intervene to see justice done.
Therefore, God empowered Christ to carry out his purpose. But what about us? Does God empower people to carry out his purpose? Is God's purpose simply to save his people? Is God's purpose something more than that? The question of why is a difficult one to answer.

text:
Mũklĩsto mwendwa:
O ũndũ wĩsĩ, Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku yĩeleetye mũno ĩũlũ wa andũ. Aingĩ moo maĩ aũme na aka aĩkĩĩku maĩ na mathĩna o ta ala matũkwataa. Maĩ na "mwĩkalĩle ũmwe naitũ." (Yakovo 5:17) Amwe moo nĩmavinyĩĩiwe mũno nĩ mathĩna na mawĩmakĩo. Namo angĩ nĩmaũmĩiw'e ngoo mũno nĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ kana ala mathaithaa namo. Na ve amwe maandũawa nĩ wasya woo wa ngoo nũndũ wa mavĩtyo moo.
Yo andũ asu nĩmamũtiĩte Yeova vyũ? Aiee. Aingĩ moo mailyĩ ta mũandĩki wa Savuli ũla wavoyie atĩĩ: "Nĩnaĩte ta ĩlondu yau; mantha mũthũkũmi waku; nũndũ ndyũlawa nĩ mĩao yaku." (Savuli 119:176) We no wasye ta mũandĩki ũsu wa Savuli?
Yeova ndolawa nĩ malondu make ala melelũkaa kuma ĩĩthyanĩ yake. Ĩndĩ nũmamanthaa na mavinda maingĩ ekaa ũu atũmĩĩte athaithi ala angĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova watetheeisye mũthũkũmi wake Yovu, ũla wakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna me kĩvathũkany'o. Yovu nĩwaaisye malĩ yake, akw'ĩĩwa nĩ andũ make, na akwatwa nĩ ũwau mũthũku mũno. O na ĩngĩ, Yovu nĩwoomĩĩisye ndeto sya kũtũla ngoo ila syaneeniwe nĩ andũ ala maaĩlĩte kũmwĩkĩa vinya. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ndaamũtia Yeova, o na kau ve ĩvinda waĩ na mosũanĩo mataĩlĩte. (Yovu 1:22; 2:10) Yeova amũtetheeisye Yovu ata ethĩwe na mawoni maseo?
Nzĩa ĩmwe ĩla Yeova watetheeisye Yovu nĩ kwĩsĩla mũthũkũmi wake weetawa Eliu. Ĩla Yovu waeleisye thĩna wake, Eliu nĩwamwĩthukĩĩisye na ĩndĩ eew'a aĩle kũneena nake. Esaa kũmwĩa ata? Esaa kwambĩĩa kũmũtũla mũtĩ kana kũmwony'a mavĩtyo make kwa nzĩa ĩkũtuma ew'a nthoni? We Eliu nĩwoonaa ta we mũseo kwĩ Yovu? Aiee. Eliu awetie ndeto ii atongoew'e nĩ veva wa Ngai. Aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩilyĩ kwa Ngai o ũndũ ũilyĩ: O nakwa nĩnoombiwe na yũmba." Na ĩndĩ amũũmĩĩsya Yovu kwa kũmwĩa atĩĩ: "Ũtĩsyo wakwa ndũkakũtelemya, o na kũvivinya kwakwa kũikethĩwa kũito ĩũlũ waku." (Yovu 33:6, 7) Kwa w'o, Yovu nĩwendaa ũtao, ĩndĩ vandũ va Eliu kũmwongeleela Yovu mũio mũito, amũnengie ũtao ũsu kwa nzĩa nzeo na amwĩkĩa vinya.
Twĩenda ũmanye kana mbulosua ĩno tũnamĩandĩkie twĩ na woni ta ũsu waĩ na Eliu. Mbee, tũnambie kwĩthukĩĩsya, na twasũanĩa kwa ũliku maũndũ ala makwatĩte ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa amwe melelũkĩte, na tweethukĩĩsya mawoni moo. (Nthimo 18:13) Na ĩndĩ twavoya na twasoma Maandĩko ala monanĩtye ũndũ Yeova watetheeisye athũkũmi make ĩvinda ya tene ala makwatiwe nĩ maũndũ asu. Ĩtina wa ũu, twaandĩka mbulosuanĩ ĩno maũndũ ala mawetetwe Maandĩkonĩ asu vamwe na maũndũ ala makwatĩte ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. Twĩũkũlya kwa ndaĩa ũsome mbulosua ĩno. Ĩthĩwa wĩsĩ kana nĩtũkwendete mũno.
Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova

translation:
Beloved brother:
In fact, Elijah was a human being just like us. He earnestly prayed that it would not rain, and there was no rain on the earth for three years and six months. Then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain. (James 5:17) Indeed, some people earnestly pray for things with tears and heartfelt appeals. And yet they do not receive them because their motive is wrong or they ask for something wicked so as to waste it on their sensual desires. And some people have been deceived into thinking that God does not care about their troubles.
Why do faithful ones trust Jehovah fully? Yes. Many feel the way Saul did when he said: "I have wandered like a lost sheep; search for your servant, for I have not forgotten your commandments." (Psalm 119:176) Should we also feel the way Psalm writer Saul felt?
Jehovah cares deeply about our problems and is always ready to help us. It may be difficult to understand why he allows certain things to happen, but he has good reasons. For example, consider how Jehovah dealt with his servant Job, who was afflicted with severe trials. Job lost his possessions, his children were killed, and he developed a painful skin disease. Yet, despite everything, Job continued to maintain his integrity and refused to renounce God. And so, Jehovah restored Job's former state and blessed him even more than before. It may seem unfair, but I trust Jehovah, and I know that he will never abandon me. (Job 1:22; 2:10) Did Jehovah restore Job even after Satan had tormented him relentlessly?
One way Jehovah helped Job was by sending a young man named Elihu. Although Job argued his case, Elihu rebuked him and pointed out his errors in reasoning. Why should anyone try to justify himself or defend his actions when doing so would only lead to further trouble? Was Elihu really showing greater wisdom than Job? No. Elihu spoke what was inspired by God's spirit. He said: "I am near to God, and I have no one like Him." And then he corrected Job by saying: "Your own righteousness does not benefit you, but it is important to please God." (Job 33:6, 7) As a result, Job humbled himself, and because of Elihu's encouragement, Job greatly appreciated this correction and finally understood.
Let us see whether this article will help us to be more thoughtful, and let us examine ourselves to see if we are like the self-righteous person and the foolish person who give heed to their own opinions. (Proverbs 18:13) Also, as we read the Bible, let us remember how Jehovah has dealt with his servants in various situations that they faced. With this in mind, let us write down in this article things that were highlighted in the Scriptures along with things that relate to the self-righteous person and the foolish person. Please take the time to read this article carefully. Consider whether it will benefit you.
The Name That Glorifies God

Matukũ aa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, nĩsyĩsĩkĩe mũno nũndũ wa wĩa wasyo wa kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, nĩsyonekaa mũno iitavany'a kũla kwĩthĩawa na andũ aingĩ iitũmĩa tũkalĩ twa kwilĩĩla mavuku.
Ĩvinda yĩte ĩasa ĩvĩtu, nzĩa ĩno ya kũtavany'a nĩnambĩĩie kũtũmĩwa mũno. Mweinĩ wa 11, 2011, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova taoninĩ ya New York nĩsyambĩĩie kũtavya andũ ũvoo matũmĩĩte mesa na tũkalĩ twa kwilĩĩla mavuku. Nzĩa ĩsu yaĩ na mosyao maseo nginya atavany'a mambĩĩa kũmĩtũmĩa taoninĩ ingĩ.
Kũvikĩĩa Mwei wa 3, 2015, tũkalĩ 165,390 nĩtwanenganĩtwe ikundinĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nthĩ yonthe. O na kwĩ na tũsũmba mũthemba wa kiosk, sitandi sya kwilĩĩla mavuku, na mesa ngili mbingĩ inenganĩtwe kwondũ wa kũtũmĩwa ũtavany'anĩ.
Kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba nĩ yo nzĩa ĩla nene Ngũsĩ itũmĩaa. Ĩndĩ kũtũmĩa tũkalĩ twa kwilĩĩla mavuku nĩkwĩthĩĩtwe na mosyao maseo. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii:
Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Raul kuma nthĩ ya Peru, nĩwaendie vala Ngũsĩ syatavanasya na kakalĩ ka kwilĩĩla mavuku na amakũlya: "Mwaaĩe va? Nĩmanthĩte Ngũsĩ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩtatũ! Na ĩla noona kakalĩ kaa kenyu, namũtũngĩa Ngai mũvea."
O na kau Ngũsĩ nĩsyatavanasya kĩsionĩ kyoo mũno, Raul ndeethĩawa mũsyĩ mũthenya, kana wikendi. Aeleisye kana vau mbeenĩ nĩweemanyĩasya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ na nĩwendaa kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya. Mĩvango nĩyeekiwe nĩ kana ambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ĩngĩ.
Nakw'o nthĩ ya Bulgaria, mũndũũme ũmwe na kĩveti kyake, mate akũũ mũno, nĩmongamie vala vaiĩtwe kakalĩ ka mavuku na moosa ĩvuku Siri ya Kupata Furaha ya Familia. Kyumwa kĩla kyaatĩĩe nĩmasyokie na moosa mavuku angĩ elĩ: Ĩvuku Yakwa ya Ngewa sya Mbivilia na Jifunze Kutoka kwa Mwalimu Mkuu. Mwana-a-asa ũla watavanasya na kakalĩ kau nĩwamakũlilye me na syana siana. Maisye atĩĩ: "Tũinamba kũkwata kana, ĩndĩ ĩla twĩkwata, tũvangĩte tũkakamanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Mavuku aa makatũtetheesya mũno."
Mũndũũme ũngĩ wa nthĩ ya Ukraine, ũla weekĩĩte ngũa sya ita nĩwaendie vala Ngũsĩ syatavanĩasya na kakalĩ ka mavuku. Asyĩie atĩĩ: "Eĩtu, ndavyei Ali–Maketoni ĩkooka ĩndĩĩ." Mũndũũme ũsu aĩ anauma kaũnĩ wa nthĩ ya Ukraine. Maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmamũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana Ali–Maketoni yĩ vakuvĩ, na aseng'aa nĩkĩ Ngai ũtaaĩsa kwosa ĩtambya. Atavany'a asu nĩmatũmĩie Mbivilia kũmũelesya kana Ngai e na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũlea kwosa ĩtambya, na kana o mĩtũkĩ nũkamina andũ onthe athũku. Mũndũũme ũsu nĩwoosie makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya, ma Amkeni!, na ĩvuku Je, Kuna Muumba Anayekujali?
Nakw'o nthĩ ya Macedonia, mũndũũme ũmwe wa mũika nĩwatavisye Ngũsĩ imwe syatavanasya na kakalĩ ka mavuku kana nĩwasomete makaseti moo ĩndĩ yu endaa ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? Ameie kana eyĩsoma avika mũsyĩ oou.
Ĩtina wa masaa elĩ ou, mũndũũme ũsu nĩwasyokie na aĩ anasoma mathangũ 79 ma mbee ĩvukunĩ yĩu. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩvuku yĩĩ nĩyĩalyũlaa andũ! Nĩnoona kana maũndũ maingĩ ala nĩĩkĩĩaa ti ma w'o. Maũndũ onthe ala ĩvuku yĩĩ yĩeleetye nĩmosanĩte na kĩlĩko. Yatuma nĩalyũla vyũ woni wakwa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ!"

translation:
On the days of Jehovah's Witnesses, I became very busy with the work of visiting houses from house to house, and I saw how this work helped many people to use scriptures to learn the truth.
This experience taught me valuable lessons, and this work of visiting has strengthened my desire to be used fully. On November 11, 2011, the headquarters of Jehovah's Witnesses in New York authorized us to help those who requested assistance and to use scriptures to learn the truth. Since then, many have been able to find solutions to their problems through another congregation.
As of March 3, 2015, 165,390 congregations were organized throughout the world to serve Jehovah's Witnesses. And also, we appreciate the help of the service cart, the publications used to learn the truth, and the assistance given to many congregations to be used in the ministry.
Visiting houses from house to house is still the main way Jehovah uses us. Using scriptures to learn the truth is appreciated by many people. Consider the following example:
A brother named Raul in Peru shared his experience with the pioneers and publications: "How are you? I have been studying with Jehovah for three years now! And I really like your publications, and I thank God for them."
And so, Jehovah continues to bless him greatly, and Raul makes an effort to visit people during the week or on weekends. He invites others to join him in studying the Bible with Jehovah's Witnesses and he enjoys helping them to learn. The arrangements are made so that he can continue to study the Bible with more people.
In Bulgaria, a man and his wife, along with their children, were grateful for the publications they received, including the brochure "Secrets of Happy Families." They enjoyed each article and used other publications such as "God's Word—The Bible" and "Learn From the Great Teacher." Their daughter, who studied with them, said: "We are happy to have this opportunity, and when we have it, we try to share the knowledge of God. These publications have helped us a lot."
In Ukraine, a brother who serves as an elder shared his experience with the pioneers and publications. He said: "I visited Ali–Maketoni several times." This brother is concerned about the situation in Ukraine. The circumstances in that land make it difficult to find Ali–Maketoni, and he prays that God will help him locate her. He asked that literature be sent to help her understand that God cares for her and that she may find comfort in her trials, and also that many others may benefit from it. This brother appreciates the magazines *The Watchtower* and *Awake!*, and the brochure "Is There a Creator Who Cares About You?"
In Macedonia, a sister contacted Jehovah's Witnesses and was grateful for the publications they received, especially when she listened to recordings of the talk "What Does the Bible Really Teach?" She said that those who listen enjoy it very much.
After spending eight hours, this brother found 79 people who were interested in the good news. He said: "This publication helps people greatly! I realized that many things I previously believed were wrong. All the information in this publication is presented clearly and concisely. It has helped me to see the truth about many things!"

WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Nĩ Wakatatũ wĩoo, na Geoff, ũla wĩ na myaka 17, nĩwamina wĩa wake, nayu eenda kũthyũmũa! Ayĩkala kĩvĩlanĩ nĩ kana eloele televiseni.
O aendeee kwĩloela televiseni, ĩthe wake ailika na aithata nũndũ eethĩa mwanae ayĩloela televiseni.
Aimũkũlya Geoff atĩĩ: "Nĩkĩ ũkwananga saa ũyĩloela televiseni na nĩwĩsĩ waĩle kwĩthĩwa ũitetheesya mũinau wĩa wa sukulu? We ndwĩw'aa nthĩ!"
Nake Geoff ainyungunyĩsya na ayasya atĩĩ: "Yu nĩwambĩĩa ĩngĩ!"
Ĩthe aithengeea vakuvĩ na aimũkũlya atĩĩ: "Aĩ wasya ata?"
Nake Geoff aisũngĩa ang'ulĩtye: "Vai ũndũ nĩnasya Tata."
Ĩthe wake athatĩte ayasya: "Ndũkambĩle kũneena nakwa ũngandĩe."
Keka nue Geoff wĩthĩwa weeka ata nĩ kana ndũkasũngĩlane na ĩthe waku?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
Kũneena na asyai no ũndũ ũmwe na kũtwaa ngalĩ. Weethĩa ve kĩndũ kĩũsiĩĩe nzĩanĩ, no wĩsĩle nzĩa ĩngĩ.
KWA NGELEKANY'O:
Mwĩĩtu wĩtawa Leah aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndwĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũneena na ĩthe wakwa. Mavinda amwe nĩndonya kwĩthĩwa ndineena nake na ndyĩw'a angũlya, 'Ninyie ũneenaa nakwa?'"
VE MAŨNDŨ ATATŨ LEAH ŨTONYA KWĨKA.
Kũmũkũnĩa ĩthe kelele.
Leah amũkũnĩe ĩthe kelele aimwĩa atĩĩ: "Tata mbĩthukĩĩsye ũndũ ũũ ngũũtavya nĩ wa vata!"
Akaeka kũneena na ĩthe.
Leah aivanga ndeneena na ĩthe ĩũlũ wa thĩna ũla eeĩ naw'o.
Ayeteela ĩvinda yĩngĩ yaĩle nĩ kana eneenea ũndũ ũsu na ĩthe.
Leah aineena na ĩthe ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu ĩvinda yĩngĩ, kana aitw'a kũmũandĩkĩa valũa amũeleetye thĩna wake.
Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtonya kwĩa Leah eke katĩ wa maũndũ asu?
KWASŨANĨA ŨNDŨ ŨŨ: Ĩthe wa Leah ena mathĩna make na ndesĩ kana nũũmĩisye mwĩĩtu wake. Leah akatũmĩa Ũndũ wa 1, ĩthe no aeme kũelewa nĩkĩ mwĩĩtu wake ũkũmũkũnĩa kelele. Kwĩka ũu no kũtume ĩthe wa Leah aema kũmwĩthukĩĩsya, na nĩkũtonya kwonany'a kana ndeũnenga ĩthe wake ndaĩa. (Aeveso 6:2) Vate nzika, kũtũmĩa nzĩa ĩsu ya mbee kũitethya.
O na kau Ũndũ wa 2, nĩw'o ũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ laisi kwĩka, tiw'o waĩle. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ethĩwa Leah nũkwenda ĩthe amũtetheesye kũmina mathĩna make ũndũ vaĩle, no nginya amũelesye nesa maũndũ ala maendeee. Kwoou o nakw'o kũvindya kũitetheesya.
Kwosana na Ũndũ wa 3, Leah ndanetĩkĩla ũndũ ũla weekĩka ũmũsiĩĩe wĩthĩe ndakaneena na ĩthe wake ĩvinda yĩngĩ. Kwoou aimantha ĩvinda yĩngĩ ya kũneena na ĩthe. O na ve ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kwĩka, no avange kũandĩkĩa ĩthe wake valũa na kwĩka ũu no kũtume ew'a eanĩwa.
Kũandĩka valũa no kũmũtetheesye akavanga nesa kĩla ũkwenda kũmũtavya ĩthe wake. Ĩla ĩthe ũkũsoma valũa ũsu nũkũelewa kĩla mwĩĩtu wake ũkwendaa kũmũtavya, na ayĩelewa nesa nĩ thĩna ũla eeĩ naw'o. Kwoou Ũndũ wa 3, nũũmũtethya Leah na ĩthe wake. O na ethĩwa Leah eneena na ĩthe menene kana emũandĩkĩa valũa, meĩthĩwa mayĩatĩĩa ũtao ũũ wĩ Mbivilia waasya, "tũatĩĩe maũndũ ala ma mũuo."—Alomi 14:19.
Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ mwaũ Leah ũtonya kwĩka?
Kwasũanĩa kana ve ũndũ ũngĩ Leah ũtonya kwĩka na ũiũandĩka vaa ĩtheo. Na ĩndĩ ũiandĩka ũndũ vatonya kwĩthĩwa Leah eeka ũndũ ũsu.
NDŨKANEENE MAŨNDŨ MATONYA KŨTUMA ŨELEEKA NAĨ
Lilikana kana kĩla waneena na ũndũ asyai maku matonya kũelewa nĩ kĩla waneena nĩ maũndũ elĩ me kĩvathũkany'o.
KWA NGELEKANY'O:
Asyai maku meũkũlya nĩkĩ ũte mũtanu, naku ũimasũngĩa atĩĩ: "Ndikwĩw'a ndyenda kũneenea ũndũ ũsu."
Asyai maku nĩmatonya kũelewa ta ũũmeaa atĩĩ: "Nyie ndimũĩkĩĩaa ũndũ ndonya kũmũtavya kĩla kĩũnthĩny'a, nĩngũtavya anyanyawa mathĩna makwa."
Kwasũanĩa wĩ na thĩna mũito na asyai maku meenda kũũtetheesya, naku ũimea atĩĩ: "Mũikathĩnĩke nũndũ no nĩmine thĩna ũsu nĩ weka."

ARE YOU STILL AWAKE?
According to this story: It's Tuesday afternoon, and Geoff, who is 17 years old, is missing his friends, and he just wants to play! He sits quietly like someone watching television.
He continues to watch television, while his mother scolds him because her son is watching television.
Geoff's mother says: "If you continue wasting time watching television and don't study hard so you can pass your school exams? I will beat you!"
Then Geoff argues and says: "You always bother me!"
Then she threatens his father and tells him: "Didn't he say anything?"
Then Geoff quickly replies: "Yes, Dad said something."
Then his mother insists he say: "Tell me what you said."
So now Geoff is alone, or maybe he's planning something with his friends?
REMEMBER THE STORY!
To remember and tell a story well, practice often, and don't be afraid to try. Because practice makes perfect, and you will improve more.
FOR EXAMPLE:
A woman named Leah said: "I hate being alone when talking to others. Sometimes I wish I could tell them and ask them, 'Are you listening to me?'"
BUT MANY THINGS BOTHERED LEAH.
To annoy someone.
Leah annoyed someone greatly, telling him: "Dad, I think this thing I'm doing is very bad!"
She stopped talking to him.
Leah refused to talk to him for several days, even though she missed him.
She told another friend about how she felt about him.
Leah talked to that friend for a long time, or she wrote him a letter explaining her feelings.
Is this a good way for Leah to deal with things?
CONSIDER THIS: Leah's parents have their own ways and sometimes misunderstand their children. Leah sent Message 1, and her parents didn't understand why their child was upset. This made Leah feel worse, and it caused her to disrespect her parents. (Ephesians 6:2) Remember, practicing speaking kindly is important.
And Message 2 is also a good way to speak without getting angry, isn't it? Why? Because Leah can explain to her parents what bothers her so they can understand and help her. Keep trying to communicate.
Consider Message 3, Leah remembered something she had said earlier while talking to her parents. Keep talking to your parents. But there is something else that can be done, and she wrote a letter to her parents and this helped her calm down.
Writing a letter helps her explain herself and she refuses to bother her parents again. If the letter you read helps you understand what your child wants, and he understands what you want, then it will be helpful. Consider Message 3, practice talking to your parents. And whether Leah speaks to her parents directly or writes a letter, it is better than saying hurtful words like those found in this Bible verse, "We should avoid harmful words." – Proverbs 14:19.
What else can Leah do?
Think about whether Leah can do something to write it down and share it with others. And if writing something makes Leah feel better, then let her write whatever she feels.

Understand that everyone interprets things differently and what seems obvious to you might not be clear to someone else.

KWASISYA visa ii. Kĩla ĩmwe yasyo yĩonany'a ũthĩny'o ũla Yeova waetie ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ya Misili. Visanĩ wa mbee nũtonya kwona Aluni aikũna Ũsĩ wa Naelo na ndata yake. Yĩla weekie ũu, kĩw'ũ kĩla kyaĩ ũsĩnĩ kyaalyũkile kyatw'ĩka nthakame. Makũyũ nĩmakwie naw'o ũsĩ wambĩĩa kũnyunga naĩ.
Ĩtina wa ũu, Yeova atuma syoa syambata kuma Ũsĩnĩ wa Naelo. Nasyo syaĩ kĩla vandũ—maikonĩ, ikaangĩonĩ, itandanĩ—kĩla vandũ. Yĩla syoa isu syakwie Amisili masyũmbanisye mavumbu manene, na nthĩ yanyunga naĩ nũndũ wasyo.
Na ĩndĩ Aluni akũna kĩtoo kya nthĩ na ndata yake, nakyo kyaalyũka kyatw'ĩka tũsamũ tũnini tũũmanaa. Ũthĩny'o wa katatũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ya Misili waĩ tũsamũ tũu tũnini.
Mothĩny'o ala angĩ maũmĩisye o Amisili oka, na ti Aisilaeli. Ũthĩny'o wa kana waĩ wa ngi mbingĩ nene, ila syetavĩĩie nyũmbanĩ sya Amisili onthe. Na ũthĩny'o wa katano waĩ ĩũlũ wa indo. Ng'ombe, na malondu, na mbũi mbingĩ sya Amisili nĩsyakwie.
Na ĩngĩ, Mose na Aluni moosa mũu na maũũlũkya nzevenĩ. Naw'o waetee andũ na nyamũ itau nthũku. Ũsu nĩw'o waĩ ũthĩny'o wa thanthatũ.
Ĩtina wa ũu Mose ookĩlya kw'oko kwake kwelekela ĩtunĩ, na Yeova aete kĩtundumo na mbua nene ya mavia. Nayo nĩyo yaĩ mbua nthũku vyũ ya mavia kua nthĩ ya Misili.
Ũthĩny'o wa nyanya waĩ nguthu nene ya ngie. Mbee o na ĩtina wa ĩvinda yĩu kũyaaĩthĩwa na ngie mbingĩ ta isu. Syaĩe mĩtĩ yonthe ĩla mbua ya mavia yatialĩtye.
Ũthĩny'o wa keenda waĩ kĩvindu. Kwa mĩthenya ĩtatũ nthĩ yaĩ na kĩvindu kingĩ mũno, ĩndĩ Aisilaeli maĩ na kyeni kũla matũĩte.
Ĩtina vyũ, Ngai atavya andũ make mavake nthakame ya katena ka mbũi kana ka ĩlondu mĩtĩnĩ ĩlĩ ĩla yĩ ndee sya mũomo. Na ĩndĩ mũlaĩka wa Ngai avĩtĩla ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ya Misili. Mũlaĩka oona nthakame ĩsu, ndoaa mũndũ o na ũmwe nyũmbanĩ ĩsu. Ĩndĩ nyũmba syonthe ila itaĩ na nthakame mĩtĩnĩ ĩlĩ ĩla yĩ ndee sya mĩomo, mũlaĩka wa Ngai nĩwoaa makithathi na nyamũ ila syasyaĩtwe mbee. Ũsu nĩw'o waĩ ũthĩny'o wa 10.
Ĩtina wa ũthĩny'o ũsu wa mũthya, Valao eea Aisilaeli mathi. Andũ ma Ngai onthe nĩmeeyũmbanĩtye kũthi, na o ũtukũ ũsu mambĩĩa kyalo kyoo kya kuma Misili.
Kuma kĩlungu kya 7 nginya 12.
Makũlyo
- Ũitũmĩa visa ii syonanĩtw'e vaa, elesya mothĩny'o atatũ ma mbee ala Yeova waetie ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ya Misili.
- Kwaĩ na kĩvathũkany'o kyaũ katĩ wa mothĩny'o atatũ ma mbee na mothĩny'o ala angĩ?
- Ũthĩny'o wa kana, wa katano na wa thanthatũ waĩ mwaũ?
- Elesya mothĩny'o ma mũonza, nyaanya na kenda.
- Yeova eeie Aisilaeli nĩmeke ata mbee wa ũthĩny'o wa ĩkũmi?
- Ũthiny'o wa ĩkũmi waĩ kyaũ, na kweekĩkie ata ĩtina wa w'o?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Kuma 7:19-8:23.
O na kau andũ oĩ na aoi ma Misili nĩmeekie syama ivw'anene na mothĩny'o ma mbee elĩ kuma kwa Yeova, mo maĩ no nginya metĩkĩle kyaũ ĩtina wa ũthĩny'o wa katatũ? (Kuma 8:18, 19; Mt. 12:24-28)
Ũthĩny'o wa kana woonanisye ata ũtonyi wa Yeova wa kũsũvĩa andũ make, na kũmanya ũu kũtumaa andũ ma Ngai mew'a ata mathengee "thĩna mũnene" ũla wathanĩtwe? (Kuma 8:22, 23; Ũvu. 7:13, 14; 2 Mav. 16:9)
- Soma Kuma 8:24; 9:3, 6, 10, 11, 14, 16, 23-25; na 10:13-15, 21-23.
Nĩ ikundi syĩva ilĩ ila syavathũkaniw'e nĩ mothĩny'o ala ĩkũmi, na kũmanya ũu kwaĩle ũtuma twĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa ikundi isu syelĩ ũmũnthĩ? (Kuma 8:10, 18, 19; 9:14)
Ĩandĩko ya Kuma 9:16 yĩtũtetheesya ata kũmanya kĩla kĩtumĩte Yeova amũeka Satani ekale nginya yu? (Alo. 9:21, 22)
- Soma Kuma 12:21-32.
Vasaka yatumie ũvonokyo ũtonyeka ata kwa andũ aingĩ, nayo yoonanasya kyaũ? (Kuma 12:21-23; Yoa. 1:29; Alo. 5:18, 19, 21; 1 Ako. 5:7)

translation:
Consider this vision. Each one resembles the glorious kingdom of Jehovah as he showed it during the time of Moses. The elders among us remember how Aaron made the Tabernacle and its furnishings. This week, let each family review what they learned about it. Let the young ones also learn about this important thing and meditate on it.
Concerning this, Jehovah sent his spirit to help them make the Tabernacle. His spirit acted upon all kinds of people—skilled craftsmen, ingenious designers, willing workers—all kinds of people. And when they finished making the Tabernacle, they rejoiced greatly, and their hearts were full of joy.
And so Aaron made all the things relating to the Tabernacle and its furnishings, just as Jehovah had commanded. And everything that was made was beautiful and impressive. The splendor of the Tabernacle resembled the glory of God as shown to Moses.
Moreover, others who heard about the work done by Aaron became zealous, not only Israelites. The splendor of those times was very great, but it did not surpass the splendor of the Tabernacle itself. And the fifth day was a day of rejoicing. Many cattle, sheep, and goats belonging to the Israelites were sacrificed.
And furthermore, Moses and Aaron consecrated him and his sons with oil. He also blessed the people with a blessing from above. That was the time of the dedication.
Concerning this, Moses went to the tent of meeting, and Jehovah appeared to him in a thick cloud. And that was the cloud that signified the glory of God over the Tabernacle.
The ninth day was a great feast. Everyone, including those who had come to see the celebration, was amazed at the abundance of food. All the trees were laden with fruit.
The tenth day was a conclusion. For seven days the land had been filled with rejoicing, and the Israelites were happy and grateful.
Concerning this, God caused the people to offer sacrifices of young bulls and lambs, and many trees bore abundant fruit. And the angel of God traveled through the camp of Israel. The angel saw everyone, and he struck down one man because he had brought someone outside the camp. In all the homes where there were sacrifices of young bulls and lambs, the angel of God passed by and spared them. That was the tenth day.
Concerning this tenth day, Pharaoh sent the Israelites away. All the people of God were eager to leave, and they left that night, leaving the land of Egypt behind.
On the seventh day of the twelfth month.
Questions:
- What lessons can we learn from the fact that Jehovah showed his glory over the Tabernacle?
- How does this account help us appreciate the importance of obedience?
- What did the first, fifth, and tenth days signify?
- What lessons do the offerings of animals, grains, and fruits teach us?
- Did Jehovah allow the Israelites to remain in the wilderness for ten years?
- What does the tenth day mean, and what does it remind us of?
Further Questions:
- Read Exodus 7:19-8:23.
How did the Egyptians react when Moses and Aaron asked Pharaoh to let God's people go, and why did they eventually agree to let them go for three days? (Exodus 8:18, 19; Matthew 12:24-28)
The first sign demonstrated Jehovah's power to save his people, and to show that he could cause those who opposed him to become "greatly troubled." (Exodus 8:22, 23; Revelation 7:13, 14; 2 Kings 16:9)
- Read Exodus 8:24; 9:3, 6, 10, 11, 14, 16, 23-25; and 10:13-15, 21-23.
What important lesson does this series of plagues teach us about how Jehovah deals with those who oppose him, and why should we remember this lesson? (Exodus 8:10, 18, 19; 9:14)
How does the account in Exodus 9:16 help us understand why Jehovah allows Satan to continue existing? (Revelation 9:21, 22)
- Read Exodus 12:21-32.
What valuable lessons can we draw from the way Jehovah protected his people, and what can we learn from this? (Exodus 12:21-23; John 1:29; Revelation 5:18, 19, 21; 1 Peter 5:7)

Andũ aingĩ ala makũlasya makũlyo asu nĩmathĩnĩte mũno na makakwata wasyo mũnene na kwoou maimanthaa mosũngĩo me moka, ĩndĩ nĩmendaa kũkwata ũkiakisyo. Angĩ monaa kũawa kwa Ayuti asu ne ũthũku mũnene vyũ, na nũndũ wa ũu, wĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kwoo kũmũĩkĩĩa Ngai.
Maũndũ mate maw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai na ũaani ũsu weekiwe nĩ Hitler
Ũvũngũ: Ti ũseo kũkũlya nĩkĩ Ngai waekie ũaani ũsu wĩthĩwe.
Kĩla kya w'o: Andũ me na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu nĩmekũlĩtye nĩkĩ Ngai wĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũthũku ũendeee. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwathani Avakuki akũlilye Ngai atĩĩ: "Nĩkĩ ũekete ũng'endu, ũtũli wa mĩao, ũng'endilĩ, na ũthũku ũendeee kĩla vandũ?" (Avakuki 1:3, Contemporary English Version) Vandũ va kũmũkany'a Avakuki, Ngai nĩweetĩkĩlilye makũlyo asu maandĩkwe Mbivilianĩ nĩ kana andũ mamasome.
Ũvũngũ: Ngai ndamakaa ĩla andũ meũthĩna.
Kĩla kya w'o: Ngai nũmenete ũthũku na mathĩna ala ũetae. (Nthimo 6:16-19) Ĩvindanĩ ya Noa Ngai 'nĩweew'ĩthiw'e woo ngoonĩ yake' nũndũ wa ũng'endu ũla waĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 6:5, 6) Kwoou, vaiĩ nzika kana Ngai nĩweewie woo mwingĩ mũno ĩla Ayuti asu aingĩ mooaiwe.—Malaki 3:6.
Ũvũngũ: Ngai atũmĩie ũaani ũsu kũkany'a Ayuti.
Kĩla kya w'o: Ngai nĩweetĩkĩlilye Yelusaleme yanangwe nĩ Alomi ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa. (Mathayo 23:37–24:2) Ĩndĩ kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu, Ngai ndanyuvaa mbaĩ ĩmwe noyo yĩthĩwe yake kana akamĩnyuva nĩ kana amĩkany'e. Methonĩ ma Ngai, "kũi kĩvathũkany'o katĩ wa Ayuti na Andũ ma mbaĩ ingĩ."—Alomi 10:12, Good News Translation.
Ũvũngũ: Kethĩwa kwĩ Ngai mwene vinya w'onthe na wĩ wendo, ethĩwa asiĩĩie ũaani ũsu wa ĩvinda ya Hitler.
Kĩla kya w'o: O na kau Ngai ndaetae mathĩna, mavinda amwe nũekaa methĩwe o kwa kavinda.—Yakovo 1:13; 5:11.
Nĩkĩ Ngai waekie Ayuti aingĩ moawe ĩvinda yu?
Ngai aekie ũaani ũsu wĩthĩwe nũndũ wa kĩtumi o kĩla kĩtumĩte aeka mathĩna maendeee ũmũnthĩ. Kĩtumi kĩu nĩ kũsũngĩa maũndũ ala maumĩlilw'e nĩ Satani. Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye nesa vyũ kana ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ, Ngai tiwe ũsumbĩkĩte nthĩ ĩndĩ nĩ Satani. (Luka 4:1, 2, 6; Yoana 12:31) O na kau ungu wa kyongo kĩĩ ve ũvoo ũeleetye mũnango nĩkĩ Ngai ũekete mathĩna methĩwe, ve itumi ilĩ nzeo kuma Mbivilianĩ itonya kũtũtetheesya kũelewa nĩkĩ Ngai waekie ũaani ũsu wĩthĩwe.
Nũũ watumie ũaani ũsu mũthũku ũu wĩthĩwa? Ngai nĩwatavisye asyai maitũ ma mbee Atamu na Eva kĩla wendaa meke, ĩndĩ ndaamalasimĩthya. Nĩmanyuvie kwĩtw'ĩaa kĩla kĩseo na kĩla kĩthũku. Ũtwi woo mũthũku, vamwe na motwi ala mekawa nĩ andũ kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu, nĩmatumĩte andũ makwatwa nĩ maũndũ mathũku. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:17; 3:6; Alomi 5:12) No ta ũndũ ĩvuku Statement of Principles of Conservative Judaism yaĩtye: "Mathĩna maingĩ ala makwataa andũ maumanĩte na andũ kũtũmĩa naĩ ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa ũla manengetwe." Vandũ va kũvena andũ ũthasyo ũsu, Ngai amanengete ĩvinda metongoesye ateũmalikĩlĩĩla.
Ngai nũtonya, na akatũngĩĩa wanangĩko w'onthe ũla waumĩlile ĩvindanĩ yĩu ya ũaani mũnene. Ngai nĩwathanĩte kũthayũũkya andũ milioni mbingĩ ala makw'ĩte, ala nĩ vamwe na Ayuti asu aingĩ mooaiwe. O na akamina woo ũla ala mavonokie ĩvinda yĩu mew'aa malilikana maũndũ mathũku ala meekiwe. (Isaia 65:17; Meko ma Atũmwa 24:15) Tũi na nzika kana Ngai akeanĩsya mawatho asu onthe nũndũ nĩwendete andũ.—Yoana 3:16.
Andũ aingĩ ala mavonokie ĩvindanĩ yĩu, maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu na nĩmaendeeie kwĩkala me atanu nũndũ nĩmaeleetwe nĩkĩ Ngai ũekete mathĩna methĩwe, na nĩmeesĩ kana akamina mathĩna asu vyũ.

translation:
Many people today live in great sorrow and have heavy burdens and face many difficulties in life, so I want to get relief. I saw the fall of Haiti and a great darkness came, and because of this, people turned their faces away from remembering God.
These words are the word of God and your heart will be given to Hitler.
Meaning: It is good to remember that God gives your heart.
For example: People with a broken spirit say to God: "How long will you judge, how long will you lament, how long will darkness continue for all people?" (Habakkuk 1:3, Contemporary English Version) To those who question Habakkuk, God answers his complaints in the book of Revelation or among the prophets.
Meaning: God always cares for his people.
For example: God has made everything beautiful in its time, he has also put eternity in their hearts (Ecclesiastes 3:16-19). In Noah's flood, God 'showed his displeasure' because of the wickedness of the earth (Genesis 6:5, 6). But now look, God shows more favor than ever to Haiti and many others.—Malachi 3:6.
Meaning: God uses his heart to comfort Haiti.
For example: God would gather Jerusalem, just as he gathered his servants (Matthew 23:37–24:2). Now, according to this gathering, God will rejoice over his chosen ones or grieve when he rejects them. The ways of God, "are not like the ways of Haiti and other peoples."—Romans 10:12, Good News Translation.
Meaning: Be pleased with God alone and love him, be pleased with his heart for the destruction of Hitler.
For example: Yes, and God does not tempt anyone, evil comes from temptation.—James 1:13; 5:11.
If God gives Haiti more trials, will they endure?
God uses his heart to show what happens when people continue to do bad things. This is to overcome the things that Satan has deceived us with. The Bible tells us clearly that if we are not careful, God will not allow Satan to deceive us (Luke 4:1, 2, 6; John 12:31). But now, if the language of the heart is not understood, then God allows bad things to happen, but the truth in the Bible can help us understand why God uses his heart to show us.
Why does God use his heart to show us these things? God tested Adam and Eve like he tests everyone, so they could prove themselves faithful. He enjoys seeing us test ourselves in everything we do. That testing of our hearts, along with all the other tests we face from Satan, causes people to get caught up in bad things. (Proverbs 2:17; 3:6; Romans 5:12) And as the Statement of Principles of Conservative Judaism says: "Many problems cause people to turn away from God and to seek satisfaction in wrong desires." Those who give in to those desires, God lets their minds be misled until they become hopeless.
God is able, and he will bring about his purpose for all creation that Satan has corrupted. God wants to awaken millions of people who have fallen asleep, including many of our dear brothers. But he also allows those who are stubborn to ruin their lives through bad choices. (Isaiah 65:17; Acts 24:15) So rejoice because God loves us enough to send his Son to die for us.—John 3:16.
Many people who live in this world are experiencing great sorrow and continue to live in ignorance, and they will be destroyed because God allows them to experience certain things, and he sees whether they will choose good.

text:
KUMA tene kumya nthembo kwĩthĩĩtwe kwĩ kwa vata ũthaithinĩ wa w'o. Aisilaeli maumasya nthembo sya nyamũ, namo Aklĩsto mesĩkĩe nesa na "nthembo ya ndaĩa." Ĩndĩ ve o nthembo ingĩ imũtanĩthasya Ngai mũno. (Aevl. 13:15, 16) Ngai nũtũathimaa na tũkekala twĩ atanu ĩla twaumya nthembo ta isu. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii iatĩĩe.
Aana aĩ mũthũkũmi mũĩkĩĩku wa Ngai na nĩwendaa mũno kũkwata kavĩsĩ, ĩndĩ ndaĩ atonya kũsyaa. Na kwoou nĩwamũvoyie Yeova amwĩa kana amũtetheesya asyae kavĩsĩ, 'akakanengane kwa Yeova mĩthenya yonthe ya thayũ wako.' (1 Sam. 1:10, 11) Aana nĩwesie kũitava na asyaa kavĩsĩ waketie Samueli. Aaĩsya Samueli nĩwamũtwaie ĩeemanĩ ya kũmbanĩa nĩ kana eanĩsye wĩvĩto wake. Yeova nĩwaathimie Aana nũndũ wa ũlau wake. Nĩwesie kũsyaa syana ingĩ itano na mwana wake, Samueli, nĩwatw'ĩkie mwathani na ũmwe wa ala maandĩkie Mbivilia.—1 Sam. 2:21.
O ta Aana na Samueli, ũmũnthĩ Aklĩsto me na mwanya wa kwĩyumya vyũ mamũthũkũme Mũmbi woo. Yesũ nĩwathanie kana kyonthe kĩla tweeyĩima nĩ kana tũmũthaithe Yeova kĩkaathimwa mũno.—Mko. 10:28-30.
Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, kwaĩ mũndũ mũka Mũklĩsto weetawa Ndolokasi weeyĩimaa maũndũ nĩ kana atetheesye ala angĩ. Eesĩkĩe nesa na "meko maseo ala wekaa vamwe na kumya motethyo." Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana avikie vandũ "akwatwa nĩ ũwau, na akw'a," na kĩu nĩkyatumie kĩkundi kĩmeta mũno. Ĩla amanyĩw'a mamanyie kana Vetelo e kĩsionĩ, nĩmamũkũlilye oke na ndakekale. Kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla meewie Vetelo avika na athayũũkya Ndolokasi! Ndolokasi nĩwe wa mbee kũwetwa Mbivilianĩ aithayũũkw'a nĩ mũtũmwa. (Meko 9:36-41) Ngai ndoolĩtwe nĩ maũndũ ala Ndolokasi weekĩte. (Aevl. 6:10) O na maũndũ ala weekie nĩmaandĩkiwe Ndetonĩ ya Ngai nĩ kana matũtetheesye kwĩyĩelekany'a nake.
O nake mũtũmwa Vaulo aĩ ngelekany'o nzeo mũno nũndũ nĩwatũmĩaa ĩvinda yake kũtetheesya angĩ na kũmethukĩĩsya. Aandĩkĩie ana-a-asa ala maĩ Kolintho amea atĩĩ: "Nyie nganengane na ũtanu mwingĩ na kwĩnengane vyũ kwondũ wenyu." (2 Ako. 12:15) Vaulo nĩweeyoneie kana kwĩyumya ũtethye angĩ nĩkũtumaa wĩkala wĩ mwĩanĩe, ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata nĩ kana kũtumaa Yeova akũathima na aikwenda mũno.—Meko 20:24, 35.
Kwoou no twasye tũte na nzika kana Yeova nũtanaa ĩla twatũmĩa ĩvinda yitũ na vinya witũ nĩ kana tũtetheesye ana-a-asa na tũitetheesya wĩanĩ wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ vo ve ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka tũkakwata kw'oko wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ? Ĩĩ! O na kau nĩtũmũtaĩaa Ngai twatũmĩa ĩvinda yitũ na vinya witũ, o nayo mĩvothi ĩla tumasya nĩmũtaĩaa. Mĩvothi ĩsu nĩtumaa wĩa wa nthĩ yonthe wa kũtavany'a ũsonga na mbee. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũmĩawa kũtetheesya amisonalĩ na athũkũmi ala angĩ ma ĩvinda yonthe ma mwanya. Na eka ũu, mĩvothi ĩla tumasya nĩyo ĩtetheeasya wĩanĩ wa kũseũvya na kũalyũla mavuku na vitio, nĩyo ĩtetheeasya ĩvinda ya mĩisyo, na ĩla kũkwakwa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ. Nĩtwĩkalei twĩsĩ kana "ũla wĩ na itho ĩlau akaathimwa." Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ĩla twanenga Yeova syĩndũ sitũ ila sya vata nĩtũtumaa ataĩwa.—Nth. 3:9; 22:9.

translation:
So then, let us offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to His name. Israel often offered animal sacrifices, but Christ perfected a better sacrifice—"a sacrifice of good conduct." Indeed, there is another song that pleases our generous God. (Heb. 13:15, 16) God delights when we remember to offer up such sacrifices regularly. Consider how valuable this practice is.
Hannah was a devoted woman of God and earnestly desired to have children, yet she was unable to conceive. And she kept praying to Jehovah about her desire to have children, saying, "I will pay my vows to Jehovah for all the days of my life." (1 Sam. 1:10, 11) Hannah continued to pray intensely, and finally she conceived and bore Samuel. She brought young Samuel to the temple and dedicated him to Jehovah, and he served there under Eli's supervision. Jehovah blessed Hannah with five more sons and her son, Samuel, grew strong and wise, becoming a prophet and judge.—1 Sam. 2:21.
Like Hannah and Samuel, Christians have the privilege of praising their Creator. Jesus showed that everything we say and do can please Jehovah if we use it to honor Him.—Matt. 10:28-30.
In the ministry, a certain disciple named Apollos powerfully demonstrated the truth and refuted the Jews publicly. He began to speak boldly and accurately about Jesus, but knew little about John the Baptist. Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately. Apollos then became very enthusiastic and helped those who had believed through the Scriptures.—Acts 18:24-28. How important it is to be willing to learn from others! Apollos humbly accepted correction and continued to grow spiritually. Consider the fine example set by Apollos and Priscilla! Apollos proved to be a faithful minister of the Word, and his zealous efforts contributed greatly to the advancement of the good news.—Acts 19:36-41. May we also imitate Apollos' zeal and dedication. (Heb. 6:10) And may we carefully study God's inspired Word so that we can accurately explain its truths.
The apostle Paul often used this principle when he preached, using his gift of speaking to persuade people and convince them. He wrote to the brothers in Corinth, saying: "Do not become unevenly yoked with people who do not share our beliefs." (2 Cor. 6:15) Paul understood that associating with those whose thinking is different could lead to compromise, which would displease Jehovah and bring reproach on us.—Acts 20:24, 35.
So how can we show discernment regarding what we allow into our minds and eyes? It is because what we allow into our minds and eyes affects how we treat others and how we conduct ourselves as Christians. To illustrate this point, what choices do we make about what we read and watch so that we do not stumble over the stumbling block of immorality? Yes! And just as we tell God what we allow into our minds and eyes, so too our choices affect what we say. Our words can build up or tear down, and they can help us maintain peace and harmony. For example, we are influenced to speak kindly to family members and friends, and also to use our tongue for good purposes. Moreover, the things we choose influence our attitude toward work and leisure, our view of money, and even our attendance at Kingdom Hall meetings. Let us always remember that "a man's heart plans his way, but Jehovah shapes his steps." What we need is to ask Jehovah for wisdom and guidance in making wise choices.—Prov. 3:9; 22:9.

text:
Wendo . . . ndwĩkaa ũndũ ũtaĩle, o na ndwĩmanthĩaa syĩndũ. —1 Ako. 13:4, 5.
Andũ ma Ngai mekĩaa kĩthito mũno maatĩĩe ũtao ũũ wĩ Mbivilianĩ: "Ũaai mamutha menyu ala me kũũ nthĩ: ũlaalai, na ũvuku, na mĩmeo mĩthũku." (Ako. 3:2, 5) Tũyĩsa kwenda wĩthĩwe wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwa Aklĩsto ala angĩ kũatĩĩa ũtao ũsu. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala maekanie na mwĩkalĩle wa ũlaalai no matonya kwĩthĩwa maendeee kũkita mũno mavete kawendi kana me nako ka kwĩka naĩ. (1 Ako. 6:9, 10) Ithyĩ tũyenda o na vanini kũmetesya maũndũ, kana nata? Ĩla twĩ na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ, mwĩkĩĩle witũ wa ngũa nĩwaĩle kũtuma mew'a kĩkundinĩ ne vandũ vaseo vate na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku. Tũivatĩtwe kwĩnyuvĩa ngũa ila tũkwenda kwĩkĩa. Ĩndĩ ithyonthe nĩtwaĩlĩte kwĩkĩa ngũa iũtuma wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa angĩ kwĩkala me atheu na maiendeea kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Ngai ĩũlũ wa ũtheu wa mosũanĩo, ndeto, na mwĩkalĩle.—1 Vet. 1:15, 16. w16.09 3:9, 10
Anake o na eĩtu atheu . . . nĩmataĩe syĩtwa ya Yeova.—Sav. 148:12, 13.
Mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mũka kuma France maisye: "Ithyĩ twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova e kw'o, ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana syana sitũ ikeethĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu." Masyokie masya: "Mũĩkĩĩo ti kĩndũ mwana ũsyaawa nakyo. Syana imeasya mũĩkĩĩo o kavola kwa kavola." Nake mwana-a-asa ũmwe kuma Australia aandĩkie ũũ: "No kwĩthĩwa ũndũ ũla wĩ vinya vyũ ũkesa kwĩka ne kũtetheesya mwana waku ethĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. . . . Mwana waku nũtonya kũũkũlya ĩkũlyo ĩna, ũkamũsũngĩa, na ũkona ta weanĩwa. Aĩ na mwĩkalangĩte ayĩsa ũkũkũlya yĩla ĩkũlyo ĩngĩ! Syana nĩsyendete kũmanya maũndũ mũno, na kwoou mosũngĩo ala ũtonya kũnenga mwana ũmũnthĩ akeanĩwa no kwĩthĩwa ũkamũnenga ĩvinda yĩngĩ atesa kwĩanĩwa. Kwoou no kwĩthĩwa ve vata wa kũtũngĩlĩĩla maũndũ o ala mwĩla kũneenea ĩvinda yĩngĩ." Ethĩwa we wĩ mũsyai, ve mavinda amwe wĩw'aa ta ũtatonya kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kyaku kya kũmanyĩsya na kũtetheesya syana syaku syĩtw'ĩka aũme na aka me mũĩkĩĩo? Ũw'o nĩ kana, vai ũmwe witũ ũtonya kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩu na ũĩ wake mwene. (Yel. 10:23) Ĩndĩ no tũvote twamwĩkwatya Ngai atũtongoesye. w16.09 5:1, 2
Ndũkamaime ũndũ ũseo ala maĩlwe nĩw'o.—Nth. 3:27.
Ti laisi aeni mamanyĩe syĩthĩo sya nthĩ ĩla mathamĩĩa. Ngelekany'o ya Luthi no ĩmatethye mũno. Mbee, Luthi nĩwanengete ndaĩa syĩthĩo sya nthĩ ĩla wathamĩĩe, na nĩkyo kĩtumi weetisye mwanya wa kũkolany'a mosyao mũũndanĩ. (Lu. 2:7) O na kau vaĩ mwĩao weetĩkĩlĩtye andũ kũkolany'a ũsyao ũla watiala mũũndanĩ, Luthi ndaaona andũ ta maĩ na thiĩ wake na kwoou aivanga elika mũũndanĩ wene akolanĩtye ateũkũlya. Kelĩ, ĩla woonw'a ũseo nĩwatũngaa mũvea. (Lu. 2:13) Ĩla aeni maatĩĩa ngelekany'o ta ĩsu ya Luthi, nĩ laisi mũno ana-a-asa vamwe na ekali ma kĩsio kĩla maĩ makamanenga ndaĩa. Yeova nĩwonetye mbaa andũ mumo mwingĩ mũno kwa kũmetĩkĩlya mew'e ũvoo mũseo o na ethĩwa nĩ ma mbaĩ yĩva. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtũtanĩthasya mũno. Ĩndĩ no kwĩthĩwa ĩla andũ amwe maĩ nthĩ ya kwoo mataaĩsa kwona mũndũ ũmamanyĩsya Mbivilia, kana makethĩwa mataĩ matonya kũlikana na andũ ma Yeova. Ĩndĩ nũndũ yu ĩtina wa kũthamĩĩa nthĩ yitũ nĩmakwatĩte mwanya wa kwĩthĩwa vamwe naitũ, tyo ũndũ ũseo tũkamatetheesya makew'a ta me mũsyĩ? w16.10 1:17-19

translation:
Love . . . perseveres in all things, and is patient. —1 Cor. 13:4, 5.
God's people demonstrate great courage when facing opposition like that experienced by the Christians in Philippi: "Always rejoice, constantly pray, and give thanks for everything." (Phil. 3:2, 5) Let us be determined to support our brothers and sisters as they face opposition so that they may continue serving Jehovah faithfully. Those who have fallen asleep in death will be awakened and will look forward to seeing God's Kingdom become a reality. (1 Cor. 6:9, 10) So, should we ever stop making efforts, or give up? No, we can imitate those faithful ones who remained loyal despite experiencing hardship and persecution, and we can strengthen ourselves spiritually through prayer and meditation on God's Word. We must keep busy doing what is right so that we may not stumble because of temptation and continue to serve Jehovah zealously, living a life that reflects his moral standards.—1 Pet. 1:15, 16. w16.09 3:9, 10
Also, both young and old . . . praise the name of Jehovah.—Ps. 148:12, 13.
A young Christian girl in France wrote: "Even though we trust in Jehovah, it is still difficult when problems arise, and we feel overwhelmed." She added: "Problems are not something a young person can avoid. They come again and again." A young man in Australia wrote: "It is hard to see how someone could endure pain caused by a broken heart. . . . It feels as if you will never get over it, and you just want to disappear. But remember that there are other joys in life! Problems help us learn valuable lessons, and they can make us more compassionate and understanding toward others who are suffering. And they can also teach us to rely on Jehovah and to seek his guidance." If you are a parent, have you considered how you can help your children cope with disappointments and build resilience? Often, we can best help them by being a good example ourselves. (Jer. 10:23) Indeed, let us continue to pray to God for strength. w16.09 5:1, 2
Always show kindness, because that is what matters most.—Prov. 3:27.
Do not be slow to forgive others. Luther's example should encourage us. Indeed, Luther readily forgave those who wronged him, and this contributed to his maintaining good relationships with people. (Luke 2:7) And just as he showed himself ready to forgive people who did him wrong, Luther also saw people with their problems and listened to them attentively, helping those who were troubled. Truly, showing kindness can move people. (Luke 2:13) Those who imitate Luther's example will find that they too can make friends easily and enjoy satisfying companionship. Jehovah has compassion on many people because of his willingness to forgive, and he wants us to be like him. Forgiveness is something very important. Some may find it difficult to forgive someone who has mistreated them, or they may struggle to associate with fellow believers. But if we want to maintain peace in our congregation, shouldn't we strive to be forgiving, so that we do not spoil the joy we experience together? w16.10 1:17-19

text:
Yĩla mwoosie . . . ĩla ndeto ya ũtũmane wa Ngai, mũtyaamyosa ta ndeto ya andũ, ĩndĩ, o ũndũ ĩtilyĩ w'o, ndeto ya Ngai.—1 Ath. 2:13.
Athũkũmi ma Yeova nĩmanengete yĩla Ĩvuku yake ĩtheu ndaĩa nene mũno. Na nĩkwĩthĩwa twĩ ene naĩ nĩtwĩkalaa tũinengwa ũtao wa Maandĩko. Twĩkaa ata twatawa? Kwaekai twambe kwona ngewa ya Euotia na Sinitike, ala maĩ Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa. Ve thĩna mũnene waumĩlile katĩ wa aka asu. Mathĩna ala maĩ vo katĩ wa Euotia na Sinitike maĩ matonya kwananga vyũ mũuo ũla waĩ kĩkundinĩ. O na kaũ Mbivilia ndĩtũtavĩtye thĩna ũsu watumie kũthi ata, eĩtu-a-asa asu elĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa meetĩkĩlile ũtao ũla mũtũmwa Vaulo wamanengie. (Avi. 4:2, 3) Ikundinĩ sya andũ ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ no kwĩsaa kumĩla thĩna ta ũsu. Ĩndĩ twaatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai, Mbivilia, nĩtũtonya kũema kwĩsa kũvika vau, kana ethĩwa ve thĩna waumĩla no tũũmine. Na ethĩwa nĩtũnengae yĩla Ĩvuku ya Yeova ndaĩa nene, tũkeekaa ũndũ yĩũtũtavya.—Sav. 27:11. w16.11 3:1-3
Ethĩwa nũnyalaa mũthenya wa thĩna, vinya waku nĩ mũnini. —Nth. 24:10.
Vai mũndũ ũtendaa kũthangaaw'a. Na mũno mũno asyai nĩmaĩle kũthangaasya syana syoo. Mwalimũ ũmwe wĩtawa Timothy Evans aeleetye ũũ: "Syana . . . nĩsyendaa kũthangaaw'a o tondũ mũtĩ wendaa kũng'ithw'a. Ĩla kana keekĩwa vinya nĩkew'aa mũyo na kaimanya kaĩ ke vata." Ĩndĩ tũtwĩe ĩvindanĩ ya mĩisyo. Andũ meyendete mo ene, mayĩthĩawa na wendo ũla waĩle kwĩthĩwa mũsyĩ, na maikothaa kwĩkĩana vinya. (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Satani ũla nĩwe Ndevili endaa tũkw'e ngoo nũndũ nĩwĩsĩ kĩu no kĩtume twonza kĩ-veva o na maũndũnĩ angĩ. Satani atatie kũtũla Yovu ngoo kwa kũmũetee mathĩna na kũtuma aneenewa maũndũ mathũku, ĩndĩ nĩwaemiwe nĩ kwĩanĩsya kĩu wendaa. (Yovu 2:3; 22:3; 27:5) No tũsinde mawĩa ma Ndevili kwa kwĩkĩa vinya andũ ma mũsyĩ witũ na ala me kĩkundinĩ. Tweeka ũu tũkeew'aa twĩ atanu na twĩ asũvĩĩku ĩla twĩ mĩsyĩnĩ yitũ na ĩla twĩ Nyũmbanĩ yitũ ya Ũsumbĩ. w16.11 1:4, 6
[Ngai nĩwamwĩtie] mume kĩvindunĩ mũlike kyeninĩ kyake kya ũseng'ya.—1 Vet. 2:9.
Mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1500 aũme amwe me na ũkũmbaũ nĩmambĩĩe kũalyũla Ndeto ya Ngai ithyomonĩ ila syaneenawa nĩ andũ aingĩ. O ũndũ andũ mambĩĩe kũkwata Mbivilia kwa wingĩ now'o mamĩsomie. Na nũndũ wa kũmĩsoma nĩmambĩĩe kũkũlya makũlyo ta aa: 'Nĩ va vau Ndetonĩ ya Ngai vawetete ũvoo wa tũalanĩ? Nĩ va ĩwetete atĩ mũthembi ndaĩle kwĩka misa ya mũkw'ũ ate mũĩve? Na nĩ va ĩwetete ĩũlũ wa vovu na kandinoo?' Atongoi ma ndĩni matalile kĩu ta kũkĩlya nduuthĩ. Nĩ ta meekũlasya andũ ta asu matonya kũũngama ata makamakũlya makũlyo ta asu! Kwoou nĩmatwie kũmosea ĩtambya. Aũme na aka aingĩ nĩmatw'ĩwe kũawa nũndũ wa kũleana na momanyĩsyo ma ĩkanisa. Atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmo matw'ĩĩaa andũ kũawa na ĩndĩ Silikalĩ ĩimoaa. Meekaa ũu nĩ kana matũle andũ ngoo maeke kũsoma Mbivilia na kwĩkĩĩa nzika momanyĩsyo moo. Na mavinda maingĩ kĩeleelo kĩu kyoo nĩkyeanĩaa. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, andũ amwe maĩ na ũkũmbaũ mayaaĩtĩkĩla kwĩkĩwa wia nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. Andũ ta asu maĩ manasama ũw'o ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai na nĩmendaa kũmanya maũndũ maingangĩ! w16.11 4:13
