translation:
Years pass… but God's standard remains the same, higher than man's, yes, because it is God's standard.—1 Thess. 2:13.
Jehovah's Witnesses understand that his Word is very reliable. And we appreciate that we can trust it and remain firm when facing opposition. Will we give up? Let us learn from the examples of Eutychus and Syniticus, but also how Christ was subjected to trials from demons. They had a strong faith despite those difficulties. Perhaps some find it hard to maintain their faith during times of trouble, but let the Bible remind them that even faithful apostles were sometimes discouraged. (Acts 4:2, 3) The love that Jehovah's people have for him motivates them to be courageous. So if we live according to God's standards, the Bible, we can remain courageous and steadfast, even when faced with difficulties, and we will continue to trust in Jehovah's Word.—Ps. 27:11. w16.11 3:1-3
Often, discouragement comes unexpectedly, like a thief. —Prov. 24:10.
Some individuals tend to become despondent. And often they dwell on negative thoughts. One teacher named Timothy Evans said: "Negative… thoughts tend to be self-fulfilling prophecies. But if recognized quickly, they can be challenged and overcome." So let us examine the reasons for our discouragement. Many people today are experiencing stress, are worried about the future, and feel overwhelmed. (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Satan, who is the Devil, wants to take advantage of such feelings to make us lose hope and to engage in wrongdoing. Satan tried to discourage Job by afflicting him with pain and causing him to suffer loss, but Job maintained his integrity. (Job 2:3; 22:3; 27:5) We can resist the influence of the Devil by associating with loyal friends and by keeping spiritually minded. Let us strengthen ourselves and our brothers and sisters so that we can face our challenges and uphold our ministry.—w16.11 1:4, 6
[God comforts] a husband in connection with the death of his wife.—1 Pet. 2:9.
In the 1500's, some husbands along with their families began to honor God's Word, though many opposed them. So husbands began to obtain Bibles so they could read them. And while reading them, they began to ask questions such as: 'How can we honor God's Word and still care for our children? How can we be sure that our faith will not cause us to neglect our responsibilities and become lazy? And how can we deal with temptation and trials?' These questions show a desire to learn. It is because they want to help people overcome problems and find solutions! That is why I was moved to write this. Husbands and others were also encouraged to seek guidance from the congregation. These questions are what motivate people to have confidence in Spiritual matters. This is why many people today are able to read the Bible and apply its principles. But many obstacles to this goal remain. Indeed, some people, along with their families, may feel drawn to Babylon the Great. People like them need to know more about honoring God's Word and should endeavor to learn many things! w16.11 4:13

text:
No wĩthĩwe waakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ũmwe kana o maũndũ maingĩ ala maneenewe mbulosuanĩ ĩno? Ethĩwa ũu nĩ w'o, ndwĩ weka. Athũkũmi aingĩ ma Ngai aĩkĩĩku ma ĩvinda ya tene na ma ũmũnthĩ nĩmonete maũndũ ta asu. Yeova nĩwamatetheeisye kũkĩlya vinya maũndũ ala mamathĩnasya, na no aũtetheesye ũkakĩlya vinya maũndũ ala meũkũthĩny'a.
O ũendeee kũmũsyokea Yeova, nũkũũtetheesya
ŨENDEEE kũmũsyokea Yeova, ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana nũkũũtetheesya. Akaũtetheesya ũmine mawĩmakĩo, ũeke kwĩthĩwa na woo ngoonĩ, na ũikwata mũuo wa kĩlĩko na wa ngoo, ũla mũndũ ũkwataa ĩtina wa kwĩthĩwa na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo. Na ĩndĩ nũtonya kwĩw'a wakwata vinya wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova ĩngĩ wĩ vamwe na athaithi make. Ũndũ ũsu ũkeethĩwa ũvw'anene na wa Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya tene ala mũtũmwa Vetelo wamaandĩkĩie atĩĩ: "Mwaendaa mwaĩte ta malondu; ĩndĩ yu nĩmũmũsyokee Mũĩthi na Mũsyaĩĩsya wa ngoo syenyu."—1 Vetelo 2:25.
Kũmũsyokea Yeova nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mũseo vyũ ũtonya kwĩka. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Kĩtumi nũndũ ũkatanĩthya ngoo ya Yeova. (Nthimo 27:11) Nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kana meko maitũ no mamũtanĩthye Yeova kana makamũthatya. Vate nzika, Yeova ndatũlasimĩthasya tũmwende na kũmũthũkũma. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 30:19, 20) Mũsomi ũmwe wa Mbivilia aisye atĩĩ: "No nginya ũvingũe ngoo yaku nũndũ vai mũndũ ũtonya kũmĩvingũa." No tũnyuve kũvingũa ngoo yitũ kwa kũmũthaitha Yeova kuma ngoonĩ nũndũ nĩtũmwendete. Tweeka ũu, twĩthĩawa twamũnenga Yeova mũthĩnzĩo wa vata mũno, naw'o nĩ ũĩkĩĩku witũ kwake, na nĩtũtanĩthasya ngoo yake mũno. Ũw'o nĩ kana vai ũndũ ũtonya kwĩanana na ũtanu ũla tũkwataa nũndũ wa kũmũthaitha Yeova ũndũ we wendaa.—Meko ma Atũmwa 20:35; Ũvuan'yo 4:11.
O na ĩngĩ, ĩla wĩmũsyokea Yeova, wendi waku wa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe nake ũkeanĩw'a. (Mathayo 5:3) Kwa nzĩa yĩva? Andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ mekũlasya, 'Nĩkĩ twĩ thayũ?' Nĩmethĩawa na mea ma kũmanya kĩeleelo kya thayũ. Andũ methĩawa na wendi ũsu nũndũ moombiwe naw'o. Twoombiwe kwa nzĩa tũtonya kwĩthĩwa twĩ eanĩe ĩla tũũmũthũkũma Yeova. Vai ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kũtuma twĩw'a twĩ eanĩe, kwĩ ũndũ twĩw'aa ĩla twamũthaitha Yeova nũndũ nĩ tũmwendete.—Savuli 63:1-5.
Mwa, manya kana Yeova nũkwenda ũmũsyokee! Nĩkĩ waĩle kũĩkĩĩa ndeto isu? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ũvoo ũla wĩ mbulosuanĩ ĩno waandĩkiwe ĩtina wa kũvoya mũno. Nokwĩthĩwa ũnaeteiwe mbulosua ĩno nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi kana Mũklĩsto o ũngĩ. Na ĩndĩ wendeew'a nĩ kũmĩsoma na kwĩka ũndũ yaĩtye. Maũndũ asu onthe mekũĩkĩĩthya kana Yeova ndaaũlwa nue. Ĩndĩ aendeee na ũkũkusya aũsũvĩĩte nĩ kana ũmũsyokee.—Yoana 6:44.
No tũkwate ũkiakisyo twamanya kana Yeova ndesa kũlwa nĩ athũkũmi make ala maaie. Ũu nĩw'o mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Donna wesie kũmanya. Aisye atĩĩ: "Naĩ natiie ũw'o, ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ nĩnasũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa ĩandĩko ya Savuli 139:23, 24, yĩla yaĩtye: 'Nthiana, ame Ngai, na manya ngoo yakwa: Ndata, na manya mosũanĩo makwa; noisisya ethĩwa ve nzĩa nthũku nthĩnĩ wakwa, noindongoesya nzĩanĩ ya tene na tene.' Nĩneesĩ kana ndyaĩ wa nthĩ, na vandũ vala vaseo naaĩle kwĩthĩwa nĩĩ, nĩ kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma Yeova. Nĩnambĩĩie kwona kana Yeova ndaĩ aaĩsa kũndia, ĩndĩ ninyie naaĩle kũmũsyokea. Na nĩ na ũtanu mũno nũndũ nĩnamũsyokeie!"
"Nĩnambĩĩie kwona kana Yeova ndaĩ aaĩsa kũndia, ĩndĩ ninyie naaĩle kũmũsyokea"
Twĩkũvoyea mũno kuma ngoonĩ wĩthĩwe ĩngĩ na "ũtanu wa Yeova." (Neemia 8:10) Ndũkesa kwĩlila nongi wamũsyokea Yeova.

translation:
Has anyone been caught doing just one thing or many things while preaching this good news? This is so, let's see. Many people of God have stumbled over old temptations and those of life, and they have regretted their actions. Jehovah forgives sins and wrongdoings, and he continues to forgive if one repents and makes amends.
Continue to seek Jehovah, and be forgiven
CONTINUE to seek Jehovah, whether through prayer or by being forgiven. Forgive others readily, do not hold grudges, and take hold of both sides of the matter, so that a person who catches you will find fault with you and praise you. And now we can learn how to avoid stumbling when trying to honor Jehovah more and his organization. This has been shown clearly by ancient Christians, as the apostle Peter wrote: "Be shepherds of God's flock that is under your care; serve as overseers, willingly leading, not because you must, but because you are eager to do so."—1 Peter 2:25.
Seeking Jehovah is something good that should not be abandoned. How then do we do this? By showing appreciation for what Jehovah does. (Proverbs 27:11) We want our hearts to love Jehovah and not disappoint him. Let us remember, Jehovah helps us to go and honor him. (The Proverbial Sayings 30:19, 20) One Bible student said: "No one appreciates his own heart until someone tries to take it." So let us appreciate our hearts by honoring Jehovah always and continuing to walk with him. With this, we show that we love Jehovah deeply, and this pleases him, and we will appreciate his name greatly. That is why it is important to continue to practice what we learn about honoring Jehovah.—Acts of the Apostles 20:35; Revelation 4:11.
Also, if you seek Jehovah, expect to experience trials along with others who are loyal. (Matthew 5:3) Why is this? Many people ask themselves, 'Will we succeed?' It is possible to have doubts and feel discouraged. People may also feel overwhelmed by their circumstances. But we can succeed if we continue to honor Jehovah. Anything that can cause us to fail is less than honoring Jehovah and continuing to walk with him.—Psalm 63:1-5.
Yes, know that Jehovah wants to help you! What will help you to remain steadfast? Consider this: The letter you hold in your hands was written so that you might live. To benefit from this letter, share it with someone or another Christian. And remember to read it carefully and apply what it says. Other things may make you doubt whether Jehovah exists. Those who persevere and continue to study will surely find help.—John 6:44.
So let us examine how we can know that Jehovah cares for his faithful ones. This is what motivated sister Donna to investigate. She says: "I prayed about it, and I often thought of Psalm 139:23, 24, which reads: 'Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me and know my thoughts. See if there is any hurtful way in me, and lead me in the way of everlasting life.' I realized that I needed to pray and ask others to pray for me, because I am one of Jehovah's people. I asked him to show me if he cared for me, and I determined to seek him!"
"I asked him to show me if he cared for me, and I determined to seek him!"
We find joy in sharing our hope with others and in "the strength of Jehovah." (Nehemiah 8:10) Take time to meditate on why you serve Jehovah.

text:
NTHĨNĨ wa Mbivilia ũkeethĩa ĩvuku yĩtawa Luthi. Ĩvuku yĩu yĩna ngewa ya andũ ma mũsyĩ maĩ thayũ ĩvinda yĩla Aisilaeli maĩ na asili. Luthi aĩ mũndũ mũka wa mũika kuma nthĩ ya Moavi. We ndaĩ wa andũ ma Ngai ma nthĩ ya Aisilaeli. Ĩndĩ yĩla Luthi weemanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai wa w'o, amwenda mũno vyũ. Naomi aĩ mũndũ mũka mũkũũ na nĩwatetheeisye Luthi kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova.
Naomi aĩ Mũisilaeli. We na mũũme na ana moo elĩ nĩmathamĩĩie nthĩ ya Moavi ĩvinda yĩmwe kwaĩ yũa nthĩ ya Isilaeli. Na ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe mũũme wa Naomi akw'a. Ĩtina ana make elĩ matwaa eĩtu Amoavi meetawa Luthi na Oliva. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ta myaka 10, ana asu elĩ ma Naomi makw'a. Naomi na eĩtu asu elĩ meewie kyeva ta kĩ! Naomi aĩ atonya kwĩka ata yu?
Mũthenya ũmwe Naomi nĩwatwie kũthi kyalo kĩasa asyoke mũsyĩ kwa andũ moo. Luthi na Oliva nĩmendaa kwĩkala nake, na kwoou o namo mathi nake. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kũendanga ĩvinda ĩnini, Naomi eethyũũa kwelekela eĩtu asu na amea: 'Endai mũsyoke mũsyĩ na mũyĩkala na aa-inyia menyu.'
Naomi nĩwamamumunyie eĩtu asu amatiĩe ũvoo. Na ĩndĩ mambĩĩa kũĩa nũndũ nĩmamwendete Naomi mũno, na masya: 'Aiee! Ithyĩ twĩthi vamwe naku kwa andũ maku.' Ĩndĩ Naomi asũngĩa: 'No nginya mũsyoke, eĩtu makwa. Ũkeethĩwa waĩlu kwenyu mwĩ mũsyĩ.' Kwoou Oliva akwata nzĩa enũka. Ĩndĩ Luthi alea kũthi.
Nake Naomi eethyũũa amwelekela na asya: 'Sisya Oliva nĩwathi. O naku mũatĩĩe mwĩnũkany'e.' Ĩndĩ Luthi asũngĩa: 'Eka ũnthing'ĩĩsya ngũtie! Eka nĩendany'e naku. Vala wĩthi ngathi, na vala wĩĩkala ngekala. Andũ maku makeethĩwa andũ makwa, na Ngai waku akeethĩwa Ngai wakwa. Vala wĩkw'ĩĩa novo nĩkw'ĩĩa, na novo nĩthikwa.' Yĩla Luthi waisye ũu, Naomi ndaatata ĩngĩ kũmwĩa asyoke mũsyĩ.
Ĩtina vyũ aka asu elĩ nĩmavikie Isilaeli. Na matũa kũu. Na vate kweteela Luthi ambĩlĩlya kũthũkũma mĩũndanĩ, nũndũ yaĩ ĩvinda ya kũketha mbaale. Mũndũ ũmwe weetawa Mboasi nĩwamũekie ombany'e iia sya mbaale mĩũndanĩ yake. We nĩwĩsĩ inyia wa Mboasi aĩ ũũ? Aĩ Laavi ũla wa ndũa ya Yeliko.
Mũthenya ũmwe Mboasi nĩweeie Luthi: 'Nĩnĩw'ĩte ũvoo w'onthe ĩũlũ waku, na ũndũ wĩthĩĩtwe wĩ mũseo kwa Naomi. Nĩnĩsĩ ũndũ watiie ĩthe na inyia waku na nthĩ yaku, na ũndũ wookie kwĩkala na andũ ũtamesĩ nongi. Yeova nĩakũathime!'
Nake Luthi asũngĩa: 'Nĩwĩthĩĩtwe wĩna tei kwakwa, mwĩaĩi. Nĩwatuma nĩw'a nesa nũndũ wa nzĩa ĩla waneena nakwa.' Mboasi nĩwamwendie Luthi mũno, na ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini matwaana. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatanĩthisye Naomi mũno vyũ! Ĩndĩ Naomi nĩwatanie ĩa mũno yĩla Luthi na Mboasi makwatie mwana woo wa mbee weetawa Oveti. Ĩtina Oveti nĩwatw'ĩkie ũmae wa Ndaviti, ũla tũkemanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wake ĩtina.
Ĩvuku ya Mbivilia ya Luthi.
Makũlyo
- Naomi esie kũtũa ata nthĩ ya Amoavi?
- Luthi na Oliva naaũ?
- Luthi na Oliva meekie ata yĩla Naomi wameie kĩla ũmwe nĩasyoke kwa andũ moo?
- Mboasi nũũ, na atetheeisye Luthi na Naomi ata?
- Kana kala Mboasi na Luthi masyaie keetawa ata, na nĩkĩ twaĩlĩtwe nĩkũkalilikana?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Luthi 1:1-17.
Nĩ ũlũmany'o mwaũ wa wendo mũseo vyũ ũla Luthi woonanisye? (Lu. 1:16, 17)
Mosũanĩo ma Luthi meonany'a nesa ata mwelekelo wa "malondu angĩ" kwa etĩkĩw'a mauta ala me ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ũmũnthĩ? (Yoa. 10:16; Nzek. 8:23)
- Soma Luthi 2:1-23.
Luthi oonanisye ngelekany'o myaũ nzeo kwa aka ma mũika ũmũnthĩ? (Lu. 2:17, 18; Nth. 23:22; 31:15)
- Soma Luthi 3:5-13.
Mboasi aĩ na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa wendi wa Luthi wa kũtwawa nĩwe vandũ va mwanake wa mũika?
Ngelekany'o ya Luthi yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa kũlũmany'a nũndũ wa wendo? (Lu. 3:10; 1 Ako. 13:4, 5)
- Soma Luthi 4:7-17.
Aũme Aklĩsto ũmũnthĩ matonya kwĩthĩwa mailyĩ ta Mboasi ata? (Lu. 4:9, 10; 1 Tim. 3:1, 12, 13; 5:8)

translation:
The people of Bethlehem grieved when they heard about Ruth. She was a woman from Moab who went with her mother-in-law to live among the Israelites after her husband died. Ruth was a good person who honored the traditions of her ancestors, the Moabites. She decided to worship the God of Israel. And so she said, "Your God will be my God." Naomi was an older woman, and she encouraged Ruth to worship the Lord.
Naomi was an Israelite. She had a husband and two sons who moved to Moab because of famine in Israel. After some time, Naomi's husband died. She was left with her two daughters-in-law, Ruth and Orpah. After about ten years, both of Naomi's sons died. Naomi was devastated and asked, "How can I go back home?"
One day, Naomi decided to return to her homeland with her daughters-in-law. Ruth and Orpah wanted to stay with her and begged her to let them come along. After much persuasion, Naomi told her daughters-in-law, "Go back to your families and find happiness with new husbands."
Naomi pleaded with her daughters-in-law to leave her. But Ruth insisted on staying with Naomi, saying, "Please don't ask me to leave you! Wherever you go, I will go. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God. Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord punish me severely if anything separates us!" Seeing Ruth's determination, Naomi stopped urging her to return.
Then Naomi said to Orpah, "Go back home, my daughter. Your sister-in-law wants you to stay with your own people." But Ruth replied, "Don't urge me to abandon you or turn back from following you. For wherever you go, I will go; and wherever you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God. I will remain loyal to you until death separates us—only death will separate us!" So Ruth made this vow, and Naomi no longer tried to persuade her to return.
They traveled together until they arrived in Israel. They came during the barley harvest. Boaz, a relative of Naomi's late husband, owned fields nearby. He was a kind man, and he allowed Ruth to gather leftover grain in his fields. Who was Boaz? He was a descendant of Elimelech.
One day Boaz spoke to Ruth: "I have heard about everything you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died. You left your father and mother and your homeland and came here to live among people you didn't know before. May the Lord reward you for what you have done! May you find full reward in the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."
Boaz continued, "I want you to continue working in my fields until the entire harvest is finished. Stay close to my young women, and let them help you. I have given orders to my men not to bother you. Whenever you are thirsty, drink from their water jars." Boaz's kindness greatly pleased Naomi. She realized how fortunate she was to have such a devoted daughter-in-law. Eventually, Ruth married Boaz, and they had a son named Obed, who became the grandfather of King David, a great leader of Israel.
The story of Ruth.
Questions
- Did Naomi try to convince Ruth to return to her people?
- What about Ruth and Orpah?
- Did Ruth and Orpah both promise to stay with Naomi, each insisting on going with her people?
- Who was Boaz, and did he help Ruth and Naomi?
- Were Boaz and Ruth ever married, and why is this important?
Further Questions
- Read Ruth 1:1-17.
What does Ruth's loyal love teach us about showing devotion to others? (Lu. 1:16, 17)
How can we imitate Ruth's example of being willing to make sacrifices for those we love? (Joh. 10:16; Pro. 8:23)
- Read Ruth 2:1-23.
In what ways did Ruth show diligence and hard work? (Ru. 2:17, 18; Num. 23:22; 31:15)
- Read Ruth 3:5-13.
Did Boaz recognize Ruth's willingness to care for his family?
What does Ruth's conduct teach us about the importance of modesty? (Ru. 3:10; 1Co. 13:4, 5)
- Read Ruth 4:7-17.
Is Jesus Christ related to Boaz through his genealogy? (Ru. 4:9, 10; 1Ti. 3:1, 12, 13; 5:8)

text:
Nĩnamũmanthie Yeova, na anzũngĩa, na ambonokya kuma w'ĩanĩ wakwa w'onthe.—Sav. 34:4.
O naitũ no tũmũtulũĩle Yeova mavata maitũ, twĩsĩ nesa kana nũkũtwĩthukĩĩsya na aitũlũlũmĩlya tũendeee kũmĩĩsya twĩ atanu. Na ĩndĩ ĩla mboya sitũ syasũngĩwa, mũĩkĩĩo witũ nũendeeaa kũlũlũmĩla. (1 Yoa. 5:14, 15) Nũndũ mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kĩlungu kĩmwe kya ũsyao wa veva, nĩtwaĩle kũendeea 'kũvoya' Ngai atũnenge veva wake mũtheu, o tondũ Yesũ watũthuthisye twĩkae. (Luka 11:9, 13) Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle o kũvoyaa kwondũ wa mavata maitũ me moka. Kĩla mũthenya no tũmũtũngĩae Yeova mũvea na tũkamũkatha nũndũ wa 'mawĩa make ma ũsengy'a,' namo nĩ "maingĩ mũno." (Sav. 40:5) O na ĩngĩ ĩla tũũvoya nĩtwaĩle 'kũmalilikanaa ala ove, ta twovetwe vamwe nao.' O na eka ũu, nĩtwaĩle kũvoyaa kwondũ wa ana-a-asa nthĩ yonthe, na mũno mũno 'ala me na ũtongoi ĩũlũ witũ.' Tũtanaa ta kĩ ĩla Yeova wasũngĩa mboya sitũ vamwe na sya ana-a-asa nthĩ yonthe!—Aevl. 13:3, 7. w16.10 3:8, 9
Nĩmũtangĩĩĩtwe na mumo kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo; naw'o ndumĩte kwa inyw'ĩ ene, nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai.—Aev. 2:8.
Ũmũnthĩ andũ ma Yeova nĩmethĩĩtwe mayonany'a nĩmaĩkĩĩte vyũ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nũsumbĩkĩte. Kĩu kĩtumĩte kwĩthĩwa na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa mbee wa milioni nyanya ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, ala mekalaa na mũuo na ngwatanĩo ikundinĩ syoo. Nĩmonanasya ũsyao wa veva wa Ngai kwa nzĩa nene mũno. (Aka. 5:22, 23) Ũsu nĩ wonany'o mũnene ta kĩ wa Aklĩsto me mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o na wendo wa w'o! Vai mũndũ wĩsa kwasya kana ũu w'onthe wĩanĩĩte nũndũ wake. Ngai e weka no we ũtonya kwĩanĩsya kĩu. Wĩa ũsu wa ũsengy'a nũetae "syĩtwa kwa Yeova, wonan'yo wa tene na tene ũla ũtakavetwa." (Isa. 55:13) Yeova nũkũendeea kũtetheesya andũ aingĩ mamesye mũĩkĩĩo vala ũĩ nginya ĩla nthĩ yonthe ĩkausũa andũ mate naĩ, alũngalu, na atanu, na kĩu kĩikalea kũtuma ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩtaĩwa tene na tene. Ekai ĩndĩ tũtw'e kũendeea kwonany'a kana nĩtũĩkĩĩaa mawatho ma Yeova! w16.10 4:18, 19
Andũ amwe . . . maendaa katĩ wenyu ũndũ ũtaĩle.—2 Ath. 3:11.
Nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia ĩla tũnengawe nĩ atumĩa. Kwalilikana ũndũ Vaulo waisye ĩũlũ wa ala matekuaa nesa kĩkundinĩ. Awetie amwe "[maĩ] elikya maũndũnĩ ma andũ angĩ." No nginya andũ asu methĩwe makanĩtw'e nĩ atumĩa ĩndĩ makalea kwĩthukĩĩsya ũtao woo na makaendeea na mwĩkalĩle ũsu. Kĩkundi kyaaĩle kwĩkana ata na andũ ta asu? Vaulo anenganie mwolooto ũũ: "Mũsisyei mũndũ ũsu, mũikavulane nake." Ĩndĩ amina kũmanenga mwolooto ũsu nĩwasyokie amea maikatale mũndũ ũsu ta mũmaitha. (2 Ath. 3:11-15) Ũmũnthĩ ũũ atumĩa nĩmatonya kumya ũvoo wa kũkany'a kĩkundi ĩũlũ wa mũndũ ũte kwenda kũekana na mwĩkalĩle ũtonya kũetee kĩkundi nthoni, ta kwĩvaany'a na mũndũ ũte Ngũsĩ. (1 Ako. 7:39) We wĩkaa ata weew'a ũkany'o ta ũsu? Ethĩwa nĩwĩsĩ ũla ũkũwetwa ũvoonĩ ũsu, we nũtataa ndũkavulane nake maũndũnĩ angĩ eka ma kĩ-veva? Weeka ũu, ũkeethĩwa ũimũtetheesya kũmanya kana mwĩkalĩle wake ndũmwendeeasya Yeova na nũtonya kũmũũmĩsya we mwene, na kĩu nĩkĩtonya kũmũtetheesya avĩndũke. w16.11 2:13

translation:
I sought Jehovah, and He listened, and delivered me from all my anxieties.—Ps. 34:4.
And if we confide in Jehovah our troubles, whether they are small or we feel overwhelmed by them, we can continue trusting in Him fully. And when that day arrives, our heart will encourage us to keep on persevering. (1 John 5:14, 15) But if our heart is just one aspect of our spiritual vitality, we should strive to 'ask' God to give us more vital force, so that Jesus might lead us to live accordingly. (Luke 11:9, 13) When we ask, we are expressing confidence in the fulfillment of our requests. Every day we should thank Jehovah sincerely and remind ourselves of his 'wonderful works,' which are "many." (Ps. 40:5) And also, what we ask should be to 'align our will with His, so that we may be united with Him.' And further than that, we should ask for help regarding all our brothers, and especially those who are 'suffering because of their loyalty.' Let us then remember that Jehovah listens to our prayers along with those of all our brothers!—Heb. 13:3, 7. w16.10 3:8, 9
We are motivated by love for our brothers; and I myself, I urge each one of you, practice self-control—God's standard.—Eph. 2:8.
The servants of Jehovah have been made outstandingly evident by their zeal and by God's spirit that empowers them. This has led to the association with millions of people throughout the entire earth, who have become loyal despite opposition and persecution. I deeply appreciate God's spiritual vitality. (Rev. 5:22, 23) Truly this is a great sign of the Christlike love of those who love him! May everyone examine himself to see whether he is measuring up to this standard. God wants us to take advantage of this opportunity. The song of praise invites us to say, "Give thanks to Jehovah, the Everlasting One, whose loving-kindness endures forever." (Isa. 55:13) Jehovah continues to strengthen many people spiritually, so that the whole earth may know about Him, learn about Him, and trust in Him, and this results in making His name endure forever. So let us continue striving to show appreciation for Jehovah's provisions! w16.10 4:18, 19
Some among you . . . are walking disorderly.—2 Thess. 3:11.
I am unwilling to correct the Bible's examples, but let us examine them carefully. In contrast, Paul himself often took the initiative to show kindness. He advised some: "[Go] back to your own homes." Now may those people become thoughtful and use their discernment to see how they can walk orderly and continue progressing spiritually. Should a congregation tolerate anyone who does not do so? Paul gave this direction: "Associate yourselves with him, and do not keep company with him." Let each one examine his own conduct so that he does not stumble and cause his brother to stumble. (2 Thess. 3:11-15) This example shows that Christians should be willing to help a fellow believer who has stumbled, but they should not associate with someone who persistently refuses to conform to God's standards, such as Stephen. (Acts 7:39) Will you also take such a stand? Consider what will strengthen your faith, and then determine whether you can kindly discuss matters with him further. Remember, if you help him to appreciate Jehovah and to desire to please Him personally, you will be helping him to save himself. w16.11 2:13

text:
Nĩ w'o atĩ ĩvindanĩ ya tene mũndũ aĩ atonya kũthi mũũndanĩ weene akavuĩa ĩia?
YESŨ awetie ndeto ii syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 13:24-26: "Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtu ũilyĩ ta mũndũ ũla wavuĩie mbeũ nzeo mũũndanĩ wake: ĩndĩ andũ makomete, mũmaitha wake ooka na avuĩĩa ĩthaaa nganũnĩ na athi. Ĩndĩ syamea na syamesya mathangũ na syasyaa iia, nĩvo ĩndĩ ĩthaaa yoonekie nayo." Aandĩki me kĩvathũkany'o nĩmethĩĩtwe na nzika ethĩwa kwa w'o ki ũndũ ũsu Yesũ wawetie ngelekany'onĩ ĩsu nĩweekĩkaa, ĩndĩ maandĩko ma tene ma Alomi ala maeleetye mĩao meonany'a kana ũsu nĩ ũndũ weekĩkaa.
Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩeleetye ndeto ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ yaĩtye: "Kũvuĩa nyeki [darnel] mũũndanĩ nĩ kana wĩyĩĩvanĩsye . . . kwaĩ kũvatane mĩaonĩ ya Lomi. Na woona vaĩ na vata wa kwĩkĩa mwĩao ũkonetye ũndũ ũsu, nĩ kwonany'a kana ũndũ ũsu nĩwakothaa kwĩkĩka." Mũsomi ũmwe wa maũndũ ma mĩao wĩtawa Alastair Kerr aeleisye kana mwakanĩ wa 533 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, mũsumbĩki wa Lomi weetawa Justinian nĩwaandĩkie kavuku (Digest), kala kaeleetye kwa ũkuvĩ mĩao ya Lomi na maũndũ mana mawetiwe nĩ asomi angĩ ma mĩao ma ĩvinda yĩla mĩao ya Lomi yaĩ mĩseo vyũ (ta mwaka wa 100-250 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa). Kwosana na kavuku kau (Digest, 22.214.171.124), mũsomi wa mĩao weetawa Ulpian nĩwawetie ĩkoani yasililwe nĩ mũtongoi wa Lomi wa myaka ya 100 na kĩndũ ũla weetawa Celsus. Ĩkoani yĩu yakonetye mũndũ waendie avuĩa ĩia mũũndanĩ weene na lĩu ũla waĩ vo waanangĩka. Kavuku kau kawetie nzĩa ila mĩao yaĩ ĩtonya kũtethya mwene mũũnda, kana ũla waũkomboete, nĩ kana aĩvwe lĩu wake nĩ ũla ũmũtetheisye wĩa ũsu mũthũku.
Ethĩwa ũndũ ũthũkĩte ũu nĩweekĩkie kĩsionĩ kyasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Lomi, no twasye kana kĩla Yesũ wawetie ĩla ngelekany'onĩ nĩ kĩndũ kyeekĩkaa.
Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa silikalĩ ya Lomi yanengete anene ma Ayuti ala maĩ ngalĩko ya Yutia ũkũmũ wĩana ata?
ĨVINDANĨ yĩu kĩsio kya Yutia kyasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Alomi, na kyeethĩawa na ngavana Mũlomi ũla waũngamĩe asikalĩ aingĩ. Wĩa mũnene wa ngavana ũsu waĩ wa kũkolany'a koti ũla Lomi yendaa vamwe na kũĩkĩĩthya mĩao nĩyaatĩĩwa na kwĩ mũuo. Alomi mayanengae mwanya mũndũ o na wĩva ũkũtũla mĩao na nĩmasilĩlaa andũ ala mekwananga mũuo. Ĩndĩ Alomi nĩmatiaa tũmaũndũ tũla twa kĩla mũthenya mokonĩ ma Ayuti ala manengetwe ũkũmũ kĩsionĩ kyu kya Yutia.
Ĩla Nzama ya Ayuti yatalawa tayo koti ũla mũnene vyũ wa Ayuti, na nĩyo yaumasya sila maũndũnĩ makonetye mĩao ya Kĩyuti. Ĩtheo wayo vaĩ koti ingĩ nini syaĩ kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o kĩsionĩ kyonthe kya Yutia. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa kaingĩ makoani ala manini na makoani angĩ makonetye ũtũli wa mĩao maminĩawa kotinĩ isu mateũlikĩlĩĩlwa nĩ anene ma Lomi. Ĩndĩ kĩndũ kĩmwe koti sya Ayuti itaĩ syĩka nĩ kũtw'ĩĩa ala matũlĩte mĩao kũawa. Kĩu nĩ kĩndũ Alomi mavangĩte kana no mo maaĩle kwĩka. Eka ĩvinda yĩla ala me Nzamanĩ ya Ayuti masilĩile Sitivini na mavanga akimangwe, vai ĩvinda yĩngĩ yĩsĩkĩe nesa Ayuti maaĩyosea ĩtambya yĩu.—Meko 6:8-15; 7:54-60.
Kwoou no twasye kana Nzama ya Ayuti nĩyanengetwe ũkũmũ mũnene. Ĩndĩ mũsomi ũmwe wĩtawa Emil Schürer aisye: "Thĩna ũmwe mũnene [Nzama] ĩsu yoonaa nĩ kana anene ma Lomi maĩ matonya kũlikĩlĩĩla ĩkoani ĩla mavanga na maiendeea mateũkũlw'a, o tondũ meekaa ĩla meesikwa ũndũ ũla wĩkĩtwe nũtonya kũetee silikalĩ mũisyo." Ĩvinda yĩmwe anene ma Lomi malikĩlĩĩile ĩkoani ya Ayuti nĩ ĩvinda ya Kilautiosi Lisiasi. Mũnene ũsu atangĩĩie mũtũmwa Vaulo kuma mokonĩ ma Ayuti ĩla wamanyie nĩ laiaa wa Lomi.—Meko 23:26-30.

translation:
Is it possible that someone sows among their enemies and then harvests wheat?
JESUS gave this illustration recorded in Matthew 13:24-26: "The Kingdom of the Heavens is like a man who sowed good seed in his field; but while men were sleeping, an enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and went away. When the growth began to sprout and produce fruit, then the weeds appeared also. And the master's slaves came and said to him, 'Sir, did you not sow fine wheat in your field? Then where did the weeds come from?' He said, 'An enemy must have done this.'" The writer explains that this illustrates what will happen when Jesus settles accounts, so that the scriptures of God may be fulfilled which were spoken through the prophets.
One publication stated this illustration as follows: "To put darnel [weed] among wheat is…to cause trouble for the landowners. And those who do this and those who know how to recognize such a thing, it is a sign that something wicked is happening." One legal scholar named Alastair Kerr explained that around 533 C.E., Emperor Justinian of Rome wrote a digest (Digest), which included laws relating to Roman land and matters pertaining to what scholars call the imperial constitutions (from about 100-250 C.E.). According to that digest (Digest, 22.214.171.124), a legal expert named Ulpian reported a case decided by a Roman judge some 100 years earlier involving a man named Celsus. That case involved a person who poisoned another, and the law allowed the injured party to seek compensation. That digest further states that laws existed regarding crops that could not be planted near others, or that damaged them, or that caused loss to the owner.
However, this practice seems to have been condemned by Rome, and we read that Jesus spoke of it as something harmful.
Does the account in the letters of Paul indicate that the early Christians were concerned about weeds in their fields?
That account concerning the field was condemned by Romans, and it was addressed by Governor Pliny the Younger, who governed several provinces. The governor's concern was that Rome wanted to maintain order and to prevent disturbances from arising. Romans often took action against anyone they considered a threat to peace and tranquility. Thus, Pliny sent reports to Emperor Trajan detailing his handling of Christians and requesting guidance. In fact, Pliny requested information on what should be done with those accused of being Christians.
The case of the Christians was brought up because of complaints made by people who hated them. It seemed good to him to investigate thoroughly everything related to the accusation against the Christians.
The province of Asia had suffered greatly because of the governor of Asia, and it was also causing trouble in the city of Ephesus. What did he do to find out the truth about the accusations against the Christians? They gathered in large numbers in private homes and in other places, meeting early in the morning to worship God. And it was reported that they refused to partake of the emperor's sacrifices and denounced the customs of the nations. So, one thing that caused trouble for the Christians was their refusal to offer sacrifices to the emperors. This is what Romans resented. But regarding the matter of the Christians, Governor Pliny wrote to Emperor Trajan asking for advice. He reported that Stephen and others had been arrested and were being interrogated, and he said that many Christians had fled and denied being Christians.—Acts 6:8-15; 7:54-60.
However, we read that the case of the Christians was investigated carefully. One scholar named Emil Schürer stated: "One important point [regarding the Christians] is that Roman governors often took action when they received reports of disturbances and unrest, especially if such reports involved violations of religious customs." A Roman governor investigated the Christians in the city of Ephesus—Governor Claudius Lysias. This governor sent Paul under guard to Caesarea, where he would be tried before Felix, a Roman official.—Acts 23:26-30.

text:
Ete kyeni kyaku na w'o waku; indongoesye.—Sav. 43:3.
Yeova nĩ "Ngai wa w'o." (Sav. 31:5) Nĩwendete syana syake na nĩwendete mũno kũsyony'a kyeni kyake kya ũla w'o nĩ kana kĩitongoesye kĩla mũthenya, na mũno mũno maũndũnĩ ma ũthaithi. Nĩ ũw'o wĩva Yeova ũtũmanyĩĩtye, na kĩu kĩtũtetheeasya ata kũmanya kana nũtwendete? Mbee, Yeova nũtũmanyĩĩtye ũla w'o ĩũlũ wake. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtũtavĩtye ũndũ wĩtawa. Ĩsyĩtwa yĩu yake yĩandĩkĩtwe mavinda maingĩ Mbivilianĩ kwĩ ĩsyĩtwa yĩngĩ o na yĩva. Kũtũtavya ĩsyĩtwa yake nĩ wonany'o wa kana eenda tũmũmanye, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu nĩwosete ĩtambya ya kũtũthengeea. (Yak. 4:8) O na ĩngĩ Yeova nũtũtavĩtye we nĩ Ngai ũilyĩ ata. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla twasisya wũmbi wake nĩtũmanyaa kana e vinya na nĩ mũĩ, na we mwene nĩwonanĩtye Maandĩkonĩ nesa kana asilaa katĩ, na mũno mũno nĩwonanĩtye kana nũtwendete vyũ. (Alo. 1:20) Ailyĩ o ta mũsyai wĩ vinya na mũĩ ĩndĩ ũte kyende na wendete syana syake. Mũsyai wa mũthemba ũsu nũtumaa syana syake syenda kũtuma ndũũ nake. w15 9/15 4:8, 9
Kw'oko kwa Yeova kũkamanyĩka kwa athũkũmi make.—Isa. 66:14.
Andũ aingĩ monaa Ngai ndalũnganaa na kĩla andũ maendeesye. O na amwe maĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai ndamakaw'a nĩ mathĩna ala makwataa andũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩla kĩuutani kĩthũku mũno (Super Typhoon Haiyan) kyakũnie kĩsio kĩmwe kĩnene kya nthĩ ya Philippines kwĩ Mwei wa 11, 2013, meya wa mũsyĩ ũmwe mũnene aisye: "No nginya Ngai ethĩwe eeĩ kũndũ kũngĩ." Naw'o mwĩkalĩle wa andũ angĩ wonanasya maikũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai nĩwene kĩla mekwĩka. (Isa. 26:10, 11; 3 Yoa. 11) Andũ ta asu mailyĩ ta ala mũtũmwa Vaulo wamawetie akyasya kana "[nĩmaleile] kwĩthĩwa na Ngai ũmanyinĩ woo." Asu Vaulo wawetaa 'mausũĩtwe nĩ ũla ũte ũlũngalu w'onthe, na ũthũku, na ĩtomo, na wai.' (Alo. 1:28, 29) Nata naitũ? Twĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na asu mawetwa vau ĩũlũ nũndũ nĩtwĩsĩ kana Yeova ethĩawa ene kyonthe kĩla tũkwĩka. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Nĩtũĩkĩĩaa kana Yeova nĩwendeeaw'a nithyĩ na kana kw'oko kwake nĩkũtũtethasya? w15 10/15 1:1-3
Nĩngũkwon'ya mũĩkĩĩo wakwa na meko makwa.—Yak. 2:18.
Kũtavany'a nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe nzeo ya kwonany'a kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nĩkwĩthĩwa mũndũ ũkũtethya wĩa ũsu no nginya ethĩwe aĩkĩĩe kana Ngai akaete mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ ĩno ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩle na "ndũkekala." (Ava. 2:3) Kwoou nzĩa ĩmwe tũtonya kũtũmĩa nĩ kana tũthime ũndũ mũĩkĩĩo witũ ũlũmĩte nĩ kũsisya ũndũ twĩthĩawa twĩyumĩtye wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Ithyĩ nĩtwĩkaa ũndũ tũtonya wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a, kwa ngelekany'o, ta kwongela ĩvinda yĩla tũtũmĩaa wĩanĩ ũsu? (2 Ako. 13:5) Vate nzika, 'kumbũla na kanyw'a kũvikĩa ũtangĩĩo' nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe nene ya kwonany'a kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ngoonĩ. (Alo. 10:10) No twonany'e twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ĩla tũkũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna ma kĩla mũthenya. Ethĩwa twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, ĩla twawaa, twakw'a ngoo, twathelelwa, kana twakwatwa nĩ thĩna o ũngĩ, tũkeethĩawa twĩsĩ nesa kana Yeova na Mwana wake mailea "kũtũtethya ĩvinda ya vata." (Aevl. 4:16) O na nĩtwonanasya twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu ĩla twavoya Yeova atũtetheesye maũndũnĩ onthe eka o ma kĩ-veva. w15 10/15 2:12-14

translation:
Send out Your light and Your truth—they led me.—Ps. 43:3.
Jehovah is "the God of truth." (Ps. 31:5) He guides his sons and he guides people to know his truth about life—yes, constantly, and always in an appropriate way. It is because Jehovah knows us that we can confidently approach him, and why should we not trust that he guides us? Indeed, Jehovah knows our life pattern. For example, we may be facing a difficult situation. His promise has been recorded in many books at Bethel and also from branches. To trust his promise means that perhaps we will come to know him better, and for this reason it becomes a source of strength for us. (Jas. 4:8) And further, Jehovah knows what kind of God he is, uniquely. For instance, when we reject his standards, we realize they are beneficial and right, and he himself shows us the Scriptures are reliable, whether they are easy or hard to understand, and always he shows us that he guides us. (Rev. 1:20) Truly, then, how good it is to know that he leads his sons! The faith of this loyal one caused his son to go forth to carry out his purpose. w15 9/15 4:8, 9
Jehovah's love is made evident through his servants.—Isa. 66:14.
Many people view God as being partial to certain individuals. And some believe that God is unjust and favors those who please him. For example, when a very powerful typhoon (Super Typhoon Haiyan) struck a large part of the Philippines on November 11, 2013, the mayor of one big city said: "I don't think God answered my prayers." Yet, many others have found comfort in knowing that God cares for everyone. (Isa. 26:10, 11; 3 John 11) People like the apostle Paul testified that he had "[failed] to be worthy of God's kindness." Apostle Paul spoke of 'struggling with the desire for what is wrong, and with sickness, and with temptations.' (Rev. 1:28, 29) Why is that? Let us consider this and the experiences of faithful ones so that we may see that Jehovah answers everything we ask of him. In fact, the question is: Do we believe that Jehovah cares for us and that his love strengthens us? w15 10/15 1:1-3
Demonstrate your faith by your works.—Jas. 2:18.
Lack of activity is like saying we have faith when we do not. Shouldn't we prove this to be true? A person may say his words are fine, yet his actions show he does not really care whether God accepts his devotion or not—he simply says, "I believe." (Acts 2:3) How then can we show that we mean what we say, that our faith is genuine? To some extent, doesn't the way we act reveal what is in our heart regarding lack of activity? (2 Cor. 13:5) Indeed, 'speaking and drinking come about through knowledge,' so it is also with demonstrating faith. (Prov. 10:10) And if we demonstrate faith, being united with others, if we are reproved, corrected, or disciplined, we will feel comforted knowing that Jehovah and his Son exercise "favor toward us" when they correct us. (Heb. 4:16) Also, if we are honest with ourselves regarding this matter, we will see that Jehovah has helped us to make progress, either gradually or quickly. w15 10/15 2:12-14

text:
ĩkũlyo
Mũklisto Nũũ?
Ũsungio
Asomi (Dictionary) maasyaa mũklisto no ta mũndũ ũla ũmbũlaa kũĩkĩa Yesũ ta Klisto kana momanyĩsyo ma Yesũ. Onakaũ ũu ni mwambĩlĩĩlyo museo ũu ti ũelesyo mwĩanĩu kwianana na mbivilia.
Ndeto mũklisto ĩtũmĩkĩte mavinda atatũ ũtianĩonĩ mweu (meko ma atũme 11:26; 26:28; 1 vetelo 4:16). Aatĩĩi mambee ma Yesũ nĩmomeetiwe aklisto ma mbee kuya Antioch (Meko ma Atũme11:26) nũndũ mũtũo woo, meko na kũneena kwoo kwai ta Kwa Klisto. Ndeto "mũklisto" ũelesyo wayo nĩ, kwĩthĩwa ngwatanĩonĩ na klisto kana mũatĩĩi wa klisto.
Kwa ĩvĩnda ndeto mũklisto nĩyaaisye kĩmanza kĩnene Kya ũelesyo wayo na nĩtũmĩkaa mũno kũelesya mũndũ mũthaithi kana wĩ meko maseo , ĩndĩ nũtonya kwitha e mũatĩĩi kana ate mũatĩĩi wa Yesũ klisto. Ve andũ aingi ala matamũĩkĩĩa Yesũ Klisto metalaa ta aklisto nũndũ nĩmaendaa kanisani kana mekalaa nthĩ ya "ũklisto". kũthi kanisani kũyĩũtwĩkĩthya mũklisto ota ũndũ kũthi vala ngalĩ iseuvĩawa kũtaũtwikithya ngali. Kwĩthĩwa ũyĩtanĩw'a na kanisa, kũthĩ ũthaithi mavinda Kwa mavinda, na kũnengane kwondũ wa wĩa wa kanisa kũyĩũtw'ikĩthya muklisto.
Mbivilia ĩtũvundiasya kana meko maitũ maseo maituma twitĩkĩlwa nĩ Ngai. Tito 3:5 yiasya "Nĩtwatangĩĩiwe, ndaatũtangĩĩa nũndũ wa meko maseo ona meva ala twekĩte, ĩndĩ ni kwondũ wa tei wake mwene, kwĩsĩla Kwa Veva wake mũtheu, ũla ũtũtusaa ũsyao mweũ Kwa kũthesya ngoo sitũ". kwou mũklisto ni mũndũ ũsyaitwe ĩngĩ nĩ Ngai (Yoana3:3; 3:7; 1Vetelo 1:23) na akaia mũĩkĩĩio wake vala ve Yesu Klisto ( Aeveso 2:8) yĩtwĩa atĩĩ " Nũndũ kwĩsĩla mũmoni wa Ngai nĩmũtangĩĩtwe kwondũ wa kũĩkĩĩa. Ti kwĩsĩla maũndũni ala mwĩkĩte ĩndĩ nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kũma Kwa Ngai".
Mũklisto wa w'o ni mũndũ ũiyĩte mũĩkĩĩo wake vala ve Klisto, vamwe na kĩkwũ kyake mũkelanyonĩ ta ndĩvi ya naĩ syake vamwe na kũthayũka mũthenya wa katatũ. Yoana 1:12 yĩtwĩa atĩĩ," ĩndĩ onthe ala mamwĩtĩkĩlile ala mamũĩkĩĩie, nĩwamanengie ũkũmũ wa kũtw'ĩka syana sya Ngai". Ũvano wa mũklisto wa w'o nĩ wendo Kwa angĩ na wĩwi Kwa ndeto ya Ngai( 1Yoana 2:4-10). Muklisto wa w'o nĩ kana ka Ngai ki, kĩlĩo kya nyumba ya Ngai, na ũmwe ũla ũnengetwe thayũ mweũ thĩnĩ wa Yesũ klisto.
We nĩwatw'a ũtwi kũmwĩtĩkĩla Klisto nũndu wa maũndũ ala wasoma vaa? Ethĩwa nĩ w'o, tina vau vaandikĩtwe "nĩnamwĩtĩkĩla Klisto umunthĩ".

translation:
indeed
Is Christ new?
Understanding
A disciple (dictionary) means someone who learns about Jesus Christ or believes in Jesus. It signifies one who is a follower and learner, constantly relating to the scriptures.
The name "disciple" was first used to describe believers in Antioch (Acts 11:26; 26:28; 1 Peter 4:16). The followers of Jesus were called Christians in Antioch (Acts 11:26) and then this name spread, becoming known throughout. Therefore, "disciple" essentially means being connected to Christ or a believer in Christ.
For instance, the term disciple carries a significant meaning of belief and is often used to refer to people who have faith or those who believe, indicating a commitment to following or believing in Jesus Christ. Many people who believed in Jesus Christ became disciples and joined churches or adopted the title "Christian." Being in church helps to nurture discipleship and being absent hinders growth. Connecting with the church, learning from each other, and sharing experiences within the community of the church fosters discipleship.
The Bible teaches us that salvation and good deeds are gifts from God. Titus 3:5 states "He saved us, not because of righteous things we had done, but because of his mercy, he saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit." Therefore, a Christian is someone born again by God (John 3:3; 3:7; 1 Peter 1:23) and whose faith is validated by grace through Jesus Christ (Ephesians 2:8), implying that "It is by grace you have been saved, not by works, so that no one can boast."
A disciple of Christ is someone who lives their life like Christ, together with His character, living according to His will, and overcoming temptation. John 1:12 says, "But to all who did receive him, who believed in him, he gave the right to become children of God." The privilege of being a disciple of Christ is fellowship with God and obedience to His command (1 John 2:4-10). A disciple of Christ is a child of God, a member of God's family, and a person chosen and sanctified through the blood of Jesus Christ.
Will you accept Christ as your savior today? That is up to you, but it is written "I have accepted Christ as my personal savior".
Christian Now?

Andũ Oĩ Maithokea Kana Yesũ
1Yesũ asyaĩwe Mbetheleemu nthĩ ya Yutia, ĩvinda yĩla Elote waĩ mũsumbĩ. Ĩtina wa ũu, andũ oĩ kuma wumĩlonĩ wa syũa nĩmookie Yelũsalemu na makũlya atĩĩ, 2"Aĩva mwana ũla ũsyaiwe ethĩwe Mũsumbĩ wa Ayuti? Nĩtwonie ndata yake wumĩlonĩ wa syũa, na nĩtwooka kũmũthaitha."
3Mũsumbĩ Elote eew'a ũu, nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩũũyũ kingĩ, we o vamwe na andũ onthe ala mekalaa Yelũsalemu. 4Nĩwoombanisye athembi anene onthe na amanyĩsya ma Mĩao, na amakũlya atĩĩ, "Klĩsto atw'ĩkaa akasyaĩwa va?"
5Namo mamũsũngĩa mamwĩa atĩĩ, "Mbetheleemu nthĩ ya Yutia o tondũ mwathani ũandĩkĩte akasya,
Mika 5.1
'We Mbetheleemu, nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ya Yuta,
ndwĩ mũnini nongi katĩ wa ndũa ila syĩ nguma sya Yuta,
nũndũ kwaku kũkauma mũsumbĩ,
ũla ũkasumbĩka andũ makwa Ĩsilaeli.' "
7Nĩvo ĩndĩ Elote wametie ala andũ oĩ vandũ me oka, na amakũlya mamũtavye ĩvinda yĩla ndata ĩsu yaumĩlile. 8Nĩvo ĩndĩ wamatũmie amea atĩĩ, "Endai Mbetheleemu mũkamanthe mwana ũsu vo na kĩthito. Mwamwona, ndeteei ũvoo nĩ kana o nakwa nĩthi ngamũthaithe."
9Andũ asu mamina kwĩthukĩĩsya mũsumbĩ, nĩmakwatie nzĩa mathi. Na sisya, ĩla ndata moonete wumĩlonĩ wa syũa yaĩ ĩendie mbee woo na yaũngama ĩũlũ wa vala vaĩ kala kana. 10Yĩla moonie ndata ĩsu, nĩmatanie mũno na ũtanu mwingĩ. 11Nĩmalikile nyũmba na moona kala kana kena Meli inyia wako, na matulya ndu makathaitha. Nĩvo ĩndĩ mathaisye mĩio yoo makanenga mĩthĩnzĩo: Thaavu, ũvani wa thooa mũnene wĩtawa ũvumba na mauta me mũuke mũseo metawa manemane.
12Nĩmakaniw'e nĩ Ngai ndotonĩ maikasyokele kwa Elote, na kwoou menũkĩla nzĩanĩ ĩngĩ.
Kũkĩa na Kũthi Misili
13Andũ oĩ mamina kũthi, mũlaĩka wa Mwĩai nĩwamumĩlĩĩle Yosevu ndotonĩ na amwĩa atĩĩ, "Ũkĩla wose kana na inyia wako na ũikĩa ũthi nthĩ ya Misili. Ĩkala kũu kũvika yĩla ngakũtavya, nũndũ Elote e vakuvĩ kwambĩĩa kũmantha kana kaa akoae."
14Yosevu nĩwookĩlile, oosa kana na inyia wako, na mauma ũtukũ mathi Misili, 15#Osea 11.1 vala mekalile kũvika Elote akw'a. Ũu weekĩkie nĩ kana wĩanĩsye ũndũ Mwĩai waneenete kwĩsĩla kwa mwathani akasya atĩĩ, "Nĩnamwĩtie Mwana wakwa aume nthĩ ya Misili."
Kũawa Kwa Syana Nini
16Yĩla Elote wamanyie kana nũkengiwe nĩ ala andũ oĩ, nĩwathatie mũno. Nĩweeaie tũvĩsĩ tũla twĩ Mbetheleemu na ndee syayo, tũla twĩ na ũkũũ wa myaka ĩlĩ na kũtheea, tũkoawe. Eekie ũu athimanĩtye na ĩvinda yĩla wamanyĩthiw'e nĩ ala andũ oĩ.
17Kwa nzĩa ĩsu, ndeto ii syaneeniwe nĩ mwathani Yelemia nĩsyeanĩie:
Yel 31.15
"Wasya nĩweew'ĩkie Lama,
kyeva na kĩĩo kĩ woo.
Laeli akĩĩa nũndũ wa syana syake,
na ndaaĩtĩkĩla kũkiakiw'a,
nĩkwĩthĩwa syonthe syaĩ ngw'ũ."
Kũsyoka Kuma Misili
19Yĩla Elote wakwie, mũlaĩka wa Mwĩai nĩwamumĩlĩĩle Yosevu ndotonĩ e Misili amwĩa atĩĩ, 20"Ũkĩla wose kana na inyia wako, na mũisyoka nthĩ ya Ĩsilaeli, nũndũ ala mendaa kũaa kana nĩ akw'ũ." 21Yosevu nĩwookĩlile, oosa kana na inyia wako, na masyoka nthĩ ya Ĩsilaeli.
22Ĩndĩ yĩla Yosevu weewie kana Alikelau nĩwe ũsumbĩkĩte Yutia vandũ va Elote ĩthe wake, nĩwakĩie kũthi kw'o. Ĩtina wa kũkanw'a nĩ Ngai ndotonĩ nĩwaekie kũthi kũu athi kĩsionĩ kĩtawa Kalilii, 23#Mk 1.24; Lk 2.39; Yoa 1.45 na atũa ndũanĩ yĩtawa Nasaleti. Kwoou kĩla kyaneenetwe nĩ athani kyeanĩa kana, "Klĩsto akeetwa Mũnasaleti."

People were troubled about Jesus
1Jesus was born in Bethlehem, in Judea, during the reign of King Herod. And some shepherds were in the fields, guarding their flocks at night, 2when they asked, "What sign has been shown to us concerning this birth? We have heard about him from afar, and we will go to see him."
3King Herod heard this, and he was greatly disturbed, along with all Jerusalem. 4He gathered all the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked them, "Where is the Messiah going to be born?"
5They replied, "Bethlehem in Judea, because it is written by the prophet:
6 #
Micah 5:1
'But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah,
you are certainly not least among the towns of Judah,
for out of you will come a ruler
who will shepherd my people Israel.' "
7So Herod secretly called for the wise men and learned from them when the star had appeared. 8Then he sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search diligently for the child. When you find him, report back to me so that I too may worship him."
9After hearing the king, the wise men set out. The star they had seen in the east guided them until it stopped over the place where the child was. 10When they saw the star, they rejoiced with great joy. 11They entered the house and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby Jesus lying in a manger. They bowed down and worshipped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
12They were warned in a dream not to return to Herod, so they went home by another route.
The Flight to Egypt
13After they departed, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, "Get up! Take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you. For Herod is looking for the child to kill him."
14Joseph got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and fled to Egypt. 15#Hosea 11:1 He stayed there until Herod died. This fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: "I called my son out of Egypt."
The Massacre of the Innocents
16When Herod realized he had been tricked by the wise men, he became furious. He ordered the killing of all boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old or younger, according to the time he had learned from the wise men. 17This fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah:
18 #
Jeremiah 31:15
"A voice is heard in Ramah—
weeping and great sorrow.
Rachel weeps for her children,
refusing to be comforted,
because they are no more."
Return from Egypt
19After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt 20and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and go back to the land of Israel, because those who tried to kill him are dead." 21So Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and returned to the land of Israel.
22But when Joseph heard that Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. Having been warned in a dream, he went to the region of Galilee. 23And he made his home in a town called Nazareth, fulfilling what had been spoken through the prophets, that he would be called a Nazarene. #Mark 1:24; Luke 2:39; John 1:45

text:
Maũndũ mate ma w'o mawetawa nĩ andũ
Ũvũngũ: Ngũsĩ sya Yeova iinyusaa ndawa na iyĩendaa sivitalĩ.
Ũw'o: Ithyĩ nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũkwate ũiiti ũla mũseo vyũ, na tũiitĩthye syana na iveti sitũ nesa vyũ. Ĩla twawaa tũmanthaa matakĩtalĩ ala mesĩ wĩa woo nesa na matonya kũtũthĩnza vate kũtwongela nthakame. Nĩtũtanĩthaw'a mũno nĩ maendeeo ala mekĩtwe maũndũnĩ ma ũiiti. O na nzĩa ila syaseũviw'e itetheesye kũiita Ngũsĩ sya Yeova vate kũtũmĩa nthakame, matukũ aa nikee kũtũmĩwa kũiita andũ ala angĩ onthe. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ mũseo nũndũ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ mbingĩ, mũndũ o na wĩva nũtonya kũtw'a kũiitwa ate kwongelwa nthakame na ayĩvathana na mathĩna ala matonya kũkwata mũndũ nũndũ wa kwongelwa nthakame. Mathĩna asu nĩ ta mowau ala makwatanaw'a kwĩsĩla nthakame, mwĩĩ kũleana na nthakame ĩte yaw'o, kana o thĩna ũtonya kumĩla nũndũ wa mavĩtyo ma ndakĩtalĩ.
Ũvũngũ: Ngũsĩ sya Yeova iĩkĩĩaa kana mũndũ avoaw'a nĩ mũĩkĩĩo wĩ w'oka.
Ũw'o: Ithyĩ tũivoasya andũ kwa nzĩa ya syama.
Ũvũngũ: Kũiitwa vate nthakame kwĩ ngalama nene mũno.
Ũw'o: Kũiita mũndũ ate kwongelwa nthakame kũtũmĩaa mbesa nini.
Sisya ĩvuku Transfusion and Apheresis Science, Volume 33, No. 3, ĩthangũ ya 349.
Ũvũngũ: Ngũsĩ mbingĩ mũno o na syana nikusaa kĩla mwaka nũndũ wa kũlea kwongelwa nthakame.
Ũw'o: Ũndũ ũsu ti wa w'o o na vanini. Matakĩtalĩ maingĩ ma kũthĩnza nĩmatemaa awau me na mowau manene ta ũwau wa ngoo, ũwau wa mavĩndĩ na malenyũ, na mowau ala wĩthĩaa mũndũ no ekĩawa mamutha angĩ. Makũnaa wĩa ũsu w'onthe mateũtũmĩa nthakame o na vanini. Andũ awau na syana ndwau ala maiitawa vate nthakame maendeeaa nesa o ta ala mongelawa nthakame kana o na makaendeea nesanga kũte ala mongelawa nthakame. Ĩndĩ o na kũkatw'ĩka kũilyĩ ata, vai mũndũ ũtonya kũĩkĩĩthya kana mũwau nũkũkw'a nũndũ wa kũlea nthakame na kana nũkũvĩta nũndũ wa kwĩtĩkĩla ongelwe nthakame.
Sisya ĩvuku The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery, Volume 134, No. 2, ĩthangũ ya 287-288; Texas Heart Institute Journal, Volume 38, No. 5, ĩthangũ ya 563; Basics of Blood Management, ĩthangũ ya 2; na ĩvuku Continuing Education in Anaesthesia, Critical Care & Pain, Volume 4, No. 2, ĩthangũ ya 39.
Sisya ĩvuku The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery, Volume 89, No. 6, ĩthangũ ya 918; na ĩvuku Heart, Lung and Circulation, Volume 19, ĩthangũ ya 658.
Nĩkĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itetĩkĩlaa kwongelwa nthakame?
Kĩla kĩtumaa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ilea kwongelwa nthakame nĩ mũĩkĩĩo woo ĩndĩ ti atĩ syĩthĩawa iilea ũiiti. Mavuku ma Mbivilia ala me nthĩnĩ wa ũtianĩo mũkũũ na ala me nthĩnĩ wa ũtianĩo mweũ onthe nĩmatũtavĩtye sanzũ kana twaĩle kwĩvathana na nthakame. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 9:4; Alivai 17:10; Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 12:23; Meko ma Atũmwa 15:28, 29) O na ĩngĩ Ngai onaa nthakame ĩanene na thayũ. (Alivai 17:14) Kwoou tũleaa nthakame nũndũ nĩtũmwĩw'aa Ngai. Ti ũu wĩ w'oka, tũmĩleaa nũndũ nĩtũnengete Ngai ndaĩa ũla nĩwe ũtũnengaa thayũ.
Kũvĩndũa woni
Ve ĩvinda matakĩtalĩ moonaa nzĩa sya kũiita ala maleete nthakame syĩ nthũku mũno na itonya kũtuma mũndũ akw'a, ĩndĩ myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ nĩmaekete kwĩthĩwa na woni ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o mwakanĩ wa 2004, ve ũvoo waandĩkiwe ĩkasetinĩ yĩmwe ya kũmanyĩsya maũndũ ma ũiiti waisye kana "myaka yũkĩte nzĩa mbingĩ sya ũiiti ila syaseũviw'e itetheesye Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ikatũmĩawa kũiita andũ onthe." Nakyo kĩlungu kĩngĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩkaseti yĩmwe (Heart, Lung and Circulation) mwakanĩ wa 2010 kyaisye kana "ndakĩtalĩ ala mathĩnzaa maĩle kũtũmĩaa 'mũthemba wa ũiiti ũla ũtatũmĩaa nthakame' kĩla ĩvinda maithĩnza awau ĩndĩ mayaĩle kũtw'a atĩ no Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩ syoka syaĩle kũiitwa ũu."
Ĩvuku Continuing Education in Anaesthesia, Critical Care & Pain, Volume 4, No. 2, ĩthangũ ya 39.
Ngili mbingĩ sya matakĩtalĩ nithĩnzaa awau iitũmĩa nzĩa ila isũvĩaa mũwau ndakasye nthakame mbingĩ mũno. Itũmĩaa nzĩa isu o na ĩla iũtema awau mekwenda kũtemwa masaa maingĩ mũno na iyĩsaa kũmongela nthakame. Mĩthemba ĩsu ya ũiiti nĩtũmĩawa o na nthĩ ila ite nthwii na awau mate Ngũsĩ nĩmakũlasya maiitwe ũu.

Explanation: Jehovah's name proves medicinal and acts reliably.
Concerning this: We will carefully examine what we say so that our speech may be pleasing, and we will speak kindly and truthfully because it is vital. But we have become accustomed to bad things, yet some of them are good and can help us to encourage others to appreciate the truth. We will also endeavor to make progress in our understanding. And regarding this matter, let no one deceive himself into thinking that he can please Jehovah and at the same time misuse his name, while being associated with those who misuse it. This is a serious thing, a very grave error, for a person to think he can please God while being associated with those who misuse his name. Those people are like lepers who have been cleansed, but they still associate with unclean ones, or they do not bother to separate themselves from vile practices.
Explanation: Jehovah's name demonstrates whether someone has truly repented.
Concerning this: We should sympathize with people because of their ignorance.
Explanation: To please him requires great effort.
Concerning this: What benefit is there in speaking kindly to a person?

Explanation: Many families regularly devote time each year to improving their speech.
Concerning this: This does not concern everyone. Many bad habits—such as lying, stealing, and adultery, and habits that cause a person to harm others—are deeply ingrained. All of these things displease God. People and families who have been involved in such practices often find it difficult to stop completely, or they may not even try to stop. It may require much effort to overcome them, but a person can improve if he strives to eliminate bad habits and to avoid associating with those who practice vile things.
See the articles "The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery," Volume 134, No. 2, pages 287-288; "Texas Heart Institute Journal," Volume 38, No. 5, page 563; "Basics of Blood Management," page 2; and the article "Continuing Education in Anaesthesia, Critical Care & Pain," Volume 4, No. 2, page 39.
See the articles "The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery," Volume 89, No. 6, page 918; and "Heart, Lung and Circulation," Volume 19, page 658.
Is Jehovah's Organization Supporting Blood Transfusions?
Every time Jehovah's Organization supports blood transfusions, it compromises its stand on remaining neutral. Bible-based publications consistently state that Christians should abstain from blood, and we should not associate with those who disregard this command. (Acts 9:4; Revelation 17:10; Titus 12:23; Acts 15:28, 29) Also, God views blood as sacred. (Revelation 17:14) We show appreciation to God when we respect his view of blood. If we do so, we demonstrate that we trust him to support us.
Further information
Some doctors may suggest alternatives to blood transfusions because they recognize the risks involved, especially for adults. For example, in 2004, a publication stated that some hospitals have a special service called "bloodless medicine" or "patient blood management" that "can help patients avoid blood transfusions while still receiving quality medical care." And another publication (Heart, Lung and Circulation) in 2010 said that "doctors can use 'blood conservation strategies' to minimize the need for transfusions, and patients may be encouraged to believe that Jehovah's Organization does not prohibit them."
The article "Continuing Education in Anaesthesia, Critical Care & Pain," Volume 4, No. 2, page 39.
Many doctors are willing to explore alternatives, but sometimes they feel pressured to give blood transfusions. They may feel obligated to spend more time researching options and explaining the risks to patients. Our hope for life depends on God, and he can strengthen us to remain firm.

"We ũla wamombie mbee, amombie mũndũ mũũme na mũndũ mũka."
Yeova * Ngai nĩwe wakwatanisye andũ elĩ ma mbee nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana amina kũmba mũndũ mũka wa mbee 'nĩwamũtwaĩie' Atamu. Ĩla Atamu wamwonie nĩweewie mũyo mwingĩ mũno na asya: "Ũũ yu nĩ ĩvĩndĩ ya mavĩndĩ makwa, na nyama ya mwĩĩ wakwa." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:22, 23) O ta ũu, Yeova endaa andũ ala matwaanĩte methĩwe na ũtanu.
Ĩla watwaana kana watwawa nũtonya kũsũanĩa kana maũndũ makeethĩawa me o maseo kĩla ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ lilikana kana o na ethĩwa andũ ala matwaanĩte mendanĩte ata, mailea kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna mana. (1 Akolintho 7:28) Nthĩnĩ wa kavuku kaa nũũkwata myolooto ya Mbivilianĩ ĩla ĩtonya kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na ũtanu nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano waku wamĩatĩĩa.—Savuli 19:8-11.
1 ĨTĨKĨLA KĨANDA KĨLA YEOVA ŨKŨNENGETE
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: Mũndũũme nĩwe mũtwe wa mũsyĩ.—Aeveso 5:23.
Ethĩwa wĩ na kĩveti, Yeova endaa ũkyony'e wendo na ũikĩsũvĩa. (1 Vetelo 3:7) Akyũmbie kĩthĩwe mũtetheesya waku, na endaa wĩthĩwe ũkyendete na kũkĩnenga ndaĩa. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:18) Waĩle kwenda kĩveti kyaku mũno ũkethĩa mawendi makyo nĩmo ma vata mũno kwaku kwĩ ala maku mwene.—Aeveso 5:25-29.
Ethĩwa wĩ mũtwae, Yeova endaa ũnenge mũũme waku ndaĩa nene, na ũimũtetheesya eanĩsye kĩanda kyake. (1 Akolintho 11:3; Aeveso 5:33) Ĩtĩkĩla motwi make, na ũimũkwata mbau na ngoo yonthe nthĩnĩ wa kũmeanĩsya. (Akolosai 3:18) Weeka ũu ũkamwendeesya mũno Yeova, o na mũũme waku.—1 Vetelo 3:1-6.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Kũlya mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana wĩthĩwe mũũme kana kĩveti kĩseo. Mwĩthukĩĩsye nesa, na ũitata ũndũ ũtonya waĩlye vala ũkwona ve na thĩna
Ĩthĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo nũndũ nĩvendaa ĩvinda kũmanya kĩla kĩtonya kũmũtanĩthya mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake
2 SŨANĨA MŨNO ŨNDŨ ŨLA ŨTWAANĨTE NAKE ŨKWĨW'A
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: Ethĩwa wĩ mũtwae kana nũtwaanĩte, nĩwaĩle kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mavata ma mũũme waku kana ma kĩveti kyaku, ĩndĩ ti o ala maku oka. (1 Akolintho 10:24) Waĩle kũmwona mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake e wa vata mũno na ũililikana kana Yeova endaa athũkũmi make methĩwe 'me auu kwa andũ onthe.' (2 Timotheo 2:24) Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Ve ũla ũneenaa mĩtũkĩ ateũsũanĩa ta kũtonyanga kwa ũvyũ; ĩndĩ ũĩmĩ wa ũla mũĩ nũvoasya." Kwoou ĩla ũũneena nĩwaĩle kũnyuva nesa ndeto ila ũũtũmĩa. (Nthimo 12:18) Veva wa Yeova ũkaũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na tei na wendo ĩla ũũneena.—Akalatia 5:22, 23; Akolosai 4:6.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Mbee wa mũtananeenea maũndũ maito, voya Yeova aũtetheesye wĩthĩwe wĩ mũuu, na wĩyũmbanĩtye kũmwĩthukĩĩsya mũũme kana kĩveti kyaku
Sũanĩa mũno ndeto ila ũũneena na ũndũ ũkũineena
3 SŨANĨAI MAŨNDŨ MWĨ NGWATANĨO
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: Ĩla mwatwaana, mũtw'ĩkaa "mwĩĩ ũmwe." (Mathayo 19:5) O na vailyĩ ũu, mwĩthĩawa mwĩ andũ elĩ me kĩvathũkany'o, na nĩvatonyeka mũkethĩwa na mawoni me kĩvathũkany'o. Kwoou, nĩmwaĩle kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩthĩwa mwĩ na ngwatanĩo nthĩnĩ wa mosũanĩo na mawoni menyu. (Avilivi 2:2) Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mũkwĩka motwi, nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Kĩla ũsũanĩo ũlũlũmĩlaw'a nĩ ũtao [kana, "kũoany'a maũndũ," NWT]." (Nthimo 20:18) Ĩla mũkwĩka motwi ma vata,ekai myolooto ya Mbivilia ĩmũtongoesye.—Nthimo 8:32, 33.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
O vamwe na kũmũelesya ũla ũtwaanĩte nake mawoni maku na maũndũ angĩ, tata ũmũelesye ũndũ we mwene ũkwĩw'a
Mbee wa ũtanatw'a kwĩka ũndũ, nũseo ũkaoany'a na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake

translation:
"We have seen the dead ones, the dead person and the dead woman."
Jehovah * God is the one who unites people in marriage. The Bible tells us whether a married woman says 'I hate him,' let her be silent. But Adam showed himself to be very wise and said: "This time it is bone from my bones, and flesh from my flesh." (Genesis 2:22, 23) So now, Jehovah comforts all his servants with hope.
But he teaches them also to live happily and to avoid things that cause sorrow or trouble every day. It is good to remember that we and others may be tempted at times, leading to being caught by bad habits. (1 Corinthians 7:28) Because of this, take advantage of the teachings of the Bible so that you can rejoice with hope in marriage.—Psalm 19:8-11.
1 REMEMBER THIS ALWAYS ABOUT JEHOVAH
BIBLE TEACHING: A man is the head of a wife.—Ephesians 5:23.
Wives, be obedient, and Jehovah will comfort you with love and kindness. (1 Peter 3:7) Encourage him to do what is right, and comfort yourself knowing that you are walking in the way of righteousness. (Genesis 2:18) Be willing to obey your husband, and show great affection for him so that you may always cherish him.—Ephesians 5:25-29.
Wife, be submissive, and Jehovah will help you respect your husband deeply, and he will teach you to honor his position. (1 Corinthians 11:3; Ephesians 5:33) Listen to his advice, and accept him with joy and wholeheartedness in order to show appreciation. (Colossians 3:18) Let this attitude please Jehovah, and your husband.—1 Peter 3:1-6.
WHAT YOU CAN DO:
If someone who is married to you does something wrong, it is possible to correct him or her. Be patient, and try to find out what caused him or her to act that way.
Be careful and considerate, and always strive to understand what might tempt someone who is married to you.
2 CONSIDER HOW TO MAKE YOUR MARRIAGE HAPPY
IMPORTANT POINTS: Wife or husband, it is important to think about the feelings of your mate or wife, and not just your own interests. (1 Corinthians 10:24) Try to see things from his or her perspective, and remember that Jehovah wants us to be "kind to all people." (2 Timothy 2:24) Important points: "The one who speaks rashly acts without thinking; the one who considers matters carefully fares well." Think carefully before speaking, and use wise words. (Proverbs 12:18) Jehovah's servants encourage each other with loving counsel.—Galatians 5:22, 23; Colossians 4:6.
WHAT YOU CAN DO:
When facing difficult situations, pray to Jehovah for guidance, and ask Him to help you respect your husband or wife.
Consider carefully how to improve your marriage.
3 DISCUSS MATTERS OPENLY
IMPORTANT POINTS: If you get married, become "one flesh." (Matthew 19:5) But even so, continue to share your thoughts with others and seek advice from them, and be honest and open in your dealings with others. Therefore, try to understand each other's feelings and needs when discussing problems. (Philemon 2:2) For example, if you disagree, it is important to discuss it openly. Important points: "Every dispute is settled when it is talked over [or, "when matters are considered," NWT]." (Proverbs 20:18) If you talk things over calmly, let Bible principles guide you.—Proverbs 8:32, 33.
WHAT YOU CAN DO:
Be willing to listen to your mate's feelings and concerns, and express your own feelings.
When faced with a problem, discuss it with your mate.
^ par. 4 The Bible teaches that God's name is Jehovah.

ANDŨ ala maĩkĩĩaa Ũtatũ mamanyĩasya kana ũngainĩ kwĩ atatũ, Asa, Mwana, na Veva Mũtheu. Asu atatũ matw'ĩkĩkaa nĩ meanene, nĩ ene vinya w'onthe, na maiĩ mwambĩlĩĩlyo. Kwĩanana na ũmanyĩsyo wa Ũtatũ, Asa nĩ Ngai, Mwana nĩ Ngai, na Veva Mũtheu nĩ Ngai, ĩndĩ asu onthe no Ngai ũmwe.
Andũ aingĩ ala maĩkĩĩaa Ũtatũ nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana maitonya kũũelesya. Ĩndĩ, masũanĩaa Ũtatũ no ta ũmanyĩaw'a Mbivilianĩ. Nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũmanya kana ndeto "Ũtatũ" ndyonekaa Mbivilianĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩsũanĩo ya Ũtatũ nĩyonekaa Mbivilianĩ? Nĩ kana tũsũngĩe ĩkũlyo yĩu, eka tũsisye mũsoa ũla aĩkĩĩi ma Ũtatũ maasya nĩw'o wonanasya kana Ngai nĩ Ũtatũ.
"NDETO YAĨ NGAI"
Ĩandĩko ya Yoana 1:1 yaasya: "Mwambĩlĩlyonĩ kwaĩ Ndeto, na ĩla Ndeto yaĩ vamwe na Ngai, na ĩla Ndeto yaĩ Ngai." Kĩlungunĩ o kĩu, mũtũmwa Yoana nĩwonanĩtye kana "Ndeto" nĩ Yesũ. (Yoana 1:
Manya kana mbeenĩ, kĩlungu kĩu kya Mbivilia kyaandĩkĩtwe na Kĩkiliki. Ĩtina Kĩkiliki kĩu nĩkyesie kũalyũlwa na ithyomo ingĩ. Ĩndĩ aalyũli amwe mayaasya, "Ndeto yaĩ Ngai." Nĩkĩ mataasya ũu? Kwĩanana na ũmanyi woo wa Kĩkiliki kĩla kyatũmĩiwe kũandĩka Mbivilia, aalyũli asu nĩmoonie kana mayaĩle kwasya "Ndeto yaĩ Ngai," ĩndĩ nĩmaĩle kũalyũla ĩandĩko yĩu ũndũ ũngĩ. Mayalyũũlile ata? Ona ngelekany'o o mbũthũ vaa: "Logos (Ndeto) aĩ wa kĩngai." (A New Translation of the Bible) "Ndeto aĩ ngai." (The New Testament in an Improved Version) "Ndeto aĩ vamwe na Ngai na avw'anene nake." (The Translator's New Testament) Kwĩanana na Mbivilia isu, Ndeto tiwe Ngai mwene. * Ĩndĩ nũndũ wa ũnene wake katĩ wa syũmbe sya Yeova, Ndeto nĩwĩtawa 'ngai.' Ndeto 'ngai' vaa ĩonany'a "mwene vinya."
MANYA MAŨNDŨ MAINGANGĨ
Andũ aingĩ mayĩsĩ Kĩkiliki kĩla kyatũmĩiwe kũandĩka Mbivilia. Kwoou ũtonya kũmanya ata ũndũ mũtũmwa Yoana woonanasya? Kwa ngelekany'o, mwalimũ akaelesya amanyĩw'a make ĩsomo ĩna na maielewa kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya amanyĩw'a asu make kũelewa nesa? Nĩmatonya kũkũlya mwalimũ amaeleangye mũnango. Kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingaingĩ no kũmatethye kũelewa ĩsomo yĩu nesa. O ta ũu, nĩ kana ũelewe ĩandĩko ya Yoana 1:1 ũndũ yonanasya, nũtonya kũsoma ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Yoana ĩũlũ wa kĩanda kya Yesũ. Weemanyĩsya maũndũ maingaingĩ ĩũlũ wa ũvoo ũsu ũkaelewa nesa.
Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ũndũ Yoana ũandĩkĩte nthĩnĩ wa Yoana 1:18: "Na vai mũndũ waamwona Ngai [Mwene Vinya W'onthe] o na ĩndĩĩ." Ĩndĩ andũ nĩmamwonie Yesũ, ũ Mwana, nũndũ Yoana easya: "Na ĩla Ndeto [Yesũ] yatw'ĩka mwĩĩ, na yatũa katĩ waitũ na ithyĩ twoona ũtheu mũtisu wake." (Yoana 1:
KŨĨKĨĨTHYA MAŨNDŨ ASU
Sũanĩa ĩngĩ ĩla ngelekany'o ya mwalimũ na amanyĩw'a make. Kwasũanĩa o na mwalimũ amaeleangya mũnango amwe me o na nzika. Amanyĩw'a asu maĩlĩte kwĩka ata? Nĩmatonya kũkũlya mwalimũ ũngĩ amaelesye ĩũlũ wa ĩsomo yĩu. Mwalimũ ũsu ũngĩ amina kũĩkĩĩthya kana maelesyo ma mwalimũ ũla wa mbee nĩ ma w'o, nzika sya amanyĩw'a aingĩ nitonya kũthela. O ta ũu ethĩwa wĩ na nzika ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũandĩki wa Mbivilia Yoana waasya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Yesũ ũileny'e na Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe, nũtonya kũsoma ĩvuku yĩngĩ Mbivilianĩ ũkwate ũvoo mwingaingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Mathayo waandĩkie. Ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo wa walany'o ũũ wa maũndũ, Yesũ nĩwaisye atĩĩ: "Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũsu na saa ũsu vai ũmwe wĩsĩ, o na alaĩka ma ĩtunĩ, o na Mwana, ĩndĩ no Asa weka." (Mathayo 24:36) Ndeto ii syonanĩtye ata kana Yesũ tiwe Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe?
Yesũ aĩtye kana Asa nĩwĩsĩ maũndũ maingĩ kwĩ Mwana. Kethĩwa Yesũ aĩ o ũndũ ũmwe na Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe, ethĩwa eesĩ maũndũ onthe ala Asa wake wĩsĩ. Kwoou Mwana na Asa maitonya kwĩthĩwa meanene. Ĩndĩ angĩ no masye: 'Yesũ aĩ na wũmbo wa mĩthemba ĩlĩ. Vaa aneenie ũu nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu aĩ mũndũ.' Ĩndĩ ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, nata ĩndĩ ĩũlũ wa veva mũtheu? Ethĩwa veva no ũndũ ũmwe na Ngai Asa, nĩkĩ Yesũ ndaasya kana veva ũsu nĩwĩsĩ o ũndũ ũmwe na Asa?
O ũendee kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ũkoona maandĩko maingĩ Mbivilianĩ maeleetye ĩũlũ wa ĩsomo yĩu. Nĩmaeleetye w'o ĩũlũ wa Asa, Mwana, na veva mũtheu.

translation:
People who know God worship Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, Asa, Child, and Veva Mutheu. These three are equal in power, are one in essence, and have infinite glory. According to their understanding of God, Asa is God, the Child is God, and Veva Mutheu is God, yet they are all one God.
Many people who know God stumble or fail to understand. However, let us seek God and understand the meaning of Revelation. It is a matter of knowing whether the name "Father" refers to Revelation. But does the revelation of God refer to Revelation? Or shall we leave this question so that those who know God may understand whether God is Father.
"THE NAME OF GOD"
The writing of John 1:1 says: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." In other words, the apostle John understood that "Word" is Jesus. (John 1:
Know that originally, this scripture from the Bible was written in Greek. The original Greek word means to be expressed through speech. But some translators say, "The Word of God." Why did they say this? According to the knowledge of the Greeks used to write the Bible, those translators understood that it was appropriate to translate "The Word of God," because it was appropriate to express the writing in that way. Did they translate correctly? See various interpretations or translations: "Logos (Word) was divine." (A New Translation of the Bible) "Word was God." (The New Testament in an Improved Version) "Word was with God and was inferior to him." (The Translator's New Testament) According to these Bibles, the Word is not God himself. * But because of his greatness within the family of Jehovah, the Word is called 'god.' The Word 'god' also means "one in essence."
KNOW MORE THINGS
Many people do not know the Greek language used to write the Bible. So how can you understand what John meant? For example, a teacher explains his lessons so that students understand them well, doesn't he try to explain his own understanding so that they can understand clearly? It is possible to help the teacher understand better. Understanding more things helps to understand the lesson clearly. Otherwise, if you understand the writing of John 1:1, you will need to read the book "Understanding the Bible" by John in the chapter on Jesus. Understand more things about this topic so that you can understand clearly.
For example, consider what John wrote at the beginning of John 1:18: "And no one has seen God [the Almighty] ever." But people have seen Jesus, the Son, and John said: "But the Word [Jesus] made himself known to us, and came among us and showed us his great glory." (John 1:
TO UNDERSTAND THESE THINGS
Consider also the teacher and his understanding. Consider whether the teacher understands something or not. Does his understanding go far? It is possible to help the teacher who explains this lesson. This teacher should be able to confirm whether the teachings of the previous teachers were correct, because the understanding of many people can help. Otherwise, just as the biblical writer John explained what Jesus did with God the Almighty, you will need to read more books of the Bible to get a deeper understanding. For example, consider what Matthew wrote. In the account of the flood, Jesus said: "About that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father." (Matthew 24:36) Doesn't this show that Jesus is not God the Almighty?
Jesus said that the Father has many important things to say to the Son. Because Jesus is one with God the Almighty, he does not know everything except what his Father tells him. The Son and the Father can therefore be distinguished. Let some say: 'Jesus had a limited hope. But he denied this truth and became a man.' However, is this true, and what about the future? He was one with God the Father, so did Jesus deny that the future was unknown to him and to the Father?
To continue studying the Bible, you will find many scriptures in the Bible that explain this lesson. They explain the relationship between the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

Nũsomete nesa makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya ala mela kuma? Ethĩwa nũu, sisya ethĩwa nũtonya kũsũngĩa makũlyo aa maatĩĩe:
Ĩla asyai ala mathamĩĩe kũndũ kũngĩ meũtetheesya syana syoo, nĩkĩ maĩle kũsũanĩa kĩthyomo mũno?
Syana no syĩmanyĩsye kĩthyomo kya kũla mathamĩĩe ĩla syĩ sukulu, kana ikemanyĩsya kuma kwa ala siũtindany'a namo. Mwana nũtonya kũtetheka ethĩwa nĩwĩsĩ ithyomo mbingĩ. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana asyai nĩmaĩle kũsũanĩa syana syoo itonya kũkwatya ũw'o na ikaendeea nesa kĩ-veva syĩ kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kĩva. Nĩ kĩkundi kya kĩthyomo kya kũla mathamĩĩe kana nĩ kya kĩthyomo kĩla kyoo? Kwoou asyai Aklĩsto mathĩnĩkĩaa mũno mavata ma kĩ-veva ma syana syoo vandũ va kũmantha kwĩuna.—w17.05, ĩth. 9-11.
Ve ĩvinda Yesũ wakũlilye Vetelo atĩĩ: "Simoni, mwana wa Yona, nũmbendete mbee wa aa?" Nĩ kyaũ kĩu Yesũ weetie "aa"? (Yoa. 21:15)
Veoneka Yesũ awetaa makũyũ kana wĩa wa kũtea makũyũ, kana o syonthe. Ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, Vetelo nĩwasyokeie wĩa ũla watethasya tene wa kũtea makũyũ. O namo Aklĩsto nĩmaĩle kũthima mamanye mendete wĩa ũla mathũkũmaa mũno wĩana ata.—w17.05, ĩth. 22-23.
Nĩkĩ Avalaamu watavisye Sala asye nĩmasyaanĩw'e? (Mwa. 12:10-13)
Kwa w'o, Sala na Avalaamu maĩ ma ĩthe ũmwe. Keka Sala aisye aĩ mũka wa Avalaamu, ũ Avalaamu ethĩwa ooaiwe na ndethĩwa aasyaa ũla ũsyao Ngai wamwathĩte.—wp17.3, ĩth. 14-15.
Elias Hutter ambĩĩisye nzĩa yĩva nzeo ya kũtumbĩthya mavuku nĩ kana atetheesye ala mendaa kwĩmanyĩsya Kĩevelania?
Endaa mavathũkany'e ndeto ila sya mũsingi (root of a word) sya Kĩevelania kĩla kĩtũmĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ, na nthoo ila syĩ mbee kana ĩtina wa ndeto isu sya mũsingi. Nĩ kana eke ũu, atũmĩaa langi mũkwatu kũandĩka ndeto ĩla ya mũsingi (root of a word) ĩndĩ aitũmĩa langi ũte mũkwatu aiandĩka nthoo ila syĩ mbee kana ĩtina wa ndeto ya mũsingi. O nayo Mbivilia ya New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References ĩtũmĩĩte nzĩa o ĩsu nthĩnĩ wa maelesyo ma kwongeleela.—wp17.4, ĩth. 11-12.
Nĩ maũndũ meva maĩle kũtetheesya Mũklĩsto ethĩwe na woni ũla waĩle ĩũlũ wa kwĩkala na mũio wa kwĩyũkitĩa avithũkĩwa nĩ andũ?
Maũndũ amwe nĩ ta: Ngai onaa thayũ wĩ mũtheu. Yesũ ndaatavya aatĩĩi make makue mbyũ sya kwĩyũkitĩa. (Luka 22:36, 38) Twaĩle kũtusya mbyũ sitũ itw'ĩke mĩthya ya maembe. Thayũ wĩ vata kwĩ syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ. Nĩtũnengae ndaĩa mawasya ma ngoo ma ala angĩ, na nĩtũtataa twĩthĩwe twĩ ngelekany'o nzeo. (2 Ako. 4:2)—w17.07, ĩth. 31-32.
Nĩkĩ maũndũ ala Mathayo na Luka maandĩkie ĩũlũ wa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ na myaka yake ya mbee matavw'anene?
Mathayo aeleetye mũno maũndũ ala makonetye Yosevu, ta ũndũ weekie eew'a Meli nĩ mũito, ndoto ila waotie mũlaĩka aimwĩa akĩĩe Misili, na aimwĩa asyoke. Luka awetete mũno mũno ĩũlũ wa Meli, ta ĩla waendie kwona Elisavethi na ũndũ weekie ĩla Yesũ e kamwana watiiwe ĩkalũnĩ.—w17.08, ĩth. 32.
Nĩ maũndũ ta meva mekwonany'a ũndũ Mbivilia yĩkalĩte ĩteũthingithĩka?
Ndeto imwe syatũmĩiwe Mbivilianĩ nĩsyambĩĩe kũeleeka ũndũ ũngĩ. Silikalĩ imwe syoosa ũtongoi kĩsionĩ kĩna nĩsyatumaa kĩthyomo kĩla kyatũmĩawa kĩsionĩ kĩu kĩeka kũtũmĩwa na kĩngĩ kĩsĩkĩe nĩ andũ aingĩ kĩyosa mwanya wakyo. Wĩa wa kũalyũla Mbivilia na ithyomo ila syĩsĩkĩe nĩ andũ aingĩ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ũivĩngwa.—w17.09, ĩth. 19-21.
Yo kĩla mũndũ nĩwĩthĩawa na mũlaĩka wa kũmũsũvĩa?
Aiee. Yesũ awetie kana alaĩka ma amanyĩw'a make nĩmonaa ũthyũ wa Ngai. (Mt. 18:10) Ndeto isu syake syoonanasya kana alaĩka nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ kĩla ũmwe wa amanyĩw'a make, ĩndĩ iyoonanasya kana kĩla ũmwe woo ethĩawa na mũlaĩka wa kũmũsũvĩa.—wp17.5, ĩth. 5.
Nĩ wendo wĩva wa vata vyũ?
Vai wendo ũvĩtũkĩte wendo wa a·gaʹpe, ũla ũtongoeaw'a nĩ myolooto mĩlũngalu. Mũndũ wĩ wendo ũsu nũthangaaĩaa ala angĩ. Ĩndĩ mũno mũno kĩla kyonanasya kana mũndũ e wendo ũsu nĩ kwĩyumya na kwĩyĩima maũndũ make nĩ kana eke angĩ ũseo.—w17.10, ĩth. 7.
