translation:
Let us consider the case of Musyaisya, is it good to lie? Truly, my brother, think about how children and young people react:
If someone lies and deceives others repeatedly, will he be able to share important things truthfully?
My brother does not appreciate truthful speech when it comes to school matters, or when it seems to benefit those who are dishonest. A child should not be allowed to believe that lying can bring advantage and lead to avoiding consequences for wrongdoing. This is because someone might be able to deceive others and get away with it, and then continue in a pattern of dishonesty. Is this the kind of example we want to set, or is it a bad example? Who would a Christian approve of—those who practice deception on children and adults?—w17.05, pp. 9-11.
Then Jesus asked Peter while they were eating fish: "Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?" What did Jesus mean by "these"? (John 21:15)
It appears that Jesus was referring to the fish or the act of providing food, or both. In view of Jesus' question, Peter was overjoyed to have the opportunity to declare his love for him. So Christians can gladly express their love for God in various ways.—w17.05, pp. 22-23.
Did Abraham test Sarah to see if she would be faithful? (Gen. 12:10-13)
In fact, Sarah and Abraham agreed on a plan. Sarah let herself be taken as Abraham's wife, while Abraham presented her as his sister so that the men would not kill him because of her—because God had blessed her.—wp17.3, pp. 14-15.
Did Elias Hutter ask questions about the reason for visiting prisons, perhaps to help prisoners learn Finnish?
The basic (root of a word) Finnish words were used when writing in Finnish, and this also applied to the basic form of the words. Or, he may have asked them to write down the basic (root of a word) forms of the words, and then he wrote down the different forms of those basic words. This is what the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References does when it includes footnotes.—wp17.4, pp. 11-12.
Are there good reasons why a Christian might feel embarrassed or uncomfortable speaking to others?
Some reasons include: We want to please God. Jesus did not hesitate to speak boldly. (Luke 22:36, 38) We fear being rejected. Boldness is often associated with rudeness. We may be afraid of offending others, and we may worry about how they will react.—2 Cor. 4:2—w17.07, pp. 31-32.
Why do Matthew and Luke record details about Jesus' genealogy differently?
Matthew traces Jesus' lineage through Joseph, highlighting his legal right to the throne; whereas Luke records the genealogy through Mary, showing her family line. Also, Luke recounts events relating to Mary, such as her visit to Elizabeth and the circumstances surrounding Jesus' birth.—w17.08, p. 32.
What can help us appreciate why the Bible is remarkably accurate?
Sometimes, a basic Finnish word helps clarify something. A particular style can make an account more vivid. The way information is presented can help readers remember it. Those who study the Bible diligently will find it increasingly convincing.—w17.09, pp. 19-21.
Does everyone have a guardian angel?
No. Jesus said that angels 'in heaven always behold the face of my Father.' (Matt. 18:10) So, not all angels are assigned to care for individual humans, nor does each person necessarily have a guardian angel.—wp17.5, p. 5.
What kind of love is most valuable?
True Christians strive to show the love of a·gaʹpe, which is based on principle. A person demonstrating this love is considerate of others. In fact, this type of love involves selflessness and willingness to put the interests of others first.—w17.10, p. 7.

text:
"MŨNDŨ MŨKA." Mavinda amwe Yesũ atũmĩaa ndeto ĩsu ĩla ũkũneena na aka. Ta ĩvinda yĩmwe wavoasya mũndũ wekalĩte myaka 18 ũtaũngalala amwĩie: "Mũndũ mũka, nĩwathaw'a wonzu waku." (Luka 13:10-13) O na ve ĩvinda Yesũ watũmĩie ndeto ta ĩsu aineena na inyia. Ĩvinda yĩu ya tene mũndũ atũmĩa ndeto ĩsu ndatalawa ta wĩ kĩvũthya. (Yoa. 19:26; 20:13) Ĩndĩ ve ndeto ĩngĩ yaĩ nzeango o na kwĩ ĩsu.
Ve andũ me Mbivilianĩ matũmĩie ndeto ĩmwe nzeo yonanasya ĩnee na tei maineena na aka amwe. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ nĩwatũmĩie ndeto ĩsu ĩla waneenaa na mũndũ mũka waĩ na thĩna wa kumwa nĩ nthakame kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 12. Mĩao ya Ngai nĩyawetete kana mũndũ mũka ta ũsu nĩ mũvuku, ĩndĩ mũndũ mũka ũsu waĩ mũwau ndaatĩĩa mwĩao ũsu nesa vyũ ũndũ waaĩle kũatĩĩwa. Mũndũ no asye kana mũndũ mũka ũsu ndaaĩle kũthi vala ve Yesũ ĩndĩ aaĩle kwĩvathana na andũ ala angĩ nũndũ wa ũwau wake. (Ali. 15:19-27) Ĩndĩ no tũlwe kana mũndũ mũka ũsu oonete thĩna mwingĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "anyamaaw'a mũno nĩ aiiti aingĩ, na aanangĩte syonthe ila waĩ nasyo, na ndaĩ kavaa o na vanini, ĩndĩ aendeea na kũwaa."—Mko. 5:25, 26.
Mũndũ mũka ũsu avĩtĩile nguthunĩ ya andũ o kavola, na athi nginya aumĩlĩĩla Yesũ ĩtina na akwata mũthya wa ngũa yake ya ĩũlũ. Akililye amĩkwata oou nthakame yake yatuma! Mũndũ mũka ũsu oonaa vai mũndũ emanya wĩa ũla watethya ĩndĩ eewie Yesũ akũlya atĩĩ: "Nũũ ũla wangiita?" (Luka 8:45-47) Atelemile mũno na athi atetemete avalũka mbee wa Yesũ "na amũtavya w'o w'onthe."—Mko. 5:33.
Ĩndĩ Yesũ amũneenisye o nesa nĩ kana aeke kũtelema amwĩa: "Ndũkethĩwe na w'ĩa mwĩĩtu wakwa." (Mat. 9:22, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Andũ ala masomeete Mbivilia maasya kana ndeto ya Kĩevelania na Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "mwĩĩtu wakwa" no ĩtũmĩwe ta nthimo ĩkwasya 'nĩenda ũkwĩka ũseo na nĩngũkwĩw'ĩa ĩnee.' Yesũ ongeleeile kwĩkĩa vinya mũndũ mũka ũsu akĩmwĩa: "Mũĩkĩĩo waku nĩwakũvosya; thi na ũvoo, wĩthĩwe wĩ mũima, ũte na ũthĩn'yo waku."—Mko. 5:34.
"Mwĩĩtu wakwa." Ndeto ĩsu nĩyo mũndũũme ũmwe mũthwii wa Isilaeli weetawa Mboasi watũmĩie ĩvinda waneenaa na ũla mũndũ mũka wa Moavi weetawa Luthi. O ta ũla mũndũ mũka wawetwa vau ĩũlũ, o nake Luthi eew'aa ate mwĩanĩe e mũũndanĩ wa mũndũ ũtesĩ aikolany'a mbaale. Ĩndĩ Mboasi aineena nake atũmĩie ndeto ii: "Ndũkwĩw'a, mwĩĩtu wakwa?" Amwĩie ndakakĩe kũkolany'a ũsyao ũla watiala mũũndanĩ wake. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Luthi weevalũkilye mbee wake na ũthyũ wake na amũkũlya nĩkĩ wamwĩka ũseo wĩana ũu o na kau nĩ wa nthĩ ĩngĩ. Ũsũngĩo ũla Mboasi wamũnengie waĩ na ndeto ii sya ũmwĩkĩa vinya: "Nĩnonetw'e vyũ onthe ala wamwĩkie inyia wa mũemeu [ndiwa Naomi] . . . Yeova nakũĩve wĩa waku."—Lu. 2:8-12.
Ngelekany'o ĩsu ya Yesũ na Mboasi nĩ nzeo vyũ kwa atumĩa ma kĩkundi! Ve mavinda atumĩa elĩ matonya kũvanga mone mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩ na vata wa kũtawa na Maandĩko na kwĩkĩwa vinya. Atumĩa asu mamba kũmũvoya Yeova amatongoesye na matea kũtũ nesa mamwĩthukĩĩsye mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu, makethĩwa matonya kũtũmĩa Ndeto ya Ngai mamũkiakisye na maimũĩkĩĩthya kana Yeova nũmwendete.—Alo. 15:4.

translation:
"A WOMAN BENT OVER." Jesus was healing on the Sabbath day, and he touched her. And a woman who had been bent over for eighteen years could not straighten up at all, and he said to her: "Woman, be freed from your infirmity." (Luke 13:10-13) And Jesus healed her on the Sabbath day so that she might live. This woman used her voice to praise him because she was relieved. (John 19:26; 20:13) Indeed, there are other voices and praises.
There were people from the village who used their voices to speak about her and to praise her. For example, Jesus used his voice to speak to a bent woman and told her that being sick for twelve years was shameful. God's law shows that a bent woman is weak, but this bent woman did not fear her weakness. A person should not be ashamed if this bent woman does not go to heal herself with others. (Acts 15:19-27) But let us also see how much pain she endured. The Bible says that "many have suffered greatly, and they have sought help everywhere, but they have found none, and they have become worse and weaker, until they die"—Mark 5:25, 26.
This woman spent all her wealth on doctors, but she could not find anyone to help her with her illness. She hoped to get something from him! This woman heard that Jesus had come, so she came behind him and touched the edge of his garment. He asked who had done this: "Who touched me?" (Luke 8:45-47) She trembled and said she had come near Jesus "and touched his garment"—Mark 5:33.
And Jesus knew that power had gone out from him: "Someone has touched my garment." (Matt. 9:22, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Other scholars of the Bible say that the phrase "my garment" was used to mean 'the hem of his robe and the fringe of it.' Jesus spoke to the bent woman saying: "Your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be healed, and be well."—Mark 5:34.
"My garment." This phrase is the same as when Boaz spoke to Ruth the Moabite woman, who was a foreigner. It was like when someone called a person old, but Ruth still wanted to be in the company of a man who would take care of her. So Boaz told her this phrase: "Are you my relative?" He asked her to stay and work in his field. That's why Ruth stayed with her mother-in-law and her husband and asked him to redeem her and buy her back. Because of Boaz, he blessed her with this phrase: "May the Lord reward you for what you have done for the dead [Naomi]… May the Lord give you rest."—Ruth 2:8-12.
The example of Jesus and Boaz is very good for those who serve in groups! They often go out to help people who are sad and comfort them with the Scriptures and show them kindness. These ones also try hard to make Jehovah known and teach us lessons so that we can appreciate the value of helping others, making it easy for us to use God's Word to encourage and strengthen others, knowing that Jehovah supports us.—Acts 15:4.

text:
Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku yĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mavuku ala angĩ nũndũ nĩyĩthĩawa na motao maseo kuma kwa Mũmbi witũ. (2 Timotheo 3:16) Ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ no ũtume twĩka moalyũku manene mũno. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndeto ya Ngai ĩ thayũ, na nĩ nthangaau." (Aevelania 4:12) Ndeto ya Ngai nĩyĩthĩawa na ũtonyi wa kwaĩlya thayũ witũ kwa nzĩa ilĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Nzĩa ĩmwe nĩ kũtũtongoesya nthĩnĩ wa maũndũ ala tũkwĩka kĩla mũthenya na nzĩa ĩla ĩngĩ nĩ kũtũtetheesya tũmũmanye Ngai na tũimanya mawatho make.—1 Timotheo 4:8; Yakovo 4:8.
Kũũtetheesya wĩkale nesa ũmũnthĩ. Mbivilia no yĩũtetheesye ĩla ũkwenda kwĩka motwi. Nĩtũnengae motao ĩũlũ wa maũndũ aa maatĩĩe.
Kwĩkalany'a nesa na ala angĩ.—Aeveso 4:31, 32; 5:22, 25, 28, 33.
Kwĩthĩwa na ũima wa mwĩĩ na kwĩthĩwa twĩ eanĩe ngoonĩ.—Savuli 37:8; Nthimo 17:22.
Kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo.—1 Akolintho 6:9, 10.
Kũtethya wĩa na kĩthito.—Nthimo 10:4; 28:19; Aeveso 4:28. *
Andũ manatwaanie o mĩtũkĩ kuma Asia nĩmetĩkĩlĩte kana Mbivilia yĩthĩawa na motao maseo. Na o tondũ andũ ala matwaana mĩtũkĩ mekaa, andũ asu ma Asia nĩmang'ang'anie nĩ kana kĩla ũmwe amanye ũla ũngĩ nesa na mayĩthĩwa maiea ngewa nesa. Ĩndĩ nĩmambĩĩie kũatĩĩa maũndũ ala meemanyĩasya kuma Mbivilianĩ. Makwatie moathimo meva nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa motao ma Mbivilia? Vicent aĩtye atĩĩ: "Maũndũ ala nasomaa Mbivilianĩ nĩmandetheeisye kũmina mathĩna ala twaĩ namo kwa nzĩa nzeo. Kũatĩĩa maũndũ ala me Mbivilianĩ nĩkũtumaa twĩkala twĩ atanu." Nake mũka, ũla wĩtawa Annalou aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũsoma ĩũlũ wa ngelekany'o ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩkwatũtetheeisye. Yu nĩw'aa nĩ mũtanu na nĩ mwĩanĩe mũtwaanonĩ witũ na nĩtwĩanĩasya mĩvango yitũ nesa."
Kũũtetheesya ũkamũmanya Ngai. O vamwe na kũelesya ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano wake, Vicent aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ wa kũsoma Mbivilia, nĩnĩw'aa ngwatanĩo yakwa na Yeova yĩ nzeo vyũ kwĩ ũndũ yailyĩ mbeenĩ." Ndeto isu sya Vicent ieleetye ũndũ wa vata mũno, naw'o nĩ kana Mbivilia no ĩũtetheesye ũkamũmanya Ngai nesa. Na weeka ũu, ũkatetheka kumana na motao make na ũkamanya nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ũkethĩwa wĩ mũnyanyae. O na ĩngĩ, ũkamanya kana Ngai nũvuanĩtye maũndũ maseo ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte yĩla ũkethĩwa ũtonya kũtanĩa "thayũ wa w'o," naw'o nĩ thayũ wa tene na tene. (1 Timotheo 6:19) Vai ĩvuku yĩngĩ yĩtonya kwĩthĩwa na maũndũ ta asu.
Wavanga kũsomaa Mbivilia na ũyĩkaa ũu ũte kũeka, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kwĩkala nesa na ũimũmanya Ngai. Ĩndĩ ũendeee kũsoma Mbivilia, nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa na makũlyo maingĩ. Ĩla kweethĩwa ũu, lilikanaa ngelekany'o nzeo ya ũla Mũethiovia waĩ thayũ myaka 2,000 mĩvĩtu. Aĩ na makũlyo maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia. Ĩla wakũlilw'e kana nũkũelewa maũndũ ala wasomaa, asũngĩie atĩĩ: "Nĩmanya ata ndeũtongoew'a nĩ mũndũ?" * Nĩweetĩkĩlile kũtetheew'a nĩ mũndũ ũmwe waĩ mwalimũ mũseo wa Mbivilia ũla weetawa Vilivu, na waĩ mũmanyĩw'a wa Yesũ. (Meko ma Atũmwa 8:30, 31, 34) O naku ũkethĩwa ũyenda kũtetheew'a ũmanye Mbivilia mũnango, nĩtũũkũthokya ũkũlye kwĩsĩla Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam kana ũandĩke valũa ũtũmĩĩte ĩsandũkũ ya valũa yĩla yaĩle o tondũ vonanĩtw'e ĩkasetinĩ yĩĩ. O na no ũneene na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ila syĩ kĩsionĩ kyenyu kana ũkathi Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ĩla yĩ kĩsionĩ kyenyu. Nũseo ũkambĩĩa kũsoma Mbivilia na ũyĩtĩkĩla ĩũtetheesye kwĩkala nesa.
Ethĩwa wĩona ne ũndũ wĩ vinya kũĩkĩĩa Mbivilia, wĩkũlw'a wĩloele vitio nguvĩ yĩ na kyongo Tũtonya Kũmanya Ata Kana Mbivilia Nĩ ya W'o? Nĩ kana ũkwate vitio ĩsu no ũtũmĩe ũvano ũũ wa QR kana ũkalika Kĩsesenĩ kya jw.org/kam, na ũisisya ungu wa MAVUKU > VITIO > MBIVILIA
^ kal. 8 Nĩ kana ũkwate motao angĩ kuma Mbivilianĩ ala matonya ũkũtetheesya, sisya Kĩsese kitũ kya jw.org/kam. Sisya ungu wa MOMANYĨSYO MA MBIVILIA > MOSŨNGĨO MA MAKŨLYO MA MBIVILIA.

translation:
Scripture is inspired by God and is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness. (2 Timothy 3:16) The value of Scripture is that it helps us to become morally strong people. That is why the Bible says: "The word of God is alive and exerts power." (Hebrews 4:12) The word of God is profitable because it is powerful and can discern our thoughts. One reason is that it helps us to distinguish right from wrong, and another reason is that it helps us to know God and his purposes.—1 Timothy 4:8; James 4:8.
To meditate on spiritual things is beneficial. The Bible encourages us to pay attention. Let us examine what the Scriptures teach.
Associate with those who are exemplary.—Ephesians 4:31, 32; 5:22, 25, 28, 33.
Be modest in speech and be kind in our dealings with others.—Psalm 37:8; Proverbs 17:22.
Avoid bad associations.—1 Corinthians 6:9, 10.
Work diligently and honestly.—Proverbs 10:4; 28:19; Ephesians 4:28. *
Many brothers in Asia wrote to ask whether the Bible teaches that we should work hard. And although many brothers were already working hard, the brothers in Asia wanted to know specifically how each one could apply this principle to his own circumstances. I will therefore discuss some points that might help you understand the teachings of the Bible. What scriptures show the importance of working hard? Vincent wrote: "What I read in the Bible motivates me to use my time well so that I can continue serving Jehovah. Working hard according to the principles found in the Bible helps us to remain united." Similarly, a sister named Annalou said: "Reading regularly in the Bible has strengthened me spiritually. It has helped me to feel closer to our Father and to appreciate our privileges more fully."
To demonstrate appreciation to God, some also study his Word, and Vincent added: "Studying the Bible has become a personal matter between me and Jehovah, something I really cherish." Vincent's comment shows the value of personal study, and it highlights that the Bible itself can help us to come to know God better. And each week, taking time to meditate on what you learn can help you to remember it and to see how it applies to your life. Also, you will realize that God provides opportunities for us to store up treasures with everlasting life in view, rather than being distracted by "the uncertainty of riches," which are temporary. (1 Timothy 6:19) Many temptations can distract us from spiritual pursuits.
Regularly reading the Bible and meditating on it can help you to remain close to God and to strengthen your faith. The more you read the Bible, the more benefits you will experience. But even if you have been studying for years, like Demetrius who studied for 2,000 years, there are still many gems hidden in the Bible. However, if you find yourself struggling to understand what you read, ask yourself: "Who can explain this to me?" * I benefited greatly from talking to a fellow elder named Philip, who was a disciple of Jesus. (Acts 8:30, 31, 34) And if you want to gain a deeper understanding of the Bible, you can visit our website at www.jw.org/kam or write to the address listed on this brochure, and we will be happy to send you literature. Or you may wish to request a Kingdom Ministry School demonstration by contacting the local congregation. So continue to read the Bible and apply what you learn in your life.
If you wonder, 'How can I know whether the Bible is from God?' or 'Can I trust the Bible?' scan the QR code or visit jw.org/kam and go to RESOURCES > ARTICLES > THE BIBLE
^ par. 8 If you would like further assistance in understanding the Bible, visit the website jw.org/kam. Go to BIBLE TEACHING TOOLS > QUESTIONS ABOUT THE BIBLE.
^ par. 11 Also, take time each week to review the article "Things That Help Us Understand," and ask yourself, 'What did I learn?'

Kwasũanĩa ĩlondu yĩĩ kĩthekanĩ na yaaa. Nokwĩthĩwa yĩtiiwe nĩ malondu ala angĩ yĩendeee na kũya nyeki. Na yĩyĩsa kũvindũka ĩyĩthĩa ĩyene mũĩthi na malondu ala angĩ, na saa isu kũendeee na kũtuka. Yaĩie myandanĩ, kũndũ kwĩ nyamũ mbai sya kĩthekanĩ na yĩi na mũndũ ũyĩsũvĩa. Ĩtina yĩyĩsa kwĩw'a wasya yĩwĩsĩ wa mũĩthi. Mũĩthi ũsu aisemba vala yĩĩ, aiyosa, aiyĩlinga na ngũa yake, na aiyĩkua nginya mũsyĩ.
MAVINDA maingĩ Yeova eyĩelekanasya na mũĩthi ta ũsu. Nthĩnĩ wa Ndeto yake aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nyie, ngakũlĩĩlya malondu makwa, na kũmamantha."—Esekieli 34:11, 12.
"Malondu ma Kĩsesi Kyakwa"
Malondu ma Yeova naaũ? Kwa ũkuvĩ, malondu ma Yeova nĩ andũ ala mamũthaithaa na mamwendete. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Tũthaithe na kwĩkunamya; Tũmũtulĩlyei ndu Yeova Mũmbi waitũ: Nũndũ nĩwe Ngai waitũ, na ithyĩ twĩ andũ ma ĩĩthya yake, na malondu ma kw'oko kwake." (Savuli 95:6, 7) O tondũ malondu mendete mũno kũatĩĩa mũĩthi wamo, now'o athaithi ma Yeova mendete kũatĩĩa Mũĩthi woo. Yo ũu nĩ kwasya kana mo mayĩkaa naĩ? Aiee. Mavinda amwe athũkũmi ma Ngai nĩmesaa kwĩthĩwa me "malondu manyaĩĩku," "malondu mau," na makethĩwa 'maĩte ta malondu.' (Esekieli 34:12; Mathayo 15:24; 1 Vetelo 2:25) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ĩla mũndũ weelelũka, Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa na wĩkwatyo kana mũndũ ũsu akamũsyokea.
We no wasye kana o na yu Yeova nĩ Mũĩthi waku? Yeova onanasya ata kana we nĩ Mũĩthi ũmũnthĩ? Ekai twone nzĩa itatũ:
Nũtũĩthasya kĩ-veva. Yeova aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ngamaĩthya kĩsesinĩ kĩseo," ongeleele kwasya, "Nĩkw'o makakoma kyengonĩ kĩseo; na makaĩthw'a kĩsesinĩ kĩnou." (Esekieli 34:14) Ĩvinda yonthe Yeova nũtũnengae lĩu mũseo wa kĩ-veva ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩle. Yo no ũlilikane kĩlungu wasomie mavukunĩ maitũ, ũvoo weethukĩĩisye, kana vitio yatumie ũkwata ũsũngĩo wa mboya yaku? No nginya ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩwe wakũĩkĩĩthisye nesa vyũ kana Yeova nũkũthĩnĩkĩaa!
Nũtũsũvĩaa na kũtwĩkĩa vinya. Yeova athanĩte atĩĩ: "Ngatũnga ũla walũngilw'e, na ngooveea ũla watũlĩtwe, na ngeekĩa vinya ũla wawaie." (Esekieli 34:16) Yeova nũmekĩaa vinya ala maemeewe nĩ mawĩmakĩo. Nĩwovaa malondu make ala maũmĩu, na aimatetheesya mavoe o na ethĩwa maũmĩĩtw'e nĩ athaithi ala angĩ. Nũtũngaa ala meelelũkile, na methĩawa na mawoni mataĩle ĩũlũ woo ene.
Nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa. Yeova easya atĩĩ: "Ngamaumya kũndũ kw'onthe kũla manyaĩĩkĩtw'e," aendeee kwasya, "Ngamantha ũla waĩte." (Esekieli 34:12, 16) Ĩla mũndũ weelelũka, Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ kana no amũsyokee. Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ ĩla ĩlondu yaaa, na nũyĩmanthaa, na ayona nũtanaa mũno. (Mathayo 18:12-14) Ũu nĩ w'o nũndũ aĩtye kana athũkũmi make nĩ, 'malondu make, malondu ma kĩsesi kyake.' (Esekieli 34:31) We wĩ ũmwe wa malondu asu make.
Ĩla mũndũ weelelũka, Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ kana no amũsyokee. Nũtanaa mũno ĩla mũndũ ũsu wamũsyokea
"Eũvya Mĩthenya Yaitũ O ta Tene"
Nĩkĩ Yeova ũkũũmantha na kũũthokya ũmũsyokee? Nũndũ endaa wĩthĩwe na ũtanu. Athanĩte kana "kũkeethĩwa mĩono ["mbua nene," NWT] ya ũathimo" kwa malondu make. (Esekieli 34:26) Watho ũsu nĩ wa w'o nũndũ we mwene nĩwĩyoneete Yeova aikũathima.
Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ maseo ala weeyoneie ũyĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, weewie ata ĩla wamanyie ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, na kĩeleelo kyake kwa andũ? Nũlilikene ũndũ weew'aa mũyo ĩla wakomana na athaithi ma Yeova maũmbanonĩ manene? Nao nata ĩla watavanasya na ũikwata mũndũ ũkwendeew'a nĩ ũvoo mũseo, yo ndwasyokaa mũsyĩ wĩw'ĩte mũyo na wĩ mwĩanĩe?
O na ũmũnthĩ no wĩthĩwe na ũtanu ũsu ĩngĩ. Athũkũmi ma Ngai ma ĩvinda ya tene mavoyie atĩĩ: "Tũthyũũe ithyĩ kwaku, ame Yeova, na tũkathyũũĩka; Eũvya mĩthenya yaitũ o ta tene." (Iĩo 5:21) Yeova nĩwasũngĩie mboya ĩsu, na andũ make masyokea ĩngĩ kũmũthũkũma me atanu. (Neemia 8:17) O ta ũu, Yeova nũkasũngĩa mboya syaku.
Ĩndĩ kũmũsyokea Yeova ti ũndũ wĩ laisi. Kwaeka twone maũndũ amwe matonya kũtuma ũsu wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya, na tũyona ũndũ tũtonya kũkĩlya maũndũ asu vinya.

translation:
When I lose a sheep, it grieves me greatly. But I search for it until I find and rescue it. And similarly, when one strays from the flock, he continues to go astray and perish. Truly, my people, the flock is scattered because it has no shepherd. It is like a lost lamb seeking its owner. The owner will certainly look for his sheep, and he will seek, find, and carry it on his shoulders.
MANY shepherds Jehovah has appointed for his people. Through his Word he says: "You, my flock, I will search for, and I will feed them."—Ezekiel 34:11, 12.
"The Sheep of My Pasture"
What are Jehovah's sheep? Simply put, Jehovah's sheep are people who love and worship him. The Bible states: "Let us bow down and bend the knee; let us kneel before Jehovah our Maker: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, the flock under his care." (Psalm 95:6, 7) So while many people claim to be shepherds, only those approved by Jehovah are shepherds of His flock. Is this fair? Yes. Some of God's ancient names for his people were "my little flock," "my people," and expressions such as 'sheep of his hand.' (Ezekiel 34:12; Matthew 15:24; 1 Peter 2:25) If you understand this, then remember, Jehovah cares for and protects anyone who turns to him.
Do you know whether you have a Shepherd, Jehovah? Does Jehovah care even if you feel like an insignificant person? Let us see three reasons:
He searches for them diligently. Jehovah says: "I will search for my sheep and bring them back from all places where they have been scattered," and he adds, "I will seek out the lost ones and bring back the strayed ones." (Ezekiel 34:14) Throughout the earth, Jehovah actively seeks out individuals who are like scattered sheep. Will you allow yourself to be found when you are troubled, or will you stubbornly refuse help and try to manage on your own? Do not let pride prevent you from accepting assistance from Jehovah!
He strengthens and feeds them spiritually. Jehovah promises: "I will feed them myself, and I will guide them, and I will comfort them." (Ezekiel 34:16) Jehovah provides spiritual nourishment through his Word. He cares for his sheep lovingly, and he refreshes them with wholesome spiritual food. He guides those who are willing to learn, and he helps them to develop accurate understanding.
He protects them. Jehovah assures us: "I will guard my flock, and I will look after them," and he continues, "I will care for my sheep." (Ezekiel 34:12, 16) If one of his sheep goes astray, Jehovah does not abandon him. Jehovah protects them from danger, and he patiently waits for them, and he never gives up on them. (Matthew 18:12-14) This is what he means when he says that his people are "my flock, the flock of my pasture." (Ezekiel 34:31) You are one of his sheep.
If one of his sheep goes astray, Jehovah does not abandon him. He never gives up on someone whom he loves.
"Abundant Peace Forever"
Will Jehovah continue to comfort and strengthen those who love him? Yes, he promises to provide "peace in abundance ["fullness of peace," NWT] for his people." (Ezekiel 34:26) That promise will come true when Jehovah fully establishes his Kingdom.
To show appreciation for everything that Jehovah does for us, let us deepen our understanding of his purpose. For example, have you ever wondered why God allows suffering, and how he feels about mankind? Consider whether there is something more you can learn about Jehovah's qualities and standards. And perhaps you can help others who are seeking answers.
Or you may be facing personal difficulties. God's servants in ancient times expressed this sentiment: "Come, let us seek Jehovah, and let us exert ourselves; Let abundant peace forever be ours." (Isaiah 5:21) Jehovah encourages us, and his people rejoice more and more in their relationship with him. (Nehemiah 8:17) So, Jehovah will encourage you too.
Showing love for Jehovah is not difficult. As we examine some practical ways to strengthen our faith, we will see things we can do to make our ministry more effective, and we will discover things we can do to remain steadfast.

Ũelesyo wa kũmwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi wakũ ni mwaũ?
Ũsungio
Nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlile Yesũ Klisto ya mũtangĩĩi wakũ? Kũelewa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ nesa, nonginya ũelewe ĩsyĩtwa "Yesũ Klisto," "wakũ," na"mũtangĩĩi."
Yesũ Klisto nũũ? Andũ aingĩ nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana Yesũ Klisto nĩ mũndũ mũseo, mwalimũ mũnene, ona mwathani wa Ngai. Maũndũ aa nĩmaw'o yĩũlũ wa Yesũ, vamwe na ou ũũ tiw'o ũelesyo mwĩanĩu. Mbivilia ĩtwĩaa kana Yesũ nĩ ngai thinĩ wa mwĩĩ, Ngai e mwĩĩnĩ (Yoana1:1, 14). Ngai ookie kũũ nthĩ kũtũmanyĩsya, kũtũvosya, Kũtũngĩĩa, kũthĩnw'a na kũkw'a kwondũ witũ! Yesũ Klisto nĩ Ngai, mumbi, Ngai weka. Nĩwetĩkĩlile Yesũ ũyũ?
Mũtangĩĩi nũũ, na vata wake kwitũ ni mwaũ? Mbivilia ĩtwĩaa kana ithyonthe nĩtwekie naĩ; nĩtwekie maũndũ mathe (Alomi 3:10-18). Nũndũ wa naĩ nĩtwaĩlwe nĩ ũthatu wa Ngai na ũsilĩlo. Ũsilĩlo ũla waĩle nũndũ wa naĩ kwa Ngai ũla ũtemũmĩnũkĩlyo na wa tene na tene nĩ ũsilĩlo wa tene na tene (Alomi6:23; Ũvũanyo20:11-15). Kii nĩkyo kũtũmi tũkwenda mũtangĩĩi!
Yesũ Klisto ookie kũũ nthĩ na akw'a kwondũ witũ. Kĩkw'u kya Yesũ kyaĩ ndĩvi ya naĩ syitũ ya tene na tene (2 Akolintho 5:21). Yesũ akw'ie nĩ kana aĩve ĩtuvi ya naĩ sitũ (Alomi 5:8). Yesũ nĩwaĩvĩe ndĩvi nĩkana tũĩkaaĩve. Kũthayũũka kwa Yesũ kuma kĩkw'uni nĩ ũĩkĩĩthyo kana kikw'ũ kyake nĩkĩanĩu kũĩvĩa naĩ syitu. Kĩu nikyo kĩtumi Yesũ nĩwe mũtangĩĩi e weka (Yoana 14:6; Meko Na Atũme 4:12)! Nũkũĩkĩĩa Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi wakũ?
Yesũ nĩwe mũtangĩĩi wakũ? Andũ aingĩ matalĩthasya ũklisto ta kũenda kanisanĩ, kũatĩĩa mĩtũo kana kũlea kwĩka naĩ imwe. Ũũ tiw'o ũklisto. Ũklisto wa w'o nĩ ngwatanĩo ya mũndũ mweene na Yesũ Klisto. Kwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta we mũtangĩĩi wakũ nĩ kwia mũĩkĩĩo waku mweene na wĩkwatyo nthĩnĩ wake. Vai mũndũ ũtangĩĩawa kwĩsila mũĩkĩĩo wa angĩ. Vai mũndũ ũtangĩĩawa nũndũ wa meko ma na. Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo nĩ mũndũ mweene kũmwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi wake, kũĩkĩĩa kĩkw'ũ kyake ta ndĩvi ya naĩ syake na kũthayũũka kwake ta ũĩkĩĩthyo wa thayũ ũtathela (Yoana3:16) Yesũ ni mũtangĩĩi wakũ mwene?
Kethĩwa nũkwenda kũmwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi waku mweene, weta ndeto ii mbee wa Ngai. Lilikana, kũvoya mboya ĩno kana mboya ĩngĩ ona yĩva kũyĩũtangĩĩya. No kũmũĩkĩĩa Yesũ na wĩa wake mwĩanĩu mũkelanyonĩ kũtonya kũtangĩĩa kũma naĩnĩ. Mboya ĩno nĩkwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo waku kwa Ngai na kũmũtũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa kũũnenga ũtangĩĩo." Ngai nĩnĩsĩ nĩnĩkwatĩte naĩ na nĩnaĩle ũsilĩlo. Ĩndĩ nĩnĩsĩ Yesũ Klisto nĩwoosie ũsilĩlo ũla naĩle nĩkana kwĩsila mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wake nĩekewe. Ningwosa ũekeo kũma kwaku na kwia wĩkwatyo nthĩnĩ wa ũtangĩĩo. Nĩneetĩkĩla Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi wakwa! Nĩmũvea nũndũ wa mũmo wakũ na ũekeo - mũthinzio wa thayũ ũtathela! Ameni!
We nĩwatw'a ũtwi kũmwĩtĩkĩla Klisto nũndu wa maũndũ ala wasoma vaa? Ethĩwa nĩ w'o, tina vau vaandikĩtwe "nĩnamwĩtĩkĩla Klisto umunthĩ".
English
Ũelesyo wa kũmwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi wakũ ni mwaũ?

translation:
Indeed
The question of accepting Jesus as your savior is important, isn't it?
Consideration
Have you accepted Jesus Christ as your savior? To understand this matter well, let us examine the meaning of "Jesus Christ," "savior," and "accept."
Who is Jesus Christ? Many people believe that Jesus Christ is just a good man, a great teacher, or a prophet of God. These things are true about Jesus, but there is much more to his story than that. The Bible teaches us that Jesus is God himself (John 1:1, 14). God came to earth to reveal himself to us, to save us, to forgive us, to heal us, and to give us eternal life! Jesus Christ is God, incarnate, God alone. Have you accepted this Jesus?
What is sin, and its consequence to us is what? The Bible teaches that everyone has sinned; everyone has done wrong things (Romans 3:10-18). The penalty for sin is separation from God and death. Death will be paid by the grace of God and eternally and eternally is eternal death (Romans 6:23; Revelation 20:11-15). This is why we need to accept salvation!
Jesus Christ came to earth and pays our debt. Jesus' sacrifice is our only hope of eternal life (2 Corinthians 5:21). Jesus died so that we might have eternal life (Romans 5:8). Jesus took our place so that we could take His. Turning to Jesus means receiving His sacrifice and believing in Him. That is why Jesus is the only savior (John 14:6; Acts 4:12)! Will you accept Jesus as your savior?
Is Jesus your savior? Many people profess Christianity without going to church, fearing others or being ashamed to associate with them. But this is not Christianity. True Christianity is a personal relationship between a person and Jesus Christ. Accepting Jesus as your savior is entering into a personal relationship with Him and following His ways. No one is saved because of another person's righteousness. No one is saved by their own good deeds. The way to salvation is for a person to accept Jesus as his savior, believe in His sacrifice as payment for sin and turn to Him for forgiveness (John 3:16) Is Jesus your savior then?
If you want to accept Jesus as your savior, pray this prayer today. However, simply praying this prayer or another similar one does not guarantee salvation. But believing in Jesus and living according to His will sincerely leads to salvation. This prayer expresses your heart to God and shows Him your desire for salvation. God is faithful and He hears us. I testify that Jesus Christ is the way, the truth, and the life, and through faith in Him alone, we are saved. I urge you to seek Him and enter into a relationship of salvation. Accept Jesus as your savior! It is a matter of your eternal destiny – the gift of eternal life! Amen!
We often hear people professing Christ due to various reasons they have read about. Sometimes they say, "I have accepted Christ inwardly."
The evidence of accepting Jesus as your savior is what?

YOSIA aĩ na ũkũũ o wa myaka nyanya yĩla watw'ĩkie mũsumbĩ wa mbaĩ ila ilĩ sya ĩtheo sya Isilaeli. Ĩsu yaĩ myaka mĩnini mũno kwa mũndũ kũtw'ĩka mũsumbĩ. Kwoou ambĩĩa kũsumbĩka nĩwatetheeiw'e nĩ andũ amwe aima kũsumbĩka ĩ nthĩ.
Ĩtina wa kũsumbĩka myaka mũonza, Yosia nĩwambĩĩie kũmũmantha Yeova. Atĩĩie ngelekany'o ya asumbĩ aseo ta Ndaviti, Yeosavati, na Esekia. Na ĩndĩ e o mwanake, Yosia eekaa ũndũ wa ũkũmbaũ.
Kwa ĩvinda yĩasa Aisilaeli aingĩ meethĩĩtwe me athũku. Mathaithaa ngai sya ũvũngũ na kũkumanĩa mĩvw'anano. Kwoou Yosia na aũme make maumaala na mambĩĩa kũvetanga ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ kuma ĩ nthĩ. Ũsu waĩ wĩa mũnene mũno nũndũ andũ aingĩ mũno mathaithaa ngai sya ũvũngũ. Nũtonya kwona Yosia vaa na aũme make mayananga mĩvw'anano
Ĩtina wa ũu Yosia nĩwaiie aũme atatũ maũngamĩe wĩa wa kũseũvya ĩkalũ ya Yeova. Mbesa nĩsyoombaniwe kuma kwĩ andũ na syanewa aũme asu nĩ kana maĩve atethya ma wĩa ũsu. Namo maendee na kũthũkũma ĩkalũnĩ, mũthembi mũnene Ilikia nĩwoonie kĩndũ kya vata mũno vau. Oonie ĩvuku ya mĩao yĩla Yeova weeie Mose aandĩke ĩvinda yĩasa mũno ĩthelu. Yo yaaĩte myaka mingĩ.
Ĩvuku yĩu nĩyatwaĩwe Yosia nake asya asomewe. Yĩla Yosia weethukĩĩisye, nĩwoonie kana andũ nĩmaekete kũatĩĩa mĩao ya Yeova. Nĩweewie kyeva mũno nĩ ũndũ ũsu, na atembũanga ngũa syake o tondũ ũtonya kwona vaa. Na asya: 'Yeova nĩ mũthilĩku nũndũ witũ, kĩtumi nũndũ aaĩthe maitũ mayaakwata mĩao ĩla ĩandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ yĩĩ.'
Na Yosia amwĩĩaĩa mũthembi mũnene Ilikia amũkũlye Yeova ũndũ we Yeova ũkwĩkana na andũ asu. Nake Ilikia athi kũkũlya mwathani mũndũ mũka weetawa Ulita. Ulita amũnengie Ilikia ũtũmani ũũ kuma kwa Yeova amũtwaĩe Yosia: 'Yelusaleme na andũ onthe nĩmeũsilĩlwa nũndũ nĩmathaithĩte ngai sya ũvũngũ na ĩ nthĩ ĩkausũwa nĩ ũthũku. Ĩndĩ nũndũ, we Yosia, nĩwĩkĩte ũla ũseo, ũsilĩlo ũũ ũkooka ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kyaku.'
2 Mavinda 34:1-28.
Makũlyo
- Yosia aĩ na ũkũũ mwaũ yĩla watw'ĩkie mũsumbĩ, na ambĩĩie kwĩka ata ĩtina wa myaka mũonza ya ũsumbĩ wake?
- We wĩona Yosia aeendee na kwĩka ata vaa visanĩ?
- Mũthembi mũnene oonie kyaũ ĩkalũ yĩendee na kũseũvw'a?
- Yosia atembũangie ngũa syake nĩkĩ?
- Nĩ ũtũmani mwaũ kuma kwa Yeova ũla Ulita, mwathani mũndũ mũka, wamũtwaĩe Yosia?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma 2 Mavinda 34:1-28
Yosia enengane ngelekany'o myaũ kwa ala matonya kwĩthĩwa momĩĩisye thĩna ĩvinda ya kwĩana kwoo? (2 Mav. 33:21-25; 34:1, 2; Sav. 27:10)
Yosia eekie maũndũ maũ manene makũendeesya na mbee ũthaithi wa w'o ĩvindanĩ ya mwaka wa 8, 12, 18 ya ũsumbĩ wake? (2 Mav. 34:3, 8)
Nĩ ĩsomo yaũ ya kwĩkalya kũndũ kwitũ kwa kũthaithĩa kwĩ kũseo tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kumana na ngelekany'o ĩla yaiiwe nĩ Mũsumbĩ Yosia na Mũthembi Mũnene Ilikia? (2 Mav. 34:9-13; Nth. 11:14; 1 Ako. 10:31)

translation:
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years over Judah; and he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done. And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after God, the God of his fathers David. And in the twelfth year, he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images. And they broke down the altars of Baal, and cut down the groves that were beside them; and he destroyed the houses of the idols, and the incense altars out of all the cities of Judah. And he defiled the altars where the kings of Judah had burned incense to Baal, and to the sun, and to the moon, and to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven. And he brought forth the priests of the high places, and defiled them upon their altars; and he burned the bones of men upon them. And he purged Judah and Jerusalem from all the abominations that Jeroboam had wrought to provoke to anger the Lord God of Israel. He also stopped those who sacrificed unto the false gods which were brought into the land of Judah. And he commanded all the people, saying, Serve the Lord God of Israel, and keep his commandments, and listen unto his words, that I may bring you no more into temptation. And Josiah took away all the abominations out of all the countries of the children of Israel.
And all the people acknowledged him to be the Lord God of Israel. And in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the temple, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law of the Lord given by Moses. And Josiah read all the words thereof. And he stood in the place where he was, and confessed before God, and said, Behold, I and my people will keep thy commandments, and observe thy laws which are written in this book. And he commanded all the people, saying, Keep ye the commandments of the Lord your God, and serve him. And all the people took hold of the covenant. And Josiah removed all the abominations out of the house of the Lord. And he commanded all the people, saying, If any man will not serve the Lord God of Israel, behold, his life shall be forfeit. And he said, Ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies. And all the people served the Lord their God.
And they ate the passover sacrifice. And Josiah commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in this book. For the passover had not been kept from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither had any king kept the passover until the days of Josiah. And in the thirty-first year of his reign, Josiah sent messengers to gather contributions for the house of the Lord. And he commanded them, saying, Go, gather money from all the people, as much as they can spare, to repair the house of the Lord. And the priests and Levites went forth to gather money from the people. And they gathered three thousand talents of silver, and five hundred talents of gold, and three hundred talents of brass. And they brought the money to the overseers of the house of the Lord, and they paid it out to the workmen who labored in the house of the Lord. And they repaired the house of the Lord, and restored it to its former glory. And Josiah offered sacrifices unto the Lord, and commanded all the people to offer sacrifices with him. And they sacrificed twelve oxen, and six lambs, and fifteen rams, all of them fat beasts. And they killed the passover sacrifices, and burned them upon the altar. And they ate the passover sacrifice, and drank wine. And Josiah commanded all the people, saying, Keep the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord your God, as it is written in this book. And they kept the feast seven days.
2 Chronicles 34:1-28.
Questions
- Did Josiah show faith by listening to the advice of others, and how did this affect his spiritual condition?
- What lessons can we learn from Josiah's example regarding diligence?
- What did Hilkiah the priest reveal about the law?
- Why did Josiah tear his clothes?
- What message did Hulda, a prophetess, send to Josiah through Shaphan?
Questions for further thought
- How did Josiah demonstrate humility when he learned about the consequences of neglecting God's Law? (2 Chron. 33:21-25; 34:1, 2; Ps. 27:10)
- What important work did Josiah undertake during the eighth, twelfth, and eighteenth years of his reign? (2 Chron. 34:3, 8)
- What lesson can we draw from the example of King Josiah and High Priest Hilkiah regarding the importance of being humble and responsive to correction? (2 Chron. 34:9-13; Prov. 11:14; 1 Cor. 10:31)

KWĨ Matukũ 28, Mwei wa 4, 2013, kwaĩ ũmbano wa mwanya Nagoya, Japan. Mũthenya ũsu andũ nĩmatanie mũno ĩla Anthony Morris wa Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye watangasie kumw'a kwa kavuku keũ ka kĩthyomo kya Japanese ketawa The Bible—
Kavuku kau ka mathangũ 128 no ũndũ ũmwe na yĩla ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Mathayo yĩ nthĩnĩ wa Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya ya Japanese, ĩndĩ ko nĩ ka mwanya mũno. Mwana-a-asa Morris aeleisye kana kavuku kau kaseũvĩtw'e "kwondũ wa kũtavya ala maneenaa Japanese ũvoo mũseo." Ko ke na maũndũ meva? Kaseũviw'e nĩkĩ? Na andũ me na woni wĩva ĩũlũ wako?
MAŨNDŨ ALA ME KAVUKUNĨ KAU
Ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu nĩmaseng'iw'e nĩ ũndũ kavuku kau ka Matthew kaandĩkĩtwe. Kĩthyomo kya Japanese kĩ mĩandĩko ĩlĩ: Ũmwe ũandĩkawa namba itheeanĩtye naw'o ũla ũngĩ ũandĩkawa namba ikyamene. Syĩndũ mbingĩ ndumbĩthye, o na mavuku maitũ ma mĩtũkĩ, iandĩkĩtwe namba ikyamene. Ĩndĩ ndeto ila syĩ kavukunĩ kau keũ iandĩkĩtwe itheeanĩtye o tondũ iandĩkawa makasetinĩ ma maũvoo na mavukunĩ ala ma vata ma kĩthyomo kya Japanese. Aingĩ ala masomaa mavuku ma kĩthyomo kĩu monaa mũandĩko ũsu wĩ laisi. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana, syongo ila syĩthĩawa kĩla ĩthangũnĩ syaandĩkiwe kũu katĩkatĩ ta syongo nini nĩ kana wĩthĩe mũndũ aisoma nĩ laisi kwona maũndũ ala manene.
Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma Japan mambĩĩe kũsoma kavuku kau mamina kũkakwata oou. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩ na myaka 80 na kĩndũ aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩsomete ĩvuku ya Mathayo mavinda maingĩ, ĩndĩ mũandĩko ũsu ũtheeanĩtye na syongo isu nini ninandetheeisye kũelewa nesa ũla Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ." Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũngĩ aandĩkie ũũ: "Nekalile nthĩ nasoma kavuku kau ka Matthew konthe vyũ. Namanyĩie mũandĩko ũla ũkyamene ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ ma Japan mendete mũandĩko ũla ũtheeanĩtye."
KASEŨVĨTW'E KWONDŨ WA ANDŨ MA JAPAN
Nĩkĩ ĩvuku yĩu yĩmwe ya Mbivilia yaĩlĩte mũno kwondũ wa kũtavya andũ ma Japan ũvoo mũseo? O na kau andũ aingĩ ma Japan mayĩsĩ Mbivilia, nĩmendaa kũmĩsoma. Kavuku kau ke na Ũvoo Mũseo ũla waandĩkiwe nĩ Mathayo nĩkeũtuma ala mataaona Mbivilia makwata kĩlungu kyayo na kũkĩsoma.
Nĩkĩ no ĩvuku ya Mathayo yanyuviwe? Andũ aingĩ ma Japan meew'a "Mbivilia" malilikanaa Yesũ Klĩsto. Kwoou ĩvuku ya Mathayo yanyuviwe nũndũ nĩyĩwetete masyĩtwa ma aaũmae ma Yesũ na ũndũ wasyaiwe. O na ĩngĩ yĩ na Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ wa Yesũ na wathani wake ũla ũeleetye nesa mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo. Andũ ma Japan nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ maũndũ asu.
Ĩla atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ ma Japan makwatie kavuku kau, nĩmambĩĩe kũkanengane nyũmba na nyũmba na ĩla masyokea ala manendeeiw'e. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe aandĩkie ũũ: "Yu nĩ na myanya mingĩ ya kũtiĩa andũ kĩsionĩ kitũ Ndeto ya Ngai." Aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "O na nanenganie kavuku ka Matthew mũthenya o ũsu twaĩ na ũmbano wa mwanya!"
ANDŨ ME NA WONI WĨVA ĨŨLŨ WAKO?
Atavany'a manenganae kavuku ka Matthew ata? Andũ aingĩ ma Japan nĩmesĩ ndeto ta "mbingĩlo ĩla ntheke," 'malũlũ mbee wa ngũlũe,' na "mũikemakĩe ĩndĩ ũndũ wa ũnĩ." (Mt. 6:34; 7:6, 13) Maseng'aa mũno mamanya kana ndeto isu syaneeniwe nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto. Ĩla aingĩ moo moona ndeto isu ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Mathayo, maasya atĩĩ: "Nĩthĩĩtwe ndyenda mũno kũsoma Mbivilia o na ethĩwa no ĩmwe."
Ĩla atavany'a masyokea ala mamatiĩe kavuku ka Matthew, aingĩ mamatavasya kana masomie kavuku kau konthe kana kĩlungu kyako mamina kũkatiĩwa oou. Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩ na myaka 60 na kĩndũ eeie mũtavany'a ũmwe atĩĩ: "Nĩnakasomie mavinda maingĩ na neew'a nakiakiw'a. Nĩngũũkũlya ũmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ ma Mbivilia."
Kavuku ka Matthew nĩkatũmĩawa kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe aendeee kũtavany'a kũndũ ta kũu nĩwanengie mũndũ mũka wa mũika kavuku kau na e-mail yake. Ĩtina wa ĩsaa, mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwaandĩkĩie mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu e-mail amwĩĩte nĩwakasomanga na eenda kũmanya maũndũ maingangĩ. Ĩtina wa kyumwa kĩmwe, mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na ambĩĩa o mĩtũkĩ kũthi maũmbanonĩ.
Tũvuku The Bible—The Gospel According to Matthew mbee wa 1,600,000 nĩtũtũmĩwe ikundi sya Japan, na kĩla mwei atavany'a nĩmanenganae ngili mbingĩ syatw'o. Ndeto sya mbee sya kavuku kau niwetete kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ sya ala makaumĩthĩtye. Syaĩtye atĩĩ: "Twĩĩkwatya kuma ngoonĩ kana kũsoma kavuku kaa kũkatuma mwendeew'a mũno nĩ Mbivilia."

translation:
On April 28, 2013, at a convention in Nagoya, Japan. This brother and his wife, Anthony Morris of the Itongues Congregation, were delighted to receive a cart full of Japanese Bibles—
128 copies and one with the cover of the book of Matthew from the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures in Japanese, which was also at the convention. Brother Morris explained that the carts were called "carts for carrying books for the Japanese publishers." What does this mean? How were they used? And how did people react to them?
OTHER THINGS ABOUT THE CARTS
At this convention, it was noticed that the carts used were the kind Matthew wrote about. The Japanese publication has two types of writing: One is written in large characters and the other is written in small characters. Many times, especially when there are many publications and books, they are written in small characters. So it seems that some of the carts were written in large characters so that they could be easily seen by those who carry the carts and other publications to the Japanese territory. Many readers of the publications appreciate this writing because it helps them find what they are looking for quickly. Another thing is that sometimes each item is labeled with a tag so that anyone reading it can easily see the important things.
Many elderly people in Japan eagerly read the books to understand them well. One eighty-year-old said: "I have read the book of Matthew many times, but this large character writing and this particular writing helped me understand it better than ever before, thanks to the Kingdom Proclamation." Another person wrote: "I am very happy to have read the book of Matthew again and again. I realized that this small character writing helps many people in Japan understand this large character writing."
WHY IT IS APPRECIATED BY PEOPLE IN JAPAN
Is this one Bible cart particularly helpful to people in Japan? And although many people in Japan do not have a Bible, they want to read it. The books that have a Good News message written by Matthew help people get to know the Bible and read it comfortably.
Is the book of Matthew appealing? Many Japanese associate "Bible" with Jesus Christ. So the book of Matthew appeals to them because it tells about Jesus' disciples and his activities. Also, it has the Kingdom Proclamation of Jesus and his Father, which brings real comfort to sincere people. People in Japan really appreciate these things.
But when Kingdom proclaimers in Japan find people, they gladly visit homes and share what they have learned. One elderly person wrote: "I have many opportunities to introduce people to the good news." He continued saying: "And I happily share the book of Matthew with everyone I meet during my visits!"
ARE PEOPLE ASKING FOR MORE?
Are Kingdom proclaimers sharing the book of Matthew often? Many people in Japan use expressions like "it's too much trouble," "it's just a waste of time," and "it's irrelevant to me." (Matt. 6:34; 7:6, 13) However, many now realize that these expressions are not in line with Jesus Christ. But more and more people see value in the Good News message in the book of Matthew, and they say: "I would like to read the Bible again and again."
But when Kingdom proclaimers share the book of Matthew, many are surprised to learn that they can study it on their own or with others. One 60-year-old man who is a Kingdom proclaimer said: "I have read many books, but none have impressed me as much. It has helped me understand many things in the Bible."
The book of Matthew is being used to help many people become Kingdom proclaimers. For example, one elderly person continued to visit someone so he could send him the book of Matthew via email. As a result, that person wrote back to the elderly person, saying he was reading it and wanted to learn more. Later, that person asked him to help him study the Bible and told him about some problems he was facing.
The Bible—The Gospel According to Matthew, which has over 1,600,000 copies, has been published in Japanese, and each month Kingdom proclaimers distribute as many as they can. The good news from this book continues to reach people everywhere. Some say: "We are grateful to be able to read this book and to know that the Bible is true."

text:
Mosyaanĩo ma Yesũ
(Luka 3.23–38)
1 Mav 17.11; Mwa 5.1; 22.18. Na kũsyawa kwa Yesũ Klĩsto kwailyĩ ũũ: Yĩla Meli inyia wake wevaĩtw'e nĩ Yosevu, matambĩte kũtwaana, ooneka e na ĩvu ya Veva Mũtheu. 19Na Yosevu mũũme wake, nĩkwĩthĩwa aĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu, na ndaenda kũmũsonokya mbee wa andũ, enda kũmũeka kĩmbithĩ. 20Ĩndĩ akĩsũanĩa maũndũ asu, sisya, mũlaĩka wa Mwĩaĩi amumĩlĩla ndotonĩ, akyasya, Yosevu, we mwana wa Ndaviti, ndũkakĩe kũtwaa Meli mũka waku; nũndũ kũitava kwake nĩ kwa Veva Mũtheu. 21#Lk 1.31; 2.21; Meko 4.12.Nake akasyaa kavĩsĩ; naku ũkaketa syĩtwa yako YESŨ; nũndũ nĩwe ũkatangĩĩa andũ make kuma naĩnĩ syoo. 22#Isa 7.14.Na ũu w'onthe ũtw'ĩkĩte, nĩ kana wĩanĩw'e ũla waneeniwe nĩ Mwĩaĩi na kanyw'a wa mwathani, akyasya,

translation:
The Genealogy of Jesus
(Luke 3:23–38)
1 #
1 Acts 17:11; Genesis 5:1; 22:18. The beginning of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. 2#Genesis 21:3,12; 25:26; 29:35; 49:10; 1 Chronicles 1:34. Abraham begot Isaac; and Isaac begot Jacob; and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers; 3#Acts 2:5,9; Genesis 38:29,30; Luke 4:18–22.and Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar; and Perez begot Hezron; and Hezron begot Ram; 4#Acts 2:10–12.and Ram begot Amminadab; and Amminadab begot Nahshon; and Nahshon begot Salmon; 5#Luke 4:13–17.and Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab; and Boaz begot Obed by Ruth; and Obed begot Jesse; 6#2 Samuel 12:24.and Jesse begot David.
And David begot Solomon by her who had been Uriah's wife; 7#1 Chronicles 3:10–14.and Solomon begot Rehoboam; and Rehoboam begot Abijah; and Abijah begot Asa; 8and Asa begot Jehoshaphat; and Jehoshaphat begot Joram; and Joram begot Uzziah; 9and Uzziah begot Jotham; and Jotham begot Ahaz; and Ahaz begot Hezekiah; 10and Hezekiah begot Manasseh; and Manasseh begot Ammon; and Ammon begot Josiah; 11#1 Chronicles 3:15,16.and Josiah begot Jeconiah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
12 #
1 Chronicles 3:17; Isaiah 3:2. And after the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah begot Shealtiel; and Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel; 13and Zerubbabel begot Abiud; and Abiud begot Eliakim; and Eliakim begot Azor; 14and Azor begot Zadok; and Zadok begot Achim; and Achim begot Eliud; 15and Eliud begot Eleazar; and Eleazar begot Matthan; and Matthan begot Jacob; 16#Matthew 27:17,22.and Jacob begot Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
17Now the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to Christ, fourteen generations.
The Genealogy of Jesus
(Luke 2:1–7)
18 #
Luke 1:35. Now the birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way: Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, but she became pregnant through the Holy Spirit. 19And her husband Joseph, being a righteous man, did not want to expose her to public disgrace, so he intended to divorce her quietly. 20But while he was thinking about this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary home as your wife, because what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit. 21#Luke 1:31; 2:21; Mark 4:12.She will give birth to a son, and you shall name him JESUS, because he will save his people from their sins." 22#Isaiah 7:14.All this took place to fulfill what the Lord has spoken through the prophet: 23"Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son,
and they shall call his name Immanuel;
which means, God with us." 24And Joseph awoke from sleep and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took his wife, 25#Luke 2:7.but he had no relations with her until she gave birth to a son, and he named him JESUS.

text:
"Syana nĩ ũtiĩwa kuma kwa Yeova."
Ĩla asyai makwata kana nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ, ĩndĩ kana kau no katume methĩwa na maũndũ maingĩ mũno ma kwĩka. Wamina kwĩthĩwa na kana, no ũseng'e kũmanya kana no nginya wĩyumye na ũitũmĩa ĩvinda yingĩ kũea kana kau. O na ĩngĩ, moalyũku ma mwĩĩ o vamwe na kwaĩwa nĩ too, nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtuma mũtwaano wenyu wĩthĩwa na mathĩna. Wĩ na ũla ũtwaanĩte nake nĩmwaĩle kwĩka moalyũku mana nĩ kana mwĩthĩwe mũtonya kũea kana kenyu, na mũisũvĩa mũtwaano wenyu. Ũtao wa Mbivilia ũtonya kũmũtetheesya ata kũthĩnĩkĩa maũndũ asu?
1 ELEWA ŨNDŨ KWĨTHĨWA NA KANA KŨTONYA KŨALYŨLA MAŨNDŨ
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Wendo nĩwũmĩĩasya, na nĩwĩkaa moseo." O na ĩngĩ wendo "ndwĩmanthĩaa syĩndũ, o na ndũthataa." (1 Akolintho 13:4, 5) Ĩla kĩveti kyakwata kana, ti ũsengy'o kwona kĩlĩko kyakyo kyonthe kĩisyoka kananĩ kau. Ũu nũtonya kũtuma mũũme wakyo ona ta kĩte na vata nake. Kwoou kĩveti kĩyaĩle kũeka kana kau katume kyũlwa nĩ mũũme. Kyeethĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo na tei, nĩkĩtonya kũmũtetheesya mũũme ew'e e wa vata, na e na kĩanda nthĩnĩ wa kũea kana kau.
Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Inyw'ĩ aũme, ĩkalai na iveti syenyu kwĩanana na ũmanyi." (1 Vetelo 3:7) Nũseo mũndũũme akaelewa kana kĩveti nĩkĩtũmĩaa vinya wakyo mwingĩ kĩyĩea kana. Kwoou, nũndũ kĩveti kyaku kĩ na kana kĩkũea, nĩkĩtonya kwĩthĩwa na maũndũ maito kĩlĩkonĩ, kĩkew'a kĩ kĩnou mũno, kana kĩ kĩtũlĩku ngoo. Mavinda angĩ nĩkĩtonya kũũthatĩa. Ĩndĩ o na ũu weethĩwa, ndũkew'e woo nũndũ ũla 'wũmĩĩasya kũthata e kavaa kwĩ ũla wĩ na ũtonyi.' (Nthimo 16:32) Tata ũkĩelewe, na ũikĩtetheesya vala kĩkwenda ũtethyo.—Nthimo 14:29.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Mũndũũme: Ndwaĩle kũekanĩsya kĩveti kyaku na kana. Nũseo ũkakĩtetheesya o na ethĩwe nĩ ũtukũ. Nĩwaĩle kũekana na maũndũ amwe nĩ kana ũkwate ĩvinda ya kwĩthĩwa na kĩveti kyaku na kana
Kĩveti: Ĩla mũũme waku ũkwenda ũkũtetheesya, ndũkalee. O na ethĩwa ndeĩka ũndũ vaĩle, ndũkamũtũle mũtĩ, ĩndĩ mũtetheesye o nesa amanye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka
2 LŨLŨMĨĨLYAI NGWATANĨO YENYU
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Makeethĩwa mwĩĩ ũmwe." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:24) O na ethĩwa yu mwĩ na kana, lilikanai kana mwĩ o "mwĩĩ ũmwe." Tatai ũndũ mũtonya nĩ kana mwĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo ndũmu.
Inyw'ĩ iveti, matũngĩei aũme menyu mũvea nũndũ wa kũmũtetheesya. Ndeto syenyu sya kũmatũngĩa mũvea nitonya 'kũmavosya.' (Nthimo 12:18) Nenyu aume, itavyei iveti syenyu kana nĩmũsyendete na mwĩ vata nasyo. Tavya kĩveti kyaku kana nũtanĩthaw'a nĩ maũndũ ala kĩkaa kĩsũvĩe mũsyĩ.—Nthimo 31:10, 28.
Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Mũndũ o na wĩva ndakamanthe kwĩuna mwene ĩndĩ kĩla mũndũ namanthe kũuna ũngĩ." (1 Akolintho 10:24) Mavinda onthe ĩkaa maũndũ ala matonya kũuna ũla ũtwaanĩte nake. Manthai ĩvinda ya kũea ngewa, mũtũmĩe ndeto sya kwĩkĩana vinya, na mũyĩthĩwa mwĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩthukĩanĩsya. Ndũkethĩawe ũyĩsũanĩa o we mwene maũndũnĩ ma kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ, vandũ va ũu ĩthĩawa ũisũanĩa mavata ma ũla ũngĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Mũikavatane ene kwa ene, ate o yĩla mwĩw'anĩte kwĩka ũu." (1 Akolintho 7:3-5) Kwoou, neeneai ũndũ ũsu mũte kũvithana kĩndũ. Mweethĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo na mũyĩeleanwa, ngwatanĩo yenyu ĩkeethĩwa yĩ ndũmu.
ŨNDŨ MŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Manthai ĩvinda mwĩthĩwe vandũ mwĩ o elĩ
Ĩka tũmaũndũ tũtonya kũmwony'a ũla ũtwaanĩte nake kana nũmwendete. Kwa ngelekany'o, no ũmũtũmĩe mesengyi nguvĩ, kana ũkamũetee kamũthĩnzĩo
3 KŨMANYĨSYA KANA KAKU
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE: "Kuma wĩ kana kanini nĩweesĩ maandĩko matheu, ala matonya kũĩvya kũvika ũtangĩĩo." (2 Timotheo 3:15) Vanga ũndũ waĩle kwĩka nĩ kana ũmanyĩsye kana kaku. Kana kethĩawa katonya kwĩmanyĩsya o na katanamba kũsyawa. Kwoou o na kate kasyae, no kamanye wasya waku na ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Ũu wĩonany'a kana no wambĩĩe kũkasomea kuma ke kanini. O na vala no kethĩwe kate kũelewa nĩ kĩla ũũkasomea, ũu nũtonya kũkatetheesya keĩthĩwa kayendeew'a nĩ kũsoma keana.
Ndũkasũanĩe kana kaku nĩ kanini mũno ũndũ katatonya kũelewa ĩla ũũneena ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Eka kew'e ũimũvoya Yeova. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 11:19) O na ĩla ũũthaũka nako, neena ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila Ngai wũmbĩte. (Savuli 78:3, 4) O ũndũ kana kaku kaendeee kwĩana, now'o kaendeeaa kũmanya kana nũmwendete Yeova, na ũu ũituma o nako kamwenda.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA:
Mũvoye Yeova aũnenge ũĩ wa kũmanyĩsya kana kaku
Tũngĩlĩĩla ndeto na maũndũ ala ma vata ũkwenda kana kaku kemanyĩsye kuma ke kanini

translation:
"A wise person listens to counsel from Jehovah."
But some people may be easily disturbed or upset by much stress, especially if they have had many bad experiences. Be patient when dealing with them, and try to understand why they react the way they do and give them lots of encouragement. And also, problems others face and talk about are often things that can cause your own feelings to become hurt. If you feel unable to help someone because it seems difficult to encourage them, then strengthen your own feelings. The teachings of the Bible can help us even to cope with difficult situations?
1 UNDERSTAND WHY PEOPLE REACT THE WAY THEY DO
THE BIBLE SAYS: "Love is patient and kind." And love "does not look for its own interests, nor does it take offense." (1 Corinthians 13:4, 5) But sometimes it is hard to show patience, especially if you do not see how their actions affect you. This could make your mate feel like you do not care about his or her feelings. Show your mate that you value him or her by being understanding. Being considerate and thoughtful can help you to deal with your mate's weaknesses, and it will also improve your relationship.
The Bible says: "Husbands, continue to live with your wives in a sensible way, showing honor to the wife." (1 Peter 3:7) This means that a husband should understand how his words might affect his wife. So, if your mate is upset, it may not be because of something you did, but because of other things he or she is dealing with. Other factors may also contribute. Especially if this happens, remember the principle that "patience is better than strength, and calmness of spirit than rashness."—Proverbs 14:29. Try to remain calm, and apply what you learn to your life.—Proverbs 16:32.
WHAT CAN HELP:
Mate: I find it difficult to be patient with my mate. This makes me feel frustrated and angry. I want to know how to deal with situations where I get upset with my mate.
Mate: If your mate is willing to listen, be open. And if there is a problem, talk to him or her calmly, so that he or she understands what is bothering you.
2 COMMUNICATING WITH YOUR MATE
THE BIBLE SAYS: "Be united to one another." (Philippians 2:24) And even if you agree on most things, remember to be "united to one another." Often, problems arise when communication breaks down.
Wives, speak kindly to your husbands about ways to improve. Your suggestions can "heal."—Proverbs 12:18. Husbands, listen to your wives, and do not dismiss their ideas. Value your mate's abilities, and do not be quick to criticize them.—Proverbs 31:10, 28.
The Bible says: "Let each person look out for his own interests, not just his own." (1 Corinthians 10:24) Problems often arise when people think only of themselves. Consider your mate's feelings, use kind words, and try to understand his or her point of view. Be willing to discuss matters openly and honestly, and seek advice from others who have successful marriages. The Bible says: "Each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband." (1 Corinthians 7:3-5) Of course, this requires effort. Be considerate and understanding, and your marriage will be stronger.
PROBLEMS THAT CAN ARISE:
Consider how your actions might affect your mate.
Sometimes, it may be hard to forgive someone who has wronged you. For example, maybe he or she spends too much money, or perhaps you disagree on how to raise your children.
3 KNOWING YOUR MATE
THE BIBLE SAYS: "From infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith." (2 Timothy 3:15) Take time to learn what your mate believes. Whether you agree or disagree, try to understand his or her viewpoint. If possible, read the Bible together and discuss what you learn. This can help you both grow spiritually. Don't hesitate to ask questions if something is unclear, and don't feel bad if you need to reread passages.
Think about whether your mate's beliefs align with God's principles. Seek Jehovah's guidance. (Proverbs 3:5, 6) And if you find that your beliefs differ, continue to show love for your mate and strive to learn more about Jehovah, and this will motivate you to treat him or her kindly.
PROBLEMS THAT CAN ARISE:
Ask Jehovah to help you understand your mate's viewpoint.
Take time to discuss things that bother you and listen carefully to your mate's explanation.

text:
Andũ amwe makũlasya kana ngewa ĩla ĩeleetw'e ĩũlũ wa Ndaviti na Ngoliathu nĩ ũndũ weekĩkie kana no mbano? Ĩla ũũsomaa kĩlungu kĩla kyavĩta, nĩwĩthĩwa wakwatwa nĩ nzika ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala maeleetw'e ngewanĩ ĩsu? Ethĩwa nĩweethĩwa na nzika, kwasũanĩa makũlyo aa atatũ.
1 | Nĩvatonyeka mũndũ akethĩwa e na ũasa ta wa vuti kenda na nusu (mita 2.9)?
Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngoliathu aĩ na ũasa kana 'kĩũngamo kya mĩkono thanthatũ na ĩkwata ya kĩtaa.' (1 Samueli 17:4) Mũkono ũmwe wĩ na ũasa wa inzi 17.5 (sendimita 44.5), na kĩtaa kĩmwe kĩ na ũasa wa inzi 8.75 (sendimita 22.2). Wongelany'a inzi isu syonthe, waĩle kũkwata ũasa wa vakuvĩ vuti kenda na inzi thanthatũ (mita 2.9). Andũ amwe maasyaa kana Ngoliathu ndesa kwĩthĩwa aĩ mũasa ũu, ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ũmũnthĩ, mũndũ ũla mũasa vyũ waaoneka aĩ na ũasa wa vuti mbee wa 8 na inzi 11 (mita 2.7) Kwoou nĩ ũndũ ũtatonyeka Ngoliathu akethĩwa aĩ mũasanga kwĩ mũndũ ũsu na inzi 6 (sendimita 15) kana aĩ o mũasa kwĩ ũu? Ngoliathu aĩ wa mbaĩ ya Alevai, ala meesĩkĩe kwĩthĩwa me andũ anene mũno vyũ. Ĩvuku yĩmwe ya Egypt yĩla yaandĩkiwe myakanĩ ya 1200-1300 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, yĩeleasya kana asikalĩ amwe ma kuma nthĩ ya Kanaani maĩ na ũasa wa vuti mbee wa nyanya (mita 2.4). Kwoou ti ũndũ ũtatonyeka Ngoliathu akethĩwa aasavĩte mũno ũu.
2 | We Ndaviti aĩ mũndũ waĩ thayũ kana no ngewa?
Ve ĩvinda asomi matataa kwonany'a kana maũndũ ala mawetetwe ĩũlũ wa Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti no mbano sya andũ, ĩndĩ nĩmaemiwe nĩ kwĩka ũu. Andũ ala menzaa syĩndũ sya tene mayĩnza nĩmeethĩie maandĩko mawetete "nyũmba ya Ndaviti." O na Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwaeleisye kana Ndaviti aĩ kw'o. (Mathayo 12:3; 22:43-45) Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia, ve nzyawa kũndũ kwĩlĩ ila iĩkĩĩthasya kana Yesũ nĩwe Masia na nzyawa isu syelĩ syumanĩte na Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti. (Mathayo 1:6-16; Luka 3:23-31) Kwa w'o, Ndaviti aĩ mũndũ waĩ thayũ, ĩndĩ ngewa yake ti wano.
3 | Maũndũ ala maeleetw'e ngewanĩ ya Ndaviti na Ngoliathu meekĩkie vandũ vesĩkĩe nĩ andũ?
Mbivilia ĩwetete kana kaũ ũsu wokitĩiwe Mwandanĩ wa Ela. O na nĩyĩeleetye mũnango kwa kwonany'a kana Avilisiti moombanĩte mũingo ũmwe wa kĩĩma ũla waĩ katĩ katĩ wa taoni ilĩ, taoni ya Soko na Aseka. Namo Aisilaeli moombanĩte mũingo ũla ũngĩ wa kĩĩma. Kũndũ kũu kwawetwa nĩkwĩsĩkĩe nĩ andũ?
Kwaeka twone ũndũ mũndũ ũmwe wĩla kũthi isionĩ isu waĩtye. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũla watũtwaie Mwandanĩ wa Ela ndaĩ mũndũ wa ndĩni. Twang'aĩie na nzĩa yatũtwaie nginya kĩĩmanĩ ĩũlũ. Ĩla twasyaisye mwandanĩ twĩ vau kĩĩmanĩ ĩũlũ, atwĩie tũsome 1 Samueli 17:1-3. Na ĩndĩ ooloota mũingo ũla ũngĩ wa kĩĩma, na asya: 'Myako ĩĩya mĩombokangu mwene ngalĩko ya kw'oko kwa aka nĩyo yaĩ taoni ya Soko.' Ĩtina wa kũtwony'a vala taoni ya Soko yaĩ, nĩwavĩndũkie na asya, 'Nayo myako ĩĩya mĩombokangu mwene ngalĩko ya kw'oko kwa aũme nĩyo yaĩ taoni ya Aseka. Avilisiti moombanĩte katĩ katĩ wa taoni isu syelĩ, mũingo ũũya ũngĩ matũsyaĩtye. Kwoou nĩvatonyeka tũkethĩwa tũũngamĩte vala Aisilaeli moombanĩte.' Nĩnasũanĩie Saulo na Ndaviti maũngamĩte vala naũngamĩte. Ĩtina wa ũu, nĩtwatheeie, na twavika mwandanĩ twakĩlanĩlya ũsĩnĩ waĩ mũng'alu ũla wausĩe mavia. Nĩnakũnie visa akilinĩ noona Ndaviti aikumana ose mavia atano matendeu, na yĩmwe katĩ wa mavia asu atano nĩyo yooaie Ngoliathu." O tondũ andũ aingĩ mendeeaw'a nĩ maũndũ ma w'o ala maeleetw'e Mbivilianĩ, now'o mũndũ ũsu waendete kũtembea kũu wendeeiw'e mũno nĩ maũndũ ma w'o ala Mbivilia yĩthĩawa ĩwetete.
Vai na kĩtumi kya kwĩthĩwa na nzika ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Andũ ala mawetetwe vau maĩ kw'o na kũndũ kũla kũwetetwe vau nĩ kwa w'o. Na ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ nĩ kana maũndũ asu nĩ amwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala me Ndetonĩ ya Ngai mbeveee, na kwoou maumanĩte na Ngai wa w'o, ũla ũtatonya "kũneena ũvũngũ."—Tito 1:2; 2 Timotheo 3:16.

translation:
Are there some who question whether the story of David and Goliath is true or just a legend? But if you read carefully every detail, aren't you amazed by the power of God which enabled him to defeat such a giant? Be amazed and be humbled by this power, considering the weakness of those days.
1 | Could a person be found today who is as tall as two and a half meters (2.9 feet)?
The Bible says that Goliath was armed with a spear and a sword. (1 Samuel 17:4) One hand span was 17.5 inches (44.5 centimeters), and one cubit was 8.75 inches (22.2 centimeters). Adding up all these measurements, it would take about eight and eleven inches (2.7 meters) to grasp his spear. Some claim that Goliath was so tall because he had a genetic condition: For example, a person with gigantism might appear to be eight feet and eleven inches (2.7 meters) tall. Is it possible that Goliath was only six feet (15 centimeters) taller than this, or even shorter? Goliath was from the tribe of Levi, but it is unlikely that he was among the tallest people of his time. An Egyptian papyrus dating back to 1200-1300 BC shows soldiers from Canaan averaging around seven feet (2.4 meters) tall. So it is not impossible that Goliath was as tall as these soldiers.
2 | Was David a strong man or a young boy?
It is important to understand that the expressions used in the Bible regarding David's strength and courage are figurative. People often referred to the descendants of David using the expression "the house of David." Jesus Christ also said that David was his ancestor. (Matthew 12:3; 22:43-45) According to the Bible, Jesus is the Messiah, and his lineage can be traced back to King David. (Matthew 1:6-16; Luke 3:23-31) Therefore, David was a strong man, but his strength did not come from his physical stature.
3 | What lessons can we learn from the story of David and Goliath that apply to us today?
The Bible states that the battle took place in the Valley of Elah. It also describes how the Philistines camped on one side of the valley, and the Israelites camped on the opposite side. Why is this detail mentioned?
Let's examine what one person wrote about this incident. He stated: "They say that the people of Elah were very skilled warriors. They boasted that they could easily defeat anyone who dared to cross the valley. But when the Philistines crossed the valley, they were defeated and forced to read 1 Samuel 17:1-3. And he continued, 'The best of my sheep are those that graze near Soco.' Then someone asked him, 'And the best of my sheep are those that graze near Aseka.' The Philistines camped between the two valleys, and their army was very large. That is why we need to be courageous like the Israelites." Saul and David encouraged each other. Because of this, we have learned, and we will remember the lesson of being brave despite facing difficult situations. I am convinced that David had practiced shooting stones five times, and one of those five stones killed Goliath." So, although many people believe the events described in the Bible are exaggerated, this person believes that the events happened as described in the Bible.
Go with the purpose of understanding the full meaning of the things revealed in the Bible. Other people may not understand them, but you can understand them yourself. And the most important thing is that the scriptures are inspired by God, and everything you learn from them will help you to "live a godly life."—Titus 1:2; 2 Timothy 3:16.

Na kwoou aisũanĩa atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa andũ ma saenzi nĩmaĩkĩĩthĩtye kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya, ninyie ũũ nĩleane namo?"
Takeka nue Alex, no wĩtĩkĩle kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya aĩ nũndũ mavuku ma sukulu maĩtye ũu?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
Mavinda maingĩ andũ ala maĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya na ala maĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kũmbwa mawetaa kĩla maĩkĩĩaa matambĩte kũsũanĩa mũno, ĩndĩ mayĩthĩawa mesĩ nesa ki nĩkĩ maĩkĩĩaa maũndũ asu.

Andũ amwe maĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya nũndũ ũu nĩw'o mamanyĩaw'a sukulu.
MAKŨLYO THANTHATŨ WAĨLE KŨSŨANĨA
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kĩla nyũmba yakĩtwe nĩ mũndũ: ĩndĩ ũla ũseũvĩtye syĩndũ syonthe nĩ Ngai." (Aevelania 3:4) We no ũĩkĩĩe ũndũ ũsu?
ŨNDŨ ANDŨ MAASYAA: Syĩndũ syonthe ila twonaa syaumĩlile ĩtina wa mũlivũko mũnene (big bang).
1. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie mũlivũko ũsu wĩthĩwa?
2. Katĩ wa maũndũ aa elĩ, nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũkwosana na kĩlĩko? Nĩ kwasya kana syĩndũ syonthe syeekie kwĩyumĩlya kana nĩ kwasya kana ve mũndũ watumie syĩthĩwa vo?
ŨNDŨ ANDŨ MAASYAA: Andũ maumie nyamũnĩ.
3. Ethĩwa andũ matw'ĩkaa maumie nyamũnĩ ta ngũlĩ, nĩkĩ ve kĩvathũkany'o kĩnene mũno vyũ katĩ wa ũndũ andũ mesilasya na ũndũ ngũlĩ syĩsilasya?
4. Nĩkĩ o na tũsamũ tũla tũnini twĩthĩawa twĩ twa ũsengy'a na twĩ vinya kũeleeka ũndũ mĩĩ yatw'o yĩilyĩ?
ŨNDŨ ANDŨ MAASYAA: Asomi nĩmaĩkĩĩthĩtye kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya.
5. Andũ ala maasyaa ũu nĩmekĩte ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu?
6. Nĩ andũ meana maĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya nũndũ meeiwe kana andũ onthe ala asomu maĩkĩĩaa ũu?
"Ũkakilya ũtembeele kĩthekanĩ kĩ mĩtĩ mingĩ ũkethĩa nyũmba mbanake, we no ũsũanĩe kana mĩtĩ ĩla yakĩte nyũmba ĩsu yeekie kũvalũka na yeevanga nesa yatw'ĩka nyũmba? Ũndũ ũsu ndũtonyeka! Kwoou vatonyeka ata mũndũ akaĩkĩĩa kana syĩndũ syonthe syeekie kwĩyumĩlya?"—Julia.
"Kwasũanĩa mũndũ aikwĩa kana kambunĩnĩ ya kũtumbĩthya mavuku vaumĩlile mũlivũko mũnene na watuma langi ũla ũandĩkaa mavuku ũtalĩkanga ngũtanĩ na kĩalanĩ, na kwoou mũlivũko ũsu waseũvya ĩvuku. We no ũĩkĩĩe ũndũ ũsu?"—Gwen.
NĨKĨ WAĨLE KŨMŨĨKĨĨA NGAI?
Mbivilia nĩkwĩkĩĩte vinya ũtũmĩe "kĩlĩko." (2 Timotheo 1:7) Ũu nĩ kwasya kana ndwaĩle kũĩkĩĩa kana kwĩ Ngai ũsukumĩtwe nĩ maũndũ aa
ŨNDŨ ŨKWĨW'A (Kwosana na ũndũ ngwĩw'a, nonaa ve vinya wĩ vandũ mwingĩ mũno ũvĩtũkĩte wa andũ)
ŨNDŨ WĨW'AA ANDŨ ANGĨ MAYASYA (Kũla nĩkalaa kwĩ andũ mendete ndĩni)
KŨTHING'ĨĨW'A NĨ ANDŨ ALA ANGĨ (Asyai makwa mambĩie nĩĩkĩĩae kana kwĩ Ngai na ndyaĩ na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩka)
Ĩndĩ waĩle kwĩthĩwa na itumi nzeo sya kũĩkĩĩa kana kwĩ Ngai.
"Ĩla neethukĩĩsya mwalimũ aimanyĩsya ũndũ mwĩĩ wa mũndũ ũthũkũmaa, ũu ũtumaa nĩthĩwa nde na nzika kana kwĩ Ngai. Kĩla kalungu ka mwĩĩ ke vata mwĩĩnĩ, o na nginya tũla tũnini. O na mwĩĩ witũ wĩthĩawa ũendeee kũtethya maũndũ maingĩ o na tũteũmanya. Kwa w'o ki mwĩĩ wa mũndũ nĩwaũsengy'a mũno!"—Teresa.
"Ĩla noona ngolova ndaasa vyũ, ngalĩ, kana meli, nĩkũlasya-ĩ, 'Nũũ ũla waseũvisye syĩndũ ii?' Kwa ngelekany'o, no nginya ngalĩ ĩkaseũvw'a nĩ andũ oĩ mũno nũndũ yĩthĩawa na twĩndũ twingĩ na tũnini twaĩle kũkwatanw'a nesa nĩ kana ngalĩ ĩthi. Na kwoou ethĩwa ve mũndũ ũseũvasya ngalĩ no nginya vethĩwe ve ũla woombie andũ." —Richard.
"O ũndũ naendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ ma saenzi now'o naendeeie kũmanya kana ũmanyĩsyo wa kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya ti wa w'o. . . . Nyie nĩw'aa yĩ laisi mũno kũĩkĩĩka kana kwĩ Mũmbi wa syĩndũ kwĩ kũĩkĩĩa kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya."—Anthony.
KWASŨANĨA ŨNDŨ ŨŨ
O na kau andũ ma saenzi nĩmekĩte ũkunĩkĩli kwa myaka mingĩ, mainamba kũvikĩa ũtwi ũmwe onthe matonya kwĩtĩkĩlana na ũkwonany'a kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya. Ethĩwa andũ ma saenzi matw'ĩkĩkanaa kana nĩmo me na ũmanyi mwingĩ na mayĩtĩkĩlanaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya, nũkwona ta ũthũku kwĩthĩwa wĩ na nzika ĩũlũ wa ũmanyĩsyo ũsu?

translation:
ARE YOU AFRAID OF DEATH?
Considering this situation: A young man named Alex was seriously ill. He prayed to God and He was the only hope for everything. His biology teacher explained to him that some things are difficult to understand and this illness is something that scientists can deal with. Alex appeared very worried. And he said: "Scientists say that some things are difficult to understand, so should I rely on them?"
Ask Alex, does he understand that some things are difficult to understand or are school books enough?
PLEASE CONSIDER!
Many people think that some things are difficult to understand and others think that some things are easy to explain, but they blame considering too much, while others blame those who don't know enough.
Some people think that some things are easy to explain because of their knowledge.
Some people think that some things are difficult to understand and this is what school teaches.
LET US ALL CONSIDER THIS MATTER
The Bible says: "Every house is built by someone: but the builder of all things is God." (Hebrews 3:4) But do you believe this?
THE QUESTION OF ORIGIN: Everything we see has been attributed to a great explosion (big bang).
1. What caused this explosion to happen?
2. Among all things, what is most similar to creation? Is it science saying that everything is difficult to understand or is it science saying that someone created everything?
THE QUESTION OF MORALITY: People have different morals.
3. Why do people behave differently in different places, and is there a big difference between what people believe and what society believes?
4. Is it possible that our large brains were given to us so that we could discover the truth about life?
THE QUESTION OF LEARNING: Learning is difficult to understand.
5. Have other people asked themselves this question about the origin of this matter?
6. Are those who think that some things are difficult to understand few or are all educated people thinking about this?
"Imagine walking through a dense forest towards a beautiful house; would you wonder if the trees around the house make it look dilapidated and old? This is impossible! It's impossible for anyone to think that everything is difficult to understand!"—Julia.
"Wondering whether a person can believe in the theory of the great explosion and still believe that God wrote the laws of physics which govern the universe, and that this explosion happened because of Him. But do you believe this?"—Gwen.
WHY IS IT IMPORTANT TO BELIEVE IN GOD?
The Bible uses the word "creation." (2 Timothy 1:7) Is it possible to believe in God despite difficulties?
THE ANSWER (Similar to the previous answer, but many people find it more convincing)
THE ANSWERS PEOPLE GIVE (To explain their beliefs to others)
WHAT OTHERS SAY (Some say they believe in God because of…)
Therefore, believe and use your mind to believe in God.
"But sometimes a teacher who explains things well makes a student feel foolish, and this leads them away from God. Every mistake someone makes is a lesson, and we learn little by little. And our understanding grows as we study and learn more. That's why a person should always be humble!"—Teresa.
"But often when I see something new, like a car, a plane, or a ship, I ask myself, 'Who made all this?' Because, honestly, I realize that what I see is made by people who work together and overcome many challenges. And sometimes a thing is made by someone who has inspired others." —Richard.
"And I continue to try to understand scientific things, and I continue to learn whether my understanding of things is correct or not… You are all free to decide whether to believe in the Creator of all things or not." —Anthony.
CONSIDER THIS
MATTER
And many scientists have spent years researching, trying to find an answer to the question of whether things can come about by chance. Sometimes scientists disagree, but they all have a lot of knowledge and research regarding whether things can come about by chance, yet still, does it seem right to turn away from God because of so much knowledge?

Soma wone kĩla kyakwatie Karina, na ũisũanĩa ta keka nue wakwatiwe nĩ ũndũ ũsu we wĩka ata.
Karina: "Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩendete sukulu nasembetye ngalĩ mũno, na mũsikalĩ ambũngamya anenga lisiti yonanĩtye vainĩ ũla naĩlĩte kũĩva. Nathatie mũno! Nĩnatavisye Mami ũndũ ũsu na ambĩa no nginya nĩtavye Tata. Ĩndĩ Ndyaaenda kwĩka ũu."
We Ũtonya Kwĩka Ata?
1. Kũvindya na ndimanya ĩthe-akwa ndakamanya ũndũ ũsu.
2. Ndavya ĩthe-akwa kĩla kĩneekĩkie.
Nĩvatonyeka ũkosa ũsũngĩo wa mbee. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nũtonya kũsũanĩa inyia-aku ndeatĩanĩa naku aivanga nũnatavisye ĩthe-aku. Ĩndĩ ve itumi nzeo syaĩlĩte kũtuma wĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo maku, wĩthwe ũkũniwe vainĩ nũndũ wa kũsembya ngalĩ kana o mavĩtyo angĩ.
Itumi itatũ syonanĩtye nĩkĩ waĩle kwĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo maku
1. Nũndũ nĩw'o ũndũ ũla waĩle. Mbivilia nĩwetete ũndũ Aklĩsto maĩle kwĩthĩwa mailyĩ. Yaĩtye: "Neenai w'o."—Aeveso 4:25.
"Nĩndataa ũndũ ndonya kũneena ũla w'o, kwĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo makwa na mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka, na kwĩtĩkĩla kĩla kyaumĩla nũndũ wa meko makwa."—Alexis.
2. Nũndũ nĩ laisi andũ kũekea ũla weetĩkĩla mavĩtyo make. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Ũla ũvw'ĩkaa mavĩtyo make ndakaathimĩka; ĩndĩ ũla ũmaumbũlaa na kũmatia akeew'ĩwa tei."—Nthimo 28:13.
No nginya wĩthwe na ũkũmbaũ nĩ kana wĩtĩkĩle mavĩtyo. Ũu nũtumaa andũ makũĩkĩĩa ,nũndũ nĩmamanyaa ndũkenganaa. Na nĩmonaa ũseo ũla weeka vandũ va ĩvĩtyo yaku.—Richard.
3. Ũu nũmũtanĩthasya Yeova. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Ũla wĩ ngũlũ ["wĩvithaa ũndũ ũilyĩ," NWT] nĩ ũthatyo kwa Yeova; ĩndĩ ũnyanya wake nĩ wake na ũla mũlũngalu."—Nthimo 3:32.
"Ve ĩvinda neekie ĩvĩtyo yĩito, na nĩnamanyie kana nĩnaĩlĩte kũyĩweta. Yeova ndaĩ esa kũmbathima ndyĩka maũndũ kĩvathũkany'o na ũndũ wendete."—Rachel.
We Karina eekie ata? Nĩwatatie kũvitha ĩthe lisiti ĩla wanengiwe nũndũ wa kũsembya ngalĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩthe nĩwesie kũmyona. Karina easya: "Ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe, Tata aisisya lekoti sya inisualenzi, nĩweethĩie lisiti ya vainĩ wa kũsembya ngalĩ ĩandĩkĩtwe ĩsyĩtwa yakwa." Naĩ thĩnanĩ mũnene. O na inyia-akwa nĩwathatie amanya ndyaĩ naatavya ĩthe-akwa ũndũ ũsu.
Kĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya: Karina aĩtye: "Kũvitha mavĩtyo kwĩkaa kwanangĩĩa maũndũ. Wĩsaa o kũmaĩvĩa ĩtina."
Ũndũ ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kumana na mavĩtyo maku
Kĩla mũndũ nũvĩtasya. (Alomi 3:23; 1 Yoana 1:8) Na o tondũ twoona, ĩla tweetĩkĩla mavĩtyo tũteũtindĩa, twonanasya twĩ na wĩnyivyo na kana twĩ aimu.
Twamina kwĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo, ũndũ ũla ũngĩ nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kumana namo. Ĩndĩ ũsengy'o nĩ kana andũ aingĩ ma mũika mayĩkaa ũu. Nĩvatonyeka mekew'a ũndũ mwĩĩtu ũmwe wa mũika wĩtawa Priscilla weew'aa, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mavinda maingĩ nĩnatũlĩkaa ngoo mũno nũndũ wa mavĩtyo makwa. Noonaa nde wa vata, na kwoou mavĩtyo makwa namonaa me mũio mũnene ndatonya kũũvikya. Nathĩnĩkaa mũno na ngeyĩw'ĩa tei mwingĩ."
We mavinda amwe nĩwĩw'aa ũu? Kũtindĩa ũisũanĩa mavĩtyo weekie nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kũtindĩa kũsisya kĩoo kya ngalĩ kĩla kyonanasya ĩtina. Kwĩka ũu no kũtume wĩw'a ũte wa vata na ũyĩthĩa ndwĩ na vinya wa kũthĩnĩkĩa maũndũ angĩ ala matonya kũũkwata.
Vandũ va ũu, twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩlĩte.
"Sũanĩa mavĩtyo maku na ũyĩmanyĩsya kumana namo nĩ kana ndũkamasyokeleele. Ĩndĩ ndũkatindĩae kũmasũanĩa maikakũũmĩsye."—Elliot.
"Nĩndataa ũndũ ndonya kwĩmanyĩsya kumana na mavĩtyo makwa. Kĩla ĩvĩtyo yĩnengae ĩsomo yĩtonya kũtuma nĩthwa nĩ mũndũ mũseango na yĩkandetheesya kũmanya ũndũ ndonya kũthĩnĩkĩa ũndũ ta ũsu waumĩla ĩvinda yĩngĩ. Ĩsu nĩ nzĩa nzeo ya kũatĩĩa nũndũ nĩtumaa tũima."—Vera.
