Three things that help us to send good words
1. This thing is what happened yesterday. Remember it is better to be reconciled with Christ than to be angry. Say: "Let there be no anger."—Ephesians 4:25.
"I realized something I needed to say, to send good words and forgive those who hurt me, and to forgive everyone who wronged me."—Alexis.
2. This thing helps people to confess their mistakes. The Bible says: "He who confesses his sins and abandons them will find mercy; but he who conceals his transgressions will not prosper."—Proverbs 28:13.
So I want you to also remember to send good words. This causes people to rejoice, and I realize how important it is. And I see that this thing helps people.—Richard.
3. This pleases Jehovah. The Bible says: "The righteous man is pleasing in the sight of Jehovah; and His favor is upon him and His posterity."—Proverbs 3:32.
"Every day I face challenges, and I wonder if I can overcome them. Jehovah helps me to think about things calmly and to do what is right."—Rachel.
But what about us? Should we continue to hold onto lists of wrongs done to us? It would be good to let go of them. What Rachel did was: "Once a year, my father reviewed insurance documents, and then he wrote a list of grievances on a piece of paper and tore it up." That felt good. And others have found that letting go of such things has helped them.
Everyone should remember: Rachel said: "Letting go of grievances brings peace of mind. So don't hesitate to forget the past."
Something to remember regarding our grievances
Everyone makes mistakes. (Ecclesiastes 3:23; 1 John 1:8) And even if we see others making mistakes, we should be patient with them and forgive them.
We need to learn to forgive, because that is what will help us to be happy. Sometimes many people find it difficult. A sister named Priscilla once said: "I used to dwell on so many wrongs done to me. But I realized that holding onto those hurts caused me more pain than they deserved. Now I try to move forward and not think about them anymore."
Are some of you feeling this way? Letting go of grievances means choosing to focus on the positive and letting go of bitterness that can ruin your happiness. Doing so can also help you avoid becoming resentful and negative, which can make it harder to enjoy life.
Friends, let us strive to forgive each other.
"Focus on the good and choose to forgive, even if it seems impossible. Once I made the decision to stop dwelling on the past."—Elliot.
"I learned that choosing forgiveness brings peace. Every hurt teaches a lesson that can help us become better people and understand how to overcome challenges and live a fuller life. It's a sign of strength to choose to forget things that cause us pain."—Vera.

text:
Kũthoka kwa andũ oĩ
Lk 2.1–7. Na Yesũ asaĩwe Mbethelemu nthĩ ya Yutia matukũ ma mũsumbĩ Elote, sisya, andũ oĩ kuma wumĩlonĩ wa syũa mooka Yelusaleme, makyasya, 2#Mot 24.17.Aĩva ũla wasyaiwe Mũsumbĩ wa Ayuti? Nũndũ nĩtwoonie ndata yake wumĩlonĩ wa syũa, na nĩtwooka kũmũthaitha. 3Na ũla mũsumbĩ Elote eew'a ũu, aũũya, na Yelusaleme yonthe vamwe nake. 4Na oomban'ya athembi anene onthe na aandĩki ma andũ, amakũlya vala Klĩsto wĩsyaĩwa. 5#Mika 5.2; Yoa 7.42.Nao mamwĩa, Nthĩnĩ wa Mbethelemu nthĩ ya Yutia: nũndũ nĩw'o kũandĩkĩtwe nĩ mwathani,
6Naku Mbethelemu, nthĩ ya Yuta,
Ndwĩ mũnini nongi katĩ wa atongoi ma Yuta:
Nũndũ kwaku we kũkauma ngavana,
Ũla ũkaĩthya andũ makwa Isilaeli.
7Nĩvo ĩndĩ Elote wametie ala andũ oĩ kĩmbithĩ, na amanyĩthw'a nĩo vyũ ĩvinda yĩla ndata ĩsu yonekie. 8Na amatũma ku Mbethelemu, na asya, Endai mũkekuũe vyũ ũndũ wa kala kana; na mwakona mũndetee ũvoo, nĩ kana nyie nakwa nĩthi nĩkathaithe. 9Nao, meew'a ndeto sya mũsumbĩ, makwata nzĩa mathi; na sisya, ndata ĩla moonie wumĩlonĩ wa syũa yamatongoesya, mũvaka yooka yalũma ĩũlũ wa vala ve kala kana. 10Na moona ĩla ndata, matana ũtanu mũnene mũno. 11#Sav 72.10,15; Isa 60.6.Na malika nyũmba nthĩnĩ na moona kana vamwe na Meli inyia wako, na mavalũka nthĩ na makathaitha; na mathasya mĩio yoo yĩ vata mũno makanenga mĩthĩnzĩo, thaavu na ũvumba na manemane. 12Nao mooniw'e nĩ Ngai ndotonĩ maikamũalũkĩle Elote, mathi kwoo na nzĩa ĩngĩ.
Kũkĩĩa Misili
Kuma 2.15. Na asu mathi, sisya, mũlaĩka wa Mwĩaĩi amumĩlĩla Yosevu ndotonĩ, akyasya, Ũkĩla wose kala kana na inyia wako, noikĩa ũthi Misili, ũkekale kw'o mũvaka yĩla ngaũtavya: nũndũ Elote nũkilĩlye kũmantha kala kana akoae. 14Nake ookĩla oosa kala kana na inyia wako ũtukũ, athi kũvika Misili; 15#Osea 11.1.na ekala kw'o mũvaka Elote akw'a: nĩ kana kwĩanĩw'e ũla waneeniwe nĩ Mwĩaĩi na kanyw'a wa mwathani, akyasya, Kuma Misili nĩnamwĩtie mwana wakwa.
Kũawa kwa syana ngenge sya Mbethelemu nĩ Elote
16Na ĩndĩ Elote, oona kana nũnavũthiw'e nĩ ala andũ oĩ, athata mũno, na atũma andũ moae tũvĩsĩ tw'onthe tũla twaĩ Mbethelemu, na ndee syonthe syayo, tũla tũvikĩtye myaka ĩlĩ na ĩtina wa vau, kwĩanana na ĩvinda yĩla wamanyĩthiw'e vyũ nĩ ala andũ oĩ. 17#Yel 31.15.Nĩvo ĩndĩ weanĩiw'e ũla waneeniwe nĩ mwathani Yelemia, akyasya,
18Wasya nĩweew'ĩkie Lama,
Kĩĩo na kĩmeto kĩnene,
Lakeli akĩĩĩa syana syake;
Mwa 35.19. Na ndetĩkĩla kũkiakiw'a, nĩkwĩthĩwa itivaĩ.
Kũsyoka kuma Misili
19Ĩndĩ Elote akw'a, sisya, mũlaĩka wa Mwĩaĩi amumĩlĩla Yosevu ndotonĩ na ku Misili, akyasya, 20#Kuma 4.19.Ũkĩla wose kana na inyia wako, ũthi nthĩ ya Isilaeli: nũndũ nĩ akw'ũ ala mamanthaa thayũ wa kana. 21Nake ookĩla, oosa kana na inyia wako, na athi nthĩ ya Isilaeli. 22Ĩndĩ eew'a kana Alikelau nũsumbĩkĩte ĩũlũ wa Yutia vandũ va Elote ĩthe wake, akĩa kũthi kw'o; na oonw'a nĩ Ngai ndotonĩ, eelelũka athi ngalĩ sya Kalilii, 23#Lk 1.26; 2.39; Isa 11.1; 53.2; Yoa 1.46.na athi atũa ndũanĩ yĩtawa Nasaleti; nĩ kana kwĩanĩw'e ũla waneeniwe nĩ athani, kana we aketwa Mũnasaleti.

translation:
2
From the time of the ancestors
1 #
Luke 2:1-7. And Jesus was born in Bethlehem in the days of King Herod, while people were registering in the census in Jerusalem, they traveled, 2#Matt 24:17. Where was the Messiah born? So we need to know his lineage in order to find him, and we will go to worship him. 3And when King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all of Jerusalem with him. 4And the scribes and priests of the people gathered together, asking where Christ would be born. 5#Micah 5:2; John 7:42. They said, "Bethlehem in Judea: because you are a small town among the clans of Judah, from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel."
6And Bethlehem, in Judea,
Is a small village among the clans of Judah:
So you, O Bethlehem, are not least among the clans of Judah,
For out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.
7This is how the birth of Jesus happened: His mother Mary was pledged to be married to Joseph, and she conceived through the Holy Spirit before they came together. 8And the angels told the shepherds in Bethlehem, "Go and look for the baby, as you have been told; and you will find him wrapped in cloths and lying in a manger." 9And suddenly there was a great company of heavenly hosts praising God and saying, "Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to those whom he favors!"
10And when the angels had departed, the shepherds said to each other, "Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has shown us." 11#Ps 72:10,15; Isa 60:6. And they went quickly and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger. 12And when they saw him, they repeated what the angels had told them about this child.
To the Magi
13 #
Matt 2:15. And having been warned in a dream, they went back to their country. The angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, "Get up! Take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, because Herod is going to search for the child to kill him." 14So he got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and left for Egypt; 15#Hos 11:1. and stayed there until the death of Herod, fulfilling what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: "Out of Egypt I called my son."
The Massacre of the Children in Bethlehem by Herod
16When Herod realized that he had been tricked by the wise men, he was furious, and he gave orders to kill all the boys in Bethlehem who were two years old or under, according to the time he had learned from the wise men. 17#Jer 31:15. This fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah:
18"A voice is heard in Ramah,
Weeping and great sorrow,
Rachel weeping for her children;
#
Matt 35:19. And she refuses to be comforted, because they are gone."
The Return from Egypt
19After the death of Herod, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, 20#Matt 4:19. and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, because those who sought the child's life are dead." 21So he got up, took the child and his mother, and went to the land of Israel. 22But when he heard that Archelaus was ruling over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there, and after being warned in a dream, he went to the district of Galilee, 23#Lk 1:26; 2:39; Isa 11:1; 53:2; John 1:46. and lived in a town called Nazareth, fulfilling what was spoken through the prophets: "He will be called a Nazarene."

text:
Wĩweteela.—Ava. 2:3.
Kuma tene athaithi ma Yeova nĩmekalaa meteele mone mawathani make maianĩa. Isaia nĩwathanie Yeova akatũnga athaithi make nthĩ yoo ĩtina wa Yuta kwanangwa. Aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩ aathime onthe ala mamweteelaa." (Isa. 30:18) O ta ũu Mika nĩwathanie maũndũ makonetye athaithi ma tene ma Ngai, na we mwene aisye kana ngalĩ ĩ yake 'akeeteelaa Mwĩai Ngai na wĩkwatyo.' (Mika 7:7, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Na ĩndĩ kwa myaka mingĩ o namo athũkũmi ma Ngai ma tene nĩmekalaa meteele mone ala mawathani makonetye Masia, kana Klĩsto, maianĩa. (Luka 3:15; 1 Vet. 1:10-12) Nũndũ ve maũndũ amwe mathaniwe ĩũlũ wa Masia maendeee kwĩanĩa o na ũmũnthĩ, athũkũmi ma Ngai no maendeee kweteela mone maianĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova akilyĩ anatũmĩa Ũsumbĩ wa Masia nĩ kana avetangĩe andũ mathĩna. Akaũtũmĩa kwananga ala athũku na kũvetea andũ make nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani. (1 Yoa. 5:19) Kwoou ekai twĩkale twĩ metho na twĩsĩ kana o mĩtũkĩ nthĩ ĩno nĩkũvetwa. w15 8/15 2:1, 2
Kĩwĩu kya nyũmba yaku kĩkandya.—Yoa. 2:17.
Aisilaeli nĩmaseũvisye ĩeema maatĩĩe mũtalatala ũla Yeova wamanete. (Kuma 25:8) O na nĩmesie kwaka ĩkalũ ya kũmũthaithĩa Yeova. (1 Asu. 8:27, 29) O na ĩngĩ, ĩla Ayuti mesie kuma ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni, mambĩĩe kũthaithĩaa masinakokenĩ. (Mko. 6:2; Yoa. 18:20; Meko 15:21) Nayo ĩvinda ya atũmwa, Aklĩsto nĩmoombanĩaa mĩsyĩ kwa ana-a-asa ala angĩ. (Meko 12:12; 1 Ako. 16:19) Na ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ, andũ ma Yeova nĩmombanĩaa Nyũmbanĩ sya Ũsumbĩ nĩ kana mamanyĩw'e na maimũthaitha Yeova. Na kũvikĩĩa yu kwĩ Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ ngili mĩongo yĩana ũna nthĩ yonthe. Yesũ nĩwendete mũno ĩkalũ ya Yeova yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme na nĩwayĩnengete ndaĩa. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ũmwe wa ala maandĩkie mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo woonanisye kana wathani ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya ũmũnthĩ nĩwamũkonetye. (Sav. 69:9) Ũmũnthĩ vai Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ o na yĩva yaĩlĩtwe vyũ nĩ kwĩtwa "nyũmba ya Yeova" ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ ĩkalũ yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme yeetawa. (2 Mav. 5:13; 33:4) O na vailyĩ ũu, Mbivilia yĩ na myolooto ĩtwonasya ũndũ kũla tũthaithĩaa ũmũnthĩ kwaĩlĩte kũtũmĩwa na kũnengwa ndaĩa. w15 7/15 4:1, 2
Ĩvw'ĩkei wendo.—Ako. 3:14.
Tũkekalany'a na andũ ala angĩ nesa ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Klĩsto? Tweemanyĩsya kũekea ala angĩ na kwĩkalany'a namo nesa, tũikaemwa nĩ kwĩka oou ĩvindanĩ yĩla yũkĩte. (Ako. 3:12, 13) Ĩla twĩlika nthĩ nzaũ, ti lasima tũkakwataa kĩndũ kĩla tũkwenda ĩvinda yĩla tũũkyenda. Kwoou o na kau Yeova akatũathimaa nũndũ wa kwĩnyivĩsya ũsumbĩki wake, no nginya ĩvinda yĩu twĩĩmanyĩsya kũtũngaa mũvea na kwĩanĩwa nĩ kĩla twĩ nakyo. Kwĩthĩwa na nguma ila Yeova ũtũmanyĩasya ũmũnthĩ nĩkũkatũtetheesya ĩvinda yĩu. Kwondũ wa ũu, tweemanyĩsya kwĩkalaa ta andũ meteele kwĩsa kũtũa nthĩ nzaũ, nĩtwĩthĩawa na nguma ila ikatũtetheesya kwĩkala tene na tene. O na ĩngĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ now'o tũlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ nthĩnĩ wa maũndũ ala matũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana kwĩ 'nthĩ yũkĩte.' (Aevl. 2:5; 11:1) Na ĩndĩ nĩtwĩkaa maũndũ mekwonany'a kana twĩ na mea mũno ma kwĩsa kwona nthĩ yusĩe ũlũngalu. Kwoou nĩ w'o vyũ, tũendeee kwĩyũmbanĩsya ĩvinda yĩla tũkekala tene na tene nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla Ngai ũtwathĩte. w15 8/15 3:11, 12

translation:
They were waiting.—Isa. 2:3.
But today the faithful ones are encouraged by what Jehovah has done for his people in recent times. Isaiah foretold that Jehovah would strengthen his people so that they could look forward to the restoration of Judah. He said: "He will be a stronghold for those who are waiting." (Isa. 30:18) So Micah prophesied about good things that Jehovah would do for his faithful ones, and he himself said or asked whether anyone was waiting 'to put his trust in Jehovah and benefit.' (Micah 7:7, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) And for many years now, the loyal friends of God have been encouraged by what his people in modern times are doing to find the Messiah, or Christ. (Luke 3:15; 1 Pet. 1:10-12) However, some of the things accomplished during the time of the Messiah continue to unfold even now, and God's friends continue to wait expectantly. For example, Jehovah allows us to share the Messianic Prophecy with others. This helps them to escape from darkness and to turn their hearts away from Satan's influence. (1 John 5:19) Let us therefore remain steadfast and courageous, knowing that our waiting will be rewarded. w15 8/15 2:1, 2
The zeal for his house moved him.—John 2:17.
Israelites showed deep devotion repeatedly to Jehovah. (2 Kings 25:8) And I have come to love speaking about Jehovah. (1 Cor. 8:27, 29) Also, when exiled to Babylon, they were eager to worship secretly. (Ps. 6:2; John 18:20; Acts 15:21) Moreover, through an angel, Christ comforted his brothers and sisters. (Acts 12:12; 1 Cor. 16:19) And today, Jehovah's people comfort themselves with the thought that those who honor Jehovah are remembered. And appreciating this truth can strengthen us as we preach. Jesus intensely loved Jehovah's name and he openly declared it. That is why one of the accusations brought against him by the Jewish religious leaders was that he opposed their tradition. (Ps. 69:9) The temple represented God's house, and because of its association with Jehovah's name, it came to be called "the house of Jehovah," just as Jerusalem was. (2 Kings 5:13; 33:4) So rightly, the Bible and our publications show us how important it is to honor God's name in connection with our ministry and our witnessing work. w15 7/15 4:1, 2
Show kindness.—Acts 3:14.
Let us examine how we can show genuine love for our brothers and sisters and at the same time maintain our zeal for the ministry. We want to be able to say that we are actively engaged in the work, yet we do not want to become overly zealous. (Acts 3:12, 13) However, if we are not careful, we may find ourselves getting carried away and doing more than we can handle. Our loving Father Jehovah encourages us to be realistic, and he helps us to see what we can accomplish. By being guided by his spirit, we can continue to make progress and enjoy our ministry. The confidence we have in Jehovah will help us to be reasonable. Because of this, we can remain humble and avoid becoming self-righteous. Also, we should not dwell on past mistakes or focus on what others have done wrong. (Eph. 2:5; 11:1) Instead, let us concentrate on the things we can do to improve and strive to make spiritual progress. Let us continue to apply ourselves diligently to the ministry, always remembering the privilege Jehovah has given us. w15 8/15 3:11, 12

text:
Alaĩka ala aĩkĩĩku nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ maũndũ makonanĩtye na andũ na nĩmethĩawa na kĩthito kingĩ kya kwĩka kwenda kwa Yeova. Ĩla Ngai woombie nthĩ, alaĩka onthe 'nĩmainie vamwe, na ana onthe ma Ngai mookĩlya mawasya ũndũ wa kũtana.' (Yovu 38:4, 7) Kuma ĩvinda ya tene vyũ, alaĩka nĩmendaa "ũkunĩkĩla" wathani ũla ũeleetye maũndũ ala makekĩka ĩvinda yũkĩte ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.—1 Vetelo 1:11, 12.
Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana ve mavinda alaĩka masũvĩie athaithi ma w'o ma Ngai nĩ kana meanĩsye kwenda kwake. (Savuli 34:7) Kwa ngelekany'o:
Ĩla Yeova waanangie ndũa nthũku sya Sotomo na Ngomola, alaĩka nĩmatetheeisye mũndũũme waĩ mũlũngalu weetawa Loto vamwe na mũsyĩ wake maume ndũanĩ isu.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 19:1, 15-26.
Ĩla Aevelania atatũ ma mũika ala maĩ Mbaviloni masilĩlwe kwĩkw'a ikonĩ ya mwaki mũnene makw'ĩĩe vo, Ngai nĩwatũmie "mũlaĩka wake, na atangĩĩa athũkũmi make."—Ndanieli 3:19-28.
Ĩla mũndũũme waĩ mũlũngalu Ndanieli wekiw'e ngunganĩ ya mĩnyambũ na ekala vo ũtukũ mũima, aisye kana 'Ngai nũtũmie mũlaĩka wake, na atumya makanyw'a ma mĩnyambũ.'—Ndanieli 6:16, 22.
ALAĨKA NĨMATETHEEASYA AKLĨSTO MA ĨVINDA YA ATŨMWA
Mavindanĩ amwe, alaĩka ma Ngai nĩmatetheeasya kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kya ĩvinda ya atũmwa ĩla ve vata nĩ kana kĩeleelo kya Yeova kĩanĩe. Kwa ngelekany'o:
Ve mũlaĩka wavingũie mĩomo ya kolokolo na atongoesya atũmwa ala maĩ ove mathi makaendeesye wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩkalũnĩ.—Meko ma Atũmwa 5:17-21.
Ve mũlaĩka weeyĩaĩie mũtavany'a weetawa Vilivu esĩle nzĩanĩ ya weũ ĩla yaumĩte Yelusaleme kũvika Ngasa akatavye ũvoo mũseo Mũethiovia waendete Yelusaleme kũthaitha.—Meko ma Atũmwa 8:26-33.
Ĩla ĩvinda ya Ngai yavikie nĩ kana andũ ala mataĩ Ayuti matw'ĩke Aklĩsto, mũlaĩka nĩwaumĩlĩĩile mũnene wa ita sya Alomi weetawa Kolinelio woninĩ na amwĩa atũmane mũtũmwa Vetelo oke kwake.—Meko ma Atũmwa 10:3-5.
Ĩla mũtũmwa Vetelo waĩ mwove, mũlaĩka nĩwamumĩlĩĩile na amumya kolokolonĩ.—Meko ma Atũmwa 12:1-11.
ŨNDŨ ALAĨKA MATONYA ŨKŨTETHYA
Ĩvindanĩ ya ũmũnthĩ, vai kĩndũ kĩtũĩkĩĩthasya kana Ngai nũtũmĩaa alaĩka matetheesye andũ kwa nzĩa ya kyama tondũ Mbivilia yonanĩtye meekaa tene. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Yesũ aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yitũ: "Ũvoo ũũ mũseo wa ũsumbĩ ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe; na ĩndĩ mũminũkĩlyo ũkyũka." (Mathayo 24:14) We nĩwĩsĩ kana amanyĩw'a ma Klĩsto nĩmaendeee na kũtethya wĩa ũsu matongoew'e nĩ alaĩka?
Ĩvuku ya Ũvuany'o yonanĩtye kana alaĩka nĩmekĩaa kĩthito kũtetheesya andũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe memanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai na kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa andũ. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Na noona mũlaĩka ũngĩ akĩũlũka ĩtunĩ katĩ, e na ũvoo mũseo wa tene na tene wa ũtavan'ya kwa ala matwĩe nthĩ, na kwa kĩla mũthemba na mbaĩ na kĩthyomo na ũko wa andũ; na aneena na wasya mũnene, Kĩai Ngai, na mũtaĩei; nũndũ saa wa kũsilĩla kwake nĩ mũku: na mũthaithei ũla wombie ĩtu na nthĩ na ũkanga na nthongo sya manzĩ." (Ũvuan'yo 14:6, 7) Maũndũ maingĩ ala mekĩkĩte ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ nĩmaĩkĩĩthasya kana alaĩka nĩmatetheeasya wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. O na ĩla mwĩki ũmwe wa naĩ weelila na amũsyokea Yeova, nĩvethĩawa "ũtanu kwa alaĩka ma Ngai."—Luka 15:10.
Kũkeethĩwa ata wĩa wa kũtavany'a wathela? Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana "ita ila syĩ ĩtunĩ" sya alaĩka ikatetheesya Yesũ Klĩsto, Mũsumbĩ wa asumbĩ, kũkita "kaũnĩ wa mũthenya mũnene wa Ngai, Mwene Vinya W'onthe" ũla wĩtawa Ali–Maketoni. (Ũvuan'yo 16:14-16; 19:14-16) Alaĩka me vinya makatũmĩwa kũsilĩla andũ ĩla Mwĩaĩi Yesũ 'ũkaĩvanĩsya kwa ala matawĩw'aa ũvoo mũseo wa Mwĩaĩi waitũ Yesũ.'—2 Athesalonika 1:7, 8.
Kwoou ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana alaĩka nĩmendeeaw'a nue mũno. O na nĩmendete mũno kwona andũ ala mendete kũmũthũkũma Ngai maendeee nesa, na ve mavinda maingĩ Yeova ũmatũmĩĩte kwĩkĩa vinya na kũsũvĩa athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku.—Aevelania 1:14.
Kwoou kĩla ũmwe witũ e na ũtwi wa vata vyũ waĩle kwĩka. Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Tũkeethukĩĩsya na kwĩw'a ũvoo mũseo ũla ũendeee kũtavanw'a nthĩ yonthe? Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kĩsionĩ kyenyu no syende ũkũtetheesya ũunĩke nĩ ũtethyo wa alaĩka me vinya ma Ngai.

translation:
When the morning stars joyously sang, it was because of my perfect works and because I was delighted with the prospect of walking with Jehovah. But God kindly reminded me, when the morning stars joyously sang, "You will praise others, and the sons of God will shout for joy over what you have done." (Job 38:4, 7) So in ancient times, they praised "the skillful worker" who produced things that made the creation beautiful and glorious.—1 Peter 1:11, 12.
I am convinced that those angels eagerly watch over God's servants and are interested in their spiritual progress. (Psalm 34:7) For example:
But Jehovah rescued Lot and his family from Sodom and Gomorrah, while destroying the wicked people of those cities along with them.—Genesis 19:1, 15-26.
But Nebuchadnezzar had an image of gold erected, exceedingly high, and he commanded that everyone fall down and worship it; God sent "his angel and delivered his servants."—Daniel 3:19-28.
But Daniel, being thrown into the lions' pit, remained calm, and he trusted that 'God would send his angel and shut the mouths of the lions.'—Daniel 6:16, 22.
ANGELS SUPPORT CHRIST IN THEIR MINISTRY
Some angels, whom God has empowered, form part of Christ's angelic organization and help to carry out Jehovah's purpose. For example:
They released the apostles from prison and directed them to continue preaching the good news without fear.—Acts 5:17-21.
An angel guided Philip to meet an Ethiopian eunuch traveling to Jerusalem to worship, and he helped him understand the scriptures.—Acts 8:26-33.
And when the household of Cornelius, a Roman army officer, showed interest in learning about Christ, an angel informed Peter of this and sent him to visit Cornelius and preach the good news to him.—Acts 10:3-5.
And when the apostle Peter was imprisoned, an angel freed him and led him away safely.—Acts 12:1-11.
WHAT ANGELS DO TO HELP US
In our time, it may be comforting to know that God uses angels to strengthen those who serve him faithfully, though the Bible does not reveal how often this happens. Jesus said about the spirit realm: "This good news of the kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all nations; and then the end will come." (Matthew 24:14) So should we expect Christians to continue to receive strength through angels?
The book of Revelation shows that angels will help to proclaim God's message and his purpose to people throughout the earth. The apostle John wrote: "And I saw another angel flying in midheaven with everlasting good news to declare to those who dwell on the earth—to every nation and tribe and tongue and people." (Revelation 14:6, 7) Many other scriptures show that angels can help to preach the good news of the Kingdom throughout the earth. And when one of us feels weak and needs encouragement, we can pray to Jehovah.—Luke 15:10.
But what about helping others to find comfort? The Bible indicates that "other sheep" would assist Jesus Christ, the great Shepherd, in guiding "the great multitude" whom they call the anointed ones. (John 16:14-16; 19:14-16) These sheep are appointed to help people learn about Jesus so that they may 'become conformed to the image of our Lord Jesus.'—2 Thessalonians 1:7, 8.
How are they empowered to do this work? They are strengthened by holy spirit. And they are strengthened further when they see others making progress in sanctifying Jehovah's name and showing increased faith.—Ephesians 1:14.
How can each of us benefit from this provision? In effect, let us be grateful for and appreciate this feature that helps to strengthen all faithful ones. Let us ask Jehovah to continue using his angels to support those who are proclaiming him and to give them strength.—Hebrews 1:14.

text:
Ũla wandũmie e vamwe nakwa; ndaandia nĩ nyioka.—Yoa. 8:29.
O na yĩla Yesũ wathĩnaw'a, aĩ na mũuo wa kĩlĩko nũndũ nĩweesĩ kana nũkũmũtanĩthya Asa wake. Amwĩw'aa mavinda onthe, o na yĩla maũndũ metu. Nĩwendete Ĩthe wake mũno, na kĩla kyaĩ kya vata vyũ kwake nĩ kũmũthũkũma Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na ataaũka kũũ nthĩ, aĩ "mũthũkũmi mũnene" wa Ngai. (Nth. 8:30) Na yĩla wesie kũka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, aĩ na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũtavya angĩ ĩũlũ wa Ĩthe wake. (Mt. 6:9; Yoa. 5:17) Wĩa ũsu watumie Yesũ ethĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno. (Yoa. 4:34-36) No tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ya Yesũ kwa kũmwĩw'a Yeova, na 'mavinda onthe kwĩthĩwa na maũndũ maingĩ ma kwĩka wĩanĩ wa Mwĩaĩi.' (1 Ako. 15:58) Twaendeea kũtavany'a na "kĩthito mũno," tũkeethĩawa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa mathĩna maitũ. (Meko 18:5) Kwa ngelekany'o, kaingĩ wĩthĩaa ala tweethĩana namo tũitavany'a me thĩnanĩ mũito o na kwĩ ũla ũtũkwatĩte. Ĩndĩ mambĩĩa kũmwenda Yeova na kũatĩĩa ũtao wake, maũndũ moo nĩmavĩndũkaa na mayambĩĩa kwĩkala me atanu mũnango. Tweeyonea ũndũ ta ũsu ũyĩkĩka, nĩtwĩthĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmangu kana Yeova nũkũendeea kũtũsũvĩa. w19.04 10-11 ¶8-9
Aingĩ ala meekaa syama sya ũwe nĩmaetie mavuku moo vamwe na mamavĩvĩsya mbee wa kĩla mũndũ.—Meko 19:19.
Andũ asu mayavũaa ngũĩ; nĩmatw'ĩte vyũ kumanwa na maveva mavuku. Mavuku asu moo maĩ ma thooa mũnene mũno. Ĩndĩ mayaaona maĩle kũnenga mũndũ ũngĩ mavuku asu kana kũmathoosya, meekie kũmananga. Kĩla mathĩnĩkĩaa mũno nĩ kũmwendeesya Yeova, ti thooa wa mavuku asu. Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya Aklĩsto asu ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa? Nũseo tũkananga kana tũkekya vyũ kĩla twĩthĩwa nakyo kĩkonanĩtye na ndaimoni. Syĩndũ isu nĩ ta mbingo, mĩthea, kana syĩndũ ingĩ awe manengae andũ mekĩe kana mekale nasyo nĩ kana mesiĩĩanĩe na maveva mavuku. (1 Ako. 10:21) Sisya nesa syĩndũ ila wĩtanĩthasya nasyo. Kwekũlye: 'Nĩnĩthĩwa nĩtanĩthasya na kĩndũ kĩkonetye kũneenany'a na maveva?' Tw'a kwĩka ũtwi ũtonya kũũtetheesya wĩvathane vyũ na syĩndũ ila Yeova ũmenete. Twĩenda kwĩka kyonthe kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana twĩthĩawe na "wasya mũtheu wa ngoo" mbee wa Ngai witũ.—Meko 24:16. w19.04 22-23 ¶10-12
Namete atumĩa.—Yak. 5:14.
Ve maũndũ atumĩa maĩle kwamba kũsũanĩa nesa makwata livoti ya mũndũ wĩkie naĩ ngito. Kĩla mathĩnĩkĩaa mũno nĩ kũĩkĩĩthya kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyekala yĩ ĩtheu. (Ali. 22:31, 32; Mt. 6:9) O na ĩngĩ, nĩmathĩnĩkĩaa mũno ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala me kĩkundinĩ. Mendaa methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai, na nĩmendaa kũtetheesya ala methĩwa maũmĩw'a nĩ naĩ yeekwa. O vamwe na ũu, ethĩwa ũla wĩkĩte naĩ e kĩkundinĩ, nĩmendaa kũmanya kana nũkwĩlila na maitata kũmũtetheesya atũngĩĩe ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova. (Yak. 5:14, 15) Mũklĩsto wĩthĩĩtwe na mĩmeo mĩthũku na ĩkatuma alika naĩnĩ ethĩawa e mũwau kĩ-veva. Na kĩu kĩonany'a kana aivika vau ndethĩawa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. No tũelekany'e atumĩa na matakĩtalĩ. Nĩmatataa ũndũ matonya 'mamũvosye ũsu mũwau [kana ũsu wĩkĩte naĩ].' No mamũnenge ũtao wa Maandĩko ũtonya kũmũtetheesya akatũngĩĩa ngwatanĩo yake na Ngai, ĩndĩ ndesa kũtetheka ethĩwa ndekwĩlila kuma ngoonĩ.—Meko 3:19; 2 Ako. 2:5-10. w19.05 10 ¶10-11

And they followed him; and he cast nets into the sea.—John 8:29.
But as Jesus continued walking, he also had a desire to please his Father and to glorify him. He healed all sorts of sicknesses, and he taught about God's Kingdom. He always honored his Father, and everything he did was to magnify Jehovah. So, when he spoke to them, he said, "I honor the glorious Father." (John 8:30) And because he loved to speak about God's Word, he also had a strong zeal for making known the good news of God's Kingdom. (Matt. 6:9; John 5:17) How much more should we imitate Jesus in our ministry! (John 4:34-36) Let us show our appreciation for Jesus by honoring Jehovah and being "steadfast in the work of the Lord," knowing that our efforts will not be in vain. (1 Cor. 15:58) We can continue with "zeal," remaining occupied with the important work until the end. (Acts 18:5) Often, though, we find ourselves getting distracted by less important things or by problems that seem urgent. It is vital to remember to put Jehovah first and to conform our lives to His will, so that our activities will be meaningful and bring joy to our heart. We need to examine ourselves to see whether we are letting worldly concerns overshadow our spiritual pursuits, and ask ourselves, 'Does Jehovah still want to use me?' w19.04 10-11 ¶8-9
Many people also experience emotional distress because of past traumas or painful experiences.—Acts 19:19.
Some individuals struggle with guilt; they feel unworthy and burdened by their mistakes. Past traumas can cause deep wounds. If someone has been hurt by another person's actions or words, it is understandable that he would feel angry or resentful. The most important thing is to draw close to Jehovah, not to dwell on past traumas. Should we allow ourselves to be paralyzed by fear or to question whether we are worthy of God's love? We must recognize that Satan wants to make us feel helpless and disconnected from Jehovah. Demons can influence people's thoughts and feelings, causing them to relive painful memories. (1 Cor. 10:21) But we do not have to give in to such influences. Ask yourself: 'Will dwelling on this help me to strengthen my relationship with Jehovah?' We should avoid obsessing over things that Jehovah has already forgiven. We want to remain loyal, no matter what challenges we face, and trust in "the power of God" to sustain us.—Acts 24:16. w19.04 22-23 ¶10-12
Pray for guidance.—Jas. 5:14.
When faced with difficult circumstances, earnest prayer can bring comfort and strength. The most important thing is to trust that God cares about our concerns. (Ps. 22:31, 32; Matt. 6:9) Also, remember that others care about you. Share your worries with trusted friends and seek spiritual counsel. By doing so, you will find encouragement and reassurance. Furthermore, if you know someone who is struggling, offer to pray for him and help him to strengthen his relationship with Jehovah. (Jas. 5:14, 15) A Christian elder may visit a sick brother or sister to offer comfort and support. He can discern whether the individual needs practical assistance or simply encouragement to maintain his faith in Jehovah. So let us value the ministry and the opportunities it provides to share hope with others. It is often possible to say something that will uplift those who are discouraged. However, we need to know how to 'speak a comforting speech' to each one. And the Bible gives us wise counsel on how to encourage others and help them to strengthen their relationship with God, while avoiding empty platitudes.—Eccl. 3:19; 2 Cor. 2:5-10. w19.05 10 ¶10-11

text:
"Ũndũ ũmwe wanthĩnasya mũno nĩendeee kwĩana nĩ kwendeew'a nĩ aũme takwa. Noonaa ta ũndũ ũvĩtĩte ĩndĩ no nĩw'aa ũu o na ũmũnthĩ."—David, 23.
David nĩ Mũklĩsto wendaa kũmwendeesya Ngai. Ĩndĩ no eke ũu o ayendeew'a nĩ aũme take? We Ngai ethĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa aũme kũkoma na aũme kana aka kũkoma na aka?
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mawoni ĩũlũ wa aũme kũkoma na aũme kana aka kũkoma na aka no methĩwe me kĩvathũkangany'o kwosana na syĩthĩo sya andũ kana kwosana na ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto mayĩatĩĩaa woni nĩkwĩthĩwa wĩ na andũ aingĩ kana "kũkuwa nĩ kĩla kĩseve kya ũmanyĩsyo." (Aeveso 4:14) Vandũ va ũu, nĩmaatĩĩaa woni wa Mbivilia ĩũlũ wa aũme kũkoma na aũme kana aka kũkoma na aka (na ũu now'o mekaa maũndũnĩ onthe makonetye mwĩkalĩle).
Mbivilia nĩwetete ũtheinĩ woni ũla waĩle ĩũlũ wa aũme kũkoma na aũme kana aka kũkoma na aka. Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye:
"Ndũkakome na mbaa aũme, o ta mbaa aka."—Alivai 18:22.
"Ngai amalekya mĩmeonĩ mĩthũku ĩla yĩ nthoni: nĩkwĩthĩwa o na aka moo makũanisye mũtuo wa mũsyawa na mũtuo ũngĩ ũtosana na ũsu."—Alomi 1:24, 26.
"Mũikakengeke: eki ma naĩ na eĩtu, o na athaithi ma mĩvw'anano, o na ilaalai, o na ala metusaa ta aka, o na ala meyĩkaa naĩ na aũme, o na ing'ei, o na ala me na ĩtomo, o na anywi, o na aumani, o na avutani, maikatiĩwa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai."—1 Akolintho 6:9, 10.
Ũw'o nĩ kana, ũtao ũla Ngai ũnenganĩte nĩ kwa andũ onthe, methĩwe nĩ aũme ala mendeeaw'a nĩ aũme, ala mendeeaw'a nĩ aka, aka ala mendeeaw'a nĩ aka, kana aka ala mendeeaw'a nĩ aũme. Kĩla twaĩle kũmanya nĩ kana kĩla ũmwe no nginya esiĩĩe ndakethĩwe na mĩmeo mĩthũku ĩla ĩtonya kũtuma eka maũndũ ala matamwendeeasya Ngai.—Akolosai 3:5.
Ũu nĩ kwasya . . . ?
Ũu nĩkwasya kana kwosana na Mbivilia aũme ala makomaa na aũme na aka ala makomaa na aka nĩmaĩlĩte kũmenwa?
Aiee. Mbivilia ndyonanĩtye kana ve mũndũ o na ũmwe waĩle kũmenwa ethĩwe nĩ mũndũũme wendeeaw'a nĩ aũme kana mũndũ mũka wendeeaw'a nĩ aka, kana mũndũũme wendeeaw'a nĩ aka kana mũndũ mũka wendeeaw'a nĩ aũme. Vandũ va ũu, Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte 'tũmanthe kwĩthĩwa na mũuo na andũ onthe,' o na ethĩwa me na mwĩkalĩle ũilyĩ ata. (Aevelania 12:14) Kwoou tũyaĩlĩte kũmena aũme ala makomaa na aũme na aka ala makomaa na aka, kana kũmathĩny'a, kana kũmeka ũndũ o na wĩ va ũtaĩlĩte.
Ũu nĩ kwasya kana Aklĩsto maĩlĩte kũvĩnga mĩao ĩla yĩtĩkĩlĩtye aũme kũtwaa aũme kana aka kũtwaa aka?
Kwosana na Mbivilia, mũvango wa Ngai nĩ kana mũndũũme ũmwe aĩlĩte kũtwaana na mũndũ mũka ũmwe. (Mathayo 19:4-6) Ĩndĩ andũ kũtinda maineenea mĩao ĩla yumĩtw'e ĩũlũ wa aũme kũtwaa aũme na aka kũtwaa aka nĩ maũndũ ma siasa. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Aklĩsto mayaĩle kwĩlikya siasanĩ. (Yoana 18:36) Kwoou, maikwataa mbau kana kũvĩnga mĩao ya silikalĩ ĩla ĩkonetye aũme kũtwaa aũme kana aka kũtwaa aka kana kũkoma ĩmwe.
Nao nata ethĩwa . . . ?
Nao nata ethĩwa mũndũ nĩwĩlikĩtye mwĩkalĩlenĩ ũsu? Mũndũ ũsu no aalyũke?
Ĩĩ. O na ve amwe meelikĩtye mwĩkalĩlenĩ ũsu ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa na maalyũka. Mbivilia yamina kwonany'a kana aũme ala makomaa na aũme na aka ala makomaa na aka maikalika Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ngai, ĩsyokete ĩkasya atĩĩ: "Na amwe menyu mwailyĩ ũu."—1 Akolintho 6:11.
Ũu nĩ kwasya kana aũme ala maĩ na kĩmanyĩo kya kũkoma na aũme na aka ala maĩ na kĩmanyĩo kya kũkoma na aka mayĩsa kũkwatwa nĩ mĩmeo ya kwĩlikya mwĩkalĩle ũsu ĩngĩ? Aiee. Mbivilia yaĩtye 'twĩvw'ĩke mũndũ mweũ, ũla ũtũngawa mweũ' kwĩsĩla ũmanyi wa w'o. (Akolosai 3:10) Kwoou kũalyũka ti ũndũ wa mũthenya ũmwe.
Nao nata ethĩwa mũndũ waĩ na kĩmanyĩo kĩu nũkwatawa nĩ mĩmeo ĩsu mĩthũku ĩndĩ nũkwenda kũmwendeesya Ngai?
O tondũ vethĩawa ĩla mũndũ wakwatwa nĩ mũmeo mũthũku, mũndũ nũtonya kũlea kwĩka kwosana na mũmeo ũsu kana akeka kwosana naw'o. Atonya kwĩka ũu ata? Mbivilia yaasya: "Kinyaai mũtongoew'e nĩ Veva, na mũikeanĩsya mĩmeo ya mwĩĩ."—Akalatia 5:16.
Wasisya mũsoa ũsu ndũnasya kana mũndũ ndakethĩawa na mĩmeo ya mwĩĩ. Vandũ va ũu, ethĩwa e na kĩmanyĩo kĩseo kya kwĩmanyĩasya Mbivilia na kũvoyaa kĩla ĩvinda, akeethĩwa e mũlũmu ndakakusw'e nĩ mĩmeo ĩsu.
David, ũla ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ, nĩwoonie ũndũ ũsu nĩ wa w'o na mũno mũno ĩtina wa kũelesya asyai make thĩna ũla waĩ naw'o. Aĩtye: "Neewie naũa mũio mũito nakuĩte." Asyokete akasya, "keka naneenie na asyai makwa ĩla thĩna ũsu wangwatie oou, nĩvatonyeka ngethĩwa natanĩie mũnango ĩvinda yĩla naĩ wa mũika."
Twekala kwosana na ũndũ Yeova ũtwĩaĩe, ĩtina twĩsaa kwĩthĩwa twĩ atanu. Tũi na nzika kana mawĩaĩo ma Yeova "nĩ ma w'o, matanasya ngoo," na kana "kwĩ ĩtuvi ĩnene kwondũ wa kũmasũvĩaa."—Savuli 19:8, 11.

translation:
"One thing that really bothered me was seeing people get married just to get married. It seemed like something they had to do."—David, 23.
David is a dedicated Christian who wants to please God. But why does he feel this pressure to get married? Does God require us to marry or does He allow us to choose?
What the Bible Says
The pressure to marry can come from family or friends or simply from society. Many Christians feel obligated to conform or are afraid of being seen as "odd" or "immature." (Ephesians 4:14) However, the Bible encourages us to marry only if we truly want to (and this advice is especially helpful for young people who are feeling pressured).
The Bible gives clear guidance about marriage:
"A man should find satisfaction in his own wife, and a woman in her own husband."—Proverbs 18:22.
"God made mankind male and female, and He gave each one different desires; then He allowed them to be attracted to each other so that they would reproduce."—Genesis 1:24, 26.
"Do you not know that those who practice immoral things—those who engage in sexual immorality, those who worship idols, those who commit adultery, those who play the role of women, those who practice homosexuality, those who steal, those who lie, those who cheat—will not inherit God's Kingdom?"—1 Corinthians 6:9, 10.
In other words, God's standard applies to everyone, whether they are already married, considering marriage, thinking about getting divorced, or have been divorced. Each of us needs to examine ourselves honestly and make sure our motives are pure and that we are not letting improper desires lead us to do things that displease God.—Colossians 3:5.
Is This Really . . . ?
Is it really wise to base decisions about marriage on what others expect of us rather than on what the Bible says?
Absolutely not! The Bible shows that a man should marry only a woman, and a woman should marry only a man, not a man marrying a man or a woman marrying a woman. But some may say, "The Bible is outdated." What does it mean to be "clean" in this regard? (Hebrews 12:14) We need to be careful not to let personal preferences or cultural norms influence our view of what is right.
Is This Really . . . ?
Is it really possible for Christians to maintain purity while associating with people who are practicing homosexual behavior?
According to the Bible, God's law requires a man to have relations only with a woman. (Matthew 19:4-6) It is up to individuals to decide how closely they will associate with those who disregard this standard. The Bible also indicates that Jesus did not condone wrongdoing. (John 18:36) Therefore, it is important to avoid situations that could tempt us to compromise our integrity.
And What About . . . ?
And what about someone who has already engaged in homosexual activity? Can such a person truly become a Christian?
Yes. And there are many who have turned away from that lifestyle and become Christians. The Bible assures us that former homosexuals can inherit God's Kingdom, stating: "And yet some of you were washed clean."—1 Corinthians 6:11.
Does This Mean That Those Who Have Been Involved in Homosexual Activity Are Forever Vulnerable to Temptation? Absolutely not! The Bible urges us to "strip off the old personality," including its improper desires. (Colossians 3:10) Thus, overcoming temptation is possible.
And What About Someone Who Feels Strongly Attracted to People of the Same Sex and Wants to Please God?
Because when someone is trapped in a strong desire, he needs to seek help to overcome it and turn to God. Can he do so? The Bible says: "Keep resisting the Devil, and he will flee from you."—James 5:16.
You May Wonder How One Can Resist Such Powerful Desires. For those individuals, focus on strengthening your faith by studying the Bible regularly and pray earnestly for assistance.
David, a man "according to [God's] heart," experienced this struggle and openly admitted his failings. He said: "I have been foolishly wicked." Then he added, "Forgive my sins, and I will be cleansed from my guilt."
Let us continue to rely on the strength Jehovah gives us, so we can resist temptation. We trust that Jehovah's laws "are upright, making the heart rejoice," and that they are "more desirable than gold."—Psalm 19:8, 11.

text:
KWASISYA mũlaĩka ũũ wĩ vaa ũvingũĩte na akakwatĩĩa mũomo wa kolokolo. Aũme asu ũkũvingũĩa nĩ atũmwa ma Yesũ. Ekai twone kĩla kyatumie mekw'a kolokolonĩ.
No ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ ĩthelu kuma yĩla veva mũtheu woonoiw'e ĩũlũ wa amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ. Na ũũ nĩw'o kweekĩkie: Vetelo na Yoana nĩmaendete ĩkalũnĩ Yelusaleme mũthenya ũmwe syũa yeeka. Vau vakuvĩ na mũomo vaĩ mũndũ weethĩĩtwe e kyonze ĩvinda yonthe ya thayũ wake. Andũ mamũkuaa makamwia vau kĩla mũthenya nĩ kana avoye mbesa kuma kwa ala meũlika ĩkalũnĩ. Na yĩla woonie Vetelo na Yoana, amavoya mamũnenge o kĩndũ. Atũmwa meekie ata?
Nĩmaũngamie na mamũketeea mũndũ ũsũ ngya. Na Vetelo amwĩa: 'Nyie ndina mbesa, ĩndĩ nĩngũũnenga kĩla nĩ nakyo. Syĩtwanĩ ya Yesũ, ũkĩla na ũithi!' Vetelo ĩndĩ amũkwata kw'oko kwa aũme, na vau kwa vau atũũlĩla aũngama na ambĩĩa kũthi. Yĩla andũ moonie ũu, maseng'a mũno na meew'a mũyo nũndũ wa kyama kĩu kĩseo.
Na Vetelo asya: 'Nĩ kwa vinya wa Ngai, ũla wathayũũkisye Yesũ kuma kwa akw'ũ, twĩkie kyama kĩĩ.' Na we na Yoana maendee o na kũneena, atongoi amwe ma ndĩni mooka. Maĩ na woo nũndũ Vetelo na Yoana matavasya andũ ĩũlũ wa kũthayũũkw'a kwa Yesũ. Kwoou mamakwata na mamekĩa kolokolonĩ.
Ũnĩ ũsu atongoi asu ma ndĩni nĩmeethĩiwe na ũmbano mũnene. Na Vetelo na Yoana, vamwe na mũndũ ũla mavoetye, maetwe. Na atongoi asu mamakũlya: 'Mũneekie kyama kĩu kwa vinya waũ?'
Nake Vetelo amea nĩ kwa vinya wa Ngai, ũla wamũthayũũkisye Yesũ kuma kwa akw'ũ. Athembi asu mayeesĩ ũndũ matonya kwĩka, nũndũ mayaĩ matonya kũkaĩa kana kyama kĩu kya ũsengy'a kwa w'o nĩkĩneekĩkie. Kwoou mamatĩsya atũmwa asu maikasyoke kũneena ĩngĩ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ na ĩndĩ mamalekya.
O ũndũ mĩthenya yaendeeie na kũvĩta, now'o atũmwa maendeeie na kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Yesũ na kũvosya awau. Ũvoo wa syama isu nĩwanyaĩĩkie. Kwoou nguthu nene ya andũ kuma ndũa ila syathyũlũlũkĩte Yelusaleme maete andũ ala awau nĩ kana atũmwa mamavosye. Ũndũ ũsu watumie atongoi ma ndĩni mew'a kĩwĩu, kwoou mamakwata atũmwa na mamekĩa kolokolonĩ. Ĩndĩ mayaaĩkala vo ĩvinda ĩasa.
Ũtukũ mũlaĩka wa Ngai nĩwavingũie mũomo wa kolokolo, o tondũ ũtonya kwona vaa. Nake asya: 'Endai, mũkaũngame ĩkalũnĩ, na mũiendeea na kũtavya andũ.' Ũnĩ ũsu kwakya, Atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmatũmie andũ kolokolonĩ makaete atũmwa, namo meethĩa nĩmaendie. Ĩtina andũ asu mamethĩa maimanyĩsya ĩkalũnĩ, na mamaete nyũmbanĩ ya Nzama Nene.
Nĩvo ĩndĩ atongoi asu maisye: 'Tũtineemũvata mũno na vinya mũikasyoke kũmanyĩsya ĩngĩ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Ĩndĩ nĩmusũĩtye Yelusaleme momanyĩsyo menyu.' Atũmwa ĩndĩ masũngĩa: 'Mũvaka tũmwĩw'e Ngai mbee wa kũmew'a andũ.' Kwoou maendeea na kũmanyĩsya "ũvoo mũseo." Ĩsu yo tyo ngelekany'o nzeo ithyĩ twaĩlĩtwe nĩkũatĩĩa?
Meko kĩlungu kya 3 nginya 5.
Makũlyo
- Kweethĩiwe ata kwa Vetelo na Yoana mũthenya ũmwe yĩla maendete ĩkalũnĩ syũa yĩneeeka?
- Vetelo amwĩie ata mũndũ kyonze, na amũnengie kyaũ kyaĩ kya vata mũno kwĩ mbesa?
- Atongoi ma ndĩni mathilĩkĩtw'e nĩ kyaũ, namo mamekie ata Vetelo na Yoana?
- Vetelo eeie atongoi ma ndĩni ata, na nĩ ũkany'o mwaũ atũmwa manengiwe?
- Nĩkĩ Atongoi ma ndĩni maĩ na kĩwĩu, ĩndĩ kweethĩiwe ata yĩla atũmwa meekĩiwe kolokolonĩ ĩvinda ya kelĩ?
- Atũmwa masũngĩie ata maetwe nyũmbanĩ ya Nzama Nene?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Meko 3:1-10.
O na kau tũinengetwe ũtonyi wa kwĩka syama ũmũnthĩ, ndeto sya Vetelo ila iandĩkĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa Meko 3:6 syĩtũtetheesya ata kwona vata wa ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ? (Yoa. 17:3; 2 Ako. 5:18-20; Avi. 3:8)
- Soma Meko 4:1-31
Yĩla twavinganĩw'a twĩ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a, nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva tũtonya kwĩyĩelekany'a na ana-a-asa maitũ Aklĩsto ma mbee? (Meko 4:29, 31; Aev. 6:18-20; 1 Ath. 2:2)
- Soma Meko 5:17-42.
Andũ amwe mate Ngũsĩ ma ĩvinda ya tene na ya ũmũnthĩ, monanasya ata kũelewa nesanga ĩũlũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a? (Meko 5:34-39)

translation:
Yesterday this thing happened and they caught the thief of the donkey. He said he would steal for the sake of Jesus. Let us see every item stolen from the donkeys.
And there was a great cry from the people who went to hear the good news of Jesus. And this is what happened: Peter and John were going to Jerusalem one day at noon. They walked with the thief, a man known throughout all the land of their time. People gathered around them every day, sometimes bringing gifts to give to the man walking to Jerusalem. And when the people saw Peter and John, they were amazed at something. What did the messengers do?
They began and told a man about it. And Peter said: 'You have gifts, I will tell everyone what I have. For the sake of Jesus, take and say!' Peter took him by the hand of his mother, and they all listened to the story and told it. When the people heard this, they rejoiced greatly and praised God because of this good deed.
And Peter said: 'It is by the power of God, who raised Jesus from the dead, that we heal this person.' And he and John continued on and came across some poor people. They and others began to teach people about raising Jesus from the dead. Many received and believed in the donkeys.
Then those people began to be healed by a large crowd. And Peter and John, along with the man who had been healed, went up. And those people asked them: 'Why are you healing this person by the power of God?'
So Peter answered that it was by the power of God, who raised Jesus from the dead. He urged them to repent and believe, so that their sins might be forgiven through faith in Him. Many were moved by the messengers who spoke more about Jesus and they left believing.
But things continued to happen and spread, and the messengers continued to preach about Jesus and testify about Him. The sound of their words was very powerful. Many people from the surrounding areas gathered in Jerusalem, and those people also joined the messengers. Things happened as they had been foretold.
That night, God appeared in the form of a donkey, but it was impossible to see him clearly. So he said: 'Go, go to the villages, and continue to preach to the people.' Then, those people sent out messengers to the villages, and they went on ahead. It was like a great joy to the people.
'We have seen what we have seen and heard what we have heard, and we will continue to tell you more about Jesus,' the messengers said.
'And if you want to come to Jerusalem, come and listen to us.' The messengers were saying: 'We must honor God because of His work among the people.' That is why they continued to proclaim "the good news." Is this not the reason we are united today, so that we can worship?
Mark chapter 3 verses 5.
Questions
- Did Peter and John ever go to the villages to preach the gospel?
- Did Peter heal anyone, and did he ask them to keep it secret?
- What was the purpose of the leaders, and did they question Peter and John?
- Did Peter obey the leaders, and why did he send out so many messengers?
- If the leaders knew about the miracles, why did Peter send out messengers to the villages again?
- Did the messengers speak to people about the great name?
Further questions
- Read Mark 3:1-10.
Did Peter's actions described in Mark 3:6 show that he understood the meaning of the Sabbath? (John 17:3; 2 Cor. 5:18-20; Acts 3:8)
- Read Mark 4:1-31
When we face opposition while preaching, how can we remain courageous and be an example to our fellow Christians? (Mark 4:29, 31; Eph. 6:18-20; 1 Thess. 2:2)
- Read Mark 5:17-42.
How can we learn from the experiences of those who sought Jesus, and what does it teach us about faith? (Mark 5:34-39)

text:
ĩkũlyo
Yesũ nĩ Ngai? Yesũ nĩ wĩthĩwa aasya kana we nĩ Ngai?
Ũsungio
Andũ amwe ala maleaa kana Yesũ nĩ Ngai masyaa kana Yesũ ndaasya we nĩ Ngai.
Yesũ nĩ Ngai? — Yesũ eeyĩtie Ngai
Kwa ngelekany'o ndeto sya Yesũ ĩvukũni ya Yoana 10:30 "Nyie na Asa twĩ ũmwe." twaĩle kũsisya ũndu Ayuti meekie nikenda tũmanye kana Yesũ niweeyĩtie Ngai. Nĩ mendie kũmũkimanga na mavia nũndu wa ndeto isu: "Wĩ mũndũ ta andũ ala angi ĩndi wĩĩtwĩkĩthya Ngai" (Yoana 10:33) Ayuti nĩmamanyaa kana Yesũ eĩtwĩkĩthya Ngai. Yĩla Yesũ waisye "Nyie na Asa twĩ ũmwe" asyaa kana we na Asa nimavw'anene kĩĩ mũmbĩle na mwĩkalĩle. Yoana 8:58 nĩ ngelekany'o ĩngi. Yesũ asya, " Ningũmũtavya ũw'o...mbee wa Avalaamu kũsyawa Naivo(Ninye ũla ninye)" ũũ nĩ mwolooto wa ĩvuku ya Kuma 3:14 vala Ngai weeyonaisye ta "Ninye ũla Ninye". Ayuti ala meewie ndeto ithi nĩmoosie mavia na menda kũmũwaa nũndũ wa kũuma Ngai, otondu mwĩao wa Mose waĩtye (Alivai 24:16).
Yesũ nĩ Ngai? — Aatĩĩi make nĩmamwĩtaa Ngai.
Yoana etũtavya ndeto ĩno ya Yesũ kwĩthĩwa e Ngai: "Na ĩla ndeto(Yesũ) yaĩ Ngaĩ " na " ĩndi ĩla ndeto yatwĩka mũndũ" ( Yoana 1:1, 14). Maandĩko Aya metwonethya Kwa ũtheu kana Yesũ nĩ Ngai thĩnĩ wa mwĩĩ. Meko 20:28 maandĩko me twĩa, "Ĩsũvĩei inyw'ĩ ene, na mũisũvĩa ĩĩthya yonthe yĩla Veva Mũtheu ũmũtw'ĩte inyw'ĩ mwĩthĩwe asyaĩĩsya nĩ kana mũĩthye ĩkanisa ya Mwĩaĩi yĩla ũthooete na nthakame yake mwene." nũũ ũla wathooie ĩkanisa na nthakame yake mweene? Yesũ Klisto. Na mũsoa usu wĩasya kana Ngai athooie ĩkanisa na nthakame yake mweene, kwoou, Yesũ nĩ Ngai.
Mũmanyĩw'a Tomasi aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ, "Mwĩai na Ngai wakwa" ( Yoana 20:28). ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaamũvata aimwĩta ou. Valũa wa Tĩto 2:3 wĩtũthuthya kũmweteela Ngai na mũtangĩĩi waitũ, Yesũ Klisto. ( Sisya 2 Vetelo 1:1). Aevelania 1:8, Asa etwĩa atĩĩ, "ĩndĩ ũvoo wa Mwana easya, Kĩvĩla kyaku kya ũsumbĩ, we Ngai, nĩ kya tene na tene; Na ndata ya ũsumbĩ ya ũlũngalu nĩyo ndata ya ũsumbĩ waku." Asa amwĩtaa Yesũ Ngai, kwoou usũ ni ũĩkĩĩthyo kana Yesũ nĩ Ngai.
Ĩvukunĩ ya ũvũanyo, Mũlaĩka eyĩaĩie Yoana athaithe Ngai e weka ( Uvuanyo 19:10). Mavinda maingi mbivilianĩ twĩona Yesũ aithaithwa. (Mathayo 2:11; 14:33; 28:9,17; Luka24:52; Yoana 9:38) Yesũ ndaakanya andũ nũndũ wa kũmũthaitha. Kethĩwa yesũ ndaĩ Ngai, ethĩwa akanasya andũ maikamũthaithe, otondũ ũla mũlaĩka wamũkanisye Yoana ĩvukunĩ ya ũvũanyo. Kũthonoka ou, ve mĩsoa mĩngĩ ya mbivilia ĩwetete kana Yesũ nĩ Ngai.
Yesũ nĩ Ngai? — Kĩtumi kya Yesũ kwĩthĩwa e Ngai.
Kĩtumi kĩla kya mwanya kya Yesũ kwĩthĩwa e Ngai ni kana akethĩwa ataĩ Ngai, nthembo yake ya ngelanyonĩ ĩyĩthĩwa yaĩ mbĩanu kuĩvĩa ĩtuvi ya naĩ syitũ. (1 Yoana 2:2) kyumbe ta mũndu kĩitonya kwĩanisya nthembo ĩla yaĩlĩte ya kuĩvia naĩ sya andũ vala ve Ngai mũnene. No Ngai e weka wĩanĩĩye nthembo ya kũĩvia naĩ. No Ngai e weka waĩ atonya kwosa naĩ sya andũ na kũmaekea. (2 Akolintho 5:21) nowe weka waĩ atonya ũkw'a na ũthayũka kwonanya ũkĩlyo ĩũlũ wa naĩ na kĩkwu.
Yesũ nĩ Ngai? ĩĩ Yesũ aaisye we nĩ Ngai. aatĩĩi make maĩkĩĩaa we nĩ Ngai. Ũtangĩĩo ũtonyeka ethĩwa Yesũ nĩ Ngai. Yesũ nĩ Ngai Mũndũnĩ, Ngai wa tene na tene. Oliva na Omega. ( Ũvuany'o 1:8 ; 22:13) na Ngai mũtangĩĩi waitũ. (2 Vetelo 1:1)
English
Yesũ nĩ Ngai? Yesũ nĩ wĩthĩwa aasya kana we nĩ Ngai?

translation:
indeed
Is Jesus God? Is Jesus a deceiver or is He God?
Response
Some people say that Jesus is God while others say that Jesus is a deceiver.
Is Jesus God?—Jesus said God
For instance verse ten of John 10:30 says "I and the Father are one." We can use this scripture to help us understand whether Jesus is indeed God. It is important to remember the context of this verse: "I did not tell anyone they were gods" (John 10:33) The scriptures show that Jesus speaks as God. Consider Jesus saying "I and the Father are one" meaning that He and the Father are equal and unified. John 8:58 is another example. Jesus said, "Before Abraham was born, I am…" which is an allusion to Exodus 3:14 where God identifies Himself as "I AM". The scriptures clearly indicate that Jesus is God, but some people twist the scriptures and refuse to accept the truth about knowing God, because of the law of Moses (Leviticus 24:16).
Is Jesus God?—They blaspheme because they call Him God.
John gives us another scripture about Jesus being God: "And the Word (Jesus) was God" and "And the Word became flesh" (John 1:1, 14). These scriptures clearly demonstrate that Jesus is God in human form. Mark 20:28 scriptures state, "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world." But who fulfilled this command and established His church with power? Jesus Christ. And if God established His church with power, then, Jesus is God.
Thomas the disciple said this when he saw the resurrected Jesus, "My Lord and my God" (John 20:28). This is what Jesus allowed him to call Him. Titus 2:13 tells us to look forward to the glorious appearing of our God and Savior Jesus Christ. (Titus 2 Verse 13). Hebrews 1:8, the son says, "But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is forever and ever: and the scepter of thy righteousness is the scepter of an everlasting kingdom." The son calls Jesus God, so surely this confirms that Jesus is God.
In Revelation, the angel told John to worship God in heaven (Revelation 19:10). Many times in the Bible we see Jesus being worshipped. (Matthew 2:11; 14:33; 28:9,17; Luke 24:52; John 9:38) Jesus accepted worship from people, and because He is God, it is right for people to worship Him, which is why the angel instructed John in Revelation. Therefore, many scriptures confirm that Jesus is God.
Is Jesus God?—Reasons Jesus is called God.
One reason Jesus is called God is because He possesses the qualities of God, His law is the law of God, and His purpose is to reflect God's character. (1 John 2:2) Because no man can perfectly represent the law of God without being sinless. Only God Himself can perfectly fulfill the law. Only God Himself can forgive sins and offer salvation. (2 Corinthians 5:21) Now God Himself can take away sin and cleanse.
Is Jesus God? Yes, Jesus showed us that He is God. He made it clear that He is God. The truth becomes clear that Jesus is God. Jesus is the Almighty God, the eternal God. Alpha and Omega. (Revelation 1:8 ; 22:13) and our Creator God. (2 Peter 1:1)
English
Is Jesus God? Is Jesus called God because He is God?

text:
ĩkũlyo
Ngai ekw'o? Ve ũw'o mwaũ wa kwonany'a kana Ngai ekw'o?
Ũsungio
Ĩkũlyo ya kana Ngai ekw'o nĩ ya vata mũno mũndũ kwenda ũmanya. Kwĩ mawoni maingĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ, ĩndĩ ũsũngĩo wayo nĩwaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa wĩ mwĩanĩu na mũliku. Maũndũ ala twonaa kũũ nthĩ matwonasya na kũtũsũngĩa atĩĩ: Nĩw'o Ngai ekw'o.
Mũno mũno ĩkũlyo yĩĩ yĩkothaa ũkũlw'a atĩĩ, "we no wonanye kana Ngaĩ ekw'o?" Thĩna nĩ atĩĩ, ona kũtwĩka vena mawonany'o maingĩ makũĩkĩĩthya kana Ngai ekw'o, vai ũndu ũtonya kwonany'a kana Ngai ekw'o ateo ũitũmĩa masavu na kĩlĩko.
Kwenda kwonw'a ũw'o ũtathingĩthĩka wa kana Ngai ekw'o nĩ ũndu ũte wa vata. Wendi wa mũndũ wa kũlea kwĩtĩkĩla kana kwĩ Ngai nĩw'o ũmũsiĩĩa ndakaĩkĩĩe, kwoou ona mũndũ akonw'a Ngaĩ mũthenya kwĩ o ala matalea ũkaĩa kana kwĩ Ngai. Mũndũ ũtekwenda kwĩtĩkĩla ona oonw'a ũw'o ndetĩkĩlaa.
Kĩla kya vata mũno nĩ mũĩkĩĩo. Ve maũndũ maingĩ mũno twĩkaa kwa muĩkĩĩo woka tũteũũnga ũmanya ũũnthĩnĩ wamo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla twalĩsa Ngalĩ tũendete kyalonĩ, tuiungaa ũkũlya ndeleva kana ngali ni nzeo ĩndĩ tulikaa na muĩkĩĩo.
Kwoou ĩkulyo ya kana kwĩ Ngai yĩtonya ũsũngiika kwa kũĩkĩĩa kw'oka. Mũndũ ona wĩva ethĩwe ndetĩkĩlaa kana nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa kwĩ Ngai, maũndũ asu elĩ matonyeka o kwa mũĩkĩĩo. (Aevelania 11:8)
Kuĩkĩĩa Ngai no nginya wĩthĩwe na ũmanyi(Yoana 20:29) Ĩndĩ no nginya vethĩwe na ũlei vala ve ũw'o ( Yoana 5:39-40) Andũ amwe nĩmendaa ũmanyi mwingĩ ite kĩtumi, ũla ũtumaa mavikĩa vandũ va kũlea kana Ngai ekw'o.
Ngai ekw'o? — Masũanĩo ma Mũndũ.
Ngewa ya kana Ngai ekw'o yambĩyaa na ngananĩo sya maũndũ o ala twĩsĩ. Ĩndĩ vai mũndũ wendaa kũatĩĩa kĩndũ kĩtesĩkĩe ũmo wakyo. Andũ maeleawa maũndũ kũatĩanĩa na maũndũ ala mamethyulũlũkĩte. Kwoou kwenda kũmanya kana Ngai ekw'o kumanaa na masũanĩa ma mũndũ.
Ũw'o wa kana Ngai ekw'o wonekaa nthĩnĩ wa syũmbe ĩla twonaa kĩla mũthenya. (Alomi 1:19 - 20; Savulĩ 19:1; Mũtavany'a 3:11). Na ũũ nĩ vamwe na mea maĩtu ma kwenda kwĩka ũseo na kũmena ũthũku. Thayũ wa mũndũ nĩ ũmũkĩaa kana Ũw'o, Ũvũngũ, Wendo, kĩmena, Ũseo, Ũvuku na maũndũ angi kana nĩ maũndũ mavata mwĩkalĩlenĩ. Masũanĩo maitũ ti maw'o ĩndĩ Ngai nĩũmatũmĩaa kũtwolootela ũw'o (Uvuanyo 3:20) Masũanĩa ma mũndũ nĩ mendaa maũsũngĩo maingi (Mathayo 7:7-8) Ala maleaa wĩtano wa Ngai maina mwanya wa kũekewa (Alomi 1:18; Psalm 14:1).
Ngai ekw'o? – Ngai nthĩnĩ witũ.
ũw'o wa kana Ngai ekw'o nĩ wonekaa mũno thĩnĩ wa mawĩsĩlo ma kĩla mũthenya. No wĩthĩwe ũtatonya kũĩkĩĩthya kana nũkwĩw'a mũyo, ĩndĩ ngoonĩ yaku ũkethĩwa na ũtanu mwingi. Mawĩsĩlo ma mĩthemba ta maũsũngĩo ma mboya na kwona syama nĩmatũmaa mũndũ etĩkĩla kana kwĩ Ngai.
Wendi wa Mũndũ wa kwĩka ũw'o nĩ ũtumaa mũndũ etĩkĩla kana kwĩ Ngai. Ngai nĩwookie we mweene ta mũndũ kũũ nthĩ. ( 2 Akolintho 4:6) nĩkenda twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo ya vakuvĩ nake ( Yoana 14:6). Ala mamũmanthaa Ngai na ngoo ntheũ makamwona ( Mathayo 7:7-8), na usũu wa Veva mutheu. (Yoana 14:26-27).
Kwoou ĩkũlyo ya kana Ngai ekw'o? tũitonya ũsungĩa na ũtheu mwĩanĩu ĩndi no twoloote ũw'o ũla wĩvo wa kwonany'a kana Ngai ekw'o. Kwĩtĩkĩla kana Ngai ekw'o nĩ kĩko kya mũĩkĩĩo woka.
English
Ngai ekw'o? Ve ũw'o mwaũ wa kwonany'a kana Ngai ekw'o?

translation:
Indeed
God exists? Or is it just talk about God existing?
Understanding
The question of whether God exists is something everyone desires to know. With many arguments surrounding this question, most people find themselves confused and lost. But things like what we see and hear often lead us to believe: It is true God exists.
Many times this question arises, "do you truly believe in God?" And it is said that seeing many signs confirms God exists, yet this matter remains difficult to believe in unless one experiences it personally and investigates it thoroughly.
To understand this topic concerning God existing is a challenging thing. The path of a person seeking to understand regarding God is what guides them, so someone who understands God well will be able to help others who are searching for God. A person who seeks understanding should continue searching.
Every desire of the heart is important. We have many desires, and through those desires, we can learn much about ourselves. For example, when we search for knowledge, we strive to eat good food and drink water, and we live with purpose.
But the question of believing in God can only be understood through investigation. Someone who has not been convinced or has not investigated God, their matters remain unclear because of lack of understanding. (Hebrews 11:8)
Knowing God leads to eternal life (John 20:29) And having the scriptures leads to knowing the way to Him (John 5:39-40) Some people seek much knowledge but without purpose, which causes them to stumble and prevents them from understanding God exists.
God exists?—Questions of Mankind.
The reason why the question of God existing troubles people is because of the mysteries of all things we experience. Yet, a person wants to confirm something based on their own judgment. People interpret things according to their own understandings. Therefore, wanting to understand if God exists relates to the thoughts of mankind.
The evidence of God's existence is seen in creation, just as we see every day. (Romans 1:19-20; Psalms 19:1; Ecclesiastes 3:11). And this is similar to how people go to school to gain wisdom and acquire skills. The nature of man is to appreciate Creation, Truth, Love, justice, Wisdom, Beauty, and other qualities that are valuable. Our thoughts are not enough to reveal God to us; He uses them to guide us to truth (2 Corinthians 3:20) Human thoughts often lead to many errors (Matthew 7:7-8) But they also reveal God's power in the space of our minds (Romans 1:18; Psalm 14:1).
God exists?—God within us.
The evidence of God's existence is clearly seen in the wonders of everyday life. It is not possible to deny or ignore His presence, yet many people are blinded by great pride. The wonders of nature and seeing goodness cause a person to turn towards God.
Love for God's creation leads a person to turn towards God. God dwells within each person. (2 Corinthians 4:6) We will be guided by the Spirit of truth (John 14:6). But those who seek God sincerely and earnestly will find Him (Matthew 7:7-8), and the veil will be lifted. (John 14:26-27).
What is the purpose of the evidence of God's existence? We can understand and learn through careful observation so that we may know the truth about God's existence. To turn toward God's existence is the key to unlocking understanding.
God exists? That is the truth about knowing God's existence.

text:
WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Kamwana ketawa Brian keew'a kĩw'ũ kyetĩka nda ĩla koona tũmwana twĩlĩ masomaa ĩmwe tũkĩte. Mavinda elĩ kyumwa kĩĩ tũmwana tũu nĩtũnamũthing'ĩĩisye anyw'e sikala, na yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya katatũ tũkwenda kwĩka ũu.
Kamwana ka mbee kaimwĩa atĩĩ:
"O nayu wĩ o weka ĩngĩ? Ndũeke ngũnenge kaindo ke o vaa."
Kayumya kĩndũ ngusunĩ na kaimũnenga Brian.
Brian asisya ayĩthĩa kamwana kau kakwete sikala. Oona ũu ayĩw'a wia mũno na ayĩw'a kĩw'ũ kyetĩka nda ĩngĩ!
Brian ayĩa tũmwana tũu atĩĩ: "Mbona nĩnamwĩie kana ndinyusaa . . . "
Atanaminĩĩa, kamwana kala kangĩ kaimũtilĩĩla na kaimwĩa atĩĩ: "Ekaa kwĩthĩwa wĩ na wia ũu!"
Brian aikasũngĩa na aikea atĩĩ: "Nyie ndi wia."
Kamwana kala kangĩ kaimwilĩĩla Brian kw'oko kĩtuo na kaimwĩa na wasya mũnini, "Naku eka kũlea."
Nako kamwana kala kangĩ kaithengeesya sikala ũthyũ kwa Brian na kaimũtavya na kĩwe, "Ndũkamake, vai mũndũ tũkatavya."
We wĩka ata keka nue Brian?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
Tw'o tũmwana tũu nĩtũsũanĩĩte kĩla tũkwĩka? Tw'o nĩtw'o twĩyĩamũĩe kwĩka maũndũ asu? Ti laisi. No nginya twĩthĩwe tweetĩkĩlile twaw'e nĩ andũ angĩ, na nũndũ twendaa twĩtĩkĩlwe nĩ andũ ala angĩ, tweetĩkĩla matwĩkĩe ũtwi.
We yu ũkakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu wakwatie Brian, wĩka ata nĩ kana wĩsiĩĩe?
ĨTHĨWA WĨYŨMBANĨTYE
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ wĩ kĩlĩko nĩwonaa ũthũku, na kwĩvitha; Ĩndĩ ala mate ũmanyi nĩmaendeeaa, na kũthĩna."—Nthimo 22:3.
Mavinda maingĩ mũndũ no amanye kana ve thĩna ũtonya kumĩla. Kwa ngelekany'o, twasye nĩwoona syana mũsomaa ĩmwe syĩ mbee waku na iinyw'a sikala. Weethĩwa ũmbanĩtye kĩlĩko kyaku, nũũmanya ũndũ ũtonya kwĩvetangana na thĩna ũsu.
SŨANĨA
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mwĩ na wasya mũseo wa ngoo."—1 Vetelo 3:16.
Ĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Maũndũ meĩthĩwa mailyĩ ata neeka maũndũ mataĩle ala meĩkwa nĩ andũ angĩ?' Ũw'o nĩ kana no wendeew'e nĩ kwĩtĩkĩlwa nĩ andũ ala angĩ kwa kavinda o kanini. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Wĩw'a ata ĩtina wa kwĩka ũu? No wende kwĩyanangĩa ĩsyĩtwa nĩ kana wendeesye syana ila mũsomaa ĩmwe?—Kuma 23:2.
ĨKA ŨTWI
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ mũĩ nũkĩaa."—Nthimo 14:16.
No nginya twĩke motwi na tũyĩkala kwosana na motwi asu tweeka. Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana Yosevu, Yovu, na Yesũ, nĩ aũme meekie motwi maseo. O na nĩwetete ĩũlũ wa Kaini, Esau, na Yutasi, ala meekie motwi mathũku. Naku we ũtonya kwĩka ata?
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũla wĩ na kĩthito ũndũnĩ ũnini mũno, e kĩthito maũndũnĩ manene." (Luka 16:10) Ethĩwa nũsũanĩĩte mathĩna ala matonya ũkũkwata weeka ũtwi ũtaĩle na ũkatw'a vyũ ndwĩĩka ũndũ ũtaĩle, nĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi mũno kwĩthĩwa na ũkũmbaũ ĩla ũkũelesya ũtwi waku, na ũndũ ũsu nũtanĩthasya.
O na ndũkamake nũndũ ti lasima ũkatinda ũtavĩtye ala ũsomaa namo maũndũ maingĩ. O kũmatavya ndeto nini ta AIEE no kwĩthĩwe kũtoetye. Kana nĩ kenda ũmatavye vyũ ũtwi waku, no wasye atĩĩ:
"Nyie ndi vo!"
"Nyie ndyĩsa kwĩka maũndũ asu!"
"Naku mbona nĩwĩsĩ ndyĩsa kũnyw'a sikala!"
Ũndũ ũla wa vata nĩ kũneena ũtekwananga ĩvinda na wĩ na ũkũmbaũ. Na weeka ũu, no ũseng'e mũno nĩ kwona ũndũ andũ ala angĩ ma mũika mekwĩvathana naku ĩla meĩka maũndũ mataĩle!
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA ĨLA WAVŨTHW'A NĨ ALA ANGĨ
Ũtonya kwĩka ata ĩla syana ila ingĩ syaũtavya ndeto sya kĩvũthya? Nao nata ĩla syakwĩa atĩĩ: "Wĩ na thĩna mwaũ, ko wĩany'a wia ata?" Nũseo ũmanye kana andũ asu ma mũika meũtavya ndeto isu nũndũ meenda kũũthing'ĩĩsya wĩke tamo. Ũtonya kwĩka ata veethĩwa ũu? Ve maũndũ elĩ ũtonya kwĩka.
No wĩtĩkĩlane na mũndũ ũsu ũkũũvũthĩĩsya. (No ũmwĩe, "Nĩwaweta w'o, nyie nĩ wia mũno!" Na ĩndĩ ũimũelesya nĩkĩ wamwĩa ũu.)
No ũmũsũngĩe kwa nzĩa ũte kũsũanĩaa. Mũtavye nĩkĩ walea kwĩka ũu, na ũimũwetea ũndũ ũũtuma asũanĩa. ("Aĩ nonaa ũilyĩ ta ũtesa kũnyw'a sikala!")
Ethĩwa andũ ala angĩ ma mũika nĩmekũendeea kũũvũthĩĩsya nũndũ wa ũtwi waku, uma vala maĩ ũthi! Lilikana kana o ũndũ waendeea kwĩkala vau, now'o mekũendeea kũũthing'ĩĩsya ĩ-ya mũno. Ĩndĩ wauma vala maĩ, wĩthĩawa woonany'a ndũkwenda mũndũ o na wĩva avĩndũe ũtwi waku.
Ũw'o nĩ kana ndwĩsa kwĩkala ũte kũthing'ĩĩw'a wĩke ũndũ ũla ũtaĩle. Ĩndĩ no ũtw'e ũndũ ũkwenda kwĩka, na ũyosa ĩtambya yĩla yaĩle. Lilikana kana nue ũtonya kwĩnyuvĩa ũndũ ũla ũkwenda kwĩka!—Yosua 24:15.

translation:
ARE YOU AFRAID OF DEATH?
Consider this story: A boy named Brian once had a dream where he saw a small child with only one shoe walking around. The child was very sad because they didn't have anyone to play with, and that's why the child wanted to die.
The boy wondered what it meant:
"Oh mother, will you help me? Let me find my father."
He cried sadly and asked Brian.
Brian ignored the boy who was crying. Then he dreamed another dream and saw him having the same dream again!
Brian asked the child, "Why do you want to die or be hurt…?"
Immediately, the boy got angry and said, "Stay away from me and this place!"
Brian ran away and shouted, "I am leaving this place."
The boy then followed Brian to the gate and said with tears, "Please help me grow up."
But the boy continued to cry at Brian and told him, "My friend, let's both grow up."
What about death, should Brian help?
PLEASE CONSIDER!
Are we children who always want to die? Are we always complaining about difficult things? Don't be foolish. Sometimes we talk badly about others, and sometimes others talk badly about us, talking hurts our ears.
If you were caught in a situation like the one that happened to Brian, would you be afraid or brave?
BE THOUGHTFUL
The Bible says: "Anyone who has little is satisfied with little, and anyone who has much worries about how to increase it."—Proverbs 22:3.
Many people don't know when they have enough. For example, we see some students who are always sad because they don't have shoes or can't go to school. Be thoughtful and appreciate what you have, and you will avoid worrying about what you lack.
CONSIDER
The Bible says: "Be respectful to everyone."—1 Peter 3:16.
Ask yourself: 'Should I worry about things that haven't happened yet, or should I care about what others think of me?' It's possible you won't be bothered by others' opinions if you focus on important things.—Jeremiah 23:2.
LISTEN TO YOUR HEART
The Bible says: "A wise person thinks carefully before acting."—Proverbs 14:16.
Sometimes we act quickly and regret it later. The Bible shows that Joseph, Job, and Jesus listened to their hearts. But Cain, Esau, and Judas did not listen to their hearts. So can you tell?
The Bible says: "Whoever is faithful in very small matters is also faithful in large ones." (Luke 16:10) Remember that small sins can lead to bigger sins, and if you allow small sins to continue, they will destroy your heart, and this will make you unhappy.
But don't let fear stop you from doing what is right or from learning more. What does AIEE have to do with making good decisions? Perhaps you are afraid of what others will say, so you say:
"I am nothing!"
"I am too foolish to speak up!"
"And why would anyone listen to me anyway!"
That kind of thinking can ruin your life and cause you much pain. And if you give in to that feeling, you might end up doing things you'll regret!
WHAT CAN HELP YOU MAKE GOOD DECISIONS
Can you make good decisions even when faced with difficult choices? Some may ask: "Do you really know what is best?" If you realize that others who seem confident are often confused, you will be less likely to rely on them. Can you make good decisions then? Here are some things that can help.
Don't isolate yourself from others. (And don't think, "They don't understand me!" because that might not be true.)
And be willing to accept advice. If you listen to wise counsel, you will learn how to avoid problems. ("Yes, I agree that it's wrong to drink alcohol!")
There are also others who want to help you make good decisions, so don't hesitate to ask them! But remember that if something seems too good to be true, it probably is. So be careful about trusting people who try to pressure you.
That is why it is important to choose to do what is right. If you always strive to do what is right, you will eventually succeed. Remember that you can make good decisions!—Joshua 24:15.

text:
ĨVINDA yĩmwe Kingsley nĩwaaĩwe kĩlungu kya kũsoma Mbivilia nthĩnĩ wa Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi. Ũsu nĩw'o waĩ ũvoo wake wa mbee. E vau mbee, eeteelile nginya mũndũ amũtine kĩtuo nĩ kana ambĩĩe kũsoma. Atamũkie kĩla ndeto nesa ateũvĩtũũkany'a o na vanini. Ĩndĩ nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ? Ayumya ũvoo wake, ndaasisya Mbivilia. Nĩkĩ?
Kingsley aĩ mwana-a-asa wekalaa Sri Lanka, na ndoonaa nthĩ. O na ndeew'aa nthĩ nesa na aendaa na kasululu ka kũsukumwa. Ĩndĩ emanyĩisye ata ĩũlũ wa Yeova, na esie ata kũandĩkĩthw'a nthĩnĩ wa Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi? Eka ngũelesye.
Ĩla nakomanie na Kingsley ya mbee, naseng'iw'e mũno nĩ wendi mwingĩ ũla waĩ naw'o wa kũmanya ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Nĩweemanyĩĩtye Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ ingĩ kauta, na ĩvuku yake ya Ujuzi Uongozao Kwenye Uhai Udumuo Milele, yĩla yaandĩkĩtwe na mũandĩko wa ala matonaa, yaĩ ĩtw'ĩkangu vyũ. * Nĩweetĩkĩlile nĩmũmanyĩsye Mbivilia, ĩndĩ vaĩ mathĩna elĩ.
Thĩna wa mbee, Kingsley ekalaa vala vasũvĩĩawa andũ akũũ na ala onzu. Nũndũ vandũ vau veethĩawa na kelele na Kingsley ndeew'aa nthĩ nesa, naĩ no nginya nalĩlĩke ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya. Naalĩlĩkaa ũkethĩa onthe vau nĩmekwĩw'a kĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya kĩla kyumwa!
Thĩna wa kelĩ nĩ kana ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya, Kingsley aĩ atonya kũsoma na kũkwatya o kaĩndũ kanini. Kwoou nĩ kana akwatye nesa, eeyũmbanasya nesa vyũ. Eekaa ũu kwa kũsoma ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ kĩla tũkwĩsa kwĩmanyĩsya, akasisya maandĩko Mbivilianĩ yake ya mũandĩko wa ala matonaa, na ĩndĩ aivanga kĩlĩkonĩ ũndũ ũkwĩsa kũsũngĩa makũlyo ala me ĩvukunĩ. Nzĩa ĩsu watũmĩaa yaĩ nzeo mũno. Ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya ekalaa nthĩ mũkekanĩ avĩlanĩtye maaũ, na ĩndĩ ew'ĩte mũyo mwingĩ aielesya na wasya mũtũlu kĩla wemanyĩsya, kavindanĩ kau o aendeee kũtinatina nthĩ. Ĩtina wa kavinda kanini, nĩtwambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya kelĩ kwa kyumwa, na kĩla ĩvinda tweemanyĩasya masaa elĩ!
ŨNDŨ WAVIKANGAA MAŨMBANONĨ NA ŨNDŨ WAAKAA ALA ANGĨ
Kingsley nĩwendaa kũthi maũmbanonĩ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, ĩndĩ kũvika vau kyaĩ kĩvalũa. Aĩ no nginya alĩsw'e kasululunĩ kake na ayĩsa kumw'a, na aisyoka alĩsw'e ngalĩnĩ na ayumw'a, na ĩndĩ ayĩsa kwambatw'a Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ kĩkundinĩ nĩmaumanĩasya kũmũtetheesya, na nĩmatanĩaa mũno kwĩka ũu. Maũmbano maendeee, Kingsley athengeeasya kũtũ sivikanĩ nĩ kana ethukĩĩsye nesa. O na nĩwaumasya maelesyo!
Ĩtina wa Kingsley kwĩmanyĩsya kwa ĩvinda ĩna, nĩweeandĩkĩthisye nthĩnĩ wa Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi. Syumwa ilĩ itiele nĩ kana athi akaumye ũvoo wake wa mbee wa kũsoma, nĩnamũkũlilye ethĩwa nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye. Anzũngĩie ate na nzika ambĩa, "Ĩĩ, Mwana-a-asa, nĩsomete mavinda ta 30." Nĩnamũkathie nũndũ wa kĩthito kyake, na namwĩa nĩngwenda nĩmwĩthukĩĩsye aisoma. Nĩwavuie Mbivilia yake, atinĩĩsya syaa syake nthoonĩ sya kĩlungu kĩla waaĩwe, na ambĩĩa kũsoma. Ĩndĩ noonie syaa syake iteũvavata mathangũ ma ĩ Mbivilia ta tene. Nĩvo namanyie kaĩ eekĩĩte ndeto sya kĩlungu kĩu kyonthe kĩlĩkonĩ!
Namũsyaisye nĩseng'ete, methoi malovotete kũlovota. Nĩnamũkũlilye atonya kũlilikana nesa wĩana ũu ata, na asomete o mavinda 30. Nĩvo ĩndĩ wanzũngĩie, "Aiee, nĩnasomaa mavinda ta 30 kwa mũthenya." Kingsley aminĩte mbee wa mwei mũima aisoma kĩtũngĩlĩĩlo kĩlungu kĩla waaĩwe, o ailyĩ ũla mũkekanĩ wake, nginya eekĩa ndeto syonthe kĩlĩkonĩ.
Na ĩndĩ mũthenya nĩwesie kũvika, na Kingsley aumya ũvoo wake Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ. Ĩla waminie, kĩkundi nĩkyakũnie mbĩ na mũyo mwingĩ mũno, o na andũ aingĩ nĩmaĩie moona ũndũ mũmanyĩw'a ũsu mweũ waĩ na kĩthito kĩana. Mũtavany'a ũmwe waĩ anaeka kumya maũvoo ma sukulu nũndũ wa wia nĩweeĩandĩkĩthisye ĩngĩ. Nĩkĩ? Aisye: "Ethĩwa Kingsley nũtonya, o nakwa ndiemwa!"
Kingsley emanyĩisye Mbivilia vandũ va myaka ĩtatũ, na ĩndĩ avatiswa Matukũ 6, Mwei wa 9, 2008, nĩ kana onany'e kana nĩwĩyumĩtye amũthũkũme Yeova. Kingsley aendeeie kwĩthĩwa e Ngũsĩ ndĩkĩĩku nginya ĩla wakwie kwĩ Matukũ 13, Mwei wa 5, 2014. Aikw'a nĩweesĩ kana akathayũũkw'a ekale Nthĩ Nzaũ, na ĩtina wa vau aiendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova e na vinya mwingĩ na ate na thĩna o na ũmwe wa mwĩĩ. (Isa. 35:5, 6)—Ngewa ĩno ĩeleetw'e nĩ Paul McManus.
^ kal. 4 Ĩvuku yĩu yaumĩthiw'e mwaka wa 1995, ĩndĩ yu yĩitumbĩthaw'a.

translation:
One brother, Kingsley, was invited to give a Bible talk at the Kingdom School of Theocratic Ministry. He was very happy about this privilege. But he was worried because he felt he didn't know how to prepare a talk. He would read each paragraph several times and then try to memorize it. Is this right? No.
Kingsley grew up in Sri Lanka, and he wasn't used to this. And he didn't feel comfortable giving a talk without notes. Did he ever ask Jehovah for help, and did he ever write his talk for the Kingdom School of Theocratic Ministry? Yes, he did.
I had the opportunity to spend time with Kingsley, and I encouraged him to learn more about preparing talks from the Bible. He began to study the Bible and the book "Leading a Bible Study," which was written by experienced publishers, and it helped him a lot. * I realized that I needed to study the Bible more, and I found that it was very helpful.
Recently, Kingsley has been able to give excellent talks to many people. Many people have been touched by Kingsley's talks, and I also feel like we can improve our ability to teach. I really appreciate the effort everyone puts into preparing each talk!
When it comes to preparing talks, Kingsley was able to read and understand things much better. Now when he prepares a talk, he understands it well. He keeps reading more and more during each preparation, and he uses his own words when writing his Bible talk, and he doesn't worry about memorizing everything. It seems that he now uses what he learns effectively. This helps us a lot. However, preparing talks can be challenging for some, and they may need more encouragement and support from others who can help them practice. In the case of difficult talks, let's encourage them to practice often, and each talk should take hours to prepare!
THIS SECTION IS MARKED TO SHOW THE STRUCTURE AND CONTENT OF OTHER SECTIONS
Kingsley wants to go to the Kingdom Hall, so that he can see how things are done there. He also feels like he needs guidance and advice, and he hopes to get guidance from the Kingdom Hall. Many people want to help him improve, and I agree with this. The meetings continue, and Kingsley strives to show us what he has learned. And he is improving quickly!
Regarding Kingsley's preparation for the next talk, he wrote a letter to the School of Evangelization. Last week, he said that he felt tired because of his busy schedule, but he encouraged himself. He told me and my wife, "I will read over 30 books." I admired his determination, and I told him that I would help him study. I gave him his Bible, and asked him to read a chapter each day, and told him to read. But he only read a few chapters of the Bible ten times. That's how I realized he didn't understand the whole chapter properly!
I helped him practice, and we had several rehearsals. I encouraged him to be able to recite this well, and to read over 30 books. So he told me, "Okay, I will read over 30 books per month." Kingsley spent almost a whole month studying diligently each day, and he finally understood everything completely.
And now the month is coming to an end, and Kingsley has achieved his goal at the Kingdom Hall. But remember, the group still needs much support, and many people are happy to see this good work and dedication. Another student was also able to finish school thanks to the letter he wrote. Why? Because he said: "Let Kingsley succeed, and I will also succeed!"
Kingsley dedicated himself to Jehovah when he was three years old, and on June 9, 2008, he may have appreciated or enjoyed serving Jehovah. Kingsley went to preach in Ngusii while still young, and then he went to June 13, 2014. He continued to serve faithfully, and because of his efforts, he helped others to serve Jehovah with great joy and enthusiasm. (Isa. 35:5, 6)—This information was provided by Paul McManus.
^ par. 4 This issue was published in 1995, when it was first introduced.

text:
Ve ĩvinda waaĩthĩwa vakuvĩ na mũndũ wĩ na kyeva nũndũ wa kũkw'ĩĩwa, na ũyĩthĩa ndwĩsĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũmũtethya? Mavinda angĩ no twĩthĩwe tũtesĩ ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka kana kwasya, na kwoou tũitw'a kũvindya twaaĩwa nĩ ũndũ tũkwĩka. Ĩndĩ ve maũndũ ma vata ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana ũtetheesye.
Mavinda maingĩ kĩla kyendekaa no kwĩthĩwa wĩ vakuvĩ na mũndũ ũsu na ũimũtavya ndeto ta, "Nĩ vole." Kwosana na syĩthĩo imwe, kũkumbatĩa mũndũ kana kũmũkwata kw'oko o kavola ĩla ũũneena nake yĩthĩawa no nzĩa ya kwonany'a kana nũũmũthĩnĩkĩa. Ethĩwa ũla ũkw'ĩĩwe nũkwenda kũneena mwĩthukĩĩsye. O na nĩ ũndũ mũseo ũkatetheesya ũla ũkw'ĩĩwe maũndũ ala ũtatonya kwĩka ta kũua, kũsũvĩa syana, kana ũkatetheesya mĩvango ya mathiko, veethĩwa ve vata. Maũndũ asu no methĩwe me ma vata mũno o na kwĩ ndeto ila nzeo ũtonya kũtavya mũndũ.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, no mũneene ĩũlũ wa mũkw'ũ, na mũno mũno maũndũ maseo mwĩthĩwa mwatanĩie vamwe kana ndaĩa nzeo ila ũnaĩ nasyo. Maũndũ ta asu no matume mũndũ ũla ũkw'ĩĩwe atana. Kwa ngelekany'o, Pam, ũla wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũũme weetawa Ian myaka thanthatũ mĩvĩtu, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mavinda maingĩ andũ nĩmandavasya maũndũ maseo na ndamesĩ ala Ian weekaa, na ũndũ ũsu nũndanĩthasya mũno."
Andũ ala mekaa ũkunĩkĩli mawetete kana andũ aingĩ ala makw'ĩĩwa nĩmatetheeaw'a ĩvindanĩ yĩla makw'ĩĩwe, ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda andũ mayũlwa nĩmo na maikwatya maũndũ moo. Kwoou, ndũkaaeke kũkũnĩa simũ kana kũtembelea mũndũ ũla ũkw'ĩĩwe o na vavĩta ĩvinda yĩana ata. * Andũ aingĩ ala me na kyeva nĩmatũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa kũtembelewa kana kũkũnĩwa simũ nũndũ nĩmew'aa makiakiw'a.
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya mũndũ mũka wa mũika wĩtawa Kaori, kuma Japan, ũla waũmĩiw'e mũno nĩ kĩkw'ũ kya inyia wake, na ĩtina wa myei 15 akw'ĩĩwa nĩ mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wake ũla mũkũũ. Ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana nĩwatetheeiw'e nĩ anyanyae. Ũmwe wa anyanya asu nĩ Ritsuko, ũla waĩ mũkũũ kwĩ Kaori, na nĩweeyumisye ethĩwe e mũnyanyae wa vakuvĩ vyũ. Kaori aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndineena ũla w'o, ũndũ ũsu ndwaambendeesya. Ndyoonaa ta nĩtonya kwenda mũndũ ũngĩ tondũ nendete inyia wakwa, na ndyasũanĩaa ũndũ ũsu ta wĩsa kwĩkĩka. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nũndũ wa kwona ũndũ twekalanasya na Ritsuko, nĩweethĩiwe e mũnyanyawa mũnene. Kĩla kyumwa nĩtwaendaa maũmbanonĩ na kũtavany'a ĩmwe. Nĩwanthokasya tũkanyw'a kyai ĩmwe, akandetea lĩu na akambandĩkĩa valũa na aindũmĩa kaati mavinda maingĩ. Maũndũ maseo ala Ritsuko wambĩkie nĩmandetheeisye mũno."
Myaka 12 nĩ mĩvĩtu kuma inyia wa Kaori akw'a, nayu e na mũũme nĩ atavany'a ma ĩvinda yonthe. Kaori easya atĩĩ: "O nayu Ritsuko no ũnthĩnĩkĩaa. Ĩla nesa kwĩnũka mũsyĩ nĩnĩendaa kwake na ngatanĩa kwĩthĩwa vamwe nake."
Ngelekany'o ĩngĩ ya mũndũ waunĩkie nũndũ wa kũtetheew'a nĩ ala angĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nĩ Poli, ũla nĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova kuma nthĩ ya Cyprus. Poli aĩ na mũũme mũseo weetawa Sozos, na nĩwamwiĩie ngelekany'o nzeo e mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi kwa kũmathokasya andũ ala ndiwa na syana ila ikw'ĩĩwe nĩ kana matane na maiya vamwe. (Yakovo 1:27) Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana Sozos e na myaka 53 nĩwakwie kumana na wimbu waĩ mũtwe (brain tumor). Poli aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnakw'ĩĩiwe nĩ mũemewa wambendete mũno na twatwaanĩte kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 33."
Ĩtina wa mathiko, Poli nĩwaendie Canada e na kamwana kake kala kanini ka myaka 15 ketawa Daniel. Mavika kũu, nĩmambĩĩie kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Poli aĩtye atĩĩ: "Anyanyawa ma kĩkundi kĩla naendie mayeesĩ maũndũ maito ala matũkwatie ĩvinda ĩvĩtu. Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa matesĩ maũndũ asu kũyaamasiĩĩa kũtũkiakisya kwa ndeto na meko maseo. Kwa w'o, maũndũ asu maĩ ma vata vyũ, na mũno mũno ĩvindanĩ yĩu kamwana kakwa kendaa vyũ ũtethyo kuma kwa ĩthe! Namo ala matongoetye kĩkundinĩ nĩmamwendete Daniel na nĩmamũthĩnĩkĩaa mũno. Ũmwe katĩ woo nĩwaĩkĩĩthasya kana nĩwamũthokya Daniel ĩla meũthi kwĩtanĩthya na anyanyae kana kũthaũka mũvĩla." Poli na Daniel maendeee nesa ũmũnthĩ.
Kwa w'o, ve nzĩa mbingĩ tũtonya kũtetheesya na kũkiakisya andũ ala me na kyeva. O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia nĩtũkiakiasya kwa kũtũnenga wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.
^ kal. 6 Andũ amwe nĩmaandĩkĩte matukũ ala anyanyae makw'ĩĩwe nĩ andũ moo nĩ kana malilikanae na maimakũnĩa simũ. Mekaa ũu matukũ asu mavika kana me vakuvĩ kũvika nũndũ yĩu nĩyo ĩvinda yĩla anyanyae matonya kwĩthĩwa mayenda ũkiakisyo.
