translation:
When experiences overwhelm us with pain and a person feels a need to be comforted, and perhaps doubts whether it's possible to express it, many times we are given something small that can hide or diminish, and sometimes we take comfort in experiencing what has overwhelmed us. Truly there are things that are difficult to hide or express.
Many experiences each time happen with pain and a person who doesn't show it, saying, "It's okay." Besides a smile, embracing someone or holding their hand often hides deep wounds that are covered with a facade of acceptance or denial. A wound like that which is hidden wants to reveal its bitterness. And it's a serious thing that hides when those hidden things become unable to hide such as death, suffering greatly, or hiding the consequences of mistakes, truly they are harmful. Things like those are shown so that they don't hide, but rather allow a person to heal.
The nature of experience is a large burden on the heart, and often many things are experienced together or alone but have an impact on them. Things like those don't make the person who experiences them forget. For example, Pam, who was hurt by a man named Ian five years ago, said: "Many people I see pretend about many things and I always blame Ian for this, and this thing keeps hurting me deeply."
Other people who live with secrets or others who are hurt are often able to understand the experience of those who have been hurt, truly the nature of experience makes people sensitive and aware of things. Sometimes, let's try to avoid judging or visiting the person who is hurt and give them space. * Other people who feel a need can find a way to be visited or judged without being exposed.
Regarding the story of a woman named Kaori from Japan, her mother's influence on her life, and the age of 15 when she was influenced by her older sister, the situation is sometimes difficult or confusing. One of the sisters is Ritsuko, who is older than Kaori, and she has been involved in various activities. Kaori said: "I hate that person, this thing bothers me. I can't go near another person because I betrayed my mother, and I am worried about this matter because it seems to be getting worse. Because of this and because of you, the fact that we compare ourselves to Ritsuko, she is involved in big problems. Every day I want to run away and hide somewhere. I want to drink tea with her, then lie down and cover myself with blankets and think about many things. Many things that Ritsuko does bother me greatly."
Twelve years later, in Kaori's life, she still hasn't forgotten everything. Kaori said: "Oh, I remember Ritsuko well. But I need to calm down and I will go to her house and try to talk to her again."
Another story of someone who experienced difficulties is that of Polly, who is one of Jehovah's Witnesses in Cyprus. Polly had a husband named Sozos, and she shared the good news with people, especially those who were poor and sick, and it was often done with little money and help from others. (James 1:27) However, unfortunately, Sozos developed a brain tumor when he was 53 years old. Polly said: "I was deeply saddened and we spent 33 years together."
After his death, Polly moved to Canada with her young son Daniel, who was 15 years old. There, she continued to serve among Jehovah's Witnesses. Polly said: "The congregations I visited always showed me kindness and helped me cope with my difficult situation. But I still missed my husband very much, and sometimes I would cry thinking about him. Despite this, I kept busy, and gradually things got better, and my son also began to recover emotionally. And I found comfort in spending time with Daniel and supporting him. Sometimes I wondered if I should remarry, but I decided not to because I wanted to continue serving alongside my brothers and sisters." Polly and Daniel continued their ministry.
Therefore, let us be compassionate and show empathy to those who are suffering. Also, remember that the Bible can help us understand how to deal with grief.
^ par. 6 Some have written letters to express their feelings to friends or family members. This can be helpful during times of sorrow, but it is important to choose carefully what we say so that our words will bring comfort rather than cause pain.

text:
MWANA-A-ASA ũmwe wĩtawa Don kuma Canada nũtataa mũno atavye ũvoo mũseo andũ ala matũlũlaa sokonĩ mate na nyũmba mekala. Don aĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa ũmwe wa andũ asu: "Ve mũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa asu mate mĩsyĩ weetawa Peter. Ndyaaona mũndũ wĩany'a kĩko take kũu isakinĩ. Ailyĩ naĩ vyũ na ndwaĩ ũmũthengeea nũndũ ndendete kũthengeanĩa na andũ. O na kau andũ nĩmatataa mũno kũmwĩka nesa, nĩwaleaa mavinda maingĩ." Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 14 Don ndaanow'a nĩ kwĩkala aitata kwĩka mũndũ ũsu ũseo.
Mũthenya ũmwe Peter akũlilye Don atĩĩ: "Ũtindaa ũmbatĩĩe nĩkĩ? Mbona andũ ala angĩ mayĩthĩawa makwetye ũu wakwa? Ũnthĩnĩkĩaa nĩkĩ?" Don atũmĩie maandĩko atatũ na ũĩ nĩ kana atate kũvikĩa Peter ngoo. Mbee vyũ ambie ũkũlya Peter ethĩwa nĩweesĩ kana Ngai e ĩsyĩtwa, na amwĩa asome Savuli 83:18 Mbivilianĩ eyonee. Don asyokie eea Peter nĩesomee ĩandĩko ya Alomi 10:13, 14 nĩ kana amanye nĩkĩ wamũthĩnĩkĩaa. Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye kana "o ũla ũkekaĩla syĩtwa ya Mwĩaĩi, nũkatangĩĩwa." Mũthya Don asomie ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 9:36, na ĩndĩ eea Peter nĩesomee one. Mũsoa ũsu waĩtye atĩĩ: "Na [Yesũ] amona makomano, amew'ĩa tei nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩmanyamaaw'a na kũnyaĩĩkw'a ta malondu mate na mũĩthi." Ĩla Peter wasomie ndeto isu, akũlilye ũũ akelemetye methoi: "Nyie nĩ ũmwe wa malondu asu?"
Peter nĩwambĩĩe kũalyũka. Nĩwathambie, aolanga kĩng'ee, na ambĩĩa kwĩkĩa ngũa nzeo ila wanengetwe nĩ Don. Peter nĩwaendeeie kwĩkĩa kĩthito ekale e mũtheu.
Peter aĩ na kavuku waandĩkaa maũndũ ala wakomana namo kĩla mũthenya. Maũndũ ala waandĩkĩte mwambĩĩonĩ maĩ ma kũmakya na ma kũtũla ngoo, ĩndĩ ala waandĩkie ĩtina maĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, vandũ vamwe aandĩkĩte atĩĩ: "Ũmũnthĩ nĩnĩmanyie ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Yu ĩla ngũvoya no nĩvoye Yeova. Nĩĩw'a mũyo mũno nũndũ nĩnĩmanyie ĩsyĩtwa yake. Don ambĩie Yeova no atw'ĩke Mũnyanyawa, ũla ũtonya kũmbĩthukĩĩsya kĩla ĩvinda, o na twĩthĩwe twĩ ĩndĩĩ kana nĩ kyaũ kĩendeee."
Ndeto syake sya mũthya kũandĩka aandĩkĩie ala masyaanĩw'e. Aandĩkie atĩĩ:
"Sua ũũ ndikwĩw'a nesa. Nĩona yu nĩngũie. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa ũũ nĩw'o mũthenya wakwa wa mũthya, nĩnĩsĩ kana ngoonana ĩngĩ na mũnyanyawa [Don] Nthĩ Nzaũ. Ethĩwa yu mũkwetye kũsoma ndeto ii, no nginya nĩthĩwe nde vo. Ĩndĩ mũkesa kwona mũndũ ũilyĩ ta ũte ũmwe witũ mathikonĩ makwa, neenai nake na mwa nĩngũmwĩsũva mũsome kavuku kaa kanini ka mbuluu. [Awetaa kavuku ka kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ketawa "W'o Ũla Ũtongoasya kwa Thayũ Ũtathela." Kavuku kau akanengetwe myaka yĩ navu ĩtina.] * Kaĩtye kana ngoona mũnyanyawa ĩngĩ Nthĩ Nzaũ. Nĩĩkĩĩte ũu na ngoo yakwa yonthe. Ninyie mwana-a-inyia wenyu, Peter."
Mathiko mathela, mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wa Peter wĩtawa Ummi aisye ũũ: "Myaka ta ĩlĩ mĩthelu Peter nĩwaneenie nakwa. Noonie e mũtanu ũndũ ndaamwona kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ. O na nĩwathekaa." Ummi eeie Don atĩĩ: "Nĩngũsoma ĩvuku yĩu nũndũ wesa kwona kĩndũ kĩũkiita mwana-a-mwaitũ, no nginya kĩthĩwe kĩ kĩndũ kya mwanya." O na ĩngĩ Ummi nĩweetĩkĩlile kũsoma yĩla ĩvuku tũtũmĩaa matukũ aa yĩtawa Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? na ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
Kwoou nĩtwĩkei ta Don. Tũikasiasye mũvwanĩle wa mũndũ. Vandũ va ũu, nĩtwendei ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ na tũyũmĩĩsya andũ ma mĩthemba yonthe. (1 Tim. 2:3, 4) Tweeka ũu, nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kũtethya andũ mailyĩ ta Peter, ala matonya kwĩthĩwa mataũnganawa namo ĩndĩ me na ngoo nzeo. Na nĩtwĩthĩwei na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana Ngai ũla 'ũsyaasya ngoo,' akatuma ũw'o wĩana ngoonĩ sya ala aĩlu.—1 Sam. 16:7; Yoa. 6:44.
^ kal. 7 Kaumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, ĩndĩ yu nĩkaekie kũtumbĩthw'a.

translation:
A certain child named Don went to Canada and greatly feared a ghost who haunted houses and markets. Don said this story about one of his friends: "There was a man among our friends called Peter. I saw a strange man carrying a sack on his back. He walked with difficulty and I tried to help him carry it along with others. But many people were afraid to approach him closely, they kept their distance." Because of this story, for fourteen years Don was afraid to meet anyone like that person.
One day Peter asked Don: "Why are you so scared? Why do other people avoid this place of yours? What should I do?" Don wrote him three letters but he couldn't make Peter understand. After some time he told Peter that perhaps God is testing him, and advised him to read Psalm 83:18 carefully. Don also urged Peter to read Romans 10:13, 14 so that he could know what to do. That scripture says that "everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved." Then Don read Matthew 9:36, and encouraged Peter to read it too. The verse reads: "When Jesus saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd." But after Peter read those scriptures, he asked him with annoyance: "Are you one of those sheep?"
Peter became stubborn. He turned away, looked around, and refused to listen to anyone except Don. Peter continued to go to the old shrine in the forest.
Peter had a habit of writing down everything he experienced every day. He wrote about things that happened during his travels and his difficulties, and he also wrote down dreams that troubled him. For example, some people wrote: "I felt the power of God. But today I praise Jehovah. This is the only truth and I feel his power. Don told me that Jehovah would give us salvation, which will protect us from every evil, and we will be healed from sickness or it will continue."
The rest of the story about writing down experiences is as follows: He wrote:
"Today I am very happy. I see that you love me. And this time, this is my best day, I am satisfied or more than ever with salvation [Don] Ntii Nzau. May you enjoy reading this story, and may it help you. If you find someone who is like us among our brothers, tell them and let them read this book, which is a large blue book. [Get the book to teach the Bible using the title "This is the Way to Eternal Life." The book was published several years ago.] * Or more salvation Ntii Nzau. I write this with all my heart. Your son-in-law, Peter."
Our brothers, Peter's sister named Ummi said this: "For over forty years Peter has been with me. I have known him for many years. And he is capable." Ummi asked Don: "I will read your story so that people can know what calls our son-in-law, and may it help them understand something about life." And Ummi agreed to read the small story we use on days called the Bible Teaching Work and one of Jehovah's Witnesses.
Let us be like Don. Let us show genuine concern for people. All people, let us go everywhere preaching and encouraging people with all their hopes. (1 Tim. 2:3, 4) With this, we can pray to continue speaking to people like Peter, but we can also be helped to unite with them and with all our hearts. And we will rejoice with the thought that God 'chooses the heart,' sending his spirit to those who are sincere.—1 Sam. 16:7; John 6:44.
^ par. 7 We learn from Jehovah's Witnesses, and you can ask to be taught.

text:
Nũsomete nesa makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya ala mela kuma? Ethĩwa nũu, sisya ethĩwa nũtonya kũsũngĩa makũlyo aa maatĩĩe:
Aklĩsto nĩmaĩle kũmũvoya Yesũ Klĩsto?
Aiee. Yesũ atũmanyĩisye kũmũvoya Yeova, na we mwene nĩweekaa ũu nũndũ amũvoyaa Ĩthe. (Mt. 6:6-9; Yoa. 11:41; 16:23) Nĩkyo kĩtumi aatĩĩi make ma mbee mavoyaa Ngai, ĩndĩ ti ũ Yesũ. (Meko 4:24, 30; Ako. 1:3)—1/1, ĩthangũ ya 14.
Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kwĩkaa kĩla mwaka nĩ kana twĩyũmbanĩsye kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ?
Ũndũ ũmwe tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kũatĩĩa nesa mũvango wa kũsoma Mbivilia ũla twĩthĩawa tũnengetwe ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka ĩvindanĩ yĩu nĩ kũtata twongele ĩvinda yĩla tũtũmĩaa ũthũkũminĩ witũ. Na ĩngĩ no tũvoye na tũisũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo ũla Ngai ũtũnengete.—15/1, ĩthangũ ya 14-16.
Ala avungwa elĩ ma Misili matavisye Yosevu ndoto syoo mesie kwĩkanwa namo ata?
Yosevu atavisye ũla wanengae Valao mbinyu kana akatũngwa wĩanĩ wake. Ĩndĩ ũla wauaa mĩkate eeiwe ndoto yake yoonanasya kana Valao akamũaa na aimwamba mũtĩnĩ. Maũndũ maendie o ũndũ Yosevu wawetete. (Mwa. 40:1-22)—1/2, ĩthangũ ya 12-14.
Ana-a-asa ma Japan makwatie mũthĩnzĩo wĩva wa mwanya?
Makwatie kavuku ke na ũvoo wa Mathayo o tondũ ũandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ ya Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya. Ana-a-asa asu nĩmanenganae kavuku kau ũtavany'a, na nĩketĩkĩlĩtwe nĩ andũ aingĩ o na matesĩ Mbivilia nesa.—15/2, ĩthangũ ya 3.
Nĩ maũndũ meva maĩ ĩvinda ya atũmwa ala matumie ũvoo mũseo ũnyaĩĩka mũno?
Nũndũ Mũuo wa Lomi (Pax Romana) wekalile kwa ĩvinda ĩasa, kĩsio kĩla kyasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Lomi kĩyaĩ na ithokoo mbingĩ. Kwaĩ malelũ maingĩ na maseo ala maĩ matonya kũtũmĩwa nĩ amanyĩw'a. Nakyo Kĩkiliki nĩkyo kyatũmĩawa nĩ aingĩ, na kwoou yaĩ laisi kũtavya andũ aingĩ ũvoo, vamwe o na Ayuti ala manyaĩĩkĩte ũsumbĩnĩ ũsu wa Lomi. Na ĩndĩ amanyĩw'a maĩ matonya kũtũmĩa mĩao ya Lomi nĩ kana mokitĩe ũvoo mũseo.—15/2, ĩthangũ ya 20-23.
Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto ma w'o matatanĩaa sikũkũ ya Isita?
Yesũ eeaĩe aatĩĩi make malilikanae kĩkw'ũ kyake, ĩndĩ ti ũthayũũkyo wake. (Luka 22:19, 20)—1/3, ĩthangũ ya 8.
Mbona matukũ aa mavuku maitũ maielesya ngewa sya Mbivilia maikothaa kũweta kyuu na kĩla kya w'o?
Mbivilia nĩwetaa kana andũ amwe maĩ syuu sya maũndũ angĩ manenange. Ngelekany'o ĩmwe ya syuu yĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akalatia 4:21-31. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ti ũseo mavinda onthe kũmanthĩthya syuu Maandĩkonĩ. Ĩla tũũsoma ĩũlũ wa andũ kana maũndũ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ, no tũmanthe nĩ kyaũ tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya ngewanĩ isu. (Alo. 15:4)—15/3, ĩthangũ ya 17-18.
Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwendeew'a mũno nĩ kalungu ka ĩkangaa kala keethĩiwe ĩvumbunĩ ĩnene ya takataka ya tene nthĩ ya Egypt?
Myakanĩ ya 1900, ve kalungu koonekie ke na ilungu imwe sya ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo wa Yoana. Kalungu kau nĩkatonya kwĩthĩwa kaseũviw'e myaka mĩongo yĩana ũna ĩtina wa Yoana kũandĩka ĩvuku yĩu yake. Ũvoo ũla wĩ kalungunĩ kau nũtũĩkĩĩthasya kana ĩvuku yĩla twĩ nayo ya Yoana nĩ ya w'o, na kana o nayo Mbivilia nĩ ya w'o.—1/4, ĩthangũ ya 10-11.
Nĩkĩ kũtenga mwĩki wa naĩ ũtekwenda kwĩlila nĩ nzĩa ya kwonany'a wendo?
Mbivilia nĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa mũvango wa kũtenga andũ. Kũtenga andũ nĩ ũndũ ũte wa ngũĩ na nũtonya kũtethya mũno. (1 Ako. 5:11-13) Mũvango ũsu nũtumaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩtaĩwa, ũkasũvĩa kĩkundi kĩikavukw'e, na no ũtume mwĩki wa naĩ avindũka kĩlĩko.—15/4, ĩthangũ ya 29-30.

translation:
Let us examine these scriptures together, shall we? However, consider this, brother, whether you will strive to understand the meaning of these verses:
Did Christ ever teach people how to pray to Jesus Christ?
Yes. Jesus taught them how to pray to Jehovah, and he himself often withdrew to pray to the Father. (Matt. 6:6-9; John 11:41; 16:23) That is why his disciples asked him to teach them how to pray, not to pray to him. (Mark 4:24, 30; Acts 1:3)—1/1, page 14.
How can we then be sure each year that we are imitating Jesus' example in our prayers?
One way we can do so is by making sure our prayer requests conform to what we read in God's Word. Another way we can conform to God's Word is by thinking about the reasons why we are asking for those things we need. And also by appreciating and valuing the privilege God gives us.—15/1, pages 14-16.
But did the rulers of Egypt interpret Joseph's dreams correctly, or did they not?
Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dream to mean there would be seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine. Because of this, Pharaoh stored up grain during the abundant years so that he could provide for his people during the famine. The outcome showed that Joseph's interpretation was correct.—Gen. 40:1-22—1/2, pages 12-14.
Have Japanese householders shown interest when presented with a Bible?
They have been receptive, and Matthew chapter 10 is used when conducting Bible studies. Some householders ask for a copy of the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures, and many others are pleased to receive literature on the Bible.—15/2, page 3.
What important points should missionaries emphasize when using this scripture?
During the Roman peace (Pax Romana), travel became relatively safe, though not entirely free from danger. In many places, roads were well maintained, making it easier for messengers to travel. However, Cilicia was often used by bandits, and some travelers found it necessary to hire guards to protect them.—15/2, pages 20-23.
Why did Christians face persecution under the reign of Easter?
Jesus foretold that his followers would be persecuted, but not to the extent that he was.—Luke 22:19, 20—1/3, page 8.
Why do many people today find it difficult to believe what the Bible says about the future?
The Bible speaks of events that may seem strange to some people. For example, read Acts 4:21-31. But even if these accounts seem unusual, they do not contradict the Scriptures. Instead, when we study the experiences of ancient people and the events described in the Bible, we can learn how to apply those lessons to our lives.—Alo. 15:4—15/3, pages 17-18.
How could archaeologists discover the massive ruins of an ancient city buried beneath tons of debris in Egypt?
In the 1900s, explorers located it using a clue from the book of Revelation. This clue helped them narrow down their search area, and after years of digging, John was able to write his account. The discovery proved that the city mentioned in Revelation is real, and that the Bible is reliable.—1/4, pages 10-11.
How can we show appreciation for Jehovah's love by striving to imitate his compassion?
The Bible provides examples of showing mercy. Showing mercy is a quality that pleases God and can be cultivated.—1 Co. 5:11-13. This quality helps us reflect God's personality, strengthens the congregation, and enables us to forgive others.—15/4, pages 29-30.

text:
"Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe kĩkundinĩ kitũ nĩwambilĩĩile kana nĩnooyĩte mbesa syake. Ĩla angĩ kĩkundinĩ mamanyie ngewa ĩsu, nĩmambĩĩie kwĩtĩkĩlana nake. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩwandavisye kana nũmanyie ti inyie noosete mbesa isu. O na kau nĩwambĩtisye ũekeo, neew'aa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwĩsa kũmũekea nũndũ ũndũ ũsu nĩwambũmĩĩtye ngoonĩ."—Linda.
WE NO ũelewe ũndũ Linda weew'aa ĩtina wa kũũmĩw'a nĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu? Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, amwe nĩmaũmĩĩtw'e nĩ meko ma angĩ nginya ũndũ ũsu ũkatuma masyoka ĩtina kĩ-veva. We no wĩthĩwe waakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu?
Ve Mũndũ Ũtonya 'Kũtũtaanany'a na Wendo wa Ngai'?
Kwa w'o no twone wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kũekea mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa. Vethĩawa vailyĩ ũu nũndũ nĩtwĩsĩ kana Aklĩsto maĩlĩte kwendana. (Yoana 13:34, 35) Ĩla twavĩtĩw'a nĩ mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa, nĩtũũmĩaa na tũkew'a woo mũno.—Savuli 55:12.
Mbivilia nĩyĩtĩkĩlĩte kana mavinda amwe Mũklĩsto nĩwĩthĩawa na "ũndũ na ũngĩ." (Akolosai 3:13) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ĩla ũndũ ta ũsu watũkwata, no twĩw'e wĩ vinya kũmĩĩsya. Yo ve ũndũ ũtonya kũtũtetheesya ĩla ũndũ ta ũsu waumĩla? Kwasũanĩa myolooto ĩĩ ĩtatũ ya Mbivilia:
Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ nĩwĩsĩ maũndũ onthe. Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa ene kĩla kĩndũ kyonthe, o na yĩla tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle ũtonya kũtũũmĩsya mũno. (Aevelania 4:13) O na ĩngĩ, Yeova nũtwĩw'ĩaa tei ĩla twaũmĩa ngoonĩ. (Isaia 63:9) Ndesa kwĩtĩkĩlya "monyamao, kana woo" o na mũthũkũmi wake 'atũtaanany'e na wendo wake.' (Alomi 8:35, 38, 39) Yo tyo twaĩle kwĩthĩwa tũilyĩ ta Yeova kwa kũlea kwĩtĩkĩlya kĩndũ o na kĩva kana mũndũ o na wĩva atũtaanany'e na Yeova?
Kũekea mũndũ ti kwĩtĩkĩlya ĩvĩtyo. Ĩla twaekea ala matũvĩtĩsya, tũyĩthĩawa tũivũthĩĩsya, kũtetea, kana kwĩtĩkĩlya meko moo mathũku. Lilikana kana Yeova ndetĩkĩlasya naĩ yĩendeee, ĩndĩ nĩ ũekeaa ethĩwa ve kĩtumi kya kwĩka ũu. (Savuli 103:12, 13; Avakuki 1:13) Ĩla ũkũtwĩkĩa vinya tũekee ala matũvĩtĩsya, Yeova ethĩawa aitwĩa nĩtũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yake. Yeova "ndekalasya ũthatu wake tene na tene."—Savuli 103:9; Mathayo 6:14.
Ĩla twaeka kwĩw'a woo nũndũ wa kũvĩtĩw'a, nĩtũtethekaa. Tũtethekaa kwa nzĩa yĩva? Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno. Ĩla woosa ĩvia yĩ na ũito mũnini, na ũiyũkĩlya kwa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩvatonyeka ũkalea kũnoa mũno. Nao nata ĩla waendeea kũkĩlya ĩvia yĩu kwa ĩvinda ĩasa? Yo no ũendeee kũyũkĩlya kwa ĩvinda ĩasanga ta ndatĩka siana ũndũ mũna, ĩsaa yĩmwe, kana o mbeange? Vai nzika kana ndũema kũnoa kw'oko! Ũito wa ĩvia yĩu ndũvĩndũkaa, ĩndĩ o ũndũ waendeea kũyũkĩlya kwa ĩvinda yĩasa now'o ũkwĩw'a yĩ yĩito. Ũu now'o vethĩawa vailyĩ twaendeea kwĩw'a woo nũndũ wa kũvĩtĩw'a. O ũndũ twaendeea kwia woo ngoonĩ sitũ nũndũ wa kũvĩtĩw'a, o na ethĩwa ti woo mwingĩ, now'o tũendeeaa na kwĩyĩũmĩsya. Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova ũtwĩkĩaa vinya tũvete woo ngoonĩ sitũ. Kwa w'o, kũveta woo ngoonĩ nĩkũtũtetheeasya.—Nthimo 11:17.
"Neew'aa Yeova Mwene ta we Ũkũneena Nakwa"
Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Linda ndakaendeee kwia woo ngoonĩ ĩla wavĩtĩiw'e nĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũngĩ? O na kau ve maũndũ angĩ mamũtetheeisye, kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa itumi ila Maandĩko manenganĩte sya kũekea ala angĩ nĩkwamũtetheeisye mũno. (Savuli 130:3, 4) Mũno mũno Linda nĩwatetheeiw'e nĩ kũmanya kana ĩla twaekea angĩ, o nake Yeova akatũekeaa ĩla twavĩtya. (Aeveso 4:32–5:2) Asũanĩa ũndũ maũndũ asu mamũtetheeisye, Linda aĩtye atĩĩ: "Neew'aa Yeova mwene ta we ũkũneena nakwa."
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda Linda nĩwavetangie woo ũla waĩ ngoonĩ. Nĩwamũekeie kuma ngoonĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũla wamũvĩtĩisye, na yu mendanĩte mũno. Linda nũendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova. O naku ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova nũkwenda kũũtetheesya o tondũ watetheeisye Linda.

translation:
"One person who loves deeply may be willing to forgive or overlook his mate's faults. But if a mate repeatedly hurts you, it is wise to distance yourself from him. In view of the seriousness, that person may have already decided or realized that you two cannot continue together, so he may initiate separation."—Linda.
DO YOU understand what Linda means when she says that that person has already made a decision? The reason why is this, sometimes people make a decision and then take steps that lead to an irreversible outcome. Do you feel trapped in such a situation?
Be a Loyal Friend—Show Love for God!
For example, we often show love for a child or a friend. Christians strive to do this because they want to please God. (John 13:34, 35) However, if a child or a friend betrays us, we can still be loving and compassionate.—Psalm 55:12.
The Bible encourages us to forgive others, even when they hurt us deeply, and to be "merciful, just as God is merciful." (Colossians 3:13) While this is true, there are times when a situation is too dangerous to endure. So how do you know when to persevere and when to separate? Consider these Scriptural principles:
First, remember that Jehovah sees everything. Jehovah knows everyone thoroughly, and He understands when we are facing a difficult situation. (Proverbs 4:13) Also, Jehovah does not force us to stay when we are being mistreated. (Isaiah 63:9) Instead, he encourages us to be courageous, yet he also wants us to show love for our brothers. (Romans 8:35, 38, 39) So how can we remain loyal to Jehovah by showing courage and compassion toward those who are disloyal to us or mistreat us?
To forgive someone does not mean to condone their wrongdoing. But if we forgive others, we demonstrate Christlike qualities, such as patience, kindness, and mercy. Just as Jehovah deals with us in his undeserved kindness, so we should extend kindness to others. (Psalm 103:12, 13; Micah 7:13) However, if we continue to allow ourselves to be harmed, Jehovah may view that as a lack of self-respect. (Proverbs 6:3) But Jehovah assures us that he will always support us and help us to uphold his standards.—Psalm 103:9; Matthew 6:14.
If we harbor resentment, we harm ourselves. How can we avoid harboring resentment? By focusing on Jehovah's forgiveness. If someone has deeply hurt you, and you find it difficult to let go of the pain, remember that Jehovah is understanding. But what if the person continues to repeat the offense? Should you simply put up with it indefinitely, allowing him to take advantage of your generosity? No, there is a limit to how much we should endure! Your feelings are important, and you have the right to protect yourself from abuse. So, while continuing to show Christian love, you may need to set boundaries. This will also help others to see the seriousness of their actions. And this is why Jehovah encourages us to be reasonable in our expectations. Thus, being reasonable helps us to maintain our spiritual health.—Proverbs 11:17.
"Praise Jah, You People!"
What motivated Linda to continue praising Jehovah despite her trials? She realized that acknowledging her mistakes was vital. Like David, she understood that the Scriptures offer guidance on how to deal with guilt. (Psalm 130:3, 4) Linda learned that admitting our errors allows Jehovah to forgive us. (Ephesians 4:32–5:2) In addition to making personal adjustments, Linda said: "Praise Jah, You people!"
Linda used the time in prison to strengthen her faith. She spoke about Jehovah to fellow inmates, and they appreciated her sincerity. Linda continued to seek Jehovah's guidance. And she felt confident that Jehovah would support her, just as he had supported her in the past.

text:
[Ĩkalanasya] na Ngai waku wĩ na wĩnyivyo.—Mika 6:8, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Nzĩa ĩmwe twonanasya twĩ na wĩnyivyo nĩ kũmanya kana Yeova nĩ mũtheu vyũ na kana vai ũngĩ ũtonya kũtũtongoesya nesa eka we na kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa myolooto yake. O na ĩngĩ, ethĩwa twĩ na wĩnyivyo tũkanengaa ndaĩa mawoni ma ala angĩ na tũielewa ũndũ mekwĩw'a. Kwoou 'twĩkalanasya na Ngai witũ twĩ na wĩnyivyo' ethĩwa nĩtwaatĩĩa myolooto yake thayũnĩ witũ na tũinavũthĩĩsya woni wa ala angĩ. Mwĩkĩĩle witũ wa ngũa ndwaĩle kũtuma andũ masũanĩa maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ witũ, ĩndĩ waĩle kũtuma mamanya kana ithyĩ twĩ athaithi ma Yeova. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa na andũ ala angĩ onthe nĩmaĩle kwona nĩtũkuĩte nesa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai witũ mũlũngalu. Myolooto yake yĩ ĩũlũ mũno na nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũmĩatĩĩe twĩ atanu. Nĩtũũmakatha ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala methĩĩtwe mayĩkĩa ngũa nesa, mayĩyanakavya nesa, na me na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Na kĩtumi nũndũ kĩu nĩkĩtumaa ala me na ngoo nzeo mendeew'a nĩ ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ na nĩkĩtumaa Yeova akwata nguma na ew'a mũyo. w16.09 3:18-20
Nĩwakĩlan'ya vinya na Ngai na ĩngĩ na andũ, na wakĩlya vinya. —Mwa. 32:28.
Yakovo nĩwatw'ĩte vyũ kũendeea kũng'ang'ana, na nĩwoonanisye kana ndeeyũmbanĩtye kũeka asindwe! (Mwa. 32:24-26) Na vate nzika, nĩwaathimiwe nũndũ wa wũmĩĩsyo wake. Nĩvo ĩndĩ wesie kũnengwa ĩsyĩtwa Isilaeli, yĩla yonanasya "Ũla Ũkĩlanasya Vinya na Ngai" kana "Ngai Nũkĩlanasya Vinya." Yakovo nĩwakwatie mũthĩnzĩo mũnene ũla o na ithyĩ twĩthĩawa tũimantha, naw'o nĩ kwĩtĩkĩlwa nĩ Yeova na kũathimwa nĩwe. Nakyo kĩveti kya Yakovo kĩla kyeetawa Lakeli kyekalaa kyeteele mũno kyone ũndũ Yeova ũkeanĩsya watho ũla wathĩte mũũme wakyo. Amwathĩte kana akaathima ũsyao wake. Ĩndĩ kĩyaĩ na syana. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu mũndũ mũka kwĩthĩwa ate na syana woonekaa wĩ thĩna mũnene mũno. Kwoou Lakeli aumisye va vinya wa kũendeea kũng'ang'ana na thĩna ũsu wamũtũlaa ngoo na ũtaĩ na ũtonyi wa kũũmina? Mbee Lakeli ndaaĩkya ngoo. Vandũ va ũu, aendeeie kũng'ang'ana na kũvoya na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo kingangĩ. Ĩtina Yeova nĩweewie mboya syake na amũathima na syana.—Mwa. 30:8, 20-24. w16.09 2:6, 7
Ndeto ya Ngai ĩ thayũ, na nĩ nthangaau, na nĩ mbũĩ kwĩ ũvyũ ũla mũĩ ngalĩ syelĩ.—Aevl. 4:12.
Nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno ũkony'a syana syaku ũseo wa kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia. (Sav. 1:1-3) Ve nzĩa mbingĩ sya kwĩka ũu. Kwa ngelekany'o, no ũitavye isũanĩe ũndũ ũũ: twasye nĩsyatw'ĩka niũthi ikekalae kĩthamanĩ kĩna kĩ vaasa na no inyuvaa ala ikekalanasya namo kũu. Ikũlye atĩĩ: "Nĩ kana mwĩkale na mũuo, mwenda kĩla ũmwe wa asu mũkũendany'a namo ethĩwe na nguma syĩva?" O na no ũielesye ũtao mũseo ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akalatia 5:19-23. Nzĩa ĩsu no ĩmanyĩsye syana syaku maũndũ elĩ ma vata. Mbee vyũ, mĩao ya Ngai nĩtumaa andũ mekalany'a na mũuo na mew'ana. Kelĩ, ĩla Ngai ũkũtũmanyĩsya ethĩawa aitũmbany'a nĩ kana twĩĩkala nthĩ nzaũ nesa. (Isa. 54:13; Yoa. 17:3) No ũtũmĩe ngewa ĩeleetw'e mavukunĩ maitũ ũitetheesye ielewe maũndũ asu nesa. Ngewa ta ĩsu no ũmĩkwate kĩla kĩlungunĩ kĩthĩawa ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya kĩtawa "Mbivilia Nĩalyũlaa Andũ." w16.09 5:13, 14

translation:
He has shown you, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?—Micah 6:8, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
One way we show our appreciation for what Jehovah does for us is by striving to live up to his standards and by being willing to obey his laws. And also, when we meditate on what is right, we can discern how to apply Bible principles to our lives. When we "meditate on God's law," we are showing that we value his standards and want to benefit from his guidance. Our brothers often spend time preparing talks that will help others understand what the Bible teaches. They want to help people see that Jehovah cares for them. Those who have had a share in the ministry and those who support them are eager to please our God and to make known His name. His law is perfect and helps us to know what we should do to be pleasing to him. Let us therefore continue to put effort into learning how to apply it in our life. We are encouraged to assist those who have a share in the ministry, to give them encouragement, and to work alongside them. But why is it important to imitate the zeal of the first-century Christians? Because it moved them to preach the good news without delay and helped Jehovah to act in their behalf. w16.09 3:18-20
When someone deals honestly with God and with men, he prospers. —Prov. 32:28.
Jacob earnestly begged to be let off, and I observed how skillfully he used persuasion so that he might succeed! (Prov. 32:24-26) And when he prevailed, he was honored with a change of name. This is why anyone who wishes to be called Israel should understand that his name means "Striving With God" or "God Strives." Jacob grasped a great truth, one that we too can benefit from, namely, that Jehovah allows himself to be entreated and delights in showing favor. And Jacob's very name reminds us that Jehovah can influence the outcome of matters involving people. He responds to their earnest appeals. Be reasonable and considerate. A person may appear humble, yet have lofty ambitions. Did Lael truly appreciate the value of striving earnestly and being modest and avoiding pridefulness? Apparently Lael did not. People like him strive earnestly for wealth and glory and self-exaltation. Let Jehovah show you his favor and bless you generously.—Prov. 30:8, 20-24. w16.09 2:6, 7
God's law is perfect, and it is trustworthy, and it is delightful to those who love it.—Ps. 19:7.
It is a fine thing to train oneself to think about what you read in the Bible. (Ps. 1:1-3) There are many ways to do this. For example, you could ask yourself questions such as: 'What main point does this section emphasize, and how does it affect me personally?' Consider this illustration: "Suppose you are walking along a road, and you come across someone who has fallen into a ditch. Would you not stop and try to help him?" Then apply the principles found at Galatians 5:19-23. These scriptures will help you discern what is right. But often, God uses his spirit to move people to be generous and compassionate. Still, God trains us to use our own conscience and discernment so that we may become skilled in distinguishing good from bad. (Isa. 54:13; John 17:3) So make good use of the publications that provide practical guidance and help you understand important truths. The brochure "The Bible—God's Word" can be a valuable tool in helping others learn about God. w16.09 5:13, 14

Kwa w'o, Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ya tene mũno. Yaandĩkiwe ĩndĩĩ? Yambĩĩie kũandĩkĩwa Middle East myaka ta 3,500 mĩvĩtu. Nĩ kana tũelewe ũndũ ũsu, myakanĩ ĩsu nĩw'o ũsumbĩ wa China wa kũtianĩa wa mũsyĩ wa Shang wasumbĩkĩte, nayo ndĩni ya Buddha yambĩĩie nthĩ ya India myaka ta 2,500 mĩvĩtu, ĩsu nĩ myaka vakuvĩ 1,000 kuma Mbivilia yambĩĩa kũandĩkwa.—Sisya ĩsandũkũ yĩ na kyongo "Maũndũ ma W'o Ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia."
Mbivilia nĩsũngĩĩte makũlyo ma vata ala twĩkũlasya
Nĩ kana ĩvuku yĩtethye andũ, no nginya yĩthĩwe yĩtonya kũeleeka nesa nĩ ala mekũyĩsoma, na makona yĩtonya kũmatethya. Mbivilia yĩilyĩ ũu. Nĩsũngĩaa makũlyo ma vata ala andũ mekũlasya.
Kwa ngelekany'o, waaĩkũlya, 'Nĩkĩ andũ moombiwe?' Kwa myaka ngili mbingĩ andũ methĩĩtwe maimantha ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu, ĩndĩ mayaaĩsa kũũkwata. Mbivilia nĩsũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu ilungunĩ ilĩ sya mbee sya ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩĩlyo. Ilungu isu ilĩ nĩsieleetye ĩũlũ wa 'mwambĩlĩĩlyo,' myaka mbilioni mbingĩ mĩvĩtu ĩla nthĩ na ĩtu syoombiwe vamwe na ndata, na ikundi sya ndata. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:1) O na nieleetye ũndũ nthĩ yatw'ĩkĩthiw'e vandũ vaseo va kwĩkala, ũndũ syũmbe ingĩ syoombiwe, na ũndũ andũ moombiwe na ikasyoka ikaelesya kĩeleelo kya Ngai ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ isu syonthe.
YĨANDĨKĨTWE KWA NZĨA ĨTONYA KŨELEEKA
Mbivilia nĩtũnengete motao matonya kũtwony'a ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna. Motao asu methĩawa me laisi kũeleeka. Maũndũ aa elĩ nĩmonanĩtye nĩkĩ motao asu me laisi kũeleeka.
Ũndũ wa mbee, Mbivilia yĩandĩkĩtwe na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi na kya kwendeesya. Vandũ va kũtũmĩa ndeto mbingĩ na syĩ vinya, Mbivilia ĩtũmĩĩte ndeto syĩ laisi kũeleeka. Maũndũ ala me vinya maeleetw'e na ndeto o ila tũtũmĩaa kĩla mũthenya.
Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ atũmĩie ngelekany'o mbingĩ syĩ laisi na sya maũndũ ala andũ meekaa kĩla mũthenya nĩ kana amanyĩsye kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũvikĩa ngoo. Yesũ aumisye mbingĩ sya ngelekany'o isu nthĩnĩ wa Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ ũla ũandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Mbivilia ya Mathayo kĩlungu kya 5-7. Mũtangaasi ũmwe aisye kana ilungu isu syĩ "ũvoo ũtonya kũtethya andũ" na kĩeleelo kyasyo "ti kũtũkũthĩĩa maũndũ ilĩkonĩ, ĩndĩ nĩ kũtũtongoesya maũndũnĩ ala tũkwĩka." No ũsome ilungu isu o kwa ndatĩka 15 nginya 20 na ũkeethĩa nĩ ilungu syĩ laisi na ndeto ila Yesũ watũmĩie syĩ ũtethyo mwingĩ kwitũ.
Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtumaa Mbivilia yĩthĩwa yĩ laisi kũeleeka nĩ kĩla ĩneeneete. Mbivilia ti ĩvuku ya mbano kana ngewa. Ĩndĩ o tondũ ĩvuku The World Book Encyclopedia yonanĩtye, Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku yĩeleetye "ĩũlũ wa andũ me nguma, na angĩ mate nguma" na yĩkonany'a "mathĩna ala moomĩĩisye, wĩkwatyo ũla maĩ naw'o, mawonzu moo, na ũsindi ũla makwataa." Nĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũmanya maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe ĩũlũ woo, kĩla kyaendeee, tũkaelewa ũndũ meew'aa na maũndũ ala twĩmanyĩasya kumana na ũvoo ũsu.—Alomi 15:4.
KĨLA MŨNDŨ NO AMĨKWATE NA KĨTHYOMO ŨTONYA KŨMĨELEWA
Nĩ kana ũelewe nĩ kĩla kĩ ĩvukunĩ no nginya yĩthĩwe yĩandĩkĩtwe na kĩthyomo ũkũelewa. Ũmũnthĩ, no ũkwate Mbivilia na kĩthyomo ũtonya kũelewa o na ethĩwa wĩkalaa nthĩ yĩva. Kwasũanĩa kĩla kĩtumĩte Mbivilia yĩthĩwa ĩtonya kũkwatĩkana kwa ithyomo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
Wĩa wa kũalyũla. Mwambĩĩonĩ Mbivilia yaandĩkĩtwe na Kĩevelania, Kĩalamu, na Kĩkiliki. Kwoou, no andũ anini maĩ matonya kũsoma Mbivilia. Nĩ kana andũ aingĩ makwate Mbivilia na kĩthyomo kyoo, aalyũli nĩmeekĩĩte kĩthito kingĩ kũmĩalyũla. Kĩthito kyoo nĩkĩthĩĩtwe na mosyao maseo nũndũ Mbivilia nĩalyũlĩtwe yĩ nima kana yĩ nusu kwa ithyomo ta 2,700. Ũu nĩkwonany'a kana andũ 90 ĩũlũ wa 100 no masome kĩlungu kĩna kya Mbivilia kwa kĩthyomo kyoo.
Wĩa wa kumĩthya. Mbivilia sya mbee syaandĩkawa syĩndũnĩ itekalaa kwa ĩvinda ĩasa ta ithuma na makangaa. Nĩ kana andũ aingĩ makwate ũvoo ũsu, maũndũ asu maumĩĩaw'a ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ, na wĩa ũsu wendaa mũndũ ethĩwe e metho mũno nĩ kana ndakavĩtũũkany'e. Mavuku asu maumĩĩw'a mathooaw'a mbesa mbingĩ, na no andũ anini maĩ matonya kũmathooa. Ĩndĩ ĩla masinĩ ya kumĩthya mavuku ya Gutenberg yambĩĩie kũtũmĩwa myaka mbee wa 550 mĩvĩtu, andũ aingĩ nĩmakwatie Mbivilia. Kwosana na livoti ĩmwe, Mbivilia mbee wa mbilioni itano yĩ nima kana yĩ nusu ninenganĩtwe.
Vaiĩ ĩvuku yĩngĩ ya ndĩni yĩtonya kũelekanw'a na Mbivilia maũndũnĩ asu. Kwa w'o Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku tũtonya kũelewa. Ĩndĩ o na kau ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kũmĩelewa, no ũtetheew'e ũkamĩmanya. Ũtonya kũkwata ũtethyo ũsu va? Na ũtonya kũtetheka ata waelewa Mbivilia? Kĩlungu kĩla kĩatĩĩe nĩkĩeleetye maũndũ asu.

For this reason, the Bible is a very old book. Was it written accurately? Tell me about writing in the Middle East for about 3,500 years ago. It may be that we understand this thing, our years are like the ancient Chinese dynasty of Shang which flourished, and the teachings of Buddha tell us about India for about 2,500 years ago, ours are 1,000 years earlier than the Bible being written.—See the box entitled "What the Bible Says."
The Bible is strengthened by its evidence for truth
It may be a book that speaks to people, and its message has been preserved well over time, and its corners have been preserved so that it can speak. The Bible is true. It strengthens its evidence for truth for people to believe.
For example, they ask, 'Are people deceived?' For many years people have believed in the strength of their own wisdom, but they fail to grasp it. The Bible strengthens your wisdom, making it more precious than the wisdom of the Creator. This teaching is now bringing the meaning of 'Creator,' billions of years ago, things that were not created together with data, and a group of data. (Genesis 1:1) And it brings the thing that was shown to those ancient people, a great thing that was not created, and the thing people are deceived by and finally understand the purpose of God throughout all things.
IT WAS WRITTEN IN A RELIABLE WAY
The Bible helps us to know what we need to know when we are troubled. These ways are available to see. The things that are found in them are like these ways that are available to see.
In fact, the Bible was written with simple language and clarity. Many people used many languages and styles, but the Bible uses simple language to make it clear. Other things that are styled are brought by style, but we use it every day.
For example, Jesus gave us many examples of simple things and about other things that people learn every day or understand in a reliable way to reach the goal. Jesus showed many examples of this teaching in the Sermon on the Mount which is written in the Book of Matthew chapters 5-7. One teacher said that this teaching is "a reliable way to teach people" and its purpose is "not to criticize things, but to organize other things we know." So read this teaching from verses 15 to 20 and realize that this is a simple teaching with language, but Jesus gave us much teaching to us.
One thing that makes the Bible unique is its consistency with everyone. The Bible is not a book of stories or myths. In fact, according to The World Book Encyclopedia, the Bible is a book that presents "the history of mankind, and many cultures" and describes "religions, morals, laws, customs, and civilizations." It is important to know what is written in this history, everything that happens, so that we can understand what is happening and the things we learn related to this life.—Proverbs 15:4.
EVERYONE NEEDS TO HAVE A HEART TO UNDERSTAND
It is possible to understand everything in the books that have been written with a heart to understand. For instance, if you have the Bible with a heart to understand it and live by it, it will be very helpful. Practicing everything in the Bible helps to connect with a heart that understands.
Ways of Translating. The Bible was originally written in Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek. However, many people now can read the Bible. Although many people have the Bible with this language, translating it has become a great challenge. This challenge is caused by the fact that the Bible has been translated into over 2,700 languages. This means that about 90 out of 100 people in the world can read some portion of the Bible in their language.
Ways of Printing. The earliest copies of the Bible were handwritten on materials such as papyrus and parchment. Though many people had access to this, information spread more and more, and this way helped someone who was previously unaware. These writings became more valuable, and many people could afford them. Since the invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg about 550 years ago, many people have obtained Bibles. According to one report, over five billion copies of the Bible have been distributed.
There are many important reasons why it is necessary to translate the Bible into different languages. Through the Bible we learn things. And if there is something you don't understand, it is explained so you can know. Can you grasp this meaning? And can you try to understand the Bible? Every language brings new things.

text:
Mũtũmwa Vaulo aeleisye kana Yeova * nĩwe 'Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe; ũla ũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe.' (2 Akolintho 1:3, 4) Kwoou Mbivilia nĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana vai mũndũ wĩsa kwasya kana ndekwenda ũtethyo wa Ngai. O na nĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana vai thĩna ũtonya kũtũkwata na Ngai akaemwa nĩ kũtũkiakisya.
Ũw'o nĩ kana no nginya twĩke maũndũ mana nĩ kenda tũkiakiw'e nĩ Ngai. Ekai tũsũanĩe ngelekany'o ĩĩ, twasye wĩ mũwau na nũkwenda kũiitwa, ndakĩtalĩ no akũiite na ndwaathi kũmwona? Mwathani Amosi akũlilye atĩĩ: "Elĩ makaendan'ya vamwe, matew'anĩte?" (Amosi 3:3) Kwoou Maandĩko matwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Mũthengeei Ngai, nake akamũthengeea inyw'ĩ."—Yakovo 4:8.
Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai akatũthengeea? Kĩtumi kya mbee nĩ kana Ngai nũtũtavĩtye mavinda maingĩ kana nĩwendaa kũtũtethya. (Sisya ĩsandũkũ yĩla yĩ ĩthangũnĩ ya 5.) Kĩtumi kya kelĩ nĩ kana ve andũ maeleetye ũndũ Ngai wamakiakiisye, amwe me thayũ na angĩ nĩmakwie.
O tondũ andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ mamanthaa ũtethyo kuma kwa Ngai, now'o Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti wendaa ũtethyo nũndũ wa mathĩna ala mamũkwatĩte. Amwĩsũvie Yeova kwa kũmwĩa atĩĩ: "Ĩw'aa wasya wa mawĩsũvano makwa, yĩla ngũkwĩkaĩla." We Ngai nĩwasũngĩie mboya sya Ndaviti? Ĩĩ nĩwamũsũngĩie, na nĩkyo kĩtumi Ndaviti waisye kana nĩwatethiw'e nĩ Ngai, na 'kwondũ wa ũu ngoo yake yatana mũno.'—Savuli 28:2, 7.
KĨANDA KYA YESŨ KYA KŨKIAKISYA ONTHE ALA MAMETAA
Ngai nĩwendaa Yesũ eĩthĩwa na kĩanda kya kũkiakisya andũ. Amwe katĩ wa mawĩa maingĩ ala Ngai wendaa Yesũ eanĩsye nĩ 'kwova ala me na ngoo ndũlĩku' na 'kũkiakisya onthe ala mametaa.' (Isaia 61:1, 2) O tondũ kwathanĩtwe, Yesũ nĩwendeeaw'a mũno nĩ kũtetheesya andũ ala 'mathĩnĩaa wĩa na maĩ na mĩio mĩito.'—Mathayo 11:28-30.
Yesũ nĩwakiakiasya andũ kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwamataa, akameka nesa, na ve mavinda angĩ wavoasya ala awau. Mũthenya ũmwe mũndũ wawaĩte mangũ amwĩsũvie Yesũ na amwĩa atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa nũkwenda, nũtonya kũnthesya." Yesũ nĩweew'ĩie mũndũ ũsu tei na amwĩa atĩĩ: "Nĩngwenda; ĩthĩwa mũtheu." (Maliko 1:40, 41) Na mũndũ ũsu avoa mangũ vau kwa vau.
Ũmũnthĩ, Mwana wa Ngai nde kũũ nthĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũtũkiakisya. Ĩndĩ Ĩthe wake, Yeova, "Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe," nũendeee kũtetheesya ala mekwenda kũkiakiw'a. (2 Akolintho 1:3) Ekai twone nzĩa inyia nene ila Ngai ũtũmĩaa kũkiakisya andũ.
Mbivilia. "Maũndũ o na meva ala mambie kũandĩkwa, nĩmaandĩkiwe nũndũ wa kũtũmanyĩasya, nĩ kana ũndũ wa wũmĩĩsyo na ũkiakisyo wa maandĩko twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo."—Alomi 15:4.
Veva Mũtheu wa Ngai. Ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ Yesũ amina kũawa, kĩkundi kyonthe kya Kĩklĩsto nĩkyeethĩiwe na ĩvinda ya mũuo. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ wa 'kũendeea kũmũkĩa Mwĩaĩi, na kũkiakiw'a nĩ veva mũtheu.' (Meko ma Atũmwa 9:31) Veva mũtheu, ũla nĩw'o vinya wa Ngai ũla ũtũmĩaa kwĩka maũndũ, wĩ ũtonyi mwingĩ mũno. Ngai no atũmĩe veva mũtheu kũkiakisya mũndũ, o na ethĩwa e na thĩna wĩana ata.
Mboya. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũikemakĩe kwa ũndũ o na wĩva." Na kwoou vandũ va kwĩmakĩa, yonanĩtye kana twaĩle 'kwĩsũvana vamwe na kũtũnga mũvea. Na mũuo wa Ngai, ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe, ũkasũvĩaa ngoo sitũ na mosũanĩo maitũ nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ.'—Avilivi 4:6, 7.
Aklĩsto Ala Angĩ methĩawa me anyanya ma w'o tũtonya kũmekwatya matũkiakisye ĩla twĩ na mathĩna. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aeleisye kana Aklĩsto ala angĩ maĩ anyanyae na 'nĩmamũkiakiisye' mavindanĩ ma 'thĩna na ũnyamao.'—Akolosai 4:11; 1 Athesalonika 3:7.
Ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa ũisaanĩw'a ũndũ maũndũ asu mawetwa matonya kũtethya mũndũ. Ekai twone ũndũ andũ amwe meekie ĩtina wa kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna ala mawetiwe kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩvĩtu. O tondũ tũkwona ngelekany'onĩ isu, o naku no wĩyonee ũndũ Yeova wĩanĩasya watho ũũ: "Ta ũla ũkiakiaw'a nĩ nyinyia, now'o ngamũkiakisya."—Isaia 66:13.

translation:
The apostle Paul explained that Jehovah * is the 'God of all comfort; the Father of all compassion.' (2 Corinthians 1:3, 4) Through the Bible we learn how a person can draw near to God and find comfort. And we learn that we have the privilege of having a close relationship with God because he comforts us.
That is why we should always be willing to share what we know about God with others. Imagine that someone lost a valuable item—would we not try to help him find it, especially if we knew where it was? The prophet Amos asked: "Will two walk together unless they have agreed?" (Amos 3:3) Similarly, the Scriptures tell us: "Draw close to God, and he will draw close to you."—James 4:8.
But how can we be sure that God will draw close to us? One reason is that God has given us many provisions showing his desire to comfort us. (See the box "What Can Comfort Us?") Another reason is that people often respond favorably when told about God's comfort, some accepting it readily and others needing more time.
Yet, despite the fact that many people need comfort from God, King David once desperately sought comfort from an improper source. He turned to spiritism, appealing to Samuel, saying: "Bring up Saul, please, that I may consult him." But did God approve of David's course? No, he disapproved, and this is why David was later told that his request was foolish and reckless.—1 Samuel 28:2, 7.
JESUS' EXAMPLE OF COMFORTING ALL PEOPLE
God sent Jesus with the purpose of comforting people. On numerous occasions, God foretold that Jesus would be one who would 'bind up the brokenhearted' and 'comfort all those mourning.' (Isaiah 61:1, 2) And true to prophecy, Jesus willingly comforted people who were 'burdened and oppressed.'—Matthew 11:28-30.
Jesus comforted people in ways that touched their hearts. For example, he healed them, fed them, and gave them hope. On one occasion, a leper approached Jesus and begged him, saying: "If you wish, you can make me clean." Jesus stretched out his hand and touched the man, saying: "I want to; be cleansed." (Mark 1:40, 41) And immediately the man was made clean.
Therefore, the Son of God knew how to provide genuine comfort. Our heavenly Father, Jehovah, "the God of all comfort," continues to comfort us through his Word and his organization. (2 Corinthians 1:3) Let us see how we can imitate God in comforting others.
The Bible. "All the Scriptures are inspired by God and beneficial for teaching, for reproving, or for correcting, with the purpose of training people in righteousness."—2 Timothy 3:16.
Give Credit to God. When Jesus performed miracles, the entire congregation of Christians glorified God with a spirit of gratitude. Why? Because they understood that 'continuously seeking the favor of Jehovah and being comforted is an expression of worship.' (Acts 9:31) Give credit to God, for it is his holy spirit that empowers us to do good things, and it has far more effect than we realize. God uses his holy spirit to comfort individuals, and he wants us to feel free to ask him to do so.
Be Empathetic. The Bible says: "Become imitators of those who show faith and are patient." And when we imitate them, let us remember whether we have 'become sympathetic toward one another, loving brothers, tenderly compassionate, humble in mind.'—1 Peter 3:8, 9.
Christians Also Need Encouragement. Sometimes fellow Christians may experience trials that discourage them. The apostle Paul expressed appreciation for those who encouraged him and said that they refreshed his soul.—Colossians 4:11; 1 Thessalonians 3:7.
We Can Be Comforted. We can be strengthened by knowing that others have faced similar difficulties. Let us remember how some people were moved to tears because of the encouragement they received from fellow believers. So, while we appreciate the help we receive, let us also recognize what Jehovah does for us: "As someone comforts you, so I will comfort you."—Isaiah 66:13.
^ par. 3 The Bible identifies God's name as Jehovah.

Twĩ thayũ, na nĩtũũthi, na twĩ na mwĩkalĩle witũ nthĩnĩ [wa Ngai].—Meko 17:28.
Nĩ maũndũ maingĩ Yeova ũtwĩkĩte ala maĩle kũtuma tũmũtũngĩa mũvea! Mbee, nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ ũũ twĩ naw'o, na kethĩwa ti vake tũyĩthĩwa vo, o na tũyĩthĩwa tũithi. Nũtũnengete mũthĩnzĩo wa vata vyũ, naw'o nĩ yĩla ĩvuku yake, Mbivilia. O tondũ ala Aklĩsto ma Thesalonika moosie ndeto ya Ngai na mamĩtĩkĩla, o naitũ nĩtũtanaa kwĩtĩkĩla Mbivilia ta ũtũmane Ngai ũtũandĩkĩe. (1 Ath. 2:13) Kwa ũtethyo wa Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia, nĩtũkwatĩte mwanya wa kũmũthengeea Yeova, nake nĩwosete ĩtambya ya kũtũthengeea. (Yak. 4:8) Nĩ ndaĩa nene mũno kwona Asa witũ atwĩtĩkĩlĩtye twĩthĩwe ũseũvyonĩ wake. Asu nĩ moathimo matumaa tũtana ta kĩ! Ũtanu ta ũsu nĩw'o mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli waĩ naw'o ĩla wainie Savuli ĩno: "Mũtũngĩei Yeova mũvea; nũndũ nĩ mũseo; nũndũ ũseo wake wĩ wendo nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene." (Sav. 136:1) Kĩsyokeo kĩĩ, "ũseo wake wĩ wendo nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene," kyonekaa mavinda 26 nthĩnĩ wa Savuli ĩsu ya 136. Twekala tũlũmanĩtye na Yeova na ũseũvyo wake, ndeto isu iseũvĩte ũu ikeanĩa ngalĩkonĩ ĩ yitũ nĩkwĩthĩwa tũkekala tene na tene! w16.11 3:18, 19
Nũndũ wa mũndũ ũmwe naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ; na kwa ũu kĩkw'ũ kyavikĩa andũ onthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa onthe nĩmeekie naĩ.—Alo. 5:12.
Mũsoa ũsu ũtũngĩlĩĩlwe mũno ĩvukunĩ Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩ laisi ũkethĩa nĩtũsomaa ĩandĩko ya Alomi 5:12 ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya na syana sitũ kana andũ angĩ kĩlungu kya 3, 5 na kya 6. Mavindanĩ ta asu no kwĩthĩwa tũtũmĩaa mũsoa ũsu kũtetheesya amanyĩw'a maitũ maelewe nĩkĩ Ngai woombie nthĩ, nĩkĩ twĩ na vata wa wovosyo, na kwĩthĩawa ata ĩla mũndũ wakw'a. Ĩndĩ nĩ mavinda meana ũsũanĩaa ũndũ ĩandĩko yĩu ya Alomi 5:12 yaĩle kũũtetheesya we mwene wĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, wĩthĩwe na meko ala mamwendeeasya, na ũyĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu wa maũndũ ala ũtwathĩte? Kĩla ũmwe witũ aĩle kwĩkalaa esĩ kana twĩ ene naĩ. Kĩla mũthenya nĩtũvĩtasya. Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kana Ngai nũlilikanaa kana twĩ kĩtoo, na we ethĩawa eyũmbanĩtye kũtwĩw'ĩa ĩnee. (Sav. 103:13, 14) Nĩkyo kĩtumi nthĩnĩ wa ĩla mboya ya Mwĩaĩi, Yesũ watũmanyĩisye kũvoyaa atĩĩ: "Ũtũekee naĩ sitũ." (Luka 11:2-4) Na kwoou ĩla Ngai watũekea mavĩtyo maitũ vayĩthĩawa vata wa kũendeea kũmaeka matũthĩny'e kĩlĩko. Ĩndĩ kwaekai twone vatonyeka ata Ngai atũekee. w16.12 1:1-3
Ala mavikĩlaa mwĩĩ malilikanaa maũndũ ma mwĩĩ.—Alo. 8:5.
Waĩ ũndũ wa vata Aklĩsto ma Lomi meyĩosye mamanye ilĩko syoo syalũmĩte maũndũnĩ meva. Mo no methĩwe mendete mũno kana masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ "maũndũ ma mwĩĩ"? O naitũ twĩ na vata wa kwĩyĩosya. Nĩ maũndũ meva twendete mũno, na nĩ kyaũ tũneeneaa mavinda maingĩ? Nĩ ũndũ wĩva twonaa wĩ wa vata? Amwe meyĩosya no methĩe kaĩ kĩla mendete mũno nĩ kũsama mbinyu syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kwanakavya nyũmba syoo, kũmantha mĩsono myeũ ya ngũa, kwĩka mĩvango ya viasala, kũthi kũtembea kũndũ, na maũndũ angĩ ta asu. Maũndũ asu ti mathũku nũndũ nĩ maũndũ andũ mekaa kĩla mũthenya. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe Yesũ nĩwaseũvisye mbinyu, na ve ĩvinda Vaulo weeie Timotheo anyusae "mbinyu nini." (1 Tim. 5:23; Yoa. 2:3-11) Ĩndĩ mo Yesũ na Vaulo nĩmoonaa ũnywi wa mbinyu taw'o ũndũ ũla mũnene kwoo? Ũsu nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mendete mũno na matindĩaa kũneenea? Aiee. Nata naitũ? Nĩ kyaũ twendete mũno kwĩka? w16.12 2:5, 10, 11

And Abraham prospered, and he became great, and he had silver and gold and cattle [of God].—Genesis 17:28.
Indeed, Jehovah has shown us much kindness in allowing us to make progress! So, let us continue to prosper together, and may we always be grateful, and may we be truthful. Let us appreciate the value of wisdom, and it is a precious treasure, the Bible. And just as the Thessalonian Christians accepted God's message with joy and conviction, so let us zealously study the Bible so that God may approve of us. (1 Thess. 2:13) By means of God's Word, the Bible, we can draw close to Jehovah, and He will draw close to us. (James 4:8) I deeply appreciate how our brother Asa encouraged us to prosper spiritually. Asa was an example showing us how to act! Today, as in the past, there is one writer who inspired Saul and also showed Saul this: "Give thanks to Jehovah generously; for his loving-kindness is enduring forever." (Ps. 136:1) Appropriately, "his loving-kindness is enduring forever" appears 26 times in Psalm 136. Let us remain united with Jehovah and his generosity, and may this constant reminder help us to remain steadfast forever! w16.11 3:18, 19
And when anyone commits a sin, it affects him, and often it affects others, resulting in everyone being saddened.—Acts 5:12.
This question may arise: Can Bible teachings help us to cope? For example, let us read Acts 5:12 and see how it can comfort young ones or others who are experiencing difficulties in chapters 3, 5, and 6. Undoubtedly, this question will motivate us to use this question to explain God's love for us, his forgiveness, and his willingness to forgive anyone. Indeed, this question helps us understand why the apostle Paul wrote: "God commended his love toward us, while we were yet sinners." (Rom. 5:8) Is this not a reason to meditate on what Acts 5:12 teaches about showing compassion to those who have made mistakes and who are trying to get back Jehovah's favor, who are repentant, and who are seeking forgiveness? Let each of us examine himself or ourselves. Every day we make progress. Indeed, we trust that God is understanding and merciful, and he is willing to help us. (Ps. 103:13, 14) That is why Jesus taught us to pray: "Lead us not into temptation." (Luke 11:2-4) And we know that God answers our prayers in line with his purpose. Indeed, let us always remember that God answers our prayers. w16.12 1:1-3
But some may feel inadequate to meet their own needs.—Acts 8:5.
Why do some Christians find it difficult to apply what they learn from the Bible? Perhaps they think that they are too old or that they lack the necessary qualities to succeed in "their own affairs." But let us be realistic. Are these really big problems, or are they excuses? Is it true that we need more abilities than we already have? What can we do to overcome this feeling of inadequacy? Some may feel discouraged because of physical limitations, health problems, financial pressures, fear of failure, and so forth. These things are not unique to us. For instance, Jesus used illustrations, and Paul asked Timothy to "stop drinking wine." (1 Tim. 5:23; John 2:3-11) So both Jesus and Paul recognized that there are certain habits that can hinder spiritual progress. Does this mean that such habits are necessarily serious problems? No. Why not? Because we can overcome them if we try. w16.12 2:5, 10, 11

NZA wa ngalawa, andũ maendeeie na mwĩkalo woo o ta tene. Mayaĩ maaĩsa kũĩkĩĩa kana Kĩw'ũ Kingĩ kĩkooka. No nginya methĩwe mathekeeaa Noa kũthonoka vu mbeenĩ. Ĩndĩ o mĩtũkĩ nĩmaekie kũmũthekeea.
Kwa kaveny'a kĩw'ũ nĩkyambĩlĩĩilye kwĩtĩka. Kyetĩkie kuma matunĩ o tondũ wĩtaa kĩw'ũ kuma ndoonĩ. Noa awetete w'o! Ĩndĩ yu vaiĩ mũndũ ona wĩva waĩ atonya kũlika ngalawanĩ, nũndũ ĩvinda ya kũlika yaĩ ĩvĩtu. Mũomo waĩ mũvinge ki nĩ Yeova.
O mĩtũkĩ nthĩ yonthe ĩla ndindimalu nĩyavw'ĩkiwe nĩ kĩw'ũ. Kĩw'ũ kyeethĩiwe o tondũ woonaa mbũsĩ nene. Nĩkyasukumie itĩ na kyavingilitya nthũngũ sya mavia, na kyaete kĩuumo kĩnene. Andũ nĩmakwatiwe nĩ w'ĩa. Malĩsile kũla kũtũlangu. Mwa! Keka tyo mamwĩthukĩĩisye Noa na kũlika ngalawanĩ yĩla mũomo waĩ mũvingũe! Ĩndĩ kũvikĩa yu maĩ aselee mũno.
Kĩw'ũ nĩkyaendeeie na kwingĩva na kwambatĩĩa. Kyetĩkie kuma yayayanĩ mĩthenya 40 na motukũ 40. Nĩkyaendeeie kwambata na kyavw'ĩka nguumo wa iĩma, na o mĩtũkĩ ĩima ila ndaasa mũno syavw'ĩkwa. Kwoou o tondũ Ngai waĩtye, andũ onthe ala maĩ nza wa ngalawa nĩmakwie o vamwe na nyamũ. Ĩndĩ kyonthe kĩla kyaĩ nthĩnĩ wa ngalawa kĩyaĩ mũisyonĩ.
Noa na ana make nĩmatethisye wĩa mũseo wa kwaka ngalawa. Kĩw'ũ nĩkyamyũkĩlilye na kyamĩthambalalya. Na ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe mbua yakya na syũa yambĩĩa kwaa. Waĩ ũndũ wa ũsengy'o ta kĩ! Kwaĩ ũkanga o ũmwe wausĩe kĩla vandũ. No ngalawa yoka yoonekaa ĩthambalele ũkanganĩ.
Ala mamũndũ mayaĩ vo ĩngĩ. Mayaĩ vo ĩngĩ kũũmĩsya andũ. Onthe maĩ manakw'a, o vamwe na aainyia moo na andũ ala angĩ athũku. Ĩndĩ kweethĩiwe ata kwa aaĩthe moo?
Aaĩthe ma mamũndũ asu mayaĩ andũ taitũ. Maĩ alaĩka ala mookĩte kwĩkala ta andũ kũũ nthĩ. Na ĩndĩ yĩla Kĩw'ũ Kingĩ kyookie, mo mayaakw'a vamwe na andũ ala angĩ. Nĩmaekie kũtũmĩa ĩla mĩĩ ya kĩmũndũ maĩ maneeseũvĩsya, na ĩndĩ masyoka ĩtunĩ me alaĩka. Ĩndĩ mayaaĩtĩkĩlw'a mavulane na alaĩka ala angĩ ewi ma Ngai. Kwoou nĩ matw'ĩkie alaĩka ma Satani. Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia alaĩka asu metawa ndaimoni.
Na Ngai ĩndĩ aete kĩuutani, na kĩla kĩw'ũ kingĩ kyambĩĩa kũng'ala. Myei ĩtano yathela ngalawa nĩyatw'ĩĩkanie kĩĩmanĩ ĩũlũ. Mĩthenya mingĩ nĩyathelile, na ala maĩ ngalawanĩ nĩmaĩ matonya kũlilya nza na kwona mĩthya ya iĩma. Kĩw'ũ nĩkyaendeeie o na kũng'ala.
Na ĩndĩ Noa alekya nyũnyi ĩmwe nziũ yĩtawa ngũngũũ kuma ngalawanĩ. Yaũlũkaa ĩkathi kwa kavinda na ĩisyoka, nũndũ ndyaaona vandũ vaseo va kũvũĩla. Yaendeeie na kwĩka ũu na kĩla ĩvinda yasyoka, yavũĩlaa ĩũlũ wa ngalawa
Noa nĩwendaa kũmanya kana kĩw'ũ nĩkĩng'alu vyũ, kwoou ivĩnda yĩĩ yĩngĩ atũma ĩvũĩ kuma ngalawanĩ. Na ĩvũĩ o nayo yasyoka nũndũ yĩyaaona vandũ va kwĩkala. Noa asyoka ayĩtũma ĩngĩ ĩvinda ya kelĩ, na yasyoka yĩna ĩtũ ya mũthata. Kwoou Noa amanya kana kĩw'ũ nĩkĩng'alu. Yĩla watũmie ĩvũĩ ĩvinda ya katatũ, yĩyaamũsyokea nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩyoonie vandũ vomũ va kwĩkala.
Yu ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwaneenie na Noa na amwĩa: 'Uma ngalawanĩ. Umya andũ maku onthe na nyamũ syonthe ila wĩnasyo.' Mekalĩte ngalawanĩ mwaka mũima na kĩndũ. Kwoou no tũtate kũsũanĩa ũndũ matanie yĩla maumaalile nza ĩngĩ na kwĩthĩwa me thayũ!
Mwambĩlĩlyo 7:10-24; 8:1-17; 1 Vetelo 3:19, 20.
Makũlyo
- Nĩkĩ kũyaĩ mũndũ waĩ atonya kũlika ngalawanĩ mbua yambĩĩa kua?
- Yeova auisye mbua mĩthenya na motukũ meana, na kĩw'ũ kĩu kyaĩ na ũliku wĩana ata?
- Ngalawa yeekie ata kĩw'ũ kyambĩĩa kũvw'ĩka nthĩ?
- Ala mamũndũ manene nĩmavonokie kĩla Kĩw'ũ Kingĩ, na kweethĩiwe ata ĩũlũ wa aaĩthe moo?
- Ĩtina wa myei ĩtano ngalawa yeekie ata?
- Noa alekilye ngũngũũ kuma ngalawanĩ nĩkĩ?
- Noa amanyie ata kana kĩw'ũ nĩkĩng'alu vyũ?
- Ngai amwĩie Noa ata ĩtina wa Noa na mũsyĩ wake kwĩkala ngalawanĩ mwaka mũima na kĩndũ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 7:10-24.
Mathayũ maanangiwe kwa kĩthimo kĩana ata ĩũlũ wa nthĩ? (Mwa. 7:23)
Kĩla Kĩw'ũ Kingĩ kyakuie ĩvinda yĩana ata kũng'ala? (Mwa. 7:24)
- Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 8:1-17.
Mwambĩlĩlyo 8:17 yonanasya ata kana Yeova ndaaekana na kĩeleelo kyake kũmyelekela nthĩ? (Mwa. 1:22)
- Soma 1 Vetelo 3:19, 20.
Alaĩka asu mate ewi masyoka ĩtunĩ, makwatie ũsilĩlo mwaũ? (Yuta 6)
Ũvoo ũsu wa Noa na mũsyĩ wake ũtwongelaa vinya ata nthĩnĩ wa ũtonyi wa Yeova wa kũtangĩĩa andũ make? (2 Vet. 2:9)

translation:
The ark was built, and people continued with their activities as usual. Some mocked, saying the dry season would never come. But Noah obeyed God and prepared for the flood. He warned his family to be saved.
Because of God's patience, salvation is offered. Believe in the truth so that you may find God in times of trouble. Noah preached about this! He told people that a great flood was coming, but they did not listen. His heart belonged to Jehovah.
All the families on earth were destroyed by the flood. God regretted creating such wicked people, and he showed great anger. It shook the earth and caused great destruction. People were swept away by the waters. Truly, let us remember Noah and the flood which showed whose heart belongs to Him! Remember to understand these things well.
God continued with judgment and punishment. Believe in the warnings of forty days and forty nights. It continued with punishment and covered the whole surface of the earth, and all the families on earth were wiped out together. This is because God is righteous, and all people who lived during the time of the ark perished together. All this happened because of the wickedness of the ark.
Noah and his sons went inside the ark to save themselves. God remembered them and protected them. After forty days, a bird flew out and returned. What a wonderful thing it is! Because someone cares for everyone. But the ark looked like a ruin.
But some people still don't believe. They don't want to turn to God. Others help those who mock and join others in evil deeds. Is there anyone who will care for them?
Those people have forgotten what God did for them. Others continue to live without fearing God. And when God's anger comes, they will perish along with others in evil deeds. It seems like they are trying to provoke God, and their end will be terrible. It is possible to be deceived by the lies of others and fall into the power of Satan. The teachings of the Bible say that those people worship demons.
And God has shown mercy, and every act of God protects us. Five years passed, and the flood was completely cleansed from the earth. Many days have passed, and now the land is fertile enough to grow crops and see the beauty of the earth. God continues to protect us.
And Noah planted a vineyard and drank wine from it. He became drunk and lay naked in his tent. His son saw him and told others. But the ark looked like a ruin.
Noah knew whether God would punish them again, so he sent out a raven to see if the water had receded. The raven went out and kept flying until it found dry land.
Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had subsided, and the dove returned because there was no place to rest its foot. After seven days, he sent out another dove, and it came back with an olive branch in its beak, showing that the land was recovering. Noah knew that God would not punish them again. He sent out a dove again after three days, and it did not return, indicating that the land was habitable.
Then God made a covenant with Noah and said, "I will bring a flood upon the earth. I will destroy all living things except those who are with you." The flood lasted for a year and ten days. But let us remember the lessons learned from this event and avoid repeating the mistakes of the past!
Luke 7:10-24; 8:1-17; 1 Peter 3:19, 20.
Questions
- Is it possible for someone to survive the flood if they are righteous?
- Did Jehovah show mercy during those days and nights, and does God still show mercy today?
- Will the flood ever happen again, and why?
- What great people were saved during the Flood, and how can we learn from their example?
- What happened during the five years after the flood?
- Why did Noah build the ark?
- Did Noah know that God would not punish them again?
- Did God tell Noah and his family to live in the ark for a year and ten days?
Further Questions
- Read Luke 7:10-24.
Did Jesus perform miracles with power and authority? (Lu. 7:23)
Does the Kingdom of God come with observable signs? (Lu. 7:24)
- Read Luke 8:1-17.
Does Luke 8:17 ask whether Jehovah is faithful to His purpose of saving people? (Ge. 1:22)
- Read 1 Peter 3:19, 20.
How can we apply the lesson of Noah's time to our lives today? (Ex. 6)
What does Noah and his family's experience teach us about Jehovah's patience in dealing with mankind? (2 Pe. 2:9)

ĨLA Mbesaleli na Ooliavu maĩ Misili, nĩmamanyĩĩte kwona myako ĩyakwa. Me ngombo kũu moombĩthĩtw'e mavali maingĩ ũkethĩa o na mayenda kũlilikana ũ wĩa. Ĩndĩ ũseo kyu kyaĩ kyavĩtũkie. Kĩla kyaĩ mbee woo yu nĩ wĩa mũnene ũla manengiwe mwakonĩ wa yĩla ĩeema, na wĩa ũsu wesie kũtuma matw'ĩka mavundi ma syĩndũ sya vata mũno. (Kuma 31:1-11) Ĩndĩ o na maseũvĩtye syĩndũ iseũvĩte ũu, no anini mũno mesaa kwona imwe sya syĩndũ isu. Kyu nĩkyesaa kũtuma makw'a ngoo? Nĩ vaĩ thĩna wĩa woo ũemete kwoneka nĩ andũ aingĩ? Nĩvethĩwa thĩna wĩa waku ũkaema kwoneka nĩ angĩ?
WĨA MŨSEO VYŨ ĨNDĨ WOONEKIE NO AVŨTHŨ
Syĩndũ imwe syaseũvĩtw'e sya vau ĩeemanĩ syaĩ sya thooa mũnene mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ala akeluvi ma thaavu maĩ ĩũlũ wa yĩla ĩsandũkũ ya ũtianĩo. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye maĩ na "ũtheu mũtisu." (Aevl. 9:5) Kwasũanĩa ũndũ maanakavĩte maseũvĩtw'e na thaavu mũtue!—Kuma 37:7-9.
Syĩndũ ila syaseũvĩtw'e nĩ Mbesaleli na Ooliavu ikesa kwoneka ũmũnthĩ, syĩthĩwa syaĩlĩte kwiwa kula kwiawa syĩndũ sya tene ila sya thooa mũnene mũno nĩ kana ikonekaa nĩ andũ na makaitanĩa mũno. Ĩndĩ wĩona ta ve andũ aingĩ moonie ũseo wasyo ĩla Mbesaleli na Ooliavu maminie kũiseũvya? Ala akeluvi maiĩtwe vala Vandũ Vatheu Mbee, na kwoou moonekaa nĩ mũthembi mũnene e weka ĩla wesa kũlika vau Mũthenya wa Wĩw'anĩthyo wavika, naw'o mũthenya ũsu weethĩawa o ĩmwe kwa mwaka. (Aevl. 9:6, 7) Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, no andũ anini mũno maaona akeluvi asu.
ĨKALAA WĨ MWĨANĨE O NA WAEMA KŨKATHWA NĨ ANDŨ AINGĨ
Keka nue Mbesaleli na Ooliavu na ũithũkũma na kĩthito ũseũvye syĩndũ iseũvĩte ũu, wĩw'a ata wesa kũmanya kana syoonekie nĩ andũ anini vyũ? Matukũ aa andũ mamanyaa nĩmeeka nesa ĩla makathwa nĩ andũ angĩ. Kĩu nĩ takyo kĩthimi kya kũsisya wĩa woo ũseũvĩte ata. Ĩndĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova mayĩilyĩ ũu. O ta Mbesaleli na Ooliavu, nĩtwĩanĩawa ĩla tweeka kwenda kwa Yeova na twamanya kana nĩweetĩkĩla kĩla tweeka.
Ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmavoyaa nĩ kana mendeesye andũ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ amanyĩisye andũ kana maĩle kũvoyaa kuma ngoonĩ mateteele makathwe nĩ ala methukĩĩsye. Ũseo wa kwĩka ũu nĩ wĩva? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Ĩthe waku ũla wonaa kĩmbithĩnĩ akakũĩva." (Mt. 6:5, 6) Kwoou ũndũ ũla wa vata ti ũndũ andũ meũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mboya sitũ, ĩndĩ nĩ ũndũ Yeova ũsyonaa. Woni wake nĩw'o ũtumaa mboya sitũ syĩthĩwa syĩ sya vata. O na ĩla tũkwĩka kĩndũ o na kĩva ũthũkũminĩ wake, woni wake now'o wa vata. Ũthũkũmi witũ ndũtw'ĩkaa nĩ mũseo atĩ nũndũ andũ aingĩ nĩmatũkatha, ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩwamwendeesya Yeova, "ũla wonaa kĩmbithĩnĩ."
Ĩla ĩeema yathelile, kwaendie ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana mũumbĩ 'nĩwavw'ĩkie yĩla ĩeema ya kũmbanĩa, na ũtheu mũtisu wa Yeova wausũa ũla wĩkalo.' (Kuma 40:34) Ũndũ ũsu woonanisye nesa vyũ kana Yeova nĩweetĩkĩlile wĩa wa Mbesaleli na Ooliavu. We wĩsũanĩa ta meewie ata ĩla Yeova woonanisye nĩweetĩkĩla wĩa woo? O na kau masyĩtwa moo mayaavanĩĩwa syĩndũnĩ ila maseũvisye, no nginya methĩwe matanie mũno ĩla mamanyie kana Ngai nĩwaathimie kĩthito kyoo. (Nth. 10:22) Ĩtina wa myaka kauta, no nginya methĩwe matanaa mũno ngoonĩ moona kana syĩndũ ila maseũvisye no syaendeee kũtũmĩwa ũthaithinĩ wa w'o. Ĩla Mbesaleli na Ooliavu makathayũũkw'a, makatana mũno kũmanya kana yĩla ĩeema nĩyaendeeie kũtũmĩwa kũmũthaitha Yeova kwa myaka ta 500!
Kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ, ve andũ matethasya mawĩa me kĩvathũkany'o, ta kũseũvya sinema sya tũtuni, kũsola mavisa, kũseũvya mbathi, kũkũna visa, na kũalyũla. Masyĩtwa ma ala matethasya mawĩa asu maitangaasawa. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu no twasye kana vai mũndũ wonaa wĩa ũla matethasya. Ũu now'o vailyĩ ikundinĩ mbee wa 110,000 nthĩ yonthe. Wĩa mwingĩ ũla ũtethaw'a ikundinĩ isu ndwonekaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, we nũũ wonaa mwana-a-asa ũla wĩkaa ĩsavu ya kĩkundi aitethya wĩa wake mũthya wa mwei? Nũũ ũla wonaa mũandĩki wa kĩkundi aiseũvya livoti ya ũtavany'a ya kĩkundi kyonthe? Na nũũ ũla wonaa mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa aitũngĩĩa kũla kwanangĩku Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ?
Mbesaleli na Ooliavu maikw'a mayaĩ na ikombe kana mĩthĩnzĩo ĩngĩ ta ĩsu matonya kwĩyona nayo nũndũ wa wĩa mũseo mũno ũla matethetye. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Yeova nĩweetĩkĩlĩte wĩa woo, kĩu nĩkyo kyaĩ kya vata kwĩ mũthĩnzĩo o na wĩva. Tũi na nzika kana Yeova nĩwoonie wĩa woo. Ekai ĩndĩ tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yoo kwa kũtethasya wĩa na ngenda na twĩnyivĩtye.

But the skilled craftsman and the artist, with missiles, have made my heart know its skill. My hands have built many strong walls for a fortress and beautiful houses to dwell in. I have found wisdom, and I know all kinds of knowledge. Every wise person will be like a great tree planted by the waters of a flowing river, which does not wither in times of drought, and whose leaves remain green to produce abundant fruit. (Proverbs 31:1-11) But also, many things are valuable, and they are often seen by others. Why then should we strive to make them known? Is it because we want to be admired by many people? Should we be proud of what we can accomplish to be praised by others?
WHAT WISDOM IS FOR AND ITS VALUE
Some things are valued because they are excellent works of art. For example, consider the exquisite carvings on ivory in the ancient Egyptian era. The apostle Paul referred to it as "skillful craftsmanship." (Acts 9:5) Consider how much value is placed on skillful work!—Proverbs 37:7-9.
These things, however, are valued by the skilled craftsman and the artist to appear humble, so they do not boast about their skills or show off their excellence to others. But why do many people admire the skill of the craftsman and the artist? Consider the exquisite carvings made by the ancient Egyptians, and how they were displayed in large temples to impress visitors, and this display was repeated annually. (Acts 9:6, 7) Therefore, many people appreciate such carvings.
LET US BE HUMBLE AND NOT BE PRAISED BY PEOPLE
Let us, like the skilled craftsman and the artist, with humility and sincerity, value the things we do, and let us not seek to be admired by others. Many people realize that they are being praised by others. It is not right to seek praise for what has been done. Let those who serve Jehovah teach us this. Like the skilled craftsman and the artist, let us go to Jehovah and ask him if we are pleasing him in everything we do.
For Jesus knew what was in the hearts of men and whether they were sincere. And Jesus showed people that it is wrong to seek glory from men because of the attention they receive from others. What is the reason for this? The Bible says: "When you pray, do not be like hypocrites." (Matt. 6:5, 6) This thing that people do is not something that pleases God, but it is something that Jehovah sees. He sees our motives when we pray. And if we pray with a bad motive, he will see it. Our prayers should be motivated by love, so that many people do not praise us, but rather we please Jehovah, saying, "Our Father."
But if a promise seems delayed, what then? The Bible says that a wise man 'watches time and circumstance,' and waits for God's appointed time. (Eccl. 8:11) This shows how much confidence we have in Jehovah, just as Abraham and Sarah had confidence in his promises. Do you wonder why Jehovah allows us to wait? Or perhaps you have already experienced some difficulties, and you feel discouraged, but remember that God has given us strength. (Phil. 10:22) Over the years, many people have felt discouraged, but they continued to trust in him. But Abraham and Sarah waited patiently, continuing to trust that the promise would come true, and they served Jehovah faithfully for about 500 years!
To help Jehovah's people spiritually, there are brothers who visit the sick, comfort those who are grieving, offer encouragement, share in the ministry, give assistance, and show hospitality. Other brothers assist in various ways to meet the needs of the congregation. Because of this, we can be sure that someone cares for us. Today, over 110,000 such full-time servants are active worldwide. Many more participate in this activity regularly. For example, does a young child in the family often help his parents with household chores? Does a secretary in the congregation volunteer to type up reports for the entire congregation? And does a young person or an adult volunteer to clean the Kingdom Hall?
Abraham and Sarah faced many trials and challenges, like sicknesses and other problems that may seem insurmountable. But because Jehovah strengthened them, they were able to endure and remain faithful. Let us therefore continue to trust in Jehovah, knowing that he will support us. Let us also remember that Jehovah hears our prayers. So let us keep praying to him and continue to preach the good news with zeal.

WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Mwĩĩtu wĩtawa Karen nĩwavika vandũ ve andũ ma mũika mekwĩtanĩthya, na ataminĩte ndatĩka ĩkũmi, ayĩw'a eetwa nĩ mũndũ mesene na aimũkũlya atĩĩ:
"Ũũngamangĩte vau ata?"
Karen aivĩndũka na ayĩthĩa nĩ mũnyanyae Jessica akwete sũva ilĩ ngunũe. Asisya sũva isu iilyĩ ta sya ũkĩ. Jessica atekwananga saa aimũnenga Karen sũva ũmwe wa ũkĩ na aimwĩa, "Naku nĩweanie, kwata kasũva kamwe wĩtanĩthye, kana kookĩa?"
Karen eenda kũlea, ĩndĩ thĩna nĩ kana Jessica nĩ mũnyanyae na Karen ndekwenda Jessica aisũanĩa ta mũsuvau. O na ĩngĩ, Karen nĩwĩsĩ kana Jessica nĩ ũmwe katĩ wa eĩtu ala aseo. Kwoou aisũanĩa kana ti ũthũku kũnyw'a ethĩwa Jessica nũtonya kwĩka ũu. Ũu ũituma Karen asũanĩa, 'Ũũ no ũkĩ, ti ũndũ ũmwe na kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila.'
We wĩka ata keka nue Karen?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
Nĩ kana wĩke ũtwi waĩle wakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu, no nginya wĩthĩwe wĩsĩ nesa wĩ mũndũ ũilyĩ ata. Ũu nĩ kwasya kana ve kĩndũ kĩ nthĩnĩ waku kĩla kĩũtetheeasya kũmanya we nue ũũ. Weethĩwa na ũmanyi ũsu, ũkeethĩawa na vinya wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi, vandũ va kwĩtĩkĩla andũ angĩ makwĩkĩe.—1 Akolintho 9:26, 27.
Ũtonya ata kũkwata vinya ũsu? Kũkwata ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyo ĩtambya ya mbee.
1 NĨ MAŨNDŨ MEVA ALA NĨ NA ŨTONYI WA KWĨANĨSYA?
Kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ maũndũ ala ũtonya kwĩanĩsya kũkaũtetheeasya wĩthĩwe ũte na nzika na maũndũ ala ũkwĩka.
NGELEKANY'O YĨ MBIVILIANĨ: Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: 'O na ngethĩwa nĩ mũndũ ũtesĩ ũneena, ũmanyinĩ ti w'o nĩilyĩ.' (2 Akolintho 11:6) Nũndũ Vaulo nĩweesĩ Maandĩko nesa, nĩweethĩawa e mũlũmu o na ĩla andũ ala angĩ mamũneenea naĩ. Ndaĩ esa kwĩtĩkĩlya mawoni mataĩle ma andũ asu matume mũĩkĩĩo wake wonza.—2 Akolintho 10:10; 11:5.
ĨYĨOSYE MWENE: Andĩka vaa ĩtheo kĩnengo wĩ nakyo kana ũndũ mũna mũseo ũtonya kwĩanĩsya.
Elesya ndaĩa ĩmwe nzeo wĩsĩ wĩ nayo. (Kwa ngelekany'o, nũthĩnĩkĩaa andũ? wĩ mũlau? wĩ wa kwĩkwatw'a? nũatĩĩaa saa nesa?)
2 NĨTHĨAWA NA MAWONZU MEVA?
O na kau no wĩthĩwe wĩ na ũtonyi wa kwĩanĩsya maũndũ maseo, kawonzu o kanini no katume ũvalũka.
NGELEKANY'O YĨ MBIVILIANĨ: Vaulo nĩweesĩ mawonzu make. Aisye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ nĩtanĩaa ĩla mĩao ya Ngai mũndũnĩ wa nthĩnĩ: ĩndĩ nĩona mwĩao wa mũthemba ũngĩ mamuthanĩ makwa, ũla wũkitaa na ũla mwĩao wĩ kĩlilikanonĩ kyakwa, na nũndavĩte ũkambĩkĩa mwĩaonĩ wa naĩ."—Alomi 7:22, 23.
ĨYĨOSYE MWENE: Nĩ mawonzu meva wĩ namo waĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito ũmasinde?
3 NĨ NA MĨVANGO YĨVA?
We no ũlĩse ngalĩnĩ na ũyĩa ndeleva aũthiũũkasye o vandũ vamwe nginya ngalĩ ĩsu ĩkesa kũthela mauta? Ku ti kũtũmĩa kĩlĩko, o na ĩngĩ, kũu nĩkwananga mbesa!
Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ? Kwĩthĩwa na mũvango mũseo nĩkũũtetheeasya ũkeanĩsya maũndũ ala ũkwenda kwĩka. Ũu nĩ kwasya kana wĩthĩawa wĩsĩ kĩla ũkwenda kwĩanĩsya na ũndũ ũkwĩka nĩ kana ũkĩanĩsye.
NGELEKANY'O YĨ MBIVILIANĨ: Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Nyie nĩsembaa, nde na nzika." (1 Akolintho 9:26) Vandũ va kũkũna maũndũ oou kĩtumbo, Vaulo aĩ na mĩvango mĩseo na nĩwamĩanĩasya.—Avilivi 3:12-14.
ĨYĨOSYE MWENE. Andĩka vaa ĩtheo maũndũ atatũ ala ũkwenda kwĩanĩsya mwaka ũũ ũatĩĩe.
4 WĨ NA MŨĨKĨĨO MŨLŨMU VYŨ?
Weethĩwa ũte na mũĩkĩĩo, ũkeethĩawa na nzika ĩla ũkwĩka motwi. Ũkaalyũkaa ta kĩmbu nĩ kana wĩw'ane na andũ ma mũika waku, na ũu nĩkwonany'a kana ndwĩyĩsĩ nesa.
Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, weethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo na maũndũ ala ũkwĩka, ũkeethĩawa wĩyĩsĩ nesa na ũtekwelelũkw'a, o na andũ ala angĩ meeka maũndũ mataĩle.
NGELEKANY'O YĨ MBIVILIANĨ: O na kau nĩvatonyeka mwathani Ndanieli akethĩwa aĩ wa mũika, "nĩwetw'ĩĩe ngoonĩ yake" kana akakwataa mĩao ya Ngai, o na kau aĩ vaasa na andũ ma mũsyĩ. (Ndanieli 1:8) Kwa kwĩka ũu, Ndanieli ndaaelelũkw'a nĩ kĩndũ o na kĩva. Ndanieli eekaa maũndũ kwosana na mũĩkĩĩo wake.
ĨYĨOSYE MWENE. Nĩ maũndũ meva ũĩkĩĩaa? Kwa ngelekany'o: Nũĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai? Ũĩkĩĩaa ũu nĩkĩ? Nĩ maũndũ meva makũĩkĩĩthasya kana kwĩ Ngai?
Nũĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai atũnengete myolooto yake nĩ kana ĩtũtethye? Ũĩkĩĩaa ũu nĩkĩ?
Katĩ wa syĩndũ ii ilĩ, wenda kwĩthĩwa ũilyĩ ta kyaũ? Ĩtũ yĩkũũlũkw'a kũũ na kũũ nĩ kĩseve kana mũtĩ ũtesa kũvalũka o na wakimwa nĩ kĩuutani kĩnene? Ĩkĩa kĩthito wĩthĩwe wĩyĩsĩ nesa na ũkeethĩwa ũilyĩ ta mũtĩ ũsu. Na weeka ũu, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũsũngĩa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ, Nyie nĩ mũndũ ũilyĩ ata?
