translation:
ARE YOU OKAY AT ALL?
Considering this scenario: A woman named Karen was wearing clothes from her mother which were too small for her, and she had only ten dollars left, she felt very sad and said:
"Are you alright at all?"
Karen was surprised and saw her friend Jessica holding a flower in her hand. She threw the flower away quickly. Jessica explained why she was bothering Karen with a flower and said, "Listen to me, take another flower instead, or forget it?"
Karen went to think, wondering if Jessica was a friend and if Karen should trust Jessica's intentions. And again, Karen wondered if Jessica was one of those people who just wanted something from her. So she considered whether it was right to accept a gift from Jessica when she was already feeling down. This made Karen think, 'This is strange, it's not just one thing and it feels like a waste of money to buy flowers.'
What is wrong with Karen then?
PLEASE CONSIDER!
It may be that you have been hit by something and feel weak, but don't let pride prevent you from seeking help from someone capable. It is important to know that sometimes it is difficult to recognize what is truly happening to you. With experience and knowledge, you can learn to listen to warnings and others can also advise you.—1 Corinthians 9:26, 27.
Is it possible to get used to your weakness? Getting used to bad habits is a dangerous path.
1 ARE THERE THINGS THAT MAKE IT DIFFICULT TO BE STRONG?
There are things that make it hard to be strong enough to deal with problems and overcome difficulties.
CONSIDER THIS EXAMPLE: The apostle Paul wrote: "Even if I am weak, I boast about my weaknesses." (2 Corinthians 11:6) Although Paul knew the Scriptures well, he was often troubled and worried about other people deceiving him. He did not hesitate to defend his ministry against those who criticized it.—2 Corinthians 10:10; 11:5.
CHECK YOURSELF: Write down what you struggle with or what makes it hard to be strong.
Think about some examples. (For example, are you afraid of public speaking? Are you easily angered? Do you procrastinate?)
2 ARE YOU AFFECTED BY NEGATIVE FEELINGS?
Even if you try to hide your negative feelings, they can still affect your decisions.
CONSIDER THIS EXAMPLE: Paul spoke about his own struggles. He said: "I find myself facing a law which says that when I intend to do good, evil is present with me; and this law seems to contradict the law of my mind, leading me captive." —Romans 7:22, 23.
CHECK YOURSELF: What negative feelings do you have that might hinder your progress?
3 DO YOU HAVE BAD ASSOCIATIONS?
If you spend time with people who encourage bad behavior, will you remain upright and continue doing what is right? Of course not, and it could be disastrous!
What should we do? Being careful about our associations helps us avoid getting involved in bad company. This is because spending time with people who practice what is wrong can influence how we think and act.
CONSIDER THIS EXAMPLE: Paul wrote: "I box my body and subdue it." (1 Corinthians 9:26) Paul was an athlete who disciplined himself so he could compete successfully.—Proverbs 3:12-14.
CHECK YOURSELF. Write down three things you want to improve this year.
4 WHAT ABOUT UNHEALTHY DESIRES?
Everyone has desires, but giving in to them can lead to trouble. It may seem harmless to associate with those who indulge their desires, but it can be dangerous.
To illustrate, everyone has desires and temptations, but yielding to them can cause problems, and associating with others who indulge in unhealthy desires can make matters worse.
CONSIDER THIS EXAMPLE: Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself with the king's food, even though it meant risking the king's anger. Yet, he remained faithful to God and did not compromise with those around him. (Daniel 1:8) As a result, Daniel pleased God and gained respect. Daniel stayed true to his principles.
CHECK YOURSELF. What principles are important to you? For example: Are they based on Bible principles? Why are they important to you? Do they please God?
Are you willing to let God guide your life, even if it means facing opposition? Why or why not?
In view of all this, will you strive to remain loyal to what you know is right? Is it worth enduring hardship, even ridicule, rather than compromising your integrity? If you do, you will prove yourself worthy, and you will have the confidence of knowing that you are pleasing God.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1982
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: POLAND
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: NĨWENDETE KŨKITA, KŨTŨMĨA NDAWA SYA KŨMILA, NA KWĨTHĨWA NA WĨA MŨSEO
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Nasyaĩwe taoninĩ nini yĩ nthĩ ya Poland ĩla ĩte vaasa na mũvaka wa German. Taoni ĩsu yathyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ mĩũnda na itheka, na nĩ kũu neew'aa nĩ mwĩanĩe. Asyai makwa nĩmanthangaasya nĩthĩwe nĩ mũndũ mũseo, na ndyĩkĩa kĩthito sukulu nĩ kana nĩkwata wĩa mũseo.
Mathĩna makwa mambĩĩie ĩla naendie kũsomea mĩao yunivasĩtĩ ĩmwe ĩla yĩ taoninĩ ya Wrocław. Nũndũ naĩ vaasa na asyai, nĩnambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na kĩtindo kĩthũku. O na nĩnendete mũvĩla, ĩndĩ nũndũ wa atindany'a makwa, nĩwambũũkisye. Timũ ĩla nendete yaumĩte Warsaw, na kĩla Wathanthatũ na Wakyumwa namaatĩĩaa vala mathi kũthaũka. Twathi kũu nĩtwanyusaa mũno, tũkatũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila, na mavinda angĩ nĩtwokitaa na ala meũkathĩĩa timũ ĩla ĩngĩ. Noonaa ĩsu tayo nzĩa ya kũmina mathĩna makwa ma kĩla mũthenya, o na kau no neesĩ ngakwatwa nĩ asikalĩ ũndũ ũsu no wanange masomo ala naendeesye ma mĩao.
Nĩ na anyanyawa nĩtwendete kũthi kĩlavu na ndisiko. Twĩ kũu nĩtwokitaa na andũ ala twakomana namo nzĩanĩ. Mavinda maingĩ nĩnakwatawa nĩ asikalĩ, ĩndĩ vai ĩvinda naavika kotinĩ nũndũ mavinda amwe nĩnamaongaa ngalekw'a. Noonaa ta naĩ mwĩanĩe vyũ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩneesĩ kana maũndũ ala neekaa mayaaĩlĩte. Nĩnaendaa ĩkanisanĩ kĩla Wakyumwa nĩ kana nĩeke kũthĩnw'a nĩ wasya wa ngoo.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Mwaka wa 2004, andũ elĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmanthokeie na neetĩkĩla kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia namo. O ũndũ naendeee kũmanya ũndũ Mũklĩsto wa w'o waĩle kwĩkala, now'o wasya wakwa wa ngoo waendeeie kũnthĩny'a. Nĩnamanyie kana nĩnaĩle kũeka kũnyw'a mũno, kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila, na kũtindany'a na andũ ala matekalaa kwosana na myolooto ya Mbivilia. O na nĩnoonie naĩle kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle wakwa nũndũ naĩ mũng'endu. O na kau nĩnamanyie nĩnaĩle kũalyũka, naendeeie kwĩka maũndũ mathũku.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnakwatiwe nĩ ũndũ watumie nĩalyũka vyũ. Nambĩĩie kũkita na aũme nyanya, o na nĩngũlilikana nĩvalũkĩte nzĩanĩ nĩmũũmĩu mũtwe. Ĩla neewie kana nĩkilĩlye kũkw'a, navoyie atĩĩ: "Yeova ndekea nũndũ ndyaaosa Ndeto yaku kwa ũito. Naema kũkw'a, nĩngwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na ndyĩkala mwĩkalĩle mũseo." Na ũndũ ũla wa kũsengy'a nĩ kana ndyaakw'a. Na kwoou nĩneanĩisye ũndũ namwathĩte Yeova kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia.
Mwaka wa 2006, nĩnathamĩĩie England. Kĩeleelo kya kũthi kũu kyaĩ kũkwata mbesa mbingĩ na ndisyoka ĩngĩ Poland nĩ kana ngaendeee kũsomea mĩao. Nĩendeee kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ve ĩandĩko yĩmwe yandetheeisye mũno. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Nĩtalaa syĩndũ syonthe kwĩthĩwa nĩ wasyo ũndũ wa ũseo mũnene wa ũmũmanya Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi wakwa: we ũla kwondũ wake naaisye syĩndũ syonthe, na kwitala kwĩthĩwa nĩ mavuthĩ, nĩ kana nĩmwone Klĩsto." (Avilivi 3:8) Nailyĩ ta mũtũmwa Vaulo nũndũ nĩwasomeete mĩao na aĩ mũng'endu. (Meko ma Atũmwa 8:3) Ĩndĩ nĩwesie kũmanya kana ũndũ ũla wa vata thayũnĩ nĩ kũmũthũkũma Ngai na kũtata ũndũ ũtonya eyĩelekany'e na Yesũ. Ĩla navindĩĩisye ngelekany'o ya Vaulo, nĩnamanyie kana kwĩthĩwa na wĩa mũseo na kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũng'endu kũietae ũtanu. Nĩnaĩkĩĩie vyũ kana o nakwa no nĩalyũke ethĩwa Vaulo nĩwaalyũkile. Kwoou nĩnatwie kwĩkala England na naeka kũsomea mĩao.
O ũndũ naendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova, now'o naendeee kũmũthengeea. Watho wake wa kana nũekeaa ala matw'ĩte vyũ kũalyũka nĩwangiitie ngoo. (Meko ma Atũmwa 2:38) Na ĩla navindĩĩisye ĩandĩko ya 1 Yoana 4:16, yĩla yaĩtye kana "Ngai nĩ wendo," nĩnamanyie nĩkĩ Ngai ũmenete ũng'endu.
Nĩnendaa kũtanĩa ngwatanĩo ĩla nonaa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova me nayo
O na ĩngĩ, nĩnendeeiw'e nĩ mwĩkalĩle wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Nĩnamanyie kana nĩmatataa kwĩkala kwosana na myolooto ya Mbivilia. Na ũu nĩwatumie nenda kũtanĩa ngwatanĩo ĩla noonaa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova me nayo. Ĩtina wa kũng'ang'ana na kwĩka moalyũku, nĩnavatisiwe na natw'ĩka Ngũsĩ ya Yeova mwakanĩ wa 2008.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Mbivilia nĩndetheesye ngaeka kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũng'endu, ndeũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila, ndanyusaa mũno, ndaũũkaw'a nĩ mũvĩla, na ĩkandetheesya ngethĩwa nĩ mũthũkũmi wa Ngai, na nĩnĩtanĩaa kũmanyĩsya andũ Mbivilia. O na yu nĩnendete kwĩloela mũvĩla, ĩndĩ ndyĩtĩkĩlaa ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩwe new'o wa vata thayũnĩ wakwa.
Nĩnatwaie Esther, kĩveti kĩmwendete Yeova o takwa. Nĩtũtanĩaa kũmanyĩsya Mbivilia andũ ala maneenaa kĩthyomo kya Polish ala mekalaa ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ ya England. Yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya mbee kwĩthĩwa nĩ mwĩanĩe. Nĩnĩthĩawa na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo, na nĩw'aa nĩ mwĩanĩe vyũ.

translation:
LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1982
THE COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: POLAND
OUR HISTORY: I REMEMBER TO DO, TO SEND FEES FOR LIVING, AND TO BE SUPPORTED BY A RICH PERSON
PERSONAL STORY:
Let it be known what this story of Poland's origin is like with the German invasion. This story is very painful and sad, and it is good to remember with sadness. Let my parents be remembered by a rich person, and I went to school and got help from a rich person.
Many years later, I went to study at one university in the city of Wrocław. But because of my parents, I preferred to be supported by a strong group. And I continued working, so that with the help of my fellow students, I was able to succeed. We went to the capital Warsaw, and every Saturday and Sunday we would visit various places. We lived well, sent fees for living, and many things we did with the help of people who were kind to us. Sometimes we lacked food for many days, but even then we didn't stop learning and studying our subjects.
I also remember how we went to work and earn money. We knew we could meet new people there. Many things were taken by the police, but some things I hid so that some things wouldn't be seen. Sometimes I felt very sad. But even though it was difficult, I didn't forget about the things I had learned. I wanted to greet everyone on Sunday and also talk to those who loved God.
THE REASON WHY I AM TELLING THIS STORY:
In 2004, people from Jehovah's Witnesses came and invited me to learn the Bible with them. And I continued to learn about Christian principles and how to live, and my family members also began to listen. I realized that I needed to stop drinking alcohol, sending fees for living, and associating with people who didn't care about the teachings of the Bible. And I decided to change my life completely. And even now I realize that I need to improve, and continue doing good things.
One day I was overwhelmed by sadness. I told myself to stay with my mother, but I remembered what I had learned and thought deeply. But I knew I couldn't give up, so I prayed: "Jehovah, please help me to obey Your commands. Help me to continue learning the Bible with Jehovah's Witnesses and to be a good person." And after that prayer, I felt better. And then I appreciated everything Jehovah did through teaching the Bible.
In 2006, I moved to England. The main reason for moving was to have more opportunities, and later I went to Poland to continue my education. I continued teaching the Bible, and one article really touched me. The apostle Paul wrote: "I count everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I consider them rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ." (Philippians 3:8) Like the apostle Paul, I realized how important spiritual matters were. (Acts 8:3) Now I understood that being zealous in this work meant honoring God and doing what pleases him, which is connected with Jesus. But I imitated Paul's example, realizing that focusing on spiritual things and focusing on material things are not compatible. I came to feel strongly that just as Paul rejoiced, I too could rejoice. Then I decided to stay in England and continue my education.
But I also continued teaching about Jehovah, and now I continue to serve him. He showed me that if I kept repenting, he would forgive me. (Acts 2:38) And when I read 1 John 4:16, which says, "God is love," I understood that God has great affection.
I wanted to share the good news that I had learned about Jehovah's organization.
And so, I requested to become a member of Jehovah's organization. I realized that I needed to be close to the Bible's counsel. And that is why I was sent to share the good news about Jehovah's organization. Because of my desire to remain loyal and to preach, I was baptized and became one of Jehovah's Witnesses in 2008.
WHAT MOTIVATED ME:
The Bible touched me deeply, helped me to make progress, brought me joy, comforted me, and made me appreciate God's forgiveness, and motivated me to teach others about the Bible. And even now, I want to live a life that honors him, and I am grateful for the opportunity to share this good news with others.
I married Esther, a woman who loves Jehovah very much. We began teaching people about the Bible, including those who speak Polish and live in the city of London, England. This is what makes our lives meaningful. I am blessed with a wonderful family, and we enjoy serving together.

text:
Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Paul wĩ kĩveti na syana ilĩ aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩla thooa wa syĩndũ wambatie mũno vyũ nthĩ yitũ, lĩu ndwakwatĩkanaa laisi na thooa waw'o waĩ ĩũlũ mũno." Aendeee kwasya: "Twoolasya lĩu masaa maingĩ ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ wathelaa tũtanesa kũvikĩwa. Andũ mamosie mũno nũndũ wa nzaa na angĩ mavalũkaa o maendete. Thooa wa syĩndũ ila sya vata wambatie mũno wavika milioni mbingĩ o na nginya mbilioni. Ĩtina, mbesa sya nthĩ yitũ nĩsyaaie valiũ vyũ. Naaisye mbesa syakwa ila syaĩ vengi, inisualenzi, na mbesa syakwa sya litaya."
Paul nĩweesĩ kana yaĩ no nginya atũmĩe "ũĩ mwĩanĩu" nĩ kana andũ ma mũsyĩ wake maendeee kwĩthĩwa thayũ. (Nthimo 3:21) Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Wĩa wakwa waĩ wa sitima ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu nathũkũmaa wĩa w'onthe ũla nakwata, na naĩvawa mbesa nini." Ongeleele kwasya: "Andũ amwe mandĩvaa o lĩu kana syĩndũ sya kũtũmĩa mũsyĩ. Ĩla naĩvwa mĩtĩ ĩna ya savunĩ, natũmĩaa ĩlĩ na ndithoosya ĩla ĩngĩ. Ĩtina nĩnakwatie tũswii 40 twa ngũkũ. Ĩla tweanie nĩnatũthooisye na nathooa tũngĩ 300. Ĩtina nakũanisye ngũkũ 50 na nanengwa tũkunila twĩlĩ twa kĩlo 50 twa mũtu wa mbemba. Twaĩe mũtu ũsu kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nĩ na andũ makwa, na andũ angĩ."
O na ĩngĩ, Paul nĩweesĩ kana ũndũ ũla wa vata mũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kũmwĩkwatya Ngai. Nũtũtetheeasya ĩla tweeka maũndũ ala ũtwĩyĩaĩe. Yesũ aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila sya vata thayũnĩ: "Mũikethĩwe na nzika nũndũ . . . Ĩthe wenyu nĩwĩsĩ mwĩ na vata wa syĩndũ isu."—Luka 12:29-31.
Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana Satani, mũmaitha mũnene wa Ngai, akengete andũ makelikya mũno maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-mwĩĩ. Andũ nĩmathĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa mavata moo. Mavata amwe methĩawa me vo, na angĩ mate vo na ũu ũituma mekĩa kĩthito mũno makwate syĩndũ o na mate na vata wasyo. Aingĩ nĩmelikasya makoaninĩ, na mayĩsa kũmanya "ũla ũkovaa nĩ mũthũkũmi wa ũla ũkovethasya" methĩawa maũmĩĩte mũno.—Nthimo 22:7.
Andũ amwe mekaa motwi mate maseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Paul aeleetye ũũ: "Atũi aingĩ maitũ nĩmatiie andũ ma mĩsyĩ yoo na anyanyae na mathi kũmantha mawĩa me na ũkwati mwingangĩ nthĩ sya nza." Aendeee kwasya: "Amwe maendie nthĩ sya nza mate na mavalũa ala maĩlĩte na nũndũ wa ũu mayaakwata wĩa. Mavinda maingĩ meevithĩlaa asikalĩ na makomaa nza wa nduka taoni. Mayaamwĩkwatya Ngai amatetheesye. Ĩndĩ nĩ na mũsyĩ wakwa twatwie kũmwĩkwatya Ngai nĩ kana tũng'ang'ane na mathĩna ma mbesa ala twaĩ namo twĩ vamwe."
KŨATĨĨA ŨTAO WA YESŨ
Paul aendeee kwasya: "Yesũ aisye: 'Mũikemakĩe ĩndĩ ũndũ wa ũnĩ; nũndũ ũnĩ ũkeemakĩa e w'o. Mũthenya nĩwĩanĩwe nĩ ũthũku waw'o.' Kwoou, kĩla mũthenya nĩnamũvoyaa Ngai 'atũnenge ũmũnthĩ lĩu ũtwĩanĩe' nĩ kana tũendeee kwĩkala thayũ. Kwa w'o Ngai nĩwatũtetheeisye, o tondũ Yesũ wathanie. Ĩndĩ ti kĩla ĩvinda twakwataa kĩla ngoo ĩkwenda. Ĩvinda yĩmwe, nĩnoolilye lainĩ nthooe lĩu, o na kau ndyeesĩ kĩla kyathooaw'a. Ĩla navikĩiwe neethĩie matesaa ĩia ĩkaatu. Nyie ndi vata na ĩia ĩkaatu, ĩndĩ nũndũ ĩia yĩu yaĩ lĩu nĩyo yatũkomisye wĩoo ũsu. Nĩtũngĩa Ngai mũvea nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu yonthe andũ makwa mayaakoma na nzaa." *
Ngai atwathĩte atĩĩ: "Ndikakũnyivĩa o na ata, na ndikakũtia o na ĩndĩĩ."—Aevelania 13:5
Paul aendeee kwasya: "Oyu tũiavinyĩĩe mũno kĩ-mbesa. Ĩndĩ kumana na maũndũ ala matũkwatĩte nĩtũmanyĩte kana ndawa ĩla nzeo vyũ ya mawĩmakĩo nĩ kũmwĩkwatya Ngai. Ĩvinda yonthe Yeova * akatũtetheeasya ethĩwa tũkeekaa kwenda kwake. Nĩtwonete ũw'o wa ndeto ii syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 34:8: 'Samai mũsisye kana Yeova nĩ mũseo: Kũathimwa nĩ mũndũ ũla wĩvithaa nthĩnĩ wake.' Na kwoou tũi na wia, o na ethĩwa ĩvinda yũkĩte kũkeethĩwa na thĩna wa mbesa."
Paul aĩtye: "Yu nĩtũmanyĩte nesa kana lĩu nĩkyo kĩndũ kya vata nĩ kana andũ mekale thayũ, ĩndĩ ti mbesa kana wĩa. Twĩ na mea maingĩ ma kwona watho ũũ wa Ngai ũyĩanĩa: 'Kũkeethĩwa lĩu mwingĩ mũno wa mbaa ngetha nthĩ.' Ĩndĩ o tweteele ĩvinda yĩu, 'tweethĩwa na kya ũya na kya kwĩvw'ĩka, syĩndũ isu ikatwĩanĩa.' Nĩtũkwataa vinya twasoma ndeto ii syĩ Mbivilianĩ: 'Mũikethĩwe na wendi wa mbesa; ĩanĩwai nĩ syĩndũ ila mwĩ nasyo: nũndũ we mwene nĩwaisye, Ndikakũnyivĩa o na ata, na ndikakũtia o na ĩndĩĩ. Kwondũ wa ũu nĩtũkwasya na ũnyiau, Mwĩaĩi nĩ mũtetheesya wakwa; ndikakĩa.'" *
Nĩ kana 'tũendanasye na Ngai' o ta Paul na andũ ma mũsyĩ wake, no nginya twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 6:9) Mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu wa Paul na ũĩ ũla watũmĩie wĩtũmanyĩsya maũndũ ma vata mũno, twĩthĩwe twĩ na mathĩna ma mbesa ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ kana makatũkwata ĩvinda yũkĩte.
Nao nata ethĩwa mathĩna ma mũsyĩ nĩmekũtuma twĩmakĩa?

translation:
One man named Paul was interviewed and said the following: "Let those who steal from others release them so that they can be reconciled with those people." He continued saying: "Consider this matter carefully for many days with many friends to discuss it. Other people also have problems and wear different clothes. Those who steal from others will pay millions and perhaps billions. Truly, our problem today is very serious. I appreciate our problem, but it is too much, especially our problem of corruption."
Paul realized that if he used the term "goodwill," it meant his colleagues would continue to work hard. (Proverbs 3:21) He said: "Those of us who travel in cars and spend time with others should be careful about what we say." He went on to say: "Some people come here just to exploit others. But I hear some good news, and I use it and share it with others. Truly, I caught forty thieves. But we released them and gave them three hundred. Then I arrested fifty thieves and sentenced them to five years in prison and a fine of fifty kilograms of meat. We found that person in a bad car with his friends, and other people."
And again, Paul realized that the reason someone might want to kill him was because of his loyalty to God. Let us examine how we can avoid such things. Jesus said something similar regarding those who steal: "Do not worry about . . . life; instead, focus on what is important."—Luke 12:29-31.
The reason for trouble is that Satan, the great enemy of God, deceives people and leads them astray. People often become victims of theft. Some thefts are minor, and others are major and cause considerable damage. Many have been cheated, and they learn "that the one who plans evil is the one who does foolish things."—Proverbs 22:7.
Some people live very carelessly. For example, Paul wrote: "Many of our former companions now harass fellow believers and make it difficult for them to live honestly." He continued: "Some go around exploiting people and ruining their lives. Many accidents happen due to carelessness and negligence. Those who fear God take precautions. It is also true that our loyalty to God means that we must be careful about the money we earn and share it with others."
TO IMITATE JESUS' EXAMPLE
Paul went on to say: "Jesus said: 'Keep an eye on yourselves; where your treasure is, there your heart will be.' So, whenever we ask God to 'grant us wisdom,' we should strive to remain alert. Because God has given us a conscience, and because Jesus died, it is not right for us to stumble at every step. One accident might teach us a lesson, but sometimes it takes several lessons to learn something. But if we heed warnings, we can avoid serious consequences. You are valuable, and your life is precious, so the way you live today affects your future. I urge God to help each of you overcome the problems that plague mankind." *
God assures us: "I will never leave you nor abandon you."—Hebrews 13:5
Paul went on to say: "Let us examine ourselves carefully. For when we face trials, we realize how important it is to fear God. Throughout our lives, Jehovah * helps us to stay on his path. We need to appreciate this gift, as David did in Psalm 34:8: 'Taste and see that Jehovah is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.' And so we have confidence, knowing that even accidents can work out for our benefit."
Paul stated: "We realize that nothing is more important than pleasing God, whether we are young or old. We have seen many examples of God's love expressed in the words: 'It is better to take refuge in God than to put confidence in princes.' So let us value our lives, 'appreciating what we have and what we can accomplish,' so that we may continue to serve. Let us remember the words found in Micah: 'With whom will you associate? Be careful about those you choose, for your companions will influence you. I will certainly give you my support; I will never leave you nor abandon you. With me, you will triumph over your enemies.'" *
So, 'let us walk alongside God,' as Paul and his fellow Christians did, and we will be strengthened by his spirit. (Galatians 6:9) The strong spirit of Paul and the example he set help us to understand important things, strengthening us with faith and helping us to persevere through difficulties.
And now, should we not also appreciate the privilege of having brothers and sisters who encourage us?

"If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink. He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water." But this spoke He of the Spirit, whom those who believed were to receive, for yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified." John 7:37-39, 13|
The Resurrection of Christ – Great Elders of them.
Apostle Paul wrote concerning the hope of our calling in Corinth, "if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen." 1 Corinthians 15:13. The verse of scripture also says, "and if Christ is not risen, then our preaching is empty and your faith is futile." 1 Corinthians 15:14
Great elders of the resurrection of Christ have been shown clearly through testimonies and teachings which the church of today follows with conviction. (For reference Acts 2:31, 4:33, 17:18; 26:23 Every book of the Old Testament speaks about the doctrine of Christ so we should not neglect its importance.
Scripture also states, "And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is worthless, and your faith is worthless too." 1 Corinthians 15:3-4
This thing which we have now is the Bible explaining things and the doctrine being more important than just stories or rumors.
Tears of our great ancestors.
God desires life and not death for mankind, This is like Adam and Eve disobeying God's command; He gave them tears as punishment. Sin that sins always leads to destruction.
Because of this, the penalty for sin is death, which separates us from God forever, through the tears of God for mankind." The story of our ancestors is serious (Romans 6:23)
And like this, many are turning away from God because of their mistakes. Consider His righteousness, "All we have become like unclean things, and all our righteous acts are like polluted rags" (Isaiah 64:6b) Since Adam's time everyone is born with sin and falls short of God's perfect standards "For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23). Sin is major issues such as stealing, lying, pride, hatred, and jealousy. Because of sin everyone is condemned - Separated from God eternally.
The price of sin is great and severe.
But God loved us so much that He sent His Son, Jesus, to take our place and suffer the consequences of our sins. He promised to send someone who would crush the serpent's head and bring an end to suffering (Genesis 3:15) --- That is why they are children of God's love: God Himself provided the solution (Jesus) who has the power to reconcile us to Him. God's beloved Son willingly went to fulfill the will of his Father, which was to seek and save lost souls. "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."(John 3:16) 2 Corinthians 5:21.
Jesus took upon himself the burden of our sins, and through three days of death, He demonstrated immense sorrow.
Jesus' sacrifice was a ransom for our sins, and His resurrection proved His victory over death; and everything connected to Jesus' sacrifice demonstrates the value of His sacrifice. Hebrews 9:24-26 states "Christ did not enter heaven to offer himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place yearly with blood, nor was it to offer himself to atone for our sins once for all------" Now is God's time. Jesus Christ offered His sacrifice completely to appease God, To show the importance of faith.
Let us accept Jesus,
The Savior and Redeemer of our lives.
That precious blood that He shed
Demonstrates His love, suffers pain,
And now resides in the holy presence of God
Because of the perfection of God
Hebrews 12:2
The gift of God's grace can be received, Resurrection demonstrates that Jesus fulfilled the law and satisfied our debt, And we also receive forgiveness of sins when we believe in Jesus and confess them openly. And because of this forgiveness, we are able to live without fear. "This is how we know that we have passed from death to life." The book of Hebrews 6:4 says this. "It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit, and who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age, Hebrews: 6b |

We are justified by the merits of faith, the perfection of the righteous, the fulfillment of many promises. (Romans 6) This is what is called reconciliation.
We are justified by believing in faith: the act of resurrection, but it is called being saved, or "receiving it for ourselves" (Romans 8:23)

God's plan is, according to scripture, to be born again and again until the fullness of time:

Aitaangasa kikwu kyake President wa oyu Uhuru Muigai Kenyatta niwaweta kana Kibaki akwa utukuni wa kwamukia umunthi, ena ukuu wa miaka 90.
Niwamuweta kwitha e mutongoi muu na mutetei wa uwo wa enethi , aii mustalini wa mbee kwailya unyanya wa nthi sya ilembetani ya Africa umiloni wa sua.
Ula wai president wa 3 wa nthi ya Kenya Mwai Kibaki niwatiwa ni thayu.
Aitangaasa mauvoo aa President wa oyu uhuru Kenyatta niwaweta kibaki alakilikanawa kumana na uthukumi wake miviani kivathukanio ya silikali wivo wa kisomo,malelu na uiiti.
Uhuru niwaweta kibaki ai mutsalini wa mbee kwailya unyanya wa nthi sya ilembeta ya Africa ya umiloni wa sua ivindani ya utongoi wake.
….UHURU KIBAKI
Atongoi kivathuaknio nimaendeeye kutuma ngethi sya ukiakisyo kwa musyi wa mututia mwai kibaki maimukathiiya kumana na uthukumi mwailu ivindani ya utongoi wake.
kati wa atongoi aa ni vamwe na munini wa President Dr. William Ruto wa Kenya Kwanza,Raila Odinga wa Azimio One Kenya Alliance kati wa atongoi angi aingi silikalini.
…..LEADERS KIBAKI
Na uu niwo thayu wa mututia MwaI Kibaki otondu FRED MULI ukuelesya…..
BIO….FRED MULI
KIBAKI'S LEGACY
President Mwai Kibaki akalilkikanawa kwa utongoi wake museo nthini wa ilungu ya myaka 10 ila watongoesye nthi ya kenya .
Mbee oselela utongoi mwakani wa 2002 niwaetie kisomo kya mana kya sukulu sya musingi na secondary vala asyai aingi meena undu wa kutania kwa kwauua muiio wa ndivi ya ilovia sya fees.
Oo kavindani kau nthini wa utongoi wake muvea wa kisomo niwethiewe na mawayluko maingi vala imanyisyo kauta kinene syavikie na kwambatwa ndeve.
Kwa ilungu yiu ya myaka 10 ukwati wa nthi ya kenya niwambatie kwa vanene vala seriklai ya Kibaki yanenganie mawithyululuko maseo kwa akenya kutrwaisya maundu ma utandithya vala sector ya Boda boda yailiwe ivindani yiu na ila mbikia oyu ni imwe kati wa mivea ila yina ukwati mwingi vaa nthi ya Kenya.
Kwi mwakani wa 2010 nthi ya kenya niyakwatia katiba keu ungu wa utongoi wa President Kibaki kala niko katumiwa kwa oyu vaa nthi ya kenya .
Ni kumanwa na utongoi wake vala nthi ya kenya yekiiewe mwolooto wa maendeo mwakani wa 2006 wa Kenya Vision 2030 vala vena milati kivathukanyo ya maendeo vala kati wa milati isu ni vamwe na ula wa ngali ya mwaki ya matuku aa SGR na soko wa dunia wa Techno City ula wendeye na kuseuvya.
Kenya makethiawa maimulilikana Mzee Kibaki wa lelu munene wa Thika Super Highway ula mbikia oyu ni kati wa malelu ala manene vaa nthi ya kenya.
Kavindani kau AKENYA maendeeye kumeta kikwu kya Mwai Kibaki…tukamulilikanaa na mauneeni make ma mathekania e kundu kivathukanio ivindani ya utongoi wake ta uuu…

….FESTUS KIBAKI
MAKUENI ANITAH NDANU 1PM NEWS 22ND APRIL
Gavana Wa kaunti ya makueni pro kivutha kibwana niwatuma ngethi sya ukiakisyo Kwa musyi wa ula wai president Wa 3 Vaa nthi ya Kenya na ula utiiwe ni thayu wake kwi umunthi

Kibwana niwaweta mututita mzee kibaki ei mutongoi Kwa kwikwatwa Vaa nthi ya Kenya aiweta ta mathukumanie nake Kuma kwi mwakani Wa 2002 vala kibwana wai muyumbe Wa makueni na kibaki amusakua ta Minister Wa itheka Vaa nthi ya Kenya oundumwe na mutai wake Kuma kwi mwakani Wa 2007 nginya 2013.
….KIBWANA
KITUI ON KIBAKI
Ula wai munini wa ngavana selekalini ya mbee kauntini ya Kitui,Penina Malonza na ukukitia kivila kya aka (Women Rep)kauntini ya Kitui,niwatuma ngethi syake sya ukiakisyo kwi musyi wa ula wai musumbi wa katatu vaa nthi ya Kenya,Emeritus Kibaki na ula watiwa ni thayu wake kwi umunthi.
Aineena na muveleleki wa mauvoo musyini wa Kitui,Penina niwamuweta mututia Kibaki ta unai mutongoi unai ngumbau, unaendete enenthi, na wookililye ukwati ya nthi ya Kenya Kenya kiwango kinene aiweta nthi ya Kenya niyasya mutongoi eina utonyi wa kuinenge ndongoi ila ikwenda ivila kivathukanyo utao.
….PENINAH MALONZA
Nake Bonny Musambi na ula ukuukitia kivila kya Kiliombunge kya Kitui kya kati niwamukumya Kibaki kwa utongoi ula wavikiiye kwailya ukwati na wina uima na uu.
Namo enenthi isioni kivathukanio countini ya masaku nimameta kikwu kya Mwai Kibaki ta uu..

translation:
The third President of the Republic of Kenya, Emilio Stanley Mwai Kibaki, has been laid to rest today.
His successor, current President Uhuru Muigai Kenyatta, led Kenyans in mourning Kibaki as he entered his final resting place, aged 90 years.
He was mourned across the country and internationally, and leaders from various African countries attended his funeral.

text:
We waaona kavila ka thaavu? Nĩ avũthũ maamantha thaavu na makawona. Ĩndĩ ve angĩ milioni mbingĩ monete kĩndũ kĩseo vyũ o na kwĩ thaavu. Kĩndũ kyu nĩ ũĩ wa Ngai, naw'o "ndũtonya kũthoowa na thaavu."—Yovu 28:12, 15.
NO TŨELEKANY'E ala mekwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ meũmantha thaavu. Andũ ta asu me na ngoo nzeo maĩlĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito na maiendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Maandĩko nĩ kana makwate ũĩ ũla wĩ vau ũtesa kwoneka vangĩ. Kwoou ekai twone maũndũ atatũ mũndũ wĩkaa nĩ kana akwate thaavu. Maũndũ asu matonya kũtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
KŨKWATA KAVILA KA THAAVU!
Twasye ũtembeele ũtee wa ũsĩ nĩwoona kaindo kailyĩ kavila keũkengakenga. Na wakumana wakosa ũyĩthĩa kaĩ nĩ kavila ka thaavu! Nĩ kanini vyũ o na kwĩ kongo ka mũsyĩ wa kĩlĩvĩtĩ, na ke mũo o na kwĩ kavila kala kaseo vyũ ka diamond. Ũnamina kũkwata kavila ku ka thaavu, ndũlea kũmanthanga vau ũtee wone kana nũkwona tũngĩ.
O ta ũu, no kwĩthĩwa ũlilikanaa mũthenya wa mbee ũla Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syavikie kwaku na syakũelesya wĩkwatyo ũla Mbivilia ĩtũnengete. O na no kwĩthĩwa ũlilikanaa nesa vyũ mũthenya waku wa mbee kũelewa ũw'o ũmwe wa vata. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa ũsu no ũla mũthenya woonie ya mbee Mbivilianĩ ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova. (Sav. 83:18) O na no kwĩthĩwa no ĩla wamanyie kana no ũtw'ĩke mũnyanyae wa Yeova. (Yak. 2:23) Ĩla wakwatie ũmanyi ũsu nĩwamanyie wakwata kĩndũ kĩseango o na kwĩ thaavu! Ĩtina wa ũu nĩ laisi ũkethĩwa wendie mũno kũendeea kũmantha ũmanyi mwingangĩ.
KŨKWATA TŨVILA TWINGANGĨ TWA THAAVU!
Mavinda amwe tũvila twa thaavu twĩyũmbĩlĩĩlaa mbũsĩnĩ, kana o kũndũ kũngĩ ta ku. Ethĩwa ala mekũmantha thaavu me na kĩthito, myei mĩvũthũ ĩithela no makwate thaavu wĩ na kĩlo iana ũna. Kĩlo isu syĩ na makili ma ndola.
Ĩla wambĩĩe kũmanyĩw'a Mbivilia nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, no kwĩthĩwa weewie ũndũ mũndũ wĩw'aa ĩla weekĩa kĩw'ũ mũthanganĩ wĩ na tũvila twa thaavu na oona tũvila tũu tweekela. Ĩla woosie ĩvinda wavindĩĩsya mũsoa ũmwe ĩtina wa ũngĩ, ũmanyi waku nĩwongelekile na kĩu kyalũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova. O ũndũ waendeeie kũmantha na kĩthito ũmanyi ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, nĩwoonie ũndũ ũtonya kũmũthengeea Yeova na ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana aendeee kũkwenda na ayũka kũkũnenga thayũ ũtathela.—Yak. 4:8; Yuta 20, 21.
O ta mũndũ ũkũmantha na kĩthito tũvila twa thaavu, no kwĩthĩwa waĩ na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũmantha ũthwii wa kĩ-veva. Wamina kwĩmanyĩsya momanyĩsyo ala ma mũsingi ma Mbivilia, nĩweewie wakwata vinya wa kwosa ĩtambya ya kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova na ũivatiswa.—Mt. 28:19, 20.
ENDEEA KŨMANTHA!
Mavinda amwe mũndũ ũkũmantha tũvila twa thaavu no atwĩthĩe mavianĩ ma mũthemba mũna (igneous rocks). Mavinda angĩ mavia amwe ta asu methĩawa makuĩte thaavu mwingĩ mũno ũkethĩa no menzawa na maitumbangwa nĩ kana ũ thaavu umw'e nesa. Ĩndĩ ũsyaĩtye ya mbee nũtonya kũema kwona thaavu ĩvianĩ yĩu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ tani ũmwe wa ĩvia yĩla ĩseo vyũ nũtonya kwĩthĩwa na o ngulamu 10 sya thaavu (10 grams)! Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, mũndũ ũsu ũkũmantha thaavu nĩwonaa ve vaita wa kwĩkĩa kĩthito aumye thaavu ũla weethĩa.
O ta ũu, no nginya mũndũ aendeee kwĩkĩa kĩthito o na aminĩte kũelewa nesa 'momanyĩsyo o ala wamanyĩiw'e ma mbee ĩũlũ wa Klĩsto.' (Aevl. 6: 1, 2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Nĩwaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito ĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nĩ kana ũmanye maũndũ meũ na maũndũ ũtonya kũtũmĩa thayũnĩ waku. Kwoou o na kau nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Maandĩko myaka mingĩ mĩvĩtu, ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana mũvango waku wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ũkũtethye?
Mavinda onthe ĩthĩawa na wendi wa kwĩmanyĩsya. Tata ndũkavĩtwe nĩ tũmaũndũ o na tũla tũnini. Endeea kwĩkĩa kĩthito na nũũkwata ũĩ wa vata mũno kuma kwa Ngai, na we mwene ndakaema kũũtongoesya. (Alo. 11:33) Nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na ũmanyi mwingangĩ wa Maandĩko, tũmĩa nesa syĩndũ sya kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ila ũtonya kũkwata kĩthyomonĩ kyaku. Ethĩwa ve makũlyo wĩ namo kana ve ũtao ũũmantha, mantha wĩ na wũmĩĩsyo. Kũlya angĩ nĩ maandĩko meva, kana nĩ ũvoo wĩva wĩ mavukunĩ maitũ monete ũtonya kũmatethya na kũmekĩa vinya. Na ĩndĩ tavya angĩ tũmaũndũ tũseo tũla ũmanyĩte ĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai.
Vate nzika, kĩeleelo kyaku kĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa o kũkwata ũmanyi mwingĩ. O na mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwakanisye Aklĩsto amea atĩĩ: "Ũmanyi ũetae ngathĩĩo." (1 Ako. 8:1) Kwoou tata mũno wĩthĩawe wĩnyivĩtye na wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Kwĩthĩwa na ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ mũteũtĩĩa na kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ũteũtĩĩa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũũtethya wĩkale ũndũ Yeova wendaa, na makakwĩkĩa vinya ũtethye angĩ. Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana ũkekalaa wĩ mũtanu nũndũ nũkwatĩte kĩndũ kĩseango kwĩ thaavu.—Nth. 3:13, 14.

translation:
Will we ever see the source of wealth? It is a valuable thing, wealth and possessions. Some have spent millions trying to find something worthwhile and to get wealth. But the fact is that it is a gift from God, and He said, "Wisdom is worth more than rubies."—Job 28:12, 15.
LET US CONSIDER how to compare the Bible with people who value wealth. People often spend a lot of time and effort trying to understand the Scriptures, but they may end up feeling frustrated and disappointed. How can we make sure that we don't become like that person who wasted his wealth? What can help us to understand things correctly?
FINDING THE SOURCE OF WEALTH!
Imagine walking along a riverbed and seeing a shiny stone—it might be a source of great wealth! But someone could easily miss it because it looks like an ordinary rock! It is often hidden deep within the earth, and it is as rare and beautiful as a diamond. If you want to find the source of wealth, you need to search carefully and diligently.
But also, remember that trusting in Jehovah's organization will help you to find the truth found in the Bible. And remembering that this truth will help you to understand the meaning of life. They will encourage you to study the Bible, which is inspired by God, Jehovah. (Ps. 83:18) And remember to show that you appreciate Jehovah. (Jas. 2:23) If you gain this knowledge, you will find something truly valuable! The result of this is that you will be motivated to continue learning more.
FINDING MORE SOURCES OF WEALTH!
Many sources of wealth are hidden, or they are difficult to reach. Remember to value wealth and to use it wisely, and always remember that wealth does not bring happiness. Wealth itself has no real value.
But understanding the Bible is from Jehovah, and remembering that everyone who wants to associate with those finding sources of wealth and also true wealth. But realize that sometimes a person may become proud because of what he learns, his knowledge increases and he forgets his relationship with Jehovah. And continuing to learn about the truths in the Bible, is the only way to draw closer to Jehovah and the only way to avoid being led astray—Jas. 4:8; Judg. 20, 21.
But if a person values sources of wealth, remember to value more the work of preaching. Continue to teach others the fundamental teachings of the Bible, and you will have the opportunity to help people come to know and love Jehovah and to live according to his will.—Matt. 28:19, 20.
CONTINUE LEARNING!
Sometimes a person valuing sources of wealth associates with people who are rich (igneous rocks). Other times people like this spend much money on things they don't need and boast about them, even though that wealth is useless. It is surprising how little it takes to make someone desire wealth. Why? Because even just a small amount of something, ten grams of gold (10 grams)! It is because of this, that a person valuing wealth sees value in seeking more wealth than he needs.
But this, and encourage him to understand well 'the sacred secrets belonging to God's Kingdom.' (Rev. 6:1, 2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) He will find value in learning the Bible and knowing more things and things that can benefit you. So continue to be willing to learn to teach the Scriptures for many years, should you ever wonder if your progress in learning the Bible is slow?
Many people are hindered from progressing. My brothers, let us focus on important things and big matters. Continue reading the scriptures and always have faith in God, and He alone will help you to succeed. (Phil. 11:33) If you are blessed with greater knowledge of the Scriptures, use it wisely so that you may gain approval. Don't be discouraged by obstacles or difficulties; persevere with determination. For often new writings, or new ideas from our ancestors, can cause confusion and misunderstanding. And yet many important things like these help us to understand God's purpose.
Dear friends, your ability to learn is limited, but having more knowledge is good. And the apostle Paul reminded Christians, saying: "Knowledge inflates." (1 Cor. 8:1) So many people are proud and boastful. Being inflated with pride and studying the Bible superficially are things that prevent us from doing what Jehovah wants, and they lead to misunderstandings. And this matter of being humble is when you find something valuable to hold onto firmly.—Prov. 3:13, 14.

text:
ĨKASETI ya The Watch Tower ya 01/09/1915 yaisye ũũ: "Makaũ onthe ma tene ti kĩndũ wamasianĩsya na kaũ mũnene ũla ũendeee yu ngalĩko ya Europe." Yawetie ũu yĩyĩelesya ĩũlũ wa ũla kaũ wa mbee wa nthĩ yonthe, ũla wesie kũkitwa nĩ nthĩ ta 30. Na nũndũ wa ũthũ ũla waĩ vo ĩvinda yĩu, ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower yawetie atĩĩ: "Wĩa [wa Ũsumbĩ] nũsiĩĩwe kwa nzĩa ĩmwe kana ĩngĩ, na mũno mũno nthĩ ya Germany na France."
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu kaũ ũsu wavyũvĩte nthĩ yonthe, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mayaeleawa nesa ũndũ matonya kũatĩĩa ũla mwolooto ũtongoeasya Aklĩsto maũndũnĩ ma kaũ na siasa na kwoou amwe nĩmalikile kaũnĩ. Ĩndĩ vailyĩ oou, nĩmatw'ĩte vyũ kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũndũ Wilhelm Hildebrandt nĩwendaa kũthũkũma a vake wĩanĩ wa Ũsumbĩ, nĩwakũlilye atũmĩwe kovi sya tulakiti yeetawa The Bible Students Monthly ya kĩthyomo kya French. Ndaendete France ta kolovota (mũtavany'a wa ĩvinda yonthe), ĩndĩ aendete kũu e mũsikalĩ wa Germany. Nĩwatavasya andũ ma France ala mavĩtĩte nzĩanĩ ũvoo mũseo wa mũuo. Andũ asu matiawa maseng'ete nũndũ Wilhelm eethĩawa ekĩĩte ngũa sya ita na aĩ mũsikalĩ wa Germany, ala maĩ nthũ syoo.
Valũa ila syesie kũtumbĩthw'a ĩkasetinĩ ya The Watch Tower syonanĩtye kana Amanyĩw'a angĩ ma Mbivilia ma Germany nĩmoonaa maĩle kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo me o itanĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mwana-a-asa Lemke aĩ wa ita sya kĩw'ũnĩ na aisye kana atano katĩ wa ala weethĩawa namo nĩmendeeiw'e mũno. Aisye: "O na nĩ melinĩ ĩno no nĩendeee kũkwata mosyao meũmũtaĩa Yeova."
Nake Georg Kayser aendie kaũnĩ e mũsikalĩ ĩndĩ ayĩnũka enũkie e mũthũkũmi wa Ngai. Ũu watonyekie ata? Akwatie ĩvuku yĩmwe ya Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia, eetĩkĩla na ngoo yonthe ũw'o wa Ũsumbĩ ũla waĩ ĩvukunĩ yĩu, na ĩndĩ atw'a kũmba nthĩ mĩio yake ya kaũ. Ĩtina oosie wĩa ũte kũmũlikya kaũnĩ ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe. Kaũ wathela nĩwatw'ĩkie vainia wĩ kĩthito kwa myaka mingĩ.
O na kau Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mayaeleawa nesa mwolooto wa kũlea kwĩlikya kaũnĩ na siasanĩ, woni woo na mwĩkalĩle woo waĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na wa andũ ala angĩ malikile kaũnĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ma siasa na atongoi ma ndĩni makwatie mbau nthĩ syoo kaũnĩ ũsu, ĩndĩ mo Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia malũmanĩtye na ũla "Mũnene wa Mũuo." (Isa. 9:6) O na kau amwe moo mayaatĩĩa nesa vyũ ũla mwolooto ũvatanĩte kũlika kaũnĩ na siasanĩ, nĩmalũmĩtye ũw'o wa vata ũla wawetiwe nĩ Mũmanyĩw'a wa Mbivilia weetawa Konrad Mörtter. Aisye: "Nĩneesĩ nesa vyũ kuma Ndetonĩ ya Ngai kana Mũklĩsto ndaĩle kũaana."—Kuma 20:13. *
Mĩao ya nthĩ ya Germany ndyawetete wĩa ũngĩ ũla mũndũ waĩ atonya kũtethya ethĩwa nĩwalea kũlika itanĩ nũndũ wa wasya wake wa ngoo. Na kwoou Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mbee wa 20 ma nthĩ ĩsu mayaaĩtĩkĩla kwĩlikya itanĩ o na vanini. Nũndũ wa ũu, amwe moo moonekaa ta andũ awau mĩtwe. Ũmwe wa asu aĩ Gustav Kujath, ũla watwaiwe vala vasũvĩĩawa andũ ma ndũũka na anengwa ndawa sya kũmũmila. O nake Hans Hölterhoff nĩwaleile kũlika itanĩ na ũu watuma atwawa yela, vala waleile wĩa w'onthe ũkonetye kaũ. Asungi ma yela mamwovanisye nginya aanda moko. Na ĩla asungi moonie ndanavĩndũka, mamwosie na meelitya nĩmeũmũaa. Ĩndĩ Hans aendeeie kwĩthĩwa e mũlũmu nginya kaũ ũsu wathela.
Ana-a-asa angĩ ala meetĩkĩlile kũlika itanĩ nĩmaleile kũkua mĩio ya kaũ na makũlya manewe wĩa ũngĩ ũte wa kũkita ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe. * Johannes Rauthe nũmwe wa asu na anengiwe wĩa kĩsesenĩ kya ngalĩ ya mwaki. Nake Konrad Mörtter anengiwe wĩa wa kũtetheanĩsya na matakĩtalĩ, nake Reinhold Weber atw'ĩka mũtetheesya wa ndakĩtalĩ. Na ĩndĩ August Krafzig nĩweewie mũyo mũno nũndũ wĩa ũla waaĩwe ndwaatuma athi kũkita. Amanyĩw'a asu ma Mbivilia vamwe na angĩ o tamo nĩmatw'ĩte kũmũthũkũma Yeova kwosana na kĩla meesĩ ĩũlũ wa wendo na ũĩkĩĩku.
Nũndũ wa mwĩkalĩle woo ĩvindanĩ yĩu ya kaũ, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmambĩĩe kũsiw'a mũno nĩ silikalĩ. Myakanĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ma Germany maĩ na makoani maingĩ mũno kotinĩ nũndũ wa wĩa woo wa kũtavany'a. Ovisi wa ũvonge wa Germany, ũla waĩ Magdeburg, nĩwaseũvisye kamitii ya maũndũ ma mĩao nĩ kana ĩmatetheesye.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyaendeeie kwongelanga ũmanyi woo ĩũlũ wa mwolooto ũla ũkonetye kwĩlikya kaũnĩ. Kwoou ĩla kaũ wa kelĩ wa nthĩ yonthe wambĩĩe, nĩmaatĩĩe mwolooto ũsu nesa kwa kũlea kwĩlikya itanĩ o na vanini. Nũndũ wa ũu matalilwe ta nthũ sya Silikalĩ ya Germany na mathĩnw'a mũno. Ĩvindanĩ yĩngĩ tũkaneenea ũvoo ũsu nthĩnĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ kya "Kwĩlilikany'a Maũndũ ma Tene."—Kwĩlilikany'a maũndũ ma tene ma Central Europe.
^ kal. 7 Wenda kũsoma ngewa ya Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ma Britain ala maĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ ya Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe, sisya "Kutoka Katika Hifadhi ya Vitu Vyetu vya Kale—Walisimama Imara Katika 'Saa ya Jaribu,'" ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 15/05/2013.
^ kal. 9 Ũtwi ũsu meekie wawetetwe Ĩvukunĩ ya 6 ya mavuku ma Millennial Dawn (1904), na ĩkasetinĩ ya Zion's Watch Tower ya Mwei wa 8, 1906, ya kĩthyomo kya German. Nayo ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower ya Mwei wa 9, 1915, nĩyaumĩlangilye kyeni ĩũlũ wa woni witũ na yaweta kana Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mayaĩle kũlika itanĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩlungu kĩla kyaeleetye ũndũ ũsu kĩyaĩ vo ĩkasetinĩ ya kĩthyomo kya German.

translation:
The Watch Tower issue of September 1, 1915, stated: "The countries at war are being devastated by a great power that continues to be in Europe." It predicted this would last for several years, perhaps about 30 years. And because of the extent of the devastation, The Watch Tower issue further stated: "Austria [of Austria] will be humbled by one way or another, and little by little both Germany and France."
This prediction has largely come true, and Jehovah's Witnesses have shown themselves to be loyal to God despite the tremendous pressure they have faced from governments and people alike. In fact, some have been imprisoned for their faith. For example, Wilhelm Hildebrandt wanted to help his fellow Austrians, so he had himself sent copies of the magazine called The Bible Students Monthly in the French language. He then went to France to distribute them (despite the overall ban), and then went to Germany. He managed to get the French brothers to send him more of this literature. Many people were moved by Wilhelm's efforts and came to listen to the German speakers, but not many.
However, this was not the only time that The Watch Tower publications or individual Bible Students in Germany showed initiative in trying to spread the good news. For instance, young Brother Lemke was in prison and wrote five letters to those who visited him, asking for assistance. He wrote: "Even now I continue to desire to devote myself to serving Jehovah."
Later, Georg Kayser also found himself in prison where he began to think about God. Did this happen by chance? Take an issue of The Bible Students Monthly, read it carefully, and see how much information about Austria it contained, and then consider how much effort it took to obtain it. It will become clear to you how much work each issue required. This work continued for many years.
And yet, Jehovah's Witnesses have shown themselves to be loyal to God and steadfast despite the great pressure, and others have appreciated their loyalty and fine conduct. For example, government officials and judges have sometimes seen how much courage these people have, and because the Witnesses proclaimed the title "King of Eternity." (Isa. 9:6) And still others have been deeply impressed by the way this pressure has motivated them to be loyal and steadfast, as illustrated by the experience of Brother Konrad Mörtter, a Witness. He said: "I became more determined than ever to preach God's Word and be a Christian."—Acts 20:13. *
In the early days in Germany, there were times when a person could be imprisoned simply for speaking to his neighbors. And during World War II, some 20 of those Witnesses were executed for remaining neutral. Because of this, some appeared to be fools to men. One of these was Gustav Kujath, who was tortured by Gestapo agents and sentenced to death. Later, Hans Hölterhoff was imprisoned for neutrality, and this led to his being sent to a concentration camp, where he remained until the end of the war. The experiences of these brothers moved many people. And although some did not understand, they showed sympathy. So Hans went through terrible suffering, but this experience strengthened him.
These brothers along with others remained faithful despite facing imprisonment and receiving harsh treatment because of their determination to preach individually. *Johannes Rauthe was one of these and was condemned to three and a half years in prison for refusing military service. Also, Konrad Mörtter was condemned for associating with Bible Students, and Reinhold Weber was labeled a seditious agitator. And so August Krafzig was given a severe sentence because his activity led to others refusing military service. These German Witnesses, together with others, continued to demonstrate their loyalty to Jehovah, showing courage and love.
Because of their steadfast faith, the Watch Tower Society provided assistance whenever possible. In 1936, the Watch Tower Society in Germany sent out letters to many congregations informing them of what was happening. The regional overseer of Germany, from Magdeburg, investigated the legal aspects of the situation and reported on them.
Jehovah's witnesses continued to proclaim the good news during this difficult time, remaining firm in their conviction. They realized that the present system would not last forever and wanted to use their time wisely to help others learn about God's Kingdom. Because of this, they were willing to endure persecution from the authorities in Germany and elsewhere. Their efforts were highlighted in the article "Defending God's Word"—Defending God's Word in Central Europe.
^ p. 7 To read more about the experiences of the Watch Tower Society in Britain during this period, see "From Our Archives—They Stood Firm During 'A Time of Trial,'" The Watchtower Study Edition of May 15, 2013.
^ p. 9 This information was first published in volume 6 of Studies in the Scriptures (1904), and in the August 1, 1906, issue of Zion's Watch Tower in German. Furthermore, the September 1, 1915, issue of The Watch Tower explained our position clearly and showed how the Watch Tower Society had acted faithfully. It also pointed out that this matter revealed the true character of the German edition.

text:
KWĨ Matukũ 26, Mwei wa 3, 1937, aũme elĩ nĩmalikile taoninĩ ya Sydney, Australia, na ngalĩ yoo ĩla yolũkĩlwe nĩ kĩtoo kingĩ mũno. Aũme asu matinĩte kyalo makew'a nthĩ. Kuma mauma taoninĩ ĩsu mwaka waĩ mũthelu, na maendete mũendo wa maili mbee wa 12,000 (kĩlomita 19,300) mesĩlĩte isionĩ syĩ vaasa mũno syĩ iĩma na ivaũũko kũu Australia. Mayakũnĩte savalĩ ĩsu yonthe atĩ nũndũ maendete kũthũima kũndũ kana kũtembea meyonee nthĩ. Aũme asu maĩ Arthur Willis na Bill Newlands, na me elĩ maĩ mavainia me kĩthito mũno ala matw'ĩte kũtwaa ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai yĩla ĩng'alatanĩ yũmũ mũno ya Australia.
Tũivika mũthyanĩ wa myaka ya 1920, Amanyĩw'a anini ma Mbivilia * ala maĩ Australia matavanĩtye mũno mũno taoninĩ ila syĩ vakuvĩ na ũkanga na isio ila ingĩ ithyũlũlũkĩte taoni isu. Ĩndĩ naku nthĩnĩ kũasa na ũkanga ve ĩng'alata yũmũ mũno yĩtũĩte andũ mataanĩe, na nĩ ĩnene kwĩ nusu ya nthĩ ya Amelika. Ana-a-asa nĩmeesĩ nesa kana aatĩĩi ma Yesũ manengetwe wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo "kũvika itulu sya nthĩ," ila nĩ vamwe na ĩng'alata yĩu ya Australia. (Meko 1:8) Ĩndĩ mesaa kũtethya ata wĩa ũsu wingĩvĩte ũu? Nĩmatwie vyũ kwĩka kĩla matonya, me na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu vyũ kana Yeova nũkũathima kĩthito kyoo.
MAVAINIA NĨMASEŨVISYE NZĨA
Mwaka wa 1929 kĩkundi kĩla kyaĩ kĩsionĩ kya Queensland na kĩla kĩngĩ kyaĩ kĩsionĩ kya Western Australia, nĩsyaseũvisye ngalĩ syĩ na kĩla kĩndũ kyendekaa nyũmba ta ũkomo na ĩiko nĩ kana syĩyũmbanĩsye kũthi kũtavany'a isionĩ ila syĩ naku nthĩnĩ. Ngalĩ isu syatwaawa nĩ mavainia me na vinya, ala maĩ matonya kũitwaa malelũnĩ mathũku na mayĩiseũvya syaanangĩka. Mavainia asu nĩmatavanisye isionĩ mbingĩ itaĩ syaatavanw'a.
Mavainia ala mataĩ mona ngalĩ maendie yĩla ĩng'alatanĩ na isululu. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 1932, Bennett Brickell, ũla waĩ na myaka 23, nĩwaumie taoninĩ ya Rockhampton, kĩsionĩ kya Queensland, na athi atavanĩtye ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya kĩsio kyu. Savalĩ ĩsu yake yakuie myei ĩtano. Kĩsululu kyake kyakuĩte kĩkanoa. Kyakuĩte syĩndũ ta mavula, ngũa, lĩu, na kĩthũmba kya mavuku. Ĩla taili sya kĩsululu syathelile, ndaaũngamya savalĩ, ĩndĩ aendeeie kũkĩsukuma e na mũĩkĩĩo Yeova nũkũmũtongoesya. Asukumie kĩsululu kĩu maili ala matiele 200 (kĩlomita 320) ma kyalo kĩu kyake esĩle kũndũ kwakw'ĩĩe aũme nũndũ wa waũni. Myaka 30 ĩla yaatĩĩe, Mwana-a-asa Brickell angangie Australia maili makili maingĩ aitavany'a na kĩsululu, kamota, na ngalĩ. Mwana-a-asa ũsu nĩwaseũvisye nzĩa ya kũvikĩsya nzyawa sya kũu ũvoo mũseo, na atetheesya kwambĩĩsya ikundi. Nũndũ wa kĩu nĩwamanyĩkie mũno ĩng'alatanĩ yĩu na andũ nĩmamũnengete ndaĩa mũno.
NĨMOOMĨANĨISYE NA MATHĨNA
Australia nĩ ĩmwe ya nthĩ ila syĩ ũtalo mũnini wa andũ, na mũno mũno yĩla ĩng'alatanĩ andũ mataanĩe vyũ. Kwoou andũ ma Yeova nĩmekĩĩte kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana mavikĩe andũ isionĩ ila syĩ naku nthĩnĩ.
Mavainia amwe meekĩie kĩthito ta kyu nĩ Stuart Keltie na William Torrington. Mwaka wa 1933, nĩmakĩlanĩlye yalata ya kĩthangathĩ kĩthei yĩtawa Simpson Desert. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu maendete kũtavany'a taoninĩ ya Alice Springs, ĩla yĩ katĩ katĩ wa nthĩ ya Australia. Ĩla kakalĩ koo kaanangĩkie, nĩmakatiie vau na maendeea na savalĩ. Mwana-a-asa Keltie, ũla weekĩĩtwe kũũ kwa mbwaũ, aendeeie na savalĩ ĩsu akuĩtwe nĩ ngamĩle! Kĩthito kya mavainia asu kĩyaĩ kya mana. Nĩmakomanie na Charles Bernhardt, ũla waĩ na ũteli tũtukanĩ twaĩ William Creek, vala vaĩ na kĩsese kya ngalĩ ya mwaki. Charles Bernhardt nĩwesie kwĩtĩkĩla ũw'o, ata ũteli wake, na akũna ũvainia myaka 15 e weka isionĩ imwe nũmũ na syĩ vaasa sya Australia.
Vate nzika, mavainia asu ma tene nĩmendaa ũkũmbaũ na ũnyiau wa kũmĩĩsya mawetu ala maĩ nzĩanĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe Arthur Willis na Bill Newlands, ala tũmawetie mwambĩĩonĩ, nĩmathĩnĩkie mũno me kĩla kyalonĩ kyoo kya kũtavany'a yĩla ĩng'alatanĩ ya Australia. Matũmĩie syumwa ilĩ kũthi ũasa wa maili 20 (kĩlomita 32) nũndũ mbua yauĩte ĩkananga ĩng'alata yĩu yĩkatw'ĩka ya ndaka nthei. Mavinda amwe maathawa nĩ sua makanyala na makanoa vyũ, na ũyĩthĩa ĩvindanĩ o yĩu no nginya masukume ngalĩ yoo ivumbunĩ nene mũno sya kĩthangathĩ, malikĩle myandanĩ yĩ mavia, na maikĩlanĩlya mbũsĩ syĩ mũthanga mwingĩ. Mavinda maingĩ ngalĩ yoo nĩyaanangĩkaa, na ĩla ũu wesa kwĩthĩwa nĩmaendaa na maaũ kana kĩsululu taoninĩ ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ. Kũthi vo makuaa mĩthenya yĩana ũna na maisyoka maivekala syumwa siana ũna meteele syĩndũ sya kũseũvya ngalĩ yoo ivike. Ĩndĩ mawetu asu mayaamatũla ngoo. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Arthur Willis aeleisye ndeto syaĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya The Golden Age asya: "Vai lelũ ũtesĩlĩka, na vai lelũ mũasa mũno kwa Ngũsĩ [sya Yeova]."
Vainia ũmwe wa ĩvinda ĩasa weetawa Charles Harris awetie kana kũtavany'a ĩng'alatanĩ yĩu na mawetu maingĩ ala wakomanie namo meekie kũmũthengeesya vakuvĩ mũnango na Yeova. Ongelile kwasya: "Nĩ kavaa mũno mũndũ akekala ate na syĩndũ mbingĩ. Ethĩwa Yesũ nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kũkoma nza vate ũndũ ũngĩ, o naitũ ĩla twĩ ũthũkũminĩ witũ nĩtwaĩle kũtana ĩla tweethĩa no nginya twĩke oou." Ũu now'o mavainia aingĩ meekie. Kĩthito kyu kyoo nĩkyatumie ũvoo mũseo ũvika kona syonthe sya nthĩ ĩsu, na andũ aingĩ mũno nĩmatetheeiw'e meeyumya kwondũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai.
^ kal. 4 Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mambĩĩe kwĩtwa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mwaka wa 1931.—Isa. 43:10.

translation:
On March 26, 1937, he was born in Sydney, Australia, and grew up with a strong sense of adventure. He loved exploring the countryside. For years he dreamed of traveling far away, and eventually embarked on a journey of 12,000 miles (19,300 kilometers) in a small plane to return to his homeland of Australia. His companions on this entire trip said that the journey would be difficult or dangerous. He traveled with Arthur Willis and Bill Newlands, and they were both experienced pilots who wanted to fly around the vast continent of Australia.
Going back to the 1920s, Bible Students in Australia were very active in their ministry despite facing opposition and persecution. They used literature to reach many people, and their territory covered half of the United States. Some zealously preached the good news, saying that Jesus commanded them to preach "to the ends of the earth," but they were limited by the boundaries of Australia. (Acts 1:8) Is it possible to expand our ministry further? It depends on our willingness and whether Jehovah blesses our efforts.
PILOTS PIONEERED NEW ROUTES
In 1929, two small groups from Queensland and Western Australia pioneered new routes by visiting homes in remote areas, sometimes traveling great distances. These trips often involved hardship and danger, but they helped spread the message. The pilots were resourceful and courageous, and they overcame many obstacles. The pilots found many interested people during their travels.
Some pilots faced challenges such as bad weather and difficult terrain. For example, in 1932, Bennett Brickell, a 23-year-old pilot from Rockhampton, Queensland, crashed his plane while trying to land on a makeshift airstrip. He survived the crash with only minor injuries. His plane was badly damaged. It had holes, broken wings, and a torn fuselage. But despite the damage to his plane, he remained determined to continue preaching, and he asked Jehovah for guidance. He repaired his plane over 200 miles (320 kilometers) from his hometown, relying on the help of local residents. Thirty years later, Brother Brickell traveled thousands of miles across Australia by plane, car, and foot. This brother pioneered the way for others to preach the good news, and he encouraged them to be bold. His example inspired many others to share the truth with more people.
I IMITATED THEIR EXAMPLE
Australia is one of the largest continents with a small population, and this has presented unique challenges to those who want to reach people with the good news. The Witnesses of Jehovah have put forth great effort to make the good news available to people throughout the continent.
Two other pioneers who showed courage were Stuart Keltie and William Torrington. In 1933, they undertook an arduous journey through the Simpson Desert. Their trip began from Alice Springs, which is located in central Australia. Despite the harsh conditions, they continued their journey on foot. Brother Keltie, who was known for his endurance, walked with his shoes worn out! The efforts of these pioneers were truly remarkable. They met Charles Bernhardt, a man from William Creek, who owned a camel team. Charles Bernhardt was willing to listen, despite his initial skepticism, and he became interested in the Bible for 15 years before moving to another part of Australia.
Later, other pioneers demonstrated similar determination and zeal in spreading the message. For example, Arthur Willis and Bill Newlands, two brothers who were experienced bushmen, traveled extensively to reach isolated areas of Australia. They often had to walk up to 20 miles (32 kilometers) through dense scrubland to find someone who would listen to their message. Some pioneers faced extreme heat and thirst, and they relied on their faith and resourcefulness to overcome obstacles, such as finding water sources and navigating difficult terrain. Many places were very remote, and sometimes it took days to travel to nearby towns or settlements. To cope with the intense heat and humidity, they often started their day early and rested during the hottest hours. These faithful brothers persevered. One pioneer, Arthur Willis, wrote in an article in The Golden Age magazine: "Go on preaching, and go on walking for God [Jehovah]."
Another pioneer named Charles Harris shared his experience of traveling throughout the territory and helping others to learn about Jehovah. He explained: "I have found that people appreciate sincerity. Jesus has empowered us to accomplish this work, so let us continue to proclaim the good news while we still have opportunity." This sentiment was echoed by many other pioneers. Their efforts helped to sow seeds of truth throughout the land, and many people came to know and love the God of heaven.
^ par. 4 Witnesses began using the name Jehovah's witnesses in 1931.—Isa. 43:10.

text:
MBIVILIANĨ yaku ĩandĩko ya Savuli 83:18 yĩalyũlĩtwe ata? Mbivilia ya Kĩkamba, 1974, ĩandĩko yĩu yaasya: "Nĩ kana mamanye no we wĩ weka, syĩtwa yaku nĩ Yeova, nue Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe." Mbivilia ingĩ syaasya oou. Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia mbingĩ syĩtwa Yeova nĩyĩvetetwe na vandũ vayo vakekĩwa "Mwĩaĩi" kana wa "Tene na Tene." Nĩ kyaũ kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa vaa? Nĩ syĩtwa ya Yeova kana nĩ syĩtwa ya ũnene?
Syĩtwa ya Ngai kwa nthoo sya Kĩevelania
Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩwetete syĩtwa. Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia ya kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania ĩandĩko yĩu yĩwetete syĩtwa. Syĩtwa yĩu yĩandĩkĩtwe יהוה (YHWH) kwa nthoo sya Kĩevalania. Kwa Kĩkamba syĩtwa yĩu yĩandĩkawa "Yeova." Syĩtwa yĩu ĩyonekaa ĩandĩkonĩ o yĩmwe ya Mbivilia. Nthĩnĩ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania yonekaa vakuvĩ mavinda 7,000.
Syĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ ya vata mũno ata? Kwa ngelekany'o mboya ya Mwĩaĩi ĩla Yesũ wamanyĩisye. Yaambĩĩte atĩĩ: "Inyw'ĩ ĩndĩ voyaai atĩĩ: Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ, syĩtwa yaku yĩtaĩwe." (Mathayo 6:9) Na ĩngĩ Yesũ avoyie atĩĩ: "Asa, taĩa syĩtwa yaku." Na Ngai asũngĩa e ĩtũnĩ asya: "Nĩnayĩtaĩa, na ngayĩtaĩa ĩngĩ." (Yoana 12:28) Kwoou syĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ ya vata vyũ. Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ alyũli aingĩ mavetete syĩtwa yĩu Mbivilianĩ na makekĩa masyĩtwa ma ũnene?
Veonekana mekĩte ũu nũndũ wa itumi ilĩ nene. Kya mbee, andũ aingĩ maasya syĩtwa yĩu ĩyaĩle kũtũmĩwa nũndũ ĩyĩsĩkĩe ũndũ yatamũkawa tene. Kĩevelania kyaandĩkawa vate nthoo ta; a, e, ĩ, i, o, ũ, u. Kwoou ũmũnthĩ vaiĩ mũndũ ũtonya kũmanya nesa ũndũ nthoo YHWH syatamũkawa tene. Ĩndĩ ũu nũtuma tũeka kũtũmĩa syĩtwa ya Ngai? Ĩvinda ya tene nĩvatonyeka syĩtwa ya Yesũ yĩkethĩwa yatamũkawa Yesua kana Yeosua nũndũ vaiĩ mũndũ ũtonya kũweta nesa ũndũ yatamũkawa. Ĩndĩ andũ nthĩ yonthe matũmĩaa syĩtwa ya Yesũ kwa nzĩa syĩkĩvathũkany'o kwosana na ũndũ yĩtamũkawa kwa ithyomo syoo. Maileaa kũyĩtũmĩa syĩtwa yĩu nĩkwĩthĩwa mayĩsĩ ũndũ yatamũkawa tene. O na we ũkathi nthĩ ĩngĩ nũtonya kwĩthĩa syĩtwa yaku yĩtamũkawa kĩvathũkany'o kwosana na kĩthyomo kya kũu. Kwoou kũlea kũmanya ũndũ syĩtwa ya Ngai yatamũkawa tene kũituma tũtayĩtũmĩa.
Kĩtumi kya kelĩ kyaũveta syĩtwa ya Ngai Mbivilianĩ kyumanĩte na kĩthĩo kya tene kya Ayuti. Aingĩ moo maĩkĩĩaa syĩtwa ya Ngai ĩyaĩle kũtamũkwa. Mũĩkĩĩo ũsu waumanĩte na kũtũmĩa naĩ mwĩao wa Mbivilia ũla waasya: "Ndũkawete syĩtwa ya Yeova Ngai waku mana; nũndũ Yeova ndakasya ũsu nde ĩvĩtyo ũla ũwetaa syĩtwa yake mana."—Kuma 20:7.
Mwĩao ũsu ũvatanĩte kũtũmĩa syĩtwa ya Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩtaĩle. Aandĩki ma Maandĩko ma Mbivilia ma Kievelania (ala metawa "Ũtianĩo Mũkũũ") maĩ andũ aĩkĩĩku na maatĩĩaa mĩao ĩla Ngai wanengete ana ma Isilaeli. Ĩndĩ nĩmatũmĩaa mũno syĩtwa ya Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩmayĩkĩie nthĩnĩ wa savuli ila syainawa nĩ athaithi. Kwoou mwĩao ũsu ũivatanĩte kũyĩtũmĩa kwa ndaĩa. O na Yeova Ngai nĩweeyĩaĩe athaithi make mekaĩlae syĩtwa yake na ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku nĩmeekie ũu. (Yoeli 2:32; Meko ma Atũmwa 2:21) Kwoou Aklĩsto nĩmaĩle kũtũmĩa syĩtwa ya Ngai kwa ndaĩa o ũndũ Yesũ wayĩtũmĩie.—Yoana 17:26.
Alyũli nĩmekaa makosa manene kwĩkĩa Mbivilianĩ masyĩtwa ma ũnene vandũ va syĩtwa ya Ngai. Matumaa Ngai oneka e vaasa na atendete andũ, ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩtũthing'ĩĩasya twĩthĩwe na 'ũnyanya na Yeova.' (Nthimo 3:32) Osa ngelekany'o ya mũnyanyau ũla mũseo vyũ. Atonya kwĩthĩwa e mũnyanyau mũseo vyũ ata ũtesĩ syĩtwa yake? O ta ũu andũ matesĩ Yeova, syĩtwa ya Ngai, matonya kũmũthengeea ata kwa w'o. Ũndũ ũngĩ andũ mateũtũmĩa syĩtwa ya Ngai mayĩsa kũmanya ũndũ yonanasya. Syĩtwa ya Ngai yonanasya ata?
Ngai mwene nĩwaeleisye mũthũkũmi wake Mose ũndũ syĩtwa yake yonanasya. Yĩla Mose wakũlilye ĩũlũ wa syĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova amũsũngĩie amwĩa: "Ninyie ũla ninyie." (Kuma 3:14) Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia ĩaliũlĩtwe nĩ mũndũ wĩtawa Lothaamu ĩandĩko yĩu yaasya: "Ngatw'ĩka kĩla nĩenda." Kwoou Yeova nũtonya kũtw'ĩka kĩla ũkwenda nĩ kana eanĩsye ieleelo syake.
Twasye we wĩna ũtonyi wa kũtw'ĩka kĩla ũkwenda. Nĩ kyaũ ũtonya kũmeka anyanyau? Ũmwe awaa nũtonya kũtw'ĩka ndakĩtalĩ ũkamũiita. Ũngĩ eethĩwa na thĩna wa mbesa nũtonya kũtw'ĩka mũthwii na ũimumya thĩnanĩ. Ĩndĩ o ta andũ ala angĩ, we ndwĩna ũtonyi ũsu. O ũendee na kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ũkatana kwona ũndũ Yeova ũtonya kũtw'ĩka kĩla ũkwenda nĩ kana eanĩsye mawatho make. Nĩwendete kũtũmĩa vinya wake kũtethya ala mamwendete. (2 Mavinda 16:9) Ala matesĩ syĩtwa yake mayĩsa kũmanya ndaĩa isu syonanasya ũndũ Yeova ũilyĩ.
Kwa w'o syĩtwa Yeova nĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa Mbivilianĩ. Kũmanya ũndũ yonanasya na kũyĩtũmĩa ũthaithinĩ waku nĩkũkũtetheeasya mũno kũmũtheengeea Yeova, Ĩthe waitũ wa ĩtunĩ.*
* Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa syĩtwa ya Ngai na ũndũ yonanasya, na nĩkĩ yaĩle kũtũmĩwa ũthaithinĩ, sisya kavuku, Jina La Mungu Litakaloendelea Milele, kakyavĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.

translation:
Has the pronunciation of Psalm 83:18 ever troubled you? The Kikamba Bible, 1974, renders this verse as: "It may be you know me by my name, which is Jehovah, and I am the God of Israel, the God of hosts." Other Bibles render it differently. In many Bibles the name Jehovah is replaced by people who call him "God" or "Lord." Why is this difference? Is it the name of Jehovah or the name of greatness?
The Name of God in Ancient Hebrew
This verse pronounces a name. The ancient Greek Septuagint Bible also pronounces a name. This name is written יהוה (YHWH) in Hebrew script. In Kikamba this name is rendered "Jehovah." This name appears to be written in almost every Bible. According to the Hebrew Scriptures it appears over 7,000 times.
Is the Name of God Important? For example, Jesus taught his followers how to pray. He said: "You must pray like this: 'Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.'" (Matthew 6:9) And again Jesus told them: "Pray, then, let your name be sanctified." And God responds to such prayers: "I have glorified [my name], and I will glorify it again." (John 12:28) Thus the name of God is important. But why do many versions omit pronouncing this name in the Bible and replace it with names of greatness?
It seems that this is a matter of tradition. Often people pronounce God's name incorrectly because they are unfamiliar with the pronunciation of certain sounds. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u. So it is difficult for someone to know precisely how to pronounce the name YHWH correctly. But does this excuse us from trying to use the name of God? It is true that some find it difficult to pronounce the name Jesus correctly—Yeshua or Yehoshua—but this does not excuse anyone from trying to learn the correct pronunciation. And yet many people use the name Jesus in a way that is disrespectful and without regard for its proper pronunciation. To continue using a name incorrectly is disrespectful. Also, you might think that it is difficult to learn the correct pronunciation because of tradition. However, learning to know the correct pronunciation of the name of God can motivate us to use it.
The main reason people avoid pronouncing the name of God is superstition connected with the teaching of the Trinity. Many fear pronouncing the name of God lest they misrepresent it. This fear has led to the use of titles instead of the divine name, such as the following statement found in the Bible: "You must not misuse the name of Jehovah your God, because Jehovah will not hold him guiltless who misuses his name." – Exodus 20:7.
This fear motivates people to avoid pronouncing the name of God in any way. The writings of the Christian Greek Scriptures (also called the "New Testament") show that early Christians used and valued God's personal name. Indeed, they were encouraged to call upon His name. For example, they quoted the prophecy: "Everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved." – Joel 2:32; Acts 2:21. Moreover, Christ encourages us to use God's name sincerely, just as Jesus did. – John 17:26.
Truly, there are serious errors involved in avoiding pronouncing the sacred name of God. It causes God to appear distant and uncaring toward people, while the Bible shows that we are drawn close to Him through 'familiarity with Jehovah.' (Proverbs 3:32) But what about the superstitious fear itself? Can this fear be based on any real reason? No, true worshipers of Jehovah, God's name, can approach Him without hesitation. When people avoid using God's name, it reveals ignorance. Does God's name cause harm?
God himself revealed to his servant Moses that his name does not cause harm. When Moses asked for God's name, Jehovah answered: "I Will Become What I Will Become." (Exodus 3:14) A Bible dictionary explains that the meaning of the name is: "I am causing myself to become." So Jehovah can fulfill whatever purpose he sets for himself.
Let us then have the courage to use His name. Is there any reason to fear pronouncing it? One might feel shy about doing so at first. Many are influenced by the traditions of their forefathers and hesitate to pronounce it. But like others, we too can have this courage. By studying the Bible diligently, you will come to know why Jehovah can fulfill whatever purpose He sets for Himself. The prophets used His name to convey His messages. (2 Kings 16:9) Those who honor His name show that they desire to understand how Jehovah fulfills His purposes.
For those who love the name Jehovah, it is delightful to mention it in connection with the Bible. Understanding and applying what it means will strengthen your faith and bring you closer to Jehovah, our God. Let us continue to share good news with others.*
* If you find further information regarding God's name and its significance, and it would be helpful to others, please share the book, The Name of God That Will Not Be Forgotten, which will help you learn more about Jehovah.

ĩkũlyo
Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo nĩ yĩva?
Ũsungio
Wĩna nzaa eka ya mwĩĩ? wĩna nzaa ya kĩndũ kĩngĩ thayũnĩ? wĩna nzaa ya nthĩnĩ ĩla ĩteanĩaw'a? kethĩwa nĩ ou, Yesũ nĩwe Nzia! Yesũ amea atĩĩ, "Nye ninye mũkate ũla ũetae thayũ. mũndũ ũla ũkaa kwakwa ndakew'a nzaa, na ũla ũndĩkĩĩa ndakew'a waoni ona vanini" ( Yoana 6:35).
Wĩmũvulanĩle? Nĩwaĩwe nĩ nzia kana kĩtũmi kya kwĩkala thayũ? wĩona ta ve mũndũ ũvoetye taa na ndũtonya kũwakanya? ethĩwa nĩ ou, Yesũ nĩwe Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo! Yesũ nĩwaneenie ĩngĩ na andũ amea atĩĩ," Nyie nĩnyie kyeni kya nthĩ. Mũndũ o na wĩva ũla ũngatĩĩaa ndakaendela kĩvindunĩ, ĩndĩ akeethĩwa na kyeni Kĩla kĩetae thayũ" (Yoana 8:12)
Waaĩw'a ta wĩ mũvingĩe nza wa thayũ? Nũtatĩte mĩomo mĩngĩ, na ũkethĩa nĩ vathei kana nĩ kindu kĩte ũtethyo? Nũũmantha nzia ya thayũ mwĩanĩu? kethĩwa nĩu, Yesũ nĩwe Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo. Nye nĩnye mũomo. Yesũ asya, "mũndũ ona wĩva ũla ũlikĩlaa vala nĩĩ akasũvĩĩka; akalikaa na kumaala na kwona kyaũya"( Yoana 10:9)
Kwĩ andũ maleaa kwĩanisya kwenda kwaku? Ngwatanĩo yakũ yĩthĩĩtwe ĩthambalele na nthei? Kĩla mũndũ enda kũũtũmia nai? kethĩwa nĩu, Yesũ nĩwe Nzia! Yesũ asya "Nye ninye mũĩthi ũla mũseo. Mũĩthi ũla mũseo niwiyumasya akw'e kwondũ wa malondu. 14 Nye nĩnye mũĩthi ũla mũseo; nĩnĩsi malondu makwa namo nĩmambĩsĩ" ( Yoana 10: 11,14)
Nũseng'aa Kĩla kĩkethĩwa ĩtina wa thayũ ũũ? Nũnoete ni kwikala thayũ kwondũ wa syindũ ĩla syanangĩkaa kana ikakwata nganga? mavinda amwe nĩwikũlasya kana thayũ wĩ kĩtũmi? nũkwenda kwikala thayũ ĩtina wa kĩkwu? Kethiwa nĩu, Yesũ nĩwe Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo! Yesũ asya ," Na ũla withayũ na ũndĩkĩĩaa ndakakw'a o na ĩndĩĩ. We nũkũĩkĩĩa ũu?" (Yoana 11:25-26).
Nzia nĩ yĩva? ũw'o nĩ mwaũ? Thayũ nĩ mwaũ? Yesũ asũngia," Nye nĩnyie nzia na nĩnyie w'o na nĩnyie thayũ. Vai mũndũ ũendaa Kwa asa atesilite vala nĩĩ" (Yoana 14:6)
Nzaa ĩla ũkwiw'a nĩ ya kĩveva na ĩtonya kwĩanĩw'a nĩ Yesũ. Yesũ nĩwe utonya kũvetanga kĩvindu. Yesũ nĩwe Nzia ya wĩanĩu na thayũ ũtathela. Yesũ nĩwe mũnyanya na mũĩthi ũla ũmanthaa. Yesũ nĩwe thayũ nthĩ ĩno na ĩla yũkĩte. Yesũ nĩwe Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo.
Kĩtũmi Kĩla wĩna mea, kĩtũmi Kĩla ũkwona tawaĩye kĩvindũnĩ, kĩtũmi Kĩla ũtekwona kĩtũmi kya thayũ, nĩkwĩithĩwa nũtaanĩsye na Ngai. mbivilia ĩtwiaa kana twi ene naĩ ithyonthe na kwoou nĩtwataaniw'e na Ngai( Mũtavanya 7:20, Alomi 3:23). Mwanya ũla ũkwiw'a ngooni yakũ nĩ Ngai ũtethayũnĩ wakũ. Wombiwe wĩthĩwe na ngwatanio na Ngai ĩndĩ nũndũ wa naĩ yakũ ngwatanĩo yanangika. Na mbee naĩ yakũ ĩkatũma ũtaanisya na Ngai thayũnĩ ũyũ na thayũ wa tene na tene (Alomi6:23, Yoana 3:36).
Thĩna ũũ ũonya kũthela ata? Yesũ nĩwe Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo! Yesũ nĩwakwĩĩe naĩ syaku (2 Akolintho 5:21). Yesũ niwakwĩe kwondũ wakũ (Alomi 5:8). Ayosa ũsilĩlo ũla ũkwaĩlĩte na ĩtina wa mithenya ĩtatũ Yesũ athayũka Kũma kĩkwũni, ayĩkĩĩthya ũkĩlyo yĩũlũ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. (Alomi 6:4-5). Yesũ ekie oũ Nĩkĩ? Yesũ nĩwasũngĩĩe ĩkũlyo yĩu: " Vai mũndũ wĩthĩwa na wendo ũthonokete ũũ, wa mũndũ kwĩyumya akw'e kwondũ wa anyanyae" ( Yoana15:13). Yesũ akwie nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na thayũ. kethĩwa nũkwia mũĩkĩĩyo waku vala ve Yesũ, na kũĩkĩĩa kĩkwũ kyake ta ndĩvi ya naĩ syaku, naĩ syakũ syonthe nĩ ndekee na kũthambwa. Na ĩndĩ ũkeanĩw'a waoni wakũ wa kĩĩveva. Taa ikakanwa, ũkethĩwa na thayũ mwĩanĩu, ũkamanya mũnyanya wa w'o na mũĩthi mũseo, ũkamanya kana ukethiwa na thayũ ĩtina wa kĩkwu — thayũ wa ũthayũkyo tene na tene vamwe na yesũ.
Nũndũ Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ mũno,nĩwanenganie mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmũĩkĩĩaa ndakae ĩndĩethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela.(Yoana 3:16).
We nĩwatw'a ũtwi kũmwĩtĩkĩla Klisto nũndu wa maũndũ ala wasoma vaa? Ethĩwa nĩ w'o, tina vau vaandikĩtwe "nĩnamwĩtĩkĩla Klisto umunthĩ".
English
Nzia ya ũtangĩĩo nĩ yĩva?
