translation:
Truly
How is the way of life?
Blessings
Where is the key to heaven? Where is the key to the precious kingdom? Where is the key to the gate that saves? The answer is yes, Jesus is the Way! Jesus said, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty again" (John 6:35).
Will you believe? Is it a path or just a means of finding heaven? Do you see people wandering around lost and unable to find their way? The answer is yes, Jesus is the Way of Life! Jesus spoke to them, saying, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life" (John 8:12)
Are there those who don't want the keys to heaven? Let us say many things, and realize whether it is truth or something you think? Shall we search for the way to heaven ourselves? The answer is yes, Jesus is the Way of Life. I am the door. Jesus says, "Whoever enters through me will be saved; he will come in and go out, and find pasture" (John 10:9)
To which sheep does the shepherd lead? What makes his voice beautiful and strong? Does everyone serve him? The answer is yes, Jesus is the Way! Jesus says, "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. 14 I am the good shepherd; I know my sheep and my sheep know me—" (John 10: 11,14)
Shall we seek the key to heaven today? Should we live in heaven because of faith or because of works? Some may stumble or heaven might seem distant? Shall we go to live in heaven through a loophole? The answer is yes, Jesus is the Way of Life! Jesus says, "And anyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?" (John 11:25-26).
What is the way? Who is the truth? Is life the truth? Jesus answered, "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me." (John 14:6)
The life that pleases is to remember and obey Jesus. Jesus is the power to overcome things. Jesus is the way of life and eternal life. Jesus is the shepherd and the good shepherd. Jesus is the life now and the life to come. Jesus is the Way of Life.
Anyone who has a heart, anyone who sees the world, anyone who experiences the life of heaven, should be reconciled with God. Those who practice evil or do wrong and sin are alienated from God (Matthew 7:20, Romans 3:23). That life that pleases God is God's gift to you. Be saved by grace and reconciliation with God instead of your own works of righteousness, so that no one can boast (Romans 6:23, John 3:36).
Can anyone truly live like this? Jesus is the Way of Life! Jesus takes your sins (2 Corinthians 5:21). Jesus bears your punishment (Romans 5:8). Accept the death that you deserve and believe in Jesus Christ who rose from the dead, and you will receive forgiveness of sins and new life (Romans 6:4-5). What did Jesus say about this? Jesus expressed his love like this: "There is no greater love than this—that someone lays down his life for his friends" (John 15:13). Jesus loved even when we were sinners. Believe in Jesus and accept him, and imitate his example, and confess his name with all your heart, and your whole life will be changed and glorified. And through obedience, experience the joy of heaven. But refuse, and continue in sin, and know the shepherd and the good shepherd, and know that you are saved by grace—eternal life with Jesus.
God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life (John 3:16).
Will we listen to Christ and live according to what is written? It is true, we are written "I am following Christ."
What is the way of life?

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1948
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: HUNGARY
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: AĨ NA WENDI WA KŨKWATA MOSŨNGĨO MA MAKŨLYO ALA MA VATA THAYŨNĨ
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Nasyaĩwe mũsyĩ wa Székesfehérvár, nthĩ ya Hungary. Nĩ mũsyĩ wĩ isitolia nzeo ya myaka mbee wa 1,000. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana no nĩlilikanaa ũndũ kaũ wa kelĩ wa nthĩ yonthe waanangie nthĩ yitũ.
Nĩ mũnini naeiwe nĩ asyai ma inyia wakwa. Nĩmalilikanaa nesa vyũ, mũno mũno sũsũ wakwa Elisabeth. Nĩwandetheeisye neethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Kuma nĩ na myaka ĩtatũ, kĩla wĩoo twasyokeleelaa Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi. O na ũu wĩ o vo, ndyaeleawa nĩ kĩla mboya ĩsu yonanasya nginya nĩ myaka vakuvĩ 30.
Naeawa nĩ asyai ma inyia wakwa nũndũ asyai makwa mathũkũmaa kĩla ĩvinda me na mũvango wa kũmbany'a mbesa mathooe nyũmba nzeo ya kwĩkala. Ĩndĩ kĩla Wathanthatũ wa kelĩ wa mwei, nĩtwakomanaa ithyonthe tũkaya lĩu vamwe. Nĩnatanĩaa mavinda asu mũno.
Mwaka wa 1958, asyai makwa nĩmeanĩisye ũndũ mendaa na mathooa nyũmba yitũ twĩ atatũ. Nĩnatanĩie mũno kwĩkala vamwe na asyai makwa! Ĩndĩ ũtanu ũsu nĩwathelile ĩtina wa myei thanthatũ, ĩla ĩthe wakwa wakwie awaĩte kanza.
Natelemile mũno. Nĩlilikanaa ndivoya atĩĩ: "Ngai, nĩnakwĩsũvie ũsũvĩe ĩthe wakwa, na nĩngũmwenda. Nĩkĩ ũtaasũngĩa mboya syakwa?" Nendaa mũno kũmanya vala ĩthe wakwa waĩ. Neekũlasya atĩĩ: 'Aendie ĩtunĩ? Akeethĩwa thayũ ĩngĩ?' Neew'ĩaa syana ila ĩngĩ syaĩ na aaĩthe moo kĩwĩu.
Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ, naendaa vala ĩthe wakwa wathikĩtwe vakuvĩ kĩla mũthenya. Natulasya ndu vu mbũanĩ na ndivoya atĩĩ: "Ngai, ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka nĩenda kũmanya vala ĩthe wakwa ũĩ." O na nĩnavoyaa nĩ kana nĩelewe vata wa thayũ.
Nĩnatwie kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya German nĩ na myaka 13. Nasũanĩaa no nĩkwate mosũngĩo ma makũlyo makwa mavukunĩ ala manene, na me maũndũ maingĩ maandĩkĩtwe kwa kĩthyomo kya German. Mwaka wa 1967, nĩnambĩĩie kũsomea mũsyĩ wa Jena, ũla ĩvindanĩ yĩu waĩ nthĩnĩ wa East Germany. Nasomaa mũno mavuku ma asomi ma German, na mũno mũno ala maneeneaa ĩũlũ wa vala mũndũ waumie. O na kau nĩnasomie maũndũ ma kwendeesya, vaiĩ o na ũmwe waasũngĩa nesa makũlyo makwa. Ndyaaeka kũvoya nĩ kana ngwate mosũngĩo.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Mwaka wa 1970, nĩnasyokie Hungary, vala nakomanie na Rose, ũla wesie kũtw'ĩka kĩveti kyakwa. Ĩvinda yĩu nthĩ ya Hungary yaũngamĩwe nĩ silikalĩ ya Communist. Ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ ĩtina wa kũtwaana, nĩtwakĩĩie nthĩ ya Austria. Kĩeleelo kitũ kyaĩ kwĩsa kũthamĩĩa Sydney, nthĩ ya Australia, vala vekalaa mũndũũme wasyaanĩw'e na inyia wakwa.
Ndyaaĩkala mũno ndakwatĩte wĩa Austria. Mũthenya ũmwe mũndũ twathũkũmaa nake nĩwandavisye kana no nĩkwate mosũngĩo ma makũlyo makwa onthe Mbivilianĩ. Nĩwanengie mavuku me kĩvathũkany'o maneenete ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia. Nasomie mavuku asu onthe, na nĩnendaa kwĩmanyĩsya mũnango. Kwoou, nĩnaandĩkĩie Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, ala maumĩthĩtye mavuku asu na nakũlya nĩtũmĩwe mavuku angĩ.
Mũthenya wa kũtanĩa mwaka witũ wa mbee wa mũtwaano, nĩtwathokeiwe nĩ mwana-a-asa wa mũika wa Austria. Nĩwambeteie mavuku ala neetĩtye, na eeyumya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia vamwe nakwa. Tweemanyĩasya mavinda elĩ kwa kyumwa, nũndũ nĩnendeeaw'a nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya. Twatũmĩaa masaa ana kĩla ĩvinda!
Nĩnendeeiw'e mũno nĩ maũndũ ala Ngũsĩ syamanyĩasya kuma Mbivilianĩ. Naseng'ie mũno ĩla mambonisye ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova, Mbivilianĩ ya kĩthyomo kya Hungary. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 27 ĩla naendaa ĩkanisanĩ, ndyaĩ naaĩw'a ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩiwetwa mũthenya o na ũmwe. Nĩnendeeiw'e mũno nĩ mosũngĩo maseo na me ũtheinĩ ma makũlyo makwa. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩneemanyĩisye kana akw'ũ mayĩthĩawa mesĩ ũndũ o na wĩva, no ũndũ ũmwe na makomete too mũito. (Mũtavan'ya 9:5, 10; Yoana 11:11-15) O na ĩngĩ, nĩneemanyĩisye kana Mbivilia nĩyathanĩte ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ, vala 'kĩkw'ũ kĩtakethĩwa vo ĩngĩ.' (Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4) Nĩĩkwatya ngoona ĩthe wakwa ĩngĩ, nũndũ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ "kũkeethĩwa ũthayũũkyo."—Meko ma Atũmwa 24:15.
Kĩveti kyakwa Rose nĩkyeeyumisye na ngoo yonthe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Nĩtweekie maendeeo na mĩtũkĩ, na twamina kwĩmanyĩsya ĩvuku yĩla twasomaa kwa ĩvinda ya myei ĩlĩ! Nĩtwaendaa maũmbanonĩ onthe ala meekawa nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ. Nĩtwendeeiw'e mũno kwona wendo woo, ũndũ matetheanĩasya, na ũndũ maĩ na ngwatanĩo.—Yoana 13:34, 35.
Mwaka wa 1976, nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa, nĩtweetĩkĩlilw'e kwĩkala Australia. Tũtekwananga ĩvinda nĩtwamanthie Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ngũsĩ ila syaĩ kĩsionĩ kĩu nĩsyatumie twĩw'a twĩ eanĩe. Mwaka wa 1978, nĩw'o twatw'ĩkie Ngũsĩ.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Nĩnesie ũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala manthĩnĩtye kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Kwa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova Ngai, nĩnakwatie Ĩthe ũla mũseo vyũ. (Yakovo 4:8) Na nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwakwa kwĩthĩwa nĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwona ĩthe wakwa ĩngĩ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ.—Yoana 5:28, 29.
Mwaka wa 1989, nĩ na Rose nĩtwasyokie Hungary nĩ kana tũkamanyĩsye anyanya maitũ na andũ ma mũsyĩ, o vamwe na andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala tweemanyĩĩtye. Nĩtwĩthĩĩtwe na kĩanda kya mwanya kya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ maana maingĩ, na andũ 70 katĩ wa asu nĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova. Inyia wakwa nĩ ũmwe katĩ wa asu.
Navoyie kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 17 nĩ kana nĩkwate mosũngĩo ma makũlyo makwa. Na yu myaka ĩngĩ 39 nĩ mĩvĩtu na no nĩvoyaa. O yu ndonya kwasya: "Nĩ mũvea Ĩthe wakwa wa ĩtunĩ, nũndũ wa kũsũngĩa mboya ila navoyaa nĩ mũnini."

translation:
LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1948
THE COUNTRY IS CALLED: HUNGARY
OUR HISTORY: BOTH OLD AND NEW TO GRASP THE PAST AND THE FUTURE TOGETHER
BACKGROUND:
Born in the city of Székesfehérvár, country of Hungary. It is an ancient city over 1,000 years old. In terms of growth, it may have been like a small part of the whole country influencing our country.
My beloved mother is also born. I remember well, especially my dear sister Elisabeth. I was baptized with a great and holy name of God. But I was three years old when we first visited the River of Life. And even now, I understand that every river eventually flows back thirty years.
I know my mother is also born, but she bore me later, every history with the intention of building beautiful houses to live in. Every month of the year, we would meet together and share food. I miss those days very much.
In 1958, my parents decided to do something important and build our house with three rooms. I really enjoyed living with my parents! For five years, it remained a haven for fifty people, but my father passed away first.
I worried a lot. I kept asking myself: "God, will you forgive my sins, and will you accept me? Will you guide my path?" I thought about knowing where my father went. I wondered: 'Will he return? Will he be remembered?' I cried a lot, but another day came with hope.
For many years, I thought about where my father had gone every evening. I struggled and asked myself: "God, please let me know where my father has gone." And I kept wondering if I could understand the truth.
I began learning German when I was 13 years old. I practiced a lot with books and large dictionaries, and many things were written in German. In 1967, I managed to go study at the University of Jena, which was then in East Germany. I studied various German subjects, and this greatly increased my understanding of life. And also, I studied pedagogy, among other things, to help me with those books. I continued to ask myself if I would succeed.
THE REASON FOR MY LATER LIFE:
In 1970, I visited Hungary, where I met Rose, who later became my wife. That period in Hungary was dominated by a communist regime. Because the situation was difficult, we moved to Austria. Our ultimate goal was to immigrate to Sydney, Australia, where I lived with my family and relatives.
I stayed in Austria for some time and married an Austrian woman. One day, someone reminded me about my desire to have books and dictionaries from Mbivili. I remembered my strong longing for Mbivili. I studied diligently, and I wanted to learn more. Later, I wrote "The Book of Jehovah," which helped many people, and I was happy to be used to help others.
During the last year of our marriage, we were visited by the son of a pastor from Austria. I told him about my experiences, and he encouraged me to learn the Bible with him. We studied several places at once, and I continued to want to learn more. We spent hours studying every day!
I am very grateful that "The Book" helped people learn about God, Jehovah, in the Hungarian part of Mbivili. For 27 years, I traveled around, and each time I learned something new about God. I am grateful for the opportunity to share good news with people, even those who seemed uninterested or had objections. (Ecclesiastes 9:5, 10; John 11:11-15) Also, I realized that the Bible teaches us to love our neighbors as ourselves, even those who seem difficult. (Revelation 21:3, 4) I feared causing pain to others, but I knew that sometimes it is necessary to "speak boldly."—Acts 24:15.
My wife, Rose, fully supported me in learning the Bible. We made progress together, and we enjoyed sharing what we learned from the Bible every day! We went to various congregations belonging to the Watch Tower Society. We were moved by their love, unity, and hospitality.—John 13:34, 35.
In 1976, my wife and I emigrated to Australia. We continued to serve Jehovah. The brothers there were very kind and helpful. In 1978, we began pioneering.
WHAT HELPS ME:
I try to remember the kindness shown to me over the years. Because of my close relationship with Jehovah God, I have gained strength. (James 4:8) And I know that I can continue to gain strength by remembering the hope of life for others.—John 5:28, 29.
In 1989, Rose and I returned to Hungary to help more people and others learn about important things. We were able to preach to many people, including some who were interested in what we taught. We were given the privilege of preaching the Bible to many people, and 70 became Jehovah's Witnesses. My family was among them.
For 17 years, I continued to travel extensively. Now, another 39 years have passed, and I am still traveling. But now I can say: "I look forward to eternal life, and I will continue to serve faithfully as long as I live."

text:
Kũmbwa kwa Syĩndũ Syonthe
1Mwambĩlĩĩlyonĩ yĩla Ngai woombie ĩtu na nthĩ, 2nthĩ ndyaĩ na wũmbo na yaĩ nthei. Kwaĩ kĩw'ũ kingĩ kyavw'ĩkĩte syĩndũ syonthe, nakyo kĩkavw'ĩkwa nĩ kĩvindu kya ngokomi. Veva wa Ngai aĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩw'ũ kĩu kingĩ. 3#2Ako 4.6 Na Ngai asya atĩĩ, "Nĩkwĩthĩwe kyeni," na kweethĩwa kyeni. 4Ngai nĩwoonie kyeni kĩu kĩ kĩseo. Nĩvo ĩndĩ wavathanisye kyeni kĩu na kĩvindu kĩu. 5Ngai nĩweetie kyeni kĩu, "Mũthenya," nakyo kĩvindu akĩta, "Ũtukũ." Nĩkwatukie na kwakya; ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa mbee.
2Vet 3.5
Na Ngai asya atĩĩ, "Nĩkwĩthĩwe yayaya yĩaany'e kĩw'ũ kũndũ kwĩlĩ." 7Kwoou Ngai nĩwoombie yayaya na aany'a kĩw'ũ kĩu; kĩmwe kyeethĩwa ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ na kĩla kĩngĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo. 8Ngai nĩweetie yayaya ĩtu. Nĩkwatukie na kwakya; ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa kelĩ.
9Na Ngai asya atĩĩ, "Kĩw'ũ kĩla kĩ ĩtheo wa ĩtu kĩsyokeanĩe vandũ vamwe na nthĩ nyũmũ yumĩle," na ũu weethĩwa. 10Ngai nĩweetie mũthanga mũmũ, "Nthĩ," na kĩw'ũ kĩla kyasyokeanĩie vandũ vamwe akĩta, "Ũkanga." Ngai nĩwasyaisye wĩa ũsu wake na endeew'a nĩw'o. 11Nĩvo ĩndĩ Ngai waisye atĩĩ, "Nĩkwĩthĩwe na mĩthemba yonthe ya mĩmea ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, mĩmea ĩla ĩsyaa mĩthemba yĩ kĩvathũkany'o ya mbeke, na mĩtĩ ĩsyaa matunda me ngii syĩ kĩvathũkany'o," na ũu weethĩwa. 12Nthĩ nĩyeethĩiwe na mĩmea; mĩmea ĩsyaa mbeke syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na mĩtĩ ĩsyaa matunda me ngii syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ngai nĩwasyaisye wĩa ũsu wake na endeew'a nĩw'o. 13Nĩkwatukie na kwakya; ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa katatũ.
14Na Ngai asya atĩĩ, "Nĩkwĩthĩwe kyeni yayayanĩ, kĩvathany'e mũthenya na ũtukũ na kwonanasya mĩthenya, myaka na mavinda me kĩvathũkany'o. 15Kyeni kĩu kĩ yayayanĩ nĩkĩmulĩkae nthĩ," na ũu weethĩwa. 16Kwoou Ngai nĩwaseũvisye syeni ilĩ nene, syũa yĩmulĩkae mũthenya na mwei ũimulĩkaa ũtukũ; o ta ũu nĩwaseũvisye ndata. 17Ngai nĩwaiie syĩndũ isu yayayanĩ, nĩ kana imulĩkae ĩũlũ wa nthĩ; 18imulĩkae ũtukũ na mũthenya na kũvathany'a kyeni na kĩvindu. Ngai nĩwasyaisye wĩa ũsu wake na endeew'a nĩw'o. 19Nĩkwatukie na kwakya; ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa kana.
20Na Ngai asya atĩĩ, "Kĩw'ũ kyusũwe nĩ syũmbe syĩ thayũ na yayaya yusũwe nĩ nyũnyi." 21Kwoou Ngai nĩwoombie nyamũ ila nene sya ũkanganĩ, na syũmbe sya mĩthemba yonthe ila syĩkalaa kĩw'ũnĩ, na nyũnyi sya mĩthemba yonthe. Ngai nĩwasyaisye wĩa ũsu wake na endeew'a nĩw'o. 22Ngai nĩwaiathimie na asya atĩĩ, "Syaanai mwingĩve musũe kĩw'ũnĩ kĩla kĩ ũkanganĩ na nyũnyi nĩsingĩve ĩũlũ wa nthĩ." 23Nĩkwatukie na kwakya; ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa katano.
24Na Ngai asya atĩĩ, "Nthĩ nĩyumĩlye syũmbe sya kĩla mũthemba: Nyamũ sya mũsyĩ na sya kĩthekanĩ, na tũsamũ tũnini," na ũu weethĩwa. 25Kwoou Ngai nĩwoombie syũmbe sya mĩthemba yonthe: Nyamũ sya mũsyĩ na sya kĩthekanĩ, na tũsamũ tũnini. Ngai nĩwasyaisye wĩa ũsu wake na endeew'a nĩw'o.
1Ako 11.7
Nĩvo ĩndĩ Ngai waisye atĩĩ, "Nĩtũmbe andũ me na mũvw'ano witũ na kĩtutya kitũ. Makeethĩwa na ũkũmũ ĩũlũ wa makũyũ, nyũnyi, nyamũ syonthe sya mũsyĩ na sya kĩthekanĩ, na tũsamũ tw'onthe tũla tũnini." 27#Mat 19.4; Mk 10.6 #Mwa 5.1-2 Kwoou Ngai nĩwoombie andũ mailyĩ take; amomba mailyĩ take. Nĩwoombie mũndũ-ũme na mũndũ mũka. 28Ngai nĩwamaathimie na asya atĩĩ, "Syaanai mwingĩve musũe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, na mũyĩthĩwa na ũtonyi ĩũlũ wayo. Ĩthĩwai na ũkũmũ ĩũlũ wa makũyũ, nyũnyi na nyamũ ila ingĩ syonthe syĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ." 29Na Ngai asyoka asya atĩĩ, "Nĩngũmũnenga mĩmea yonthe ĩla ĩsyaa mbeke na mĩtĩ yonthe ĩla ĩsyaa matunda yĩthĩwe lĩu wenyu. 30Nĩnĩnenganĩte nyeki na matũ syĩthĩwe lĩu wa nyamũ na nyũnyi syonthe, na tũsamũ tw'onthe tũla twĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ," na ũu weethĩwa. 31Ngai nĩwasyaisye wĩa ũsu wake na kwa w'o nĩwamwendeeisye mũno. Nĩkwatukie na kwakya; ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa thanthatũ.

translation:
1
The Creation of Heaven and Earth
1In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth, 2the earth was without form and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters. And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. 4God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness. 5God called the light day, and he called the darkness night. And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
6 #
2Gen 3.5
And God said, "Let there be an expanse between the waters to separate water from water." 7So God made the expanse and separated the water under the expanse from the water above it. 8God called the expanse sky. And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.
9And God said, "Let the water under the sky be gathered to one place, and let dry ground appear," and it was so. 10God called the dry ground land, and the gathering together of the waters he called seas. And God saw that it was good. 11Then God said, "Let the land produce vegetation—seed-bearing plants and trees bearing fruit yielding seed according to their kinds," and it was so. 12The land produced vegetation—plants bearing seed according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed in them. And God saw that it was good. 13And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.
14And God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs to mark seasons and days and years, 15and let them be lights in the expanse of the sky to shine on the earth." And it was so. 16God made two great lights—the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars. 17God set them in the expanse of the sky to shine on the earth; 18to govern the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good. 19And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.
20Then God said, "Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky." 21God created great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teem, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good. 22God blessed them and said, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth." 23And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.
24Then God said, "Let the land produce living creatures according to their kinds—livestock, creeping things, and wild animals each according to its kind." And it was so. 25God made the wild animals each according to its kind, the livestock each according to its kind, and all the creatures that creep along the ground each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
26 #
1Genesis 11.7
Thus says God, "I will bless them with my covenant and my fear. They shall be afraid of you, every beast of the field, every bird of the air, all creatures that crawl on the ground, and all fish of the sea under the heavens that move about. 27#Matthew 19.4; Mark 10.6 #Exodus 5.1-2 Thus says God, I have created all these creatures; I have given them life. I have blessed mankind; I have given them dominion over all creatures, over beasts and birds, and everything that crawls on the ground." 28God commanded them and said, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, and every living creature that moves on the ground." 29And God also said, "I give you every plant yielding seed that is on the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed in its fruit. This shall be food for you." 30"And to every beast of the earth, every bird of the air, and every creature that creeps on the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it—I have given all green plants for food." And it was so. 31God saw all that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.

text:
Aisilaeli, ala maĩ andũ ma Ngai ĩvindanĩ ya tene nĩmathĩnaw'a. Na kwoou nĩmamũvoyaa Ngai mavinda maingĩ nĩ kana amatetheesye, ĩndĩ mayaakwata ũtethyo ũsu vau kwa vau. Andũ ala mamathĩnasya maĩ Amisili, ala maĩ na vinya kũmakĩla. (Kuma 1:13, 14) Aisilaeli asu nĩmeeteelile myaka mingĩ nĩ kana Ngai amaumye ũkombonĩ wa Amisili. Ĩtina ĩvinda ya Ngai ya kwosa ĩtambya nĩyavikie. (Kuma 3:7-10) Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai nĩwe wokitie na Amisili. Aeteie Amisili mokũno maatĩanĩe, na amwananga mũsumbĩ wa Misili na nguthu yake nthĩnĩ wa Ũkanga Mũtune. (Savuli 136:15) Yeova Ngai nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana aĩ "mũndũ wa kaũ" kwondũ wa andũ make.—Kuma 15:3, 4.
Nũndũ Ngai nĩwe wokitie na Amisili, ũu wĩonany'a kana ndaleanĩte na makaũ onthe. O na ve mavinda angĩ wameĩaĩie Aisilaeli makokite. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwameie makokite na Akanaani ala maĩ athũku mũno. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 9:5; 20:17, 18) Nĩwamwĩaĩie mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli weetawa Ndaviti akokite na Avilisiti ala mamathĩnasya mũno. O na Ngai nĩwamũtavisye Ndaviti ũndũ mekwĩvanga nĩ kana masinde kaũ ũsu.—2 Samueli 5:17-25.
Maũndũ asu maandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ meonany'a kana ĩla mbaĩ ila syathyũlũlũkĩte Aisilaeli syamavinyĩĩa kana syameka maũndũ mathũku, Ngai nĩweetĩkĩlasya kaũ nĩ kana asũvĩe andũ make vamwe na ũthaithi wa w'o. Ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa atatũ ĩũlũ wa makaũ asu Ngai wambĩĩasya.
NGAI NĨWE WAWETAA ŨLA WAĨLE KŨKITA. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Ngai eeie Aisilaeli atĩĩ: "Mũtikethĩwa na vata wa kũkita kaũnĩ ũũ." Nĩkĩ Ngai waisye ũu? Nũndũ nĩwe wesaa kũkita kwondũ woo. (2 Mavinda 20:17; 32:7, 8) Ve mavinda maingĩ wamokitĩie o tondũ vonanĩtw'e mwambĩĩonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ. Mavinda angĩ Ngai nĩwameyĩaĩaa andũ make Aisilaeli mokite makaũ ala weetĩkĩlĩtye. Mokitaa makaũ asu nĩ kana mose Nthĩ ya Watho na maimĩsiĩĩa.—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 7:1, 2; Yosua 10:40.
NGAI NĨWE WAWETAA ĨLA KAŨ ŨSU WAĨLE KŨKITWA. Athũkũmi ma Ngai maaĩle kweteela nginya ĩla wĩmatavya ĩvinda yĩla yaĩlĩte ya kũkita na amaitha ala mamathyũlũlũkĩte. Ngai atanesa kũmeyĩaĩa, mayaĩlĩte kũkita. Na ĩla meeka ũu, Ngai ndeethĩawa vamwe namo. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana ĩla Aisilaeli mathi kaũnĩ Ngai atameyĩaĩe, nĩmasindawa. *
NGAI NDENDEEAW'A NĨ KĨKW'Ũ KYA ANDŨ, O NA ALA ATHŨKU. Yeova nĩwe wĩ na mbuluti ya thayũ na nowe Mũmbi witũ. (Savuli 36:9) Kwoou ndendeeaw'a nĩ kwona andũ maikw'a. Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, ve andũ mavangaa kũũmĩsya ala angĩ kana kũmoaa. (Savuli 37:12, 14) Mavinda amwe Yeova nĩweetĩkĩlasya kaũ nĩ kana amine ũthũku ta ũsu. O na ũu wĩ o vo, ĩvinda yonthe yĩla Ngai weetĩkĩlasya Aisilaeli mokite eethĩawa e "tei" na "mũmĩĩsya wa kũthata" kwelekela ala mavinyĩaa Aisilaeli. (Savuli 86:15) Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩweeyĩaĩe Aisilaeli kana matanamba kũthi kũkita na mbaĩ o na yĩ va maaĩle 'kũmĩkũlya wĩw'ano' nĩ kana manenge ekali ma nthĩ ĩsu mwanya wa kũalyũla nzĩa syoo nĩ kana maikokite namo. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 20:10-13) Kwa kwĩka ũu, Ngai nĩwoonanisye kana 'ndatanĩthaw'a nĩ kĩkw'ũ kya mũthũku; ĩndĩ endaa ũla mũthũku ethyũũe atie mũendele wake na kwĩkala thayũ.'—Esekieli 33:11, 14-16. *
Kumana na maũndũ asu mawetwa, twoona kana ĩvinda ya tene Ngai oonaa kaũ neyo nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte ya kũmina ũthũku vamwe na andũ ala mavinyĩĩaa angĩ. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, no Ngai mwene, ĩndĩ ti mũndũ, wawetaa ĩla kaũ ũsu waaĩlĩte kũkitwa na ũla waaĩlĩte kũwũkita. Ũu nĩkwonany'a kana Ngai nĩwendeeaw'a mũno nĩ kaũ? Aiee. Ũw'o nĩ kana nũmenete ũng'endu. (Savuli 11:5) Woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ nĩwaalyũkile ĩla Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, wambĩĩie kũtavany'a kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ?
^ kal. 7 Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe Aisilaeli nĩmasindiwe ĩtina wa kũthi makokite na Aamaleki na Akanaani, Ngai atamanengete mwanya wa kwĩka ũu. (Motalo 14:41-45) Ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ, mũsumbĩ waĩ mũĩkĩĩku Yosia nĩwaendie kaũnĩ Ngai atamwĩtĩkĩlĩtye, na ũu nĩwatumie oawa.—2 Mavinda 35:20-24.
^ kal. 8 Aisilaeli mayaakũlya Akanaani wĩw'ano matanamba kũkita namo. Nĩkĩ mataaĩka ũu? Nũndũ Akanaani nĩmanengetwe myaka 400 nĩ kana matie ũthũku woo. Ĩvinda yĩla Aisilaeli mookie kũkita namo, Akanaani maĩ mathũkĩĩie ĩ ya mũno.(Mwambĩlĩlyo 15:13-16) Kwoou maaĩlĩte kwanangwa vyũ. O na ũu wĩ o vo, Akanaani ala maalyũkile mayaanangwa.—Yosua 6:25; 9:3-27.

translation:
Israelites, do not associate with people who worship false gods. For God will become angry with you if you imitate those who practice idolatry, each one encouraging his neighbor. Those people have turned away from me, Israelites, they do not understand. (Psalm 1:13, 14) The Israelites spent many years without recognizing that God was rescuing Egypt. His powerful hand was stretched out. (Psalm 3:7-10) The Bible teaches that God defeated Pharaoh and Egypt. He struck Egypt with plagues, and he destroyed the firstborn of Egypt with great severity. (Psalm 136:15) Jehovah God showed that he was an "everlasting God" toward his people.—Psalm 15:3, 4.
Therefore, since God defeated Pharaoh, it should be clear that we should not rely on military strength. But there were many other nations whom Israel conquered. For example, he conquered the Canaanites who lived in that land. (Joshua 9:5; 20:17, 18) He helped King David of Israel conquer the Philistines who troubled them greatly. And God made David successful in everything he did.—2 Samuel 5:17-25.
The things written in the Bible show that if the Israelites repeatedly disobeyed and did wicked things, God would sometimes feel sorry for his people and spare them from destruction. Because of his compassion for his people, God would forgive their sins.
GOD IS THE ONE WHO GIVES VICTORY. Once God told the Israelites: "Do not be afraid of anyone because I will give you victory." Why was God able to say this? Because he has the power to give victory. (2 Kings 20:17; 32:7, 8) There have been many times when they were outnumbered, yet God gave them victory. In some cases, God encouraged his people, the Israelites, to fight against their enemies. Fighting those battles showed his power and his faithfulness.—Joshua 7:1, 2; 10:40.
GOD IS THE ONE WHO GIVES VICTORY EVEN WHEN IT SEEMS IMPOSSIBLE. Sometimes God allows his servants to face difficult situations so that they can demonstrate their faith and trust in him during battle and hardship. God tests their loyalty, proving whether they will continue to trust him. And when they do, God supports them. The Bible shows that when the Israelites trusted that God would help them, they were saved.*
GOD SHOWS FAVOR TO PEOPLE, BOTH GOOD AND BAD. Jehovah is the one who shines his favor on us and is our Creator. (Psalm 36:9) Showing favor means being kind to people. One reason why there is injustice is that wicked people oppress others and harm them. (Psalm 37:12, 14) However, Jehovah sometimes shows kindness even to imperfect humans. But even though he does, the victories that God gives the Israelites are described as being due to his "loving-kindness" and "steadfast love," which are qualities that he shows to his people. (Psalm 86:15) For example, he reminded the Israelites that if they continued to sin and did not stop practicing idolatry, he would no longer 'forgive their sins' and they would suffer the consequences of their actions. (Joshua 7:10-13) Therefore, God made it clear that 'his heart pained him over the wickedness of the people; he wanted the wicked person to turn away from his evil ways and live.'—Ezekiel 33:11, 14-16.*
In view of all these things, we see that God often acts in harmony with his purpose of showing mercy to those who exercise faith, while also dealing justly with those who oppose him. In fact, because he is God, he has the right to decide when to show mercy and when to carry out judgment. This raises the question: Does God show favoritism? No. He is righteous. (Psalm 11:5) The way God acted toward his Son, Jesus Christ, proves this beyond doubt.
^ par. 7 For example, when the Israelites were about to fight against Amalek and Canaan, God encouraged them to do so. (Numbers 14:41-45) Many years later, King Josiah showed himself to be faithful to God, and God rewarded him for it.—2 Kings 35:20-24.
^ par. 8 The Israelites did not completely annihilate the Canaanites. Why was this? Because the Canaanites had been allowed to live for 400 years, during which time they committed great wickedness. By allowing the Israelites to coexist with the Canaanites, God gave them an opportunity to repent.(Proverbs 15:13-16) However, most of them did not take advantage of this opportunity. And so they met their deserved end.—Joshua 6:25; 9:3-27.

Maiũ ma Sũsũ
Catherine Groenewald
Sũsũ aĩ vakuvĩ mĩaka mĩongo mwonza. Aĩ mũthangaau. Mũũndanĩ kwake avandaa mũvya, mwee, manga na maiũ. Sũsũ akethaa maiũ kĩla ĩvinda ya mwaka.
Sũsũ aĩna syana mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ katĩka onthe, nyie na aamwaiya na eetwiya kwa kĩmbithĩ nĩtwesĩ sũsũ nũtwendete kũvĩta ala angĩ. Nau nĩwe waĩ ĩlumaita ya sũsũ kwou atũkua kwa nzĩa ya mwanya. Kwa ngelekany'o nĩwokaa mũsyĩ kwitũ mavinda maingĩ.
Na kĩngĩ nowatwĩtaa nyũmba kwake mavinda maingĩ. Ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ syonthe sũsũ nĩwatũtavasyaa syĩmbithĩ syake ĩndĩ ve kĩmbithĩ kĩmwe ũtatũtavya: vala waindĩa maiũ make. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnonie kĩkavũ kya malala kiĩtwe suanĩ nza wa nyũmba ya sũsũ. Ĩla nakũlilye nĩ kyakĩ nanengiwe ũsũngĩo ũmwe kana nĩ kĩkavũ kya syama. Sũsũ anzũngĩa ou nĩwendee kũalyũla kĩtembe kya maiũ methĩ kĩla watĩlĩte kĩokonĩ kĩu.
Vakuvĩ na kĩkavũ vaĩna mathangũ ma maiũ wekalaa akwalyũla ĩvinda kwa ĩvinda. "Mathangũ asu nĩmakĩ sũsũ?" nĩnamũkũlilye na anzũngĩa, "Aa nĩ mathangũ makwa ma kwĩka syama." Mũminũkĩlyo, sũsũ nĩwombĩanĩe maiũ onthe ala maĩ nyekinĩ. Kyaĩ kĩndũ kya kwendeesya kwona sũsũ, ĩiũ ĩnene matũ ma maiũ na kĩkavũ kya malala kĩnene. Onew'a nĩnendaa kwĩloela nĩmanye ũndũ sũsũ ũkũtũmĩa syĩndũ isu syonthe, sũsũ nĩwandũmie ngeete kĩndũ kuma vala ve mwaitũ.
Ndililikana kĩndũ kĩu kyaĩ kyaũ. Nĩnamwĩsũvie ngũmwĩa, "Sũsũ naku eka nambe kwona wĩsovya." "Eke kwĩthĩwa kana keemu, ĩka ũndũ watavwa." Sũsũ nĩwasũngĩie. Nĩnaumie nĩsembete. Nasyokethya nethĩie sũsũ ailye nza wa nyũmba. "Sũsũ, kĩkavũ kĩva na maiũ na?" ĩndĩ ũsũngĩo ũla nakwatie nĩkana, "Syĩvandũnĩ vakwa va syama." Nĩnendaa kũmanya vandũ vau va syama ĩndĩ namũkũlya sũsũ nĩwendee kwĩtwĩkĩthya kana ndakwĩw'a na aendea kw'ina wathi. Nĩnakwie ngoo.
Matukũ elĩ mathela sũsũ aĩna mĩtũkĩ ya kũthi mũkutano ndũanĩ. Nĩwandũmie ngamwosee ndata yake lumunĩ ya kũkoma. Ĩla navingũie mwango wa lumu ĩsu nĩnathokiswe nĩ muuke wa maiũ makwĩw'a.
Lumunĩ ya nzĩnĩ ĩũsũĩte syĩndũ sya sũsũ nĩvo vaĩna kĩla kĩkavũ kya sũsũ kya syama kĩvĩthĩtwe nĩ ĩvula ĩkũũ. Nĩnavwĩkũie ĩvula na muuke wa maiũ wongelekela. Wasya wa sũsũ nĩwandelemilye akwasya, "Wĩka ata we? Ngalatĩle ndata yakwa." Nĩnamũsembeesye ndata na angũlya, "Nĩ kyaũ ukwetye kwenyea kũtheka?" Ĩkũlyo yake nĩyatumiswe ngũmanya kana nonendee kwenyeea ĩtheka nũndũ wa kũmanya vala vandũ va syama.
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe sũsũ ooka kũnena na mwaitũ nĩnosie kamwanya ka kũsemba nyũmbanĩ kwake ngasisye maiũ ĩngĩ. Vaĩ kĩtembe kĩmwe kyew'ĩte vyũ. Nĩnaumisye ĩiũ ĩmwe na navitha ĩlindanĩ. Natũngĩa kĩla kĩndũ nĩnasyokie nyũmba na naya ĩiũ yakwa na mĩtũkĩ. Ndyaya ĩiũ yany'a mũyo ũu ĩngĩ!
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe nĩnetelile sũsũ athi kuuna mboka nasemba kũsisya ala maiũ. Vakuvĩ onthe nĩmew'ĩte. Ndyenamba kũmĩĩsya kũlea kwosa. Nĩnosie ana na nekalata kuumala nolwa kũvwĩka kĩkavũ.
Nuumalĩte kavola na mĩthya ya syaa sya maaũ Nĩnew'ie sũsũ akũkoa vu nza. Nĩnatatie kũvitha maiũ asu ĩlindanĩ. Namina kũya nĩnasyokie na wethĩa sũsũ ndanamanya mĩvango yakwa. Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe waĩ wa ndũnyũ. Sũsũ nĩwokĩlile tene nũndũ kĩla wa ndũnyũ nĩwatwaa maiũ meu na manga kũta. Ndyekalata kũthi kũmũkethya mũthenya ũsu. Ĩndĩ ndyenamba kũmwĩvitha kĩlungu kyaasa.
Masaa ma wĩyoo ĩla netiwe nĩ mwaitũ na nau na sũsũ nĩneesĩ kĩla ngwĩtĩwa. Ũtukũ ngũkoma nĩneesĩ kana ndikang'ea kĩndũ kya sũsũ kana kya asyai makwa kana kya mũndũ ũngĩ.

The tears of Susu
Catherine Groenewald
Susu is eighty years old. She is beautiful. Her garden has flowers, trees, and fruits. Susu harvests fruits every season of the year.
Susu has many children. Some live far away, others visit and stay for a while, and we miss Susu when they leave to go to other places. She is the source of Susu's strength so that she can grow with time. Because of this, she remains young for many years.
And often we spend time at her home for many days. The smell of all the food Susu cooks makes us feel comfortable and happy; there is always something to eat: delicious fruits from her garden. One day I saw a small bird perched on the roof of Susu's house. But I realized it was just a dream or a vision. Susu teaches us to appreciate the value of fruits whenever we finish eating them.
Eighty years old and with wisdom, she has treasures of fruits which she harvests daily. "What are those things Susu?" I asked her, and she replied, "They are special fruits for making juice." Smiling, Susu shares all the fruits with everyone. It is a wonderful thing to see Susu, her large hands full of fruits and a small bird perched nearby. Sometimes I want to understand what Susu means when she says everything is good, Susu loves people more than anything else.
I remember this one thing about her. I told her, "Susu, please let me help you carry some." "Just sit down or rest, let whatever needs to be done be done." Susu insisted. I obeyed and waited patiently. I was surprised to see Susu eating the leftovers from the house. "Susu, does the bird also like fruits?" I asked, and she answered, "Her children love juice." I wanted to know who her children were, and I saw Susu going to call someone or perhaps she went to meet someone elsewhere. I wondered then.
Many days passed and Susu continued to hold meetings with people. I loved watching her share her wealth generously. But I didn't understand why she always trusted the children of those who came.
The story of today is that Susu and her family have a lot of birds whose songs are heard everywhere. I noticed the birds and the children of the house increasing. The mother of Susu scolded them saying, "Are you not ashamed? Show me your wealth." I showed her my wealth and she asked, "Is this enough to make a living?" Her question made me realize that maybe I should go look for ways to earn a living so I can help the children.
Yesterday, when she finished talking to our father, she gave me a little task of sweeping her house instead of the others. They walked together for a while. I followed her and completed the task. I carried everything I swept from the house and took it outside with the children. What a great day it was!
Yesterday, she sent Susu to tell us to stop bringing fruits. All the elders agreed. I decided to try and learn how to live well. She gave me a child and a letter to take to the person who taught her about birds.
Finally, I returned with news from the land of the Maasai. I found Susu digging up roots. I tried to help her with the work but she told me to go and find out what the children were doing. I went and saw that they knew their tasks very well. Yesterday was a good day. Susu was happy because everyone had taken their animals home and eaten well. I wrote a letter asking her to teach me more about yesterday. Today I want to ask her for advice.
Those times when she visited our father and me and Susu, she always remembered something. At night, I wondered if I would ever forget what Susu did for me or what my mother did or what another person did.

"Tũsũanĩe Vamwe"
Yeova ndatiaa ala melilaa nũndũ nĩmekĩte naĩ. Ũw'o nĩ kana nũmamanthaa mamũsyokee! Nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya mwana kĩmaamai, Yesũ aelekanĩtye Yeova na ĩthe wĩ wendo ũla mwana wake watiie mũsyĩ na athi kwĩlikya maũndũnĩ mathũku. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda mwana ũsu nĩwatwie kũsyoka mũsyĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye, 'Ĩndĩ e kũasa, ĩthe wake amwona, na eew'a ĩnee, asemba, amũkwatĩla ngingonĩ, na amũmumunya.' (Luka 15:11-20) No wĩthĩwe wendaa kũmũthengeea Yeova ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa wĩĩw'a wĩ o "kũasa" nake? Lilikana kana o ta ĩthe ũla ũwetetwe ngelekany'onĩ ya Yesũ, Yeova nũkwĩw'ĩaa tei na ĩnee. E na mea ma kũũthokya ũmũsyokee.
Nao nata ethĩwa wĩona naĩ syaku syĩ mbingĩ kana syĩ ngito ũkethĩa Yeova ndesa ũkũekea? Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ndeto ii sya Yeova syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Isaia 1:18: "Ũkai yu, tũsũanĩe vamwe, easya ũu Yeova: o na ethĩwa naĩ syenyu nĩ ndune mũno, ikeethĩwa nzaũ ta ĩa." Ĩĩ, o na naĩ ila twonaa tũtaekewa, Yeova no atũekee.
Yeova ndendaa ũtindĩe kũthĩnĩka nũndũ wa ĩvĩtyo weekie. Kwoou ũtonya kũtanĩa ata kũekewa naĩ nĩ Ngai, na kwĩthĩwa na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo? Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa matambya elĩ Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti woosie. Mbee, aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩngũmumbũlĩla Yeova mavĩtyo makwa." (Savuli 32:5) Lilikana kana Yeova nũkũthoketye ũmũvikĩae mboyanĩ na 'kũsũanĩa' vamwe nake. Ndũkalee aikũthokya. Mumbũlĩle Yeova naĩ syaku na ũimũelesya ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Kumana na maũndũ ala mamũkwatie Ndaviti aĩ atonya kũvoya ũũ na ũkũmbaũ: "Nthesya naĩ yakwa. . . . Ngoo ĩla ndũlĩku na yĩ na wĩlilo, we Ngai, ndũkamĩvũthya."—Savuli 51:2, 17.
Kelĩ, Ndaviti nĩwatetheeiw'e nĩ mwathani Nathani, ũla wanyuvĩtwe nĩ Yeova. (2 Samueli 12:13) Ũmũnthĩ Yeova nũnenganĩte atumĩa ma kĩkundi ala mamanyĩĩtw'e kũtetheesya andũ ala meelila ĩtina wa kwĩka naĩ, nĩ kana matũngĩĩe ngwatanĩo yoo na Yeova. Ĩla wĩthi kwona atumĩa ma kĩkundi, makatũmĩa Maandĩko na maivoya mboya itonya kũkiakisya ngoo yaku, ikaolanga woo ũla ũkwĩw'a, kana ikavetanga woo ũsu vyũ na iũtetheesya kũkwata vinya kĩ-veva.—Yakovo 5:14-16.
"Kũathimwa Nĩ Mũndũ Ũla Ũekewe Ĩvĩtyo Yake"
Ũw'o nĩ kana no wĩw'e kũmũelesya Yeova Ngai naĩ syaku na kũmavikĩa atumĩa ne ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala me vinya vyũ. Vate nzika, Ndaviti eew'aa o taku. Ambie 'kũvindya' o kwa ĩvinda ĩũlũ wa naĩ syake. (Savuli 32:3) Ĩndĩ ĩtina nĩwesie kwona ũseo wa kwĩthĩwa aumbũlile naĩ syake na alũnga mwĩkalĩle wake.
Ũathimo ũmwe mũnene Ndaviti wakwatie nĩkwĩthĩwa na ũtanu ĩngĩ. Aandĩkie ũũ: "Kũathimwa nĩ mũndũ ũla ũekewe ĩvĩtyo yake, ũla naĩ yake ĩvw'ĩkĩtwe." (Savuli 32:1) O na ĩngĩ avoyie atĩĩ: 'Ame Mwĩaĩi, tumũkany'a ilomo syakwa; na kanyw'a wakwa ũkoonany'a ndaĩa syaku.' (Savuli 51:15) Ĩla Ndaviti waekie kũthĩnĩka ngoonĩ nũndũ wa naĩ syake na oona ũekeo wa Ngai wĩ wa vata, maũndũ asu nĩmatumie atavya angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova.
Yeova endaa ũtanĩe kwĩthĩwa na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo. Na endaa ũtavye angĩ ĩũlũ wake na ieleelo syake, ũte kũthĩnĩka nũndũ wa mavĩtyo weekie, ĩndĩ wĩ mũtanu na kuma ngoonĩ. (Savuli 65:1-4) Lilikana kana nũkũthoketye nĩ kana 'naĩ syaku syanangwe, na nĩ kana kũtonye kũka mavinda ma ũvuũkyo kuma ũthyũnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi.'—Meko ma Atũmwa 3:19.
Ũu nĩw'o veethĩiwe kwa Martha. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mwanawa nĩwandũmĩaa makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Amkeni! O ũndũ ĩvinda yaendeee na kũvĩtũka, now'o naendeee kũmũsyokea Yeova. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla waĩ vinya vyũ waĩ kwĩtya ũekeo kwondũ wa mavĩtyo makwa. Ĩndĩ ĩtina nĩnavoyie Ngai andekee. Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kũĩkĩĩa kana naminie myaka 40 ndamũsyokea Yeova. Ngelekany'o yakwa yĩonany'a kana mũndũ no akwate mwanya wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova ĩngĩ na kwĩkala wendonĩ wake, o na ethĩwa nĩ ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ."

translation:
"My children, I always wanted to send them to a good school so they could get an education, and I also wanted them to learn good manners. I encouraged them to attend meetings regularly, to associate with good people, and to respect others. I prayed, and for over 40 years I kept trusting in Jehovah's organization and continued trusting in it. And as time went on and I benefited, I continued to see that Jehovah was helping me. And I have never regretted it. This is the reason why I continue to learn good manners today."—Martha.
CONSIDER this point when you feel discouraged. King David wrote: "I have become numb and deeply distressed because of my groaning." (Psalm 38:4) Many Christians experience similar feelings when they feel Jehovah has forsaken them. (2 Corinthians 2:7) But does Jehovah really forsake his servants? Or perhaps he is testing your faith to see if you will remain loyal to him despite difficulties? No, absolutely not!
"Let Us Reason Together"
Jehovah wants us to be honest about our feelings. He understands how we feel! Think of the illustration of the prodigal son. Jesus showed that Jehovah feels love for each of his children, just like a father loves his son and desires to forgive him when he makes mistakes. The father in the illustration eagerly waited for his son to return home. The Bible says: "While he was still a distance off, his father caught sight of him and felt compassion, and ran quickly and embraced him and kissed him warmly." (Luke 15:11-20) So would you not want to approach Jehovah and ask for forgiveness if you make a mistake? Remember that just as the father welcomed his son back, Jehovah will welcome you back too if you sincerely repent. And do not hesitate to pour out your heart to him.
But what if you feel that you have repeatedly made mistakes and that Jehovah has forsaken you? Consider the powerful words found in Isaiah 1:18: "'Come now, let us settle the matter,' says Jehovah. 'Though your sins are scarlet, they will become white as snow.'" Yes, even if we stumble, Jehovah is willing to forgive us.
He is ready to help us.
Jehovah desires that we confide in him regarding our anxieties. How can we find comfort knowing that God cares for us and is aware of our difficulties? Consider the example of King David. He openly said: "I confessed my transgression to Jehovah, and I did not conceal my error." (Psalm 32:5) Realize that Jehovah is eager to listen to your heartfelt expressions and to forgive you. Do not delay expressing them. Confess your sins to Jehovah and honestly explain how you feel. Like David, you may then experience relief and peace: "Wash me thoroughly from my guilt… Make me hear joy and gladness again, that the bones you have crushed may rejoice."—Psalm 51:2, 17.
Indeed, David acknowledged his sin to Nathan the prophet, whom Jehovah had sent. (2 Samuel 12:13) Today, Jehovah uses congregations to help imperfect people confess their wrongdoing and seek forgiveness. These groups can also provide spiritual assistance and strengthen your relationship with Jehovah. If you need such help, do not hesitate to approach elders; they will use the Scriptures and offer practical advice to restore you, encourage you, or guide you in making needed changes.—James 5:14-16.
"Forgiveness Is Granted by the Generous One"
This includes showing appreciation for what Jehovah does for us and trusting in his willingness to forgive sincere individuals. Fortunately, David set a fine example. He admitted his "error" and took responsibility for it. (Psalm 32:3) We too can benefit from examining why we should confide in him and how we can maintain a close relationship with him.
One important lesson David learned was the value of confession. He wrote: "Happy is the man to whom transgression is forgiven, to whom sin is covered." (Psalm 32:1) He also prayed: "Wash me thoroughly from my wickedness, and cleanse me from my sin." (Psalm 51:15) However, David did not simply feel remorseful; he actively sought Jehovah's favor and demonstrated faith in God's generosity.
Jehovah desires to forgive sins sincerely confessed. And he wants to bless those who turn to him in repentance, helping them to overcome feelings of guilt and enjoy peace of mind. (Psalm 65:1-4) Remember that repentance involves more than just feeling sorry; it means "changing your mind" and turning away from wicked ways.—Acts 3:19.
This was true of Martha. She said: "I used to spend hours reading The Watchtower and Awake! But I realized that I needed to devote more time to getting to know Jehovah. I wanted to use my time wisely so that I could show appreciation for what Jehovah does for me. I am grateful to God for allowing me to serve him. It has been such a joy to worship Jehovah for over 40 years. I hope that others will find opportunities to tell people about Jehovah and become his friends, and I pray that they will experience this joy for many years."

text:
MWEI WA 11 wangĩe kũthela, mwaka wa 1932, ve ũndũ wa mwanya weekĩkie Mexico City. Kyumwa kĩmwe ũndũ ũsu ũtanamba kwĩkĩka, kĩla kyawetawa mũno maũvoonĩ nĩ mataa ma lelũnĩ, ala maĩ maneekĩwa taoninĩ ĩsu yaĩ na andũ mbee wa milioni ũmwe. Ĩndĩ yu vai mũndũ wakwetye ngewa ĩsu. Kĩla kyaĩ maũvoonĩ nĩ ũndũ ũsu wa mwanya weeteelwe. Aandĩki ma maũvoo mekalĩte kĩsesenĩ kya ngalĩ ya mwaki meteele na kamela syoo mũeni wookĩte. Mũeni ũsu aĩ Joseph F. Rutherford, nake nĩwe waũngamĩe Watch Tower Society ĩvinda yĩu. O nasyo Ngũsĩ ila syaĩ kĩsionĩ kĩu syeeteelete kũmũthokya na moko elĩ. Mwana-a-asa ũsu ookĩte ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ.
Ĩkaseti ya The Golden Age yaisye atĩĩ: "Vate nzika, ũmbano ũũ mũnene wĩĩthĩwa wĩ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala ma vata makethĩwa matetheeisye Ũw'o kũthi na mbee nthĩ ya Mexico." Ĩndĩ nĩ kyaũ kyatumie ũmbano ũsu waĩ na andũ o 150 ũwetwa ta ũndũ wa mwanya?
Ũmbano ũsu ũtanamba kwĩkwa, ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ ndwanyaĩĩkĩte mũno nthĩ ya Mexico. Ve maũmbano manene meekĩtwe kuma mwaka wa 1919, ĩndĩ myakanĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe ikundi syeekie kũthi iolekete. Ĩla ovisi wa ũvonge wavingũiwe Mexico City mwaka wa 1929, maũndũ moonekaa ta meũya kavaa. Ĩndĩ ve mathĩna malikile. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla makolovota meeiwe maikakwatanĩsye kũtavany'a na viasala, ũmwe woo nĩwathatie na akola ũw'o na ambĩĩa kĩkundi kyake kya kũmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Na kavindanĩ kau mũsyaĩĩsya wa ovisi wa ũvonge nĩweelikilye mwĩkalĩlenĩ mũthũku na kwoou weethĩa no vamanthawa ũngĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, Ngũsĩ ila syalũmanĩtye na Yeova nthĩ ya Mexico syaĩ na vata wa kwĩkĩwa vinya.
Ĩla Mwana-a-asa Rutherford wookie, nĩweekĩie ana-a-asa asu vinya na maũvoo elĩ maseo mũno ala waumisye ũmbanonĩ ũsu mũnene, na angĩ atano waumisye kĩsesenĩ kya letiũ. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda ya mbee kwĩw'a isese sya letiũ sya Mexico iitangaasa ũvoo mũseo nthĩ ĩsu. Ũmbano wathela, mwana-a-asa ũla wanyuviwe ta mũsyaĩĩsya wa ovisi wa ũvonge nĩwavangĩthisye wĩa wa ũtavany'a. Ĩtina wa ũu Ngũsĩ ila syaĩ nthĩ ĩsu nĩsyoosie vinya na syaendeea na wĩa ũsu kwa vinya wa Yeova.
Mwaka ũla waatĩĩe nĩkweethĩiwe na maũmbano angĩ manene elĩ nthĩ ĩsu. Ũmbano ũmwe weekĩiwe taoninĩ yĩ kĩlĩndĩnĩ ya Veracruz na ũla ũngĩ weekwa Mexico City. Ana-a-asa nĩmatavanisye na kĩthito na mambĩĩa kwona moseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwaka wa 1931 kwaĩ na atavany'a 82. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa myaka ĩkũmi, mongelekete mala ĩkũmi! Mwakanĩ wa 1941 andũ ta 1,000 nĩmaendie ũmbanonĩ ũmwe mũnene waĩ Mexico City (Theocratic Assembly).
"LELŨ II NA ŨTHEI"
Mwakanĩ wa 1943 Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syakuie mathangũ maũmu manene matangaasaa ũmbano mũnene ("Free Nation's" Theocratic Assembly), ũla weekiwe taoninĩ 12 sya Mexico. * Mũndũ eethĩawa akuĩte mathangũ elĩ maũmu. Ooveeaa yĩmwe kĩthũi na yĩngĩ mũongo, na ũu nĩw'o Ngũsĩ syeekaa kuma 1936.
Ĩkaseti yĩmwe (La Nación) nĩyawetie ũndũ mathangũ asu matumie andũ aingĩ moka ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Yaisye atĩĩ: "Mũthenyanĩ wa mbee [wa ũmbano], [Ngũsĩ] maneeiwe mathokye andũ angĩ aingĩ. Mũthenya wa kelĩ mainaĩ meanĩa vala manoombanĩe." Atongoi ma Ĩkanisa ya Katholeki moona ũu mayaaendeew'a, na nũndũ wa ũu mambĩĩa kũvĩnga Ngũsĩ. O na kau nĩmavĩngiwe, mayaasyoka ĩtina ĩndĩ nĩmaendeeie kumaalũka matangaase ũmbano ũsu. Ĩkaseti yĩu yasyokete yĩkasya: "Vai mũndũ wĩ taoni ũtaneemona . . . , na wamasisya onthe, aũme na aka, kĩla ũnoonaa no ala mathangũ maũmu manakuĩte ma kũtangaasa ũmbano ũsu." Ũvoo ũsu waĩ ĩkasetinĩ yĩu waĩ na visa wa ana-a-asa asu mavĩtĩle lelũnĩ sya Mexico City. Ĩtheo wa visa ũsu vaĩ ndeto ii: "Lelũ ii na ũthei."
"ŨKOMO MŨSEO NA WĨ MUUTĨA KWĨ NTHĨ SIMITINĨ"
Myakanĩ ĩsu, Ngũsĩ mbingĩ syeeyĩimaa maũndũ maingĩ nĩ kana ithi maũmbanonĩ manene ala meekawa Mexico, o na kau mayaĩ maingĩ. Aingĩ maumaa isio syĩ kũndũ kũasa kũtavikaa ngalĩ ya mwaki, o na kũtaĩ malelũ. Kĩkundi kĩmwe kyaandĩkie kyasya: "Kĩla kĩwetwa kĩsionĩ kitũ no telegraph." Kwoou ala meũthi ũmbanonĩ mũnene maendaa na nyũmbũ kana makathi na maaũ kwa mĩthenya mingĩ mayĩsa kũtw'ĩka nĩmavika vandũ mosa ngalĩ ya mwaki.
Aingĩ ala maĩ Ngũsĩ ĩvinda yĩu maĩ ngya ũkethĩa mayona tikiti wa kũmavikya ũ ũmbanonĩ mũnene. Mavika kũu, aingĩ moo makomaa kwa ana-a-asa, ala mamathokasya na ngoo yonthe. Angĩ namo makomaa Nyũmbanĩ sya Ũsumbĩ. Ĩvinda yĩmwe ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ta 90 ala mookĩte ũmbanonĩ mũnene nĩmakomie ovisinĩ wa ũvonge. Kĩla ũmwe alanĩilw'e "makotoni 20 ma mavuku atũmĩe ta ũkomo, na mavangiwe maatĩanĩe." Ĩvuku ya Kitabu cha Mwaka yawetie kana ala mookĩte ũmbanonĩ ũsu maisye kana ũsu waĩ "ũkomo mũseo na wĩ muutĩa kwĩ nthĩ simitinĩ."
Vate nzika, ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asu meew'aa mũyo mũno mayũmbana vamwe, na maũndũ ala meeyĩimaa mathi ũmbanonĩ mayamatalaa ta kĩndũ. Ũmũnthĩ atavany'a ala me Mexico maendeee kwongeleka na yu nĩ vakuvĩ milioni ũmwe. Kĩthito kĩla maĩ nakyo nokyo kĩkw'o ũmũnthĩ. * Livoti ĩmwe yaumiw'e mwakanĩ wa 1949 nĩ ovisi wa ũvonge wa Mexico yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa ana-a-asa asu: "O na kau nĩmakomanĩte na ĩvinda yũmũ, kĩthito kyoo kwondũ wa ũw'o kĩyaaoleka nũndũ ũmbano mũnene wathela maendeeaa kũũneenea kwa ĩvinda ĩasa, na ĩkũlyo yĩla matindĩaa kũkũlya no, Tũkeethĩwa na ũmbano ũngĩ mũnene ĩndĩĩ?" O na ũmũnthĩ livoti ta isu nosyo tũkwataa.—Kwĩlilikany'a maũndũ ma tene ma Central America.

translation:
ON November 11th they began, in 1932, with the work of proclaiming the good news in Mexico City. Although this work seemed small at first, each witness diligently shared the truth with people in various towns and cities, but many were touched by this message and joined the ranks of over one million followers. There was also someone who accepted the truth. Every witness diligently shared this good news. Writers of experiences related stories of how they used cameras and flashlights during their ministry. This man was Joseph F. Rutherford, who was then the president of the Watch Tower Society organization. And so, brothers and sisters eagerly embraced this opportunity to cooperate with others. This young man showed great zeal in those three years.
The Golden Age magazine stated: "Consider this, this large gathering of people is one among the gatherings that have been held to testify to God's name throughout Mexico." Is this why this gathering was used to reach out to about 150 people with the good news?
This gathering seemed important, because the branch office was established in Mexico City. Since large assemblies had been held since 1919, they helped strengthen the local congregations. In 1929, when the district overseer visited Mexico City, things appeared promising. But there were some challenges. For example, some publications were confiscated by authorities, and one of them was arrested and accused of working with a group that spread Bible teachings. And due to the efforts of the district overseer, he was eventually released from prison and allowed to continue his work. Because of this, brothers and sisters in Mexico continued to share the good news with people.
Brother Rutherford arrived, encouraging the brothers to preach widely and helping organize this large assembly, and he also helped arrange for the printing of literature. This resulted in an increased interest in the Bible throughout Mexico. After the assembly, the brother who had been imprisoned was appointed to help with the preaching work. As a result of this, brothers and sisters in this country showed greater zeal in serving Jehovah.
In the following years, several more large assemblies were held in this country. One assembly was held in the state of Veracruz, and another was held in Mexico City. The brothers faced opposition and persecution. For example, in 1931 there were 82 arrests. But despite ten years, look at how much progress has been made! By 1941, 1,000 people attended a large assembly in Mexico City (Theocratic Assembly).
"LIGHT AND TRUTH"
In 1943, Jehovah's Witnesses published a special edition of their magazine announcing a large assembly ("Free Nation's" Theocratic Assembly), which was held in 12 cities in Mexico. * Many people were interested in this special edition. Some accepted it readily, while others were skeptical, but this is what Jehovah allowed since 1936.
One article (La Nación) discussed the great benefit that this assembly would bring to many people. It stated: "The success of the assembly [of the Witnesses] attracted many more people. The success was so great that it filled the halls." Catholic Church leaders opposed this activity, and because of this opposition, they tried to hinder the Witnesses. However, despite this opposition, many continued to attend the assemblies. That article also said: "Go to anyone who does not come… and urge him, implore him, beg him to see the great benefits that come from attending this assembly." Thus, the brothers used those articles to obtain visas to travel to Mexico City. The theme of those visas was: "Light and Truth."
"GREATER INTEREST AND MORE ARE COMING FROM DIFFERENT PLACES"
That year, many Witnesses reported that there was much interest in the large assemblies being held throughout Mexico, and many attended. Many came from distant places, often traveling long distances. One group wrote: "Every message received is without telegraph." So, the large assemblies were conducted with buses and trains, and many traveled long distances to attend them.
Many of the Witnesses made arrangements to get tickets to attend the large assemblies. They traveled far, many arriving with their families, fully prepared. Others went to the United States. One witness and his family, consisting of about 90 people, attended the assembly and occupied an entire train car. Everyone was given "20 coupons for meals during the convention, and they were exchanged for food." The Year Book report mentioned that those who attended the assembly said that it was "greater interest and more are coming from different places."
Later on, families began to gather together, and reports came in regarding the large assemblies taking place in various places. It is estimated that the number of people from Mexico has increased to over a million. Every year this number continues to increase. * One resolution passed at the 1949 assembly of the Mexican Watch Tower Society stated: "And since we have been able to reach so many with the good news, let us continue to make efforts to spread the truth further among the masses, and let our zeal be intensified so that we can feed them, Let us also be strengthened by this great privilege?" And so, people continued to take hold of this work.—Considering matters in Central America.

text:
ĩkũlyo
Nĩwaekeiwe? Ndonya ũkwata ũekeo Kũma Kwa Ngai ata?
Ũsungio
Nĩwaekeiwe? ndonya ũkwata ũekeo Kũma Kwa Ngai ata? Meko ma atũme 13:38, yasyaa atĩĩ, "kwoou ana-a-asa, manyai kana nĩ kwĩsĩla Kwa Yesũ ũvoo wa ũekeo wa naĩ ũũtavanw'a kwenyu."
Kũekewa ni kwaũ na vata wakw'o ni mwaũ
Ndeto "Ũekeo" ũelesyo wayo nĩ kũthambya, kũekea, kũekea ikoani. ĩla twakosea mũndũ, nĩtwĩtasya ũekeo nĩ kana ngwatanĩo yĩendeeye. mũndũ ndaekeawa nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwaĩle kũekewa. Va yĩ ũmwe waile kũekewa, ũekeo ni wiko wa wendo, tei na mumo. Kũekea ni utwi wa kũlea kũkua kĩndũ yĩũlũ wa mũndũ ona etha akwĩkĩte ata.
Mbivilia ĩtwiaa kana ithyonthe nĩtwaĩlwe nĩ ũekeo, ĩthyonthe nĩtwekie naĩ. Mũtavanya 7:20," Kwa w'o, kũi mũndũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ wĩkaa ũlũngalu kĩla ĩvinda, ũtesaa kwĩka naĩ." 1Yoana 1:8," Ethĩwa twĩasya tũi na naĩ, nĩtũkwĩkenga ithyĩ ene, na ũla w'o ndwĩ nthĩnĩ waitũ."
Naĩ syonthe nĩ wiko wa ũng'endũ kũla Kwĩ Ngai (Savuli 51:4). kwondũ wa ou nĩtũkwenda kũekewa nĩ Ngai mũno. Kethĩwa naĩ sitũ itiekewa, tũkekala thĩnanĩ wa tene na tene kwondũ wa naĩ (Mathayo 25:46; John 3:36).
Ũekeo - Ndonya kũkwata ata?
Twĩtungĩa Ngai mũvea nũndũ wa wendo na tei wake, ena wendi wa kũtũekea naĩ sitũ! 2Vetelo 3:9 "Mwĩai ndaseleawa nĩ kwĩanĩsya kĩla wathanĩte kwĩka ũndũ andũ amwe mesilasya. Ĩndĩ omĩĩasya eteelete ũalyũle ngoo, nĩkwĩthĩwa ndendaa mũndũ o na wĩva ae; kwenda kwake nĩ andũ onthe melile kwondũ wa naĩ syoo." Ngai niwendeeaw'a ni ũtũekea, kwou niwatũnengie ũekeo.
ĩtuvi yĩla yaĩle naĩ nĩ kĩkw'u. Kĩlũngũ Kya mbee Kya Alomi 6:23 kyasyaa, "Nũndũ ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ..." Kĩkw'ũ Kya tene na tene nĩkyo ĩtũvi ya naĩ syitũ. Mũvangonĩ mũseo, Ngai atw'ĩkie mũndũ - Yesũ Klisto (Yoana 1:1, 14). Yesũ akwie mũkelanyoni oosa ĩtũvi yĩla yatwaĩlĩte - kĩkw'ũ. 2 Akolintho 5:21 itũvundĩasya atĩĩ, "Klĩsto ndaĩ na naĩ, ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwamũkuĩthisye naĩ kwondũ witũ, nĩ kana kwĩsĩla kwake tũtonye kũtw'ĩka andũ alũngalu ma Ngai." Yesũ akw'ie mũkelanyoni oosa ĩtũvi yĩla yatwaĩlĩte! Ta Ngai, kĩkw'ũ Kya Yesũ kyatũnengie ũekeo wa naĩ ya nthĩ yonthe. 1Yoana 2:2 yasyaa atĩĩ, "Klĩsto nĩwe nthembo ya kũveta naĩ sitũ, na ti sitũ syoka, ĩndĩ o vamwe na naĩ sya andũ onthe ma nthĩ." Yesũ athayũkie kũma kĩkwunĩ, aitangaasa ũkĩlyo yĩũlũ wa kĩkwũ (1 Akolintho 15:1-28). Ataĩwe Ngai kwisila kũkw'a na kũthayũũka Kwa Yesũ Klisto, kĩlũngu Kya keelĩ Kya Alomi 6:23 nĩw'o, "ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela kwĩsĩla kwa Mwĩai waitũ Yesũ Klisto."
Nũkwenda naĩ syakũ siekewe? Nukwĩw'a ũyĩsilĩla? Ũekeo wa naĩ syakũ wĩvo kethĩwa nũkũĩkĩĩa Yesũ Klisto nĩwe mũtangĩĩi. Aeveso 1:7 yasyaa atĩĩ, "Nĩkwĩthĩwa kwondũ wa kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto nĩtwoovoiw'e, na twaekewa mavĩtyo maitũ kwĩanana na wingĩ wa mumo wa Ngai." Yesũ nĩwaĩvie kĩla twataĩtwe nĩ kana tũekewe. Kĩla twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kwĩtya ũekeo kũma kũla kwi Ngai kwisila vala ve Yesũ Klisto, kũĩkĩĩa kana Yesũ nĩwakwie kwondũ wa naĩ sitũ na Ngai aiũekea! Yoana 3:16-17 yĩna ũvoo mũseo, ""Nũndũ Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ mũno, nĩwanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmũĩkĩĩaa ndakae ĩndĩ ethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela. Ngai ndaatũma Mwana wake kũũ nthĩ oke kũmĩsilĩla, ĩndĩ nĩ kana atw'ĩke Mũtangĩĩi wayo."
Ũekeo - wĩ laisi oũ?
Yĩĩ wĩlaisi oũ! Ndũtonya kwiyosea ũekeo kũma kũla kwi Ngai. Ndũtonya kũthoowa ũekeo kũma kũla kwi Ngai. Utonya o kũwosa Kwa mũĩkĩĩo kwisila mũmonĩ na teinĩ wa Ngai. Kethĩwa Nũkwenda kũmwĩtĩkila Yesũ Klisto ta mũtangĩĩi wakũ na kũkwata ũekeo kũma Kwa Ngai ĩĩ nĩyo mboya ĩla ũtonya kũvoya. Kuvoya mboya ĩno kana mboya ĩngĩ ona yĩva kũyĩũtangĩĩa. Nokũmũĩkĩĩa Yesũ Klisto kũtonya kũete ũekeo wa naĩ. ĩno nĩ mboya ya kũmwonya Ngai mũĩkĩĩo waku na kũmũtũngĩa mũvea nũndu wa ũekeo. "Ngai, Nye nĩnĩsi nĩ mweene naĩ na nĩnaĩle ũsililo. Ĩndĩ Yesũ Klisto nĩwasilĩilwe kwondũ wakwa nĩkenda kwĩsĩla kwa kũmũĩkĩĩa nĩekewe naĩ sywakwa. Nĩia mũĩkĩĩo wakwa kwakũ kwondũ wa ũtangĩĩo. Nĩmũvea nũndũ wa mũmo waku mwingĩ na ũekeo! Amen!"
We nĩwatw'a ũtwi kũmwĩtĩkĩla Klisto nũndu wa maũndũ ala wasoma vaa? Ethĩwa nĩ w'o, tina vau vaandikĩtwe "nĩnamwĩtĩkĩla Klisto umunthĩ".
English
Nĩwaekeiwe? Ndonya ũkwata ũekeo Kũma Kwa Ngai ata?

translation:
Forgiveness
Is it possible? Does he have forgiveness with God at all?
Confession
Is it possible? Does he have forgiveness with God at all? Verse from Matthew 13:38 says, "Just as weeds are sown among wheat, so too will the enemy sow enemies among you until the day of harvest."
To be forgiven is to be with your people and family
The meaning of "forgiveness" is to cover, to pardon, to forgive completely. When we sin against someone, we seek forgiveness through reconciliation. A person who has been forgiven is cleansed through forgiveness. Forgiveness is a gift of love, not life. To forgive is the act of nurturing growth in another person, even when they don't deserve it.
Scripture shows that everything is covered by forgiveness, everything is pardoned. Refer to Colossians 1:20, "Through him, to reconcile all things to himself, whether things on earth or things in heaven, by making peace through his blood shed on the cross." 1 John 1:8, "If we say that we have fellowship with him while walking in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth."
All this is an act of grace from God (Psalm 51:4). Because of this, we need to seek forgiveness from God alone. Those who believe it are condemned to eternal punishment because of this (Matthew 25:46; John 3:36).
Forgiveness – Is it really possible?
Let us praise God for his loving kindness and mercy, especially his willingness to forgive us! 2 Peter 3:9, "The Lord is not slow in keeping his promise, as some understand slowness. He is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance." God is merciful and willing to grant us forgiveness, let us embrace it.
Sin is terrible and shameful. Proverbs 6:23 states, "For adultery is a dishonest thing…" Dishonesty and shamefulness are the nature of sin. Therefore, God sent his Son – Jesus Christ (John 1:1, 14). Jesus took upon himself the penalty for all our sins – dishonesty. 2 Corinthians 5:21 explains, "God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God." Jesus took upon himself the penalty for all our sins! Through God, the dishonesty of Jesus grants us forgiveness for all our sins. 1 John 2:2 states, "He is the propitiation for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the whole world." Jesus rose from the dead, conquering the power of sin (1 Corinthians 15:1-28). Give thanks to God for salvation through Jesus Christ, Proverbs 6:23 says, "But the wages of sin is death, though the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord."
Will you accept this gift today? Will you believe? The forgiveness of your sins is available if you turn to Jesus Christ. Ephesians 1:7 states, "In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace." Jesus offers forgiveness to everyone who believes. Every time we sin, it is an opportunity to return to God through faith in Jesus Christ, believing that Jesus died for our sins and God accepts us! John 3:16-17 says, "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn it, but to save it."
Forgiveness – will you receive it?
Yes, you can receive it! I urge you to receive forgiveness today. I urge you to embrace forgiveness today. Don't let pride stand in the way of experiencing God's love and peace. Turn to Jesus Christ now and accept forgiveness today; this is the only way to be saved. Salvation is now and for eternity, offering a chance to experience true freedom. By accepting Jesus Christ, you can obtain the gift of forgiveness. This is a moment to know God personally and worship Him with a heart full of gratitude. "God, I confess my sins and I am sorry. Through Jesus Christ, my debt has been paid and I accept Your forgiveness. I surrender my life to You and receive Your grace. I desire a life filled with Your abundance and forgiveness! Amen!"
Will we listen to Christ's call regarding all things we read about? It is true, they were written "I accepted Christ as my savior".
What is forgiveness? Can you receive God's forgiveness today?

text:
Mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Janet aeleetye atĩĩ: "Ĩvinda ĩte ĩasa ĩtina wa ĩthe wakwa kũkw'a, mũũme wakwa nĩwandavisye kana e ndũũ na mũndũ mũka ũngĩ." Aendeee kwasya: "Ĩtina wa ũu, nĩwakuie ngũa syake syonthe o na atandavĩtye, na andia na syana syakwa ilĩ." O na kau Janet nĩwakwatie wĩa, mbesa ila wakwataa iyeanĩtye kũũngamĩa mavata ma mũsyĩ wake. O na eka mavata ma kĩ-mbesa, Janet aĩ na mathĩna angĩ maingĩ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũndũ ũla watumaa nĩmakĩa mũno nĩ kana natiĩwe kĩanda kĩ vinya mũno kya kũũngamĩa mũsyĩ wakwa nĩweka." Aendeee kwasya: "Naũmĩaa mũno ngoonĩ nũndũ ndyaĩ ndonya kwĩanĩsya nesa mavata ma syana syakwa ta asyai ala angĩ. O na ũmũnthĩ no nĩkũlasya ũndũ andũ ala angĩ mambonaa nĩ na syana syakwa. Yo no methĩwe monaa ta ndaaĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana mũtwaano witũ ndũkanangĩke?"
Mboya nĩyo ĩtetheeasya Janet kũolanga mawĩmakĩo make na aiendeea kwĩthĩwa na ũnyanya na Ngai. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũtukũ ĩla kũkilĩtye nĩw'o nĩthĩawa na ĩvinda yĩla yũmũ vyũ, nũndũ ndiekaa kwĩsilya na kwĩmakĩa. Ĩndĩ kũvoya na kũsoma Mbivilia nĩkũndetheeasya kũkwata too. Ĩandĩko yĩmwe nendete mũno nĩ Avilivi 4:6, 7 yĩla yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Mũikemakĩe kwa ũndũ o na wĩva; ĩndĩ kĩla ũndũnĩ mavata menyu nĩmatavanw'e kwa Ngai na kũvoya na kwĩsũva vamwe na kũtũnga mũvea. Na mũuo wa Ngai, ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe, ũkasũvĩaa ngoo syenyu na mosũanĩo menyu.' Nĩnĩthĩĩtwe ndivoya mĩthenya mingĩ ũtukũ, na nĩnĩw'ĩte mũuo wa Yeova ũingiakisya."
Ndeto sya Yesũ ĩũlũ wa mboya ila wawetie nthĩnĩ wa Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ no itũtetheesye ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mawĩmakĩo o na ethĩwa nĩ ma mũthemba wĩva. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩthe wenyu nĩwĩsĩ ila mwĩ na vata nasyo, mbee wa inyw'ĩ mũtanamũvoya." (Mathayo 6:8) Na kwa w'o nĩtwaĩlĩte kũmũvoya nũndũ mboya nĩyo nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ ya 'kũmũthengeea Ngai.' Na tweeka ũu, nake 'akatũthengeea.'—Yakovo 4:8.
Vate nzika, o vamwe na kwĩw'a twĩ eanĩe ĩla twaelesya Yeova mawĩmakĩo maitũ, mboya nĩtũtetheeasya kwa nzĩa nene vyũ. O na ĩngĩ, Yeova, "Ũla wĩw'aa mboya," nũtetheeasya ala mamũmanthaa me na mũĩkĩĩo. (Savuli 65:2) Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ wamanyĩisye aatĩĩi make 'mavoyae mĩthenya yonthe mateũleela.' (Luka 18:1) No nginya tũendeee kũmũvoya Yeova atũtongoesye na aitũtetheesya. Twaĩle kwĩka ũu twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana akatũathima. Tũyaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa na nzika kana we e na ũtonyi na mea ma kũtũtetheesya. 'Kũvoya tũtekũeka' kwonanasya kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo.—1 Athesalonika 5: 17.
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KWONANY'A KANA TWĨ NA MŨĨKĨĨO
Ĩndĩ yo mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kyaũ? Ũndũ ũmwe wonanasya kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nĩ 'kũmũmanya' Ngai ũkethĩa nĩ wa w'o kwitũ. (Yoana 17:3) Nzĩa ĩmwe ĩla twĩkaa ũu nĩ kwa kũsoma na kwĩkĩa ngoonĩ ndeto syake ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ. Nĩtũmanyaa kana we nĩwonaa kĩla ũmwe waitũ, na nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ kũtũtetheesya. Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kwonanaw'a nĩ maũndũ maingĩ, ĩndĩ ti o kũmanya maũndũ mana ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Ũndũ ũngĩ wonanasya kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na ũnyanya na Ngai. O tondũ vethĩawa vailyĩ kwa andũ, tũyĩsa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ĩsu vamwe na Ngai oou kĩtumbo. Mũĩkĩĩo witũ ũendeea 'kwĩana' o ũndũ tũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai, 'kwĩka maũndũ ala mamwendeeasya,' na o ũndũ twaendeea kũkwata ũtethyo wake. (2 Akolintho 10:15; Yoana 8:29) Mũĩkĩĩo ta ũsu nĩw'o ũmũtetheeasya Janet kũmĩanĩsya na mawĩmakĩo.
Janet aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwa w'o, kĩla kĩndetheesye kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu nĩ kwona ũndũ Yeova ũndetheeasya kĩla ũndũnĩ." Aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Mavinda maingĩ nĩtwakwatawa nĩ mathĩna maito mũno, ala twoonaa ta tũtomĩanĩsya namo. Nĩnavoyaa Yeova mũno, nake nĩwatũtetheeasya kwa nzĩa o na tũteĩtaĩĩe. Ĩla namũtũngĩa mũvea nĩnĩlilikanaa maũndũ maingĩ ala ũmbĩkĩte. Nĩwĩthĩĩtwe aitũtetheesya kĩla ĩvinda, na mavinda maingĩ atũtetheeasya ĩla tũkwenda ũtethyo wake vyũ. O na nũndetheesye kwĩthĩwa na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa Aklĩsto ala nĩ anyanya ma w'o. Nĩmandetheeasya kĩla ĩvinda na nĩmethĩĩtwe me ngelekany'o nzeo kwa syana syakwa." *
Janet aendeee kwasya: "Nĩnĩsĩ nĩkĩ Yeova waĩtye ĩandĩkonĩ ya Malaki 2:16, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language, kana 'Nũmenete mũndũ aitaanĩsya na mũka wake.' Ĩla mũũme na mũka mataanĩsya na ũyĩthĩa ũmwe woo nde na mavĩtyo, nĩwĩw'aa aũmĩw'a ngoonĩ mũno. Kuma mũũme wakwa andia, myaka mingĩ nĩ mĩvĩtu ĩndĩ mavinda angĩ nĩw'aa ndyĩmena na ndyenda kwĩthĩwa na mũndũ vakuvĩ. Ĩla neew'a ũu, nĩndataa kũtetheesya andũ angĩ na ũndũ ũsu nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ũindetheesya mũno." Kwoou kũatĩĩa ũtao wa Mbivilia wa kũlea kwĩvathana na ala angĩ, nĩkũmũtetheesye Janet kũolanga mawĩmakĩo make. *—Nthimo 18:1.
Ngai nĩwe "ĩthe wa ala makw'ĩĩwe nĩ aaĩthe, na mũsili wa aka ndiwa."—Savuli 68:5
Janet aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũkiakisyo ũla mũnene umanaa na kũmanya kana Ngai nĩwe 'ĩthe wa ala makw'ĩĩwe nĩ aaĩthe, na mũsili wa aka ndiwa.' Nĩnĩsĩ nesa vyũ kana Ngai ndakaatũtia tondũ mũũme wakwa watũtiie." (Savuli 68:5) Janet nĩwĩsĩ nesa kana Ngai ndatũtataa na maũndũ 'mathũku.' Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, nĩ ũnengae "andũ onthe na ũlau" ũĩ wake, na "vinya mũnene ũvĩtũkĩte" nĩ kana tũmĩanĩsye na mathĩna.—Yakovo 1:5, 13; 2 Akolintho 4:7.
Nao nata ethĩwa twĩmakĩĩte nũndũ thayũ witũ wĩ mũisyonĩ?

translation:
A certain woman named Janet reported saying: "The darkness that came was like the shadow of death, my husband has been bewitched or he is out there with another woman." She continued to say: "The shadow of this, I have tasted its bitterness and it has troubled me, and also my children are suffering." And so Janet began to weep, greatly distressed and trying to understand the troubles of her life. And from those troubles of distress, Janet had many thoughts. She said: "This thing that is happening to me is perhaps because I was given a cursed gift to try and understand my life." She continued to say: "I am afraid that maybe I will never be able to rest until the troubles of my children are resolved. And truly, it is painful when others see my children suffering. It is not good to see them crying and I wonder if our disagreement could cause this?"
Prayer helped Janet to calm down and she turned to seek help from God. She said: "That night I lay awake thinking about what happened, and I decided to pray and meditate. Reading and studying the Bible helps me to cope. One scripture that really helped me is Proverbs 4:6, 7 which says: 'Do not forsake wisdom and discernment; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart. Then your devotion to God will secure your favor and understanding.' I realized that I needed to spend more time praying to Jehovah."
Jesus' example during his ministry and his trust in the Father shows us how we can deal with anxieties and rely on the strength of our faith. He said: "So do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will take care of itself." (Matthew 6:8) And with that, I learned to trust in prayer, realizing that prayer is the means of 'approaching God.' And now, I practice 'approaching Him.'—James 4:8.
Therefore, when we share our anxieties with Jehovah through prayer, prayer helps us greatly. Also, Jehovah, "The Hearer of Prayer," comforts my soul and gives me peace of mind. (Psalm 65:2) That is why Jesus encouraged his followers to 'pray constantly.' (Luke 18:1) Let us continue to pray to Jehovah so that he may guide and comfort us. We should not give up because of difficulties or disappointments. We should turn to him for help regardless of whether we feel worthy or unworthy. 'Constant prayer' is essential even when we face difficulties.—1 Thessalonians 5:17.
PRAYER IS ESSENTIAL EVEN WHEN WE FACE DIFFICULTIES
What is prayer? One way prayer helps us is by 'knowing' God better and closer. (John 17:3) Another way we can pray is by reading and meditating on his Word, especially the Bible. He knows each of us individually, and he wants to comfort us. Being comforted by prayer involves many things, including learning more about God's will. Another way prayer helps us is by being strengthened spiritually and having a close relationship with God. So while others rely on people, let us seek strength from God alone. Our conscience encourages us to 'expand' in our understanding of God's will, 'to practice what we learn,' and to live according to his teachings. (2 Corinthians 10:15; John 8:29) A good conscience helps Janet to align herself with her faith.
Janet says: "For me, everything that comforts me through prayer is knowing what Jehovah is doing for me personally." She continues: "Many times we face difficult situations, but we realize that we don't have to cope with them alone. I trust Jehovah so much, because he comforts us in various ways and helps us endure. But I also appreciate that I have learned many things along the way. I feel encouraged to continue seeking his comfort every day, and many days his comfort helps us to find his guidance. And I am comforted knowing that fellow Christians—both young and old—feel the same way. I am comforted every day and I am very grateful for this close relationship with my Creator." *
Janet continues: "I was struck when Jehovah helped me understand Malachi 2:16, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language, which says, '"'The man who hates divorce,' says Jehovah.'" But a husband and wife who resolve their differences and work on their marriage will be blessed. However, if a husband looks elsewhere for years, he may end up feeling drawn to another person. But now, I am determined to help others, and I feel encouraged to do so." To show respect for the Biblical principle of being considerate of others, we encouraged Janet to reflect on her experiences.—Proverbs 18:1.
God is "a father to the fatherless and a protector of widows"—Psalm 68:5
Janet said: "Realizing that our loving Father is 'a father to the fatherless and a protector of widows' really comforted me. I felt that God could truly help my husband." (Psalm 68:5) Janet also realized that God understands our 'weaknesses.' For those people, she offered her sincere "compassion" and showed them "great kindness" when dealing with them.—James 1:5, 13; 2 Corinthians 4:7.
And how can we show practical wisdom in our ministry?

text:
Waasoma ĩũlũ wa andũ amwe maeleetw'e Mbivilianĩ makathĩtwe mũno nginya ũkasũanĩa ũndũ ta ũũ: 'Nyie ndyĩsa kwĩthĩwa nĩilyĩ tamo!' No wasye, 'Nyie ndi mũlũngalu na vate nzika mavinda onthe ndyĩkaa maũndũ ala maseo.'
Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yovu: "Aĩ mwĩanĩu na mũlũngalu." (Yovu 1:1) Nake Loto etĩtwe "mũndũ mũlũngalu." (2 Vetelo 2:8) Mbivilia yongeleele kwasya kana Ndaviti eekaa "ũla ũseo" methonĩ ma Ngai. (1 Asumbĩ 14:8) Ĩndĩ, ekai twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingangĩ ĩũlũ wa andũ asu mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Nĩtũkwĩmanyĩsya kana (1) nĩmavĩtasya, (2) no twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ kumana na ngelekany'o yoo, na (3) andũ me na naĩ kana mate eanĩu no mamwendeesye Ngai.
NĨMAVĨTASYA
Yovu akwatiwe nĩ maũndũ maingĩ maĩ momũ. Ndaaelewa nesa nĩkĩ maũndũ asu mamũkwatĩte, na nũndũ wa ũu atw'a kana Ngai ndoonaa mũĩkĩĩo ũla waĩ naw'o. (Yovu 9:20-22) Yovu oonaa e mũlũngalu vyũ nginya weethĩa andũ ala angĩ meona ta ũkwasya we nĩ mũlũngalu kwĩ Ngai.—Yovu 32:1, 2; 35:1, 2.
Loto ndaaĩka ũtwi ũla waaĩlĩte na mĩtũkĩ, o na kau waĩ o ũtwi wa ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe na wĩ laisi. Athĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa mwĩkalĩle mũthũku wa andũ ala mekalaa Sotomo na Ngomola, nginya "athĩn'ya ngoo yake ndũngalu." (2 Vetelo 2:8) Ngai aisye kana nũkwananga ndũa isu nthũku na anenga Loto mwanya wa kũvonoka vamwe na mũsyĩ wake. No ũsũanĩe kana nũndũ Loto nĩwathĩnĩkaa mũno, nĩwe waaĩle kwĩthĩwa e wa mbee kuma ndũanĩ isu. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa ũsengy'a nĩ kana ndaaosa ĩtambya ya mĩtũkĩ. Alaĩka ala matũmĩtwe makamavonokye malasimĩkie kũmakwata moko na kũmaumya ndũanĩ ĩsu, na mamatwaa vandũ vate mũisyo.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 19:15, 16.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩmwe Ndaviti nĩwaemiwe nĩ kwĩsiĩĩa na kwoou eeka ũlaalai na kĩveti kya mũndũũme ũngĩ. Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, nĩwoowaie mũũme wa kĩveti kĩu nĩ kana avithe naĩ yake. (2 Samueli, kĩlungu kya 11) Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ũndũ ũla Ndaviti weekie "nĩwamwĩw'ĩthisye Yeova woo."—2 Samueli 11:27.
Yovu, Loto, na Ndaviti nĩmavĩtisye, na mavĩtyo amwe moo maĩ maito mũno. Ĩndĩ o tondũ tũkwĩsa kwona, nĩmeeyumĩtye kũmũthũkũma Ngai na ngoo yonthe, na kwĩthĩwa me ewi. O na nĩmeetĩkĩlaa mavĩtyo moo, na mayĩka moalyũku ala maĩlĩte. Na nũndũ wa ũu, Ngai nĩwendeeiw'e nĩmo, na Mbivilia ĩmetĩte aũme aĩkĩĩku.
TŨTONYA KWĨMANYĨSYA KYAŨ?
Nũndũ twĩ andũ me na naĩ, mavinda amwe nĩtũvĩtasya. (Alomi 3:23) Ĩndĩ ĩla twavĩtya nĩtwaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo, na tũitata ũndũ tũtonya tũlũnge maũndũ.
Yovu, Loto, na Ndaviti meekie ata nĩ kana malũnge mavĩtyo moo? Yovu aĩ mũĩkĩĩku kuma ngoonĩ. Yovu nĩwalũngile mosũanĩo make na eetĩkĩla ĩvĩtyo yake ĩtina wa Ngai kũneena nake. (Yovu 42:6) Naw'o woni wa Loto ĩũlũ wa mwĩkalĩle mũthũku wa andũ ma Sotomo na Ngomola woosanĩte nesa vyũ na ũndũ Ngai wonaa ũthũku. Ĩndĩ thĩna wake waĩ kũlea kwosa ĩtambya ya mĩtũkĩ. Ĩtina nĩwesie kuma ndũanĩ isu Ngai wavangĩte kũsyananga na avonoka ũsilĩlo wa Ngai. Nũndũ aĩ mwĩwi ndaasisya syĩndũ ila watiĩte ĩtina. O na kau Ndaviti nĩweekie naĩ ngito kwa kũtũla mwĩao wa Ngai, nĩwoonanisye kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ yake ĩla weetĩkĩlile mavĩtyo make, na eetya Ngai ũekeo.—Savuli 51.
Ũndũ Ngai woonaa aũme asu, kwĩtwony'a woni mũseo ũla wĩthĩawa naw'o kwa andũ me na naĩ. Ngai "nĩwĩsĩ wũmbe witũ; nũlilikanaa kana twĩ kĩtoo." (Savuli 103:14) Kwoou, ethĩwa Ngai nĩwĩsĩ kana mavinda amwe nĩtũvĩtasya, endaa twĩke ata?
Ngai "nĩwĩsĩ wũmbe witũ; nũlilikanaa kana twĩ kĩtoo."—Savuli 103:14
ŨNDŨ ANDŨ ME NA NAĨ MATONYA KŨMWENDEESYA NGAI
Ũtao ũla Ndaviti wanengie mwana wake Solomoni nũtũtetheeasya kũmanya ũndũ tũtonya kũmwendeesya Ngai. Amwĩie atĩĩ: "Naku, Solomoni mwana wakwa, mũmanye Ngai wa ĩthe waku, noimũthũkũma na ngoo mbĩanĩu." (1 Mavinda 28:9) Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Ngoo mbĩanĩu nĩ kyaũ? Nĩ kũmwenda Ngai na kwĩthĩwa mũndũ atw'ĩte kwĩmanyĩsya kwenda kwake, na kwĩka kĩla weemanyĩsya. Ũu ti kwasya kana mũndũ ndatonya kwĩka naĩ, ĩndĩ nĩkwĩthĩwa na mea ma kũmũthũkũma Ngai wĩ mwĩwi na kwĩthĩwa wĩyũmbanĩtye kũlũngwa. Kũmwenda Ngai na kwĩthĩwa e mwĩwi nĩkw'o kwatumie Yovu awetwa ta "mwĩanĩu," nake Loto awetwa ta "mũlũngalu," na Ndaviti awetwa ta weekaa "ũla ũseo" methonĩ ma Ngai. Nĩmamwendeeisye Ngai o na kau onthe nĩmavĩtasya.
Mũndũ wĩ na ngoo mbĩanĩu nĩwĩthĩawa endete kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai na kũmũthũkũma e mwĩwi
Kwoou, ĩla tweethĩwa na mosũanĩo mate maseo, twaneena ndeto iũtuma twĩw'a nthoni, kana tweeka maũndũ mate maseo, nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwosa vinya kumana na ngelekany'o isu twaneenea. Ngai nĩwĩsĩ kana ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũilea kwĩka naĩ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩwendaa tũmwende na tũitata ũndũ tũtonya twĩthĩwe twĩ ewi. Tweethĩwa na ngoo mbĩanĩu kwa kũmwenda na kwĩthĩwa twĩ ewi, no twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana no tũmwendeesye.
