translation:
Those who read extensively among people were enlightened by Mbiviliani to understand this thing: 'You should not be ashamed to speak the truth!' And he said, 'You are righteous and have good reasons for defending yourselves against all accusations.'
Mbivilia stated this about the story of Job: "He remained righteous." (Job 1:1) Luke also called him a "righteous man." (2 Peter 2:8) The Bible further states that David acted with "integrity" according to God's will. (1 Samuel 14:8) Therefore, let us examine more deeply the stories of people who were praised in the Bible. Let us examine whether (1) they were perfect, (2) we can learn much from their example, and (3) people who sin and confess their sins are forgiven by God.
THEY WERE IMPERFECT
Job was afflicted with many terrible things. I understand that it is difficult for some people to believe that God allows such suffering, and why He does so. (Job 9:20-22) Job realized that he was imperfect like others, and he admitted that his defense before God was imperfect.—Job 32:1, 2; 35:1, 2.
Luke showed kindness to those who had suffered, and he did not judge each person individually. It happened that when he was with Sodom and Gomorrah, they "longed for her righteousness." (2 Peter 2:8) God knew that he would continue to show compassion to others and rescued Lot from destruction along with his family. But despite this, Lot felt distressed because he saw what was happening around him. This shows that even though Lot was saved, he still longed for better conditions. However, the reason for my concern is that I have heard of many mistakes. Some people use them as excuses to associate with bad company and to justify their actions.—Proverbs 19:15, 16.
One instance involving David was when he committed adultery and killed a man. The reason for his mistake was that he stayed home instead of going out with the army. (2 Samuel, chapter 11) The Bible says that what David did was "displeasing to Jehovah."—2 Samuel 11:27.
Lot, Luke, and David made mistakes, and we can learn much from their experiences. So let us strive to please God in everything we do, and to be obedient to him. And let us remember their mistakes so that we do not make similar ones. Because of this, God will help us, and the Bible will guide our steps.
WHAT CAN WE LEARN FROM THIS?
We are all imperfect humans, and we all make mistakes. (Ecclesiastes 3:23) But if we acknowledge our mistakes, we can correct them and avoid repeating them.
Did Lot, Luke, and David ever regret making those mistakes? Job regretted his words. Job admitted his foolishness and humbled himself before God, acknowledging his error. (Job 42:6) Also, Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and Gomorrah and was turned into a pillar of salt because she disobeyed God. But her death served as a warning to others not to disobey God. It reminds us that God does what he says and that his laws are just. But she did not heed the warning. And King David also sinned when he committed adultery with Bathsheba, but he repented and God forgave him—Psalm 51.
God understands our imperfections, so let us approach him confidently knowing that he will forgive us. God "is mindful of our weakness; he remembers that we are dust." (Psalm 103:14) Therefore, if God is merciful even when we make mistakes, shouldn't we be too?
God "is mindful of our weakness; he remembers that we are dust."—Psalm 103:14
HOW IMPERFECT HUMANS CAN PLEASE GOD
King David advised his son Solomon to strive to know how to please God. He told him: "Solomon my son, get to know the God of your forefathers, and serve him with all your heart." (1 Chronicles 28:9) So, what does serving God involve? It means loving God and striving to live according to his standards, and doing everything we can to imitate him. This doesn't mean that anyone can perfectly meet those standards, but it means trying our best to honor God and striving to live up to his expectations. Loving God and striving to do so is what made Job known as "upright," Lot known as "righteous," and David known as "a man after [God's] own heart." Let us continue to please God, and may we never give up.
A person who has a wholehearted desire pleases God by living according to his standards and honoring him.
However, if we are influenced by bad associations, we often make mistakes that cause us pain, or we do things that lead to regret—things that we wish we had not done. God is willing to forgive us if we confess our sins to him. But even so, we need to learn from our mistakes. We should strive to love and obey him more fully, and we should be careful about the influences that affect us. Let us have a wholehearted desire to love and obey him, and let us avoid bad associations or stop associating with them.

text:
KWOONA mĩnyololo ĩĩ yovete Vaulo, na kwasisya mũsikalĩ ũya Mũlomi ũkũmũsunga. Vaulo ovewe Lomi. Eteele nginya Kaisali Mũlomi atw'e ũndũ ũkwĩkana nake. Na e o mwove, andũ nĩmanengawa mwanya wa kũmwona
Mĩthenya ĩtatũ ĩtina wa Vaulo kũvika Lomi nĩwatũmanie nĩ kana atongoi amwe Ayuti moke kũmwona. Na kwoou, Ayuti aingĩ kũu Lomi mooka. Vaulo nĩwamatavisye ĩũlũ wa Yesũ na ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Amwe nĩmaĩkĩĩie na matw'ĩka Aklĩsto, ĩndĩ angĩ mayaaĩkĩĩa.
Na ĩngĩ Vaulo nĩwamatavisye ũvoo mũseo asikalĩ me kĩvathũkany'o ala mamũsungaa. Kwa myaka ĩlĩ ĩla Vaulo wekalile vaa e mwove, nĩwamatavasya ũvoo mũseo andũ onthe ala waĩ atonya kũmatavya. Na nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu, o na andũ ma nyũmba ya Kaisali meew'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ, na amwe moo matw'ĩka Aklĩsto.
Ĩndĩ mũeni ũũ wĩ mesanĩ ũkũandĩka nũũ? We nũtonya ũtalĩthya? Ũũ nĩ Timotheo. Timotheo o nake aĩ kolokolonĩ nũndũ wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ, ĩndĩ yu aĩ mũthasye. Nake ookĩte vaa kũtetheesya Vaulo. We nĩwĩsĩ Timotheo eandĩka kyaũ? Ekai twone.
We nũũlilikana ndũa sya Vilivi na Eveso nthĩnĩ wa Ngewa ya 110? Vaulo nĩwatetheeisye kwambĩlĩĩlw'a kwa ikundi sya Kĩklĩsto ndũanĩ isu. Ĩndĩ e o kolokolonĩ, Vaulo nĩwaandĩkĩie Aklĩsto asu valũa. Valũa isu syĩ Mbivilianĩ, na syĩtawa Aeveso na Avilivi. Vaulo yu etavya Timotheo ũndũ ũkũandĩkĩa Aklĩsto anyanyae ndũanĩ ya Vilivi.
Avilivi maĩ na ĩnee mũno kwa Vaulo. Nĩmamũtũmĩie mũthĩnzĩo e vaa kolokolonĩ, na kwoou Vaulo amatũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa w'o. Evavilotito nĩwe waetie mũthĩnzĩo ũsu. Ĩndĩ awaa na eethĩwa e vakuvĩ kũkw'a. Yu aĩ mũima ĩngĩ na nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kwĩnũka. Na aĩ akue valũa ũsu kuma kwa Vaulo na Timotheo na aisyoka naw'o Vilivi.
E o kolokolonĩ Vaulo nĩwaandĩkie valũa ingĩ ilĩ ila twĩ nasyo Mbivilianĩ. Ũmwe aandĩkĩie Aklĩsto ma ndũa ya Kolosai. We nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ valũa ũsu wĩtawa? Wĩtawa Akolosai. Ũla ũngĩ aandĩkie mũnyanyae wake weetawa Vilemona ũla o nake wekalaa Kolosai. Valũa ũsu wĩelesya ĩũlũ wa Onesimo mũthũkũmi wa Vilemona.
Onesimo nĩwaĩ anatoloka kuma kwa Vilemona akoka Lomi. Kwa nzĩa na, Onesimo nĩwamanyie kana Vaulo aĩ kolokolonĩ Lomi. Nake ooka kũmũsisya, na Vaulo amũtavya ũvoo mũseo. O kwa mĩtũkĩ, Onesimo o nake nĩwatw'ĩkie Mũklĩsto. Nĩweelilile nũndũ wa kũtoloka. Kwoou we nĩwĩsĩ kĩla Vaulo waandĩkie valũanĩ wake kwa Vilemona?
Vaulo akũlilye Vilemona amũekee Onesimo. Vaulo aandĩkie, 'Nĩngũmũtũma we mwene asyoke kwaku. Ĩndĩ yu we nĩ mũthũkũmi waku na mwana-a-asa Mũklĩsto mũseo.' Yĩla Onesimo wakee kũsyoka Kolosai, nĩwakuie valũa isu syelĩ, ũmwe kwa Akolosai na ũngĩ kwa Vilemona. Nĩtũtonya kũsũanĩa ũndũ Vilemona watanie nĩkũmanya kana mũthũkũmi wake nũtw'ĩkĩte Mũklĩsto.
Yĩla Vaulo waandĩkĩie Avilivi na Vilemona, aĩ na ũvoo mũseo mũno. Vaulo eeie Avilivi: 'Nĩtũma Timotheo kwenyu. Ĩndĩ o nakwa ngooka kũmwona inyw'ĩ o mĩtũkĩ.' Na kwa Vilemona aandĩka ũũ: 'Nzeũvĩsya vandũ va kwĩkala kũu.'
Vaulo athaw'a nĩwathokeie ana-a-asa na eĩtu-asa Aklĩsto kũndũ kwingĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩtina Vaulo nĩwooviwe ĩngĩ kũu Lomi. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩweesĩ nũkũawa. Kwoou aandĩkĩa Timotheo na amũkũlya oke mĩtũkĩ. Vaulo aandĩkie: 'Nĩthĩĩtwe nĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai. Na Ngai nũkanduva.' Myaka mĩvũthũ ĩtina wa Vaulo kũawa, Yelusaleme nĩyaanangiwe ĩngĩ, ĩvinda yĩu nĩ Alomi.
Ĩndĩ kwĩ maũndũ maingĩ Mbivilianĩ. Yeova Ngai nĩweeie mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩke mavuku mayo ma mũthya, o vamwe na ĩvuku ya Ũvuany'o. Ĩvuku yĩĩ yĩtavanasya ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte. Ekai yu twĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala makekĩka ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte.
Meko 28:16-31; Avilivi 1:13; 2:19-30; 4:18-23; Aevelania 13:23; Vilemona 1-25; Akolosai 4:7-9; 2 Timotheo 4:7-9.
Makũlyo
- Vaulo atavisye aaũ yĩla waĩ kolokolonĩ Lomi?
- Nthĩnĩ wa visa ũũ, mũeni ũũ wĩ mesanĩ nũũ, na eĩka ata kwondũ wa Vaulo?
- Evavilotito nũũ, nake akuie kyaũ asyoka nakyo Vilivi?
- Nĩkĩ Vaulo wamũandikĩie valũa mũnyanyae wake Vilemona?
- Vaulo eekie ata yĩla wathaiw'e, na ĩtina kweethĩiwe ata kwake?
- Nũũ Yeova watũmĩie kũandĩka mavuku ma mũthya ma Mbivilia, na ĩvuku ya Ũvuany'o yĩtavanasya ĩũlũ wa kyaũ?
Makũlyo ma kwongeleela
- Soma Meko 28:16-31 na Avilivi 1:13.
Vaulo atũmĩie ĩvinda yake ata e kolokolonĩ Lomi, na mũĩkĩĩo wake ũtathingithĩka weekĩie vinya ata kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto? (Meko 28:23, 30; Avi. 1:14)
- Soma Avilivi 2:19-30.
Vaulo aneenie ndeto syĩva sya kwonany'a nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ Timotheo na Evavilotito, na tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Vaulo ata? (Avi. 2:20, 22, 25, 29, 30; 1 Ako. 16:18; 1 Ath. 5:12, 13)
- Soma Vilemona 1-25.
Nĩ kwondũ wa kyaũ Vaulo wakũlilye Vilemona eke ũndũ kwaĩlĩte, na ũndũ ũsu ũtũmĩkaa ata ta woneleelyo kwa atumĩa ma kĩkundi ũmũnthĩ? (Vil. 9; 2 Ako. 8:8; Aka. 5:13)
Ndeto sya Vaulo ila syĩ nthĩnĩ wa Vilemona 13, 14 syĩonany'a ata kana nĩwanengete ndaĩa wasya wa ngoo wa ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ? (1 Ako. 8:7, 13; 10:31-33)
- Soma 2 Timotheo 4:7-9.
O ta mũtũmwa Vaulo, ithyĩ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu ata kana Yeova akatũnenga mũthĩnzĩo twaendeea kwĩthĩwa twĩ aĩkĩĩku nginya mũminũkĩlyo? (Mt. 24:13; Aevl. 6:10)

translation:
Indeed many people troubled Paul, and sought a way to destroy him. Paul pleased God. Pray for me, brothers, that God may make my journey successful. For if I go, you will rejoice, and I also will be glad. But if I do not go, no one will accuse you of wrongdoing.
Three days ago I went to see Paul from Jerusalem; he showed me even how he was imprisoned by the Lord. And Paul said, "Many of my brethren encouraged me in the Lord, not fearing chains."
And again, Paul reminded them of his imprisonment for the sake of the gospel, so they might not be discouraged. For many years Paul had been traveling, and he reminded them of his imprisonment for the sake of the gospel, and some were unable to travel. And because of this, both those from Caesar's household and others believed in the gospel, and some became disciples of Christ.
Why then did I write this? What can I say? It is Timothy. Timothy, our brother, has been sent by us to strengthen and encourage you in your faith, so that no one may be shaken. He also reminds you of my ways. So let us see.
Do you remember the story of Priscilla and Aquila from the book of Acts chapter 18? Paul testified strongly to the community of Christians about them. And in this connection, Paul wrote to Christ concerning several places. These places include Philippi, and Ephesus and Laodicea. Paul asked Timothy to write to Christ about these places in Laodicea.
Laodicea was good to Paul. He sent greetings through him, and Paul mentioned his name because of this. Epaphroditus was the one who brought the greetings. Give him honor, for he almost died serving us. He risked his life for the sake of Christ, and now he is returning to you with Paul and Timothy.
In this connection Paul wrote to several other places besides Philippi. One wrote to the church in Colossae. Why is this place called what it is? It is called Colossae. Another wrote to his dear friend named Philemon, who lived in Colossae. This person spoke of Onesimus, a servant of Philemon.
Onesimus had run away from Philemon and gone to Rome. However, Onesimus learned that Paul was in prison in Rome. So he returned to ask for forgiveness, and Paul helped him greatly. Now, however, Onesimus is returning to Christ. He has been changed. Why is it important that Paul wrote to his friend Philemon?
Paul begged Philemon to receive Onesimus. Paul wrote, "I send him back to you, my own child. For he is useful to you and a brother in Christ." If Onesimus returns to Colossae, he will be helpful to you, both in Colossae and to Philemon. We hope that Philemon will understand that his servant has become a Christian.
When Paul wrote to Laodicea and Philemon, he also had another request. Paul said to Laodicea, "I am sending Timothy to you. I hope to see him soon." And to Philemon he wrote this: "Prepare a room for me."
Paul longed to visit his children and fellow believers in Christ again. Because it seemed good to Paul to go to Rome. That time he could not come. Why did he write to Timothy and urge him to come quickly? Paul wrote: "I thank God for you. And may God have mercy." Many years later when Paul died, Jerusalem was destroyed again, and that time it was by Titus.
And about many things concerning the Millennial Kingdom. Jehovah God sent his angel John to write his new messages, and others about the book of Revelation. This book explains the meaning of those things that happen. Let us study the meaning of those things that happened during that time.
Acts 28:16-31; Laodiceans 1:13; 2:19-30; 4:18-23; Hebrews 13:23; Philemon 1-25; Colossians 4:7-9; 2 Timothy 4:7-9.
Questions
- What caused Paul to be imprisoned in Rome?
- What is the reason for this, why is this matter important now, and what does it have to do with Paul?
- If Laodicea is willing, can she send someone to help Laodicea?
- Why did Paul write to his dear friend Philemon?
- Did Paul mention any trials, and were they resolved in his favor?
- Why did Jehovah cause new messages from the Bible and the book of Revelation to be written, and how does this book explain things?
Further Questions
- Read Acts 28:16-31 and Laodiceans 1:13.
Did Paul use his imprisonment in Rome and his freedom to preach the good news without hindrance even among Christians? (Acts 28:23, 30; Laod. 1:14)
- Read Laodiceans 2:19-30.
What reasons did Paul give for being zealous with Timothy and Laodicea, and can we learn something from Paul's example? (Laod. 2:20, 22, 25, 29, 30; 1 Cor. 16:18; 1 Thess. 5:12, 13)
- Read Philemon 1-25.
For what reason did Paul appeal to Philemon regarding Onesimus, and will this matter affect the unity of the Christian congregation? (Philem. 9; 2 Cor. 8:8; Col. 5:13)
Does Paul's statement in Philemon 13, 14 show that he would be willing to sacrifice his own rights for the benefit of others? (1 Cor. 8:7, 13; 10:31-33)
- Read 2 Timothy 4:7-9.
As a faithful apostle, can we find comfort knowing that Jehovah will strengthen us when we face difficulties while continuing to serve him faithfully? (Matt. 24:13; Eph. 6:10)

text:
NĨKĨ ũtaĩle kwĩthĩwa na nzika na ndeto isu syaweta kana Yeova nũkũsũvĩaa? Kĩtumi kĩmwe nĩ kana Mbivilia nĩyo ĩwetete ũu. Ĩandĩko ya 1 Vetelo 5:7 yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Mũkĩmwiĩa kwĩmakĩa kwenyu kw'onthe, nũndũ nĩwe ũmũsũvĩaa.' Nĩ kyaũ kĩĩkĩĩthasya vyũ kana Yeova Ngai nũkũthĩnĩkĩaa?
NGAI NĨWE WĨANĨASYA MAVATA MA ANDŨ
Ũndũ ũmwe nĩ kana Ngai e nguma ila mũndũ wendaa anyanyae methĩwe nasyo. Kaingĩ ala me ĩnee na ũlau nĩmatumaa ndũũ ngamu na ala angĩ mailyĩ o tamo. Na o tondũ wĩsĩ, Yeova e ĩnee na nĩ mũlau. Kĩla mũthenya andũ nĩmatethekaa nĩ nguma isu syake. Sũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno ĩmwe: "We nũmaumĩasya syũa yake athũku na aseo, na kũmauĩsya mbua ala mekaa ũlũngalu na ala matekaa ũlũngalu." (Mt. 5:45) Nũseo wĩva ũetawe nĩ mbua na syũa? Ve moseo maingĩ ĩndĩ ũseo ũmwe nĩ kana kĩu kĩtumaa Ngai 'ausũĩsya andũ lĩu na ũtanu ngoonĩ syoo.' (Meko 14:17) Vate nzika, Yeova nũĩkĩĩthasya kana nthĩ nĩyaumya ũsyao mwingĩ vyũ, na kĩndũ kĩmwe tũtanĩaa mũno nĩ kũya lĩu mũue nesa.
Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ methĩawa na yũa? Nũndũ asumbĩki ma andũ masiasya mũno kĩla kĩtonya kũtuma methĩwa me nguma maũndũnĩ ma siasa na maiseũvya mbesa vandũ va kũtethya andũ. Ĩndĩ o mĩtũkĩ Yeova nũkũmina thĩna ũsu andũ maetete nũndũ wa ĩtomo. Akavetanga silikalĩ ila syĩ kw'o na aiete Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtunĩ, ũla ũkethĩwa ũtongoew'e nĩ Mwana wake e tawe Mũsumbĩ. Ĩvinda yĩu vai mũndũ ũkakwatwa nĩ yũa. Ĩndĩ kavindanĩ kaa tũĩ Ngai nũmanthĩaa athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku kya ũya. (Sav. 37:25) Ũndũ ũsu tyo ũũtũĩkĩĩthya kana Ngai nũtũsũvĩaa?
YEOVA NŨTŨMĨAA ĨVINDA YAKE VAMWE NAITŨ
Mũnyanyau ũla mũseo nũtũmĩaa ĩvinda yake vamwe naku. O na no atũmĩe masaa maingĩ naku mũineenea kĩndũ inywelĩ mwendete. Na mũnyanyau ũla mũseo nũkwĩthukĩĩasya nesa ĩla ũendeee kũmũtavya mathĩna maku. We Yeova nũtwĩthukĩĩasya ũu? Ĩĩ, nĩwĩkaa ũu. Nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya sitũ. Nĩkyo Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya ĩkatwĩa 'nĩtwĩkale na ũlũmu mboyanĩ,' o na nĩtwĩaa 'tũvoyae tũtekũeka.'—Alo. 12:12; 1 Ath. 5:17.
We Yeova atonya kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yĩana ata ethukĩĩsye mboya syaku? Ve ngelekany'o yĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩkũtũtetheesya kũkwata ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu. Yesũ atanamba kũnyuva atũmwa make, amanthie ĩvinda "ekala ũtukũ w'onthe akĩvoya Ngai." (Luka 6:12) Mboyanĩ ĩsu Yesũ nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aneeneie kĩla mũmanyĩw'a e weka aimũweta na ĩsyĩtwa. No kwĩthĩwa aneeneie nguma sya kĩla ũmwe na mawonzu make, na avoya Ĩthe amũtetheesye kũmanyuva. Syũa yĩyĩsa kũtw'ĩka nĩyauma, Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana nĩwanyuva ala maaĩlĩte vyũ kũtw'ĩka atũmwa. Nũndũ Yeova nĩwe "ũla wĩw'aa mboya," nũtanaa kwĩthukĩĩsya mboya syonthe ila andũ mavoya kuma ngoonĩ. (Sav. 65:2) O na mũndũ akamina masaa meana ata aivoya nũndũ wa ũndũ ũũmũthĩny'a mũno, Yeova ndatalaa ta waanangĩwa ĩvinda.
NGAI NĨWĨYŨMBANĨTYE KŨEKEA
Mavinda amwe o na andũ me ndũũ nĩmew'aa ve vinya kũekeanĩa. O na ĩmwe andũ nĩmooaa ndũũ matumĩte kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nũndũ wa kũemwa vyũ nĩ kũekeanĩa. Yeova we ndailyĩ ũu. Mbivilia nĩthoketye mũndũ w'onthe ũla wĩ na ngoo nzeo amwĩtye ũekeo "nũndũ akamũekea vyũ." (Isa. 55:6, 7) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa Ngai aekea nesa wĩana ũu?
Kĩla kĩtumaa Ngai eka ũu nĩ kana we e wendo ũte maela. Nĩwendete nthĩ mũno na nũndũ wa ũu nĩwanenganie Mwana wake, Yesũ, nĩ kana atangĩĩe andũ kuma ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na thĩna ũla makwatĩte nũndũ wa ĩ naĩ. (Yoa. 3:16) Na ti ũu wĩ w'oka. Nũndũ wa nthembo ĩsu Klĩsto waumisye, Ngai nũekeaa na ngenda onthe ala ũmendete. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa nĩtũkumbũla naĩ sitũ, we e kĩthito, na nĩ mũlũngalu wa utũekea naĩ sitũ." (1 Yoa. 1:9) Nũndũ Yeova nũekeaa andũ, nĩmatonya kũendeea kũtanĩa ngwatanĩo nzeo nake. Na nũndũ Ngai nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa na nzĩa ĩsu, ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtwĩkĩaa vinya mũno.
NŨKŨTETHASYA ĨLA WĨ NA THĨNA
Mũndũ wendete ũngĩ kuma ngoonĩ nũmũtethasya ĩla wĩ na vata. We Yeova nĩwĩkaa ũu? Ndeto yake ĩtwĩĩte atĩĩ: "O na [mũthũkũmi wa Ngai] avalũka, ndakavika nthĩ vyu; nĩkwĩthĩwa Yeova nĩwe ũnũũmũkwata na kw'oko." (Sav. 37:24) Yeova 'akwataa athũkũmi make kw'oko' na nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwaeka wone ũndũ kyu kyonanĩtw'e nesa nĩ ngewa ĩmwe yumĩte kĩthamanĩ kya Caribbean kĩtawa St. Croix.
Ve kamwĩlĩtu kamwe kaleile kũkũnĩa kĩvendela saluti nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wako, na kyu kyatuma kathĩnw'a nĩ syana ila kasomaa nasyo. Nĩkavoyie Yeova akatetheesye na katw'a kana kaiekela ngewa ĩsu vau. Ĩla ĩvinda yako yavikie ya kumĩsya kĩlasi ũvoo, katũmĩie mwanya ũsu kũelesya ĩũlũ wa kũkũnĩa kĩvendela saluti. Katũmĩie Ĩvuku Yakwa ya Ngewa sya Mbivilia kũelesya ũndũ ĩla ngewa ya Satalaki, Mesaki, na Aveti-neko yakatetheeisye kwĩka ũtwi ũla keekie. Katavisye kĩlasi kĩu atĩĩ: "Yeova nĩwasũvĩie Aevelania asu atatũ nũndũ mayaaĩtĩkĩla kũthaitha mũvw'anano." Na ĩndĩ keea syana syonthe ila syaĩ vau kana syenda no kainenge ĩvuku yĩu. Syana ĩkũmi na kamwe nĩsyendie kũkwata ĩvuku yĩu. Kamwĩlĩtu kau nĩkamanyie kana Yeova nĩwe wakanengie ũkũmbaũ na ũĩ wa kumya ũkũsĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ta ũsu wĩany'a vinya ũu, na kĩu nĩkyatumie katana mũno.
Ũkesa kũya nzika kana Yeova nũkũsũvĩaa, vindĩĩsya mĩsoa ta ĩno ya Mbivilia: Savuli 34:17-19; 55:22; na 145:18, 19. Kũlya ala methĩĩtwe me Ngũsĩ ĩvinda ĩasa ũndũ Yeova wĩthĩĩtwe aimasũvĩa. Na wesa kũkwatwa nĩ vata, voya Ngai ũmũtavye vata waku. Weeka ũu, ndwĩema kwĩthĩa kaĩ Yeova 'nĩwe ũkũsũvĩaa'!

translation:
Will you be disturbed by sickness and old age even if Jehovah sustains you? One reason is that the Bible does not guarantee perfect health. The scripture from 1 Peter 5:7 says: 'Cast all your worry upon him, because he cares for you.' Is it therefore comforting to know that Jehovah God cares for you?
GOD SHOWS COMPASSION TO PEOPLE
One thing is that God allows humans to experience suffering. Many also suffer due to accidents and bad decisions made by others. But despite this, Jehovah cares and is compassionate. Every day people are affected by problems they did not cause. Consider this example: "You must love your enemies and pray for those who mistreat you, and do good to those who hate you and pray for those who falsely accuse you." (Matt. 5:45) So how can you show love and compassion? Well, there are many ways, and one way is that doing so pleases God 'with joy and generosity.' (Mark 14:17) Therefore, Jehovah appreciates that we feel sorry for others deeply, and something we can do is to help them when possible.
Why do many people struggle with sorrow? Because they often focus on their own problems and fail to see the needs of others. They may become preoccupied with material things and neglect spiritual matters. How can you avoid becoming self-absorbed? Jehovah helps us to remember that we should care about others. He sent his Son to earth, who showed the greatest expression of love. This demonstrates that God values human life. A person might be overwhelmed by sorrow. But remember that God understands our feelings. (Ps. 37:25) Does this mean that God will always prevent us from experiencing difficulties?
JEHOVAH GIVES US HELP IN TIME OF NEED
Often, we ask for his help in prayer. And he may use hours or days to answer our requests. But often, we get discouraged if we don't receive an immediate response. Do we trust that Jehovah will help us? Yes, we can be sure of that. He encourages us to persevere. That is what the Bible teaches when it tells us to 'be patient in tribulation,' and to 'keep on making urgent appeal in prayer.'—Acts 12:12; 1 Thess. 5:17.
Can Jehovah give us strength even when we feel deeply discouraged? Yes, consider how the Bible encourages us to maintain a positive outlook. Jesus spent nights in prayer, asking God for guidance. (Luke 6:12) Through him, Jesus can help us remain steadfast even when facing trials. He can strengthen us individually and give us the courage to endure. Furthermore, Jesus assures us that Jehovah will send angels to assist us. So, while Jehovah is "the One who heals," he does not eliminate all suffering, but he comforts those who turn to him. (Ps. 65:2) And even if someone spends years struggling with a problem, Jehovah will never abandon them.
GOD IS COMPASSIONATE
Sometimes people may find it difficult to accept comfort. But you too can benefit from this comfort if you humbly seek it. Jehovah wants what is best for you. The Bible promises everyone who desires forgiveness a way to receive it. (Isa. 55:6, 7) What motivates God to show such compassion?
God's love is the primary reason he offers comfort. His greatest act of love was sending his Son, Jesus, to die so that we might have everlasting life. (John 3:16) And that is not all. Because of his loyalty, God provides further comfort through his Word and his organization. The apostle John wrote: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us our sins." (1 John 1:9) Thus, because Jehovah forgives us, we can continue to enjoy a close relationship with him. And knowing that God cares for us deeply gives us great hope.
TO KEEP ENCOURAGED AND HOPEFUL
When someone faces difficulties, it is good to encourage them and offer support. Does Jehovah feel the same way? His answer is found in these words: "Even though the upright stumble, they will not be completely overthrown, for Jehovah supports them with his hand." (Ps. 37:24) Jehovah 'supports his loyal ones.' Consider the example of a woman living on the island of St. Croix in the Caribbean.
One young woman decided to focus on her spiritual goals, and this helped her to cope with problems she was facing. She prayed to Jehovah asking for strength and comfort. But her greatest need was to stop missing classes regularly, so she used her time to prepare to attend meetings. Using the book What Does the Bible Really Say?, she learned about the faith of Sarah, Rebekah, and Abimelech. She then shared what she had learned with others, saying: "Jehovah has shown me how to remain faithful despite my challenges." And she made sure to study regularly, even when she felt tired or discouraged. One young man realized that Jehovah was the one who gave him the courage to face life's difficulties, and he began to appreciate the value of spending time in prayer. This helped him to stay strong spiritually.
Be confident that Jehovah will support you, and consider these scriptures: Psalm 34:17-19; 55:22; and 145:18, 19. As we meditate on what Jehovah does for us, our confidence grows. And remember that Jehovah is always willing to help those who turn to Him.

text:
We ũeleawa kyaũ ĩla weew'a andũ mayasya, "Mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ?" Ũkũnaa visa ya mũtavany'a aũngye yukwaanĩ ayĩkya moko kũũ na kũũ akwete Mbivilia aineena ĩũlũ wa maũndũ mathũku meĩkĩka? Kana ũkũnaa visa wa mũtumĩa wĩ na kĩng'ee kĩnene aũngye ũtee wa nzĩa vandũ taoni, ekĩĩte kanzũ ndaasa yovetwe na ũlii kĩnyunyu akwete ĩthangũ yĩ na ũvoo wa mũthenya wa wanangĩko? Kũsũanĩa maũndũ ta asu no kũtume andũ amwe methĩwa na nzika, kana kũkatuma angĩ mona ta ũndũ wa ngũĩ.
Mbivilia yaĩtye kana 'mũminũkĩlyo ũkooka.' (Mathayo 24:14) Ĩsyĩtwa yĩngĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo nĩ "mũthenya mũnene wa Ngai" na "Ali–Maketoni." (Ũvuan'yo 16:14, 16) Ndĩni nieleasya ũndũ ũsu kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, sya ũsengy'a, na ite sya kwendeesya. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye maũndũ ala ma w'o na ĩkavuany'a ala mate ma w'o ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo. Ndeto ya Ngai nĩtũtetheeasya kũmanya kana mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ. Na ũndũ ũla wa vata nĩ kana nĩtwonasya ũndũ tũtonya kũvonoka! Mbee, ekai twone maũndũ amwe andũ mawetaa ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo mate ma w'o, na ĩndĩ tũyĩmanyĩsya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo. Yo Mbivilia yaĩtye "mũminũkĩlyo" nĩ kyaũ?
MAŨNDŨ MATE MA W'O ĨŨLŨ WA MŨMINŨKĨLYO
MŨMINŨKĨLYO NĨ MWAKI MŨNENE ŨKANANGA NTHĨ.
Mbivilia yaasya atĩĩ: 'Ngai ambĩlĩlye myambĩlĩlyo ya nthĩ, nĩ kana ndĩkaathingithĩke tene na tene.' (Savuli 104:5) Ĩandĩko yĩu na angĩ maingĩ monanĩtye kana Ngai ndakananga nthĩ kana etĩkĩlye yanangwe o na ĩndĩĩ! —Mũtavan'ya 1:4; Isaia 45:18.
MŨMINŨKĨLYO ŨKOOKA VATE MŨVANGO.
Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana mũthenya wa mũminũkĩlyo nũvangĩĩwe. Ũu nĩkwasya kana Ngai nũvangĩte nesa mũthenya ũla mũminũkĩlyo ũkoka. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũsu na saa ũsu vai ũmwe wĩsĩ, o na alaĩka me ĩtunĩ, o na Mwana, ĩndĩ no Asa. Ĩsũvĩei, syaĩĩsyai, na voyai: nũndũ mũtyĩsĩ ĩvinda yĩu nĩ ĩndĩĩ." (Maliko 13:32, 33) Ngai ("Asa") nũvangĩte nesa vyũ "ĩvinda" yĩla ũkaete mũminũkĩlyo.
MŨMINŨKĨLYO ŨKAETWE NĨ ANDŨ KANA SYĨNDŨ ĨKAVALŨKA KUMA YAYAYANĨ.
Mũminũkĩlyo ũkaetwe nĩ kyaũ? Ĩandĩko ya Ũvuan'yo 19:11 yaĩtye: "Na noona ĩtu yĩvingũkĩte; na sisya, mbalasi nzaũ, na ũla ũmĩtũlĩte, eetawa Mũkĩthito na Mũw'o." Naw'o mũsoa wa 19 ũendeee kwasya: "Na noona ĩla nyamũ, na asumbĩ ma nthĩ, na ita syoo, mombanĩte makwatye kaũ na ũla wĩkalĩle ĩla mbalasi, na ita syake." (Ũvuan'yo 19:11-21) O na kau ndeto ila itũmĩĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu nĩ sya ngelekany'o, twĩĩmanyĩsya kana Ngai akatũma nguthu ya alaĩka kwananga amaitha make.
MAŨNDŨ MA W'O ĨŨLŨ WA MŨMINŨKĨLYO
NĨ MŨTHYA WA SILIKALĨ SYA ANDŨ.
Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Ngai wa ĩtunĩ akaũngamya ũsumbĩ ũtakaanangĩka tene na tene, o na ũsumbĩki waw'o ndũkaatiĩwa ũko ũngĩ wa andũ; ĩndĩ ũkatilanga ilungu na kũmina mosumbĩ asu onthe, naw'o ũkekalaa tene na tene." (Ndanieli 2:44) O ta ũndũ tũwetie ũndũnĩ wa 3, "asumbĩ ma nthĩ, na ita syoo" ala makethĩwa "mombanĩte makwatye kaũ na ũla wĩkalĩle ĩla mbalasi, na ita syake" makaanangwa.—Ũvuan'yo 19:19.
NĨ MŨTHYA WA KAŨ, ŨNG'ENDU, NA ŨSILI ŨTE WA KATĨ.
"[Ngai] nũtumaa makaũ mathela kũvika kĩtulu kya nthĩ." (Savuli 46:9) "Ala alũngalu makatũa ĩ nthĩ, Na ala eanĩu makamĩkalaa. Ĩndĩ ala athũku makavetwa kuma ĩ nthĩ, Na nzeleke ikakũanĩw'a na mĩi syume nthĩnĩ wayo." (Nthimo 2:21, 22) "Sisya, nĩngũtw'a maũndũ onthe meũ."—Ũvuan'yo 21:4, 5.
NĨ MŨTHYA WA NDĨNI ILA IMŨVĨTĨSYE NGAI NA IKASYA ANDŨ.
'Athani nĩmathanaa ũvũngũ na athembi nĩmasumbĩkaa me mokonĩ moo, na mũminũkĩlyo mũkeeka ata?' (Yelemia 5:31) "Mũthenya ũsu nĩ aingĩ makambĩa, Mwĩaĩi, Mwĩaĩi, tũiaathana na syĩtwa yaku, na kumya ndaimoni na syĩtwa yaku, na kwĩka mavinya maingĩ na syĩtwa yaku? Nĩvo ĩndĩ ngamatavya vyũ, Ndyaamũmanya o na ĩndĩĩ: umai vala nĩĩ, inyw'ĩ mwĩkaa mothũku."—Mathayo 7:21-23.
NĨ MŨTHYA WA ANDŨ ALA MAKWATAA MBAU MAŨNDŨ MA NTHĨ ĨNO.
Yesũ Klĩsto aisye atĩĩ: "Na ũũ nĩw'o ũsilĩlo, nũndũ kyeni nĩ kyũku kĩkalika kũũ nthĩ, na andũ nĩmendie kĩvindu kũte kyeni; nũndũ mawĩa moo maĩ mathũku." (Yoana 3:19) Mbivilia nĩeleetye kwanangwa kwa nthĩ ĩvindanĩ ya mũndũũme mũĩkĩĩku Noa. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nthĩ ĩla yaĩ vo yaaa, ĩkĩvwĩkwa nĩ manzĩ: ĩndĩ matu ala me vo yu, na nthĩ, sĩĩwe mwaki ũndũ wa ndeto o ĩsu, ikĩsũvĩwa kũvika mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo na kwanangwa kwa andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai."—2 Vetelo 3:5-7.
"Mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo na kwanangwa" ũelekanĩtw'e na wanangĩko wa "nthĩ" ya ĩvinda ya Noa. Nĩ nthĩ yĩva ĩla yaanangiwe? Nthĩ ĩĩ twĩkalaa ndyaanangwa, ĩndĩ kĩla kyaanangiwe kana 'kyaaa' nĩ amaitha ma Ngai, ũu nĩkwasya "andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai." Ĩvinda ya "mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo," ala meenyuvĩie kwĩthĩwa me amaitha ma Ngai o namo makaanangwa. Ĩndĩ anyanyae ma Ngai makatangĩĩwa o ta Noa na mũsyĩ wake.—Mathayo 24:37-42.
Kwakũna visa ũndũ nthĩ ĩno ĩkethĩwa ĩseũvĩte ĩtina wa Ngai kũveta ũthũku w'onthe! Vate nzika, ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo nĩ ũvoo mũseo, ĩndĩ ti mũthũku. Ĩndĩ no wĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Yo Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye mũminũkĩlyo ũkooka ĩndĩĩ? No wĩthĩwe wĩ vakuvĩ? Naĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana nĩtangĩĩwa?'

translation:
Do you understand what it means when people ask, "Why are believers suffering?" Does having a travel visa allow someone to cross borders easily, just like possessing the Bible allows one to overcome many difficulties? Or does having the authority of a leader with a large following enable them to judge others harshly, causing pain and sorrow, and leading to bitterness and resentment among people? To explain things clearly and send some people away with peace, or to cause anger over a matter of opinion.
The Bible says whether a "believer" is genuine. (Matthew 24:14) Many characteristics of a believer are "God's great day" and "Armageddon." (Revelation 16:14, 16) I want to explain this issue so that you can understand it well, think about it, and investigate it. Now and then, the Bible reveals things about those who are genuine and exposes things about those who are false regarding believers. God's purpose is to help us determine whether a believer is genuine. And the benefit of that is that we will be able to save ourselves! Therefore, let us examine some things people have said about believers, both true and false, and let us learn from them about believers. So what does the Bible mean by "believer"?
THINGS ABOUT BELIEVERS
A BELIEVER IS A STRONG FOUNDATION.
The Bible states: 'God founded the earth firmly, so that it would never wobble.' (Psalm 104:5) This scripture and many others show that God created the earth skillfully and carefully!—Genesis 1:4; Isaiah 45:18.
THE BELIEVER'S LIFE IS SUPPORTED BY GOD.
The Bible shows that the life of a believer is sustained. This means that God sustains the life of a believer. The Bible says: "Concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, but only the Father. Be on guard, stay awake; for you do not know when the time will come." (Mark 13:32, 33) God ("the Father") sustains the very "hour" when the believer's life will end.
THE BELIEVER IS ATTACKED BY PEOPLE OR SATAN THE DEVIL.
What attacks a believer? Revelation 19:11 says: "And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse, and he who sat on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and wages war." Moreover, Revelation 19 continues to say: "And his eyes are like a flame of fire, and on his head are many crowns, and he has a name written which no one knows except himself, and he rides on a white horse, and his name is called Word of God." (Revelation 19:11-21) And although that scripture is used figuratively, we realize that God sends his angels to fight against his enemies.
THE THINGS THAT ARE INVOLVED IN A BELIEVER'S LIFE
ARE A MATTER OF SPIRITUAL DISCERNMENT.
The Bible states this way: "The God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, and his kingdom shall not pass away to another people; it shall crush all other kingdoms and bring them to nothing, and it shall stand forever." (Daniel 2:44) Also, the expression in verse 3, "kingdoms," and "dominion" are shown to be "crushed and given to the saints, and dominion to the people of the Most High"—Revelation 19:19.
IT IS A MATTER OF FAITH, ENDURANCE, AND TRUE LOVE.
"[God] sends forth his wars to battle." (Psalm 46:9) "The wicked bend their bow and aim their arrow at the upright in heart, and those who tremble are hidden. But the righteous have refuge in times of trouble, and the Lord knows the thoughts of the upright." (Proverbs 2:21, 22) "Be watchful, then, over all things."—Revelation 21:4, 5.
IT IS A MATTER OF LOYALTY TO GOD AND HELPING PEOPLE.
"The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests dominate over them, and my people love it. What will you do in the end?" (Jeremiah 5:31) "Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not do many mighty works in your name, and expel demons in your name, and perform many miracles in your name?' To them I will declare, 'I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of lawlessness.'"—Matthew 7:21-23.
IT IS A MATTER OF PEOPLE WHO TAKE THE WORDS OF THIS TIME SERIOUSLY.
Jesus Christ said: "And this is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light because their deeds were evil. For everyone doing evil hates the light and does not come to the light." (John 3:19) The Bible shows the reason for the flood during the time of righteous Noah. It says: "But the world that was at that time was flooded with water and perished; but the heavens and the earth that are now exist because he reserved them for the judgment of ungodly people by fire."—2 Peter 3:5-7.
"Judgment by flood and fire" is illustrated by the account of "the world" of Noah's time. Is this world already judged? This world we live in, whether it is judged or 'perishes,' is due to God's appointed times, which is why "ungodly people" are mentioned. The "judgment by flood," however, happened to those who rejected God's commands and did not listen. God's warnings were given to Noah and his household.—Matthew 24:37-42.
Consider how important this matter is, so that we may prove ourselves worthy in God's eyes! Please note that the purpose of the Bible's warning to mankind is very serious, and it is not something trivial. It also asks: 'Will the Bible really fulfill its prophecy? Will they be saved? And what if someone rejects it or ignores it?'

text:
"No kakalĩ kamwe kethĩawa na sivika kala katũmĩawa wĩanĩ wa Mwĩaĩi nthĩ ya Brazil, na andũ milioni mbingĩ makesĩ ta, 'kala kakalĩ ke na sivika ka Watch Tower.'"—Ndeto sya Nathaniel A. Yuille, mwakanĩ wa 1938.
MYAKANĨ ya 1930, nthĩ ya Brazil ndyaaĩka maendeeo manene wĩanĩ wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1935, Nathaniel na Maud Yuille, ala maĩ mavainia, nĩmaandĩkĩie Joseph F. Rutherford valũa. Ĩvinda yĩu Mwana-a-asa Rutherford nĩwe waũngamĩe wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Nĩmeeyumisye matũmĩwe ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova na maandĩka kana mew'a "mũyo mũno makatũmwa o na ethĩwa nĩ va."
Ĩvinda yĩu Nathaniel aĩ na myaka 62 na aĩ anathyũmũĩa wĩa. We aĩ ingyinia wa malelũ na myako. O na ĩngĩ eethĩĩtwe e mũũngamĩi wa ũthũkũmi wa kĩkundi kĩmwe kya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kĩla kyaĩ San Francisco, California, Amelika. E kĩkundinĩ kĩu nĩwavangĩthasya ũtavany'a na nĩwatũmĩĩte syĩndũ ta kĩnanda kũtavany'a. Kwoou ũmanyi wake na wendi wake syongelanw'a nĩsyatetheeisye wĩanĩ ũla wanengiwe. Atw'ĩkĩthiw'e mũsyaĩĩsya wa ovisi wa ũvonge wa nthĩ ĩsu nene ya Brazil na ĩneenawa ithyomo mbingĩ.
Nathaniel na Maud mavikie Brazil mwakanĩ wa 1936, na maendanisye na vainia ũngĩ weetawa Antonio P. Andrade na no we waĩ mũtavuta woo. Maendie Brazil na mĩio ya vata mũno, nayo yaĩ inanda 35 vamwe na kakalĩ kamwe ke na sivika. O na kau ĩũlũ wa nthĩ Brazil nĩyo ya katano kwa ũnene, ĩvinda yĩu yaĩ na atavany'a o ta 60! Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa myaka mĩvũthũ, syĩndũ o isu syalikile nthĩ ĩsu nĩsyatetheeisye andũ milioni mbingĩ mamanya ũvoo mũseo.
Mwana-a-asa na mwĩĩtu-a-asa Yuille mavika Brazil vathelile mwei o ũmwe na ovisi wa ũvonge wavanga kwĩthĩwe na ũmbano mũnene (service convention). Ũmbano ũsu nĩw'o waĩ wa mbee Brazil na weekĩiwe taoninĩ ya São Paulo. Kala kakalĩ nĩkalikile wĩanĩ katwaĩtwe nĩ Maud. Kaendie kaithokya andũ moke methukĩĩsye ũvoo wa andũ onthe, na andũ 110 nĩmookie! Ũmbano ũsu nĩwatumie atavany'a mosa vinya, na nũndũ wa ũu mongela kĩthito kyoo kya kũtavany'a. O na nĩmamanyie ũndũ matonya kũtũmĩa mavuku ũtavany'anĩ vamwe na ila kaati sya kumya ũkũsĩ. O na ĩngĩ nĩmamanyie kũtũmĩa inanda syĩ na maũvoo ma Kĩsũngũ, German, Hungarian, Polish, Spanish na ĩtina, Portuguese.
Mwakanĩ wa 1937 ve maũmbano angĩ atatũ ta ũsu wawetwa ala meekĩiwe São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, na Curitiba. Maũmbano asu nĩmatumie atavany'a mosa vinya ĩngĩ mongela kĩthito ũtavany'anĩ. Ala maĩ maũmbanonĩ asu maatĩanĩaa na kala kakalĩ matavanĩtye nyũmba na nyũmba. Ĩvinda yĩu José Maglovsky aĩ o kavĩsĩ na awetie ũndũ kwailyĩ asya: "Twoosaa mavuku maitũ tũkamailĩĩla kamesanĩ, na ĩndĩ ũvoo ũendeee kũtangaaswa nĩ kala kakalĩ ke na sivika twaendaa tũkaneena na ala maumaala masisye nĩ kyaũ kĩendeee."
Andũ mavatisĩwe mbũsĩnĩ, na kwaĩ andũ angĩ mookĩte kũthambĩa meyanĩkĩe syũa. Ũsu ko ũtaĩ mwanya mũseo vyũ wa kũtũmĩa kala kakalĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo! Sivika isu syatumie ũvoo wa ũvatiso wa Mwana-a-asa Rutherford wĩw'ĩka kũasa. Andũ ala maendie kũmbĩĩa kakalĩ kau mamanye nĩ ka kĩ, nĩmeethukĩĩisye ũvoo ũsu ũialyũlwa na kĩthyomo kya Portuguese. Na ĩndĩ andũ mambĩĩa kũvatiswa, mbathi sya Ũsumbĩ sinĩtwe na kĩthyomo kya Polish nĩsyeekĩiwe. Namo ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa mooseleela mbathi isu mainĩte na ithyomo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ĩvuku ya Kitabu cha Mwaka (Kĩsũngũ) ya 1938 yaisye ũũ: "Mũndũ e vau alilikanaa ũndũ ĩvinda ya Vendekosito kĩla mũndũ weewie [ũvoo] na kĩthyomo ĩ kyake."
Kuma maũmbano asu mathela, kĩla Wakyumwa kwĩthĩwe kwĩ mbua kana kwĩ syũa, andũ nĩmeew'aa maũvoo ma Mbivilia kuma kala kakalĩnĩ, methĩwe mathũmũĩte iwanzanĩ, me nyũmba, kana me kambunĩnĩ ila syĩ São Paulo nthĩnĩ na taoninĩ ingĩ ila syĩ vau vakuvĩ. Na kĩla mwei kakalĩ kau nĩkaendaa vandũ vangĩ vekalaa andũ 3,000 mavathĩtwe nũndũ wa kũwaa mangũ nĩ kana o namo mew'e ũvoo. Vandũ vau vaĩ maili 60 (kĩlomita 97) kuma São Paulo, ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ kwelekela ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa. Vau nĩvesie kwambĩĩw'a kĩkundi kĩseo mũno. O na kau ũwau ũsu mawaĩte nĩ ũwau wĩ thĩna, atavany'a ma kĩkundi kĩu nĩmeetisye mwanya wa kũthokea angĩ tamo nĩ kana mamakiakisye na ũvoo wa Mbivilia.
Mwaka wa 1938 ũithela, maũvoo malekotiĩtwe na kĩthyomo kya Portuguese nĩmavikie Brazil. Na kwoou mũthenya wa sikũkũ ĩla yĩtawa All Souls' Day, ana-a-asa nĩmatũmĩie kala kakalĩ kũthyũũka iwanzanĩ ila syathikawa andũ nĩ kana mekĩĩe ala mookĩte kũmeta maũvoo me na kyongo "Akw'ũ maĩva?," "Yeova," na "Ũthwii." Maimina kũthyũũka, andũ mbee wa 40,000 nĩmakwatie ũvoo!
Ndongoi sya makanisa syeew'aa woo mũno ũvoo wa Mbivilia ũielew'a ũtheinĩ mũthemba ũsu, na kaingĩ syathing'ĩĩasya anene ma silikalĩ mavindĩthye kakalĩ kau. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Yuille nĩwalilikanaa ĩvinda mũthembi ũmwe woombanisye andũ makombĩĩe. Ĩndĩ ĩla meya na asikalĩ angĩ mavavikie meethukĩĩisye ũvoo w'onthe. O na ũ meya avaumie na mavuku. Vai mũndũ waalua nduuthĩ sua ũsu. Ĩndĩ o na mathĩnĩtw'e oou, livoti ya nthĩ ya Brazil ĩla yaandĩkiwe ĩvukunĩ ya Kitabu cha Mwaka (Kĩsũngũ) ya 1940 yaisye kana mwaka wa 1939 "nĩw'o waĩ ĩvinda ĩseo vyũ ya kũthũkũma ũla Mũsumbĩ Mũnene na kũtavany'a ĩsyĩtwa yake."
Vate nzika, "kala kakalĩ ke na sivika ka Watch Tower" katetheeisye mũno wĩa ũla watethaw'a Brazil wa kũtavany'a. Katethisye mũno kũvikĩsya andũ milioni mbingĩ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. O na kau kakalĩ kau nĩkesie kũtewa mwakanĩ wa 1941, nguthu nene ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova no ĩendeee kũtavya ala me na ngoo nzeo ũvoo mũseo nthĩ ĩsu nene ya Brazil.—Kwĩlilikany'a maũndũ ma tene ma nthĩ ya Brazil.

translation:
"Not a few people were shocked and became concerned when they heard about the work of Jehovah's Witnesses in Brazil, and many millions made remarks like, 'That work and those from Watch Tower.'"—From the 1938 report of Nathaniel A. Yuille.
DURING the 1930's, Brazil experienced great progress of the good news. By 1935, Nathaniel and Maud Yuille, an elderly couple, wrote to Joseph F. Rutherford regarding this matter. Brother Rutherford was the one directing the work of expansion. I am pleased to share how Jehovah has blessed us and his Word, even though some say "it is just a foolish idea."
Brother Nathaniel was 62 years old and was physically weak. He was a carpenter and had children. He also served as an elder in the congregation of the San Francisco, California, United States branch of the Watch Tower Society. In that capacity he supervised the preaching work and sent out pioneers to preach. Because of his knowledge and experience, he was able to help many others. He was appointed to oversee the visit of overseers to large congregations in Brazil and to provide much encouragement.
Nathaniel and Maud arrived in Brazil in 1936, and associated with a fine brother named Antonio P. Andrade who was a pioneer. They traveled throughout Brazil in old cars, some of which were over 35 years old and in poor condition. And yet, because of the size of Brazil—five times larger than the state of California—there were only about 60 full-time preachers! Within a few years, thousands of others joined them in proclaiming the good news to millions of people.
The missionary and his wife, the Yuilles, visited Brazil for about one month and attended a service assembly. This assembly was held in Brazil and drew together people from São Paulo. Not a few people were deeply moved by the talk given by Sister Maud. The attendance reached 110! That assembly helped strengthen the zeal of the publishers, and it proved to be a milestone in the preaching work. And I learned something about using photographs to aid in the ministry, along with illustrated booklets. Also, I learned to use 35 languages, including French, German, Hungarian, Polish, Spanish and, of course, Portuguese.
In 1937 three more assemblies were held in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Curitiba. These assemblies also strengthened the zeal of the publishers. At those assemblies the publishers were organized into groups to conduct house-to-house ministry. One brother, José Maglovsky, expressed himself as follows: "We will take our books and go out in unity, and may this work continue to expand so that not a few of us can rejoice when we meet with other faithful ones and see what has been accomplished."
Many people were interested, and some others began to investigate the truth. So do not miss the opportunity to use the time to strengthen the zeal of the publishers! Indeed, this work of witnessing about God's Kingdom was approved by Jehovah, as shown by the fact that Rutherford readily agreed to it. Those who went out to preach in groups found it helpful, and I personally experienced that this work was blessed because of prayer. The 1938 Year Book stated: "Every individual should endeavor to present the book [Vendekosito] in his own language." And many people responded favorably to being invited, and the Society provided publications in various languages. Brothers and sisters eagerly made use of these publications to help people understand the message.
The 1938 Year Book also said: "During the month of November, over 3,000 publishers traveled to the territory to share in the house-to-house ministry, going from door to door and from business place to business place, especially in São Paulo and other cities. And during each week, they contacted an average of three people, some accepting literature. These publishers were located 60 miles (97 kilometers) from São Paulo, traveling through difficult terrain to reach those interested in the truth. They were encouraged by the fine example set by this group. But sometimes this enthusiasm waned, and the group did not always take advantage of the opportunity to make return visits and further assist people with their Bible studies. In 1938, publications in Portuguese were distributed throughout Brazil. And on the eve of All Souls' Day, the brothers used the opportunity to gather together, and people were often curious and asked questions such as "What is life?" "Jehovah," and "Salvation." As a result of this gathering, over 40,000 people accepted literature!
Many clergymen opposed this work of Bible instruction, and some used their influence to cause trouble for the publishers. Brother Yuille courageously defended the faith and helped many to remain steadfast. This incident, along with others, was reported in the 1940 Yearbook (English edition), which stated that 1939 "was a year of great advancement for the Most High God and for the proclamation of His Kingdom." Later, the article "November Number of The Watch Tower" described how the efforts in Brazil resulted in the proclamation of the good news to millions of people. And although this activity slowed down in 1941, the work of Jehovah's Witnesses continued to expand throughout Brazil.—See the accompanying article on the history of Brazil.

text:
MAVINDA onthe ĩla andũ ma Yeova moombana vamwe mamanyĩw'e nĩwe nĩmethĩawa na ũtanu mwingĩ. Na ĩndĩ ĩla mesa kũĩsanĩa lĩu me maũmbanonĩ asu, kaingĩ kũĩsanĩa kũu nĩkwongelaa ũtanu woo.
Ĩvinda yĩmwe kwĩ Mwei wa 9, 1919, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmeekĩie ũmbano mũnene wa mĩthenya nyanya Cedar Point, Ohio, Amelika. Kwavangĩtwe ala mekuma mũingo makakomaa motelinĩ na maiya vo, ĩndĩ kwookie aingĩ ki kwĩ ala meteelwe. Ĩla athũkũmi ma moteli asu moonie ũu, moosanie nguthu nene mamba kũkola ũ wĩa. Ũmwe wa anene ma moteli asu atuanĩwe nĩ nthĩ nginya akũlya ethĩwa ve amũika amwe katĩ wa ala mookĩte matonya kũtetheesya. Aingĩ nĩmeetĩkĩlile na ngenda. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Sadie Green aĩ ũmwe woo. Aisye: "O na kau ndyaĩ naanengane lĩu ũtelinĩ, nĩtwatanĩie mũno wĩa ũsu."
Myakanĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe, mũvango wa kũua maũmbanonĩ manene (cafeteria) nĩwanengie andũ aingĩ mũno mwanya wa kwĩyumya na ngenda mathũkũme ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa moo. Nũndũ mũvango ũsu nĩwatumaa ana-a-asa mathũkũma vamwe, nĩwatetheeisye amũika aingĩ mende kwĩka maendeeo. Ũmwe wamo aĩ Gladys Bolton ũla watetheesye kũua ũmbanonĩ mũnene mwakanĩ wa 1937. Aisye atĩĩ: "Nakomanie na andũ kuma kũndũ kwingĩ, na nĩneew'aa maiweta kĩla meekĩte masinde mathĩna ala maĩ namo. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o nambĩĩe kwenda mũthenya ũmwe nĩtw'ĩka vainia."
Mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Beulah Covey aisye ũũ e ũmbanonĩ ũmwe mũnene: "Nũndũ ala mekũua nĩmeyumĩtye vyũ, metuma kũtethya wĩa ũsu kwĩthĩwa ne katheeo." Ĩndĩ wĩa ũsu waĩ na mathĩna maw'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 1969, Angelo Manera nĩwaendie kĩwanzanĩ kya Dodger Stadium kĩla kĩ Los Angeles, California, kwondũ wa ũmbano mũnene. Ĩndĩ avika oou nĩw'o wamanyie kana nĩwe ũnyuvĩtwe aũngamĩe wĩa wa kũua. Aisye ũũ: "Natelemile ũndũ ndaatelema!" Ũndũ ũmwe waaĩle kwĩkwa nĩ kwĩnza mũtaũ wĩ na ũasa wa mita 400, nĩ kana vesĩlw'e mũvaivũ wa kũtwaa gas ikonĩ. Na wĩa ũsu waaĩle kũtethw'a ũmbano ũtambĩĩe!
Namo angĩ ma Sierra Leone mwakanĩ wa 1982 yaĩ no nginya mambe kwenga kĩtheka na ĩndĩ mayaka iko maitũmĩa kĩla kyaĩ mokonĩ. Ana-a-asa asu nĩmeeyumisye vyũ kũthũkũma. Na ĩndĩ ana-a-asa amwe ala maĩ Frankfurt, Germany, mwakanĩ wa 1951 nĩmatũmĩie kĩlĩko makomboa kyongo kya ngalĩ ya mwaki nĩ kana kĩmanenge mĩthũmũ matonya kũtinĩsya masilia 40. Ĩvinda yĩu ĩsaa yĩmwe yĩithela aui meethĩawa mevũĩte masaani 30,000. Andũ ala mookie ũmbanonĩ ũsu mekuĩe tũvyũ na ũma nĩ kana maole wĩa wa andũ 576 ala meeyumĩtye mathambye mĩio. Eka asu maĩ Germany, aui ala maĩ Yangon, Myanmar, nĩmasũanĩie ĩũlũ wa ala maumĩte mũingo na nũndũ wa ũu mamauĩa malĩu mate ndũlũ mbingĩ.
"MAĨSAA MAŨNGYE"
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Annie Poggensee nũlilikanaa ũathimo ũla wakwatie ĩvinda yĩmwe wooletye lainĩ mũasa aathĩtwe nĩ syũa. Aĩ ũmbanonĩ ũmwe mũnene waĩ Amelika mwakanĩ wa 1950. Aisye: "Nĩ vau nataviwe nĩ ngewa nzeo yaeawa nĩ eĩtu-a-asa elĩ maumĩte Europe na ĩsiwa." Kĩla ũmwe woo atavasya ũla ũngĩ ũndũ Yeova wamũtetheetye kũvika vau. Annie aisye ũũ: "Vai mũndũ ũngĩ noonaa e mũtanu kwĩ mo. Mayatalaa ta ũndũ kũũngama syũanĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa movetye lainĩ."
Maũmbanonĩ maingĩ manene kweethĩawa na maeema me na mesa ndũlu sya kũĩĩa, na kyu kyatumaa andũ maya mĩtũkĩ nĩ kana mathũkĩe angĩ. Na nengĩ vai ũndũ ũngĩ makili asu ma andũ maĩ matonya kũĩthw'a onthe kavindanĩ kau ate o kĩla ũmwe aiya aũngye. Mũndũ ũmwe ũtaĩ Ngũsĩ esie kwasya ũũ aseng'ete: "Ĩkanisa yĩu ko yĩtasaanĩtye. Maĩsaa maũngye."
Anene ma ita na ma silikalĩ nĩmaseng'aa moona ũndũ wĩa ũsu watethaw'a nesa na ngwatanĩo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe mũndũ ũmwe wathũkũmanaa na United States Army nĩwaendie akesyaĩsye ũndũ wĩa wa kũua watethaw'a ũmbanonĩ mũnene waĩ Yankee Stadium, New York City. Kĩla woonie kyatumie ekĩa vinya Major Faulkner ũla wathũkũmanaa na British War Department athi o nake akesyaĩsye. Kwoou mwakanĩ wa 1955, Major Faulkner na mũka nĩmaendie ũmbanonĩ mũnene waĩ na kyongo "Triumphant Kingdom" ũla waĩ Twickenham, England. Aisye kana nĩwoonie wendo ũituma mũvango wa kũua waĩla ũmbanonĩ ũsu.
Kwa myaka mingĩ, andũ nĩmaendeeie kwĩyumya na ngenda mauĩe ala mooka malĩu maseo na mate ngalama. Ĩndĩ wĩa ũsu ndwaĩ laisi na kaingĩ wendaa andũ aingĩ meyumye na maithũkũma masaa maingĩ. O na kyu nĩkyatumaa matew'a ilungu imwe sya ũmbano kana o na ũmbano ũkathela matew'a kĩndũ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi kũndũ kwingĩ mũthyanĩ wa myaka ya 1970 mũvango ũsu wavĩndũiwe weethĩa ndwĩ na maũndũ maingĩ. Na ĩndĩ kwambĩĩa na mwaka wa 1995, andũ nĩmakũlilw'e makekuĩaa lĩu mayũka maũmbanonĩ manene. Kyu kyatetheeisye mũno weethĩa ala mauaa na makevũa lĩu no matanĩe ũmbano vamwe na kũea ngewa na ala angĩ. *
Yeova ndalea kwĩthĩwa ew'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ wa onthe ala maĩ na kĩthito kĩana ũu kya kũthũkũma ana-a-asa moo. Amwe no kwĩthĩwa meliĩlaa mavinda asu matetheeasya kũua. Ĩndĩ twĩ na ũw'o wa kĩndũ kĩĩ kĩmwe: Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, wendo nĩ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ma vata ala matumaa maũmbano maitũ manene maĩla.—Yoa. 13:34, 35.
^ kal. 12 Ĩndĩ o na matukũ aa ve o mwanya wa kwĩyumya nĩ kana mũndũ atetheesye mĩvĩanĩ ĩmwe maũmbanonĩ manene.

translation:
MAVINDA onthe was among those of Jehovah who joyfully embraced the truth, and he shared it with others enthusiastically. And at times he would spend hours reasoning with people, often spending time explaining the truth to them.
On September 9, 1919, Bible Students held a large gathering at Cedar Point, Ohio, America. Many came from far away, traveling by train and boat, and some had difficulty finding lodging. The grounds were crowded with people, so they made arrangements to accommodate as many as possible. One of the hotel managers was kind enough to allow some to sleep in the hallways to provide shelter. Many were satisfied with the arrangements. Sister Sadie Green was one of them. She said: "Oh, how happy I was to be able to find a place to stay, we appreciated this kindness very much."
In subsequent years, a large dining hall (cafeteria) was built to accommodate more people, providing a convenient place to eat and rest during conventions. This arrangement also helped young ones to get to know each other, and it gave them opportunities to associate with older ones. One of them was Gladys Bolton, who served in the large dining hall in 1937. She said: "I enjoyed being with the brothers and sisters, and I learned a lot from observing how they handled things and treated others. That experience encouraged me to go out in the ministry with confidence."
Another person named Beulah Covey spoke about a large dining hall: "I remember enjoying myself very much, which made it easier to preach the good news." It was a pleasant time for everyone involved. For example, in 1969, Angelo Manera went to Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, California, for a large assembly. He said he didn't know whether he would ever witness such an event again. He stated: "I will never forget what I saw!" Another incident involved running around a track with a 400-meter dash, or perhaps participating in a relay race to obtain a gas token. And those events were truly enjoyable assemblies!
Some people from Sierra Leone in 1982 had to flee their homes because conditions became unbearable and they spent several years in refugee camps. Many others enjoyed themselves immensely. Also, some people in Frankfurt, Germany, in 1951 sent a shipment of timber worth approximately 40 million marks. One ship alone carried over 30,000 tons of wood. Other people at that gathering expressed their joy and happiness, and there were reportedly 576 families who enjoyed the occasion. In addition to Germany, people in Yangon, Myanmar, have experienced similar situations where they have lost many possessions due to various disasters.
"GREAT THINGS"
A woman named Annie Poggensee recalled a time when she and her family were forced to leave their home during World War II. It was a difficult period in America in the 1950s. She said: "I remember being very frightened when I learned that my parents and siblings in Europe and the islands had to flee." Each of them trusted that Jehovah would help them survive. Annie added: "There was always someone who encouraged us. We knew we could rely on God's help during this crisis."
Many large gatherings took place and caused great excitement, and this led people to feel happy and joyful. But often there was something missing for those people—they did not know how to cope with the difficulties they faced, and each person felt lonely. One man named Joseph said: "That church really helped us. Great things."
Those who served and those who remained were eager to see what would happen next and waited patiently. For example, one man who served in the United States Army went to witness the event that happened during the large gathering at Yankee Stadium, New York City. Everyone remembered Major Faulkner, who served in the British War Department, and he also went to witness it. In 1955, Major Faulkner and his wife attended the large gathering with the theme "Triumphant Kingdom" at Twickenham, England. He said that everyone present felt the joy of witnessing such a large gathering.
For many years, people continued to enjoy traveling and seeing wonderful places and beautiful cities. Because of this, many people traveled far and spent many hours serving. And because of this, some became tired from the journey or the journey exhausted them. That is why in the 1970s, the joy was diminished due to many things. And since 1995, people have been reminded to avoid large gatherings. This has helped them to remain healthy and to avoid getting sick and infecting others. *
Jehovah continues to show compassion for all people, both young and old, and appreciates their willingness to learn about him. Some may find it difficult to attend meetings. Let us remember this important principle: Whether we can go personally or not, love is one thing that unites all God's servants.—John 13:34, 35.
^ par. 12 So, whether someone attends meetings or not, they should be given an opportunity to share in the ministry.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1971
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: FRANCE
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: AĨ MŨNG'ENDU, AĨ NA MWĨKALĨLE MŨTHŨKU, NA NĨWATŨMĨAA NDAWA SYA KŨMILA
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Twekalaa kĩsio kĩtawa Tellancourt kĩ ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ ya France. Ĩthe wakwa aumĩte nthĩ ya France na inyia wakwa nĩ wa Italy. Nĩ na myaka nyanya nĩtwathamĩĩie Rome, ĩla yĩ Italy na twathi kwĩkala kũla kwĩkalaa andũ ala ngya na mathũkũmaa mawĩa ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ. Ĩla twaendie kũu maũndũ mayaĩ laisi. Asyai makwa nĩmaemanawa mũno nũndũ wa mathĩna ma mbesa.
Nĩ na myaka 15, inyia wakwa ambĩie nĩthi ngamanthe andũ ma kũtindany'a namo vandũ va kwĩkalaa nĩ weka. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, nĩnambĩĩie kwĩkala ndekwĩnũka mũsyĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩnambĩĩie kũtinda na kĩtindo kĩthũku. Mũthenya ũmwe, nĩnakomanie na mũndũũme noonaa e mũseo. Nĩwanengie ndawa sya kũmila na nainyw'a nũndũ nendaa andũ mamanye nĩ mũndũ mũima. Kuma vau, nĩnambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku na weethĩa ndyĩkala ndanyw'ĩte ndawa sya kũmila. Mavinda maingĩ andũ nĩmangwataa na vinya na makambĩka maũndũ mathũku. Ndyoonaa vata wa kwĩthĩwa thayũ; naĩ neeyĩtũkie, o na andũ mayanũngaa. Nĩ na myaka 16, nĩnatatie kwĩyũaa kwa kũnyw'a sũva wa whiskey na neeyĩkya ĩianĩ yausĩe kĩw'ũ. Nekalile mĩthenya ĩtatũ ndekwĩyĩw'a.
Ĩtina wa ũu nĩnambĩĩie kũng'ang'ana na maũndũ na neethĩwa nĩ mũng'endu na nĩ nzeleke. Nĩneeyumasya ngathi kwa andũ mũsyĩ ngeke ũlaalai namo na ndimanenga ndawa sya kũmila na ĩtina wa ũu ndimoyĩa syĩndũ sya thooa mũnene ila me nasyo. Nguthu ila nene sya imaamai nĩsyandũmĩaa kũtwaa ndawa sya kũmila kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o nthĩ ya Italy. Mavinda maingĩ nĩnathĩnanasya mũno na asikalĩ. Naendeee kwaa mana, o na kau nĩnoonaa no nginya vakethĩwa kĩtumi kya kwĩthĩwa nĩ thayũ. Nĩnavoyie Ngai na namũkũlya anenge mwaka o ũmwe nĩthĩwe na ũtanu na mũuo.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Nĩ na myaka 24, nĩnatwie kũthamĩĩa England. Naĩ mũisyonĩ nũndũ wa kũtindany'a na andũ ala matesaa ndawa sya kũmila. Ndanamba kũthi, nĩnavangie kũthi kwona inyia wakwa. Navika nĩnaseng'ie mũno kwĩthĩa mũndũũme weetawa Annunziato Lugarà aimanyĩsya inyia wakwa Mbivilia. * Nũndũ nĩneesĩ aĩ kĩng'endilĩ nĩneewie wia na namũkũlya eĩka ata vau. Angeleisye moalyũku manene ala weekie nĩ kana atw'ĩke Ngũsĩ ya Yeova na ambĩa navika England, nĩmanthe Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmanyĩsye namo. Nĩneetĩkĩlile kwĩka ũu, ĩndĩ ĩla navikie kũu nasyokea mwĩkalĩle wakwa wa tene.
Mũthenya ũmwe, nĩnakomanie na mũndũũme ũmwe waĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova ainengane makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Amkeni! lelũnĩ ũmwe wĩ mũsyĩ wa London. Nĩnalilikanile ũndũ neeie Annunziato kana ngeemanyĩsya Mbivilia, na nakũlya mũndũũme ũsu wanenganae makaseti twambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia.
Nĩnendeeiw'e nĩ maũndũ ala neemanyĩasya Mbivilianĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩnendeeiw'e nĩ ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Yoana 1:9, ila syaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai: 'Ethĩwa nĩtũkumbũla naĩ sitũ, we e kĩthito, na nĩ mũlũngalu wa kũtũekea naĩ sitũ, na kũtũthesya ũndũ ũte ũlũngalu w'onthe.' Mũsoa ũsu nĩwangiitie mũno nũndũ neew'aa nĩ kĩko mũno nũndũ wa maũndũ ala neekaa. Nĩnambĩĩie kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na nathokw'a nesa. Ĩla noonie ũndũ mendene, wendo ũla nakosete kwa myaka mingĩ, nĩnendie kwĩthĩwa nĩ ũmwe woo nũndũ mekalaa ta andũ ma mũsyĩ ũmwe.
O na kau ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũeka kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila na kũekana na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku, ũndũ ũla waĩ vinya kwakwa nĩ kũalyũla ũndũ nailyĩ ngoonĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩnamanyie kana nĩnaaĩle kũnenga andũ ala angĩ ndaĩa na ndyĩthĩwa ndimaelewa. O na nginya ũmũnthĩ ve o maũndũ nĩendeee kũng'ang'ana nĩekane namo. Ĩndĩ Yeova nũndetheesye ngeka maendeeo. Neemanyĩisye Mbivilia vandũ va myei thanthatũ na navatiswa natw'ĩka ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mwaka wa 1997.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Ĩtina wa kũvatiswa nĩnatwaie Barbara ũla waĩ anatw'ĩka ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩla mũndũũme ũmwe twaĩ ndũũ woonie ũndũ neekĩte moalyũku manene, o nake nĩwambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, nĩwatw'ĩkie ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova e na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia. O na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wa ũsũe wakwa ũla waĩ myaka 80 na kĩndũ nĩwambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na avatiswa na ĩtina wa ĩvinda akw'a.
Yu nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto, nake mũka wakwa nĩ mũtavany'a wa ĩvinda yonthe, amanyĩasya Mbivilia andũ ala mekalaa London maneenaa kĩthyomo kya Italian. Mavinda amwe nĩnĩũmĩaa ngoo mũno nũndũ wa mwĩkalĩle ũla nekalaa tene, ĩndĩ Barbara nũndetheeasya mũno. Yu nĩ na mũsyĩ wĩ na ũtanu na Ĩthe ũmbendete ũndũ nendaa kuma tene. Namũkũlilye Ngai anenge mwaka o ũmwe nĩthĩwe nĩ na mũuo na ũtanu, ĩndĩ nũnengete maũndũ maingĩ kwĩ ũndũ namwĩtisye!
Yu nĩ na mũsyĩ wĩ na ũtanu na Ĩthe ũmbendete ũndũ nendaa kuma tene
^ kal. 10 Sisya kĩlungu "Biblia Inabadili Maisha—Nilitembea na Bunduki Kila Wakati," kĩla kĩeleetw'e nĩ Annunziato Lugarà, ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 01/07/2014, ĩthangũ ya 8-9.

LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1971
THE COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: FRANCE
OUR PARENTS: THOSE WHO TRAVELLED, THOSE WITH A GOOD HEART, AND THEY USED TO SEND US GIFTS TO HELP WITH SCHOOL FEES
FAMILY HISTORY:
We lived in a small village called Tellancourt in the north of France. The father's country of origin is France and the mother's is Italy. I have very old memories of Rome, a city in Italy and we used to go there to live with relatives and friends who were also students in high school classes. We went there to learn many things without difficulty. This family was known for their generosity and kindness towards others.
When I was 15 years old, my mother told me about the difficulties people face when they stay alone. Because of this situation, she advised me to stay close to my older siblings. During the holidays, she advised me to work hard. One day, I met a friend at the museum. I enjoyed helping with school fees and I learned many things from those who knew him well. But because of them, I advised myself to be kind and generous so that I could help with school fees. Many parents get angry and complicate matters unnecessarily. I saw those who wanted to be kind; and I understood, even though some people criticized. When I was 16 years old, I tried to drink a glass of whiskey and I felt a strange sensation in my head. I stayed awake for three nights.
During that time, I advised myself to focus on things and I realized I was wrong. I felt sorry for those who couldn't live with me and I needed help with school fees. That time I lost something very important, but I also had it. However, that thing which is important to me has been causing me trouble trying to get help with school fees from a certain place in Italy. Many times I have suffered greatly with friends. I continue to pray to God, and I believe that next year will be better than this one.
THIS IS A MESSAGE FROM YOUR SIBLING:
I am 24 years old, I came to study in England. My mission is to associate with people and help them with school fees. I decided to come because I wanted to see my family. I found someone named Annunziato Lugarà who knows my family in Mbivilia. * The reason I am telling you this is because I remember a little bit about everything. He told me about a big opportunity, but he said to go to the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah's Witnesses and tell them that I came from England, so they would know the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah's Witnesses and introduce me to him. I agreed to do this, and then I realized I should return to my sibling's home soon.
One day, I met someone from the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah's Witnesses who had cassettes of "The Watchtower" and "Awake!" magazines in one of the cities of London. I asked him about Annunziato or whether he knew Mbivilia, and I found someone who had those cassettes and we talked about introducing Mbivilia.
I was encouraged by what I learned about Mbivilia. For example, I was encouraged by verse 1 John 1:9, which speaks of God's law: 'If we confess our sins to him, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and make us clean from all wrongdoing.' This statement really helped me because it reminded me of things I had done. I told them about the Christian meetings of the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah's Witnesses and I was very happy. But I realized something, the love I had kept for many years, I needed to show it to someone who lived in the same city.
And also, there is another thing that makes it difficult to use school fees and deal with a difficult situation, the problem that comes with it is to forget what I did wrong. For example, I realized that I could offend people and they wouldn't understand me. And now I pray that I continue to be able to correct myself. With Jehovah's help, I can continue. I introduced Mbivilia to many people and I was baptized as one of Jehovah's Witnesses in 1997.
LESSONS I HAVE LEARNED:
The joy of baptism came through Barbara, who is one of Jehovah's Witnesses. But one day, someone we knew showed great interest, and I told her about learning about Mbivilia. In addition, I met one of Jehovah's Witnesses and his relatives. And his relative who was 80 years old asked me to learn about Mbivilia and was baptized with the joy of addition.
I am a member of the Christian congregation, and my wife is a pioneer throughout the whole area, introducing Mbivilia to people who live in London and speak Italian. Some days I feel very sad about the situation I am in, but Barbara encourages me a lot. I have five children and Theth has helped me a lot with this matter. I thank God that every year I am with my family and five children, and I have learned many things from what I have taught them!
I have five children and Theth has helped me a lot with this matter.
^ par. 10 The article "Bible Changes Lives—I Used to Carry a Gun All the Time" featured in *Awake!* (Swahili) of 01/07/2014, pages 8–9.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1954
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: CANADA
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: MŨVENANI NA MŨTHI WA KALATA
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Neanĩie kĩsionĩ kĩtaĩ maendeeo nthĩnĩ wa taoni ya Montreal. Ĩthe wakwa akwie nĩ na myei thanthatũ, na ũu watuma inyia wakwa atiĩwa mawĩa onthe ma mũsyĩ. Twasyaĩtwe twĩ nyanya na ninyie naĩ ĩlumaita.
O nĩendeee na kwĩana, nendete maũndũ ta kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila, kũtha kalata, ũng'endu, na kũtindany'a na ing'endilĩ. Nĩ na myaka ĩkũmi, nathũkũmanaa na malwaya na andũ ala makovethasya mbesa nĩ kana metũngĩwa syĩ na ũsyao mũnene. Mavinda maingĩ nĩnakengaa andũ, o na nĩneew'aa mũyo ĩla natũmĩa mawũĩ kũmavena. Naĩ namanyĩie kwĩka ũu.
Ndyĩsa kũtw'ĩka nĩnavikya myaka 14, nĩneemanyĩĩtye nzĩa mbingĩ sya kũkenga andũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩnathooaa saa, mbangili, na mbete syanakavĩtw'e na thaavu, na ndisyĩkĩa katang'a kekwonany'a iseũvĩtw'e na thaavu. Katang'a kaũ keethĩawa konanĩtye kana kĩndũ kĩu kĩseũvĩtw'e na thaavu (14-carat gold). Nĩnatanĩaa mũno kũseũvya mbesa kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi. Ve mũthenya ũmwe naseũvisye ndola 10,000!
Nĩ na myaka 15, nĩnalũngilw'e sukulu ya kũlũnga mwĩkalĩle na weethĩa ndi vandũ nĩkala. Nakomaa ũtee wa nduka taoni, kũndũ kũla andũ mathyũmũaa, kana mĩsyĩ kwa anyanyawa ala manthokya.
Nũndũ wa syĩko syakwa sya ũkengani, mavinda maingĩ nĩnakwatawa nĩ asikalĩ. Nũndũ ndyatesaa syĩndũ sya ũng'ei, ndyaaĩsa kwovwa. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, nĩnaĩvaa koti mũnene nũndũ wa kũkengana nĩ kana nĩkwate mbesa, kũthoosya syĩndũ sya makendo, o na kũthoosya syĩndũ nde na laĩsenzi. Nde na wia nĩnoosanasya mbesa sya andũ ala makovethasya nĩ kana metũngĩwa mbesa syĩ na ũsyao mũnene. Wĩa ũsu waĩ ũtonya kũtuma nũawa laisi, na mavinda angĩ nĩnakuaa ĩvuti. O na mavinda angĩ nĩnathũkũmanaa na ikundi sya ing'endilĩ.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Noonie Mbivilia ya mbee nĩ na myaka 17. Ĩvinda yĩu nekalanasya na mwĩĩtu twaĩ ndũũ na ambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩnaleanaa na myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩnatianie na mwĩĩtu ũsu na nathi kwĩkalany'a na mũndũ mũka ũngĩ naĩ ndũũ nake.
Maũndũ maalyũkile ĩla o nake mũndũ mũka ũsu wa kelĩ wambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ! Nĩnatanie mũno ĩla weekie moalyũku, ambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa e mũuu na e na wũmĩĩsyo. Nĩneetĩkĩlile ĩla nathokiw'e ũthaithinĩ, Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Navika, nĩnathokiw'e nĩ andũ maĩ atheu na maĩ aseo. Ũndũ ũsu waĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na maũndũ ala namanyĩĩte. Kuma nĩ kana kanini ndyoonaa andũ ma mũsyĩ me vata nakwa, o na neew'aa andũ matambendete. Wendo ũla nooniw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩw'o natwĩe nĩmanthaa. Na kwoou, ĩla meeyumisye kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nakwa neetĩkĩlile vate kwananga ĩvinda.
Nĩvatonyeka maũndũ ala neemanyĩasya Mbivilianĩ makethĩwa nomo matangĩĩie thayũ wakwa. Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩ na aũme angĩ elĩ tweekaa mũvango wa kũthi kũya nĩ kana nĩĩve ĩkoani ya ndola 50,000 ila nataĩtwe kyũthinĩ. Nĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ nĩnaumie mũvangonĩ ũsu! Ĩndĩ aũme asu nĩmaendie kũya. Mayũya, ũmwe woo nĩwakwatiwe nĩ asikalĩ, na ũla ũngĩ ooawa.
O ũndũ naendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, now'o noonie maũndũ maingĩ ala naaĩle kũeka. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩneemanyĩisye ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye ĩvukunĩ ya 1 Akolintho 6:10: "Ing'ei, o na ala me na ĩtomo, o na anywi, o na aumani, o na avutani, maikatiĩwa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai." Ĩla nasomie mũsoa ũsu na nalilikana ũndũ maũndũ ala neekĩte mathũkĩte, ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie nĩĩa. Vau nĩvo namanyie kana nĩnaaĩlĩte kũalyũka vyũ. (Alomi 12:2) Naĩ ngũlũ mũno, naĩ mũng'endu, na naĩ namanyĩie kũkengana.
O na vailyĩ ũu, nĩneemanyĩisye kuma Mbivilianĩ kana Yeova e tei na nũekeaa. (Isaia 1:18) Nĩnamũvoyie na kĩthito na namwĩsũva andetheesye nĩalyũle mwĩkalĩle wakwa wa tene. Na kwa ũtethyo wake, nĩnaendeeie kwĩka moalyũku. Twoosie ĩtambya ĩnene ĩla twaandĩkĩthisye mũtwaano nĩ na mũndũ mũka ũla twaĩ ndũũ.
Ũmũnthĩ nĩ thayũ nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia
Ĩvinda yĩu naĩ na myaka 24, na naĩ na kĩveti na syana itatũ. Yaĩ no nginya nĩmanthe wĩa mũseo wa kũthũkũma, o na kau ndyaĩ mũsomu mũno. Ĩngĩ nĩnamũvoyie Yeova na kĩthito, na nathi kũmantha wĩa. Nĩnatavasya ene wĩa kana nĩneeyumĩtye kũalyũka, na kũtethya wĩa nde na ũlũsani. O na mavinda angĩ nĩnamaeleasya kana nĩneemanyĩasya Mbivilia, na nĩnendaa kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũndũ mũseo. O na ũu wĩ o vo, aingĩ moo nĩmaleaa kũnandĩka. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kũelesya mũnene ũmwe ũndũ mwĩkalĩle wakwa wailyĩ, ambĩie atĩĩ: "Ndyĩsĩ nĩkĩ, ĩndĩ nĩona naĩle kũkũandĩka." Ũndũ ũsu wandĩkĩĩthisye nesa kana Yeova nĩwasũngĩie mboya yakwa. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, nyie na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtwavatisiwe na twatw'ĩka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Ũmũnthĩ nĩ thayũ nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia, na kwĩkala mwĩkalĩle wa Kĩklĩsto. Nĩ na kĩveti na syana syĩ na ũtanu. O na nĩ na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo nũndũ nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana Yeova nĩwandekeie.
Kwa myaka 14 mĩvĩtu, nĩnĩthĩĩtwe ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe nditetheesya andũ memanyĩsye Mbivilia, na ĩvinda ĩvĩtu yĩte yĩasa, o nakyo kĩveti kyakwa nĩkyambĩĩie ũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe. Na ũndũ ũla ũndanĩthasya nĩ kana kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 30 mĩvĩtu, nĩnĩtetheesye andũ 22 tũthũkũmaa ĩmwe makethĩwa me athũkũmi ma Yeova. Na wĩsĩ kĩ, yu nĩnĩendaa ndukanĩ nene sya viasala nĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo, ĩndĩ ti kũvena andũ o tondũ neekaa tene. Mavinda maingĩ ĩla nathi vo nĩndavasya andũ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wakwa. Nendaa kũmatavya ũvoo wa vata mũno, naw'o nĩ wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ, ĩla ĩtakethĩwa na ũvenani.—Savuli 37:10, 11.

LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1954
COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: CANADA
OUR HISTORY: GRANDFATHER AND THE LETTER WRITER
MY STORY:
I remember a certain occasion when I went to the city of Montreal. My father was with many people, and he sent his children to look at the shops. We were surprised with our mother and we enjoyed it very much.
And I continued with my story, telling about things like sending medicine to heal, writing letters, traveling, and dealing with debts. I was ten years old, associating with thieves and others who cheated people, sometimes being deceived myself with great loss. Many histories involved people, but I learned a lesson from them to avoid evil. And I understood this well.
I started working when I was 14 years old, learning many ways of deceiving people. For example, I used to sell watches, rings, and bracelets made of brass, and I would claim they were made of gold. A certain one was actually made of 14-carat gold. I wanted to make money by deceiving people in this way. Once I earned $10,000!
When I was 15 years old, I was expelled from school because I associated with bad company. I worked as a shop assistant in the city, cheating people, or stealing from drunkards and fools.
Because of my life of crime, many times I was arrested by police. This situation caused me a lot of trouble, so I decided to stop. But even then, I still wore big coats to deceive people, steal their belongings, or steal things from travelers. And I also stole from those who cheated people themselves with great loss. Those who had wealth often didn't bother to report small losses, and many times I got away with it. And many times I associated with gangs of thieves.
THE REASON I AM TELLING MY LIFE STORY:
My name is Noonie Mbivilia and I am 17 years old. This history began when I met two people who invited me to learn about Mbivilia and the teachings of Jehovah. Because I loved the teachings of Mbivilia, I spoke with this person and we agreed to associate with another man and I followed him.
Things happened that made this man tell me to learn about Mbivilia and the teachings! I was happy when I heard this message, inviting me to think about it and consider it. I realized that I had been misled, the Kingdom Hall of the Teachings of Jehovah. However, I was misled by some good people and some bad ones. This matter troubled me greatly with what I knew. But sometimes I saw people who were worse than me, and I pitied those who suffered. The love I have for Jehovah is what makes me strong. And now, since I have decided to learn about Mbivilia with you, I realize they want to change my life.
I will explain the things I learned about Mbivilia so that you can understand them well. One time, I was with some friends and we planned to go and rob someone, maybe even a bank worth 50,000 shillings, but I refused to participate. That was a good thing that I avoided that plan! My friends went on to rob.
Today, one was arrested, and the other escaped.
And because I continued to learn about Mbivilia, I now know many things that I didn't know before. For example, I learned from Mbivilia in 1 Corinthians 6:10: "Thieves, or those who take advantage, or drunkards, or abusers, or extortionists will not inherit God's kingdom." I read this scripture and understood that the things I used to do were wrong, and this helped me. That's why I try to avoid doing evil things. (Romans 12:2) Now I am careful, and I try to be honest, and I strive to live righteously.
And also, I learned from Mbivilia that Jehovah does not condone wickedness. (Isaiah 1:18) I felt sorry and confessed my sins and asked him to forgive me. And through his guidance, I continue to improve my life. We wrote a large letter together with another person.
This is a story about overcoming the mistakes of Mbivilia
.
I am 24 years old, married, and have three children. Before, I thought being a thief was okay, and I enjoyed stealing. But now I feel sorry for Jehovah and want to please him. I regret ever trying to escape, and I apologize for my past behavior. And many times I have been ashamed to share Mbivilia, and I don't like being associated with bad people. And today, I am happy to write. One day, when visiting someone's home, he said to me: "Please write something for me, so I can remember it." This made me realize how much Jehovah has helped me. The family and their children were invited to attend meetings at the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah.
MORE THINGS THAT HELPED ME:
This is a story about overcoming the mistakes of Mbivilia and living as a Christian. I am married and have five children. And I had a bad habit, but I realized that Jehovah doesn't approve of it.
For 14 years, I worked hard to help others learn about Mbivilia, and many families benefited, and their children also appreciated the work. And this encouraged me to continue for another 30 years, helping 22 people become dedicated servants of Jehovah. And because of this, I always try to be kind and helpful, and I don't want to offend anyone. Many people appreciate my efforts to help them. I want to continue sharing good news, and I know that staying neutral is important—Psalm 37:10, 11.
