ĨLA Antoine Skalecki waĩ kamwana ndekalaa ate na mbalasi, yĩthĩwe nĩ nene kana nĩ nini. E na mbalasi yake malikaa ngunganĩ ĩte kyeni kingĩ yĩnzĩtwe mita 500 (vuti 1,600) ungu wa nthĩ malatĩtye makaa ma mwaki. Manoaa ki nũndũ wa wĩa ũsu. Ĩthe wa Antoine athũkũmaa ngunganĩ ta ĩsu na ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩyatumbũkie na aũmĩa mũno weethĩa andũ make mai na ũndũ ũngĩ meka ate o kũmũtũma Antoine athi akathũkũmae wĩa o ũsu masaa kenda kwa mũthenya. O nake Antoine avĩtĩie o vanini ĩvinda ĩna ngunga ĩmwe yatumbũkie.
Myakanĩ ya 1920 na 1930 syana mbingĩ nĩsyasyaĩwe France nĩ asyai ma kuma Poland, na Antoine nĩ ũmwe wa syana isu. Nĩkĩ andũ ma Poland mathamĩĩe France? Ĩla nthĩ ya Poland yoosie wĩyathi ĩtina wa Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe, andũ nĩmasyaanie weethĩa nthĩ ĩsu nĩyamesya andũ aingĩ mũno nginya vaete thĩna mũnene. Nayo nthĩ ya France yaĩ na vata mũnene wa andũ matonya kwĩnza makaa ma mwaki nũndũ aũme mbee wa milioni ĩmwe ma nthĩ ĩsu makw'ĩĩe kaũnĩ ũsu. Nũndũ wa ũu, Mweinĩ wa 9, 1919, silikalĩ ya France na ya Poland nĩsyaandĩkanie kana andũ ma Poland no mathamĩĩe France. Kũvika mwaka wa 1931, ala mathamĩĩe France maĩ andũ 507,800, na aingĩ moo matũĩte isionĩ ila syenzawa makaa ma mwaki ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya France.
Andũ asu maumie Poland maĩ kĩthito mũno na maendie France na syĩthĩo syoo. Syĩthĩo isu syoo syaĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ, na mo ene maĩ andũ makwatĩĩe ndĩni mũno. Antoine, ũla yu wĩ na myaka 90, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũmau, Joseph, nĩwanengete Maandĩko Matheu ndaĩa nene mũno, na amanyĩĩtw'e ũu nĩ ĩthe." Wakyumwa wavika, andũ asu maumĩte Poland meekĩaa ngũa syoo ila nzeo vyũ na maithi kanisanĩ o tondũ mekaa me nthĩ yoo. Kĩndũ kĩu kyatumie andũ amwe ma France ala matakwatĩĩe maũndũ ma ndĩni mambĩĩa kũmavũthya.
Andũ aingĩ ma Poland moonanie ya mbee na Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ĩla maĩ vandũ vetawa Nord-Pas-de-Calais. Amanyĩw'a asu ma Mbivilia matavanĩtye kĩsio kĩu na kĩthito kuma mwaka wa 1904. Mwakanĩ wa 1915, ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower (Mũsyaĩĩsya) nĩyambĩĩe kũtumbĩthw'a kĩla mwei na kĩthyomo kya Polish, nayo ĩkaseti ya The Golden Age (ũmũnthĩ yĩtawa Amkeni!) yambĩĩe kũtumbĩthw'a kĩthyomonĩ o kĩu mwakanĩ wa 1925. Nũndũ makaseti asu maĩ na ũvoo umĩte Maandĩkonĩ, andũ aingĩ nĩmeewie mũyo nũndũ wamo. O na nĩmatanĩthiw'e nĩ ũvoo ũla waĩ ĩvukunĩ ya kĩthyomo kya Polish yĩla yeetawa The Harp of God, nũndũ o naw'o waumĩte Maandĩkonĩ.
Mwendw'e-inyia wa Antoine aendie ũmbanonĩ wake wa mbee mwaka wa 1924, na nĩwe watavisye aa-Antoine ĩũlũ wa Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia. Mwakanĩ o ũsu now'o Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia meekie ya mbee ũmbano mũnene wa kĩthyomo kya Polish me vandũ veetawa Bruay-en-Artois. O na vatathelete mwei, Joseph F. Rutherford nĩwaumie ovisinĩ mũnene ooka taoninĩ o ĩsu na eeka ũmbano mũnene, na andũ 2,000 nĩmookie. Ĩla Mwana-a-asa Rutherford woonie ũndũ andũ ma Poland maingĩvĩte ũmbanonĩ ũsu, ameie atĩĩ: "Yeova amũetie France mwĩmanyĩsye ũla w'o. Yu inyw'ĩ na syana syenyu no nginya mũtetheesye andũ ma France! Ve wĩa mwingĩ mũno wa kũtavany'a waĩle kũtethw'a, na Yeova nũkũmantha andũ matethye wĩa ũsu."
Na ũu now'o Yeova Ngai weekie! Aklĩsto asu ma Poland nĩmeeyumisye na ngoo ĩmwe wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a o tondũ meeyumĩtye wĩanĩ wa kwĩnza makaa ma mwaki! O na amwe moo masyokie Poland makatavye andũ ma kũu ũw'o wa vata ũla memanyĩĩtye, na maitavany'a vyũ nthĩ ya Poland o na kũtw'ĩka yĩ isio nene mũno. Amwe meekie ũu nĩ ta Teofil Piaskowski, Szczepan Kosiak, na Jan Zabuda.
Ĩndĩ atavany'a aingĩ ma Poland maendeeie kwĩkala France na matavany'a na kĩthito me vamwe na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma kũu France. Mwakanĩ wa 1926 ve ũmbano mũnene weekĩwe vandũ vetawa Sin-le-Noble, na vaĩ andũ 1,000 ngalĩko ya kĩthyomo kya Polish na angĩ 300 ngalĩko ya kĩthyomo kya French. Ĩvuku Kitabu cha Mwaka cha 1929 (Kĩsũngũ) yaisye atĩĩ: "Ũtalo wa mwaka w'onthe wĩonany'a kana ana-a-asa 332 ma Poland nĩmaneeyumisye mamũthũkũme Yeova na manoonany'a ũu ĩla manavatisiwe." Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe ũtambĩĩe, kwaĩ ikundi 84 nthĩ ya France na katĩ wa isu, 32 syaĩ sya kĩthyomo kya Polish.
Mwakanĩ wa 1947, silikalĩ ya Poland nĩyakũlilye andũ mayo masyoke Poland na Ngũsĩ mbingĩ nĩsyeetĩkĩlile kwĩka ũu. O na mamina kũthi, wĩa ũla matethetye vamwe na ana-a-asa ma France nĩwoonekie nesa nũndũ mwaka ũsu nĩkweethĩiwe na wongeleku wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ 10 katĩ wa 100. Ĩtina wa ũu, kuma mwaka wa 1948 nginya 1950, nĩkweethĩiwe ĩngĩ na wongeleku wa atavany'a 20 katĩ wa 100, 23 katĩ wa 100, o na 40 katĩ wa 100! Mwakanĩ wa 1948 nĩw'o ovisi wa ũvonge wa France wanyuvie ya mbee ana-a-asa atano matw'ĩke asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko nĩ kana mamanyĩsye atavany'a asu eũ. Katĩ wa asu atano, ana maĩ ma Poland, na Antoine Skalecki aĩ ũmwe woo.
Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ ũũ, Ngũsĩ mbingĩ syĩ France no syĩtanĩaw'a na aa-ũmae moo ma Poland, ala maĩ na kĩthito wĩanĩ wa kwĩnza makaa ma mwaki na wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. O na ĩngĩ, ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ mathamĩĩe France no maendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ũw'o. Ala mathamĩĩaa kũu France matw'a kũsyoka kwoo kana o matw'a kũtũa kũu, maendeeaa kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ me kĩthito, o ta ala atavany'a ma Poland maĩ kũu tene.

translation:
However, Antoine Skalecki was a young man who had a bicycle, which was given to him by his mother or someone else. And with his bicycle he would go to school every day, covering about 500 meters (about 1,600 feet) along the dusty road. He did this because of the need for education. The story of Antoine begins with him going to school daily and one incident happened where he helped some people with something, and because of this act, Antoine was praised by people for being kind and generous. It so happened that Antoine met another person on the road with a bicycle.
Between 1920 and 1930 many Poles emigrated to France from Poland, and Antoine was one of those people. Did the Polish people settle in France? Well, the land of Poland was small compared to the whole world, and people emigrated from there to find better opportunities elsewhere. However, the land of France had a large population of immigrants, reaching around one million people, and this land was very welcoming to them. On September 9, 1919, an agreement between France and Poland was signed stating that Polish people could settle in France. Until 1931, over 507,800 Polish people settled in France, and many more wanted to come but were prevented by the economic conditions of France.
These people who left Poland came with great difficulty and went to France with hope. This hope was often dashed, and many people found themselves in difficult situations. Antoine, who is now 90 years old, says: "Truly, Joseph, I remember Matthew's scriptures very well, and what happened then was terrible." It is understood that these people who left Poland faced many hardships but endured them with courage. This situation caused some French people to resent the newcomers.
Many people from Poland arrived in the spring and Bible Students in the Nord-Pas-de-Calais region helped them. These Bible Students began their work in this area in 1904. In 1915, the magazine The Watch Tower was published monthly in Polish, and in 1925, the magazine The Golden Age began to be published in that language as well. With these magazines and the good news of the Scriptures, many people learned the truth. And it was through this that the Polish edition of The Harp of God became known, and many people read the Scriptures through it.
Antoine's pioneer brother visited his home in 1924, and he encouraged the Antoine family to support the Bible Students. That year, the Bible Students held a large assembly in Polish for those in Bruay-en-Artois. Then, the following month, Joseph F. Rutherford gave a significant discourse, and 2,000 people attended. But Brother Rutherford saw that many Poles were coming to this gathering, so he said: "Jehovah has greatly blessed France. You and your children should help the French people! There is much work to be done to proclaim the message, and Jehovah will bless those who do so."
Yes, let us praise Jehovah God! Those Christian brothers in Poland rejoiced because they had an opportunity to preach, and they were eager to share the good news! Some Polish brothers traveled throughout the country to find those interested, and they made many contacts and helped build up the congregation. Among these were Teofil Piaskowski, Szczepan Kosiak, and Jan Zabuda.
Many Polish publishers went to France and worked alongside local pioneers and families there. In 1926, a large assembly was held in Sin-le-Noble, with about 1,000 attending from the Polish-speaking territory and some 300 from the French-speaking territory. The 1929 Year Book stated: "During the entire year, 332 Polish pioneers have been baptized and have entered further into the service." The Watchtower of November 1, 1929, reported that there were 84 companies in France, and of these, 32 spoke Polish.
In 1947, the Polish branch office encouraged those who could leave Poland to do so, and many responded favorably. And surprisingly, among those who associated with the families in France, the percentage of publishers increased to 10 out of 100. As a result, during the years 1948 to 1950, this increased to 20 percent, 23 percent, and even 40 percent! In 1948, the French Bethel overseer invited five experienced pioneers to help strengthen the congregations. Among these five were two Poles, including Antoine Skalecki.
Up until then, many in France had little contact with former Polish pioneers, but they showed interest in their experience in preaching and in their zeal for publishing. Moreover, many people in France continued to move to this country. But those moving to France often lacked the spiritual qualities needed to be good publishers, or they did not come from strong spiritual backgrounds, making it difficult for them to maintain their zeal for publishing.

text:
Ũtanamba kwĩka ũndũ o na wĩva, no kwĩthĩwa wĩkũlasya-ĩ, 'W'o ũndũ ũũ ũtonya kũndethya ata?' Vo ve ũthũku kwĩkũlya ĩkũlyo ta yĩu ĩũlũ wa mboya? Aiee, nũndũ nĩtwendaa kũmanya ethĩwa mboya nĩtonya kũtũtethya. O na mũndũũme mũĩkĩĩku Yovu akũlilye ũũ: 'Kethĩwa nĩneetanie, nĩwĩthĩwa anzũngĩie?'—Yovu 9:16.
Ilungunĩ mbĩtu, nĩtwonie maũndũ ala matũĩkĩĩthisye kana tũyaĩle kwona mboya ta o ũndũ wĩkawa nĩ ndĩni, kana ta ndawa ya kũtetheesya kĩlĩko kĩusye. Vate nzika Ngai wa w'o nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya. Kwoou, ethĩwa tũkavoyaa maũndũ ala maĩlĩte na kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte, akatwĩthukĩĩasya. O na nũtũthuthĩtye tũmũthengeee. (Yakovo 4:8) Kwoou, tũkatethekaa ata kwa kũvoyaa kĩla ĩvinda? Ekai twone moathimo amwe ala tũkwataa twavoya.
Mũuo wa kĩlĩko.
We nĩwĩmakĩaa mũno ĩla wakwatwa nĩ mathĩna? Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya 'tũvoyae tũtekũeka' mavindanĩ ta asu, na tũimũtavya Ngai 'mavata maitũ.' (1 Athesalonika 5:17; Avilivi 4:6) O na ĩngĩ Mbivilia nĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana ĩla twamũvoya Ngai, 'mũuo Wake, ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe, ũkasũvĩaa ngoo sitũ na mosũanĩo maitũ.' (Avilivi 4:7) Kwoou, no tũkwate mũuo wa kĩlĩko wĩana ũndũ mũna twamwonoesya Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ mavata maitũ onthe. Na vate nzika ũu nĩw'o ũtwĩkĩaa vinya twĩke. Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 55:22 yaĩtye: "Mwaũĩe Yeova mũio waku, nake akakũtw'ĩĩka."
"Mwaũĩe Yeova mũio waku, nake akakũtw'ĩĩka." —Savuli 55:22
Andũ aingĩ mũno ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmakwatĩte mũuo ta ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o Hee Ran, kuma South Korea, aĩtye: "O na kau nĩ na mathĩna maingĩ, ĩla navoya nĩw'aa nathũmũw'a mũio ũla nĩĩ naw'o na ndikwata vinya wa kũmĩĩsya." Nake Cecilia, kuma Philippines, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩthĩnĩkĩaa eĩtu makwa mũno na inyia wakwa ũla ũwaĩte ũkethĩa ndamanya ninyie ũũ. Ĩndĩ mboya nĩndetheesye ndikemakĩe mũno. Nĩnĩsĩ kana Yeova akandetheeasya kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna makwa."
Ũkiakisyo na ũkũmbaũ ĩla twakwatwa nĩ matatwa.
No wĩthĩwe na ũndũ ũũkũthĩny'a kĩlĩko, ta mũisyo kana ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma wasya thayũ waku? Kũvoya "Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe" no kũũtetheesye wĩthĩwe na mũuo wa kĩlĩko. Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte kana Ngai 'nũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe.' (2 Akolintho 1:3, 4) Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe ĩla Yesũ wathĩnĩkĩte mũno kĩlĩkonĩ 'atulilye ndu na avoya.' Kweethĩiwe ata ĩtina wa ũu? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Aumĩlĩlwa nĩ mũlaĩka kuma ĩtunĩ, amwĩkĩa vinya." (Luka 22:41, 43) Nake mũndũũme ũngĩ mũĩkĩĩku weetawa Neemia nĩwavĩngawa nĩ andũ athũku ĩla watethasya wĩa wa Ngai. Avoyie atĩĩ: "Ĩndĩ yu, ame Ngai, mbĩkĩa moko makwa vinya." Maũndũ ala meekĩkie ĩtina wa vau meonany'a kana Ngai nĩwamũtetheeisye aeka kũkĩa na aendeea nesa wĩanĩ wake. (Neemia 6:9-16) Reginald, kuma Ghana, nũeleetye ũndũ wĩw'aa avoya, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩla navoya, na mũno mũno ĩvinda yĩla nakwatwa nĩ mathĩna maito, nĩnĩw'aa neanĩwa nũndũ wa kũmũelesya Ngai mathĩna makwa nũndũ e na ũtonyi wa kũndetheesya na nũndĩkĩĩthasya kana vai vata wa kwĩmakĩa." Kwa w'o, Ngai e na ũtonyi wa kũtũkiakisya ĩla twavoya.
Ũĩ kuma kwa Ngai.
Motwi amwe twĩkaa no methĩwe na ũsyao mũseo kana mũthũku kwitũ na kwa andũ maitũ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mũno. Tũtonya kwĩka motwi maseo ata? Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa ũmwe wenyu nũtielye ũĩ, [mũno mũno ĩla twakwatwa nĩ matatwa] namũvoye Ngai, ũla ũnengae andũ onthe na ũlau na ndeũkan'ya; nake akanengwa." (Yakovo 1:5) Ĩla twavoya ũĩ, Ngai no atũmĩe veva mũtheu ũtũtongoesye twĩkae ũtwi ũla waĩle. Vate nzika, no tũvoye veva mũtheu nũndũ Yesũ atũĩkĩĩthĩtye atĩĩ: 'Ĩthe wenyu ũla wa ĩtunĩ akamanenga veva mũtheu ala mamwĩtasya.'—Luka 11:13.
O na Yesũ nĩwoonie vata wa kũmũvoya Ĩthe wake ũtethyo ĩla weekaa motwi ma vata. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana ĩla Yesũ wendaa kũnyuva aũme 12 matw'ĩke atũmwa make, 'ekalile ũtukũ w'onthe akĩvoya Ngai.'—Luka 6:12.
O ta Yesũ, andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ nĩmekĩawa vinya ĩla moona ũndũ Ngai ũmatethasya mamũvoya ũtethyo wa kwĩka motwi maseo. Regina, kuma Philippines, nũwetete mathĩna ala mamũkwatĩte, ta kwasya wĩa, kũea syana e weka na kwĩanĩsya mavata make ĩtina wa mũũme kũkw'a. Nĩ kyaũ kĩmũtetheesye kwĩka motwi maseo? Aĩtye atĩĩ, "Nĩnĩmũvoyaa Yeova andetheesye." Kwabena, kuma Ghana, nũwetete kĩla kyatumie avoya Ngai ũtethyo. Aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩnaaisye wĩa wa mwako ũla wanengae mbesa mbingĩ." Aielesya ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla wamanthaa wĩa aĩtye atĩĩ, "Nĩnamũvoyaa Yeova kĩla ĩvinda nĩ kana andongoesye kwĩka ũtwi mũseo." Aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩtũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ Yeova nĩwandetheeisye nanyuva wĩa ũndetheeasya kwĩanĩsya mavata makwa na ũtanziĩĩaa kwĩka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva." O naku wamũvoya Ngai ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala matonya kũtuma ngwatanĩo yaku nake yanangĩka akaũtetheesya.
Twaneenea moathimo manini ala mboya ĩtũeteae. (Nĩ kana ũkwate ngelekany'o mbingangĩ, sisya ĩsandũkũ "Moathimo Ala Tũkwataa Ĩla Twavoya.") Ĩndĩ nĩ kana ũkwate moathimo asu, waĩle kwamba kũmũmanya Ngai na kwenda kwake. Wenda kwĩka ũu, twĩũkũlya ũneene na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩ kana iũtetheesye kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. * Yĩu nĩyo yĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yĩ ĩtambya yaku ya mbee ya kũmũthengeea "ũla wĩw'aa mboya."—Savuli 65:2.

translation:
You will search diligently and thoroughly, and if you seek him, he will let himself be found—'Where is this one who is so skilled at destroying?' Yes, today we ask ourselves whether a young person can truly know God well enough to teach us. And the afflicted man Job asked him this: 'How can a mortal be righteous before God?—Job 9:16.'
Often, we wonder about things that have confused us or that seem impossible, or whether something is within our power, or whether we are capable of understanding fully. But remember, the God of this one allows himself to be sought. Come now, let us examine those things that are important and those that are less important, and allow himself to be found. And let us humble ourselves. (James 4:8) Come now, can we really understand everything by searching every detail? Let us see some examples of what we hold onto when we search.
The end of the matter.
Do you become discouraged when you are overcome by difficulties? The Bible encourages us to 'pray constantly' without ceasing, and to present our requests to God 'with thanksgiving.' (1 Thessalonians 5:17; Philippians 4:6) And also, the Bible teaches us that if we search for God, 'his spirit, which knows everything, will enlighten our minds and show us our faults.' (Philippians 4:7) Come now, let us embrace the end of the matter with a willingness to learn from everything we experience, so that our Father in heaven may accept all our efforts. But remember, this is how he encourages us. Psalm 55:22 says: "Cast your burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain you."
"Cast your burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain you." —Psalm 55:22
Many people throughout history have embraced this principle. For example, Hee Ran, from South Korea, says: "Although I had many problems, I knew that I could pour out my heart to him and find comfort." And Cecilia, from the Philippines, relates: "I used to worry about many things and was afraid of what others would think of me. Finally, I began to confide in someone. I realized that Jehovah helped me to cope with those worries."
Perseverance and patience when we face trials.
But how can we remain steadfast when confronted with a difficult situation, especially when we don't see an immediate solution? Pouring out your heart to "the God of all comfort" can help you feel comforted. The Bible assures us that God 'comforts us in all our tribulation.' (2 Corinthians 1:3, 4) Consider, for instance, the account of Jesus Christ who, while facing great distress, 'prayed more earnestly.' Was his prayer answered? The Bible states: "An angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him." (Luke 22:41, 43) Also, a man named Nehemiah was disturbed by reports from some who were trying to intimidate him and hinder his work for God. He said: "But I prayed to the God of heaven, and I said, 'Please, let these men be dismayed.'" What happened? The Bible tells us that "God frustrated their scheme." (Nehemiah 6:9-16) Reginald, from Ghana, shared an experience he had, saying: "Even though I was worried, during the time I faced those problems, I felt encouraged because I could talk to God about them and I did not feel alone or helpless." So, God can give us strength when we are worried.
Trust in God.
Often we may find ourselves in situations that seem overwhelming, both personally and affecting others around us. Can we really trust that things will improve? The Bible answers: "If any of you lacks wisdom, let him request it from God, who gives generously to everyone without reproach; and it will be given him." (James 1:5) So, if we are worried, God can provide us with guidance to help us cope. Furthermore, he encourages us to ask him, as Jesus taught us to pray: 'Give us today the bread for this day.'—Luke 11:13.
And Jesus showed the importance of praying regularly, setting aside time to commune with his Father. The Bible relates that Jesus went off to the mountains to spend the whole night in prayer.—Luke 6:12.
Like Jesus, many people have found strength in knowing that God hears their prayers and responds when they seek his guidance. Regina, from the Philippines, faced numerous challenges, including financial difficulties, raising children alone, and dealing with family problems. What helped her to trust in God? She says, "I felt Jehovah listening to me." Kwabena, from Ghana, struggled with an addiction. He explains: "I realized I needed God's help to overcome my bad habits." Ayesha, a young woman facing difficult circumstances, shared: "I feel that Jehovah hears my prayers every day." She adds: "I am able to remain calm because Jehovah has comforted me through his Word and has helped me to deal with my problems." And when you trust God, you experience peace of mind, which can strengthen your resolve and give you courage.
We will now examine some examples of how prayer has helped others. (If you would like more information, see the brochure "Answers to Bible Questions.") Many have also found comfort in studying the Bible and getting to know God better. In this way, we draw closer to God, and Jehovah can help us to understand the Bible. * This is why the psalmist could confidently say about God: "You are the God who answers prayer."—Psalm 65:2.

MŨNDŨŨME atonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana mũka wake ethĩwe e mwĩanĩe? Andũ aingĩ meanaa mesĩ kana wĩa ũla mũnene wa mũndũũme nĩ kũmanthĩa mũsyĩ wake. Ĩndĩ iveti imwe ila syĩthĩawa na syĩndũ mbingĩ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ syĩw'aa itendetwe, na syĩ na wia. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Rosa wa nthĩ ya Spain aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa mũũme, "Eethĩawa e mũndũ mũseo ĩla wĩ andũnĩ, ĩndĩ ĩla twĩ mũsyĩ ndeethĩawa na tei." Nake mũndũ mũka ũngĩ wĩtawa Joy wa nthĩ ya Nigeria easya ũũ ĩũlũ wa mũũme, "Ĩla tũtaeleanawa ambĩaa, 'Nĩwaĩle kwĩka kyonthe kĩla ngwenda nũndũ ninyie mũemeu.'"
Mũndũũme ũtwaanĩte atonya ata kwĩanĩsya nesa kĩanda kyake? Mũndũũme aĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana mũsyĩ wake wĩthĩwe "ũthũmũo" kwondũ wa mũka wake?
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAĨTYE ĨŨLŨ WA ŨKŨMŨ WA MŨNDŨŨME
O na kau mũndũũme ũtwaanĩte na mũndũ mũka mũtwae nĩmeanene methonĩ ma Ngai, Mbivilia yaasya kana kĩla ũmwe ethĩawa na kĩanda kĩ kĩvathũkany'o nthĩnĩ wa mũsyĩ. Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 7:2 yaĩtye kana mũndũ mũka mũtwae nĩwovetwe nĩ 'mwĩao wa mũũme.' O tondũ kũndũ kwingĩ kwĩthĩawa na mũndũ wa kũũngamĩa maũndũ, Ngai nũnyuvĩte mũndũũme ethĩwe mũtwe wa mũka wake. (1 Akolintho 11:3) Aũme ala matwaanĩte nĩmo maĩle kũtongoesya mĩsyĩ yoo.
Inyw'ĩ aũme ala mũtwaanĩte, mwaĩle kũtũmĩa ũkũmũ ũla mũnengetwe nĩ Ngai ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Endai iveti syenyu, o ũndũ Klĩsto wendie ĩkanisa." (Aeveso 5:25) O na kau Yesũ Klĩsto ndaatwaana, vate nzika ngelekany'o yake no ĩmũtetheesye mũkethĩwa aũme aseo. Ekai twone ũndũ mũtonya kwĩka ũu.
YESŨ NĨWATIĨIE AŨME NGELEKANY'O NZEO
Yesũ nĩwathĩnĩkĩaa andũ na kũmathũmũsya mĩio yoo. Yesũ eeie onthe ala manyamaaw'a na makuĩte mĩio mĩito atĩĩ: "Ũkai kwakwa, . . . nakwa ngamũthũmũsya." (Mathayo 11:28, 29) Mavinda maingĩ nĩwathĩnĩkĩaa ala mathĩnaa na aimatetheesya methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. Kyu nĩkyo kĩtumi andũ aingĩ mamwendete nũndũ nĩmeethĩawa mesĩ ndalea kũmatetheesya!
Ũndũ aũme matonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Tata ũndũ ũtonya ũtetheesye kĩveti kyaku mawĩanĩ ma mũsyĩ. Iveti imwe syĩw'aa ta Rosa ũla waisye ũũ e na kĩmako kingĩ: "Mũemewa ambosaa ta nĩ mũthũkũmi wake." Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Kweku ũla wĩthĩĩtwe na mũtwaano mũseo aĩtye ũũ: "Mavinda maingĩ nĩnĩkũlasya kĩveti kyakwa ũndũ ndonya kũkĩtetheesya. Na nũndũ nĩnĩkyendete nĩnosaa ĩtambya ya kũkĩtetheesya mawĩanĩ ma mũsyĩ."
Yesũ nĩweew'ĩaa andũ tei na kũmatethya. Ve mũndũ mũka ũmwe waĩ ngya na wathĩnĩtw'e nĩ ũwau mũthũku kwa myaka 12. Ĩla weewie ĩũlũ wa syama ila Yesũ weekaa sya kũvosya aisye, "Nakiita o na ethĩwa no ngũa syake, nĩngũvoa." Vate nzika ũu nĩw'o kweethĩiwe. Amũthengeeie Yesũ na akiita mũthya wa ngũa yake na avoa. O na kau andũ amwe ala maĩ vo moonie mũndũ mũka ũsu e na mĩng'athĩlĩlyo, Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana eekie ũu nũndũ ndaĩ na ũndũ ũngĩ wĩka. * Yesũ e na tei mwingĩ eeie mũndũ mũka ũsu: 'Mwĩĩtu, . . . ĩthĩwa wĩ mũima, ũte na ũthĩny'o waku.' Yesũ ndaakandĩa mũndũ mũka ũsu kana akeka ũndũ ũtuma ew'a nthoni ĩndĩ nĩwaeleiwe ũndũ weew'aa. Kwa kwĩka ũu, Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana aĩ mũndũũme wĩ tei.
Ũndũ aũme matonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Ĩla woona kĩveti kyaku kĩte kwĩw'a nesa, waĩle kwonany'a kana nũũkĩelewa na ũyĩthĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo. Kwoou kĩla ĩvinda tata ũelewe kĩveti kyaku. Kwa ngelekany'o mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Ricardo aĩtye ũũ: "Ĩla noona kĩveti kyakwa kĩithata mĩtũkĩ nĩndataa ũndũ ndonya ndikaneene kana kwĩka maũndũ ala matonya kũtuma kĩthata mũnango."
Yesũ nĩwaeaa ngewa na amanyĩw'a make. Yesũ nĩwaeleasya amanyĩw'a make maũndũ maingĩ na aimatavya ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Ameie atĩĩ: "Maũndũ onthe ala neewie kwa Asa nĩmo nĩmũmanyĩthĩtye." (Yoana 15:15) Nĩ w'o ki kana mavinda amwe Yesũ nĩwendaa kwĩthĩwa e weka aisũanĩa na kũvoya. Ĩndĩ mavinda kwa mavinda nĩwamaeleasya amanyĩw'a make maũndũ ala me ngoonĩ. Ũtukũ wa mũthya Yesũ atanamba kũsilĩlwa ta kĩng'ei na kũawa, amatavisye sanzũ kana 'ngoo yake yaĩ na kĩũũyũ mũno.' (Mathayo 26:38) O na yĩla amanyĩw'a make mavĩtya, Yesũ ndaekaa kũmaneeny'a.
Ũndũ aũme matonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Ea ngewa na kĩveti kyaku. Kĩtavye ũndũ ũkwĩw'a na kĩla wĩsilĩtye kuma ngoonĩ. Iveti nitonya kwĩw'a ite mbĩanĩe ĩla syoona aũme masyo mendete kũneena ĩla me andũnĩ ala angĩ, ĩndĩ me mĩsyĩ kwoo mayĩthĩwa mavindĩtye. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Ana ew'aa mũyo ĩla mũũme wake wamũtavya ũndũ ũkwĩw'a kuma ngoonĩ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩw'aa ambendete mũno, na e mũnyanyawa."
Ndũkavindĩsye kĩveti kyaku ũyenda kĩmanye kana nĩkĩũvĩtĩisye. Mũndũ mũka ũmwe easya ũũ: "Ĩla namũthatya mũũme wakwa nũtonya kũmbindĩsya o na kwa mĩthenya mingĩ. Atumaa nĩtũla mũtĩ na ndyĩw'a atambendete." Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, Edwin nũtataa kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩla nathata nditũngĩthasya kĩveti kyakwa ĩndĩ nĩmanthaa ĩvinda yĩla yaĩle ya kũneenea ũndũ ũsu."
Ũla mũndũ mũka ũwetiwe mwambĩlĩlyonĩ wĩtawa Joy nĩwonete ũndũ mũũme wake ũalyũkĩte kuma ambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Joy easya ũũ: "Mũũme wakwa nũendeee nesa na nũmbendete o ũndũ Yesũ wendete andũ." Andũ milioni mbingĩ matwaanĩte nĩmatethekete nĩ motao asu ma Mbivilia. We no wende kũtetheka o tamo? No ũneene na ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova aũtetheesye kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia vate ndĩvi.
^ kĩl. 10 Kwosana na Mĩao ya Mose mũndũ mũka ũsu aĩ mũvuku, na kwoou mũndũ o na wĩ va ũla wamũkiita eethĩawa e mũvuku.

translation:
Does a husband cheat even if his wife is pregnant? Many people believe that the biggest sin a husband can commit is betraying his wife. One study showed that among many factors influencing infidelity, jealousy was a major one. For example, a woman named Rosa from Spain told a story about her husband, saying, "He cheated on me with someone I knew, someone we both trusted." Another woman named Joy from Nigeria shared a story about her husband, saying, "He would always tell me, 'You're beautiful no matter what you wear, you're perfect.'"
Can a husband ever justify cheating on his wife? Can a husband cheat even if his wife has been labeled "infertile" because of her husband?
THE REASONS FOR HUSBAND INFIDELITY
Some husbands who cheat claim they have been greatly tempted by God. The Bible says that each person is tempted by their own desires. Proverbs 7:2 states that a married man is bound by "the covenant of his marriage." But since many people cheat with someone who understands them, God allows husbands to be led astray by their wives. (1 Corinthians 11:3) These men often think they are justified in their actions.
If these men are so easily deceived, should we blame God for this? The Bible says: "Love your wives, just as Christ loved the church." (Ephesians 5:25) And just as Jesus Christ was faithful, he set an example for husbands to love their wives. Let us examine this issue further.
JESUS SETS THE EXAMPLE FOR HUSBANDS
Jesus associated with people and felt compassion for them. Jesus repeatedly invited everyone, especially those who were burdened and exhausted, saying: "Come to me, . . . and I will give you refreshment." (Matthew 11:28, 29) Many people were drawn to him because he showed genuine concern and empathy. That is why many people today find comfort in knowing that they are understood and appreciated!
Husbands can learn from Jesus' example. Consider how important it is to understand your wife's feelings. One sister named Rosa shared this experience: "My husband used to say that he didn't understand me." Similarly, a brother named Kwaku, who had struggled with temptation, said: "Many times I found myself thinking about what my wife wanted, so that I could please her. And eventually I realized that pleasing her made me happy too."
Jesus was willing to help people and show compassion. Once, a man who had been paralyzed for 12 years came to see him. But when Jesus saw his faith, he told him, "Your sins are forgiven," which surprised the man. Then Jesus healed him, and the man walked away restored. Seeing this, some people began to glorify God, while others wondered whether Jesus had committed blasphemy. * Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man: "Friend, your sins are forgiven." Jesus demonstrated to that man that he had the authority to forgive sins. To prove this, Jesus then said to the man: "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—he turned to the paralytic and said, "Get up, pick up your cot, and go home."
The man got up and went home.
Some found it difficult to accept Jesus' miracles. But truly, if you examine your own heart, you will realize that you need forgiveness and mercy. Every day, take time to understand your own heart. For example, one man named Ricardo said: "I realized that my heart was very hard and I needed to change my attitude and way of life."
Jesus always did what pleased his Father. Jesus revealed many things to his disciples and taught them how to do what pleased him. He once said: "All the things I have learned from my Father I tell you." (John 15:15) It is therefore fitting that Jesus should be willing to submit to his Father's will. Time and again, he showed his disciples many things about his Father. On the night before his execution, he became deeply distressed and prayed, expressing his feelings of great anguish. (Matthew 26:38) Yet despite his intense emotional pain, Jesus remained obedient.
The man got up and went home. Consider this and your own heart. It teaches us how to live and helps us to remain faithful. Your heart can be changed, but sometimes people find it difficult to believe, especially those who are stubborn and proud, and who refuse to listen to advice. In connection with this, a woman named Anna experienced something similar when her husband taught her how to live faithfully. She said: "I felt so much peace, and it comforted me."
Examine your own heart and see if it needs changing. One man said: "I used to hate my wife, but now I want to please her, and after many years, I began to love her and appreciate her." In connection with this, Edwin decided to accept Jesus' miracles. He said: "I realized that I needed to change my heart because I wanted to experience the joy of being forgiven."
But a woman named Joy was disappointed when she learned that her mother had stopped studying the Bible and attending meetings at the Kingdom Hall. Joy said: "My mother kept saying that Jesus helped others, but not her." Millions of people have found comfort in God's Word. Will you also seek comfort there? Why not talk to one of Jehovah's Witnesses and ask him to help you study the Bible?
^ par. 10 Like Moses, this man repented, and anyone who wants can repent and turn back to God.

text:
MŨISYO ŨLA WAĨ VO: Vai kĩndũ kyaĩ kĩsa kũmina Mbivilia o na kau mavuku ala matũmĩawa maĩ matonya kwoa na ve andũ mendaa kũmĩmina. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, andũ ala mamyumĩĩasya na aalyũli nĩmendaa kũvĩndũa ũvoo ũla waĩ Mbivilianĩ. Mavinda amwe, meethĩawa mayenda kũvĩndũa Mbivilia yĩtĩkĩlane na momanyĩsyo moo ma ndĩni, vandũ va mavĩndũe momanyĩsyo moo metĩkĩlane na Mbivilia. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii iatĩĩe:
Vandũ va kũthaithĩa: Katĩ katĩ wa myaka ya 400-200 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, aandĩki ma Samaritan Pentateuch nĩmongeleeile ndeto ii ĩandĩkonĩ ya Kuma 20:17 "kĩĩmanĩ kya Ngelisimu makaaka kĩthembeo vo." Kwa kwĩka ũu, Asamalia mendaa Maandĩko makwate mbau mũvango woo wa kwaka ĩkalũ kĩĩmanĩ kya Ngelisimu.
Ũmanyĩsyo wa ũtatũ mũtheu: Myaka ta 300 Mbivilia yamina kũandĩkwa, mũandĩki ũmwe ũĩkĩĩaa ũmanyĩsyo wa ũtatũ ongeleeile ndeto ii ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Yoana 5:7 "ĩtunĩ, Asa, Ndeto, na Veva Mũtheu: na asu me atatũ no ũmwe." Ndeto isu iyaĩ nthĩnĩ wa maandĩko ma mbee ala maandĩkiwe nĩ aandĩki ma Mbivilia. Mũsomi ũmwe wa Mbivilia wĩtawa Bruce Metzger aisye atĩĩ: "Kuma myakanĩ ya 500 na kũendeea ndeto isu nĩsyaendeeie kwongeleelwa mũno mavukunĩ ma tene ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia ma Old Latin na [Latin] Vulgate."
Ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai: Aalyũli aingĩ ma Mbivilia nĩmaamũie kumya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai kuma Maandĩkonĩ, na meekaa ũu maatĩĩe kĩthĩo kya Ayuti kyaumanĩte na maũndũ ma Satani. Matũmĩie masyĩtwa ma ũnene ta "Ngai" kana "Mwĩaĩi." O na kau Mbivilianĩ masyĩtwa asu nĩmatũmĩĩtwe kũelesya ĩũlũ wa Mũmbi, no matũmĩĩtwe Maandĩkonĩ amwe kwonany'a andũ, syĩndũ ila ĩtũmĩawa kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa mĩvw'anano, o na ĩsyĩtwa ngai nĩyĩtũmĩĩtwe kũelesya Ndevili.—Yoana 10:34, 35; 1 Akolintho 8:5, 6; 2 Akolintho 4:4. *
KĨLA KYATUMIE MBIVILIA ĨTAMINWA: O na kau andũ amwe ala maumĩĩasya Mbivilia mayaĩ aĩkĩĩku, ve angĩ aingĩ maĩ na ũmanyi mwingĩ na nĩmaĩkĩĩthasya kana mamyumĩĩsya ũndũ yailyĩ. Andũ meetawa Masoretes nĩmaumĩĩisye Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania katĩ katĩ wa myaka ya 500 na 1000, Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa na mavuku asu moo meetanĩw'a na ĩsyĩtwa yoo. Mayumĩĩsya, matalaa kĩla ndeto nĩ kana maĩkĩĩthye kana vai ndeto ĩnatiwa ĩla mekumĩĩasya. Ĩla meethĩa vandũ vekĩtwe mavĩtyo, nĩmaandĩkaa ndeenĩ sya mavuku asu. Andũ asu meetawa Masoretes mayaaĩtĩkĩla kũvĩndũa kĩla kyaandĩkĩtwe Maandĩkonĩ. Mũsomi ũmwe wĩtawa Moshe Goshen-Gottstein aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Naĩ ĩla nene mũndũ waĩ atonya kwĩka nĩ kũvĩndũa kĩla kyaandĩkĩtwe o esĩ."
Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana, mavuku maingĩ ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia nĩmatetheeasya asomi makamanya kũla kweekĩtwe makosa. Kwa ngelekany'o, atongoi aingĩ ma ndĩni mamanyĩĩtye andũ kwa myaka mingĩ kana Mbivilia ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe kwa kĩthyomo kya Kĩlatinĩ nĩyo ya w'o. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi nthĩnĩ wa ĩandĩko ya 1 Yoana 5:7, mongeleeile ila ndeto ite sya w'o iwetiwe kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ. O na ndeto isu ĩte sya w'o nĩsyeekĩiwe Mbivilianĩ ĩla ĩtũmĩawa nĩ andũ aingĩ yĩtawa King James Version! Ĩndĩ veethĩiwe ata ĩla mavuku ala angĩ matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia moonekie? Mũndũũme wĩtawa Bruce Metzger aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ndeto isu syongelilwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya [1 Yoana 5:7] iyaĩ vo mavukunĩ ma tene ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia (Syriac, Coptic, Armenian, Ethiopic, Arabic, Slavonic) ate o nthĩnĩ wa yĩla ya Kĩlatinĩ." Na nũndũ wa ũu, Mbivilia ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya King James Version na Mbivilia ingĩ nĩsyaumisye ndeto isu.
Mavuku ma tene ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia nĩmaĩkĩĩthĩtye kana ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩw'o waandĩkiwe nĩ aandĩki ma Mbivilia? Ĩla Mavuku ma Ũkanga wa Mũnyũ makwatĩkanie mwaka wa 1947, asomi nĩmakwatie mavuku matonya kũsianĩsya Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania ala maumĩĩw'e nĩ Masoretes na maandĩko ala maĩ mavukunĩ ma kũkũnzwa ala maĩ maandĩkiwe myaka mbee wa ngili mĩvĩtu. Mũndũ ũmwe waĩ nthĩnĩ wa kamitii ĩla yeekaa ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa Mavuku ma Ũkanga wa Mũnyũ aisye kana ĩvuku yĩmwe ya kũkũnzwa "yaĩkĩĩthisye nesa vyũ kana Ayuti ala maumĩĩasya Maandĩko ma Mbivilia kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa ngili mĩvĩtu, maĩ aĩkĩĩku na maĩkĩĩthasya kana nĩmaumĩĩsya nesa ũndũ vaĩle."
Nyũmba ya kwia mavuku ĩla yĩtawa Chester Beatty Library ĩla yĩ Dublin, Ireland, yĩthĩawa na vakuvĩ mavuku onthe ma Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto ala maumĩĩw'e makangaanĩ, o vamwe na mavuku ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia ma kuma myakanĩ ya 100-200 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, ĩsu nĩ myaka vakuvĩ 100 kuma Mbivilia yaminwa kũandĩkwa. Ĩvuku yĩtawa The Anchor Bible Dictionary yaĩtye atĩĩ: "O na kau mavuku ma makangaa methĩawa na ũvoo mwingĩ ũtonya kũĩkĩĩthya ndeto ila syatũmĩĩtwe, nĩmonanasya nesa kana ala maumĩĩisye Maandĩko, meekie ũu kwa ũĩkĩĩku vyũ."
"No twasye tũte na nzika kana vai ĩvuku yĩngĩ ya tene yaalyũlwa na kumĩĩw'a nesa ta Maandĩko asu"
ŨNDŨ ŨSU ŨTETHETYE ATA?: Vandũ va kwanangĩĩa Maandĩko, mavuku ma tene ala matũmĩawa kũalyũla Mbivilia mekĩte kũmĩseũvĩĩsya. Mũndũũme wĩtawa Sir Frederic Kenyon ayĩandĩka ĩũlũ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto aisye atĩĩ: "Vai ĩvuku yĩngĩ ya tene yĩilyĩ ta Mbivilia, nũndũ Mbivilia yĩ mavuku maingĩ ma tene ma kũĩkĩĩthya kana kĩla kĩandĩkĩtwe vo nĩ kya w'o. O na mũsomi ũte kyende ndesa kwasya kana ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩwavĩndũiwe." Mũsomi ũngĩ wĩtawa William Henry Green awetie ũũ ĩũlũ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania: "No twasye tũte na nzika kana vai ĩvuku yĩngĩ ya tene yaalyũlwa na kumĩĩw'a nesa ta Maandĩko asu."
^ kal. 6 Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ sisya ũvoo wa kwongeleela ũla wĩ ĩthangũnĩ ya 195-197 ĩvukunĩ Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata?, o na no ũyĩkwate Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam.

translation:
HISTORY TELLS US: There is something important to remember about the Bible and how its various parts were compiled and the people who worked hard to compile it. Because of this and its importance, people have always been interested in understanding the history of the Biblical texts. Some people, having studied diligently to understand the Bible closely and thoroughly, others study thoroughly to understand the texts of the Bible. To illustrate this point further:
People who research: Between 400-200 years Before Christ, the authors of the Samaritan Pentateuch quoted verse 20:17 of Exodus which states "you shall not covet your neighbor's wife." In order to do so, Samaritans needed scriptures that contained that specific commandment regarding adultery.
The Trinity Doctrine: About 300 years later the Bible was written, one author included the doctrine of the trinity quoting verse 1 John 5:7 "For there are three that bear witness in heaven—the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit—and these three are one." This verse is absent from most ancient manuscripts and is believed to be added by scribes of the Bible. One biblical scholar named Bruce Metzger stated: "During the fifth century and thereafter this verse began to creep into more and more copies in the Old Latin and [Latin] Vulgate versions."
The Name of God: Many Biblical writers avoided mentioning the name of God in the Scriptures, and instead used titles like 'God' or 'Lord' to refer to Satan. They used names such as "God" or "Creator". But some Biblical names are used to describe the character of the Creator, and they are used in the Scriptures sometimes to distinguish them from humans, however these names are also used in connection with false worship, and the name God is used to refer to the Devil.—John 10:34, 35; 1 Corinthians 8:5, 6; 2 Corinthians 4:4. *
WHY THE BIBLE IS INSPIRED: Some people believe the Bible is inspired because it has helped them, while others have much knowledge and think it is accurate or true. The people called Masoretes preserved the Hebrew Scriptures between the years 500 and 1000 C.E., carefully copying them and using certain methods. However, when checking each verse, they would either correct it or omit a verse that seemed wrong. But despite their efforts, they made mistakes, and these mistakes were passed on. These people called Masoretes took great care to accurately copy everything that was written in the Scriptures. One scholar named Moshe Goshen-Gottstein wrote: "It is doubtful whether anyone can claim to have been completely accurate."
This is why many manuscripts used to translate the Bible are inaccurate and cause scholars to make errors. For example, many ancient copies of the Bible that people had for centuries, or the Bible that was translated into Latin, were incorrect. And this is why the ending of 1 John 5:7, which we see today, was added later. Also, those verses that were added were included in the Bible that is used by many people called the King James Version! Have you ever wondered what happened to the manuscripts that were originally used to translate the Bible? A man named Bruce Metzger wrote: "These verses [1 John 5:7] are absent from all the oldest manuscripts of the Bible (Syriac, Coptic, Armenian, Ethiopic, Arabic, Slavonic), as well as from the Latin version." Because of this, the Bible that was revised by the King James Version and other Bibles contain those verses.
Many manuscripts used to translate the Bible are incomplete, so how can we be sure that the Bible we have was written by the authors of the Bible? The Dead Sea Scrolls were discovered in 1947, and scholars found manuscripts that were almost identical to the Hebrew Scriptures that were preserved by the Masoretes and manuscripts from earlier periods that were written hundreds of years before Christ. One scholar who was on the committee that studied the Dead Sea Scrolls said that one of the fragments "proved beyond a doubt that the texts of the biblical books had been accurately preserved over a period of more than a thousand years, and they were accurate and reliable."
The library where these manuscripts are kept, called the Chester Beatty Library, is located in Dublin, Ireland, and contains thousands of ancient Christian scriptural manuscripts, some of which are manuscripts used to translate the Bible dating back to the years 100-200 AD, meaning about 100 years after the Bible was written. The book called The Anchor Bible Dictionary says: "Although many ancient manuscripts contain much valuable information that cannot be verified, it is still important because they show what the scriptures were like."
"We should rejoice and be glad that there are many ancient manuscripts that have been carefully preserved and passed down to us."
IS THIS REALLY SO?: Critics of the Scriptures say that these ancient manuscripts used to translate the Bible are unreliable. A scholar named Sir Frederic Kenyon wrote in his book The Text of the Greek New Testament that: "Many ancient manuscripts differ from the Bible, and the Bible has many ancient variations that make it difficult to know what the original wording was. And a careful reader will find that the text of the Bible has been changed." Another scholar named William Henry Green stated this in his book Introduction to Old Testament Criticism: "We should rejoice and be glad that there are many ancient manuscripts that have been carefully preserved and passed down to us."
^ ref. 6 Perhaps you would like to examine more information on pages 195-197 in the book Is the Bible God's Word?, or visit www.jw.org/kam.

text:
Mo Aklĩsto matwaanĩte makatũmĩa IUD ("intrauterine device," kana "coil") kũsiĩĩa kũkua ĩvu nĩmethĩwa maitũla myolooto ya Maandĩko?
Mũndũ na mũka nĩmaĩlĩte kwĩkala nthĩ masũanĩe myolooto ya Mbivilia, na maisũanĩa ũndũ IUD ithũkũmaa. Na ĩndĩ mayĩka ũtwi ũũmatia na wasya mũseo wa ngoo.
Ĩla andũ maĩ elĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ (na ĩla maĩ nyanya ĩtina wa mbua ya ĩvinda ya Noa), Yeova anenganie mwĩao ũũ: "Ongelekai, mwingĩve, musũsye nthĩ." (Mwa. 1:28; 9:1) Mbivilia ndĩwetete kana mwĩao ũsu nĩwaĩlĩte kũatĩĩwa nĩ Aklĩsto. Kwoou mũndũ na mũka nĩmo maĩlĩte kũtw'a ethĩwa nĩmeũtũmĩa nzĩa ya kũsiĩĩa kũkua ĩvu nĩ kana mavange mesyaa syana iana ata, na mesyaa ĩtina wa ĩvinda yĩana ata. Maĩlĩte kũsũanĩa maũndũ meva?
Nzĩa ĩla Aklĩsto meũtũmĩa ndyaĩlĩte kũtũla mĩao ya Mbivilia. Kwoou mayĩsa kumya ĩvu nĩ kana maikasyae syana mbingĩ. Mũndũ aumya ĩvu na ngenda ethĩawa eeka kĩvathũkany'o na woni wa Mbivilia, nũndũ Mbivilia yaasya thayũ nĩwaĩle kũnewa ndaĩa. Mũklĩsto ndaĩlĩte kumya ĩvu nũndũ ethĩawa aananga thayũ wa mwana ũkwĩsaa kwĩana na aisyawa. (Kuma 20:13; 21:22, 23; Sav. 139:16; Yel. 1:5) Ĩndĩ nata ĩũlũ wa kũtũmĩa IUD?
Ũvoo ũsu nĩwaneeneiwe ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya Kĩswaili ya 15/10/1979, ĩthangũ ya 22-23. IUD mbingĩ ila syaĩ kw'o myakanĩ ĩsu (inert IUD) syaĩ tũsamũ twa vulasitiki twalikaw'a waonĩ wa mwana (nyũmba ya mwana) nĩ kana mũndũ mũka ndakaitave. Ĩkaseti yĩu yaisye kana ĩvindanĩ yĩu andũ mayeesĩ nesa ũndũ IUD syathũkũmaa. Myakanĩ ĩsu andũ aingĩ ma saenzi maasya kana IUD isu ve ũndũ syeekaa navu nthĩnĩ ũkethĩa mbeũ sya mũndũũme iyamba kũkomana na ĩtumbĩ ya mũndũ mũka. Na kwoou ethĩwa iinakomana, vai kana kanoombĩka.
Ĩndĩ vaĩ o ũkunĩkĩli woonanasya mavinda amwe mbeũ sya mũndũũme syaĩ itonya kũvĩta ikakomana na ĩtumbĩ. Syakomana, ĩtumbĩ yĩu yaĩ yĩtonya kwambĩĩa kũtw'ĩka mwana yĩ mwĩkivanĩ (an ectopic pregnancy) kana o yĩkatheea waonĩ. Ethĩwa nĩyatheea na yeethĩana na ĩla IUD, weethĩaa yĩitonya kwĩkwatĩlĩĩlya waonĩ nĩ kana mwana aendeee kũmbĩka nesa. Ĩtumbĩ yĩu yetĩka weethĩaa kĩu no ũndũ ũmwe na kumya ĩvu. Ĩkaseti yĩu yaminĩĩe na kwasya: "Mũklĩsto ũkwĩkũlya ethĩwa IUD nĩ nzeo kana ti nzeo, aĩlĩte kũsũanĩa mũno maũndũ asu aililikana kana Mbivilia yaĩtye nĩtwaĩlĩte kũnenga thayũ ndaĩa nũndũ nĩ mũtheu."—Sav. 36:9.
Vo nĩvethĩĩtwe maendeeo maũndũnĩ ma saenzi kana ma ũiiti kuma ũvoo ũsu watumbĩthw'a 1979?
Kuma ĩvinda yĩu nĩkũseũvĩtw'e mĩthemba ĩngĩ ĩlĩ ya IUD. Mũthemba ũmwe nĩ wa copper, na wambĩĩe kũtũmĩwa mũno myaka mĩongo yĩana ũna mĩvĩtu. Naw'o mũthemba ũla ũngĩ nĩ wa hormone, na wambĩĩe kũtũmĩwa myaka kauta ĩtina wa ũsu wa copper. Twĩ na ũvoo mwaũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mĩthemba ĩsu ĩlĩ ĩthũkũmaa?
IUD ya Copper: O tondũ twoona, IUD yĩ waonĩ ti laisi mbeũ sya mũndũũme kũvĩta ivikĩe ĩtumbĩ. Kwongela kĩu, IUD ya copper nĩyũaaa mbeũ sya mũndũũme. * Na eka ũu, IUD ya copper ĩtw'ĩkĩkaa nĩetae moalyũku waonĩ nthĩnĩ.
IUD ya Hormone: IUD ya mũthemba ũũ yĩthĩawa na kĩndũ kĩtawa hormone. Kĩndũ kĩu kĩilyĩ o kĩla kĩthĩawa mbekenĩ ila aka mamelasya maikaitave. IUD isu ithũkũmaa o ta ila sya tene (inert), ĩndĩ ve maũndũ angĩ syĩkaa. Ũndũ ũmwe nĩ kwathũkĩa hormone ĩkanyaĩĩka waonĩ. Veonekana kana ĩla aka amwe meũtũmĩa IUD ĩsu, nĩmaekaa kumya matumbĩ. Na kwoou vate ĩtumbĩ, mbeũ ya mũndũũme ndĩsa kũitavya mũndũ mũka. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana IUD ya hormone ĩtw'ĩkĩkaa nĩtumaa wao wa mwana ũvũtha ĩla yĩ mwĩĩnĩ. * O na ĩngĩ, nĩkamasya kĩmia kĩla kĩ nzĩanĩ (cervix) ya kũlika waonĩ, na kwoou ũyĩthĩa mbeũ sya mũndũũme iitonya kũlika waonĩ.
O tondũ twoona, mĩthemba ĩsu ĩlĩ ya IUD ĩtw'ĩkĩkaa nĩetae moalyũku waonĩ nthĩnĩ. Ĩndĩ nata ĩtumbĩ yĩkauma na yĩikomana na mbeũ sya mũndũũme? No yĩtheee waonĩ (nyũmbanĩ ya mwana), ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa yĩitonya kwĩkwatĩlĩĩlya ũ waonĩ nũndũ ndũilyĩ ũndũ waĩle kwĩthĩwa ũilyĩ. Kĩu no kĩtume ĩvu yĩtĩka yĩ o ĩnini. Ĩndĩ andũ ma saenzi maasya kana ũndũ ũsu wĩ vinya mũno kwĩsa kwĩkĩka, o tondũ mbeke ila aka mamelasya itakothaa kũtuma ĩvu yĩtĩka.
Kwoou vai mũndũ wĩsa kwasya vyũ kana IUD sya copper kana sya hormone nisiĩĩaa vyũ mbeũ sya mũndũũme iikomana na ĩtumbĩ. Ĩndĩ ũkunĩkĩli wa saenzi wonanĩtye kana nũndũ wa maũndũ asu twaneenea vau ĩũlũ mekawa nĩ IUD isu, nĩ vinya mũno mũndũ mũka akaitava e nayo.
Ethĩwa wĩ na mũkau kana mũemeu nĩmũkwenda kũtũmĩa IUD, no mũneene na ndakĩtalĩ wĩsene na maũndũ asu. Ndakĩtalĩ ũsu no amũtavye nĩ mĩthemba yĩva ya IUD ĩkwatĩkanaa vala mũĩ, ũseo nĩ wĩva wa kũmĩtũmĩa, na nĩ mathĩna meva matonya kũkwata kĩveti kyamĩtũmĩa. Mũyaĩlĩte kwĩkwatya kana kwĩtĩkĩlya mũndũ o na wĩva amwĩkĩe ũtwi, o na ethĩwa nĩ ũ ndakĩtalĩ. (Alo. 14:12; Aka. 6:4, 5) Ũsu nĩ ũtwi wenyu mwĩ elĩ. Aklĩsto matwaanĩte maĩlĩte kwĩka ũtwi ũsu me elĩ, me na kĩeleelo kya kũmwendeesya Ngai na kũtiwa na wasya mũseo wa ngoo.—Sianĩsya na 1 Timotheo 1:18, 19; 2 Timotheo 1:3.
^ kal. 4 Livoti ĩmwe ya England's National Health Service yaĩtye: "IUD ila syĩ na copper mbingangĩ ithũkũmaa nesa mũno, ũseo wasyo wĩ mbee wa 99 kwa 100. Ũu nĩ kwasya kana nthĩnĩ wa mwaka ũmwe, katĩ wa iveti 100 itũmĩaa IUD nĩ vinya kũkwata kĩmwe kĩkũitava. IUD ila syĩ na copper ninangi iithũkũmaa nesa ũu."
^ kal. 5 Nũndũ ĩla mũndũ wĩkĩĩtwe IUD sya hormone wao wake nũvũthaa, mavinda amwe eĩtu na iveti nĩmeawa nĩ ndakĩtalĩ maitũmĩe ethĩwa ĩvinda ya mwei nĩmonaa nthakame mbingĩ mũno.

translation:
Does a Christian woman who uses an IUD ("intrauterine device," or "coil") show that she does not value life as sacred according to the Bible?
A husband and wife may find themselves facing a moral dilemma regarding the use of an IUD. And they may wonder whether the IUD is Scripturally right. Also, some doctors may recommend it and offer it as a form of family planning.
But God gave humans this command (and he gave it even before the flood of Noah's day): "Be fruitful and become many and fill the earth." (Gen. 1:28; 9:1) The Bible shows that procreation is something that God approves of. So a husband and wife may want to consider what alternatives there are to using an IUD, and also other methods of family planning. Can they make a satisfying decision?
Alternatives that a Christian can use do not violate Biblical principles. Some couples may choose to practice abstinence during certain times. A person who values life will weigh his conscience carefully in harmony with the Bible, knowing that the Bible's counsel is reliable. A Christian can practice abstinence because he wants to please God and because he respects the sanctity of human life. (Rom. 20:13; 21:22, 23; Ps. 139:16; Jer. 1:5) Is there anything wrong with using an IUD?
This question was considered by the Governing Body of Jehovah's Witnesses on October 15, 1979, pages 22-23. Many IUDs today are inert (inert IUDs) made of plastic that prevent implantation of a fertilized egg (conception) or cause a miscarriage. That publication stated that if an IUD causes a miscarriage, it is viewed as taking a life. Inert IUDs have been shown to sometimes interfere with the body's normal functioning, and some scientists believe that such IUDs can cause inflammation that leads to a miscarriage. And if a miscarriage occurs, it can be emotionally distressing.
Is there evidence that some methods of birth control may actually end a life? Sometimes, a miscarriage can result from a method of birth control. A miscarriage could lead to an ectopic pregnancy (an ectopic pregnancy) or a dangerous complication. If a miscarriage occurs due to an IUD, it can be difficult to determine whether it was caused by the device or whether the woman would have miscarried anyway. The miscarriage itself can also be physically and emotionally traumatic. That publication concluded with the statement: "Whether a Christian should or should not use an IUD is a matter for each individual to decide, but he should carefully examine his conscience and seek guidance from the Bible, knowing that its counsel is trustworthy."—Ps. 36:9.
What has further scientific research revealed since this question was discussed in 1979?
There are several types of IUDs available. One type is made of copper, which can be used for up to ten years. Another type contains hormones, which can be used for three to five years. But does this mean that these devices are always effective?
Copper IUD: In essence, a copper IUD does not prevent a fertilized egg from implanting. Furthermore, a copper IUD can harm a fertilized egg. * And on top of that, a copper IUD can cause severe cramping.
Hormonal IUD: This type of IUD releases a hormone. This hormone thickens cervical mucus, making it difficult for sperm to pass through. Some IUDs are considered inert, meaning they don't release anything. However, one concern is that the hormone released can affect a developing baby. It seems that some women who use these IUDs experience miscarriages. And if a miscarriage occurs, a fertilized egg may be lost. Another concern is that hormonal IUDs can cause inflammation of the uterine lining, which can make it difficult for a fertilized egg to implant. * Additionally, it can alter the cervix, making it harder for sperm to enter.
In essence, some types of IUDs can cause severe cramping. Does implantation occur when an egg implants in the uterus? No, it doesn't (miscarriage), but it can make it more difficult for a woman to get pregnant later. This is because it can thicken the uterine lining. This can also cause irregular periods. And scientists believe this may be due to the difficulty of implantation.
It is possible for a woman to become pregnant even if she has a copper or hormonal IUD, especially if the IUD moves out of place. Scientific studies suggest that there is a small chance of pregnancy with these IUDs, but it is still possible for a woman to get pregnant despite them.
If you and your husband want to use an IUD, discuss the matter thoroughly with your doctor. Your doctor will explain the risks associated with IUDs, including the possibility of ectopic pregnancy, and the difficulties involved in removing it. Remember to pray about it or seek advice from someone experienced, and if you feel uncomfortable, talk to your doctor. (Ps. 14:12; Prov. 6:4, 5) This is your body. Christians should take good care of their bodies, and with a clear conscience, please God and maintain a good reputation.—Compare 1 Timothy 1:18, 19; 2 Timothy 1:3.
^ par. 4 One report from England's National Health Service states: "Copper IUDs are very effective, over 99 in 100 women who use them correctly. This means that fewer than 1 in 100 women using a copper IUD will become pregnant in a year."
^ par. 5 However, some women who have a hormonal IUD fitted may experience side effects, and some studies show that they may be more likely to contract pelvic inflammatory disease.

text:
Ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya
Mbivilia ndĩvĩngaa. O na kau mĩsoa ĩmwe ya Mbivilia nĩtonya kũtuma twona Mbivilia ta yĩvĩngaa, no tũmĩelewe tũkatũmĩa maũndũ aa maeleetw'e vaa ĩtheo:
Sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mĩsoa ĩla ĩthyũlũlũkĩte mũsoa ũla wasoma. Ndeto no ieleeke naĩ mũndũ akaisoma ate kũsũanĩa maũndũ ala mawetetwe mbee wa ndeto isu na ĩtina wasyo.
Sũanĩa nĩkĩ mũandĩki waandĩkie ũvoo ũsu ũilyĩ ũndũ ũilyĩ. Andũ me kĩvathũkany'o manoonie ũndũ ũmwe no maũelesye nesa vyũ, ĩndĩ mateũtũmĩa ndeto ivw'anene kana mate kũelesya maũndũ onthe kwa nzĩa ĩmwe.
Sũanĩa nĩ ĩndĩĩ ũvoo ũla ũũsoma waandĩkiwe na ũndũ maũndũ mailyĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu.
Vathũkany'a maandĩko ala maandĩkĩtwe kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o na ala maandĩkĩtwe kwa nzĩa ĩte ya ngelekany'o.
Elewa kana ve maũndũ amwe mawetawa ta meekiwe nĩ mũndũ mũna, o na ethĩwa tiwe mwene wamekie. *
Tũmĩa Mbivilia ĩalyũlĩtwe nesa.
Ndũkatate kũvĩndũa momanyĩsyo ma w'o ma Mbivilia mosane na momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ ma ndĩni.
Ngelekany'o ii iatĩĩe nikwonany'a ũndũ tũtonya kũtũmĩa maũndũ asu mawetwa kũelesya mĩsoa ĩmwe ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ yonekaa ta ĩkũvĩngana.
Ũndũ wa 1: Ndeto ila ithyũlũlũkĩte ĩandĩko
Ethĩwa Ngai athyũmũie mũthenya wa mũonza, nĩkĩ Mbivilia yaasya kana no ũendeee na kũthũkũma? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai 'athũmũie mũthenya wa mũonza ũndũ wa wĩa wake w'onthe ũla watethasya.' Mĩsoa ĩla ĩthyũlũlũkĩte mũsoa ũsu wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mwambĩlĩlyo yĩonany'a kana wĩa ũla Ngai wathyũmũĩie waĩ wa kũmba syĩndũ ila syĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:2-4) Yesũ ndavĩngaa ndeto isu ĩla waisye kana Ngai "nũtethasya wĩa," nũndũ aneenaa ĩũlũ wa mawĩa angĩ eka wĩa wa wũmbi. (Yoana 5:17) Amwe ma mawĩa ala Ngai ũtethasya nĩ kũandĩkĩthya Mbivilia, kũtongoesya andũ na kũmasũvĩa.
Ũndũ wa 2 na wa 3: Ũndũ mũandĩki waandĩkie ũvoo mũna ũilyĩ na ĩvinda yĩla waandĩkie
Ũla mũndũ waĩ kĩlalinda avoeiw'e va nĩ Yesũ? Ĩvuku ya Luka yaĩtye kana Yesũ avoisye mũndũ waĩ kĩlalinda 'athengeee Yeliko,' nayo ĩvuku ya Mathayo yĩwetete ĩũlũ wa aũme elĩ maĩ ilalinda, na yĩkasya kana mavoiw'e ĩla Yesũ 'waumĩte Yeliko.' (Luka 18:35-43; Mathayo 20:29-34) Maũndũ asu elĩ mawetetwe maeleetw'e nĩ andũ elĩ me kĩvathũkany'o, ĩndĩ kĩla ũmwe aeleetye ũndũ ũtaawetwa nĩ ũla ũngĩ. Mathayo aiweta ĩũlũ wa aũme asu, awetete nesa kana maĩ elĩ, nake Luka awetete ĩũlũ wa mũndũũme ũmwe ũla Yesũ waneenie nake. Asomi mawetaa kana ĩvindanĩ ya Yesũ, Yeliko yaĩ na taoni ilĩ, taoni ĩla ngũũ yambĩĩiw'e nĩ Ayuti na yaĩ kĩlomita kĩmwe na nusu (maili 1) kuma vala ve taoni ĩla yaĩ nzaũ yambĩĩiw'e nĩ Alomi. Nĩvatonyeka Yesũ akethĩwa aĩ nzĩanĩ katĩ wa taoni isu ilĩ ĩla weekie kyama kĩu.
Ũndũ wa 4: Vathũkany'a maandĩko ala maandĩkĩtwe kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o na ala maandĩkĩtwe kwa nzĩa ĩte ya ngelekany'o
Yo nthĩ ĩkaanangwa? Ĩvukunĩ ya Mũtavan'ya 1:4, Mbivilia yaasya kana nthĩ "nĩyĩkalaa tene na tene," na andũ amwe maasyaa kana ndeto isu nivĩnganaa na ila syaĩtye kana "nthĩ na mawĩa ala me nthĩnĩ wayo makavĩvw'a." (2 Vetelo 3:10) Mbivilianĩ, ndeto "nthĩ" ĩtũmĩawa kwonany'a nthĩ ĩno twĩkalaa, na no ĩtũmĩawa kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o kwonany'a andũ ala mekalaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:1; 11:1) Nakw'o kwanangwa kwa "nthĩ" kũla kũwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya 2 Vetelo 3:10, kwonanasya "kwanangwa kwa andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai," ĩndĩ ti kũvĩvw'a kwa nthĩ ĩno twĩkalaa.
Ũndũ wa 5: Tata ũmanye nũũ ũla weekie ũndũ mũna
Yesũ e Kavelinaumi, nũũ wamũeteie livoti ya mũnene wa Asikalĩ ĩana? Ĩvuku ya Mathayo 8:5, 6 yaĩtye kana mũnene wa asikalĩ nĩwe waendie vala ve Yesũ, nayo ĩvuku ya Luka 7:3 yonanĩtye kana mũnene ũsu wa asikalĩ atũmie atumĩa ma Ayuti makaneene na Yesũ. O na kau ndeto isu no syoneke ta iũvĩngana, sionany'a kana mũnene wa asikalĩ nĩwe waumanie na mũvango ũsu wa kũneena na Yesũ, ĩndĩ atũma atumĩa makaneene kwondũ wake.
Ũndũ wa 6: Tũmĩa Mbivilia ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe nesa
Ithyonthe twĩ na naĩ? Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana ithyonthe nĩtwatiĩwe naĩ nĩ Atamu. (Alomi 5:12) Mbivilia imwe ialyũlĩtwe kwa nzĩa ĩkũvĩnga ndeto isu nũndũ syaĩtye kana mũndũ mũseo "ndekaa naĩ." (1 Yoana 3:6, The Bible in Kikamba, 1974; The Bible in Basic English) Kĩthyomonĩ kya Kĩkiliki, ndeto "naĩ," ĩla ĩtũmĩĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Yoana 3:6 yĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a ũndũ ũendeee na kwĩkĩka. Ve kĩvathũkany'o katĩ wa naĩ ĩla tũsyaawa twĩ nayo, na mavĩtyo ala twĩkaa ĩla twalea kwĩw'a mĩao ya Ngai. Kwoou Mbivilia imwe nialyũlĩte ĩandĩko yĩu kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle kwa kwasya kana mũndũ mũseo "ndaendeeaa kwĩka naĩ."
Ũndũ wa 7: Ndũkatate kũvĩndũa momanyĩsyo ma w'o ma Mbivilia mosane na momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ ma ndĩni
We Yesũ nĩwĩanene na Ngai? Ve ĩvinda Yesũ waisye: "Nyie na Asa twĩ ũmwe," na ndeto isu no syoneke ta iũvĩngana na ndeto ii ingĩ wawetie ĩla waisye, "Asa nĩ mũnene kwĩ nyie." (Yoana 10:30; 14:28) Nĩ kana tũelewe mĩsoa ĩsu nesa, no nginya tũmanye kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa Yeova na Yesũ, vandũ va kũmantha ũndũ ũmanyĩsyo ũsu wa ũvũngũ ũkwosana na mĩsoa ĩsu. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana Yeova nĩwe Ĩthe wa Yesũ na nowe Ngai ũla Yesũ ũthaithaa. (Mathayo 4:10; Maliko 15:34; Yoana 17:3; 20:17; 2 Akolintho 1:3) Kwoou Yesũ ndeanene na Ngai.
Mĩsoa ĩla ĩthyũlũlũkĩte ndeto sya Yesũ ila syaĩtye kana 'we na Asa nĩ ũmwe' yoonanasya kana e na Ĩthe wake, Yeova Ngai, methĩawa na ngwatanĩo na kĩeleelo kĩmwe. Ĩtina Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Asa e nthĩnĩ wakwa, nakwa nĩ nthĩnĩ wa Asa." (Yoana 10:38) Yesũ aĩ na ngwatanĩo na kĩeleelo kĩmwe e na aatĩĩi make na nĩkyo kĩtumi wamavoyeie kwa Ngai akyasya atĩĩ: "Ũtao ũla wanengie nĩnĩmanengete w'o; nĩ kana methĩwe me ũmwe, o ũndũ ithyĩ twĩ ũmwe; nyie nthĩnĩ woo, naku nthĩnĩ wakwa."
^ kal. 8 Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvuku ya Encyclopædia Britannica yĩiweta ĩũlũ wa mwako wa Taj Mahal, yaasya kana mwako ũsu "waakiwe nĩ mũtongoi wa Mughal weetawa Shah Jahān." Ĩndĩ tiwe mwene waakie mwako ũsu nũndũ kĩlungu kĩu kĩ ĩvukunĩ yĩu kĩendeee kwasya kana "mavundi mbee wa 20,000 nĩmaandĩkĩtwe mathũkũme" mwakonĩ ũsu.

translation:
The Book of Proverbs
Proverbs are wise. And if someone reads just one verse of Proverbs, it can help us see Proverbs as being wise, and we will understand and use the words that have been given to us from God:
Read a chapter of verses each day while reading a verse. Then it will be clear to someone who reads it and to understand the words that are contained within that verse and its meaning.
Reading is when an author writes something good and meaningful. People who think about things carefully should focus on one thing and explain it well, rather than trying to understand too many things at once.
Reading is also when what you read is written with a purpose and the words are meaningful to you.
Consider the writings that were written with intention and those that were written without intention.
Understand whether some words are hidden or revealed by a person, or whether their own mind has revealed them. *
Use the Bible wisely.
Don't confuse the teachings of this world with the teachings of truth inside.
Intention here means understanding something that helps us use the words that are hidden in some verses of the Bible so they appear to be more understandable.
Point 1: A verse that is meaningful is writing
May God guide the heart of the reader, whether the Proverbs are useful or continue to explore? The Bible says that God "guides the heart of the reader towards all his people who listen." Verses that are meaningful like this are a gift from Jehovah, showing how God guides those who want to learn the truth. (Jehovah 2:2-4) Jesus is wise enough to say that God "listens," meaning he cares for all kinds of people. (John 5:17) Some of the ways God listens are by inspiring the Bible, guiding people, and saving them.
Point 2 and 3: What an author writes meaningfully and clearly
Did a man protect himself when he asked Jesus? The account in Luke says that Jesus healed a man who was blind 'near Jericho,' while the account in Matthew tells a story about two blind men near the city, and states that Jesus healed them 'near Jericho.' (Luke 18:35-43; Matthew 20:29-34) These differences are because the writers were eyewitnesses, each remembering what seemed most important to him. Matthew mentions two blind men, stating specifically that there were two, while Luke mentions only one man whom Jesus healed. Readers know that Jericho had two walls, one built by Hiel and about 1.5 kilometers (1 mile) away from the other wall built by Benhadad. It seems Jesus stopped near both walls, perhaps because they were crowded.
Point 4: Understand the scriptures that are written with intention and those that are written without intention
Why is this important? The scripture at Revelation 1:4 states that time "will be no more," and some understand this to mean that time will completely cease to exist, while others understand it to mean "time and times and seasons." (2 Peter 3:10) In Scripture, the term "time" is used to refer to an appointed time, and also used intentionally to refer to people living during a certain period of time. (Ecclesiastes 1:1; 11:1) Also, the importance of "time" in 2 Peter 3:10 should be understood as referring to "the time of those who seek God," rather than the end of time itself.
Point 5: Know how to identify what is important
In Capernaum, why did he heal the centurion's servant? The account in Matthew 8:5, 6 says that the centurion went to Jesus himself, while the account in Luke 7:3 states that the centurion sent friends from Capernaum to ask Jesus. Although there is a difference, it does not contradict, because the centurion showed humility by sending friends to plead his case to Jesus.
Point 6: Understand scriptures that have been mistranslated
What about this? The Bible explains that everything was created through him by Adam. (Romans 5:12) Some scriptures were translated in such a way that they say someone "lives in him." (1 John 3:6, The Bible in Kikamba, 1974; The Bible in Basic English) According to the Greek text, the phrase "in him" in 1 John 3:6 refers to continuing on in obedience. Therefore, let us strive to live according to God's laws, so we can continue to abide in him. Other scriptures were also translated in a way that implies someone "continues to live in him."
Point 7: Be careful not to mix interpretations of scriptures with personal opinions
Did Jesus claim to be equal to God? Jesus once said: "You and I are one," and he made another statement which some understand to mean he said, "The Father is greater than I." (John 10:30; 14:28) However, if we carefully examine those statements, we will realize that the Bible explains the relationship between Jehovah and Jesus, two distinct individuals who share a common purpose. The Bible clarifies that Jehovah is the Father of Jesus and the only true God whom Jesus worshiped. (Matthew 4:10; Mark 15:34; John 17:3; 20:17; 2 Corinthians 1:3) Thus, Jesus acknowledged God as his superior.
Statements that seem to suggest that Jesus is equal to God, like the saying 'you and I are one,' clarify that he and his Father, Jehovah God, have a close bond and a shared purpose. Jesus himself stated: "The Father is in me, and I am in the Father." (John 10:38) Jesus had a close bond with his Father, and that is why God approved of him and declared: "This is my Son, whom I have chosen; listen to him."
^ par. 8 For example, the latest edition of the Encyclopædia Britannica describes the construction of the Taj Mahal, stating that the mausoleum "was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahān." It goes on to explain that building the mausoleum took approximately "20,000 laborers" over several years.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1964
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: ENGLAND
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: EETHĨIWE NA SYANA E O WA MŨIKA NA AĨ NA MWĨKALĨLE MŨTHŨKU
KWĨANA KWAKWA
Nasyaĩwe Paddington, vandũ vekalaa andũ aingĩ mũno mũsyĩnĩ wa London, England. Nekalaa na inyia wakwa na eĩtu angĩ atatũ akũũa. Ĩthe wakwa ndatũthĩnĩkĩaa ũndũ vaĩle nũndũ aĩ mũthengi.
Ĩla naĩ mũnini, inyia wakwa nĩwamanyĩisye kũvoyaa kĩla wĩoo. Naĩ na Mbivilia nini yaĩ na ĩvuku ya Savuli yĩ yoka, na nĩneeseũvĩsye tũwathi ngainaa nĩ weka. Nĩngũlilikana ndisoma ndeto syakiitie ngoo yakwa mũno kuma ĩvukunĩ yĩmwe ila syaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ve mũthenya ũtakethĩwa thayũ." Ndeto isu syatumie ndakoma ũtukũ mũima ndisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Nasũanĩie kana no nginya vethĩwe ve kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩthĩwa nĩ thayũ. O na neekũlasya nĩkĩ noombiwe? Ndyendaa kũkw'a!
Nĩnendaa mũno kũmanya ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma ũwe. Nĩnatataa kũneena na andũ akw'ũ, nĩnaendaa tũvulĩnĩ nĩ na anyanyawa ala twasomaa ĩmwe, na nĩnasiasya sinema sya kũtelemya vamwe namo. O na kau nĩtwendeeaw'a nĩ kwĩloela sinema isu, nĩsyatumaa tũtelema.
Nĩnambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku nĩ o na myaka ĩkũmi. O na nĩnanyusaa sikala na wesa kwĩthĩa ndyĩkala ndamĩnyw'ĩte. Ĩtina nĩnambĩĩie kũnyw'a vangi. Nĩ na myaka 11 nĩnambĩĩie kũnyw'a ũkĩ. O na kau ndyendeeaw'a nĩ ũndũ wasamaa, nĩneew'aa mũyo ĩla namilwa. O na nĩnendete mbathi na kũsũnga. Na ĩla vatonyeka, nĩnaendaa kũndũ kũla andũ makomanaa metanĩthye, o na nĩnaendaa disco sya ũtukũ. Nĩnatolokaa ũtukũ na ndisyoka ĩngĩ mũsyĩ kũtanakya. Na nũndũ naamũkaa nĩnoete, nĩnatĩaa sukulu ndawetete. Na ĩla nathi sukulu, nĩnanyusaa ũkĩ masomo maendeee.
Nĩnavalũkile mũno mũtianinĩ ũla neekie wa kũmina sukulu. Inyia wakwa nĩwathĩnĩkie mũno na athata nũndũ ndeesĩ kana naĩ na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku. Nĩtwaemaniwe nake na natoloka mũsyĩ. Kwa ĩvinda yĩana ũna nĩnekalanilye na kĩmwana twaĩ ndũũ kyeetawa Tony, kĩla kyaĩ kya ndĩni ya Rastafari. Aĩ kĩng'ei na nĩwathooasya ndawa sya kũmila, o na nĩweesĩkĩe ta mũndũ wendete kũkita. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩnaitavie, na nĩ na myaka 16, nasyaa kamwana.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA
Nĩnakomanie na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kwa ĩvinda ya mbee ĩla nekalaa kũndũ kũla kũsũvĩĩawa aka ala masyaa mate atwae vamwe na syana syoo. Nĩ kũu, nĩnanengetwe nyũmba ya kwĩkala nĩ anene ma silikalĩ. Aka elĩ maĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmatembeleaa aka amwe twekalaa namo. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩneethukĩĩisye kĩla maneeneaa. Nĩnendaa kũĩkĩĩthya Ngũsĩ isu kana momanyĩsyo moo ti ma w'o. Ĩndĩ nĩmasũngĩie makũlyo maingĩ ala naĩ namo me auu na kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle matũmĩĩte Mbivilia. Maĩ andũ aseo mũno na mauĩtye, na ũndũ ũsu nĩwambendeeisye mũno. Kwoou nĩneetĩkĩlile kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia namo.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩneemanyĩisye ũndũ kuma Mbivilianĩ ũla waalyũlile mwĩkalĩle wakwa. Kuma ĩla naĩ mũnini, nĩnakĩĩte kũkw'a. Ĩndĩ nĩnamanyie ũndũ Yesũ wamanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa ũthayũũkyo! (Yoana 5:28, 29) O na nĩnamanyie kana Ngai nũnthĩnĩkĩaa. (1 Vetelo 5:7) Nĩnakiitiwe ngoo mũno nĩ ndeto ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Yelemia 29:11, ila syaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ nĩnĩsĩ mosũanĩo ala nĩsũanĩaa kwondũ wenyu, easya Yeova, mosũanĩo ma mũuo, na ti ma ũthũku, kũmũnenga wĩkwatyo mũminũkĩlyo wenyu." Nĩnambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa Nthĩ Nzaũ tene na tene.—Savuli 37:29.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyambonisye wendo wa w'o. Ĩla naendie maũmbanonĩ moo ĩvinda ya mbee, noonie me na ũnyanya na mendete kũthokya aeni! (Yoana 13:34, 35) Maũndũ ala neekiwe vau maĩ kĩvathũkany'o mũno na maũndũ ala neekawa ĩkanisanĩ yĩla naendaa. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyanthokisye nesa o na kau naĩ na mathĩna maingĩ. Nĩmambĩthukĩĩisye, manzũvĩa, na mandethya maũndũnĩ maingĩ. Neew'aa ta nĩ nthĩnĩ wa mũsyĩ mũnene wa andũ mendanĩte.
Nũndũ wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, nĩnamanyie kana no nginya nĩke moalyũku mana thayũnĩ wakwa nĩ kana nĩkale kwosana na myolooto ya Ngai. Ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũeka kũnyw'a sikala. Ĩvindanĩ o yĩu, nĩnamanyie kana mbathi imwe neethukĩĩasya syatumaa nendeew'a mũno nĩ kũnyw'a vangi, na kwoou naeka kũsyĩthukĩĩsya. Nĩ kana nĩvathane na syĩndũ isu na ndyĩkala nesa, nĩnaekie kũthi kũla andũ makomanaa metanĩthye na naeka kũthi disco sya ũtukũ nũndũ nĩneesĩ nathi kũu ndiema kũnyw'a ũkĩ. Na nĩnamanthie anyanya angĩ ala maĩ matonya kũndetheesya nĩthĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseo.—Nthimo 13:20.
Ĩvindanĩ o yĩu, Tony nĩweemanyĩasya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩla wasũngĩiwe makũlyo make kuma Mbivilianĩ, o nake nĩwaĩkĩĩie kana kĩla weemanyĩasya nĩ kya w'o. Nĩweekie moalyũku manene, kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwaekie kũtindany'a na andũ ala maĩ ang'endu, aekana na ũng'ei, na aeka kũnyw'a vangi. Nĩ kana tũmwendeesye Yeova vyũ, nĩtwoonie ve vata wa kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle witũ mũthũku na tũyĩthĩwa tũtonya kũea mwana witũ kwa nzĩa nzeo. Nĩtwatwaanie mwaka wa 1982.
"Yu ndyaĩawa nĩ too ũtukũ mũima ndithĩnĩka ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte kana kĩkw'ũ"
Nĩnĩlilikanaa ndyĩka ũkunĩkĩli makasetinĩ ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Amkeni! * ĩũlũ wa andũ meekie moalyũku ta ala nendaa kwĩka. Nĩneekĩiwe vinya mũno nĩ ngelekany'o syoo. Nĩneewie neekĩwa vinya nĩendeee vyũ nde kũkw'a ngoo. Nĩnamũvoyaa Yeova andetheesye. Mwei wa 7, 1982, nĩ na Tony nĩtwavatisiwe na twatw'ĩka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE
Kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova nĩkwatangĩĩie thayũ wakwa. O na ĩngĩ, nĩ na Tony nĩtwonete Yeova aitũtetheesya mavindanĩ ma thĩna. Nĩtwĩmanyĩĩtye kũmwĩkwatasya Yeova mavindanĩ ma thĩna, na nĩtwonete aitũtetheesya.—Savuli 55:22.
Nĩnatanĩie mũno kũtetheesya syana syakwa imũmanye Yeova o tondũ nĩmwĩsĩ. Yu nĩw'aa mũyo mũno noona syana syoo iendeee kũmũmanya Ngai.
Yu ndyaĩawa nĩ too ũtukũ mũima ndithĩnĩka ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte kana kĩkw'ũ. Nĩ na Tony nĩtũendaa ikundinĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kĩla kyumwa kwĩkĩana vinya na ana-a-asa ala angĩ. Nĩtũendaa kũmanyĩsya andũ ala angĩ Mbivilia twĩ vamwe na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asu nĩ kana andũ ala twamatavya mamũĩkĩĩa Yesũ, meĩthĩwa matonya kũtanĩa kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene.
^ kal. 17 Matumbĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
