LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1964
THE COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: ENGLAND
OUR PARENTS: WERE BORN BY A WOMAN AND A MAN WHO LOVED EACH OTHER
FOR MY OWN SAKE
I was born Paddington, many people live in this large city of London, England. They have children and several grandchildren. My family has always been doing good things and helping others.
And because I am young, my family teaches me to greet everyone I meet. And I have read the Bible and the book of Psalms many times, and I have learned many lessons from them. I remember reading a story about someone who said: "Don't be afraid of tomorrow." This story helped me sleep peacefully at night and think about the future. I wondered if I could also be brave enough to face whatever comes my way. But I am still learning!
I want to know more about the world. I find it difficult to talk to strangers, so I prefer to go with friends and classmates, and I enjoy watching movies with them. Maybe we can go watch a movie together, which will help us learn.
I remember being forced to love school when I was ten years old. But I enjoyed playing and running around instead of studying. Then I started drinking alcohol when I was eleven years old. But maybe if I went back, it would be different, and I would appreciate it. And I started smoking and going out with friends, and when they got tired, I would go home to study, and when I finished school, I enjoyed the subjects that were taught.
I had a lot of problems during the time I wanted to finish school. My parents worried a lot and sometimes scolded me. I failed and dropped out early. During those days, I befriended a boy named Tony, who belonged to the Rastafarian faith. He introduced me to drugs, and I didn't realize how dangerous he was. Later in life, I regretted it, and when I was sixteen, I became a father.
THIS IS WHAT THE BIBLE TAUGHT MY PARENTS
I associated with Jehovah's Witnesses for some time because I lived near their place of worship, and they often visited our home with their publications. It is true, I was invited to their hall, which was very beautiful. Sometimes we would visit them together. One day I realized something important. I decided to investigate Jehovah's Witnesses and find out what they believe. Now I read many articles with them and learned from the Bible. Many people felt the same way, and this helped me a lot. That's why I want to share the Bible with others.
In those days, I learned about a scripture in the Bible that spoke about resurrection. Because of this, I began to hope. Then I understood what Jesus taught about life everlasting! (John 5:28, 29) And I learned that God cares for us. (1 Peter 5:7) I was comforted by this, especially when I remembered Jeremiah 29:11, which says: "For I know the thoughts that I have toward you, says Jehovah, thoughts of peace, and not of calamity, to give you an expected future." I resolved to trust in God and live forever—Psalm 37:29.
Jehovah's Witnesses showed me love. But I still had questions because of my past experiences, and I needed help to overcome them! (John 13:34, 35) The things I experienced affected me deeply, and the things I saw troubled me. Jehovah's Witnesses reassured me and helped me cope with many difficulties. I became more confident, courageous, and willing to talk about my faith. Now I am one of the many people who preach the good news.
Because I studied the Bible, I realized that I could be different from the people around me and live according to God's standards. It wasn't easy to stop doing the things I used to do. In time, however, I realized that bad associations can lead to harmful habits, and that it is important to avoid them. Even though I struggled with some temptations, I continued to pray and sought God's help, and I stopped going to bars and nightclubs because I knew they would hinder my spiritual progress. And I learned to associate with people who were encouraging and supportive.—Proverbs 13:20.
In time, Tony introduced me to the Bible and Jehovah's Witnesses. He had been studying the Bible for some time, and he encouraged me to see if what he was learning was true. I made significant changes in my life; for example, I quit associating with bad company, stopped drinking alcohol, and avoided harmful habits. If we continue to love Jehovah, we will enjoy the privilege of living forever and raising our children in righteousness. We got married in 1982.
"I remember feeling very afraid the night I first considered whether what I was being taught was right."
I began to write letters to the publishers of The Watchtower and Awake! magazines, asking questions that were on my mind. They kindly answered my questions, which helped me to understand matters more clearly. I felt that they were sincere and wanted to help me find the truth. I prayed to Jehovah for guidance. On July 7, 1982, Tony and I dedicated ourselves to Jehovah and started attending meetings at the Kingdom Hall.
OTHER THINGS THAT HELPED ME
Having a close relationship with Jehovah has transformed my life. Also, Tony and I asked Jehovah to bless us in our ministry. We endeavored to put Jehovah first in our lives, and we asked him to bless our efforts.—Psalm 55:22.
I am so grateful that I took the initiative to learn about Jehovah, even though I was hesitant. If you have a similar desire, never give up on getting to know God.
I remember feeling very afraid the night I first considered whether what I was being taught was right. Tony and I would often go to the Kingdom Hall each week just to observe the meetings and see how others responded. We enjoyed helping people learn about the Bible, especially young ones and those who had never met anyone who followed Jesus. We realized how important it was to share the good news with everyone we could.
^ par. 17 Our Meetings at the Kingdom Hall.

text:
KWASŨANĨA wĩ ũmwe katĩ wa Aklĩsto ala maĩ ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa. Kĩkundi kĩla ũthaithĩaa kĩiandĩkĩwa valũa kuma kwa mũtũmwa Vaulo. O ũendeee kwĩthukĩĩsya valũa ũsu ũisomwa, ũyĩw'a mũtũmwa Vaulo awetete mavinda maingĩ "maandĩko matheu," ala nĩ Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania. (2 Timotheo 3:15) Na ũndũ ũsu ũituma wenda kwona vala maandĩko asu mawetwa valũanĩ maumĩte. Ĩndĩ ũu ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi. Nĩkĩ?
MAANDĨKO MATHEU MAYAĨ NA ILUNGU NA MĨSOA
Kwasisya wone ũndũ mavuku ala maĩ na "maandĩko matheu" ĩvindanĩ ya mũtũmwa Vaulo mailyĩ. Kĩlungu kĩmwe kya ĩvuku ya Isaia nĩkyonanĩtw'e visanĩ ũũ, nakyo kyeethĩiwe nthĩnĩ wa Mavuku ma Ũkanga wa Mũnyũ (Dead Sea Scrolls). Kĩlungu kĩu kyonanĩtye Maandĩko mate na ilungu kana mĩsoa, na mate mavange nesa ũndũ twamanyĩie kwonaa Mbivilianĩ.
Andũ ala maandĩkie Mbivilia mayaamĩkĩa ilungu na mĩsoa. Maandĩkaa ũvoo w'onthe kuma kwa Ngai nĩ kenda asomi maũsome w'onthe wũmbanĩte, vandũ va kwĩthĩwa ũaanĩtw'e tũlungu tũnini. Ũu tyo w'o wenda vethĩwe vailyĩ ĩla ũũsoma valũa ũandĩkĩwe nĩ mũndũ wendete? Nũsomaa valũa ũsu w'onthe, ĩndĩ ti tũlungu tũnini.
Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa maandĩko asu mate na ilungu kana mĩsoa nĩkwaetie mathĩna. Vaulo eekaa o kũweta maandĩko asu aitũmĩa ndeto ta "o tondũ kũandĩkĩtwe" kana "tondũ Isaia wambie ũneena." (Alomi 3:10; 9:29) Na waĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kũkwata maandĩko asu ateo wĩthĩwe ũsomete mũno "maandĩko matheu."
O na ĩngĩ, "maandĩko matheu" maneeneaa maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o kuma kwa Ngai. Myaka ĩana ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto yĩ vakuvĩ kũthela, Mbivilia yaĩ na mavuku 66 me kĩvathũkany'o! Na nũndũ wa ũu, asomi aingĩ ma Mbivilia nĩmatanĩaa kwĩthĩwa yĩ na ilungu na mĩsoa ila imatetheeasya kũmanya vala matonya kũkwata ũvoo mũna. Kwa ngelekany'o, no tũmanye maandĩko maingĩ ala Vaulo ũwetete valũanĩ syake.
Na kwoou no wĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Naaũ meekĩie ilungu na mĩsoa Mbivilianĩ?'
NAAŨ MEEKĨIE ILUNGU?
Mũtongoi wa ndĩni weetawa Stephen Langton, ũla wesie kũtw'ĩka Mbisovu Mũnene wa Canterbury, nũkumĩtw'e nũndũ wa kwĩkĩa ilungu Mbivilianĩ. Eekie ũu mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1200 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, ĩla waĩ mwalimũ wa University of Paris, ĩla yĩ France.
Ĩvinda ĩasa mbee wa Langton kwĩka ũu, asomi maĩ matatie nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya kũaany'a Mbivilia kwa tũlungu tũnini, na veonekana meekaa ũu nĩ kana wĩthĩe nĩ laisi kũkwata kĩlungu kĩla mũndũ ũkwenda kũsoma. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ wĩthĩwa waĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũkwata ũvoo mũna kĩlungunĩ kĩmwe vandũ va kũũmantha ĩvukunĩ yĩu yonthe, na yĩi na ilungu na mĩsoa. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwasũanĩa ũimantha ũvoo mũna ĩvukunĩ ya Isaia yĩla yĩ ilungu 66 na saa isu yĩi na ilungu na mĩsoa.
Ĩndĩ nzĩa isu sya kwĩkĩa ilungu nĩsyaumĩlilye mathĩna. Asomi asu maanĩtye maandĩko ma Mbivilia kwa ilungu syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Maliko yaanĩtw'e vakuvĩ ilungu 50, vandũ va ilungu 16 ila syĩ vo yu. Ĩvindanĩ ya Langton, taoninĩ ya Paris, kwaĩ amanyĩw'a aingĩ kuma nthĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na nĩmookie na Mbivilia kuma nthĩ syoo. Ĩndĩ ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa alimũ na amanyĩw'a kũeleany'a vala ũvoo mũna umĩte. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Mbivilianĩ isu, ilungu syaanĩtw'e kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
Kwoou, Langton nĩwaumĩlilye nzĩa nzaũ ya kũaany'a ilungu. Kwosana na ĩvuku yĩtawa The Book—A History of the Bible, nzĩa ĩsu yake "nĩyendeeisye asomi na aandĩki," na "yamanyĩka kũndũ kwingĩ Europe." Langton nĩwe weekĩie ilungu ila twonaa Mbivilianĩ mbingĩ ũmũnthĩ.
NAAŨ MEEKĨIE MĨSOA?
Myaka ta 300 ĩtina wa Langton kwĩkĩa ilungu Mbivilianĩ, mũsomi ũmwe weesĩkĩe mũno weetawa Robert Estienne kuma France nĩwatumie kũsoma Mbivilia kwĩthĩwa kwĩ laisangi. Robert Estienne eekie ũu katĩkatĩ wa myaka ya 1501 nginya 1600. Nũndũ nĩwendaa andũ aingĩ mendeew'e nĩ kũsoma Mbivilia, nĩwoonie wĩ ũndũ wa vata yĩthĩwe na nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũvanga ilungu na mĩsoa.
Estienne tiwe waetie woni wa Mbivilia kwĩthĩwa na mĩsoa. Ve andũ angĩ maĩ meekie ũu. Kwa ngelekany'o, myaka maana maingĩ mĩvĩtu, aandĩki amwe ma Kĩyuti nĩmeekĩie Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania mĩsoa, ĩndĩ mayaaĩkĩa ilungu. Maandĩko asu ma Kĩevelania nomo metawa Ũtianĩo Mũkũũ. O tondũ ilungu syaanĩtw'e kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, now'o mĩsoa ĩsu yavangĩtwe kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
Estienne nĩwatũmĩie nzĩa nzaũ kũaany'a Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto kana Ũtianĩo Mweũ meethĩwa na mĩsoa. Nzĩa ĩsu nzaũ watũmĩie kũaany'a maandĩko asu noyo watũmĩie kũaany'a Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania. Mwaka wa 1553, nĩwaumĩthisye Mbivilia ya mbee yĩ nima (kwa kĩthyomo kya French) yĩ na ilungu na mĩsoa ĩvangĩtwe o tondũ Mbivilia mbingĩ ila itũmĩawa ũmũnthĩ syĩthĩawa iilyĩ. Andũ amwe nĩmaleaa na maasya kana mĩsoa ĩsu yaanĩtye Mbivilia ĩkatw'ĩka tũlungu tũnini nginya ũkethĩa wĩoneka ta ũvoo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ĩndĩ nzĩa ĩsu ya Estienne nĩyeetĩkĩlilwe nĩ atumbĩthya aingĩ ma Mbivilia, na mambĩĩa kũmĩtũmĩa.
ŨNDŨ ASOMI MA MBIVILIA MATETHEKAA
Nzĩa ĩsu ya kwĩkĩa ilungu na mĩsoa Mbivilianĩ nĩ nzeo. Ĩtumaa kĩla mũsoa Mbivilianĩ wĩthĩwa na namba yaw'o. Kwa w'o, namba ila syeekĩiwe syonanasye ilungu na mĩsoa iyaaveveewa nĩ Ngai, na ve kũndũ kũmwe siaanĩtye Mbivilia ũkethĩa ti laisi kũmanya nĩkĩ yaanĩilw'e vau. Ĩndĩ ilungu na mĩsoa nitumaa wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũkwata maandĩko ala tũkwenda na maũndũ manene. O na nitũtetheeasya kũmanya mĩsoa ĩmwe ĩtonya kũtũtethya, o tondũ tũtonya kũkululĩĩla kũndũ kũla kwa vata tũkwenda kũlilikana ĩvukunĩ tũũsomaa.
O na kau ilungu na mĩsoa ĩla yeekĩiwe Mbivilianĩ nĩtũtethasya, ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana twaĩle kũelewa nĩ ũvoo w'onthe ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Ĩmanyĩsye kũsomaa kĩlungu kĩla kĩthyũlũlũkĩte mĩsoa mĩna vandũ va kũsomaa mũsoa o ũmwe. Weeka ũu, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũelewa nesanga "maandĩko matheu, ala matonya ũkũĩvya kũvika ũtangĩĩo."—2 Timotheo 3:15.

FROM INFANCY one among Christians but scriptures were revealed through the apostles. Every group has been written value according to the apostle Paul. And continue to be amazed value until you read, this is the apostle Paul who explained many "sacred writings," but they are Writings of Revelation. (2 Timothy 3:15) And this thing makes you want to see that the scriptures are established with truth. This is why this matter is important. Why?
SACRED WRITINGS OLD AND NEW AND COPIES
Consider seeing what centuries and also "sacred writings" revealed through the apostle Paul contain. One fragment of the book of Isaiah was found recently, and it was confirmed by experts from the Dead Sea Scrolls. That fragment shows writings old and new copies, and old versions show us what we know about the Bible.
People who study the Bible understand old and new copies. The writings all come from God and are good to read thoroughly, people who are shown are amazed by large fragments. So you want to be shown fully when you read what is written by someone else? Read all of this, because it is large fragments.
Because being shown scriptures old and new copies is essential. Paul said he wrote scriptures using quotations like "as it is written" or "as Isaiah said." (Romans 3:10; 9:29) But sometimes it is difficult to get scriptures that have been shown to read carefully "sacred writings."
Also, "sacred writings" contain many things that are hidden from God. Years before the birth of Christ they existed, the Bible had 66 things that are hidden! And because of this, many readers of the Bible are amazed to be shown with old and new copies but find it easy to understand what secrets to get from it. For example, we don't know many writings that Paul explained with his own words.
And so you might ask, 'Why did people show old and new copies in the Bible?'
WHY DID PEOPLE SHOW [THE] OLD COPIES?
A man named Stephen Langton, who later became Archbishop of Canterbury, was given the task of showing the old copies in the Bible. He did this in the 1200s years before the birth of Christ, while he was a teacher at the University of Paris, which is in France.
Before Langton did this, scholars had difficulty organizing the Bible into large fragments, and it seemed that it was easier to understand each fragment when everyone wanted to read it. It meant that it was easier to get a good understanding in one language and people understood everything completely, including old and new copies. For example, it meant understanding everything in the book of Isaiah which has 66 chapters and also old and new copies.
The ways of organizing the Bible were difficult. Scholars found it hard to organize the writings of the Bible into fragments. For example, the story of the New Testament in Mark's Gospel was divided into 50 fragments, while 16 fragments were missing. According to Langton, the teachers of Paris knew much about organizing things well, and they worked with the Bible on those matters. One thing that was easy for teachers and scholars was to agree on how to arrange everything. Why? Because the Bible was organized in a certain way.
So, Langton improved the ways of organizing the Bible. According to the book called The Book—A History of the Bible, his work "helped scholars and writers," and "spread widely throughout Europe." Langton showed the Bible as we see the Bible today.
WHY DID PEOPLE SHOW NEW COPIES?
About 300 years after Langton organized the Bible, a scholar named Robert Estienne from France was sent to read the Bible in order to correct it. Robert Estienne lived between the years 1501 and 1600. Because people wanted to read the Bible, he saw the need for a new way of arranging the Bible and showing copies.
Estienne did not just show copies of the Bible; others also did this. For example, many years later, some writers from Germany showed copies of the German Writings, which helped organize the Bible. These German writings also included the Old Testament. But because the Bible was organized in a certain way, new copies were also arranged in a certain way.
Estienne used his resources to examine the Greek Writings of Christ or the New Testament shown in copies. He also used his resources to examine these writings and then used them to examine the German Writings. In 1553, he published a complete Bible (in French) with the Bible and copies being arranged so that the Bible could be understood more easily. Some people complained that the copies or new versions of the Bible made the language too difficult and the meaning unclear. However, Estienne's copies were praised by many Bible scholars, and they continued to use them.
THE STUDY OF THE BIBLE IS IMPORTANT
It is important to have the Bible in languages and copies. It helps each copy of the Bible to be identified by its number. Because of this, the number can help us understand the languages and copies approved by God, and we can together study the Bible without knowing which version was read. The languages and copies help us avoid having inaccurate texts and going astray with great errors. Also, they help us recognize some verses that may confuse us, because we can refer back to other verses to compare while reading.
And when languages and copies are considered Biblical, it is important for those who teach to know how to explain the entire message of the Bible. Understand that reading each passage carefully will help those who read a verse or one copy. Like this, it is possible to understand the meaning "sacred writings, but they can help you from childhood."—2 Timothy 3:15.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA 1987
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE AZERBAIJAN
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU ĨTHE AĨ MŨISILAAMU NA INYIA AĨ WA NDĨNI YA AYUTI
KWĨANA KWAKWA: Nasyaĩwe vandũ vetawa Baku, nthĩ ya Azerbaijan.
Asyai maitũ maĩ na syana ilĩ na ninyie wa kelĩ. Ĩthe wakwa aĩ Mũisilaamu na inyia wakwa aĩ wa ndĩni ya Ayuti. Asyai makwa nĩmendanĩte na kĩla ũmwe nĩwanengete ndaĩa mũĩkĩĩo wa ũla ũngĩ. Inyia wakwa nĩwakwataa ĩthe wakwa mbau ĩvinda ya sikũkũ ya Ramadan, na ĩthe wakwa nĩweekaa ũu ĩla inyia wakwa ũkũlilikana Vasaka. Mũsyĩ kwitũ veethĩawa na Mbivilia, ĩvuku ya Koran, na ya Torah.
Neetalaa ta nĩ Mũisilaamu. O na kau nĩnaĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai, ve maũndũ ndaeleawa nesa. Neekũlasya-ĩ, 'Yo nĩkĩ Ngai woombie andũ?' O na ĩngĩ neekũlasya-ĩ, 'Ve vata mwaũ wa mũndũ kũng'ang'ana thayũnĩ wake w'onthe, na ĩtina ayĩsa kũvĩvw'a ĩianĩ ya mwaki?' Nũndũ andũ maasya maũndũ onthe mekĩkaa nũndũ wa kwenda kwa Ngai, neekũlasya-ĩ, 'Ngai ko ũeteae andũ mathĩna na aitana ĩla meũthĩna?'
Nĩ na myaka 12, nĩnambĩĩie kũvoya mboya ya Aisilaamu yĩtawa namaz, ĩla ĩvoyawa mala atano kwa mũthenya. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu ĩthe witũ nĩwatũtwaie sukulu ya Kĩyuti nĩ na mũkũũa. Katĩ wa masomo maingĩ, nĩtwamanyĩaw'a syĩthĩo ila iandĩkĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa Torah vamwe na kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania. Kĩla mũthenya masomo matanambĩĩa, twavoyaa kwĩanana na kĩthĩo kya ndĩni ya Ayuti. Kwondũ wa ũu, kwakya ndanauma mũsyĩ navoyaa namaz, na ĩla nĩ sukulu ndivoya mboya ya Kĩyuti.
Naĩ na waũni mwingĩ vyũ wa kũkwata mosũngĩo maseo ma makũlyo ala neekũlasya. Natindĩaa ũkũlya alimũ ma ndĩni ya Kĩyuti makũlyo aa: "Nĩkĩ Ngai woombie andũ? Nũndũ ĩthe wakwa nĩ Mũisilaamu, Ngai amwonaa ata? Onekaa e mũvuku nĩkĩ, na nyie nonaa e mũseo? Ngai amũmbaa nĩkĩ?" Mosũngĩo manini ala nakwataa mayaĩ maseo na matonya kũĩkĩĩka.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA: Mwakanĩ wa 2002, nĩneewie nanow'a nĩ kũmũĩkĩĩa Ngai.
Twaĩ tũnathamĩĩa nthĩ ya Germany, na ĩtina wa kyumwa kĩmwe ĩthe wakwa awaa ũwau wa stroke na weethĩa ndekwĩyĩw'a. Kwa myaka mingĩ nĩnavoyaa kwondũ wa andũ ma mũsyĩ witũ maikaaĩse kũwaa. Nũndũ naĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana Mwene Vinya W'onthe nĩwe wĩthĩawa na ũtonyi ĩũlũ wa thayũ kana kĩkw'ũ, nĩnamwĩsũvaa kĩla mũthenya asũvĩe ĩthe wakwa. Noonaa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa Ngai kũmbĩthukĩĩsya nũndũ naĩ o kelĩtu kanini, na navoyaa kuma ngoonĩ. Naĩ na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana ndalea kũsũngĩa mboya yakwa. Ĩndĩ ĩtina ĩthe wakwa nĩwakwie.
Ũndũ ũla wanzeng'isye nĩ kana noonie Ngai atailyĩ ũndũ nasũanĩaa, na ũndũ ũsu wandũla ngoo vyũ. Neekũlasya atĩĩ: 'Yo ninyie mboyaa kwa nzĩa ĩla ĩtaĩlĩte, kana kũi Ngai?' Nĩnakwatiwe nĩ kĩmako na naeka kũvoya mboya ya namaz. Ndyendeeaw'a nĩ ndĩni ila ingĩ, na kwondũ wa ũu natw'a kana kũi Ngai.
Ĩtina wa myei thanthatũ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyatũthokeie. Nũndũ tũyendeeaw'a nĩ Ũklĩsto, nĩ na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wakwa nĩtwendaa kũmamanyĩthya kwa ndaĩa kana me mavĩtyo. Twamakũlilye atĩĩ: "Aklĩsto matonya ata kũthaitha Yesũ, ngelany'o, Meli, na mĩvw'anano, na ĩla Mĩao Ĩkũmi ndĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũndũ ũsu?" Nĩmatũmĩie Maandĩko kũtũĩkĩĩthya kana ũthaithi wa mĩvw'anano ndwaĩlĩte kwa Aklĩsto ma w'o na kana maĩlĩte kũvoya Ngai e weka. Ũndũ ũsu wanzeng'isye mũno.
O na ĩngĩ twamakũlilye atĩĩ: "Nao nata ĩũlũ wa ũmanyĩsyo wa Ũtatũ? Ethĩwa Yesũ nĩ Ngai, vatonyekie ata ekala kũũ nthĩ, na esa kũawa nĩ andũ?" Masũngĩie makũlyo asu matũmĩĩte Mbivilia na matũelesya kana Yesũ ti Ngai na ndeanene na Ngai. Na matũtavya kana nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩu, mo maiĩkĩĩaa Ũtatũ. Naseng'ie mũno na noona me Aklĩsto masaanĩtye.
O na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩnendaa kũmanya nĩkĩ andũ makusaa na nĩkĩ Ngai ũekete mathĩna methĩwe vo. Nĩmambonisye ĩvuku yĩtawa Ujuzi Uongozao Kwenye Uhai Udumuo Milele, * yĩla yĩ na ilungu isũngĩĩte makũlyo ala neekũlasya. Vau kwa vau, nĩmambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nakwa.
Kĩla ĩvinda tũyĩmanyĩsya, nĩnakwataa mosũngĩo maseo kuma Mbivilianĩ. Nĩnamanyie kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ Yeova. (Savuli 83:18) O na namanya kana ndaĩa yake ĩla nene vyũ nĩ wendo. (1 Yoana 4:8) O na nĩnamanyie kana oombie mũndũ nũndũ nĩwendaa syũmbe ingĩ syĩthĩwe thayũ take. Nĩnesie kũelewa kana o na kau Ngai nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũsili ũte wa katĩ ũendeee, we ndawendete na o mĩtũkĩ nũkũũvetanga. Namanyie kana ũlei wa Atamu na Eva nĩw'o waeteie andũ mathĩna. (Alomi 5:12) Ũmwe katĩ wa mathĩna ala maetiwe nĩ ũlei ũsu nĩ kĩkw'ũ kya endwa maitũ, ta ũndũ ĩthe wakwa wakwie. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, Ngai akavetanga mathĩna nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ, na aithayũũkya ala makwie.
Ũw'o wa Mbivilia nĩwaminie waũni ũla naĩ naw'o wa kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala neekũlasya. Nĩnambĩĩie kũĩkĩĩa ĩngĩ kana kwĩ Ngai. O ũndũ naendeeie kũmanya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nesa, now'o namanyie kana methĩawa na ngwatanĩo nthĩ yonthe. Nĩnendeeiw'e mũno nĩ wendo na ngwatanĩo yoo. (Yoana 13:34, 35) Maũndũ ala neemanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩmatumie nenda kũmũthũkũma, na kwoou, natw'a kwĩthĩwa Ngũsĩ ya Yeova. Navatisiwe Matukũ 8, Mwei wa 1, 2005.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE: Nĩnasomie ũvoo wa kũĩkĩĩka kuma Mbivilianĩ na wandetheesya neethĩwa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa thayũ.
Maũndũ ma kũĩkĩĩka ala nasomie Ndetonĩ ya Ngai nĩmatumie nĩthĩwa na mũuo wa ngoo. Nĩnatanie mũno na nakiakiw'a nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũmwona ĩthe wakwa athayũũka o tondũ Ndeto ya Ngai yathanĩte.—Yoana 5:28, 29.
Nũndũ mũũme wakwa Jonathan nũmũkĩĩte Ngai, nĩtwĩthĩĩtwe na mũtwaano wĩ na ũtanu kwa myaka thanthatũ. Nĩtũmanyĩte kana ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai nĩwakũĩkĩĩka, wĩ laisi, na nĩ mũthĩnzĩo ũtathooeka. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi ithyĩ tũtanĩaa kũelesya angĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo witũ na wĩkwatyo mũseo ũla twĩ naw'o. Ũmũnthĩ nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ti Aklĩsto "masaanĩtye," ĩndĩ nĩmo Aklĩsto ma w'o.
^ kĩl. 15 Yumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, ĩndĩ yu nĩyaekie kũtumbĩthw'a.

LET IT BE THE YEAR 1987
WITHIN WHICH IS LOCATED AZERBAIJAN
OUR LANDS ARE THOSE OF MUSLIMS AND PEOPLE OF THE INNER AYUTI
ACCORDING TO THIS: Remember those who were in Baku, the land of Azerbaijan.
Let us be united and have peace among yourselves. Their lands are Muslim lands and their people are from within Ayuti. Our lands are beautiful and each one strives for the betterment of life. Their people observe their religious duties during the holy month of Ramadan, and their lands celebrate when their people gather at Easter. Let our teachings come from the Bible, the book of the Quran, and the Torah.
My belief is Islam. And I ask myself or God, but things are understood clearly. I question, 'Who is God who guides people?' And again I question, 'Are they looking for the path of a person according to his own desires, and ignoring the importance of the truth of life?' Therefore people do everything they can to go to God, I question, 'God why do you create people and call them to hardship?'
When I was 12 years old, I began to practice the Islamic prayer called namaz, which is practiced five times a day. Our family sent us to Kyuti school with enthusiasm. Among many lessons, we learned stories written in the Torah and the history of Ukraine. Every day the lessons continued, we went to learn about the religion of Ayuti. Because of this, sometimes I would prefer to pray namaz, and even at school I would practice the Kyuti prayer.
And I had many questions about taking responsibility for the good deeds that I questioned. I pondered over eating food from the Kyuti religion saying: "Who is God who guides people? Are their lands Muslim, does God see them at all? Please tell me the book, and you show me the responsibility? Does God guide me?" Many responsibilities I took upon myself and struggled to fulfill.
THIS BIBLE STORY INSPIRED MY LIFE: In the year 2002, I realized I needed to seek God.
We traveled to Germany, and one of their relatives suffered a stroke and became paralyzed. For many years I visited those relatives to help them. But I believed that the Almighty God is the one who heals with great power or ability, so I prayed for him every day to recover. I saw that there were things beyond human capability with God, and I went to pray. And I believed that I would continue practicing my faith. That relative recovered.
The thing that troubled me was whether God accepts what I ask for, and whether He will answer my prayers. I wondered: 'Why do you pray for something that has already been decided, or against God?' I was confused and stopped praying namaz. I searched for answers in many places, and because of this I came to believe in God.
In the year nineteen ninety, Jehovah's Witnesses preached to us. We learned about Christ, and through them we wanted to know the truth about these matters. They asked: "Does Christ have any authority apart from Jesus, besides Michael, and the ten angels, does he have any power?" I used the scriptures to show them that the authority of the angels is limited compared to Christ and that they can only act with God's permission. This matter troubled me greatly.
And again they asked: "Do I understand the doctrine of the Trinity? Is Jesus God, does he have a separate existence from the Father, and is he equal to the Father?" I researched these questions using the Bible and explained that Jesus is not God and is subordinate to God. And I understood that the doctrine of the Trinity is wrong. I felt sad and the teachings of Christ disappointed me.
But now I want to know what people believe and what God expects of us. I testified to the book entitled "Knowledge That Leads to Everlasting Life," which has helped many people to understand the scriptures. Step by step, I showed them how to study the Bible and learn from it.
Every time we studied, I always took notes from the Bible. I came to know that God's name is Jehovah. (Psalm 83:18) And I realized that his love is great and endless. (1 John 4:8) And I understood that everyone wants to live forever. I was happy to realize that God will resurrect those who desire this life, so that they may continue to live on earth. I learned that Adam and Eve were the first humans. (Romans 5:12) Because of their sin, all mankind inherited sin, and this is why we die. If you wish, God will forgive mankind and give them another opportunity, and he will help them to improve.
I learned that the serpent deceived Eve, causing her to disobey God.
The message of the Bible comforted me and gave me hope. I wanted to share my faith with others. So I continued to learn about God's Kingdom, and now I know that it will soon bring peace to the earth. I am eager to show my love and loyalty to God. (John 13:34, 35) The things I have learned about Jehovah motivate me to tell others about him, and together, we can spread the good news of Jehovah. I signed this on August 8, 2005.
WHAT I HAVE LEARNED: I have studied the Bible and been convinced of its truthfulness by many scriptures.
The things I have learned from God's Word have given me comfort and hope. I am confident that those who obey God will be rewarded with everlasting life, because God's promise is reliable.—John 5:28, 29.
My dear friend Jonathan was devoted to God, and we shared a close friendship for over fifty years. We realized that God's purpose is to gather people, both living and dead, and that he is capable of fulfilling his purpose. That is why we were determined to help others learn about our Creator and to remain loyal to him. It makes me happy to know that Jehovah God through Christ "will revive" them, which means Christ will resurrect them.
^ par. 15 We believe in God's Kingdom, and we look forward to being ruled by it.

text:
Ũmũnthĩ andũ nĩmathĩnaw'a. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi aingĩ mamwĩkaĩlaa Ngai amaumye thĩnanĩ ũsu, o na kau nĩmaseng'aa kana ũkathela. We Ngai nĩwĩthukĩĩasya kĩĩo kyoo? Nao nata ĩũlũ wa ala mokitaa nĩ kana maeke kũthĩnw'a? We Ngai nũmakwataa mbau ĩla mekũkita?
Ndeto ii no iũkiakisye: Ngai nĩwĩthĩawa ene mathĩna ma andũ ũmũnthĩ na nũvangĩte kũmamina. (Savuli 72:13, 14) Nthĩnĩ wa Ndeto yake, Mbivilia, aĩtye kana 'ala mathĩnaw'a' makakwata "ũthũmũo." Makaũkwata ĩndĩĩ? "Ĩvinda yĩla Mwĩaĩi Yesũ ũkavuanw'a kuma ĩtunĩ vamwe na alaĩka ma vinya wake . . . akĩĩvanĩsya kwa ala matamwĩsĩ Ngai, na ala matawĩw'aa ũvoo mũseo wa Mwĩaĩi waitũ Yesũ." (2 Athesalonika 1:7, 8) Kũvuanw'a kũu kwa Yesũ kũkeethĩwa ĩvinda yũkĩte yĩla Mbivilia yĩtĩte 'kaũ wa mũthenya mũnene wa Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe,' na now'o wĩtawa Ali–Maketoni.—Ũvuan'yo 16:14, 16.
Ngai ndakatũmĩa andũ kũkita kaũ ũsu, ĩndĩ akatũmĩa Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, e na syũmbe ingĩ sya veva syĩ vinya nĩ kana amine ũthũku. Syũmbe isu sya veva ikaveta andũ ala athũku.—Isaia 11:4; Ũvuan'yo 19:11-16.
O na ũmũnthĩ woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kaũ ndwaalyũka. Onaa kaũ new'o nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ ya kũmina ũthũku. Na o tondũ kwailyĩ kuma tene, no Ngai e weka ũtonya kũtw'a ĩla kaũ ũsu waĩle kũkitwa na ũla waĩle kũwũkita. Na o tondũ twoona, Ngai nĩwonanĩtye kana kaũ wa kũmina ũthũku na wa kũĩvanĩsya ala mathĩnaw'a nĩ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte, na ũkokitwa nĩ Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto. Ũu nĩkwonany'a kana kaũ ũla ũkitawa ũmũnthĩ ndwĩtĩkĩlĩtw'e nĩ Ngai o na ethĩwa andũ mena kĩtumi kya kũwũkita.
Kwa ngelekany'o: Sũanĩa tũmwana twĩlĩ tũyũkita ĩthe athi, na tũivika vandũ tũieka kũkita, tũikũnĩa ĩthe simũ na tũimũtavya. Kamwana kamwe kayasya kana kala kangĩ nĩko kambĩĩisye kaũ, nako kau kangĩ kayasya kana kau kangĩ nĩko kambĩĩie kũkathĩny'a. Onthe maimwĩkaĩla ĩthe maisũanĩa kana nũkwĩtĩkĩlana namo. Ĩthe eethukĩĩsya, ayĩa tũmwana tũu tũeke kũkita, asyoka nũkũka kũmina thĩna ũsu. Tũmwana tũyĩeka kũkita o kwa ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ tũyambĩĩa kũkita ĩngĩ. Ĩthe esa kũsyoka, aithatw'a nĩ ũndũ ũsu na aitũkany'a tw'onthe nũndũ wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a.
Ũmũnthĩ andũ ala mokitaa mamwĩkaĩlaa Ngai nĩ kana amatethye. Ĩndĩ Ngai ndatetheeasya ngalĩko o na ĩmwe ĩla andũ mekũkita. Vandũ va ũu aĩtye ũũ Ndetonĩ yake, Mbivilia: "Mũikekũle kwa mũndũ o na wĩva," na "Mũikeĩvanĩsye." (Alomi 12:17, 19) O na nũtũmanyĩthĩtye kana twaĩle 'kũmweteela na wũmĩĩsyo' nĩ kana ose ĩtambya, na akeeka ũu kaũnĩ wa Ali–Maketoni. (Savuli 37:7) Ĩla andũ malea kũmweteela Ngai ose ĩtambya na vandũ va ũu mayĩyũkitĩa, onaa kaũ ũsu ta kĩko kya ũng'endu na ũu nũmũthatasya. Kwoou, kaũnĩ wa Ali–Maketoni Ngai akoonany'a ũthatu wake na aimina ithokoo ila mbaĩ syĩthĩawa nasyo nũndũ 'akatuma makaũ mathela kũvika itulu sya nthĩ.' (Savuli 46:9; Isaia 34:2) Ali–Maketoni nĩw'o ũkethĩwa wĩ kaũ wa kũmina makaũ onthe.
Ũmwe wa moathimo ala Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkaete nĩ kũmina makaũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Yesũ nĩwaneenie ĩũlũ wa silikalĩ ĩsu nthĩnĩ wa ĩla mboya yĩsĩkĩe mũno, aisye atĩĩ: "Ũsumbĩ waku wũke. Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ o ta kũya ĩtunĩ." (Mathayo 6:10) Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkamina makaũ onthe o vamwe na ũthũku, nũndũ nĩw'o ũtumaa andũ mokita. * (Savuli 37:9, 10, 14, 15) O na ti ũsengy'o kwona aatĩĩi ma Yesũ mena wendi wa kwona moathimo ala Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkamaetee.—2 Vetelo 3:13.
Twĩeteela kwa ĩvinda yĩana ata nĩ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wũke kũmina mathĩna na ũthũku? Kwĩanĩw'a kwa wathani wa Mbivilia kwĩonany'a kana twĩkalĩte "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo" ya nthĩ ĩno. (2 Timotheo 3:1-5) * O mĩtũkĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkilye kũmina mĩthenya ĩno mĩthũku kwĩsĩla kaũnĩ wa Ali–Maketoni.
O tondũ twonie, ala makanangwa kaũnĩ ũũ wa mũthya nĩ ala "matawĩw'aa ũvoo mũseo wa Mwĩaĩi waitũ Yesũ." (2 Athesalonika 1:8) Ĩndĩ lilikana kana Ngai ndendeeaw'a nĩ kĩkw'ũ kya mũndũ, o na ethĩwa nĩ mũthũku. (Esekieli 33:11) Nũndũ Ngai 'ndendaa ũmwe o na wĩva ae,' kana anangwe kaũnĩ ũsu wa mũthya, nĩwendaa ũvoo mũseo ĩũlũ wa Mwĩaĩi Yesũ 'ũtavanw'e nthĩ yonthe nĩ kana wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe' mũminũkĩlyo ũtanamba kũka. (2 Vetelo 3:8, 9; Mathayo 24:14; 1 Timotheo 2:3, 4) Kwĩsĩla wĩa ũla Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itethasya wa kũtavany'a, andũ ũmũnthĩ me na mwanya wa kũmũmanya Ngai, kwĩw'a ũvoo mũseo ĩũlũ wa Yesũ, na kwĩsa kwona ĩvinda yĩla kũtakethĩwa kaũ.
^ kal. 9 Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkamina mũmaitha mũnene ũla ũthĩnasya andũ, nake nĩ kĩkw'ũ. O tondũ vonanĩtw'e kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩ ĩthangũnĩ ya 16, Ngai akathayũũkya andũ aingĩ o vamwe na ala makw'ĩĩe kaũnĩ.
^ kal. 10 Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo, sisya kĩlungu kya 9 kya ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? yĩla yumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.

translation:
People and children are valuable. And that is why many listen to God's command to raise up a family, or to care for others. Why does God show such concern? Because he knows that people can become righteous or wicked. God cares about those who seek him.
This poem shows: God cares about people and has compassion for them. (Psalm 72:13, 14) According to his purpose, the Bible says that 'valuable people' have "life." What does this mean? "The life that Jesus Christ gives is like a ransom paid for many, so that they may be freed from sin and death . . . and may be approved by God, and by those who know the name of our Lord Jesus." (2 Thessalonians 1:7, 8) Giving life through Jesus means giving hope, just as the Bible calls him 'the great and mighty God,' also known as Almighty.—Revelation 16:14, 16.
God sends people to give hope, and he sent his Son, Jesus Christ, and soon more of his servants will share good news. Soon more of his servants will bring good news to people.—Isaiah 11:4; Revelation 19:11-16.
And God's purpose for people will come true. See how this hope is like a bright light shining on us. And even though it seems far off, God will make sure that his purpose for people is fulfilled and that those who want to live right can do so. And as we see, God wants people to live right and to approve those who are valuable, and this is done through his Son, Jesus Christ. This is what makes his purpose different from what humans think—God allows people to choose whether or not to live right.
For example: Imagine children playing games, and we teach them how to play, we encourage them often and we correct them. One child might realize quickly that something is wrong, and another child might take longer to understand what is happening. But everyone learns at their own pace. Often mistakes are made when children try to learn together. Sometimes they get frustrated, but children always need encouragement to continue learning. A child who is taught how to play also needs to practice. We children need to be encouraged to play more. That way, eventually, they will become skilled and will enjoy the game.
Truly people who honor God are like those who listen to him. God listens to those who honor him, and he helps those who seek him. People of this world obey his Son, Jesus Christ, and the Bible says: "Be kind to others and forgive," and "Be generous." (Luke 12:17, 19) And if we want to show 'love through works' then we should remember that doing so can sometimes cause problems, and it can lead us to the path of Ali-Maketoni. (Proverbs 37:7) But people who love God always show love and people of this world appreciate it, because such kindness is a sign of strength and it encourages them. Therefore, Ali-Maketoni's path God recognizes his loyalty and he stops evil, but he allows some things to happen so that we can learn 'to send armies to fight until the sky shines'. (Psalm 46:9; Isaiah 34:2) Ali-Maketoni is the one who is praised for stopping armies from fighting.
One of the ways God's Kingdom will stop armies from fighting is by removing wickedness from the earth. Jesus told his disciples about this future time when there would be peace, saying: "Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven." (Matthew 6:10) God's Kingdom will stop all wars and violence, and it will help people to live peacefully. * (Psalm 37:9, 10, 14, 15) And don't think that Jesus did not know what was happening when he spoke about God's Kingdom coming.—2 Peter 3:13.
Should we therefore wait for God's Kingdom to solve all our problems and end violence? The Bible shows that we can become "instruments of righteousness" in this world. (2 Timothy 3:1-5) * And we can use God's Kingdom to help solve these problems, just as Ali-Maketoni did.
But remember that those who oppose God's Kingdom will experience "punishment with everlasting destruction" at Armageddon. (2 Thessalonians 1:8) God does not want anyone to perish, but he allows people to make their own choices, and some choose wickedness. (Ezekiel 33:11) However, God "does not desire one to go down into Sheol," and so he will allow the good news of God's Kingdom to be preached throughout the entire inhabited earth so that everyone has an opportunity to learn about him and choose life.—2 Peter 3:8, 9; Matthew 24:14; 1 Timothy 2:3, 4. Because Jehovah's Witnesses preach this good news, people have the opportunity to get to know God, accept the good news of Jesus, and see how they can benefit.
^ kal. 9 God's Kingdom will eliminate much suffering caused by mankind, because it is righteous. But since we are living in the 16th century, God is already saving many people from harm.
^ kal. 10 If you find more information on the topic of Bible prophecies, read the brochure What Does God Require of Us?, which was published by Jehovah's Witnesses.

text:
WE NŨTONYA kũsoma kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania kĩla kyatũmĩiwe kũandĩka Mbivilia? Noĩthwa ũteka ũu. O na noĩthwa ũtaaona Mbivilia ya Kĩevelania. Ĩndĩ, kũmanya mũsomi wĩtawa Elias Hutter, ũla waĩ thayũ myakanĩ ya 1501-1600, na waumĩthisye Mbivilia ilĩ sya Kĩevelania no kũũtetheesye ũkonaa Mbivilia yaku yĩ ya vata mũno.
Elias Hutter asyaiwe mwaka wa 1553, taoninĩ nini ya Görlitz, yĩ vakuvĩ na vala Germany ĩvakanĩe na Poland na Czech Republic. Hutter asomeie ithyomo ila ineenawa nthĩ sya Middle East e Lutheran University, Jena. E o na myaka 24, nĩwanyuviwe ethĩwe vulovesa wa kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania taoninĩ ya Leipzig. Na nũndũ nĩwendaa kũete moalyũku maũndũnĩ ma kĩsomo, nĩwesie kwambĩĩsya sukulu Nuremberg, vala amanyĩw'a maĩ matonya kwĩmanyĩsya Kĩevelania, Kĩkiliki, Kĩlatinĩ, na kĩthyomo kya German kwa myaka ĩna. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu, vai sukulu kana yunivasĩtĩ ĩngĩ yeekaa ũu.
'ŨSEO WA MBIVILIA ĨSU'
Mwakanĩ wa 1587, Hutter nĩwaumisye Mbivilia ĩla yĩsĩkĩe mũno ta Ũtianĩo Mũkũũ kwa kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania. Mbivilia ĩsu yaĩ na kyongo kyaĩ na ndeto ii, Derekh ha-Kodesh, kuma ĩvukunĩ ya Isaia 35:8, na ũalyũlo wasyo nĩ "Nzĩa ya Ũtheu." Mũandĩko mũseo wa Mbivilia ĩsu nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye ũw'o wa ndeto ila syaasyaa kana "kĩndũ kyonthe kĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩno nĩkyonanĩtye ũseo wayo." Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩsu yaĩ ya vata vyũ nũndũ amanyĩw'a nĩmamĩtũmĩaa ĩmatetheesye kwĩmanyĩsya Kĩevelania.
Nĩ kana ũelewe nĩkĩ Mbivilia ya Kĩevelania ĩla Hutter waalyũlĩte yaĩ ya vata, eka twone maũndũ elĩ maĩ vinya kũeleeka nĩ mũmanyĩw'a ũkũsoma Mbivilia kwa Kĩevelania. Ũndũ wa mbee, Kĩevelania kĩandĩkawa na nthoo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na itesĩkĩe, na ũndũ wa kelĩ, ndeto ila syongeleelawa mbee kana mũthya wa ndeto syatumaa yĩthĩwa ne vinya kũmanya ndeto ĩsu nesa. Nĩ kana tũelewe ũndũ ũsu, sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ndeto ya Kĩevelania נפשׁ (ĩalyũlawa ta ne'phesh), na yonanasya "thayũ." Ĩvukunĩ ya Esekieli 18:4, nthoo ya mbee ya ndeto ĩsu nĩ ה (ha), na kwoou syonthe syakwatanw'a iiseũvya ndeto ĩmwe הנפשׁ (han·ne'phesh), nayo nĩ "thayũ" (the soul). Methonĩ ma mũndũ ũtamanyĩĩtw'e nesa, ndeto הנפשׁ (han·ne'phesh) no yoneke yĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ndeto נפשׁ (ne'phesh).
Nĩ kana Hutter atetheesye amanyĩw'a make, atũmĩie ũtũĩka aumĩlya nzĩa nzaũ ya kũtumbĩthya mavuku. Atũmĩie mũandĩko wa nthoo sya Kĩevelania waĩ na langi mũkwatu na ũngĩ ũte mũkwatu. Atũmĩaa langi mũkwatu kũandĩka ndeto ĩla ya mũsingi (root of a word). Ĩndĩ atũmĩaa langi ũte mũkwatu aiandĩka nthoo ila syĩ mbee kana ĩtina wa ndeto ya mũsingi. Nzĩa ĩsu yĩ laisi nĩyatetheeisye amanyĩw'a mamanyae na mĩtũkĩ ndeto ĩla ya mũsingi ya Kĩevelania, na ũu nĩwamatetheeasya mayĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩu. O nayo Mbivilia ya New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References ĩtũmĩĩte nzĩa o ĩsu nthĩnĩ wa maelesyo ma kwongeleela. * Ndeto ĩla ya mũsingi ĩandĩkĩtwe na langi mũkwatu, nasyo nthoo ila syĩ mbee na ĩtina wa ndeto ĩsu syĩ na langi ũte mũkwatu. Visa ila syĩ ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ syĩ na kũndũ kwĩ na langi mweũ wonanĩtye nzĩa ĩla Hutter watũmĩie kũalyũla ĩandĩko ya Esekieli 18:4 Mbivilianĩ yake ya Kĩevelania, na nzĩa ĩsu noyo ĩtũmĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ ya Reference Bible maelesyonĩ ma kwongeleela o mũsoanĩ ũsu.
MBIVILIA YA "ŨTIANĨO MWEŨ" YA KĨTHYOMO KYA KĨEVELANIA
Hutter nĩwasyokie aumya kwa ithyomo 12 Mbivilia ĩla yĩsĩkĩe mũno ta Ũtianĩo Mweũ. Mbivilia ĩsu yaumĩthĩiw'e Nuremberg mwakanĩ wa 1599, na yĩtawa Nuremberg Polyglot. Hutter nĩwendaa vethĩwe Mbivilia ya Kĩevelania ya Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto. Ĩndĩ aisye kana o na keka "nĩwendaa kumya mbesa mbingĩ" nĩ kana Mbivilia ĩsu ya Kĩevelania ĩkwatĩkane, ũsu wĩthĩwa wĩ o wĩa wa mana. * Kwoou nĩwatwie kũalyũla Mbivilia ya Ũtianĩo Mweũ kwa Kĩevelania atũmĩĩte Mbivilia ya kĩthyomo kya Kĩkiliki. Hutter nĩwaekanie na maũndũ ala angĩ nĩ kana aalyũle Mbivilia ĩsu, na kwoou amĩmina na mwaka o ũmwe!
Mbivilia ya Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto ya Kĩevelania ĩla Hutter waalyũlile yaĩ na ũseo mwaũ? Mũsomi ũmwe waĩ nguma wĩtawa Franz Delitzsch, aandĩkie ndeto ii mwakanĩ wa 1891: "Maandĩko ala [Hutter] waalyũlĩte kwa Kĩevelania meonany'a nĩweesĩ kĩthyomo kĩteesĩkĩe nĩ Aklĩsto aingĩ na ũmũnthĩ nĩmatũmĩawa andũ mayĩka ũkunĩkĩli, nũndũ kaingĩ atũmĩĩte nesa ndeto ila syaĩlĩte."
WĨA ŨLILIKANAWA KWA ĨVINDA YĨASA
Hutter ndaathua nũndũ wa wĩa wake wa kũalyũla, na veonekana Mbivilia ila waalyũlĩte iyaathoow'a mũno. Ĩndĩ wĩa wake nũtethetye andũ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia ya Ũtianĩo Mweũ ya Kĩevelania ĩla waalyũlile nĩyeekiwe moalyũku na yatumbĩthw'a ĩngĩ mwakanĩ wa 1661 nĩ William Robertson na mwakanĩ wa 1798 nĩ Richard Caddick. Ĩla waalyũlaa kuma kĩthyomonĩ kya Kĩkiliki, Hutter nĩwaalyũlile ũndũ vaĩle masyĩtwa ma ũnene Kyʹri·os (Mwĩaĩi) na The·osʹ (Ngai) kwonany'a "Yeova" (יהוה, JHVH), vala ndeto syeethĩawa syumĩtw'e Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania kana vala woona ta iũneenea Yeova. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya nũndũ o na kau Mbivilia mbingĩ sya Ũtianĩo Mweũ iitũmĩaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai mwene, Mbivilia ya Hutter nĩtũmĩĩte ĩsyĩtwa yĩu, na kwoou nĩyĩĩkĩĩthasya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyaĩle kũtũngwa vala yaĩlĩte Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto.
Yĩla woona ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova, Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto, kana woona maelesyo ma kwongeleela nthĩnĩ wa Reference Bible, lilikanaa wĩa wa Elias Hutter na Mbivilia nzeo sya Kĩevelania ila waumĩthisye.
^ kal. 7 Sisya maelesyo ma kelĩ ma kwongeleela ĩandĩkonĩ ya Esekieli 18:4 na Ũvoo wa Kwongeleela (Appendix 3B) nthĩnĩ wa Reference Bible.
^ kal. 9 Veonekana asomi nĩmaumĩthĩtye Mbivilia ya Ũtianĩo Mweũ kwa Kĩevelania. Ũmwe woo nĩ Simon Atoumanos, ũla weeyumĩtye vyũ maũndũnĩ ma ndĩni na wekalaa Byzantium, ta myakanĩ ya 1360. Ũngĩ eetawa Oswald Schreckenfuchs, na aĩ mũsomi kuma German, ta myakanĩ ya 1565. Mbivilia isu iyaaumĩthw'a nayu nĩsyaaie.

translation:
ARE WE wondering how the Bible came to be written in German? This is the story. And this is the oldest German Bible. Indeed, know the scholar named Elias Hutter, who lived from 1501-1600, and who printed the German Bible and helped establish the foundation for future Bibles.
Elias Hutter was born in 1553, in the town of Görlitz, which lies on the border between Germany and Poland and the Czech Republic. Hutter studied theology at the Lutheran University, Jena in the Middle East. And at age 24, he was appointed professor of theology in Leipzig. But he wanted to further his studies, so he became a teacher at a school in Nuremberg, where he taught Hebrew, Greek, Latin, and German grammar for several years. In addition, he attended other schools or universities like this one.
'THE HISTORY OF THE BIBLE'
In 1587, Hutter published the first complete German Bible in Wittenberg. The Bible had its own font and design, Derekh ha-Kodesh, based on Isaiah 35:8, and its title was "The Way of Holiness." The preface to the first Bible stated that all the designs or "everything in this Bible is designed to be beautiful." Indeed, the first Bible was very valuable and people used it to learn German.
It may be understood why the German Bible that Hutter published was so valuable; let us look at some things that make learning the Bible in German difficult. Firstly, German is written with many letters that are unfamiliar and difficult, and secondly, the font and style of the font can make it difficult to recognize the correct letter. It may be understood thus, the meaning of the German letter נפשׁ (pronounced ne'phesh), which means "soul." According to Ezekiel 18:4, the first letter of this letter is ה (ha), and all the letters connected to it form the letter הנפשׁ (han·ne'phesh), which also means "soul" (the soul). For those who do not understand well, the letter הנפשׁ (han·ne'phesh) seems very different from the letter נפשׁ (ne'phesh).
It may be that Hutter knew this, he used a method of marking vowels to help clarify words. He used Hebrew letters with signs above and below to indicate the vowel. He used signs above to write the root of a word. Then he used signs below to write the letters that are part of the root. This method helped people who knew the roots of German words, and this is how they clarified their understanding. And the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References uses this method too in some cases of added information. * The root is written with signs above, and the letters that are part of the root are also written with signs below. These methods are similar to how Hutter used them when explaining the writing of Ezekiel 18:4 in his German Bible, and this method is also used in the Reference Bible with added information on this matter.
THE GERMAN BIBLE OF "TRUE UNDERSTANDING"
Hutter discovered about 12 German Bibles that were earlier than the True Understanding. This Bible was published in Nuremberg in 1599, and it was called the Nuremberg Polyglot. Hutter wanted to revise the German Bible of Christian Greek Scriptures. But whether or not he succeeded in making it "more understandable," it became more accurate. * It seems he used the True Understanding Bible in German when revising the Christian Greek Scriptures. Hutter worked on other things too, and it took him one year!
What did Hutter actually translate from the Christian Greek Scriptures into German? One scholar named Franz Delitzsch wrote in 1891: "[The writings] that [Hutter] translated into German are so clear and precise that many Christians and even ordinary people can use them without difficulty, especially using only a few key words."
WHY IT WAS REJECTED BY THE MAJORITY
Hutter understood the importance of translating, and the Bibles he translated were very good. However, his work was opposed by others. For example, the German Bible of the True Understanding was reprinted in 1661 by William Robertson and in 1798 by Richard Caddick. Although he translated from the Christian Greek Scriptures, Hutter translated the important names Kyʹri·os (Lord) and The·osʹ (God) as "Jehovah" (יהוה, JHVH), while most translations of the German Bible did not or did not consistently use Jehovah. This is why many Bibles of the True Understanding use the name of God, but Hutter's Bible uses this name, and it has helped to restore the correct pronunciation of the name of God as it appeared in the Christian Greek Scriptures.
To find out what the name of God, Jehovah, means in the Christian Greek Scriptures, or to learn more about the reference material in the Reference Bible, compare the work of Elias Hutter with modern German Bibles that have been published.
^ See footnotes on pages 7 for information regarding Ezekiel 18:4 and the Appendix (Appendix 3B) in the Reference Bible.
^ See footnote 9. It seems scholars have studied the German Bible of the True Understanding. One of them was Simon Atoumanos, who lived in Constantinople and worked in Byzantium around 1360. Another was Oswald Schreckenfuchs, a German scholar, around 1565. This Bible continues to be studied today.

text:
Mũklĩsto nĩwaĩle kwĩkala na mũio wa kwĩyũkitĩa avithũkĩwa, ta ĩvuti kana vasitola?
Aklĩsto nĩmatonya kwosa matambya mana nĩ kana mesũvĩe, ĩndĩ mayosaa matambya me ũtee wa myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ. Myolooto ĩsu nĩvatĩte andũ kwĩkala na mĩio ya kaũ, ta vasitola, mavuti, na mĩio ĩngĩ ta ĩsu, me na kĩeleelo kya kwĩyũkitĩa makesa kũvithũkĩwa nĩ andũ angĩ. Kwasũanĩa myolooto ĩno ĩatĩĩe:
Yeova onaa thayũ wĩ mũtheu, na mũno mũno thayũ wa mũndũ. Ndaviti nĩweesĩ kana Yeova nĩwe "wĩ na mbuluti ya thayũ." (Sav. 36:9) Kwoou o na ethĩwa Mũklĩsto nũkwosa ĩtambya esũvĩe kana asũvĩe malĩ yake, ndaĩle kwĩsa kwosa ĩtambya yĩtonya kũtuma mũndũ ũngĩ akw'a, na kĩu kĩimũlikya ĩvĩtyonĩ ya kwĩtĩkya nthakame.—Kũt. 22:8; Sav. 51:14.
O na kau nĩ syĩndũ mbingĩ itonya kũtuma mũndũ etĩkya nthakame, nĩ laisi mũno kũaana ũtũmĩĩte ĩvuti, wĩthĩwe weeka ũu ũvangĩte kana ũtavangĩte. * Na eka ũu, ethĩwa ũla waũvithũkĩa nĩwoona ũkwete ĩvuti nake nĩ mũtelemu, maũndũ nĩmatonya kũthũka, na ti vinya kwĩthĩa ũmwe wenyu oaie ũla ũngĩ.
Ĩla Yesũ weeie aatĩĩi make makue mbyũ ũtukũ wa mũthya ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ, ndameaa makue nĩ kana maitũmĩe kwĩyũkitĩa. (Luka 22:36, 38) Yesũ ameie makue mbyũ nũndũ ve kĩla wendaa kũmamanyĩsya. Endaa kũmamanyĩsya kana mayaĩlĩte kwĩyũkitĩa, o na mavithũkĩwa nĩ nguthu ya andũ makuĩte mĩio ya kaũ. (Luka 22:52) Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩla Vetelo watemie ĩla ngombo ya mũthembi mũnene na ũvyũ Yesũ wamwĩie: "Tũngĩa ũvyũ waku vandũ vaw'o." Amina kũmũtavya ũu asyokie aweta mwolooto ũngĩ waaĩle kũatĩĩwa nĩ atĩĩi make kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ. Aisye: "Onthe ala makwataa ũvyũ makaanangwa na ũvyũ."—Mt. 26:51, 52.
Ĩandĩko ya Mika 4:3 yathanie kana andũ ma Ngai "makatusya mbyũ syoo itw'ĩke mĩthya ya maembe ma ng'ombe, na matumo moo tũvyũ twĩ ngoto twa ũsea." Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩ andũ ma mũuo, na kĩu kyosanĩte na ndeto ila mũtũmwa Vaulo waveveeiwe aandĩka. Atwĩkĩie vinya tũatĩĩe ndeto ii: "Mũikekũle kwa mũndũ o na wĩva. . . . Ethĩwa nũtonyeka, kwa ngalĩ ĩla yenyu, mwĩthĩwe na mũuo na andũ onthe." (Alo. 12:17, 18) Vaulo akomanie na mathĩna maingĩ mũno, o na nĩwakwatiwe nĩ "mĩisyo ya ing'ei." Ĩndĩ nĩwaatĩĩaa ndeto isu waandĩkie, na kwoou ndaaenda kwĩsũvĩa atũmĩĩte nzĩa ĩleanĩte na myolooto ya Maandĩko. (2 Ako. 11:26) Amwĩkwatisye Ngai na aatĩĩa ũĩ ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. Ũĩ ũsu "wĩ kavaa kwĩ mĩio ya kaũ."—Mũta. 9:18.
Aklĩsto monaa thayũ wĩ wa vata kwĩ syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ. Yesũ aisye: "Thayũ wa mũndũ ndumaa syĩndũnĩ syake." (Luka 12:15) Kwoou ethĩwa nĩwavithũkĩwa nĩ kĩng'ei kĩkuĩte mũio wa kaũ na watata kũneena nakyo nesa na kyaema, Mũklĩsto mũĩ aatĩĩaa mwolooto ũla wĩ ndetonĩ ii sya Yesũ: "Mũikakĩlan'ye vinya na mũndũ mũthũku." O na no ũmũekee kĩtonyeo kyaku na ngũa yaku ya ĩũlũ, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ũmũekee kyonthe kĩla ũkwenda kwosa. (Mt. 5:39, 40; Luka 6:29) * Ĩndĩ kĩndũ kĩla kĩseo vyũ kĩtonya kũũtethya nĩ kũtata ndũkeke kĩndũ kĩtonya kũtuma ũtw'ĩka wa kũatĩĩawa nĩ ing'ei. Tweesũvĩana na "wĩyĩan'yo wa thayũ," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kwĩyonany'a malĩ yitũ, na atũi maitũ mekala matwĩsĩ ta Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syendete mũuo, no kwĩthĩwa tũkaema kũatĩĩwa nĩ mbũlĩli.—1 Yoa. 2:16; Nth. 18:10.
Aklĩsto nĩmanengae ndaĩa mawasya ma ngoo ma ala angĩ. (Alo. 14:21) Aklĩsto amwe nĩmatonya kũseng'a mũno, o na makalulutĩka, mesa kũmanya kana ve Mũklĩsto ũngĩ kĩkundinĩ wĩkalaa na ĩvuti ya kwĩyũkitĩa avithũkĩwa nĩ andũ. Nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩtwendete ala angĩ, nĩtũsũanĩaa mawoni moo o na ethĩwa twĩekana na kĩndũ twĩsĩ nesa vyũ kana silikalĩ nĩtwĩtĩkĩlĩtye twĩthĩwe nakyo.—1 Ako. 10:32, 33; 13:4, 5.
Aklĩsto nĩmatataa methĩwe me ngelekany'o nzeo. (2 Ako. 4:2; 1 Vet. 5:2, 3) Ethĩwa Mũklĩsto nĩwanewa ũtao wa Maandĩko na ĩtina wa vau aendeea kwĩkala na ĩvuti ya kwĩyũkitĩa avithũkĩwa nĩ andũ, ndesa kũtalwa ta ngelekany'o nzeo. Nũndũ wa ũu, ndesa kũnengwa mawĩa kĩkundinĩ, kana akanewa ianda sya mwanya. Vethĩawa vailyĩ oou kwa Mũklĩsto ũla ũthũkũmaa wĩa ũũtuma ekala na ĩvuti. Ti kavaa akamantha wĩa wa mũthemba ũngĩ? *
Vate nzika, Mũklĩsto nĩwĩthĩawa na ũthasyo wa kũnyuva wĩa ũla ũkũthũkũma, ũthasyo wa kũmantha ũndũ ũkwĩsũvĩa, na ũndũ ũkũsũvĩa andũ make, kana malĩ yake. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩtũtetheeasya kwona ũndũ Ngai wĩ ũĩ wĩana na ũndũ ũtwendete. Aklĩsto ala me ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai nĩmanengete ndaĩa myolooto ĩsu. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩmatusaa kwĩkala mate na syĩndũ sya kwĩyũkitĩa, ta mavuti, mavithũkĩwa nĩ andũ. Nĩmesĩ kana ala monanasya kana nĩmamwĩkwatĩtye Ngai kwa kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia, nĩmo methĩawa na ũsũvĩo wa w'o na ũtakathela.—Sav. 97:10; Nth. 1:33; 2:6, 7.
^ kal. 3 Mũklĩsto nũtonya kwona nũseo ekale na ĩvuti, vasitola, kana mũio ũngĩ ta ũsu kwondũ wa nzyĩma kana kwĩsũvĩa ĩla wavithũkĩwa nĩ nyamũ sya kĩtheka. Ĩndĩ ĩla ũteũtũmĩa mĩio ta ĩsu nũseo akaumya isasi, kana o na akamĩsingũlany'a na aimĩvingĩa vaasa vyũ. Aklĩsto ala matwĩe nthĩ ila ivatĩte andũ kwĩkala na mavuti, kana syĩ na mĩao ĩngĩ ya ũko ũsu, nĩmaĩle kũatĩĩa mwĩao wa silikalĩ.—Alo. 13:1.
^ kal. 2 Ĩkaseti ya Amkeni! ya 08/03/1993 ungu wa kyongo, "Jinsi ya Kukinza Kunajisiwa," na ĩvuku Maswali Ambayo Vijana Huuliza—Majibu Yafanyayo Kazi, Ĩvuku ya 1, kĩlungu kya 32, ungu wa kyongo, "Ninawezaje Kujilinda na Washambuliaji wa Kingono?," nĩmonanĩtye ũndũ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩsũvĩa ndakavukw'e.
^ kal. 4 Wenda kũkwata ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa wĩa ũũtuma wĩkala na ĩvuti, no ũsisye ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 01/11/2005, ĩth. 31; na ya 15/12/1983, ĩth. 19-21.

translation:
A Christian might face the challenge of dealing with feelings of guilt, does this trouble you or others?
A Christian can often overcome bad habits, whether they are old or new, including those related to alcohol abuse which is common in Mbiviliani. Many people struggle with habits such as smoking, drinking, and other addictions, and with the desire to feel good which can lead to harmful behavior that others condemn. Let us examine this issue:
Jehovah sees everything clearly, and he understands human imperfection. David knew that Jehovah is the one "who is forgiving." (Ps. 36:9) Therefore, as a Christian, we should not be quick to judge someone who has made a mistake, but rather strive to avoid judging them in a way that could cause them pain and discourage them from repenting.—Prov. 22:8; Ps. 51:14.
There are many factors that can contribute to someone's wrongdoing, including a lack of proper training, personal weaknesses, and circumstances beyond their control. * But also, the influence of those around us can have a significant impact, both positive and negative.
However, Jesus was aware of the betrayal that Judas Iscariot would commit against him, yet he continued to associate with him. (Luke 22:36, 38) Jesus knew what Judas was planning, but he did not reveal it to prevent him from making his own choice, and because betrayers are often motivated by selfish desires. (Luke 22:52) This is why when Peter drew a sword to defend Jesus, Jesus told him: "Put your sword back in its place." Indeed, he allowed himself to be arrested so that the prophecies could be fulfilled. He said: "Am I not to drink from the cup that the Father has given me?"—Matt. 26:51, 52.
The prophecy in Micah 4:3 foretold that God's people would "beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks." Christians today are peaceful people, and this attitude is in harmony with what the apostle Paul wrote. He urged us to live peaceably with all men, saying: "Continue to love one another and to encourage one another." (1 Thess. 12:17, 18) Paul endured many hardships, and he was afflicted with "bodily discomforts." Yet, he continued to write encouraging letters, and he always sought to align his conduct with the teachings of the Scriptures. (2 Cor. 11:26) He appealed to God and asked for His strength. That strength "excelled in weakness."—2 Cor. 9:18.
A Christian may find himself in a difficult situation. Jesus said: "A man's enemies will be those of his own household." (Luke 12:15) But even when confronted with opposition from relatives who do not share our faith, a Christian can apply Jesus' principle: "Continue to give to whoever asks you." And whether it is a small request or a large one, continue to give generously. (Matt. 5:39, 40; Luke 6:29) * One reason why it is so important to maintain neutrality is to avoid being drawn into political affairs. We want to remain neutral, like those who are loyal to Jehovah's organization and desire to please him, and to avoid becoming involved in worldly things.—1 John 2:16; Prov. 18:10.
Christians are also willing to forgive offenses committed against them. (Acts 14:21) A Christian may have been wronged, perhaps deeply hurt, yet he strives to show mercy, remembering that fellow Christians may be imperfect and influenced by Satan. We should endeavor to be understanding toward others, avoiding harsh judgments, and recognizing that we too have imperfections and make mistakes.—1 Cor. 10:32, 33; Acts 13:4, 5.
Christians are also concerned about spiritual shepherds. (2 Tim. 4:2; 1 Pet. 5:2, 3) They appreciate that elders need Bible-based counsel and encouragement as they strive to shepherd God's flock, and they offer such support willingly. Furthermore, they are quick to comfort those who are discouraged or sick, or who are experiencing difficulties. Experienced ones know how to strengthen their brothers.—1 Thess. 5:14.
Indeed, Christians are motivated by love for God and for people. They want to help others understand the truth, and they desire to see people benefit from it materially and spiritually. In view of this, the example of the apostle Paul is encouraging, showing us how Jehovah views our ministry. Christians who are zealous in their service to God are eager to share the good news. But does this mean they condemn those who do not accept the message?—Rom. 9:3.
So, Christians are moved by a deep sense of urgency, a desire to defend the truth, and a concern for people's welfare, both material and spiritual. With this in mind, the account of Apollos is helpful in illustrating how God feels about our ministry. Christians who are devoted to God are willing to endure hardships, trials, and opposition. I ask myself, 'Am I determined to continue serving God faithfully despite obstacles, and am I cultivating a spirit of perseverance?'—Ps. 97:10; Luke 1:33; 2:6, 7.
^ par. 3 A Christian endeavors to remain neutral in political affairs, taking no part in war or violence, or in any activity that would compromise his integrity or bring reproach on God's name. He avoids becoming entangled in worldly affairs or aligning himself with political factions. Christians recognize that following this course may result in persecution, or even imprisonment. However, they maintain their neutrality, knowing that their allegiance is to God's Kingdom.—Acts 13:1.
^ par. 2 The article "How to Resist Sexual Temptation" in The Watchtower of March 8, 1993, and the book Questions Young People Ask—Answers That Work, Volume 1, page 32, under the heading "How Can I Protect Myself From Sexual Assault?" provide valuable guidance on how a person can protect himself.
^ par. 4 For further assistance in dealing with feelings of inferiority, please refer to the Kingdom Ministry (Swahili) of November 1, 2005, pages 31; and December 15, 1983, pages 19-21.

text:
Kwosana na ĩvuku yĩmwe, saenzi nĩ "kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ syĩndũ syũmbĩtwe, na ũndũ nthĩ na syĩndũ ila syĩ yayayanĩ iilyĩ kwa kũsisya syĩndũ isu nesa, kũithima, na kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli mũliku ĩũlũ wasyo, kwa kũtũmĩa masinĩ." Wĩa ũsu wĩ vinya mũno na mavinda maingĩ nũtũlaa mũndũ ngoo. Andũ ma saenzi matethasya wĩa ũsu kwa syumwa, myei, kana myaka. Mavinda amwe mokĩlaa moko mathei, ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ nĩmekaa maũndũ makatethya andũ. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii syĩ vaa ĩtheo.
Kambunĩ ĩmwe ya Europe nĩyavulanilye vulasitiki ĩla nzeo (strong plastic) na syĩndũ sya matukũ aa ila ikelaa kĩw'ũ (filters), na yaseũvya masinĩ nzeo ya kĩw'ũ ĩla ĩtetheeasya andũ maikakwatwe nĩ mowau ala maetawe nĩ kũnyw'a kĩw'ũ kĩthũku. Masinĩ ta isu nitũmĩkaa ĩla kweethĩwa na mĩisyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩyatũmĩiwe mwaka wa 2010 nthĩ ya Haiti ĩla kweethĩiwe kĩthingitho.
Yayayanĩ ve satellites mbingĩ ila ithũkũmaa vamwe, na nĩsyo iseũvĩtye kĩla kĩtawa Global Positioning System (GPS). O na kau GPS yaseũvĩtw'e ĩtetheesye ita sya kaũ, yu nĩtũmĩawa kũtetheesya atwai ma ndeke, ngalĩ, na meli, o na nĩtetheeasya asyĩmi na alĩsi ma iĩma nĩ kana mamanye nzĩa nesa. Andũ ma saenzi nĩmeekie nesa mũno kũseũvya GPS nũndũ nĩtetheeasya andũ kũvika vala mekwenda kũthi.
Nĩwĩthĩwa ũtũmĩaa simũ, kombiũta, kana Indaneti? Nĩwĩthĩwa ũnaĩ mũwau na ũkatũmĩa ndawa sya matukũ aa na ikaũtetheesya? Nũendaa kũndũ na ndeke? Ethĩwa nĩwĩkaa maũndũ asu, nũtanĩĩte maũndũ amwe maseo ala saenzi ĩetee andũ. Vate nzika, saenzi nĩetee andũ maũndũ maingĩ maseo.
MAŨNDŨ ALA SAENZI ĨTESA KWĨKA
Nũndũ wa kwenda kwongela ũmanyi ũla me naw'o, andũ ma saenzi nĩmaendeee kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli mwingĩ ĩũlũ wa wũmbi. Andũ ala masomaa physics ya niũkĩlĩa (nuclear) nĩmekaa ũkunĩkĩli mwingĩ mayenda kũmanya ũndũ atomu (atom) ĩthũkũmaa. Namo ala mekaa ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila syĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, na ila syĩ yayayanĩ (astrophysicists), nĩmekaa ũkunĩkĩli nĩ kana mamanye vala syaumie. O ũndũ andũ ma saenzi maendeee kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli mũno, o na ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila itonekaa na itatonya kũkwatwa, now'o amwe moo maasya kana ethĩwa Ngai ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ e vo, nĩmaĩle kũmwona.
Namo asomi na andũ amwe ma saenzi me nguma maendete mbeange wa vau. Vandũ va kũtũmĩa saenzi kũĩkĩĩthya kana kwĩ Ngai, mamĩtũmĩĩaa kũĩkĩĩthya andũ kana kũi Ngai o tondũ mũandĩki ũmwe wa saenzi wĩtawa Amir D. Aczel waisye. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũsomi ũmwe wa physics aisye atĩĩ: "Kwĩthĩwa vate ũndũ ũtonya kũĩkĩĩthya kwĩ Ngai ũthĩnĩkĩaa syĩndũ ila syĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, nĩ ũkũsĩ mwĩanĩu wa kwonany'a kana kũi ngai ta ũsu." Angĩ namo monaa wĩa wa Ngai ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ ta o "kyama" kana "maũndũ matatonya kwĩkĩka." *
Ĩndĩ ve ĩkũlyo yĩĩ andũ maĩle kwĩkũlya: Mo andũ ma saenzi nĩmemanyĩĩtye nesa vyũ ũkethĩa no meke motwi matesa kwĩkĩwa nzika? Ũsũngĩo nĩ aiee. Andũ ma saenzi nĩmekĩte maendeeo maingĩ mũno ĩndĩ aingĩ moo nĩmesĩ nesa kana ve maũndũ maingĩ matesĩ, o na angĩ matonya kũlea kwĩsa kũmamanya. O na mũsomi ũmwe wa physics ũla nĩ mũsindi wa Nobel, wĩtawa Steven Weinberg aisye atĩĩ: "Tuikesa kũmanya maũndũ nesa vyũ." Aisye ũu aineena ĩũlũ wa wũmbi. O nake Professor Martin Rees, ũla nĩ Astronomer Royal wa Great Britain, aandĩkie ũũ: "Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa ve maũndũ andũ matakesa kũelewa." Ũw'o nĩ kana, andũ ma saenzi mayaaĩsa kũmanya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa wũmbi, twambĩĩe na twĩndũ tũnini tũla tũseũvĩtye syĩndũ ila syĩ thayũ (cells), nginya syĩndũ nene ta nthĩ na yayaya. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii syĩ vaa ĩtheo:
Andũ ala masomaa syĩndũ ila syĩ thayũ (biologists) mayĩeleawa nesa kĩla kĩendeeaa nthĩnĩ wa tũla twĩndũ tũnini tũseũvĩtye syĩndũ ila syĩ thayũ. O na ĩngĩ, mayaaĩsa kũmanya nesa ũndũ twĩndũ tu tũtũmĩaa vinya ũla twakwata kuma mwĩĩnĩ, ũndũ tumasya proteins, na ũndũ tũaanĩkaa.
Vinya ũla ũtumaa syĩndũ syekw'a ĩũlũ isyoka nthĩ, nũtũmĩkaa kĩla ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ asomi ma physics mayaaĩsa kũũelewa nesa. Mayaaĩsa kũmanya nesa ũndũ vinya ũsu ũtũngaa mũndũ nthĩ ĩla weeyĩkya, kana ũndũ ũtumaa mwei ũatĩĩa nzĩa yaw'o (orbit) ĩla ũthyũlũlũkĩte nthĩ.
Andũ ala masomaa ĩũlũ wa vala nthĩ na yayaya syaumie (cosmologists) maasya kana 95 katĩ wa 100 ya syĩndũ ila iseũvĩtye nthĩ na yayaya iyonekaa o na matũmĩĩte masinĩ sya saenzi. Maaanĩtye syĩndũ isu kũndũ kwĩlĩ, dark matter na dark energy. Ĩndĩ mayĩsĩ ũndũ syĩndũ isu iilyĩ.
Ve maũndũ angĩ andũ ma saenzi matamesĩ na mamasaanĩasya. Kũmanya ũu kũtonya kũtũtethya ata? Mũandĩki ũmwe wa saenzi wĩsĩkĩe mũno aisye atĩĩ: "Maũndũ ala tũtesĩ nĩmo maingĩ kwĩ ala twĩsĩ. Saenzi yaĩle kũtuma mũndũ atana na akaseng'a, na ũu waĩle kũtuma enda kũmanya maũndũ maingangĩ."
Kwoou, ethĩwa wĩĩkũlya kana saenzi yĩ vakuvĩ kwosa mwanya wa Mbivilia na ĩituma andũ maeka kũmũĩkĩĩa Ngai, sũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Andũ ala oĩ mũno ma saenzi matũmĩĩte masinĩ syĩ vinya mũno na makamanya tũmaũndũ tũnini ĩũlũ wa wũmbi. Ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, wĩona tamesa kũmanya maũndũ ala matesa kũmanyĩka mũndũ atũmĩĩte masinĩ sya saenzi? Ĩtina wa ĩvuku yĩtawa Encyclopedia Britannica kũneenea kwa ũliku ĩũlũ wa isitoli na maendeeo ala mekĩtwe nĩ andũ ala masomaa ndata yaisye atĩĩ: "Ĩtina wa myaka vakuvĩ 4,000 ya kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na yayaya, tũi kĩvathũkany'o na andũ ma tene ma Mbaviloni ala meesĩ maũndũ manini mũno vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na yayaya."
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩthĩawa syĩsĩ kana kĩla mũndũ e na ũthasyo wa kwĩyĩkĩa ũtwi ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu. Nĩtwendaa mũno kũatĩĩa ũtao ũũ wa Mbivilia: "Wũmĩĩsyo wenyu ũmanyĩke nĩ andũ onthe." (Avilivi 4:5) Twĩ na woni o ta ũsu, nĩtũũmũthokya mũsome ĩũlũ wa ũndũ saenzi na Mbivilia ikwatĩanĩaa.
^ kal. 9 Andũ amwe maleanaa na Mbivilia nũndũ wa momanyĩsyo ma tene, na ma ĩvinda yĩĩ ma makanisa. Momanyĩsyo amwe nĩ ta, nthĩ nĩyo yĩ katĩkatĩ wa syĩndũ syonthe ila syĩ yayayanĩ na kana Ngai oombie syĩndũ syonthe kwa mĩthenya thanthatũ ya masaa 24.—Sisya ĩsandũkũ yĩ na kyongo ""Mbivilia na Maũndũ ma W'o ma Saenzi."

With sorrow and a dream, science is "to understand the nature of a difficult problem, and the thing with problems unless it spreads well to stop the same issue now, to heal it, and to avoid excessive consumption of water, using machines." Many people suffer greatly with many diseases because of this person. People who study science help many people through pain, tears, or years. Some diseases kill many people, while many diseases cause suffering to people. Fortunately, this does not happen often.
One European country recycles strong plastic and things like old clothes (filters), and cleans strong water filters that help people who are affected by dirty water which they get from drinking unclean water. These machines are very useful and can be used easily. For example, they were used in 2010 during the earthquake in Haiti to clean water.
Satellites orbit above us, and that's what powers the Global Positioning System (GPS). And with GPS technology helping them, they can track the location of cars, ships, and planes, and also help farmers and others find their way easily. Scientists have worked hard to make GPS so that it helps people reach where they want to go.
Do you use a phone, computer, or internet? Do you have a car and use fuel and it helps you travel? Do you travel by plane? These are some things we have, but let's remember some things that science has done for people. Truly, science has done many good things for people.
OTHER THINGS SCIENCE HAS DONE
In order to explain something to you, scientists continue to research more and more about the world. People who study nuclear physics have researched a lot to understand how an atom works. Others who research about matter, including solid matter, and those astrophysicists, have researched and perhaps know much about space. And the things scientists continue to research more and more, and the matter that seems and doesn't seem to be touched, sometimes even people who believe in God who was revealed to Moses, try to see him.
Also, some scholars and some scientists say they have gone beyond limits. People use science to prove or disprove God, they try to prove people or disprove God, as one scientist named Amir D. Aczel said. For example, one physicist said: "Believing that something can't be proven to God, which researches about matter including solid matter, is just a matter of perspective or disbelieving in God." But also seeing the God who was revealed to Moses is like seeing a "mystery" or "things that are hard to understand." *
Indeed, there are many questions people ask themselves: Do scientists really know anything substantial or are they just guessing when they talk about origins? The answer is yes. Scientists have made many advances over time and often they don't know much or they have many guesses, but they can still learn to understand. Also, one physicist who won the Nobel Prize, named Steven Weinberg said: "We don't know anything substantial." He said this because of his humility. And also Professor Martin Rees, who is the Astronomer Royal of Great Britain, writes this: "It is impossible to know things that people struggle to understand." That is, scientists admit they don't know many things, we see and hear big things that we only research about cells, then bigger things like planets and galaxies. To illustrate this point further:
People who study cells (biologists) don't fully understand everything about how those small things work. And also, they admit they don't know what things we use daily, such as proteins, and what happens.
The forces that make cells function properly, happen constantly. Indeed, physicists admit they don't understand them. They don't know what force makes an object fall down, or what causes a moon to move in its orbit.
People who study the origin of the universe (cosmologists) say that 95 out of 100 of the things in the universe are invisible and we don't know their composition using scientific instruments. Meaning there are things we don't see, dark matter and dark energy. Indeed, they don't know what those things are.
But many scientists research and investigate. Is knowing this going to help us somehow? One science writer once said: "What we don't know is much more than what we know. Science has made people skeptical, and this has made them want to learn more."
However, some wonder whether science goes too far when it contradicts the Bible and leads people to reject God, saying this: People who use scientific instruments often come up with theories about the origin of the universe. Some believe this, but does it really help someone understand something using scientific instruments? The encyclopedia Britannica states regarding the history of astronomy and developments made that: "For nearly 4,000 years of recorded history, knowledge of the heavens was advanced by the Babylonians who made significant observations about the stars and planets."
Jehovah's Witnesses believe that everyone has the right to examine matters for themselves. We appreciate this statement from the Bible: "Your own understanding will help you." (Proverbs 4:5) If you wish, we can discuss the relationship between science and the Bible further.
^ par. 9 Some have approached the Bible with a spirit of investigation, and they have found it to be reliable information like those in churches. One observation is that the earth is round, not flat, and that God created everything in six periods of time of 24 hours each.—See the box "The Bible and Science."

text:
Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũtetheesye ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala mathũawa nĩ mauta me mũuke?
Ala mathũawa nĩ mĩuke methĩawa me thĩnanĩ mũnene. Na mũno mũno vethĩawa vate ũndũ meka makesianĩa na mĩuke nũndũ kĩla mũthenya makomanaa na andũ me kĩvathũkany'o. O na amwe nĩmethĩĩtwe maikũlya ethĩwa no vatonyeke ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa makakũlw'a maeke kwĩvuva mauta me mũuke ĩla meũthi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi na maũmbanonĩ manene.
Vate nzika vai Mũklĩsto wĩsa kwĩka na ngenda ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma ũla ũngĩ ew'a e thĩnanĩ ĩla wooka ũmbanonĩ. Na ũu nĩ w'o nũndũ vai mũndũ ũtendaa kũthangaaw'a nĩ maũmbano. (Aevl. 10:24, 25) Kwoou nũseo ũla ũthũawa nĩ mĩuke nginya ũkethĩa nũkũemwa nĩ kũthi ũmbanonĩ akaneena na atumĩa ma kĩkundi. Kwĩkĩĩa andũ mĩao ĩũlũ wa kũtũmĩa mauta me mũuke ti ũndũ wosanĩte na Maandĩko na ti ũndũ waĩle, ĩndĩ atumĩa nĩmatonya kũtetheesya kĩkundi kĩelewe thĩna ũla ũkwataa ala mathũawa nĩ mĩuke. Atumĩa nĩmatonya kũtw'a kũneenea maũvoo ala maneeneete ũndũ ũsu ĩvinda ya Ũmbano wa Ũthũkũmi kĩlungunĩ kya mavata ma kĩkundi, ethĩwa ũu nĩwaĩle kĩkundinĩ kyoo, kana makatangasa kwa ũĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu. * Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana atumĩa maĩle kũtindaa mayumya imanyĩthya sya mũthemba ũsu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ kĩla ĩvinda andũ ala mekwendeew'a na aeni nĩmokaa ũmbanonĩ, na mayĩthĩawa mesĩ mathĩna ma kĩkundi, na tũitonya kwenda mew'e mate eanĩe. O na ĩngĩ, ti ũseo kũtuma ala mevuvaa mauta mate mũuke mwingĩ mew'a mate eanĩe.
Ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka atumĩa no meke mũvango ala methĩawa na thĩna ũsu makavathĩwa vandũ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ vala makekalaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, no mekalae lumunĩ matonya kwĩw'a kĩla kĩũneenwa ĩla ũmbano ũendeee. Ethĩwa ũu ndũtonyeka na thĩna ũsu wĩ o vo, kĩkundi nĩkĩtonya kũlekoti maũmbano kana kũvanga ala me na thĩna ũsu methukĩĩsye ũmbano maitũmĩa simũ me mũsyĩ kwoo, o tondũ vekawa kwondũ wa ala matatonya kuma mũsyĩ.
Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ, Ũthũkũmi Witũ wa Ũsumbĩ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ũyĩkĩa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa vinya masũanĩe ala angĩ ũndũnĩ ũsu ĩla meũthi maũmbanonĩ manene ma mĩthenya ĩtatũ. Nũndũ kũndũ kwingĩ maũmbano asu mekĩawa nyũmbanĩ nthĩnĩ, ala meũthi maũmbanonĩ asu nĩmakũlaw'a maikatũmĩe mũno mauta me mũuke mwingĩ. Mũno mũno twĩawa ũu ĩla tũũthi maũmbanonĩ manene ma mĩthenya ĩtatũ nũndũ ve vinya kũvatha vandũ vate mĩuke vatonya kwĩkalwa nĩ ala me thĩna ũsu. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũsu ndũandĩkawa nĩ kana ũtw'ĩke mwĩao wa kũatĩĩwa ikundinĩ, na ndwaĩle kwoswa ũu.
Nũndũ twĩkalĩte nthĩ ĩte nzeo, tũilea kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna ala maumanaa na naĩ ĩla twatiĩwe. Kwondũ wa ũu, nĩtũtũngaa mũvea mũno ĩla angĩ meekĩa kĩthito nĩ kana matũtetheesye tũikathĩne mũno. Nĩ kana wĩthĩe mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa ndethĩna ĩla wooka ũmbanonĩ, nĩtũtonya kũtw'a kwĩvata mauta me mũuke mwingĩ. Ũsu ti ũndũ wĩ vinya ethĩwa nĩtwendete ala angĩ.
Eka Mbivilia, ve syĩndũ ingĩ iĩkĩĩthasya kana Vondio Vilato aĩ kw'o?
Vondio Vilato esĩkĩe nĩ asomi ma Mbivilia nũndũ wa kĩla weekie ĩvinda ya kũsilĩlwa na kũawa kwa Yesũ. (Mt. 27:1, 2, 24-26) Ĩndĩ ĩsyĩtwa yake nĩyonekete mavinda kauta syĩndũnĩ ingĩ sya ĩvinda yĩu. Kwosana na ĩvuku yĩmwe, ũvoo ũla ũandĩkĩtwe ĩũlũ wake syĩndũnĩ sya tene nĩ "mwingĩ kwĩ wa ngavana Mũlomi o na wĩva wa kĩsio kya Yutia."—The Anchor Bible Dictionary.
Ĩsyĩtwa ya Vilato nĩyonekaa kaingĩ mavukunĩ maandĩkiwe nĩ mũsomi wa maũndũ ma tene ũla waĩ Mũyuti na weetawa Josephus. Awetie mavinda atatũ ĩla Vilato wavonee syũa ĩasa e ngavana wa Yutia. Nayo ĩvinda ya kana yaandĩkiwe nĩ Philo, Mũyuti o ũngĩ waĩ mũsomi wa maũndũ ma tene. Nake mũandĩki Mũlomi weetawa Tacitus, ũla waandĩkie maũndũ ma tene makonetye atongoi ma Lomi, nĩwaandĩkie kana Vondio Vilato nĩwe waumisye mwĩao Yesũ oawe ĩla Tivelio wasumbĩkĩte.
Mwakanĩ wa 1961, akunĩkĩli ma maũndũ ma tene mayĩnza vandũ ve Kaisalea, Isilaeli, vala veekĩawa mathaũ tene nĩ Alomi, nĩmoonie ĩvia yĩ na ĩsyĩtwa ya Vilato kwa kĩthyomo kya Latin. Visa ũũ (wĩ vaa) nĩ kĩlungu kya ĩvia yĩu na kyonekaa ta kyaandĩkĩtwe atĩĩ: "Kwa ngai syaĩle kũnengwa ndaĩa (mwako ũũ) Tiberieum Vondio Vilato, Mũnene wa Yutia, nũwumĩtye." Mwako ũla wawetawa vau no wĩthĩwe waĩ ĩkalũ yaakĩtwe kwondũ wa kũmũkatha Tivelio, ũla waĩ mũsumbĩki wa Lomi.
We mũndũ mũka mũtavany'a wa Ũsumbĩ nĩwaĩle kwĩvwĩka mũtwe ĩla ũkũmanyĩsya mũndũ Mbivilia ve mũtavany'a mũndũũme?
Kĩlungu kya "Makũlyo Kuma kwa Asomi Maitũ" ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 15/07/2002 (Kĩswaili) kyawetie kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa nĩwaĩle kwĩvw'ĩka mũtwe ĩla ũkũmanyĩsya mũndũ ve mũtavany'a mũndũũme, mũtavany'a ũsu mũndũũme ethĩwe nĩ mũvatise kana ti mũvatise. Ĩtina wa kũsũanĩa ũndũ ũsu nesa ve vata wa kũvĩndũa maũndũ amwe.
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa aĩle kwĩvw'ĩka mũtwe ĩla ũkũmanyĩsya mũndũ matũaa memanyĩasya ethĩwa ve mũtavany'a mũndũũme mũvatise. Eeka ũu ethĩawa ayonany'a kana nũnengete ndaĩa ũkũmũ ũla Yeova wiĩte kĩkundinĩ nũndũ eanĩsya wĩa waĩle kwĩthĩwa ũitethw'a nĩ mwana-a-asa ũsu. (1 Ako. 11:5, 6, 10) Ethĩwa ti ũu, no atavye ũ mwana-a-asa amanyĩsye mũmanyĩw'a ne we, ethĩwa nĩwaĩle na no atonye.
Ĩndĩ ethĩwa mwĩĩtu-a-asa emanyĩsya mũndũ matũaa memanyĩasya na ve mũtavany'a mũndũũme ũte mũvatise, na ũte mũũme wake, ti lasima kwosana na Maandĩko evw'ĩke mũtwe. O na vailyĩ ũu, eĩtu-a-asa amwe nĩmatonya kũsukumwa nĩ wasya woo wa ngoo mevw'ĩke mũtwe o na ethĩwa ti lasima kwosana na Maandĩko.
^ kal. 4 Nĩ kana ũmanye maũndũ maingangĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũũ, sisya "ũvoo wĩ na kyongo "Kuwasaidia Walio na MCS" ĩkasetinĩ ya Amkeni! ya 08/08/2000, ĩthangũ ya 8-10.
