We wonder if it is possible we are deceiving children and their possessions while people are asking about mature things?
But people are mature with matters of great importance. And often those things cause problems and maturity comes with every day's experience with people who understand. And some have been shown how to eat food and they don't deceive children and their possessions because of difficult situations caused by small groups and large groups.
They went somewhere, Christians, to ask if it is possible to make something happen to help someone reach an important place, but it was blocked by a group. And this is why someone who wants to progress is involved in gatherings. (Acts 10:24, 25) So then, those things which are mature should be understood with appreciation by leaving the gathering and sending small groups. To encourage people to use mature things is not right according to the Scriptures and is wrong, since those using them can deceive a group so that it understands what holds people back, but people are mature. Those using them can take advantage of opportunities, but this situation is like the Kingdom Hall being filled with furniture from small groups, and this is wrong today, or it could be discussed in a way that causes this situation. * Since this is not a reason for those using it to reject good advice from a faithful brother. Why? Because every time people who want to move forward and others remain in a gathering, and there are many issues with small groups, and we wonder if we should go elsewhere. And also, it is not right to make people use mature things more than necessary elsewhere.
However, they should allow those using them to have some influence on you, and those who oppose them should be forgiven. For example, they can learn something about how a gathering proceeds. However, this should not cause you to let a group decide whether to involve people or exclude people who are against you, or to send someone to speak badly about them, or to act unfairly towards them.
In recent years, our Almighty God has shown concern for both young and old because of the serious problems caused by large gatherings. Because many gatherings have become places where people misuse mature things greatly. This is why we need to remember that large gatherings can only benefit people when they allow mature people to associate with those who are against us. Regarding this matter, it is written so that we can think about its importance, and it is right to do so.
Therefore, if we remain firm in what is righteous, we will avoid being influenced by wrong things and people, and we will be guided. In view of this, we can find ways to help others see the truth without forcing them. If someone—young or old—questions why a gathering is held, we can explain the benefits of associating with mature people. It is not right to behave like those who oppose us.
But according to the Bible, was Pilate really innocent, or was Pontius Pilate guilty?
Pontius Pilate knew that the Bible spoke of Jesus' suffering and death, yet he allowed him to be crucified. (Matt. 27:1, 2, 24-26) But his innocence became apparent in light of other evidence. As one scholar put it, "the account shows that he acted more like a political pragmatist than a moral idealist."—The Anchor Bible Dictionary.
Pilate's innocence is also evident from the writings of historians such as the Jew Josephus. He gives an account of three instances where Pilate showed harshness toward the Jews. Also, there is an account by Philo, another Jew and historian. And the Roman historian Tacitus, who wrote about Roman emperors, mentions that Pontius Pilate caused trouble over the banner depicting Caesar.
In 1961, archaeologists excavating the ruins of Caesarea, Israel, discovered a stone inscription bearing Pilate's name. The inscription (shown here) is part of a dedication and reads: "To the emperor Tiberius Augustus [Tiberium], Pontius Pilate, prefect of Judea." This discovery confirms that Pilate was governor of Judea when Jesus was executed.
Would a guilty person have bothered to investigate whether the Bible's account of his trial was accurate?
The article "Archaeology Confirms the Bible," in the July 15, 2002, issue of Awake! (Swahili), stated that evidence suggests that a governor would be concerned about how he was viewed by Rome and would want to avoid causing trouble. Whether or not a governor was actually guilty could depend on how he handled matters.
Evidence suggests that a governor would be concerned about maintaining peace and would not want to cause unrest unless absolutely necessary. In this regard, he might consider what Jehovah considers important and try to act in a way that would please him. (1 Cor. 11:5, 6, 10) Otherwise, he might face consequences, and he would not want that to happen.
However, if a governor were determined to condemn someone despite a lack of evidence, and also condemned his family, he would be acting contrary to the Scriptures. And yet some governors have been influenced by their own personal interests and have acted contrary to the Scriptures.
^ par. 4 If you know more about this subject, see the August 8, 2000, issue of Awake!, pages 8-10, under the heading "Helping Those With MCS."

text:
Mũndũ no asũanĩe kana woni ũla ũeleetye ĩũlũ wa aũme ana ala makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi wĩ vinya kũeleeka na nĩ wa kũtelemya, ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o vailyĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Mbivilia, vamwe na maũndũ ala mekĩkĩte ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ nĩmatũtetheeasya kũmanya kĩla ũmwe wa aũme asu makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi onanasya ata. O na kau woni wa mbalasi isu na ala makuĩtwe nĩsyo wĩonany'a maũndũ mathũku mekwĩkĩka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, no wĩthĩwe wĩ ũvoo mũseo kwaku na andũ ma mũsyĩ waku. Ũu ũtonyeka ata? Mbee, ekai tũneenee kĩla kyonanaw'a nĩ aũme ana ala makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi isu.
ŨLA ŨKUĨTWE NĨ MBALASI NZAŨ
Woni ũsu wambĩĩe na ndeto ii: "Na noona, na sisya, mbalasi nzaũ, na ũla ũmĩtũlĩte aĩ na ũta; na anengwa ngovia ya ũsumbĩ: na aumaala aikĩlan'ya, na nĩ kana akĩlan'ye."
Nũũ ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi nzaũ? Kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya kũmanya ũndũ ũsu nĩ ndeto ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ o yĩu ya Ũvuan'yo ila imwĩtĩte ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi ĩsu "Ndeto ya Ngai." (Ũvuan'yo 19:
Nũũ ũnengete Yesũ ũkũmũ wa kũsinda? (Ũvuan'yo 6:2) Mwathani Ndanieli oonie woninĩ Masia, ũla ũelekanĩtw'e na "mwana wa mũndũ" ainengwa "ũsumbĩko, na ndaĩa, na ũsumbĩ" nĩ "mũtumĩa wa matukũ," ũla nĩ Yeova Ngai. * (Ndanieli 7:
Nĩ ĩndĩĩ aũme asu mambĩĩie kũkuwa nĩ mbalasi? Mũndũũme wa mbee, ũla nĩ Yesũ, ambĩĩie ĩla wanengiwe ngovia ya ũsumbĩ. (Ũvuan'yo 6:2) Yesũ atw'ĩkĩthiw'e Mũsumbĩ ĩtunĩ ĩndĩĩ? Ndaatw'ĩkĩthw'a Mũsumbĩ ĩla wasyokie ĩtunĩ oou ĩtina wa kũthayũũkw'a. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana vaĩ ĩvinda ya kweteela kuma asyoka ĩtunĩ. (Aevelania 10:
Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ maũndũ mathũkĩĩe vandũ va kũseũva kuma ĩla Yesũ watw'ĩkĩthiw'e Mũsumbĩ mwakanĩ wa 1914? Kĩtumi nũndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu Yesũ ambĩĩie kũsumbĩka ĩtunĩ, ĩndĩ ti kũũ nthĩ. Atw'ĩkĩthw'a Mũsumbĩ, kaũ nĩwookĩlile ĩtunĩ, na Yesũ, ũla wĩtĩtwe Mikaeli, amwĩkya Satani vamwe na ndaimoni syake kũũ nthĩ. (Ũvuan'yo 12:
ŨLA ŨKUĨTWE NĨ MBALASI NDUNE
"Na mbalasi ĩngĩ ndune yaumaala: na ũla ũmĩtũlĩte anengwa kũveta mũuo kũũ nthĩ, nĩ kana moaane ene kwa ene: na anengwa ũvyũ mũnene."
Ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi ĩno onanasya kaũ. Aendeee kũvetanga mũuo nthĩ yonthe, ĩndĩ ti isio imwe sya nthĩ. Kwa ĩvinda ya mbee kuma nthĩ yoombwa, kaũ nĩwokitiwe nthĩ yonthe mwakanĩ wa 1914. Kaũ wa kelĩ wa nthĩ yonthe nĩwaatĩĩie, naw'o nĩwaetie wanangĩko mũnenange. Kũtw'ĩkĩkanaa kana andũ ala makw'ĩte nũndũ wa makaũ kuma mwaka wa 1914 nĩ mbee wa milioni 100! Na ve andũ angĩ aingĩ maũmĩie mũno nũndũ wa makaũ.
Kaũ wingĩvĩte ata ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ? Kwa ĩvinda ya mbee, mũndũ nĩwonanĩtye e na ũtonyi wa kũmina andũ onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. O na ngwatanĩo ila isũvĩaa mũuo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, ta Ngwatanĩo ya Nthĩ (UN), niemetwe nĩ kũsiĩĩa mũtwai wa mbalasi ndune.
ŨLA ŨKUĨTWE NĨ MBALASI NZIŨ
"Na noona, na sisya, mbalasi nziũ; na ũla ũmĩtũlĩte aĩ na kĩthimi kw'okonĩ kwake. Na neew'a ta wasya katĩ wa ila syũmbe inya syĩ thayũ ũkyasya, Kĩvava kya nganũ nĩ silingi, na ivava itatũ sya mbaale nĩ silingi na mauta na mbinyu ndũkaithũkye."
Ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi ĩno onanasya yũa. Woni ũsu wĩonany'a kana kwĩ ũnyivu wa lĩu nũndũ kĩvava (kĩlo 0.7) kya nganũ kĩthoow'a silingi kana ndinalĩ ĩmwe, ĩla yaĩ mũsaala wa mũthenya ũmwe ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa! (Mathayo 20:2) Ndinalĩ ĩmwe yaĩ ĩtonya kũthooa ivava itatũ (kĩlo 2.1) sya mbaale, na mbaale yoonekaa ĩte nzeo ta nganũ. Lĩu wĩana ũu wesaa kũĩthya mũsyĩ mũnene kwa ĩvinda yĩana ata? Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ, andũ meawa kana maĩle kũtũmĩa syĩndũ nesa vamwe na malĩu ala matũmĩaa kĩla mũthenya, na ũu nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ ĩvindanĩ ya tene andũ maaĩle kũtũmĩa nesa syĩndũ ila sya vata ta mauta na mbinyu.
Yo ve maũndũ mekĩkĩte kuma mwaka wa 1914 matũĩkĩĩthasya kana mũndũũme ũsu no ũendeee kũkuwa nĩ mbalasi nziũ? Ĩĩ me vo! Andũ ta milioni 70 nĩmakwie nũndũ wa yũa myakanĩ ya 1901-2000. Ngwatanĩo ĩmwe yoonanisye kana "andũ milioni 805, ala nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na mũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa andũ kenda ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, makwataa kalĩu kanini mũno myakanĩ ya 2012-
ŨLA ŨKUĨTWE NĨ MBALASI YA LANGI WA MŨKŨYŨ KANA MŨTUKU
"Na noona, na sisya, mbalasi yĩ mũkũyũ: na ũla ũmĩtũlĩte, syĩtwa yake nĩ kĩkw'ũ; na Mbũa yaatĩanĩe nake. Nao manengwa ũkũmũ ĩũlũ wa kĩlungu kya kana kya nthĩ, moae na ũvyũ, na yũa, na kĩkw'ũ, na nyamũ mbai sya nthĩ."
Ũla ũkuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi ya kana onanasya kĩkw'ũ nũndũ wa mowau mathũku kana o maũndũ angĩ. Kavinda kanini ĩtina wa mwaka wa 1914, ũwau wĩtawa Spanish flu nĩwooaie andũ milioni mbingĩ. Nĩvatonyeka andũ ta milioni 500 makethĩwa makwatiwe nĩ ũwau ũsu, na ũu nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya, mũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa kĩla andũ atatũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu aĩ na ũwau ũsu!
Ĩndĩ ũwau ũsu wa Spanish flu waĩ o mwambĩlĩlyo. Asomi matalĩthasya kana andũ milioni maana maingĩ nĩmakwie nũndũ wa ũwau wĩtawa ndũng'ũ (smallpox) myakanĩ ya 1901-2000. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmakusaa nũndũ wa ũkimwi, ũwau wa kĩthũi (tuberculosis), na ndetema, o na kau andũ nĩmatatĩte kũmantha nzĩa nzeango sya ũiiti.
Maũndũ asu twaneenea ta kaũ, ũnyivu wa lĩu, kana mowau mathũku, onthe maetae kĩkw'ũ. Andũ onthe makw'a maendaa Mbũanĩ na ndĩsaa kũmanenga wĩkwatyo.
VE ĨVINDA ĨSEO YŨKĨTE!
Ĩvinda yĩla yĩ kw'o ya mathĩna yĩkilyĩ kũthela. Lilikana kana Yesũ aendie "aikĩlan'ya" mwaka wa 1914, na amwĩkya Satani kũũ nthĩ, ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaamina kũkĩlany'a kwake ĩvindanĩ yĩu. (Ũvuan'yo 6:2; 12:
Vandũ va kaũ kũkeethĩwa mũuo. Yeova akatuma "makaũ mathela kũvika kĩtulu kya nthĩ; nũtũlaa ũta, na ĩtumo aitilanga ilungu." (Savuli 46:9) Namo andũ ala mendete mũuo, "makeetan'ya mũuonĩ mwingĩ."
Vandũ va mayũa, kũkeethĩwa lĩu mwingĩ mũno. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũkeethĩwa lĩu mwingĩ wa mbaa ngetha nthĩ iĩmanĩ ĩũlũ."
Vandũ va mowau na kĩkw'ũ, andũ onthe makeethĩwa na ũima wa mwĩĩ na thayũ ũtathela. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai "akavyaĩa methoi onthe methonĩ moo; na kĩkw'ũ kĩikethĩwa vo ĩngĩ; o na kũikethĩwa ĩngĩ kũmeta, kana kũĩa, kana woo."
Maũndũ ala Yesũ weekie e kũũ nthĩ nĩmoonanisye kana akeeka maũndũ maseo mũno e Mũsumbĩ. Nĩwamanyĩasya andũ kwĩkalany'a na mũuo, nĩwaĩthisye andũ ngili mbingĩ kwa nzĩa ya kyama, avosya awau, na nĩwathayũũkisye ala akw'ũ.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmeũtana kũkwony'a Mbivilianĩ ũndũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩyũmbanĩtye ĩla ĩvinda ya ala aũme ana makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi yĩkathela. We no wende kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingangĩ?
^ kal. 7 Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ Yeova.

translation:
A person should not boast or think that their life brings shame to their mother and father who were afflicted with disease and suffering, because it is not good. Is it true? According to the Bible, some things cause pain and we struggle to understand each affliction that befalls our mothers and fathers who suffer from illness. And if there is a disease affecting someone and they are afflicted with disease, they see difficult things happening in the world, and they are not forgiven for their sins and those of their families. Will this ever end? Perhaps, let us examine everything that happens to people affected by disease.
THE DISEASE CALLED SIN
This verse tells us the following: "And I saw, and behold, a pale horse, and its rider's name was Death, and Hell followed him: and power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth."
What is this disease called sin? Everything can be understood to mean that this verse is a prophecy about the disease known as "The Word of God." (Revelation 19:
How did Jesus show his loyalty? (Revelation 6:2) Daniel prophesied about the Messiah, who would be identified as "a son of man" who would be given "dominion, and glory, and a kingdom," who is Jehovah God. * (Daniel 7:
Is it possible for people to recover from sin? The most important thing, which is Jesus, told us that many have been granted power over dominion. (Revelation 6:2) Was Jesus appointed Ruler in heaven first? He was appointed Ruler when he completed his work on earth. The Bible shows that some will experience a resurrection. (Hebrews 10:
Why have so many become disillusioned with the hope that Jesus was appointed Ruler in 1914? Because according to this prophecy, Jesus said he would rule, but not yet. He was appointed Ruler, and now he has fulfilled his purpose, and Jesus, who is called Michael, has driven Satan and his demons away. (Revelation 12:
THE DISEASE CALLED DEATH
"And there will be a great disease; and such as are found false will be put to death, one by one: and there will be a great slaughter."
This disease called death is very devastating. It continues to claim lives throughout the earth, not just a few lives. For a period of time, during the year 1914, it claimed countless lives. And those who survived were left deeply saddened. It is estimated that around 100 million people died because of the world war of 1914! And many more people continue to suffer because of wars.
Has this devastation ever stopped? Some people believe that mankind can bring peace to the whole earth. But organizations like the United Nations (UN) have failed to stop the disease called death.
THE DISEASE CALLED OLD AGE
"And behold, and lo, old age; and such as are found without strength in their own bodies. And he will go like a shepherd among his sheep, if they stumble, the staff of the strong is broken, and three sheep of the flock are broken and scattered."
This disease called old age is also devastating. Imagine how weak someone becomes when they reach old age (around 0.7 kilograms) and can barely stand, yet they still need to work hard like a young man! (Matthew 20:2) One person may struggle to carry three sheep (2.1 kilograms), and the sheep may appear healthy but are actually weak. Does this situation cause great sorrow for some? Indeed, people often feel sorry for others and help them with their burdens, and this is similar to what happened to ten men who helped each other carry their loads, but some refused to help others.
You have seen how things were in 1914 and whether this old age continues to grow. Yes, it does! Over 70 million people died from diseases between 1901 and 2000. One report stated that "over 805 million people, or about one in nine people worldwide, suffered from chronic hunger in 2012—
THIS IS CALLED THE DISEASE OF HEAVEN OR DEATH
"And behold, and lo, an ancient disease: and such as are found, its name is weakness; and God has compassion on them. And many suffer greatly from pain or sickness, hunger, weakness, and various ailments."
This disease called weakness devastates people's bodies and minds. After the terrible year of 1914, the epidemic known as Spanish flu killed millions of people. About 500 million people were infected with this disease, and this means that one out of every three people around the world suffered from this illness!
Indeed, this Spanish flu was very severe. Scholars estimate that more people died from the disease called smallpox between 1901 and 2000. Until recently, millions of people have been affected by AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria, and many people struggle to find adequate medical care.
These things we see today, like poverty, suffering, or epidemics, cause great weakness. Many people turn to God and pray for help.
BUT THERE IS HOPE!
That hope is based on what is already certain. It is reported that Jesus began to "rule" in 1914, and he ousted Satan from heaven, so Jesus trusts his rule will be successful. (Revelation 6:2; 12:
Ancient people were comforted. Jehovah sent "fortresses to reach the ends of the earth; he broke the bow and shattered the spear." (Psalm 46:9) So people can now be comforted, "rejoicing greatly."
Young people, they experience much pain nowadays. The Bible says: "They experience much sorrow because of wickedness that fills the land."
Sick and weak people, many are afflicted with physical and emotional weakness. The Bible states that God "will wipe away every tear from their eyes; and death will be no more; neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore."
What Jesus did when he came to earth demonstrates how he will do these things perfectly in the future. He taught people to trust in God, healed many through miracles, comforted the sick, and showed compassion to everyone.
Jehovah's spirit has helped us understand the Bible in a way that makes its message clear, especially regarding that final hope for those who are being killed by war. But will you want to learn more?
^ par. 7 The Bible teaches that God's name is Jehovah.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1960
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: FRANCE
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: AĨ MŨNG'ENDU, NĨWATŨMĨAA NDAWA SYA KŨMILA, NA NĨWAVŨTHĨTYE AKA
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Nasyaĩwe taoninĩ yĩtawa Mulhouse, yĩ ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya France. Taoni ĩsu yekalaa andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ na nĩyeesĩkĩe mũno nũndũ wa ũng'endu. Maũndũ ala nĩlilikanaa ĩũlũ wa ĩla naĩ mũnini nĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ andũ ma mĩsyĩ yĩ kĩvathũkany'o kĩsionĩ kitũ matindĩaa kũkita. Aka nĩmavũthĩtw'e mũno mũsyĩ kwitũ na mavinda maingĩ aũme mayamakũlasya mawoni. Namanyĩĩtw'e kana aka mekalaa ikonĩ maisũvĩa aũme moo na syana.
Nakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna maingĩ mũno ĩla naĩ mũnini. Nĩ na myaka ĩkũmi, ĩthe wakwa nĩwooaiwe nĩ ũkĩ. Ĩtina wa myaka ĩtano, ũmwe wa akũũa nĩweeyũaie. Mwakanĩ o ũsu, nĩnoonie mũndũ wa mũsyĩ ooaa ũngĩ nũndũ wa kĩneene kya mũsyĩ, na ũndũ ũsu nĩwanũmĩisye mũno. Andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmamanyĩĩtye ũndũ naĩle kũkita nĩtũmĩĩte tũvyũ na mavuti ĩla ve vata. Mathĩna asu onthe matumie nĩsolwa tattoo mwĩĩ w'onthe na nambĩĩa kũnyw'a.
Nĩ na myaka 16, kĩla mũthenya nĩnanyusaa sũva 10 kũvika 15 sya ũkĩ, na ĩtina wa kavinda kanini nambĩĩa kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila. Nĩ kana nĩkwate mbesa sya kwĩka maũndũ asu mathũku, nĩnatesaa sikilevu na nambĩĩa kũya. O na ndivikya myaka 17 naĩ nakomie yela. Nĩnatw'ĩĩwe kyovo mavinda 18 nũndũ wa kũya na ũng'endu.
Nĩ na myaka 20 na kĩndũ, nĩnathũkĩĩie ĩ ya mũno. Kĩla mũthenya nanyusaa mĩsokoto 20 ya vangi na nĩnanyusaa heroin na ndawa ingĩ nthũku sya kũmila. Mavinda maingĩ neethĩawa nĩ vakuvĩ kũkw'a nũndũ wa kũnyw'a mũno syĩndũ isu. Nĩnambĩĩie kũta ndawa sya kũmila na kwoou nekalaa nguĩte tũvyũ na mavuti. Ve ĩvinda yĩmwe natatie kũatha mũndũ, ĩndĩ ũseo kĩsasi kyeelelũka na kyaatha ngome ya mũsivi! Nĩ na myaka 24, inyia wakwa nĩwakwie na ũu watuma nĩthilĩka mũno. Nũndũ andũ nĩmangĩaa, makilasya moona tũkĩte kũkomana makakĩla ngalĩko ĩla ĩngĩ ya lelũ. Nũndũ wa kũkita na andũ, mawathanthatũ na mawakyumwa maingĩ mathelaa nĩ volisi kana nĩ sivitalĩ nditumwa itau.
Nĩnatwaanie nĩ na myaka 28. O tondũ ũtonya kũsũanĩa, ndyanengete kĩveti kyakwa ndaĩa. Nĩnakĩumangaa na ngakĩvũa. Vai ũndũ o na ũmwe twaaĩsa kwĩka ta mũndũ na mũka. Nasũanĩaa kana kũmũnenga syĩndũ sya kwĩyanakavya sya aka ila nooyaa nĩkũtoetye. Ĩndĩ, ve ũndũ ndataĩĩe weekĩkie. Kĩveti kyakwa nĩkyambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kwa ĩvinda ya mbee, nĩkyaekanie na sikala, kyalea syĩndũ sya ũng'ei ila nakĩnengae, na kyandũngĩa syĩndũ sya kwĩyanakavya ila nakĩnengete. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie nĩthata mũno. Nĩnambĩĩie kũmũvĩnga ndakemanyĩsye Mbivilia, o na nĩnamũtoeeasya syũki ya sikala ũthyũnĩ. Nĩnaendaa nĩmwanangĩĩte ĩsyĩtwa kĩla vandũ ũtũinĩ.
Ũtukũ ũmwe nĩnakwatisye nyũmba yitũ mwaki nĩmũmile. Ĩndĩ kĩveti kyakwa nĩkyatwovoisye nĩna kelĩtu kaitũ ka myaka ĩtano. Ĩla namilũkilwe, nathĩnĩkie mũno nũndũ wa kĩko kĩu. Neew'aa Ngai atesa kũndekea. O na nĩnalilikanile ĩvinda yĩmwe neewie mũtavany'a ayasya kana ala athũku makavĩvw'a ĩianĩ ya mwaki. O na ndakĩtalĩ wakwa wa kyongo ambĩie atĩĩ: "We ndwĩsa kũtetheka o na ũkekanwa naku ata!"
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Ĩtina wa nyũmba yitũ kũvya twaendie kwĩkalaa na asyai ma kĩveti kyakwa. Ĩla Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syookie kũtembelea kĩveti kyakwa, namakũlilye atĩĩ, "Ngai no andekee naĩ syonthe ila nĩkĩte?" Mambonisye Mbivilianĩ ĩandĩko ya 1 Akolintho 6:9-11. Ĩandĩko yĩu yonanĩtye mwĩkalĩle mũthũku ũla Ngai ũmenete, ĩndĩ yongeleele kwasya: "Amwe menyu mwailyĩ ũu." Ndeto isu nĩsyandĩkĩĩthisye kana no nĩalyũke. Na ĩndĩ Ngũsĩ isu syanzomea ĩandĩko ya 1 Yoana 4:8 kũndĩkĩĩthya kana Ngai nũmbendete. Maũndũ asu nĩmambĩkĩie vinya mũno na kwoou nakũlya Ngũsĩ isu twĩmanyĩasye Mbivilia kelĩ kwa kyumwa, na nambĩĩa kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto. O na nĩnamũvoyaa Yeova kĩla ĩvinda.
Mwei ũmwe ũte mũthelu nĩnatwie kũekana na ndawa sya kũmila na kũnyw'a ũkĩ. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩnambĩĩie kũthĩnw'a nĩ mwĩĩ nũndũ wa kũekana na ndawa sya kũmila. Nĩnaĩsawa nĩ mũtwe mũno, mwĩĩ nĩwaalasya, na kũota ndoto nthũku na sya kũtelemya. Ĩndĩ nĩneew'aa Yeova aindetheesya na aimbĩkĩa vinya. Neew'aa ta mũtũmwa Vaulo ũla waandĩkie ũũ aineena ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Ngai wamũtetheeisye: "Nĩndonya maũndũ onthe nthĩnĩ wake ũla ũndonyethasya." (Avilivi 4:13) Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩnaekie vyũ kũnyw'a sikala.—2 Akolintho 7:1.
Mbivilia nĩyandetheeisye kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo na yandetheesya kwĩthĩwa na mũsyĩ mũseo. Nĩnambĩĩie kwĩkalany'a na kĩveti kyakwa nesa. Nĩnambĩĩie kũkĩnenga ndaĩa na kũtũmĩa ndeto nzeo ta "nĩ mũvea." O na nĩneethĩiwe nĩ ĩthe mũseo. Ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kwa mwaka ũmwe, nĩneeyumisye kũmũthũkũma Yeova na navatiswa nĩatĩĩe ngelekany'o nzeo ya kĩveti kyakwa.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Ndi na nzika kana Mbivilia nĩyatangĩĩie thayũ wakwa. O na andũ ma mũsyĩ ala mate ngũsĩ nĩmesĩ kana nĩthĩwa nakwie nũndũ wa kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila kana ngoaĩwa kaũnĩ.
Mbivilia nĩyatumie mũsyĩ witũ wĩthĩwa na ũtanu nũndũ nĩyamanyĩisye kana naĩle kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũũme mũseo na ĩthe mũseo. (Aeveso 5:25; 6:4) Nĩ na andũ makwa nĩtwambĩĩie kwĩka maũndũ twĩ ngwatanĩo. Vandũ va kĩveti kyakwa kwĩkũngũmĩa ikonĩ nĩ wia, yu nĩnĩtanĩaa kũkĩtetheesya wĩanĩ wa ũtavany'a wa ĩvinda yonthe. Nakyo nĩkĩndetheeasya kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kyakwa nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi.
Wendo na tei wa Yeova nũtumĩte nĩalyũka vyũ. Nĩnĩthĩawa na wendi wa kũtavya andũ ala mate na wĩkwatyo ĩũlũ wa ndaĩa nzeo sya Yeova, nũndũ andũ aingĩ moonaa nĩ ũmwe wa andũ asu mate na wĩkwatyo. Nĩnĩsĩ vyũ kana Mbivilia yĩ na ũtonyi wa kũtetheesya mũndũ o na wĩva ethĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseo na aimanya vata wa kwĩthĩwa e thayũ. Mbivilia nĩtumĩte nĩnenga aũme na aka ndaĩa na ngethĩwa nĩmendete, o na nĩtumĩte nĩnenga ndaĩa.

translation:
LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1960
THE COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: FRANCE
OUR HISTORY: THEY ARE TRAVELERS, THEY SHOWED US HOW TO LIVE, AND THEY TAUGHT US THIS
PERSONAL DETAILS:
I was born in the beautiful town of Mulhouse, which is in the east of France. This town has many people of different nationalities and is known for its industrial activity. These things made me love the country of origin and my motherland, which is a land of peace where people live together harmoniously. This is what we learned from them and their history is full of stories worth remembering. We remember that this place was once a source of great joy and happiness for many. We also know that it was a place of suffering and tears.
I am surrounded by many friends and family. I am twenty years old, and my father passed away when I was young. Five years ago, my older brother died. Today, I met a kind person who showed me a lot of respect, and this thing touched my heart. The people around me understand my situation and help me with their support and advice. My friends always encourage me to drink water.
I am sixteen years old, every day I smoke between 10 and 15 cigarettes, and because of bad company I started using drugs to live. It seems like I got used to doing wrong things, so I went to school and started drinking alcohol. Now I am seventeen years old and I have stopped completely. I joined eighteen friends to go out and travel.
I am twenty years old now, and I regret everything. Every day I use twenty packets of marijuana and I use heroin and other drugs to live. Many friends led me astray and encouraged me to drink alcohol excessively. I tried to stop using drugs and stay away from bad company. But one time I almost killed someone, and luckily the police arrived quickly and saved his life! I am twenty-four years old, today my father would be proud of me. People around me are increasing, they are destroying our society and causing chaos everywhere. The problem of living with people, many conflicts and misunderstandings lead to violence or I don't want to be involved in such matters.
I got married when I was twenty-eight years old. And because of poverty, I decided to steal from others. I became greedy and envious. Then one day we were caught stealing from someone's house. I regretted it and wished I hadn't done it, but it was too late. However, something happened to me then. My wife told me about the Bible and Jehovah's Witnesses. Because of studying the Bible for some time, I changed my behavior, it helped me overcome evil deeds but I still struggled, and it helped me avoid bad habits but I continued struggling. This thing made me hate alcohol. I tried to forgive those who had taught me about the Bible, and I began to appreciate their advice. I am going to tell everyone what I have learned.
One night our house caught fire while I was asleep. But my wife woke me up and we saved our five-year-old child. But despite this, I remained very sad because of the loss of property. Thank God he protected me. And I remembered one dream I had where someone said to me: "You will suffer and be imprisoned because of you!"
THE BIBLE HELPED ME CHANGE MY LIFE:
The reason we built our house was so that we could live near my wife's parents. But Jehovah's Witnesses began visiting our home, and they showed me that, "God protects you completely, but why is that?" They showed me the scripture from 1 Corinthians 6:9-11. That scripture condemns those who do not live according to God's standards, and also says: "Some of you used to be like that." From then on I started thinking about whether I should change or not. And now I use the scripture from 1 John 4:8 to remind myself that God loves me. These things made me feel bad and I wanted to know what the Bible teaches, and I wanted to live according to Christ's teachings. And I pray to Jehovah every day.
One time I had a problem with smoking and drinking alcohol. My family told me to stop smoking. I felt very troubled, I became restless, and I had terrible dreams. But Jehovah helped me and strengthened me. He helped me just like he helped the apostle Paul who wrote about how God supported him: "I can do all things through the One who gives me strength." (Philippians 4:13) My family encouraged me to stop drinking too.—2 Corinthians 7:1.
The Bible shows us how to live a moral life and it strengthens us to live a moral life. It encourages us to examine our own heart. It encourages us to tell the truth and to avoid lying and saying things like "It doesn't matter." And I realized I was wrong. After studying the Bible for a year, I felt grateful to Jehovah and I wanted to make changes in my life.
IMPORTANT OR I REGRET:
I have faith that the Bible will guide my way. And others who feel the same way as me also believe that we should avoid using drugs or getting involved in bad company.
The Bible helps our families to be united and it teaches us how to treat each other with love and respect. (Ephesians 5:25; 6:4) We need to teach our children what is right. The people in my community appreciate this, and I am happy to share the good news of the Kingdom with everyone. This is why I try to be a good example in all aspects of my life.
Jehovah's love and laws help us a lot. I want to show love to others and to demonstrate the importance of living according to Jehovah's standards so that more people may see that we are part of a group of people who value morality. I am glad that the Bible has the power to change people and to help them overcome their problems, and that it helps us to tell the truth and to live honestly.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1974
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: MEXICO
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: E WA MŨIKA, AĨ MŨNG'ENDU NA NĨWENDETE KŨKITA
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Nasyaĩwe kĩsionĩ kyanake kĩtawa Ciudad Mante, kĩla kĩ mũsyĩnĩ wa Tamaulipas, Mexico. Andũ aingĩ ma kĩsio kĩu methĩawa me alau na me aseo. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana kĩsio kĩu kyaĩ na ikundi sya ing'endilĩ, na ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumaa kĩthĩwa kĩ kĩsio kĩthũku mũno.
Tũsyaĩtwe twĩ imwana inyia na ninyie wa kelĩ. Asyai makwa nĩmandwaie ngavatisĩwe Katholeki, na ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩnalikile kwayanĩ ya makanisa ma Katholeki ala maĩ kĩsionĩ kĩu. Nĩnendaa mũno kũmwendeesya Ngai nũndũ nĩnakĩaa kwĩsa kũsilĩlwa na ndivĩvw'a ĩianĩ ya mwaki.
Nĩ na myaka ĩtano, ĩthe witũ nĩwatolokile mũsyĩ atũtia. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwanũmĩisye mũno na neethĩwa nde na wĩkwatyo. O na kau nĩtwamwendete mũno, ndyaaelewa kĩla kyatumie atoloka mũsyĩ. Ĩthe wakwa amina kũtoloka, inyia wakwa nĩwaendaa kũthũkũma vaasa na mũsyĩ masaa maingĩ mũno nĩ kana atũmanthĩe lĩu twĩ ana.
Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩnatolokaa sukulu nĩ kana ngatindany'e na syana ila syaĩ ngũũ mbee wakwa. Syana isu nĩsyamanyĩisye kũumana, kũnyw'a sikala, kũya, na kũkita. Na nũndũ nĩnendete kwĩthĩwa nĩ ĩũlũ wa andũ ala angĩ na nĩmasumbĩkĩte, nĩnaendie kwĩmanyĩsya kaũ wa mĩthemba yonthe vamwe na kũtũmĩa mĩio ya kaũ. Nĩneethĩiwe nĩ mũng'endu mũno nĩ wa mũika. Mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtwokitaa na mavuti, o na ve mavinda amwe naũmĩaa mũno vyũ nginya ngatiwa nĩ vakuvĩ kũkw'a. Inyia wakwa nĩwaũmĩaa ngoo mũno ambĩthĩa nĩvalũkĩte vau nĩmũũmĩu na aimbosa ainzembya sivitalĩ!
Nĩ na myaka 16, kĩmwana kĩmwe twaĩ ndũũ twĩ anini kĩtawa Jorge nĩkyookie mũsyĩ. Atwĩie kana nĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova na eenda kũtũtavya ũvoo wa vata. Nĩwambĩĩie kũtũtavya maũndũ ala ũĩkĩĩaa, na atũmĩaa Mbivilia. Ndyaĩ naasoma Mbivilia, na nĩnatanie mũno kũmanya syĩtwa ya Ngai na kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa nthĩ. Jorge nĩweeyumisye atũmanyĩasye Mbivilia na tweetĩkĩla.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Neewie ta nathyũmũw'a ĩla namanyie ũmanyĩsyo wa kana andũ makavĩvwa ĩianĩ ya mwaki ndwĩ Mbivilianĩ. (Savuli 146:4; Mũtavan'ya 9:5) Ĩla namanyie ũu, nĩnaekie kwĩthĩwa na wia ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Vandũ va ũu, nĩnambĩĩie kwona Ngai e Ĩthe wĩ wendo ũla wendeaa syana syake moseo.
O ũndũ naendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, now'o noonaa naĩle kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle wakwa. Nĩnendaa kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo na ndiekana na ũng'endu. Ũtao ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 15:33 nĩwandetheeisye mũno. Ũtao ũsu wonanĩtye kana itindo nthũku "nĩsyanangaa mwĩkalĩle mũseo." Nĩnamanyie kana nĩ kenda nĩekane vyũ na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku, naaĩle kũekana na itindo nthũku. Kwoou nĩnaekie kũtindany'a na andũ ala maĩ anyanyawa tene, na namantha kĩtindo kĩseo nthĩnĩ wa kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto nũndũ nĩkyo kĩthĩawa na andũ maminaa mathĩna moo matũmĩĩte myolooto ya Mbivilia, vandũ va kũkita.
Ĩandĩko yĩngĩ yandetheeisye mũno kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle wakwa nĩ Alomi 12:17-19. Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũikekũle kwa mũndũ o na wĩva. . . . Ethĩwa nũtonyeka, kwa ngalĩ ĩla yenyu, mwĩthĩwe na mũuo na andũ onthe. Mũikeĩvanĩsye, . . . nũndũ nĩkũandĩkĩtwe, Ũĩvanĩsyo nĩ wakwa; ngaĩvanĩsya, easya ũu Ngai." Nĩnesie kwĩtĩkĩla kana Yeova nĩwe ũkavetanga ũsili ũte wa katĩ ĩvindanĩ yake na kwa nzĩa yake. O kavola kwa kavola, nĩnaekie kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũng'endu.
Ndikolwa nĩ ũndũ ũmwe weekĩkie nĩnũkĩte ĩa-mawĩoo. Kĩkundi kĩmwe kya imwana ila tweethĩawa ĩmwe maũndũnĩ ma ũng'endilĩ nĩkyambũie, na mũtongoi wamo angũna mũongo na ambĩa, "Ethĩwa wĩ mũndũũme ĩtetee!" Saanĩ ũsu nĩnavoyie o mboya nguvĩ, na namũkũlya Yeova anenge vinya nĩyũmĩĩsye. O na kau neew'aa ndyenda kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya, naumie vau ndeka ũndũ mũthũku. Mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe, nĩnakomanie na mũtongoi wa kĩkundi kĩu kya imwana isu e weka. Nĩnathatie mũno ĩla namwonie na neew'a naĩle kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya, ĩndĩ nĩnamũvoyie Yeova ĩngĩ andetheesye ndikaĩvanĩsye. Ũndũ ũla wanzeng'isye nĩ kana kĩmwana kĩu kyookie vala nĩĩ na kyambĩa atĩĩ: "Mwa ndekea nũndũ wa maũndũ ala mekĩkie ĩyoo wĩoo. No nende ngethĩwa nĩilyĩ taku. Nĩenda kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia." Natanie mũno nũndũ nĩnesiĩĩie ndikeke ũndũ ũtaĩle! Na nũndũ wa ũu, nĩtwambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nĩ na mwanake ũsu.
Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana ĩvindanĩ yĩu tweemanyĩasya, andũ ala angĩ ma mũsyĩ nĩmaemiwe nĩ kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ĩndĩ nĩnavangie kana ndiĩtĩkĩla kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kĩnziĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Nĩneesĩ kana naendeea kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo na andũ ma Ngai, ngeethĩwa nĩ mũtanu na ndyĩthĩwa na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa manthĩnĩkĩaa. Nĩnaendeeie kwĩka maendeeo ma kĩ-veva, na mwakanĩ wa 1991, navatiswa na neethĩwa nĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Mbeenĩ, nĩnew'aa woo, nĩnendete kũsumbĩka andũ, na naĩ mũng'endu. Ĩndĩ ndeto ya Ngai nĩalyũlĩte mwĩkalĩle wakwa vyũ. Yu nĩnĩtavasya andũ ala mekwendeew'a ũvoo mũseo wa mũuo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. O na nĩnĩthĩĩtwe ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe kwa myaka 23 mĩvĩtu.
Ve ĩvinda neeyumisye ngatetheesye wĩa ovisinĩ wa ũvonge wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũla wĩ Mexico. Nĩ ovisinĩ ũsu, nĩnakomanie na mũndũ mũka mwanake wĩtawa Claudia, na twatwaana mwaka wa 1999. Nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũngathima na kĩveti kĩseo na kĩĩkĩĩku!
Nĩtwaendie kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kya ala matew'aa kya nthĩ ya Mexico kũtetheesya andũ memanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩtweeiwe tũthamĩĩe nthĩ ya Belize tũkamanyĩsye andũ Mbivilia. O na kau tũyĩthĩawa na syĩndũ mbingĩ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ, nĩtwĩthĩawa na kyonthe kĩla twendaa nĩ kana twĩthĩwe twĩ atanu. Vai kĩndũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũeka kũmũthũkũma Yeova.
Inyia wakwa nĩwesie kwambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ĩngĩ na avatiswa. O na mũkũũa na kĩveti kyake na syana syoo yu nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. O na ve anyanyawa amwe natavasya ũvoo mũseo matw'ĩkie athũkũmi ma Yeova.
Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, andũ amwe ma mũsyĩ nĩmakwie nũndũ mayaaĩtĩkĩla kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle woo mũthũku. O nakwa keka nĩnaendeeie kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũsu mũthũku, nĩvatonyeka ngethĩwa nakwie. Nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mũno nũndũ nĩwangusisye kwake. O na nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa mũvea nũndũ nĩwangusisye kwa athaithi make ala mamanyĩisye me na wũmĩĩsyo kũtũmĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia thayũnĩ wakwa.

translation:
LET US REMEMBER THE YEAR: 1974
THE COUNTRY OF ORIGIN: MEXICO
OUR PARENTS: FROM THE VILLAGE, THEY WALKED AND I FOLLOWED TO SEE
MY BIRTHPLACE:
I was born in a small town called Ciudad Mante, in the state of Tamaulipas, Mexico. Many people in that town were poor and dirty. Because of poverty, the town was small and had few buildings, and this caused the town to be very quiet.
We were raised with one brother and several sisters. My parents were devout Catholics, and the tradition of our family was to attend Catholic churches throughout that town. I always wanted to serve God because I grew up hearing stories about the power of prayer.
When I was five years old, my father left us to work. This saddened me greatly and affected me deeply. But we continued to live there, and I understood why he went to work. After he finished working, my mother would go to visit him and spend many hours with him, sometimes taking us along with her.
Because of this, I started school, but I didn't like it much because I missed my father. Those days were spent playing, drinking soda, eating, and seeing. And although I wanted to be with all the children and I struggled, I tried to make friends with all the boys together and help them with their tasks. I was helped by my mother who was from the village. Our parents worked hard and often faced difficulties, but they persevered. My mother especially endured many hardships, sacrificing herself for us and enduring insults without complaint!
When I was 16 years old, a young man named Jorge came to our house. He told us about Jehovah's Witnesses and began to teach us the truth. He encouraged us to learn about everything, and he gave us the Bible. I started reading the Bible, and I quickly became interested in learning God's name and his purpose for humanity. Jorge patiently taught us the Bible and explained it clearly.
WHAT THE BIBLE TAUGHT ME:
Don't put your trust in humans, but rely on God, the Creator of everything. (Psalm 146:4; Ecclesiastes 9:5) Once I understood this, I felt comforted knowing that God cares. All people should strive to know God and show love for His Son, who loves all mankind.
And as I continued studying the Bible, I realized something important. I wanted to be comforted and associate with good people. The saying found in 1 Corinthians 15:33 deeply moved me. That verse says that "bad company corrupts good habits." I realized that I needed to avoid bad associations, even if it meant distancing myself from certain friends. So I decided to associate with those who loved God, and I joined the Christian congregation where many others also valued and applied the teachings of the Bible.
Another scripture that helped me greatly was Romans 12:17-19. It reads: "Repay no one evil for evil… 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him.… Conquer evil with goodness.'" I came to understand that Jehovah is the One who sets the standard for what is right and wrong. And more and more, I wanted to live according to his standards.
I recall one experience I had while in my teens. A group of young people whom I associated with began to get involved in bad company, and one boy started using abusive language and said, "Go ahead, hit me!" At first, I felt provoked, but then I remembered what Jehovah had taught me and I calmed down. He had given me strength. And instead of getting into trouble, I walked away from the group. Later, I spoke to the boy privately and told him how I felt. I realized that I had been able to control myself because of what I had learned from Jehovah. What impressed me was that this young man admitted: "You are right. I shouldn't have provoked you like that. I want to learn about the Bible." I was so happy that I had responded in a peaceful way! And because of this, we were able to share the Bible with him and others.
In fact, many people who initially oppose us are willing to listen when they see our desire to share the Bible. I have found that even if someone insults me, I can still offer to study the Bible with them. I am convinced that continuing to associate with God's people—being encouraged by them and encouraging others—is vital. I continue to make progress spiritually, and in 1991, I was appointed as a pioneer by Jehovah.
EXPERIENCES THAT HAVE STRENGTHENED ME:
Truly, I have always enjoyed helping people, and I find it rewarding. God's love has motivated me to use my life to help others learn about his Word, the Bible. And I spent 23 years serving as a full-time evangelizer.
Then I was assigned to serve where there was a greater need, in the branch office of the Watch Tower Society in Mexico. There, I met a wonderful sister named Claudia, and we got married in 1999. I thank Jehovah for giving me such a loving, supportive, and spiritual wife!
We were asked to assist in the work in Belize, sharing the Bible with the people there. And although we faced many challenges, we were confident that Jehovah would strengthen us in whatever we needed. This conviction helped us remain steadfast in our ministry.
My family also supports my activity as a full-time evangelizer. And along with my wife and children, we serve Jehovah. Also, many of my relatives have begun to appreciate the truth and have joined us in proclaiming the good news.
In fact, some people initially react negatively because they feel their way of life is being challenged. But even if I face opposition from someone, I try to maintain a respectful attitude. I thank Jehovah for helping me stay calm in such situations. And I thank him for helping me remember what he has taught me through his organization.
Many people who initially oppose us are willing to listen when they see our genuine interest in them. And even if someone insults me, I can still offer to study the Bible with them. I thank Jehovah for allowing me to experience this and for helping me to remain loyal to him. And I thank him for helping me to remember what I have learned from his faithful servants.

text:
YESŨ atanamba kwambata ĩtunĩ eeie amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "Mũkeethĩwa mwĩ ngũsĩ syakwa . . . kũvika itulu sya nthĩ." (Meko 1:8) Aklĩsto asu ma ĩvinda yĩu maĩ matonya ata kwĩanĩsya wĩa ũsu?
Mũsomi ũmwe wĩtawa Martin Goodman wa Oxford University aisye kana "wendi mwingĩ [wa kũtavany'a] nĩw'o watumaa Aklĩsto methĩwa me kĩvathũkany'o na ndĩni ya Ayuti, vamwe na ndĩni ila ingĩ syeethĩawa mwambĩĩonĩ wa ũsumbĩki wa Lomi." Ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ aendaa kũndũ na kũndũ aitavany'a. Aklĩsto ala ma w'o nĩmeesĩ kana ethĩwa nĩmekwenda kũnyaĩĩkya "ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai," maĩ no nginya mamanthe andũ ala mekwenda kũmanya ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Kwa kwĩka ũu meethĩawa maiatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. (Luka 4:43) Kyu nĩ kĩtumi kĩmwe kyatumaa kĩkundi kya ĩvinda ya atũmwa kĩthĩwa na 'atũmwa,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, andũ ala matũmawa mathi kũndũ kũngĩ. (Mko. 3:14) Yesũ anengie atĩĩ make mwĩao ũũ: "Endai ĩndĩ mũkatw'ĩkĩthye mbaĩ syonthe amanyĩw'a."—Mt. 28:18-20.
Ũmũnthĩ tũi na ala atũmwa ma Yesũ 12, ĩndĩ kwĩ athũkũmi aingĩ ma Yeova methĩawa na veva wa ũmisonalĩ. Na nũndũ nĩmathoketw'e matũmĩe ĩvinda yingangĩ ũtavany'anĩ, mo metĩkĩlĩte makasya, "Ninyioo; ndũma nyie." (Isa. 6:8) Amwe nĩmathamĩĩe nthĩ ingĩ, ta kwa ngelekany'o, ala methĩawa masomee Sukulu ya Ngileati. Ve angĩ namo mathamĩĩe isionĩ ingĩ sya nthĩ yoo. Aingĩ nĩmemanyĩĩtye ithyomo ingĩ nĩ kana matetheesye ikundi na tũkundi twa ithyomo isu. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala mathamĩĩe kũndũ ta kũu na memanyĩĩtye ithyomo ingĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa maĩ na maũndũ mana meũmathĩny'a, na no kwĩthĩwa ũtaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwoo kwĩka ũu. Kwoou nĩ kana meke maũndũ asu maĩ no nginya methĩwe na veva wa kwĩyumya nĩ kenda monany'e nĩmamwendete Yeova na nĩmendete atũi. Na nũndũ wa ũu nĩmeekie masavu na meeyumya. (Luka 14:28-30) Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala mekaa ũu methĩawa meanĩsya ũndũ wa vata mũno.
O na ũu wĩ o vo, andũ maivw'ananaa. Ti kĩla Ngũsĩ yĩthĩawa ĩtonya kũthamĩĩa kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a kana kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩngĩ. Kwoou wĩ o kĩkundinĩ kyenyu, we no wĩthĩwe na veva ũla wĩthĩawa na amisonalĩ?
TETHYA WĨA TA MISONALĨ KĨKUNDINĨ KĨLA WĨTHĨAWA
Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa maĩ na veva ũla wĩthĩawa na amisonalĩ, ĩndĩ nĩ laisi mũno ũkethĩa aingĩ mayaathamĩĩa kũndũ kũngĩ. Ĩndĩ ũtao ũla wanengiwe Timotheo nĩwamaĩlĩte vyũ, o na nĩwaĩle athũkũmi onthe ma Ngai. Eeiwe atĩĩ: "Tethya wĩa wa mũtavan'ya wa ũvoo mũseo ĩanĩsya ũthũkũmi waku." (2 Tim. 4:5) Mwĩao wa kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ na kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a ũnengetwe Aklĩsto onthe o na ethĩwa mekalaa va. O na eka ũu, maũndũ ala amisonalĩ meanĩasya no ũmeke kĩkundinĩ kĩla wĩthĩawa.
Kwa ngelekany'o, no nginya amisonalĩ ala me nthĩ sya ũeninĩ memanyĩsye mĩkalĩle ya kũla maĩ. Makomanaa na maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ala mamanyĩie. Naitũ tũtonya kwĩka ata ethĩwa tũi na ũtonyi wa kũthamĩĩa kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a? Nĩtwaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa atĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kĩsio kya kĩkundi kitũ nesa? Kana kĩla kyaĩle nĩ kũtũmĩa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya kũtavya andũ ũvoo mũseo? Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 1940, ana-a-asa nĩmakũlilw'e mevangĩĩe kũtavanasya valavalanĩ mũthenya ũmwe kĩla kyumwa. We naku no wĩke tamo? Kana wĩona ata ũkatata kũtũmĩa tũla tũkalĩ twa kũtavany'a? Kwa ũkuvĩ twĩkũlya atĩĩ: We nũtatĩte kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo ũitũmĩa nzĩa ila ũtatũaa ũtũmĩaa?
Kwĩthĩwa na woni ũla waĩle kũkaũtetheeasya wĩthĩwe na kĩthito na ũthangaau ũtavany'anĩ. Mavinda maingĩ atavany'a ala aseo vyũ nĩmo makothaa kwĩyumya makatavany'e kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a kana makemanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩngĩ nĩ kana matavye andũ ma kĩthyomo kyu ũvoo mũseo. Kwoou ĩla matavany'a na kĩthito methĩawa me ũathimo kwa andũ aingĩ. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana mũno mũno amisonalĩ nĩmo matongoeasya ikundi nginya ĩla ana-a-asa ma kĩsio kĩu makethĩwa maĩle kũkwatĩĩa maũndũ. Ethĩwa wĩ mwana-a-asa mũvatise, we 'nĩwendaa' kwĩka maendeeo nĩ kana wĩthĩwe ũtonya kũthũkũma ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ?—1 Tim. 3:1.
ĨTHĨWA WĨ "ŨTETHYO MŨNENE"
Ve maũndũ angĩ ũtonya kwĩka kĩkundinĩ kĩla wĩthĩawa eka kũtavany'a na kĩthito na kũkwatĩĩa maũndũ. Kĩla ũmwe kĩkundinĩ, ethĩwe nĩ wa mũika kana nĩ mũkũũ, ethĩwe nĩ mũndũũme kana nĩ mũndũ mũka, no ethĩwe "ũtethyo mũnene."—Akol. 4:11, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Nĩ kana tũtetheesye ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa tũmesĩ nesa. Mbivilia ĩtũthangaaĩtye "[tũlilikanane] ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ" ĩla twakomana tũthaithe. (Aevl. 10:24) Ndeto isu syĩonany'a kana o na kau tũyĩlikasya maũndũnĩ meene, nĩtwaĩlĩte kũtata tũmanye mathĩna ma ana-a-asa na tũimaelewa. No kwĩthĩwa ana-a-asa asu mayenda kũtetheew'a kĩ-mwĩĩ, kana makethĩwa me na mavata ma ngoonĩ, kana o makethĩwa mayenda kũlũlũmĩlw'a na Maandĩko. Atumĩa na atetheesya ma kĩkundi mayaĩle kũekewa wĩa wa kũtetheesya ana-a-asa. Kũneena ũla w'o, mavinda amwe wĩthĩaa no mo maĩlĩte kũtetheesya. (Aka. 6:1) Ĩndĩ ĩla ve na vata, kĩla ũmwe witũ no atetheesye ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala akũũ, kana ala me na mĩsyĩ vamwe na mĩsyĩ yoo.
Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Salvatore wasaanĩaw'a akaumya mũthya nata e na andũ make. Ĩvinda yĩu atheleilwe vyũ weethĩa no atesaa viasala wake, na aita vala mekalaa vamwe na syĩndũ imwe maĩ nasyo. Ĩndĩ ve mũsyĩ ũngĩ wa Ngũsĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩla maĩ woonie thĩna ũla wamakwatie. Mũsyĩ ũsu nĩwamatetheeisye kĩ-mbesa na watetheesya Salvatore na mũka makwate wĩa. O na mavinda maingĩ wĩoo andũ ma mũsyĩ ũsu nĩmaeaa ngewa na Salvatore na andũ make nĩ kana mamekĩe vinya. Mĩsyĩ ĩsu yelĩ yatumie ndũũ ngamu ĩminĩte myaka. Ĩvinda yĩu yaĩ ya thĩna mũthei, ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ mĩsyĩ ĩsu yelĩ yalilikana ĩvinda yĩu ĩlilikanaa moseo ala yatanĩie yĩ vamwe.
Mũklĩsto wa w'o nĩwĩsĩ kana ũthaithi ti kĩndũ kya mũndũ ũmwe. O tondũ Yesũ weekaa, o naitũ nĩtwaĩlĩte kũtavya kĩla mũndũ mawatho maseo ki ala me Mbivilianĩ. Twĩthĩwe nĩtũtonya kũthama kana tũitonya, no tũtate a vaitũ twĩke onthe nesa. Na vandũ vamwe tũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩka angĩ nesa nĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩla twĩthĩawa. (Aka. 6:10) Tweeka ũu tũkeew'aa mũyo nũndũ wa kũtetheesya, naitũ ene tũkasyaaa "ũsyao kĩla wĩanĩ mũseo."—Ako. 1:10; Meko 20:35.

translation:
JESUS will rejoice greatly over them with his loving-kindness; he says: "A mother forgets her child…but I will never forget you." (Isaiah 1:8) Did Christ have many followers who were willing to die for him?
One scholar named Martin Goodman from Oxford University stated that "much [of the motivation] was caused by Christians being honored by association with the Roman authorities, along with association with others who were considered important people." The reason Jesus went from place to place was to seek out and find those who were motivated. Christians also believed that this was to demonstrate "the supreme power of God," and they wanted others to learn about that power which was revealed through the apostles. Because of this belief, they eagerly accepted Jesus' invitation. (Luke 4:43) This is one reason why the group of disciples was called 'apostles,' or more accurately, men who were sent forth to another place. (Acts 3:14) Jesus instructed his followers thus: "Go and make disciples of all nations."—Matt. 28:18-20.
Today we see that like those 12 apostles of Jesus, many of Jehovah's Witnesses are full-time evangelizers. And yet, they often feel inadequate when faced with the challenge of reaching people, saying, "Who am I?" (Isaiah 6:8) Some may also feel discouraged, especially when facing opposition, but they continue to share the good news despite their feelings. Others may feel that they lack the necessary skills to effectively teach, and they may be afraid of what others might say or do to them, and they may hesitate because of this fear. However, they realize that making plans requires careful consideration and a willingness to work hard, and they know that they need to keep seeking Jehovah and keep praying to him. And so they persevere and remain courageous. (Luke 14:28-30) Those who take this attitude show that they appreciate the value of spiritual things.
But even if we do not have such qualities, we can still serve God acceptably. Not everyone is able to speak eloquently or to reason convincingly. But how can you strengthen your faith and maintain zeal in your ministry?
REASONS TO REMAIN ZEALOUS IN YOUR MINISTRY
Christian ministers, like those full-time evangelizers, often feel inadequate. It is not uncommon for them to feel overwhelmed or discouraged. Timothy was encouraged to make his ministry a priority and to focus on pleasing God. He was told: "Be diligent in your ministry, fully accomplishing your service." (2 Timothy 4:5) The importance of being diligent in our ministry and helping others learn about Christ should motivate us to keep going. And remember, personal qualities are not the only factor in whether someone will respond favorably to the message.
For example, I may not possess the eloquence needed to deliver an impressive talk. However, I try to prepare thoroughly and pray earnestly. Can we always expect to be successful in reaching people with the good news? Is it possible that we sometimes lack confidence because we place too much emphasis on our own abilities? Or could it be that we are simply afraid of facing opposition? For instance, in the 1940s, some Witnesses were assigned to preach in areas where they faced strong hostility. What would you have done in their situation? Or do you ever feel hesitant to use certain publications in your ministry? Let us ask ourselves: Are we saying, 'I am not capable of preaching effectively unless I have this or that?'
With time, you will learn to overcome your fear and speak courageously. Many experienced preachers also felt inadequate at first, but they persevered and became effective witnesses. They learned to trust in Jehovah and relied on his spirit. Often, those who are shy find that being involved in the ministry helps them gain confidence. A young brother once said, "I used to dread going from house to house, but now I enjoy it." How did he overcome his shyness?—1 Tim. 3:1.
THE "GREAT COMMISSION"
There are many ways to share the good news and help others come to know God. Whether you are young or old, male or female, everyone can be a "minister."—Col. 4:11, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
When we encourage others to study the Bible, we are doing something very important. The Bible urges us to "[pay] attention to yourselves" so that we can continue to strengthen our faith. (Heb. 10:24) However, sometimes we may wonder whether we are truly helping others understand the truth, or whether we are just repeating what we have been taught. And when a young person shows interest, should we try to force him to accept our beliefs, or should we let him examine the Scriptures for himself? Experienced Christians often use various methods to teach people about the Bible. But some find that one method works best for them. (Acts 6:1) In fact, each one of us should strive to teach people the truth in a way that suits their personality and background.
For example, imagine a young Christian named Salvatore who had difficulty understanding certain teachings. His parents patiently explained those teachings to him, and he eventually came to appreciate them. They did not pressure him, but allowed him to come to his own conclusions. A family may also be able to help someone by sharing personal experiences that illustrate a principle. Many families have found that inviting people to spend time with them and observe how they live can be effective. Years may pass before someone makes a decision. Imagine a parent who consistently sets a fine example, and then sees his child eventually adopt similar values. That parent's influence may not be obvious, but it has had a lasting effect.
A true disciple is not concerned about what others think. Just as Jesus was, we should be willing to speak the truth regardless of whether people accept it or reject it. We want to help people understand the Bible, and we will continue to do so as long as they are willing to listen. And some people may need repeated exposure to the truth before they accept it. (Acts 6:10) Let us therefore continue to show kindness when witnessing, knowing that we may be sowing seeds that will later sprout.—Acts 1:10; Mark 20:35.

text:
Kũtũmanĩa mesengyi, visa, kana vitio mbuku nĩ kwasya ata?
Nĩ kũtũmanĩa simũnĩ mesengyi, visa, kana vitio syonanĩtye ũtheinĩ maũndũ matonya kũamũkya wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. Aineenea ũndũ ũsu, mũndũũme ũmwe aĩtye atĩĩ: "Matukũ aa ĩsu no tayo nzĩa ĩla ĩtũmĩawa kũea ngewa. Andũ mambĩĩaa na kũtũmĩana o tũmesengyi na maendeangĩe mayambĩĩa kũtũmĩana visa itonya kũamũkya wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ."
Nĩkĩ andũ mekaa ũu? Mũndũ ũmwe ũsomeete mĩao awetetwe nthĩnĩ wa ĩkaseti ya The New York Times aĩtye kana, kwosana na andũ amwe ma mũika, "kwĩthĩwa na visa ya mwĩĩtu kana mwanake mwĩ ndũũ e mũthei simũnĩ yaku, nĩ wonany'o wa kana nĩwendete kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ." O nake mwĩĩtu ũmwe wa mũika aĩtye kana kwĩka ũu nĩ "nzĩa ya kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ ĩte mũisyo," nũndũ "ndwĩsa kũitava o na ndwĩsa kũkwatw'a mowau."
Itumi ingĩ itumaa andũ ma mũika matũmanĩa mesengyi sya mũthemba ũsu nĩ:
Nĩ kana mathaũkĩe mũndũ ũngĩ meũsũanĩa ta matonya kwambĩĩsya ndũũ nake.
Nũndũ ve mũndũ ũnamatũmĩie visa ta ĩsu na meĩw'a maĩle kũtũma o namo.
Kũtũmanĩa mesengyi, visa, kana vitio mbuku kwĩ ũthũku mwaũ?
Wamina kũtũma visa kuma simũnĩ yaku, yĩthĩawa yauma mokonĩ maku, na kwoou ndũtonya kũsiĩĩa ũndũ ĩkũtũmĩwa kana ũkasiĩĩa ndĩkatũmĩwe kũkwanangĩa ĩsyĩtwa. Mũnene ũmwe na mũandĩki wĩtawa Amanda Lenhart, kuma ovisinĩ ũmwe wa kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli wa Pew Research Center, aandĩkie ũũ ĩũlũ wa kũtũmanĩa mesengyi mbuku: "Ũmũnthĩ nĩ laisi vyũ andũ kũtũma na kwia kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mesengyi ikwonany'a maũndũ mathũku mũndũ ũngĩ wĩkĩte nĩ kana mony'e andũ angĩ."
Mavinda angĩ
Mũndũ ũla watũmĩwa visa sya andũ athei o nake nũinyaĩĩkasya ayenda kũtanĩthya anyanyae.
Imwana ila syatiwa nĩ eĩtu meeĩ ndũũ, ninyaĩĩkĩasya andũ angĩ visa sya eĩtu asu me athei nĩ kana syĩĩyĩvanĩsye.
WE WAAMANYA? Mavinda maingĩ kũtũma visa sya andũ athei simũnĩ kwonekaa ũndũ ũmwe na kũvukya kana kanini kana kũnyaĩĩkya vunongulavia ya syana. Andũ amwe ma mũika nĩmatwaĩtwe kotinĩ nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu.
Mbivilia yaĩtye ata?
Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana kũtanĩa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano nĩ ũndũ waĩlĩte. (Nthimo 5:
"Ĩndĩ ũlaalai, na ũvuku w'onthe, na wendi, maikawetwe katĩ wenyu, . . . o na ũla wĩ nthoni, o na kũneena na ũtumanu, kana kũvũa ngũĩ."
—Aeveso 5: 3, 4.
"Ũaai mamutha menyu ala me kũũ nthĩ: ũlaalai, na ũvuku, na mĩmeo mĩthũku, na kwenda maũndũ mathũku, na ĩtomo."
—Akolosai 3:5.
Maandĩko asu maitũkanĩtye o ĩũlũ wa "ũlaalai," (ũla nĩ kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ katĩ wa andũ matatwaanĩte) ĩndĩ o na nĩmatũkanĩtye ĩũlũ wa "ũvuku" (ndeto ĩla ĩtũmĩawa kwonany'a mwĩkalĩle o na wĩva mũthũku). Ĩngĩ nĩmatũkanĩtye ĩũlũ wa "mĩmeo mĩthũku" (ĩla nĩ wendi ũla ũtonya kũtuma mũndũ elikya mwĩkalĩlenĩ mũthũku, ĩndĩ ti wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ ũla wĩthĩawa nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano).
Ĩkũlye atĩĩ:
Nĩkĩ kũtũma visa sya andũ athei nĩ "ũvuku"?
Nĩkĩ kwĩka ũu kũtonya kwongeleela "mĩmeo mĩthũku"?
Nĩkĩ wendi wa kwĩloela na kũnyaĩĩkya visa sya andũ athei nĩ 'ũndũ mũthũku'?
Maandĩko aa angĩ maatĩĩe nĩmonanĩtye kĩtumi kĩngĩ kĩseo kya kwĩvathana na kũtũma visa, mesengyi, kana vitio mbuku.
"Thangaa kwĩnengane mwene wĩtĩkĩlwe nĩ Ngai, mũtethya wa wĩa ũtasonokw'a."
—2 Timotheo 2: 15.
"Inyw'ĩ mwaĩle kwĩthĩwa andũ mailyĩ ata mwĩkalĩlenĩ mũtheu wa thayũ na kũmũkĩa Ngai"?
—2 Vetelo 3: 11.
Maandĩko asu monanĩtye ũseo wa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Weethĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo, ndũkekalaa na wia ũisũanĩa ta ve ũndũ mũthũku ũtonya kũũkwata nũndũ wa meko maku.
Ĩkũlye atĩĩ:
Nyie nĩ mũndũ wĩ ndaĩa syĩilyĩ ata?
Nĩnĩsũanĩaa ũndũ ndonya kwanangĩa ala angĩ ĩsyĩtwa?
Nyie nĩnendeeaw'a nĩ kwĩtanĩthya na maũndũ matonya kũũmĩsya andũ angĩ?
Kũtũmĩana mesengyi mbuku simũnĩ kũtonya kũmbanangĩa ĩsyĩtwa ata?
Asyai makwa makaendeea kũndĩkĩĩa mamanya kana nĩnĩtũmaa na ngatũmĩwa mesengyi mbuku simũnĩ?
NGEWA YA W'O "Ve mwĩĩtu ũmwe mũnyanyawa waĩ ndũũ na kĩmwana, ĩndĩ nĩwavithaa. O maendeee, nĩmatũmanĩie visa syoo me athei. Mĩthenya ĩlĩ ĩte mĩvĩtu, ĩthe wa mwĩĩtu ũsu nĩwoosie simũ yake asisye kĩla kĩ nthĩnĩ. Nĩwoonie mesengyi isu, na avatelema atiwa ate na ũndũ wa kwasya. Ĩthe nĩwamũkũlilye nake eetĩkĩla kĩla kĩndũ. O na kau we nĩw'ĩwaa akosie, ũndũ ũsu nĩwatelemilye asyai make na watuma mathata mũno! Mayonaa ta makesa kũmũĩkĩĩa ĩngĩ."
Ũw'o wa maũndũ: Kũtũmanĩa mesengyi mbuku simũnĩ nĩkwanangĩaa mũndũ ũla ũkũitũma ndaĩa o na ũla ũkũtũmĩwa. Mwĩĩtu ũmwe ũla wathing'ĩĩiw'e nĩ mwanake me ndũũ amũtũmĩe visa syake e mũthei aĩtye atĩĩ, "Ũndũ ũsu ũtumaa nĩĩmena na nĩw'a nde wa vata."
Nũndũ kũtũmĩana mesengyi mbuku nĩ mwĩkalĩle mũthũku, nĩkũtonya kwananga ĩsyĩtwa yaku na ya angĩ, na nĩkũtonya kũtuma wovwa nũndũ wa kũtũla mĩao, nũseo ũkaatĩĩa ũtao ũũ wa Mbivilia:
"Kĩa mĩmeo ya wana."
—2 Timotheo 2:22.
"Thyũũa metho makwa matikasisye maũndũ ma mana."
—Savuli 119: 37.
We ũtonya kwĩka ata?
Sũanĩa ũndũ ũtonya kũtũmĩa ũtao wa Mbivilia ũndũnĩ ũũ weekĩkie. Soma ũndũ ũũ wakwatie Janet, na ũisakũa ũtwi ũla ũkwona ta waĩle.
"Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnakomanie na mwanake mũna, anenga namba yake ya simũ, nakwa namũnenga yakwa. O na kyumwa kĩmwe kĩte kĩthelu, nĩwaambĩĩie kũngũlya nĩmũtũmĩe visa syakwa nĩkĩĩte ngũa sya kũthambĩa."
—Janet.
We wĩsũanĩa Janet ta waĩle kwĩthĩwa eekie ata? We ũtonya kwĩka ata?
ŨTWI WA 1 No wasye: 'Ndikwona ve ũthũku, nũndũ ta keka tũendie ĩmwe kũthambĩa, ethĩwa ambonie nĩkĩĩte ngũa sya kũthambĩa.'
ŨTWI WA 2 No wasye: 'Nũndũ ndyĩsĩ nesa kĩla ũkwenda, eka nĩmũtũmĩe visa ndekwoneka nĩ mũthei mũno na ĩndĩ ndyeteela none eĩka ata.'
ŨTWI WA 3 No wasye: 'Mwanake ũũ no nĩsĩ kĩla ũkwenda. Nĩĩka kũvuta mesengyi ĩĩ ũnandũmĩie.'
Ũtwi wa 3 wĩoneka waĩle, kana ti w'o? O na Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Mũndũ wĩ kĩlĩko nĩwonaa ũthũku, na kwĩvitha; ĩndĩ ala mate ũmanyi nĩmaendeeaa, na kũthĩna."
Ũndũ ũũ twoona wĩonany'a kĩtumi kĩla kĩnene kĩtumaa andũ mambĩĩa kũtũmanĩa mesengyi mbuku na melikya mĩkalĩle ĩngĩ mĩthũku, nakyo nĩ kĩĩ: Kũlea kũnyuva nesa anyanya moo. (Nthimo 13:20) Mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Sarah aĩtye ũũ: "Waĩle kũtindany'a na andũ ala wĩsĩ mayendete mwĩkalĩle mũthũku." Mũndũ mũka ũngĩ wĩtawa Delia o nake easya, "Andũ amwe monekaa ta anyanya mayĩsa kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseo, ĩndĩ mekaa kũwananga." Ethĩwa mwĩkalĩle woo ndwosanĩte na mĩao ya Ngai, o naku wambĩĩaa kwenda kwĩka o ta mo. We no wende mwĩkalĩle waku wanangĩke nũndũ wa kũtindany'a na anyanya mailyĩ ũu?"

Is understanding news, visas, or books difficult at all?
It's understanding information about news, visas, or books that makes people want to quickly grasp the meaning of things. Someone once said: "These days we don't have time to read newspapers thoroughly. Many people and wanting to understand news and developments quickly leads to wanting to get visas quickly to be able to grasp the meaning of things."
So are people like this? One person who wrote an article for The New York Times said that, compared to some people, "being issued a visa or a passport is easy for someone with money, and it's a sign that they can afford to grasp the meaning of things." Another person from that place said that this "is a sign of grasping the meaning of things," adding "it's better to have it and not need it than to need it and not have it."
Many other reasons cause people to want to understand news about this issue are:
It's because sometimes a person doesn't have enough ability to explain their own situation.
And also a person might want a visa just to show off their wealth to others.
Is understanding news, visas, or books important today?
Being able to get visas easily allows someone to travel anywhere, experience different cultures, and learn something new that can help them improve themselves or become more knowledgeable. One researcher and writer named Amanda Lenhart, from a website called Pew Research Center, wrote this short piece about understanding news: "The truth is that people want to understand and know what's happening in the world so that when someone asks them, they can say they know other people."
Other points
Someone who has been given a visa by other people might feel compelled to share their experiences.
This child who was raised is a good example, and feeling compelled to tell other people about the visa of those children is often seen as showing off.
DO YOU KNOW? Many reasons for getting visas from other people seem to be about showing off or bragging or being proud. Some people in that place were surprised by this.
What does it mean?
It means that wanting to connect with others through social media is a common thing. (Proverbs 5:
"Be adulterous, and foolish, and lazy, let your words be sweet to your neighbor, . . . and your tongue speak deceitfully, or commit evil."
—Proverbs 5: 3, 4.
"Put to death therefore your earthly members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, lustful passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry."
—Colossians 3:5.
These scriptures explain the meaning of "adultery," (which is having an intimate connection between two people who are not married) and they explain the meaning of "foolishness" (which is behavior that shows disrespect or lack of consideration). They also explain the meaning of "lustful passions" (which is a desire that makes someone act inappropriately, and is not a healthy connection between two people).
Think about this:
Is wanting to get visas from other people "foolishness?"
Can talking about this encourage "lustful passions?"
Is spending time sharing and boasting about visas from other people 'something bad?'
These scriptures also show us how important it is to avoid getting involved in things like getting visas, messengers, or online platforms.
"Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed."
—2 Timothy 2: 15.
"Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, give diligence that ye may be found of him in peace without spot, and blameless."
—2 Peter 3: 11.
These scriptures show us the importance of being careful with our connections. Being careful with our connections will help us avoid getting caught up in something bad that can cause problems.
Think about this:
Are you a person who easily gets influenced?
Am I able to resist temptations that could lead to trouble?
Are you willing to get involved in things that could harm others?
Using messengers and online platforms can sometimes lead to temptation, right?
Should we continue to share what we know or should we be careful when using messengers and online platforms?
THE EXAMPLE OF A FATHER "Imagine there is a father with a child, and he disciplines him. But then, he continues to send him on errands. Wouldn't it be better if he first taught him well, so that he knows what to do in every situation? He would teach him lessons, and explain to him why certain things are wrong. Then he would trust him more. But if you let him go without teaching him, you will only create problems for yourself! Don't expect him to understand everything."
The lesson here is: Using messengers and online platforms can influence both the person sending and the person receiving. A parent who sends his child on an errand teaches him well, saying, "This is what happens when you disobey, and you will suffer the consequences."
Getting involved with messengers and online platforms is dangerous, because it can lead to temptation for you and others, and it can cause you to lose time that could be used for spiritual activities, just as the Bible says:
"Flee youthful lusts."
—2 Timothy 2:22.
"Turn away mine eyes from vain things."
—Psalm 119: 37.
Can you avoid it?
Consider how you can use the Bible's principles to guide you. Read this experience of Janet, and pay attention to the advice she received.
"One day I argued with my husband, got his phone number, and called him. And when I felt lonely, I told him to send me pictures so I could feel comforted."
—Janet.
What do you think about Janet's actions? Can you avoid doing the same?
ADVICE 1 She said: 'I thought I was being clever, but now I realize we should have gone together to get comfort, instead of letting him send me pictures to feel comforted.'
ADVICE 2 She said: 'I shouldn't have been so quick to respond, but I wanted him to see that I was still attractive and that I hadn't lost interest.'
ADVICE 3 She said: 'My husband wasn't paying attention. I needed to talk to someone.'
Which piece of advice seems most helpful, don't you think? And the Bible says: "A wise person sees danger coming and avoids it, but a foolish person keeps going and suffers the consequences."
This situation shows how easily people can be led to make bad decisions that lead to problems and cause them to spend much time and money trying to fix things, and it also shows: It is better to be cautious than to regret it later. (Proverbs 13:20) A sister named Sarah once said: "It's easy to get carried away when talking to others who aren't loyal." Another sister named Delia shared, "Some people seem to enjoy making others feel insecure, and then they offer help." Instead of getting involved in such schemes, seek God's guidance and ask Him to help you avoid those situations. Should you get involved in schemes where someone tries to flatter you and make you feel special?

text:
NDĨNI syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ta Ĩkanisa ya Katholeki, makanisa maingĩ ma Orthodox, ndĩni ya Buddha, na ndĩni ingĩ mbingĩ, syendaa atongoi moo mekale matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae. Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ monaa kana ũndũ ũsu nĩw'o ũtumĩte atongoi ma ndĩni mbingĩ methĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku wa ũlaalai.
Kwoou nĩ ũndũ waĩle kũkũlya atĩĩ, Maandĩko nĩmaleete atongoi ma ndĩni maitwaana kana maitwawa? Nĩ kana tũsũngĩe ĩkũlyo yĩu, ekai twone ũndũ ũmanyĩsyo wa atongoi ma ndĩni kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae wambĩĩie, na woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu.
ŨMANYĨSYO WA ATONGOI MA NDĨNI KWĨKALA MATATWAANĨTE WAMBĨĨIE ATA?
Ĩvuku yĩtawa Encyclopædia Britannica yĩyĩelesya ĩũlũ wa kwĩkala ũtatwaanĩte kana ũte mũtwae, yaĩtye kana 'mũndũ ndesaa kũtwaana, na kwoou aĩlĩte kwĩvathana na kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ, na mũno mũno ethĩwa mũndũ ũsu nĩ mũtongoi wa ndĩni, kana eyumĩtye vyũ maũndũnĩ ma ndĩni.' Mwakanĩ wa 2006, Pope Benedict XVI, aineena na nzama ĩla yĩthĩawa ĩtongoesye maũndũ Kanisanĩ wa Katholeki yĩtawa Roman Curia, oonanisye kana mwĩao wa atongoi ma ndĩni kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae "nĩ kĩthĩo kyambĩĩie myakanĩ ya vakuvĩ na ĩvinda ya Atũmwa."
Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya Atũmwa mayaĩ na mũvango ũsu wa andũ kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae. O na mũtũmwa Vaulo, ũla waĩ wa ĩvinda ya Atũmwa, nĩwakanisye Aklĩsto kana kũkeethĩwa na andũ me na momanyĩsyo ma 'ũkengani' na makeethĩwa "maivata andũ kũtwaana."—1 Timotheo 4:1-3.
Mũvango ũsu wa atongoi ma ndĩni kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae wambĩĩie makanisanĩ ma Kĩklĩsto (Western "Christian" churches) kuma myakanĩ ya 100 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa. Kwosana na ĩvuku yĩtawa Celibacy and Religious Traditions, ũndũ ũsu "woosanĩte na mĩao ĩla andũ meekĩĩwe Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Lomi yamavatĩte kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ."
Myaka maana maingĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe, nzama sya makanisa na ala meetawa Avea ma Makanisa, nĩmakwatie mbau mũvango ũsu wa atongoi ma ndĩni kwĩkala matatwaanĩte. Masũanĩaa kana atongoi ma kanisa mayaaĩlĩte kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ nũndũ ũndũ ũsu waĩ ũtonya kũmavukya. Ĩndĩ ĩvuku Encyclopædia Britannica yonanĩtye kana "myakanĩ ya 901-1000 athembi aingĩ na mambisovu amwe maĩ na iveti."
Mũvango wa atongoi ma ndĩni kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae nĩwatw'ĩkie mwĩao wa lasima ĩvindanĩ yĩla Nzama sya Lateran (Lateran Councils) syoombanĩie Lomi mwakanĩ wa 1123 na 1139. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu mwĩao ũsu nĩw'o ũatĩĩawa nĩ Kanisa wa Katholeki. Mwĩao ũsu nĩwatetheeisye kanisa ndĩkaendeee kwasya malĩ na ũkũmũ wayo, ũndũ ũla weethĩawa ĩla athembi ala matwaanĩte manenga syana syoo malĩ ya kanisa ta ũtiĩwa.
WONI WA NGAI ĨŨLŨ WA KWĨKALA ŨTATWAANĨTE KANA ŨTE MŨTWAE
Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia, nĩyonanĩtye ũtheinĩ woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kwĩkala ũtatwaanĩte kana ũte mũtwae. Mbivilianĩ, nĩtũsomaa ũndũ Yesũ wawetie ĩũlũ wa ala mekalile matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae, o tondũ we weekie, "kwondũ wa ũsumbĩ wa ĩtu." (Mathayo 19:12) O na ĩngĩ, mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwaneenie ĩũlũ wa Aklĩsto ala manyuvie kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake ya kwĩkala atatwaanĩte "kwondũ wa ũla ũvoo mũseo."—1 Akolintho 7:37, 38; 9:23.
Ĩndĩ Yesũ na Vaulo mayaumasya mwĩao athũkũmi ma Ngai mekale matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae. Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana ti kĩla Mũklĩsto wĩ na mũthĩnzĩo wa kwĩkala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae. Na ĩla Vaulo waandĩkie ĩũlũ wa "eĩtu [kana, ala mataaĩsa kũtwaana kana kũtwawa]," aisye ũũ: "Ndi na mwĩao wa Mwĩaĩi: ĩndĩ nĩmũtavya ũndũ ngwona."—Mathayo 19:11; 1 Akolintho 7:25.
O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana Aklĩsto aingĩ ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa, ta mũtũmwa Vetelo, nĩmatwaanĩte. (Mathayo 8:14; Maliko 1:29-31; 1 Akolintho 9:5) O na nũndũ wa mwĩkalĩle mũthũku wa ũlaalai ũla waendeee isionĩ ila syaĩ ungu wa Ũsumbĩ wa Lomi, Vaulo nĩwaandĩkie kana ethĩwa mũsyaĩĩsya nũtwaanĩte, aaĩle kwĩthĩwa "mũũme wa kĩveti o kĩmwe" na ayĩthĩwa na "syana syĩ na wĩnyivyo."—1 Timotheo 3:2, 4.
Ĩsu ndyaĩ mĩtwaano andũ maaĩle kwĩkalany'a mate kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ, nũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye nesa kana "mũndũ mũũme namũnenge mũka wake ũla ũmwaĩle," na kana ala matwaanĩte mayaĩle 'kũvatana' kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. (1 Akolintho 7:3-5) Kwoou, Mbivilia ndyumĩtye mwĩao andũ mekale matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae, na ti lasima athũkũmi ma Ngai meke ũu.
KWONDŨ WA ŨLA ŨVOO MŨSEO
Ethĩwa ti lasima mũndũ kwĩkala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae, nĩkĩ ndeto sya Yesũ na Vaulo syĩkwonany'a kana nĩ kavaa mũndũ akekala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae? Nũndũ ĩla mũndũ wekala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae nĩwĩthĩawa na ĩvinda yingĩ ya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo. Ala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae nĩmethĩawa matonya kwĩyumya mũnango ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai nũndũ mayĩthĩawa na mawetu ala makwataa ala matwaanĩte.—1 Akolintho 7:32-35.
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya David, ũla watwie kũtia wĩa wa mbesa mbingĩ taoninĩ ya Mexico City na athamĩĩa nthĩ ya Costa Rica kũmanyĩsya andũ Mbivilia. We David nĩwonaa kwĩthĩwa atatwaanĩte kwamũtetheeisye eanĩsye ũndũ ũsu? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Vate nzika kwĩthĩwa ndatwaanĩte nĩkwandethisye." Ongeleele kwasya: "Ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũmanyĩa kwĩkala kũndũ kwĩ syĩthĩo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mawetu maingĩ, ĩndĩ nũndũ ndyaĩ na andũ angĩ ma kũsũvĩa, kũmanyĩa kwaĩ laisangi."
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Claudia, ũla wathamĩĩie isionĩ syĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma ũvoo mũseo, aĩtye: "Nĩndanĩaa kũmũthũkũma Ngai. Noona ũndũ Ngai ũnzũvĩĩte, mũĩkĩĩo wakwa na ngwatanĩo yakwa nake nilũlũmĩĩlaa."
"Wamũthũkũma Yeova Ngai na ngoo yonthe, ndũema kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu, wĩthĩwe nũtwaanĩte kana ndũtwaanĩte."—Claudia
Ethĩwa ndũtonya kwĩkala ũtatwaanĩte kana ũte mũtwae, ti nginya wĩkale ũu. Claudia ongeleele kwasya atĩĩ: "Wamũthũkũma Yeova Ngai na ngoo yonthe, ndũema kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu, wĩthĩwe nũtwaanĩte kana ndũtwaanĩte."—Savuli 119:1, 2.
