translation:
Within each religion—whether Catholic Church, many Orthodox churches, Buddhist religions, and many other religions—people often use images or statues. For many people, this may seem like using images in many religions is acceptable and respectful, and pleasing to God in this matter.
The question is whether it is right to eat meat; do the scriptures allow the use of religious images or statues? Or should we examine this issue carefully, so that we understand the truth about the use of religious images being acceptable or unacceptable, and the will of God regarding this matter.
IS THE USE OF RELIGIOUS IMAGES ACCEPTABLE AT ALL?
According to the Encyclopædia Britannica, "an idol is an image worshipped as a god or spirit, and which is believed to have power to influence or control events, and thus such an image is considered sacred." In 2006, Pope Benedict XVI, together with the council that was established to oversee matters of the Catholic Church known as the Roman Curia, stated that the use of religious images being acceptable or unacceptable "is a matter of historical and theological debate."
For early Christians and members of the apostolic church, there was opposition to the practice of people using images or statues. And the apostle Paul condemned Christians who were influenced by the teaching of "demonism" and those who practiced "immorality."—1 Timothy 4:1-3.
This opposition to the use of religious images became prominent in Western ("Christian") churches from about the 100's CE onward. According to the book Celibacy and Religious Traditions, this "was associated with ideas that those dedicated to the service of God should abstain from sexual relations."
Over many centuries, councils and leaders of various churches gradually accepted this practice of using religious images. It seems that clergy who were allowed to marry had less incentive to remain celibate. The Encyclopædia Britannica states that "in the years 901–1000 there was a considerable increase in reports of clerical marriage."
The opposition to the use of religious images became formalized through decrees issued by the Councils of Lateran, which forbade priests to marry in 1123 and 1139. From then on, this law was enforced by the Catholic Church. This law affected the church greatly and continued to cause problems and its influence, an issue that caused much trouble among the clergy and lay people alike.
THE ISSUE OF CELIBACY OR MARRIAGE
God's Word, the Bible, sheds light on the issue of celibacy or marriage. In the Bible, we read that Jesus spoke favorably of those who chose to remain unmarried "for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven." (Matthew 19:12) Also, the apostle Paul recommended that Christians who wanted to devote themselves fully to their ministry could choose to remain unmarried "to give undivided attention to the Lord."—1 Corinthians 7:37, 38; 9:23.
Jesus and Paul respected God's laws regarding celibacy or marriage. Jesus indicated that not every Christian has the gift of remaining unmarried or being married. And when Paul wrote about "virgins [or, those who have dedicated themselves to remaining unmarried]," he said: "I have no command from the Lord."—Matthew 19:11; 1 Corinthians 7:25.
Furthermore, the Bible shows that many early Christians, such as the apostle Peter, were married. (Matthew 8:14; Mark 1:29-31; 1 Corinthians 9:5) And concerning overseers—men who take the lead in congregations—Paul wrote that they should be "married only once," and that they should have "children who conduct themselves properly."—1 Timothy 3:2, 4.
So while some individuals may choose to remain unmarried, the Bible also states that "marriage is honorable," and that those who marry may find 'comfort' in doing so. (1 Corinthians 7:3-5) Clearly, the Bible does not require everyone to remain unmarried or to get married, but leaves this decision up to each individual according to God's law.
THE MATTER OF PERSONAL CHOICE
Is it wrong for a person to remain unmarried or to get married? Is it possible that a person could make a mistake in deciding whether to remain unmarried or to get married? The fact that a person remains unmarried or gets married can involve many personal factors. Those who remain unmarried or get married should give priority to pleasing Jehovah and living in harmony with his standards.—1 Corinthians 7:32-35.
Consider the example of David, who traveled thousands of miles from Mexico City to preach the good news in Costa Rica. Did David feel that remaining unmarried hindered him in this service? He says: "I found that being single allowed me to devote more time to serving Jehovah." Furthermore, he explains: "I realized that I had an opportunity to experience greater spiritual growth because I was free from many responsibilities and pressures that come with marriage, and I enjoyed my association with others."
A sister named Claudia, who has served as a full-time evangelizer for many years, says: "I want to please Jehovah. I have learned that what Jehovah provides—spiritual strength and emotional support—is far more valuable than what a husband could offer."
"Love Jehovah your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength, whether you are unmarried or married."—Claudia
It is therefore possible to be happy whether unmarried or married, but it requires effort. Claudia further explains: "Love Jehovah your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength, whether you are unmarried or married."—Psalm 119:1, 2.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA 1952
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE UNITED STATES
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU NATHATAA NA MĨTŨKĨ
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Neanĩie Los Angeles, California, U.S.A., isionĩ syĩsĩkĩe mũno nũndũ wa ũng'endu na ndawa sya kũmila. Twasyaĩtwe twĩ thanthatũ, na ninyie naĩ wa kelĩ.
Inyia wakwa atũeeie ndĩninĩ ya evangelical. Nĩ wa mũika, ndyekalaa kwosana na maũndũ ala neemanyĩasya ndĩninĩ. Wakyumwa nainaa kwaya ĩkanisanĩ, nayo mĩthenya ĩla ĩngĩ naendaa kwĩtanĩthya, kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila, na kwĩka ũlaalai.
Nathataa mĩtũkĩ na naĩ mũng'endu, na natũmĩaa kĩndũ kyonthe kĩla nakwata nĩkũne mũndũ. Maũndũ ala neemanyĩasya kanisanĩ mayandethasya. Naasya atĩĩ, "Ũĩvanĩsyo nĩ wa Mwĩaĩi, na ninyie ũtũmĩaa kũĩvanĩsya!" Nĩ sekondalĩ myakanĩ ya 1960, nĩnalikanile na kyama kya siasa kyeetawa Black Panthers. Kyama kĩu kĩsĩkĩe nũndũ wa kũtetea andũ na kũkitĩa mavata ma ene nthĩ. O na nĩnalikile kĩkundinĩ kya kũtetea mavata ma syana sya sukulu. Mavinda maingĩ nĩtwaluaa nduuthĩ na kĩla ĩvinda ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumaa sukulu ĩvingwa kwa ĩvinda.
Nũndũ naĩ mũng'endu mũno, navikie vandũ weethĩa kũlua nduuthĩ kũyĩũmbĩanĩa. Na nũndũ wa ũu, nĩneelikilye maũndũnĩ maingĩ ma ũng'endu nũndũ wa kĩmena. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩ na anyanyawa nĩtwasyaisye sinema syoonanasya ũndũ andũ ma Africa ala maĩ ngombo mathĩnĩaw'a nthĩ ya United States. Nĩtwathatiw'e mũno nĩ ũndũ ũsu, na twamavũa andũ ma mũika asũngũ ala mookĩte kũsisya sinema. Ĩtina wa ũu, twaendie isionĩ ila syaĩ vakuvĩ syekalaa asũngũ tũimamantha tũmavũe.
Nĩ vakuvĩ myaka 20, nĩ na aũme ala tũsyaanĩw'e nĩtweesĩkĩe kana twĩ ing'endilĩ. Nĩtwathĩnanasya na volisi mavinda maingĩ. Mũinawa ũmwe aĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩthũku kya ing'endilĩ na nĩneethĩawa na ngwatanĩo namo. Naendeee kũthũkĩĩa.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Naĩ na mũnyanyawa ũmwe ũla asyai make maĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Nĩmanthokisye maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto, na neetĩkĩla kũthi. Kuma mwambĩĩonĩ, nĩnoonie Ngũsĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kĩla mũndũ aĩ na Mbivilia yake na nĩwamĩtũmĩaa ĩla maũmbano maendeee. O namo andũ ma mũika nĩmaumisye maũvoo ũmbanonĩ ũsu! Ũndũ ũla wambendeeisye mũno nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ Yeova, na kwĩw'a yĩitũmĩwa. (Savuli 83:18) Andũ ala maĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩu maĩ ma mbaĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, ĩndĩ mayaanĩkĩte.
Mwambĩĩonĩ ndyendaa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ, ĩndĩ nĩnendete kũthi maũmbanonĩ moo. Wĩoo ũmwe nĩ maũmbanonĩ asu, kĩkundi kĩmwe kya anyanyawa nĩkyaendie wathinĩ vandũ. Me kũu, nĩmakũnie kamwana kamwe kakw'a nũndũ nĩkaleile kaimanenga ngyaketi (leather jacket) yako. Mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe, meekũnaa kĩthũi nũndũ wa kũwaa kamwana kau. O na me kotinĩ maisilĩlwa, mayoonaa ta ve ũndũ mekĩte. Aingĩ moo matw'ĩĩiwe kwovwa nginya ĩla mekw'a. Nĩnatanie mũno nũndũ ndyaĩ namo wĩoo ũsu. Nĩnatwie kũalyũka na sndyambĩĩsya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia.
Nũndũ kwa myaka mingĩ nĩnekalanasya na andũ mamenete andũ ala mataĩ ma mbaĩ yoo, ve maũndũ amwe Ngũsĩ syeekaa manzeng'asya. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mũsũngũ ũmwe waĩ Ngũsĩ wavangie kũthi nthĩ ĩngĩ, atiie syana syake iyĩewa nĩ mũsyĩ ũmwe wa andũ aiũ. O na ĩngĩ, mũsyĩ ũmwe wa mũsũngũ nĩwoosie kamwana kamwe ka mũndũ mwiũ kala kataĩ na vandũ kekala. Maũndũ asu matumie nĩĩkĩĩa kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova niatĩĩaa ndeto ii sya Yesũ syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Yoana 13:35, yĩla yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Na kwondũ wa ũu andũ onthe makamanya kana mwĩ amanyĩw'a makwa, ethĩwa mwĩthĩwa na wendo inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ.' Nĩnamanyie kana nĩnakwata ana-a-asa ma w'o.
Ĩla neemanyĩisye Mbivilia nĩnamanyie kana naaĩlĩte kũalyũla mosũanĩo makwa. Yaĩ no nginya nĩvĩndũe mosũanĩo makwa nĩ kana nĩthĩwe na mũuo na andũ ala angĩ, na ndyona ũsu wĩ ũndũ wa vata vyũ thayũnĩ wakwa. (Alomi 12:2) Nĩnaendeeie kwĩka maendeeo, na Mwei wa 1, 1974 navatiswa na natw'ĩka Ngũsĩ ya Yeova.
Yaĩ no nginya nĩvĩndũe mosũanĩo makwa nĩ kana nĩthĩwe na mũuo na andũ ala angĩ, na ndyona ũsu wĩ ũndũ wa vata vyũ thayũnĩ wakwa
Ĩndĩ o na ĩtina wa kũvatiswa, yaĩ nginya nĩendeee kũng'ang'ana wĩthĩe ndiũthata mĩtũkĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũthenya ũmwe nĩ ũtavany'a wa nyũmba na nyũmba, nasembanisye na kĩng'ei kĩmwe kyooyĩte letiũ ngalĩnĩ yakwa. Ĩla nakĩthengeeie kyalekilye letiũ ĩsu na kyasemba. Ĩla naeleisye ala angĩ twatavanasya ĩmwe, mũtumĩa ũmwe wa kĩkundi ũla waĩ vau angũlilye atĩĩ: "Stephen, keka nũkwatie kĩng'ei kyu wĩthĩwa wĩkanie nakyo ata?" Ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩyatumie nzũanĩa mũno na noona naĩlĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩthĩwe nĩ mũndũ wa mũuo.
Mwei wa 10, 1974, nĩnatw'ĩkie mũtavany'a wa ĩvinda yonthe na natavanasya masaa 100 kĩla mwei. Ĩtina wa ũu, nĩnakwatie kĩanda kya kũthũkũma ovisinĩ ũla mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũla wĩ Brooklyn, New York. Mwaka wa 1978, nĩnasyokie Los Angeles nĩ kana ngasũvĩe inyia wakwa nũndũ aĩ mũwau. Ĩtina wa myaka ĩlĩ, nĩnatwaie kĩveti kyakwa kĩla kĩtawa Aarhonda. Kĩveti kyu kyakwa nĩkyandetheeisye mũno kũsũvĩa inyia wakwa kũvika ĩla wakwie. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, nĩtweetiwe Sukulu ya Mbivilia ya Ngileati na twatũmwa nthĩ ya Panama ta amisonalĩ.
Kuma navatiswa nĩngomanĩte na maũndũ matonya kũtuma nĩthilĩka mũno. Nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye kana nĩnaĩle kwĩvetangana na andũ ala meũnthokoa, kana ngatata ũndũ ndonya nĩthĩwe nĩ mũuu. Kĩveti kyakwa vamwe na andũ angĩ aingĩ methĩĩtwe maindũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa ũndũ nĩthĩĩtwe ndyĩka ĩla nakwatwa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtuma nĩthata. O nakwa mavinda maingĩ nĩnzeng'aa! Ĩndĩ nditonya kwasya nĩalyũkĩte kwa vinya wakwa. Vandũ va ũu, ũndũ ũsu ũndĩkĩĩthasya ũtonyi ũla Mbivilia yĩ naw'o wa kũalyũla andũ.—Aevelania 4:12.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Mbivilia nĩndetheesye kũmanya nĩkĩ nĩ thayũ, o na nĩmanyĩĩtye ũndũ ndonya kwĩkala na mũuo na andũ ala angĩ. Yu vandũ va kũvũa andũ, nĩmatetheeasya kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye Mbivilia mũndũ ũmwe twamenanĩte twĩ sukulu! Avatiswa, nĩtwekalile nyũmba ĩmwe kwa ĩvinda, na nginya ũmũnthĩ twĩ ndũũ mũno. Kũvikĩĩa ũmũnthĩ, nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtwĩmanyĩĩtye Mbivilia na andũ mbee wa 80, na makatw'ĩka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
Nĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kũtuma nĩmanya vata wa kwĩthĩwa nĩ thayũ, na akandetheesya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu nĩ katĩkatĩ wa ana-a-asa.

translation:
LET IT BE THE YEAR 1952
WHEN I WAS IN THE UNITED STATES
MY HANDS WERE DIRTY WITH DUST
FOR EXAMPLE:
Recently Los Angeles, California, U.S.A., has become very famous for drug trafficking and murder. We were arrested several times, and you too will be caught.
My children became evangelicals. They are good, and I stayed away from things that could lead them astray. They joined a church choir, and many others went to preach, using drugs and causing chaos.
My hands were dirty with dust, and I used everything I had to help people. Things that led people astray destroyed the church. And they said, "Salvation comes from God, and you use it to destroy!" It was in the second half of the 1960s when I joined a political group called the Black Panthers. This group sought to defend people and fight against injustice. And I joined the struggle to protect the rights of schoolchildren. Many schools were closed due to violence, and each incident caused schools to be shut down.
The situation was very bad, and I saw people struggling to survive. And because of this, I experienced many hardships during my youth. For example, once we showed a film about how African Americans were being oppressed in the United States. We were greatly disturbed by this, and we encouraged local people to stop watching the film. Because of this, we went to places where young people gathered to educate them and encourage them.
I was 20 years old, and I had friends who thought we were crazy. We clashed with police many times. One man was involved in a lot of trouble and I helped him escape arrest. I continued to cause problems.
THIS IS WHAT I WANT TO TELL YOU:
I have a friend who shows his books from Jehovah's Witnesses. I appreciate the Christian teachings, and I want to learn more. However, I told him I don't like being bothered. Everyone has their own Bible and I use mine at meetings. Oh, but local people really appreciate this good news! What moved me deeply was realizing that God's name is Jehovah, and wanting to be used by Him. (Psalm 83:18) Those who hate His name and bother people, will be destroyed.
However, I want to learn about the Bible and Jehovah, so I continue to study the teachings. One thing is certain, a group of young people goes out to teach others. Just now, I reminded a boy who did something wrong to return your leather jacket. The day he returned it, I told him to remember what it means to steal from someone. Also, even though I am still learning, I hope you understand what I mean. Many things happened that I can't explain. I am truly grateful for everything you have done for me. I decided to try to learn about the Bible.
For many years I associated with people who were different from those around us, and some didn't believe in God. For example, one man from our area said that his daughter got sick because of someone else's child. And another time, someone stole a boy from a family and they couldn't find him. These things made me realize that Jehovah God cares for us, and He showed this through Jesus Christ, as stated in John 13:35, which says: "By this everyone will know that you are my disciples—if you have love for one another." I realized I had been wrong.
After studying the Bible, I realized I needed to change my thinking. It seemed strange to me that I was treated badly by others and yet I continued to trust them, but now I see how important it is to avoid bad associations. (Romans 12:2) I continued to progress, and on May 1, 1974, I was baptized and began to worship Jehovah.
It seemed strange to me that I was treated badly by others and yet I continued to trust them, but now I see how important it is to avoid bad associations.
Despite the challenges of being baptized, I continued to strive to be honest in all my dealings. For instance, one day while going from house to house, I spoke with a neighbor who asked me about the literature I was carrying. But I refused to leave the literature with him and went on my way. However, I later learned that he and others were discussing what we were doing, and one member of the group told him: "Stephen, why don't you let me take the literature so I can read it?" That situation helped me understand that sometimes people need time to think about things before they accept the truth.
On October 10, 1974, I began pioneering throughout the circuit and spent 100 hours each month in the ministry. As a result, I was able to obtain a small room in the large Bethel Home of the Watch Tower Society in Brooklyn, New York. In 1978, I moved to Los Angeles where I hoped to find more opportunities to help others. Over the years, I drove my own car—a Honda Civic—to meetings and in the ministry. My car was very reliable and helped me reach people far and wide. While in the circuit, I was invited to Gilead School and then assigned to serve in Panama as a missionary.
I have been grateful for the training I received and for the opportunity to share the good news. I realize that I may face opposition from some people, or that someone might mistreat me, but I will continue to trust in Jehovah. Like many others, I have experienced difficulties and trials, but I have found strength in knowing that God cares for us and helps us cope with problems. And I have had many wonderful experiences! I am determined to keep progressing in the truth. Brothers, this matter should make us feel the seriousness of the Bible's counsel regarding discerning people.—Revelation 4:12.
LESSONS I HAVE LEARNED:
The Bible has helped me understand what is right, and it has also taught me how to maintain peace with other Christians. You young ones, please allow yourselves to be guided by sincere love for God. For example, I learned much about the Bible from a friend I met at school! As missionaries, we lived in one house during our service, and often we shared meals together. Because of this arrangement, I was able to study the Bible with over 80 people, and they came to worship Jehovah.
I thank Jehovah for helping me learn how to discern what is right, and he has enabled me to remain neutral in times of difficulty.—Proverbs 3:5, 6.

text:
WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA?
Mwĩĩtu wĩtawa Annette ayĩelesya ũndũ wakwatiwe easya kana ayĩsa kũmanya eeyĩthĩĩile ekiw'e nthĩ nĩ mũndũ ũla wamũkwatie. Easya atĩĩ: "Nĩnatatie ũndũ ndonya nĩmũsiĩĩe. O na nĩnatatie kua mbu ĩndĩ wasya ndwaauma. Namũkunie ngundi, namũsukuma na vinya, namũtheelanga, na namũkalangya. Nakililye nĩendeee kwĩka maũndũ asu neew'a andinĩĩsya kavyũ. Ĩla neewie kavyũ kau, neewie vinya wathela vyũ!"
Ũkakwata nĩ ũndũ ta ũũ wakwatie Annette wĩka ata?
AMBA KŨSŨANĨA!
O na kau no wĩthĩwe wĩ metho ndũkakwatwe nĩ ũndũ mũthũku, mavinda angĩ maũndũ mathũku nĩmatonya kũũkwata. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũsemba ũkĩlanyonĩ ti kwa ala me mĩtũkĩ, . . kana ũseo kwa ala me na ũtũĩka; ĩndĩ ĩvinda na ĩvuso [kana, "ũndũ ũtataĩĩwe," NWT] nĩsyĩkĩkaa kwa onthe."—Mũtavan'ya 9:11.
Andũ amwe ma mũika ta Annette, makwatawa kya vinya nĩ andũ matamesĩ. Angĩ namo makwatawa nĩ anyanyae kana andũ ma mũsyĩ. Mwĩĩtu wĩtawa Natalie akwatiwe nĩ kĩmwana kyekalaa vakuvĩ na kwoo. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mbeenĩ nĩnatelemile mũno na neew'aa nthoni ũkethĩa o na nditavya mũndũ."
NDŨKETŨLE MŨTĨ
O na kũvika ũmũnthĩ Annette nĩwĩw'aa aithĩnĩka ngoonĩ nũndũ wa ũndũ ũla wamũkwatie. Easya atĩĩ: "Ũndũ ũsu weekĩkie mũthenya ũsu ũtindĩaa kũka kĩlĩkonĩ kĩla ĩvinda. Nonaa naaĩle kũng'ang'ana mũno mũndũ ũsu ndakangwate. Ũw'o nĩ kana ĩla mũndũ ũsu wandonyie na kavyũ oou, neewie vinya wathela vyũ. Ndyaĩ ũndũ naĩ nĩka ĩndĩ nonaa naaĩle kũng'ang'ana mũnango."
Nake Natalie no ũthĩnĩkaa nũndũ wa kĩko kĩu kĩthũku weekiwe. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndyaaĩle kũĩkĩĩa kĩmwana kĩu mũno. Asyai maitũ maĩ matũtavisye nĩ na mwĩĩtu tũsyaanĩw'e kana twaĩle kwĩthĩawa vamwe kĩla ĩvinda ĩla tũũthaũka, ĩndĩ ndyaaĩthukĩĩsya. Kwoou nonaa no inyie nanengie kĩmwana kĩu mwanya. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwaũmĩisye andũ ma mũsyĩ, na nonaa naĩle kũtũlwa mũtĩ nũndũ wa kũtuma maũmĩa. Kũmanya ũu nĩkũnũmĩasya ngoo mũno."
Ethĩwa wĩw'aa ta Annette kana Natalie, lilikana kana mũndũ ũla wakwatwa kya vinya ndethĩawa ayenda kũkoma na mũndũ ũla wamũkwata. Andũ amwe nĩmavũthĩĩasya ũndũ ũsu na mayasya kana nĩ ũndũ wĩthĩawa kwa imwana kwĩka maũndũ asu, kana mayasya wĩthĩawa wĩ thĩna wa kwĩmanthĩa kwa ala makwatwa. Vai mũndũ wĩsa kwenda kũkwatwa. Ethĩwa waaĩkwa kĩko kĩu kĩthũkĩte ũu, ndwaĩle kwĩtũla mũtĩ!
Kwasya kana "ndwaĩle kwĩtũla mũtĩ" no woneke wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi, ĩndĩ ti laisi kũĩkĩĩa ũndũ ũsu. Andũ amwe nĩmavithaa ũndũ ũsu vyũ, na ũu ũituma maũmĩa mũno kana mambĩĩa kwĩtũla mũtĩ. Ĩndĩ nũũ ũla waĩle kũvitha ũndũ ũla weekĩkie? Nue kana nĩ ũla waũkwatie? Ethĩwa ũtwĩe ũvithĩte ũndũ ũsu, yu nĩwaĩle kũsũanĩa ũndũ ũngĩ wa kwĩka.
KŨELESYA KĨLA KYEETHĨIWE
Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ĩla Yovu waĩ na mathĩna maingĩ vyũ aisye atĩĩ: "Nganeena ũũnĩ wa ngoo yakwa." (Yovu 10:1) O naku no ũtetheke ũkeka ta Yovu. Kũelesya mũndũ ũmũĩkĩĩe ĩũlũ wa kĩla kyaũkwatie no kũũtetheesye ũkew'a ngoo yausya, na ũkaeka kũthĩnĩka.
Ũndũ ũsu nĩwamũtethisye Annette. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnatavisye mũnyanyawa ũndũ ũsu, na ambĩa nĩneene na atumĩa ma kĩkundi. Nĩ na ũtanu mũno nũndũ nĩneekie ũu. Nĩmaneenie nakwa mavinda maingĩ na mandetheesya kũmanya kana ndyaĩ ngenda yakwa mũndũ ũsu angwate. Ũsu nĩw'o ũndũ ũla nendaa kwĩw'a andũ maindavya. Vai ũndũ o na ũmwe naaĩka waĩle kũtuma nĩtũlwa mũtĩ."
Nake Natalie aneenie na asyai make. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩmandetheeisye mũno. Nĩmambĩkĩie vinya nĩmaelesye kĩla kyeekĩkie na kwĩka ũu nĩkwandetheeisye nĩeke kwĩmakĩa na kwĩthĩwa na woo ngoonĩ."
Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kyamũtetheeisye Natalie nĩ mboya. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũneena na Ngai nĩkwandetheeisye, na mũno mũno mavinda ala neew'aa vate mũndũ ndonya kũmũtavya ũndũ ngwĩw'a. Ĩla ngũvoya no nĩelesye Ngai kĩla kyonthe kĩ ngoonĩ, na ũu nũtumaa nĩthĩwa na mũuo na ndyĩw'a nausya."
Weeka ũu, o naku ũkamanya kana 've ĩvinda ya kũvoa.' (Mũtavan'ya 3:3) Ĩka maũndũ meũkũtetheesya ndũkaendeee kũũmĩsya ngoo na mwĩĩ waku, na ũyĩĩkĩĩthya kana nĩwakoma too wĩanĩtye. Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kũmwĩkwatya Yeova, Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe.—2 Akolintho 1:3, 4.
ETHĨWA NŨVIKĨTYE MYAKA ŨTONYA KWAMBĨĨA KWĨVAAW'A
Ethĩwa wĩ mwĩĩtu na nũũthing'ĩĩw'a wĩke ũndũ ũtaĩle, ti ũthũku kwĩa mũndũ ũsu ũte na wia atĩĩ, "Ndekye!" kana "Ndikwenda ngũĩ ĩsu!" O na ethĩwa mwĩ ndũũ, ndũkaeme kũmũtavya nũndũ wĩkĩa ayĩũtia. Akaũtia nũndũ nĩwamũvata kwĩka ũu, waĩle kũmanya kana ũsu ti mũndũũme mũseo! Mũndũũme mũseo aĩle kũnenga mwĩĩ waku ndaĩa na ainenga ndaĩa myolooto yaku ĩla ũatĩĩaa.
SŨNGĨA MAKŨLYO AA
"Twĩ sukulu, imwana syakusasya sindilia yakwa syĩ ĩtina wakwa na iindavya ndeto itaĩle ta kũmbĩa, 'Mwa ngakoma naku koo nĩnĩw'a mũyo.'"—Coretta.
We wĩona imwana isu ta syeekaa ũndũ wĩva katĩ wa maũndũ aa:
Kũmũvũĩa ngũĩ?
Kũmũthaũkĩa?
Kũmũthĩny'a?
"Twĩ ngalĩnĩ, kĩmwana kĩmwe kyambĩĩie kũndavya maũndũ mathũku na kyambĩĩa kũngwatanga. Nakĩkanĩsye moko asu kũasa na nakĩa kĩvetange vala nĩĩ. Kĩmwana kĩu kyoonie nĩ mũtumanu mũno."—Candice.
We wĩona kĩmwana kĩu ta kyeekaa ũndũ wĩva katĩ wa maũndũ aa:
Kũmũvũĩa ngũĩ?
Kũmũthaũkĩa?
Kũmũthĩny'a?
"Mwaka mũvĩtu, ve kĩmwana kyatindĩaa kũmbĩa kana kĩenda tũthi vandũ, o na kau natindĩaa kũkĩa kana ndikwenda. Mavinda amwe kyangwatangaa kw'oko. Ĩndĩ nakĩaa kĩeke kũngwatanga na kĩilea. Na ĩndĩ ĩla nakumanie nove kĩatũ, kyangũna kĩtimba."—Bethany.
We ũtonya kwasya kĩmwana kĩu kyeekaa ũndũ wĩva katĩ wa maũndũ aa:
Kũmũvũĩa ngũĩ?
Kũmũthaũkĩa?
Kũmũthĩny'a?
Ũsũngĩo ũla wa w'o wa makũlyo asu me atatũ nĩ namba 3.
Ve kĩvathũkany'o kyaũ katĩ wa kũthĩny'a mũndũ na kũmũvũĩa ngũĩ kana kũmũthaũkĩa?
Kũthĩny'a mũndũ kwonanasya kana ũla ũngĩ ndekwendeew'a nĩ maũndũ ala ũkwĩkwa. O na ĩla mũndũ ũla ũkũthĩnw'a wasya ndekwenda kĩla ũla ũngĩ ũkũmwĩka, ũsu ũngĩ aendeeaa kwĩka kĩla wavatwa.
Kũthĩny'a mũndũ ti ũndũ waĩle kwoswa laisi nũndũ ũla ũkũthĩnany'a aema kũsiĩĩwa no alasimĩthye ũsu ũngĩ makome ĩmwe.

translation:
ARE YOU WORTH IT?
The beautiful woman Annette wondered whether her marriage was easy or whether she knew why her husband loved her. She said: "I thought I did something to deserve it. And I thought being beautiful made him love me. But I flattered him, I pleased him, I cooked for him, and I dressed nicely for him. And still I kept asking myself what he would think if he knew my secrets. But knowing his secrets doesn't make him love me more!"
What is it about marriage that makes Annette wonder like this?
CONSIDER THIS!
And even if you were married because of some mistake, many things can make a marriage worth saving. The Bible says: "Wisdom is better than weapons of war, . . . or a foolish person who has come to ruin; even a little bit of wisdom and discipline [or, "something good," NWT] is better than ruling."—Ecclesiastes 9:11.
Some women like Annette have been hurt by abusive husbands. Others have been hurt by their boyfriends or former husbands. A woman named Natalie was abused by her much older husband. She said: "I felt so helpless and I didn't know where to turn."
LET US REASON TOGETHER
And sometimes Annette feels frustrated because of the way her husband treats her. She says: "This situation really bothers me because it happens almost every day. Sometimes I feel like giving up on this man I married. It's like he doesn't appreciate me at all, and he just wants to be pleased. I wish I knew what I could do to make him happy."
Natalie also feels frustrated because of the pain she has experienced. She says: "I don't want to raise a child in this environment. I see my parents fighting all the time and I don't want our children to grow up seeing that, I would be very upset. That's why I think I need to separate from this man. This situation has affected many people, and I don't want to continue suffering because of sending messages."
Whether it's Annette or Natalie, or anyone who has been hurt by an abusive husband, they should seek help from someone who can advise them. Some people sympathize with this situation and wonder if it's something that happened to a child due to some mistakes, or they wonder if it's a result of being raised badly by those who were abused. Don't let anyone force you to get involved. This situation is serious, so please seek help!
When someone says "don't let yourself get involved" it seems like a small thing, but it's not a small thing when it comes to this issue. Some people understand this matter well, and it causes them pain or fear to get involved. But how will you feel if you witness this happening? Or if it happens to you? Let us learn from this experience, so that we can avoid making similar mistakes.
TO UNDERSTAND EVERY SITUATION
Job once said: "Even if I speak about my sorrow, it will never end." (Job 10:1) So, remember to be patient with Job. To comfort someone who is experiencing difficulty and to encourage them to express their feelings, and to listen carefully.
This situation also affected Annette. She says: "I have suffered greatly because of this, and I told her to report it to the authorities. I have been through a lot and I want to know if this person will ever arrest my abuser. This is what makes me want to leave him."
Natalie also shared her experience. She says: "I was very worried. I tried to understand everything that was happening and I realized that I needed help and support."
Another thing that helped Natalie was prayer. She says: "Praying to God has given me strength, and now I believe that someone will come to help me. I trust in God completely, and this helps me to cope and to forgive others."
Remember that 'there is a time to be courageous.' (Ecclesiastes 3:3) So, continue to strengthen your faith and confidence in God, and don't give up hope. And always remember that fearing Jehovah, the Almighty God, is the beginning of wisdom.—2 Corinthians 1:3, 4.
LET US LEARN FROM THE PAST TO AVOID REPEATING IT
When we see someone making a mistake, we may feel like saying, "I told you so!" or "I knew something like this would happen!" But instead, let us try to help them without criticizing. Helping them can show them how to avoid repeating the same mistake in the future, and it shows that you are considerate! A considerate person does not judge others harshly and does not hold grudges, even when they have been wronged.
CONSIDER THESE QUESTIONS
"In school, a child might struggle with a subject and need extra help, but he doesn't want to admit it," says Coretta.
Let's look at some ways a child might express feeling this way:
Is he frustrated?
Is he embarrassed?
Is he angry?
"At first, one student told me she was having trouble with her homework and asked me to explain it again. I happily agreed to help her. The student then showed me how much she had improved," says Candice.
Let's look at some ways that student might express feeling this way:
Is he frustrated?
Is he embarrassed?
Is he angry?
"Last year, a child started to cry or run away from people, or sometimes he just refused to speak or cooperate. Many times, I found myself wanting to get upset with him and scold him. But I realized that he needed encouragement and support." — Bethany.
Let's look at how that child might express feeling this way:
Is he frustrated?
Is he embarrassed?
Is he angry?
The next part of this series will be in issue number 3.
What is the difference between disciplining a person and frustrating them or embarrassing them?
Disciplining a person should always be done calmly and respectfully, and it should focus on correcting behavior, not attacking character. But when a person who disciplines gets upset and loses control, they often end up causing more harm than good.
Disciplining a person is not easy, especially when the person being disciplined resists and refuses to listen or cooperate. But it is important to remain calm and respectful.

text:
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũlya . . . nyũnyi sya yayaya, na ikakũtavya: Nũũ ũla ũtesĩ kwondũ wa isu syonthe, Kana kw'oko kwa Yeova nĩkwĩkĩte ũu"?—Yovu 12:7, 9.
MBEE wa myaka 3,000 mĩvĩtu, Yovu nĩwoonanisye kana nyũnyi sya yayaya nitũmanyĩasya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa wũmbi wa Ngai. Nyũnyi no itũmĩke ta ngelekany'o ya kũmanyĩsya kana ya kũelekany'a syĩndũ kumana na ũndũ syũmbĩtwe na ũndũ syĩkaa maũndũ. Mbivilianĩ ve kũndũ kwingĩ nyũnyi sya yayaya itũmĩĩtwe ta ngelekany'o sya kũtũmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ twaĩlĩte kwĩkala na ĩũlũ wa ngwatanĩo yitũ na Ngai. Ekai twone ngelekany'o imwe.
VALA NTHŨNGŨLŨLŨ SYAKAA NDALA
Andũ ala mekalaa Yelusaleme nĩmeesĩ maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthũngũlũlũ, ila syakaa ndala syoo ungu wa iala sya nyũmba. Imwe syakaa ndala ĩkalũnĩ ya Solomoni. Nĩvatonyeka nthũngũlũlũ ila syaakaa ndala ĩkalũnĩ kĩla mwaka ikethĩwa syeew'aa ve vandũ vauĩtye, itonya kũeea tũswii twasyo iteũthĩnw'a.
Mũandĩki wa ĩvuku ya Savuli 84, ũla waĩ ũmwe wa syana sya Kola, na wathũkũmaa ĩkalũnĩ kyumwa kĩmwe nthĩnĩ wa kĩla myei thanthatũ nĩwoonie ndala isu syaĩ ĩkalũnĩ. Nũndũ aĩ na mea ma kwĩthĩwa ailyĩ ta nthũngũlũlũ ila mavinda onthe ndala yasyo yeethĩawa nyũmbanĩ ya Yeova, aisye atĩĩ: "A! mawĩkalo maku nĩ maseo, We Yeova wa nguthu! Ngoo yakwa yĩ na mea, ĩĩ, o na kũthelekela kwondũ wa nza sya Yeova; . . . Ĩĩ, mũthoonzwe nĩwĩyoneete nyũmba, Na nthũngũlũlũ ndala, vala ĩtonya kwia tũswii twayo, O ithembeonĩ syaku, we Yeova wa nguthu, Mũsumbĩ wakwa, na Ngai wakwa." (Savuli 84:1-3) Ithyĩ, vamwe na syana sitũ, nĩtwĩthĩawa na wendi mwingĩ wa kwĩthĩwa kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma Yeova kĩla ĩvinda?—Savuli 26:8, 12.
ĨSAŨ NĨYĨSĨ MAVINDA MAYO
Mwathani Yelemia aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ĩsaũ ya yayaya nĩyĩsĩ mavinda mayo." Nĩweesĩ nesa vyũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ masaũ mathamaa mesĩlĩte Nthĩ ya Watho. Ĩvinda ya mbevo yathela, masaũ mbee wa 300,000 nĩmathamaa kuma Africa nginya Northern Europe mesĩle Jordan Valley. Masaũ asu nĩmethĩawa na kĩndũ nthĩnĩ wamo (internal clock) kĩla kĩmatetheeasya kũmanya ĩvinda ya kũsyoka ĩngĩ kũla masyaanĩaa ĩvinda ya thano yavika. O ta nyũnyi ila ingĩ ithamaa, masaũ 'nĩmalilikanaa ĩvinda ya kũsyoka kwamo.'—Yelemia 8:7.
Ĩvuku yĩtawa Collins Atlas of Bird Migration yonanĩtye kana ũndũ ũla wa ũsengy'a nĩ kana ve kĩndũ kĩ nthĩnĩ wa nyũnyi kĩtumaa imanya ĩvinda yĩla syaĩle kũthama. Yeova Ngai oombie nyũnyi syĩ na kĩndũ kĩu kĩitetheeasye kũmanya ĩvinda yĩla syaĩle kũthama, ĩndĩ anenga mũndũ ũtonyi wa kũmanya mavinda. (Luka 12:54-56) Kĩvathũkany'o na ũĩ ũla wĩthĩawa masaũnĩ, ũmanyi wa Ngai nĩw'o ũtumaa mũndũ aelewa maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na aimanya atwĩe ĩvinda yĩva. Ĩvindanĩ ya Yelemia, Aisilaeli nĩmavũthĩĩisye maũndũ ala maaĩle kũmatetheesya kũmanya matwĩe ĩvinda yĩva. Ngai nĩwaeleisye vala vaĩ thĩna kwa kwasya atĩĩ: "Nĩmaleete ndeto ya Yeova; na nĩ ũĩ mwaũ wĩ nthĩnĩ woo?"—Yelemia 8:9.
Ũmũnthĩ ve maũndũ matũĩkĩĩthasya nesa vyũ kana tũilyĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩla Mbivilia yĩtĩte "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo." (2 Timotheo 3:1-5) We nũkũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya ĩsaũ na kũmanya nĩ "ĩvinda" yĩkũ twĩkalĩte?
NDIŨ YONAA VAASA
Ndiũ kana kĩlũĩ niwetetwe mavinda maingĩ nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia, na nĩsyoonekaa mũno Nthĩ ya Watho. Ndiũ yĩ ndalanĩ yayo ĩũlũ wa kĩĩma, "nĩthianaa [kana, kũmantha] sya nzyĩma; metho mayo mamyonaa yĩ kũasa." (Yovu 39:27-29) Ndiũ yĩ ũtonyi mwingĩ mũno wa kwona vaasa ũkethĩa no yone kavũkũ ke nusu maili kana kĩlomita kĩmwe.
O ũndũ ndiũ 'yonaa vaasa,' now'o Yeova wĩ na ũtonyi wa kũmanya ĩvinda yũkĩte ũndũ yĩkethĩwa yĩilyĩ. Na kwoou Yeova aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ngĩtavan'ya mũminũkĩlyo kuma mwambĩlĩlyonĩ, na kuma tene tene maũndũ ala matanamba kwĩkwa." (Isaia 46:10) Kwa kũatĩĩa ũtao wa Yeova, no tũtetheke kumana na ũĩ wake ũte maela na ũtonyi wake wa kũmanya maũndũ ala makekĩka ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte.—Isaia 48:17, 18.
O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia yĩelekanasya ala mamũĩkĩĩaa Ngai na ndiũ. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ala mamweteelaa Yeova makeeũvw'a vinya woo; makambata na nthwau ta ndiũ." (Isaia 40:31) Ndiũ ĩtetheeaw'a kũũlũka yambatĩte na ĩũlũ nĩ nzeve yambatĩte yĩ na ũvyũvu. Ĩla ndiũ yavika vandũ ve nzeve ĩsu mbyũ, ĩtambũũkasya nthwau syayo na ĩyambĩĩa kũthiũũka o vau ve nzeve ĩsu. O ũndũ ndiũ ĩsu yĩendeee kũthiũũka vau ve nzeve ĩsu yambatĩte, now'o yĩendeeaa kwambata ĩũlũ o kavola kwa kavola. Ndiũ ndĩtũmĩaa vinya wayo kũũlũka yambatĩte na ĩũlũ kana ĩla yĩũlũkĩte kũndũ kũasa. O ta ũu, athũkũmi ma Yeova nĩmamwĩkwatasya nũndũ nũmathĩte kana akamanenga 'vinya mũnene ũvĩtũkĩte.'—2 Akolintho 4:7, 8.
"ŨNDŨ NGŨKŨ YŨMBANASYA TŨSWII TWAYO"
Kavinda kakuvĩ Yesũ atambĩte kũawa, nĩwaũngamie asyaĩĩsye mũsyĩ mũnene wa Ayuti na asya: "We Yelusaleme, Yelusaleme ũla wũaa athani, na kũmakimanga na mavia ala matũmiwe kwaku! nĩ mavinda meana nendie kũmban'ya vamwe syana syaku, o ũndũ ngũkũ yũmbanasya tũswii twayo vamwe nthwaunĩ syayo, nenyu mũtyaaĩtĩkĩla!"—Mathayo 23:37.
Kĩndũ kĩmwe Ngai weekĩie nthĩnĩ wa nyũnyi nĩ wendi wasyo mũnene wa kũsũvĩa tũswii twasyo. No nginya nyũnyi ila itakaa ndala ta ngũkũ syĩkale syĩtũĩĩe nũndũ nĩ laisi mũno kũvithũkĩwa. Ĩla ngũkũ yoona kĩlũĩ kĩithiũũkanga yayayanĩ, yumasya wasya ũtumaa tũswii tũmanya kana ve mũisyo wĩ vandũ, na ĩndĩ tũisemba tũkevithe nthwaunĩ syayo. O na ĩngĩ, ungu wa nthwau sya ngũkũ ĩsu, tũswii nĩtwĩthĩawa tũtonya kwĩvitha mbua na sua ĩvyũ. O ta ũu, Yesũ nĩwendaa kũtetheesya andũ ala matwĩe Yelusaleme methĩwe me ũsũvĩonĩ wa Yeova na mayĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe nake. Ũmũnthĩ Yesũ nũtũthoketye nĩ kana tũkwate ũthyũmũo na ũsũvĩo kumana na mĩio mĩito na mawĩmakĩo ma kĩla mũthenya.—Mathayo 11:28, 29.
Kwa w'o, no twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ kumana na nyũnyi. Ĩla ũũsisya maũndũ ala nyũnyi syĩkaa, tata ũlilikane Maandĩko ala maeleetye ĩũlũ wa nyũnyi. Eka ngelekany'o ya nthũngũlũlũ ĩũtetheesye kwonaa nyũmba ya Yeova ya kũthaitha yĩ ya vata mũno. Na o tondũ ndiũ yambataa ĩũlũ ĩtetheew'e nĩ nzeve, o naku mwĩkwatye Ngai nĩ kana aũnenge wĩkwatyo na vinya. Na o tondũ nthwau sya ngũkũ isũvĩaa tũswii, now'o twaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ atũtetheesye kũkwata ũsũvĩo na tũyĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na Yeova. Nayo ngelekany'o ya ĩsaũ nĩyĩũlilikany'e ũkekalaa wĩ metho nĩ kana ũmanyae kĩla maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ mekũtũmanyĩsya.

translation:
The scriptures say: "To eat… dreams of vanity, and it will trouble you: Will not the abundance of visions take you away, Or will a divine utterance carry you off?"—Job 12:7, 9.
For over 3,000 years, Job has shown that dreams of vanity can reveal many important things about God's purposes. Dreams can be used both to communicate and to conceal matters relating to what is sacred and what is common. Many scriptures show that dreams of vanity are used to communicate information about our situation and about our relationship with God. Let us examine one example.
CONSIDER ANOTHER EXAMPLE
Those who lived in Jerusalem experienced many things during their dreamlike state, but another state was like the walls of a house. Another state was Solomon's temple. They would remember the dreamlike state, but each year another state would come to them, causing them to see new things.
The writer of Psalm 84, one of the sons of Korah, and who visited the temple courts every month, saw another such state. Because he had a longing to visit the temple, he said: "Oh, how blessed are those who dwell in Your house! May they continue seeking You, and may they find strength in the courtyards of Your God; …May they walk uprightly in Your house, And in the dreamlike state, may they not wander astray, O Lord God of hosts, My stronghold and my God." (Psalm 84:1-3) Indeed, like the sons of Korah, we too have a great desire to worship Jehovah regularly.—Psalm 26:8, 12.
LET US EXAMINE THESE STATES
The prophet Jeremiah wrote: "The migratory birds know the time of their coming." It is amazing how animals can sense changes in the weather. The swallow flies thousands of miles from Africa to Northern Europe across the Jordan Valley each spring. Birds have an internal clock that helps them know when to begin their migration. But even if they migrate on time, birds 'miss the time of their coming.'—Jeremiah 8:7.
The book *Collins Atlas of Bird Migration* explains that birds use various methods to determine direction during their flight. Jehovah God equipped birds with this ability to navigate, but he also gives humans the capacity to understand directions. (Luke 12:54-56) Just as knowledge of God enables a person to understand things about life and to foresee events, so the prophecies of Jeremiah helped the Israelites to understand future events. God revealed to them what was going to happen, saying: "They will certainly look for the prophecy; and, 'Where is the word of Jehovah?'"—Jeremiah 8:9.
Today we live in times that resemble what the Bible calls "difficult times." (2 Timothy 3:1-5) How then can we discern the sign of the times and know that it is "the end"?
THIS IS WHAT THEY SAY
Some say that there are many signs in the Bible, and they point to world events. But the question is, does this interpretation align with the way the Bible itself defines a sign? The Bible says: "An eagle will actually fly in the expanse of the sky."—Job 39:27-29. It is remarkable that eagles have the ability to soar to heights of up to 6 miles [9 kilometers].
So when Jehovah says, "I foretell the outcome from the beginning," he demonstrates his ability to know details about events long before they take place. And he declares: "My purpose will stand, and I will carry out all my pleasure."—Isaiah 46:10. By trusting in Jehovah's sovereignty, we can face the future with confidence, knowing that his wisdom and his ability to foreknow events will guide us.—Isaiah 48:17, 18.
Moreover, the Bible connects God's foreknowledge with his name. It states: "Those who hope in Jehovah will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles."—Isaiah 40:31. This illustration suggests that those who trust in Jehovah gain spiritual strength and resilience. However, just as an eagle needs to flap its wings to stay aloft, we need to continue to put faith in Jehovah and regularly seek his guidance. And only then will we be able to maintain our spiritual strength and endurance. We use our faith to soar spiritually, even when facing challenges. Also, Jehovah's servants often feel inadequate or weak, yet they possess "a treasure in clay vessels."—2 Corinthians 4:7, 8.
"A WAY TO RECONCILE US WITH HIMSELF"
On one occasion, Jesus was approaching Jerusalem, and he expressed heartfelt sorrow, saying: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you kill those prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I longed to gather your children together, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings! But you were unwilling." Then he added: "Look! Your house is left desolate."—Matthew 23:37.
One way God shows his love for us is by providing a means to reconcile ourselves to him. But many people believe that it is impossible to have a close relationship with God because they feel unworthy. Yet God sees potential in each of us, and he wants to help us overcome our imperfections and draw closer to him. Moreover, through the power of God's Word, we can learn about his qualities and purposes, and we can pray to him sincerely. And so, Jesus wanted to gather the inhabitants of Jerusalem to himself, to comfort them with the truth and protect them from danger. In this way, Jesus showed that he cares deeply for those who are burdened and distressed and that he offers them rest and refreshment.—Matthew 11:28, 29.
Therefore, let us continue to learn more about God's love. However, if some aspects of God's ways seem difficult to understand, do not hesitate to study the Scriptures carefully. Also, take advantage of the opportunity to visit Kingdom Halls to worship God and receive encouragement. And even though life may present challenges, remember that God is able to strengthen you and give you courage. And since God's Word comforts us, let us trust that Jesus will help us find peace and enjoy a close relationship with Jehovah. Furthermore, the example set by others can encourage us to persevere and deepen our understanding of God's purpose.

text:
"Kĩla kũnengwa kũseo na kĩla kũnengwa kwĩthĩanu nĩkumaa ĩũlũ, kũtheeaa kuma kwa Ĩthe wa syeni." (Yakovo 1:17) Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩelesya ĩũlũ wa ũlau wa Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ, Yeova Ngai. Ĩndĩ katĩ wa mĩthĩnzĩo ĩla Ngai ũnengete andũ, ve ũmwe mũnene vyũ kwĩ yonthe. Mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nĩ wĩva? Ndeto sya Yesũ ila syĩsĩkĩe mũno ĩandĩkonĩ ya Yoana 3:16, syaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ, nĩwanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmwĩtĩkĩlaa ndakae, ĩndĩ ethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela."
Mũthĩnzĩo ũla Ngai watũnengie ĩla waumisye Mwana wake e ũmwe nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ, nũndũ mũthĩnzĩo ũsu no ũtume tũthaw'a kuma ũkombonĩ wa naĩ, ũkũũ, na kĩkw'ũ. (Savuli 51:5; Yoana 8:34) O na tũkatata mũno wĩana ata, tũyĩsa kwĩyumya ũkombonĩ ũsu. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Ngai nũtwendete mũno, nĩwatũnengie kĩla kyendekaa nĩ kana tũthaw'e kuma ũkombonĩ ũsu. Ĩla Yeova Ngai wanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe, Yesũ Klĩsto, ethĩwe wovosyo, nĩwatumie andũ ala ewi methĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Wovosyo nĩ kyaũ? Nĩkĩ wovosyo nĩ wa vata? Na tũtonya kũtetheka ata kumana naw'o?
Wovosyo nĩ thooa ũla ũĩvawa kwondũ wa kĩndũ kyaĩte kana kwondũ wa kũthasya mũndũ kuma ũkombonĩ. Mbivilia ĩeleasya kana asyai maitũ ma mbee, Atamu na Eva, moombĩtwe mate na naĩ, na maĩ matanĩe thayũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene vamwe na ũsyao woo. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:26-28) Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, nĩmaaisye maũndũ asu onthe ĩla matwie kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai, na kwoou matw'ĩka ene naĩ. Kweethĩiwe ata ĩtina wa ũu? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ wa mũndũ ũmwe naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ; na kwa ũu kĩkw'ũ kyavikĩa andũ onthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa onthe nĩmeekie naĩ." (Alomi 5:12) Vandũ va Atamu kũtiĩa ũsyao wake thayũ ũte na naĩ, aũtiĩe naĩ na kĩkw'ũ.
Nĩ kana wovosyo umw'e, kĩla kĩĩvawa kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa kĩanene na kĩla kyaaiw'e. Atamu nĩwavĩtisye ĩla waleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai na ngũlũ, na kwoou aasya thayũ wake ũte na naĩ. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana naĩ ya Atamu nĩyatumie ũsyao wake ũlika ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. Kwoou, yaĩ no nginya mũndũ ũngĩ wĩ na thayũ ũte na naĩ, nake nĩ Yesũ, aumye thayũ wake nĩ kana tũthaw'e kuma ũkombonĩ ũsu. (Alomi 5:19; Aeveso 1:7) Nũndũ Ngai nĩwatwendie na aumya wovosyo, andũ me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũtanĩa kĩla kyaaiw'e nĩ Atamu na Eva, nakyo nĩ thayũ ũtathela ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ.—Ũvuan'yo 21:3-5.
Kwosana na kĩla wovosyo wĩanĩasya, vai nzika kana nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ kuma kwa Ngai, nũndũ ũkatuma andũ makwata thayũ ũtathela. Nĩ kana tũmanye ũndũ mũthĩnzĩo wa wovosyo wĩthĩawa wĩ 'mwĩthĩanu' kana wĩ mũseo, ekai twone ũndũ ala maũndũ tũneeneie kĩlungunĩ kĩvĩtu matũmĩiwe kwa kĩwango kĩnene nthĩnĩ wa kumya nthembo ya wovosyo. Maũndũ asu me kĩlungunĩ kĩvĩtu nĩ ala monanĩtye ũndũ twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana tũnengae andũ mĩthĩnzĩo ĩtonya kũmendeesya.
Wovosyo nĩwĩanĩasya wendi witũ. Andũ mombĩtwe me na wendi mũnene wa kũendeea kwĩkala thayũ. O na kau tũitonya kwĩanĩsya wendi ũsu, wovosyo no ũtume wendi ũsu wĩanĩa. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ; ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ."—Alomi 6:23.
Wovosyo nĩwĩanĩasya vata witũ. Andũ mayaĩ matonya kwĩnenga wovosyo. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Wovosyo wa mathayũ moo wĩ thooa mũnene, ndũĩvĩka tene na tene." (Savuli 49:8) Kwoou, twaĩ na vata mũnene wa kũtetheew'a nĩ Ngai nĩ kana tũthaw'e kuma ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ "kwondũ wa wovosyo ũla wĩ nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ," Ngai nĩwanenganie kĩla kyendekaa.—Alomi 3:23, 24.
Wovosyo waumiw'e ĩvinda yĩla yaĩle vyũ. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Yĩla twaĩ athe, Klĩsto nĩwakwie kwondũ witũ.' (Alomi 5:8) Nũndũ wovosyo wanenganiwe "yĩla twaĩ athe," nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana Ngai nũtwendete mũno o na kau twĩ na naĩ. Na wovosyo nũtumaa twĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũtanĩa maũndũ maingĩ maseo ĩvinda yũkĩte, o na kau ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ no nginya tũmĩĩsye mathĩna ala matũkwataa nũndũ wa naĩ.
Wovosyo wonanasya kana Ngai aĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo vyũ. Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye kĩla kyatumie Ngai aumya Mwana wake ta wovosyo. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũndũnĩ ũũ wendo wa Ngai nĩwonanĩtw'e kwitũ, nũndũ Ngai nĩwamũtũmie Mwana wake kũũ nthĩ, ũla wasyaiwe e ũmwe, nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na thayũ kwondũ wake. Ũũ nĩw'o wendo, ti ithyĩ twamwendie Ngai, ĩndĩ nĩwe watwendie ithyĩ."—1 Yoana 4:9, 10.
Ũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nũtũngaa mũvea kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ? Lilikana kana ndeto sya Yesũ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Yoana 3:16 syonanĩtye kana no ũla "ũmwĩtĩkĩlaa [kana, ũmũĩkĩĩaa]" ũkatangĩĩwa. Kwosana na Mbivilia, mũĩkĩĩo nĩ "kĩla kĩmanyĩthasya vyũ maũndũ ala mekwatĩtw'e." (Aevelania 11:1) Nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ũĩkĩĩthyo ũsu, nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ũmanyi wa w'o. Kwoou, wĩkũlw'a wĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai, Mũnengani wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu 'mwĩthĩanu,' na ũyĩmanyĩsya maũndũ ala waĩle kwĩka nĩ kana wĩtanĩa thayũ ũtathela ũla ũkethĩwa nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo ya Yesũ.
No wĩmanyĩsye maũndũ asu onthe kwa kũsoma ũvoo wumĩte Mbivilianĩ ũla wĩ Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmeũtanĩa kũũtetheesya wĩmanyĩsye. Twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana weemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu mũnene na watetheka kumana naw'o, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũneena ndeto ii: "Nĩmũtũngĩa Ngai mũvea nĩ ũndũ wa Yesũ Klĩsto Mwĩaĩi waitũ."—Alomi 7:25.

translation:
"Every good gift and every perfect present is from above, coming down from the Father of lights." (James 1:17) This scripture illustrates God's love for us, Jehovah God. Among the many ways God shows his love for people, one stands out prominently. What is this way? Jesus himself explained it when he quoted John 3:16, saying: "God loved the world so much that he gave his only Son, in order that everyone who has faith in him might not perish but have everlasting life."
The greatest expression of God's love for mankind is that He gave His only Son, and this expression moves us to appreciate what we have—life, health, and freedom. (Psalm 51:5; John 8:34) And even though we make mistakes, we can draw comfort from knowing about this provision. Because God loves us so much, He forgives our sins and helps us to live up to our potential. But Jehovah God gave his only Son, Jesus Christ, as a ransom, and sent men forth with a message of reconciliation. So the question is, What is a ransom? Why is a ransom needed? And how can we benefit from it?
A ransom is something given to free someone from a difficult situation or to restore someone to a former state. The Bible explains how Adam and Eve, the first humans, disobeyed God and brought sin and imperfection into the world, resulting in endless suffering and eventual death. (Genesis 1:26-28) As a result, humanity has inherited a tendency toward wrongdoing and a desire to please oneself rather than God. Is there any hope for escaping this condition? The Bible answers: "Just as through one man sin entered into the world and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because they had all sinned." (Romans 5:12) Adam's descendants inherit his imperfect nature, and they struggle with sin and its consequences.
So a ransom was needed—something equal in value to what was lost. Adam forfeited his perfect life when he disobeyed God, and his descendants share in his imperfect condition. The Bible shows that Adam's sin caused him to pass on an imperfect life to all mankind, along with its consequences. Therefore, anyone desiring to live forever must find a way to overcome the effects of Adam's sin, and that is where Jesus comes in, who gave his life as a ransom to deliver us from sin. (Romans 5:19; Ephesians 1:7) Because God loved us and provided a ransom, people can benefit from the perfection of Adam and Eve, and this opens up the prospect of everlasting life for obedient ones.—Revelation 21:3-5.
In harmony with each ransom sacrifice, there is a legal basis for extending forgiveness to those who exercise faith toward God, thus enabling people to gain everlasting life. Whether we view the ransom as a 'price' or a 'sacrifice,' we see that it highlights the great importance of what Jehovah has done to satisfy justice and redeem humankind from the penalty of sin. Other aspects of this provision also show how much Jehovah values our obedience and encourages us to make important adjustments in our lives.
The ransom is vital to us. People throughout history have longed for life. But unless we appreciate the significance of this ransom, the ransom will not make our life meaningful. The Bible states: "The wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life through Christ Jesus our Lord."—Romans 6:23.
The ransom benefits all mankind. Many people desire to accept the ransom. The Bible says: "Redemption itself requires a great price." (Psalm 49:8) Indeed, we need God's help to be released from bondage to sin and death. By means of "the redemption that is by Christ Jesus," God credits righteousness to everyone who exercises faith.—Romans 3:23, 24.
The ransom provides a lasting solution. The Bible states: 'While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.' (Romans 5:8) Because the ransom was provided while we were still sinners, it demonstrates Jehovah's love for us and his willingness to forgive us. Also, the ransom enables us to enjoy many blessings and to look forward to a future where injustice will no longer exist, and where even the dead will be resurrected.
The ransom shows how much God loves us. The Bible explains why God sent his Son as a ransom. It says: "God loved the world so much that he gave his only-begotten Son, in order that everyone exercising faith in him might not perish but have everlasting life." This is what love is—not that we loved God, but that he loved us first.—1 John 4:9, 10.
Can you imagine how grateful we should be for this great provision? Consider how John 3:16 describes the extent to which God showed his love when he gave his Son. According to the Bible, faith is "the assured expectation of things hoped for." (Hebrews 11:1) If we exercise such faith, we can experience its benefits now. Therefore, continue to learn about Jehovah God, the Provider of this ransom 'with conviction,' and let your faith move you to take action, so that you may benefit fully from the value of Jesus' ransom sacrifice.
Learn more about these things by reading the entire Bible, available online at www.jw.org/kam. Jehovah's Witnesses would be happy to help you learn. And if you desire to show your gratitude for this great provision and want to get to know him better, you can confidently say: "I will thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord."—Romans 7:25.

text:
ĩkũlyo
We Yesũ Klisto nũũ?
Ũsungio
Eka ũkũlyo wa " Ngai evo?" Ĩkũlyo ya kana we Klisto Yesũ aivo ĩkũlaw'a nĩ andũ avũthũ. Aingĩ metĩkĩlaa kana Yesũ Klisto aĩ ota ũmwe wa andũ na ekalaa ĩsilaeli miaka 2000 mĩvĩtu. Ũneenany'a wa mbeenĩ ni kũneenany'a yĩũlũ wa ũmo wa Yesũ. Ndĩni mbingĩ ĩvundĩasya Yesũ ta mwathani, mũmanyĩsya mũseo na angĩ ta mũndũ wamũkiaa Ngai. Ĩndĩ, Mbivilia ĩmũwetaa ta ũmwe waĩ mbee wa mwathani, mũmanyĩsya mũseo ona mbee wa mũndũ ũmũkĩaa Ngai.
C.S. Lewis ĩvũkũni yake "mere christianity" aandĩkie ũũ: "Nĩtataa nĩ kana nĩtethye aingĩ ala mawetaa kwa kũlea kũmanya kana na ũtũmanũ maũndũ mataĩle yĩũlũ wake [Yesũ Klĩsto]: ĩngĩ nĩngwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ ta mũmanyĩsya mũseo ũla waĩ mwĩanĩu, ĩndĩ ndĩkwĩtĩkĩla ũneeni wake kwĩthĩwa e Ngai. Ũsũ nĩ ũndũ ũmwe ũla tũtaĩlĩtwe kũweta. Mũndũ waĩ o mũndũ waĩ aiweta maũndũ ala Yesũ wawetie ndai atwĩka mũmanyĩsya mũseo wa maũndũ ma ndaĩa. Utee na oũ ai atonya kwĩtw'a mũndũ wa ndũũka - vamwe na ũla wĩvũthasya ũneeninĩ wake-kana kwĩthĩwa ta devĩlĩ wa yĩia ya mwakĩ mũnene wakanĩte na mũvĩlĩtĩ. Ve vata wa ũtw'a ũtwĩ waku. Nĩvatonyeka mũndũ ũũ aĩ kana nowe, mwana wa Ngai, kethĩwa ndai mũndũ wa ndũũka kana kĩndũ mbee wa oũ. Nũtonya ũmũvindĩthya ta ũmwĩsĩ wa ala atumanũ, kũmũtw'ĩla mata na kũmũvũthya kana kũkumya thayũ ta ndaimoni; kana ũkavaluka ũngũ wa nyaaĩ syake na kũmwĩta Mwĩai Ngai. Ĩndĩ tũikavikĩĩye ũsili wa ũtumanu yĩũlũ wa kwĩthĩwa aĩ mũmanyĩsya mũnene wa ngo syonthe sya andũ. Ndaatia mwanya tũtonye kũmanya ũw'o kana kwĩthĩwa na kĩsũanio ta kyũ." ( Macmillan, 1952, ĩthangũnĩ. 55 - 56).
Ĩndĩ yũ, Yesũ aneenie yĩũlũ wake ta ũũ? Nayo Mbivilia ĩneenaa ata yĩũlũ wake? Ũndũ wa mbee, we nĩ Ngai nthĩnĩ e mwĩĩnĩ ta mũndũ. Yoana 10:30, " Nyĩe na Asa twĩ ũmwe." Ũneeni ũũ, nĩ mwĩanĩu kũmwĩananya na Ngai. Ndeto isũ syai ngito mũno kwa Ayuti. Namo matataĩe mamũkime na mavia, " kwondũ wa kwĩyonany'a ta Ngai, nũndũ we, e mũndũ, eyĩtĩe Ngai." (Yoana 10:33). Kwĩanana namo, monie ta weyĩta Ngai kũatiania na ndeto syake. Mũsoa ũũ waatĩĩe, Yesũ ndaatata kũmatũnga ta mavĩtisye kana kũlũlũmĩĩlya ndeto ndeto syake kwoo. Ndaasya kana we nĩ Ngai. Ĩndĩ ĩla waisye, " Nyĩe na Asa twi ũmwe." (Yoana 10:30), nĩw'o weyĩananasyĩ na Ngai.
Ĩvũkũni ya Yoana 8:28, Yesũ easya atĩĩ, aikw'o kũma mbeenĩ, ũelesyo wa Ngai: "Nĩw'o nĩw'o nĩngũmwĩ,' Yesũ asũngĩa, 'Avalaamu atevo, nĩkw'o!'" Kwondũ wa ndeto isũ, Ayuti moosie mavia nĩ kana mamũkimange namo ( Yoana 8:29). Kwondũ wa kũweta ai kw'o mbeenĩ, Yesũ atũmĩie syĩtwa ya Ngai kũneena yĩũlũ wake mweene - Ninyie ũla nĩnyĩe (Kuma 3:14). Ayuti mamũleile Yesũ ta Ngai ũla wĩ thayũ tene na tene, ona kaũ nĩmamanyĩe maũndũ onthe ala wa nenaa.
Mbĩvĩlĩa nĩmwonany'a Yesũ ta Ngai ena mwĩĩ ta mũndũ kwĩsĩla Yoana 1:1, ũla ũasya, " Nayo ĩ ndeto yai Ngai," vamwe na Yoana 1:14, vala ĩnĩkwasya, "Nayo ĩ ndeto yoosa mwĩĩ." Thoma mũmanyĩw'a wake amwĩie, "Mwĩai wakwa na Ngai wakwa " (Yoana 20:28), na Yesũ ndaamũtala mavĩtyo. Vaulo elesya Yesũ ta, " Ngai mũnene na mũtangĩĩi, Yesũ Klisto " (Tito 2:13). Mũtũmwa Vetelo aneenie oũ ingĩ, aimwĩta Yesũ, "Ngai wĩtu na Mwĩai waĩtu." ( 2 Vetelo 1:1).
Ngai Asa nũkũsĩĩa ũkũsĩ wa Yesu Klisto ota w'o: "ĩndĩ ũvoo wa Mwana easya, Kĩvĩla kyaku kya ũsumbĩ, we Ngai, nĩ kya tene na tene; Na ndata ya ũsumbĩ ya ũlũngalu nĩyo ndata ya ũsumbĩ waku." (Aevelania 1:8 Savulĩ 45:6). Mawathani ma ũtianĩo mũkũũ ta Ĩsaĩa 9:6 mawetaa ũũngai wa Klisto "Nũndũ nĩkũsyaĩtwe kana kwondũ witũ, nĩtũnengetwe mwana mũndũ mũũme; na ũsumbĩko ũkeethĩwa kĩtuonĩ kyake: na syĩtwa yake akeetwa Ũseng'yo, Mũtai, Ngai Mwene Vinya, ĩthe wa Tene na Tene, Mũnene wa Mũuo."
Nĩkĩ ĩkũlyo ya kumanya Yesu nũũ yĩ vata? Nĩkĩ ve vata wa kumanya kana Yesu nĩ Ngai? Ve itumi kĩvathũkany'o:
• Oundũ mũandĩkĩ C.S Lewis waaisye, kethĩwa Yesu ti Ngai, ethĩwa e mukengani munene.
• Kethĩwa Yesu ti Ngai, ona amanyĩw'a make methĩwa maĩ akengani.
• Yesu nonginya ethĩwe aĩ Ngai nundu Masia athanĩtwe kwĩthĩwa e "Ũla mũtheu" (Savulĩ 16:5). Nũndũ vai umwe mũlũngalu mbee wa Ngai. ( Savulĩ 53:1; 143:2), Ngai we mwene yaĩ o nginya oke kũũ nthĩ ta mũndũ.
• Kethĩwa Yesu ti Ngai, kĩkw'u kyake kĩthĩwa kĩteanĩtye kũĩvĩa naĩ sya nthĩ yonthe (1 Yoana 2:2). Ngai weka nowe ũtonya kwĩyũmya nthembo mbĩanĩu ya ũekeo wa naĩ (Alomi 5:8; 2 Akolintho 5:21).
• Ngai no we mũtangĩĩi weka. ( Osea 13:4 ; 1 Timotheo 2:3) ethĩwa Yesũ nĩ Mũtangĩi, no nginya ethĩwe e Ngai.
Yesũ aĩ nginya ethĩwe e mũndũ na Ngaĩ mwĩĩnĩ ũmwe. Ta Ngaĩ, Yesũ aĩ eanĩsye ũthatu wa Ngai. Ta mũndũ, Yesũ aĩ na ũtonyi wa kũkw'a. Ta Ngai mũndũ Yesũ nĩ we mwĩw'anĩthya mwĩanĩu katĩ wa ĩtu na nthĩ ( 1 Timotheo 2:5). Utangĩĩo ũkwatĩkanaa kwa nzĩa ya kũmũĩkĩĩa Yesũ weka. Oũndũ waisye, "Nyie ninyie nzĩa, na ninyie w'o, na ninyie thayũ: vai mũndũ wũkaa kwa Asa, atesĩle kwakwa." (Yoana 14:6)
English
We Yesũ Klisto nũũ?

translation:
Indeed
Are you Jesus Christ?
Response
Like the question of "God exists?" Indeed, whether Christ Jesus existed among people of old. Many believe that Jesus Christ was not one of the people and lived in Israel 2000 years ago. The essence of faith is the understanding of the life of Jesus. It is important to understand Jesus as a mediator, to know his character and also as a person who knows God. Truly, the Bible shows him as a mediator, to know his character and also as a person who knows God.
C.S. Lewis in his book "Mere Christianity" writes thus: "I am trying here, perhaps, to meet far more of the difficulties than I shall actually be able to resolve. The real trouble is that people want to have ideas about things they haven't bothered to think out for themselves [Jesus Christ]: first they adopt an idea, then they look around for facts to support it. But I am going to try to make you see that this is a silly way of approaching the matter. A man who wants to find out what Jesus was really like has to start by considering what He claimed about Himself. And he will find that He made no claim to be a good man, or a great teacher, but to be the Son of God. Now, if He were not the Son of God, He would be a liar and a deceiver. And if He were a liar and a deceiver, He could not possibly be a good man. So you see, the point is not whether He was a good man, but whether He was telling the truth. And if He was telling the truth, then He is the Son of God. But if He was not telling the truth, then He is a very bad man indeed. We must therefore decide whether we believe Him or not." (Macmillan, 1952, page. 55 - 56).
And so, did Jesus claim to be divine? Does the Bible claim His divinity? Furthermore, He is God incarnate in human form. John 10:30, "I and the Father are one." This statement, is equivalent to identifying with God. However, some accuse them of blasphemy, saying, "Because you, being a man, make yourself God." (John 10:33). Identifying with Him, means claiming to be God in relation to His nature. This teaching implies, Jesus did not hesitate to express His claims or diminish His statements at all. It shows that He is God. For instance, "I and the Father are one." (John 10:30), is how He identifies with God.
In John 8:28, Jesus said, intending to reveal Himself, demonstrating the glory of God: "Indeed, indeed I tell you," Jesus declared, "Before Abraham was born, I am!" Because of this statement, the Jews picked up stones to throw at Him (John 8:29). In order to avoid revealing Himself, Jesus used the name of God to declare His identity – You are all gods (Psalm 82:6). The Jews misinterpreted Jesus as God who always exists, and they understood His words incorrectly.
The Bible presents Jesus as both God and man, as stated in John 1:1, which says, "And the Word was God," and also in John 1:14, which states, "And the Word became flesh." Thomas confessed his belief, "My Lord and my God" (John 20:28), and Jesus accepted his confession. Paul described Jesus as, "Our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ" (Titus 2:13). The apostle Peter testified further, calling Jesus, "Our God and Savior." (2 Peter 1:1).
God the Father revealed the glory of Jesus Christ through these words: "Concerning Your Son, O God, Your throne is forever and ever; And the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of Your kingdom." (Hebrews 1:8 Psalm 45:6). Prophecies about salvation, such as Isaiah 9:6, describe the character of Christ: "For a child will be born to us, a son will be given to us; And the government will rest on His shoulders, And His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace."
Is it possible to know Jesus truly? Is it possible to know whether Jesus is God? Consider these points:
• As author C.S. Lewis put it, if Jesus is not God, He is either a madman or something worse.
• If Jesus is God, then His claims and teachings have immense significance.
• Jesus claimed to be God, fulfilling the prophecy of the Messiah being called "The Holy One" (Psalm 16:5). No mere creature could possess the attributes of God. (Psalm 53:1; 143:2), God alone can forgive sins like a human.
• If Jesus is God, His death was an atonement for sin (1 John 2:2). God alone has the power to satisfy divine justice and offer forgiveness (Romans 5:8; 2 Corinthians 5:21).
• God is our mediator. (Hosea 13:4; 1 Timothy 2:3) Therefore, Jesus is the Mediator, and not a mediator between God and Himself.
Jesus is both fully God and fully man. As God, Jesus possesses the fullness of deity. As man, Jesus experienced limitations. As the God-man, Jesus is the perfect bridge between humanity and divinity (1 Timothy 2:5). Salvation is achieved through faith in Jesus alone. As someone once said, "I am the way, and the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Me." (John 14:6)
Are we talking about Jesus Christ now?

text:
"Nũndũ wa mũndũ ũmwe [Atamu] naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ."—Alomi 5:12
Ũkakũlw'a kana no wende kwĩkala tene na tene ũsũngĩa ata? Andũ aingĩ no masye kana no mende, ĩndĩ monaa ũndũ ũsu ũtatonyeka. Maasya kana kĩkw'ũ nĩ lasima na kana mũndũ asyawa no nginya akw'e.
Nao nata ũkakũlw'a kana no wende kũkw'a, we ũsũngĩa ata? Andũ aingĩ no masye kana maikwenda kũkw'a. Ũndũ ũsu wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Kĩla mũndũ nĩwĩthĩawa na wendi wa kwĩkala thayũ o na akwatwa nĩ mathĩna maingĩvĩte ata. Mbivilia nĩyonanasya kana Ngai oombie andũ me na wendi wa kwĩkala thayũ tene na tene.
Ũw'o nĩ kana andũ mayĩkalaa tene na tene. Thĩna wambĩĩie va? No twĩkũlye-ĩ, Ngai ekĩte ata nĩ kana andũ meĩkala tene na tene? Mbivilia nĩtũnengete mosũngĩo ma kũtwĩkĩa vinya, na mosũngĩo asu nĩmekũtũtetheesya kũmanya nĩkĩ Yesũ wathĩniw'e na akw'a.
THĨNA WAMBĨLĨĨILYE VA?
Ilungu sya mbee itatũ sya ĩvuku ya Mbivilia ya Mwambĩlĩlyo nitũeleetye kana Ngai amombie asyai maitũ ma mbee, Atamu na Eva, me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩthĩwa na thayũ ũtathela, na amatavya ũndũ matonya kwĩka nĩ kana maũkwate. O na ilungu isu nĩsyonanĩtye ũndũ maleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai na maasya wĩkwatyo ũsu wa kwĩkala tene na tene. Ngewa ĩsu yĩeleetw'e kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi vyũ ũkethĩa andũ amwe no masye nĩ wano. O ta mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo, ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩĩlyo yĩeleetye maũndũ ma w'o meekĩkie. *
Nĩ kyaũ kyeethĩiwe nũndũ wa Atamu kwĩthĩwa ate mwĩwi? Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte atĩĩ: "Nũndũ wa mũndũ ũmwe [Atamu] naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ; na kwa ũu kĩkw'ũ kyavikĩa andũ onthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa onthe nĩmeekie naĩ." (Alomi 5:12) Nũndũ wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai, Atamu nĩweekie naĩ. Na nũndũ wa ũu, nĩwaaisye wĩkwatyo wa kwĩthĩwa na thayũ ũtathela, na ĩtina esa kũkw'a. Nũndũ ithyĩ twĩ ũsyao wake, nĩwatũtiĩe naĩ. Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi tũwaa, tũkakũa, na ĩtina tũkakw'a. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwosanĩte na ũkunĩkĩli ũla andũ ma saenzi mekĩte ũkwonany'a kana syana nĩsyĩthĩawa na mĩtuo ya mũsyawa kuma kwa asyai masyo. Ĩndĩ ve ũndũ Ngai weekie nĩ kana atũtangĩĩe kuma thĩnanĩ ũsu?
MŨVANGO ŨLA NGAI WEEKIE
Ngai nĩweekie mũvango nĩ kana enenga andũ thayũ ũtathela, ũla Atamu waaisye. Eekie mũvango wĩva?
Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 6:23: "Ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ." Ũu wĩonany'a kana kĩkw'ũ kĩetawe nĩ naĩ. Atamu nĩweekie naĩ, na nĩkyo kĩtumi wakwie. O ta ũu, o naitũ nĩtwĩkaa naĩ, na nĩkyo kĩtumi tũkwataa ĩtuvi ya naĩ, nayo nĩ kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ o na kau ti ithyĩ twavĩtisye, tũsyaawa twĩ na naĩ. Nũndũ Ngai e wendo, nĩwatũmie Mwana wake, Yesũ, nĩ kana akwate "ĩtuvi ya naĩ" kwondũ witũ. Ũndũ ũsu watonyekie ata?
Nũndũ nĩ mũndũ ũmwe ũtaĩ na naĩ ũla watũeteie naĩ na kĩkw'ũ kwĩsĩla kũlea kwĩw'a, nĩvendekaa mũndũ ũngĩ ũte na naĩ ethĩwe e mwĩwi nginya kĩkw'ũ nĩ kana atũthasye kuma ũkombonĩ wa kĩkw'ũ. Mbivilia yĩeleetye ũndũ ũsu kwa kwasya atĩĩ: "Nũndũ wa kũlea kwĩw'a kwa mũndũ ũmwe aingĩ matwiwe athe, o ta ũu kwondũ wa kwĩw'a kwa ũmwe, aingĩ makatuwa alũngalu." (Alomi 5:19) Yesũ nĩwe mũndũ ũsu "ũmwe" ũla ũkatuma andũ matuwa alũngalu. Yesũ aumie ĩtunĩ, asyawa ate na naĩ *, na ĩtina esa kũkw'a kwondũ witũ. Na ũu nũtumaa twĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela.
NĨKĨ YESŨ WATHĨNIW'E NA AKW'A?
Nĩkĩ yaĩ no nginya Yesũ akw'e nĩ kana eanĩsye ũndũ ũsu? O na no twĩkũlye-ĩ, We Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe ndaĩ atonya kumya mwĩao nĩ kana ũsyao wa Atamu ũkekala tene na tene? Kwa w'o, Ngai aĩ na ũkũmũ wa kwĩka ũu. Ĩndĩ keka nĩweekie ũu ethĩwa avũthĩĩisye mwĩao wake ũla waĩtye kana ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ. Ũsu ndwaĩ mwĩao ũtonya kũvĩndũawa o kĩla ĩvinda ĩla maũndũ mathũka. Ĩndĩ mwĩao ũsu nĩ wa vata mũno nthĩnĩ wa ũsili wa katĩ.—Savuli 37:28.
Takethĩwa Ngai nĩwavũthĩĩisye mwĩao ũsu ũndũnĩ ũũ, andũ no methĩwe mambĩĩie kũsũanĩa ta ũtonya kwĩka ũu maũndũnĩ angĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, no methĩwe mambĩĩie kwĩkũlya kana Ngai akanyuva nesa ala maĩle kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. O na ĩngĩ, no mambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na nzika kana akeanĩsya mawatho make. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Ngai nĩwaatĩĩie ũsili wa katĩ ũndũnĩ ũsu ũkonetye ũtangĩĩo witũ, nĩtwĩthĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo kana mavinda onthe akeekaa ũla waĩle.
Kwĩsĩla kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, Ngai nĩwavingũĩe andũ nzĩa ya kũkwata thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Nthĩ Nzaũ. Kwasisya ndeto ii sya Yesũ ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Yoana 3:16: "Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ, nĩwanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmwĩtĩkĩlaa ndakae, ĩndĩ ethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela." Kwoou, kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ nĩkyoonanisye kana Ngai nũsilaa katĩ, na ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ, nĩkyoonanisye kana nĩwendete andũ mũno vyũ.
Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Nĩkĩ yaĩ no nginya Yesũ athĩnw'e na aikw'a kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo o tondũ vaeleetw'e mavukunĩ ma Ũvoo Mũseo? Nĩ kenda aĩkĩĩthye kana Ndevili nĩwakenganie ĩla waisye kana andũ mayĩsa kwĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku ĩla makwatwa nĩ motato. Oonanisye ũu kwĩsĩla wĩnyivyo wake na kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku nginya kĩkw'ũ. (Yovu 2:4, 5) Satani nũtonya kwoneka ta waneenaa ũw'o ĩla wamũtatie Atamu eke naĩ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ, ũla ũtaĩ na naĩ o ta Atamu, nĩweethĩiwe e mwĩwi o na ĩla wakwatiwe nĩ motato momũ. (1 Akolintho 15:45) Kwa kwĩka ũu, Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana o nake Atamu aĩ atonya kwĩthĩwa e mwĩwi keka nĩwendaa. Kwa kũmĩĩsya, Yesũ nĩwatũtiĩe ngelekany'o ya kũatĩĩa. (1 Vetelo 2:21) Nũndũ Yesũ nĩweethĩiwe e mwĩwi vyũ, ĩla waendie ĩtunĩ, Ngai nĩwamũnengie mũthĩnzĩo wa thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KŨTETHEKA
Kwa w'o ki, Yesũ nĩwakwie. Nayu ve nzĩa ya kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. We no wende kwĩkala tene na tene? Yesũ nĩwoonanisye ũndũ twaĩle kwĩka ĩla waisye atĩĩ: "Na thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto."—Yoana 17:3.
Aumĩthya ma ĩkaseti yĩĩ nĩmeũkũthokya wĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Yeova, Ngai ũla wa w'o, na ĩũlũ wa Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ila syĩ kĩsionĩ kyenyu nĩmeũkũtetheesya kwĩka ũu. O na no ũkwate ũvoo ũngĩ ũtonya kũũtetheesya kwa kũvingũa Kĩsese kya www.jw.org/kam.
^ kal. 8 Sisya kyongo kyaĩtye "The Historical Character of Genesis," nthĩnĩ wa Ĩvuku ya 1 ya Insight on the Scriptures, yĩla yumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, ĩthangũ ya 922.
^ kal. 13 Ngai nĩwathamisye thayũ wa Mwana wake kuma ĩtunĩ, awĩkĩa ĩvunĩ ya Meli, na Meli aitava. Veva mũtheu wa Ngai nĩwamũsũvĩie Yesũ ndakakue naĩ kuma kwa Meli.—Luka 1:31, 35.

translation:
"The feeling of one person [Atamu] was like this, and his heart was troubled because of it." – Psalm 5:12
Do you ever feel like you can't cope at all? Many people feel overwhelmed and sometimes they don't see a way out. Sometimes the heart is heavy and when someone cries, they find relief.
And do you ever feel like you can't handle it, are you overwhelmed at all? Many people feel overwhelmed or want to give up. What causes this? Everyone is faced with the desire to be free or is held back by many things. I believe it is comforting to know that God cares about people who want to be free at all.
That is why people feel so overwhelmed. Why don't you tell me how? Let us think—does God really care about people being free at all? I believe we should seek more ways to understand, and through those means He has shown me how Jesus was tempted.
WHY DON'T YOU TELL ME HOW?
The story of the three years of the Bible of Revelation shows that God cared about our ancestors Adam and Eve, who were given the desire to be free from endless punishment, and they disobeyed what was right. And this story also shows the importance of turning away from sin and overcoming this desire to be free at all. Today, this message has been brought to some people who are willing. Or like the books of Old Testament, the book of Revelation brings such things to light.*
Was Adam tempted to disobey so that he would become a sinner? The Bible explains: "Through one man [Adam] sin entered into the world, and death through sin; and in this way death came upon all men, because all sinned." (Romans 5:12) Because of his desire to turn away from God, Adam chose to sin. And because of this, he passed on the desire to be free from endless punishment, and it continues to this day. What we inherit from him, we practice. And that is why we fall, we grow, and it continues to happen. This thing is similar to the scientific understanding that humans can develop good or bad habits depending on their environment and upbringing. But does God allow this to happen?
THE REASON GOD ALLOWS
God allows reason so that He may judge people freely, which Adam misused. What reason did He give?
The Bible says in Romans 6:23: "The wages sin pays is death." This shows that death is the result of sin. Adam misused it, and that is why he died. Because of this, we also die, and that is the wages sin pays. If you have never done wrong, you will live forever. Since God loves us, He sent His Son, Jesus, so that He might take "the wages sin pays" from us. Does this sound reasonable?
It is like someone who owes a debt and wants to pay it off with something less than what is owed, then another person comes along and offers to pay the full debt. The Bible illustrates this point by saying: "Because of one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one man many will be made righteous." (Romans 5:19) Jesus is that "one" man who makes many righteous. Jesus was perfect, He lived without sin*, and it continues to this day. And this causes us to be reconciled to God and to have the desire to avoid endless punishment.
WHY WAS JESUS CRUCIFIED AND DIED?
Why did Jesus die if He was innocent? Well, we know that our mighty God can undo everything that Adam did wrong, right? Of course, God has the power to do this. But let Him show His justice by allowing His beloved Son to take "the wages sin pays". This way, everyone can benefit, regardless of their past mistakes. So everyone can have eternal life.—Psalm 37:28.
God allowed His Son to suffer this fate, and people mocked those who tried to understand this matter. For example, some mocked them for believing that God would allow an innocent one to suffer endless punishment. Others mocked them for trusting in God's promises. But since God has set a time limit for this system of things, we can be confident that all his purposes will succeed.
By means of Jesus, God gives people the opportunity to escape endless destruction. Consider this important scripture found in John 3:16: "For God loved the world so much that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who puts faith in him might not perish but have everlasting life." Truly, Jesus' sacrifice shows how much God cares for us, and also shows how much He loves mankind.
But some may ask, 'Why did Jesus suffer and undergo such a trial when Adam was already judged imperfect?' It is because Satan claimed that humans could not remain faithful under trial. This proved the loyalty of Job and demonstrated the importance of integrity. (Job 2:4, 5) Satan tried to show that just as he caused Adam to fall, he could cause anyone to fail. But Jesus, unlike Adam, remained loyal despite intense pressure and suffering. (1 Corinthians 15:45) Thus, Jesus showed that a perfect man can stay faithful even under severe test. As an example, Jesus provided a pattern of obedience. (1 Peter 2:21) Because Jesus remained faithful, God resurrected him, giving him the opportunity to gain everlasting life.
THIS CAN BE REVERSED
Because of this, Jesus ascended to heaven. Now he holds out hope for those who desire everlasting life. Will you continue to exercise faith? Jesus prayed about his followers, saying: "And everlasting life means knowing you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent."—John 17:3.
May this publication help you learn more about Jehovah, the only true God, and his Son, Jesus Christ. May the Bible and its teachings strengthen your faith. And may you find comfort in knowing that you are not alone in facing trials. For further information, visit our website at www.jw.org/kam.

^ par. 13 God sent his Son to earth, being born of Mary, and Mary conceived miraculously. God's spirit empowered her to conceive Jesus perfectly.—Luke 1:31, 35.

ERNST e na myaka 70 na kĩndũ na easya ũũ amakĩte: "Nĩtindĩaa o kũthĩnw'a nĩ mwĩĩ." * We waaĩsa kwĩw'a ta Ernst? Ethĩwa nũendeee kũkũa na nũkwĩw'a ũithĩnw'a nĩ mwĩĩ kwĩ tene kana nũkwĩw'a ũyaa vinya, no kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kwĩyĩelesya ũitũmĩa ndeto iilyĩ ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mũtavan'ya kĩlungu kya 12. Nthĩnĩ wa mũsoa wa 1 wa kĩlungu kĩu, mĩthenya ya mũndũ mũkũũ yĩtĩtwe "mĩthenya mĩthũku." Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa nũvikĩte mĩthenyanĩ ĩsu ũu ti kwasya kana ndũkona nesa. No ũendeee kwĩkala nesa ũimũthũkũma Yeova wĩ mũtanu.
NDŨKAEKE MŨĨKĨĨO WAKU ŨLEELE
Inyw'ĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa akũũ, mũikamake mũyona ta mwĩ inyw'oka. Ve o athũkũmi angĩ ma Yeova matwĩe tene na makwatiwe nĩ mathĩna ta asu mwĩ namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Isaka, Yakovo, na Aiya nĩmaaie metho. (Mwa. 27:1; 48:10; 1 Asu. 14:4) Nake Sala eew'aa e "mũtumĩu." (Mwa. 18:11, 12) Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti 'ndeew'aa muutĩa.' (1 Asu. 1:1) Mbalisilai nake o na kau aĩ mũthwii, avikĩte vandũ ũkethĩa ndatonya kũtanĩa wathi kana mũsamo wa lĩu. (2 Sam. 19:32-35) Na ĩndĩ nake Avalaamu nĩwakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũka na Naomi akw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũũme.—Mwa. 23:1, 2; Lu. 1:3, 12.
Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie kĩla ũmwe wa athũkũmi asu ma tene amũthũkũma Yeova e mũĩkĩĩku na aendeea kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu? Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Avalaamu. O na ĩla waĩ mũkũũ nĩwaĩkĩĩe mawatho ma Ngai, na nũndũ wa ũu "ongeleelwa vinya nĩ mũĩkĩĩo wake." (Alo. 4:19, 20) O naitũ twaĩle kwĩkala na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Na nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu ti lasima twĩthĩwe ma ĩika ĩna, kana twĩthĩwe na ũtonyi mũna, kana maũndũ mana. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya Yakovo. O na ĩla metho mameisye mbindu na onza weethĩa o na ndokĩla ũkomonĩ, aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana mawatho ma Ngai makeanĩa. (Mwa. 48:1-4, 10; Aevl. 11:21) Ũmũnthĩ ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Ines wĩ na myaka 93. O na kau ethĩawa na thĩna wa kwonza malangũ, easya: "Nonaa Yeova aingathima mũno kĩla mũthenya. Nĩsũanĩaa Nthĩ Nzaũ kĩla mũthenya. Kĩu nĩkĩtumaa nĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo." We ndũkwona mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu e na woni mũseo mũno?
Tũlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ ĩla twavoya, tweemanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai, na twathi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwathani Ndanieli. O na ĩla waĩ mũkũũ, nĩwavoyaa mavinda atatũ kwa mũthenya ateũtĩĩa, na ndaaeka kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai. (Nda. 6:10; 9:2) Nake Ana o na kau aĩ mũkũũ na aĩ ndiwa, "ndaumaa ĩkalũnĩ." (Luka 2:36, 37) O naku ĩla wesa kũthi maũmbanonĩ na waumya maelesyo maingĩ ũndũ ũtonya, nũkwataa vinya na ũkekĩa ala onthe me vau vinya. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana mavinda onthe Yeova nũtanaa ĩla wamũvoya o na ethĩwa ndũtonya kwĩanĩsya maũndũ maingĩ.—Nth. 15:8.
Aingĩ menyu no mwende mũno kwĩsomea syĩndũ na no mwende kũkwata vinya wa kũthi maũmbanonĩ, ĩndĩ no kwĩthĩwa ũndũ mũendeee kũkũa mwonaa kwĩka maũndũ asu kwĩ vinya kana kũtatonyeka. Kwoou nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya? Ĩka nesa maũndũ ala ũtonya. Kwa ngelekany'o, aingĩ ma ala matatonya kũthi maũmbanonĩ methukĩĩasya maũmbano na simũ. Nake mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Inge wĩ na myaka 79 ndonaa nthĩ nesa ĩndĩ o na ailyĩ ũu, aseũvasya maũmbano aitũmĩa mathangũ me na manamba manene. Mathangũ asu aumĩaw'a kombiũtanĩ nĩ mwana-a-asa me kĩkundinĩ kĩmwe.
Nĩwĩsĩ nĩ kyaũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa nakyo ala angĩ mate nakyo? Nĩ ĩvinda. Wĩona ata ũkosa ĩvinda yĩu wĩ nayo ũkethukĩĩsya syĩndũ ila ilekotiĩtwe, ta Mbivilia, mavuku, maũvoo, na ndulama? O na ĩngĩ no ũtũmĩe ĩvinda yĩu kũkũnĩa Aklĩsto ala angĩ simũ nĩ kana ũmekĩe vinya na 'mũithangaany'a mũĩkĩĩonĩ.'—Alo. 1:11, 12, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
NDŨKAOLE KĨTHITO KYAKU KYA KŨMŨTHŨKŨMA NGAI
Christa nũvĩtũkĩtye myaka 80 na easya ũũ e na kyeva: "Ndwĩsa kwĩw'a mũyo ĩla watw'ĩka ndũtonya kwĩanĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ta tene." Kwoou mũndũ mũkũũ atonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ekale e mũtanu? Peter e na myaka 75 na asũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu akasya atĩĩ: "Nĩ kwa kwĩthĩwa na woni mũseo. Ndũkatindĩe kũsũanĩa maũndũ ala ũtatonya kwĩka, ĩndĩ tanĩa kwĩka maũndũ ala ũtonya."
Nũtonya kũsũanĩa nzĩa imwe sya kũtavany'a ila we ũtonya kũtũmĩa? Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Heidi. E na myaka mbee wa 80 na yu ndatonya kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba ta tene. Nũndũ wa ũu nĩweemanyĩisye kũtũmĩa kombiũta e o na myaka ĩsu nĩ kana akaandĩkaa mavalũa. Namo Aklĩsto angĩ akũũ nĩmatavanasya ĩla me iwanzanĩ sya kũthyũmũa kana sya ngalĩ. Na ĩndĩ ethĩwa wĩkalaa kũla kũsũvĩawa ala akũũ, wĩona ata ũkosa kĩu ta kĩsio kyaku kya kũtavany'a na ũitavasya ndakĩtalĩ ila iũkũsũvĩa vamwe na andũ ala angĩ me vau ũvoo mũseo?
Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti aĩ na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũmũthaitha Yeova o na e o mũkũũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwaumisye mĩvothi na eeka mĩvango ya ũndũ ĩkalũ yĩkakwa. (1 Mav. 28:11–29:5) O naku no wĩke ta Ndaviti kwa kwĩthĩwa na wendi wa kũmanya kĩla kĩendeee wĩanĩ wa Ũsumbĩ nthĩ yonthe, na ũitata ũndũ ũtonya ũtetheesye wĩanĩ ũsu. Wĩona ata ũkakwata mbau wĩa wa mavainia na atavany'a angĩ me kĩthito kĩkundinĩ kyenyu kwa kũmekĩa vinya, kana kũmanenga kamũthĩnzĩo kanini, kana kũmaathĩsya? O na ĩla ũũvoya no ũvoyee amũika, andũ me na mĩsyĩ, ala me ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe, ala awau, kana ala makwatĩĩe maũndũ maito.
We mwene wĩ wa vata na wĩa ũla ũtethasya nĩ wa vata mũno. Inyw'ĩ ala akũũ, Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ ndakaamwĩkya. (Sav. 71:9) Yeova nũmwendete na onaa mwĩ ma vata mũno. O mĩtũkĩ ithyonthe tũkilyĩ tũnavika ĩvinda yĩla tũkekala myaka mingĩ tũte na thĩna o na ũmwe. Ĩvinda yĩu tũkethĩwa na vinya mwingĩ na tũikathĩnw'a nĩ mwĩĩ, na nũndũ wa ũu tũkaendeea kũmũthũkũma Ngai witũ wĩ wendo, Yeova, tene na tene!
^ kal. 2 Masyĩtwa amwe nĩ mavĩndũe.
