ERNST is 70 years old and recently he expressed this: "I am still thinking about it." * What can we learn from Ernst? It is good to continue growing spiritually and to think deeply about things, but also to be willing to accept correction when necessary—even if it comes from someone younger than ourselves, like the brother who wrote the article "Keep Your Heart Active" in The Watchtower of December 12. On the first day of that week, older men were called "presiding overseers." Consider whether you can apply what you have learned from this scripture without being discouraged or feeling inadequate. And continue to remain close to Jehovah through prayer.
MAKE YOUR DECISIONS WISELY
Many people make decisions based on their feelings. However, wise individuals seek direction from God and ask Him for guidance. For example, Isaac, Jacob, and Leah made good choices. (Gen. 27:1; 48:10; 1 Chron. 14:4) Sarah once laughed at the thought of having a son. (Gen. 18:11, 12) King David was once called "a man of loving-kindness." (1 Chron. 1:1) Mephibosheth, despite his physical limitations, showed courage and loyalty during a difficult time. (2 Sam. 19:32-35) Also, Ruth showed kindness to her mother-in-law Naomi.—Ruth 23:1, 2; Luke 1:3, 12.
What can each of us learn from these examples about seeking Jehovah's guidance and striving to please him? Consider the example of Abraham. He always put Jehovah's standards first, and as a result he was "declared righteous" because of his faith. (Rom. 4:19, 20) Let us also cultivate strong faith. And even if we face trials, disappointments, or hardships, let us remember the example of Jacob. Despite facing difficulties and challenges, he continued to trust in God's promises and remained faithful. (Gen. 48:1-4, 10; Heb. 11:21) There was a sister named Agnes who was 93 years old. Despite her advanced age and the challenges of getting around, she said: "I still try to praise Jehovah every day. I thank Him every day. This helps me to stay spiritually strong." What can we learn from this sister's example?
Let us examine our own faith and see how we can strengthen it by studying God's Word and applying Christian principles. Consider the example of Daniel. He resolutely prayed three times a day, despite the risk involved, and continued to uphold God's standards. (Dan. 6:10; 9:2) Anna, an elderly widow, also showed great devotion when she "continued serving night and day" in the temple, praising God. (Luke 2:36, 37) And even though she faced many hardships and anxieties, she kept her focus on spiritual things and found strength in prayer. The more we pray to Jehovah, the more we will appreciate His loving care and be able to cope with life's challenges.—Ps. 15:8.
Many of you likely find it beneficial to spend time in personal study and to meditate on ways to apply what you learn. However, do you ever feel that you are making little progress or that you are getting discouraged? What can help you stay motivated? Focus on the positive aspects. For instance, many people find it helpful to share their faith with others. A sister named Inge, who was 79 years old, felt compelled to do so, and she began offering publications at local markets. She often struck up conversations with young ones while their parents were shopping.
Is there something else that can help us stay motivated? Yes, zeal. Do you take the initiative to use your zeal to accomplish worthwhile goals, such as preaching, teaching, witnessing, and helping others? Or do you use your zeal to support fellow Christians and 'strengthen their hearts'?—Acts 1:11, 12, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
EXAMINE YOURSELF REGARDING YOUR DEVOTION TO GOD
Christa was over 80 years old when she said: "I want to make good use of whatever ability I have to do much more." Can an elderly person still achieve significant results? Peter was 75 years old and continued to serve diligently, saying: "I am grateful for my health. I will continue to do everything I can, as long as I am able."
Can you set realistic goals, yet still strive to do your best? Consider the example of Heidi. She was nearly 80 years old and could no longer travel from house to house. Nevertheless, she found ways to preach by writing letters. And many Christians find that they can witness effectively despite physical limitations or age. But if you are physically able, why not join others in the ministry and offer assistance to those who may need it?
The psalmist David had a strong desire to honor Jehovah throughout his life. For instance, he expressed his delight in God's law and meditated on it day and night. (Ps. 1:2; 119:97) He also prayed earnestly to know God's will fully and to live in harmony with it. Do you ever feel overwhelmed by the amount of work there is to do, or discouraged because of mistakes you have made, or fearful? If so, remember that Jehovah understands our feelings. He knows that we are imperfect and that we live in a world filled with problems.
We grow older, and our abilities decline. However, like Asa, we can remain steadfast. (Ps. 71:9) Jehovah supports us and gives us strength. All of us want to enjoy life to the fullest for as long as possible. Life presents us with many challenges, but we can face them with courage, and we will continue to love our loving God, Jehovah, forever!
^ par. 2 Some advice may be helpful.

text:
MŨTHENYA wa Wakwambĩlĩlya Ĩtukũ 1, Mwei wa 9, 1919, kwaĩ kaũvyũvu na kasyũla o na kau mĩthenya ĩla yaĩ ĩnavĩta kwaĩ kĩuutani kingĩ na mbua. Saa sya mũthenya iivika kwaĩ aeni ta 1,000, ala moombanĩe vandũ vetawa Cedar Point, vala ve Ohio, Amelika, ĩsũmbanĩ yaĩ na ivĩla 2,500 nĩ kana methukĩĩsye kĩlungu kya kwambĩĩa kya ũmbano mũnene. Syũa yĩkilyĩ kũthũa, angĩ 2,000 nĩmavikie matũmĩĩte masiwa, ngalĩ, na ngalĩ sya mwaki sya mwanya. Ũnĩ ũũngĩ Wakelĩ, ala mookie maingĩvie weethĩa ũmbano ũsu no ũminũkĩlĩĩlaw'a andũ mailyĩ nza vandũ vaĩ mĩtĩ mĩnene na myanake.
Syũa nĩyaathĩte ĩndĩ kwaĩ o kwanake nũndũ syuu sya matũ syeesoleele makotinĩ ma aũme makekala ta me na malesi. Namo maw'ĩa ala maĩ ngovianĩ sya aka meleelaa nzevenĩ mavuvĩtwe nĩ kaseve kaumĩte o vau vakuvĩ Ĩianĩ ya Erie. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe aisye ũũ: "Ũmbano ũsu weekĩwe vandũ vaseo na vauĩtye vaasa na kũla kwĩthĩawa kelele, na kwoou tweew'aa ũu ta twĩ valatiso."
O na kau vala voombanĩwe vaĩ vanake, wanake ũsu waĩ vathei waelekanw'a na ũtanu ũla woonekaa mothyũnĩ ma ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Ĩkaseti yĩmwe ya kĩsio kĩu yaandĩkie: "Onthe meoneka makwatĩĩe ndĩni mũno, ĩndĩ nĩ atanu vyũ na nĩ athalĩku." Amanyĩw'a asu ma Mbivilia meew'aa kũmbana kwoo vamwe kwĩ mũyo mũno nũndũ nĩmakwatĩtwe nĩ matatwa maingĩ myaka mĩvũthũ ĩla yaĩ ĩnavĩta. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩmavĩngiwe ĩvindanĩ yĩla kwaĩ kaũ, kwaĩ mũaanĩko mũthũku ikundinĩ, Mbetheli ya Brooklyn nĩyavingĩtwe, aingĩ nĩmekĩtw'e kolokolonĩ nũndũ wa kũlũmany'a na Ũsumbĩ, o na ala ana-a-asa nyanya matongoesye nĩmekĩtw'e kolokolonĩ na amwe moo makatw'ĩĩwa kwovwa myaka 20. *
Amanyĩw'a amwe ma Mbivilia nĩmakw'ĩte ngoo na makatuanĩwa nũndũ wa mathĩna ala mamakwatĩte myakanĩ ĩsu, na kwoou nĩmaekete kũtavany'a. Ĩndĩ aingĩ matatĩte ũndũ matonya momĩĩsye, o na kau silikalĩ nĩyatatĩte kũmavindĩthya. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ ũmwe aisye o na kũtw'ĩka Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmakanĩtw'e mũno makewa maikatavany'e, ala wathianie maisye kana mo "meendeea kũtavany'a ndeto ya Ngai nginya mwĩso."
Myaka ĩsu yonthe ya mathĩna, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku mekalĩte "masyaĩtye Mwĩaĩi amatongoesye, . . . maivoya kĩla ĩvinda nĩ kana Asa amony'e nzĩa." Na yu ĩvinda yĩĩ maĩ na ngwatanĩo na ũtanu mombanĩe Cedar Point kwondũ wa ũla ũmbano mũnene. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe nĩwawetie ũndũ we mwene na ala angĩ molanĩalw'a ũndũ matonya kwĩsa "kwambĩĩa kũthyũũkya ĩngĩ ndĩa sya wĩa wa kũtavany'a." Vai kĩndũ kĩngĩ mendaa mũno kwĩka ta kwambĩĩa ĩngĩ wĩa wa kũtavany'a!
NĨMANENGIWE MŨIO MWEŨ!
Kyumwa kĩu kyonthe ala mookie ũmbanonĩ ũsu nĩmoonaa nthoo "GA" iandĩkĩtwe tũthangũnĩ twa walany'o wa ũmbano, tũvalũanĩ twa kũthokany'a, na ivwaũnĩ ila syaĩ kĩwanzanĩ kya ũmbano, na kwoou maseng'aa nthoo isu syaũngamĩe kyaũ. Mũthenya wa Wakatano ũla mawĩtie "Co-Laborers' Day," Joseph F. Rutherford nĩwesie kũmaumbũka andũ onthe 6,000 ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu kĩla nthoo isu syaũngamĩe. Nthoo isu "GA" syaũngamĩe ĩkaseti yeũ ya kũtũmĩawa ũtavany'anĩ, yĩla yaumiw'e ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Ĩkaseti yĩu yeetawa The Golden Age. *
Mwana-a-asa Rutherford aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Aklĩsto ala angĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta: "O na kau yĩĩ nĩ ĩvinda ya thĩna, mũĩkĩĩo woo ũtumaa mekala mene Ĩvinda Ĩseo [Golden Age] ĩla ũsumbĩki mũseo ki wa Masia ũkasumbĩka. . . . Matalaa kana kũtavya nthĩ yonthe ĩũlũ wa kũka kwa yĩla Ĩvinda Ĩseo nĩkyo kĩanda kyoo kĩla kĩnene maĩle kwĩanĩsya na kana nĩ ndaĩa nene kwoo kũtethya wĩa ũsu. Ũsu nĩ ũmwe katĩ wa mawĩa ala manengetwe nĩ Ngai."
Ĩkaseti ya The Golden Age yaandĩkĩtwe kavanĩ "Ĩkaseti yĩwetaa Ũw'o, yĩnenganae Wĩkwatyo, na yĩwetaa maũndũ Vate Nzika." Ĩkaseti yĩu yaaĩlĩte kũtũmĩwa kwambĩĩsya nzĩa nzaũ ya kũnyaĩĩkya ũw'o. Nzĩa ĩsu yaĩ kũthi nyũmba na nyũmba ũmanthĩte ala mekwenda kwĩyĩandĩkĩthya nĩ kana mayĩkwatae. Vakililye vaikũlw'a naaũ mekwenda kũtethya wĩa ũsu, onthe ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu maũngama me atanu. Na ĩndĩ "me na kĩthito na wendi ũtesa kwĩthĩwa na angĩ eka ala maatĩĩaa nyaaĩ sya Yesũ," nĩmainie wathi wĩ na ndeto: "Ete kyeni kyaku na w'o waku, ame Mwĩaĩi." Mwana-a-asa J. M. Norris aĩtye: "Ndikolwa nĩ ũndũ noonie mĩtĩ yathingitha."
Kĩlungu kĩu kya ũmbano kyathela, ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu mavangie lainĩ masaa maingĩ mayenda methĩwe katĩ wa ala ma mbee kwĩyĩandĩkĩthya makwatae ĩkaseti yĩu. Aingĩ moo meewie o ta Mabel Philbrick. Aisye atĩĩ: "Twatanie mũno kũmanya kana nĩtwakwata ĩngĩ wĩa wa kũtethya!"
"KWONDŨ WA ALA MANENGETWE ŨLA WĨA"
Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ta 7,000 nĩmeeyũmbanisye malike wĩanĩ. Kavuku keetawa Organization Method na kala kangĩ To Whom the Work Is Entrusted (Kwondũ wa Ala Manengetwe Ũla Wĩa) nĩtwaeleisye mũvango ũla waĩ vo. Twawetie maũndũ aa: Mbee, ve Mũvĩa wa Ũthũkũmi ũla wambĩĩw'e ovisinĩ ũla mũnene nĩ kana ũũngamĩe wĩa ũũ. Kelĩ, Kamitii ya Ũthũkũmi nĩyaaĩle kwambĩĩw'a kĩla kĩkundinĩ, na mũũngamĩi ainyuvwa nĩ kana akatavasya ala angĩ kĩla weewa kyaĩle kwĩkwa. Katatũ, isio syaaĩle kũaanw'a na kĩla kĩsio kyaaĩle kwĩthĩwa na nyũmba katĩ wa 150 na 200. Na ĩndĩ maaĩle kwĩka Ũmbano wa Ũthũkũmi kĩla Wakana ĩ ya wĩoo nĩ kana ana-a-asa mawete maũndũ ala monie ũtavany'a na mayumya livoti syoo.
Mwana-a-asa Herman Philbrick aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩla twavikie mĩsyĩ kwitũ, ithyonthe twalikile kambeininĩ ya kũmantha andũ ala mekwenda kwĩyĩandĩkĩthya makwatae makaseti." Kĩla vandũ meethĩaa andũ mekwenda kwĩthukĩĩsya. Beulah Covey aisye kana "veoneka ĩtina wa kaũ na kyeva kingĩ, kĩla mũndũ nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ kũmanya kana ve ĩvinda ĩseo yũkĩte." Nake Arthur Claus aandĩkie: "Kĩkundi kyonthe kyaseng'iw'e mũno nĩ kwona ũndũ andũ ala meeyĩandĩkĩthisye maingĩvĩte." Kũithela myei ĩlĩ kuma yambĩĩa kũtumbĩthw'a, vakuvĩ makaseti nusu milioni ma The Golden Age nĩmanenganĩtwe, na andũ 50,000 makeyĩandĩkĩthya.
Mwana-a-asa A. H. Macmillan aisye kana kĩla kĩlungu kyaĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya The Watch Tower ya 01/07/1920 kyaĩ na kyongo, "Ũvoo Mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ," nĩkyo kyaĩ "kya mbee vyũ kwĩkĩa vinya ana-a-asa matavany'e nthĩ yonthe o tondũ kũtilyĩ ũmũnthĩ." Kĩlungu kyu nĩkyathangaaisye Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta "makũsĩĩe nthĩ yonthe kana ũsumbĩ wa ĩtu ndwĩ vaasa." Ũmũnthĩ, "ala manengetwe ũla wĩa," namo nĩ ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto, nĩmakwetwe mbau nĩ andũ milioni mbingĩ, ala matavanasya ndeto na kĩthito meteele yĩla ĩvinda ĩseo yĩkaetwe nĩ Masia.

translation:
The spirit of Wakwambilya on November 1, 1919, came with great force and a whirlwind and many spirits went to a large gathering and a beast. The size of the spirit was about 1,000, but people from Cedar Point, near Ohio, America, estimated it to be around 2,500 and perhaps exaggerated the story of the huge assembly. It seemed to move towards us, about 2,000 were armed with spears, shields, and the light of fire. It was like Wakeli, but many entered the assembly which was frightening and made people afraid like those who see big trees and snakes.
It appeared closer and clearer than before, like many small boats floating on the lake and the waves. Then they saw it and many said it was a monster moving on the surface of Lake Erie. One child said: "This assembly is for brave people and those who fear children and its sound is terrifying, and we will run away from here if it comes close."
And many people gathered there, this place was chosen and prepared for this huge assembly. One paper read: "Anyone who looks closely will see five stars and they are shining." Messengers from Mbivilia came together to share this news and it was seen by many people over several years. For example, it was reported that a certain place, a beautiful mountain, Bethel of Brooklyn was built, and many were sent to colonies to preach the truth, and also old men and women traveled to colonies and some were imprisoned for 20 years. *
Some messengers from Mbivilia went and were imprisoned because of their preaching work, and those places became known for being difficult. And many experienced great trials, and some felt like giving up. For example, one person wanted to stop sending messengers from Mbivilia, but he was persuaded by his friends not to give up on God's purpose.
For many years, messengers from Mbivilia who were considered "loyal witnesses, . . . who testified in every city and even Asia" had an experience near Cedar Point during a large gathering. One old man shared his story and others discussed how difficult it was to say "I will continue to testify despite everything." What a wonderful thing it is to continue testifying despite everything!
I HAVE BEEN ENCOURAGED!
Throughout that year and the following gatherings, the letters "GA" were printed on the program of the assembly, on badges for identification, and on various items related to the assembly, and they stood for something important. On Labor Day, Joseph F. Rutherford organized over 6,000 people at that gathering and they all wore those letters. Those letters "GA" represented a special assignment to be sent out to preach, which was announced at that gathering. That assignment was called The Golden Age. *
The young man Rutherford said to the Christians and others: "And so if this is the time, our efforts will make this Golden Age shine brightly as the kingdom of the Messiah shines. . . . Let us forget all difficulties and let the Golden Age be the means by which we can show our loyalty and prove ourselves worthy of His favor. You are one of the chosen ones among many whom God has selected."
The Golden Age assignment was described as "An assignment to tell, to explain, and to offer life everlasting." It involved going from house to house and offering literature, even if people did not want it. Publishers would call back repeatedly to try to reach people, sometimes making five visits to each household. And with "zeal and energy, go forth and proclaim the good news of Jesus," he urged them with emphasis: "Go now and do what you have to do, O faithful servants." Young man J. M. Norris said: "I am convinced that I have never seen such enthusiasm."
During that assembly, people at that gathering spent many hours distributing the literature to those who wanted to receive it. Many were like Mabel Philbrick. She said: "We were very eager to know if we could get more to distribute!"
"THE ACTIVITY OF THE CHOSEN PEOPLE"
About 7,000 Bible students were organized into groups. The method was called Organization Method and also To Whom the Work Is Entrusted ("The Activity of the Chosen People"). This arrangement helped to expand the work. We learned these things: First, the congregation should be large enough to support a full-time minister or several ministers. Second, the congregation overseer should visit each publisher regularly, and the supervisor should encourage him or help him if he is discouraged. Third, each congregation should cooperate with every other congregation within a radius of 150 to 200 miles. And they should arrange for Kingdom Hall assemblies every month or so, and young people should present programs that will appeal to voters.
Young man Herman Philbrick said: "Although we started small, we quickly realized the need to unite those who wanted to preach the good news." Many people want to learn more. Beulah Covey said that "it seems like yesterday, and yet everyone feels that this important event has already happened." Brother Arthur Claus wrote: "The entire group was eager to see what those who had been baptized would do." In addition to being encouraged, half a million copies of The Golden Age magazine were distributed, and 50,000 people requested literature.
Young man A. H. Macmillan said that the July 1, 1920 issue of The Watch Tower, with the title "God's Kingdom," contained something "that will help young people throughout their lives to remain loyal." That week's issue urged Christians to be bold and proclaim "the kingdom of God" to others. Loyalty, "although tested repeatedly," also helped millions of Christian youths to maintain their zeal and continue serving Jehovah despite opposition from Satan.

text:
Ĩla twasoma ũvoo ũla ũeleetye ĩũlũ wa wũmbi ĩvukunĩ ya Mwambĩlĩlyo, nĩtwĩmanyĩasya kana mũndũ wa mbee, Atamu, eeiwe nĩ Ngai atĩĩ: "Wa kĩla mũtĩ wa mũũndanĩ nũtonya ũya o ũndũ ũkwenda: ĩndĩ wa mũtĩ wa kũmanyĩthya ũseo na ũthũku, ndũkaye: nĩkwĩthĩwa mũthenya ũla ũkaya waw'o ndũkatĩa ũkw'a." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:16, 17) Ndeto isu syĩonany'a nesa kana kethĩwa Atamu nĩweewie mwĩao wa Ngai, ndethĩwa aakw'a ĩndĩ ethĩwa aendeeie kwĩkala mũũndanĩ wa Eteni.
Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana vandũ va Atamu kwĩw'a mwĩao wa Ngai na kwĩkala tene na tene, nĩwatwie kũleana naw'o na aya ĩtunda yĩla kĩveti kyake, Eva, kyamũnengie o na kau nĩmavatĩtwe. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:1-6) Maũndũ ala mamakwatie nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa mate ewi no matũkwataa ũmũnthĩ. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aeleisye ũndũ ũsu kwa ndeto ii: "Nũndũ wa mũndũ ũmwe naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ; na kwa ũu kĩkw'ũ kyavikĩa andũ onthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa onthe nĩmeekie naĩ." (Alomi 5:12) "Mũndũ ũmwe" ũla ũwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu aĩ Atamu. Ĩndĩ naĩ ĩla yeekiwe nĩ yĩva, na nĩkĩ yaetie kĩkw'ũ?
Ũndũ ũla Atamu weekie, naw'o nĩ kũtũla mwĩao wa Ngai o esĩ, nĩ naĩ. (1 Yoana 3:4) Na ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ, o tondũ Ngai watavisye Atamu. Kethĩwa Atamu na ũsyao wake nĩmaendeeie kwĩw'a mwĩao wa Ngai, mayĩthĩwa maakwatwa nĩ naĩ na mayĩthĩwa maakw'a. Ngai ndaaũmba andũ makusae, ĩndĩ amombie mekalae tene na tene.
Vai nzika kana kĩkw'ũ 'nĩkyavikĩie andũ onthe,' o tondũ Mbivilia yaitye. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Ve kĩndũ kĩ nthĩnĩ witũ kĩendeeaa kwĩkala thayũ ĩla twakw'a? Andũ aingĩ no masye ĩĩ nũndũ maĩkĩĩaa kana thayũ ndũkusaa. Ĩndĩ vakethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, ndeto ila Ngai watavisye Atamu syĩthĩwa syaĩ sya ũvũngũ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ keka ve kĩndũ kĩ nthĩnĩ witũ kĩendeeaa kwĩkala thayũ vandũ vangĩ ĩla mũndũ wakw'a, kĩkw'ũ kĩyĩthĩwa ĩtuvi ya naĩ, o tondũ Ngai waisye. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũitonyeka Ngai kũneena ũvũngũ." (Aevelania 6:18) Kwa w'o, Satani nĩwe wakenganie ĩla wamwĩie Eva atĩĩ: "Mũikakw'a nongĩ."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:4.
Ũndũ ũsu no ũtũme twĩkũlya-ĩ, Ethĩwa ũmanyĩsyo wa kana thayũ ndũkusaa umanĩte na ũvũngũ wa Satani, kwĩthĩawa ata ĩla mũndũ wakw'a?
MBIVILIA NĨTŨTETHEEASYA KŨMANYA MAŨNDŨ NESA
Ũvoo ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mwambĩlĩlyo wa wũmbi waĩtye atĩĩ: "Yeova Ngai oomba mũndũ na kĩtoo kya nthĩ, na amũvevea mĩthũmũ ya thayũ manyiũũnĩ make; na mũndũ atw'ĩka kyuu kĩ thayũ." Ndeto "kyuu kĩ thayũ" ĩalyũlĩtwe kuma ndetonĩ ya Kĩevelania yĩtawa ne'phesh, * ĩla yonanasya "kyũmbe kĩũveva."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:7.
Kwoou Mbivilia yonanĩtye nesa kana andũ mayũmbĩtwe me na thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a. Ĩndĩ kĩla mũndũ nĩ "kyuu kĩ thayũ." Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi o na ũkamantha ata, ndwĩsa kwona vandũ Mbivilia ĩtũmĩĩte ndeto "thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a."
Nũndũ Mbivilia ndyaĩtye kana andũ me thayũ ũtakusaa, nĩkĩ atongoi aingĩ ma ndĩni mamanyĩasya ũndũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o? Nĩ kana tũkwate ũsũngĩo, ekai twone maũndũ meekĩkaa ĩvindanĩ ya tene nthĩ ya Misili.
ŨNDŨ ŨMANYĨSYO WA ANDŨ MATAMŨTHAITHAA NGAI WANYAĨĨKIE
Mũsomi ũmwe wa maũndũ ma tene waĩ Mũkiliki weetawa Herodotus, ũla waĩ kw'o myaka 2,400 mĩvĩtu, aisye kana Amisili nĩmo maĩ "ma mbee kũtetea ũmanyĩsyo wa kana thayũ ndũkusaa." O namo andũ ma Mbaviloni ya tene nĩmeetĩkĩlanile na woni ũsu. Ĩvinda yĩla Alexander Ũla Mũnene wasindie nthĩ sya Middle East mwakanĩ wa 332 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, asomi maĩ Akiliki nĩmamanyĩĩtye ũmanyĩsyo ũsu, na kwa ĩvinda ĩnini wanyaĩĩkw'a kĩla vandũ Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ũkiliki.
Ndwĩsa kwona vandũ Mbivilia ĩtũmĩĩte ndeto "thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a"
Ĩvindanĩ ya Atũmwa, ndĩni ilĩ sya Kĩyuti syaĩ nguma, nasyo nĩ sya Avalisi na Aasene (Essenes), nĩsyamanyĩasya kana thayũ ndũkusaa. Ĩvuku yĩtawa The Jewish Encyclopedia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ayuti mambĩĩie kũĩkĩĩa kana thayũ ndũkusaa ĩla meetĩkĩlanile na momanyĩsyo ma Akiliki, na mũno mũno kwĩsĩla momanyĩsyo ma Plato." O na ĩngĩ, mũsomi waĩ Mũyuti weetawa Josephus, ũla waĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, nĩwaeleisye kana ũmanyĩsyo ũsu ndwaumanĩte na Maandĩko Matheu, ĩndĩ waumanĩte na 'kĩla Akiliki maĩkĩĩaa.' Na oonaa isu ne mbano ila syaumanĩte na andũ ala maeaa mbano sya ĩvinda ya tene.
O ũndũ andũ aingĩ maendeeie kwĩtĩkĩla kĩthĩo na maũndũ ala Akiliki meekaa, ala meeyĩtaa Aklĩsto nĩmeetĩkĩlanile na ũmanyĩsyo ũsu wa andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai, o vamwe na kwĩtĩkĩla syĩthĩo isu. Kwosana na ndeto sya mũsomi weetawa Jona Lendering, "ũmanyĩsyo wa Plato wa kana ve ĩvinda thayũ witũ wekalaa vandũ vaseango na yu wĩkalaa nthĩ yĩ mathĩna nĩwatumie wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũlikany'a momanyĩsyo ma Plato na ma Kĩklĩsto." Kwoou, mũĩkĩĩo wa kana thayũ ndũkusaa, ũla waumanĩte na andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai, nĩwalikile kanisanĩ wa "Kĩklĩsto" na watw'ĩka ũmwe katĩ wa momanyĩsyo ala manene ma kanisa.
"ŨLA W'O ŨKAMŨTHASYA"
Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, mũtũmwa Vaulo aumĩsye ũkany'o ũũ: "Veva eneena vyũ, kana mavinda ma mũminũkĩlyo amwe makatia ũla mũĩkĩĩo, makĩthukĩĩsya maveva ala makenganaa, na momanyĩsyo ma ndaimoni." (1 Timotheo 4:1) Ndeto isu nĩsyamanyĩkie kana syaĩ sya w'o vyũ! Mũĩkĩĩo wa kana thayũ ndũkusaa nĩ ngelekany'o ĩmwe ya "momanyĩsyo ma ndaimoni." Mbivilia ndĩtĩkĩlanaa na ũmanyĩsyo ũsu, ĩndĩ umanĩte na ndĩni sya tene sya andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai na momanyĩsyo ma andũ.
Nĩtũtanĩthaw'a nĩ ndeto ii Yesũ wawetie. Aisye atĩĩ: "Mũkamanya ũla w'o, na ũla w'o ũkamũthasya." (Yoana 8:32) Ĩla tweethĩwa na ũmanyi ũla waĩlĩte wa ũw'o wa Mbivilia, nĩtũthaaw'a kuma momanyĩsyonĩ ala matamũnengae Ngai ndaĩa na maũndũ ala mekawa nĩ ndĩni mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. O na ĩngĩ, ũw'o ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai nũtũthaasya kuma ũkombonĩ wa syĩthĩo na maũndũ ala makonanĩtye na ndaimoni mekawa ĩla mũndũ wakw'a.—Sisya ĩsandũkũ yĩ na kyongo "Akw'ũ Maĩva?"
Mũmbi witũ ndendaa andũ mekalae myaka 70 kana 80 ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na mayĩsa kũthi makekalae tene na tene wĩkalonĩ ũngĩ. Kĩeleelo kyake kyaĩ andũ mekalae tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ me syana mbĩwi. Kĩeleelo kyu kya Ngai nĩ wonany'o wa wendo wake kwa andũ na kĩikasiĩĩwa. (Malaki 3:6) Aiĩkĩĩthya ndeto isu, mũandĩki wa Savuli aisye atĩĩ: "Ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makatũa vo kũvika tene na tene."—Savuli 37:29.
^ kal. 9 Mbivilia imwe ta King James Version na Catholic Douay Version, ialyũlĩte ndeto ne'phesh ta "kyuu kĩ thayũ," nasyo Mbivilia mbingĩ sya matukũ aa ialyũlĩte ndeto ĩsu ta "kyũmbe kĩ thayũ." Nayo Mbivilia ya The New English Bible; New International Version na The Jerusalem Bible; ĩalyũlĩte ndeto ĩsu ta "mũndũ wĩ thayũ," nayo Today's English Version ĩalyũlĩte ndeto ĩsu ta "eethĩwa thayũ."

translation:
So we read how the serpent brought trouble to Eve in the garden of Eden, and they both, Adam and Eve, disobeyed God, who said: "From every tree of the garden you may eat freely, but from the tree of the knowledge of good and bad you must not eat from it." (Eden 2:16, 17) But unfortunately she did not listen and disobeyed Adam, and she was the first one to disobey God and begin to live as an imperfect human.
The result was that Adam also lost his standing with God and became like her, and together with her and their first child, Eve, they produced children and multiplied. (Eden 3:1-6) These things happened as a test of whether they would obey God or not. The apostle Paul explained this point by saying: "Through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin, and in this way death spread to all men, because all have sinned." (Romans 5:12) That "one man" referred to above was Adam. And what was the result of his disobedience, and why was it so serious?
What Adam did, and which was to reject God's authority, was a sin. (1 John 3:4) And the consequence of this was sin, because God allowed Adam to be disobedient. Because Adam and his descendants continued to reject God's authority, they were condemned to die and to perish. God does not want people to perish, he wants them to live forever.
But ask yourself why 'sin spread to all men,' as the Bible says. The reason is that we all inherit imperfection from our first parents. So what can we do to escape death? Many people believe that they can save themselves from death. But those who think this way, this teaching of God about Adam's disobedience shows us the truth. Why is it that we all inherit imperfection from our first parents, just as Adam did, and why is it so important, because God allows it? The Bible says: "Practicing righteousness means life." (Proverbs 6:18) Therefore, Satan was the deceiver when he told Eve: "You will not surely die."—Eden 3:4.
This should make us think, and understand that the belief that we can save ourselves is connected with Satan's deception, and even though someone might succeed, is it worth it?
THE BIBLE HELPS US TO UNDERSTAND IMPORTANT THINGS
The account in Eden tells us: "Jehovah God formed man out of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul." The expression "living soul" has been translated in the Greek version of the Scriptures as *psyche,* which means "life force."—Eden 2:7.
So the Bible clearly shows that humans are not immortal souls. Every human is a "living soul." And that is why it is important to pay attention to what the Bible teaches about "life force."
Why does the Bible say that humans are imperfect, and how does this help us to understand things better? Or shall we look at examples of what happened in recent times in Brazil.
UNDERSTANDING WHAT PEOPLE WHO REJECT GOD WANT
One ancient historian named Herodotus, who lived over 2,400 years ago, said that Egyptians considered themselves to be "the most religious people on earth." They also had a lot of superstitions. This explains why when Alexander the Great conquered the Middle East around 332 BCE, Greek scholars learned about their beliefs, and for centuries they influenced people throughout the Mediterranean region.
Pay attention to what the Bible teaches about "life force"
The sect of the Essenes, which included groups in Qumran, as well as those in Alexandria and Ascalon, greatly emphasized life force. The Jewish Encyclopedia states: "Many Essenes devoted themselves to the study of Egyptian beliefs, and often incorporated Platonic philosophy." Also, the Jewish historian Josephus, who wrote about this sect, explained that this belief was connected with the book of Matthew, and was associated with 'every Egyptian priest.' And indeed, this idea has parallels with the beliefs of other peoples from ancient times.
However, many people believe that the Egyptians had influence on the beliefs of the Greeks, who called Christ, were influenced by this belief of people who revered God, and some also embraced it. According to scholar Jon Lendering, "Plato's philosophy may have been a source for the Essenes, who saw themselves as foreigners and considered their wisdom superior to that of Plato and Christians." Therefore, the concept of life force, which was associated with people who revered God, became linked to the term "Christian" and they integrated it into the core doctrines of the church.
"THE ONE WHO WILL BE EXALTED"
In his letter, the apostle Paul warned: "For there will be times when people will be self-absorbed, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, revilers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy, having no love, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, fierce, opposed to goodness, treacherous, reckless, puffed up with pride, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God." (1 Timothy 4:1) Let us examine whether today's situation reflects those characteristics! The concept of life force is like one of the "philosophies of demons." I agree with this belief because it originates from people who revere God and the philosophies of men.
We will be set free by knowing what Jesus said. He said: "You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free." (John 8:32) But if we are freed by the knowledge of this truth found in the Bible, we will be able to reject the teachings that dishonor God and the things that originate from demonic sources—things that enslave a person.—Consider the brochure "What Does God Require?"
Our Creator wants people to live about 70 or 80 years on earth and to enjoy life to the fullest during those years. His purpose is for people to live forever on earth in peace. God's purpose shows his love for mankind and his generosity. (Malachi 3:6) In harmony with this, the psalmist wrote: "The righteous will reside forever on the earth, and their hope is everlasting." —Psalm 37:29.
^ par. 9 The King James Version and the Catholic Douay Version often use the expression "hell fire," while many modern Bibles render it "Gehenna fire." Also, The New English Bible; New International Version and The Jerusalem Bible; render it "valley of Hinnom," whereas Today's English Version renders it "place of burning."

text:
Mbona tene mavuku maitũ maielesya ngewa sya Mbivilia makothaa kũweta maũndũ elĩ, kyuu na kĩla kya w'o, ĩndĩ yu ti mũno. Nĩkĩ matekaa ũu?
Ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩsũngũ) ya 15/09/1950 nĩyaeleisye ĩũlũ wa ndeto "kyuu" na "kĩla kya w'o." Yaisye atĩĩ: "Kyuu nĩ ngelekany'o ya ũndũ kana kĩndũ kĩkekĩka ĩvinda yũkĩte. Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũsu kana kĩndũ kyu kyesa kwĩkĩka kĩitalwa takyo kĩla kya w'o."
Myaka mingĩ mĩvĩtu mavuku maitũ nĩmawetete kana aũme na aka aĩkĩĩku ta Ndevola, Eliu, Yevitha, Yovu, Laavi, Leveka na angĩ aingĩ maĩ syuu sya etĩkĩw'a mauta kana "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ." (Ũvu. 7:9) Kwa ngelekany'o, Yevitha, Yovu, na Leveka moonekaa maĩle kũelekanw'a na etĩkĩw'a mauta, namo Ndevola na Laavi matw'ĩkĩkaa kana maelekanĩtye yĩla ĩkomano ĩnene. Ĩndĩ myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ tũieleasya ũvoo woo ũu. Nĩkĩ tũtekaa ũu?
Maandĩko nĩmonanĩtye kana andũ amwe ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ maĩ kyuu kya ũndũ ũngĩ mũnenange. Ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akalatia 4:21-31 mũtũmwa Vaulo nũwetete "ngelekany'o" yĩ na aka elĩ. Akali, ũla waĩ mwĩĩtu mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu, aĩ ngelekany'o ya mbaĩ ya Isilaeli, ĩla yaĩ mbaĩ ya Yeova kwosana na ĩla Mĩao ya Mose. Ĩndĩ Sala, ũla waĩ mũndũ mũka "ũte ngombo," aĩ ngelekany'o ya kĩveti kya Ngai kĩla nĩkyo kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Ngai kya ĩtunĩ. Ĩla Vaulo waandĩkĩie Aevelania valũa, nĩwakonanisye Yesũ na Melikiseteki, ũla waĩ mũthembi na mũsumbĩ, na oonany'a ũndũ mavw'anene maũndũnĩ me kĩvathũkany'o. (Aevl. 6:20; 7:1-3) O na ĩngĩ, Vaulo nĩwoonanisye kana Isaia na ana make maĩ ngelekany'o ya Yesũ na aatĩĩi make etĩkĩw'a mauta. (Aevl. 2:13, 14) Nũndũ Vaulo aandĩkaa e mũveveee, tũyĩsa kũlea maũndũ asu ũandĩkĩte ĩũlũ wa kyuu na kĩla kya w'o.
Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ĩla Mbivilia yaweta kana mũndũ mũna nĩ kyuu kya mũndũ ũngĩ, tũyaĩle kũtw'a kana maũndũ onthe ala maaĩkĩka thayũnĩ wa mũndũ ũsu ũkwĩtwa kyuu nĩ ngelekany'o ya maũndũ angĩ manenange. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na kau Vaulo nũtũtavĩtye kana Melikiseteki aĩ kyuu kya Yesũ, ndaaweta yĩla ĩvinda Avalaamu wasindie asumbĩ 4, na Melikiseteki amũetee kĩmũtũ na mbinyu nĩ kana aitanĩe. Kwondũ wa ũu, Maandĩko maitũnengete kĩtumi kya kũmanthĩthya kĩla kyonanaw'a nĩ kĩko kĩu kya Melikiseteki.—Mwa. 14:1, 18.
Myaka maana meana ũna kuma Klĩsto akw'a, aandĩki amwe nĩmakwatiwe nĩ mũthemba wa kũmanthaa syuu ngewanĩ sya Mbivilia o na kũla ite vo. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩla yĩeleetye momanyĩsyo ma Origen, Ambrose, na Jerome yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Matataa kũmanthĩthya syuu Maandĩkonĩ, namo nĩmasyonaa nthĩnĩ wa ngewa o na yĩva ĩeleetw'e kana nthĩnĩ wa kaũndũ o na keva kala kaaĩkĩka, o na katw'ĩke kanyivĩte ata. O na ũndũ ũte wa vata mũno na weekawa kĩla mũthenya woonekaa ta ũvithanĩtye ũw'o ũtamanyĩka mĩtũkĩ . . . , o na nĩ ũsengy'o ũndũ amwe matatie kũmanthĩthya kĩla kyoonanaw'a nĩ ũtalo wa ala makũyũ 153 makwatiw'e nĩ amanyĩw'a ũtukũ ũla Mwovosya wamaumĩlĩle amina kũthayũũkw'a!"—The International Standard Bible Encyclopaedia.
Mũndũ weetawa Augustine wa Hippo nĩwaeleisye mũno ĩũlũ wa ũla ũvoo ũwetete Yesũ ayĩĩthya aũme 5,000 atũmĩĩte imũtũ itano sya mbaale (barley) na makũyũ elĩ. Nũndũ mbaale nĩyavũthĩtw'e yaelekanw'a na nganũ, Augustine aisye atĩ imũtũ isu itano no ũndũ ũmwe na ala mavuku atano ma Mose (kũvũthw'a kwa "mbaale" kwaelekanaw'a na kũvũthya kũla andũ mavũthĩtye "Ũtianĩo Mũkũũ"). Nata ala makũyũ elĩ? Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩtesĩkĩe, amaelekanilye na mũsumbĩ na mũthembi. Nake mũsomi ũngĩ wendete mũno kũmanthĩthya syuu aisye atĩ ũndũ Yakovo wathooie ũkithathi wa Esau aitũmĩa ũsũũ wa ndengũ ndune, no ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ Yesũ wathooeie andũ ũtiĩwa kũya ĩtunĩ aitũmĩa nthakame yake ndune!
Ethĩwa nũkwona maelesyo asu moo ma syuu masaanĩtye, vate nzika nĩwakwatya ũndũ kũmantha syuu kĩla vandũ kũtonya kũete thĩna wĩana. Andũ mayamba kũmanya nĩ ngewa syĩva sya Mbivilia syĩthĩawa ne syuu sya maũndũ ma ĩvinda yũkĩte, na nĩ syĩva syĩthĩawa ite syuu. Kwoou o kwa ũkuvĩ ũla ũseo nĩ atĩĩ: Vala Maandĩko maweta kana mũndũ mũna, kana ũndũ weekĩkie, kana o kĩndũ kĩna nĩ kyuu kya ũndũ ũngĩ, twĩtĩkĩlanaa namo mailyĩ ũu. Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kũsembea kũtalĩthya mũndũ mũna kana ũndũ mũna nĩ kyuu kya ũngĩ ethĩwa vai ĩandĩko yĩwetete ũu sanzũ.
Kwoou-ĩ, maũndũ ala mawetetwe Maandĩkonĩ vamwe na ngelekany'o ila iwetetwe vo itonya kũtũtethya kwa nzĩa yĩva? Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 15:4: 'Maũndũ o na meva ala mambie kũandĩkwa, nĩmaandĩkiwe nũndũ wa kũtũmanyĩasya, nĩ kana ũndũ wa wũmĩĩsyo na ũkiakisyo wa maandĩko twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo.' Vau Vaulo awetaa kana ana-a-asa make etĩkĩw'a mauta ala maĩ kw'o ĩvinda yĩu maĩ matonya kũtetheka vyũ masoma maũndũ ala maandĩkiwe Maandĩkonĩ. Ĩndĩ andũ onthe ala maamũthũkũma Ngai, methĩwe nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta kana nĩ ala "malondu angĩ," nĩmatethekete vyũ masoma "maũndũ o na meva ala mambie kũandĩkwa." O na ala matwĩe 'mĩthenyanĩ ĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo' no matetheke vyũ mamasoma, na vate nzika nĩmatethekete.—Yoa. 10:16; 2 Tim. 3:1.
Vandũ va kwona ngewa sya Mbivilia ta ikonetye kĩkundi kĩmwe kya andũ, kĩthĩwe nĩ kya etĩkĩw'a mauta kana nĩ kya yĩla ĩkomano ĩnene, kana vandũ va kũsyosa ta ikonetye o andũ matwĩe ĩvinda ĩna, andũ onthe ma Ngai vala mavika no matũmĩe maũndũ ala ngewa isu iũmamanyĩsya. Ta kwa ngelekany'o, vai vata wa kwona ĩvuku ya Yovu ta yĩkonetye o thĩna ũla etĩkĩw'a mauta moonie ĩvindanĩ ya Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ athũkũmi aingĩ ma Ngai, matw'ĩke nĩ aka kana nĩ aũme, nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta kana nĩ ala ma ĩkomano ĩnene, nĩmakwatĩtwe nĩ maũndũ ta ala makwatie Yovu, na "[nĩmonete] mũminũkĩlyo wa Mwĩaĩi, ũndũ Mwĩaĩi wusũĩte ĩnee na tei."—Yak. 5:11.
Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ĩla twĩ ikundinĩ sitũ tyo twonaa eĩtu-a-asa akũũ mekalĩte me aĩkĩĩku ta Ndevola, kana atumĩa ma mũika me na ũĩ ta wa Eliu, kana o mavainia me na ũkũmbaũ na kĩthito ta Yevitha, na aũme na aka aĩkĩĩku me na wũmĩĩsyo ta wa Yovu? Twĩw'aa mũyo ta kĩ kwona ũndũ Yeova waĩkĩĩthisye nĩtwakwata maũvoo ala me na "maũndũ o na meva ala mambie kũandĩkwa," nĩ kana "ũndũ wa . . . ũkiakisyo wa maandĩko twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo"!
Nũndũ wa itumi isu syawetwa, matukũnĩ aa mavuku maitũ makindĩlĩlaa mũno kĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya twasoma ngewa sya Mbivilia, vandũ va kũtata kũmanthĩthya syuu na kĩla kya w'o, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ kĩla kĩkwonanw'a nĩsyo.

translation:
Why then do our ancestors seem to despise the books of Revelation because of their difficulty, seeing that each of them is good? Is this right?
The letter from Musyaiisya (Kisungu) dated September 15, 1950 explains the meaning of "because" and "each of them." He says: "Because is an explanation of something or a certain thing that is clearly stated. And each thing or matter that is said to be clear is considered 'each of them.'"
For many years our ancestors have been confused or troubled by those who went to Ndovola, Eliu, Evita, Job, Levi, Levica and many others who were called servants of demons or "the great congregation of people." (Rev. 7:9) For example, Evita, Job, and Levica appear to be connected to the servants of demons, while Ndovola and Levi are said to be or associated with the great congregation. In recent years we have understood this matter. Is this right?
The scriptures show us that some people were despised by the Revelations because of something important. The account of Galatians 4:21-31 shows an "explanation" with this connection. Abraham, the father of Avaramu, was an explanation of the nation of Israel, which was God's nation like the Law of Moses. And Sarah, his wife, was an explanation of the covenant of God, which is beautiful and glorious. Paul wrote to the Hebrews, comparing Jesus to Melchizedek, the priest and king, and showing how great things are related to the fulfillment of promises. (Heb. 6:20; 7:1-3) Also, Paul showed that Isaiah and his children were explanations of Jesus and his prophecies about the servants of demons. (Heb. 2:13, 14) Therefore, when Paul writes, let us pay attention to what he has written regarding "because" and "each of them."
And in addition to this, the Bible teaches that a person is important because of someone else, so we should understand that things happen because of the influence of that person who is considered important through an explanation of other important things. For example, Paul explained that Melchizedek was important because of Jesus, and he showed that Abraham gave him a tenth of his possessions, and Melchizedek blessed him with words. Because of this, the scriptures help us to understand the importance of each comparison with the type of Melchizedek.—Gen. 14:1, 18.
Many years later, when Christians were being persecuted, some writers wrote about their hope of understanding the truth according to the Bible and learning more about it. One statement from Origen, Ambrose, and Jerome says: "It is difficult to interpret scripture, but it is necessary to examine its meaning carefully and to see what has been revealed through it, and to accept only what is clear. And the matter of faith requires that everyone be careful to avoid everything that seems doubtful… and it is helpful to have something to compare each comparison with, like the 153 fish caught by the disciples during the night when Peter confessed his love!"—The International Standard Bible Encyclopaedia.
Augustine of Hippo explained this point further, saying that Jesus fed 5,000 people using five loaves of barley bread and two fish. Since barley is often associated with poverty, Augustine said that the five loaves represented the first five books of Moses (the association of "barley" with teaching people "Instruction"). But what about the two fish? He suggested they symbolized the Old and New Testaments. A scholar who wanted to interpret this passage said that Jacob deceived Esau by giving him a bowl of lentil stew, and just as Jesus gave people life by offering them his body!
It seems that there are some lessons we can learn from these stories, so let us explore how each person can apply them to their own lives. People began to understand that the stories of the Bible are full of deeper meanings, and those meanings are also relevant today. The main point of this whole thing is this: Whether it's Scripture itself, a person, an event, or something else entirely, let us discuss it together. Let us strive to understand a person or an event more fully, because this story shows us how important it is to look beyond the surface.
However, some things written in the Scriptures are connected and explained, while others are left open to interpretation. Was Paul trying to show us how to interpret these scriptures when he wrote Romans 15:4: 'Everything that was written in the past was written to teach us,' or was it about the encouragement and comfort found in the scriptures that were given to us? Paul showed that what he had written could help people understand these deeper meanings within the scriptures. Indeed, those who seek God diligently, whether they are called "scholars" or not, will benefit from studying 'everything that was written.' And even those who have 'a spirit of discernment' will benefit from reading, and indeed, they already do.—John 10:16; 2 Timothy 3:1.
People who read portions of the Bible often form their own groups, sometimes referred to as "scholarship" or large schools of thought, and people who criticize them may also form their own groups, those who are devoted to God often use these different viewpoints to better understand things. For example, they might look at Job's story to see how scholarship can affect someone's understanding of life, like the way it affected Job, and "[they see] the patience of Job, which Jehovah commended."—James 5:11.
Consider this: Are we not inclined to view matters from our own perspective, just as the scholars did in ancient times, or as Elihu used his reasoning, or as the opponents used their arguments and accusations against Job, or even as Job himself used his defense? We would do well to remember that Jehovah has shown us how to value "both the good and the bad points mentioned in the writings," or even "the meaning of expressions found in the Scriptures that have been clarified"!
The importance of this matter is that when we regularly read portions of the Bible, people who try to reason will find something to focus on, or perhaps some new angle to consider.

ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1974
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: NDAĨKĨĨAA KANA NGAI E KW'O
KWĨANA KWAKWA
Nasyaĩwe vandũ vetawa Saxony, ĩla yĩ kĩsionĩ tene kyeetawa German Democratic Republic (GDR). Mũsyĩ kwitũ twekalanasya nesa na nĩtwendanĩte, na asyai makwa nĩmamanyĩĩtye kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Andũ aingĩ kĩsionĩ kya Saxony mayendeeaw'a nĩ maũndũ ma ndĩni nũndũ German Democratic Republic yaĩ ungu wa kyama kya Communist. O nakwa ndyaĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai e kw'o. Ve maũndũ elĩ noonaa me ma vata kwakwa myakanĩ yakwa ya mbee 18. Maũndũ asu nĩ kũĩkĩĩa kana kũi Ngai na ngwatanĩo ya Communism.
Nĩkĩ noonaa ngwatanĩo ya Communism yĩ nzeo? Nũndũ nĩnendeeaw'a mũno nĩ woni wa kana andũ onthe nĩmeanene. O na nĩnaĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syonthe syaĩle kũaanw'a nesa vate kyende, nũndũ kwĩka ũu no kũtume andũ methĩwa meaneny'e ũkwati. Na nũndũ wa ũu, nĩnalikile ngwatanĩonĩ ya andũ ma mũika ya Communist. Nĩ na myaka 14, natũmĩie ĩvinda yakwa yingĩ ndithũkũma wĩa waendeee wa kũthesya mawĩthyũlũlũko. Andũ taoninĩ ya Aue nĩmendeeiw'e mũno nĩ kĩthito kyakwa na kwoou anene ma kĩsio kĩu manenga mũthĩnzĩo. O na kau naĩ mũnini, nĩnamanyie amwe ma atongoi anene ma siasa ma German Democratic Republic. Noonaa nĩ na mĩvango ĩla yaĩle na ĩvinda yakwa yĩla yũkĩte yĩ ĩseo vyũ.
Ĩtina wa kavinda o kanini, maũndũ makwa nĩmaalyũkile. Mwaka wa 1989, Ũkũta wa Berlin (Berlin Wall) nĩwavalũkile vamwe na ngwatanĩo ya Communist ya Eastern Europe. Maũndũ mate maseo maendeee kwĩkĩka. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ nĩnamanyie kana kũyaĩ sila wa katĩ kĩsionĩ kya German Democratic Republic. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ala mateetĩkĩlanaa na ngwatanĩo ya Communism moonekaa mate ma vata. Ũndũ wa mũthemba ũsu ũtonya kwĩthĩwa waendeee ata na kyama kitũ kya Communist kyaĩkĩĩaa kana andũ onthe nĩmeanene? Kwani ngwatanĩo ĩsu ko yaemetwe nĩ wĩa wayo? Nĩnakwatiwe nĩ mawĩmakĩo maingĩ.
Maũndũ asu nĩmatumie nambĩĩa kwona kwina na kũsola nemo maũndũ ala ma vata vyũ kwakwa. Nũndũ nĩneemanyĩisye kwina sukulunĩ ya sekondalĩ nĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũthi yunivasĩtĩ, nĩnavangie kwĩthĩwa nĩ mwini na mũndũ wa kũsola mavisa. O na nĩnaekie kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo ũla namanyĩĩtw'e nĩ mũnini. Ũndũ ũla waĩ wa vata kwakwa waĩ kwĩtanĩthya na kũtuma ndũũ na twĩlĩtu twingĩ. Ĩndĩ kwina, kũsola, na kwĩtanĩthya kwa nzĩa ĩtaĩle kũyaatuma nĩeka kwĩthĩwa na mawĩmakĩo. O na mavisa ala nasolaa moonanasya kana naĩ na wia na ndyaĩ mũtanu. Neekũlasya-ĩ, Kũkeethĩwa kũilyĩ ata ĩvinda yũkĩte? Na nĩkĩ andũ moombiwe?
Ĩla nesie ũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala neekũlasya, nĩnaseng'ie mũno. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩ sukulu, nĩnekalile na kĩkundi kya amanyĩw'a maneeneaa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ve mwĩĩtu weetawa Mandy * twasomaa ĩmwe na waĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova. Mũthenya ũsu Mandy nĩwanengie ũtao mũseo. Ambĩie atĩĩ: "Andreas, ethĩwa nũkwenda kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala wĩkũlasya ĩũlũ wa thayũ na ĩvinda yũkĩte, ĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia kwa ũliku."
Ndyaĩkĩĩaa vyũ maũndũ ala natavĩtw'e, ĩndĩ nĩnatwie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nĩ kana nĩkwate mosũngĩo. Mandy ambonisye ĩandĩko ya Ndanieli kĩlungu kya 2, na maũndũ ala nasomie vau nĩmanzeng'isye. Wathani ũsu nũeleetye ĩũlũ wa silikalĩ nene mũno ĩũlũ wa nthĩ (world powers) ila syaĩ syĩthĩwe kw'o kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ. Mandy nĩwambonisye wathani ũngĩ wa Mbivilia ũkonetye ĩvinda yitũ yũkĩte. Nĩnambĩĩie kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala neekũlasya! Ĩndĩ nĩneekũlasya-ĩ, Nũũ waandĩkie wathani ũsu, na nũũ waĩ atonya kũweta ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte ate kũvĩtya? Nĩvatonyeka Ngai akethĩwa e kw'o?
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA
Mandy nĩwambonanisye na mũndũũme weetawa Horst na mũka wake Angelika, ala maĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, na nĩmandetheeisye kũmanya Ndeto ya Ngai nesa. Kwa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩnamanyie kana ndĩni ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩyo yendete kũtũmĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova. (Savuli 83:18; Mathayo 6:9) Nĩneemanyĩisye kana Yeova Ngai nũnengete andũ wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ. Savuli 37:9 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ala mamweteelaa Yeova, asu makatiĩwa nthĩ." Nĩnendeeiw'e nĩ kũmanya kana ndeto isu nĩ kwondũ wa onthe ala mekĩaa kĩthito mekale kwosana na myolooto ya Ngai ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ.
Ĩndĩ, nĩnang'ang'anie mũno kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle wakwa nĩ kana nĩkale kwosana na Mbivilia. Kwĩthĩwa nĩ mwini mũseo na mũsoli wa mavisa nĩkwatumĩte nĩthĩwa na mĩyimbyo, kwoou nĩnaĩlĩte kwamba kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo. O na ĩngĩ, ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũekana na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku ũla naĩ naw'o. Nĩnĩtũngaa mũvea nũndũ Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa na wũmĩĩsyo, tei, na nĩ ũeleawa andũ ala matataa ũndũ matonya meke kwosana na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya!
O na kau kwa myaka 18 naĩ ngwatanĩonĩ ya Communism na ndyaĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai e kw'o, Mbivilia nĩtumĩte nĩalyũka vyũ kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Maũndũ ala neemanyĩisye nĩmatumie nĩeka kwĩmakĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte na matuma nĩmanya kĩeleelo kya kwĩthĩwa nĩ thayũ. Mwakanĩ wa 1993, nĩnavatisiwe na natw'ĩka Ngũsĩ ya Yeova, na mwakanĩ wa 2000, nĩnatwaie Tabitha, mũndũ mũka wĩ kĩthito kingĩ maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Nĩtũtũmĩaa ĩvinda yingĩ kũtetheesya andũ mamanye Mbivilia. Andũ aingĩ tũkomanaa namo me ngwatanĩonĩ ya Communism na maiĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai o tondũ nailyĩ tene. Nĩnĩw'aa neanĩwa mũno ĩla namony'a ũndũ matonya kũmũmanya Yeova.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE
Ĩla nambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, asyai makwa nĩmakĩaa. Ĩndĩ kuma ĩvinda yĩu, nĩmonete ũndũ nĩtethekete nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo na Ngũsĩ. Ũndũ ũla ũndanĩthasya nĩ kana nĩmasomaa Mbivilia na makathi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
Nĩ na Tabitha nĩtũtanĩaa mũtwaano witũ nũndũ nĩtũtataa vyũ kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla ũnenganĩtwe Mbivilianĩ ĩũlũ wa andũ ala matwaanĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla wonanĩtye kana ala matwaanĩte maĩle kwĩthĩwa maĩkĩĩanĩte nĩkũlũlũmĩĩlasya mũtwaano witũ.—Aevelania 13:4.
Nĩnaekie kwĩthĩwa na wia na kwĩmakĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Nĩnĩtanĩaa kwĩthĩwa nĩ ũmwe wa ana-a-asa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe ala matanĩaa mũuo wa w'o na ngwatanĩo nzeo. Ithyonthe twĩthĩawa twĩanene na ũsu nĩ ũndũ nendeeaw'a nĩw'o kuma tene.

LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1974
WITH THE COUNTRY: GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC
OUR HISTORY: I REMEMBER OR GOD KNOWS
MY OWN STORY
I was born in the region of Saxony, a country which at that time was called German Democratic Republic (GDR). From childhood we were taught well and we understood, and years passed and I came to know about the leadership of the state. Many people in the region of Saxony went through things inside the German Democratic Republic during the era of the Communist party. And now I remember or God knows. These things happened when I was around 18 years old. Those things involved believing in God and opposing Communism.
Is this opposition to Communism good? The situation was such that many people did not understand. And I remembered that everything would be better if people could go wherever they wanted, because this would help people live happily. And because of this, I disliked the ideology of the Communist people. And at 14 years old, I used my history a lot to try to understand the world. The people of Aue were affected greatly by my attitude and had great respect for my knowledge. And also then, I learned some important things about politics in the German Democratic Republic. Sometimes I had ideas that were different and my history was always full of questions.
The end of childhood and youth, those times were difficult. In 1989, the Berlin Wall fell along with the Communist system in Eastern Europe. Many more things began to happen. At the end of my school days, I realized how bad life was in the German Democratic Republic. For example, people who disagreed with the Communist system suffered a lot. Will the hope for freedom ever come true, even though the Communist system still doesn't understand many people? Why is this system so hated by its own people? I was overwhelmed by many thoughts.
These things motivated me to see and learn about other good things in the world. While I was finishing secondary school with the intention of going to university, I became interested in traveling and getting a visa. And I also became interested in working with my uncle who had connections. This good thing helped me to get involved and send many letters. Studying, traveling, and getting involved in important matters made me feel better. And the visas I got sometimes took up to five days to process. Furthermore, will education help even in a fallen state? And what about the poor people?
But since I wanted to take advantage of the opportunities available, I prayed earnestly. One day at school, I met a group of students who were very interested in the fallen state. With a girl named Mandy * we studied together and preached about Jehovah. On that day, Mandy invited me to her home. She told me: "Andreas, if you want to take advantage of the opportunities available in today's world and the fallen state, study the Bible carefully."
I thought about the things I had heard, and I decided to study the Bible and perhaps take advantage of the opportunities. Mandy showed me Daniel chapter 2, and the things I read really impressed me. That day she explained the history of great nations (world powers) but they have all failed and disappeared. Mandy showed me another scripture from the Bible that explains our fallen state. She encouraged me to take advantage of the opportunities available! So I thought, can I write about this matter, and can someone understand the history of the fallen state and believe it? Will God allow it?
THE BIBLE EXPLAINED TO MY UNCLE
Mandy introduced me to a man named Horst and his wife Angelika, who are Jehovah's Witnesses, and I was happy to learn more about God's name. For this reason, I realized that Jehovah's Witnesses are the ones sent to preach God's name, Jehovah. (Psalm 83:18; Matthew 6:9) I understood that Jehovah God cares about those who want to live forever on earth. Psalm 37:9 says: "But the meek will inherit the earth." I was convinced that learning more was important so that I could align myself with God's laws as found in the Bible.
So, I seriously considered explaining it to my uncle and seeing if he would align himself with the Bible. Being a businessman and having influence, he could use his resources to help others understand and appreciate it. And also, there is no harm in talking about this important matter with my uncle. I trust that Jehovah will guide those who sincerely seek him, and he will help people understand what the Bible teaches!
And for about 18 years, I lived under Communist rule and came to realize that God exists, and the Bible helped me see things clearly during those difficult times. The things I learned helped me cope with life's challenges and made me desire to know the truth. In 1993, I began associating with Jehovah's Witnesses, and in 2000, I married Tabitha, a sister who has been very supportive. We spend much time helping people learn about the Bible. Many people we meet have lived under Communist rule and come to believe in God because of it. I am grateful for the opportunity to learn more about Jehovah.
MOTIVATIONS THAT MOVED ME
It is because of my association with Jehovah's Witnesses that I feel this way. During those times, I noticed something that impressed me regarding their association with Jehovah. What especially moved me was when I saw them reading the Bible and interacting with fellow Christians from Jehovah's Witnesses.
Tabitha and I strengthened our resolve to help others benefit from the comfort found in the Bible, like those who had benefited us. For example, helping others overcome difficulties and encouraging them spiritually strengthens our bond.—Proverbs 13:4.
I enjoy serving and comforting others and strengthening their faith. I want to continue serving as part of a large family of spiritual brothers and sisters who share our beliefs. Above all, we want to keep praising God and living according to his principles.

text:
Ngoki wa Makoki ũla ũwetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Esekieli nũũ?
Maasya ũu nũndũ ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo yĩeleetye kana Satani, ũla nĩwe Ndevili, nĩwe mũtongoi wa ala makavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai nthĩ yonthe. (Ũvu. 12:1-17) Kwoou tweesilasya kana Ngoki nĩ ĩsyĩtwa yĩngĩ Satani wĩtĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa wathani.
Ĩndĩ maelesyo asu mavuku maitũ maeleasya nĩmaumĩlilye makũlyo mana ma vata. Nĩkĩ? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Yeova eeie Ngoki atĩĩ aiweta ĩvinda yĩla ũ Ngoki ũkasindwa: "Ngakũnengane kwa nyũnyi mbai sya kĩla mũthemba, na kwa nyamũ sya kĩthekanĩ ũĩwe nĩsyo." (Esek. 39:4) Na ĩndĩ Yeova ongela kwasya: "Na kũkethĩwa mũthenya ũsu, nganenga Ngoki vandũ va kũthika andũ nthĩ ya Isilaeli . . . Na ku nĩkw'o makenzĩa Ngoki nthĩ na wingĩ w'onthe wa andũ make." (Esek. 39:11) Yu ĩkũlyo nĩ, Kyũmbe kya veva kĩtonya ata kũtw'ĩka lĩu kwa "nyũnyi mbai sya kĩla mũthemba, na kwa nyamũ sya kĩthekanĩ"? O na ĩngĩ, vatonyeka ata Satani akesa kũtwawa "vandũ va kũthika andũ" kũũ nthĩ? Lilikana Mbivilia yaĩtye nesa kana Satani akekw'a ĩimanĩ yĩte kĩtulu vandũ va myaka 1,000, ĩndĩ ti atĩ akaĩwa kana athikwe.—Ũvu. 20:1, 2.
Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ĩla myaka 1,000 yĩthela, Satani akathaw'a kuma yĩla ĩimanĩ yĩte kĩtulu, na kana "akauma akenge mbaĩ ila syĩ ikotonĩ inya sya nthĩ, Ngoki na Makoki, kũmomban'ya vamwe kaũnĩ." (Ũvu. 20:8) Ĩndĩ ethĩwa Satani nĩwe ũ Ngoki, atonya kũkenga Ngoki ata? Kwoou, "Ngoki" ũla ũwetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Esekieli na ya Ũvuan'yo ti Satani.
Kwoou-ĩ, we Ngoki wa Makoki nũũ? Nĩ kana tũkwate ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu, twaĩle kũsisya Maandĩko nesa nĩ kana tũmanye nũũ ũla ũkavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai. Mbivilia nĩwetete kana ve ĩvinda andũ ma Ngai makavithũkĩwa nĩ 'Ngoki wa Makoki,' mavithũkĩwe nĩ "mũsumbĩ wa ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ," na "asumbĩ ma nthĩ." (Esek. 38:2, 10-13; Nda. 11:40, 44, 45; Ũvu. 17:14; 19:19) Mo maandĩko asu meonany'a kana andũ ma Ngai makavithũkĩwa mavinda atatũ me kĩvathũkany'o? Ti lasima. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Mbivilia yĩkĩte kũtũmĩa masyĩtwa me kĩvathũkany'o ĩiweta ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda o yĩmwe yĩla andũ ma Ngai makavithũkĩwa. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nũndũ Maandĩko mawetete kana mbaĩ syonthe sya nthĩ ikooka vamwe ĩvinda yĩu nĩ kana ivithũkĩe andũ ma Ngai. Syamavithũkĩa nĩw'o kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni wĩambĩĩa.—Ũvu. 16:14, 16.
Kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maandĩko asu onthe mawetete kũvithũkĩwa kwa andũ ma Ngai nĩkũũtuma tũmanya kana Ngoki wa Makoki ti Satani, ĩndĩ nĩ mbaĩ ikethĩwa syĩ ngwatanĩo. Syo mbaĩ isu ikoka vamwe ikeethĩwa itongoew'e nĩ "mũsumbĩ wa ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ"? Tũyĩsa kwĩkinyĩa nthĩ tũkasya kana ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũsu nĩwosanĩte na ũndũ Yeova ũtavĩtye Ngoki. Amwĩĩte atĩĩ: 'Ũkauma vandũ vaku kuma itulunĩ sya ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ, we, na ngo mbingĩ sya andũ vamwe naku, onthe makuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi nguthu nene na ita syĩ ũtonyi.'—Esek. 38:6, 15.
O ta ũu, mwathani Ndanieli, ũla waĩ kw'o ĩvinda ya Esekieli, aĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa mũsumbĩ wa ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ: "Maũvoo ala makauma wumĩlonĩ wa syũa na ala makauma ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ nĩmakamũthĩn'ya; nake nũkauma athi na ũthilĩku mũnene kwananga na kũmaveta vyũ aingĩ. Na nũkamba maeema ma nyũmba yake nene mbanakavye katĩ wa ũkanga na kĩla kĩĩma kĩseo kĩtheu; ĩndĩ nũkavika mũminũkĩlyo wake, na vati ũmwe ũkamũtethya." (Nda. 11:44, 45) Maũndũ asu mawetetwe nĩmosanĩte vyũ na kĩla ĩvuku ya Esekieli yĩwetete ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala Ngoki ũkeka.—Esek. 38:8-12, 16.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩkaatĩĩa ĩtina wa andũ ma Ngai kũvithũkĩwa? Ndanieli aĩtye atĩĩ: "Na ĩvinda yĩu Mikaeli [Yesũ Klĩsto] nũkaũngama [ĩvinda ya Ali–Maketoni], ũla mũnene wĩ mbee mũno ũsumbĩnĩ ũla ũũngamaa [kuma 1914] kwondũ wa ana ma andũ maku; na nĩkũkethĩwa ĩvinda ya thĩna [ũla thĩna mũnene], o tondũ ũtaaĩthĩwa kuma kweethĩwa mbaĩ kũvika ĩvinda o yĩu: Na ĩvinda yĩu, andũ maku nĩmakatangĩĩwa, kĩla ũmwe ũkoneka aandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ." (Nda. 12:1) Ũndũ ũsu Yesũ ũkeka atũmĩtwe nĩ Ngai nũsyokete ũkaelew'a ĩandĩkonĩ ya Ũvuan'yo 19:11-21.
Ĩndĩ nũũ ũla wĩtĩtwe "Ngoki na Makoki" ĩandĩkonĩ ya Ũvuan'yo 20:8? Ĩvinda yĩla andũ makethĩwa maitatwa ya mũthya ĩtina wa ĩla myaka 1,000, ala makaleana na Yeova makeethĩwa na veva wa ũaani ta ũla wa ila mbaĩ ikethĩwa inavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai mũthyanĩ wa ũla thĩna mũnene, ila nĩsyo 'Ngoki wa Makoki.' Asu makavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai mũthyanĩ wa ũla thĩna mũnene vamwe na ala makaleana na Yeova ĩvinda ya yĩla ĩtatwa ya mũthya makakwatwa no ũndũ ũmwe, naw'o nĩ kĩkw'ũ kya tene na tene! (Ũvu. 19:20, 21; 20:9) Kwoou, nĩ ũndũ waĩle kwasya kana "Ngoki na Makoki" nĩ andũ ala makaleana na Yeova mũthyanĩ wa ĩla Myaka Ngili.
Nũndũ ithyĩ nĩtwĩmanyĩasya Ndeto ya Ngai nesa vyũ, nĩtweteele na mea mũno twone o mĩtũkĩ nũũ ũla ũkatw'ĩka "mũsumbĩ wa ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ." Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa nũũ ũkatongoesya mbaĩ isu ikosana ivithũkĩe andũ ma Ngai, ve maũndũ elĩ ithyĩ tũte na nzika namo: (1) Ngoki wa Makoki vamwe na ita syake makasindwa na mayanangwa; na (2) Mũsumbĩ witũ, Yesũ Klĩsto, ũla ũsumbĩkĩte yu, akatangĩĩa andũ ma Ngai, na aimalikya nthĩ nzaũ vala andũ makekala na mũuo na me asũvĩĩku.—Ũvu. 7:14-17.

translation:
Was Makoki's name mentioned in Ezekiel's vision?
This matter concerns the vision of Revelation, which speaks of Satan, who is the Devil, the originator of all evils and deceiver of God's people throughout time. (Rev. 12:1-17) It is said that Makoki is greatly feared by Satan because of his faith.
These scriptures show us how important it is to be loyal to Jehovah. Why? Because Jehovah foretold what would happen when Makoki was defeated: "I will lay my vengeance upon every high hill, and upon every fortified tower." (Ezek. 39:4) And Jehovah also stated: "And it must come about that on that day I will magnify Makoki among them among the people of Israel… and they will know that I am Jehovah their God." (Ezek. 39:11) So, does this mean that the symbolic "high hills and fortified towers" refer to those who oppose Jehovah? And furthermore, will Satan ever succeed in turning such ones into "people for cutting off"? The Bible shows that Satan was allowed to deceive nations for 1,000 years, but it does not say he succeeded in destroying them.—Rev. 20:1, 2.
The Bible indicates that after the 1,000 years, Satan will be released from his imprisonment, and he will again "mislead the nations," leading them astray, and gathering them together for battle against Jehovah and his people. (Rev. 20:8) But can Satan really challenge Jehovah? No, the "God" mentioned in the prophecies in Ezekiel and Revelation is not Satan.
But what about the "God of Forces"? Is it possible that we misunderstand the Scriptures and thus fail to identify who truly opposes God's people? The Bible shows that those whom God's enemies call "God of Forces" are described as being a "foe of sanctuaries," and "forces of the nations." (Ezek. 38:2, 10-13; Dan. 11:40, 44, 45; Rev. 17:14; 19:19) Do these scriptures show that God's people are attacked by three distinct forces? Not at all. They demonstrate that the Bible uses figurative language to describe the way God's enemies attack. So why bother understanding this? Because the Scriptures reveal that all the nations will gather together for war against God's people. This is what the apostle Paul meant when he said—Rev. 16:14, 16.
To understand the meaning of these scriptures, it is vital to know whether the "God of Forces" is Satan, and if so, how this fits in with what Jehovah has revealed about him. He describes himself saying: "I will also turn your face against Gog ["God of Forces"], and I will strike your mighty blows, and I will judge him." – Ezek. 38:6, 15.
But look at Daniel, whose vision parallels Ezekiel's, describing the same "God of Forces": "And tidings from the east and from the north shall alarm him, and he will go forth to put them to great anger, and he will do according to all that has been said, and he will act powerfully, with deceitful designs. And he will speak very lofty things against the Most High, and he will wear out the holy ones, and he will think to change times and laws; and they will be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time." (Dan. 11:44, 45) These events harmonize fully with each prophetic depiction in Ezekiel concerning what God allows.—Ezek. 38:8-12, 16.
What, then, motivates God's people to witness? Daniel says: "And Michael [Jesus Christ] himself will stand up, the great prince who stands guard over the sons of my people; and there will be a time of distress such as never was since there came to be a nation until that time. And at that time your people will be saved, everyone who is found written in the book." (Dan. 12:1) This shows Jesus commissioned by God to execute the prophecy described at Revelation 19:11-21.
But what about those referred to as "the Kings and Priests" at Revelation 20:8? These are individuals who survive the great tribulation and live through the 1,000 years, associating with Jehovah and serving as priests during the entire period of Thousand Year Reign, but they are not 'Kings and Priests.' Some associate with God's people during the entire period of Thousand Year Reign along with others associating with Jehovah during the entire period of the great tribulation, and they too will have eternal life! (Rev. 19:20, 21; 20:9) Truly, this is something to look forward to, whether or not "the Kings and Priests" are others associating with Jehovah during the entire Thousand Years.
However, if we want to demonstrate our appreciation for God's Kingdom fully, let us be zealous and diligent in proclaiming the good news while we can, so that we do not become "worthless for the day of vengeance." But how can we do so effectively in reaching God's people, especially when facing difficulties? We can do so by remembering two things: (1) The Kings and Priests, together with their families, were persecuted; and (2) Our Leader, Jesus Christ, who led the way, faced opposition from God's people, and ultimately he was put to death, yet he remained faithful and loyal.—Rev. 7:14-17.

text:
Mũndũũme wĩtawa Don na kĩveti kyake Margaret * nĩmatanĩie kũthokewa nĩ mwĩĩtu woo e na mũũme na syana syoo. Nĩ kenda maye lĩu wa mũthya me vamwe nĩ kana mataanĩsye, Margaret, ũla tene wathũkũmaa wĩa wa kũua na esa kũlitaya, nĩwauie macaroni na cheese, lĩu ũla esũkũũe make elĩ mendete.
Ĩla andũ onthe mekalile mesanĩ meteele lĩu, Margaret nĩwaetie lĩu ũla wauĩte. Ĩla wakunũie mbakũli, nĩwamakie ĩla wamanyie kana mbakũlinĩ ĩsu vaĩ o suvu wa cheese. Margaret nĩwoolĩtwe nĩ kwĩkĩa macaroni lĩunĩ ũsu!
O na twĩthĩwe twĩ na ũkũũ wĩana ata kana ũmanyi wĩana ata, ithyonthe nĩtũvĩtasya. No tũneene ũndũ tũtambĩte kũsũanĩa, tũkeka ũndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩla yĩtaĩle, kana o tũkavũthĩĩsya ũndũ mũna kana tũkolwa nĩ kũwĩka. Nĩkĩ andũ mavĩtasya? Twaĩle kwĩka ata ĩla twavĩtya? No twĩsiĩĩe tũikavĩtye? Kwĩthĩwa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa mavĩtyo nĩkũũtũtetheesya kũsũngĩa makũlyo asu.
WONI WA NGAI NA WONI WITŨ ĨŨLŨ WA MAVĨTYO
Nĩtũtanaa ĩla twakathwa nũndũ nĩtweeka ũndũ nesa, na tũyĩw'a twĩĩaĩle kũkathwa. O na ĩla twavĩtya, nĩ ũndũ waĩle tũketĩkĩla mavĩtyo maitũ, o na ethĩwa tũyĩĩna kĩeleelo kĩthũku kana andũ mainamanya mavĩtyo maitũ. Kwĩtĩkĩla mavĩtyo maitũ nĩ ũndũ wendaa wĩnyivyo.
Ethĩwa twĩsũanĩa mũno o ĩũlũ witũ ene, no tũolange ũito wa mavĩtyo maitũ, tũkambĩĩa kũilĩĩla andũ angĩ mavĩtyo maitũ, kana tũkasya tũivĩtĩtye. Kwĩka ũu no kũtume maũndũ mathũkĩĩa. Thĩna ũsu no ũeme kũthela, na andũ ala angĩ no matalĩlwe mavĩtyo mate moo. O na kau ũmũnthĩ no twĩke ĩvĩtyo na tũkaema kũkwata ũkany'o, nĩtwaĩle kũlilikana kana "kĩla ũmwe waitũ akaumya ũvoo wake mbee wa Ngai."—Alomi 14:12.
Ngai ethĩawa na woni ũla waĩle ĩũlũ wa mavĩtyo. Ĩvuku ya Savuli yonanĩtye kana Ngai "e tei na nĩ mũseo," na "ndakateta mavinda onthe; o na ndekalasya ũthatu wake tene na tene." Nĩwĩsĩ kana andũ masyaawa me na naĩ, na nĩ ũeleawa kana me mawonzu, o na "nũlilikanaa kana twĩ kĩtoo."—Savuli 103:8, 9, 14.
Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana Ngai nĩ Ĩthe witũ wĩ tei, na nĩwendaa twĩthĩawe na woni ta wake ĩũlũ wa mavĩtyo. (Savuli 130:3) Ndetonĩ yake, nũtũnengae motao na myolooto ya kũtũtetheesya tũmanye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ĩla twavĩtya na ĩla andũ angĩ mavĩtya.
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KWĨKA ĨLA TWAVĨTYA
Mũno mũno ĩla mũndũ wavĩtya, atũmĩaa ĩvinda na vinya mwingĩ ayilĩĩla andũ angĩ mavĩtyo kana aitata oneke ndavĩtĩtye. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwĩka ũu, ĩla waneena ndeto na syaũmĩsya mũndũ ũngĩ, nĩ ũndũ mũseo ũketya ũekeo, ũkelũnga, na mũyĩendeea kũlũlũmĩĩlya ũnyanya wenyu. Nĩwĩthĩwa wĩkĩte ũndũ ũtaĩle na ũkatuma maũndũ mathũka, kana ũndũ ũsu ũkatuma ũemanwa na mũndũ ũngĩ, kana we mwene wĩw'a woo? Vandũ va kwĩw'a woo kana kwilĩĩla andũ angĩ mavĩtyo maku, nũseo ũkatata ũndũ ũtonya ũlũnge maũndũ. Waendeea kũkwatĩĩa mawoni ma kana ndũvĩtĩtye, nũtonya kũendeea kwĩthĩwa ũte mwĩanĩe na thĩna ũyongeleka. Vandũ va kwĩka ũu, ĩmanyĩsye kumana na mavĩtyo maku, lũnga maũndũ, na ũyĩka kĩla kyaĩle.
Ĩndĩ ĩla mũndũ ũngĩ wavĩtya, nĩ laisi kwĩka maũndũ mekwonany'a kana tũinendeew'a nĩ kĩla weeka. Kwoou nĩ ũndũ mũseo mũno kũatĩĩa ũtao wa Yesũ Klĩsto ũla waĩtye atĩĩ: "Maũndũ onthe ĩndĩno o na meva ala mũkwenda andũ mamwĩke inyw'ĩ, nenyu mekei o ta ũu." (Mathayo 7:12) Ĩla wavĩtya, o na ethĩwa ĩvĩtyo yĩu nĩ ĩnini, vate nzika nĩwendaa andũ ala angĩ makwĩw'ĩe tei kana makũekee. Kwoou nĩ ũseo o naku ũkew'ĩa andũ ala angĩ tei na ũkamaekea ĩla mavĩtya.—Aeveso 4:32.
MYOLOOTO ĨTONYA KŨTŨTETHEESYA KŨOLANGA MAVĨTYO
Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩyĩelesya ĩũlũ wa mavĩtyo yaĩtye kana mũndũ avĩtasya nũndũ wa "kwĩthĩwa na woni ũtaĩle ĩũlũ wa ũndũ, kwĩthĩwa ate na ũmanyi wĩanĩtye, kana kũlea kwĩthukĩĩsya nesa." Nĩtwaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla kana mavinda kwa mavinda kĩla mũndũ nĩwĩkaa ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ asu mawetwa. Ĩndĩ kũsũanĩaa myolooto ĩmwe kuma Mbivilianĩ kũkatũtetheeasya kũolanga mavĩtyo.
Mwolooto ũmwe ũtonya kũtũtethya wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Nthimo 18:13, ũla waĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũla ũsũngĩaa atanamba kwĩw'a, kwake nĩ ũtumanu na nthoni." Kwosa ĩvinda wĩthukĩĩsye nesa nĩ kana wambe kũelewa maũndũ onthe, na ĩndĩ ũimanya ũndũ waĩle kũsũngĩa kũkaũtetheeasya ndũkaneene ndeto itaĩle kana ndũkeke ũndũ ũtambĩte kũsũanĩa. Ũmanyi ũla tũkwataa ĩla tweethukĩĩsya ũndũ nesa nĩ wa vata vyũ nũndũ nũtumaa tũtethĩwa na woni mũthũku ĩla andũ mavĩtya, na nũtumaa twĩvathana na mavĩtyo.
Mwolooto ũngĩ wa Mbivilia waĩtye atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa nũtonyeka, kwa ngalĩ ĩla yenyu, mwĩthĩwe na mũuo na andũ onthe." (Alomi 12:18) Tata ũndũ ũtonya wĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo na mũuo vamwe na andũ ala angĩ. Ĩla ũũthũkũma na andũ ala angĩ, mony'e kana nũmathĩnĩkĩaa na nũmanengae ndaĩa, makathae na ũimekĩaa vinya. Weeka ũu, ĩkeethĩawa yĩ laisi kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene ĩla mwavĩtanĩsya kwĩsĩla o ndeto kana meko, o na mũkeethĩawa mũtonya kũlũnga maũndũ ala momũ kwa nzĩa ya mũuo.
Tataa mũno wĩmanyĩsye maũndũ matonya ũkũtethya kumana na mavĩtyo maku. Vandũ va kwĩtetea nũndũ wa mavĩtyo maku, waĩle kũtũmĩa mwanya ũsu kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa nzeango. No wĩkũlye-ĩ, No ĩthĩwa mavĩtyo makwa mayonany'a kana nĩnaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa ya wũmĩĩsyo, ũseo, kana wĩting'o? No ĩthĩwa naĩle kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa ingĩ ta ũuu, mũuo, na wendo? (Akalatia 5:22, 23) O na ethĩwa ĩvĩtyo yaku yĩilyĩ ata, no ũmanye maũndũ ala waĩle kwĩvathana namo nĩ kana ndũkasyokeleele ĩvĩtyo yĩu. Ndũkatindĩe ũisũanĩa mũno ũndũ ũkwĩw'a nũndũ wa ĩvĩtyo yaku, ĩndĩ o vamwe na ũu, ndũkavũthĩĩsye ĩvĩtyo yaku. Mavinda angĩ kũmantha twĩndũ twa mathekany'a kuma mavĩtyonĩ maku no kũũtetheesye ndũkemakĩe mũno.
KWĨTHĨWA NA WONI WAĨLE NO KŨTŨTETHEESYE
Kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩle ĩũlũ wa mavĩtyo kũkatũtetheeasya twĩke maũndũ kwa nzĩa yaĩle ĩla twavĩtya kana andũ angĩ mavĩtya. Tũkeethĩawa na mũuo wa kĩlĩko na tũkekalaa na mũuo na andũ angĩ. Tweekĩa kĩthito kya kwĩmanyĩasya kumana na mavĩtyo maitũ, tũkeethĩawa twĩ oĩ na andũ ala angĩ makatwenda. Tũikatũlĩka ngoo na tũikew'aa ta tũtaĩle. Kũelewa kana andũ ala angĩ nĩmavĩtasya na nĩmathĩnĩkaa nũndũ wa mavĩtyo moo kũkatuma tũendeea kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo namo. Na ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana, no tũtetheke tweemanyĩsya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Ngai ya wendo na kũekea andũ mavĩtyo moo.—Akolosai 3:13.
Yo ĩvĩtyo ya Margaret yĩla yĩwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ nĩyatumie mũsyĩ wake ũtethĩwa na ũtanu? Aiee. Vandũ va kũthatw'a nĩ ũndũ ũsu, onthe moonie ũndũ ũsu wĩ wa kũsengy'a, na mũno mũno Margaret, na onthe matanĩa kũya lĩu ũsu o na kau ũyaĩ na macaroni! Ĩtina wa ĩvinda yĩasa, ala esũkũũe elĩ ma Margaret nĩmatavisye syana syoo ĩũlũ wa lĩu ũla wamauĩe ũtesa kũla na maitavya maũndũ maseo makonetye ũmae na ũsũe woo. Ũndũ ũla Margaret weekie waĩ o ĩvĩtyo tũ!
^ kal. 2 Masyĩtwa nĩ mavĩndũe.

My beloved husband Don and his wife Margaret * made me realize how to be with someone who has children and their families. I really wish just one day we could be together, Margaret, so you can see how people die and go away, I'll make macaroni and cheese, a meal that makes everything better.
But some people who have been hurt feel this way, Margaret wants a meal that will satisfy her. But buy groceries, let's make them, maybe those groceries or some cheese will suffice. Margaret would love to eat macaroni again!
And we argue and fight over small things, even if we don't understand them, still we persevere. We shouldn't dwell on trying to understand, let's leave what happened in the past, or we might regret something or be punished for being stubborn. Are people persevering? Let's just forget about what we did? Or should we remember and forget? Arguing with someone about the pain of perseverance is exhausting.
GOD'S WILL AND THE PAIN OF PERSEVERANCE
We continue even when we are overwhelmed with problems, and we try to continue. And when we persevere, it's a way to honor our perseverance, or sometimes we find comfort or others appreciate our perseverance. Honoring our perseverance is a good thing.
Sometimes we need help or our lives are difficult, and we protect the value of our perseverance, telling others about our perseverance, or we can share our experiences. Forgetting this and causing trouble. This and believing in healing, and others also experience great perseverance. And sometimes someone needs to forgive and accept responsibility, we are able to compare or "each of us cares for his own life, but God cares."—Proverbs 14:12.
God understands and knows the pain of perseverance. Saul's prayer showed that God "is compassionate," and "forgives all sins; and heals all diseases." It is wonderful that he is patient with us, and understands our weaknesses, and "does not treat us as our sins deserve."—Psalm 103:8, 9, 14.
This is because God is our Father who is compassionate, and it is good that we trust in his compassion. (Psalm 130:3) Therefore, let us confess our mistakes and seek forgiveness so that we know what we should do when we persevere and what others persevere.
WHAT WE SHOULD DO WHEN WE PERSEVERE
Often when someone perseveres, they use energy and effort to help others with their perseverance or may seem to have overcome it. For those people, when someone tells them a story and encourages that person, it is a compassionate act that is appreciated, respected, and helps them feel better. It is important to understand what is right and cause things to go well, or whether this will cause resentment towards that person, or you yourself will be upset? People who are upset can tell others about their perseverance, which is compassionate and causes things to improve. Continue to listen to advice from those who have persevered, and strive to be more humble and understanding. Those who forget this, learn from great perseverance, respect things, and remember everything.
For when someone perseveres, it is easy to overlook matters or we continue to think about it every week. This is a compassionate thing to do to follow the example of Jesus Christ who said: "All things whatever you want men to do to you, you also do to them." (Matthew 7:12) But when you persevere, and your own compassion is great, visit prisoners and show compassion to others who are not helped or honored. This is why you should be kind to others and make them feel valued and persevere.—Ephesians 4:32.
FORGIVENESS HELPS US TO OVERCOME PERSEVERANCE
Sometimes it is difficult to overcome perseverance when someone feels a sense of "being wronged, being treated unfairly, or feeling insulted." It is important to realize that everyone has different perspectives on things. For example, to understand forgiveness, we can look at an example from the Bible to help us overcome perseverance.
One example that helps us understand this is found in Proverbs 18:13, which says: "He who answers before he hears, shows himself foolish and contentious." Often, insults come because someone does not fully understand things, and if you know something, it is better to try to explain it clearly than to get angry. The knowledge we gain that makes us feel insulted is often due to misunderstandings that cause us to speak harshly to others, and causes us to struggle with perseverance.
Another biblical example states: "If possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all men." (Romans 12:18) Try to live peacefully with those around you and with others. But if you have problems with others, remember to forgive and forget, and avoid holding grudges. This week, let us strive to reconcile with each other, whether through words or deeds, and let us strive to resolve issues peacefully.
Therefore, carefully consider the things that make you angry. Many people react to difficult situations, using their time to focus on anger and resentment. But ask yourself, will dwelling on such negative feelings or bitterness lead to forgiveness, peace, or happiness? (Galatians 5:22, 23) And even if another person has wronged you, can you find ways to move past it and overcome your hurt? Let us examine ourselves and see how we can deal with our own hurts, and then help others overcome theirs. Other times, we might be tempted to retaliate against those who have wronged us, but should we do that?
LIVING PEACEABLY AND UNDERSTANDING EACH OTHER
Living peacefully involves understanding why others act the way they do, whether it's because of their upbringing or the influence of others. We need empathy and patience when dealing with others. While we strive to maintain peace with others, we also recognize that there are times when others may not show us the same consideration. We shouldn't become discouraged or give up easily. Understanding why others behave the way they do can help us respond with compassion rather than anger. And remember, showing this kind of tolerance demonstrates our gratitude for God's undeserved kindness and encourages others to live more peacefully.—Colossians 3:13.
So, did Margaret's cooking really make her husband happy? Yes. People often say that food is the way to a man's heart, and certainly Margaret knew how to cook—she could whip up a casserole and macaroni in no time! The smell of baking was wonderful, but evenings were especially nice when Margaret would prepare a large meal that everyone enjoyed, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. What Margaret cooked was truly delicious!
