text:
Nĩwĩthĩwa waaĩkwa kĩko kya ũng'endu kana mũndũ wa mũsyĩ wenyu akethĩwa eekiwe ũndũ ta ũsu? Nĩwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wia ũyona ta wĩsa kũkwatwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu? Ũng'endu nĩ "thĩna mũnene ũnyaĩĩkĩte nthĩ yonthe." Sũanĩa ngelekany'o ii.
ŨNG'ENDU NTHĨNĨ WA MŨSYĨ NA ANDŨ KŨKWATWA KYA VINYA: Livoti ĩmwe ĩla yaumiw'e nĩ Ngwatanĩo ya Nthĩ yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ mũka ũmwe katĩ wa kĩla aka atatũ nũvũawa kana akakwatwa kya vinya nĩ mũndũ me ndũũ." O na ũndũ ũngĩ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, "nĩvatonyeka mũndũ mũka ũmwe katĩ wa kĩla aka atano akakwatwa kya vinya kana akavĩtĩa syatemana."
ŨNG'ENDILĨ: Livoti kuma nthĩ ya Amelika yĩonany'a kana ve ikundi mbee wa 30,000 sya ing'endilĩ ila ithĩnasya andũ nthĩ ĩsu. Nasyo nthĩ sya Latin America, vakuvĩ mũndũ 1 katĩ wa kĩla andũ 3 nĩwakomanie na ing'endilĩ.
ŨAANI: Livoti ieleasya kana nĩvatonyeka andũ vakuvĩ nusu milioni makethĩwa mooaiwe mwaka wĩ o navu ĩtina, andũ asu mooaiwe mwaka ũsu maĩ aingĩ kwĩ ala mooaĩwe kaũnĩ. Nthĩ ila syĩ Southern Africa na Central America nĩsyo syaĩ na ũaani ũla mwingĩ vyũ nũndũ andũ ala mooaĩtwe ku maĩ mbee wa kũndũ kũna kwa ala mooaĩtwe nthĩ yonthe. Kwa ĩvinda ya mwaka ũmwe, andũ mbee wa 100,000 nĩmooaiwe nthĩ ila syĩ Latin America na angĩ ta 50,000 mooawa Brazil. Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Nĩvatonyeka ũng'endu ũkesa kũthela vyũ?
W'O ŨNG'ENDU NO WĨSE KŨTHELA VYŨ?
Nĩkĩ ũng'endu usĩe kĩla vandũ? Ve maũndũ maingĩ matumĩte kwĩthĩwa na ũng'endu ta andũ kũete ithokoo nũndũ wa kwona andũ angĩ mayonw'a kyende, syana nini kwona andũ aima mayĩka syĩko sya ũng'endu, kũtũmĩa ũkĩ na ndawa sya kũmila naĩ, andũ kwona thayũ ũte wa vata, na ing'endilĩ kwĩthĩwa itoseawa ĩtambya.
Vate nzika, kwĩ nthĩ imwe itatĩte kũolanga ũng'endilĩ. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩkũmi mĩthelu, taoni ĩmwe yĩ nthĩ ya Brazil ĩla yĩthĩawa na andũ aingĩ yĩtawa São Paulo, nĩyĩthĩĩtwe na ũoleku mũnene wa ũaani kwa kĩlungu kya 80 ĩũlũ wa 100. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, syĩko mbingĩ sya ũng'endilĩ nĩsyĩkawa taoninĩ ĩsu, na ũaani no ũendeee nũndũ andũ vakuvĩ 10 katĩ wa kĩla andũ 100,000 nĩmoaawa. Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Nĩ kyaũ kĩkesa kũmina ũng'endu vyũ?
Nĩ kana ũng'endu ũthele vyũ no nginya andũ maalyũke na mayĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Nĩ kana andũ ang'endu methĩwe mate na ĩtomo, mĩyono, na kwĩyenda, no nginya memanyĩsye kwĩthĩwa na wendo, kũnenga angĩ ndaĩa, na kũthĩnĩkĩaa andũ ala angĩ.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya mũndũ kwĩka moalyũku asu manenevete ũu? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye:
"Nũndũ kũmwenda Ngai nĩ kũũ, tũkwatae mĩao yake: na mĩao yake ti mĩito."—1 Yoana 5:3.
"Kũmũkĩa Yeova nĩkw'o kũmena ũthũku." *—Nthimo 8:13.
Kũmwenda Ngai na kũmũkĩa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtetheesya andũ ala methĩawa me ang'endu makaalyũka vyũ makatw'ĩka andũ eũ. Kwa w'o ũndũ ũsu no ũtonyeke?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Alex, * kuma Brazil, ũla watwĩe e mwove kwa myaka 19 nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa e kĩng'endilĩ. Atw'ĩkie Ngũsĩ ya Yeova mwaka wa 2000, ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ. Nĩwaekanie na ũng'endu vyũ? Ĩĩ, na Alex nĩwĩlilaa mũno nũndũ wa maũndũ mathũku ala weekaa. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Yu nĩnĩmwendete Ngai nũndũ nĩnĩw'aa andekeie vyũ. Kũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea na kũmwenda nĩmo maũndũ ala mandetheesye mũno kũalyũka."
Nake César kuma Brazil, aĩ kĩng'ei kĩthũku na ooyaa atũmĩĩte mĩio mĩthũku mũno. Ũsu nĩw'o wĩa ũla watethasya kwa myaka ta 15. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie aalyũka? E kolokolonĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyamũthokeie na eemanyĩsya Mbivilia. César aĩtye atĩĩ: "Yĩu nĩyo ĩvinda ya mbee namanyie kana no nĩthĩwe na ũtanu thayũnĩ wakwa. Nĩneemanyĩisye kũmwenda Ngai. O na nĩneemanyĩisye kũmũkĩa Ngai kana kũmena ũla ũthũku nĩ kana ndikamũthatye Yeova. Ndyendaa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũkwonany'a kana ndikũmũtũngĩa Ngai mũvea nũndũ wa ũseo wake. Kũmwenda Ngai na kũmũkĩa nĩkwandetheeisye nĩalyũle mwĩkalĩle wakwa."
Ngelekany'o isu syĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Syĩtũmanyĩsya kana Mbivilia yĩ na ũtonyi wa kũalyũla andũ vyũ kwa kũalyũla o na mosũanĩo moo. (Aeveso 4:23) Alex, ũla ũwetiwe kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ ongeleele kwasya atĩĩ: "Maũndũ ala neemanyĩasya Mbivilianĩ maĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kwĩtĩkĩw'a kĩw'ũ kĩtheu, o kavola kwa kavola kĩendeee na kũthambya mosũanĩo mathũku ala naĩ namo. Noonaa ndesa kũekana na maũndũ asu mathũku neekaa." Ĩla twausũsya akili sitũ ũvoo mũtheu ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, no tũvetange vyũ mosũanĩo mathũku. Ndeto ya Ngai yĩ ũtonyi wa kũthesya mũndũ. (Aeveso 5:26) Ĩla mũndũ mũng'endu na wĩyendete wasoma Ndeto ya Ngai, nĩmũalyũlaa akethĩwa endete mũuo na e mũndũ mũseo. (Alomi 12:18) Nĩwĩthĩawa na mũuo nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa mĩao ya Ngai.—Isaia 48:18.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mbee wa milioni nyanya ila syĩthĩawa nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ 240 nĩsyĩsĩ kĩla kĩtonya kũvetanga ũng'endu vyũ. Andũ kuma mbaĩ syonthe na ngo sya kĩla mũthemba nĩmemanyĩĩtye kũmwenda na kũmũkĩa Ngai vamwe na kwendana mo ene, na kwĩkala me na mũuo. (1 Vetelo 4:8) Mo nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo yonanasya kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka kũkethĩwa na nthĩ ĩte na andũ ang'endu.
NTHĨ ĨTE NA ANDŨ ANG'ENDU YĨ VAKUVĨ!
Mbivilia nĩyathanĩte kana o mĩtũkĩ Ngai akavetanga andũ ala ang'endu. Nthĩ ĩno yusĩe ũng'endu yeteele "mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo na kwanangwa kwa andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai." (2 Vetelo 3:5-7) Andũ ala ang'endu maikethĩwa matonya kũthĩny'a ala angĩ. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai akilyĩ analikĩlĩĩla maũndũ na aivetanga vyũ andũ onthe ala ang'endu?
Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai nũmenete "ũla wendete ũng'endu." (Savuli 11:5) Mũmbi witũ nĩwendete mũuo na ũsili wa katĩ. (Savuli 33:5; 37:28) Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Ngai ũtaketĩkĩla andũ ala ang'endu methĩwe vo tene na tene.
Nthĩ nzaũ yusĩe mũuo yĩ vakuvĩ. (Savuli 37:11; 72:14) Twĩũkũlya wĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩla waĩle kwĩka nĩ kana wĩĩkala nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩsu nzaũ ĩtakethĩwa na andũ ang'endu!

Are you troubled because of a journey or someone from your family has been injured on the way somewhere? Are you worried about being troubled by something like that? A journey is "a great danger that affects everyone." Consider this carefully.
JOURNEY AND INJURY TO PEOPLE DUE TO ACCIDENTS: One study showed that according to the National Safety Council: "One in three people will be involved in an accident during their lifetime." And another statistic is that, "one in five people will be involved in an accident or suffer serious injury."
ACCIDENTS: Studies in the United States show that around 30,000 people die each year due to accidents. And in Latin America, one in three people have experienced an accident.
DEATHS: Statistics show that approximately half a million people are injured annually, and more than one million people die each year globally. Areas such as Southern Africa and Central America have the highest death rates, with over one million deaths per year compared to the global average of one million deaths. For the past year, over 100,000 people have died in Latin America, and about 50,000 in Brazil alone. Therefore, does this accident rate seem high?
WHY ARE JOURNEYS DANGEROUS AND HOW CAN THEY BE MADE SAFER?
Is a journey dangerous for everyone? There are many factors that contribute to journeys endangering people, such as seeing other people driving recklessly, ignoring traffic laws and signs, people driving while tired, and accidents caused by speeding.
Fortunately, there are ways to reduce the risk of accidents. Over the last ten years, one city in Brazil, São Paulo, has significantly reduced its accident rate by implementing an 80 to 100 percent increase in road safety measures. However, despite these efforts, the accident rate remains high, with around 10 out of every 100,000 people dying. Therefore, what can be done to further minimize accidents?
It could be that making journeys safer requires people to be more careful and responsible. It could also be that if people were more considerate, patient, and courteous, they would be less likely to cause accidents, avoid conflicts, and harm others.
What can someone do to remain safe during a difficult journey? Consider what the Bible says:
"The love of God consists in this, that we observe his commandments; and his commandments are not burdensome."—1 John 5:3.
"To fear Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom."—Proverbs 8:13.
Loving God and fearing him can help individuals make better decisions and become more cautious travelers. How does this work?
Consider the experience of Alex, from Brazil, who worked as a driver for 19 years before becoming involved in full-time ministry. He learned about Jehovah's Witnesses in 2000, which led to his interest in studying the Bible and the organization. Was he surprised by what he learned? Yes, and Alex now appreciates the value of good conduct. He said: "I began to love God because I realized how much he cares for us. Honoring Jehovah and loving him have helped me to become a more careful driver."
César, also from Brazil, had a difficult childhood and faced many challenges. This is why he was troubled for about 15 years. What helped him to change? In prison, Jehovah's Witnesses showed him kindness and helped him study the Bible. César says: "That is when I found something meaningful in life, even though I was surrounded by bad people. I learned to love God. And I learned to fear God, or to respect what is right and avoid doing wrong, so that I could please Jehovah. I want to continue serving and showing gratitude for everything God has done for me. Loving God and fearing him has made me a better person."
How can we show kindness? We can show kindness by helping others understand what the Bible teaches about forgiveness and compassion. (Ephesians 4:23) Alex, a young man who used to get angry easily, explains: "I started studying the Bible regularly and little by little, I began to control my anger and stop getting upset over small things. Now I try to deal calmly with problems that come up." But we need to work hard to apply what we learn from the Bible and practice compassion. God's law is meant to help people. (Ephesians 5:26) So, if someone makes an effort to live by God's law, he will benefit himself and those around him. (Romans 12:18) He will have peace of mind knowing that he is doing what pleases God.—Isaiah 48:18.
Jehovah's Witnesses visit millions of homes, and in over 240 languages, they offer to help people learn about God. People everywhere appreciate having someone to talk to and someone who cares about them and their spiritual well-being, and who encourages them to stay morally clean. (1 Peter 4:8) But how can we be sure that our desire to share the good news is motivated by genuine concern for others?
SHOW GENUINE CONCERN FOR OTHERS!
The Bible shows that God wants people to know Him and to love Him. This is why He allows us to tell others about "the hope of everlasting life" and to help them find comfort in His Word. (2 Peter 3:5-7) Other people may face difficulties. Does this mean that God does not care about them or that He does not want to help them?
The Bible assures us that God is "patient toward all of you." (Psalm 11:5) Our Creator is loving and merciful. (Psalm 33:5; 37:28) That is why God does not give up on imperfect humans.
He gives them time to make changes. (Psalm 37:11; 72:14) Let us always remember that we can learn much from each person we meet, and let us continue to show genuine concern for those around us!

text:
Kũmantha mũthĩnzĩo ũtonya kwendeesya mũndũ ũngĩ ti ũndũ wĩ laisi. Vate nzika, ũla ũkũnengwa mũthĩnzĩo nĩwe ũtonya kũtuma mũthĩnzĩo woneka wĩ wa vata. Na mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũndũ ũmwe ũtonya kwona wĩ mũseo vyũ kwake, no wĩthĩwe ũte mũseo kwa mũndũ ũngĩ.
Kwa ngelekany'o, ũkanenga mũndũ wa mũika syĩndũ sya mĩtũkĩnĩ sya tekinolongyia ta simũ kana o kĩndũ kĩngĩ, no one ũsu wĩ mũthĩnzĩo mũseo vyũ. Nake mũndũ mũima no endeew'e mũno nĩ kũkwata mũthĩnzĩo ũtonya kũmũkiita ngoo ta kũnengwa kĩndũ kya vata kiĩtwe nĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ kwa myaka mingĩ. Nasyo isionĩ ingĩ, andũ ma mũika vamwe na ala akũũ no mendeew'e nĩ kũnengwa mbesa ta mũthĩnzĩo nũndũ no maitũmĩe kũũa kĩla mekwenda.
O na kau ti ũndũ wĩ laisi, andũ aingĩ nĩmamanthaa na kĩthito mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũseo vyũ kwondũ wa mũndũ mendete. Nũndũ ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kũmantha mũthĩnzĩo ta ũsu, kũsũanĩa maũndũ amwe no kũũtetheesye ũkakwata mũthĩnzĩo ũla waĩlĩte. Ekai tũneenee maũndũ ana matonya ũkũtetheesya ũkamanya mũthĩnzĩo ũla ũtonya kũnenga mũndũ ũkamũtanĩthya.
Wendi wa ũla ũkũnengwa mũthĩnzĩo. Mũndũũme ũmwe kuma Belfast, Northern Ireland, aisye kana kĩsululu kya mathaũ kĩla wanengiwe e na myaka 10 kana 11 nĩkyo kyaĩ mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũseo vyũ. Nĩkĩ waisye ũu? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Neew'aa ndyenda kwĩthĩwa nakyo." Ndeto isu syĩonany'a kana wendi wa mũndũ no ũtume endeew'a nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kana akaema kwendeew'a. Kwoou, sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mũndũ ũla ũkwenda kũnenga mũthĩnzĩo. Tata vyũ ũmanye maũndũ ala matonya kwendeesya mũndũ, nũndũ mũndũ endeeaw'a nĩ kĩndũ kĩla wonaa kĩ kĩseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mavinda maingĩ andũ ala akũũ mew'aa wĩ ũndũ wa vata vyũ kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yoo vamwe na andũ ma mũsyĩ. Nĩmendaa kwona syana syoo na esũkũũe mavinda maingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka. O na nĩmatanaa mũno ĩla andũ ma mũsyĩ mavanga kũthi kũtembea vamwe namo. Kwĩka ũu no kũmendeesye kwĩ kũmanenga mũthĩnzĩo o na wĩva.
Kwĩthukĩĩsya nesa nĩkw'o kũtonya ũkũtetheesya ũmanye wendi wa mũndũ. Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya twĩthĩwe twĩ 'ewi ma mĩtũkĩ, na kũlea kũneena mĩtũkĩ.' (Yakovo 1:19) Ĩla mũkũea ngewa na anyanyau kana andũ ma mũsyĩ, ĩthukĩĩsye nesa nĩ kana ũmanye maũndũ matonya ũkũtetheesya kũmanya kĩla mendete na kĩla matendete. Weeka ũu ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũnenga mũndũ mũthĩnzĩo ũtonya kũmũtanĩthya.
Mavata ma ũla ũkũnengwa mũthĩnzĩo. Mũndũ ũla ũkũnengwa mũthĩnzĩo no one wĩ wa vata mũno ethĩwa nĩweanĩsya mavata make, o na kau no wĩthĩwe wĩ mũnini kana ũte wa mbesa mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ ũtonya kũmanya ata mavata ma mũndũ ũngĩ?
Nzĩa ĩla ĩtonya kwoneka yĩ laisi nĩ kũkũlya mũndũ kĩla wĩ na vata nakyo. Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ ala manenganae mũthĩnzĩo no maeme kũtanĩa kũnenga mũndũ mũthĩnzĩo matũmĩa nzĩa ĩsu nũndũ monaa ũndũ ũla mũseo nĩ kũetee mũndũ mũthĩnzĩo ũteetaĩĩe na ũtonya kwĩanĩsya vata wake. Na o na kau andũ amwe no maelesye maũndũ ala mendete na ala matendete, mavinda amwe no maeme kũweta mavata moo.
Kwoou ĩthĩwa wĩ metho nĩ kana ũmanye mavata ma mũndũ ũsu. No wĩkũlye-ĩ, Nĩ mũndũ wa mũika, nĩ mũkũũ, nũtwaanĩte kana ndatwaanĩte, nĩwathaisye mũtwaano, nĩwakw'ĩĩwe nĩ ũla matwaanĩte, nũthũkũmaa, kana nĩwoosie litaya? Wamanya maũndũ asu, sũanĩa nĩ mĩthĩnzĩo yĩva ĩtonya kwĩanĩsya mavata make.
Nĩ kana ũmanye nesa mavata ma ũla ũkwenda kũnenga mũthĩnzĩo, neena na andũ angĩ maĩ na mavata ta asu. Andũ asu no methĩwe matonya kũũtavya mavata ma mwanya matesĩkĩe mũno nĩ andũ angĩ. Wamanya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa vata ũla mũndũ wĩ naw'o, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũmũnenga mũthĩnzĩo ũkwĩanĩsya vata wake ũtesĩkĩe nĩ andũ angĩ.
Ĩvinda yĩla ũũnengane mũthĩnzĩo. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndeto ĩvindanĩ yayo, kote nzeo!" (Nthimo 15:23) Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩonany'a kana nĩtwaĩle kũmanya ĩvinda yĩla yaĩle ya kũneena ũndũ mũna nĩ kana ndeto sitũ syĩthĩwe na mosyao maseo. Ũu now'o vaĩle kwĩthĩwa vailyĩ mekonĩ maitũ. O ũndũ ndeto ila syaneenwa ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩle itonya kũtanĩthya mũndũ, now'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla wanenganwe ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩle ũtonya kũtanĩthya ũla wanengwa.
Kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa mekwonany'a mavinda amwe ma mwanya ũtonya kũnenga mũndũ mũthĩnzĩo. Noĩthwa wĩsĩ kana mũnyanyau e na alũsi, wĩsĩ mũndũ wa mũika ũkilyĩ kũmina sukulu, kana ve andũ matwaanĩte me vakuvĩ kũkwata mwana. Andũ amwe monaa wĩ ũndũ mũseo kũandĩka ĩvinda yĩla anyanyae kana andũ moo ma mũsyĩ makethĩwa na ũndũ mũna wa mwanya, o na ethĩwa ũndũ ũsu ũkekĩka mwaka ũkĩte. Meeka ũu, methĩawa matonya kwĩyũmbany'a tene menengane mũthĩnzĩo ũla waĩle ĩvinda yĩla yaĩle. *
Ti lasima ũkanenganae mĩthĩnzĩo mavindanĩ o ala kwĩ maũndũ ma mwanya. No ũtanĩe kũnengane mĩthĩnzĩo kĩla ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ, nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa twĩ oĩ ĩla tũũnengane mĩthĩnzĩo nĩ kana tũikese kũeleeka naĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa mũndũũme nĩwanenga mũndũ mũka mũthĩnzĩo na ndanaelesya nesa kĩtumi kya kwĩka ũu, mũndũ mũka ũsu no asũanĩe kana mũndũũme ũsu emũnengae mũthĩnzĩo e na kĩeleelo kya kũtuma ndũũ nake. Ethĩwa kĩu tikyo kĩĩ kĩeleelo, mũthĩnzĩo ta ũsu no ũtume mũndũ aeleeka naĩ kana ũkaumĩlya mathĩna. Ũndũ ũsu wĩtuma twenda kũsũanĩa ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata, naw'o nĩ kĩeleelo kya ũla ũkũnengane mũthĩnzĩo.
Kĩeleelo kya ũla ũkũnengane mũthĩnzĩo. O tondũ twoona ngelekany'onĩ ĩsu yawetwa, nũseo tũkamanya ethĩwa ũla tũũnenga mũthĩnzĩo nũkũelewa naĩ kĩeleelo kitũ. Nake ũla ũkũnengane mũthĩnzĩo nĩwaĩle kwĩyĩosya nesa amanye kĩeleelo kyake kya kwĩka ũu. O na kau andũ aingĩ no masũanĩe kana methĩawa na kĩeleelo kĩseo mainengane mũthĩnzĩo, aingĩ mekaa ũu mavinda amwe ma mwaka nũndũ nĩ lasima manenge andũ mũthĩnzĩo. Namo angĩ manenganae mĩthĩnzĩo nĩ kana mendeesye andũ kana makwate kĩndũ kĩngĩ.
Ũtonya kwĩka ata ũkaĩkĩĩthya kana wanengane mũthĩnzĩo wĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Maũndũ onthe ala mwĩkaa mekaei na wendano." (1 Akolintho 16:14) Ethĩwa wanenga mũndũ mũthĩnzĩo nũndũ nũmwendete na nũmũthĩnĩkĩaa, mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nũtonya kũmũtanĩthya, naku ũyĩthĩwa na ũtanu nũndũ wa ũlau waku. Ĩla wanengane kuma ngoonĩ, nũtanĩthasya Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ. Ĩla Aklĩsto ma Kolintho meeyumisye na ngoo ya kwenda matetheesye Aklĩsto ma Yutia ala maĩ na mathĩna, mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwamakathie nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu. Ameie atĩĩ: "Ngai endete mũndũ ũnenganae na ũtanu."—2 Akolintho 9:7.
Kũsũanĩa maũndũ asu twaneenea no kũũtetheesye mũno ũkanengae andũ mĩthĩnzĩo ĩtonya kũmatanĩthya. Maũndũ asu na angĩ maingĩ nĩmatumĩte mũvango wa Ngai wa kũnenga andũ mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ wĩanĩa. Twĩũthokya ũsome kĩlungu kĩla kĩatĩĩe nĩ kana ũmanye mũthĩnzĩo ũsu mũnene kuma kwa Ngai nĩ wĩva.
^ kal. 13 Andũ aingĩ nĩmanenganae mĩthĩnzĩo ĩvinda ya kũlilikana mũthenya wa kũsyawa na ĩla kwĩ sikũkũ ingĩ. Ĩndĩ, mavinda maingĩ maũndũ ala mekawa sikũkũnĩ isu mayosanĩte na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya. Sisya kĩlungu kĩla kĩ ĩkaseti yĩĩ kĩ na kyongo "Asomi Maitũ Mekũlya Atĩĩ—Mo Aklĩsto Nĩmaĩle Kũtanĩa Kĩlisimasi?"

translation:
To understand a small thing about a person is not a simple matter. Sometimes, the ability to interpret something is what makes the thing appear good or bad. And the thing that one person can see well in their life, is different from how another person sees it.
For example, when you meet someone who uses various technological tools such as a phone or something else, you may find that they have a unique perspective. Because people often want to capture things that can remind them of events experienced by others over many years. And increasingly, people around the world are learning to interpret messages so that they can understand everything that happens.
But this is not a simple matter, many people struggle with interpreting their own perspectives on things. It's not a simple matter to understand things because of differences and to be able to grasp the meaning of what you have learned. Let us continue discussing things that can help you understand the thing that can make a person confused and frustrate them.
Regarding the interpretation of something. Someone in Belfast, Northern Ireland, said that he remembered being very happy when he was 10 or 11 years old because of his unique perspective. Why did he say that? He said: "I wish I could go back to that time." Therefore, it depends on a person's time and whether it makes them happy or sad. However, consider the situation of the person who wants to interpret something. Don't just know other things that can affect a person, but also remember that a person's experience is something everyone sees differently. For example, many people around the world think that an event is good because it allows them to connect with others. I want to see more examples of how things happen and why they are important. But I also appreciate the fact that people from other places come together to travel with them. This is also a way to learn to understand things and to improve.
To be patient is to learn to control yourself and understand a person's time. Proverbs says we have 'ears to hear and eyes to see,' (James 1:19) but when dealing with others or people from different backgrounds, patience means understanding what affects someone and what motivates them. In this way, it becomes easier to understand something and to help someone.
The benefits of interpreting something. The person who interprets something should always try to understand their own limitations, and they may be considered wise or a leader among many. How can you know the limitations of another person?
One way to find out is to listen to a person and understand their point of view. Many people who misinterpret things often fail to understand a person's perspective, so they focus on their own views instead of trying to understand the person's true feelings and limitations. And sometimes people do things that seem right and wrong, but some fail to recognize their mistakes.
Consider how important it is to understand a person's background. Is he a child, an adult, educated or uneducated, has he experienced hardship, has he been influenced by those around him, is he humble, or is he arrogant? Knowing these things will help you understand his limitations.
To understand the limitations of someone you want to interpret, share them with others who also have similar experiences. These people may be able to show you ways to overcome obstacles that you didn't realize were there. Understanding many things about a person's life helps you interpret them and understand their limitations in relation to others.
Take time to carefully consider the interpretation. The Bible says: "A thoughtful answer is better than a hasty reply." (Proverbs 15:23) This scripture shows that it is important to take time to understand what is being said before offering an opinion, especially when dealing with sensitive matters. Today, this advice is more relevant than ever. However, sometimes a quick response can encourage a person, just as a careful interpretation can encourage the person being interpreted.
Sometimes understanding certain things can help you interpret a person correctly. For example, knowing whether someone is rich or poor, whether someone is a child going to school, or whether people around them are raising a child. Some people think it is okay to write down what they observe about a person, even if those observations are based on limited information, but it is best to let such things remain unspoken until the right time. Therefore, it is important to be careful to interpret the limitations that a person has shown. *
Don't rush to interpret people or rely on superficial things. Don't try to interpret everything a person does. Instead, we should strive to interpret things so that we don't cause harm or create misunderstandings. For instance, if someone interprets another person harshly and unfairly because of their own biases, that person may become upset and feel misunderstood. If there is no good reason for the interpretation, the harshness will only make the person feel worse and resentful. Such behavior causes us to lose sight of the real issue, and it stems from the desire to interpret harshly.
The reason for interpreting harshly. Often when we encounter difficulties, we tend to think that we understand the situation fully. But often the reason for interpreting harshly is due to our own lack of understanding. And many people struggle with this tendency to interpret harshly, and they repeat this mistake throughout their lives, constantly misinterpreting people. Sometimes interpreting harshly can lead to conflict or create problems.
Should we avoid being harsh or interpreting harshly with this understanding? The Bible advises us: "All things should be done for edification." (1 Corinthians 16:14) If we understand a person generously and show them kindness, this harshness will not affect them, and it will be beneficial for your own well-being. But if we interpret everything negatively, we will disappoint our Father in heaven. However, the Christians in Corinth were generous in their willingness to help the Christians in Judea with money and supplies, so the apostle Paul commended them for this attitude. He said: "God loves a cheerful giver."—2 Corinthians 9:7.
Understanding these things helps us to be more considerate and kind towards those who cause us difficulty. Many things are used to fulfill God's purpose of interpreting people generously and showing compassion. We should strive to learn from each experience so that we may know how pleasing this generosity is to God.
^ kal. 13 Many people are generous with their time to share the good news and especially during large gatherings. Indeed, many events happen during gatherings that are often highlighted in publications. Learn from each event and see what the Bible teaches. Consider each gathering and ask yourself, "What does this mean—How can Christmas be celebrated as a Christian?"

text:
Vitio ĩmwe ĩnaumiw'e mĩtũkĩ ĩkwonany'a maũndũ mathũku na makũtelemya ĩnaĩ na kyongo Antichrist.
Kĩkundi kĩmwe kya aini kyeetie kaseti ĩmwe yoo ya wathi Antichrist Superstar.
Mũsomi ũmwe wĩtawa Friedrich Nietzsche wa myaka ya 1800 na kĩndũ eetie ĩvuku yĩmwe yake The Antichrist.
Mavinda maingĩ asumbĩ ma tene (Middle Ages) meetaa amaitha moo nthũ sya Klĩsto
Mũtongoi wa kyama kya German Reformation, Martin Luther, aisye kana atongoi ma Roman Catholic (popes) nĩ nthũ sya Klĩsto.
NŨNDŨ ndeto "nthũ ya Klĩsto" nĩtũmĩĩtwe kwa ĩvinda ĩasa vakuvĩ syĩndũnĩ syonthe, kwa ngelekany'o, masyĩtwanĩ ma asumbĩ, o na vitionĩ na syĩndũnĩ ingĩ no twĩkũlye: Yo nthũ ya Klĩsto nũũ? Yo ndeto ĩsu nĩtũkonetye ũmũnthĩ? Vate nzika, vandũ vala vaseo vyũ va kwambĩĩa kũmantha kĩla kyonanaw'a nĩ ndeto nthũ ya Klĩsto nĩ Mbivilianĩ, nũndũ ĩtũmĩĩtwe vo mavinda atano.
KŨVUANW'A KWA NTHŨ YA KLĨSTO
Mũtũmwa Yoana nowe e weka katĩ wa aandĩki ma Mbivilia watũmĩie ndeto "nthũ ya Klĩsto." Aeleisye ata ĩũlũ wa nthũ ya Klĩsto? Kwoona ndeto ii syĩ nthĩnĩ wa valũa wake wa mbee: "Syana nini, nĩ saa wa mũminũkĩlyo: na tondũ mweewie kana nthũ ya Klĩsto nĩnĩkũka, o na yu nthũ sya Klĩsto nĩsyaingĩvie; na ũndũ wa ũu nĩtwĩsĩ kana nĩ saa wa mũminũkĩlyo. Nĩmeeyumisye kwitũ, ĩndĩ matyaĩ maitũ . . . Ũla wĩ ũvũngũ nũũ, ate o ũla ũnũũlea kana Yesũ nĩwe Klĩsto? Ũsu nĩwe nthũ ya Klĩsto, ũla ũkaĩaa Asa na Mwana."—1 Yoana 2:18, 19, 22.
Mũtũmwa Yoana nĩwaeleetwe nesa kana nthũ ya Klĩsto nĩ andũ onthe ala manyaĩĩkasya na ngenda ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ Klĩsto na momanyĩsyo make
Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na ndeto isu? Mũtũmwa Yoana awetie "nthũ sya Klĩsto," kwonany'a kana nthũ ya Klĩsto ti ndeto yonanasya mũndũ ũmwe, ĩndĩ nĩ kĩkundi kya andũ. Ikundi sya andũ ila nĩsyo nthũ ya Klĩsto, inyaĩĩkasya ũvũngũ, ikalea kana Yesũ nĩwe Klĩsto, kana Masia, na ikatata kũvithany'a kĩvathũkany'o kĩla kĩ vo katĩ wa Ngai na Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto. Andũ ala ne nthũ sya Klĩsto meyĩtaa Klĩsto, kana maketw'a matũmĩtwe nĩ Klĩsto, ĩndĩ nũndũ "nĩmeeyumisye kwitũ" nĩmatiie momanyĩsyo ma w'o ma Mbivilia. O na ĩngĩ, andũ asu maĩ o kw'o ĩvinda yĩla Yoana waandĩkaa valũa wake, "saa wa mũminũkĩlyo" na nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa aneeneaa mũminũkĩlyo wa atũmwa.
Yoana aandĩkie ũndũ ũngĩ mwaũ ĩũlũ wa nthũ ya Klĩsto? Aumisye ũkany'o ũũ aineena ĩũlũ wa athani ma ũvũngũ: "Kĩla veva wumbũlaa kana Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwokie e na mwĩĩ nĩ wa Ngai: Na kĩla veva ũtaumbũlaa Yesũ, ti wa Ngai: na ũsu nĩw'o veva wa ĩla nthũ ya Klĩsto, ũndũ mweewie kana ũkooka; o na yu wĩ kũũ nthĩ." (1 Yoana 4:2, 3) Na ĩndĩ, valũanĩ wake wa kelĩ Yoana atũngĩlĩĩla ũndũ ũsu kwa kwasya atĩĩ: "Akengani aingĩ nĩmaumĩlĩte kũũ nthĩ, na nĩ ala mataumbũlaa kana Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwokie na mwĩĩ. Ũsu nĩ mũkengani na nthũ ya Klisto." (2 Yoana 7) Vate nzika, Yoana nĩwaeleetwe nesa kana nthũ ya Klĩsto nĩ andũ onthe ala manyaĩĩkasya na ngenda ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ Klĩsto na momanyĩsyo make.
"ATHANI MA ŨVŨNGŨ" NA "ŨLA MŨNDŨ WA NAĨ"
Ĩvinda yĩasa mbee wa Yoana kũandĩka ĩũlũ wa akengani asu ma ndĩni, Yesũ aĩ anengie aatĩĩi make ũtao ũũ: "Ĩsũvĩei athani ma ũvũngũ, ala mokaa kũla mũĩ mevw'ĩkĩte ngũa sya malondu, ĩndĩ nthĩnĩ nĩ nzũi mbai." (Mathayo 7:15) O nake mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwakanisye Aklĩsto ma Thesalonika kwa ndeto ii: "Mũndũ o na wĩva ndakamũkenge na ũndũ o na wĩva: nũndũ mũthenya ũsu [wa Yeova] ndũkoka, ũalyũko ũtambĩte kũka, na ũla mũndũ wa naĩ kũvuanw'a, mwana wa wanangĩko."—2 Athesalonika 2:3.
Kwoou, ĩvinda ya atũmwa, athani ma ũvũngũ na akaĩi ma mũĩkĩĩo maĩ kw'o, me na kĩeleelo kya kwonzya kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto. Andũ onthe ala manyaĩĩkasya na makamanyĩsya ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa Klĩsto na momanyĩsyo make nĩ "nthũ ya Klĩsto" o tondũ Yoana wawetie. Vaulo nĩwoonanisye ũndũ Yeova wonaa andũ asu ĩla waisye kana mo nĩ "mwana wa wanangĩko."
ĨSŨVĨANE NA MAWĨA MA NTHŨ YA KLĨSTO
Nao nata ũmũnthĩ? Ikundi sya andũ ala nĩ nthũ ya Klĩsto nĩmavĩngaa Klĩsto na momanyĩsyo make ũmũnthĩ. Manyaĩĩkasya na ngenda ũvũngũ mayenda andũ maikamanye nesa ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Asa, Yeova Ngai, na Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto. Kwoou, ve vata wa kwĩsũvĩana na ũvũngũ ta ũsu wa andũ ma ndĩni. Ekai twone ngelekany'o ilĩ sya ũvũngũ ũla manyaĩĩkasya.
Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ, ndĩni syĩthĩĩtwe iinyaĩĩkya ũmanyĩsyo wa Ũtatũ iyasya kana Asa na Mwana nĩ kĩndũ kĩmwe. Kwoou, nthũ ya Klĩsto ĩmanyĩasya ũndũ ũtaeleeka na ĩkavithany'a ũw'o wa kana Yeova Ngai na Yesũ Klĩsto me kĩvathũkany'o. Ũmanyĩsyo ũsu ũtaeleeka ũtumĩte andũ me na ngoo nzeo mataatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ Klĩsto na matamũthengeea Ngai, o na kau Mbivilia ĩmekĩĩte vinya meke ũu.—1 Akolintho 11:1; Yakovo 4:8.
Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtumĩte andũ methĩwa mate kũkwatya kĩvathũkany'o katĩ wa Yeova na Yesũ nĩ kana ndĩni mbingĩ itũmĩaa Mbivilia ila syumĩtye ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova, vala yaĩle kwĩthĩwa yĩĩ. Mekaa ũu o na kau Maandĩkonĩ ma mbee ma Mbivilia ĩsyĩtwa Yeova yĩtũmĩĩtwe mavinda ta 7,000. Kwĩka ũu kũtumĩte maũndũ methĩwa mailyĩ ata? Kũtumĩte wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya andũ kũelewa nesa ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai.
Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, kũmanya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova, nĩkũtetheesye andũ aingĩ me ngoo nzeo makamũthengeea Ngai. Ũu nĩw'o kweethĩiwe kwa Richard, ũla waĩtye ũũ aililikana ũneenany'a ũla waĩ naw'o na ngũsĩ ilĩ sya Yeova: "Mambonisye Mbivilianĩ kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai wa w'o nĩ Yeova. Neewie mũyo mũno ĩla namanyie kana Ngai e ĩsyĩtwa. Ndyaĩ naaĩw'a ũndũ ũsu." Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, Richard nĩwavĩndũie mwĩkalĩle wake nĩ kenda ekale kwosana na motao ma Mbivilia, na aimwendeesya Yeova. Aendeee na kwasya: "Kũmanya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩkũndetheesye kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe nake."
Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ, nthũ ya Klĩsto nĩtumĩte andũ milioni mbingĩ methĩwa me kĩvindunĩ kya kĩ-veva. Ĩndĩ kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia, twĩthĩawa tũtonya kũmanya nthũ ya Klĩsto nũũ, na tũkathaw'a kumana na momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ ma ndĩni, ala nthũ ya Klĩsto ĩmanyĩasya.—Yoana 17:17.

translation:
One evil thing is revealed through signs resembling dark days and deceits with the spirit of Antichrist.
One group of people released a cassette called Antichrist Superstar.
One scholar named Friedrich Nietzsche from the 1800s had a book called The Antichrist.
Many events during the Middle Ages met with opposition against Christ.
The leader of the German Reformation movement, Martin Luther, said that the leaders of the Roman Catholic Church (popes) were against Christ.
The phrase "against Christ" is used throughout history for various reasons; for example, conflicts in ancient times, and also in modern times we ask: What is against Christ? And this phrase is used to question everything; people often say that anyone who opposes something is against Christ, a phrase used by five events.
THE OPPOSITION TO CHRIST
The apostle John, one of the writers of the Bible, used the phrase "against Christ." Did he explain what opposition to Christ means? Indeed, this phrase is part of his important message: "Little children, it is the last hour: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last hour. We are of God: whosoever knoweth God heareth our words; he that is not of God heareth not our words. Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error… Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He that denieth the Father and the Son, even he is the antichrist." – 1 John 2:18, 19, 22.
The apostle John was informed that opposition to Christ refers to those who deny the true teachings about Jesus Christ and his identity.
What can help us identify such opposition? The apostle John used the term "antichrist," meaning that opposition to Christ does not refer to just one person, but to a group of people. This group of people oppose, reject the idea that Jesus is the Christ, or Messiah, and they stubbornly refuse to accept the evidence that links God and his Son, Jesus Christ. Others claim to be Christ, or imitate Christ, but the expression "I am of God" indicates their understanding of Biblical teachings. Moreover, these others may not fully grasp the sense of John's statement, "the last hour" and fail to appreciate the importance of the apostles' testimony.
What did John write about this matter to further clarify the identity of those opposing Christ? He explained his test for determining whether someone truly loves God: "By this everyone will know that you are disciples of mine—if you have love for one another." (1 John 4:2, 3) Furthermore, he reminded his fellow Christians of this point by saying: "Many impostors have gone out into the world who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in flesh. Anyone who does so is an imposter and an antichrist." (2 John 7) Therefore, John clearly showed that the spirit of antichrist is manifested by those who deny that Jesus Christ is God's Son and his teachings.
"LOVERS OF PLEASURE" AND "SELFISH PEOPLE"
One reason why John wrote about identifying such opposers was that Jesus had warned his followers: "Watch out for false prophets. They come to you dressed as sheep, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves." (Matthew 7:15) Also, the apostle Paul cautioned the Christians in Thessalonica with these words: "Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will come unexpectedly, like a thief in the night. But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should catch you off guard, and you should not be selfish people." (2 Thessalonians 2:3)
Clearly, false teachers, lovers of pleasure, and those having improper motives pose a danger to the Christian congregation. Those who misrepresent the truth about Christ and his teachings are part of "the spirit of antichrist," as John called it. Paul identified those whom Jehovah considers to be "sons of destruction."
BEWARE OF THE SPIRIT OF ANTICHRIST
What does this mean? The group of people who are part of the spirit of antichrist oppose Christ and his teachings. Misrepresenting the truth can lead people away from a correct understanding of God, Jehovah, and his Son, Jesus Christ. Clearly, we need to be careful not to be misled by such people. Let us examine some ways in which this misrepresentation manifests itself.
For many years, some have taught that the Trinity—God and the Son—are one and the same person. However, the spirit of antichrist distorts the teaching regarding the relationship between Jehovah God and Jesus Christ, causing confusion. This distortion leads people to disregard important truths about Jesus Christ and to offend God, contrary to what the Bible teaches.—1 Corinthians 11:1; James 4:8.
One reason why people are influenced to distort the relationship between Jehovah and Jesus is that many rely on tradition rather than seeking guidance from the Bible and learning God's name, Jehovah. Consider this: For over 7,000 years, the Bible has preserved God's name, Jehovah. Why then would anyone reject using it? Using God's name helps people understand the true meaning of his Word.
Understanding this, knowing God's name, Jehovah, can move people to worship God more sincerely. That is what happened to Richard, who at first did not like what he was learning about the name of God, Jehovah: "I was shocked when I learned that God's name is Jehovah. It was something new to me, and I had never known that God had a name. But it made sense." Since then, Richard has helped his family learn about the Bible, and he has drawn closer to Jehovah. He continues by saying: "Knowing God's name has motivated me to worship and associate with others who feel the same way."
For many years, Christendom has led millions of people astray. By relying on traditions instead of the Bible, we have been misled to misunderstand the teachings of Christ, and we have become vulnerable to false doctrines. However, the teachings of Christ clarify matters.—John 17:17.

text:
ŨLA w'o ĩũlũ wa kyaũ? Ĩũlũ wa makũlyo amwe ma vata andũ matwĩe makũlasya. No wĩthĩwe ũseng'aw'a nĩ makũlyo amwe ta aa:
- We Ngai nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa?
- Kaũ na mathĩna ikathela?
- Kwĩthĩawa ata yĩla twakw'a?
- Ve wĩkwatyo kwa ala akw'ũ?
- Ndonya kũvoya ata nĩw'ĩke nĩ Ngai?
- Ndonya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu ata?
Mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu ũtonya kũmakwata va? Wakũlya andũ me kĩvathũkany'o, ũkwataa mosũngĩo me kĩvathũkany'o. O na ũkakũlya andũ ala maendaa makanisanĩ kana atongoi ma ndĩni, ũkwata o mosũngĩo meũleana. Mosũngĩo amwe monekaa ta maĩlĩte ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kavinda kanini andũ mayĩthĩa maitethya.
Ĩndĩ ve ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩ mosũngĩo ma kwĩkwatw'a. Ĩvuku yĩtawetaa ũvũngũ. Yesũ Klĩsto aivoya Ngai amwĩie: "Ndeto yaku nĩyo w'o." (Yoana 17:17) Ũmũnthĩ Ndeto ĩsu nĩ Mbivilia. Ũvoonĩ ũũ ũatĩĩe nũũkwata mosũngĩo ma w'o ma makũlyo asu kwa ũkuvĩ kuma Mbivilianĩ.
We Ngai Nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa?
NĨKĨ ANDŨ MAKŨLASYA ĨKŨLYO YĨU?: Nthĩ ĩno tũĩ yusũĩte ũng'endu na sila ũte wa katĩ. Ndĩni mbingĩ imanyĩasya kana nĩ kwenda kwa Ngai tũthĩnae.
KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA: Ngai ndaetae ũthũku. Ĩandĩko ya Yovu 34:10 yaĩtye: "Nĩkwĩthĩwe kũasa na Ngai, atĩ eke ũthũku, na kũasa na Mwene Vinya W'onthe, atĩ eke naĩ!" Ngai e na kĩeleelo kyonanĩtye wendo kwa andũ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ watũmanyĩisye tũvoyae atĩĩ: "Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ…ũsumbĩ waku wũke. Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ o ta kũya ĩtunĩ." (Mathayo 6:9, 10) Ngai atũthĩnĩkĩaa mũno vyũ, nĩkyo kĩtumi wĩkĩte maũndũ maingĩ nĩ kana kĩeleelo kyake kĩanĩe.—Yoana 3:16.
Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:26-28; Yakovo 1:13; na 1 Vetelo 5:6, 7.
Kaũ na Mathĩna Ikathela?
NĨKĨ ANDŨ MAKŨLASYA ĨKŨLYO YĨU?: Andũ aingĩ maendee kũkw'a nũndũ wa kaũ. Ithyonthe nĩtũthĩnĩkaa ngoonĩ nũndũ wa mathĩna ala makwataa andũ.
KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA: Ngai nĩwathanĩte ĩvinda ũkaete mũuo nthĩ yonthe. Ũsumbĩnĩ wake, kana nthĩnĩ wa silikalĩ yake ya ĩtunĩ, andũ 'matikemanyĩsya kaũ ĩngĩ.' Ĩndĩ "makatusya mbyũ syoo itw'ĩke maembe." (Isaia 2:4) Ngai akamina sila ũte wa katĩ na mathĩna onthe. Mbivilia yathanĩte: "[Ngai] akavyaĩa methoi onthe methonĩ moo; na kĩkw'ũ kĩikethĩwa vo ĩngĩ; o na kũikethĩwa ĩngĩ kũmeta, kana kũĩa, kana woo: maũndũ ma mbee [o vamwe na sila ũte wakatĩ na mathĩna] nĩ mavĩtu."—Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4.
Soma Savuli 37:10, 11; 46:9; na Mika 4:1-4.
Kwĩthĩawa Ata Yĩla Twakw'a?
NĨKĨ ANDŨ MAKŨLASYA ĨKŨLYO YĨU?: Ndĩni mbingĩ sya nthĩ ĩno imanyĩasya kana yĩla mũndũ wakw'a ve kĩndũ kĩtakusaa. Angĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana akw'ũ nĩmatonya kũthĩny'a andũ ala me thayũ, kana Ngai asilĩlaa andũ ĩianĩ ya mwaki tene na tene.
KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA: Mũndũ akw'a ethĩawa aeka kwĩthĩwa thayũ. Ĩandĩko ya Mũtavan'ya 9:5 yaĩtye: "Ala akw'ũ matyĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva." Nũndũ akw'ũ matyĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva, na mayĩw'aa ũndũ o na wĩva, maitonya kũũmĩsya kana kũtethya ala me thayũ.—Savuli 146:3, 4.
Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:19 na Mũtavan'ya 9:6, 10.
Ve Wĩkwatyo kwa ala Akw'ũ?
NĨKĨ ANDŨ MAKŨLASYA ĨKŨLYO YĨU?: Nĩtwendaa kwĩkala na kũtanĩa thayũ vamwe na endwa maitũ. Nĩtwĩthĩawa na mea ma kwona ĩngĩ endwa maitũ ala makwie.
KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA: Andũ aingĩ ala makwie makathayũũkw'a. Yesũ athanie kana "ala me mbũanĩ…makauma." (Yoana 5:28, 29) Kwĩanana na kĩeleelo kya mbee kya Ngai, ala methayũũkw'a matonya kwĩkala valatisonĩ. (Luka 23:43) Ĩvinda yĩu yũkĩte kũkeethĩwa ũima mwĩanĩu wa mwĩĩ na thayũ ũtathela kwa andũ ala ewi. Mbivilia yaasyaa: "Ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makatũa vo kũvika tene na tene."—Savuli 37:29.
Soma Yovu 14:14, 15; Luka 7:11-17; na Meko ma Atũmwa 24:15.
Ndonya Kũvoya Ata Nĩw'ĩke nĩ Ngai?
NĨKĨ ANDŨ MAKŨLASYA ĨKŨLYO YĨU?: Andũ ma ndĩni vakuvĩ syonthe nĩmavoyaa. Ĩndĩ aingĩ mew'aa mboya syoo itasũngĩawa.
KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA: Yesũ atũmanyĩisye kana tũyaĩle kũsyokeleelaa mboya sitũ ta wathi. Aisye: "Na mũkĩvoya mũikatindĩe ndeto." (Mathayo 6:7) Twenda Ngai ethukĩĩsye mboya sitũ, twaĩle kũvoyaa ũndũ wĩtĩkĩlaa. Nĩ kana twĩke ũu twaĩle kũmanya kwenda kwa Ngai na tũyĩka kwĩanana nakw'o. Ĩandĩko ya 1 Yoana 5:14 yĩeleetye kana: "Ethĩwa tũkavoya ũndũ kwĩanana na kwenda kwake [Ngai], nũtwĩw'aa."
Soma Savuli 65:2; Yoana 14:6, 14; na 1 Yoana 3:22.
Ndonya Kwĩthĩwa na Ũtanu Ata?
NĨKĨ ANDŨ MAKŨLASYA ĨKŨLYO YĨU?: Andũ aingĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana mbesa, nguma, kana wanake nitonya kũmaetee ũtanu. Nĩkyo kĩtumi mamanthaa syĩndũ isu, ĩndĩ mailea kwĩsa kũkwata ũtanu.
KĨLA MBIVILIA ĨMANYĨASYA: Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kĩla kĩtumaa tũkwata ũtanu yĩla waisye: "Nĩ aathime ["mena ũtanu," NW] ala me na ũkya wa ngoo." (Mathayo 5:3) Tũtonya kũkwata ũtanu wa w'o tweeyumya kwĩanĩsya wendi witũ ũla mũnene vyũ wa kĩveva wa kũmanya ũla w'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai na kĩeleelo kyake kwitũ. W'o ũsu wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Kũmanya w'o kũtonya kũtũtethya kũvathũkany'a maũndũ ala ma vata na ala mate ma vata. Kwĩtĩkĩla w'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ũtũtongoesye maũtwinĩ na mekonĩ maitũ nĩkũtonya kũtuma twĩkala thayũ wĩ na kĩeleelo.—Luka 11:28.
Soma Nthimo 3:5, 6, 13-18 na 1 Timotheo 6:9, 10.
Asu nĩ mosũngĩo makuvĩ ma Mbivilia ma ala makũlyo thanthatũ. Nũkwenda kũmanya mbeange? Ethĩwa wĩ ũmwe wa ala mena "ũkya wa ngoo" no wĩthĩwe ũyenda kũmanya mbeange. Nowĩthĩwe ũyĩkũlya makũlyo angĩ ta: 'Ethĩwa Ngai nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa nĩkĩ wĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũthũku mwingĩ na mathĩna maendee? Ndonya kwaĩlya mwĩkalĩlye wa mũsyĩ wakwa ata?' Mbivilia nĩnenganĩte mosũngĩo matoetye ma makũlyo aa na angĩ maingĩ.
Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ mayendete kũmanya nesa ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye. Monaa ta ĩvuku ĩnene mũno na mavinda angĩ yĩ vinya kũelewa. We nowende kũtetheew'a kũkwata mosũngĩo kuma Mbivilianĩ? Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nitonya kũũteetheesya na nzĩa ilĩ.
Ĩvuku yĩtawa Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? yĩandĩkĩtwe nĩ kana yĩtetheesye andũ ala mate na mwanya mwingĩ mesomee mosũngĩo ma Mbivilia ĩũlũ wa makũlyo ma vata. Nzĩa ĩngĩ nĩ mũvango wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia mũsyĩ kwaku. Ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũtonya kũmanyĩsya Mbivilia no oke kwaku kana vandũ vangĩ mwĩw'anĩte, o ĩvinda ĩvũthũ kĩla kyumwa, na mũyĩmanyĩsya ĩmwe vate ndĩvi. Andũ milioni mbingĩ nthĩ yonthe nĩmatethekete nũndũ wa mũvango ũsu. Aingĩ nĩmavikĩĩe kwasya: "Nĩnĩkwatĩte ũla w'o!"
Vaiĩ ũthwii ũthonokete kũmanya w'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. W'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nũtũthaasya kumana na maũndũ ma maimũ, ũthokoanu wa akili, na w'ĩa. Nũtũnengae wĩkwatyo, kĩeleelo, na ũtanu. Yesũ aisye: "Mũkamanya ũla w'o, na ũla w'o ũkamũthasya."—Yoana 8:32.

translation:
What is the purpose of life? Life is a series of questions that trouble people deeply. Here are some common questions:
- How can we please God?
- Why is there suffering?
- Is there hope for the future?
- What happens after death?
- Is it okay to ask God for help?
- Is it okay to be happy?
Many questions remain unanswered. When people are confused, they seek answers. And when people encounter others who have different opinions or beliefs, they seek their own answers. Some questions seem like small drops of water in a vast ocean of uncertainty.
There is one source of answers. That source is truth. Jesus Christ said about God's Word: "Your word is truth." (John 17:17) Therefore, the Word is the Bible. This shows us how important it is to find answers to these questions from the Bible.
How can we please God?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: Often this question arises during times of difficulty. The heart yearns to know what pleases God.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: God cares about people. Job 34:10 states: "He says, 'I will teach you wisdom, and show you the way.'" God has a loving reason for caring about people. This is why Jesus taught us to pray: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name...May your will take place on earth, as it is in heaven." (Matthew 6:9, 10) God loves us very much, which is why he allows many things and his purpose remains.—John 3:16.
Read Psalm 1:26-28; James 1:13; and 1 Peter 5:6, 7.
Why is there suffering?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: Many people struggle with the problem of suffering. Ultimately, we want to understand why suffering exists.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: God foretold that humans would experience pain. His promise, or hope for a better future, helps people 'to endure more.' It encourages them to continue trusting. Isaiah 2:4 says: "They will hammer their swords into plowshares." God will bring peace and justice. The Bible states: "[God] will wipe away every tear from all faces; and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore; the former things have passed away." (Revelation 21:3, 4).
Read Psalm 37:10, 11; 46:9; and Micah 4:1-4.
Will Things Ever Get Better?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: Many wonder if life ever has meaning. Some believe that life is simply a matter of survival, or that God does not care about people.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: God showed his love by sending his Son. His kingdom, or government, will help people 'to find relief.' It assures them that they will not be forgotten. Isaiah 2:4 says: "They will hammer their swords into plowshares." God will establish peace and justice throughout the earth. The Bible states: "[God] will wipe away every tear from all faces; and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore; the former things have passed away." (Revelation 21:3, 4).
Read Psalm 37:10, 11; 46:9; and Micah 4:1-4.
How Can We Cope With Suffering?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: We naturally want to be surrounded by friends and family. We feel sad when we lose loved ones.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: Most people suffer at some point in their lives. Jesus said that "those in the memorial tombs" will live again. (John 5:28, 29) Because of God's loving purpose, those who have died can have hope. (Luke 23:43) Your loved one's memory will remain precious to you, and this thought can give you comfort. The Bible promises: "The righteous will reside forever on the earth, and they will never be abandoned." (Psalm 37:29).
Read Proverbs 3:19 and Revelation 9:6, 10.
Can We Really Trust That God Cares?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: Many people wonder if anyone truly cares about them. It is easy to feel helpless and overwhelmed.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: Jesus showed us that he understands our feelings. He said: "All those in the memorial places...will come out." (John 5:28, 29) In harmony with God's loving arrangement, those who have died can experience life again. (Luke 23:43) This hope can help you cope with grief and provide strength during difficult times. The Bible assures us: "The upright will dwell forever on the earth, and their offspring will never be abandoned."—Psalm 37:29.
Read Job 14:14, 15; Luke 7:11-17; and Acts 24:15.
Why Does God Allow Suffering?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: Most people find it hard to understand why suffering exists. Many believe that bad things happen randomly.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: Jesus taught us to pray for God's Kingdom to come. He said: "Pray then: 'Let your kingdom come.'" (Matthew 6:7) We trust that God will fulfill his purposes, and we ask him to use his power for good. When we do so, we show that we respect God's wisdom and submit to his will. 1 John 5:14 states: "If we ask something according to his will [God's], he hears us."
Read Psalm 65:2; John 14:6, 14; and 1 John 3:22.
Why Is Life Sometimes Unfair?
WHAT DO PEOPLE DEEPLY QUESTION?: Many people feel that life is unfair, especially when they see others prosper while they struggle. This can lead to resentment and discouragement.
THE BIBLE ANSWERS: Jesus recognized that injustice exists. He said: "Happy are those who mourn, for they will be comforted." (Matthew 5:4) We can find comfort in knowing that God sees our pain and promises to make things right. He wants us to focus on what is truly important—living in harmony with his will and enjoying a meaningful life. That is why the Bible says: "Happy are those who observe Saturday, so that they do not do any work." (Isaiah 58:13) Focusing on spiritual matters brings lasting joy and peace.—Luke 11:28.
Read Proverbs 3:5, 6, 13-18 and 1 Timothy 6:9, 10.
This is just one of many comforting truths found in the Bible. But how can you learn more? If you have ever wondered what the expression "the time of distress" means, you may want to investigate further. Perhaps you have asked yourself questions like: 'Does God really care about my problems and concerns? Why does he allow such terrible conditions to exist?' The Bible provides satisfying answers to these and many other questions.
Many people find that understanding what the Bible teaches requires effort. It takes time and concentration to grasp its meaning. So, would you like help in learning more about the Bible? Jehovah's Witnesses can assist you with your search.
Does the Bible Really Answer Questions? It has been copied and translated into numerous languages, giving millions access to its guidance. Many find that studying the Bible regularly helps them cope with challenges and live a more fulfilling life. One of Jehovah's Witnesses can study the Bible with you at home, or we can arrange for someone to visit you. Millions around the world are benefiting from this arrangement. Many express feelings similar to these: "I finally understand!"
What will motivate you to learn more about what the Bible teaches? What the Bible teaches can affect your relationships, your thinking, and your future. It can give you hope, purpose, and direction. Jesus said: "You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."—John 8:32.

text:
ASYAIWE MWAKA WA: 1953
NTHĨ ĨLA WUMĨTE: AUSTRALIA
ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU: ENDETE MŨNO KWĨLOELA MAVISA MA ŨLAALAI
KWĨANA KWAKWA:
Ĩthe wakwa athamĩĩie Australia aumĩte Germany mwaka wa 1949. Aendete ku kũmantha wĩa wa kwĩnza syĩndũ ta thaavu na nĩwamanthaa wĩa kambunĩnĩ sya kũseũvya sitima, na nũndũ wa ũu atũa vandũ vaĩ vaasa na taoni veetawa Victoria. E ku nĩw'o watwaie inyia wakwa, na nasyawa mwaka wa 1953.
Myaka mĩnini ĩtina wa vau inyia wakwa nĩwambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, na kwondũ wa ũu maũndũ ala nĩlilikanaa neesĩ nĩ mũnini nĩ ala neew'aa inyia wakwa aimanyĩw'a. Ĩndĩ, ĩthe wakwa ndendeeaw'a nĩ ndĩni o na ĩmwe. Na nũndũ wa ũu nĩwambĩĩie kũvũa inyia wakwa na kũmũthĩny'a na ũu watumaa inyia wakwa amũkĩa mũno. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩwaendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia evithĩte na endeew'a mũno nĩ momanyĩsyo mayo. Ĩla ĩthe wakwa ũte kw'o, nĩwatũmanyĩasya nĩ na mũinawa maũndũ ala weemanyĩsya. Nĩwatũtavisye ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ na atũtavya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa twĩ atanu twaatĩĩa myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ.—Savuli 37:10, 29; Isaia 48:17.
Nĩ na myaka 18, nĩnaumie mũsyĩ nũndũ ĩthe wakwa aĩ na ithokoo mbingĩ. O na kau nĩnaĩkĩĩaa maũndũ ala inyia wakwa wamanyĩasya kuma Mbivilianĩ, ndyoonaa matonya kũndethya, na nũndũ wa ũu ndyaamaatĩĩa. Nĩnambĩĩe kũthũkũma wĩa wa sitima kũla kwĩnzawa makaa ma mwaki. Natwaanie nĩ na myaka 20. Nĩtwakwatie kelĩtu kaitũ ka mbee ĩtina wa myaka ĩtatũ, na nasũanĩa kĩndũ kya vata kĩla naaĩle kwĩka. Nĩneesĩ kana Mbivilia no ĩtetheesye mũsyĩ wakwa, na kwoou nambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩndĩ kĩveti kyakwa kĩyamendete o na vanini. Ĩla naendie ũmbanonĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, kyambĩie nĩnyuve ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ aa elĩ, nĩeke kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kana nume vau mũsyĩ nĩthi vyũ. Nũndũ noonie nde ũndũ nĩka nĩneetĩkĩlanile na ũndũ kyendaa na naeka kwĩmanyĩsya na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩtina nĩnesie kwĩlila mũno nĩkĩ ndaatĩĩa maũndũ ala neesĩ nĩ maseo.
Mũthenya ũmwe, andũ ala twathũkũmaa ĩmwe nĩmambonisye mavisa ma ũlaalai. Woonekaa wĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya ĩndĩ wa kũtelemya, na ĩla naminie kũsisya visa isu nthũku neewie wasya wakwa wa ngoo wathũka vyũ. Ĩla nalilikanile maũndũ ala neemanyĩisye Mbivilianĩ, nĩneesĩ nesa vyũ kana Ngai ndaema kũnzilĩla. Ĩndĩ o ũndũ naendeeie kwĩloela mavisa asu ma ũlaalai, now'o woni wakwa waalyũkile. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, weethĩie ndyĩkala ndeloele visa isu nthũku.
Myaka 20 kuma ĩvinda yĩu, nĩnathũkĩĩie na weethĩa vai ũndũ o na ũmwe nĩatĩĩaa katĩ wa maũndũ ala inyia wakwa wamanyĩisye. Mwĩkalĩle wakwa nĩwoonanasya nesa maũndũ ala maĩ kĩlĩkonĩ. Ũneeni wakwa waĩ mũthũku na nendete kũtũmĩa ndeto ikonetye maũndũ ma ũlaalai ĩla ngũvũa ngũĩ. O na nĩnambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na mawoni mathũku ĩũlũ wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. O na kau nekalaa na kĩveti kyakwa, nĩnakomaa na aka angĩ. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩneesiisye kĩoonĩ na neew'a neemena vyũ. Vandũ va kwĩw'a nĩnengete ndaĩa ũndũ neew'aa tene, neewie neemena vyũ.
Mũtwaano wakwa nĩwathelile na maũndũ mathũka vyũ. Nĩnamũvoyie Yeova kuma ngoonĩ na nambĩĩa ĩngĩ kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, o na kau nĩvavĩtĩte ĩvinda ya myaka ta 20 ndemanyĩsya. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ĩthe wakwa aĩ akwie, na inyia wakwa aĩ avatisiwe na atw'ĩka Ngũsĩ ya Yeova.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA YAALYŨLILE MWĨKALĨLE WAKWA:
Mwĩkalĩle wakwa waĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya. Ĩndĩ yu nĩnatw'ĩte vyũ kũkwata mũuo wa kĩlĩko ũla Mbivilia ĩwetete. Nĩnavangie kũeka kũtũmĩa ndeto nthũku na kwĩthĩwa ndeũthata mĩtũkĩ. O na nĩnatwie kũekana na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku, kũtha kalata, kũnyw'a mũno, na kũyĩa mũnene ũla wambandĩkĩte.
Andũ ala twathũkũmaa ĩmwe mayamanyaa nĩkĩ ngwenda kwĩka moalyũku asu manenevete ũu. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ta ĩtatũ matindĩaa kũnthing'ĩĩsya nĩsyokee maũndũ asu mathũku. Ĩla nesa kũvĩtũũkany'a o vanini na ndineena ndeto nthũku kana ngew'a woo, andũ asu twathũkũmaa namo meew'aa mũyo mũno na mayasya "ekai mwone aisyoka vala ũnatũaa." Ndeto isu syanũmĩasya mũno! O na syatumaa nona ta ndesa kũalyũka.
Vala nathũkũmaa yaĩ laisi vyũ kwona visa sya ũlaalai. Andũ ala twathũkũmaa ĩmwe matindĩaa kũtũma visa nthũku na kombyũta o tondũ natwĩe nĩkaa. Natatĩte mũno kũekana na kĩmanyĩo kya kũsisya visa isu nthũku, ĩndĩ namo matataa ũndũ matonya nĩ kana nĩsyokee kĩmanyĩo kĩu. Nĩnaneenie na ũla tweemanyĩasya Mbivilia ĩmwe nĩ kana andetheesye na aimbĩkĩa vinya. Nĩweethukĩĩisye nesa vyũ maũndũ ala namũtavasya kuma ngoonĩ. Nĩwatũmĩie Maandĩko kũmbony'a ũndũ ndonya kũekana na kĩmanyĩo kĩu, na ambĩkĩa vinya nĩmwĩkwatasye Yeova kĩla ĩvinda kwĩsĩla mboya.—Savuli 119:37.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnoombanisye andũ onthe ala twathũkũmaa ĩmwe. Ĩla moombanie nameie manenge aũme elĩ maĩ vau ũkĩ, na nĩneesĩ kana maĩ na thĩna wa kũnyw'a mũno ĩndĩ matw'ĩte kũekana na kĩmanyĩo kĩu. Namina kũmatavya ũu, andũ asu onthe mew'ĩte woo mambĩie atĩĩ: "Tũitonya kũnenga aũme aa ũkĩ nũndũ maendeee kũng'ang'ana ũndũ matonya maeke kũnyw'a!" Mambĩa ũu nakwa nameie atĩĩ: "O nakwa nĩendeee kũng'ang'ana tamo." Kuma mũthenya ũsu andũ asu nĩmamanyie kana nĩendeee kũng'ang'ana nĩekane na kĩmanyĩo kĩu kya kũsisya visa sya ũlaalai, na mayaambĩla ĩngĩ kũnthing'ĩĩsya nĩkĩsyokee.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, Yeova nĩwandetheeisye mũno naekana na kĩmanyĩo kĩu kya kũsisya visa sya ũlaalai. Mwaka wa 1999, nĩnavatisiwe natw'ĩka ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, na nĩnatanie mũno nũndũ nĩnakwatie ĩngĩ mwanya wa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo na kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu ĩngĩ.
Yu nĩnĩsĩ nesa nĩkĩ Yeova ũmenete maũndũ asu natwĩe nĩmendete kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Nũndũ nĩ Ĩthe wakwa ũmbendete, endaa kũnzũvĩa ndikakwatwe nĩ maũndũ mathũku ala maumanaa na kwĩloela visa sya ũlaalai. Kwa w'o ndeto ii syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Nthimo 3:5, 6 nĩ sya w'o. Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩkĩĩa Yeova na ngoo yaku yonthe, Na ndũkekwatye ũmanyi waku mwene: Mĩendelenĩ yaku yonthe mũkũsĩĩe we, Na akaũlũngalĩlya nzĩa syaku." O vamwe na kũtũsianĩa na mĩisyo, mĩao ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩtũtetheeasya kũendeea nesa.—Savuli 1:1-3.
MOATHIMO ALA NĨKWATĨTE:
Ĩvinda ĩvĩtu nĩtwĩe ndyĩw'a nĩmenete, ĩndĩ yu nĩnĩnengete ndaĩa na nĩnĩthĩawa na mũuo wa kĩlĩko. Nĩnĩthĩawa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo, na nĩnĩw'aa Yeova andekeie na nĩnonaa aindetheesya. Mwaka wa 2000, nĩnatwaie mwĩĩtu-a-asa mwanake wĩtawa Karolin, ũmwendete Yeova o takwa. Twĩkalanasya na mũuo nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa. Nĩtwĩw'aa ne ũathimo mũnene kwĩthĩwa twĩ kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto kya nthĩ yonthe kĩla kĩthĩawa na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa me mwĩkalĩle mũseo na mendene.

translation:
LET IT BE THE YEAR OF: 1953
THE COUNTRY IS CALLED: AUSTRALIA
OUR HISTORY: STARTED LONG AGO TO LOOK FOR GOOD THINGS THAT ARE USEFUL
DETAILS ABOUT THIS:
The people of Australia and Germany joined in 1949. He started working on building things like roads and he worked in companies dealing with vehicle repair, and because of this he brought many people who came and settled in Victoria. And so he continued his work, and now it's 1953.
Many years later, my father told me about learning the Bible and God's Organization, and because of this, I didn't agree with him at first and I didn't understand what my father was teaching. However, my father persevered and he was patient with me. And because of this, he helped me learn about my father and appreciate what he did which made my father happy. But even though it was like this, I continued learning the Bible diligently and persevered with what he taught me. But when my father wasn't there, I learned from others what they were teaching. We showed him the importance of faith and we taught him something worth knowing. We showed him the value of time and we taught him something important to remember for five years while studying the Bible.—Psalm 37:10, 29; Isaiah 48:17.
I was 18 years old, and I struggled with things because my father had many expectations. And then I started to see things that my father was teaching about the Bible, so I wanted to try, and because of this, I obeyed. I told myself to avoid bad company and stay away from evil influences. I worked until I was 20 years old. We got married after three years, and I realized the importance of working hard every day. I wondered if the Bible would help me with my problems, and that's why I decided to study the Bible with someone from God's Organization. But his advice didn't work well with others. But I went to another member of God's Organization who explained something to me about those things, and I agreed to study the Bible again even if it took a long time. Because of this, I understood that I needed to continue learning with God's Organization. Later, I realized how much I appreciated the things I had learned and felt grateful.
One day, some people we were associating with showed us false information. It seemed like a way to get rich quickly, but I refused to give them my visa money because I feared they would misuse it. But I remembered what I had learned from the Bible, and I believed that God would help me. So I continued to refuse to give them my visa money, and eventually, they left. Later, I regretted being associated with such people.
At age 20, I met someone who encouraged me to do something that contradicted what I had been taught. My conscience reminded me of the good things I had learned. My friend was stubborn and insisted on doing wrong things despite my warnings. And I told myself to be careful and avoid getting involved in bad associations. And also, I stayed away from his bad influence and avoided him. One day, I saw him behaving badly. The people around him noticed his behavior and disapproved of it.
His family was troubled by his actions. I spoke to Jehovah about this matter and asked for strength to preach the Bible, and I spent nearly 20 years preaching. During those years, his situation worsened, and his family suffered because he did not listen to the advice of Jehovah's Witnesses.
WHAT THE BIBLE TAUGHT MY CONSCIENCE:
My conscience bothered me greatly about what the Bible says. Because of this, I decided to reject worldly wisdom and accept the guidance of the Bible. I resolved to stop using harmful substances and engaging in immoral practices. And I stopped associating with bad company, writing letters, drinking alcohol, and indulging in selfish desires.
Some people we were associating with may think we are foolish to reject their offers of quick wealth. For almost thirty years, I have been trying to remember the good things I have learned. But it is important to remain vigilant and continue to seek guidance from the Bible, and our friends may mock us and say, "Look at how naive you are!" These comments should not discourage us! And they can cause problems for others.
But I continued to see the value of maintaining neutrality. Some people we were associating with kept urging us to use violence and computers, but we refused. I realized that rejecting the use of violence could lead to difficulties, but I still believed it was right. I am convinced that teaching people about the Bible, even if it offends some, is the best way to please Jehovah. I have seen firsthand how it has helped others. I used the Scriptures to show them why it is right to maintain neutrality, and they came to appreciate Jehovah more and more.—Psalm 119:37.
On one occasion, I spoke to several people we were associating with. They said that my attitude would cause me trouble, and I knew that they were hoping I would resort to violence. But I decided against it, and those people told me: "You are foolish to refuse to defend yourself when you can easily get revenge!" I replied: "I will continue to refuse." On that occasion, those people realized that I would not resort to violence, and they stopped bothering me.
In time, Jehovah blessed my efforts to remain neutral. In 1999, I was assigned to work with an elder in our congregation, and I learned much from his example of being courageous and principled.
I am convinced that Jehovah has helped me through everything I have faced. Because of my faith, I have avoided getting involved in serious trouble and becoming entangled in legal matters. That is why Proverbs 3:5, 6 is so meaningful to me. It reads: "Trust in Jehovah with all your heart, And do not rely on your own understanding. Acknowledge him in all your ways, And he will make your paths straight." Also, like David, I find comfort in the company of others who love Jehovah.—Psalm 1:1-3.
LESSONS I HAVE LEARNED:
It is important to be humble and teachable, and I have always tried to be that way. I have benefited from the guidance of elders, and I am grateful to Jehovah for supporting me. In 2000, I married a wonderful woman named Karoline, who also loves Jehovah. We enjoyed a happy marriage. We also experienced the joy of serving together in full-time Christian ministry along with brothers and sisters in the local congregation and circuit.

text:
ANITA * amina kũvatiswa oou na kũtw'ĩka wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, mũũme nĩwambĩĩe kũmũvĩnga naĩ mũno. Easya ũũ: "Nĩwambatie kũthi maũmbanonĩ, o na nĩwambatie kũweta ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Nakilasya natamũka Yeova oou akaimba na aitw'ĩka wa kĩlonzo kĩthei."
Ũndũ ũngĩ waĩ kaũ kwa Anita waĩ kũmanyĩsya syana syake ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Easya: "Navatĩtwe vyũ kumũthaitha Yeova, nakwa nĩ o kwakwa. Namanyĩasya syana syakwa twĩvithĩte, na ndyaĩ nĩtonya kũthi nasyo maũmbanonĩ."
O tondũ ngewa ĩsu ya Anita ĩkwonany'a, kũvĩngwa nĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩkũtonya kũtata mũno mũĩkĩĩo wa Mũklĩsto. Maũndũ angĩ matonya kũtata mũno mũĩkĩĩo wa Mũklĩsto nĩ kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna manene ma mwĩĩ, kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mwana kana ũla ũtwaanĩte nake, kana o mũndũ wa mũsyĩ kũmũtia Yeova. Kwoou kyo nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũmũnenga Mũklĩsto vinya wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova e mũĩkĩĩku?
We ũkakwatwa nĩ mathĩna ta asu mawetwa wĩka ata? Mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye atĩĩ: "Mwĩ na vata wa wũmĩĩsyo." (Aevl. 10:36) Ĩndĩ ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũmĩĩsye?
MŨVOYE YEOVA AŨTETHEESYE
Ũndũ ũmwe mũnene ũtonya kũtũnenga vinya wa kũmĩĩsya matatwa nĩ kũmũvoya Ngai atũtetheesye. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩmwe. Mũthenya ũmwe kwĩ Wakwambĩlĩĩlya mawĩoo, Ana na mũsyĩ wake nĩmakwatiwe nĩ mũisyo mũna. Makwatie livoti kana mũũme wa Ana, ũla mekalanĩtye kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 30, nĩwakw'a. Ana easya: "Athi wĩanĩ ndaasyoka. Aikw'a aĩ o na myaka 52."
Ana atethiw'e nĩ kyaũ? O na kau wĩa ũla wathũkũmaa ndwaaveta vyũ woo ũla weew'aa, nĩwamũtetheeisye nũndũ ndwanengae kĩlĩko kyake mwanya wa kũsũanĩa maũndũ angĩ. Ĩndĩ Ana asyokete akasya: "Nĩnamũtulũĩle Yeova ngoo yakwa na namwĩsũva andetheesye nũmĩanĩsye na wasyo ũsu mũnene nakwatie." We Yeova nĩwamũsũngĩie? Ana nde na nzika kana nĩwasũngĩiwe. Easya: "Mũuo ũla Ngai wanengie nĩwatumie nĩusya na wandetheesya ndikese kũvũavũana. No Ngai e weka ũtonya kũnengane mũuo ta ũsu. Nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana Yeova akathayũũkya mũemewa."—Avi. 4:6, 7.
We "ũla wĩw'aa mboya" nĩwathĩte athũkũmi make kana akamanengae kyonthe kĩla kĩtonya kũmatetheesya mamũthũkũmae me aĩkĩĩku. (Sav. 65:2) We ndũkwona kana watho ũsu nũtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo waku? Na tyo ũkwona kana watho ũsu nũũtuma ũmanya kĩla kĩtonya kũũtetheesya o naku ũmĩĩsye?
MAŨMBANO NĨMATWĨKĨAA VINYA
Nzĩa ĩngĩ Yeova ũtũmĩaa kũnenga vinya andũ make nĩ kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩla kĩkundi kya Thesalonika kyathĩnĩtw'e mũno, Vaulo nĩwathangaaisye Aklĩsto ala maĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩu akĩmea: "Kiakian'yai, na kĩla mũndũ akyaka ũla ũngĩ, o ũndũ mwĩkaa." (1 Ath. 2:14; 5:11) Nũndũ Aklĩsto ma Thesalonika maĩ na ngwatanĩo na nĩmendene, na ĩngĩ nĩmatethanasya, nĩmoomĩĩisye ĩvinda yĩu mathĩnaw'a mũno. Ngewa yoo nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo mũno kwitũ, na nĩtũmanyĩasya kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmĩĩsye.
Kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ no kũtume "kĩla ũmwe aka [ũla] ũngĩ." (Alo. 14:19) Na mũno mũno, kwakana kwĩthĩawa kwĩ kwa vata mũno ĩla kwĩ mathĩna. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Vaulo. Nĩwakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna maingĩ mũno, na Yeova nĩwamũnengie vinya wa kũmĩĩsya mathĩna asu. Mavinda amwe Ngai nĩwatũmĩaa ana-a-asa ma Vaulo kũmũkiakisya mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Vaulo watũmanaa ngethi kĩkundinĩ kya Kolosai, aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa asu wakethasya: "Nĩmethĩĩtwe me ũtethyo mũnene kwakwa." (Akol. 4:10, 11, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Vate nzika, ana-a-asa asu nĩmamũkiakiisye Vaulo na mamwĩkĩa vinya ĩvindanĩ yĩla waĩ na thĩna nũndũ nĩmamwendete. Nĩvatonyeka o naku ũkethĩwa ũtethetw'e kwa nzĩa ta ĩsu nĩ ana-a-asa ala me kĩkundinĩ kyenyu.
ATUMĨA NĨMATONYA KŨKWĨKĨA VINYA
Ngai nũtũmĩaa kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kũtũnenga ũtethyo ũngĩ. Ũtethyo ũsu nĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi. Atumĩa asu me na ũĩ mwingĩ na no methĩwe "ta vandũ va kwĩvitha kĩseve, na ta kwĩvitha kĩuutani, ta tũlũsĩ twa manzĩ vandũ vomũ, ta muunyĩ wa ĩvia ĩnene yĩ nthĩ yĩ mĩnoo." (Isa. 32:2) Ũsu nĩ ũndũ mũseo ta kĩ! Nĩ mũvango ũtwonasya kana Yeova nũtwendete. Kwoou-ĩ, we waaĩsa kwona atumĩa nĩ kana makwĩkĩe vinya? Atumĩa nĩmatonya kũũkiakisya na makakwĩkĩa vinya nĩ kana ũendeee kũmĩĩsya.
Kũneena ũla w'o, atumĩa ti andũ mekaa syama. Asu nĩ andũ me na naĩ, na nĩ andũ 'mailyĩ taitũ.' (Meko 14:15) Ĩndĩ o na mailyĩ oou, mboya ila matonya kũvoya kwondũ witũ no itũtethye mũno. (Yak. 5:14, 15) Kwa ngelekany'o, ve mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩ Italy wũmĩĩsye kwa myaka mingĩ ũwau mũthũku ũla ũmwonzetye malangũ (muscular dystrophy). Mwana-a-asa ũsu aĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa atumĩa: "Ana-a-asa asu nĩmambendete mũno na nĩmanthokeaa mavinda maingĩ, na kĩu nĩkĩtumĩte nũmĩĩsya." We no wose ĩtambya ũkatũmĩa mũnango mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa atumĩa Yeova ũtũnengete?
TŨNGA KĨLĨKO MAŨNDŨNĨ MA KĨ-VEVA
Ve maũndũ angĩ tũtonya kwĩka makatũtetheesya kũmĩĩsya. Ũmwe wa maũndũ asu nĩ kũtũnga kĩlĩko maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya mwana-a-asa wĩ na myaka 39 wĩtawa John. Ĩvinda yĩmwe eeiwe kana e na mũthemba mũna wa kanza ũtethĩawa na andũ aingĩ. John easya atĩĩ: "Noonaa ta ngũkengwa nũndũ naĩ mũnini mũno." Ĩvinda yĩu mwanae aĩ na myaka o ĩtatũ. Easya: "Nũndũ wa ũu, kĩveti kyakwa nokyo kyaĩ kĩtonya kũea mwana witũ na kĩisyoka kĩnzũvĩe, na nokyo kyandũngaa sivitalĩ." Ũiiti ũla John wanengawe (chemotherapy) wamũtiaa na mĩnoo mingĩ na ũitia wamũthokoany'a ĩvu nginya akambĩĩa kwĩw'a ngoo. Ĩndĩ mathĩna ma John mayaathelela vau. Ĩthe awaie weethĩa ndavĩta na nũndũ wa ũu nĩvendekaa mũndũ wa mũsyĩ amũsũvĩe.
John na andũ make meekie ata ĩvindanĩ yĩu yeetete ũu? John awetete atĩĩ: "O na kau nekalaa na mĩnoo, natataa ũndũ ndonya nyie na andũ makwa tũtũnge ilĩko sitũ maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Twaendaa maũmbanonĩ onthe, na kĩla kyumwa nĩtwatavanasya na tũkeka ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ, o na ĩla tũkwĩw'a vinya wa kwĩka ũu." Ĩĩ nĩ w'o, John nĩwamanyie kana mũndũ enda kũmĩĩsya ĩtatwa o na yĩva no nginya atũnge kĩlĩko maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Na we John nĩwĩthĩwa na ũndũ ũtonya kũtavya mũndũ ũkwatĩtwe nĩ thĩna mũito? Ĩĩ, easya: "Kũtelema kũla kwingĩ kwathela, tũmesilya tũla tũtialaa tũminawa nĩ vinya ũla Yeova ũtũnengaa na wendo ũla ũtwonasya. Yeova nũtonya kũũnenga vinya, o tondũ ũnengete vinya."
Tũi na nzika kana kwa vinya wa Ngai no tũmĩĩsye matatwa momũ kana o mathĩna maito, methĩwe matũkwatĩte ũmũnthĩ kana makatũkwata ũnĩ. Kwoou nĩtũendeee kũmũvoya Yeova atũtetheesye, na tũitata twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na ana-a-asa ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ. O na ĩngĩ nĩtũtatei kwona atumĩa nĩ kana matwĩkĩe vinya, na tũitũnga ilĩko sitũ maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Tweeka maũndũ asu onthe tũkeethĩwa twaatĩĩa ndeto ii sya Vaulo: "Mwĩ na vata wa wũmĩĩsyo."
^ kal. 2 Masyĩtwa amwe nĩ mavĩndũe.

translation:
ANITA * I was encouraged to share the good news and to make disciples of Jehovah, so I told him about my desire to do so. Here's how: "I want to preach from house to house, and I want to tell people about God's name." Then I prayed to Jehovah and asked Him to bless my ministry and help me to be a zealous minister.
One thing that helped Anita stay motivated was thinking about what Jehovah does for her. She said: "I love to praise Jehovah, and it makes me happy. I teach my children to appreciate Jehovah, and I don't want to disappoint Him."
But sometimes Anita feels discouraged because she sees Christians being persecuted by others. Some things that can discourage a Christian are experiencing serious illness, losing a child or someone they love, or having someone turn them away from Jehovah. Is there something you can do to remain loyal to Jehovah when facing such trials?
Have you ever been overwhelmed by problems? The apostle Paul wrote: "Keep working diligently." (Heb. 10:36) Can you continue to work hard even when you feel discouraged?
JEHOVAH STRENGTHENS US
One important way to remain steadfast when facing difficulties is to ask God to strengthen us. Consider this example. A sister named Anna and her husband were going through a difficult time. Her husband lost his job, and they had debts of over $30,000. Anna said: "I felt helpless. I was worried and also 52 years old."
What helped Anna cope? And how can you benefit from her experience, which shows how to deal with stressful situations? Anna explained: "I begged Jehovah for help, and I asked Him to give me strength and courage to face this big problem." How did Jehovah respond? Anna says she received an answer right away: "God answered my prayers and gave me peace of mind. He helped me to focus on what was truly important. He reminded me that He would never abandon me."—Ps. 4:6, 7.
The expression "peace of mind" refers to inner calm and confidence that things will work out, despite our worries. (Prov. 65:2) But how can you cultivate such peace of mind? And how can you be sure that your prayers will be heard and answered?
WAYS TO REMAIN STEADFAST
In addition to prayer, Jehovah helps his people to remain steadfast by means of the Christian congregation. For instance, when the Thessalonian congregation was experiencing problems, Paul encouraged fellow Christians to "encourage one another and build one another up." (1 Thess. 2:14; 5:11) The Thessalonian Christians were united and loving, and they took the time to encourage each other. This strengthened their faith. Today, too, we can learn much from their example and find ways to support one another.
Being associated with faithful Christians can help us to "spur one another on to love and fine works." (Heb. 10:24) Moreover, being around mature Christians can strengthen our resolve to stay busy in spiritual activities. Consider the example of Paul. He faced many trials, but Jehovah helped him to persevere. On occasion, God used fellow servants to comfort Paul. For example, when Paul traveled to Colossae, he sent Tychicus to report on his situation, saying: "He will tell you about my circumstances." (Col. 4:10, 11, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Similarly, fellow servants comforted Paul and strengthened him during difficult times. So do not hesitate to seek encouragement from brothers and sisters in your congregation.
PRAYER CAN BRING PEACE OF MIND
God provides the Christian congregation to help us cope with stress. This help comes through fellow Christians. These brothers and sisters are often those who have experienced "trouble, affliction, abuse, hardship, violent attacks, people lying, and great anxieties" themselves. (Isa. 32:2) That is very comforting, isn't it? It shows that Jehovah cares for us. But how can you be sure that prayer will bring peace of mind? Prayer can help you cope and find strength if you continue to trust in Him.
However, ministers are not perfect humans. They are imperfect men and women, and they are also "ailing in spirit." (Acts 14:15) Because of their own limitations, they may sometimes say or do things that hurt our feelings. (Jas. 5:14, 15) For example, a young man in Italy ministered for many years to a brother who had muscular dystrophy. The young man said about his experience with the ministers: "The brothers were very kind and offered much encouragement, and this helped me to persevere." Can you also benefit from this practical support that Jehovah provides through his ministers?
DISCUSS SCRIPTURES IN YOUR MINISTRY
There are ways we can make our ministry more effective. One way is to discuss scriptures in your ministry. Consider the example of a 39-year-old man named John. A sister shared her concern about her husband's drinking problem with many people. John listened and said: "I felt sorry for them because of this situation." His wife was only three years old at the time. He explained: "Because of this, I thought it would be impossible for us to have a child, and I worried about it greatly." John's chemotherapy treatments caused him a lot of pain and made him feel weak and nauseous. But despite John's difficulties, he remained positive. He realized that this situation gave him an opportunity to talk to others about God.
John and his family experienced this benefit during one particular visit? John explained: "Yes, and while I was receiving treatment, I was able to help others and along with my family we discussed scriptures in our ministry. We went to many appointments, and each time we were able to share the truth and show compassion, and sometimes we could offer encouragement." So, John learned that someone who is suffering might appreciate having someone discuss scriptures with them. And John wondered if being able to help someone facing a trial would bring him joy? He explained: "The more we give, the more we receive; we are blessed when we use what Jehovah gives us with love and appreciation. Jehovah can provide comfort, even if circumstances don't improve."
Let us remember that because of God's love we can endure trials even if they cause us pain, knowing that he cares for us. Let us continue to trust in Jehovah to strengthen us, and let us be grateful for the support of fellow believers and our Christian brothers and sisters. And may we always be ready to offer comfort to others and to discuss scriptures in our ministry. We will find that doing so will help us to imitate the example of Paul, who said: "Rejoice with those rejoicing."
