MATUKŨ 26, Mwei wa 12, 2004, kĩthingitho kyaĩ na vinya mwingĩ mũno nĩkyathingithisye kĩthama kya Simeulue, kĩla kĩ ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya Sumatra, nthĩ ya Indonesia. Andũ onthe ala matwĩe vakuvĩ na ũkanga nĩmasyaisye ũkanganĩ nĩ kana mone kĩla kĩkwĩkĩka. Nĩmoonie kĩw'ũ kyambĩĩa kũoleka ũkanganĩ na mĩtũkĩ mũno kwĩ ũndũ kĩkaa. Ĩla moonie ũu nĩmambĩĩe kũsemba iĩmanĩ mauĩte mbu maĩtye "Smong! Smong!" ũu nĩw'o ekali ma kũu metaa tsunami. Ĩtina wa ndatĩka 30, itulumo nene syĩ na kĩseve kingĩ nĩsyakimie ũtee wa ũkanga na syaananga nyũmba mbingĩ kĩsionĩ kĩu.
Kĩthama kya Simeulue nĩkyo kyaĩ kya mbee kũkimwa nĩ tsunami kana kĩuutani kyaĩ na vinya mwingĩ na kyakuĩte kĩw'ũ kingĩ. Katĩ wa andũ 78,000 ala mekalaa kĩthamanĩ kĩu, no 7 makwie. Nĩkĩ no andũ anini makwie? * Ve ndeto imwe ekali ma ithamanĩ maasya: 'Ĩla kweethĩwa na kĩthingitho kĩnene na kĩw'ũ kya ũkanga kĩyĩoleka na mĩtũkĩ, semba iĩmanĩ nũndũ ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini kĩw'ũ kingĩ kya ũkanga nĩkĩũkĩla kĩlike nthĩ nyũmũ.' Kumana na maũndũ ala moonete, ekali ma Simeulue maĩ matonya kũmanya tsunami yĩ vakuvĩ masisya ũndũ kũilyĩ ũkanganĩ. Kwĩthukĩĩsya ũkany'o nĩkwoovoisye mathayũ moo.
Mbivilia nĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa mũisyo wĩ vakuvĩ mũno, naw'o nĩ "thĩna mũnene, ũndũ ũtaaĩthĩwa kuma mwambĩlĩlyo wa nthĩ kũvika yu, o na kũikethĩwa ũngĩ nongi." (Mathayo 24:21) Thĩna ũsu mũnene ndũkaetwe nĩ andũ kwananga nthĩ, o na ndũkethĩwa wĩ mũisyo ta ũla wakwatie kĩthama kya Simeulue, nũndũ Ngai oombie nthĩ yĩkale tene na tene. (Mũtavan'ya 1:4) Vandũ va ũu, Ngai nĩwe ũkaete thĩna ũsu mũnene nĩ kana anange "ala manangaa nthĩ." Ũkeethĩwa wĩ mũthya wa mathĩna na mothũku onthe. (Ũvuan'yo 11:18; Nthimo 2:22) Vate nzika, ũsu nĩ ũathimo mũnene mũno!
Wanangĩko ũla wũkĩte ndũkananga andũ ala aseo tondũ mĩisyo ta tsunami, ithingitho sya nthĩ, na kũlivũka kwa iĩma, syũaa andũ onthe aseo na athũku. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "Ngai nĩ wendo." Ngai ũsu, ũla syĩtwa yake nĩ Yeova, athanĩte kana "ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makatũa vo kũvika tene na tene." (1 Yoana 4:8; Savuli 37:29) Ũtonya ata kũtangĩĩwa kuma thĩnanĩ ũsu mũnene na ndũtanĩa moathimo ala Ngai ũtwathĩte? Ũndũ ũla ũtonya kwĩka nĩ: Kwĩthukĩĩsya ũkany'o!
ĨTHĨWA WĨ METHO WOONA MAŨNDŨ MAENDEEE NA KŨALYŨKA
Tũitonya kũmanya ĩla mũminũkĩlyo wĩũka nũndũ Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Mũthenya ũsu na saa ũsu vai ũmwe wĩsĩ, o na alaĩka ma ĩtunĩ, o na Mwana, ĩndĩ no Asa weka." Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Yesũ atwĩkĩie vinya 'tũsyaĩĩsye.' (Mathayo 24:36; 25:13) Nĩkĩ watwĩie tũsyaĩĩsye? Mbivilia nĩeleetye maũndũ ala maĩ mekĩke ĩũlũ wa nthĩ Ngai atanamba kũete mũminũkĩlyo. O tondũ ekali ma kĩthama kya Simeulue moonie kĩw'ũ kyaoleka ũkanganĩ na mĩtũkĩ na mamanya kana kĩseve kingĩ kĩkuĩte kĩw'ũ nĩkyũkĩte, now'o moalyũku ala tũkwona ũmũnthĩ mekwonany'a kana mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ. Ĩsandũkũ yĩu yĩ vaa ĩũlũ yonanĩtye moalyũku amwe ala Mbivilia ĩwetete.
Amwe ma moalyũku asu mawetetwe ĩsandũkũnĩ yĩu nĩmekĩkĩte kwa kĩasi kĩana ũndũ mũna ĩvindanĩ ĩvĩtu. Ĩndĩ Yesũ aisye kana ĩla twĩona 'maũndũ asu onthe,' twĩmanya kana mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ mũno. (Mathayo 24:33) Ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nĩ ĩndĩĩ maũndũ asu mawetwa (1) meekĩkie ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, (2) meekĩkie ĩvindanĩ yĩmwe, na (3) maendeeie kũthũkĩĩa?' Kwa w'o ki, maũndũ asu maendeee kwĩkĩka ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ.
ŨNDŨ NGAI WONANASYA KANA NŨTWENDETE
Mũsumbĩ ũmwe wa Amelika aisye atĩĩ: 'Andũ aingĩ no matangĩĩwe kũkethĩwa na syĩndũ sya kũmatetheesya kũmanya ĩla mũisyo wũkĩte.' Ĩtina wa nthĩ mbingĩ kũkimwa nĩ tsunami mwaka wa 2004, nĩkweekĩiwe syĩndũ sya kũtetheesya andũ kũmanya ĩla mũisyo ta ũsu wũkĩte nĩ kana maikethĩwe nĩ mũisyo ũsu matataĩĩe na mayasya mathayũ moo. O ta ũu, ũmũnthĩ Ngai nĩwĩkĩte mũvango andũ makanw'e mũminũkĩlyo ũtanamba kũka. Mbivilia yathanie atĩĩ: 'Na ũvoo ũũ mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe; na ĩndĩ mũminũkĩlyo ũkyũka.'—Mathayo 24:14.
Mwaka mũvĩtu, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmatũmĩie masaa mbee wa mbilioni 1.9 maitavany'a ũvoo mũseo nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ 240 na kwa ithyomo mbee wa 700. Ũndũ ũsu wĩtũĩkĩĩthya vyũ kana mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ. Nũndũ nĩmendete andũ mũno, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmatũmĩaa vinya woo mwingĩ maikany'a andũ ĩũlũ wa mũthenya wa Yeova wa ũsilĩlo ũla wĩ vakuvĩ vyũ. (Mathayo 22:39) Ũtethyo ũla ũtonya kũkwata kumana na ũvoo ũũ ũtavanaw'a nĩ wonany'o wa kana Yeova nũkwendete. Lilikana, '[Ngai] ndendaa mũndũ o na wĩva ae, ĩndĩ endaa onthe mavikĩe ũalyũlo wa ngoo.' (2 Vetelo 3:9) We nũkũatĩĩa ũkany'o ũla Ngai ũkũnengete ũkwonany'a kana nũkwendete?
OSA ĨTAMBYA YĨLA YAĨLE NA MĨTŨKĨ!
Lilikana kana ekali ma Simeulue nĩmasembie iĩmanĩ na mĩtũkĩ ĩla moonie kĩw'ũ kyaoleka ũkanganĩ, ĩndĩ mayaaeteela kĩsyoke nĩ kana masembe. Ĩtambya ya mĩtũkĩ yĩla moosie nĩyatangĩĩie mathayũ moo. Nĩ kana twĩtangĩĩwa ũla thĩnanĩ mũnene wũkĩte, no nginya twose ĩtambya na mĩtũkĩ ĩvinda yĩtanathi mũno. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Mwathani Isaia nĩwaveveeiwe aandĩka ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Ngai ũtũthoketye 'mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo,' nayo nĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũilyĩ. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ũkai inyw'ĩ, twambate kĩĩmanĩ kya Yeova, . . . nake akatũmanyĩasya nzĩa syake, na tũkaendaa nzĩanĩ syake."—Isaia 2:2, 3.
Ĩla mũndũ walĩsa kĩĩmanĩ ethĩawa atonya kwona kĩla kĩendeee na ayĩthĩwa e ũsũvĩonĩ. O ta ũu, andũ milioni mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmekĩte moalyũku thayũnĩ woo nũndũ wa kũmũmanya Ngai ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. (2 Timotheo 3:16, 17) Meeka ũu, methĩawa mambĩĩa 'kũendaa nzĩanĩ' sya Ngai, nake nũmasũvĩaa na mayĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo nake.
We nũkwĩtĩkĩla kũthokw'a na ũitetheka nĩ ũndũ Ngai ũtũsũvĩaa kwa nzĩa ya wendo ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũisyo? Twĩũkũlya ũsisye maũndũ ala mawetetwe Maandĩkonĩ ala me ĩsandũkũnĩ yĩu yĩ vau ĩũlũ mekũĩkĩĩthya kana yu twĩ "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo." Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kĩsionĩ kyenyu ikaũtetheesya ũelewe nesa nĩ Maandĩko ala monanĩtw'e vau na ũndũ ũtonya kũmatũmĩa. O na no ũkwate mosũngĩo ma makũlyo maku Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam. Sisya ungu wa MOMANYĨSYO MA MBIVILIA > MOSŨNGĨO MA MAKŨLYO MA MBIVILIA.
^ kal. 3 Mwaka wa 2004, tsunami nĩyooaie andũ mbee wa 220,000. Kĩu nĩ kĩmwe kya iuutani ila syooaie andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.

translation:
DECEMBER 26, 2004, a very strong earthquake and large waves struck the island of Simeulue, near the west coast of Sumatra, Indonesia. Many people there were able to save themselves because they knew how to react when the ground shook. I heard a sound that seemed to indicate an earthquake and many tremors before something happened. But this time it was different to hear voices shouting loudly saying "Smong! Smong!" which is what people call a large tsunami. Within about 30 minutes, a huge wave and a strong current destroyed many houses and infrastructure.
The island of Simeulue is one of the islands least affected by the tsunami or large waves and had a strange experience. Out of approximately 78,000 people who lived on the island, only 7 died. Why did so few people die? * One old story from the ancestors says: 'If there is a big earthquake and the ground shakes violently, immediately run inland to higher ground.' Because of these ancestral teachings, the people of Simeulue were able to recognize a tsunami and save themselves when the ground shook. Remembering this knowledge is very important.
The Bible also gives us a sign to look for, and it says: 'For there will be great distress upon the earth… and men's hearts will fail them because of fear and expectation of those things coming upon the world.' (Luke 21:11) This great distress is caused by humans fearing the earth, and it is like the sign experienced by the people of Simeulue, but God wants the earth to remain forever. (Psalm 1:4) In fact, God causes this great distress so that he can say to those fearing the earth, 'Be strong!' It will be tested with faith and true loyalty. (Revelation 11:18; Proverbs 2:22) Therefore, this is a very significant event!
When you see these things happening—like earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, and volcanic eruptions—remember that all people are affected, including the righteous. The Bible teaches that 'God is love.' Our God, whose name is Jehovah, assures us that 'love endures forever.' (1 John 4:8; Psalm 37:29) How then can we cope with this great distress and maintain our spirituality while God allows these things to happen? The answer is: Keep busy in meaningful activities!
LIVE BY TRUE PRINCIPLES AND REMAIN LOYAL
We need to remember what Jesus said when asked about the sign of his presence: "Concerning that day and hour nobody knows, neither the angels of heaven nor the Son, but only the Father." (Matthew 24:36; 25:13) So why did he tell us to be vigilant? The Bible reveals that there will be events that will show when God begins to act. For example, the experience of the people of Simeulue Island shows how important it is to pay attention to warnings and to prepare. Because they were familiar with the signs of a coming tsunami, they were able to save themselves. This event illustrates how vital it is to heed warnings and to remain loyal. Many accounts in the Bible demonstrate the importance of being prepared.
Some of those accounts have been highlighted because they teach us lessons about how to use our time wisely. Jesus also said that when we see "these things," we will know that his presence has begun. (Matthew 24:33) In other words, "What are these things that will happen (1) throughout the earth, (2) in one place, and (3) repeatedly?" To answer this question, let's examine some recent events.
GOD'S KINGDOM IS NEAR
An American researcher said: "More and more people are becoming concerned about the possibility of disasters." The devastating tsunami of 2004 showed people how vulnerable they are. Some believe that such disasters are simply random events, while others think they are caused by environmental problems. However, God assures us that he will intervene to help those who are loyal. The Bible foretold: "This good news of the kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all nations; and then the end will come."—Matthew 24:14.
Each year, Jehovah's Witnesses spend over 1.9 billion hours preaching the good news to people in 240 lands and territories and in over 700 languages. This work shows how much Jehovah values mankind. But there is something else that Jehovah is doing to show his love for those who seek him: He is providing an abundance of spiritual food through his organization. (Matthew 22:39) The truth about this matter can help us understand why Jehovah cares for us. As stated earlier, "[God] is not willing that any should perish but that all should attain to repentance." (2 Peter 3:9) Will you take advantage of God's provision so that you may continue to benefit from his care?
DO NOT BE IDLE AND INDIFFERENT!
Like the inhabitants of Simeulue Island who quickly responded when they saw signs of a tsunami, we too must act promptly. Being idle and indifferent can be disastrous. A lack of activity often leads to stagnation. When faced with a serious challenge, all of us need to be active and diligent. Can we do this? Isaiah prophetically wrote about what God would accomplish through his "faithful ones," and it has come true. Isaiah says: "Come, let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah… and he will instruct us in his ways, and we will walk in his paths."—Isaiah 2:2, 3.
Someone who appreciates Bible truth can see its practical value and experience its benefits personally. Otherwise, millions of people around the world have become disillusioned because they did not get to know God properly or allow the Bible to guide them. (2 Timothy 3:16, 17) Therefore, make it a point to 'walk in' God's ways, and you will find satisfaction and enjoy genuine peace.
Will we show our gratitude to God by being zealous in sharing the good news with others? Let us examine some scriptures that help us understand what it means to be "faithful ones." Jehovah's organization can help you learn more and provide guidance on how to use the Bible effectively. Visit our website at www.jw.org/kam. Go to HOME > PUBLICATIONS > BIBLE TEACHING.

text:
ĩkũlyo
Nĩnaia mũĩkĩĩo wakwa nthĩnĩ wa Yesũ...Kwoou?
Ũsungio
Nĩ useo! Wasakũa ũndũ wa vata muno! No wĩthĩwe uyĩkulya "kwoou? nĩ tonya kwambĩlĩĩlya kyalo kyakwa na Ngai ata?" Matambya aya atano mawetetwe vau ĩthĩo nĩmeũkunenga mwolooto wa mbivilia. Ethiwa wĩna makũlyo kyalonĩ kyaku kya mũĩkiio, ũka: https://www.gotquestions.org/Kikamba
1. Nĩ waĩle kwĩthĩwa ũielewa ũtangĩĩo.
1 Yoana 5:13 yĩ twĩa atĩĩ, "Maũndũ asu namũandĩkĩa, nĩ kana mũmanye mwĩ na thayũ wa tene na tene, inyw'ĩ ala mwĩtĩkĩlaa syĩtwa ya Mwana wa Ngai." Ngai nũkwenda tũelewe ũtangĩĩo. Ngaĩ nũkwenda twĩthĩwe na ũkũmbaũ wa kũmanya kana kwa w'o wĩmũtangĩĩe. Kwa ũkuvĩ, tũkũnĩkĩle maundũ me vata ĩulũ wa ũtangĩĩo:
(a) Ithyonthe nĩtũvĩtĩtye. Ithyonthe nĩtwĩkaa maundũ ala matamwendeeasya Ngai (Alomi 3:23)
(b) Nũndũ wa naĩ syĩtu, nĩtwaĩlwe nĩ ĩtuvi ya ũthĩnyo wa tene na tene ( Alomi 6:23)
(c) Yesũ nĩwakw'ie mũkelanyonĩ nũndũ wa kũĩvĩa na syitu. (Alomi 5:8; 2 Akolintho 5:21) Yesũ akwie kĩkw'ũ kĩla kyatwaĩlĩte, eyosea ũthĩnyo ũla watwaĩlĩte ithye nũndũ wa naĩ syitu. Ũthayuko wake woonanisye kana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kyaĩ kĩanu kũivĩa naĩ syitu.
(d) Ngai nũmaekeaa onthe ala maiaa mũĩkĩĩo woo vala ve Yesũ — ala metĩkĩlaa kĩkw'u kya Yesu ta ndĩvi mbĩanĩu ya naĩ syĩtu syoonthe ( Yoana 3:16; Alomi 5:1; Romans 8:1).
Ũsu nĩw'o ũvoo wa ũtangĩĩo, ethĩwa nĩ ũmũĩkĩĩe Yesũ ta mũtangĩĩi waku, wĩmutangĩĩe! Naĩ syaku syoonthe nĩndekee, na Ngai athanĩte kana ndakakũtia kana ũkũeka. (Alomi 8:38-39; Mathayo 28:20). Lilikana ũtangĩĩo waku nĩmũsũvĩe nĩ Yesu (Yoana 10:28-29) Ethĩwa nĩũmũĩkĩĩe Yesu weka ta mũtangĩĩi waku, wĩna ũkũmbaũ kana ũkekala tene na tene wĩna Ngai ĩtunĩ.
2. Mantha Kanisa mũseo ũla ũmanyiasya mbivilia kwa nzĩa ya w'o.
Ndukasuanĩe kanĩsa nĩ mwako kana nyũmba. Kanĩsa nĩ andu. Nĩ ũndũ wa vata etĩkĩli ma Yesũ kũmbana na kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo vamwe. Ũsu nĩw'o vata wa mbee wa kanisa. Yu nĩ kwĩthĩwa nĩwaia mũĩkĩĩo waku vala ve Yesũ, nĩtũkũũthuthya ũmanthe kanisa ũla ũmanyĩasya ndeto ya Ngai kwa nzĩa yaw'o na ũineena na mutavany'a wa kanisa ũsu. Mũkũsĩĩe ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo waku mweu nthĩnĩ wa Yesũ.
Vata wa kelĩ wa kanisa nĩkũmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Nĩwaĩle ũmanyĩw'a ũndũ waĩle kũatĩĩa mĩtalatala ya Ngai thayũnĩ waku. Kũelewa Mbivilia nĩ ũndũ wĩ kĩtumi na wakũũtonyethya kwĩkala thayũ wĩna ũkĩlyo wa Mũklisto. 2 Timotheo 3:16 - 17 yĩasya aatĩĩi, "Kĩla Ũandĩko nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai, naw'o nĩwaĩle wa kũmanyĩsya, na kũĩkĩĩthya andũ mavĩtyo, na kũmatũngĩĩa, na kũsilĩla kwa ũlũngalu: nĩ kana mũndũ wa Ngai atonye kwĩthĩwa e mwĩanĩu, eanĩe kũtethya kĩla wĩa mũseo."
Vata wa katatũ wa kanisa nĩ ũthaithi. Ũthaithi nĩ kũtũngĩa Ngai mũvea nũndũ wa maũndũ ala wĩkĩte. Ngai nũtutangĩĩyĩte. Ngai nũtwendete. Ngai nũtũsũvĩaa. Ngai nũtũtongoesya na kũtwonya mwolooto. Tũtonya ata ũlea kũmũtũngĩa mũvea? Ngai nĩ mũtheu, mũlũngalu, ausĩwe nĩ wendo, mweene tei, na ausĩwe nĩ mumo. Ũvuany'o 4:11 yĩasya, "Nĩwaĩle we, Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Ngai waitũ, kwosa ndaĩa na nguma na vinya: nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwoombie syĩndũ syonthe, na kwondũ wa kwenda kwaku syaĩ kw'o, na ĩngĩ syoombwa."
3. Iya mwanya kĩla mũthenya wa ũkwatanĩa na Ngai.
Nĩ ũndũ wĩ vata kwĩthĩwa na mwanya wa ũkwatanĩa na Ngai kĩla mũthenya. Andũ amwe nĩmakothaa kwasya "Ĩvinda ya mwanya" kana ĩvinda ya "kwĩthukĩĩsya Ngai" nũndũ nĩ ĩvinda ya kwĩnengana vala ve Ngai. Andũ amwe nĩmakothaa kwosa ĩvinda kĩokonĩ na angĩ nĩmakothaa kwosa mwanya ũũ mawĩyoo. Ĩyĩũkũlw'a ũndũ wĩtaa mwanya ũũ kana yĩla wĩosaa mwanya ũũ. Kĩla kya vata nĩ kwĩthĩwa ũyosa ĩvinda na kwĩthukĩanĩsya na Ngai. Nĩ nzĩa syĩva ila wĩthukĩanĩasya na Ngai?
(a)Mboya. Mboya kwa ũkũvĩ nĩ kũneena na Ngai. Kũtavya Ngai maundũ ala me ũkũthĩnya. Kũkũlya Ngai aunenge ũĩ na mwolooto. Kũkũlya Ngai aũtetheesye mavatani maku. Kũtavya Ngai ũndũ ũmwendete na kũmũtũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa maũndũ ala wĩkĩte. Ou nĩ w'o mboya yĩthĩawa yĩilye.
(b)Kũsoma Mbivilia. Ĩũlũ wa kũmanyĩw'a mbivilia kanisanĩ, kana ikundinĩ sya mbivilia, nĩwaĩlĩte kwĩsomea mbivilia. Mbivilia yĩna maũndũ onthe ala waĩle ũmanya nĩkana wĩkale thayũ wa ũtangĩĩo wĩna ũkĩlyo. Mbivilia yĩna mwolooto wa Ngai wa ũndũ waĩle kwĩka maũtwi mena ũĩ, ũndũ waĩle kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai, ũndũ waĩle kwĩkala na andũ na kwĩana mũĩkĩĩonĩ. Mbivilia nĩ valũa wa Ngai kũla tũĩ. Mbivilia nĩ mwolooto wa Ngai wa ũndũ twaĩlĩtwe nĩ kwĩkala kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte mbee wa Ngai na kwĩanĩwa.
(4) Nyanyana na andũ ala matonya kũũtethya kwĩana mũĩkĩĩonĩ.
1 Akolintho 15:33 yĩ twĩa, "Mũikakengeke: Itindo nthũkũ nĩsyanangaa mwĩkalĩle mũseo." Mbivilia yũsĩwe nĩ maũkanyo maingĩ ma ũndũ "andũ" athũku matonya ũtwananga. Kũtindanya na andũ ala mekaa maũthũku na naĩ nĩkũtonya ũtulikya matatwanĩ ma kwambĩlĩlya kwĩka maũthũku asu. Mikalĩle ya andũ ala tũtindanasya namo nĩyonekaa nthĩnĩ wa mathayũ maitũ. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi twaĩle kutindanya na andũ ala mendete Ngai na mekaa kwenda kwake.
Tata ũmanyane mũnyanya ũmwe kana elĩ kuma vau kanisanĩ ũla ũtonya kũũthuthya na kũũtethya mũĩkĩĩonĩ.( Aevelania 3:13; 10:24) Kũlya anyanyau maũteetheesye kwĩthĩwa wĩ kĩthito maundũni ma kũmũmanya Ngai. Makũlye kana no ũmatetheesye maũndũnĩ ota w'o. Kwĩka ou ti kwasya kana nĩwaĩle kũekana na anyanya onthe ala matamwĩtĩkĩlĩte Yesu Klisto. Endeea kwĩthĩwa na ũnyanya namo na kũmenda. Ĩndĩ matavye kana Yesu nĩwavĩnduie thayũ waku na ndũtonya kũendeea kwĩka maũndũ ala mweekaa matamwendeeasya Ngai. Voya Ngai avingũĩe ĩvũso ya kũmatavya ũla ũvoo mũseo.
5. Nĩ waĩle ũvatiswa.
Andũ aingĩ maieleawa ũvatiso. Ũvatiso nĩ "kũlikya na kũthika kĩw'unĩ." Ũvatiso nĩ yo nzĩa ya mbivilia ya kwonany'a sanzũ kana wĩ mũĩkĩĩi wa Yesũ Klisto na nĩwĩyumĩtye kũmũthũkũma. Kĩko kya kũthikwa kĩw'unĩ kwonanasya kũthikwa vamwe na Klisto. Kĩko kya kuma kĩw'unĩ kwonanasya ũthayũũkyo wa Yesu Klisto. Kũvatiswa kĩw'unĩ nĩ kwĩtĩkĩlana na Kĩkw'u, Kũthikwa na Ũthayũũkyo wa Yesu Klisto ( Alomi 6:3-4).
Ũvatiso ti w'o ũtangĩĩyaa mũndũ . Ũvatiso ndũtonya ũthesya mũndũ naĩ syake. Ũvatiso nĩ wonany'o wa wĩw'i, wonany'o wa sanzũ wa wĩtĩkĩlo wa kana Yesu e weka no we ũtonya ũtangiia. Ũvatiso nĩ wa vata nũndũ nĩ ĩtambya ya wĩw'i — kũtangaasa sanzũ kwĩyumya kwaku vala ve Klisto. Ethĩwa nũkwenda ũvatiso, neena na Mũtavany'a.
English
Nĩnaia mũĩkĩĩo wakwa nthĩnĩ wa Yesũ...Kwoou?

translation:
Indeed
I have a question for you about Jesus…What is it?
Greeting
It is good! Spread this important message! And don't hesitate to ask yourself "what if I die and ask God 'why?'" These five points were written so that you may understand the truth of the Bible. Read more about salvation, here: https://www.gotquestions.org/Kikamba
1. It is important to be sure you understand assurance.
1 John 5:13 says, "I write these things to you who believe in the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life—right now—and continue to grow in your faith." God wants us to be assured. God wants us to be confident in knowing whether we are truly saved. Therefore, let us examine some truths about assurance:
(a) Everyone sins. Everyone falls short of God's standards (Romans 3:23)
(b) The penalty for sin is eternal separation from God ( Romans 6:23)
(c) Jesus paid the price for our sins. (Romans 5:8; 2 Corinthians 5:21) Jesus took the punishment for every sin we have committed, bearing the wrath of God that we deserved. His sacrifice demonstrates that Jesus' payment is sufficient to cover all our sins.
(d) God offers forgiveness and eternal life to everyone who believes in Jesus—anyone who receives Christ's gift of salvation (John 3:16; Romans 5:1; Romans 8:1).
This is what assurance is, read more about it and receive Jesus as your savior, believe! All your sins are forgiven, and God promises He will never leave you nor forsake you. (Romans 8:38-39; Matthew 28:20). Secure your salvation with Jesus (John 10:28-29) Read more and receive Jesus alone as your savior, have confidence and live forever with God in heaven.
2. Tell the church this good news about the bible for others.
Share the church with your friends or family. The church is people. It is a group of those who love Jesus coming together and encouraging each other. This is why the church exists. You can share your faith in Jesus, and help others understand the truth of God through the teachings of the church. Strengthen your faith with Jesus.
The purpose of the church is to teach the Bible. It helps you learn how to live according to God's principles. Understanding the Bible is essential and enables you to live righteously with Christ. 2 Timothy 3:16-17 states, "All Scripture is breathed out by God, and it is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be competent, equipped for every good work."
The third purpose of the church is worship. Worship is giving thanks to God for all things. God created us. God loves us. God saves us. God guides us and protects us from evil. Why would we not give thanks to Him? God is holy, righteous, full of love, merciful, and full of life. Revelation 4:11 says, "Worthy are you, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for you created all things, and by your will they existed and were created."
3. Make time for daily fellowship with God.
It is important to make time for daily fellowship with God. Some people call this "quiet time" or "spending time with God," but it is simply spending time getting closer to God. Some people find it difficult to set aside dedicated time while others struggle to find the right time. Don't worry about what others do or how much time they spend; just prioritize making time. The most important thing is to consistently seek God and draw near to Him. How can we draw near to God?
(a)Prayer. Prayer is talking to God. Telling God everything that is on your mind. Asking God for help with your problems. Thanking God for blessings. Telling God what you need and giving thanks for all things. This is how prayer works.
(b)Reading the Bible. A key part of understanding the Bible is reading the Bible regularly, or having a Bible study. The Bible has so much information that you can learn and apply to your life. The Bible reveals God's plan for your life, His path for you, His way of living among people, and how to have relationships. The Bible is God's Word to us. The Bible is God's guidance for how we should live as followers of God and how to behave.
(4) Fellowship with other believers to encourage each other.
1 Corinthians 15:33 says, "Do not be deceived: 'Evil company corrupts good habits.'" The Bible warns us about the influence of "bad" people who can lead us astray. Associating with bad people can cause us to fall into temptation and turn away from God. The habits of those we associate with greatly affect our lives. That is why we should associate with people who love God and walk in His ways.
Therefore, choose carefully whom you spend time with, whether it's one person or a group, so that you can encourage and build each other up. (Hebrews 3:13; 10:24) Encouraging words can strengthen faith and help others know God better. Be willing to offer encouragement, even when it's difficult. Don't isolate yourself from other Christians who love Jesus Christ. Continue to fellowship with them and support them. If you stumble, remember that Jesus forgives and helps us get back on track and continue walking in the ways that please God. Ask God to give you opportunities to encourage others.
5. Be disciplined.
Many people misunderstand discipline. Discipline is "training oneself." Discipline is what the Bible means by becoming a disciple of Jesus Christ and committing to following Him. Being trained involves being molded like clay. Being immersed involves sharing in the death of Jesus Christ. Being baptized signifies dying to our old way of life and rising to new life in Christ. (Romans 6:3-4).
Discipline doesn't just change a person. Discipline transforms a person's nature. Discipline is a renewal of the mind, a renewal of the heart, a transformation that happens when someone truly turns to Jesus—it's a turning away from sin to live like Christ. Embrace discipline, together with perseverance.

RENEÉ nĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩ na myaka 30 na kĩndũ, na aeewe Australia nĩ asyai Ngũsĩ. Easya ũũ: "Twathamĩie kũndũ kwingĩ mũno kũla kwaĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Mami na Tata matumaa twĩkala twĩ atanu na tũtanĩa maũndũ maingĩ! Ĩla nesie kũkwata syana syakwa, nendaa o nasyo syĩkale ũndũ twekalaa."
Shane nĩwe mũũme wa Reneé na akilyĩ kũvikya myaka 40. O nake aĩ na mĩvango ta ya mũka na easya: "Ĩla twakwatie kana kaitũ ka kelĩ, nĩtwasomie ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa mũsyĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ ũla waendie na kasiwa kaw'o kũtavanĩlya ithamanĩ sya Tonga, ila syĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya ũkanga wa Pacific, welekele ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa. * Ngewa ĩla twasomie ĩkasetinĩ yĩu nĩyatumie tũandĩkĩa ovisi wa ũvonge wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova wa Australia na wa New Zealand tũkũlĩtye nĩ va ve na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. * Valũa ũla twakwatie watũthokisye tũthamĩĩe Tonga, o vala twasomete ĩũlũ wa vo yĩla ĩkasetinĩ!"
Shane, Reneé, na syana syoo, Jacob na Skye, nĩmekalile Tonga ta mwaka ũmwe, ĩndĩ mwaka ũsu ũithela nduuthĩ ila syaumĩlĩte kũu nĩsyatumie masyoka Australia. Ĩndĩ mayaaũlwa nĩ wendi woo wa kwongela kĩthito ũtavany'anĩ. Mwakanĩ wa 2011, nĩmathamĩĩe kathamanĩ ketawa Norfolk Island kala ke maili ta 900 (kĩlomita 1,500) kuma Australia, welekele wumĩlonĩ wa syũa. Kwaendie ata mathi kũu? Jacob, ũla yu wĩ na myaka 14, easya ũũ: "Yeova nĩwatũtetheeisye na atuma tũtanĩa kũtavany'a!"
ŨNDŨ MĨSYĨ YĨKĨĨTE KĨTHITO ĨTAVANY'E ĨMWE
O ta Shane, Reneé, na syana syoo, ve mĩsyĩ ĩngĩ mingĩ ya Ngũsĩ yĩyumĩtye na ngenda ĩthi kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumĩte methĩwa na wendi ũsu?
"Andũ aingĩ nĩmendete kwĩthukĩĩsya ũvoo mũseo. Twaendie kũu nĩ kana tũmanenge mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kĩla ĩvinda."—Burnett
Burnett na mũka, Simone, me na myaka 30 na kĩndũ na imwana syoo, Eston na Caleb, syĩ na myaka 12 na 9. Onthe mathamĩĩie taoni yĩ kũasa yĩtawa Burketown ĩla yĩ Queensland, Australia. Burnett easya: "Ngũsĩ syesaa kũtavany'a kũu kĩla ĩtina wa myaka ĩtatũ kana ĩna. Na andũ aingĩ nĩmendete kwĩthukĩĩsya ũvoo mũseo. Twaendie kũu nĩ kana tũmanenge mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kĩla ĩvinda."
Nake Mark na Karen, ala me na myaka 50 na kĩndũ, tene meethĩawa ikundinĩ syĩ vakuvĩ na Sydney, Australia. Ĩndĩ me vamwe na syana syoo, Jessica, Jim, na Jack, nĩmatwie kũthamĩĩa Nhulunbuy, kala nĩ kataoni kenzawa mavia ma vata ke kĩsionĩ kya Northern Territory. Mark easya: "Nĩnendete andũ, na kwoou nendaa kũthamĩĩa vandũ vaĩ na wĩa mwingĩ wa kũtethya kĩkundinĩ na ũtavany'anĩ." Karen nake eew'aa aikĩa kũthama, ĩndĩ easya: "Ĩla Mark na andũ angĩ mambĩkĩie vinya, nĩnatwie kũtata none. Ũmũnthĩ nĩnĩtanaa nũndũ nĩneetĩkĩlile!"
Mwakanĩ wa 2011, Benjamin na Carolyn vamwe na twĩlĩtu twoo tũla twaĩ nasalĩ, Jade na Bria, nĩmaumie Queensland, Australia, mathi Timor-Leste. Kau nĩ kasio ke kĩthamanĩ kĩmwe kya Indonesia kĩtawa Timor Island. Ben easya atĩĩ: "Ĩla twaĩ mavainia ma mwanya nĩ na Carolyn twatũmĩtwe Timor-Leste. Ĩvinda yĩu twatanĩie mũno kũtavany'a kũu, na ana-a-asa nĩmatũtetheeisye mũno. O na tweewie thĩna mwingĩ kuma kw'o. Ĩndĩ twaumie ku twaĩtye no tũkakũsyoka. Ĩla twakwatie syana, nĩtwambie kũkũĩĩsya mũvango wa kũsyoka ĩndĩ tũyaakola mũvango ũsu." Carolyn ongelete kwasya: "Twendaa syana sitũ syambe kwĩanĩa vandũ ve amisonalĩ, athũkũmi ma Mbetheli, na mavainia ma mwanya, na twendaa itanĩe vyũ kũmũthũkũma Yeova."
ŨNDŨ MEEYŨMBANISYE
Yesũ akũlilye aatĩĩi make atĩĩ: "Nũũ kwenyu, akyenda kwaka nyũmba yĩ mũnyoolo ũtambaa kwĩkala nthĩ na kũtala mbesa sya kũmyakĩthya?" (Luka 14:28) O ta ũu, ĩla mũsyĩ wa Ngũsĩ wenda kũthamĩĩa vandũ vangĩ, nĩwaĩlĩte kwamba kwĩvanga nesa. Ĩndĩ waĩlĩte kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mavata ta meva?
MAVATA MA KĨ-VEVA: Ben easya: "Twendaa kũthũkũma angĩ ĩndĩ ti kũmatw'ĩkĩa mũio. Kwoou tũtanamba kũthama, nĩtwoosie ĩvinda tweeyaka kĩ-veva. O na nĩtwongelile kĩthito kĩla twaĩ nakyo ũtavany'anĩ na mawĩanĩ angĩ ma kĩkundi."
Ũla mwanake wĩtawa Jacob aĩtye ũũ: "Tũtanamba kũthamĩĩa Norfolk Island, twasomie ngewa mbingĩ makasetinĩ ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Amkeni!, ila syaeleetye ũndũ mĩsyĩ ĩmwe yatavanĩtye kũla kwĩ vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Nĩtwaneeneie vamwe mathĩna ala mĩsyĩ ĩsu yakomanĩte namo na ũndũ Yeova wamĩtetheetye." Nake ũla mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wa Jacob wĩtawa Skye, ũla yu wĩ na myaka 11, easya: "Navoyie mboya mbingĩ mũno! Na imwe navoyie nĩ na Mami na Tata."
MAVATA MA NGOONĨ: Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Reneé awetete atĩĩ: "Tweew'aa twĩ eanĩe tũtwĩe o vala twaĩ nũndũ nĩvo nendete na twatwĩe vakuvĩ na andũ ma mũsyĩ na anyanyae maitũ. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kũtinda nĩsũanĩĩte ũseo ũla nesaa kũtia ĩtina, nasũanĩaa ũndũ kũthama kũtonya kũtũtetheesya."
SYĨTHĨO: Mĩsyĩ mingĩ nĩyĩkaa ũkunĩkĩli nĩ kana ĩmanye kũla ĩkũthamĩĩa ũndũ kũilyĩ. Mark easya atĩĩ: "Twasomie mavuku ala twaĩ twona ĩũlũ wa Nhulunbuy. Ana-a-asa ala matwĩe taoni ĩsu nĩmatwĩkie nesa nũndũ matũtũmĩie makaseti ma maũvoo ma kũu. Makaseti asu nĩmatumie tũmanya ũndũ andũ ma ku mailyĩ vamwe na syĩthĩo ila maatĩĩaa."
Ũla mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Shane wathamĩĩe Norfolk Island ongelete ndeto ii: "Neekĩie kĩthito kingĩ mũnango nĩthĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseo wa Kĩklĩsto. Nĩneesĩ kana natata nĩkale nĩ mũĩkĩĩku maũndũnĩ, nĩ na kĩthito, na nĩuĩtye, vai vandũ vanema kwĩkala o na ethĩwa nĩ va."
ŨNDŨ MOMĨANĨSYE NA MATHĨNA
Ala mathamĩĩte vala ve vata mũnene wa atavany'a na makona mosyao maseo, nĩmawetaa kana nũseo kwĩthĩwa na woni mũseo ĩla wakwatwa nĩ mathĩna ũteetaĩĩe na kwĩtĩkĩlanaa na kĩla kyaumĩla. Kwoona ũndũ aa amwe mawetete:
Reneé easya: "Nĩneemanyĩisye nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya kwĩka maũndũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mavinda angĩ ngalĩko ya Norfolk Island, ũkanga ũuutanaa ũkethĩa meli iyũka kĩlĩndĩnĩ. Na nũndũ wa ũu wĩthĩaa lĩu wĩ na mũo na ũla wĩ vo ndũthooeka. Kwoou ĩla ngũua nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye kũtũmĩaa syĩndũ nesa." Nake mũũme, Shane, easya: "Ũndũ ũngĩ twĩkaa nĩ kũsisya nesa mĩtũmĩĩle yitũ ya mbesa nĩ kana iikavĩtũke ila tũvangĩĩe kũtũmĩa kĩla kyumwa."
Mwana woo, Jacob, nũwetete thĩna ũngĩ. Easya: "Kĩkundi kĩla twathamĩĩie kyaĩ na atavany'a angĩ mũonza, na onthe maĩ andũ aima. Kwoou vayaĩ mũndũ twĩ ĩika naĩ nĩtonya kũtuma ndũũ nake! Ĩndĩ ĩla natavanisye na asu aima, nĩtwatumie ndũũ mĩtũkĩ mũno."
O nake Jim, ũla yu wĩ na myaka 21, aĩ na thĩna ta ũsu. Easya ũũ: "Kĩkundi kĩla kĩ vakuvĩ vyũ kĩ maili mbee wa 450 (kĩlomita 725) kuma Nhulunbuy, kwoou tũtũmĩaa ĩvinda nesa vyũ ĩla kwesa kwĩthĩwa na maũmbano manene. Ĩla kwĩ maũmbano asu tũvikaa tene nĩ kana tũee ngewa na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. Kĩla mwaka vai ũndũ ũngĩ twonaa wĩ mũnene kwĩ maũmbano asu!"
"NĨW'AA MŨYO MŨNO NŨNDŨ NĨTWOOKIE KŨŨ!"
Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Ũathimo wa Yeova, naw'o nũthuasya." (Nth. 10:22) Ana-a-asa onthe ala maathi kũndũ makatetheesye kũtavany'a nĩmeyoneete kana ndeto isu mbeveee nĩ sya w'o.
Mark easya ũũ: "Ũathimo ũla mũnene vyũ wa kũthama nĩ kwona ũndũ syana sitũ itethekete. Syana ila ilĩ sya mbee syĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu vyũ kana Yeova ndaleaa kũtetheesya ala mambaa kwĩka maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ mbee. Vai vandũ ũtonya kũthooa mũĩkĩĩo ta ũsu."
Shane easya: "Ndũũ ĩla nĩtumĩte na kĩveti kyakwa na syana syakwa nĩ ngamu kwĩ tene. Ĩla neew'a maiweta ũndũ Yeova ũmatetheetye, nĩw'aa neanĩwa vyũ." Mwanae, Jacob, nĩwĩtĩkĩlanĩte nake vyũ nũndũ easya: "Nĩnĩtanĩĩte vyũ kwĩkala kũũ. Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ nĩtwookie kũũ!"

translation:
Reneé is a 30-year-old woman, and she was born in Australia but is originally from Kenya. She said this: "We used to live in a very big house with a large garden in South Africa. My mother and father had five children and we did many things together! But I wanted to have my own family, so I also moved to where we lived."
Shane is Reneé's husband and he is almost 40 years old. He also has some challenges with his health and said: "But we can get another small car, we studied at the Missionary School for one year in Kenya which was sent to help with the work in Tonga, but because of the heat of the Pacific region, we were transferred to cooler places. * However, since we studied at that school, it helped us write letters to the branch office of Jehovah's Witnesses in Australia and New Zealand to request to be sent with a large garden in South Africa. * The value of having that opportunity made us want to return to Tonga, but we continued studying throughout the year at the school!"
Shane, René, and their children, Jacob and Skye, have been living in Tonga for about a year, and this year will be coming to an end but they miss Australia. They are looking forward to returning to their homeland. In 2011, I visited a beautiful island called Norfolk Island which is about 900 miles (1,500 kilometers) from Australia, due to cooler climates. Why go there again? Jacob, who is now 14 years old, said: "Jehovah helps us and allows us to do missionary work!"
ANOTHER REASON TO BE THANKFUL FOR MISSIONARY WORK
Along with Shane, René, and their children, there are many other Kenyan families who enjoy serving with a large garden in South Africa. What makes them stay motivated and hopeful?
"Many people find it difficult to remain positive. We went there because we could make time to study the Bible every day."—Burnett
Burnett and his wife, Simone, aged 30 and with their children, Easton and Caleb, aged 12 and 9. Recently they moved to a town called Burketown in Queensland, Australia. Burnett said: "Our family has been doing missionary work for three or four years. And many people find it difficult to remain positive. We went there because we could make time to study the Bible every day."
Also Mark and Karen, both aged 50, used to live in Sydney, Australia. With their children, Jessica, Jim, and Jack, they moved to serve in Nhulunbuy, a town in the far north of the Northern Territory. Mark said: "I wanted to help people, and I also wanted to meet people who had a lot to say about spirituality and missionary work." Karen added that she was initially hesitant to move, but said: "But when Mark and others encouraged me, I agreed to come. I am very happy that I did!"
In 2011, Benjamin and Carolyn, along with their two young daughters, Jade and Bria, moved from Queensland, Australia, to Timor-Leste. It is an island nation near Indonesia known as Timor Island. Ben explained: "We had been praying about where we could go, and Carolyn and I felt directed to Timor-Leste. From the beginning, we enjoyed being there, and our children quickly adapted. But we missed our friends and family back home. However, we were determined to stay, and we knew that with Jehovah's help, we could cope." Carolyn further stated: "We want our children to learn to associate with people from different backgrounds, experienced missionaries, and those who are interested, and we want to teach them how to praise Jehovah."
A THOUGHT-PROVOKING QUESTION
Jesus once asked his followers: "Who among you would build a tower without first calculating the cost?" (Luke 14:28) Of course, if someone wants to move to another country, it is important to be realistic. But are you willing to examine your priorities?
Are you willing to adjust your lifestyle?
EXPERIENCES: Ben explained: "We wanted to serve where there was greater need. We realized that when things got difficult, we needed to focus on the positive. And we have learned to appreciate the small blessings that we enjoy each day." A young man named Jacob said: "We will be moving to Norfolk Island, where we hope to share many publications such as The Watchtower and Awake!, but we also look forward to helping others overcome obstacles and find real joy. We feel confident that Jehovah will bless our efforts." Jacob's younger sister, Skye, who is 11 years old, added: "I'm really excited! And I'm excited to go with Mom and Dad."
LOOKING AHEAD: Sister René shared: "We are so grateful that we took this step of faith, and we have already made new friends and acquaintances. For those considering a similar move, I encourage you to pray earnestly and to trust that Jehovah will support you."
REASONS: Many families find it helpful to discuss what they would be willing to sacrifice. Mark said: "We sold our home and belongings to move to Nhulunbuy. Our children were initially sad about leaving their friends, but they quickly adjusted and appreciated the opportunity to help others learn about the truth. Those experiences helped them mature." Young son Shane, who moved to Norfolk Island, wrote this note: "I miss my friends, but I am happy to be serving at the Kingdom Hall. I know that Dad and Mom will always support me, and I am learning to be courageous, like the people in the Bible."
WHAT MOTIVATES FAMILIES
Families who are willing to make significant changes and face challenges often find that their faith grows stronger and that they experience increased unity. Here are some thoughts from others:
Reneé said: "I realized how little things really matter. For example, moving from Norfolk Island meant giving up a comfortable life, but we felt it was important to be where there was greater need. And although it was difficult, I knew that Jehovah would sustain us." Her son, Shane, said: "It took courage for us to give up our possessions, but we were determined to use everything we had to help others."
Younger son, Jacob, also shared his feelings. He said: "I missed my friends and family very much, and I cried a lot. But I learned that when we put Jehovah first, he helps us cope with difficulties! I have become closer to those who remained faithful." Older son, Jim, who is 21 years old, had this to say: "Our family traveled over 450 miles (725 kilometers) to reach Nhulunbuy, where we used our resources to build a new hall. Building that hall brought us closer together as a family, and we enjoyed working alongside our children and grandchildren. Every year, we look forward to seeing the impact that hall has on so many people!"
"WE ARE SO GLAD WE MADE THAT DECISION!"
This sister commented: "The spirit of Jehovah empowers us." (Heb. 10:22) Many children also express appreciation for their parents' selflessness.
Mark said: "One of the greatest blessings of serving Jehovah is seeing the truth touch people's hearts. The truth can transform lives, and knowing that Jehovah uses us to share the good news is deeply rewarding. It takes faith to leave behind what is familiar."
Shane added: "We gave up a lot to serve Jehovah, including our home and belongings, but we don't regret it. Knowing that Jehovah supports us gives us strength." His son, Jacob, enthusiastically agreed, saying: "I am so glad we moved here! We are so glad we made that decision!"

YESU NIWE NZIA
"Yesu amwia, nyie ninyie nzia, na ninyie w'o, na ninyie thayu vai mundu wukaa kwa Asa, atesile kwakwa." (Yoana 14:6)
Mundu kwa vinya na meko make mwene ndatonya kwiw'ana na Ngai. Ngai niwamunenganie Yesu akw'e ngelany'oni ni kana atwike kiao kati witu na Ngai, nikana atuete kwa Ngai.
Yuyu undu wa Kana nuukumanyithya undu utonya kwlw'ana na Ngai thayuni waku.
4. NO MUVAKA UMWOSE YESU ETHIWE MWOVOSYA NA MUSUMBI WA THAYU WAKU
Kwa nzia ii now'o utonya kumanya wendo na walay'o wa Ngai thayuni waku.
TUMWOSAA YESU KWA MUIKIIO
"Nundu nimutangiitwe na mumo kwondu wa muikiio, naw'o ndumite kwa inywi ene, ni muthinzio wa Ngai: ti undu wa meko kana kuikethiwe ona wiva kwikathiia." (Aeveso 2:8,9)
NO MUVAKA UMUTHOKYE YESU THAYUNl WAKU
"Sisya, niungeme muomoni na kuvingusya: ethiwa mundu o na wiva akeew'a wasya wakwa na kumbinguia muomo ngalika kwake, na ngaisania nake, nake akaisania nakwa." (Uvuany'o 3:20).
Kumwosa Yesu Klisto ni:
- 1. Kumanya we wi mwene nai, na kwithyuua thayuni na kumbula kwa Ngai.
- 2. Kumwikwatya Ngai kukuekea vyu.
- 3. Kumuthoky'a Yesu Klisto asumbike thayuni kwa muikiio, ni kana wikale undu we unukwenda.
Oyu tui thayu waku uilyi ta visa wiva?
Oyu wienda thayu waku wikale ta visa wiva?
Uvoo uu uatiie nuukumanyisya undu utonya kumuthokya Yesu Klisto nthini wa thayu waku.
NUTONYA KUMUTHOKY'A YESU THAYUNI WAKU O YU
Ngai ni wene kwenda kwa ngoo yaku na nukwenda kwianisya kwilila kwa ngoo yaku. Mboya ino nitonya ukutetheesya kumuthokya Yesu Klisto ethiwa nukumuvoya na ngoo ya w'o na muikiio vate ithau.
"Mwiaii Yesu Klisto nina vata naku nundu nyie ni mwene nai. Ningwitikila ni nisumbikite thayu wakwa mwene na kutaanisya naku. Ni muvea nundu wa kikw'u kyaku ngelany'oni nundu wa nai syakwa. Yuyu ni ngwithyuua na kumbula. Mwiaii, ninguuthoky'a ulike thayuni wakwa na kunzumbika vyu. Ni muvea nundu wa kundekea nai syakwa syonthe. Alyula thayu wakwa wikale undu we ukwenda. Amina." Ameni
Ndeto sya mboya ino nundu umwe na kwenda kwa ngoo yaku?
Ethiwa nukwitikilana nayo, voya yu ni kana umuthokye Yesu thayuni waku.
UNDU UTONYA KUMANYA KANA YESU ETHAYUNI WAKU
Yila wavoya niwaikiia kana Yesu niwalika thayuni waku? Aiva yuyu? Lilikana Uvuany'o 3:20, Yesu aisye akalika thayuni waku, nutonya ukukenga? Wimanya ata kana Ngai niweew'a mboya yaku? Ngai nutwathite kana o undu wonthe ula tukavoya kwa muikiio akatwiw'a na kutwianisya.
ULA WINA YESU ENA THAYU UTATHELA
"Na ukusi niw'o uu, kana Ngai niwatunengie thayu wa tene na tene, na thayu usu wi nthini wa Mwana wake. Ula wina mwana ena thayu usu; na ula ute na Mwana wa Ngai nde na thayu usu. Maundu asu namuandikia, ni kana mumanye mwina thayu wa tene na tene, inyw'i ala mwitikilaa syitwa ya Mwana wa Ngai." (I Yoana 5:11-13)
Mutungiae Ngai muvea kila muthenya nundu Yesu ekalaa thayuni waku. Ithiwa na muikiio kana, ndakakutia nongi (Mathayo 28:20). Na nukunengete thayu wa tene na tene.
NDUKAATIIE UNDU MWII WAKU U KWIW'A
Mii yitu nitonya kwithiwa na utanu umunthi na uni ikethiwa na uthatu. Ona weew'a ata, Yesu ndaalyukaa thayuini waku.
Ikumbi ya iloli tiyo yikusasya indi ni kyongo ethiwa kina mauta.
- W'o wa Ngai niw'o wivinya wa kututongoesya.
- Nitukwatanaw'a na vinya wa w'o kwa muikiio.
- Yila tweanisya u-w'o, kwiw'a kwa mwii na mesilya nitongoeaw'a nesa.
- Twikwatasya Ngai na uw'o wake indi ti undu wa kwiw'a kwa mwii na ngoo.
Kwouu ndukekwatye miwนile yaku indi ikwatye ndeto ya Ngai kwa muikiio.
NUNDU YUYU NIWAMWOSA YESU
Kuma wamwosa Yesu maundu maingi nimekikite:
- Yesu nulikite thayuni waku. (Uvuany'o 3:20)
- Nuekeetwe nai syaku. (Akolosai 1:14)
- Nutwikite kana ka Ngai. (Yoana 1:12)
- Nukuendeea kumanya ieleelo sya Ngai thayuni waku. (II Akolintho 5:14,15,17)
Nukwlsily'a tave undu ungi museo kwi kumwosa Yesu thayuni waku?
Nukwenda kumutungia Ngai muvea oyu nundu wa ukuekea nai?
Twonanasya muikiio witu kwa kumutaia Ngai na kumutungia muvea kwa mboya.
EKA TUMUTUNGIE NGAI MUVEA OYU KWA MBOYA
UNDU UTONYA KWIANA KIVEVA
Ta kana kaukenge niwaile kwiana. Ukaendeea nesa nthini wa thayu wa kiveva, ethiwa ukaatiia maundu aa me vaa itheo kila muthenya:
- Neena na Ngai mboyani. (Yoana 15:17)
- Soma ndeto ya Ngai. (Meko 17:11)
- Iw'a Ngai maunduni monthe. (Yohane 14:21)
- Mukusiie Yesu kwa ndeto na meko maku. (Mathayo 4:19)
- Mwikwate Ngai maunduni monthe nthini wa thayu waku. (Veleto 5:7)
- Mwitikily'e Veva Mutheu akusumbike na aikususya na vinya thayuni waku wa kila muthenya na nthini wa kutavany'a uvoo wa Ngai. (Akalatia 5:16-18, Meko 1:8)
NUNDU WA VATA AKLISTO KUMBANA VAMWE
Mbivilia itutavasya tumbane vamwe. (Aevelania 10:25) Twose ngelekany'o ya mwaki. Ngu mbingi syeekiwa vamwe syakanaa muno mwaki munene, indi woosa uku umwe waiwa wi w'oka nuvoaa.
Nota uu, ndutonya kwikala thayu wa u-klisto wi weka. ni undu wi vata muno kukomanaa na andu ala angi maminite kumwosa Yesu Klisto ta Mutangiii na Mwiaii woo.
Endaa kyumwa vala Aklisto ala angi maendaa ala metikilaa ki kana mbivilia ni yaw'o na ala mekaa kwianana na undu Yesu Klisto umatavasya meke.

translation:
1. GOD LOVES YOU AND HE GAVE HIS ONLY SON, JESUS CHRIST, TO DIE FOR YOUR SINS AND THE SINS OF ALL PEOPLE.
"For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life." (John 3:16)
"I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly." (John 10:10).
Many people ask what is life?
Indeed…
2. MAN IS A SINNER
His sin separates him from God. Through Jesus Christ we can know God's love and forgiveness.
EVERYONE IS A SINNER
"By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another." (John 13:35)
"For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God." (Romans 3:23)
God wants everyone to turn away from their sins and accept His forgiveness, so that people may learn to love God. Seek His ways and worship Him, and that is life. That is the fullness of life. And when someone loves and worships God then they will also live through the life of faith.
MAN RECONCILED WITH GOD
"But your iniquities have separated you from your God." (Isaiah 59:2)
MAN IS A SINNER
His sin separates him from God. Through Jesus Christ we can know God's love and forgiveness.
EVERYONE IS A SINNER
"By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another." (John 13:35)
"For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God." (Romans 3:23)
God wants everyone to turn away from their sins and accept His forgiveness, so that people may learn to love God. Seek His ways and worship Him, and that is life. That is the fullness of life. And when someone loves and worships God then they will also live through the life of faith.
MAN RECONCILED WITH GOD
"But your iniquities have separated you from your God." (Isaiah 59:2)
God is holy and perfect. He has a great desire for man and a deep love for mankind. Man needs to return to God in many ways. Pride, selfishness, greed and others. But all can be forgiven. Indeed there is forgiveness.
There is one way to return to God…
3. JESUS CHRIST IS THE ONLY WAY TO REMOVE SIN
He came so that we may know God's love and forgiveness through our lives.
HE CAME SO THAT WE MAY BE RECONCILED WITH GOD AND THROUGH LIFE
"For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God." (1 Peter 3:18)
"Christ died according to the scriptures; and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures." (1 Corinthians 15:3,4)
JESUS IS THE WAY
"Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me." (John 14:6)
Through his own effort and righteousness, man can never reconcile himself with God. God provided Jesus so that He could bridge the gap between us and Himself, so that He might bring us to God.
This is how you can understand what it means to reconcile yourself with God through life.
4. NOW ACCEPT JESUS AND RECEIVE THE GIFT OF ETERNAL LIFE
In this way you can experience God's love and forgiveness in your life.
ACCEPT JESUS BY FAITH
"But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name." (John 1:12)
"For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast." (Ephesians 2:8,9)
NOW ACCEPT JESUS INTO YOUR LIFE
"Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me." (Revelation 3:20).
Accepting Jesus Christ is:
- 1. Recognizing Him as your personal Lord, and turning from sin and back to God.
- 2. Trusting God to meet your needs.
- 3. Believing that Jesus Christ died for your sins, and that His sacrifice makes salvation possible.
Is there something preventing you from receiving eternal life today?
Will you allow eternal life to be yours today?
This message will help you understand what it means to accept Jesus Christ into your life.
YOU CAN ACCEPT JESUS TODAY IF YOU WANT TO
God wants to go where you are and to address your concerns. Today you can decide to accept Jesus Christ and invite Him into your life through prayer.
"Pray to Jesus Christ and tell Him that you are a sinner. Believe that He died for your sins and rose again. Invite Him to take control of your life and forgive your sins. Pray, trusting that He will answer your prayers. He will forgive your sins and give you eternal life. Amen." Amen
What will you do with this message today?
If you want to, pray now and accept Jesus into your life.
WHAT HELPS YOU KNOW THAT JESUS IS IN YOUR LIFE
How will you know if Jesus has come into your life? Believe it! Read John 3:20, Jesus says He comes into your life, can you trust Him? Understand that God knows your heart. God shows us everything we need to know about forgiveness and reconciliation.
JESUS GIVES ETERNAL LIFE
"And this is the testimony: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life, and whoever does not have the Son of God does not have eternal life. I write this so that you may know that you have eternal life, if you believe in the name of the Son of God." (1 John 5:11-13)
Tell God that you believe that Jesus lives in your life. And through prayer, remember that He is always with you (Matthew 28:20). And receive eternal life.
I WILL DO WHAT MY HEART TELLS ME
Our lives can be filled with pain and suffering, but they can also be filled with joy. See, even now, Jesus is alive in your life.
The foundation of a building is strong and provides support for the walls.
- God's people are those who lead us to righteousness.
- We connect with God's people through prayer.
- If we seek God, our hearts and minds will be renewed.
- Let us draw near to God and His Word, which is the source of renewal and hope.
Therefore, let my eyes look to those who are faithful to God through prayer.
WHAT JESUS DOES FOR YOU
Here are some things Jesus does for you:
- Jesus lives in your life. (John 3:20)
- He redeemed you. (Colossians 1:14)
- He makes you children of God. (John 1:12)
- He helps you understand the mind of God in your life. (II Corinthians 5:14,15,17)
Will you allow Him to continue doing these things in your life?
Will you tell God what you want from Him?
Let us strengthen our faith by praising God and telling Him what we desire.
LET US TELL GOD WHAT WE WANT FROM HIM
WHAT CAN HINDER GROWTH
But if you struggle to grow, continue to walk in the light of eternal life, and remember these things every day:
- Have fellowship with God. (John 15:17)
- Study God's Word. (Acts 17:11)
- Obey God in all things. (John 14:21)
- Follow Jesus in your words and deeds. (Matthew 4:19)
- Walk with God in all things in the light of your life. (Psalm 5:7)
- Allow the Holy Spirit to dwell within you and fill you with power in your daily life and in spreading the Gospel of God. (Galatians 5:16-18, Acts 1:8)
THE FRUIT OF THE CHRISTIAN LIFE TOGETHER
The Bible teaches us to love each other. (Hebrews 10:25) We need encouragement. A large tree needs many branches, and just as one branch doesn't make up the whole tree, neither can one person do everything alone.
Note this, growth in Christian life is unique. It is something that happens when you associate with other people who are committed to knowing Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord.
Go now and join fellow Christians who also seek to live according to the Bible and who strive to grow in the things Jesus Christ teaches them.

text:
No kwĩthĩwa weewie ĩũlũ wa Nthĩ Nzaũ kana Valatiso! Ve mavuku monanasya kũndũ kũseo kũla andũ matonya kũthi kũtembea na kwĩtanĩthya, na nĩmatumaa andũ menda kũthi 'kũndũ kũu kũseo' maketanĩthye na mayũlwa nĩ mathĩna. Ĩndĩ o tondũ twĩsĩ, andũ asu masyoka mũsyĩ, maendeeaa kwĩkala o ũndũ manekalaa tene.
O na vailyĩ ũu, andũ nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ kwĩkala nthĩ nzeo na mbanake. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi twĩkũlasya-ĩ, 'Yo nthĩ nzaũ na mbanake nĩ kĩndũ kya w'o kana no ũndũ wa kũsũanĩa? Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, nĩkĩ andũ mendeeaw'a mũno nĩ kwĩkala nthĩ nzeo na mbanake? Na nĩvatonyeka ĩkesa kwĩthĩwa vo?'
WONI WA ANDŨ ĨŨLŨ WA VALATISO, KANA NTHĨ NZEO
Myaka maana maingĩ mĩvĩtu, andũ nĩmendeeaw'a nĩ nthĩ nzeo na mbanake. Andũ aingĩ nĩmendeeiw'e nĩ ũndũ ũsu kumana na ndeto ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ iwetete "mũũnda ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa syũa, nthĩnĩ wa Eteni." Nĩkĩ mũũnda ũsu waĩ wa kwendeesya? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Yeova Ngai amesya mũthanganĩ kĩla mũtĩ wendeeasya kwoneka, na mũseo wa kũya." Mũũnda ũsu waĩ wa kwendeesya na waĩ vandũ vaseo va kwĩkala. Na ũndũ ũla wa kwendeesya vyũ nĩ kana mũũndanĩ ũsu katĩ vaĩ "mũtĩ wa thayũ."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:8, 9.
Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩlyo nĩyĩwetete mbũsĩ inya syumĩte mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. Mbũsĩ ilĩ katĩ wa isu nĩsyĩsĩkĩe ũmũnthĩ, nasyo nĩ Itekeli na Euvalati. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:10-14) Mbũsĩ isu ilĩ itwaĩte kĩw'ũ mwandanĩ wa Persian Gulf syĩsĩlĩte Iraq, ĩla tene yaĩ kĩsio kya Velisia.
Kwoou ti ũsengy'o kwasya ekali ma Velisia methĩĩtwe mayendeew'a kwa ĩvinda yĩasa nĩ kwĩkala yĩ nthĩ nzeo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũkeka ũmwe wa Velisia wa myakanĩ ya 1501-1600, ũla wĩ Philadelphia Museum of Art, ĩla yĩ Pennsylvania, U.S.A., wonanasya mũũnda wiĩĩwe na ũkũta wĩ na mĩtĩ na malaa manake. Ndeto "mũũnda wiĩĩwe na ũkũta" kwa kĩthyomo kya Velisia yonanasya "valatiso" kana nthĩ nzeo, namo mavisa ala me mũkekanĩ ũsu mailyĩ ta mũũnda mwanake wa Eteni ũla ũeleetw'e Mbivilianĩ.
Kwa w'o, ngewa sya valatiso nieawa mũno ithyomonĩ na syĩthĩonĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩla andũ maendeeie kũthamĩĩa isionĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, maendaa na ngewa itavw'anene vyũ na ĩla ya mbee, na ĩtina wa myaka maana maingĩ, nĩmavulanilye ngewa isu na mĩĩkĩĩo na mbano ila syaumĩlaa kĩsionĩ kĩla mathi. O na ũmũnthĩ, andũ nĩmakothaa kũelesya kũndũ kũla kwanake mũno ta valatiso.
KĨTHITO KYA MŨNDŨ KYA KŨMANTHA NTHĨ NZEO
Andũ amwe ala maendaa kũthũima kũndũ maasyaa kana nĩmonete valatiso ĩla yaaie. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũnene wa ita wa Britain, Charles Gordon, athi kũtembea Seychelles mwaka wa 1881, nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ wanake wa Vallée de Mai, kĩsio kĩla kĩtalawa ta kĩmwe katĩ wa isio ila nzeo vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ (World Heritage site), nginya eeta kĩsio kĩu mũũnda wa Eteni. O na mwakanĩ wa 1492, Christopher Columbus wa Italy, ũla waĩ mũtembei wa kũndũ kũasa (navigator), asũanĩĩa kana aĩ vakuvĩ kũmanya vala mũũnda wa Eteni waĩ avika kĩthamanĩ kya Hispaniola, kĩla ũmũnthĩ kĩtawa Dominican Republic na Haiti.
Ĩvuku yĩtawa Mapping Paradise, yĩ mevu sya tene mbee wa 190, na mbingĩ syasyo syonanĩtye Atamu na Eva me mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. Ĩmwe ya mevu isu nĩ mevu ĩtesĩkĩe mũno yĩ ĩvukunĩ ya mũndũũme weetawa Beatus, kuma Liébana. Ĩvuku yĩu yaandĩkiwe myaka ta 800 mĩvĩtu. Ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya mevu ĩsu ve kasandũkũ, na katĩkatĩ wako ve nthĩ mbanake. Na ve mbũsĩ inya syumĩte vau nasyo nĩ "Itekeli," "Euvalati," "Indus," na "Yolotani," na kĩla ũmwe wasyo wĩsĩlĩte ngalĩkonĩ yaw'o wĩ w'oka kasandũkũnĩ kau. Noĩthwa ũu ũyonany'a ũndũ Ũklĩsto wanyaĩĩkie itulunĩ inya sya nthĩ. Maũndũ asu meonany'a kana o na kau vala Valatiso ya mbee yaĩ vayĩsĩkĩe, andũ mayaaũlwa nĩ valatiso na nĩmasũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wayo.
Mũandĩki wa voemu sya Kĩsũngũ wĩtawa John Milton, ũla wasyaiwe myaka mbee wa 400 mĩvĩtu, nĩwĩsĩkĩe nũndũ wa kũandĩka voemu yĩtawa Paradise Lost, ĩla yumanĩte na ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩĩlyo yĩla yĩeleetye naĩ ĩla Atamu weekie na ũndũ walũngilw'e Eteni. Voemunĩ ĩsu, nĩwaeleisye watho ũla andũ mathĩtwe wa kũkwata ĩngĩ thayũ ũtathela vaa nthĩ. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩvindanĩ yĩu nthĩ ĩkatw'ĩka valatiso." Ĩtina, Milton nĩwaandĩkie voemu ĩngĩ yeetawa Paradise Regained.
ANDŨ NĨMAALYŨLILE MAWONI MOO
Kwa w'o, kuma tene andũ nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ kũmanya kana kwaĩ valatiso ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na yaa. Kwoou nĩkĩ ũmũnthĩ andũ mavũthĩĩasya ũndũ ũsu? Nĩkwĩthĩwa o tondũ ĩvuku Mapping Paradise yonanĩtye, "asomi ma maũndũ ma ndĩni . . . nĩmaekie vyũ kwendeew'a nĩ kũmanya vala valatiso yaĩ."
Andũ aingĩ ala maendaa kanisanĩ mamanyĩaw'a kana wĩkalo woo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte wĩ ĩtunĩ, ĩndĩ ti ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzeo na mbanakavye. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 37:29: 'Ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makatũa vo kũvika tene na tene.' Nũndũ nthĩ ũmũnthĩ ti valatiso, twĩsĩ ata kana watho ũsu ũkeanĩa? *
ŨĨKĨĨTHYO WA KANA NTHĨ YONTHE ĨKATW'ĨKĨTHW'A NZAŨ
Yeova Ngai, ũla woombie nthĩ yĩ nzeo, athanĩte kana akamĩtw'ĩkĩthya valatiso ĩngĩ. Akeeka ũu ata? Lilikana kana Yesũ atũmanyĩisye tũvoyae atĩĩ: "Ũsumbĩ waku wũke. Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ o ta kũya ĩtunĩ." (Mathayo 6:10) Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩ silikalĩ ya nthĩ yonthe ĩla ĩkatongoew'a nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto, na ĩkasumbĩka vandũ va mosumbĩ ma andũ. (Ndanieli 2:44) Ungu wa Ũsumbĩ ũsu, kwenda kwa Ngai ĩũlũ wa nthĩ kwĩthĩwa yĩ valatiso kana yĩ nzaũ 'kũkeekĩka.'
Ĩvindanĩ ya tene, mwathani Isaia nĩwaveveeiwe aelesya ũndũ Nthĩ Nzaũ ĩla yathanĩtwe ĩkethĩwa ĩilyĩ. Oonanisye kana nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩsu, mathĩna onthe makathela. (Isaia 11:6-9; 35:5-7; 65:21-23) Wĩkũlw'a wose o ndatĩka nini ũsome mĩsoa ĩsu Mbivilianĩ yaku. Weeka ũu, ũkamanya nesa kĩla Ngai wiĩe ala ewi. Ala makethĩwa ĩvindanĩ yĩu makatanĩa moseo ala Atamu waaisye, namo nĩ kwĩkala nthĩ yĩ nzaũ na kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai.—Ũvuan'yo 21:3.
Nĩkĩ tũte na nzika kana wĩkwatyo wa Nthĩ Nzaũ ti ndoto, ĩndĩ nĩ ũndũ wa w'o? Nũndũ Mbivilia yaitye atĩĩ: "Matu nĩ matu ma Yeova; ĩndĩ nthĩ nũnengete ana ma andũ." Wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala Nthĩ Nzaũ wathaniwe nĩ 'Ngai mbee wa mavinda ma tene tene, nake ndatonya kũneena ũvũngũ.' (Savuli 115:16; Tito 1:2). Ũsu nĩ wĩkwatyo mũseo vyũ Mbivilia ĩtwathĩte, naw'o nĩ kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yĩ nzeo na yĩ mbanake tene na tene!
^ kal. 15 Nĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya kũmanya kana Koran, mũsoa wa 105 kĩlungu kya 21, Al-Anbiya' [Athani], yaĩtye: "Athũkũmi Makwa ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ."

translation:
Don't be like those people who boast about their wealth or possessions! They often deceive others to appear important and attract attention, leading people to say 'their place is higher' while being envied and hated. If we are honest, people usually become arrogant when they have something good, and remain so.
And regarding this matter, people often want to be close to the wealthy and powerful. That's why we ask ourselves, 'Is being with the wealthy and powerful a good thing, or just a way of benefiting?' This question is crucial, because people often desire to be near the wealthy and powerful. And they wonder how to achieve it.
THE VOICE OF PEOPLE IN THE MATTER OF POSSESSIONS OR WEALTH
For many years, people have desired wealth and power. Many are deceived into thinking that possessing things is equivalent to salvation, but the Bible clearly states: "The abundance of riches belonging to a wicked person does not profit him, unlike the wealth of the righteous." Is such an abundance worth pursuing? The Bible answers: "Jehovah God has made everything beautiful in its time, also putting eternity in their hearts, without mankind ever discovering the work that the true God has done from beginning to end." Such an abundance is worthless and will eventually fade away. And the pursuit of it can lead to dissatisfaction—like chasing after wind.—Ecclesiastes 2:8, 9.
Another example is found in Ecclesiastes, which speaks of Solomon's building project. This construction involved skilled workers, including Hiram and Huram. (Ecclesiastes 2:10-14) This construction was located near the Persian Gulf, bordering Iraq, but also included parts of Bahrain.
Consider how Bahrain's pearls were valued by ancient travelers because they were considered very precious. For instance, a Bahraini pearl from the period 1501-1600, now housed in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, in Pennsylvania, U.S.A., is described as being "studded with gold and adorned with trees and flowers." The phrase "studded with gold" when referring to Bahraini pearls signifies "beauty," while other features of this particular piece resemble the wealth of Solomon mentioned in the Bible.
Thus, the value of beauty lies in its association with artistry and skill. But people often focus on superficial aspects of beauty, becoming obsessed with appearances, and over many years, they exhaust themselves trying to attain perfection and satisfaction. And ultimately, people find it difficult to be satisfied with what they already possess.
THE KEY TO FINDING TRUE HAPPINESS
Some people continue searching for something better or believe beauty exists elsewhere. For example, British officer Charles Gordon, during his visit to Seychelles in 1881, was captivated by the Valley de Mai, a unique place considered one of the most beautiful places in the world (World Heritage site), which reminded him of the Garden of Eden. And in 1492, Italian explorer Christopher Columbus, while sailing across the ocean, believed he had discovered the Garden of Eden when he arrived at Hispaniola, which today comprises the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
The book titled Mapping Paradise, published around 1900, suggests Adam and Eve were located in the Garden of Eden. One of the oldest illustrations is an illustration from the work of a monk named Beatus, from Liébana. This book was written about 800 years ago. The maps in this book are very detailed, and some have names of islands. They include names like "Itekeli," "Euvalati," "Indus," and "Yolotani," each having its own legend explaining its location on the map. It is said that this story shows how Christians understood their world. Some suggest that the stories about the Garden of Eden influenced those who searched for paradise and inspired them to explore the world.
The author of the Kikuyu version, John Milton, who lived about 400 years ago, wrote the poem called Paradise Lost, which is related to the biblical story of Adam and his fall from grace in Eden. In this poem, he describes the reason why people often struggle to overcome evil. He says: "This first sin brought ruin." Later, Milton also wrote another poem called Paradise Regained.
PEOPLE ARE SEARCHING FOR MEANING
For others, the question of whether there is a real paradise in the world remains. Why do people continue to search for this thing? Perhaps because the book Mapping Paradise states, "reading these things... makes one want to know where paradise is."
Many people go to church hoping to find out if the kingdom will ever be restored, if there will truly be a paradise on earth. Psalm 37:29 in the Bible says: 'The righteous will inherit the earth, and they will live forever.' But does this mean that paradise is certain, or just a hope? *
WILL ALL THE EARTH EVER BE PARADISE?
Jehovah God, who created the earth, has allowed us to hope for a future paradise. Will he make it happen? Consider what Jesus taught us when he said: "Your Kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven." (Matthew 6:10) This Kingdom is the only hope for all the earth, and it will bring blessings to obedient people. (Daniel 2:44) Through this Kingdom, God's will for the earth will be fulfilled, and it will become a true paradise—'restored.'
In time, Isaiah foretold how the earth would be transformed into a beautiful paradise. He described a time when humans and animals would live together peacefully. (Isaiah 11:6-9; 35:5-7; 65:21-23) We can look forward to living in that paradise, and we can learn more about it from the Bible. By doing so, you will get to know God better. Those who live in that paradise will enjoy life fully, unlike imperfect Adam and his descendants, and they will have a close relationship with God.—Revelation 21:3.
But do we have proof that God's promise of paradise is genuine, or is it just wishful thinking? The Bible states: "The heavens belong to Jehovah, but he has given the earth to mankind." Living in paradise will be a gift from 'God, the Creator of all things,' and he wants us to benefit from it. (Psalm 115:16; Titus 1:2). This is a wonderful prospect that the Bible offers, and it means living forever on a beautiful earth!
^ par. 15 The Quran also expresses this hope, as Surah 21, verse 105, of chapter 21, Al-Anbiya' [The Prophets], states: "We have promised the righteous ones that the earth will be theirs."

text:
WAKYUMWA ũmwe kwakya mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1520, ekali ma taoni yĩtawa Meaux, ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ na Paris, mayaaĩkĩĩa ũndũ ũla meewie ĩkanisanĩ. Meewie Mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo masomwa na kĩthyomo kyoo kya French vandũ va Kĩlatinĩ kĩla matwĩe mew'aa!
Mũndũ ũla wambĩĩisye wĩa ũsu eetawa Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples, (Kĩlatinĩ nĩ, Jacobus Faber Stapulensis), na aandĩkĩie mũnyanyae amwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Ndwĩsa kũĩkĩĩa ũndũ Ngai ũtetheesye [andũ] ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ kuma kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o makwate Ndeto yake."
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu, Ĩkanisa ya Katholeki na asomi angĩ ma Mbivilia ala maĩ Paris mayendaa andũ masome Mbivilia na kĩthyomo kyoo. Kwoou, nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Lefèvre aalyũla Mbivilia kwa kĩthyomo kya French? Na eekie ata nĩ kana atetheesye andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ maelewe Ndeto ya Ngai?
NĨWENDAA KŨMANYA MAANDĨKO NESA
Lefèvre atanambĩĩa wĩa wa kũalyũla Mbivilia, nĩwaĩ eeyumisye atũngĩĩe momanyĩsyo ma andũ ma tene vamwe na momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni kwosana na ũndũ kwaandĩkĩtwe mavukunĩ ma tene. Nĩwamanyie kana ve kũndũ maandĩko ma Mbivilia ma tene maĩ mavĩndũiwe nũndũ wa mavĩtyo ala meekĩtwe nĩ aalyũli. Nĩ kana akwate ũw'o ũla waĩ maandĩkonĩ ma Mbivilia ma tene, nĩwambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya kwa ũliku Mbivilia ya Kĩlatinĩ ĩla yatũmĩawa nĩ Ĩkanisa ya Katholeki yĩtawa Vulgate.
Kĩthito kyake kya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kyatumie amanya kana "kwĩmanyĩsya ũw'o wa Ngai kwĩ kw'oka nĩkũetae . . . ũtanu mwingĩ mũno." Kwoou, Lefèvre nĩwaekie kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli amanye kũla momanyĩsyo ma andũ maumie na eeyumya vyũ wĩanĩ wa kũalyũla Mbivilia.
Mwaka wa 1509, Lefèvre nĩwaumisye ĩvuku yaeleetye mavuku atano ma Savuli * ala maandĩkĩtwe kwa Kĩlatinĩ, na nĩwaumisye ĩvuku yĩla weekĩte moalyũku ya Vulgate. Kĩvathũkany'o na asomi aingĩ ma ndĩni ma ĩvinda yĩu, nĩweeyumĩtye kũelesya Mbivilia kwa nzĩa ĩkũeleeka nesa. Nzĩa yake ya kũelesya Maandĩko nĩyatetheeisye asomi angĩ ma Mbivilia na andũ angĩ ala maetie moalyũku nthĩnĩ wa ĩkanisa.—Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Ũndũ Martin Luther Watetheeiw'e Nĩ Wĩa wa Lefèvre."
Nũndũ Lefèvre asyaiwe e Mũkatholeki, nĩweesĩ nesa kana nĩ kenda momanyĩsyo ma ĩkanisa ala maĩle matũngĩĩwe, no nginya andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ makamanyĩw'a Maandĩko matheu ũndũ vaĩle. Ĩndĩ andũ asu mesaa kũtetheka ata nĩ Maandĩko matheu, na ĩvinda yĩu Maandĩko maingĩ makwatĩkanaa kwa Kĩlatinĩ?
MBIVILIA YAĨ ĨTONYA KŨKWATĨKANA NĨ KĨLA MŨNDŨ
Nũndũ Lefèvre nĩwendete Ndeto ya Ngai mũno, nĩwatw'ĩte kũĩkĩĩthya kana andũ aingĩ nĩmamĩkwata. Na nĩ kana mũvango ũsu wake wĩanĩe, Mwei wa 6, 1523, nĩwatumbĩthisye tũvuku twĩlĩ tũnini twaĩ tũtonya kwĩanĩa mũvukonĩ wa ĩkoti twa Mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo kwa kĩthyomo kya French. Tũvuku tũu twathooaw'a nusu ya mbesa ila mũndũ watũmĩaa kũthooa Mbivilia, na ũu nĩwatumie andũ aingĩ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ methĩwa na Mbivilia.
Andũ aingĩ maĩ na mea ma kũsoma ndeto sya Yesũ na kĩthyomo kyoo, na nĩkyo kĩtumi mathooie tũvuku twa mbee 1,200 twathela ĩtina wa myei mĩvũthũ. Ũndũ ũsu woonanisye kana andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ nĩmatanie ĩla Mbivilia ĩsu yaumiw'e.
AĨ NA ŨKŨMBAŨ WA KŨTETEA MBIVILIA
Nthĩnĩ wa ndeto sya kwambĩĩa sya mavuku asu ana ma Ũvoo Mũseo, Lefèvre nĩwaeleisye kana aalyũlĩte Maandĩko asu kwa kĩthyomo kya French nĩ kana "andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ" ala mookaa ĩkanisanĩ "methĩwe mesĩ nesa ũw'o wa Mbivilia o ta ala meethĩawa nayo kwa Kĩlatinĩ." Nĩkĩ Lefèvre waĩ na wendi mwingĩ wa kũtetheesya andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ memanyĩsye momanyĩsyo ma w'o ma Mbivilia?
Lefèvre nĩweesĩ nesa ũndũ momanyĩsyo na mĩao ya andũ yaanangĩte Kanisa wa Katholeki. (Maliko 7:7; Akolosai 2:8) Na nĩweesĩ nesa ki kana ĩvinda yaĩ yĩnavika Ũvoo Mũseo "ũtavanw'e ũndũ vaĩle ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, na nĩ kana andũ maeke kwaw'a nĩ momanyĩsyo na mĩao ya andũ."
O na ĩngĩ, Lefèvre nĩwaendeeie kũvuany'a ate kũkĩa mawoni mathũku ma andũ ala matendaa Mbivilia ĩyĩalyũlwa kwa kĩthyomo kya French. Ayĩelesya ĩũlũ wa wangangany'o ũla andũ asu maĩ naw'o aisye atĩĩ: "Makamanyĩsya [andũ] ata kũkwataa mĩao yonthe ĩla Yesũ Klĩsto weeyĩaĩie [Aklĩsto] ethĩwa maikwenda andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ maisoma Ũvoo Mũseo wa Ngai kwa kĩthyomo kyoo?"—Alomi 10:14.
Kwoou ti ũndũ wa kũsengy'a kũmanya kana asomi ma Mbivilia ala maĩ University of Paris, ĩla yeetawa Sorbonne, nĩmendaa kũmũvindĩthya Lefèvre vyũ. Mwei wa 8, 1523, asomi asu nĩmaleanile na kũalyũla Mbivilia na kũandĩka mavuku maeleetye ĩũlũ wa Maandĩko matheu, nũndũ maasya kana kwĩka ũu "nĩkũkwananga Ĩkanisa." Takethĩwa mũsumbĩ wa France ũla weetawa King Francis I, ndaalikĩlĩĩla ũndũ ũsu, Lefèvre ethĩwa asilĩilwe ta mũlei.
LEFÈVRE NĨWESIE KŨMINA KŨALYŨLA MBIVILIA
Lefèvre ndaaĩtĩkĩlya ngananĩo ĩũlũ wa wĩa wake imũsiĩĩe kũalyũla Mbivilia. Mwaka wa 1524, ĩtina wa kũmina kũalyũla Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki (Ũtianĩo Mweũ), Lefèvre nĩwaumisye ĩvuku ya Savuli kwa kĩthyomo kya French nĩ kana Aklĩsto methĩwe matonya kũmũvoya Ngai "kuma ngoonĩ na me na kĩthito kingĩ."
Asomi ma Mbivilia ala maĩ Sorbonne nĩmoosie ĩtambya ya mĩtũkĩ kũsoma mavuku ala Lefèvre waalyũlĩte, o na kau maisoma mayaĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, nĩmaumisye mwĩao andũ maikasome Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ala maalyũlĩtwe nĩ Lefèvre, na nĩmaleanile na mavuku angĩ ala waandĩkĩte mayasya kana mavuku asu "makwataa mbau momanyĩsyo ma Luther." Ĩla asomi asu meeie Lefèvre aĩkĩĩthye kana mawoni make nĩ ma w'o, avangie "kũkilya" na atoloka athi Strasbourg. E kũu nĩwaendeeie kũalyũla Mbivilia. O na kau andũ amwe masũanĩaa kana Lefèvre athamie nũndũ wa wia, we aĩkĩaa kana ũndũ ũla wa ũĩ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kũema kũkananĩa na andũ ala matoonaa ũw'o wa Mbivilia ta 'lũlũ.'—Mathayo 7:6.
Vakuvĩ mwaka ũmwe ĩtina wa athama, ũla mũsumbĩ weetawa King Francis I nĩwamũnyuvie Lefèvre ethĩwe e mwalimũ wa kamwana kake kala keetawa Charles kaĩ na myaka ĩna. Wĩa ũsu Lefèvre wanengiwe nĩwatumie ethĩwa na ĩvinda yingĩ ya kũmina wĩa wake wa kũalyũla Mbivilia. Mwakanĩ wa 1530, Emperor Charles V * nĩwaumisye mwĩao Mbivilia nima ĩla Lefèvre waalyũlĩte ĩtumbĩthĩw'e taoninĩ yĩtawa Antwerp.
LEFÈVRE AĨ NA WĨKWATYO MŨLŨMU, ĨNDĨ ŨYAAĨANĨA
Thayũnĩ wake w'onthe, Lefèvre eekwatasya kana ĩkanisa yĩkatia momanyĩsyo ma andũ na yĩisyokea momanyĩsyo ma w'o ala me Maandĩkonĩ. Nĩwaĩkĩĩe vyũ kana "kĩla Mũklĩsto e na ũthasyo, na kĩanda kya kũsoma na kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia e we mwene." Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi waĩ na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũĩkĩĩthya kana kĩla mũndũ e na Mbivilia. O na kau wendi wake wa kwona ĩkanisa ĩyĩka moalyũku ala maĩle ndwaaĩanĩa, vaiĩ mũndũ wĩsa kũlea kana Lefèvre nĩwatetheeisye andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ mamanya Ndeto ya Ngai. ▪
^ kal. 8 Ĩvuku ya Fivefold Psalter yaanĩtye ĩvuku ya Savuli kũndũ kũtano na yaĩ na kyati kyaĩ na masyĩtwa ma ũnene ma Ngai, vamwe na ila nthoo inya sya Kĩevelania syĩtawa Tetragrammaton sya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai.
^ kal. 21 Ĩtina wa myaka ĩtano, mwakanĩ wa 1535, mũalyũli wa kĩthyomo kya French wĩtawa Olivétan nĩwaumisye Mbivilia ĩla waalyũlĩte atũmĩĩte ithyomo sya tene ila syatũmĩĩtwe kũandĩka Mbivilia. Aialyũla Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki, nĩwatũmĩie mũno maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe nĩ Lefèvre.
