translation:
One was born around the year 1520, in the town of Meaux, though he lived near Paris, seeking to understand something important. These commentaries on the Psalms were read with great enthusiasm by French and Latin scholars alike!
The author of this work was called Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples, (in Latin, Jacobus Faber Stapulensis), and he wrote briefly stating: "I desire to help those of the lower class to understand God's decree [people] so they can embrace His will."
Because of this, the Catholic Church and other biblical scholars in Paris opposed people reading the Bible in their own language. Why, then, did this encourage Lefèvre to translate the Bible into French? And could it be that he helped those of the lower class understand God's will?
I WANT TO KNOW THE TEXTS BETTER
Lefèvre stated that when translating the Bible, he relied on the opinions of ancient authors as well as the opinions of modern ones concerning what was written in ancient books. He realized that some texts in ancient Bibles had been changed by certain scribes who altered them. If he found such a passage in an ancient Bible, he would compare it to the Latin Bible used by the Catholic Church, called the Vulgate.
His effort to compare Bibles led him to realize that "to interpret God's word incorrectly is… very dangerous." Therefore, Lefèvre set out to carefully examine both ancient and modern opinions and to clarify the difficulties involved in translating the Bible.
In 1509, Lefèvre published a book containing five commentaries on Samuel—written in Latin—and he published another book that criticized the Vulgate. Despite opposition from many scholars of his time, he continued to strive to translate the Bible in a more accurate way. His method of translating the Scriptures influenced other Bible students and others who sought a deeper understanding of church teachings.—See the box "What Martin Luther Got From Lefèvre."
Although Lefèvre remained a Catholic, he dared to question church traditions, and he wanted people of all social classes to have access to the Scriptures themselves so they could learn for themselves. Why did some people feel it necessary to hide the Scriptures from the masses, and why were many Scriptures available only in Latin?
THE BIBLE SHOULD BE UNDERSTOOD BY EVERYONE
Lefèvre boldly faced opposition, and he feared that many would misunderstand. But on May 6, 1523, he published two large volumes that contained a new translation of the Psalms from the original Hebrew into French. These books cost about half a year's wages, but they enabled people to have a Bible, and this helped many common people become acquainted with the Bible.
Many people desired to read God's Word and understand its message, and that is why 1,200 copies sold out quickly. This demonstrated that people of all social classes wanted the Bible that was made available.
COURAGE TO DEFEND THE BIBLE
In view of the controversy surrounding the translations of the New Testament, Lefèvre explained that he had translated the Scriptures into French so that "the common people"—or those who did not know Latin—"might be able to understand the Bible itself or at least compare it with the Latin version." Did Lefèvre have good reason to help people of all social classes gain a better understanding of Bible truths?
Lefèvre was right to challenge man-made traditions that conflicted with God's Word. (Mark 7:7; Colossians 2:8) And he was right to say that the scholars at the Sorbonne were "afraid to let the truth reach the ears of the people, and they want people to be satisfied with their own interpretations."
Moreover, Lefèvre endeavored to discern whether the views of others were in harmony with what the Bible actually taught in French. He expressed his concern in these words: "How can [people] expect to grasp all things unless Jesus Christ himself is proclaimed [Christ] to the common people who study God's Word in their own language?"—Romans 10:14.
However, the faculty members at the University of Paris, known as the Sorbonne, decided to investigate Lefèvre further. On August 8, 1523, these scholars condemned his translation of the Bible and his writing of books that contained erroneous teachings, accusing him of undermining "the Church." The king of France, Francis I, took an interest in the matter, and Lefèvre was spared severe punishment.
LEFÈVRE WAS RIGHT TO CHALLENGE THE BIBLE TRANSLATIONS
Lefèvre faced opposition from some of his contemporaries because of his desire to translate the Bible. In 1524, under pressure to refrain from translating the Scriptures into the vernacular (common language), Lefèvre published a commentary on Paul's letter in French, stating that Christ deserved to be understood by people "with heart and mind."
Scholars at the Sorbonne examined Lefèvre's commentaries, and some found fault with them. Under pressure from the authorities, they ordered that copies of the Greek Scripture translations made by Lefèvre be burned, and they condemned other writings of his as containing "Lutheran errors." But these scholars allowed Lefèvre to recant his views, sending him away to Strasbourg. There he continued to translate the Bible. Some also accused Lefèvre of being biased, while he maintained that his purpose was simply to help people understand the meaning of the Bible without relying on those who misrepresented it as 'pearls.'—Matthew 7:6.
After about a year in exile, King Francis I appointed Lefèvre as tutor to his son, later known as Charles, who was only ten years old. As a result, Lefèvre was given ample opportunity and resources to continue his work of translating the Bible. In 1530, Emperor Charles V authorized the printing of the Bible, including Lefèvre's translation, in the city of Antwerp.
LEFÈVRE HAD A STRONG DESIRE, A DESIRE WORTH HAVING
Throughout his life, Lefèvre believed that the church obscured the truth from the people and revealed its own interpretations of the Scriptures. He insisted that "every Christian should have access to the Scriptures, and the ability to read and understand the Bible for himself." This conviction motivated him to strive to ensure that everyone had a Bible. However, some feared that allowing the church to interpret the scriptures would lead to disagreement, and they accused Lefèvre of misleading ordinary people and leading them astray from the knowledge of God. ▪
^ footnote 8 The fivefold Psalter contained the book of Psalms five times, each time with different notes and commentaries on the majesty of God, along with this sacred name of the Hebrews called Tetragrammaton, the proper name of God.
^ footnote 21 After five years, in 1535, a French translator named Olivétan published the Bible based on Lefèvre's translation using a new version that had not previously been used to write the Bible. Translating the Greek texts, he utilized various sources that were also used by Lefèvre.

text:
Andũ makwatawa nĩ mathĩna me kĩvathũkany'o. Ũw'o nĩ kana tũyĩsa kũelesya mathĩna onthe ala makwataa andũ nthĩnĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ, ĩndĩ ekai tũneenee kwa ũliku ngelekany'o inya ila tũwetie mwambĩĩonĩ wa ĩkaseti yĩĩ. Sisya wone ũndũ andũ amwe makwatĩtwe nĩ mathĩna me kĩvathũkany'o, na ũndũ Ngai wamakiakiisye.
ĨLA WAVUTWA KANA WAMANTHA WĨA WAA
Mũndũũme wĩtawa Seth * aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtwavutiwe wĩa ĩvinda yĩmwe." Ongeleele kwasya atĩĩ: "Kwa myaka ĩlĩ, twatetheeaw'a nĩ andũ ala angĩ na kũthũkũma ivalũa. Na nũndũ wa mathĩna asu, kĩveti kyakwa Priscilla, nĩkyakwatiwe nĩ kĩmako kingĩ mũno na kyeew'aa kĩkw'ĩte ngoo vyũ, nakwa naĩ neemenie vyũ."
"Nĩ kyaũ kyatũtetheeisye kũmĩĩsya? Kĩla ĩvinda Priscilla nĩwalilikanaa ndeto sya Yesũ ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo 6:34. Ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu Yesũ oonanasya kana tũyaĩle kwĩmakĩa ũndũ wa ũnĩ, nũndũ ũnĩ ũkeethĩwa na mawĩmakĩo maw'o. Kũvoya kuma ngoonĩ nĩkwamũtetheeisye Priscilla aendeee kwĩyũmĩĩsya. Nakwa nĩnakwatie ũkiakisyo kuma ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 55:22. O ta mũandĩki ũsu wa Savuli, nĩnamwaũĩie Yeova mathĩna makwa na kwa w'o nĩwandetheeisye. O na kau yu nĩnakwatie wĩa, nĩtũtataa mũno tũikethĩwe na malĩ mbingĩ, o tondũ Yesũ waumisye ũtao ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 6:20-22. Na ũndũ ũla wa vata mũno nĩ kana nĩtũmũthengeee Yeova kwĩ ũndũ vailyĩ mbeenĩ, na ngwatanĩo yakwa na kĩveti kyakwa nĩ ndũmu."
Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Jonathan aĩtye atĩĩ: "Naseng'aa tũkeeka ata ĩtina wa kũthelelwa na kũvinga viasala yitũ." Aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Nũndũ wa mathĩna ma mbesa ala makwatie nthĩ yitũ, mbesa ila twathũkũmĩe myaka 20 syanyw'ie kĩw'ũ. Nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa twambĩĩie kũemanĩwa mbesa. Tũyaĩ tũtonya kũtũmĩa kaati yitũ ya kũthooa syĩndũ nũndũ twoona ta ĩtetĩkĩlwa."
Jonathan aielesya kĩla kyamatetheeisye aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndeto ya Ngai na veva wake nĩsyatũtetheeisye kwĩka motwi maseo. Nĩneemanyĩisye kana ndyaĩle kũsakũaa wĩa, na nĩtwaekie kũthooa syĩndũ ite sya lasima. Na nũndũ twĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, nĩtwatethaw'a nĩ ala angĩ tũthaithaa ĩmwe. Nĩmatumie tũeka kwĩvũthya na nĩmatũtetheeasya mavindanĩ ala tũtaĩ mbee na ĩtina."
ĨLA ANDŨ MATWAANĨTE MATAANĨSYA
Mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Raquel aĩtye atĩĩ: "Naũmĩie ngoo mũno ĩla mũemewa wandiie." Aendeee na kwasya atĩĩ: "Nĩnakwatiwe nĩ kyeva kingĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ nĩnamũthengeeie Ngai, na angiakisya. Ĩla namũvoya Ngai kĩla mũthenya new'aa mũuo wake wasũvĩa ngoo yakwa, na ndyĩw'a ngoo yakwa yausya."
Aĩtye ũũ aielesya kĩla kyamũtethisye: "Mbivilia nĩyandetheeisye naeka kwĩthĩwa na ũthatu ngoonĩ, na kwĩw'a ndyenda kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya. Nĩnatetheeiw'e nĩ ndeto ii sya mũtũmwa Vaulo syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 12:21: 'Mũikakĩlw'e vinya nĩ ũthũku, ĩndĩ kĩlyai ũthũku vinya na ũseo.'"
Aendeee na kwasya: "Ve mũnyanya wambonisye ũndũ ndonya kũeka kwĩmakĩa na ndiendeea na maũndũ ala makwa. Ambonisye ĩandĩko ya Mũtavan'ya 3:6 na andavya kana ve ĩvinda mũndũ wĩthĩawa aĩle kwĩtĩkĩla 'kwasya' kĩla waĩ nakyo. Ũtao ũsu waĩ mũito ĩndĩ nĩwambaĩle. Yu nĩ na mĩvango ĩngĩ nĩvangĩĩe kwĩanĩsya."
Mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Elizabeth aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩla andũ matwaanĩte mathasya mũtwaano, mũndũ ũla watiwa nĩwendaa kũkiakiw'a." Aendeee na kwasya atĩĩ: "Naĩ na mũnyanyawa wandetheeasya kĩla ĩvinda. Nĩwaĩaa nakwa, akangiakisya, na nĩwatumaa nĩw'a nĩ wa vata vandũ va kwĩthĩwa nĩmenete. Nĩnĩsĩ nesa vyũ kana Yeova atũmĩie mũnyanyawa ũsu kũndetheesya nĩw'e nesa."
ĨLA TWAWAA KANA TWAKŨA
Mũndũũme wĩtawa Luis, ũla ũwetiwe kĩlungunĩ kya mbee, ethĩawa na ũwau wa ngoo, na ve mavinda elĩ waĩ vakuvĩ vyũ kũkw'a. Yu ekalaa ekĩĩtwe nzeve masaa 16 kwa mũthenya. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩmũvoyaa Yeova kĩla ĩvinda." Aendeee na kwasya atĩĩ: "Na ĩla namũvoya Ngai, nĩnĩw'aa veva wake wambĩkĩa vinya. Mboya nĩtumaa nĩendeea kwĩyũmĩĩsya nũndũ nĩnĩmũĩkĩĩaa Ngai na nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana nũnthĩnĩkĩaa."
Nake Petra, ũla wĩ na myaka 80 na kĩndũ aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩw'aa ndyenda mũno kũtethya maũndũ maingĩ, ĩndĩ vaitonyeka." Aendeee na kwasya: "Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwona nĩendeee na kũthela vinya. Nĩw'aa nĩ mũnou vyũ na nĩkalaw'a nĩ ndawa. Mavinda maingĩ nĩnĩsũanĩaa ũndũ Yesũ weeie Ĩthe wake kana ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka amũvetangĩe thĩna ũla waĩ mbee wake. O ũndũ Yeova wamũnengie Yesũ vinya eyũmĩĩsye, now'o ũnengae vinya nĩyũmĩĩsye. Ĩla navoya kĩla mũthenya nĩw'aa nakwata vinya. Nĩnĩw'aa kavaanga ĩtina wa kũneena na Ngai."—Mathayo 26:39.
Julian, ũla wĩthĩĩtwe na ũwau wa kũanda na kũma kwa mamutha ma mwĩĩ (multiple sclerosis) kwa ĩvinda ya myaka vakuvĩ 30 ew'aa o ta Petra. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Naĩ wĩanĩ mũseo mũno ĩndĩ yu vai ũndũ nĩyĩka nũndũ nĩthĩawa kĩvĩlanĩ kya kũsukumwa. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩnĩw'aa nĩ mwĩanĩe nũndũ nĩnĩyumĩtye kũtetheesya andũ angĩ. Kũtetheesya ala angĩ nĩkũolangaa mathĩna makwa, na Yeova nĩwĩanĩasya watho wake wa kũmbĩkĩa vinya ĩla nĩ na mathĩna. O ta mũtũmwa Vaulo no nasye kana vate nzika: 'Nĩndonya maũndũ onthe nthĩnĩ wake ũla ũndonyethasya.'"—Avilivi 4:13.
ĨLA TWAKW'ĨĨWA
Antonio aililikana maũndũ ala meekĩkie aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndyaaĩkĩĩa ĩla neewie kana ĩthe wakwa nũkongiwe nĩ ngalĩ akw'a." Aendeee kwasya: "Noonie ũndũ ũsu ũtaaĩle kwĩkĩka nũndũ ĩthe wakwa akongiwe esĩle ũtee wa nzĩa. Ĩndĩ ndyaĩ ũndũ naĩ nĩka. Ekalile sivitalĩ mĩthenya ĩtano ate kwĩyĩw'a ayĩsa kũkw'a. No natataa ndikaĩe mami ambene, ĩndĩ ĩla nĩ weka naĩaa mũno vyũ, na ndyĩkũlya, 'Nĩkĩ? nĩkĩ ũndũ ũũ wĩthĩiwe?'"
Antonio ayĩelesya kĩla kyamũtetheeisye aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mavindanĩ asu onthe naĩ na kyeva kingĩ ndyaaeka kũmũvoya Yeova andetheesye nĩyũmĩĩsye na ndyĩthĩwa na mũuo. Na o ũndũ ĩvinda yaendeee na kũvĩta now'o naendeee kũkwata mũuo wa kĩlĩko. Nĩnalilikanile kana Mbivilia yaĩtye kana vai mũndũ ũtakwatwa nĩ 'ĩvuso' kana ũndũ ũtataĩĩwe. Nũndũ Ngai ndesa kũkengana, nĩnĩsĩ nesa ki kana ngoona ĩthe wakwa ũthayũũkyonĩ."—Mũtavan'ya 9:11; Yoana 11:25; Tito 1:2.
O nake Robert, ũla ũwetiwe kĩlungunĩ kya mbee, e o na mawoni ta ma Antonio. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa, nĩtweethĩiwe na mũuo wa kĩlĩko ũla ũwetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Avilivi 4:6, 7. Twakwatie mũuo ũsu ĩla twavoyie Yeova. Mũuo ũsu nĩwatumie tũtavya atangaasi ma maũvoo ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo wa ũthayũũkyo ũla twĩ naw'o. O na kau kĩmwana kitũ nĩkyakw'ĩĩe mũisyonĩ ũsu wa ndeke, nĩtũlilikanaa maũndũ maingĩ maseo ala tweekaa ĩmwe. Maũndũ asu maseo nĩmo tũtataa kũsũanĩaa mũno."
Aendeee na kwasya atĩĩ: "Ĩla Ngũsĩ ila ingĩ syoonie tũielesya ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo witũ nthĩnĩ wa televiseni tũuĩtye, twameie kana vate nzika ũndũ ũsu wĩkĩkie nũndũ wa mboya mbingĩ ila syaumiw'e kwondũ witũ. Kwa w'o nĩnĩsĩ nesa vyũ kana Yeova atũmĩie Ngũsĩ isu kũtũtetheesya nũndũ nĩmatũtũmĩaa mesengyi mbingĩ sya kũtwĩkĩa vinya."
O tondũ ngelekany'o isu syĩkwonany'a, Ngai no akiakisye andũ me na mathĩna me kĩvathũkany'o. Nao nata ĩũlũ waku, nũkwona ta ũtonya kũũkiakisya? O na wakwatwa nĩ thĩna ũilyĩ ata, no ũkwate ũkiakisyo mavindanĩ asu wĩ na thĩna. * Kwoou Yeova no aũtetheesye nũndũ nĩwe "Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe."—2 Akolintho 1:3.

translation:
People who stumble are often foolish. This is because we tend to judge people based on their appearance, forgetting that we ourselves are also imperfect and need forgiveness from others. So don't think you are better than anyone else, but rather be humble and ask for mercy like everyone else. Indeed some people who stumble are foolish, and this is what God allows.
BUT YOU ARE FALLING OR DYING NOW
One man named Seth * said: "My life has been saved from death." He continued saying: "For years, we have suffered with other people and struggled with poverty. And because of foolishness, my wife Priscilla, was captured by a great evil spirit and she began to act strangely, and I did not understand why."
"Is this what has happened to us? Every time Priscilla acted against the teachings of Jesus but only according to Matthew 6:34. For Jesus taught us not to worry about material things, which are temporary. To encourage her, Priscilla continued to focus on spiritual matters. And I found comfort in Psalm 55:22. Oh, the psalmist David, I entrusted my worries to Jehovah and he comforted me. Oh, and just like him, we can entrust our burdens to God, because Jesus commanded in Matthew 6:20-22. And that matter of trusting completely in Jehovah to handle everything, and my life and my family are safe."
One brother named Jonathan said: "Let us seek to avoid being influenced and led astray by false religions." He went on to say: "Because of past mistakes, we have suffered much, but for over 20 years we have been living in truth. With your permission, let us remind ourselves of the past. Let us learn from our experiences so that we do not repeat the same mistake."
Jonathan explained how he had felt, saying: "The law of God and his commandments have been forgotten. I realize that I may have stumbled, and I am determined to correct my mistakes. And since we are servants of Jehovah, we will be united with others who are loyal. Let us strive to preach and let us strengthen each other so that we can remain steadfast."
BUT MANY PEOPLE ARE BEING DECEIVED
One sister named Raquel said: "I am saddened by the bad influence that surrounds me." She continued, explaining: "I was affected by a strong feeling. At first, I prayed to God, and he helped me. But I felt that God was testing me with this difficult situation, and I gave him my problem."
She added, explaining how she had felt: "I realized that I needed to overcome my fear and deal with the negative influence, and I wanted to find comfort. I was encouraged by the words of the apostle Paul found at Romans 12:21: 'Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.'"
She went on to explain: "A publisher showed me something that helped me to see things clearly and made me feel better. He showed me the scripture at Proverbs 3:6 and explained that when a person truly seeks guidance, he should always listen to counsel. That advice really touched my heart. Yes, there are many ways in which we can get help."
Another sister named Elizabeth said: "But those who have been disappointed often lose their zeal, and the person who is discouraged wants to give up." She continued, explaining: "I also had moments when I felt overwhelmed. I prayed to him, and he helped me, and I kept serving despite the difficulties I faced. I am convinced that Jehovah uses our brothers to encourage us and to strengthen us."
BUT WE CAN KEEP GOING
A brother named Luis, who has served as an elder, struggled with feelings of inadequacy, and he sometimes wondered if he was qualified to serve. He would often spend about 16 hours a day thinking about it. He said: "I feel that I need to pray to Jehovah every day." He continued, saying: "And although I pray to God, I still feel unworthy. However, I realize that if I continue to humble myself before God and remain steadfast, he will use me."
Also, Sister Petra, who is 80 years old, said: "I have experienced many trials, but they have never caused me to stop." She went on to say: "The most important thing is to keep praying. I always feel strengthened and comforted. On many occasions, I have meditated on what Jesus did when he was facing his death, how he prayed fervently to his Father. And I know that Jehovah heard Jesus' prayers and answered them, so he will hear and answer mine too. But I pray every day that I may continue to be strong. I feel that I can endure because of my close relationship with God."—Matthew 26:39.
Julian, a brother who has been battling multiple sclerosis for over 30 years, feels similarly to Petra. He says: "At times, I feel very weak and think that I won't be able to cope. But even then, I try to focus on helping others. Helping others gives me strength, and Jehovah strengthens me to deal with my difficulties. The apostle Paul also expressed this sentiment when he said: 'I can do all things through him who strengthens me.'"—Philippians 4:13.
BUT WE HAVE FOUND THAT
Antonio shared some experiences that moved him deeply, saying: "I realized that whether something happens to us or to someone we love, it affects us all." He continued: "Sometimes, we may not understand why something bad happens to us. But I believe that there is a reason. It took five days of intense prayer before I found comfort. I kept asking myself, 'Why? Why is this happening?'"
Antonio reflected on how his faith helped him, saying: "Many times, I have felt that I needed help to trust that Jehovah cares and that he will support me. And yet, time and again, I have seen that he does. I used to think that the Bible was just stories about people who were not affected by 'suffering' or difficult situations. But I have come to realize that God allows trials so that we can demonstrate our faith."—Job 9:11; John 11:25; Titus 1:2.
Robert, who works as an elder, shares similar feelings to those of Antonio. He says: "I have often been comforted by the promise found in Philippians 4:6, 7. We need to rely on Jehovah for strength. That strength helps us to face the challenges of life and maintain our hope. Even young ones can experience this comfort, and we can learn from their examples. Many of them show remarkable resilience."
He adds: "When my wife and I first started watching television programs, we sometimes wondered if they would affect our thinking. However, we realized that we could choose what we watch and limit our exposure to things that might be harmful. In fact, I am convinced that Jehovah helps us to make wise choices when we ask him for guidance."
Since each of us faces unique trials, God understands our emotions. So why should we hesitate to ask for his help? And if you are struggling with a painful emotion, remember that you can find comfort in prayer. * Trust in Jehovah, and he will strengthen you—'the God of all comfort.'—2 Corinthians 1:3.

text:
Naĩ na myaka 17, na nathĩnĩkĩaa maũndũ o ala andũ aingĩ ma mũika mathĩnĩkĩaa. Nĩnendete kwĩthĩwa vamwe na anyanyawa, kũthambĩa, na kũthaũka mũvĩla wa maaũ. Ĩndĩ, mũthenya ũmwe thayũ wakwa nĩwaalyũkile ĩveny'a na ĩsalukya. Mũthenya ũsu nĩnavalũkile na kamota na naũmĩa mũno vyũ, nonza mamutha kuma ngingo nginya maaũ. Maũndũ asu onthe meekĩkie myaka ta 30 mĩvĩtu, na nĩthĩĩtwe ndauma kĩtandanĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa.
Neanĩie Alicante, Spain, taoni yĩ ũtee wa ũkanga ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa syũa. Andũ ma mũsyĩ witũ mayekalanasya nesa na kwoou natũmĩaa ĩvinda yingĩ ndyanganga sokonĩ. Vakuvĩ na vala nekalaa vaĩ nduka ya kũlia taili. Ndukanĩ ĩsu nĩvo namanyanĩie na José María, ũmwe wa ala mathũkũmaa vau. Aĩ mũnyanyawa mũseo, ũla watumaa nĩw'a nĩ mwĩanĩe kĩvathũkany'o na ũndũ neew'aa nĩ kwitũ. Nũndũ aĩ mũnyanyawa vyũ, eethĩawa ailyĩ ta mwana-a-inyia wakwa mavinda ala neethĩawa nĩkw'ĩte ngoo, o na kau aĩ mũkũũ mbee wakwa na myaka 20.
José María aĩ anambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Nĩnoonaa endete Maandĩko na mavinda maingĩ nĩwandavasya ũw'o wa Mbivilia. Nĩnamwĩthukĩĩasya nesa vyũ, ĩndĩ ndyendeeaw'a nĩ maũndũ ala wandavasya. O na kau naĩ o wa mũika, neethĩawa nĩkwatene mũno. Ĩndĩ maũndũ nĩmaalyũkile o mĩtũkĩ.
MŨISYO ŨLA WAALYŨLILE THAYŨ WAKWA
Ndyendaa kũea ngewa mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa mũisyo ũsu wangwatĩie lelũnĩ. Ĩndĩ ndonya kwasya kana naĩ mũtumanu na ndyatwaĩte kamota kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte. Thayũ wakwa waalyũkile vyũ na mũthenya ũmwe. Naĩ kĩmwana kĩ na vinya, ĩndĩ ĩveny'a na ĩsalukya naĩ mwonzu vyũ, nĩkomete sivitalĩ ndekũna ngi itho. Waĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kwĩtĩkĩlana na ũalyũku ũsu mũnene thayũnĩ wakwa. Ĩvinda yonthe nekalaa ndyĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Yo ve vata wa kwĩthĩwa nĩ thayũ?'
José María nĩwookie kũnzisya, na o kwa mĩtũkĩ avanga Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kuma kĩkundinĩ kĩla kyaĩ vakuvĩ syũke kũmbona sivitalĩ. Kũnthokea kwoo nĩkwangiitie ngoo mũno. Naumw'a vala vasũvĩĩawa ala awau mũno (intensive care unit) nĩnambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Nĩnamanyie nĩkĩ andũ mathĩnaa na maikw'a, na nĩkĩ Ngai ũekaa maũndũ mathũku mekĩke. O na nĩneemanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa mawatho ma Ngai ma ĩvinda yũkĩte nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩla ĩkausũwa nĩ andũ mate na naĩ vate ũmwe ũkwasya, "Nyie nĩ mũwau." (Isaia 33:24) Nĩnambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũseo thayũnĩ wakwa.
Naumw'a sivitalĩ, nĩnaendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kĩthito. O na nĩnaendaa maũmbanonĩ amwe ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na kũtavany'a vamwe namo ndũmĩĩte kĩvĩla kya ndĩa. Mwei wa 11, Matukũ 5, 1988, nĩ na myaka 20, nĩnavatisĩiwe kalaĩnĩ kanene ka kũthambĩa (bathtub). Yeova Ngai nũndetheesye kwĩthĩwa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa thayũ wakwa. Ĩndĩ naĩ ndonya kũtũnga mũvea ata?
NĨNĨENDEEE KŨMŨTHŨKŨMA YEOVA O NA KAU NĨ MWONZU
Nĩnatw'ĩte vyũ kũlea kwĩtĩkĩlya wonzu wakwa ũnziĩĩe kũmũthũkũma Yeova ũndũ ndonya. Nĩnendaa kwĩka maendeeo. (1 Timotheo 4:15) Mbeenĩ, ũsu ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwakwa nũndũ andũ ma mũsyĩ mayaaendeew'a nĩ mũĩkĩĩo wakwa. Ĩndĩ naĩ na eĩtu-a-asa na ana-a-asa Aklĩsto. Nĩmandetheeasya mũno kũtavany'a na kĩthito na kũthi maũmbanonĩ onthe.
Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda, yaĩ no nginya nĩkale nĩ ungu wa ũsũvĩo wa mwanya kĩla ĩvinda. Ĩtina wa kũmantha kwa ĩvinda ĩasa, nĩnakwatie vandũ vaseo vasũvĩĩawa ala matetonya, taoninĩ ya Valencia, ĩla yĩ maili 100 (kĩlomita 160), ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya Alicante. Ũsu nĩw'o ũtũo wakwa.
O na kau ndyuma kĩtandanĩ, nĩnĩtw'ĩte kũendeea kũtavya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wakwa
O na kau ndyaĩ numa kĩtandanĩ, nĩnatw'ĩte kũendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova. Nĩnathooie kombiũta na mbesa ila inengawe andũ ala matetonya. Kombiũta ĩsu yaiiwe vakuvĩ na kĩtanda kyakwa. O na nĩnathooie simũ wa kw'oko. Na kĩla kwakya, mũsũvĩi wakwa nĩwe wangwatĩasya kombiũta na simũ yakwa. Nĩ kana nĩtũmĩe kombiũta ĩsu, ndũmĩaa kamasinĩ (joystick) nĩtinaa na ngolu. O na ĩngĩ, nĩnĩthĩawa na kamũtĩ ka mwanya kala nĩkwataa na mũnuka. Kamũtĩ kau nĩkandetheeasya kũtina namba nthĩnĩ wa keyboard na simũnĩ.
Tekinolongyi ĩsu ĩndethetye ata? Ũndũ wa mbee, nĩndetheeasya kũlika Kĩsesenĩ kya jw.org na nthĩnĩ wa LIBRARY INDANETINĨ. Ũsu nĩ ũtethyo mũnene mũno! Mavinda maingĩ nĩnĩtũmĩaa ĩvinda ĩasa ndyĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na ndyĩka ũkunĩkĩli ndũmĩĩte mavuku me na ũvoo kuma Mbivilianĩ, nĩ kana nĩendeee kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Ngai na nguma syake sya ũsengy'o. Na kĩla ĩvinda neew'a nĩkw'ĩte ngoo kana ndyenda kwĩthĩwa na mũndũ vakuvĩ, nĩngwataa ũndũ wa kũmbĩkĩa vinya nthĩnĩ wa Kĩsese kya jw.org.
Ũndũ wa kelĩ, nĩndũmĩaa kombiũta yakwa kwĩthukĩĩsya na kumya maelesyo maũmbanonĩ. Nĩnumasya maũvoo, ngavoya, na ngasoma ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ĩla nanengwa kĩanda kĩu. O na kau nditonya kũvika maũmbanonĩ asu, nĩw'aa nĩ vamwe na kĩkundi kitũ.
Ũndũ wa katatũ nĩ kana nĩndũmĩaa simũ na kombiũta kũtavany'a. Kwa w'o nditonya kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, o tondũ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mbingĩ syĩkaa, ĩndĩ ũu ndũnziĩaa kũtavany'a. Nĩndũmĩaa syĩndũ isu kũelesya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wakwa. O na nĩndanĩaa mũno kũtavany'a ndũmĩĩte simũ, na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi atumĩa ma kĩkundi mangũlilye nĩvangĩthasye kambeini sya kũtavany'a na simũ. Mũno mũno kambeini isu nitetheesye atavany'a ma kĩkundi ala matatonya kuma mũsyĩ makatavany'e.
Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana tekinolongyi yoka nĩyo ĩndetheeasya. Kĩla mũthenya anyanyawa nĩmokaa kũmbona. Mokanasya na andũ moo ma mũsyĩ, na andũ angĩ ala mendeeaw'a nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Mavinda maingĩ nĩmangũlasya ne inyie nĩneenany'e namo. Mavinda angĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ ũmwe nĩmanthokeaa na tũyĩthĩwa na ũthaithi woo wa mũsyĩ vamwe namo. Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno ĩla syana syekala kĩtandanĩ kyakwa na iindavya kĩla kĩtumaa imwenda Yeova.
Nĩnĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na aeni aingĩ. Mavinda maingĩ lumu wakwa wĩthĩawa wusũĩte anyanyawa, amwe maumĩte kũndũ kũasa na angĩ o vakuvĩ. O tondũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũisũanĩa, ũndũ ũsu nũsaanĩasya asũvĩi ma vala nĩthĩawa. Kĩla mũthenya nĩndũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũnenga ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa Aklĩsto aseo.
NO NĨENDEEE KŨKITA
Kĩla ĩvinda mũndũ angethya ayenda kũmanya ũndũ nĩendeee nĩmwĩaa atĩĩ: "Nĩ o vaa nĩendeee kũkita!" Vate nzika nĩnĩsĩ kana ti inyie nyioka nĩ na thĩna ta ũsu. O na ethĩwa twĩ na mathĩna mailyĩ ata, ũw'o nĩ kana Aklĩsto onthe mokitaa "kaũ ũla mũseo wa ũla mũĩkĩĩo." (1 Timotheo 6:12) Nĩ kyaũ kĩndetheesye kũkita kaũ ũsu kwa ĩvinda ĩasa? Nĩvoyaa Yeova kĩla mũthenya na ndimũtũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa kũndetheesya kũelewa vata wa thayũ. Nĩndataa ũndũ ndonya nĩthĩwe na maũndũ maingĩ ma kwĩka ndimũthũkũma Ngai, na nĩnĩsũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.
Mavinda maingĩ nĩnĩsũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ, na ũndũ ngatanĩa ĩngĩ kũsemba na kũtũlĩlanga. Mavinda amwe nĩmbũaa ngũĩ na José María, ũla wĩthĩawa awaĩte volio (polio), ĩũlũ wa ũndũ tũkasemba tũtianĩte. Nĩmũkũlasya-ĩ, "Nũũ ũla ũkasinda?" Nake anzũngĩaa ũũ: "Vai thĩna o na ethĩwa nũũ ũla ũkasinda, ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata nĩkwĩthĩwa Nthĩ Nzaũ nĩ kana twĩsemba."
Ndwĩthĩĩtwe wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwakwa kwĩtĩkĩla kana ndyĩtonya. Nĩnĩsĩ kana ĩla naĩ wa mũika, nĩneekie ũndũ wa ũtumanu, na watuma nĩlika thĩnanĩ mũnene. Ĩndĩ nĩndũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ Yeova ndaandia. Nũnengete ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ, nũtumĩte nĩthĩwa na mea ma kwĩkala thayũ, nĩthĩwa na ũtanu nũndũ wa kũtetheesya andũ angĩ, na akanenga wĩkwatyo mũseo vyũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ngaelya kwĩwa nĩwete o kwa ũkuvĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ nĩw'aa, nasya Yeova nũnengete syĩndũ mbingĩ mbee wa ila nĩ na vata nasyo.

translation:
I am 17 years old, and I experience things like others my age experience. I prefer being with friends, dancing, and enjoying life. Recently, one day at home I woke up feeling strange and uncomfortable. Today I feel better with a car and I don't have much pain anymore, but my teeth still hurt a lot when I eat. These things have been happening for about 30 years now, and I think I need to separate myself from this situation for a while.
I come from Alicante, Spain, a city where the climate is similar to that of a tropical country. The people of our neighborhood usually get along well and we spend a lot of time together doing various activities. They have shops and restaurants where you can find everything you need. This place is where I met José María, one of those young men. He is a good friend, who has made me feel comfortable and welcome here. But he is also a very attractive boy, who makes me want to be more intimate with him, and sometimes I think he feels the same way too, or maybe he is just being nice because he is 20 years older than me.
José María invited me to study the Bible and the teachings of Jehovah. So I started reading the Scriptures and many books explaining his beliefs. I liked it a lot, but I realized that some of the things they taught didn't make sense to me. And even though I tried to understand, I couldn't fully grasp them. That's why I felt confused.
THIS IS HOW THAT DAY FELT
I went to bed thinking a lot about how this situation affected me. But then I wondered if I was crazy and if I had imagined the car accident. That day I felt very bad and uncomfortable, and I cried a lot, but I managed to calm down a little bit. It was as if something big had happened to me that day. All the shops were closed, and I asked myself, 'What will happen to me?'
José María visited me, and he and others from the teachings of Jehovah came to encourage me because they knew I was feeling sick. Because of that, I felt much better. And when they took me to intensive care, they invited me to study the Bible. I remembered that there were many people and families, and I believed that God could do wonderful things. And I also remembered the words of God through Isaiah, which said, "The sick ones you will strengthen." (Isaiah 33:24) They encouraged me to trust in him and to have hope for the future.
And despite being sick, I continued studying the Bible diligently. And I went to some meetings of the teachings of Jehovah and helped others find food. On May 11, 1988, at age 20, I was given a large tub for bathing. Jehovah God strengthened me to survive that difficult time. But did I deserve such help?
I CONTINUED TO THANK JEHOVAH AND ALSO MY FAMILY
I wanted very much to continue showing my gratitude to Jehovah by continuing to thank him. I needed to make progress. (1 Timothy 4:15) However, sometimes it seemed that those who had been doing well were becoming discouraged. I also had ups and downs as a Christian. I appreciate this encouragement to persevere and to continue attending meetings regularly.
During my recovery, I often thought about how I would spend my life. During the last weeks of my recovery, I met many people in the hospital, including those from Valencia, which is about 60 miles (160 kilometers) from Alicante. That's where my family lives.
And now, looking back, I want to continue helping others show their gratitude.
And now, looking back, I wanted to continue thanking Jehovah. I have benefited greatly from the help of others in the hospital. Others helped me get around using a wheelchair. And I benefited from physical therapy. With each session, my physiotherapist showed me how to use the wheelchair and the walker. Sometimes I used both the wheelchair and the walker, controlling them with a joystick and my hands. And also, I practiced moving my arms and legs. This exercise helped me practice pressing buttons and using switches.
Is modern technology helpful? Well, I can access JW.ORG and the ONLINE LIBRARY. That is a great help! Many days I use my tablet to read the Bible and research information so that I can share what I learn with others, and I can also learn more about God and his purposes. And almost every day I try to find something positive, even when I feel down or am visited by someone from the hospital, I focus on finding something encouraging in the material on JW.ORG.
Recently, I have been trying to stay active and receive phone calls. I take notes, pray, and listen to recordings that were made earlier. And even though I cannot visit people personally yet, I work with a group.
Thirdly, sometimes I use the computer and the wheelchair to preach. Because there are many Kingdom Halls of Jehovah, and because this is my assignment, I can preach. I use these tools to help others in my territory. And I really enjoy preaching with the computer, and that is why the circuit overseers have encouraged us to conduct video demonstrations of computer preaching. These demonstrations have helped others in the hospitals to start preaching with computers.
This is not about whether technology itself is bad. Every day people are getting used to it. We associate with many people, and others also want to learn about the Bible. Many experiences encourage us, and we are strengthened by them. Other times, some people get discouraged and we comfort them with their problems. But this is something that helps us to stand firm and always praise Jehovah.
But this is something that happens when many people are involved. Many experiences in our lives happen unexpectedly, some good and others bad. But since you can be involved, this thing will strengthen the faith of those who are being comforted. Every day I thank Jehovah for allowing me to share the good news with his children and Christian brothers.
NO I DO NOT WANT TO GIVE UP
Every time someone faces a challenge, they wonder what they should do and say: "How can I give up?" They may feel weak or think that they no longer have strength. But even though we face many difficulties, this is how Christ fought "a good fight of faith." (1 Timothy 6:12) Why is it important to persevere through challenges in life? Because Jehovah helps us every day and strengthens us so that we can understand his purpose. I realize that many things happen that teach me about God, and I appreciate this precious gift of perseverance.
Many experiences make me value prayer and meditation. Some people like José María, who was affected by polio, taught us a lesson while we were praying together. He asked, "What will happen?" I replied, "Even if something happens, remember that whatever happens is allowed by Holy Spirit, and we pray."
We often find ourselves in situations where we don't know what to do or how to react. We may feel helpless, and our problems seem overwhelming. But I trust that Jehovah will help me. Many brothers and sisters encourage us with their words of comfort, and they show us how to help others, and they also strengthen our faith during difficult times. In fact, I have learned that everything has a reason, and I thank Jehovah for helping me see things from his perspective.

text:
Kwasũanĩa ũtatonya kũsiĩĩa mamutha ma mwĩĩ waku maikeke ũndũ mũna, ate o metho me moka. Ũsu nĩw'o thĩna ũla mwana-a-mwaitũ, Jairo wĩthĩawa naw'o. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nũtanĩaa thayũ. Ndanamba kũelesya kĩla kĩtumaa thayũ wake wĩthĩwa wĩ mũseo, ekai nĩmũelesye ĩũlũ wake.
Jairo asyaiwe e na ũwau mũthemba wa cerebral palsy wĩtawa spastic quadriplegia. * Na nũndũ wa ũu, ndethĩawa atonya kũsiĩĩa mamutha make. Kĩlĩko kyake kĩitonya kũkwatĩanĩa na malangũ, na ũu ũtumaa maaũ make na moko mathĩlĩa. Mavinda amwe nĩwũũmĩaa nũndũ wa kwĩkya moko na maaũ make na mĩtũkĩ. O na andũ ala me vakuvĩ nake no maũmĩe meethĩwa mate metho. Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana moko na maaũ make moveeawa kĩvĩlanĩ kyake kya kũsukumwa nĩ kana ndakaũmĩe na ayĩũmĩsya ala me vakuvĩ.
MATHĨNA ALA MAMŨKWATIE AENDEEE KWĨANA
Jairo eanĩte na thĩna mwingĩ mũno. E na ũkũũ wa myei ĩtatũ, ambĩĩie kũng'athũka ũkethĩa o na ndesa kwĩyĩw'a. Ĩla ũu weekĩka, inyia witũ amũkwataa amũlũmĩtye na aimũsembya sivitalĩ ayona ta mũkw'ũ.
Nũndũ wa mwĩĩ wake kwĩkusĩanĩsya mavĩndĩ make nĩmambĩĩie kwĩkumba. E na myaka 16, nĩwakitũkie ĩvĩndĩ ya kĩnyunyu na ũu watuma athĩnzwa ĩtako, nthũnũ, na kĩnyunyu. O na yu no nĩlilikanaa ũndũ Jairo waalaw'a kĩla ũtukũ ĩla wathĩnziwe.
Ũwau wa Jairo ũtumaa ethĩwa ate ũndũ wĩyĩka. Atetheeaw'a kĩla ũndũnĩ ta kũya, kwĩkĩa ngũa, na kũlĩsa kĩtandanĩ. Mavinda maingĩ atetheeaw'a nĩ asyai maitũ kwĩka maũndũ asu. O na kau kĩla ĩvinda no nginya Jairo atetheew'e nũndũ ndetonya, asyai maitũ mamũlilikanasya kana ndasũvĩawa nĩ andũ me oka ĩndĩ o na Ngai nũmũsũvĩaa.
NĨVAUMĨLILE NZĨA YA KŨEA NGEWA NA JAIRO
Asyai maitũ nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, na methĩĩtwe maisomea Jairo maũndũ ala me Mbivilianĩ kuma e kana kanini. Mavinda onthe nĩmeethĩawa mesĩ kana mũndũ ethĩawa na ũtanu ĩla wĩ na ũnyanya mũseo vamwe na Ngai. Jairo eethĩawa na mwĩĩ mwonzu na moko na maaũ make nĩmeetukaa vakuvĩ kĩla ĩvinda. O na vailyĩ ũu, aĩ atonya kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũseo na mũlũmu wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ĩndĩ asyai maitũ nĩmasaanĩaw'a kana Jairo akesa kũkwata ũmanyi wa Mbivilia.
Mũthenya ũmwe Jairo e kana kanini Tata amwĩie atĩĩ: "Jairo, nĩngũkwĩsũva ũneene nakwa." Ongeleeile kũmwĩa: "Neena nakwa ethĩwa kwaw'o ki nũmbendete!" Ĩla Tata waendeee na kũmwĩsũva amũneeny'e, Jairo nĩwakelemilye methoi. O na kau nĩwatataa kũweta ũndũ weew'aa, aumasya wasya ũte kwĩw'ĩka nesa na ũtekũeleeka. Tata eewie avĩtya mũno nũndũ wa kũtuma Jairo aĩa. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũsu woonanisye kana Jairo nĩwamanyie kĩla Tata wamũkũlilye. Thĩna ũla waĩ vo nĩ kana ndaĩ atonya kũneena.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini, asyai maitũ nĩmamanyie kana mavinda amwe Jairo nĩwavĩndũaa metho make na mĩtũkĩ, aitata kũmony'a kĩla ũkwenda kana ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Ndwaĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya kwa Jairo kũmanya kana ti mavinda onthe andũ maeleawa ũndũ ũkwasya kana kĩla ũkwenda. Ĩndĩ ĩla asyai maitũ meemanyĩisye kũelewa kĩla metho make mekwonany'a na maimũnenga kĩla ũkwenda, ũthyũ wa Jairo nĩwoonanasya kana nĩwatana. Ĩsu yaĩ nzĩa yake ya kwonany'a kana nĩwatũnga mũvea.
Mũndũ mũka ũmwe ũsomeete nzĩa sya kũneena na andũ ala matesĩ kũneena nesa atwĩie kana no tũkĩlasye moko elĩ ĩla tũũmũkũlya ĩkũlyo yĩkwenda ũsũngĩo wa kwonany'a kana nĩwalea, kana nĩweetĩkĩla ũndũ. Kũkĩlya kw'oko kwa aũme kwoonanasya kana nĩweetĩkĩla ũndũ, nakw'o kw'oko kwa aka kwoonanasya kana nĩwalea ũndũ mũna. Kwoou oonanasya kĩla ũkwenda kwa kũketeea mũno kw'oko kũla ũkwenda.
ĨTAMBYA ĨNENE YĨLA JAIRO WOOSIE
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩthĩawa na maũmbano manene katatũ kwa mwaka, ala methĩawa na maũvoo maumĩte Mbivilianĩ kwondũ wa andũ onthe. Kĩla ĩvinda ũvoo kwondũ wa ala mekũvatiswa ũyumw'a, Jairo nĩwatanaa mũno. Mũthenya ũmwe, ĩla Jairo waĩ na myaka 16, Tata amũkũlilye atĩĩ: "Jairo, we nũkwenda kũvatiswa?" Atekwananga ĩvinda aketeeie kw'oko kwa aũme kwa Tata, na ũu woonany'a kana e na wendi wa kũvatiswa. Na ĩndĩ Tata amũkũlya atĩĩ: "Nũmũvoyete Ngai na ũkamwatha kana ũkamũthũkũmaa kũvika tene na tene?" Ĩngĩ Jairo nĩwasyaisye kw'oko kwa aũme kwa Tata. Ũu woonanisye nesa vyũ kana Jairo nĩweeyumĩtye kũmũthũkũma Yeova.
Ĩtina wa kũneenea Mbivilia mavinda maingĩ, Jairo nĩwoonekie aielewa ĩũlũ wa vata wa kũvatiswa. Kwoou, mwakanĩ wa 2004, Jairo nĩwasũngĩie ĩkũlyo yĩ vata ũtaĩ aakũlw'a. Akũlilw'e atĩĩ: "We nĩwĩyumĩtye kũmũthũkũma Ngai na kwĩka kwenda kwake?" Asũngĩie ĩkũlyo yĩu kwa kũsisya ĩũlũ. Ũsu nĩw'o mũvango ũla weekĩtwe wa kwonany'a kana nĩweetĩkĩla. Kwoou nĩwavatisiwe e na myaka 17, na atw'ĩka Ngũsĩ ya Yeova.
AMWĨKWATASYA NGAI MAVINDA ONTHE
Mwakanĩ wa 2011, nzĩa nzaũ ya kũneena nĩyaumĩlile, nayo nĩ kũtũmĩa kombiũta ĩthũkũmaa kwosana na ũndũ mũndũ ũkũveny'a. Nĩ kenda Jairo avingũe syĩndũ ila syĩ kombiũtanĩ ĩsu, avenasya, na ĩ kombiũta ĩisoma ũndũ metho make mekũveny'a. Ĩla waketeea kana wavenesya kombiũta ĩsu wĩthĩaa no ũndũ ũmwe na kũtũmĩa mouse. Kombiũta ĩla Jairo ũtũmĩaa ĩseũvĩtw'e yĩ na tũvisa tũnini tũmũtetheeasya kũneena na andũ. Ĩla wavenesya kavisa kamwe kombiũtanĩ ĩsu, vaumaa wasya ũkwonany'a kĩla ũkwendaa kũweta.
O ũndũ Jairo waendeee kũelewa ũw'o wa Mbivilia, now'o wendi wake wa kũtetheesya andũ kĩ-veva waendeee kwongeleka. Ĩla tũendeee na ũthaithi witũ wa mũsyĩ, mavinda maingĩ Jairo ekasya metho kombiũtanĩ yake na ainzisya. Ĩsu nĩyo nzĩa ĩla ũtũmĩaa kũndilikany'a kana naĩlĩte kũandĩka maũndũ ala ũkasũngĩa nthĩnĩ wa kĩlungu kya makũlyo na mosũngĩo maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto.
Ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ, Jairo atũmĩaa metho make kũmantha kavisa kala ũkwenda. Na ĩndĩ akona aikavenesya, na vayumĩla wasya ũkwĩw'ĩka nĩ kĩla mũndũ. Nĩwĩthĩawa na ũtanu kĩla ĩvinda weekĩa kĩkundi vinya kwa kũsũngĩa. Mũnyanyae wa Jairo wĩtawa Alex aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno ĩla neew'a Jairo asũngĩa twĩ maũmbanonĩ."
O na ĩngĩ, Jairo nũtũmĩaa metho make kũelesya ala angĩ mũĩkĩĩo wake. Nzĩa ĩmwe ĩla ũtũmĩaa nĩ kũvenesya kavisa kamwe nthĩnĩ wa kombiũta yake, na kayonany'a mũũnda mũseo wĩ na nyamũ, na andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe mekalanĩtye na mũuo. Ĩtina wa kũvenesya kavisa kau kombiũtanĩ yake, vaumĩlaa wasya waĩtye atĩĩ: "Wĩkwatyo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩ kana nthĩ yonthe ĩkeethĩwa yĩ nzeo na yĩ nzaũ, kũte mowau na kĩkw'ũ, Ũvuan'yo 21:4." Ũla ũkũtavaw'a ũvoo endeew'a, Jairo aveneasya kavisa kangĩ na vayumĩla wasya ũũkũlya atĩĩ: "We no wende ngũmanyĩsye Mbivilia?" Ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana ĩthe wa inyia witũ nĩweetĩkĩlile kũmanyĩw'a Mbivilia nĩ Jairo. Nĩ ũndũ wa kũtanĩthya kwona Jairo aimanyĩsya ũmae Mbivilia atetheew'e nĩ mwana-a-asa ũngĩ! Ũmae witũ avatisĩiwe ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ, mũsyĩnĩ wa Madrid, Mwei wa 8, 2014.
Kĩthito kya Jairo kya kũmũthũkũma Ngai nĩkyonekaa nĩ alimũ ma sukulu ĩla ũsomeaa. Ũmwe wa alimũ make ũsomeete nzĩa sya kũneena na andũ ala matesĩ kũneena nesa wĩtawa Rosario, aisye atĩĩ: "Ngesa kũsũanĩa kwĩthĩwa nĩ wa ndĩni, nĩtw'ĩka wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Nĩnonete ũndũ mũĩkĩĩo wa Jairo ũmũtetheesye kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũseo, o na kau nĩwĩthĩawa na mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ."
Jairo nĩwĩthĩawa na ũtanu ĩla namũsomea watho ũũ wa Mbivilia: "Nĩvo mũndũ ũthuaa wĩtũlĩla ta ndaatai nũme, na ũĩmĩ wa ũla ũtaneenaa wĩina." (Isaia 35:6) O na kau mavinda amwe Jairo nũtũlĩkaa ngoo, mavinda ala maingĩ ethĩawa e mũtanu. Ekalaa e mũtanu nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na ũnyanya mũseo vamwe na Ngai, na Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Mũĩkĩĩo na ũtanu ũla wĩthĩawa naw'o niĩkĩĩthasya kana kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩkũtumaa mũndũ atanĩa thayũ, o na ethĩwa e na mathĩna maingĩ.
^ kal. 5 Ndeto cerebral palsy (CP) ĩtũmĩawa kwonany'a ũwau wa kĩlĩko ũla ũtumaa moko ma mũndũ malea kũthũkũma ũndũ vaĩle na ũyĩthĩa maaũ maitonya kũtambya. O na ũwau ũsu no ũtume mũndũ ethĩwa na mathĩna ma kũya, mũng'athũko, na kũemwa nĩ kũneena nesa. Mũthemba ũla mũthũku vyũ wa ũwau ũsu nĩ spastic quadriplegia nũndũ no ũtume ngingo yĩthĩwa yĩ ndeelu, na ũyĩthĩa maaũ na moko mayĩsa kũthingitha.

translation:
He struggles to hold food to his mouth, yet he tries with all his might. He is like a small child, Jairo perseveres nonetheless. I see him and understand his situation, I will help him. I remember trying to teach him how to use his hands, but I couldn't fully teach him how.
Jairo was diagnosed with severe cerebral palsy known as spastic quadriplegia. * Despite this, he strives to bring food to his mouth. His body finds it difficult to coordinate with his hands, and this causes food and saliva to spill. Sometimes people try to help him feed himself and others. The act of feeding is often slow and requires patience because his ability to chew is limited and he needs assistance from those around him.
OTHER CHILDREN ALSO STRUGGLE TO EAT
Jairo has a lot of energy. At three years old, he attempts to walk with support. But recently, his mother noticed something different and she suspects there is a problem.
The difficulty with coordinating his movements makes things harder. At 16 years old, he experienced seizures which caused weakness in his legs, trunk, and arms. And sometimes he refuses to accept what Jairo experiences every night when he is weak.
Jairo's condition also affects his speech. He can't say everything he wants to, such as going, eating, and telling stories. Many things he can't say are expressed through his eyes. And often every time someone looks at Jairo, they wonder what he is thinking, expressing their concern or hoping God will help him.
I LEARNED A LOT BY SPENDING TIME WITH JAIRO
His parents are Jehovah's Witnesses, and they taught Jairo many things about the Bible, even though he is very young. Often people think that someone who is sick has lost hope and doesn't have a close relationship with God. Jairo has a strong faith and his heart is touched by his friends every day. And lately, he has been able to express himself more clearly and communicate his feelings during the day. I realized his parents were concerned that Jairo would learn to understand the Bible.
One day, while visiting Tata, he told Jairo: "Jairo, I want to help you." He replied: "Helping me means helping my mother!" But Tata continued to encourage him, and Jairo became very happy. And although he hesitated to accept what was happening, he began to see how important it was and how much it helped. Tata saw the need to help Jairo speak. Because of this, Jairo came to realize how much Tata cared for him. It showed him that he could be helped.
During a recent visit, his parents noticed that some of Jairo's movements were strange and he struggled to control them. They wanted to know if Jairo understood what was happening and whether those movements had a purpose. So his parents asked him to show them what he meant by his movements, trying to understand what he was communicating. The truth about Jairo was revealed – he was imitating. His way of communicating was mimicking.
Someone who studies speech often tells others that speaking well involves being able to express oneself clearly so that people can understand what they mean, whether it's something good or bad. Being able to say things clearly helps people understand what is happening, and being able to explain things helps them learn.
THE BIG QUESTION JAIRO ASKED
Jehovah's Witnesses hold large gatherings three times a year, but sometimes they also have smaller meetings at the Mbiviliani Hall for everyone. Every time there was such a meeting, Jairo would imitate. One day, when Jairo was 16 years old, Tata asked him: "Jairo, do you want to get baptized?" He thought about the question and considered what Tata had said, and he realized he wanted to get baptized. Then Tata asked him: "Will you pray to God and ask Him to continue guiding you forever?" So Jairo decided to talk to his parents about it. This showed how much Jairo appreciated learning to worship Jehovah.
To help people understand the Bible better, Jairo began to research the meaning of baptism. In 2004, Jairo made a decision about baptism. He was asked: "Do you appreciate worshipping God and following His guidance?" He made that decision because he understood its importance. That is why he continued to improve, and he got baptized at age 17 and joined Jehovah's Organization.
SHOW APPRECIATION FOR GOD IN EVERY WAY
In 2011, I started giving speeches, and this helped me to use computers to communicate with people more effectively. I went to Jairo and asked him to teach me how to use computers, and he agreed, and he taught me a lot about computers. But he noticed that some people didn't know how to use a computer and needed help using a mouse. The computer Jairo used was very helpful because it allowed him to communicate with people easily. But when they tried to use the computer, they were afraid to click on anything.
So Jairo continued to learn about the Bible, and his ability to help others improved. But we need to be patient, and Jairo learned a lot from computers and used them often. This is why we use them to remind us and to write down important points during our meetings and conventions.
But through those conventions, Jairo used his skills to help people with technology. And he always offered to help, and he was happy to see everyone succeed. He was also involved in organizing activities for each group. Jairo's friend, Alex, said: "He is a good example of someone who helps others at conventions."
And again, Jairo used his skills to help others with their problems. One way he helped was by fixing a computer problem, and he showed kindness and compassion, and all the brothers appreciated his efforts. After fixing the computer problem, they were happy to say: "The Bible says that everything has its time, both bad times and good times, to enjoy life, Ecclesiastes 3:1." That situation reminded him, and Jairo fixed another computer problem and they were happy to ask: "Did I explain the Bible well?" The effort to help others understand the Bible was something that made us feel grateful to Jairo. It is an opportunity to show how Jairo helps others understand the Bible, like a young man! Our brother was assigned a large responsibility, the office in Madrid, on May 8, 2014.
Jairo's desire to honor God was evident from his school days. One of his classmates who spoke to people about the truth, named Rosario, said: "I remember when I first met him, we talked about Jehovah's Witnesses. I noticed that Jairo's problem touched him deeply, and also many others were affected by it."
Jairo was encouraged by five scriptures during his study of the Bible: "This is what the Almighty will do for us; He will wipe away our tears, and death will be no more." (Isaiah 35:6) And many times Jairo felt very sad, many times those feelings came up during his studies. Being in the ministry brought him closer to God, and to other Christians. His experience with those five scriptures helped him to honor Jehovah and to encourage others, and it happened with many others.
^ p. 5 Cerebral palsy (CP) refers to a group of disorders that affect a person's ability to move and maintain balance and posture. And this disorder can also cause a person to have difficulty speaking, eating, and communicating. The most severe form of this disorder is spastic quadriplegia, which causes all four limbs to become stiff, and makes movement difficult.

text:
Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie kana Yeova "ndakamũeka mũtatwe kũvĩtũka vinya wenyu." (1 Ako. 10:13) Kyo kĩu kĩonany'a kana Yeova ambaa kũthima akamanya kĩla tũtonya kũmĩĩsya na ĩndĩ aitũnyuvĩa matatwa ala meũtũkwata?
Kwasũanĩa thĩna ũla ũtonya kumĩla nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na woni ta ũsu. Ĩla kĩmwana kya mwana-a-asa ũmwe kyeeyũaie, mwana-a-asa ũsu akũlilye atĩĩ: 'Yeova ambie kũthima amanya kana nyie na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtũtonya kũmĩĩsya kwĩyũaa kwa mwana witũ? Ũndũ ũsu wĩkĩkie nũndũ Ngai amanyie nĩtũtonya kũwũmĩĩsya?' Vo ve kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũĩkĩĩa kana Yeova avangĩthasya kaũndũ konthe kala katonya kũtũkwata thayũnĩ witũ?
Twasisya nesanga ndeto sya Vaulo ila iandĩkĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 10:13 tũmanyaa ũndũ ũũ: Vai vandũ Maandĩkonĩ vonanĩtye kana Yeova nĩwambaa kũthima kĩla tũtonya kũmĩĩsya, na ĩndĩ amanya ũu ainyuva nĩ matatwa meva maĩle kũtũkwata. Ekai tũneenee maũndũ ana ala meũtuma tũĩkĩĩa kĩu.
Mbee vyũ, Yeova nĩwanengie andũ mũthĩnzĩo wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Endaa twĩnyuvĩe ithyĩ ene twĩenda kwĩkala mwĩkalĩle ũilyĩ ata. (Kũt. 30:19, 20; Yos. 24:15) Twanyuva kũatĩĩa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte, no twĩkwatye kana Yeova nũkũtongoesya matambya maitũ. (Nth. 16:9) Ĩndĩ twanyuva nzĩa ĩtaĩle, no nginya twĩthĩwe twĩyũmbanĩtye kũketha kĩla twavanda. (Aka. 6:7) Kwoou we wĩona ata? Yeova akatw'ĩka nĩwe ũnyuvaa matatwa ala meũtũkwata, we ndethĩwa aitũvena mũthĩnzĩo ũla ũtũnengete wa kwĩnyuvĩa?
Kelĩ, Yeova ndatũsiĩĩanĩaa na maũndũ ala matũkwataa nũndũ wa "ĩvinda na ĩvuso," kana ũndũ ũtataĩĩwe. (Mũta. 9:11) Mĩisyo, o na ĩmwe mĩthũku mũno, no ĩtũkwate nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa twĩ vandũ vataĩle ĩvinda yĩla yĩtaĩle. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ nĩwawetie mũisyo wakwatie andũ 18 ala makwie nũndũ wa kũtumbwa nĩ nyũmba. Nĩwoonanisye kana kũyaĩ kwenda kwa Ngai andũ asu makw'e. (Luka 13:1-5) We nũkwona ta ũndũ wosanĩte na kĩlĩko kũsũanĩa kana Ngai nĩwĩkalaa avangĩte ala mekwĩkala thayũ na ala meũkw'a ĩla vaumĩla mĩisyo?
Katatũ, kĩla ũmwe witũ nũkonetw'e nĩ kĩla Satani wawetie. Lilikana kana Satani aisye andũ maimũthũkũmaa Yeova nũndũ nĩmamwendete. Aisye makakwatwa nĩ matatwa mayĩsa kwĩkala me aĩkĩĩku kwake. (Yovu 1:9-11; 2:4; Ũvu. 12:10) Wĩsũanĩa ata? Yeova akatũsiĩĩa tũikakwatwe nĩ matatwa amwe aĩ nũndũ eona me maito mũno ũkethĩa tũimatonya, kyu kĩituma Satani oneka ta waneenaa ũw'o ĩla waisye atĩ tũmũthũkũmaa Ngai nĩ kana twĩyĩune?
Kana, ti lasima Yeova akamanya kyonthe kĩla kĩkatũkwata. Kwasya kana Ngai nũnyuvaa matatwa ala meũtũkwata nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya no nginya ethĩwe esĩ kyonthe kĩla kĩ mbee witũ. Ĩndĩ woni ũsu ndwosanĩte na Maandĩko. Vate nzika, Ngai e ũtonyi wa kũmanya maũndũ ma ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte. (Isa. 46:10) Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana nũnyuvaa maũndũ ala ũkwenda kũmanya ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte, na ala ũtekwenda kũmanya. (Mwa. 18:20, 21; 22:12) Kwoou, o na kau we akenda no amanye maũndũ onthe ala mokĩte, vai ĩvinda wĩsaa kũlikĩlĩĩla ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ithyĩ tyo twendaa kũthaitha Ngai ta ũsu ũnengete ndaĩa ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa, na ũla kĩla ĩvinda ũtũmĩaa ũtonyi wake ũndũ vaĩlĩte?—Kũt. 32:4; 2 Ako. 3:17.
Kwoou-ĩ, twaĩle kũelewa ndeto ii sya Vaulo ata: "Ngai . . . ndakamũeka mũtatwe kũvĩtũka vinya wenyu"? Ĩla Vaulo wawetie ndeto isu aeleasya kĩla Yeova wĩkaa ĩla twĩ matatwanĩ ĩndĩ ti tũtambĩte kũkwatwa nĩ matatwa. Ndeto isu sya mũtũmwa Vaulo syĩtũĩkĩĩthya kana twamwĩkwatya Yeova, ndalea kũtũtw'ĩĩka ĩla twakwatwa nĩ matatwa o na ethĩwa nĩ meva. (Sav. 55:22) Ekai twone maũndũ elĩ ala matumie Vaulo aweta ndeto isu syĩ na ũkiakisyo.
Mbee vyũ, matatwa ala matũkwataa no ala "mũndũ ũtonya kũmomĩĩsya." Ũu nĩ kwasya kana tũkwatawa no matatwa o ala methĩĩtwe maikwata andũ kuma tene. Tũkamwĩkwatya Ngai, ve vinya tũkesa kũemwa nĩ kũmĩĩsya matatwa asu. (1 Vet. 5:8, 9) Vaulo atanamba kũweta ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 10:13 awetie ĩũlũ wa matatwa ala makwatie Aisilaeli me weũnĩ. (1 Ako. 10:6-11) Katĩ wa matatwa asu wawetie vai ĩtatwa o na yĩmwe yĩtaĩ yaakwata andũ, kana yaĩ yĩsa kũmaema vyũ kũmĩĩsya. Ĩndĩ Vaulo awetie mavinda ana mĩsoanĩ ĩsu asya kana "amwe moo" nĩmaemie kwĩthĩwa me ewi. Kĩla kyatumie Aisilaeli asu masindwa nĩ mĩmeo mĩthũku nĩ kwĩthĩwa mayaamwĩkwatya Ngai.
Kelĩ, "Ngai e kĩthito," kana nĩ mũĩkĩĩku. Ũvoo ũla ũandĩkĩtwe ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Ngai wĩkalanĩtye na andũ make wonanĩtye nesa kana nĩwonasya "ala mamwendaa na kũkwata mĩao yake" ũseo wake wĩ wendo. (Kũt. 7:9) Ũvoo ũsu nũsyokete ũkonany'a kana kĩla ĩvinda Ngai nĩwĩanĩasya mawatho make. (Yos. 23:14) Kwoou twasũanĩa ũndũ Ngai wĩthĩĩtwe e mũĩkĩĩku, nĩtwonaa kana ala mamwendete na ala mamwĩw'aa no mekwatye vyũ kana ĩla me matatwanĩ, ndakaema kwĩanĩsya maũndũ aa elĩ ũwetete: (1) Ndakaeka tũtatwe nginya tũvikĩĩe vandũ wĩthĩe nĩtwaemwa vyũ nĩ kũmĩĩsya ĩtatwa yĩu, na (2) 'akatũmanthĩa nzĩa ya kũthonoka.'
Yeova amanthĩaa ata ala mamwĩkwatasya nzĩa ya kũthonoka ĩla me matatwanĩ? Yeova no atũvetee ĩtatwa ethĩwa nĩ kwosana na kwenda kwake. Ĩndĩ kwasyoka ũlilikane ndeto sya Vaulo. Aisye: 'Yeova akamantha nzĩa ya kũthonoka, nĩ kana mũtonye kũmomĩĩsya.' Kwoou mavinda maingĩ atũmanthĩaa "nzĩa ya kũthonoka" kwa kũtũnenga kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũvote kũmĩĩsya matatwa. Kwasũanĩa nzĩa ii imwe Yeova ũtonya kũtũmĩa nĩ kana atũmanthĩe nzĩa ya kũthonoka:
We 'nũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe.' (2 Ako. 1:3, 4) Yeova no atũtetheesye tũkausya kĩlĩkonĩ na ngoonĩ atũmĩĩte Ndeto yake, veva wake mũtheu, na lĩu ũla tũnengawe nĩ ĩla ngombo yĩ na kĩthito.—Mt. 24:45; Yoa. 14:16; Alo. 15:4.
Nũtonya kũtũtongoesya atũmĩĩte veva wake mũtheu. (Yoa. 14:26) Ata? Ĩla matatwa mooka, veva ũsu nũtonya kũtũtetheesya kũlilikana ngewa syĩ Mbivilianĩ na myolooto ĩla yĩ vo, na ĩndĩ tũimanya nĩ ĩtambya yĩva ya ũĩ twaĩle kwosa.
Nũtonya kũtũma alaĩka matũtetheesye.—Aevl. 1:14.
No atũmĩe Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Aklĩsto asu no 'matũkiakisye,' kana makatwĩkĩa vinya, kwĩsĩla ndeto syoo na meko moo.—Ako. 4:11.
Kũvikĩa vau tũtonya kwasya ila ndeto sya Vaulo syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 10:13 syonanasya kyaũ? Syonanasya kana Yeova ndanyuvaa matatwa ala meũtũkwata. Ĩndĩ ĩla matatwa mesa kumĩla, no twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu vyũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũũ: Twamwĩkwatya Yeova ndakaaeka matatwa ala matũkwatĩte mavike vandũ wĩthĩe tũyamba kũmomĩĩsya, na kĩla ĩvinda akatũmanthĩaa nzĩa ya kũthonoka nĩ kana tũmomĩĩsye. Vate nzika, ũndũ ũsu nũtwĩkĩaa vinya mũno!

translation:
The apostle Paul wrote that Jehovah "has put his heart to prove what you are thinking." (1 Cor. 10:13) Does this show that Jehovah looks into our hearts and knows exactly what motivates us to act in certain ways?
Considering this, how can we be sure about the sincerity of others toward us? For example, if a child asks his parent, the parent might say: 'Does Jehovah know what you and I are thinking when we consider whether to allow this child to go out?' This question shows that we recognize that God knows whether we are sincere. But does this mean that Jehovah always intervenes whenever we are capable of making wrong decisions ourselves?
Let us examine Paul's words as they appear in the original Greek text of 1 Corinthians 10:13 so that we may understand this better: The original Greek reveals that Jehovah looks into people's hearts to test their thoughts, and he knows who is truly loyal to him. So, let us now consider some things that will help us to understand this.
Truly, Jehovah is gracious to people in view of the imperfection of mankind. Let us therefore continue to appreciate this fact and strive to remain humble. (Prov. 30:19, 20; Josh. 24:15) We are grateful for the way he deals with us, and we trust that Jehovah will guide our steps. (Ps. 16:9) And when we make mistakes, let us humbly ask for forgiveness so that we can improve. (Acts 6:7) What do you think? Jehovah has shown that he is gracious to imperfect humans, so should we not also extend grace to those around us and be understanding?
Certainly, Jehovah is concerned about the things that trouble our hearts, such as "anxiety and worry." (Matt. 9:11) Often, though, we ourselves contribute to our own distress, and we become anxious because of the actions of others. For instance, Jesus spoke of an incident where 18 men were killed when a house collapsed on them. He showed that their death was due to their lack of spiritual discernment. (Luke 13:1-5) Do you see a connection between this account and the need to discern whether God approves of the way people conduct themselves?
Furthermore, each of us is tested in ways similar to how Job was tested. Satan claims that people turn away from Jehovah only because of what he does to them. He alleges that they worship God only for personal gain. (Job 1:9-11; 2:4; Ex. 12:10) Consider this: Does Jehovah allow us to experience trials simply to see if we will abandon him, or does he permit Satan to test our integrity in order to prove that we do not worship God for selfish reasons?
Of course, Jehovah knows everything that happens to us. He understands why we face certain trials, and he also knows what we need. So rely on the Bible. Remember, God has the ability to foreknow events. (Isa. 46:10) The Bible explains why God allows bad things to happen, and it helps us understand his purpose. (Gen. 18:20, 21; 22:12) Yes, God could prevent all suffering, but would that truly be in our best interests? Would it not undermine our faith and trust in him, and would it not deprive us of the opportunity to demonstrate our loyalty?—Prov. 32:4; 2 Cor. 3:17.
Yes, let us consider Paul's words: "God . . . comforted us in all our tribulation"? Actually, Paul wrote those words to assure us that Jehovah cares about our feelings and wants to comfort us when we are troubled. Those words from the apostle Paul remind us that we can draw strength from Jehovah, knowing that he feels for us when we suffer and will help us cope. (Ps. 55:22) Let us now examine some examples of how Paul applied those words and showed empathy.
Truly, the tribulations that trouble us may seem like an "overload." This is because they may be similar to trials others have experienced. We can confide in God, knowing that he understands our suffering and will help us bear it. (1 Pet. 5:8, 9) Paul explained how to apply this principle in his letter of 1 Corinthians 10:13, where he spoke of the tribulations that befell Israel in the wilderness. (1 Cor. 10:6-11) Like those ancient Israelites, we too may face temptations or difficulties that test our faith or make it hard to remain steadfast. Paul also pointed out that there is a limit to what we can endure, saying that "no temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to mankind." What happened to the Israelites in the wilderness shows us that being disloyal to God led to disastrous consequences.
However, "God is impartial." The way he dealt with people in the past demonstrates that he treats everyone fairly and does not show favoritism—"but accepts men who fear him and practice righteousness." (Acts 7:9) Therefore, we can be sure that God will always respect the choices we make. (Josh. 23:14) So when we face trials, we can rest assured that God will give us the strength to endure them, provided we meet two requirements: (1) We must trust that Jehovah cares about us and will help us to cope with our tribulation, and (2) 'we must watch out for ourselves so that we do not fall into sin.'
Does Jehovah really care about those who want to remain faithful during times of difficulty? Yes, he does, and he provides comfort and support. Consider Paul's words: "Jehovah knows how to deliver devout persons out of trial." Many find that "delivering" means giving them the strength to persevere through their difficulties. But sometimes Jehovah delivers us from trouble altogether:
Let 'our hearts be properly disposed.' (2 Cor. 1:3, 4) Jehovah helps us to stay focused on his Kingdom and to use his Word effectively, so that we may continue to serve him faithfully. Sometimes he does this by providing opportunities:
We should 'make full proof of our ministry.' (Prov. 1:3, 4) Jehovah supports us as we preach the good news, and he gives us the privilege of helping others to learn about his purposes, his love, and what the future holds.—Matt. 24:45; John 14:16; Acts 15:4.
He can empower us by his spirit. (John 14:26) In fact, even though tribulations may come, his spirit can strengthen us to remain courageous, like the ancient Christians who faced persecution, and we can be confident that Jehovah will never abandon us.
He can move others to assist us.—Eph. 1:14.
And he uses fellow Christians. These brothers and sisters also 'exert themselves,' often making sacrifices to help us.
How can we show appreciation for such assistance, especially when considering Paul's words at 1 Corinthians 10:13? By remembering that Jehovah cares about each of us individually. If we face trials, let us remember that we are not alone, and let us trust that Jehovah will give us the strength to endure, and whenever he provides an opportunity to prove our faith, let us seize it. Remember, this is a real blessing!

text:
AKLĨSTO ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa nĩmeekĩie kĩthito kingĩ matavye andũ aingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ.' (Mt. 24:14) O na angĩ nĩmaendie kũtavany'a nthĩ ingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwatavanisye mũno kĩsionĩ kĩmwe kĩla ũmũnthĩ kĩtawa Turkey. Ĩvinda yĩu aĩ kyalonĩ kyake kya ũmisonalĩ. * Twĩ mwakanĩ wa 2014, myaka ta 2,000 kuma ĩvinda yĩu ya Vaulo, ve kambeini ya mwanya ya kũtavany'a yeekiwe nthĩ ya Turkey. Nĩkĩ yeekiwe? Naaũ maĩ kambeininĩ ĩsu?
"NĨ KYAŨ KĨENDEEE?"
Nthĩ ya Turkey yĩ andũ milioni 79, namo atavany'a nĩ mbee wa 2,800. Kwoou katĩ wa andũ 28,000 mũtavany'a no ta 1. Kĩu kĩonany'a no andũ avũthũ ala matavĩtw'e ũvoo mũseo nthĩ ĩsu. Kĩla kyatumie kambeini ĩsu ĩvangwa nĩ kana ana-a-asa mendaa andũ aingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka matavw'e ũvoo kwa kavinda kakuvĩ. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ta 550 maneenaa kĩthyomo kya Turkish nĩmaumie nthĩ ingĩ mathi Turkey nĩ kana matavany'e vamwe na atavany'a ma kũu ĩvinda ya kambeini ĩsu. Kwaendie ata?
Ũkũsĩ nĩwaumiw'e kĩsionĩ kĩnene. Kĩkundi kĩmwe kĩ Istanbul kyaandĩkie ũũ: "Andũ matwona makũlasya, 'Ko kwĩ na ũmbano wa mwanya? Kĩla vandũ wasisya no Ngũsĩ sya Yeova!'" Nakyo kĩkundi kĩ taoninĩ ya Izmir kyaandĩkie: "Mũndũ ũmwe wathũkũmaa kwa taxi atumũisye mũtumĩa ũmwe wa kĩkundi wa kũũ amũkũlya, 'Nĩ kyaũ kĩendeee? Mbona mwĩ na kĩthito kingĩ mũtanaĩ nakyo?'" Ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a kana kĩla mũndũ nĩwamanyie ve kambeini ĩendeee.
Atavany'a ala maumĩte nthĩ ingĩ nĩmatanĩie mũno kũtavany'a. Steffen aumĩte Denmark, na aisye: "Kĩla mũthenya nĩnakomanaa na andũ mataaĩw'a ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Kĩu kyatumie nĩw'a kana nĩnatatĩte vyũ kũmanyĩthya andũ ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova." Nake Jean-David, kuma France, aandĩkie: "Nĩngũlilikana ũndũ twaminie masaa maingĩ kasĩlanĩ kamwe tũitavany'a. Twatanĩie ta kĩ! Andũ aingĩ mayeesĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Vakuvĩ kĩla nyũmba nĩtwakitasya mũndũ tũtonya kũneena nake, tũkamwony'a vitio, na tũkamũtiĩa ĩvuku."
Atavany'a asu 550 manenganie mavuku vakuvĩ 60,000 kwa ĩvinda ya syumwa ilĩ tũ! Vate nzika, ũkũsĩ nĩwaumiw'e kĩsionĩ kĩnene.
Atavany'a nĩmathangaaie mũnango. Kambeini ĩsu nĩyathangaaisye ana-a-asa ma Turkey. Aingĩ nĩmambĩĩie kwenda ũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe. O na kwa ĩvinda ya myei 12 ĩtina wa kambeini ĩsu, nĩkwongelekile mavainia ma kĩla ĩvinda 82.
Atavany'a ala maumĩte nthĩ ingĩ nĩmawetie ũndũ kambeini ĩsu yatumie menda ũtavany'a mũno o na ĩtina wa kũsyoka kwoo. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Şirin wa kuma Germany aĩtye: "Ana-a-asa ma Turkey maikĩaa kũtavany'a ĩla me maũndũnĩ moo. Nyie nĩw'aa nthoni mũno kũtavany'a ĩla nĩ maũndũnĩ makwa. Ĩndĩ nũndũ wa kambeini ĩsu, kwona ngelekany'o nzeo ya ana-a-asa ma Turkey, na kũvoya na kĩthito, nĩnakwatie ũkũmbaũ wa kũtavany'a ĩla nĩ maũndũnĩ makwa. O na nĩnatavanisye vandũ vaũngamaa ngalĩ sya mwaki na nanengane tulakiti mbingĩ! Yu ndi na nthoni ila naĩ nasyo."
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Johannes, kuma Germany, aisye: "Nĩneemanyĩisye maũndũ ndonya kwĩka ĩla ngũtavany'a. Ana-a-asa ma Turkey nĩmendete mũno kũtavya andũ aingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka ũla w'o. Maileaa kũtavany'a kĩla ĩvinda vaumĩla mwanya. Nakwa nĩnatwie kwĩka oou nasyoka Germany. Nũndũ wa ũu, yu nĩtavasya andũ aingĩ ũvoo kwĩ ũndũ neekaa."
Nake Zeynep, kuma France, aisye: "Kambeini ĩsu yandethisye mũno naaĩlangya ũtavany'a wakwa. O na nĩyandetheeisye neethĩwa na ũkũmbaũ mwingangĩ na namwĩkwatya Yeova mũnango."
Atavany'a nĩmendanie mũnango. Ngwatanĩo ĩla yaĩ vo katĩ wa ana-a-asa na wendo ũla maĩ naw'o o na kau maĩ ma nthĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, nĩ maũndũ matamba kũla. Jean-David, ũla wawetwa, aisye: "Nĩtweeyĩw'ĩie ũndũ wendo wa ana-a-asa 'ũsamaa.'" O na aisye: "Matwosie ta anyanya vyũ na ta andũ moo ma mũsyĩ. Nĩmatũthokisye kwoo. Nĩneesĩ nĩtwendanĩte o na ethĩwa twĩ ma nthĩ yĩva, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩnasomete kĩu mavinda maingĩ mavukunĩ maitũ. Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu nĩneeyoneie ũndũ ũsu na metho makwa. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'aa ne ndaĩa nene vyũ kwĩthĩwa nĩ ũmwe wa andũ ma Yeova, na nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa mũvea nũndũ wa ndaĩa ĩsu."
O nake Claire, kuma France, aisye ũũ: "Twĩthĩwe twaĩ ma Denmark, France, Germany, kana Turkey, ithyonthe twailyĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ ũmwe. No nasye Ngai nĩ ta woosete kĩvuti akavuta mĩvaka yonthe ĩla ĩsoletwe ya kũaany'a nthĩ isu."
Na ĩndĩ ve Stéphanie, kuma France, ũla waisye atĩĩ: "Kambeini ĩsu ya mwanya yatũmanyĩisye kana ngwatanĩo yitũ yĩ vo nũndũ ithyonthe nĩtũmwendete Yeova, ĩndĩ ti ũndũ wa syĩthĩo kana ithyomo sitũ."
IKUNDI NITETHEKETE MŨNO KŨVIKA O NA ŨMŨNTHĨ
Aingĩ ala maĩ kambeninĩ ĩsu nĩmambĩĩe kũsũanĩa kũthamĩĩa Turkey nĩ kenda matetheesye kũtavany'a nũndũ nthĩ ĩsu yĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Aingĩ moo nĩmosete ĩtambya yĩu. Ana-a-asa nĩmew'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ wa atavany'a asu metũmĩte kĩsionĩ kĩu.
Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kakundi kamwe ke koka vandũ kala kaĩ na atavany'a 25. Kakundi kau kaminĩte myaka ke na mũtumĩa o ũmwe wa kĩkundi. We wĩona atavany'a asu ta meewie mũyo wĩana ata ĩla mwakanĩ wa 2015, atavany'a thanthatũ kuma Germany na Netherlands mathamĩĩie kũu mamatetheesye?
KŨTETHEESYA VALA VE NA VATA MŨNENE WA ATAVANY'A
Ala metũmĩte Turkey maasya ata masũanĩa ĩvinda yĩla mekalĩte kũu? Nĩ w'o kana mavinda amwe maũndũ methĩawa me metu, ĩndĩ nĩmakwatĩte moathimo maingĩ me kĩsionĩ kĩu kĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Kwasisya ũndũ amwe maĩtye:
Mwana-a-asa ũtwaanĩte na wĩ na myaka 40 na kĩndũ wĩtawa Federico, ũla waumie Spain athi Turkey, aisye: "Nĩw'aa kwĩkala nde na syĩndũ mbingĩ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ kũinenga nzeve na nĩkũtumaa nĩtũngĩanĩa kĩlĩko kyakwa maũndũnĩ ala ma vata vyũ." We no ekĩe angĩ vinya meke o take? Easya: "Ĩĩ, vyũ! Ĩla wathamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ nĩ kana ũtetheesye andũ mamũmanye Yeova, wĩthĩawa weenengane mokonĩ make. Ũkwataa mwanya mũseo vyũ wa kwona Yeova aikũsũvĩa."
Mwana-a-asa ũtwaanĩte wĩtawa Rudy, kuma Netherlands, ũla wangĩe myaka 60, aĩtye ũũ: "Kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a na kũtavya ũw'o andũ aingĩ vyũ mataaĩsa kũwĩw'a o na ĩndĩĩ, kũtumaa twĩw'a twĩ eanĩe vyũ. Tũtanaa mũno ĩla twoona ũndũ andũ mekwĩw'a mũyo nũndũ wa kũmanya ũla w'o."
Mwana-a-asa ũtwaanĩte wĩtawa Sascha, kuma Germany, ũla wĩ na myaka 40 na kĩndũ, aĩtye ũũ: "Kĩla ĩvinda nathi kũtavany'a nĩkomanaa na andũ mataaĩw'a ũla w'o. Kũtavya andũ ta asu ĩũlũ wa Yeova kũndeteae ũtanu mwingĩ mũno."
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa mũtwae wĩtawa Atsuko, kuma Japan, ũla wĩ na myaka 30 na kĩndũ, aĩtye ũũ: "Navu ĩtina nĩneekũlasya Ali–Maketoni ĩkavika ĩndĩĩ. Ĩndĩ kuma ĩla nookie Turkey, nĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ nũekete ĩvinda yĩvĩte atanamba kũete mũminũkĩlyo. Kĩla ĩvinda noona ũndũ Yeova ũtongoesye maũndũ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a nthĩ yonthe, nĩw'aa namwenda mũno."
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Alisa, kuma Russia, ũla wĩ na myaka 30 na kĩndũ, easya: "Kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩ ũthũkũminĩ ũũ kũtumĩte nĩsama ngona we nĩ mũseo ki." (Sav. 34:8) Aendeee na kwasya: "Yeova nĩ Asa wakwa, na nĩ Mũnyanyawa mũnene. Kũka kũũ nĩkũtumĩte nĩmũmanya nesanga. Nĩyoneete maũndũ maingĩ mũno maseo na ma kũtanĩthya, na nĩnĩkwatĩte moathimo maingĩ!"
'SISYAI MĨŨNDA'
Andũ aingĩ nthĩ ya Turkey nĩmavikĩĩtwe nĩ ũvoo mũseo nũndũ wa kambeini ĩla yeekiwe kũu. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ve kĩsio kĩnene kĩtatavanĩtw'e. Kĩla mũthenya, atavany'a ala mathamĩĩe Turkey makomanaa na andũ mataaĩw'a ĩũlũ wa Yeova. We no wende kũthamĩĩa vandũ ve na vata mũnene wa atavany'a? Inyw'onthe ala mwĩ na wendi ũsu twĩmwĩa atĩĩ: "Ũngalalyai metho menyu, mũsisye mĩũnda, kana nĩ mĩathĩku kũvika ũkethwa o na yu." (Yoa. 4:35) No wende kũthi kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩmwe katĩ wa ila siilyĩ ta 'mĩũnda mĩathĩku'? Ethĩwa no wende, ambĩĩa kwosa ĩtambya oyu. Weeka ũu, manya atĩĩ: Kwongelanga kĩthito kyaku kya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo "kũvika itulu sya nthĩ," kũkatuma ũkwata moathimo maingĩ ũtamaelekany'a na kĩndũ o na kĩva!—Meko 1:8.
^ kal. 2 Sisya mbulosua 'Ona Nchi Nzuri,' ĩth. 32-33.

translation:
CHRIST's prophecy regarding "the sign of [his] presence" has been fulfilled in a remarkable way among many people when they see 'this generation.' (Matt. 24:14) But how can we know when this generation began? For example, the apostle Paul personally visited Ephesus, a city in what is now Turkey. That visit was part of his missionary work. * In 2014, about 2,000 years after Paul's visit, branches in Turkey held a special campaign to reach people in that land. Was it successful? And what about other countries?
"WHAT WILL HAPPEN NEXT?"
Turkey has 79 million inhabitants, and there are some 2,800 Witnesses. This means that there is approximately 1 Witness for every 28 people. This ratio is similar to that in many other lands where the good news is being preached. What motivates our brothers to keep trying despite facing opposition and sometimes experiencing persecution? Some 550 full-time preachers who speak Turkish have moved to areas of Turkey where there are few Witnesses, so that they can preach to more people. What does the future hold?
There is growing interest. One congregation in Istanbul wrote: "Many people are asking, 'What is happening? Why are Jehovah's Witnesses different?'" Similarly, a congregation in İzmir reported: "A man took a taxi and asked the driver, a member of the congregation, 'What is going on? Why are you so interested in this matter?'" It is clear that people want to know what is happening.
Other Witnesses also find that people are receptive. Steffen, from Denmark, says: "Every day I meet people who are searching for spiritual things. This motivates me to continue helping people learn about Jehovah." Likewise, Jean-David, from France, writes: "I often spend hours engaging in conversations with people during our ministry. We really enjoy it! Many people are accepting Jehovah's Witnesses. Often we call at a home and find someone willing to talk, listen, and accept publications."
These Witnesses, along with 550 others, reached 60,000 people in just one month! As you can see, there is growing interest.
The Witnesses are organizing more activity. Our brothers in Turkey are arranging special assemblies. Many are traveling long distances to attend them. Also, during the past 12 months, the number of congregations has increased to 82.
Other Witnesses also find that their efforts are bringing good results. A sister named Şirin, from Germany, says: "The Turkish brothers are very zealous in their ministry. You too can be zealous in your ministry. As part of our family, seeing the zeal of the Turkish brothers and their positive attitude, I felt encouraged to be more zealous in my ministry. And I have had wonderful experiences sharing with others, and we have made many new friends! I am grateful for this opportunity."
A brother named Johannes, from Germany, says: "I have learned much about how to be effective in the ministry. The Turkish brothers are an example to us in helping many people. They take time to reach out to people who may be interested. I was able to return to Germany after being away for some time. Because of this, I am now helping many people again."
Another sister named Zeynep, from France, says: "Our organization has helped me to remain loyal in my personal ministry. And it has strengthened my faith and my love for Jehovah."
The ministry is rewarding. Although there are challenges when dealing with people and their reactions, and sometimes we feel discouraged, these are minor things. Jean-David, who was mentioned, says: "I appreciate the encouragement the brothers give each other—'keep busy.' " He also says: "We see many people who are troubled and sad. We comfort them. I have come to realize that when we spend time with others, especially when we share our experiences, it can be very helpful. On one occasion, someone really appreciated what I said and told me that because of our conversation, he wanted to learn more about Jehovah, and he asked to be visited by one of Jehovah's Witnesses, and I promised to arrange it."
And another sister named Claire, from France, says: "Whether we are in Denmark, France, Germany, or Turkey, we always meet kind people. I trust that God will help us to cope with all the difficulties we face in preaching the good news."
Also, Stéphanie, from France, said: "Our recent experience has taught us that no matter what happens, we continue to worship Jehovah, regardless of our circumstances."
THE NEED FOR PRACTICAL HELP AND TRAINING
Many of our brothers in this area want to move to Turkey but need practical help to make the move. Some may lack confidence. The brothers are eager to support those who want to move here and are using the congregation as a means of doing so.
Consider the example of one group that helped over 25 publishers. This group worked closely with an experienced brother who was part of the local Kingdom Hall construction team. Have you seen how the publishers in Germany and the Netherlands were encouraged when they received practical help in 2015?
PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO PUBLISHERS WHO WANT TO MOVE
Are there any in our congregation who would like to move to Turkey but are unsure whether they can? Perhaps they feel that they don't have enough skills or resources, but they could benefit from practical assistance and encouragement. Here is one suggestion:
A sister named Federico, a Spanish pioneer serving in Turkey, said: "I was very hesitant because I didn't know anyone and I was afraid of making mistakes. But I decided to trust Jehovah and see what he would do." What did she learn? She explained: "Yes, definitely! Especially when you associate with people who love Jehovah, you will find that they will always encourage you."
Another sister named Rudy, from the Netherlands, who is about 60 years old, stated: "Moving to serve where there is greater need and helping others to get involved has made me happier and more grateful. It has also helped us to stay spiritually strong."
A sister named Sascha, from Germany, who is 40 years old, said: "Every time I help someone move, I meet wonderful people. Helping people to learn about Jehovah has brought me much joy."
A sister named Atsuko, from Japan, who is 30 years old, shared: "I used to be shy, so I practiced giving talks in front of a mirror. After serving in Turkey, I began to trust Jehovah more fully and felt able to speak boldly. Every time I experience Jehovah's support in the ministry, I am deeply moved."
A sister named Alisa, from Russia, who is 30 years old, said: "Trusting in Jehovah is the best decision I have ever made because he is reliable." (Ps. 34:8) Then she added: "Jehovah is my God, and he is the greatest Comforter. He helps me to cope with difficulties and challenges, and he gives me strength!"
'KEEP IMITATING THEM'
Many in Turkey are being reached through the ministry because of the fine example set by the local brothers. They face obstacles, but they persevere. Each month, they help hundreds of people in Turkey learn about Jehovah and his Kingdom. How can we encourage them and show our appreciation for their perseverance? All of us can remember this saying: "Lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they may become ripe for harvesting." (John 4:35) Can we also ask ourselves, 'What specific steps can I take to imitate those zealous ones?' If we do, let us consider how we can apply this counsel: Diligently cultivate your personal study habit so that you will continue to grow spiritually and be able to give a powerful witness.—Acts 1:8.
