text:
Ĩvinda yĩmwe mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Blessing * nĩwaendie Europe athĩtwe wĩa wa kũsuka na kwenza nzw'ĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kũkũnwa kwa ĩvinda ya mĩthenya ĩkũmi na kũtĩsw'a kana mũsyĩ wake nũũvithũkĩwa, nĩwalasimĩthiw'e kũthũkũma ta ĩlwaya.
Ũtukũ ũmwe, Blessing aaĩle kũkwata euros katĩ wa 200 nginya 300 nĩ kana aĩve mbesa ila mũndũ mũka ũla wamũũngamĩe wendaa. Mũndũ mũka ũsu endaa Blessing aĩve euros mbee wa 40,000. * Blessing aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mavinda maingĩ nĩnasũanĩaa kũtoloka, ĩndĩ nĩnakĩaa ndyona ta matonya kũvithũkĩa mũsyĩ wakwa. Vayaĩ ũndũ naĩ nĩka." Ngewa yake nĩyonanĩtye kĩla kĩkwataa andũ ta milioni inya nthĩ yonthe ala me viasalanĩ ya ũmalwaya.
Vakuvĩ myaka 4,000 mĩvĩtu, mwanake weetawa Yosevu nĩwathooiw'e nĩ ana-a-ĩthe. Athoow'a, nĩwatw'ĩkĩthiw'e ngombo mũsyĩnĩ wa mũnene ũmwe nthĩ ya Misili. Kĩvathũkany'o na Blessing, Yosevu ndaathĩnw'a nĩ mũnene wake mbeenĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla wesie kũlea aikoma na kĩveti kya vwana wake, Yosevu nĩwailĩĩlwe ũvũngũ wa kana endaa kũkoma nakyo na vinya. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩwekiw'e yela na oovwa na mĩnyololo ya kĩaa.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 39:1-20; Savuli 105:17, 18.
Yosevu aĩ ngombo tene vyũ, ĩndĩ Blessing atũmĩawa ta ngombo myakanĩ ya 2000 na kĩndũ. Ĩndĩ onthe makwatiwe nĩ ũndũ o ũmwe, naw'o nĩ kũthoow'a ta ngombo. Viasala ũsu wĩthĩĩtwe ũendeee kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mũno, na kĩeleelo kya ala mamathooasya nĩ kũkwata mbesa, ĩndĩ mayĩthĩawa maimendea ũseo.
KAŨ NŨTUMAA ANDŨ AINGĨ MATHOOW'A TA NGOMBO
Kaũ nĩw'o waĩ nzĩa ĩla yĩ laisi vyũ ya nthĩ kũkwata ngombo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mũsumbĩ wa Misili weetawa Thutmose III atw'ĩkĩkanaa ve ĩvinda watavie avungwa 90,000 e kaũnĩ nthĩ ya Kanaani. Avungwa asu mambĩĩie kũthũkũmĩthw'a ta ngombo wĩanĩ wa kwĩnza syĩndũ ta thaavu, kwaka makalũ ma kũthaithĩa, na kwĩnza mĩtaũ ya kĩw'ũ.
O na Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Lomi, kaũ nĩwatumaa ngombo mbingĩ ikwatĩkana, na mavinda amwe ĩla kweethĩwa vata mũnene wa ngombo nĩkwaumĩlaa kaũ. Ũkunĩkĩli wonanĩtye kana myakanĩ ya ĩvinda ya atũmwa, vakuvĩ nusu ya andũ ma nthĩ ya Lomi maĩ ngombo. Ngombo mbingĩ sya Misili na sya Lomi nĩsyathĩnaw'a mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, katĩ wa andũ ala mathũkũmaa ta ngombo kũla kwĩnzawa syĩndũ ta thaavu nthĩ ya Lomi, mũndũ ũla wekala mũno akusaa e na myaka ta 30.
O ũndũ ĩvinda yavĩtĩte, now'o ngombo syaendeeie kũthĩnw'a. Kuma mwaka wa 1500 na kĩndũ nginya myakanĩ ya 1800 na kĩndũ, viasala wa kũthoosya andũ ta ngombo ũla waendeee katĩ wa Africa na Amelika waĩ ũmwe katĩ wa viasala ila syalikasya mbesa mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Livoti ĩmwe ya ngwatanĩo yĩtawa UNESCO yaĩtye ũũ: 'Aũme, aka, na syana ila itonya kwĩthĩwa syathooiw'e ta ngombo nĩ katĩ wa milioni 25 na milioni 30.' Andũ ngili maana maingĩ matw'ĩkĩkanaa nĩmakwie maikĩla ũla ũkanga wĩtawa Atlantic. Mũndũũme wĩtawa Olaudah Equiano, ũla wavonokie ĩvindanĩ yĩu aisye ũũ: "Mbu sya iveti na kũkaya kwa andũ maikw'a, kwatumaa ũndũ ũsu woneka wĩ mũthũku mũno o na ũkethĩa ti laisi kũelesya."
Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana ũndũ ũsu ũthũkĩte ũu wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ ngombo ndwaathela. Kwosana na ũkunĩkĩli ũla wĩkĩtwe nĩ International Labour Organization, o na ũmũnthĩ aũme, aka, na syana milioni ta 21, no mathũkũmaa ta ngombo, mate kũĩvwa kana maiĩvwa o tũvesa tũnini. Ũmũnthĩ ngombo ithũkũmĩthaw'a kũndũ kũla kwĩnzawa syĩndũ ta thaavu, kambunĩnĩ nene sya kũtuma ngũa, kambunĩnĩ sya kũmba mavali, nyũmbanĩ sya kũkũnĩa ũmalwaya, na nyũmbanĩ sya andũ ene. Ũkombo wa mũthemba ũsu ũendeee na kwongeleka mũno, o na kau ũyĩtĩkĩlĩtw'e nĩ mĩao.
KŨTHAW'A KUMA ŨKOMBONĨ
Nũndũ ngombo mbingĩ syĩthĩĩtwe iithĩnw'a mũno, ũu nũtumĩte mbingĩ syasyo syũkitĩa ũthasyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, myaka vakuvĩ 2,100 mĩvĩtu, mũkiti ũmwe weetawa Spartacus e na andũ angĩ vakuvĩ 100,000 ala maĩ ngombo nĩmatatie kũleana na silikalĩ ya Lomi, ĩndĩ mayaatonya. Myakanĩ ya 1701-1800, ngombo ila syaĩ kĩthamanĩ kya Hispaniola kĩla kĩ Caribbean nĩsyambĩĩie kũleana na anene masyo. Ngombo isu syathĩniw'e mũno iithũkũma mĩũndanĩ mĩnene ya kũvanda iwa na kĩu kyookĩlilye kaũ kĩthamanĩ kĩu kwa myaka 13, ũla watumie Haiti yĩsumbĩka kuma mwaka wa 1804.
Ĩndĩ vai kũthaw'a kũngĩ o na kũmwe kwa ngombo kũtonya kũelekanw'a na kũla kweekĩkie ĩla Aisilaeli mathaiw'e kuma ũkombonĩ wa Misili. Mbaĩ yonthe ya Aisilaeli, ĩla ĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yaĩ andũ milioni itatũ, nĩyathaiw'e kuma ũkombonĩ wa Misili. Kwa w'o, Aisilaeli nĩmaaĩlĩte kũthaw'a kuma ũkombonĩ ũsu. Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye ũndũ Amisili mamakũnĩthasya wĩa. Yonanĩtye kana 'ũthũkũminĩ woo w'onthe, mamathũkũmĩthasya na vinya mũno.' (Kuma 1:11-14) Nĩ kana Aisilaeli maikaingĩve mũno, Valao nĩwambĩĩisye mũvango wa kũaa twana tũla tũnini.—Kuma 1:8-22.
Kũthaw'a kwa Aisilaeli kuma ũkombonĩ wa Misili kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ nũndũ Ngai nĩwe woosie ĩtambya amatetheesye kũvonoka. Ngai amwĩie Mose atĩĩ: 'Nũndũ nĩnĩsĩ mathĩna moo; nĩngũtheea ngamavonokye.' (Kuma 3:7, 8) Kũvika ũmũnthĩ, Ayuti kĩla vandũ nĩmatanĩaa Vasaka kĩla mwaka maililikana ũndũ ũsu weekĩkie.—Kuma 12:14.
ŨKOMBO ŨKAVETWA VYŨ
Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana "Yeova Ngai waitũ nde na ũthũku," na ĩkatũĩkĩĩthya kana we ndaalyũkaa. (2 Mavinda 19:7; Malaki 3:6) Ngai nĩwamũtũmie Yesũ "kũtavan'ya ũthasyo kwa ala atave, . . . Na kũthasya ala mavivinyĩtwe." (Luka 4:18) Syo ndeto isu syĩonany'a kana Yesũ atũmĩtwe kũthasya andũ onthe ala matũmĩawa ta ngombo? Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa ũu ti w'o. Yesũ atũmĩtwe ovosye andũ kuma ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. Yesũ esie kwasya atĩĩ: "Ũla w'o ũkamũthasya." (Yoana 8:32) Kũvikĩa o na yu, ũw'o ũla Yesũ wamanyĩisye nũthaasya andũ kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.—Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Kũthaw'a Kuma Ũkombonĩ wĩ Kĩvathũkany'o."
Kwa w'o, Ngai nĩwavonokisye Yosevu na Blessing kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. No ũsome ngewa ya kwendeesya ya Yosevu ĩvukunĩ ya Mwambĩlĩlyo kĩlungu kya 39 nginya 41. O nakyo kĩthito kya Blessing kya kũmantha ũthasyo nĩ kyakwendeesya mũno.
Ĩtina wa Blessing kũlũngw'a kuma nthĩ ĩmwe yĩ Europe, aendie nthĩ ya Spain, ĩla yĩ o Europe. E kũu, nĩwakomanie na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na ambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia namo. Nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwatw'ĩte vyũ kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle wake, nĩwamanthie wĩa na amwĩsũva ũla mũndũ mũka wamũũngamĩe tene amũolangĩle mbesa ila wendekaa aĩve kĩla mwei. Mũthenya ũmwe Blessing nĩwakũnĩiwe simũ nĩ mũndũ mũka ũsu. Endaa kũmwĩtya Blessing ũekeo na aimũekea ila mbesa waaĩle kũĩva. Nĩ kyaũ kyeekĩkĩte? O nake aĩ anambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova! Blessing aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũw'o nũthaasya mũndũ kwa nzĩa sya ũsengy'a."
Yeova Ngai nĩwaũmĩaa ĩla Aisilaeli mathĩnaw'a Misili, na no nginya ũmũnthĩ ethĩwe aũmĩaa ĩla andũ mekwĩkwa maũndũ mataĩle. Nĩ kana ũkombo w'onthe ũthele vyũ, no nginya vethĩwe ũalyũku mũnene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, na Ngai nĩwathanĩte kũete ũalyũku ũsu. Mbivilia yathanĩte atĩĩ: "Kwĩanana na watho wake, tweteele matu meũ na nthĩ nzaũ, naw'o ũlũngalu ũtwĩe nthĩnĩ wayo."—2 Vetelo 3:13

translation:
One day, a woman named Blessing decided to go to Europe hoping to succeed and improve her life. She was told that if she took ten days and prayed diligently, her prayers would be answered and she would overcome difficulties.
One night, Blessing managed to get between 200 and 300 euros, but she didn't have enough money, so another woman helped her. That woman gave Blessing 40,000 euros. * Blessing said: "Many people want to leave, but I am afraid of dying before seeing my family. This journey is difficult." Her wealth grew with each person she helped, reaching millions across the entire world and becoming a source of healing.
About 4,000 years ago, her son named Joseph was imprisoned and sold. He was taken as a slave to a wealthy man in Egypt. Like Blessing, Joseph suffered with his master, but he remained faithful. Because of this, he was able to rise up and eventually govern alongside his master, and he was given honor and authority over the land—Genesis 39:1-20; Psalm 105:17, 18.
Joseph had great success, while Blessing was enslaved for 2000 years. But despite everything she went through, she continued to serve. This story continues with the next generation, and the lesson for all those who suffer is to persevere, even when things seem hopeless.
WHY MANY PEOPLE SUFFER IN SLAVERY
One reason is that they are captured in war. For example, the Egyptian Pharaoh Thutmose III recorded that he took 90,000 prisoners during a campaign in Canaan. These prisoners were often forced into slavery to build cities, work in mines, and cultivate the land.
And the Assyrian Empire also sent many slaves to conquer territories, and some captives were appointed as overseers of slaves. It is estimated that half the population of the people of Israel were slaves. Many slaves from Egypt and Assyria suffered greatly. For example, among those who suffered in slavery in Assyria, a man could be enslaved for up to 30 years.
And when the slave trade began, slaves began to be transported. Between 1500 and 1800 AD, the transatlantic slave trade involved millions of Africans and Americans, one of the most brutal forms of trade in history. One estimate by an organization called UNESCO states: 'Adults, men, and women who were able to survive the journey into slavery numbered between 25 and 30 million.' Many people were taken captive and sold across the Atlantic. A man named Olaudah Equiano, who experienced this captivity himself, said: "The stench of sweat and the cries of the people made the situation so horrific that it was impossible to describe."
The tragedy is that this situation continued to cause suffering to many people. According to statistics from the International Labour Organization, approximately 21 million adults, men, and women are currently enslaved, whether formally or informally, in various ways. Slavery takes many forms, including forced labor, large-scale smuggling operations, domestic servitude, sexual exploitation, and child labor. The impact of this problem continues to grow, and today it is a major issue.
TO END SLAVERY
Many slaves have historically been subjected to severe hardship, and this has often led to rebellion. For example, around 73 BC, a slave named Spartacus and about 100,000 others revolted against the Roman Republic, causing significant disruption. Between 1701 and 1800, slaves on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean rebelled against their oppressors. These rebellions were often driven by immense desire for freedom and resulted in prolonged conflicts, such as the 13-year struggle that ultimately led to Haiti's independence in 1804.
It is interesting to note how the story of slavery parallels the plight of the Israelites when they were enslaved in Egypt. The entire nation of Israel, numbering approximately three million people, was enslaved in Egypt. Because of this, the Israelites longed to be freed from bondage. The Bible shows how God intervened to deliver them. It states that "all the nations" will eventually "become rebellious."—Exodus 1:11-14. But even though the Israelites desired freedom, Pharaoh opposed letting them go.—Exodus 1:8-22.
The deliverance of the Israelites from Egyptian bondage vividly illustrates how God can intervene to save his people. God told Moses: "I have positively seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt." (Exodus 3:7, 8) To this day, Jews commemorate the Passover annually to remember this deliverance.—Exodus 12:14.
THE DELIVERANCE WAS MEMORABLE
The Bible describes Jehovah God as "the One who does wondrous things," and it assures us that he is able to help us. (2 Kings 19:7; Malachi 3:6) God sent Jesus "to proclaim good news to the poor…and to release those held captive." (Luke 4:18) So, does this mean that Jesus has been commissioned to free all people from all forms of bondage? Let us examine what the Scriptures say. Jesus has been empowered to free people from spiritual bondage. Jesus himself said: "If you continue abiding by my words, you will really be my disciples." (John 8:32) By means of this teaching, Jesus empowers people to gain true freedom.—See the article "Deliverance From Spiritual Bondage."
Therefore, God liberated Joseph and Benjamin in an extraordinary way. You may find the account of Joseph's experiences in Genesis chapters 39 through 41 particularly moving. And Benjamin's experience in being accused of theft was also remarkable.
Benjamin was assigned to serve in one branch in Europe, then to another branch in Spain, both in Europe. There, he associated with the Witnesses of Jehovah and offered to share the Bible with them. He was touched by their willingness to spend time helping him, and he appreciated how they would visit him regularly, often walking miles to do so. On one occasion, Benjamin received a surprise visit from a brother. He went to see Benjamin again, and this time brought a gift. What did he bring? It was a Bible to help him study with the Witnesses of Jehovah! Benjamin said: "This will empower a person by means of truthful knowledge."
Jehovah God led the Israelites out of Egypt, and later he led people to lands where they could enjoy better conditions. Even when facing great obstacles, they experienced miraculous deliverance, and God proved able to provide for them. The Bible states: "By his name people put forth strength, and they themselves will walk about and prove strong."—2 Chronicles 3:13

text:
Vai mũndũ wĩsĩ nesa ũndũ Yesũ wailyĩ nũndũ ndaaĩa mũndũ amũkũne visa kana ase ĩvisa yake. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, kwa myaka maana maingĩ, asoli aingĩ nĩmethĩĩtwe maisola visa sya kwonany'a ũndũ Yesũ wailyĩ.
Kwa w'o, asoli asu mayeesĩ nesa ũndũ Yesũ wailyĩ. Mavinda maingĩ matongoeaw'a nĩ maũndũ ta syĩthĩo, mĩĩkĩĩo ya ndĩni, na wendi wa ala meenda kũsolelwa visa wa Yesũ nĩ kana mamanye ũndũ meũmũsola ailyĩ. O na ũu wĩ o vo, visa ũla masola waĩ ũtonya kũtuma andũ methĩwa na woni ũtaĩle ĩũlũ wa Yesũ, o na waĩ ũtonya kũtuma matamũmanya na mataelewa momanyĩsyo make.
Asoli amwe masolaa Yesũ e mwonzu, e na nzwĩĩ ndaasa na kĩng'ee, na emakĩe. Nasyo visa ingĩ syoonanasya Yesũ e na vinya ũvĩtũkĩte wa mũndũ, athyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ kyeni kĩtheu mũtwe, kana e mũndũ ũtendete kũtindany'a na andũ. Syo visa isu nĩsyonanasya nesa ũndũ Yesũ wailyĩ? Tũtonya kũmanya ata? Nzĩa ĩmwe ya kwĩka ũu nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ me Mbivilianĩ matonya kũtũtetheesya kũelewa ũndũ Yesũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa ailyĩ. O na maũndũ asu no matũtetheesye kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩle ĩũlũ wa Yesũ.
'NĨWANZEŨVĨSYE MWĨĨ'
Yesũ awetie ndeto isu mboyanĩ yake, na veonekana aiwetie ĩvindanĩ yĩla wavatisawa. (Aevelania 10:5; Mathayo 3:13-17) Mwĩĩ ũsu wailyĩ ata? Vathelete ta myaka 30 ĩtina wa mũlaĩka Kavilieli kũtavya Meli atĩĩ: "Ũkaitava, na ũkasyaa kana kavĩsĩ, . . . Mwana wa Ngai." (Luka 1:31, 35) Kwoou, Yesũ aĩ mũndũ mwĩanĩu kana ũte na naĩ, o tondũ Atamu woombĩtwe ailyĩ. (Luka 3:38; 1 Akolintho 15:45) No nginya Yesũ ethĩwe aĩ mũndũũme mũmbe nesa, na no ĩthĩwa avw'anene na inyia wake Meli, ũla waĩ Mũyuti.
Kĩvathũkany'o na Alomi, Yesũ nĩwaĩthasya kĩng'ee nũndũ kĩu nĩkyo kyaĩ kĩthĩo kya Ayuti. Kĩng'ee kya Ayuti kĩyeethĩawa kĩ kĩasa mũno na nĩmakĩsanũaa nesa nũndũ nĩkyatumaa mũndũ anengwa ndaĩa. Vate nzika, no nginya Yesũ ethĩwe eenzaa kĩng'ee na nzw'ĩĩ yake nĩ kana iikasave mũno. No Anasili me oka, ta Samusoni, mateenzaa nzw'ĩĩ yoo.—Motalo 6:5; Asili 13:5.
Yesũ atavikĩtye myaka 30, athũkũmaa wĩa wa mbwaũ ate kũtũmĩa masinĩ sya sitima ila ĩtũmĩawa wĩanĩ ũsu ũmũnthĩ. (Maliko 6:3) Kwoou no nginya ethĩwe aĩ na mwĩĩ mũlũmu. Kavinda kanini ĩtina wa kwambĩĩa wĩa wake wa ũtavany'a, 'nĩwalũngilye onthe ĩkalũnĩ, vamwe na malondu moo na ng'ombe; na mbesa sya ala meũvunzya atulũla, na mesa syoo akulumany'a,' na eekie ũu e o weka. (Yoana 2:14-17) Ũndũ ta ũsu ũtonya kwĩkwa nĩ mũndũ wĩ na vinya. Yesũ atũmĩaa mwĩĩ mũseo ũla wanengetwe nĩ Ngai kwĩanĩsya wĩa ũla wanengetwe. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi waisye atĩĩ: "Mũvaka nĩtavan'ye ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ndũanĩ ila ingĩ nasyo: nũndũ natũmiwe nũndũ wa ũu." (Luka 4:43) No nginya Yesũ ethĩwe aĩ na vinya mwingĩ nĩ kana ethĩwe atonya kũthi na maaũ kũndũ kwingĩ nthĩ ya Valestina aitavany'a ũvoo mũseo.
"ŨKAI KWAKWA, . . . NAKWA NGAMŨTHŨMŨSYA"
Nĩkwĩthĩwa Yesũ aĩ mũtanu na nĩwendete andũ, no nginya andũ ala 'mathĩnĩaa wĩa na maĩ na mĩio mĩito' methĩwe mendeeiw'e nĩ ndeto isu syake. (Mathayo 11:28-30) Ũndũ wendeeaw'a nĩ andũ na ũndũ wamew'ĩaa tei nĩ maũndũ maĩkĩĩthasya kana watho wake wa kũthũmũsya ala mendaa kwĩmanyĩsya kuma kwake nĩ wa w'o. O na syana nini nĩsyendaa kũtindany'a na Yesũ nũndũ Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana nĩwasyosie na "aivĩtĩĩsya moko make."—Maliko 10:13-16.
O na kau Yesũ nĩweewie woo mwingĩ mũno atanamba kũkw'a, ndekalaa emakĩe kana ate mũtanu. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda waendie mũtwaanonĩ ũla waĩ Kena, na e kũu nĩwaseũvĩisye andũ mbinyu kwa kũvĩndũa kĩw'ũ kyatw'ĩka mbinyu nzeo. (Yoana 2:1-11) Nĩwaendaa kũndũ kũngĩ andũ mombanĩe, na akamamanyĩsya maũndũ ma vata matesa kũla.—Mathayo 9:9-13; Yoana 12:1-8.
Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata mũno nĩ kana nzĩa ĩla Yesũ watũmĩaa kũtavany'a yatumaa ethukĩĩsya make matanĩa kũmanya kana me na wĩkwatyo wa thayũ ũtathela. (Yoana 11:25, 26; 17:3) Ĩla ala amanyĩw'a 70 mamũtavisye maũndũ maseo ala monie me ũtavany'anĩ, 'nĩwatanie' mũno na amea atĩĩ: "Tanai nũndũ masyĩtwa menyu nĩmaandĩkĩtwe ĩtunĩ."—Luka 10:20, 21.
"ĨNDĨ INYW'Ĩ MŨTIKETHĨWE MŨILYĨ ŨU"
Atongoi ma ndĩni ma ĩvinda ya Yesũ nĩmatũmĩaa nzĩa sya ũseleke nĩ kana meyendeesye andũnĩ na malũlũmĩĩlye ũkũmũ woo. (Motalo 15:38-40; Mathayo 23:5-7) Kĩvathũkany'o namo, Yesũ eeie atũmwa make kana mayaĩle 'kũsumbĩka' andũ angĩ. (Luka 22:25, 26) O na Yesũ nĩwakanisye amanyĩw'a make amea atĩĩ: "Ĩsũvĩei aandĩki, ala mendaa kũtambũka mekĩe ngũa ndaasa, na kũkethw'a ing'ang'anĩ."—Maliko 12:38.
Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndeekaa tamo nũndũ nĩwavulanaa na andũ, o na ve ĩvinda andũ mataamanya kana e namo ĩkomanonĩ. (Yoana 7:10, 11) O na e katĩ wa amanyĩw'a make 11, ndwaĩ ũtonya kũmũvathũkany'a namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yutasi, ũla wamũvũnyanĩie Yesũ, eekie kũmũmumunya, nũndũ ũsu nĩw'o waĩ "wonan'yo" ũla wavangĩte kũtũmĩa atetheesye ala wookĩte namo mamũmanye Yesũ.—Maliko 14:44, 45.
Kwoou o na kau ve maũndũ maingĩ matesĩkĩe ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Yesũ wailyĩ, vate nzika no twasye kana ũndũ ũsolawa ailyĩ mavinda maingĩ, ti w'o wailyĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩla kya vata vyũ nĩ ũndũ tũmwonaa Yesũ ĩvinda yĩĩ, ĩndĩ ti ũndũ wailyĩ.
"KŨTIELE ĨVINDA ĨNINI, NA NTHĨ NDĨKAMBONA ĨNGĨ"
O mũthenyanĩ ũla Yesũ wawetie ndeto isu now'o wakwie na athikwa. (Yoana 14:19) Aumisye thayũ wake nĩ kana "wĩthĩwe wovosyo kwondũ wa aingĩ." (Mathayo 20:28) Na mũthenya wa katatũ Ngai nĩwamũthayũũkisye "vevanĩ" na "amumĩlya onanw'e" kwa amanyĩw'a amwe make. (1 Vetelo 3:18; Meko ma Atũmwa 10:40) Yesũ ailyĩ ata ĩvindanĩ yĩu wamaumĩlĩĩle amanyĩw'a make? Veonekana aĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ũndũ wailyĩ atanamba kũawa, nũndũ o na amanyĩw'a make mayaamũmanya na mĩtũkĩ. Ĩla Meli Makatalene wamwonie Yesũ, asũanĩie nĩ mũsũvĩi wa mũũnda, namo ala amanyĩw'a make elĩ maendete Emau mamwona masũanĩie no mũndũ ũendete o vandũ.—Luka 24:13-18; Yoana 20:1, 14, 15.
Ũmũnthĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Yesũ ũilyĩ? Ĩtina wa myaka 60 kuma Yesũ akw'a, mũtũmwa Yoana nĩwoonie mawoni ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Mawoninĩ asu, Yoana ndaaona mũndũ wambĩtwe ngelany'onĩ. Ĩndĩ oonie "Mũsumbĩ wa asumbĩ na Mwĩaĩi wa eaĩi," nake nĩ Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, ũla o mĩtũkĩ ũkilyĩ kũsinda amaitha onthe ma Ngai, namo nĩ ndaimoni na andũ athũku, na ĩndĩ aietee andũ moathimo ma tene na tene.—Ũvuan'yo 19:16; 21:3, 4.

translation:
If anyone is willing to know what Jesus did, let them seek and find his way. For a long time, many people have been taught about what Jesus did.
Therefore, those people should be willing to know what Jesus did. Many problems they face are things like temptation, inner struggles, and the world's influence preventing them from seeking Jesus or understanding what he taught. But despite this, those who seek will be able to send others to know and understand the truth of Jesus, and they will be able to send knowledge and understanding of his teachings.
Some people learn about Jesus through stories, through dreams and visions, and through miracles. And many times, Jesus is revealed through the difficult circumstances of life, sometimes through severe pain in the head, or through someone being mistreated by others. So why is it important to know what Jesus did? Can we really know? One way to approach this is to compare the things of the Bible that can help us understand what Jesus was trying to teach. And some things will help us understand and know the truth of Jesus.
'I HAVE BEEN ANOINTED'
Jesus received this message from his Father, and it was shown that he received a voice from heaven while he was baptizing. (Revelation 10:5; Matthew 3:13-17) What does this mean? About 30 years later, an angel Gabriel told Mary: "You will conceive and give birth to a son… The Son of God." (Luke 1:31, 35) Truly, Jesus was a perfect man, though Adam was created first. (Luke 3:38; 1 Corinthians 15:45) Now, because Jesus was made a human, and because he was born of Mary, the daughter of David.
In connection with Adam, Jesus showed himself to be like a descendant of God. The descent of God means something pure and holy, and it makes a person righteous. Therefore, because Jesus was made like us, he also experienced temptation with his desires.—Proverbs 6:5; Genesis 13:5.
Jesus was about 30 years old when he began his ministry and used simple methods, unlike those used today. (Mark 6:3) It seems he did not have much money. Once, he went to a large wedding feast, and they told him, "They have run out of wine; whatever you tell them to do, they will do," and he performed this miracle. (John 2:14-17) A person with insight would realize that this was not an ordinary occurrence. Jesus used his authority from God to help people who were helped by God. And that is why he said: "I must preach the good news of the Kingdom of God to other cities too, because that is what I was sent to do." (Luke 4:43) So Jesus had a lot of work to do, so much so that he could not rest for very long, as happened with Valentine during that time.
"YOUR WILL, . . . AND YOUR DESIRE"
It is reported that Jesus felt compassion for people, and when people came to him, they 'brought their sick and afflicted' and he healed them. (Matthew 11:28-30) Those who were healed were people who needed help, and they were willing to submit to his direction. But how can we imitate Jesus and be moved by the Bible's account or show sympathy towards "those who are different"?—Mark 10:13-16.
And yet Jesus often did more than just heal a few people, sometimes healing many. For example, he healed a man in Cana, and he proved to people through this miracle that he had power over water. (John 2:1-11) He also went to many places, and he showed kindness to those who were suffering.—Matthew 9:9-13; John 12:1-8.
Indeed, what makes this remarkable is that Jesus used his power to resurrect people, giving them hope and proving that death is reversible. (John 11:25, 26; 17:3) And on one occasion, 70 disciples returned excitedly, saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name."—Luke 10:20, 21.
"IN THIS WAY YOU WILL BE PROVEN GENUINE"
Some of Jesus' followers misused their authority, acting self-importantly and lording it over others. (Titus 15:38-40; Matthew 23:5-7) However, Jesus instructed his disciples not to act like rulers or try to dominate others. (Luke 22:25, 26) And Jesus rebuked some of his followers, telling them: "Beware of scribes, who like to walk around in robes and greet people with respectful greetings."—Mark 12:38.
Jesus often spoke to people openly, and he did not shy away from public gatherings. (John 7:10, 11) Yet, among his eleven apostles, there was one weak link. For example, Judas Iscariot, who initially associated with Jesus, later betrayed him, becoming the one "who handed [him] over."—Mark 14:44, 45.
However, despite all the things that happened during Jesus' ministry, people still needed proof that he was truly the Messiah, and they wanted more than just his words. Indeed, everything that happened proved that Jesus was genuine, and not someone claiming to be something he wasn't.
"TO MAKE THE OUTSTANDING FEATURE EVIDENT, AND SO THAT MY FAITH MAY ABOUND"
Jesus made this request while near Jerusalem shortly before his death. (John 14:19) He explained that he came "to give his soul as a ransom for many." (Matthew 20:28) And God validated his Son by resurrecting him and exalting him to heaven.—1 Peter 3:18; Acts 10:40. Did Jesus appear only to those whom he had already chosen to save, or did he also reveal himself to others who were sincere? It seems not, because his apostles were amazed and doubtful. But Mary Magdalene saw Jesus, and two disciples on the road to Emmaus recognized him when he revealed himself to them.—Luke 24:13-18; John 20:1, 14, 15.
How then can we know what Jesus accomplished? About 60 years after Jesus' death, the apostle John had a vision regarding Jesus. In this vision, John said he saw "one like a son of man." This One was "loyal and true," and he had eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet were like burnished bronze, and he spoke with authority. He will judge demons and wicked people, and he will liberate faithful ones from eternal destruction.—Revelation 19:16; 21:3, 4.

text:
WE WĨW'AA ata ĩla wasũanĩa kana ũkesa ũkũa? Andũ aingĩ ĩla meesilya ĩũlũ wa kũkũa nĩmathĩnĩkaa, makakwatwa nĩ kĩmako na wia. Mekaa ũu nĩkwĩthĩwa mavinda maingĩ kũkũa kũkonanaw'a na maũndũ mate maseo ta kwĩthĩwa na ũthyũ mũkũnzanu, mwĩĩ ũte na vinya, kũlwa nĩ maũndũ, na kũkwatwa nĩ mowau mathũku.
Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, andũ makũaa kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Amwe moo o na makũa mayĩthĩawa na mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ, o na mayũlawa mũno nĩ maũndũ. O na ĩngĩ, ũiiti wa matukũ aa nũtetheesye amwe kũiitwa kana makethĩwa matonya kwĩkala ĩvinda ĩasa mawaĩte mowau mathũku. Na nũndũ wa ũu, andũ nthĩ imwe methĩĩtwe matonya kwĩkala mate na mathĩna ma mwĩĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa.
Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ methĩwe me na mathĩna makonetye ũkũũ kana mai namo, mendaa kũkũa me atanu. Ũu ũtonyeka ata? Nzĩa ĩmwe nĩ kwa kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩle, kwĩthĩwa meyũmbanĩtye na matonya kwĩtĩkĩla ũalyũku ũsu. Nĩ kana twone ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ũu, ekai twone myolooto ĩmwe ya Mbivilia ĩla ĩtonya kũtũtethya.
ĨTHĨWA NA WĨNYIVYO: "Ũĩ wĩ na ala menyivasya." (Nthimo 11:2) Kwosana na maũndũ ala tũũneenea no twasye kana "ala menyivasya" nĩ andũ ala akũũ na metĩkĩlĩte kana mayĩsa kwĩka kĩla kĩndũ, o tondũ meekaa tene. Mũndũũme ũmwe wa Brazil wĩtawa Charles, wĩ na myaka 93, awetete ũw'o wa maũndũ kwa kwasya atĩĩ: "Ĩla wekala myaka mingĩ no nginya ũkũe. Vai ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ũkatw'ĩka wa mũika ĩngĩ."
Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa wĩnyivĩtye ti kwĩthĩwa na woni ũtaĩle wa kana, "Nyie nĩ mũkũũ na ndi kĩndũ kĩngĩ neteele." Woni ta ũsu no ũtume mũndũ atethĩwa e mũtanu. Ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 24:10 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa nũnyalaa mũthenya wa thĩna, vinya waku nĩ mũnini." Vandũ va ũu, mũndũ wĩ na wĩnyivyo nĩwonanasya ũĩ kwa kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩle na kwĩka maũndũ kwosana na ũtonyi wake.
Nake Corrado, ũla wĩ na myaka 77, kuma Italy, awetete kana ethĩwa mũndũ akũa nũkwenda kũendeea nesa, no nginya emanyĩsye kwĩka maũndũ kavola kwĩ ũndũ ũtwĩe ekaa. Vate nzika, mũndũ nĩwaĩlĩte kwĩka moalyũku mana ĩla wakũa. Corrado na kĩveti kyake nĩmavangĩte nesa mawĩa moo ma mũsyĩ ũkethĩa mayĩũnoa mũno. Marian, kuma Brazil, ũla wĩ myaka 81, e na woni ta ũsu. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩmanyĩte maũndũ ala ndonya kwĩanĩsya kwa ĩvinda ĩna." Aendeee kwasya, "Nĩnthyũmũaa mavinda kwa mavinda ĩla ngũthũkũma. Nĩnĩkalaa nthĩ ngasoma mavuku kana ngethukĩĩsya mbathi. O na nĩnĩsĩ kana ndyĩsa kwĩka maũndũ o tondũ neekaa tene."
ĨTHĨWA NA MĨVAKA ĨLA ŨKWĨKA MAŨNDŨ: 'Aka meyanakavye na kwĩvw'ĩka ngũa imaĩle, vamwe na wĩnyivyo na kĩlĩko.' (1 Timotheo 2:9) Ndeto "ngũa imaĩle" syonanasya kwĩthĩwa na mĩvaka na kwĩkĩa ngũa nzeo. Mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Barbara, ũla wĩ na myaka 74, wa Canada, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩndataa nĩthĩwe nĩ mũtheu na nĩkĩĩte nesa. Ndyĩlekeleelasya nĩ aĩ nĩ mũkũũ, kana ũkethĩa ndikũlasya ũndũ andũ meona nĩilyĩ." Nake Fern, ũla wĩ na myaka 91, kuma Brazil, aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩnĩũaa ngũa nzaũ mavinda kwa mavinda, na ũndũ ũsu nũndanĩthasya." Nao nata aũme ala akũũ? Mũndũũme ũmwe wĩtawa Antônio wĩ na myaka 73, kuma Brazil, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩndataa mũno kwĩkĩa ngũa nzeo na ntheu." Aendeee na kwasya ũũ ĩũlũ wa ũtheu: "Nthambaa na ngenza kĩng'ee kĩla mũthenya."
O na ũu wĩ o vo, tũyaĩlĩte kũthĩnĩkĩa mũno ũndũ tũilyĩ nginya ũkethĩa tũyĩũtũmĩa "kĩlĩko" mĩkĩĩlenĩ yitũ. Bok-im, ũla wĩ na myaka 69, kuma South Korea, e na woni ũkwonany'a kana nĩwĩthĩawa na mĩvaka mĩkĩĩlenĩ yake. Awetete ũũ: "Nĩnĩsĩ nesa kana ndyaĩlĩte kwĩkĩa ngũa imwe ila neekĩaa nĩ wa mũika."
ĨTHĨWA NA WONI MŨSEO: "Mĩthenya yonthe ya ala mathĩnaa nĩ mĩthũku; ĩndĩ ũla wĩ na ngoo ndanu e na mboka ĩtatw'ĩkanaa." (Nthimo 15:15) Ĩla ũendeee na ũkũa nĩvatonyeka ũkakw'a ngoo walilikana vinya ũla waĩ naw'o na maũndũ maingĩ ala weekaa wĩ wa mũika. Ti ũthũku kwĩw'a ũu. Ĩndĩ tata ndũkakĩlw'e vinya nĩ mawoni asu mate maseo. Kũsũanĩa mũno maũndũ ala mavĩtie no kũkũwae ngoo na kũkatuma ũteka maũndũ ala yu wĩ na ũtonyi wa kwĩka. Joseph, ũla wĩ na myaka 79, kuma Canada, onanĩtye woni mũseo kwa kwasya atĩĩ: "Ndataa mũno kũtanĩa kwĩka maũndũ ala yu ndonya kwĩka, vandũ va kwĩliĩla maũndũ ala neekaa tene ĩndĩ ndatonya kwĩka oyu."
O na ĩngĩ, kũsoma na kwĩmanyĩsya no kũtume wĩthĩwa na woni mũseo na kũvingũa kĩlĩko kyaku nĩ kana ũmanye maũndũ meũ. Kwoou, ĩthĩwa wĩ metho kũtũmĩa myanya ĩla yaumĩla ya kũsoma na kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ meũ. Ernesto, ũla wĩ na myaka 74, kuma Philippines, nũendaa kũla kwiawa mavuku akamanthe mavuku makwendeesya ũtonya kũsoma. Aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩnĩw'aa mũyo ĩla nasoma mavukunĩ maũndũ ma kũtanĩthya na matesa kũla, nũndũ nĩmatumaa ndesilya ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma o vu mũsyĩ." Nake Lennart, ũla wĩ na myaka 75, kuma Sweden, nĩwambĩĩisye ũndũ ũte laisi wa kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩngĩ.
ĨTHĨWA WĨ MŨLAU: "Nenganei, nenyu mũkanengwa." (Luka 6:38) Ĩmanyĩsye kũtũmĩaa ĩvinda na malĩ yaku kũtetheesya ala angĩ. Ũndũ ũsu ũkatuma wĩthĩwa wĩ mwĩanĩe na wĩ na ũtanu. Hosa, ũla wĩ na myaka 85, kuma Brazil, atataa mũno kũtetheesya ala angĩ o na kau we nĩ mũkũũ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩngũnĩaa simũ anyanyae makwa ala awau kana makw'ĩte ngoo, o na nĩnĩmaandĩkĩaa valũa. Mavinda angĩ nĩnĩmatũmĩaa o tũmĩthĩnzĩo. O na ĩngĩ, nĩnendete kũuwĩa ala awau."
Weethĩwa wĩ mũlau, o namo ala angĩ makakwony'a ũlau. Jan, ũla wĩ na myaka 66, kuma Sweden, awetete ũũ: "Ĩla wamenda ala angĩ, o namo nĩmakwendaa." Vate nzika, mũndũ mũlau nũtumaa angĩ mamwenda na methĩwa me atanu ĩla me nake.
TUMA NDŨŨ NA ANDŨ: "Ũla wĩvathaa amanthaa kwenda kwake mwene, na alonzanĩlasya ũĩ w'onthe mwĩanĩu." (Nthimo 18:1) O na kau ve mavinda amwe ũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũyenda kwĩthĩwa wĩ weka, ndũkevathanae na andũ vyũ. Innocent, ũla wĩ na myaka 72, kuma Nigeria, nũtanĩaa kwĩthĩwa vamwe na anyanyae. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩndanĩaa mũno kũtindany'a na andũ ma mũika wĩ kĩvathũkany'o." Nake Börje, ũla wĩ na myaka 85, kuma Sweden, aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩndataa kũtindany'a na andũ ma mũika. Nĩnĩw'aa ta nĩ wa mũika ĩngĩ ĩla noona ũndũ methĩawa na vinya." Osa ĩtambya ya kũthokasya anyanyau mavinda kwa mavinda. Han-sik, ũla wĩ na myaka 72, kuma South Korea, easya: "Nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtwendete kũthokya anyanyae maitũ tũĩsanĩe vamwe, methĩwe nĩ akũũ, kana nĩ ma mũika."
Andũ me ndũũ nĩmaeaa ngewa na nĩmethukĩanĩasya. Onany'a kana nũkwendeew'a nĩ andũ angĩ. Helena, ũla wĩ na myaka 71, kuma Mozambique, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩndumaa ndũũ na andũ na nĩnĩthĩawa nĩmanengete ndaĩa. Nĩnĩmethukĩĩasya nĩ kana nĩmanye mawoni moo na maũndũ ala mamendeeasya." Nake José, ũla wĩ na myaka 73, kuma Brazil, aĩtye: "Andũ nĩmendeeaw'a nĩ kwĩkalany'a na andũ mekũmethukĩĩsya, mekũmony'a kana nĩmekwendeew'a nĩmo, matonya kũmatũngĩa mũvea ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩle, na methĩawa me atanu."
Ĩla ũkwĩyĩelesya mbee wa andũ, tata mũno ndeto syaku "isamae mũnyũ." (Akolosai 4:6) Sũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa ndeto ila ũũneena nĩ kana syĩthĩwe syĩ sya kwĩkĩa vinya.
TŨNGAA MŨVEA: "Ĩthĩwai na mũvea." (Akolosai 3:15) Tũnga mũvea watetheew'a. Ndeto sya kwonany'a kana nĩwatũnga mũvea nitumaa andũ methĩwa me anyanyau. Marie-Paule, ũla wĩ na myaka 74, kuma Canada, aĩtye: "Nĩ na mũũme wakwa nĩtũnathamĩĩie ngolovanĩ. Tũithama anyanyae aingĩ maitũ nĩmatũtetheeisye. Tũyeesĩ tũtonya kũmanenga kyaũ. Nĩtwatũmĩie kĩla ũmwe woo kaati sya kũtũnga mũvea, o na amwe nĩtwamathokisye twaya lĩu vamwe." Nake mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Jae-won, ũla wĩ na myaka 76, kuma South Korea, nũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ nũkuawa na ngalĩ akatwawa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ. Aĩtye: "Nĩndũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ wa ũtethyo ũsu, o na nĩnumasya mbesa sya kwĩkĩa ngalĩ mauta. Mavinda angĩ nĩndũmaa tũmĩthĩnzĩo o vamwe na kaati sya kũtũnga mũvea."
Ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ, tũngaa mũvea nũndũ wĩ thayũ. Mũsumbĩ mũĩ Solomoni aisye: "Ngitĩ yĩ thayũ yĩ kavaa kwĩ mũnyambũ mũkw'ũ." (Mũtavan'ya 9:4) Vate nzika, kwĩthĩwa na woni ũla waĩlĩte, vamwe na kwĩtĩkĩla moalyũku ala maetawe nĩ ũkũũ, no kũtume ũkũa wĩ o ũtanu.

translation:
Are we able to understand or learn growth? Many people find the process of growing difficult, caught up in confusion and pain. This situation often involves many challenges in growing, dealing with various issues, sometimes being overwhelmed by problems, and getting stuck in difficulties.
Concerning this matter, people grow in different ways, some experiencing significant changes with many lessons, others facing numerous obstacles. And again, the days pass and some are called or chosen to become a solution to problems, to be a help in times of difficulty. And because of this, people often strive to become good examples with valuable lessons for future generations.
For many people who have experienced hardships or faced losses, they desire to grow to fivefold. Is this possible? Some find themselves struggling with weaknesses, grappling with challenges and failing to achieve their full potential. Or perhaps we see something we can overcome, let us look at one verse from the Bible that can guide us.
ACT AND BE PERSISTENT: "He who is slow to act is foolish." (Proverbs 11:2) Considering other things we have discussed, when someone says "be persistent," it refers to those who persevere and remain steadfast in everything, or continue despite difficulties. A man named Charles from Brazil, aged 93, shared his experience saying: "If I had known I would live this long, I wouldn't have done certain things."
To act persistently does not mean acting recklessly or saying, "You are strong and I am nothing else." Such words can discourage a person. Proverbs 24:10 states: "Do not give way to discouragement, for wisdom is sweet." Therefore, a person with persistence should encourage himself by acting decisively and overcoming obstacles according to his ability.
Recently, Corrado, aged 77, from Italy, shared how helping someone in need made him feel good and reminded him of something important. He said, "A person realizes what life is worth when he grows old." Corrado and his wife often help others, giving their time and energy willingly. Marian, from Brazil, aged 81, has a supportive family. She says: "I have learned lessons that I will never forget." She continues, "I face challenges step by step as they come. I still read books and try to learn new things. And I realize that I can overcome obstacles despite difficulties."
THE BIBLE SAYS: 'Adorn yourselves with modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety.' (1 Timothy 2:9) The expression "modest apparel" refers to dressing appropriately and maintaining a dignified appearance. A sister named Barbara, aged 74, from Canada, says: "I want to please Jehovah and look presentable. I am willing to make adjustments so that people see that I care." Sister Fern, aged 91, from Brazil, says this: "I always try to dress modestly, and doing so makes me feel good." But what about brothers? A brother named Antônio, aged 73, from Brazil, says: "I always strive to maintain a dignified appearance and conduct." He adds, explaining his routine: "I comb my hair and get dressed neatly every day."
And if we find it difficult to know how to dress modestly, we can ask mature Christians for advice. Bok-im, aged 69, from South Korea, appreciates having fellow elders who give him counsel. He explains: "I feel relieved when I can ask others for advice on how to dress properly."
THE BIBLE ALSO SAYS: "The heart of the righteous is cheerful; the face of the unhappy is gloomy." (Proverbs 15:15) However, sometimes we may struggle with sadness because of past experiences or current difficulties. It is normal to feel downcast at times. But dwelling on negative thoughts can lead to discouragement and prevent us from enjoying life. To overcome this, focus on positive things and cultivate gratitude. Joseph, aged 79, from Canada, found it helpful to reflect on what he has. He says: "I think about the blessings I have, and I realize there are many things I still enjoy."
Also, reading and meditating on Bible principles can help us maintain a positive outlook and cope with challenges. Of course, prayer is essential for receiving strength and guidance. Ernesto, aged 74, from the Philippines, used to struggle with reading. He says: "I realized that when I read scriptures and meditate on them regularly, it helps me to deal with problems more effectively." And Lennart, aged 75, from Sweden, learned something important through his experience.
A GOOD PRINCIPLE: "Give, and you will receive." (Luke 6:38) Practicing generosity brings joy and strengthens relationships. Hosa, aged 85, from Brazil, enjoys helping others, even though she has limited means. She says: "I share whatever little I have with those in need, and I write notes of encouragement. Small acts of kindness make me happy. Also, I try to be understanding."
When fellow believers show generosity, it touches our hearts. Jan, aged 66, from Sweden, commented: "When someone helps me, it really encourages me." Often, generous people give not only material things but also their time and attention.
SHARE WITH OTHERS: "The one who gives to the poor lends to Jehovah himself." (Proverbs 19:17) Even if you have limited resources, you can find ways to share with others. Innocent, aged 72, from Nigeria, enjoys associating with his brothers and sisters. He says: "I always try to spend time with people who uplift me." And Börje, aged 85, from Sweden, explains: "I enjoy spending time with people. I feel like I belong to another family that understands me and cares about me." It takes effort to strengthen bonds with others. Han-sik, aged 72, from South Korea, observes: "I make an effort to encourage my family members and friends, whether they are young or old, or from different backgrounds."
Many people appreciate genuine kindness and thoughtfulness. They may be touched even by small gestures. Helena, aged 71, from Mozambique, says: "I love being around people and sharing encouraging words. I feel strengthened when I see others happy and when I know I have helped them." Similarly, José, aged 73, from Brazil, states: "People encourage me by taking the time to get to know me, by showing interest in what I do, and by offering practical help when I need it—even just a kind smile."
To speak favorably of others will contribute to their well-being. So let your speech always be seasoned with salt.—Colossians 4:6. Be sincere in your expressions, and avoid saying anything that might discourage them.
REASON FOR ENCOURAGEMENT: "Be thankful." (Colossians 3:15) Expressing gratitude is refreshing. Kind words can lift the spirits of those who may be feeling downhearted. Marie-Paule, aged 74, from Canada, shares: "My husband and I used to argue frequently. We realized we needed to express our appreciation more often. We made an effort to notice the good things each other did. It really changed our relationship, and now we try to thank each other daily." Also, Jae-won, a 76-year-old man from South Korea, found that expressing encouragement helped him cope with a serious illness. He says: "I began to look for opportunities to praise others, and it gave me strength to face my health challenges. Many times, I felt better because of the joy I brought to others through encouragement."
Above all, express encouragement sincerely. King Solomon wrote: "Good news makes the heart rejoice." (Proverbs 9:4) Indeed, receiving positive comments, along with thoughtful consideration and avoiding harsh criticism, can greatly improve someone's outlook and make a lasting impression.

text:
Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmũvoya Ngai?
Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana Ngai ethukĩĩsye mboya sitũ?
Ngai asũngĩaa mboya sitũ ata?
1, 2. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmyona mboya ta ũndũ wa ndaĩa nene, na nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmanya ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa mboya?
METHONĨ ma Yeova, "ũla watw'ĩkĩthisye ĩtu na nthĩ," mbaĩ no ta kavoloto ka kĩw'ũ ndoonĩ. (Savuli 115:15; Isaia 40:15) Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Yeova e vakuvĩ na onthe ala mamwĩkaĩlaa, onthe ala mamwĩkaĩlaa na w'o. Akeanĩsya kwenda kwa ala mamũkĩaa; o na akeew'a kũkaya kwoo, na kũmatangĩĩa." (Savuli 145:
2 Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda Yeova ethukĩĩsye mboya sitũ, nĩtwaĩle kũmũvoya kwa nzĩa ĩla wĩtĩkĩlĩtye. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata tũtesĩ ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa mboya? Nũndũ wa vata kũmanya ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye ĩũlũ wa mboya, nũndũ mboya nĩtũtetheeasya kũmũthengeea Yeova.
NĨKĨ TWAĨLE KŨMŨVOYA YEOVA?
3. Kĩtumi kĩmwe kĩnene kĩtumaa tũvoya Yeova nĩ kyaũ?
3 Kĩtumi kĩmwe kĩnene kĩtumaa tũvoya Yeova nĩkwĩthĩwa nũtũthoketye twĩke ũu. Ndeto yake ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya ĩitwĩa: "Mũikemakĩe kwa ũndũ o na wĩva; ĩndĩ kĩla ũndũnĩ mavata menyu nĩmatavanw'e kwa Ngai na kũvoya na kwĩsũva vamwe na kũtũnga mũvea. Na mũuo wa Ngai, ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe, ũkasũvĩaa ngoo syenyu na mosũanĩo menyu nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ." (Avilivi 4:
4. Kũmũvoyaa Yeova kũlũlũmĩĩlasya mũamba witũ nake ata?
4 Kĩtumi kĩngĩ kya kũvoya nĩ kana kũmũvoyaa Yeova nĩkũlũlũmĩĩlasya mũamba witũ nake. Andũ me ũnyanya maineenaa o yĩla me na mathĩna. Ĩndĩ nĩmendanĩte na ũnyanya woo ũendeea kũlũma o ũndũ mekũeleany'a mawoni moo, na maũndũ ala me ngoonĩ. Mavinda amwe mũamba witũ na Yeova Ngai wĩthĩawa ũilye o ta ũu. Nĩwĩmanyĩĩtye maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlu wa ũndũ Yeova ũilye na ieleelo syake ĩvukunĩ yĩĩ. Nũmũmanyĩte nesa vyũ. Mboya nĩkũtonyethasya kũtavya Ĩthe waku wa ĩtunĩ mosũanĩo maku na maũndũ ala me ngoonĩ. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtumaa ũmũthengeea Yeova.
NĨ MAŨNDŨ MEVA TWAĨLE KWĨANĨSYA?
5. Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana Yeova ndethukĩĩasya mboya syonthe?
5 Yeova ethukĩĩasya mboya syonthe? Sũanĩa ũndũ weeie Aisilaeli mamũlea ĩvinda ya mwathani Isaia: "Yĩla mwĩvoya mboya mbingĩ, ndikethukĩĩsya: moko menyu nĩmausũĩte nthakame." (Isaia 1:
6. Ũndũ ũmwe mũnene twaĩle kwĩanĩsya nĩ kana Ngai ethukĩĩsye mboya sitũ nĩ mwaũ, na tũtonya kũwĩanĩsya ata?
6 Ũndũ ũmwe mũnene twaĩle kwĩanĩsya nĩkwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. (Maliko 11:24) Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ: "Vate mũĩkĩĩo kũitonyeka kũmwendeesya [Ngai]; nũndũ ũla wũkaa kwa Ngai mũvaka etĩkĩle kana e vo, na ĩngĩ kana nũmanengae ĩtuvi ala mamũmanthaa." (Aevelania 11:6) Kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o ti o kwĩthĩwa twĩsĩ kana Ngai e vo, na kana nĩwĩw'aa mboya sitũ na kũisũngĩa. Mũĩkĩĩo ũĩkĩĩthaw'a na meko. No nginya twonany'e mũĩkĩĩo kwĩsĩla mwĩkalĩlenĩ witũ wa kĩla mũthenya.
7. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwonany'a ndaĩa yĩla tũũmũvoya Yeova? (b) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo na ngoo ntheu yĩla tũũvoya Ngai?
7 Ũndũ ũngĩ Yeova wendaa twĩanĩsye yĩla tũũvoya nĩ kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo na ngoo ntheu. Nĩtwaĩle kwĩnyivya yĩla tũũneena na Yeova. Yĩla andũ meũneena na mũsumbĩ, maneenaa nake kwa ndaĩa, maimanya kana we nĩ mũndũ mũnene. Ũu nĩkwonany'a twaĩle kwĩnyivya mũno yĩla tũũmũvoya Yeova. (Savuli 138:6) We nĩwe "Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 17:1) Yĩla tũũvoya Ngai nĩtwaĩle kwĩka ũu kwa nzĩa ĩkwonany'a kana twĩna wĩnyivyo mbee wake. Wĩnyivyo ta ũsu ũkatumaa tũmũvoya kuma ngoonĩ, tũtekũtindĩa ndeto o imwe mboyanĩ.
8. Tũtonya kwĩka kwĩanana na ũndũ twavoya ata?
8 Ũndũ ũngĩ wendekaa nĩ kana Ngai ethukĩĩsye mboya sitũ nĩ kwĩka kwĩanana na ũndũ twavoya. Yeova endaa twĩke ũndũ tũtonya twĩanĩsye ũndũ twamũvoya. Kwa ngelekany'o, twamũvoya, 'Atũnenge ũmũnthĩ lĩu witũ ũtwĩanĩe,' nĩtwaĩle kũthũkũma na kĩthito. (Mathayo 6:
MAKŨLYO NA MOSŨNGĨO ĨŨLŨ WA MBOYA
9. Twaĩle kũvoyaa ũũ, na kwĩsĩla kwĩ ũũ?
9 Twaĩle kũvoyaa kũla kwĩ ũũ? Yesũ amanyĩisye amanyĩw'a make mavoyae "Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ." (Mathayo 6:9) Kwoou twaĩle kũvoya Yeova Ngai e weka. Yeova nĩwendaa tũmanye ũnene wa Yesũ Klĩsto, mwana mũsyawa wake weka. O ũndũ tweemanyĩisye Kĩlungunĩ kya 5, Yesũ ookie kũũ nthĩ ethĩwe wovosyo atũtangĩĩe kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ. (Yoana 3:
10. Nĩkĩ vayendekaa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalo mũna wa mwanya yĩla tũũvoya?
10 Yĩla tũũvoya nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalo mũna wa mwanya? Aiee, nũndũ Yeova ndendaa mwĩkalo mũna. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana no ũvoye wĩkalĩte nthĩ, ũkunamĩtye mũtwe, ũtulĩtye ndu, kana ũũngeme. (1 Mavinda 17:16; Neemia 8:6; Ndanieli 6:
11. Nĩ mavata meva ma ngoonĩ ala tũtonya kũweta mboyanĩ sitũ?
11 Twaĩle kũvoya kyaũ? Mbivilia ĩeleetye: "Ethĩwa tũkavoya ũndũ kwĩanana na kwenda kwake, [Yeova] nũtwĩw'aa." (1 Yoana 5:
12. Tũtonya ata kũtongosya maũndũ ala makonetye Ĩthe waitũ wa ĩtunĩ mboyanĩ sitũ?
12 Maũndũ ala makonetye Yeova Ngai maĩle kwĩthĩwa me ma mbee mboyanĩ sitũ. Twĩna kĩtumi kya kũtaĩa Yeova kuma ngoonĩ vamwe na kũmũtũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa ũseo wake. (1 Mavinda 29:
13. Maandĩko monanasya ata ĩũlũ wa ũasa wa mboya ila syĩtĩkĩlĩkaa?
13 Mboya sitũ syaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ũasa wĩana ata? Mbivilia ndĩwetete ũasa kana ũkuvĩ wa mboya yĩla mũndũ ũkwĩvoyea kana ũkũtongoesya andũ angĩ mboyanĩ. Nĩtũtonya kumya mboya nguvĩ mbee wa kũya, kana mboya ndaasa twĩ ithyoka yĩla tũkwenda kũmwonoeesya Yeova ngoo sitũ. (1 Samueli 1:
14. Yĩla Mbivilia ĩkũtwĩa 'tũvoyae tũtekũeka' yĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a ata, na nĩkĩ ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa ũkiakisyo?
14 Twaĩle kũvoya mavinda meana ata? Mbivilia ĩtwĩaa 'tũvoyae mĩthenya yonthe,' 'twĩkalae na ũlũmu mboyanĩ,' na 'tũvoyae tũtekũeka.' (Luka 18:1; Alomi 12:12; 1 Athesalonika 5:
15. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwasya "Ameni" mũminũkĩlyonĩ wa mboya sitũ ene kana ĩtina wa mũndũ mũna kũtũtongoesya mboyanĩ?
15 Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwasya "Ameni" mũminũkĩlyonĩ wa mboya? Ndeto "ameni" yonanasya "ũu ũtw'ĩke ũu." Mbivilia yonanasya nĩwaĩlu kwasya "Ameni" mũminũkĩlyonĩ wa mboya. (1 Mavinda 16:36; Savuli 41:13) Twasya "Ameni" mũminũkĩlyonĩ wa mboya yitũ ene, twĩthĩawa tũyĩĩkĩĩthya kana ndeto sitũ syumĩte ngoonĩ. Yĩla twasya "Ameni"
ŨNDŨ NGAI ŨSŨNGĨAA MBOYA SITŨ
16. Twĩna mũĩkĩĩo mwaũ ũkonanĩtye na mboya?
16 We Yeova nũsũngĩaa mboya? Ĩĩ, nũsũngĩaa! Twĩna mũsingi mũlũmu wa kũĩkĩĩa kana "Ũla wĩw'aa mboya" nũsũngĩaa mboya sya kuma ngoonĩ sya andũ milioni mbingĩ. (Savuli 65:2) Yeova asũngĩaa mboya sitũ kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
17. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Ngai nũtũmĩaa alaĩka na athaithi make kũũ nthĩ kũsũngĩa mboya sitũ?
17 Yeova nũtũmĩaa alaĩka na athaithi make kũũ nthĩ kũsũngĩa mboya. (Aevelania 1:
18. Yeova atũmĩaa veva wake mũtheu na Ndeto yake ata kũsũngĩa mboya sya athaithi make?
18 Yeova Ngai nũtũmĩaa veva wake mũtheu na Ndeto yake Mbivilia kũsũngĩa mboya sya athaithi make. Nũtonya kũsũngĩa mboya sitũ sya kwĩtya ũtethyo wa kũmĩĩsya matatwa kwa kũtũnenga ũĩ na vinya kwĩsĩla veva wake mũtheu. (2 Akolintho 4:7) Mavinda maingĩ mboya sitũ nisũngĩawa kwĩsĩla Mbivilianĩ vala Yeova ũtũnengae ũtethyo wa kũtw'a maũndũ kwa ũĩ. Nĩtũtonya kũkwata maandĩko maũtũtethya yĩla tũũsoma Mbivilia ithyĩ ene na yĩla tũũsoma mavuku ma Kĩklĩsto ta ĩvuku yĩĩ. Nĩtũtonya kwĩw'a maandĩko matonya ũtũtethya mawũmbanonĩ ma Aklĩsto kana kwĩsĩla ndeto sya mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi ũkwenda tũendee nesa.
19. Twaĩle kũlilikana ata yĩla twoona mboya sitũ ta iteũsũngĩwa?
19 Twoona Yeova ateũsũngĩa mboya sitũ mĩtũkĩ, ũu ti kwonany'a ndatonya kũisũngĩa. Twaĩle kulilikana kana Yeova asũngĩaa mboya kwĩanana na kwenda kwake na ĩvinda yĩla yaĩle. Nĩwĩsĩ mavata maitũ na nĩwĩsĩ nesa mũno mbee witũ ũndũ mavata asu matonya kwĩanĩw'a. Mavinda amwe nũtũekaa tũendee 'kũvoya, kũmantha, na kũvingũsya.' (Luka 11:
20. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũtũmĩa nesa vyũ mwanya wa vata wa mboya ũla tũnengetwe?
20 Nĩtwaĩle kũtũnga mũvea nũndũ Mũmbi wa nthĩ yonthe e vakuvĩ na onthe ala mamũvoyaa kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle! (Savuli 145:18) Ekai tũtũmĩe nesa vyũ mwanya ũsu wa vata wa mboya tũnengetwe. Tweeka ũu, tũkeethĩwa na ũtanu wa kũthengeeaa Yeova, ũla Wĩw'aa mboya.

translation:
Are we truly appreciating God?
Do we sometimes wonder whether God even notices us?
Does God really care about us at all?
1, 2. Why are we able to see value in people, and why are we able to understand what the Bible says about our worth?
The nations of Jehovah, "gave them the lands," so they could have a place to live. (Psalm 115:15; Isaiah 40:15) The Bible states: "Jehovah supports everyone who falls, and straightens up those who are bent over. He pays attention to the needs of his people; he looks closely at their plight." (Psalm 145:
2 If we want Jehovah to notice us, we need to appreciate him in the way he wants to be appreciated. Can we then wonder whether we should learn what the Bible says about our worth? Understanding what the Bible teaches about our worth will help us to show more appreciation for Jehovah.
WHY ARE WE TRULY APPRECIATING JEHOVAH?
3. What important reason motivates us to appreciate God?
3 An important reason that motivates us to appreciate God is because he first showed love for us. His promise assures us: "Give thanks to him and bless his name. For he is good; his loving-kindness is forever, and his faithfulness extends to all generations. He remembers his wonderful works, he is gracious and compassionate, he is slow to anger and abundant in loving-kindness." (Psalm 118:
4. Does appreciating Jehovah strengthen our relationship with him?
4 Another reason to appreciate [God] is that appreciating Jehovah strengthens our relationship with him. Many people find this to be true. I have found that when I focus on the positive things, my outlook improves, and I feel better overall. Thinking about our relationship with Jehovah God helps us to stay focused on what is important. We come to know many things about what Jehovah does and how his purpose will work out. This knowledge is very encouraging. It moves us to share the good news with others and to talk about the things that matter most. Wondering about this motivates us to draw closer to Jehovah.
WHAT ELSE DO WE NEED TO APPRECIATE?
5. Why should we ask ourselves whether Jehovah answers all our prayers?
5 Does Jehovah answer all our prayers? Consider what the Israelites did, as recorded in Isaiah's prophecy: "You people keep praying more and more, but I do not listen; your hands are full of blood." (Isaiah 1:
6. A vital thing we need to appreciate is that God hears our prayers, and we can trust that he will answer them at the right time?
6 A vital thing we need to appreciate is being confident. (Mark 11:24) The apostle Paul wrote: "Without faith it is impossible to please [God]; for whoever wants to approach God must believe that he exists and that he becomes the rewarder of those who earnestly seek him." (Hebrews 11:6) Being confident does not mean that we tell God what to do, nor does it mean that we expect him to always answer our prayers in the way we want. Confidence is based on knowing what is involved. So let us examine confidence in the light of our daily life.
7. (a) How can we show that we appreciate what Jehovah does for us? (b) How can we be confident when facing difficult situations and still trust in God?
7 One thing Jehovah expects of us is to be confident when facing difficult situations. We need to express our feelings to Jehovah. Just as a person confides in a friend, we can speak to God openly and honestly, knowing that he cares about us. This shows that we appreciate what Jehovah does for us. (Psalm 138:6) He is "the Great God." (Revelation 19:1) What we believe about God should affect how we view his promises. If we have strong faith, we will not allow circumstances to discourage us, and we will continue to pray earnestly.
8. Can we ask for things that we do not really need?
8 One thing that would be wrong is to ask God for things that we do not really need. Jehovah wants us to ask for things that we can use to accomplish his purpose. He encourages us to ask for what we need to do his will. For example, if we pray, "Help me to be a better parent," we should be willing to put forth effort. (Matthew 6:
REASONS FOR PRAYING
9. Should we pray often, and why?
9 Should we pray regularly? Jesus taught his disciples to pray: "Our Father in the heavens, hallowed be your name." (Matthew 6:9) We should pray to Jehovah consistently. Jehovah wants us to know the value of his Son, Jesus Christ, his only-begotten son. And as explained in Chapter 5, Jesus showed the way by praying to his Father and asking for guidance. (John 3:
10. Why can we be confident when praying to Jehovah?
10 When we pray, can we be sure that Jehovah hears us? Yes, because Jehovah cares about our feelings. The Bible assures us that whether you are sick, discouraged, sad, or afraid. (1 Kings 17:16; Nehemiah 8:6; Daniel 6:
11. What practical benefits can come from prayer?
11 What else can prayer help us with? The Bible says: "If we ask according to his will, [Jehovah] listens to us." (1 John 5:
12. Can prayer help us to cope with difficult circumstances?
12 Difficult circumstances can strengthen our faith in Jehovah God. We have reason to trust Jehovah and to praise him for his loving-kindness. (1 Kings 29:
13. Does the Bible give examples of people who prayed during times of great stress?
13 Is our prayer heard when we are under pressure? The Bible shows that prayer helped individuals when they were facing problems or when they needed to guide others. We can find comfort in prayer, or prayer can help us to show Jehovah appreciation. (1 Samuel 1:
14. Does the Bible encourage us to pray constantly, and what does this involve?
14 Should we pray on every occasion? The Bible encourages us to 'pray without ceasing,' 'be joyful in hope,' and 'persevere in prayer.' (Luke 18:1; Romans 12:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:
15. What does it mean to say "Amen" at the end of our prayers, and why is it appropriate to do so?
15 Should we say "Amen" at the end of our prayers? "Amen" means "so be it." The Bible shows that it is proper to say "Amen" at the end of our prayers. (1 Kings 16:36; Psalm 41:13) When we say "Amen" at the end of our prayers, we express our heartfelt desire or confirm our belief. Saying "Amen"
GOD HEARS OUR PRAYERS
16. What confidence can we have when we pray?
16 Does Jehovah hear our prayers? Yes, he hears them! We have good reason to believe that "the listening ear" hears our prayers from millions of people. (Psalm 65:2) Jehovah hears our prayers because he cares about us.
17. How does Jehovah use angels and holy spirit to support our prayers?
17 Jehovah uses angels and holy spirit to assist in answering our prayers. (Revelation 1:
18. Does Jehovah use his Son and his Word to answer our prayers?
18 Jehovah God uses his Son and his Word, the Bible, to answer our prayers. We can trust that he will help us find strength when facing trials by guiding us through his Word. (2 Corinthians 4:7) Many scriptures show that our prayers are answered through the Bible, which Jehovah inspires to give us direction. We can benefit from carefully considering what we read in the Bible and what we learn from Christian publications such as this magazine. We can also apply what we learn from faithful Christians or from the circuit overseer when he visits our congregation.
19. What can we do to improve our prayers?
19 We know that Jehovah answers our prayers, but sometimes we may wonder why they are not answered right away. We can be confident that Jehovah hears our prayers and answers them in harmony with his purpose and timing. It is comforting to remember that Jehovah cares for us and wants what is best for us. Some of us may feel like giving up, becoming 'discouraged, tired, and frustrated.' (Luke 11:
20. How can we approach Jehovah confidently when we pray?
20 We can come boldly to him because our Creator loves us and is interested in everything we do! (Psalm 145:18) Let us therefore approach Jehovah confidently when we pray. Remember, we are motivated by our love for Jehovah, who hears our prayers.

text:
WE NĨWĨSĨ ũvw'anene na ala athani ma tene kwa nzĩa yĩva? Kĩlungunĩ kĩtawa "Glossary of Bible Terms" kĩla kĩ ĩla Mbivilianĩ ya 2013 ya New World Translation ndeto "mwathani" ĩeleetw'e ũũ: "Ũla ũtavasya ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa ieleelo sya Ngai. Athani matavasya andũ ndeto sya Ngai. Na maũndũ amwe mamatavasya nĩ mawathani ma Yeova na momanyĩsyo make, vamwe na mĩao yake, na mosilĩlo make." Naku we o na kau ndwĩthĩawa ũyathana, nũtavanasya ndeto sya Ngai kwa kũtavya andũ kĩla kĩ Ndetonĩ yake.—Mt. 24:14.
Nĩtũnengetwe ndaĩa nene mũno ya kũtavya ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa Ngai witũ, Yeova, na kũmamanyĩsya kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa andũ. Tũtethasya wĩa ũsu vamwe na ũla 'mũlaĩka ũũlũkĩle ĩtunĩ katĩ.' (Ũvu. 14:6) Ĩndĩ nĩtũtonya kũkwatwa nĩ maũndũ me vinya nginya tũkona kũtethya wĩa ũsu tate ndaĩa nene. Maũndũ amwe matonya kũtũkwata nĩ meva? Nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mĩnoo, tũkakw'a ngoo, kana tũkona ta tũte ma vata. O namo ala athani aĩkĩĩku ma tene nĩmakwatiwe nĩ maũndũ ta asu, ĩndĩ mayaaĩkya ngoo. Nake Yeova nĩwamatetheeisye meanĩsya mawĩa ala wamanengete. Kwaekai tũneene ĩũlũ wa amwe moo nĩ kana twone ũndũ tũtonya kwĩyĩelekany'a namo.
MAĨ NA KĨTHETHEESYO WĨANĨ WOO
Mavinda amwe nĩtũtonya kũnow'a nĩ maũndũ ala twĩkaa kĩla mũthenya ũkethĩa twĩĩw'a tũtathi ũtavany'a. Vate nzika, ti ũthũku kũthyũmũa nũndũ o nake Yesũ na atũmwa make nĩmathyũmũaa. (Mko. 6:31) Ĩndĩ kwamba kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Esekieli ĩvinda waĩ Mbaviloni. E kũu vamwe na Aisilaeli ala angĩ maĩ manatavwa Yelusaleme makatwawa kũu nĩwanengiwe wĩa mũna atethye. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Ngai amwĩie ose ĩvali na aivana ĩũlũ wayo ndũa ya Yelusaleme. Na nĩ kana ndũa ĩsu wavanie ĩvalinĩ yĩkale ta yĩlingĩlĩtwe nĩ ita, Esekieli eeiwe nĩekumbĩĩe ĩvali yĩu akomete na ĩvava yake ya kw'oko kwa aka kwa ĩvinda ya mĩthenya 390, na aisyoka eke oou akomete na ĩvava yake ya kw'oko kwa aũme kwa ĩvinda ya mĩthenya 40. Yeova eeie Esekieli atĩĩ: "Sisya, nĩngũkwĩkĩa syĩndũ sya ũkwova, na ndũkealyũla, kũvika yĩla ũkeanĩsya mĩthenya ya kũtw'ĩkanĩw'a kwaku." (Esek. 4:1-8) No nginya Aisilaeli asu maĩ atave makethĩwa mendie kũmanya nĩ kyaũ Esekieli waendeesye. Esekieli eeaĩwe athũkũme wĩa ũsu wĩ mĩnoo kwa ĩvinda yĩthonokete mwaka ũmwe. Mwathani ũsu esaa kwĩanĩsya wĩa ũsu ata?
Esekieli nĩweesĩ nĩkĩ wanengiwe wĩa wa kwathana. Ĩla Ngai wamũtũmaa amwĩie atĩĩ: "Nao, ethĩwa [Aisilaeli] makeew'a, kana matikew'a . . . , nĩmakamanya kana kwaĩ mwathani katĩ woo." (Esek. 2:5) Esekieli ekalaa alilikene nĩkĩ wanengiwe wĩa wa kwathana. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu atethisye na ngenda wĩa ũla wanengiwe wa kũkoma ekumbĩĩe yĩla ĩvali wavanĩte ndũa ya Yelusaleme. Kwĩka ũu kwoonanisye aĩ mwathani wa w'o. Ĩtina e na Aisilaeli ala angĩ maĩ Mbaviloni nĩmakwatie livoti ĩkwasya kana "ndũa nĩ ngũne." Vate nzika, Aisilaeli nĩmamanyie kana kwaĩ mwathani katĩ woo.—Esek. 33:21, 33.
Ũmũnthĩ nĩtũtavasya andũ kana nthĩ yonthe ya Satani yeteele kwanangwa. O na ethĩwa twĩ anou, nĩtũtũmĩaa vinya witũ kũtavya andũ ĩũlũ wa Ndeto ya Ngai, kũsyokea ala mendeew'a, na kũmamanyĩsya Mbivilia. Na ĩla twoona mawathani ala makonetye mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ ĩno maendeee kwĩanĩa, twĩw'aa twĩ eanĩe nũndũ twĩthĩawa twatũmĩwa ta "ũla ũtavasya ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa ieleelo sya Ngai."
O NA KAU NĨMAKUSAA NGOO, NĨMOOSAA VINYA
Tũtethasya wĩa witũ na kĩthetheesyo tũtetheew'e nĩ veva wa Yeova. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtũtonya kũkw'a ngoo twoona andũ mailea ũvoo ũla tũũmatavya. Kwoou nũseo tũkalilikanaa ngelekany'o ya mwathani Yelemia. Nĩwavũĩwe ngũĩ, aumangwa, na athekeewa nũndũ wa kũtavya Aisilaeli ũvoo wa Ngai. O na ve vandũ vavikiwe Yelemia asya: "Ndikamũweta, kana kũneena ĩngĩ syĩtwanĩ yake." Yelemia aĩ mũndũ o taitũ. Ĩndĩ o na kau nĩwakusaa ngoo, ndaaeka kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ngai. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ asyokie asya atĩĩ: "Ngoonĩ yakwa ve ta mwaki mwakanu ũvingĩĩtwe mavĩndĩnĩ makwa, na nĩ na mĩnoo ũndũ wa kũmĩĩsya, o na nditonya kwĩsiĩĩa."—Yel. 20:7-9.
O naitũ no twĩke ta Yelemia ĩla twakw'a ngoo nũndũ wa kwona andũ mate kwĩtĩkĩla ũvoo witũ. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũvoo ũla tũtavanasya. Tweeka ũu tũkeew'aa ta ve 'mwaki mwakanu ũvingĩĩtwe mavĩndĩnĩ maitũ.' Na tweethĩwa na kĩmanyĩo kya kũsomaa Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya, mwaki ũsu ũkekalaa wakanĩte mavĩndĩnĩ maitũ.
NĨMATATIE METHĨWE NA WONI MŨSEO
Aklĩsto amwe nĩmew'aa mate eanĩe manewa wĩa mate kũũelewa nesa. O nake mwathani Osea nũtonya kwĩthĩwa eewie oou. Yeova amwĩaĩe atĩĩ: "Enda, wĩtwaĩe kĩveti ĩlwaya na syana sya ũmalwaya." (Osea 1:2) Kwasũanĩa ũvangĩte kũtwaana na ũyĩwa nĩ Ngai ũthi ũtwae mũndũ mũka ĩlwaya! Ĩndĩ Osea nĩweetĩkĩlile kwĩka ũu. Nĩwatwaie Ngomeli na mekalangĩte Ngomeli asyaa kavĩsĩ. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩwasyaie kelĩtu na asyoka asyaa kavĩsĩ kangĩ. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa syana isu ilĩ sya ĩtina syaĩ sya ũmalwaya. Yeova nĩwatavĩtye Osea kana mũndũ mũka ũla ũkatwaa "akaatĩĩa endwa make." Ndeto ĩsu "endwa" yĩonany'a kana kĩveti kĩu kyendete aũme aingĩ. Na ĩndĩ kyamina kũsembany'a na endwa makyo Yeova aĩtye kĩkatata kũmũsyokea Osea. Yu keka nue mwathani ũsu, nĩwĩtĩkĩla kĩveti kĩu ĩngĩ? Ĩndĩ ũu nĩw'o Yeova weeie Osea nĩeke! O na mwathani ũsu aumisye mbesa mbingĩ mũno nĩ kana akyose ĩngĩ.—Osea 2:7; 3:1-5.
Osea nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aseng'aa kwĩka maũndũ asu weeĩtwe eke kwesaa kũtethya ata. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Osea nĩweekie ũndũ weeĩtwe, ũmũnthĩ nĩtũmanyaa nesa vyũ woo ũla Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe weewie ĩla Aisilaeli mamũtiie na maatĩĩa ngai ingĩ. Na ũw'o nĩ kana Aisilaeli amwe ala maĩ na ngoo nzeo nĩmamũsyokeie Ngai.
Vai mũndũ o na ũmwe ũmũnthĩ waaĩwa nĩ Ngai 'atwae kĩveti ĩlwaya.' Ĩndĩ ve kĩndũ tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya twasisya ũndũ Osea weetĩkĩlile na ngenda kwĩka ũndũ weeĩtwe. Ũndũ ũmwe tũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩ kana nĩtwaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla na ngenda wĩa wa kũtavany'a "andũnĩ, [na] nyũmba na nyũmba," o na ethĩwa twĩw'aa tũte eanĩe tũyĩka ũu. (Meko 20:20) No kwĩthĩwa wonaa nzĩa imwe sya kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ syĩ vinya mũno. O na andũ aingĩ memanyĩasya na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova maasyaa kana nĩmatanĩaa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ĩndĩ maasyaa mayĩsa kũthi maikũnanga mĩomo ya andũ angĩ mamatavye ũvoo. Mũthya aingĩ moo mekalaa makesa kũtethya wĩa ũsu moonaa mataũtonya. Ve ũndũ weemanyĩsya vau?
Ve ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya twasisya ũndũ Osea weetĩkĩlile kwĩka ũndũ weeĩtwe nĩeke. Keka nĩwendaa ethĩwa eesũvanie ndakatwae kĩla kĩveti. Na we kwasũanĩa nĩ mũndũ ũngĩ wĩva wĩthĩwa aamanya kana Osea nĩwatavĩtw'e eke ũndũ ũsu keka ũ Osea mwene ndaandĩka ũvoo ũsu? O naitũ no tũkwatwe nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu. Nĩtũtonya kũkwata mwanya mũseo wa kũtavya mũndũ ũngĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova na ũyĩthĩa vai mũndũ ũngĩ wĩsĩ kana nĩtũnakwatie mwanya ta ũsu. Ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Anna kuma Amelika wakwatiwe nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu e sekondalĩ na mũthenya ũmwe me kĩlasinĩ meeiwe nĩ mwalimũ woo nĩmaandĩke ũvoo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũna kĩla ũmwe waĩkĩĩe vyũ, na ĩndĩ kĩla ũmwe ayũka eyũmbanĩtye kũelesya ala angĩ nginya metĩkĩlane nake. Anna ethĩwa aemie kũtũmĩa mwanya ũsu kumya ũkũsĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩwamanyie kana ũsu waĩ mwanya wanengwa nĩ Ngai. Nĩweesĩ kana ĩla ũkũmatavya nĩmatonya kũema kwĩtĩkĩlana nake, ĩndĩ nĩwavoyie Yeova na eew'a amesya wendi wa kũtũmĩa mwanya ũsu nesa. Aandĩkie ũvoo wĩ na kyongo "Syũmbe Syeekie Kwĩyumĩlya: Ũu Nĩ W'o?"
Kĩlasinĩ kyoo vaĩ mwĩĩtu ũmwe waĩkĩĩaa kana syũmbe syeekie kwĩyumĩlya. Ĩla Anna wasomeie kĩlasi kĩu ũla ũvoo waandĩkĩte, mwĩĩtu ũsu amũkananĩisye na makũlyo kĩatĩanĩsyo. Ĩndĩ Anna nĩweeteteie nesa. Mwalimũ woo nĩwendeeiw'e mũno na anenga Anna mũthĩnzĩo nũndũ nowe waandĩkĩte ũvoo mũseo ũkethĩa mũndũ no etĩkĩlane naw'o. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu Anna nũneenete mavinda kauta ĩũlũ wa wũmbi e na mwĩĩtu ũsu wamũkananĩasya. Nũndũ nĩwatũmĩie mwanya ũsu wanengiwe nĩ Yeova nesa, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Yu nĩndavanasya vyũ ũvoo mũseo ndeũkĩa."
O na kau ithyĩ tũi athani tondũ ala athani ma tene meethĩawa mailyĩ, ĩla tweeyumya vyũ o tondũ Esekieli, Yelemia, na Osea meeyumisye, no twĩanĩsye kĩla Yeova wendaa twĩke ũmũnthĩ! Ĩvinda ya ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ kana o ĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya wĩ weka, wĩona ata ũkemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa athani angĩ ma tene na ũisũanĩa ũndũ ũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o syoo

translation:
ARE WE witnesses who are outstandingly zealous in proclaiming good news? The book "Glossary of Bible Terms," on page 19 of the 2013 edition of the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures, defines "zealous" as follows: "Eagerly devoted to a cause or purpose. Zealous people are devoted to God. And some things to which they are devoted are Jehovah's name and his worship, others his laws, and still others his service." But if you also personally feel this way, let us zealously proclaim God's purposes by helping people of all nations to become disciples of Jesus.—Matt. 24:14.
Let us be deeply moved by our desire to proclaim God's purposes to mankind, Jehovah, and to make known his Kingdom. Let us cooperate with the force of the "large angel" who flies in midheaven. (Rev. 14:6) Indeed, we want to avoid getting caught up in anxieties that could hinder our cooperation in this important work. What are some things that might catch us off guard? We might be distracted by material possessions, get discouraged, or simply lose sight of what is vital. So those zealous ones who are truly active are often confronted with trials, yet they remain courageous. Because Jehovah strengthens them to cope with difficulties. Let us therefore examine ourselves to see if we can continue to improve in this regard.
MORE AND FURTHER INFORMATION
Some of us may find it difficult to deal with situations that trouble us daily and prevent us from being productive. But remember, it is not because Jesus and his angels stop supporting us. (Mark 6:31) Indeed, let us consider the vision of Ezekiel concerning Babylon. And just as the Israelites of ancient times were taken captive to Jerusalem and then allowed to return home, God showed Ezekiel a vision of a symbolic wall around Jerusalem. In that vision, God commanded him to measure its length and width, and he measured 490 cubits on each side. Then he saw a gate on the east side measuring 40 cubits. Jehovah told Ezekiel: "Go, take a roll of papyrus and sketch out a representation of Jerusalem, and write upon it." (Ezek. 4:1-8) However, the ancient Israelites did not understand why Ezekiel was doing these things. Ezekiel acted like this for 390 days, lying on his left side for a year to symbolize their sins. How can we apply this lesson to ourselves today?
Ezekiel was initially considered responsible for the people's captivity. But God reassured him, saying: "As for the house of Israel, they are rebellious, exceedingly rebellious…they will know that I am Jehovah." (Ezek. 2:5) Ezekiel felt responsible for the people's captivity. He had been appointed to warn them, and he feared that they would blame him when Jerusalem fell. This is why he asked how he could bear such responsibility. Just as Ezekiel warned the Israelites about the consequences of their actions, we too should use our voice to help people learn about God's Kingdom, especially those who are suffering, and to share the Bible. And when we see events unfolding that seem to confirm the truth of prophecy, we should be confident that we have been assigned to proclaim "the good news of God's kingdom."
However, we must always remember that Satan tries to mislead people. So even though we are zealous, we must use our voice to help people learn about God's Kingdom, to comfort the distressed, and to share the Bible. And when we see events unfolding that seem to confirm the truth of prophecy, we should be confident that we have been assigned to proclaim "the good news of God's kingdom."
AND IF YOU ARE STRONG, USE YOUR VOICE
We can speak to others with boldness, relying on Jehovah's support. In fact, if we want to reach people who are deeply affected by the message we deliver, we need to be courageous. We can take courage from Jeremiah's example. He was persecuted, imprisoned, and threatened because of his warning the Israelites to turn back to God. Yet, despite facing such opposition, Jeremiah said: "I will continue speaking, or I will fall silent." Jeremiah was a determined man. And if you are strong, do not hesitate to declare God's purpose. Why? Because he said: "My words are like a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary of holding them in, and I cannot contain myself."—Jer. 20:7-9.
Like Jeremiah, we may encounter opposition when we try to help people understand the truth. We can cope with this by focusing on the importance of the message we are delivering. Let us resolve to be like those who "will not hold back their words." And by regularly studying the Bible, that fire can remain burning within us.
LET US BE BOLD AND ZEALOUS
One Christian sister found it difficult to express herself clearly. She studied the prophecy of Hosea and learned how to be more effective. Jehovah told him: "Go, take yourself a wife among adulteresses and have children of adultery." (Hosea 1:2) Imagine how shocking it would be for a man to be instructed by God to marry an immoral woman! Hosea accepted this assignment. He married Gomer, and she repeatedly proved unfaithful. The pain this caused him was similar to what someone feels when betrayed by a beloved child. He did not give up on her. Jehovah did not condemn Hosea for being associated with "adultery," but rather used it to illustrate a vital point. Just as Gomer kept returning to her immorality, so too Israel repeatedly turned away from Jehovah. But Jehovah continued to show compassion toward Hosea and his unfaithful wife. So ask yourself, will you also extend forgiveness?—Hos. 2:7; 3:1-5.
Hosea's experience shows us how important it is to speak truthfully, even when it is difficult. However, Hosea's story teaches us something deeper—something that helps us understand why our heavenly Father allows his people, Israel, to suffer and endure trials. And this understanding can help us remain loyal to God despite facing difficulties.
Like Hosea, each of us has been shown undeserved kindness by God. To appreciate fully what Hosea experienced, let us consider what he symbolized. One thing we can learn from his example is that we should be willing to forgive others, even those who wrong us severely, and continue to associate with them. (Matt. 20:20) This does not mean that we should approve of their wrongdoing, but it does require us to demonstrate love. Many find it challenging to apply this principle, especially when they feel hurt or offended. They may struggle to put aside their feelings and continue associating with the person who wronged them. What can help us do so?
Let us again consider what Hosea experienced to illustrate what he symbolized. Imagine that someone deeply loves another and would do almost anything to save him. Would that person wonder whether God feels the same way about us, and whether God truly values us? We need to remember that God is willing to forgive us. It is vital that we take time to reflect on this truth. We can strengthen our resolve to remain loyal to Jehovah by asking ourselves: 'What if someone like Anna, an American sister, were struggling with a similar situation?' This sister explained that she was attending secondary school and had a classmate who constantly made fun of her because of her faith. She also said that this classmate often tried to get others to ridicule her. Anna decided to use this opportunity to share the good news with her classmate. She realized that God might be giving her an opportunity to show love. She prayed to Jehovah and asked for his guidance in knowing how to respond. She wrote a letter and included the question, "Why Should People Care About You?"
In class, one student asked why people should care about anyone. But Anna read the letter she had written, and the student responded with genuine interest. Anna felt encouraged. The teacher noticed this and praised Anna for writing such a thoughtful letter. Because of this, Anna had further opportunities to talk to the student. Over time, Anna helped the student see things from a different perspective and eventually became friends with her. This shows that when we use our ministry, we may be helping someone whom Jehovah cares about deeply, and they may say, "You have really touched my heart with your message."
But sometimes we feel discouraged because people seem unresponsive, yet Ezekiel, Jeremiah, and Hosea did not give up, and we too can please Jehovah if we persevere! If you find yourself feeling isolated, remember that there are many others who feel the same way, and don't hesitate to seek support from fellow believers.

text:
KWASŨANĨA nĩ mavinda meva wĩw'aa mũyo wamalilikana. Nĩ ĩla watwaanie kana watwaiwe, kana nĩ ĩla mwasyaie kana kenyu ka mbee? Nao nĩwĩthĩwa ne mũthenya ũla wavatisiwe? Mũthenya ũsu waĩle kwĩthĩwa new'o mũthenya wa vata vyũ thayũnĩ waku na waĩle kũtana mũno vyũ waũlilikana. Namo Aklĩsto ala angĩ matanie mũno ĩla moonie woonany'a ũtheinĩ kana nĩwendete Ngai na ngoo yaku yonthe, na thayũ waku w'onthe, na kĩlĩko kyaku kyonthe, na vinya waku w'onthe!—Mko. 12:30.
No nginya wĩthĩwe ũtanĩĩte mũno kũmũthũkũma Yeova kuma ĩla wavatisiwe. Ĩndĩ atavany'a amwe ma Ũsumbĩ nĩmaekete kwĩthĩwa me atanu tondũ mailyĩ tene. Nĩkĩ vekalĩte ũu? Twĩ na itumi syĩva sya kũendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ atanu?
KĨLA KĨTUMĨTE AMWE MAEKA KŨMŨTHŨKŨMA YEOVA ME ATANU
Ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ nũtumaa tũtana mũno. Ũvoo ũsu nĩ kana o mĩtũkĩ Yeova nũkwananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku na aiete nthĩ ĩngĩ nzaũ. O na ĩngĩ ĩandĩko ya Nzevania 1:14 yĩtũĩkĩĩthasya ũũ: "Mũthenya mũnene wa Yeova wĩ vakuvĩ, wĩ vakuvĩ na nĩwĩkalaatĩte mũno." Ĩndĩ nĩtũtonya kwona mũthenya wa Yeova ta wĩkalĩte mũno kũte ũndũ twasũanĩaa. Kĩu nĩ kĩndũ kĩtonya kũtuma twasya ũtanu na tũileela ũthũkũminĩ witũ.—Nth. 13:12.
Kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ya kwaka vamwe na andũ ma Ngai nĩkũtwĩkĩaa vinya tũendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ atanu. O na no kwĩthĩwa mwĩkalĩle wa athũkũmi ma Yeova now'o watumie twenda ũla w'o na watuma twambĩĩa kũmũthũkũma twĩ atanu. (1 Vet. 2:12) Ĩndĩ nata Mũklĩsto akosewa ĩtambya nũndũ wa kũema kwĩkala kwosana na mĩao ya Ngai? Vekala ũu amwe ala mendeeiw'e nĩ ũw'o nũndũ wa kwona mwĩkalĩle mũseo wa andũ ma Yeova nĩmatonya kũkw'a ngoo na maieka kwĩthĩwa me atanu.
Kwenda malĩ mũno o nakw'o nĩkũtonya kũtuma Mũklĩsto aeka kwĩthĩwa e mũtanu ta tene. Ndevili atũmĩaa nthĩ ĩno yake nĩ kana atume tũĩkĩĩa kana twaĩle kũthooa syĩndũ mbingĩ o na ila ite sya vata. Ĩndĩ nũseo tũkalilikanaa ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Kũi mũndũ ũtonya kũthũkũma mavwana elĩ: nũndũ akamũmena ũmwe, na akamwenda ũla ũngĩ; kana akalũman'ya na ũmwe, na akamũvũthya ũla ũngĩ. Mũitonya kũthũkũma Ngai o na ũthwii." (Mt. 6:24) Vaitonyeka tũkamũthũkũma Yeova twĩ atanu na ũyĩthĩa ngalĩko ĩla ĩngĩ twĩkĩĩte kĩthito twĩthĩwe na syĩndũ syonthe ila tũtonya kũkwata nthĩ ĩno.
'KŨTANĨA NGAI WA ŨTANGĨĨO WITŨ'
Ala mendete Yeova mayĩw'aa vinya wa kũmũthũkũma. (1 Yoa. 5:3) Lilikana kana Yesũ aisye: "Ũkai kwakwa, inyw'othe ala mũthĩnĩaa wĩa na ala mwĩ na mĩio mĩito, nakwa ngamũthũmũsya. Ĩyĩkĩei ĩsoki yakwa, na mũimanyĩw'a ninyie; nũndũ nyie nĩ mũuu na nĩ na wĩnyivyo ngoonĩ: nenyu mũkasyonea ngoo syenyu ũthũmũo. Nũndũ ĩsoki yakwa yĩti vinya, na mũio wakwa naw'o nĩ mũvũthũ." (Mt. 11:28-30) Kwoou kwĩyĩkĩa ĩsoki ya Ũklĩsto wa w'o kũtumaa tũtana na twĩw'a twathũmũa. Na vate nzika, twĩ na kĩtumi kya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno ĩla tũũmũthũkũma Yeova. Ekai ĩndĩ tũneenee maũndũ atatũ ma vata ala meũtwony'a nĩkĩ nĩtũtonya 'kũtanĩa Ngai wa ũtangĩĩo witũ.'—Ava. 3:18.
Tũthũkũmaa ũla watũnengie thayũ, nake nĩ Ngai mũtanu. (Meko 17:28) Nĩtwĩsĩ kana keka ti va Mũmbi witũ tũyĩthĩwa vo. Na kwoou o na ethĩwa vavĩtĩte myaka yĩana ata kuma twavatiswa, tũendeeaa kũmũthũkũma twĩ atanu.
Kwasũanĩa mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Héctor, ũla wamũthũkũmie Yeova e mũsyaĩĩsya wa kũthyũlũlũka kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 40. O na 'e mũkũu' no ũendeee kũtanĩa kũmũthũkũma Yeova. (Sav. 92:12-14) Mũka nĩ mũwau na kĩu nĩkĩtumĩte Héctor ethĩwa atatonya kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yingĩ aimũthũkũma Ngai ta tene. Ĩndĩ thĩna ũsu ndũtumĩte aeka kwĩthĩwa e mũtanu. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "O na kau ndyĩw'aa mũyo noona kĩveti kyakwa kĩithĩnw'a nĩ mwĩĩ na kũkĩsũvĩa ti ũndũ wĩ laisi, ndyaaĩsa kwĩtĩkĩlya ũndũ ũsu ũtume nĩeka kũtanĩa kũmũthũkũma ũla Ngai wa w'o. Kĩla kĩndetheeasya kũmwenda Yeova vyũ na kũmũthũkũma na ngoo yonthe nĩ kũmanya kana nĩwe ũtumĩte nĩendeea kwĩthĩwa nĩ thayũ na kana oombie mũndũ e na kĩtumi. Nĩ kana ndikaeke kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũtanu, nĩtataa mũno nĩthĩwe na kĩthito ũtavany'anĩ na nĩnĩtataa kwĩkala nĩlilikene maũndũ ala Ũsumbĩ ũkatwĩka."
Yeova nĩwatũnengie nthembo ya wovosyo, na kwoou atuma twĩthĩwa tũtonya kwĩkala twĩ atanu. Nĩ w'o vyũ, nũndũ "Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ, nĩwanenganie mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmwĩtĩkĩlaa ndakae, ĩndĩ ethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela." (Yoa. 3:16) Kwoou nĩtũtonya kũekewa naĩ sitũ na tũyĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa thayũ ũtathela twaĩkĩĩa nthembo ya Yesũ ĩla Ngai watũnengie nũndũ nũtwendete. Ve kĩtumi kĩseo ta kĩu kya kũmũtũngĩa Ngai mũvea? Na tyo w'o kana ethĩwa nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo, tũilea kwĩthĩwa tũimũthũkũma Yeova twĩ atanu?
Mwana-a-asa Jesús kuma Mexico aisye ũũ: "Wĩa wakwa wandw'ĩte ngombo, na mavinda amwe nathũkũmaa masaa maingĩ mũno o na kau ndyaĩ lasima nĩke ũu. Nathũkũmaa ũu nĩ kana nzeũvye mbesa mbingangĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩnesie kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova na ũndũ waumisye Mwana wake mwendwa kwondũ wa andũ. Kyu kyatumie nĩthĩwa na wendi mwingĩ mũno wa kũmũthũkũma. Nĩneeyumisye nĩmũthũkũme Yeova, na natia kambunĩ ĩla nathũkũmĩe vandũ va myaka 28 nĩ kana nĩtw'ĩke mũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe." Kuma vu aminie myaka aimũthũkũma Yeova e mũtanu.
Mwĩkalĩle ũla yu twĩ naw'o ndũtumaa twĩmakĩa, ĩndĩ ũtumaa tũtana mũno. Nũlilikene ũndũ wekalaa ũtambĩte kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova? Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkĩe Aklĩsto ala maĩ Lomi amalilikanĩtye kana ĩvinda yĩmwe maĩ "ngombo sya naĩ," ĩndĩ nĩmaalyũkĩte makatw'ĩka "ngombo sya ũlũngalu." Ũsyao wa Aklĩsto asu 'nĩwavikĩte kũvathĩka,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, mwĩkalĩle woo waĩ mũtheu, na kwoou waĩ ũtonya kũtuma mesa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. (Alo. 6:17-22) O naitũ twĩkalaa mwĩkalĩle mũtheu, na kwoou tũyĩmakĩaa nũndũ tũikwatawa nĩ mathĩna ala makwataa andũ me na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku na wa ũng'endu. We wĩona ũsu ta ũtanu wĩana ata?
Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Jaime. Tene ndaĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai na ndaĩkĩĩaa kana syĩndũ syeekie kũmbwa. O na nĩwathaũkaa ĩthaũ ya kũkita yĩtawa boxing. Nĩwambĩĩe kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto na endeew'a mũno nĩ wendo ũla woonie vau. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana aekane na mwĩkalĩle wake, eethĩie no nginya amũvoye Yeova amũtetheesye aĩkĩĩe kana e kw'o. Jaime easya atĩĩ: "O kavola kwa kavola nesie kũmanya kana kwĩ Asa ũtwendete na we nĩ Ngai wĩ tei." Aendeee kwasya: "Kũkwata ĩla mĩao mĩlũngalu ya Yeova nĩkwĩthĩĩtwe kũinzũvĩa. Keka ndyaalyũka nĩthĩwa nakwie o tondũ amwe ala twathaũkaa ĩmwe yĩla ĩthaũ ya boxing makwie. Myaka ĩla mĩseo vyũ ya thayũ wakwa nĩ ĩla nĩthĩĩtwe ngĩmũthũkũma Yeova."
NDŨKANOE!
We wĩona ta twaĩle kwĩw'a ata kavindanĩ kaa tweteele mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno nthũku? Lilikana kana 'tũvuĩaa ũla veva,' na kwoou 'tũkaketha thayũ ũtathela.' Nũndũ wa ũu, "tũikanoe nĩ kwĩka nesa: nũndũ kyathĩ kyavika tũkaketha, ethĩwa tũileela." (Aka. 6:8, 9) Kwoou kwa vinya wa Yeova, ekai tũendeee kũmĩĩsya, tũendeee kwĩkĩa kĩthito twĩthĩwe na nguma ila itonya kũtũtetheesya twĩvonoka "thĩnanĩ ũla mũnene," na nĩtũendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ atanu o na twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna.—Ũvu. 7:9, 13, 14; Yak. 1:2-4.
No twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana tũkanewa ĩtuvi twoomĩĩsya. Twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu nũndũ Ngai nĩwonaa nesa vyũ ũndũ tũmũthũkũmaa, na nĩwĩsĩ nesa kana nĩtũmwendete na nĩtwendete ĩsyĩtwa yake. Twaendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ atanu, tũkekala ta mũandĩki wa Savuli, Ndaviti, ũla waisye atĩĩ: "Nĩmwiĩte Yeova mbee wakwa mavinda onthe: nĩkwĩthĩwa e kw'okonĩ kwakwa kwa aũme, ndikathingithangw'a. Kwondũ wa ũu ngoo yakwa yĩ na ũtanu, na ũnene wakwa nũtanaa: mwĩĩ wakwa naw'o ũkatũaa vate mũisyo."—Sav. 16:8, 9.
