translation:
IT IS wonderful to have new friends who are interested in the truth. Is it because they were invited or because they came themselves, or is it because you spoke to them or visited them? And are they being strengthened by those who were baptized? This week try to strengthen those newly interested people and help them to progress. And let Christians always have this goal: to use their entire life to praise God and to preach to all people, and to all places, and with all their energy!—Matt. 12:30.
Do not let anything hinder you from praising Jehovah among those who were baptized. Some may feel that they need to spend five minutes each day doing so. Is this true? Should we not have good reasons for wanting to praise Jehovah daily?
EVERY REASON TO PRAISE JEHOVAH DAILY
The Bible urges us to progress. This means that if you love Jehovah, you will want to show more zeal. Also, the scripture at Romans 1:14 encourages us, saying: "I am eager to declare the good news to you also." So we should be eager to see Jehovah's work progress. It is something that can motivate us to serve him more fully.—Phil. 13:12.
Being associated with others who love God helps us to continue praising Jehovah daily. Also, being around zealous servants of Jehovah motivates us to go out and motivates us to praise him daily. (1 Pet. 2:12) But how can a Christian make sure he does not become too busy with his own affairs to give priority to spiritual things? By regularly examining himself, he can see whether his attitude toward the congregation is helping him to stay zealous and to praise Jehovah daily.
Going forward daily and doing so is something that can help a Christian remain zealous in his service forever. However, Satan uses this to try to get us to think that we have done enough and to stop serving. But we must remember Jesus' warning: "No one can slave for two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will cling to the one and despise the other. You cannot slave for God and wealth." (Matt. 6:24) We can continue praising Jehovah daily and reject any other interests that might distract us from our worship.
'SERVE THE GOD OF OUR FOREFATHERS'
Also, Jehovah appreciates sincere affection. (1 John 5:3) Remember what Jesus said: "Come to me, all those who are toiling and burdened, and I will refresh you. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am mild-tempered and lowly in heart, and you will find refreshment for yourselves. For my yoke is easy and my load is light." (Matt. 11:28-30) By applying the teachings of Christ, we can be strengthened to endure trials and difficulties. And when we do, we show that we are serious about praising Jehovah. Let us therefore make sure that we do everything we can to 'serve the God of our forefathers.'—Acts 3:18.
We praise him for the life we have, because he is the living God. (Acts 17:28) Let us always remember that he is our Creator and that we owe him our lives. And let us continue to praise him daily, no matter how old we become.
Consider the example of a young man named Héctor, who praised Jehovah for over 40 years while facing challenges. He continued to 'excel' in serving Jehovah. (Ps. 92:12-14) His family saw his zeal and were encouraged to use their time to praise God more fully. They realized that they needed to give priority to spiritual matters. One of them said: "I came to realize that my life was meaningless without a purpose, so I decided to devote my life to serving the true God. The more I learned about Jehovah and praised him with all my heart, the more I understood that he uses people to help others and that he cares for us. If I stop giving him priority, I know that I will feel empty and dissatisfied, and I will not be able to enjoy life as much."—
1 Cor. 13:1.
Jehovah gives us the gift of everlasting life, and through his Son, he makes it possible for us to live forever. That is why we can confidently say: "God loved the world so much that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who puts faith in him may have everlasting life." (John 3:16) Through this provision, we can look forward to living eternally under peaceful conditions thanks to the sacrifice of Jesus, which God provided for us. But what can we do to show our gratitude to God? And how can we make sure that we continue to benefit from the gift of everlasting life by remaining loyal to Jehovah?
A young brother named Jesús from Mexico shared this experience: "I used to get very angry, and sometimes I would spend hours thinking about things that bothered me and feeling sorry for myself. This made me feel miserable. So I decided to learn more about Jehovah and his love for mankind expressed through his Son. This motivated me to serve as a full-time evangelizer. I am now very happy to be able to help others learn about Jehovah, and I have been serving as an evangelizer for 28 years." He has been helping people to learn about Jehovah for five years now.
How can we imitate Paul's example and make our ministry more effective? The apostle Paul wrote to the Christian congregation at Rome and encouraged them to support those who were "outstanding among" them, rather than saying they were "outstanding in the community." Christians should strive to be "distinctive," and when we face opposition, we need to remain courageous and continue preaching the good news without being discouraged. (Rom. 6:17-22) Let us therefore be courageous and continue to preach, knowing that Satan will try to use people to discourage us and hinder our progress. Do you find this to be true?
Consider the experience of Jaime. He explains that he prays to Jehovah and also prays about his secular work. He used to enjoy watching boxing. He told himself that he needed to associate with fellow Christians and that his love for them would help him. But even though he stopped associating with his former companions, he still felt drawn to boxing. Jaime admits: "I kept struggling to know whether I was pleasing Asa and whether he was pleased with me." He continues: "Being immersed in Jehovah's organization helped me to see things clearly. Let me give an example: I used to enjoy watching boxing matches, but now I feel that my time is better spent thinking about spiritual things and serving Jehovah."
DO NOT BE DISCOURAGED!
How can we avoid being influenced by bad associations, even when we have made progress? By remembering that 'we should be vigilant,' and by avoiding 'companions who are ruining themselves.' (Proverbs 13:20) In other words, "we should be careful to determine what kind of company we keep, because whatever they do will influence us." (Acts 6:8, 9) Also, let us continue to seek Jehovah's guidance, continue to ask for wisdom, and allow God's spirit to strengthen us so that we can cope with "great trials" and continue to praise Jehovah despite opposition.—Revelation 7:9, 13, 14; James 1:2-4.
We may face challenges or temptations. However, we can trust that God sees our efforts to please him, and he will support us if we strive to live according to his will. Let us continue to praise Jehovah faithfully, like King David, who said: "I have set Jehovah before me at all times; because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart rejoices, and my tongue exults; moreover my body dwells in security."—Psalm 16:8, 9.

text:
ĨVINDA yĩmwe mũndũ mũka wĩtawa Alexandra e ngalĩnĩ meteele kũkĩla mũvaka wa nthĩ yĩ South America malike nthĩ ĩngĩ yĩ o kũu, eewie ndeto ii: "Ngalĩ no ĩthi, ĩndĩ vai vandũ mũndũũme ũũ wa China ũendete!" Ĩla Alexandra waumie ngalĩnĩ nĩ kana amanye kĩla kĩendeee, eethĩie mũndũũme ũsu wa China aitata kũelesya mũsikalĩ wa mũvakanĩ mathĩna make atũmĩĩte kĩthyomo ũtakĩsĩ nesa kya Spanish. Nũndũ Alexandra aendaa kĩkundinĩ kya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kya kĩthyomo kya Chinese, nĩweeyumisye atetheesye kũalyũla kĩthyomo kya mũndũũme ũsu nĩ kana mũsikalĩ ũsu aelewe.
Mũndũũme ũsu aisye kana nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩtw'e nĩ mĩao kwĩkala nthĩ ĩsu, ĩndĩ nĩwooyĩĩtwe mbesa na mavalũa ala maĩkĩĩthĩtye ũndũ ũsu. Mbeenĩ, mũsikalĩ ũsu ndaaĩtĩkĩla ndeto sya mũndũũme ũsu, o na nĩwambĩĩie kwona kana Alexandra aĩ na mũvango wa kũtwaa andũ nthĩ ĩngĩ makathũkũme ta ngombo. Ĩtina mũsikalĩ ũsu nĩweetĩkĩlanile na ndeto sya mũndũũme ũsu, o na kau nĩweeiwe aĩve vainĩ nũndũ ndaĩ na mavalũa ala maĩlĩte. Na nũndũ ndaĩ na mbesa, Alexandra nĩwamũnengie ndola 20. Mũndũũme ũsu nĩwatũngie mũvea mũno na amwĩa Alexandra kana akamũtũngĩa kĩasi kĩthonokete ndola 20 ila wamũnengete. Nake Alexandra amwĩie kana eĩkaa o kũmũtethya na eĩw'a e mũtanu nũndũ eeka ũndũ ũla waĩle. Nĩwanengie mũndũũme ũsu mavuku maeleetye Mbivilia na amũkũlya emanyĩsye Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
Nĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya mũno kwĩw'a kana ve andũ methĩawa me alau o na kwa andũ ala matamesĩ, na vate nzika, maũndũ ta asu nĩmekawa nĩ andũ ma ndĩni syonthe o na andũ ala mate ndĩni. We no wĩthĩwe na wendi wa kũtetheesya andũ ala angĩ ũte kwenda makũĩve? Ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩ ya vata nũndũ Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Kwĩ mũyo kũnengane kwĩ kwosa." (Meko ma Atũmwa 20:35) O na ĩngĩ, andũ ma saenzi nĩmesĩte kũmanya kana kũnengane no kũũtetheesye. Ekai twone nĩ nzĩa syĩva kwĩka ũu kũtonya kũtũtethya.
ŨLA "ŨNENGANAE NA ŨTANU"
Maũndũ ala mekĩkĩte meonany'a kana kũnengane nĩkũtumaa mũndũ atana. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie kana "Ngai endete mũndũ ũnenganae na ũtanu." Aneeneaa ĩũlũ wa Aklĩsto ala maumasya mĩvothi nũndũ maĩ alau nĩ kana matetheesye Aklĩsto ala angĩ maĩ na mathĩna. (2 Akolintho 8:4; 9:7) Vaulo ndaasya kana ũtanu ũla maĩ naw'o nĩw'o watumaa manengane. Ĩndĩ meethĩawa me atanu nũndũ nĩmanenganae syĩndũ syoo.
Kwosana na ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe, ũw'o nĩ kana kũnengane 'nĩkũtumaa ilungu sya kĩlĩko ila itumaa mũndũ ethĩwa e mũtanu, ethĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na andũ, na ethĩwa enengete ndaĩa ithũkũma nesa, na ũu ũituma ew'a e mwĩanĩe nũndũ wa kũnengane.' Naw'o ũkunĩkĩli ũngĩ woonanisye kana "kũnenga mũndũ ũngĩ mbesa nĩkũtumaa ũla wanengane atana mũno kwĩ ũndũ ũkwĩsaa kũtana ĩla waitũmĩa e weka."
We waaĩw'a ũtesa kũtethya andũ ala angĩ mũno nũndũ ndwĩ na ũtonyi? Ũw'o nĩ kana kĩla mũndũ no akwate ũtanu ũla umanaa na 'kũnengane na ũtanu.' Na ethĩwa wĩnengane wĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo, ti nginya kĩla ũũnengane kĩthĩwe kĩ kĩnene. Ve mũndũ mũka ũmwe Ngũsĩ ya Yeova watũmĩie aumĩthya ma ĩkaseti yĩĩ mĩvothi na amatavya ndeto ii: "Myakanĩ ĩno yonthe numasya mbesa nini Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ." Ĩndĩ aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Yeova Ngai nũnengete mbingĩ kwĩ ila numĩtye. . . . Nĩ mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kũndonyethya kumya mũthĩnzĩo ũũ, kwĩka ũu kũmbĩkĩaa vinya mũno."
Syĩndũ ila mũndũ ũtonya kũnengane ti o mbesa tũ, ĩndĩ ve nzĩa mbingĩ mũno sya kũnengane.
KŨNENGANE NĨKŨTUMAA WĨTHĨWA ŨTE NA MATHĨNA MAINGĨ MA MWĨĨ
Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ wĩ tei nĩwĩkaa ngoo yake nesa; Ĩndĩ ũla mwai nũthĩnasya mwĩĩ wake mwene." (Nthimo 11:17) Andũ ala me tei nĩmethĩawa me alau, nĩmatũmĩaa ĩvinda na vinya woo kũtethya ala angĩ, na nĩmamathĩnĩkĩaa na makameka maũndũ angĩ maseo. Kwĩka maũndũ asu nĩkũmatetheeasya kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ĩmwe ya nzĩa isu nĩ kũtuma methĩwa mate na mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ.
Ũkunĩkĩli wĩonany'a kana andũ ala meyumasya matetheesye angĩ maithĩnaw'a mũno nĩ kyalya na mayĩmakĩaa mũno. Mavinda maingĩ mayĩthĩawa na mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ. Ũlau nũtumaa andũ amwe ala methĩawa na mowau mathũku ta ũkimwi, na ũwau ũngĩ wĩtawa multiple sclerosis, mew'a kavaanga. Ũndũ ũngĩ ũmanyĩkĩte nĩ kana andũ ala maendeee kũng'ang'ana maeke kũnyw'a ũkĩ na matetheeasya angĩ, nĩmaolangaa mawĩmakĩo na nĩmatonya kũsinda wendi wa kwenda kũsyokea ũthengi.
Nũndũ wa ũu, vatw'ĩkĩkanaa kana "kwĩthĩwa na tei na kwĩka andũ ala angĩ maũndũ maseo nĩkũtumaa mũndũ ethĩwa ate na mosũanĩo mathũku." O na ĩngĩ, kũnengane nĩkũolangaa mesilya na thĩna wa kwambatwa nĩ nthakame. Na andũ ala makw'ĩĩwa nĩ aũme kana iveti syoo maikuaa ĩvinda yĩasa me na mawĩmakĩo ĩla matetheesya andũ ala angĩ.
Vate nzika kũnengane nĩkũũtetheeasya.
KŨNENGANE NĨKŨTUMAA ANDŨ ANGĨ MENDA KŨNENGANE
Yesũ eeie aatĩĩi make atĩĩ: "Nenganei, nenyu mũkanengwa; kĩthimi kĩseo, kĩlate, kĩthingithye, na kĩtĩkĩlĩlye, makamũnenga kĩthũinĩ kwenyu. Nĩkwĩthĩwa kĩthimo kĩla mũthimaa, nokyo mũkathimĩwa." (Luka 6:38) Ĩla wanenga andũ ala angĩ syĩndũ, nĩvatonyeka o namo makendeew'a nĩ ũlau waku na makethĩwa me alau. Kwoou, kũnengane nĩkũtumaa andũ meka maũndũ me ngwatanĩo na methĩwa me anyanya.
Andũ ala masomeete ĩũlũ wa ũndũ andũ maĩle kwĩkalany'a nĩmesĩte kũmanya kana "andũ ala matetheeasya ala angĩ kĩla ĩvinda mate na kĩeleelo kya kũĩvwa nĩmatumaa andũ angĩ meyĩelekany'a namo." Ũw'o nĩ kana "o kũsoma ĩũlũ wa maũndũ manene ala andũ meekie nĩ kana matetheesye angĩ nĩkũtumaa andũ methĩwa me alau." Na nĩkyo kĩtumi ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe weekiwe wonanĩtye kana 'mũndũ no atume andũ aingĩ, amwe wĩsĩ na angĩ ũtaamona, meka ũla waĩle.' Kwa ndeto ingĩ, ũu nĩ kwasya kana o ũndũ ũmwe wa ũlau no ũtume mũndũ ũngĩ ethĩwa e mũlau na kĩsio kĩnene kĩyĩthĩwa na andũ alau. We tyo wende kwĩkala vandũ ve andũ mailyĩ ũu? Vate nzika andũ no makwate moseo maingĩ makemanyĩsya kwĩthĩwa me alau.
Ũndũ ũla weekĩkie Florida, ĩla yĩ Amelika, no ũtũtetheesye kũelewa ũndũ andũ mekaa ĩla meekwa maũndũ maseo. Kĩkundi kya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩkyeeyumisye kĩtetheesye andũ ĩla kweethĩiwe kĩuutani kĩnene. Meteele mĩio ya kũtũngĩĩa nyũmba ĩmwe, nĩmoonie wiio wa mũtũi wĩ mwanangĩku na meeyumya maũseũvye. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda mũtũi ũsu aandĩkĩie ovisi mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa mũvea mavinda onthe. Katĩ wa andũ onthe ala naakomana namo, andũ aa nĩmo aseo vyũ." Nĩ kana atũnge mũvea nĩwaumisye mũvothi ũtũmĩwe wĩanĩ ũla wawĩtie wĩa wa vata vyũ wa Ngũsĩ.
ATĨĨA NGELEKANY'O YA MŨNENGANI ŨLA MŨNENE VYŨ
Kwosana na ũkunĩkĩli ũmwe wa andũ ma saenzi, "veonekana ve kĩndũ kya vata mũno kĩtumaa mũndũ enda kũtetheesya ala angĩ." Ũkunĩkĩli ũsu waĩtye kana "syana nĩsyonasya andũ ũlau o na itanamanya kũneena." Nĩkĩ vailyĩ ũu? Mbivilia nĩsũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu nũndũ yaĩtye kana andũ moombiwe "na mũvw'ano wa Ngai," na ũu nĩ kwasya kana andũ methĩawa na ndaĩa nzeo ta ila Ngai wĩthĩawa nasyo.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:27.
Ũlau nĩ ĩmwe katĩ wa ndaĩa nzeo vyũ ila Mũmbi witũ, Yeova Ngai, wĩthĩawa nasyo. Nũtũnengete thayũ na syĩndũ syonthe ila twendaa nĩ kana twĩthĩwe twĩ atanu. (Meko ma Atũmwa 14:17; 17:26-28) No tũmũmanye Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ na tũkamanya kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ witũ kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto yake, Mbivilia. O na Mbivilia nĩvuanĩtye kana Ngai nĩwĩkĩte mĩvango mĩseo nĩ kana ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte twĩĩkala twĩ atanu. * (1 Yoana 4:9, 10) Nũndũ Yeova Ngai nĩwe Mwambĩlĩlya wa ũlau na tũmbĩtwe na mũvw'ano wake, ti ũndũ wa ũsengy'a kwona tũyĩyĩelekany'a nake kwa kwĩthĩwa twĩ alau, na ĩla tweeka ũu nithyĩ tũtethekaa, na nũtwĩtĩkĩlaa.—Aevelania 13:16.
Nũlilikene ũla mũndũ mũka tũwetie mwambĩĩonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ wĩtawa Alexandra? Ngewa yake yesie kumya mũthya nata? O na kau me ngalĩnĩ ve mũndũ weeie Alexandra kana mbesa syake syanyw'a kĩw'ũ, ĩla ngalĩ yavikie taoninĩ yakothaa kũũngama, ũla mũndũũme wamũtetheetye nĩwakũnĩie anyanyae simũ. Anyanyae asu nĩmamũnengie mbesa na amũtũngĩa Alexandra ndola 20 ila wamũnengete. O na ĩngĩ, mũndũũme ũsu nĩweekie ũndũ Alexandra wamwĩie na ambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Alexandra nĩwatanie mũno ĩla wakomanie na mũndũũme ũsu ĩtina wa myei ĩtatũ me ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova wa kĩthyomo kya Chinese ũla weekĩiwe Peru. Nĩ kana amũtũngĩe Alexandra mũvea nũndũ wa maũndũ maseo ala wamwĩkĩte, mũndũũme ũsu nĩwathokisye Alexandra na anyanyae ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu ũtelinĩ wake.
Kũnengane na kũtetheesya ala angĩ nĩkũetae ũtanu mwingĩ. Na mũno mũno ethĩwa ĩla ũũnenga andũ syĩndũ, nũmatetheeasya mamũmanye Mũnengani wa mĩthĩnzĩo yonthe mĩseo, Yeova Ngai! (Yakovo 1:17) We nũendeee kũtanĩa moseo ala mũndũ ũkwataa ĩla wanengane kwa nzĩa ĩsu?

translation:
One day, a woman named Alexandra was in a shop looking at a map of South America and other maps too, and she heard this statement: "This place is not good, go back people, this land belongs to China!" Alexandra wondered about the shopkeeper's words and whether they were true, because someone from China would not bother to learn the languages of the countries where he trades using a difficult language like Spanish. So Alexandra went to the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah Witnesses learning Chinese, and she happily offered to help teach the language to that person so that the person could understand.
That person said that maybe he wouldn't stay in that country for long, but he would try to remember what happened today. However, the person did not remember the words of that person, or he didn't want to know if Alexandra had a reason to bring people to other places far away across the sea. Then that person remembered the words of that person, and even now he remembers them well, and also remembers that he had some money. And although he had little money, Alexandra gave him 20 dollars. That person thanked the woman very much and told Alexandra that if he ever needed her, he would give her more than 20 dollars. But Alexandra told him that it wasn't necessary to repay her and that she only wanted five dollars for the trouble she had gone through. She thanked that person for allowing her to preach the Bible and for listening to her talk about the Bible and the Kingdom of Jehovah.
It is a good thing to be generous to others, especially to those who have less, and to help those who need it, because such things please God and all people, and they please those who are poor. So don't hesitate to share with others when you can, should you go forward? This teaching is based on what Jesus said: "It is more blessed to give than to receive." (Acts 20:35) And often, people are happy to give and to share. Let us see how we can show our generosity.
THE "GIVE AND IT WILL BE GIVEN" PRINCIPLE
Things like giving and generosity cause a person to be happy. The apostle Paul wrote that "God loves a cheerful giver." True Christians always enjoy helping fellow Christians, especially those who are in need. (2 Corinthians 8:4; 9:7) Paul explained that this giving comes from the heart and causes happiness. Therefore, let everyone give according to their ability.
Consider an illustration, which shows that giving 'causes joy because it makes a person feel good, it makes him happy among people, it makes him appreciate life more, and it encourages him to continue being generous.' Another illustration showed that "giving to someone in need causes the giver to be happy because he knows he has helped someone avoid trouble."
So how can we show our willingness to help others generously and cheerfully? It is when each person has a cheerful attitude towards 'giving and generosity.' And although some may give little, do not think that every gift is small. For example, a sister of Jehovah's Witnesses told about an experience she had with her family and possessions: "All these years I have been very grateful to the Society." Then she continued saying: "Jehovah God has greatly blessed me, so I am willing to use whatever I have to support his work, even if it means sacrificing something."
Therefore, if a person is not able to give much, there are still many ways to be generous.
GIVING BRINGS JOY AND MANY BENEFITS
The Bible says: "A generous man benefits himself; and whoever refreshes others will also be refreshed." (Proverbs 11:17) Many people who are not wealthy use their time and resources to help others, and they find satisfaction in doing so. However, sometimes it is difficult to know what kind of help would be most appreciated.
An illustration shows that people who are grateful for the help they receive are often eager to share with others. Many problems are caused by selfishness and greed. Poverty drives some people to commit crimes, and others suffer from diseases such as AIDS and multiple sclerosis. One reason this happens is that people who continue to pursue wealth and material things become dissatisfied and unable to enjoy simple pleasures in life.
In view of this, we can conclude that "giving and being generous and helping others brings joy and peace of mind." Moreover, giving teaches us humility and helps us avoid becoming selfish. And those who are helped appreciate the kindness and generosity shown to them.
Therefore, giving is an act of love.
GIVING ALSO ENCOURAGES OTHERS TO GIVE
Jesus said: "Give, and you will receive; measure out, and it will be measured to you. The amount you give will be poured back into your own lap—packed tight and overflowing. For whatever measure you use, it will be used to measure back to you." (Luke 6:38) But when we give to others without expecting anything in return, we show our love and concern for them. So, giving encourages people to do good deeds and to be more generous.
Some people think that it is better to know whether "those who help others always have their needs met and feel appreciated" than to say, "reading great books about people who were kind and generous encourages people to be loving and compassionate." This is because "it is important to remember that someone who helps many people may not be recognized or rewarded, but they still find satisfaction in knowing they made a difference." In addition, it is possible that a good deed done by someone may lead another person to do something good, creating a ripple effect of kindness and compassion. How then should we live among people so that we can be like those who are known for their kindness? Therefore, people who have received much kindness often want to share their blessings with others.
The case of Florida, which is in America, shows how understanding people's backgrounds can help us understand why they behave the way they do. The Watch Tower Society has been commended for helping people who have experienced great suffering. While visiting homes, I met a young man who was very grateful for the comfort he had received. A sister told this young man about a large publication of the Watch Tower Society, saying: "I will bring you more publications free of charge. Among those whom I associate with, there are many who are also interested." She then arranged for a return visit to continue sharing the good news from the Watch Tower.
LET US CONSIDER THE EXAMPLE OF A GREAT PREACHER
According to one scientist, "it seems that the ability to empathize causes people to want to help others." This scientist said, "compassion motivates people to act kindly, even when they don't fully understand the situation." Is this true? My experience has taught me that people who are motivated by "love of God" are more likely to show genuine concern for others—which demonstrates that people who are truly loving are moved by God's spirit.—1 Timothy 3:27.
Compassion is one expression of love for our Creator, Jehovah God. We can show our appreciation for everything He provides by striving to live up to His standards. And we can learn what those standards are by studying His Word, the Bible. The Bible teaches that God cares deeply about us and wants us to live forever. * (1 John 4:9, 10) Because Jehovah God is the source of love and because we are loved by Him, we should be pleased to conform our lives to His will, and when we do so, we will find satisfaction, and we will be happier.—Hebrews 13:16.
I recently heard about a sister who befriended a woman named Alexandra. What was her reason for doing so? And how did she help Alexandra, who had little interest in spiritual things, to appreciate the truth? This sister learned that Alexandra had a difficult past, but she didn't give up on her. Instead, she continued to show kindness to Alexandra and spent time with her. She also invited Alexandra to attend meetings at the Kingdom Hall. Furthermore, this sister helped Alexandra to study the Bible. Alexandra responded positively, and she began attending meetings regularly at the large assembly hall of Jehovah's Witnesses in Chinese territory that was held in Peru. She then shared the good news with others, and this sister assisted Alexandra and her family, and they all benefited from the association.
To continue showing compassion and being generous requires effort. But such effort is worthwhile, especially when it helps others to come to know the Giver of all good things, Jehovah God! (James 1:17) So let us keep reaching out to people who need help and show them compassion in imitation of God!

text:
Ayĩelesya nĩkĩ wĩw'aa silikalĩ ĩtesa kũmina ũlũsani, mũnene ũmwe wa nthĩ ya Nicaragua ũla ũsiasya ũndũ silikalĩ ĩtũmĩĩte mbesa aisye: "Athũkũmi ma silikalĩ methĩawa mate aĩkĩĩku, nũndũ o namo nĩ ene nthĩ, na ethĩwa ene nthĩ nĩ alũsani no nginya athũkũmi ma silikalĩ methĩwe me alũsani."
We nũkwĩtĩkĩla kana nĩ vinya mũno ala me silikalĩnĩ kwĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku, ethĩwa ene nthĩ ti aĩkĩĩku? Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, silikalĩ ndĩkĩĩku ndĩsa kũetwe nĩ mũndũ. Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye nesa kana silikalĩ ndĩkĩĩku nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũla Yesũ weeie amanyĩw'a make mavoyae.
Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ silikalĩ ĩsumbĩkĩte kuma ĩtunĩ. Ĩkavetanga silikalĩ syonthe sya andũ. (Savuli 2:8, 9; Ũvuan'yo 16:14; 19:19-21) Ũathimo ũmwe Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkaetee andũ nĩ kũvetanga ũlũsani silikalĩnĩ. Kwasũanĩa maũndũ thanthatũ ala matũĩkĩĩthasya kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkeanĩsya ũndũ ũsu.
1. ŨTONYI
THĨNA ŨLA WĨTHĨAWA VO: Mavinda maingĩ silikalĩ sya andũ ikwataa mbesa kwĩsĩla koti ũla andũ maĩvaa. Kwondũ wa ũu, athũkũmi amwe ma silikalĩ nĩmoyaa mbesa, na angĩ mayĩtĩkĩla kũongwa nĩ andũ ala mekwenda maolangĩlwe koti kana matekwenda kũwũĩva. Thĩna ũsu no ũtume silikalĩ yongela koti nĩ kana yĩĩvĩe mbesa ila syooywa na ũu ũituma ũlũsani ũendeea kwingĩva. Ũu weethĩwa, andũ ala aĩkĩĩku nĩmo matonya kũũmĩa mũno.
ŨNDŨ THĨNA ŨSU ŨKAMINWA: Yeova Ngai * Mwene Vinya W'onthe nĩwe ũnengete silikalĩ yake ũtonyi. (Ũvuan'yo 11:15) Silikalĩ ĩsu ndĩthĩawa na vata wa kũmbany'a koti nĩ kana ĩendeesye maũndũ mayo. Vandũ va ũu, nũndũ Ngai 'e vinya ũtonyinĩ' na nĩ mũlau, akaĩkĩĩthya kana Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩweanĩsya mavata onthe ma ala makasumbĩkwa nĩw'o.—Isaia 40:26; Savuli 145:16.
2. MŨSUMBĨ
THĨNA ŨLA WĨTHĨAWA VO: Ũla mũndũ mũka ũwetiwe kĩlungunĩ kĩvĩtu wĩtawa Susan Rose-Ackerman aisye kana nĩ kenda ũlũsani ũthele, "no nginya wambĩĩe kũminwa kuma ĩũlũ." Andũ nĩmaekaa kũĩkĩĩa silikalĩ ĩla syatata kũmina ũlũsani athũkũminĩ ala ma nthĩ silikalĩnĩ ta volisi na mailea kũatĩanĩa na ala anene silikalĩnĩ. O na atongoi ala aseo methĩawa na naĩ ĩla twatiĩwe nĩ asyai maitũ ma mbee. Na ũu wosanĩte nesa na ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "kũti mũndũ mũlũngalũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, ũla wĩkaa nesa."
Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwaleile kũongwa
ŨNDŨ THĨNA ŨSU ŨKAMINWA: Kĩvathũkany'o na andũ me na naĩ, Yesũ Klĩsto, ũla nĩwe ũnyuvĩtwe ethĩwe Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ndesa kũtatwa akeka ũthũku. Yesũ oonanisye ũu ĩla waleile ayĩongwa kwa kũnengwa "mosumbĩ onthe ma nthĩ, na ndaĩa syamo." Ndevili, ũla nĩ mũsumbĩ wa nthĩ, athĩte Yesũ syĩndũ isu eetĩkĩla kũmũthaitha. (Mathayo 4:8-10; Yoana 14:30) Yesũ nĩwatw'ĩte vyũ kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku o na kũvika ĩla waĩ mwambe. Oonanisye ũu ĩla waleile mbinyu nũndũ nĩweesĩ no yĩolange woo, na yaĩ ĩtonya kũtuma ethĩwa ate kwĩyĩw'a. (Mathayo 27:34) Kuma Yesũ athayũũkw'a na athi ĩtunĩ, nũĩkĩĩthĩtye nesa kana nĩwe waĩle kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai.
3. ĨVINDA YĨLA SILIKALĨ ĨTONYA KŨSUMBĨKA
THĨNA ŨLA WĨTHĨAWA VO: Nthĩ mbingĩ nĩsyĩthĩawa na ũnyuvani ũla andũ monaa ta ũtonya kũtetheesya kũvetanga andũ ala alũsani kĩvĩlanĩ. Ĩndĩ ũw'o nĩ kana o na nthĩ ila iendeee nĩsyĩthĩawa na ũlũsani ĩvindanĩ ya kambeini na ũnyuvani. Kwa kũnenga andũ ma siasa mbesa sya kambeini na kũmeka maũndũ angĩ, andũ ala athwii no malikĩlĩĩle ũnyuvani na ũu ũituma andũ mataĩlĩte malika kĩvĩlanĩ.
Mũsili wa makoani wa Koti Mũnene wa Amelika John Paul Stevens aisye kana kũlikĩlĩĩla maũndũ kwa nzĩa ĩsu kũietae mũisyo ĩũlũ wa "ũĩkĩĩku na ũseo wa silikalĩ w'oka, ĩndĩ nĩkũtumaa andũ maeka kũmĩĩkĩĩa." Kwoou, ti ũndũ wa ũsengy'a kũmanya kana andũ aingĩ monaa syama sya siasa ne syo syĩthĩawa na ũlũsani ũla mwingĩ mbee wa mĩvĩa ĩla ĩngĩ yonthe.
ŨNDŨ THĨNA ŨSU ŨKAMINWA: Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ndwĩthĩawa na kambeini kana ũlũsani ũla wĩthĩawa ĩvinda ya ũnyuvani nũndũ w'o nĩ mũlũmu na nĩ wa tene na tene. (Ndanieli 7:13, 14) Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ndũnyuvawa kana kũvetangwa nĩ andũ nũndũ Mũsumbĩ waw'o anyuvĩtwe nĩ Ngai. Nũndũ Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩ wa tene na tene, ũu ũĩkĩĩthasya kana maũndũ ala wĩkaa methĩawa me ma kũtetheesya andũ na maikathela.
4. MĨAO
THĨNA ŨLA WĨTHĨAWA VO: Mũndũ nũtonya kũsũanĩa kana kũseũvya mĩao ĩngĩ no kwaĩlye maũndũ. Ĩndĩ kwĩanana na ũkunĩkĩli wa asomi, mavinda maingĩ ĩla mĩao yeethĩwa yĩ mingĩ now'o andũ makwataa myanya mingĩ ya kwĩthĩwa me alũsani. O na ĩngĩ, ala maseũvasya mĩao nĩ kana ĩtetheesye kũolanga ũlũsani matũmĩaa mbesa mbingĩ ĩndĩ mayĩanĩsya maũndũ manini.
ŨNDŨ THĨNA ŨSU ŨKAMINWA: Mĩao ya Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai yĩthĩawa yĩ mĩseo vyũ mbee wa ya silikalĩ sya andũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, vandũ va kũandĩkĩa andũ mĩao mingĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ maĩle kwĩka na ũndũ mataĩle kwĩka, Yesũ anenganie ũla mwolooto wĩ nguma ĩũlũ wa mwĩkalĩle. Aisye atĩĩ: "Maũndũ onthe ĩndĩno o na meva ala mũkwenda andũ mamwĩke inyw'ĩ, nenyu mekei o ta ũu." (Mathayo 7:12) Ũndũ ũla wa vata nĩ kana mĩao ya Ũsumbĩ ndĩkonetye meko ma andũ tũ, ĩndĩ nĩneeneaa kĩla kĩtumaa andũ meka maũndũ asu. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ waisye atĩĩ: "Mwende mũtũi waku o tondũ wĩyendete." (Mathayo 22:39) Vate nzika, no Ngai ũtonya kũtwĩyĩaĩa tũatĩĩe mĩao ĩsu nũndũ e na ũtonyi wa kũsoma ngoo sitũ.
5. IELEELO
THĨNA ŨLA WĨTHĨAWA VO: Ĩtomo na kwĩyenda nĩsyo itumaa kwĩthĩwa na ũlũsani. Mavinda maingĩ athũkũmi ma silikalĩ na ene nthĩ nĩmethĩawa mailyĩ ũu. Athũkũmi ma silikalĩ ma taoni ya Seoul ĩla ĩwetiwe kĩlungunĩ kĩvĩtu, maĩ maongiwe nĩ ala maakaa nyũmba nene ya kũthooesya syĩndũ ĩla yavalũkile mũsyĩnĩ ũsu. Asu maakaa nĩmeesĩ kana maongana, maĩ matonya kũtũmĩa mbesa nini kwĩ ila mesaa kũtũmĩa maaka na mĩio ĩla yaĩle, na maatĩĩa mĩao ya myako.
Nĩ kana ũlũsani ũthele vyũ, no nginya andũ mamanyĩw'e ũndũ matonya kũsinda imanyĩo nthũku ta ĩtomo na kwĩyenda. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana silikalĩ sya andũ iyĩthĩawa na wendi na ũtonyi wa kũmanyĩsya andũ maũndũ asu.
ŨNDŨ THĨNA ŨSU ŨKAMINWA: Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũvetangaa vyũ ũlũsani kwa kũmanyĩsya andũ ũndũ matonya kũsinda imanyĩo nthũku ila itumaa kwĩthĩwa na ũlũsani. * Kĩsomo kĩu nĩkĩmatetheeasya 'matw'ĩkĩthw'e eũ vevanĩ wa ilĩko syoo.' (Aeveso 4:23) Memanyĩasya kwĩthĩwa me eanĩe na kwendeew'a nĩ andũ ala angĩ vandũ va kwĩthĩwa na ĩtomo na kwĩyenda.—1 Akolintho 10:24; 1 Timotheo 6:6.
6. ALA MASUMBĨKĨTWE
THĨNA ŨLA WĨTHĨAWA VO: O na kũndũ kũla andũ mamanyĩĩtw'e kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo na mate alũsani, amwe mailea kũnyuva kwĩthĩwa mate aĩkĩĩku na me alũsani. Asomi maasya kana kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi silikalĩ itesa kũmina ũlũsani. Kĩla silikalĩ itonya kwĩanĩsya no kũolanga ũlũsani na mathĩna ala ũetae.
ŨNDŨ THĨNA ŨSU ŨKAMINWA: Ngwatanĩo yĩtawa United Nations Convention Against Corruption yaĩtye kana nĩ kenda silikalĩ imine ũlũsani syaĩle kũthuthya andũ matate kwĩthĩwa me "aĩkĩĩku na maimanya kana me na kĩanda kya kũmina ũlũsani." O na kau kĩu nĩ kĩeleelo kĩseo, Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wĩkaa ũndũ mũseango kwĩ kũthuthya andũ, nũndũ no nginya ala masumbĩkĩtwe nĩw'o methĩwe me aĩkĩĩku na mate alũsani. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "ala me na ĩtomo" na "ala maneenaa ũvũngũ" maikatiĩwa Ũsumbĩ.
O ta Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa, andũ no kũatĩĩa myolooto ĩsu mĩtheu ya Yeova mwĩkalĩlenĩ woo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mũmanyĩw'a ũmwe weetawa Simoni watatie kumya mbesa nĩ kana akwate veva mũtheu, atũmwa nĩmaleile aimaonga na mamwĩa atĩĩ: "Alyũla ngoo ĩndĩno ũndũ wa ũthũku ũũ waku." Ĩla Simoni wamanyie mũisyo ũla wesaa kũmũkwata nũndũ wa wendi wake mũthũku, nĩwakũlilye atũmwa mamũvoyee nĩ kana aũsinde.—Meko ma Atũmwa 8:18-24.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨKA NĨ KANA WĨTHĨWE UNGU WA ŨSUMBĨ WA NGAI
Wĩ na mwanya wa kũnyuva kwĩthĩwa ũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai o na ethĩwa wĩ wa nthĩ yĩva. (Meko ma Atũmwa 10:34, 35) Mũvango wa kwĩmanyĩsya ũla ũendeeaw'a nĩ Ũsumbĩ ũsu ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe no ũkũtetheesye kwĩka ũu. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ikatanĩa kũkwony'a ũndũ ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia vate ndĩvi kwa ndatĩka ta ĩkũmi kĩla kyumwa. No wĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai' na ũndũ ũkavetanga silikalĩ ila syĩthĩawa na ũlũsani o vamwe na maũndũ angĩ maingĩ. (Luka 4:43) Nũũthokw'a ũneene na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ila syĩthĩawa kĩsionĩ kyenyu kana ũlike Kĩsesenĩ kitũ kya jw.org/kam.

translation:
The church is like a hospital that treats sick people, one prominent leader from Nicaragua who has experienced this treatment said: "Many churches today have become weak, but remember that one body, and one spirit in that body is the church and its members."
We wonder whether it is possible for such weak churches to be strengthened, is that one body strengthening? This is very important, a church becomes strong through a person. I believe it shows clearly that a strong church is God's Kingdom where Jesus Christ teaches his followers.
God's Kingdom is a powerful kingdom. It overcomes all the kingdoms of men. (Psalm 2:8, 9; Revelation 16:14; 19:19-21) One way God's Kingdom strengthens people is by overcoming sicknesses. Considering these things will help you understand how God's Kingdom can solve problems.
1. TITLE
THEME OF THE TEXT: Many people's churches are failing because they are being influenced by worldly people. Because of this, some church leaders are becoming weak, and others are not paying attention to those who go astray or those who want to leave. This theme helps the church grow stronger and also shows why it is important to avoid being influenced by the world. Those who are wise will listen.
THE PROBLEM WITH THIS: Jehovah God * The Almighty Ruler is the one who strengthens his church. (Revelation 11:15) His church is characterized by loyalty and doing what is right. Therefore, when God 'strengthens his people,' he demonstrates that his Kingdom is able to overcome all other powers that oppose him.—Isaiah 40:26; Psalm 145:16.
2. KINGDOM
THEME OF THE TEXT: A man named Susan Rose-Ackerman once said, "I don't want to be involved in politics." People often feel that it is difficult to remain neutral when political issues affect their lives and when politicians make decisions that impact them. But she realized that neutrality is possible and that it can be beneficial. This teaches us that we should always maintain our neutrality.
Jesus Christ was willing to be judged
THEME OF THE TEXT: Through his example and teachings, Jesus Christ, who is the Prince of the Kingdom of God, showed us how to endure suffering without complaining. Jesus knew that he would be judged and condemned, yet he remained steadfast, saying, "This world is evil, and I will overcome it." Indeed, as the prince of this world, he had the power to resist temptation and remain faithful to God. (Matthew 4:8-10; John 14:30) Jesus taught us how to face challenges with courage and perseverance, and he promised that he would never leave us alone. He knew that he would be betrayed and abandoned, but he trusted that God would deliver him from evil. (Matthew 27:34) So when Jesus cried out and said, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" he was showing us that even he experienced pain and suffering, but he still trusted in God.
3. POWER TO OVERCOME EVIL
THE ISSUE OF CHOICE: Many people believe they have the right to choose what is best for themselves, even if it means harming others. This belief often leads to selfishness and disregard for the rights of others. By encouraging people to prioritize their own desires and pursue their own interests, it can lead to a society where individuals are more concerned with their own well-being than with the common good.
Justice John Paul Stevens of the United States Supreme Court stated that allowing certain practices could create a climate of "lawlessness and disrespect for the law," which could encourage people to take matters into their own hands. However, it is difficult to determine whether most people would abuse their freedom if given the opportunity, especially considering the influence of morality and social norms.
THIS IMPORTANT QUESTION: The sovereignty of God is challenged by earthly governments or human systems, but this challenge is futile and will ultimately fail. (Daniel 7:13, 14) God's sovereignty cannot be overthrown by humans; rather, God allows human rulers to exercise authority under his supervision. Because God's sovereignty is eternal, it guarantees that justice will prevail and wrongs will be corrected.
4. RIGHTS
THE ISSUE OF CHOICE: A person has the right to make decisions about their own life, but exercising those rights should not harm others. In line with the principles of compassion, many societies recognize various rights that protect individual freedoms. However, some misuse their rights to justify harmful actions, causing significant damage and suffering.
THIS IMPORTANT QUESTION: The rights granted by God's Kingdom differ from those recognized by secular systems of government. For example, while legal codes often define rights based on what is permissible or prohibited, Jesus emphasized the principle of treating others as you would like to be treated. He said: "All things therefore that you want men to do to you, you also do to them." (Matthew 7:12) This means that the rights granted by God are always balanced with consideration for the well-being of others, promoting love and kindness. That is why Jesus further stated: "Love your neighbor as yourself." (Matthew 22:39) Therefore, God expects us to use our rights responsibly, recognizing that we have obligations toward others and a need to show empathy.
5. LOYALTY
THIS MATTER IS WORTH CONSIDERING: Loyalty and friendship are essential for happiness. Many people experience difficulties in life and feel lonely because of this. Recent studies in Seoul, South Korea, showed that people who live alone tend to develop larger homes and more possessions, yet they still feel empty inside. Those who live alone may become self-centered, focusing only on their own needs and desires, and neglecting the importance of relationships.
Even when faced with challenges, it is important for Christians to help others find meaning and purpose in life through loyalty and friendship. It is vital that governments recognize the value of supporting individuals and fostering a sense of community.
THIS MATTER IS WORTH CONSIDERING: God's love motivates us to show concern for others and help them find meaning and purpose in life, which can lead to happiness and fulfillment. * This lesson teaches us "to be concerned about the interests of others." (Philippians 4:23) Showing genuine care and consideration for others demonstrates our love and respect.—1 Corinthians 10:24; 1 Timothy 6:6.
6. OTHER POINTS TO CONSIDER
THIS MATTER IS WORTH CONSIDERING: Often, people are drawn to those who share similar values and beliefs, and some may seek out friends who will support their harmful habits. Some believe that material possessions can solve problems and bring happiness. Every individual has the potential to make choices that promote well-being and avoid negative influences.
THIS MATTER IS WORTH CONSIDERING: The United Nations Convention Against Corruption defines corruption as abuse of power for private gain, including "taking advantage of someone's vulnerability or need." However, even without such a formal definition, God's standards condemn exploitation, and any form of taking advantage of another person's weakness is wrong. The Bible condemns both "fraudulent dealings" and "deceptive practices."—
Even Christians in the first century were tempted to misuse their authority. For example, a man named Simon once tried to buy spiritual gifts with money, but the apostles rebuked him severely, saying: "Your money should go where you are!" But Simon repented and humbly requested that they pray for him so that nothing he said would be insincere.—Acts 8:18-24.
EVERY EFFORT SHOULD BE MADE TO UPHOLD GOD'S STANDARDS
You have a reason to trust that God's standards are fair and just. (Acts 10:34, 35) The principle of impartiality is fundamental to God's Law and applies to everyone. Jehovah's Witnesses strive to apply this principle when considering whether a Bible teaching is being misrepresented or distorted. They carefully examine each point in light of the entire Bible and determine whether it aligns with sound doctrine. (Luke 4:43) To learn more about Jehovah's standards, visit our website jw.org/kam.

text:
Vaa ĩtheo ve na ngelekany'o ya ũndũ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova ĩtonya kũea ngewa na mũtũi. Twasye mũndũ ũmwe wĩtawa Brian ũla nĩ Ngũsĩ, nĩwavika mũsyĩ kwa mũndũ ũngĩ wĩtawa Eric, na mambĩĩa kũea ngewa.
MBIVILIA YĨTHĨAWA NA MAŨNDŨ MA W'O MA ISITOLI
Eric: Eka ngũtavye, nyie ndi mũndũ wa ndĩni. Kwoou ndiona ta twĩneenea maũndũ maingĩ.
Brian: Nĩ mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kũndavya ũu. Na ndanamba kũendeea mũno, nyie nĩtawa Brian. Naku wĩtawa ata?
Eric: Nĩtawa Eric.
Brian: Nĩnatana mũno kũkomana naku, Eric.
Eric: O nakwa nĩneew'a mũyo.
Brian: Kwaeka ngũkũlye, wĩanĩe mũsyĩ wa andũ ma ndĩni?
Eric: Ĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla naendie kolengyi, nĩnaekanie na maũndũ ma ndĩni.
Brian: Nĩnakũelewa. Weekie masomo meva kolengyi?
Eric: Neekie ĩsomo ya social studies na isitoli. Nĩ vata na ĩsomo ya isitoli nũndũ nĩyĩmanyĩasya vala mũndũ waumie.
Brian: Ũu nĩw'o, ĩsomo ya isitoli yĩthĩawa yĩ ya kwendeesya. No kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ kana Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ya isitoli. Ĩla wasomaa, waaĩka ũkunĩkĩli ũtũmĩĩte Mbivilia?
Eric: Aiee. Nĩnĩsĩ Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ĩseo ĩndĩ ndyaaĩsa kũsũanĩa kana yo nĩ ĩvuku ya isitoli.
Brian: Wĩoneka nĩwendete kũmanya maũndũ. Ethĩwa wĩ na ndatĩka nini, mbĩtĩkĩlye ngwony'e ngelekany'o nini sya maũndũ ma w'o ma isitoli ala me Mbivilianĩ.
Eric: Nĩ sawa. Ĩndĩ ndi na Mbivilia.
Brian: Vai thĩna, no tũtũmĩe ĩno yakwa. Ngelekany'o ya mbee nĩ ĩno yĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Mavinda kĩlungu kya 29 mũsoa wa 26 na 27. Mĩsoa ĩsu yaĩtye: "Na ĩndĩ Ndaviti mwana wa Yese asumbĩka Isilaeli onthe. Na ĩvinda yĩla wasumbĩkie Isilaeli yaĩ myaka mĩongo ĩna; asumbĩka myaka mũonza Eviloni, na myaka mĩongo ĩtatũ na ĩtatũ Yelusaleme."
Eric: Ĩsu ĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ya isitoli ata?
Brian: Ve ĩvinda yĩmwe andũ ala matetĩkĩlanaa na Mbivilia maasya kana Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti ndaaĩthĩwa kw'o.
Eric: O w'o ki? Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kyatumaa masya kana ndaaĩthĩwa kw'o?
Brian: Kwaĩ maũndũ manini eka ala me Mbivilianĩ maĩkĩĩthasya kana Ndaviti aĩ kw'o. Ĩndĩ mwaka wa 1993, andũ amwe ala menzaa syĩndũ sya tene nĩmaumbũie ĩvia ya tene yaĩ na ndeto ialyũlĩtwe ũũ: "Nyũmba ya Ndaviti."
Eric: Ũsu ko nĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesyaa.
Brian: Mũndũ ũngĩ andũ moonaa ta ũtaaĩthĩwa kw'o nĩ Vondio Vilato ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ na waĩ ngavana ĩvinda ya Yesũ. Awetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩĩ ya Luka kĩlungu kya 3, mũsoa wa 1 vamwe na anene angĩ ma silikalĩ ma ĩvinda yĩu.
Eric: Ĩĩ, Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye kana 'yĩla Vondio Vilato waĩ ngavana wa Yutia, nake Elote aĩ mũsumbĩ wa Kalilii.'
Brian: Nĩw'o. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ asomi amwe methĩĩtwe na nzika kana Vondio Vilato aĩ kw'o. Ĩndĩ, myaka ta 50 mĩvĩtu, ve ĩvia yoonekie Middle East yĩ na ĩsyĩtwa yake.
Eric: Ĩĩ. Nditũaa nĩsĩ ũu.
Brian: Nĩnatana kũneenea maũndũ asu vamwe naku.
Eric: Ndiũtavya ndeũkũvitha, nyie nonaa Mbivilia ta ĩvuku o ta ala angĩ, ĩndĩ ndyaaĩsa kũsũanĩa ta yĩsa kũtũtethya ũmũnthĩ. No yĩthĩwe yĩ na isitoli ya w'o, ĩndĩ ndikwona ta ĩtũtethya kwa nzĩa o na yĩva.
MBIVILIA NĨ ĨVUKU YA TENE, ĨNDĨ YĨ NA MOTAO MATONYA KŨTŨTETHYA
Brian: Andũ aingĩ no metĩkĩlane na ndeto isu. Ĩndĩ nyie ndyĩtĩkĩlanaa na ũu. Kĩĩ nĩkyo kĩtumaa ndetĩkĩla ũu: Kuma tene mavata maitũ ma lasima mayaavĩndũka. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtwĩthĩawa na vata wa lĩu, ngũa, na vandũ va kwĩkala. Na kĩla ĩvinda nĩtwĩthĩawa na wendi wa kũneena na andũ ala angĩ na kwĩthĩwa na mũsyĩ wĩ na ũtanu. Yo ithyonthe tyo twonaa syĩndũ isu syĩ sya vata?
Eric: Ĩĩ.
Brian: Mbivilia no ĩtũtetheesye maũndũnĩ asu onthe. Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi tũtonya kwasya kana Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ya tene, ĩndĩ yĩ na motao matonya kũtũtethya.
Eric: Ũu nĩ kwasya ata?
Brian: Kwaeka ngũelesye kwa nzĩa ĩngĩ. Mbivilia yĩ na myolooto ĩtũmĩkaa ũmũnthĩ o ũndũ yatũmĩkaa ĩla yaandĩkiwe ya mbee myaka maana maingĩ mĩvĩtu.
Mbivilia yĩ na myolooto ya vata mũno ĩtũmĩkaa ũmũnthĩ o ũndũ yatũmĩkaa ĩla yaandĩkiwe ya mbee myaka maana maingĩ mĩvĩtu
Eric: Sawa. Maũndũnĩ ta meva?
Brian: Myolooto ya Mbivilia no ĩtũtetheesye kwĩthĩwa na woni ũla waĩle ĩũlũ wa mbesa, mũsyĩ wĩ na ũtanu, kana kwĩthĩwa twĩ anyanya aseo. O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia no ĩtũtongoesye tũkethĩwa na thayũ mũseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, we tyo wĩtĩkĩle kana ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũũme mũseo na ũũngamĩe mũsyĩ waku nesa?
Eric: Nĩw'o, nĩngwĩtĩkĩlana naku. Yu nĩ ta mwaka ũmwe mũvĩtu kuma natwaana, ĩndĩ ti laisi kwĩtĩkĩlana na kĩveti kyakwa mavinda onthe.
Brian: Waneena w'o. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yĩthĩawa na myolooto yĩ laisi ĩtonya kũtũtethya ũmũnthĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩandĩko ya Aeveso kĩlungu kya 5. Kwaeka tũsome mũsoa wa 22, 23, na wa 28. No ũsome mĩsoa ĩsu?
Eric: Ĩĩ. Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Inyw'ĩ iveti, ĩnyivĩsyei aũme menyu ta mwĩnyivĩsye Mwĩaĩi. Nũndũ mũndũ mũũme nĩ mũtwe wa kĩveti, o tondũ Klĩsto nake nĩ mũtwe wa ĩkanisa, nake nĩ mũtangĩĩi wa mwĩĩ." Naw'o mũsoa wa 28 waĩtye atĩĩ: "O ta ũu aũme namo nĩmaĩlwe nĩ kũsyenda iveti syoo o ũndũ mendete mĩĩ yoo ene. Ũla wendaa kĩveti kyake eyendaa mwene."
Brian: Nĩ mũvea. Nĩwasoma nesa. Wĩona ata, kĩla mũndũ akatata kũatĩĩa ũtao ũsu wĩ laisi, mĩsyĩ tyo yĩthĩwe na ũtanu?
Eric: Ĩĩ, nĩĩkwatya ũu. Ĩndĩ ti laisi kwĩka ũu.
Brian: Nĩw'o kana vai mũndũ ũtavĩtasya. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi kĩlungunĩ kĩu kya Mbivilia ve mũsoa ũtwĩkĩaa vinya tũikekwatye mũndũ ũla ũngĩ eke maũndũ matesa ũtonyeka. * Kĩla ũmwe aĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩle kwelekela ũla ũngĩ na eyũmbanĩtye kwĩtĩkĩlana nake veethĩwa ve vata. Nyie, na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtũmanyĩte kana Mbivilia no ĩtũtetheesye kwĩthĩwa na woni waĩle katĩ witũ.
Eric: Ũu nĩ w'o.
Brian: Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩthĩawa na Kĩsese kĩthĩawa na ũvoo mũseo ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano na thayũ wa mũsyĩ. Ethĩwa wĩ na ndatĩka nini, no nĩkwony'e maũndũ ala methĩawa vo.
Eric: Nĩ sawa. No nĩtũmĩe ndatĩka nini.
Brian: Nĩ mũvea. Nĩ kana ũlike Kĩsesenĩ kitũ ũandĩkaa www.jw.org/sw. Wakĩvingũa kĩthĩawa kĩilyĩ ũũ.
Eric: Ko kĩ na mavisa maseo.
Brian: Mavisa asu meonany'a kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o kũla tũtavanasya ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. Nĩtwavika vala tũkwendaa. Kĩlungu kĩĩ kĩ na kyongo kĩkwasya "Msaada kwa Wenzi wa Ndoa na Wazazi." Nthĩnĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ ve maũvoo makuvĩ mekũneenea maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o. Ve ũmwe ũũkwendeesya mũno?
Eric: Ĩĩ. "Kusuluhisha Matatizo Katika Ndoa Yako." Nĩona ũvoo ũũ no ũndethye!
Brian: Kĩlungu kĩĩ kĩ na maũndũ ana matonya kũmina mathĩna. Kwoona ũndũ kalungu kaa kaĩtye. Eric, no wende kũkasoma?
Eric: Ĩĩ. Vaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mawasiliano katika ndoa ni kama damu ya uhai mwilini, na upendo na heshima ni kama moyo na mapafu yanayosukuma damu hiyo." Nĩnendeew'a nĩ ũndũ maeleetye ũndũ ũsu.
Brian: Nĩ mũvea nũndũ wa kũsoma nesa. Ve mũsoa wa Mbivilia ũwetetwe vaa. Wenda kũũvingũa no ũvinyĩĩe vau ve mũsoa ũsu.
Eric: Ĩĩ, nĩnawona. Nĩ ĩandĩko ya Aeveso 5:33. Yaĩtye ũũ: "Ĩndĩ kĩla mũndũ wenyu nakyende kĩveti kyake o ũndũ wĩyendete mwene; na kĩveti nĩkĩmũkĩe mũũme."
Brian: Nĩwaelewa kana mũsoa ũsu ũeleetye ĩũlũ wa kwĩka kĩla ũkwenda ũla ũngĩ akwĩke?
Eric: Wĩenda kwasya ata?
Brian: Kwoosa kwa ngelekany'o mũndũũme. Vate nzika, mũndũũme nĩwendaa kĩveti kyake kĩmũnenge ndaĩa na o ta ũu, nakyo kĩveti nĩkyendaa mũũme akĩĩkĩĩthye kana nũkyendete. Kana ti w'o?
Eric: Ĩĩ. Nĩngwĩtĩkĩlana naku.
Brian: Ethĩwa mavinda maingĩ mũndũũme nũmanthaa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya kwony'a kĩveti kyake kana nũkyendete, tyo nginya o nakyo kĩveti kĩu kĩkew'a wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũmũnenga ndaĩa?
Eric: Nĩona ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka.
Brian: O na kau mũsoa ũsu waandĩkiwe myaka vakuvĩ 2,000 mĩvĩtu, nĩwonanĩtye ũndũ mũndũũme na kĩveti maĩle kwĩka, na ũkanengane ũtao waĩle ũla ũtonya kũtuma mũtwaano woo wĩthĩwa wĩ mũseo maũatĩĩa. Na o tondũ vawetiwe ĩla ngelekany'onĩ "moyo na mapafu" ila nĩ wendo na ndaĩa ikeethĩawa vo kĩla ĩvinda.
Eric: Nĩneetĩkĩla kana Mbivilia yĩ maũndũ maingĩ kwĩ ũndũ nĩneesilasya.
Brian: Nĩnatana mũno kwĩw'a ũu. No nende kũsyoka ĩngĩ nĩ kenda twĩneenea kĩlungu kĩĩ kĩ na kyongo "Hatua Nne za Kusuluhisha Matatizo" nthĩnĩ wa ũvoo ũũ wĩ Kĩsesenĩ kitũ. *
Eric: Nĩ sawa. Nĩngũsisya ũvoo ũsu nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa.
Nĩvethĩwa ve ĩkũlyo wendaa kũkwata ũsũngĩo wayo kuma Mbivilianĩ? Nĩwĩthĩwa wendaa kũmanya ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo kana maũndũ ala Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩkaa? Ethĩwa nĩwendaa ũu, ndũkalee kũneena na ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Akatanĩa kũneena naku ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu.

translation:
When I understood that Jehovah's organization was helping people, I felt happy and encouraged. We had a brother named Brian who was from England; he spoke with a brother named Eric, and he wanted to be encouraged.
PROBLEMS FACED AND SOLUTIONS
Eric: Hello brother, I am a local person. Let us see if we can discuss many things.
Brian: It is good to meet you, and my name is Brian. What is your name?
Eric: My name is Eric.
Brian: I am happy to meet you, Eric.
Eric: Oh yes, I agree.
Brian: By the way, do you speak the language of the locals?
Eric: Yes. I go to school, and I learn about local languages.
Brian: I understand. Do you have lessons at school?
Eric: I have social studies and history lessons. I struggle with history because it involves remembering many dates.
Brian: That is true, history lessons are difficult. Some say the Bible is a history book. But when you read it, does it help you remember important information from the Bible?
Eric: Yes. I think the Bible is a good book that helps me reason, while history is just a book.
Brian: You seem eager to learn. Tell me what you know about this problem and what principles from this historical issue and the Bible can help.
Eric: Okay. I have the Bible.
Brian: Great, let us use mine then. The reference is 1 Samuel chapter 29 verses 26 and 27. Other verses state: "And David became king over all Israel. And he reigned over Israel forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron, and thirty-three years in Jerusalem."
Eric: Can this verse be used as a solution to history problems?
Brian: In some cases, people connect the Bible with historical figures like King David.
Eric: Oh really? How can this connection help them solve their problems?
Brian: There are many things in the Bible that relate to David's reign. For example, in 1993, some people discovered a stone inscription with the following writing: "House of David."
Eric: So this is something to investigate.
Brian: One person who wasn't mentioned there is Pontius Pilate, who was governor of Judea and authorized Jesus' crucifixion. This is recorded in Luke chapter 3 verse 1 along with other officials during his governorship.
Eric: Yes, that scripture says 'that Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee.'
Brian: That's right. For many years scholars debated whether Pontius Pilate existed. But recently, around 50 years ago, an inscription was found in the Middle East confirming his existence.
Eric: Yes. I agree with you.
Brian: Let me explain more to you.
Eric: I'm willing to listen, you people from Mbivila, both old and young, because I want to understand and learn something. It has been written about, and I see it being discussed everywhere.
MBIVILA IS AN OLD BOOK, BUT IT HAS MANY THINGS TO TEACH US
Brian: Many people don't connect with this inscription. But I connect with it. The reason I connect with it is because ancient stones tell us about our ancestors. For instance, we learn about the lives of kings, wars, and people's settlements. And in every era, we learn about communication with others and their customs and traditions. Don't we find similar things in the scriptures?
Eric: Yes.
Brian: Mbivila teaches us many important things. And that's why we say Mbivila is an old book, but it has many things to teach us.
Eric: Is that so?
Brian: Consider it from another perspective. Mbivila has information that can help us understand ourselves or issues that have been documented for many years.
Mbivila has information about past events that can help us understand ourselves or issues that have been documented for many years.
Eric: Okay. What else does it say?
Brian: The information in Mbivila teaches us about being judged by the great judge, customs and traditions, or being judged by anyone who cleans themselves. And also, Mbivila teaches us to be guided by truth. For instance, do you think someone would refuse to be judged honestly and fairly?
Eric: That's true, I agree with you. It's been one year since we started studying, but it doesn't mean we shouldn't continue learning from the teachings of our ancestors.
Brian: You speak well. Because Mbivila is filled with information that helps us understand ourselves. For example, read section 5 of the book of Aeveso carefully. Also, read verses 22, 23, and 28. Should we read more verses?
Eric: Yes. This verse says: "Husbands, love your wives just as Christ loved the church. Since the husband is the head of the wife, so Christ is the head of the church, which is his body." And verse 28 says: "So husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself."
Brian: That's good. I will read again. You see, everyone struggles to accept their own mistakes, why then should they be judged by others?
Eric: Yes, I fear that. But it doesn't mean we shouldn't learn.
Brian: That's right, or maybe someone is stubborn. And that's why this part of Mbivila, these verses, make us afraid because someone else might cause problems when things get difficult. * Everyone should be judged by their own standards and should not try to force their opinions on others. You, and your family, don't know if Mbivila teaches us to be judged by our own standards within our community.
Eric: That is true.
Brian: Jehovah's Witnesses are helped by articles and publications about marriage and raising children. Read them and see what they say, I think they have helpful information.
Eric: Okay, I will. And what shall we discuss next?
Brian: It's good. Or perhaps you like Kisessen, you can find it at www.jw.org/sw. You will find more helpful information there.
Eric: Does it have more verses?
Brian: These articles offer help to strengthen families and overcome challenges. We can also look at the article titled "Help for Couples and Parents." This article has several points that can help strengthen families. Would anyone want to read it?
Eric: Yes. "Resolving Problems in Your Marriage." I see this topic is important!
Brian: The article has many useful tips. Let's see what this section says. Eric, would you like to read?
Eric: Yes. It says: "Communication in marriage is like the blood of life in the body, and love and respect are like the heart and lungs that pump that blood." I continue to feel this is very insightful.
Brian: It's good to read such things. There is also a Bible verse that supports this. Go ahead and read it and understand its meaning.
Eric: Yes, I see. It is Ephesians 5:33. It reads: "However, each one of you should also love his wife as himself; and the wife should respect her husband."
Brian: Do you understand how this verse helps us to appreciate our relationship and show affection?
Eric: Is that so?
Brian: To put it simply, a husband should love his wife as much as he loves himself, and the wife should respect her husband, and vice versa. Isn't that right?
Eric: Yes. I agree with you.
Brian: Often, couples misunderstand each other when it comes to showing affection, so how can we ensure that we always meet each other's needs?
Eric: I see your point is complex.
Brian: And since this verse was written almost 2,000 years ago, I think it shows how important it is for a couple to have a strong emotional connection, and to avoid letting small issues ruin their happiness. And even though they were addressed as "heart and lungs" it is about love and respect being essential for every couple.
Eric: I realize the Bible has many principles to help us.
Brian: I feel the same way. And perhaps we could discuss another topic called "Four Steps to Resolving Conflicts" which will help us in this regard. *
Eric: That sounds good. I will consider your suggestion.
Is it possible to find more guidance on this matter in the Bible? Would you like to learn more about God's Kingdom and what Jehovah's Witnesses believe? If so, I would be happy to talk to one of Jehovah's Witnesses. They can talk to you about these matters.

text:
KWAKŨNA visa ũtembeete ũtukũ vandũ kasĩlanĩ na ũtataĩĩe ũyĩw'a mũndũ akũatĩĩe. Wamwĩw'a oou, ũyĩũngama, nake ũyĩw'a aũngama. Ũivanga kwĩkalaata, nake ayambĩĩa kwĩkalaata. Woona vekala ũu, ũisemba nginya nyũmba kwa mũnyanyau ũtwĩe vakuvĩ. Mũnyanyau aũvingũĩa na walika nyũmba kwake, nũtonya kwĩw'a wauuta.
No wĩthĩwe ũtaakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu, ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa ve maũndũ angĩ matumaa ũthĩnĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, we no wĩthĩwe ũng'ang'anaa na wonzu mũna, ĩndĩ mavinda kwa mavinda ũyĩthĩa ũsyokeie thĩna ũsu? No wĩthĩwe ũmanthĩte wĩa kwa myaka mingĩ na ũyĩthĩwa ũtaaũkwata o na kau nĩwĩkĩaa kĩthito mũno kũũmantha? Nĩwĩw'aa ũithĩnĩka wasũanĩa maũndũ ala matonya kũũkwata wakũa? Kana ve kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtumaa ũthĩnĩka?
O na ethĩwa wĩ na thĩna wĩva, we tyo wĩw'e mũyo ũkethĩwa na mũndũ ũtonya kũmũtavya mathĩna asu na aiũtetheesya ĩla maũkwata? We wĩ na mũnyanyau ta ũsu? Ĩĩ, Yeova nĩ mũnyanyae waku o tondũ waĩ mũnyanyae wa Avalaamu kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Isaia 41:8-13. Nthĩnĩ wa mũsoa wa 10 na 13, Yeova atavĩtye athũkũmi make atĩĩ: "Ndũkakĩe, nũndũ nĩ vamwe naku; ndũkateve, nũndũ nyie nĩ Ngai waku; ngakwĩkĩa vinya; ĩĩ, ngakũtethya; ĩĩ, ngakũũngamya na kw'oko kwa aũme kwa ũlũngalu wakwa. Nũndũ nyie, Yeova Ngai waku, ngakũkwata kw'oko kwaku kwa aũme, ngĩkwĩa, Ndũkakĩe; ngakũtethya."
"NGAKŨŨNGAMYA"
We nĩwĩw'aa ndeto isu sya Yeova iyĩũkiakĩsya? Kwatata kũsũanĩa kĩla Yeova ũkwathĩte mũsoanĩ ũsu. Mũsoa ũsu ndũkwasya kana ũkaendanasya na Yeova aũkwatĩte kw'oko. Ũkatw'ĩka ũkaendanasya na Yeova aũkwete, kw'oko kwake kwa aũme kwĩthĩwa kũkwete kwaku kwa aka. Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye kana "kw'oko kwa aũme kwa ũlũngalu" kwa Yeova kũkakwata 'kw'oko kwaku kwa aũme.' Ũu no ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya kana Yeova akaũkusasya nĩ kana akumye mathĩnanĩ ala makaũkwata. Aendeee na kũũkusya, ekwĩa atĩĩ: 'Ndũkakĩe, nĩngũũtethya.'
We nĩwonaa Yeova ta Ĩthe waku wĩ wendo na Mũnyanyau ũla ũtonya kũũtethya ĩla wĩ na thĩna? Yeova nĩwendeeaw'a nue, nũkũthĩnĩkĩaa, na nũvangĩte vyũ ũkũtethya. Ĩla wakwatwa nĩ mathĩna, Yeova endaa ũkew'aa wĩ mwĩanĩe nũndũ nũkwendete mũno. Kwa w'o, Yeova nĩ "ũtethyo wĩ vakuvĩ twĩ thĩnanĩ."—Sav. 46:1.
KWĨW'A ŨITHĨNĨKA NŨNDŨ WA NAĨ WEEKIE ĨVINDA ĨVĨTU
Andũ amwe nĩmathĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa naĩ meekie tene mayona Ngai ta ũtaaĩsa kũmaekea. Ethĩwa wĩw'aa ũu, sũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Yovu, ũla weetĩkĩlile 'mothũku ma wana wake.' (Yovu 13:26) O nake mũandĩki wa Savuli, Ndaviti, eew'aa o ta Yovu, na nĩkyo kĩtumi wamwĩsũvie Yeova akĩmwĩa atĩĩ: "Ndũkalilikane naĩ sya wana wakwa, o na mavĩtyo makwa." (Sav. 25:7) Nũndũ tũi eanĩu, ithyonthe 'nĩtweekie naĩ, na tũivikĩaa ũtaĩo wa Ngai.'—Alo. 3:23.
Mwambĩĩonĩ, ũvoo ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Isaia kĩlungu kya 41 waandĩkĩiwe andũ ma Ngai ma tene. Maĩ mamũvĩtĩisye Yeova mũno nginya atw'a kũmakany'a kwa kũmaeka methĩwe ngombo Mbaviloni. (Isa. 39:6, 7) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Ngai nĩwasũanĩaa ĩvinda yĩla ũkamatangĩĩa ala makelila na maimũsyokea! (Isa. 41:8, 9; 49:8) Ũmũnthĩ, Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa eyũmbanĩtye vyũ kũmew'ĩa tei na kũmony'a wendo ala meelila na mekwenda kũmwendeesya.—Sav. 51:1.
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Takuya, * ũla wang'ang'anaa nĩ kana aeke kĩmanyĩo kĩthũku kya kũsisya visa sya ũlaalai na kũkwatanga mamutha make ma ũsyai nĩ kana eanĩsye wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. Mavinda kwa mavinda nĩwasyokeaa imanyĩo isu nthũku. We wĩona Takuya ta weew'aa ata? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Neew'aa nĩ mũndũ wa mana mũno, ĩndĩ ĩla namwĩsũva Yeova andekee, nĩwangwataa kw'oko, na akambũkĩlya." Yeova eekaa ũu ata? Atumĩa ma kĩkundi kya Takuya mamwĩie no amakũnĩae simũ mavinda ala wasyokea thĩna ũsu. Takuya aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Ũyaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũkũnĩa atumĩa simũ, ĩndĩ kĩla ĩvinda namakũnĩa, neew'aa neekĩwa vinya mũno." O na atumĩa nĩmavangie mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko athi kwa Takuya nĩ kana akamwĩkĩe vinya. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu wa mũthyũlũlũko amwĩie Takuya atĩĩ: "Ndinoka vaa kwaku oou kĩtumbo. Nĩ vaa nũndũ atumĩa mendaa ngũthokee. Nue manyuvie nĩ kana nũke ũkwĩkĩa vinya." Takuya easya atĩĩ: "Ninyie neekĩte naĩ, ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwe weeyumisye kũndetheesya aitũmĩa atumĩa." O na Takuya nĩweekie maendeeo atw'ĩka vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda na yu athũkũmaa ovisinĩ wa ũvonge. Kwoou o tondũ kweethĩiwe kwa mwana-a-asa ũsu, Ngai akakũkĩlya wavalũka.
KŨTHĨNĨKA NŨNDŨ NDWĨ NA WĨA
Andũ aingĩ nĩmathĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa kwaĩwa nĩ wĩa. Namo angĩ nĩmavutawa wĩanĩ na ũyĩthĩa ti laisi kũkwata wĩa ũngĩ. We wĩw'a ata ũkatw'ĩka kĩla vandũ wathi ũimantha wĩa ũkeawa ndwĩandĩkwa? Veethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, andũ amwe mew'aa mate vata. Yeova atonya kũũtetheesya ata? No aeme kũũtethya ũkakwata wĩa ũla ũkwenda vau kwa vau, ĩndĩ no aũtetheesye ũkalilikanaa ndeto ii sya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti: "Naĩ mũnini, na yu nĩ mũkũu; ĩndĩ ndyaaona mũlũngalu atiĩtwe, kana ũsyao wake ũkĩvoya lĩu." (Sav. 37:25) Yeova nĩwonaa wĩ wa vata mũno vyũ, na akaũkwata na "kw'oko kwa aũme kwa ũlũngalu" nĩ kana aũtetheesye kwĩthĩwa na syĩndũ ila sya lasima ila syendekaa nĩ kana ũendeee na kũmũthũkũma.
Nake Sara, ũla wĩkalaa Colombia, nĩwoonie kw'oko kwa Yeova. Aandĩkĩtwe kambunĩnĩ wathũkũmaa ĩvinda yonthe na waĩvawa nesa. Ĩndĩ nũndũ endaa kwongela ũthũkũmi wake kwa Yeova, nĩwatiie wĩa ũsu na ambĩĩa ũvainia. Ĩndĩ ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũkwata wĩa ũtonya kũthũkũma mĩthenya ĩmwe. Ambĩĩisye nduka nini ya kũta ice-cream, ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda athelelwa na avunga nduka ĩsu. Sara aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩvavĩtie myaka ĩtatũ nde na wĩa, ĩndĩ nĩndũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mũno nũndũ nĩwandetheeisye kũmĩĩsya." Ĩvinda yĩu, nĩweemanyĩisye kũvathũkanasya katĩ wa syĩndũ ila sya lasima na ila sya kwĩtanĩthya, na eemanyĩsya kwĩkala ate kwĩmakĩa kwondũ wa mũthenya ũla ũatĩĩe. (Mt. 6:33, 34) Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, mũndũ ũla wamũandĩkĩte nĩwamwĩtĩie wĩa ĩngĩ, na amũtũnga o vala waĩ atanamba kũtia wĩa. Sara eeie mũnene wake kana nũkwĩtĩkĩla wĩa ũsu ethĩwa akamwĩtĩkĩlasya athũkũmae mĩthenya ĩmwe na mĩthenya ĩla ĩngĩ ayĩthĩawa ayĩka maũndũ make ma kĩ-veva. O na kau Sara ndakwataa mbesa siana ila wakwataa tene, kĩla ũkwataa nĩkĩmũtetheeasya kũendeea kwĩthĩwa e vainia. Aiweta ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩu waĩ na mathĩna, Sara aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnoonie kw'oko kwa Yeova."
KŨTHĨNĨKA NŨNDŨ WA MAŨNDŨ ALA MATONYA KŨŨKWATA WAKŨA
Ũndũ ũngĩ ũthĩnasya andũ nĩ kũthĩnĩkĩa maũndũ ala makamakwata makũa. Andũ aingĩ mathengeea myaka ya kuma wĩanĩ nĩmasaanĩaw'a kana nĩmakethĩawa na mbesa sianĩĩe wĩthĩe no mekale me eanĩe. O na nĩmathĩnĩkaa ĩũlũ wa mowau ala matonya kwĩsa kũmakwata makũa. Nĩvatonyeka Ndaviti akethĩwa nowe wamwĩsũvie Yeova akĩmwĩa atĩĩ: "Ndũkaambĩkye kũasa ĩvinda ya ũkũu; ndũkaandie yĩla vinya wakwa wĩthela."—Sav. 71:9, 18.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũmatetheesya athũkũmi ma Yeova makethĩwa me eanĩe ĩla makũa? Nĩ kwa kũendeea kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kũla kwĩ Ngai, na maimanya kana akeanĩsya mavata moo ma kĩla mũthenya. Ethĩwa vu tene manaĩ na malĩ mbingĩ, yu no matheesye kĩlasi na mayĩmanyĩsya kwĩanĩwa nĩ syĩndũ nini. No methĩe kana "kũya nyũnyi" kwĩ kavaa kwĩ kũya "ng'ombe" o na no kũmatetheesye makesianĩa na mowau! (Nth. 15:17) Ethĩwa nũtw'ĩte kũmwendeesya Yeova, akaũtetheesya o na ĩla wĩkũa.
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya José na Rose, ala methĩĩtwe me athũkũmi ma ĩvinda yonthe mbee wa myaka 65. Kwa myaka mingĩ, nĩmasũvĩaa ĩthe wa Rose ũla waĩ mũwau na wendaa mũndũ wa kũmũsũvĩa kĩla ĩvinda. O nake José aĩ mũwau kanza na nĩwaendeee kũng'ang'ana na ũiiti wayo (chemotherapy). We Yeova nũtetheesye José na Rose ala methĩĩtwe me aĩkĩĩku kwake? Ĩĩ, nũmatetheesye. Atũmĩie Tony na Wendy, ala maĩ ma kĩkundi kyoo, maumya nyũmba yoo na manenga athũkũmi asu ma Yeova. Tony na Wendy mavangĩte kũnengane nyũmba ĩsu mana kwa mavainia ma ĩvinda yonthe. Myaka yĩ na vu ĩtina Tony e sukulu, asiĩlasya ndĩlĩsyanĩ akona José na Rose maendete ũtavany'a. Nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ kĩthito kĩla woonaa me nakyo, na ũndũ ũsu nĩwamũkiitie ngoo mũno. Nũndũ nĩmoonie mwana-a-asa ũsu na mũka meyumĩtye kũmũthũkũma Yeova na kĩthito o na nginya me akũũ, Tony na Wendy nĩmamanengie nyũmba ĩsu mekalae vo. Kwa myaka 15, Tony na Wendy nĩmethĩĩtwe maimasũvĩa José na Rose, ala yu me na myaka 80 na kĩndũ. José na Rose monaa ũtethyo ũla makwataa kuma kwa mwana-a-asa ũsu na mũka wĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Yeova.
O naku, Ngai nũkũtambũũkĩsye "kw'oko kwa aũme kwa ũlũngalu." Nũkwĩtĩkĩla kũtambũũkya kw'oko kwaku ũmũnenge Yeova ũla ũkwathĩte ũũ: "Ndũkakĩe; ngakũtethya"?
^ kal. 11 Masyĩtwa amwe nĩ mavĩndũe.
