translation:
There are times when dreams come at night to people, and they become confused and disturbed. The dream of an owl, or a dove, or the dream of a hawk. It happens with letters, or someone tells through letters. Look at this thing, it seems like something is calling me from the grave to bring gifts. The grave is filled and flies home, refusing to be bothered by anyone.
Don't be surprised if something doesn't happen as you wish, because sometimes things happen that make you sad. For example, will you be upset and argue with others, so that each person blames the other for causing sadness? Don't be saddened by working for years and being disappointed, and then finding yourself alone and unable to achieve anything? Is dreaming making you forget important things and preventing you from getting help? Or is there another reason that makes you sad?
But if you trust in God, you will not be ashamed, and you will not be afraid of anyone who tries to harm you or deceive you. Do you have a friend who can help you? Yes, Jehovah is your friend, just as he was Abraham's friend, as stated in Isaiah 41:8-13. In verses 10 and 13, Jehovah assures his people, saying: "Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, yes, I will help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand." "I WILL HELP YOU"
Are these comforting words from Jehovah meaningful to you? It is reassuring to know that Jehovah cares about you. Your faith strengthens when you see that Jehovah supports you. When you rely on Jehovah, he supports you, just as he supports those who trust in him. For this reason, the scripture says that Jehovah supporting someone 'with his righteous right hand' means supporting them with his power. This shows that Jehovah is able to protect those who trust in him. He continues to support them, saying: 'Do not fear, I will help you.'
Do you find that Jehovah is a loving and loyal Friend who helps you when you need it? Jehovah is always ready to listen, comfort, and give guidance. If you are facing difficulties, Jehovah will never abandon you, and he will continue to love you unconditionally. That is why Jehovah is "our refuge and strength"—Ps. 46:1.
TO REMAIN LOYAL AND ENJOY TRUE FRIENDSHIP
Some people become discouraged when they face trials and feel that God has abandoned them. Consider Job, who felt that God was treating him unfairly. (Job 13:26) Even King David, a man pleasing to God, sometimes felt like Job, and that is why he begged Jehovah: "Deal with me favorably, O Jehovah!" (Ps. 25:7) But we can be confident that 'his loyalty will sustain us,' and we can trust in God's promise.—Lam. 3:23.
My brothers, the prophecy recorded in Isaiah chapter 41 was originally addressed to God's people who were facing exile. Jehovah assured them that he would deliver them from Babylon. (Isa. 39:6, 7) And today too, God assures us that he will strengthen us and help us to overcome any obstacles! (Isa. 41:8, 9; 49:8) Therefore, Jehovah is eager to forgive and show compassion to those who acknowledge their mistakes and strive to please him.—Ps. 51:1.
Consider also the example of Onesiphorus, who readily searched for Paul while he was imprisoned and did not hesitate to refresh him spiritually. He repeatedly showed his concern for Paul. Did Onesiphorus' efforts go unnoticed by Jehovah? The apostle Paul commended him publicly and said: "He often refreshed me, and he was not ashamed of my chains." Jehovah remembers such loyal support. Paul continued to say: "May the Lord grant mercy to his household."—2 Tim. 1:16-18.
Like Onesiphorus, we can show our love for our brothers by actively searching for opportunities to encourage them and to assist them in times of need. Repeatedly showing genuine interest in others can have a powerful effect. Have you noticed how true this is? Paul wrote: "Onesiphorus was a very faithful man, and he knew well what a comfort he gave me." And Jehovah rewarded Onesiphorus' kindness by blessing him and his family. Onesiphorus continued to demonstrate his willingness to serve faithfully, always being ready to share the good news. So let us imitate the example of this fine man, and may God richly bless our efforts.
WHY PEOPLE CHANGE THEIR STANDARDS
Many people find it difficult to maintain their standards when faced with pressure from others. Some give in because they want to be accepted by those around them. Have you ever felt pressured to compromise your principles in order to fit in? It is not uncommon for young ones especially to feel this way. But remember that Jehovah is able to strengthen us. He can help us remain firm in our resolve, and he will never abandon us. As David sang: "I have been young, and now I am old, yet I have not seen anyone righteous forsaken or his offspring begging for bread." (Ps. 37:25) Jehovah sees the value of our loyalty, and he supports us with "the power of his might," helping us to stand firm despite difficulties and temptations.
Sara, who lives in Colombia, experienced this firsthand. She was raised in a home where standards were relaxed, and she often felt insecure. Because she wanted to please Jehovah, she began to study the Bible and pray earnestly. She realized that maintaining her standards would not always be easy. She recalls wanting to join her friends for ice cream, but they were going to a place known for questionable activity. Sara explains: "I had been associating with them for three years, but I started to see that pleasing Jehovah was more important than pleasing them." She made the decision to choose her friends carefully and to avoid situations that could lead to temptation. (Matt. 6:33, 34) Over time, her friends respected her decision, and some even admired her courage to stick to her convictions. And like Sara, we may face challenges, but we can trust that Jehovah will strengthen us to continue doing what is right. She learned to discern between good associations and bad influences, and she resolved to live in harmony with her conscience.
Recently, Sara's older brother tried to persuade her to lower her standards, but she firmly refused. She helped him to understand how important it was to adhere to moral principles and to avoid compromising oneself. Even though Sara still faces trials, she remains confident that Jehovah will support her. She says: "I trust in Jehovah."
WHY IT IS IMPORTANT TO SET HIGH STANDARDS
One thing that can help us is setting high standards for ourselves. Many young people spend years trying to figure out what is acceptable or what others are doing. But it is vital to focus on what is approved by God. King David pleaded with Jehovah to help him maintain his integrity, saying: "Keep me upholding myself, and I shall be saved."—Ps. 71:9, 18.
How can we stay determined to uphold Jehovah's standards when faced with pressure from others? By continuing to seek guidance from God through prayer and diligent study of the Bible, and by being mindful of the consequences of our choices. Do not get distracted by trivial matters or become preoccupied with what others think. Do not waste time debating whether something is "wrong" or simply "bad," or comparing yourself to others! (Prov. 15:17) Instead, let us strive to please Jehovah, and he will bless our efforts.
Consider the example of José and Rose, who have served Jehovah faithfully for over 65 years. For many years, Rose suffered from a serious illness and needed someone to care for her daily. Yet, José continued to support her and also underwent chemotherapy himself. How did Jehovah strengthen José and Rose during this difficult time? Yes, he helped them. They were assisted by Tony and Wendy, members of their congregation, who offered their home and provided practical support. Tony and Wendy willingly shared their home with José and Rose throughout their ordeal. Years later, Tony was able to attend school, while still making time to visit José and Rose regularly. He said that he felt privileged to do so, and he cherished those visits. It warmed his heart to see how much his son and daughter appreciated Jehovah. So Tony and Wendy continued to share their home with them. For 15 years, Tony and Wendy lovingly cared for José and Rose, who lived to be well over 80 years old. José and Rose saw the fruitage of their son and daughter's dedication to Jehovah.
And now, God reminds us with the words: "To comfort all who mourn." We can be confident that God will fulfill his promise: "I will fortify you; I will help you."
^ par. 11 Some experiences are heartwarming.

text:
YOSEVU WA ALIMATHIA o na ndakwatasya ũndũ ũkwatie ũkũmbaũ wa kũneena na ngavana Mũlomi, Vondio Vilato. Andũ nĩmeesĩ kana Vilato aĩ mũndũ mũmũ mũno vyũ. Ĩndĩ Yosevu nĩweesĩ kana ethĩwa Yesũ nũkũthikwa na ndaĩa, yaĩ no nginya mũndũ eyumye athi akũlye Vilato amũnenge ũ mwĩĩ. Ĩla Yosevu waendie kũneena nake eethĩie kaĩ o na ndeĩsaa kũmũetee thĩna ũndũ ũkũsũanĩaa. Vilato akũlilye ũmwe wa maovisa make ethĩwa kwa w'o Yesũ nĩ mũkw'ũ, na ĩla weethĩie nũkwie nĩweetĩkĩlilye Yosevu ose mwĩĩ wake. O na kau Yosevu aĩ na kyeva kingĩ, anengwa mwanya nĩweekalaatile asyoke vala Yesũ wooaĩwe.—Mko. 15:42-45.
Yosevu wa Alimathia aĩ ũũ?
Ataeny'e ata na Yesũ?
Na ve ũseo mwaũ wa kwenda kũmanya ĩũlũ wake?
AĨ MŨSAMI NZAMANĨ YA AYUTI
Ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Maliko yaĩtye kana Yosevu aĩ "mũndũ wa nzama wĩ ndaĩa." Twasisya mĩsoa ĩla yĩ ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu nĩtũkwona kana nzama ĩla yaneeneawa vau ti ĩngĩ ĩndĩ nĩ ĩla Nzama ya Ayuti. Nzama ĩsu nĩyo yaĩ koti ũla mũnene vyũ wa Ayuti, na nĩyo yaũngamĩe maũndũ ma Ayuti. (Mko. 15:1, 43) Kwoou Yosevu aĩ ũmwe wa ala matongoesye Ayuti na nũndũ wa ũu ti ũsengy'o kwona ainengwa mwanya wa kũlika aneene na ngavana ũsu Mũlomi. O na tũiseng'aa ĩla twasoma kana aĩ mũthwii.—Mt. 27:57.
We nĩwonanasya ũtheinĩ kana nũmwĩtĩkĩlĩte Yesũ aũsumbĩke?
Nzama ya Ayuti nĩyamenete Yesũ. Ala maĩ nzamanĩ ĩsu nĩmeekĩte mũvango mamũae. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yosevu "aĩ mũndũ mũseo na mũlũngalu." (Luka 23:50) Aĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na asami aingĩ nzamanĩ ĩsu, nũndũ we aĩ mũlũngalu na aĩ na mĩendele mĩseo, na nĩwatataa ũndũ ũtonya aatĩĩe mĩao ya Ngai. O na ĩngĩ "nĩweteele ũsumbĩ wa Ngai." No kwĩthĩwa kĩu nekyo kĩtumi watw'ĩkĩte ũmwe wa amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ. (Mko. 15:43; Mt. 27:57) Na ti vinya ũkethĩa endie ũvoo wa Yesũ nũndũ ngoo yake nĩyendaa kũmanya ũla w'o na nĩyendaa kwona ũsili wa katĩ ũiatĩĩwa.
AĨ MŨMANYĨW'A WA YESŨ KWA KĨMBITHĨ
Ĩvuku ya Yoana 19:38 yaĩtye kana Yosevu "aĩ mũmanyĩw'a wa Yesũ, ĩndĩ kwa kĩmbithĩ nũndũ wa ũkĩa Ayuti." Yosevu akĩaa kĩ? Nĩweesĩ ũndũ Ayuti mamenete Yesũ na ũndũ matw'ĩte kana mũndũ w'onthe ũkũmũĩkĩĩa nĩmeũmũlũngya ĩsinakokenĩ. (Yoa. 7:45-49; 9:22) Mũyuti walũngw'a ĩsinakokenĩ avũthaw'a mũno nĩ Ayuti ala angĩ, akamenwa, na akavathwa. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yosevu wakĩaa kũweta andũnĩ kana we nũmũĩkĩĩe Yesũ. Keka nĩwatataa ethĩwa avetiwe Nzamanĩ na akeyanangĩa ndaĩa.
Yosevu ti we e weka walianĩlwe nĩ nthĩ. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Yoana 12:42, "o na aingĩ ma anene nĩmamwĩtĩkĩlile [Yesũ]; ĩndĩ kwondũ wa Avalisi maiaamumbũla, maikalũngw'e ĩsinakokenĩ." Mũsami ũngĩ wa Nzama ya Ayuti waĩ thĩnanĩ o ũsu aĩ Nikotemo.—Yoa. 3:1-10; 7:50-52.
Ĩndĩ we Yosevu nĩwatw'ĩkĩte mũmanyĩw'a o na kau ndaĩ na ũnyiau wa kũweta ũu mbee wa andũ. Ũsu waĩ thĩna mũnene wasũanĩa ndeto ii Yesũ wawetie: "Kĩla mũndũ . . . wĩmbumbũlaa mbee wa andũ, nakwa ngamumbũlaa mbee wa Asa wakwa ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ. Ĩndĩ o ũla wĩngaĩaa mbee wa andũ nakwa ngamũkaĩaa mbee wa Asa wakwa ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ." (Mt. 10:32, 33) Tũyĩsa kwasya Yosevu nĩwamũkaĩe Yesũ, ĩndĩ ndaĩ na ũnyiau wa kũwetea andũnĩ kana nũmwĩtĩkĩlĩte. We wĩ ũkũmbaũ wa kwĩka ũu?
Ũseo nĩ kana Mbivilia nĩtũtavĩtye ũseo ũmwe wa Yosevu nũndũ yaĩtye kana ndaakwatĩanĩa na mũvango ũla Nzama ya Ayuti yaĩ naw'o wa kũmũmina Yesũ. (Luka 23:51) Andũ amwe maasya kana Yosevu ndaĩ vo ĩla Yesũ wasilĩlawa, na ũsu no ũndũ ũtonyeka. Ĩndĩ o na kwĩthĩwe kwailyĩ ata, Yosevu ndalea kwĩthĩwa athĩnĩkie mũno oona ũndũ andũ mekwelelũkya vyũ ũsili wa katĩ, na we mwene nde ũndũ wĩka akalũnga maũndũ!
NĨWESIE KWOSA ĨTAMBYA
No twasye kana Yesũ ayũka kũawa, Yosevu aĩ anatw'a kũvetanga wia wake na ayĩkwatany'a na aatĩĩi ma Yesũ. Kĩu twĩkyona nesa ĩandĩkonĩ ya Maliko 15:43. Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye kana Yosevu nĩwaendie 'na ũnyiau kwa Vilato, amwĩtya mwĩĩ wa Yesũ.'
Nĩ laisi ũkethĩa Yosevu aĩ vo Yesũ aikw'a. Twĩasya ũu nũndũ amanyie kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ o na Vilato atemũvikĩsye livoti. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩla Yosevu waendie kwĩtya Vilato mwĩĩ wa Yesũ, Vilato 'waseng'ie ethĩwa nũminie kũkw'a.' (Mko. 15:44) Kwoou ethĩwa Yosevu nĩwoonie ũndũ Yesũ wathĩnĩie ũla mũtĩnĩ wa mathĩna, no kwĩthĩwa kĩu ne kyo kyatumie wasya wake wa ngoo ũkwata vinya na ayĩka ũtwi wa kwĩtĩkĩla ũtheinĩ kana we nĩ ũmwe wa amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ. Tũi na nzika kana o na eka maũndũ aangĩ, kĩu nĩkyanengie Yosevu ũnyiau wa kwosa ĩtambya. Nĩwatwie kana ndeendeea kwĩthĩwa e mũmanyĩw'a wa Yesũ kwa kĩmbithĩ.
YOSEVU NĨWATHIKIE YESŨ
Mĩao ĩla Ayuti manengetwe yawetete kana ala mooawa maaĩlĩte kũthikwa mũthenya o ũsu syũa yĩtanathũa. (Kũt. 21:22, 23) Ĩndĩ mo Alomi moaa kĩng'endilĩ matiaa mwĩĩ wakyo ũsũĩte o mũtĩnĩ ũoee vau kana makawĩkya ĩimanĩ vamwe na mĩĩ ĩngĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩu ti kyo Yosevu wendaa kĩmũkwate Yesũ. O vakuvĩ na vala Yesũ wooaĩwe, Yosevu aĩ na mbũa yenzĩtwe ĩvianĩ ĩtaĩ yaathikwa mũndũ. Nũndũ mbũa ĩsu ndyaĩ yaathikwa mũndũ, veonekana no ĩndĩ Yosevu waĩ anathamĩĩa Yelusaleme aumĩte Alimathia, * na no kwĩthĩwa avangĩte kana andũ make makathikawa vau. (Luka 23:53; Yoa. 19:41) Ĩtambya yĩu Yosevu woosie ya kũnengane mbũa yake yoonanisye ũndũ ũlaĩte, na nĩyatumie Maandĩko meanĩa ala mathanĩte ĩũlũ wa Masia makasya kana akathikwa "vamwe na ũla mũthwii."—Isa. 53:5, 8, 9.
Ve kĩndũ wonaa kĩ kya vata kwĩ ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova?
Mavuku onthe ana ma Ũvoo Mũseo monanĩtye kana mwĩĩ wa Yesũ waumw'a ũla mũtĩnĩ, Yosevu aũlingile na ngũa nzeo ya katane na awia ĩla mbũanĩ yake. (Mt. 27:59-61; Mko. 15:46, 47; Luka 23:53, 55; Yoa. 19:38-40) No Nikotemo e weka ũwetetwe na ĩsyĩtwa akewa nĩwatetheeisye Yosevu kwa kũete mĩtĩ yĩ mũuke mũseo ya kũvaka mwĩĩ wa Yesũ. Nũndũ asu maĩ andũ me nguma, ti laisi makethĩwa makuie mwĩĩ ũsu ne mo. Nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa manengie athũkũmi wĩa ũsu wa kũkua mwĩĩ na kũũthika. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa kwaendie ũu, wĩa ũsu aũme asu elĩ makũnie ndwaĩ ũndũ mũnini. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mũndũ akiita kimba atalawa ta mũvuku kwa ĩvinda ya mĩthenya mũonza, na kwoou mĩthenyanĩ ĩsu akiita kĩndũ o na kĩva, o nakyo kyatalawa ta kĩvuku. (Mot. 19:11; Akai 2:13) Mũndũ mũvuku ndaĩ atonya kũvulana na ala angĩ kyumwanĩ kyonthe kya Vasaka na ndaĩ esa kwĩka maũndũ ala meekawa kyumwanĩ kĩu. (Mot. 9:6) Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana anyanyae ma Yosevu mamanya nũmanthie ũndũ Yesũ ũkũthikwa nĩmaĩ matonya kũmũmena mũno. Ĩndĩ kũvikĩĩa vau Yosevu nĩwatw'ĩte kana kũmĩanĩsya na maũndũ asu ti ũndũ ta kũthika Yesũ na ndaĩa, na kwĩmanyĩthany'a andũnĩ kana we nĩ mũatĩĩi wa Klĩsto.
NGEWA YA YOSEVU ĨTHELETE ATA?
Mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo mamina kũweta ĩũlũ wa kũthikwa kwa Yesũ, vai vangĩ Mbivilianĩ vawetete ĩũlũ wa Yosevu wa Alimathia. Nũndũ wa ũu mũndũ no ende kũmanya-ĩ, Yo ngewa yake yang'okeile va? Vai mũndũ wĩsĩ ũsũngĩo. Ĩndĩ maũndũ ala mawetwa vau ĩũlũ meonany'a kana nũtonya kwĩthĩwa awetie ũtheinĩ kana we nĩ Mũklĩsto. Na ũu nĩw'o nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu mũĩkĩĩo wake watatiwe, weekie kwingĩvĩĩa vandũ va kũnyiva na akwata ũkũmbaũ. Kĩu kĩonany'a kana aendeeie nesa.
Ngewa ĩno ya Yosevu yĩtuma twenda kwĩkũlya ĩkũlyo yĩĩ ya vata: 'Ve kĩndũ o na kĩmwe twonaa kĩ kya vata kwĩ kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova, ta kwa ngelekany'o kĩvĩla kĩla tũnengetwe, wĩa ũla tũtethasya, malĩ ĩla twĩ nayo, andũ ma mũsyĩ, kana ũthasyo ũla twĩ naw'o?'
^ kal. 18 Noĩthĩwa ndũa ya Alimathia neyo Lama. Ũmũnthĩ taoni ya Rentis (Rantis) nĩyo yĩ vala Lama yaĩ. Mwathani Samueli asyaĩtwe ndũanĩ ya Lama, na yaĩ maili ta 22 (kĩlomita 35) ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya Yelusaleme welekele ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa.—1 Sam. 1:19, 20.

translation:
JOSPEH OF ARIMATHEA and he took the body and wrapped it in clean linen cloths and laid it in a new tomb which had been cut out of the rock, and rolled a stone onto the entrance of the tomb. And people were witnesses that Pilate was a very good man. But Joseph himself wanted Jesus to be crucified, yet because of fear he asked that they take Pilate aside so that he might eat with him. But Joseph went to speak to him about this matter and he begged him to let him have the body. Pilate wondered that Jesus was already dead, and called the centurion to ask if he was really dead. And when Joseph had taken the body, he spread fine linen and laid Jesus on it. And because he wanted to show respect for Joseph, he did not allow anyone to touch his body. And also Joseph had another thing, he was afraid to delay so that Jesus would not remain there overnight.—Mk. 15:42-45.
Joseph of Arimathea was who?
Did he know Jesus?
And what reason did he have for wanting to know his burial place?
ARE YOU SATISFIED WITH THE ANSWER
The account in Mark's Gospel says that Joseph was "a prominent man and righteous." Let us examine some scriptures to see whether this prominence was due to wealth or whether it was due to his being a member of the Sanhedrin. Wealth is what distinguished prominent men in those days, and it was used to influence matters in the Sanhedrin. (Mk. 15:1, 43) So Joseph was one of those who supported the Sanhedrin and because of this he was able to request the body from Governor Pilate. And let us investigate whether he was wealthy.—Mt. 27:57.
Do we understand why he respectfully buried Jesus?
The Sanhedrin honored Jesus. But they did not honor him because of his position, but because of their own laws. The Bible says that Joseph was "a good and generous man." (Luke 23:50) He had been greatly moved by what he saw during Jesus' trial, and because he was good and had great possessions, he dared to ask for Jesus' body. And he also "waited expectantly for God's Kingdom." Now knowing this reason is why he became one of Jesus' followers. (Mk. 15:43; Mt. 27:57) And it is not surprising that he showed respect for Jesus' body because his heart was inclined toward him and he wanted to see justice done.
ARE YOU ONE OF JESUS' FOLLOWERS IN FAITH
?
John 19:38 says that Joseph was "a follower of Jesus, though secretly out of fear of the Jews." What motivated Joseph? It was because Jesus honored God and because he knew that anyone who would acknowledge him would be excommunicated. (Jn. 7:45-49; 9:22) Many Jewish leaders feared excommunication more than God, so they remained silent and were cast out. This is why Joseph dared to ask for his body so that he could show others that he believed in Jesus. Let us dare to live according to our faith and proclaim the truth.
Joseph was not the only one influenced by fear. In harmony with John 12:42, "Many of the rulers actually believed in [Jesus]; but they did not confess him publicly for fear of being expelled from the synagogue." Another member of the Sanhedrin was Nicodemus.—Jn. 3:1-10; 7:50-52.
So Joseph acted as a secret disciple, and he took pains to carry out this act of kindness toward the people. He understood the weightiness of Jesus' words: "Everyone who acknowledges me before men, I will also acknowledge him before my Father who is in heaven; but whoever disowns me before men, I will also disown him before my Father who is in heaven." (Mt. 10:32, 33) Consider how Joseph risked disapproval by showing honor to Jesus, even when others did not believe. How can we imitate this quality?
This is similar to what the Bible shows about how some of Joseph's actions reflected his concern for complying with the law of the Jewish authorities regarding Jesus. (Luke 23:51) Some might say that Joseph was simply trying to please those in power, and that there was nothing noble about his conduct. But even if that were true, Joseph continued to show courage, and he personally benefited from the good standing he had among the people!
PLEASE CONSIDER THIS QUESTION
When Jesus stopped dying, Joseph requested permission to take his body down from the stake and buried him with his friends. This is related in Mark 15:43. That scripture says that Joseph went "to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus."
It is interesting to note that Joseph dared to approach Pilate. We learn this from the account in Matthew 27:57, 58, which states that Joseph "took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and laid it in his own newly made tomb, which he had cut out of the rock." So Joseph showed boldness in asking Pilate for Jesus' body, and Pilate "gave orders to hand over the body." (Mark 15:44) It seems that Joseph realized that Jesus had fulfilled prophecy, and he wanted to be associated with honoring Jesus' memory, so that he could be known as one of Jesus' followers. Let us remember this example, because it demonstrates Joseph's willingness to take action.
JOSEPH HONORED JESUS
On the day after the Sabbath, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered together and urged Pilate to order a guard to watch the tomb. (Matt. 27:62, 63) They were afraid that the disciples might come and steal the body and then report that God had raised him from the dead. But this did not deter Joseph from honoring Jesus. While they were guarding and sealing the tomb, Joseph had already shown courage by requesting the body. Furthermore, Joseph was a distinguished member of the Sanhedrin and lived in Arimathea, * and it is said that he was also among those who were waiting for the Kingdom of God. (Luke 23:53; John 19:41) The fact that Joseph took such steps shows how deeply he appreciated what Jesus had done, and it helped fulfill the scriptures that foretold that the Messiah would be put to death "with the wicked ones."—Isa. 53:5, 8, 9.
What can we learn from Joseph's example regarding our relationship with Jehovah?
Many others, including Nicodemus, who had previously visited Jesus by night, assisted Joseph in preparing the body for burial. (John 19:38-40; Matt. 27:57-61; Mark 15:42-47; Luke 23:50-53) Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes—about 75 pounds in weight—to embalm Jesus' body. Although many prominent men were disturbed by what happened, they did not openly express their feelings for fear of being expelled from the synagogue. It is important to remember that there will always be times when taking a stand for the truth requires courage. Why? Because people often react strongly when someone challenges their beliefs, and they may become hostile. (Prov. 19:11; Acts 2:13) A wise person recognizes that it is better to control his tongue than to risk losing everything because of reckless speech, and he understands that patience can help him avoid trouble. (Prov. 9:6) And so, like Joseph, we may need to exercise discretion about when and how we share our faith, while still remaining firm in our conviction that Jesus died for our sins and that he is the Christ.
WAS JOSEPH'S TOMB EMPTIED?
The account in John's Gospel states that Joseph prepared Jesus' body for burial, just as wealthy individuals commonly prepared bodies for burial in those days. But why does Matthew say that Joseph was from Arimathea? Or perhaps the question should be: What does this detail mean? Some scholars believe that Arimathea was a small village near Jerusalem, and that Joseph was a respected member of the Jewish Sanhedrin. The fact that Joseph was willing to take such a bold step shows that he must have been deeply moved by what happened. This incident reminds us that we should never prejudge anyone, assuming that they are beyond reach of God's influence.
Joseph's example encourages us to examine our own hearts and ask ourselves: 'What can I do to show gratitude to Jehovah for his undeserved kindness, especially now during this time of great tribulation, considering all that he has done for us, our families, and fellow worshipers?'
^ par. 18 The town of Ramah lay near Arimathea. The tomb of Samuel the prophet was located near Ramah, about 22 miles (35 kilometers) northwest of Jerusalem.—1 Sam. 1:19, 20.

text:
NĨ KYAŨ wĩsĩ kĩ na ũito wa vakuvĩ kĩlo kĩmwe na nũsu, ĩndĩ kũvika ũmũnthĩ kĩawa nĩkyo "kĩndũ kĩla kĩ vinya vyũ kũeleeka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ"? Kĩndũ kĩu nĩ w'ongo wa mũndũ. W'ongo wa mũndũ nĩ kĩndũ kya ũsengy'a mũno. O ũndũ twaendeea kwĩmanyĩsya mũno ĩũlũ wa w'ongo, now'o twonaa mawĩa ma Yeova me ma "ũseng'ya." (Sav. 139:14) Kwaeka twone ũtonyi ũmwe w'ongo wĩ naw'o. Ũtonyi ũsu nĩ kũsũanĩa.
Ũtonyi wa kũsũanĩa ũtonya kũelew'a ata? Ĩvuku yĩmwe yaĩtye kana ũsu nĩ ũtonyi ũla mũndũ wĩ naw'o "wa kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ kana kwĩsilya ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ũtaamona na meũtuma asanzamũka, kana maũndũ ũtaakomana namo." Wasũanĩa ũndũ ũsu, we tyo ũkwona nũtũmĩaa ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa mavinda maingĩ? Kwa ngelekany'o, waasoma kana ũkew'a ĩũlũ wa vandũ ũtaavavika? Kũtw'ĩka ndwaavavika nĩkwatumie ũemwa nĩ kũsũanĩa ũndũ vailyĩ? Kwoou ĩla tũkwetye kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kĩndũ tũtene, kana kĩndũ tũteũkĩw'a, kana tũtatonya kũkĩsama, kũkĩkwata, kana kũkĩnyungĩa, twĩthĩawa tũitũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa.
Mbivilia nĩtũtetheeasya kũelewa kana andũ moombiwe na kĩtutya kya Ngai. (Mwa. 1:26, 27) Kwoou no twasye kana o nake ũ Yeova mwene e ũtonyi wa kũsũanĩa. Nũndũ nĩwoonie nũseo atũnenge ũtonyi wa kũsũanĩa, e na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwenda ithyĩ tũtũmĩe ũtonyi ũsu kũelewa kĩla wendaa twĩke na tũikũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ twone maũndũ ala ũtwathĩte. (Mũta. 3:11) Tũtonya kũtũmĩa ata ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa nesa, na nĩ maũndũ meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a twĩũtũmĩa naĩ?
KĨLA KYONANASYA WĨTŨMĨA ŨTONYI WAKU WA KŨSŨANĨA NAĨ
(1) Kũvindĩĩsya maũndũ maku ĩvinda yĩla yĩtaĩle kana kũsũanĩa maũndũ ala mataĩle.
Ti ũthũku kũvindĩĩsya maũndũ maku. O na ve ũkunĩkĩli wonanĩtye kana kwĩka ũu nĩkũtethasya mũno. Ĩndĩ ĩandĩko ya Mũtavan'ya 3:1 yaĩtye ũũ: "Kwondũ wa kĩla kĩndũ ve ĩvinda." Kwoou nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka mũndũ akeka maũndũ amwe ĩvindanĩ yĩla yĩtaĩle. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũkambĩĩa kũsũanĩa maũndũ maku ĩla wĩ ũmbanonĩ kana ĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa wĩthĩwa ũiũtethya-ĩ, kana wĩthĩwa ũikwananga? O na Yesũ mwene nĩwatũkanisye atwony'a kana ve ũthũku wa kũeka ilĩko sitũ syambĩĩe kũsũanĩa maũndũ mate maseo, ta maũndũ makonetye ũlaalai. (Mt. 5:28) Maũndũ amwe tũtonya kũeka ilĩko sitũ isũanĩe nĩ maũndũ matonya kũmũthatya Yeova mũno. Wasũanĩa maũndũ makonetye ũlaalai, nũtonya kwĩsa kwĩka kĩndũ kĩthũku. Kwoou tw'a vyũ kana ndũketĩkĩla kũmũtia Yeova nũndũ wa mosũanĩo maku!
(2) Kũsũanĩa atĩ malĩ noyo ĩtonya ũkũtethya.
Malĩ nĩ ya vata na nĩtethasya. Ĩndĩ tũkambĩĩa kũsũanĩa kana malĩ noyo ĩkatũtethya na ĩitũetee ũtanu wa w'o, tũiema kwĩsa kũsonoka. Ũla mũndũ mũĩ weetawa Solomoni aisye atĩĩ: 'Syĩndũ sya mũndũ mũthwii nĩ ndũa yake yĩ vinya, na ta wako mũtũlu ũsũanĩonĩ wake.' (Nth. 18:11) Sũanĩa kwa ngelekany'o kĩla kyeekĩkie ĩla mbua nene mũno yauie na yaete kĩw'ũ kingĩ mũno kĩsionĩ kĩnene kya Manila, nthĩ ya Philippines, kwĩ Mwei wa 9, 2009. Mũisyo ũsu nĩwaemie kũkwata ala maĩ na malĩ? Mũndũ ũmwe mũthwii waaisye syĩndũ mbingĩ aisye atĩĩ: "Mbua ĩsu yatumie ithyonthe twĩanana, nũndũ yaetie mathĩna maingĩ mũno ĩteũvathũkany'a mũthwii na ngya." Nĩ laisi mũndũ akasũanĩa kana malĩ noyo ĩtonya kwĩsa kũmũtethya na kũmũsũvĩa. Ĩndĩ ũsu nĩ ũvũngũ.
(3) Kũtinda tũmakĩte nũndũ wa mathĩna o na matonya kwĩsa kũema kũtũkwata.
Yesũ atũtaĩte akatwĩa 'tũikemakĩe' mũno. (Mt. 6:34) Mũndũ ũla ũtindaa emakĩe mũno athyũũkasya kĩlĩko kyake mũno. Nĩ laisi tũkananga vinya mwingĩ mũno tũithĩnĩka kĩlĩkonĩ nũndũ wa mathĩna mate vo, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, mathĩna matanesa kwambĩĩa kana o na matonya kwĩsa kũema kumĩla. Maandĩko monanĩtye kana kũthĩnĩka kwa mũthemba ũsu nĩkũtonya kũtuma mũndũ akw'a ngoo kana o na eyĩtũka. (Nth. 12:25) Kwoou nĩ w'o, nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kũtũmĩa ũla ũtao wa Yesũ kwa kwĩkala tũte kwĩmakĩa mũno na tũteũmakw'a nĩ mathĩna matanamba kũtũkwata.
KĨLA KYONANASYA WĨTŨMĨA ŨTONYI WAKU WA KŨSŨANĨA NESA
(1) Kwonea thĩna vaasa na kũwathũkĩa.
Maandĩko matwĩkĩaa vinya twĩthĩwe na kĩlĩko na tũyoneaa maũndũ vaasa. (Nth. 22:3) Kwoou no tũtũmĩe ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa tũkamanya mũthya wa ũtwi tũkwenda kwĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũkathokw'a vandũ ve maya, ũtonya kũtũmĩa ata ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa ũmanye nũũthi kana ndwĩthi? Amba kũsũanĩa maũndũ ta aa: ala angĩ mathoketw'e naaũ, nĩ andũ meana ata makoka, na vala ĩ kyathĩ kĩkekĩwa, na ĩndĩ ũyĩkũlya: 'Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũendeea kyathĩnĩ kĩu? No nĩkwatye vyũ kana maũndũ ala makaendeea kyathĩnĩ kĩu makeethĩwa mosanĩte na myolooto ya Mbivilia?' Kwĩka ũu no kũũtetheesye ũkakũna visa wa kyathĩ kĩu kĩlĩkonĩ. Kwoou kũtũmĩa ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa nĩ kana wĩke motwi maseo no kũũvathane na mĩisyo ĩtonya kwananga ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova.
(2) Kũsũanĩa kĩlĩkonĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũmina thĩna mũna.
Ũtonyi wa kũsũanĩa no wĩtwe "ũtonyi wa kũmanya ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ĩla wakwatwa nĩ thĩna." Twasye nĩwaemanwa na mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa. Waĩle kũtũmĩa nzĩa yĩva nĩ kana wĩw'ane nake? Ve maũndũ maingĩ waĩle kwamba kũsũanĩa. We aeaa ngewa ata? Nĩ ĩvinda yĩva yaĩlĩte vyũ ya kũneenea thĩna ũsu vamwe nake? Waĩle kũtũmĩa ndeto syĩva na wasya ũilyĩ ata? Kwoou no ũtũmĩe ũtonyi waku wa kũsũanĩa ũkeyũmbany'a nesa ũmanye ũtonya kũtũmĩa nzĩa syĩva syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nĩ kana ũmine thĩna ũsu, na ĩndĩ ũinyuva nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ na ĩla ũkwona watũmĩa nĩmũkwĩw'ana. (Nth. 15:28) Nzĩa ta ĩsu ya kũmina thĩna no ĩtume kĩkundi kĩthĩwa na mũuo. Na ĩsu nĩ nzĩa nzeo mũno ya kũtũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa.
(3) Kũtũmĩa ũtonyi waku nesa nĩ kana wĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia nesanga na ũimĩsoma nesanga.
Nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũsoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya. Ĩndĩ kĩeleelo kitũ kĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ne o kũsoma ilungu mbingĩ kĩla mũthenya. Twaĩle kũsoma twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũelewa nĩ maũndũ meva me vau Mbivilianĩ matonya kũtũtethya na ũndũ tũtonya kũmatũmĩa. Kũsoma Mbivilia kwaĩle kũtuma tũelewa meko ma Yeova. Kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩke ũu nĩ kũtũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa. Ata? Kwasũanĩa ĩvuku Igeni Imani Yao. Kũsoma ngewa sya andũ ala mawetetwe ĩvukunĩ yĩu nĩkũtonya kũũtetheesya ũkũne visa kĩlĩkonĩ ũitũmĩa ũtonyi wa kũsũanĩa. Na ĩndĩ kyu nĩkĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũelewe nesa mũndũ ũla ũũsoma ngewa yake aeiwe ata na maũndũ ala weekie amekĩie va. Ũtonyi ũsu nũkũtetheeasya kwona vala waĩ, kwĩw'a mawasya ala maĩ vo, kwĩw'a mĩuke, na kũelewa ũndũ weew'aa. Kĩu kĩtumaa twĩmanyĩsya maũndũ ma vata na twĩkĩwa vinya nĩ ngewa imwe syĩ Mbivilianĩ twonaa ta tũsyĩsĩ nesa. Kũtũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa kwa nzĩa ĩsu ĩla tũũsoma Mbivilia nĩkũtonya kũtũtethya mũno.
(4) Kũsũanĩa ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa andũ me ĩnee.
Ĩnee nĩ nguma nzeo mũno. Nguma ĩsu ĩeleetw'e ta kwĩw'a woo ũla mũndũ ũngĩ ũkwĩw'a. Nũndũ Yeova na Yesũ nĩmonanĩtye nguma ĩsu, nũseo naitũ tũkaatĩĩa ngelekany'o yoo. (Kuma 3:7; Sav. 72:13) Tũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa na nguma ĩsu ata? Nzĩa ĩmwe nzeo vyũ ya kwĩka ũu nĩ kũtũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa. No kwĩthĩwa tũtaakwatwa nĩ ũndũ mũna ũkwatĩte mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa. Ĩndĩ no wĩkũlye-ĩ: 'Keka ninyie nĩkwatĩtwe nĩ ũndũ ũsu nĩw'a ata? Nĩthĩwa ndyenda ũtethyo wĩva?' Kũtũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa kũsũngĩa makũlyo asu nĩkũtonya kũtũtetheesya kwĩw'ĩa angĩ ĩnee mũnango. Kwa w'o nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa Aklĩsto aseango tweew'ĩa ala angĩ ĩnee ĩla tũũtavany'a na ĩla tũkwĩka maũndũ vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ.
(5) Kũsũanĩa ũndũ tũkekala twĩ nthĩ nzaũ.
Maandĩko nĩmaeleetye mũno ũndũ maũndũ makethĩwa mailyĩ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla twathĩtwe nĩ Ngai. (Isa. 35:5-7; 65:21-25; Ũvu. 21:3, 4) Namo mavuku maitũ me na mavisa maingĩ ala masoletwe kwosana na kyu kĩ Mbivilianĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mavisa nĩmatumaa tũsũanĩa na nĩmatũtetheeasya kũkũna visa tũitanĩa maũndũ asu maseo twathĩtwe. Nũndũ Yeova nĩwe watũnengie ũtonyi wa kũsũanĩa, nĩwĩsĩ nesa kwĩ mũndũ ũngĩ o na wĩva kana ũtonyi ũsu wĩ vinya mũno. Kwoou tũkaũtũmĩa kũsũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala ũtwathĩte, nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana maũndũ asu makeanĩa na kĩu kĩituma tũendeea kwĩthĩwa twĩ aĩkĩĩku, o tũendeee kũmĩĩsya mathĩna ala matũkwataa.
Yeova atũnengie ũtonyi ũsu mũseo vyũ wa kũsũanĩa nũndũ nũtwendete. No ũtũtetheesye kũmũthũkũma nesa kĩla mũthenya. Ekai tũendeee kwonany'a kana nĩtũtũngĩaa mũvea ũla watũnengie mũthĩnzĩo ũsu mũseo kwa kũũtũmĩa nesa kĩla mũthenya.

translation:
I ask myself why someone would spend half their life trying to figure out what it means when they say "everything happens for a reason"? That thing is human reasoning. Human reasoning is a matter of personal praise. So we try to praise ourselves with the reasoning, but we see the wonderful works of Jehovah which are "praise." (Ps. 139:14) Let us look at another example of reasoning. This example is forgiveness.
Can forgiveness be understood at all? One might think that this is the kind of reasoning a person has about "covering up sins or ignoring bad things that you don't want to remember or sending others away," or things you can't cope with. By forgiving something, wouldn't you then use the ability of forgiveness more often? For instance, have you read or heard about people who are unforgiving? To become unforgiving is to use our ability to forgive badly? Often we find it hard to forgive something completely, or something we were wronged on, or something we can't understand, grasp, or accept, then we fail to use our ability of forgiveness.
It helps us to understand whether people please God. (Gen. 1:26, 27) Often too we ask if Jehovah himself uses the ability of forgiveness. It is because of this that he teaches us the ability of forgiveness, and because of his example we go forward using this ability to understand everything we face and to deal with things that trouble us. (Prov. 3:11) Can we really use our ability of forgiveness well, and are there reasons why we sometimes struggle to use it?
EVERY TIME YOU USE YOUR ABILITY OF FORGIVENESS
(1) Consider what happened—the specific details or what was forgiven.
Don't hesitate to consider what happened. And if you feel unable to forgive or if you find it hard to talk about it, remember what Proverbs 3:1 says: "In all that you do, be considerate." Often it takes effort for a person to let some matters be forgiven. For instance, if you try to forgive what happened when someone hurt you badly or when they wronged you according to the Bible, will your ability of forgiveness work effectively, or will it seem inadequate? Also, did Jesus show us that there is a limit to how much we should forgive others, especially serious offenses? (Matt. 5:28) Some things we can let go of easily are things that could deeply offend Jehovah. Forgive serious offenses, and don't hesitate to seek help. Often we wonder if we are pleasing Jehovah by forgiving others!
(2) Forgiving does not mean forgetting.
Memories remain and are important. But when we decide to forgive, even if memories still bother us, we strive to move on. A wise man named Solomon once said: "The insight of a man makes his anger subside, and it is his glory to overlook transgression." (Prov. 18:11) Consider, for example, the great damage caused by the severe flood that struck Manila, in the Philippines, in September 2009. Did those who experienced this disaster forget their losses and pain? One survivor said: "The flood took everything from us, but it also brought us closer together." It is possible for a person to forgive without forgetting the pain and suffering. This is realistic.
(3) Patience helps us to deal with difficult situations and to learn to cope.
Jesus urges us to "make first things first." (Matt. 6:34) The person who prioritizes material possessions becomes anxious about them. Let us not become overly concerned about tomorrow, or worry about whether we will have enough to eat. The scriptures warn that excessive anxiety can lead a person to act foolishly or recklessly. (Prov. 12:25) Truly, it is vital that we apply Jesus' teachings by keeping our priorities right and avoiding being consumed by anxieties about material things.
EVERY DECISION INVOLVES A PERSONAL CHOICE TO FORGIVE
(1) To be considerate and understanding.
The Bible shows us how to deal with others and encourages us to be considerate. (Prov. 22:3) So let us use our power of discernment to determine when to forgive. For example, would you readily forgive someone who has wronged you, even if the offense was serious? Consider these questions: Is the offender truly repentant? Are they showing genuine regret? And ask yourself: 'What would be the best way to handle this situation?' Or perhaps you might wonder: 'Will forgiving him cause further problems, or will it help him to improve his conduct and appreciate the value of Bible principles?' Thinking carefully about such matters will help you make a wise decision. Using your power of discernment means also recognizing when forgiveness is not appropriate and protecting yourself from abusive individuals.
(2) Discernment helps us to decide what is important.
Discernment is defined as "the ability to judge well what is right and wrong." It is like being mature, whether physically or emotionally. Would we want to associate with immature people? There are many reasons why discernment is vital. Do we want to be influenced by those who have poor judgment? Does discernment help us avoid getting involved in harmful situations? Let us use our power of discernment to determine whether a person's words or actions are genuinely motivated by love and whether their conduct is consistent with what they say. (Prov. 15:28) Words that promote peace can build up a congregation. And peace is an excellent reason to use our power of discernment.
(3) Using your power of discernment involves studying the Bible regularly and praying earnestly.
It is beneficial to read the Bible daily. In fact, it is wise to read several chapters each day. We should read with the purpose of understanding the meaning of the scriptures and how they apply to us personally. Reading the Bible helps us understand Jehovah's thinking. One way we demonstrate that we value discernment is by using our power of discernment. Yes! Practicing discernment shows genuine faith. Reading the publications of God's organization also helps us strengthen our discernment. And when we take the time to understand what someone else is saying, we show that we value his thoughts and feelings. Discernment helps us see things from another's perspective, appreciate their efforts, overcome prejudices, and understand others. This enables us to learn valuable lessons from the examples found in the Bible and to benefit from the wisdom contained therein. By using our power of discernment while reading the Bible, we can grow spiritually.
(4) Practicing discernment helps us reach out to others.
Others respond well to kindness. Kindness can make a big difference in how people react. Both Jehovah and Jesus exemplify kindness, so let us imitate them in our dealings with others. (Prov. 3:7; Ps. 72:13) Can we show kindness to others by practicing discernment? One practical way to do so is by using our power of discernment. Do not judge others harshly because of past mistakes or imperfections. Instead, ask yourself: "Would I want others to be judged by my shortcomings?" Using our power of discernment to overlook offenses will help us maintain peaceful relationships. Thus, we can speak favorably about fellow Christians, even those with whom we may disagree.
(5) Practicing discernment requires constant effort.
The Scriptures reveal that future conditions will be far better than those we experience now under God's Kingdom. (Isa. 35:5-7; 65:21-25; Rev. 21:3, 4) However, many people today face difficulties and hardships. Why? Because imperfections cause us to stumble and make decisions that affect our lives. But Jehovah gives us the ability to discern, and he helps us improve and make wise choices. So let us continue to practice discernment in all aspects of life, and let it guide us when dealing with difficult situations or making important decisions.
Jehovah gives us this ability to discern so that we can progress. Let us therefore strive to use it regularly and appreciate its value.

text:
ĨVINDA ya atũmwa yangĩe kũthela, Kaio na Aklĩsto ala angĩ nĩmakomanie na mathĩna mana. Ve andũ mamanyĩasya momanyĩsyo ma ũvũngũ na matataa kũaany'a na kwonzya ikundi. (1 Yoa. 2:18, 19; 2 Yoa. 7) Ũmwe wa asu aĩ Ndioteleve, ũla waneenaa "ndeto mbathe" ĩũlũ wa mũtũmwa Yoana na angĩ. O na nĩwaleaa kũthokya Aklĩsto ala mesĩlaa kũu me kyalonĩ, na nĩwatataa kwasya angĩ meke o take. (3 Yoa. 9, 10) Ĩvinda yĩu maũndũ mailyĩ ũu nĩw'o Yoana waandĩkĩie Kaio valũa. Valũa ũsu waandĩkiwe nĩ mũtũmwa ũsu ta mwakanĩ wa 98 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, na nĩw'o ũla Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto wĩtĩtwe "Valũa wa Katatũ wa Yoana."
Kaio aendeeie kũmũthũkũma Yeova e mũĩkĩĩku o na kũtw'ĩka nĩwakomanie na maũndũ asu. Oonanisye ata kana aĩ mũĩkĩĩku? Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Kaio ũmũnthĩ? Valũa wa Yoana ũtũtetheeasya ata twĩke ũu?
VALŨA KWA MŨNYANYA MWENDWA
Mũandĩki wa Valũa wa Katatũ wa Yoana eyĩtĩte "ũla mũtumĩa." Ndeto isu syĩ syoka nĩsyatetheeisye Kaio, ũla waĩ ta mwana wa Yoana mwendwa, amanya kana valũa ũsu waumĩte kwa mũtũmwa ũsu. Valũanĩ ũsu Yoana eetie Kaio "mwendwa, ũla nĩmwendaa w'o." Yoana asyokie aelesya kana eĩkwatya kana Kaio aendeee nesa kĩ-mwĩĩ o ũndũ waendeee nesa kĩ-veva. Isu ko itai ndeto nzeo mũno!—3 Yoa. 1, 2, 4.
Kaio nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi o na kũtw'ĩka valũa ũsu ndũwetete ũu. Yoana akathie Kaio nũndũ wa kũthokya ana-a-asa o na kau ndamesĩ. Yoana oonaa ũsu ne ũndũ waĩkĩĩthisye kana Kaio nĩ mũĩkĩĩku nũndũ mavinda onthe athũkũmi ma Ngai methĩĩtwe me andũ mathokasya aeni.—Mwa. 18:1-8; 1 Tim. 3:2; 3 Yoa. 5.
Ndeto isu Yoana watũmĩie kũkatha Kaio nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa e mũthokya wa aeni syĩonany'a kana ana-a-asa nĩmookaa vala ve Yoana kuma isionĩ ingĩ ila syaĩ na ikundi kana makauma kĩsionĩ kĩla waĩ maendete ikundinĩ, na kwoou no nginya methĩwe mamũtavasya kĩla moona. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa ana-a-asa asu nomo matumaa Yoana amanya kĩla kĩendeee ikundinĩ.
Waĩ ũseo Aklĩsto ala me kyalonĩ mathũmũĩle kwa Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Mĩkaawa ĩla yaĩ na kũndũ kwakomawa yaĩ na nguma nthũku, ala makomela kw'o mayasũvĩawa nesa, na ĩngĩ yaĩ kĩtina kya mĩkalĩle mĩthũku. Kwoou vatonyeka aendi ma kyalo ala oĩ mathũmũĩlaa kwa anyanyae moo. Na kwoou ethĩwa nĩ Aklĩsto makomaa kwa Aklĩsto ala angĩ.
"NĨMAUMIE KWOO NŨNDŨ WA YĨLA SYĨTWA"
Yoana nĩweekĩie Kaio vinya aendeee kũthokasya aeni nũndũ amwĩie 'amaumaasye kyalonĩ kyoo ũndũ waĩle kwa Ngai.' Ĩla waandĩkie ĩũlũ wa kũmaumaasya aasya kana nũseo kũmamanthĩa kĩla maĩ na vata nakyo kwondũ wa kyalo kĩla kyaĩ mbee woo nginya ĩla mevika kũla maendete. Tũyĩsa kũlea kana Kaio nĩwamekĩte ũu ala maĩ mela kũthyũmũĩla kwake nũndũ nĩmatavisye Yoana maũndũ maseo ĩũlũ wa wendo wake na mũĩkĩĩo wake.—3 Yoa. 3, 6.
Aeni asu nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa meethĩawa me amisonalĩ, asyaĩĩsya ala mathokeaa ikundi, kana o ala matũmwa nĩ Yoana. O na methĩwe maĩ aaũ, kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana maendaa kwondũ wa ũvoo mũseo. Yoana aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩmaumie kwoo nũndũ wa yĩla Syĩtwa." (3 Yoa. 7) Nũndũ Yoana aĩ anaweta Ngai (sisya mũsoa wa 6), no twasye kana ndeto ii, "nũndũ wa yĩla Syĩtwa," syĩweta ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova. Kwoou nũndũ ana-a-asa asu maĩ ma kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto, nĩmaaĩle kũthokw'a nesa. Ũu wosanĩte nesa na ndeto ii Yoana waandĩkie: "Nĩtwaĩle kũthokya andũ ta asu, nĩ kana twĩthĩwe atethan'ya ma wĩa ma ũla w'o."—3 Yoa. 8.
ŨTETHYO KWONDŨ WA ĨTATWA YĨLA YAĨ VO
Ĩla Yoana waandĩkĩe Kaio valũa ndendaa o kũmũtũngĩa mũvea tũ. No wendaa kũmũtetheesya amanye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nũndũ wa thĩna ũla waĩ vo. Nũndũ wa itumi itesĩkĩe, mwana-a-asa ũmwe kĩkundinĩ weetawa Ndioteleve nĩwaleaa kũthokya Aklĩsto ala me kyalonĩ. O na nĩwatataa kũsiĩĩa angĩ maikamathokye.—3 Yoa. 9, 10.
Vate nzika, vai Mũklĩsto mũĩkĩĩku waĩ esa kwenda kwĩkala kwa Ndioteleve o na keka nĩwathokiw'e. Endete ũnene kĩkundinĩ, vai kĩndũ kyaumaa kwa Yoana wanengete ndaĩa, na aneenaa ndeto mbathe ĩũlũ wa mũtũmwa ũsu na angĩ. O na kau vai ĩvinda Yoana waaĩta Ndioteleve mwalimũ wa ũvũngũ, Ndioteleve nĩwaleanaa na momanyĩsyo ma mũtũmwa ũsu. Ndioteleve endete nguma na kwoou mwĩkalĩle ũsu wake ũtaĩlĩte Mũklĩsto woonanisye kana ndalũmanĩtye na Ngai. Ngewa ĩsu ya Ndioteleve yĩonany'a ũndũ andũ me na veva wa ũlei na wa kwĩtũlya matonya kũete mũaanĩko kĩkundinĩ na makatuma angĩ melelũka. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yoana weeie Kaio na kĩla ũmwe witũ atĩĩ: "Ndũkeelekan'ye na ũndũ ũthũku."—3 Yoa. 11.
KĨTUMI KĨSEO VYŨ KYA KWĨKA ŨLA ŨSEO
Ve Mũklĩsto ũngĩ weetawa Ndemetelio waĩ kĩvathũkany'o na Ndioteleve. Mũklĩsto ũsu awetetwe nĩ Yoana ta ũmwe waĩ ngelekany'o nzeo. Yoana aandĩkie ũũ ĩũlũ wake: "Ndemetelio nũkũsĩĩwe . . . Ĩĩ, o na ithyĩ nĩtũũkũsĩĩa; na nĩwĩsĩ ũkũsĩ witũ nĩ wa w'o." (3 Yoa. 12) Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Ndemetelio nĩwendaa ũtethyo wa Kaio, na Yoana nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aandĩkie valũa wake wa katatũ nĩ kana aelesye Kaio ĩũlũ wa Ndemetelio na nguma syake. No kwĩthĩwa Ndemetelio mwene no we watwaĩe Kaio valũa ũsu. Ndemetelio nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aĩ ũmwe wa ala matũmawa nĩ Yoana kana o akethĩwa aĩ mũsyaĩĩsya wa kũthyũlũlũka. Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, anenga Kaio valũa nũtonya kwĩthĩwa eekĩie vinya ndeto ila syaĩ valũanĩ ũsu.
Nĩkĩ Yoana weeie Kaio ethĩwe e mũthokany'a wa aeni o na kau no weekaa ũu? We Yoana nĩwĩthĩwa endaa kwĩkĩa Kaio vinya? Kana nĩwĩthĩwa asũanĩaa kana Kaio no atulw'e ngoo nĩ Ndioteleve, ũla wendaa kũlũngya Aklĩsto ala mekũthokya angĩ kĩkundinĩ? Tũitonya kũmanya nesa, ĩndĩ Yoana nĩwamwĩkĩie Kaio vinya na ndeto ii: "Ũla wĩkaa nesa nĩ wa Ngai." (3 Yoa. 11) Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi kĩla kĩseo vyũ kya kũendeea kwĩka ũla ũseo tũtekũeka.
W'o valũa wa Yoana nĩwatetheeisye Kaio aendeea kwĩthĩwa e mũthokya wa aeni? No twasye ũu nũndũ Valũa wa Katatũ wa Yoana nĩ ũmwe wa mavuku ala meekĩiwe Mbivilianĩ nĩ kana wĩkĩe angĩ vinya maendeee 'kwĩyĩelekany'a na ũla ũseo."
MAŨNDŨ ALA TŨKWĨMANYĨSYA VALŨANĨ WA KATATŨ WA YOANA
Vai maũndũ angĩ twĩsĩ ĩũlũ wa mwana-a-asa mwendwa, Kaio. O na vailyĩ ũu, kĩu kĩnini twĩsĩ ĩũlũ wake no kĩtũmanyĩsye maũndũ mana.
Mbee vyũ, nĩvatonyeka aingĩ maitũ tũkethĩwa twamanyĩiw'e ũw'o nĩ ana-a-asa kana eĩtu-a-asa aĩkĩĩku, ala meeyumĩtye kuma kwoo moke matũmanyĩsye. Tũikwasya kana nĩ Aklĩsto onthe ũmũnthĩ maendaa kũasa kwondũ wa ũvoo mũseo. Ĩndĩ no twĩke ta Kaio tũkatetheesya na tũkekĩa vinya ala mathyũlũlũkaa, ta kwa ngelekany'o, mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko na mũka. O na eka ũu, no tũmanthe ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka tũkakwata mbau ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala mathamĩĩa kũndũ kũngĩ, o nthĩ yoo kana nthĩ ĩngĩ, nĩ kana matetheesye kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Kwoou ekai tũendeee 'kũthokya aeni na ũlau.'—Alo. 12:13; 1 Tim. 5:9, 10.
Kelĩ, tũyaĩle kũseng'a tũkesa kwona mũndũ kĩkundinĩ alika kũneenea naĩ ala matongoesye, o na kau ũsu ti ũndũ wĩkĩkaa mũno. Tũiseng'a kĩtumi nũndũ Yoana nĩwaneeneiwe naĩ, o na mũtũmwa Vaulo. (2 Ako. 10:7-12; 12:11-13) Kwoou twaĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa maũndũ ta asu nĩmaumĩla kĩkundinĩ? Vaulo anengie Timotheo ũtao ũũ: "Ngombo ya Mwĩaĩi ndyaĩlwe nĩ ũkandanĩa, ĩndĩ nĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ĩ nduu kwa andũ onthe, ĩ na ũtonyi wa kũmanyĩsya, ĩ na wũmĩĩsyo: ĩkĩmataa na ũuu ala akananĩi." Kwĩkala tũuĩtye o na ĩla angĩ meũtũneenea naĩ no kũtume amwe mekwĩka ũu mesa kũalyũla mũtuo woo. Meeka ũu, "no kwĩthĩwa Ngai emanenga ũalyũlo wa ngoo kũvika ũmanyi wa ũla w'o."—2 Tim. 2:24, 25.
Katatũ, ve Aklĩsto mamũthũkũmaa Yeova me aĩkĩĩku o na kau nĩmathĩnaw'a. Aklĩsto ta asu nĩtwaĩle kũmakatha na kũmony'a kana nĩtũũmaelewa. Mũtũmwa Yoana nĩweekĩie Kaio vinya na amũĩkĩĩthya kana eekaa kĩla kyaĩle. O ta ũu, ũmũnthĩ atumĩa nĩmaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yoana kwa kwĩkĩa vinya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa nĩ kana 'maikanoe.'—Isa. 40:31; 1 Ath. 5:11.
Valũa wa Kĩkiliki ũla Yoana waandĩkĩe Kaio wĩ o ndeto 219. Kwoou yĩu nĩyo ĩvuku yĩla ĩkuvĩ vyũ Mbivilianĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩ ya vata mũno kwa Aklĩsto ũmũnthĩ.

translation:
The spirit of the world does not love truth, Caius and Aclystus also, but they are opposed by the wicked spirits. And many are deceived by false teachings and become confused and lose their identity. (1 John 2:18, 19; 2 John 7) One who was named Diotrephes loved to be first, saying "I have authority" like the apostle John said. But he refuses to acknowledge Aclystus and does not want to listen to me, and he opposes those who want to speak truthfully, and he does evil himself. (3 John 9, 10) The reason these things are mentioned is because John wrote this letter to Caius. This letter was written by this apostle around the year 98 CE, and it is what the Christian Greek Scriptures call "Third Letter of John."
Caius continued to honor Jehovah faithfully and to strengthen us with truthful things. Do we appreciate his faithfulness? Can we imitate Caius' example? Will John's letter help us to do so?
A LETTER TO A BELOVED BROTHER
The writer of Third Letter of John calls him "the beloved." It seems that this letter was originally sent to Caius, who was like a son to the beloved John, and it concerns this letter. In this letter, John addresses Caius as "beloved, whom I love." John did not express concern about whether Caius was continuing to walk in truth or whether he was continuing to walk in faith. Let us consider this point carefully!—3 John 1, 2, 4.
Caius deserves to be called a faithful minister and to receive this letter which is very beneficial. John commended Caius for showing hospitality to traveling brothers and for being generous. John knew that he was trustworthy and that Caius was faithful in honoring God among the people who were testifying.—Matt. 18:1-8; 1 Tim. 3:2; 3 John 5.
It seems that John wrote to encourage Caius to continue showing hospitality to traveling brothers, so that they might share the good news, and also to remind them that if anyone does not accept the message of John, they should not offer assistance or companionship, and let no one support those who misrepresent the truth. They will be held accountable for their actions when John arrives.
Those who followed Christ faithfully were persecuted by those who opposed Christ. Years passed with hardship and suffering, but they persevered in faith, and others experienced times of peace and prosperity. Let them go where they are welcomed by others. And let it be known that Christ honors those who honor Christ faithfully.
"I WILL HELP YOU IN YOUR TIME OF NEED"
John commended Caius for continuing to show hospitality to traveling brothers and told him that he was doing what is pleasing to God. But he warned against supporting anyone who rejects the message or refuses to acknowledge the authority of the apostles, and let no one welcome such people into their homes or give them encouragement—3 John 3, 6.
Traveling ministers often face challenges and opposition, or they are sent out by John. And we can be sure that they are acting in harmony with the truth. John said: "I will help you in your time of need." (3 John 7) The expression "your time of need" refers to the time when they needed spiritual food, and we can understand that this expression, "your time of need," refers to the time when they needed spiritual nourishment from Jehovah. Those who assist traveling ministers in their ministry work are helping fellow Christians, and this is in line with what John wrote: "I want to help those who travel and preach the good news."—3 John 8.
SUPPORT FOR THE TRUTH
John wrote to Caius to encourage him and to strengthen his faith. He wanted to assure him that he was right to extend hospitality to deserving brothers. Because of the importance of this matter, one young man named Demetrius had a fine reputation among believers and was recommended for his faithful service to Christ. And he deserved to receive support.—3 John 9, 10.
Therefore, dear friends, we should give support to people like Demetrius who go about doing good work and who faithfully share the truth. Remember how well John spoke of Demetrius, praising his loyalty and everything he does, and how he lives according to the teachings of the apostles. So let us give him the support he deserves, so that we may cooperate with the truth. The reason why John wrote to Caius and to each of us is: "Keep supporting those who travel around and preach the good news." —3 John 11.
WHY THIS IS IMPORTANT
Let us also show our appreciation for brothers like Demetrius who diligently serve the congregation. This brother has been commended by John, along with others who have shown themselves loyal. John writes about him: "Demetrius has a fine reputation… and what he does is true; and I can bear witness to his faithfulness." (3 John 12) It is encouraging to know that Demetrius is eager to live up to the example of Gaius, and John encourages us to write to Gaius so that he may continue to support Demetrius and his work. But let us not forget that Demetrius himself is someone who travels around and preaches. He may be among those whom John encouraged us to support. However, this is not the only reason why we should help Gaius, as there are others who deserve our support. Let us remember that Gaius is someone who eagerly welcomes brothers and sends them on their way in a manner worthy of God.
(3 John 11) That is why it is important for all of us to imitate his generosity.
So how did John encourage Gaius to show hospitality to traveling brothers? What can we learn from the fact that John reminded Gaius that he had previously welcomed brothers and sent them on their way in a manner pleasing to God? Let us examine this further, as John wrote to Gaius: "Dear friend, do not imitate what is bad, but imitate what is good." (3 John 11) This principle applies to all aspects of our lives, including how we extend hospitality.
What motivated John to commend Gaius for showing hospitality to traveling brothers? How can we apply the lesson found in John's third letter to our own lives?
OTHER THINGS WE CAN LEARN FROM JOHN'S THIRD LETTER
There are certain things we may not fully understand about dear brother Gaius. Yet, despite this, there is much we can learn from his example.
Often, we meet many people who claim to be Christians or who appear to be devout, yet their actions do not reflect genuine faith. We should remember that true Christians will strive to live up to the high standards set by Christ. So let us follow Gaius' example and continue to support traveling brothers and sisters, especially those who preach the good news. And in doing so, let us not neglect to care for needy ones, whether they are family members or strangers, and let us always be generous toward those who work hard and serve others faithfully. By doing so, we will demonstrate our love for our brothers and sisters.—Acts 12:13; 1 Timothy 5:9, 10.
Indeed, we want to show hospitality to fellow believers and share what we have with them, especially when they are in need. But how can we determine whether someone is truly deserving of our help? Paul commended Timothy for his discernment, saying: "A slave must be trustworthy, not given to drink, not pursuing questionable gain, but honest and upright, so that he may adorn the teaching about our Savior God in everything." Let us therefore use our discernment and avoid supporting those who exploit the generosity of others. In this way, "let us adorn the teaching about our God in everything."—2 Timothy 2:24, 25.
Furthermore, true Christians make zealous efforts to imitate Jehovah and demonstrate love. They do not simply claim to be followers of Christ but strive to live up to their profession. The apostle John wrote to Gaius, commending him for showing hospitality to traveling brothers and sending them on their way in a fitting manner. He also noted that Gaius was careful to discern who was worthy of such assistance, refusing to support those who were spreading false teachings.—Isaiah 40:31; 1 Thessalonians 5:11.
The value of the papyrus containing John's letter to Gaius has been estimated at $219,000. It is now part of the Papyri Library. This discovery provides further evidence of the dedication of early Christians.

text:
MŨNDŨ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Panayiota eanĩie kĩthamanĩ kĩ ũkanganĩ wa Mediterranea. E wa mũika, nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ maũndũ ma siasa. Ĩtina nĩwesie kwĩthĩwa e mũandĩki wa kyama kya siasa ũtũinĩ ũla wekalaa. O na nĩwaendaa nyũmba na nyũmba nĩ kana asangĩthye mbesa sya kyama kĩu. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda Panayiota nĩwakwie ngoo. Kĩla kyamũthĩnasya nĩ kana andũ ala meethĩawa nake kyamanĩ kĩu maĩ na kyende, nĩmendete ũnene, meethĩawa na ngusanĩsyo mbingĩ, na maĩ na kĩwĩu o na kau maasyaa nĩmendene.
Daniel asyaĩwe nthĩ ya Ireland na andũ ma mũsyĩ wake nĩmendete ndĩni mũno. Daniel nũlilikanaa nesa ũndũ atongoi na ndĩni maĩ angangany'a nũndũ nĩmanyusaa mũno, makotha kalata na makoya nthembo. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa kũmakya nĩ kana matindĩaa kũmwĩa akavĩvw'a ĩianĩ ya mwaki eeka naĩ.
Jeffery atũmĩie myaka mingĩ mũno aitethya wĩa wa kũthoosya syĩndũ sya kambunĩ ya meli ĩla ene methĩawa nthĩ ya United Kingdom na Amelika. Nũlilikene ũndũ mavinda maingĩ andũ ala makũnaa viasala o ta wake maongaa anene ma silikalĩ nĩ kana manengwe wĩa mũna. Nũndũ maĩ angangany'a, maĩ matonya kwathana kwĩka kĩndũ o na kĩva nĩ kana makwate wĩa ũsu.
Ũndũ wa ũsengy'a nĩ kana ve o maũndũ angĩ ta asu maendeeaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Wangangany'o wĩthĩawa vakuvĩ maũndũnĩ onthe, siasanĩ, ndĩninĩ, na maũndũnĩ ma viasala. Ndeto ya Kĩsũngũ "mwangangany'a" yumanĩte na ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla yonanasya mumya wa ũvoo kana mũthaũki wa sinema wĩvw'ĩkĩte ũthyũ nĩ kana ndakamanyĩke. Ĩndĩ ĩtina ndeto ĩsu yambĩĩie kũtũmĩwa kwonany'a mũndũ ũkũkenga ala angĩ etw'ĩte nĩ mũseo nĩ kana eyĩune mwene.
Andũ ala meekwa maũndũ nĩ angangany'a mew'aa maũmĩa mũno ngoonĩ na nĩ vinya mũno kumya ũndũ ũsu ngoonĩ. O na no mekũlye, "Wangangany'o ũkesa kũthela?" Ũndũ ũla wa kwendeesya nĩ kana Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye kana wangangany'o ũkathela.
ŨNDŨ NGAI NA MWANA WAKE MONAA WANGANGANY'O
Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana wangangany'o ndwaambĩĩw'a nĩ andũ ĩndĩ wambĩĩiw'e nĩ kyũmbe kya veva. Mwambĩĩonĩ, Satani e na kĩeleelo kya kũmwasya mũndũ mũka wa mbee, Eva, atũmĩie nzoka nĩ kana amwony'e no amũtetheesye. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:1-5) Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, andũ aingĩ nĩmekaa ũu kwa kwĩtw'a ta aseo ĩndĩ me na kĩeleelo kya kũkenga angĩ nĩ kana meanĩsye wendi woo.
Ĩla Aisilaeli ma tene malikilye wangangany'o ũthaithinĩ na mambĩĩa ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ, Ngai nĩwamakanisye mavinda maingĩ ĩũlũ wa mosyao mathũku ma ũndũ ũsu. Kwĩsĩla mwathani Isaia, Yeova Ngai ameie atĩĩ: "Andũ aa nĩmanthengeeaa, na nĩmandaĩaa na kanyw'a woo na ilomo syoo, ĩndĩ nĩmavetete ngoo syoo kũasa nakwa." (Isaia 29:13) Ĩla mbaĩ ĩsu yaleile kũalyũka, Ngai nĩwaanangie Yelusaleme na ĩkalũ yĩla yaakĩtwe vo. Mwambĩĩonĩ yaanangiwe nĩ Ambaviloni mwaka wa 607 mbee wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, na ĩndĩ yesa kwanangwa vyũ nĩ ita sya Lomi mwaka wa 70 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto. Kwa w'o ki, Ngai ndaketĩkĩlya wangangany'o wĩthĩwe vo tene na tene.
Ngai na Mwana Wake, Yesũ, nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ andũ ala aĩkĩĩku. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwambĩĩonĩ wa ũtavany'a wa Yesũ vaĩ mũndũ ũmwe weetawa Nathanaeli ũla wookie vala ũĩ. Ĩla Yesũ wamwonie aisye atĩĩ: "Onai, Mũisilaeli ki, ũte ũseleke!" (Yoana 1:47) Nathanaeli, ũla kwa ĩsyĩtwa yĩngĩ wĩtawa Valitholomayo atw'ĩkie ũmwe wa atũmwa 12 ma Yesũ.—Luka 6:13-16.
Yesũ nĩwatũmĩaa ĩvinda na aatĩĩi make na nĩwamatavasya nzĩa sya Ngai. Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ mayaaĩle kwĩthĩwa me angangany'a. Yesũ nĩwaleanile na wangangany'o ũla atongoi ma ndĩni maĩ naw'o ĩvinda yĩu na amakany'a. Aa nĩ amwe ma maũndũ ala meekaa.
Moonanasya "ũlũngalu" mbee wa andũ nĩ kana moneke. Yesũ ameie ethukĩĩsya make atĩĩ: "Ĩsũvĩei mũikekae ũlũngalu wenyu mbee wa andũ, nĩ kana mwoneke nĩo . . . tondũ angangan'ya mekaa." O na ameie kana ĩla meũnengane motethyo, meke ũu 'kĩmbithĩnĩ.' O na ĩngĩ maaĩle kũvoya vandũ me oka ĩndĩ ti kũvoya nĩ kana moneke nĩ andũ. Meeka ũu ũthaithi woo weethĩawa wĩ mũseo na Ĩthe wake aiwĩtĩkĩla.—Mathayo 6:1-6.
Nĩmendete kũsilĩla andũ ala angĩ. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Mwangangan'ya we, amba kwĩyumya mũamba ũsu wĩ ithonĩ yaku; na ĩndĩ ũkoona nesa kumya kaũvavathĩ kala ke ithonĩ ya mwana-a-au." (Mathayo 7:5) Ĩla mũndũ wambĩĩa kwona mavĩtyo ma ala angĩ me manene kwĩ ala make, ethĩawa ayenda andũ mamwone ũndũ ũtailye. Ũndũ ũsu ndwaĩle nũndũ "onthe nĩmeekie naĩ, na maivikĩaa ũtaĩo wa Ngai."—Alomi 3:23.
Meethĩawa na kĩeleelo kĩte kĩseo. Ĩvinda yĩmwe, amanyĩwa ma Avalisi na aatĩĩi ma kyama kya Elote nĩmookie vala ve Yesũ na mamũkũlya ĩkũlyo ĩũlũ wa kumya koti. Nũndũ maĩ nzeleke mamwĩie Yesũ atĩĩ: "Mũmanyĩsya, nĩtwĩsĩ kana wĩ wa w'o, na nzĩa ya Ngai nũmanyĩasya w'o." Na ĩndĩ mamũtea na ĩkũlyo yĩĩ, "Nĩkwosana na ĩla mĩao kũnenga Kaisali koti, kana ti w'o?" Yesũ amasũngĩie amea: "Nĩkĩ mũũndata, inyw'ĩ angangan'ya?" Yesũ ndaavĩtya ĩla wametie angangany'a nũndũ mayendaa ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu, ĩndĩ mendaa "kũmũtea ndetonĩ syake."—Mathayo 22:15-22.
Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmethĩawa na "wendo ũla wumaa ngoonĩ ntheu na wasyanĩ mũseo wa ngoo na mũĩkĩĩo ũte na wangangan'yo."—1 Timotheo 1:5
Ĩla kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kyambĩĩie Vendekosito mwaka wa 33, kyaĩ vandũ vaseo kwa andũ ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku na mendete ũw'o. Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmatatie ũndũ matonya kũvetanga wangangany'o mwĩkalĩlenĩ woo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Vetelo, ũmwe wa ala atũmwa 12, amekĩie vinya Aklĩsto methĩwe me ew'i "kwa ũla w'o kũvika kwenda ana-a-asa kũte wangangan'yo." (1 Vetelo 1:22) O nake mũtũmwa Vaulo amekĩie vinya Aklĩsto ala angĩ methĩwe na "wendo ũla wumaa ngoonĩ ntheu na wasyanĩ mũseo wa ngoo na mũĩkĩĩo ũte na wangangan'yo."—1 Timotheo 1:5.
ŨTONYI WA NDETO YA NGAI
Momanyĩsyo ma Yesũ na ma atũmwa make ala me Mbivilianĩ me ũtonyi o tondũ mailye ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa. Aineenea ũndũ ũsu, mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye atĩĩ: "Ndeto ya Ngai ĩ thayũ, na nĩ nthangaau, na nĩ mbũĩ kwĩ ũvyũ ũla mũĩ ngalĩ syelĩ, nayo ĩtonyaa kũvika kũaan'ya thayũ na veva, na maleenyũ na mũthungo, na ĩ mĩtũkĩ ya kũmanya mosũanĩo na kwenda kwa ngoo." (Aevelania 4:12) Andũ aingĩ nĩmatethekete nĩ momanyĩsyo ma Mbivilia na kwĩkala kwosana namo na nũndũ wa ũu, makevetangana na wangangany'o na makethĩwa me aĩkĩĩku. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o sya andũ aa atatũ mawetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ.
Panayiota aalyũkile ĩla wathokiw'e na eetĩkĩla kũthi maũmbanonĩ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩla waendie vo, ndaaona andũ mekwĩtw'a ta alũngalu nĩ kana mendeesye andũ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnoonie wendo wa w'o na noona andũ mendeeaw'a nĩ ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ. Ũndũ ũsu ndyaĩ naawona myaka yonthe ĩla naĩ siasanĩ."
Panayiota ambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na eeka maendeeo nginya avatiswa. Kuma avatiswa e na myaka 30, na aendeee kwasya atĩĩ: "Ndyatũmĩaa thayũ wakwa nesa ĩla naendaa nyũmba na nyũmba ndisangĩthya mbesa sya kyama kya siasa, ĩndĩ nesie kũmanya kũũtũmĩa nesa ĩla nambĩĩie kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, ũla nĩw'o ũkaete nthĩ yĩ na ũlũngalu."
Daniel nĩweekie maendeeo ma kĩ-veva na anengwa kĩanda kĩna kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. Ĩtina wa myaka yĩana ũndũ mũna, nĩweekie naĩ na wasya wake wa ngoo wambĩĩa kũmũthĩny'a. Ĩla walilikanile wangangany'o ũla woonaa ndĩninĩ aisye atĩĩ, "Noonie ũndũ ũla waaĩlĩte nĩ kũtia ianda ila naĩ nasyo. Ndyaĩ nĩsa kwĩkala na Aklĩsto ala angĩ mayona ta nĩ mũseo na tiw'o nĩilye."
Ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana ĩtina wa ĩvinda yĩana ũndũ mũna, Daniel nĩwaalyũlile nzĩa syake na eethĩwa na wasya mũseo wa ngoo na ĩndĩ asyokea ianda ila waĩ nasyo kĩkundinĩ. Andũ ala mamũthaithaa Ngai mate na wangangany'o methĩawa me aĩkĩĩku ta Daniel. Nĩmemanyĩasya 'kumya mũamba' ũla wĩ ithonĩ yoo matanosa ĩtambya ya "kumya kaũvavathĩ" kala ke ithonĩ ya mwana-a-asa.
Jeffery, ũla wĩthĩĩtwe e mũkũni wa viasala myaka yake yonthe aĩtye: "O ũndũ naendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia now'o namanyie kana ndyaĩle kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũlũsani na nĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩka ũndũ o na ethĩwa nĩ wĩva nĩ kana nĩkwate wĩa. Wasya wakwa wa ngoo nĩwamanyĩĩtw'e nĩ maandĩko ta Nthimo 11:1, yĩla yaĩtye kana 'kĩthimi kya ũkengani nĩ ũthatyo kwa Yeova.'" Kĩvathũkany'o na ala mamũkũlasya Yesũ ĩkũlyo ĩũlũ wa kumya koti, Jeffery nĩwamanyie kwĩka maũndũ ate na kĩeleelo kĩthũku o na ethĩwa maũndũ asu eĩka Mũklĩsto kana mũndũ ũte Mũklĩsto.
Ngũsĩ sya Yeova milioni mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩsyĩthĩawa syĩyũmbanĩtye kũatĩĩa maũndũ ala syeemanyĩsya kuma Mbivilianĩ. Nĩmekĩaa kĩthito kingĩ mũno nĩ kana 'mevw'ĩke mũndũ mweũ, ũla woombiwe na mũvw'ano wa Ngai nthĩnĩ wa ũlũngalu na ũtheu wa w'o.' (Aeveso 4:24) Twĩũkũlya wĩmanyĩsye ĩũlũ wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, kĩla maĩkĩĩaa, na ũndũ matonya ũkũtetheesya ũkemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla Ngai ũtwathĩte. Kũikethĩwa wangangany'o nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩsu nzaũ nũndũ "ũlũngalu ũtwĩe nthĩnĩ wayo."—2 Vetelo 3:13.
