translation:
A woman named Panayiota wrote a valuable letter regarding the Mediterranean Sea. Regarding her situation, she is troubled by political matters. The story continues to be told about a political party leader who recently passed away. And she goes from house to house perhaps finding support for that party. Today the story of Panayiota has begun. Every politician seems to find people who support their party with money and power, I have observed greatly, supported by many resources, and money and food and even cattle I have seen.
Daniel was born in Ireland and his parents observed him closely. Daniel refused this thing he inherited from his parents which was a joyful life, preferring letters and composing songs. Today this matter may cause difficulties in seeing the future of wood clearly.
Jeffery spent many years working in the field of investigating issues related to a shipping company located between the United Kingdom and America. He noticed that many things people know or don't know can cause great problems and sometimes lead to madness. These things are complicated, small things can become big things and cause trouble.
The issue of confusion often involves many things such as lies, politics, crimes, and legal matters. The Swahili word "confusion" is similar to the Greek word that means a state of chaos or a film director who makes mistakes and causes misunderstanding. Today this other word is used to describe someone who wanders around aimlessly or gets lost.
People who understand things are confused today and it is difficult to understand this matter today. And they ask themselves, "Is confusion necessary?" This matter of questioning is like God's question whether confusion is necessary.
GOD AND HIS SON SAW CONFUSION
History shows that confusion was introduced by people who were deceived by evil spirits. For example, Satan used a snake to tempt Eve, leading her astray and causing her to disobey. (Genesis 3:1-5) Similarly today, many people are easily misled because of their desire to wander away from God and be deceived.
But the Israelites repeatedly experienced confusion during their history and through their religious practices, God showed them many signs throughout his purpose. To illustrate this point, Isaiah quoted Jehovah God saying: "These people honor me with their mouths and praise me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me." (Isaiah 29:13) But despite this failure to obey, God preserved Jerusalem and its temple. For instance, it was destroyed by Babylon in 607 BC, and again it was devastated by the Romans in 70 AD. Because of this, God has consistently shown that he hates confusion and will always correct it.
God and his Son, Jesus, are deeply concerned about honesthearted people. As an illustration, the account of Jesus' ministry tells us about a man named Nathanael who was considered sincere. However, Jesus said about him: "Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!" (John 1:47) Nathanael, whose name Bartholomew also went by, became one of the 12 apostles of Jesus.—Luke 6:13-16.
Jesus taught people the truth and demonstrated what pleases God. The teachings of Jesus helped people to overcome confusion and understand God's purposes. He dealt with confusion that arose from false traditions and exposed them. These are some of the things that he did.
People often seek "popularity" among others to gain recognition. Jesus warned his followers: "Do not be anxious over what you shall put on," so that you may not become preoccupied with gaining the approval of others. And he explained that those who practice hypocrisy are like "actors" who pretend to be something they are not. Also, he cautioned against trying to please men rather than pleasing God and seeking his approval.—Matthew 6:1-6.
I want to help people to see this. Jesus said: "Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will clearly see how to remove the splinter from your brother's eye." (Matthew 7:5) But a person who is preoccupied with the faults of others often overlooks his own serious imperfections. This attitude leads to the thinking: "Everyone else is doing wrong, but I am right."—Romans 3:23.
Be reasonable and have good judgment. On one occasion, Pharisees and Sadducees questioned Jesus and asked him to perform a sign to prove his authority. They were testing him, but he replied: "A wicked generation asks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah." Then he left, and they wondered among themselves whether he had rebuked them for their lack of faith.—Matthew 16:1-4.
The Christians of that time were known for their "love for one another," which motivated them to show kindness and hospitality.—1 Timothy 1:5
However, in 33 C.E., the Christian congregation sent delegates to various places to meet with fellow believers and encourage them. The Christians of that time faced the challenge of remaining united despite differences of opinion. For example, Peter, one of the 12 apostles, once made a mistake that caused some Christians to stumble. (Galatians 2:11-14) Later, the apostle Paul corrected Peter and other Christians, reminding them of the importance of showing love and avoiding stumbling others.—1 Timothy 1:5.
THE IMPORTANCE OF GOD'S STANDARD
Jesus and his apostles emphasized the value of God's standard as found in the inspired Scriptures. He explained this principle when he said: "God's word is alive and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, penetrating to divide soul from spirit, and joints from marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart." (Hebrews 4:12) Many people find comfort in Bible principles and apply them to their lives, which helps them remain united and avoid serious mistakes. In contrast, those who disregard God's standards often experience difficulties.
Panayiota realized this when she was invited to attend a Kingdom Hall meeting at a local congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses. She says: "I enjoyed what I heard, and I noticed that the brothers and sisters were genuinely interested in helping people. They told me: 'We want to show you love and help you learn about God's Word.' I felt that sincerity and have been associating with them ever since."
Panayiota began studying the Bible and making changes in her life. Although she was only 30 years old, she decided to devote more time to sharing the good news, saying: "I used to think that going house to house was pointless, but I soon learned how much people appreciate being helped to understand the Bible and how grateful they are for the hope it offers."
Daniel made progress spiritually and became a dedicated member of the Christian congregation. After several years, he shared his faith with his wife, encouraging her to join him. However, she resisted, and he admits: "I was very frustrated because she would say, 'I don't need religion; I am happy just the way I am.' But I continued praying for her, and eventually she agreed to investigate."
As time went on, after several years, Daniel noticed the effect he was having on others, and he was encouraged by his wife's eventual interest in the truth. Others who knew Jehovah were also impressed by the changes Daniel had made. He explains the expression 'to plant seed,' which is similar to the expression 'to sow seed,' referring to the work of spreading the good news.
Jeffery, who spent most of his life working as a security guard, said: "The reason I started studying the Bible is that I wondered if I could find comfort from a counselor and overcome this problem. My wife supported me in this, and I found help in the scriptures, especially Proverbs 11:1, which says that 'honest scales are pleasing to Jehovah.' By associating with those who imitate Jesus, Jeffery came to realize the value of true worship and to appreciate what Christians can offer.
Millions of Jehovah's Witnesses around the world are eager to share what they have learned from the Bible. I recently met a brother who said that he felt like 'a new person, clothed with the new personality' because of God's loving discipline. (Ephesians 4:24) As we continue to learn about Jehovah's organization, we will be able to apply more fully the principles that God teaches us. To show our zeal, we should always be ready to talk about "the hope to which you were called."—2 Peter 3:13.

text:
MWANA-A-ASA ũmwe wĩtawa Allen * aĩtye atĩĩ: "No neew'aa ndikĩa kũthamĩĩa vaa. Ndyeesĩ kana nĩngũthokw'a kũũ, na kana nĩngwĩthĩwa na anyanya." Allen aendeee kũmanyĩa kwĩkala kĩkundinĩ kyeũ kĩ ũasa wa maili ta 900 (mbee wa kĩlomita 1,400) kuma kwoo.
O naku nũtonya kwĩw'a ũte mwĩanĩe ethĩwa nũthamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya wĩkale wĩ mwĩanĩe kĩkundinĩ kĩu wathamĩĩa? Ũtonya kwĩka ata ethĩwa kũmanyĩa kwĩ vinya kũte ũndũ ũnasũanĩaa? Kana ethĩwa tuuwe ũthamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ, ũtonya kũtetheesya ata ala mathamĩĩe kwenyu mamanyĩe mĩtũkangĩ?
ŨTONYA ATA KŨMANYĨA NA ŨYĨKA MAENDEEO?
Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Mũtĩ wakũwa na ũivandwa vandũ vangĩ, no wambaa kwĩthwa na mathĩna. Vethĩawa vailyĩ ũu nũndũ ĩla mũtĩ ũsu ũũkũwa, mĩi mingĩ nĩtilawa nĩ kana ũkuĩke nesa. Na wavandwa oou no nginya wambĩĩe kumya mĩi ĩngĩ. O ta ũu, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũithĩnĩka ĩtina wa kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ. Na ũu wĩthĩawa nũndũ wĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩla kĩngĩ ũnaĩ na mĩi, nĩkwĩthĩwa ũnaĩ na anyanya wendete na ũnaĩ na mĩvango mĩseo ya kwĩka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva. Wamina kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kyeũ, no nginya umye mĩi ĩngĩ nĩ kana wĩke maendeeo. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya wĩke ũu? No kũtũmĩa myolooto ĩla yĩ Maandĩkonĩ. Ekai tũneenee ĩmwe.
Ũla ũsomaa Ndeto ya Ngai ateũtĩĩa "ailyĩ ta mũtĩ ũvandĩtwe ũtee wa mbũsĩ syĩ manzĩ, ũla ũsyaaa ũsyao waw'o ĩvinda yaw'o, na ĩtũ yaw'o yĩtivovaa; na ũndũ o na wĩva wĩkaa nĩwaĩlaa."—Sav. 1:1-3.
No nginya mũtĩ ũnyw'e kĩw'ũ nesa kĩla ĩvinda nĩ kana wĩkalae ũsanzamũkĩte. O ta ũu, no nginya Mũklĩsto asomae Ndeto ya Ngai kĩla ĩvinda nĩ kana aendeee nesa kĩ-veva. Kwoou endeea kũsoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya na ndũkatĩĩe maũmbano. Ndũkanange mĩvango ĩla wĩthĩawa nayo ya ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ na kwĩmanyĩsya we mwene. Maũndũ onthe ala ũneekaa kĩkundinĩ kĩla ũnaĩ nĩ kana ũendeee kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, no mo waĩle kũendeea kwĩka.
"Ũla ũnyithasya akanyithw'a mwene."—Nth. 11:25.
Ũkakwata vinya na ũimanyĩa mĩtũkĩ weethĩwa na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũtavany'a. Mũtumĩa ũmwe wa kĩkundi wĩtawa Kevin aĩtye: "Kĩla kyandethisye mũno nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa nĩ kwosa ũvainia mũtetheesya twathamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kyeũ oou." Aendeee kwasya, "Tũyaakua ĩvinda ĩasa tũimanyana na ana-a-asa, mavainia, na tũimanyĩa kĩsio." Nake Roger, ũla wathamĩĩe kĩkundi kĩ mbee wa maili 1,000 (mbee wa kĩlomita 1,600) kuma vala wekalaa, aĩtye: "Nzĩa nzeo vyũ ya kũmanyĩa kĩkundi kyeũ nĩ kũthi ũtavany'a mavinda maingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka. O na ĩngĩ, tavya atumĩa kana no wĩyumye kũtetheesya maũndũnĩ ta kũthambya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ, kumya ũvoo ethĩwa ũla eĩ naw'o ndanoka, kana kũkua mũndũ ũmũtwae maũmbanonĩ. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa moona mũndũ mweũ ũkwĩyumya mũno nĩmamũthokasya nesa."
"Nenevai ngoonĩ syenyu."—2 Ako. 6:13.
Nenevanga ngoonĩ yaku kwa kũmantha ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ũtonya kũtuma ndũũ namo. Melissa e na mũũme vamwe na kelĩtu koo mathamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kyeũ, nĩmatatie mũno mamanthe anyanya angĩ. Aĩtye: "Nĩtwavulanaa na ala angĩ tũtanambĩĩa maũmbano, na ĩtina wa maũmbano. Kĩu nĩkyatũnengae ĩvinda ya kũea ngewa vandũ va kwĩka kũkethya andũ tũsembete." O na kwĩka ũu nĩkwatetheeisye mũsyĩ ũsu kũmanya masyĩtwa ma ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa mĩtũkĩ. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana nĩmanenevangie ngoonĩ kwa kũthokya ala angĩ kwoo mũsyĩ, na kĩu kyatuma ndũũ yoo yĩthĩwa yĩ ngamu. Asyokete akasya, "Nĩtwamanengie namba sitũ sya simũ naitũ twoosa syoo nĩ kana wĩthĩe no matũkũnĩe simũ na maitũtavya ĩla kwĩ maũndũ ma kĩkundi mekwenda kwĩkwa kana o maũndũ angĩ."
Ethĩwa nĩwĩw'aa vinya kũea ngewa na andũ ũtamesĩ, no wambĩĩe na tũmaũndũ tũla tũnini. Kwa ngelekany'o, tataa kwĩthĩwa na ũthyũ mũtanu o na ethĩwa ya mbee wĩĩw'a ũtekwenda. Andũ moona wĩ mũtanu, makendeeaw'a nue. O na Mbivilia yaĩtye "kyeni kya metho nĩkĩtanasya ngoo." (Nth. 15:30) Rachel, ũla wathamĩĩe kũasa na kũla weanĩie, aĩtye: "Nyie nĩ mũndũ wĩ nthoni. Mavinda amwe nĩkaa kwĩlasimĩthya kũneena na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa kĩkundinĩ kĩla nathamĩĩe. Nĩmanthaa mũndũ ũilyĩ nthĩ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ateũneena na ũngĩ. Mũndũ ũsu nũtonya kwĩthĩwa e nthoni o takwa." Wĩona ata ũkavanga kũneenaa na mũndũ mweũ mbee wa kĩla ũmbano kana ĩtina wa kĩla ũmbano?
Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũndũ wendete mũno kũea ngewa na andũ mwakomana ya mbee. Ĩndĩ o ũndũ ĩvinda yĩvĩtĩte, wendi ũsu nũtonya kũthela. Vakekala ũu nĩwaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana ũendeee kũmantha anyanya angĩ aingangĩ.
ĨNENGE ĨVINDA YA KŨMANYĨA
Mĩtĩ ĩmwe yakũĩĩw'a nĩyĩkalaa mũno ĩikaaumya mĩi nesa kũte ĩngĩ. O ta ũu, ĩvinda yĩla ũmwe ũkuaa aikaamanyĩa kĩkundi kyeũ ti yo ũngĩ ũtonya kũkua. Ethĩwa wĩ na kavinda kuma wathamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ na wĩĩw'a ũtaaĩsa kũmanyĩa, kũtũmĩa myolooto ĩĩ ya Mbivilia no kũũtethye:
"Tũikanoe nĩ kwĩka nesa: nũndũ kyathĩ kyavika tũkaketha, ethĩwa tũileela."—Aka. 6:9.
Ongelanga ĩvinda yĩla ũnasũanĩaa ta ũtonya kũmina ũitw'ĩka nĩwamanyĩa kĩkundi kyeũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, amisonalĩ nĩmekalaa myaka yĩana ũna nthĩ ĩla matũmwa mayĩsa kũtw'ĩka nĩmavangĩĩa savalĩ ya kũthi kũkethany'a mũsyĩ. Kwĩkalanga kũmanengae mwanya wa kũtuma ndũũ na ana-a-asa na kũmanyĩa kĩthĩo kya kũu maĩ.
Mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Alejandro nũthamĩte mavinda kauta, na kwoou nĩwĩsĩ kana vai ũndũ mũndũ wĩka akakalaata ĩvinda yĩla ũkũkua aikaamanyĩa. Aisye: "Ĩla twĩla kũthama ya mũthya kĩveti kyakwa kyaisye, 'Anyanyawa onthe namatia kĩkundinĩ kĩla twauma!'" Alejandro alilikanilye mũka kana ũu now'o waisye ĩla ĩngĩ mathamaa myaka ĩlĩ yĩ ĩtina. Ĩndĩ myakanĩ ĩsu ĩlĩ aĩ anatuma ndũũ na andũ angĩ na makatw'ĩka anyanyae.
"Ndũkasye, Kĩtumi nĩ kyaũ kya mĩthenya ya tene kwĩthĩwa kavaa kwĩ ĩno? nũndũ ndũkũlasya na ũĩ ũndũnĩ ũsu."—Mũta. 7:10.
Ndũkasianĩsye kĩkundi kĩla ũthamĩĩe na kĩla ũnaumie. Kwa ngelekany'o, ana-a-asa kĩkundinĩ kĩla ũthamĩĩe nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa me aneenu mũno kana me akilu mũno kũte ala ũnamanyĩĩte. Sisya mũno nguma syoo ila nzeo o tondũ o naku ũtonya kwenda masisye nguma ila syaku nzeo. Andũ amwe maseng'aa mesa kwĩthĩa kaĩ kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ kwamanengie mwanya wa kwĩthiana mamanye ethĩwa kwa w'o 'nĩmendete ana-a-asa' onthe!—1 Vet. 2:17.
"Voyai, na mũkanengwa."—Luka 11:9.
Endeea kũvoya Yeova aũtethye. Mũtumĩa ũmwe wĩtawa David aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndũketw'ĩkĩthye ngũmbaũ. Maũndũ maingĩ tũtonya kũmeanĩsya o tũtetheew'e nĩ Yeova. Voya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu." Ũla Rachel eĩ anawetwa nĩwĩtĩkĩlanĩte na ũndũ ũsu. Aĩtye ũũ: "Ethĩwa nyie na mũemewa nĩtwavika vandũ tweew'a ta tũte na ngwatanĩo nzeo na kĩkundi, tũmũvoyaa Yeova tũkamwĩa atĩĩ: 'Mwa tũtetheesye tũmanye ethĩwa ve ũndũ tũkwĩka ũũtuma aangĩ maemwa nĩ kũtuma ndũũ naitũ.' Ĩtina wa ũu nĩtũtataa tũtũmĩe ĩvinda yingangĩ na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa."
Asyai, ethĩwa syana syenyu nikũemwa nĩ kũmanyĩa, voyai nasyo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu. Ĩkai mĩvango ya kwĩthĩwa na ana-a-asa nĩ kana mũitetheesye itume ndũũ namo.
TETHEESYA ALA MATHAMĨĨA KWENYU MEKALE ME EANĨE
Vo ve ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ũkatetheesya ala mathamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kyenyu? Tata we mwene ũtume ndũũ namo kuma mavika oou. Nĩ kana wĩke ũu tata kũsũanĩa nĩ maũndũ meva wenda wĩkwe takeka nue mweũ, na ĩndĩ ũimeka maũndũ asu. (Mt. 7:12) Wĩona ata ũkamathokya mwĩke ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ ĩmwe kana mwĩloele ĩla vulongulamu ya kĩla mwei ya JW Broadcasting? Kana wĩona ata ũkamathokya mũtavany'e ĩmwe? Ũkamathokya mũĩsanĩe lĩu vamwe, mayĩsa kũlwa nĩ ũseo ũsu ũmekie. Nĩ maũndũ angĩ meva ũtonya kwĩka ũtetheesye ala eũ?
Carlos aĩtye: "Ĩla twavikie kĩkundinĩ kyeũ, ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa watũandĩkĩie nduka ila itesaa syĩndũ laisi. Kĩu kyatũtethisye mũno." Ala mathamĩĩa kwenyu maumĩte kũndũ kwĩ nzeve yĩ kĩvathũkany'o nĩmatonya kũtana mũno ũnamaelesya nĩ ngũa syĩva matonya kwĩkĩa ĩla kũvyũ, kũthithu, kana kwĩ mbua. Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kwĩka ũkamatethya mavikie ngoo sya andũ me ũtavany'a nĩ kũmaelesya ũndũ andũ ma kĩsio kyenyu mekalaa kuma tene kana ũkamaelesya mĩĩkĩĩo yoo.
KĨTHITO KYAKU KYA KŨTATA ŨMANYĨE KĨYĨSA KWAA MANA
Ũla Allen ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ nĩwĩkalĩte kĩkundinĩ kĩla wathamĩĩe mbee wa mwaka mũima. Aĩtye ũũ aililikana navu ĩtina: "Mbeenĩ yaĩ no nginya nĩlasimĩthye kũmanyana na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. Ĩndĩ yu nĩmonaa ta andũ ma mũsyĩ, na nĩ mũtanu." Allen esĩte kũmanya kana kũthama kũyaatuma asya anyanyae. Vandũ va ũu, nĩwameisye angĩ, na nĩmatonya kwĩkala me anyanyae ĩvinda yonthe.
^ kal. 2 Masyĩtwa amwe nĩ mavĩndũe.

translation:
One child named Allen said: "I don't want to go to school anymore. I prefer staying home, and I like being with my friends." Allen continued to learn about a certain place approximately 900 miles (about 1,400 kilometers) from there.
And you might want to know about another interesting place. Is it possible to discover a new interesting place while going to school? Can you find out something useful that concerns you? Or if you just went to another interesting place, can you share some experiences with your knowledgeable friends?
CAN YOU LEARN AND UNDERSTAND THINGS?
Consider this example: A tree has many roots, and it is supported by soil. People often say that if a tree is strong, many birds will perch on it, and if its roots are deep, it won't fall easily. And those roots also help it absorb water from many places. But if that happens, you may be tempted to stay longer in that other interesting place. And if that happens and that other place has trees, you will be surrounded by friends and have access to various ways of learning things. Continue going to school, and then you can explore more places when you grow up. Is it possible to do that? And use the tools found in textbooks. Let us think about this together.
That person who reads God's Word diligently "is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither—whatever he does prospers."—Ps. 1:1-3.
And so a tree needs water regularly to remain alive and healthy. Similarly, a Christian should read God's Word daily to continue growing spiritually. Keep reading the Bible every day and attending meetings. Make good use of the principles you learn regarding honesty and self-control. Other things too can make you strong and help you continue to please Jehovah and always want to learn.
"The generous man will prosper."—Prov. 11:25.
You may face challenges and experience difficulties. One elder named Kevin says: "Every time I feel down, knowing that my brothers and sisters are thinking of me comforts me greatly." He adds: "We spend time together, share meals, and get to know each other better." Also, Roger, who travels about 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers) to attend the congregation meeting, says: "The greatest benefit of associating with the congregation is that it helps me overcome many discouragements. And also, it encourages me to be diligent in serving, whether it means going from house to house, helping others when they need assistance, or supporting those who organize events. Families and individuals really appreciate someone who is willing to help."
"Keep encouraging one another."—2 Cor. 6:13.
I enjoy encouraging families and individuals whenever I can. Melissa and her husband, along with some friends, often visit people in their homes, offering practical help. She says: "We talk to them about their problems and offer suggestions. This has helped us build confidence in approaching people and helping them spiritually." And this approach has also helped me become more sensitive to the needs of families and individuals. It has also motivated me to reach out to others, which has brought much joy. Finally, she states: "We have learned to listen carefully and to speak kindly, so that we can comfort them and encourage them in their service to the congregation and in other ways."
Sometimes it is easy to be kind to those who are already inclined to respond favorably, but it may be difficult to show kindness to someone who seems unfriendly. However, Solomon wrote: "The loving-kindness of a righteous man is a blessing." (Prov. 15:30) Rachel, a sister who excels at being hospitable and welcoming, says: "I try to view everyone as worthy of attention. Often, I find myself wanting to spend time talking to families and individuals, especially those who seem discouraged. That person might need encouragement from Jehovah's organization." Such a person may be more receptive than you think. Do you ever wonder how to start a conversation with someone at an assembly or convention?
You can often find opportunities to befriend people who are alone or appear shy. If you sense they would appreciate it, take the initiative. Remember, a little effort on your part can make a big difference.
LESSONS FOR DEVELOPING EMPATHY
Some trees grow tall and strong because their roots go deep. Similarly, our empathy grows when we cultivate a close relationship with Jehovah. Kindness stems from genuine love and a desire to help others, motivated by Bible principles and a heartfelt concern.
We should 'make earnest efforts to discern what is pleasing to [God].'—Col. 6:9.
Consider how you react when someone treats you unkindly. Instead of becoming upset, try to understand why that person may be acting that way. For example, some young ones have had negative experiences that make them distrustful of adults. It takes patience to gain their confidence and help them see that not everyone will disappoint them.
A young man named Alejandro once felt hurt because a classmate was unfriendly. He recalls: "I wanted to tell him, 'Why are you treating me this way?' " Alejandro realized, however, that his classmate might be struggling with problems at home. After time, he saw that the boy became more approachable. Over the years, Alejandro has made an effort to show kindness to others.
"Father, why am I facing such trials? Is it because I have done something wrong?"—Job 7:10.
Try to empathize with those who are suffering. For instance, young ones who are experiencing difficulties may feel insecure or inadequate. Do not dismiss their feelings as silly or unimportant. Instead, take the time to listen to them and offer encouragement. Some people may be hesitant to accept help, but continue to reach out to them. Others may be quick to criticize, so be patient.—1 Pet. 2:17.
"Keep asking, and it will be given you."—Luke 11:9.
Continue to pray to Jehovah for guidance. King David wrote: "I call upon You, O Jehovah. Many times I need Your help and direction. Please answer my prayers." Rachel also learned to rely on prayer. She said: "Let us unite and ask Jehovah to help us teach our children to be honest and respectful, and to avoid bad associations. Let us pray to Jehovah, saying: 'Please help us train our children to choose good friends and to avoid those who would lead them astray.' We want our children to grow up to be fine Christians."
So, let your desire to understand motivate you to pray regularly. Be willing to put forth effort to get along with young ones, even if they frustrate you.
KEEP PRACTICING FORGIVENESS
Is there something someone has done that makes it hard for you to practice forgiveness? Our loving Father encourages us to forgive others. It is like letting go of a weight that is dragging you down, and it will benefit you greatly. (Matt. 7:12) Have you ever felt refreshed after watching the JW Broadcasting program "School For Making Disciples"? Have you ever felt encouraged by a kind comment from someone? Remember how you felt when someone forgave you. Are there other things that make it difficult for you to practice forgiveness?
Carlos says: "When we forgive, it is as if we give that person a gift—freedom from guilt. It feels so good." Practicing forgiveness can protect your heart from becoming bitter and can help you maintain a close relationship with Jehovah. It can also prevent you from being influenced by negative emotions such as anger, resentment, or jealousy. This can help you avoid causing pain to others or damaging your reputation.
YOUR DECISION TO KEEP TRYING IS IMPORTANT
Allen, who was disfellowshipped, found it difficult to forgive his family during the first year. He explains: "I kept replaying everything in my mind. I would think about those who had hurt me, and I got angry." Allen realized that holding on to his anger was hurting him more than anyone else. Like many others, he needed to work at forgiving them, and it took time for him to feel completely healed.

text:
MYAKA mĩna mĩvĩtu Cesar na mũka, Rocio, mekalaa nesa mũno California. Cesar athũkũmaa masaa maingĩ kwa kyumwa aithũkũmana na masinĩ sya kwongela kana kũolanga muutĩa nyũmba na kũlikya nzeve nyũmba. Nake Rocio athũkũmaa ovisinĩ wa ndakĩtalĩ masaa manini kwa kyumwa. Maĩ na nyũmba yoo na mayaĩ na syana. Ĩndĩ ve kaũndũ kamwe keekĩkie kaalyũla maũndũ moo vyũ. Kaũndũ keva?
Kwĩ Mwei wa 10, 2009, ovisi wa ũvonge wa Amelika nĩwatũmĩie ikundi syonthe sya nthĩ ĩsu valũa ũwetete vata wa kwongelanga myako ya ovisi wa ũvonge ũla wĩ Wallkill, New York, na ũkakũlya ala me na ũtũĩka mũna meyumye mausũsye valũa makũlĩtye mathi Mbetheli makatetheesye wĩa ũsu kwa kavinda. O na ala mavĩtũkĩtye myaka ĩla yendekaa nĩmakũlilw'e mausũsye valũa ũsu. Cesar na Rocio measya ũũ: "Nũndũ wa ũkũũ witũ, twamanyie twalea kwĩka ũu no tũeme kwĩsa kũkwata mwanya ũngĩ wa kũthũkũma Mbetheli o na twenda. Kwoou tũyaĩ tũeka mwanya ũsu wae oou mana!" Nũndũ wa ũu nĩmatũmie valũa woo mate kwananga saa.
Mwaka nĩwathelile Cesar na Rocio matetwa Mbetheli. Ĩndĩ no maendeeie kwĩka ũndũ matonya nĩ kana meanĩsye mũvango woo. Meekie ũu kwa kwĩtheeangya kĩlasi. Cesar easya: "Twaseũvisye vala twaiaa ngalĩ vatw'ĩka kasũmba ka lumu ũmwe nĩ kana wĩthĩe no tũkomboethye nyũmba ĩla twekalaa." Na ĩndĩ mauma nyũmba yoo ya ngolova ĩmwe yĩ na lumu mũonza, ĩla maakĩte ũndũ mendete tũmyaka o tũvũthũ tũvĩtu, na mathamĩĩa kala kasũmbanĩ. Cesar easya atĩĩ: "Kwĩka moalyũku asu nĩkwatumie wĩthĩwa wĩ laisi kwitũ kũthi Mbetheli tũkesa kũtw'ĩka nĩtweetwa." Ĩtina wa kĩu kwaendie ata? Rocio easya: "Twathamĩĩa kala kasũmbanĩ vathelile o mwei ũmwe na twakwata valũa twĩtĩtwe tũkatetheesye kwa kavinda wĩa ũla waĩ Wallkill. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o twamanyie kana ĩla twetheeisye kĩlasi, now'o tweekie kĩndũ Yeova ũtonya kũathima."
NĨMAATHIMĨTWE NŨNDŨ WA VEVA WOO WA KWĨYUMYA
O namo ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maana maingĩ nĩmeyĩimĩte maũndũ mana nĩ kana matetheesye wĩa wa kwaka ũla wĩ New York State, o tondũ Cesar na Rocio meekie. Amwe ma asu nĩmeyumĩtye matetheesye wĩa ũla wĩ Wallkill, namo angĩ aingĩ manengetwe kĩanda kya mwanya kya kũthi Warwick makatetheesye kwaka ovisi mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. * Nĩ kana mamũthũkũme Yeova nesanga, andũ aingĩ matwaanĩte nĩmatiĩte nyũmba syoo nzeo, mawĩa maseo, o na nyamũ ila maĩthĩtye. We Yeova nũmaathimĩte nũndũ wa veva ũsu woo? Vate nzika, nũmaathimĩte!
Kwa ngelekany'o, Way athũkũmanaa na maũndũ ma sitima na e na mũka, Debra, mangĩe myaka 60. Tene mekalaa Kansas, ĩndĩ mata nyũmba yoo na syĩndũ mbingĩ ila maĩ nasyo na mathamĩĩa Wallkill nĩ kana makaendaa Mbetheli kũtetheesya wĩa. * O na kau yaĩ lasima meke moalyũku mana nĩ kana mavote kũthamĩĩa Wallkill, nĩmonaa mayaaĩyĩima syĩndũ syoo mana. Debra aĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa wĩa ũla yu manengetwe: "Mavinda angĩ nonaa ta nalika mavisanĩ ala masolawa mavukunĩ maitũ monanĩtye ana-a-asa mayaka nyũmba me Nthĩ Nzaũ!"
Melvin na Sharon nĩmatee syĩndũ syoo vamwe na nyũmba yoo ĩla mekalaa me South Carolina nĩ kana makatetheesye wĩa ũla wĩ Warwick. O na kau vayaĩ laisi kwĩyĩima maũndũ ala meeyĩimie, mew'aa mũyo nũndũ me na kĩanda kya kũtetheesya wĩa ũsu wa vata mũno. Measya: "Vai kĩndũ kĩ mũyo ta kũmanya kana wĩkũna wĩa ũkatetheesya ũseũvyo witũ ũla wĩ nthĩ yonthe."
Kenneth na Maureen, ala me na myaka 50 na kĩndũ, nĩmathamie California mathi kũtetheesya wĩa Warwick. Kenneth aĩ wa myako na athyũmũĩa wĩa ũsu. Nĩ kana mathame nĩmavanganie na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe amasũvĩĩe nyũmba, na nũndũ ĩthe wa Kenneth nĩ mũkũũ makũlya andũ ma mũsyĩ mamũsũvĩe. Mo nĩmeliĩlaa maũndũ ala matiie? Aiee! Ken easya: "Nĩtũtethekete mũno. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ kwasya tũyĩsaa kũthĩna? Aiee, ĩndĩ twĩ na moathimo maingĩ, na ũũ nĩ wĩa tũtonya kwathĩĩa ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ."
ŨNDŨ MASINDIE MAWETU
Aingĩ matanamba kwĩyumya maĩ na mawetu mana maaĩlĩte kũmasinda. Kwa ngelekany'o, William na Sandra kuma Pennsylvania me na myaka 60 na kĩndũ na maĩ mamanyĩie kwĩkala kũu. Kambunĩ yoo ya kũseũvya syĩndũ sya masinĩ yaĩ na athũkũmi 17 na yaendeee nesa. Mekalĩte kĩkundinĩ kyoo kuma me anini, na andũ aingĩ ma mũsyĩ mekalaa vau ũtũinĩ. Kwoou ĩla meetiwe maendae Mbetheli ĩla yĩ Wallkill, nĩmamanyie kana yu no nginya matiaa vakuvĩ andũ onthe ala mamanyĩĩte na kyonthe kĩla meesĩ. William easya: "Tweew'aa twavikie kũla twaendete, na kwoou vate nzika kũthama nĩkw'o ũndũ ũla waĩ vinya vyũ kwitũ." Ĩndĩ e na mũka nĩmavoyie mũno na ĩtina wa ũu mathama, na kũvika ũmũnthĩ mayĩlilaa. William easya ũũ: "Mũyo ũla twĩw'aa nũndũ wa kũthũkũma vamwe na kũtindany'a na ala me Mbetheli tũyĩsa kũũkwata vandũ vangĩ o na va. Nĩ na Sandra twĩ na ũtanu mwingĩ tũtaĩ twaawona!"
Ricky athũkũmaa wĩa wa kũũngamĩa myako Hawaii. Nĩwathokiw'e aendae kũtetheesya wĩa ũla wĩ Warwick. Mũka, Kendra, nĩwendaa mũno mũũme etĩkĩle kũthi. Ĩndĩ ve ũndũ mũna mũito wamathĩnasya: moolanĩlaw'a nĩ ũndũ makaea mwana woo Jacob, ũla waĩ na myaka ĩkũmi na ũmwe. Masaanĩaw'a ethĩwa nĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ onthe mathamĩĩe New York State, na ethĩwa mwana woo akamanyĩa kwĩkala kũu.
Ricky easya: "Katĩ wa maũndũ ala twavangĩte kwĩka twathama oou, nĩ kũmantha kĩkundi kĩ na amũika maendeee nesa kĩ-veva. Twendaa Jacob akwate kĩtindo kĩseo." Ĩndĩ kĩkundi kĩla mesie kũkwata kĩ twana o twa ũtala, o na kau ve amwe vau mathũkũmaa Mbetheli. Ricky easya ũũ: "Mũthenya wa mbee ũla twaendie maũmbanonĩ vau nakũlilye Jacob woni wake ĩũlũ wa kĩkundi kĩu kyeũ mũno mũno nũndũ vayaĩ mũndũ me ĩika. Ambĩie, 'Ndũkamake, Tata. Nĩngũtuma ndũũ na ana-a-asa ma mũika ala mathũkũmaa Mbetheli.'"
Namo ana-a-asa asu ma mũika nĩmatumie ndũũ na Jacob. Kĩu kyamũtethisye ata? Ricky aeleetye akasya atĩĩ: "Mũthenya ũmwe kwĩ ũtukũ nesĩle vakuvĩ na vala mwanawa ũkomaa na noona atanesa kũvosya taa. Neesĩ nĩngũmũkwatya aithaũka ĩthaũ ya vitio, ĩndĩ namwĩthĩie aisoma Mbivilia! Ĩla nakũlilye Jacob eĩkata, ambĩie, 'Nĩtw'ĩte ta nĩ mũthũkũmi mweũ wa Mbetheli, na kwoou no nginya nĩsome Mbivilia yonthe na mwaka ũmwe.'" Vai nzika kana Ricky na Kendra me na mũyo mwingĩ nũndũ mbee Ricky e na kĩanda kya kũtetheesya mwako ũla wĩ Warwick, na kelĩ kũthama nĩkũtumĩte mwana woo eana kĩ-veva.—Nth. 22:6.
MAIMAKAW'A NĨ ŨNĨ
Mũthenya ũmwe wĩa ũla wĩ Wallkill na Warwick no ũkathela, na kwoou ala mathoketw'e matetheesye wĩa Mbetheli no mesĩ wĩa woo nĩ wa kavinda. Mo ana-a-asa asu na eĩtu-a-asa asu nĩmethĩwa maimakw'a nĩ kũla methi kana ũndũ meĩka wĩa ũsu wathela? Ai aiee! Aingĩ me na woni ta wa John na mũka, Carmen, kuma Florida, ala me na myaka 50 na kĩndũ na mathokiw'e matetheesye o kwa kavinda wĩa ũla wĩ Warwick. Wĩa wa John nĩ kũũngamĩa myako, na measya: "Kũvikĩa vu nĩtwonete ũndũ Yeova wĩanĩĩtye mavata maitũ. Tũikwona Yeova ethwa aatũete vaa nĩ kana etũtia." (Sav. 119:116) Nake Luis aseũvasya masinĩ sya kũvosya mwaki na e na mũka, Quenia, matetheeasya wĩa Wallkill. Measya atĩĩ: "Nĩtwonete Yeova aianĩsya mavata maitũ ma kĩ-mwĩĩ nũndũ we nĩ mũlau. O na kau tũyĩsĩ akeanĩasya mavata maitũ ata, na ĩndĩĩ, kana twĩ va, tũi na nzika kana we ndakaaeka kũtũsũvĩa."—Sav. 34:10; 37:25.
"ŨATHIMO, MŨVAKA VAE ŨTHEI WA KŨWĨANĨA"
Aingĩ ma ala maendete kũtetheesya wĩa ũla wĩ New York methĩwa mamanthie itumi sya kwĩlingya maikeyumye. Ĩndĩ nĩmatwie kũmũtata Yeova o tondũ we mwene ũtwĩĩte nĩtwĩke. Aĩtye: "Ndatai . . . , ethĩwa ndimũvingũĩa mbũthi sya ĩtunĩ, na kũmũtulũĩla ũathimo, mũvaka vae ũthei wa kũwĩanĩa."—Mal. 3:10.
We naku ũkamũtata Yeova nĩ kana wone ũndũ ũkakũathima mũno wĩana? Ĩthiane na ũivoya nĩ kana ũmanye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩvanga ũtetheesye wĩa ũũ mũseo ũendeee, wĩthwe wĩenda kũtetheesya wĩa ũla wĩ New York kana wĩenda kũtetheesya myako ĩngĩ ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Weeka ũu ũkeeyonea we mwene ũndũ Yeova ũkakũathima.—Mko. 10:29, 30.
Dale nĩ ingyinia wa myako na e na Cathy maumĩte Alabama. Elĩ metetheesya wĩa Wallkill na measya ũsu nĩ wĩa mũseo vyũ. Mongelete kwasya: "Ethĩwa wĩ na ũkũmbaũ wa kũtia vala wendete na wĩw'aa wĩ mwĩanĩe, ndũkaema kwona ũndũ veva wa Yeova ũtethasya wĩa." Ĩndĩ ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana wĩyumye? Dale easya: "Ola, ũole, na ũisyoka ũole o ĩngĩ ngalama ila ũtũmĩaa. Ndũkaaĩlila!" Gary kuma North Carolina ethĩĩtwe aiũngamĩa myako kwa myaka 30. E na mũka, Maureen, measya kana ũathimo ũmwe makwatĩte nũndũ wa kũthi Warwick nĩ kũkwata mwanya wa "kũmanyana na kũthũkũma na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ na aseo ki ala matũmĩĩte ĩvinda yoo yonthe maimũthũkũma Yeova me Mbetheli." Gary asyokete kwasya atĩĩ: "Wenda kũthũkũma Mbetheli no nginya wĩtheesye kĩlasi, na nengĩ vai nzĩa ĩngĩ yĩ kavaa ya kwĩsa kũvonoka nthĩ ĩno." Nake Jason na Jennifer maumĩte Illinois, na Jason tene aandĩkĩtwe nĩ mũndũ wosaa mawĩa ma sitima, na elĩ measya kana kũthi Wallkill makatetheesye wĩa ũla ũvangĩtwe nĩ Mbetheli "nĩ ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala mathengeanĩe na kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ." Jennifer ongelete ũũ: "Ve mũyo mwingĩ vyũ kũmanya kana kyonthe kĩla ũkwĩka Yeova nũkyonaa kĩ kya vata, na kũmanya kana kĩu ũkwĩka kĩkaũtethya mũno o na ĩvindanĩ yĩla Yeova ũtwathĩte. Yeova akekalaa ayĩkĩĩthya kana nĩwakũathima mũno kũthonoka o na ũndũ ũtonya kũsũanĩa."

translation:
Four years ago, Cesar and his wife, Rocio, moved to a beautiful place in California. Cesar works many hours because he enjoys working with machines whether it's repairing things around the house or fixing cars. Meanwhile, Rocio also works many hours in an office. We have a house and children and grandchildren. There is always something interesting happening. What's up?
On March 10, 2009, the American Immigration Service sent us the entire group of people who were waiting for news about their immigration case from the Wallkill, New York Immigration Service, and they told us to come with them and stay with them until our cases were resolved at Bethel. And those people who had been waiting for years were finally resolved with them. Cesar and Rocio said: "Our dream has come true, we thought we would never get this opportunity to work at Bethel and go. Now we will take advantage of this opportunity and make the most of it!" This matter has helped many people find hope.
The year passed and Cesar and Rocio were assigned to Bethel. But things didn't turn out as expected or as they had hoped. They found themselves attending classes. Cesar said: "We were surprised to learn that we were given only one small room to live in, which was very different from what we were used to." And indeed, their new home was a small room with just one bed, which made things difficult for them and their family, and sometimes they slept on the floor. Cesar added: "It seemed like a challenge to adjust to life at Bethel and to be able to fit into such a small space." What did Rocio think? Rocio said: "We slept on the floor for about a month and then we got mattresses and stayed at the Wallkill branch. That branch is where we learned how to attend classes, and now we can teach others about Jehovah."
THIS IS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU TRUST IN GOD
Many brothers and sisters have experienced great changes because they have dedicated their lives to serving in places like New York State, and this is true of Cesar and Rocio. Some of them have moved to Wallkill, while many others have served in the large Kingdom Hall near Warwick. * If we want to please Jehovah, we need to be willing to make sacrifices, give up our comfort, and even our possessions. Why does Jehovah allow us to face such trials? Let's see!
For example, Wayne enjoyed working with cars and his wife, Debra, was over 60 years old. They lived in Kansas, in a comfortable home with many things, but they felt drawn to Bethel to serve there. * And despite their age, they were willing to move to Wallkill, and they saw many blessings as a result. Debra shared this experience: "I never thought I would enjoy living in such a simple place, but I am so grateful for the opportunity to serve here!"
Melvin and Sharon also made changes, leaving their comfortable home in South Carolina to serve in Warwick. And although they missed some of the comforts of life, they found joy in being able to contribute to the work. She said: "It's a wonderful feeling to know that what you give up allows others to preach the good news."
Kenneth and Maureen, who are in their fifties, moved from California to serve in Warwick. Kenneth worked as a carpenter and enjoyed his work. He had been helping someone renovate a house when he received an invitation to serve, and Kenneth realized how much he enjoyed helping people. But did he hesitate? No way! Ken explained: "We really wanted to. Was it easy to leave everything behind? No, but we have many blessings, and this is a way to show our gratitude."
IMPORTANT INFORMATION
Many find it refreshing to simplify their lives. For example, William and Sandra in Pennsylvania, in their sixties, decided to downsize. Their modest home had 17 rooms and required constant maintenance, and many neighbors were impressed. The couple recently visited Bethel headquarters at Wallkill and were delighted to see so many brothers and sisters working together harmoniously. William said: "We felt very encouraged while visiting, and seeing them work so hard motivated us to do more." They both feel blessed and look forward to continuing. William added: "This change has allowed us to focus on spiritual things and spend time with those at Bethel, which helps us to strengthen our relationships with others. My wife Sandra and I have a lot of peace!"
Ricky decided to pursue his dream of moving to Hawaii. He was accepted to serve at the Warwick branch office. His wife, Kendra, fully supported his decision. They faced a challenge: their son Jacob, who is eleven years old. Moving would mean uprooting him from his school in upstate New York, where he was doing well.
Ricky said: "Despite all the adjustments we will have to make, we are determined to stay united as a family and continue serving Jehovah. We want Jacob to be happy." This move will allow the family to associate with other families who also serve at Bethel. Ricky added: "I remember one evening when we were saying goodnight to Jacob, he hugged me tightly and said, 'Dad, please take me with you to Bethel.' Then he added, 'I want to be with the people who love Jehovah.'"
So they took their son Jacob with them. Did this work out? Ricky happily reported: "One night I found him reading his Bible under the covers with a flashlight so he could finish reading before going to sleep. I quietly told him, 'I'm proud of you for wanting to read the Bible!' And I encouraged Jacob, telling him, 'Let's make a goal to read through the entire Bible together within a year.'" It is clear that Ricky and Kendra have much faith, and Ricky is grateful for the opportunity to serve at the Warwick branch office, and they are eager to help their son progress spiritually.—Ps. 22:6.
THEIR SECRET
One day at the Wallkill and Warwick assemblies, they learned that those who attend the Bethel assemblies also benefit greatly. So why did they take their children along when they went to Bethel? Was it easy? Not really! Many, like John and his wife, Carmen, from Florida, find it challenging to travel with their children, especially since they are over 50 years old. John says: "We realized that we need to show Jehovah how much we value spiritual things. We want Jehovah to know that we trust in him." (Ps. 119:116) Also, Luis enjoys helping others spiritually, and he and his wife, Quenia, attended the Wallkill assembly. He said: "We need to let Jehovah direct our lives, and we should be realistic. Even if we can't always accomplish everything we set out to do, we can be sure that he will support us." —Ps. 34:10; 37:25.
"PRAYER, A VALUABLE TOOL FOR STAYING STRONG"
Many in the New York area found it difficult to cope with the challenges of modern life. They wanted to please Jehovah, so they prayed to him: "Please test me…and examine my heart, and see if there is anything painful in me." —Mal. 3:10.
Are you praying to Jehovah regularly, even when you face difficulties? If you would like help to stay strong spiritually, perhaps you could talk to someone who attends the New York assemblies or to another mature Christian. This week's article will show you how Jehovah can strengthen you.—Mark 10:29, 30.
Dale and his wife, Cathy, moved from Alabama. He served at Wallkill and then he was assigned to serve in a circuit. He commented: "I felt I needed to prove myself reliable and dependable, so I could see what Jehovah could accomplish through me." Did he find a way to make adjustments? Dale explained: "Yes, we sold our home and most of our possessions, but we used the money wisely." Gary, from North Carolina, has been serving as an elder for 30 years. He and his wife, Maureen, were thrilled when they received an invitation to attend the Warwick school to take up the assignment of "getting acquainted with and training brothers and sisters, both young and old, who come from various lands to Bethel." Gary added: "Serving at Bethel was more enjoyable than attending a class, and I learned so much more about spiritual things." Jason and Jennifer, from Illinois, had a son who worked as a train conductor, and he was happy to join them at Wallkill. He said that being able to support Bethel was "one of the best decisions he ever made." Jennifer stated: "It means so much to know that everything you give to Jehovah is appreciated, and to know that what you give is used to help others learn about Jehovah and His Kingdom. Jehovah always seems to bless you abundantly when you try to be generous."

text:
KŨTAVANY'A ũvoo mũseo nĩw'o wĩa ũla wa vata ũendeee kũtethw'a ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Nũndũ wĩ mũthũkũmi wa Yeova no nginya wĩthĩwe wonaa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a ne kĩanda kya mwanya. Ĩndĩ nĩwĩsĩ nesa ki kana mavainia na atavany'a nĩmakwatawa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtuma maleela ũtavany'anĩ.
Atavany'a amwe nĩmaĩawa nĩ mũndũ matonya kũtavya ũvoo ĩla meũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ andũ aingĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa mate mũsyĩ. Na ĩla meethĩa amwe mũsyĩ na maneena namo, nĩmatonya kũlea kwendeew'a nĩ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ kana o makalea kũmathokya. Namo atavany'a angĩ nĩmatonya kwĩw'a maiemeewa nĩ kũmina kũtavany'a kĩsio kyoo nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩ kĩnene na andũ nĩmethukĩĩasya. Na ĩndĩ angĩ nĩmakw'ĩte ngoo nũndũ matavanĩtye ĩvinda ĩasa, na mayambĩĩa meesĩ mũthya wĩ vakuvĩ.
Yo nĩtwaĩlĩte kũseng'a nũndũ andũ onthe ma Yeova nĩmakwatawa nĩ mawetu matonya kũtuma maleela ũtavany'anĩ? Aiee. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ vai ũmwe witũ ũtonya kũsũanĩa aĩ nĩtũtonya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo tũteũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna twĩ nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ "ũla mũthũku," Satani, kana kwa ĩsyĩtwa yĩngĩ, Ndevili.—1 Yoa. 5:19.
O na ethĩwa ũkwatawa nĩ mawetu meva ĩla ũũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, ĩthĩwa wĩsĩ kana Yeova nũtonya kũũtethya ũmakĩlye vinya. Ĩndĩ ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana wongele kĩthito kyaku ũtavany'anĩ? Eka tũsũanĩe maũndũ amwe matonya kũũtethya.
TETHEESYA ALA MATE NA ŨMANYI MWINGĨ
Kĩla mwaka andũ ngili mbingĩ nĩmavatisawa makatw'ĩka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ethĩwa ũnavatisiwe o mĩtũkĩ, no wende mũno kũtetheew'a nĩ ala me na ũmanyi mwingĩ wa kũtavany'a nũndũ methĩĩtwe me atavany'a kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mbee waku. Naku ethĩwa wĩthĩĩtwe wĩ mũtavany'a wa Ũsumbĩ kwa myaka mingĩ, tyo nginya wĩthĩwe wĩw'aa mũyo kũtetheesya ala mate na ũmanyi mwingĩ?
Yesũ nĩweesĩ yaĩ no nginya amanyĩw'a make matongoew'e nĩ kana methĩwe me atavany'a aseo, na nĩwoonanisye ũndũ wĩa ũsu waĩlĩte kũtethw'a. (Luka 8:1) O na ũmũnthĩ kwĩ na vata wa kũmanyĩsya angĩ methĩwe atavany'a aseo.
Tũyaĩle kũsũanĩa mũtavany'a mweũ akamanyĩa kũmanyĩsya ala angĩ atĩ nũndũ nũendaa ũtavany'a. Aĩlĩte kũmanyĩw'a nesa nĩ mũndũ wĩ na tei na wendo. Mũtavany'a mweũ aĩlĩte kũmanyĩw'a maũndũ ta ũndũ ũtonya (1) kwĩyũmbanĩsya kĩla ũkũthi kũweta athi kũtavany'a, (2) kwambĩĩa kũneena na mwene nyũmba kana na mũndũ ũvĩtĩte, (3) kũnengane mavuku, (4) kũsyokea ala mendeew'a, na (5) kwambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ. Nĩvatonyeka mũno mũtavany'a ũsu mweũ akethĩwa e mũtavany'a mũseo ethĩwa akasisya na aiatĩĩa nzĩa sya kũtavany'a ila ũkwonw'a nĩ ũla ũkũmũtetheesya. (Luka 6:40) Vate nzika mũtavany'a ũsu mweũ ndalea kwĩw'a mũyo nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na mũndũ ũtonya kũmwĩthukĩĩsya na kũmũtetheesya ĩla ve na vata. O na ĩngĩ, mũtavany'a ũsu ũte na ũmanyi mwingĩ no atetheke mũno nũndũ wa kũkathwa na kũnengwa motao.—Mũta. 4:9, 10.
MŨIKAKILANĨLYE ĨLA MWĨ ŨTAVANY'ANĨ
O na kau no ũtate mũno kũea ngewa na ene nyũmba, mĩthenya ĩmwe ngewa sya kwaka ila wĩsaa kwĩthĩa ũneenie ĩla ũũtavany'a, wĩthĩaa ũneenie na ũla ũũtavany'a nake. Lilikana kana Yesũ atũmie amanyĩw'a make makatavany'e "elĩ na elĩ." (Luka 10:1) Maitavany'a vamwe maĩ matonya kwĩkĩana vinya. Kwoou, ĩla andũ meũtavany'a ĩmwe nĩmakwataa mwanya wa 'kũthangaany'a.'—Alo. 1:12, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
Nĩ maũndũ ta meva mũtonya kũneenea? Ve ũmwe wenyu ũtonya kũelesya ũndũ ũneekĩkie wa kwaka? Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũnoonie kaũndũ ka kwendeesya ũyĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia wĩ weka kana wĩ na andũ ala angĩ ma mũsyĩ? Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũnaakiwe nĩ kaũndũ ũneewie ũmbanonĩ? Mavinda angĩ nũtonya kwĩthĩa mũndũ ũla ũũtavany'a nake ti we ũtavanasya nake kĩla ĩvinda. Kwoou ĩkũlyo nĩ: Nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ wamanyie ũla w'o? Nĩ kyaũ kyamũĩkĩĩthisye kana ũũ nĩw'o ũseũvyo wa Yeova? Akwatĩte ianda syĩva na nĩ maũndũ meva wĩyoneete? O naku no ũmũelesye maũndũ ala wĩyoneete. O na kau andũ nĩmatonya kwendeew'a kana makalea kwendeew'a nĩ ũla w'o, kũtavany'a na mũndũ ũngĩ nĩkũtetheeasya 'kĩla ũmwe kwaka ũla ũngĩ.'—1 Ath. 5:11.
NDŨKAEKE KWĨMANYĨSYA NESA O ŨNDŨ WĨKAA
Ũndũ ũmwe ũtonya kũtũtetheesya tũikaleele ũtavany'anĩ nĩ kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya nesa. "Ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" nĩyandĩkaa maũvoo maneeneete maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o. (Mt. 24:45) Kwoou maũndũ ala ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya nĩ kana wĩyĩĩthye kĩ-veva nĩ maingĩ mũno. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ mũseo ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya: Nĩkĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ nĩ kwa vata mũno? Ĩsandũkũ yĩla yĩ na kyongo, "Nĩkĩ Tũtaĩle Kũleela Ũtavany'anĩ?" nĩyĩwetete itumi imwe.
Kũsũanĩa itumi ila iwetetwe ĩsandũkũnĩ yĩu nĩkũtonya kũtuma ũendeea kũtavany'a na kĩthito. No ũtũmĩe ĩvinda yĩla wĩmanyĩasya kũmantha itumi ingĩ eka isu. Ĩtina wa vau no ũsũanĩe itumi isu vamwe na maandĩko ala maikwete mbau. Kwĩka ũu kũkaũtetheesya wongele kĩthito kyaku ũtavany'anĩ.
ATĨĨA NZĨA SYA KŨTAVANY'A ILA TWONAW'A
Mavinda kwa mavinda ũseũvyo wa Yeova nũtũnengae motao ma kũtũtetheesya kwaĩlangya ũtavany'a witũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, eka kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, no tũtavany'e tũitũmĩa valũa, simũ, o na no tũtavany'e malelũnĩ kana kũndũ kũla kwĩthĩawa na andũ aingĩ. O na ĩngĩ no tũtavany'e ũvoo mũseo ĩla twĩ maũndũnĩ maitũ na isionĩ sya viasala. Ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kwĩvanga nesa nĩ kana tũthi tũkatavany'e isio ila itatavanaw'a mũno.
We nĩwĩtĩkĩlanaa na maũndũ ala tweewa nĩtwĩke makonetye ũtavany'a? Nũtatĩte kũtũmĩa maũndũ amwe ta asu ĩla ũũtavany'a? Andũ amwe nĩmekĩte ũu na makatanĩa mũno. Sũanĩa ngelekany'o ii itatũ.
Ngelekany'o ya mbee ĩkonetye ũndũ wawetetwe nthĩnĩ wa Ũthũkũmi wa Ũsumbĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ tũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na andũ. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwathangaaisye mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa April akũlya andũ atatũ ala ũthũkũmaa namo kana nĩmekwenda kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Nĩwaseng'ie na atana mũno ĩla onthe me atatũ meetĩkĩlile kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na mambĩĩa kũthi maũmbanonĩ.
Ngelekany'o ya kelĩ ĩkonetye kũnengane makaseti. Nĩtweekĩiwe vinya tũmanthae andũ ala matonya kwendeew'a nĩ maũvoo mana makasetinĩ maitũ. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũmwe wa mũthyũlũlũko nthĩ ya Amelika aisye kana nĩwatũmĩie ũvoo ũla waneeneete taili. Aũtũmĩie kũnenga anene ma viasala sya kũthoosya taili ĩkaseti ya Amkeni! kĩsionĩ kĩna. O na ĩngĩ, we na mũka nĩmatwaie makaseti ala maĩ na ũvoo wĩ na kyongo "Kuwaelewa Madaktari" movisinĩ mbee wa 100 ma matakĩtalĩ ala maĩ mũthyũlũlũkonĩ woo. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwĩka ũu kwatũtethisye mũno tũmanyĩke na tũinengane mavuku maitũ. Ĩla twamanyĩanĩie na andũ ala twamanengae makaseti, nĩtwambĩĩe kũmathokea mũnango."
Nayo ngelekany'o ya katatũ ĩkonetye kũtavany'a na simũ. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Judy nĩwaandĩkĩie ovisi mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova atũngĩte mũvea nũndũ wa motao ala tũnengawe maitũthangaasya tũtavany'e tũitũmĩa simũ. Aisye kana inyia wake, ũla wĩ na myaka 86 na ũla wĩ mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ, nĩwatavanasya mavinda maingĩ aitũmĩa simũ na nĩwatanĩaa mũno kũmanyĩsya mũndũ mũka wĩ na myaka 92 Mbivilia!
Motao ma kũtavany'a ala me mavukunĩ maitũ nĩmatethasya mũno. Matũmĩe! Nĩmatonya kũũtetheesya ũendeee kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũtanu na ndũkaleele ũtavany'anĩ.
VANGĨĨA MAŨNDŨ ALA ŨTONYA KWĨANĨSYA
Mũndũ ndatw'ĩkaa aendeee nesa ũtavany'anĩ aĩ nũndũ nũnenganae mavuku maingĩ, e na amanyĩw'a aingĩ ma Mbivilia, kana nũtetheesye aingĩ makatw'ĩka athũkũmi ma Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, Noa aatetheesya mũndũ o na ũmwe atw'ĩke mũthũkũmi wa Yeova eka andũ make? Ĩndĩ tũyasya kana ndaĩ mũtavany'a mũseo. Kĩla kya vata nĩ kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ aĩkĩĩku.—1 Ako. 4:2.
Atavany'a aingĩ ma Ũsumbĩ nĩmamanyĩte kana no nginya mavangĩĩe kwĩanĩsya maũndũ ala matonya nĩ kana matanĩe wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Maũndũ ta meva? Amwe mamo nĩmawetetwe ĩsandũkũnĩ yĩla yĩ na kyongo "Vangĩĩa Maũndũ Ala Ũtonya Kwĩanĩsya."
Voya Yeova akũtetheesye na ũimantha nzĩa sya kũtanĩa na kwaĩlangya ũthũkũmi waku nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na mosyao. Weanĩsya maũndũ ala ũvangĩĩe, ũkatana na ũkeew'a wĩ mwĩanĩe nũndũ wa kũmanya kana nĩwĩkaa kĩla kyonthe ũtonya ũtavany'e ũvoo mũseo.
Vate nzika kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo kwĩ o mawetu makw'o. Ĩndĩ ve maũndũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana wĩthĩwe mũtavany'a wa Ũsumbĩ wĩ kĩthito. Maũndũ amwe nĩ ta, kwakana na ũla ũũtavany'a nake, kwĩmanyĩsya nesa, kũatĩĩa motao ma ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ, na kũvangĩĩa kwĩanĩsya maũndũ ala ũtonya. Na eka ũu, lilikana kana Ngai nũkũnengete kĩanda kya mwanya mũno kya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ syake. (Isa. 43:10) Ũkakwata ũtanu mwingĩ mũno waendeea kũtavany'a ũteũleela!

translation:
To help people improve their lives, we need to continue teaching them God's Word. The faithful and discreet slave is continuing to provide us with spiritual food through publications and meetings. Indeed, we are living in difficult times, and those who try to help others spiritually often face opposition and persecution.
Some opposers are motivated by personal interests to discourage us from house-to-house ministry. Why? Because many people are easily influenced. And some religious leaders and influential people may feel threatened by the preaching work and may try to stop it. Also, some opposers may be affected by false accusations and slander, causing people to distrust us. But many remain loyal despite such trials, and they courageously defend the truth.
So why should we not be discouraged when people oppose our efforts to share the good news? Well, remember that Satan, "the god of this system of things," tries to blind people so that they will not accept the light of the truth.—1 John 5:19.
But if we allow ourselves to be influenced by the world's thinking, how can we expect Jehovah to bless our efforts to preach? Can we even maintain our own zeal for the ministry? Let us examine some ways to strengthen our resolve.
SHOW REAL ZEAL AND INITIATIVE
Each year, many people look forward to attending conventions of Jehovah's Witnesses. If you have been invited to attend a convention, make full use of the opportunity to receive encouragement and practical instruction on how to improve your witnessing skills. And if you have been a publisher for many years, do you still find it beneficial to show real zeal and initiative?
Jesus knew that his disciples would face opposition, and he helped them to prepare for it. (Luke 8:1) Also, each one of us can cultivate the quality of self-initiative.
Let us examine what self-initiative involves—namely, taking the lead in doing things rather than waiting to be told. Self-initiative is demonstrated by a person who is proactive and shows love. A self-initiator does not wait for instructions on what to do (1) to respond quickly when seeing a need, (2) to speak to homeowners or people who are interested, (3) to offer assistance, (4) to visit those who are sick, and (5) to share Bible knowledge with others. Such a self-initiator will surely succeed in his work, unlike someone who needs constant supervision.—Luke 6:40. Those who take the initiative often find themselves in a position where they can help others and encourage them. And furthermore, such a self-initiator has much insight and is able to accomplish more because he is not constantly being directed and corrected.—Prov. 4:9, 10.
SELF-RELIANCE AND INITIATIVE
And even if you do not have a specific assignment, you may see a need around the house or in the congregation. In such cases, do not hesitate to take the initiative; instead, use your discernment. Discernment helps you determine what kind of initiative to take. Jesus used the expression "each and everything" to emphasize this point.—Luke 10:1. Some self-initiators may encounter difficulties. However, many people appreciate those who show initiative and avoid the feeling of being 'pushed'.—Acts 1:12, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
What can help you to be more proactive? Does one of you find it difficult to identify a need in the congregation? Are you hesitant to offer to read the Bible aloud or to join others in their ministry? Are you afraid of making a mistake? Many times, the reason why someone does not take the initiative is because he does not feel qualified. But remember this: Do you know your abilities? What qualities does Jehovah give you to help you succeed? Strengthen your confidence and look for ways to apply what you learn. And if others are slow to respond or seem uninterested, do not let that discourage you from continuing to encourage 'each one individually'.—1 Thess. 5:11.
LET US CONTINUE TO SHOW INITIATIVE AND DO WHAT WE CAN
One thing that can help us to remain zealous is to show initiative. The illustration of the "slave and the steward" highlights how important it is to be proactive. (Matt. 24:45) There are also other things we can do to show initiative: Have you considered whether you could do more in your personal study? Consider this question: Is my conscience clear when I think about the time I spend in spiritual activities? The brochure *Are You Ready to Meet Jehovah?*, with its thought-provoking questions, can be a helpful tool.
Consider using that tool to motivate yourself to be more proactive. Do not hesitate to use the time you have available to prepare thoroughly. Also, make good use of the publications that contain practical suggestions. By doing so, you will strengthen your confidence and continue to be proactive.
SHOW INITIATIVE EVEN WHEN FACED WITH OBSTACLES
From house to house, our brothers and sisters often encounter obstacles to showing initiative. For example, people may not be home, or they may be busy, or they may not be interested in discussing spiritual matters. And sometimes we face unexpected difficulties or problems. But we can still show initiative by making full use of the opportunities we have to share the good news. We can strive to overcome obstacles and continue to preach whenever possible.
How can we maintain our zeal and continue to show initiative? What specific steps can we take to improve? Some have found it helpful to set goals for themselves. Let us examine an example.
For instance, a sister scheduled time each week to prepare for Bible studies. She began in April and invited three individuals to study the Bible with her. She prayed to Jehovah for his blessing and was delighted to see that all three accepted her offer to study the Bible regularly. She felt strengthened and encouraged.
Another suggestion is to make arrangements to demonstrate. I recently received a letter from a brother in America who wrote about how he used a demonstration effectively. He sent a cassette recording of the talk "Awake!" to someone who had expressed interest in learning more. Also, my wife and I send cassette recordings featuring the song "Understanding Doctors" to 100 doctors in our territory. One doctor wrote: "This has helped us greatly to understand our patients better. By associating with those who listen to the cassettes, we can reach their hearts."
Also, another suggestion is to practice using the ministry regularly. A sister named Judy wrote a fine article in The Watchtower encouraging us to include demonstrations in our ministry and to use them often. She mentioned her mother, who is 86 years old and has poor eyesight, still demonstrates frequently and enjoys helping a 92-year-old man read the Bible!
Regular practice makes perfect. Try it! You will find it easier to give a demonstration each time you practice.
OTHER THINGS YOU CAN DO TO IMPROVE
A person may continue to improve his ability to give demonstrations by studying the Bible more and becoming familiar with many scriptures, or by practicing giving talks to fellow publishers. For example, did Noah practice speaking to just one person before giving his testimony to his family? It is good to rehearse what you plan to say so you will be able to express yourself clearly.—1 Cor. 4:2.
Many experienced ministers realize that they need to keep rehearsing demonstrations even though they have given them many times. Why is this? Some reasons are that people are different, and we want to be able to adapt our demonstrations to their needs.
May Jehovah help you to remain zealous in the work of preaching and teaching and strengthen you spiritually. Review the points you wish to cover, prepare thoroughly, and then trust that Jehovah will enable you to speak effectively and touch hearts.
Don't hesitate to practice this skill with others. It is also helpful to ask elders for suggestions on how to improve your demonstrations. Some things to work on are speaking clearly, being enthusiastic, choosing appropriate scriptures, and preparing well. And remember that God can bless your efforts to improve your ability to give effective demonstrations. (Isa. 43:10) You will then enjoy your ministry much more!

Nĩnaĩwe nĩ mũndũ kĩkundinĩ, na ndikwenda nĩse kũkũa nĩ weka."
"Aũme amwe mate Ngũsĩ me tei, nĩ andũ ũtonya kũmenda, na nĩmethukĩĩasya mũndũ. Maileaa ndĩni yakwa, na monekaa me aseo kũte ana-a-asa amwe."
Athũkũmi amwe ma Ngai mendaa kũtwawa kana kũtwaana nĩmawetete ndeto ta isu. Ĩndĩ ti atĩ mayĩsĩ ũla ũtao wa Vaulo waĩle kũatĩĩwa nĩ Aklĩsto onthe. Ũtao ũsu waĩtye Aklĩsto maĩle kũtwaana o "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi." (1 Ako. 7:39) Na yu nĩkĩ methwa mawetaa ndeto ta isu?
NĨKĨ AMWE METHĨAWA NA NZIKA?
Ala maneenaa ũu no kwĩthĩwa monaa ana-a-asa ala meanĩe kũtwaana me avũthũ kwĩ eĩtu-a-asa ala mate atwae. Na nengĩ kũilyĩ ũu nthĩ mbingĩ. Kwasũanĩa nthĩ ya Korea. Woosa nguthu ya Ngũsĩ 100 itatwaanĩte na ite ndwae, nũtonya kwĩthĩa 57 nĩ eĩtu-a-asa na 43 nĩ ana-a-asa. O na ĩngĩ sũanĩa nthĩ ya Colombia. Woosa nguthu ya Ngũsĩ 100, nũtonya kwĩthĩa 66 nĩ eĩtu-a-asa na 34 nĩ ana-a-asa.
Na ĩndĩ nthĩ ingĩ, kĩndũ kĩla kyanangaa maũndũ nĩ kana asyai mate Ngũsĩ nĩmatonya kwĩtya malĩ mbingĩ ya ngasya ũkethĩa mwana-a-asa ũte na ũtonyi mwingĩ nũkũemwa. Nũndũ wa maũndũ ta asu, mwĩĩtu-a-asa nĩkwona ta ũtesa kũkwata mũũme "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi." Nũndũ wa ũu no ekũlye-ĩ, "Nĩvatonyeka ngesa kũkwata mwana-a-asa ũmbaĩle?" *
KŨMWĨKWATYA YEOVA NĨ KWA VATA VYŨ
Ethĩwa waaĩkũlya ĩkũlyo ta yĩu yĩ kalungunĩ kau kavĩta, manya kana Yeova nũkũeleawa vyũ. Nĩwĩsĩ nesa ki ũndũ wĩw'aa.
Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, Yeova nũwetete Ndetonĩ yake kana andũ maĩle kũtwawa o nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kĩtonya kũtethya andũ make. Endaa kũmasiĩĩa maikaaĩse kũkwatwa nĩ thĩna ũla umanaa na kwĩka ũtwi mũthũku, na nĩwendaa mekale me atanu. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ĩvinda ya Neemia. Ĩla andũ mambĩĩie kũtwaa aka mate Ayuti na matamũthaithaa Yeova, Neemia nĩwamalilikanilye ũndũ Solomoni weekanisye. Amalilikanilye kana o na kau Solomoni 'nĩwendetwe nĩ Ngai wake, aka ma nthĩ ĩngĩ nĩmatumie avĩtya.' (Nee. 13:23-26) Kwoou ĩla Ngai watũtavya tũikatwawe nĩ andũ angĩ eka o athaithi ma w'o, ethĩawa aitũtethya. (Sav. 19:7-10; Isa. 48:17, 18) Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmatũngaa mũvea nũndũ Ngai nũmendete, na nũndũ wa ũu nĩmekwatasya ũtao wake.
Kwa w'o, ndwenda 'kwovanĩw'a ĩsoki yĩmwe' na mũndũ ũtonya kwĩsa kũũvathany'a na Ngai. (2 Ako. 6:14) Ũtao ũsu nũatĩĩwe kwa ĩvinda ĩasa na ũkoneka no ũtethye. Aklĩsto aingĩ ala maũatĩĩie nĩmesie kũmanya ĩtina kana meekie nesa kũũatĩĩa. Ĩndĩ amwe nĩmaleanĩte naw'o.
NĨ ŨNDŨ ŨTONYEKA
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Maggy * wa nthĩ ya Australia nũeleetye ũndũ kwaendie ĩla watumie ndũũ na mũndũ ũte Ngũsĩ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩnatĩĩie maũmbano maingĩ mũno no kana nĩthĩwe nĩ nake. Ngwatanĩo yakwa na Ngai yaanangĩkie ndatĩka." Nake ũngĩ wĩtawa Ratana kuma India nĩwambĩĩe kwenda mwanake masomaa ĩmwe na waĩ anambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Nake mwanake ũsu emanyĩasya Mbivilia no ũndũ nĩwamwendaa Ratana. Ũndũ ũsu watumie Ratana esa kũtia ũla w'o, na alika ndĩni ĩngĩ nĩ kana atwawe.
Ngelekany'o ĩngĩ nĩ ya Ndenguè kuma Cameroon. Atwaiwe e na myaka 19. Ũla wamwĩvaasya amwathĩte kana matwaana ndakamũvata kũthaitha o kũla watwĩe athaithaa. Ĩndĩ makililye mamina syumwa ilĩ, mũũme amũvata kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto. Ndenguè easya: "Natindaa nĩmakĩe na nĩĩte. Nĩvo namanyie kana ti ĩla nekaa kĩla ngwenda. Natindĩaa kwĩlila."
Kũneena ũla w'o, ti aũme onthe mate Ngũsĩ methĩawa me athũku na me ngoo mbetu. Ĩndĩ o na wĩthĩwe ndũkakwatwa nĩ thĩna ta ũsu ũkwataa ala matwawa nĩ andũ mate Ngũsĩ, nata ĩũlũ wa ngwatanĩo yaku vamwe na Ĩthe waku wa ĩtunĩ wĩ wendo? We wĩona ta ũkekalaa ũyĩw'a ata nũndũ wa kũlea kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla waũnengete nĩ kana ũkũtethye? Na ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo yĩla ya vata nĩ, Ũkew'aa ata ĩũlũ wa ũtwi waku?
Ve ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ala matonya kũkũsĩĩa kana nzĩa ĩla nzeo ya kũtwaana "no nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi." Ala mate atwae nĩmethĩawa matw'ĩte kũmantha mũndũ ũmaĩle katĩ wa athaithi ma Ngai nĩ kana matanĩthye ngoo yake. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Michiko ũla wĩkalaa Japan. Ĩla ũtaĩ mũtwae ve ĩvinda andũ ma mũsyĩ matatie kũmũthing'ĩĩsya atwawe nĩ mũndũ ũte Ngũsĩ. Na ĩndĩ eka kũmĩĩsya thĩna ũsu, nĩwoonaa anyanyae vamwe na angĩ mesene maikwata mũndũ ũmaĩle kĩkundinĩ. Easya: "Ngoo yakwa nĩyandĩkĩĩthasya kana nũndũ Yeova nĩ 'Ngai mũtanu,' mũndũ no ekale e mũtanu, ethĩwe nĩ mũtwae kana ti mũtwae. O na ĩngĩ nĩnĩsĩ kana ndaleaa kũtwĩanĩsya wendi ũla wĩ ngoonĩ. Kwoou ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda kũtwawa na nĩtwaaĩwe nĩ mũndũ, nũseo tũkamba kwĩkalanga nginya ĩla twĩkwata mũndũ." (1 Tim. 1:
Ve o ana-a-asa amwe o namo mekalile mayĩsa kũkwata mũndũ ũmaĩle. Ũmwe wa asu nĩ Bill kuma Australia. Nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa kana ve mavinda wendeeaw'a nĩ aka mate Ngũsĩ. Ĩndĩ we mwene nĩwatataa kyonthe kĩla ũtonya ndakese kũtuma ndũũ ngamu namo. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ we mwene ndendaa kwĩka ũndũ ũtuma esa 'kwovanĩw'a ĩsoki yĩmwe' na mũndũ ũte mwĩtĩkĩli. Myakanĩ ĩsu ũtatwaanĩte no wendeeaw'a nĩ eĩtu-a-asa amwe, ĩndĩ vai ũmwe katĩ wa asu wamwendaa. Bill ekalile myaka 30 ayĩsa kũkwata mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwaĩle. Ĩndĩ easya: "Ndyĩlilaa." Awetete atĩĩ: "Nĩw'aa naathimiwe nũndũ tũendaa ũtavany'a ĩmwe, tũkemanyĩsya ĩmwe, na tũkathaitha ĩmwe. Na nũndũ anyanyae onthe ma kĩveti kyakwa nĩ athaithi ma Yeova, nĩnĩtanaa mũno kũmamanya na kũtindany'a namo. Tũlũlũmĩlasya mũtwaano witũ tũitũmĩa myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ."
ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA KAVINDANĨ KALA ŨMWETEELE YEOVA?
Ũtonya kwĩka ata kavindanĩ kala ũmweteele Yeova? Kĩndũ kya mbee nĩ kwĩkũlya nĩkĩ ũtaatwawa. Weethĩa kĩtumi kĩla kĩnene kĩkonetye ũla ũtao wa Mbivilia ĩũlũ wa kũtwawa o "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi," mwa waĩle kũkathwa mũno nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa ũtao ũsu Ngai ũkũnete. Ndũkethwe na nzika kana Yeova nĩwĩw'aa mũyo ĩla woona ũtw'ĩte vyũ kũatĩĩa Ndeto yake. (1 Sam. 15:22; Nth. 27:11) Endeea 'kũmũtulũĩla ngoo yaku.' (Sav. 62:8) Wamũvoyaa na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo na ũteũtĩĩa, ũkesa kwĩthĩa ũimũelesya nesa ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Na waendeea kwĩka ũndũ ũtonya ũsinde matatwa na ũikĩlya vinya mĩmeo mĩthũku, ngwatanĩo yaku na Ngai ĩkaendeeaa kwĩthĩwa yĩ nzeo. Ĩkalaa wĩsĩ kana Ũla wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe nũthĩnĩkĩaa athũkũmi make ala aĩkĩĩku na nũmonaa me ma vata. Nĩwĩsĩ mavata maku na kĩla wendaa. Ndaĩtye kana nĩ lasima ekũetee mũndũ. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa kuma ngoonĩ nũkwenda kũtwawa, Ngai nĩwĩsĩ nzĩa ĩla nzeo ya kwĩanĩsya mawendi maku ala maĩle.
Mavinda amwe no wĩw'e ta Ndaviti ĩla waisye: "Ĩkalaate kũnzũngĩa, ame Yeova; veva wakwa nũũthelekela: Ndũkambithe ũthyũ waku." (Sav. 143:5-7, 10) Ĩla weew'a ũu, nengae Ĩthe waku wa ĩtunĩ ĩvinda akwony'e kĩla wendaa wĩke. Nzĩa ĩmwe ya kwonany'a nũmũnengete ĩvinda nĩ kũsoma Ndeto yake na kũvindĩĩsya kĩla ũũsoma. Weeka ũu ũkamanya mĩao yake, na ũkoona ũndũ tene watethisye andũ make. O na ĩngĩ kwĩka maũndũ asu kũkatuma wĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmangu kana kũmwĩw'a nĩw'o ũndũ ũla wa ũĩ.
Nĩ kyaũ kĩngĩ kĩtonya kũtuma yu ũte mũtwae (kana ũtatwaanĩte) wĩkala ũte kwĩmakĩa na ũte kwĩw'a ũtulu? No ũtũmĩe ĩvinda yĩĩ kwĩka maendeeo nĩ kana wĩthĩwe wĩ mũndũ wĩ ũmanyi, mũlau, mũseo, mũthangaau, ũnengetwe ndaĩa, na wĩ kĩthito kya kũmũthũkũma Ngai. Asu onthe nĩ maũndũ matetheeasya andũ matwaanĩte mekalany'e nesa. (Mwa. 24:16-21; Lu. 1:16, 17; 2:6, 7, 11; Nth. 31:10-27) Mantha Ũsumbĩ mbee kwa kwĩyumya vyũ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a na mawĩanĩ angĩ ma Kĩklĩsto. Weeka ũu ũkatetheka mũno. Bill nũwetete ĩũlũ wa myaka ĩla waaĩwe nĩ mũndũ wa kũtwaa. Aĩtye: "Yavĩtie mĩtũkĩ vyũ! Namĩtũmĩie kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩ vainia."
Nĩ w'o, matukũ aa kũtwaana o "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi" nĩkũtonyeka. Waatĩĩa ũtao ũsu ũkatuma Yeova ataĩwa, naku ũkekalaa wĩ mwĩanĩe. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩmũathime mũndũ ũla ũmũkĩaa Yeova, ũla ũtanĩaa mũno mĩao yake. Ũthwii na syĩndũ syĩ nyũmbanĩ yake; na ũlũngalu wake nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene." (Sav. 112:1, 3) Nũndũ wa ũu, tw'a na ngoo ĩmwe kũatĩĩa mwĩao ũla Ngai ũtũnengete wa kũmantha mũndũ o "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi."
