I have always been a loving person, and I want to become like you."
"Some people hate God because they are afraid to approach Him, and I have disappointed someone. Please forgive me, and let me cleanse myself completely."
Sometimes people fear being saved or being rescued from difficult situations. It is possible that some did not understand Paul's teachings about Christ properly. This teaching helped Christ rescue people from "the power of darkness." (1 Cor. 7:39) And how can we show that we appreciate this rescue?
HOW CAN WE SHOW APPRECIATION AND GRATITUDE?
Well, many people show their appreciation by helping others, and many people help those who are suffering. But I will explain this more clearly. Consider the example of Korea. During the Korean War, 100 out of every 100 people were either killed or wounded, with 57 being men and 43 being women. And also consider the example of Colombia. Out of every 100 people, 66 were killed and 34 were wounded.
And in many other cases, things happen so that people might think that God hates them because they suffer greatly when a young woman dies while giving birth. Because of such things, many men feel reluctant to embrace "the power of darkness." Because of this reluctance, they ask themselves, "Is it really worth embracing a young woman?" *
TO DRAW CLOSE TO JEHOVAH REQUIRES EFFORT
Imagine trying to learn a language that you find very difficult, knowing that Jehovah understands your effort. It takes time and practice.
In view of this, Jehovah patiently bears with his people when they stumble as they try to apply "the power of darkness." Why? Because he knows that each person has weaknesses. To help us remember this, spend some time thinking about how Solomon felt when he was threatened and how he prayed earnestly. For example, read the account of Nehemiah. Although many Jews had intermarried with people from Egypt and had disregarded Jehovah, Nehemiah firmly upheld what Solomon had decreed. He reminded them that Solomon had said, "May God judge between you and me!" (Neh. 13:23-26) Remember that God allows us to be tested by others so that we may prove our loyalty, and those who teach us can benefit. (Ps. 19:7-10; Isa. 48:17, 18) The Christians of that time were able to see how God answered their prayers, and they learned to trust him more fully.
Therefore, I encourage you to 'become united to someone' who is spiritually strong and who can help you to strengthen your relationship with God. (2 Cor. 6:14) This will be possible if you take the initiative and ask for assistance. Many Christians have found it helpful to study with a mature friend and to seek his advice. Some of us have done so.
A REAL CHALLENGE
A sister named Maggie,* from Australia, shared an experience that illustrates this point. She wrote: "I used to feel very inadequate because of my past. My relationship with Jehovah seemed distant." Her son, Ratana, from India, encouraged her to attend meetings with him and offered to help her study the Bible. As her son helped her to understand the Bible, she began to appreciate Ratana. This helped Ratana to stay loyal, and he continued to support her, even though there were obstacles.
Another example is that of Ndenguè from Cameroon. He was baptized when he was 19 years old. After his baptism, he felt insecure and wondered whether he would remain faithful. Because of his feelings, he sought the help of a mature Christian. Ndenguè explains: "I confessed my fears and weaknesses. That is how I learned that it is okay to admit our imperfections. I also learned to pray."
Considering these experiences, do you feel that you could benefit from associating with mature brothers and sisters? Perhaps you struggle with a particular weakness or temptation. Would a close friendship with such ones help you to maintain your loyalty to Jehovah and to continue progressing spiritually? And what if you feel unable to confide in anyone, are you willing to try praying about it?
Very often, young people find it difficult to resist peer pressure to engage in activities that are harmful or that displease God, which they call "fun." Some young people who have succumbed to such pressure have later regretted their foolish decisions and have deeply hurt their parents. For instance, there is the case of Michiko, a young man from Japan. He began experimenting with drugs because his friends pressured him into doing so. Later, he realized that he had made a mistake and desperately wanted to stop. But he found himself trapped, addicted to drugs and owing money to dangerous people. He explains: "My life became unbearable, and I kept thinking that if only Jehovah were truly 'the Almighty God,' someone who has unlimited power, then perhaps he could deliver me. But I continued taking drugs, hoping that somehow things would get better." (1 Tim. 1:
Some young people also struggle with pornography. One of them, Bill, from Australia, admits: "I felt that looking at pornography was something I could do without anyone finding out." However, he soon discovered that this secret sin caused him great distress. Why? Because he felt alienated from Jehovah and unable to enjoy a close relationship with Him. He says: "I realized that I had lied to myself. I thought I could continue living a double life—doing what I wanted to do while pretending to be a Christian—but I was wrong. It is impossible to serve two masters."
WHY IS IT SO DIFFICULT TO RESIST PEER PRESSURE?
Why is it so difficult to resist peer pressure? One reason is that we naturally want to belong. The Bible shows that Satan the Devil uses this desire to influence us to disregard God's standards. (Prov. 1:10-15) He appeals to our selfish desires, making wrongdoing seem appealing. (Gal. 5:19, 20) But remember that Jehovah sees through our pretense and knows our true motives. (1 Sam. 16:7) So, confide in Him about your struggles. (Ps. 62:8) Be honest with yourself and others, and seek help when needed. And remember that strengthening your relationship with God will give you the courage to stand up for what is right. The Bible assures us that "God is able to make you stand firm" despite temptation. (1 Cor. 10:13)
Don't underestimate the power of prayer! God cares about your feelings and wants to help you. He promises to give holy spirit to those who ask Him.—Luke 11:13.
David often expressed his feelings to Jehovah, saying: "Examine me, O Jehovah, and prove me; try my kidneys and my heart." (Ps. 139:23, 24) Similarly, pour out your heart to God in prayer, telling Him everything that troubles you. By regularly studying God's Word and meditating on what you read, you come to know His thoughts and ways. This will strengthen your resolve to please Him and to reject anything that would displease Him.
What can help you remain steadfast (or regain your stability) when facing difficulties? Consider how others have dealt with similar situations—people who were loyal, courageous, honest, kind, modest, and appreciative. Also, remember the example of those who showed faith in God. Often, their experiences can be very encouraging and helpful. (Prov. 24:16-21; Luke 1:16, 17; 2:6, 7, 11; Acts 31:10-27) May this information help you to cope with trials and to maintain your spiritual strength. Remember the advice given by an elderly Christian man. He said: "I thank you for all the good things! I want to continue praising Jehovah with zeal."
So, times when we feel discouraged are often temporary. By taking steps now, you can make Jehovah proud and remain close to him. The Bible assures us: "Happy is the man who fears Jehovah, who greatly delights in his commandments. His offspring will be mighty in the land; the upright will be rewarded." (Psalm 112:1, 3) Therefore, let us strive to live in such a way that we earn the title of "friend of God."

text:
MŨTŨMWA Vaulo nĩwaveveewe aandĩka nguma kenda ila tũtonya kwĩthĩwa nasyo tũtetheew'e nĩ veva mũtheu. (Aka. 5:22, 23) Nguma isu syĩ vamwe nĩsyo syĩtawa "ũsyao wa Veva." * Ũsyao ũsu nĩ ũmwe mũndũ wĩthĩawa naw'o eevw'ĩka ũla "mũndũ mweũ." (Ako. 3:10) Mũndũ eetĩkĩlya veva mũtheu ũthũkũme nesa nthĩnĩ wake, nĩwĩthĩawa na ũsyao wa veva o tondũ mũtĩ wasũvĩwa nesa umasya ũsyao.—Sav. 1:1-3.
Wendo nĩw'o kĩlungu kya mbee katĩ wa ila ilungu kenda sya ũsyao wa veva Vaulo wawetie. Yo nguma ĩsu nĩ ya vata mũno ata? Vaulo aisye kana ate na wendo we "ti kĩndũ." (1 Ako. 13:2) Ĩndĩ mũndũ wĩ wendo ethĩawa ailyĩ ata, na tũtonya kwĩka ata twĩthĩwe na nguma ĩsu kĩla mũthenya?
ŨNDŨ MŨNDŨ WONANASYA NĨWENDETE ALA ANGĨ
O na kau ti laisi kũelesya nesa wendo nĩ kyaũ, Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye ũndũ mũndũ wonanasya nĩwendete ala angĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwetete kana mũndũ wendete angĩ "nĩwũmĩĩasya, na nĩwĩkaa moseo." O na yaĩtye nĩ ũla "ũtanaa vamwe na ũla w'o" na "nũvw'ĩkaa maũndũ onthe, nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa maũndũ onthe, nĩwĩkwatasya maũndũ onthe, nĩwũmĩĩasya maũndũ onthe." O na ĩngĩ mũndũ wendete angĩ ew'aa e vata namo vyũ kuma ngoonĩ na nũmathĩnĩkĩaa, na ethĩawa alũmanĩtye namo vyũ. Nake mũndũ ũte nguma ĩsu nĩ mũndũ wĩyendete, wĩ kĩwĩu, wĩ mĩtũlyo, wĩ mwĩkalĩle ũtaĩle, na woveeaa ũthatu atekũekea. Wendo ũla tũkwenda kwĩthĩwa naw'o wĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na nguma isu nthũku nũndũ w'o "o na ndwĩmanthĩaa syĩndũ," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ndũmanthaa kwĩyĩuna.—1 Ako. 13:4-8.
YEOVA NA YESŨ NĨ NGELEKANY'O NZEO VYŨ
"Ngai nĩ wendo." Wendo nĩw'o nguma ĩla Yeova wĩsĩkĩe nayo vyũ. (1 Yoa. 4:8) Maũndũ onthe ala wĩkaa nĩmonanasya nesa kana we nĩ Ngai wĩ wendo. Ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ weekie oonany'a nĩwendete andũ mũno nĩ kũmũtũma Yesũ oke athĩne na aikw'a kwondũ witũ. Mũtũmwa Yoana aĩtye: "Ũndũnĩ ũũ wendo wa Ngai nĩwonanĩtw'e kwitũ, nũndũ Ngai nĩwamũtũmie Mwana wake kũũ nthĩ, ũla wasyaiwe e ũmwe, nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na thayũ kwondũ wake. Ũũ nĩw'o wendo, ti ithyĩ twamwendie Ngai, ĩndĩ nĩwe watwendie ithyĩ, na atũma Mwana wake ethĩwe nthembo ya wĩw'anĩthyo kwondũ wa naĩ sitũ." (1 Yoa. 4:9, 10) Nũndũ Ngai nũtwendete, nũtũekeaa mavĩtyo maitũ, akatũnenga wĩkwatyo, na akatwatha thayũ ũtathela.
Yesũ nĩwoonanisye ũndũ wendete andũ ĩla weetĩkĩlile kwĩanĩsya kĩla Ngai wendaa. Vaulo aandĩkie: "Nĩvo ĩndĩ [Yesũ] waisye, Sisya, nĩnooka kwĩka kwenda kwaku. . . . Na nũndũ wa kwenda kwake nĩtwavathiwe twĩthĩwe atheu kwondũ wa kũthembwa kwa mwĩĩ wa Yesũ Klĩsto o ĩmwe tũ." (Aevl. 10:9, 10) Vai mũndũ wĩthĩwa na wendo mũnene kũkĩla ũsu. O nake Yesũ aisye: "Vai mũndũ wĩ wendo mwingĩ ũvĩtũkĩte ũũ, wa mũndũ kũwia thayũ wake nthĩ nũndũ wa anyanyae." (Yoa. 15:13) Ĩndĩ andũ me na naĩ taitũ no methĩwe na wendo o ta ũsu wa Yeova na Yesũ? Ĩĩ! Eka twone tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata.
'KŨENDAA NTHĨNĨ WA WENDO'
Vaulo atwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Ĩthĩwai mũkĩelekan'ya na Ngai, ta twana twendetwe; na mũkĩendaa nthĩnĩ wa wendo, o ũndũ Klĩsto nake wamwendie inyw'ĩ, na eeyumya mwene kwondũ witũ." (Aev. 5:1, 2) Nĩ kana 'tũendae nthĩnĩ wa wendo,' kĩla ĩvinda nĩtwaĩle kwonany'a nĩtwendete angĩ. Na twĩkaa ũu kwa meko, ti o ndeto syoka. Yoana aandĩkie ũũ: "Syana syakwa nini, tũikendane na ndeto, kana na ũĩmĩ; ĩndĩ twendane na kwĩka, na twendane w'o." (1 Yoa. 3:18) Kwa ngelekany'o, kũmwenda Ngai na mũtũi nĩkũtũsukumaa tũkatavya angĩ 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ.' (Mt. 24:14; Luka 10:27) O na ĩngĩ kwĩthĩwa twĩ na wũmĩĩsyo, kwĩka angĩ nesa, na kũekea nĩ kwonany'a nĩtũendaa nthĩnĩ wa wendo. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩtũnengete ũtao ũũ: "O tondu Mwĩaĩi wamũekeie, inyw'ĩ nenyu ĩkaai o ta ũu."—Ako. 3:13.
Wendo ũla tũũneenea vaa ti ũla wa kũnany'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũsyai ũnanasya kana kake nũtonya kũkanenga kyonthe kĩla kekwenda aĩ nũndũ nĩkekũĩa. Ĩndĩ mũsyai wendete mwana wake kwa w'o, nũũngamaa na ĩvĩndĩ ya mũongo ĩla ve kĩtumi. O ta ũu, Ngai nĩ wendo, ĩndĩ Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "ũla Mwĩaĩi ũmwendaa nũmũsilĩlaa." (Aevl. 12:6) Ethĩwa nĩtwendete ala angĩ, tũikaemaa kumya ũkany'o ũla waĩle ethĩwa ve vata. (Nth. 3:11, 12) Ĩndĩ nĩtũlilikane kana o naitũ twĩ ene naĩ, na no twĩke maũndũ mekwonany'a tũyendete ala angĩ. Kwoou kĩla ũmwe witũ nĩwaĩlĩte kwĩka maendeeo vala wendo wake wĩthwa ũsulĩte. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya? Eka twone maũndũ atatũ.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨTHĨWA NA WENDO
Mbee vyũ, mũvoye Ngai aũnenge veva mũtheu. Veva ũsu nĩw'o ũtũtetheeasya twĩthĩwe na wendo. Yesũ aisye kana Yeova ndalea "kũmanenga Veva Mũtheu ala mamwĩtasya." (Luka 11:13) Twavoya tũnengwe veva mũtheu na tweekĩa kĩthito 'tũkinyae tũtongoew'e nĩ veva,' tũkeekaa maũndũ mekwonany'a nĩtwendete ala angĩ. (Aka. 5:16) Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa wĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi, no ũvoye ũkwate veva mũtheu ũũtetheesye umasye ũtao wa Maandĩko kwa nzĩa ya wendo. Kana ethĩwa wĩ mũsyai, no ũmũvoye Ngai aũnenge veva mũtheu nĩ kana ũũtetheesye ĩla ũũkany'a syana syaku wĩkae ũu na wendo, ĩndĩ ti ũthilĩkĩte.
Kelĩ, sũanĩa ũndũ Yesũ woonanasya nĩwendete ala angĩ o na ĩla ũkũthĩnw'a. (1 Vet. 2:21, 23) Kũsũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Klĩsto no kũtũtetheesye mũno mũno ĩla twavĩtĩw'a kana tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle. Mavinda ta asu nũseo tũkekũlya, 'Kethĩwa nĩ Yesũ eka ata?' Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Leigh nĩwoonie kũsũanĩa ĩkũlyo yĩu kwamũtethya ndakose ĩtambya atasũanĩĩte nesa. Aĩtye: "Mũthenya ũmwe ve mũthũkũmi twathũkũmaa ĩmwe watũmĩie athũkũmi ala angĩ e-mail ambumanĩtye na akaumany'a wĩa wakwa. Naũmĩie mũno. Ĩndĩ neekũlya, 'Takeka nĩ Yesũ, we ekana na mũndũ ũsu ata?' Ĩla nasũanĩie ũndũ Yesũ ũtonya kwĩka, noonie nĩ kavaa ngaekana na ũndũ ũsu vandũ va kũkĩlya ithokoo. Tũendeangĩe nesie kwĩthĩa kana mũthũkũmi ũsu nĩwathĩnĩtw'e mũno nĩ ũwau na eew'aa aithĩnĩka kĩlĩko mũno. Nasũanĩa maũndũ asu noonie ti ta weesĩ kĩla ũkwĩka aiandĩka e-mail ĩsu. Kũsũanĩa ũndũ Yesũ woonanisye nĩwendete angĩ o na ĩla ũkũthĩnw'a, nĩkwandetheeisye o nakwa neeka oou o na kau mũthũkũmi ũsu nĩwambĩtĩisye." Vate nzika, tweeka ta Yesũ, tũkekalaa twendete andũ ala angĩ.
Katatũ, ĩthĩwa na wendi wa kwĩyumya kuma ngoonĩ ũtetheesye ala angĩ. Wendo ũsu nĩw'o ũvano ũla mũnene wa Aklĩsto ma w'o. (Yoa. 13:34, 35) Nĩkyo kĩtumi Maandĩko matwĩkĩĩte vinya twĩthĩwe na "kĩlilikano" ta kya Yesũ. Ĩla waumie ĩtunĩ eetheeisye "eeyĩkalya e mũthei" kwondũ witũ "o na kũvika kĩkw'ũ." (Avi. 2:5-8) Tweekĩa kĩthito twĩthĩwe na wendo ta ũla Yesũ waĩ naw'o, tũkeethĩawa na mesilya o ta make, na kĩu kĩkatumaa twenda kũtethya ala angĩ vandũ va kwĩyĩuna ithyĩ ene. Ve ũseo ũngĩ wa kwĩthĩwa na wendo?
ŨSEO WA KWENDA ALA ANGĨ
Ve maũndũ maingĩ maseo tũtonya kũtanĩa tweethĩwa na wendo. Kwasũanĩa aa elĩ:
TWĨTHĨAWA TWĨ NGWATANĨO NA ANA-A-ASA ONTHE ĨŨLŨ WA NTHĨ: Nũndũ nĩtwendanĩte, nĩtwĩsĩ o na tũkathi kĩkundinĩ kĩva ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tũthokw'a nesa vyũ. Mwa tũtanaa ta kĩ kwona twendetwe nĩ 'ana-a-ĩthe maitũ ala me kũũ nthĩ'! (1 Vet. 5:9) Nĩ va vangĩ eka katĩ wa andũ ma Ngai wendo ũsu ũtonya kwoneka?
MŨUO: 'Kũmĩanĩsya ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo' nĩkũtumaa tũtana "wovanonĩ wa mũuo." (Aev. 4:2, 3) Nĩtwĩyoneaa mũuo ũsu ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi na maũmbanonĩ manene. Ve mũndũ ũlea kana mũuo ta ũsu wĩ mũo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩno ĩte ngwatanĩo? (Sav. 119:165; Isa. 54:13) Ĩla tweethĩwa na mũuo na andũ ala angĩ, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a ũndũ tũmendete, na kĩu nĩkĩtanĩthasya Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ.—Sav. 133:1-3; Mt. 5:9.
"WENDO NĨWAKAA"
Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Wendo nĩwakaa." (1 Ako. 8:1) Wakaa ata? Vaulo nũeleetye ũndũ wendo wakaa nthĩnĩ wa kĩlungu kya 13 kya valũa wa mbee ũla waandĩkĩe Akolintho. Kĩlungu kĩu kĩtawa nĩ amwe "Savuli ya Wendo." Ũndũ ũmwe nĩ kana mũndũ wĩ wendo amanthaa kũuna ala angĩ. (1 Ako. 10:24; 13:5) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana, mũndũ wĩ wendo nũsũanĩaa ala angĩ, nũmomĩĩasya, na nĩwendete kũmeka nesa. Kwoou ala me wendo ũsu methĩawa na mĩsyĩ yĩ ngwatanĩo na ikundi syĩ ngwatanĩo.—Ako. 3:14.
Ithyonthe nĩtũmwendete Ngai, na wendo ũsu nĩw'o wendo ũla wa vata vyũ. Kũmwenda Ngai nĩkw'o kũkwatanasya andũ ma ithyomo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, maumĩte kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na mbaĩnĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o makatw'ĩka kĩndũ kĩmwe. Andũ asu mamũthũkũmaa Yeova "na ngoo ĩmwe" me atanu. (Nzev. 3:9) Ekai kĩla mũthenya tũtw'e vyũ kũendeea kwĩthĩwa na wendo, ũla nĩ kĩlungu kĩmwe kya ũsyao wa veva kĩ vata mũno.
^ kal. 2 Yĩĩ nĩyo ĩsomo ya mbee nthĩnĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ kĩkwĩthĩwa na masomo kenda. Kĩla ĩsomo yĩkaneeneaa nguma ĩmwe, kana kĩlungu kĩmwe kya ũsyao ũsu wa veva.

translation:
Paul the apostle was imprisoned often, but we continue preaching, and we are encouraged because he showed courage. (Acts 5:22, 23) Some scriptures show that they also called him "God's slave." * This slave is a perfect human who reflects God's personality. (Acts 3:10) A person who shows courage does not fear anyone, and he is considered God's slave, so do not be afraid of people—fear only God.—Prov. 1:1-3.
Love is what makes a person willing to endure much for the name of God's slave Paul mentioned. But do some scriptures say something different? Paul said that love is "all you need." (1 Cor. 13:2) If a person has love, will he always act kindly, and can we always feel encouraged by such scriptures every day?
IMPORTANT THINGS TO REMEMBER ABOUT LOVE
Even though it may seem difficult to show love at times, the Bible teaches us important things about love. For example, it says that a loving person "is kind and considerate." It also says "he does not rejoice over wrongdoing" and "he does not practice fraud, he does not get involved in dishonest dealings, he does not take advantage of others, and he is kind." And another loving person does not become angry or hold grudges, and he remains peaceful. However, a person who lacks these qualities is selfish, boastful, arrogant, and easily provoked, and he becomes very upset when wronged. Love that we want to imitate is like a mirror that helps us examine ourselves and see how we measure up to the standard of "being kind," or perhaps, in other words, being generous.—1 Cor. 13:4-8.
JEHOVAH AND JESUS ARE EXCELLENT EXAMPLES
OF LOVE
"God is love." Love is what Jehovah values most highly. (1 John 4:8) Everything God does shows his love, because he is a loving God. The greatest thing he has done to demonstrate his love for mankind is sending his Son Jesus to die for us. The apostle John wrote: "By this the love of God was manifested in our case, that God sent forth his only begotten Son into the world, so that we might live through him. This is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son to be a propitiation for our sins." (1 John 4:9, 10) Because God loves us, he gives us many blessings, forgives our mistakes, and protects us from danger.
Jesus showed how much God loves people who want to please him. Paul wrote: "For just as [Jesus] died once for all sinners, . . . and by means of his death we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all time." (Heb. 10:9, 10) No one has shown greater love than Jesus did. He said: "No one has greater love than this, that someone give his life for his friends." (John 15:13) So, do we show love to others as much as Jehovah and Jesus love us? Yes! Let us see how we can do so right now.
'SHOWING LOVE IN ACTION'
Paul encouraged us, saying: "Become imitators of God, as beloved children, and walk in love." (Eph. 5:1, 2) To 'walk in love' means that each day we strive to show love in everything we do. And when we do so consistently, it will be obvious. John wrote: "Little children, let us love, not in word or speech, but in deed and truth." (1 John 3:18) For example, loving God and our neighbor motivates us to share the good news of the Kingdom. (Matt. 24:14; Luke 10:27) Also, showing kindness to others, being generous, and speaking kindly are ways to show that we 'walk in love.' This is why the Bible urges us: "And may the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and to the endurance of Christ."—2 Thess. 3:13.
The love that we demonstrate is not merely emotional. For instance, a parent might feel affection for his child, yet still discipline him because he knows it is for the child's good. Similarly, we may lovingly correct a brother or sister, helping them to see their mistake. But above all, God shows love, and the Bible says that "God is love." (1 John 4:8) Let us therefore continue to show love to others, always seeking to imitate Jehovah's example. (Prov. 3:11, 12) So, let us make sure that our words and actions reflect our love for Jehovah and for our fellow humans. How can we strengthen our resolve to do so? Let us now consider some practical steps.
WAYS TO SHOW LOVE
Often, we ask God to help us. Asking Him gives us strength to show love. Jesus prayed to Jehovah, asking Him to grant people "the sacred spirit to those who request it." (Luke 11:13) We can ask for His spirit to help us speak kindly and act lovingly toward others. (Acts 5:16) For example, if you are an elder, you might pray for guidance to give loving counsel based on the Scriptures. Or if you are a parent, you might ask God to help you discipline your children in a way that is both firm and loving, and that will benefit them.
Truly, consider how Jesus felt about others and what troubled them. (1 Peter 2:21, 23) Showing empathy means understanding how someone feels and what they are going through. Some may wonder, 'How can I really care?' A sister named Leigh realized she needed to make a conscious effort to show empathy. She said: "I used to think, 'I need to send emails to all my brothers and sisters to find out how they are doing.' But I realized I needed to listen more. I began to ask myself, 'What does this person need? What troubles him?' And I found that when I listened, I was able to offer practical help. We should strive to be sensitive to the needs of our brothers and sisters and to respond with genuine concern. I have learned that listening to others is often more valuable than writing an email. Showing empathy, like Jesus did, involves feeling what others feel and being moved to help them. It requires effort and a willingness to put ourselves in their place." So, let us continue to imitate Jesus in showing love to others.
Furthermore, love motivates us to share the good news with others. This love is a reflection of God's great love for us. (John 13:34, 35) That is why the Bible encourages us to be known for our "love," which is identified with Jesus'. However, avoid using the expression "easygoing" instead use "kindness and thoughtfulness." (Proverbs 2:5-8) As we demonstrate love like Jesus did, we will be a blessing to others, and this will motivate us to speak to people about God. How can we show love in our ministry?
WAYS TO SHOW LOVE
There are many ways we can show love in our ministry. Here are some examples:
SHOWING INTEREST IN ALL OUR BROTHERS AND SISTERS: Often, we take time to talk to those who seem downcast and offer encouragement. Let us not forget to reach out to 'those who are faithful and active in spiritual activities!' (1 Peter 5:9) Are there others among Jehovah's people whose love might not be obvious?
POINT: The expression "to sympathize with someone" means to feel "with another." (Acts 4:2, 3) We show sympathy when we visit fellow believers who are sick or experiencing difficulties. What if someone seems strong and does not appear to need help? (Psalm 119:165; Isaiah 54:13) Yet, showing sympathy toward others helps us get to know their needs, and this strengthens our bond with them.—Psalm 133:1-3; Matthew 5:9.
"LOVE NEVER FAILS"
Paul wrote: "Love never fails." (1 Corinthians 8:1) Does that mean love is perfect? Paul illustrated what love never fails by describing 13 qualities in his letter to the Corinthians. One quality is that a loving person is not self-seeking. (1 Corinthians 10:24; 13:5) Another quality is that a loving person is patient, kind, and willing to forgive. Such love is marked by loyalty and devotion.—1 Corinthians 3:14.
Above all, let us love God, and such love is like no other love. Loving God means being united with those who love righteousness, with those who appreciate truth, and with those who cherish peace. Those people have one thing in common—they honor Jehovah "with one accord." (Zechariah 3:9) Daily, let us strive to show love in everything we do, because love is an important part of living according to God's will.
^ par. 2 This is one lesson in a series of lessons on Christian qualities. Each lesson focuses on one quality or aspect of this vital quality.

text:
Mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Gianni na ũngĩ wĩtawa Maurizio methĩĩtwe me ndũũ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ta 50. Ĩndĩ ve ĩvinda ndũũ yoo yalikile thĩna. Maurizio aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ve ĩvinda nakwatiwe nĩ thĩna mũna mwetu na neeka mavĩtyo manene ala matumie tũtaanĩsya." Nake Gianni ongeleele kwasya: "Ĩla nambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya, Maurizio nĩwe waĩ mwalimũ wakwa wa Mbivilia. Aĩ ngelekany'o nzeo kwakwa na nĩwandetheeasya mũno maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Kwoou o na ndyaaĩkĩĩa ĩla wesie kũvĩtya. Natelemile mũno na nasaanĩw'a nĩ ũndũ ngwĩka nũndũ nĩneesĩ ndũũ yitũ ndĩendeea. Neewie ta natiwa nĩ weka."
MŨNYANYA mũseo nĩ wa vata mũno, na andũ matekĩĩte kĩthito ti laisi ndũũ yoo ĩkaendeea kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Ĩndĩ ndũũ yenyu ĩkalika thĩna, nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũmĩtangĩĩe? No twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ twasisya andũ amwe mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ ala maĩ na ndũũ ngamu na ĩtina yalika thĩna.
NATA MŨNYANYAU AKAVĨTYA?
Vai nzika kana Ndaviti, ũla waĩ mũĩthi na ĩtina atw'ĩka mũsumbĩ, aĩ na anyanya aseo. Yonathani nĩ ũmwe wa anyanya asu. (1 Sam. 18:1) Ĩndĩ aĩ o na anyanya angĩ ta mwathani Nathani. Mbivilia ndĩwetete ndũũ yake na Nathani yambĩĩe ĩndĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩmwe Ndaviti nĩwamumbũlĩle Nathani ũndũ mũna wasũanĩaa kwĩka o tondũ o naku ũtonya kumbũlĩla mũnyanyau kĩmbithĩ kyaku. Ndaviti nĩwamumbũlĩle kana aĩ na wendi wa kwakĩa Yeova nyũmba. No nginya akethĩwa endeeiw'e mũno nĩ woni wa Nathani nĩkwĩthĩwa aĩ mũnyanyae na aĩ na veva wa Yeova.—2 Sam. 7:2, 3.
Ĩndĩ ve ũndũ weekĩkie ũla walikilye ndũũ yoo mũisyonĩ. Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti nĩweekie ũlaalai na Mbathi-sieva na ĩtina avanga Ulia, mũũme wa Mbathi-sieva, oawe. (2 Sam. 11:2-21) Ndaviti eethĩĩtwe e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova na aiatĩĩa ũsili wa katĩ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ. Ĩndĩ eeka naĩ ĩsu nthũku mũno! Nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie mũsumbĩ ũsu waĩ mũseo? We no weene ũito wa naĩ ĩsu yake? We asũanĩaa no avithe Ngai naĩ ĩsu yake?
We Nathani esaa kwĩka ata? Esaa kweteela mũndũ ũngĩ aneene na mũsumbĩ ĩũlũ wa naĩ ĩsu? Ve andũ angĩ meesĩ mũvango ũla Ndaviti weekie wa kũmũaa Ulia. Kwoou Nathani aĩ o asũanĩa kana ndeĩlikya ũndũnĩ ũsu nũndũ kwĩka ũu kwaĩ kũtonya kwananga ndũũ yoo ya ĩvinda ĩasa. O na kwĩka ũu kwaĩ kũtonya kũtuma Nathani oawa. Na ũu nĩw'o nũndũ Ndaviti aĩ anavanga Ulia akoawa o na ate na ĩvĩtyo.
Ĩndĩ Nathani aĩ mũneeni wa Ngai. Na mwathani ũsu nĩweesĩ kana aema kũneena na Ndaviti ĩũlũ wa naĩ ĩsu, ngwatanĩo yoo nĩkwanangĩka na wasya wake wa ngoo ũithũka. Mũnyanyae, Ndaviti, eekĩte ũndũ ũtamwendeeasya Yeova. Na kwoou mũsumbĩ ũsu nĩwendaa kũtetheew'a mũno nĩ kana atũngĩĩe ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova. Kwa w'o, ũla waĩ atonya kũtethya Ndaviti no mũnyanya wa w'o. Nake Nathani aĩ mũnyanya wa w'o vyũ. Avangie kwambĩĩsya ĩ ngewa na ngelekany'o yesaa kũkiita Ndaviti ngoo nesa nũndũ aĩ mũĩthi tene. Nathani nĩwatavisye Ndaviti ũvoo ũla watũmĩtwe nĩ Ngai, ĩndĩ amũtavisye kwa nzĩa nzeo weethĩa nĩwakwatya ũito wa naĩ syake na ũu watuma osa ĩtambya.—2 Sam. 12:1-14.
We wĩka ata mũnyanyau akesa kwĩka ĩvĩtyo ĩnene kana akeka naĩ ngito? Nũtonya kũtatĩka ũkambĩĩa kũsũanĩa kana waumbũla naĩ yake ndũũ yenyu nĩkwanangĩka. O na kau atumĩa nĩmatonya kũmũtetheesya, nũtonya kwambĩĩa kwona kana wamatavya naĩ ĩsu, mũnyanyau nũkũũmĩa. We wĩka ata vekala ũu?
Ũla mwana-a-asa tũmũwetie wĩtawa Gianni aĩtye ũũ aililikana ũndũ kweethĩiwe: "Nĩnamanyie kana Maurizio ndailyĩ ta tene. Ndandavasya maũndũ ũtheinĩ tondũ weekaa vau mbeenĩ. Nĩnavangie kũneena nake ĩũlũ wa kĩla kyeekĩkĩte o na kau ũndũ ũsu ndwaĩ laisi kwakwa o na vanini. Neekũlasya, 'Yu nĩmũtavya kyaũ kĩla ũtesĩ? Ko ũtew'a woo namũtavya?' Ĩndĩ nalilikana maũndũ onthe ala tweemanyĩĩtye nĩ nake, neewie nakwata vinya wa kũneena nake. O nake Maurizio nĩwandetheetye ĩvinda nendaa ũtethyo. Ndyendaa ndũũ yitũ ĩkw'e ĩndĩ kĩla nendaa nĩ kũmũtetheesya nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩnamũthĩnĩkĩaa."
Nake Maurizio ongeleele ũũ: "Gianni aneenie kuma ngoonĩ na kĩla wawetie kyaĩ kya w'o. Nĩnamanyie kana kĩla kyangwatie nũndũ wa mavĩtyo makwa ti we watumĩte kĩngwata, o na ti Yeova. Na kwoou nĩneetĩkĩlile ũtao ũla nanengiwe nĩ atumĩa, na ĩtina wa ĩvinda ngwatanĩo yakwa na Yeova yaseũva."
NATA MŨNYANYAU ANAKWATWA NĨ THĨNA?
Ndaviti aĩ na anyanya angĩ ala malũmanilye nake ĩvindanĩ ya thĩna. Ũmwe wa anyanya asu eetawa Usiai, ũla Mbivilia ĩmwĩtĩte "mũnyanyae wa Ndaviti." (2 Sam. 16:16; 1 Mav. 27:33) Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa athũkũmaa kwa mũsumbĩ na aĩ mũnyanya na mũtindany'a wa mũsumbĩ. O na nũtonya kwĩthĩwa atũmawa akeke maũndũ mana maaĩle kwĩkwa na kĩmbithĩ.
Ĩvinda yĩla Avisalomu, mwana wa Ndaviti, waĩ aneeyosea ũsumbĩ, Aisilaeli aingĩ nĩmaendie ngalĩko yake ĩndĩ Usiai ndaaĩka ũu. Na ĩla Ndaviti watolokile akĩĩte Avisalomu, Usiai nĩwaendie vala waĩ. Ndaviti nĩwaũmĩie mũno nũndũ mwana wake vamwe na anyanyae make angĩ ala wamaĩkĩĩte mayaalũmany'a nake. Ĩndĩ we Usiai nĩwaendeeie kũlũmany'a nake na nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kwanangĩa Avisalomu mũvango wake o na ethĩwa nũkwasya thayũ wake ayĩka ũu. Usiai ndaalũmany'a na Ndaviti aĩ nũndũ ũu nĩw'o wendekaa eke e mũthũkũmi wa mũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ eekie ũu nĩkwĩthĩwa we aĩ mũnyanya wa w'o.—2 Sam. 15:13-17, 32-37; 16:15–17:16.
Ũmũnthĩ nĩtũtanaa mũno kwona ũndũ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa methĩawa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu. Mayĩthĩawa na ngwatanĩo ĩsu aĩ nũndũ wa ianda ila manengetwe kĩkundinĩ, ĩndĩ ve kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtumaa mekala mendanĩte mũno. No ta methĩawa mayasya ũũ kwĩsĩla meko moo: "Nĩ mũnyanyau nũndũ nĩnonaa wĩ mũndũ wa vata, ĩndĩ ti aĩ nũndũ nĩtũnengetwe mwĩao wa kwendana."
Mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Federico nĩweeyoneie ũw'o wa ndeto isu. Mwana-a-asa me ndũũ vyũ wĩtawa Antonio nĩwamũtetheeisye mũno omĩĩsye ũndũ mũna mũmũ wamũkwatĩte. Federico aeleetye ũũ: "Ĩla Antonio wathamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kitũ, nĩtwatumie ndũũ vatavĩtĩte ĩvinda ĩasa. Ithyelĩ twaĩ atetheesya ma kĩkundi na nĩtwatanĩaa mũno kũthũkũma vamwe kĩkundinĩ. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ Antonio nĩwatw'ĩkie mũtumĩa. Aĩ mũnyanyawa na nĩwandetheeasya mũno maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva." Ĩtina Federico nĩweekie naĩ. Nĩwamanthie ũtethyo kuma kwa atumĩa na mĩtũkĩ ĩndĩ ndaaendeea kwĩthĩwa e vainia na mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi. We Antonio eekie ata vathi ũu?
Federico aĩtye: "Nĩnoonaa kana Antonio nĩwambĩw'ĩaa tei. Nĩwatatie ũndũ ũtonya andetheesye nĩusye. Nĩwendaa mũno nĩtũngĩĩe ngwatanĩo yakwa na Yeova na ndaandia o na vanini. Nĩwambĩkĩaa vinya nĩtate kũsyokea maũndũ ma kĩ-veva ta tene na ndikakw'e ngoo." Nake Antonio aeleetye ũũ: "Nĩnatũmĩaa ĩvinda yingĩ na Federico. Nendaa ethĩwe e mũthalĩku kũndavya maũndũ onthe ala mamũthĩnasya, o na woo ũla weew'aa." Ũseo nĩ kana ĩtina wa ĩvinda Federico nĩwakwatie vinya ĩngĩ kĩ-veva na esa kũtw'ĩka vainia ĩngĩ na mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi. Antonio aminĩĩe na kwasya: "O na kau yu twĩ ikundinĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, ndũũ yitũ nĩ ngamu o na kũte ũndũ yailyĩ tene."
ŨTONYA KWĨKA ATA MŨNYANYAU AŨVĨTĨSYA?
Ũtonya kwĩw'a ata mũnyanyau mwĩ ndũũ mũno akaũtia ĩvindanĩ yĩla wĩ na vata vyũ na ũtethyo wake? Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũkwĩw'ĩthya woo mwingĩ mũno. We no ũmũekee? Ngwatanĩo yenyu no ĩendeee kwĩthĩwa yĩ ndũmu ta tene?
Kwasũanĩa kĩla kyakwatie Yesũ mĩthenyanĩ yake ya mũthya kũũ nthĩ. Ekalĩte mũno na atũmwa make aĩkĩĩku na maĩ na ndũũ ya mwanya. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ wametie anyanyae. (Yoa. 15:15) Ĩndĩ kweethĩiwe ata ĩla Yesũ wakwatiwe? Atũmwa asu nĩmamũtiie. Vetelo nĩweevĩtĩte akasya we ndakamũtia Vwana wake, ĩndĩ ũtukũnĩ o ũsu nĩwamũkananĩie Yesũ!—Mt. 26:31-33, 56, 69-75.
Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana akoomĩanĩsya na ĩtatwa yĩu ya mũthya e weka. Ĩndĩ kĩu kyeekĩkie kyaĩ o kĩtonya kũtuma akw'a ngoo na aũmĩa. O na vailyĩ ũu, ngewa ĩla waeie na atũmwa make mĩthenya mĩvũthũ amina kũthayũũkw'a, ndyonanĩtye o na vanini kana we nĩwakwie ngoo, athata, kana ambĩĩa kwĩlila. Yesũ ndaaona ve vata wa kũtinda atalĩle atũmwa make mavĩtyo ala maamwĩka vamwe na ĩvĩtyo yĩla meekie ũtukũnĩ ũla wakwatiwe.
Vandũ va ũu, Yesũ nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye Vetelo vamwe na atũmwa ala angĩ kana nĩwamendete. Amonisye kana nũmaĩkĩĩte ĩla wamanengie motao ĩũlũ wa wĩa wa kũmanyĩsya andũ, ũla nĩw'o wĩa ũla wa vata mũno vyũ waatethw'a. Kwoou Yesũ ndaaeka kũmona atũmwa asu ta anyanya make. Wendo ũla wamonisye nĩwamamanyĩisye ũndũ wa vata mataaũlwa nĩw'o. Mamanyie kana no nginya matate vyũ maikamũsonokye Vwana woo ĩngĩ. Na vate nzika, nĩmeanĩisye nesa wĩa ũla Yesũ wanengie aatĩĩi make.—Meko 1:8; Ako. 1:23.
Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Elvira nũlilikanaa nesa ĩvinda yĩmwe wamũvĩtĩisye mũnyanyae wĩtawa Giuliana. Elvira aĩtye: "Ĩla Giuliana wandavisye kana nĩwaũmĩĩtw'e mũno nĩ kĩla namwĩkĩte, nathĩnĩkie mũno. Aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũnthatĩa. Ĩndĩ kĩla kyanzeng'isye nĩ kwona ainthĩnĩkĩa mũno na aithĩnĩka nũndũ wa kĩla kyesaa kũngwata nũndũ wa ĩvĩtyo yakwa. Ndikaaĩsa kũlwa nĩ ũseo ũla wambĩkie nũndũ ndaasũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa ĩkosa yĩla namwĩkĩte, ĩndĩ asũanĩaa ũndũ ĩvĩtyo yĩu yaĩ yĩtonya kũmbũmĩsya nyie mwene. Nĩnamũtũngĩie Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na mũnyanya ũnthĩnĩkĩaa vandũ va kũsũanĩa ũndũ we ũkwĩw'a."
Kwoou we ũtonya kwasya mũnyanya mũseo aĩle kwĩka ata ĩla ndũũ yoo yalika thĩna? Mũnyanya ta ũsu aĩle kwĩthĩwa eyũmbanĩtye kũneena e na tei ĩndĩ ateũvithany'a kĩndũ ĩla ve vata wa kwĩka ũu. O na ĩngĩ aĩle kwĩthĩwa ailyĩ ta Nathani na Usiai ala malũmanilye na Ndaviti o na ĩla waĩ thĩnanĩ, na ta Yesũ, ũla weeyũmbanĩtye kũekea. We nĩwĩthĩawa ũilyĩ ũu kwa anyanyau?

translation:
The son of the master, Gianni, and his brother Maurizio were together for about 50 years in prison. Prison has been a long time for them. Maurizio said: "Prison has caught up with us with our brother and we have made big mistakes which we will try to correct." Then Gianni responded quickly: "But tell me to reconcile, Maurizio is my teacher from Mbivilia. He didn't show me respect and I wasted a lot of good things. Come now and I will show you how to behave. I have suffered enough and I have realized that this life is not ours and we need to move forward. It's too late to be stubborn."
THE OLD MAN is strong, and people who commit crimes don't learn until their lives are spent in prison. If your life goes wrong, is it possible to fix it? Let's reconcile many things and leave some people behind in Mbivilia and live with peace and let life go well.
WHAT DID THE OLD MAN DO?
Whether Ziba or David, who was a man of honor and integrity, had an old man. Jonathan was one of those old men. (1 Sam. 18:1) And he also had other old men like Nathan. The Bible tells us about David and Nathan. And once David confessed to Nathan a sin he had committed so that he could confess his sin to God. David confessed that he had wanted to build Nathan a house. But Nathan told him that God would establish his kingdom forever—2 Sam. 7:2, 3.
And there is something you should know about what happened. King David desired a woman and saw Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, and took her. (2 Sam. 11:2-21) David displeased Jehovah and carried the consequences of his actions for many years. But she still has hope! What caused this king to fall? Do you think he knew his mistake? Did he offend God with his mistake?
Did Nathan say anything about it? He went to tell a certain man who had done a great wrong. There were others who followed David's example in taking Bathsheba. So Nathan did not hesitate to tell him the truth about his wrongdoing so that he might repent. And because of this, David desired Bathsheba and she became pregnant.
Indeed, Nathan was a man of God. And it would be good if he could speak to David about this matter, so that his loyalty to Jehovah would not be weakened by his own desires. My friend, David, you have deeply offended Jehovah. And now this wrongdoing will never leave you until you turn back to Him. For this reason, you will always remember what you have done. Nathan rebuked him severely and explained to him how he had greatly angered Jehovah by doing this evil thing—2 Sam. 12:1-14.
What makes a person commit a serious sin when they know it is wrong? It may be due to their desire to please themselves rather than thinking about what pleases Jehovah. But even then, it is possible to help them, by speaking to them truthfully and showing them how their actions affect their relationship with Jehovah, my friend. What should we do?
Recently, a young man named Gianni told us about a problem he was facing: "I realized that Maurizio was lying to me. I noticed some things were strange because he kept avoiding certain topics. I tried to talk to him several times, but he always changed the subject or made excuses. Finally, I asked him, 'Are you really telling me the truth? Why are you hiding things from me?' Then I discovered many things that I didn't know before, and I felt hurt because I couldn't trust him anymore. So I decided to stop talking to him. But Maurizio continued to lie and refused to admit his mistakes. I wanted to help him, but I also felt betrayed and disappointed."
Maurizio responded: "Gianni accused me of many things, and I didn't like it. I realized that everything he suspected was true, and I wasn't being honest, either with him or with Jehovah. And that's why I avoided answering his questions and damaged my relationship with Jehovah."
WHY DOES A FRIEND GET ANGRY?
Sometimes people get angry when they feel betrayed by a friend. One example is Shimei, who severely insulted David, which the Bible calls "cursing David." (2 Sam. 16:16; 1 Kings 27:33) It can be upsetting to be criticized by someone you thought was loyal, or to have someone reveal your secrets. And it can be frustrating to see others succeed while you struggle.
For instance, Absalom, David's son, rebelled against him, and many Israelites went to support him in Jerusalem. When David heard about this, Shimei went to meet him and began to insult him. David showed restraint and did not harm Shimei or his companions. However, Shimei continued to curse David and throw stones at him. Shimei's actions demonstrated his loyalty to Absalom and his desire to see David fail. David understood that Shimei was acting out of anger and allowed him to express himself.—2 Sam. 15:13-17, 32-37; 16:15–17:16.
It is normal to feel hurt when someone disappoints us or does something wrong. But holding on to resentment can be damaging, both emotionally and spiritually. Sometimes, our reaction to injustice is more harmful than the injustice itself. As an illustration, consider this saying: "Resentment is like drinking poison and hoping it will kill your enemy."
A young man named Federico experienced this firsthand. His childhood friend, Antonio, deeply disappointed him. Federico explained: "Antonio did something very hurtful, so we stopped being friends. At first, I felt terrible and wanted revenge. But then I realized that getting even would only cause more problems. So I decided to focus on forgiving him and moving forward." Eventually, Federico came to terms with what happened. He prayed about it and sought help from mature Christians. What about Antonio?
Did he ever apologize?
Federico said: "I don't know if Antonio ever regretted what he did. He never apologized to me. I just want to continue serving Jehovah faithfully and remain neutral. I won't allow past hurts to prevent me from enjoying life now and in the future." Later, Antonio admitted: "I really messed up my friendship with Federico. I should have been more considerate and less selfish." That is why Federico was able to forgive him and maintain his relationship with mature Christians. Antonio added with regret: "If only we had shown each other more love, perhaps things wouldn't have turned out this way."
IS IT WRONG TO FEEL HURT WHEN SOMEONE OFFENDS US?
Is it wrong to feel upset when someone wrongs us, especially when it involves serious harm or unfair treatment? Of course not! It is natural to feel pain. But how can we deal with those feelings? Is your resentment consuming you and preventing you from making spiritual progress?
To illustrate how Jesus dealt with betrayal, remember his final night. He knew one of his apostles would betray him. This deeply troubled Jesus. (John 15:15) How did Jesus respond to this betrayal? He prayed to his Father about it. Consider this example so that you too may pray to God and find comfort.—Matt. 26:31-33, 56, 69-75.
Jesus also showed remarkable self-control under extreme provocation. He could have used his power to retaliate, but he chose not to. And despite knowing that his apostles often failed him, he continued to trust them, patiently correcting them whenever necessary. Jesus understood that humans are imperfect and prone to mistakes, just like his apostle who betrayed him.
Friends, Jesus entrusted himself to Jehovah along with his apostles, even though some of them disappointed him. He demonstrated faith by continuing to use them in his ministry, realizing that they were valuable despite their imperfections. By doing so, Jesus set an example for us to show confidence in our brothers. His attitude reminds us that we should not quickly dismiss others because of past errors. And let us remember that Jesus' prayers helped him endure what he faced.—Acts 1:8; 1 Cor. 1:23.
A sister named Elvira was encouraged by a fellow worshiper named Giuliana. Elvira said: "Giuliana always reminded me that I am loved and appreciated, and she showed genuine interest in me. She had a way of making me feel important. What especially touched my heart was seeing her pray earnestly and sincerely on my behalf. I began to cope better with the challenges I faced, and I felt strengthened to continue serving Jehovah despite my limitations. I thank Jehovah for using such loving friends to help me when I am discouraged."
What can help you to be more encouraging? A friend may need encouragement without asking for it, and sometimes it takes effort to discern what someone needs. Others may need encouragement like Nathan and Ahijah did when dealing with David, and like Jesus did when facing opposition. Are you willing to be that kind of friend?

text:
Vaa ĩtheo ve na ngelekany'o ya ũndũ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova ĩtonya kũea ngewa na mũtũi. Twasye mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Megan ũla nĩ Ngũsĩ, nĩwavika mũsyĩ kwa mũndũ mũka ũngĩ wĩtawa Shirley, na mambĩĩa kũea ngewa.
"ĨKAAI ŨU ŨNDŨ WA KŨNDILIKANA"
Megan: Ũvoo waku Shirley. Nĩnĩnatanie mũno nũndũ nũnookie ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kyumwa kĩla kĩnavĩtie. * Ũnoonie ata ũmbanonĩ ũsu?
Shirley: Nĩnĩneewie mũyo kũka, ĩndĩ ndeũkũvitha ndinaaelewa nĩ maũndũ onthe ala mananeeneiwe. Nĩnĩw'ĩte andũ aingĩ mayasya nĩmalilikanaa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ mũthenya wa Kĩlisimasi na kũthayũũka kwake mũthenya wa Isita ĩndĩ ndyaaĩw'a mũndũ o na ũmwe ũkwasya nũlilikanaa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ.
Megan: Kwa w'o Kĩlisimasi na Isita nĩ sikũkũ syĩ nguma mũno ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyonaa wĩ ũndũ wa vata kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Ethĩwa wĩ na ndatĩka nini no nĩkwony'e nĩkĩ twĩkaa ũu.
Shirley: Nĩ sawa, vai thĩna.
Megan: Kĩla kĩtumaa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ililikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ nũndũ we mwene nĩweeyĩaĩie aatĩĩi make mekae ũu. Kwasũanĩa kĩla kyeekĩkie ũtukũ wa mũthya Yesũ atanamba kũkw'a. Nũlilikene mboka ya mwanya Yesũ waĩe vamwe na amanyĩw'a make aĩkĩĩku?
Shirley: Wĩweta Mesa ya Mwĩaĩi?
Megan: Ĩĩ. Kwa ĩsyĩtwa yĩngĩ yĩtawa Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi. Maiya kyaũya kĩu Yesũ nĩwameyĩaĩie ũndũ makekaa. Kwasoma ndeto syake ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ yĩĩ ya Luka 22:19.
Shirley: Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nake oosa kĩmũtũ, na amina kũtũnga mũvea, atilanga, na amanenga, akyasya, Kĩĩ nĩkyo mwĩĩ wakwa ũla wanenganiwe nũndũ wenyu: ĩkaai ũu ũndũ wa kũndilikana."
Megan: Nĩ mũvea. Kwasisya ndeto ii sya mũthya sya ĩandĩko yĩu. Yesũ ameie: "Ĩkaai ũu ũndũ wa kũndilikana." Na atanamba kũmatavya ndeto isu, Yesũ nĩwamatavisye nesa kĩla maaĩle kũlilikana ĩũlũ wake. Ameie kana akaumya thayũ wake kwondũ wa aatĩĩi make. Yesũ aeleisye ũndũ ũsu kwa ndeto ingĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 20:28. Mũsoa ũsu waĩtye atĩĩ: "Mwana wa mũndũ ndaaũka kũthũkũmwa, ĩndĩ nĩ kũthũkũma, na kũnengane thayũ wake wĩthĩwe wovosyo kwondũ wa aingĩ." Kwa ũkuvĩ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ililikanaa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kĩla mwaka nũndũ syĩthĩawa iililikana nthembo ya wovosyo ĩla Yesũ waumisye. Kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ no kĩtume andũ onthe ala ewi makwata thayũ.
NĨKĨ VAĨ VATA WA NTHEMBO YA WOVOSYO?
Shirley: Nĩnĩw'ĩte andũ mayasya kana Yesũ akwie nĩ kana twĩkwata thayũ. Ĩndĩ kwa w'o, ndieleawa ũndũ ũu ũtonyeka.
Megan: Tiiwe wĩ weka ũsũanĩaa ũu. Ũvoo ĩũlũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo wĩ maũndũ maingĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ũsu nĩ ũmanyĩsyo ũmwe wa kwendeesya mũno nthĩnĩ wa Ndeto ya Ngai. Ndiasya wĩ o na mwanya tũendeee?
Shirley: Ĩĩ, nĩ na ndatĩka siana ũna.
Megan: Nĩ sawa. Nĩthĩĩtwe ndyĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo na nĩngũtata ngũelesye kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi.
Shirley: Aaya.
Megan: Nĩ kana tũelewe wovosyo, no nginya tũkamanya kĩla kyeethĩiwe ĩla Atamu na Eva meekie naĩ me mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. Nĩ kana tũmanye ũndũ veethĩiwe, kwaeka tũsome ĩandĩko ya Alomi 6:23. No ũsome mũsoa ũsu?
Shirley: Ĩĩ. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ; ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ."
Megan: Nĩ mũvea. Kwaeka tũsũanĩe ndeto isu. Ũndũ wa mbee, kwasisya ũndũ mũsoa ũsu wambĩĩe na kwasya: "Ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ." Ũsu nĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi ũla Ngai wawetie vaaya mwambĩĩonĩ. Kwa w'o mwambĩĩonĩ vai mũndũ waĩ na naĩ. Atamu na Eva moombĩtwe mate na naĩ, na syana syoo syesaa kwĩthĩwa iilyĩ oou. Kwoou andũ mayesaa kũkw'a. Atamu na Eva o vamwe na nzyawa syoo mesaa kwĩkala tene na tene me atanu. Ĩndĩ o tondũ twĩsĩ maũndũ mayaaĩthĩwa mailyĩ ũu, kana?
Shirley: Nĩ w'o nũndũ Atamu na Eva nĩmaĩe ũsyao wa mũtĩ ũla meeaĩwe maikaye.
Megan: Ĩĩ, ĩla Atamu na Eva manyuvie kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai nĩmeekie naĩ. Na kwoou manyuva mo ene kwĩthĩwa me ene naĩ. Ũtwi ũsu meekie nĩwamaeteie mathĩna maingĩ vamwe na nzyawa syoo.
Shirley: Wĩenda kwasya ata?
Megan: Kwaeka ngũnenge ngelekany'o. We nĩwendete kũua kyavati?
Shirley: Ĩĩ! Nĩnendete kũkĩua.
Megan: Kwasũanĩa wĩ na kalaĩ ka kũua kyavati ke na yĩima vandũ. Yu wĩona ata? Kyavati kyonthe kĩla kĩkũuwa na kalaĩ kau kĩkeethĩawa kĩilyĩ ata? Nowĩtĩkĩlane nakwa kana kĩkeethĩawa kĩ kĩũngũu vala ve yĩima yĩu?
Shirley: Ĩĩ, ũu nĩ w'o.
Megan: O ta kalaĩ kau, ĩla Atamu na Eva manyuvie kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai meethĩiwe na "yĩima," kana ĩlanga nũndũ wa naĩ ĩla meekie. Na nũndũ meekie naĩ matanamba kũsyaa, syana ila mesaa kũsyaa ĩtina wa vau syaĩ syĩthĩwe na "yĩima." Ũu nĩ kwasya kana syonthe syaĩ isyawe syĩ na naĩ. Mbivilianĩ, ndeto "naĩ" ndyonanasya o kĩla Atamu na Eva meekie, ĩndĩ nĩyonanasya kĩla kyatũkwatie nũndũ wa naĩ ĩsu. Kwoou, o na kau ti ithyĩ tweekie naĩ ĩsu, o na tũyaĩ asyae ĩla mamĩkie, Atamu na Eva matũlikilye naĩnĩ nũndũ twĩ nzyawa syoo. Na naĩ ĩsu noyo ĩetae kĩkw'ũ. Na o tondũ tũsomie ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 6:23, ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ.
Shirley: Ndikwona ũu waĩle. Andũ onthe matonya kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna ata na nĩ Atamu na Eva meekie naĩ?
Megan: Waneena w'o, ũu ndwaĩle. Ĩndĩ ve maũndũ maingĩ makonetye ũndũ ũsu. Ngai nĩwatũmĩie ũsili wake wa katĩ, na atw'a kana Atamu na Eva maĩle kũkw'a kwondũ wa naĩ syoo, ĩndĩ ũsyao woo nĩwanengiwe wĩkwatyo. Ngai nĩweekie mũvango mũseo nĩ kana atumye thĩnanĩ ũsu asyai asu maitũ matũlikilye. Mũvango ũsu nĩ nthembo ya wovosyo ĩla Yesũ waumisye. Kwasisya ĩngĩ ĩandĩko ya Alomi 6:23. Ĩtina wa mũsoa ũsu kũweta kana "ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ," ũendeee kwasya: "Ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ." Kwoou kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ nĩkyo kĩtũvingũĩaa nzĩa ya kũvonoka kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ. *
WOVOSYO—MŨTHĨNZĨO WA VATA VYŨ KUMA KWA NGAI
Megan: Ve ũndũ ũngĩ ngwenda kũkwony'a mũsoanĩ ũsu.
Shirley: Ũndũ mwaũ?
Megan: Kwoona mũsoa ũsu ũndũ waĩtye: "Mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ." Ethĩwa Yesũ nĩwe wathĩnie na akw'a kwondũ witũ, nĩkĩ mũsoa ũũ ũkwasya kana nthembo ya wovosyo nĩ "mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai"? Nĩkĩ ũte kwasya kana nĩ "mũthĩnzĩo wa Yesũ"? *
Shirley: Vau nyie ndyĩsĩ.
Megan: Ngai nĩwe woombie Atamu na Eva, na nĩwe mavĩtĩisye ĩla maleile kwĩw'a me mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. No nginya Ngai e Ĩthe woo akethĩwa aũmĩie mũno ngoonĩ ĩla syana isu syake sya mbee syaleile kũmwĩw'a. Ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwoosie ĩtambya na mĩtũkĩ. * Nĩwavangie ũmwe wa syũmbe syake sya veva oke kũũ nthĩ, ethĩwe e mũndũ ũte na naĩ, na ĩtina ayumya thayũ wake wĩthĩwe nthembo ya wovosyo. Kwoou mũvango wa nthembo ya wovosyo waĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai. O na ve o ũndũ ũngĩ ũkwonany'a kana nthembo ĩsu yaĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai. Nĩwĩthĩwa waasũanĩa ũndũ Ngai weewie ĩla Yesũ wooaiwe?
Shirley: Aiee, ndyaasũanĩa ũndũ ũsu.
Megan: Nĩona vaa wĩ na twĩndũ twa syana twa kũthaũka, no nginya ũkethĩwa wĩ na syana.
Shirley: Ĩĩ, nĩ na twana twĩlĩ, kamwana na kelĩtu.
Megan: Kwasũanĩa ta wĩ mũsyai ũndũ Ĩthe wa Yesũ wa ĩtunĩ, Yeova Ngai, ũtonya kwĩthĩwa eewie mũthenya ũla Yesũ wakwie. Kwa ndeto ingĩ, we wĩona ta weewie ata e ĩtunĩ asyaĩĩsye Mwana wake ũla wendete aikwatwa, akathekeewa, na kũkũnwa ngũmi? Na nĩ ta weewie ata ĩla Mwana wake waathĩĩiwe mũtĩnĩ, na atiwa vau akw'e o kavola kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo?
Shirley: No nginya akethĩwa eewie woo mwingĩ mũno. Ndyaasũanĩa ũndũ ũsu!
Megan: Kwa w'o tũitonya kũmanya nesa vyũ ũndũ Ngai weewie mũthenya ũsu. Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kana no nginya ethĩwe eewie woo mũno, na ĩngĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kĩla kyatumie etĩkĩla ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩwe. Ũndũ ũsu ũeleetw'e nesa vyũ ĩandĩkonĩ yĩsĩkĩe mũno ya Yoana 3:16. No ũsome ĩandĩko yĩu?
Shirley: Ĩĩ, yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ, nĩwanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe, nĩ kana o ũla ũmwĩtĩkĩlaa ndakae, ĩndĩ ethĩwe na thayũ ũtathela."
Nthembo ya wovosyo nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ wonanasya wendo wa Ngai kwitũ
Megan: Nĩ mũvea mũno. Kwasisya ĩngĩ ndeto isu syambĩĩe mũsoanĩ ũsu. Syaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ." Nĩwoona kĩla kyatumie Ngai atũma Mwana wake kũũ nthĩ nĩ kana akw'e kwondũ witũ? Nĩ wendo. Kwa w'o nthembo ya wovosyo nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ wonanasya wendo wa Ngai kwitũ. Na kyu nĩkyo kĩtumi Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syũmbanaa kĩla mwaka ililikane kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Maũndũ asu twaneenea nĩmakũtethya?
Shirley: Ĩĩ, nĩmandethya. Nĩ mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yaku kũmbony'a maũndũ asu.
Nĩvethĩwa ve ĩkũlyo wendaa kũkwata ũsũngĩo wayo kuma Mbivilianĩ? Nĩwĩthĩwa wendaa kũmanya ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo kana maũndũ ala Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩkaa? Ethĩwa nĩwendaa ũu, ndũkalee kũneena na ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Akatanĩa kũneena naku ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu.
^ kal. 5 Mũthenya ũmwe kĩla mwaka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyũmbanaa vamwe nĩ kana ililikane kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Mwaka ũũ kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kũkeethĩwa Wakatano, Matukũ 3, Mwei wa 4.
^ kal. 32 Vakeethĩwa kĩlungu kĩngĩ kĩilyĩ ta kĩĩ kĩla kĩkonany'a ũndũ nthembo ya wovosyo ya Yesũ ĩtũtetheeasya kũvonoka kuma naĩnĩ, na ũndũ twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana nthembo ĩsu ĩtũtethye.
^ kal. 36 Kwosana na Mbivilia Ngai na Yesũ nĩ andũ elĩ me kĩvathũkany'o.
^ kal. 38 Sisya Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:15.

translation:
When I was a teenager, I struggled with low self-esteem. I remember one girl named Megan who was a Christian, she confided in another girl named Shirley, and wanted to feel good about herself.
"THIS IS WHAT SELF-RESPECT MEANS"
Megan: Shirley, how do you feel? I have been thinking about what it means to show respect for Jesus' command to love one another. * Do you have any thoughts on this?
Shirley: I think it's important, because I realize that there are so many things I don't understand. I know many people struggle to show respect for Jesus during Christmas and Easter, and to appreciate his sacrifice, they need to learn what it means to show respect for Jesus.
Megan: For me, Christmas and Easter are just days that pass quickly. As a Witness of Jehovah, I believe it is important to show respect for Jesus' command. Tell me what you think and I will tell you what I think too.
Shirley: That's fine, go ahead.
Megan: Everything that the Witnesses of Jehovah do to show respect for Jesus' command is something that everyone should imitate. It is important to remember everything Jesus did the night he died. Did you ever wonder why Jesus chose his apostles and companions?
Shirley: Do you mean the Memorial?
Megan: Yes. In fact, many call it the Commemoration of Christ's Death. Because Jesus showed us what it means to be humble. Read his example, but first read Luke 22:19.
Shirley: It says: "And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me."
Megan: That's right. Let's examine that scripture more closely. Jesus said: "This do in remembrance of me." And he commanded that they repeat that act, so Jesus instituted the Memorial each year to remind us of his sacrifice. He also showed his followers how to be humble. Jesus explained this further in another scripture found in Matthew 20:28. It reads: "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many." Therefore, the Witnesses of Jehovah commemorate Jesus' death each year so that we can remember the value of the ransom Jesus provided. Remembering Jesus helps people everywhere to be humble.
WHAT IS THE VALUE OF THE RANSOM?
Shirley: I think people question whether Jesus really cares if we become humble. But honestly, I understand why this is important.
Megan: Don't feel bad about questioning this. The value of the ransom is much greater than we realize. For one thing, it is an expression of God's love for us. Would you like to discuss this further?
Shirley: Yes, I would like to learn more.
Megan: Okay. Let me explain the value of the ransom and then I will show you scriptures to support what I say.
Shirley: Fine.
Megan: If we understand the ransom, it will help us appreciate what Adam and Eve forfeited when they disobeyed God. If we know what was lost, let's read Romans 6:23. Will you read that scripture?
Shirley: Yes. It says: "The wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord."
Megan: That's right. So let's analyze that scripture. The second part of that scripture tells us what God has given us freely. This is something everyone has. Adam and Eve lost this when they sinned, and their descendants have been dying ever since. Many people want this. Adam and Eve were once perfect, but they chose to disobey God, and now none of us are perfect. Because of this, we need to learn things like this, don't we?
Shirley: That's how it seems to me about Adam and Eve losing the gift of eternal life.
Megan: Yes, but Adam and Eve showed disregard for God's law when they did so. And many people still show disregard for his law. This scripture shows that most people are imperfect because of what happened to them.
Shirley: Are you going to say more?
Megan: Before I continue, let me ask you something. Do you want to live forever?
Shirley: Yes! I want to live.
Megan: To appreciate why you can live, think about what it takes to live forever and what it means to be alive. Do you see anyone who lives forever without getting sick? Does anyone stay healthy indefinitely? Think about whether someone could remain young and strong forever without needing blood transfusions?
Shirley: Yes, that is true.
Megan: Oh yes, but Adam and Eve showed disregard for God's law when it was said, "alive," or perhaps this is just my understanding of it. And my understanding of it makes it difficult to accept, because it seems like everything is affected by being "alive." This is hard to understand, or maybe everything is influenced by it. Frankly, I believe that "it" affects everything Adam and Eve did, and I believe it affects everything we do. Many, including us, have accepted it, Adam and Eve have been associated with it, and it has become part of our nature. And it continues to affect us. And because of this, we should read Romans 6:23, which speaks of its effect.
Shirley: I understand now. Do many people get caught up in this situation and is it because of what Adam and Eve did?
Megan: Exactly so, this is true. There are many things that contribute to this situation. God sent his Son to die for us, and although Adam and Eve failed to obey him, his sacrifice was sufficient. God made a provision so that those who believe can be saved. This provision is the gift of salvation through Jesus Christ. Read also Romans 6:23. The rest of that verse, following "the wages of sin is death," continues: "but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." Truly, Jesus' sacrifice is what enables us to escape from death and corruption. *
SALVATION—A GIFT FROM GOD TO MAN
Megan: There is something else I want to discuss about this matter.
Shirley: What is it?
Megan: Notice how the verse reads: "The gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." Since Jesus died and paid the price for us, does this verse mean that the gift of salvation is "God's gift"? Or does it mean that it is "Jesus' gift"? *
Shirley: I don't understand.
Megan: God is the One who created Adam and Eve, and He allowed them to fail in order to demonstrate His love for mankind. So it is fitting that God should provide the means for saving his children. Jehovah shows mercy and compassion. * He gives one of his beloved sons to die for us, and anyone who believes in Him will have their sins forgiven and receive the gift of salvation. That is why the gift of salvation is called God's gift. And yet there is something else regarding this gift of salvation being God's gift. Did God need to send Jesus to die for us?
Shirley: Oh, I understand now.
Megan: We all make mistakes, and it is fitting that we should repent.
Shirley: Yes, I have children, a son and a daughter.
Megan: Do you realize how much God the Father loved his only Son, Jehovah God, so that he would allow him to die? Furthermore, do you realize that he watched his Son suffer, be beaten, and crucified? And did he watch his Son being buried, knowing that he would rise again?
Shirley: So it is fitting that He did so very much. I understand now!
Megan: Now let's see if we can learn more about what God did for us. If we believe that He did so much, and also believe that everything He has done is for our benefit. This thing brings us great comfort, as shown in John 3:16. Would you like to read the scripture?
Shirley: Yes, it says: "God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him shall not perish, but have everlasting life."
The gift of salvation is such a wonderful thing showing God's love for us.
Megan: That is true. Let's look at another scripture to help you understand this better. It says: "God so loved the world." Do you see how much God loves us that He sent His Son to die for us? It is love. Therefore, the gift of salvation is such a wonderful thing showing God's love for us. And that is why Jehovah's Witnesses commemorate Jesus' death every year. What else should we discuss?
Shirley: Yes, I appreciate that. It is good to share information that will help people understand things.
Would you like to find out how to get more help from the Bible? Would you like to learn more about what Jehovah's Witnesses believe? If you want, I can arrange for someone from Jehovah's Witnesses to talk to you. They can answer your questions.
^ par. 5 Once a year Jehovah's Witnesses commemorate Jesus' death. This year the commemoration of Jesus' death will be held on Wednesday, March 3, April month.
^ par. 32 Read paragraph 32 to find out how the gift of salvation through Jesus helps us escape destruction, and how important it is that we value this gift.
^ par. 36 According to the Bible, God and Jesus are two distinct persons.
^ par. 38 Read Psalm 3:15.

text:
Kikamba
Peter Ngila
Tene tene muno andu matembeaa na moko na maau, ta nyamu sya kithekani. Matembeaa mituki kuvituka tuvaluku na ikoyo. Maau na moko syai nduu kuvituka mamutha angi; ituo, inyuunyuu, itiinyo na moko masyo ni mavw'anene. Moko na maau mai na syaa itano. Syaa sya moko na mauu syavangitwe undu umwe. Matuku asu kyaa kya yumbumbu kyeanene na kila kya kinene kya kuu; na kyathengeanie na syaa iingi. Maau na moko meetanaa mwendy'a.
Matetheaniasya kukua mwii kila vandu wendaa kuthi ta; ndunyu, ndukani, mitini na iimani; vandu voonthe vala mwii wendaa kuthi. Ona kiw'uni maau na moko mathukumaa nesa kutetheesya mwii kuthambia. Nimeew'anaa. Mavoyaa utethy'o wa mamutha angi ta munuka; meew'aa na matu, maveva'a na manyu'u na matumiaa metho kwona.
Mwiw'ano uu woo museo watumie mamutha angi ma mwii makwatwa ni kiwiu. Mambiisya kulea kutetheesya maau na moko. Kiwiu kyamalinda metho moolw'a kana moko na maau nisyo imatw'aa kundu na kundu. Mambiisya kuvanga nzama ya kumina moko na maau.
Munuka wambiisya kuvoya Akili muvango na wautumia mituki. Munuka wambiisya kuseng'a na wasya, kuneena usengete muno iulu wa vinya wa moko na maau. Wakuly'a ula wai na vinya mwingi kati wamo eli. Endw'ethe asu eli mavoya wasya wa munuka na kila umwe ambiia kwasy'a ni wa vata mwiini kuvituka ula ungi. Kuma vau mamutha mambiee kusindana ula wai na vinya mwingi. Moko mambiie kwiyona nundu wa syaa syamo; mathekeea syaa sya maau nundu wa unou na ukuvi.
Nasyo syaa sya maau syeetetea iyasya syaa sya moko ni ntheke na iiisaa. Masindano maendee vandu va mithenya yiana undu muna. Mavinda angi moko na maau mayaimatonya kuthukuma vamwe nesa. Mwiso vatw'ika ni ikulyo ya vinya. Nuu ula wi vinya mwing'i kuvituka ungi? Mathi kula kwi mamutha angi ni kana masilan'we.
Munuka waisye nimasindane. Mamutha aangi nimeetikilile woni usu nundu wai museo. Ona vailye uu angi maisye mavalukany'e. Angi maisye mokite na mbanga, kusembany'a; itina mawoni aa oonthe mayaaitikilwa'. Munuka niwo' wasindie ingi, itina wa kuvoya mesilya kuma kula kwi Akili; ula waisye kila imutha ikooka na isindano, kila umwe kwa ivinda. Maau na moko nimeetikilile.
Masindano mai kithekani, vakuvi na usi. Mamutha oonthe mai ngunuu kusiiia mbanga ona yiva ila yai itonya kukia mwi'i kavindani kau matataiie nundu mai na kau wa kiinthini. Metho masisya kila vandu kana nimekwona muisyo, matu meetekie kwiw'a kawasya koonthe, ona ithwa kaninivite ata, manyuu mathesya mithumu ni kana matonye kunyungia mbanga yoonthe ila itonya kuvituka metho na matu, na munuka niweeyumbanitye kukuna kelele veethy'a muisyo.
Kiuutani kyanyaaikisye uvoo wa masindano asu mawithyululukoni ana ma kitheka kiu, nginya kiw'uni na kiseveni. Nyamu ila syi maau ona nisyo syai sya mbee kuvika, mbingi nthini wa ila nene syakwete maketi kwonany'a kana syookite kwa ngoo ntheu. Yai ikomano ya malangi ma Kikoyo, Mbiti, Nzou, Ndwia, Ngamile, Ng'ombe ya uvya munene na Mboo ya uvya mukuvi, Nzui, Mbaluku, Mbia na Mukoto. Ala mekalaa kiwuni, Nguu, Makuyu, Kingang'i, mai utee wa usi. Ala me mauu eli ta Nyaa makunganisye mathwau moo nundu wa nzasu; tusuni twainaa twi mitini, Ngeli ainaa saa syonthe. Mbwambui, mwinthooe, Ing'aui, Ngongoo syatembeaa muthangani kana mitini. Kiimbu kyakinyaa nesa na kovola. Ing'ala yasembaa kila vandu yitekuthumua. Nguli syathaanyukaa kuma ukava umwe kuthi uungi. Nginya miti na ikuthu syathingithaa kuma ngaliko imwe kuthi ingi, ivinda kwa ivinda.
Munuka wavinguie masindano na wathi:
Twiika uu ni kana twithwe na utanu
Nundu ithyoonthe
Tumite vandu vamwe
Moko na maau meevitia masya nimeitikila kila kiumila itina wa masindano vate thina. Moko nimo maumie na isindano ya mbee ila malekilywe kalungu ka uku nthi. Kuu kumwe kati wa kwa aume na kwa aka kana mavulanite maile maile kwona kalungu kau na kukekya. Mauu eli mai matonya kwiw'ana ivindani yonthe ya masindano aya na kutumia syaa syamo syi syonthe kana kimwe itina wa kiingi, ni kenda masinde. Matatie kukavindua na kukasukuma. Undu mai matonya kwika museo wai kukatheleela kakathi vaasa vanini. Ila Syaa syoonie uu syavoyie wasya kuma kula kwi munuka na syatheka muno vyu. Moko nimeyuumbanisye nundu nimo masindanaa na maau. Moosie kalungu kau ka uku, na makekya vaasa muno vyu kithekani; asindani angi na na ala makathiaa nimakumisye moko. Moko moonanisye utuika ungi; moosie tulungu twa kithangathi kuma mbakulini ya musele; maseuvisye tumitalu tunini twa kuvitukuthya ngu ngito; maseuvisye maangi na mamekya vaasa muno; syindu ila syaa sya maau itai itonya kwika. Maau makitite kwikila nthi meloeele endw'ethe moo amosu mayonany'a utuika woo. Moko ma ala makathiaa makunanganisye mbii kwonany'a ngwatanio yoo na moko aangi, kindu kila kyathatisye mauu muno vyu. Ona vailye uu maau mayai vakuvi na kwitikila kusindw'a mailye vau nthi ma uthyu moo me matuku na syaa syoo nene siisola kithangathini. Mayisily'a undu matonya kusinda.
Ivinda ya maau kuete isindano yoo niyavikie. Maisye isindano yoo iyai vinya; moko meeiwe nimakue mwii w'onthe kuma vandu vamwe nginya vangi. Syaa syai na ngulu, na syeesililye isindano yiu ya maau yai ya utumanu. Yila moko mambiisye kukua mwii, kila kindu mwiini kyai kikulumanu. Moko makwatite nthi; metho mai vakuvi na nthi, na mayaimatonya kwona vaasa; kitoo kyalikile many'uu na maathimua; maau na syaa syamo mathambalilite kiseveni. Ala makathiaa mausasya ngemi mayasya:
Nyaai Nyaai iulu.
Vai thina
Atiia Nyaai
Vai thina
Tuuluke (kiseveni)
Ona vailye uu matianiite na moko, ala ivinda ivuthu ivitu moonanasya utuika munene yu mayaimathingitha. Matambya manini moko nimaiie nundu wa woo na malekya mwii nthi. Nimathumuie na indi matata ingi. Ivinda yii matatie kutambuukya syaa nesa nikana mekwatile nthi lakini syaa ila nene nosyo syai itonya kutambuuka. Matatie kwituluma lakini itambya yii niyaleilwe nundu mayai matonya matekutumia maau. Ivinda ya syaa sya maau ya kutheka. Mavoyie tuwasya tutheke twa muluku kuma kwi munuka ni kana maikatheke na wasya muito ta ula wa syaa ivinda inini ivituku. Ila moko meew'ie maithekeewa nimathatie muno na matata ingi na vinya kukua mwii. Nimaimewi, na ila syaa syanoie nisyakolile. Mauu nimatanie kwonany'a utonyi wa maau moo; nimasembie, mathaanyuka; ivinda yii yoonthe matekuvalukya mwii.
Maau oonthe nimakinyie nthi kwonany'a witikilano. Moko nimaleanile na wonany'o uu muthuku wa mathau, molitwe kana nimo mambeeisye mathau asu. Ona vailye uu, oonthe nginya akathii, nimoonie kindu kya usengy'o kya moko; Syaa sya moko nene ila syalungele ila moko matataa kukua mwii nisyaanikie na syaa ila ingi. Mamutha ala angi makilye kuendeea na kutheka ila moonie kindu kingi; vaasa kute kyaa kya yumbumbu kila kyai kyoka na kyatumaa moko matathukuma nesa, kyongeleeile vinya wa syaa wa kukwata. Kii kyai kyau? Uthuku utw'ikite vinya wa kuseuvya!
Mauneenany'a nthini wa mamutha ni kana makwate musindi maendeei kwa mithenya itano, utalo wa syaa moko na maau. Itina wa kutata monu mayaatonya kukwata musindi; moko elie nimatheaniasya undu vatonyeka. Mambiee kilungu kya kutatithya mesilya; makulikye mwii wai kyau, na meethia wai (mwii) mo oonthe. Ila muthenya yathiitwa kutethya wia ni kenda oonthe makwatianie.
Ona vailye oou ni kenda vaikaithiwe masindano ma muthemba usu ivinda yukite, mamutha oonthe meew'anie mwii ukakinyaa uungamite, maau makinyite nthi nesa na moko kiseveni. Mwii niwatanie nundu wa itambya yiu onakau waisye ukeetikilasya syana kuthi na moko na maau ni kana siikolwe ni umo woo. Mamutha nimaanie mawia; mauu makakuaa mwii lakini mavika vala makethaa maendete moko makatethasya wia ta kuseuvya maembe na ivanga. Maau na nyaai mathethisye wia muito wa kukua mwii, moko maimii ni kana liu wa munuka ukwatike. Maeo ma munuka makatanyukaa liu, na mayiutuma kwisila muluka nginya ivu. Ivu yikavinyiaa muyo usu w'onthe na kuwita tumitaluni tula tukatwaa u liu mamuthani kivathukany'o. Indi ivu yikoosaa kila kyatumiwa na kukiuwa ikoni yayo, na indi mwii ukathikaa muthangani nundu wa kwongela unou. Miti ikeanaa na kusyaa matunda; moko makatusaa amwe nthini wa matunda aya na kumekia kany'wa. Ii, kithyululu kya thayu.
Nginya mathau maaniw'e nesa; kwina, kutheka na kuneena kwanengiwe munuka; kusemba na (kukuna) muvila syatw'ikie sya maau; muvila wa kikavu wanengiwe moko, eka mauu nimo maile kusemba. Mauu manengiwe kusemba me moka. Kuaanw'a kuu kwa mawia kwatumie mwii uiva kute nyambu ila nene sya kitheka.
Ona vailye uu mamutha ma mwii meethia kuaanw'a kwa mawia no kuete ngusanisyo. Kyongo ki yiulu wa mwii kyai kisa kwiw'a takyo kinene kute mamutha aangi. Mamutha nimakindiliile kana kiivinya, kyongo kianene na mamutha aangi ala me nthi wakyo. Nundu wa kukindiliila undu mbeange, mamutha oonthe meew'anie woo na muyo ikew'ikaa undumwe ni mamutha oonthe. Makanisye munuka ila ukwasa kii na kia, ukethaa uineena ta mwii wonthe.

Kikamba
Peter Ngila
Very very here people travel with children and good things, like food from the store. People hurry to reach their destinations and homes. Good things and children are important to reach other places; strength, health, wealth and things that are beautiful. Children and good things are five. Five of those good things are combined into one thing. Days pass like dreams of a large house and everything big and strong; and they are completed with many things. Good things and children agree together.
Let us grow up well so that everyone can understand this; respect, kindness, discipline and faith; all people live well and understand this. See how good things and children come together to teach life's lessons. I have understood. Stories tell of other places far away; understand with ears, see with eyes and use hands skillfully.
This story tells of how others used other places that were captured with wisdom. Teach them to learn good things and children. Wisdom protects greatly because good things and children are taken little by little. Teach them to combine the power of learning good things and children.
Far away teach them to take intelligence forward and use it quickly. Far away teach them to associate with elders, to find peace here in the world of good things and children. They eat well when they have much peace among them. Today they tell stories of faraway lands and each person speaks about what they saw while traveling to find more peace. Let them tell other places to share peace and much tranquility. Children should be shown the path of finding their own peace; appreciate the good things on the path of growth and development.
And those good things help those things of children with love and care. Disputes happen among people who don't understand something properly. Other times good things and children become tired of helping others. Finally they are left with only peace. Is there much peace beyond that? Think about using other places and also being patient.
Faraway they say there is no dispute. Other places I believe are truly yours. See those others who are lost. Others are weak and helpless, showing how everything has been destroyed. Faraway those are the ones who will share more, showing how to take wisdom to eat well; peace is always found in every situation. Good things and children I believe.
Disputes are finished, agreements and unity. Other places everyone remembers helplessness seeing this, but some can still see it clearly in difficult situations. This is because everyone sees differently, some remember everything, others forget easily, and faraway he is the one who makes noise like a child.
Gathering has brought together the reasons for disputes today and tomorrow, bringing together what is possible and what is achievable. But sometimes good things are hidden from view, often they don't get market value or aren't recognized at first glance. These are the clans of the Kikuyu, Mbiti, Nzou, Ndwia, Ngamile, Ng'ombe of the big herd and Mboo of the small herd, Nzui, Mbaluku, Mbia and Mukoto. Also trees like Kiwuni, Nguu, Makuyu, Kingang'i, which provide shade. Also fruits like Nyaa mixed with seeds; branches of trees, Ngeli throughout the day. Mbwambui, mwinthooe, Ing'aui, Ngongoo walk around the plains or in the forest. The sound of birds is beautiful and calming. Ing'ala helps everyone to move forward. Nguli rejoices when one finds another. Sometimes trees and roots shake when one falls over another, place after place.
Faraway he encouraged disputes and said:
Let us start if we are given strength
Everything is ready
Let us invite others
Some and those who have seen things have been bothering me every time regarding the issues they raise. Some also bother me with the issue of a goat but let it be forgiven because of this land. This one among the men and women has traveled very far to see this land and understand it. These words are enough to cover all aspects of these issues and use all kinds of tools or just one thing concerning abundance, it's about resolving disputes. Let them try to discover and push forward. Things are enough to go to the museum to learn something from our ancestors. But some people don't want to hear what is said here and stumble around aimlessly. Some I have combined everything with issues and words. Forget about this land and understand it well; resolve other disputes too. Some I have shown another way; forget the paths of the forest; let us improve large structures to build houses; let us improve farms and understand them well; this matter is enough to show. Words can be understood everywhere on this earth where someone can explain this path. Some of those who have resolved things have gathered together to discuss their problems and some others, each thing has explained these words well. See how these words are like seeds that grow and understand the resolution of matters on this earth with days and years and these big trees standing firmly. Let us simplify things to resolve disputes.
The aspect of words regarding dispute resolution is important. Let the dispute be resolved quickly; some we should embrace everyone equally. Some with wealth and let us resolve the dispute of these words of tradition. Let some try to grow up, everything inside is manageable. Some hold onto the earth; their eyes are on the earth and they can understand it well; a story has many chapters and lessons; words and tools are scattered everywhere. Those who have resolved things say these things:
Nyah Nyaah, a song.
Go ahead.
Say Nyah.
Go ahead.
Let us rejoice (everywhere).
See how these things happen and some, this great event shows its importance. Many stories I have heard about this and understood it well. I am tired of many other things. This event tries to overcome obstacles but this big tree doesn't manage to overcome them. It tries to help but this story is remembered and understood through words. The aspect of the words of locking up. People wander around trying to lock themselves up in heaven and it seems like they are locked up with the power of words and this big event. But some who are locked up are bothered by many things and quick growth. I am confused and yet this person hasn't forgotten. Words are enough to understand the meaning of words; I remember, I recall; this whole event will be understood.
All words are rooted in the earth to understand relationships. Some lean on someone during difficult times, prayer or helping others. See how these things happen, everyone says something; this thing is big but it isn't ready, but some difficulties growing up make me forget and this thing too. Elders say others continue and lock themselves up but there is another thing; people look at foolishness, everything they see and do makes some people suffer greatly, especially those who want to grab. What is this? Darkness hides the truth!
Understanding the minds of elders is like grabbing a handful of sand with five fingers, the journey of some people and words. The way of suffering is like grabbing a handful of sand; appreciate what is good and despise what is bad (everything). But the finger that points out wrongdoing is also involved.
See how these things happen, people are judged based on their actions, elders speak well and some are seven. Everything is connected to the path of guidance, so don't be surprised when someone doesn't understand because of age. Elders have wisdom; words grow up but their roots remain locked, making it hard to hide secrets from the world and its surroundings. Words and stories show the way to growth, some believe it is possible to grab it. Stories about the past bring joy, and they cause trouble like a thorn in the flesh. The flesh remembers the pain of growth, some remember it but it is hidden from view. This memory brings peace, and it causes problems like cutting down trees in the forest. That memory destroys everything it touches and loses its shape, and everything becomes a story to tell. Trees bear fruit; some taste the fruits and become satisfied. Yes, this is the essence of life.
Everyone has a reason; to live, to lock oneself up and to speak truthfully; to help and (to nurture) the seeds of words; the seed of dryness is appreciated by some, just like words and helping. These truthful words are important. Growing up with wisdom causes everything to fall like rain but it is still strong.
See how those things lead to growing up with wisdom and gaining experience. Language is the strength of everything, it can build a big house for people. People are confused sometimes, language is powerful and people use it wisely. The ability to confuse others is good, everyone lives together peacefully. Let us celebrate our culture
