text:
WE VE mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩsĩ wathamĩĩe nthĩ ĩngĩ yĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ? Na waaĩsa kwĩkũlya makũlyo ta aa: 'Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa menda kũthi nthĩ ĩngĩ makatavany'e? Mekaa ata nĩ kana meyũmbanĩsye ũndũ ũsu? Nyie no nĩtonye kwĩka tamo?' Nzĩa nzeo ya kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ta asu nĩ kũneena na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asu. Kwoou ekai yu twĩw'e measya ata.
NĨ KYAŨ KĨTUMAA MENDA KŨTHI NTHĨ ĨNGĨ?
Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie wambĩĩa kũsũanĩa kũthi kũtavany'a nthĩ yĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a? Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Amy e na myaka 30 na kĩndũ na kwoo nĩ Amelika. Amy easya ta ũũ: "Naminie myaka mingĩ ngĩsũanĩa kũthi kũtavany'a nthĩ ĩngĩ, ĩndĩ noonaa ndesa kwĩanĩsya mũvango ũsu." Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie avĩndũa woni wake? Easya atĩĩ: "Mwakanĩ wa 2004 mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mũka ala matavanasya Belize nĩmambĩie nĩthi ngamakethye na ngĩkũna ũvainia namo vandũ va mwei ũmwe. Nĩneekie ũu, na nenda mũno mũvango ũsu. Ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe nĩnathamĩĩe Ghana ngatavanasye kw'o nĩ vainia."
Myaka mĩna mĩvĩtu Stephanie, ũla yu wangĩĩe myaka 30 na umĩte Amelika, nĩwasyaisye maũndũ make na asũanĩa ũũ: 'Ndi mũwau na ndi na andũ ngũĩthya. No nĩmũthũkũme Yeova mbeange wa ũndũ yu ngũmũthũkũma.' Kwĩthiana kũu nĩkwatumie ethĩwa na wendi wa kũthamĩĩa Ghana nĩ kana akatavany'e mũnango. Filip na mũka Ida me na myaka 60 na kĩndũ na nĩ mavainia ma kuma Denmark. Meethĩawa na wendi wa kũthi kĩsionĩ kĩ na vata wa atavany'a. Na kwoou nĩmambĩĩe kũmanthĩthya ũndũ makeanĩsya wendi woo. Filip easya: "Ĩla mwanya wesie kumĩla, ithyĩ twoonie no ta Yeova watwĩa: 'Nũu yu endai!'" Mwakanĩ wa 2008 nĩmathamĩĩe Ghana na matavany'a kw'o mbee wa myaka ĩtatũ.
Mwana-a-asa Hans na mũka Brook nĩ mavainia me na myaka 30 na kĩndũ na methĩawa Amelika. Mwakanĩ wa 2005 nĩmatetheeisye kũnengane ũtethyo ĩtina wa kĩla kĩuutani kĩthũku kyeetiwe Katrina. Maendeangĩe nĩmausũisye valũa nĩ kana matetheeasye myako nthĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩndĩ mayaaĩtwa. Hans aeleetye ũũ: "Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu ve ũvoo waumiw'e ũmbanonĩ mũnene ũla wawetie ũndũ Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti ũtaakananĩsya ĩla weeiwe ndeaka ĩkalũ. Vandũ va ũu eekie kũalyũla mũvango wake. Ndeto isu syatumie nĩmanya kana ti ũthũku kũvĩndũa mĩvango ĩla wĩĩ nayo ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova." (1 Mav. 17:1-4, 11, 12; 22:5-11) Nake Brook ongelete kwasya: "Yeova endaa tũkũnange mũango ũngĩ."
Hans na Brook nĩmanengiwe ngewa mbingĩ syĩ mũyo nĩ anyanyae moo ala matavanasya nthĩ ingĩ, na kĩu nĩkyatumie methĩwa na wendi wa kũthi nthĩ ĩngĩ makatavany'e kw'o. Mwakanĩ wa 2012 nĩmaendie nthĩ ya Ghana, na makũtavany'a myei ĩna maitetheesya kĩkundi kya kĩthyomo kya ala matew'aa. O na kau nĩmasyokie Amelika, maũndũ ala moonie maitavany'a Ghana nĩmatumie methĩwa na wendi mwingangĩ wa kwambaa kwĩanĩsya maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ mbee. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu nĩmatetheesye kwaka Ovisi wa Ũvonge wa Micronesia.
MATAMBYA ALA MOOSIE NĨ KANA MEANĨSYE MŨVANGO WOO
Weeyũmbanisye ata nĩ kana ũthamĩĩe kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a? Stephanie awetete ũũ: "Neekie ũkunĩkĩli makasetinĩ ma Mũsyaĩĩsya ala me na maũvoo maneenete ĩũlũ wa kũtavany'a kũndũ kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a." * Ongelete ndeto ii: "O na nĩnaneenie na atumĩa maitũ ma kĩkundi na mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko na mũka na namatavya wendi wakwa wa kũthamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ ngatavany'e kw'o. Na ĩndĩ mbee wa andũ asu onthe, mavinda maingĩ ngĩvoya nĩnamũtavasya Yeova mũvango wakwa." Na ũndũ ũngĩ Stephanie weekie nĩ kũendeea kũsisya mĩtũmĩĩle yake ya mbesa nĩ kana atonye kũvithĩlĩĩla imwe syĩmũtetheesya ĩla ũkathamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ.
Nake Hans aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩtwamũvoyie Yeova atũtongoesye nũndũ kĩla twendaa nĩ kũthi vala we ũkwenda tũthi. O na tũivoya nĩtwawetie nesa matukũ ala twendaa kwĩanĩsya mũvango witũ." Hans na mũka nĩmaandĩkĩie movisi ana ma ũvonge valũa. Ĩtina wa kũkwata ũsũngĩo kuma ovisi ũla wĩ Ghana, nĩmakũendie me na kĩeleelo kya kũkwĩkala myei ĩlĩ. Hans easya: "Twatanĩie mũno kũthũkũma na kĩkundi kĩla twaendie mũvaka twatw'a kwĩkalanga."
George na mũka Adria, makilyĩ kũvikya myaka 40 na kwoo nĩ Canada. Kĩla ĩvinda nĩmeethĩawa mesĩ kana Yeova nũathimaa motwi maseo ĩndĩ ti o kĩeleelo kĩla mũndũ wĩ nakyo. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu nĩmoosie matambya ma kwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kyoo. Ũndũ ũmwe meekie nĩ kũneena na mwĩĩtu-a-asa weetũmĩte Ghana na mamũkũlya makũlyo maingĩ. O na nĩmaandĩkĩe ovisi ũla wĩ Canada na ũla wĩ Ghana. Adria easya: "Na ĩndĩ nĩtwatatie kũsisya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩtheeangya kĩlasi mũnango." Kwosa matambya ta asu nĩkwatumie mavota kũthamĩĩa Ghana mwakanĩ wa 2004.
ŨNDŨ MEEKIE MAKWATWA NĨ MATHĨNA
Wakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna meva wathamĩĩa kũu, na weekie ata ũmakĩlye vinya? Amy awetete kana thĩna wa mbee waĩ kwĩw'a ayenda kũsyoka mũsyĩ. Aeleetye ũũ: "Kĩla kĩndũ kyaĩ kĩvathũkany'o na kĩla namanyĩĩte." Atethiw'e nĩ kyaũ? Asũngĩĩte ũũ: "Andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmangũnĩaa simũ makandavya ũndũ mew'aa mũyo kwona nĩtũmĩte ngatavany'e, na kĩu nĩkyatumie nĩkala nĩlilikene kĩeleelo kyakwa kya kũthama. Tũendeangĩe nĩnambĩĩe kũneena namo twenene vitionĩ. Nũndũ yu twaĩ tũtonya kwonana vau vitionĩ, nĩnaekie kwĩw'a ta me vaasa vyũ." O na Amy nũwetete kana kũtuma ndũũ na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wa kũu waĩ mũtavany'a kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nĩkwatumie aelewa syĩthĩo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Easya: "Mũnyanyawa ũsu nĩwe neekwatasya andetheesye ĩla nesa kwona maũndũ ndesĩ mayĩkwa nĩ andũ. Ũtethyo wake nĩwatumie nĩmanya maũndũ ala naĩle kwĩka na ala ndaĩle, na kĩu nĩkyandethisye mũno natavany'a na ũtanu."
George na Adria maĩtye kana ĩla mavikie Ghana oou meewie ta masyoka ĩla myaka ya tene. Adria easya: "Vandũ va kũvũa ngũa tũitũmĩa masinĩ twatũmĩaa ndoo. Ndatĩka sya kũua lĩu nĩ ta syongelekile mavinda ĩkũmi mbee wa ila twatũmĩaa twĩ kwitũ. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kavinda, maũndũ asu twonaa ta metu nĩtwambĩĩe kũmatanĩa o na weethĩa no tũtavye andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wamo." Brook easya: "O na kau ithyĩ mavainia nĩtwonaa mathĩna maingĩ, twĩkalaa twĩ eanĩe. Twatata kũlilikana maũndũ onthe maseo ala twonete tũtiawa na visa nzeo kĩlĩkonĩ ĩtesa kũla."
MOATHIMO ALA MAKWATĨTE ŨTHŨKŨMINĨ WOO
Nĩkĩ ũtonya kwĩa angĩ kana ũthũkũmi ũũ wa Ũsumbĩ nĩ mũseo? Stephanie aneenete akasya ũũ: "Nĩ ũtanu mwingĩ mũno kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ ũũkomana na andũ me na mea ma kwĩmanyĩsya ũla w'o nginya ũkethĩa meenda ũmamanyĩsye Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya. Kwĩtũma kĩsionĩ kĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a nĩ ũtwi ũmwe mũseo vyũ neekie!" Mwakanĩ wa 2014 Stephanie nĩwatwaiwe nĩ Aaron, na ũmũnthĩ ũũ methĩawa ovisinĩ wa ũvonge ũla wĩ nthĩ ya Ghana.
Nake Christine, ũla nĩ vainia wa kuma Germany na wĩ na myaka 30 na kĩndũ, easya: "Ũsu nĩ ũndũ mũndũ ũtanĩaa mũno." Christine atanamba kũthamĩĩa Ghana atavanasya nthĩ ya Bolivia. Asyokete akasya: "Nũndũ nĩkalaa vaasa na andũ ma mũsyĩ, nĩmwĩkwatasya Yeova andethye. Oyu nĩ na ngwatanĩo nzeo vyũ nake kwĩ ĩla naĩ nayo tene. O na nĩnĩtanĩaa mũno kwĩthĩwa ũmwe wa andũ ma Yeova me ngwatanĩo ĩtoneka vangĩ. Ũthũkũmi ũũ ũtumĩte nĩkwata moathimo maingĩ." Christine nũnatwaiwe nĩ Gideon na elĩ no maendeee kũtavany'a nthĩ ya Ghana.
Filip na Ida nĩmatũtavĩtye ũndũ meekie nĩ kana matetheesye amanyĩw'a moo ma Mbivilia meke maendeeo. Measya: "Tene tweethĩawa na amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia 15 kana o mbeange, ĩndĩ twamaola weethĩa maivĩtũka 10 nĩ kana tũtonye kũmamanyĩsya nesa." Kyu nĩkyatethisye amanyĩw'a asu? Filip easya: "Ve mwanake nemanyĩasya nake wĩtawa Michael. Twasomaa kĩla mũthenya na nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa aseũvasya nesa vyũ, twasomie ĩvuku Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya na mwei ũmwe. Ĩtina wa ũu, Michael nĩwatw'ĩkĩthiw'e mũtavany'a ũte mũvatise. Mũthenya ũ wa mbee kumaala ũtavany'a angũlilye, 'No ũndetheesye kũmanyĩsya amanyĩw'a amwe ma Mbivilia nĩ namo?' Namũsyaisye nĩseng'ete. Michael angeleisye kana aĩ anambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya na andũ atatũ, na kwoou nĩwendaa mũndũ amũtetheesye kũmamanyĩsya." Kwamba kũsũanĩa kĩĩ, atĩ vata ũla wĩ vo wa amanyĩsya nĩ mũnene ũkethĩa o na amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmatw'ĩkĩte amanyĩsya!
Amy nũwetete ũndũ wamanyie na mĩtũkĩ vata mũnene ũla wĩ kw'o. Easya: "Twavika Ghana oou twatavanisye ndũanĩ ĩmwe nini tũimantha ala methĩawa na thĩna wa matũ. Tũyaakwatya o mũndũ ũmwe ĩndĩ twakwatisye andũ nyanya ndũanĩ ĩsu yoka!" Ĩvindanĩ o yĩu Amy nĩwatwaanie na Eric, na ũmũnthĩ nĩ mavainia ma mwanya. Methĩawa kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kya ala matew'aa na me vau nĩmatetheeasya amwe ma andũ mbee wa 300, ala matũmĩaa kĩthyomo kĩu nthĩ ĩsu. Andũ asu nĩ atavany'a vamwe na angĩ mekwendeew'a. Namo George na Adria monaa kũtavany'a Ghana nĩkwatumie masama wĩa ũla ũtethaw'a nĩ amisonalĩ. Na kwoou nĩmatanie mũno ĩla meetiwe kĩlasi kya 126 kya Sukulu ya Ngileati! Yu tũĩ nĩ amisonalĩ nthĩ ya Mozambique.
WENDO NŨMATHANGAASYA
Nĩ ũndũ wĩkĩaa vinya mũno kwona Aklĩsto ma nthĩ ingĩ mayĩkĩa kĩthito matetheanĩsye na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma nthĩ ĩla mathamĩĩa wĩanĩ wa kũketha. (Yoa. 4:35) No twasye kana andũ ta 120 nĩmavatisawa kĩla kyumwa nthĩ ya Ghana. O ta Aklĩsto 17 ala mathamĩĩe nthĩ ya Ghana matetheesye ũtavany'a, atavany'a ngili mbingĩ mũno nthĩ yonthe "nĩmeĩthembaa na ngoo ya kwenda" nũndũ wa kũmwenda Yeova. Atavany'a asu maendaa kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Vate nzika, atavany'a ta asu meyumĩtye na ngoo ya kwenda nĩmatanĩthasya ngoo ya Yeova!—Sav. 110:3; Nth. 27:11.
^ kal. 9 Kwa ngelekany'o, sisya kĩlungu kĩĩ, "Je, Unaweza Kutumika Mahali Penye Uhitaji Mkubwa Zaidi wa Wahubiri?" na kĩĩ, "Je, Unaweza Kuvuka na Kuingia Makedonia?"—Ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 15/04/2009 na 15/12/2009.

translation:
DO WE have a child who resembles a white person among many people and has a large family from America? And she wonders about eating food like this: 'What makes me want to go and look for another family?' Perhaps she even thinks I messed up something? You don't seem to understand what I mean.' The reason for wanting to eat such food is to talk to children and their families. Let's see if we can help her somehow.
WHAT MAKES ME WANT TO GO AND LOOK FOR ANOTHER FAMILY?
What makes someone desire to separate and search for another family? A white person named Amy, 30 years old, lives in America. Amy said this: "I spent many years trying to find another family, but now I realize I need to accept this situation." What made her think of leaving her own family? She explained: "In 2004, a child and his mother traveled to Belize and told me they had met and befriended someone there with whom they shared a connection. I felt this way too, and I went along with the situation. After a year, I traveled to Ghana searching for him, and I found a connection."
For several years, Stephanie, also around 30 years old and living in America, shared her experiences and said: 'I am grateful and have friends. But I worship Jehovah, the God of all mankind.' To prove this, she traveled to Ghana hoping to find a family. Philip and his wife Ida, both around 60 years old and from Denmark, spoke about their experience traveling to find a family. They were encouraged by the thought of sharing their story. Philip said: "Even though we didn't have much money, we trusted that Jehovah would say: 'Go ahead!'" In 2008, I traveled to Ghana and stayed there for three years.
Hans and his wife Brook, both around 30 years old and from America, talked about when they helped those affected by Hurricane Katrina in 2005. They used their resources and even offered their home to those who needed it. Hans explained: "During that difficult time, we remembered the example of David, who showed great faith when he asked God for help. People saw how he honored God's name. We wanted to use our resources to show that we too trust in Jehovah." (1 Kings 17:1-4, 11, 12; 22:5-11) Then Brook added: "Jehovah helps us to be generous."
Hans and Brook were moved by what they saw—people helping each other despite having little themselves—and they felt motivated to do more. In 2012, they moved to Ghana, where they joined a group of volunteers assisting those recovering from a disaster. And although they missed America, they found that their work in Ghana was very rewarding and allowed them to share Bible truths with others. Later, they had the opportunity to serve on the island of Pohnpei in Micronesia.
OTHER THINGS THAT HELPED US TO BE GENEROUS
Have you ever wondered what can motivate us to be generous? Stephanie explained: "I realized that I could simplify my life and use some of the money saved to help others." * She added: "And I began to associate with people who were interested in spiritual things and who used their time and resources to help others. Seeing how happy they were encouraged me to do more." Also, Stephanie made it a point to focus on what she did have rather than on what she lacked.
Her husband, Hans, said: "We pray to Jehovah to guide us in our decisions and to help us see ways to expand our ministry." Hans and his wife wrote letters to branches and Bethel homes. They learned that there was a need for volunteers at the branch office in Ghana, and they applied. Hans explains: "We quickly came to appreciate the close-knit brotherhood we experienced while serving at the branch."
George and his wife, Adria, served as missionaries for 40 years in Canada. Every experience taught them to trust in Jehovah and to value the principles found in the Bible. One way they showed their faith was by simplifying their lives. For example, they corresponded with brothers in Ghana and received many encouraging letters. And they wrote letters to the branches in Canada and Ghana. Adria says: "We also made it a point to focus on what we had rather than on what we were missing." As a result of their efforts, they were able to move to Ghana in 2004.
SOMETHING HAPPENED THAT LED TO THIS
She was shocked by the news she heard, and did she ever feel helpless? Amy admits that at first she felt overwhelmed and wanted to give up. She explains: "Everything seemed so dark and hopeless." What helped her? She reflects: "The people in my congregation encouraged me to pray about it and reminded me that Jehovah understands how I feel. They urged me to continue speaking with others about the truth. Let us reason together and see what we can learn from this experience. The fact that we can confide in others helps us cope." And Amy admits that sending a letter to a dear brother who was facing a similar challenge helped her understand how things could be viewed differently. She says: "Sharing our feelings with others allows us to see that we are not alone in our struggles, and listening to others helps us realize that there is always hope."
George and Adria wondered if they would ever return to Ghana after spending ten years abroad. Adria says: "People often become attached to material possessions. It took a lot of courage to let go of the comforts we had enjoyed for so long. But we realized that true happiness does not come from wealth, but from helping others and living in harmony with God's will." Brook adds: "We have seen many wonderful things during our travels, and we have learned to appreciate what we have. We were able to overcome obstacles because we trusted in Jehovah and relied on his guidance."
IMPORTANT LESSONS LEARNED FROM THIS EXPERIENCE
Are you struggling with anxiety or depression? Stephanie shared the following: "It takes courage to reach out for help when you are feeling overwhelmed, but it is important to remember that you are not alone. Sharing your feelings with trusted friends and family members can bring relief. Speaking to someone about your concerns can make a difference." In 2014 Stephanie married Aaron, and this event led to a deeper appreciation for the culture and traditions of Ghana.
Also, Christine, who comes from Germany and is around 30 years old, says: "This is something I really enjoy." Christine decided to move to Ghana after serving in Bolivia. She explains: "I was able to associate with kind people, which strengthened my faith in Jehovah. This has been a very rewarding experience, and I am grateful for the opportunity to serve alongside fellow worshippers. This experience has helped me develop many qualities." Christine married Gideon and continues to serve in Ghana.
Philip and Ida found that offering Bible studies was effective when they visited people regularly. They say: "Sometimes we would start up to 15 Bible studies, but often only about 10 would continue long enough for us to help them make progress." What motivated them to persevere? Philip explains: "We met a man named Michael. We started studying with him every week, and soon we were using the book *What Does the Bible Really Teach?* with him. Because of this, Michael began inviting others to study. One day, after finishing our visit, he asked, 'Could you also help me study the Bible?' I readily agreed. Michael invited three more people to study, and eventually someone else helped him conduct those studies." Clearly, showing genuine interest in people and offering Bible studies can be very fruitful!
Amy realized something important about being successful in ministry. She says: "We moved to Ghana and initially struggled to find anyone interested in learning the truth. But we kept trying, and eventually we found one person who led us to many others!" In time, Amy and Eric started a congregation, and their circuit overseer commended them for their zealous activity. They helped over 300 people attend a special talk, and many of those people showed further interest. Others joined them in the ministry. For example, George and Adria decided to move to Ghana as pioneers. And now there is a class of 126 students attending the Kingdom School! You know, there are many missionaries from Mozambique.
GOOD NEWS TO SHARE
It is often possible to help people appreciate the Bible when they see fellow Christians showing love for one another and treating each other kindly. (John 4:35) So we were thrilled when over 120 Ghanaian brothers and sisters volunteered to assist with the Ghana branch's campaign to invite people to the Memorial. Also, 17 Ghanaian missionaries readily offered to participate, saying, "I am willing to go wherever I am needed," expressing their desire to support Jehovah's work. These missionaries are eager to return to the field and join the ranks of full-time preachers in the United States. Indeed, these volunteers demonstrate that willingness to serve brings joy to Jehovah!—Ps. 110:3; Prov. 27:11.

text:
Andũ maasya nĩvw'anene na ĩthe wakwa vyũ. Nĩilyĩ ĩthe wakwa na metho makwa matutĩtye ala make, o na andũ maasya nĩthekasya andũ o take. Ĩndĩ ve kĩndũ kĩngĩ ũnengete, nakyo nĩ ũtiĩwa wĩkalĩte nginya nzyawa ya mũonza. Ekai nĩmũelesye ĩũlũ wa ũtiĩwa ũsu.
Ũmae wakwa wa tene mũno weetawa Thomas1 * Williams asyaĩwe Horncastle, England, Matukũ 20, Mwei wa 1, 1815. Inyia wake akwie ĩtina wa myaka ĩlĩ, na kwoou we vamwe na syana ingĩ itatũ masyaanĩw'e maeiwe nĩ ĩthe woo, John Williams. John nĩwamanyĩisye Thomas wĩa wa mbwaũ, ĩndĩ Thomas endeeaw'a nĩ wĩa ũngĩ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu maũndũ ma ndĩni maendeee kũnyaĩĩka na mĩtũkĩ nthĩ ya England. Mũtavany'a weetawa John Wesley nĩwatiie kanisa weetawa Church of England nĩ kana ambĩĩsye kĩkundi kĩngĩ kya ũthaithi kyeetawa Society of Methodists, kĩla kyeekĩaa andũ vinya memanyĩsye Mbivilia na mayĩthĩwa me atavany'a. Momanyĩsyo ala Wesley wamanyĩasya manyaĩĩkie na mĩtũkĩ mũno, na mũsyĩ wa Williams nĩweetĩkĩlile na walũmya momanyĩsyo asu vyũ. Thomas nĩwatw'ĩkie mũtavany'a wa ĩkanisa ya Wesley, na eeyumya atw'ĩke misonalĩ ngalĩ ya South Pacific. Mwei wa 7, 1840, Thomas na kĩveti kyake Mary,2 nĩmaendie kĩthamanĩ kya Lakeba, * kĩla kĩ Fiji, kĩla ĩvindanĩ yĩu kyatwĩe andũ ala maĩsaa nyama sya andũ kana malyandũ.
KWĨKALANY'A NA MALYANDŨ
Thomas na Mary nĩmoomĩĩisye maũndũ maito myakanĩ yoo ya mbee me Fiji. Mathũkũmaa masaa maingĩ mũno mavĩte nĩ syũa kũndũ kũte maendeeo. O na nĩmakomanaa na maũndũ ma kũtelemya ta kaũ, andũ kwita na kũaa iveti ila ikw'ĩĩwe nĩ aũme, kũaa tũũkenge, na malyandũ. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana andũ ma kũu nĩmaleaa ũvoo ũla mamatavasya. Mary na mwana wake ũla mũkũũ, John, nĩmawaie mũno weethĩa me vakuvĩ kũkw'a. Mwakanĩ wa 1843, Thomas aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Natũlĩkĩte ngoo mũno. . . . Neew'aa nĩvikie mũthya wa maũndũ." Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Thomas na Mary nĩmeeyũmĩĩisye mũno na makwata vinya nũndũ wa kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova Ngai.
Ĩvindanĩ o yĩu, Thomas, nĩwaakie nyũmba Fiji atũmĩĩte ũmanyi ũla waĩ naw'o wa ũvundi. Nyũmba ĩsu nĩyo yaĩ ya mbee vyũ kwakwa na mwakĩle wa Europe. Nyũmba ĩsu yaakĩtwe yĩmbũkĩlye ũkethĩa yĩ na kũndũ kwa kũvĩtĩlya nzeve, na syĩndũ ingĩ syamyanakavĩtye na syendeeasya ekali ma Fiji mũno. Nyũmba ĩsu ĩtanamba kwakwa ĩkathela, Mary nĩwasyaie mwana wake wa kelĩ weetawa, Thomas Whitton3 Williams, ũla nĩ ũngĩ wa aaũmae makwa ma tene.
Mwakanĩ wa 1843, ũmae wakwa wa tene Thomas, nĩwatetheeisye kũalyũla Ũvoo Mũseo wa Yoana kwa kĩthyomo kya Fiji, o na kau wĩa ũsu ũyaĩ laisi. * Ĩndĩ aĩ na kĩnengo kya kũmanya mwĩkalĩle na syĩthĩo sya andũ (anthropologist) na aĩ na ũtonyi mũnene wa kũmanya andũ nesa kwa o kũmasisya. Nĩwaandĩkie nesa maũndũ ala wamanyĩte ĩũlũ wa andũ ma Fiji ĩvukunĩ yake, Fiji and the Fijians (1858), yĩla yĩeleetye nesa ũndũ andũ ma kũu mekalaa myakanĩ ya 1800 na kĩndũ.
Nũndũ wa kũtethya wĩa mũito kwa myaka 13 nthĩ ya Fiji, Thomas nĩwawaie mũno na kwoou we na mũsyĩ wake mathamĩĩa Australia. Ĩtina wa kũtethya wĩa mũseo, e mũtongoi wa ndĩni, Thomas akw'ĩĩie Ballarat, Victoria, mwaka wa 1891.
"THAAVU" WESTERN AUSTRALIA
Mwaka wa 1883, Thomas Whitton Williams na kĩveti kyake Phoebe,4 nĩmathamĩĩie Perth, Western Australia. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu mwana woo wa kelĩ Arthur Bakewell 5 Williams, aĩ na myaka kenda na nĩwe ũngĩ katĩ wa aaũmae makwa ma tene.
Ĩla Arthur wavikisye myaka 22, nĩwamanthie wĩa Kalgoorlie, taoni yenzawa thaavu ĩla yaĩ maili 370 (kĩlomita 600) ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa syũa ya Perth. E kũu nĩwasomie mavuku maandĩkĩtwe nĩ International Bible Students. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syeetawa ũu. O na ĩngĩ, nĩwakũlilye atwaĩawe ĩkaseti ya Zion's Watch Tower. Nũndũ Arthur nĩwendeeiw'e nĩ maũndũ ala wasomaa, nĩwambĩĩie kũtavya andũ ala angĩ maũndũ meũ ala weemanyĩĩtye, na nĩwatongoeasya maũmbano ma kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ũu nĩw'o wĩa mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũla ũendeee nthĩ ya Western Australia wambĩĩie.
O na ĩngĩ, Arthur nĩwatavisye mũsyĩ wake ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala weemanyĩasya. Ĩthe wake, Thomas Whitton, nĩweetĩkĩlanile na ũtwi wa Arthur wa kũthaitha vamwe na Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia (Bible Students) ĩndĩ, Thomas nĩwakwie ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ. O na inyia wake Phoebe, na eĩtu-a-inyia make Violet na Mary nĩmatw'ĩkie Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia. Violet nĩwatw'ĩkie mũtavany'a wa ĩvinda yonthe, kana vainia. Arthur aisye kana Violet nĩwe "vainia ũla waĩ mũseo vyũ na waĩ kĩthito Western Australia." Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Arthur aĩ na kyende aiweta ndeto isu ĩndĩ, ũw'o nĩ kana ngelekany'o nzeo ya kĩthito kya Violet nĩyaetie mosyao maseo kwa nzyawa ĩla yaatĩĩe ya Williams.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda Arthur nĩwatwaanie na athamĩĩa Donnybrook, taoni ĩvandawa matunda yĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya Western Australia. E kũu atw'ĩĩiwe ĩsyĩtwa, "Mũtumĩa Waũũkiw'e Nĩ 1914!" nũndũ wa kĩthito kyake kya kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa mawatho ma Mbivilia ala mawetete ĩũlũ wa mwaka ũsu. * Andũ maekie kũmũvũĩa ngũĩ ĩla Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe wambĩĩie. Mavinda maingĩ Arthur nĩwatavasya makasitoma ũvoo mooka ndukanĩ kwake. Eethĩawa aiĩte mavuku maeleetye Mbivilia ndĩlĩsyanĩ ya nduka yake vala andũ maĩ matonya kũmona. O na ĩngĩ, ndĩlĩsyanĩ ĩsu vaĩ kĩvwaũ kyaĩtye kana akanenga mũndũ ũla waĩ atonya kũĩkĩĩthya ũmanyĩsyo wa Ũtatũ atũmĩĩte Mbivilia vaondi 100, (100 pounds). Ũmanyĩsyo ũsu ndumĩte Mbivilianĩ na Arthur nĩwaleanaa naw'o vyũ. Vai mũndũ waaĩsa kwosa mbesa isu.
Nyũmba ya Williams ĩla yaĩ Donnybrook, nĩvo andũ meemanyĩĩasya Mbivilia na makekĩa maũmbano ma kĩkundi. Ĩtina Arthur nĩwaakie Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ kana vandũ va kũmbanĩaa taoninĩ ĩsu. Ĩsu yaĩ ĩmwe katĩ wa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ sya mbee ila syaakiwe Western Australia. O na Arthur e na myaka 70 na kĩndũ, eekĩaa suti na tai, na aithi na mbalasi ngũũ yeetawa Doll kũtavany'a kũndũ kũasa mũno kĩsionĩ kya Donnybrook.
Syana sya Arthur nĩsyaatĩĩie ngelekany'o ya ĩthe, ũla waĩ mũndũ wakilĩtye, wanengetwe ndaĩa, ĩndĩ waĩ kĩthito. Mwĩĩtu wake Florence6 aĩ mũmisonalĩ nthĩ ya India. Imwana syake, Arthur Lindsay7 na Thomas, syaĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi kwa myaka mingĩ o ta ĩthe woo.
MATUNDA ME MŨYO MEETAWA LADY WILLIAMS
Ũmae wakwa wa tene Arthur Lindsay Williams, nĩweesĩkĩe mũno, na andũ nĩmamwendete nũndũ aĩ tei. Nĩwanengete andũ ndaĩa, na nĩwamethukĩĩasya ĩla mekwenda kũneena nake. O na nĩwathaũkaa mathaũ ma kũtila na kwatũa mĩtĩ, na nĩwasindie mavinda 18 masindano ma kũtila mĩtĩ ala meekawa kĩsionĩ kyoo kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 12.
Ĩndĩ Arthur ndaaĩw'a mũyo ĩla kamwana kake ka myaka ĩlĩ keetawa Ronald8 (ũmae wakwa) katemie o vanini na ĩthoka mũtĩ wa mũevo ũla waĩ vakuvĩ na mũsyĩ. Inyia wa Ronald nĩwoovie nesa mũtĩ ũsu vala watemetwe, na ĩtina wesa kũsyaa maevo (apples) maĩ mũyo mwingĩ mũno. Maevo asu mambĩĩie kwĩtwa Lady Williams, na nĩvo maevo angĩ mesĩkĩe mũno metawa Cripps Pink maumie.
Ĩtina Ronald, kana Gramp, kwosana na ũndũ nĩmwĩtaa, nĩwambĩĩie kwĩka maũndũ angĩ ma vata. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ ũmae wakwa na sũsũ nĩmatetheeisye kwaka nyũmba ikonetye maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ sya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nthĩ ya Australia na Ithama sya Solomon. Yu ũmae wakwa Gramp e na myaka vakuvĩ 80, na no mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi, na nũtetheeasya wĩa wa kwaka na kũtũngĩĩa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ Western Australia.
KŨTŨMĨA ŨTIĨWA WAKWA NESA
Asyai maitũ Geoffrey 9 na Janice10 Williams, nĩmoonanisye kana nĩmendeeaw'a nĩ ũtiĩwa ũla mũsyĩ witũ waĩ naw'o kwa kwĩkĩa kĩthito mũno matũee nesa nĩ na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wakwa Katharine nĩ kana twendeew'e nĩ kũatĩĩa mĩao ya Kĩklĩsto. Nĩ na myaka 13, nĩnatwie kũatĩĩa maũndũ ala namanyĩĩtw'e. Nĩ ũmbanonĩ mũnene nĩneewie John E. Barr, wa Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ayĩa andũ ma mũika atĩĩ: "Mũikatate kũtũmĩa naĩ mwanya mũseo vyũ ũla mwĩ naw'o wa kũmũmanya na kũmwenda Yeova." Wĩoo ũsu nĩneeyumisye kũmũthũkũma Yeova, na ĩtina wa myaka ĩlĩ nambĩĩa ũvainia.
Ũmũnthĩ nĩnĩtanĩaa12 mũno kũtavany'a ĩvinda yonthe nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa Chloe,11 taoninĩ yĩnzawa mavia ma vata yĩtawa Tom Price, yĩ ngalĩ ya ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa ya Western Australia. Nĩtũtethasya wĩa mĩthenya ĩmwe nĩ kana twĩanĩsye mavata maitũ. Asyai makwa vamwe na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wakwa Katharine na mũũme Andrew, methĩawa me mavainia Port Hedland, maili ta 260 (kĩlomita 420) ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya vala nĩkalaa. Nĩ na ĩthe wakwa twĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi.
Nzyawa mũonza mbĩtu, ũmae wakwa wa tene mũno Thomas Williams nĩweeyumisye kũmũthũkũma Yeova Ngai. Ũtiĩwa ũsu wa mũĩkĩĩo na kũmũthũkũma Yeova nũvĩtĩle nzyawanĩ mbingĩ nginya wesa kũmbikĩa. Nĩw'aa nĩ mũathime mũno nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na ũtiĩwa ũsu mũseo vyũ wa kĩ-veva.
^ kal. 5 Namba ĩla yonanĩtw'e yosanĩte na visa ila syĩ ĩthangũnĩ ya 12 na 13.
^ kal. 6 Kĩthama kĩu mbeenĩ kyeetawa Lakemba, na kĩ ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa syũa ya Lau Group ĩla yĩ Fiji.
^ kal. 10 Mũmisonalĩ weetawa John Hunt nĩwaalyũlile mavuku maingĩ ma Ũtianĩo Mweũ Mbivilianĩ ya kĩthyomo kya Fiji ĩla yatumbĩthiw'e mwaka wa 1847. Mbivilia ĩsu yaalyũlilwe nesa nũndũ yĩ na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, "Jiova," ĩandĩkonĩ ya Maliko 12:36, Luka 20:42, na Meko ma Atũmwa 2:34.
^ kal. 16 Sisya ũvoo wa kwongeleela wĩ na kyongo "Mwaka wa 1914 Nĩ wa Vata Nthĩnĩ wa Wathani wa Mbivilia" nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? yĩla yĩtumbĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, o na no ũyĩkwate Kĩsesenĩ kya www.jw.org/kam.

translation:
The people were very sad and their land was full of sorrow. It was a dark land with bad things happening everywhere, and the people were oppressing others. There was another important thing that happened, and it is called the story of the missionary. This is how the story began.
His father's name was Thomas1 * Williams born in Horncastle, England, on January 20, 1815. His mother lived for many years, and he had three more siblings who grew up with him, his brother, John Williams. John knew Thomas from childhood, and Thomas always had a good heart.
This story will continue to be told with the history of England. A man named John Wesley left the Church of England and started another religious group called the Society of Methodists, which taught people to read the Bible and understand its teachings. Through Wesley's teaching, many people learned about history, and the spirit of Williams was strengthened by this knowledge. Thomas became a follower of Wesley's church, and he decided to go preach the gospel in the South Pacific. On July 7, 1840, Thomas and his wife Mary,2 went to the island of Lakeba, * an island in Fiji, where they continued to teach people about God and his commandments.
IN CONNECTION WITH COMMANDMENTS
Thomas and Mary spent many years working among the people of Fiji. Often they would spend many hours visiting homes. And they were concerned about helping people overcome their problems, being honest, and following commandments. This is because the people needed help to improve their lives. Mary and her eldest son, John, often helped those who were in need. In 1843, Thomas wrote: "I have been very busy. . . . I am always thinking about the work." Despite this and everything else, Thomas and Mary remained dedicated and eager to worship Jehovah God.
This story, Thomas, shows how he used his skills to build houses in Fiji. These houses were different from the traditional Fijian houses and were built like European houses. These houses were constructed with nails and tools, and many things were done differently than the way Fijians usually did them. The house was almost finished when Mary gave birth to her youngest son, Thomas Whitton3 Williams, who later became a skilled carpenter.
In 1843, young Thomas, the carpenter, began studying the history of Fiji, and he soon became interested in it. * He also became acquainted with an anthropologist and developed a great interest in learning about the people and their customs. He wrote down what he learned in a book called Fiji and the Fijians (1858), which provides valuable information about the life of the Fijian people during the 1800s.
After spending 13 fruitful years in Fiji, Thomas returned home with his family to Australia. After leaving missionary work, in December, Thomas moved to Ballarat, Victoria, in 1891.
"THE HAVEN" WESTERN AUSTRALIA
In 1883, Thomas Whitton Williams and his wife Phoebe,4 moved to Perth, Western Australia. With them came their youngest son Arthur Bakewell 5 Williams, who was eight years old and also became a skilled carpenter.
When Arthur reached the age of 22, he moved to Kalgoorlie, a mining town 370 miles (600 kilometers) east of Perth. There he studied pamphlets published by the International Bible Students. This group later became known as Jehovah's Witnesses. And often, he distributed recordings from Zion's Watch Tower. Because Arthur was impressed by what he read, he told others about the things he was learning, and he organized meetings for Bible study. This is how the large organization of Jehovah's Witnesses continued to expand throughout Western Australia.
And further, Arthur shared his faith with his family. His father, Thomas Whitton, came into contact with Arthur's associates among the Bible Students, and Thomas embraced the truth. Along with his wife Phoebe, and their daughters Violet and Mary, they became Bible Students. Violet especially took an active interest in the entire work, or ministry. Arthur said that Violet was "the minister who traveled most extensively and effectively throughout Western Australia." It happened that Arthur and his friend went on a journey together, and it was during this trip that Violet's influence extended even to the remote area of Williams.
Arthur's ministry led him to Donnybrook, a town known for its abundant fruit production in the southwest of Western Australia. He published a pamphlet titled, "The Watchman Announces 1914!" which explained his understanding of biblical prophecy concerning the end of the world. *People were eager to hear what the Governing Body of Jehovah's Witnesses had to say. Many times Arthur would visit customers and leave literature at their homes, and often people would find it difficult to refuse it. And furthermore, sometimes they would offer a reward of up to £100 (100 pounds) to anyone who could refute the teachings of God as presented through the Bible. This teaching benefited the Bible students and Arthur associated closely with them. There was someone who offered to pay this amount.
The Williams family home in Donnybrook was where people gathered to study the Bible and hold meetings. Arthur's ministry took him to the Williams home and he joined those meeting there. It was one of the homes used by the Bible Students in Western Australia. And Arthur, being about 70 years old, dressed neatly and cleanly, and traveled with a horse named Doll to cover territory around Donnybrook.
Arthur's children were educated privately, unlike most people, who attended public schools, due to his beliefs. His wife Florence6 was originally from India. His sons, Arthur Lindsay7 and Thomas, served as missionaries for many years in various places.
FRUIT FROM THE LADY WILLIAMS GARDEN
The eldest son of the late Arthur Lindsay Williams, was well-known, and people remembered him because he was kind. He treated people fairly, and he was willing to listen to others and discuss matters with them. And he was skilled in grafting and pruning trees, and he planted 18 acres of grafted trees which became an orchard for the farm over 12 years.
When Arthur was alive, his young son, about eight years old, named Ronald8 (the eldest son), would often go with him when inspecting the apple trees. Ronald enjoyed seeing the trees bear fruit, and he liked eating apples from the orchard. Those apples were known as Lady Williams, and they were a variety called Cripps Pink apples.
Ronald, also known as Gramp, continued what his father started, and he encouraged others to do so. For many years, the eldest son and his family supported the work of Jehovah's Witnesses in Australia and the Solomon Islands. Now the eldest son Gramp is over 80 years old, still serves as a missionary, and continues to support the work and preach in Western Australia.
SUPPORTING HIS FAMILY THROUGH FRUIT GROWING
My parents, Geoffrey 9 and Janice10 Williams, decided or felt led to use the income from their orchard to help us children, especially our sister Katharine, to attend Christian meetings. At age 13, I began attending those meetings regularly. I greatly appreciated an article by John E. Barr, of The Watchtower Bible and Tract Society, which said: "Parents can help their children develop a love for Jehovah by spending time with them and helping them get to know Him." That encouragement helped me to strengthen my faith in Jehovah, and in the following years, it grew stronger.
I remember vividly traveling with my parents and my sister Chloe,11 on trips to remote places like Tom Price, in the Pilbara region of Western Australia. We enjoyed visiting our friends there. My parents, along with our sister Katharine and her husband Andrew, later moved to Port Hedland, some 260 miles (420 kilometers) inland. They continue to serve as part of a circuit.
My maternal grandfather, Thomas Williams, also strengthened his faith in Jehovah God. This example of dedication and strengthening one's faith in Jehovah motivated many others in my family to do the same. It was truly inspiring to see this happen.
^ kal. 5 These verses are related to the visas mentioned in paragraphs 12 and 13.
^ kal. 6 The island is called Lakemba, and it is part of the Lau Group islands of Fiji.
^ kal. 10 A missionary named John Hunt documented much about the work of the Seventh-day Adventist Church in Fiji, which was established in 1847. This church used the name "Jehovah" for God, as seen in Mark 12:36, Luke 20:42, and Acts 2:34.
^ kal. 16 For more information on the topic "Why 1914 Marked the Beginning of the Time of the End," see the publication Your Bible Answers Questions, published by Jehovah's Witnesses, or visit our website at www.jw.org/kam.

text:
Ĩla mũndũ woona nũtonya kũũmĩa, ekwatĩlaa vandũ. Ĩndĩ nyie nditonya kwĩka ũu nũndũ ndyĩthĩawa na moko. Naĩ na myaka mũonza ĩla moko makwa matililwe nĩ kana thayũ wakwa ũtangĩĩwe.
Inyia wakwa aĩ na myaka 17 ĩla wanzyaie mwaka wa 1960. Nake ĩthe wakwa atũtiie o na ndambĩte kũsyawa. Nĩ na inyia wakwa twekalaa na ũmau na ũsũa taoninĩ nini yĩtawa Burg, ĩla yĩ kĩsionĩ kyeetawa German Democratic Republic, kana East Germany. Andũ aingĩ mayaĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai, o na andũ ma mũsyĩ witũ maĩkĩĩaa oou. Tũyoonaa Ngai e wa vata kwitũ.
Nĩendeee na kwĩana, nĩnatanaa mũno nũndũ ũmau nĩwambendete. Nĩwamanyĩisye kwĩka maũndũ maingĩ ta kũlĩsa mĩtĩnĩ ngatilange ngava. Na nũndũ naĩ o kamwana, nĩnatanĩaa maũndũ asu mũno. Nekalaa nĩ mũtanu, na neekaa maũndũ ndeũkĩa na ndeũmaka.
VE MŨISYO WAALYŨLILE THAYŨ WAKWA
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩ na myaka mũonza, nĩkweekĩkie ũndũ wa kũmakya mũno. No ĩndĩ naĩ mwaka wa kelĩ kuma nambĩĩa kũthi sukulu. Mũthenya ũmwe numĩte sukulu, nĩnalĩsile kĩtuĩ kya sitima. Ĩla nalĩsile ũtũlu wa vuti 25 (mita 8), nĩnakũniwe nĩ sitima waĩ na mwaki mwingĩ mũno. Nesie kũvĩndũka nĩ sivitalĩ na weethĩa nĩĩw'a ta nde na moko. Na nũndũ moko asu mavĩte naĩ mũno vyũ, yaĩ no nginya matilwe nĩ kana maikatume mwĩĩ ũla ũngĩ wambĩĩa kũwaa. Inyia wakwa, ũmau na ũsũa nĩmaũmĩiw'e mũno nĩ ũndũ ũsu. Ĩndĩ nũndũ naĩ o mũnini, ndyamanyaa nesa ũndũ maũndũ makethĩwa mailyĩ nũndũ wa kũtilwa moko onthe.
Ĩtina wa kuma sivitalĩ, nĩnasyokie sukulu. Syana nĩsyanthekeaa, ikanzukumanga, na kũngimanga nũndũ ndyaĩ nĩtonya kwĩsiĩĩa. Neew'aa ndiũmĩa mũno nũndũ wa kũthĩnw'a na kũtavw'a ndeto sya kĩvũthya. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, nĩnatwaiwe sukulu ya syana ila syĩ na mathĩna ma mamutha ĩla yeetawa Birkenwerder School for the Disabled. Na nũndũ sukulu ĩsu yaĩ vaasa na mũsyĩ, inyia wakwa, ũmau na ũsũa mayaĩ matonya kũka kũmbona, na kwoou namonaa o ĩla twavinga sukulu. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩkũmi ĩla yaatĩĩe, neanie nĩ vaasa namo.
KWĨANA NDE NA MOKO
Nĩneemanyĩisye kwĩka maũndũ maingĩ nĩtũmĩĩte maaũ makwa. Kwasũanĩa ũiya lĩu ũkwete kĩsiko kana ũma na syaa sya maaũ! Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũmwe neemanyĩisye kwĩkaa nĩtũmĩĩte maaũ makwa. O na ĩngĩ, nĩneemanyĩisye kũswakaa maeo na kũsanũa nzw'ĩĩ nĩtũmĩĩte syaa sya maaũ. O na ĩla ngũneena na andũ, nĩnatũmĩaa maaũ makwa ĩla ngũelesya maũndũ. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu, maaũ makwa nĩmo mathũkũmaa ta moko.
Nĩ vakuvĩ kũvikya myaka ĩkumi na ĩtatũ, nĩnendete mũno kũsoma mavuku ala maelesya ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma saenzi ala masũanĩawa ta matonya kwĩkĩka ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte (science fiction). Mavinda amwe nasũanĩaa kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ngethĩwa na moko maseũvĩtw'e kwa nzĩa yĩ mwanya nginya ũkethĩa no meke kĩla ũndũ w'onthe. Nambĩĩie kũnyw'a sikala nĩ na myaka 14. Nanyw'a sikala, neew'aa nĩ mũndũũme o ta ala angĩ. No ta naasya atĩĩ: 'O nakwa no nĩke ũu. Sikala ĩnyusawa nĩ andũ aima, methĩwe me na moko kana mai na moko.'
Nĩnakwatene mũno na maũndũ ala meekawa kĩsionĩ kitũ. Nĩnalikile kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma mũika kĩla kyeetawa Free German Youth, na kyatetheeaw'a nĩ silikalĩ. Naĩ mũandĩki kĩkundinĩ kĩu na kĩu kyaĩ kĩanda kyanengetwe ndaĩa kĩsionĩ kitũ. O na ĩngĩ, nĩnalikile kĩkundinĩ kya kwina, nĩnaandĩkaa mavuku ma voemu na nĩnendete kũisoma, na nĩnathaũkaa mathaũ ma andũ ala me na mathĩna ma mamutha. Ĩtina wa kũmanyĩw'a maũndũ maingĩ, nĩnambĩĩie kũthũkũma kambunĩnĩ ĩla yaĩ taoninĩ yitũ. Nĩendeee na kwĩana, nĩneekĩaa moko ma kũseũvya nũndũ nendaa kwĩthĩwa ta andũ ala angĩ.
ŨNDŨ NEEMANYĨISYE ŨW'O WA MBIVILIA
Mũthenya ũmwe neteele kũlĩsa ngalĩ ya mwaki nĩthi wĩanĩ, ve mũndũũme wookie kũneena nakwa. Tũendeee na kũneena, angũlilye kana nĩnonaa ve ĩvinda yĩkavika Ngai andetheesye nĩthĩwe na moko makwa ĩngĩ. Ĩkũlyo yĩu yatumie nĩseng'a mũno. Nĩnendaa nĩthĩwe na moko makwa ĩngĩ, ĩndĩ noonaa ũndũ ũsu ta ndoto na ũtatonyeka! Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ndyaĩkĩĩaa kana kwĩ Ngai. Nũndũ wa ũu, kuma mũthenya ũsu ndyendaa kwĩsa kũkomana na mũndũũme ũsu.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, ve mũndũ mũka twathũkũmaa ĩmwe wanthokisye mũsyĩ kwoo. Tũendeee o na kũnyw'a kaawa, asyai make nĩmambĩĩie kũneena ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kwĩw'a kana Ngai e ĩsyĩtwa. (Savuli 83:18) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, naisye na ngoo atĩĩ: 'O na ethĩwa Ngai etawa ata, nyie nĩnĩsĩ kũi Ngai. Na nĩngũĩkĩĩthya andũ aa kana ũu nĩ w'o.' Na nũndũ ndyaĩ na nzika ĩũlũ wa mawoni makwa, nĩneetĩkĩlile kũneenea Mbivilia vamwe namo. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũsengy'a nĩ kana ndyaĩ nĩĩkĩĩthya kana kũi Ngai.
O ũndũ twaendeee kũneenea kwa ũliku ĩũlũ wa mawathani ala me Mbivilianĩ, now'o mawoni makwa ma kana kũi Ngai maendeeie mathelete. Mawathani maingĩ ala me Mbivilianĩ nĩmeanĩie o na kau maandĩkĩtwe myaka maana maingĩ kana ngili mbingĩ mĩvĩtu. Ĩvindanĩ yĩmwe tũineenea Mbivilia, nĩtwasianĩisye maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na wathani ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo kĩlungu kya 24, Luka kĩlungu kya 21, na 2 Timotheo kĩlungu kya 3. O tondũ ndakĩtalĩ ũtũmĩaa maũndũ ala waelew'a nĩ mũwau kũmanya kĩla waĩle kũthima, now'o maũndũ ala maeleetw'e nthĩnĩ wa mawathani asu mandetheeisye kũmanya kana tũilyĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩla Mbivilia yĩtaa 'mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo.' * Maũndũ asu manzeng'isye mũno nũndũ nĩnoonaa mayĩkĩka, ĩndĩ ndyamanyaa kana maendeee kwĩanĩsya wathani wa Mbivilia.
Naĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana neemanyĩasya ũla w'o. Nĩnambĩĩe kũmũvoya Yeova Ngai na naeka kũnyw'a sikala o na kau namĩnyw'ĩte mbee wa myaka ĩkũmi. Naendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia vakuvĩ mwaka ũmwe. Matukũ 27, Mwei wa 4, 1986, navatisĩiwe kalaĩnĩ kanene kaĩ vandũ veevithanĩtye nũndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu wĩa wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova waĩ mũkũne maluvuku kĩsionĩ kya East Germany.
KŨTETHEESYA ANDŨ ANGĨ MAMANYE ŨW'O
Nũndũ wĩa witũ waĩ mũkũne maluvuku, twoombanaa twĩ ikundi nini mĩsyĩ kwa andũ na kwondũ wa ũu neesĩ o Ngũsĩ nini. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩkweethĩiwe ũndũ ndataĩĩe, silikalĩ nĩyambĩtĩkĩlilye nĩthi West Germany, vala Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itaĩ ngũne maluvuku. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kũthi maũmbanonĩ manene ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na kwonana na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ngili mbingĩ. Ndyaĩ naaona ũndũ ta ũsu.
Ĩtina wa Ũkũta wa Berlin (Berlin Wall) kũvalũka, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyavetewe maluvuku. Yu twaĩ tũtonya kũmũthaitha Yeova Ngai twĩ na ũthasyo. Nĩnendaa kwongeleela masaa ala natũmĩaa ũtavany'anĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩnakĩaa kũneena na andũ ndesĩ. Neew'aa ndaĩlĩte nũndũ wa wonzu ũla naĩ naw'o, na nũndũ nĩ mũnini naeeiwe kũla kwĩkalaa andũ ala mena thĩna wa mamutha ma mwĩĩ. Ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1992, nĩnatatie kũtavany'a masaa 60 mweinĩ ũmwe. Nĩnatavanisye nesa na ũu watuma nĩthĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ. Kwondũ wa ũu, nĩnatwie kwĩkaa ũu kĩla mwei kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩtatũ.
Kĩla ĩvinda nĩnĩlilikanaa ndeto ii syĩ Mbivilianĩ: 'Nũũ ũla mwonzu, nakwa ndi mwonzu?' (2 Akolintho 11:29) Nũndũ nĩ na kĩlĩko na wasya, nĩnĩtataa ũndũ ndonya kũtetheesya angĩ o na ethĩwa nĩnĩthĩawa na wonzu wa mwĩĩ. Nũndũ ndi moko, nĩnĩthĩawa ndonya kũmew'ĩa tei andũ ala me na mawonzu ma mwĩĩ. Nĩnĩsĩ ũndũ mũndũ wĩw'aa aũmĩa ngoo ĩla ũkwenda kwĩka ũndũ na ũyĩthĩa ndatonya kũwĩka. Nĩnĩtataa ũndũ ndonya nĩmekĩe vinya ala mekwĩw'a ũu. Kũtetheesya andũ ala angĩ kwa nzĩa ĩsu nĩkũtumaa nĩthĩwa nĩ na ũtanu.
YEOVA NŨNDETHEEASYA KĨLA MŨTHENYA
Kwa w'o, ve mavinda amwe nĩw'aa nĩtũlĩkĩte ngoo. Nĩnĩw'aa ndyenda kwĩthĩwa nĩilyĩ andũ ala angĩ. O na kau nĩnĩthĩawa ndonya kũtethya mawĩa ma kĩla mũthenya, nĩkuaa ĩvinda yingĩ, na nĩnĩtũmĩaa vinya mwingĩ kwĩ ũndũ naĩle kwĩka takethĩwa ndyĩthĩawa na wonzu wa mamutha. Ndeto ii nĩsyo imbĩkĩaa vinya kĩla mũthenya: 'Nĩndonya maũndũ onthe nthĩnĩ wake ũla ũndonyethasya.' (Avilivi 4:13) Yeova nũnengae vinya wĩanĩtye wa kũtethya maũndũ ma kĩla mũthenya. O na nĩnĩmanyĩte kana Yeova ndaaeka kũndetheesya, na nĩkyo kĩtumi ndakesa kũeka kũmũthũkũma.
Yeova nũngathimĩte kwa kũnenga mũsyĩ, na ũndũ ũsu nĩ wa mwanya nũndũ ĩla naĩ mũnini, o na nĩ wa mũika, ndyaaĩkala na andũ makwa ma mũsyĩ. Yu nĩ na kĩveti kĩseo mũno kĩtawa Elke, na nĩkĩmbendete na kĩ tei. O na eka ũu, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova milioni mbingĩ nĩsyĩthĩĩtwe syĩ ũndũ ũmwe na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa makwa, ũu nĩ kwasya kana nthĩ yonthe, twĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ ũmwe.
Nĩnĩkiakiaw'a mũno nĩ watho wa Ngai wa kũtw'a "maũndũ onthe meũ," nthĩnĩ wa Nthĩ Nzaũ. Na ũmwe wa maũndũ ala Ngai ũkatw'a meũ nĩ kũnenga moko makwa. (Ũvuan'yo 21:5) Nĩnĩeleawa nesa watho ũsu nalilikana maũndũ ala Yesũ weekie ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwavoisye mũndũ ũmwe vau kwa vau ũla waĩ mwonzu maaũ, o na ĩvinda yĩla mũndũ ũmwe watililwe kũtũ, Yesũ nĩwamũkiitie na o vau kwa vau avoa. (Mathayo 12:13; Luka 22:50, 51) Mawatho ma Yeova na syama ila Yesũ weekaa nĩtumaa nĩĩkĩĩa vyũ kana o mĩtũkĩ nĩkilye nĩnavetewa mawonzu onthe ma mwĩĩ.
Ũathimo ũla mũnene vyũ naakwata nĩ kũmũmanya Yeova Ngai. Yeova nĩwĩthĩĩtwe e Ĩthe wakwa na Mũnyanyae wakwa, na nĩwe ũngiakiasya na akanenga vinya. Nĩw'aa o tondũ Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti weew'aa. Aandĩkie atĩĩ: 'Yeova nĩwe vinya wakwa, nũndetheeasya. Kwondũ wa ũu ngoo yakwa nĩtanaa mũno.' (Savuli 28:7) Ndeto isu nĩ nzeo mũno na nĩsyo ngwenda kũkwata nĩlũmĩtye vyũ thayũnĩ wakwa w'onthe. Ngekalaa nĩilũmĩtye vyũ o na kau ndi moko.

translation:
When a person remembers, they meet people. I also remember this thing with someone. And with years, when two children were born, my father was transferred.
My father was 17 years old when he completed his schooling in 1960. Later my father started working as a soldier. I have a father who lived with peace and tranquility in a city called Burg, but it wasn't called German Democratic Republic, or East Germany. Many people believed or prayed to God, and our parents also believed in Him. We know God is watching over us.
I continued to grow up, and I lost many things because of age. I realized many things while trying to live until today. And with age, I forgot many things. But I remain with good and bad memories.
REMEMBER YOUR FATHER'S STORY
One day, when I was older, I understood the importance of life. Then, in 1962, I went back to school. One day at school, I finished building a toy car. But I finished a section of about 25 feet (8 meters), and I collided with a car with a lot of force. I tried to avoid it, but it was too late and hit me hard. And then something happened which I will never forget, it was like an accident where someone wanted to kill me. My father, peace and tranquility were very important to him. Because with age, I understand that many things happen in life, some are good and others are bad.
It's like sometimes being given a chance to live. The pain of life, peace and tranquility are very important, they are a great thing. I think with age, I realize that many things are done intentionally in life.
The difficulty of life is not easy, I continued going to school. Later, I became stubborn, rebellious, and did things that I shouldn't have done. I got involved in many problems because of trying to steal and destroy other people's property. The difficulty of avoiding trouble, I went to school again but it was a special school for disabled children called Birkenwerder School for the Disabled. And this school was also far away, my father, peace and tranquility made it difficult to go there, and he worried about us going to school. After ten years of hardship, I finally managed to cope.
TO LIVE WITH PEOPLE
I have learned many things through my experiences. To appreciate what little you have, whether it's good or bad! This is one thing I have learned through my experiences. Also, I have learned to forgive and forget mistakes through my experiences. And even when I am with people, I use my experiences to teach them. For now, my experiences are helping two families.
It took me thirteen years to understand that I needed to read books that would help me understand the world of science and technology (science fiction). Some stories I read seem impossible, but someone somewhere has thought about everything. I started drinking alcohol when I was 14. When I drank alcohol, I felt like a different person than usual. And then I realized: 'This is how it feels. Alcohol makes people happy, whether alone or together.'
I got involved in various organizations. I joined an organization called Free German Youth, which was very popular. I wrote articles for this organization more and more often, and they were published. Also, I joined a sports club, I played volleyball and I liked reading, and I spent time with people who had interesting ideas. To learn more things, I decided to go to a school that wasn't ours. I continued playing, I met people who inspired me to think differently from others.
THIS IS THE STORY OF MY LIFE
One day I woke up feeling strange, like someone was calling me. We continued talking, wondering if this was a dream God sent us with some purpose. This feeling made me think deeply. I felt like something was happening, something unreal! And I wondered if I should pray to God. Because of this, today I want to meet that person.
Because of the dream, a man among us showed great courage. Let's continue drinking coffee, so I can tell you about Jehovah God. That is my reason for living, to praise God always. (Psalm 83:18) And because of this, I say with conviction: "Even though God is powerful, you must praise God. And I will remind people that this is true." And with this hope and with the help of these thoughts, I am happy to talk about the Bible with you. And when it comes to praying, I also remember to pray to God.
And we continue talking about the important things in the Bible, and these thoughts about God continue to strengthen us. Many passages in the Bible teach us about many important things. Because we live according to the Bible, we have learned about the things that will happen in the future, like what Matthew chapter 24, Luke chapter 21, and 2 Timothy chapter 3 describe. So, since I want you to understand clearly, I will explain these things so you can know how to think, and these things that are happening show that we are living in the time the Bible calls "the last days." * These things are very interesting, and I believe they will help you to better understand the teachings of the Bible.
I also hope that you will come to appreciate this. I thank Jehovah God and I am still enjoying life after many years. I continue learning from the Bible every year. On April 27, 1986, I was appointed an elder among many brothers who were part of the congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses in a large city in East Germany.
TO HELP OTHERS TO KNOW THIS
Like our fellow believers, we often ask ourselves what more we can do to help people and to tell them about this good news. One day, I was given an assignment—I was sent to serve in West Germany, where Jehovah's Witnesses had a large organization. This allowed me to visit many large assemblies of Jehovah's Witnesses and meet many brothers and sisters. And I saw something remarkable.
After the fall of the Berlin Wall, Jehovah's Witnesses flourished. We were able to preach to Jehovah God with greater freedom. I continued to spend much time in the ministry and used the door-to-door work. At times, I found it difficult to speak to people. But I remembered the example of those faithful ones who persevered despite facing opposition. In January 1992, I reached a goal of spending 60 hours each month in the ministry. This made me very happy, and it helped me to stay active. Because of this, I was able to maintain this routine for three years every month.
Each month I asked myself this question: "Am I zealous, or am I becoming lukewarm?" (2 Corinthians 11:29) Although I had weaknesses, I was determined to remain diligent and I was encouraged by seeing the zeal of others. Like them, I wanted to be an example and not discourage others with my lukewarmness. I realized that a person can become discouraged if he focuses on his difficulties instead of on what he can accomplish. I was determined to avoid letting that happen to me. Remaining busy in the ministry with others helped me to stay motivated. It encouraged me to continue being zealous.
JEHOVAH ENCOURAGES EACH ONE OF US
For instance, there were times when I felt overwhelmed. I wanted to give up trying to encourage others. But then I remembered that it is important to speak about the good news to everyone, and I would find strength to keep going and I used much time to make sure that I did not allow discouragement to rob me of my joy. This thought comforted me each time: "I may have many problems, but you deliver me from them all." (Psalm 4:13) Jehovah gives us the strength we need to face our challenges. And I know that Jehovah will never abandon me, and that is why I strive to remain loyal to him.
Jehovah has also strengthened me through my brothers and sisters, and their support is very comforting, and they set a fine example, and I enjoy associating with them. For example, I recently met a sister named Elke, and she impressed me with her positive attitude. Also, at the recent assembly, millions of Jehovah's Witnesses around the world united as one family, showing that despite differences, we can work together harmoniously.
I appreciate that God wants to give us "everything that is good," according to his wisdom. One way God shows his goodness to us is by giving us free will. (Proverbs 21:5) I understand this more fully now because of what Jesus did for us. For example, he healed a man on the Sabbath, and when some people criticized him for doing so, Jesus defended the man and healed him again. (Matthew 12:13; Luke 22:50, 51) The principles that Jehovah and Jesus taught help us to reason correctly and to make wise decisions.
The most important thing I have learned is to know Jehovah God. Jehovah reveals himself through his Son and through his organization, and he helps us to find strength. He is the one who inspired King David to write: "Jehovah is my strength and my deliverer. My heart trusts in him, and he helps me." (Psalm 28:7) So this thought comforts me greatly and motivates me to continue serving him wholeheartedly. As long as I serve him faithfully, I too will be blessed.

text:
Ũtonya kũtw'ĩka mũnyanyae wa Ngai ata?
Ũkananĩsya wa Satani ũkũkonetye ata?
Nĩ mwĩkalĩle wĩva ũtamwendeeasya Yeova?
Ũtonya kwĩkala mwĩkalĩle ũmwendeeasya Ngai ata?
1, 2. Nengane ngelekany'o sya andũ amwe ala Yeova wamatalile ta anyanyae.
ŨTONYA kũnyuva mũndũ ũilye ata ethĩwe mũnyanyau? No wende mũndũ wĩna mawoni, na mwĩkalĩle ũvw'anene na waku, na wendete maũndũ ala wendete. Na nũtonya kwendeew'a nĩ mũndũ wĩna ndaĩa nzeo ta ũlũngalu na tei.
2 Ngai nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ainyuva andũ methĩwe anyanyae. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova amwĩtie Avalaamu mũnyanyae. (Isaia 41:8; Yakovo 2:
3. Nĩkĩ Yeova ũnyuvaa andũ amwe methĩwe anyanyae?
3 Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Yeova ameta Avalaamu, Ndaviti, na Ndanieli anyanyae? Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa e mũnyanyae wa ala kwa wĩnyivyo mekaa ũndũ wameaĩa. Amwĩie Avalaamu: "Nĩweew'a wasya wakwa." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 22:18) Na eeie ana ma Isilaeli 'meethukĩĩsye wasya wake, na akeethĩwa Ngai woo, namo makeethĩwa andũ make.' (Yelemia 7:23) O naku nũtonya kwĩthĩwa mũnyanyae wa Yeova wamwĩthukĩĩsya.
YEOVA NŨMEKĨAA VINYA ANYANYAE
4, 5. Yeova onanasya ata vinya wake kwa andũ make?
4 Sũanĩa ũndũ kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũnyanyae wa Ngai kwonanasya. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yeova endaa "eyonany'e e vinya kwondũ wa ala ngoo syoo imwelekele syĩ mbĩanĩu." (2 Mavinda 16:9) Yeova atonya kwĩyonany'a e vinya kwaku ata? Nzĩa ĩmwe ĩwetetwe Mbivilianĩ ĩvuku ya Savuli 32:
5 Yeova nũthĩnĩkaa mũno ĩũlũ wa andũ. Akaũnenga ũtongosya ũla waĩle na kũũsũvĩa yĩla ũendee na kũũatĩĩa. Ngai nĩwendete kũũtetheesya ũsinde matatwa. (Savuli 55:22) Kwoou wamũthaitha Yeova na ngoo mbĩanĩu, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa mũandĩki wa Savuli ũla waisye: "Nĩmwiĩte Yeova mbee wakwa mavinda onthe: Nĩkwĩthĩwa e kw'okonĩ kwakwa kwa aũme, ndikathingithangw'a." (Savuli 16:8; 63:8) Yeova nũtonya kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na mwĩkalĩle ũla ũmwendeeasya. Ĩndĩ, ve mũmaitha wa Ngai ũla ũtonya kũũsiĩĩa ndũkeke ũu.
ŨKANANĨSYA WA SATANI
6. Satani aisye ata ĩũlũ wa andũ?
6 Kĩlungu kya 11 ĩvukunĩ yĩĩ kĩeleetye ũndũ Satani ũla Ndevili wakananĩisye ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai. Satani aisye Ngai nĩ mũkengani na oonany'a kana Yeova ndaaĩka nesa kũlea kũeka Atamu na Eva kwĩtw'ĩĩa ũthũku na ũseo. Yĩla Atamu na Eva mavĩtisye na nthĩ yaendeea kusũa ũsyao woo, Satani nĩwaumĩlilye nzika ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩtumaa andũ mamũthaitha Ngai. Satani aisye "andũ maimũthaithaa Ngai nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩmamwendete." Kwoou eea Ngai, "Ũkanenga mwanya, no nĩalyũle kĩla mũndũ akamũtia Ngai." Ũvoo wa ũla mũndũ weetawa Yovu nĩwonanĩtye ũu nĩw'o Satani weesilasya. Yovu aĩ ũũ, na ũkananĩsya wa Satani wamũkonetye ata?
7, 8. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Yovu etwa mũndũ ũla mũseo vyũ katĩ wa andũ ala ma ĩvinda yake? (b) Satani aumĩlilye nzika ata ĩũlũ wa kĩla kyatumaa Yovu amũthaitha Ngai?
7 Yovu aĩ thayũ vakuvĩ myaka 3,600 mĩvĩtu? Aĩ mũndũ mũseo nũndũ Yeova aisye: "Kũti ũngĩ take ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, mũndũ mwĩanĩu na mũlũngalu, ũla ũmũkĩaa Ngai, na wĩthyũũĩte akatia ũthũku." (Yovu 1:8) Yovu nĩwamwendeeasya Ngai.
8 Satani nĩwaumĩlilye nzika ĩũlũ wa kĩla kyatumaa Yovu amũthaitha Ngai. Ndevili eeie Yeova: "Ndwĩkĩĩte wiio kũmũthyũlũlũka, o na nyũmba yake, na kyonthe kĩla wĩ nakyo, ngalĩ syonthe? nũathimĩte wĩa wa moko make, na ũthwii wake nĩwingĩvĩte nthĩ. Ĩndĩ tambũũkya kw'oko kwaku yu, noikiita kyonthe kĩla wĩ nakyo, nake akakũuma ũthyũnĩ waku."
9. Yeova asũngĩie ũkananĩsya wa Satani ata, na nĩkĩ?
9 Satani oonanisye kana Yovu amũthaithaa Ngai nũndũ wa ĩtuvi yĩla wakwataa. O na Ndevili nĩwaisye kana Yovu akatatwa no amũtie Ngai. Yeova asũngĩie ũkananĩsya wa Satani ata? Nũndũ ũndũ ũsu wakonetye kĩla kyatumaa Yovu amũthaitha Yeova, Yeova nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlilye Satani amũtate Yovu. Yu ĩndĩ kwaĩ kũtonya kũmanyĩka nesa kana Yovu nũmwendete Ngai kana ndamwendete.
KŨTATWA KWA YOVU
10. Yovu akwatiwe nĩ matatwa meva, na eekie ata?
10 Satani nĩwamũtatie Yovu kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Indo imwe syake nĩsyooyiwe, na ingĩ syooawa, o na athũkũmi aingĩ make mooawa. Maũndũ asu mamũeteie thĩna mwingĩ mũno. Maũndũnĩ asu onthe, "Yovu ndaavĩtya, kana kwilĩĩla Ngai na ũtumanu."
11. (a) Satani aisye ata ĩũlũ wa Yovu, na Yeova eekie ata? (b) Yovu aisye ata yĩla wakũniwe na ũwau mũthũku?
11 Satani ndaamũeka. No nginya ethĩwe asũanĩie kana o na kau Yovu aĩ atonya kũmĩĩsya kwasya malĩ, athũkũmi, na syana, ũwau waĩ ũtonya kũtuma amũtia Ngai. Yeova nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlilye Satani akũne Yovu na ũwau mũthũku. Ĩndĩ o na ũu ndwaatuma Yovu amũtia Ngai. Yovu aisye: "Kũvika nakw'a ndikaveta kwakwa wĩanĩu ["wĩanĩu mũĩkĩĩku," NW ] wakwa."
12. Yovu asũngĩie ũkananĩsya wa Ndevili ata?
12 Yovu ndamanyaa kana Satani nĩwe wamũeteae mathĩna asu. Nũndũ ndeesĩ ĩũlũ wa ũkananĩsya wa Ndevili wa ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova, Yovu oonaa ta Ngai ũmũeteete mathĩna. (Yovu 6:4; 16:
13. Kweekĩkie ata nũndũ wa Yovu kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai?
13 Ũĩkĩĩku wa Yovu nĩwatumie Yeova asũngĩa ũkananĩsya wa Satani. Kwa w'o Yovu aĩ mũnyanyae wa Yeova, na Ngai nĩwamũathimie nũndũ wa mwĩkalĩle wake mũĩkĩĩku.
ŨNDŨ MAŨNDŨ ASU MAŨKONETYE
14, 15. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ũkananĩsya wa Satani ĩũlũ wa Yovu ũkonetye andũ onthe?
14 Ũkũlyo ĩũlũ wa wĩanĩu mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai, ũla waumĩlilw'e nĩ Satani ũyakonetye Yovu e weka. O naku nũkũkonetye. Ũu nĩw'o, nũndũ Ndeto ya Yeova yĩasya: "Mwana wakwa, ĩthĩwa mũĩ, noitanĩthya ngoo yakwa, nĩ kana nĩmũsũngĩe ũla ũmbũthasya." (Nthimo 27:11) Ndeto isu syaandĩkiwe myaka mingĩ ĩtina wa Yovu kũkw'a, na syonanasya kana Satani no waendee kũmũvũthya Ngai na kũsitaka athaithi make. Yĩla twekala mwĩkalĩle ũũmwendeesya Yeova, nĩtũtetheeasya kũsũngĩa ũkananĩsya wa Satani na tũitanĩthya ngoo ya Ngai. Ũndũ ũsu ũkwĩw'ĩthasya ata? Tyo wĩthĩwe wĩ ũndũ mwaĩlu kũtetheesya kũsũngĩa ũvũngũ wa Ndevili, o na ethĩwa kwĩka ũu kwĩtuma ũalyũla mwĩkalĩle waku?
15 Satani aisye: 'Kyonthe kĩla mũndũ wĩ nakyo nũnenganae kwondũ wa thayũ wake.' (Yovu 2:4) Kwasya "kĩla mũndũ," Satani oonanisye kana ũkananĩsya wake wakonetye andũ onthe ĩndĩ ti Yovu e weka. Ũsu nũndũ wa vata mũno. Satani nĩwĩkĩĩte nzika ĩũlũ wa wĩanĩu mũĩkĩĩku waku kwa Ngai. Ndevili endaa ũlee kũmwĩw'a Ngai na ũitia mwĩkalĩle mũlũngalu yĩla wĩ thĩnanĩ. Satani atonya kwĩka ũu ata?
16. (a) Satani atũmĩaa nzĩa syĩva kũalyũla andũ mamũtie Ngai? (b) Ndevili atonya kũtũmĩa nzĩa isu ata akũalyũle?
16 O ta ũndũ Kĩlungu kya 10 kĩwetete, Satani atũmĩaa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o kũalyũla andũ mamũtie Ngai. We amanthaa andũ "ta mũnyambũ ũkũluma, aimantha mũndũ aye." (1 Vetelo 5:8) Kwoou, vinya wa Satani nũtonya kwoneka yĩla anyanyau na andũ ma mũsyĩ, kana o andũ angĩ meũkũvinganĩsya ndũkaendee kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kwĩka ũndũ ĩkwasya. * (Yoana 15:
KWĨW'A MĨAO YA YEOVA
17. Kĩtumi kĩla kĩnene kĩtumaa twĩw'a mĩao ya Yeova nĩ kyaũ?
17 Weethĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũla ũmwendeeasya Ngai nũtonya kũsũngĩa ũkananĩsya wa Satani. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Mwende Yeova Ngai waku na ngoo yaku yonthe, na thayũ waku w'onthe, na vinya waku w'onthe." (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 6:5) Wendo waku kwa Ngai waendeea kwingĩva, ũkeethĩwa na mea ma kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie: "Nũndũ kũmwenda Ngai nĩ kũũ, tũkwatae mĩao yake." Wamwenda Yeova na ngoo yaku yonthe, ũkeethĩa "mĩao yake ti mĩito."
18, 19. (a) Mĩao ĩmwe ya Yeova nĩ yĩva? (Sisya ĩthangũ ya 122.) (b) Twĩsĩ ata kana Yeova ndatwĩaa twĩke maũndũ tũtatonya?
18 Mĩao ya Yeova nĩ yĩva? Ĩmwe ĩkonanĩtye na mĩkalĩle ĩla twaĩle kwĩvathana nayo. Kwa ngelekany'o, sisya ĩthangũ ya 122, kyongonĩ kyaĩtye "Ĩvathane na Kĩla Yeova Ũmenete." Vau nũkwona mĩkalĩle ĩla Mbivilia ĩvatanĩte. Maũndũ asu mawetetwe vau no moneke ta mate mathũku mũno. Ĩndĩ wasũanĩa na kĩthito maandĩko ala monanĩtw'e vau, nũkũelewa nĩ ũĩ ũla wĩ mĩaonĩ ya Yeova. Kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle waku nĩkũtonya kwĩthĩwa ne ũndũ ũla wĩ vinya vyũ waaĩka. Ĩndĩ kwĩkala mwĩkalĩle ũmwendeeasya Ngai kũtumaa wĩthĩwa wĩ mwĩanĩe na kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ. (Isaia 48:
19 Yeova ndatwĩaa twĩke maũndũ tũtatonya. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 30:
KWĨTHĨWA NA NDAĨA ILA IMWENDEEASYA NGAI
20. Nĩ ndaĩa syĩkũ imwendeeasya Ngai waĩle kwĩthĩwa nasyo, na nĩkĩ nĩ sya vata?
20 Kwĩ maũndũ maingĩ mendekaa nĩ kana tũmwendeesye Yeova ĩndĩ ti o kwĩvathana na maũndũ ala ũmenete kw'oka. Twaĩle kwenda maũndũ ala Yeova wendete. (Alomi 12:9) Nĩtwendaa kwĩthĩwa na ũnyanya na andũ ala mena mawoni na mawendi o ta ala twĩ namo? Yeova ailyĩ o ta ũu. Kwoou ĩmanyĩsye kwenda maũndũ ala Yeova wendete. Maũndũ amwe Yeova wendete nĩmonanĩtw'e nthĩnĩ wa Savuli 15:
21. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa ila imwendeeasya Ngai?
21 Kũsoma na kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kĩla ĩvinda nĩkũũtetheeasya kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa ila imwendeeasya Ngai. Kũmanya ũndũ Ngai wendaa kũkaũtetheesya kũsũanĩaa kwĩanana na kwenda kwake. (Isaia 30:
22. Nĩ kyaũ wĩĩthĩwa weanĩsya wekala mwĩkalĩle ũla ũmwendeeasya Ngai?
22 Nĩ kana wĩkale mwĩkalĩle ũũmwendeesya Yeova no nginya wĩthĩwe na kĩthito. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle no ta ũndũ ũmwe na kumya mũndũ ũla wa tene na kwĩvw'ĩka mũndũ mweũ. (Akolosai 3:
^ kal. 16 Ũu ti kwasya kana o ala maũvinganĩasya methĩawa matongoew'e nĩ Satani. Ĩndĩ Satani nĩwe ngai ya nthĩ ĩno, na nthĩ yonthe ĩtwĩe nthĩnĩ wake. (2 Akolintho 4:4; 1 Yoana 5:19) Kwoou no twĩtĩkĩle kana mwĩkalĩle ũla ũmwendeeasya Ngai ndwendekete nĩ andũ aingĩ, na amwe makaũvinganĩsya.

translation:
Are you afraid to denounce false worship?
Will Satan tempt you to compromise?
Will you remain neutral and fail to support Jehovah?
Are you afraid to remain neutral and support God?
1, 2. Consider how some people have pleased Jehovah by denouncing false worship.
ARE YOU afraid to offend someone by denouncing false religion? No, stand firm for what is right, be courageous and speak out, and say things that need to said. And do not be afraid to speak up because someone may dislike you or oppose you.
2 God approves those who denounce false religion. For example, Jehovah commended Abraham for his loyalty. (Isaiah 41:8; James 2:
3. Does Jehovah encourage some people to denounce false religion?
3 What motivated Jehovah to commend Abraham, David, and Daniel for their loyalty? Jehovah approves of those who show loyalty to him when faced with difficult circumstances. He told Abraham: "Be a father of many nations." (Genesis 22:18) And he said about the Israelites, 'They followed my laws, and they honored me, and they did not honor their people.' (Jeremiah 7:23) So do not be afraid to be loyal to Jehovah and to denounce false worship.
JEHOVAH COMMENDS LOYALTY
4, 5. Does Jehovah ever reward his servants for their loyalty?
4 Understand that being loyal to God brings rewards. The Bible shows that Jehovah can "reward those who earnestly seek him." (2 Kings 16:9) Can Jehovah reward you for your loyalty? Read Psalm 32:
5 Jehovah is always concerned about people. He will help you cope with difficulties and guide you in the right way. God is willing to comfort you during times of trouble. (Psalm 55:22) Therefore, trust in Jehovah and earnestly seek him, and do not be afraid like the psalmist David wrote: "I will call upon Jehovah, my refuge: I will be loyal to him in my time of need, and he will answer me." (Psalm 16:8; 63:8) Jehovah is willing to comfort those who are loyal to him. Indeed, take advantage of this provision from God.
SATAN'S TEMPTATION
6. How does Satan influence people?
6 In chapter 11, we saw how Satan deceived Eve and caused her to rebel against God. Satan accused God of being selfish and claimed that Jehovah did not want Adam and Eve to know what is good and bad. After Adam and Eve disobeyed and began to sin, Satan led all humans astray. Satan accused them of being disloyal to God. He said, "Anyone who fears God does so only because God protects him." This is why God allowed Satan to test Job. Did Satan have the right to say such things about Job?
7, 8. (a) What made Job an outstanding man among people of his time? (b) What lie did Satan use to try to make Job turn away from God?
7 Did Job live over 3,600 years ago? God described him as "blameless and upright, a man who feared God and turned away from evil." (Job 1:8) Job was loyal to God.
8 What lie did Satan use to try to make Job turn away from God? The Devil told Jehovah: "Will not Job fear God for nothing? Have you not put up a protective fence around him and his household and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has multiplied. But stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face."
9. Did Jehovah allow Satan to test Job, and why?
9 Satan claimed that Job served God only because of blessings. But Jehovah knew that Job would remain faithful even when tested. So Jehovah allowed Satan to harm Job. However, there was a limit to what Satan could do. Jehovah did not permit Satan to take Job's life. This way, it could be proven whether Job truly loved God or not.
THE TESTING OF JOB
10. What trials did Job experience, and what happened?
10 Satan afflicted Job with terrible sores all over his body. His sons and daughters were killed, and most of his livestock died. He lost almost everything he owned. People said, "Job has sinned, or he wouldn't be suffering like this."
11. (a) What further lie did Satan tell about Job, and how did Jehovah respond? (b) How did Job react when faced with intense pain?
11 Satan continued to lie. He suggested that if Job was touched personally, he would certainly curse God. Jehovah then permitted Satan to afflict Job with painful boils. This was meant to make Job turn against God. Job said: "I came naked from my mother's womb, and I will return naked. Jehovah gave, and Jehovah has taken away. May Jehovah's name be praised." ["Blessed be the name of Jehovah," NW]
12. Did Job blame Jehovah for his troubles?
12 Job did not accuse Jehovah of causing his problems. Instead, he showed that he recognized Satan as the source of his suffering. He maintained his integrity and demonstrated his faith in Jehovah. Job did not say that God had wronged him. (Job 6:4; 16:
13. What lesson can we learn from Job's example regarding our relationship with God?
13 Job's attitude pleased Jehovah and helped expose the lies of Satan. Because Job was loyal to Jehovah, God restored his former condition.
IMPORTANT LESSONS FROM THIS ACCOUNT
14, 15. How can we learn from what happened to Job to deal with Satan's influence?
14 Like Solomon's wise counsel to seek correction from God, Satan's affliction of Job proved beneficial. It also proves something else. That is, the Bible's warning: "My son, do not despise the discipline of Jehovah, and do not feel disgusted when he corrects you." (Proverbs 3:11) This advice was written centuries before Job lived, and it shows that Satan consistently tries to tempt people to turn away from God and abandon their integrity. If we remain loyal to Jehovah, we will be able to resist Satan's temptations and maintain our integrity toward God. Does this mean that we should look for opportunities to test our ability to withstand trials, or should we avoid such tests if possible?
15 Satan claimed: "Everything that a man has he will give up for his life." (Job 2:4) By saying "everything," Satan implied that his challenge affected everyone, not just Job. This is an important point to remember. Satan continues to question the motives of those who serve God. The Devil constantly seeks ways to turn faithful ones away from God and cause them to stumble. Can Satan succeed?
16. (a) What deceptive tactics does Satan use to mislead people away from God? (b) Can the Devil use similar tactics to mislead us?
16 As pointed out in Chapter 10, Satan uses subtle tactics to mislead people away from God. He often appeals to people's selfishness, telling them, "Every man for himself." (1 Peter 5:8) However, Satan's methods can appear appealing to some, especially those who are materialistic or who want to seem intelligent and independent. * (John 15:
MAINTAINING LOYALTY TO JEHOVAH
17. What is one key reason why we need to maintain loyalty to Jehovah?
17 Being loyal to Jehovah requires effort and helps us resist Satan's influence. Can we do this? The Bible says: "You shall love Jehovah your God with all your heart and all your soul and all your strength." (Deuteronomy 6:5) Your love for God grows as you appreciate what he does for you. The apostle John wrote: "If anyone loves God, God loves him." When you love Jehovah with all your heart, you obey his commandments.
18, 19. (a) What are some of Jehovah's commands? (See page 122.) (b) Are we able to fulfill all of Jehovah's requirements?
18 What are some of Jehovah's commands? Some involve principles that we can apply in our lives. For example, on page 122, the heading reads "Be United With Jehovah's Organization." But how do we apply those principles? The Bible gives guidance, and often there is more than one way to apply it. As you meditate on the scriptures, ask yourself, 'What would please Jehovah?' To illustrate, think about the command to use your possessions wisely. Being loyal to Jehovah means using them to support worship and being generous. (Isaiah 48:
19 Jehovah expects us to do what we can. (Deuteronomy 30:
OBEYING COMMANDMENTS THAT PLEASE JEHOVAH
20. What is one way to be loyal to Jehovah, and why is it important?
20 Often we show loyalty to Jehovah by doing what his organization teaches us. We want to go along with what Jehovah directs. (Proverbs 12:9) Do we want to be united with others who have sound views and act honestly? Jehovah does too. So cooperate with what Jehovah directs. One thing Jehovah directs is found at Psalm 15:
21. Why is it wise to seek direction when obeying commandments that please Jehovah?
21 Reading and meditating on the Bible daily helps us to seek direction when obeying commandments that please Jehovah. Knowing what Jehovah wants will help us to reason and to act in harmony with his ways. (Isaiah 30:
22. How can you make sure that you are obeying Jehovah's commands?
22 If you are loyal to Jehovah, pray for his guidance. The Bible encourages us to look to Jehovah for direction and to avoid relying on our own understanding. (Colossians 3:

Ũu tyo w'o aumĩthya ma koti mekaa? 47Ethĩwa mũkethasya anyanyae menyu oka, mwĩona ta mwĩkĩte ũndũ ũthonokete ũla andũ ala angĩ mekaa? It is better for you to enter life maimed than to go into hell with both hands. ³⁰#Mat 18.8; Mk 9.43 And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to be thrown into hell with both feet.
The Parable of Divorce
(Mat 19.9; Mk 10.11-12; Lk 16.18)
³¹ #
Col 24.1-4; Mat 19.7; Mk 10.4 "Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery."
³²#Mat 19.9; Mk 10.11-12; Lk 16.18; 1Cor 7.10-11 I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for marital unfaithfulness, makes her an adulteress, and anyone who marries the divorced woman commits adultery.
The Teaching on Not Causing Anyone to Stumble
³³ #
Ali 19.12; Pro 30.2; Col 23.21 "Anyone who says to his neighbor, 'I will repay you,' and puts his money in the bag, is committing sin, because he will surely repay it to God."
³⁴#Jas 5.12; Isa 66.1; Mat 23.22 I tell you that everyone who swears—by heaven, by earth, or by anything else—is bound by that oath.
³⁵#Isa 66.1; Psa 48.2 Anyone who says, "By heaven," is bound by heaven, and anyone who says, "By earth," is bound by earth.
Anyone who says, "By Jerusalem," is bound by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the Great King.
³⁶On no account should anyone swear by their own head, because they have no control over even one hair.
³⁷Let your 'yes' be 'yes,' and your 'no' be 'no,' otherwise you will be condemned.
The Teaching on Non-Retaliation
(Lk 6.29-30)
³⁸ #
Luk 21.24; Ali 24.20; Col 19.21 "Give to everyone who asks you, and do not ask for what was stolen from you."
³⁹And give to those who want something from you, and don't turn away from someone who wants to borrow from you.
⁴⁰When someone slaps you on the cheek, offer him the other one too, and when someone takes your coat, let him have your shirt as well.
⁴¹Give to everyone who asks you, and do not ask for what was stolen from you.
⁴²To anyone who wants something from you, give it, and do not expect to get it back.
Going the Extra Mile
(Lk 6.27-28,32-36)
⁴³ #
Ali 19.18
"But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you!"
⁴⁴And give to those who want something from you, and do not refuse to lend to them.
⁴⁵Because God is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
He sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous alike.
⁴⁶If you greet only your friends, what are you doing more than others?
Even pagans do that!
⁴⁷And if you lend to those who will pay you back, what credit is that to you?
Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
