text:
Mũthenya ũmwe mwakanĩ wa 1941 ĩthe-akwa akanisye inyia-akwa amwĩa: "Ũmanye wavatiswa nĩnaũtia!" Inyia-akwa ndaaĩtĩkĩlya ndeto isu imũtũle ngoo, ĩndĩ nĩwatwie kũvatiswa nĩ kana amũthũkũme Yeova Ngai. Ĩla wavatisiwe, ĩthe-akwa nĩweekie o ũndũ waĩtye. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu naĩ o wa myaka nyanya.
INYIA wakwa aĩ aamũkisye wendi wakwa wa kwĩmanyĩsya ũw'o wa Mbivilia tene. Nĩwoosete mavuku me na ũvoo wa Mbivilia, nakwa nĩnendete kũsoma ũvoo ũsu, na mũno mũno nendete kũsisya mavisa. Ĩndĩ Tata ndendaa Mami aingelesya kĩla weemanyĩasya. O na vailyĩ oou, naĩ na wendi wa kũmanya kĩla weemanyĩasya na nĩnamũkũlasya makũlyo, na kwoou ĩla Tata ũte kw'o nĩwamanyĩasya Mbivilia. Nũndũ wa ũu o nakwa nĩnatwie kwĩyumya nĩmũthũkũme Yeova. Navatisĩwe taoninĩ ya Blackpool, England, mwakanĩ wa 1943, nĩ wa myaka ĩkũmi.
NĨNAMBĨĨE KŨMŨTHŨKŨMA YEOVA
Kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu, nĩ na Mami twaendaa ũtavany'a twĩ ĩmwe tũte kũtĩĩa. Twatũmĩaa inanda kũtavya andũ ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Inanda isu syeethĩawa syĩ nene na syĩ na ũito wa vakuvĩ kĩlo inya na nusu. Kwasũanĩa kamwana kanini takwa katetengete kĩmwe!
Nambĩĩe kwenda kwosa ũvainia nĩ na myaka 14. Mami aisye kana naĩle kwamba kũneena na mũthũkũmi wa ana-a-asa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu (ũmũnthĩ mũthũkũmi ta ũsu etawa mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko). Ĩla naneenie nake ambĩie nĩtate nambe kwĩmanyĩsya wĩa ũtonya kũndetheesya ĩla ngesa kwosa ũvainia. Nĩneekie ũu wambĩie. Ĩtina wa kũthũkũma myaka ĩlĩ, nĩnaneenie na mũsyaĩĩsya ũngĩ wa mũthyũlũlũko namũelesya kana nĩnendaa kwosa ũvainia. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu ambĩie: "Osa!"
Kwoou Mweinĩ wa 4, 1949, nĩ na Mami nĩtwavangie kũthama nyũmba ĩla twakomboete na nũndũ wa ũu nĩtwatee syĩndũ sya nyũmba na ingĩ twanengane. Twathamĩĩe taoninĩ ya Middleton, ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ na Manchester, na twaambĩĩa kũkũnĩa ũvainia kũu. Ĩtina wa myei ĩna nĩnanyuvie mwana-a-asa ũmwe nĩkũne ũvainia nake. Ovisi wa ũvonge watwĩie nĩtũthamĩĩe kĩkundi kyaĩ kĩnaambĩĩw'a ũtũinĩ wa Irlam. Ĩvindanĩ o yĩu inyia wakwa aendeeie kũvainia na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũngĩ kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ.
O na kau naĩ o na myaka 17, nĩ na mwana-a-asa ũsu ũngĩ nĩtwanengiwe kĩanda kya kũtongoeasya maũmbano kĩkundinĩ kĩu twathamĩĩe nũndũ kyaĩ o na ana-a-asa anini matonya kũtongoesya. Ĩtina nĩnesie kũkũlw'a ngatetheesye Kĩkundi kya Buxton, kĩla kyaĩ na atavany'a anini mũno na kyaĩ na vata wa kũtetheew'a. Kĩla ĩvinda nonaa mawĩa asu nanengiwe mandetheeisye nĩyũmbany'e kwondũ wa mawĩa ala angĩ nesie kũnengwa.
Mwakanĩ wa 1951, nĩnakũlilye nĩthi Sukulu ya Mbivilia ya Ngileati. Ĩndĩ Mweinĩ wa 12, 1952, nĩneetiwe nĩlike ũthũkũminĩ wa ita sya kaũ. Nĩnakũlilye koti ĩmbĩtĩkĩlye ndikalike itanĩ nĩkwĩthĩwa naĩ mũtavany'a wa ĩvinda yonthe. Ĩndĩ nĩyaleile kwĩtĩkĩla kana nĩ mũtavany'a, na vandũ va ũu nekiw'e yela myei thanthatũ. Nĩ kũu yela nĩw'o nakwatie valũa wa kũnthokya nĩthi kĩlasi kya 22 kya Sukulu ya Ngileati. Kwoou Mweinĩ wa 7, 1953, nĩw'o nalikile meli yĩtawa Georgic, nĩ kana nĩthi New York.
Navika New York nĩnaendie ũmbanonĩ mũnene ũla waĩ kw'o mwakanĩ ũsu wa 1953 (New World Society Assembly). Nauma vau naendie na ngalĩ ya mwaki taoninĩ ya South Lansing, New York, vala sukulu ĩsu yeekĩawa. Nũndũ naumĩte yela, naĩ o na tũvesa tũnini. Ĩla naumie ngalĩnĩ ya mwaki, nalikile mbasi ya kũthi South Lansing. Tikiti wa kũthi kũu waĩ mũnini, ĩndĩ ndyaĩ na mbesa ianĩĩte tikiti ũsu na kwoou nakũlilye mũndũ ũmwe twalikanĩtye nake mbasinĩ ĩsu andĩvĩe.
NĨNATŨMIWE NTHĨ ĨNGĨ
Sukulu ya Ngileati nĩyatũmanyĩisye maũndũ maseo mũno, ala matũtetheeisye kũtw'ĩka "maũndũ onthe kwa andũ onthe" wĩanĩ wa ũmisonalĩ. (1 Ako. 9:22) Twamina sukulu, natũmiwe Philippines nĩ na ana-a-asa angĩ elĩ, namo nĩ Paul Bruun na Raymond Leach. Tweeteelile myei yĩana ũna nĩ kana visa sitũ syume. Ĩla syaumie twalikile meli ya kũthi Philippines twĩsĩle Rotterdam, twainga na Mediterranean Sea, twalikĩla Suez Canal, twakwatanĩsya Indian Ocean, na kuma vau twesĩla Malaysia, na Hong Kong. Savalĩ ĩsu yonthe yakuie mĩthenya 47! Twesie kũvika Manila, Philippines, Matukũ 19, Mwei wa 11, 1954.
Philippines kwaĩ kũndũ kweũ kwitũ na yaĩ no nginya tũmanyĩe syĩthĩo tũtesĩ, o na kũmanyĩa kĩthyomo kyeũ. Ĩndĩ twĩ atatũ twambie kũtũmwa kĩkundi kĩ Quezon City. Aingĩ taoninĩ ĩsu maneenaa Kĩsũngũ. Kyu kyatumie wĩthĩa o na ĩtina wa myei thanthatũ, tweesĩ ndeto sya kũtala sya kĩthyomo kya Tagalog. Ĩndĩ kũla twatũmiwe ĩtina wa vau nĩkwatũtetheeisye kũmina thĩna ũsu.
Mũthenya ũmwe kwĩ Mwei wa 5, 1955, twaumie ũtavany'a na twavika mũsyĩ tweethĩa kavumbu ka mavalũa katweteele nĩ na Mwana-a-asa Leach. Valũa isu syatwĩĩte nĩtwanengwa wĩa ũngĩ wa kũtw'ĩka asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko. O na kau naĩ o wa myaka 22, wĩa ũsu nĩwanengie mwanya wa kũtw'ĩka "maũndũ onthe kwa andũ onthe" kwa nzĩa ingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
Kwa ngelekany'o, ũvoo wakwa wa mbee wa andũ onthe nĩ mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko nawumĩisye nza wa katuka kaĩ ũtũinĩ mũna. Nesie kwĩthĩa kaĩ ana-a-asa ma Philippines meew'a ũvoo nĩ wa andũ onthe, moonaa waĩle kumĩw'a nza vandũ ve wingĩ! Kwoou ikundinĩ mbingĩ ila naendie naumasya maũvoo ma andũ onthe nĩ tũsũmbanĩ kana iwanzanĩ sya kũthyũmũa, nĩ masokonĩ, nza wa masũmba ma kanzũ, iwanzanĩ sya mathaũ, na mavinda maingĩ malelũnĩ. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩ San Pablo City kwauie mũno namo ana-a-asa ala makwatĩĩe maũndũ mavangĩte ũvoo wa andũ onthe umĩw'e sokonĩ. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwaemelile na kwoou namakũlya tũthi Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ngaumĩsye ũvoo ũsu vo. Ĩtina wa ũmbano, ana-a-asa asu mangũlilye kana ũmbano ũsu no ũtalwe ta ũmbano wa andũ onthe nũndũ ndũnaumĩw'a nza vandũ ve andũ aingĩ!
Kĩla ĩvinda nakomelaa mĩsyĩ kwa ana-a-asa. O na kau mĩsyĩ ĩsu ndyaĩ na syĩndũ mbingĩ, yekalaa yĩ mĩtheu. Mavinda maingĩ nakomaa kamũkekanĩ kaiĩtwe nthĩ mbwaũnĩ. Andũ ma kũu mayaĩ na mbavu wĩvingĩa nthĩnĩ nesa ũkathamba, na kwoou nĩnemanyĩisye kũthambĩa nza nĩsũvĩĩte. Naendaa na mbasi, na mavinda angĩ ĩla nĩendete ithamanĩ ingĩ ngĩthi na ĩsiwa. Myaka yonthe ĩla naaĩthĩwa ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe ndyaaĩsa kwĩthĩwa na ngalĩ yakwa.
Wĩa wa kũtavany'a na kũthokea ikundi nĩwandetheeisye kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya Tagalog. Ndyaathi kĩlasinĩ, ĩndĩ neemanyĩisye kĩthyomo kĩu kwa kwĩthukĩĩsya ana-a-asa ĩla twĩ ũtavany'a na maũmbanonĩ. Ana-a-asa maĩ na mea ma kũndetheesya nĩmanyĩsye kĩthyomo kyu, na nĩneew'aa mũyo nũndũ nĩmambũmĩĩisye na nĩmandavasya ũndũ nĩendeee mate kũmbithany'a.
O ũndũ ĩvinda yavĩtie, now'o naendeeie kũkwata ianda nzaũ, na ũu watumie nĩka moalyũku maingangĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 1956, ĩla Mwana-a-asa Nathan Knorr wookie nthĩ ĩsu, nĩtweethĩiwe na ũmbano mũnene. Ũmbanonĩ ũsu nanengiwe wĩa wa kũneena na andũ ma mĩvĩa ya maũvoo. Nũndũ ndyeesene na wĩa ũsu, ana-a-asa ala angĩ nĩmeeyumisye mandetheesya. Mwaka ũmwe ũte mũthelu, ũmbano ũngĩ mũnene nĩwavangiwe na Mwana-a-asa Frederick Franz kuma ovisinĩ mũnene nĩwookie kũu. Ninyie naĩ mũsyaĩĩsya wa ũmbano ũsu, na nĩnemanyĩisye maũndũ ma vata kuma kwa Mwana-a-asa Franz. Mwana-a-asa ũsu nĩwatatie eke kĩla andũ ma kũu meekaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, ayumya ũvoo wa andũ onthe eekĩĩte mũthemba wa ngũa ya Filipino wĩtawa Barong Tagalog, na ana-a-asa ma kũu nĩmeewie mũyo kũmwona ekĩĩte ũu.
Ĩla natw'ĩkie mũsyaĩĩsya wa kĩvalo, nĩneekie moalyũku angĩ maingangĩ. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu twoonasya andũ sinema yeetawa The Happiness of the New World Society. Vakuvĩ kĩla ĩvinda twamyonanĩasya nza kũndũ kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ. Na nũndũ wa ũu mavinda amwe nĩtwathĩnaw'a nĩ tũsamũ. Tũsamũ tũu twakusaw'a nĩ kyeni kya masinĩ ĩla twatũmĩaa (projector) na tũilũma kĩoonĩ kyayo. Na kote waĩ wĩa mwingĩ kũvangũla masinĩ ĩsu ĩtina wa kwonany'a sinema! O na kau ũyaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũvangĩthya sinema ta isu, tweew'aa tweanĩwa ĩla twoona andũ aingĩ maitana mamanya kana ũseũvyo wa Yeova nĩ wa nthĩ yonthe.
Athembi ma Katholeki nĩmasukumaa anene amwe ma silikalĩ matũvate valũa sya kwĩka maũmbano manene. Kana mavinda angĩ makũnaa ngengele sya kanisa ĩla tũendeee kumya maũvoo vakuvĩ na kanisa syoo nĩ kana mathomboosany'e ũmbano witũ. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, wĩa witũ nĩwaendeeie na yu andũ aingĩ isionĩ isu nĩ athaithi ma Yeova.
IANDA INGĨ NZAŨ NĨSYATUMIE NĨKA MOALYŨKU MAINGANGĨ
Mwakanĩ wa 1959, nĩnakwatie valũa ũwetete kana nĩnanengwa wĩa wa kũthũkũma ovisinĩ wa ũvonge. Kũthũkũma ovisinĩ ũsu nĩkwatumie nĩmanyĩsya maũndũ angĩ maingĩ. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩnanengiwe kĩanda kya kũthokeaa nthĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩ savalĩnĩ isu nĩnakomanie na Janet Dumond, ũla waĩ misonalĩ nthĩ ya Thailand. Nĩtwaandĩkanĩie valũa o kwa ĩvinda, na mũthya twatwaana. Kuma twatwaana nĩtũtanĩĩte kũmũthũkũma Yeova kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 51.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu yonthe, nĩnĩtanĩĩte kũthokea andũ ma Yeova nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ 33. Nĩnĩtũngaa mũvea mũno nĩkwĩthĩwa ianda ila nakwatie nĩ mũnini nĩsyandetheeisye namanya kũlikana na andũ ma mĩthemba yĩ kĩvathũkany'o kũla kw'onthe naathi! Wĩa ũsu wa kũthokea ana-a-asa nĩwatumie naamangya kĩlĩko kyakwa na wandetheesya kũmanya kana Yeova endete andũ ma mĩthemba yonthe.—Meko 10:34, 35.
O NA YU NO TŨNEEKA MOALYŨKU
Mwa nĩnĩtanĩĩte mũno kũthũkũma na ana-a-asa ma Philippines! Yu atavany'a ma kũũ nĩ ta kũndũ ĩkũmi kwa ala neethĩie ĩla navikie kw'o. Nĩ na Janet no tũendeee kũthũkũma ovisinĩ wa ũvonge ũla wĩ Quezon City, kũũ Philippines. O na kau nĩthũkũmĩte nthĩ ĩno ya ũeninĩ myaka mbee wa 60, nĩnonaa nĩ na vata wa kũendeea kwĩthĩwa nĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩka moalyũku ala Yeova wenda nĩke. Kwa ngelekany'o, moalyũku ala me ũseũvyonĩ nĩmatumĩte tũmanya kana no nginya twĩthĩwe twĩyũmbanĩtye kũalyũkana na maũndũ ĩla tũendeee kũmũthũkũma Ngai na ana-a-asa maitũ.
Nĩtwatwie kwĩtĩkĩlanaa na maũndũ onthe mosanĩte na kwenda kwa Yeova, na ũndũ ũsu nũtumĩte twĩkala nesa twĩ eanĩe. O na ĩngĩ, nĩtũtatĩte kwĩka moalyũku ala maĩlĩte nĩ kana tũthũkũme ana-a-asa maitũ nesa. Kwa w'o, nĩtũtw'ĩte vyũ kũtw'ĩka "maũndũ onthe kwa andũ onthe" ĩvindanĩ yonthe yĩla Yeova ũkũendeea kũtũtũmĩa.

translation:
One day in 1941, I was shocked when my father said to me: "You are disfellowshipped!" I was very upset, especially because I had been taught to fear being disfellowshipped more than to fear God Jehovah. But despite being disfellowshipped, I continued to attend meetings secretly. I remember that time well, as it was many years ago.
MY FATHER then began to take me along to Bible studies. I enjoyed the visits and the Bible reading, and gradually I started to ask questions. My parents helped me understand things. And although they did not always explain everything clearly, they would say that Father was teaching them from the Bible. Because of this, I also began to learn to love Jehovah. I was baptized at Blackpool, England, in 1943, when I was ten years old.
I APPRECIATED FEARING JEHOVAH
At that time, my parents and I used to go out together to distribute literature. We used small bags to carry Bible publications. One bag was so full that it weighed about eight pounds! It was quite a burden for a little girl to carry!
I began pioneering when I was 14 years old. My mother allowed me to speak to the congregation elder about my desire to serve (the elder could give permission for a young person to pioneer). But I asked him if I could first try to see if I really wanted to continue pioneering. He agreed to let me try. After a year of fearing Jehovah, I spoke to the circuit overseer and told him that I wanted to pioneer. The circuit overseer told me: "Go ahead!"
On April 4, 1949, my parents and I moved from our home, which we had rented, and we bought a small house with some land. We moved to Middleton, but there were more people in Manchester, and we were assigned to preach there. A few months later, I met a young woman who loved her husband. The branch office wrote us saying that we should move to a group in Irlam. At that time, this sister went on to pioneer with another young woman in that group.
When I was 17 years old, this young woman and I were invited to attend a school to improve our ability to conduct meetings in that group where we lived. Then I requested to be transferred to the Buxton Congregation, which had many publishers and also experienced brothers. Every week I would meet with those brothers and sisters, and they would help me to improve.
In 1951, I began attending the Gilead Missionary School. On December 12, 1952, I was appointed to serve in the island country of Jamaica. I began studying so that I could become a full-time minister and be sent out with the brothers throughout the island. But I realized that I wasn't a full-time minister, and many people didn't know about my situation. It was then that I was able to graduate from class 22 of the Gilead School. On April 7, 1953, I boarded the ship Georgic, heading toward New York.
I arrived in New York and attended a large assembly called the "New World Society Assembly" in the summer of 1953. I stayed with a family named Brother South Lansing, New York, near the school grounds. After the assembly, I returned home, but I still had much work to do. However, I found lodging with the family, and I took a bus to South Lansing. The bus fare was expensive, so I sold my watch to pay for the ticket, and on the bus, I met a man we had studied with.
I WAS SENT AGAIN
The Gilead School taught us many important things, but they emphasized teaching "all things to all people" in accordance with our understanding. (1 Cor. 9:22) After graduating from school, I was sent to the Philippines along with two others, namely Paul Bruun and Raymond Leach. We traveled for many days and did not have proper visas. But thankfully, when we boarded the ship to the Philippines, we stopped in Rotterdam, sailed through the Mediterranean Sea, passed through the Suez Canal, crossed the Indian Ocean, and finally reached Malaysia and Hong Kong. The entire journey took 47 days! We arrived in Manila, Philippines, on November 19, 1954.
The Philippines presented us with new challenges, but we were eager to learn how to preach effectively and to understand the local customs. Soon, three of us were assigned to a congregation in Quezon City. Many there spoke Visayan. Because of this need and the desire to help more people, we started learning the Tagalog language. And soon, we were assigned to areas where we could use what we learned.
One day in May 1955, we experienced something unusual when we visited a small town with Brother Leach. This town had been devastated by a typhoon. There was a young man, only 22 years old, who was willing to help us teach "all things to all people" in a way that would appeal to the people.
For example, the lifestyle of the poor people there is very different from our own, and it reminded me of the hardships of traveling around. I remember visiting families in the Philippines where their lifestyle was similar to that of the poor people here, and they were happy despite having so little! It saddens me greatly, but I see that the lifestyles of the poor people are often characterized by hardship, poverty, lack of clothing, inadequate food, and many other difficulties. One day in San Pablo City, I saw this firsthand and met families who had experienced many hardships due to the lifestyle of the poor people being associated with poverty. This situation has motivated me, and I hope to share this experience with the Department of Social Welfare so that they can address this issue. In conclusion, those families may or may not accept this message, but I believe that the hardships faced by the poor people affect many families!
Every time I visit families, I feel sorry for them. Although I don't have much to give, I still try my best. Many families I visit are struggling to make ends meet. People in the countryside suffer greatly from hunger and thirst, and I am moved to help them because it touches my heart. I travel by bus, and sometimes the fare is quite high considering the distance. Throughout the year, I dedicate my time to visiting all the families, and I am grateful for the opportunity to do so.
Those who want to learn and understand the language have encouraged me to study Tagalog. I started taking lessons, and I am now able to communicate with families more easily when we visit and interact with them. The families are pleased that I am trying to learn their language, and I am happy to be able to connect with them and continue helping them.
And since I visited that place, I always try to find ways to help, and this has led to many good things. For example, in 1956, Brother Nathan Knorr came to visit us, and he was greeted by a large crowd. That gathering was organized to speak to people from various places. Because of that, many families were touched. A year later, another large gathering was held by Brother Frederick Franz at a large school, and many people came. You should also remember that gathering, and I appreciate the things learned from Brother Franz. That brother cared about everyone. For example, he admired the national costume of the Filipino people called Barong Tagalog, and the people were happy to show him that.
But we realized the importance of demonstrations, so I began to prepare more thoroughly. This demonstration showed people a film called The Happiness of the New World Society. Every time we showed this film, we tried to invite many people. And because of this, sometimes we had to struggle to get a place to show the film. We struggled to find a place to set up our equipment (projector) and adjust its focus. But despite many difficulties in finding a place to show the film, we continued to show it, and we were happy to see many people come together to learn about God's Kingdom or Jehovah's purpose.
Catholic priests often strongly opposed large meetings. Sometimes they would go to churches to prevent us from speaking to people, and those churches or their leaders would oppose our gatherings. However, despite these challenges, we continued to preach to many people, and we helped them become Witnesses of Jehovah.
MORE WAYS TO HELP ARE NEEDED
In 1959, I accepted a challenging assignment—to help organize a circuit assembly. Organizing this assembly helped me to learn many things. Because of the assembly, I was assigned to travel to different congregations. During one trip, I met Janet Dumond, a missionary serving in Thailand. We wrote to each other regarding the assembly, and eventually we married. Together we served Jehovah for 51 years.
Throughout my life, I have endeavored to speak to Jehovah's people for over 33 years. I am very grateful for this privilege, and I thank Jehovah for allowing me to associate with his faithful people throughout my life! This work of speaking to others has brought me great joy, and I have been able to encourage others to know that Jehovah cares for all mankind.—Acts 10:34, 35.
AND YOU CAN JOIN US
I also had the joy of helping those in the Philippines! You can share in this work by spending just ten minutes talking to your neighbors. Janet and I continue to serve in the circuit assembly work in Quezon City, Philippines. And now that I am approaching 60 years of service, I still hope to remain active as long as Jehovah allows. Of course, many brothers and sisters may wonder whether they will be able to stay active as they get older and face challenges in continuing to preach God's Word.
We have become accustomed to facing difficulties and trusting in Jehovah, and this has helped us to remain steadfast. Also, we should not give up when we encounter obstacles in our efforts to help others learn about Jehovah. Therefore, let us continue to "make all things new" throughout our lives as Jehovah continues to use us.

text:
Kĩvathũkany'o kya Mbivilia na mavuku ala angĩ nĩ kyaũ?
Mbivilia ĩtonya kũũtethya ata kũmĩĩsya mathĩna?
Nĩkĩ ũtonya kũĩkĩĩa wathani wa Mbivilia?
1, 2. Nĩkĩ Mbivilia nĩ mũthĩnzĩo mũseo mũno kuma kwa Ngai?
WE WAAKWATA mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwĩ mũnyanyau mũseo vyũ? No wĩthĩwe weewie mũyo ngoonĩ. Muthĩnzĩo wonanasya kana mũndũ ũla wakũnenga nĩwonaa ũnyanya wenyu wĩ vata. Yĩla wakwatie mũthĩnzĩo ũsu no nginya wĩthĩwe watũngie mũvea.
2 Mbivilia nĩ mũthĩnzĩo kuma kwa Ngai na twaĩle kũtũnga mũvea nũndũ waw'o. Ĩvuku yĩĩ nĩyonanĩtye maũndũ tũtaĩ twĩsa kũmanya. Nĩwetete ũndũ Ngai woombie matu ala me ndata, nthĩ, na mũndũ wa mbee na mũka wake. Mbivilia yĩna myolooto ĩtonya ũtũtethya kũmĩĩsya mathĩna. Ĩeleasya ũndũ Ngai ũkeanĩsya ieleelo syake na kũseũvya maũndũ kũũ nthĩ. Mbivilia nĩ mũthĩnzĩo mũseo ta kĩ!
3. Kwĩthĩwa na Mbivilia kũtwonasya ata ĩũlũ wa Yeova, na nĩkĩ ũũ nĩ ũndũ wa kũtanĩthya ngoo?
3 Mbivilia nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa kũtanĩthya ngoo nũndũ nĩtwonasya ũndũ mũna ĩũlũ wa ũla Ũmĩnenganĩte, Yeova Ngai. Kũtũnenga Mbivilia kũĩkĩĩthasya kana nĩwendaa tũmũmanye nesa. Mbivilia nĩtonya kũũtetheesya kũmũthengeea Yeova.
4. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkwendeeasya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Mbivilia ĩnyaĩĩkĩtw'e?
4 Ethĩwa we wĩ na Mbivilia ndwĩ weka. Mbivilia ĩalyũlĩtwe kwa ithyomo mbee wa 2,300 na kwoou vakuvĩ kĩla mũndũ nthĩ nũtonya kũsoma Mbivilia na kĩthyomo kyake. Kĩla kyumwa Mbivilia mbee wa milioni ninyaĩĩkaw'a. Mbilioni mbingi sya Mbivilia nĩseũvĩtw'e. Vaiĩ ĩvuku yĩngĩ yĩnyaĩĩkĩtw'e ta Mbivilia.
5. Nĩ kwa nzĩa myaũ kĩla Ũandĩko Mbivilianĩ "nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai"?
5 Kĩla Ũandĩko Mbivilianĩ "nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai." (2 Timotheo 3:16) Waveveewe ata? Mbivilia yaasya: "Andũ maneenie ndeto syaumie kwa Ngai, maitongoew'a nĩ Veva Mũtheu." (2 Vetelo 1:21) Kwa ngelekany'o, mũnene wa wĩa nũtonya kũmwĩa kalanĩ wake aandĩke valũa. Ndeto ila syĩ valũanĩ ũsu nĩ sya mũnene. Kwoou valũa ũsu nĩ wake ti wa kalanĩ. O ta ũu Mbivilia nĩ ndeto ya Ngai ĩndĩ ti ya andũ ala mamĩandĩkie. Kwoou, kwa w'o Mbivilia yonthe nĩ "ndeto ya Ngai."
YĨ WĨW'ANO NA NĨ YA W'O
6, 7. Nĩkĩ wĩwano wa Mbivilia nĩ wa kwendeesya mũno?
6 Mbivilia yaandĩkiwe kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 1,600. Ala mamĩandĩkie maĩ andũ me kĩvathũkany'o na ma nzyawa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Amwe maĩ aĩmi, angĩ maĩ atei ma makũyũ, na aĩthi. Na angĩ maĩ athani, asili, na asumbĩ. Luka, ũla waandĩkie ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo ya Luka, aĩ ndakĩtalĩ. O na kau andũ asu maĩ kĩvathũkany'o, Mbivilia yĩ wĩw'ano kuma mwambĩlĩlyo kũvika mũminũkĩlyo. *
7 Ĩvuku ya mbee ya Mbivilia yĩtũtavasya ũndũ mathĩna ma andũ mambĩĩie. Ĩvuku ya mũthya yonanasya kana nthĩ yonthe ĩkatw'ĩka valatiso. Mbivilia ĩeleetye maũndũ maingĩ na ma myaka mingĩ makonanĩtye na kĩeleelo kya Ngai. Wĩw'ano wa Mbivilia nĩwendeeasya na ũu now'o tũtonya kwĩkwatya ĩvuku ya Ngai yĩthĩwe yĩilyĩ.
8. Nengana ngelekany'o ya kwonany'a kana Mbivilia ĩneenaa w'o ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma saenzi.
8 Mbivilia nĩneenaa w'o ĩũlũ wa saenzi. O na yĩ na ũvoo wawetetwe mbee wa ĩvinda yaw'o yĩte ĩviku. Kwa ngelekany'o, nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku ya Alivai, Aisilaeli nĩmanengetwe mĩao ĩũlũ wa ũtheu na kũvatha andũ ala awau. Mbaĩ ila ingĩ syamathyũlũlũkĩte iyeesĩ maũndũ asu. O na yĩla andũ maĩ na mawoni mate maw'o ĩũlũ wa ũndũ nthĩ ĩilyĩ, Mbivilia nĩyaĩtye kana nthĩ nĩ kilinge. (Isaia 40:22) Mbivilia nĩyawetete kana nthĩ 'ĩsũnzũũlĩtw'e vate kĩndũ.' (Yovu 26:7) Mbivilia ti ĩvuku ya saenzi. Ĩndĩ yĩla ĩnĩũweta maũndũ ma saenzi ĩwetaa w'o. Ũu tyo w'o tũtonya kwĩkwatya ĩvuku ya Ngai yĩthĩwe yĩilyĩ?
9. (a) Mbivilia yonanasya ata kana nĩ ya w'o na ya kũĩkĩĩka ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma isitoli? (b) Ũlũngalu wa ngoo wa andũ ala maandĩkie Mbivilia ũkwonasya ata ĩũlũ wayo?
9 Mbivilia nĩneenaa w'o ĩũlũ wa Isitoli. Ĩwetaa maũndũ mate ma ũtalĩthya. Ĩwetaa masyĩtwa ma andũ na nzyawa syoo. * Kĩvathũkany'o na andũ ala angĩ matawetaa mothũku moo, ala maandĩkie Mbivilia mayaĩ na ũseleke, nĩmaandĩkie mothũku moo. Kwa ngelekany'o Mose, mũandĩki wa ĩvuku ya Motalo nũwetete ĩkosa yake yĩla yatumie akanw'a kwa ũito. (Motalo 20:
ĨVUKU YĨNA ŨĨ ŨTETHYA
10. Nĩkĩ ti ũndũ wa ũsengy'a kana Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku yĩna ũĩ ũtethya?
10 Nũndũ kĩla Ũandĩko wa Mbivilia nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai, "nĩwaĩle wa kũmanyĩsya, na kũĩkĩĩthya andũ mavĩtyo, na kũmatũngĩĩa." (2 Timotheo 3:
11, 12. (a) Nthĩnĩ wa Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ, Yesũ atavanisye ĩũlũ wa maũndũ meva? (b) Nĩ maũndũ angĩ maũ maũtethya mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ, na nĩkĩ ũtao wayo nũtonya ũtethya kĩla mũndũ ĩvinda yonthe?
11 Sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ nthĩnĩ wa Mathayo kĩlungu 5 kũvika 7. Nthĩnĩ wa ũtavany'a ũsu wĩ ũĩ mwingĩ, Yesũ atavanisye ĩũlũ wa maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o, ta ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu wa w'o, kũmina mathĩna, kũvoya, na kwĩthĩwa na mawoni maseo ĩũlũ wa malĩ. Ndeto isu sya Yesũ nitonya ũtethya o na ũmũnthĩ.
12 Myolooto ĩmwe ya Mbivilia ĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa mwĩkalĩle wa mũsyĩ, wĩa, na kwĩkalany'a na andũ. Myolooto ya Mbivilia ĩtethasya kĩla mũndũ ĩvinda yonthe. Ũĩ ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ũwetetwe nĩ Ngai kwĩsĩla Isaia: "Ninyie Yeova Ngai waku, ũla ũkũmanyĩasya kwaĩla."
ĨVUKU YA WATHANI
13. Yeova avevee Isaia kũandĩka maũndũ meva ĩũlũ wa Mbaviloni?
13 Mbivilia yĩ wathani na mwingĩ waw'o nĩwĩanĩĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwĩsĩla mwathani Isaia Yeova nĩwathanie ĩũlũ wa kwanangwa kwa mũsyĩ wa Mbaviloni. (Isaia 13:19; 14:
14, 15. Wathani wa Isaia ĩũlũ wa Mbaviloni weanĩie ata?
14 Matukũ 5 Mwei wa 10, mwaka wa 539 M.I.Y. myaka 200 kuma wathani ũsu wawetwa, ita nĩsyookie Mbaviloni. * Mũnene wa ita isu aĩ Mũvelisi weetawa Kulusi. Yu wathani wookĩte kwĩanĩa. Ĩndĩ ita sya Kulusi nĩsyaĩ itonya kũlika Mbaviloni vate kaũ?
15 Andũ ma Mbaviloni maĩ na mboka nene mũno ũtukũ ũsu mate na w'ĩa nũndũ mũsyĩ ũsu wathyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ ũkũta mũnene mũno. Ĩvinda o yĩu, Kulusi aeendee kwathũkĩsya ũsĩ ũla wesĩle mũsyĩ ũsu. Kĩw'ũ kyaoleka ũndũ andũ maĩ matonya kũinga kũvikĩĩa ũkũta wa mũsyĩ ũsu. Ita sya Kulusi syaĩ itonya kũkĩla ũkũta wa Mbaviloni ata? Kwa kĩtũmi kĩtesĩkĩe mĩango ya mũsyĩ ũsu ndyaavingwa ũtukũ ũsu!
16. (a) Isaia athanĩte ata ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo wa Mbaviloni? (b) Wathani wa Isaia ĩũlũ wa kwanangwa kwa Mbaviloni weanĩie ata?
16 Kwathanĩtwe ta ũũ ĩũlũ wa Mbaviloni: "Ndĩkatũwa nĩ andũ o na ĩndĩĩ, o na ndĩkekalwa kuma nzyawa na nzyawa: o na Mwalavu ndakamba ĩeema kw'o; o na aĩthi maikatindisya ndĩthya syoo sya mbũi na malondu kw'o." (Isaia 13:20) Wathani ũũ ndwawetete kũvalũka kwa ndũa ĩsu kw'oka. Woonanĩtye Mbaviloni ĩkaanangwa na ndĩkakwa ĩngĩ. O na ũmũnthĩ nũtonya kwona wĩanĩu ũsu. Vala Mbaviloni yaĩ, kĩlomita 80 ĩtheo wa Mbakitati, mũsyĩ mũnene wa Ilaki, vaitwĩwe ũmũnthĩ. Ũu nĩkwonany'a kwĩanĩa kwa wathani wa Yeova kwĩsĩla Isaia ũla waĩtye: "Ngamĩvyaĩa na ũvyaĩo wa wanangĩko."
17. Wĩanĩu wa wathani wa Mbivilia ũlũlũmĩĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo ata?
17 Kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũĩkĩĩku wa wathani wa Mbivilia nĩ kũlũlũmĩĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo. Ethĩwa Yeova Ngai nĩwĩanĩĩtye mawatho amwe make twĩna kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũĩkĩĩa kana akeanĩsya watho wake ĩũlũ wa valatiso. (Motalo 23:19) Twĩ na "wĩkwatyo wa thayũ ũtathela, ũla Ngai wathie mbee wa mavinda ma tene tene."
"NDETO YA NGAI Ĩ THAYŨ"
18. Mũtũmwa Mũklĩsto Vaulo awetete ata ĩũlũ wa "ndeto ya Ngai"?
18 Kwĩanana na ũndũ twasoma kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ, nĩw'o kana Mbivilia nĩ ĩvuku ya mwanya. Ĩndĩ ũseo wayo nũvĩtũkĩte wĩw'ano wayo, ũw'o ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma saenzi na isitoli, na ũĩ ũtethya, na wathani ũtonya kũĩkĩĩka. Mũtũmwa Mũklĩsto Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ndeto ya Ngai ĩ thayũ, na nĩ nthangaau, na nĩ mbũĩ kwĩ ũvyũ ũla mũĩ ngalĩ syelĩ, nayo ĩtonyaa kũvika kũaan'ya thayũ na veva, na maleenyũ na mũthungo, na ĩ mĩtũkĩ ya kũmanya mosũanĩo na kwenda kwa ngoo."
19, 20. (a) Mbivilia ĩtonya ũkũtetheesya ata wĩkuũe nesa vyũ? (b) Ũtonya kwonany'a mũvea nũndũ wa Mbivilia, mũthĩnzĩo wa mwanya kuma kwa Ngai ata?
19 Kũsoma "ndeto" ya Ngai nĩkũtonya kũalyũla thayũ waku. Nĩkũtonya kũtuma twĩkuũa ithyĩ ene nesa vyũ. Nĩtũtonya kwasya nĩtũmwendete Ngai, ĩndĩ ũndũ twĩkaa twasoma ũndũ Mbivilia, Ndeto yake mbevee ĩmanyĩasya, nĩkwonanasya mesilya maitũ maw'o o na maw'oni maitũ ma ngoonĩ.
20 Mbivilia kwaw'o nĩ ĩvuku kuma kwa Ngai. Nĩ ĩvuku yaĩle kũsomwa, kwĩmanyĩw'a, na kwendwa. Onany'a kana wĩna mũvea kwa mũthĩnzĩo ũũ wa Ngai kwa kwĩmanyĩsya. Weeka ũu ũkaelewa nesa kĩeleelo kya Ngai ĩũlũ wa mũndũ. Kieleelo kĩu na ũndũ kĩkeanĩa nĩkĩeleetw'e kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ kĩatĩĩe.

translation:
What about the account of Bilhah and her maids?
Does Bilhah try to justify herself or excuse her actions?
Why does she attempt to blame others for what happened?
1, 2. Why is Bilhah an outstanding example for us to imitate when serving God?
DO YOU APPRECIATE having such fine examples? If so, let this encourage you. A good example can help a person overcome temptation. Consider how helpful it is to have friends who set a good standard. Imitate their fine qualities and be determined to live up to them.
2 Bilhah is an outstanding example for us to imitate when serving God, and we can learn much from her account. This verse highlights some things we should strive to understand. It reminds us that God sees our thoughts, feelings, and motives. He knows what each individual—including a husband and his wife—is thinking. Bilhah's story shows that we can always trust Jehovah to discern our true intentions and to deal with matters justly. Bilhah is a truly outstanding example, isn't she!
3. Does associating with Bilhah help us to know Jehovah better, and if so, how?
3 Bilhah is an example of how to serve Jehovah faithfully, and it helps us to see what pleases him. By learning from Bilhah, we may be motivated to get to know Jehovah more fully. Studying Bilhah will help us to appreciate Jehovah's ways.
4. What can we do to make the account of Bilhah come alive for us?
4 Take time to read Bilhah carefully. Bilhah has been translated into over 2,300 languages, and copies are available to people everywhere. Millions of Bibles are distributed each year. Billions of Bible portions have also been printed. Indeed, much effort has been put forth to make the Bible accessible.
5. Why does the inspired Scriptures call it "God's breath"?
5 The inspired Scriptures call it "God's breath." (2 Timothy 3:16) Is it truly breathed out by God? The Bible says: "Men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit." (2 Peter 1:21) For instance, a secretary may write down what her employer dictates. But the words she writes belong to the employer, not to the secretary. Similarly, God used men to write his thoughts. Therefore, throughout the Bible, it is properly called "God's word."
WHY IT IS WORTH KNOWING
6, 7. Why is the Bible worth knowing?
6 The Bible was written over a period of about 1,600 years. It was written by some 40 different men, who lived at various times and under varying circumstances. Some were kings, others were shepherds, and still others were fishermen. And some were doctors, tentmakers, and farmers. Luke, the writer of the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts, was a physician. Yet despite the varied backgrounds of those who wrote it, the Bible is harmonious from beginning to end. *
7 Many parts of the Bible have been found to be remarkably accurate. Its prophecies often come true in detail. The Bible deals with many subjects and covers thousands of years, yet it consistently upholds God's principles. Knowing the Bible helps us understand God's will and purpose more fully.
8. How does the Bible compare with books on science?
8 The Bible is not a science textbook. However, it does contain information that agrees with scientific findings. For example, the account in Genesis describes the earth as round long before scientists proved this fact. But it does not give detailed scientific explanations. Also, while people today have much greater knowledge of the physical world, the Bible accurately states fundamental truths. (Isaiah 40:22) The Bible does not attempt to explain how things work scientifically; rather, it tells us what is true. (Job 26:7) The Bible is not a science book, but it can help us appreciate the wonders of creation and strengthen our faith in God.
How can knowing this help us better understand God's will?
9. (a) Does the Bible claim to be a history book or to provide a comprehensive record of events? (b) What does the way people from ancient times viewed the Bible show about its reliability?
9 The Bible is not a history book. It focuses on important spiritual lessons. It mentions people and events briefly. * Consider how others view historical accounts—if they are biased, their records may be inaccurate. For instance, Moses, the writer of the first five books of the Bible, admitted his limitations when writing. (Exodus 20:
A BOOK WORTH EXAMINING
10. Why is it important to examine whether the Bible is truly God's inspired Word?
10 Because every scripture is inspired by God and beneficial "for teaching, for reproving, and for correcting," (2 Timothy 3:
11, 12. (a) In his Sermon on the Mount, what main points did Jesus emphasize? (b) What other important teachings are found in the Bible, and why is understanding them essential for everyone?
11 Read Matthew chapters 5 through 7 to find out what Jesus emphasized in his Sermon on the Mount. In this extensive discourse, Jesus addressed matters such as avoiding hypocrisy, being merciful, forgiving, and resisting materialism. His principles can guide our lives today.
12 One key theme of the Bible is how to live a moral life, how to worship God, and how to associate with others. The Bible's guidance benefits everyone. God inspired Isaiah to write: "You are Jehovah my God, the One who teaches me what is beneficial."
THE PROPHETS
13. Did Jehovah inspire Isaiah to write about future events concerning Babylon?
13 The Bible often foretold future events. For example, through the prophet Isaiah, Jehovah foretold the fall of Babylon. (Isaiah 13:19; 14:
14, 15. What does Isaiah's prophecy regarding Babylon reveal?
14 On October 5, 539 B.C.E., some 200 years after that prophecy was given, Babylon fell. * The ruler of the conquering army was Cyrus. Why is Cyrus' conquest significant? Can we be sure that Cyrus' conquest fulfilled Isaiah's prophecy?
15 The people of Babylon felt secure, but in one night their city was conquered. This demonstrates the futility of trusting in human rulers. Furthermore, Cyrus went on to fulfill another aspect of the prophecy. How did this show that the people could not prevent the fulfillment of the prophecy? Cyrus' forces were able to divert the Euphrates River, exposing the city's foundations!
16. (a) What did Isaiah prophesy regarding Babylon's downfall? (b) What does Isaiah's prophecy regarding Babylon reveal?
16 Regarding Babylon's fall, Isaiah had foretold: "Every foundation stone will come loose, and every hired hand will go away; and I will stir them up from their places," and "their gods will not save them." (Isaiah 13:20) This prophecy proved accurate when Babylon was overthrown. It became a desolate ruin. But Babylon was located about 80 kilometers (50 miles) south of present-day Baghdad, in Iraq, a very fertile area. So how could Isaiah have known what would happen to it? Jehovah inspired Isaiah to say: "I have declared the end from the beginning."
17. How do Bible prophecies demonstrate Jehovah's power?
17 To fulfill Bible prophecies is to demonstrate Jehovah's power. By revealing his purpose in advance, Jehovah shows his ability to control events and to bring about his will. (Proverbs 23:19) We can have confidence in "the strength of God's spirit."
"THE POWER OF GOD AT WORK"
18. What did the apostle Paul mean when he spoke of "the power of God"?
18 As we read earlier, the Bible is "God's powerful force." Its message has survived through the centuries, despite opposition from science and philosophy, and despite those who try to discredit it. The apostle Paul wrote: "The power of God is manifest in [its] wisdom, in [its] majesty, in [its] strength, in [its] ability to reach out to the depths, and in [its] capacity to discern thoughts and intents of hearts."
19, 20. (a) How can the Bible help us to cope with difficult situations? (b) How can we show appreciation for the Bible as God's inspired Word?
19 Reading "the power of God" can strengthen our faith. It can help us to face life's challenges with courage. It can motivate us to draw closer to God, and as we study the Bible, God's Word, we gain a deeper understanding of his personality and his purposes.
20 The Bible is God's gift to mankind. It is a book to be read, studied, and lived by. Consider how you can show greater appreciation for this provision from God by meditating on it. May this knowledge become clear to you in the light of God's guidance. This meaning and its context are best understood when presented in simple language.

text:
MWANA-A-ASA wĩtawa Julian aĩtye ũũ: "Mũthenya ũla neewie kwatangaswa kana mwanawa nĩwatengwa, neewie nthĩ ta yakulumana. Nĩwe wakwa mũkũũ, na twaĩ ndũũ mũno. Twatethasya maũndũ maingĩ mũno nĩ nake. Eanĩte e mwana mũseo mũno ĩndĩ o na tũtataĩĩe nĩwambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũte mũseo. Kĩveti kyakwa kyekalaa kĩkaĩa, na nĩnaaĩawa nĩ ũndũ ngũkĩkiakisya. Twekalaa tũkesa kwĩkũlya nĩ va twĩthĩwa twavĩtũũkanisye matambya tũimũea."
Ethĩwa mũndũ atiawa na woo wĩana ũu, vatonyeka ata tũkasya kana kũtenga Mũklĩsto nĩ nzĩa ya kwonany'a wendo? Maandĩko matũnengete kĩtumi kĩva kya kwosa ĩtambya ta yĩu yĩvyũvĩte ũu? Na kyo nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa mũndũ atengwa?
MAŨNDŨ ELĨ MATUMAA MŨNDŨ ATENGWA
Ve maũndũ elĩ matumaa ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova atengwa. Maũndũ asu no nginya moneke savalĩ ũmwe. Ũndũ wa mbee, no nginya mũndũ Ngũsĩ na mũvatise akethĩwa ekĩte naĩ ngito. Ũndũ wa kelĩ, no nginya mũndũ ũsu ethĩwe ate kwĩlila nũndũ wa naĩ ĩla wĩkĩte.
O na kau Yeova ndendaa twĩkale ta andũ eanĩu, ve ũtheu ũla wendaa athũkũmi make methĩwe naw'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova nĩwendaa mũno twĩvathane na naĩ ngito ta maũndũ ma ũlaalai, ũthaithi wa mĩvw'anano, ũng'ei, ũvutani, ũaani, na kũneenany'a na maveva mavuku.—1 Ako. 6:9, 10; Ũvu. 21:8.
We tyo ũkwĩtĩkĩla kana myolooto ĩla Yeova ũtũnengete ya mwĩkalĩle mũtheu nĩyaĩle na kana atũnengete ĩtũsũvĩe? Na nengĩ we nũũ ũtendaa kwĩkalany'a na andũ atheu, me mũuo, na matonya kwĩkwatw'a? Andũ ma ũko ũsu tũmonaa katĩ wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ, na vailyĩ ũu nũndũ wa wĩvĩto ũla twĩvĩtaa ĩla tweyumya tũmũthũkũme Ngai. Nĩtwĩvĩtaa kana tũkekalaa kwosana na myolooto ĩla ũtũandĩkĩe Ndetonĩ yake.
Ĩndĩ nata Mũklĩsto mũvatise akeka naĩ ngito nũndũ wa naĩ ĩla tũkuĩte? Ve o andũ amwe ma tene meekie naĩ ta ĩsu o na kau mamũthũkũmĩte Yeova me aĩkĩĩku, ĩndĩ ndaamakola vyũ. Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti nĩ ngelekany'o yĩsĩkĩe nesa. Nĩwalaalaie na oaana, ĩndĩ o na ekĩte oou mwathani Nathani amwĩie atĩĩ: "Yeova nũvetete naĩ yaku."—2 Sam. 12:13.
Ngai aekeie Ndaviti nũndũ nĩwoonie eelila kuma ngoonĩ. (Sav. 32:1-5) No ta ũu ũmũnthĩ. Mũthũkũmi wa Yeova atengawa ethĩwa ndekwenda kwĩlila na ndekũekana na mwĩkalĩle wake mũthũku. (Meko 3:19; 26:20) Atumĩa ala me kamitiinĩ ya sila moona mũndũ ũsu ndekwĩlila kuma ngoonĩ, no nginya mamũtenge.
Mwambĩĩonĩ no twone ũtwi ũla weekwa wa kũtenga mwĩki wa naĩ ta mũkalĩ mũno na ta ũte wa tei, na mũno mũno ethĩwa mũndũ ũla mũtenge nĩ mũndũ twĩ ndũũ mũno. Ĩndĩ Ndeto ya Yeova nĩtũnengete itumi nzeo ila itũtetheeasya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana kũtenga mũndũ nĩ nzĩa ya kwonany'a wendo.
ŨNDŨ MŨVANGO WA KŨTENGA ŨTONYA KŨTETHYA KĨLA MŨNDŨ
Yesũ nĩwawetie kana "ũĩ nũtalĩlawa ũlũngalu nĩ syana syaw'o." (Mt. 11:19) Kwoou mũvango ũũ mũseo wa kũtenga ala mate kwĩlila naĩ syoo nũetae ũsyao mũseo. Kwasũanĩa mosyao aa atatũ:
Kũtenga eki ma naĩ nĩkũtumaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩtaĩwa. Andũ mosaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova kwosana na ũndũ moona mwĩkalĩle witũ, nũndũ twĩtanĩaw'a nake. (Isa. 43:10) Mavinda amwe andũ mamũeleawa Yeova kwosana na ũndũ moona mwĩkalĩle wa andũ ala metanĩaw'a nake, wĩthĩwe nĩ mũseo kana nĩ mũthũku, o tondũ mwĩkalĩle wa mwana ũtonya kũtuma asyai make makathwa kana o makavũthw'a. Ĩsyĩtwa ĩseo ya Ngai nĩyĩtaĩawa ĩla ala metanĩaw'a nake maatĩĩa mwĩkalĩle ũla wonaa waĩle. Ĩvinda ya Esekieli nĩyendaa kũtutya ũndũ ta ũsu. Ĩvinda yĩu andũ ma mbaĩ ingĩ makilasya moona Mũyuti makamũlilikana Yeova.—Esek. 36:19-23.
Kwoou tweethĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku twĩthĩawa tũituma andũ mavũthya ĩsyĩtwa ĩtheu ya Ngai. Nĩkyo kĩtumi mũtũmwa Vetelo wanengie Aklĩsto ũtao ũũ: "Ta syana mbĩwi, mũtekwĩvw'anan'ya na mĩmeo yenyu mĩthũku ya tene ĩvinda yĩla mũteesĩ: ĩndĩ o tondũ ũla wamwĩtie nĩ mũtheu, o ta ũu ĩthĩwai atheu mwĩkalĩlenĩ wenyũ w'onthe wa thayũ; nĩkwĩthĩwa nikũandĩkĩtwe, Ĩthĩwai atheu; nũndũ nyie nĩ mũtheu." (1 Vet. 1:14-16) Vate nzika, mwĩkalĩle mũtheu nũtumaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩtaĩwa.
Ethĩwa ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩwĩkaa naĩ, nĩ laisi anyanyae na andũ angĩ mamwĩsĩ makethĩwa mesĩ naĩ ĩsu. Kwoou ĩla mũndũ ta ũsu watengwa, kyu kyonanasya kana Yeova e na kĩkundi kyake kya andũ atheu ala maatĩĩaa myolooto ĩla yĩ Maandĩkonĩ nĩ kana maendeee kwĩthĩwa na ũtheu ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve mũndũ ũmwe waendie ũmbanonĩ mũna waendeee Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ yĩ Switzerland na asya kana eenda kũtw'ĩka ũmwe wa kĩkundi kyu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mwĩĩtu-a-inyia aĩ anatengwa nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku. Aisye eenda kwĩkwatany'a na andũ ala "matesa kũmĩanĩsya na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku."
Kũtenga mwĩki wa naĩ nĩkũtetheeasya kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kĩkale kĩ kĩtheu. Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwatavisye Aklĩsto ala maĩ Kolintho ũthũku wa kwĩtĩkĩlya eki ma naĩ maendeee kũvulana namo. Aisye kana mwĩkalĩle wa eki ma naĩ no ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ ĩlawa yimbasya mũtu. Aandĩkie: "Ĩlawa ĩnini nĩyĩkaatasya kĩmũtũ kyonthe." Na ĩndĩ amea: "Mũvetei ĩndĩ ũsu mwathe, aume katĩ wenyu."—1 Ako. 5:6, 11-13.
Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa mũndũ "ũsu mwathe" Vaulo wawetie akũnaa ũlaalai o na atekwĩw'a nthoni. Namo ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa maĩ manambĩĩa kũmũtetea. (1 Ako. 5:1, 2) Takethĩwa mũndũ ũsu nĩwaekaniwe nake aendeee na naĩ yake e o vau kĩkundinĩ, no kwĩthwa Aklĩsto ala angĩ mesaa kwambĩĩa kũatĩĩa mĩkalĩle mĩthũku ya mũsyĩ ũsu wa Kolintho, naw'o nĩw'o weesĩkĩe na mwĩkalo ũvukĩte. Na ũu nĩ w'o nũndũ kũekana na andũ ala mekwĩka naĩ na ngũlũ kũtumaa ala angĩ mambĩĩa kũlekeleelya myolooto ya Ngai. (Mũta. 8:11) Na eka ũu, ala matesaa kwĩlila no matw'ĩke "mavia matonekaa" me ungu wa kĩw'ũ ala matonya kwananga vyũ mũĩkĩĩo wa ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ, o tondũ meli yanangawa nĩ mavia matenekee.—Yuta 4, 12.
Kũtenga mwĩki wa naĩ no kũtume avindũka kĩlĩko. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Yesũ nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa mwanake mũna kĩmaamai waumie mũsyĩ kwa ĩthe na athi kwanangĩa ũtiĩwa wake mwĩkalĩlenĩ ũte mũseo. Mwana ũsu esie kũmanya e mũselee kana eka mũsyĩ kwa ĩthe, vai vangĩ waĩ atonya kwĩkala e mũtanu kana e na andũ matonya kũmũtethya. Ĩndĩ nĩwesie kũvindũka kĩlĩko, eelila, na we mwene atw'a kwĩnũka. (Luka 15:11-24) Yesũ nĩwaeleisye ũndũ ĩthe wa mwana ũsu watanie ĩla woonie mwanae aalyũla ngoo, na kĩu nĩkĩtũtetheeasya kũmanya ũndũ Yeova wĩw'aa. Yeova mwene atũĩkĩĩthasya atĩĩ: "Nditanĩthaw'a nĩ kĩkw'ũ kya mũthũku; ĩndĩ nĩ kana ũla mũthũku ethyũũe atie mũendele wake na kwĩkala thayũ."—Esek. 33:11.
O ta ũu, kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kĩthĩawa kĩilyĩ o ta mũsyĩ, na kwoou andũ atenge nĩmatonya kwĩsa kũvindũka kĩlĩko makalilikana kĩla maaisye. Ũsyao wa mwĩkalĩle woo mũthũku vamwe na kũlilikana ũtanu ũla maĩ naw'o tene ĩla maĩ na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na Yeova na andũ make, nĩkũtonya kũtuma mavindũka kĩlĩko.
Nĩ kana ũtetheesye mũndũ mũtenge aalyũke, no nginya ũmwony'e nũmwendete na ũyĩthĩwa wĩ mũlũmu. Ndaviti aisye atĩĩ: "Ũla mũlũngalu nangũne, kũkeethĩwa kũseo; na nangan'ye, kũkeethĩwa ta mauta ĩũlũ wa mũtwe." (Sav. 141:5) Kwaelekany'a ũndũ ũsu na ũũ: Twasye mũndũ eekwetye kũya, na aendeee ayitwa nĩ kĩkũlũ kya nyama. Kĩlũmĩte vau mũlũkũ ndesa kũveva nesa na ndesa kwĩtethya. O na ndatonya kũneena. Mũndũ ũngĩ akaema kũmwĩtaana na mĩtũkĩ ndalea kũkw'a. Ĩndĩ ailangye ũu, mũnyanyae ayũka na aimũlumya mũongo nĩ kana kĩkũlũ kĩu kĩkĩle. O na kau ngundi ĩsu yĩ woo, nĩtonya kũmũtethya ndakakw'e. O ta ũu, Ndaviti nĩweesĩ kana mavinda angĩ nĩwaaĩle kũkanw'a nĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu nĩ kana aendeee nesa, o na ethĩwa etiwa ew'ĩte woo.
Mavinda maingĩ ũtonya kwĩthĩa ũkany'o ũla ũtonya kũtethya mwĩki wa naĩ no kũmũtenga. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwana wa Julian, ũla ũwetetwe mwambĩĩonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ, ekalile e mũtenge kwa myaka ta ĩkũmi, ĩndĩ mũthyanĩ wa myaka ĩsu nĩwaalyũlile mwĩkalĩle wake, asyoka kĩkundinĩ, nayu nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Mwana ũsu easya: "Kũtengwa nĩkw'o kwatumie nĩmanya nesa ũthũku wa mwĩkalo wakwa. Ũkany'o ũsu nĩw'o wambaĩle."—Aevl. 12:7-11.
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KŨKUA ALA ATENGE KWA NZĨA YA WENDO
Nĩ w'o kana ĩla mũndũ watengwa ngwatanĩo yake na Ngai yĩthĩawa yaanangĩka. Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana ngwatanĩo ĩsu yĩthĩawa yaanangĩka vyũ ũndũ ĩtatũngĩĩwa. Kwoou kĩla ũmwe witũ e na kĩanda waĩle kwĩanĩsya nĩ kana kĩeleelo kya kũtenga mwĩki wa naĩ kĩanĩe.
Atumĩa ala me na kĩvalũa kya kũtavya mũndũ kana nĩwatengwa maĩle kũtata methĩwe na wendo ta ũla wa Yeova. Ĩla meũmũtavya ũtwi woo, maĩle kũmũelesya me na tei, na maimũtavya nesa matambya ala waĩle kwosa enda kũtũngwa. Nĩ kana ala atenge mekale malilikene ũndũ matonya kwĩka nĩ kana mamũsyokee Yeova, mavinda kwa mavinda atumĩa no mamathokee ethĩwa ve ũndũ mekĩte makonany'a kana nĩmekwenda kũalyũka. *
Andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmatonya kwonany'a kana nĩmendete kĩkundi vamwe na mũndũ ũsu woo mũtenge kwa kwĩtĩkĩlana na ũtwi wa atumĩa. Julian easya atĩĩ: "Vai ĩvinda waĩ esa kũtw'ĩka ti mwanawa, ĩndĩ mwĩkalĩle wake nĩwatũvathanĩtye."
Onthe kĩkundinĩ nĩmaĩle kwonany'a wendo ũla waĩle kwa kũtata maikavulane na mũndũ mũtenge kana kũea ngewa nake. (1 Ako. 5:11; 2 Yoa. 10, 11) Meeka ũu matumaa ũkany'o ũla Yeova ũnengete mũndũ ũsu kwĩsĩla kũla kwĩ atumĩa ũmũtethya. Ũndũ ũngĩ ala me kĩkundinĩ matonya kwĩka nĩ kwenda mũnango andũ ma mũsyĩ ma ũla mũtenge na kũmakwata kw'oko. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nĩmethĩawa moomĩiw'e nĩ kũtengwa kwa mũndũ ũsu na mayaĩle kwĩkwa ũndũ ũtuma mona o namo ta mavathanĩtw'e na Aklĩsto ala angĩ.—Alo. 12:13, 15.
Mwana-a-asa Julian aminĩĩe na kwasya atĩĩ: "Mũvango wa kũtenga nũtwaĩle na nũtũtethasya twĩkale kwosana na myolooto ya Yeova. O na kau nĩ ũndũ ũtumaa andũ mew'a woo, ĩtina nũetae mosyao maseo. Keka nĩnananisye mwanawa ndethĩwa aaĩsa kũendeea nesa."

translation:
The child named Julian said this: "Tomorrow will be announced or a person will be dismissed, tomorrow is not a day for arguing. You are our elder, and we have come very far. We have discussed many things today because of him. Tell that young child to come here so that we can advise him on how to behave with respect. Your chair is very beautiful, and I am impressed by its craftsmanship. Let us sit down and eat so that when we are called, we will find ourselves prepared."
Someone who is loved by God, do they stumble or dismiss Christ for the sake of showing love? Can scriptures provide an answer regarding this difficult situation? And what causes a person to be dismissed?
REASONS WHY A PERSON IS DISMISSED
Here are some reasons why someone from Jehovah's organization is dismissed. These reasons may seem unfair to some. Firstly, refusing to associate with someone who has been disfellowshipped. Secondly, refusing to allow someone to preach to them while they are still in their wrongdoing.
But Jehovah wants us to be among those who please him, and there are qualities he dislikes. For example, Jehovah hates lying, stealing, adultery, violence, and associating with bad company.—1 Cor. 6:9, 10; Prov. 21:8.
So how should we feel about the standards Jehovah sets, or should we think they are too strict? And shouldn't we strive to align ourselves with good people, remain loyal, and avoid getting involved? Such people are often seen among children and young ones, and this is why we need to teach them to honor God. We need to teach them to obey his commandments.
Is it possible for a disfellowshipped Christian to regain favor with God? There are some who believe they can earn back God's favor through good works. King David is a good example. He sinned, but after repenting, Nathan told him: "Jehovah has also forgiven your sin."—2 Sam. 12:13.
God forgave David because he showed genuine remorse. (Ps. 32:1-5) But that is not all. One who pleases Jehovah is willing to confess his sins and turn away from wickedness. (Acts 3:19; 26:20) He uses others to help him see his errors so that he may repent and change.
Therefore, let us examine our hearts to see if we are determined to live up to Jehovah's standards, and let us not allow pride or fear to prevent us from confessing our sins and seeking forgiveness.
THE IMPORTANCE OF CONFESSION IN MAINTAINING LOYALTY
Jesus said that "the humble and mild-tempered ones" will inherit the earth. (Matt. 11:19) This principle applies when it comes to confessing our mistakes. Here are three reasons why:
Confessing shows that we value Jehovah's friendship. Many people value Jehovah's friendship more than their own life, and they want to remain close to him. (Isa. 43:10) Often, those who truly love Jehovah are deeply affected when they disappoint him, whether intentionally or unintentionally, and they want to repair any damage they have caused. Jehovah's spirit helps those who cherish his friendship to appreciate how their actions affect others. The account of Ezekiel illustrates this point. That prophecy foretold that God would cleanse his people and restore their relationship with him.—Ezek. 36:19-23.
We are motivated to live in a way that honors Jehovah because we value our relationship with him. This is why the apostle Peter wrote to fellow Christians: "Always be ready to give a reason for the hope that you have, but do so with gentleness and respect. Have a clear conscience, so that those who speak against your good conduct as Christians may be put to shame when they misrepresent you. For it is better to suffer for doing good, if it is God's will, than to suffer for doing wrong. Remember that Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example to follow." (1 Pet. 3:15-17) Therefore, a good reputation promotes Jehovah's name.
One of Jehovah's qualities is that he cares about his servants and feels their pain. When a person feels wronged, it can affect his view of Jehovah and his organization. Does he feel that Jehovah allows injustice? Or does he continue to trust in Jehovah's justice? For instance, imagine a man who decides to take his case to the European Court of Human Rights in Switzerland, hoping to find someone in the court who will side with him. Why might he do this? Because he feels alienated and wants to be vindicated by someone outside the Christian congregation. He may want to associate with people who will "sympathize with his feelings."
To isolate oneself is to weaken the Christian congregation. The apostle Paul urged the Christians in Corinth to unite and stop forming factions. He pointed out that such divisions reveal a fleshly attitude. He wrote: "A large body part causes more shame." And he added: "So, then, let us strive to maintain the unity of the Spirit with the bond of peace."—1 Cor. 12:25, 13.
Paul was appealing to them to put "spiritual things" first and not allow personal preferences to cause division. But some found it difficult to remain neutral and wanted to defend their favorite humans. (1 Cor. 3:1, 2) Such a person may have felt loyal to a certain elder and wanted to support him, even if that meant taking sides in a dispute among the Corinthians, and he may have been influenced by emotional appeals. And this could lead to associating with those who were causing trouble and encouraging others to disregard God's standards. (Matt. 8:11) Also, they may have been tempted to listen to "persuasive words" from opposers who could cleverly exploit their emotions, even though those words were deceptive.—Acts 4:12.
To maintain spiritual stability and avoid being misled, we need to strengthen our faith. Jesus illustrated this with the parable of the prodigal son, showing how a young man foolishly squandered his inheritance and ended up in a desperate situation. That young man came to his senses and realized that he could return home and be accepted by his father, even if he had to approach him humbly. We can also strengthen our faith, pray regularly, and seek Jehovah's guidance. (Luke 15:11-24) Jesus taught us the importance of a repentant attitude like that of the father who eagerly welcomed back his wayward son, and this helps us understand what Jehovah desires. Jehovah himself assures us: "I will take pleasure in the repentance of the wicked; I do not desire the death of anyone dying."—Ezek. 33:11.
Therefore, the Christian congregation provides a safe environment, and its members can help one another to stay spiritually strong despite various challenges. The joy of belonging to such a loving family and enjoying regular association with Jehovah and his people can motivate us to remain steadfast and continue preaching.
If you notice a brother or sister starting to stumble, kindly approach them with encouragement and offer assistance. David prayed: "Correct me when I stray, for I have acted unwisely." (Ps. 141:5) Consider this illustration: A dog may wander off, but we call it back so that it does not get lost or injured. Similarly, we should lovingly try to help those who are straying. And we must be willing to listen. A person who stubbornly refuses correction is likely to suffer serious consequences. If we do this, we show compassion and help others to regain their spiritual health. But sometimes, despite our best efforts, someone may choose to continue on a wrong course. In such cases, we have done our part, and we cannot force them to accept our counsel. However, David was confident that Jehovah would forgive even grievous sins if there was genuine repentance.
Many find it difficult to discipline children, especially when they themselves were raised without proper guidance. For example, Julian's son, who had been rebellious during his teenage years, began to improve after spending ten years in a boarding school. His father then tried to control him again, which led to resentment and eventually caused him to leave home and join a bad group. The young man later said: "Being sent away made me realize how much I valued my family. This time I will not make the same mistake."—Prov. 12:7-11.
WHY DISCIPLINE IS NEEDED TO SHOW LOVE
It shows that we care about an individual's relationship with God. It is not simply about enforcing rules, but about helping someone avoid doing something that could damage their spirituality. Let each of us examine ourselves and ask whether we appreciate the value of constructive criticism.
We can help others by being willing to correct them when they err, showing them love like that of Jehovah. But let us be tactful, speaking kindly and gently, and let us offer practical suggestions rather than just complaining. Sometimes those disciplined may initially resist, but if we continue to show them love, they may eventually accept our counsel and benefit from it.*
Experienced elders know that people respond better when they feel understood and when they sense that those disciplining them are sincerely interested in their welfare. Julian noted: "Sometimes the things we say to our children seem harsh, but they need to understand that we care."
The congregation can also help by demonstrating love for those who have erred by continuing to associate with them and offering encouragement. (1 Cor. 5:11; 2 John 10, 11) This can motivate such ones to regain Jehovah's favor and to cooperate with the Christian congregation. Why is this important? Because isolation can lead a troubled person to become discouraged and to drift away.—Acts 12:13, 15.
Young Julian admitted: "The thought of being disfellowshipped frightened me, but I realized that remaining loyal to Jehovah was more important than pleasing my friends. And I found that true friends will support you."—See The Watchtower of April 15, 1991, pages 21-23.

text:
"Nĩwakĩlan'ya vinya na Ngai na ĩngĩ na andũ, na wakĩlya vinya."
MBATHI: 23, 38
1, 2. No nginya athũkũmi ma Yeova mang'ang'ane na maũndũ meva?
KUMA ĩvindanĩ ya Aveli kũvika ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ yitũ, athaithi ala aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova methĩĩtwe maing'ang'ana mũno. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkĩie Aklĩsto Aevelania ĩũlũ wa ũndũ 'moomĩĩsye ũkĩlany'onĩ mũnene wa mathĩna' nĩ kana Yeova amende na aimaathima. (Aevl. 10:
2 Mbee vyũ, nĩtũkĩlanasya vinya na Satani na nthĩ ĩno yake nthũku. (Aev. 6:
3. Ngai atũmanyĩasya ata nĩ kana tũkite amaitha maitũ?
3 Ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Nĩvatonyeka tũkasinda masindanonĩ asu metete ũu? Nĩvatonyeka, ĩndĩ no nginya tũkite mũno. Mũtũmwa Vaulo eeyĩelekanilye na mũndũ wĩ ĩthaũnĩ ya ngundi asya: "Nĩkasya ngundi, ndeũkũna vathei." (1 Ako. 9:
4. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũikasindwe nĩ ũthũku?
4 Amaitha maitũ nĩmatonya kũtũkita ĩla tũtataĩĩe na maitũvalũkya ĩla tũte na vinya, na kwoou no nginya twĩkalae twĩ metho kĩla ĩvinda. Mbivilia ĩtũkanĩtye ĩkatwĩa: "Mũikakĩlw'e vinya nĩ ũthũku, ĩndĩ kĩlyai ũthũku vinya na ũseo." (Alo. 12:21) Ndeto ii, "Mũikakĩlw'e vinya nĩ ũthũku," nitwĩkĩĩte vinya nũndũ syĩtwony'a kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka tũkasinda ũthũku. No tũsinde ũthũku twaendeea kũwũkita. Ĩndĩ tũkaeka kwĩkala twĩ metho na tũkaeka kũkita, no tũsindwe nĩ Satani, nthĩ ĩno yake nthũku, na mĩĩ ĩno yitũ yĩ na naĩ. Mwa ndũkaaĩtĩkĩlye Satani atume ũleela na kũsindwa!
5. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũendeee kũng'ang'ana nĩ kana tũathimwe nĩ Ngai? (b) Twĩneenea andũ meva mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ?
5 Ethĩwa ala mekũkita nĩmeenda kũsinda, mayaĩle kũlwa nĩkĩ maendeee kũkita kaũ ũsu. Nĩ kana maathimwe nĩ Ngai na aimetĩkĩla, nĩmaĩle kwĩkalaa malilikene watho ũũ wa Ngai tũsomaa ĩandĩkonĩ ya Aevelania 11:6: "Ũla wũkaa kwa Ngai mũvaka etĩkĩle kana e vo, na ĩngĩ kana nũmanengae ĩtuvi ala mamũmanthaa." Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "mamũmanthaa" ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu nĩtũmĩawa kwonany'a mũndũ ũkwĩthing'ĩĩsya mũno na ũkwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ vyũ. (Meko 15:17) Maandĩko nĩmatũnengete ngelekany'o nzeo mũno sya aũme na aka amwe mething'ĩĩisye mũno mamanthe ũathimo wa Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve mavinda Yakovo, Lakeli, Yosevu, na Vaulo maitavĩwe nĩ maũndũ, ĩndĩ ngelekany'o yoo nĩyaĩkĩĩthisye vyũ kana mũndũ omĩĩsya nũathimawa mũno. Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya andũ asu ana mang'ang'anie mũno?
WŨMĨĨSYO NŨETAE MOATHIMO
6. Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Yakovo omĩĩsya, na ĩtina atuviwe ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
6 Kĩla kyatetheeisye mũthũkũmi ũmwe wa tene wa Ngai weetawa Yakovo aendeee kũng'ang'ana na ayũmĩĩsya, nĩ kũmwenda Yeova, kũsũvĩa ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova, na kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana Yeova akaathima nzyawa syake o tondũ wamwathĩte. (Mwa. 28:
7. (a) Nĩ thĩna wĩva mũnene wakwatie Lakeli? (b) Lakeli eekie ata nĩ kana aendeee kũng'ang'ana na ĩtina ayĩsa kũathimwa?
7 Nakyo kĩveti kya Yakovo kĩla kyeetawa Lakeli kyekalaa kyeteele mũno kyone ũndũ Yeova ũkeanĩsya watho ũla wathĩte mũũme wakyo. Ĩndĩ ve thĩna ũmwe kyoonaa ta kĩtesa kũũkĩlya vinya. Lakeli ndaĩ na syana. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu mũndũ mũka kwĩthĩwa ate na syana woonekaa wĩ thĩna mũnene mũno. Kwoou Lakeli aumisye va vinya wa kũendeea kũng'ang'ana na thĩna ũsu wamũtũlaa ngoo na ũtaĩ na ũtonyi wa kũũmina? Mbee Lakeli ndaaĩkya ngoo. Vandũ va ũu, aendeeie kũng'ang'ana na kũvoya na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo kingangĩ. Ĩtina Yeova nĩweewie mboya syake na amũathima na syana. Kwoou ti ũsengy'o kana ĩvinda yĩmwe Lakeli awetie ndeto ii e mũtanu mũno: "Nakĩlan'ya . . . na mokĩlan'yo manene, nakwa nakĩlya."
8. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva mũmũ wamũkwatie Yosevu kwa ĩvinda ĩasa, na nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva ũndũ weekie ne ngelekany'o nzeo kwitũ?
8 Vai nzika kana ngelekany'o ĩsu nzeo ya Yakovo na Lakeli nĩyatetheeisye mũno mwana woo ũla weetawa Yosevu amanya ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka akwatwa nĩ matatwa. Ĩla Yosevu waĩ na myaka 17 maũndũ make nĩmaalyũkile vyũ. Ata? Ana-a-ĩthe nĩmamũthooisye ũkombonĩ nũndũ wa kĩwĩu kĩla mamwĩw'ĩaa. Na ĩndĩ e Misili nĩwekiw'e yela mana na avekala myaka mingĩ. (Mwa. 37:
9. Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya Yakovo, Lakeli, na Yosevu nĩ kana tũkwate ũathimo wa Yeova?
9 Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũmwe ũendeee kũng'ang'ana naw'o na ũtonya kwĩthwa wĩ ĩtatwa kwaku. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa ũithĩnw'a mana vate ĩvĩtyo wĩkĩte, kana ũkethĩwa ũimenwa nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa wĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kana o kũneenewa naĩ. O na ĩngĩ, no kwĩthĩwa ve mũndũ ũkwilĩĩle maũndũ mate ma w'o no ũndũ wa kĩwĩu. Vandũ va kũeka ũsindwe nĩ matatwa asu, lilikana kĩla kyatetheeisye Yakovo, Lakeli, na Yosevu maendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova me atanu. Ngai nĩwamanengie vinya na amaathima nũndũ kĩla ĩvinda moonaa ngwatanĩo yoo nake yĩ ya vata vyũ. O na nĩmaendeeie kũng'ang'ana na kwĩka maũndũ kwosana na mboya syoo. Kwoou nũndũ twĩ mũthyanĩ vyũ wa mĩthenya ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo, ve vata mũnenange wa kũendeea kũlũmany'a na wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o! We nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye ũendeee kũkĩlany'a vinya, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ũendeee kwĩthing'ĩĩsya nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova?
ĨTHĨWA NA WENDI WA KŨNG'ANG'ANA ŨKWATE MOATHIMO
10, 11. (a) Nĩ maũndũ meva matonya kũtũkwata ũkethĩa no nginya tũng'ang'ane nĩ kana tũathimwe nĩ Ngai? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkae motwi maseo na tũivota kwĩkala tũte kũkw'a ngoo na kũvĩngĩĩswa?
10 Nĩ maũndũ meva matonya kũtũkwata ũkethĩa no nginya tũng'ang'ane nĩ kana tũkwate moathimo ma Ngai? Ũndũ ũmwe aingĩ mokitanaa naw'o nĩ mawendi mate maseo. Angĩ namo no nginya mang'ang'ane nĩ kana methĩwe na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Kana ũtonya kwĩthĩa we mwene ũing'ang'ana na thĩna wa mwĩĩ kana o ũkethĩwa wĩw'aa ta wĩ weka. O na ĩngĩ, tũyaĩle kũlwa kana amwe nĩmang'ang'anĩte mũno nĩ kana maekee mũndũ wamew'ĩthisye woo kana mũndũ wamavĩtĩisye. O na tũkethĩwa tũmũthũkũmĩte Yeova ĩvinda yĩana ata, no nginya ithyonthe tũendeee kũng'ang'ana nĩ kana tũkĩlye vinya maũndũ ala matonya kũtũsiĩĩa kũmũthũkũma Ngai ũla ũtuvaa ala aĩkĩĩku.
11 Kũneena ũla w'o, ti laisi o na vanini kwĩka motwi maseo na kũendeea kwĩkala twĩ Aklĩsto. Na kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩtumaa maũndũ asu methĩwa me vinya kwĩka nĩ ethĩwa ngoo yitũ nĩkũtũsukuma twĩke maũndũ mate maseo. (Yel. 17:9) Ethĩwa nũkwona ta ve vandũ ũtaendeee nesa, ndũkaeme o na vanini kũvoya ũnengwe veva mũtheu. Mboya na veva mũtheu nitonya kũũnenga vinya wĩke maũndũ ala wĩsĩ nĩ maseo na matonya kũtuma ũathimwa nĩ Yeova. Kwoou wamina kũvoya, ĩka kwĩanana na maũndũ ala waweta mboyanĩ. Tata mũno ũsomae kalungu kana ka Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya, na ũimantha ĩvinda ya kwĩmanyĩsya we mwene vamwe na ya kwĩka Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ.
12, 13. Aklĩsto amwe elĩ matetheeiw'e ata mokitane na wendi mũthũku?
12 Ve ngelekany'o mbingĩ syonanĩtye ũndũ Ndeto ya Ngai, veva wake, na mavuku maitũ itetheesye Aklĩsto kũsinda mawendi mathũku. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwanake ũmwe wa mũika nĩwasomie kĩlungu kyaĩ na kyongo, "Unawezaje Kushinda Tamaa Mbaya?," kĩla kyaĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Amkeni! ya 08/12/2003. Amina kũkĩsoma eekie ata? Aĩtye: "Nĩendeee kũtata nĩeke mosũanĩo mathũku. Ĩla nĩnasomie kĩlungunĩ kyu kana 'andũ aingĩ maendeee kũng'ang'ana mũnango nĩ kana masinde mosũanĩo asu,' nĩnĩnamanyie kana ndi weka ĩndĩ ve ana-a-asa aingĩ me na thĩna ta wakwa." O na ĩngĩ mwanake ũsu nĩwatethekie asoma kĩlungu kyaĩ na kyongo, "Je, Mungu Anakubali Ngono Isiyo ya Asili?," kĩla kyaĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Amkeni! ya 08/10/2003. Asoma kĩlungu kyu eethĩie kaĩ kwa andũ amwe ũsu nĩ ta "mwĩw'a mwĩĩnĩ" woo! (2 Ako. 12:7) Ĩndĩ maendeea kũng'ang'ana nĩ kana methĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseo, no methĩwe na wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Mwanake ũsu asyokie asya: "Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, nĩona no nĩtate kwĩkala nĩ mũĩkĩĩku kĩla mũthenya. Nĩmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kũtũmĩa ũseũvyo wake atũtetheesye kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku kĩla mũthenya ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ĩthũku."
13 O na ĩngĩ kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wa Amelika. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Nĩenda kũmũtũngĩa mũvea mwingĩ nũndũ wa kũendeea kũtũnenga kĩla twĩ na vata nakyo, ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩlĩte. Mavinda maingĩ nonaa nĩ ta inyie nandĩkĩwe maũvoo asu. Kwa myaka mingĩ nĩthĩĩtwe ndyũkitana na wendi wa kwĩka ũndũ mũna Yeova ũmenete. Mavinda amwe nĩw'aa ta nĩkya moko na ndieka kũkitana na wendi ũsu. Nĩnĩsĩ kana Yeova e tei na nũekeaa, ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩ na wendi ũsu mũthũku na nĩnĩsĩ nesa ndiũmenete na ngoo yonthe, nĩw'aa ta ndaĩle kwĩw'ĩwa tei nĩ Yeova. Kĩu nĩkĩtumĩte nĩkala ngĩthĩnĩka mũno. . . . Ĩla nĩnasomie kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, 'We wĩ na "Ngoo ya Kũmũmanya" Yeova?' ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/03/2013, nĩnĩnamanyie nesa vyũ kana Yeova ethĩawa na mea ma kũndetheesya."
14. (a) Vaulo eew'aa ata nũndũ wa mawonzu ala waĩ namo? (b) Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũsinde mawonzu ala twĩ namo?
14 Soma Alomi 7:
15. Nĩkĩ mboya ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũendeee kũmĩĩsya na tũyĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku?
15 Ve mavinda Ngai ũtonya kũtũeka nginya twonany'e twĩthĩnĩkĩa ũndũ mũna mũno wĩana ata. Kwa ngelekany'o, twasye ithyĩ ene (kana o mũndũ wa mũsyĩ) nĩtwakwatwa nĩ ũwau mũthũku kana nĩtweekwa ũndũ mũthũku. Twaĩle kwonany'a kana nĩtũmwĩkwatĩtye Yeova vyũ kwa kũmũvoya atũnenge vinya wa kũendeea kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku, atũtetheesye tũikasye ũtanu witũ, na aitũtetheesya ngwatanĩo yitũ nake ndĩkanangĩke. (Avi. 4:
ENDEEA KŨNG'ANG'ANA ŨKWATE MOATHIMO MA YEOVA
16, 17. Ũtw'ĩte kwĩka ata?
16 Ndevili endaa mũno kwona ũkw'ĩte ngoo, o na endaa mũno kwona ũyĩkya moko na kũeka kũng'ang'ana. Ĩndĩ tw'a vyũ 'kũlũmasya ũla ũseo.' (1 Ath. 5:
17 Kwoou o na maũndũ mathi ata, ndũkaleele. Endeea kwĩthing'ĩĩsya. Endeea kũng'ang'ana. Endeea kũmĩĩsya. Na ũyĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova 'akakũtulũĩla ũathimo, mũvaka vae ũthei wa kũwĩanĩa.'
