translation:
"I will praise God and also people, and they will praise."
MBATHI: 23, 38
1, 2. Why do Jehovah's witnesses feel concerned about new things?
FROM Abel's murder until today, many have felt that Jehovah is slow to act. The apostle Paul wrote to Christians in Rome about 'being convinced of the greatness of God's kindness' because God is patient. (Rom. 10:
2 However, we should remember that we are praising Satan and his works. (Rom. 6:
3. Will God forgive us even if we make mistakes?
3 That is why he asks: "Should we continue sinning so that grace may abound?" We should not, for this is what we do when we sin. The apostle Paul reasoned with a man who was troubled in conscience: "If you practice sin, then you become its slave." (1 Cor. 9:
4. Should we try even if we might fail?
4 Our mistakes can lead us to despair if we dwell on them instead of looking forward to success, and sometimes we may feel like giving up. But the Bible encourages us: "Do not let victory be snatched from you by calamity, for calamity does not come from God." (Prov. 12:21) Therefore, "Do not let victory be snatched from you" means that we should not give up just because something seems difficult. If we persevere and keep trying, we will overcome Satan and his works, and our future will be bright. Let us not allow Satan to send us into defeat!
5. (a) What can help us to remain steadfast even if we are afflicted by God? (b) How can we comfort new ones who are discouraged?
5 True worshipers often face trials, but they continue to serve faithfully despite their difficulties. They know that they have been approved by God and want to live up to the fine example set forth in Hebrews 11:6: "The man who approaches God must believe that he exists and that he becomes the rewarder of those who earnestly seek him." The Greek word rendered "earnestly seek" in this scripture conveys the idea of striving hard to please someone. (Mark 15:17) The Scriptures show us how important it is to please Jehovah by being diligent in our ministry. For instance, Jacob, Leah, Joseph, and Paul were tested, and their examples teach us that we can remain faithful even when facing great pressure. Can we learn anything from the examples of others who have remained steadfast?
WHY WE CAN REMAIN FAITHFUL
6. What helped Jacob to remain steadfast, and what resulted from it? (See accompanying picture on page 8.)
6 What helped a humble man named Jacob to stay active and zealous in his service was his desire to please Jehovah, his close relationship with Jehovah, and his confidence in Jehovah's promises to care for him. (Gen. 28:7.)
7. (a) What challenge did Leah face? (b) How did Leah show that she continued to strive to please Jehovah?
7 And Jacob's wife Leah also proved to be fertile, and Jehovah kept noticing her worth as a wife. Indeed, she had six sons! Leah knew that she was blessed. She felt grateful to have children. It seems that Leah realized that having children was a privilege. Did Leah ever wonder why she was so fruitful while Rachel was barren? Yes, Leah did. But instead of becoming jealous, she actively engaged in worship and showed appreciation. Jehovah responded favorably to her prayers and gave her more sons. So do not despair if you feel inadequate or if you face difficulties. Leah reminds us that we can continue to serve zealously despite our imperfections.
8. Why did Joseph's brothers resent him, and how did this lead to trouble for Joseph?
8 How did Jacob's favorite son, Joseph, become the object of his brothers' jealousy? Joseph was just 17 years old when he began receiving special attention from his father. Was this because he was particularly outstanding? No, it simply made his brothers envious. Eventually, they sold him into slavery in Egypt, where he spent many years. (Gen. 37:)
9. What lessons can we learn from the examples of Jacob, Leah, and Joseph about cultivating Jehovah's favor?
9 Consider how one mistake can lead to another, often with disastrous results. People may start out by telling small lies, then bigger ones, or they may begin associating with bad company. And so on, until they find themselves doing things they never imagined they would. The brothers who mistreated Joseph thought they had gotten away with their deed, but their actions continued to affect Jacob, Leah, and Joseph and ultimately led them closer to Jehovah. God understands our weaknesses and imperfections, yet he expects us to strive to do what is right. He also wants us to reflect on the consequences of our actions. So let us examine ourselves honestly and ask: 'Am I letting pride influence my decisions, or am I allowing myself to be drawn into wrongdoing?' If we do, we will strengthen our determination to live in harmony with Jehovah's standards! Are you determined to continue examining yourself honestly, or will you allow yourself to drift away from Jehovah?
LIVE BY PRINCIPLES THAT PLEASE GOD
10, 11. (a) What can make it difficult for us to remain faithful when faced with trials, and how can we cope? (b) Why is it important that we listen to our conscience and avoid becoming self-righteous?
10 What can make it difficult for us to remain faithful when faced with trials, and how can we cope with God's discipline? One factor is the pressure from others. We might feel tempted to compromise our principles because of fear of disapproval. Or we may be inclined to rationalize our mistakes, thinking that everyone makes them. Furthermore, we may struggle when someone has wronged us or when someone has hurt our feelings. But we should remember that Jehovah always supports those who love him, and we need to keep striving to please him, even when facing difficulties that seem insurmountable.
11 In this regard, do not hesitate to seek advice from mature Christians. One thing that can help us stay spiritually strong is to focus on positive things. (Jer. 17:9) Be willing to accept correction, and do not let pride prevent you from making changes. Pride can lead to foolish decisions and can cause us to stumble. However, being humble will enable us to draw closer to Jehovah. So continue to pray, and reflect on what you have learned. Regularly read your Bible and meditate on its meaning, and strive to apply Scriptural principles in your life.
12, 13. How did one Christian sister deal with a difficult situation?
12 Many find it helpful to study the Bible regularly, to share with others, and to imitate Christ's example. For instance, one young woman was helped by an article titled "How Can You Conquer Bad Habits?" in the December 8, 2003, issue of Awake!. Did she put it to good use? She says: "I kept thinking about how I could overcome my bad habits. But when I read that 'many people struggle with similar temptations,' I realized I wasn't alone." Another young woman found help in the October 8, 2003, issue of Awake!, in an article titled "Does God Approve of Same-Sex Relations?" Reading that article helped her to see why some feel "different." (2 Cor. 12:7) Those who struggle with temptation may be influenced by negative thoughts or by feelings of inadequacy. This young woman explains: "Because of what I learned, I make it a point to spend time in prayer each day. I thank Jehovah for his loving guidance and for helping us to remain morally clean."
13 And so did a brother in America. This brother writes: "I want to express my deep gratitude for the continued spiritual food, especially during this time of difficulty. Many times I have felt as though I were being carried along. For years I battled with a secret sin that separated me from Jehovah. At times I felt as though I had reached rock bottom and could go no further. Yet I knew that Jehovah would forgive me if I confessed, and I also knew that I needed to work at repairing my relationship with him. So I made up my mind to stay close to him. . . . But then I read the article 'Do You Have "The Knowledge" of Jehovah?' in The Watchtower of March 1, 2013, and I realized that Jehovah truly cares about my welfare."
14. (a) What can strengthen our resolve? (b) How can we strengthen our resolve?
14 Read Romans 7:
15. How can we receive help to continue making progress and to remain spiritually strong?
15 God can help us cope when we face difficult trials. For example, we might be tempted to give up because of some mistake we have made or something bad that has happened to us. We need to remember that Jehovah is willing to forgive us if we repent, he will help us correct our mistakes, and he will comfort us when we feel discouraged. (Ps. 4:
KEEP BUSY IN JEHOVAH'S SERVICE
16, 17. What can we do?
16 It is good to find ways to stay busy, or to find things to occupy your mind. In fact, we should strive "to make the best use of our time." (1 Thess. 5:
17 Whether you are young or old, keep yourself occupied. Keep busy. Keep learning. Keep progressing. And trust that Jehovah will "strengthen your heart, so that you may be courageous and not fear."

text:
MYAKANĨ ya 1930, asyai makwa, James na Jessie Sinclair, maumie Scotland mathamĩĩa kĩsio kya New York City kĩtawa Bronx. Ũmwe katĩ wa andũ ala mamanyanie mbee aĩ Willie Sneddon, ũla o nake waumĩte Scotland. Makomanie na ĩtina wa ndatĩka nini mambĩĩa kũneena ĩũlũ wa mĩsyĩ yoo. Kĩu kyeekĩkie myaka kauta ndanamba kũsyawa.
Inyia-akwa atavisye Willie kana vakililye vatiele o vanini ũla Kaũ Mũnene wambĩĩe, ĩthe na mwanake mũkũũwe makw'ĩĩa ũkanganĩ (North Sea) ĩla ĩsiwa yoo ya kũtea makũyũ yakimie mbomu yateketwe kĩw'ũnĩ. Willie amũsũngĩie amwĩa, "Ĩthe-aku e hell!" * Willie aĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na o na kau inyia-akwa nĩwatelemile mũno nĩ kwĩw'a ũu, ũu nĩw'o wakwatie ũw'o wa Mbivilia.
Kĩla Willie wawetie nĩkyasaanĩisye Mami nũndũ we eesĩ ĩthe aĩ mũndũ mũseo. Ĩndĩ Willie asyokie amũkũlya atĩĩ: "No ũtane ngakwĩa o nake Yesũ aendie hell?" Nĩvo ĩndĩ Mami walilikanile ĩmanyĩsyo ya kanisa yĩla mbeenĩ vyũ yaĩtye kana Yesũ aendie hell na athayũũkw'a mũthenya wa katatũ. Kwoou ambĩĩe kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Ethĩwa hell nĩ vandũ ve mwaki vathĩnĩaw'a ala athũku, nĩkĩ Yesũ waendie vo?' Kĩu nĩkyatumie Mami enda mũno kũmanya ũla w'o. Ambĩĩe kũendaa maũmbanonĩ Kĩkundinĩ kya Bronx na avatiswa mwaka wa 1940.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu asyai Aklĩsto mayeekĩawa vinya mũno memanyĩsye Mbivilia na syana syoo. Kwoou nĩ mũnini natiawa na Tata wikendi ĩla Mami wĩ maũmbanonĩ na ũtavany'a. Ĩtina wa myaka ĩte mingĩ nĩ na Tata nĩtwambĩĩe kũthi ũmbanonĩ na Mami. Mami aĩ na kĩthito kingĩ mũno kya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, na nĩweemanyĩasya Mbivilia na andũ kauta. O na ve ĩvinda weemanyĩasya na amanyĩw'a amwe make me kĩkundi nũndũ maĩ atũi. Naendaa nake ũtavany'a ĩla twavinga sukulu. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩnamanyie Mbivilia mũno na namanya ũndũ ndonya kũmanyĩsya angĩ kĩla yaasya.
Nĩnĩlilaa nũndũ ĩla naĩ mũnini ndyoosaa ũw'o kwa ũito. Neekaa kũũthaũkĩa. Ĩndĩ nĩ na myaka ta 12 nĩnatw'ĩkie mũtavany'a wa Ũsumbĩ na nambĩĩa kũtavany'a ndeũtĩĩa. Na nĩ na myaka 16 nĩneeyumisye nĩmũthũkũme Yeova na navatisĩwa ũmbanonĩ mũnene waĩ Toronto, Canada, kwĩ Matukũ 24, Mwei wa 7, 1954.
KŨTHŨKŨMA MBETHELI
Ana-a-asa amwe kĩkundinĩ kitũ mathũkũmaa Mbetheli tene na mauma, na vaĩ angĩ maendeee na ũthũkũmi ũsu. Ngelekany'o yoo yandethisye mũno. Naw'o ũtũĩka ũla maĩ naw'o wa kumya maũvoo na kũmanyĩsya angĩ ũw'o nĩwambendeeasya mũno. O na kau alimũ makwa mendaa nĩthi yunivasiti, kĩeleelo kyakwa kyaĩ kũthi Mbetheli. Kwoou nĩ ũla ũmbanonĩ naendie Toronto nĩnanenganie valũa wakwa wa kũkũlya nĩthi Mbetheli. Nĩneekie ũu ĩngĩ mwakanĩ wa 1955 nĩ ũmbanonĩ mũnene waĩ Yankee Stadium, New York City. Nekalangile o vanini na neetwa Mbetheli ya Brooklyn kwĩ Matukũ 19, Mwei wa 9, 1955. Ĩvinda yĩu naĩ na myaka 17. Mũthenya wa kelĩ nathi Mbetheli natwaiwe kũthũkũma 117 Adams Street, vala mavuku makwatanĩaw'a na kũseũvw'a. O na vatathelete ĩvinda ĩasa, nĩnambĩĩe kũthũkũma na masinĩ yakwatanasya tũvunge twa mathangũ 32 na ĩitũtwaa masinĩnĩ ĩngĩ ĩla yatumanasya tũvunge tũu tũkatw'ĩka ĩvuku.
Nekalile mũvĩanĩ ũsu wa kũseũvya mavuku mwei ũmwe na nathamĩĩw'a Mũvĩanĩ wa Makaseti nũndũ nĩneesĩ kũkũna kyavuleta. Ĩvinda yĩu ethĩwa mũndũ nĩwakũlya atũmĩawe makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Amkeni! ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa moosaa tũvati tũnini (stencils) makatumba ĩsyĩtwa yake na vala wĩkalaa nĩ kana makatũtũmĩaa kĩla mwei kũtumba ĩthangũnĩ yĩla meũmũtũmĩa makaseti nayo. Ĩtina wa myei mĩvũthũ nĩnathamĩĩiw'e mũvĩanĩ ũngĩ wĩtawa Idara ya Upakizi na Usafirishaji. Klaus Jensen nĩwe waũngamĩe mũvĩa ũsu na nĩwangũlilye ethĩwa no nende kũendanasya na ndeleva ũla watwaaa makotoni ma mavuku kĩlĩndĩnĩ nĩ kana matwawe nthĩ ingĩ. Na eka ũu, veethĩawa na mbumbu sya makaseti syaaĩlĩte kũtwawa vosita nĩ kana itũmwe ikundinĩ ila syaĩ Amelika. Mwana-a-asa Jensen ambĩie kana wĩa ũsu ndwĩlea kũmbaka mwĩĩ. Ĩvinda yĩu naĩ o na kĩlo ta 57 na nathekevete ta leli, ĩndĩ wĩa ũsu nĩwatumie nĩkwata vinya. Vate nzika, Mwana-a-asa Jensen nĩweesĩ kĩla kyaĩ kĩtonya kũndethya!
O na ĩngĩ Mũvĩa wa Makaseti nĩw'o woombanĩasya ikundi makaseti ala syeetya. Wĩa ũsu nĩw'o watumie nĩmanya kaĩ Brooklyn vatumbĩawa makaseti ma ithyomo mbingĩ na maitũmwa isionĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ! Ithyomo mbingĩ katĩ wa isu ndyasyĩsĩ, ĩndĩ nĩnatanaa mũno kũmanya kana vaĩ makaseti ngili na ngili matũmawa kũndũ kũasa mũno ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ nĩnesie kũthi isionĩ mbingĩ syatũmĩaa ithyomo isu, o na kau ĩvindanĩ yĩu ndyeesĩ kana kĩu kĩkeekĩka.
Mwakanĩ wa 1961 nĩnambĩĩe kũthũkũma Ovisinĩ wa Mũii wa Kĩnandũ na naũngamĩwe nĩ Grant Suiter. Ĩtina wa kũthũkũmanga myaka o kauta, nĩngũlilikana mũthenya ũmwe ndyĩtwa ovisinĩ wa Nathan Knorr. Myakanĩ ĩsu Mwana-a-asa Knorr nĩwe waũngamĩe wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a nthĩ yonthe. Ambĩie kana mwana-a-asa ũmwe ũthũkũmaa nake nũkũthi Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Ũsumbĩ mwei ũmwe, na amina ethi Mũvĩanĩ wa Ũthũkũmi. Kwoou ambĩie ninyie ngwosa mwanya wake, na ngathũkũmaa na Don Adams. Ũsengy'o nĩ kana Don nĩwe nanengie ũla valũa wakwa wa kũkũlya nĩtwe Mbetheli ĩla naĩ ũla ũmbanonĩ mũnene nĩwetie weekiwe mwaka wa 1955. Ovisinĩ ũsu wa Nathan Knorr, vaĩ ana-a-asa angĩ elĩ mathũkũmaa vo, namo maĩ Robert Wallen na Charles Molohan. Twĩ ana twathũkũmie ĩmwe kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 50. Ũtanu ũla ngwatĩte nũndũ wa kũthũkũma na aũme ta asu alũmu kĩ-veva nĩ mwingĩ mũno!—Sav. 133:1.
Kwambĩĩa mwaka wa 1970, kĩla ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe kana ĩlĩ, nĩnanengawe syumwa iana ũna nĩthokee movisi mana ma ũvonge ma Watch Tower Society. Ĩsu nĩyo yeetawa ndambũka ya mũsyaĩĩsya wa kĩsio kya nthĩ. Ndambũkanĩ isu nĩnaneenaa na ala mathũkũmaa Mbetheli vamwe na amisonalĩ nĩ kana nĩmekĩe vinya. O na nĩnasiasya lekoti sya ovisi wa ũvonge. Natanaa ta kĩ nakomana na amwe maĩ ilasinĩ ila syaĩ sya mbee vyũ sya Sukulu ya Ngileati na maendeee kũmũthũkũma Ngai me o kũla matũmĩtwe! Nĩmĩtalaa ta ndaĩa nene mũno kwona nĩkwatĩte mwanya wa kũthyũũka nthĩ mbee wa 90 nĩ wĩanĩ ũsu!
NĨNAKWATIE MŨTINDANY'A MŨSEO
Athũkũmi onthe ma Mbetheli ya Brooklyn maaĩĩwe ikundi ila syaĩ New York City. Nyie naaĩĩwe kĩkundi kyaĩ kĩsionĩ kya Bronx. Kĩkundi kĩla kyaĩ kya mbee Bronx kyaĩ kyeanie na kĩkasyaa kĩngĩ. Kyaanĩka, kĩla kyaĩ kĩkũũ nĩkyo kyatw'ĩkie Kĩkundi kya Upper Bronx na nĩkyo neethĩawa.
Myakanĩ ya 1960, mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mũsyĩ wake ma kuma Latvia nĩmakwatie ũw'o me ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya Bronx, na mathamĩĩa kĩsionĩ kya kĩkundi kĩu neethĩawa. Mwĩĩtu woo mũkũũ wĩtawa Livija nĩwoosie ũvainia wa kĩla ĩvinda amina sekondalĩ oou. Ĩtina wa myei mĩnini, nĩwathamĩĩe Massachusetts nũndũ vaĩ vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Athi nĩnambĩĩe kũmũandĩkĩaa valũa ngamũtavya maũndũ maseo ala maendeee kĩkundinĩ, nake asyokaa akambandĩkĩa moseo ala wonete aitavany'a taoninĩ ĩla weethĩawa ya Boston.
Myaka o mĩnini ĩtina wa ũu, Livija nĩwatw'ĩkie vainia wa mwanya. Nũndũ nĩwendaa kwĩka kyonthe kĩla ũtonya kwondũ wa Yeova, nĩwausũisye valũa wa Mbetheli na eetwa mwaka wa 1971. Noonie kau ta kaũndũ Yeova weeka ambony'e kana Livija no atw'ĩke kĩveti kĩseo. Twatwaanie Matukũ 27, Mwei wa 10, 1973, na tweewie mũyo mũno Mwana-a-asa Knorr eetĩkĩla kũtumĩsya ũvoo wa alũsi. Ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 18:22 yaĩtye: "Ũla ũmeasya kĩveti nũmeasya kĩndũ kĩseo; na kwona ũseo kuma kwa Yeova." Yeova nũmbonetye ũseo nĩ na Livija kwa kũtwĩtĩkĩlya tũmũthũkũme Mbetheli kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 40. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, twĩthĩawa kĩkundinĩ kĩ kĩsionĩ kya Bronx.
KŨTHŨKŨMA VAMWE NA ANA-A-ASA MA KLĨSTO
Nĩnatanĩaa mũno kũthũkũma na Mwana-a-asa Knorr. Ndanoaw'a nĩ kũmũthũkũma Yeova na nĩwendete amisonalĩ mũno o na methĩwe me va ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Mavinda maingĩ weethĩaa amisonalĩ asu nĩmo maĩ Ngũsĩ sya mbee kũkinya nthĩ ĩla matũmĩtwe. Tweewie thĩna mũno Mwana-a-asa Knorr eethĩwa na kanza mwaka wa 1976. Ĩla wavikie vandũ weethĩa ndokĩla kĩtandanĩ, mũthenya ũmwe nĩngũlilikana aingũlya nĩmũsomee ũvoo mũna ũtanamba kũtumbĩthw'a. Ndanamũsomea ambĩie nĩte Frederick Franz o nake ethukĩĩsye. Nesie kwĩthĩa kaĩ Mwana-a-asa Knorr atanawaa atũmĩaa ĩvinda yingĩ aisomea Mwana-a-asa Franz maũvoo ta asu nũndũ aĩ na thĩna wa metho!
Mwana-a-asa Knorr akwie mwaka wa 1977, ĩndĩ ala mamwĩsĩ na mamwendete nĩmakiakĩiw'e nĩ kũmanya kana ekalĩte e mũĩkĩĩku nginya mũthya. (Ũvu. 2:10) Ĩtina wa vau Mwana-a-asa Franz nĩwe wooseleeile kĩanda kya kũtongoeasya wĩa witũ.
Mwana-a-asa Knorr aikw'a, naĩ mũandĩki wa Milton Henschel, ũla wathũkũmĩte na Mwana-a-asa Knorr kwa myaka mingĩ mũno. Mwana-a-asa Henschel ambĩie kana wĩa ũla mũnene yu ngatethasya Mbetheli nĩ kũtetheeasya Mwana-a-asa Franz maũndũnĩ onthe ala ũkwenda. Mavinda maingĩ namũsomeaa maũvoo matanamba kũtumbĩthw'a. Mwana-a-asa Franz aĩ kĩlilikano kĩseo mũno na kĩlĩko kyake kĩyeelelũkaa ĩla ũkũsomewa kĩndũ. Nĩnatanĩie mũno kũmũtetheesya nginya ĩla waminie ũthũkũmi wake ĩũlũ wa nthĩ kwĩ Mwei wa 12, 1992.
Myaka 61 ĩla nthũkũmĩte Mbetheli ĩthelete ta ĩveny'a. Asyai makwa nĩmakwie, ĩndĩ maĩ aĩkĩĩku na nĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kũmathokya kũũ nthĩ ĩla ĩkethĩwa yĩ nzaũ. (Yoa. 5:28, 29) Vai kĩndũ nthĩ ĩno ĩtonya ũtũnenga tũkakĩelekany'a na ndaĩa ya mwanya ĩla tũkwatĩte ya kũthũkũma vamwe na aũme na aka aĩkĩĩku nĩ kana tũtetheesye andũ ma Ngai ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Nĩ na Livija no twasye tũte na nzika kana myaka yonthe ĩla twĩthĩĩtwe ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe, "ũtanu wa Yeova [nũtw'ĩkĩte] vinya" witũ.—Nee. 8:10.
Vai mũndũ wĩsa kũtw'ĩka aĩ ate vo ũseũvyo wa Yeova ndũsonga, na wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ ndũendeea. Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno na nĩtalaa ta ũndũ mũnene kwona nthũkũmĩte na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ me mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu myaka ĩsu yonthe. Aklĩsto aingĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta ala naathũkũma namo yu tũi namo kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩndũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mwanya ũla ngwatĩte wa kũtethya wĩa wa Yeova nĩ vamwe na Aklĩsto ta asu aĩkĩĩku.

translation:
In the 1930s, a couple, James and Jessie Sinclair, emigrated from Scotland to the borough of New York City known as the Bronx. One of the people they quickly got to know was Willie Sneddon, who also came from Scotland. They enjoyed conversations and often discussed various subjects. A certain incident happened years later that I will recount.
Willie once told me that when he was a boy, his father took him and his older brother on a trip (North Sea) to an island where they would catch fish which were then cooked over a fire. Willie mimicked him saying, "It smelled like hell!" * Willie was one of Jehovah's Witnesses and he said this experience helped him appreciate the truth, which is found in the Bible.
Whenever Willie spoke about it, he always asked Mother, "Don't you think Jesus went to hell?" That is how Mother began to investigate the church's teaching regarding whether Jesus went to hell and suffered for three days. She reasoned that if hell is where wicked people suffer torment, why would Jesus go there? This prompted Mother to look further into the matter. She started attending meetings at Kingdom Hall in the Bronx and was baptized in 1940.
From then on, she became a dedicated Christian, diligently studying the Bible and sharing its message. She was very active in the ministry, and Father joined her in the field service. For many years, Father and I accompanied Mother in the ministry. Mother had a strong desire to share the good news with others, and she enthusiastically used the Bible in her witnessing work. She often invited those interested to our home and shared what she learned with them. We also attended school while doing so. Because of this, I came to learn much about the Bible and developed a love for sharing it with others whenever possible.
I remember well how devoted my parents were to the truth. I admired their steadfastness. When I was about 12 years old, I took part in the summer pioneer service and enjoyed it immensely. And when I was 16 years old, I symbolized my dedication to Jehovah and was sent to serve in a large territory in Toronto, Canada, on July 24, 1954.
MY LIFE STORY
Some brothers and sisters lovingly encouraged me to join Bethel, and others continued to support me in my ministry. However, she advised me against it. But I felt that I needed more training and experience so that I could better help others. So I went back to school to finish university, with the goal of returning to Bethel. It was during this time that I met my future wife in Toronto while serving in the Bethel home. I recall that in the spring of 1955, there was a large gathering at Yankee Stadium, New York City. We traveled there and then went to Bethel headquarters in Brooklyn on September 19, 1955. I was just 17 years old. The next day we began our assignment at 117 Adams Street, near the subway and bus stops. There, we helped to prepare meals for the construction workers who were building a new wing of 32 apartments and installing many more windows.
I spent some time working in the shipping department each month, assisting with the preparation of packages for the Massachusetts circuit. At that time, we would use stencils to create large signs that were displayed in the territory to advertise the publications. The printing department also prepared smaller signs that were used to promote the magazines. During those busy months, I worked in another department called the Packing and Shipping Department. Klaus Jensen supervised this work and he taught us how to load trucks with cartons of literature, often requiring us to lift heavy loads. And sometimes, we had to unload boxes of books from ships arriving from America. My brother Jensen asked me if I wanted to stay longer. At that time, I weighed about 57 kilograms and I was quite thin, but I felt strong enough to handle the work. Later, my brother Jensen always said that I was capable of doing anything!
And furthermore, the Massachusetts circuit overseer was very accommodating. We were able to send publications to Brooklyn where they were distributed to many congregations and pioneers, which greatly helped to expand the work. Many people responded favorably, and I was happy to learn that the publications were being put to good use. Over the years, I have seen many people benefit from the publications, and I am glad that I had a part in making them available.
In 1961, I began serving at the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead and was assigned to Grant Suiter. After several years of training, I was appointed as an instructor at Gilead under Nathan Knorr. In recent years, Brother Knorr oversaw all our teaching work. He told us about one brother who trained with him at the Kingdom Ministry School for a month, and he commented on how capable the ministerial servant was. He asked me if I knew what his assignment was, and I said that he was training with Don Adams. It seems that Don was the one who recommended that I take over the Bethel home cooking when the cook became seriously ill in 1955. This Gilead class of Nathan Knorr's, included many brothers who later became prominent, such as Robert Wallen and Charles Molohan. We trained together for almost 50 years. The joy I experienced in connection with the training work and seeing so many become zealous ministers was great indeed!—Ps. 133:1.
From 1970 onward, each year or so, I would receive an invitation to visit various congregations and give talks sponsored by the Watch Tower Society. That is how I came to know the circuit work. This circuit work brought me into contact with many brothers serving at Bethel and also with individuals whom I encouraged. And I continued to write letters to those in full-time service. I was grateful to be able to associate with them and to continue supporting them in their ministry! I realize now how much I appreciated having nearly 90 years to preach the good news!
I APPRECIATED MY ASSIGNMENT
All the Bethel homes in Brooklyn were located in the borough of New York City. We lived in a neighborhood called the Bronx. Each congregation in the Bronx had its own unique characteristics. For example, the largest congregation was known as the Upper Bronx Congregation and it was quite active.
In the 1960s, a young couple from Latvia moved to this area of the Bronx, and they attended meetings at our congregation. The husband's name was Livija and he worked part-time as a second-hand store clerk. After some time, they moved to Massachusetts where his sister lived and who was a pioneer. He wrote to me asking me to send encouraging literature to her and others, and she promised to share it with the pioneers in the Boston area.
Several years later, Livija expressed a desire to serve full-time. And so, I encouraged him to apply to Bethel and he was accepted in 1971. Soon after, Jehovah showed his approval when Livija also qualified for Bethel service. We were married on March 27, 1973, and Brother Knorr kindly arranged for us to be sent out as regular pioneers. Proverbs 18:22 says: "A man finds joy when he finds favor, but kindness comes to a man who seeks God." Jehovah has shown us favor, both Livija and myself, by allowing us to serve at Bethel for over 40 years. Until now, we continue serving in the congregation at the Kingdom Hall in the Bronx.
TO HELP OTHERS AND CHILDREN OF CHRIST
I especially enjoyed working with Brother Knorr. More than that, I enjoyed pleasing Jehovah and I appreciated his personal interest in me and my brothers. Many times his personal visits brought encouragement to those of us who were relatively new. We worked closely with Brother Knorr from about 1976 onward. On occasion, when he visited various congregations, someone would ask him to comment on a particular scripture. I remember once he asked me if I could find a scripture to support a certain point. He then told me that Frederick Franz had suggested it. It seemed that Brother Knorr often used scriptures that Brother Franz had researched—and he did so skillfully!
Brother Knorr died in 1977, and while we missed him and appreciated his counsel, we were comforted knowing that he was in God's memory. (Eccl. 2:10) In time, Brother Franz took the lead in giving direction to our work.
Brother Knorr was succeeded by Milton Henschel, who had worked closely with Brother Knorr for many years. Brother Henschel explained that the Governing Body wanted to assist Brother Franz in whatever way possible. Many times I assisted him in preparing talks. Brother Franz always had a great deal of material and his notes were very thorough, making it easy to research a subject. I especially enjoyed helping him until his death on December 12, 1992.
The 61 years I spent serving at Bethel passed quickly. Though I have grown older, I still enjoy thinking about the hope of eternal life that was set before us. (John 5:28, 29) And how grateful I am that this hope motivates us to continue sharing the good news with others and to help people learn about God's purposes. My wife, Livija, and I are thankful for all the years we devoted to proclaiming the Kingdom message, "that they may know there is Jehovah [who] makes them secure."—Nah. 8:10.
There is someone who will remind us that Jehovah's organization is superior, and those who oppose the truth will be thwarted. This is my joy and I rejoice to see so much being accomplished by Bethel and its auxiliary pioneers throughout the years. Many Christians appreciate the assistance given to them by brothers who continue to serve faithfully. So I gladly use what little strength I have left to speak about Jehovah with fellow Christians and to encourage them.
[Footnotes]
^ par. 5 The terms Sheol and Hades refer to the common grave, also called Gehenna, unlike the hell taught by some religions. The Bible uses the term "hell."

Ndĩni syonthe nimwendeeasya Ngai?
Tũtonya kũmanya ndĩni ĩla yaw'o ata?
Ala mathaithaa Ngai kwa w'o ũmũnthĩ naaũ?
1. Tũkatetheka ata twamũthaitha Ngai ũndũ vaĩle?
YEOVA NGAI nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa mũno na endaa tũtetheke kumana na ũtongoi wake. Twamũthaitha ũndũ vaĩle, tũkatana na kwĩsũvĩana na mathĩna maingĩ. O na akatũathima na kũtũtetheesya. (Isaia 48:17) Ĩndĩ kwĩ ndĩni mbingĩ ũmũnthĩ ila syaasya imanyĩasya w'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Ĩndĩ imanyĩasya maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai nũũ na ũndũ wendaa twĩke.
2. Tũtonya kũmanya ata ũndũ twaĩle kũmũthaitha Yehova, na nĩ ngelekany'o yĩva ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya kũelewa nesa?
2 Ũtonya kũmanya ata kũmũthaitha Yeova ũndũ vaĩle? Ti o nginya wĩmanyĩsye ũmanyĩsyo wa kĩla ndĩni nĩ kana ũisyaanĩsye. Waĩle kwĩmanyĩsya ũndũ yo Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa ũthaithi wa w'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, nthĩ mbingĩ nĩsyĩthĩawa na mbesa ite sya w'o. Ũkanengwa wĩa wa kũnyuva mbesa ila ite sya w'o wĩka ata? No nginya ũmanye nesa vyũ mbesa ila ite sya w'o? Aiee. Nĩkavaa ũkamanya nesa mbesa ila sya w'o. Ĩndĩ wamanya nesa mbesa ila sya w'o ũndũ siilye ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũmanya ila ite sya w'o, nũndũ iyĩilye ta ila sya w'o. O ta ũu twamanya ũndũ tũtonya kũmanya ndĩni ya w'o, nĩtũtonya kũmanya ila sya ũvungũ.
3. Kwĩanana na ũndũ Yesũ waisye, twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩtĩkĩlĩke nĩ Ngai?
3 Nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kũmũthaitha Yeova kwa nzĩa ĩla wĩtĩkĩlaa. Andũ aingĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana ndĩni syonthe nimwendeeasya Ngai ĩndĩ Mbivilia ndĩmanyĩasya ũu. O na kwasya wĩ Mũklĩsto kũitoetye kũmwendeesya Ngai. Yesũ aisye: "Ti kĩla mũndũ ũmbĩtaa mwĩaĩi, mwĩaĩi, ũkavota ũsumbĩnĩ wa ĩtu; ĩndĩ nĩ ũla wĩkaa kwenda kwa Asa wakwa ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ." Kwoou nĩ kana tũmwendeesye Ngai no nginya twĩmanyĩsye ũndũ wendaa twĩke na kwĩka ũu. Yesũ eetie ala matekaa kwenda kwa Ngai 'eki ma mothũku.' (Mathayo 7:
4. Ndeto sya Yesũ ĩũlũ wa ila nzĩa ilĩ syonanasya ata, na kĩla ĩmwe ĩelete va?
4 Yeova nũnengete kĩla mũndũ kũũ nthĩ mwanya wa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. Nĩ kana tũkwate thayũ wa tene na tene Valatisonĩ nĩtwaĩle kũthaitha Ngai ũndũ vaĩle na kwĩkala na mwĩkalĩle ũla wendete. Nĩ kyeva nũndũ andũ aingĩ nĩmaleaa kwĩka ũu. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ waisye: "Votai inyw'ĩ nthĩnĩ wa mbingĩlo ĩla ntheke: nũndũ mbingĩlo nĩ nthanthau, na nzĩa nĩ mbaamu, ĩla ĩelete wanangĩkonĩ, nao nĩ aingĩ ala mavotelaa mbingĩlonĩ ĩsu. Nũndũ mbingĩlo nĩ ntheke, na nzĩa nĩ nziĩĩe, ĩla ĩelete thayũnĩ, nao nĩ avũthũ ala mamyonaa." (Mathayo 7:
ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KŨMANYA NDĨNI ĨLA YA W'O
5. Tũtonya kũmanya ala maatĩĩaa ndĩni ya w'o ata?
5 'Nzĩa ĩla ĩelete thayũnĩ' ĩtonya kwoneka ata? Yesũ aisye kana ndĩni ya w'o ĩkeethĩwa ĩtonya kũmanyĩka kwĩsĩla mwĩkalĩlenĩ wa ala mamĩatĩĩaa. Yesũ aisye: "Mũkamamanya nĩ mosyao moo. Kĩla mũtĩ mũseo nũsyaa ũsyao mũseo." (Mathayo 7:
6, 7. Athũkũmi ma Ngai mosaa Mbivilia ata, na Yesũ oonanisye ngelekany'o ata?
6 Athaithi ma Ngai ma w'o mamanyĩasya kwĩanana na ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Kĩla Ũandĩko nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai, naw'o nĩwaĩle wa kũmanyĩsya, na kũĩkĩĩthya andũ mavĩtyo, na kũmatũngĩĩa, na kũsilĩla kwa ũlũngalu: nĩ kana mũndũ wa Ngai atonye kwĩthĩwa e mwĩanĩu, eanĩe kũtethya kĩla wĩa mũseo." (2 Timotheo 3:
7 Yesũ Klĩsto oonanisye ngelekany'o nzeo kwa kumya momanyĩsyo make Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. Aivoya kũla kwĩ Ĩthe wake wa ĩtunĩ, aisye: "Ndeto yaku nĩyo w'o." (Yoana 17:17) Yesũ nĩwaĩkĩĩe Ndeto ya Ngai, na ũndũ w'onthe ũla wamanyĩasya waendanasya na Maandĩko. Mavinda maingĩ aasya: "Nĩkũandĩkĩtwe." (Mathayo 4:
8. Nĩ maũndũ meva mendekaa nthĩnĩ wa kũmũthaitha Yeova?
8 Ala maatĩĩaa ndĩni ya w'o mathaithaa Yeova e weka na nĩmakũsĩĩaa syĩtwa yake. Yesũ aisye: "Mũthaithae Mwĩaĩi [Yeova] Ngai waku, na mũthũkũmae we, e weka." (Mathayo 4:
9, 10. Aklĩsto ma w'o mendanaa kwa nzĩa syĩva?
9 Andũ ma Ngai nĩmendanĩte kwa ngoo ntheu. Yesũ aisye: "Na kwondũ wa ũu andũ onthe makamanya kana mwĩ amanyĩw'a makwa, ethĩwa mwĩthĩwa na wendo inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ." (Yoana 13:35) Aklĩsto ma mbee mendanĩte oou. Wendo ũilye ta wa Ngai nũtumaa twendana kwa w'o o na ethĩwa tũi ma langi ũmwe, kana mbaĩ ĩmwe, kana nthĩ ĩmwe na nũtũthengeanasya ta ana-a-asa ma w'o. (Akolosai 3:
10 Wendo wa w'o ti o kũlea kũaana. Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmatũmĩaa ĩvinda, vinya, na syĩndũ syoo kũtetheanĩsya kwa ngoo ntheu. (Aevelania 10:
11. Nĩkĩ nĩtwaĩle kũmwĩtĩkĩla Yesũ Klĩsto tawe ũnenganĩtwe nĩ Ngai atangĩĩe andũ?
11 Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmetĩkĩlaa Yesũ Klĩsto tawe watũmiwe nĩ Ngai atangĩĩe andũ. Mbĩvilia yaĩtye: "O na kũti ũtangĩĩo kwa ũngĩ o na wĩva w'onthe: nũndũ kũti syĩtwa yĩngĩ ĩtheo wa ĩtu, yĩnengetwe andũ, yĩtwaĩle ithyĩ kũtangĩĩwa nayo." (Meko ma Atũmwa 4:
12. Kwĩthĩwa tũte mũamba na nthĩ ĩno kũlikasya maũndũ maũ?
12 Athaithi ma w'o mai mũamba na nthĩ. Yesũ e mbee wa Vilato ngavana wa Lomi aisye: "Ũsumbĩ wakwa ti wa nthĩ ĩno." (Yoana 18:36) Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ ma w'o masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtunĩ me o vala maĩ nthĩ yonthe, kwoou mayĩlikasya siasanĩ sya nthĩ ĩno. Na mailikĩlĩĩlaa ithokoo syayo. Athaithi ma Yeova o na mailikĩlĩĩlaa ũtw'i wa andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa kũlika kyamanĩ kya siasa, kũtetea kĩvĩla kya siasa, kana kũkũna kula. O na kau athaithi ma w'o ma Ngai mayĩlikasya siasanĩ sya nthĩ ĩno, mo nĩmaatĩĩaa mĩao ya silikalĩ. Nĩkĩ maatĩĩaa mĩao? Nũndũ ndeto ya Ngai ĩmeyĩaĩe 'methĩwe me ewi kwa ala mena ũkũmũ' silikalĩnĩ. (Alomi 13:1) Yĩla ũndũ Ngai ũkwenda ũtekwĩw'ana na ũndũ silikalĩ sya siasa syĩkwenda, athaithi ma w'o maatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ya atũmwa ma Yesũ yĩla maisye: "Mũvaka tũmwĩw'e Ngai mbee wa kũmew'a andũ."
13. Atĩĩi ma Yesũ ma w'o methĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, na ũu ũtumaa meka ata?
13 Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ ma w'o matavanasya kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩw'o wĩkwatyo wa andũ w'oka. Yesũ athanie: "Na ũvoo ũũ mũseo wa ũsumbĩ ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe; na ĩndĩ mũminũkĩlyo ũkyũka." (Mathayo 24:14) Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ Klĩsto ma w'o mayĩkĩaa andũ vinya kwĩkwatya silikalĩ sya andũ kũmavetea mathĩna, ĩndĩ matavanasya kana Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtunĩ wa Ngai now'o wĩkwatyo wa andũ w'oka. (Savuli 146:3) Yesũ atũmanyĩisye kũvoyeaa silikalĩ ĩsu mbĩanĩu yĩla waisye: "Ũsumbĩ waku wũke. Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ o ta kũya ĩtunĩ." (Mathayo 6:
14. We wĩona nĩ ndĩni yĩva yĩkaa maũndũ ala ndĩni ya w'o yaĩle kwĩka?
14 Kwĩanana na maũndũ asu twoona, kweekũlye, 'Nĩ ndĩni yĩva ĩla ĩmanyĩasya kwĩanana na ũndũ Mbivilia yaasya, na ĩmanyĩasya andũ ĩũlũ wa syĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova? Nĩ aatĩĩi ma ndĩni yĩva ala monanasya wendo o ũndũ Ngai ũtũmanyĩasya, monanasya mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa Yesũ, mate mũamba na nthĩ ĩno, na matavanasya kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai now'o wĩkwatyo wa andũ w'oka? Katĩ wa ndĩni syoonthe kũũ nthĩ, nĩ yĩva yĩkaa maũndũ asu?' Wasisya nesa wĩthĩa nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.
WAĨLE KWĨKA ATA?
15. Ngai endaa twĩke ũndũ ũngĩ mwaũ vamwe na kũĩkĩĩa e kw'o?
15 O kũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai e kw'o kũitoetye kũmwendeesya. O na Mbivilia yaasya o nasyo ndaimoni nĩsyĩtĩkĩlaa kana Ngai ekw'o. (Yakovo 2:
16. Ethĩwa wĩ mũamba na ndĩni ya ũvũngũ waĩle kwĩka ata?
16 Mũtũmwa Vaulo oonanisye kana tũyaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũamba na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ. Aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Umai katĩ woo, na mwĩthĩwe mwĩvathanĩte nao, eneena ũu Mwĩaĩi, Na mũikakiite kĩndũ kĩvuku; Nakwa ngamwosa." (2 Akolintho 6:
17, 18. "Mbaviloni ĩla Nene" nĩ kyaũ, na nĩkĩ twaĩle 'kuma nthĩnĩ wayo' mĩtũkĩ?
17 Mbivilia yonanasya kana ndĩni syoonthe sya ũvũngũ syĩtawa "Mbaviloni ĩla Nene." * (Ũvuan'yo 17:5) Syĩtwa yĩu yĩtũlilikanasya mũsyĩ wa tene wa Mbaviloni vala ndĩni ya ũvũngũ yambĩĩie ĩtina wa kĩla kĩw'ũ Kingĩ kya ĩvinda ya Noa. Momanyĩsyo na imanyĩo mbingĩ ila syendekete nĩ ndĩni sya ũvũngũ syaũmie Mbaviloni. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ma Mbaviloni mathaithaa ngai sya ũtatũ. Ũmũnthĩ ũtatũ nĩw'o ũmanyĩsyo ũla mũnene nthĩnĩ wa ndĩni mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana kwĩ Ngai o ũmwe wa w'o, Yeova, na kana Yesũ Klĩsto nĩ Mwana Wake. (Yoana 17:3) Andũ ma Mbaviloni maĩkĩĩaa kana andũ me thayũ ũtakusaa na yĩla mũndũ wakw'a, thayũ ũsu nũtianaa na mwĩĩ na nũtonya kũthĩnĩa ĩianĩ ya mwaki. O na ũmũnthĩ ndĩni mbingĩ imanyĩasya kana thayũ ndũkusaa na kana nũtonya kũthĩnĩa ĩianĩ ya mwaki.
18 Nũndũ ũthaithi wa Mbaviloni ya tene nĩwanyaĩĩkie nthĩ yonthe, Mbaviloni ĩla Nene ũmũnthĩ nĩ ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ sya nthĩ yonthe. Na Ngai nĩwathanĩte kana ndĩni isu ikathela kĩthũlũmũkĩlo. (Ũvuan'yo 18:8) Nũkwona nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩvathana vyũ na Mbaviloni ĩla Nene? Yeova Ngai eenda 'ume nthĩnĩ wake' mĩtũkĩ ĩvinda yĩtanathela.
19. Ũkatetheka ata kwa kũthaitha Yeova?
19 Watw'a kwĩvathana na ndĩni ya ũvũngũ anyanyau amwe nĩmatonya kũũtia. Ĩndĩ waendeea kũthaitha Yeova vamwe na andũ make ũkatetheka vate wasyo. O ta amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ ala matiie syĩndũ nĩ kana mamũatĩĩe, ũkamesya ana-a-asa aingĩ ma kĩveva. Ũkeethĩwa wĩ ũmwe nthĩnĩ wa nguthu nene ya nthĩ yonthe ya Aklĩsto ma w'o ala monanasya wendo wa w'o. Na ũkeethĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũseo mũno wa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela "ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte." (Maliko 10:
20. Ala maatĩĩaa ndĩni ya w'o meteele kyaũ ĩvinda yũkĩte?
20 Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai akaananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku na ayĩete nthĩ nzaũ yĩ ũlũngalũ ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wake. (2 Vetelo 3:
^ kal. 17 Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa nĩkĩ tũkwasya Mbaviloni ĩla Nene nĩ ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ sya nthĩ yonthe, sisya Ũvoo wa Kwongeleela ĩthangũ ya 219-220.

translation:
Why is it important to praise God?
Should we care whether He knows we appreciate Him?
But how can we show God that we love Him?
1. Should we simply try to please God when we can?
JEHOVAH GOD teaches us so that we can worship Him in a way that pleases Him. When we try to please Him, we will have many blessings. And He will help us and strengthen us. (Isaiah 48:17) It is good to know more about what Jehovah expects of us and to learn His ways. Learning about God's standards helps us make wise decisions and do what is right.
2. Should we care whether we please Jehovah, and why is it vital that we strive to understand what pleases Him?
2 Should we care whether we please Jehovah? Perhaps you think this question is foolish or unimportant. The Bible explains why pleasing Him is important. For example, many people are motivated by their conscience. But what makes your conscience reliable? Do you really understand what your conscience tells you? I bet you don't fully understand what your conscience tells you. If you understand what your conscience tells you, you won't find it hard to understand what is right, and you will be able to do what is right. So when we learn what pleases Him, we also learn about righteousness.
3. Like Jesus said, should we worry about whether we are approved by God?
3 It is very important to please Jehovah because of the way He feels about us. Many people believe that everything God wants from us is found in the Bible. But being a Christian means more than just following what the Bible says. Jesus said: "Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the Kingdom of Heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven." That's why we need to please God so that we can show that we mean what we say. Jesus taught that we should pray to God 'earnestly.' (Matthew 7:
4. What did Jesus illustrate with those examples, and what does each one teach?
4 Jehovah gives each person freedom to choose whether he will accept his guidance. So we can choose to take our direction from Satan and disobey God, or we can choose to obey Him and live according to His standards. However, many people reject this counsel. This is why Jesus said: "Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives; and he who searches finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened." (Matthew 7:
IMPORTANT THINGS TO KNOW
5. How can we know what God approves of?
5 How can 'searching' be done? Jesus explained that God's approval can be discerned by observing the conduct of those who claim to be worshipers. Jesus said: "By their fruits you will recognize them. Every good tree bears fine fruit, but the rotten tree bears worthless fruit." (Matthew 7:
6, 7. How does God view the Bible, and how did Jesus demonstrate its importance?
6 Those who truly desire to please God will endeavor to harmonize their lives with what the Bible says. The Bible states: "All Scripture is inspired by God and beneficial, for teaching, for reproving, for setting matters straight, for disciplining with a view to righteousness, so that the man who belongs to God may be fully competent, equipped for every good work." (2 Timothy 3:
7 Jesus Christ demonstrated deep respect for God's Word by making it the basis of his teachings. While on earth, he said: "My food is to do the will of the One who sent me." (John 17:17) Jesus upheld God's Law, and everything he taught was in harmony with the Scriptures. On many occasions, he said: "It is written." (Matthew 4:
8. What things should we meditate on in order to please Jehovah?
8 Those who seek God's approval meditate on his ways and strive to imitate his name. Jesus said: "You must love Jehovah your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." (Matthew 4:
9, 10. Why do true Christians meet together?
9 People who belong to God enjoy close fellowship. Jesus said: "By this everyone will know that you are my disciples—if you have love for one another." (John 13:35) True Christians show their love for one another actively. This love, which comes from God, motivates us to associate closely with our brothers and sisters, whether at meetings, in the ministry, or in everyday life, and to encourage one another. (Colossians 3:
10 That love does not lead to complacency. True Christians use their time, energy, and resources to help others. (Hebrews 10:
11. How can we show that we appreciate Jesus Christ and the opportunity to become reconciled to God?
11 True Christians support Jesus Christ and those whom God sends to preach the good news. The Bible says: "Be courageous and speak up . . . do not be afraid of anyone to whom you speak; for I will be with you and will protect you." (Acts 4:
12. What will we discuss in the following chapters?
12 We will discuss how to remain neutral in political matters. Jesus, when questioned by Pilate, the governor of Judea, said: "My kingship is not part of this world." (John 18:36) His followers were persecuted because they refused to participate in politics or worship Roman emperors. But they remained loyal to Jehovah and did not compromise their conscience to avoid trouble, nor did they seek political power or influence. They knew that God would bless them if they maintained neutrality. Why should we obey governmental authorities? Because the Bible instructs us to "be obedient to the government officials" and to pay taxes. (Romans 13:1) However, what if obeying the state conflicts with obedience to God? Then we must always side with God, just as the apostles told Jewish rulers: "We must obey God as ruler rather than you men."
13. How did Jesus' followers respond to opposition during the first century, and what can we learn from their example?
13 Jesus' followers continued to preach despite persecution and opposition. Jesus foretold: "The good news of the kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all nations; and then the end will come." (Matthew 24:14) Like those early Christians, we can maintain our confidence in God's Kingdom, even when facing opposition. (Psalm 146:3) Jesus reminded his disciples about the importance of remaining neutral when he taught them to pray: "Let your kingdom come. Let your will take place on earth, as in heaven." (Matthew 6:
14. What reasons do we have for maintaining Christian neutrality?
14 In view of what we see happening, we might ask ourselves, 'Does Bible prophecy not indicate that there would be wars and unrest, and that people would disregard God's name, Jehovah? Are not current events confirming what God has foretold, confirming Jesus' warnings, and showing that opposition to God's Kingdom is intensifying? If so, should we not expect things to get worse?' The answer is yes, because this is what Jehovah's prophecy indicates.
WHY REMAIN NEUTRAL?
15. Why does God allow suffering and injustice?
15 To allow humans free will and to vindicate His sovereignty. Also, the Bible shows that Satan the Devil influences people to oppose God. (James 2:
16. How can we remain firm when faced with pressure from others?
16 The apostle Paul explained that we can remain faithful despite pressure from others. He wrote: "Therefore, 'Come out from among them, and stop associating with them,' says Jehovah, 'and quit touching the unclean thing'; 'and I will take you in.'" (2 Corinthians 6:
17, 18. What is "Babylon the Great," and why should we 'keep aloof' from her?
17 The Bible identifies all false religion as "Babylon the Great." * (Revelation 17:5) This name appropriately describes the origin of the world's religions, tracing back to ancient Babylon, which was associated with rebellion against God, similar to Noah's day. Much error and idolatry originated in ancient Babylon. For example, the Babylonians practiced spiritism. Idolatry is a major feature of many religions. The Bible clearly teaches that there is only one true God, Jehovah, and that Jesus Christ is his Son. (John 17:3) People associated with "Babylon the Great" often promote nationalistic sentiments and encourage violence, causing hatred and division. Moreover, many religions teach doctrines that contradict God's Word.
18 Since ancient Babylon has fallen completely, "Babylon the Great" represents all false religion today. And God will soon bring all false religion to ruin. (Revelation 18:8) So how can we avoid getting involved with "Babylon the Great"? Jehovah God 'keeps to his own people.'
19. Will you remain loyal to Jehovah?
19 By associating only with those who worship Jehovah, you can maintain spiritual strength. To show loyalty to Jehovah and his people, be determined to separate yourself from false worship. Also, remember what Jesus said about being no part of the world. Be zealous in proclaiming the good news of God's Kingdom, imitating the fine example set by fellow Christians. And be courageous in applying the principle of remaining "in the world, but not belonging to it." (Mark 10:
20. How can we show that we are no part of this world?
20 The Bible shows that God does not approve of this wicked world and that he will shortly cleanse it by fire. (2 Peter 3:
^ par. 17 As we discussed earlier, "Babylon the Great" represents all false religion today, so stay away from all forms of false worship. See the article "Keep Yourselves Unspotted From the World," on pages 219-220.

"It's just a small thing to protect everyone here."
"Oh. That's not a big deal."
"Really! It's important to you! Tell me, let me confirm whether you have forgiven our debt in Kathama," she said, and my wife laughed at her joke. She stared at her phone and listened to music; sometimes she likes to comfort her husband when he's upset or worried.
We continued walking. I felt like my wife was getting stronger; she wasn't afraid anymore.
"I believe you."
"Let's agree to continue discussing this matter; but I will also try to find solutions and ask for help from anyone involved."
"That's fine. I agree and am ready."
"Ready for what?"
"He uses his hands to speak through the gate," his wife told me.
My spouse opened the door to the kitchen. Inside, a young man was eating and drinking milk. She led her spouse inside and scolded him.
"Wow, you speak excellent English. Hey! You look like someone who went to university. Wow, why are you wearing such old clothes?" my spouse asked.
The sun was setting. The wind was blowing strongly.
"What did she tell you about the bees? Bring the bees. I hate everything that causes pain," his wife said; she hated everything related to men and women. My wife calmed down a bit and started to feel better.
She was given honey and bread to eat during the meeting.
Someone reminded me of the past and the things you did. I forgave them.
"Why does she always ask about your well-being?" my mother asked, and sat down comfortably. She looked at her feet while leaning on the table. She pointed at two children playing near her, saying they were tired of being disturbed.
"Sorry Mom…," I said in Kikamba.
"I don't want to bother you; I just want to talk."
They left very early; and now I wanted to talk to her. I noticed someone approaching from afar. My eyes were filled with tears and sadness.
"I will teach you Machakos Kikamba until you understand," I told her and asked her to write a letter to her friend.
"Okay," that's what she wrote," I remembered. My mother thanked her and congratulated her.
And the lesson continued.
"That too is good," I said and added more details.
"I can't remember all those details."
My mother brought a small child who was studying hard and smiled happily because she had learned a lot today.
"Let's go somewhere else. We have been here for a long time," she grabbed my hand gently. She tried to stand up but they remained seated discussing something important. They talked for a long time like they hadn't seen each other in years. My mother took out her tablet and began searching online.
I watched her and saw everything happening around us. I understood the message.
Your sister has a beautiful dress. She adjusted her clothes and then touched her hair, feeling embarrassed; 'I need to go to town to buy some things; let me find a nice place to sit.'
I picked up the tablet and zoomed in on the picture and admired her figure wearing jeans. Your body is amazing; her skin looks smooth and shiny, especially when exposed to light; her breasts and thighs are perfect! Perfect! That's how attractive she is. She made me fall in love with her again.
She wiped her body with a tissue from her bag. She dressed quickly and left.
The attraction towards her led me astray. I regretted it but she went to Ikangi to relax and enjoy herself listening to music. My wife felt sorry for your friend. Your friend locked herself in the house and started crying silently. The door was unlocked and she saw her husband returning home.
And I fell asleep.
My wife's friend locked herself in the house and sat on the mat. I pleaded with her. Your friend sat on the mat, ashamed because so many people were watching her. The attraction towards her made her act foolishly.
Look at this beautiful woman who is causing problems between you and your wife. I feel bad for her.
And I am confused.
"Just leave me alone. Your clothes smell like another woman."
"Let's go outside," the attraction towards her said to me, asking me to call the DJ.
"Go away. I want to be alone."
"Why?"
"I don't want to stay here anymore. This is making me think about taking her somewhere."
I pretended to understand.
"That's true - it's a roster." The attraction towards her said.
I calmed down a bit. To forget about everything and stop thinking about having too much fun.
Sadness and tears. The DJ turned up the volume; loooooooud.
I looked at the people around me.
"You see this man who attracts people we met at the club. He's very charming," your wife said.
I pretended to agree with her.
She continued to show off her beauty, which makes someone lose their mind.
"What?" I asked.
"You are remembering."
You should go back to your place and sit down and talk; and speak in English; shall we, my dear. But I forgot what she was saying.
Her body trembled with excitement. My heart told me to continue and enjoy. It seems I will continue to indulge in excessive drinking. I thanked her for helping me overcome my shyness. I pleaded with her and the people who came to ruin your home; I saw them trying to make you fall in love with someone else.
Please listen to my advice and talk to your wife and tell her. I realized she had been listening to her since yesterday. She took a sip of beer and started playing on her tablet while lying on the floor – then she stopped.
She covered herself with a shawl and told me to relax instead of getting more excited; tell me something.
The owner of your wife's house has problems. She dreams of a black cow and doesn't feel comfortable, but she feels connected; you and your wife. Yes, my wife sees signs of discomfort in your home, or perhaps it's just a small problem. The owners have become accustomed to ruining things that are good. This owner is like a black animal that can be chased away from the house; it walks around rubbing against the carpet. She makes a strange sound and shakes her head and says brrrrr; I laugh a lot. This owner doesn't bother your wife. Your wife scratches his neck; this owner doesn't bite him or cause trouble, just to comfort him. This owner dreams of your phone and tablet among the other owners and people in the village; and speaks about everything he sees.

text:
1. Nũũ watũnengie thayũ?
YEOVA nĩ "Ngai wĩ thayũ." (Yelemia 10:10) Nĩwe Mũmbi witũ, na nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩwoombie syĩndũ syonthe, na kwondũ wa kwenda kwaku syaĩ kw'o, na ĩngĩ syoombwa." (Ũvuan'yo 4:11) Vate nzika, Yeova nĩwendaa twĩthĩwe thayũ. Na thayũ nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa vata kuma kwake.—Soma Savuli 36:9.
2. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũendeee nesa?
2 Yeova nũtũnengae syĩndũ ila twĩ na vata nasyo nĩ kana tũendeee kwĩthĩwa thayũ. Syĩndũ isu nĩ ta lĩu na kĩw'ũ. (Meko ma Atũmwa 17:28) Ĩndĩ o na kau nũtũnengete syĩndũ isu, endaa tũtanĩe thayũ. (Meko ma Atũmwa 14:15-17) Nĩ kana tũendeee nesa, twaĩle kũkwata mĩao ya Ngai.—Isaia 48:17, 18.
WONI WA NGAI ĨŨLŨ WA THAYŨ
3. Yeova eekie ata ĩla Kaini wooaie Aveli?
3 Mbivilia ĩtũmanyĩasya kana Yeova onaa thayũ wa andũ onthe wĩ wa vata mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Kaini, ũla waĩ mwana wa Atamu na Eva, wathatĩie mũinae Aveli, Yeova nĩwamũkanisye amwĩa kana nĩwaĩle kũsiĩĩa ũthatu wake. Vandũ va kwĩthukĩĩsya, Kaini nĩwathatie mũno na "amũkĩlĩla mwana-a-inyia Aveli, na amũaa." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:3-8) Yeova nĩwamũumanĩie Kaini nũndũ wa kũaa Aveli. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:9-11) Kwoou ũthilĩku na kĩmena nĩ maũndũ mataĩlĩte nũndũ no matume mũndũ eka maũndũ mathũku. Na mũndũ ũla ũilyĩ ũu ndesa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. (Soma 1 Yoana 3:15.) Nĩ kana tũmwendeesye Yeova, no nginya twĩmanyĩsye kwenda andũ onthe.—1 Yoana 3:11, 12.
4. Mwĩao ũmwe katĩ wa mĩao ĩla Ngai wanengie Aisilaeli wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa mũthĩnzĩo wa thayũ?
4 Ĩtina wa myaka ngili mbingĩ, Yeova nĩwoonanisye kana thayũ nĩ wa vata mũno kwake ĩla wanengie Mose ĩla Mĩao Ĩkũmi. Ũmwe wa mĩao ĩsu waĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndũkoae." (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 5:17) Mũndũ aaĩle kũawa ethĩwa nĩwoaa mũndũ ũngĩ na ngenda.
5. Ngai ethĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa kumya ĩvu?
5 Ngai ethĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa kumya ĩvu? O na thayũ wa kana ke ĩvunĩ ya inyia kate kasyae nĩ wa vata mũno kwa Yeova. Mĩaonĩ ĩla Yeova wanengie Aisilaeli, ameie kana mũndũ aũmĩsya kĩveti kĩito na kana kaikw'a, mũndũ ũsu aaĩle kũawa. (Soma Kuma 21:22, 23; Savuli 127:3.) Ũu wĩtũmanyĩsya kana kumya ĩvu nĩ ũndũ mũthũku.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 28.
6, 7. Tũtonya kũmwony'a Yeova ata kana nĩtwonaa thayũ wĩ wa vata?
6 Tũtonya kũmwony'a Yeova ata kana nĩtwonaa thayũ witũ na wa andũ ala angĩ wĩ wa vata? Nĩ kwa kwĩvathana vyũ na ũndũ o na wĩva ũla ũtonya kũlikya thayũ witũ kana wa andũ angĩ mũisyonĩ. Kwoou tũyaĩle kũtũmĩa mbakĩ, sikala, vangi, kana ndawa sya kũmila, nũndũ no iũmĩsye mĩĩ yitũ na no itũae.
7 Ngai nĩwe watũnengie mĩĩ ĩno twĩ nayo vamwe na thayũ, na kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũũtũmĩa nesa ũndũ we wendaa. Ũu wĩonany'a kana nĩtwaĩle kũsũvĩa mĩĩ yitũ. Twaema kwĩka ũu, tũkeethĩwa tũte atheu methonĩ ma Ngai. (Alomi 6:19; 12:1; 2 Akolintho 7:1) Ethĩwa tũyonaa thayũ wĩ wa vata, Yeova, ũla nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ, ndesa kwĩtĩkĩla ũthaithi witũ. O na kau no wĩthĩwe wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũekana na imanyĩo isu nthũku, Yeova no atũtetheesye ethĩwa nĩtũkwĩkĩa kĩthito tũsinde imanyĩo isu, nũndũ twĩona thayũ wĩ wa vata.
8. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũĩkĩĩthye tũinalikya thayũ witũ kana wa ala angĩ mũisyonĩ?
8 Nĩtweemanyĩsya kana thayũ nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa vata. Yeova nĩwĩsĩ kana no tũtate ũndũ tũtonya tũikalikye thayũ witũ kana wa ala angĩ mũisyonĩ. Twĩkaa ũu kwa kũtwaa ngalĩ nesa, tũmota, kana o isululu. O na nĩtwĩvathanaa na mathaũ ala matonya kũtũũmĩsya. (Savuli 11:5) O na ĩngĩ, nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũsũvĩe nyũmba sitũ nĩ kana iikese kũtuma tũlika mũisyonĩ. Yeova eeie Aisilaeli atĩĩ: "Waaka nyũmba nzaũ, nĩvo ĩndĩ akĩĩa wiio ũengonĩ wa kĩala kyayo, nĩ kana ndũkaete nthakame ĩũlũ wa nyũmba yaku, ethĩwa mũndũ akavalũka kuma vo."—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 22:8.
9. Twaĩle kwĩkalany'a na nyamũ ata?
9 O na ĩngĩ, Yeova nĩwendaa twĩkalany'e na nyamũ nesa. Nũtũnengete mwanya tũae nyamũ kwondũ wa lĩu na ngũa, na ethĩwa nitonya kũtũũmĩsya. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:21; 9:3; Kuma 21:28) Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kũthĩny'a nyamũ kana kũsyũaa nĩ kana twĩtanĩthye.—Nthimo 12:10.
NENGA THAYŨ NDAĨA NŨNDŨ NĨ MŨTHEU
10. Twĩsĩ ata kana nthakame nĩyo thayũ?
10 Nthakame nĩ ntheu methonĩ ma Yeova nũndũ nĩyo thayũ. Ĩla Kaini wooaie Aveli, Yeova amwĩie atĩĩ: "Wasya wa nthakame ya mwana-a-mwenyu nũĩngaĩla kuma nthĩ." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:10) Nthakame ya Aveli yaũngamĩe thayũ wake, na Yeova nĩwamũumanĩie Kaini nũndũ wa kũaa Aveli. Ĩtina wa ĩla mbua ya kĩw'ũ kingĩ ya ĩvinda ya Noa, Yeova nĩwoonanisye ĩngĩ kana nthakame nĩyo thayũ. Nĩwanengie Noa na mũsyĩ wake mwanya maĩsae nyama sya nyamũ. Ameie atĩĩ: "Kĩla kĩndũ kĩendaa kĩ thayũ kĩkeethĩwa lĩu kwenyu; o ta nyũnyi nziũ nĩnĩmũnengete syonthe." Ĩndĩ ve kĩndũ kĩmwe Yeova wameie maikaye. Ameie atĩĩ: "Ĩndĩ nyama ĩ na thayũ wayo, nĩw'o nthakame yayo, mũtikaye."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:29; 9:3, 4.
11. Nĩ mwĩao wĩva ĩũlũ wa nthakame Ngai wanengie mbaĩ ya Isilaeli?
11 Myaka ta 800 Yeova amina kũtavya Noa kana nthakame ndyaĩle kũĩwa, nĩwasyokie eeaĩa andũ make atĩĩ: "Na mũndũ o na wĩva wa ana ma Isilaeli, o na wa aeni ala mekalaa ũeni kwoo, ũla wĩũaa nyamũ o na yĩva akĩsyĩma kana nyũnyi o na yĩva ĩla ĩtonya kũĩwa; akete nthakame yayo, na kũmĩvw'ĩka na mũthanga." Na ĩndĩ ongeleela kũmea atĩĩ: "Mũtikaye nthakame." (Alivai 17:13, 14) Ũu wĩonany'a kana Yeova endaa andũ make monae nthakame yĩ kĩndũ kĩtheu. Maaĩle kũya nyama ĩndĩ ti nthakame. Ĩla mooaa nyamũ nĩ kana makwate nyama, maaĩle kwĩta nthakame yayo mũthanganĩ.
12. Aklĩsto methĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa nthakame?
12 Myaka mĩnini kuma Yesũ akw'a, atũmwa na atumĩa ala maĩ kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto kĩla kyaĩ Yelusaleme nĩmoombanie matw'e nĩ mĩao yĩva katĩ wa Mĩao ĩla yanengetwe Aisilaeli yaaĩle kũatĩĩwa nĩ Aklĩsto. (Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 15:28, 29; 21:25.) Yeova nĩwamatetheeisye kũelewa kana nthakame nĩ ya vata mũno kwake na kana nĩmaaĩle kũmyonaa yĩ ntheu. Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa mayaĩ metĩkĩla kũya kana kũnyw'a nthakame, na mayaĩ metĩkĩla kũya nyama ĩtaumĩtw'e nthakame nesa. Kũya nthakame kwaĩ kũthũku ta kũthaitha mĩvw'anano kana kwĩka ũlaalai. Kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu, Aklĩsto ma w'o mayaaya nthakame kana kũmĩnyw'a. Nao nata ũmũnthĩ? Yeova nĩwendaa twonae nthakame yĩ kĩndũ kĩtheu.
13. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto matetĩkĩlaa kwĩkĩwa nthakame mĩkivanĩ?
13 W'o ũu wĩonany'a kana Aklĩsto mayaĩle kwĩkĩwa nthakame mĩkivanĩ? Ĩĩ. Yeova aĩtye kana tũyaĩle kũya kana kũnyw'a nthakame. Ndakĩtalĩ akakwĩa kana ndwaĩle kũnyw'a ũkĩ, we no wĩtĩkĩle kwĩkĩwa ũkĩ mĩkivanĩ? Vate nzika ndwĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla! O ta ũu, mwĩao ũla waĩtye kana tũyaĩle kũnyw'a kana kũya nthakame wĩonany'a kana tũyaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla kwĩkĩwa nthakame mĩkivanĩ.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 29.
14, 15. O na kau Aklĩsto nĩmonaa thayũ wĩ wa vata, mo nĩmatũlaa mĩao ya Ngai nĩ kana mekalange thayũ? Elesya.
14 Nao nata ndakĩtalĩ akatwĩa kana nĩtũũkw'a twalea kwĩkĩwa nthakame? No nginya kĩla mũndũ etw'ĩĩe e we mwene kana nũkũatĩĩa mwĩao wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa nthakame. Aklĩsto nĩmanengete thayũ ndaĩa, na nĩmamanthaa nzĩa ingĩ syaĩle sya ũiiti nĩ kana maendeee kwĩkala thayũ, ĩndĩ mayĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla kwĩkĩwa nthakame mĩkivanĩ.
15 Nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũsũvĩe mĩĩ yitũ, ĩndĩ nũndũ thayũ nĩ wa vata kwa Ngai, tũyĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla kwĩkĩwa nthakame mĩkivanĩ. Kũmwĩw'a Yeova nĩkw'o kwa vata vyũ kwĩ kũtata twĩkalange thayũ kwa kũtũla mĩao yake. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Ũla ũnũkwenda kũvĩtya thayũ wake akawasya: na o ũla ũkawasya thayũ wake kwondũ wakwa akawona ĩngĩ." (Mathayo 16:25) Twaĩle kũmwĩw'a Yeova nũndũ nĩtũmwendete. Yeova nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kĩtwaĩle, na nĩtwonaa thayũ wĩ wa vata na wĩ mũtheu, o ũndũ we ũwonaa.—Aevelania 11:6.
16. Nĩkĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai mamwĩw'aa?
16 Athũkũmi aĩkĩĩku ma Ngai nĩmatw'ĩte vyũ kũkwata mwĩao wake ĩũlũ wa nthakame. Mayĩsa kũya kana kũnyw'a nthakame, na mayĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla kwĩkĩwa nthakame yĩla mekũiitwa. * Ĩndĩ nĩmetĩkĩlaa nzĩa ingĩ sya ũiiti nĩ kana matangĩĩe thayũ woo. Mayĩthĩawa na nzika kana Mũmbi wa thayũ na nthakame nĩwe wĩsĩ kĩla kĩmaĩle vyũ. We nũkũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kĩkwaĩle vyũ?
NZĨA ĨLA YEOVA WEETĨKĨLĨTYE YA KŨTŨMĨA NTHAKAME
17. Mbaĩnĩ ya Isilaeli, Yeova eetĩkĩlĩtye nthakame ĩtũmĩawe ũndũnĩ wĩva?
17 Mĩaonĩ ĩla Yeova wanengie Mose, atavisye Aisilaeli atĩĩ: "Thayũ wa mwĩĩ wĩ nthakamenĩ; na nĩnĩmũnengete yo kĩthembeonĩ yĩthĩwe wĩw'anĩthyo [kana, kwĩtya ũekeo] kwondũ wa mathayũ menyu: nũndũ nthakame nĩyo yĩw'anĩthasya mũndũ." (Alivai 17:11) Yĩla Aisilaeli mavĩtya, maĩ matonya kũmũkũlya Yeova amaekee kwa kũtwaĩa mũthembi nyamũ nĩ kana amĩthembe na ayĩta nthakame ĩmwe kĩthembeonĩ kĩla kyaĩ ĩkalũnĩ. Yeova eetĩkĩlĩtye nthakame ĩtũmĩawe ũndũnĩ o ũsu wĩ w'oka.
18. Nthembo ĩla Yesũ waumisye ĩtonya kũtũtethya ata?
18 Yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ, nĩwaumisye thayũ wake, kana nthakame yake nĩ kana tũekewe naĩ sitũ, na ũu nĩwatumie nthembo sya nyamũ ieka kumw'a. (Mathayo 20:28; Aevelania 10:1) Thayũ wa Yesũ waĩ wa vata mũno, na nĩkyo kĩtumi kwĩsĩla nthembo ĩla Yesũ waumisye, Yeova ũnengete andũ onthe mwanya wa kwĩkala tene na tene.—Yoana 3:16; Aevelania 9:11, 12; 1 Vetelo 1:18, 19.
19. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana 'tũikaakũlw'e nthakame ya mũndũ o na wĩva'?
19 Nĩtũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa mũthĩnzĩo wa thayũ ũla ũtũnengete! Nĩtwendaa kũtavya andũ kana mamũĩkĩĩa Yesũ, no mekale tene na tene. Nũndũ nĩtwendete andũ, tũkeekĩaa kĩthito tũmamanyĩsye maũndũ ala matonya kwĩka nĩ kana mekwata thayũ. (Esekieli 3:17-21) Na tweeka ũu, tũkeethĩwa tũtonya kwasya o ta mũtũmwa Vaulo, ũla waisye atĩĩ: "Ndikakũlw'a nyie nthakame ya mũndũ o na wĩva. Nũndũ ndyaatundua kũmũtavya inyw'ĩ ũtw'ĩo w'onthe wa Ngai." (Meko ma Atũmwa 20:26, 27) Nĩtwonanasya kana nĩtũnengete thayũ na nthakame ndaĩa nene ĩla twatavya ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova na ũndũ wonaa thayũ wĩ wa vata.
^ kal. 16 Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ũeleetye ĩũlũ wa kwĩkĩwa nthakame mĩkivanĩ, sisya ũvoo ũla wĩ ĩthangũnĩ ya 77-79, ĩvukunĩ "Ĩyĩkalyei Ene Wendonĩ wa Ngai," yĩla yumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova.

translation:
1. Why should we worship God?
JEHOVAH is "the true God." (Jeremiah 10:10) He is our Creator, and he makes things beautiful. The Bible says about him: "I have made everything, even the farthest stars." (Revelation 4:11) So naturally, Jehovah wants us to worship him. And worship is proper because of what he does.—Read Psalm 36:9.
2. Can we please God even if we make mistakes?
2 Jehovah knows we are imperfect, but he still wants us to keep trying to worship him. We are like children learning. (Acts 17:28) He has given us a conscience to help us learn what is right. (Acts 14:15-17) If we try to please him, we can receive his forgiveness.—Isaiah 48:17, 18.
GOD'S LOVE IS AMAZING
3. Did Jehovah care when Cain killed Abel?
3 The Bible shows that Jehovah cares deeply about people, even those who do wrong. For example, when Cain, the son of Adam and Eve, angrily killed his brother Abel, Jehovah showed that he was saddened by what happened. People were shocked, and Cain was punished severely for "killing his brother Abel." (Genesis 4:3-8) Jehovah warned Cain about the consequences of killing Abel. (Genesis 4:9-11) This illustrates how much Jehovah values life and hates wickedness. And anyone who deliberately chooses to do bad things will lose out on God's approval. (Read 1 John 3:15.) If we love Jehovah, we will also show love for others.—1 John 3:11, 12.
4. What is one way God helped the Israelites understand how important worship is?
4 Many years ago, Jehovah showed how important worship is to him when he gave Moses the Ten Commandments. One of those commandments said: "Do not murder." (Exodus 20:13) Someone who kills another person is taking a life and violates God's law.
5. How does God view the matter of taking a life?
5 How does God view the matter of taking a life? Yes, the value of a human life is very precious to Jehovah. He told the Israelites that if someone intentionally took a life, that person had to be put to death. (Read Deuteronomy 21:22, 23; Psalm 127:3.) Taking a life is a serious offense.—Read Proverbs 6:16-19.
6, 7. How can we show that we value life, even when faced with violence?
6 How can we show that we value life, even when faced with violence—our own or that of others? We can do so by avoiding violent thoughts and actions and by refusing to let anger control us. Instead of seeking revenge, we should pray for help to forgive others, and we should strive to live peaceably with everyone.
7 God gives us the opportunity to enjoy life, and he wants us to use our resources wisely. This shows that we appreciate what he provides. Also, we want to avoid doing anything that would cause us regret. By doing so, we will please God. (Ecclesiastes 6:19; 12:1; 2 Corinthians 7:1) Even when faced with violence, remember that Jehovah is the One who values life, and trust in his promise to protect those who love him. And if something bad happens because of circumstances beyond our control, Jehovah will comfort us and help us cope with the situation.
8. Should we ever try to defend ourselves or others?
8 We should always respect life. Jehovah knows that there may be times when we need to defend ourselves or others. Let us make this decision carefully, considering whether it is necessary, reasonable, or legal. But we must also avoid associating with violent people. (Psalm 11:5) Furthermore, we should think about whether defending ourselves might lead to further problems. Jehovah told the Israelites: "When you build a new house, you must construct a parapet around its roof, so that you do not bring guilt on yourself if anyone falls from the roof." – Deuteronomy 22:8.
9. How can we deal with fear?
9 Moreover, Jehovah wants us to face our fears courageously. He encourages us to pray regularly, both morning and evening, and asks us to trust in him. (Philippians 3:21; 9:3; Proverbs 21:28) It is important to acknowledge our fears and talk about them. – Psalm 12:10.
REMEMBER THE VALUE OF LIFE
10. Why is life precious?
10 Life is precious because it comes from Jehovah. For example, when Cain killed Abel, Jehovah told him: "The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground." (Genesis 4:10) Abel's life was valuable to God, and Jehovah held Cain accountable for taking it. Also, after the global flood in Noah's time, Jehovah again showed that he values life. He instructed Noah and his family to eat animals, but he said: "Every moving creature that is alive will be food for you; but you must never eat flesh with its lifeblood." God made this clear. He said: "As for any animal that has lifeblood, I will require its lifeblood." – Genesis 1:29; 9:3, 4.
11. What law did God give the Israelites regarding life?
11 About 800 years after the Flood, Jehovah gave the Israelites this command: "Anyone who strikes a man so that he dies must certainly be put to death. And anyone who kills an animal must make restitution for it, both to its owner and to himself." And he added: "You must not eat flesh with its lifeblood." (Leviticus 17:13, 14) This shows how much Jehovah values human life. It is wrong to take a life needlessly. But if someone accidentally takes a life, he must make amends for it.
12. How do Christians view the value of life?
12 Many years after Jesus died, apostles and older men sent letters to congregations of Christians in Jerusalem asking them about a matter involving laws that had been given to ancient Israel. (Read Acts 15:28, 29; 21:25.) Jehovah helped them understand whether those laws were still binding and whether they should apply to Christians. The apostles and older men decided that Christians did not need to observe those laws regarding food, nor did they need to abstain from eating meat offered to idols. Eating certain foods could cause some to stumble or weaken their faith. Therefore, Christians were free to choose whether or not to eat such foods. However, Jehovah wants us to value life greatly.
13. Why do Christians not feel obligated to obey those ancient laws?
13 Do you think Christians are free to disregard all ancient laws? No. Jehovah has allowed us to choose what we eat and drink. So if someone feels wrong about eating or drinking something, should you pressure him to do so? Of course not! Remember that our freedom to choose does not mean we are free to disobey God's law.
14, 15. How can Christians show respect for God when dealing with matters of conscience? Explain.
14 What if someone asks us whether we will partake of certain foods? We should kindly explain that each person must decide for himself whether he can eat those foods without violating his conscience. Christ respects people's consciences, and he wants us to be considerate of others, so that we do not cause them to stumble.
15 We need to train our thinking to align with God's view of things, remembering that pleasing God is vital. Our love for Jehovah motivates us to be considerate of others and to respect their consciences. Jesus said: "Anyone who wants to save his life must lose it; but anyone who loses his life for my sake will find it." (Matthew 16:25) To show our love for Jehovah, we are willing to put his interests first. Jehovah knows what is best for us, and he will help us to make good decisions.—Hebrews 11:6.
16. Why should we value godly counsel?
16 Godly counselors help us to apply God's principles to our lives. They encourage us to avoid harmful practices and to refrain from doing anything that would damage our conscience. *They also help us to examine our hearts and motives.* Trust in God, knowing that he cares for us and understands our feelings. Are you convinced that God truly cares for you?
HOW JEHOVAH HELPS US TO USE OUR CONSCIENCE
17. How did Jehovah help the Israelites use their conscience?
17 On one occasion, Jehovah instructed Moses to tell the Israelites: "Your lifeblood I will require at the hand of everyone among you; and each man's brother I will require at the hand of every man [or, avenge].'" (Leviticus 17:11) By enforcing this law, Israel learned to deeply respect life and to show consideration for one another. Jehovah helps us to use our conscience when we face difficult choices.
18. What example did Jesus set, and how can it help us?
18 While on earth, Jesus always prioritized his Father's will, even when it meant making sacrifices. This is why he could say: "I seek not my own will, but the will of the One who sent me."—John 5:30; Hebrews 10:1. Jesus' willingness to sacrifice himself demonstrates the depth of his love for God and for mankind. Because of the sacrifice Jesus made, Jehovah can offer eternal life to those who exercise faith in him.—John 3:16; Hebrews 9:11, 12; 1 Peter 1:18, 19.
19. How can we show that we 'take to heart' someone's conscience?
19 Let us be grateful to Jehovah for giving us a sense of right and wrong! We want to encourage others to follow Jesus' example and live forever. When we teach people, we should try to help them understand how Bible principles apply to their personal circumstances. (Ezekiel 3:17-21) And like the apostle Paul, we should be willing to say: "I have kept clear of bloodguilt. From this day forward I am innocent of the blood of all men." (Acts 20:26, 27) We demonstrate that we respect people's consciences when we help them make decisions that please Jehovah.
^ par. 16 If you find an article helpful in understanding Bible teachings, you may wish to share it with others. See pages 77-79, under the heading "Enjoy Teaching People About God," for suggestions.

2 Kwa andũ ma Yeova, kwĩkĩa ngũa ila syaĩle nĩ kwa vata mũno, o na nĩ kwa vata kwa Ngai ũsu tũthaithaa. (Mwa. 3:
3. Mĩao ĩla Ngai wanengete Aisilaeli yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa mĩkĩĩle ya ngũa?
3 Kwa ngelekany'o, mĩao ĩmwe katĩ wa mĩao ĩla Ngai wanengete Aisilaeli nĩyamasũvĩanaa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku vyũ wa mbaĩ ila syamathyũlũlũkĩte. Mĩao ĩsu nĩyoonanisye ũndũ Yeova waleanĩte vyũ na mĩkĩĩle ya ngũa ĩla ĩtonya kũtuma mũndũ mũka oneka ta mũndũũme na mũndũũme oneka ta mũndũ mũka. (Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 22:5.) Kwoou ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a nesa kana Ngai ndendeeaw'a nĩ mĩkĩĩle ya ngũa ĩla ĩtumaa aũme mekala aka, aka mekala aũme, kana wĩthĩa ndũvathũkany'a mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka.
4. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya Aklĩsto meke motwi maseo ĩũlũ wa ngũa?
4 Ndeto ya Ngai yĩ na myolooto ya kũtetheesya Aklĩsto meke motwi maseo ĩũlũ wa ngũa ila maĩle kwĩkĩa. Na myolooto ĩsu no ĩtũmĩwe nĩ Aklĩsto onthe, methĩwe mekalaa va, syĩthĩo syoo nĩ syĩva, kana nzeve ya kwoo ĩilyĩ ata. Ti nginya tũnengwe mĩao mingĩ ĩeleetye mĩsono ya ngũa ĩla yĩtĩkĩlĩkĩte na ĩla ĩtetĩkĩlĩkĩte. Vandũ va ũu, tũtongoeaw'a nĩ myolooto ya Maandĩko. Nayo myolooto ĩsu ndĩtwovete ũkethĩa tũyamba kwĩnyuvĩa ithyĩ ene kĩla tũkwenda kwĩkĩa. Ekai twone myolooto ĩmwe yĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya kũmanya "kwenda kwa Ngai kũla kũseo na kũla kwĩtĩkĩlĩka na kũla kwĩanĩu" ĩla tũũnyuva nĩ ngũa syĩva tũkwĩkĩa.
'NĨTŨKWĨYĨĨKĨĨTHYA TA ATHŨKŨMI MA NGAI'
