Andũ aingĩ nĩmambĩĩaa kũtũsũanĩa kwa nzĩa na, kana makethĩwa na woni mũna ĩũlũ witũ kwosana na 'mũvw'anĩle witũ wa ũtheinĩ.' (1 Sam. 16:7) Kwoou ithyĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩtũeleawa kana kwĩkĩa ngũa ti o kwĩkĩa kĩndũ kyonthe kĩla tũkwĩw'a kĩitwendeesya. Myolooto ĩla twĩsĩ kuma Ndetonĩ ya Ngai nĩyaĩle kũtuma twĩvathana na ngũa itũkwete mũno, iũtũtia tũilyĩ ta twĩ athei, kana ikũamũkĩsya angĩ wendi mũthũku. O na ũu nĩ kwonany'a kana tũyaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa syonanĩtye kana syumĩlĩtye mamutha maitũ ala mataĩle kwoneka. Tũyaĩle kũtuma mũndũ o na wĩva alasimĩka kũsisya ũtee oona ũndũ twĩkĩĩte.
6 Ĩla tweekĩa ngũa ila syaĩle, ngũa ntheu, na twasyĩkĩa nesa nĩvatonyeka andũ makatũnenga ndaĩa na maimũkumya Mwĩaĩi Mũsumbĩ Mũnene Yeova. O na nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka makendeew'a nĩ kũmũthaitha Ngai ũla tũthaithaa. O na ĩngĩ, mwĩkĩĩle mwaĩlu wa ngũa nũeteae ndaĩa ũseũvyo wa Yeova. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩvatonyeka mũno andũ makethukĩĩsya ũvoo ũla tũmatavasya.
7, 8. Nĩ ĩvinda yĩva mũno mũno twaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa ila syaĩle?
7 Twĩ na thiĩ na Ngai witũ mũtheu, na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ, vamwe na andũ ala me ũtũinĩ. Thiĩ ũsu nĩ kwĩkĩa ngũa ila itonya kũtuma ũvoo ũla tũtavanasya ũnengwa ndaĩa na itonya kũtuma Yeova ataĩwa. (Alo. 13:
8 Soma 1 Akolintho 10:31. Ĩla tũendete maũmbanonĩ manene twaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa syĩ na kĩasi na syaĩle, ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kwĩkĩa naĩ tondũ twonaa andũ ma nthĩ ĩno mekĩĩte. O na ĩngĩ ĩla tũendete kana tumĩte motelinĩ na ĩla tũthyũmũĩte ĩvindanĩ ya maũmbano asu, tũyaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa oou ta tũteũmaka. Tweekĩa ngũa nesa tũikew'aa nthoni kũtavya angĩ kana ithyĩ nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. O na tũkeew'aa twĩ na ũthasyo wa kũtavya andũ ũvoo mũseo ĩla vaumĩla mwanya.
9, 10. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Avilivi 2:4 ĩla tũũnyuva kĩla tũkwĩkĩa?
9 Soma Avilivi 2:4. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto maĩle kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ana-a-asa ala angĩ ĩla meũnyuva ngũa? Kĩtumi kĩmwe nĩ kana andũ ma Ngai mekĩaa kĩthito mũno maatĩĩe ũtao ũũ wĩ Mbivilianĩ: "Ũaai mamutha menyu ala me kũũ nthĩ: ũlaalai, na ũvuku, na mĩmeo mĩthũku." (Ako. 3:
10 Ĩla twĩ na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ, mwĩkĩĩle witũ wa ngũa nĩwaĩle kũtuma mew'a kĩkundinĩ ne vandũ vaseo vate na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku. Ũndũ ũsu nĩ wa vata twĩthĩwe twĩ ũmbanonĩ kana twĩ vandũ vangĩ. Tũivatĩtwe kwĩnyuvĩa ngũa ila tũkwenda kwĩkĩa. Ĩndĩ ithyonthe nĩtwaĩlĩte kwĩkĩa ngũa iũtuma wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa angĩ kwĩkala me atheu na maiendeea kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Ngai ĩũlũ wa ũtheu wa mosũanĩo, ndeto, na mwĩkalĩle. (1 Vet. 1:
NGŨA ILA SYAĨLE, ĨVINDANĨ YĨLA YAĨLE, NA VANDŨ VALA VAĨLE
11, 12. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva twaĩle kũsũanĩa ĩla tũũnyuva kĩla tũkwĩkĩa?
11 Ĩla athũkũmi ma Ngai meĩka motwi ĩũlũ wa kĩla mekwĩkĩa, nĩmamanyaa "kwĩ ĩvinda kw'o kwondũ wa kĩla ũndũ na kĩla wĩa." (Mũta. 3:
12 Ti laisi kwa andũ ala mekalaa kũla kũvyũ kũĩkĩĩthya kana meekĩa ngũa syĩ na ndaĩa na syĩkwonany'a mũndũ e na kĩlĩko. Kwoou ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa nĩmew'aa mũyo ĩla tweevathana na kwĩkĩa ngũa itũkwete mũno kana iũtuma wĩthĩa no ta twĩ athei. (Yovu 31:1) O na ĩngĩ ĩla tũthyũmũĩlĩte ũtee wa ũkanga kana ĩla twĩ kũla kũtuvĩaa andũ nĩtwaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa sya kũthambĩa ila syaĩle. (Nth. 11:
13. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũsũanĩa mwolooto ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 10:
13 Ve mwolooto ũngĩ wa vata ũtonya kũtũtetheesya kũnyuva ngũa ila syaĩle. Mwolooto ũsu nĩ kana ithyĩ nĩtũsũanĩaa wasya wa ngoo wa angĩ, methĩwe nĩ ala tũthaithaa namo kana nĩ andũ angĩ. (Soma 1 Akolintho 10:
14. Asyai matonya ata kũmanyĩsya syana syoo imũkumasye Ngai kwĩsĩla mwĩkĩĩle wasyo wa ngũa?
14 Asyai Aklĩsto me na kĩanda kya kũmanyĩsya mĩsyĩ yoo kũatĩĩa myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ. Ũu nĩ vamwe na kũĩkĩĩthya kana mo ene vamwe na syana syoo nĩmeekĩa kĩthito mamũtanĩthye Ngai kwa kwĩkĩa ngũa ila syaĩle na kwĩyanakavya kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle. (Nth. 22:6; 27:11) Ĩla asyai meethĩwa me ngelekany'o nzeo kwa syana syoo na maitaa kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte, kĩu nĩkĩitetheeasya ikamanya kũnenga ndaĩa Ngai mũtheu ũla tũthaithaa. Wĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ mũseo ta kĩ ĩla asyai moony'a syana syoo ũndũ itonya kũnyuva ngũa nzeo na vala itonya kũithooa! Kwoou maĩlĩte kũtetheesya syana syoo imanye kana ĩla iũthooa ngũa, iyaĩlĩte kũnyuva ngũa no ũndũ nĩsyendeew'a nĩsyo ĩndĩ syaĩle kũnyuvaa ngũa ila itonya kũitetheesya ianĩsye kĩanda kĩla syĩ nakyo kya kũkua ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova Ngai.
TŨMĨA NESA ŨTHASYO WAKU
15. Nĩ kyaũ twaĩlĩte kũlilikana ĩla tũũnyuva ngũa?
15 Ndeto ya Ngai yĩ na motao maseo matonya kũtũtetheesya twĩke motwi maseo ala matonya kũmũtaĩa Ngai. Nĩ w'o kana mĩkĩĩle yitũ ya ngũa yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kĩla ũmwe e ngũa ila wendete na ũkwati witũ ndwĩanene. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, kĩla ĩvinda ngũa sitũ nĩsyaĩle kwĩthĩwa syĩ ntheu, syĩ mbaĩlu, syosanĩte na ũndũ ũla tũkwĩka, na syĩtĩkĩlĩkĩte kĩsionĩ kĩla tũĩ.
16. Nĩkĩ tũyĩthĩawa tũitethya wĩa wa mana ĩla tweekĩa kĩthito tũkwate ngũa mbaĩlu?
16 Nĩtwĩsĩ kana ti laisi kĩla ĩvinda kwĩka ũtwi ũkwonany'a kana twĩ na kĩlĩko, na kana nĩtwambĩte kũsũanĩa maũndũ onthe nesa. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ nduka mbingĩ ithooasya ngũa ila syendetwe nĩ andũ aingĩ, na kwoou nĩvendekaa kĩthito kingĩ na ĩvinda yingĩ kũmantha ngũa mbaĩlu na itatũkwete mũno, syĩthĩwe nĩ sikati, itonyeo, sati, suti, kana mĩvuuto. Ĩndĩ tweekĩa kĩthito nĩ kana tũkwate ngũa nzeo na mbaĩlu, nĩvatonyeka Aklĩsto ala angĩ makona ũu na makew'a mũyo. Na o na kau nĩtũtonya kũthĩnĩka mũno tũimantha ngũa ila mbaĩlu, nĩtwĩw'aa tweanĩwa mũno nũndũ kĩthito kitũ nĩkĩtumaa Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ akwata ndaĩa.
17. Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva matonya kũtuma mwana-a-asa aĩthya kĩng'ee kana akalea kũkĩĩthya?
17 Nao nata kũĩthya kĩng'ee? Kwosana na Mĩao ya Mose, yaĩ lasima aũme maĩthye kĩng'ee. Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto mai ungu wa Mĩao ya Mose, o na ti nginya mamĩatĩĩe. (Ali. 19:27; 21:5; Aka. 3:
18, 19. Ĩandĩko ya Mika 6:8 yĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ata ĩla tũendeee kwĩkĩa kĩthito tũnyuve ngũa iũmũetea Ngai ndaĩa?
18 Nĩtũtanaa mũno nũndũ Yeova ndatwĩkĩĩe mĩao mingĩ ya ũndũ twaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa na kwĩyanakavya. Vandũ va ũu, nũtwĩtĩkĩlĩtye tũtũmĩe ũthasyo witũ kwĩka motwi maseo tũtongoew'e nĩ myolooto ĩla yĩ Maandĩkonĩ. Tweeka ũu tũkoonany'a nĩtũkwenda 'kwĩkalany'a na Ngai witũ twĩ na wĩnyivyo,' kwĩsĩla mwĩkĩĩle witũ wa ngũa na kwĩyanakavya kwitũ.
19 Nzĩa ĩmwe twonanasya twĩ na wĩnyivyo nĩ kũmanya kana Yeova nĩ mũtheu vyũ na kana vai ũngĩ ũtonya kũtũtongoesya nesa eka we na kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa myolooto yake. O na ĩngĩ, ethĩwa twĩ na wĩnyivyo tũkanengaa ndaĩa mawoni ma ala angĩ na tũielewa ũndũ mekwĩw'a. Kwoou 'twĩkalanasya na Ngai witũ twĩ na wĩnyivyo' ethĩwa nĩtwaatĩĩa myolooto yake thayũnĩ witũ na tũinavũthĩĩsya woni wa ala angĩ.
20. Ngũa sitũ na kwĩyanakavya kwitũ kwaĩle kũtuma angĩ meka ata?
20 Mwĩkĩĩle witũ wa ngũa ndwaĩle kũtuma andũ masũanĩa maũndũ angĩ ĩũlũ witũ, ĩndĩ waĩle kũtuma mamanya kana ithyĩ twĩ athaithi ma Yeova. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa na andũ ala angĩ onthe nĩmaĩle kwona nĩtũkuĩte nesa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai witũ mũlũngalu. Myolooto yake yĩ ĩũlũ mũno na nĩtũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũmĩatĩĩe twĩ atanu. Nĩtũũmakatha ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala methĩĩtwe mayĩkĩa ngũa nesa, mayĩyanakavya nesa, na me na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Na kĩtumi nũndũ kĩu nĩkĩtumaa ala me na ngoo nzeo mendeew'a nĩ ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ na nĩkĩtumaa Yeova akwata nguma na ew'a mũyo. Kwa w'o, twaendeea kwĩka motwi maseo ĩũlũ wa kĩla tũkwĩkĩa, tũkaendeea kũmũkumya Ngai ũla wĩvw'ĩkĩte "ndaĩa na ũnene."

translation:
"Let us make man in our image."
MBATHI: 34, 29
1, 2. Why does Jehovah's organization allow its members to get involved in politics? (Consider the points mentioned.)
One cassette from a Dutch series stated this about being neutral: "Many people think that neutrality means doing nothing, and often it involves taking a stand." The cassette went on to say: "This is not showing loyalty to Jehovah's organization. . . . A child and his parents can take sides and support something, and also someone can support something and oppose something . . . because they believe it is right, and it is not disloyalty to their conscience." This shows how much Jehovah's organization allows its members to become involved in "worldly affairs, associations and activities . . . or things that are worldly . . . but always with the purpose of honoring God." (1 Tim. 2:
2 For Jehovah's people, getting involved in such affairs is proper, and it is pleasing to God who is able to help us. (Gen. 3:
3. How did God permit Israel to learn lessons from foreign political powers?
3 For example, some of the ways God permitted Israel to come into contact with the political powers were through treaties and agreements. These ways showed what Jehovah thinks about political powers that try to make a person side with one nation and another person side with another nation. (Read 2 Kings 22:5.) Does this mean that God approves of political powers that cause families to be divided, or nations to fight against each other?
4. What can help a Christian to remain neutral regarding politics?
4 God's Word has clear direction for Christians to remain neutral regarding politics, but it does not give specific details. However, this direction is based on Christ's example, who did not become involved in politics himself, nor did he encourage his followers to do so. Let us examine more scriptures that show how we can stay clean from the world's politics and maintain our neutrality. We should let Bible principles guide us. And these principles will help us to apply wisdom when making decisions. For instance, the principle found in Micah shows us how to understand "what Jehovah asks of us—to practice justice, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with our God"—when dealing with political matters.
'WE MUST BE LOYAL TO GOD'S KINGDOM'
5, 6. Why might a Christian find it difficult to remain neutral?
5 The apostle Paul explained why it is important to be different from those around us, reading 2 Corinthians 6:4. (Read.) Many people feel strongly about their political views and may look down on those who do not share them, or they may judge us because we do not get involved in "their way of thinking." (1 Sam. 16:7) It takes discernment to know when it is appropriate to speak up or when it is best to remain silent. The direction we receive from God's Word helps us to avoid getting involved in things that could compromise our spirituality or cause us to stumble. This direction also helps us to make wise decisions and to avoid associating with those whose values and morals are questionable. We want to be careful not to allow anyone to pressure us into doing something wrong.
6 But when such situations arise, it is often difficult, and we may feel distressed when others oppose us and reproach us for serving the Most High God, Jehovah. And it can be upsetting when others try to force us to disobey God. Furthermore, remember the example of those who loyally served Jehovah despite facing opposition. Because of this, many people have been strengthened in their determination to stand firm.
7, 8. Why is it vital that we be different?
7 We love our heavenly Father, and we value his standards, as well as the standards of fellow Christians. One reason why we take a stand is so that our ministry will not be discredited and so that Jehovah will be honored. (Phil. 13:
8 Read 1 Corinthians 10:31. Whether we are doing great things or small things, we want to please God. Also, whether we eat or travel or engage in any activity, we want to be different from those in this world. Furthermore, whether we work or spend time relaxing, we want to be different so that we do not become conformed to their ways. Let us always be mindful that we need to give a fine witness to the name of Jehovah. And let us strive to show consideration for those who may be honesthearted.
9, 10. How does the principle at Proverbs 2:4 help us to know what to say?
9 Read Proverbs 2:4. Did Christ use wisdom when dealing with people? One way he showed wisdom was by applying the principle found in the proverb: "Call out for wisdom itself and ask earnestly for understanding." (Prov. 3:
10 So, when speaking to family members and others, let our speech be thoughtful and beneficial. Our words can have a powerful effect on others, either for good or for bad. We should speak in a way that will move people toward God rather than cause them to stumble. In fact, we want to speak in such a manner that our message will be pleasing to God and will help others to appreciate his laws and principles. (1 Thess. 1:
MATTERS THAT ARE PLEASING, IMPORTANT, AND BENEFICIAL
11, 12. What matters are pleasing to God?
11 God's faithful servants are interested in "approving what is acceptable to [God] and discerning what his will is." (Eph. 3:
12 It is not enough simply to avoid doing things that are clearly wrong. We must also avoid associating with those who practice wickedness or engage in harmful activities. Family members and others can influence us to do what is wrong, so we need to be careful about the company we keep. (Job 31:1) And we must not allow ourselves to become complacent or to think that we can associate with bad people without being affected by their negative influence. (Prov. 11:
13. How does 1 Corinthians 10:13 help us to understand this?
13 This scripture warns us against allowing anything to lead us astray. It says that temptations may come from sources outside our congregation, perhaps from well-meaning individuals or even from strangers. (Read 1 Corinthians 10:
14. Why is it important to discern whether something is truly pleasing to God?
14 Why should Christians be cautious about getting involved in questionable pursuits? Because such pursuits could lead them away from Jehovah, causing them to stumble and fall. (Acts 22:6; 27:11) But those who are determined to remain loyal to Jehovah will seek his guidance and will carefully examine themselves to see if they are engaging in anything that displeases him. They will realize that even seemingly harmless things can have a corrupting influence! So let us always be vigilant and ask ourselves: 'Is this activity truly pleasing to God, or might it lead me astray?' If we are unsure, let us thoroughly investigate the matter and determine whether it is consistent with Bible principles and would honor Jehovah God.
USE SELF-CONTROL
15. What can help us to resist temptation?
15 God's spirit can give us strength to resist temptation and to please God. However, we must also make diligent effort. Each of us has personal weaknesses. Some may struggle with anger, others with greed, and still others with improper desires. We need to identify our own weaknesses and take steps to overcome them.
16. How can we maintain spiritual health when faced with trialsome situations?
16 Let us examine whether we are listening to our conscience and whether we have a good reputation, and whether we are eager to correct wrong behavior. Why? Because a bad habit can easily lead to more serious sins, such as stealing, lying, adultery, or violence. If we allow ourselves to fall into sin, we risk damaging our relationship with God and losing his favor.
17. What factors can contribute to a young person becoming rebellious or disobedient?
17 And what about giving in to temptation? The Law of Moses showed that yielding to temptation could have dire consequences. Christians are under the Law of Christ, but this does not mean they are immune to its effects. (Acts 19:27; 21:5; 1 Cor. 3:
18, 19. How does Micah 6:8 help us to determine whether we are truly walking with God?
18 We should strive to please Jehovah by obeying his laws and principles. As Christians, let us use our discernment to make wise decisions and be guided by the teachings of the Bible. In this way, we will show that we are determined "to harmonize with our God through our hearts," rather than simply following religious rituals and traditions.
19 One way to harmonize with our hearts is to cultivate faith in Jehovah and trust that he will guide us and protect us from harm. By doing so, we demonstrate that we are willing to submit to his authority and accept his discipline. Furthermore, when we study the Bible and pray earnestly, we gain a deeper understanding of his will and purpose. Thus, "harmonizing with our God through our hearts" means submitting to his authority and allowing him to mold us into the people he wants us to be.
20. Can our desire to maintain a good reputation cause us to compromise our integrity?
20 Our desire to have a good name can lead us to try to impress others, which could result in us concealing the truth about Jehovah. However, both young and old ones can learn to prioritize pleasing God above pleasing men. His standards are always right, and we can benefit greatly by striving to meet them. Let us therefore imitate those who put spiritual things first, who value righteousness, and who seek to live in harmony with God's will. And let us remember that the consequences of compromising our integrity can be devastating, as was the case with Demas, who "became enamored with the present system of things" and abandoned Paul. Therefore, let us continue to give diligent attention to what we hear, so that we may remain steadfast in our faith and worship "God with sincerity and fullness."

KWASŨANĨA Sala e nyũmbanĩ yake aimĩloela. Kwakũna visa ĩũlũ wa mũndũ mũka wĩ na metho ma kwendeesya kuma nthĩ yĩ wumĩlonĩ wa sua (Middle East). We mũndũ mũka ũsu nũkwoneka emakĩe? Ethĩwa nĩwĩmakĩe, ti vinya kũmanya nĩkĩ ũilyĩ ũu. Ve maũndũ maingĩ mũndũ mũka ũsu watanĩĩte nyũmbanĩ ĩsu nũndũ nĩwekalanasya nesa na mũũme wake, Avalaamu, kwa myaka mingĩ. * Ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mũsyĩ woo.
Mekalaa Ulu, mũsyĩ mũnene waĩ na andũ me na ũtũĩka wa kũseũvya syĩndũ na moko moo, na atandĩthya. Kwoou no nginya methĩwe maĩ na malĩ. Ĩndĩ Sala ndoonaa nyũmba ĩsu yoo yĩ ya vata nũndũ nĩ vo maiaa malĩ, ĩndĩ ve itumi ingĩ. E na mũũme nĩmekalĩte nyũmba ĩsu kwa myaka mingĩ me atanu o na kau ve mavinda meethĩawa na mathĩna. O na ĩngĩ me nyũmbanĩ ĩsu, nĩmamũvoyaa Yeova Ngai mavinda maingĩ mũno nũndũ nĩmamwendete. Kwoou, Sala aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo mũno kya kwenda vandũ vau.
Ĩndĩ Sala nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kũtia syĩndũ isu syonthe wamanyĩĩte. O na kau nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa aĩ vakuvĩ myaka 60, aaĩle kũthi kũndũ ũteesĩ, na kwĩkala kũndũ kwĩ na mĩisyo na mawetu, ate na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũsyoka ĩngĩ. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie eka moalyũku asu manenevete ũu? Naitũ ũmũnthĩ tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na mũĩkĩĩo wake?
"UMA NTHĨ ĨNO YAKU"
Nĩvatonyeka Sala akethĩwa eanĩie Ulu. Ũmũnthĩ kĩla kĩtiele taoninĩ ĩsu no myako mĩombokangu. Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ ya Sala, atandĩthya kuma kũndũ kũasa nĩmaetae mĩio ya vata mamĩthoosye taoninĩ ya Ulu, ĩla yaĩ na maendeeo maingĩ. Maetae mĩio ĩsu mesĩlĩte Ũsĩnĩ wa Euvalati. Taoni ĩsu ya Ulu yeethĩawa yusĩe andũ, meli sya kũkua syĩndũ syaĩ mbingĩ, na mĩio yausũaa kĩla vandũ tũsokonĩ tũla twaĩ vau. Kwasũanĩa Sala eanĩĩte taoninĩ ĩsu yaĩ na maũndũ maingĩvĩte ũu, na nĩweesĩ andũ aingĩ mayo na masyĩtwa. O namo no nginya methĩwe mamũlilikanaa nĩkwĩthĩwa aĩ mũndũ mũka mwanake mũno. O na andũ aingĩ ma mũsyĩ woo maĩ taoninĩ ĩsu.
Mbivilianĩ, Sala esĩkĩe ta mũndũ mũka wĩ mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, ĩndĩ ndaĩkĩĩaa ngai ya mwai ĩla yathaithawa nĩ andũ aingĩ taoninĩ ya Ulu. Taoninĩ ĩsu nĩvaakĩtwe mwako mũtũlu mũno wa ngai ĩsu ya mwai. Ĩndĩ Sala athaithaa Yeova, Ngai ũla wa w'o. Maandĩko mayonanĩtye ũndũ wakwatie mũĩkĩĩo ũsu. Ve ĩvinda yĩmwe ĩthe wake wathaithaa ngai sya mĩvw'anano. Sala nĩwesie kũtwaana na Avalaamu, ũla wamũtiĩte na myaka ĩkũmi. * (Mwambĩlĩlyo 17:17) Avalaamu nĩwesie kũtw'ĩka "ĩthe wa onthe ala metĩkĩlaa." (Alomi 4:11) Na e na mũka wake Sala maĩ na mũtwaano mũlũmu nũndũ nĩmanenganĩte ndaĩa, nĩmaeaa ngewa nesa, na nĩmomĩĩasya mathĩna me ngwatanĩo. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla mũnene nĩ kana, maĩ na ngwatanĩo nzeo nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩmamwendete Ngai.
Sala nĩwendete mũũme wake mũno na nĩmaakie mũsyĩ woo taoninĩ ya Ulu vala andũ moo ma mũsyĩ matwĩe. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini, nĩmakwatiwe nĩ ũndũ mũito. Mbivilia ĩtũtavĩtye kana Sala "aĩ ngũngũ; ndaĩ mwana." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 11:30) Kwosana na syĩthĩo sya ĩvinda yĩu, ũndũ ũsu waĩ mũito mũno kwa Sala. Ĩndĩ nĩwaendeeie kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai na kwa mũũme wake. Avalaamu na Sala nĩmoosie Loto, ũla wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ ĩthe, mekalae nake na atw'ĩka ta mwana woo. Ĩthe wa Loto asyaanĩw'e na Avalaamu. Maendeeie kwĩkala Ulu nginya ĩla maũndũ mesie kũvĩndũka.
Avalaamu nĩwookie vala ve Sala e na ũtanu mwingĩ. Ũndũ ũla waĩ ũneekĩka wamũseng'isye mũno. Ngai ũla mathaithaa nĩwaneenie nake kwĩsĩla mũlaĩka! Kwasũanĩa Sala asiĩĩsye mũũme wake aimũkũlya-ĩ: "Akwĩie ata? Mwa naku ndavye!" Noĩthwa Avalaamu ambie kwĩkala nthĩ asũanĩe ũndũ ũkũmũsũngĩa, na ĩndĩ amũtavya ũndũ Yeova waisye. Yeova amwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Uma nthĩ ĩno yaku, ũtie andũ maku, ũthi nthĩ ĩla ngakwon'ya." (Meko ma Atũmwa 7:
No tũsũanĩe kana tũyĩsa kũkwatwa nĩ ũndũ waĩle kũtuma twĩka ũtwi ta ũla Sala waaĩle kwĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, no tũsũanĩe atĩĩ: 'Vai ĩvinda Ngai waaĩsa kũmbĩa, kana akea ũla ndwaanĩte nake eke ũndũ ũilyĩ ta ũsu!' Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ithyonthe nĩtwaĩle kwĩka ũtwi ta ũla Sala waaĩle kwĩka. Tũtwĩe nthĩ yĩ na andũ mendete malĩ, na ũu no ũtume tũthĩnĩkĩa mũno kwĩanĩsya mawendi maitũ, kwĩthĩwa na malĩ, na kwenda kwĩthĩwa twĩ ũsũvĩonĩ. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya twĩke ũtwi ũngĩ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o, naw'o nĩ kũvĩtya maũndũ ma kĩ-veva mbee, na tũimwendeesya Ngai vandũ va kwĩyendeesya ithyĩ ene. (Mathayo 6:33) Tũisũanĩa ũtwi ũla Sala wesie kwĩka, no twĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nĩ ũtwi wĩva nĩvangĩte kwĩka?'
NĨMAUMIE NTHĨ ĨSU
Sala aendeee na kũmbany'a syĩndũ syake, nĩwasaanĩaw'a ekua syĩndũ syĩva na etia syĩva. Ndaĩ akua mũio mũnene mũno ũtatonya kũkuwa nĩ mang'oi na ngamĩle, nĩkwĩthĩwa aaĩlĩte kwĩkala aithamathama. Vate nzika, maĩ mate kana manengane malĩ yoo mbingĩ. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ mesaa kũtia nĩ moseo ma kwĩkala taoni, ta kwĩthĩwa me vakuvĩ na soko vala maendaa kũũa lĩu, nyama, matunda, ngũa na syĩndũ ingĩ.
No kwĩthĩwa waĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya Sala kũtia nyũmba yake. Nyũmba ĩsu ĩkethĩwa yailyĩ ta nyũmba ila syaakawa taoninĩ ya Ulu, ila imanyĩkĩte ũndũ syaseũvĩte nĩ andũ ala menzaa syĩndũ sya tene, no nginya Sala ethĩwe atiie maũndũ maseo mũno. Imwe sya nyũmba isu syaĩ na lumu mbingĩ, kĩw'ũ kĩtheu kya kĩthima na kya mĩveleki. O na nyũmba ya kĩlasi kya nthĩ yaĩ ĩtonya kwĩthĩwa na kĩala kĩlũmu, ngũta, na mĩomo ĩtonya kũvingĩka. Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Ĩeema yĩla Sala mesaa kũthi kwĩkala nĩ yaĩ yĩtonya kũsiĩĩa ing'ei o tondũ nyũmba isu syaĩ itonya kũsiĩĩa? Kana nĩ yaĩ yĩtonya kũsiĩĩa mĩnyambũ, ngo, nduva, na nzũi, ila syaĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ yĩu?
Nao nata ĩũlũ wa andũ ma mũsyĩ? Naaũ ala Sala wesaa kũtia? Mwĩao ũla Ngai wamatavĩtye wa 'kuma nthĩ yoo na kũtia andũ moo' nũtonya kwĩthĩwa waĩ vinya mũno kwake. Sala nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aĩ na eĩtu-a-inyia, ana-a-inyia, syana sya ala masyaanĩw'e nake, andũ angĩ masyaanĩw'e na asyai make, na andũ asu onthe amendete mũno na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa atesaa kũmona ĩngĩ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu w'onthe wĩ vo, Sala nĩwaendeeie na kwĩyũmbany'a.
O na mawũmũ asu me o vo, Sala nĩweeyũmbanĩsye mũthenya ũla maaĩle kuma Ulu. Tela, ũla waĩ ĩthe woo, aĩ aendany'e na Avalaamu na Sala o na kau aĩ vakuvĩ kũvikya myaka maana elĩ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 11:31) No nginya Sala ethĩwe esaa kwĩthĩwa na wĩa mwingĩ wa kũsũvĩa mũsyai ũsu woo mũkũũ. O nake Loto aaĩle kũendany'a namo ĩla maatĩĩie mwĩao wa Yeova wa 'kuma nthĩ ya Akalitei.'
Savalĩnĩ yoo ya mbee, maendie maili vakuvĩ 600 (kĩlomita 960) nginya Aalani, maatĩĩe Ũsĩ wa Euvalati. Nĩmekalangile kwa kavinda kũu Aalani. Nĩvatonyeka Tela akethĩwa aĩ mũwau me kũu, na ataĩ atonya kũendeea na savalĩ. Maendeeie kwĩkala kũu nginya ĩla wakwie e na myaka 205. Matanambĩĩa savalĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe, Yeova nĩwaneenie na Avalaamu ĩngĩ na amwĩa atie nthĩ ĩsu na aithi nthĩ ĩla wĩmwony'a. Yeova nĩwamwathie ũndũ ũmwe wa kwendeesya. Amwĩie atĩĩ: "Ngakũtw'ĩkĩthya mbaĩ nene." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 12:
O na maũndũ mailyĩ oou, nĩmaumie Aalani na maendeea na savalĩ. Ĩndĩ ve andũ angĩ maendanisye namo. Ngewa ĩsu yonanĩtye kana Avalaamu na mũsyĩ wake maumie na malĩ ĩla moombanĩtye, vamwe na "andũ ala matw'ĩkĩte ngombo syoo me Aalani." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 12:
"ATHEEA MISILI"
Ĩtina wa kũinga Ũsĩ wa Euvalati, na nĩvatonyeka kũkethĩwa kwaĩ Matukũ 14 ma mwei wa Nisani, 1943 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, nĩmatheeie nginya nthĩ ĩla Yeova wamathĩte. (Kuma 12:
Ĩndĩ, mũsyĩ woo waĩ o ũtonya kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna ma nthĩ ĩno. Nzaa mbingĩ nĩyaumĩlile Kanaani, na kwoou Avalaamu avanga kuma kũu na atheea Misili na mũsyĩ wake. Ĩndĩ, nĩwoonie ve mũisyo ũtonya kumĩla kĩsionĩ kĩu. Na kwoou aneena na Sala aimwĩa atĩĩ: "Na yu ĩndĩ, nĩnĩsĩ wĩ mũndũ mũka mwanake mũno kwa kũsiw'a: na kũkeethĩwa, yĩla Amisili mekwona, makasya, Ũũ nĩ mũka wake: na makambũaa, ĩndĩ we makakũeka wĩ thayũ. Nĩngũkwĩsũva, asya wĩ mwĩĩtu-a-ia; nĩ kana kwĩthĩwe kwĩ kũseo kwakwa kwondũ waku, na kyuu kyakwa kĩkale thayũ kwondũ waku." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 12:
Avalaamu ndakenganaa na ndakĩaa, tondũ andũ amwe maasyaa. Kwa w'o, Sala na Avalaamu maĩ ma ĩthe ũmwe. Na Avalaamu aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩkala etũĩĩe. Avalaamu na Sala nĩmeesĩ kana ũndũ ũla waĩ wa vata vyũ nĩ kwĩanĩw'a kwa kĩeleelo kya Ngai kya kumĩlya ũsyao wa mwanya na mbaĩ kwĩsĩla Avalaamu, kwoou yaĩ no nginya esũvĩe. O na ũkunĩkĩli ũla wĩkĩtwe wa maũndũ ma tene, wonanĩtye kana aũme ala maĩ na ũkũmũ ma Misili nĩmavenaa aũme iveti syoo na maimoaa. Kwoou Avalaamu nĩwatũmĩie ũĩ, nake Sala nĩweetĩkĩlanile na ũtwi ũsu wa mũũme.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, maũndũ ala meekĩkie nĩmoonanisye nesa kana Avalaamu aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩthĩwa etũĩĩe, nũndũ anene amwe me mbee ũsumbĩnĩ wa Valao nĩmoonie Sala e mwanake mũno o na kau aĩ mũkũũ. Nĩmamũtavisye Valao, nake aumya mwĩao mũndũ mũka ũsu aetwe kwake! Nĩ vinya mũno kũsũanĩa ũndũ Avalaamu wathĩnĩkaa ngoonĩ, kana ũndũ Sala watelemete. Ĩndĩ veonekana Sala akuiwe nesa, vandũ va kũtũmĩwa ta ngombo. No kwĩthĩwa Valao avangie kũmũsesenga Sala na aimũtanĩthya na malĩ yake, na ĩndĩ aineena na "mwana-a-inyia" nĩ kenda amũtwae.
Kwasũanĩa Sala ayĩloela kũndũ kwanake Misili e valandanĩ wa nyũmba ya mũsumbĩ. Eewie ata ĩla wambĩĩie kwĩkala nyũmbanĩ yĩ na ngũta, kĩala, na lĩu mũseo? Na nũndũ nĩvatonyeka maũndũ nyũmbanĩ ya mũsumbĩ makethĩwa maĩ maseango o na kwĩ ũndũ Ulu kwailyĩ, we Sala nĩwĩthĩwa akengekie? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Satani wĩthĩwa atanie kethĩwa Sala nĩwatwie kũmũtia Avalaamu na aitw'ĩka kĩveti kya Valao! Ĩndĩ nũndũ Sala aĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa mũũme wake, mũtwaano wake, na kwa Ngai wake, ndaaĩka ũndũ wa mũthemba ũsu. Mwa kethĩwa kĩla mũndũ ũtwaanĩte kana mũtwae nĩwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku ũu o na kau tũilyĩ nthĩ yĩ na andũ me mwĩkalĩle mũthũku! No wĩthĩwe wĩ mũĩkĩĩku ta Sala maũndũnĩ onthe ala ũkwĩka mũndũ ũla ũmwendete kana mũnyanyau?
Yeova nĩwalikĩlĩĩle nĩ kana asũvĩe mũndũ mũka ũsu, na eekie ũu kwa kũmũtũmĩa Valao na nyũmba yake mothĩny'o. Ĩla Valao wamanyie kana Sala nĩ mũka wa Avalaamu, nĩwamwĩie nasyokee mũũme, na amũtavya Avalaamu vamwe na andũ make maume Misili. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 12:
^ kal. 3 Mbeenĩ meetawa Avalamu na Salai, ĩndĩ mesĩkĩe nesa na masyĩtwa ala Yeova wesie kũmanenga.
^ kal. 8 Sala na Avalaamu maĩ ma ĩthe ũmwe. Tela nĩwe waĩ ĩthe woo, ĩndĩ mayaĩ ma inyia ũmwe. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 20:12) O na kau mũtwaano wa mũthemba ũsu ndwaĩlĩte ũmũnthĩ, nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũlilikana kana maũndũ maĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩvinda yĩu. Andũ maĩ vakuvĩ na wĩanĩu ũla Atamu na Eva matanĩaa na mesa kwasya. Kwa andũ ta asu maĩ na mĩĩ mĩseo, mĩtwaano katĩ wa andũ maileny'e ũndũ ndyaumĩlasya mathĩna ala matonya kwĩthĩwa na syana sya andũ ala matwaana me ma ũko ũmwe. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa myaka ta 400, andũ mekalaa myaka yĩanene na ĩla twĩkalaa ũmũnthĩ. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu Mĩao ya Mose nĩyaleile mĩtwaano katĩ wa andũ maileny'e ũndũ.

Sadly, Sarah was weeping in her house. Because of the visa issue, a man was trying to go to another country (Middle East). Is this man known anywhere? Perhaps he is, but it's hard to know until this happens. Many times this man stayed in our house for a long time and befriended my husband, Abraham, for many years. * This is his story.
Mr. Olu, a great elder with people who have the ability to understand things and a certain type, and he began. He bought goats and cows with money. For Sarah, our house is very good because it has been able to provide a lot, and there are many uses. And my husband has lived in our house for many years, five or so, and we have had many children and daughters. And also in our house, I praised Jehovah God many times until I worshipped him. So, Sarah had a special opportunity to visit people.
For Sarah, she decided to help everyone she knew. And even though she was over 60 years old, she went to preach the truth, and to live the truth with joy and peace, and to continue to strive forward. What made her strong enough to do this? How can we learn to be like her example?
"UNTIL THIS DAY"
She helped Sarah introduce Ulu. Every person has their own family and relatives. For Sarah's sake, she started going to houses to share the good news about Ulu, which had many benefits. The good news spread to the Ushinini ward of Evalati. Ulu's family was known to many people, a place where many people gathered, and the news reached everyone we visited. Sadly, Sarah introduced this family to many things, and she helped many people with advice. And also many people from his village came to this family.
Truly, Sarah became a friend to someone who had a difficult situation, a story I will tell about how many people in Ulu were helped. This family was built on a solid foundation of faith. For Sarah, believing in Jehovah, the true God, was important. Scriptures show how to overcome difficulties. See how one of her descendants believed in gods of ancestors. Sarah was willing to associate with Abraham, who was blessed with children at an old age. * (Genesis 17:17) Abraham was told to be "father of many nations." (Romans 4:11) And with her husband Sarah had a deep love, despite being barren, she remained hopeful, and she trusted in God's timing. But the most important thing is that having hope and trust is pleasing to God.
Sarah treated her servant well and gave her gifts to the people of Ulu, because those gifts meant something to them. Because of this event, it was said that Sarah "laughed; she had a son." (Genesis 11:30) Just like the joy of that event, this good news was also great for Sarah. So she continued to please God and her husband. Abraham and Sarah had a son named Lot, who was given land and he had a son. The land of Lot was shown to Abraham. Continue to live in Ulu so that things don't become complicated.
Abraham took Sarah and went on a long journey. That journey was very challenging for him. The God who helped him showed him angels! As Sarah listened to her husband speaking harshly to her: "Will you really do this? I have wronged you!" Then Abraham asked her to stay while he considered what God had done. Jehovah told him: "This place is yours, bless your people, and say this land is mine." (Acts 7:
Let us learn and be careful not to be troubled by such things, so we can focus on what Sarah did. For example, let us think: 'Seek God's kingdom first, or do what I want and then everything else!' But even now, we need to focus on what Sarah did. Let us seek it with others who love it, and this will help us understand our lives better, please God, and go forward with confidence. Genesis tells us how important it is to focus on spiritual things, and we should make pleasing God and his servants our priority. (Matthew 6:33) We need to ask ourselves the question Sarah asked: 'Is this thing worth focusing on?'
THIS IS WHAT I LEARNED
Sarah continued to care for her possessions, and she was able to have good things and enjoy them. But if someone has a great desire that cannot be satisfied with little, they will always feel dissatisfied. Therefore, remember that water, food, or medicine are very important. Another thing to remember is the importance of being comfortable, having shelter, clothes, meat, fruits, vegetables, and other necessities.
And yet, there are times when Sarah needs to improve her house. Our house may not be as beautiful as the houses of the rich, but it is enough if it provides comfort and security. And if Sarah wants to add more rooms, she can do so without worrying about what others think. Some houses have many rooms, a large kitchen, and a spacious living room. Or a simple class of house can be built with mud, wood, and doors that can be locked. So, why does Sarah sometimes wish to live in a house that can provide more comfort when our house can already provide comfort? Or a house that can provide luxuries like cars, goats, cows, and fences, but doesn't offer true peace?
Now I ask, what about the feelings of others? What about those who are less fortunate than Sarah? The law of God which says 'love your neighbor and help people' should also apply to her. Sarah can also show kindness to her relatives, neighbors, children of those who helped her, other people who helped her family, and even strangers who need help. In fact, despite everything, Sarah continues to be generous.
And because of her generosity, Sarah pleased God greatly. Later, when this happened, she went with Abraham and Sarah and their servants to stay for many years. (Genesis 11:31) And again Sarah was blessed with many opportunities to demonstrate her faith. Like Lot who went with them, he chose to obey Jehovah's command to 'love righteousness.'
For several years, they traveled approximately 600 miles (960 kilometers) to Haran, in Mesopotamia. I stayed in a camp near Haran. They continued to travel from there, and Lot also continued his journey. They traveled until they reached a place that would become 205 years old. Remembering that journey, Jehovah showed me Abraham and his wife and told me about his future and his past. Jehovah revealed something to me. He said: "I will bless you abundantly." (Genesis 12:
And during those days, I visited Haran and continued my journey. There were other people traveling with them. It seems that Abraham and his family settled in places where they found water, along with "people who built cities around Haran." (Genesis 12:
"LAUNCH THE ROCKET"
As they approached Mesopotamia, and they continued to remember the 14th day of Nisan, 1943 AD, when Christ was resurrected, I realized what Jehovah had planned. (Chapter 12:
However, their family could be affected by the events of this time. Because I saw Canaan, and how Abraham went there and launched the Rocket with his family. However, I saw a sign that did not seem good. And then I heard Sarah say: "And now, behold, I have been afflicted by a man, so let me bear children; and if I do not bear children, may I be considered barren. May she find favor in your eyes, and may her descendants be numerous, and may she be like thousands upon thousands; and may her blessings be abundant." (Genesis 12:
Abraham disagreed and argued because some people opposed him. So Sarah and Abraham had a disagreement. And Abraham had a reason to stay away. Abraham and Sarah both agreed that whatever God would do was to fulfill His promise to multiply them and bless Abraham, and He would make nations great through them. But he didn't understand what those things were, and he wondered if they would happen through his own efforts, and whether his offspring would be blessed. Then Abraham sent me, and Sarah was reconciled with her husband.
The story continues, and those things happened just as Abraham had a reason to distance himself, but she also saw that the servant of Valao had found Sarah a good wife, and she knew he was older. I praised Valao, and he gave his servant someone from his house to go with him! It is important to understand what Abraham thought about, or what Sarah decided. It seemed Sarah was happy, and people sent gifts. But to distance Valao, he wanted to send Sarah and take her with his possessions, and he believed that "a daughter-in-law" would come with him.
To understand Sarah's desire to go to her brother Misili in the land of her father's house. Truly, did she tell them to stay in her house with food, water, and a good place? And why were things in the father's house made difficult for them, and because of this thing, did Sarah want to see? To understand that Satan wanted to tempt Sarah so that she would turn away from Abraham and become like Valao! It seems Sarah was proud of her husband, her servant, and her God, despite this matter of trouble. Let everyone who wants to be helped or taken be humbled in this situation, and let us learn something from those who live nearby! But how can you be humble like Sarah when things happen to you, or when you are troubled?
Jehovah remembers and will help anyone who is troubled, and truly this is for sending Valao and his family first. But Valao knew that Sarah was Abraham's wife, and he told her to comfort her mother, and he took Abraham with his young men Misili. (Chapter 12:

VE WANO ũmwe wanawa ĩũlũ wa kamwana kamwe kakya katwĩe ndũanĩ ĩmwe yĩ vaasa vyũ. Andũ ma ndũa ĩsu masũanĩaa kamwana kau kayaĩ kakye vyũ na kwoou nĩmakathekeeaa. Aeni mesa kũka, atũi amwe makosaa makakavũĩa ngũĩ mbee wa anyanyae moo. Makonasya mĩthemba ĩlĩ ya koini. Koini ĩmwe yeethĩawa yĩ ya vetha na yĩ nene. Nayo ĩla ĩngĩ yeethĩawa yĩ ya thaavu na yĩ ninangi, o na kũtw'ĩka thooa wayo waĩ kũndũ kwĩlĩ kwa ĩsu ya vetha. Makony'a koini isu makeaa atĩĩ: "Kwanyuva ĩla ũkwenda." Kamwana kau koosaa koini ĩla ya vetha na kaisemba kaithi.
Mũthenya ũmwe mũeni ũmwe akũlilye kamwana kau atĩĩ: "No wĩsĩ kana thooa wa koini ya thaavu nĩ kũndũ kwĩlĩ kwa ĩla ya vetha?" Kamwana kau kathekie na kamwĩa, "Ĩĩ, nĩnĩsĩ." Mũeni ũsu asyokie akakũlya: "Nayu nĩkĩ wosaa ĩla ya vetha? Woosa ĩla ya thaavu wĩĩthĩwa na mbesa kũndũ kwĩlĩ!" Ĩndĩ kamwana kau kamũsũngĩie: "Ngaelya kwosa koini ya thaavu, andũ asu maisyoka kũthaũka ĩthaũ yĩu nakwa. Nĩwĩsĩ nũmbanĩtye koini iana ata sya vetha?" Kamwana kau kaĩ na nguma ĩtonya kũtethya andũ aima mũno. Nguma ĩsu nĩ ũĩ mwĩanĩu.
Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Sũvĩa ũĩ mwĩanĩu na kĩlĩko. Nĩvo ĩndĩ wĩendaa mĩendelenĩ yaku wĩyelele [kana, wĩ mũsũvĩĩku], na kũũ kwaku kũtikalulutĩka." (Nth. 3:21, 23) Kwoou kũmanya "ũĩ mwĩanĩu" nĩ kyaũ, na kũmanya ũndũ tũtonya kũũtũmĩa nĩ ũsũvĩo kwitũ. Kũtũtethasya tũikasyoke ĩtina kĩ-veva nĩ kana "kũũ" kwitũ kũikalulutĩke.
ŨĨ MWĨANĨU NĨ ŨĨ ŨILYĨ ATA?
Kwĩthĩwa na ũĩ mwĩanĩu kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o na kwĩthĩwa na ũmanyi na kũelewa maũndũ. Mũndũ wĩ ũmanyi ekaa kwĩthĩwa esĩ maũndũ maingĩ. Nake mũndũ ũeleawa maũndũ nĩwonaa nata ũndũ ũmwe ũkonanĩtye na ũla ũngĩ. Ĩndĩ mũndũ ũla mũĩ nĩwĩthĩawa atonya kũtũmĩa ũmanyi ũla wĩ naw'o vamwe na maũndũ ala ũeleetwe kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũmũtethya.
Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ no asome na akaelewa ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata? o kwa kavinda kakuvĩ. Aendeee kũmanyĩw'a nũtonya kũsũngĩa makũlyo o nesa. O na nũtonya kwambĩĩa kũthi maũmbanonĩ na kumya maelesyo maseo. Maũndũ asu onthe nĩmatonya kwonany'a nũendeee kwĩka maendeeo ma kĩ-veva. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ kwasya kana nũkwatĩte ũĩ? Ti lasima ethĩwe akwatĩte ũĩ. No kwĩthĩwa mũndũ ũsu ekĩte kwĩthĩwa na ũtonyi wa kũkwatya maũndũ na mĩtũkĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla wambĩĩa kũatĩĩa ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ kwa kũtũmĩa nesa ũmanyi ũla ũkwatĩte vamwe na maũndũ ala ũeleetwe, no twasye yu nĩwambĩĩa kũkwata ũĩ. Na ĩndĩ ethĩwa motwi ala ũkwĩka me na mosyao maseo, kwonany'a kana nĩeeambĩte kũsũanĩa nesa, no twasye kana kũvika vau nĩwonanĩtye e na ũĩ mwĩanĩu.
Ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 7:24-27 nĩyĩeleetye ngelekany'o ĩla yanenganiwe nĩ Yesũ ya andũ elĩ meyakĩie kĩla mũndũ nyũmba yake. Ũmwe woo eĩtwe aĩ "mũĩ." Mũndũ ũsu nĩwambie kũsũanĩa kĩla kĩtonya kwĩsa kumĩla na kwoou aaka nyũmba yake ĩvianĩ. Nĩweene vaasa na nĩweesĩ atonya kwĩka ata akatetheka. Ndaasya eaka nyũmba yake kĩthangathĩnĩ nũndũ vau nĩvo ĩtekua ĩvinda ĩasa kũmyaka na ndĩlikya ngalama nene. Vandũ va ũu nĩwatũmĩie ũĩ asũanĩa kũkeethĩwa ata ĩvinda yũkĩte eeka ũndũ ũkwĩka. Kwoou ĩla kĩuutani kyesie kũka, nyũmba yake yatiiwe o ĩũngye. Yu ĩkũlyo nĩ, Tũtonya kwĩka ata twĩthĩwe na nguma ĩsu nzeo ya ũĩ mwĩanĩu, na tũtonya kũmĩsũvĩa ata?
NDONYA KWĨKA ATA NĨTHĨWE NA ŨĨ MWĨANĨU?
Mbee, kwasisya ĩandĩko ya Mika 6:9. Kwosana na Mbivilia ya New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩtye: "Ala me na ũĩ mwĩanĩu makakĩa ĩsyĩtwa [ya Ngai]." Kũkĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova kwonanasya kana nũmũnengete ndaĩa. Kũkĩa kũu nĩ kũnenga ndaĩa nene kĩla ĩsyĩtwa yĩu yĩũngamĩe vamwe na myolooto yake. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana ũnenge mũndũ ndaĩa nĩwaĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ asũanĩaa ata. Ĩtina wa ũu nĩwĩthĩawa ũtonya kũmũĩkĩĩa na kwĩmanyĩsya kuma kwake, na kũendeea nesa o ũndũ we ũendeeaa. Ethĩwa nĩtũsũanĩaa ũndũ meko maitũ matonya kwĩsa kũseũvya kana kwananga ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova, na ethĩwa nĩtwĩkaa motwi tũsũanĩĩte myolooto yake, no twasye kana nĩtũendeee kũkwata ũĩ mwĩanĩu.
Kelĩ, ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 18:1 yaĩtye: "Ũla wĩvathaa amanthaa kwenda kwake mwene, na alonzanĩlasya ũĩ w'onthe mwĩanĩu." Tũkaema kwĩsũvĩa no twĩse kwĩvatha na Yeova na andũ make. Na kwoou nĩ kana tũikevathe, nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩa ĩvinda na ala makĩaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai na manengae ndaĩa myolooto yake. Ethĩwa vai ũndũ ũũtũsiĩĩa, nĩtwaĩle kũendaa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ nĩ kana wĩthĩe tũinatĩĩa kwĩthĩwa vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ. Na ĩndĩ ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ nĩtwaĩle kũvingũa ilĩko sitũ na ngoo sitũ na tũyĩtĩkĩla kĩla kĩũmanyĩw'a kĩtũtethye.
Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana twamũtulũĩla Yeova ngoo sitũ ĩla tũũmũvoya, tũikalea kũmũthengeea mũnango. (Nth. 3:5, 6) Na eka ũu, twavingũa ilĩko sitũ na ngoo sitũ ĩla tũũsoma Mbivilia na mavuku ala tũnengawe nĩ ũseũvyo wa Yeova, nĩtũmanyaa meko maitũ matonya kwĩsa kũtũetee mosyao meva, na kwoou kĩu no kĩtũtethye twĩke ũla waĩle. O na ĩngĩ nĩtwaĩle kwĩtĩkĩlya ũtao ũla twanengwa nĩ ana-a-asa aima ũlike ngoonĩ. (Nth. 19:20) Tweeka ũu tũikethĩwa 'tũilonzanĩlya ũĩ w'onthe mwĩanĩu,' ĩndĩ tũkeethĩwa tũisũvĩa nguma ĩsu ya vata.
ŨĨ MWĨANĨU ŨTONYA KŨTETHYA MŨSYĨ WAKWA ATA?
Ũĩ mwĩanĩu nũtonya kũsũvĩa mĩsyĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia nĩtavĩtye kĩveti "nĩkĩmũkĩe" mũũme. (Aev. 5:33) Mũndũũme atonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana mũka amũkĩe, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, amũnenge ndaĩa nene? Akeyĩtĩsya ndaĩa ĩsu na vinya amĩnengwa o kwa kavinda kakuvĩ. Mũka wa mũndũ ta ũsu akamũnengae o ndaĩa ĩla wĩ vo nĩ kana maikatindĩe kũkita. Ĩndĩ we nũkwona ta ũkamũnengae ndaĩa ĩla ũte vo? No twasye ndakekaa ũu. Kwoou mũndũũme nĩwaĩle kũsũanĩa kĩla ũtonya kwĩka akanengawe ndaĩa mavinda onthe. Eethĩwa na nguma ta wendo na ũseo, ila nĩ ilungu sya ũsyao wa veva, mũka akamũnenga ndaĩa nene o na ateyĩtĩsye. Ĩndĩ o na vethĩwe vailyĩ ata, kĩveti nĩkyaĩle kũnenga mũũme ndaĩa, ethĩwe nĩwaĩlĩte kana ndaĩlĩte.—Aka. 5:22, 23.
Mbivilia nĩsyokete ĩkasya kana mũndũũme nĩwaĩle kwenda kĩveti kyake. (Aev. 5:28, 33) Ĩndĩ kĩveti kĩyenda kyendwe nĩ mũũme nĩkĩtonya kũsũanĩa kana nĩ kavaa kĩkamũvitha maũndũ amwe mate maseo o na kau nĩwaĩle kũmamanya. Ĩndĩ kĩveti kĩkwĩka ũu kĩ na ũĩ mwĩanĩu? Mũndũũme akesa kũmanya maũndũ ala mũka ũvithĩte vethĩwa vailyĩ ata? Nũmwenda mũno kwĩ ũndũ ũtwĩe amwendete? Ũsu ũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kwĩka. Vandũ va kĩveti kĩke ũu, nĩkyaĩle kũmantha ĩvinda ĩseo kĩelesye mũũme maũndũ asu mate maseo kĩuĩtye. Kyeeka ũu nĩvatonyeka mũũme akew'a endeew'a nĩkyo nũndũ kĩimũvithaa maũndũ. Kyu kĩkatuma mũũme enda kĩveti kyake mũnango.
Syana nĩsyaĩle kũmew'a asyai moo na syaĩle kũkanw'a kwosana na myolooto ya Yeova. (Aev. 6:1, 4) Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ kwasya kana kĩla asyai maĩle kwĩka nĩ kwĩkĩĩa syana syoo mĩao mingĩ? Mũsyai ndaĩle kwĩka o kũtavya mwana mĩao ya mũsyĩ ũsu tũ, kana ũndũ ũkwĩkwa aema kũmĩatĩĩa. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, mũsyai wĩ na ũĩ mwĩanĩu nũtetheeasya mwana wake aelewe nĩkĩ waĩle kwĩthĩwa e mwĩwi.
Kwa ngelekany'o, twasye mwana nĩwaneeny'a mũsyai naĩ. Kũmũkandĩa kana kũmũkũna vu kwa vu nĩkũtonya kũmwĩkĩĩthya nthoni kana kũkatuma ekũnza. Ĩndĩ mwana ũsu nũtonya kwoveea ũthatu ngoonĩ na kĩu kĩituma ambĩĩa kwĩvathana na asyai make.
Asyai ala mekũtata methĩwe na ũĩ mwĩanĩu nĩmambaa kũsũanĩa ũndũ meũkany'a syana syoo, na ũndũ ũkany'o ũsu ũtonya kũtuma syana isu syĩthĩwa iilyĩ ĩvinda yũkĩte. Asyai mayaĩle kwosa ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ aĩ nũndũ meĩw'a kĩko kya mwana woo kyamekĩĩthya nthoni. Ĩndĩ no mose mwana makamũtwaa vandũ ũtee, na maimũelesya o nesa kwa nzĩa ya wendo kana Yeova nĩwendaa syana syĩw'e asyai nĩ kana maũndũ masiendee nesa tene na tene. Ĩla mwana ũsu wesa kwonany'a nũnengete asyai make ndaĩa, akamanyaa kana emũtaĩa Yeova. (Aev. 6:2, 3) Mũsyai atũmĩa nzĩa ĩsu kũtetheesya mwana wake, mwana ũsu akeew'aa e mwĩanĩe. Akamanyaa kana asyai make nĩmamũthĩnĩkĩaa na kwoou akamanengae ndaĩa nenange. Veethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, mwana akeew'aa e na ũthasyo wa kũkũlya ũtethyo ĩla wakomana na maũndũ momũ.
Asyai amwe nĩmatonya kũlea kũlũnga mwana mayona meeka ũu nĩmeũtuma aũmĩa. Ĩndĩ malea kũlũnga mwana, eana ailyĩ ata? We akamũkĩa Yeova na akamanya kana kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Ngai nĩkw'o ũĩ? We akeethĩawa ayenda kũvingũa ngoo na kĩlĩko kyake amanyĩw'e nĩ Yeova, kana akeevatha aeke kũatĩanĩa na maũndũ ma kĩ-veva?—Nth. 13:1; 29:15.
Mũndũ ũla wĩsĩ kwasa mavisa nesa nũvangĩĩaa nesa kĩla ũkwenda kũseũvya. Ndasaa oou kĩtumbo na ayĩkwatya kĩla ũkwenda kũseũvya nĩkyo kĩkwasĩka. Asyai ala me ũĩ mwĩanĩu matũmĩaa ĩvinda yingĩ mayĩmanyĩsya na maitũmĩa myolooto ya Yeova. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu monanasya nĩmakĩaa ĩsyĩtwa yake. Kwoou kwa ũkuvĩ, ĩla asyai malea kwĩvathana na Yeova na ũseũvyo wake, nĩmameasya ũĩ mwĩanĩu na nĩmamanyaa ũndũ matonya kũũtũmĩa make mĩsyĩ yoo.
Kĩla mũthenya nĩtwĩkaa motwi matonya kũseũvya kana o kwananga thayũ witũ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ. Kwoou vandũ va kwĩka ũndũ na mĩtũkĩ, nũseo ũkamba kwosa ĩvinda ũsũanĩe. Sũanĩa nesa ũndũ ũsu ũtonya kwĩsa kũtuma maũndũ mekala ata ĩvinda yũkĩte. Voya Yeova aũtongoesye na ũitũmĩa ũĩ wake. Tweeka maũndũ asu, tũkeethĩwa tũisũvĩa ũĩ mwĩanĩu, naw'o ũkatũnenga thayũ.—Nth. 3:21, 22.

translation:
They say one day a certain child went to fetch water and found a beehive full of honey. People from his village were angry with the child because of the bees and they almost killed him. But luckily, he met some mistakes which helped him escape from the hands of those people. He collected flowers from various places. Some flowers were white and others red. And others were yellow and others brown, and when he reached the house of the old woman, she told him: "Because of this, you will go." The child took the flowers to the old woman and waited patiently.
One day an elder asked the child: "Is it possible to get the flower of the brown bee to the house of the white bee?" The child agreed and said, "Yes, it is possible." The elder then told him: "Then why did you take the flower of the white bee? Take the flower of the brown bee and bring it here!" So the child replied: "If I take the flower of the brown bee, people will be able to recognize my path and find me. Is it not better for me to take another flower, even from the white bee?" The child then spoke with a clear voice to the people present. That voice was very sweet.
The Bible says: "Taste and see that Jehovah is good; blessed is the man who takes refuge in him." (Ps. 34:8, 22) To understand "goodness," we need to know what it means to apply it to our lives. To help us appreciate it more, let's examine how "refuge" can be strengthened.
IS GOODNESS REALLY GOOD?
Being good involves acting kindly and having knowledge and understanding. A knowledgeable person can often do many things. But a person who understands things sees even one thing connected to another. Therefore, such a person is able to use his knowledge and also help others with matters he has understood well.
For example, someone who reads and understands the book "What Does the Bible Really Teach?" or similar books. He continues to learn and is not easily swayed by lies or falsehoods. And he is able to speak truthfully about matters and explain things clearly. Things like this enable him to continue progressing in spiritual growth. Is this not important or beneficial to you? It's certainly worthwhile to benefit from it. Being good means being able to grasp things with your mind. Therefore, speaking truthfully about what you have learned from the Bible using the knowledge you have gained, we encourage you to do so. And if there are other people who ask you questions and seek clarification, continue to help them until they understand things properly.
The account of Matthew 7:24-27 illustrates an example given by Jesus regarding people who claim to be disciples. One of them is called "wise." This person is encouraged to practice everything he learns to apply it diligently and build his house firmly. He believes he can do it and is confident he can accomplish anything. But when a flood comes and damages his house, it shows that the foundation was weak and could not withstand the pressure. Those people will regret not having built their foundations well enough. Building a strong foundation is essential, otherwise, the house may collapse. That is why we should strive to build our faith strongly, and should we not also work hard?
SHOULD WE STRIVE TO BUILD OUR FAITH STRONGLY?
Indeed, consider the account of Micah 6:9. The New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures renders this verse: "What does Jehovah ask of you except to practice justice?" Practicing justice toward Jehovah involves showing loyalty to him. To do so means to demonstrate great loyalty in all aspects of your life and in harmony with his principles. It means being loyal to someone even if they don't deserve it. The result of doing so is that you will find joy in pleasing him and proving yourself faithful, and you will continue to walk in what is right. Let us therefore practice doing what is right so that we may not fail to show appreciation for God's love and forgiveness, and let us remain united in practicing his principles, so that we may never turn away from him.
Furthermore, Psalm 18:1 states: "The one who is innocent will conduct himself blamelessly; happy is he who walks uprightly." We can prove our loyalty and walk with Jehovah and his people. And when we do so, we will be able to use our time and energy to promote God's name and to support his Kingdom faithfully. This is something truly worthwhile, and we will not fail to go to the Kingdom Hall and gladly associate with all fellow Christians. And while we are there, we will be able to share our experiences and encourage one another.
When we love Jehovah with all our heart, we will want to please him. (Prov. 3:5, 6) Also, as we read the Bible and publications that teach us about Jehovah's ways, we come to appreciate how much he cares for us, and this motivates us to live in harmony with his standards. So we will strive to apply what we learn. Moreover, we will benefit from the advice of experienced elders. (Prov. 19:20) Thus, we will continue "to conduct ourselves blamelessly," always striving to be loyal subjects of the King.
HOW CAN YOU MAKE YOUR LIFE COUNT?
Your life can count for so much. For example, the Bible does not forbid marriage. (Eph. 5:33) Can a Christian marry even if a former mate refuses to let him or her go, or for some other reason, the situation is difficult? Some have found it helpful to seek legal counsel. A wife may feel she has grounds for divorce if her husband mistreats her physically or emotionally. But should she get a divorce just because she is unhappy? Let us consider this. Sometimes a wife may feel she has no choice but to leave an abusive husband. However, each individual must decide for himself whether he or she has Scriptural grounds for divorce. It is important to remember that God values marriage and expects both mates to work at making it succeed. And even if a couple do divorce, it does not mean that they are automatically disfellowshipped.—Acts 5:22, 23.
The Bible also acknowledges that a Christian may choose to remain unmarried. (Eph. 5:28, 33) Is remaining unmarried the right course for you? If a person chooses to marry, he or she should be willing to put effort into making the marriage a success and be prepared to deal with challenges. Does remaining unmarried offer advantages? Can a Christian learn valuable lessons from being single? Should you pray about this decision and ask yourself, 'What will make me more effective in serving Jehovah?' You can then make a thoughtful decision. Those who choose to remain unmarried may find that they have more time and energy to devote to spiritual activities. This can help them to stay focused on their ministry. So, they may be able to accomplish more in their service.
However, Christians are encouraged to get married. Getting married and having children can bring great joy and satisfaction. (Eph. 6:1, 4) But does this mean that everyone should get married? Or is it wise to consider whether you are emotionally and spiritually ready for such a responsibility? A parent has a serious obligation to train his or her children properly. Therefore, parents need to carefully consider whether they can provide a stable home environment for their children.
For example, we might encourage our child to become independent. Constantly correcting or criticizing him could discourage him or cause him to resent us. If a young person feels pressured, he may struggle to maintain a close relationship with his parents.
Parents who are overly protective can hinder their children's development, and this can lead to problems later in life. Some parents may be tempted to shield their children from difficult experiences, but doing so can prevent them from learning valuable lessons. It is important to remember that Jehovah loves obedient children, and He wants what is best for them. (Eph. 6:2, 3) When parents take time to reason with their children, those children are more likely to mature emotionally. They will realize that their parents care about them and want what is best for them. With this understanding, children are more likely to accept discipline and cooperate willingly.
Some parents may find it difficult to allow their children to make mistakes, believing they know what is best. But should parents always intervene, even when their children are capable of making their own decisions? Will such intervention help them to trust in Jehovah and appreciate that honoring God's laws is vital? Or will it cause them to resent restrictions and rebel against authority?—Prov. 13:1; 29:15.
A wise parent knows when to offer guidance and when to allow his child to learn through experience. Often, allowing a child to face the consequences of his actions is the most effective teacher. Parents who are overly involved may inadvertently undermine their children's efforts to imitate Jehovah. By doing so, they may miss an opportunity to see their children demonstrate faith. However, if parents maintain a close relationship with Jehovah and seek his direction, they can be confident that they are providing the best possible upbringing for their children.
Each of us at times may struggle to accept discipline or feel unjustly treated because of past experiences. But remember that time and circumstances can change. It is important to recognize that our reactions may not always be reasonable. Consider how easily we might become discouraged if things did not work out as planned. Trust that Jehovah will direct your steps and use his wisdom. Let us examine ourselves, strive to remain humble, and avoid becoming bitter.—Prov. 3:21, 22.

text:
Ve mũthenya namandĩkĩte vandũ isasi ikwetye kũvĩtĩla ĩũlũ wa mũtwe wakwa. Kĩtuu kĩu kĩendeee nookĩlilye katambala keũ kavola. Asikalĩ ala matwĩkasya isasi isu makona mandonzeile mambĩĩte nume vau neevithĩte. Nookĩlile nathi vala maĩ nĩsũvĩĩte ndesĩ kana nĩmeũmbũaa kana nĩmeũndeka. Ĩndĩ neeyĩthĩie thĩnanĩ ũsu ata?
NASYAĨWE ndũanĩ nini yĩ nthĩ ya Greece yĩtawa Karítsa. Kwitũ tũsyaĩtwe twĩ nyanya na asyai makwa maĩ andũ me kĩthito mũno. Ninyie wa mũonza kwitũ na nasyaiwe mwaka wa 1926.
Mwaka ũmwe ndanamba kũsyawa, asyai makwa nĩmakomanie na John Papparizos. Ũsu aĩ ũmwe wa Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia na aĩ mũndũ mũneenu na wĩ kĩthito mũno. Ĩvinda yĩu Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyo syeetawa Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia. Asyai makwa nĩmendeeiw'e mũno nĩ kwona ũndũ John wamaeleasya Maandĩko nesa, na kwoou nĩmambĩĩe kũendaa maũmbanonĩ ma Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia o vau ndũanĩ. Mami nĩwamũĩkĩĩie Yeova Ngai mũno, na o na kau ndeesĩ kũsoma, akwata mwanya mũseo nĩwatavasya angĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo ũsu wake. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana Tata nĩwaekie mavĩtyo ma ala angĩ mamũlulutĩkye, na kwoou nĩwakolile maũmbano.
Nyie nĩ na ala tũsyaanĩw'e nĩtwanengete Mbivilia ndaĩa, ĩndĩ twĩ anini tũyaaĩka maendeeo nũndũ twaĩ kolokolo mwingĩ. Ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1939, ĩvinda yĩla Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe wambĩĩe Europe, ve ũndũ weekĩkie vau ndũanĩ watũsaanĩsya. Ve mwanake ũmwe wa mũsyĩ witũ weetawa Nicolas Psarras weetiwe alike itanĩ sya Greece. Nicolas aĩ mũtũi na aĩ anavatisiwe o mĩtũkĩ. Ĩndĩ o na kau aĩ na myaka 20, atavisye anene ma ita ndeto ii ateũkĩa kĩndũ: "Nditonya kũkita nũndũ nĩ mũsikalĩ wa Klĩsto." Asilĩilwe nĩ koti wa ita na atw'ĩĩwa kyovo kya myaka ĩkũmi. Twatelemile mũno!
Ĩndĩ ũseo nĩ kana mwakanĩ wa 1941 ita sya Britain na asikalĩ ala angĩ maĩ ngwatanĩo nasyo nĩsyalikile Greece kwa kavinda, na kwoou Nicolas nĩwathaiw'e. Athaw'a nĩwasyokie ndũanĩ ya Karítsa. Avika mwanake mũkũũa wĩtawa Ilias nĩwamũkũlilye makũlyo maingĩ mũno ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia. Neethukĩĩsye ngewa ĩsu yoo nesa mũno. Ĩtina Ilias, nakwa, na kamwĩlĩtu kalumaita ketawa Efmorfia nĩtwambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kũendaa maũmbanonĩ ma Ngũsĩ tũteũtĩĩa. Mwaka ũla waatĩĩe, twĩ atatũ nĩtweeyumisye tũmũthũkũme Yeova na twavatiswa. Na tũendeangĩe oou, angĩ ana tũsyaanĩw'e nĩmatw'ĩkie Ngũsĩ ndĩkĩĩku.
Mwakanĩ wa 1942 Kĩkundi kya Karítsa kyaĩ na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma mũika kenda, ala maĩ na myaka katĩ wa 15 na 25. Ithyonthe nĩtweesĩ kana nĩtweteelwe nĩ matatwa momũ mũno. Kwoou nĩ kana twĩyĩkĩe vinya, nĩtwakomanaa kĩla ĩvinda vatonyeka tũkemanyĩsya Mbivilia, tũkaina mbathi sya Ũsumbĩ, na tũkavoya. Kĩu kyalũlũmĩlye mũĩkĩĩo witũ mũno.
KAŨ WA ENE KWA ENE
Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe ũkilyĩ kũthela ala ma kyama kya communist nĩmaleanile na silikalĩ ya Greece, na kyu kyatuma kũkĩla kaũ mũthũku wa ene kwa ene nthĩ ĩsu. Ala mokitĩaa kyama kĩu mangangaa ndũanĩ mailasimĩthya andũ malikane namo. Mavika ndũanĩ yitũ nĩmatavie Ngũsĩ itatũ sya mũika. Asu mataviwe maĩ Antonio Tsoukaris, Ilias, nakwa. Twatatie kũmesũva tũimea ithyĩ twĩ Aklĩsto na tũilikaa siasanĩ na kaũnĩ, ĩndĩ matũlasimĩthisye tũthi na maaũ nginya Kĩĩma kya Olympus, kĩla kĩ mũendo wa masaa 12 kuma ndũanĩ yitũ.
Vatavĩtĩte ĩvinda ĩasa, mũnene ũmwe wa kyama kya communist atwĩie twosane na asu maendaa maitava andũ ndũanĩ tũthi tũkalasimĩthye andũ angĩ malike kyamanĩ. Ĩla twamũeleisye kana Aklĩsto mayoseaa ala angĩ mĩio ya kaũ, athatie mũno na atũtwaa mbee wa mũnene wake. Twatavisye mũnene ũsu o ũndũ twatavĩtye ũla ũngĩ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ mũnene ũsu wake watwĩie: "Osai nyũmbũ ĩndĩ mũkakue ala maũmĩĩie kaũnĩ mũmatwae sivitalĩ."
Twamũkũlilye: "Nao nata tũkakwatwa nĩ asikalĩ ma silikalĩ? Mayona o naitũ ta twĩ o kaũnĩ ũũ?" Asyokie atwĩa: "Ĩndĩ twaĩai ala me kaũnĩ mĩkate." Naitũ twasũanĩa twamũkũlya: "Ko tũtoneka nĩ mũnene o ũngĩ twĩ na nyũmbũ ĩsu na aitwĩa nĩtwose mĩio ya kaũ tũtwaĩe ala me kaũnĩ?" Nĩvo ĩndĩ mũnene ũsu woo watatie kũthiũũkya mũtwe. Ĩtina esie kwasya ũũ e mũsaanĩsye: "Ethĩwa nũu, mũikambĩe ĩndĩ mũitonya kũĩthya malondu! Ĩkalai vaa kĩĩmanĩ mũĩthye malondu."
Twasũanĩie twoona mawasya maitũ ma ngoo no matwĩtĩkĩlye tũĩthye malondu, ala angĩ maendeee kũkita. Ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe, Ilias, ũla nĩwe mũkũũ vyũ kwitũ, nĩweetĩkĩlilw'e kwĩnũka akasũvĩe Mami ĩtina wa Tata kũkw'a. Nake Antonio nĩwawaie na eewa no enũke. Nyie no inyie ndaalekw'a.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu nasyo ita sya silikalĩ ya Greece syaendeee kũthengeea alei asu ma kyama kya communist. Kĩkundi kĩla kyambosete nĩkyavangie kũsembela iĩmanĩ kyelekele nthĩ ya Albania. Twĩ vakuvĩ na mũvaka twesie kwĩyĩthĩĩla tũthyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ asikalĩ ma Greece. Alei asu matelemile na masemba. Nakwa namandĩkie ĩtina wa mũtĩ wavalũkĩte, na vau nĩvo vaĩ kĩla kĩtuu nĩwetie mwambĩĩonĩ.
Ĩla natavisye asikalĩ asu ma Greece kana neekĩte kũtavwa nĩ alei asu ma communist, mandwaie kambinĩ ya ita ngakũlw'e makũlyo. Kambi ĩsu yaĩ vakuvĩ na vandũ vetawa Véroia, vala nĩvo Mbivilianĩ vetĩtwe Velia. Kũu kambinĩ ĩsu neeiwe nĩthi ngenze mĩtaũ ĩla yatũmĩawa nĩ asikalĩ me kaũnĩ. Ĩla naleile, mũnene ũla wanengete mwĩao ũsu aisye nĩnĩtwawe kathamanĩ ka Makrónisos (Makronisi). Kathama kau kakĩĩtwe mũno nũndũ ala matwawa vo maendaa kũthĩnw'a mũno.
KATHAMA KA THĨNA
Kathama ka Makrónisos ke kĩsionĩ kya Attica kĩla kĩ ũtee wa ũkanga, ũasa wa maili ta 30 (kĩlomita 50) kuma taoni ya Athens. Kathama kau ti kanake, na nĩ komũ, kai kĩw'ũ, na no ta ka ĩvia ĩthei. Ke ũasa wa maili nyanya (kĩlomita 13), na vala vathanthau vyũ nĩ va mita 500. Ĩndĩ kuma mwakanĩ wa 1947 nginya 1958, vau kathamanĩ kau vathĩnĩiw'e andũ mbee wa 100,000. Asu maĩ ala mokitĩaa kyama kya communist kana ala moonekaa ta ma kyama kĩu. Na angĩ nĩ ala tene mokitĩaa ũthasyo, na Ngũsĩ mbingĩ mũno sya Yeova.
Natwaiwe kũu mwaka wa 1949 ũyambĩĩa na neethĩa avungwa mavangĩtwe kambi iana ũna. Kambi ĩla natwaiwe ndyasungawa mũno na yaĩ na andũ angĩ maana meana ũna. Twakomaa ĩeemanĩ ya kyandalũa twĩ ta 40 o na kau yaseũvĩw'e andũ 10. Twanyusaa kĩw'ũ kyou, na mũno mũno twaĩsaa ndengũ na makondu. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kyatũthĩnasya mũno nĩ kĩtoo kĩtathelaa na iseve itathelaa. Ĩndĩ twaĩ kavaa nũndũ ithyĩ tũyakũnĩthaw'a wĩa wa kũtinda tũtetengete mavia. Avungwa aingĩ makũnĩthaw'a wĩa ũsu nĩ kana mathĩnw'e, na nĩwamaũmĩasya mĩĩ na ũkamathokoany'a ilĩko.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩsĩlĩte ũtee wa ũkanga nĩnakomanie na Ngũsĩ ingĩ kuma kambinĩ ingĩ. Twatanie ta kĩ ĩla twakomanie! Nĩtwambĩĩe kũmbana ĩla vatonyeka twĩsũvĩĩte mũno tũikoneke. O na nĩtwatũmĩaa ũĩ mũno kũtavya avungwa ala angĩ ũvoo mũseo, na amwe moo nĩmesie kũtw'ĩka Ngũsĩ. Maũndũ asu vamwe na mboya nĩmatũtetheeisye mũno twaendeea nesa kĩ-veva.
KŨNYAMAW'A MŨNO
Nathĩnĩiw'e kũu myei ĩkũmi nĩ kana noneke kana nĩnĩvĩndũa kĩlĩko, na ĩndĩ vatw'ĩka yu nĩnaĩle kwĩkĩa ngũa sya kaũ. Ĩla naleile, nakusũlanilw'e natwawa mbee wa mũnene wa kambi. Namũnengie kathangũ naandĩkĩte: "Nĩenda o kũtw'ĩka mũsikalĩ wa Klĩsto." Ambie kũndelemya, na ĩndĩ anengeleelya ũla wamũatĩĩe ũnenenĩ. Ũsu aĩ mũtongoi wa Greek Orthodox, na eekĩĩte ngũa ila syĩkĩawa nĩ atongoi ma makanisa asu. Ĩla namũsũngĩie makũlyo make ndeũkĩa nĩtũmĩĩte Maandĩko, aisye ũũ e mũthatu mũno: "Mũvetangei vaa. Ũũ nĩ mũndũ wa makinda!"
Ũnĩ wake asikalĩ nĩmambĩie ĩngĩ nĩnĩkĩe ngũa sya kaũ. Ĩla naleile mandumangilye na mangũna na thimbũ. Kuma vau mandwaie vala vaiitĩawa ala aũmĩu nĩ kenda masisye kana nĩnatũlĩkanga mavĩndĩ. Ĩla meethĩie ndinatũlĩkanga mangusũlanilye mandũnga ĩeemanĩ yakwa. Nathĩniw'e ũu kĩla mũthenya vandũ va myei ĩlĩ.
Nũndũ nĩnaleile vyũ kũkaĩa mũĩkĩĩo wakwa, asikalĩ asu nĩmavangie kũtũmĩa nzĩa ĩngĩ nĩ woo ũla meew'ĩte. Mambovanisye moko mũongonĩ na ĩndĩ mangũna nyaaĩ na makanda mateũmbĩw'ĩa tei. Saanĩ ũsu neew'ĩte woo mwingĩ mũno ĩndĩ nĩnalilikanile ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Mwĩ aathime inyw'ĩ yĩla andũ meũmũkava, na kũmũthĩn'ya . . . Tanai, na ĩthĩwai na mũyo mũnene: nĩkwĩthĩwa ĩtuvi yenyu nĩ ĩnene ĩtunĩ: nũndũ ũu nĩw'o mathĩnisye athani ala maĩ mbee wenyu." (Mt. 5:11, 12) Nakũniwe navika vandũ navalũka na naeka kwĩyĩw'a.
Ndyũkĩla neeyĩthĩie kasũmbanĩ kanini ke mbevo ki nde na kĩndũ nĩya, nde na kĩw'ũ, kana ĩvula. O na vailyĩ ũu, ndyaavũvũana. O tondũ Mbivilia yathanĩte, "mũuo wa Ngai" nĩw'o 'wasũvĩie ngoo yakwa na mosũanĩo makwa.' (Avi. 4:7) Ũnĩ wake mũsikalĩ ũmwe waĩ mũseo anengie mũkate na kĩw'ũ na kavuti. Na ĩndĩ ũngĩ anenga lĩu wake. Maũndũ asu maseo na angĩ noonie nĩmambĩkĩĩthisye kana Yeova nĩwanzũvĩaa.
Anene ala maĩ vau moonie nĩ mũndũ mũthũku mũno ũtavĩndũka, na kwoou mandwaa Athens ngasilĩlwe kotinĩ wa ita. Koti ũsu wandw'ĩĩe kyovo kya myaka ĩtatũ yelanĩ yĩmwe yaĩ kĩthamanĩ kya Yíaros (Gyaros). Kĩthama kĩu kĩ ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa sua ta maili 30 (kĩlomita 50) kuma Makrónisos.
"NĨTŨMŨĨKĨĨE"
Yela ya Yíaros yaĩ nene mũno na yaakĩtwe na mavali matune, na yaĩ na avungwa mbee wa 5,000 moovetwe nũndũ wa maũndũ ma siasa. Vau vaĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mũonza, na syonthe syoovetwe nũndũ wa kũlea kũlika siasanĩ na kaũnĩ. Twoombanaa twĩvithĩte twĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia o na kau ũndũ ũsu waĩ mũvatane vyũ. O na nĩtwaeteawa makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na kĩmbithĩ kĩla ĩvinda na ĩndĩ tũimaumĩĩsya na kw'oko nĩ kana tũmatũmĩe kwĩmanyĩsya.
Mũthenya ũmwe tũmbanĩte mũsikalĩ ũmwe nĩwatũkitisye na atũvena mavuku ala twakwete. Nĩvo ĩndĩ tweetiwe nĩ mũnini wa mũnene wa yela ĩsu. Twaendie vo twĩsĩ kyovo kitũ kĩĩka kwongelangwa, ĩndĩ mũnini ũsu atwĩie: "Nĩtwĩsĩ ninyw'e aaũ, na nĩtũnengete ndaĩa mawoni menyu. Nĩtũmũĩkĩĩe. Syokai wĩanĩ." O na nĩwaolangĩĩle amwe maitũ mawĩa. Twamũtũngĩie Yeova mũvea mũno. Nĩtwoonie kana kwĩkala twĩ Aklĩsto aĩkĩĩku o na twĩ o kũu yela nĩkwatumie Yeova ataĩwa.
Ũĩkĩĩku witũ nĩwaetie maũndũ angĩ maseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũvungwa ũmwe waĩ vulovesa wa ĩsavu ekalile o atũsyaĩĩsye na ĩla woonie mwĩkalĩle witũ mũseo ambĩĩa kũtũkũlya ĩũlũ wa kĩla tũĩkĩĩaa. Ĩla ithyĩ Ngũsĩ twalekilw'e mwambĩĩonĩ wa mwaka wa 1951, o nake nĩwalekilw'e. Mũthya nĩwesie kũvatiswa na alika ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe.
O NA ŨMŨNTHĨ NĨ MŨSIKALĨ
Nyie nalekw'a nasyokie Karítsa kũla kwĩ andũ maitũ. Ĩtina nĩ na andũ angĩ aingĩ ma nthĩ yitũ nĩnathamĩĩie Melbourne, Australia. Nĩ kũu nĩnakomanie na mwĩĩtu-a-asa mũseo wĩtawa Janette na twatwaana. Twasyaie kamwana na twĩlĩtu tũtatũ na twamaea nesa ta Aklĩsto.
Ũmũnthĩ ũũ nĩnĩvĩtũkĩtye myaka 90, ĩndĩ nĩ o mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. O na vailyĩ ũu, nũndũ wa ũndũ naũmĩiw'e tene, nĩnalaw'a nĩ mwĩĩ na maaũ mavinda kwa mavinda, na mũno mũno ĩla nathi ũtavany'a. Ĩndĩ nĩthĩawa nĩtw'ĩte vyũ kwĩkala nĩ 'mũsikalĩ wa Klĩsto.'—2 Tim. 2:3.
