translation:
In the evening I wrote letters to people below to explain about my head. This thing continues because it has become a habit to steal. They don't care how much pain they cause me and they don't understand. Because I have closed my eyes I see nothing whether I am dreaming or I am awake. Is there anyone who will help me at all?
BY THE WAY, my mother's name is Karítsa from Greece. We used to play with our grandmother and her children would come with water to those who were working hard. You came to us and by the way in the year 1926.
One year later I wanted to learn, her children were bothered by John Papparizos. He was one of the Witnesses of the Bible and he was a good person to those who were working hard. The book "The Kingdom of God" is what they call the Witnesses of the Bible. Her children liked it very much when John explained the Scriptures well, and then they encouraged me to go to meetings of the Witnesses of the Bible with them. I thanked Jehovah this good God, and even though I didn't know how to read, he gave me time to learn and showed me his kingdom. It is a matter of remembering that Father gave others gifts so that they could be released, and then I attended meetings.
We also learned together to study the Bible diligently, because we always found something new when we studied a lot. In 1939, during World War II which covered Europe, things became difficult for our brothers. One brother from our congregation named Nicolas Psarras was imprisoned in Greece. Nicolas was young and had no children. But when he was 20 years old, he courageously spoke about the truth and said: "I want to become a Christian minister." He was sentenced to eight years in prison and spent ten years in exile. We remember him fondly!
In the meantime, in 1941, while Britain and its allies were fighting, Greece was invaded again, and Nicholas was arrested. They took him to the island of Karítsa. There his older brother Ilias helped him escape many times during the war. I am grateful for this help. After Ilias, my mother and her sister Efmorfia helped us to hide in the mountains and go to different villages to preach. That year, we three dedicated ourselves to Jehovah and were baptized. And we continued to work hard, so that we could always praise God.
In 1942, the group on Karítsa consisted of young men and women, some between the ages of 15 and 25. All of us felt that we were supported by this unity. Often we would meet secretly, and every day we would try to preach the Bible, sing songs of worship, and pray. This strengthened our faith.
WORLD WAR II
The war in northern Greece intensified as the communists gained control, which led to increased hardship for everyone. But despite this difficulty, the people continued to support those who preached the good news. We also received help from brothers like Antonio Tsoukaris, Ilias, and my mother. We decided to climb Mount Olympus, a journey of about 12 hours, to reach our friends.
One day, a leader of the communist party summoned us and asked us to help them transport weapons to other areas. However, we refused to cooperate with the communists. Instead, we told him that Christians do not take sides in politics, and he sent us away with his superior. We thanked this man because he let us go that time. He said to us: "Go home and stop bothering me with such things."
We wondered: "Will we be arrested by the police or soldiers? Is there any way we can escape?" He replied: "I will give you some advice." Then we asked: "Can we leave with this man and tell others about our experience so they too can avoid trouble?" This man then began to think deeply. His final words were: "Listen carefully, and remember what I am telling you! Go quickly and don't get caught!"
We agreed to follow his advice and left, while they continued their work. After a year, Ilias, who was older than us, decided to visit his aunt in Athens. Antonio and I stayed behind and waited. And now, goodbye to all of you.
The Greek military government continued to persecute those suspected of being communists. Every organization was forced to denounce its beliefs in favor of Albania. We and our families had to hide among the people of Greece. Those people were kind and hospitable. But I remembered my father's words, and they were always true.
But I feared that the Greek authorities would discover me and hand me over to the communists, so I joined a group heading towards Macedonia. Our camp was located near Veroia, which we called Mbiviliani, also known as Velia. In that camp, we lived under difficult conditions, similar to those imposed by the authorities. But eventually, the man who led us said he would take us to the island of Makrónisos (Makronisi). That island was terrible, full of suffering, but we had no choice.
ISLAND OF PAIN
The island of Makrónisos is part of Attica, about 30 miles (50 kilometers) from Athens. The island is barren, rocky, dry, and has no vegetation. It is 13 nautical miles long, and its bays are only 500 meters wide. Between 1947 and 1958, approximately 100,000 people were imprisoned on that island. These included those accused of supporting communism or those merely suspected of doing so. And others who did not support anything, and many sincerely worshipped Jehovah God.
I arrived there in 1949, initially assigned to a separate camp. This camp was very crowded and contained many different people. We slept on the ground in groups of 40 or more, and ten guards watched over us. We suffered greatly from the heat, and we were constantly bitten by insects and scorpions. Another thing that tormented us was the constant thirst and lack of food. We often went days without eating, hoping to find something to eat. Many prisoners tried to escape, but most were caught and severely punished.
One day, while working in the fields, I met another brother in a different camp. What a joy it was to meet him! We encouraged each other, knowing that we could endure. We also used this opportunity to help other prisoners, and some were moved to learn about God. Many things happened, including beatings, but we persevered and continued to preach the good news.
We realized how important it was to stay close to God and continue our ministry. We rejoiced when we saw others respond positively to the truth.
REMEMBERING IT WELL
I was imprisoned there for almost ten years, and sometimes I wondered if I would ever be released. But I remained steadfast, and eventually, I was appointed as an elder in the camp. I wrote a letter stating: "I want to serve as a minister of Christ." He responded favorably, and then he promoted me to a higher position. He was a Greek Orthodox priest, and he allowed us to hold meetings in his church along with other churches. However, I continued to rely on the Scriptures, always remembering this verse: "Be courageous! For I am with you!"
The life of a minister often brings challenges, and sometimes I felt discouraged. But I remembered my experiences with my parents and my upbringing. Sometimes people treated us badly, but we continued to forgive them. I believed that through prayer, I could overcome any obstacle. I remembered that every day, many people face similar trials.
I also realized that I needed to focus on my own spiritual growth, and other believers helped me to find new ways to serve. I shared stories with two friends, and they listened attentively. It's wonderful to know that so much power comes from Jesus' words: "Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Rejoice and be glad, for great is your reward in heaven; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you." (Matt. 5:11, 12) And I learned to love those who mistreated me and pray for their salvation.
Like a sheep, I was vulnerable to predators and dangers, such as wolves or jackals. But despite this, I persevered. As the Bible states, "the God of love" wants us to "love one another wholeheartedly." (1 John 4:7) The life of a dedicated servant involves facing difficulties and enduring hardships. And some may lose their lives. Many things happen that test whether Jehovah truly cares about us.
Some people believe that there is no righteous God who intervenes in human affairs, and they point to the example of Athens, which was once considered a center of learning. That city experienced three years of plague during the time of Pericles (Gyáros). This island is located about 30 miles (50 kilometers) from Makrónisos.
"LET US REASON TOGETHER"
The island of Gyáros was desolate and inhabited by criminals, and it housed over 5,000 political prisoners. They were Jehovah's Witnesses, and they were imprisoned because of their faith and refusal to compromise. We humbly request that you examine the Bible and consider this situation carefully. And we encourage you to seek out recordings of Christian testimonies and to meditate on them so that you can be convinced.
On one occasion, we spoke with a guard who was moved by our courage. This was how he described the warden of the prison. We asked him what would happen if we tried to escape, and he replied: "I will let you go, and I will close my eyes to your departure. Let us reason together. Just don't cause trouble." And he allowed some of us to leave. We thanked Jehovah deeply. We realized that being true Christians and remaining loyal to Jehovah could save our lives.
Our organization has experienced many challenges. For example, one prisoner, a former thief, began to harass us and threatened to make our life miserable unless we gave him food every day. But thankfully, the Watchtower Society helped us in 1951, and he stopped bothering us. He also regretted his actions throughout the rest of his life.
AND THE GUARD WAS KIND
I left my homeland to visit relatives in various countries. It happened that many others from my family had emigrated to Melbourne, Australia. There I met a wonderful woman named Janette, and we married. We had a child and raised three children as Christians.
This man turned 90 years old, and he served as an elder in the congregation. And despite his age and the hardships he endured, he continued to serve faithfully, going from house to house. He felt honored to be called a 'minister of Christ.'—2 Tim. 2:3.

text:
MWĨĨTU ũmwe mũinawa wĩtawa Araceli andavisye ũũ na wasya mũnene: "Eka kũneeny'a. Ndienda kwĩw'a ũndũ ũngĩ ĩũlũ wa ndĩni ĩsu yaku. Ĩtumaa nĩw'a ngoo. Nĩngũmenete!" Ũmũnthĩ ũũ nĩ na myaka 91, ĩndĩ ndyaaũlwa nĩ woo ũla neewie ĩla nataviw'e ndeto isu. No ve ũndũ ũmwe ũwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mũtavan'ya 7:8, yĩla yaĩtye "mũminũkĩlyo wa ũndũ nĩ kavaa kwĩ wambĩlĩlyo." Ũu nĩw'o vesie kũthi.—Felisa.
Felisa: Kwitũ twaĩ andũ ma ndĩni mũno. Ve andũ 13 ma mũsyĩ witũ mathũkũmaa kanisa wa Katholeki, amwe moo me athembi. O na ve mũndũ wa mũsyĩ wa Mami waĩ mũthembi na mwalimũ wa sukulu ya Katholeki, ũla watw'ĩkĩthiw'e nĩ Pope John Paul II ũmwe wa ala aathime maĩle kwĩsa kũtw'ĩka "atheu." Ĩndĩ ithyĩ tũyaĩ athwii. Tata atuaa syũma nake Mami aĩ mũĩmi. Tũsyaĩtwe twĩ nyanya, na ninyie mũkũũ.
Nĩ na myaka 12 kaũ wa ene kwa ene nĩwambĩĩe nthĩ yitũ ya Spain. Kaũ ũsu wathela ĩthe wakwa nĩwooviwe yela. Nũndũ silikalĩ nĩyekalĩle andũ mũno, Tata okitĩaa ũthasyo wa andũ na kĩu nĩkyo kyamĩthatisye. Ĩtina wa vau Mami athĩnaa mũno aitũmanthĩa lĩu, na kwoou mũndũ mũka ũmwe maĩ ndũũ amwĩie natwae eĩtu atatũ ainawa taoninĩ ya Bilbao, Spain, nĩ kana makekalae vala aka ala meyumĩsye ndĩni ya Katholeki (nuns) mekalaa. Ainawa asu nĩ Araceli, Lauri, na Ramoni. Eka maũndũ aangĩ, kũu mayaĩ makoma na nzaa.
Araceli: Tũitwawa kũu ũmwe witũ aĩ na myaka 14, ũũngĩ myaka 12, na ũla ũngĩ myaka 10, na kwoou tweewie wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kũtiana na andũ ma mũsyĩ. Kũu Bilbao wĩa witũ waĩ kũthesya. Twekalile kũu myaka ĩlĩ na ĩndĩ twathamĩĩw'a mũsyĩ ũngĩ mũnenange wa nuns, ũla waĩ taoninĩ ya Zaragoza. Vau navo vasũvĩĩawa ala akũũ. Twanengiwe wĩa wa kũthesya ikonĩ, na wĩa ũsu waĩ mĩnoo mũno kwitũ nũndũ twaĩ o twĩlĩtu twa myaka ĩkũmi na kĩndũ.
Felisa: Ĩla eĩtu asu twasyaanĩw'e maendie Zaragoza, inyia wakwa na mũinae wake, ũla waĩ mũthembi kanisanĩ wa kwitũ, nĩmavangie nĩtwawe o kũu ainawa matwaiwe ngathũkũmae kw'o. Meekie ũu nũndũ moonaa nathi kũu nĩmeũndaanany'a na kamwana ka vau ũtũinĩ kambendaa. Ĩndĩ nũndũ naĩ wa kanisa mũno, nĩneewie mũyo ĩla neeiwe nĩngũthi ngekalange vala nuns mekalaa. Vai mũthenya natĩĩaa Misa, na nĩnasũanĩĩte kũtw'ĩka misonalĩ ta mwana-a-mwendya ũmwe waĩ misonalĩ Africa.
Ndyaatetheew'a nĩ nuns asu neethĩie kũu nĩanĩsye wendi wakwa wa kũthamĩĩa mũingo nĩmũthũkũme Ngai, o na nĩ kũu neew'aa ta nĩ mwove. Kwoou nĩnatwie kwĩnũka ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe ngasũvĩe ũla mũinae wa Mami waĩ mũthembi. Natethasya wĩa wa nyũmba, na kĩla wĩoo nĩnavoyaa ila mboya sya Ndasivii nĩ nake. O na nĩnendete kũvanga malaa ma kanisa na kwanakavya ĩvisa ya Meli na mavisa ala angĩ ma "atheu."
Araceli: Ĩtina wa ĩvinda maũndũ nĩmavĩndũkie vau twekalaa. Ĩla twĩ atatũ twaĩe kĩavo kya mbee kya kũtw'ĩka nuns, nĩtwataananiw'e. Ramoni atiiwe Zaragoza, Lauri atwawa Valencia, nakwa natwawa Madrid, na navika vau nĩw'o naĩe kĩavo kya kelĩ. Vala natwaiwe Madrid nĩvo vaĩ ũkomo wa amanyĩw'a, andũ ala akũũ, na aeni angĩ, na kwoou veethĩawa wĩa mwingĩ mũno. Nathũkũmaa sivitalĩnĩ ũla waĩ vau nthĩnĩ.
Kũneena ũla w'o ũndũ neethĩie kũu kũilyĩ ti w'o neesĩ. Neesĩ ngasomaa Mbivilia na ngĩmĩelewa nesa. Ĩndĩ vai mũndũ waneenaa ĩũlũ wa Ngai kana Yesũ, o na tũyasomaa Mbivilia. Twamanyĩaw'a Kĩlatinĩ vanini, tũkasoma ĩũlũ wa "atheu," na tũkathaitha Meli. Mbee wa ũu no wĩa mũmũ twatethasya.
Tũendeangĩe nĩnambĩĩe kwĩw'a ndithĩnĩka na kwoou nĩnaendie kũneena na nun ũla watũũngamĩe. Namwĩie kana noonaa vate vata nĩthũkũmae mũno wĩana ũu ngĩseũvĩsya andũ mbesa na now'o kwitũ kwĩ na maũndũ maingĩ ndonya kũtetheesya. Namũtavya ambingĩie kasũmbanĩ kanini ayĩkwatya kana kwĩka ũu nĩkũũtuma nosa mũtwe ũngĩ na kũimbĩkĩa wia wa kuma vau.
Nĩnavingũĩwe katatũ, ĩndĩ mambingũĩaa mayenda kwona ethĩwa no ngwenda kuma vau. Nũndũ nĩmoonie ndikwenda kũvĩndũa ũtwi wakwa, mambĩie nĩnĩandĩke valũa wĩ na ndeto ii: "Nĩuma vaa nũndũ nĩenda kũmũthũkũma Satani vandũ va Ngai." Kyu mambĩie nĩnĩandĩke kyandelemilye mũno, ĩndĩ o na kau neew'aa ndyenda kuma vau mũno, ndyaĩ nĩsa kũandĩka ndeto ta isu. Nakũlilye nĩtĩkĩlw'e kwona mũthembi nĩ kana numbũle, na kwoou ĩla namwonie nĩnamũtavisye kĩla kyaendeee. Nĩweetisye bishop mwanya wa kũnthamya vau andũnge Zaragoza. Nekalile Zaragoza myei mĩnini na neetĩkĩlw'a kũthi. Kavinda kanini ĩtina wa ũu o nake Lauri na Ramoni nĩmeetĩkĩlilw'e maume vala maĩ.
ĨVUKU YĨLA YATŨAANISYE
Felisa: Nĩnesie kũtwawa na twathamĩĩa Cantabria. No naendeeie kũthi Misa ndeũtĩĩa. Na kwoou Wakyumwa ũmwe neewie mũthembi atangaasa kĩndũ e mathivaũnĩ anzengy'a. Aisye ũũ e mũthatu: "Nĩmwene ĩvuku yĩĩ?" Atwonisye ĩvuku W'o Ũla Ũtongoasya kwa Thayũ Ũtathela. Aendeeie kwasya, "Ethĩwa ve mũndũ ũnakũnengie ĩvuku yĩĩ, mbetee yo kana ũyĩkye vaasa!"
Ndyaĩ na ĩvuku yĩu ĩndĩ neewie nenda kwĩthĩwa na yĩmwe mĩtũkĩ mũno. Ĩtina wa mĩthenya mĩvũthũ Ngũsĩ ilĩ nĩsyakũnangie kwakwa, na syanenge ĩvuku yĩu twavatĩtwe. Nĩnayĩsomie ũtukũ ũsu, na ĩla aka asu masyokie nĩneetĩkĩlile kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia namo.
O na vatathelete ĩvinda yĩana ũndũ nĩneewie ũw'o wangiita. Kwĩyumya kw'onthe kũla neeyumĩsye ndĩni yakwa kwavĩndũkie weethĩa yu nĩ na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũtavany'a na nĩnendete Yeova mũno. Navatisiwe mwaka wa 1973. Ĩndĩ o na kau ndyaĩ na ĩvinda yingĩ ya kũtavya andũ ma mũsyĩ ũw'o, nĩnatatie ũndũ naĩ ndonya. Ĩndĩ o tondũ nĩeleisye mwambĩĩonĩ, nĩmambĩngie mũno vyũ, na mũno mũno mwĩĩtu-a-mwaitũ Araceli.
Araceli: Thĩna ũla nooneie kũla kũndũ twekalaa na nuns ala angĩ watumie noveea ũthatu ngoonĩ. O na vailyĩ ũu, nĩnaendeeie kũthi Misa kĩla Wakyumwa na kĩla mũthenya nĩnavoyaa ila mboya sya Ndasivii. No neew'aa ndyenda mũno kũelewa Mbivilia na kwoou nĩnavoyie Ngai andetheesye. Ĩndĩ ĩla mwĩĩtu-a-mwaitũ Felisa wandavisye ĩũlũ wa kĩla waĩ anambĩĩa kũĩkĩĩa, andavisye na kĩthikii kingĩ nginya atuma nĩsũanĩa ndĩni ĩsu yĩkĩte kũmũtumany'a. Kyu kyatumie tũemanwa mũno.
Ĩtina wa myaka mĩvũthũ nĩnasyokie Madrid ngathũkũme na nesa kũvatwaĩwa. Na nĩendeee oou nĩnatw'ĩkie mũndũ ũtaĩkĩĩaa ndĩni. Nesie kwĩthĩa kaĩ andũ ala mataĩ matĩĩa Misa mayaatĩĩaa kĩla kĩandĩkĩtwe ala Mavukunĩ ma Ũvoo Mũseo! Kyu kyatumie nĩeka kũthi kanisanĩ vyũ. Ndyaasyoka kũĩkĩĩa kana kwĩ "atheu," kana ĩia ya mwaki, na ndyaasyoka kumbũlĩla mũthembi. O na nĩnaanangie mĩvw'anano yonthe ĩla naĩ nayo. Ndyeesĩ kana maũndũ asu neekie nĩmaaĩle. O na kau neew'aa nĩkw'ĩte ngoo, naendeeie kũvoya Ngai ndimwĩa: "Nĩngwenda kũũmanya. Ndethya!" Nĩnĩlilikanaa kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyookie kwakwa mavinda meana ũna, ĩndĩ ndyaaĩsa kwivingũĩa mũomo. Ndyaĩkĩĩaa ndĩni o na ĩmwe.
Myakanĩ ya 1980, Lauri ekalaa France na Ramoni ekalaa Spain na elĩ nĩmambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ. Nasũanĩie o namo mekĩte kũkengwa o tondũ Felisa wakengetwe. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩnamanyanie na mũtũi weetawa Angelines na twatuma ndũũ. O nake aĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Angelines na mũũme matindĩaa kũmbĩa nĩnĩĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia. No meesĩ kana o na kau naasyaa ndi ndĩni nĩĩkĩĩaa, nĩnendaa mũno kũmanya kĩla kĩ Mbivilianĩ. Mũthya nesie kũmatavya: "Nĩ sawa. Ĩndĩ nĩĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nenyu ethĩwa ngatũmĩaa Mbivilia ĩla yakwa." Mbivilia ĩsu nawetaa nĩ ĩla ya Nácar-Colunga.
MBIVILIA NĨYO YESIE KŨTŨKWATANY'A
Felisa: Ĩla navatisiwe mwakanĩ wa 1973, kwaĩ o Ngũsĩ ta 70 taoninĩ ya Santander, ĩla nĩyo taoni nene kĩvalonĩ kya Cantabria, Spain. Twaĩ na kĩsio kĩnene mũno kya kũtavany'a. Mbeenĩ twaendaa ũtavany'a na mbasi, na ĩtina twambĩĩa kũthi na ngalĩ nini kĩsionĩ kĩu kyonthe. Kĩsionĩ kyu ve ndũa maana meana ũna na nĩtwaitavanisye syonthe.
O ũndũ myaka ĩvĩtĩte nĩnĩtanĩĩte kũmanyĩsya andũ aingĩ Mbivilia, na amanyĩw'a 11 nĩmavatisĩtwe. Aingĩ moo maĩ ma Katholeki. Nĩneesĩ kana nĩnaĩlĩte kũmomĩĩsya na kũmaelewa nũndũ o nakwa ndambĩte kwĩmanyĩsya naĩ Mũkatholeki wakwete ndĩni mũno. Nĩnamanyie kana nĩ kenda maeke mũĩkĩĩo ũla makwete makalũmya maĩ no nginya makue ĩvinda, na ĩngĩ maĩ no nginya makiitwe nĩ Mbivilia na veva mũtheu wa Yeova nĩ kana mone vala ũw'o ũĩ. (Aevl. 4:12) Tene mũemewa, Bienvenido, aĩ mũsikalĩ ĩndĩ nĩwesie kũvatiswa mwaka wa 1979. Nake inyia-akwa nĩwambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ĩndĩ akw'a atanaendeea mũno.
Araceli: Naĩ na nzika mũno ndyambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ. Ĩndĩ tũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya nesie kwĩthĩa ĩkundo yĩla yaĩ ngoonĩ yakundũkie. Kĩla nendie kya Ngũsĩ nĩ kana syo syekalaa kwosana na kĩla syatavanasya. Vandũ va nzika nambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo, na nambĩĩa kwĩkala nĩ mũtanu. O na atũi amwe mandavisye atĩĩ: "Araceli, kinyĩla o vau ũkinyĩle!"
Nĩlilikanaa ndivoya atĩĩ: "Nĩ mũvea mũno Yeova nũndũ ndwaambĩkĩsya ngoo na nĩwanengie myanya mingĩ mũno ya kũkwata kĩla namanthaa, nakyo nĩ ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ." Nĩneetisye mwĩĩtu-a-mwaitũ Felisa ũekeo nũndũ wa kũmũtavya naĩ. Vandũ va kũtindaa tũitetany'a twambĩĩie kũea ngewa syĩ mũyo mũno sya Mbivilia. Nesie kũvatiswa mwaka wa 1989 nĩ na myaka 61.
Felisa: Yu nĩ na myaka 91, nĩ ndiwa, na ndi na vinya ũla naĩ naw'o tene. Ĩndĩ nĩnĩsomaa Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya, ngathi maũmbanonĩ ĩla mwĩĩ wambĩtĩkĩlya, na nĩndanĩaa kũtavany'a mũno ũndũ ndonya.
Araceli: Nendete kũtavya ũvoo nuns na athembi ala neethĩana namo nĩ ũtavany'a. Nonaa nendete kwĩka ũu nũndũ o nakwa naĩ nun. Nĩnĩmanengete mavuku maingĩ na nĩnĩtanĩĩte kũneena na aingĩ moo. Nĩlilikanaa mũthembi ũmwe namũsyokeie mavinda kauta. Esie kũndavya atĩĩ: "Araceli, nĩtĩkĩlanĩte naku vyũ, ĩndĩ nĩthi va ngũĩte ũu ngũĩte? Ala ndongoesye na andũ makwa ma mũsyĩ makambona ata?" Nakwa namũkũlilye: "Nake Ngai akakwona ata?" Athingithisye mũtwe amakĩte, ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu nĩwaemiwe vyũ nĩ kũendeea kũmantha ũw'o.
Ve kaũndũ kamwe kaseo mũno katakambũla. Nĩnĩlilikanaa mũthenya ũla mũemewa wandavisye ya mbee nũkwenda tũendany'e ũmbano. Kuma mũthenya ũsu ndaatĩĩa ũmbano o na ũmwe, o na kau aĩ na myaka mbee wa 80. Nĩweemanyĩisye Mbivilia na eeka maendeeo nginya atw'ĩka mũtavany'a ũte mũvatise. Ndyaaũlwa nĩ mavinda maseo ala twatanĩie ĩmwe ũtavany'a. Ĩndĩ akwie vatiele o myei ĩlĩ avatiswe.
Felisa: Kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩndanĩthasya vyũ nĩ kwona ainawa atatũ maitw'ĩka eĩtu-a-asa makwa ma kĩ-veva, o na kau mbeenĩ mambĩngaa mũno. Tũtanĩĩte mũno kwĩthĩwa ĩmwe tũineena ĩũlũ wa Ngai witũ mũseo, Yeova, na ĩũlũ wa Ndeto yake! Ĩtina wa maũndũ onthe, yu tũmũthũkũmaa Yeova twĩ ngwatanĩo. *
^ kal. 29 Ũmũnthĩ Ramoni e na myaka 83, Felisa e na 91, nake Araceli e na 87, na onthe maendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova na kĩthito. Lauri akwie mwaka wa 1990 e o mũĩkĩĩku.

translation:
One day, a woman named Araceli visited her mother and said to her: "Come here and listen. I want to tell you something important about your future. Send me away now. I will take care of everything!" This woman was 91 years old, and she had been praying for this opportunity for a long time. But there was one thing mentioned in Matthew 7:8, which says, "Ask and it shall be given." That's what happened to her.—Felisa.
Felisa: We were many children in our family. There were 13 children in our family who attended the Catholic church, some more devoted than others. And there was a member of my mother's family who was a devout person and a teacher at a Catholic school, who was honored by Pope John Paul II with one of the awards for being "faithful." We really appreciated that. My father always supported my mother in her faith. We grew up with our grandmother, and you too, elders.
I was 12 years old when, one by one, they told us about our origins in Spain. One of them ended badly because he got lost. Many people suffered, but my father comforted the people and that is what strengthened him. The relatives of my mother helped a lot, and one man from among them took us to visit our aunt in Bilbao, Spain, where we stayed for a while with the Catholic sisters (nuns) who lived there. Our aunts were Araceli, Lauri, and Ramona. In those days, life was hard and difficult.
Araceli: We were called because our older sister was 14 years old, another was 12, and the youngest was 10, and all of us wanted to go somewhere to be with our family. From Bilbao, our parents sent us to study. We stayed there for several years, and then we were transferred to a larger convent of nuns, located in Zaragoza. They also received other girls. We were prepared to learn lessons, and in that place, we were very young, only ten years old.
Felisa: Later, we went to Zaragoza with my mother and her brother, who was a priest in our town, so she could take us to see our aunts. I remember this well because I became friends with the daughter of one of the mothers, who was very kind to me. At that time, I was in church, and I learned a lot because I had been with the nuns for a long time. They taught me prayers, and I wanted to teach them songs from my homeland in Africa.
They sent me to the nuns so that they would help me understand how to worship God properly, or because I was stubborn. Then I spent a year visiting my mother's brother, who was a priest. I helped around the house, and every day I went to buy vegetables at the Ndasivii market nearby. And I continued to collect donations for the church and sell postcards of Italy and other "foreign" cards.
Araceli: That trip was very important to us. But when the three of us left, we were afraid to go with them, so they convinced us. Ramona went to Zaragoza, Lauri went to Valencia, and I went to Madrid, and there we found what we were looking for. In Madrid, I met many people, both old and young, and I made many good friends. I really liked being with those girls.
Because of that, I realized that I didn't know anything. I didn't read the Bible and didn't understand anything. So whenever someone talked about God or Jesus, we would read the Bible together. We knew Latin a little, so we read the stories of the "pagans," and we cursed Italy. This situation was very difficult for us.
We will continue with my story, telling you how I felt and how I went to talk to the nun who guided us. I don't know if they understood how much I suffered, seeing so many people and things, and wanting to tell everything. I asked her to give me some advice, so I wouldn't hurt my head anymore and stop thinking about going back home with them.
I had three dreams, and in those dreams I saw myself going to hell. Then I decided to go to my house, and I wrote this letter with tears: "From today on, I want to reject Satan and serve God." So I wrote it carefully, and even though I didn't know how to write, I still wrote the letter. And I promised myself that I would never again trust anyone, and that I would always listen to my mother's advice. I asked Bishop Mwanya to pray for those people in Zaragoza. When I arrived in Zaragoza, I was very happy and I couldn't wait to get there. The journey was very long, but thanks to Lauri and Ramona, I enjoyed it very much.
THE STORY THAT MOVED US
Felisa: I remember traveling and arriving in Cantabria. Then I went to attend Mass. And then a man came up to me and asked me something strange. He said these words: "Have you heard about the story?" He showed me a book called "The Story of the Suffering of Holy Thursday." He continued saying, "Whoever hears this story, either believe it or leave it alone!"
And so the story began, and it involved many things. It happened during the difficult times when Ngusi was trying to harm us, and she wanted this story to be known. I spent that night thinking, and now I realize that I should have studied the Bible more.
And they told me another story about someone who was like me. To understand everything, I needed to open my heart and let God help me overcome this difficulty. I dedicated myself in 1973. And even though I had many opportunities to deceive people in that way, I refused to do so. And so I became a pioneer, and I helped many people, including my dear sister Araceli.
Araceli: That time I remember how we used to live together and how our mother always encouraged us to pray diligently. And because of that, I continued to attend Mass every Wednesday and every Sunday, but I still felt a longing for something more. But then I realized how important it was to understand the Bible and to know that God loves us. And my mother, Felisa, always reminded me to read it, and she also showed me examples that helped me appreciate our home and get to know God better. This has helped us a lot.
During those difficult years, I lived in Madrid, feeling lonely and wanting to be understood. And I kept hoping to find someone who would truly understand me. It's good to remember how Sister Misa taught us everything about the teachings and practices of the Catholic Church! This is why I want to go back to church often. I used to read or say "amen," or light a candle, and I used to confess my sins. And I cherished all the experiences I had. I also learned that some things aren't easy. And even though I didn't understand everything, I continued to seek God, saying: "I want to know you. Help me!" I was saddened when I heard that the Kingdom Hall of Jehovah's Witnesses was being demolished, but I decided to investigate further. I read it myself and so did others.
In the 1980s, Lauri lived in France and Ramona lived in Spain, and we were happy to share the Bible and the truth. I rejoiced because I was able to meet Felisa, who had been disfellowshipped. During those years, I became close friends with a woman named Angelines, and we wrote letters to each other. She was one of Jehovah's Witnesses. Angelines and her husband helped me to study the Bible. But even though I was studying with them, I wanted to learn everything in the Bible myself. So I said: "It's okay. I will study the Bible with you using your own Bible." The Bible they had was the Nacar-Colunga version.
THE BIBLE IS WHAT UNITED US
Felisa: I was baptized in 1973, at age 70, in Santander, which is in the province of Cantabria, Spain. We had a great desire to preach. At first, we preached on foot, and then we started traveling by bus, and during those trips, we saw what a beautiful country it was. That country has many beautiful places, and I visited them all.
For many years, I continued to share the Bible with many people, and 11 of them got baptized. Many of them were Catholics. Sometimes I hesitated to reason with them and explain things to them, because I was afraid of offending the Catholic priest who was close to my family. I realized that I needed to be courageous and speak boldly, so that others could see the truth and appreciate the power of Jehovah. (Heb. 4:12) Then we met Bienvenido, who was also willing to get baptized in 1979. He told his family about wanting to share the Bible with them.
Araceli: And now I want to share how I began to share the Bible and the truth. We continue to share because of the love that God has shown us. Every time I think about the truth, I remember how much effort it took to find it. People from my area encouraged me to persevere, and they encouraged me to stay strong. Some of my relatives even said to me: "Araceli, don't give up!"
I replied, saying: "This is Jehovah's work, and I want to dedicate myself fully to it and use all my energy to seize every opportunity, and this is what the Bible teaches." I then spoke to my sister-in-law Felisa about it. The people in our neighborhood often asked us to read portions of the Bible with them. In 1989, when I was 61 years old, I got baptized.
Felisa: Well, I am 91 years old now, and I still have the desire to serve. I read the Bible every day, and I enjoy the spiritual food that it provides, and I always try to apply what I learn in my life.
Araceli: I began to share the good news because I felt compelled to do so, and I enjoyed doing it. Later, I started thinking about this matter and wondering how I could continue. I had many questions, and I wanted to talk to more people. Once, a minister visited me and asked me: "Araceli, don't you think you should be baptized? Why haven't you done so yet?" And I responded: "Will God accept me?" He shook his head and said that my heart was already moved by the truth, and he encouraged me to get baptized.
On one occasion, something happened that touched my heart. I remember one day being invited to attend a meeting. At that meeting, there was an elderly man who was over 80 years old. He showed me the Bible and explained some points that helped me understand the importance of getting baptized. We talked together, and I decided to get baptized. But he told me that I needed to pray about it first.
Felisa: One thing that has always impressed me is seeing our brothers and sisters preaching from house to house, especially those who are older. We have been sharing the good news for many years and praising the name of our God, Jehovah, and the Kingdom of His Son! Despite everything, we continue to thank Jehovah with gratitude. *
^kal. 29 Ramona is 83 years old, Felisa is 91, and Araceli is 87, and they all continue to thank Jehovah faithfully. Laurie was born in 1990 and became a pioneer.

text:
1. Nĩ va tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte?
WAAĨTHUKĨĨSYA maũvoo letiũnĩ kana televiseninĩ na ũkekũlya-ĩ, 'Yo nthĩ ĩno yelekele va?' Kwĩ na mĩisyo mingĩ na ũng'endu mwingĩ, na ũu nũtumaa andũ masya kana no nginya twĩthĩwe twĩ vakuvĩ na mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ w'o? Ve kĩndũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũkamanya kĩla kĩkekĩka ĩvinda yũkĩte? Ĩĩ kĩ vo. O na kau andũ maitonya kũmanya ũndũ kũkethĩwa ĩvinda yũkĩte, Yeova Ngai nũtonya. Nũtũtavĩtye Mbivilianĩ ũndũ ĩvinda yitũ yũkĩte yĩkethĩwa yĩilyĩ, na ũndũ nthĩ ĩkethĩwa yĩilyĩ.—Isaia 46:10; Yakovo 4:14.
2, 3. Amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ mendaa kũmanya kyaũ, na Yesũ amasũngĩie ata?
2 Ĩla Mbivilia ĩkũweta ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ, ndĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a kana nĩ nthĩ ĩno twĩkalaa ĩkanangwa, ĩndĩ nĩ ala athũku makanangwa. Yesũ nĩwamanyĩisye andũ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkasumbĩka nthĩ. (Luka 4:43) Amanyĩw'a make mendaa kũmanya ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wĩũka na nĩkyo kĩtumi mamũkũlilye Yesũ atĩĩ: "Maũndũ asu makethĩwa ĩndĩĩ? na wonan'yo nĩ wĩva wa kũka kwaku, na wa wĩanĩu wa ĩvinda yĩĩ?" (Mathayo 24:3) Yesũ ndaamatavya mũthenya ũla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkoka, ĩndĩ amatavisye maũndũ ala mesaa kwĩkĩka mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ ũtanamba kũvika. Maũndũ ala Yesũ wawetie nĩmaendeee kwĩkĩka ũmũnthĩ.
3 Kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ nĩtũũneenea maũndũ meũtũĩkĩĩthya kana twĩkalĩte vakuvĩ vyũ na mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ. Mbee, twĩamba kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa kaũ weethĩiwe ĩtunĩ nĩ kana tũmanye nĩkĩ maũndũ methĩĩtwe me mathũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
KAŨ WEETHĨIWE ĨTUNĨ
4, 5. (a) Kweethĩiwe ata ĩtunĩ ĩla Yesũ watw'ĩkie Mũsumbĩ? (b) Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Ũvuan'yo 12:12, nĩ ũndũ mwaũ waĩ wĩthĩwe Satani ekw'a ĩũlũ wa nthĩ?
4 Kĩlungunĩ kya 8 nĩtũneemanyĩisye kana Yesũ atw'ĩkie Mũsumbĩ ĩtunĩ mwaka wa 1914. (Ndanieli 7:13, 14) Ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo nĩyĩtũtavĩtye ũndũ kweethĩiwe asumbĩka. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwaĩ kaũ ĩtunĩ: Mikaeli [ũla nĩ Yesũ] na alaĩka make maithi kũkita na ũla mũkũnga mũnene [ũla nĩ Satani]; na mũkũnga ũsu na alaĩka maw'o mokita." * Satani na ndaimoni syake nĩmasindiwe na mekw'a kũũ nthĩ. Kwasũanĩa ũtanu ũla alaĩka meewie! Ĩndĩ nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie andũ vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana nĩmeethĩiwe na mathĩna maingĩ kuma ĩvinda yĩu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Ndevili ethĩĩtwe na ũthilĩku mwingĩ "akĩmanya kana e na kavinda o kanini."—Ũvuan'yo 12:7, 9, 12.
5 Ndevili nĩ ũetete mathĩna maingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. E na ũthilĩku nũndũ vatiele kavinda o kanini nĩ kana Ngai amwanange. Ekai yu twone maũndũ ala Yesũ waisye makekĩka mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 24.
MĨTHENYA YA MŨMINŨKĨLYO
6, 7. Ndeto sya Yesũ ĩũlũ wa makaũ na yũa iendeee kwĩanĩa ata?
6 Kũkeethĩwa kaũ. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Mbaĩ ĩkookĩlĩla mbaĩ, na ũsumbĩ ũkookĩlĩla ũsumbĩ." (Mathayo 24:7) Kuma mwaka wa 1914, andũ aingĩ nĩmakw'ĩte nũndũ wa kaũ kwĩ myakanĩ ya navu ĩtina. Livoti ĩmwe kuma kĩkundinĩ kĩkaa ũkunĩkĩli wa maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ (Worldwatch Institute) yonanĩtye kana kuma mwaka wa 1914, andũ mbee wa milioni 100 nĩmakw'ĩte nũndũ wa kaũ. Andũ ala makwie nũndũ wa kaũ kuma mwaka wa 1900 nginya mwaka wa 2000 maĩ aingĩ kwĩ ala mooaiwe myaka 1,900 ĩla yaĩ mbee. Kwasũanĩa kyeva na woo ũla andũ milioni mbingĩ makwatĩte nũndũ wa kaũ!
7 Kũkeethĩwa mayũa. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Kũkeethĩwa mayũa." (Mathayo 24:7) O na kau yu kwĩ na lĩu mwingĩ kwĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva, andũ aingĩ mayĩthĩawa na lĩu ũtoetye. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mayĩthĩawa na mbesa itoetye sya kũthooa lĩu, kana mĩũnda yĩanĩtye ya kũĩma. Andũ mbee wa mbilioni ĩmwe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ mayĩthĩawa na mbesa itoetye sya kũtũmĩa kĩla mũthenya. Ngwatanĩo ya Nthĩ Yonthe ya Ũiiti (World Health Organization) yaĩtye kana syana milioni mbingĩ nikusaa kĩla mwaka nũndũ wa kũkosa lĩu wĩanĩtye ũtonya kũitetheesya kwĩthĩwa na mĩĩ mĩseo.
8, 9. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkwonany'a kana wathani wa Yesũ ĩũlũ wa itetemo sya nthĩ na mowau nĩwĩanĩĩte?
8 Kũkeethĩwa itetemo sya nthĩ. Yesũ athanie kana kũkeethĩwa na "itetemo nene sya nthĩ." (Luka 21:11) Kĩla mwaka nĩkwĩthĩawa na itetemo sya nthĩ nene mũno. Kuma mwaka wa 1900, andũ mbee wa milioni ilĩ nĩmakw'ĩte nũndũ wa ithingitho sya nthĩ. Na o na kau tekinolongyia nĩtetheesye kũkethĩwa na masinĩ sya kũthima ithingitho itanaumĩla, andũ no makusaa nũndũ wa ithingitho.
9 Kũkeethĩwa na mowau. Yesũ athanie kana kũkeethĩwa na "mĩimũ." Mowau mathũku maĩ manyaĩĩke na mĩtũkĩ na mayũaa andũ aingĩ. (Luka 21:11) O na kau matakĩtalĩ nĩmasomeete ũndũ matonya kũiita mowau maingĩ, kwĩ o mowau mate ndawa. O na ve livoti ĩmwe ĩeleetye kana kĩla mwaka andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmakusaa nũndũ wa mowau ta kĩthũi (tuberculosis), ndetema, na kĩvĩndũvĩndũ. O na eka mowau asu, matakĩtalĩ nĩmesĩte kũmanya kana kwĩ mowau angĩ 30 maumĩlĩte, na amwe mai ndawa.
ŨNDŨ ANDŨ MAĨ METHĨWE MAILYĨ MĨTHENYANĨ YA MŨMINŨKĨLYO
10. Ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 2 Timotheo 3:1-5 iendeee kwĩanĩa ata ũmũnthĩ?
10 Ĩvuku ya 2 Timotheo 3:1-5 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo kũkeethĩwa mavinda ma mũisyo." Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwaeleisye ũndũ andũ aingĩ makethĩwa mailyĩ mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo. Aisye andũ makeethĩwa
makĩyenda ene
makyenda mbesa
matew'aa asyai
mate atheu
mate na wendo waĩle
mate na wĩting'o
ai
endi ma motanu ma nthĩ mbee wa kũmwenda Ngai
me na mũvw'ano wa kĩkĩo kwa Ngai, ĩndĩ nĩmakaĩĩte vinya wakyo
11. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Savuli 92:7, andũ ala athũku makeekwa ata?
11 Andũ aingĩ kĩsionĩ kyenyu mailyĩ ũu? Vate nzika, andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ mailyĩ ũu. Ĩndĩ o mĩtũkĩ Ngai nũkwosa ĩtambya. Atwathĩte atĩĩ: "Yĩla athũku maumĩlanga ta nyeki, na yĩla onthe ala mekaa ũthũku maĩlaa; ũu wĩthĩawa nĩ kana makanangwa tene na tene."—Savuli 92:7.
ŨVOO MŨSEO MĨTHENYANĨ YA MŨMINŨKĨLYO
12, 13. Nĩ maũndũ meva Yeova ũtũmanyĩĩtye mĩthenyanĩ ĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo?
12 Mbivilia nĩyathanie kana mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo nthĩ ĩkeethĩwa yusĩe mathĩna. Ĩndĩ nĩwetete ĩngĩ kana ve maũndũ maseo makethĩwa.
13 Kwongeleka kwa ũmanyi wa Mbivilia. Mwathani Ndanieli nĩwaandĩkie ĩũlũ wa mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ũmanyi ũkongeleka." (Ndanieli 12:4) Ngai aĩ anenge andũ ũtonyi wa kũelewa Mbivilia nesanga kwĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva. Yeova nĩwĩkĩte ũu, na mũno mũno kuma mwaka wa 1914. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtũmanyĩĩtye ũw'o ĩũlũ wa ĩsyĩtwa yake, kĩeleelo kyake kwa nthĩ, ũw'o ĩũlũ wa wovosyo, ũndũ kwĩthĩawa ĩla mũndũ wakw'a, na ũw'o ĩũlũ wa ũthayũũkyo. Nĩtũneemanyĩisye kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai now'o ũtonya kũtũminĩa mathĩna onthe. O na nĩtwĩmanyĩĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu, na ũndũ tũtonya kwĩkala kwa nzĩa ĩkũmwendeesya Ngai. Ĩndĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai maĩle kũtũmĩa ata kĩla meemanyĩsya? Ve wathani ũngĩ ũtonya kũtũtetheesya kũkwata ũsũngĩo.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 21 na 25.
14. Ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ ũtavanĩtw'e kũvika va, na naaũ maũtavanasya?
14 Wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. Aiweta ĩũlũ wa mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo, Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Ũvoo ũũ mũseo wa ũsumbĩ ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe." (Mathayo 24:3, 14) Ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ nũtavanĩtw'e nthĩ mbee wa 230, na kwa ithyomo mbee wa 700. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kuma 'mbaĩnĩ na ngo' syonthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nitetheesye andũ mamanye Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ kyaũ, na ũndũ ũkatethya andũ. (Ũvuan'yo 7:9) Na mekaa ũu vate ndĩvi. O na kau nĩmamenetwe na nĩmathĩnaw'a nĩ andũ aingĩ, vai kĩndũ kĩtonya kũsiĩĩa wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũiendeea, o tondũ Yesũ wathanie.—Luka 21:17.
WAĨLE KWĨKA ATA?
15. (a) We nũĩkĩĩaa kana twĩkalĩte mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, na nĩkĩ ũĩkĩĩaa ũu? (b) Kũkeethĩwa ata kwa andũ ala mamwĩw'aa Yeova na kwa ala matamwĩw'aa?
15 We nũĩkĩĩaa kana twĩkalĩte mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo? Mawathani maingĩ ma Mbivilia ala maeleetye ĩũlũ wa mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo maendeee kwĩanĩa. Yeova akilye kũũngamya wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, na ĩndĩ "mũminũkĩlyo" ũyũka. (Mathayo 24:14) Mũminũkĩlyo nĩ kyaũ? Mũminũkĩlyo nĩ ĩvinda yĩla Ngai ũkavetanga ũthũku w'onthe, na akeeka ũu kaũnĩ wa Ali–Maketoni. Yeova akatũmĩa Yesũ Klĩsto na alaĩka make me vinya mũno kwananga andũ ala matamwĩw'aa na matew'aa Mwana wake. (2 Athesalonika 1:6-9) Ĩtina wa ũu, Satani na ndaimoni syake maikakenga andũ. Na onthe ala mekwenda kũmwĩw'a Ngai na kwĩtĩkĩla Ũsumbĩ wake makoona maũndũ onthe ala ũtwathĩte mayĩanĩa.—Ũvuan'yo 20:1-3; 21:3-5.
16. Nũndũ mũminũkĩlyo wĩ vakuvĩ vyũ, nĩ maũndũ meva waĩle kwĩka?
16 Nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Satani ĩkilyĩ kwanangwa. Kwoou nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno ũkekũlya atĩĩ: 'Nyie naĩle kwĩka ata?' Yeova eenda wĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka kuma Mbivilianĩ. Nĩwaĩle kwosa kwa ũito maũndũ ala ũkwĩmanyĩsya. (Yoana 17:3) O na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩthĩawa na maũmbano kĩla kyumwa ma kũtetheesya andũ mamĩelewe Mbivilia. Tata ũndũ ũtonya ũendae maũmbanonĩ asu ũteũtĩĩa. (Soma Aevelania 10:24, 25.) Wamanya kana nĩwaĩle kwĩka moalyũku maũndũnĩ mana, ndũkethĩwe na wia wa kwĩka ũu. Weeka moalyũku asu, ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova ĩkaendeea kũlũlũmĩla.—Yakovo 4:8.
17. Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ makaseng'a ĩla mũminũkĩlyo wĩũka?
17 Mũtũmwa Vaulo aeleisye kana kwanangwa kwa andũ athũku kũkavika andũ aingĩ matataĩĩe, "o ũndũ kĩng'ei kyũkaa ũtukũ." (1 Athesalonika 5:2) Nake Yesũ athanie kana andũ aingĩ makavũthĩĩsya maũndũ ala mekwonany'a kana twĩkalĩte mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo. Aisye atĩĩ: "O ũndũ kwailyĩ matukũ ma Noa, now'o kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ Mwana wa mũndũ akyũka [kana, mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo]. Nũndũ o tondũ matukũnĩ asu ala maĩ mbee wa kĩla kĩw'ũ kingĩ, andũ meethĩiwe makĩya na makĩnyw'a, makĩtwaana na makĩtwawa, kũvika mũthenya ũla Noa walikile ngalawanĩ, na matyeesĩ mũvaka kĩla kĩw'ũ kingĩ kyooka, kyamatwaa onthe; now'o kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ Mwana wa mũndũ akyũka."—Mathayo 24:37-39.
18. Nĩ ũkany'o wĩva Yesũ watũnengie?
18 Yesũ atũkanisye kana tũyaĩle kũemeewa nĩ "kũya mũno, na ũthengi, na mawĩmakĩo ma thayũ ũũ." Aisye kana mũminũkĩlyo ũkooka na kĩthũlũmũko "ta kĩtei." Asyokie asya kana "ũkamokĩa andũ onthe ala me ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe." Na ĩndĩ ongeleela kwasya atĩĩ: "Ĩkalai mũsyaĩĩsye matukũ onthe, mũkĩvoya, nĩ kana mũnengwe kũvonoka maũndũ asu onthe ala makoka, na kũũngama mbee wa Mwana wa mũndũ." (Luka 21:34-36) Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwĩthukĩĩsya ũkany'o wa Yesũ? Nũndũ nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani ĩkilyĩ kwanangwa. No ala meĩthĩwa metĩkĩlĩtwe nĩ Yeova na Yesũ makavonoka ĩla mũminũkĩlyo wĩũka, na andũ asu makekala tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ.—Yoana 3:16; 2 Vetelo 3:13.

translation:
1. Should we be concerned about the future at all?
Perhaps you have heard it on the radio or television—or read it somewhere—'How will things turn out?' There are many opinions and much uncertainty, and this can cause people to worry or feel helpless about the future. What is the reason for this? Because people want to know what is going to happen. But is it possible to know the future? Yes, it is. And there is One who knows what will come to pass, Jehovah God. He has foretold many things about the future, and he fulfills what he foretells.—Isaiah 46:10; James 4:14.
2, 3. What did Jesus' disciples ask him to teach them, and how did Jesus answer?
2 The Bible shows that people want to know about the future, whether it is their own future or the future of mankind in general. Jesus knew that Satan could influence people to misunderstand God's purpose. (Luke 4:43) His disciples asked him to teach them when the end of the Jewish system would come, and they also asked: "What will be the sign of your presence and of the conclusion of the system of things?" (Matthew 24:3) Jesus gave them a prophecy about the sign of the conclusion of the system of things, and he said that certain events would occur before then. Those events Jesus foretold are still happening today.
3 It is important that we pay attention to current events and think about what they mean in connection with Bible prophecy. Let us now examine what happened during one occasion when Jesus was with his disciples.
WHAT THE SIGN MEANS
4, 5. (a) What question did Jesus ask his disciples? (b) According to Revelation 12:12, what is the main thing that Satan wants to do to mankind?
4 In 1914, Jesus began to fulfill the sign described in Daniel chapter 7, verses 13 and 14. The book of Revelation explains what this means. It says: "And in those days there will be great tribulation such as has never occurred since the beginning of the world until now, no, nor will occur." * Satan and his demons were cast down to earth. How does this affect people on earth? The Bible indicates that much trouble has been caused because "the Devil . . . has deceived the whole inhabited earth." (Revelation 12:7, 9, 12)
5 The Devil uses many methods to mislead people. He takes advantage of people's desire for security, and he makes them believe that he can give it to them if they oppose God. Let us see how Jesus helped his disciples discern spiritual truths.—Read the section titled "Discern Spiritual Truth" in Chapter 24.
DISCERNING SPIRITUAL TRUTHS
6, 7. Why did Jesus ask questions, and how can we imitate him?
6 Consider this. Jesus said: "Nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom." (Matthew 24:7) Since 1914, many nations have been involved in numerous wars. A report from an organization called Worldwatch Institute stated that from 1914 onward, some 100 million people died in wars. Many more people suffered during the 20th century—perhaps as many as 1,900 million in total. Think of the suffering experienced by millions!
7 Consider this further. Jesus said: "Consider this further." (Matthew 24:7) Also, there has been a great increase in sickness and disease, and many people are afflicted with deadly illnesses. Why? Because diseases spread easily due to travel, or because of outbreaks. Some billion people worldwide suffer from deadly diseases each year. The World Health Organization estimates that millions die annually from preventable diseases caused by lack of clean water.
8, 9. What shows that Jesus' prophecy regarding the end of the world and its signs is being fulfilled?
8 Consider the end of the world. Jesus foretold that there would be "great earthquakes." (Luke 21:11) There have been many severe earthquakes each year. In the 20th century, about eight million people died as a result of earthquakes. And despite advances in technology that allow us to predict earthquakes, people continue to suffer from them.
9 Consider famines. Jesus prophesied that there would be "food shortages." Famines cause suffering and death to many people. (Luke 21:11) However, modern farming methods can produce more food than ever, yet famine still exists. For example, millions die each year from malnutrition (tuberculosis), malaria, and diarrhea. Furthermore, scientists estimate that about 30 new viruses emerge each year, some of which are resistant to drugs.
THE WICKEDNESS OF PEOPLE IN THE LAST DAYS
10. How does 2 Timothy 3:1-5 describe the attitude that many will have in the last days?
10 Second Timothy 3:1-5 states: "People will be lovers of themselves." The apostle Paul described how many people would behave in the last days. He said they would be
selfish
loveless
headstrong
brutish
disloyal
unloving
without self-control
and
enemies of what is good, including worship of God
impudent toward their parents, and without understanding
11. According to Psalm 92:7, what happens to wicked people eventually?
11 What do you observe about most people today? Notice that most people today are wicked. But God does not overlook wickedness. He has declared: "The wicked flourish like grass, and all evildoers meet their end."—Psalm 92:7.
WHY WICKEDNESS INCREASES
12, 13. What does Jehovah allow to happen so that we can identify the wickedness in the last days?
12 The Bible foretold that wickedness would increase in the last days. But it also indicates that certain things would take place.
13 An increase in Bible knowledge. Daniel prophesied about a feature of the last days, saying: "Knowledge will increase." (Daniel 12:4) God purposed that people would have increasing opportunity to understand the Bible during this time, and especially from 1914 onward. For example, we have come to understand more fully the meaning of his prophecies, his purpose regarding the earth, the meaning of the ransom, why humans suffer, and the meaning of righteousness. We appreciate that God's Word now helps us to understand matters better than ever before, and we realize that we need to be able to discern what is true and what is false, and what we should believe and how we should live in harmony with God's direction. But do God's servants always find it easy to apply what they learn? Consider how we can strengthen our resolve.—Read Proverbs 21 and 25.
14. How does the influence of Satan affect people, and what questions will we answer?
14 He misleads people in every way. He distorts the truth, Jesus said: "This good news of the kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth." (Matthew 24:3, 14) The influence of Satan has been felt throughout almost 230 years, and for over 700 years. Because of Jehovah's allowing 'every sort of wickedness' to develop, people in all lands have become familiar with false religion, and this has misled them. (Revelation 7:9) And often those who are deceived are numerous, so it may be difficult to see how to resist such influence, unless Jesus guides us.—Luke 21:17.
ARE YOU TAKING A STAND?
15. (a) Why are we determined to remain spiritual people, and what helps us to do so? (b) What responsibility do we have toward others who know Jehovah and toward those who do not know him?
15 Why are we determined to remain spiritual people? Many scriptures show that the truth about spiritual people continues to progress. Jehovah allows the influence of Satan to continue for a time, so that "spiritual people" can be identified. (Matthew 24:14) Who are the spiritual people? They are those whom God uses to care for his organization, and they include the faithful men like Alistair MacLean. Jehovah sends Jesus Christ and his associates to punish those who do not appreciate his Son. (2 Thessalonians 1:6-9) Meanwhile, Satan and his demons deceive people. And all others who oppose God and reject his Kingdom cause all sorts of trouble.—Revelation 20:1-3; 21:3-5.
16. Since spiritual people are few, what things should we take note of?
16 This Kingdom is being opposed by Satan, and he keeps trying to get us to ask ourselves: 'Are we really taking note?' Jehovah will reveal many things through his Word. Take note of the things that help you to appreciate him more. (John 17:3) Also, the spirit of Jehovah works through the congregation to strengthen those who want to know the Bible. Make an effort to attend meetings regularly, so that you can benefit from them. (Read Hebrews 10:24, 25.) Ask yourself whether you are taking note of the things that matter, and then draw close to God by means of prayer. Keep drawing close to Jehovah, and he will continue to enlighten you.—James 4:8.
17. What do many people think about spiritual people?
17 The apostle Paul explained that when people are deceived, they often lead others into trouble, saying, "It is late!" (1 Thessalonians 5:2) Jesus warned that many people would be surprised when they realize how near the end is. He said: "The presence of the Son of man will be like the days of Noah. For just as they were eating and drinking and marrying and giving in marriage until the flood came and swept them all away, so too the presence of the Son of man will be. . . . They did not know until the flood came and swept them all away, so too the presence of the Son of man will be." —Matthew 24:37-39.
18. How does Jesus show that he cares for us?
18 Jesus showed that he cares for us by warning us about being "careless, and intoxicated, and preoccupied with the anxieties of daily life." He told his followers to be ready and to "keep looking out" for the sign of his presence. And he urged them: "Pay attention to yourselves, that your hearts may never become burdened with overeating or excessive drinking or the anxieties of this life, and that day may not come upon you unexpectedly." (Luke 21:34-36) So, what can we do to show that we appreciate Jesus' concern? We must remember that Satan's world is deceiving. Only those who are approved by Jehovah and Jesus will survive, and the rest will perish during the great tribulation.—John 3:16; 2 Peter 3:13.

text:
YEOVA NGAI athangaasya Aklĩsto mende mũno kwĩkalany'a na mũuo. Endaa twĩkale tũlilikene kana mũuo nĩ kĩndũ kya vata mũno kwitũ. Twatata kũmantha mũuo, Aklĩsto onthe makatanĩaa mũuo mwingĩ mũno. Kĩu kĩtumaa kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kĩthĩwa kĩ vandũ vaseo mũno vekwĩliĩlwa nĩ onthe ala matendete ithokoo.
Kwa ngelekany'o, ve mũndũ mũe ũmwe waĩ nguma mũno nthĩ ya Madagascar wendete mũno kwona ũndũ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩkalaa syĩ ngwatanĩo. Mũndũ ũsu ekalaa ayasya ũũ ngoonĩ yake, 'Ngesa kwenda kũlika ndĩninĩ, nĩtw'ĩka wa ndĩni ĩsu.' Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩwaekanie na maũndũ ma ũwe, aaĩlya mũtwaano wake woosana na Maandĩko o na kau nĩwakuie myei kauta, na ĩndĩ atw'ĩka mũthaithi wa Yeova, ũla nĩwe Ngai wa mũuo.
O tondũ mũndũ ũsu weekie, andũ aingĩ kĩla mwaka nĩmokaa kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto na maikwata mũuo ũla matũaa mamanthaa mũno. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩwetete nesa vyũ kana "kĩwĩu kyai na ngananĩo" syalika kĩkundinĩ no itume andũ me ndũũ maemanwa na vailika thĩna. (Yak. 3:14-16) Ũseo Mbivilia nĩtũtavĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka mathĩna ta asu maikalike na ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka tũlũlũmĩlye mũuo ũla wĩ vo. Nĩ kana tũmanye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ũu, ekai twone ngelekany'o imwe sya mathĩna malikile andũnĩ.
MATHĨNA ALA MATONYA KUMĨLA NA ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KŨMAMINA
"Ndyeew'anaa na mwana-a-asa ũla twanenganĩw'e wĩa. Nĩngũlilikana ĩvinda twatetanisye mũno na tweethĩwa nĩ andũ elĩ tũendeee kwĩkanĩsya ndeto."—CHRIS.
"Nakililye ndataĩĩe mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe twakothaa kũtavany'a ĩmwe avangũa mĩvango ĩla tweekĩte ya ũtavany'a. Kuma vau ndaaneeny'a ĩngĩ. Ndyeesĩ nĩkĩ wĩkie ũu."—JANET.
"Mũthenya ũmwe naneenaa simũnĩ nĩ na andũ angĩ elĩ. Ũmwe wa asu elĩ aneenie ta wamina ngewa na kwoou nyie neesilya nĩwatila simũ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ nambĩĩe kũtavya ũla natiiwe nake simũnĩ maũndũ mate maseo ĩũlũ wake, na kaĩ o na ndatilĩte simũ."—MICHAEL.
"Kĩkundinĩ kitũ ve eĩtu-a-asa elĩ mavainia meethĩĩtwe na mathĩna. Ũmwe akwatisye kũsomeaa ũla ũngĩ. Ala angĩ meew'aa naĩ mũno moona maitetany'a."—GARY.
No wone asu ta maĩ mathĩna manini mũno. Ĩndĩ mathĩna asu onthe maĩ matonya kũũmĩsya ala angĩ na kũtuma maleela kĩ-veva. No ũtane nĩ kũmanya kana ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asu nĩmaekie Mbivilia yamatetheesya kũtũngĩĩa mũuo katĩ woo. We wĩona ta maatĩĩie myolooto yĩva?
"Sisyai mũikatetan'ye mwĩ nzĩanĩ." (Mwa. 45:24) Ũsu nĩ ũtao Yosevu wanengie ana-a-ĩthe ĩvinda yĩla masyokete kwĩ ĩthe woo. Ũsu waĩ ũtao mũseo ta kĩ! Ethĩwa mũndũ nũkũemwa nĩ kũtũngatũnga ngoo yake na nũkũthata mĩtũkĩ, nũtonya kũtuma ala angĩ mathilĩka. Chris esie kwĩthĩa kana thĩna wake waĩ mĩtũlyo na ndendete kũtavw'a ũndũ ũkwĩka. Nũndũ Chris nĩwendaa kũalyũka, nĩwaneenie na mwana-a-asa ũla matetanasya amwĩtya ũekeo na kuma vau atata mũno ndakathatae mĩtũkĩ. Nake mwana-a-asa ũsu ũngĩ nĩwatatie a vake aalyũke ĩtina wa kwona Chris aitata kwĩka maendeeo. Ũmũnthĩ matanĩaa mũno kũmũthũkũma Yeova me vamwe.
"Vala vate ũtao, maũndũ ala masũanĩĩtwe kwĩkwa nĩmanangĩkaa." (Nth. 15:22) Janet eethĩie kaĩ nĩwaaĩlĩte kũkwata ũtao ũsu nesanga! Kwoou nĩwatwie kũmantha "ũtao," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kũneena na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũla ũngĩ. Maendeee kũea ngewa, Janet nĩwatũmĩie ũĩ nĩ kana atetheesye mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu ũngĩ eyĩelesye kuma ngoonĩ nĩkĩ weew'aa woo. Mayambĩĩa kũea ngewa vai ũmwe weew'aa e mwĩanĩe vyũ, ĩndĩ maũndũ maendeeie kũseũva o ũndũ maendeeie kũneenea thĩna woo mauĩtye. Nĩvo mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu ũngĩ wamanyie kana eekĩte kũelewa maũndũ naĩ na kĩla weesĩ o na kĩyakonetye Janet. Kwoou nĩweetisye ũekeo na ũmũnthĩ ũũ mamũthũkũmaa Yeova me ngwatanĩo.
"Ethĩwa ĩndĩ nũũnengane mũthĩnzĩo waku kĩthembeonĩ, na ũkĩlilikanĩla vu kana mwana-a-au e ũndũ naku, tia mũthĩnzĩo waku vu mbee wa kĩthembeo, noithi, wambe kwĩw'ana na mwana-a-au." (Mt. 5:23, 24) Ethĩwa nũũlilikana, ũsu nĩ ũtao Yesũ wanenganie ĩvinda ya ũla Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ. Michael eewie thĩna mwingĩ mũno asũanĩa ũndũ waneeneie ũla ũngĩ naĩ o na ateũsũanĩa. Ĩndĩ nĩwatw'ĩte kũtata ũndũ ũtonya atũngĩĩe mũuo ũla waĩ vo. Kwoou nĩweenyivisye na athi kwĩtya mwana-a-asa ũla wakoseete ũekeo menene. Maũndũ mekalile ata ĩtina wa ũu? Michael easya: "Mwana-a-asa ũsu andekeie vyũ kuma ngoonĩ." Ndũũ yoo nĩyasokie.
"[Endeeai] kũmĩĩasya ũmwe kwa ũla ũngĩ, na kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene, ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva e na ũndũ na ũngĩ." (Ako. 3:12-14) Ala mavainia elĩ matavanĩtye kwa ĩvinda ĩasa matetheeiw'e nĩ mũtumĩa ũmwe waĩ tei. Amatetheeisye masũanĩe makũlyo ta aa: 'Ve vata mwaũ wa kũeka ala angĩ makw'e ngoo nũndũ witũ? Twĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũlea kũmĩanĩsya na kũendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ ngwatanĩo?' Nĩmeethukĩĩisye ũtao wa mũtumĩa ũsu na maũatĩĩa. Yu nĩmew'anaa na matavanasya ĩmwe nesa.
Ethĩwa mũndũ nĩwakũũmĩsya, kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ nthĩnĩ wa Akolosai 3:12-14 no kũtetheesye mũno. Aingĩ methĩĩte meetĩkĩla kwĩnyivya no maekee ũla ũmavĩtĩsye na mayũlwa nũu. Ethĩwa nĩwatata kwĩka ũu ĩndĩ wĩĩw'a ve vandũ vatiele, mwolooto ũla ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 18:15 no ũkũtetheesye? Ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu Yesũ awetaa ĩtambya yĩla mũndũ waĩle kwosa ethĩwa nĩweekwa naĩ ngito nĩ ũngĩ. Ĩndĩ mwolooto ũla wĩ vo no kwĩthwa ũtethya mũno. Mantha mwanya ũthi wone mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa, na ũiea ngewa nake nesa na wĩnyivĩtye nĩ kana mũtate kwona ũndũ mũtonya kwĩw'ana.
Vate nzika, ve motao angĩ maseo Mbivilia ĩtũnengete. Nĩ kana motao asu maũtethye, waĩle kwĩthĩwa na "ũsyao wa Veva," naw'o nĩ "wendo, ũtanu, mũuo, wũmĩĩsyo, kwĩka angĩ nesa, ũseo, kĩthito, ũuu, wĩting'o." (Aka. 5:22, 23) O tondũ oilo ũtumaa masinĩ ĩthũkũma nesa, nguma isu nimũtetheeasya kũea ngewa nesa ĩla mũũtata kwĩw'ana.
NĨ ŨATHIMO KWĨTHĨWA NA AKLĨSTO ME KĨVATHŨKANY'O KĨKUNDINĨ
Tũmbĩtwe kĩvathũkany'o, na kwoou kĩla ũmwe witũ e ũndũ ũilyĩ, na ũndũ wĩkaa maũndũ. Kĩu no kĩtume ndũũ syĩthĩwa syĩ ngamu. Ĩndĩ kĩvathũkany'o o kĩu no kĩete mũaanĩko. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩthĩĩtwe e mũtumĩa kwa ĩvinda ĩasa anenganĩte ngelekany'o ĩno: "Mũndũ wĩ nthoni no athĩne mũno ekalany'a na mũndũ mũsanzamũku na ũtaemawa nĩ kũneena. O na kau kĩvathũkany'o ta kĩu no kyoneke kĩte na thĩna, no kyumĩlye kĩthokoo kĩnene." Ĩndĩ we wĩona ata? Nĩ lasima andũ ala mombĩtwe me kĩvathũkany'o mekalae maithokoana kĩla ĩvinda? Kwaeka twose ngelekany'o ya atũmwa elĩ matonya kwĩthĩwa maĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ. We Vetelo ailyĩ ata? No twasye aĩ mũneenu na atamũkaa o kĩla kyooka mũtwe. Nake Yoana? No twasye we nĩwendete andũ mũno na kaingĩ nĩwasũanĩaa mũno atanamba kũneena na ndasembeaa maũndũ. Asu ti maũndũ tweeka kũsũanĩa nũndũ ve o kĩtumi kya kwasya atũmwa asu mailyĩ ũu. Ĩndĩ o na kĩvathũkany'o kĩu kĩ vo, mathũkũmaa me ngwatanĩo. (Meko 8:14; Aka. 2:9) O ta ũu ũmũnthĩ, Aklĩsto no mathũkũme me ngwatanĩo o na matw'ĩke mavathũkene ata.
No kwĩthĩwa kĩkundinĩ kyenyu ve mwana-a-asa ũũthokoaa kĩlĩko nũndũ wa mũneenele wake kana meko make. Ĩndĩ nũseo kũlilikana kana Klĩsto nĩwakwie kwondũ wa Mũklĩsto ũsu na kana nĩwaĩlĩte kũmwenda. (Yoa. 13:34, 35; Alo. 5:6-8) Kwoou vandũ va kũtila kĩtindo kyaku nake kana kũtata mũikese kũkomanĩa vandũ, ĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'We mwana-a-asa ũũ eĩka kĩndũ kĩvatanĩtwe vyũ nĩ Maandĩko? We eĩka kũnthokoa na ngũlũ? Kana twĩkĩte kũmbwa twĩ kĩvathũkany'o?' Ĩkũlyo yĩngĩ ya vata vyũ ũtonya kwĩkũlya nĩ yĩĩ: 'Ndonya kwenda kũmũtutya ũndũnĩ wĩva mũseo wĩkaa?'
Ĩkũlyo yĩu ya mũthya nĩ ya vata. Nĩkĩ? Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii iatĩĩe. Ethĩwa Mũklĩsto ũla ũngĩ nĩ mũneenu naku wĩ mũkilu, kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũtaemawa nĩ kũneena na andũ ĩla wĩ ũtavany'a. Kwoou wĩona ata ũkeka mũvango ũtavany'e nake nĩ kana wĩmanyĩsye o kĩndũ? Kana ethĩwa Mũklĩsto ũla ũngĩ nĩ mũlau mũno kwĩ we, wĩona ata ũkasũanĩa ũtanu ũla ũtonya kũkwata watetheesya ala akũũ, awau, kana me na vata? Kĩla tũũweta nĩ kĩĩ: O na ethĩwa mũmbĩtwe mwĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kĩla ũmwe wenyu asũanĩa ũseo wa ũla ũngĩ, thĩna ũla wĩ katĩ wenyu no ũoleke. Ti lasima mũtume ndũũ ngamu ĩndĩ kĩu no kĩlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yenyu, na no kyongelange mũuo katĩ wenyu na kĩkundinĩ.
Euotia na Sinitike nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa moombĩtwe kĩvathũkany'o kana maĩ na nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya kwĩka maũndũ. Ĩndĩ mũtũmwa Vaulo amesũvie "methĩwe na kĩlilikano kĩmwe nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi." (Avi. 4:2) We no wĩke ũu na no ũtate kũmanthaa mũuo?
NDŨKAEKE THĨNA ŨLA MWĨ NAW'O ŨENDEEE
Ĩia yĩkaekwa kĩvuĩonĩ kya malaa yĩana mũno na yĩyingĩva. O ta ũu, tũkaema kũveta mĩtũkĩ thĩna twĩ naw'o ngoonĩ kwelekela mũndũ ũngĩ, thĩna ũsu wĩkaa kwingĩvĩĩa. Woo wasumbĩka ngoo, thĩna no wĩse kũlika kĩkundinĩ. Ethĩwa nĩtwendete Yeova na ana-a-asa maitũ, tũkatataa ũndũ tũtonya kĩvathũkany'o kĩla twĩ nakyo na mũndũ kĩikese kwananga mũuo wa andũ ma Ngai.
Ĩla twekala nthĩ tũneenee thĩna twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũmantha mũuo, tũtonya kũkwata mosyao maseo tũkavaseng'a. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũũ ũmwe. Easya: "Ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa noonaa aingua ta nĩ kana. Neew'aa thĩna mwingĩ mũno. Na nũndũ wa kũtinda nĩw'ĩte woo, nambĩĩe kũmũneeny'a naĩ. Natavasya ngoo yakwa ũũ, 'Ndanengete ndaĩa ĩla ĩmbaĩle, kwoou o nakwa ndimũnenga ndaĩa.'"
Ĩndĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩwambĩĩe kũsũanĩa ũndũ weekanasya. Easya: "Nambĩĩe kwona mawonzu makwa na noona nĩvĩtĩtye mũno. Nĩvo namanyie kana nĩnaaĩlĩte kũvĩndũa mosũanĩo makwa. Kwoou nĩnavoyie Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu, nathooea mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu ũngĩ kamũthĩnzĩo, na namũandĩkĩa kavalũa nĩmwĩtĩtye ũekeo. Nĩtwakumbatĩanĩie na tweetĩkĩlana kana kĩu nĩkyathela. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu tũyaathokoana ĩngĩ."
Kĩla andũ mekwenda mũno nĩ mũuo. Ĩndĩ aingĩ moo mesa kwona ta meũlikĩlĩĩlwa na kũvũthw'a nĩmaetae ithokoo. Aingĩ mate athaithi ma Yeova mekaa ũu, ĩndĩ Ngũsĩ syake nĩsyĩsĩ kana syaĩle kwĩkalany'a na ngwatanĩo na mũuo. Ngai aveveee Vaulo aandĩka atĩĩ: "Nyie . . . nĩngũmwĩsũva mũendae o ũndũ waĩle wĩtano ũla mweetiwe naw'o, na wĩnyivyo w'onthe na ũuu, na wũmĩĩsyo, mũkyũmĩanĩsya inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo; mũkĩthing'ĩĩsya kũsũvĩa wĩw'ano ũmwe wa Veva wovanonĩ wa mũuo." (Aev. 4:1-3) Kwĩkala twĩ "wovanonĩ wa mũuo" nĩ kĩndũ kya vata mũno. Ame! Nĩtũlũlũmĩlyei mũuo ũla twĩ naw'o na tũitw'a vyũ kũminaa ithokoo ila syaumĩla.
