translation:
JEHOVAH God has made Christ head over everything for the benefit of the congregation. Let us therefore be united in thought and purpose, because unity is something pleasing to Jehovah. We rejoice in being united, and Christ is making his congregation strong. This is why the Christian congregation stands out among people as those who are taught by God and who practice righteousness.
For example, a brother in Madagascar recently showed great zeal when he learned about Jehovah's organization. He told his wife, "Let's go to learn more, and we will serve together." His desire to find out more was strengthened by what he read in the Bible, and he came to appreciate Jehovah, the true God.
Because this man took action, many others each year are joining the Christian congregation and are benefiting from the spiritual food. The Bible warns against "envy and rivalry," which can cause division in the congregation and lead people to act improperly. (Jas. 3:14-16) So the Bible helps us to avoid things that could weaken our spirituality and make us stumble. And if we know about such things, we can also help others who may be struggling.
OTHER THINGS THAT CAN WEAKEN OUR SPIRITUALITY
"I used to associate with a bad companion. I realized that we were influencing each other negatively, so I stopped associating with him."—CHRIS.
"I once felt resentful toward a fellow believer because of something she said. But I prayed about it and realized that I needed to forgive her. It really helped me to feel better."—JANET.
"There was a time when I associated with many people. One of them began to pressure me to do wrong, and I almost gave in. That is why I decided to stop associating with people who do not value Bible principles, and I have been much happier since then."—MICHAEL.
"The congregation is like a family, and there will always be problems. Someone might say something hurtful. But most people are kind and considerate."—GARY.
So do not isolate yourself from the brothers. The Bible shows that some problems can be solved by talking things over, while others require more effort and may take time to resolve. But it is important to remember that fellow believers—both young and old—can benefit from Bible counsel. Do you see how practical Bible advice is?
"Put away abusive speech." (Prov. 45:24) This is what Joseph did when he resisted temptation. And we can do the same! To show love for our neighbor, we need to control our tongue and choose our words carefully, so as not to hurt others. Chris realized that his temper caused him problems. He would often lose his job because of his angry outbursts. So Chris asked Jehovah to help him, and he started studying the Bible with his son. His son encouraged him to apply what he learned, and gradually Chris gained better self-control. Now his son is happy to see that Chris has made progress. It makes him feel good to know that Chris is determined to please Jehovah.
"A listening ear brings wisdom, and a heart open to understanding gives insight." (Prov. 15:22) Janet was very pleased to hear those words! She realized that she needed to be a better listener, especially to her children. Keep practicing, Janet thought, and I will try my best to really listen to my children and understand their feelings. By being a good listener, you can help your children feel loved and understood, and they will be more likely to confide in you. That way, your children will learn to trust you and respect your guidance. She also realized that this would help her to strengthen her relationship with Jehovah.
"So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there at the altar, and go reconcile yourself with your brother first." (Matt. 5:23, 24) It is important to make peace, because Jesus taught that our relationship with God is affected by how we treat others. Michael found it difficult to forgive someone who had wronged him deeply. He felt that he could not simply forget what had been done. But he realized that holding on to anger would only hurt himself. So he decided to try to see things from the other person's perspective. He also prayed for help to forgive his child who had disappointed him greatly. What helped him to succeed? Michael said: "I focused on my child's positive qualities." And that made a difference.
"[Continue] to appeal to each individual, and to show kindness to each one." (Acts 3:12-14) Many people feel insignificant when facing problems they view as too big for them to handle. They may ask themselves: 'How can I possibly make a difference in this world? How can I use my time to support Jehovah's organization and still care for my own needs?' I was encouraged by the example of this publisher and his wife. They were willing to adjust their schedules to help others.
To be compassionate, we need to imitate the attitude described at Colossians 3:12-14 and put it into practice. Many have found it helpful to take the initiative and offer assistance to those who seem to be struggling. To what extent should we go in trying to help our brothers, as illustrated by the account at Matthew 18:15? In that illustration, Jesus explained the steps to take when a fellow believer offends us. The principle here is that we should try to resolve matters peacefully. Perhaps you know of a brother or sister who is having difficulty, and you feel moved to help him or her, but you are unsure how to approach the situation.
So, let us all examine ourselves and see if we are applying Bible principles. If we find that we are lacking, we can pray for "the spirit of meekness and supplication," which includes qualities such as "love, gentleness, humility, mild temper, willingness to forgive, patience, kindness, self-control, peace." (Gal. 5:22, 23) But simply praying for these qualities will not automatically produce them; we must actively work at cultivating them.
IS IT WISE TO BE CONCERNED ABOUT MATERIAL THINGS?
Let us be modest in our thinking, and each one of us should view things realistically. This will help us avoid becoming overly concerned about material possessions. Modesty does not necessarily mean being poor. A young man once expressed his concern to a friend, saying: "I am afraid that I might become too attached to worldly things and forget my spiritual goals. And if I become preoccupied with material pursuits, I fear that I will lose sight of what is truly important." What do you think? It seems that many people today struggle with maintaining a balanced view of material things. However, the apostle Paul wrote: "Whatever you undertake, do it without distractions." (1 Cor. 7:35) So, while there is nothing wrong with working hard to provide for our needs, we must not allow material concerns to consume our thoughts and time. Like John, we should be more interested in helping others than in accumulating wealth. And like Paul, we should be willing to endure hardship rather than compromise our integrity. Are material possessions inherently bad? No, but they can easily distract us from serving Jehovah if we are not careful.
(Matt. 6:24) Therefore, let us examine ourselves regularly to see if our thinking is modest. (Ps. 119:32) And if we find that we are becoming too attached to material things, let us take steps to correct our thinking.
But how can we show love for our brothers and sisters? By following the example of Jesus, who laid down his life for us. (John 13:34, 35; 1 John 5:6-8) Some may ask: "What if someone treats me badly?" Or, "What if someone refuses to listen to my counsel?" Should we respond by saying, 'This young man has done something very wrong according to the Scriptures?' Or, 'He has offended me and my feelings?' Or, 'Should we simply overlook this offense?' Often, the best course of action is to ask oneself: 'Would I want to be forgiven if I had done something similar?'
The reason why it is difficult to forgive others is often because we have difficulty forgiving ourselves. Remember that Christians are imperfect people, and they will sometimes make mistakes. But if you find yourself harboring resentment toward someone, ask yourself whether you have been equally considerate of others. Or, if a Christian brother or sister has wronged you, would you not try to reconcile with him or her? It is important to remember that we all need forgiveness, so let each of us examine himself and strive to be more understanding and compassionate towards others. Do not allow pride or selfishness to hinder your relationships with your brothers and sisters.
Even Satan can disguise himself as an angel of light, making false teachings appear appealing. The apostle Paul wrote: "Be sober, be vigilant." (1 Pet. 4:7) So, do not accept everything you hear without questioning it.
LET US EXAMINE OURSELVES AND BE HONEST WITH EACH OTHER.
It is easy to become discouraged when facing challenges and difficulties. However, we should always remember that Jehovah and his Son Jesus Christ are with us, and they will help us overcome whatever obstacles we face. Let us continue to trust in them and to live our lives in harmony with God's principles.
If we remain humble and teachable, we can learn from our mistakes and grow spiritually. Consider the example of one young man. He said: "I used to think I knew everything. But then I realized how much I still had to learn. And now I am eager to listen to others and to receive their guidance."
This young man also learned the importance of being honest with himself. He said: "I need to examine my own motives and actions carefully. Only then can I identify areas where I need to improve. And I need to pray to Jehovah for strength and wisdom to make the right choices. And I will strive to apply what I learn in my life, so that I may be a better person."
We can strengthen ourselves through prayer and meditation on God's Word. Remember, we are not alone.
Every individual has his own struggles. Many find it difficult to cope with feelings of inadequacy and failure. But those who love Jehovah and seek his guidance can find comfort and hope. The apostle Paul wrote: "You… should not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God; and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus." (Phil. 4:6-8) To be "peaceful" is a great blessing. Truly! Let us cherish the peace that we have and strive to maintain it despite our challenges.

text:
1, 2. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa mũthĩnzĩo wĩthĩwa wĩ wa vata? (b) Nĩkĩ wovosyo nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla wa vata vyũ kuma kwa Ngai?
NĨ MŨTHĨNZĨO wĩva wa vata vyũ waanengwa? Ti lasima mũthĩnzĩo wĩthĩwe wĩ wa thooa mũnene nĩ kana ũtw'ĩke nĩ wa vata. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa mũthĩnzĩo nĩwatuma ũtana kana nĩweanĩsya vata mũnene wĩĩ naw'o, wĩthĩawa wĩ wa vata.
2 Katĩ wa mĩthĩnzĩo yonthe ĩla Ngai ũtũnengete, ve mũthĩnzĩo ũmwe wa vata mũno kwĩ kĩndũ o na kĩva. Nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ kuma kwa Ngai. Kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ nĩtũkwĩmanyĩsya kana Yeova nĩwatũmie Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, nĩ kana tũkwate thayũ ũtathela. (Soma Mathayo 20:28.) Ĩla Yeova wamũtũmie Yesũ kũũ nthĩ nĩ kana ethĩwe wovosyo, nĩwoonanisye kana nũtwendete mũno.
WOVOSYO NĨ KYAŨ?
3. Nĩkĩ andũ makusaa?
3 Wovosyo nĩ nzĩa ya Yeova ya kũtangĩĩa andũ kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ. (Aeveso 1:7) Nĩ kana tũelewe nĩkĩ vaĩ na vata wa wovosyo, nĩtwaĩle kũmanya kĩla kyeekĩkie mũũndanĩ wa Eteni myaka ngili mbingĩ mĩvĩtu. Asyai maitũ ma mbee, Atamu na Eva, nĩmeekie naĩ, na nũndũ wa naĩ ĩsu, nĩmakwie. O naitũ tũkusaa nũndũ Atamu na Eva nĩmatũtiĩe naĩ.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 9.
4. Atamu aumie va, na nĩ kyaũ wanengetwe?
4 Ĩla Yeova woombie mũndũũme wa mbee, Atamu, nĩwamũnengie kĩndũ kya vata mũno. Amũnengie thayũ ũte na naĩ. Aĩ na kĩlĩko kĩanĩu na mwĩĩ ũte na naĩ. Atamu ndesaa kũwaa, kũkũa, kana kũkw'a. Nũndũ Yeova nĩwe wamũmbie Atamu, nĩwe waĩ ĩthe wake. (Luka 3:38) Yeova nĩwaneenaa nake mavinda kwa mavinda. Ngai nĩwamũeleisye Atamu nesa kĩla waaĩle kwĩanĩsya na amũnenga wĩa mũseo wa kũtethya.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:28-30; 2:16, 17.
5. Ĩla Mbivilia ĩkwasya kana Atamu oombĩtwe na "mũvw'ano wa Ngai," yĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a ata?
5 Atamu oombĩtwe na "mũvw'ano wa Ngai." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:27) Yeova amũmbie e na ndaĩa ivw'anene na syake ta wendo, ũĩ, ũsili wa katĩ, na vinya. O na ĩngĩ, Yeova nĩwamũnengie Atamu ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Atamu ndailyĩ ta masinĩ nũndũ Ngai amũmbĩte atonya kwĩnyuvĩa kwĩka kĩla kĩseo kana kĩla kĩthũku. Kethĩwa Atamu nĩwanyuvie kũmwĩw'a Ngai, ethĩwa ekalile tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
6. Atamu aaisye kyaũ ĩla waleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai? Ũndũ ũsu watumie tũkwatwa nĩ kyaũ?
6 Atamu aaisye kĩndũ kya vata mũno ĩla wamũvĩtĩisye Ngai na atw'ĩĩwa kĩkw'ũ. Aaisye ngwatanĩo ya mwanya ĩla waĩ nayo na Yeova, thayũ ũte na naĩ, na alũngw'a mũũndanĩ mũseo vala watwĩe. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:17-19) Atamu na Eva nĩmanyuvie kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai, na kwoou meethĩwa mate na wĩkwatyo. Nũndũ wa kĩla Atamu weekie, "naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ; na kwa ũu kĩkw'ũ kyavikĩa andũ onthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa onthe nĩmeekie naĩ." (Alomi 5:12) Ĩla Atamu weekie naĩ, 'nĩweethooisye' na atũthoosya ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. (Alomi 7:14) Yo ithyĩ twĩ na wĩkwatyo? Ĩĩ, twĩ naw'o.
7, 8. Wovosyo nĩ kyaũ?
7 Wovosyo nĩ kyaũ? Mũno mũno wovosyo wonanasya maũndũ elĩ. Ũndũ wa mbee, wovosyo nĩ kĩla kĩĩvawa nĩ kana mũndũ athaw'e kana kĩndũ kĩĩtavĩtwe kĩtũngwe. Ũndũ wa kelĩ, wovosyo nĩ kĩla kyumaw'a nĩ kana kĩĩvĩe wanangĩko ũla ũetetwe nĩ kĩndũ kĩngĩ.
8 Vai mũndũ waĩ atonya kũĩvĩa kĩla Atamu waaisye ĩla wamũvĩtĩisye Ngai na atuma tũkwatwa nĩ kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwaumĩlilye nzĩa ya kũtũtangĩĩa kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ. Ekai twĩmanyĩsye ũndũ nthembo ya wovosyo ĩthũkũmaa na ũndũ ĩtonya kũtũtethya.
KĨLA YEOVA WEEKIE NĨ KANA OVOSYE ANDŨ
9. Wovosyo ũla wendekaa nĩ wĩva?
9 Vai ũmwe witũ waĩ atonya kumya wovosyo nĩ kana tũtũngĩwe thayũ ũte na naĩ ũla Atamu waaisye. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ithyonthe twĩ na naĩ. (Savuli 49:7, 8) Wovosyo ũla wendekaa nĩ thayũ wa mũndũ ũngĩ ũte na naĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yesũ eenenganie "ethĩwe mbovosya ya andũ onthe." (1 Timotheo 2:6) Kwoou, thayũ ũte na naĩ ũla Yesũ waumisye waĩ na thooa wĩanene na thayũ ũla Atamu waaisye.
10. Yeova eekie ata nĩ kana atwovosye?
10 Yeova eekie ata nĩ kana atwovosye? Atũmie Mwana wake mwendwa kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Mwana ũsu, ũla nĩ Yesũ, nĩwe waĩ wa mbee kũmbwa nĩ Ngai. (1 Yoana 4:9, 10) Yesũ nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kũmũtia Ĩthe wake na kũtia wĩkalo wake wa ĩtunĩ. (Avilivi 2:7) Yeova nĩwathamisye thayũ wa Yesũ kuma ĩtunĩ nginya kũũ nthĩ, na Yesũ asyawa e mũndũ ũte na naĩ.—Luka 1:35.
11. Vatonyekie ata mũndũ ũmwe eethĩwa wovosyo kwondũ wa andũ aingĩ?
11 Ĩla mũndũũme wa mbee Atamu wamũvĩtĩisye Yeova, atumie andũ onthe methĩwa na naĩ. Yo ve mũndũ waĩ atonya kũvetea nzyawa syonthe sya Atamu kĩkw'ũ? Ĩĩ. (Soma Alomi 5:19.) Yesũ ndaĩ na naĩ, na kwoou nĩwaumisye thayũ wake wĩthĩwe wovosyo. (1 Akolintho 15:45) Thayũ wake ũte na naĩ waĩ ũtonya kũtũmĩwa kũvetea nzyawa syonthe sya Atamu kĩkw'ũ.—1 Akolintho 15:21, 22.
12. Nĩkĩ yaĩ no nginya Yesũ athĩnw'e mũno?
12 Mbivilia nĩyĩeleetye ũndũ Yesũ wathĩniw'e atanakw'a. Nĩwavũiwe mũno, aathĩĩwa mũtĩnĩ, na akw'a kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo mũno. (Yoana 19:1, 16-18, 30) Nĩkĩ yaĩ no nginya Yesũ athĩnw'e mũno wĩana ũu? Nũndũ Satani oonanisye kana vai mũndũ ũtonya kũendeea kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai e thĩnanĩ mwingĩ. Yesũ nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana mũndũ ũte na naĩ nũtonya kũendeea kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai o na e thĩnanĩ wingĩvĩte ata. No nginya Yeova ethĩwe atanĩthiw'e mũno nĩ ũndũ ũsu Yesũ weekie!—Nthimo 27:11; soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 15.
13. Yesũ eekie ata asyoka ĩtunĩ?
13 Kwĩ matukũ 14 ma mwei wa Ayuti wĩtawa Nisani, mwaka wa 33, Yeova nĩweetĩkĩlile Yesũ oawe nĩ amaitha make. (Aevelania 10:10) Mĩthenya ĩtatũ kuma Yesũ akw'a, Yeova nĩwamũthayũũkisye e na mwĩĩ wa veva. Athayũũkw'a, Yesũ nĩwasyokie ĩtunĩ na athi mbee wa Ĩthe wake akaĩvĩe naĩ sitũ. Na Ĩthe wake nĩweetĩkĩlile thayũ ũla Yesũ waumisye kwondũ witũ wĩthĩwe ndĩvi. (Aevelania 9:24) Kwa kwĩka ũu, Yesũ nĩwatũthaisye kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ.—Soma Alomi 3:23, 24.
WOVOSYO ŨTONYA KŨTŨTETHYA ATA?
14, 15. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũekewe naĩ sitũ?
14 O na ũmũnthĩ nĩtũtethekaa nĩ mũthĩnzĩo ũsu mũnene kuma kwa Ngai. Ekai twone ũndũ tũtethekaa ũmũnthĩ na ũndũ tũkatetheka ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte.
15 Nĩtũekeawa naĩ. Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩka kĩla kyaĩle mavinda onthe. Nĩtũvĩtasya, na mavinda amwe nĩtũneenaa kana tũkeka ũndũ ũtaĩle. (Akolosai 1:13, 14) Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũekewe? Nĩtwaĩle kwĩlila kuma ngoonĩ nũndũ wa kĩla twĩkĩte na tũimwĩsũva Yeova atũekee. Tweeka ũu, nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana nĩtũkũekewa naĩ sitũ.—1 Yoana 1:8, 9.
16. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo?
16 Nĩtwĩthĩawa na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo. Ĩla wasya witũ wa ngoo watũtavya kana nĩtwĩkĩte ũndũ mũthũku, nĩtwĩw'aa tũte eanĩe na no twĩw'e tũte vata. Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kũkw'a ngoo. Twamwĩsũva Yeova atũekee, no twĩthĩwe tũte na nzika kana nũkũtwĩthukĩĩsya na aitũekea. (Aevelania 9:13, 14) Yeova endaa tũmũtavasye thĩna kana wonzu o na wĩva ũla twĩ naw'o. (Aevelania 4:14-16) Na tweeka ũu, tũkeethĩawa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai.
17. Nĩ moathimo meva tũtonya kũkwata nũndũ Yesũ nĩwakwie kwondũ witũ?
17 Twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ; ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ." (Alomi 6:23) Nũndũ Yesũ nĩwakwie kwondũ witũ, twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene na tũitanĩa kwĩthĩwa tũte na thĩna o na ũmwe wa mwĩĩ. (Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4) Ĩndĩ twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũkwate moathimo asu?
WE NŨKWĨTĨKĨLA WOVOSYO?
18. Twĩsĩ ata kana Yeova nũtwendete?
18 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ wĩw'aa mũyo ĩla mũndũ waũnenga mũthĩnzĩo mũseo. Wovosyo nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla wa vata vyũ, na nĩtwaĩle kũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea mũno nũndũ waw'o. Ĩandĩko ya Yoana 3:16 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ Ngai nĩwendete nthĩ, nĩwanenganie Mwana wake e ũmwe." Yeova nũtwendete mũno na nĩkyo kĩtumi wanenganie Mwana wake mwendwa, Yesũ, kwondũ witũ. Na nĩtwĩsĩ kana o nake Yesũ nũtwendete nũndũ nĩweeyumisye akw'a kwondũ witũ. (Yoana 15:13) Kwoou mũthĩnzĩo wa wovosyo nĩwaĩle ũkũĩkĩĩthya vyũ kana Yeova na Yesũ nĩmakwendete mũno.—Akalatia 2:20.
19, 20. (a) Ũtonya kũtw'ĩka mũnyanya wa Yeova ata? (b) Ũtonya kwonany'a ata kana wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ya wovosyo ya Yesũ?
19 Nũndũ yu nĩwamanya ũndũ Yeova ũtwendete mũno wĩana, ũtonya kũtw'ĩka mũnyanyae ata? Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwenda mũndũ ũtamwĩsĩ. Ĩandĩko ya Yoana 17:3 yonanĩtye kana nĩtũtonya kũmũmanya Yeova. O ũndũ ũendeee kũmũmanya, ũkaendeea kũmwenda mũnango, ũkeethĩawa ũyenda kũmwendeesya, na ũitw'ĩka mũnyanyae. Kwoou, endeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nĩ kana ũmũmanye Yeova mũnango.—1 Yoana 5:3.
20 Ĩtĩkĩla nthembo ya wovosyo ya Yesũ. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa [kana, ũmũĩkĩĩaa] ũ Mwana e na thayũ ũtathela." (Yoana 3:36) Kũmũĩkĩĩa Mwana nĩ kwĩka ata? Nĩ kwĩka kyonthe kĩla Yesũ ũtwĩĩte twĩke. (Yoana 13:15) Tũyaĩle o kwasya kana nĩtũmũĩkĩĩe Yesũ. Ve ũndũ twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana twonany'e kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa wovosyo. Ĩandĩko ya Yakovo 2:26 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũĩkĩĩo ũte na meko nĩ mũkw'ũ."
21, 22. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũendaa ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto kĩla mwaka? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ kĩlungunĩ kya 6 na kya 7?
21 Endaa ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto. Ũtukũ wa mũthya Yesũ atanakw'a, nĩwawetie kana twaĩle kũlilikanaa kĩkw'ũ kyake. Twĩkaa ũu kĩla mwaka, na mũvango ũsu wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ wĩtawa "kyaũya kya wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi." (1 Akolintho 11:20, NWT; Mathayo 26:26-28) Yesũ nĩwendaa tũlilikanae kana nĩwaumisye thayũ wake wĩthĩwe wovosyo kwondũ witũ. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩkaai ũu ũndũ wa kũndilikana." (Soma Luka 22:19.) Ĩla twathi ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtũlilikene wovosyo, na ũndũ Yeova na Yesũ matwendete mũno wĩana.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 16.
22 Wovosyo nĩw'o mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũnene vyũ twaakwata. (2 Akolintho 9:14, 15) O na mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa vata ũkatethya andũ milioni mbingĩ ala makwie. Nĩtũkwĩmanyĩsya ũndũ makatetheka kĩlungunĩ kya 6 na kya 7.

translation:
1, 2. (a) What causes sincere Christians to be zealous in their ministry? (b) Why is zeal important when it comes to pleasing God?
IS CHRISTIAN ZEAL commendable? Certainly zeal is praiseworthy, but it should not overshadow our desire to please God. Otherwise, zeal might lead us to pursue goals that are not truly important or to compromise on principles.
2 Of all the qualities that God values, zeal stands out as being particularly vital. It is what motivates us to do our best in serving God. For example, we show our zeal when we eagerly share the good news with others. (Read Matthew 20:28.) Because Jehovah sent his Son, Jesus Christ, to earth so that we could gain everlasting life, we are motivated to demonstrate our gratitude by zealously supporting him.
WHY IS ZEAL IMPORTANT?
3. What will we discuss?
3 Zeal is an expression of Jehovah's love for obedient people. (Ephesians 1:7) To appreciate why zeal is so important, we need to understand its origin and how it has been displayed throughout history. Loyal humans like Adam and Eve initially demonstrated zeal, but they later lost it. So let us examine the example of Adam and Eve—Read Genesis chapter 9.
4. What did Adam have, and why was he blessed?
4 Jehovah generously blessed perfect man, Adam, with abundant opportunities. He blessed him with a beautiful home and meaningful work. He gave him the prospect of living forever. Adam had no inclination to disobey or to question Jehovah's authority. Jehovah was his Creator, and Adam appreciated this fact. (Luke 3:38) Jehovah dealt with Adam directly and showed him kindness. God explained to Adam what was required of him to maintain a close relationship with Him.—Genesis 1:28-30; 2:16, 17.
5. How does the Bible explain that Adam was created with "the image of God," and what does this mean?
5 Adam was created with "the image of God." (Genesis 1:27) Jehovah endowed him with qualities reflecting those of His personality, such as love, justice, and wisdom. Also, Jehovah granted Adam the capacity to think and reason. Adam could make decisions, and God allowed him to exercise free will. However, Adam realized that his perfection depended on maintaining a close relationship with God. Otherwise, he would gradually lose his likeness to God, becoming imperfect in every way.
6. What mistake did Adam make, and what lesson can we learn from it?
6 Adam made the mistake of giving importance to what someone else said about God's command and disobeying it. He valued the approval of another creature more than his standing with Jehovah, and he let desire influence his decision. (Genesis 3:17-19) Adam and Eve chose to please themselves rather than pleasing God, and this had serious consequences. To this day, each human says, "I did what was wrong in my own eyes, and I disregarded your law; and because of this wrongdoing, all mankind has inherited sin and imperfection." (Romans 5:12) But Adam also blamed others, saying, "The woman you gave me made me do it," and tried to shift responsibility onto her. (Romans 7:14) Why is this relevant to us? Because we are inclined to do the same.
7, 8. What is selfishness?
7 What is selfishness? Selfishness involves putting one's own desires first. In some cases, it means doing something harmful to oneself or to others to get what one wants. In other cases, it means being preoccupied with one's own interests and disregarding the needs of others.
8 It is easy to see how Adam's selfish act led to our present difficulties and brought guilt upon us. We are grateful that Jehovah provides an opportunity for us to recover from the effects of that selfishness. Let us examine why selfishness is so dangerous and what it can lead to.
SELFISHNESS IS WHAT LED TO THE FALL OF MAN
9. Where does selfishness originate?
9 Can anyone completely avoid selfishness, even when faced with temptation like Adam was? No. The Bible shows that all humans are imperfect. (Psalm 49:7, 8) Selfishness is inherent in humankind. As Jesus explained, "From inside people come forth wicked thoughts." (1 Timothy 2:6) Therefore, the tendency toward selfishness is greater in us than it was in Adam.
10. Does Jehovah care whether we are selfish?
10 Does Jehovah care whether we are selfish? He showed his love for us by sending his Son. That Son, Jesus, was perfect as a man. (1 John 4:9, 10) Jesus willingly offered himself as a ransom and demonstrated obedience to God's law. (Hebrews 2:7) Jehovah accepted Jesus' sacrifice as a means of rescuing mankind from sin, and Jesus proved to be a perfect human.—Luke 1:35.
11. Can a perfect man redeem many people?
11 But if one perfect man, Adam, could bring about such widespread ruin, can one perfect man undo the damage? No. (Read Romans 5:19.) Jesus himself said that he would give his life as a ransom. (1 Corinthians 15:45) His perfect life can thus pay off the penalty for Adam's sin for all mankind.—1 Corinthians 15:21, 22.
12. Why, then, did Jesus need to die?
12 The Bible explains why Jesus had to die. He was tortured, impaled on a stake, and died. (John 19:1, 16-18, 30) Why, though, did Jesus have to suffer such a brutal death? Because Satan challenged whether anyone could remain loyal to God under trial. Jesus proved that a perfect man could remain faithful to God even under great pressure. And because Jehovah loves righteousness, he approved of what Jesus did!—Proverbs 27:11; read The Watchtower article "Is Death Truly the End?" No. 15.
13. Will Jesus ever leave heaven?
13 On Nisan 14, 33 C.E., Jehovah allowed Jesus to give his life as a ransom. (Hebrews 10:10) Three days later, after Jesus died, Jehovah resurrected him in spirit form. As a spirit, Jesus was able to give perfect direction to his followers and strengthen them. And Jehovah allowed this so that Jesus could carry out the work he promised to do for us. (Hebrews 9:24) In this way, Jesus showed us that we can have hope.—Read Romans 3:23, 24.
WHAT CAN HELP YOU STAY LOYAL?
14, 15. What can we do to stay loyal?
14 We need to appreciate fully how much God loves us. Let us examine what we believe and how we live our lives.
15 Be honest with yourself. Is there something you know is wrong but continue doing? We may be tempted, and sometimes we may stumble. (Colossians 1:13, 14) What can we do to stay loyal? We can pray regularly and ask Jehovah to help us. By doing so, we will be more likely to resist temptation and remain loyal.—1 John 1:8, 9.
16. What can we do if we feel guilty about something we have done?
16 We all make mistakes. But our loving Father will forgive us if we confess our sins, and he will help us to correct our wrongdoing. So do not hesitate to ask for forgiveness. Ask Jehovah to help you, and he will comfort you and cleanse you from sin.—Hebrews 9:13, 14. Jehovah wants to restore us, even when we have seriously sinned. (Hebrews 4:14-16) And when we do, we enjoy a closer relationship with God.
17. How can we benefit from remembering what Jesus did for us?
17 We should never forget what Jesus sacrificed for us. The Bible says: "The wages sin pays is death, but the gift God gives is everlasting life through Christ Jesus our Lord." (Romans 6:23) Because of what Jesus did for us, we have hope of eternal life and the opportunity to please God further. (Revelation 21:3, 4) So how can we show that we appreciate this generous gift?
DO WE APPRECIATE THE GIFT OF SALVATION?
18. Does Jehovah really care for us personally?
18 Absolutely! He loves each of us deeply. Salvation is a precious gift, and we need to thank Jehovah sincerely for his love. The scripture at John 3:16 states: "For God loved the world so much that he gave his only-begotten Son." Jehovah cares for us very much, and that is why he sent his beloved Son, Jesus, to die for us. And we can be sure that Jesus also cares for us because he willingly gave his life for us. (John 15:13) This great gift of salvation shows just how much Jehovah and Jesus care for us.—Acts 2:20.
19, 20. (a) How can we deepen our appreciation for Jehovah? (b) How can we make sure that we have genuine faith in the sacrifice of Jesus?
19 Since you know how much Jehovah loves you, how can you deepen your appreciation for him? It takes effort, just like getting to know someone well. The scripture at John 17:3 tells us that knowing Jehovah is an ongoing process. As you continue to learn about him, you will love him more, you will want to obey him, and you will feel closer to him. Therefore, keep studying the Bible so that you may come to know Jehovah better.—1 John 5:3.
20 Show faith in the sacrifice of Jesus. The Bible says that "the one who exercises faith in [or puts trust in] the Son has everlasting life." (John 3:36) What does it mean to exercise faith in the Son? It means doing everything Jesus asks us to do. (John 13:15) We must not take our faith for granted. What we need to do is demonstrate that we have genuine faith in the provision for salvation. The scripture at James 2:26 states: "Faith without works is dead."
21, 22. (a) Why should we remember Christ's death each year? (b) What will we discuss in paragraphs 6 and 7?
21 Remember Christ's death. On the night Jesus died, he instituted the Memorial. We observe this each year, and this annual observance of Jesus' death is called "the Lord's Evening Meal." (1 Corinthians 11:20, NWT; Matthew 26:26-28) Jesus wants us to remember his sacrifice because he gave his perfect human life as a ransom for us. He said: "Keep doing this in remembrance of me." (Read Luke 22:19.) By observing the Memorial, we show that we appreciate the value of the ransom, and Jehovah and Jesus are pleased with what we do.—Read the section titled "What Does This Mean?" on page 16.
22 The ransom is a precious gift that we have received. (2 Corinthians 9:14, 15) And this precious gift benefits millions of people around the world. We will now see how it affects paragraphs 6 and 7.

text:
Twĩsĩ ata kana kwa w'o ũthayũũkyo ũkeethĩwa?
Yeova e na mea ma kũthayũũkya akw'ũ?
Naaũ ala makathayũũkw'a?
1-3. Nĩ mũmaitha wĩva ũtũatĩĩe ithyonthe, na nĩkĩ kũmanya ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya nĩkũtũnengae wĩkwatyo?
KWASŨANĨA nũsembete ũkĩĩte mũmaitha mũthũku vyũ. E na vinya na ndũmũtia. Nĩwĩsĩ nde tei nũndũ nĩwonete ayũaa anyanyau. O ũndũ ũsembete, now'o ũkũthengee. Ĩndĩ ũte na wĩkwatyo, vayumĩla mũndũ ũtonya kũũvonokya. E na vinya kũvĩtũka mũmaitha waku, na nĩwĩyumĩtye kũũtetheesya. Wĩw'a wakiakiw'a mũno!
2 Nũatĩĩwe nĩ mũmaitha ta ũsu. Ithyonthe nĩtũatĩĩwe nĩ mũmaitha ũsu. O ta ũndũ tũneemanyĩisye Kĩlungunĩ kya 6, Mbivilia yĩtĩte kĩkw'ũ mũmaitha. Vaiĩ mũndũ ũtonya kũsiĩĩa kĩkw'ũ kana kũkĩveta. Nĩtwonete mũmaitha ũsu ayũaa endwa maitũ. Ĩndĩ Yeova e vinya kũvĩtũka kĩkw'ũ. Nĩ Mũvonokya wĩ wendo ũla ũminĩte kwonany'a e ũtonyi wa kũsinda kĩkw'ũ. Nĩwathanĩte kũvetanga kĩkw'ũ tene na tene. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya: "Mũmaitha wa mũminũkĩlyo ũla ũkanangwa nĩ kĩkw'ũ." (1 Akolintho 15:26) Ũsu nĩ ũvoo mũseo!
3 Eka tũsũanĩe ũndũ twĩw'aa yĩla mwendwa witũ wakw'a. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũũtũtetheesya kũelewa ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya ũtũtanĩthya. Yeova nĩwathanĩte kana akw'ũ makathayũũka. (Isaia 26:19) Makeethĩwa thayũ ĩngĩ. Kwoou ve wĩkwatyo wa ũthayũũkyo.
YĨLA MWENDWA WAKW'A
4. (a) Nĩkĩ ũndũ Yesũ weewie Lasalo akw'a ũtũmanyĩasya ũndũ Yeova wĩw'aa twakw'ĩĩwa? (b) Yesũ endete mũno aaũ?
4 Waakw'ĩĩwa nĩ mwendwa waku? Kũmĩĩsya kwĩthĩawa kwĩ vinya nũndũ wa woo ũla wĩw'aa. Yĩla twĩ ĩvindanĩ yũmũ ta yĩu, nĩtwaĩle kũmantha ũkiakisyo Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. (2 Akolintho 1:
5, 6. (a) Yesũ eekie ata yĩla waĩ na andũ ma mũsyĩ ma Lasalo maimeta? (b) Nĩkĩ kwĩw'a woo vevanĩ kwa Yesũ nĩkũtwĩkĩaa vinya?
5 Yesũ eewie ata akw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũnyanyae? Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte Yesũ nĩwaendie mũsyĩ kwa andũ maa Lasalo na eethwa vamwe namo na anyanyae maimeta. Amona nĩweewie tei, na "eew'a woo vevanĩ, na aũũya." Na ĩngĩ Mbivilia yĩtwĩa, 'Yesũ nĩwaĩie.'(Yoana 11:
6 Kyeva kya Yesũ nĩkĩtwĩkĩaa vinya. Kũtũmanyĩasya kana Yeova na Yesũ nĩmamenete kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ Yeova e ũtonyi wa ũmina kĩkw'ũ! Nĩtũkwona ũndũ Ngai wamũtonyethisye Yesũ kwĩka.
"LASALO, UMAALA"
7, 8. Ĩtina wa Lasalo kũkw'a nĩkĩ andũ moonaa vate wĩkwatyo, ĩndĩ Yesũ eekie ata?
7 Lasalo athikĩtwe ngunganĩ na Yesũ asya ĩvia yĩla yamĩvingĩte yĩvetangwe. Matha nĩwaleile nũndũ mĩthenya 4 yaĩ mĩvĩtu kuma Lasalo akw'a, na mwĩĩ wake no nginya wĩthĩwe wanyungaa. (Yoana 11:39) Kwosana na mawoni ma mũndũ, vayaĩ wĩkwatyo o na ũmwe.
8 Ĩvia yĩu nĩyavetangiwe na Yesũ aneena na wasya mũnene asya: "Lasalo, umaala." Kweekĩkie ata? 'Ũla waĩ mũkw'ũ nĩwaumaalile.' (Yoana 11:
9, 10. (a) Yesũ oonanisye ata vala waumĩtye vinya wa kũthayũũkya Lasalo? (b) Kũmanya ũvoo ũsu wa Mbivilia ĩũlũ wa ũthayũũkyo kũtonya ũtũtethya ata?
9 Yesũ ndaaasya kana eekie kyama kĩu na vinya wake. Mboyanĩ yake atanamwĩta Lasalo, nĩwoonanisye nesa kana Yeova nĩwe wamũnengie vinya ũsu wa kũmũthayũũkya. (Yoana 11:
10 Andũ ala Yesũ wathayũũkisye nĩmakwie ĩngĩ. Ũu nĩkwonany'a kana ndwaĩ ũndũ wa vata kũmathayũũkya? Ũu ti w'o. Ũvoo ũsu wa Mbivilia nũĩkĩĩthasya ũw'o wa vata ũmanyĩĩtw'e Mbivilianĩ na nũtũnengae wĩkwatyo.
KWĨMANYĨSYA KUMANA NA ŨVOO WA ŨTHAYŨŨKYO
11. Kũthaayũũkw'a kwa Lasalo kũĩkĩĩthasya ata ũndũ Mũtavan'ya 9:5 yaasya?
11 Mbivilia ĩtũmanyĩasya kana akw'ũ "matyĩsĩ ũndũ o na wĩva." Maithayũ na mai vandũ maĩ matonya kwĩwa ũndũ. Kũthaayũũkw'a kwa Lasalo nĩkũĩkĩĩthĩtye ũw'o ũsu. Yĩla Lasalo wathayũũkiw'e, we aaelesya andũ ĩũlũ wa ĩtunĩ? Kana akamatelemya kwa ngewa ya ĩia ya mwaki? Aiee, ndaaĩka ũu nũndũ Mbivilia ndĩwetete maũndũ asu. Mĩthenya ĩna yĩla waĩ mũkw'ũ, 'ndeesĩ ũndũ o na wĩva.' (Mũtavan'ya 9:5) Lasalo nĩwakomete kĩkw'ũnĩ.
12. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũĩkĩĩthya kana kwa w'o Lasalo nĩwathayũũkiw'e?
12 Kũthaayũũkw'a kwa Lasalo kũtũmanyĩasya kana ũthayũũkyo nĩ ũndũ wa w'o ĩndĩ ti wano. Yesũ athayũũkisye Lasalo andũ aingĩ mene. O na atongoi ma ndĩni ala mamũmenete Yesũ mayaakaĩa kyama kyu. Ĩndĩ maisye: "Twĩĩka ata? nũndũ mũndũ ũũ [Yesũ] ekaa syama mbingĩ? " (Yoana 11:47) Andũ aingĩ nĩmaendie kũmwona Lasalo athayũũkw'a. Na aingĩ moo nĩmamũĩkĩĩie Yesũ. Nũndũ wa kũthayũũkya Lasalo andũ asu nĩmoonie ũĩkĩĩthyo kana Yesũ atũmĩtwe nĩ Ngai. Ũĩkĩĩthyo ũsu waĩ mũlũmu nginya watuma atongoi ma ndĩni ya Ayuti ala maĩ na ngoo nyũmũ matw'a kũaa Yesũ na Lasalo.
13. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũĩkĩĩa kana Yeova kwa w'o akathayũũkya akw'ũ?
13 Kwĩtĩkĩla kana kwĩ ũthayũũkyo nĩ ũndũ ũtatonyeka? Ti ũndũ ũtatonyeka nũndũ Yesũ amanyĩisye kana "onthe ala me mbũanĩ" makathayũũkw'a. (Yoana 5:28) Yeova nĩwe Mũmbi wa syĩndũ syonthe syĩ thayũ. Nĩwĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ ũtatonyeka kwake kũmatũnga thayũ andũ ala makwie? Wĩkwatyo wĩvo nũndũ wa kĩlilikano kya Yeova. Yeova nũtonya kũlilikana endwa maitũ ala makwie? Matunĩ kwĩ Ndata itatalĩka ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwĩsĩ syĩtwa ya kĩla ĩmwe! (Isaia 40:26) Kwoou Yeova Ngai nũtonya kũlilikana endwa maitũ ala makwie na maũndũ onthe ĩũlũ wamo, na e na ũtonyi wa kũmathayũũkya.
14, 15. Kwĩanana na ũndũ Yovu waisye, nĩ kyaũ kĩkwonany'a kana Yeova e na mea ma kũthayũũkya andũ?
14 Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Yeova e na mea ma kũthayũũkya akw'ũ. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kũĩkĩĩa ũu? Yovu ũla waĩ mũlũngalu akũlilye atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa mũndũ akakw'a, akeethĩwa thayũ ĩngĩ? " Yovu aneeneaa ĩũlũ wa kweteela mbũanĩ kũvikĩa Ngai amũlilikane. Amwĩie Yeova: 'Naku ũkeetana, nakwa ngakwĩtĩka: Ũkeethĩwa na mea ma wĩa wa moko maku.'
15 Kwasũanĩa! Yeova e na mea mũno ma kũthayũũkya andũ. Nĩ ũndũ wa ũtanu kũmanya Yeova e na mea asu. Ĩndĩ nata ĩũlũ wa ũthayũũkyo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte? Naaũ makathayũũkw'a, na makathayũũkw'a kuma va?
"ONTHE ALA ME MBŨANĨ"
16. Akw'ũ makathayũũkw'a mekale nthĩ ĩilye ata?
16 Ũthayũũkyo ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ ũtũmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa ũthayũũkyo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Andũ ala mathayũũkiw'e kũũ nthĩ nĩmasyokeanĩie na endwa moo. Ũthayũũkyo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte ũkeethĩwa ũvw'anene na ũsu ĩndĩ wĩ mũseango. O tondũ tweemanyĩisye Kĩlungunĩ kya 3, kĩeleelo kya Ngai nĩ nthĩ yonthe ĩtw'ĩke valatiso. Kwoou akw'ũ maikathayũũkw'a nthĩ yĩ kaũ, ũng'endilĩ kana ũwau. Makeethĩwa matonya kwĩkala tene na tene kũũ nthĩ me na mũuo na ũtanu.
17. Ala methayũũkw'a makeethĩwa meana ata?
17 Naaũ makathayũũkw'a? Yesũ aisye 'onthe ala me mbũanĩ makew'a wasya wake, namo makauma.' (Yoana 5:
18. "Ala alũngalu" methayũũkw'a nĩ meva, na wĩkwatyo ũsu ũtonya kũũtethya ata?
18 Aingĩ "ala alũngalu" makathayũũkw'a nĩ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ maĩ thayũ mbee wa Yesũ atanoka kũũ nthĩ. Amwe nĩ ta Noa, Avalaamu, Sala, Mose, Esita, na angĩ aingĩ. Aũme na aka asu maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nĩ mawetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Aevelania kĩlungu kya 11. Angĩ "ala alũngalu" nĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova ala makusaa ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ. Kũmanya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa kĩkw'ũ nĩkũtũthaasya kumana na w'ĩa wa kũkw'a.
19. Nĩ aaũ ala "mate alũngalu," na Yeova kwa ũseo wake amanengete mwanya wa kwĩka ata?
19 Kũkeethĩwa ata kwa andũ onthe ala mataamũthaitha Yeova nĩkwĩthĩwa mayamwĩsĩ? Andũ asu mbilioni mbingĩ "mate alũngalu" maikola. O namo makathayũũkw'a na mainengwa mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai ũla wa w'o na kũmũthaitha. Nthĩnĩ wa ĩvinda ya myaka 1,000 akw'ũ makathayũũkw'a na maithaithaa Yeova vamwe na andũ ala angĩ aĩkĩĩku kũũ nthĩ. Ĩkeethĩwa ĩvinda ya ũtanu. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩyo yĩtawa Mũthenya wa Sila Mbivilianĩ. *
20. Ngĩena nĩ kyaũ, na nĩ andũ meva ala maendaa vau?
20 Ũu nĩkwonanay'a kana andũ onthe ala makwie makathayũũkw'a? Ũu tiw'o, nũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye akw'ũ amwe me "Ngienanĩ." (Luka 12:5) Syĩtwa yu Ngiena yaumanie na ĩima ya mavuti yĩla yaĩ nza wa Yelusaleme ya tene. Mavuti na andũ ala makw'a mavĩvĩaw'a ĩimanĩ yĩu yeetawa Ngiena. Andũ ala makusaa na mayĩkw'a vau moonekaa nĩ Ayuti mataĩle kũthikwa na kũthayũũkw'a. Kwoou Ngiena nĩ wonany'o waĩle wa kwanangwa vyũ ũtakoneka ĩngĩ tene na tene. O na kau Yesũ nũnengetwe mwĩao wa kũsilĩla ala me thayũ na akw'ũ, Yeova nĩwe Mũsili wa mũthya. (Meko ma Atũmwa 10:42) Ndakathayũũkya ala ũsilĩlĩte na kũmatw'ĩĩa kwĩthĩwa athũku na matekwenda kũalyũka.
ŨTHAYŨŨKYO WA ĨTUNĨ
21, 22. (a) Nĩ ũthayũũkyo ũngĩ wĩva ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ? (b) Nũũ wa mbee weethĩiwe na ũthayũũkyo wa veva?
21 Mbivilia nĩwetete ĩũlũ wa ũthayũũkyo ũngĩ wa kũthayũũkw'a na mwĩĩ wa veva na kũthi ĩtunĩ. No ngelekany'o ĩmwe ya ũthayũũkyo ũsu ĩnenganĩtwe Mbivilianĩ nayo nĩ ũthayũũkyo wa Yesũ.
22 Yĩla Yesũ wooaiwe e mũndũ mũĩkĩĩku, Yeova ndaamũeka Mwana ũsu Wake ekale mbũanĩ. (Savuli 16:10; Meko ma Atũmwa 13:
23, 24. "Ĩĩthya ĩnini" ya Yesũ naaũ, na meana ata?
23 Nũndũ Yesũ nĩweesĩ akasyoka ĩtunĩ, nĩweeie amanyĩw'a make kana 'akamaseũvĩsya vandũ' kũu ĩtunĩ. (Yoana 14:2) Yesũ ametie ala makathi ĩtunĩ "ĩĩthya ĩnini" yake. (Luka 12:32) Nĩ andũ meana me nthĩnĩ wa ĩĩthya yĩu ĩnini ya Aklĩsto aĩkĩĩku? Kwĩanana na ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo 14:
24 Aklĩsto asu 144,000, o vamwe na atũmwa aĩkĩĩku ma Yesũ, mathayũũkaw'a na maithi ĩtunĩ. Ũthayũũkyo woo wambĩĩaa ĩndĩĩ? Mũtũmwa Vaulo andĩkie waĩ wambĩĩe ĩvinda ya kũka, kana kwĩthĩwa vo kwa Klĩsto. (1 Akolintho 15:23) O ta ũndũ ũkemanyĩsya Kĩlungunĩ kya 9, yu twĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Kwoou ala matiele ma andũ asu 144,000, ala makusaa ũmũnthĩ, mathayũũkaw'a vate kweteela. (1 Akolintho 15:
25. Tũkeemanyĩsya kyaũ Kĩlungunĩ kya 8?
25 Yeova akasinda kĩkw'ũ, mũmaitha witũ vyũ, na kĩikethwa vo ĩngĩ! (Isaia 25:8) Ĩndĩ, ala makathayũũkw'a kũthi ĩtunĩ, makathi kwĩka ata kũu? Makatw'ĩka asumbĩ Ũsumbĩnĩ wa ĩtu. Tũkeemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũsumbĩ usu Kĩlungunĩ kya 8.

translation:
Are you ever bothered by what others say?
Does Jehovah care how we feel?
Why is it important to be courageous?
1-3. It is normal to get upset, and it is good to understand why the Bible gives this advice.
BE ASSURED that feeling bad is normal. It happens to everyone. It doesn't mean you are weak. But when you feel bad, don't let it control you. If you let it, you might become discouraged. It can also make it hard to deal with problems, and you may end up feeling sorry for yourself. Don't let that happen!
2 We should be honest about our feelings. Everyone gets upset sometimes. The Bible says that being emotional is okay. No one should feel ashamed or embarrassed about their feelings. We need to be honest about our feelings so that Jehovah can help us. He is a caring God who understands our difficulties. He wants to help us cope with them. The Bible says: "The heartfelt grief of the upright is pleasing to him." (1 Corinthians 15:26) That is comforting!
3 Let us discuss how we can remain courageous. One way is to try to understand why we get upset. Jehovah understands how we feel. (Isaiah 26:19) He will give us strength. Focus on what you *can* do.
HOW TO REMAIN COURAGEOUS
4. (a) What did Jesus tell Lazarus that shows how Jehovah feels about us? (b) How did Jesus show courage?
4 Are you encouraged by knowing that Jehovah cares for you? To remind yourself of this, take time to think about his love for you. When we face trials, we can find comfort in God's promise. (2 Corinthians 1:
5, 6. (a) Did Jesus ever feel sorry for people like Lazarus and his sisters? (b) Why does Jesus' example encourage us?
5 Did Jesus ever feel deeply moved? The Bible tells us that Jesus felt compassion for Lazarus and his sisters and wept with them. And yet he was confident, and "became very indignant," and then raised Lazarus. Also, the Bible says, 'Jesus groaned.' (John 11:
6 Jesus' example encourages us because it shows that Jehovah and Jesus understand our emotions. Jehovah is not indifferent to our pain! We can trust that God will support us when we are grieving, just as he supported Jesus.
"LAZARUS, COME FORTH!"
7, 8. What lesson can we learn from Lazarus' experience, and how did Jesus show courage?
7 Lazarus' family were surrounded by sympathetic friends, but Jesus knew that he could do something more. He allowed four days to pass before going to Lazarus, and his heart was deeply touched. (John 11:39) It is natural to grieve, and it is right to express our sorrow.
8 Then Jesus did something remarkable: He called out, "Lazarus, come forth!" Imagine their amazement! 'The man who had been dead came forth.' (John 11:
9, 10. (a) How did Jesus demonstrate faith when raising Lazarus? (b) Why is understanding this Bible account helpful to us?
9 Jesus first prayed to his Father, showing his confidence in Jehovah's power. By praying, he showed that he believed Jehovah would restore Lazarus to life. (John 11:
10 Many others whom Jesus resurrected also experienced a full recovery. Does this mean that death is always reversible? No. This Bible account helps us to appreciate the importance of valuing the lives of those who are still alive and of comforting those who are grieving.
UNDERSTANDING THE RESURRECTION HOPE
11. What does Lazarus' resurrection illustrate, as shown in Matthew 9:5?
11 The Bible teaches that God has the power "to make all things new." People often lose hope when faced with difficult situations. Lazarus' resurrection demonstrates that power. After Lazarus was brought back to life, did he remain weak and frail? Or did he suddenly regain his strength? Clearly, the Bible does not give us details about such matters. We should remember the principle found elsewhere in the Scriptures, 'to make all things new.' (Matthew 9:5) Lazarus fully recovered.
12. What can we learn from the fact that Lazarus was raised back to life?
12 Understanding the resurrection helps us see that death is not the end. Jesus resurrected Lazarus before many people. And he wanted them to believe that he was the Messiah. Some said: "Can we really be sure that this man [Jesus] performed such a remarkable sign?" (John 11:47) Many people came to witness Lazarus' resurrection. And many more began to put their faith in Jesus. The resurrection of Lazarus showed that Jesus had been authorized by God. This event helped some Jews who were present to realize that Jesus was the Messiah.
13. How does understanding what happened with Lazarus help us trust Jehovah when someone we love dies?
13 Consider whether the resurrection is something impossible? Is it an impossible thing since Jesus said that "all those in the memorial tombs will come out"? (John 5:28) Jehovah is the Creator of everything that lives. Would it be difficult for him to restore life to dead ones? Reflect on Jehovah's limitless power. Can Jehovah truly limit himself when restoring life to those who have died? Let us turn to Isaiah 40:26! (Isaiah 40:26) Truly, Jehovah God can restore life to those who have died and remember all things about them, and also has the ability to resurrect them.
14, 15. What Job asked shows why it is important to recognize that Jehovah has reasons for allowing suffering.
14 The Bible reveals that Jehovah has reasons for allowing suffering. But how can we be convinced of this? Job, a faithful man, once asked: "If a man dies, will he live again?" Job earnestly desired to prove his integrity to God. He told Jehovah: 'I reproach you, but I will not charge you with wrong; let me explain my reasonings.'
15 Think about it! Jehovah has valid reasons for allowing suffering. It is wise to trust that Jehovah has good reasons. Does the prospect of future resurrection offer comfort? Indeed it does, and it does so greatly!
"ALL THOSE IN THE MEMORIAL TOMBS"
16. How many people might be resurrected—a few or a great many?
16 The resurrection that is foretold in the Bible indicates that there will be a vast resurrection. Those who are resurrected to life will be overjoyed to receive another opportunity to live. This future resurrection will be completely different from what they experienced in their past. As we learned in Chapter 3, God's purpose includes making the earth a paradise. Therefore, many people will be resurrected to live forever on earth, and they will experience true life. They will be able to enjoy life fully and meaningfully.
17 Will those who are resurrected be perfect humans?
17 Indeed they will! Jesus said, "All those in the memorial tombs will come forth—those who practiced good deeds to a resurrection of life, and those who did wicked deeds to a resurrection of judgment." (John 5:
18. What do "other sheep" mean, and why is this important to understand?
18 Many "other sheep" have been gathered from all nations and tribes. These include such faithful men as Noah, Abraham, Shelah, Moses, Joshua, and many others. Their names are listed in chapter 11 of the book of Revelation. Other "other sheep" are imperfect humans who exercise faith in Jehovah and zealously preach the good news. Understanding this helps us to appreciate how much Jehovah loves mankind.
19 Is it possible that some may not want to accept Jehovah's salvation, and what will happen then?
19 Will everyone respond favorably when given an opportunity to learn about Jehovah? Billions of people are already "other sheep" who have shown themselves unappreciative. But they will still be given an opportunity to demonstrate whether they truly desire to know God's will and to worship him. During the 1,000-year day of judgment, those who refuse to accept Jehovah will be destroyed along with the wicked ones. That will be a time of final decision. That period is called the Day of Judgment. *
20 Why is this good news, and who are the ones benefiting now?
20 Does this mean that only those who are resurrected will benefit? No, because the Bible says: "Be ready." (Luke 12:5) Jesus foretold signs that would identify the time of his presence and the conclusion of the system of things. Those signs and the zealous preaching work being done today show that we are living in that time. People who respond favorably to the good news are seen as sheep deserving of life and resurrection. However, those who reject it will be like goats to be cut off and destroyed. Soon, Jesus will take action to separate the sheep from the goats, and Jehovah himself will be the One to execute judgment. (Acts 10:42) I have been gathering those who seek refuge and who wish to escape destruction.
THE GATHERING OF THE SHEEP
21, 22. (a) What is one aspect of the fulfillment of the prophecy regarding the "other sheep"? (b) How does the hope of everlasting life strengthen our resolve to preach?
21 The Bible foretells the gathering of "other sheep" and their association with the anointed Christians. In fact, a large part of the fulfillment of that prophecy has been taking place since 1931.
22 As Jesus sent out his disciples, Jehovah showed that he considers them his beloved Son, especially now. (Psalm 16:10; Acts 13:
23, 24. What is the "great crowd" that Jesus spoke about, and what does it mean to belong to it?
23 Since Jesus is the first to be resurrected, he knows what they need—perhaps they need 'comfort.' (John 14:2) Jesus referred to this group as his "great crowd." (Luke 12:32) Who are the people making up this great crowd of Christ's followers? See the explanation in chapter 14 of *The Watchtower*.
24 These 144,000 faithful ones, along with the angels of Jesus, will reign with him in heaven. What does this gathering mean to you? The apostle Paul wrote about a resurrection, or a rising to life, for those who are loyal to Christ. (1 Corinthians 15:23) But according to Revelation 9, there is another resurrection too. So those who prove to be among the 144,000 will receive a heavenly reward, while others will live forever on earth. (1 Corinthians 15:
25. What does Revelation 8 help us understand?
25 Jehovah has determined to wipe out death itself, yes, to end it completely! (Isaiah 25:8) Soon, those who are resurrected will have the opportunity to live on earth again, but what will their future be? They will experience the fulfillment of God's promise. Let us examine what that promise is, as explained in chapter 8 of *The Watchtower*.

We Ngai nũkũsũvĩaa?
Ngai ailyĩ ata? We e syĩtwa?
Nũndũ ũtonyeka kũthengeea Ngai?
1, 2. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ mũseo kũkũlasya makũlyo?
NĨWONAA ũndũ syana ikũlasya makũlyo? Mbingĩ syambĩlĩĩlasya kũkũlya syamanya kũneena oou. Ikũsyaasya isalukĩtye vyũ na iiũkũlya maũndũ ta aa: Nĩkĩ matu nĩ ma mbuluu? Ndata iseũvĩtw'e na kyaũ? Ũla wamanyĩisye nyũnyi kwina nũũ? Nũtonya kũtata mũno kũsũngĩa ĩndĩ ti ũndũ mũvũthũ. O na wasũngĩa nesa vyũ ata, itonya ũkũkũlya: Nĩkĩ?
2 Ti o syana syoka ikũlasya makũlyo. O tũendee na kwĩana, nĩtũendeeaa ũkũlya makũlyo. Tũkũlasya nĩ kana tũelewe nĩ maũndũ, tũmanye mĩisyo ĩla twaĩlĩte kwĩsiĩĩa, kana o kwenda tũmanye maũndũ. Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ nĩmaekaa ũkũlya makũlyo, ala ma vata vyũ. Mũno mũno nĩmaekaa ũmantha mosũngĩo.
3. Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ maekaa kũmantha mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala ma vata mũno?
3 Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩkũlyo yĩla yĩ kavanĩ ya ĩvuku yĩĩ, kana ala me ĩthangũnĩ ya mwambĩlĩlyo, kana o ala me mwambĩlĩlyonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ. Aa nĩ makũlyo ma vata mũno tũtonya ũkũlya. Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ nĩmaekete kũmantha mosũngĩo. Nĩkĩ maekete? Yo Mbivilia nĩmasũngĩĩte? Andũ amwe mew'aa mosũngĩo mayo me vinya mũno kũelewa. Angĩ nĩmew'aa nthoni kana aivũ kũkũlya makũlyo. O na angĩ maasyaa makũlyo ta asu maĩle kũsũngĩwa nĩ atongoi na amanyĩsya ma ndĩni. We ũsũanĩaa ata?
4, 5. Nĩ makũlyo amwe meva ma vata mũno ala tũtonya kwĩkũlya thayũnĩ, na nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kũmantha mosũngĩo?
4 Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wendeeaw'a nĩ kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala ma vata thayũnĩ. No nginya wĩthĩwe nĩwĩkũlasya: 'Kĩeleelo kya thayũ nĩ kyaũ? Thayũ now'o ũũ? Kwa w'o Ngai ailyĩ ata?' Nĩ ũndũ mũseo kũkũlya makũlyo ta asu, na nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũendeea nginya ũkwate mosũngĩo meanĩu na maĩkĩĩku. Mũmanyĩsya mũnene Yesũ Klĩsto aisye: "Voyai, na mũkanengwa; manthai, na mũkoona; vingũsyai, na mũkavingũĩwa."
5 Waendeea 'kũmantha' mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala ma vata, ũkeethĩa kũmantha nĩkũunaa. (Nthimo 2:
WE NGAI E TEI NA NŨTHĨNĨKAA ĨŨLŨ WITŨ?
6. Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ monaa Ngai totathĩnĩkaa nũndũ wa mathĩna ma andũ?
6 Andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana Ngai ndatũthĩnĩkĩaa na nde tei. Makũlasya, 'Kethĩwa Ngai e tei, yo nthĩ yĩthĩwa ĩilyĩ ũndũ ĩilyĩ?' Twasisya kũũ nthĩ yonthe twonaa yusĩe makaũ, kĩmena, na mathĩna maingĩ. Na ithyĩ nĩtũwaa, tũkathĩna na endwa maitũ makakw'a. Nĩkyo kĩtumi andũ aingĩ maasyaa, 'Kethĩwa Ngai nũthĩnĩkaa nũndũ witũ na mathĩna maitũ, ethĩwa asiĩaa maũndũ asu maikekĩke.'
7. (a) Amanyĩsya ma ndĩni matumĩte ata andũ aingĩ masũanĩa kana Ngai nde tei? (b) Mbivilia yo ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa matatwa ala matũkwataa?
7 Ũthũku nĩ kana, mavinda angĩ amanyĩsya ma ndĩni nĩmatumaa andũ masũanĩa kana Ngai nde tei. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nũndũ yĩla mĩisyo yooka maasyaa ku nĩ kwenda kwa Ngai. Amanyĩsya asu ma ndĩni methĩawa maimũtw'a Ngai mavĩtyo nũndũ wa maũndũ mathũku ala mekĩkaa. Ũsu nĩw'o ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai? Mbivilia yo ĩmanyĩasya ata? Yakovo 1:
8, 9. (a) Ũtonya kũelekany'a ata kĩvathũkany'o kya kũeka ũthũku wĩthĩwe na kũũete? (b) Nĩkĩ wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ ũtaĩle kũmũtũla Ngai mũtĩ nũndũ wa kũeka andũ maendee kwĩka maũndũ mathũku?
8 Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya ĩthe mũĩ wĩ wendo wĩna mwana mũima wĩkalaa mũsyĩ vamwe na asyai make. Mwana ũsu akatw'ĩka kĩng'endilĩ na aitw'a kuma mũsyĩ, ĩthe ndamũvata. Mwana ũsu akathi kwĩkala mwĩkalĩle mũthuku na ailika mathĩnanĩ, we ĩthe nĩwe ũetete mathĩna make? Aiee. (Luka 15:
9 Ngai e na itumi nzeo sya kũeka andũ maendee kwĩka maũndũ mathũku. Ta mũmbi mũĩ na wĩ vinya, ti o nginya atũelesye itumi syake. Ĩndĩ nũndũ wa wendo nũtũeleasya. Kĩlungunĩ kya 11 ũkeemanyĩsya mũnango ĩũlũ wa itumi isu. Ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana Ngai tiwe ũetae mathĩna ala twĩ namo. Ĩndĩ atũnengae wĩkwatyo o ũmwe tu wa kũmamina!
10. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai akamina mathĩna onthe ala ũthũku ũetete?
10 O na ĩngĩ, Ngai nĩ mũtheu. (Isaia 6:3) Ũu nĩkwasya we nde ũvuku. Nde ũndũ ũthũku o na ũmwe nthĩnĩ wake. Kwoou nĩtũtonya kũmũĩkĩĩa vyũ. Ũu tiw'o tũmaĩkĩĩaa andũ nũndũ mavinda angĩ nĩmatonya kũtw'ĩka akengani. O na atongoi ma andũ ala meyumĩtye vyũ, mavinda maingĩ mayĩthĩawa na ũtonyi wa kũmina wanangĩko ũla andũ athũku maetete. Ĩndĩ Ngai e ũtonyi. Ngai e na ũtonyi wa kũmina mathĩna ala ũthũku ũetete andũnĩ na akamina. Yĩla Ngai ũkosa ĩtambya yĩu akamina ũthũku tene na tene!
NGAI EW'AA ATA ĨŨLŨ WA ŨSILI ŨTE WA KATĨ?
11. (a) Ngai ew'aa ata ĩũlũ wa sila ũte wa katĩ? (b) Ngai ew'aa ata ĩũlũ wa thĩna waku?
11 Yu-ĩ, Ngai ew'aa ata ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala maendee kwĩkĩka nthĩ yonthe na thayũnĩ waku? Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai "nũwendete sila wa katĩ." (Savuli 37:28) Kwoou nĩwosaa kwa ũito maũndũ ala malũngalu na ala mate malũngalu. Nũmenete mũthemba w'onthe wa sila ũte wa katĩ. Mbivilia yaasya kana Ngai 'nĩweew'ĩthiw'e woo ngoonĩ yake' yĩla ũthũku wausũie nthĩ ĩvinda ya tene. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 6:
12, 13. (a) Ithyĩ twĩthĩawa na ndaĩa nzeo ta wendo nĩkĩ, na wendo ũtumaa twĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ mate malũngalu ala me kũũ nthĩ? (b) Nĩkĩ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ũw'o kana Ngai akamina mathĩna ma nthĩ?
12 Tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ũw'o kana Ngai nũmenete kwona thĩna ata? Ũkũsĩ ũngĩ nĩ ũũ. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai oombie mũndũ na mũvw'ano wake. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:
13 Ũndũ ũmwe mũseo vyũ ĩũlũ wa andũ nĩ kwĩthĩwa tũtonya kwendana. Ũu nĩw'o Ngai ũilyĩ, nũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana "Ngai nĩ wendo." (1 Yoana 4:8) Twĩ wendo nũndũ Ngai e wendo. Wendo nũtonya kũũsukuma kũmina thĩna na sila ũte wa katĩ kũũ nthĩ? Kethĩwa wĩ na ũtonyi wa kwĩka ũu, we no wĩke ũu? Ĩĩ, no wĩke ũu! Ngai akamina sila ũte wa katĩ. Maũndũ ala mathanĩtwe mwambĩlĩlyonĩ wa ĩvuku yĩĩ ti ndoto kana mawĩkwatyo ma mana. Maũndũ asu Ngai wathanĩte makeanĩa! Nĩ kana ũĩkĩĩe maũndũ asu mathanĩtwe, nĩwaĩle kũmanya mũnango ĩũlũ wa Ngai ũla ũmathanĩte.
NGAI NŨKWENDA ŨMŨMANYE
14. Syĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ yĩva, na nĩkĩ twaĩlĩtwe nĩ kũyĩtũmĩa?
14 We wenda mũndũ akũmanye ũtonya kwĩka ata? Ndũmũtavya syĩtwa yaku? Ngai e syĩtwa? Ndĩni mbingĩ syaasyaa syĩtwa yake ni "Ngai" kana "Mwĩaĩi," ĩndĩ asu ti masyĩtwa make mwene. Nĩ masyĩtwa ma ũnene o tondũ "mũsumbĩ" kana "mũtongoi" nĩ masyĩtwa ma ũnene. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai e masyĩtwa maingĩ ma ũnene. Amwe mamo nĩ "Ngai" na "Mwĩaĩi." Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai e syĩtwa yake mwene. Syĩtwa yĩu nĩ Yeova. Savuli 83:18 yaasya: "No we wĩ weka, syĩtwa yaku nĩ Yeova, nue Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe." Kethĩwa Mbivilia yaku ndĩ syĩtwa yĩu no ũsisye Ũvoo wa Kwongeleela ĩthangũnĩ ya 195-197 ĩvukunĩ yĩĩ ũmanye nĩkĩ. Ũw'o nĩ kana syĩtwa ya Ngai yonekaa mavinda maingĩ nthĩnĩ wa mavuku ma Mbivilia ma tene. Kwoou Yeova endaa ũmanye syĩtwa yake na ũiyĩtũmĩa. Kwĩsĩla Mbivilianĩ Ngai nĩwĩmanyĩthanasya kwaku.
15. Syĩtwa ya Yeova yonanasya ata?
15 Ngai eenengie syĩtwa yĩ na kĩtumi. Syĩtwa yake,Yeova, yonanasya kana Ngai nũtonya kwĩanĩsya ũndũ o wĩva ũla wathanĩte na nũtonya kwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo o na kĩva kĩla ũsũanĩĩte. * Syĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ ya mwanya, yĩiĩ maela. Nĩ yake e weka. Yeova nĩ wa mwanya kwa nzĩa mbingĩ. Syĩva?
16, 17. Tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova kumana na masyĩtwa aa make ma ũnene: (a) "Mwene Vinya W'onthe"? (b) "Mũsumbĩ wa tene na tene"? (c) "Mũmbi"?
16 Tũsomie kana Savuli 83:18 yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova: 'No we wĩ weka Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe.' O na ĩngĩ, Yeova e weka awetetwe ta we "Mwene Vinya W'onthe." Ũvuan'yo 15:3 yaasyaa ũũ: "Mawĩa maku nĩ manene na maũsengy'a, Mwĩaĩi Ngai, Mwene Vinya W'onthe; moendelo maku nĩ malũngalu na ma w'o, we Mũsumbĩ wa tene na tene." Syĩtwa yĩu ya ũnene "Mwene Vinya W'onthe" yĩtũmanyĩasya kana Yeova nĩwe wĩ vinya vyũ kũthonoka onthe. Vinya wake ndwĩ maela; nĩ mũnene vyũ. Na syĩtwa ya ũnene "Mũsumbĩ wa tene na tene" yĩtũlilikanasya kana Yeova nĩ wa mwanya kwa nzĩa ĩngĩ. No we e weka ũte mwambĩlĩlyo kana mũminũkĩlyo. Savuli 90:2 yaasyaa ũũ: "O kuma tene na tene kũvika tene na tene, nue Ngai." Yĩsilya yĩu nĩyĩetae kĩkĩo, kana tiw'o?
17 Yeova nĩ wa mwanya nũndũ nowe Mũmbi e weka. Ũvuan'yo 4:11 yaasyaa: "Nĩwaĩle we, Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Ngai waitũ, kwosa ndaĩa na nguma na vinya: nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwoombie, syĩndũ syonthe na kwondũ wa kwenda kwaku syaĩ kw'o, na ĩngĩ syoombwa." Syĩndũ syonthe ila ũtonya kũsũanĩa
NŨTONYA KŨMŨTHENGEEA YEOVA?
18. Nĩkĩ andũ amwe mew'aa matesa kũmũthengeea Ngai, ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata?
18 Kũsoma ĩũlũ wa ndaĩa sya Yeova syĩ kĩkĩo, kũtumaa andũ amwe methĩwa na w'ĩa. Monaa matatonya kũmũthengeea Ngai na e ĩũlũ mũno ũndũ ũtesa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ woo. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩw'o? Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ũndũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Yaasyaa atĩĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova: "Nde kũasa na kĩla ũmwe waitũ." (Meko ma Atũmwa 17:27) O na ĩngĩ Mbivilia ĩtũthing'ĩĩasya ũũ: "Mũthengeei Ngai, nake akamũthengeea inyw'ĩ."
19. (a) Tũtonya ata kwambĩlĩlya kũthengeea Ngai, na ũunĩko nĩ mwaũ? (b) Nĩ ndaĩa syĩva sya Ngai ikwendeeasya?
19 Ũtonya kũmũthengeea Ngai ata? Ũndũ wa mbee, endeea kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai o ũndũ ũkwĩka yu. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Na thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto." (Yoana 17:3) Nĩw'o, Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova na Yesũ kũkatuma ũkwata "thayũ ũtathela"! O tondũ twonie, "Ngai nĩ wendo." (1 Yoana 4:
20-22. (a) Kwĩthĩwa tũtatonya kũmwona Ngai no kũtũsiĩĩe kũmũthengeea? Elesya. (b) Andũ amwe mate na ũthũku matonya kwĩka ata, ĩndĩ waĩle kwĩka ata?
20 Ndũtonya kũmwona Ngai nũndũ Ngai nĩ veva. (Yoana 1:
21 Ũkaelewa nĩkĩ Mbivilia ĩtũmanyĩasya kũmwona Yeova ta Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ. (Mathayo 6:9) O vamwe na kwĩthĩwa thayũ witũ umĩte kwake, atwendeaa thayũ mũseo ũndũ vatonyeka
22 O ũendee na kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ kuma Mbivilianĩ, nũtonya kwona andũ amwe mate na ũthũku maiũthing'ĩĩsya ũeke kwĩmanyĩsya. No methĩwe mayona ta ũkũekana na maũndũ ala ũĩkĩĩaa. Ĩndĩ ndũkaeke mũndũ o na ũmwe aũsiĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na ũnyanya na Ngai.
23, 24. (a) Nĩkĩ nĩwaĩlĩte kũendeea kũkũlya makũlyo ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala ũkwĩmanyĩsya? (b) Nĩ ũndũ mwaũ ũkũelew'a kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe?
23 Ve maũndũ wĩĩthĩwa ũtatonya kũelewa wambĩlĩlya kwĩmanyĩsya. O na kau kũkũlya ũtethyo nĩkwendaa wĩnyivyo, ndũkew'e nthoni kũkũlya. Yesũ aisye nũndũ mũseo kwĩnyivya, ta syana nini. (Mathayo 18:
24 Nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ ya kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ kũkunĩkĩla Mbivilia. Yĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mavuku ala angĩ onthe. Kwa nzĩa yĩva? Kĩlungu kĩĩ kĩatĩĩe nĩkĩkũelesya ũndũ ũsu.
^ kal. 15 Ve ũvoo wa kwongeleela ĩũlũ wa kĩla syĩtwa ya Ngai yonanasya na ũndũ yĩtamũkawa ĩthangũnĩ ya 195-197.
