translation:
Who is God to us?
Does God care? What is His name?
What makes worship pleasing to God?
1, 2. Is it important to share food?
DOES sharing food matter? Many people enjoy eating—especially delicious food. Consider these questions: Are bananas good? Why were they created? Does someone remember their origin? It's not right to be selfish. And even if you share sometimes, you might ask yourself: Why?
2 It doesn't matter whether you share food or not. Let's go on and eat, let's go on and enjoy our food. Whether we understand things or not, whether we know the reasons why we are here, or don't know things. For many people enjoying food is enough, but they miss something. This thing is remembering its source.
3. Why do many people enjoy food without remembering its source?
3 To appreciate the value of food like a ripe fruit, or even a gift from a friend, or even a gift from a stranger. These are foods that have a source we should remember. For many people remembering its source is enough. Why is it enough? Yes, the Bible teaches this. Some people remember their source because they want to understand. Others remember it out of habit or necessity to enjoy food. But others forget about the source and are satisfied with what they receive without being reminded. Do you feel the same way?
4, 5. Are there some foods that are better enjoyed without thinking about their source, and why do we often forget its source?
4 It's possible to be distracted while enjoying food that has a source. Don't let anyone distract you from asking: 'What is the purpose of life? What is life really? Where is God?' It is important to share food, and it is also important to continue seeking meaning and understanding. The great Jesus Christ said: "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you."
5 When you try to 'remember' the source of food, realize that remembering means understanding. (Proverbs 2:
GOD AND THE PURPOSE OF LIFE
6. Why do many people think God doesn't care about human problems?
6 Many people wonder whether God cares about them at all. They ask, 'Does God really care, or is it just wishful thinking?' Let us look at everything we see around us—the sun, the earth, and countless things. And yet we still struggle, facing difficulties and challenges. This is why many people say, 'God cares about our lives and our problems, but nothing seems to happen.'
7. (a) What reasons cause many people to question whether God exists? (b) Does the Bible offer an answer to the problem of suffering?
7 However, there are reasons why some people question whether God exists. But why is this so? The way God allows things to be is often beyond our comprehension. Reasons for allowing certain things may seem strange to us. Is this truly God's way? Does the Bible offer an answer to this? James 1:
8, 9. (a) How can you apply the principle of being quick to listen and slow to speak? (b) Why is it important to remember that God wants people to live according to his standards when trying to help others?
8 Consider how a loving parent would react when their child makes a mistake. The child might try to hide it, fearing punishment. But the parent understands. Would the parent then scold the child and ignore their feelings? Of course not. (Luke 15:
9 God has valid reasons for allowing bad things to happen. He does not delight in wickedness, but he respects human free will. His love moves him to allow us to learn through experience. Psalm 11 highlights the importance of understanding God's purpose. Remember that God does not cause everything that happens, but he permits it. Let us therefore not be too quick to judge!
10. How can we show confidence that God cares about our feelings?
10 Indeed, God is compassionate. (Isaiah 6:3) This is what motivates him. It is because of his compassion that he allows suffering. We find it difficult to understand why. But we should not let this lead us to distrust him. Many people have faced similar trials, and they have found comfort in knowing that God cares. God has the power to prevent all suffering, yet he chooses not to. Because God values our freedom, he allows us to make choices, even those that cause pain. Yes, God gives humans the opportunity to prove themselves, and he patiently waits to see what they will do!
GOD HAS A REASON FOR ALLOWING SUFFERING—BUT WHAT IS IT?
11. (a) What reason does God have for allowing suffering? (b) What reason does God have for allowing imperfection?
11 Yes, God has a reason for allowing bad things to happen so that people can demonstrate their loyalty under trial. The Bible shows that God "takes pleasure in those who fear him." (Proverbs 37:28) Therefore, he allows people to face challenges so that they can demonstrate their faith. He wants them to trust in him completely. The Bible assures us that God "will not forsake his people" when they are experiencing difficulties. (Hebrews 6:
12, 13. (a) Why are we deeply affected by injustice, and how does love move us to feel sorrow over the injustices suffered by others? (b) How can we remain confident that God cares about our feelings?
12 Can we be sure that God cares about our feelings? Absolutely. The Bible shows that God empathizes with human suffering. (Hebrews 1:
13 One important reason why people suffer is because they often make poor choices. This is why God gave humans free will, and the Bible says that "God is love." (1 John 4:8) Because God is love, he allows us to make choices, even though some of those choices may lead to suffering. But does this mean that God causes suffering? No, he does not! God hates suffering. Bad things happen because of imperfections and mistakes made by humans. The events described in the book of Revelation are not fantasies or imaginary stories. They show what God will accomplish! If you find it difficult to believe this, take time to meditate on God's purpose.
GOD IS LOVING AND UNDERSTANDING
14. God's name is glorious, so why should we use it?
14 Does loving someone involve getting to know his name? Why is God's name important? God has a personal name. While some refer to Him as "God" or "Creator," others have used different names. These names, such as "the Almighty" or "the Most High," describe qualities God possesses. The Bible shows that God has many wonderful names. Some of them are "God" and "Creator." However, the Bible also reveals that God has a unique personal name—Jehovah. Psalm 83:18 states: "You whose name is Jehovah, you alone are the Most High over all the earth." To learn more about God's name, see the publication Glorifying Jehovah's Name, pages 195-197. That is why God's name appears thousands of times throughout the Biblical manuscripts. Knowing Jehovah's name and using it honors him. By learning from the Bible, you can come to know and appreciate God better.
15. Does the name Jehovah matter?
15 God values his name greatly. His name, Jehovah, matters because it identifies God as the One who has the power to fulfill his purpose and the One who cares about those who love and obey him. * God's name is sacred, majestic. It belongs to him alone. Jehovah is unique in many ways. How so?
16, 17. What does knowing Jehovah's name mean in connection with his other titles: (a) "Sovereign Ruler of All"? (b) "Eternal Father"? (c) "Creator"?
16 Consider Psalm 83:18, which speaks of Jehovah: 'You whose name is Jehovah, are the Sovereign Ruler of All.' Also, Jehovah is uniquely identified as "Sovereign Ruler of All." Isaiah 15:3 says: "Your glory is great and magnificent, O God, Sovereign Ruler of All; your accomplishments are wonderful and awe-inspiring, O Eternal Father." This important title "Sovereign Ruler of All" shows that Jehovah is the One who possesses supreme authority over everything. His rulership is unmatched; it is powerful. And the title "Eternal Father" indicates that Jehovah is unique in his loving care. He is always there for us. Psalm 90:2 states: "Before the mountains themselves were born, or you gave birth to the earth and the seas, from eternity to eternity you are God." Does this description not inspire confidence?
17 Jehovah is unique as Creator as well. Isaiah 4:11 says: "I am Jehovah, your God, the One who takes hold of your hand—the One who comforts you, the One who says to you, 'Do not be afraid.' I will help you." Everything demonstrates his creative power.
CAN WE PLEASE JEHOVAH?
18. Do some find it difficult to please God, and what does the Bible show?
18 Reading about Jehovah's qualities can help people feel closer to him. However, some may struggle to please God, and they may feel that it is too hard to understand his ways. Why is this so? The Bible reveals something helpful. It says that Jehovah desires: "That all men should be saved." (Acts 17:27) Furthermore, the Bible teaches us: "Worship God, and he will worship you."
19. (a) How can we make our worship pleasing to God, and why? (b) What vital truth does God want us to know?
19 Can we really please God? In essence, it means living according to what God knows is best. Jesus said: "This means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and your son, Jesus Christ." (John 17:3) Thus, the Bible shows that getting to know Jehovah and Jesus leads to "everlasting life!" And because "God is love." (1 John 4:
20-22. (a) Why can we trust that God wants to draw close to us and help us to worship him? Yes. (b) Some people face challenges that make it hard for them to believe—how can we view such ones?
20 We can come to know God because he wants us to. (John 1:
21 Understand how the Bible helps us to get to know Jehovah better than we could on our own. (Matthew 6:9) Also, just as we enjoy spending time with dear friends, we can enjoy drawing near to God.
22 Moreover, as you study more in the Bible, you will likely meet people who have doubts. Be patient with those who struggle to believe, and do not look down on them. Instead, remember that everyone needs time to learn and grow spiritually. A person may need encouragement and support to strengthen his faith in God.
23, 24. (a) Why might someone find it hard to accept and apply Bible principles? (b) What can help you to express yourself clearly when speaking to others?
23 There are reasons why someone might find it hard to understand and apply Bible principles. But like learning any new skill, practice makes perfect. Jesus explained that persistent effort is needed, saying: (Matthew 18:
24 One way to improve your understanding of God's Word is to meditate on what you read in the Bible. This involves thinking deeply about the meaning of the scriptures and relating them to your life. How does this help? Clear thinking will enable you to express yourself effectively.
^ par. 15 Consider ways to expand your personal ministry by sharing the good news with others, as outlined on pages 195-197.

text:
"Mũthengeei Ngai, nake akamũthengeea inyw'ĩ." —YAK. 4:8.
1. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũtata ngwatanĩo yitũ vamwe na Yeova yĩthĩwe yĩ ndũmu?
WE NĨWEEYUMISYE ũmũthũkũme Yeova na wavatiswa watw'ĩka Ngũsĩ yake? Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, wĩ na kĩndũ kya vata mũno nakyo nĩ ngwatanĩo vamwe na Ngai. Ĩndĩ ngwatanĩo ĩsu wĩ nayo vamwe na Ngai nĩtonya kwanangwa nĩ nthĩ ĩno ya Satani, na naĩ ĩla twĩthĩawa nayo. Vai Mũklĩsto ũte thĩnanĩ ũsu. Nũndũ wa ũu, twaĩle kũtata ngwatanĩo yitũ vamwe na Yeova yĩthĩwe yĩ ndũmu vyũ ũndũ vatonyeka.
2. (a) Ngwatanĩo ĩtonya kũelew'a ata? (Sisya maelesyo ma kwongeleela.) (b) Tũtonya ata kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ vamwe na Yeova?
2 Ngwatanĩo yaku vamwe na Yeova ĩlũmĩte ata? No wende yĩthĩwe yĩ ndũmangu kwĩ ũndũ yu ĩilyĩ? Ĩandĩko ya Yakovo 4:8 nĩyĩũtavĩtye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ũu. Yaĩtye: "Mũthengeei Ngai, nake akamũthengeea inyw'ĩ." Ĩandĩko yĩu yonanĩtye kana ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova yĩ na ngalĩ ilĩ. * Ata? Twoosa ĩtambya ya kũmũthengeea Ngai o nake ekaa oou. Ĩla twoosa matambya tũteũtĩĩa na tũyona o nake Yeova oosa matambya, ngwatanĩo yitũ nake nĩendeeaa kũlũlũmĩla. Na kyu kĩtumaa twĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana ngwatanĩo yitũ nake yĩ vo. Twĩthĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo o ta ũla waĩ na Yesũ ĩla waisye, 'Ũla wandũmie nĩ wa w'o, na nyie nĩnĩmwĩsĩ.' (Yoa. 7:28, 29) Ĩndĩ mo nĩ matambya meva ũtonya kwosa nĩ kana ũmũthengeee Yeova?
3. Ũtonya kũea ngewa na Yeova ata?
3 Kũea ngewa na Yeova kĩla ĩvinda nĩ ũndũ ũmwe wa vata waĩle kwĩka ethĩwa nũkwenda kũmũthengeea. Ĩndĩ ũtonya ata kũea ngewa na Ngai? Kwesilye-ĩ, ethĩwa wĩ mũnyanyau wĩkalaa kũasa, we ũeaa ngewa nake ata? No kwĩthĩwa mũandĩkanĩaa mavinda maingĩ kana mũkekala mũikũnanĩa simũ. O ta ũu, ũneenaa na Yeova ĩla wamũvoya kĩla ĩvinda. (Soma Savuli 142:2.) Na ĩndĩ ĩla wasoma Ndeto yake kĩla ĩvinda na wamĩvindĩĩsya, wĩthĩawa ũimwĩtĩkĩlya aneene naku. (Soma Isaia 30:20, 21.) Ekai twone ũndũ kũea ngewa na Yeova kũlũlũmĩlasya ngwatanĩo yitũ nake na kũkatuma twĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana ngwatanĩo ĩsu nĩ ya w'o.
YEOVA NŨNEENAA NAKU ĨLA ŨKWĨMANYĨSYA MBIVILIA
4, 5. Yeova atũmĩaa Ndeto yake ata kũneena naku? Nengane ngelekany'o.
4 Ndũema kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ kana Ngai aandĩkĩthisye Mbivilia kwondũ wa kĩla mũndũ. Ĩndĩ yo no twasye kana Mbivilia nĩkwonasya ũndũ we mwene ũtonya kũmũthengeea Yeova? Ĩĩ, no twasye ũu. Ĩndĩ ĩkwonasya ata? Mantha mwanya ũteũtĩĩa nĩ kana ũsome na ũyĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ĩla ũũmĩsoma sisya ũndũ ũkwosa maũndũ ala wasoma na ũisyoka ũsũanĩe ũndũ we mwene ũtonya kũtũmĩa kĩu wasoma. Weeka ũu wĩthĩawa ũimwĩtĩkĩlya Yeova aneene naku aitũmĩa Ndeto yake. Kyu kĩtumaa wĩthĩwa wĩ na ngwatanĩo nũmangu vamwe nake.—Aevl. 4:12; Yak. 1:23-25.
5 Kwa ngelekany'o, kwa soma na ũivindĩĩsya ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Mũikeyiĩe ũthwii kũũ nthĩ." Ethĩwa ngoonĩ yaku nũkwĩw'a kana nĩwambaa kwĩanĩsya maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ mbee, ndeto isu syĩtuma wona kana Yeova nĩwĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ waku. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa nũkwĩw'a waĩle kwĩtheeangya kĩlasi, na waĩle kũtata mũnango wĩanĩasye maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ mbee, ndeto isu syĩũtetheesya kwona kana Yeova eĩka kũkwoneleelya kĩndũ we mwene waĩle kwĩka nĩ kana ũmũthengeee mũnango.—Mt. 6:19, 20.
6, 7. (a) Ĩla tweemanyĩsya Mbivilia tũmwendaa Yeova ata, nake atwendaa ata? (b) Twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na kĩeleelo kĩva ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya twĩ ithyoka?
6 O na kau kwĩmanyĩsya Maandĩko nĩkũtumaa twona moalyũku ala twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana tũmũthũkũme Yeova nesanga, no kũtũtetheeasya maũndũnĩ angĩ. Meva? Nĩkũtumaa tũmũmanya Yeova nesanga na ũu ũituma tũmwenda. Na ĩndĩ ĩla twamwenda mũnango, o nake nũtwendaa vyũ na ngwatanĩo yitũ nake ĩilũma.—Soma 1 Akolintho 8:3.
7 Ĩndĩ nĩ kana tũmũthengeee Yeova, nũseo tũkemanyĩasya Mbivilia twĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo. Ĩandĩko ya Yoana 17:3 yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto.' Kwoou kĩeleelo kitũ kĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ne o kwĩmanyĩsya tũmaũndũ tũteeĩsĩ, ĩndĩ kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ne 'kũmũmanya' nesa Ngai ũla wĩtawa Yeova.—Soma Kuma 33:13; Sav. 25:4.
8. (a) Mũndũ atonya kwĩkũlya ata amina kũsoma ngewa ĩla yĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 2 Asumbĩ 15:1-5, ĩla yonanĩtye ũndũ Yeova weekanie na Mũsumbĩ Asalia? (b) Kũmũmanya Yeova kũtonya kũtũtetheesya ata tũikaye nzika ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala wĩkaa?
8 Twamũmanya Yeova o tondũ tũmwĩsĩ ũla mũnyanyae witũ mũnene, tũikatindaa tũithĩnĩka ĩla twasoma ngewa imwe Mbivilianĩ na twatiwa tũsaanĩw'e nĩkĩ weekie ũndũ weekie. Kwa ngelekany'o, we wĩw'aa ata ĩla wasoma ũndũ Yeova weekanie na mũsumbĩ ũmwe wa Yuta weetawa Asalia? (2 Asu. 15:1-5) Wasoma ngewa ĩsu ya Asalia, wĩĩthĩa kana o na kau andũ "nĩmaendeeaa na kũthemba na kũtoeesya ũvani kũla kũndũ kũtũlu," we Asalia "eekaa ũla Yeova wonaa wĩ ũseo." Ĩndĩ o na ekĩte ũu weekĩte, 'Yeova nĩwamũkũnie, na eethĩwa na mangũ kũvika mũthenya wa kĩkw'ũ kyake.' Nĩkĩ weekie ũu? Ngewa ĩsu ndĩwetete. Ĩndĩ kyo kyu nĩkyaĩle kũtuma tũthĩnĩka kana kĩkatuma tũtiwa tũyĩkũlya ethĩwa Yeova ooseie Asalia ĩtambya vate kĩtumi? Tũyĩsa kwĩka ũu ethĩwa nĩtũmwĩsĩ Yeova nesa vyũ. Ũndũ ũmwe wonanasya nĩtũmwĩsĩ Yeova nesa nĩ kwĩkalaa twĩsĩ kana akanasya andũ 'athimĩte.' (Yel. 30:11) Kũmanya ũu kũtumaa twĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana ĩtambya yĩla wooseie Asalia nĩyaaĩle, o na ethĩwa tũyĩsĩ nĩkĩ weekie ũndũ weekie.
9. Nĩ maũndũ meva matumaa tũelewa nĩkĩ Yeova wakũnie Asalia na mangũ?
9 Ĩndĩ ũseo nĩ kana maandĩko angĩ no maeleetye mũnango ngewa ĩsu ya Asalia. Mũsumbĩ Asalia nowe weetawa Mũsumbĩ Usia. (2 Asu. 15:7, 32) Nũndũ wa ũu, ngewa ĩla ĩvw'anene na ĩsu yĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku ya 2 Mavinda 26:3-5, 16-21 nĩtũtetheeasya kũmanya kana o na kau Usia nĩweekie ũla Yeova woonaa wĩ ũseo kwa kavinda, avikie vandũ "ngoo yake yeetũlya, kwondũ wa ũu eeka naĩ mũno." Nũndũ wa mĩtũlyo ĩsu, ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwatatie kũtethya wĩa wa mũthembi o esĩ ti wake. Ayenda kwĩka ũu athembi 81 nĩmamũatĩĩie na matata kũmũkany'a. Usia eekie ata? Eekie kĩko kyoonanisye ũndũ waĩ na mĩtũlyo ĩana. 'Athilĩkĩle' athembi asu. Mwa o na Yeova ndaĩ alea kũmũkũna na mangũ!
10. Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kũtindaa tweteele tũelew'e maũndũ onthe ala Yeova wĩkaa? Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũĩkĩĩe vyũ kana Yeova ekaa kĩla kyaĩle?
10 Ve ũndũ tũtaĩle kũlwa nĩw'o. Twasye Ndeto ya Ngai ĩeleetye ngewa ĩsu kwa ũkuvĩ o tondũ ĩeleetye ngewa imwe, we no wambĩĩe kwona Ngai ta ũte mũlũngalu? Kana ũtw'a Mbivilia nĩtũtavĩtye maũndũ matoetye ĩũlũ wa Yeova ala matũĩkĩĩthasya vyũ kana ĩvinda yonthe ekaa ũla waĩle, na nowe waĩle kũtw'a ũla ũseo na ũla ũthũku? (Kũt. 32:4) Twamũmanya nesa Ngai ũsu wĩtawa Yeova, tũkamwenda mũnango na tũielewa nesa ũndũ wĩkaa maũndũ nginya wĩthĩe o na ti lasima tũkatinda tũeleaw'a maũndũ onthe ala wĩkaa. Ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana o ũndũ ũkwĩkĩa kĩthito kĩana kya kwĩmanyĩsya na kũvindĩĩsya kĩla Ngai ũkũtavĩtye Ndetonĩ yake, now'o ũkũendeea kũelewa nesa ũndũ wĩkaa maũndũ. (Sav. 77:12, 13) Na ĩndĩ kĩu kĩkalũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova, wĩthĩe o naku nũkwĩw'a yĩ vo.
ĨLA ŨŨVOYA WĨTHĨAWA ŨINEENA NA YEOVA
11-13. Ũtonya kũmanya ata kana Yeova nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 19.)
11 Kũvoya nĩkũtũtetheeasya kũmũthengeea Yeova. Nĩtũmũvoyaa nĩ kana tũmũkathe, tũmũtũngĩe mũvea, na tũimũkũlya atũtongoesye. (Sav. 32:8) Ĩndĩ nĩ kana ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova yĩthĩwe yĩ ndũmu vyũ, no nginya ũĩkĩĩe nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya.
12 Andũ amwe monaa mboya no kĩndũ kya kũtetheesya mũndũ ausye kĩlĩko. Maasya atĩ ĩla wesa kwona mboya yaku ta ĩsũngĩiwe, yĩthĩawa yĩkie kũũtetheesya ũmanye thĩna waku vala ũĩ, na wamina kũũmanya, we mwene wemanthĩa nzĩa ya kũũmina. Ĩndĩ o na kau ũu no w'o, ũtonya kũmanya ata kana ĩla wavoya kuma ngoonĩ Yeova nũkwĩthukĩĩasya?
13 Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. O na e ĩtunĩ nĩweeyoneaa we mwene ũndũ Yeova wasũngĩaa mboya sya athaithi make aĩkĩĩku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Na ĩndĩ ĩla watavanasya e kũũ nthĩ, nĩwatũmĩaa mboya kũelesya Ĩthe wake wa ĩtunĩ kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ. O na mũthenya ũmwe nĩwavoyie ũtukũ mũima. We nĩwĩthĩwa eekaa ũu takethĩwa nĩwasũanĩaa kana Yeova ndamwĩthukĩĩsye? (Luka 6:12; 22:40-46) We nĩwĩthĩwa amanyĩisye amanyĩw'a make kũvoya takethĩwa asũanĩaa ũtethyo ũla mboya ĩtonya kũnengane no kũtuma kĩlĩko kĩusya? Vate nzika, Yesũ nĩweesĩ nesa kana ĩla mũndũ ũkũvoya ethĩawa aineena na Yeova. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩvinda yĩmwe waisye atĩĩ: "Asa, nĩngũũtũngĩa mũvea nũndũ nĩwambĩw'a. Nakwa nĩnĩsĩ kana mavinda onthe nũmbĩw'aa." O naitũ no tũĩkĩĩe vyũ kana Yeova nĩwe "wĩw'aa mboya."—Yoa. 11:41, 42; Sav. 65:2.
14, 15. (a) Kũweta maũndũ tũteũvithany'a ĩla tũũvoya kũtonya kũtũtetheesya ata? (b) Mboya yatetheeisye ata mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe alũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova?
14 Waweta maũndũ ũteũvithany'a ĩla ũũvoya, nĩwĩthĩawa ũtonya kũmanya ĩla Yeova waũsũngĩa, o na ethĩwa aũsũngĩa kwa nzĩa yĩvithanĩtye. Naku ĩla woona aikũsũngĩa mboya syaku ndũkethĩawa na nzika kana nĩ w'o Yeova e vo. O na ĩngĩ, o ũndũ waendeea kũmũelesya Yeova kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ, now'o ũkaendeea kũũthengeea.
15 Sũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Kathy. * O na kau nĩwatavanasya kĩla ĩvinda, ndatanĩaa wĩa ũsu wa ũtavany'a. Easya: "Neew'aa kũtavany'a kwĩ ũtulu. Ti ngũĩ, neew'aa kwĩ ũtulu vyũ. Ĩndĩ ĩla nathyũmũĩe wĩa, mũtumĩa ũmwe nĩwandavisye kana eĩkwatya nĩngwosa ũvainia wa kĩla ĩvinda. O na nĩwanengie vomu nusũsye. Nĩnoosie ũvainia, na nambĩĩa kũmũvoya Yeova kĩla mũthenya andetheesye nĩeke kwĩw'a kũtavany'a kwĩ ũtulu." We Yeova nĩwamũsũngĩie? Easya atĩĩ: "Ũũ nĩ mwaka wa katatũ kuma noosa ũvainia. Nũndũ nĩnĩtavanasya mũno kwĩ tene na nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye maũndũ kuma kwĩ eĩtu-a-asa ala angĩ, nzĩa yakwa ya kũtavany'a ĩendeee na kũseũva. Matukũ aa ndyaasya ũtavany'a ndwĩ ũtulu, ĩndĩ naasya nĩnĩwendete. Na eka ũu, ngwatanĩo yakwa na Yeova nĩ ndũmu o na kwĩ ũndũ yailyĩ tene." Nĩ w'o, mboya sya Kathy nĩsyamũtetheeisye kũlũlũmĩlya vyũ ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova.
TETHYA A VAKU
16, 17. (a) No nginya twĩke ata nĩ kana ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova ĩendeee kũlũlũmĩla? (b) Nĩ thĩna wĩva wa mwanya ũneeneetwe ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
16 Vai ĩvinda yĩkesa kũvika wasye nĩwaeka kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova. No nginya twose matambya nĩ kana tũmũthengeee Ngai ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda atũthengeee. Kwoou o na kwĩthĩwe kũilyĩ ata, tũikaaeke kũea ngewa na Ngai witũ kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kũvoya. Nũndũ wa ũu ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova ĩkaendeeaa kũlũlũmĩla, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu ĩitũtetheesya kũkĩlya vinya matatwa.
17 Ĩndĩ nĩtũtonya kũkwatwa nĩ thĩna ũmwe mũito. Thĩna wĩva? Mavinda amwe nĩtũtonya kwona mathĩna ala twĩ namo mateũthela o na kau nĩtũvoyete mũno na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo. Mavindanĩ ta asu nĩtũtonya kwambĩĩa kũemwa nĩ kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova ũndũ tũnamũĩkĩĩaa tene. Nĩ laisi tũkambĩĩa kwĩkũlya ethĩwa Yeova nĩwĩthukĩĩasya mboya sitũ, na ethĩwa nũtũtalaa ta twĩ anyanyae. Ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mesilya ta asu tũtonya kũmakĩlya vinya ata twĩsĩ kana ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova yĩ o vo? Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩneeneete thĩna ũsu.

translation:
"Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you." —Jas. 4:8.
1. Is it possible for us to strengthen our friendship with Jehovah by being humble?
DO YOU HUMBLE yourself to honor Jehovah and let his Spirit guide you? If so, you are showing that you value your friendship with God. Our friendship with God helps us to remain loyal during this time of Satan's influence, and it gives us strength. Dear Christian, cultivate humility. For this reason, we can strengthen our friendship with Jehovah by remaining humble and obedient.
2. (a) What does it mean to be humble? (Consider the examples.) (b) How can we strengthen our friendship with Jehovah?
2 How can you strengthen your friendship with Jehovah? Perhaps you wonder what it means to be humble. The scripture at James 4:8 sheds light on this. It says: "Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you." This scripture shows that your friendship with Jehovah depends on your initiative. * What does it involve to draw near to God? It involves praying regularly and earnestly and seeing how Jehovah answers our prayers. When we do this, our friendship with him grows stronger. And why does this help us to stay spiritually strong when we face trials? Because we feel close to Jehovah. We are reminded of the example of Jesus, who said: "My teaching is not my own; it comes from the One who sent me." (John 7:28, 29) So, what practical steps can we take to draw near to Jehovah?
3. Can you become closer to Jehovah?
3 Becoming closer to Jehovah each day is one way to show your love for him and to express your desire to please him. But how can you become closer to God? Of course, if you were trying to get to know someone better, would you spend little time with that person? No, you would make an effort to get to know him well. Similarly, spend time with Jehovah each day. (Read Psalm 142:2.) Also, if you read his Word daily and meditate on it, you will come to appreciate him more. (Read Isaiah 30:20, 21.) See how becoming closer to Jehovah strengthens our friendship with him and helps us to remain spiritually strong when we face trials.
JEHOVAH APPRECIATES YOUR EFFORTS
4, 5. Does Jehovah use his Word to encourage you? Consider how.
4 It is encouraging to know that God has caused the Bible to be written for each individual. But does this mean that the Bible reveals something personal about our desire to please Jehovah? Yes, it does. How so? By carefully studying and applying the Bible. However, if you simply read without thinking, you may miss important points and fail to see what the Bible means to you personally. When you do this, you will come to appreciate Jehovah more and realize that he uses his Word to help you.—Heb. 4:12; Jas. 1:23-25.
5 For example, consider Jesus' command: "Seek first the kingdom of God." This reminds us that if we want to please God, we must prioritize spiritual things. The Bible helps us to understand how Jehovah feels about us and our circumstances. So, when we apply this principle to our daily life and make spiritual matters a priority, the Bible can help us to see how Jehovah can bless us in practical ways.—Matt. 6:19, 20.
6, 7. (a) How does meditating on the Bible show that we love Jehovah, and how does Jehovah show that he loves us? (b) What can motivate us to meditate on the Scriptures regularly?
6 Indeed, meditating on the Scriptures helps us to see how much Jehovah values us and how he wants to strengthen our faith. Why? Because it helps us get to know Jehovah better and strengthens our love for him. And the more we love him, the more we value his guidance and discipline.—Read 1 Corinthians 8:3.
7 If we truly love Jehovah, we will be motivated to study the Bible regularly and thoughtfully. John 17:3 says: "This means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent forth." Notice that knowing God involves more than just being aware of his existence; it also involves 'knowing' him personally—that is, getting to know Jehovah intimately.—Read Psalm 33:13; Prov. 25:4.
8. (a) What can a brother learn from reading 2 Samuel chapter 15, verses 1-5, which tells what Jehovah allowed to happen to Absalom? (b) How can getting to know Jehovah help us cope with difficult situations?
8 We get to know Jehovah by speaking to him in prayer, by meditating on what we read in the Bible, and by seeing how he acts. For example, did you ever wonder what Jehovah allowed to happen to Absalom, a son of King David of Judah? (2 Sam. 15:1-5) As you read about Absalom, you likely noticed that he was a handsome man who had many friends and who was skilled in gaining their support. Yet, despite all this, Absalom rebelled against his father, and the Bible says that "Absalom made himself known so that Jehovah might look upon him." What does this mean? It shows that Absalom wanted Jehovah's approval. He thought that if he could impress people, Jehovah would favor him. But he was wrong! This account reminds us that simply doing good deeds is not enough to please Jehovah unless our motive is right. One way we show that we know Jehovah is by avoiding those who practice idolatry. (Jer. 30:11) Knowing this helps us remain loyal when faced with trials like those Absalom brought upon himself, and it encourages us to trust in Jehovah completely.
9 What things can help us understand why Jehovah favored Absalom?
9 There are several reasons why Jehovah favored Absalom. The Bible calls Absalom "beautiful." (2 Sam. 15:7, 32) Also, the account in 2 Kings 26:3-5, 16-21 helps us see that Absalom was concerned about justice, and he showed kindness to people. However, despite these qualities, Absalom proved unfaithful. A faithful man named Ahithophel gave Absalom bad counsel. Apparently, Ahithophel resented David and sought revenge. Did Absalom listen to Ahithophel? Yes, and this led to disastrous results. "The counsel of Ahithophel was like an oracle of God" in Absalom's eyes. But Jehovah will never approve of someone who turns away from righteousness!
10 How can we make sure that we truly understand what Jehovah looks for? Is it possible that we may think something pleases Jehovah when it really doesn't?
10 Let us consider how we can find out. We should study God's Word and meditate on its meaning. Does it seem reasonable that God would want us to be humble and obedient? Or would the Bible teach us something different than what our conscience tells us is right, and would it encourage us to disregard principles? (Prov. 32:4) We know that our God is called Jehovah, so we should love him wholeheartedly and try to understand what he looks for. Meditate on what God values, and ask yourself whether your thoughts and actions please him. (Ps. 77:12, 13) And if you have a close relationship with Jehovah, you will feel motivated to live in harmony with his will.
TO DEEPEN YOUR LOVE FOR JEHOVAH
11-13. How can you tell if Jehovah approves of you? (See footnote 19.)
11 To deepen your love for Jehovah is to strive to imitate him. We show this when we obey him, praise him, and trust in him. (Ps. 32:8) So, even if your relationship with Jehovah seems strained, do not think that he does not approve of you.
12 Some people may feel unworthy because of their past mistakes. They reason that if they were truly approved by Jehovah, they would not make such errors, and they would not struggle to overcome them. But remember that even if you feel this way, you can still find out if Jehovah accepts you.
13 Consider Jesus' example. He knew that Jehovah valued his ministry, so he spent much time in prayer. And even though Satan tempted him repeatedly, he continued to use his time to help others and to preach the good news. Did he ever wonder whether Jehovah still approved of him? (Luke 6:12; 22:40-46) Did he share his feelings with anyone, seeking reassurance that he was still pleasing Jehovah? No. Instead, like Jesus, we should be confident that Jehovah knows our heart. That is why one elder said: "I always try to pour out my heart to Jehovah. And I know that he understands me better than anyone else." Let us also confidently say: "Father, I thank you that you listen to me. And I trust that you will hear my prayers."—John 11:41, 42; Ps. 65:2.
14, 15. (a) What questions might we ask ourselves if we wonder whether we can please Jehovah? (b) How did one sister strengthen her relationship with Jehovah?
14 If you find yourself wondering whether you are pleasing Jehovah, remember that he values those who seek him earnestly, and he sees their efforts. Also, realize that if you are doing your best to serve Jehovah, he is aware of it. Furthermore, the more you endeavor to get to know Jehovah, the more you will trust in him.
15 Consider the example of Kathy. * She used to struggle with anxiety every day, often feeling overwhelmed. She says: "I would get anxious about school. Then I would get anxious about being anxious. I started making a list each day of things I was grateful for, and I tried to focus on positive things. And I prayed to Jehovah every evening, asking for help to cope with my anxiety. Did Jehovah help me? She explains: "It took about three months, but gradually my anxiety lessened. Now I can manage much better, and I have learned so much about coping with problems and staying calm. Some days I still feel anxious, but now I am able to deal with it. And most importantly, my relationship with Jehovah has grown stronger than ever." So, Kathy's experience shows how prayer can strengthen our relationship with Jehovah.
TRUE STORIES
16, 17. (a) Why is it important that our relationship with Jehovah continue to grow? (b) What practical step can we take to improve our spirituality?
16 Every day presents an opportunity to deepen your relationship with Jehovah. How can we make sure that we always appreciate what God does for us and continue to draw close to him? One way is to regularly study the Bible and pray. By doing so, our relationship with Jehovah will remain strong, and we will be better equipped to face life's challenges.
17 We may also struggle with personal weaknesses. What can help? Some find it helpful to identify specific areas where they need improvement and then work on them through prayer and self-discipline. Others may benefit from seeking advice from mature Christians. But most importantly, we must strive to love Jehovah and to imitate his qualities. It is vital that we remind ourselves of the reasons why we serve Jehovah and that we do not allow distractions to hinder our progress. If we stumble, can we still maintain our relationship with Jehovah? Yes, this scripture offers encouragement in this regard.

text:
1. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa alaĩka?
YEOVA nĩwendaa tũmanye ĩũlũ wa ala wĩkalaa namo ĩtunĩ, na alaĩka nĩ amwe katĩ wa asu. Mbivilianĩ, alaĩka metĩtwe 'ana ma Ngai.' (Yovu 38:7) Alaĩka matethasya wĩa mwaũ? Matetheeisye andũ ata ĩvindanĩ ĩvĩtu? Na nĩmatonya kũtũtetheesya ũmũnthĩ?—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 8.
2. Alaĩka maumie va? Nĩ alaĩka meana moombiwe?
2 Nĩtwaĩle kũmanya vala alaĩka maumie. Ĩandĩko ya Akolosai 1:16 nĩyonanĩtye kana ĩtina wa Yeova kũmũmba Yesũ, nĩwasyokie oomba syĩndũ ila ingĩ syonthe "sya ĩtunĩ na sya kũũ nthĩ." Na alaĩka nĩ amwe moombiwe. Nĩ alaĩka meana moombiwe? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana kwĩ alaĩka milioni maana maingĩ.—Savuli 103:20; Ũvuan'yo 5:11.
3. Ĩandĩko ya Yovu 38:4-7 yonanĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa alaĩka?
3 Mbivilia nĩtũmanyĩĩtye kana Yeova oombie alaĩka atanamba kũmba nthĩ. Mo meewie ata ĩla moonie nthĩ yoombwa? Ĩvuku ya Yovu yonanĩtye kana nĩmatanie. Alaĩka mamũthũkũmaa Yeova me na ngwatanĩo.—Yovu 38:4-7.
ALAĨKA NĨMATETHEEASYA ANDŨ MA NGAI
4. Twĩsĩ ata kana alaĩka nĩmendeeaw'a nĩ andũ?
4 Kuma tene alaĩka methĩĩtwe mayendeew'a nĩ andũ, na mayendeew'a nĩ kĩeleelo kya Yeova kwondũ wa nthĩ na andũ. (Nthimo 8:30, 31; 1 Vetelo 1:11, 12) No nginya methĩwe meewie woo mũno ĩla Atamu na Eva mamũvĩtĩisye Ngai. Na no nginya ũmũnthĩ methĩwe mew'aa woo mũnango moona andũ aingĩ mateũmwĩw'a Yeova. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, alaĩka nĩmatanaa ĩla mũndũ weelila na amũsyokea Ngai. (Luka 15:10) Alaĩka nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai. Yeova nũmatũmĩaa kũtetheesya na kũsũvĩa athũkũmi make ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Aevelania 1:7, 14) Ekai twone ngelekany'o imwe syĩkwonany'a ũndũ ũsu.
5. Alaĩka matetheeisye athũkũmi ma Ngai ata ĩvindanĩ ya tene?
5 Yeova nĩwatũmie alaĩka elĩ makatetheesye Loto na mũsyĩ wake kũvonoka ĩla ndũa sya Sotomo na Ngomola syaanangawa. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 19:15, 16) Myaka maana maingĩ ĩtina wa vau, mwathani Ndanieli nĩwekiw'e ngunganĩ ya mĩnyambũ, ĩndĩ ndaalĩka nũndũ 'Ngai nĩwatũmie mũlaĩka wake, na atumya makanyw'a ma mĩnyambũ.' (Ndanieli 6:22) Ĩvindanĩ yĩngĩ, yĩla mũtũmwa Vetelo waĩ yela, Yeova nĩwatũmie mũlaĩka amũthasya. (Meko ma Atũmwa 12:6-11) O na ĩngĩ, alaĩka nĩmatetheeisye Yesũ yĩla waĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩtina wa kũvatiswa 'alaĩka nĩmamũthũkũmie.' (Maliko 1:13) Ĩngĩ, kavinda kakuvĩ Yesũ atanoawa ve mũlaĩka wookie "amwĩkĩa vinya."—Luka 22:43.
6. (a) Twĩsĩ ata kana alaĩka nĩmatetheeasya andũ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ? (b) Twĩsũngĩa makũlyo meva?
6 Ũmũnthĩ alaĩka mayumĩlĩĩlaa andũ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Ngai nũtũmĩaa alaĩka kũtetheesya athũkũmi make. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũlaĩka wa Yeova nũmathyũlũlũkaa ngalĩ syonthe ala mamũkĩaa, na kũmavonokya." (Savuli 34:7) Nĩkĩ twĩ na vata wa kũsũvĩwa nĩ alaĩka? Nũndũ twĩ na amaitha me vinya mũno ala mendaa kũtũũmĩsya. Amaitha asu naaũ? Maumie va? Matataa kũtũũmĩsya kwa nzĩa syĩva? Nĩ kana tũsũngĩe makũlyo asu, ekai twone kĩla kyeekĩkie kavinda kakuvĩ Atamu na Eva mamina kũmbwa.
AMAITHA MATONEKAA
7. Andũ mekĩte ata nũndũ wa kũkengwa nĩ Satani?
7 Kĩlungunĩ kya 3, nĩtweemanyĩisye kana ve mũlaĩka waleanile na Ngai na eethĩwa na wendi wa kũsumbĩka ala angĩ. Mbivilia yĩtĩte mũlaĩka ũsu Satani, ũla nĩwe Ndevili. (Ũvuan'yo 12:9) Satani endaa andũ o namo mamũlee Ngai. Nĩwamũkengie Eva, na kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu nũkengete andũ aingĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ andũ amwe ta Aveli, Enoko, na Noa nĩmaendeeie kwĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova.—Aevelania 11:4, 5, 7.
8. (a) Alaĩka amwe matw'ĩkie ndaimoni ata? (b) Ndaimoni syeekie ata nĩ kana ivonoke ĩla mbũa mbingĩ?
8 Ĩvindanĩ ya Noa alaĩka amwe nĩmaleanile na Ngai, matia wĩkalo woo wa ĩtunĩ, na mooka kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ me na mĩĩ ya andũ. Nĩkĩ meekie ũu? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana mendaa kũtwaana. (Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 6:2.) Ĩndĩ alaĩka asu mayaaĩlĩte kwĩka ũu. (Yuta 6) O ta alaĩka asu, andũ aingĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu nĩmathũkie mũno na meethĩwa me ang'endu. Kĩu nĩkyo kyatumie Yeova atw'a kwananga andũ onthe athũku kwa kũete mbua mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩwatangĩĩie athũkũmi make ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 7:17, 23) Namo ala alaĩka athũku nĩmasyokie ĩtunĩ nĩ kana mavonoke. Mbivilia yĩtĩte alaĩka asu athũku ndaimoni. Nĩmanyuvie kwĩthĩwa me alei ta Satani, na kwoou Ndevili atw'ĩka mũnene woo.—Mathayo 9:34.
9. (a) Kweethĩiwe ata ĩla ndaimoni syasyokie ĩtunĩ? (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ tũlungunĩ tũla tũatĩĩe?
9 Yeova ndaaĩtĩkĩla ndaimoni syĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo na alaĩka ala angĩ ĩtunĩ nũndũ nĩsyatw'ĩkie alei. (2 Vetelo 2:4) Ũmũnthĩ ndaimoni iyĩsa kwĩthĩwa na mĩĩ ta ya andũ, ĩndĩ no iendeee 'kũkenga andũ nthĩ yonthe.' (Ũvuan'yo 12:9; 1 Yoana 5:19) Ekai twĩmanyĩsye ũndũ ndaimoni isu ikengaa andũ aingĩ.—Soma 2 Akolintho 2:11.
ŨNDŨ NDAIMONI IKENGAA ANDŨ
10. Ndaimoni itũmĩaa nzĩa syĩva kũkenga andũ?
10 Ndaimoni ikengaa andũ kwa nzĩa mbingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ nũtonya kwĩlikya maũndũnĩ ma ndaimoni nowe mwene, kana akeka ũu kwĩsĩla mũndũ mũe, kana mũndũ ũngĩ wĩ na ũtonyi wa kũneenany'a na maveva. Maũndũ onthe ala makonanĩtye na ndaimoni nĩ maũndũ ma ũwe, ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩtũkanĩtye twĩvathane vyũ na maũndũ asu. (Akalatia 5:19-21) Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o tondũ mũsyĩmi ũtũmĩaa kĩtei kũkwatya nyamũ, now'o ndaimoni itũmĩaa ũkengani kũkwatya, na kũsumbĩka andũ.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 26.
11. Kũaũsya nĩ kyaũ, na nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩvathana nakw'o?
11 Nzĩa ĩmwe ndaimoni itũmĩaa kũkenga andũ nĩ kũaũsya. Kũaũsya nĩ kũtata kũmanya ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte kana ĩũlũ wa maũndũ matesĩkĩe ũtũmĩĩte vinya wa ndaimoni. Mũndũ no atate kwĩka ũu kwa kũsoma ndata, kũsoma moko, kwĩkya mbũũ, na kũkũna ũta. Andũ aingĩ monaa kwĩka maũndũ asu ta kũtesa kũmaetee mũisyo, ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o. Maũndũ asu no maetee mũndũ mũisyo mũnene mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia nĩtũtavĩtye kana awe me ngwatanĩo na ndaimoni. Ĩandĩko ya Meko ma Atũmwa 16:16-18 yonanĩtye kana ve "veva wa kũaũsya" watetheeisye mwĩĩtu ũmwe "kũaũsya." Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa mũtũmwa Vaulo kũlũngya veva ũsu, kana ndaimoni, ũtonyi wa kũaũsya wa mwĩĩtu ũsu nĩwathelile.
12. (a) Nĩkĩ tũtaĩlĩte kũneenany'a na akw'ũ? (b) Nĩkĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai matelikasya syĩthĩonĩ ikonetye maũndũ ma ndaimoni?
12 Ve nzĩa ĩngĩ ndaimoni itũmĩaa kũkenga andũ. Nitataa kũtũkenga tũĩkĩĩe kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka tũkaneena na andũ ala makwie. O na no itũkenge tũĩkĩĩe kana akw'ũ me thayũ, na no tũneene namo, no matũtetheesye, kana makatũũmĩsya. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mũndũ wakw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũnyanyae kana o mũndũ wa mũsyĩ, no athi kwa mũndũ waasyaa e na ũtonyi wa kũneena na ala akw'ũ. Mũndũ ũsu nũtonya kũweta ũndũ wa kwendeesya ĩũlũ wa mũndũ ũsu mũkw'ũ, kana akeka ũndũ vakauma wasya ũvw'anene na wa mũndũ ũsu mũkw'ũ. (1 Samueli 28:3-19) O na ĩngĩ, maũndũ maingĩ ala andũ mekaa mũndũ akw'a monanasya kana nĩmaĩkĩĩaa kana akw'ũ me thayũ vandũ vangĩ. Amwe ma maũndũ asu nĩ syĩthĩo ila iatĩĩawa ĩvinda ya mathiko, mĩthenya ya kũlilikana ala akw'ũ, kũthembea ala akw'ũ, na maũndũ angĩ ala mekawa mathiko matambĩĩe ta kũlikya mwĩĩ wa ũla mũkw'ũ nyũmba, kũsunga mbũa, na kwĩkĩa ngũa nziũ nũndũ nĩ mũthenya wa mathiko. Ĩla Aklĩsto malea kwĩlikya maũndũnĩ asu, andũ ma mũsyĩ kana ma ndũa yoo nĩmatonya kũmaumany'a, kũmaneenea naĩ, kana makaeka kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo namo. Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto nĩmesĩ kana mũndũ akw'a ndaendeeaa kwĩthĩwa thayũ vandũ vangĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, tũitonya kũneena na akw'ũ na maitonya kũtũũmĩsya. (Savuli 115:17) Kwoou ndũkaatate kũneenany'a na akw'ũ kana ndaimoni, na ndũkaatate kwĩlikya syĩthĩonĩ ikonetye maũndũ ma ndaimoni.—Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 18:10, 11; Isaia 8:19.
13. Andũ aingĩ ala tene makĩaa ndaimoni mekĩte ata?
13 O vamwe na kũkenga andũ, ndaimoni nitumaa andũ mekala me na wia. Ũmũnthĩ, Satani na ndaimoni syake nĩmesĩ matialĩtye "kavinda o kanini" Ngai amavetange ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, na nĩkyo kĩtumi me na ũng'endu na ũthilĩku mwingĩ. (Ũvuan'yo 12:12, 17) O na ũu wĩ o vo, andũ ngili mbingĩ ala tene makĩaa ndaimoni nĩmaekete kũikĩa. Nĩ kyaũ kyamatetheeisye maeka kũkĩa ndaimoni?
ĨVATHANE VYŨ NA MAŨNDŨ MA NDAIMONI
14. O ta Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa, tũtonya ata kwĩvathana na ndaimoni?
14 Mbivilia nĩtũtavĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩsiĩĩa na kwĩvathana na ndaimoni. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ amwe ndũanĩ ya Eveso nĩmaneenanasya na ndaimoni matanamba kũmanya ũla w'o. Nĩ kyaũ kyamatetheeisye maeka kwĩka ũu? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Andũ aingĩ ala meekaa maũndũ ma ũwe maete mavuku moo na moomban'ya vamwe, na mamavĩvĩsya mbee wa andũ onthe." (Meko ma Atũmwa 19:19) Nũndũ nĩmendaa kũtw'ĩka Aklĩsto, nĩmavĩvisye mavuku moo onthe ala makonetye maũndũ ma ũwe. O na ũmũnthĩ andũ onthe ala mekwenda kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩmaĩle kwosa ĩtambya ta yĩu. Nĩmaĩle kwananga syĩndũ syonthe ila me nasyo ikonetye ndaimoni. Syĩndũ isu nĩ ta mavuku, makaseti, sinema, mbathi, mathaũ, na kĩndũ kyonthe kĩla kĩtumaa ndaimoni kana ũwe syoneka syĩ sya kwendeesya na ta itatonya kũetee mũndũ mũisyo. O na syĩndũ ila andũ mekĩaa nĩ kana mesiĩĩe maikakwatwe nĩ ũndũ mũthũku no ikonanĩtye na ndaimoni.—1 Akolintho 10:21.
15. Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana tũmũsiĩĩe Satani na ndaimoni syake?
15 Myaka yĩana ũndũ mũna ĩtina wa andũ ma Eveso kwananga mavuku moo ala maĩ na maũndũ makonetye ũwe, mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie kana nĩmaaĩle kũendeea "kũkĩlan'ya vinya" na "nguthu sya maveva ma ũthũku." (Aeveso 6:12) Kwoou, o na kau maĩ mavĩvisye mavuku asu, ndaimoni no syaendeee kũtata kũmaũmĩsya. Nũndũ wa ũu, maaĩle kwĩka ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva? Vaulo ameie atĩĩ: 'Osai ngao ya mũĩkĩĩo, ĩla kwondũ wayo mũkatonya kũvosya [kana, kũsiĩĩa] mĩsyĩ yonthe yĩ na mwaki ya ũla mũthũku.' (Aeveso 6:16) O ũndũ ngao ĩsũvĩaa mũsikalĩ ndakaũmĩw'e e kaũnĩ, now'o mũĩkĩĩo ũtonya kũtũsũvĩa. Twaĩkĩĩa vyũ kana Yeova no atũsũvĩe, tũkamũsiĩĩa Satani na ndaimoni syake.—Mathayo 17:20.
16. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũmũĩkĩĩe Yeova mũnango?
16 Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũmũĩkĩĩe Yeova mũnango? Nĩtwaĩle kũsomaa Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya na tũyĩmanyĩsya kũmwĩkwatasya Yeova atũsũvĩe. Twamũĩkĩĩa Yeova vyũ, Satani na ndaimoni maikatonya kũtũũmĩsya.—1 Yoana 5:5.
17. Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva tũtonya kwĩka tũkesũvĩana na ndaimoni?
17 Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva Aklĩsto ma Eveso maaĩle kwĩka? Nũndũ mekalaa ndũanĩ yausĩe maũndũ ma ndaimoni, Vaulo ameie atĩĩ: 'Voyaai mavinda onthe.' (Aeveso 6:18) Maaĩle kũmũvoya Yeova amasũvĩae mavinda onthe. Nao nata naitũ? Twĩkalaa nthĩ yusĩe maũndũ ma ndaimoni, na kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũmũkũlya Yeova atũsũvĩae. O na nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩaa ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩla tũũvoya. (Soma Nthimo 18:10.) Yeova ndakalea kũsũngĩa mboya sitũ twaendeea kũmũvoya atũsũvĩane na Satani.—Savuli 145:19; Mathayo 6:13.
18, 19. (a) Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũsinde Satani na ndaimoni syake? (b) Nĩ ĩkũlyo yĩva yĩsũngĩĩtwe kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe?
18 Twaananga syĩndũ syonthe ila twĩ nasyo ikonanĩtye na ndaimoni na twamwĩkwatya Yeova atũsũvĩe, nĩtũtonya kũsinda Satani na ndaimoni. Vai vata wa kũendeea kũkĩa Satani na ndaimoni. (Soma Yakovo 4:7, 8.) Yeova e vinya mwingĩ kwĩ ndaimoni. Nĩwasyoseie ĩtambya ĩvindanĩ ya Noa, na ĩvinda yũkĩte akasyananga. (Yuta 6) O na ĩngĩ, lilikana kana tũikũkita na ndaimoni twĩ ithyoka. Yeova nũtũmĩaa alaĩka make nĩ kana atũsũvĩe. (2 Asumbĩ 6:15-17) Kwoou, no twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana twamwĩkwatya Yeova, nĩtũtonya kũsinda Satani na ndaimoni.—1 Vetelo 5:6, 7; 2 Vetelo 2:9.
19 Ĩndĩ ethĩwa Satani na ndaimoni nĩmo matumĩte kwĩthĩwa na thĩna wingĩvĩte ũu, nĩkĩ Ngai ũtaamananga? Ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩyĩsũngĩĩtwe kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe.

translation:
1. Are we able to appreciate God's creation?
JEHOVAH wants us to appreciate his creation and to live forever, and creation is part of his family. In fact, angels are called 'sons of God.' (Job 38:7) How did creation begin? Did it happen gradually or quickly? And why should we care?—Read Proverbs chapter 8.
2. What about the angels? Are they created beings?
2 We need to know what the angels are. The scripture at Colossians 1:16 tells us that when Jehovah made Jesus, he created everything else "in heaven and on earth." And the angels are created beings. Are they created beings? The Bible shows that there are millions of them.—Psalm 103:20; Hebrews 5:11.
3. What does Job 38:4-7 tell us about the beginning of creation?
3 The Bible teaches us that Jehovah created the angels at some point. Was there a time when nothing existed? The book of Job shows that it is possible. The angels rejoice because of Jehovah's work.—Job 38:4-7.
ANGELS REJOICE BECAUSE OF GOD
4. Does this mean that angels are like humans?
4 It is true that angels can appear like humans, and they act as Jehovah's representatives to help people. (Proverbs 8:30, 31; 1 Peter 1:11, 12) But remember what happened when Adam and Eve disobeyed God. And remember that humans often make mistakes and turn away from Jehovah. So angels are happy when someone returns to God. (Luke 15:10) Angels are servants of God. Jehovah uses them to teach us and encourage his servants forever. (Ephesians 1:7, 14) Let us now consider how this applies to us.
5. How did angels rejoice because of humans in the past?
5 Jehovah sent angels to rescue Lot and his family from Sodom and Gomorrah just before they were destroyed. (Genesis 19:15, 16) Many years later, Daniel was in a lion's den, an angel told him: "God sent his angel and shut the mouths of the lions." (Daniel 6:22) On another occasion, the apostle Peter was in prison, Jehovah sent an angel to free him. (Acts 12:6-11) Also, angels helped Jesus during his ministry on earth. For example, it is said that "angels ministered to him." (Mark 1:13) Once, while Jesus was praying, an angel strengthened him.—Luke 22:43.
6. (a) What does it mean that angels rejoice over humans? (b) What will we discuss next?
6 Angels take a keen interest in humans. In fact, God sends angels to help those who love him. The Bible says: "The angel of Jehovah encamps around those who fear him, and rescues them." (Psalm 34:7) Should we be comforted by this? Why? What qualities do we need to show so that angels will assist us? What qualities should we avoid? Is it easy to please God? Or is it difficult to get his assistance? Perhaps we can learn something by considering what happened to Adam and Eve.
QUALITIES THAT MATTER
7. How did Satan influence people?
7 In Chapter 3, we learned about angels who remained loyal to God and those who rebelled against him. The Bible identifies one rebellious angel as Satan, also known as the Devil. (Revelation 12:9) Satan misleads people and turns them away from God. He tempted Eve, and as a result, many people have chosen to disobey God. Some men, such as Abel, Enoch, and Noah, remained faithful to Jehovah.—Hebrews 11:4, 5, 7.
8. (a) Did some angels become demons? (b) What do demons do, and how does their activity affect us?
8 During the Flood, some angels sided with wicked humans, engaged in improper relations with human women, and produced offspring called Nephilim. Why did they do this? The Bible indicates that they desired power. (Read Genesis 6:2.) However, most angels remained loyal. (Jude 6) Both angels and humans were affected by the wickedness of the Nephilim. This is why God decided to flood the earth, wiping out most of mankind. But he preserved those who were righteous. (Genesis 7:17, 23) Those wicked angels lost their position in heaven and were imprisoned. The Bible calls those angels demons. We can be sure that Satan and the Devil are behind much of the trouble caused by demons.—Matthew 9:34.
9. (a) What happens when demons try to harm us? (b) What can we learn from this discussion?
9 Jehovah allows demons to influence people to test our loyalty. (2 Peter 2:4) Demons use temptation and deception to lead people away from God, and they continue "to mislead the entire inhabited earth." (Revelation 12:9; 1 John 5:19) Consider how demons deceive people.—Read 2 Corinthians 2:11.
HOW DEMONS DECEIVE PEOPLE
10. How do demons deceive people?
10 Demons deceive people in many ways. For example, a person might be attracted to demonic teachings, or demons might exploit someone's weaknesses, or a person might have a strong desire for things that are harmful. Anything that promotes false worship is connected to demons, and the Bible warns us to avoid such things. (Galatians 5:19-21) Why? Because what may seem harmless can actually give demons an opportunity to control us, and they take advantage of our weaknesses.—Read Proverbs 26.
11. To summarize, what have we learned, and why is it important?
11 One way demons deceive people is through superstitions. Superstition is believing that future events are determined by magic or occult forces. A person who gives in to superstition may consult fortune-tellers, read horoscopes, practice witchcraft, or wear charms. Many people believe in such practices because they offer comfort during difficult times, but this is misguided. Such beliefs can lead to great distress. For instance, the Bible condemns consulting spirit mediums. The account in Acts 16:16-18 shows how a "spirit of divination" enabled a certain girl "to foretell." But when Paul expelled the demon, the girl's ability to tell fortunes was gone.
12. (a) Why should we avoid associating with those who practice the occult? (b) Why do true Christians reject superstitious beliefs?
12 In another way, demons deceive people. It is often hard to determine whether something is truly demonic or simply a coincidence. They may also deceive us through dreams, and we might be influenced by them without realizing it or being aware of it. For example, a person grieving over a loved one might feel compelled to talk to the dead. That person may try to learn what his departed loved one is doing or thinking. (1 Samuel 28:3-19) Also, many others seek guidance from spirits or pretend to communicate with the dead. Some of these practices involve rituals like sacrifices, offerings, seances, and various ceremonies—all of which are condemned in God's Word, as well as things like interpreting omens, practicing astrology, and looking for meaning in unusual occurrences. But Christians should avoid such practices, because those who practice spiritism or witchcraft can easily become obsessed with them, manipulated by them, or controlled by demons. Indeed, a Christian should never attempt to get involved with spirits or seek their help. Through them, we can be deceived and misled. (Psalm 115:17) Therefore, do not consult spirits or demons, and do not try to understand the meanings of demonic activities.—Read Proverbs 18:10, 11; Isaiah 8:19.
13. Many people wonder why so many believe in demons.
13 Besides deceiving people, demons cause them great suffering. Actually, Satan and his demons constantly strive to make humans believe "the lie" that God does not care about them, and this contributes to much distress and unhappiness. (Revelation 12:12, 17) So it is not surprising that many people believe in demons and want to know more about them. What makes people susceptible to believing in demons?
HOW TO DEAL WITH DEMONIC INFLUENCES
14. Since Christians have the Holy Spirit, can they ever come into contact with demons?
14 The Bible shows us how we can protect ourselves from coming into contact with demons. For example, some men in Ephesus tried to perform exorcisms, but they were attacked by a demon. What made them vulnerable? The Bible says: "Many of those who practiced occult arts brought their books together and publicly burned them in front of everyone." (Acts 19:19) By turning to Christ, they destroyed many valuable objects that were connected with the occult. Also, those who sincerely desire to please Jehovah will discard any object that might lead them into association with demons. This includes things like amulets, charms, séances, ouija boards, superstitions, and anything else that may glorify demons or give them attention. Furthermore, things that people believe in—such as magic, astrology, and spiritism—can also involve demons.—1 Corinthians 10:21.
15. What is one way we can avoid being influenced by Satan and his demons?
15 Years ago, when people in Ephesus discarded their amulets and objects connected with the occult, the apostle Paul wrote to encourage them to continue "wrestling" against "the wicked spiritual forces." (Ephesians 6:12) Today, too, even if we have already gotten rid of harmful objects, demons will keep trying to mislead us. So, what can help us resist them? Paul advised: "Take up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to extinguish all the fiery darts shot forth by the wicked one." (Ephesians 6:16) Just as a shield protects a soldier, faith can protect us. We need to trust that Jehovah will strengthen us so that we can resist Satan and his demons.—Matthew 17:20.
16. How can we show that we trust Jehovah?
16 How can we show that we trust Jehovah? We can do so by regularly reading the Bible and meditating on how Jehovah can help us. The more we get to know Jehovah, the less susceptible we will be to the influence of Satan and his demons.—1 John 5:5.
17. What can we do to remain separated from demons?
17 What did the Christians in Ephesus do to remain separated from demons? They were encouraged by Paul to "pray constantly." (Ephesians 6:18) Constant prayer shows our reliance on Jehovah. And what about us? We should avoid getting involved in spiritistic practices, and we should keep asking Jehovah to help us. Also, we should make good use of God's Word. (Read Proverbs 18:10.) Jehovah is willing to help those who turn to Him for protection from Satan.—Psalm 145:19; Matthew 6:13.
18, 19. (a) Can we succeed in resisting Satan and his demons? (b) What important lesson can we learn from this?
18 Although we are imperfect, if we stay close to Jehovah and ask him for help, we can resist Satan and his demons. It takes effort to resist Satan and his demons. (Read James 4:7, 8.) Jehovah has great power over demons. He allowed Noah to survive the global flood, and he destroyed the wicked angels. (Jude 6) So, even if demons harass us, we can be confident that Jehovah will protect us. (2 Corinthians 6:15-17) Therefore, if we humble ourselves under God's hand and seek his help, we can resist Satan and his demons.—1 Peter 5:6, 7; 2 Peter 2:9.
19 One way Satan and his demons try to influence people is by appealing to their pride. Does God care about our pride? This is an important lesson to remember.

text:
1, 2. Nĩ ĩkũlyo yĩva waĩle kwĩkũlya, na nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩkũlya ũu?
KWA kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, nũmanyĩte kana andũ aingĩ ala maasyaa nĩmamũthaithaa Ngai, mamanyĩasya na makeka maũndũ ala Ngai ũmenete. (2 Akolintho 6:17) Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova ũtũtavĩtye tume ndĩninĩ sya ũvũngũ, kana 'Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene.' (Ũvuan'yo 18:2, 4) Waĩle kwĩka ata? Kĩla ũmwe witũ e na ũtwi waĩle kwĩka, na kwoou twaĩle kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Nyie nĩngwenda kũmũthaitha Ngai kwosana na ũndũ we ũkwenda, kana nĩenda kũmũthaitha kwosana na ũndũ nĩthĩĩtwe ndimũthaitha?'
2 Ethĩwa nĩwumĩte ndĩninĩ ya ũvũngũ, nĩwĩkĩte nesa. Ĩndĩ nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wendeeaw'a nĩ maũndũ kana syĩthĩo imwe iatĩĩawa ndĩninĩ sya ũvũngũ. Ekai tũneenee syĩthĩo imwe na tũyona nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata tũsyonae kwa nzĩa ĩla Yeova ũsyonaa.
KŨTHAITHA MĨVW'ANANO NA AAŨMAE MAITŨ ALA MAKWIE
3. (a) Nĩkĩ andũ amwe matonya kwona ne ũndũ wĩ vinya kũeka kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ũthaithinĩ woo? (b) Mbivilia yaasyaa ata ĩũlũ wa kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ĩla tũũmũthaitha Ngai?
3 Kwa myaka mingĩ, andũ amwe nĩmethĩĩtwe maitũmĩa mĩvw'anano kana mathembo mĩsyĩnĩ kwoo ĩla mekũthaitha Ngai. Ethĩwa nĩwĩkaa ũu, no wĩw'e ne ũndũ wĩ vinya kana ũte ũndũ waĩle kũthaitha Ngai ũteũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ĩsu. Ĩndĩ lilikana kana Yeova nũtũmanyĩasya ũndũ twaĩle kũmũthaitha. Na Mbivilia nĩtũtavĩtye nesa kana Yeova ndendaa tũtũmĩe mĩvw'anano ĩla tũũmũthaitha.—Soma Kuma 20:4, 5; Savuli 115:4-8; Isaia 42:8; 1 Yoana 5:21.
4. (a) Nĩkĩ tũtaĩle kũthaitha aaũmae maitũ ala makwie? (b) Nĩkĩ Yeova weeie andũ make maikaaneene na akw'ũ?
4 Andũ amwe nĩmatonya kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yingĩ na vinya mwingĩ nĩ kana matanĩthye aaũmae moo ala makwie. O na no mamathaithe. Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩmanyĩĩtye kana akw'ũ maitonya kũtũtethya na maitonya kũtũũmĩsya. O na nĩtwĩmanyĩĩtye kana vai vandũ maendaa kwĩkala makw'a. Kwa w'o, nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũtũlikya mũisyonĩ kũneena na akw'ũ nũndũ ndeto ila itonya kwoneka ta syumĩte kwa mũndũ witũ wakwie, syĩthĩawa syumĩte kwa ndaimoni. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova weeaĩe Aisilaeli maikaaneene na ala akw'ũ, kana kwĩlikya ũndũnĩ o na wĩva ũkonanĩtye na ndaimoni.—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 18:10-12; soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 26 na 31.
5. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũeke kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ũimũthaitha Ngai kana ũeke kũthaitha aaũmae maku ala makwie?
5 Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya ũeke kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ũimũthaitha Ngai kana ũeke kũthaitha aaũmae maku ala makwie? Nĩwaĩle kũsomaa Mbivilia na ũisũanĩa kwa ũliku ũndũ Yeova wonaa maũndũ asu. Yeova onaa maũndũ asu me "ũthatyo" kana me mathũku. (Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 27:15) Voyaa Yeova kĩla mũthenya nĩ kana aũtetheesye wĩthĩwe na woni ta wake ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu, na aikũtetheesya ũmũthaithe kwa nzĩa ĩla wendaa. (Isaia 55:9) Manya kana Yeova nũkũũnenga vinya ũla ũkwenda nĩ kana wĩvathane vyũ na kĩndũ kyonthe kĩkonanĩtye na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ.
YO NĨTWAĨLE KŨTANĨA KĨLISIMASI?
6. Nĩkĩ andũ manyuvie Matukũ 25, Mwei wa 12, wĩthĩwe mũthenya wa kũlilikanaa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ?
6 Ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, Kĩlisimasi nĩ ĩmwe ya sikũkũ ila syĩ nguma mũno, na andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana sikũkũ ĩsu nĩ ya kũlilikana kũsyawa kwa Yesũ. Ĩndĩ ũw'o nĩ kana Kĩlisimasi yumanĩte na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩeleetye kana Alomi ala matamũthaithaa Ngai nĩmatanĩaa mũthenya wa kũsyawa kwa syũa Matukũ 25, Mwei wa 12. Atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmendaa andũ aingĩ ala matamũthaithaa Ngai matw'ĩke Aklĩsto, kwoou o na kau Yesũ ndaasyawa Matukũ 25, Mwei wa 12, nĩmatwie kũlilikanaa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ matukũ asu. (Luka 2:8-12) Amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ mayatanĩaa Kĩlisimasi. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yaĩtye kana kwa myaka 200 kuma Yesũ asyawa, "vai mũndũ weesĩ nesa vyũ ĩla wasyaiwe, na no andũ anini mendaa kũmanya ũu." (Sacred Origins of Profound Things) Sikũkũ ya Kĩlisimasi yambĩĩie myaka maana meana ũndũ mũna Yesũ aumie kũũ nthĩ.
7. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto ma w'o matatanĩaa Kĩlisimasi?
7 Andũ aingĩ nĩmesĩ kana Kĩlisimasi na syĩthĩo ila syĩkawa mũthenya ũsu, ta kũnengane mĩthĩnzĩo na kũmbana nĩ kana andũ metanĩthye, syaumanie na andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, nthĩ ya England na isionĩ imwe sya Amelika, ve ĩvinda andũ mavatĩtwe kũtanĩa sikũkũ ya Kĩlisimasi nũndũ yaumanĩte na andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai. Mũndũ ũla weethĩwa aitanĩa sikũkũ ĩsu nĩwooseawa ĩtambya. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda, andũ nĩmambĩĩie ĩngĩ kũtanĩa sikũkũ ya Kĩlisimasi. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto ma w'o matatanĩaa Kĩlisimasi? Nũndũ nĩmendaa kũmwendeesya Ngai maũndũnĩ onthe ala mekwĩka.
YO NĨTWAĨLE KŨTANĨA MŨTHENYA WA KŨSYAWA?
8, 9. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya tene matatanĩaa mũthenya wa kũsyawa?
8 Sikũkũ ĩngĩ ĩtanĩawa nĩ andũ aingĩ mũno nĩ sikũkũ ya mũthenya wa kũsyawa. Yo Aklĩsto nĩmaĩle kũtanĩa mũthenya woo wa kũsyawa? Sikũkũ sya mũthenya wa kũsyawa ila iwetetwe Mbivilianĩ syaĩ sya andũ matamũthaithaa Yeova. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 40:20; Maliko 6:21) Sikũkũ sya mũthenya wa kũsyawa syaĩ sya kũkumya ngai sya ũvũngũ. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa "moonaa kũtanĩa mũthenya wa kũsyawa ne kĩthĩo kya andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai."—The World Book Encyclopedia.
9 Alomi na Akiliki ma tene maĩkĩĩaa kana ve veva weethĩawa vo ĩla kĩla mũndũ ũkũsyawa, na veva ũsu wasũvĩaa mũndũ ũsu thayũnĩ wake w'onthe. Andũ ala mataĩ Aklĩsto ĩvindanĩ yĩu nĩmatanĩaa mũthenya woo wa kũsyawa nũndũ masũanĩaa kana kwĩka ũu no kũtume ngai syoo isũvĩa mũndũ ũla wasyaiwe mũthenya ũsu.
10. Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto mataĩle kũtanĩa sikũkũ ya mũthenya wa kũsyawa?
10 We nũkwona Yeova ta wĩtĩkĩlaa sikũkũ ikonanĩtye na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ? (Isaia 65:11, 12) Ndesa kwĩtĩkĩla. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi tũtatanĩaa mũthenya wa kũsyawa kana sikũkũ ĩngĩ yumanĩte na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ.
VE VATA WA KŨMANYA MWAMBĨLĨĨLYO WA SIKŨKŨ ISU?
11. Nĩkĩ andũ amwe matanĩaa sikũkũ? Nĩ ũndũ wĩva waĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩ wa vata vyũ kwaku?
11 Andũ amwe nĩmesĩ kana sikũkũ ya Kĩlisimasi na sikũkũ ingĩ syumanĩte na andũ matamũthaithaa Ngai, ĩndĩ nĩmaendeeaa kũitanĩa. Monaa kana ĩvinda yĩu ya sikũkũ nĩ mwanya mũseo wa kũkomana na andũ ma mũsyĩ. We wonaa ũu? Ti ũthũku kwenda kwĩthĩwa vamwe na andũ maku ma mũsyĩ. Yeova nĩwe wambĩĩisye mũsyĩ, na endaa twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe namo. (Aeveso 3:14, 15) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, twaĩle kwĩthĩwa tũisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova vandũ va kwendeesya andũ maitũ ma mũsyĩ kwa kwĩtanĩthya na sikũkũ sya ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi mũtũmwa Vaulo waisye atĩĩ: "Mũkĩthima maũndũ ala mamwendeeasya Mwĩaĩi."—Aeveso 5:10.
12. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma sikũkũ yĩthĩwa ĩteũmwendeesya Yeova?
12 O na kau andũ aingĩ monaa kana ti ũndũ wa vata kũmanya mwambĩĩo wa sikũkũ ila andũ matanĩaa, Yeova ndethĩawa na woni ta ũsu. Yeova ndetĩkĩlaa sikũkũ ila syumanĩte na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ kana ila ikumasya andũ kana nthĩ yoo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Amisili nĩmeethĩawa na sikũkũ mbingĩ sya kũkumya ngai syoo sya ũvũngũ. Ĩtina wa Aisilaeli kuma nthĩ ya Misili, nĩmeekie ũndũ weekawa nĩ andũ ala matamũthaithaa Ngai ma nthĩ ya Misili, na meeta ũndũ ũsu "mboka kwondũ wa Yeova." Ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwamasilĩile nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu. (Kuma 32:2-10) Kwoou o tondũ mwathani Isaia waisye, tũyaĩle 'kũkiita kĩndũ kĩvuku.'—Soma Isaia 52:11.
ĨKALANY'A NA ANDŨ ALA ANGĨ KWA ŨĨ
13. Nĩ makũlyo meva ũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũyĩkũlya ĩla watw'a kũeka kũtanĩa sikũkũ?
13 Watw'a kũeka kũtanĩa sikũkũ no wĩthĩwe na makũlyo maingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, no wĩkũlye-ĩ, Naĩle kwĩka ata andũ ala tũthũkũmaa ĩmwe mangũlya nĩkĩ ndatanĩaa Kĩlisimasi vamwe namo? Naĩle kwĩka ata mũndũ akanenga mũthĩnzĩo wa Kĩlisimasi? Naĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa ũla tũtwaanĩte nake nũkwenda nĩtanĩe sikũkũ? Ndonya kũtetheesya syana syakwa ata nĩ kenda iikew'e ta ve kĩndũ ikosete nũndũ wa kũlea kũtanĩa sikũkũ kana mũthenya wa kũsyawa?
14, 15. Ũtonya kwĩka ata ethĩwa mũndũ akwĩa wĩthĩwe na sikũkũ nzeo kana nĩwakũnenga mũthĩnzĩo?
14 Nĩ ũndũ wa vata ũtũmĩe kĩlĩko ĩla watw'a kũneenea ũndũ mũna kana kũwĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla andũ meũkwĩa nĩwĩthĩwe na sikũkũ nzeo, ndwaĩle kũmavũthĩĩsya. No ũmasũngĩe kwa kũmea atĩĩ: "Nĩ mũvea." Ĩndĩ ĩla mũndũ wenda kũmanya maũndũ maingangĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo waku, no ũtw'e kũmũelesya nĩkĩ ũtatanĩaa sikũkũ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, mavinda onthe ĩkaa ũu kwa nzĩa nzeo, tũmĩaa ũĩ, na ũyĩthĩwa na ndaĩa. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndeto syenyu syĩthĩwe na mumo mavinda onthe, isamae mũnyũ, nĩ kana mũmanye ũndũ mwaĩlwe nĩ ũsũngĩa kĩla mũndũ." (Akolosai 4:6) No ũsũngĩe mũndũ kwa kũmwĩa kana nĩwendete kũtũmĩa ĩvinda vamwe na andũ ala angĩ na kũmanenga mĩthĩnzĩo, ĩndĩ ndwĩkaa ũu maũndũnĩ makonanĩtye na kũtanĩa sikũkũ.
15 Ũtonya kwĩka ata mũndũ aũnenga mũthĩnzĩo? Mbivilia ndĩtũnengete mĩao ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu, ĩndĩ nĩyonanĩtye kana nĩtwaĩle kũtata ũndũ tũtonya twĩthĩawe na wasya mũseo wa ngoo. (1 Timotheo 1:18, 19) Nĩvatonyeka ũla ũkũũnenga mũthĩnzĩo akethĩwa atesĩ kana ndũtanĩaa sikũkũ. Kana no akwĩe atĩĩ: "Nĩnĩsĩ ndũtanĩaa sikũkũ, ĩndĩ nĩngwenda kũũnenga mũthĩnzĩo ũũ." Maũndũnĩ asu me kĩvathũkany'o, nue waĩle kũtw'a ethĩwa nũkwĩtĩkĩla mũthĩnzĩo ũsu kana ndwĩwĩtĩkĩla. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa wĩtw'a kwĩka ata, tata mũno wĩthĩwe na wasya mũseo wa ngoo. Tũyenda kwĩka ũndũ ũtonya kwananga ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova.
WAĨLE KWĨKALANY'A ATA NA ANDŨ MA MŨSYĨ WAKU?
16. Waĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa andũ ma mũsyĩ waku meenda kũtanĩa sikũkũ?
16 Waĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa andũ ma mũsyĩ waku nĩmekwenda kũtanĩa sikũkũ? Ndwaĩle kũmasiĩĩa. Lilikana kana nĩmo maĩle kwĩtw'ĩĩa ũndũ maĩle kwĩka. Ĩkalany'a namo nesa na ũinenga motwi moo ndaĩa o ũndũ ũkwenda manenge motwi maku ndaĩa. (Soma Mathayo 7:12.) Ĩndĩ waĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa andũ ma mũsyĩ waku meenda ũtũmĩe ĩvinda vamwe namo ĩla mekũtanĩa sikũkũ? Ũtanamba kwĩka ũtwi, mũvoye Yeova aũtetheesye kwĩka ũtwi mũseo. Sũanĩa ũndũ ũsu nesa na ũyĩka ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ waw'o. Lilikana kana wendi waku nĩ kũmwendeesya Yeova mavinda onthe.
17. Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũtetheesye syana syaku iikew'e ite mbĩanĩe ĩla andũ ala angĩ mekũtanĩa sikũkũ?
17 Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũtetheesye syana syaku ĩla syoona andũ angĩ maitanĩa sikũkũ? No ũvangae mavinda kwa mavinda ũkasyĩkaa tũmaũndũ tũseo. O na no ũinengae mĩthĩnzĩo itataĩĩe. Na mũthĩnzĩo ũla mũseo vyũ ũtonya kũinenga nĩ kũtũmĩa ĩvinda vamwe nasyo na kwĩthĩwa ũsyendete.
THAITHA NGAI KWA NZĨA ĨLA WE WENDAA
18. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũendaa maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto?
18 Nĩ kana tũmwendeesye Yeova, nĩtwaĩle kũtia ndĩni sya ũvũngũ vamwe na syĩthĩo na sikũkũ ila syumanĩte na ndĩni isu. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩtwaĩle kũthaitha Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Nzĩa ĩmwe nĩ kwa kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto tũte kũtĩĩa. (Soma Aevelania 10:24, 25.) Maũmbano nĩ ma vata mũno ũthaithinĩ wa w'o. (Savuli 22:22; 122:1) Nĩtwĩkĩanaa vinya ĩla twoombana vamwe.—Alomi 1:12.
19. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũtavya andũ angĩ ũw'o wa Mbivilia ũla wĩmanyĩĩtye?
19 Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kwĩka ũkonany'a kana nũnyuvĩte ũthaithi wa w'o nĩ kũneena na andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩla wĩmanyĩĩtye kũma Mbivilianĩ. Andũ aingĩ nĩmathĩnĩkaa nũndũ wa mothũku ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa wĩsĩ amwe mathĩnĩkaa, na no ũmatavye ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte ũla wĩ naw'o. Wathi maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto na watavya angĩ ũw'o wa Mbivilia, ndũkew'aa ũyenda kwĩthĩwa ndĩninĩ ya ũvũngũ kana ũyenda kwĩka maũndũ ala mekawa vo. Ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana watw'a kũmũthaitha Yeova kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte ũkeethĩwa wĩ mũtanu na Yeova akaathima kĩthito kyaku.—Malaki 3:10.
