translation:
1, 2. Is it possible to come out from her so as to survive, and what is this "her" that one needs to separate oneself from?
ACCORDING to the Bible, many faithful ones have separated themselves from the world and have cleansed themselves from the things defiling, pleasing God. (2 Corinthians 6:17) And that is why Jehovah has called his people to leave her, that is, "Babylon the Great." (Revelation 18:2, 4) How is this done? Each one of us can do so by asking himself: 'Do I want to please God along with my way of life, or do I want to please him according to what he approves?'
2 However, to remain neutral, one must be courageous. It is not easy to resist the pressure from the world and its philosophies. Let us examine how we can maintain our neutrality and show that we value what Jehovah values.
TO KEEP NEUTRALITY REGARDING THE WORLD'S ISSUES
3. (a) Why do some find it difficult to take a stand on issues involving politics? (b) What Scriptural principles can help us to remain neutral when pleasing God?
3 For many years, some have felt compelled to get involved in politics or to support certain parties because they believe it is the only way to please God. But if this is the case, does it mean that one cannot please God without getting involved in politics? No, because Jehovah knows how we can please him. And the Bible shows that Jehovah wants us to remain neutral in political matters.—Read Exodus 20:4, 5; Psalm 115:4-8; Isaiah 42:8; 1 John 5:21.
4. (a) How can we show respect for those in authority? (b) How does Jehovah view his loyal servants who are persecuted?
4 Some may spend much time and energy trying to influence people in positions of power. However, they often fail. We realize that their power is limited and that they can be influenced by others. Also, we know that bad people sometimes gain power. Therefore, it is important to be cautious when dealing with them, realizing that they may appear reasonable to us, but actually be motivated by demons. This is why Jehovah allowed ancient Israel to experience persecution at the hands of wicked rulers—to help them distinguish between true worship and demonism.—See Deuteronomy 18:10-12; read The Watchtower magazine articles numbered 26 and 31.
5. What can help you to remain neutral in political affairs and still please God, or show due respect for those in authority?
5 What can help you to remain neutral in political affairs and still please God, or show due respect for those in authority? By regularly reading the Bible and meditating on what it says, you will come to understand how Jehovah views matters. Jehovah understands our feelings and thoughts. (Deuteronomy 27:15) Jehovah knows each individual's heart and sees his motives, and he can discern whether someone is sincere or has ulterior motives. (Isaiah 55:9) Remember that Jehovah is able to accomplish his purpose regardless of all opposition from those who oppose true worship.
WHY SHOULD WE CELEBRATE CHRISTMAS?
6. Why do many people observe December 25 as a special day commemorating Jesus' birth?
6 In reality, Christmas is just one of many customs with pagan origins, and many people wonder if such days truly honor Jesus. In fact, Christmas has become associated with commercialism. One source states that ancient peoples celebrated the winter solstice by holding festivals honoring their gods. Historians say that many who claim to worship God observed December 25 as the birthday of the sun god. It seems that they later transferred this celebration to Christ, though Jesus was actually born on October 3, and not December 25, so they began celebrating Jesus' birth on that date. (Luke 2:8-12) There is no Scriptural basis for celebrating Christmas. Another source notes that for over 200 years after Jesus' death, "there was no observance of his birth at all, and Christians did not celebrate it." (Sacred Origins of Profound Things) The celebration of Christmas gradually developed over the centuries.
7. How did Christ feel about Christmas?
7 Many people associate Christmas with goodwill and kindness, but it often involves excessive spending and competition, rather than true spirituality and worship of God. For example, in England and some parts of America, people have come to view Christmas more as a social event than a religious holiday. Anyone who wishes can attend such celebrations. But despite this, people continue to observe Christmas. How did Christ feel about Christmas? They want to please God in everything they do.
DO WE NEED TO OBSERVE BIRTHDAYS?
8, 9. How did early Christians feel about observing birthdays?
8 Another day observed by many people is their birthday. Did Christ encourage his followers to observe birthdays? Birthdays were condemned by early Christians as being pagan in origin. (Ezekiel 40:20; Mark 6:21) Birthdays were associated with the worship of false gods. This is why early Christians were sent "to mourn for the customs of the people."—The World Book Encyclopedia.
9 Herod and Archelaus readily celebrated because they believed that everyone had a good day, and they wanted to make the person whose birthday it was happy. Others who followed Christ's teachings observed this birthday custom only if it meant showing respect or avoiding offending someone.
10. Should Christians observe birthdays?
10 Will Jehovah be pleased if we celebrate days connected with false religion? (Isaiah 65:11, 12) Of course not. That is why we should not observe birthdays or any other days linked with false religion.
WHAT CAN HELP YOU TO UNDERSTAND THE BIBLE'S VIEW OF BIRTHDAYS?
11. Why do some people observe birthdays? Is it right to feel pressured to join in such practices?
11 Some say that Christmas and other holidays connected with those who do not worship God are harmless traditions. Consider whether the joy you experience on such occasions is worth risking displeasing God. Do you not think it would be better to associate with sincere Christians? Jehovah created mankind, and he wants us to have a close relationship with him. (Ephesians 3:14, 15) So, instead of feeling obligated to participate in celebrations that may displease Jehovah, let us seek approval from him and from fellow worshippers who want to help others learn about Bible truth. That is why the apostle Paul wrote: "Prove what is acceptable to the Lord."—Ephesians 5:10.
12. What can motivate you to make Jehovah happy when celebrating days?
12 Many people realize that observing birthdays is wrong, but they still feel pressured to do so. Jehovah understands our feelings and will help us. Jehovah does not approve of days associated with spiritism or idolatry or any practice that dishonors him. For example, Ammonites celebrated many festivals honoring their false gods. The Israelites were reminded of this when dealing with the Moabites, and they learned a lesson about how to stand firm for true worship—to be "loyal to Jehovah." Jehovah helped them to overcome this temptation. (Numbers 32:2-10) Like Isaiah said, we need to 'get away from unclean things.'—Read Isaiah 52:11.
BE LOYAL TO JEHOVAH
13. What practical steps can you take to avoid being influenced to celebrate birthdays?
13 There are several practical steps you can take to avoid being influenced to celebrate birthdays. For instance, would you invite non-Witness friends over to your home for a Christmas party? Would you associate with someone who promotes Christmas? Would you allow yourself to be persuaded to participate in birthday celebrations? But what if family members insist, and you fear it might damage your relationship with them? Is it worth risking your spiritual health just to please others?
14, 15. How can you tactfully explain to someone why you do not celebrate birthdays or why you disapprove of the practice?
14 It is important to speak truthfully yet kindly. For example, when people invite us to parties, we tactfully decline. So when invited to a birthday celebration, we can politely say, "Thank you." Then, if the person expresses interest in learning more about our beliefs, we can share Bible principles with him. Otherwise, let your conduct be exemplary so that they may see your fine works and glorify God. The apostle Paul wrote: "Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to respond to each one." (Colossians 4:6) Be kind to others, but do not compromise your standards or join those who engage in practices that conflict with Bible principles.
15 Will you ever find yourself in a situation where someone pressures you to compromise your standards? The Bible gives guidance on this matter, helping us to determine whether something is wrong or whether we are simply being overly cautious. (1 Timothy 1:18, 19) We should not yield to pressure just because someone insists or threatens us. Instead, if you feel that compromising your standards would displease Jehovah, firmly say, "I am determined to maintain my integrity." Such determination will help you to stand firm and avoid compromising your conscience. But even if you are unsure, seek counsel from mature Christians. Let us strive to do what is pleasing to Jehovah.
DO YOU FIND IT DIFFICULT TO ASSOCIATE WITH PEOPLE AT WORK?
16. Are you finding it difficult to associate with people at work?
16 Are you finding it difficult to associate with people at work who engage in questionable conduct? It may be helpful to reflect on this. Consider whether there is something you can do to improve the situation. Apply the Golden Rule—treat others as you would like them to treat you. (Read Matthew 7:12.) But are you finding it difficult to associate with people at work who use abusive language or engage in immoral activity? Pray to Jehovah for strength and ask him to help you maintain a positive attitude. Examine your own heart and see if there is anything you can change. Remember that your employer may expect you to cooperate with certain individuals.
17. Will you ever find yourself in a situation where you are pressured to approve of the bad association of others?
17 Will you ever find yourself in a situation where you are asked to condone the bad associations of others? Then carefully weigh the scriptures. Also, examine your own heart and make sure you are not becoming desensitized to wrongdoing. And remember that approving of bad company can lead to spiritual deterioration.
SHOW RESPECT FOR THOSE WHO ARE DIFFERENT
18. How can we show respect for those who are different?
18 If we want to please Jehovah, we will endeavor to be considerate of others' feelings and customs, especially when dealing with those from different backgrounds. So how can we demonstrate our respect for God by the way we treat others? We should ask ourselves, "Is this something I would want done to me?" One way is by showing interest in Christian gatherings. (Read Hebrews 10:24, 25.) These meetings provide valuable spiritual refreshment. (Psalm 22:22; 122:1) Let us encourage one another.—Romans 1:12.
19. Why is it important to be able to explain Bible truths clearly?
19 We can help others appreciate and accept God's Word by expressing ourselves in a way that they can understand. Many people are prejudiced because of their upbringing. They may need time to overcome their misconceptions, and we must be patient with them. By attending Christian meetings and being able to explain Bible truths clearly, you will be equipped to share the good news with others effectively. You will also show genuine love for your neighbor and prove yourself worthy of Jehovah's favor.—Malachi 3:10.

text:
1, 2. Tũtonya kũkwata wĩvitho va ũmũnthĩ?
KWASŨANĨA ũtembeete nza mũthenya kũkĩte mbua mbingĩ na yĩ na kĩuutani. Ĩtina wa kavinda kanini, ũyona kwekala kĩvindu, na kũyambĩĩa kũtisa na kũtunduma. Na ĩndĩ kũyambĩĩa kua. Nũndũ wa ũu, ũimantha vandũ wĩvithe. Ũkona vandũ ũtonya kwĩvitha na vatekusya, wĩw'a wausya mũno!
2 Twĩkalĩte ĩvindanĩ yĩilyĩ ũu. Maũndũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ maendeee kũthũkĩĩa. No wĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nĩ va ndonya kũkwata wĩvitho?' Mũandĩki wa Savuli aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Nganeena ũndũ wa Yeova, Nĩwe wĩvitho wakwa na ngome yakwa yĩ vinya; Ngai wakwa, ũla nĩmũĩkĩĩaa." (Savuli 91:2) Yeova no ethĩwe wĩvitho witũ ĩla twĩ mathĩnanĩ, na nũtũnengae wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.
3. Tũtonya kũmũtw'a Yeova wĩvitho witũ ata?
3 Yeova atonya kũtũsũvĩa ata? No atũtetheesye tũkamanya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna, na e na ũtonyi mwingĩ kwĩ mũndũ o na wĩva ũla ũtonya kwenda kũtũũmĩsya. Ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mũisyo, twaĩle kwĩthĩwa twĩsĩ nesa vyũ kana ĩvinda yũkĩte Yeova akamina mathĩna asu. Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩaa vinya na ndeto ii: "Ĩyĩkalyei ene wendonĩ wa Ngai." (Yuta 21) Twaĩle kwĩkala vakuvĩ na Yeova nĩ kana atũtetheesye ĩla twĩ na mathĩna. Ĩndĩ tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata?
MWENDE NGAI NŨNDŨ NŨKWENDETE
4, 5. Yeova onanasya ata kana nũtwendete?
4 Nĩ kana twĩkale vakuvĩ na Yeova, twaĩle kũmanya ũndũ ũtwendete mũno wĩana. Sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ onthe ala Yeova wĩkĩte kwondũ witũ. Nũtũnengete nthĩ mbanake yusĩe mĩtĩ na nyamũ sya kwendeesya. O na nũtũnengete lĩu mũseo na kĩw'ũ kĩtheu kya kũnyw'a. Yeova nũtũmanyĩĩtye ĩũlũ wa ĩsyĩtwa yake na ndaĩa syake sya kwendeesya nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia. Na ũndũ ũla mũnene mũno nĩ kana nĩwatwonisye wendo ĩla watũmie Mwana wake mwendwa, Yesũ, oke kumya thayũ wake kwondũ witũ. (Yoana 3:16) Na nũndũ wa nthembo ĩsu, twĩ na wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.
5 Yeova nĩ ũũngamĩtye Ũsumbĩ wa Masia, ũla nĩ silikalĩ ya ĩtunĩ, na o mĩtũkĩ ũkamina mathĩna onthe. Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũkatw'ĩkĩthya nthĩ ĩno nzaũ, na kĩla mũndũ akekala e mũtanu na e na mũuo tene na tene. (Savuli 37:29) Ũndũ ũngĩ ũkwonany'a Yeova nũtwendete nĩ kana nũtũmanyĩasya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩkala nesa vyũ ũmũnthĩ. O na nũtũthoketye tũmũvoyae, na ethĩawa eyũmbanĩtye kwĩthukĩĩsya mboya sitũ. Kwa w'o, Yeova nĩwendete kĩla ũmwe witũ.
6 Ũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ Yeova nũkwendete? Ũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũmũtũngĩaa mũvea nũndũ wa maũndũ onthe ala wĩkĩte kwondũ waku. Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana, andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ maitũngaa mũvea. Na ũu now'o kwailyĩ ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ waĩ vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩvinda yĩmwe, Yesũ nĩwavoisye aũme ĩkũmi mawaĩte mangũ, ĩndĩ no ũmwe wamũtũngĩie mũvea. (Luka 17:12-17) Twaĩle kwĩthĩwa tũilyĩ ta mũndũũme ũsu kwa kũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mavinda onthe.
7 O naitũ nĩtwaĩle kũmwenda Yeova. Yesũ eeie amanyĩw'a make kana no nginya mamwende Yeova na ngoo yoo yonthe, thayũ woo w'onthe, na kĩlĩko kyoo kyonthe. (Soma Mathayo 22:37.) Oonanasya ata?
8, 9. Tũtonya kũmwony'a Yeova ata kana nĩtũmwendete?
8 Kwasya nĩtũmwendete Yeova nĩkũtoetye? Aiee. Ethĩwa nĩtũmwendete Yeova na ngoo yitũ yonthe, thayũ witũ w'onthe, na kĩlĩko kitũ kyonthe, tũkoonanasya ũu kwĩsĩla meko maitũ. (Mathayo 7: 16-20) Mbivilia ĩtũmanyĩasya kana ethĩwa nĩtũmwendete Ngai, tũkeew'aa mĩao yake. Nĩ vinya kwĩka ũu? Aiee, nũndũ mĩao ya Yeova "ti mĩito."—Soma 1 Yoana 5:3.
9 Ĩla twamwĩw'a Yeova, twĩkalaa twĩ atanu na twĩ eanĩe. (Isaia 48:17, 18) Ĩndĩ nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkalae vakuvĩ na Yeova? Ekai twone.
ENDEEA KŨMŨTHENGEEA YEOVA
10. Nĩkĩ waĩle kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova?
10 Watw'ĩkie mũnyanyae wa Yeova ata? Ĩla weemanyĩisye Mbivilia, nĩwamũmanyie Yeova mũnango na wambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo nake. Ngwatanĩo ĩsu yaku na Yeova no ĩelekanw'e na mwaki ũtekwenda ũivoa. O tondũ mwaki wendaa kwongelwa ngũ nĩ kana ndũkavoe, now'o o naku waĩle kũendeea kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ kana ngwatanĩo yaku nake yĩthĩwe yĩ ndũmu.—Nthimo 2:1-5.
11. Momanyĩsyo ma Mbivilia maĩle kũtuma wĩw'a ata?
11 Waendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, kwa w'o ũkamanya maũndũ matonya kũkiita ngoo yaku. Kwoona ũndũ amanyĩw'a elĩ ma Yesũ meewie ĩla wamaeleisye wathani wa Mbivilia. Maisye atĩĩ: "Ngoo sitũ itinew'a muutĩa yĩla ũnũũneenaa naitũ nzĩanĩ, aitũvuanĩsya maandĩko?"—Luka 24:32.
12, 13. (a) Wendo witũ kwa Ngai ũtonya kwĩka ata twaema kwĩsisya? (b) Tũtonya ata kũsiĩĩa wendo witũ kwa Yeova ndũkavoe?
12 O tondũ amanyĩw'a makiitiwe ngoo ĩla maeleiwe nĩ Maandĩko, o naku no wĩthĩwe weewie ũu ĩla wambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Kwĩka ũu nĩkwatumie ũmũmanya Yeova na ũmwenda, na ndwĩsa kwenda wendo ũsu ũvoe.—Mathayo 24:12.
13 Watw'ĩka mũnyanya wa Ngai, nĩwaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana ũendeee kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu nake. No nginya ũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wake na ĩũlũ wa Yesũ, na ũisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala ũkwĩmanyĩsya na ũndũ ũtonya kũmatũmĩa. (Yoana 17:3) Ĩla ũũsoma kana ũkwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ĩkũlasye makũlyo aa: 'Ũndũ ũũ wĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai? Nĩkĩ naĩle kũmwenda na ngoo yonthe na thayũ wakwa w'onthe?'—1 Timotheo 4:15.
14. Mboya ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ata tũendeee kũmwenda Yeova mũnango?
14 Ĩla wĩ na mũndũ wendete, nũneenaa nake kĩla ĩvinda, na ũu nũtumaa ngwatanĩo yenyu yĩthĩwa yĩ ndũmu. O ta ngelekany'o ĩsu, twaneena na Yeova kĩla ĩvinda kwĩsĩla mboya, wendo witũ kwake nĩwongelekaa. (Soma 1 Athesalonika 5:17.) Mboya nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa vata vyũ kuma kwa Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ. Twaĩle kũneenaa nake kĩla ĩvinda kuma ngoonĩ. (Savuli 62:8) Tũyaĩle kũtũngĩlĩĩlaa mboya sitũ, ĩndĩ syaĩle kwĩthĩwa syumĩte ngoonĩ. Twaendeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kũvoya kuma ngoonĩ, tũkamwenda Yeova mũnango.
TAVYA ANDŨ ANGĨ ĨŨLŨ WA YEOVA
15, 16. Wĩthĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a?
15 Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda kũendeeaa kwĩthĩwa vakuvĩ na Yeova, nĩtwaĩle kũneena na andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo witũ. Kũtavya andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ kĩanda kya mwanya mũno. (Luka 1:74) Na ũsu nĩ wĩa Yesũ wanengie Aklĩsto onthe ma w'o. Kĩla ũmwe witũ nĩwaĩle kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. We nĩwĩkaa ũu?—Mathayo 24:14; 28:19, 20.
16 Mũtũmwa Vaulo oonaa wĩa wa kũtavany'a wĩ wa vata mũno, na nĩkyo kĩtumi wawĩtie 'ũthwii.' (2 Akolintho 4:7) Kũtavya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova na kĩeleelo kyake nĩw'o wĩa ũla wa vata vyũ ũtonya kwĩka. Nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũmũthũkũma Yeova, na nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ kĩthito kitũ. (Aevelania 6:10) Wĩa wa kũtavany'a no ũkũtetheesye kũmũthengeea Yeova na ũyĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. O na ĩngĩ, wĩa ũsu no ũtetheesye ala meũkwĩthukĩĩsya mamũthengeee Yeova na mayĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. (Soma1 Akolintho 15:58.) Ve wĩa ũngĩ ta ũsu ũtonya kũtuma wĩthĩwa wĩ mwĩanĩe?
17. Nĩkĩ wĩa wa kũtavany'a waĩle kũtethw'a na mĩtũkĩ?
17 Wĩa wa kũtavany'a waĩle kũtethw'a na mĩtũkĩ vyũ. Nĩtwaĩle 'kũtavany'a ĩla ndeto,' na twaĩle kwĩka ũu twĩ 'athangaau.' (2 Timotheo 4:2) Andũ nĩmaĩle kwĩw'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũthenya mũnene wa Yeova wĩ vakuvĩ, wĩ vakuvĩ na nĩwĩkalaatĩte mũno." Mũminũkĩlyo "ndũkekala." (Nzevania 1:14; Avakuki 2:3) Kwoou, o mĩtũkĩ Yeova nũkwananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani. Ũndũ ũsu ũtanethĩwa, andũ nĩmaĩle kũkanw'a nĩ kana methĩwe matonya kũnyuva kũmũthũkũma Yeova.
18. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmũthaitha Yeova twĩ vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ ma w'o?
18 Yeova endaa tũmũthaithe twĩ vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ ma w'o. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩtũlilikanan'ye ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ kũthangaan'ya wendonĩ na mawĩanĩ maseo; tũtekũeka kũmbana kwitũ vamwe, o tondũ amwe mekaa, ĩndĩ tũkĩtaana; na mbee mũno, mũkyona mũthenya ũsu ũkĩthengeea." (Aevelania 10:24, 25) Nĩtwaĩle kũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũendae maũmbanonĩ onthe. Maũmbano nĩmatũnengae mwanya wa kwĩkĩana vinya na kũthangaany'a na ala angĩ.
19. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmende ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa Aklĩsto?
19 Wathi maũmbanonĩ, ũkakwata anyanya aseo ala makaũtetheeasya kũmũthaitha Yeova. Maũmbanonĩ asu, ũkakomana na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa me kĩvathũkany'o, ala matataa ũndũ matonya mamũthaithe Yeova o taku. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana masyaiwe me na naĩ o taku, na nĩmavĩtasya. Ĩla mavĩtya, ĩthĩwa wĩyũmbanĩtye kũmaekea. (Soma Akolosai 3:13.) Mavinda onthe tataa mũno wone ndaĩa nzeo ila ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa Aklĩsto methĩawa nasyo, nũndũ kwĩka ũu kũkaũtetheesya ũmende na ũimũthengeea Yeova mũnango.
THAYŨ WA W'O
20, 21. "Thayũ wa w'o" nĩ kyaũ?
20 Yeova endaa anyanyae onthe mekale nesa ũndũ vatonyeka. Mbivilia ĩtũmanyĩasya kana ĩvinda yũkĩte tũkekala thayũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũmũnthĩ.
21 Ĩvinda yũkĩte, tũkekala tene na tene, ĩndĩ ti o myaka 70 kana 80. Tũkatanĩa "thayũ wa tene na tene" twĩ na ũima wa mwĩĩ, mũuo, na twĩ atanu nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ na mbanake. Thayũ ũsu nĩw'o Mbivilia yĩtĩte "thayũ wa w'o." Yeova nĩwathanĩte kana akatũnenga thayũ ũsu wa w'o, ĩndĩ no nginya twĩke kyonthe kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana 'tũũlũmye.'—1 Timotheo 6:12, 19.
22. (a) Tũtonya kũlũmya "thayũ wa w'o" ata? (b) Nĩkĩ tũtesa kwĩmanthĩa thayũ wa tene na tene?
22 Tũtonya 'kũkwata [kana, kũlũmya] thayũ wa w'o' ata? No nginya 'twĩkae nesa' na 'tũyĩthĩwa twĩ athwii ma kwĩkaa nesa.' (1 Timotheo 6:18) Ũu wĩonany'a kana nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩa kĩla twĩmanyĩasya Mbivilianĩ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, tũikwata thayũ wa w'o nũndũ wa kĩthito kitũ ene. Tũyĩsa kwĩmanthĩa thayũ ũtathela. Thayũ ũtathela nĩ mũthĩnzĩo Yeova watwie kũnenga athũkũmi make ala aĩkĩĩku, na nĩ wonany'o wa "mumo" kana ũseo wake mwingĩ. (Alomi 5:15) Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ nĩwendaa vyũ kũnenga athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku mũthĩnzĩo ũsu.
23. Nĩkĩ waĩle kwĩka motwi ala maĩlĩte ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ?
23 Ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nyie nĩnĩmũthaithaa Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla wendaa?' Woona ve moalyũku waĩle kwĩka, ĩka ũu na mĩtũkĩ. Twamwĩkwatya Yeova na tweeka kyonthe kĩla tũtonya tũmwĩw'e, akeethĩwa e wĩvitho witũ. Akasũvĩaa andũ make ala aĩkĩĩku mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo ya nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani. Na ĩndĩ akaĩkĩĩthya kana tũkekala Nthĩ Nzaũ tene na tene, o tondũ wathanĩte. Vate nzika, no ũkwate thayũ wa w'o weeka motwi ala maĩlĩte ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ!

translation:
1, 2. Should we be anxious about our future?
TO BE reassured, remember that Jehovah cares deeply for us and has the power to help. Consider the example of a strong fortress, which offers security, and provides a place of refuge and protection. And it can also offer peace. Therefore, this is what he does for his people. He comforts those who are worried, so don't be afraid!
2 Let us examine this further. Many things in life are uncertain. So how can we answer the question, 'Should we be anxious about our future?' The psalmist David wrote: "I will say of Jehovah, 'He is my refuge and my stronghold, my God, in whom I trust.'" (Psalm 91:2) Jehovah is a refuge for us when we are troubled, and he strengthens us to face life's challenges.
3. Can we confidently turn to Jehovah for refuge?
3 Can Jehovah really sustain us? Yes, he can help us to cope with difficult situations, and he can teach us what we need to know to deal with problems, as well as give us strength to carry on. When we are sick, we may ask for help from doctors or seek treatment, knowing that Jehovah can bless their efforts. The Bible reminds us of this important principle: "Trust in Jehovah with all your heart." (Proverbs 3:5) We can remain close to Jehovah even when we are facing difficulties. But can we be sure of this?
LET GOD GUIDE YOU
4, 5. Does Jehovah ever abandon us?
4 When we stay close to Jehovah, we can learn how he feels about things. He understands our feelings because he created us. We can confide in him regarding our anxieties and fears. And we can also talk to him about our desires. Jehovah knows what is best for us and guides us through his Word, the Bible. Most importantly, he has shown us his love by sending his beloved Son, Jesus, to die for us. (John 3:16) And despite our imperfections, we can have confidence in his forgiveness.
5 Jehovah supports those who put faith in his Kingdom, which will soon bring peace and justice. This Kingdom will enable people to live forever in perfect health. (Psalm 37:29) Another way Jehovah shows us his love is by helping us to understand what we need to do to live a meaningful life. And he encourages us to pray to him regularly, assuring us that he listens. Therefore, Jehovah loves each one of us.
6 Can you imagine how much Jehovah cares for you? You can show your appreciation for everything he does for you by telling him so. Many people find it hard to express their gratitude. But Jesus gave an example of how to show thankfulness. On one occasion, Jesus healed ten men, but only one thanked him. (Luke 17:12-17) We can imitate those ten men by thanking Jehovah for all his blessings.
7 So let us continue to love Jehovah. Jesus emphasized that the most important thing is to love Jehovah with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. (Matthew 22:37.) Does that sound reasonable to you?
8, 9. How can we show our love for Jehovah?
8 Is loving Jehovah difficult? No. To show our love for Jehovah, we need to love him with all our heart, with all our soul, and with all our mind, and we should try to live according to his will. (Matthew 7: 16-20) The Bible helps us understand what it means to love God and obey his commands. How is this possible? Because Jehovah's commands "are not burdensome."—Read 1 John 5:3.
9 When we love Jehovah, we feel happy and peaceful. (Isaiah 48:17, 18) So why would we hesitate to draw close to Jehovah? Let us see.
LET US KEEP DRAWING CLOSE TO JEHOVAH
10. What will help you to keep drawing close to Jehovah?
10 Do you value your relationship with Jehovah? If you study the Bible regularly, you will get to know Jehovah better and appreciate his qualities more fully. Your personal relationship with Jehovah will become stronger when you meditate on what you learn. So even if you face difficulties, remember that keeping your relationship with Jehovah strong is vital.—Proverbs 2:1-5.
11. Can Bible reading ever become routine?
11 As you continue to read the Bible, you will learn many things that can improve your life. Notice how Jesus showed his disciples the importance of understanding the Scriptures. He asked them: "Did not my heart burn within me while he was speaking to me on the road and opening up the Scriptures to me?"—Luke 24:32.
12, 13. (a) How does our love for God motivate us to do good works? (b) How can we strengthen our love for Jehovah over time?
12 Since you appreciate the truths found in the Scriptures, you likely want to express your faith. This will help you to get to know Jehovah and love him more, and it will encourage you to demonstrate your love further.—Matthew 24:12.
13 We want to please God, so we should strive to remain close to him through prayer and study. Keep deepening your appreciation for his Word and the example of Jesus, and reject worldly values that could hinder your spiritual progress. (John 17:3) As you read or study the Bible, ask yourself these questions: 'Does what I am learning reveal Jehovah God's personality? Does this help me to love him more and to value his standards?'—1 Timothy 4:15.
14 What can help us to stay motivated as we continue to show our love for Jehovah?
14 But if you have a friend, you speak to him daily, and this strengthens your friendship. Similarly, if we speak to Jehovah each day through prayer, our love for him will grow stronger. (Read 1 Thessalonians 5:17.) Prayer is a vital means of communicating with our heavenly Father. We should speak to him daily. (Psalm 62:8) We need to make prayer a priority, setting aside specific times to be alone with him. By continuing to pray and meditate on God's Word, we strengthen our love for Jehovah.
WHY OTHER PEOPLE VALUE JEHOVAH'S FRIENDSHIP
15, 16. Why do people appreciate genuine friendships?
15 People enjoy being around those who share their beliefs and values, and they cherish the opportunity to discuss things that matter to them. Associating with others who love Jehovah is a privilege. (Luke 1:74) And this is what Jesus commissioned all Christians to do. Each of us has a responsibility to share the good news of God's Kingdom. Ask yourself this:—Matthew 24:14; 28:19, 20.
16 The apostle Paul recognized the importance of sharing his faith, and he referred to it as "ministry." (2 Corinthians 4:7) Sharing the truth about Jehovah and his purposes is a rewarding activity. It is a way to show gratitude to Jehovah, and it brings us joy. (Ephesians 6:10) This ministry also helps us to remain zealous and active in supporting God's Kingdom. Moreover, this ministry can help others to become zealous and active in supporting God's Kingdom. (Read 1 Corinthians 15:58.) So, how can you make your ministry more meaningful?
17. How can you prepare for the ministry?
17 We can prepare for the ministry by studying regularly. We should be ready to "give a defense" and be able to explain our beliefs clearly. (2 Timothy 4:2) People are often influenced by what they hear from others. The Bible says: "Jehovah is great and greatly to be praised." The expression "greatly to be praised" means "very powerful." (Nehemiah 1:14; Habakkuk 2:3) Therefore, we want to let Jehovah's qualities impress us so that we will not be misled by Satan's lies. If we are determined, people will be more likely to listen to us and accept the good news.
18. How can we cooperate with fellow Christians in the ministry?
18 Jehovah wants us to cooperate with fellow Christians in the ministry. The Bible says: "Let us consider how to incite one another to love and fine works, not forsaking the gathering of ourselves together, but encouraging one another, especially as we see the day drawing near." (Hebrews 10:24, 25) So we need to make an effort to attend meetings regularly. Meetings give us an opportunity to encourage each other and learn from others.
19. What can help us to succeed in helping young ones and new ones to become established Christians?
19 In the ministry, you may meet people who are interested in learning about Jehovah. At such times, you can associate with young ones and new ones who have a good reputation, and help them to stay zealous in serving Jehovah. And if they make mistakes, be forgiving. But always encourage them to continue progressing. (Read Colossians 3:13.) Parents and older Christians should set a fine example so that young ones will want to imitate their zeal and devotion to Jehovah.
WHY IT IS IMPORTANT
20, 21. What is "the time of the end"?
20 Jehovah wants all his servants to be active. The Bible shows that there will come a time when wickedness will abound and love will cool off.
21 That time is now, as we live during what the Bible calls "the time of the end." We might live for only another 70 or 80 years. We are living in "the last days," a time marked by wars, earthquakes, famines, and lawlessness. This time of the end is what the Bible refers to as "the time of distress." Jehovah has allowed this time of distress to test our faith and to show us whether we truly 'care for' spiritual things.—1 Timothy 6:12, 19.
22. (a) How can we 'lay hold of' "the time of the end"? (b) Why should we value "the last days"?
22 How can we 'lay hold of' "the time of the end"? By being 'generous' and 'ready to share.' (1 Timothy 6:18) This means using our time and resources to support God's work. Whether we can do much or little, we lay hold of "the time of the end" by making full use of our opportunities. Let us appreciate "the last days." These are precious times when Jehovah is gathering his faithful servants and strengthening them. They are a sign of his great love and concern for us.—Acts 5:15. So let us use our time wisely to serve Jehovah and to help others learn about him.
23. What will help you to remain spiritually alert during these last days?
23 Finally, ask yourself, 'Am I showing gratitude to God by the way I am living?' Yes, be determined to stay busy in doing good. Be loyal to Jehovah and devote whatever time you have to serving him, always remembering his purpose. He protects those who are loyal from the influence of Satan's wicked world. And even if we live through "the time of the end," he will sustain us. Therefore, lay hold of "the time of the end" and remain spiritually alert!

text:
"Woona wathi kũtavany'a ndũkasyoke vaa. Wasyoka nĩũtũlanga a maaũ." Natwie kũthi vyũ nũndũ wa ndeto isu ĩthe-akwa wandavisye. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kũtia syĩndũ nĩ kana nĩatĩĩe Mwĩaĩi. Ĩvinda yĩu naĩ o na myaka 16.
VAENDIE ata maũndũ mayĩsa kwĩkala ũu? Eka ngũelesye. Nasyaiwe Matukũ 29, Mwei wa 7, 1929, na neanĩa kĩsionĩ kya Bulacan, kĩla kĩ nthĩ ya Philippines. Tũyaĩ na syĩndũ mbingĩ nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu nthĩ yitũ yaĩ na thĩna mwingĩ wa mbesa (economic depression). Nĩkwambĩĩe kau ĩla naĩ wa mũika. Tũendeangĩe ita sya Japan nĩsyavithũkĩie nthĩ ya Philippines. Ĩndĩ nũndũ twekalaa vaasa na taoni, kaũ ũsu ndwaavika kĩsionĩ kitũ. Tũyaĩ na letiũ, televiseni, o na tũyakwataa makaseti ma maũvoo, kwoou twamanyaa maũndũ twatavw'a nĩ andũ angĩ.
Kwitũ tũsyaĩtwe twĩ nyanya, na ninyie wa kelĩ. Ĩla naĩ na myaka nyanya ũmau na ũsũa nĩmambosie ngekalae namo. O na kũtw'ĩka twaĩ ma Katholeki, Ũmau ndaleanaa na maũndũ ma ndĩni ingĩ, na kwoou nĩwoombanĩtye mavuku maingĩ ma ndĩni ala wanengawe nĩ anyanyae. Nĩngũlilikana aimbony'a tũvuku tũtatũ tweetawa Protection, Safety, na Uncovered tũla twaandĩkĩtwe na kĩthyomo kya Tagalog. * O na nĩwambonisye Mbivilia. Nĩnatanĩaa kũsoma Mbivilia, na mũno mũno ala mavuku ana ma Ũvoo Mũseo. Kĩu nĩkyatumie nenda kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ.—Yoa. 10:27.
ŨNDŨ NAMBĨĨE KŨMŨATĨĨA MWĨAĨI
Ita sya Japan syesie kuma Philippines mwakanĩ wa 1945. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu asyai makwa nĩmambĩie nĩnĩsyoke mũsyĩ. Ũmau nĩwambĩkĩie vinya nĩnũke. Kwoou nĩnenũkie.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini, twĩ Mwei wa 12, 1945, kakundi ka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kaumĩte taoninĩ ya Angat nĩkookie kũtavany'a ndũanĩ yitũ. Mũtumĩa ũmwe Ngũsĩ nĩwookie kwitũ na atũmanyĩsya kĩla Mbivilia yaĩtye kĩkethĩwa "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo." (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Nĩwatũthokisye tũi vandũ vamanyĩaw'a Mbivilia ũtũinĩ mũna waĩ vakuvĩ na witũ. Nyie nĩnaendie o na kau asyai makwa mayaathi. Vaĩ andũ ta 20, na amwe nĩmakũlilye makũlyo ma Mbivilia.
Nũndũ ndyaeleawa kĩla maneeneaa, noonie nĩ kavaa nũkĩle nĩthi. Ĩndĩ nakililye ndyũkĩla mambĩĩa kwina wathi wa Ũsumbĩ. Neewie wathi ũsu wĩ mũseo mũno, na nũndũ wa ũu navanga kwĩkala. Wathi na mboya syathela, kĩla ũmwe nĩwathokiw'e ũmbanonĩ waĩ taoninĩ ya Angat Wakyumwa ũla waatĩĩe.
Nyie na angĩ twaendie mũendo wa vakuvĩ maili atano (kĩlomita 8) tũyĩsa kũvika mũsyĩ kwa mwana-a-asa weetawa Cruz nũndũ nĩvo ũmbano ũsu waĩ. Vookie andũ 50. Kĩla kyanzeng'isye mũthenya ũsu nĩ kwona syana nini iyumya maelesyo o na kau maũndũ ala maneeneawa kuma Mbivilianĩ maĩ maito. Nĩnaendangie maũmbanonĩ asu na ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe nathokw'a nĩ mwana-a-asa ũmwe mũkũũ weetawa Damian Santos nĩkomele kwake. Tene mwana-a-asa ũsu aĩ meya ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu aĩ vainia. Ũtukũ ũsu twekalile nthĩ mũno tũineenea Mbivilia.
Tene ũsu aingĩ maitũ twoosaa ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ twamanya ũw'o wa mũsingi wa Mbivilia. Ĩtina wa kũthi maũmbanonĩ mavinda kauta, ana-a-asa mangũlilye nĩ na angĩ, "Nĩmũkwenda kũvatiswa?" Namasũngĩie namea, "Ĩĩ, nĩngwenda." Nĩneesĩ kana nĩnendaa 'kũmũthũkũma Mwĩaĩi Klĩsto.' (Ako. 3:24) Kwĩ Matukũ 15, Mwei wa 2, 1946, twaendie ũsĩnĩ waĩ o vau vakuvĩ na navatiswa nĩ na mwana-a-asa ũngĩ.
Nĩtwamanyie kana nũndũ yu twaĩ Aklĩsto avatise, nĩtwaaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya kũtavany'a tũteũtĩĩa. Ĩtambya yĩu noosie yĩyaatanĩthya ĩthe-akwa. Ambĩie atĩĩ: "We wĩ mũnini mũno, ndwaĩle kũtavany'a. Na eka ũu, kũindwa ũsĩnĩ kũikũtw'ĩkĩthya mũtavany'a." Namũeleisye kana nĩ kwenda kwa Ngai tũtavany'e ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. (Mt. 24:14) Na nasyoka namwĩa, "Nĩnaĩle kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto ũla namwĩvĩtĩe Ngai." Ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o ĩthe-akwa wandavisye ndeto ila nĩwetie mwambĩĩonĩ wa ngewa ĩno. Nĩwatw'ĩte vyũ kũmbata ndikatavany'e. Na ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mũthenya wakwa wa mbee kũtia syĩndũ nĩ kana nĩanĩsye mĩvango ya kĩ-veva.
Cruz na mũsyĩ wake nĩmambosie nĩkalae namo taoninĩ ya Angat. O na nĩmambĩkĩie vinya nĩtw'ĩke vainia, na meekĩa vinya mwĩĩtu ũla woo ĩlumaita wĩtawa Nora eke oou. Ithyelĩ twoosie ũvainia Ĩtuku 1, Mwei wa 11, 1947. Nora aendie taoninĩ ĩngĩ, nakwa naendeea kũtavany'a Angat.
MWANYA ŨNGĨ NAKWATIE WA KŨTIA KĨLA NAĨ NAKYO
Mwakanĩ wakwa wa katatũ kuma noosa ũvainia, mwana-a-asa weetawa Earl Stewart nĩwaumie ovisinĩ wa ũvonge ooka kumĩsya andũ mbee wa 500 ũvoo, ala moombanĩe kĩwanzanĩ kĩna taoninĩ ya Angat. Aumisye ũvoo ũsu na Kĩsũngũ, na ĩndĩ amina nalika vo nĩelesye kwa ũkuvĩ na kĩthyomo kya Tagalog kĩla waneenea. Naendete sukulu myaka mũonza tũ, ĩndĩ kĩla kyandethisye nĩ kana alimũ maitũ makothaa kũtũmĩa Kĩsũngũ maitũsomethya. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kyatumie nĩmanya Kĩsũngũ nĩ kana mavuku ma Tagalog ma kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia maĩ manini mũno. Nũndũ wa ũu maingĩ ala nasomaa maĩ ma Kĩsũngũ. Kwoou nĩnamanyĩte Kĩsũngũ kya kwĩana ũkethĩa no nĩtw'ĩke mũtavuta ũvoonĩ ũsu na mavindanĩ angĩ ĩtina wa vau.
Mũthenya ũsu naĩ mũtavuta wa ũvoo wa Mwana-a-asa Stewart, nĩwaweteie kĩkundi kĩla kyaĩ vau Angat kana ovisi wa ũvonge nĩwendaa kwĩta vainia ũmwe kana elĩ mathi makathũkũme Mbetheli. Maaĩle kũthi kũkwatĩĩa amisonalĩ ala maendaa ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa Theocracy's Increase Assembly ũla weekiwe mwaka wa 1950, New York, Amelika. Ninyie ũmwe neetiwe nĩthi. Nĩnatiie ĩngĩ syĩndũ imwe naĩ nasyo, natia kũndũ neesĩ na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa nathi kũtetheesya wĩa Mbetheli.
Navikie Mbetheli Matukũ 19, Mwei wa 6, 1950, na nambĩĩa wĩa ũla nanengiwe. Mbetheli yaĩ nyũmba nene ngũũ yathyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ mĩtĩ mĩnene. Yaakĩtwe kĩwanzanĩ kyaĩ kya eka ilĩ na nusu (1 ha). Vathũkũmaa ana-a-asa ta ĩkũmi na elĩ matatwaanĩte. Kwakya tene natethasya wĩa ikonĩ. Na ĩndĩ kuma saa itatũ ũu nathũkũmaa vala vavũĩawa ngũa, na wĩa wakwa waĩ kũkũna vasi. Ĩtina wa lĩu wa mũthenya naatĩĩa mũtalatala o ũsu. Ĩla amisonalĩ masyokie kuma ũla ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa nthĩ mbingĩ ndyaaĩnũka ĩndĩ naendeeie o kũthũkũma vau Mbetheli. Noovaa makaseti nĩ kana matũmwe, ngavanga ũndũ ala metĩtye makaseti meũmakwata, na nĩnathũkũmaa ovisinĩ wa kũthokya aeni. No twasye nathũkũmaa wĩa w'onthe ũla nanengwa.
KŨTIA PHILIPPINES NĨTHI SUKULU YA NGILEATI
Nĩ na angĩ thanthatũ kuma nthĩ ya Philippines nĩtwathokiw'e tũthi kĩlasi kya 20 kya Sukulu ya Ngileati mwaka wa 1952. Ũndũ ũsu wandanĩthisye mũno. Ĩndĩ syĩndũ mbingĩ ila twoonie na maũndũ maingĩ ala tweekie twĩ Amelika maĩ maũndũ tũtaĩ twaaona. Kwaĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũndũ maũndũ mailyĩ kaũtũinĩ kaitũ.
Kwa ngelekany'o, twaĩ no nginya twĩmanyĩsye kũtũmĩa masinĩ imwe sya sitima na mĩio ya nyũmba tũteesene nayo. Nayo nzeve ya kũu yaĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ya kwitũ! Mũthenya ũmwe naamũka kwakya naumaalile nza noona kwĩ kweũ mũno na kwĩ kwanake. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kwona ĩa. Na nĩw'o namanyie kaĩ kwĩ ĩa kwĩthĩawa kũthithĩte mũno ũu!
Ĩndĩ kwĩka moalyũku asu kũyaĩ thĩna mũnene nũndũ nĩnatanĩaa mũno maũndũ maseo ala tweemanyĩasya kũu Ngileati. Ala matũmanyĩasya nĩmatũmĩaa nzĩa nzeo syatũvikĩaa ngoonĩ. O na nĩtweemanyĩisye kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli nesa na kwĩmanyĩsya nesa. Vate nzika, maũndũ ala nemanyĩisye nĩ Ngileati nĩmandetheeisye naseũvangya ngwatanĩo yakwa na Yeova.
Namina sukulu natũmiwe ta vainia wa mwanya kwa kavinda kĩsionĩ kya New York City kĩtawa Bronx. Kĩu nĩkyanengie mwanya wa kũthi ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa New World Society Assembly ũla weekĩiwe o kũu Bronx kwĩ Mwei wa 7, 1953. Ĩtina wa ũmbano ũsu mũnene nĩnasyokie Philippines ngatethye wĩa ũngĩ nanengiwe.
KŨTIA MOSEO MA TAONI
Ana-a-asa ala maĩ ovisinĩ wa ũvonge mambĩie atĩĩ: "Yu twĩenda ũthi ũkatethye wĩa wa kũthyũlũlũka." Kĩu nakyo kyesaa kũnenga mwanya wa kũatĩĩa nyaaĩ sya Mwĩaĩi, ũla o nake waendaa taoninĩ syĩ kũasa na ndũanĩ syĩ kũasa akatetheesye malondu ma Yeova. (1 Vet. 2:21) Kĩsio kĩla naaĩwe nĩthyũlũlũkae kyoosete kĩsio kĩnene kya kĩthama kĩla kĩnene vyũ kya Philippines kĩtawa Luzon. Kĩsio kĩu naaĩwe nĩthyũlũlũkae kyakuĩte ivalo nene sya Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, na Zambales. Nĩ kana nĩvike taoni imwe naĩ no nginya nĩsĩle ila Iĩmanĩ sya Sierra Madre syĩ ivaũũko na mavia. Kũyaĩ ngalĩ syaendaa taoninĩ isu. Nũndũ wa ũu, neekaa kũkũlya atwai ma maloli ethĩwa no nĩlĩse ngekalĩla iting'ĩ ila meethĩawa makuĩte. Mavinda maingĩ nĩmambĩtĩkĩlasya, ĩndĩ kũthi na maloli asu kũyaĩ mũyo.
Ikundi mbingĩ iyaĩ nene mũno na iyekalĩte mũno kuma syambĩĩw'a. Kwoou ana-a-asa ikundinĩ isu nĩmatanĩaa mũno namatetheesya kũvanga maũmbano na ũtavany'a nesa.
Ĩtina nĩnesie kũaĩwa kĩsio kĩngĩ kya kũthyũlũlũka, kĩla kyakwete ngalĩko ya Bicol yonthe. Tũkundi twingĩ tũla twaĩ vau twataanĩsye mũno, na mavainia ma mwanya no ĩndĩ maĩ manambĩĩa kũtavany'a kũu. Mũsyĩ ũmwe naendie neethĩie wĩ kyoo kĩsaeny'e. Meekĩte kwĩnza kalima na ĩndĩ makakelany'a mĩtĩ ĩlĩ ĩũlũ wako. Ĩla nakinyie mĩtĩ ĩsu navotie nayo kalimanĩ. Ndikaaĩtw'a ĩta nambie kũvatethya wĩa mwingĩ mũno wa kwĩthesya!
Nĩ kũu Bicol nĩw'o nambĩĩe kũsũanĩa Nora, ũla wambĩĩe ũvainia ngalĩko ya Bulacan. Ĩvinda yĩu namũsũanĩaa aĩ vainia wa mwanya Dumaguete City, na nĩnaendie kũmwona kw'o. Nĩtwatinie kũandĩkanĩa valũa na ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kavinda twatwaana mwaka wa 1956. Kyumwa kya mbee twatwaana twaendie kũthyũlũlũka kĩkundi kĩ Kĩthamanĩ kya Rapu Rapu. Vau kĩthamanĩ kĩu nĩtwalasimĩkie kũthi mũno na maaũ twĩsĩle kũndũ kwĩ iĩma, ĩndĩ natanĩie ta kĩ kũtetheesya ana-a-asa me isionĩ syĩ vaasa nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa!
KWĨTWA MBETHELI ĨNGĨ
Twatethisye wĩa wa kũthyũlũlũka nĩ na Nora kwa kĩlungu kya myaka ta ĩna na ĩndĩ tweetwa ovisinĩ wa ũvonge tũkathũkũme vo. Twambĩĩe kũthũkũma Mbetheli Mwei wa 1, 1960, na kwoou nĩtũvekalĩte mũno. Ĩvindanĩ yĩla nĩtwĩe Mbetheli nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye maũndũ maingĩ nũndũ wa kũthũkũma na ana-a-asa me na ianda nene, nake Nora nũthũkũmĩte mawĩa meana ũna Mbetheli.
Nũndũ wĩ Mbetheli nũmanyaa maũndũ maingĩ, nĩnĩw'aa nĩ mũathime kwĩyonea ũndũ wĩa wa Yeova wĩanĩte nthĩ ya Philippines. Ĩla nakinyie Mbetheli ya mbee nĩ mwanake, nthĩ ya Philippines yaĩ atavany'a ta 10,000. Ũmũnthĩ ũũ kwĩ atavany'a mbee wa 200,000 na athũkũmi ma Mbetheli maana maingĩ, ala mathũkũmaa na kĩthito nĩ kana wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũendeee.
O ũndũ wĩa waendeeie na kũsonga mbee, now'o ovisi ũla waĩ vo wa Mbetheli waendie ũnyivĩte. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye yatwĩie tũmanthe kĩwanza twake ovisi ũngĩ mũnenange. Noosanie na mwana-a-asa ũla waũngamĩe mũvĩa wa kũtumbĩthya mavuku twalika ũtũinĩ, ũla watwĩe andũ aingĩ ma China. Twaendie kĩla nyũmba tũikũlya ene kana ve ũmwe wenda kũtũthooesya kĩwanza. Tũyaakitya mũndũ ũkwenda kũtũteea. O na mũtũi ũmwe eekie kũtwĩa: "Ithyĩ andũ ma China tũitesaa. Twĩkaa kũthooa."
Mũthenya ũmwe tũtataĩĩe mũndũ ũmwe waĩ na kĩwanza nĩwookie atũkũlya kana no twende kũkĩthooa nũndũ nĩwathamaa athi Amelika. Maũndũ ala meekĩkie ĩtina wa vau matũsaanĩisye nginya twoona ta tũkũota. Mũtũi ũngĩ nake avangie nũkũta kĩwanza na eekĩa ala angĩ maĩ vakuvĩ nake vinya o namo mathoosye. O na nĩtwesie kũthooa kĩwanza kya ũla mũndũ watwĩĩte "Ithyĩ andũ ma China tũitesaa." Ĩtina wa kavinda kanini twakwatie kĩwanza kyaĩ kĩnene mala atatũ kwĩ kĩla kyaakĩtwe ovisi wa Mbetheli. Ndi na nzika kana Yeova Ngai nĩwendaa ũndũ ũsu wĩkĩke.
Mwaka wa 1950 ninyie naĩ mũnini vyũ katĩ wa ala maĩ Mbetheli. Yu nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa nithyĩ akũũ vyũ. Ndyĩlilaa nĩ kwĩthĩwa naatĩĩie Mwĩaĩi o kũla kw'onthe wambonisye. Nĩ w'o asyai makwa nĩmandũngilye, ĩndĩ Yeova nũnengete mũsyĩ ũngĩ mũnene wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. Ndi na nzika o na vanini kana o na ethĩwa twanengwa wĩa wĩva, Yeova ndaleaa kũtũnenga kyonthe kĩla twĩ na vata nakyo. Nyie nĩ na Nora nĩtũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mũno nũndũ wa moseo ala ũtwĩkĩte, na nĩtũkwĩkĩa angĩ vinya mamũtate.—Mal. 3:10.
Ve ĩvinda Yesũ wathokisye mumya ũmwe wa koti weetawa Mathayo Livai amwĩa atĩĩ: "Mbikĩla." Athokw'a eekie ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Nake atia syĩndũ syonthe, na ookĩla amũvikĩla." (Luka 5:27, 28) O nakwa nĩnĩkwatĩte myanya ta ĩsu, na nĩngwĩkĩa onthe vinya kuma ngoonĩ meke oou nĩ kana mone moathimo maingĩ.
^ kal. 6 Twaumĩthĩtw'e nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, ĩndĩ yu nĩtwaekie kũtumbĩthw'a.

translation:
"She said she would return tomorrow. She left very early in the morning." I remember thinking about the story of my grandmother when I saw it. That is the story of a girl who almost didn't believe in God. That girl was only 16 years old.
DOES IT matter what happened then? Let me explain. She was born on February 29, 1929, in the province of Bulacan, which is part of the Philippines. We lived through many things during that time, and that story coincided with a great economic crisis. I will tell you something; it was a difficult time. We were invaded by Japan while they occupied the Philippines. And because we lived there then and always, our province suffered greatly. We had radios, televisions, and we listened to records of songs, so we knew what was happening with other people.
When we were young, and you too were young. It was a long time ago, and it seems like yesterday. And being raised as Catholics, I grew up with many religious traditions, and that is why I learned many good values from my parents. I recall three words we used to say: Protection, Safety, and Uncovered, which we wrote using the Tagalog language. * And I witnessed the Bible. I enjoyed reading the Bible, and little by little I learned the teachings of the New World Society. That is what motivated me to want to imitate Jesus' example.—John 10:27.
REASONS TO WANT TO IMITATE GOD
The invasion of Japan came to the Philippines in 1945. During that time, my grandmother told me she almost died. I grew up experiencing hardship. That is why I appreciate it.
On December 12, 1945, a group of Jehovah's Witnesses visited our house in Angat and offered us publications. One Witness explained to us that the Bible teaches things that are "beneficial for training in righteousness." (2 Tim. 3:1-5) We were happy to meet those knowledgeable people of the Bible who visited us, and you also experienced that during those times. There were about 20 of them, and some carried large Bibles.
I understood everything clearly, and now I still remember it well. I have always loved speaking about the Kingdom. Lately, this work has been very busy, and I feel that I need help. But with prayer, everyone received assistance in the house of Angat Wakyumwa where they preached.
You and I walked about five miles (8 kilometers) until we reached the home of a boy named Cruz, which was where our meeting was held. There were about 50 people. The main purpose of this visit was to see what information and teachings were found in the Bibles they brought. I appreciated those meetings, and on one occasion I stayed with a young man named Damian Santos at his home. That boy had no knowledge of our beliefs, and he listened attentively. That night we stayed up late studying the Bible.
Then we began to share the good news of the Bible with others. On the way to more meetings, children asked us, "Will you teach us?" I gladly replied, "Yes, I will." I realized that I was going 'to turn people away from darkness to light.' (Acts 3:24) On February 15, 1946, we went to another place with those visitors and were accommodated by a young man.
We learned that since Christ died, we should strive to imitate Jesus' example of preaching so that we might be saved. This message touched my heart deeply. He told me: "You are a fine person, I want to preach. And now, spreading the good news will help save lives." I understood that going to God would mean saving souls. (Matt. 24:14) And then I said, "I am willing to dedicate myself fully to serving God." That experience moved me greatly, though I still felt some fear. But I continued to preach despite my fears. Now that was the beginning of my life, and it made me realize the importance of dedicating myself to the truth.
Cruz and his family welcomed me to stay with them near Angat. And I helped them build a small house, and they also built another house for a woman named Nora. We dedicated that house on November 1, 1947. Nora went to another place, but I continued to preach in Angat.
ANOTHER EXPERIENCE THAT HELPED ME TO DEDICATE MYSELF FURTHER
During my third year of service, a young man named Earl Stewart organized a gathering of over 500 people, all interested in learning about Angat. He did this through the assistance of the Kapampangan language, which is widely spoken. I used that opportunity to share what I had learned about the Tagalog language. I attended school for several years, and during that time I realized that our teachers were trying to teach us Kapampangan. Another thing that helped me learn Kapampangan was that many Tagalogs used it to explain the Bible more clearly. Many of those things helped me read the Kapampangan Bible. Because of this, I became proficient in Kapampangan and we were able to spread the good news further with the help of others.
This experience with young man Stewart led me to join a group of Kapampangans who wanted to preach the good news, either individually or in groups, going from house to house. They invited me to attend a large assembly called "Theocracy's Increase Assembly" held in 1950 in New York, America. I was among those invited. I also took my wife and children and together we served at Bethel.
I arrived at Bethel on June 19, 1950, and was impressed by what I saw. Bethel was a large building surrounded by tall trees. It covered an area of about one and a half hectares (1.5 ha). About twenty children lived there. I too had the opportunity to serve. And almost every day at three o'clock we would go out in groups, and the local brothers would accompany us. This daily routine made this experience very enjoyable. But the most important thing was that this large assembly strengthened my desire to continue serving at Bethel. We received cassettes, sometimes several, and I enjoyed listening to them, and I continued to learn new things. We were happy to be among those invited.
GOING TO THE PHILIPPINES AND THEN GILEAD SCHOOL
In 1952, I went to the Philippines and was assigned to class 20 of Gilead School. That experience benefited me greatly. There were many things we learned that we hadn't seen in America. However, we adapted to the conditions there, and we found that life was simpler.
It was a good training period, and it helped us mature spiritually.
For example, we learned how to use simple tools like carts and household items to get around. But the best part was being able to return home! One day I woke up feeling unwell, so I asked permission to visit my family and my parents. That visit reminded me of the importance of staying close to our spiritual family. And that's when I realized how much I loved the truth!
Later, I began to appreciate the great value of the knowledge I gained at Gilead. That knowledge helped me to make wise decisions and to remain faithful. With time, the lessons I learned at Gilead strengthened my love for Jehovah and my determination to serve him.
After school, I was assigned to pioneer in the borough of the Bronx in New York City. The assignment involved attending a large assembly of the New World Society held in the Bronx in July 1953. The main purpose of that assembly was to encourage those who served in the Philippines.
GOING TO MANY PLACES
Some of the brothers told us: "You will go out and preach the good news." This meant that we would have the opportunity to share the truth with people in areas where there were few Witnesses, and we could help them to learn about God's Kingdom. (1 Pet. 2:21) As a result, several of us were sent to the island of Luzon in the Philippines. We preached in provinces such as Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, and Zambales. On one occasion, my companion and I had to cross the Sierra Madre mountains on foot because there were no roads. We walked for days, but we kept going. At times, we had to eat very little food, but we remained optimistic. Many people were interested, and we often found ourselves walking long distances to reach them.
Another challenge was that some places were difficult to reach. However, the brothers in those areas were always willing to help us arrange meetings and accommodations.
We also wanted to preach in another area, which covered all of the Bicol region. Several groups went there, and the local people were happy to hear the good news. One brother said that he felt refreshed when he heard it. He invited us to sit down and rest under the shade of his trees. But we declined, saying that we needed to continue our ministry. We wanted to help more people learn the truth!
It was in Bicol that I met Sister Nora, who came from Bulacan. She arranged for me to visit her family in Dumaguete City, and I traveled there to see them. We began corresponding regularly, and in 1956 we got married. After we got married, we went to preach to the congregation at Rapu Rapu. The brothers there helped us a lot, and we were grateful for their hospitality. I remember how happy we were to be able to serve Jehovah together!
TO BE CONTINUED
We continued preaching with Nora for about ten years, and we enjoyed our ministry very much. We moved to Bethel on January 1, 1960, and we were very happy there. While at Bethel, I learned many things about pioneering and raising children, and Nora also became skilled in caring for others at Bethel.
Because Bethel learns so much, it has become a training center for those serving Jehovah in the Philippines. But the Bethel home that I served in was small, with only about 10,000 pioneers in the Philippines. Now there are over 200,000 pioneers and many more Bethel homes, but continuing to train them is still important.
As the work progressed and expanded, many former Bethelites began to feel the need to go out again. That is why the Governing Body asked us to start a school to help them improve their skills. Along with our son, we helped those who wanted to return to China. We visited every house, sometimes staying overnight just to get to know people. We always looked for someone willing to listen to us. And one brother said to us: "The people in China need help. Let's go help them."
One day we met a man who was interested, and he invited us to stay overnight so we could discuss things further, especially since he had come from America. Other experiences like this helped us see how eager people were to hear the good news. Another brother also expressed his desire to return to China and said that he would continue to preach. And we were encouraged to preach the good news to those who said, "The people in China need help." During our travels, we often found large groups of people who were eager to learn more about the Bible and the truth. But we knew that Jehovah God wants this work to succeed.
In 1950, I joined the full-time ministry along with my wife. I had a strong desire to serve Jehovah fully. I realized that I needed to devote myself completely to the ministry, and Jehovah generously blessed me with strength and endurance. He helped me raise our children and grandchildren. But I knew that whether we live or die, Jehovah will support us in everything we do. My wife, Nora, and I continued to praise Jehovah for all his blessings, and we were grateful for the opportunity to experience so much joy.—Mal. 3:10.
Jesus once healed a man named Matthew Levi while he was sitting at the tax office and told him: "Follow me." What did he do? The Bible says: "He left everything behind and rose and followed him." (Luke 5:27, 28) And like him, I too abandoned my old life and experienced great joy in serving Jehovah.
^ kal. 6 We have learned that it is Jehovah's will for us to be zealous in proclaiming the good news.

text:
1. Nũũ waĩle kũtũtavya ũndũ twaĩle kũmũthaitha Ngai?
NDĨNI mbingĩ syasyaa imanyĩasya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o nũndũ ndĩni imanyĩasya maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai na ũndũ twaĩle kũmũthaitha. Tũtonya kũmanya ũthaithi wa w'o ata? No Yeova e weka ũtonya kũtũtavya ũndũ twaĩle kũmũthaitha.
2. Ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya ata ũndũ ũtonya kũmũthaitha Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle?
2 Yeova nũtũnengete Mbivilia nĩ kana twĩmanyĩsye ũndũ twaĩle kũmũthaitha. Kwoou ĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia, na nũndũ Yeova nũkũthĩnĩkĩaa, akaũtetheesya ũtetheke kumana na maũndũ ala ũkwĩmanyĩsya.—Isaia 48:17.
3. Ngai endaa twĩke ata?
3 Andũ amwe maasyaa kana Ngai etĩkĩlaa mothaithi onthe, ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o Yesũ wamanyĩisye. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ti kĩla mũndũ ũmbĩtaa, Mwĩaĩi, Mwĩaĩi, ũkavota ũsumbĩnĩ wa ĩtu; ĩndĩ nĩ ũla wĩkaa wende wa Asa wakwa." Kwoou nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa kwenda kwa Ngai na tũikwĩka. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ mũito nũndũ Yesũ oonanisye kana andũ ala matamwĩw'aa Ngai no ũndũ ũmwe na alei, kana ala 'mekaa mothũku.'—Mathayo 7:21-23.
4. Yesũ aisye ata ĩũlũ wa ala mekaa kwenda kwa Ngai?
4 Yesũ nĩwawetie kana tũkakwatwa nĩ motato nũndũ wa kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Aisye atĩĩ: "Votai inyw'ĩ nthĩnĩ wa mbingĩlo ĩla ntheke: nũndũ mbingĩlo nĩ nthanthau, na nzĩa nĩ mbaamu, ĩla ĩelete wanangĩkonĩ, nao nĩ aingĩ ala mavotelaa mbingĩlonĩ ĩsu. Nũndũ mbingĩlo nĩ ntheke, na nzĩa nĩ nziĩĩe, ĩla ĩelete thayũnĩ, nao nĩ avũthũ ala mamyonaa." (Mathayo 7:13, 14) Nzĩa ntheke, ĩla nĩyo ũthaithi wa w'o, ĩtongoeasya thayũnĩ ũtathela. Nayo nzĩa ĩla nthanthau, ĩla nĩyo ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ, ĩtongoeasya kĩkw'ũnĩ. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, Yeova ndendaa mũndũ o na ũmwe akw'e. Nũnengete kĩla mũndũ mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wake.—2 Vetelo 3:9.
ŨTHAITHI ŨLA ŨMWENDEEASYA NGAI
5. Tũtonya kũmanya ata ala mamũthaithaa Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte?
5 Yesũ aisye kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka kũmanya ala mamũthaithaa Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa kĩla maĩkĩĩaa na meko moo. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Mũkamamanya nĩ mosyao moo." Ongeleeile kwasya atĩĩ: "Kĩla mũtĩ mũseo nũsyaaa ũsyao mũseo." (Mathayo 7:16, 17) Ũu ti kwonany'a kana ala mamũthaithaa Ngai maivĩtasya. Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yonthe athũkũmi ma Ngai nĩmatataa kwĩka kĩla kyaĩlĩte. Yu nĩtũkwona kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmanye ala mamũthaithaa Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte.
6, 7. Nĩkĩ ũthaithi wa w'o waĩle kwĩthĩwa wosanĩte na Mbivilia? Ngelekany'o ya Yesũ yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
6 Ũthaithi witũ waĩle kwĩthĩwa wosanĩte na kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kĩla Ũandĩko nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai, naw'o nĩwaĩle wa kũmanyĩsya, na kũĩkĩĩthya andũ mavĩtyo, na kũmatũngĩĩa, na kũsilĩla kwa ũlũngalu: nĩ kana mũndũ wa Ngai atonye kwĩthĩwa e mwĩanĩu, eanĩe kũtethya kĩla wĩa mũseo." (2 Timotheo 3:16, 17) Nake mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkĩe Aklĩsto atĩĩ: "Yĩla mwoosie kwitũ ĩla ndeto ya ũtũmane wa Ngai, mũtyaamyosa ta ndeto ya andũ, ĩndĩ o ũndũ ĩtilyĩ w'o, ndeto ya Ngai." (1 Athesalonika 2:13) Momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni ya w'o maumanĩte na Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia. Mayumanĩte na mawoni ma andũ, syĩthĩo, kana kĩndũ kĩngĩ.
7 Maũndũ onthe ala Yesũ wamanyĩasya maumĩte Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. (Soma Yoana 17:17.) Mavinda maingĩ nĩwawetaa ũndũ Maandĩko maĩtye. (Mathayo 4:4, 7, 10) Athũkũmi ma w'o ma Ngai nĩmaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ na maũndũ onthe ala mamanyĩasya methĩawa maumĩte Mbivilianĩ.
8. Yesũ atũmanyĩisye kyaũ ĩũlũ wa kũmũthaitha Yeova?
8 Twaĩle kũthaitha Yeova e weka. Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 83:18 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "We wĩ weka, syĩtwa yaku nĩ Yeova, Nue Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe." Yesũ endaa andũ mamanye Ngai wa w'o nũũ, na nĩwamanyĩisye andũ ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. (Soma Yoana 17:6.) Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Mũthaithae Mwĩaĩi Ngai waku, na mũthũkũmae we, e weka." (Mathayo 4:10) Kwoou, nũndũ twĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai, nĩtũatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Tũthaithaa Yeova e weka, tũkatũmĩa ĩsyĩtwa yake, na nĩtũmanyĩasya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai na maũndũ ala ũkeka kwondũ witũ.
9, 10. Twonanasya ata kana nĩtwendanĩte ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ?
9 Nĩtwaĩle kwenda andũ kuma ngoonĩ. Yesũ amanyĩisye amanyĩw'a make mendane ene kwa ene. (Soma Yoana 13:35.) Maĩle kwĩka ũu o na ethĩwa maumĩte kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o, me na syĩthĩo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kana o na ethĩwa nĩ athwii kana nĩ ngya. Wendo witũ kwa ala angĩ waĩle kũtuma twĩthĩwa twĩ na ngwatanĩo ta ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. (Akolosai 3:14) Kwoou tũiendaa kaũnĩ na tũyũanaa. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũndũnĩ ũũ syana sya Ngai nikwonanw'a, o na syana sya ndevili: o mũndũ ũla ũtekaa ũlũngalu ti wa Ngai, o na ũla ũtamwendaa mwana-a-ĩthe." Yongeleele kwasya atĩĩ: "Twendane ene kwa ene: na ti ta Kaini ũla waĩ wa ũla mũthũku, na ooaa mwana-a-inyia."—1 Yoana 3:10-12; 4:20, 21.
10 Nĩtũtũmĩaa ĩvinda yitũ, vinya witũ, na syĩndũ sitũ kũtetheesya angĩ na kwĩkĩana vinya. (Aevelania 10:24, 25) Nĩtwĩkaa "andũ onthe nesa."—Akalatia 6:10.
11. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmũĩkĩĩa Yesũ ta we nzĩa ya ũtangĩĩo?
11 Nĩtwaĩle kũmũĩkĩĩa Yesũ nũndũ nĩwe nzĩa ya ũtangĩĩo. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũti ũtangĩĩo kwa ũngĩ o na wĩva w'onthe: nũndũ kũti syĩtwa yĩngĩ ĩtheo wa ĩtu, yĩnengetwe andũ, yĩtwaĩle ithyĩ kũtangĩĩwa nayo." (Meko ma Atũmwa 4:12) Kĩlungunĩ kya 5 kya ĩvuku yĩĩ, nĩtweemanyĩisye kana Yeova nĩwamũtũmie Yesũ oke kumya thayũ wake wĩthĩwe wovosyo kwa andũ ala ewi. (Mathayo 20:28) Yeova nũmũnyuvĩte Yesũ eĩthĩwa Mũsumbĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩtũtavasya kana no nginya tũmwĩw'e Yesũ nĩ kana twĩkwata thayũ ũtathela.—Soma Yoana 3:36.
12. Nĩkĩ tũtelikasya siasanĩ?
12 Tũyaĩle kwĩlikya siasanĩ. Yesũ ndaaĩlikya siasanĩ. Ĩla wasilĩlawa, eeie mũsumbĩki wa Lomi weetawa Vilato atĩĩ: "Ũsumbĩ wakwa ti wa nthĩ ĩno." (Soma Yoana 18:36.) O ta Yesũ, twĩthĩawa tũlũmanĩtye na Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtunĩ wa Ngai, na kwoou tũyĩlikasya siasanĩ o na twĩthĩwe twĩkalaa va. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte tũmew'e "ala me na ũkũmũ," namo nĩ silikalĩ sya andũ. (Alomi 13:1) Nĩtũnengae ndaĩa mĩao ya nthĩ ĩla twĩkalaa. Ĩndĩ ĩla mĩao ĩsu yaleana na mĩao ya Ngai, twĩkaa ta atũmwa, ala maisye atĩĩ: "Mũvaka tũmwĩw'e Ngai mbee wa kũmew'a andũ."—Meko ma Atũmwa 5:29; Maliko 12:17.
13. Nĩ maũndũ meva tũtavanasya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai?
13 Tũĩkĩĩaa kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai now'o ũkamina mathĩna ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Yesũ aisye kana "ũvoo . . . mũseo wa ũsumbĩ" ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe. (Soma Mathayo 24:14.) Vai silikalĩ ya mũndũ ĩtonya kwĩka maũndũ ala Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkatwĩka. (Savuli 146:3) Yesũ atũmanyĩisye kũvoyaa ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ĩla waisye atĩĩ: "Ũsumbĩ waku wũke. Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ o ta kũya ĩtunĩ." (Mathayo 6:10) Mbivilia ĩtũtavĩtye kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkaananga silikalĩ sya andũ syonthe, "naw'o ũkekalaa tene na tene."—Ndanieli 2:44.
14. We wĩona naaũ mamũthaithaa Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte?
14 Ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ asu, no wĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Naaũ ala mamanyĩasya kwosana na Mbivilia? Naaũ ala matavasya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai? Naaũ methĩawa mendanĩte kuma ngoonĩ na maĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai nĩwatũmie Yesũ nĩ kana atũtangĩĩe? Naaũ ala matelikasya siasanĩ? Naaũ matavanasya kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai now'o ũkamina mathĩna ala matũkwataa?' No Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩ syoka.—Isaia 43:10-12.
WAĨLE KWĨKA ATA?
15. Nĩ maũndũ meva twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana Ngai etĩkĩle ũthaithi witũ?
15 Kũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai e kw'o kũitoetye. O na ndaimoni niĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai e kw'o, ĩndĩ iyĩatĩĩaa mĩao yake. (Yakovo 2:19) Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda Ngai etĩkĩle ũthaithi witũ, o vamwe na kũĩkĩĩa kana e kw'o, no nginya twĩke ũndũ ũkwasya.
16. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũleana na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ?
16 Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana no nginya tũleane na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ nĩ kenda Ngai etĩkĩle ũthaithi witũ. Mwathani Isaia aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Umai katĩ wayo; ĩthesyei." (Isaia 52:11; 2 Akolintho 6:17) Nĩkyo kĩtumi twaĩle kũleana vyũ na kĩndũ kyonthe kĩkonanĩtye na ndĩni ya ũvũngũ.
17, 18. "Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene" nĩ kyaũ, na nĩkĩ twaĩle kuma nthĩnĩ wayo na mĩtũkĩ?
17 Ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ nĩ kyaũ? Nĩ ũthaithi w'onthe ũla ũmanyĩasya andũ kũthaitha Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩleanĩte na Ndeto yake. Mbivilia yĩtĩte ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ "Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene." (Ũvuan'yo 17:5) Nĩkĩ? Ĩtina wa mbua ya ĩvinda ya Noa, momanyĩsyo maingĩ ma ndĩni sya ũvũngũ nĩmambĩĩie ndũanĩ ya Mbaviloni. Momanyĩsyo asu ma ũvũngũ nĩmanyaĩĩkie ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ala mekalaa Mbaviloni nĩmathaithaa ngai syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya ũtatũ. O na ũmũnthĩ, ndĩni mbingĩ imanyĩasya kana Ngai nĩ Ũtatũ, ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai wa w'o no ũmwe, nake nĩ Yeova, na Yesũ nĩ Mwana wake. (Yoana 17:3) O na andũ ala mekalaa Mbaviloni maĩkĩĩaa kana ve kĩndũ kĩ nthĩnĩ wa mũndũ kĩtakusaa mũndũ akw'a na kĩtonya kũthĩnĩa ĩianĩ ya mwaki. Ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 14, 17, na 18.
18 Ngai nĩwathanĩte kana o mĩtũkĩ ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ ikaanangwa. (Ũvuan'yo 18:8) Nũkũelewa nĩkĩ waĩle kuma ndĩninĩ sya ũvũngũ na mĩtũkĩ? Yeova Ngai eenda wĩke ũu na mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka.—Ũvuan'yo 18:4.
19. Watw'a kũmũthũkũma Yeova, akaũsũvĩa kwa nzĩa syĩva?
19 Ĩla watw'a kuma ndĩninĩ ya ũvũngũ nĩ kana wambĩĩe kũmũthũkũma Yeova, anyanyau amwe na andũ ma mũsyĩ no maeme kũelewa nĩkĩ wĩkie ũtwi ũsu na no mambĩĩe kũũsiĩĩa kana kũũvĩnga. Ĩndĩ Yeova ndesa kũũtia. Ũkeethĩwa kĩkundinĩ kya andũ milioni mbingĩ ala methĩawa mendanĩte kuma ngoonĩ, na ũkeethĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ. (Maliko 10:28-30) Nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka anyanya amwe maku na andũ ma mũsyĩ ala meũkũvĩnga makesa kũtw'a kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia.
20. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũmũthaitha Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle?
20 O mĩtũkĩ, Ngai akavetanga ũthũku w'onthe na Ũsumbĩ wake ũisumbĩka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (2 Vetelo 3:9, 13) Yĩu yĩkeethĩwa ĩvinda ĩseo vyũ! Andũ onthe makeethĩwa maimũthũkũma Yeova kwa nzĩa ĩla wendaa. Kwoou nĩ ũndũ wa vata wose ĩtambya oyu ya kũmũthaitha Ngai kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle.
