translation:
1. How can we make sure that what we do pleases God?
INDEED many people desire to know God's will. But how can we be certain that our actions please God and that what we do pleases him? Can we ever really know this? Yes, Jehovah provides us with help to make sure that what we do pleases him.
2. How can we find out what pleases God?
2 Jehovah has given us the Bible so that we may learn what pleases him. By studying the Bible, and if Jehovah blesses our efforts, he will help us to understand matters relating to what pleases him.—Isaiah 48:17.
3. What does God want from us?
3 Some people think that God doesn't care about small things, but Jesus showed that this is not true. He said: "Not everyone saying to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter into the Kingdom of the Heavens, but the one doing the will of my Father who is in the heavens will enter." That is why it is important to learn what God's will is and to live according to it. It is vital that Jesus emphasized that those who claim to worship God but do not do his will, or who are 'hypocrites.'—Matthew 7:21-23.
4. What did Jesus say about those who do God's will?
4 Jesus warned us that we can be misled if we only talk about living according to God's will. He said: "Not everyone saying to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter into the Kingdom of the Heavens, but the one doing the will of my Father who is in the heavens will enter. Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, we prophesied in your name and expelled demons in your name and performed many powerful works in your name,' yet I will declare to them, 'I never knew you.'" (Matthew 7:13, 14) The narrow gate, which is the way to life, is difficult to find. But the wide gate, which is the way to destruction, is easy to find. So remember this, Jehovah cares for each person individually. Let each one prove his own loyalty.—2 Peter 3:9.
WHAT PLEASES GOD
5. How can we learn what pleases God?
5 Jesus explained that it is possible to learn what pleases God. We can do so by applying our heart to understanding his requirements and principles. Jesus said: "Keep on asking, and it will be given you." He further explained: "Every tree good produces fine fruit." (Matthew 7:16, 17) This does not mean that we can always tell what pleases God easily. It takes effort to understand what God requires. That is why we need to keep trying to learn what pleases God.
6, 7. How does the example of the lost sheep show how much value God places on individuals? What lesson did Jesus teach regarding this illustration?
6 Our Father values each individual highly. The Bible states: "All Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial, for teaching, for reproving, for correcting, for disciplining with a view to righteousness, so that the man who belongs to God may be fully competent, equipped for every good work." (2 Timothy 3:16, 17) The apostle Paul wrote to Christians: "In fact, when you received God's word from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but, just as it truly is, as God's word." (1 Thessalonians 2:13) True worship is based on God's Word, the Bible, and not on human opinions, traditions, or anything else.
7 All of Jesus' teachings were in harmony with God's Law. (Read John 17:17.) Many people find it helpful to meditate on what the Scriptures say. (Matthew 4:4, 7, 10) Those approved by God appreciate Jesus' example and all his teachings that harmonize with the Bible.
8. What did Jesus teach us about how to please Jehovah?
8 We need to worship Jehovah exclusively. Psalm 83:18 says: "O God, you whose name is Jehovah, you alone are the Most High over all the earth." Jesus helped people learn about this God and taught them the importance of knowing God's name. (Read John 17:6.) Jesus said: "It is Jehovah your God you must worship, and it is him you must render sacred service." (Matthew 4:10) Therefore, as followers of God, we imitate Jesus' example. We worship Jehovah exclusively, obey his commands, and help others learn about God's name and his purposes.
9, 10. How can we show that we are united in our faith?
9 We should love our brothers and sisters. Jesus showed his disciples a new commandment—to love one another. (Read John 13:35.) Love helps us to overlook offenses, both big and small, whether intentional or unintentional. Our love for others moves us to be forgiving, just as Christ forgave us. (Colossians 3:14) So let us continue to unite and encourage one another. The Bible says: "The love of God has been manifested among us in that God sent forth his only begotten Son into the world, so that we might live through him." It also states: "Let us love one another, because love originates with God, and everyone who loves has been born from God." —1 John 3:10-12; 4:20, 21.
10 Let us not neglect meeting together, but encourage one another, especially as we see the day drawing near. (Hebrews 10:24, 25) Let us be "kindly disposed toward all." —Titus 3:10.
11. How can we prove ourselves loyal to Jesus as we face opposition?
11 We can prove ourselves loyal to Jesus by supporting him as the sole channel for worship. The Bible says: "There is no other name under heaven given among men by which you must be saved." (Acts 4:12) During the fifth century C.E., we learned that Jehovah appointed Jesus to be King and to deliver His people. (Matthew 20:28) Jehovah honored Jesus by making him the Head of the congregation. And this is why the Bible shows that we need to show loyalty to Jesus by following his lead. —Read John 3:36.
12. Why is unity important?
12 We need to maintain unity. Jesus valued unity. However, a Roman governor named Pilate said: "I find no fault in this man." (Read John 18:36) But Jesus, along with his followers, remained united in support of God's Kingdom, and they did not allow themselves to become divided. In fact, the Bible tells us to be "completely humble" and to respect others. (Romans 13:1) Let us always endeavor to maintain peace. If our interests clash with those of God, we should take sides with God, just like the apostles who said: "We must obey God as ruler rather than men." —Acts 5:29; Mark 12:17.
13. What reasons do we have for supporting God's Kingdom?
13 We know that God's Kingdom will soon bring relief. Jesus foretold that the "sign of the kingdom" would mean trouble for the earth. (Read Matthew 24:14) It is foolish for anyone to think that God's Kingdom will fail. (Psalm 146:3) Jesus taught us to pray for God's Kingdom, saying: "Let your kingdom come. Let your will take place, on earth as in heaven." (Matthew 6:10) The Bible assures us that God's Kingdom will crush all human governments, "and the kingdom itself will stand forever." —Daniel 2:44.
14. How can we show faith in God when faced with opposition?
14 As we strive to do what is right, we might ask ourselves, 'How can I harmonize my actions with the Bible? How can I help others learn about God's purpose? Am I showing courage in defending Jehovah's organization? Am I remaining neutral? Am I maintaining unity? Am I supporting God's Kingdom despite difficulties?' If so, Jehovah will be with us.—Isaiah 43:10-12.
SHOULD WE TAKE SIDES?
15. What should we remember if we feel pressured to take sides?
15 Remember that God remains neutral. Satan and the demons try to make it appear that God is taking sides, but this is a lie. (James 2:19) Therefore, we want to remain neutral, while at the same time being loyal to God and doing what is right.
16. How can we maintain neutrality toward political affairs?
16 One way to stay neutral toward political affairs is to remain loyal to God. The prophet Isaiah wrote: "Get out from among them, separate yourselves." (Isaiah 52:11; 2 Corinthians 6:17) This is why we avoid getting involved in politics and everything connected with worldly governments.
17, 18. What is "Babylon the Great," and how can we distance ourselves from her influence?
17 What does worldliness stand for? It stands for the entire system of things that misleads people into disobeying God and violating his standards. The Bible calls all the world's organizations "Babylon the Great." (Revelation 17:5) Why? Because just as Babylon was the source of false worship in Noah's day, so too the world's organizations are the source of much false worship today. Worldly philosophies pollute people's minds. For example, those who live in Babylon often practice religions that dishonor God and deny that he is our Father. And yet, the Bible clearly shows that God is one, and his name is Jehovah, and Jesus is his Son. (John 17:3) Also, those who live in Babylon often believe in superstitions and consult spirit mediums. But this is wrong.—Read the accompanying article, paragraphs 14, 17, and 18.
18 God knows that people throughout the entire world are being misled. (Revelation 18:8) How can we discern what is worldly and what is not? Jehovah God helps us to discern. Revelation 18:4 says:
19. How can we show appreciation for Jehovah, and how will he help us?
19 We can show appreciation for the world's organizations by exposing them as misleading people from worshipping Jehovah, along with others who want to understand what is true and who are willing to learn and accept correction. Jehovah supports those who take a stand for him. You join millions of faithful Christians around the earth, and you experience the joy of living in harmony with God's laws. (Mark 10:28-30) This is something that many others appreciate, including some who previously opposed us and were reluctant to let us share the Bible with them.
20. What is involved in worshipping God in a way that pleases him?
20 People, God hates wickedness and his patience has an end. (2 Peter 3:9, 13) How glad we should be that this is so! All people will have an opportunity to worship Jehovah in a way that pleases him. It is important to seize this opportunity to worship God in a way that pleases him.

text:
Neeie mũsikalĩ ũla naĩ nake kana ve ĩvinda yĩngĩ noovetwe yela nũndũ nĩnaleete kũkita. Namũkũlilye: "Wĩndũnga vo ĩngĩ?" Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda ya kelĩ kwĩtwa nĩtw'ĩke mũsikalĩ wa United States Army.
NASYAĨWE ũtũinĩ wa Crooksville, Ohio, nthĩ ya Amelika, mwakanĩ wa 1926. Twasyaiwe twĩ syana nyanya, na o na kau Mami na Tata mayaĩ andũ ma kanisa, matwĩie nĩtũendae kanisanĩ. Nyie natwie kũthaitha na Kanisa wa Methodist. Nĩ na myaka 14, mũtavany'a wa ĩkanisa yĩu nĩwanengie mũthĩnzĩo nũndũ naminĩte mwaka ndatĩĩa kyumwa.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu ve mũtũi ũmwe Ngũsĩ weetawa Margaret Walker, ũla wambĩĩe kũthokea Mami amũmanyĩsye Mbivilia. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnatwie kwĩkala nĩthukĩĩsye. Na nũndũ Mami oonaa ta ngũmavĩngĩĩsa maisoma, nĩwandũngilye. Ĩndĩ nĩnatataa mũno nĩw'e kĩla meũneenea. Ĩtina wa Margaret kũka mavinda angĩ kauta, angũlilye atĩĩ: "We nĩwĩsĩ Ngai etawa ata?" Namũsũngĩie ũũ: "Naku vai mũndũ ũtesĩ. Etawa Ngai." Nĩvo ĩndĩ wambĩie, "Kwoosa Mbivilia yaku noivua ĩandĩko ya Savuli 83:18." Nĩneekie ũu, na ĩla nasomie neethĩie kana Ngai etawa Yeova. Nakuthũkie nathi kũla kwaĩ anyanyawa namea, "Mwenũka wĩoo, endai mũsome ĩandĩko ya Savuli 83:18 mũmanye Ngai etawa ata." Wenda no wasye kana nambĩĩe kũtavany'a mũthenya o ũsu.
Nĩnambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na nesa kũvatiswa mwaka wa 1941. Naminie ĩvinda o ĩnini ĩtina wa kũvatiswa na nanengwa kĩanda kya kũtongoeasya ũmbano ũla weetawa Funzo la Kitabu la Kutaniko. Nĩneekĩie vinya inyia wakwa na ala tũsyaanĩw'e mokae ũmbanonĩ ũla natongoeasya, na onthe nĩmeekie ũu. Ĩndĩ Tata ndakwetye ũu.
THĨNA ŨLA WAUMĨLILE MŨSYĨ
Nĩnaendeeie kwongelwa ianda mbingangĩ kĩkundinĩ, na nũndũ wa ũu, nĩnoombanisye mavuku maingĩ ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Mũthenya ũmwe Tata olootile mavuku asu na asya: "Nĩwene syĩndũ ii? Ndikwenda kũsyona vaa, na mantha vala ũũthi nasyo." Nĩnakwatie kasũmba taoninĩ ya Zanesville, o kũu Ohio, na nathama, ĩndĩ nĩnaendangaa mũsyĩ ngekĩe ala angĩ vinya.
Tata nĩwatataa kũsiĩĩa Mami ndakathi maũmbanonĩ. Mavinda amwe akilasya amwona aendete akamũsembany'a na aimũkusũlany'a amũtũngĩte nyũmba. Mami eetithũkany'a, asembaa akaumĩlĩĩla mũomonĩ ũla ũngĩ na ĩndĩ aithi maũmbano. Ĩndĩ neeie Mami atĩĩ: "Ndũkemakĩe. Mũthenya ũmwe akanow'a nĩ kũũsembany'a." Tata nĩwesie kũnow'a nĩ kũmũsiĩĩa, na kwoou Mami aendeea kũthi maũmbanonĩ vate thĩna.
Mwakanĩ wa 1943, kĩkundi kitũ nĩkyambĩĩisye Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi, na kwoou nĩnambĩĩe kũnengwa maũvoo sukulunĩ ĩsu. Ũtao ũla nanengawe namina kumya ũvoo wakwa nĩwatumie nĩmanya kumya maũvoo nesanga.
NĨNALEILE KŨLIKA KAŨNĨ
Myakanĩ ĩsu nĩw'o ũla Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe waendeee. Kwoou mwakanĩ wa 1944, nĩneetiwe itanĩ sya kaũ. Naendie vandũ vetawa Fort Hayes, vala ve Columbus, Ohio, nĩ kana nĩthimwe na ngĩsiw'a, na ngĩsyoka nusũsye mathangũ ala mendekaa. Ũu wathela, nĩnatavisye anene ala maĩ vo kana ndyĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla kũtw'ĩka mũsikalĩ. Nĩmaekanie nakwa nathi. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa mĩthenya mĩvũthũ, mũsikalĩ ũmwe nĩwookie kwakwa na ambĩa: "Corwin Robison, natũmwa nũke ngwĩkĩe mbĩnĩ."
Ĩtina wa syumwa ilĩ, nĩnatwaiwe kotinĩ, na twĩ vau mũsili ũla watwaĩĩsye ĩkoani aisye: "Takeka ninyie ngũtusaa ĩkoani yĩĩ, ngũtw'ĩĩa kwĩkala yela myaka yonthe. Wĩ na ndeto ũtonya kũweta?" Namũsũngĩie namwĩa: "Mũnene, nĩĩaĩle kũtalwa ta nĩ mũtavany'a. Kĩla mũomo wa mũndũ nĩũtalaa ta kĩng'ang'a kyakwa kya kũtavanĩsya, na kwoou ala ndavĩtye ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ maitalĩka." Nĩvo ĩndĩ mũsili ũsu waneenie na ala masilaa ĩkoani yĩu amea: "Mũyũkĩte vaa mũtw'e ethĩwa mwanake ũũ nĩ mũtavany'a kana ti mũtavany'a. Mwĩ vaa mũtw'e ethĩwa nĩwaatĩĩie mwĩao wa kũlika itanĩ sya kaũ kana ndaatĩĩa." O na ndatĩka 30 ite nthelu, asili asu nĩmanenganie ũtwi woo. Maisye kana nĩnatũlĩte mwĩao. Mũsili ũla watwaĩĩsye ĩkoani akũnĩie nzũma nthĩ asya kana naĩle kwovewa Ashland, Kentucky, kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩtano.
YEOVA NĨWANZŨVĨIE NĨ YELA
Syumwa ilĩ sya mbee, nambie kũtwawa yela yĩ Columbus, Ohio, na mũthenya ũla wa mbee natindie mbingĩwe seli. Namwĩkaĩlile Yeova namwĩa: "Ndikwona nĩvota kũmina myaka ĩtano selinĩ. Ndyĩsĩ nĩĩka ata."
Ũnĩ wake, asungi nĩmambingũĩie naumaala. Naendie kũũngamĩla vandũ vaũngye mũvungwa ũngĩ waĩ mũasa na waĩ na kĩthũi kĩnene, na ĩndĩ ithyelĩ twaũngama vau tũsyaĩlĩtye ndĩlĩsyanĩ. Mũvungwa ũsu angũlilye: "Wovewe kĩ, kamandaa kaa?" Namũsũngĩie, "Nĩ wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova." Asyokie angũlya, "Ata? Na wĩĩka ata vaa?" Namwĩie, "Ngũsĩ sya Yeova iyũkitaa na iyũaaa andũ." Nĩw'o ĩndĩ waisye, "Makwovete nũndũ nũleile kũaa andũ. Na ve angĩ movetwe nũndũ wa kũaa andũ. We ndũkwĩw'a ũndũ ũsu ũyũlanĩlya?" Nakwa namũtavya, "Ĩĩ nĩ w'o, mũndũ nĩkũlanĩlw'a."
Ĩtina wa ũu ambĩie ũũ: "Ndanoka vaa noovewe vangĩ myaka 15, na nĩ vau nĩnasomie mavuku amwe menyu." Ĩla waisye ũu, navoyie nasya: "Yeova, eka mũndũ ũũ oke ngalĩ yakwa." Ndatĩkanĩ o ĩsu, aathamisye ambĩa, "Ĩla wĩvũũw'a nĩ mũndũ vaa, wĩuw'a mbu. Ngakwony'a ũndũ ngekana nake." Mũvungwa ũsu eetawa Paul. Na kwoou vai mũndũ waanthĩny'a katĩ wa avungwa 50 ala maĩ vau twaĩ.
Nĩnesie kũthamĩĩw'a yela yĩla yaĩ Ashland, na vau navethĩie ana-a-asa meana ũna aima kĩ-veva. Kĩtindo kyoo nĩkyandetheeisye nĩkale na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Kĩla kyumwa ana-a-asa asu nĩmatũaĩaa ilungu sya kũsoma Mbivilia, naitũ nĩtwamanthaa makũlyo na mosũngĩo mamo nĩ kana matũmĩwe maũmbanonĩ twametaa Bible Bees. O na ve mwana-a-asa ũmwe weethĩawa anyuvĩtwe aũngamĩe kĩsio kĩla twatavanasya. Ĩsũmba yĩla twalikĩtw'e yaĩ na itanda syavangĩtwe itinĩĩe ũkũta. Ĩvinda kwa ĩvinda mwana-a-asa ũsu ookaa akambĩa atĩĩ: "Robison, ũaĩwe kĩtanda kĩna na kĩna. Mũndũ w'onthe ũkwĩsa kũetwe kĩtandanĩ kyu, eĩthwa alika kĩsionĩ kyaku. Ndakese kũvetwa vau ũtamũtavĩtye ũvoo." Mĩvango ĩsu nĩyatũtetheeisye kũtavany'a nesa.
ŨNDŨ MAŨNDŨ MAENDEEIE NAMINA KŨTHAW'A
O na kau Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe wathelile mwaka wa 1945, nĩnekalangile nĩ mwove kwa kavinda. Kĩla kyamakasya nĩ andũ ala angĩ maĩ mũsyĩ, nũndũ Tata ambĩĩte atĩĩ: "Ngakwata nzĩa ya kũũveta, aa angĩ mainema." O na kũtw'ĩka Tata ndaĩ aaeka kũvĩnga, neethĩie andũ mũonza vau mũsyĩ maendaa maũmbanonĩ na mwĩĩtu mũinawa e mũvatise.
Ĩla Kaũ wa Korea wambĩĩe mwaka wa 1950, nĩneetiwe ya kelĩ nĩlike itanĩ na kwoou nĩnaendie Fort Hayes. Masisya kĩla mendaa, mũnene ũmwe ambĩie, "We wĩ ũmwe katĩ wa ala mooneka maĩlĩte vyũ." Nakwa namũsũngĩie, "Nĩ sawa, ĩndĩ nyie ndiũlika itanĩ." Nasyokie naweta ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 2 Timotheo 2:3, na namwĩa, "Nyie nĩnatw'ĩkie mũsikalĩ wa Klĩsto." Ambie o kũvindya, na ĩndĩ esa kũmbĩa atĩĩ: "No ũthi."
Twekalangile o vanini na nathi ũmbanonĩ mũnene ũla waĩ Cincinnati, Ohio. Nĩ vau nĩnaendie ũmbanonĩ wa ala mekwenda kũthi Mbetheli, na nĩvo Mwana-a-asa Milton Henschel watwĩie kana ethĩwa mwana-a-asa nũkwenda kũthũkũma na kĩthito kwondũ wa Ũsumbĩ, ũseũvyo no ũmũtũmĩe nesa e Mbetheli. Kwoou nĩnausũisye valũa wa kũthi Mbetheli na neetwa nĩthi Mbetheli ya Brooklyn kwĩ Mwei wa 8, 1954. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, nĩthĩĩtwe ngĩthũkũma Mbetheli.
Ndi ĩndĩ naaaĩwa nĩ wĩa nĩtethya Mbetheli. Nĩnaminie myaka kauta ngĩthũkũmana na matangi ma kumya mĩuke ya kũthyũũkya masinĩ ila syatũmĩawa movisinĩ na kũla kwatumbĩthĩaw'a mavuku. Myakanĩ ĩsu no naseũvasya ivulĩ ila syaanangĩka vamwe na masinĩ ila syaanangĩka. O na nĩnathũkũmaa Nyũmbanĩ sya Maũmbano Manene ila syĩ New York City.
Nĩw'aa nditanĩa mũno mĩvango ya maũndũ ma kĩ-veva ĩla yĩ Mbetheli. Mĩvango ĩsu nĩ ta ũthaithi wa kwakya, ĩsomo ya Mũsyaĩĩsya yĩla twĩthĩawa nayo twĩ ithyonthe, vamwe na kũtavany'a na ikundi ila tũaĩwe. Ũkekala nthĩ ũsũanĩe mĩvango ta ĩsu wĩthĩa kana vai mũsyĩ wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũtesa kwĩthĩwa nayo, na nengĩ ũu nĩw'o vaĩle kwĩthĩwa vailyĩ. Asyai na syana makatata masome ĩandĩko ya kĩla mũthenya me vamwe, na mayĩkaa Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ mateũtĩĩa, na maisyoka methĩwe na kĩthito kya kũthi maũmbanonĩ na kumya maelesyo vamwe na kĩthito kya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka kĩla ũmwe akekala e na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova.
Andũ ala ndumĩte ndũũ namo Mbetheli na kĩkundinĩ nĩ aingĩ. Amwe maĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta na nĩmakwatie ĩtuvi yoo ya kũthi ĩtunĩ. Namo angĩ mayaĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. Ĩndĩ vai mũthũkũmi o na ũmwe wa Yeova ũte naĩ, vamwe o na ala me Mbetheli. Kwoou nesa kũvĩtũũkana na mwana-a-asa, nĩnĩtataa kũtũngĩĩa mũuo. Nĩnĩlilikanaa ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 5:23, 24 yĩla yonanĩtye kĩla twaĩle kwĩka twaemanwa na angĩ. Vai kĩndũ kĩ vinya ta kwĩtya ũekeo, ĩndĩ nĩnonete kana kaingĩ ĩla neetya mũnyanyawa ũekeo, maũndũ maileaa kũseũva.
MOATHIMO ALA NGWATĨTE ŨTHŨKŨMINĨ WAKWA
Ũkũũ ũla nĩ naw'o ũtumaa nĩemwa kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, ĩndĩ kĩu kĩitumaa nĩkw'a ngoo. Kwoou nĩnĩmanyĩĩtye o vanini kĩthyomo kya Mandarin Chinese, na nũndũ wa ũu ĩla ngũtavany'a nzĩanĩ nĩnĩtanĩaa kũtumũsya andũ ma kĩthyomo kĩu nĩmatavye ũvoo. Mavinda amwe nĩnenganae makaseti 30 kana 40 o na saa sita ite mbiku.
Aĩ na eka ũu, ĩvinda yĩmwe naĩ na ĩsyokeo yĩ China! Ũu watonyekie ata? Mũthenya ũmwe kamwĩlĩtu kamwe katanu nĩkanengie kathangũ kaeleetye ĩũlũ wa vandũ vatesawa matunda. Kanengie kathangũ kau kantheketye, kwoou o nakwa nĩnakathekisye na nakanenga ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya na ya Amkeni! ya kĩthyomo kya Chinese. Nĩkamosie na kambĩa ketawa Katie. Kuma mũthenya ũsu Katie akilasya ambona akoka kũndumũsya. Naendaa ngamũtavya ũndũ matunda na syĩndũ sya mbaa mboka syĩtawa na Kĩsũngũ, nake aitũngĩlĩĩla masyĩtwa asu nĩ kana akwatye. O na nĩnamũmanyĩisye maandĩko mana ma Mbivilia na eetĩkĩla ĩvuku Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya. Ĩndĩ tũimina syumwa siana ũna, nĩnaekie kũmwona.
Twamina kwaanwa vathelile myei kauta na nakomana na kamwĩlĩtu kangĩ kainengane tũthangũ ta tũla, na kwoou nĩnakanengie makaseti na koosa. Kyumwa kĩla kyaatĩĩe kanengie simũ yako na kambĩa, "Neena China." Nakeie, "Ndi mũndũ nĩsĩ China." Ĩndĩ kanthing'ĩĩisye nginya noosa ĩ simũ na nasya, "Hello, nĩ Robison." Nĩw'o neewie mũndũ ũla waĩ simũnĩ ambĩa, "Robby, nĩ Katie. Nĩnasyokie China." Namũkũlilye, "Aĩ China?" Katie asũngĩie asya, "Ĩĩ. Robby, nũkwona kelĩtu kau kaũnenga simũ? Nĩ kalinawa. Wamanyĩisye maũndũ maingĩ maseo. Mwa nĩkwĩsũva ũkamanyĩsye o ũndũ wamanyĩisye." Nakwa namũsũngĩie ũũ: "Katie, nĩngũtata ũndũ ndonya. Nĩ mũvea nũndũ wa kũndavya vala ũĩ." Ĩtina wa mũthenya ũsu noonanie na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wa Katie ĩvinda yĩngĩ yĩmwe na twaanwa vyũ. Nĩĩkwatya kũla eĩtu asu elĩ maendie nĩmekwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova.
Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 73, ndi wĩa ũngĩ nĩthĩĩtwe ngĩtethya eka kũmũthũkũma Yeova. Nĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ Yeova nĩwandetheeisye nalea kũlika kaũnĩ na nekala nĩ mũĩkĩĩku ĩla naĩ mwove. Na ĩngĩ ala tũsyaanĩw'e mambĩaa kana moosie vinya moona ũndũ naendeeie kwĩkala nĩ mũĩkĩĩku o na kau Tata nĩwanthĩnasya. Mami na angĩ thanthatũ katĩ wa ala tũsyaanĩw'e nĩmavatisiwe. O na Tata nĩwaekie kwetya ngoo, na atanamba kũkw'a nĩwaendete maũmbano ma kũtala.
Ethĩwa nĩ kwenda kwa Ngai, andũ ma mũsyĩ na anyanyawa ala makwie makathayũũkw'a mekale nthĩ nzaũ. Kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla tũkew'a tũimũthaitha Yeova tene na tene twĩ vamwe na ala twendete! *
^ kal. 32 Mwana-a-asa Corwin Robison akwie e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova ĩla ũvoo ũũ waendeee kũseũvw'a nĩ kana ũtumbĩthw'e.

translation:
I remember a time when I was young and had many dreams that were never realized, and now I regret not paying attention. He asked me: "What more could there be?" That's why I decided to join the United States Army.
I WAS BORN in Crooksville, Ohio, in America, in 1926. We were raised by our grandmother, and also by Mom and Dad who were church people, and we always went to church. We joined the Methodist Church. When I was 14 years old, the youth leader of that church challenged us to dedicate a year to service.
In that area lived a woman named Margaret Walker, who told my mother about the Bible. One day I happened to be sitting and thinking. And although my mother didn't force me to read, I wanted to. I found that I couldn't concentrate very well. Margaret asked about other scriptures, saying: "Don't you know God has a name?" I replied to her: "I know someone who knows. God has a name." She then told me, "Read the Bible and find Psalm 83:18." I did so, and through it I learned that God's name is Jehovah. And I began to tell everyone I met, "Friends, go read Psalm 83:18 and learn what God's name is." Some would listen and some wouldn't.
She encouraged me to study the Bible and helped me get baptized in 1941. I appreciated this great privilege and was happy to participate in something called the Assembly Book Study. I enjoyed spending time with them and others, and I continued to enjoy it. My father supported this.
THE REASON FOR MY DECISION
I continued to speak to people about it enthusiastically, and because of this, I shared many truths from God's Word. One day Father asked me questions like: "What is this all about? I will go see for myself, and perhaps I will understand." I accompanied him to Zanesville, Ohio, and we went, and I was glad he went with us.
Father initially opposed Mother participating in our activities. Sometimes neighbors saw him scolding her and trying to prevent her from going out. Mother persevered, continuing to attend meetings despite his opposition. I heard Mother say: "I will continue to attend anyway." Father allowed her to continue attending meetings regularly.
In 1943, a group of us were invited to the Theocratic School, and then I was given the opportunity to serve in that school. The training I received there helped me improve my ability to teach and improved my speaking skills.
I LEARNED TO BE BOLD
The years that followed were those when the Watch Tower Society expanded. In 1944, I was appointed a conductor in the congregation. I traveled to places such as Fort Hayes, near Columbus, Ohio, and often stayed overnight with strangers, and I would find kind people who welcomed me. At times, I felt very tired, but I kept pushing myself to preach. I enjoyed it immensely. On one occasion, some weeks later, a brother approached me and said: "Corwin Robison sent me to commend you."
On the third day, I was taken to court, and we had a trial where the judge asked: "Will you cease your activity, or will you continue for another year? If you do not stop, can you pay a fine or go to jail?" I replied to him: "Sir, I am willing to suffer imprisonment rather than quit. Every person has a right to freedom of conscience, and I have exercised that right under the Constitution." That trial resulted in our being released from custody, but the judge warned us: "You may be brought back here again, depending on whether you stop or do not stop. If you are brought back here, it will be up to the court to decide whether to impose a fine or send you to jail." And thirty days passed, and nothing happened. But then I received a notice stating that I was to report. The judge who presided over the trial informed me that I would be allowed to visit Ashland, Kentucky, for five years.
JEHOVAH HAS SUSTAINED ME ALL ALONG
On the third day thereafter, I was permitted to return home to Columbus, Ohio, and on that same day I found my wife in prison. I told Jehovah: "I will gladly spend five years in prison. I will not abandon her."
The next day, guards came to interrogate me. They took me to question prisoners who were violent and those who had committed serious crimes, and during that time we discussed many things and reasoned together. One guard asked: "What are you doing, brother?" I replied, "I am one of Jehovah's Witnesses." He said, "What? Are you also one of them?" I said, "Jehovah's Witnesses help people to live and to die." That is when he said, "You should not try to make people become like you. And they should not let you make them become like you. Why should I listen to what you say?" But I answered him, "That is your privilege; a person has a choice."
On this occasion, he told me: "I used to work for 15 years, and I saw some of you young men." Then he added: "But now I want to say: 'Jehovah, please take this man away from here.' " Shortly afterward, he sent for me, saying: "If you cause trouble, you will regret it. I will not tolerate anything like that." This guard was named Paul. And there were about 50 prisoners who listened to us at times.
I enjoyed returning to the circuit assembly in Ashland, and I met many fine brothers and sisters who showed genuine hospitality. The hall was decorated beautifully and was very spacious. Every week the brothers would arrange for us to read the Bible, and we practiced our presentations and demonstrations, sometimes using material prepared for the Bible Bees. And often a young boy would volunteer to give a talk on whatever subject we discussed. It seemed that each assembly was held in a different Kingdom Hall. Again and again that young boy would stand up and say: "Robison, you have gone too far! Anyone who tries to force us to study the Bible, we will report his conduct. I ask that you stop trying to influence us." These comments made us feel discouraged.
IMPORTANT THINGS TO REMEMBER
IN THE MINISTRY
After Brother Jarrell served as a full-time pioneer in 1945, I began to work with him in the ministry. Almost every day we found people who were interested, so Father told me: "Keep a list of those who are interested." So to help Father, I started making notes, and soon many people went forward with the truth with the assistance of a publisher.
During the Korean War in 1950, I was assigned to serve in a company similar to my previous assignment and was sent to Fort Hayes. Nearly every day someone would tell me, "You are one of the few who looks like he belongs here." I would reply, "Yes, I feel out of place." But I remembered the scripture from 2 Timothy 2:3, which reads, "Be a loyal soldier of Christ." He said something about this, and later he reminded me: "Don't be afraid."
We worked in the large territory around Cincinnati, Ohio. We often visited congregations that were going to Bethel, and that is what brother Milton Henschel told us when he came to encourage brothers to go to headquarters and receive training in the Theocratic School, so they could use what they learned at Bethel. I applied to go to Bethel, and I was accepted to Bethel in Brooklyn on August 8, 1954. From that time on, I continued serving at Bethel.
I am now among those who talk about Bethel. I have spent years serving with brothers who have had much experience in dealing with problems, but they have not been moved by worldly things and have not allowed their hearts to become hardened. In recent years I have also enjoyed association with brothers who have not been influenced by the world. And I have served in the large congregation in New York City.
I always appreciate the privileges I have had while in Bethel. These privileges include the opportunity to preach, the study of the Watchtower Society publications we have had throughout, associating with the brotherhood, and being able to maintain spiritual zeal. It is a joy to see how Jehovah's organization has helped us to maintain this zeal, and I know this is what pleases him. Also, and especially, the brothers' diligent study of the Bible, and their keeping the principles of truth, and their remaining zealous in proclaiming the good news and in maintaining Christian neutrality, is something that each one can cultivate and strengthen his personal relationship with Jehovah.
And there are many others who have encouraged me while at Bethel, and they have shown me kindness and have given me support. There are also many others who have shown me kindness. In fact, some brothers and sisters have been very generous toward me, both those from Jehovah and those from Bethel. Sometimes it is necessary to deal with a child, and I try my best to discipline him. I remember Matthew 5:23, 24 which teaches us to settle matters before presenting our gifts. So when there is a problem that needs attention, I try to resolve it quickly so that nothing hinders my worship.
MORE BROTHERS WHO HAVE ENCOURAGED ME
The time came when I was assigned to pioneer from house to house, and this led me to go out more. Sometimes I would practice my Mandarin Chinese ministry, and because of this assignment I was able to help people in that language, which pleased me greatly. Some days I could visit 30 or 40 homes in about six hours.
But on one occasion, one day in China! It was amazing, wasn't it? One publisher shared five tracts, and they resulted in an interest among the people. They took those tracts, and we were able to place a cassette of "The Greatest Man Who Ever Lived" and a cassette of "Awake!" in Chinese. And I also met a sister named Katie. Recently Katie has been able to learn how to present a demonstration. And I am happy to help her with that. Also, I have helped her prepare Bible study articles and she enjoys reading the Bible Insight book. But we need to work together, and I hope to see her again soon.
We went to the market where there were many people buying and selling, and I met another publisher who was distributing tracts, and we were able to place cassettes and books. Every time he handed out a tract, he would say to them, "From China." Then I said, "I am not from China." So he asked me my name and I said, "Hello, I am Robison." That is when the man recognized me and said, "Robby, it's Katie. I came from China." I replied, "China?" Katie explained further, "Yes. Robby, can you help me distribute some tracts? I am new. You know so much more than I do. Perhaps you can teach me something." So I told Katie, "Katie, I don't mind helping at all. I am willing to help you in any way I can." This afternoon I met Katie's mother and we talked for a while. I felt encouraged to see this woman because I had already learned about Jehovah.
For 73 years, I have been among those actively proclaiming Jehovah. It is a joy to see how Jehovah has blessed me with strength despite my age and limitations. And often we appreciate the support of our brothers and sisters when we face difficulties and our loving Father strengthens us. My family and many others have experienced similar blessings. Our Father allows us to endure, and He does not abandon us when we attend meetings.
It is important to pray to God, and all humble and obedient ones will experience great things. Let us continue to cherish this work and always cooperate with our brothers and sisters! *
^ par. 32 Young man Corwin Robison is among those actively proclaiming Jehovah and continues to serve faithfully, even though he faces challenges.

text:
"Ndeto ya Ngai ĩ thayũ, na nĩ nthangaau."—AEVL. 4:12.
MBATHI: 37, 48
1. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkũĩkĩĩthasya kana Ndeto ya Ngai yĩ vinya? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
ITHYĨ andũ ma Yeova nĩtwĩsĩ nesa vyũ kana ndeto ya Ngai, ĩla nĩyo ũvoo ũla ũnengete andũ, yĩ "thayũ, na nĩ nthangaau." (Aevl. 4:12) Aingĩ maitũ nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ikwonany'a kana Mbivilia yĩ ũtonyi wa kũalyũla andũ. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa amwe me kĩkundinĩ ũmũnthĩ tene maĩ ing'ei, angĩ matũmĩaa ndawa sya kũmila, na angĩ nĩmeelikĩtye mwĩkalĩlenĩ mũthũku wa ũlaalai. Angĩ maĩ andũ me mbesa na maweteka, ĩndĩ mekalaa mayĩw'a ve kĩndũ makosete thayũnĩ woo. (Mũta. 2:3-11) Aingĩ ala moonekaa maĩtye nzĩa na mate vandũ maumĩlĩĩla nĩmesĩte kũalyũlwa nĩ ũtonyi wa Mbivilia na ũmũnthĩ ũũ me nzĩanĩ ĩla yaĩle. No kwĩthĩwa ũtanĩaa mũno kũsoma ngewa sya andũ ta asu nthĩnĩ wa kĩla kĩlungu kĩthĩawa ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya kĩ na kyongo "Mbivilia Nĩalyũlaa Andũ." Na nĩwonete kana o na Aklĩsto mamina kũmanya ũla w'o, no nginya mekĩe kĩthito meke maendeeo matetheew'e nĩ Maandĩko.
2. Vinya wa Ndeto ya Ngai watetheeisye andũ ata ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa?
2 Ve kĩtumi kya kũseng'a aĩ nũndũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ nĩmekĩte moalyũku manene ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai? Vai kĩtumi o na kĩmwe! Ngewa ta isu itũlilikanasya ĩũlũ wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa ala maĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. (Soma 1 Akolintho 6:9-11.) Vaulo atalanĩilye Aklĩsto asu andũ me mĩkalĩle yĩ kĩvathũkany'o ala matakatiĩwa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, na ĩndĩ aandĩka atĩĩ: 'Amwe menyu mwailyĩ ũu.' Aimaandĩkĩa ndeto isu maĩ maalyũkile matetheew'e nĩ Maandĩko na veva mũtheu wa Ngai. Ĩndĩ o na ĩtina wa kũtw'ĩka Aklĩsto, ve amwe masyokie kwĩka mavĩtyo manene ala mambie kwananga ngwatanĩo yoo na Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilianĩ nĩvawetetwe Mũklĩsto ũmwe mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta wa ĩvinda ya atũmwa ũla watengiwe na ĩtina esa kũtũngwa kĩkundinĩ. (1 Ako. 5:1-5; 2 Ako. 2:5-8) Yo kũsũanĩa mathĩna onthe ala Aklĩsto ala angĩ maakomana namo na makatetheew'a nĩ Ndeto ya Ngai mamakĩlye vinya tyo kũtwĩkĩaa vinya?
3. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Nũndũ nĩtũnengetwe Ndeto ya Ngai na nĩtwĩsĩ kana yĩ vinya, nĩtwaĩle kũmĩtũmĩa nesa ũndũ vatonyeka. (2 Tim. 2:15) Nĩkyo kĩtumi kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ tũkwenda kũneenea ũndũ tũtonya kũeka Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũtetheesye (1) thayũnĩ witũ, (2) ũtavany'anĩ, na (3) ĩla tũũmanyĩsya maũmbanonĩ. Maũndũ asu nĩmeũtũtetheesya tũmanye ũndũ tũtonya kwony'a Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ kana nĩtũmwendete na nĩtũmũtũngĩaa mũvea nũndũ nĩwe ũtũmanyĩasya kwaĩla.—Isa. 48:17.
THAYŨNĨ WITŨ
4. (a) Twaĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda kũtetheka nĩ Ndeto ya Ngai? (b) Wĩkĩte mĩvango yĩva nĩ kana ũkwate ĩvinda ya kũsoma Mbivilia?
4 Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũtethye no nginya tũmĩsomae kĩla ĩvinda. Vatonyeka twaĩle kwĩkaa ũu kĩla mũthenya. (Yos. 1:8) Nĩ w'o aingĩ maitũ twĩthĩawa tũkwatene mũno. Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kwĩtĩkĩlya ũndũ o na wĩva, o na ethĩwa nĩ maũndũ ala ma lasima mavĩngĩĩse mũvango witũ wa kũsoma Mbivilia. (Soma Aeveso 5:15, 16.) Athũkũmi aingĩ ma Yeova nĩmavangĩte maũndũ moo nesa ũkethĩa nĩmeũkwata ĩvinda ya kũsoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya. Amwe masomaa kwakya tene, angĩ katĩkatĩ wa mũthenya, na ala angĩ wĩoo. Mew'aa o ta mũandĩki wa Savuli ũla waandĩkie atĩĩ: "Mĩao yaku ko nĩnĩmyendetee! Nĩyo nzũanĩaa mũthenya w'onthe."—Sav. 119:97.
5, 6. (a) Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũvindĩĩsya kĩla twasoma? (b) Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũtetheke ĩla tũũvindĩĩsya kĩla tũũsoma? (c) We mwene ũtethekete ata nũndũ wa kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai na kũmĩvindĩĩsya?
5 Tũisoma Mbivilia, nĩtwaĩle kwosa mwanya wa kũvindĩĩsya kĩla tũũsoma. (Sav. 1:1-3) Tũkaema kwĩka ũu tũyĩsa kũtetheka thayũnĩ witũ nĩ ũĩ ũte maela ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Kĩeleelo kya kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ne kwĩkĩa maũndũ ala tũũsoma ngoonĩ, tũtw'ĩke twĩsoma ĩ Mbivilia mbene, kana twĩmĩsoma simũnĩ kana kombiũtanĩ.
6 Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũtetheke ĩla tũũvindĩĩsya kĩla tũũsoma? Aingĩ nĩmonete kana masoma kalungu kana ka Maandĩko nũseo makamba kũũngamya kũsoma vanini na maisũanĩa makũlyo ta aa: 'Kĩu nasoma kĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova? Nyie nĩtũmĩĩte ata mwolooto ũla wĩ mĩsoanĩ ĩno ya Ndeto ya Ngai thayũnĩ wakwa? Naĩle kwĩka moalyũku maũndũnĩ meva?' O ũndũ twavoya na twavindĩĩsya kĩla tũũsoma Ndetonĩ ya Ngai, now'o tũkew'aa twĩ na mea ma kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ Maandĩkonĩ. Tweeka ũu tũkeethĩawa tweetĩkĩlya vinya wa Ndeto ya Ngai ũthũkũme thayũnĩ witũ.—2 Ako. 10:4, 5.
ĨLA TWĨ ŨTAVANY'ANĨ
7. Twaĩle kwĩka ata tũtũmĩe nesa vyũ Ndeto ya Ngai ĩla twĩ ũtavany'anĩ?
7 Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũtũmĩe Ndeto ya Ngai nesa ĩla twĩ ũtavany'a? Mbee vyũ, nĩtwaĩle kũmĩtũmĩa mũno ĩla tũũtavany'a na ĩla tũũmanyĩsya. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe aeleisye ũndũ ũsu ũũ: "Twasye wĩtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba wĩ na Yeova mwene, nue ũneena kĩla vandũ-ĩ, kana no ũeke akaneena?" Kĩla wawetaa nĩ atĩĩ: Ĩla twasomea mwene nyũmba Ndeto ya Ngai, twĩthĩawa tũieka Yeova ne we aneene nake. Ndeto syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ tũnyuvĩte nesa nitonya kũkiita mwene nyũmba mũno kũte ndeto sitũ ene. (1 Ath. 2:13) Kwoou ĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Nyie nĩnĩmanthaa vyũ myanya ya kũsomea andũ Ndeto ya Ngai ĩla ngũmatavya ũvoo mũseo?'
8. Nĩkĩ tũtaĩle kũsũanĩa kana kũsoma maandĩko kwĩ kw'oka ĩla tũũtavany'a nĩkũtoetye?
8 Kũsomea mũndũ o kĩla kĩandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ kw'oka kũitoetye. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nũndũ aingĩ maieleawa kĩla kĩ Mbivilianĩ kana o na ethĩwa nĩmekũelewa maeleawa o vanini. Ũu now'o kwailyĩ ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, na ũmũnthĩ kũilyĩ oou. (Alo. 10:2) Kwoou tũyaĩle kũsũanĩa mũndũ nĩwaelewa kĩla tũkwenda kũmũmanyĩsya aĩ no kwĩthĩwa nĩtwamũsomea ĩandĩko. Nĩtwaĩle kwosa ĩvinda tũkamwony'a kĩla tũkwenda akwatye mũsoanĩ ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o, no tũtũngĩlĩĩle ĩngĩ ndeto imwe syĩ mũsoanĩ ũsu na ĩndĩ tũimũtetheesya kũelewa syĩweta kyaũ. Kwĩka ũu kũkatumaa Ndeto ya Ngai ĩlika ilĩkonĩ na ngoonĩ sya ala meũtwĩthukĩĩsya.—Soma Luka 24:32.
9. Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũtanamba kũsomea mũndũ ĩandĩko nĩ kana tũmũtetheesye anenge Mbivilia ndaĩa? Nengane ngelekany'o.
9 O na ĩngĩ, tũtanamba kũsomea mũndũ ĩandĩko nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩa ndeto itonya kũtuma anenga Mbivilia ndaĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, no twasye, "Eka twone woni wa Mũmbi witũ ĩũlũ wa kĩĩ tũũneenea." Nao tũineena na mũndũ wa ndĩni ĩte ya Kĩklĩsto no tũmwĩe atĩĩ: "Eka twone kĩla Maandĩko Matheu matũtavĩtye." Kana ethĩwa twĩneena na mũndũ ũtakwatĩĩaa maũndũ ma ndĩni, no tũmũkũlye-ĩ, "Ndyĩsĩ kana waaĩw'a nthimo ĩno yaneeniwe tene?" Kwoou nũndũ kĩla mũndũ e kĩla ũĩkĩĩaa na e ũndũ ũeetwe, tũkatataa mũno tũneene na kĩla ũmwe kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũmwendeesya.—1 Ako. 9:22, 23.
10. (a) Elesya kĩla mwana-a-asa ũmwe woonie aitavany'a. (b) We wonete vinya wa Ndeto ya Ngai ũithũkũma ata ĩla ũũtavany'a?
10 Aingĩ nĩmonete kana kũtũmĩa Ndeto ya Ngai maitavany'a no kũtethye mũno ala meũneena namo. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno. Mũthenya ũmwe mwana-a-asa ũmwe nĩwasyokeie mũtumĩa mũna wasomete makaseti maitũ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ. Mũthenya ũsu, vandũ va kwĩka o kũmũnenga ĩkaseti ya mĩtũkĩ vyũ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya, ambie kũmũsomea ĩandĩko yaĩ ĩkasetinĩ yĩu. Ĩandĩko yĩu yaĩ 2 Akolintho 1:3, 4 yĩla yaasya: "Ĩthe wa matei na Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe; [nĩwe] ũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe." Mũtumĩa ũsu eewie akiitwa nginya eea mwana-a-asa ũsu atũngĩlĩĩle ĩandĩko yĩu ĩngĩ. Ĩtina nĩwamũeleisye ũndũ we na mũka meew'aa me na vata mũnene wa kũkiakiw'a, na kuma vau nĩwendie kũmanya maũndũ maingangĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. O naku tyo wĩtĩkĩle kana Ndeto ya Ngai yĩ ũtonyi mwingĩ mũno wa kũtetheesya ala twakomana namo tũitavany'a?—Meko 19:20.
ĨLA TŨŨMANYĨSYA MAŨMBANONĨ
11. Ana-a-asa ala methĩawa na ilungu maũmbanonĩ maĩle kwĩka ata?
11 Ithyonthe nĩtũtanĩaa kwĩthĩwa maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi na maũmbanonĩ manene. Kĩtumi kĩla kĩnene kya kũthi maũmbanonĩ asu nĩ kũmũthaitha Yeova. O na ĩngĩ motao ala tũkwataa kuma Maandĩkonĩ nĩmatũtethasya mũno. Kwoou ana-a-asa ala methĩawa manengetwe ilungu maũmbanonĩ asu methĩawa manengetwe kĩanda kya mwanya. O na ĩngĩ nĩmaĩle kũmanya kana kũnewa ilungu ta isu ti ũndũ wa ngũĩ. (Yak. 3:1) Kĩla ĩvinda nĩmaĩle kũĩkĩĩthya kana kĩla meũmanyĩsya nĩkyosanĩte vyũ na Ndeto ya Ngai. Wanengwa kĩlungu ũmbanonĩ ũtonya kwĩka ata ũĩkĩĩthye kana vinya wa Ndeto ya Ngai nĩwatethya ala makwĩthukĩĩsye?
12. Ũla wĩ na ũvoo atonya kũĩkĩĩthya ata kana Maandĩko nĩmo mũsingi wa ũvoo wake?
12 Maandĩko nĩmo maĩle kwĩthĩwa me mũsingi wa ũvoo waku. (Yoa. 7:16) Kwoou waĩle kwĩka ata? Mbee ĩsũvĩe ndũkanengane ngewa sya maũndũ monekete kana ngelekany'o kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũtuma andũ malilikana mũyo wasyo kũte kĩla ũkwendaa memanyĩsye Maandĩkonĩ. O na ĩngĩ nzĩa yaku ya kumya ũvoo ndyaĩle kũtuma andũ maũsũanĩa ne uwe vandũ va kũsũanĩa Maandĩko. Ũndũ ũngĩ waĩle kũlilikana nĩ kana kũsoma maandĩko maingĩ ti kw'o kũmanyĩsya kĩla kĩ Mbivilianĩ. O na kaingĩ wĩthĩaa wasoma maandĩko maingĩ andũ matiawa vate yĩmwe malilikene. Kwoou nyuva maandĩko ala ma vata nesa, na ũyosa ĩvinda ũmasome, ũmaelesye nesa, ũtũmĩe ngelekany'o sya kũtetheesya ethukĩĩsya mamaelewe, na ũyonany'a ũndũ matonya kũtethya ethukĩĩsya. (Nee. 8:8) Ethĩwa nĩwanengwa ũvoo (muhtasari), ũsome nesa vamwe na maandĩko ala matũmĩĩtwe. Tata ũelewe ũndũ maandĩko ala monanĩtw'e mosanĩte na ũvoo ũsu. Na ĩndĩ ũinyuva maandĩko ala ũũtũmĩa kũelesya maũndũ ala me ũvoonĩ ũsu. (No ũkwate ũvoo ũtonya kũũtetheesya nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku, Faidika na Elimu ya Shule ya Huduma ya Kitheokrasi, ĩsomonĩ ya 21-23.) Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana nĩwaĩle kũmũvoya Yeova aũtetheesye nĩ kana ũmanyĩsye nesa maũndũ ma vata ala me Ndetonĩ yake.—Soma Esala 7:10; Nthimo 3:13, 14.
13. (a) Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe atethekie ata nĩ ĩandĩko yatũmĩiwe ũmbanonĩ? (b) We mwene ũthekete ata nĩ maandĩko amwe maatũmĩwa ũmbanonĩ?
13 Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe kuma Australia eewie akiitwa ngoo mũno nĩ ĩandĩko yatũmĩiwe ũmbanonĩ ũmwe wa Kĩklĩsto. O na kau nĩwakwatĩtwe nĩ mathĩna maito e mũnini, nĩwaĩ aneetĩkĩla ũw'o na akeyumya amũthũkũme Yeova. O na vailyĩ ũu, ndaĩkĩĩaa kana we nĩwĩsa kwendwa nĩ Yeova. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩwesie kũĩkĩĩa kana Ngai nũmwendete. Atetheeiw'e nĩ kyaũ? Kĩla kyamũtethisye nĩ kũvindĩĩsya ĩandĩko yasomiwe ũmbanonĩ mũthenya ũmwe vamwe na mĩsoa ĩngĩ yĩ Mbivilianĩ. * We naku ve ĩvinda waaĩw'a wakiitwa ta mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩ maandĩko matũmĩiwe ũmbanonĩ wa kĩkundi kana ũmbanonĩ mũnene?—Nee. 8:12.
14. Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa Ndeto ya Ngai?
14 Mwa tũtũngaa mũvea ta kĩ nũndũ wa Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia! Ngai nĩwanengie andũ Mbivilia nũndũ nũmendete na aĩkĩĩthya ĩkekalaa tene na tene o tondũ wathanĩte. (1 Vet. 1:24, 25) Kwoou nũseo tũsomae Ndeto ya Ngai kĩla ĩvinda, tũtũmĩae maũndũ ala tweemanyĩsya, na tũimĩtũmĩa kũmanyĩsya angĩ. Tweeka ũu tũkeethĩawa tũyonany'a nĩtũũtũnga mũvea na nĩtwendete ĩ Mbivilia, vamwe na Mũandĩkĩthya wayo, Yeova Ngai.

translation:
"The word of God is living, and it is powerful."—Hebrews 4:12.
FOOTNOTES: 37, 48
1. What makes God's Word unique? (Consider its qualities.)
TRUE Christians value God's Word because it is what moves people, being "living, and powerful." (Hebrews 4:12) Many people today do not give much importance to the Bible as a tool for teaching and correcting others, and some have become discouraged because they see little practical benefit from it. Others may be busy with worldly pursuits, and still others may feel that they lack the ability to understand it. But many people who are honest and sincere recognize that the Bible has a power that nothing else possesses. (Matthew 2:3-11) More and more individuals are realizing that the Bible can help them find answers to life's important questions and provide guidance. It is vital, therefore, that we continue to share the good news with those who are willing to listen. To assist us in doing so, we can use the publication "The Bible Teaches," which offers a clear explanation of basic Bible teachings. And we can assure our brothers that Jehovah will bless our efforts to help others learn about his Word. We should also remember to spend time personally studying God's Word and meditating on its meaning.
2. How does God's Word affect people, even those who do not accept it?
2 What reason do we have for believing that God's Word can have a great impact on people's hearts? Consider the case of those who were influenced by the apostles' ministry. (Read 1 Corinthians 6:9-11.) Paul told fellow Christians that some of them had been immoral people, yet they had been sanctified. He wrote: "Some of you used to practice such things, but you have been washed clean." The Bible shows that God's Word has the power to transform lives. So when we preach, let us always remember that it is God's spirit that touches people's hearts. For example, the Bible tells of a Christian slave owner named Onesimus who was converted through the ministry of an apostle. (1 Cor. 5:1-5; 2 Cor. 2:5-8) Why, then, is it important for us to rely on God's spirit when we try to help others appreciate the value of the Bible?
3. What will we discuss next?
3 We are motivated by our love for God and our desire to see others benefit from his Word. (2 Tim. 2:15) That is why it is vital that we strive to present God's Word in a way that is (1) appealing to their heart, (2) easy to understand, and (3) convincing. By doing so, we can help them come to know Jehovah and appreciate what he requires of them.—Isa. 48:17.
OUR HEART
4. (a) How can we make sure that we are presenting God's Word in an appealing way? (b) What steps can you take to improve your ability to read the Bible?
4 To present God's Word in an appealing way, we need to meditate on it regularly. It is important that we set aside time for this each day. (Josh. 1:8) Many find that they can do this best first thing in the morning. Otherwise, we may neglect it because of other pressing matters. Also, making Bible reading a priority will help us to use our time wisely. (Read Ephesians 5:15, 16.) Many of Jehovah's servants have found that setting a specific time for daily Bible reading helps them stick to it. Some read first thing in the morning, others during their lunch hour, and still others in the evening. The psalmist expressed a similar sentiment when he wrote: "How I love your law! I meditate on it all day long."—Ps. 119:97.
5, 6. (a) Why is it important to meditate on what we read? (b) How can we be sure that we are truly meditating on what we read? (c) Have you benefited personally from meditating on God's Word?
5 As we read the Bible, we should make it a point to meditate on it. (Ps. 1:1-3) We can ask ourselves whether we understand what we are reading and how it applies to us personally. Meditating on God's Word helps us to remember what we read and to appreciate its meaning more fully. It also motivates us to apply what we learn from the Bible in our lives, either individually or with others.
6 How can we be sure that we are truly meditating on what we read? Many find it helpful to ask themselves questions about the scripture they are studying, such as: 'What does this teach me about Jehovah?' 'How can I apply this principle in my life?' 'Does this scripture touch my heart?' By pondering what we read and meditating on it, we will strengthen our faith and deepen our appreciation for God's Word. We will also be better equipped to share the truths of the Scriptures with others. —2 Cor. 10:4, 5.
IS IT BENEFICIAL TO MEDITATE?
7. Why is it beneficial to meditate on God's Word, especially when facing difficulties?
7 It can be comforting to meditate on God's Word when we are going through trials. But why is it important to meditate regularly, not just during difficult times? Because regular meditation strengthens our spirituality and deepens our understanding. One young man explained his experience like this: "When I face problems at home and at school, I often ask myself, 'What would Jehovah want me to do?' This helps me to see things from his perspective." When we study the Bible diligently, we draw closer to Jehovah and feel his support. The scriptures can provide practical guidance and comfort in times of need. (1 Thess. 2:13) So, ask yourself: 'Am I making time to help others learn about God's Word, even when I am busy?'
8. What can we do to improve our ability to meditate when facing difficulties?
8 Studying the Bible regularly will help us to meditate effectively. Why is this so? Many find it easier to understand what they read in the Bible if they have studied it before. This is because familiarizing ourselves with the Scriptures makes them more meaningful. (Acts 10:2) Therefore, we should make an effort to help people understand the Bible whenever we have the opportunity to share it with them. We can also take the time to review what we have taught them to ensure they grasp the key points. For example, we might offer to study another scripture with them and help them apply its principles to their life. Doing so will make God's Word come alive and encourage them to continue learning.—Read Luke 24:32.
9 Can we expect to always feel motivated to meditate on the scriptures, even if we try hard to understand the Bible? Consider an illustration.
9 Furthermore, we may not always feel motivated to meditate on the scriptures, but we can still use scriptures to help others appreciate the Bible. For instance, when speaking to someone, we might say, "Let us look at what our Creator says about this matter." Then we can discuss it with a fellow Christian and ask him: "What does Matthew chapter such and such teach us?" Or if we are talking to someone who is skeptical, we could ask: "Would you be willing to examine this verse with me?" In each case, we let the person decide whether he wants to investigate further, and we respect his decision.—1 Cor. 9:22, 23.
10. (a) How can we show genuine interest in others? (b) What benefits will we experience if we remain interested in those we teach?
10 Many people respond favorably when they see that we are genuinely interested in them and in their thoughts. Consider this example. One young man had been listening to cassette tapes for years. Recently, some publishers brought him a cassette containing recordings of talks given at a recent assembly. He listened to the tape and then asked them to read 2 Corinthians 1:3, 4, which said: "The God of all comfort; who comforts us in all our tribulation." The young man was so moved that he asked the publishers to visit him again so that he could hear more scriptures. This shows how important it is to help people understand that Jehovah's Word has practical value and can help them cope with life's problems.—Ps. 19:20.
LET US REMEMBER
11. What questions will we address in the following discussion?
11 We will discuss how to deal with objections and strong feelings. One reason why we want to be able to handle objections effectively is to glorify Jehovah. And, of course, we want to help others find comfort from the Scriptures. It is often difficult for young people to express themselves clearly. So it is important to determine whether an objection is sincere or simply a way of testing us. (Jas. 3:1) At all times, we should make sure that our thinking is in harmony with Bible principles. Would you feel comfortable if someone challenged your beliefs and showed you scripture that contradicted what you believe?
12. How can we ensure that the Bible is the foundation of our thinking?
12 The Bible can help us build a solid foundation for our thinking. (John 7:16) How can this be done? By carefully considering the scriptures, we can avoid being misled and help others to understand God's Word. But we must also use discernment so that our understanding does not cause division among those who love Jehovah. It is better to study the Bible thoroughly than to try to impress others with our knowledge. Often, those who have studied extensively find that they still disagree on certain points. Consider how to present information in a clear and understandable way, and always strive to explain things accurately. (Neh. 8:8) Briefly review the main points, read the relevant scriptures together, and then explain their meaning. Make sure you understand how the scriptures apply to your own life. Then, use them to strengthen your convictions. (But do not adopt a rigid attitude, Fáilika na Elimu ya Shule ya Huduma ya Kitheokrasi, pages 21-23.) And remember that the goal is to help people turn to Jehovah and appreciate his teachings—to understand the truth about him.—Read Psalm 7:10; Proverbs 3:13, 14.
13. (a) What might motivate someone to share a scripture with another person? (b) What might motivate you to share a scripture with someone?
13 A young man in Australia named Noah shared a scripture with a fellow student. He had been studying the Bible with his mother, and he wanted to help his friend learn about Jehovah. Over time, he realized that his friend seemed interested in what he was saying. He wondered if his friend felt drawn to Jehovah. He decided to ask him if he would like to know more about God. Why did he do that? Because he wanted to help his friend benefit from the scripture he had shared earlier. * Perhaps you too have had an opportunity to share a scripture with someone. Have you ever asked them if they would like to study the Bible with you or with the congregation?—Neh. 8:12.
14. How can we show that we value God's Word?
14 We can show that we value God's Word, the Bible! God has given us the Bible so that we may come to know him and love him more and more. (1 Pet. 1:24, 25) So let us read God's Word regularly, apply what we learn, and use it to teach others. By doing so, we will prove that we value it and that we are devoted to the Bible, along with its Author, Jehovah God.

text:
MŨTHENYA ũmwe mũsikalĩ wa KGB * andavisye ũũ angalĩkĩle: "We ndwĩ tei o na vanini!" Asyokie ambĩa: "Watiie kelĩtu kaku na kĩveti kyaku kĩ kĩito maithĩna. Nũũ ũkamamanthĩaa lĩu na aimasũvĩa? Ekana na maũndũ ala ũendeesye na ũyĩnũka!" Nĩvo nakwa namwĩie: "Aiee, ndyaatia andũ makwa. Ninyw'ĩ mwangwatie! Mũngwatĩe kĩ?" Nake anzũngĩlile ambĩa, "O na kavaa keka ũkwatĩwe ĩvĩtyo yĩngĩ ti kwĩthĩwa wĩ Ngũsĩ."
Twaneenanisye na mũsikalĩ ũsu mwakanĩ wa 1959 nĩ selinĩ ĩmwe yaĩ taoninĩ ya Irkutsk, Russia. Ekai nĩmũtavye nĩkĩ nyie na kĩveti kyakwa, Maria, tweeyũmbanĩtye 'kũthĩnw'a kwondũ wa ũlũngalu,' na moathimo ala tũkwatĩte nũndũ wa kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku.—1 Vet. 3:13, 14.
Nasyaiwe mwaka wa 1933 ũtũinĩ wa Zolotniki, nthĩ ya Ukraine. Mami aĩ na mwĩĩtu masyaanĩw'e na e na mũũme maĩ Ngũsĩ. Mũthenya ũmwe mwakanĩ wa 1937, nĩmookie kũtũkethya maumĩte France na matũtiĩa ĩvuku yeetawa Government na yĩngĩ yeetawa Deliverance, ala maumĩthiw'e nĩ Watch Tower Society. Tata asoma mavuku asu nĩwambĩĩe kũĩkĩĩa Ngai ĩngĩ. Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana mwakanĩ wa 1939, nĩwavinyĩĩiwe nĩ ũwau, ĩndĩ atanakw'a eeie Mami atĩĩ: "Ũw'o wĩ vaa. Manyĩsya syana ũw'o ũũ."
NĨTWAKWATIE MWANYA WA KŨTAVANY'A SIBERIA
Twĩ Mwei wa 4, 1951, silikalĩ nĩyambĩĩie kũthamya Ngũsĩ ila syaĩ ngalĩko ya ũthũĩlonĩ wa sua ya USSR ĩitwaĩte Siberia. Nyie, Mami, vamwe na kĩvĩsĩ kĩinawa kĩtawa Grigory, nĩtwaumiw'e West Ukraine. Twaendie na ngalĩ ya mwaki ũasa wa maili mbee wa 3,700 (kĩlomita 6,000) tũikaavika taoni ya Tulun, Siberia. Ĩtina wa syumwa ilĩ nake mwanake mũkũũa wĩtawa Bogdan nĩwavikiw'e kambinĩ yaĩ taoninĩ ya Angarsk, ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ na Tulun. Nake atw'ĩĩwe kyovo kya myaka 25 kya kũthũkũmĩthw'a wĩa mũmũ.
Nyie, Mami, vamwe na Grigory nĩtwatavasya andũ ala maĩ vakuvĩ na Tulun ũvoo mũseo, ĩndĩ yaĩ no nginya tũtũmĩe kĩlĩko. Ta kwa ngelekany'o, twakothaa kũkũlya andũ, "Vaa ve mũndũ ũkũta ng'ombe?" Twakitya ũmwe, twamũtavasya ũndũ ng'ombe yũmbĩtwe kwa nzĩa ya ũsengy'o. Ĩtina wa ũu vayaĩ vinya kwĩthĩa twambĩĩie kũea ngewa ĩũlũ wa Mũmbi. Ĩndĩ twĩkalangĩte, mathangũ ma kũnyaĩĩkya maũvoo nĩmaandĩkie kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itinie kũthi iikũlya ĩũlũ wa ng'ombe, ĩndĩ kĩla iũmantha nĩ malondu! Na o w'o ki, nĩtwakwatisye andũ mailyĩ ta malondu! Nĩtwatanĩaa mũno kwĩmanyĩsya Maandĩko na andũ auu na alau, ala maĩ kĩsionĩ kĩu. Sua ũũ taoni ya Tulun yĩ kĩkundi kĩ atavany'a mbee wa 100.
ŨNDŨ MŨĨKĨĨO WA MARIA WATATIWE
Kĩveti kyakwa, Maria, kyemanyĩĩisye ũw'o Ukraine ĩvinda yĩla Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe waĩ mũvyũ. Maria e wa myaka 18, mũsikalĩ ũmwe wa KGB nĩwambĩĩe kũmũthĩny'a aimwenda, na atata kũmũthing'ĩĩsya meke ũlaalai ĩndĩ amũlea vyũ. Mũthenya ũmwe enũka, eethĩie ũla mũndũ eyĩilĩĩle kĩtandanĩ kyake. Maria eekie ũsemba. Mũsikalĩ ũsu athatie mũno na amwĩa nũkũmũtwaa seli ovwe nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa nĩ Ngũsĩ. Ũu nĩw'o vaendie. Mwakanĩ wa 1952 Maria nĩwatw'ĩĩiwe kyovo kya myaka ĩkũmi. Eew'aa ta Yosevu, ũla wooviwe nũndũ wa kũlũmany'a na Ngai. (Mwa. 39:12, 20) Ndeleva ũla waumisye Maria kotinĩ amũtwaa yela amwĩie: "Ndũkakĩe. Ve aingĩ maendaa yela na mayĩsa kuma mataaĩyanangĩa ĩsyĩtwa." Ndeto isu syamwĩkĩie vinya mũno.
Kuma mwaka wa 1952 nginya 1956, Maria ekalile kambinĩ ya wĩa mũmũ ĩla yaĩ vakuvĩ na taoni ya Gorkiy (ũmũnthĩ yĩtawa Nizhniy Novgorod), Russia. Anengetwe wĩa wa kũkũa mĩtĩ o na ĩla kũthithu vyũ. Kĩu nĩkyatumie akwatwa nĩ mathĩna ma mwĩĩ, ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1956 nĩwathaiw'e na athi Tulun.
KŨTAANANW'A NA KĨVETI NA SYANA SYAKWA
Ĩla mwana-a-asa ũmwe tweethĩawa nake Tulun wandavisye kana ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũkĩte, noosie kĩsululu na nathi kũmũthaũa sitengyi nĩmũkuĩĩsye mĩio. Ngoo yakwa yendie Maria o ĩla namwonie oou. Ĩndĩ navatethisye wĩa mwingĩ mũno ayĩsa ũtw'ĩka nĩwambenda. Twatwaanie mwaka wa 1957. Mwaka ũithela, nĩtwakwatie kelĩtu kaitũ ka mbee kala ketawa Irina. Ĩndĩ o na ndyaaĩkalany'a nako ĩvinda yĩana ũndũ. Neekĩiwe mbĩnĩ mwaka wa 1959 nũndũ wa kũtumbĩthya mavuku ma Mbivilia. Naminie nusu mwaka nĩvingĩwe vandũ nĩ weka. Kĩla kyandethisye ndikathĩnĩke ĩvinda yĩu yonthe nĩ kũvoya ndeũtĩĩa, kwina mbathi sya Ũsumbĩ, na kũsũanĩa ũndũ ndonya kũtavany'a nesa kũlekw'a.
Nĩ vau yela, mũndũũme ũmwe nĩwookie kũngũlya makũlyo. Avikie vandũ angũthũkĩa na wasya mũtũlu ambĩa, "Twĩmũkinyangĩa nthĩ ta mbĩa tũmũmine vyũ!" Nakwa namũsũngĩa: "Yesũ aisye kana ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ ŨKATAVANW'A kwa mbaĩ syonthe, na vai mũndũ ũtonya kũũngamya wĩa ũsu." Mũndũũme ũsu eew'a ũu, oonie vandũ va kũndelemya, nĩ kavaa ambĩsũve nĩkaĩe mũĩkĩĩo wakwa. Kĩu nĩkyo nĩwetie mwambĩĩonĩ wa ngewa ĩno. Ĩla kĩu nakyo kyaemelile, nĩnatw'ĩĩwe kwovwa myaka mũonza kambinĩ ya wĩa mũmũ, ĩla yaĩ vakuvĩ na taoni ya Saransk. Ndanamba ũvika kambinĩ ĩsu nĩnakwatie ũvoo kana kelĩtu kaitũ ka kelĩ, Olga, kaĩ kanasyawa. O na kau naĩ vaasa vyũ na kĩveti kyakwa na twĩlĩtu twakwa, neew'aa nakwata ũkiakĩsyo nalilikana kana nyie na Maria nĩtwalũmanĩtye na Yeova.
Mũthenya ũmwe kwa mwaka, Maria nĩwaumaa Tulun akoka Saransk kũmbona. Kuma Tulun kũthi Saransk na kũsyoka na ngalĩ ya mwaki kwakuaa mĩthenya 12. Kĩla mwaka andeteae mbuti nzaũ. Asyokaa akavitha makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya ala ma mĩtũkĩ itiinyonĩ sya mbuti isu. Mwaka ũmwe ũtakola nĩ ũla Maria wookie kũmbona e na twĩlĩtu twitũ twĩlĩ. Kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla neewie ĩla namonie na natũmĩa ĩvinda namo!
KŨTHAMĨĨA ISIO INGĨ NA MAWETU ALA TWAKOMANIE NAMO
Nathaiw'e mwaka wa 1966, na twĩ ana twathamĩĩa taoninĩ ya Armavir, ĩla yĩ vakuvĩ na Black Sea. Imwana sitũ ilĩ, Yaroslav na Pavel, syasyaĩwe kũu.
Twekalangile o vanini na asikalĩ ma KGB mooka kũvekesa mũsyĩ witũ maimantha mavuku ma Mbivilia. Mamanthie kĩla vandũ o na kũla twaiĩte ũĩthyo wa ng'ombe. Mũthenya ũmwe mamanthie nginya manyala na ngũa syoo syatw'ĩka sya kĩtoo kĩthei. Maria amew'ĩie tei mũno nũndũ kũyaĩ kwenda kwoo, meekaa kũatĩĩa mwĩao. Kwoou nĩwamekĩĩie kĩw'ũ kya matunda, na amanenga kĩndũ kya kũvangũla kĩtoo, vamwe na kĩw'ũ, na taũlo. Ĩla mũnene woo wavikie, asikalĩ asu nĩmamũtavisye ũndũ makuwa nesa. Makwata nzĩa mathi, mũnene ũsu atũkĩlĩilye kw'oko ew'ĩte mũyo. Ũtanu witũ waĩ kwona ũseo wa 'kũkĩlya ũthũku vinya na ũseo.'—Alo. 12:21.
O na kau asikalĩ asu nĩmakothaa mũno kũka kwitũ, tũyaaeka kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩu kya Armavir. O na nĩtwatatie kwĩkĩa vinya kakundi ka atavany'a kala kaĩ taoninĩ yĩ o vau vakuvĩ yĩtawa Kurganinsk. Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno kwona Armavir ve ikundi thanthatũ, na Kurganinsk ve inya.
Myakanĩ ĩsu ve mavinda twaleelaa kĩ-veva. Ĩndĩ nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ nĩwatũmĩie ana-a-asa aĩkĩĩku matũlũnga, na matũtetheesya twalũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ nake. (Sav. 130:3) Ĩtatwa yĩngĩ yetu yaĩ kũthũkũma vamwe na andũ matũmĩtwe nĩ KGB, na makalika kĩkundinĩ o na tũteũmanya. Andũ asu moonekaa me kĩthito, na mayatĩĩaa ũtavany'a. O na amwe nĩmanengiwe ĩanda ũseũvyonĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩtwesie kũmekuũa na twamamanya.
Mwakanĩ wa 1978, Maria nĩwaitavie ĩngĩ e na myaka 45. Ayĩitava aĩ na ũwau mũthũku wa ngoo, na matakĩtalĩ moonaa atevĩta, kwoou matata kũmũsesenga aumye ĩvu yĩu. Ĩndĩ Maria ndaaĩtĩkĩla. Nũndũ wa ũũ matakĩtalĩ amwe matindaa mamũatĩĩe kĩla vandũ sivitalĩ ĩla waĩ makuĩte singano mayenda kũmũtonya ndawa nĩ kana asyae kana kate kaviku. Nĩ kana Maria asũvĩe kana kake, eekie kũkĩla auma ĩ sivitalĩ.
Anene ma KGB matwĩie tume taoninĩ ĩsu vyũ. Kwoou nĩtwathamĩĩe ndũanĩ ĩmwe yĩ vakuvĩ na taoni ya Tallinn, ĩla yĩ kĩsionĩ kya Estonia. Ĩvinda yĩu kĩsio kĩu kyaĩ ungu wa USSR. Kĩvathũkany'o na ndeto sya ila ndakĩtalĩ, twĩ kũu Tallinn, Maria asyaie nesa kavĩsĩ kaseo kate na ũndũ, kala twaketie Vitaly.
Nĩtwesie kuma Estonia twathi ngalĩko ya Nezlobnaya, ĩla yĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya nthĩ ya Russia. Nĩtwatavanasya taoninĩ ila syatũthyũlũlũkĩte nũndũ syaĩ na andũ aingĩ matembeaa kũu maumĩte isionĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya Russia, o na kau tweekaa ũu twĩtũĩe. Andũ asu mookaa kũu maimantha ũiiti, ĩndĩ amwe maumaa vo me na wĩkwatyo wa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela.
KŨMANYĨSYA SYANA SITŨ KŨMWENDA YEOVA
Nĩtweekĩie kĩthito kingĩ mũno twatetheesya syana sitũ imwende Yeova na iyĩthĩwa na wendi wa kũmũthũkũma. Nĩtwakothaa kũthokya ana-a-asa mũsyĩ, namo nĩmatetheeisye mũno syana sitũ. Ũmwe twathokasya nĩ mwana-a-mwaitũ, Grigory, ũla waĩ mũsyaĩĩsya wa kũthyũlũlũka kuma 1970 nginya 1995. Ithyonthe nĩtwew'aa mũyo twamwona nũndũ ekalaa e mũtanu na aĩ mathekany'a. Ĩla twathokewa nĩtwakothaa kũthaũka mathaũ ma maũndũ me Mbivilianĩ. Na nũndũ wa ũu, syana sitũ syeanie syendete mũno ngewa ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ.
Mwakanĩ wa 1987, mwana witũ ũla wĩtawa Yaroslav, nĩwathamĩĩie taoninĩ ya Riga, nthĩ ya Latvia, vala waĩ atonya kũtavany'a na ũthasyo. Ĩndĩ ĩla wesie kũlea kũthũkũma na ita, nĩwooviwe mwaka ũmwe na nusu na atwaiwe yela kenda syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ngewa ila namũtavĩtye ĩũlũ wa ĩla nyie naĩ mwove, nĩsyamũnengie vinya wa kũmĩĩsya. Tũendeangĩe nĩwoosie ũvainia. Mwakanĩ wa 1990 mwana witũ, Pavel, ũla waĩ na myaka 19 ĩvinda yĩu, aisye nũkwenda kũkũna ũvainia kĩthamanĩ kya Sakhalin, kĩla kĩ ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya Japan. Mbeenĩ tũyendaa kũmũlekya. Kĩthama kĩu kyaĩ na atavany'a 20 tũ, na kyaĩ ũasa wa maili mbee wa 5,500 (kĩlomita 9,000) kuma vala twatwĩe. Nĩtwesie kũmwĩtĩkĩlya athi na ũsu waĩ ũtwi mũseo. Andũ ma kĩthama kĩu nĩmeethukĩĩisye ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩtina wa myaka o mĩnini, ikundi nyanya nĩsyaambĩĩiw'e kũu. Pavel ekalile Sakhalin nginya mwaka wa 1995. Kũvika ĩvinda yĩu, ũla twatiĩtwe nake mũsyĩ no ĩlumaita yitũ, Vitaly. Endete kũsoma Mbivilia kuma e kana. Vitaly oosie ũvainia e wa myaka 14, na nakũna ũvainia nĩ nake kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩlĩ. Twatanĩie ta kĩ! Vitaly atw'ĩkie vainia wa mwanya e na myaka 19, na ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o waumie mũsyĩ.
Navu ĩtina mwakanĩ wa 1952, mũsikalĩ ũmwe wa KGB eeie Maria atĩĩ: "Maũndũ no elĩ: ũkaĩe mũĩkĩĩo waku, kana wovwe myaka ĩkũmi. Naku woovwa, ũkesa kũthaw'a wakũie na ũte mũndũ wĩta waku." Ĩndĩ kũyaathi ũu. Twĩthĩĩtwe na anyanya matwendete, ta Ngai witũ mũĩkĩĩku, Yeova, syana sitũ, na angĩ aingĩ ala twakwatie mwanya wa kũmamanyĩsya ũla w'o. Nĩ na Maria nĩtwakwatie mwanya wa kũtembea kũla syana sitũ syatũmĩtwe. Nĩtwatanĩaa mũno kwona ala matetheeiw'e nĩ syana sitũ kũmũmanya Yeova mayĩw'a mũyo nũndũ wa kĩthito kyoo.
NĨNĨTŨNGAA MŨVEA NŨNDŨ WA ŨSEO WA YEOVA
Mwakanĩ wa 1991 silikalĩ nĩyanengie Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mwanya wa kũtethya wĩa woo. Ũthasyo ũsu nĩwatumie ana-a-asa mongela kĩthito wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. O na nĩngũlilikana kĩkundi kitũ kĩithooa mbasi ya kũendaa isionĩ na taoninĩ ila syĩ vakuvĩ kĩla wikendi.
Nĩndũngaa mũvea kwona Yaroslav na mũka, Alyona, na Pavel na mũka, Raya, me Mbetheli, nake Vitaly na mũka, Svetlana, me wĩanĩ wa kũthyũlũlũka. Mwĩĩtu witũ ũla mũkũũ, Irina, na andũ make mekalaa Germany. Mũũme, ũla wĩtawa Vladimir, na imwana syoo itatũ, nĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi. Nake mwĩĩtu witũ, Olga, ekalaa nthĩ ya Estonia na nũngũnĩaa simũ kĩla ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ nĩ na kyeva kũweta kana kĩveti kyakwa, Maria, nĩkyakwie 2014. Neteele mũno kũmwona ĩla wĩthayũũkw'a! Ũmũnthĩ nĩkalaa taoninĩ ya Belgorod, na ana-a-asa ala me vaa nĩ ũtethyo mũnene kwakwa.
Myaka ĩla nĩmũthũkũmĩte Yeova ĩmanyĩĩtye kana kũlũmany'a nake kũi laisi, ĩndĩ mũuo ũla ũkũnengae ndũelekanw'a na kĩndũ kĩngĩ o na kĩva. Moathimo ala nĩ na Maria twakwatie nũndũ wa kũlũmany'a na Yeova nĩ maingĩ kwĩ ũndũ nataĩaa. USSR ĩtanamba kũvalũka mwaka wa 1991, atavany'a ala maĩ kĩsionĩ kĩĩ mathonokete 40,000 o vanini. Ũmũnthĩ, nthĩ ila syaĩ ungu wa Soviet Union syĩ na atavany'a mbee wa 400,000! Yu nĩ na myaka 83, na nĩ o mũtumĩa kĩkundinĩ kitũ. Ĩvinda yonthe Yeova nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ainenga vinya wa kũmĩĩsya. Vate nzika, Yeova nũngathimĩte mũno.—Sav. 13:5, 6.
^ kal. 4 KGB nĩ ũkuvĩ wa ĩsyĩtwa ya kĩthyomo kya Russian ya Soviet State Security Committee.
