translation:
There is a visa for Timothy who has been circumcised, who also comes from a circumcised family like his mother. He is praised because he has good behavior among the young people. And when things go well, he will continue to serve the list, which is full of the words of many believers. Timothy is ready to explain this matter and teach five cities, and also travel with someone to help him. But why should he explain to others what they already know?
Little by little, the apostle Paul remembered and encouraged Timothy with various things. Paul was sure that Timothy was sincere and had faith in his teachings. So he asked Timothy how old he was, whether sixty or seventy years old, and he went with Paul and helped him greatly. Timothy traveled with a good companion who was very kind and helpful. We have sent them to you to encourage you, and they will tell you everything about our situation. Timothy may be able to come soon.
Why did Timothy go with Paul? How can we learn to be humble? And how can we understand Timothy's example?
'COME AND HELP US'
After three years of serving in the Lystra region, Timothy continued to work there. They encouraged Timothy with the reports they received from him. The news about this service spread, and the believers were strengthened. They encouraged the people to be faithful to the teaching of Cilicia and Iconium. One day, the people in the area gathered together and attacked them. The apostle Paul and Barnabas fled to Lystra and Iconium, where they stayed for a long time in Lystra. While traveling through those areas, Paul saw a man who was lame and had always been crippled. He noticed that the man had faith!—Acts of the Apostles 14:5-10.
It seems that many people in Lystra thought Paul and Barnabas were gods who had come down from heaven because they spoke in their language. They called Paul Zeus and Barnabas Hermes! They wanted to offer sacrifices to them! But the apostles told them that they were just men and urged them to turn away from such foolish ideas.—Acts of the Apostles 14:11-18.
Some people in Lystra believed Paul and Barnabas because they had performed miracles, but others were skeptical and wondered what was happening. For example, there was Eunice, a Jewish woman who was known for her devotion to God, and her mother Lois, who was influenced by the things Paul and Barnabas taught. Paul and Barnabas taught about the hope of life everlasting, which helped people to believe that the Messiah would come and fulfill the prophecies found in the Scriptures!
To strengthen Timothy's faith, Paul reminded him of the faith his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice had. Timothy had learned the Sacred Writings "from infancy." (2 Timothy 3:15) And like his mother and grandmother, Timothy came to believe that Paul and Barnabas were teaching the truth about the Messiah. To strengthen his faith further, Paul sent Timothy on a journey to visit the brothers in Lystra. He wanted Timothy to encourage them and help them to remain strong in the faith! Just as Eunice and Lois showed faith in Christ, so did Timothy. May we also be able to say that we have learned much from faithful women like Lois and Eunice. What can we learn from their example?
"SHOW GREAT GRATITUDE"
When Paul and Barnabas visited Lystra, they met people who had never heard of Christ, yet they worshiped idols. But Paul and Barnabas explained to them what Jesus had done. They helped those people to turn away from idolatry and toward the true God. However, some people from Iconium and Antioch stirred up trouble, and they turned the crowds against Paul and Barnabas. So Paul and Barnabas fled to nearby cities. Despite this, they continued to preach the good news. And they strengthened the disciples, encouraging them to continue in the faith.—Acts 14:19.
Paul and Barnabas were able to return to Lystra and strengthen the brothers. Then they went on to Derbe, where they made more disciples. But they faced opposition everywhere they went! How did they cope? They relied on Jehovah and kept preaching. They remembered the words: "We must undergo much tribulation to enter the Kingdom of God." That is why Timothy, a young man whom Paul greatly valued, joined them in their work of spreading the good news, even though there was danger. They said: "Let us firmly encourage the brothers, telling them that we must endure many hardships to enter God's Kingdom." —Acts 14:20-22.
Timothy accompanied Paul while he traveled from town to town, strengthening the brothers in faith. He learned from Paul how to remain courageous despite facing difficulties. And he saw how the brothers in Lystra and other places responded to his encouragement. Timothy realized that he needed to be zealous in serving Jehovah. Many others also benefited from his example of courage and determination.
"A SERVANT WHO IS QUALIFIED TO BE TRUSTED"
As we have seen, Paul often entrusted important assignments to faithful Christians. For instance, when he sent Timothy, along with Silas, on a journey to visit the congregations, he knew that they would be able to deliver his message effectively. He trusted them to use their time wisely and to persevere. Some of the qualities that Paul looked for in those he assigned tasks to were loyalty and a sincere faith, like that of Lois and Eunice, Timothy's mother and grandmother, who had "unhypocritical devotion." Paul recognized that such qualities were vital.—2 Timothy 1:5. What about you?
Paul knew that Timothy would continue to serve faithfully wherever he went. Timothy 'was spoken well of by the brothers' in Lystra and Iconium, cities some 20 miles (32 kilometers) apart in the province of Galatia. (Acts 16:2) Why was Timothy spoken well of?
"Holy Writings" helped Timothy to 'stand firm' in the face of opposition from people in the community. (2 Timothy 3:15) One principle found in the Holy Scriptures is: "Remember your Creator while young." (Ecclesiastes 12:1) This counsel was especially helpful to Timothy because he wanted to please Christ. Paul understood that if Timothy continued to remember his Creator, he would not easily be influenced by false teachings during the time of Christendom, the Son of God. Timothy made a point of being associated with those who were loyal and of benefiting from their example of remaining courageous in serving Jesus Christ.
Furthermore, I have strong affection for Timothy, so I sent him on my way. And I hope to come to see you soon, if Jehovah allows me. God has shown great love for us, and He will strengthen us to do good works in connection with everything Timothy does. But Paul also realized that Timothy did not always feel confident. So he encouraged him, along with others in Lystra, to remain steadfast. I remind you of my own example, so that you may know how you should conduct yourselves in God's house—1 Timothy 1:18; 4:14.
And we should remember that Timothy was a young man when he began traveling and speaking, yet he proved himself reliable. He accompanied Paul. *But what made Timothy willing to travel with Paul despite his youth? What qualities did he display that showed his mother and grandmother had trained him well? And what about his father and his background? It seems that he came from a Jewish family, and his mother was a believing woman. Did those five factors help to prepare Timothy for taking hold of the truth? This is something to think about carefully.
The thing we see is that Timothy was willing to go on this trip. So because they went through the cities one by one, Timothy traveled with Paul during his second journey to spread the good news. And then he continued to travel with them later on to visit the brothers. From Lystra there came a disciple named Timothy who had a Jewish mother and a Christian father. While they were passing through Iconium, Timothy joined them. Then Paul instructed Timothy to be circumcised so that he might preach the good news along with him and Silas as they went through the towns and villages. And he saw to it that he would have the opportunity to share the message of Christ in Iconium. (Acts 16:4, 5) That's how it happened.
From there they passed through Phrygia and Galatia, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia; and when they reached Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit did not permit them. So they passed through Troas and sailed from there to Macedonia. (Acts 16:6-12) After seeing this vision, Paul told Timothy to join him. And he sent men ahead to wait for them in Thessalonica. (Acts 17:14) And he sent him to Thessalonica. Timothy then reported back about the things concerning which you have inquiries, and this is what he sent to us regarding your faith.—1 Thessalonians 3:1-3.
Paul wrote this about Timothy: "I have no one equal to him who will genuinely care for your welfare." (Philippians 2:20) Today, too, we need people like Timothy. They are identified by their genuine concern, their loyalty, and their courage in facing opposition. Let us imitate their zeal in serving others! Do not hesitate to offer yourself to be used in this important work. Elders, you can provide opportunities for others to serve by training them to help you in proclaiming Jehovah our God and teaching others the truth.—
"KEEP SHINING YOUR LIGHT"
For over 14 years, Timothy accompanied Paul on many journeys as a missionary. Like Paul, Timothy faced many difficulties and experienced much hardship. (2 Corinthians 11:24-27) Yet, he proved himself faithful in his ministry. (Hebrews 13:23) Also, Timothy visited fellow Christians often and encouraged them because he knew how Paul felt. That is why Paul wrote about him: "I miss your affection deeply." (2 Timothy 1:4) It seems that Timothy was reminded to 'associate with those who are thinking correctly,' and to avoid those who were causing division and stumbling others. (Romans 12:15) Let each of us take this to heart!
Truly, we can learn a lot from Timothy's example of being a fine member of the Christian congregation. Paul entrusted Timothy with many responsibilities, including helping the congregation to remain united, even if some got discouraged, by encouraging mature brothers to spend time with and assist troubled ones.—1 Timothy 5:22.
Paul treated Timothy like a son, and he gave him many loving corrections to help him. He also reminded Timothy to continue putting spiritual things first and to make progress. (1 Timothy 4:15, 16) Paul urged Timothy to train young men and to teach them how to conduct themselves properly and defend the truth. (1 Timothy 1:3; 4:6, 7, 11, 12) And he advised him regarding matters that could affect his health, suggesting that he drink a little wine for his frequent illnesses.—1 Timothy 5:23.
The time came when Paul realized that his end was near. So he sent for Timothy, his beloved companion. He asked him to come quickly. He wrote: "Do your best to get here before winter." (2 Timothy 4:9) Because Paul loved Timothy so much, he called him "my dearly loved son in the faith."—1 Corinthians 4:17) And that is why he wanted his loyal companion to be with him at his final hour! Let each of us ask ourselves, 'If I were in their place, would I have shown such love and concern?'
Did Timothy travel to see Paul during those last days? Yes, we know this because the Bible does not say whether anyone else accompanied Paul and Luke, but it mentions that Timothy was there. Timothy remained close to his conviction, "A Minister of God." And let us remember what we learn from them, so that we may remain faithful, even when faced with difficulties.
^ kal. 20 Also, Timothy traveled with Paul on many missionary journeys. This shows his loyalty to Christ, and because Paul planned to visit Ephesus again, he sent Timothy ahead to prepare the brothers there.—Acts 16:3.

text:
"Nyeki nĩyũmaa, na ĩlaa nĩyĩvovaa; ĩndĩ ndeto ya Ngai waitũ ĩkekala tene na tene."—ISA. 40:8.
MBATHI: 43, 48
1, 2. (a) Maũndũ methĩwa mailyĩ ata keka tũi na Mbivilia? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũtetheka mũnango nĩ Ndeto ya Ngai?
WE WĨONA ta wĩthĩwa va takeka ndwaaĩthĩa Mbivilia? Ve vangĩ ũkwata ũtao mũseo ta ũla ũkwataa Mbivilianĩ? O na wĩona ta wĩsa kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala wĩthĩwa namo ĩũlũ wa Ngai, thayũ witũ, kana ũndũ maũndũ matonya kwĩthĩwa mailyĩ ĩvinda yũkĩte? O na eka ũu, keka ti Mbivilia, ndwĩsa kũmanya ũndũ Yeova wĩthĩĩtwe aitetheesya andũ kuma tene.
2 Ĩndĩ ithyĩ nĩtwĩsĩ maũndũ asu onthe. Tũtũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ Yeova nũtũnengete Ndeto yake, Mbivilia. O na nũtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana ũvoo ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ũkekala tene na tene. Mũtũmwa Vetelo nĩwawetie ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Isaia 40:8. O na kau mũsoa ũsu ũneeneete ũvoo ũla Ngai wanengie andũ, no ũtũmĩwe kwonany'a ĩ Mbivilia mbene. (Soma 1 Vetelo 1:24, 25.) Kũneena ũla w'o, Mbivilia ĩkethĩwa ĩtũmĩĩte kĩthyomo tũte kũelewa nesa, ndĩsa kũtũtethya mũno. Kuma tene, ala mendete Ndeto ya Ngai nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana ũu nĩ w'o. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka maana maingĩ, amwe maĩ na ngoo ntheu nĩmatatie kũalyũla na kũnyaĩĩkya Maandĩko o na kau wĩa ũsu ndwaĩ laisi. Kĩthito kĩu maĩ nakyo kyoosanĩte na kwenda kwa Ngai, "ũla wendaa andũ onthe matangĩĩwe, na moke mamanye ũla w'o."—1 Tim. 2:3, 4.
3. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 18.)
3 Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ nĩtũkwona maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o mekwonany'a ũndũ Ndeto ya Ngai yĩkalĩte ĩteũthingithĩka o na kũtw'ĩka (1) ithyomo nĩsyĩthĩĩtwe iivĩndũkanga, (2) silikalĩ imwe syoosa ũtongoi kĩsionĩ kĩna nĩsyatumaa kĩthyomo kĩla kyatũmĩawa kĩsionĩ kĩu kĩeka kũtũmĩwa na kĩngĩ kĩsĩkĩe nĩ andũ aingĩ kĩyosa mwanya wakyo, na (3) wĩa wa kũalyũla Mbivilia nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ũivĩngwa. Kũneenea maũndũ asu kwĩtũtethya ata? Kĩu no kĩtume twenda mũno Ndeto ya Ngai. O na ĩngĩ, kũneenea maũndũ asu no kũtume tũmwenda mũnango Mũandĩkĩthya wa Mbivilia, ũla watũnengie yo nĩ kana ĩtũune.—Mika 4:2; Alo. 15:4.
ŨALYŨKU WA ITHYOMO
4. (a) Ithyomo ialyũkaa ata? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana Ngai ndendeeasya andũ ma kĩthyomo kĩmwe, na kĩu kĩtumaa wĩw'a ata?
4 Ithyomo nĩsyĩkalaa iialyũka. O ũndũ ĩvinda yĩvĩtĩte, ndeto imwe nitonya kũalyũka ikambĩĩa kũeleeka ũndũ ũngĩ. No kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kũsũanĩa ũndũ ndeto imwe sya kĩthyomo wĩsĩ ivĩndũkĩte. Ũu now'o ithyomo sya Kĩevelania na Kĩkiliki syavĩndũkie. Ithyomo isu nĩsyo syatũmĩiwe kũandĩka mavuku ala maingĩ ma Mbivilia. Ũmũnthĩ andũ ala maneenaa Kĩevelania na Kĩkiliki maitũmĩaa ndeto ila syatũmĩawa ĩvinda ya andũ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Kwoou vakuvĩ kĩla mũndũ ũkwenda kũelewa Ndeto ya Ngai no nginya amĩsome yĩ mbalyũle, o na atw'ĩke nĩwĩsĩ Kĩevelania na Kĩkiliki kĩla kĩneenawa ũmũnthĩ. Andũ amwe monaa maĩle kwĩmanyĩsya Kĩevelania na Kĩkiliki kya tene nĩ kenda masome Mbivilia na kĩthyomo kĩla yaandĩkiwe nakyo mwambĩĩonĩ. Ĩndĩ kwĩka ũu kũimatethya ũndũ masũanĩaa. * Ũseo nĩ kana Mbivilia yonthe kana o ilungu imwe syayo nialyũlĩtwe na ithyomo mbee wa 3,000. Ũu nĩ kwonany'a nesa vyũ kana Yeova endaa andũ ma "kĩla mũthemba na mbaĩ na kĩthyomo" maunĩke nĩ Ndeto yake. (Soma Ũvuan'yo 14:6.) We wĩona ata? Ũsu tyo ũndũ ũtuma ũmũthengeea Ngai witũ wĩ wendo na ũte mwendeesya wa andũ?—Meko 10:34.
5. Nĩkĩ Mbivilia ya King James Version yaĩ ya vata mũno?
5 Nĩtwoona kana ithyomo nĩsyĩkalaa iialyũka. Kwoou o nasyo ithyomo ila syatũmĩiwe nĩ ala maalyũlile Mbivilia syeekie oou. Nũndũ wa ũu, Mbivilia nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yaeleekaa nesa yamina kũalyũlwa ya mbee oou, ĩndĩ no yĩkale ĩkesa kũeka kũeleeka. Kwasũanĩa Mbivilia ĩmwe yaalyũlilwe na Kĩsũngũ. Mbivilia ĩsu nĩ King James Version, na yaumĩthiw'e ya mbee mwaka wa 1611. Yatw'ĩkie ĩmwe ya Mbivilia ila syĩsĩkĩe vyũ sya Kĩsũngũ na nĩyatethisye mũno kĩthyomo kya Kĩsũngũ nũndũ ala maneenaa kĩthyomo kĩu nĩmambĩĩe kũtũmĩaa ndeto imwe syatũmĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ ĩsu ngewanĩ syoo sya kĩla mũthenya. * O na Mbivilia ĩsu ya King James Version nĩyatũmĩie ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai o na kau yeekie ũu o kũndũ kũvũthũ. Yatũmĩie ĩsyĩtwa "Yeova" mĩsoanĩ mĩnini Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania, na yatũmĩa ndeto "MWĨAĨI" ĩandĩkĩtwe na nthoo nene mĩsoanĩ ĩngĩ o Maandĩkonĩ o asu kũla kwaaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Mbivilia ila ingĩ sya King James Version syesie kumw'a ĩtina syatũmĩie ndeto "MWĨAĨI" ĩandĩkĩtwe na nthoo nene mĩsoanĩ ĩmwe Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu, Mbivilia ya King James Version nĩyoonanisye kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa Maandĩkonĩ ala metawa nĩ andũ aingĩ Ũtianĩo Mweũ.
6. Nĩkĩ tũtanaa kwĩthĩwa na Mbivilia ya New World Translation?
6 Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda, Kĩsũngũ kĩla kyatũmĩiwe nĩ King James Version nĩkyesie kũvĩtwa nĩ ĩvinda. Na ũu now'o vethĩĩtwe vailyĩ na Mbivilia ila syaalyũlilwe tene na ithyomo ingĩ. We tyo ũtanaa kũmanya kana mĩvango nĩyĩkĩtwe nĩ kana Mbivilia ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe na kĩthyomo kya matukũ aa ya New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures ĩkwatĩkane kwa ithyomo mbingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka? Mbivilia ĩsu yuyu nĩalyũlĩtwe yĩ nima kana yĩ nusu na ithyomo mbee wa 150, na kwoou andũ aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ũmũnthĩ no mamĩkwate. Nũndũ ĩtũmĩĩte kĩthyomo kĩkũeleeka nesa, mũndũ aimĩsoma no ew'e Ndeto ya Ngai ĩilika nesa ngoonĩ yake. (Sav. 119:97) Ĩndĩ kĩndũ kĩla kĩseo vyũ na Mbivilia ya New World Translation nĩ kana nĩtũngĩĩe ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai vala yaĩle kwĩthĩwa yĩandĩkĩtwe Maandĩkonĩ.
KĨTHYOMO KĨSĨKĨE NĨ ANDŨ AINGĨ
7, 8. (a) Nĩkĩ Ayuti aingĩ ala mekalaa myakanĩ ya 200 Klĩsto ate mũsyae mataĩ matonya kũelewa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania? (b) Nĩ ĩvuku yĩva yĩtawa Septuagint?
7 Silikalĩ ĩngĩ yoosa ũtongoi kĩsionĩ kĩna nĩtonya kũtuma kĩthyomo kĩla kĩnatũmĩawa kĩeka kũtũmĩwa na kĩngĩ kĩsĩkĩe nĩ andũ aingĩ kĩyosa mwanya wakyo. Ngai eekie ata aĩkĩĩthye kana o na moalyũku asu meethĩwa andũ nĩmaendeea kũkwata Ndeto yake na kĩthyomo mekũelewa? Ve ngelekany'o ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya kũkwata ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu. Mavuku ma mbee 39 ma Mbivilia maandĩkiwe nĩ Aisilaeli, kana Ayuti. Asu nĩmo maĩ ma mbee 'kũnengwa motũmani ma Ngai.' (Alo. 3:1, 2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Ĩndĩ kũvika myakanĩ ya 200 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, Ayuti aingĩ mayaeleawa Kĩevelania. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu Ũsumbĩ wa Ũkiliki ũtongoew'e nĩ Alexander Ũla Mũnene nĩwavalũkĩtye nthĩ mbingĩ na ũkaisumbĩka. (Nda. 8:5-7, 20, 21) Na kwoou kĩthyomo kya Kĩkiliki nĩkyanyaĩĩkie nthĩ ila syasumbĩkiwe nĩ Ũkiliki na andũ aingĩ mambĩĩa kũkĩtũmĩa. O na Ayuti ala maĩ isionĩ isu nĩmakĩtũngie ta kyo kĩthyomo kyoo. O ũndũ myaka yavĩtie now'o Ayuti aingĩ meethĩiwe matatonya kũelewa nesa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania nũndũ kĩthyomo kĩu kyaendeee kũla. Mesie kũunwa nĩ kyaũ?
8 Myakanĩ ĩsu ya 200 na kĩndũ Klĩsto ate mũsyae ĩivika katĩ, mavuku atano ma mbee ma Mbivilia ala maandĩkĩtwe na Kĩevelania nĩmaalyũlilwe na Kĩkiliki. Mavuku ala angĩ ma Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania maminie kũalyũlwa myakanĩ ya 100 na kĩndũ Klĩsto ate mũsyae. Maandĩko asu maalyũlilwe na Kĩkiliki na makwatanw'a nĩmo mesie kwĩtwa Septuagint. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvuku ya mbee yĩ na Maandĩko onthe ma Kĩevelania me maalyũle.
9. (a) Yĩla ĩvuku yesie kwĩtwa Septuagint na ilungu ila sya Maandĩko syaalyũlilwe tene syatetheeisye ata ala masomaa Ndeto ya Ngai? (b) Nĩ kĩlungu kĩva kya Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania wĩw'aa wendete mũno?
9 Ĩvuku ya Septuagint nĩyatetheeisye Ayuti aingĩ vamwe na ala angĩ matũmĩaa kĩthyomo kya Kĩkiliki mesomee nesa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ meew'aa masomewa kana masoma Ndeto ya Ngai na kĩthyomo kĩla yu kyaĩ kĩnatw'ĩka kyoo! Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, ilungu imwe sya Mbivilia nĩsyesie kũalyũlwa na ithyomo ingĩ syeesĩkĩe nĩ andũ aingĩ ta kĩthyomo kya Kĩlatinĩ, kya Asilia, na kya andũ meetawa Goths. Andũ maĩ matonya kũsoma mũno Maandĩko Matheu na kĩthyomo mekũelewa, na nũndũ wa ũu aingĩ nĩmendeeiw'e nĩ ilungu imwe o tondũ twĩkaa ũmũnthĩ. (Soma Savuli 119:162-165.) Vate nzika, Ndeto ya Ngai nĩyĩkalĩte ĩteũthingithĩka o na ĩla kweethĩwa ũalyũku wa kĩthyomo.
WĨA WA KŨALYŨLA MBIVILIA NĨWAVĨNGIWE
10. Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ mataĩ makwata Mbivilia ĩvindanĩ ya John Wycliffe?
10 Ve mavinda amwe andũ me ũkũmũ mũnene matatie kũsiĩĩa andũ ala moonekaa mate asomu maikakwate Mbivilia. Ĩndĩ ve andũ aĩkĩĩku meekĩie kĩthito nĩ kana Mbivilia ĩvikĩe andũ onthe. Ũmwe wa andũ asu aĩ John Wycliffe, ũla wekalaa England vakuvĩ myaka 600 mĩvĩtu. Aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana kĩla mũndũ nĩwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na Ndeto ya Ngai nĩ kana ĩmũtethye. Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu watwĩe, vakuvĩ andũ onthe ma England ala moonekaa mate asomu mayaĩ na Mbivilia. Nĩkĩ vailyĩ ũu? Kĩtumi kĩmwe nĩ kana andũ aingĩ mayaĩ mathooekya Mbivilia nũndũ kovi sya Mbivilia ĩvinda yĩu syaumĩĩaw'a na kw'oko, na kwoou kumya kovi ĩmwe kwaĩ ngalama nene mũno. Na eka ũu, andũ aingĩ mayeesĩ kũsoma. Ĩndĩ o na kau nĩmaendaa kanisanĩ makethukĩĩsya Mbivilia ĩisomwa, no laisi ũkethĩa mayakwatasya kĩla kĩũsomwa. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Mbivilia ĩla yatũmĩawa nĩ Ĩkanisa yaandĩkĩtwe na Kĩlatinĩ (Mbivilia ĩsu yeetawa Vulgate). Ĩndĩ myakanĩ ĩsu kĩthyomo kya Kĩlatinĩ kĩyeesĩkĩe nĩ andũ aingĩ ala moonekaa mate asomu. Kwoou nũndũ wa thĩna ũsu waĩ vo, andũ mesaa kũtetheka nĩ Mbivilia ata?—Nth. 2:1-5.
11. Ĩla Mbivilia yeetawa Wycliffe Bible yatethisye ata?
11 Mwakanĩ wa 1382, Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ ĩla yesie kwĩtwa Wycliffe Bible nĩyaumĩthiw'e. O na vatavĩtĩte ĩvinda ĩasa, aatĩĩi ma Wycliffe meetawa Lollards nĩmamyendie. Ĩvinda yĩu aatĩĩi asu ma Wycliffe nĩmendie andũ ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ makwate mwanya wa kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai na ĩilika ngoonĩ syoo. Kwoou maendaa na maaũ ũtũi ũmwe kũthi ũla ũngĩ nthĩ ya England maitavany'a. Mavinda maingĩ aatĩĩi asu ma Wycliffe masomeaa andũ ilungu Mbivilianĩ ĩsu na maimatiĩa ilungu imwe syaumĩĩw'e na kw'oko mesomee. Kĩthito kĩu kyoo kyavĩndũie maũndũ vyũ nũndũ nĩkyatumie andũ mambĩĩa kwendeew'a ĩngĩ nĩ Ndeto ya Ngai.
12. Atongoi ma ndĩni moosie ĩtambya yĩva nũndũ wa Wycliffe na kĩthito kyake?
12 Atongoi ma ndĩni meekie ata moona ũu? Mamenanĩisye Wycliffe na Mbivilia yake, vamwe na aatĩĩi make. O na nĩmambĩĩe kũthĩny'a aatĩĩi ma Wycliffe na mamantha kovi syonthe sya Wycliffe Bible ila maĩ makwata na masyananga vyũ. O na Wycliffe akw'a mayaamũeka. Mamũtangaasie ta nthũ ya Ĩkanisa. Nĩtwĩsĩ vayaĩ vatonyeka kwosea mũndũ mũkw'ũ ĩtambya. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmavangĩthisye andũ menza mavĩndĩ ma Wycliffe kavulĩnĩ, mamavĩvya, na ũ mũu wekw'a ũsĩnĩ wĩtawa Swift. O na kũtw'ĩka Ĩkanisa nĩyatethisye maũndũ asu onthe, yĩyaĩ yĩtonya kũsiĩĩa Ndeto ya Ngai ndĩkavikĩe andũ ala mendaa kũmĩsoma na kũmĩelewa. Myakanĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe, andũ aingĩ Europe na kũndũ kũngĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmaambĩĩe kũalyũla Mbivilia na kũmĩnyaĩĩkya nĩ kana ĩvikĩe andũ aingĩ.
"ŨLA ŨKŨMANYĨASYA KWAĨLA"
13. Nĩ kyaũ twĩsĩ nesa vyũ, na kĩlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ ata?
13 Aklĩsto ũmũnthĩ mayaĩle kũsũanĩa kana Ngai nĩwaveveee wĩa wa kũalyũla Septuagint, Wycliffe Bible, na King James Version, kana o Mbivilia ĩngĩ yĩthĩwa yaalyũlwa. Ĩndĩ twasisya nesa maũndũ asu makonetye kũalyũlwa kwa Mbivilia isu na ingĩ mbingĩ syaumĩthiw'e, nĩtwonaa kana ũndũ ũũ nĩ wa w'o: Ndeto ya Yeova ndyaathingithĩka o tondũ wathanie. Ũndũ ũsu tyo wĩkĩaa mũĩkĩĩo waku vinya na ũkaũtetheesya kwona nesa vyũ kana mawatho onthe ma Yeova makeanĩa?—Yos. 23:14.
14. Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũtetheeasya ata tũmwende mũnango?
14 Nĩtwoona kana kwĩmanyĩsya ũndũ Mbivilia yĩkalĩte myaka ĩsu yonthe ĩteũthingithĩka nĩkũlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ. Ĩndĩ o vamwe na ũu, nĩkũtũtetheeasya kũmwenda Yeova mũnango. * Na nengĩ we wĩona nĩkĩ Ngai watũnengie Ndeto yake? Na wĩona nĩkĩ watũĩkĩĩthisye kana ĩkekala tene na tene? Kĩtumi nũndũ nũtwendete na endaa kũtũmanyĩsya ũndũ tũtonya kwaĩla. (Soma Isaia 48:17, 18.) Kwoou o na tũte kũtavw'a, nĩtwĩsĩ kana nũseo kũmwenda Yeova o ũndũ ũtwendete na kũkwata mĩao yake.—1 Yoa. 4:19; 5:3.
15. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
15 Nũndũ nĩtwendete Ndeto ya Ngai mũno, twaĩle kũtata ũndũ tũtonya tũtetheke nĩyo. Ĩndĩ tũtonya kwĩka ata tũtetheke vyũ ĩla tũũsoma Mbivilia? Tũtonya kũtetheesya ata ala tũũkomana namo ũtavany'a mone ũndũ Mbivilia ne ya vata? Ala mamanyĩasya kĩkundinĩ maĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana maĩkĩĩthye kyonthe kĩla meũmanyĩsya kyumĩte Maandĩkonĩ? Twĩsũngĩa makũlyo asu ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe.

^ kal. 5 Ndeto imwe itũmĩawa kĩthyomonĩ kya Kĩsũngũ ũmũnthĩ syaumie Mbivilianĩ ĩsu ya King James Version. Ndeto imwe ta isu nĩ ta 'kũvalũka na ũthyũ,' na 'kũtulũla ngoo.'—Mot. 22:31; Sav. 62:8.

translation:
"The Word is living, and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword."—ISA. 40:8.
FOOTNOTES: 43, 48
1, 2. (a) What are some reasons why we may find it difficult to meditate on the Bible? (b) What can help us to appreciate God's Word?
DO YOU ever struggle to concentrate when reading the Bible? Perhaps your mind wanders, or you feel overwhelmed by the amount of material. Or do you find it hard to relate what you read to your life, or to see how it applies to you personally? If so, you are not alone. Many sincere Christians find it a challenge to meditate on God's Word. But Jehovah wants us to benefit from his Word, so he has helped us in various ways.
2 Today we will discuss some practical suggestions. By applying them, we can strengthen our desire to learn about Jehovah and his purposes, as expressed in the Bible. And we can make sure that God's Word remains alive and meaningful to us. The apostle Peter quoted Isaiah 40:8 to emphasize this point. He was reminding fellow believers that God's word would never become ineffective. (Read 1 Peter 1:24, 25.) In effect, Peter was saying that the Bible has the power to move us to action. Over the years, many people have found that regular meditation on the Scriptures helps them to grow spiritually and to stay close to Jehovah. This is because "the inspired utterance" guides us to an accurate knowledge of God's will.—1 Tim. 2:3, 4.
3. What will we examine now? (See paragraph 18.)
3 We will now consider how to make our personal study more effective so that God's Word will continue to be a source of strength and encouragement to us (1) when we feel discouraged, (2) when we face difficult questions that could weaken our faith if left unanswered, and (3) when we want to help others appreciate the Bible. Why is it important to address these points? Because they will help us to love God's Word even more. Moreover, addressing these points will motivate us to imitate the Bible writers, who valued it highly.—Micah 4:2; Acts 15:4.
QUESTIONS FOR REVIEW
4. (a) How does the Bible benefit us? (b) Why does God allow suffering, and why is it important to understand this?
4 The Bible is truly beneficial. However, sometimes one scripture may seem to contradict another. It is therefore vital to harmonize scriptures. This is what scholars did when translating the Greek Scriptures. Many scriptures were used to write most of the books in the Bible. In fact, people who know Greek and Hebrew often use scriptures that have already been harmonized to help those who are studying the Bible. So, whenever anyone wants to understand God's Word properly, he should read it carefully and ask for an explanation if necessary, and he should compare the Greek and Hebrew texts whenever possible. Some people find it helpful to consult commentaries on the Greek and Hebrew languages to better understand the meaning of the scriptures. Let us see how we can make our study more effective. * Did you know that the entire Bible or portions of it have been translated into over 3,000 languages? This demonstrates Jehovah's desire to reach people with "good news of his kingdom" in their own language. (Read Proverbs 14:6.) What do you think? Does this not show how much God loves us and cares about us?—Matthew 10:34.
5 Was the King James Version accurate?
5 We will see whether the translations are consistent. Some translations are used but were not based on the oldest Bible manuscripts available. Because of this, the Bible may not be completely reliable when it comes to accurately conveying God's message, and it may have become corrupted over time. The Bible was originally written in Hebrew. Our Bible is the King James Version, and it was completed in 1611. It is one of the Bibles that was not based on the Hebrew manuscripts and it interprets the Hebrew texts differently than others, and some people say that this translation is inaccurate and we should use another Bible instead. * And our King James Version Bible uses the name of God and shows respect for Him. It uses the name "Jehovah" often in the Greek Scriptures, and it uses the title "ALMIGHTY" written in capital letters often in the scriptures to show reverence for the name of God. This Bible, like the King James Version, does not always use the title "ALMIGHTY" written in capital letters in the Christian Greek Scriptures. For this reason, the King James Version is considered to be more accurate when it comes to conveying God's message in the scriptures than many other versions in Christendom.
6 Why should we stick to the New World Translation Bible?
6 In recent times, the Hebrew manuscripts that were used by the King James Version have been found to be unreliable. And now they are being corrected and updated by newer translations. But how can you know whether the changes made are correct or whether the Bible translated from the modern Hebrew texts is more accurate than older translations? This Bible has been translated both fully and partially with over 150 translations, and many people find it helpful. However, using an accurate translation helps a person understand God's Word better. (Ps. 119:97) One thing that makes the New World Translation stand out is that it uses the name of God where it is accurate according to the scriptures.
THE NAME OF GOD IS IMPORTANT
7, 8. (a) Why did many Christians in the second century AD feel it necessary to explain the Greek Scriptures? (b) What is the significance of the Septuagint?
7 Many scholars believe that it is important to use reliable sources when studying so that the message remains consistent and does not become distorted. Does God care whether his people continue to grasp his purpose through accurate translations? Of course! It is vital that we strive to maintain our understanding. The 39 books of the Old Testament were originally written in Hebrew, to the Israelites. These are sometimes called "inspired writings." (Acts 3:1, 2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Until the second century AD, many Greeks understood Hebrew. Why? Because the Greek translation of the Hebrew Scriptures, known as the Septuagint, was widely circulated and became very popular. (Neh. 8:5-7, 20, 21) Also, the Greek language was common, but the Hebrew Scriptures were read to the Greeks by those who knew Hebrew. So, many Greeks had access to the meaning of the scriptures. Over time, however, many Greeks found it difficult to understand the Greek Scriptures, and the need for explanation arose. Is this surprising?
8 During the 2nd and 1st centuries AD, five more books of the Old Testament were written in Greek and then translated into Kikamba. Other portions of the Greek Scriptures began to be translated during the 100 years following Christ's death. These Greek translations came to be known as the Septuagint. This was the first major translation of the entire Hebrew Scriptures.
9. (a) What is the Septuagint, and why did its translators make an effort to accurately translate the Hebrew Scriptures? (b) What benefit did the Greek translation provide to sincere individuals?
9 The Septuagint helped many people who spoke Greek to read the Greek Scriptures instead of the Hebrew ones. Consider how beneficial it is to be able to read God's Word in your own language! Over time, other versions of the Bible were also translated into various languages, such as Latin, Syriac, and Gothic, so that more people could understand them. (Read Psalm 119:162-165.) Indeed, God's Word has proved to be powerful and can accomplish its purpose regardless of the language used.
REASONS FOR TRANSLATING THE BIBLE ARE MANY
10. Why did many people embrace the Bible after John Wycliffe's efforts?
10 Some courageous men risked their lives to make the Bible available to others. They believed that everyone should have access to the Bible. One of those men was John Wycliffe, who lived in England about 600 years ago. He had a strong conviction that everyone should be able to learn from God's Word for himself. Because of his work, many people in England began to read the Bible. But why was this important? Previously, most Bibles were handwritten, making them expensive and difficult to obtain. Also, many people could not read. So, he and others worked hard to get the Bible translated and made available for reading. Why? Because the Bible was originally written in languages that most people did not know—Hebrew and Greek. However, a Latin version of the Bible (called the Vulgate) was commonly used by the church. But over time, even the Latin version became inaccessible to many. Did people really want to understand the Bible?—Ps. 2:1-5.
11. Was the Bible called the Wycliffe Bible accurate?
11 In 1382, an English Bible that came to be known as the Wycliffe Bible was completed. Those in authority opposed it, and followers of Wycliffe were labeled Lollards and persecuted. The opponents of Wycliffe feared that it would allow the lower classes to read God's Word and challenge the established order. This led to widespread opposition throughout England. Many copies of the Wycliffe Bible were burned, and anyone caught possessing one faced severe penalties. Yet, this effort helped spread the truth and lead more people to God's Word.
12. What principles motivated Wycliffe and his efforts?
12 What motives did these individuals have? Examine Wycliffe and his Bible, along with his followers. They wanted to oppose the teachings of Wycliffe and destroy all copies of the Wycliffe Bible, but they failed to stop its influence. Wycliffe also faced much opposition. He challenged the authority of the Church. It was dangerous to speak out against the Church. Despite this, these individuals promoted Wycliffe's ideas among the people through sermons, writings, and a man named Swift. And because the Church had forbidden so much, it caused people to desire to read and understand God's Word. Over time, many people in Europe and beyond began to demand access to the Bible and to interpret it themselves.
"THE IMPORTANCE OF UNDERSTANDING"
13. Why is understanding important, and how can we improve our comprehension?
13 Christians may wonder whether God approves of translations such as the Septuagint, the Wycliffe Bible, and the King James Version, or other Bibles that have been translated. We should be concerned about whether the translations accurately reflect the original manuscripts. Is it possible that Jehovah's purpose is being thwarted because of inaccurate translations?—Josh. 23:14.
14. Does God's Word still guide us today?
14 We can see that studying the Bible throughout the years has helped us to improve our comprehension. But more than that, it helps us to draw close to Jehovah. * How do you feel about God giving us his Word? And do you believe he wants us to continue learning from it forever? This is why we need to keep seeking knowledge and striving to understand what we learn. (Read Isaiah 48:17, 18.) Furthermore, if we want to remain faithful, we must continue to draw close to Jehovah and accept his direction.—1 John 4:19; 5:3.
15. What can help us to study effectively?
15 As we strive to live by God's Word, we need to ensure that we truly understand what we learn. Can we really understand something if we only read the Bible once? Can we fully grasp its meaning without meditating on it repeatedly? It is important to be humble enough to admit when we do not fully comprehend something in the Scriptures. Let us consider some practical suggestions for effective study.

text:
"Ngaseũvya vandũ va maũũ makwa vethĩwe va ndaĩa."—ISA. 60:13.
MBATHI: 28, 136
1, 2. Ndeto ii, "Kavĩla kakwa [ka] nyaĩĩ," itũmĩĩtwe ata Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania?
YEOVA NGAI awetie nesa asya atĩĩ: "Ĩtu nĩ kĩvĩla kyakwa kya ũsumbĩ, na nthĩ nĩ kavĩla kakwa [ka] nyaĩĩ." (Isa. 66:1) Asyokie asya ũũ ĩũlũ wa 'kavĩla kau kake ka nyaĩĩ': "Ngaseũvya vandũ va maũũ makwa vethĩwe va ndaĩa." (Isa. 60:13) Ekaa ũu ata? Na nũndũ ithyĩ twĩkalaa 'kavĩlanĩ kau kake ka nyaĩĩ,' kĩu kĩtũkonetye ata?
2 O na kau ndeto isu "kavĩla kakwa [ka] nyaĩĩ" iwetete ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, nisyokete ikatũmĩwa ĩngĩ Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o kwonany'a ĩkalũ ya tene yĩla yatũmĩawa nĩ Aisilaeli. (1 Mav. 28:2; Sav. 132:7) Nũndũ ĩkalũ yĩu yaĩ kũũ nthĩ, vai vangĩ athaithi ma w'o maĩ matonya kũkomanĩa nĩ kana mathaithe. Na nũndũ nĩvo athaithi ma w'o moombanĩaa mathaithe, ĩkalũ yĩu yaĩ kĩndũ kyanake vyũ methonĩ ma Yeova. Nĩkwĩthĩwa ĩkalũ yĩu yaĩ kũũ nthĩ, nĩyaseũvĩtye vandũ va Yeova va maaũ vakethĩwa va ndaĩa.
3. Ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva nĩ kyaũ, na mũvango ũsu wambĩĩe ĩndĩĩ?
3 Ũmũnthĩ vai ĩkalũ yakĩtwe vandũ vana ũkethĩwa no vo ve voka athaithi ma w'o matonya kũmbanĩa mathaithe. Ĩndĩ kwĩ ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva yĩla yĩkumasya Yeova mũno kũte ũndũ mwako o na wĩva ũtonya kũmũkumya. Ĩkalũ yĩu ya ngelekany'o nĩ kyaũ? Nĩ mũvango ũla ũtumaa andũ mew'anĩthw'a na Ngai. Mũvango ũsu wĩ vo nũndũ wa nthembo ĩla Yesũ Klĩsto waumisye vamwe na wĩa wake wa ũthembi. Mũvango ũsu wambĩĩe mwakanĩ wa 29, ĩla Yesũ wavatisiwe na etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩ kana atw'ĩke Mũthembi Mũnene wa ĩkalũ ya ngelekany'o ya Yeova, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva ya Yeova.—Aevl. 9:11, 12.
4, 5. (a) Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Savuli 99, athaithi ala ma w'o ma Yeova methĩawa na mea ma kwĩka ata? (b) Twaĩle kwĩkũlya ata?
4 Nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ wa mũvango ũla Yeova wĩkĩte wa ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva. Kwondũ wa ũu, nĩtũmũkathaa kwa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa ĩsyĩtwa yake na nĩtũmũtaĩaa nũndũ wa tei ũla watwonisye eeka mĩvango tũkwate wovosyo. Nĩ ũndũ wa kũtanĩthya mũno kũmanya kana Aklĩsto mbee wa milioni nyanya ũmũnthĩ nĩmamũtaĩaa Yeova na kĩthito! Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na andũ amwe ma ndĩni ala maĩkĩĩaa atĩ makataĩa Ngai mavika ĩtunĩ. Ngũsĩ syonthe nĩsyĩsĩ kana syaĩle kũmũtaĩa Ngai ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ syĩ vaa nthĩ.
5 Kwa kwĩka ũu twĩthĩawa tũiatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya athũkũmi aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova ala mawetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 99:1-3, 5. (Soma.) Ĩandĩko yĩu yonanĩtye kana Mose, Aluni, na Samueli nĩmakwete mbau vyũ mũvango wa ũthaithi wa w'o ũla waĩ kw'o ĩvinda yoo. (Sav. 99:6, 7) Ũmũnthĩ ana-a-asa ma Yesũ ala matiele kũũ nthĩ matanamba kũthi kũthũkũma ta athembi ĩtunĩ vamwe na Yesũ, mamũthũkũmaa Ngai me aĩkĩĩku, me kĩwanzanĩ kĩla kĩ nza wa ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva. Methĩawa makwetwe mbau nĩ milioni mbingĩ sya "malondu angĩ." (Yoa. 10:16) O na kau ikundi isu syelĩ ii na wĩkwatyo ũvw'anene, syonthe imũthaithaa Yeova syĩ ngwatanĩo. Ĩndĩ kĩla ũmwe witũ aĩle kwĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Nyie nĩnĩkwataa mbau nesa vyũ mũvango ũla Yeova wĩkĩte wa ũthaithi wa w'o?'
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KŨMANYA ALA MATHAITHĨAA ĨKALŨNĨ YA KĨ-VEVA
6, 7. Nĩ thĩna wĩva walikile kĩkundinĩ kya mbee kya Kĩklĩsto, na nĩ kyaũ kyeekĩkie ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ mũno?
6 Myaka 100 ĩte mĩthelu kuma kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kyambĩĩw'a, andũ nĩmambĩĩe kũkaĩa ũla mũĩkĩĩo o tondũ kwathanĩtwe. (Meko 20:28-30; 2 Ath. 2:3, 4) Kuma ĩvinda yĩu kwaĩ vinya mũno kũmanya mo naaũ ala mathaithĩaa Ngai ĩkalũnĩ yake ya kĩ-veva. Ĩtina wa myaka maana maingĩ ĩvinda ya Yeova nĩyavikie ya kũtetheesya andũ maelewe nesa naaũ mamũthaithaa ũndũ vaĩle. Eekie ũu aitũmĩa Mũsumbĩ ũla waĩ anekalĩla kĩvĩla, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto.
7 Kũvikĩĩa mwaka wa 1919, ala meetĩkĩlĩtwe nĩ Yeova, namo nĩ ala mamũthũkũmĩaa ĩkalũnĩ yake ya kĩ-veva, nĩmamanyĩkie nesa. Kũvikĩĩa vau nĩmeekĩte moalyũku ũthaithinĩ woo nĩ kana Ngai awĩtĩkĩle nesa vyũ. (Isa. 4:2, 3; Mal. 3:1-4) Na kwa nzĩa ĩsu, ũla woni mũtũmwa Vaulo woonete myaka mingĩ mũno mĩvĩtu nĩwambĩĩe kwĩanĩa o vanini.
8, 9. Elesya maũndũ atatũ makonetye 'ũseo' ũla Vaulo woonie woninĩ.
8 Woni ũsu wa Vaulo wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya 2 Akolintho 12:1-4. (Soma.) Woni ũsu Vaulo wooniw'e nĩ Yeova weetiwe ũvuany'o. Kĩla Vaulo wooniw'e kĩyesaa kwĩanĩa ĩvinda yake, ĩndĩ kyaĩ kĩanĩe ĩvinda yĩngĩ yaĩ mbee. Kwoou-ĩ, we Vaulo oonie 'ũseo' wĩva ĩla 'wambatiw'e kũvika ĩtu ya katatũ'? Ũseo ũsu Vaulo woonie ũkeanĩa ĩvinda yĩmwe kwa nzĩa itatũ. Nzĩa ya mbee no yĩthĩwe ĩkonetye nthĩ nzaũ. (Luka 23:43) Nzĩa ya kelĩ no yĩthĩwe ĩkonetye mũuo ũla andũ ma Yeova makatanĩa nesa vyũ me nthĩ nzaũ. Na nzĩa ya katatũ no yĩthĩwe ĩkonetye ũseo ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ nũndũ nĩkw'o Yeova ũĩ. Kũu nĩkw'o kwĩtĩtwe 'mũũnda wa Ngai.'—Ũvu. 2:7.
9 Nĩkĩ ĩndĩ Vaulo waisye kana 'eewie ndeto ila itaweteka, na ila itaĩle mũndũ kwineena'? Aisye ũu nũndũ ĩvinda yĩyaĩ ĩviku ya kũelesya mũno maũndũ ma ũsengy'o ala woonete woninĩ ũsu. Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ nĩ ũndũ waĩlĩte kũneena ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala andũ ma Ngai me namo!
10. Nĩkĩ mũuo wa andũ ma Yeova tiw'o yĩla ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva?
10 Mavinda maingĩ nĩtũkothaa kũweta ĩũlũ wa mũuo wa andũ ma Yeova. Ĩla twaweta ĩũlũ wa mũuo wa andũ ma Yeova yĩthĩawa ne nzĩa ya kwasya kana ithyĩ nithyĩ twĩ na ũthwii mwingĩ mũno wa kĩ-veva kwĩ andũ angĩ o na meva, na ũthwii ũsu nĩw'o ũtumaa twĩthĩwa na mũuo vamwe na Ngai na ana-a-asa maitũ. Ĩndĩ mũuo wa andũ ma Yeova tiw'o yĩla ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva. Ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva nĩ mũvango wa ũthaithi wa w'o ũla Ngai ũseũvĩsye andũ make. Naw'o mũuo wa andũ ma Yeova nĩw'o ũtumaa vamanyĩka naaũ Ngai wĩtĩkĩlĩte ũmũnthĩ mamũthũkũmae me yĩla ĩkalũnĩ yake ya kĩ-veva.—Mal. 3:18.
11. Nĩ ndaĩa yĩva tũnengetwe ũmũnthĩ ĩla ĩkonanĩtye na mũuo ũla Yeova ũnengete andũ make?
11 Nĩtũtanaa mũno twamanya kana kuma mwaka wa 1919, Yeova nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩte andũ make, o na kau me na naĩ, matethye wĩa vamwe nake. Wĩa ũsu nĩ kwĩka maũndũ matonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũuo ũla Yeova ũnengete andũ make. We nũtethasya a vaku wĩanĩ ũsu ũseũvĩte ũu? We nũkwĩw'a weekĩwa vinya ũendeee kũthũkũma vamwe na Yeova wĩanĩ ũũ wa kũseũvya 'vandũ va maaũ make' vethĩwe va ndaĩa?
ŨNDŨ YEOVA ŨENDEEE KWANAKAVYA KĨKUNDI KYAKE
12. Twĩsĩ ata kana ĩandĩko ya Isaia 60:17 nĩyĩanĩĩte? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 7.)
12 Ĩandĩko ya Isaia 60:17 (soma) nĩyathanie ĩũlũ wa moalyũku maseo mũno ala makonetye kĩkundi kya andũ ma Yeova. Ala ma mũika mũnini kana ala manemanyĩisye ũw'o mĩtũkĩ nĩmasomete kana o makatavw'a nĩ angĩ maũndũ ala maĩkĩĩthasya kana moalyũku asu mawetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu nĩmeanĩĩte. Ĩndĩ ve ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa mew'aa mũyo mwingĩ nũndũ nĩmeyoneete moalyũku asu mayĩkwa. Kwoou ti ũsengy'o kwona ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asu mate na nzika kana Yeova nũtongoesye andũ make aitũmĩa Mũsumbĩ ũla yu ũsumbĩkĩte! Nĩmesĩ nesa kana kĩu maĩkĩĩaa nĩ kya w'o, na o naitũ ithyonthe twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo o ta ũsu. Woosa ĩvinda wĩthukĩĩsye Aklĩsto asu mayĩyĩelesya kuma ngoonĩ ũkaaka mũĩkĩĩo waku mũno, na ũkatetheew'a ũmwĩkwatasye Yeova mũnango.
13. Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 48:12-14 yĩtũnengete wĩa wĩva?
13 Ĩndĩ o na twĩthĩwe twamanyie ũw'o ĩndĩĩ, no nginya tũtavye ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa athaithi ma Yeova. Nĩ kyama kĩnene mũno kwona mũuo ũla andũ ma Ngai me naw'o, o na kau matwĩe nthĩ nthũku yĩ na andũ athe na matendene! Nũndũ wa ũu no nginya tũtavye 'nzyawa ĩla yũkĩte' ĩũlũ wa mũuo ũla Yeova ũnengete athaithi make, vamwe na maũndũ ma ũsengy'a ĩũlũ "Saioni," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ĩũlũ wa athũkũmi ma Yeova ala me ĩtunĩ na ala me kũũ nthĩ.—Soma Savuli 48:12-14.
14, 15. Nĩ moalyũku meva meekiwe myakanĩ ya 1970? Moalyũku asu matethetye andũ ma Yeova ata?
14 Kwa myaka mingĩ, ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala akũangũ nĩmeyoneete moalyũku amwe ala matumĩte kĩkundi kya andũ ma Yeova kĩendeea kwanakava. Nĩmalilikanaa ĩla ikundi syeethĩawa na mũsyaĩĩsya ũmwe wa kĩkundi vandũ va nzama ya atumĩa. O na nĩmalilikanaa ĩla nthĩ syaũngamĩawa nĩ mũsyaĩĩsya ũmwe wa ovisi wa ũvonge vandũ va Kamitii ya Ovisi wa Ũvonge. Na ĩndĩ no malilikanaa ĩvinda yĩla motwi meekawa nĩ mũnene wa Watch Tower Society vandũ va kwĩkwa nĩ Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ana-a-asa asu meethĩawa meyumĩtye mũno na maĩ na atetheesya aĩkĩĩku. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, weethĩaa no mwana-a-asa ũla ũmwe ũtongoesye ũkwĩsa kwĩka ũtwi, ethĩwe nĩ ũla ũtongoesye kĩkundinĩ, ovisinĩ wa ũvonge, kana ethĩwe nĩ ũla wĩ ovisinĩ ũla mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩndĩ myakanĩ ya 1970 maũndũ nĩmavĩndũkie na kwatw'ĩka kana atumĩa meana ũna nĩmo makaũngamĩaa maũndũ, na ti mũndũ ũmwe.
15 Moalyũku asu nĩmatethetye? Ĩĩ, na ve kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwasya ũu. Nĩ kĩtumi kĩva? Nũndũ moalyũku asu meekawa kwosana na ũndũ ũmanyi witũ wa Maandĩko waendeee kũkenũka. Kwoou vandũ va motwi kwĩkawa nĩ mũndũ ũmwe, yu mekawa nĩ atumĩa kauta, na nũndũ wa ũu andũ ma Yeova nĩmatethekete nũndũ wa nguma nzeo sya aũme onthe ala Yeova ũtũnengete ta "mĩthĩnzĩo."—Aev. 4:8; Nth. 24:6.
16, 17. Wendete moalyũku meva katĩ wa ala mela kwĩkwa, na nĩkĩ?
16 Kwasyoka ũsũanĩe moalyũku ala mela kwĩkwa. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ũndũ matukũ aa mavuku maitũ manakavĩtw'e, maũndũ ala yu makothaa kũandĩkwa mavukunĩ asu, na ũndũ o nasyo nzĩa ila tũtũmĩaa kũmanengane ivĩndũkĩte. Ĩla we ũũtavany'a, tyo ũtanaa mũno ĩla wanengane mavuku manake, matonya kũtethya andũ, na me na ũvoo ũũmendeesya? O na ĩla twatũmĩa syĩndũ ila sya matukũ aa kũnyaĩĩkya ũw'o, kwa ngelekany'o Kĩsese kitũ kya jw.org, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana twĩ na wendi ta ũla wa Yeova wa kũnenga andũ kĩla vandũ motao. Andũ aingĩ mũno maikwataa motao ta asu na mekũlasya matonya kũmaumya va.
17 Ũndũ ũngĩ tũtaĩle kũlwa nĩw'o nĩ ũalyũku ũla weekiwe nĩ kana tũkwate mwanya wa kwĩka Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ, kana wa kwongelanga ĩvinda yĩla tũtũmĩaa kwĩmanyĩsya ithyĩ ene. O na nĩtũtanĩaa mũno ala moalyũku makonetye maũmbano maitũ manene. Kĩla mwaka ĩtina wa ũmbano mũnene twaasya kana ũmbano ũsu nĩ mũseango kwĩ ũla ũnavĩtie! Na vate nzika nĩtũtanaa mũno nũndũ twĩ na sukulu mbingĩ na kĩsomo kĩla tũkwataa kũu nĩkyongelekete. Tũi na nzika kana Yeova nũathimĩte moalyũku asu onthe mekĩtwe. Nũendeee kwanakavĩĩsya kĩkundi kyake na kũlũlũmĩlya mũuo ũla tũtanĩaa kũvika ũmũnthĩ!
KĨLA WE ŨTONYA KWĨKA ŨLŨLŨMĨLYE MŨUO ŨLA TWĨ NAW'O
18, 19. Tũtonya ata kũlũlũmĩlya mũuo ũla tũnengetwe nĩ Ngai?
18 Nĩ ũndũ mũnene mũno kwĩthĩwa twĩtĩkĩlĩtw'e nĩ Yeova tũtetheesye kũlũlũmĩlya mũuo ũla ũnengete andũ make. Twĩkaa ũu ĩla twatavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ twĩ na kĩthito na twatw'ĩkĩthya andũ aingangĩ amanyĩw'a. Kĩla ĩvinda twatetheesya mũndũ eeyumya amũthũkũme Yeova, twĩthĩawa tũitetheesya andũ aingangĩ methĩwe na mũuo ũla Yeova ũnengete andũ make.—Isa. 26:15; 54:2.
19 O na ĩngĩ tũtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũuo ũla Yeova ũnengete andũ make kwa kũtata twĩthĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseango. Tweeka ũu tũkatumaa andũ ala angĩ menda kwĩthĩwa na mũuo ta ũsu twĩ naw'o. Mavinda maingĩ kĩla kĩtumaa andũ menda kwĩkwatany'a na andũ ma Ngai vamwe na ũ Ngai mwene na Klĩsto nĩ mwĩkalĩle witũ mũseo na ũuu ũla twĩ naw'o, ĩndĩ ti mũno ũmanyi wa Mbivilia ũla twĩthĩawa naw'o.
20. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 14:35, twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wendi wa kwĩka ata?
20 No nginya Yeova na Yesũ makethĩwa matanaa mũno ĩla moona mũuo ũla twĩ naw'o ũmũnthĩ! Ũtanu ũla twĩthĩawa naw'o ĩla tũũlũlũmĩlya mũuo ũsu no mũnini waelekanw'a na ũtanu ũla tũkakwata ĩla tũkethĩwa tũiseũvya nthĩ ĩno yĩkale ũndũ mũũnda wa Eteni wailyĩ. Kwoou kĩla ĩvinda nĩtwĩkalei tũlilikene ndeto ii syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Nthimo 14:35, ila syaĩtye: "Wonan'yo wa ũseo wa mũsumbĩ welekele mũthũkũmi ũla wĩkaa na ũĩ." Ekai ĩndĩ tũkekaa maũndũ na ũĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũendeee kwĩkĩa kĩthito tũlũlũmĩlye mũuo ũla Yeova ũtũnengete!

translation:
"Let them sanctify themselves, those who carry sacred objects."—ISA. 60:13.
BATHS: 28, 136
1, 2. How does the expression "sacred objects [of] beauty" apply even to the Christian Greek Scriptures?
JEHOVAH God kindly explains: "The temple is his sacred object, and he is an object [of] beauty." (Isa. 66:1) He uses the phrase "sacred objects of beauty" in this way: "Let them sanctify themselves, those who carry sacred objects."—(Isa. 60:13) What does this mean? And why should we be concerned about being "objects of beauty"?
2 But how does the expression "sacred objects [of] beauty" relate to what happened in the past, as reflected in the Greek Scriptures through the example of Israel? (1 Ki. 28:2; Ps. 132:7) In time, that tabernacle came to represent something more than just a tent. And because that tabernacle foreshadowed something better, that tabernacle became something pleasing in Jehovah's eyes. It was honored, and it sanctified those carrying its sacred objects.
3. What is involved in sanctifying something, and what does this principle teach us?
3 In ancient times, the sanctification of the tabernacle helped people to appreciate how important it was to approach God acceptably. What did that sanctification signify? It was a way to make peace with God. This principle illustrates the importance of Jesus Christ's sacrifice on behalf of his faithful followers. This principle is explained in paragraph 29, where Jesus was presented and anointed with holy oil to become the High Priest of Jehovah's sanctified tabernacle—or, in effect, Jehovah's heavenly tabernacle.—Acts 9:11, 12.
4, 5. (a) Based on Psalm 99, what qualities in Jehovah's servants move him to act in their behalf? (b) What can we learn from this?
4 We are moved by the principle that Jehovah applies in connection with the sanctified tabernacle. Because of this, we are motivated to uphold the dignity of his name and to show appreciation for the means he has provided for our salvation. It is vital to remember whether millions of Christians truly honor Jehovah with devotion! Jehovah's standards are uncompromising toward those who claim to worship God hypocritically. All such individuals will eventually find out that they were mistaken.
5 To illustrate this, let us examine the example of faithful men of old, as recorded at 1 Samuel 99:1-3, 5. (Read.) That scripture shows that Moses, Aaron, and Samuel zealously upheld the law of their forefathers. (1 Sam. 99:6, 7) Today, true followers of Jesus Christ imitate them in being zealous to preach the good news along with Jesus, honoring God among mankind, and safeguarding the sanctity of the tabernacle. There are many millions of "other sheep." (John 10:16) And though each of us may have different assignments, all true worshippers of Jehovah are united. Let each one ask himself, 'Am I zealous to uphold the law that Jehovah applies in connection with their worship?'
IMPORTANT THINGS TO KNOW ABOUT THE TABERNACLE
6, 7. What questions does the Christian congregation face, and what will we discuss?
6 For over 100 years now, Christians have been shepherded by the elders, and they have given much attention to matters relating to sound doctrine. (Acts 20:28-30; 2 Thess. 2:3, 4) It is vital to understand why this is so important in maintaining our spiritual health. Over the past many years, Jehovah's organization has helped his people to discern sound doctrine. This work is accomplished primarily through Jesus Christ.
7 Since 1919, those approved by Jehovah, and thus those who honor his name, have shown increasing discernment. Because of this, they have demonstrated faith in God's ability to care for his worship. (Isaiah 4:2, 3; Malachi 3:1-4) And rightly so, for the apostle Paul foretold that there would be a time when some would go astray.
8, 9. What did the apostles do to counteract the "features" that Paul warned about?
8 Consider what Paul wrote at 2 Corinthians 12:1-4. (Read.) In this vision, Paul was taken up to Paradise by Jehovah. While there, Paul saw things that were beyond human comprehension. So, how did Paul view the "features" he saw – features that appeared "extraordinary"? These features Paul saw served to distract him from his primary ministry. Also, what Paul experienced reminded him of the importance of remaining humble. (Luke 23:43) What he saw also highlighted the privilege enjoyed by Jehovah's people of being closely united. And the third feature had to do with a revelation regarding Jehovah's purpose. To appreciate this, we need to understand what it means to be "God's minister." – Acts 2:7.
9 Did Paul realize that such visions could become "a thorn in the flesh, so that I might not become overly proud"? He understood that such experiences could easily distract him from giving full attention to the needs of the brothers. Truly, it is a blessing to be among those who zealously serve Jehovah!
10. Why is it important for Jehovah's servants to maintain spiritual health?
10 Many find it challenging to maintain spiritual health. But maintaining spiritual health is vital because it enables us to continue serving Jehovah despite difficulties and opposition, and it strengthens our bond with God and our fellow worshipers. Spiritual health is essential for enjoying life and appreciating the blessings that come from Jehovah's favor.—Mal. 3:18.
11. How can we benefit from meditating on what Jehovah has done for his people?
11 Beginning in 1919, Jehovah distinguished his people, and he continues to do so today, by means of his organization. This helps us to discern what truly constitutes spiritual health. So how does Jehovah's organization help us to show appreciation for his care? And why should we be willing to support it as we endeavor to identify "his precious people" and associate with them?—Isa. 60:17.
KEEP EXPANDING JEHOVAH'S ORGANIZATION
12. What will we discuss in this article? (See accompanying box, "Isaiah 60:17—What Does It Mean?")
12 Isaiah 60:17 (read) foretold a time when Jehovah's people would become numerous and beautiful. As they grow in numbers and spirituality, they need more overseers. But what if there is a shortage of qualified men who can serve as elders? Or what if some brothers feel inadequate to meet the needs of the congregation? The faithful slave has been giving attention to this matter, and arrangements have been made to provide assistance. Many zealous brothers have been invited to attend special courses. These courses will equip them to expand their ministry and assist congregations in need. However, remember that those attending such courses are not being appointed to positions of authority. Rather, they are being trained to support the existing elders and to work under their direction. Let us therefore continue to pray for Jehovah to bless the efforts of the faithful slave to train and send out capable men! I am sure that this is what we all desire, and we appreciate the effort that is being put forth. Consider how Christ sent out his disciples two by two to preach the good news and to strengthen fellow believers, and let us imitate his example in supporting Jehovah's organization.
13. What does Psalm 48:12-14 teach us?
13 Indeed, we have learned from experience that it is important to cooperate with God's arrangement for worship. It is a great privilege to be among those who know and love the name of the Most High God, and we should cherish this privilege and associate with others who are spiritual! Therefore, let us cooperate with the 'lawful king' in promoting the Kingdom interests, just as Jehovah directs his people to proclaim the message.—Read Psalm 48:12-14.
14, 15. What changes were made in the 1970's? Did these changes affect Jehovah's people?
14 For many years, brothers and sisters in various lands experienced a change in how congregations were organized. This involved appointing elders to serve as a congregation committee to shepherd the flock. And this also involved appointing circuit overseers to visit congregations. Also, there was an increase in the number of traveling overseers from the Watch Tower Society to assist branches in conducting evangelizing work. Brothers and sisters appreciated this increased attention and assistance. In connection with this, when a brother was appointed to serve as an elder, he was often interviewed by members of the congregation committee, by a circuit overseer, or by a representative from the branch office. During the 1970's things became more formalized and standardized, and it was not uncommon for several individuals to be interviewed.
15 Why did some elders feel apprehensive? Yes, because they felt inadequate for the responsibility. What caused this feeling? Often elders felt unqualified to explain our understanding of Bible prophecy clearly. They feared being alone when dealing with difficult questions, and so Jehovah strengthened them by means of "encouragement."—Acts 4:8; Matt. 24:6.
16, 17. How did traveling overseers help those who were newly appointed as elders, and why?
16 Traveling overseers took the initiative in helping newly appointed elders. For example, they discussed practical situations that elders commonly face, problems that may arise, and how to use the publications effectively. But more importantly, they showed genuine interest in the brothers and sisters, encouraging them and offering assistance. Also, by using tools like the website jw.org, we can strengthen ourselves and others in our faith, and we can be confident that we are teaching people accurate information about God's Kingdom. Many individuals have come to appreciate this effort and have been motivated to learn more.
17 One way we can support this work is by taking time to prepare for and attend meetings at the Kingdom Hall or by participating in the field ministry. Also, we should continue to support large gatherings and conventions. Every year, we look forward to the international convention, and often the local convention is a highlight of the year! And we are grateful for the spiritual food we receive from the school and the meetings we attend. We trust that Jehovah will continue to bless us abundantly. Let us remain united and zealous in proclaiming the good news!
ALWAYS BE WILLING TO SHARE THE GOOD NEWS
18, 19. Why should we always be willing to share the good news that we have received?
18 It is a privilege to tell others about Jehovah and his purpose for mankind. We want people to know the truth about God's Kingdom and to benefit from it. Whenever we help someone come to know Jehovah, we are helping them find life everlasting.—Isa. 26:15; 54:2.
19 Moreover, we should be eager to share the good news because we appreciate what Jehovah has done for us. We do not want others to miss out on the blessings that we enjoy. Many people are longing for genuine friendship and for a meaningful relationship with God and Christ. The Bible knowledge we share with them is a valuable gift.
20. As stated in Proverbs 14:35, what can happen if we are willing to share?
20 Yes, Jehovah and Jesus deeply value our willingness to share the good news! The joy we experience when we share the good news is similar to the joy experienced by Ethan the Ethiopian when he came to understand the scriptures. Every time we share, we give people an opportunity to associate with God's people and to learn about God himself and Christ. This is something they will greatly appreciate! Like the wise man mentioned in Proverbs 14:35, we can say: "The insight of a shrewd person is to discern direction." So let us continue to zealously share the good news that Jehovah provides!

NĨNGŨLILIKANA kwakya kũmwe twaĩ ngalĩko ya Brookings, kĩsionĩ kya South Dakota, Amelika. Kwakya ku kwaĩ kũthithu mũno na nzeve ĩla yaĩ kw'o yandilikanilye kana ĩvinda ya mbevo ĩla mbingĩ yĩ nzĩanĩ. Ũsengy'o nĩ kana kũthithĩte ũu kwathithĩte, mũthenya ũsu nĩ na andũ angĩ anini twaĩ vandũ kĩsũmbanĩ kya kwia syĩndũ sya mũũndanĩ na sya indo. Kĩsũmba kĩu kĩyaĩ na kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kya kũtũkwatya muutĩa. Na mbee witũ vaĩ katangi indo syanyw'ĩĩaa kĩw'ũ, kala keekĩĩtwe kĩw'ũ kĩthithu kakew'a kusũa. Kwaeka nambe kũũnenga ũvoo mũnini ĩũlũ wakwa nĩ kana ũelewe nĩkĩ twaĩ vau.
MŨSYĨ WITŨ
Nasyaiwe Matukũ 7, Mwei wa 3, 1936. Tũsyaĩtwe twĩ ana na ninyie ĩlumaita. Twekalaa ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa sua ya South Dakota, na twaĩ aĩmi na nĩtwaĩthasya indo. Nĩtwendete mũno kũĩma na kũĩthya indo ĩndĩ ũsu ti w'o ũndũ ũla twendete mũno vyũ. Asyai makwa mavatisiwe mwakanĩ wa 1934. Maivatiswa nĩmamwathie Asa witũ, Yeova, kana makamũthũkũmaa na ngoo yonthe, na kwoou ũndũ ũla waĩ wa vata mũno vyũ kwoo nĩ kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Ĩthe wakwa, Clarence, na ĩtina mwana-a-inyia, Alfred, nĩmesie kũtw'ĩka athũkũmi ma kĩkundi (ũmũnthĩ metawa avangĩthya ma nzama ya atumĩa) kĩkundinĩ kĩla twaĩ taoninĩ ya Conde, South Dakota.
Vai ĩvinda twaatĩĩa maũmbano ma Kĩklĩsto, na vai ĩvinda twaaĩkala tũteũthi nyũmba na nyũmba tũtavye angĩ ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo mũseo mũno ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Asyai maitũ nĩmatwiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo mũno na matũmanyĩsya nesa, na ũndũ ũsu nĩwatũtethisye mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, nyie nĩ na mwĩĩtu tũsyaanĩw'e wĩtawa Dorothy twatw'ĩkie atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ twĩ na myaka thanthatũ. Mwakanĩ wa 1943 nĩw'o Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi yambĩĩw'e, na mwaka o ũsu now'o nalikile sukulunĩ ĩsu.
Nĩtwendete mũno kũthi maũmbanonĩ manene. Nĩngũlilikana Mwana-a-asa Grant Suiter ayumya ũvoo ũmbanonĩ ũmwe mũnene, ũla weekiwe mwaka wa 1949 taoninĩ ya Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Ndyaaũlwa nĩ ũvoo ũla waumisye waĩ na kyongo, "Ĩvinda Nĩ Ĩendu kwĩ Ũndũ Ũũsũanĩa!" Akindĩlĩĩle kana Aklĩsto onthe avatise maĩlĩte kwĩyumya na ngoo yonthe matavany'e ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Ũvoo ũsu watumie nenda kwĩyumya nĩmũthũkũme Yeova. Ũmbano ũla waatĩĩe wa mũthyũlũlũko weekĩiwe Brookings na nĩvo navatisĩwe kĩla kĩsũmbanĩ kĩ mbevo nĩwetie. Ala twavatisiwe mũthenya ũsu wa Matukũ 12, Mwei wa 11, 1949, twaĩ ana, na twavatisĩwe kala katanginĩ ka ĩvati.
Ĩtina wa vau nĩnavangie kũtw'ĩka vainia. Noosie ũvainia Ĩtukũ 1, Mwei wa 1, 1952, nĩ na myaka 15. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Endaa na andũ oĩ, ũkeethĩwa mũĩ." No nasye ve andũ aingĩ mũno oĩ ma mũsyĩ witũ ala mangwatie kw'oko ũndũnĩ ũsu. (Nth. 13:20) Kwa ngelekany'o, vainia ũla natavanasya nake aĩ mwana-a-inyia wa Tata weetawa Julius, ũla ĩvinda yĩu waĩ na myaka 60. O na kau aĩ mũkũũ mũno kwĩ inyie, twatanĩie ũtavany'a mũno. Eeyoneete maũndũ maingĩ mũno, na kwoou ũĩ ũla nakwatie kwake waĩ mwingĩ. Twĩkalangĩte o nake mwĩĩtu-a-mwaitũ, Dorothy, nĩwoosie ũvainia.
ASYAĨĨSYA MA MŨTHYŨLŨLŨKO NĨMANDETHISYE MŨNO
Nĩ wa mũika asyai maitũ nĩmathokasya asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko na iveti syoo makomele kwitũ. Amwe ta asu maĩ Jesse na Lynn Cantwell na nĩmandethisye vanene. Kĩndũ kĩmwe kyatumie nosa ũvainia nĩ kũnthangaasya kũla manthangaaisye. Na wendo woo nĩwatumie nenda mũno kwĩka mũvango wa kwĩanĩsya maũndũ mana ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, mavinda amwe matw'a kũthyũlũlũka ikundi ila syĩ vakuvĩ na kwitũ nĩmangũlasya nĩthi ũtavany'a namo. O na ndiwetekya ũndũ kĩndũ kĩu kyanthangaaisye na kyambĩkĩa vinya!
O nake Mwana-a-asa Bud Miller, na mũka, Joan, nĩmesie kũtũthyũlũlũka. Maitũthyũlũlũka naĩ na myaka 18 na nĩneesĩ ndiema kwĩtwa ngathũkũme itanĩ. Kamitii ĩla yaandĩkĩthasya andũ itanĩ yaĩ ĩnavanga kana nĩnaĩle kũlika itanĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩneesĩ kana kwĩka ũu nĩ kũtũla mwĩao ũla Yesũ wanengie aatĩĩi make amea maikatate kwĩlikya siasanĩ. Na eka ũu, nyie nendaa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. (Yoa. 15:19) Kwoou nĩneekaĩlile kamitii ĩsu ĩndale ta nĩ mũtavany'a.
Ĩla Mwana-a-asa Miller wambĩie nũkũendany'a nakwa mbee wa kamitii ĩsu neewie nakiitwa ngoo mũno. Miller aĩ mũndũ mũneenu na ndatelemangaw'a oou nĩ maũndũ. Kũendany'a na mũndũ wa kĩ-veva ta ũsu kwanengie ũkũmbaũ mwingĩ mũno. Kamitii ĩsu nĩyatwĩthukĩĩisye, na nũndũ wa ũu thano wa mwaka wa 1954 ũithela nĩyandalile ta mũtavany'a. Nũndũ wa ũtwi ũsu naĩ nĩtonya kwĩanĩsya mũvango ũngĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu nĩw'o nakwatie valũa wa kũthũkũma Mbetheli. Neetiwe nĩthũkũmae vala tene veetawa Watchtower Farm, ngalĩko ya Staten Island, New York. Nekalile vau myaka ta ĩtatũ. Ĩndĩ nĩnatanĩie mũno kũvekala nũndũ nĩnathũkũmie na andũ angĩ aingĩ oĩ.
ŨTHŨKŨMI WA MBETHELI
Vau Watchtower Farm nĩvo vaĩ kĩla kĩsese kya letiũ kyeetawa WBBR. Kĩsese kĩu kyaĩ kya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kuma 1924 nginya 1957. Na ũtalo wa athũkũmi ma Mbetheli ala maĩ vau Watchtower Farm waĩ katĩ wa 15 na 20. Aingĩ maitũ twaĩ ma mũika na no ĩndĩ twaĩ tũnooka. Ĩndĩ ũseo twaĩ na mwana-a-asa ũmwe mũkũũ weetawa Eldon Woodworth. Eldon aĩ mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta na nũmwe wa ala oĩ mandethisye. Atwendete ta syana syake na ũtethyo wake nĩwalũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova. Ĩla Mwana-a-asa Woodworth wesa kwona tũiemanwa nũndũ wa mawonzu maitũ akothaa kwasya, "Nĩ ũndũ wa ũsengy'o mũno kwona maũndũ ala Mwĩaĩi wĩanĩĩtye na ala ũthũkũmaa namo."
O na nĩtwathũkũmie vau na Mwana-a-asa Frederick W. Franz, na ũsu waĩ ũndũ mũnene mũno kwitũ. Ũĩ wake na ũmanyi mwingĩ wa Maandĩko ũla waĩ naw'o nĩwatũtethisye mũno. Nake mwene nĩwendete kĩla ũmwe witũ. Na ĩndĩ vaĩ Harry Peterson. Mwana-a-asa ũsu nĩwe watũuĩaa na twendete kũmwĩta Peterson vandũ va kũmwĩta Papargyropoulos. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ yake mwene ĩndĩ tweew'aa kũyĩtamũka kwĩ vinya mũno. O nake aĩ mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta na aĩ kĩthito kingĩ mũno ũtavany'anĩ. O na kau Mwana-a-asa Peterson nĩweeyumĩtye vyũ eanĩsye wĩa wake Mbetheli, ndaavũthĩĩsya ũtavany'a. Avalũkasya makaseti mbee wa ĩana kĩla mwei. O na nĩtwamũkũlasya makũlyo maingĩ na akatũsũngĩa nũndũ ũmanyi ũla waĩ naw'o wa Maandĩko waĩ mwingĩ mũno.
EĨTU-A-ASA OĨ NĨMANDETHISYE
Vau Watchtower Farm nĩtwaseũvasya matunda na mbaa mboka nĩ kana tũsyĩkĩe ivavanĩ kwondũ wa athũkũmi onthe ma Mbetheli. Kĩla mwaka twaseũvasya matunda na mboka itoetye kwĩkĩwa ivavanĩ ta 45,000. Nĩnatanie mũno kũkwata mwanya wa kũthũkũma wĩa ũsu na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe mũĩ wĩtawa Etta Huth. Etta nĩwe waandĩkaa mũtalatala ũla ũkũatĩĩwa tũiseũvya matunda na mboka isu. Kĩla ĩvinda twesa kũtw'ĩka nĩtũũtethya wĩa ũsu, eĩtu-a-asa ala maĩ ikundinĩ ila syaĩ vau vakuvĩ nĩmookaa kũtetheesya, na Etta nĩwe wamonasya kĩla mekwĩka. O na kau Etta nĩweekwetw'e mũno wĩanĩ ũsu, nĩwatatie mũno atiĩe ala angĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ya kwĩnyivĩsya ana-a-asa ala maũngamĩe maũndũ vau twaĩ. Noonie naĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake ya kwĩnyivĩsya ala matongoesye maũndũ ũseũvyonĩ.
Ũmwe wa eĩtu-a-asa ala mookaa kũtetheesya aĩ Angela Romano. Angela nĩwatethetw'e mũno nĩ Etta amina kwĩmanyĩsya ũla w'o. Kwoou no nasye ĩvinda yĩu nathũkũmaa Mbetheli nĩnakomanie na Mũklĩsto ũngĩ mũĩ, ũla nĩthĩĩtwe ngĩendany'a nake kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 58. Natwaie Angie Mwei wa 4, 1958, na nĩtũtanĩĩte maũndũ maingĩ mũno ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai. Myakanĩ ĩsu yonthe Angie ekalĩte alũmanĩtye na Yeova, na kĩthito kĩu kyake nĩkĩtumĩte mũtwaano witũ wĩkala wĩ mũlũmu. Nĩthĩawa nĩmwĩkwetye vyũ o na twakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ũnenevete ata.
ŨTHŨKŨMĨ WA ŨMISONALĨ NA WĨA WA KŨTHYŨLŨLŨKA
Kĩsese kya WBBR kĩla kyaĩ Staten Island nĩkyesie kũthoow'a mwaka wa 1957. Ĩtina wa vau nathũkũmangie Mbetheli ya Brooklyn kwa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, na ĩvindanĩ yĩu nĩw'o natwaanie na Angie. Twatwaana nĩnaumie Mbetheli na twakũna ũvainia o vau Staten Island kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ta ĩtatũ. O na ve ĩvinda myakanĩ ĩsu naandĩkiwe nĩ ala mathooie kĩla kĩsese kitũ kya letiũ. Makĩthooa makĩvĩndũie ĩsyĩtwa makĩta WPOW.
Nĩ na Angie nĩtwavangie kana tũikeyũmbĩlĩĩla maũndũ maingĩ nĩ kana wĩthĩe nĩ laisi kũthi kw'onthe kũla tũtonya kwĩsa kũtũmwa. Nũndũ wa ũu, vayaĩ vinya kwitũ kwĩtĩkĩla kũthi ngalĩko ya Falls City, kĩsionĩ kya Nebraska, ta mavainia ma mwanya ĩla twakũlilw'e twĩke ũu mwambĩĩonĩ wa mwaka wa 1961. Twakililye twavika kũu twatũmiwe oou, twakwata valũa wa kũthi Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Ũsumbĩ. Sukulu ĩsu yeekĩiwe South Lansing, New York, kwa ĩvinda ya mwei ũmwe. Twatanĩie mũno kũmanyĩw'a na nĩtwendaa mũno kũtũmĩa kĩsomo kĩu twasyoka Nebraska. Kwoou twaseng'ie mũno sukulu yathela tũinengwa valũa wa kũtũmwa ta amisonalĩ nthĩ ya Cambodia! Nthĩ ĩsu mbanake yĩ ngalĩko ya Southeast Asia yaĩ na kũndũ kũseo mũno kwa kwĩloela, tũwasya tũseo, o na syĩndũ syĩ mĩnyungo mĩseo. Syonthe syaĩ syĩndũ tũtaĩ twaaona kana kwĩw'a. Kwoou twaĩ na mea maingĩ ma kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo mũseo kũu.
Ĩndĩ twĩkalangĩte kũu kwathokoanie weethĩa no tũthamĩĩaa South Vietnam. Myaka ĩlĩ ĩithela nĩnawaie mũno, na nũndũ wa ũu tweeiwe nĩ kavaa twambe kũsyoka mũsyĩ. Nĩnakuie ĩvinda ndikwata vinya, ĩndĩ nakwata vinya oou nĩtwalikile ĩngĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe.
Mwei wa 3, 1965, nĩnanengiwe wĩa wa kũthyũlũlũka na nĩtwatanĩaa kũtetheesya ikundi. Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 33, nĩtwatanĩie kũthũkũma vamwe nĩ mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko na mũsyaĩĩsya wa kĩvalo. O na myakanĩ ĩsu nĩtwatanĩie kũtetheesya kũvanga maũmbano manene na kũtethya mawĩa maũmbanonĩ asu. Kuma tene nĩnendete maũmbano manene na kwoou nĩneew'aa mũyo mũno nditethya wĩa wa kũmavanga. Nĩtwaminie myaka kauta twĩ kĩsionĩ kya New York City, na myakanĩ ĩsu ve maũmbano meana ũna manene meekĩiwe Yankee Stadium.
KŨSYOKA ĨNGĨ MBETHELI NA KŨKWATĨĨA SUKULU SYA KĨTHEOKULASI
O tondũ aingĩ ala me ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe meyoneete, myakanĩ ĩsu yonthe nĩtũkwatĩte ianda syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, imwe sya kũtanĩthya mũno na ingĩ syĩ vinya. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 1995 nĩnakũlilw'e nĩmanyĩasye Sukulu ya Kũmanyĩsya Maũndũ ma Ũthũkũmi (MTS). Myaka ĩtatũ ĩtina wa vau nĩtweetiwe Mbetheli. Natanie ta kĩ kũsyoka vala nambĩĩe ũthũkũmi wakwa wa ĩvinda yonthe myaka mbee wa 40 mĩvĩtu! Nathũkũmangie Mũvĩanĩ wa Ũthũkũmi na nĩnamanyĩisye sukulu siana ũna. Mwakanĩ wa 2007, Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye yatwie kana sukulu syonthe ila syĩkĩawa Mbetheli ikeethĩawa iũngamĩwe nĩ Mũvĩa wa Masukulu ma Kĩtheokulasi. Ũsu nĩ mũvĩa mweũ waĩ ũnambĩĩw'a, na nĩnanengiwe kĩanda kya kwĩthĩwa mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũvĩa ũsu kwa ĩvinda ya myaka kauta.
Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ nĩtwonete moalyũku manene ala mekĩtwe mũno mũno maũndũnĩ ma sukulu. Kwa ngelekany'o, Sukulu ya Atumĩa ma Kĩkundi nĩyambĩĩw'e mwaka wa 2008. Myaka ĩlĩ kuma yambĩĩw'a, atumĩa mbee wa 12,000 nĩmamanyĩiw'e sukulunĩ ĩla yeekĩiwe Patterson na Mbetheli ya Brooklyn. Sukulu ĩsu nĩendeee kũndũ kwingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na yĩ na alimũ amanyĩsye nesa. Mwakanĩ wa 2010, Sukulu ya Kũmanyĩsya Maũndũ ma Ũthũkũmi (MTS) nĩyavĩndũiwe ĩsyĩtwa yeetwa Sukulu ya Mbivilia ya Ana-a-asa Matatwaanĩte, na mwakanĩ o ũsu Sukulu ya Mbivilia ya Aklĩsto Matwaanĩte nĩyambĩĩw'e.
Mwaka wa ũthũkũmi wa 2015 ũyambĩĩa, sukulu isu ilĩ syakwataniw'e syatw'ĩka Sukulu ya Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Vatw'ĩkĩkanie kana ala matonya kũthi sukulunĩ ĩsu no methĩwe mũndũ na mũka, ana-a-asa matatwaanĩte, kana eĩtu-a-asa mate atwae. Kĩla vandũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa matanie mũno ĩla meewie sukulu ĩsu ĩkeekawa movisinĩ maingĩ ma ũvonge. Nĩ ũtanu mwingĩ kwona aingĩ makwatĩte mwanya wa kũthi sukulu isu, na nĩnĩtanĩaa mũno kũkomana na aingĩ ala mekĩte moalyũku nĩ kana matonye kũthi sukulu isu.
Nalilikana myaka ĩla nĩkalĩte kuma o na ndanamba kũindwa kala katanginĩ kũvika yu, nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mwingĩ nũndũ wa andũ onthe oĩ ala mandetheetye nĩendeee kũkinyĩla nzĩanĩ ya ũla w'o. Amwe moo nĩtwavĩtũkanĩte myaka na angĩ tũyaumĩte kũndũ kũmwe. Ĩndĩ maĩ andũ mamwendete Yeova kuma ngoonĩ. Mawoni moo na maũndũ ala meekaa nĩmoonanasya ũtheinĩ kana nĩmamwendete Yeova. Vate nzika, ũseũvyonĩ wake twĩ na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ oĩ tũtonya kũendany'a namo. Nyie mwene nĩnĩkĩte ũu na ngakwata moathimo maingĩ.
