translation:
We met with colleagues from Brookings, a city in South Dakota, America. The place was very cold and the wind blew strongly, almost like a large herd of buffaloes. It seems like it's always been this way, and many people with us came from different places to discuss issues of peace and development. This meeting was good and had something to do with trying to help us. And our elders started talking about old things, remembering how things used to be done. Perhaps because we were looking for someone important, we thought we saw them.
OUR PEOPLE
Born on March 7, 1936. We grew up with you and remember you well. We lived near a small town in South Dakota, and we had a hard time making a living. We worked hard to survive and provide for ourselves, but it wasn't easy. They gave us land in 1934. It was given to us by our father, Jehovah, so that we could work hard and honor God. My brother, Clarence, and my younger brother, Alfred, helped me organize a group (many farmers who share information) to support each other in Conde, South Dakota.
We attended Christian meetings, and we went from house to house preaching the good news of the Bible. Our parents encouraged us to be zealous and diligent, and this helped us a lot. For example, you and I remember Dorothy, whom we knew from childhood for fifty years. In 1943, the Theocratic School was started, and that year I finished school.
We then attended large assemblies. I recall Brother Grant Suiter delivering a fine talk, which he gave in 1949 at the Sioux Falls, South Dakota, assembly. It was about his experience, and its title was, "It Pays to Investigate!" He explained how Christ himself took time to learn about God's Word. That talk motivated many to learn more about Jehovah. The assembly at Brookings was also memorable, and I always remembered the feeling I had during that convention. We were baptized on December 12, 1949, and we were given a certificate.
My parents appreciated our zeal. On January 1, 1952, I began pioneering at the age of 15. My territory included this advice: "Go among people, and let them make you known." And so I met many fine people, and my parents supported me in this service. (Prov. 13:20) For example, the person I associated with most during that time was a young man named Julius, whose father had been serving for 60 years. He was much older than me, but we enjoyed working together. I learned a lot from him, and I especially appreciated his encouragement. We also kept in close touch with our sister, Dorothy, who also began pioneering.
EXPERIENCES IN THE MINISTRY ARE VERY ENCOURAGING
It is very comforting to hear reports about experiences in the ministry and to see how Jehovah is blessing our efforts. Recently, Jesse and Lynn Cantwell shared an encouraging experience with me. One thing that helped me appreciate their report was remembering what they had told me earlier. With their permission, I would like to share this experience to encourage all of us to preach and to show confidence in God's power. For example, some publishers were discouraged when a group did not respond favorably, but they continued to call back and were able to start a study. They realized that sometimes things may seem discouraging, but we should not give up.
Also, my friend Bud Miller and his wife, Joan, have been helping me in the ministry. They are now in their teens and are eager to be full-time ministers. A recent article encouraged young people to get involved, and it made me wonder if I could do more. I realize that if I want to do more, it is by following Jesus' instruction to leave everything behind and become his disciple. And with that, you too can enjoy the peace of Paradise. (John 15:19) I am determined to continue doing everything I can.
But Brother Miller reminded me to spend time with my family and to remember them. Miller is a fine brother, and I value his advice. Spending time with experienced Christians will help you greatly. That article inspired us, and since 1954, we have been determined to continue. The importance of maintaining spiritual goals has impressed us.
This year I had the privilege of visiting Bethel. It was wonderful to visit the place known as Watchtower Farm, near Staten Island, New York. I spent several days there. I really enjoyed being with so many brothers and sisters.
BETHEL LIFE
At Watchtower Farm they had their own radio station called WBBR. This station broadcasted the Good News from 1924 to 1957. And during our time at Bethel, those at Watchtower Farm numbered between 15 and 20. Many of us were married, and some had children. We also had a kind brother named Eldon Woodworth. Eldon was known for his generosity, and he often helped others. He set an excellent example through his life and speech, strengthening our relationship with Jehovah. But Brother Woodworth wisely cautioned us about becoming overly concerned with material things, saying, "It is a very good thing to see what God has done and to be grateful for it."
And we appreciated being with Brother Frederick W. Franz, who was a great help to us. His knowledge of the Scriptures was extensive, and he explained matters clearly. He personally visited each of us. And then there was Harry Peterson. This brother was the one who introduced us to people whom we later came to know as Papargyropoulos. That is how he got his nickname among us. And he was known for his generosity and had a remarkable spirit of selflessness. Also, Brother Peterson would spend hours carefully reviewing the work of his Bethel family, offering helpful suggestions. He would listen to dozens of tapes each month. And we benefited greatly from his insightful comments and increased understanding of the Scriptures.
BROTHERS WHO WERE HELPFUL
At Watchtower Farm, we harvested fruits and vegetables, and sometimes we were able to supply the needs of all the Bethel homes. Each year we harvested enough fruits and vegetables to feed about 45,000 people. It was a privilege to work alongside him and another sister named Etta Huth. Etta was the one who kept records of our fruit and vegetable harvest. Every week we would submit reports to her, and the brothers and sisters were very cooperative, but some were hesitant to report, and Etta would make sure everything was accurate. Also, Etta was very kind and considerate, and she often encouraged us to be generous with what we had. She always remembered their kindness and thoughtfulness.
One of the sisters who helped with the reporting was Angela Romano. Angela worked closely with Etta to ensure accuracy. I remember when I first came to Bethel, I became acquainted with a brother, who has been serving faithfully for 58 years. I married Angie on April 4, 1958, and we have experienced many blessings in our ministry. Throughout those years, Angie remained loyal to Jehovah, and her faith strengthened our bond. We have faced many challenges, but we have always felt supported.
PERSONAL HISTORY AND A LIFE OF SERVICE
The WBBR radio station on Staten Island began broadcasting in 1957. Shortly thereafter, we moved from Bethel in Brooklyn to serve at that station, and that is where I met Angie. We enjoyed serving at Bethel and then at the station on Staten Island for about three years. Over the years, I have received many letters from various stations. These letters are now archived at WPOW.
Angie and I often wondered what more we could do, and whether we should request further assignments. In time, we were invited to serve in the circuit covering Falls City, Nebraska, for several months in 1961. We happily accepted and were assigned to attend the School for Kingdom Evangelizers. That school was held in South Lansing, New York, for one month. We greatly benefited from the training and looked forward to returning to Nebraska. However, upon completing the school, we were given an assignment to serve as missionaries in Cambodia! At that time, Southeast Asia was still relatively closed to preaching, so we were thrilled to be sent there, despite the dangers involved. We did not know what lay ahead. We had many opportunities to prove our faith during that time.
Meanwhile, we continued to think about serving in South Vietnam. Several years passed, and eventually we received permission to leave at any time. I remember feeling very happy, and I also felt happy when we completed our full ministry throughout that month.
On March 3, 1965, I was interviewed for the pioneer work, and we began to plan how to expand our ministry. For 33 years, we worked alongside dedicated pioneers and publishers. And over those years, we planned to expand our ministry to form large groups and to deliver talks to larger audiences. But then I organized large groups, and later I was appointed to give talks on organizing. We spent many years in New York City, and at times large gatherings were held at Yankee Stadium.
ANOTHER ASSIGNMENT AND ATTENDING THE SCHOOL FOR EVANGELIZERS
Over many months of full-time ministry, several years passed, and we attended various schools, some for improving our speaking ability and others for happiness. For example, in 1995, I graduated from the School for Ministerial Training (MTS). Three years later, I was assigned to Bethel. I am grateful to have had another assignment lasting almost 40 years of my life! I enjoyed being a circuit overseer and trained many schools. In 2007, Brother Ila Itongesye visited all the schools except Bethel, which was inspected by the Overseer of Schools for Evangelizers. Now he is an older brother, and I was invited to serve as a helper to this overseer for many years.
In recent years, we have seen large expansions in school facilities. For example, the School of Kingdom Preachers was built in 2008. Within a few years, over 12,000 publishers were trained in schools located near Patterson and Bethel in Brooklyn. This school continues to expand greatly, and many people are being trained there. In 2010, the School for Ministerial Training (MTS) was renamed the School of Biblical Instruction for Mature Christians, and in that year the School of Biblical Instruction for Christian Ministers was also established.
From the 2015 service year onward, this school has been reorganized and named the School of Evangelizers. Those who qualify include both married couples and mature Christian singles, or families. Every year, many mature Christians and families attend this school, receiving much spiritual food. It is very encouraging to see so many taking time off to attend this school, and it is a privilege to associate with so many who are willing to take time off to attend this school.
I remember those years when I served here and traveled from place to place, and I thank Jehovah for the great love he shows to his people and for continuing to bless the work. Sometimes we spend years together. Many people have come to know Jehovah through them. The lessons and things they teach help us to appreciate how much Jehovah loves us. So please, let us continue to support our brothers and sisters who are able to join them. You too can benefit greatly from this.

1, 2. Nĩ makũlyo meva andũ mekũlasya mavinda maingĩ?
SYANA nĩsyendete mũno kũkũlya makũlyo. No ũsielesye ũndũ mũna, ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ ikũlasya, 'Nĩkĩ?' Na ĩla watata kũisũngĩa, no iũkũlye ĩngĩ, 'Na nĩkĩ?'
2 Twĩthĩwe twĩ anini kana twĩ akũũ, ithyonthe nĩtwĩthĩawa na makũlyo. No twĩthĩwe na makũlyo ĩũlũ wa kĩla tũũya, kĩla tũkwĩkĩa, kana kĩla tũkũthooa. Kana no twĩthĩwe na makũlyo ma vata ĩũlũ wa thayũ na ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte. Ĩndĩ twaema kũkwata mosũngĩo maseo ma makũlyo asu, no tũeke kũmantha mosũngĩo.
3. Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana mayĩsa kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ma vata ala mekũlasya?
3 Yo Mbivilia nĩyĩthĩawa na mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ma vata ala twĩkũlasya? Andũ amwe no masũanĩe kana Mbivilia yĩ na mosũngĩo asu, ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa monaa yĩ vinya mũno kũeleeka. No masũanĩe kana no alimũ na atongoi ma ndĩni matonya kũsũngĩa makũlyo asu. Namo angĩ nĩmew'aa nthoni kũweta kana mayĩsĩ mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu. We wĩona ata?
4, 5. Nĩ makũlyo meva ma vata wĩkũlasya? Nĩkĩ waĩle kũendeea kũmantha mosũngĩo?
4 No wĩthĩwe wendaa kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ta: Nĩkĩ noombiwe? Nĩ kyaũ kĩkangwata nakw'a? Ngai ailyĩ ata? Yesũ, ũla waĩ Mwalimũ wĩ nguma, aisye atĩĩ: "Voyai, na mũkanengwa; manthai, na mũkoona; vingũsyai, na mũkavingũĩwa." (Mathayo 7:7) Ndũkaeke kũmantha mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala wĩkũlasya mũvaka ĩla ũkakwata mosũngĩo ma w'o.
5 Waendeea 'kũmantha' mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala wĩkũlasya, ũkamakwata Mbivilianĩ. (Nthimo 2:1-5) Mosũngĩo asu me laisi mũno kũeleeka. Maũndũ ala ũkwĩmanyĩsya makatuma wĩthĩwa wĩ mũtanu ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ, na ũyĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Ekai tũneenee ĩkũlyo yĩmwe yĩthĩnĩtye andũ aingĩ.
WE NGAI NŨTŨTHĨNĨKĨAA NA E TEI?
6. Nĩkĩ andũ amwe monaa kana Ngai ndathĩnĩkaa ĩla meũthĩna?
6 Andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana Ngai ndatũthĩnĩkĩaa. Monaa kethĩwa Ngai nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa, nthĩ yaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa yĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũndũ yĩilyĩ. Nthĩ yusĩe makaũ, kĩmena, na mathĩna maingĩ. Andũ nĩmawaa, nĩmathĩnaa na nĩmakusaa. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi andũ amwe mekũlasya-ĩ, 'Ethĩwa Ngai nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa, nĩkĩ ũtavetangaa mathĩna?'
7. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva atongoi ma ndĩni mamanyĩasya andũ kana Ngai nde tei? (b) Nĩkĩ tũte na nzika kana Ngai tiwe waĩle kũtũlwa mũtĩ nũndũ wa maũndũ mathũku ala mekĩkaa?
7 Mavinda amwe atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmatumaa andũ maĩkĩĩa Ngai nĩ mũthũku na nde tei. Ĩla kweekĩka ũndũ mũthũku, maasyaa nĩ kwenda kwa Ngai. Maasyaa Ngai nĩwe ũkwendaa ũndũ ũsu wĩkĩke. Na ĩla masya ũu, methĩawa maimũtũla Ngai mũtĩ. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai tiwe ũetae mothũku. Ĩandĩko ya Yakovo 1:13, yonanĩtye kana Ngai ndatataa mũndũ na maũndũ mathũku. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ o na wĩva atatwa ndakasye, Nĩngũtatwa nĩ Ngai; nũndũ Ngai ndatonya kũtatwa nĩ ũthũku, o nake mwene ndatataa mũndũ." Ndeto isu syĩonany'a kana o na kau Ngai ndasiĩaa maũndũ mathũku mayĩkĩka, tiwe ũtumaa mekĩka. (Soma Yovu 34:10-12.) Ekai twone ngelekany'o.
8, 9. Nĩkĩ ti ũndũ waĩle kũmũtũla Ngai mũtĩ nũndũ wa mathĩna ala matũkwataa? Nengane ngelekany'o.
8 Kwasũanĩa mwanake wa mũika wĩkalaa na asyai make. Ĩthe wake nũmwendete mũno na nũmũmanyĩĩtye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka motwi maseo. Ĩndĩ mwanake ũsu aileana na ĩthe wake na ayuma mũsyĩ. Ĩtina wa kuma mũsyĩ, ayambĩĩa kwĩka maũndũ mathũku na kwoou ailika thĩnanĩ. We no ũmũtũle mũtĩ ĩthe wa mwanake ũsu nũndũ ndaasiĩĩa mwanae ayuma mũsyĩ? Vate nzika ndwĩka ũu! (Luka 15:11-13) O ta ĩthe wa mwanake ũsu, Ngai ndaasiĩĩa andũ ĩla manyuvie kũleana nake na kwĩka maũndũ mathũku. Kwoou ĩla maũndũ mathũku meekĩka, tũlilikanae kana ti Ngai ũtumaa mekĩka. Ti ũndũ waĩle kũmũtũla Ngai mũtĩ.
9 Ngai e na kĩtumi kĩseo mũno kya kũeka maũndũ mathũku maendeee kwĩkĩka. Ũkeemanyĩsya kĩla Mbivilia yaĩtye ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu Kĩlungunĩ kya 11 kya ĩvuku yĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana Ngai nũtwendete na tiwe waĩle kũtũlwa mũtĩ nũndũ wa mathĩna ala matũkwataa. Na ũw'o nĩ kana no Ngai ũtonya kũmina mathĩna maitũ.—Isaia 33:2.
10. Nĩkĩ tũte na nzika kana Ngai akamina mathĩna onthe ala maetetwe nĩ andũ athũku?
10 Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana Ngai nĩ mũtheu. (Isaia 6:3) Maũndũ onthe ala wĩkaa nĩ matheu na nĩ maseo. Na kwoou no tũmwĩkwatye vyũ. Andũ mayĩilyĩ ũu nũndũ mavinda amwe nĩmekaa maũndũ mataĩle. O na atongoi ala methĩawa me aĩkĩĩku vyũ, mai na ũtonyi wa kũmina mathĩna onthe ala maetawe nĩ andũ athũku. Vai mũndũ wĩ vinya ta Ngai, na nũndũ e ũtonyi, akamina mathĩna onthe ala maetawe nĩ andũ athũku. Akavetanga ũthũku tene na tene.—Soma Savuli 37:9-11.
NGAI EW'AA ATA ĨLA ANDŨ MEŨTHĨNA?
11. Ngai ew'aa ata ĩla ũũthĩna?
11 Ngai ew'aa ata ĩla woona maũndũ ala maendeee ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na ĩla woona ũithĩna? Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Ngai "nũwendete sila wa katĩ." (Savuli 37:28) Kwoou nĩwosaa kwa ũito maũndũ ala malũngalu na ala mate malũngalu. Ndendaa andũ maithĩna. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai 'nĩweewie woo ngoonĩ yake' ĩla woonie nthĩ yusĩe ũthũku ĩvindanĩ ya tene. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 6:5, 6) Ngai ndaaĩsa kũalyũka. (Malaki 3:6) Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Ngai nũkũsũvĩaa.—Soma 1 Vetelo 5:7.
12, 13. (a) Nĩkĩ twendete ala angĩ na tũmathĩnĩkĩaa? Twĩw'aa ata twoona mathĩna ala me kw'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ? (b) Nĩkĩ tũtaĩle kwĩthĩwa na nzika kana Ngai akavetanga mathĩna onthe na ũsili ũte wa katĩ?
12 O na ĩngĩ Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana Ngai atũmbie na mũvw'ano wake. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 1:26) Ũu wĩonany'a kana Ngai atũmbie twĩ na ndaĩa nzeo ta syake. Kwoou ethĩwa we nĩ ũũmĩaa ĩla woona andũ maithĩna, Ngai nĩwe wĩw'aa aũmĩĩte mũnango ĩla andũ meũthĩna! Twĩsĩ ũu ata?
13 Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana "Ngai nĩ wendo." (1 Yoana 4:8) Ngai ekaa maũndũ onthe nũndũ wa wendo. Kwoou twendaa andũ ala angĩ nũndũ o nake Ngai nũmendete. Kwasũanĩa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ: Ũkethĩwa na ũtonyi, we no ũvetange mathĩna onthe na ũsili ũte wa katĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ? Vate nzika ndũema kwĩka ũu nũndũ nĩwendete andũ. Nao nata Ngai? Nũndũ e ũtonyi na nũtwendete, akavetanga mathĩna onthe na ũsili ũte wa katĩ. Ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana mawatho onthe ma Ngai ala mawetetwe mwambĩĩonĩ wa ĩvuku yĩĩ makeanĩa! Ĩndĩ nĩ kana ũĩkĩĩe mawatho asu vyũ, nĩwaĩle kũmanya maũndũ maingangĩ ĩũlũ wa Ngai.
NGAI NŨKWENDA ŨMŨMANYE
14. Ngai etawa ata, na twĩsĩ ata kana nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩa ĩsyĩtwa yake?
14 Ethĩwa nũkwenda kũtuma ndũũ na mũndũ, nĩ ũndũ wĩva wambaa kũmũtavya mbee? Ũmũtavasya ĩsyĩtwa yaku. We Ngai e ĩsyĩtwa? Ndĩni mbingĩ imanyĩasya kana etawa Ngai kana Mwĩaĩi, ĩndĩ asu ti masyĩtwa make mwene. Asu no masyĩtwa ma ũnene, ta "mũsumbĩ" kana "mũtongoi." Ngai nũtũtavĩtye kana ĩsyĩtwa yake nĩ Yeova. Savuli 83:18 yaĩtye: "Nĩ kana mamanye no we wĩ weka, syĩtwa yaku nĩ Yeova, Nue Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe." Aandĩki ma Mbivilia nĩmatũmĩie ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai mavinda ngili mbingĩ. Kwoou Yeova nĩwendaa ũmanye ĩsyĩtwa yake na ũiyĩtũmĩa. Ngai aũtavĩtye ĩsyĩtwa yake nĩ kana ũtw'ĩke mũnyanyae.
15. Ĩsyĩtwa Yeova yonanasya ata?
15 Ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova, yonanasya ũndũ wa vata mũno. Yonanasya kana Ngai nũtonya kwĩanĩsya ũndũ o na wĩva ũla wathana na nũtonya kwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kyake. Vai kĩndũ kĩtonya kũmũsiĩĩa. No Yeova e weka ũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ĩsyĩtwa yonanasya ũu. *
16, 17. (a) Ĩsyĩtwa "Mwene Vinya W'onthe" yonanasya ata? (b) Ĩsyĩtwa 'Mũsumbĩ wa tene na tene' yonanasya ata? (c) Ĩsyĩtwa "Mũmbi" yonanasya ata?
16 O tondũ twoona, Savuli 83:18 yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova: 'No we wĩ weka Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe.' O na ĩngĩ ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo 15:3 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Mawĩa maku nĩ manene na ma ũseng'ya, Mwĩaĩi Ngai, Mwene Vinya W'onthe; moendelo maku nĩ malũngalu na ma w'o, we Mũsumbĩ wa tene tene." Ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai ya ũnene "Mwene Vinya W'onthe" yonanasya ata? Yonanasya kana Yeova nĩwe wĩ na vinya mwingĩ vyũ kwĩ syũmbe syonthe ĩtunĩ na kũũ nthĩ. Nayo ĩsyĩtwa ya ũnene 'Mũsumbĩ wa tene na tene' yonanasya Yeova nde mwambĩlĩlyo kana mũminũkĩlyo. Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 90:2 yĩeleetye kana Ngai nĩ wa kuma tene na tene kũvika tene na tene. Ũndũ ũsu kote wa kwendeesya mũno!
17 Yeova e weka nĩwe Mũmbi. Ĩandĩko ya Ũvuan'yo 4:11 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩwaĩle we, Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Ngai waitũ, kwosa ndaĩa na nguma na vinya: nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwoombie syĩndũ syonthe, na kwondũ wa kwenda kwaku syaĩ kw'o, na ĩngĩ syoombwa." Syĩndũ syonthe ila ũtonya kũsũanĩa ta alaĩka, ndata ila syĩ matunĩ, matunda, na makũyũ, syoombiwe nĩ Yeova!
NŨTONYA KWĨTHĨWA MŨNYANYA WA YEOVA?
18. Nĩkĩ andũ amwe masũanĩaa mayĩsa kũtw'ĩka anyanya ma Ngai? Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu?
18 Ĩla andũ amwe masoma ĩũlũ wa ndaĩa nzeo sya Yeova makwatawa nĩ wia na maisũanĩa ũũ: 'Nũndũ Ngai e vinya mwingĩ vyũ, nĩ mũnene mũno, na e vaasa vyũ, vatonyeka ata akanthĩnĩkĩa?' Ĩndĩ ũu nĩw'o Ngai wendaa tũsũanĩe? Aiee. Yeova endaa kũtũthengeea, na nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "nde kũasa na kĩla ũmwe waitũ." (Meko ma Atũmwa 17:27) Ngai nĩwendaa ũmũthengeee, na weeka ũu athanĩte kana 'akakũthengeea.'—Yakovo 4:8.
19. (a) Ũtonya kwĩthĩwa mũnyanya wa Ngai ata? (b) Nĩ ndaĩa syĩva sya Yeova ikwendeeasya vyũ?
19 Ũtonya kwĩthĩwa mũnyanya wa Ngai ata? Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Na thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto." (Yoana 17:3) Endeea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nũndũ kwĩka ũu kũkatuma ũmũmanya Yeova na Yesũ. Na weeka ũu, ũkakwata thayũ ũtathela. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtweemanyĩsya kana "Ngai nĩ wendo." (1 Yoana 4:16) Ĩndĩ Ngai e ndaĩa ingĩ mbingĩ na nzeo. Mbivilia yaasyaa kana Yeova nĩ "Ngai wĩ tei na mũseo, ũtathataa mĩtũkĩ, na wĩ na wingĩ wa ũseo wĩ wendo na w'o." (Kuma 34:6) Yeova nĩ 'mũseo, na nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye kũekea.' (Savuli 86:5) Ngai e wũmĩĩsyo na nĩ mũĩkĩĩku. (2 Vetelo 3:9; Ũvuan'yo 15:4, NWT) Waendeea kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova, ũkamanya mũnango ĩũlũ wa ndaĩa isu nzeo syake.
20-22. (a) Tũtonya ata kwĩthĩwa anyanya ma Ngai ethĩwa tũitonya kũmwona? (b) Waĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa andũ meenda ũeke kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia?
20 Vatonyeka ata ũkethĩwa wĩ mũnyanya wa Ngai ethĩwa ndũtonya kũmwona? (Yoana 1:18; 4:24; 1 Timotheo 1:17) Ĩla weemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova Mbivilianĩ nũmũmanyaa nesa. (Savuli 27:4; Alomi 1:20) Waendeea kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova ũkamwenda mũno na ũkeethĩwa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu nake.
21 O na ĩngĩ, ũkaelewa kana Yeova nĩwe Ĩthe waitũ. (Mathayo 6:9) Nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ na nĩwendaa tũũtanĩe ũndũ vatonyeka. Maũndũ asu nomo ĩthe wĩ wendo wendeaa syana syake. (Savuli 36:9) Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana no wĩthĩwe mũnyanya wa Yeova. (Yakovo 2:23) We kwasũanĩa kĩu. Yeova, Mũmbi wa syĩndũ syonthe, nũkwenda wĩthĩwe mũnyanyae!
22 Andũ amwe no makwĩe ũeke kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nũndũ meona ta ũtonya kũtia ndĩni yaku. Ĩndĩ ndũketĩkĩle mũndũ o na wĩva aũsiĩĩe kwĩthĩwa mũnyanya wa Yeova. Nĩwe Mũnyanya ũla mũseo vyũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa nake.
23, 24. (a) Nĩkĩ ũtaĩle kũeka kũkũlya makũlyo? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe?
23 O ũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, ve maũndũ amwe ũtakaeleawa. Ndũkew'e nthoni kũkũlya makũlyo kana kũkũlya ũtetheew'e. Yesũ aisye kana twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo ta syana nini. (Mathayo 18:2-4) Syana nikũlasya makũlyo maingĩ. Ngai nũkwenda ũkwate mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ala wĩkũlasya. Kwoou ĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia nesa nĩ kana wĩthĩwe ũte na nzika kana maũndũ ala ũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩmo ma w'o.—Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 17:11.
24 Nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ ya kũmũmanya Yeova nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe, nĩtũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩkĩ Mbivilia yĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mavuku ala angĩ onthe.

translation:
1, 2. Are there many people who enjoy eating too much food?
It is good to be careful about enjoying food. But if someone eats a lot, they ask themselves, 'Why?' And they continue to overeat, and then ask again, 'Why?'
2 Whether we are rich or poor, we are always tempted by food. And we are tempted by food every day, every time we get full, or every time we feel hungry. Or we are tempted by delicious food whenever there is a celebration or when something good happens. Because we often want to hold onto the pleasures of food, and we cling to them tightly.
3. Why do many people struggle or fail to let go of the pleasures of delicious food?
3 Does the Bible tempt us to seek the pleasures of delicious food? Some people argue that the Bible does not have such temptations, because it teaches moderation. And they argue that it also has warnings against being greedy and indulging in too much food. However, others claim that it encourages us to desire or seek the pleasures of delicious food. What do you think?
4, 5. Is there delicious food that is harmful to eat? Is it wise to keep trying to cling to its pleasures?
4 But you are tempted to hold onto the pleasures of food if you ask yourself: Am I praying about this? Am I relying on God? Does God care? Jesus, our great Teacher, said: "Ask, and it will be given to you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you." (Matthew 7:7) So, try to cling to the pleasures of food only if you have already sought God's guidance.
5 If you keep seeking 'pleasures' from delicious food, you will end up disappointed. (Proverbs 2:1-5) Such pleasures are fleeting and unsatisfying. The things you focus on can cause you to become anxious and worried, and you will be troubled by the consequences. Consider how one meal alone can lead many people astray.
GOD CAN HELP US
6. Why do some people feel that God does not help them overcome their desires?
6 Many people wonder whether God helps them overcome their desires. They may feel that God does not listen to their prayers, or they may think that their problems are too difficult. They may also feel guilty, ashamed, and hopeless. This is why some people conclude, 'God does not help me overcome my desires, so I might as well give in to temptation.'
7. (a) What reasons do imperfect humans have for thinking that God doesn't care? (b) Why should we be confident that God is willing to help us when we face difficult situations?
7 Some imperfect humans reason that God is uncaring and indifferent. However, it is reasonable to believe that God cares, because he created mankind. God is the One who can truly solve our problems. But if we want his help, we must turn to him. The Bible shows that God does not tempt anyone. James 1:13 clearly states that God does not cause trouble. It says: "With bad things God cannot be tempted, and he himself tempts no one." Therefore, we can be sure that if God allows difficult trials to come upon us, he has a good reason for doing so. (Read Job 34:10-12.) Let us consider this further.
8, 9. Is it possible to please God despite facing temptations? How so?
8 Consider a loving father and his son. He would guide his son and warn him about dangers. If his son disobeyed and got into trouble, the father would lovingly try to help him correct his mistake. Would you conclude that the father did not love his son just because the son made mistakes? Of course not! (Luke 15:11-13) In the same way, God loves people even though they sometimes choose to do wrong. When bad things happen to us, we can be confident that God did not cause them. It is not possible to please God while continuing to practice wrongdoing.
9 God has a powerful reason for allowing wickedness to continue. The Bible reveals this reason in Revelation chapter 11. It explains that God will eventually intervene and restore true worship. And so, we can trust that God will bring an end to injustice.—Isaiah 33:2.
10. Can we be certain that God will eliminate all suffering caused by wicked people?
10 The Bible assures us that God is almighty. (Isaiah 6:3) All things are possible with him. But why does he allow evil to persist? Many people feel this way, and some have doubts. However, those who are patient and trust in God's timing will see that he *can* and will eliminate all suffering caused by wicked people. A righteous person waits for God, and he trusts in God's power to act.—Psalm 37:9-11.
WHY DOES GOD ALLOW SUFFERING?
11. Does God delight in causing suffering?
11 Does God delight in seeing people experience pain and hardship? The Bible shows that God "does not rejoice over the misfortune of the wicked." (Psalm 37:28) He wants what is best for us, both now and in the future. He cares for faithful ones. The Bible says that God 'takes pleasure in their heartiness' when they show loyalty to him. (Proverbs 6:5, 6) God hates wickedness. (Malachi 3:6) The Bible also states that God is compassionate.—1 Peter 5:7.
12, 13. (a) How can we remain confident when faced with difficulties? Can we be sure that God will fulfill his promises? (b) What should we remember when we wonder whether God truly cares about our feelings?
12 Moreover, the Bible assures us that God sympathizes with us. (Proverbs 1:26) This means that he understands how we feel and is moved by our plight. When you see others suffering, remember that God feels deeply for them! Are we not grateful for that?
13 The Bible states that "God is love." (1 John 4:8) Everything God does is motivated by love. As we show love to others, we imitate God's love. Consider this illustration: If you were unjustly accused, would you still care about the well-being of those who falsely accused you? A loving person would. And what about God? Despite our imperfections and despite showing him little love, he continues to care about us. Be comforted by the fact that all of God's laws are expressions of his love! Indeed, if you obey God's commands, you demonstrate your love for him and deepen your understanding of his ways.
GOD WANTS YOU TO KNOW HIM
14. Does God expect too much of us, and are we able to meet his expectations?
14 It pleases God when we try to please him, even if we don't always succeed perfectly. But how can we learn what pleases him? By studying the Bible. However, God doesn't have a personal name like humans do. Some translations use titles such as "Lord" or "God." But God has revealed his name to be Jehovah. Psalm 83:18 says: "You whose name is Jehovah, you alone are the Most High over all the earth." Many Bible writers used God's name frequently. Jehovah wants you to know his name and to use it. God considers his name sacred.
15. Is the name Jehovah important?
15 God's name, Jehovah, is vital. It distinguishes him from all others. It reminds us that God cares about justice and righteousness and that he will act in defense of his integrity. He deserves our respect. And Jehovah shows respect for his name when he defends its honor. *
16, 17. (a) What does the title "Sovereign Lord" reveal about God? (b) What does the title "Eternal Father" reveal about God? (c) What does the title "Creator" reveal about God?
16 Notice, Psalm 83:18 refers to Jehovah as "the Sovereign Lord." Also, Isaiah 15:3 reads: "Your greatness and your glory are God, O Sovereign Lord, Eternal Father." What does the title "Sovereign Lord" reveal about God? It reveals that Jehovah is supreme ruler over all creation and everything in it. And the title "Eternal Father" reveals that Jehovah is everlasting and unchanging. Psalm 90:2 states that God is from time indefinite to time indefinite. That thought is comforting!
17 Jehovah is also the Creator. Isaiah 4:11 says: "I will extol you, O Jehovah my God, and I will glorify your name forever and ever. For you have done wonderful things, and according to your abundant loving-kindness there is truth." Everything, except Satan the Devil, originates with Jehovah! He created the heavens, the earth, plants, animals, and humans.
DO YOU WANT TO DRAW CLOSE TO JEHOVAH?
18. Do some find it hard to feel close to God? Does the Bible give us insight into why this is so?
18 However, some people who study the Bible become discouraged because they reason: 'If God has so much power, he is too great to be concerned with me personally.' Is that what God wants us to think? No. Jehovah wants to get close to us, and that is why the Bible says that he is near to each one of us. (Acts 17:27) God wants to have a relationship with us, and he makes himself approachable.—James 4:8.
19. (a) Can you draw close to God? (b) What aspects of Jehovah encourage us?
19 Can you draw close to God? Jesus said: "This means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent forth." (John 17:3) Continue to learn from the Bible so that you can better know Jehovah and Jesus. And as you do, strive to apply what you learn. For example, meditate on the fact that "God is love." (1 John 4:16) God has many wonderful qualities. The Bible reveals that Jehovah is "a God of justice," "slow to anger," and "abundant in loving-kindness and truth." (Exodus 34:6) Jehovah is "merciful and compassionate."—Psalm 86:5. He is wise and discerning. (2 Peter 3:9; Proverbs 15:4, NWT) As you learn more about Jehovah through the Bible, you will come to appreciate his unique personality and his outstanding qualities.
20-22. (a) Can we draw close to God even if we cannot see him? (b) How can we help others to draw close to God?
20 Can we draw close to God even though we cannot see him? (John 1:18; 4:24; 1 Timothy 1:17) Yes, by learning about Jehovah from the Bible, we can get to know him well. (Psalm 27:4; Amos 1:20) As you learn more about Jehovah, you will love him more and be motivated to please him.
21 Moreover, you will realize that Jehovah is our Father. (Matthew 6:9) He gives us everything we need, and he wants us to have good things. His heart overflows with love for his children. (Psalm 36:9) The Bible shows that it pleases Jehovah when we reflect his qualities. (James 2:23) So strive to imitate him. Jehovah, the Creator of all things, wants us to imitate his beautiful qualities!
22 Some people find it difficult to study the Bible because they feel unworthy. But remember that everyone who desires to draw close to Jehovah is welcome. He is the One who makes it possible for imperfect humans to draw close to him.
23, 24. (a) What will motivate you to keep progressing? (b) What can we resolve to do?
23 Keep studying the Bible, and do not become discouraged if there are some things you do not understand. Do not give up just because something seems complicated or difficult. Jesus taught that we should have the attitude of little children. (Matthew 18:2-4) Little children are eager to learn. God wants you to be diligent in your search for knowledge and to continue studying so that you may grow spiritually.—Read Acts 17:11.
24 In fact, the best way to get to know Jehovah is to study the Bible. Every day, let us examine the Scriptures and meditate on the wonderful truths they contain.

text:
"Ninyie Yeova Ngai waku, ũla ũkũmanyĩasya kwaĩla, ũla ũkũtongoeasya nzĩanĩ ĩla waĩle kũthi nayo."—ISA. 48:17.
1. Aklĩsto methĩĩtwe maikwatwa nĩ mathĩna meva ĩla meũtavany'a?
MŨTHYANĨ wa myaka ya 1800 na mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1900, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia * nĩmakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna maingĩ. Matavanasya ũvoo ũtendetwe nĩ andũ o tondũ Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa meekaa. Mayaĩ aingĩ, na andũ moonaa me andũ mate asomu. O na ĩngĩ nĩmesie kũthĩnw'a ĩla Satani, ũla nĩwe Ndevili, wekiw'e kũũ nthĩ e na "ũthilĩku mũnene." (Ũvu. 12:12) Na eka ũu, kuma ĩvinda yĩu methĩĩtwe maitavany'a "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo" ĩla yusũĩtwe nĩ "mavinda ma mũisyo."—2 Tim. 3:1.
2. Yeova ethĩĩtwe ayĩka ata nĩ kana akwate mbau wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ?
2 Ĩndĩ o na maũndũ asu me o vo, Yeova nĩwatw'ĩte kana andũ make no nginya matavany'e ũvoo mũseo nthĩ yonthe, na vai kĩndũ kyamba kũsiĩĩa kĩeleelo kĩu kyake kĩikeanĩe. O ũndũ Yeova woovoisye mbaĩ ya Isilaeli kuma Mbaviloni, now'o wovoetye athũkũmi make kumana na 'Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene,' ĩla nĩ ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ. (Ũvu. 18:1-4) O na nũtũmanyĩĩtye nĩ kana twaĩle, akatũathima na mũuo, na akatũtetheesya tũkamanya ũndũ tũtonya kũmanyĩsya angĩ Mbivilia. (Soma Isaia 48:16-18.) Ũu ti kwasya kana Yeova nũvangĩĩaa kĩla ũndũ wĩkĩkaa kũũ nthĩ nĩ kana wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ ũendeee. O na kau ve maũndũ amwe mekĩkĩte vaa nthĩ makatũtetheesya wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a, Yeova nĩwe ũtũtetheeasya tũmĩĩsye kũthĩnw'a na maũndũ angĩ ala maumanaa na nthĩ ĩno ya Satani, na ala matumaa wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a wĩthĩwa ũte laisi.—Isa. 41:13; 1 Yoa. 5:19.
3. Ũmũnthĩ "ũmanyi" wĩthĩĩtwe wĩ mwingĩ ata?
3 Mwathani Ndanieli nĩwaveveewe nĩ Yeova athane kana "ũmanyi" ũkeethĩwa wĩ mwingĩ ĩvinda ya mũminũkĩlyo. (Soma Ndanieli 12:4.) Yeova nĩwatetheeisye Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maelewe momanyĩsyo ma vata ma Maandĩko, ala matwĩe mavithanaw'a nĩ ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. Ũmũnthĩ atũmĩaa andũ make kũtavany'a ũmanyi wa w'o nthĩ yonthe. Kwoou wathani wa Ndanieli nĩwĩanĩĩte. Vakuvĩ andũ 8,000,000 nĩmemanyĩĩtye ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ na nĩmaendeee kũũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. Nĩ maũndũ ta meva ala matetheesye wĩa wa kũtavany'a nthĩ yonthe?
KŨALYŨLWA KWA MBIVILIA
4. Mbivilia yalyũlilwe mũno wĩana ata myakanĩ ya 1800?
4 Ũndũ ũmwe ũla ũtetheesye wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo nĩ kana andũ aingĩ me na Mbivilia. Kwa myaka mingĩ atongoi ma ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto nĩmavataa andũ kũsoma Mbivilia o na nĩmooaie amwe ala mamyalyũlaa. Ĩndĩ myakanĩ ya 1800 ngwatanĩo ila ialyũlaa Mbivilia nĩsyanyaĩĩkisye Mbivilia, yĩ nima kana o kĩlungu kyayo, kwa ithyomo ta 400. Kũvikĩĩa mwakanĩ wa 1900, andũ aingĩ maĩ na Mbivilia o na kau mayaeleawa ũmanyĩsyo ũla wa w'o wa Maandĩko.
5. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩkĩte maũndũ meva makonetye kũalyũla Mbivilia?
5 Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmeesĩ kana nĩmaĩlĩte kũtavany'a, na nĩkyo kĩtumi meekie ũu na kĩthito. O na ĩngĩ, andũ ma Yeova nĩmatũmĩĩte na makanyaĩĩkya Mbivilia sya ũalyũlo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kuma mwaka wa 1950 nĩmaumĩthĩtye Biblia Takatifu—Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya yĩ nima kana kĩlungu kyayo, kwa ithyomo mbee wa 120. Mwakanĩ wa 2013 nĩmanaumĩthisye Mbivilia ya Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya ya Kĩsũngũ yĩ laisi kũalyũlwa kwa ithyomo ingĩ. Kũtũmĩa Mbivilia yĩ laisi kũeleeka na kũsomeka nĩkũtũtetheeasya ũtavany'anĩ.
MAVINDA MA MŨUO
6, 7. (a) Kwĩthĩĩtwe na makaũ meana ata ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ? (b) Kwĩthĩwa kwĩ o na mũuo nthĩ imwe kũtũtetheeasya ata wĩanĩ witũ wa kũtavany'a?
6 Nũtonya kũseng'a na ũkekũlya atĩĩ: 'Yo kwaaĩthĩwa mũuo wĩ vala ũĩ?' Kwa ngelekany'o, myakanĩ ya 1900 andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmooaiwe nũndũ wa kaũ, na mũno mũno ĩvinda ya ala makaũ elĩ manene ma nthĩ. Ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1942 ĩla Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe waĩ mũvyũ, Nathan Knorr, ũla watongoesye wĩa wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, nĩwaumisye ũvoo mũna e ũmbanonĩ mũnene. Ũvoo wake waĩ na kyongo kyakũlĩtye "Mũuo no Ũendeee Kwĩthĩwa Kw'o?" Ũvoo ũsu waeleisye nesa ĩandĩko ya Ũvuan'yo kĩlungu kya 17, woonany'a kana kwaĩ kwĩthĩwe ĩvinda ya mũuo ĩtina wa kaũ ũla waendeee, ĩndĩ ti Ali–Maketoni.—Ũvu. 17:3, 11.
7 Ĩla Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe wathelile kũyaaĩthĩwa mũuo vyũ. Kwosana na livoti ĩmwe, kwaĩ na makaũ 331 kwambĩĩa mwaka wa 1946 nginya mwaka wa 2013. Makaũ asu moaĩte andũ milioni mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ myakanĩ o ĩsu, nthĩ mbingĩ nĩsyĩthĩĩtwe syĩ o na mũuo, na andũ ma Yeova nĩmatũmĩĩte myanya ĩsu kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo. Maũndũ methĩĩtwe mailyĩ ata ĩtina wa kwĩka ũu? Mwakanĩ wa 1944 kwaĩ atavany'a matavika 110,000 nthĩ yonthe. Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ makilyĩ manavika 8,000,000! (Soma Isaia 60:22.) Twaĩlĩte kũtũnga mũvea ta kĩ nũndũ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo kũuĩtye!
NĨ LAISI KŨTHI KŨNDŨ
8, 9. Nĩ maendeeo meva mekĩtwe maũndũnĩ ma ũkui, na matũtethetye ata wĩanĩ witũ?
8 Maendeeo ala me kw'o maũndũnĩ ma ũkui nĩmatetheesye mũno wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo. Mwakanĩ wa 1900, myaka ta 21 kuma ĩkaseti ya mbee ya Watch Tower yatumbĩthw'a, kwaĩ o ngalĩ 8,000 ila syaandĩkĩthĩtw'e kwosana na mĩao nthĩ ya Amelika, na kwaĩ o malelũ manini maseo. Ĩndĩ yu nthĩ yonthe kwĩ ngalĩ mbee wa mbilioni ĩmwe na nusu ila iandĩkĩthĩtw'e kwosana na mĩao, na kwĩ malelũ maingĩ ki maseo. Ngalĩ na malelũ nitetheeasya aingĩ maitũ kũtavya andũ ala mekalaa kũndũ kũasa ũvoo mũseo. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa kũla twĩkalaa kũi malelũ maseo na ngalĩ mbingĩ, na nĩtũlasimĩkaa kũthi na maaũ kũndũ kũasa, nĩtwĩkĩaa kĩthito tũtavany'e ũvoo mũseo.—Mt. 28:19, 20.
9 Ve nzĩa ingĩ sya kũthi kũndũ kana sya kũkua mĩio itũtetheeasya wĩanĩ witũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũtũmĩaa maloli, meli, na ngalĩ sya mwaki kũtwaa mavuku kũndũ kũasa na maivika ĩtina wa syumwa nini. Nasyo ndeke nitetheeasya asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko, ana-a-asa ma Kamitii ya Ovisi wa Ũvonge, amisonalĩ, na angĩ kũthi mĩtũkĩ maũmbanonĩ manene kana kũtethya mawĩa ala manengetwe. O na ĩngĩ, ana-a-asa ma Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye na ana-a-asa angĩ kuma ovisinĩ ũla mũnene nĩmaendaa nthĩ mbingĩ na ndeke nĩ kana mekĩe ana-a-asa vinya na maimamanyĩsya. Kwoou maendeeo maũndũnĩ ma ũkui nĩmatetheesye athũkũmi ma Yeova maendeee kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo.—Sav. 133:1-3.
KĨTHYOMO
10. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Kĩsũngũ nĩ kĩthyomo kĩneenawa nĩ andũ aingĩ?
10 Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, andũ aingĩ Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Lomi matũmĩaa Kĩkiliki kyeetawa Koine. Ũmũnthĩ nĩvethĩwa kĩthyomo kĩneenawa nĩ andũ aingĩ ũu? Ĩĩ, Kĩsũngũ nĩkĩneenawa nĩ andũ aingĩ. Ĩvuku yĩmwe (English as a Global Language) yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Vakuvĩ [mũndũ 1 katĩ wa 4] ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nũneenaa kana nĩwĩsĩ Kĩsũngũ nesa." Kĩthyomo kĩeni kĩla kĩsomethaw'a andũ aingĩ vyũ nĩ Kĩsũngũ nũndũ nĩkĩtũmĩawa nĩ andũ nthĩ mbingĩ maũndũnĩ ma viasala, siasa, saenzi, na tekinolongyia.
11. Kĩsũngũ kĩtethetye ata ũthaithinĩ wa w'o?
11 Kĩsũngũ nĩkĩtetheesye mũno ũthaithi wa w'o nũndũ nĩkĩtũmĩkaa kũndũ kwingĩ. Kwa myaka mingĩ ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya na mavuku angĩ maitũ matumbĩthaw'a na kĩthyomo kya Kĩsũngũ. Kĩthyomo kĩu nokyo kĩtũmĩawa maũndũnĩ makonetye wĩa ovisinĩ mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Na nĩkĩtũmĩawa mũno kũmanyĩsya amanyĩw'a ala mathi Watchtower Educational Center ĩla yĩ Patterson, New York, Amelika.
12. Athũkũmi ma Yeova maalyũlĩte mavuku moo mũno wĩana ata, na tekinolongyia ĩmatethetye ata?
12 Nũndũ nĩtũnengetwe wĩa wa kũtavya andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ, nĩtũalyũlĩte mavuku maitũ kwa ithyomo ta 700. Maendeeo maũndũnĩ ma kombiũta vamwe na kũtũmĩwa kwa MEPS (Multilanguage Electronic Publishing System) nĩmatũtetheesye mũno wĩanĩ ũsu. Maũndũ asu nĩmatũtethetye mũno kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ, na makatũtetheesya kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nthĩ yonthe. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla mũnene ũtumĩte twĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nĩ kũneena "kĩthyomo kĩtheu" kya ũw'o wa Maandĩko.—Soma Nzevania 3:9.
MĨAO
13, 14. Aklĩsto ũmũnthĩ matethekete ata nĩ mĩao na motwi ma koti?
13 O tondũ ĩsomo ĩvĩtu yĩeleetye, Aklĩsto nĩmatethekie mũno nĩ mĩao ya Lomi ĩla yatũmĩkaa ũsumbĩnĩ ũsu w'onthe. O ta ũu, Aklĩsto nĩmatethekaa mũno nĩ mĩao ĩla yĩ kw'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, Amelika nĩvo ve ovisi witũ mũnene, na mĩao ya nthĩ ĩsu nĩyĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũthasyo wa ũthaithi, wa ũneeni, na wa kũmbana. Mĩao ĩsu nĩtumĩte ana-a-asa nthĩ ya Amelika methĩwa me na ũthasyo wa kũmbana ũtheinĩ maneenee maũndũ ala me Mbivilianĩ, na wa kũtavya ala angĩ kĩla meĩmanyĩsya. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩ kana makwate ũthasyo maũndũnĩ amwe yaĩ lasima mathi kotinĩ makawũkitĩe. (Avi. 1:7) Na ĩndĩ ĩla koti isu sya Amelika syesa kũmasikata, nĩmaendaa kotinĩ ila nene kwĩtetea, na mavinda maingĩ koti isu nĩsyamanengae ũthasyo wa kũtavany'a.
14 O na koti sya nthĩ ingĩ nitũnengete ũthasyo wa ũthaithi na wa kũtavany'a. Ĩndĩ kwĩ kũndũ kũmwe tũsindĩtwe makoaninĩ na tũkekaĩla koti ila nene sya nthĩ mbingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, kũvikĩĩa Mwei wa 6, 2014, nĩtwasindĩte makoani 57 kotinĩ ũmwe mũnene (European Court of Human Rights). Ũtwi wa koti ũsu wĩthĩawa waĩlĩte kũatĩĩwa nĩ nthĩ syonthe ila syĩ Nzamanĩ ya Europe. O na kau 'nĩtũmenetwe nĩ mbaĩ syonthe,' koti sya nthĩ mbingĩ nitwĩtĩkĩlĩtye tũendeee kũmũthaitha Yeova twĩ na ũthasyo.—Mt. 24:9.
MAŨNDŨ ANGĨ MATŨTETHETYE
15. Nĩ maendeeo meva mekĩtwe maũndũnĩ ma kũtumbĩthya syĩndũ, na matũtethetye ata?
15 Maendeeo ala mekĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa kũtumbĩthya mavuku nĩmatetheesye wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a nthĩ yonthe. Kwa myaka mingĩ andũ matũmĩaa masinĩ sya kũtumbĩthya sya mũthemba wa platen ila syambĩlĩlw'e nĩ Johannes Gutenberg vakuvĩ mwakanĩ 1450. Ĩndĩ myaka ta 200 mĩvĩtu, nĩkwĩthĩĩtwe na moalyũku maingĩ maũndũnĩ ma kũtumbĩthya syĩndũ. Nĩkũseũvĩtw'e masinĩ nene sya kũtumbĩthya syĩ mĩtũkĩ na nzeo mũno. Mathangũ nĩmaekete kwĩthĩwa me na mbesa mbingĩ na kũmakwatany'a mamina kũtumbwa kũi na ngalama nene. Masinĩ sya matukũ aa sya kũtumbĩthya ithũkũmaa mĩtũkĩ na syumasya mavisa maseo. Ũndũ ũsu ũtũtethetye ata? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ĩkaseti ya mbee ya Watch Tower (Mwei wa 7, 1879) yatumbĩthiw'e kovi 6,000 na yĩyaĩ na mavisa na yaĩ o ya Kĩsũngũ. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu nginya ũmũnthĩ vavĩtĩte myaka 136, na kovi mbee wa 50,000,000 sya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya nitumbĩthaw'a na ikanyaĩĩkw'a. Ĩkaseti yĩu yĩthĩawa na mavisa me na langi nzeo na yumĩthaw'a kwa ithyomo mbee wa 200.
16. Nĩ maendeeo meva matũtethetye wĩanĩ witũ wa kũtavany'a nthĩ yonthe? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 24.)
16 Kwasũanĩa maendeeo ala mekĩtwe vandũ va myaka 200 ala matetheesye andũ ma Ngai kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo. Nĩtwaweta syĩndũ ta ngalĩ sya mwaki, ngalĩ, na ndeke, ĩndĩ no tũtũmĩĩte isululu, kyavuleta, masinĩ sya mũandĩko wa ala matonaa, telegraph, simũ, kamela, syĩndũ sya kũlekoti wasya na sya kwosa vitio, letiũ, televiseni, sinema, kombiũta, na Indaneti. Syĩndũ isu nitũtetheesye kwĩanĩsya wĩa ũla twanengiwe wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a. Nĩ kana twĩanĩsye wathani wa kana andũ ma Yeova 'makoonga ĩia ya i mbaĩ,' nĩtũtũmĩĩte nesa syĩndũ isu sietetwe nĩ mbaĩ, ta tekinolongyia, nĩ kana tumĩthye Mbivilia na mavuku kwa ithyomo mbingĩ.—Soma Isaia 60:16.
17. (a) Maũndũ ala twaneenea metũĩkĩĩthya kyaũ? (b) Nĩkĩ Yeova ũtwĩtĩkĩlĩtye twĩthĩwe "atethya ma wĩa vamwe" nake?
17 Kwa w'o maũndũ asu onthe metũĩkĩĩthya ki kana Ngai nũtũathimĩte. Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana Yeova nũtwĩkwatasya tũmũtetheesye eanĩsye kĩeleelo kyake. Vandũ va ũu, nũndũ we nĩ Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ wĩ wendo, nũtwĩtĩkĩlĩtye twĩthĩwe "atethya ma wĩa vamwe" nake, na ũu ũkatuma twĩthĩwa tũtonya kwonany'a kana nĩtũmwendete na nĩtwendete atũi. (1 Ako. 3:9; Mko. 12:28-31) Ekai ĩndĩ tũtw'e vyũ kũtũmĩa kamwanya kala twakwata tũnyaĩĩkye ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ nũndũ nĩw'o wĩa ũla wa vata vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. O na ĩngĩ, tũmũtũngĩae Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũtũtongoesya na kũathima wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a nthĩ yonthe, kwĩ kwiũ na kwĩ kweũ!
^ kal. 1 Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mambĩĩe kwĩtwa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova mwakanĩ wa 1931.

translation:
"You, Jehovah God of mine, are the One who taught me what is right and what is good."—ISA. 48:17.
1. What challenges did early Christians face regarding their faith?
During the 1800s and 1900s, Bible Students * faced many challenges. Opposition was often stirred up by people who disliked Christ and his followers. In many places, they were opposed by religious leaders and those in positions of authority. And much of this opposition came from Satan, who is the Devil, and who is determined to deceive people and to promote "grandstand religion." (Rev. 12:12) Furthermore, during that time, many experienced "times of distress" caused by "critical times."—2 Tim. 3:1.
2. Does Jehovah allow his servants to be attacked simply because they want to remain faithful?
2 To some extent, yes, Jehovah permits his people to experience opposition so that they may demonstrate their loyalty to him and prove the value of his name. Just as Jehovah allowed the Israelites to be taken captive to Babylon, he now allows his people to contend with 'Babylon the Great,' which represents the world empire of false religion. (Rev. 18:1-4) But he also assures us that he will strengthen us, comfort us, and help us to understand the truth of his Word. (Read Isaiah 48:16-18.) This does not mean that Jehovah is indifferent to our suffering or that he approves of the attacks made by Satan and his wicked system. Rather, he empowers us to stand firm and to resist the influence of Satan and the forces that oppose true worship.—Isa. 41:13; 1 John 5:19.
3. How can we show greater appreciation for "knowledge"?
3 Daniel foretold that "knowledge" would increase greatly during the time of the end. (Read Daniel 12:4.) Jehovah has caused Bible knowledge to spread through publications and preaching work, exposing the falsehoods of this world empire. He uses his organization to help his people to increase in knowledge. As Daniel foretold, millions—over 8,000,000—have learned about God's Kingdom and continue to proclaim his message throughout the earth. Are these developments evidence that we are living in the time of the end?
UNDERSTANDING BIBLE PROPHECY
4. Has Bible prophecy been fulfilled within the last 1800 years?
4 One development that shows we are living in the time of the end is that more and more people have access to the Bible. For centuries, only clergy could read the Bible, and most people were unable to study it themselves. But since the 1800's, Bibles have become available in increasing numbers, and now there are over 400 translations. In the 1900's, more and more people had their own Bibles and began to understand the meaning of scripture.
5. How does Jehovah's organization assist in making the Bible understandable?
5 Bible scholars work hard to make accurate translations, and this benefits us greatly. Also, Jehovah's Witnesses use simplified Bible publications to help people learn about God's Word. In 1950, they published the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures, which has been used extensively. In 2013, they released the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures in plain language, making it easier to read. Using easy-to-understand Bibles helps us to study effectively.
INSIGHTS FOR UNDERSTANDING
6, 7. (a) What questions can motivate us to examine our hearts? (b) How can personal reflection help us to improve our study habits?
6 Consider asking yourself: 'Am I truly motivated to serve?' For example, in the 1900s millions were affected by wars, and many faced economic hardship. In 1942, during World War II, Nathan Knorr, president of the Watch Tower Society, gave a talk that had a profound impact. His talk was entitled "Should We Keep Asking Questions?" This talk explained the meaning of Isaiah chapter 17, showing that the question of whether a war would continue was important, just like the case of Ali–MacIntyre.—Isa. 17:3, 11.
7 During World War II, there was an urgent need to find out about people's motivation. As one illustration, some 331 congregations reported a total of 1946 baptisms from 1946 to 2013. These baptisms represented millions of individuals. In recent years, many more have become interested because of their desire for truth, and Jehovah's Witnesses have been using this interest to share the good news. Are such efforts worthwhile? In 1944, over 110,000 new ones began serving. By now, there are over 8,000,000! (Read Isaiah 60:22.) How thrilled we are to be part of this work of helping people learn the truth!
TO KEEP MOTIVATED
8, 9. What practical steps can we take to stay motivated, and what will help us to do so?
8 Practical steps to stay motivated include focusing on the importance of making disciples. In 1900, just 21 years after the first issue of Watch Tower was published, there were only 8,000 publishers, and most of them were in America, with relatively few elsewhere. Today, there are well over a billion people worldwide, and there are many more territories to work. There are also many more opportunities to reach those who are honest-hearted and seek the truth. So, while we may feel overwhelmed by the size of the territory and the number of people, we can remain confident that we can make progress in helping people learn the truth.—Matt. 28:19, 20.
9 There are many ways to overcome obstacles or find solutions to problems. For example, we use airplanes, trains, and ferries to travel to distant lands and islands. But these are not the only means of reaching people, such as through large conventions, meetings at Kingdom Halls, personal study, and by assisting others with their spiritual needs. Others assist with disaster relief work and help build places of worship or provide assistance to those affected by calamities. Furthermore, those associated with Bethel and other large offices often need volunteers and skilled workers. The advancement of God's Kingdom is greatly aided by the unity of Jehovah's Witnesses—Ps. 133:1-3.
QUESTION
10. Is the ministry something enjoyable to most people?
10 According to an article, many people around the world use English, which is called Koine Greek. Why is English considered a global language today? Yes, English is a global language. A recent report (English as a Global Language) states: "About [one in four] people worldwide either speak or understand English." This widespread knowledge of English makes it easier for people from different countries to communicate in areas like commerce, politics, science, and technology.
11. Does English influence international relations?
11 English has had a significant impact on international affairs because it is used so widely. For many years, missionaries and other dedicated individuals have used English to spread the good news. That is why it is used extensively in connection with the large office of the Watch Tower Society. And it is also used to prepare publications that are distributed from the Watchtower Educational Center in Patterson, New York, United States.
12. How do Jehovah's Witnesses make effective use of tools and technology?
12 Because we want to help people everywhere learn about God's Kingdom, we have been producing publications in over 700 languages for decades. Advances in computer technology and the use of MEPS (Multilanguage Electronic Publishing System) have greatly increased our ability to do so. These tools enable us to convey the message of the Kingdom clearly, and they allow translations to be reviewed by numerous translators. One important way we show respect for accurate communication is by using "clear language" when discussing God's Word.—Read Proverbs 3:9.
QUESTIONS
13, 14. What factors contribute to clear communication?
13 As the foregoing discussion illustrates, clarity depends on the audience's cultural background. For example, Christ's teachings were clear to those familiar with Jewish customs. However, his teachings might not be as clear to others. The United States is a nation with a diverse population, and different cultures may interpret things differently—such as gestures, expressions, and ways of speaking. Different cultures may also view concepts such as honesty, loyalty, and hospitality in varying ways. Therefore, it is vital to understand the cultural context when trying to communicate effectively. (Prov. 1:7) And even within American culture, there are regional differences that can affect how something is understood, and many Americans are sensitive to cultural nuances.
14 Moreover, we need to be mindful of legal and social sensitivities. For instance, in some countries we may face restrictions and challenges that differ from those in other lands. For example, on June 6, 2014, we appealed to the European Court of Human Rights in 57 countries. That court ruling was considered binding on all nations belonging to the Council of Europe. But despite being "bound by their decisions," rulings by higher courts do not prevent us from continuing to proclaim Jehovah's name boldly.—Matt. 24:9.
OTHER POINTS TO CONSIDER
15. What factors can hinder communication, and what can we do about them?
15 Advances in printing technology have greatly aided communication, but they also present challenges. For centuries people used handwritten manuscripts, but these were time-consuming to produce until Johannes Gutenberg developed the printing press around 1450. Within 200 years, there were many more printing facilities. Today, advanced printing methods allow for mass production at low cost. However, this has led to an abundance of publications, making it difficult to distinguish valuable information from worthless material. Modern printing techniques can quickly produce millions of copies, often filled with misleading or inaccurate data. Does this pose a challenge? Consider this: The July 7, 1879, issue of The Watch Tower was printed in an edition of 6,000 copies and distributed primarily in the United States and Canada. Now, 136 years later, over 50,000,000 copies of The Watchtower magazine are printed in numerous languages each month. This publication is distributed widely and reaches people in nearly 200 lands.
16. Are recent advances helping us to communicate effectively worldwide? (Consider paragraph 24.)
16 Consider the advances made in the past 200 years that have helped God's people to spread the good news. We now have things like steam engines, electricity, and oil, as well as tools such as the typewriter, telephone, telegraph, automobile, airplane, radio, television, cinema, computers, and the Internet. These tools have greatly facilitated our ability to reach people everywhere. If we use them to help Jehovah's Witnesses 'make known his glory among the nations,' we will be using these resources wisely, rather than letting technology distract us from spreading the Bible message.—Read Isaiah 60:16.
17. (a) What means of communication are available to us today? (b) Why does Jehovah encourage us to become "extensive communicators"?
17 Many different means of communication are available to us today because God has enabled this. However, it is important that Jehovah does not cause us to focus so much on communicating that we neglect his direction. For example, when we are encouraged to become "extensive communicators," this helps us to be more zealous in sharing the truth and in defending our faith. (1 Cor. 3:9; Mark 12:28-31) It is vital that we use our time wisely to take advantage of the opportunities we have to preach the good news. And above all, let us continue to thank Jehovah for enabling us to communicate effectively and for giving us the desire to share the good news worldwide, both near and far!
^ par. 1 The Bible Students were renamed Jehovah's witnesses in 1931.

text:
"Ngatavan'ya syĩtwa ya Yeova: . . . Ngai wa kĩthito na ũte na naĩ."—KŨT. 32:3, 4.
MBATHI: 15, 2
1, 2. (a) Navothi na ana make meekiwe ũndũ wĩva ũtaĩle? (b) Twĩneenea nguma syĩva ilĩ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
KWASŨANĨA ũndũ ũũ. Ĩvinda yĩmwe vaĩ mũndũ mũna watw'ĩkĩte atĩ nĩweekĩte ĩvĩtyo yaĩle kũtuma oawa. Andũ ma mũsyĩ na anyanyae mavaseng'eie mũno mayĩw'a atĩ mũndũ ũsu nĩwatw'ĩĩwa kũawa! Kĩla kyamaseng'isye mũno nĩ kũtw'ĩka ũkũsĩ ũla wethukĩĩiw'e ndwaĩ wa w'o na waumiw'e nĩ andũ meesĩkĩwe nĩ andũ vathei. Onthe ala mendete ũsili wa katĩ meewie thĩna mũno mayona mũndũ ũsu ũte na ĩvĩtyo ayũawa vamwe na ana make. Ndũkese kũsũanĩa ũsu nĩ wano. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ wamũkwatie mũthũkũmi mũĩkĩĩku wa Yeova weetawa Navothi watwĩe Isilaeli ĩvinda ya Mũsumbĩ Aavu.—1 Asu. 21:11-13; 2 Asu. 9:26.
2 Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩneenea ngewa ya Navothi na tũisyoka tũneene ĩũlũ wa mũtumĩa waĩ kĩla kĩkundinĩ kya ĩvinda ya atũmwa weekie ũtwi ũtaĩ mũseo. Tũineenea ngewa isu syĩ Mbivilianĩ, nĩtũkwona kana ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda kwĩthĩwa na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ, no nginya twĩthĩwe twĩnyivĩtye. Nĩtũũsyoka twone ũndũ kũekea ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ ĩla meeka ũndũ ũtaĩle kũtonya kwonany'a kana twĩ na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ.
ANDŨ MATAATĨĨA ŨSILI WA KATĨ O NA VANINI
3, 4. Navothi ailyĩ ata, na nĩkĩ waleile kũthooesya Mũsumbĩ Aavu mũũnda wake wa mĩsavivũ?
3 Ĩvindanĩ ya Navothi Aisilaeli aingĩ maatĩĩaa ngelekany'o nthũku ya Mũsumbĩ Aavu na kĩla kĩveti kyake kĩthũku kyeetawa Yeseveli, ĩndĩ we Navothi aĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova. Athaithi asu ma Mbaali mayamũnengete Yeova ndaĩa, o na mayoonaa mĩao yake ta kĩndũ. Ĩndĩ we Navothi oonaa ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova yĩ ya vata o na kwĩ thayũ wake mwene.
4 Soma 1 Asumbĩ 21:1-3. Ĩla Aavu weeie Navothi amũthooesye mũũnda wake wa mĩsavivũ, kana o etĩkĩle amũkũanĩsye na ũngĩ mũseango, Navothi nĩwaleile. Aleile nĩkĩ? Aeleisye ũũ na ndaĩa: "Yeova ndakandeke nĩkũnenge ũtiĩwa ũla natiĩwe nĩ aaĩthe makwa." Navothi aleanile na ngewa ya Aavu nũndũ nĩweesĩ mwĩao ũla Yeova wanengete mbaĩ ya Isilaeli. Yeova ameete kana mũndũ ndakaatate kũthoosya vyũ ũtiĩwa wa mbaĩ ya aa-ĩthe make. (Ali. 25:23; Mot. 36:7) Vate nzika, Navothi oonaa maũndũ ũndũ Yeova ũmonaa.
5. Yeseveli eekie ata nĩ kana oaĩthye Navothi?
5 Ũndũ wa kyeva nĩ kana ĩla Navothi waleile kwĩka kĩla Mũsumbĩ Aavu wendaa, ooseiwe matambya mathũku nĩ mũsumbĩ ũsu na mũka. Nĩ kana Yeseveli osee mũũme mũũnda wa Navothi, avangĩthisye andũ maumye ũkũsĩ ũte wa w'o ĩũlũ wa Navothi, na kĩu kyatumie Navothi oawa vamwe na ana make. Yeova eekie ata nũndũ wa ũndũ ũsu ũthũkĩte ũu?
ŨNDŨ NGAI WASILILE KATĨ
6, 7. Yeova oonanisye ata kana nĩwendete ũsili wa katĩ, na nĩkĩ ũndũ ũsu waĩle kwĩthĩwa wakiakĩisye andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Navothi na anyanyae?
6 Yeova atũmie Eliya ate kwananga ĩvinda athi akaneene na Aavu. Moonana amũtavisye nesa kana aĩ mũaani na kĩng'ei. Kwoou we Yeova amũtw'ĩĩe ata? Aisye kana Aavu, mũka, na ana make makakwatwa nĩ kĩla kyamũkwatie Navothi na ana make.—1 Asu. 21:17-25.
7 O na kau andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Navothi na anyanyae nĩmakwatiwe nĩ kyeva nũndũ wa kĩko kĩu kĩthũku kya Aavu, maiema kwĩthĩwa maakiakiw'a nĩ kũmanya kana Yeova nĩwoona ũndũ ũsu, na kana nĩwoosa ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa matatĩkie mũno nĩ kĩla kyeekĩkie ĩtina wa vau. Mo nĩmesaa kũendeea kwĩkala menyivĩtye na mamwĩkwatĩtye Yeova?
8. Aavu eekie ata ĩla weewie ũsilĩlo wa Yeova, na kwaendie ata ĩtina wa vau?
8 Aavu akililye eew'a ndeto ila Yeova wamũsilĩle nasyo, "atembũanga ngũa syake, na eevw'ĩka makunia mwĩĩ wake, na atĩĩa ũya, na akomea makunia, na aenda eyondetye." Kĩu kĩonany'a ũndũ Aavu weenyivisye. Kwaendie ata eenyivya? Yeova nĩwanengie Eliya ũtũmane ũngĩ amũtwaĩe. Amũtũmie akamũtavye kana nũndũ nĩweenyivya, sila ũla waĩ anamũtw'ĩĩa na nyũmba yake ndũkeanĩa e thayũ. (1 Asu. 21:27-29) Yeova nĩweew'ĩie Aavu tei nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe ũla 'ũtataa ngoo,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nĩwe ũla ũtonya kwona ũndũ ithyĩ tũilyĩ ngoonĩ.—Nth. 17:3.
WĨNYIVYO NŨTŨSŨVĨAA
9. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya kana wĩnyivyo now'o waĩ ũtonya kũsũvĩa mũsyĩ wa Navothi na anyanyae?
9 Andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Navothi na anyanyae meekie ata ĩla mamanyie kana mũsyĩ wa Aavu wesaa kweteelw'a wĩosewa ĩtambya ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kya Aavu? No kwĩthĩwa ũndũ ũsu matataĩĩe watatie mũĩkĩĩo woo mũno. Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vaendie, kĩla kyesaa kũmatetheesya no kwĩkala menyivĩtye. Wĩnyivyo nĩw'o wesaa kũtuma maendeea kũmũthaitha Yeova me aĩkĩĩku na mate na nzika o na vanini kana Ngai woo ndesa kũsila ũsili ũte wa katĩ. (Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 32:3, 4.) Navothi, ana make, na mĩsyĩ yoo makoona ũsili wa katĩ nesa ĩla Yeova wĩĩthĩwa aithayũũkya ala alũngalu. (Yovu 14:14, 15; Yoa. 5:28, 29) O na ĩngĩ, mũndũ wĩnyivĩtye ndolawa kana "Ngaĩ akaete kĩla wĩa ũsilĩlonĩ, vamwe na kĩla ũndũ ũvithĩtwe, ethĩwa nĩ ũseo kana ethĩwa nĩ ũthũku." (Mũta. 12:14) Ũu nĩ kwasya ĩla Yeova ũkũsilĩla mũndũ nũsiasya maũndũ o na ithyĩ tũtesa kũmona. Kwoou wĩnyivyo nũtũsũvĩaa tũikaeke kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova.
10, 11. (a) Nĩ maũndũ ta meva matonya kũtuma twĩthĩwa na woni ũte mũseo ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ? (b) Wĩnyivyo ũkatũtetheeasya ata?
10 We wĩka ata atumĩa makeka ũtwi na ũyĩthĩa ndũnaũelewa kana ndũnetĩkĩlana naw'o? Kwa ngelekany'o, we wĩka ata ũkewa ndwĩendeea kũkwatĩĩa kĩanda kĩna kana o mũndũ wendete akewa ndeendeea kũkwatĩĩa kĩanda kĩna ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova? Nao nata mũemeu kana mũkau, mwanau kana mwĩĩtu waku, kana o mũnyanyau anatengwa na ũyĩthĩa ndũkwĩtĩkĩlana na ũtwi wa atumĩa? Kana wĩka ata atumĩa makony'a tei mũndũ ũvĩtĩtye na we ndũkwona eeaĩlĩte kwonw'a tei? Maũndũ ta asu nĩmatonya kũtuma tũya nzika ĩũlũ wa Yeova na ũseũvyo wake. Wĩnyivyo ũtonya kũũsũvĩa ata ũnakomana na ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ asu? Ekai tũsũanĩe nzĩa ilĩ.
11 Mbee vyũ ethĩwa ve ũndũ weekĩka, wĩnyivyo ũkatumaa twĩtĩkĩla kana ve maũndũ amwe tũtesa kũmanya. Na o na ethĩwa twĩona ta twĩsĩ nesa kĩla kĩendeeie, tũikolwe kana no Yeova e weka ũtonya kũsoma ngoo ya mũndũ. (1 Sam. 16:7) Tũyĩsa kũkananĩsya kĩu. Kũmanya ũu kũkatumaa twĩkala twĩnyivĩtye, twĩkala twĩsĩ kana ve maũndũ tũtesa kũmanya, na kũkatumaa tũvĩndũa mawoni maitũ. Kelĩ, wĩnyivyo ũkatũtetheeasya tũendeee kwĩthĩwa twĩ ewi na twĩ na wũmĩĩsyo. O na ũkatũtetheeasya tweteele nginya ĩla Yeova ũkalũnga maũndũ ethĩwa ve sila ũte wa katĩ ũendeeie. Maũndũ mailea kũthi o tondũ ũla mũndũ mũĩ waandĩkie. Aandĩkie ũũ: "Kũkeethĩwa ũseo kwa ala makĩaa Ngai, . . . ĩndĩ kũtikethĩwa ũseo kwa ũla mũthũku o nake ndakongeleela mĩthenya yake." (Mũta. 8:12, 13) Vate nzika, tweeka maũndũ twĩnyivĩtye ithyĩ ene tũkatetheka vamwe na ala angĩ onthe makonetw'e nĩ ũndũ ũla wĩkĩkĩte.—Soma 1 Vetelo 5:5.
WANGANGANY'O WOONEKIE KĨKUNDINĨ
12. Twĩneenea ngewa yĩva, na nĩkĩ?
12 Ve ũndũ weekĩkie ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa waĩ ĩtatwa kwa Aklĩsto ala maĩ ndũanĩ yaĩ Silia yeetawa Andiokia. Mo nĩmesaa kwĩkala menyivĩtye na nĩmesaa kũekea ala mamavĩtĩsye? Ekai tũneenee ngewa ĩsu na tũyona kĩla tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya vo ĩũlũ wa kũekea. O na nĩkũtũtetheesya tũelewe ũndũ Yeova wonanasya nũsilaa katĩ kwa kũekea ala meeka naĩ.
13, 14. Mũtũmwa Vetelo anengiwe ianda syĩva, na oonanisye ata kana aĩ na ũkũmbaũ?
13 Mũtũmwa Vetelo aĩ mũtumĩa weesĩkĩe mũno kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. Aĩ ũmwe katĩ wa ala matindanasya na Yesũ, na nĩwanengetwe ianda ngito. (Mt. 16:19) Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 36 Vetelo nĩwatũmiwe akatavye Kolinelio na mũsyĩ wake ũvoo mũseo. Ũsu ndwaĩ ũndũ mũnini nũndũ Kolinelio aĩ Mũndũ-wa-mbaĩ-ingĩ ũte mwaĩke. Ĩla Kolinelio na andũ make metĩkĩĩiw'e veva mũtheu, Vetelo aisye atĩĩ: "Ve mũndũ ũtonya kũmavata aa manzĩ, maikavatiswe, ala mosete Veva Mũtheu o taitũ?"—Meko 10:47.
14 Mwakanĩ wa 49 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, atũmwa na atumĩa ala maĩ Yelusaleme nĩmakomanie nĩ kana maoany'e ethĩwa yaĩ lasima Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ, ala matw'ĩkĩte Aklĩsto, maĩkwe. Ũmbanonĩ ũsu Vetelo aneenie na ũkũmbaũ alilikany'a ana-a-asa kana myakanĩ yaĩ navu ĩtina Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ nĩmanengiwe veva mũtheu o na mate aĩke. Ũkũsĩ ũsu wa Vetelo nĩwatetheeisye mũno nzama ĩla ĩtongoesye yĩke ũtwi. (Meko 15:6-11, 13, 14, 28, 29) Ti vinya ũkethĩa Aklĩsto Ayuti vamwe na ala mataĩ Ayuti matanie mũno nũndũ wa ũkũmbaũ wa Vetelo wa kũelesya maũndũ. We nũũ ũla waĩ aemwa nĩ kũĩkĩĩa mũtumĩa ta ũsu waĩ mũima ũu kĩ-veva?—Aevl. 13:7.
15. Vetelo eekie ĩvĩtyo yĩva ĩla waĩ ndũanĩ ya Silia yeetawa Andiokia? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 23.)
15 Vavĩtie o ĩvinda ĩnini kuma ũmbano ũsu weekwa mwaka wa 49 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa na ĩndĩ Vetelo athokea Aklĩsto ala maĩ ĩla ndũanĩ ya Silia yeetawa Andiokia. Avika ndũanĩ ĩsu nĩwatanĩie mũno kũvulana na ana-a-asa ala mataĩ Ayuti. Maiema kwĩthĩwa matethekie mũno nĩ ndambũka ĩsu nũndũ Vetelo aĩ mwana-a-asa wĩ ũmanyi mwingĩ na weeyoneete maũndũ maingĩ. Ĩndĩ makililye matataĩĩe Vetelo akola kũĩsanĩa namo. No nginya kĩu kĩthĩwe kyamatelemilye mũno na kyamatũla ngoo. Kĩko kĩu kya Vetelo nĩkyaaisye Aklĩsto angĩ Ayuti, o na Valanava, mambĩĩa kwĩka take. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie mũtumĩa mũima ta ũsu eka ũtwi mũthũku ta ũsu waĩ ũtonya kũaany'a kĩkundi? Na ĩkũlyo yĩla ya vata vyũ tũtonya kũkũlya nĩ, Ngewa ĩsu ya Vetelo ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ata ĩla mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi waneena kana weeka ũndũ watũũmĩsya?
16. Vetelo akaniw'e ata, na kĩu kĩtuma twĩkũlya makũlyo meva?
16 Soma Akalatia 2:11-14. Vetelo akwatiw'e nĩ kĩtei kya kũkĩa andũ. (Nth. 29:25) O na kũtw'ĩka nĩweesĩ nesa ũndũ Yeova woonaa Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ, nĩwakĩie kwoswa naĩ nĩ Aklĩsto Ayuti ala matembeete kũu maumĩte Yelusaleme nũndũ mo maĩ aĩke. Me o kũu Andiokia, mũtũmwa Vaulo, ũla waĩ vo ũmbanonĩ ũla weekĩwe Yelusaleme mwaka wa 49 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, nĩwakanisye Vetelo menene amũtavya kana ũsu waĩ wangangany'o. (Meko 15:12; Aka. 2:13) Aklĩsto mate Ayuti ala mavathũlilwe nĩ Vetelo mesaa kwĩka ata? Nĩmesaa kwĩtĩkĩla kũlulutĩka? Nake Vetelo nĩwaveniwe ianda syake nũndũ wa ĩvĩtyo yĩu weekie?
EKEAA ALA ANGĨ
17. Vetelo aunĩkie ata nũndũ wa kũekewa nĩ Yeova?
17 Twasisya nesa nĩtwonaa kana Vetelo nĩweenyivisye na eetĩkĩla ũkany'o ũla wanengiwe nĩ Vaulo. Vai vandũ Maandĩkonĩ vonanĩtye kana nĩwaveniwe ianda ila waĩ nasyo. O na ĩtina wa vau nĩwaveveewe aandĩka valũa ilĩ ila syesie kwĩkĩwa Mbivilianĩ. Ve kaũndũ kamwe wawetie valũanĩ wake wa kelĩ kala katwendeeasya mũno. Valũanĩ ũsu eetie Vaulo, "mwana-a-asa waitũ Vaulo, ũla tũmwendete mũno." (2 Vet. 3:15) O na kau ũtwi mũthũku ũla Vetelo weekie nũtonya kwĩthĩwa waũmĩisye Aklĩsto ala mataĩ Ayuti, Yesũ, ũla nĩwe mũtwe wa kĩkundi, ndaaeka kũmũtũmĩa. (Aev. 1:22) Kĩndũ kĩu nĩkyanengie ala maĩ kĩkundinĩ mwanya wa kwĩyĩelekany'a na Yesũ na Ĩthe wake kwa kũekea Vetelo. Twĩĩkwatya kana vai ũmwe woo waaĩtĩkĩla kũlulutĩka nũndũ wa ĩvĩtyo ya mũndũ wĩ na naĩ.
18. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtonya kũtũkwata ũkethĩa twĩ na vata wa kwĩthĩwa na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ?
18 Atumĩa ala me kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto ũmũnthĩ nĩ andũ me na naĩ o ta ala maĩ kĩla kĩkundinĩ kya ĩvinda ya atũmwa. Ũu nĩw'o nũndũ "ithyonthe mavinda maingĩ nĩtũvĩtasya." (Yak. 3:2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) O na kau kĩu nĩ kĩndũ twĩsĩ nesa, thĩna ũlikaa ĩla ithyĩ ene twavĩtĩw'a nĩ mwana-a-asa. Tũkesa kũvĩtĩw'a, no twonany'e twĩ na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ? Kwa ngelekany'o, we wĩka ata ũkew'a mũtumĩa aneena ndeto ikwonany'a nĩ ta ve mbaĩ ĩmwe nzeo kwĩ ila ingĩ? We wĩka kũlulutĩka mũtumĩa akaelya kũneena ũndũ mũna atasũanĩĩte na aikũthatya kana aikũũmĩsya? Vandũ va kũsembea kwasya mwana-a-asa ũsu ndaĩlĩte kũendeea kwĩthĩwa mũtumĩa, we nĩwĩthĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo wĩsĩ kana Yesũ nũkũseũvya maũndũ nũndũ nĩwe mũtwe wa kĩkundi? Vandũ va kũsisya o mavĩtyo make, we no ũtate kũsũanĩa maũndũ maseo, ta myaka mingĩ ĩla mwana-a-asa ũsu wĩthĩĩtwe e mũĩkĩĩku? Mwana-a-asa ũsu ũkũvĩtĩsye akatw'ĩka nũkũendeea kwĩthĩwa e mũtumĩa kana o akatw'ĩka nũkwongelwa ianda ingĩ, we no ũtane vamwe nake? Weethĩwa na veva wa kũekea, ũkoonany'a kana wĩ na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ.—Soma Mathayo 6:14, 15.
19. Twaĩle kũtw'a kwĩka ata?
19 Onthe ala mendete ũlũngalu me na mea ma kwona mũthenya ũla Yeova wĩveta vyũ maũndũ onthe mate maseo ala makwatĩte andũ nũndũ wa Satani na nthĩ ĩno yake nthũku. (Isa. 65:17) Ekai tũendeee kweteela mũthenya ũsu na tũyĩkalaa tũtw'ĩte vyũ kwĩthĩwa na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ. Tũkoonanasya ũu kwa kwĩtĩkĩla kana ve maũndũ tũtesa kũelewa, na kwa kwĩthĩwa twendete vyũ kũekea ala matũvĩtĩsya.
