translation:
"Jehovah's witnesses: . . . The God of kindness and truth."—PS. 32:3, 4.
PARAGRAPH: 15, 2
1, 2. (a) What lesson can we learn from Naboth's experience? (b) Why should we be concerned about justice?
CONSIDER this situation. Imagine someone falsely accuses another of wrongdoing so that he will be punished. His neighbors eagerly spread false reports, wanting the man punished! Every such injustice is a violation of the moral principles that were established by our Creator and are upheld by righteous people. Often, though, the wicked prosper while the innocent suffer along with their families. Let us examine why this is so. This is the story of a loyal man named Naboth who lived in Israel during the reign of King Ahab.—1 Ki. 21:11-13; 2 Ki. 9:26.
2 We can learn much from Naboth's example and come to understand how important it is for each of us to uphold the standards set forth in God's Word. We can also learn from the example of Jehu, and see whether we measure up to Jehovah's requirements in connection with upholding justice, and whether we would act courageously. We will then see why it is vital that we zealously defend Jehovah's laws in connection with upholding justice.
THOSE WHO UPHOLD JUSTICE AND THOSE WHO DO NOT
3, 4. Why did Naboth refuse to give his vineyard to King Ahab?
3 Naboth's vineyard was dear to him, because it had been an inheritance from his ancestors, and it reminded him of Jehovah. Also, Ahab's wife Jezebel hated Jehovah and disregarded His law. She saw Naboth's devotion to Jehovah as an affront to her own worship of Baal. Therefore, she determined to get the vineyard for Ahab.—1 Ki. 21:15-17.
4 Read 1 Kings 21:1-3. When Ahab asked Naboth to give him the vineyard, or offered to give him another vineyard in exchange, Naboth refused. Why? He replied firmly: "Jehovah forbid that I should ask something back from you that my forefathers have possessed." Naboth showed respect for Jehovah's ownership of the land of Israel. Jehovah approves when someone refuses to compromise on what is right. (Ps. 25:23; Prov. 36:7) In effect, Naboth demonstrated that he trusted in Jehovah's ability to protect him.
5. What did Jezebel do to Naboth?
5 The account shows that when Naboth refused to give his vineyard to Ahab, Jezebel arranged for false witnesses to accuse him of blasphemy against God and king. Then she had Naboth stoned to death, and she seized his vineyard so that Ahab could plant a vegetable garden there. Did Jehovah overlook this wicked scheme?
THE MATTER IS SETTLED IN HEAVEN
6, 7. How did Jehovah show that he was aware of the injustice, and how did he cause those involved in Naboth's death and those who supported them to suffer consequences?
6 Jehovah sent Elijah to confront Ahab and denounce him. He told him that dogs would lick up his blood. Do you know why Jehovah said this? Because Ahab, his wife, and his sons would meet a violent end because of their treatment of Naboth and his family.—1 Ki. 21:17-25.
7 And those men of Ahab's city and the nobles were wiped out because of the curse that came upon Ahab's house, proving that Jehovah sees everything and that he will punish wickedness. Indeed, they reaped what they had sown. May we never become complacent and think that Jehovah does not notice our wrong actions!
8. What did Ahab do to show his lack of repentance toward Jehovah, and what happened to him as a result?
8 Ahab humbled himself somewhat, but Jehovah told him through Elijah, "Have you seen how you have provoked me? For the sake of the deed you did, I will bring disaster upon you, and I will wipe away your posterity." This shows Ahab's attitude. What lesson can we learn from this? Jehovah inspired Elijah to go meet Ahab. He instructed him to tell Ahab about the consequences, just as he had spoken to him in his palace. (1 Ki. 21:27-29) Jehovah showed Ahab that he was the One who would carry out this judgment, and that he was the One who could see everything.—Ps. 17:3.
LESSONS FOR US TODAY
9. Why should we be careful not to imitate the wicked example set by Ahab and those associated with him?
9 Did the people associated with Ahab and those connected with him realize the extent to which Ahab's wickedness would lead to disastrous results? No, they did not understand the seriousness of the situation. That is why it is important to remain spiritually alert. Lessons from the past show us what happens when people become complacent.
10, 11. (a) What things might move us to disregard Bible principles? (b) How can lessons from the past help us?
10 Do you ever find yourself minimizing sin or excusing it? For example, do you ever feel inclined to compromise on standards because of pressure from peers or because someone you respect does so? Or perhaps you struggle with secret sins? Do you ever rationalize wrongdoing by telling yourself that others do worse things? These are some of the factors that can cause us to lose our appreciation for Jehovah's standards. What can help us avoid such a decline? Let us examine some examples.
11 Often, when we encounter a situation that challenges our conscience, we may wonder whether there is something wrong with what we are considering. And even if we initially feel unsure, we should remember that Jehovah gives us the ability to discern right and wrong. (1 Sam. 16:7) We need to pray for guidance. Being able to recognize our own weaknesses, being honest about what troubles us, and being willing to examine our motives will help us. Also, let us strive to continue growing spiritually and to rely on God's strength. This will enable us to view matters from Jehovah's perspective. It will also help us to appreciate why certain principles are important. Consider this advice: "Be cautious so that your heart does not entice you to transgress… be cautious so that you do not listen to the entreaties of another." (Prov. 8:12, 13) So, let us carefully examine our thoughts and feelings and then act in harmony with what we know is right.—Read 1 Peter 5:5.
CONSIDER THESE EXAMPLES
12. Why is it important to be humble, and how?
12 In the first century, some Christians in Antioch began associating with non-Jewish believers. Did I find it easy to associate with those who had different backgrounds? Perhaps we can learn from their example and see how they were able to adjust. Also, let us endeavor to understand what Jehovah expects of us when dealing with people from various backgrounds.
13, 14. What assignment did Peter receive, and what questions might he have had?
13 The apostle Peter was given an unusual assignment. He was one of the apostles closest to Jesus, yet he was imperfect. (Matt. 16:19) For instance, in the year 36 C.E., Peter was sent to visit Cornelius and his household. At first, Peter likely wondered why he was being asked to go to the home of a Gentile, because Jews generally avoided close contact with Gentiles. However, when Cornelius and his family showed genuine interest, Peter said: "I truly understand that God does not show partiality, but in every nation the man who fears him and does righteousness is acceptable to him."—Acts 10:47.
14 In the year 49 C.E., just before Christ's ascension, the apostles and others in Jerusalem faced a challenge regarding whether Gentile converts needed to observe the Mosaic Law. Because of this situation, Peter explained what had happened when he visited Cornelius and his household, relating how God had shown that Gentiles were also acceptable to Him. This helped them realize that it was wrong to impose Jewish customs on Gentile believers. Peter's experience taught them a valuable lesson about humility.—Acts 15:6-11, 13, 14, 28, 29. It is vital that all Christians today imitate Peter's willingness to reconsider their views when presented with Scriptural evidence. How can we cultivate such a spirit?—Gal. 13:7.
15. Why did Peter travel to Cilicia and the region around Antioch? (See paragraph 23.)
15 Apparently, Peter made an important journey to Cilicia and the area around Antioch in the year 49 C.E. He went there to report to the apostles about his experiences with Cornelius and the Gentile household. This visit likely served to strengthen the bond between the apostles and fellow believers in those areas. It seems that Peter's explanation was well received, and it helped the brothers appreciate the importance of showing kindness to all people. Peter's travels also gave him opportunities to encourage and comfort those who were facing difficulties. But why does this account emphasize that Peter went "also" to Cilicia and Antioch, rather than simply saying that he traveled to those places? Perhaps it highlights that Peter was actively seeking out opportunities to preach to both Jews and Gentiles, demonstrating his zeal. What lessons can we learn from Peter's example regarding our ministry? And how can we apply the principle illustrated by his actions—that we should be willing to adjust our approach when necessary—in order to reach more people with the good news?
16. What questions may arise, and what will help us to resolve them?
16 Read Acts 2:11-14. Peter was motivated by his desire to reach people. (Prov. 29:25) And he wanted to assure his brothers that Jehovah supports the work of Christians, especially those who, like himself, had gone up to Jerusalem to present their case. From Antioch, the apostle Paul, who also visited Jerusalem in 49 C.E., later confirmed Peter's view, assuring the brothers that Peter did not compromise his principles. (Acts 15:12; 2:13) Did the apostles in Antioch accept Peter's explanation without question? Were they satisfied with his reasoning? Why did Peter feel compelled to explain his conduct to the brothers?
CONSIDER THIS
17. How did Peter demonstrate his loyalty to Jehovah?
17 Let us examine whether Peter truly believed what he explained to the brothers regarding Paul's visit. Some Jewish Christians questioned whether Peter had compromised his standards. But the record shows that he carefully wrote a letter explaining his viewpoint. In that letter, he referred to Paul as "our beloved brother Paul," showing deep respect. (2 Pet. 3:15) Also, he reminded them of the truth about Jesus Christ, the head of the congregation, and how Jehovah has appointed him. (Eph. 1:22) This matter highlights the importance of aligning ourselves with Jesus and his Father when upholding Bible principles. We should be willing to correct our thinking if we realize that we have been influenced by wrong ideas.
18. What can help us to remain firm when faced with pressure from others to lower Jehovah's standards?
18 As Christians, we need to imitate Christ's humility and be considerate of others, rather than being proud and boastful. That is why the apostle James said: "Let many utterances be made." (Jas. 3:2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) However, this does not mean that we should say whatever comes to mind without careful thought. Should we be quick to criticize a brother who makes a mistake? Should we be willing to forgive a brother who offends us, just as Jehovah readily forgives us? For example, would you quickly condemn someone who accidentally damages something valuable? Would you be willing to forgive someone who intentionally harms you or misrepresents you? Those who seek to please God will strive to be forgiving toward a brother who errs, and they will not allow pride to hinder their relationship with Jehovah or with Jesus. Will those who are self-righteous continue to dwell on past mistakes for years? Our beloved brother should encourage us to maintain integrity toward God and also encourage us to improve, or should he simply remind us of our imperfections? Are we willing to accept correction, knowing that Jehovah readily forgives us?—Read Matthew 6:14, 15.
19 How can we show that we are willing?
19 Let us always remember that Jehovah sees our heartfelt desire to remain loyal despite the opposition from Satan and his wicked system. (Isa. 65:17) So let us continue to strengthen our resolve and to demonstrate our loyalty to Jehovah through our words and actions. We can do this by carefully considering what we say and by striving to speak kindly and encouragingly.

text:
"Kũkũsĩĩa ũla ũvoo mũseo wa mumo wa Ngai." —MEKO 20:24.
MBATHI: 10, 25
1, 2. Mũtũmwa Vaulo oonanisye ata kana nĩwatũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mumo wa Ngai?
MŨTŨMWA Vaulo aisye ũũ kuma ngoonĩ: "Mũmo wake [Ngai] nanengiwe ndwaĩ wa mana." (Soma 1 Akolintho 15:9, 10.) Nũndũ Vaulo nĩwathĩnĩtye Aklĩsto tene, nĩweesĩ nesa kana nde ũndũ wathũkũmĩĩte tei wa Ngai, o na tei ũsu wa Ngai ndwamwaĩle.
2 Vaulo akilyĩ kũkw'a aandĩkĩie Timotheo ũũ: "Nĩmũtũngĩa mũvea ũla wandonyethisye, nake nĩ Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ, nũndũ nĩwandalile kwĩthĩwa na kĩthito akĩndw'a wa kũmũthũkũma." (1 Tim. 1:12-14) Anengetwe ũthũkũmi wĩva? Vaulo nĩwawetie ũthũkũmi ũsu nĩ wĩva. Atavisye atumĩa ma kĩkundi kya Eveso ndeto ii: 'Ndiũtala thayũ wakwa ta kĩndũ kwakwa, nĩ kana nĩtonye kwĩanĩsya mũendo wakwa, na ũthũkũmi ũla noosie kwa Mwĩaĩi Yesũ, kũkũsĩĩa ũla ũvoo mũseo wa mumo wa Ngai.'—Meko 20:24.
3. Nĩ ũthũkũmi wĩva wa mwanya wanengetwe Vaulo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 26.)
3 Nĩ "ũvoo mũseo" wĩva Vaulo watavanasya ũla woonanasya mumo wa Yeova? Eeie Aklĩsto ma Eveso atĩĩ: "Nĩmwĩw'ĩte ũvoo wa walan'yo wa mumo wa Ngai ũla nanengiwe kwondũ wenyu." (Aev. 3:1, 2) Vaulo anengetwe kĩanda kya kũtavya andũ ala mataĩ Ayuti ũvoo mũseo nĩ kana o namo meĩthĩwa na Klĩsto Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Masia. (Soma Aeveso 3:5-8.) Nũndũ wa kĩthito kĩla Vaulo waĩ nakyo ũthũkũminĩ wake, we nĩwatiĩe Aklĩsto ma ũmũnthĩ ngelekany'o nzeo na oonany'a kana mumo ũla woonetw'e nĩ Ngai "ndwaĩ wa mana."
MUMO WA NGAI NŨKŨTHANGAASYA?
4, 5. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ' now'o ũvoo mũseo wa "mumo wa Ngai"?
4 Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo andũ ma Yeova nĩmanengetwe wĩa wa kũtavany'a "ũvoo ũũ mũseo wa ũsumbĩ . . . nthĩ yonthe wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe." (Mt. 24:14) Ũvoo ũla tũtavanasya o naw'o nĩ "ũvoo mũseo wa mumo wa Ngai" nũndũ moathimo onthe ala tweteele kwĩsa kũkwata tũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, tũkamakwata no ũndũ wa mumo wa Yeova kwĩsĩla vala ve Klĩsto. (Aev. 1:3) We nũtavanasya na kĩthito ta Vaulo nĩ kana wonany'e nũũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa mumo wa Yeova?—Soma Alomi 1:14-16.
5 Ĩsomo ĩvĩtu nĩyĩtũtetheesye kũmanya ũndũ ithyĩ ta twĩ eki ma naĩ tũtethekaa kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nũndũ wa mumo wa Yeova. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, twĩ na kĩanda kya kwĩkĩa kĩthito ũndũ tũtonya nĩ kana tũtavye andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa wendo wa Yeova na kũmony'a ũndũ matonya kũtetheka nĩw'o. Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva makonetye mumo wa Ngai ala twaĩle kũtetheesya angĩ matũngae mũvea kwondũ wamo?
TAVANY'A ŨVOO MŨSEO ĨŨLŨ WA NTHEMBO YA WOVOSYO
6, 7. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ĩla tũũtavya angĩ ĩũlũ wa wovosyo twĩthĩawa tũitavany'a ũla ũvoo mũseo wa mumo wa Ngai?
6 Andũ aingĩ ala mekalĩte nthĩ ĩno mekaa ũndũ mekwenda na kwoou mayonaa kwĩka naĩ ta ũndũ, na nũndũ wa ũu mayĩsĩ vata wa wovosyo. Ĩndĩ kwĩ angĩ aingĩ mesĩte kũmanya kana kwĩka o ũndũ mo mekwenda kũyĩsa kũmaetee ũtanu wa w'o. Mesa kũneena na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova now'o mamanyaa naĩ nĩ kyaũ, ĩtumĩte tũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna meva, na tũtonya kwĩka ata tume ũkombonĩ wa naĩ. Ala me na ngoo nthalĩku nĩmew'aa mũyo ĩla mamanya kana nũndũ Yeova nũtwendete mũno na e mumo mwingĩ, nĩwatũmie Mwana wake kũũ nthĩ atwovosye kuma ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ.—1 Yoa. 4:9, 10.
7 Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ aiweta Mwana mwendwa wa Yeova: "Nthĩnĩ wake [Yesũ] twĩ na wovosyo witũ kwondũ wa nthakame yake, ũekeo wa mavĩtyo maitũ, kwĩanana na ũthwii wa mumo wake [Yeova]." (Aev. 1:7) Nthembo ya Klĩsto ya wovosyo nĩw'o ũĩkĩĩthyo ũla mũnene vyũ wa kana Ngai nũtwendete, na nĩ wonany'o mũseo wa ũndũ wĩ mumo wingĩvĩte. Nĩ ũndũ wa kũkiakisya kũmanya kana tweethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthakame ya Yesũ ĩla yetĩkiw'e, naĩ sitũ ikaekewa na wasya witũ wa ngoo ũkathew'a! (Aevl. 9:14) We ndũkwona ũsu nĩ ũvoo mũseo twaĩle kũũtavya angĩ?
TETHEESYA ANDŨ METHĨWE NA NGWATANĨO NZEO NA NGAI
8. Nĩkĩ andũ maĩle kwĩw'anĩthw'a na Ngai?
8 Twĩ na kĩanda kya kũtetheesya andũ ala angĩ mamanye kana no methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Mũmbi woo. Andũ matanamba kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ya Yesũ, Ngai amosaa ta amaitha make. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa [kana, ũmũĩkĩĩaa] ũ Mwana e na thayũ ũtathela; ĩndĩ ũla ũtamwĩtĩkĩlaa Mwana ndakona thayũ, ĩndĩ ũthatu wa Ngai wĩkalaa ĩũlũ wake." (Yoa. 3:36) Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana nthembo ya Klĩsto nĩtumaa twĩw'anĩthw'a na Ngai. Vaulo aisye atĩĩ: "Inyw'ĩ, mwekalĩte ĩvinda ya tene mũte na wĩw'ano na mwĩ amaitha ilĩkonĩ syenyu na mĩkĩlenĩ yenyu mĩthũku, ĩndĩ yu nũmwĩw'ĩthanĩtye na mwĩĩ wake [Yesũ] wa nyama kwondũ wa kũkw'a."—Ako. 1:21, 22.
9, 10. (a) Klĩsto anengie ana-a-asa make etĩkĩw'a mauta kĩanda kĩva? (b) Ala "malondu angĩ" matetheeasya ana-a-asa moo etĩkĩw'a mauta ata?
9 Klĩsto nũnengete ana-a-asa make etĩkĩw'a mauta ala me vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ kĩla Vaulo wĩtĩte "ũthũkũmi wa wĩw'anĩthyo." Vaulo nĩwaeleisye kyu nĩ kyaũ ĩla waandĩkĩe Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa ndeto ii: "Ĩndĩ maũndũ onthe nĩ ma Ngai, ũla watwĩw'anĩthye nake mwene kwondũ wa Klisto, na watũnengie ũthũkũmi wa wĩw'anĩthyo; naw'o nĩ ũũ, Ngai aĩ nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto, aimĩw'anĩthya nthĩ nake Klĩsto, aimĩw'anĩthya nthĩ nake mwene, ateũmatalĩla andũ mavĩtyo moo, na nũtwĩkĩĩte nthĩnĩ waitũ ĩla ndeto ya kwĩw'anĩthya. Na ĩndĩno twĩ atũmwa kwondũ wa Klĩsto, o ta Ngai ũnũkwĩsũvanĩla kwitũ: Nĩtũũmwĩsũva kwondũ wa Klisto, mwĩw'anĩthw'e na Ngai."—2 Ako. 5:18-20.
10 Ala "malondu angĩ" monaa ne kĩanda kya mwanya kũtetheesya ana-a-asa moo etĩkĩw'a mauta wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. (Yoa. 10:16) Na nũndũ no twasye nĩmathũkũmaa ta atũmwa kwondũ wa Klĩsto, nĩmo matethasya wĩa ũla mwingĩ nthĩnĩ wa kũmanyĩsya andũ ũw'o na kũmatetheesya methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. Kĩu nĩ kĩlungu kya vata wĩanĩ wa kumya ũkũsĩ ĩũlũ wa ũvoo mũseo wa mumo wa Ngai.
TAVANY'A ŨVOO MŨSEO WA KANA NGAI NĨWĨTHUKĨĨASYA MBOYA
11, 12. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya nĩ ũvoo mũseo kũmanyĩsya andũ kana no mamũvoye Yeova?
11 Andũ aingĩ mavoyaa nũndũ mavoya nĩmew'aa mausya, ĩndĩ maiĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai nĩwĩw'aa mboya syoo. Nĩmaĩlĩte kũmanya kana Yeova nĩwe "ũla wĩw'aa mboya." Mũandĩki wa Savuli, Ndaviti, aandĩkie: "We ũla wĩw'aa mboya, mĩĩ yonthe ĩkooka kwaku. Mothũku nĩmangĩlasya vinya: ũkaekea mavĩtyo maitũ."—Sav. 65:2, 3.
12 Yesũ atavisye amanyĩw'a make ũũ: "Ethĩwa mũkavoya ũndũ o na wĩva syĩtwanĩ yakwa, ngawĩka." (Yoa. 14:14) Vate nzika, "ũndũ o na wĩva" ũla ũwetetwe vau nĩ ũndũ w'onthe ũla wosanĩte na kwenda kwa Yeova. Yoana aeleetye ũũ: "Ũũ nĩw'o ũnyiau ũla twĩ naw'o vala ũĩ, ethĩwa tũkavoya ũndũ kwĩanana na kwenda kwake, nũtwĩw'aa." (1 Yoa. 5:14) Nĩ ũndũ mũseo mũno kũmanyĩsya andũ kana mboya ti kĩndũ kya kũtuma kĩlĩko kĩusya, ĩndĩ nĩ nzĩa ya mwanya ya kũthengeea Yeova 'kĩvĩlanĩ kyake kya ũsumbĩ kya mumo'! (Aevl. 4:16) Twamamanyĩsya kũvoya ũndũ vaĩle, kũvoya ũla waĩlĩte, na kũvoya kĩla kyaĩlĩte, tũkeethĩawa tũimatetheesya mamũthengeee Yeova na maikwata ũkiakisyo ĩvindanĩ ya thĩna.—Sav. 4:1; 145:18.
MUMO WA NGAI ĨVINDANĨ YA NTHĨ NZAŨ
13, 14. (a) Etĩkĩw'a mauta makakwata ndaĩa yĩva ya mwanya ĩvinda yũkĩte? (b) Etĩkĩw'a mauta makathũkũma andũ wĩa wĩva wa ũsengy'o?
13 Mumo wa Yeova wĩendeea kwĩthĩwa kw'o o na ĩtina wa nthĩ ĩno nthũku kwanangwa. Vaulo nĩwawetie ndaĩa ya mwanya ĩla Ngai ũnengete ala 144,000 manyuvĩtwe makasumbĩke na Klĩsto ĩtunĩ Ũsumbĩnĩ wake. Aandĩkie ũũ: "Ngai, nĩkwĩthĩwa aĩ na tei mwingĩ, nũndũ wa wendo wake mũnene ũla watwendie naw'o, o na yĩla twaĩ akw'ũ kwondũ wa mavĩtyo maitũ, atũnengie thayũ vamwe na Klĩsto (nĩmũtangĩĩĩtwe nĩ mumo), naitũ nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ nĩwatũthayũũkisye vamwe nake, na kũtwĩkalya nthĩ vamwe nake ĩtunĩ: nĩ kana mavinda ala mokĩte atonye kwonan'ya ũthwii mwingĩ wa mumo wake kwondũ wa ũseo wake kwitũ nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ."—Aev. 2:4-7.
14 Ti laisi kũsũanĩa maũndũ ma ũsengy'o ala Yeova wiĩe Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ĩla makethĩwa masumbĩkĩte na Klĩsto ĩtunĩ. (Luka 22:28-30; Avi. 3:20, 21; 1 Yoa. 3:2) Aklĩsto asu nĩmo mũno mũno makonw'a nĩ Yeova "ũthwii mwingĩ wa mumo wake." Nĩmo makethĩwa "Yelusaleme mweũ," mũtwawa wa Klĩsto. (Ũvu. 3:12; 17:14; 21:2, 9, 10) Makatetheanĩsya na Yesũ wĩanĩ wa "kũvosya mbaĩ" ĩla makethĩwa mayoneleelya ala ewi kĩla kĩtonya kũmathũmũsya mũio wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ nĩ kana mekale mate na naĩ.—Soma Ũvuan'yo 22:1, 2, 17.
15, 16. Ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte Yeova akoony'a ata "malondu angĩ" mumo wake?
15 Ĩandĩko ya Aeveso 2:7 yaĩtye kana Ngai nũkonany'a mumo wake "mavinda ala mokĩte," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nthĩ nzaũ. Vate nzika, nthĩ nzaũ kũkeethĩwa "ũthwii mwingĩ wa mumo" wa Yeova. (Luka 18:29, 30) Ũndũ ũmwe mũnene Yeova ũkeka vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ onany'e kana e ũseo mwingĩ nĩ kũthayũũkya andũ kuma "Seoli." (Yovu 14:13-15; Yoa. 5:28, 29) Andũ aĩkĩĩku ma tene ala makwie Klĩsto ataumĩtye nthembo yake, vamwe na "malondu angĩ" ala makw'a me aĩkĩĩku ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, makathayũũkw'a maendeee kũmũthaitha Yeova.
16 O na andũ milioni mbingĩ ala makwie matamwĩsĩ Ngai makathayũũkw'a. Makanengwa mwanya wa kwĩnyivĩsya ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova. Yoana aandĩkie ũũ: "Na noona akw'ũ, anene na anini, maũngeme mbee wa kĩvĩla kyu kyeũ; na mavuku mavuanw'a: na ĩvuku yĩngĩ yavuanw'a, nayo nĩ ĩvuku ya thayũ: na ala akw'ũ masilĩlwa na maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe mavukunĩ asu, kwĩanana na meko moo. Na ũkanga waumya akw'ũ ala maĩ nthĩnĩ waw'o; na kĩkw'ũ na [Mbũa] syaumya akw'ũ ala maĩ nthĩnĩ wasyo: na masilĩlwe kĩla mũndũ kwĩanana na meko make." (Ũvu. 20:12, 13) Vate nzika, ala makathayũũkw'a makeethĩwa mayendeka mamanye ũndũ maĩle kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Ngai ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ. O na eka ũu, makeethĩwa no nginya maatĩĩe motao meũ ala me ala "mavukunĩ." Mavuku asu makethĩwa maeleetye ũndũ Yeova ũkwenda andũ mekale me nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ. Kũvuanw'a kwa maũndũ ala me mavukunĩ asu kũkeethĩwa kwĩ wonany'o ũngĩ wa mumo wa Yeova.
ENDEEA KŨTAVANY'A ŨVOO MŨSEO
17. Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kwĩkalaa tũlilikene ĩla tũũtavany'a?
17 O ũndũ mũminũkĩlyo ũthengeee, now'o twĩ na vata mũnene wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ! (Mko. 13:10) Vate nzika, ũvoo mũseo wonanasya kana Yeova e mumo. Twaĩle kũlilikanaa kyu ĩla tũũtavany'a. Kĩeleelo kitũ ĩla tũũtavany'a nĩ kũmũtaĩa Yeova. No twĩke ũu kwa kũtavya andũ kana mawatho ala twathĩtwe ĩla twĩlika nthĩ nzaũ nĩ wonany'o wa ũseo wa Yeova.
18, 19. Tũkumasya mumo ũla Yeova wĩ naw'o ata?
18 Ĩla tũũtavya angĩ ũvoo no tũmaelesye kana ungu wa Ũsumbĩ wa Klĩsto, andũ makakwata moathimo onthe ala maetawe nĩ nthembo ya wovosyo na kana makavetewa naĩ kavola kwa kavola. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Syũmbe nasyo ikathaw'a kuma ũkombonĩ wa wanangĩko, kũlika ũthasyonĩ wa ũtaĩo wa syana sya Ngai." (Alo. 8:21) Keka ti ũseo wa Yeova ũndũ ũsu ndũtonyeka.
19 Twĩ na kĩanda kya mwanya kya kũtavya andũ onthe ala matonya kwĩthukĩĩsya watho ũũ mũseo ki wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Ũvuan'yo 21:4, 5: "[Ngai] akavyaĩa methoi onthe methonĩ moo; na kĩkw'ũ kĩikethĩwa vo ĩngĩ; o na kũikethĩwa ĩngĩ kũmeta, kana kũĩa, kana woo: maũndũ ma mbee nĩ mavĩtu." Na Yeova, ũla wĩkalĩte kĩvĩlanĩ kya ũsumbĩ, aĩtye, "Sisya, nĩngũtw'a maũndũ onthe meũ." Ongelete kwasya, "Andĩka: nĩkwĩthĩwa ndeto ii nĩ sya kĩthito na nĩ sya w'o." Ĩla twatavya angĩ ũvoo mũseo na kĩthito, twĩthĩawa tũikumya mumo ũla Yeova wĩ naw'o!

translation:
"To make full proof of my ministry." —ACTS 20:24.
PAGE 10, 25
1, 2. How did the apostle Paul show that he was eager to preach the good news?
THE apostle Paul wrote truthfully: "The God of all comfort comforted me." (Read 1 Corinthians 15:9, 10.) Paul was very fond of Christ, and he was determined to prove himself worthy of God's trust, and of God's love.
2 Paul later wrote to Timothy: "I am appointed a preacher and an apostle—a teacher of nations." (1 Tim. 1:12-14) What motivated him? Paul explained that his motivation came from the fact that he had once persecuted Christians. He told the elders from the congregation at Ephesus: 'Therefore, be on guard yourselves and be shepherds of the flock of God, to fulfill what our Lord Jesus Christ purchased with his own blood, to make full proof of my ministry.'—Acts 20:24.
3. What kind of motivation did Paul have? (See paragraph 26.)
3 What is this "full proof" that Paul was so anxious to make? Does it mean proving that Jehovah gives life? Yes, the Christians in Ephesus were reminded: "That you may know what is the glorious inheritance of the saints." (Eph. 3:1, 2) Paul felt obligated to travel to all parts of Asia to help them understand how Christ, as the Messiah, could bring about this glorious inheritance. (Read Ephesians 3:5-8.) So, with this conviction, Paul continued to carry out his ministry, knowing that Christ would strengthen him and that God's gift of life is "with power."
IS GOD'S GIFT COMPLETE?
4, 5. How can we determine whether 'the full measure of the sacred secret' is the same as the "gift of life"?
4 In their zealous preaching work, Jehovah's Witnesses have been commissioned to proclaim "this good news of the kingdom . . . in all the inhabited earth." (Matt. 24:14) The message we preach today is also "the gift of life," because it helps people learn about God's Kingdom and how they can obtain everlasting life through Christ. (Eph. 1:3) But why did Paul feel such urgency to help others understand this gift?—Read Romans 1:14-16.
5 Lessons from the past can teach us how important it is to be able to explain things clearly so that people will appreciate the value of God's gift. For example, we need to be able to show how our understanding affects our zeal in sharing the good news and our desire to please Jehovah. Are there aspects of God's gift that we find difficult to explain?
SHARE THE GOOD NEWS WITH URGENCY
6, 7. Why should we strive to share the good news with urgency, knowing that God's gift is precious?
6 Many people are preoccupied with daily concerns and may not realize their spiritual need. They may not see the value of Bible truth. Some may not know how to apply what they learn to their lives. So speak to people about Jehovah now, showing them that he cares for them and that he has provided a way out of trouble. Let them know that Jehovah sent his Son to die for them so that they might be delivered from sin and death.—1 John 4:9, 10.
7 Paul wrote about what motivates us to love God's beloved Son: "By means of him [Jesus] we have redemption through his ransom, the forgiveness of our sins." (Eph. 1:7) Christ's ransom is evidence of God's great love for us, and it shows the importance he places on life. It is something to be deeply grateful for, and we do not want to take it for granted! (Eph. 9:14) So why is it urgent that we share this good news with others?
HELP PEOPLE WHO ARE DISTRESSED BY BAD NEWS
8. Why are people urgently needing to hear from God?
8 We live in a time when many people are distressed by bad news. They need to know whether they are loved by someone who cares for them. Many are responding favorably to the good news about Jesus' ransom, and God wants to show them his mercy. The apostle John writes: "The one who exercises faith in [or, puts faith in] the Son has everlasting life; but the one who does not exercise faith in the Son will not have everlasting life, but the wrath of God remains upon him." (John 3:36) Exercising faith in Christ's ransom is what moves people to respond to God. Paul urges us: "Therefore, brothers, go on walking in harmony with one another and build up one another, just as you are also doing."—Acts 1:21, 22.
9, 10. (a) How did Christ strengthen his followers during times of trial? (b) What "practical things" can help strengthen fellow worshipers during trials?
9 Christ strengthened his followers during times of trial by reminding them of God's love. Paul referred to this strengthening as "fellowship." Paul explained why it is so important when he wrote to Christians facing persecution: "For God is the One who works in you both the willingness and the power to accomplish his purpose. It is God who is working in you, both to will and to act for his pleasure, so that he may demonstrate his favor toward others and cause you to give thanks. And we pray to God through Christ, that he may grant us opportunity to declare his message."—2 Corinthians 5:18-20.
10 Also, "other sheep" were brought into the fold to help shepherd the flock. (John 10:16) And as we have seen, the apostles encouraged fellow Christians to support one another and to strengthen one another with their faith and zeal for Jehovah. This is vital because we live in a time when there is a great need to fortify ourselves spiritually.
TO FORTIFY OUR SPIRITUALITY AND SHOW LOYALTY
11, 12. How can we fortify our spirituality and show loyalty whether people appreciate Jehovah or not?
11 Many people feel discouraged because they see wickedness all around them, and they wonder if God really cares. It is essential to remember that Jehovah *does* care. The psalmist David wrote: "All the earth belongs to him, but he has given the heavens to mankind." He added: "He quiets the storm and makes the waves calm."—Psalm 65:2, 3.
12 Jesus told his followers: "If you ask me something in my name, I will do it." (John 14:14) In effect, "asking something" that is approved by him means making requests that are in harmony with Jehovah's will. John explained: "This is the confidence we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us." (1 John 5:14) It is therefore important to teach others that prayer is not a magical formula, but a way to draw close to Jehovah and express our heartfelt devotion to him! (Acts 4:16) We should pray specifically, pray often, and pray confidently, knowing that Jehovah listens to those who seek him and responds to their sincere prayers.—Psalm 4:1; 145:18.
GOD'S LOVE EMBRACES ALL WHO ARE RIGHTEOUS
13, 14. (a) What does it mean to be righteous in God's eyes? (b) How does this truth encourage us when dealing with imperfect humans?
13 Jehovah's love extends to all who strive to please him and live up to his standards. He has made available the opportunity for salvation to 144,000 faithful Christians who will reign with Christ in heaven. Paul wrote: "God, whom I serve with a clear conscience, . . ., generously gives to all people things they need, both small and great, so that those who love God may be richly provided for through Christ Jesus (who was made alive by God's spirit), and also that we might inherit everlasting life along with Christ Jesus, because God lovingly forgave us our trespasses and kindly wiped out the handwritten record of decrees that stood against us, which held us captive; and he removed it from our path by nailing it to the torture stake!"—Eph. 2:4-7.
14 Let us appreciate the privilege Jehovah gives to Christ of administering the paradise earth. (Luke 22:28-30; Heb. 3:20, 21; 1 John 3:2) Christ himself is the one whom Jehovah designated as having "everlasting life." He is the "new Jerusalem," the capital city of Christ's kingdom. (Rev. 3:12; 17:14; 21:2, 9, 10) By associating with Jesus, we can share in the "conquest" that results in the sanctification of God's name and brings glory to Him, yes, even as the nations come to know and worship Him.—Read Revelation 22:1, 2, 17.
15, 16. How does Jehovah show that he has "other sheep"?
15 The account of Acts 2:7 explains that God considers his people as "sheep without a shepherd," or, more literally, sheep needing a shepherd. These sheep need to be guided to the "everlasting life" that Jehovah provides. (Luke 18:29, 30) One important way Jehovah shows his love is by resurrecting people from "Sheol." (Job 14:13-15; John 5:28, 29) Those faithful ones who have followed Christ will fulfill their vow, and others among those "other sheep" will continue to seek to please Jehovah.
16 But many millions of people do not yet know God and therefore do not yet seek him. They are unaware of the immense value of Jehovah's sovereignty. John wrote: "And I saw, and behold, a white cloud, and upon the cloud one like a son of man; and to him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, so that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed." (Dan. 7:13, 14) These ones who are resurrected will learn to live in harmony with God's righteous laws. And they will also learn to appreciate what Jehovah has done for them. The resurrection will help them to understand Jehovah's purpose. To see how this is possible, let us examine some scriptures. The information in these scriptures will help us to understand why Jehovah values human life.
END TO CONSIDER DANIEL FURTHER
17. Why should we remain confident as we continue to preach?
17 Because we have strong reasons for confidence, we can boldly proclaim the good news of the Kingdom! (Acts 13:10) We are assured that the good news demonstrates that Jehovah lives. We should remain confident as we continue to preach. The reason for our confidence is our desire to honor Jehovah. Let us show this by helping others to learn about the Kingdom, even though some may reject our message. This shows respect for Jehovah's sovereignty.
18, 19. How can we show appreciation for what Jehovah does for us?
18 As we continue to preach, we must remember that the Christian congregation is a spiritual family. Its members are united by love and are willing to support one another. The Bible says: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity!" (Ps. 133:1) Do not take Jehovah's organization for granted.
19 We need to be generous in extending help to fellow believers who may be struggling spiritually. Remember Revelation 21:4, 5: "[God] will wipe out every tear from their eyes; and death will be no more, neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore." And Jehovah, who values worship, says, "I shall certainly give them joy over my people." Furthermore, he says, "Write down: For these words are faithful and true." So as we generously share in this work, we demonstrate our appreciation for what Jehovah does for us!

text:
"Tũngĩai Yeova mũvea; nũndũ nĩ mũseo."—SAV. 106:1.
1. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea?
YEOVA nĩwe umanaa na "kĩla kũnengwa kũseo na kĩla kũnengwa kwĩthĩanu," na nũndũ wa ũu nĩtwaĩle vyũ kũmũtũngĩaa mũvea. (Yak. 1:17) Na nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe Mũĩthi witũ na nũtwendete, nũtwĩanĩasya nesa mavata onthe, ma kĩ-mwĩĩ na ma kĩ-veva. (Sav. 23:1-3) Nĩwĩthĩĩtwe e "wĩvitho witũ na vinya witũ," na mũno mũno ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ! (Sav. 46:1) Kwondũ wa ũu, twĩ na itumi mbingĩ sya kwĩtĩkĩlana vyũ na mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli ũla waisye atĩĩ: "Tũngĩai Yeova mũvea; nũndũ nĩ mũseo; nũndũ ũseo wake wĩ wendo nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene."—Sav. 106:1.
Ĩandĩko yitũ ya 2015: "Tũngĩai Yeova mũvea; nũndũ nĩ mũseo."—Savuli 106:1
2, 3. (a) Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kwona moathimo ala tũkwatĩte ta mate ma vata? (b) Twĩsũngĩa makũlyo meva ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
2 Nĩkĩ tũũneena ĩũlũ wa kũtũnga mũvea? Nũndũ o tondũ kwathanĩtwe, ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo andũ maendeee kwĩthĩwa mate na mũvea. (2 Tim. 3:2) Aingĩ mayonaa moathimo ala makwatĩte ta ma vata mũno. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ maũndũ ma viasala na matangaso ala makonetye viasala nĩmatumĩte andũ milioni mbingĩ masembany'a na syĩndũ, vandũ va kwĩanĩwa nĩ kĩla me nakyo. O naitũ no tũkwatwe nĩ veva ta ũsu. O tondũ mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yeekie, no twĩse kũtw'ĩka andũ mate mũvea na tũyambĩĩa kwona ngwatanĩo ya mwanya ĩla twĩ nayo na Yeova tate ya vata mũno, kana moathimo ala ũtũnengete ta mate ma vata.—Sav. 106:7, 11-13.
3 O na ĩngĩ, kwasũanĩa kĩla kĩtonya kũtũkwata ĩla twakomana na mathĩna maito. Nĩ laisi mũno ĩvindanĩ ta yĩu tũkew'a twaemeewa na tũyũlwa nĩ moathimo ala tũkwatĩte. (Sav. 116:3) Kwoou, kyo nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkalae twĩ andũ me mũvea? Na nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩthĩawe na woni mũseo o na ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ mũito? Ekai twone.
'NĨ MAINGĨ MŨNO MAWĨA MAKU ALA ŨTETHETYE, WE YEOVA'
4. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkalae twĩ andũ me mũvea?
4 Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda twĩkalae twĩ andũ me mũvea, no nginya twĩtĩkĩle kana Yeova nũtũathimĩte na tũisũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa moathimo asu, vamwe na maũndũ angĩ maseo wĩkĩte ala matũĩkĩĩthasya kana nũtwendete. Ĩla mũandĩki wa Savuli weekie ũu, nĩwendeeiw'e mũno nĩ maũndũ maingĩ ma ũsengy'a ala Yeova weekĩte.—Soma Savuli 40:5; 107:43.
5. Ngelekany'o ya mũtũmwa Vaulo yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa kwĩthĩwa na mũvea?
5 Ngelekany'o ya mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩtonya kĩtũmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa kũtũnga mũvea. Nũndũ nĩwatũngaa mũvea mavinda maingĩ, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa asũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala wakwatĩte. Vaulo nĩweesĩ nesa kana mbeenĩ aĩ "mũumi wa Ngai, na mũthĩn'ya wa andũ, na kũmeka naĩ." Ĩndĩ nĩwatũngaa mũvea nũndũ o na kau tene athũkĩte ũu, Ngai na Klĩsto nĩmamwĩw'ĩie ĩnee na mamũnenga wĩa wa mwanya. (Soma 1 Timotheo 1:12-14.) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana Vaulo nĩwoonaa ana-a-asa make me ma vata mũno, na nũndũ wa ũu mavinda maingĩ nĩwamũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa ana-a-asa ta asu aĩkĩĩku na maĩ na nguma nzeo. (Avi. 1:3-5, 7; 1 Ath. 1:2, 3) Na ĩndĩ ĩla wakwatwa nĩ mathĩna na ayona ũndũ ana-a-asa make mamũnenga ũtethyo ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩlĩte, nĩwamũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea saanĩ ũsu. (Meko 28:15; 2 Ako. 7:5-7) Kwoou, ti ũndũ wa ũsengy'o kwona Vaulo ayĩkĩa vinya Aklĩsto akĩmea atĩĩ: "Ĩthĩwai na mũvea . . . , na kũtaana inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ na savuli na mbathi sya kũmũkumya Ngai na mbathi sya veva, mũkĩmwinĩa . . . na mumo [kana, mũvea]."—Ako. 3:15-17.
KŨVOYA NA KŨSŨANĨĨA MAŨNDŨ NĨ KWA VATA
6. Nĩ kyaũ mũno mũno kĩtumaa ũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea?
6 Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana wĩthĩwe mũndũ wĩ mũvea ta Vaulo? Waĩlĩte kũsũanĩĩa maũndũ ala Yeova ũkwĩkĩte o tondũ Vaulo weekaa. (Sav. 116:12) We ũkakũlw'a ũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa moathimo meva katĩ wa ala Yeova ũkũnete, ũsũngĩa ata? We no ũwete ũnyanya wa mwanya ũla wĩ naw'o vamwe na Yeova? Kana no ũwete mwanya ũla wĩ naw'o wa kũekewa naĩ nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ya Klĩsto ya wovosyo? No ũwete masyĩtwa ma ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala maaũkwata kw'oko ĩvinda ya mathĩna? Vate nzika ndũlea kũweta mũemeu kana kĩveti kyaku na syana syaku. Kũsũanĩa moathimo asu maumĩte kũla kwĩ Ĩthe waku wa ĩtunĩ, Yeova, kũkatumaa ũmũtũngĩa mũvea kĩla mũthenya.—Soma Savuli 92:1, 2.
7. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kũvoya mboya sya kũtũnga mũvea? (b) Ũkatetheka ata watũngaa mũvea ĩla ũũvoya?
7 Twekala tũlilikene moathimo ala tũkwatĩte, tũkeethĩawa tũtonya kũmũvoya Yeova twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũmũtũngĩa mũvea. (Sav. 95:2; 100:4, 5) Andũ aingĩ monaa mboya ta nzĩa o ya kũmwĩtya Ngai syĩndũ. Ĩndĩ ithyĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kana Yeova nĩwĩw'aa mũyo ĩla twatũnga mũvea nĩ syĩndũ ila twĩ nasyo. Mbivilia yĩ na mboya mbingĩ nzeo sya kũtũnga mũvea, ta ĩla yaumiw'e nĩ Aana na ĩla yaumiw'e nĩ Esekia. (1 Sam. 2:1-10; Isa. 38:9-20) Kwoou atĩĩa ngelekany'o ya athũkũmi asu aĩkĩĩku ala maĩ na veva wa kũtũnga mũvea. Mũtũngĩae Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa moathimo ala wĩ namo. (1 Ath. 5:17, 18) Weeka ũu ũkakwata moathimo maingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũkekalaa wĩ mũtanu, ũkamwenda Yeova mũnango, na ũkamũthengeea mũnango.—Yak. 4:8.
8. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma twambĩĩa kwona moathimo ala Yeova ũtũnengete ta mate ma vata?
8 Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa twĩ metho tũikaatw'ĩke andũ matatũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa ũseo wa Yeova? Nũndũ tũsyaĩtwe twĩ na veva wa kũlea kũtũnga mũvea. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Asyai maitũ ma mbee, Atamu na Eva, manengiwe mũũnda waĩ mũseo mũno. Kĩla kyonthe maĩ na vata nakyo kyaĩ vo, na maĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene me na mũuo. (Mwa. 1:28) Ĩndĩ mayaaona moathimo asu moo me ma vata. Vandũ va ũu, nĩmakwatiwe nĩ ĩtomo ya kwenda syĩndũ mbingangĩ. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, maaisye kĩla kĩndũ. (Mwa. 3:6, 7, 17-19) O naitũ no twambĩĩe kũlwa nĩ maũndũ ala Yeova ũtwĩkĩte nũndũ tũthyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ andũ matatũngaa mũvea nĩ kĩla me nakyo. No twambĩĩe kwona ũnyanya witũ na Yeova tate ũndũ wa vata mũno. Nĩtũtonya kwambĩĩa kũeka kwona ne ũndũ wa vata kwĩthĩwa twĩ ngwatanĩo na ana-a-asa onthe. O na no twambĩĩe kũsembany'a na maũndũ ma nthĩ ĩno ala makilyĩ manavetwa. (1 Yoa. 2:15-17) Nĩ kana tũikakwatwe nĩ thĩna ũsu, twaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala tũkwatĩte, na ĩvinda yonthe tũimũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũtwĩtĩkĩlya tũtw'ĩke andũ make.—Soma Savuli 27:4.
ĨVINDANĨ YA MATHĨNA
9. Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa moathimo ala twĩ namo ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna maito?
9 Kwĩkalaa twĩ andũ me mũvea nĩkũtonya kũtũtetheesya kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna. No twĩw'e twĩ aemeee mũno ĩla twakwatwa nĩ ũndũ mũmũ ta ũwau ũtonya kũtuma tũkw'a, ĩla twakw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũndũ tũmwendete, ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mũisyo ta kĩthingitho kya nthĩ, kana ĩla mũũme kana mũka witũ wathi nza wa mũtwaano. Kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala twĩ namo ĩla twakwatwa nĩ maũndũ ta asu nĩkũtonya kũtũkiakisya na kũkatwĩkĩa vinya. Ata? Kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa meekĩkie.
10. Irina atethekete ata nũndũ wa kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala ũkwatĩte?
10 Ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Irina * wĩkalaa Amelika. Irina nĩ vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda na aĩ mũtwae nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Ĩndĩ mũũme ũsu wake nĩwaumaalile nza wa mũtwaano na akola Irina vamwe na syana syake. Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Irina aendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova e mũĩkĩĩku? Aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩnĩmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũnzũvĩa. Kũtalaa kĩla mũthenya moathimo ala nĩkwatĩte nĩkũndetheeasya kwona ũndũ ne ũndũ wa mwanya kwĩthĩwa nendetwe na ngĩsũvĩwa nĩ Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ. Nĩnĩsĩ kana ndakaandia." O na kau Irina nũkwatĩtwe nĩ maũndũ me vinya mũno, ala angĩ nĩmew'aa mayakwa nũndũ wake, na ũtanu wake nũtumaa aendeea kwĩthĩwa e na vinya.
11. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtetheetye Kyung-sook omĩanĩsye na ũwau mũthũku?
11 Nake mwĩĩtu-a-asa Kyung-sook ekalaa Asia, na eethĩĩtwe e vainia vamwe na mũũme kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 20. Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwathimiwe na eethĩwa e na kanza nthũku ya mavũi na eewa kana atielye katĩ wa myei ĩtatũ na thanthatũ na aikw'a. O na kau e na mũũme nĩmakwatĩtwe nĩ mathĩna manini na manene, mayaĩ maaĩsa kũsũanĩa kana ũmwe woo no akwatwe nĩ ũwau ta ũsu. Aĩtye: "Neewie ũwau ũsu wambũaa ngoo vyũ. Natelemile mũno, na neew'a ta naasya kĩla kĩndũ." Nĩ kyaũ kĩtetheesye Kyung-sook omĩanĩsye na thĩna ũsu? Easya atĩĩ: "Kĩla mũthenya ndanamba kũkoma nĩendaa kĩalanĩ kya nyũmba yitũ na ngĩvoya na wasya ĩũlũ wa maũndũ atano ala ngũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wamo mũthenya ũsu. Neeka ũu nĩw'aa neanĩwa, na ũu ũituma nenda kwony'a Yeova ũndũ nĩmwendete." Kyung-sook atethekete ata nĩ mboya isu sya wĩoo? Aĩtye ũũ: "Nĩnĩsĩte kũmanya kana Yeova nũtũtetheeasya tũmĩanĩsye na mathĩna, na ngamanya kana moathimo ala twĩ namo nĩ maingĩ kwĩ matatwa ala matũkwataa."
12. Nĩ kyaũ kyamũtetheeisye Jason ĩtina wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũka?
12 Mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Jason, ũla wĩthĩawa ovisinĩ wa ũvonge wa nthĩ ĩmwe ya Africa, ethĩĩtwe e ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 30. Aĩtye ũũ: "Myaka mũonza mĩvĩtu, kĩveti kyakwa nĩkyakwie na ũndũ ũsu wĩ woo mũno. Kũsũanĩa thĩna ũla kyoonie nũndũ wa kanza ĩla kyawaĩte kũtumaa nĩkw'a ngoo mũno." Nĩ kyaũ kĩtetheesye Jason omĩanĩsye na thĩna ũsu? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Sua ũmwe nĩnalilikanile ĩvinda ĩna ĩseo mũno naĩ vandũ nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa. Namũtũngĩie Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũlilikana ĩvinda yĩu. Ũndũ ũsu watumie nĩw'a neanĩwa, na kuma vu nambĩĩa kũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea kĩla ĩvinda nũndũ wa mavinda maseo ala neethĩawa nakyo. Kũtũnga mũvea nĩkũalyũlĩte woni wakwa vyũ. O na kau ũmũnthĩ no nĩw'aa nĩ na kyeva, kũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea nũndũ naĩ na mũtwaano mũseo na nũndũ wa kũnenga mwanya wa kũmũthũkũma na mũndũ wamwendete mũno nĩkũtumĩte nĩthĩwa na woni waĩlĩte."
"Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ Yeova nĩ Ngai wakwa."
13. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Sheryl omĩĩsya ĩla wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ andũ aingĩ ma mũsyĩ?
13 Kamwĩlĩtu ketawa Sheryl kaĩ na myaka 13 ĩvinda yĩla kĩuutani kĩthũku mũno (Super Typhoon Haiyan) kyakũnie kĩsio kĩmwe kya nthĩ ya Philippines mũthyanĩ wa mwaka wa 2013. Ĩvinda yĩu Sheryl aaisye vakuvĩ kĩla kĩndũ. Easya: "Nyũmba yitũ yaanangĩkie vyũ na andũ aingĩ maitũ makw'a." Inyia, ĩthe, na ainae atatũ nĩmooaiwe nĩ kĩuutani kĩu. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumĩte Sheryl omĩĩsya mũisyo ũsu e o mũtanu? Nĩ kũtũngaa mũvea na kwĩkalaa alilikene moathimo ala ũkwatĩte. Easya atĩĩ: "Nĩnoonie ũndũ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa matataa maetee ũtethyo ala maĩ na thĩna na maimekĩa vinya. Nĩneesĩ ana-a-asa nthĩ yonthe nĩmamboyeaa." Aminĩie kwasya: "Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ Yeova nĩ Ngai wakwa. Ĩvinda yonthe nũtũnengae kĩla twĩ na vata nakyo." Vate nzika twekala tũililikana moathimo ala tũkwatĩte, tũikaaemeewa nĩ kyeva. Na twekala twĩ andũ me mũvea, tũikaaemeewa o na twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna mailyĩ ata.—Aev. 5:20; soma Avilivi 4:6, 7.
"NYIE NGATANA NTHĨNĨ WA YEOVA"
14. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva mũseo tweteele? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
14 Ĩvinda yonthe athũkũmi ma Yeova nĩmatanaa nũndũ wa moathimo ala makwatĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩla Aisilaeli mavonokie kuma mokonĩ ma Valao na ita syake me Ũkanganĩ Mũtune, nĩmamwinĩie Ngai mbathi nzeo sya kũmũkatha na kũmũtũngĩa mũvea nũndũ wa ũtanu ũla maĩ naw'o. (Kuma 15:1-21) O naitũ ũmũnthĩ twĩ na moathimo maingĩ twendete vyũ, na ũathimo ũmwe katĩ wa asu nĩ wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũvetewa maũndũ onthe ala matumaa tũthĩna. (Sav. 37:9-11; Isa. 25:8; 33:24) Kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla tũkew'a ĩla Yeova ũkananga amaitha make vyũ, na aitũthokya tũlike nthĩ nzaũ yĩ na mũuo na ũlũngalu! Mũthenya ũsu mwa tũkatũnga mũvea ta kĩ!—Ũvu. 20:1-3; 21:3, 4.
15. Ũtw'ĩte kwĩka ata mwakanĩ wa 2015?
15 Nĩtweteele mũno kũathimwa nĩ Yeova mwakanĩ wa 2015. Nĩ w'o, tũiema kũkwatwa nĩ matatwa. Ĩndĩ o na twakwatwa nĩ kyaũ, nĩtwĩsĩ kana Yeova ndakaatũtia nongi. (Kũt. 31:8; Sav. 9:9, 10) Akatũnengae kyonthe kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmũthũkũme twĩ aĩkĩĩku. Kwondũ wa ũu, ekai tũtw'e kwĩthĩwa na woni ta ũla waĩ na mwathani Avakuki. Aisye atĩĩ: "O na ethĩwa mũkũyũ ndũkalaũka, o na mĩsavivũ ndĩkasyaa; wĩa wa mũthata ũkethĩwa wa mana; na mĩũnda ndĩkasyaa lĩu; ndĩthya sya mbũi na malondu ikavetwa kyengonĩ, na vaikethĩwa ndĩthya sya ng'ombe itũũnĩ: ĩndĩ nyie ngatana nthĩnĩ wa Yeova, ngatanĩa Ngai wa ũtangĩĩo wakwa." (Ava. 3:17, 18) Ĩĩ, ekai mwakanĩ ũũ ũkĩte twĩkale tũisũanĩa na ngoo syĩ na ũtanu ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala twĩ namo, na nũndũ wa ũu tũyĩka o tondũ ĩandĩko yĩĩ ya mwaka wa 2015 yaĩtye: "Tũngĩai Yeova mũvea; nũndũ nĩ mũseo."—Sav. 106:1.
^ kal. 10 Masyĩtwa amwe kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ nĩ mavĩndũe.

translation:
Praise Jehovah generously; for his loving-kindness is forever.—PS. 106:1.
1. How can we praise Jehovah generously?
JEHOVAH is the One who gives "every good gift and every perfect present," and so we have much reason to praise him generously. (Jas. 1:17) And he is our Shepherd and sustains us, comforts us during distressing times, both old and new. (Ps. 23:1-3) He is truly "our refuge and strength," and how grateful we should be! (Ps. 46:1) Therefore, we have many reasons to associate with the psalmist who wrote: "Praise Jehovah generously; for his loving-kindness is forever; his loving-kindness will endure forever." —Ps. 106:1.
Our 2015 text: "Praise Jehovah generously; for his loving-kindness is forever."—Psalm 106:1
2, 3. (a) Why should we examine the examples that help us to show appreciation? (b) What new features will this publication contain?
2 Why do we need to cultivate generosity? Because despite their imperfections, faithful Christians continue to show appreciation. (2 Tim. 3:2) Many face difficult circumstances. Why? Often because they uphold righteous standards and refuse to compromise, influencing millions to live by moral principles and to seek truth. Or we might be affected by personal trials. So let us learn from the example of ancient Israel, and let us strive to remain appreciative of the relationship we have with Jehovah and avoid taking it for granted—Ps. 106:7, 11-13.
3 Also, regularly considering individual instances helps us to cope with difficulties. It is often comforting to recall times when we were answered in prayer and comforted during trials. (Ps. 116:3) Indeed, what can motivate us to remain close to those who are generous? And what can motivate us to be more concerned about showing appreciation? Let us see.
'MANY GOOD THINGS YOU HAVE DONE, O JEHOVAH'
4 What can motivate us to remain close to those who are generous?
4 As we associate with generous people, we will likely imitate them, and we will come to appreciate that Jehovah blesses those who are liberal, along with other qualities that please him. The psalmist David experienced this, and he expressed his deep gratitude to Jehovah for his goodness.—Read Psalm 40:5; 107:43.
5 How does Paul's example teach us about appreciating generosity?
5 Paul's example teaches us much about being appreciative. Although he had many opportunities to benefit from the generosity of others, he was always grateful for the kindness shown to him. Paul readily acknowledged that he was "God's slave, an apostle of Christ Jesus." He knew that God and Christ were supporting him. (Read 1 Timothy 1:12-14.) Furthermore, Paul realized that despite his past imperfections, Jehovah continued to show him favor. (Acts 1:3-5, 7; 1 Thessalonians 1:2, 3) And even when he was imprisoned and faced difficulties, he continued to be thankful to Jehovah for the support he received from fellow believers. (Acts 28:15; 2 Corinthians 7:5-7) So, like Paul, let us also remember what Christ said: "Keep on being generous . . . , and lend without expecting anything in return, so that Jehovah may reward you, and the life of your soul may be abundant."—Acts 3:15-17.
TO SHOW AND EXPRESS APPRECIATION IS IMPORTANT
6. What important reason should motivate us to be appreciative of Jehovah?
6 Are you willing to imitate Paul's example and express gratitude? Consider how Jehovah has blessed you, just as he blessed Paul. (Psalm 116:12) Would you enjoy strengthening your relationship with Jehovah by showing appreciation? Do you want to experience the joy of being closely united with Jehovah? Or do you desire to have a greater share in fulfilling the ministry of proclaiming the good news? Do you feel motivated to use your gifts and abilities to serve Jehovah? Take time to reflect on this personally. Expressing heartfelt gratitude will draw you closer to Jehovah—the One who deserves our praise.—Read Psalm 92:1, 2.
7. (a) How can we show more appreciation? (b) What can help us to be more appreciative?
7 Let us regularly think about what Jehovah does for us so that we can gratefully show our love for him. (Psalm 95:2; 100:4, 5) Many people find it difficult to express their feelings toward God. Sometimes we may wonder whether Jehovah truly values our expressions of appreciation. The Bible shows that there are many ways to show appreciation, such as those used by Hannah and Hezekiah. (1 Samuel 2:1-10; Isaiah 38:9-20) How did they demonstrate their thankfulness? Be generous in expressing your gratitude to Jehovah for his blessings. (1 Thessalonians 5:17, 18) This will bring you great joy. For instance, you might spend five minutes each day meditating on Jehovah's goodness and telling him how you feel.—James 4:8.
8. What can help us to focus on the blessings Jehovah gives us despite difficulties?
8 How can we train ourselves to notice the good things that others do in supporting Jehovah's work? We need to cultivate the habit of looking for reasons to be grateful. Consider this example: Our first parents, Adam and Eve, were given a beautiful garden. They had everything they needed, and they could enjoy life forever. (Genesis 1:28) But they focused on what they lacked. Because of their disobedience, they suffered many hardships. (Genesis 3:6, 7, 17-19) So let us not allow ourselves to be influenced by those who are ungrateful, but instead concentrate on what Jehovah provides for us. Let us also cherish our relationship with Jehovah and not take it for granted. We can learn to appreciate even small blessings and not compare them unfavorably with what others have. Also, let us avoid being preoccupied with material possessions. (1 John 2:15-17) If we become obsessed with wealth, we will find it harder to focus on the blessings we already have and to continue showing our gratitude to Jehovah by helping others.—Read Psalm 27:4.
THE IMPORTANCE OF GRATITUDE
9. How can we train ourselves to be grateful even when facing difficulties?
9 To remain positive when experiencing trials, we need to associate with people who are optimistic. We should also try to see the good side of bad situations, such as when we make a mistake, when someone disappoints us, when we face an unexpected challenge, or when a family member causes us grief. Being able to focus on the positive aspects of difficult circumstances helps us to cope and to maintain hope. Why? By focusing on the good, we strengthen our faith.
10. What can help us to train ourselves to be more grateful?
10 There is a sister named Irina who lives in America. Irina makes it a point to express gratitude daily and she encourages her children to do the same. Her husband passed away unexpectedly, and Irina and her children supported each other. What helped Irina to continue serving Jehovah faithfully? She explains: "I always remind myself that I am blessed to know the truth. Taking time each day to think about the blessings I have received helps me to appreciate what I have and to feel comforted by our loving Father. I am determined to stay focused." Despite facing many challenges, Irina has remained steadfast in her determination, and her faith continues to motivate her to persevere.
11. What helped Kyung-sook to remain optimistic during a difficult time?
11 Sister Kyung-sook lived in Asia, and she experienced hardship along with her family for over 20 years. One experience involved being imprisoned and subjected to severe interrogation for several days and nights. And although she and her family faced great trials and tribulations, they maintained their loyalty to God. She says: "My husband really encouraged me a lot. I was very grateful, and he helped me to endure everything." What helped Kyung-sook to maintain her optimism? She explains: "Each day I would force myself to clean our house and organize things so that I could focus on just one thing for that day. This gave me some relief, and it helped me to turn to Jehovah in prayer." Did Kyung-sook ever feel discouraged? She states: "I often wondered if Jehovah would help us through our trials, and I wondered if we had done enough to deserve his help."
12. What helped Jason cope with imprisonment?
12 A young man named Jason, who grew up in a war-torn country in Africa, spent most of his youth in prison for over 30 years. He says: "For many years, I felt that my life was meaningless and without purpose. Maintaining my faith helped me to survive those difficult times." What helped Jason to maintain his faith? He explains: "One time I shared my experiences with a fellow prisoner who showed me kindness. I began to pray to Jehovah regularly, asking him to help me endure my imprisonment. This brought me some relief, and it motivated me to continue praying to Jehovah during all my remaining years in prison. Praying helped me to stay connected to him. And even though that brother also faced difficulties, praying to Jehovah regularly and maintaining his integrity despite the challenges he faced helped me greatly.
"This strengthened my conviction that Jehovah is my God."
13. What helped Sheryl to cope when disaster struck her family?
13 A teenager named Sheryl experienced a devastating super typhoon (Haiyan) that hit the Philippines in November 2013. The typhoon took everything from Sheryl's family. She said: "Our house was completely destroyed, along with so many others." Thankfully, she and her parents and younger siblings survived the storm. What helped Sheryl to cope with this tragedy? It was her spirituality and her close relationship with Jehovah. She states: "I realized how precious life is and how important it is to value our loved ones. I prayed to Jehovah for strength." She added: "I know that Jehovah is my God. Everything we have, we owe to Him." Let us remember that when we face trials, we can find comfort in prayer. And let us be united with others in worship, knowing that we are not alone in our suffering.—Rev. 5:20; read Proverbs 4:6, 7.
"HOLD FAST TO JEHOVAH"
14. What lesson can we learn from this? (See paragraph 8.)
14 Throughout history, Jehovah's servants have faced trials. For example, when the Israelites were about to enter the Promised Land, they remembered God's deliverance from Egypt and trusted in Him to help them conquer their enemies. (Numbers 15:1-21) Often, we too experience many difficulties, and sometimes one particular trial seems overwhelming. (Ps. 37:9-11; Isa. 25:8; 33:24) So, let us always remember what Jehovah does for us and appreciate his love and loyalty! How grateful we are that he helps us to cope!—Job 20:1-3; 21:3, 4.
15. What will we discuss in 2015?
15 We will focus on showing our appreciation to Jehovah in 2015. Yes, we want to remain steadfast despite challenges. If we face problems, we will trust that Jehovah will strengthen us. (Prov. 31:8; Ps. 9:9, 10) He will enable us to witness and to continue preaching. To this end, let us be encouraged by the words of Ezekiel and his fellow exiles. Ezekiel said: "And I myself also became their watchman, and I heard from them concerning my voice, saying, 'Your words are becoming a delightful song,' and they kept listening willingly. But they did not act according to my words, nor did they do any of those things that I had spoken to them.' Therefore, hold fast to Jehovah, and do not turn away from your God." (Ezek. 3:17, 18) Thus, during this year, may we stay close to Jehovah and enjoy the peace that comes from obedience, and may we resolve to make the theme for 2015 meaningful: "Keep Searching for Jehovah; Keep Talking About Him."—Ps. 106:1.

"Mũikolwe nĩ kũmon'ya aenĩ wendo."—AEVL. 13:2.
MBATHI: 50, 25
1, 2. (a) Nĩ mathĩna meva aeni aingĩ makomanaa namo ũmũnthĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Mũtũmwa Vaulo alilikanilye Aklĩsto ũndũ wĩva, na ũndũ ũsu umĩlĩtye makũlyo meva?
MBEE wa myaka 30 mĩvĩtu, Osei, [1] ũla ũtaĩ Ngũsĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu, nĩwavikie Europe aumĩte Ghana. Aĩtye ũũ aililikana ĩvinda yĩu: "Ĩla navikie nĩnoonie kana andũ aingĩ mayaũnganaa nakwa. O na nzeve ya kũu yambie kũndelemya. Numĩte kĩwanzanĩ kya ndeke neewie mbevo mbingĩ ndaaĩw'a nginya nambĩĩa kũĩa." Nũndũ Osei ndeesĩ kĩthyomo kya kũu nesa, aminie mbee wa mwaka ũtakwata wĩa mũseo. Na nũndũ aĩ vaasa na andũ moo, eew'aa ta wĩ weka na eew'aa e na mea ma kũsyoka kwoo.
2 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũtonya kwenda ala angĩ makwĩke ũkesa kwĩyĩthĩĩla thĩnanĩ ta ũsu wamũkwatie Osei. Tyo wĩw'e mũyo ũkathokw'a nesa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, o na kũtw'ĩka wĩ wa nthĩ yĩ kĩvathũkany'o kana wĩ wa langi wĩ kĩvathũkany'o? Mbivilia nĩthuthĩtye Aklĩsto ma w'o ĩkamea atĩĩ: "Mũikolwe nĩ kũmon'ya aenĩ [kana, ekali ma ũeninĩ] wendo." (Aevl. 13:2) Nũndũ wa ũu ekai tũneenee makũlyo aa: Yeova onaa aeni ata? Nĩkĩ vatonya kwĩthĩwa vata wa kũalyũla woni witũ ĩũlũ wa aeni? Na tũtonya ata kũtetheesya ala maumĩte nthĩ ingĩ mew'e ta me mũsyĩ ĩla me kĩkundinĩ kitũ?
ŨNDŨ YEOVA WONAA AENI
3, 4. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Kuma 23:9, Ngai endaa Aisilaeli makue aeni ata, na nĩkĩ?
3 Ĩtina wa Yeova kũkomboa andũ make kuma Misili, nĩwamanengie mĩao yamonetye ũndũ maaĩle kwĩkalany'a nesa na andũ mate ma mbaĩ yoo ala maumanĩtye namo kũu. (Kuma 12:38, 49; 22:21) Nũndũ kaingĩ andũ ala me ũeninĩ monaa ĩvinda yetu, Yeova nĩweekie mĩvango nĩ kana mekale me asũvĩĩku. Mũvango ũmwe waĩ kũmanenga mwanya wa kũkolany'a ũsyao ũla watiala mĩũndanĩ.—Ali. 19:9, 10.
4 Vandũ va kũmalasimĩthya Aisilaeli manenge aeni ndaĩa, Yeova endaa maelewe ũndũ mekwĩw'a. (Soma Kuma 23:9.) Nĩkĩ? Nĩkwĩthĩwa Aisilaeli 'nĩmeesĩ ngoo ya mwĩkali wa ũeninĩ,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nĩmeesĩ ũndũ mũndũ wĩw'aa e ũeninĩ. Na kĩtumi nũndũ o na matatw'ĩkĩthĩtw'e ngombo nĩ Amisili, nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa makuawa naĩ nĩmo nĩkwĩthĩwa maĩ ma mbaĩ yĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ndĩni yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. (Mwa. 43:32; 46:34; Kuma 1:11-14) O na kau Aisilaeli nĩmathĩnie mũno ĩvindanĩ yĩu maĩ aeni Misili, Yeova amendaa makue aeni ala maĩ katĩ woo 'ta ala masyaawa' mbaĩnĩ yoo.—Ali. 19:33, 34.
5. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmathĩnĩkĩe andũ kuma nthĩ ingĩ o tondũ Yeova wĩkaa?
5 O ta ũu, nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kana ũmũnthĩ Yeova nũthĩnĩkĩaa andũ ala mooka ikundinĩ sitũ maumĩte nthĩ ingĩ. (Kũt. 10:17-19; Mal. 3:5, 6) Twatata kũmanya mathĩna ala andũ asu makomanaa namo ta kũvathwa nĩ ala angĩ, kana kwĩthĩwa matesĩ kĩthyomo kitũ nesa, tũilea kũmantha ũndũ tũũmeka ũseo na kũmony'a kana nĩtũkũelewa ũndũ mekwĩw'a.—1 Vet. 3:8.
WE NŨKWONA WĨ NA VATA WA KŨALYŨLA WONI WAKU ĨŨLŨ WA AENI?
6, 7. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkwonany'a kana Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa nĩmeemanyĩĩtye ũndũ matonya kwĩka maikethĩwe na kĩmena?
6 Ayuti nĩmamenete mũno andũ mate ma mbaĩ yoo, ĩndĩ Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa nĩmeemanyĩĩtye ũndũ matonya kwĩka maikekale tamo. Ĩvinda ya Vendekosito ya mwaka wa 33, Aklĩsto ala mekalaa Yelusaleme nĩmoonisye wendo ala matw'ĩkie Aklĩsto ĩvinda yĩu o na kũtw'ĩka maumĩte mbaĩnĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. (Meko 2:5, 44-47) Nũndũ wa kũmathĩnĩkĩa Aklĩsto ma mbaĩ ingĩ, Aklĩsto asu Ayuti moonanisye kana nĩmeesĩ kĩla kyonanaw'a nĩ ndeto ii, "kũmon'ya aenĩ wendo."
7 Ĩndĩ kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kĩendeee kwĩana nĩvaumĩlile thĩna. Ayuti ala maneenaa Kĩkiliki nĩmambĩĩe kũnyungunyĩsya mayasya kana aka moo ndiwa mayakuawa ta ala angĩ. No kwĩthĩwa thĩna ũsu waumĩlĩte nũndũ maĩ ma mbaĩ yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. (Meko 6:1) Nĩ kana atũmwa mamine thĩna ũsu, nĩmanyuvie aũme mũonza nĩ kenda maĩkĩĩthye vai mũndũ ũnavathũlwa. Aũme onthe ala manyuviwe maĩ na masyĩtwa ma Kĩkiliki. No kwĩthĩwa atũmwa manyuvie aũme asu me na wumo wa Kĩkiliki nĩ kana thĩna ũla waĩ katĩ wa Aklĩsto asu ma mbee ũoleke.—Meko 6:2-6.
8, 9. (a) Tũtonya kũmanya ata kana twĩ na kamena ke vandũ kwelekela andũ ana kana nĩ ta tũkwona mbaĩ yitũ tayo nzeo kwĩ iingĩ? (b) Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kũveta vyũ ngoonĩ sitũ? (1 Vet. 1:22)
8 Maũndũ maingĩ tũkothaa kwĩka tũmekaa tũatĩĩe kĩthĩo kitũ, twĩthĩwe twĩkaa ũu twĩsĩ kana twĩkaa tũtesĩ. (Alo. 12:2) O na mavinda angĩ nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa twĩw'aa atũi, kana ala tũthũkũmaa namo, kana o ala tũsomaa namo maivũthya andũ ma wumo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o, mbaĩ yĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kana o langi wĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwoou nũseo tũkekũlya-ĩ, 'Nĩtwĩthĩwa tũlikĩtwe mũno nĩ kĩthĩo kitũ vamwe na mawoni ala andũ methĩawa namo ĩũlũ wa andũ mate ma kwoo? Na twĩw'aa ata ĩla mũndũ watũthekeea nũndũ wa wumo witũ, kana watata kumany'a kĩthĩo kĩna kya mbaĩ yitũ?'
9 Ve ĩvinda mũtũmwa Vetelo wavathaa ala mate Ayuti, ĩndĩ nĩwesie kũveta o kavola mawoni mathũku ala waĩ namo ngoonĩ. (Meko 10:28, 34, 35; Aka. 2:11-14) Kwoou tũkaelya kwĩsa kwĩthĩa nĩ ta twĩ na kamena ke vandũ kwelekela andũ ana, kana nĩ ta tũkwona mbaĩ yitũ tayo nzeo kwĩ iingĩ, twaĩlĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ mũno tũvete kĩndũ kĩu ngoonĩ. (Soma 1 Vetelo 1:22.) Kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya nĩ kũvindĩĩsya ũndũ ũũ: vai o na ũmwe witũ ũtonya kwasya no nginya etangĩĩwa. Nĩkĩ? Nĩkwĩthĩwa ithyonthe twĩ ene naĩ o na twĩthĩwe tumĩte va. (Alo. 3:9, 10, 21-24) Kwoou ve vata mwaũ wa kwona ta twĩ aseo kwĩ andũ amwe? (1 Ako. 4:7) Woni witũ waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa ũilyĩ o ta ũla mũtũmwa Vaulo waĩ naw'o. Ĩvinda yĩmwe aandĩkĩie Aklĩsto angĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta valũa amathangaasya aimea ũũ: "Mũti aeni na avĩti ĩngĩ, ĩndĩ mwĩ . . . andũ ma nyũmba ya Ngai." (Aev. 2:19) Kũng'ang'ana mũno twambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa andũ ma mbaĩ ingĩ kũkatũtetheesya twĩvw'ĩke ũla mũndũ mweũ.—Ako. 3:10, 11.
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KŨMONY'A AENI WENDO
10, 11. Mboasi oonanisye ata kana aĩ na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa andũ ala me ũeninĩ?
10 Ũla mũndũ mũĩkĩĩku weetawa Mboasi aĩ na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa andũ ala me ũeninĩ. Ũu nĩw'o twasisya ũndũ wakuie ũla mũndũ mũka wa Moavi weetawa Luthi. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe Mboasi nĩwaendie kũoa mũũnda wake ĩvinda ya ngetha na avika vau nĩwoonie mũndũ mũka ũte Mũisilaeli e na kĩthito kingĩ mũno kya kũkolany'a ũsyao ũla akethi matia ĩtina. Ĩla Mboasi wamanyie atĩ mũndũ mũka ũsu ambie kwĩtya mwanya wa kũkolany'a ũsyao mũũndanĩ, o na kau mwĩao waĩ vo wamwĩtĩkĩlĩtye kũkolany'a kĩla kyatialw'a, eewie mũyo nginya atavya athũkũmi mamũsumũlĩle iia imwe syovenĩ nĩ kana aikolany'e.—Soma Luthi 2:5-7, 15, 16.
11 Ngewa ĩla Mboasi waeie e na Luthi ĩtina wa vau nĩtumaa twona ũndũ Mboasi wathĩnĩkaa asũanĩa thĩna ũla Luthi ũkwona nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa e mũeni nthĩ ĩsu. Mbee ambie kwĩa Luthi nathi vakuvĩ na athũkũmi make ma eĩtu nĩ kana ndakathĩnw'e nĩ aũme ala mathũkũmaa vau mũũndanĩ. Na eka ũu, atiie amanya kana Luthi nĩwanengwa kĩw'ũ na lĩu ũmwĩanĩte o tondũ ala aandĩke manengawe. Na ĩndĩ o na kau Luthi aĩ mũeni na ngya, Mboasi ndaamũneeny'a na kĩvũthya ĩndĩ aneenie nake kwa nzĩa ĩkũmwĩkĩa vinya.—Luthi 2:8-10, 13, 14.
12. Kwĩka nesa aeni ala maumĩte kũndũ kũngĩ kũtonya kũmatethya ata?
12 Kĩndũ kĩmwe kyendeeisye Mboasi nĩ kwona ũndũ Luthi wendete inyia wa mũũme na ngoo yonthe, o na nĩwakiitiwe ngoo amanya kaĩ nĩwatw'ĩte kũmũthaitha Yeova! Ũseo ũla Mboasi woonisye Luthi ũtumaa twona ũndũ Yeova wendete mũndũ mũka ũsu mũno wĩana nũndũ wa 'kwĩvitha nthwaunĩ sya Ngai wa Isilaeli.' (Lu. 2:12, 20; Nth. 19:17) Twaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Mboasi kwa kwĩka "andũ onthe" ũseo, tũkatuma mona ũla w'o na tũkatuma mamanya kana Yeova nũmendete mũno.—1 Tim. 2:3, 4.
13, 14. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũtata mũno tũkethasye aeni ala mooka Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtethya ethĩwa nũemawa nĩ kũea ngewa na mũndũ wa mbaĩ ĩngĩ?
13 Nzĩa ĩmwe ya kwĩka nesa aeni ala maumĩte kũndũ kũngĩ nĩ kũmakethya wĩ mũtanu ĩla wamona Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ. No kwĩthĩwa wonete kana aeni ala mooka nĩmakothaa kwĩthĩwa na nthoni na nĩmaemawa nĩ kũlikana na andũ ala angĩ. No kwĩthĩwa aeni asu masũanĩa mũeele woo kana kĩlasi kyoo mew'aa me vathei meeyĩelekany'a na angĩ ma ũko wĩ kĩvathũkany'o kana nthĩ ĩngĩ. Kwoou nũseo tũkosa ĩtambya ya mbee ne ithyĩ nĩ kana tũmony'e nĩtũkwendeew'a nĩmo kuma ngoonĩ. Ethĩwa kĩthyomonĩ kyenyu mwĩ na ĩla vulongulamu ya JW Lugha, no ũmĩtũmĩe ĩũtetheesye kũmanya ũndũ ũtonya kũkethya aeni na kĩthyomo kĩla kyoo.—Soma Avilivi 2:3, 4.
14 Nũtonya kwĩw'a ũiemwa nĩ kũea ngewa na mũndũ wa mbaĩ ĩngĩ. Wenda ũeke kwĩw'a ũu no ũtate kũmũtavya ũndũ mũna ĩũlũ waku we mwene. Weeka ũu ndũlea kwĩthĩa vala mũvathũkanĩe nĩ vanini mũno waelekany'a na maũndũ ala mũtuteny'e. Na ndũlea kwĩthĩa kana kĩla kĩthĩo kĩ ũseo wakyo na ũthũku wakyo.
MATETHEESYE MEW'E TA ME MŨSYĨ
15. Ethĩwa ve aeni meũtata kũmanyĩa kwĩkala kũla twĩkalaa, nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmaelewe?
15 Nĩ kana ũtetheesye aeni ala me kĩkundinĩ kyenyu mew'e ta me mũsyĩ, ĩkũlye ĩkũlyo ta yĩĩ, 'Takethĩwa ninyie nĩthamĩĩe nthĩ ĩngĩ nenda andũ mangue ata?' (Mt. 7:12) Kwoou momĩĩsye ĩla maendeee kũtata mamanyĩe kwĩkala kũu. Ya mbee no tũlee kũelewa ũndũ masũanĩaa maũndũ kana ũndũ mekaa makwatwa nĩ maũndũ mana. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwona kana maĩle kũmanyĩa na kwĩtĩkĩla kĩthĩo kya kwenyu, wĩona ata ũkametĩkĩla mailyĩ o ũndũ mookie mailyĩ?—Soma Alomi 15:7.
16, 17. (a) Ithyĩ tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũtume ndũũ na ala maumĩte kũndũ kũngĩ? (b) Nĩ matambya meva tũtonya kwosa tũtetheesye aeni ala mathamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kitũ?
16 Kwĩkĩa kĩthito tũmanye maũndũ mana ĩũlũ wa kũla aeni asu maumĩte na syĩthĩo syoo, no kũtũtetheesye ũkethĩa nĩ laisi kũlikana namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla tũkwĩka ũthaithi witũ wa mũsyĩ no tũvange kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa syĩthĩo sya aeni ala mathamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kitũ kana kĩsionĩ kitũ. Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kũtũtetheesya tũtume ndũũ na aeni ta asu nĩ kũmathokya kwitũ tũĩsanĩe namo. Ethĩwa Yeova nũmavingũĩe "Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ mũomo wa mũĩkĩĩo," nĩkĩ tũteka take tũkavingũĩa aeni ala methĩwa me "ma nyũmba ya mũĩkĩĩo" mĩomo yitũ?—Meko 14:27; Aka. 6:10; Yovu 31:32.
17 Twamantha ĩvinda ya kũtindany'a na ala methĩwa mathamĩĩe kwitũ, tũkeethĩwa tũtonya kwona nesa ũndũ mekĩĩte kĩthito mamanyĩanĩe na syĩthĩo sitũ. Ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka tũkona ve ĩtambya twaĩle kwosa tũmatetheesye mamanye kĩthyomo kitũ nesa. O na ĩtambya yĩngĩ tũtonya kwosa nĩ kũmamanthĩĩsya mĩvĩa mĩna ya silikalĩ ĩla ĩtonya kũmatetheesya kũkwata wĩkalo mũseo kana wĩa wĩ kavaa. Kwosa matambya ta asu no kũtethye mũno ana-a-asa ala aeni.—Nth. 3:27.
18. Nĩ ngelekany'o yĩva ĩtonya kũtethya aeni ala mathamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ?
18 Ĩndĩ o na kũtw'ĩka ithyĩ nĩtũũtata tũtetheesye ala aeni, mo ene nĩmaĩle kwĩka kyonthe kĩla matonya mamanyĩe syĩthĩo sya nthĩ ĩla mathamĩĩa. Ngelekany'o ya Luthi no ĩmatethye mũno. Mbee, Luthi nĩwanengete ndaĩa syĩthĩo sya nthĩ ĩla wathamĩĩe, na nĩkyo kĩtumi weetisye mwanya wa kũkolany'a mosyao mũũndanĩ. (Lu. 2:7) O na kau vaĩ mwĩao weetĩkĩlĩtye andũ kũkolany'a ũsyao ũla watiala mũũndanĩ, Luthi ndaaona andũ ta maĩ na thiĩ wake na kwoou aivanga elika mũũndanĩ wene akolanĩtye ateũkũlya. Kelĩ, ĩla woonw'a ũseo nĩwatũngaa mũvea. (Lu. 2:13) Ĩla aeni maatĩĩa ngelekany'o ta ĩsu ya Luthi, nĩ laisi mũno ana-a-asa vamwe na ekali ma kĩsio kĩla maĩ makamanenga ndaĩa.
19. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa twĩka nesa aeni ala me naitũ?
19 Yeova nĩwonetye mbaa andũ mumo mwingĩ mũno kwa kũmetĩkĩlya mew'e ũvoo mũseo o na ethĩwa nĩ ma mbaĩ yĩva. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtũtanĩthasya mũno. Ĩndĩ no kwĩthĩwa ĩla andũ amwe maĩ nthĩ ya kwoo mataaĩsa kwona mũndũ ũmamanyĩsya Mbivilia, kana makethĩwa mataĩ matonya kũlikana na andũ ma Yeova. Ĩndĩ nũndũ yu ĩtina wa kũthamĩĩa nthĩ yitũ nĩmakwatĩte mwanya wa kwĩthĩwa vamwe naitũ, tyo ũndũ ũseo tũkamatetheesya makew'a ta me mũsyĩ? O na kau no kwĩthĩwa ũkwati witũ wĩ mũnini kana tũkethĩwa tũtamatethya mũno, ĩla twameka nesa twĩthĩawa tũimaĩkĩĩthya kana Yeova nũmendete. Kwoou, ekai 'twĩyĩelekany'e na Ngai' kwa kũtata ũndũ tũtonya twĩke nesa aeni ala me naitũ.—Aev. 5:1, 2.
