translation:
"Love is patient and kind."—1 COR. 13:4.
PAGE 50, 25
1, 2. (a) Why is it important to show empathy toward others? (Consider practical examples.) (b) What did the apostle Paul learn about this, and what benefits resulted?
A young man named Osei, [1] who grew up in Ghana, moved to Europe at age 30. He explains why he made that decision: "I felt I needed to see if I could get along with more people. And I wanted to prove to myself that I could manage on my own. I thought, 'If I can survive in a new place, it will give me confidence.'" But despite his desire to be independent, Osei missed his family and friends. And although he was surrounded by people, he often felt lonely and isolated.
2 Consider how Osei's experience illustrates an important truth. Do you ever feel disconnected from others, even when you are among them? Or do you sometimes wonder whether Jehovah truly cares about you personally, or whether he understands your feelings? The Bible assures Christians that: "Love is patient and kind" [or, love puts others first]. (1 Cor. 13:4) But does that assurance really comfort us? Does it help us to answer questions like: 'Does Jehovah know what I am going through?' and 'Can we trust that he will always act in our best interests?'
WHAT JEHOVAH KNOWS ABOUT US
3, 4. According to Exodus 23:9, what did God tell the Israelites to remember regarding those in need, and why?
3 Jehovah's deliverance of his people from Egypt moved him to be considerate of their needs, especially because they had been mistreated by others for so long. (Ex. 12:38, 49; 22:21) Today, too, when people around us are suffering, Jehovah feels deeply affected. He sets standards for how we should treat others—standards that protect individuals from exploitation.—Prov. 19:9, 10.
4 When the Israelites were being exploited, Jehovah showed that he understood what was happening. (Read Exodus 23:9.) How so? He reminded the Israelites to show compassion toward 'the alien resident'—that is, those who were vulnerable and needed help. And because of their experiences in slavery in Egypt, the Israelites could appreciate how easily someone might become helpless and be taken advantage of. (Deut. 43:32; 46:34; Ex. 1:11-14) Moreover, Jehovah told the Israelites to remember their own time of hardship in Egypt so that they would continue to show kindness to those in need.—Prov. 19:33, 34.
5 Why can we be confident that Jehovah will continue to care about our needs?
5 Yes, we can be sure that Jehovah will always be concerned about those who love and worship him, even during difficult times. (Ps. 10:17-19; Mal. 3:5, 6) We can trust that he understands the challenges we face, whether caused by others or by circumstances beyond our control, and that he will help us to maintain integrity and to discern what is right.—1 Pet. 3:8.
ARE YOU SHOWING COMPASSION TO THOSE IN NEED?
6, 7. Why is it important for Christians to imitate the empathy shown by Jehovah and the angels?
6 Indeed, we should strive to show empathy toward others, imitating the example set by Jehovah and his angels. In 33 CE, while in Jerusalem, Jesus showed deep concern for his disciples and encouraged them to preach the good news despite opposition. (Acts 2:5, 44-47) To demonstrate his empathy, Jesus and his apostles traveled from place to place strengthening the brothers.
7 As the Christian congregation progresses, continue to show empathy. The apostles appointed capable men to assist with the distribution of food so that they could devote more time to prayer and teaching. This helped to avoid resentment. (Acts 6:1) If the apostles themselves were willing to perform this humble task, we too should be happy to use our time and energy to help those in need. Those appointed were well-received by the congregation, and their service contributed to peace among the brothers.
The apostles chose seven men who were full of spirit and wisdom.—Acts 6:2-6.
8, 9. (a) How can we determine whether we truly empathize with others, especially when we do not fully understand their circumstances? (b) What can we learn from the example of Jesus? (1 Pet. 1:22)
8 Often, we find it easy to feel compassion when someone is facing an obvious difficulty. However, we may struggle to show empathy when we do not see a clear reason for their distress. (Phil. 12:2) We might wonder why they are upset, or we may dismiss their feelings as unimportant. But remember, there are times when people are struggling with hidden burdens, such as loneliness, fear, or disappointment. So let us ask ourselves, 'How can we show genuine concern for our fellow humans, considering that many have painful experiences? And how can we respond when someone confides in us, or when we sense that something is troubling him?'
9 Consider the example of Peter, who visited Cornelius, a Roman officer. He was willing to set aside his own prejudices and listen to Cornelius' heartfelt plea. (Acts 10:28, 34, 35; Acts 2:11-14) Let us also strive to be empathetic, recognizing that others may face challenges we know little about. As we discussed earlier, we need to make an effort to put ourselves in their place. (Read 1 Peter 1:22.) One thing that can help us is this: Remember that each of us has limitations and makes mistakes. Why? Because we are imperfect and influenced by our past experiences. (Prov. 3:9, 10, 21-24) So how can we show love toward those who seem difficult to deal with? (1 John 4:7) Our loving Father sets the perfect example. In a letter, the apostle Paul described Christians as being "fellow citizens" and "members of God's household."—Eph. 2:19. Therefore, let us endeavor to show empathy and kindness to all people, regardless of their background.—Acts 3:10, 11.
WHAT CAN HELP US TO SHOW EMPATHY
10, 11. What lessons can we learn from the example of Boaz regarding showing empathy to others?
10 The Israelite man Boaz showed empathy to Ruth, a foreigner who had become devoted to Jehovah. We see this illustrated in the account of Boaz and Ruth the Moabite woman. On one occasion, Boaz commended Ruth for seeking refuge under his wings, and he noticed that she was kind enough to care for his mother-in-law Naomi. But Boaz realized that Ruth's foreign background might present obstacles to her finding a suitable husband within Israel, and he encouraged her to continue working in his fields so that she would have opportunities to meet someone. He did not take advantage of her vulnerable situation.—Read Ruth 2:5-7, 15, 16.
11 Furthermore, Boaz treated Ruth with kindness and consideration, which helped her to feel secure and valued. This reminds us of how Jehovah feels about those who put their trust in him. Boaz also allowed Ruth to glean alongside his female workers, and he instructed them to be generous toward her. Moreover, he made sure that Ruth was given refreshment during the hot harvest season. And because Boaz appreciated Ruth's loyalty and hard work, he blessed her, saying: "May Jehovah reward you for what you have done."—Ruth 2:8-10, 13, 14.
12. What practical steps can we take to show empathy?
12 One way Boaz showed empathy was by recognizing Ruth's feelings and circumstances, and by treating her with dignity. He understood that she was a foreigner and a widow, yet he encouraged her to find security under the wings of Jehovah! By doing so, Boaz demonstrated that he respected Jehovah's view of people and that he recognized the value of each individual.—1 Tim. 2:3, 4.
13, 14. (a) How can we imitate Boaz when dealing with those who come to our place of worship? (b) Why is it important to show empathy when speaking to someone from a different background?
13 One aspect of showing empathy is taking time to get to know individuals and their backgrounds. This involves listening attentively and trying to understand their perspective and challenges. It also means avoiding making assumptions about them based on their ethnicity, culture, or social class. We should strive to see others as valuable individuals deserving of respect and consideration. To do this, we may need to overcome personal biases and prejudices. The article "Showing Empathy" in The Watchtower of [date] offers practical suggestions on how to show empathy.—Read Proverbs 2:3, 4.
14 Another way to show empathy is to put yourself in another person's shoes. Try to imagine what they might be feeling and experiencing. Then, offer encouragement and support. Be willing to listen without judgment and to share your own experiences when appropriate. And remember to treat everyone with kindness and compassion.
SHOW EMPATHY TO OTHERS
15. How can we improve our ability to empathize with others?
15 Ask yourself, "What would I want someone to do for me in a similar situation?" (Matt. 7:12) Also, make an effort to learn more about people's backgrounds. Often, we misunderstand people because we lack information or have inaccurate ideas. If others seem unwilling to open up or share their feelings, ask yourself, 'Could there be a reason why?'—Read Romans 15:7.
16, 17. (a) What can help us to take the initiative in getting to know others? (b) What specific steps can we take to show empathy to those who are facing difficulties?
16 To truly understand someone, we need to get to know them as individuals and try to see things from their perspective. For example, instead of quickly judging someone, we can take the time to find out what challenges they are facing. This can help us to approach them with kindness and understanding. Showing genuine interest in others can motivate us to reach out to them. Jehovah calls his servants "a brotherhood," so let us strive to treat fellow believers as members of our spiritual family.—1 Pet. 2:17; Acts 6:10; Job 31:32.
17 We should be willing to listen to those who confide in us, and we can then discern how best to offer comfort and encouragement. Sometimes, simply listening without offering advice is the most helpful thing we can do. And at times, we can offer practical assistance by helping them solve problems or cope with difficult circumstances. Be generous with your time and attention, and be considerate of others.—Prov. 3:27.
18. How can we show consideration for others?
18 Both by being thoughtful and by striving to assist others, especially when they are experiencing difficulties. The example of Ruth is instructive. Ruth showed thoughtfulness by working hard to provide for her mother-in-law Naomi, and this earned her Naomi's gratitude. (Ruth 2:7) Also, she did not hesitate to work diligently alongside other women to glean grain, and Naomi noticed that Ruth was making an effort to remain loyal. Clearly, her efforts were appreciated. (Ruth 2:13) Like Ruth, we can demonstrate consideration by going the extra mile.
19. What motivates us to show kindness to others?
19 Jehovah loves people very much and wants to use us to comfort those who are grieving. Showing kindness is something pleasing to him. It is also important to remember that some may be hesitant to accept help from someone who preaches the Bible, or they may have had unpleasant experiences with Jehovah's Witnesses. So, if we want to maintain a good relationship with them, should we not try to find out what their needs are? And even if they reject our assistance or if we feel inadequate to meet their needs, can we still pray for them so that Jehovah will bless them? Indeed, let us 'appeal to God' to help us determine how best to show kindness to others.—2 Cor. 5:1, 2.

MWĨĨTU-A-ASA wĩtawa Sylviana wĩ na myaka 27 aisye: "Anyanyawa amwe nĩmeetũmie kũndũ kwĩ na vata mũnene wa mavainia, na ĩla mangeleisye maũndũ ala moonete kũu, neewie nenda kũthi kũtanĩa kĩla matanĩĩte kũu. Ĩndĩ noonaa ndatonya kwĩtũma kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a."
We nĩwĩw'aa ta Sylviana? Nĩwĩw'aa ũyenda mũno kũthi kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ, ĩndĩ ũisyoka kũsaanĩw'a ethĩwa no ũvote kũthi kũu? Ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, ndũkakw'e ngoo. Kwĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ngili mbingĩ maĩ na isiĩĩi syamavataa kwongelanga kĩthito kyoo, ĩndĩ Yeova amanenga vinya wa kũsinda. Ekai twone ũndũ Yeova wavingũĩe amwe nzĩa nĩ kana matonye kũtetheesya wĩa wa kũtavany'a kĩthamanĩ kya Madagascar, kĩla nĩkyo kya kana katĩ wa ithama ila nene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
Kwa kĩlungu kya myaka ĩkũmi mĩvĩtu, mbee wa atavany'a 70 me kĩthito na mavainia kuma nthĩ 11, * nĩmaendete kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩĩ kĩseo mũno kya Africa na kĩ andũ aingĩ manengete Mbivilia ndaĩa. O na ve atavany'a aingĩ maumĩte isionĩ imwe sya Madagascar makathi isionĩ ingĩ o kĩthamanĩ kĩu nĩ kana ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ ũnyaĩĩke nesa kĩthamanĩ kĩu. Kwaekai twone amwe moo.
MAYAATULW'A NĨ WIA NA KŨKW'A NGOO
Mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Louis na mũka, Perrine, me na myaka 30 na kĩndũ, na mathamĩĩe Madagascar maumĩte France. Maminĩte myaka maisũanĩa kũthi kũtavany'a nthĩ ĩngĩ, ĩndĩ Perrine nĩwakĩaa. Perrine easya: "Nakĩaa kũthi kũndũ ndesĩ. Na neew'aa ndimaka mũno nasũanĩa kana nĩngũtia andũ maitũ, nĩtie kĩkundi, nyũmba yitũ, kĩsio kitũ, na tũieka kwĩka maũndũ ala tũnamanyĩĩte. No nasye kĩsiĩĩi kĩla kĩnene kyanziĩĩaa nĩ kwĩmakĩa." Ĩndĩ tũivika mwaka wa 2012, Perrine nĩwoosie vinya, na e na Louis matw'a kũthama. Perrine ew'aa ata yu? Easya: "Yu no nasye kana nĩtwĩkĩĩtwe vinya mũno nũndũ wa kwona ũndũ kw'oko kwa Yeova kwĩthĩĩtwe vamwe naitũ." Nake Louis aĩtye, "Mwa twatanie ata ĩla twoonie andũ ĩkũmi katĩ wa ala twamanyĩasya mooka ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ ũla ithyĩ twoombanĩe ya mbee Madagascar!"
Ĩla Louis na Perrine makwatiwe nĩ mathĩna, maumisye vinya wa kũmĩĩsya va maikatie ũtavany'a woo? Mamwĩsũvie Yeova amanenge vinya ũsu. (Avi. 4:13) Louis easya: "Nĩtweeyoneie nesa Yeova aisũngĩa mboya sitũ na kũtũnenga 'mũuo wa Ngai.' Kĩu nĩkyatumie twĩthĩwa tũtonya kũsũanĩa mũno maũndũ ala twatanĩaa twĩ ũtavany'a. Na ĩngĩ anyanya maitũ ala maĩ mũsyĩ nĩmakothaa kũtũtũmĩa e-mail na mavalũa matwĩkĩĩte vinya."—Avi. 4:6, 7; 2 Ako. 4:7.
Yeova nĩwaathimie Louis na Perrine mũno nũndũ wa wũmĩĩsyo woo. Louis easya: "Kwĩ Mwei wa 10, 2014, nĩtwaendie France kwondũ wa Sukulu ya Mbivilia ya Aklĩsto Matwaanĩte. * Ũsu waĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa mwanya Yeova watũnengie, na ndũkatũla." Mamina sukulu, matanie mũno kũmanya kana metũmwa Madagascar.
"TŨKEEW'AA MŨYO MŨNO NŨNDŨ WENYU!"
Mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Didier na mũka, Nadine, o namo maumĩte France, na mathamĩĩe Madagascar mwaka wa 2010. Ĩvinda yĩu maĩ na myaka 50 na kĩndũ. Didier easya: "Ĩla twaĩ ma mũika twaĩ mavainia, ĩndĩ tũendeangĩe twakwata syana itatũ sya kũea. Ĩla syana syeanie, nĩtwambĩĩe kũsũanĩa kũthi nthĩ ĩngĩ tũkatavany'e kw'o." Nake Nadine awetete atĩĩ: "Nambie kwĩw'a ndekwenda kũthi nasũanĩa kana ngeethĩawa nĩ vaasa na syana syakwa. Ĩndĩ syana isu syatwĩie, 'Mwathi kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a, tũkeew'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ wenyu!' Kĩu matũtavisye kyatumie twosa vinya na twathama. O na kau yu twĩ vaasa vyũ na syana sitũ, nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ no tũneenaa nasyo kĩla ĩvinda."
Ndwaĩ ũndũ mũvũthũ kwa Didier na Nadine kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya Malagasy. Nadine aisye ũũ athekete: "Ti ta ĩla twaĩ na myaka 20." Kwoou nĩ kyaũ kyamatetheeisye? Mbee mambie kũlika kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kya French. Na ĩndĩ ĩla meethukisye meew'a no mekwatane na kĩthyomo kya Malagasy, nĩmathamĩĩe kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kĩu. Nadine easya: "Tũkomanaa na andũ aingĩ mũno mekwenda kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Na kaingĩ nĩmatũtũngĩaa mũvea nũndũ wa kũmathokea. Mĩthenyanĩ ya mbee noonaa ta ngũota. Ũvainia wĩ mũyo mũno kĩsionĩ kĩĩ. Kĩla kwakya naamũka nĩthĩaa ndyasya, 'Mwa ndikwĩw'a mũyo! Ũmũnthĩ nĩtinda ndavanĩtye!'"
Didier athekaa mũno alilikana ĩvinda yĩla wambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya Malagasy. Easya: "Nĩngũlilikana mũthenya ũmwe nakwatĩĩe kĩlungu kĩmwe kya maũmbano. Ndyaeleawa nĩ kĩla ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa meũweta ĩla meũsũngĩa. Kwoou masũngĩa neekaa o kũmea, 'Asandi.' Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe nĩwasũngĩie na namũtũngĩa mũvea, ĩndĩ ala maĩ ĩtina wake mambony'a kana ũsũngĩo wake ti wa w'o. Na kwoou nĩneetie mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mĩtũkĩ nĩ kana anengane ũsũngĩo, na nĩĩkwatya anenganie ũsũngĩo wa w'o."
EETĨKĨLILE EW'ĨTE MŨYO MŨNO
Kwĩ mwaka wa 2005, Thierry na mũka, Nadia, nĩmaendie ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ na meeloela ndulama ĩla yaĩ na kyongo, "Fuatia Miradi Inayomletea Mungu Heshima." Ndulama ĩsu yaĩ ĩũlũ wa Timotheo, na nĩyakiitie ngoo syoo mũno. O na nĩyatumie methwa na wendi mwingangĩ wa kũthamĩĩa kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Thierry easya: "Tũendeee kũkũnanga mbĩ ndulama yathela, neekie ngalĩko ĩla yĩ kĩveti kyakwa na nakĩkũlya, 'Wĩona twĩthamĩĩa va?' Kyambĩie kĩĩkũlasya ĩkũlyo o yĩu." Mauma ũmbanonĩ ũsu nĩmambĩĩe kwĩka mĩvango nĩ kana mone ũndũ mekwĩanĩsya kĩu. Nadia aĩtye ũũ: "Twambĩĩe kũolanga syĩndũ ila twaĩ nasyo o kavola kavola mũvaka twesa kũtiwa na syĩndũ itonya kwĩanĩa o masandũkũnĩ ana!"
Mathamĩĩie Madagascar mwaka wa 2006, na mambĩĩie kũtanĩa ũtavany'a kuma mũthenya ũ wa mbee. Nadia aĩtye, "Andũ ala tũkomanaa namo matumaa twĩw'a mũyo mũno."
Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa myaka thanthatũ nĩmakwatiwe nĩ thĩna. Inyia wa Nadia, Marie-Madeleine, nĩwavalũkile atũlĩka kw'oko na aũmĩa mũtwe. Nadia na mũũme nĩmakũlilye ndakĩtalĩ wa Marie-Madeleine ethĩwa inyia woo no aume France akoka kwĩkala namo Madagascar na eetĩkĩla. Ĩla makũlilye inyia woo kana no ende kũka ku maĩ, eetĩkĩlile ew'ĩte mũyo mũno o na kau aĩ na myaka 80 ĩvinda yĩu. Marie-Madeleine ew'aa ata yu? Easya: "Ti laisi kũmanyĩa kwĩkala kũũ, ĩndĩ o na kau ndi na ũtonyi mwingĩ, nĩw'aa nĩ wa vata kĩkundinĩ. Na kĩla kĩtumaa nĩw'a mũyo mũno nĩ kana kũka kũũ nĩkũnengete syana ii syakwa mwanya wa kũendeea kũtanĩa kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩĩ."
"NOONIE KW'OKO KWA YEOVA KWANDETHYA"
Riana nĩ mwana-a-asa wĩ na myaka 22, na eanĩe vandũ vetawa Alaotra Mangoro. Kĩu nĩ kĩsio kĩ ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa syũa ya Madagascar, na kĩ mũthanga mũnou mũno. Riana aĩ mũĩ e sukulu, na aĩ na mũvango wa kũatĩanĩa na kĩsomo kya ĩũlũ. Ĩndĩ ĩla wambĩĩie kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nĩwavĩndũie mĩvango yake. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Neekĩie kĩthito kingĩ mũno nĩmine sekondalĩ nĩ o mũnini na namwatha Yeova atĩĩ, 'Navĩta mũtiani wakwa wa mũthya, nĩngwosa ũvainia.'" Riana amina sukulu ndaaũlwa nĩ kĩla wamwathie Yeova. Oosanie na mwana-a-asa ũngĩ vainia mekala ĩmwe, amantha wĩa wa masaa o manini, na ĩndĩ oosa ũvainia. Easya, "Vai ũtwi ũngĩ mũseo ta ũsu naaĩka."
Ĩndĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Riana mayamũeleawa moona atekwenda kũsembany'a na wĩa wĩ nguma. Aisye ũũ: "Tata, mũinae wa mũndũũme, na mũndũ mũka ũmwe mũinae wa sũsũ mambĩkĩaa vinya mũno nĩsembany'e na kĩsomo kya ĩũlũ. Ĩndĩ ndyendaa kũatĩanĩa na kĩndũ kĩũmbata kũkũna ũvainia." Ĩtina wa kavinda, Riana nĩwendie mũno kũthamĩĩa vandũ ve na vata mũnenange wa atavany'a. Wendi ũsu waumie va? Easya: "Mũthenya ũmwe ing'ei syatũlile vala twekalaa na syambũyĩa syĩndũ mbingĩ mũno. Kĩndũ kĩu kyatumie nĩsũanĩa mũno ndeto ila Yesũ wawetie ĩũlũ wa kwĩyiĩa 'ũthwii ĩtunĩ.' Na kwoou natw'a kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩke kwĩyũmbanĩsya ũthwii wa kĩ-veva." (Mt. 6:19, 20) Riana nĩwavangie kũthamĩĩa kĩsio kĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo vyũ ya Madagascar. Kĩsio kĩu waendie kĩthĩawa kĩ kyũmũ ki, na kĩ maili 800 (kĩlomita 1,300) kuma vala watwĩe. Kĩsio kĩu kĩkalaa andũ ma mbaĩ ya Antandroy. Nĩkĩ watwie kũthi kũu?
Mwei ũmwe ila ing'ei itanamba kũtũla kwoo, Riana aĩ anambĩĩa kũmanyĩsya Mbivilia aũme elĩ ma mbaĩ ĩsu ya Antandroy. Ĩtina wa kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kyoo o vanini, nĩwambĩĩe kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa andũ angĩ aingĩ ma mbaĩ ĩsu ala mataĩ manavikĩwa nĩ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Easya, "Namũvoyie Yeova andetheesye mũthenya ũmwe nĩtonya kũthamĩĩa kĩsionĩ kĩu kĩneenawa kĩthyomo kya Tandroy."
Ĩndĩ Riana avika kĩsionĩ kĩu oou ambĩanĩisye na thĩna. Amanthie wĩa waa. Mũndũ ũmwe amũkũlilye, "Ũkie kũũ kĩ?" Na ĩndĩ amwĩa, "Andũ ala meũmantha wĩa kũũ maendaa ku umie!" Ĩtina wa syumwa ilĩ nĩwakwatie savalĩ athi ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ. Aithi ũmbanonĩ ũsu nĩ ta watiĩtwe ate na silingi ngusunĩ na ndeesĩ eĩka ata. Mũthenyanĩ wa mũthya wa ũmbano ũsu, Riana eewie mwana-a-asa ũmwe amwĩkĩa kĩndũ ngusunĩ ya ĩkoti. Asisya eethĩie nĩ kavunda ka mbesa itoetye kũmũĩvĩa tikiti wa kũsyoka Antandroy na kũvingũa kaviasala ka kũta yogurt. Riana easya: "Noonie kw'oko kwa Yeova kwandethya o ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩlĩte. Yu naĩ ndonya kũendeea kũtetheesya ala mataĩ manakwata mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova!" Na eka ũu vaĩ na wĩa mwingĩ mũno wa kũtethw'a kĩkundinĩ. Riana ongelete kwasya: "Naumya ũvoo wa andũ onthe nakĩlaa kyumwa kĩmwe na kĩla kĩatĩĩe ngĩnengwa ũngĩ. Noonaa Yeova aendeee kũmanyĩsya aitũmĩa ũseũvyo wake." O na ũmũnthĩ Riana no ũendeee kũneena na andũ ma kĩthyomo kya Tandroy ala mekwenda kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ kana amatavye ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ.
'AKEEATHIMA NTHĨNĨ WA NGAI WA W'O'
Yeova atũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana "ũla wĩĩathimaa mwene kũũ nthĩ akeeathimaa nthĩnĩ wa Ngai wa w'o." (Isa. 65:16) Tweekĩa kĩthito tũsinde isiĩĩi ila iũtũvata kwongelanga kĩthito kitũ kya kũtavany'a, tũilea kwona Yeova aitũathima. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya ũla mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Sylviana ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ wa ngewa ĩno. Ethĩwa nũũlilikana, aisye kana oonaa atatonya kwĩtũma kũndũ kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Nĩkĩ woonaa ũu? Easya: "Kũũ kwakwa kwa aka nĩ kũkuvĩ kwĩ kũla kwa aũme na inzi ta itatũ na nusu (sendimita 9). Kwondũ wa ũu nĩkinyaa ndithua na nĩnoaa mĩtũkĩ."
Ĩndĩ o na Sylviana ailyĩ oou, mwakanĩ wa 2014 oosanie na mwĩĩtu-a-asa wa mũika na vainia kĩkundinĩ kyoo wĩtawa Sylvie Ann, na mathamĩĩa ndũanĩ nini yĩ maili 53 (kĩlomita 85) kuma ndũanĩ yoo. Kĩsiĩĩi kĩla waĩ nakyo kĩyaamũvata kwĩanĩsya kĩla weew'aa ayenda mũno kwĩanĩsya, na nũndũ wa ũu akwatĩte moathimo maingĩ mũno! Easya, "Ĩtina wa kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩĩ mwaka ũmwe, kĩveti kĩmwe kya mũika neemanyĩasya nakyo kĩtawa Doratine nĩkyavatisĩwe ũmbanonĩ ũla tweekie wa mũthyũlũlũko."
"NGAKŨTETHYA"
Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala twaneenea nĩmoonany'a ũndũ me mũĩkĩĩo ũlũmĩte, na maelesyo moo matũĩkĩĩthya kana ĩla twasinda isiĩĩi ila twĩ nasyo nĩ kana twongelange kĩthito kitũ kya kũtavany'a, nĩtwĩyoneaa nesa vyũ ũw'o wa watho ũũ Yeova wanengie athũkũmi make: "Ngakwĩkĩa vinya; ĩĩ, ngakũtethya." (Isa. 41:10) Kĩu nakyo kĩtumaa ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova ĩlũlũmĩla. Na ĩngĩ, kwĩyumya ithyĩ ene na ngenda tũtetheesye wĩa wa kũtavany'a kĩsionĩ kĩla tũĩ kana nthĩ ĩngĩ, kũtũmbanasya kwondũ wa mawĩa ala tũkatethya tũimũthũkũma Ngai nthĩ nzaũ. No tondũ ũla mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Didier ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ waisye, "Ĩla wathi kũtetheesya kũla kwĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a, wĩthĩawa ũyĩyũmbany'a kwondũ wa wĩa ũla wĩ mbee witũ!" Ekai twose ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ twĩyumye tũtetheesye wĩanĩ ũũ ũũtũmbany'a kwondũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte!
^ kal. 4 Atavany'a asu maumĩte Amelika, Canada, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Guadeloupe, Luxembourg, New Caledonia, Sweden, Switzerland, na United Kingdom.
^ kal. 8 Ũmũnthĩ sukulu ĩsu yĩtawa Sukulu ya Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ. Mavainia ala me nthĩ ingĩ maitavany'a kw'o na meanĩĩe kũthi sukulu ĩsu no makũlye metwe kĩlasi kĩla kĩkethwa nthĩ yoo, kana o kĩkethĩwa nthĩ ĩngĩ yĩkaa sukulu ĩsu na kĩthyomo kyoo kana kĩngĩ maeleawa nesa.

translation:
Sylviana, a 27-year-old woman, says: "Sometimes I feel like sending myself away to a place with older people who understand things, and if possible I would go somewhere to be alone so I can think calmly. Truly, I am afraid to send myself away to a place with older people."
Who is Sylviana? She is a young woman who wants to be among older people who understand things in Sumburu, and she hopes to find comfort and peace there? This is true, it's a good thing. Many young women and old women have often spoken about this problem, but Jehovah gives strength to endure. Let us see what Jehovah has helped some people to do—they were able to help those who want to be understood, like in Madagascar, where they found a way to overcome their shame despite having a difficult past.
For over ten years, about 70 people with problems and illnesses from more than 11 countries,* have been able to receive help through a special program in Africa, and many people have benefited from reading the Bible. And many people from Madagascar have also received help, and this has helped them to improve their lives in Sumburu. Let us see how.
REASONS FOR FEELING THIS WAY AND HOW TO COPE
A young couple named Louis and his wife, Perrine, were 30 years old and living in France when they moved to Madagascar. After several years of trying to get pregnant, Perrine became pregnant. Perrine said: "I was very happy. But I was worried because I didn't know what we would do—our family, our home, our possessions, and everything we had worked for. I was afraid of losing everything." Since 2012, Perrine has been feeling better, and she and Louis decided to move. Perrine says: "We were worried about whether we could continue serving Jehovah with others." Then Louis said, "We met about ten people who told us about the wonderful way Jesus helps us to cope with difficulties in life on the island of Madagascar!"
But did Louis and Perrine let their anxieties prevent them from continuing to serve? They prayed to Jehovah for help. (Ps. 4:13) Louis says: "I realized that Jehovah cares about us and wants to give us 'the peace of God.' This helped us to face the challenges we encountered with courage. And many of our brothers and sisters encouraged us by sending us emails and letters."—Ps. 4:6, 7; 2 Cor. 4:7.
Jehovah blessed Louis and Perrine with strength. Louis says: "On May 10, 2014, I traveled to France for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers. * We are grateful for the opportunity Jehovah gives us, and we appreciate it." After school, they returned to Madagascar.
"LET US SPEAK OF YOUR LOVING-KINDNESS!"
A young couple named Didier and his wife, Nadine, moved from France to Madagascar in 2010. At that time, she was pregnant and had five children. Didier says: "We left our comfortable life, and we knew that we would face difficulties. But despite those difficulties, we were determined to continue serving Jehovah." Nadine adds: "I remember thinking, 'How will I cope with raising children in a foreign land?' But when our children saw how much we loved serving Jehovah, they said, 'Mom, if you can endure hardships for Jehovah, we too will endure! Let us speak of your loving-kindness!'" Their faith strengthened them and motivated them to persevere. And they found joy in helping others and their children to remain spiritual.—
That is what sustained them.
One significant challenge for Didier and Nadine was learning the Malagasy language. Nadine recalls saying: "It felt like we were starting over at age 20." What helped them to succeed? They relied on their love for the French language. And because they already had some knowledge of the Malagasy language, it made learning this language easier. Nadine says: "We met many people who were willing to help us learn about the Bible. And often we would visit them and share a meal. The more I learned, the more I appreciated the language. Every time my husband heard me speaking it, he would say, 'Well done! You are making progress!'"
Didier also admits that he struggled to learn the Malagasy language. He says: "I struggled for a while until I found a way to make connections. I realized that children and adults alike enjoy being encouraged. So I started encouraging them, saying, 'Keep going.' One child encouraged me and I visited his family, and I discovered that his mother was very happy, or her encouragement was genuine. And then I met another child whose parents were struggling, and I wanted him to experience that same encouragement."
LET US KEEP ENCOURAGING EACH OTHER
In 2005, Thierry and his wife, Nadia, attended a large gathering of pioneers and shared their experience with the theme, "Follow Projects That Bring Glory to God." The talk was based on Timothy's example, and it touched many hearts. They were assigned to work with a circuit overseer to help strengthen brothers in Reunion. Thierry said: "We continued to look for ways to apply what we had learned, and we often asked ourselves, 'Are we really strengthening them?' It motivated us to put more effort into it." This gathering helped them to see how important it is to be willing to adjust our methods. Nadia added: "We learned to focus on things we could do, rather than dwelling on limitations and feeling overwhelmed by problems!"
They returned to Madagascar in 2006 and were thrilled to continue helping the pioneers. Nadia said, "The people we associate with have strengthened our faith."
After six years of service, they faced a challenge. Nadia's mother, Marie-Madeleine, became seriously ill and needed care. Nadia and her husband decided to take a break from pioneering so that she could go to France to stay with Marie-Madeleine and provide support. But they planned to return as soon as possible, and they did—after about eight months. Did Marie-Madeleine recover? She explained: "I didn't realize how much I wanted to be with my family, and although I was very weak, I recovered because of the love I received. And everything that helped me to recover made me want to come back with them and continue supporting the Kingdom work."
"JEHOVAH'S ORGANIZATION STRENGTHENED ME"
Riana is a young woman of 22 years old, and she comes from Alaotra Mangoro. This is a region known for its beautiful landscapes in eastern Madagascar, and it is a very poor area. Riana did well in school, and she had a desire to pursue higher education. However, when someone showed her the Bible, she changed her goals. She says: "I remember distinctly what my older brother told me when he taught me about Jehovah: 'How can you use your life if not to serve Him?'" Riana left school to devote herself fully to serving Jehovah. Along with another young pioneer, she spent many hours each day, and she enjoyed this ministry. She explains, "Every experience is precious, like finding treasure."
But Riana's parents were initially disappointed because they wanted her to get an education and have a good career. Her father said: "My daughter, and my other children, I worked so hard to provide for them so that they could study. And now you want to abandon your studies to focus on something else?" Despite their objections, Riana continued to help people learn about the truth. How did she feel? She explains: "There was a time when I felt discouraged because I thought I would disappoint my family. But this motivated me to pray more earnestly to Jesus to give me 'wisdom from above.' And through prayer, I learned to value spiritual things over material possessions." (Matt. 6:19, 20) Riana volunteered to preach in a remote area of Madagascar. This area is difficult to reach, and it is about 500 miles (800 kilometers) from the nearest town. This area is inhabited by the Antandroy tribe. What challenges did she face?
One day, while traveling there, Riana took the opportunity to share the Bible with some people from another Antandroy village. As she shared the good news with them, she realized how much the people in that region needed help, especially since they had been affected by famine. She says, "I thanked Jehovah for allowing me to experience the privilege of sharing the good news with the people of the Tandroy region."
Then Riana showed them a picture that she had taken. They were very happy. One person asked her, "What does this mean?" And she told him, "These people are rejoicing because they have found relief!" The joy that was expressed was so great that it filled three baskets. But this joy was short-lived, as there was still much suffering and hardship. Because of the intense heat, Riana saw a young boy who was sick with a fever. She noticed that he was weak and unable to walk, so she helped him get a ticket to leave Antandroy and buy medicine to make yogurt. Riana said: "Jehovah's love has touched my heart and given me strength. I will continue to share the good news with those who want to learn about Jehovah!" And she went with many others to preach enthusiastically. Riana continued to say: "I feel sorry for these people who suffer and struggle with every problem they face. May Jehovah continue to strengthen us as we share his message!" And so Riana continued to speak to the people of the Tandroy region, and many of them wanted to learn about Jehovah, even though they faced challenges in Madagascar.
'THE GOD OF TRUTH WILL BE THEIR STRENGTH'
Jehovah assures us that "the God of truth will be their strength." (Isa. 65:16) So while we may not fully understand why bad things happen, we can trust that Jehovah cares for us. Consider the experience of a sister named Sylviana who lives in a small village. She explained that she once dreamed that she could not send letters to her family because of the difficulty of traveling. Was this dream fulfilled? She said: "The road to our village is narrow—only about nine meters [ten yards] wide. Because of this, it is often blocked by trees."
Sylviana and her husband moved in 2014 to live closer to relatives and to help a sister named Sylvie Ann with her farming. They now live about 53 miles [85 kilometers] away. Despite the challenges, they enjoy helping others and feel blessed! She explains, "The difficulty of traveling motivated me to learn sign language so I could visit Sister Doratine, who became paralyzed and was confined to her home."
"TO PROVE MYSELF LOYAL"
Sisters and brothers often face difficult situations, and sometimes we may feel inadequate. But we can find strength in prayer and remind ourselves of what Jehovah has done for us. He assures us: "Do not be afraid; I am with you. Do not look around anxiously, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, I will truly help you, I will surely uphold you with my right hand." (Isa. 41:10) This promise gives us confidence in Jehovah. Also, when we meditate on examples of those who showed loyalty, we are encouraged to remain steadfast despite our fears and difficulties, always trusting in God. For example, young Didier was recently appointed as an auxiliary pioneer. He said, "I wanted to prove myself loyal and to show my great appreciation for the support I have received from my family!" Let us all imitate their fine example and continue to prove ourselves loyal to the full extent!
^ p. 4 Pioneers in America, Canada, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Guadeloupe, Luxembourg, New Caledonia, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
^ p. 8 A school called Pioneer Service School. Many pioneers attend this school to improve their skills, and they receive assignments to different congregations, either temporarily or permanently. They also learn how to conduct effective Bible studies.

text:
Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa Kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ũthaithinĩ?
Aklĩsto methĩawa na mawoni maũ ĩũlũ wa sikũkũ sya ndĩni?
Ũtonya kũelesya andũ angĩ ata ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo waku ũteũmathatya?
1, 2. Wamina kuma ndĩninĩ ya ũvũngũ waĩle kwĩkũlya ata, na nĩkĩ ũtonya kwasya ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa vata?
ŨKETHĨA vala mũutaa kĩw'ũ vekĩiwe sumu, we wĩka ata? Nũndũ nĩ mũisyo kũnywa kĩw'ũ kĩu, no ũmanthe vandũ vangĩ ũtonya kũkwata kĩw'ũ kĩseo. Na ũyĩka ũu no nginya wĩkũlye, 'Yo nĩnĩthwa nĩnanywie sumu?'
2 No ta ũu ĩũlũ wa ndĩni ya ũvũngũ. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana momanyĩsyo na imanyĩo sya ndĩni isu nivukĩtye ũthaithi woo. (2 Akolintho 6:
KŨTHAITHA MĨVW'ANANO NA AA-ŨMAU ALA MAKWIE
3. (a) Mbivilia yaĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa kũtũmĩa mĩvw'anano ũthaithinĩ, na nĩkĩ woni wa Ngai ũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ vinya kwa amwe kũwĩtĩkĩla? (b) Waĩle kwĩkana ata na syĩndũ ila wĩthwa nasyo ikonanĩtye na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ?
3 Andũ amwe nĩmethĩawa na mĩvw'anano na mathembo mĩsyĩ kwoo. We wĩ na syĩndũ isu? Ethĩwa wĩnasyo nũtonya kwona wĩ ũndũ ũtatonyeka kana mũthũku kũvoya Ngai ũteũtetheew'a nĩ kĩndũ kyenekee. Na syĩndũ isu nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wonaa syĩ sya vata mũno kwaku. Ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwe ũwetaa ũndũ ũkwenda kũthaithwa, na Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana ndendaa tũitũmĩa mĩvw'anano kũmũthaitha. (Kuma 20:
4. (a) Twĩsĩ ata kana kũthaitha aa-ũmau ala makwie nĩ kwa mana? (b) Nĩkĩ Yeova wavatie andũ make kũneenany'a na akw'ũ kana kũkwatana na maũndũ ma ũwe?
4 Ũthaithi wa aa-ũmau ala makwie wĩokw'o ndĩninĩ mbingĩ sya ũvũngũ. Andũ matanamba kũmanya w'o kwĩanana na ũndũ Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya maĩkĩĩaa kana akw'ũ maendeeaa kwĩkala vandũ vangĩ matonekaa na nĩmatonya o kũtethya kana kũthĩny'a andũ. O na nokwĩthĩwa waatata na vinya mũno kũvoovya aa-ũmau ala makwie. Ĩndĩ kwĩanana na ũndũ tweemanyĩisye Kĩlungunĩ kya 6 ĩvũkunĩ yĩĩ, mai vandũ maĩ me thayũ. Kwoou kũneenany'a namo nĩ kwa mana. Wasya w'onthe ũla ũtonya kwĩw'ĩka ta wumĩte kwa mwendwa waitũ wakwie wĩthĩawa wumĩte kwa ndaimoni. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova wavatie Aisilaeli kũneenany'a na akw'ũ kana kũkwatana na maũndũ ma ũwe.
5. Ethĩwa nĩwatũmĩaa mĩvw'anano kana kũthaitha aa-ũmau ala makwie, ũtonya kwĩka ata?
5 Ethĩwa nĩwatũmĩaa mĩvw'anano kana kũthaitha aa-ũmau ala makwie, ũtonya kwĩka ata? Soma na kũsũanĩa mũno maandĩko ma Mbivilia ala monanĩtye mawoni ma Ngai ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu. Mũvoye Yeova kĩla mũthenya na ũimũtavya wendi waku wa kũlũmany'a na ũthaithi wa w'o, mũkũlye aũtetheesye kũsũanĩaa take.
AKLĨSTO MA MBEE MAYATANĨAA KĨLISIMASI
6, 7. (a) Kĩlisimasi kĩtw'ĩkaa nĩ mũthenya wa kũlilikana kyaũ, na amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ nĩmatanĩaa Kĩlisimasi? (b) Kũtanĩa mĩthenya ya kũsyawa kwakonanĩtye na kyaũ yĩla amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ maĩ kũũ nthĩ?
6 Ũthaithi wa mũndũ nũtonya kũvukw'a nĩ ndĩni sya ũvũngũ kwĩsĩla sikũkũ ila syendetwe nĩ andũ. Ĩmwe nĩ ta Kĩlisimasi. Kĩlisimasi kĩtw'ĩkaa nĩ mũthenya wa kũlilikana kũsyawa kwa Yesũ Klĩsto, na vakuvĩ ndĩni syonthe ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto nitanĩaa mũthenya ũsu. Ĩndĩ vai kĩndũ kyonanasya kana amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ nĩmatanĩaa sikũkũ ta ĩsu. Ĩvuku yĩtawa Sacred Origins of Profound Things yaĩtye: "Vandũ va ĩvinda ya myaka ta 200 ĩtina wa Klĩsto asyawa, vai mũndũ weesĩ yĩla wasyaiwe na ti andũ aingĩ mendeeaw'a nĩ kũmanya yĩla wasyaiwe."
7 O na kethĩwa amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ nĩmeesĩ nesa matukũ ala Yesũ wasyaiwe mayĩthĩwa maatanĩa kũsyawa kwake. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ kwĩanana na ũndũ ĩvuku yĩmwe, The World Book Encyclopedia yaasya, "Aklĩsto ma mbee monaa kũtanĩa ĩsyawa ne kĩmwe katĩ wa imanyĩo sya andũ ala matesĩ Ngai." Mbivilia ĩwetete mĩthenya ya kũsyawa o ĩlĩ, nayo yatanĩiwe nĩ asumbĩ matathaithaa Yeova. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 40:20; Maliko 6:21) O na andũ nĩmatanĩaa mĩthenya ya kũsyawa kwa ngai sya mũvw'anano. Kwa ngelekany'o, matukũ 24 Mwei wa 5, Alomi matanĩaa ĩsyawa ya ngai yoo yeetawa Ndaiana. Mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe matanĩaa ĩsyawa ya ngai yoo ĩngĩ ya sua yeetawa Avolo. Kwoou kũtanĩa mĩthenya ya kũsyawa kwakonanĩtye na ũthaithi wa andũ ala mateesĩ Ngai, ĩndĩ ti Aklĩsto.
8. Elesya ũndũ kũtanĩa mũthenya wa kũsyawa kũkonanĩtye na maimũ.
8 Ve kĩtumi kĩngĩ kyatumaa Aklĩsto ma mbee matatanĩa ĩsyawa ya Yesũ. Nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa meesĩ kana kũtanĩa mĩthenya ya kũsyawa nĩkwakonanĩtye na maimũ. Ta Akiliki na Alomi aingĩ ma tene maĩkĩĩaa kana ve yĩimũ yookaa yĩla kĩla mũndũ ũkũsyawa, nayo nĩyo yamũsũvĩaa thayũnĩ wake w'onthe. Ĩvuku yĩtawa The Lore of Birthdays yaĩtye: "Yĩimũ yĩu yeethĩawa na ũtiany'o mũna wa kĩmbithĩ ũtamanyĩka na ngai ĩla yasyaĩtwe mũthenya ũmwe na mũndũ ũsu wasyaawa." Yeova ndesa kwĩw'ĩthw'a mũyo nĩ andũ maitanĩa sikũkũ ĩkũkonany'a Yesũ na maimũ. (Isaia 65:
ŨNDŨ KĨLISIMASI KYAAMBĨĨE
9. Matukũ 25 Mwei 12 manyũviwe ata matw'ĩke mũthenya wa kũtanĩa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ?
9 Mũthenya wa kũlilikana kũsyawa kwa Yesũ matukũ 25 Mwei wa 12 wambĩĩe kũtanĩwa myaka maana maingĩ ĩtina wa Yesũ auma kũũ nthĩ. Ĩndĩ ũsu tiw'o mũthenya ũla Yesũ wasyaiwe nũndũ we asyaiwe Mwei wa 10. * Nĩkĩ matukũ 25 Mwei 12 manyũviwe kũtanĩa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ? Veonekana andũ amwe meeyĩtaa Aklĩsto "mendaa kũsyawa kwa Yesũ kũthimane na mboka ya Alomi mateesĩ Ngai ya 'kũsyawa kwa sua yĩtasindawa.' " (The New Encyclopædia Britannica) Ĩvinda ya mbevo, yĩla kũteethĩawa sua yingĩ kũya nthĩ sya umĩlonĩ wa sua na Ũlaya, andũ ala mateesĩ Ngai meethĩawa na mboka nĩ kana mesũve sua yĩsyoke kuma kũla yeethĩawa yĩendete. Monaa kana sua yambĩĩa kũsyoka matukũ 25 Mwei 12. Atongoi ma ndĩni moosie mũthenya wa mboka ĩsu maũtw'a ta wa "Aklĩsto" nĩ kana maalyũle andũ ala mateesĩ Ngai matw'ĩke Aklĩsto. *
10. Nĩkĩ andũ amwe mayatanĩaa Kĩlisimasi tene?
10 Kuma tene andũ nĩmeesĩ kana Kĩlisimasi kyaumanĩte na andũ ala mateesĩ Ngai. Kĩlisimasi nĩkyavatanĩtwe nĩ mĩao kũya Ũngelesa, na nthĩ ingĩ sya Amelika ila syasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũngelesa myaka ya 1600, nũndũ kĩyaumanĩte na Maandĩko. Andũ ala malea kũthi wĩanĩ mũthenya wa Kĩlisimasi nĩmaĩvaa vainĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini, syĩthĩo isu sya tene syasyokewa na ingĩ itaĩvo syongelwa. Kwoou Kĩlisimasi kyatw'ĩka sikũkũ nene ĩngĩ, na ũu nĩw'o kĩilye ũmũnthĩ nthĩ mbingĩ. Nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa Kĩlisimasi kyumanĩte na ndĩni ya ũvũngũ, ala mendaa kũmũtanĩthya Ngai maikĩtanĩaa kana kũtanĩa sikũkũ ila ingĩ syumanĩte na ũthaithi wa andũ ala matesĩ Ngai. *
NĨ ŨNDŨ WA VATA KŨMANYA MWAMBĨLĨĨLYO WASYO?
11. Andũ amwe matanĩaa sikũkũ nĩkĩ, ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla waĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩ wa vata vyũ kwitũ nĩ mwaũ?
11 Andũ amwe nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana sikũkũ ta Kĩlisimasi syumanĩte na andũ ala matesĩ Ngai ĩndĩ monaa ti ũthũku kũitanĩa. Maasya kana mayĩthĩawa maisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ yĩla meũtanĩa sikũkũ ĩsu. Mavinda asu andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmatonya kũsyokeanĩa vamwe. We wĩthĩawa na woni ta ũsu? Ethĩwa woni waku nũsu, nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa kĩla kĩtumaa kũlũmany'a na ndĩni ya w'o kwĩthĩwa na vinya kwaku nĩ kũmenda andũ ma mũsyĩ, ĩndĩ ti kũmyenda ndĩni ya ũvũngũ. Ĩndĩ manya nesa kana Yeova, ũla waambĩlĩĩlye mũsyĩ, nĩweendaa wĩthĩwe na mũamba na andũ ma mũsyĩ waku. Ĩndĩ nũtonya kũlũlũmĩĩlya mũamba ũsu kwa nzĩa ila syĩtĩkĩlĩtwe nĩ Ngai. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũla waĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩ wa vata vyũ kwitũ: 'Thimai maũndũ ala mamwendeeasya Mwĩaĩi.'
12. Nengane ngelekany'o ya kwonany'a nĩkĩ twaĩle kũekana na syĩthĩo na sikũkũ syumĩtw'e kũndũ kũvuku.
12 No ũtonya kwasya mwambĩlĩĩlyo wa sikũkũ ndwĩna mũamba na ũndũ itanĩawa ũmũnthĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũmanya mwambĩlĩlyo wa sikũkũ isu? Ĩĩ! Kwa ngelekany'o, ũkona ngelemende ĩvalũkĩte mũtaũnĩ wĩna kĩko, we no wose na ũkaya? Ndũmyosa nũndũ ngelemende ĩsu yĩna kĩko. O ta ngelemende ĩsu, sikũkũ nitonya kwoneka syĩ nzeo ĩndĩ syumĩtw'e kũndũ kũvuku. Nĩ kana tũlũmany'e na ũthaithi wa w'o no nginya twĩthĩwe na woni ta ũla wa mwathani Isaia ũla weeie athaithi ma w'o atĩĩ: "Mũikakiite kĩndũ kĩvuku."
KWĨKALANY'A NA ANDŨ ALA ANGĨ KWA ŨĨ
13. Kwĩkalany'a na andũ kũtonya kũmesya vinya ata walea kũtanĩa sikũkũ vamwe namo?
13 Kwĩkalany'a na andũ nĩkũtonya kũmesya vinya walea kũtanĩa sikũkũ namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ala mũthũkũmaa vamwe nĩmatonya kũseng'a nĩkĩ ũtatanĩaa sikũkũ vamwe namo. Ũkanewa mũthĩnzĩo wa Kĩlisimasi wĩka ata? Wĩthĩwa wĩ ũthũku kũwosa? Nata ethĩwa ũla mũtwaanĩte ena mũĩkĩĩo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ũ waku? Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana syana syaku iikew'e ta ikosete kĩndũ nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa iitanĩaa sikũkũ?
14, 15. We ũtonya kwĩka ata ũkakethw'a ngethi ya sikũkũ kana ũkanewa mũthĩnzĩo?
14 Ũĩ nĩwaĩle nĩ kana ũmanye ũndũ waĩle kwĩka maũndũ ũndũ vaĩle. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa nĩwakethw'a ngethi ya sikũkũ, nũtonya kũsũngĩa kwa ũĩ. Nata ethĩwa wakethw'a nĩ mũndũ ũmwĩsĩ kana mũthũkũmaa ĩmwe? Nũtonya kũmũelesya mũnango ĩũlũ wa sikũkũ ĩsu. Mavinda onthe nĩwaĩle kũtũmĩa ũĩ. Mbivilia ĩtũtaa: "Ndeto syenyu syĩthĩwe na mumo mavinda onthe, isamae mũnyũ, nĩ kana mũmanye ũndũ mwaĩlwe nĩ ũsũngĩa kĩla mũndũ." (Akolosai 4:6) Ndũkalee kũnenga ala angĩ ndaĩa. Ĩndĩ elesya mũĩkĩĩo waku kwa ũĩ. Elesya nesa kana ti aĩ ndwendete kũnengane mĩthĩnzĩo kana kwĩthĩwa vamwe na ala angĩ kwĩtanĩthya, ĩndĩ wendeeaw'a nĩkwĩka ũu ĩvinda yĩngĩ.
15 Nata ĩndĩ ethĩwa mũndũ nĩwenda kũũnenga mũthĩnzĩo? Nũtonya kwenda kũmanya kĩtumi kya ũkũnenga mũthĩnzĩo ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtonya ũkwĩa: "Nĩnĩsĩ ndũtanĩaa sikũkũ ĩno. Ĩndĩ nĩngwenda ũkũne mũthĩnzĩo ũũ." Nũtonya kũtw'a kana kwĩtĩkĩla mũthĩnzĩo ũsu ti ũndũ ũmwe na kũtanĩa sikũkũ ĩsu. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa ũsu ũkũũnenga mũthĩnzĩo ndesĩ mũĩkĩĩo waku nesa nĩ ũseo kũmũtavya kana ndũtanĩaa sikũkũ ĩsu. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtonya kũmũtetheesya kũmanya nĩkĩ we ndwĩmũnenga mũthĩnzĩo, o na kau we nũkũũnenga. Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla mũthĩnzĩo ethĩwa twĩnengwa nĩ kana twonw'e kana tũilũmĩtye mũĩkĩĩo witu, na kana no tũemwe kũlũmany'a na w'o no ũndũ wa kwenda kũnewa syĩndũ.
NATA ĨŨLŨ WA ANDŨ MA MŨSYĨ?
16. Ũtonya kũtũmĩa ũĩ ata yĩla ũkũelesya mũĩkĩĩo waku ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala makonetye sikũkũ?
16 Nata ĩndĩ ethĩwa andũ ma mũsyĩ mena mũĩkĩĩo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ũ waku? Tũmĩa ũĩ. Vai vata wa kũkananĩaa ĩũlũ wa kĩla ũndũ wa kĩthĩo kana o sikũkũ ila andũ ma mũsyĩ menda kũtanĩa. Nenga woni woo ndaĩa o tondũ we wendaa manenge woni waku ndaĩa. (Mathayo 7:
17. Ũtonya kũtetheesya syana syaku ata nĩ kana iikew'e ta ikosete kĩndũ yĩla syoona angĩ maitanĩa sikũkũ?
17 Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana syana syaku iikew'e ta ikosete kĩndũ nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa iitanĩaa sikũkũ itetĩkĩlĩtw'e Mbivilianĩ? Nũtonya kũitetheesya na maũndũ ala wĩkaa mĩthenya ĩla ĩngĩ. Asyai amwe nĩmosaa ĩvinda ya kũnenga syana syoo mĩthĩnzĩo. Mũthĩnzĩo ũmwe mũseo vyũ ũtonya kũnenga syana syaku nĩ kwĩthĩwa na ĩvinda vamwe nasyo na kũsyony'a wendo.
LŨMANY'A NA ŨTHAITHI WA W'O
18. Kũmbana mawũmbanonĩ ma Aklĩsto, kũtonya kũtũtetheesya ata kũlũmany'a na ũthaithi wa w'o?
18 Nĩ kana wendeesye Ngai, nĩwaĩle kũlea ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ na ũilũmany'a na ũthaithi wa w'o. Kwoou waĩle kwĩka maũndũ meva? Mbivilia yaasya: "Na nĩtũlilikanany'e ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ kũthangaany'a wendonĩ na mawĩanĩ maseo; tũtekũeka kũmbana kwitũ vamwe, o tondũ amwe mekaa, ĩndĩ tũkĩtaana; na mbee mũno, mũkyona mũthenya ũsu ũkĩthengeea." (Aevelania 10:
19. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũtavya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩĩtye kuma Mbivilianĩ?
19 Nzĩa ĩngĩ ũtonya kũlũmany'a na ũthaithi wa w'o nĩ kũtavya andũ angĩ maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩĩtye vamwe na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova kuma Mbivilianĩ. Kwa w'o andũ aingĩ 'nĩmavevũũkaa na makaĩa' nũndũ wa mothũku ala mekawa kũũ nthĩ ũmũnthĩ. (Esekieli 9:4) No kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ andũ amwe mavevũũkaa na kũĩa nũndũ wa mothũku. Nũtonya kũmatavya ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo waku kuma Mbivilianĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte. Waendeea kũmbana na Aklĩsto ma w'o na kũtavya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa w'o ũla wĩmanyĩĩtye kuma Mbivilianĩ, imanyĩo sya ndĩni ya ũvũngũ ila syĩthwa itiele ngoonĩ yaku ikathela. Ĩthĩwa wĩsĩ nesa kana ũkeethĩwa wĩ mũtanu na ũkakwata moathimo maingĩ walũmany'a na ũthaithi wa w'o.

Will people ever stop being shocked at the practice of immoral behavior?
Does Christ approve of those who practice homosexuality?
Is it possible to help others stop practicing vile habits, even if it seems hopeless?
1, 2. Why are many people drawn to wicked company, and can resisting such association be difficult?
LET us say someone offers you poison—would you accept it? Of course not! Yet many people willingly take in something harmful, and they encourage others to do the same. They might reason, "What harm could it do?"
2 This is true of the influence of bad associations. Immoral practices can seem appealing, and associating with those who indulge in them can weaken our spiritual resolve. (2 Corinthians 6:
IMMORAL PRACTICES AND THEIR CONSEQUENCES
3. (a) How does the Bible view the practice of homosexual conduct, and why does God disapprove of it? (b) What reasons do some give for condoning homosexuality, and how does this compare with what the Bible says?
3 Some people practice both heterosexual and homosexual immorality. What about you? Perhaps you feel that it is a personal matter and that God does not care what you do. But God's standards are clear, and the Bible shows that engaging in immoral activity displeases him. (Romans 20:
4. (a) Is it right to condemn those who engage in immoral practices? (b) Does Jehovah want his servants to isolate themselves from everyone who has flaws or makes mistakes?
4 The moral state of most people is very poor. Many people are willing to accept immorality as normal, and they may view Bible principles as outdated or unreasonable. They may also be quick to judge others. However, we should remember what we learned in paragraph 6 of this publication—that there is a difference between showing compassion and approving of wrongdoing. It is important to show compassion, but not to condone immoral conduct. Jehovah wants us to associate with imperfect people and to help them improve.
5 Can Christians use immoral means or condemn those who engage in immoral practices?
5 Can Christians use immoral means or condemn those who engage in immoral practices? Read and discuss relevant scriptures that reveal God's viewpoint on this issue. Pray to Jehovah regularly, asking him to help you understand what is right and wrong, and then strive to apply his standards in your life.
CHRISTIANS AND THE CELEBRATION OF CHRISTMAS
6, 7. (a) Why is Christmas often associated with materialism, and how does this affect our appreciation of Jesus? (b) How can we focus on the spiritual aspects of Christmas and maintain our love for Jesus?
6 A person's values can be influenced by the culture around him, especially during certain times of the year. This is true of Christmas. Christmas has become associated with materialism, and this can distract us from appreciating the real meaning of Jesus Christ's birth. Many people celebrate Christmas simply because it is a tradition. But what truly honors Jesus? The book Sacred Origins of Profound Things states: "For nearly two centuries after Christ's death, there was no widespread celebration of his birthday among Christians."
7 So why did the celebration of Jesus' birth eventually become so popular? One reason is that it coincided with existing pagan festivals. As The World Book Encyclopedia explains, "The winter solstice festival was a time when people honored gods who were believed to have control over life and death." The Bible highlights the importance of remembering birthdays, and Jehovah approved of joyful celebrations. (Proverbs 40:20; Mark 6:21) People also celebrated the birthdays of their rulers and deities. For example, on May 24, the Romans celebrated the birthday of their goddess Maia. And December 25, they celebrated the birthday of Mithras, a god who was very popular at that time. Thus, the celebration of birthdays became linked to the customs of those who did not worship the true God, including Christmas.
8. Let us examine how the celebration of birthdays came about.
8 Another factor that contributed to the popularity of celebrating Jesus' birth was the desire to honor him. It may have seemed harmless to celebrate birthdays or to commemorate the anniversary of someone's birth. But Tertullian and Origen strongly opposed the practice, saying that it was a custom associated with pagans and that it distracted people from worshipping God. The book The Lore of Birthdays states: "The observance of birthdays originated in ancient times among heathens who believed that each person had a guardian spirit present at his birth." Jehovah does not approve of practices that associate Jesus with pagan customs. (Isaiah 65:
THE ORIGIN OF CHRISTMAS
9. Why do many observe December 25 as the date for commemorating the birth of Jesus?
9 The choice of December 25 to commemorate the birth of Jesus has its roots in ancient sun worship. In earlier times, the Romans marked December 25 as the day when the sun began to regain strength. However, Jesus was actually born in October. * So why do many observe December 25 as the birth of Jesus? Some scholars believe that Christians adopted this date so they could compete with the celebrations honoring the sun god Mithras, which were popular in Rome and throughout Europe. They reasoned that by associating Christ's birthday with this date, they might make Christianity more appealing. Thus, December 25 became a compromise date. Also, the name "Christmas" itself may be derived from an old pagan festival. *
10. Why do some object to Christmas traditions?
10 Many feel that Christmas has become commercialized and mixed with pagan customs. Christmas originated in England, but much of what is now associated with it came from America in the 1600s, and it is not based on the Bible. Those who want to honor God often find Christmas traditions displeasing. Despite the objections, however, many continue to celebrate it because of family tradition and social pressure. Moreover, Christmas has become such a big event that many view it as harmless fun. But while Christmas may be enjoyable for some, others feel that it distracts from true worship of God and associates them with practices that displease Him. *
IS THERE A BIBLE BASIS FOR CHRISTMAS CUSTOMS?
11. Some observe holidays, but does the Bible give us guidance on whether we should participate in them?
11 Some wonder if celebrating holidays like Christmas dishonors those who worship God, especially when they know that these celebrations have pagan origins. They realize that many customs associated with these holidays contradict Biblical principles. However, others believe that they can enjoy these celebrations without compromising their faith. It is important for each individual to examine his own heart. Are you influenced by peer pressure? If so, ask yourself why you want to conform—is it simply to please others, or is it because you truly believe that participating in these celebrations will not offend God? Remember that Jehovah, who cares about our feelings, wants us to associate with those who share our beliefs. But he does not force us to shun everyone who does not share our views. The apostle Paul wrote regarding this matter: "Continue approving the things that are fine."
12. Consider how reasonable it would be to avoid certain associations and places that could weaken your spirituality.
12 Can you discern whether an association will strengthen or weaken your faith? Of course! For example, imagine finding a rotten apple among good ones. Would you eat it just because it is mixed with the good apples? Certainly not! Similarly, bad associations can spoil our spiritual health. So, while some celebrations may seem harmless, they can expose us to influences that draw us away from God. If we understand this, we will be more careful about the company we keep, remembering the words of Isaiah, who warned: "Associate yourselves, people, and you will certainly crash together."
TO ASSOCIATE WITH PEOPLE OF DIFFERENT OPINIONS
13. To what extent is it possible to associate with others without being influenced by their questionable practices, especially when celebrating holidays with them?
13 Associating with others can sometimes lead to compromising principles, particularly during holiday celebrations. For instance, those around us might encourage us to engage in activities that conflict with our beliefs. Have you ever felt pressured to participate in something you were uncomfortable with simply because everyone else was doing it? Perhaps you have been asked to join in a practice that goes against your conscience. Could it be that your children are exposed to harmful influences through their friends?
14, 15. How then can you maintain your integrity during holidays or when faced with pressure from others?
14 It is important to know where you stand and what you believe. For example, if you are invited to an event that violates your conscience, you can politely decline. But what if the invitation comes from a family member or close friend? You can still respectfully explain your position without causing offense. Many Christians find it helpful to prepare beforehand. The Bible states: "Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to respond to each person." (Colossians 4:6) Consider some examples. Think about your own situation. Examine your convictions carefully. If you feel uncertain about whether to attend certain gatherings or associate with particular individuals, pray for guidance—and be willing to accept the answer you receive.
15 What if someone pressures you to compromise your standards? You can calmly explain the reason for your stance. For instance, you might say: "I appreciate the invitation, but I would like to maintain my integrity." You can refuse to participate in something you believe is wrong without ruining the relationship. If they continue to pressure you, remember that your primary loyalty is to Jehovah and maintaining a good standing with him. This will help you to tactfully explain why you cannot go along with their request, or even why you choose not to. Let us strive to avoid situations where we are tempted to compromise our integrity because of fear, affection, or a desire to please others.
ARE THERE BENEFITS TO STANDING FIRM?
16 Can you think of ways to use your words to encourage others who are facing similar challenges?
16 What if someone pressures fellow Christians, causing them to feel uncomfortable or guilty about a certain activity? Speak up! Offer support to those who may be struggling to remain steadfast, and remind them that they are not alone. Remember what you have learned and share it with others. (Matthew 7:
17 Will you defend your children even if it means going against popular opinion?
17 Would you hesitate to defend your children if they were wrongly accused of doing something harmful, even if it meant disagreeing with others? Don't be afraid to speak up and defend what is right. Sometimes, defending your children requires courage and conviction. Maintaining integrity involves teaching your children the importance of principles and helping them develop a love for truth.
LEARN FROM OTHERS' EXPERIENCE
18 When dealing with difficult situations, can you benefit from learning from the experiences of other Christians?
18 If you seek God's guidance, will you be willing to learn from the wisdom of others and apply their insights to your own life? Consider this advice: "Let us think of ways to encourage each other to show love and to do good deeds. Let us not neglect our meetings together, as some people do, but encourage one another, especially as the day approaches." (Hebrews 10:
19 Is it appropriate to judge others based on personal preferences when the Bible provides clear guidance?
19 Another way to demonstrate respect for others is to help those who need assistance, just as Jehovah helped the ancient Israelites. Many people 'mark themselves with a sign' because they feel deeply affected by someone's death. (Ezekiel 9:4) But some may mark themselves and grieve excessively. We should avoid judging them harshly. Continue to associate closely with fellow Christians and help those who need encouragement, remembering that spiritual strength can be contagious. Be diligent in examining yourself and making adjustments if necessary.

text:
"Mũalyũkw'e mũtũngwe eũ ilĩkonĩ syenyu."—ALO. 12:2.
MBATHI: 29, 52
1-3. (a) Nĩ moalyũku ta meva matonya kwĩthĩwa me vinya kwĩka mũndũ aminĩte kũvatiswa? (b) Nĩ makũlyo meva tũtonya kwĩkũlya ethĩwa twĩĩw'a kwĩka maendeeo kwĩ vinya mbee wa ũndũ twasũanĩaa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
ĨLA Kevin [1] weemanyĩisye ũla w'o, kĩla wendaa mũno nĩ kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na Yeova. Ĩndĩ atambĩte kwĩmanyĩsya ũla w'o, aminĩte myaka mingĩ ekaa maũndũ ta kũtha kalata, kũnyw'a sikala, kũnyw'a ũkĩ mũno, na kũtũmĩa ndawa sya kũmila. Na kwoou nĩ kana etĩkĩlwe nĩ Ngai, aĩ no nginya aekane na mwĩkalĩle ũsu ũtosanĩte na Maandĩko. Na nĩ kana eanĩsye kĩu, amwĩkwatisye Yeova vamwe na ũtonyi ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ yake wa kũalyũla andũ.—Aevl. 4:12.
2 Ĩndĩ ĩla Kevin wavatisiwe nĩwaekie kwĩka moalyũku? Aiee, ndaaeka nũndũ aĩ no nginya ekĩe kĩthito aendeee kwĩthĩwa na nguma ila Aklĩsto maĩle kwĩthĩwa nasyo. (Aev. 4:31, 32) Kwa ngelekany'o, eethĩie kana kũtata ndakathatae mĩtũkĩ kwaĩ vinya mbee wa ũndũ wataĩaa. Kevin aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩsiĩĩa ndikathate mĩtũkĩ kwaĩ vinya mũno mbee wa kũekana na mothũku ala neekaa!" Kĩla kyesie kũtethya Kevin nĩ kũvoya na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo na kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kĩthito.
3 O ta Kevin, aingĩ maitũ tweekie moalyũku manene tũtambĩte kũvatiswa nĩ kana twĩkale kwosana na myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ. Ĩtina wa ũvatiso, nĩtwoonie ve vata wa kũendeea kwĩka moalyũku angĩ tũmaũndũnĩ tũla tũnini nĩ kana tũtate kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Ngai na Klĩsto nesanga. (Aev. 5:1, 2; 1 Vet. 2:21) Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩte kũmanya kana nĩwumanasya angĩ, wĩ wia wa andũ, wĩ nzukũ, kana wĩ wonzu o ũngĩ. We no kwĩthĩwa wonete kũkĩlya vinya mawonzu ta asu kwĩ vinya mbee wa ũndũ wasũanĩaa? Nũndũ wa ũu, no wĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Na now'o nĩkĩte moalyũku manenevete-ĩ, nĩemwa nĩ kwĩka tũmoalyũku tũũ tũnini nũndũ wa kyaũ? Ndonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana nĩendeee kwĩtĩkĩlya Mbivilia yĩke moalyũku nthĩnĩ wakwa?'
NDŨKONE TA ŨTESA KŨMWENDEESYA YEOVA
4. Nĩkĩ vethĩawa ve vinya kwitũ kũmwendeeasya Yeova kĩla ũndũnĩ?
4 Ithyĩ ala twĩsĩ Yeova na tũmwendete nĩtwĩthĩawa tũyenda kuma ngoonĩ kwĩka kĩla kĩmwendeeasya. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa twĩ na wendi wĩana ata wa kũmwendeesya Ngai, naĩ ĩla tũsyaĩtwe nayo ĩtumaa tũemwa vyũ nĩ kwĩanĩsya kyu ĩvinda yonthe. Twĩsaa kwĩthĩa tũyĩw'a ta mũtũmwa Vaulo, ũla waandĩkie: 'Kwenda kwĩ vo, ĩndĩ kwĩka ũla ũseo kũi vaĩ.'—Alo. 7:18; Yak. 3:2.
5. Nĩ moalyũku meva tweekie tũtanamba kũvatiswa? Nĩ mawonzu meva matonya kwĩthĩwa matũthĩnasya nginya ũmũnthĩ?
5 Nĩtwaekanie na mwĩkalĩle w'onthe ũla ũtonya kũtuma tũeka kũtalwa ta twĩ Aklĩsto. (1 Ako. 6:9, 10) Ĩndĩ o na twĩkĩte ũu, twĩ o andũ me na naĩ. (Ako. 3:9, 10) Kwoou ti ũndũ wosanĩte na kĩlĩko kũsũanĩa kana aĩ nũndũ nĩtwavatisiwe kana twĩkalĩte ũw'onĩ myaka mingĩ tũikavĩtya, kana tũikathĩnw'a ĩngĩ nĩ wonzu twaĩ naw'o tene, kana tũikaaĩsa kũthĩnw'a nĩ mawendi mathũku. No tũkue myaka tũyĩsa kũkĩlya mawonzu amwe vinya.
6, 7. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa twĩthĩwa tũtonya kũtanĩa ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova o na vala twĩ andũ me na naĩ? (b) Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kũemwa nĩ kũmwĩtya Yeova ũekeo?
6 O na kau tũsyaĩtwe na naĩ, naĩ ĩsu ndyaĩlĩte kũtũsiĩĩa kũtanĩa ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova kana kũendeea kũmũthũkũma. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ĩla Yeova watũkusisye kwake nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo nake, no weesĩ kana tũkavĩtasya mavinda kwa mavinda. (Yoa. 6:44) Nũndũ Ngai nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ tũilyĩ na kĩla kĩthĩawa ngoonĩ sitũ, we no weesĩ nesa vyũ mawonzu ala matonya kũtũthĩny'a mũno. Na nĩweesĩ tũikaleaa kũmũvĩtĩsya. Ĩndĩ o esĩ o ũu, kĩu kĩyaatuma alea kũtũtala ta anyanyae.
7 Wendo nĩw'o watumie Ngai atũnenga mũthĩnzĩo wa mwanya mũno, naw'o nĩ ĩla nthembo ya wovosyo ya Mwana wake mwendwa. (Yoa. 3:16) Ethĩwa tũkatũmĩaa nthembo ya wovosyo kwĩtya Yeova ũekeo, tũikethĩwe na nzika kana ndũũ yitũ nake ndĩkesa kũkw'a. (Alo. 7:24, 25; 1 Yoa. 2:1, 2) Nĩtwaĩle kũemwa nĩ kwĩtya ũekeo tũitũmĩa nthembo ya wovosyo aĩ nũndũ twĩĩw'a ta twĩ avuku kana twĩ na naĩ? Aiee, tũyaĩle! Kwĩka ũu no ũndũ ũmwe na kũlea kũtũmĩa kĩw'ũ tũthambe moko namo me na kĩko. Ndũkolwe kana wovosyo wĩ vo kwondũ wa ala mekwĩlila. Nĩtũtũngaa mũvea mũno kwondũ wa wovosyo, nĩkwĩthĩwa nũtũtetheeasya twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na Yeova o na kau twĩ ene naĩ.—Soma 1 Timotheo 1:15.
8. Nĩkĩ tũtaĩlĩte kũlekeleelya mawonzu maitũ?
8 Ũu ti kwonany'a kana tũimakaw'a nĩ mawonzu ala twĩ namo. Nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo na Yeova, twaĩlĩte kũtata tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yake na ya Klĩsto na tũyĩkala ũndũ mendaa. (Sav. 15:1-5) O na ĩngĩ twaĩlĩte kũkitana na mawonzu maitũ na tũimina ala tũtonya. Twĩthĩwe tũnavatisiwe o mĩtũkĩ kana twĩthĩĩtwe ũw'onĩ kwa myaka mingĩ, no nginya tũendeee 'kũtata twĩkale nesa.'—2 Ako. 13:11, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
9. Twĩsĩ ata kana kwĩvw'ĩka mũndũ mweũ nĩ ũndũ wa kũendeea?
9 Tũyaĩlĩte kwĩsa kũola kĩthito kitũ kya kũendeea kũtata 'twĩkale nesa' na kwĩvw'ĩka "mũndũ mweũ." Vaulo alilikanilye Aklĩsto ala angĩ ndeto ii: "Ũndũ wa mwĩkalĩle wenyu wa tene, mumyei mwĩkye kũasa mũndũ wa tene, ũla wanangĩkaa kwa ũvikĩlaa mĩmeo ya ũkengani; mũtw'ĩkĩthw'e eũ vevanĩ wa ilĩko syenyu, na mwĩvw'ĩke mũndũ mweũ, ũla wombiwe na mũvw'ano wa Ngai nthĩnĩ wa ũlũngalu na ũtheu wa w'o." (Aev. 4:22-24) Ndeto ĩla yaalyũlilwe "mũtw'ĩkĩthw'e eũ" yonanasya kana kwĩvw'ĩka mũndũ mweũ nĩ ũndũ wa kũendeea. Ũndũ ũsu nĩ wa kwendeesya nũndũ ũtũĩkĩĩthasya kana o na ethĩwa tũmũthũkũmĩte Yeova ĩvinda yĩana ata, no nginya tũendeee kwĩka maendeeo twĩthĩwe na nguma ila itumaa Mũklĩsto amanyĩka nĩwĩvw'ĩkĩte mũndũ mweũ. Kwoou vate nzika, Mbivilia nĩtonya kũendeea kũtũalyũla.
NĨKĨ ŨSU TI ŨNDŨ MŨVŨTHŨ?
10. Twaĩlĩte kwĩka ata ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda Mbivilia ĩtũtetheesye tũendeee kwĩka moalyũku, na nĩ makũlyo meva tũtonya kwĩkũlya?
10 Nĩ kana Ndeto ya Ngai ĩendeee kũtũalyũla, twaĩlĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito kingĩ? Ethĩwa Yeova nũathimaa kĩthito kitũ, nĩkĩ ĩndĩ ti ũndũ mũvũthũ kwĩka maendeeo? Tene we Yeova tyo atũvetangĩe mawonzu maitũ vyũ nĩ kana wĩthĩe nĩwatũvũthĩsya wĩa wa kũtata twĩthĩwe na nguma sya Kĩklĩsto?
11-13. Nĩkĩ Yeova wendaa twĩkĩe kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana tũkĩlye vinya mawonzu maitũ?
11 Ĩla twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila Yeova woombie nĩtũmanyaa kana e ũtonyi mwingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, syũa yĩ ũtonyi mwingĩ mũno. Kĩla sekendi yumasya kyeni kingĩ mũno na muutĩa mwingĩ mũno. O na kau no kaũtonyi kanini kayo kavikaa kũũ nthĩ, kaũtonyi kau nĩkeanĩte kũnenga syũmbe ila syĩ vaa nthĩ kyeni na muutĩa ũtoetye kũsyĩkalya thayũ. (Sav. 74:16; Isa. 40:26) O ta ũu, Yeova ew'aa mũyo ĩla ũkũnenga athũkũmi make ũtonyi ũla ũmeanĩtye ĩla me na vata naw'o. (Isa. 40:29) Ngai akenda no atũnenge ũtonyi ũkethĩa no tũkĩlye vinya wonzu o na wĩva tũte kũng'ang'ana mũno, o na tũte kũvĩtya vandũ. Nayu nĩkĩ ũtekaa ũu?
12 Yeova nũtũnengete mũthĩnzĩo wa mwanya vyũ, naw'o nĩ ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ĩla twanyuva kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai na twatata na kĩthito twĩanĩsye kyu, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtũmwendete mũno na nĩtwendete vyũ kũmwendeesya. O na ĩngĩ twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtũkwete mbau ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. Satani oonanisye kana Yeova ti we waĩlĩte kũsumbĩka, na kwoou ĩla tweeyumya na ngenda na tweekĩa kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana tũũkwate mbau, Ĩthe witũ wĩ wendo nĩwonaa kĩthito kĩu kĩ kya vata na nĩwĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ wa ũu. (Yovu 2: 3-5; Nth. 27:11) Keka Yeova ekaa o kũvetanga mawonzu maitũ ũkethĩa tũi na vata wa kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana tũmwendeesye, vayĩsa kwĩthĩwa na ũkũsĩ ũkwonany'a kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye nake na nĩtũkwete mbau ũsumbĩki wake mũnene.
13 Kyu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova ũtwĩĩte twĩthĩwe na "ũthangaau" nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na nguma sya Kĩklĩsto. (Soma 2 Vetelo 1:5-7; Ako. 3:12) Endaa twĩkĩe kĩthito tũikasumbĩkwe nĩ mosũanĩo maitũ na ngoo sitũ. (Alo. 8:5; 12:9) Twatata vyũ ũndũ tũtonya ũndũnĩ ũũ, nĩtwonaa ũndũ Mbivilia ĩendeee kũtũalyũla na kyu nĩkĩtumaa twĩw'a twĩ eanĩe.
ĨTĨKĨLYA NDETO YA NGAI ĨENDEEE KŨKŨALYŨLA
14, 15. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na nguma ila Yeova wendete? (Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Mbivilia na Mboya Nĩsyamaalyũlile.")
14 Nĩ kyaũ tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na nguma sya Kĩklĩsto na tũimwendeesya Yeova? Ve ũndũ ũngĩ twaĩle kwĩka eka o kwĩtw'ĩĩaa nĩ va tũkwona twaĩle kũalyũla. Twaĩlĩte kũendeea kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ na kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla Ngai ũtũnengete. Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 12:2 yaĩtye ũũ: "Mũikavw'ananw'e na nthĩ ĩno: ĩndĩ mũalyũkw'e mũtũngwe eũ ilĩkonĩ syenyu, nĩ kana mwĩkuũe ũndũ kũilyĩ kwenda kwa Ngai kũla kũseo na kũla kwĩtĩkĩlĩka na kũla kwĩanĩu." Yeova nũtũmĩaa Ndeto yake na veva wake mũtheu nĩ kana atũtetheesye tũelewe kwenda kwake, tũkwĩke, na tũialyũka ũndũ vatonyeka nĩ kana twĩkale ũndũ wendaa. Maũndũ amwe twaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito twĩanĩsye nĩ ta kũsoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya, kũsũanĩa kĩla twasoma Maandĩkonĩ, na kũvoya tũnengwe veva mũtheu. (Luka 11:13; Aka. 5:22, 23) Tweetĩkĩla kũtongoew'a nĩ veva mũtheu wa Ngai na twaeka woni witũ wosane na wa Yeova o tondũ ũvuanĩtw'e Ndetonĩ yake, tũkeethĩwa tũtonya kũvĩndũa mosũanĩo maitũ, ndeto sitũ, na meko maitũ mamwendeesye mũnango. Ĩndĩ o na twĩkĩte oou, no nginya twĩkale twĩ metho tũikese kũsindwa nĩ wonzu mũna ũtũthĩnasya.—Nth. 4:23.
15 Eka o kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai kĩla mũthenya, twĩ na vata wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩ Ndeto tũitũmĩa mavuku maitũ ma Kĩklĩsto, na tũyĩka ũu twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yeova. Angĩ nĩmatethetw'e nĩ mĩsoa na makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Amkeni! ala me na ũvoo ũtonya kũmatetheesya memanyĩsye kwĩthĩwa na nguma sya Kĩklĩsto na maikĩlya vinya mawonzu mana. Mombanasya mĩsoa ĩsu na maũvoo asu nĩ kana mekalae maimasoma ĩvinda kwa ĩvinda.
16. Nĩkĩ tũtaĩle kũkw'a ngoo twoona ta twĩkĩte moalyũku kavola?
16 Kwĩthĩwa na nguma sya Kĩklĩsto nĩ kĩndũ kĩkuaa ĩvinda, kwoou ndũkakw'e ngoo woona ta wĩkĩte moalyũku kavola. Kũtata twĩthĩwe na nguma isu nĩ ũndũ wa kũendeea. Kwoou no nginya twĩthĩwe na wũmĩĩsyo ĩla tũendeee kwĩkĩa kĩthito tũeke Mbivilia ĩtũtetheesye kwĩka moalyũku. No kwĩthĩwa mwambĩĩonĩ twaĩle kwĩsiĩĩa tũikese kwĩka maũndũ ala matosanĩte na Maandĩko. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda, o ũndũ twatata mesilya maitũ na meko maitũ mosane na ala ma Yeova Ngai, now'o tũtakew'aa vinya wa kwĩka maũndũ na kũsũanĩa o take.—Sav. 37:31; Nth. 23:12; Aka. 5:16, 17.
ĨKALAA ŨLILIKENE YĨLA ĨVINDA ĨSEO TWATHĨTWE
17. Twaendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova twĩ aĩkĩĩku tũkeethĩawa na wĩkwatyo wĩva mũseo?
17 Ala mamũthaithaa Yeova me aĩkĩĩku makesa kũkwata ndaĩa ya mwanya ya kũmũthũkũma tene na tene mate na naĩ. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu kwĩthĩwa na nguma sya Kĩklĩsto kũikethĩawa kwĩ vinya ĩndĩ kũkeethĩawa kwĩ mũyo. Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ nũndũ wa wovosyo, Ngai nũtwĩtĩkĩlaa tũmũthaithe. O na kau twĩ ene naĩ, nũtwĩtĩkĩlĩtye tũmũthaithe ethĩwa nĩtũkũeka Ndeto yake ĩendeee kũtũalyũla.
18, 19. Twĩsĩ ata kana Mbivilia yĩ na ũtonyi wa kũtũalyũla?
18 Ũla Kevin ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ, eekĩie kĩthito kingĩ mũno ayĩsa kũtw'ĩka nĩwaeka mũtuo wake wa kũthata mĩtũkĩ. Kĩndũ kĩmwe kyamũtethisye nĩ kũvindĩĩsya myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ na kũmĩatĩĩa, o na no watethiw'e nĩ kwĩtĩkĩla ũtethyo na ũtao wa Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Ĩtina wa myaka kauta, Kevin eekie moalyũku manene mũno. O na nĩwesie kũtw'ĩka mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi, na yu myaka 20 nĩ mĩthelu kuma atw'ĩka mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Ĩndĩ kũvika o nayu nĩwĩsĩ kana no nginya esũvĩe mũno ndakese kũsyoka vala waĩ.
19 Ngelekany'o ya Kevin yĩtũtetheesya kũmanya kana Mbivilia nĩtetheeasya andũ ma Ngai maendeee kwĩka moalyũku. Kwoou tũikaaĩse kwĩkĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai ngoo. Vandũ va ũu nĩtũendeei kũmĩtĩkĩlya ĩendeee kũtũalyũla na kũtũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na Yeova. (Sav. 25:14) Tweekĩa kĩthito na twoona ũndũ Yeova ũathimaa kĩthito kĩu, tũkamanyaa nesa vyũ kana Mbivilia yĩ na ũtonyi wa kũendeea kũtũalyũla.—Sav. 34:8.
