translation:
"Be loyal to the faithful slave."—MATT. 24:45.
NOTES: 29, 52
1-3. (a) How can loyalty help us resist temptation? (b) What benefits do we experience when we remain loyal despite difficulties? (Consider the example mentioned.)
BROTHER Kevin [1] learned this lesson, and his main reason was his desire to please Jehovah. He spent years practicing loyalty by resisting bad associations, avoiding worldly publications, refusing immoral entertainment, and rejecting blood transfusions. And he realized that doing so pleased God, and helped him maintain a close relationship with Him based on the Bible. And he found strength, as he clung to Jehovah and used the power of His spirit to preach the good news.—Eph. 4:12.
2 Why was Brother Kevin able to remain loyal? Yes, because he knew that remaining loyal would help him stay close to Jehovah and his fellow Christians, even though it meant facing opposition. (Eph. 4:31, 32) For instance, he admitted that sometimes it was difficult to refuse certain things that others offered. Kevin said: "Practicing loyalty has helped me say 'No' to things that could damage my spirituality!" The key to Kevin's success was prayer and diligent study of the Bible.
3 So like Kevin, many of us want to remain loyal despite pressures from the world and temptations we face. The reward for our loyalty is that we can continue to enjoy a close relationship with Jehovah and Christ. (Eph. 5:1, 2; 1 Pet. 2:21) However, what if you find yourself drawn to bad associations—perhaps through friends, magazines, or the internet? Would you be willing to make changes in your life, even if it means giving up something you enjoy, so as not to jeopardize your spirituality? If so, you might ask yourself, 'But how can I remain loyal when I am constantly exposed to worldly influences?' Then, perhaps you should pray, "Help me to resist worldly influences and to focus on more important spiritual matters."
KEEP LOYALTY A PRIORITY IN YOUR LIFE
4 How can we show that we are determined to remain loyal to Jehovah in everything we do?
4 Let us always remember that we love Jehovah and that we want to please him in everything we do. If we do not actively work at remaining loyal to God, we may gradually start to feel less loving and become indifferent to spiritual things. We need to be careful not to imitate the apostle Paul, who wrote: "What I do, I do not understand."—Rom. 7:18; Jas. 3:2.
5 What can help us to remain loyal? What questions can we ask ourselves when faced with temptation?
5 We can strengthen our determination to remain faithful by associating with fellow Christians. (1 Cor. 6:9, 10) Also, we can examine ourselves honestly. (Acts 3:9, 10) Consider whether you are spending too much time with people who do not share your values, whether you have been influenced by harmful publications or websites, or whether you have allowed yourself to get involved in questionable activities. Do not let years go by without addressing such problems.
6, 7. (a) What helps us to stay close to Jehovah and to maintain our zeal for preaching? (b) How can we show that we love Jehovah by obeying him?
6 And even if we stumble, we should not give up. Jehovah is willing to forgive us if we sincerely try to draw close to him and repent. Think about this: Jehovah has given us free will, so he allows us to make choices, even bad ones. (John 6:44) But God knows what is best for us, and he can help us to resist temptation. He can also strengthen our resolve. So, if we humbly pray for his guidance, he will help us to avoid serious mistakes.
7 Love is what moved God to provide the ransom sacrifice of his beloved Son. (John 3:16) Let us appreciate the value of the ransom and use it to demonstrate our gratitude to Jehovah by remaining obedient to him, even when faced with trials or persecution. (Acts 7:24, 25; 1 John 2:1, 2) Would we truly be showing appreciation for the ransom if we were to abandon our worship or become inactive? Certainly not! To do so would be like rejecting the very thing that makes our salvation possible. The ransom is a precious gift, and we must continue to rely on it. By doing so, we will remain close to Jehovah and enjoy his continued favor.—Read 1 Timothy 1:15.
8. How can we keep our hearts responsive?
8 This requires effort and vigilance on our part. If we maintain a strong relationship with Jehovah, we will strive to conform our thinking and conduct to his and Christ's standards and live a life pleasing to him. (Ps. 15:1-5) And we will also endeavor to deal honestly with ourselves and others. Even if we have been Christians for many years, we must continue "to work out [our] own salvation."—2 Pet. 13:11, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
9. Is it ever right to give up on someone?
9 We should be careful not to make it a habit to give up on people and to become discouraged. Paul reminded Christians with these words: "Let your manner of life be worthy of the good news you proclaim. Do not become immoral men, so that those who practice immorality may never find occasion to speak against you, but rather imitate you, and let your behavior be free from greed, and give attention to being brothers." (Eph. 4:22-24) The expression "give attention to being brothers" suggests that giving up on someone is not always right. Such a course would be especially unwise if there is still hope that we can help that person to appreciate Jehovah and respond to his loving provision through Christ. In fact, the Bible encourages us to keep trying to help others. The Bible does not encourage us to give up on people.
IS THIS A WRONG VIEW?
10. Should we be willing to study the Bible with someone again if he seems uninterested, and what reasons might we have for doing so?
10 If God's Word encourages us to persevere, why should we be willing to try once more? Is it possible that Jehovah has given us an assignment that will test our patience? And if so, could this be because He wants to see whether we will continue to show the same kindness toward others that Jesus showed?
11-13. Why does Jehovah want us to be patient with others, and how can we show that we are?
11 We are imperfect, yet Jehovah is understanding. For example, think about how much energy we have. Most of us get tired easily and need a lot of rest. Also, sometimes we may feel overwhelmed by problems, and those problems may seem insurmountable. (Ps. 74:16; Isa. 40:26) But remember, Jehovah gives strength to those who are weary and power to those who are feeling weak. (Isa. 40:29) God wants to help us to endure difficulties so that we can use our time and energy wisely and so that we can help others. So how can we do that?
12 Jehovah will give us wisdom from above, and wisdom is more than just knowledge. However, we need to seek God's guidance and pray earnestly, then we will be able to discern whether we are doing his will and whether we are progressing spiritually. And often we will be able to discern whether we deserve his favor. Satan has tried to make people believe that Jehovah is not generous, and he has deceived them into thinking that if we want something good, we must earn it ourselves. But our loving Father sees our efforts and appreciates them, and he will reward us generously. (Job 2:3-5; Prov. 27:11) Let Jehovah take care of our needs and concerns, and trust that if we are doing his will, he will help us to cope with challenges and will enable us to appreciate his generosity.
13 That is why Jehovah encourages us to be "moderate" in what we ask for and in our desires. (Read 2 Peter 1:5-7; Acts 3:12) We should always strive to please him and others. (Phil. 8:5; 12:9) We pray earnestly about this matter, and we see how the Bible helps us to understand things better, which motivates us to live differently.
TO HELP PEOPLE SEE THE TRUTH
14, 15. Why should we be willing to share the truth, even if people reject it? (See the box "The Bible Can Change Lives.")
14 How can we remain zealous in serving Jehovah despite opposition from people? One way is to remember that we want to help them learn the truth. We need to continue preaching diligently and trust that God will bless our efforts. The apostle Paul wrote at Romans 12:2: "Do not conform to this system of things, but transform yourselves by making your mind over." Jehovah gives us his Holy Spirit and provides us with powerful support, even when he allows us to face trials. This shows that he wants us to prove our loyalty, strengthen our faith, and appreciate the value of his friendship. Some ways we can show zeal include reading the Bible daily, meditating on what we read, and praying earnestly for guidance. (Luke 11:13; Acts 5:22, 23) By allowing God's spirit to direct us and by aligning ourselves with his purpose, we can remain determined to overcome obstacles, resist temptation, and maintain a good conscience. And even if we stumble, we can get up again and continue striving to please Jehovah.—Prov. 4:23.
15 In addition to reading God's Word daily, we should use the Bible to teach others about Christ and encourage them to live according to its principles. We can also benefit from attending meetings at Kingdom Halls and taking advantage of publications like The Watchtower and Awake!, which provide timely spiritual food. Let us make full use of these tools to stay strong spiritually and to help others find comfort and hope. Regularly reviewing our personal study notes can also help us retain information.
16 What can we do to stay motivated and continue preaching?
16 Staying busy in Christian activities is vital for maintaining motivation. Regular participation in the ministry helps us remain zealous. However, we need to be careful not to become overly ambitious and try to do too much. Instead, let us focus on making progress and diligently studying the Bible so that we can accurately represent God's Word. And when we encounter difficulties, let us seek guidance from the Scriptures. Above all, we must trust in Jehovah God and rely on his strength to help us succeed.—Prov. 37:31; Eccl. 23:12; Acts 5:16, 17.
KEEP REMEMBERING WHAT IS IMPORTANT
17 How can we show appreciation to Jehovah for all that he does for us?
17 One way to express our gratitude to Jehovah is by continuing to support his organization and zealously proclaiming his Kingdom. By staying busy in Christian activities, we strengthen our faith. Moreover, knowing that God cares for us encourages us to keep serving him faithfully and to conform our lives to his will.
18, 19 What practical steps can we take to stay motivated?
18 Kevin, a brother who was feeling discouraged, found it helpful to set realistic goals for himself. He began by focusing on personal study of the Bible and applying what he learned, as well as imitating the fine example of fellow Christians. Over time, Kevin regained his zeal. He also enjoyed sharing his experiences with others, and for 20 years he served as an elder, helping others to maintain their motivation. He realized that even though he may not always feel enthusiastic, he could still continue to serve faithfully.
19 Kevin's experience reminds us that the Bible can help people of all ages remain zealous. Let us examine ourselves to see whether we are living up to our dedication to God. May we all continue to seek ways to stay motivated and to be encouraged by our relationship with Jehovah. (Prov. 25:14) As we observe how Jehovah blesses our efforts, we will become more convinced than ever that the Bible has practical value.—Ps. 34:8.

text:
"Ndeto ya Ngai ĩ thayũ."—AEVL. 4:12.
MBATHI: 37, 43
1. (a) Ngai anengie Atamu wĩa wĩva? (b) Kuma ĩvinda yĩu andũ ma Ngai methĩĩtwe maitũmĩa kĩthyomo ata?
YEOVA NGAI oombie syũmbe syake syĩ na ũtonyi wa kũneena. Na ĩla wamũtwaie Atamu mũũndanĩ wa Eteni nĩwamũnengie wĩa wa kũtw'ĩĩa nyamũ masyĩtwa. Keka kũyaĩ kĩthyomo Atamu ndaĩ atonya wĩa ũsu. Atamu atũmĩie ũĩ ũla waĩ naw'o na kĩlĩko nĩ kana anenge kĩla nyamũ ĩsyĩtwa yĩla yaĩle. (Mwa. 2:19, 20) Kuma ĩvinda yĩu andũ ma Ngai methĩĩtwe maitũmĩa ũtonyi wa kũneena, kana wa kũtũmĩa kĩthyomo, kũmũtaĩa na kũtetheesya angĩ mamanye kwenda kwake. Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ, andũ ma Ngai nĩmatũmĩĩte kĩthyomo kwa nzĩa ya mwanya kũendeesya ũthaithi wa w'o, na nzĩa ĩsu ya mwanya nĩ kũalyũla Mbivilia.
2. (a) Ĩla kamitii yĩtawa New World Bible Translation Committee yatũmĩie myolooto yĩva ĩitethya wĩa wa kũalyũla? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
2 Mbivilia ila ialyũlĩtwe nĩ mbingĩ ĩndĩ imwe syĩthĩawa ialyũlĩtwe nesa kwĩ ingĩ. Myakanĩ ya 1940, kamitii yĩtawa New World Bible Translation Committee nĩyatwie kũtũmĩaa myolooto ĩtatũ ya kũalyũla Mbivilia, na myolooto ĩsu yu yĩthĩĩtwe ĩitũmĩwa nĩ aalyũli ma ithyomo mbee wa 130. Myolooto ĩsu nĩ: (1) Kũtaĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai kwa kũyĩtũngĩĩa vala yaĩle Maandĩkonĩ. (Soma Mathayo 6:9.) (2) Kũalyũla maandĩko ndeto kwa ndeto ethĩwa nĩvatonyeka, ĩndĩ ethĩwa vaitonyeka aalyũli maialyũla ũvoo ũsu kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũeleeka nesa. (3) Kũtũmĩa ndeto ite vinya nĩ kana wĩthĩe mũsomi nũkwendeew'a nĩ kũsoma. * (Soma Neemia 8:8, 12.) Kwaekai twĩmanyĩsye ũndũ myolooto ĩsu ĩtũmĩĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa kũalyũla Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ ya New World Translation ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya 2013, vamwe na ila ingĩ ite sya Kĩsũngũ.
MBIVILIA ĨTAĨAA ĨSYĨTWA YA NGAI
3, 4. (a) Nĩ mavuku meva ma tene methĩawa na ila nthoo syĩtawa Tetragrammaton? (b) Mbivilia mbingĩ syĩkanĩte ata na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai?
3 Andũ ala masomaa mavuku ma tene ma Mbivilia ma kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania, ta ala Mavuku ma Ũkanga wa Mũnyũ, nĩmaseng'aa mũno nũndũ wa kwona ũndũ ila nthoo syĩtawa Tetragrammaton singĩvĩte mavukunĩ asu. Isu nĩ ila nthoo inya sya Kĩevelania itũmĩawa kũandĩka ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Eka mavuku asu ma tene ma Kĩevelania, ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova no yonekaa nthĩnĩ wa kovi sya Septuagint ya Kĩkiliki, ila syaandĩkiwe katĩ wa myaka ta 200 Klĩsto ate mũsyae na myaka 100 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa.
4 O na kau maũndũ asu nĩmekũĩkĩĩthya nesa vyũ kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa yĩ Mbivilianĩ, aalyũli aingĩ nĩmavetangaa ĩsyĩtwa yĩu vyũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia ya New World Translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures yaumw'a mwakanĩ wa 1950, vathelile o myaka ĩlĩ na ĩndĩ Mbivilia yĩtawa Revised Standard Version yaumĩthw'a. Aalyũli ma Mbivilia ĩsu meekie kwosa ĩla Mbivilia ĩngĩ yĩtawa American Standard Version ya 1901 mamĩka moalyũku mavetete ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Nĩkĩ mayĩvetie? Ndeto sya mbee Mbivilianĩ ĩsu syaĩtye: "Kũtũmĩa ĩsyĩtwa o na yĩva kwondũ wa Ngai ũla ũmwe . . . kũyaĩlĩte o na vanini mũĩkĩĩonĩ wa Ĩkanisa yonthe ya Kĩklĩsto." Ĩla maminie kwĩka ũu matumie aalyũli ala angĩ ma Mbivilia sya Kĩsũngũ na ite sya Kĩsũngũ meka tamo.
5. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũekana na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai vala yaĩlĩte Mbivilianĩ?
5 Nĩkĩ ti ũndũ mũnini kũveta kana kũtũngĩĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai Mbivilianĩ? Mũalyũli wĩsĩ wĩa wake nesa nĩwĩsĩ kana nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũelewa nesa kĩeleelo kya mũandĩki wa ũvoo ũla ũkũalyũla. Kũmanya ũu nĩkũmũtongoeasya ĩla ũkũtethya wĩa wake nĩ kana eke motwi ala maĩlĩte. Ve mĩsoa mingĩ mũno Mbivilianĩ yonanĩtye vata wa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai na vata wa kũthew'a kwayo. (Kuma 3:15; Sav. 83:18; 148:13; Isa. 42:8; 43:10; Yoa. 17:6, 26; Meko 15:14) Yeova Ngai nĩwe Mũandĩkĩthya wa Mbivilia na aveveeie aandĩki mayo matũmĩe ĩsyĩtwa yake mateũkĩa. (Soma Esekieli 38:23.) Kwoou kũvetanga ĩsyĩtwa yĩkwatĩkanaa mavukunĩ ala ma tene mavinda ngili kauta kwonanasya kana mũndũ ndeũnenga Mũandĩkĩthya wa Mbivilia ndaĩa.
6. Nĩkĩ Mbivilia ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya New World Translation yongelete ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai mavinda angĩ thanthatũ?
6 Ũmũnthĩ maũndũ ala mekwonany'a kana nĩtwaĩlĩte kũtũmĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai maendeee kwongeleka. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia ya New World Translation ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya 2013 yĩ na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai mavinda 7,216. Ũu nĩ kwonany'a kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyonekaa mavinda angĩ 6 mate ĩla Mbivilianĩ ĩngĩ ya 1984. Mavinda atano katĩ wa asu me ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Samueli 2:25; 6:3; 10:26; 23:14, 16. Ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yatũngĩiwe mĩsoanĩ ĩsu ĩtano nũndũ ala Mavuku ma Ũkanga wa Mũnyũ me na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai mĩsoanĩ ĩsu. Mavuku asu ma Ũkanga wa Mũnyũ makũĩe ala maandĩkiwe na kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania nĩ andũ meetawa Masoretes na myaka mbee wa 1,000. O na ĩngĩ ĩtina wa kũsoma mũnango mavuku angĩ ma tene, ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩyatũngiwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Asili 19:18.
7, 8. Ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yonanasya kyaũ?
7 Aklĩsto ma w'o monaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩ ya vata mũno. Ũvoo wa kwongeleela ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ya New World Translation ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya 2013 nũeleetye ũndũ ũsu nesanga. Ĩla kamitii yĩtawa New World Bible Translation Committee nĩeleawa nesa kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yumanĩte na ndeto ya Kĩevelania ha·wah,' ĩla ũalyũlo wayo nĩ "Ũla Ũtumaa Kwĩthĩwa." * Navu tene mavuku maitũ manaeleasya kĩla kyonanaw'a nĩ ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova matũmĩĩte ndeto ila iwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Kuma 3:14, yĩla yaĩtye: "Ninyie Ũla Ninyie." Kyu nĩkyo kyatumie Mbivilia ya New World Translation ya 1984 yasya kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yonanasya kana "we mwene nũtumaa ethĩwa Mwĩanĩsya wa mawatho." * Ĩndĩ ũvoo wa kwongeleela namba A4 wa Mbivilia ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya 2013 waĩtye ũũ: "O na kau ĩsyĩtwa Yeova no yonany'e kana nũtumaa ethĩwa kĩla ũkwenda kũtw'ĩka, yĩyonanasya o ũu wĩ w'oka. No yonanasya kana nũtumaa syũmbe syake syĩthĩwa kĩla kĩkwendeka, kana akatuma ũndũ mũna wĩkĩka nĩ kana eanĩsye kĩeleelo kyake."
8 Yeova nũtumaa syũmbe syake syĩthĩwa kĩla ũkwenda. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwosana na kĩla ĩsyĩtwa yake yonanasya, Ngai nĩwatumie Noa atw'ĩka vundi wa ngalawa, atuma Mbesaleli atw'ĩka ndũĩka ya kũseũvya syĩndũ, atuma Ngiteoni atw'ĩka ngũmbaũ ya kaũ, na atuma Vaulo atw'ĩka mũtũmwa kwa mbaĩ ingĩ. Maũndũ asu meonany'a kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai nĩ ya vata mũno andũnĩ make. Na ĩla kamitii yĩtawa New World Bible Translation Committee ndyaĩ ĩvũthĩĩsya ũndũ ũsu kwa kũveta ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai Mbivilianĩ.
9. Nĩ ũndũ ũmwe wĩva mũnene ũtumĩte kwĩkĩwa kĩthito kingĩ mũno kya kũalyũla Mbivilia na ithyomo ingĩ?
9 Mbivilia ya New World Translation, ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe kwa ithyomo mbee wa 130, nĩnengete ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai ndaĩa nũndũ yĩ na ĩsyĩtwa yĩu vala yaĩlĩte. (Soma Malaki 3:16.) Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ila ialyũlawa matukũ aa iyĩthĩawa na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Vandũ va ũu syĩ na masyĩtwa ma ũnene ta "Mwĩaĩi" kana masyĩtwa ma ngai sya kĩthĩo. Kĩu nĩ kĩtumi kĩmwe kĩnene kĩtumĩte Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ĩtata ũndũ vatonyeka ĩĩkĩĩthye kana andũ aingĩ vyũ nĩmakwata Mbivilia ĩla ĩnengete ndaĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai.
MBIVILIA ĨALYŨLĨTWE NESA NA ĨTE VINYA KŨELEEKA
10, 11. Aalyũli ma Mbivilia ila ite sya Kĩsũngũ sya New World Translation makomanie na mathĩna meva maialyũla?
10 Ala matethetye wĩa wa kũalyũla Mbivilia ya New World Translation na ithyomo ingĩ nĩmakomanĩte na mathĩna maingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, o ta Mbivilia ingĩ sya Kĩsũngũ, tene Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ ya New World Translation yatũmĩaa ndeto ya Kĩevelania "Seoli" (Sheol) mĩsoanĩ ta Mũtavan'ya 9:10. Tene mũsoa ũsu waasyaa ũũ Mbivilianĩ ĩsu: "Kũi wĩa kana ũsũanĩo kana ũmanyi kana ũĩ Seoli, vala ũendete." Aalyũli aingĩ ma ithyomo ite sya Kĩsũngũ maĩ na thĩna ũũ: Ndeto "Seoli" ndĩsĩkĩe nĩ aingĩ ma ala maneenaa ithyomo syoo, o na ndĩ mavukunĩ ala maeleasya ndeto, na ĩsomekaa ũu ta ĩsyĩtwa ya vandũ. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu aalyũli nĩmanengiwe mwanya maalyũle ndeto ĩsu "Seoli" (Kĩevelania) na ĩla ĩngĩ "Andesi" (Kĩkiliki) maitũmĩa ndeto "Mbũa." Ndeto ĩsu nĩyaĩlĩte na nĩtumaa andũ maelewa nesa kĩla meũsoma.
11 Namo aalyũli ma ithyomo ingĩ maĩ na thĩna wa kũtũmĩa ndeto o ĩla ĩla kũalyũla ndeto ya Kĩevelania neʹphesh na ya Kĩkiliki psy·kheʹ, o tondũ aalyũli ma Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ matũmĩĩte ndeto "soul" (thayũ) kw'onthe kũla kwaĩ na ndeto isu. Thĩna waĩ va? Ndeto ĩla maĩ matonya kũtũmĩa yatumaa wĩthĩa ne laisi mũndũ kwona thayũ ta kĩndũ kĩtonekaa kĩ mũndũnĩ. Ũndũ ũsu waĩ ũtonya kũtuma mũndũ ona thayũ ta ĩimũ kana ĩveva ya mũndũ ĩndĩ ti ũ mũndũ mwene. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, aalyũli nĩmanengiwe mwanya maalyũlae ndeto ĩsu kwosana na kĩla kĩũneenewa vau maatĩĩe ũvoo wa kwongeleela wa Mbivilia ya New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References. Kwoou kĩla kyoonekie kĩ kya vata vyũ nĩ kũtetheesya andũ maelewe mĩsoa ĩla yĩ na ndeto ĩsu mateũthĩna, na mavinda maingĩ aalyũli makomana na ndeto ĩsu nĩmeekĩaa maelesyo ma kwongeleela nĩ kana matetheesye mũsomi aelewe kĩla kĩũwetwa.
12. Nĩ moalyũku ta meva meekiwe Mbivilianĩ ya New World Translation ya 2013? (No ũsisye kĩlungu kĩĩ, "Mbivilia Ĩla Yĩkĩtwe Moalyũku ya 2013 ya New World Translation," ĩkasetinĩ yĩĩ.)
12 Makũlyo ala aalyũli makũlilye maialyũla nĩmatumie vamanyĩka kana vaĩ ndeto ingĩ o ta isu syaĩ itonya kũeleeka naĩ. Kwoou kwĩ Mwei wa 9, 2007, Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye nĩyanenganie mwanya Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ yĩkwe moalyũku. Ala manengiwe wĩa ũsu nĩmasyokeleeile makũlyo ngili mbingĩ ala makũlĩtw'e nĩ ala maalyũlaa Mbivilia na ithyomo ingĩ. Ndeto sya Kĩsũngũ ila syavĩtiwe nĩ ĩvinda nĩsyavetangiwe na vatũmĩwa ila sya matukũ aa, na aalyũli asu ma Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ nĩmeekĩie kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana matũmĩe ndeto ite vinya kũeleeka ĩndĩ ialyũlĩtwe ũndũ vaĩle. Kwoou kũatĩĩa kĩla aalyũli ma ithyomo ingĩ meekie nĩkwanoie ndeto ila itũmĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ ya Kĩsũngũ.—Nth. 27:17.
ŨNDŨ ANDŨ MATŨNGĨTE MŨVEA WINGĨVĨTE
13. Andũ aingĩ mekĩte ata ĩtina wa kũkwata Mbivilia ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya 2013?
13 Andũ methĩĩtwe na woni mwaũ kuma makwata Mbivilia ya Kĩsũngũ ya New World Translation? Aingĩ nĩmatũmĩte valũa syoo sya kũtũnga mũvea ovisinĩ mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũla wĩ Brooklyn. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩ kana ũelewe ũndũ aingĩ meewie, no ũsũanĩe ndeto ii mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe waandĩkie: "Mbivilia ĩilyĩ ĩsandũkũ yusũĩte tũvila twa thooa mũnene. Kwoou kũsoma ndeto sya Yeova ũitũmĩa Mbivilia ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku ya 2013 no ũndũ ũmwe na kũsisya nesa kĩla kavila wone ũndũ kailyĩ, ũndũ katheete, ũndũ ke na langi ũilyĩ, na ũndũ kanakavĩte. Nũndũ Maandĩko asu maalyũlĩtwe na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi, nĩmandetheesye nĩelewe Yeova nesanga, na kĩu kĩtumaa nĩw'a ta ngũsomewa nĩ ĩthe wakwa ndeto syake syĩ na mũyo angwatĩlĩte kĩtuo."
14, 15. Mbivilia ya New World Translation ya ithyomo ingĩ ĩtumĩte andũ methĩwa na woni mwaũ?
14 Mbivilia ya New World Translation ya Kĩsũngũ ti yo yĩ yoka ĩtumĩte andũ mew'a mũyo. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Kwasũanĩa ndeto sya mũtumĩa ũmwe umĩte vandũ vetawa Sofia, Bulgaria. Aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia ya kĩthyomo kya Bulgarian: "Nĩsomete Mbivilia myaka mingĩ, ĩndĩ ndyaasoma Mbivilia ĩalyũlĩtwe nesa ta ĩno yĩ laisi kũeleeka, na yĩ na ndeto iũlika ngoonĩ ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe." O ta ũu, ĩla mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe kuma Albania wakwatie Mbivilia ya New World Translation aisye atĩĩ: "Ndeto ya Ngai ko ĩte mũyo kĩthyomonĩ kya Albanian! Nĩ ndaĩa nene mũno kũmwĩthukĩĩsya Yeova aineena naitũ atũmĩĩte kĩthyomo kitũ!"
15 Kũndũ kwingĩ Mbivilia itesawa mbesa mbingĩ na kũsyona nĩ thĩna, kwoou kũkwata Mbivilia o ĩmwe nĩ ũathimo mũnene. Livoti ĩmwe kuma nthĩ ya Rwanda yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kwa ĩvinda ĩasa, andũ aingĩ ala mamanyĩaw'a Mbivilia nĩ ana-a-asa mayeekaa maendeeo nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa mate na Mbivilia. Mayaĩ na ũtonyi wa kũthooa Mbivilia ila syatesawa nĩ makanisa ma kũu kwoo. Na mavinda maingĩ mayaeleawa nesa mĩsoa mĩna na kwoou weethĩaa mayĩka maendeeo." Ĩndĩ maũndũ nĩmavĩndũkie ĩla makwatie Mbivilia ya New World Translation kĩthyomonĩ kyoo. Mũsyĩ ũmwe wa kuma Rwanda wĩ na syana inya sya mũika waisye atĩĩ: "Twĩmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea mũno vamwe na ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ nũndũ wa kũtũnenga Mbivilia ĩno. Twĩ ngya na tũinaĩ twona mbesa sya kũthooa Mbivilia itwĩanĩe. Ĩndĩ yu kĩla ũmwe e na Mbivilia yake mwene. Nĩ kana tũmwony'e Yeova kana nĩtũmũtũngĩaa mũvea, tũmbanaa ithyonthe ta mũsyĩ kĩla mũthenya nĩ kana tũmĩsome."
16, 17. (a) Yeova endaa ata? (b) Twaĩlĩte kũtw'a kwĩka ata?
16 Mbivilia ya New World Translation ĩkesa kũalyũlwa na ithyomo ingĩ mbingangĩ. O na kau Satani nũtataa mũno kũsiĩĩa ũndũ ũsu ndũkeanĩe, nĩtwĩsĩ kana Yeova endaa andũ make onthe mamwĩthukĩĩsye aimaneeny'a na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi na kĩkũeleeka. (Soma Isaia 30:21.) Mũthenya ũkavika ĩla "nthĩ ĩkausũw'a nĩ kũmũmanya Yeova, o tondũ manzĩ mekunĩkĩlye ũkanga."—Isa. 11:9.
17 Nĩtũtw'ei vyũ tũtũmĩe nesa mĩthĩnzĩo yonthe ĩla tũnengetwe nĩ Yeova. Mũthĩnzĩo ũmwe nĩ ĩla Mbivilia ĩnengete ndaĩa ĩsyĩtwa yake. Mwĩtĩkĩlye aneene naku kĩla mũthenya aitũmĩa Ndeto yake. Na nũndũ e na ũtonyi mwingĩ, no atwĩthukĩĩsye nesa ĩla tũũmũvoya. Kũea ngewa na Yeova kwa nzĩa isu kũtumaa tũmũmanya nesanga na nĩkũtumaa tũmwenda mũnango.—Yoa. 17:3.
^ kal. 2 Sisya ũvoo wa kwongeleela namba A1 nthĩnĩ wa New World Translation ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku, na kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, "Jinsi ya Kuchagua Tafsiri Nzuri ya Biblia," ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/05/2008.
^ kal. 7 Mavuku amwe nĩmaeleetye ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai ũu o na kau ti asomi onthe metĩkĩlanaa ũndũnĩ ũsu.
^ kal. 7 Sisya ũvoo wa kwongeleela namba 1A ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ya New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References, wĩ na kyongo,"The Divine Name in the Hebrew Scriptures," ĩth. 1561.

translation:
"God's sword is two-edged."—Heb. 4:12.
FOOTNOTES: 37, 43
1. (a) How did God view Adam's decision? (b) Why can we be sure that God's standards have not changed?
JEHOVAH shows his personality through his speech and his way of communicating. And because he loves Adam, a descendant of Seth, he showed him how to worship acceptably. Allow this scripture to help Adam understand what he must do. Adam used his free will, and whether he chooses to obey or not depends on him. (Gen. 2:19, 20) Why can we be sure that God's standards regarding speech, or how to worship, have not changed, and that they are still valid? Over the centuries, God's people have used his Word to guide them in applying principles correctly, and another way to apply principles is by studying the Bible.
2. (a) What motivated the New World Bible Translation Committee to produce an accurate translation? (b) What should we aim for when doing our personal study?
2 The Bible has been translated into many languages, some of which are more accurate than others. In the 1940's, the New World Bible Translation Committee was assigned to prepare new translations of the Bible, and their work resulted in over 130 different language editions. Their goals were: (1) To restore God's name by using his personal name Jehovah throughout the Scriptures. (Read Matthew 6:9.) (2) To translate the scriptures literally as far as possible, so that even inexperienced translators could use the translation to convey the meaning accurately. (3) To use simple wording that would make the scriptures easy to read and understand. * (Read Nehemiah 8:8, 12.) As we appreciate these goals, we can better value the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures, which was updated in 2013, along with several other translations.
THE BIBLE RESTORES GOD'S NAME
3, 4. (a) What evidence indicates that ancient copies of the Hebrew Scriptures contained the Tetragrammaton? (b) Does most of the Bible mention God's name?
3 Many who have studied ancient manuscripts of the Bible, such as the Dead Sea Scrolls, have noticed that the Tetragrammaton frequently appeared in those texts. It is this Tetragrammaton that was used to write God's name. Besides these ancient Hebrew manuscripts, God's name Jehovah also appears in the Greek Septuagint version, which was written between 200 BCE and 100 CE.
4 However, some translations omit God's name altogether, while others render it only a few times. For example, the New World Translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures published in 1950 closely follows the Revised Standard Version. Other Bible translators, like those of the American Standard Version of 1901, often replace God's name. Why is this done? The preface to one Bible says: "To use the name at all . . . implies that we know how to pronounce it correctly." But this reasoning does not justify the omission of God's name in numerous translations of the Holy Scriptures.
5 Then, what about being consistent with God's name as found in the ancient manuscripts?
5 Is it really important to restore or emphasize God's name in the Bible? Many feel that it is not essential, or that it is difficult to determine the correct pronunciation of God's name. Knowing this can help us appreciate why some translators choose to omit it. Yet, on many occasions the Bible itself shows the importance of God's name and of honoring it. (Ps. 3:15; 83:18; 148:13; Isa. 42:8; 43:10; John 17:6, 26; Acts 15:14) Jehovah God is the Author of the Bible, and he wants people to know his name. (Read Ezekiel 38:23.) Therefore, restoring God's name accurately helps individuals to magnify and honor the Author of the Bible.
6 Does the New World Translation alone give prominence to God's name more than most other modern translations?
6 The number of times God's name appears continues to increase. For example, the 2013 edition of the New World Translation includes God's name 7,216 times. This compares with about 6,000 occurrences in the 1984 edition. Five of those additions are found at 1 Samuel 2:25; 6:3; 10:26; 23:14, 16. God's name was restored in five other places because of discoveries made in ancient manuscripts. Ancient copies of the Hebrew Scriptures were carefully preserved by a group of men called the Masoretes over a period of about 1,000 years. And in further study of ancient manuscripts, God's name was restored at Genesis 19:18.
7, 8 What does knowing Jehovah's name accomplish?
7 True Christians value knowing Jehovah's name. The foreword to the 2013 edition of the New World Translation highlights this important point. It states that the New World Bible Translation Committee learned that Jehovah's name is represented by the Tetragrammaton, 'YHWH,' which literally means "I Am That I Am." * However, many ancient manuscripts use what is known as the Tetragrammaton to represent God's name, as indicated at Psalm 3:14, which reads: "You Are Jehovah." This is why the 1984 New World Translation rendered Jehovah's name as "Jehovah" rather than as a title. * The updated foreword on page A4 of the 2013 edition explains: "And so the name Jehovah is used throughout this translation, where it appeared in the original Hebrew texts. It also represents the personal name of God when referring to his self-declaration, 'I Am.' And it represents his purpose concerning mankind."
8 Jehovah uses his active forces to accomplish his will. For example, to save Noah and his family from the flood, God sent an angel; to free Israel from slavery, he sent Moses; to deliver Gideon and his army, he sent an angel; and to preach the good news, he sent Paul. These examples show that God's active forces are effective in helping his servants. And the New World Bible Translation Committee recognized this fact when they decided to restore God's name in their translation of the Bible.
9. Is there another compelling reason to study the Bible and other publications?
9 The New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures, which has been published in over 130 languages, restores God's name throughout its pages. (Read Malachi 3:16.) This Bible, however, is not the only publication that highlights God's name. Many people use nicknames for God, such as "the Lord" or names of false gods. This is one reason why the Watch Tower Society publishes the magazine The Watchtower, so that people may come to know the Bible and appreciate God's name.
THE BIBLE IS BEING TRANSLATED AND MADE AVAILABLE
10, 11. What challenges have those involved in producing the New World Translation faced, and how have they met them?
10 Those who translate the New World Translation face many challenges. For example, some translations of the Bible use the Greek word "Sheol" at Matthew 9:10. But this translation says: "To hell, or Hades, or Gehenna, or Sheol, you go." Other similar expressions found in various translations include the term "Sheol," which can be confusing because it is used to refer to different places, and it does not help people understand what the Bible actually teaches. Therefore, translators often strive to replace the term "Sheol" (Greek) and others like "Hades" (Greek) with terms like "grave." These terms are more accurate and help readers better understand the meaning.
11 Also, other translators try to use terms or words to translate the Greek words nephesh and psyche, while Bible translators use the word "soul" consistently throughout. Why is this? The terms they use can make someone think of the soul as something invisible about a person. This can lead someone to believe that the soul is an immortal part of a person. Therefore, translators often strive to replace those terms with something that accurately reflects what the scriptures teach, as shown in the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—With References. Every effort has been made to help people understand these terms and the many references translators have made regarding them to further assist the reader in understanding each point.
12 Is there a reason why the 2013 edition of the New World Translation was revised? (Please see the brochure, "The New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures—Revised Edition," for details.)
12 Many translators revise their translations based on increased knowledge or new terms, so it is possible to improve them. On September 9, 2007, the Governing Body authorized a revision of the Swahili Bible. This revision was done to ensure consistency with other translations of the Bible. The Swahili terms used were updated to reflect current usage, and translators of the Swahili Bible included footnotes to explain certain terms and provide insight for readers. In order to maintain consistency with the Swahili Bible, translators of other languages should also use similar terms.—Prov. 27:17.
IMPORTANT POINTS TO REMEMBER
13 Why do many people want to have a Bible that has been revised in 2013?
13 Many people appreciate having a copy of the Swahili New World Translation Bible. They often send letters to the world headquarters of Jehovah's Witnesses in Brooklyn. For example, some may write, "This Bible is very helpful because it uses simple language. By reading the footnotes in this Bible that was revised in 2013, I can understand things more clearly, and I am able to remember important points, difficult concepts, and scriptures. It helps me to see how the Scriptures apply to my life, and it motivates me to continue studying God's Word."
14, 15 How does the New World Translation help many people to understand spiritual matters?
14 The Swahili New World Translation is not the only Bible that has helped people to learn about God. Why is this so? Consider the experience of a sister named Sofía from Bulgaria. She wrote: "I have been reading the Bible for many years, but I never really understood it until I started reading this easy-to-understand translation, especially with the footnotes." Also, a brother in Albania wrote: "The Bible is now clear in Albanian! I deeply appreciate Jehovah for providing us with this translation!"
15 Many Bibles are available in various languages, and having a Bible of your own can be very encouraging. A sister from Rwanda said: "In recent times, many people who did not know how to read have become interested in learning so they can read the Bible. They often go to the large churches to get a Bible. And many have come to understand its message through those efforts." Indeed, many have obtained a New World Translation in their language. Another Rwandan brother, who has eight children, wrote: "We thank Jehovah very much for giving us the Bible in our language so that we can study it. We also pray that we will always have the opportunity to preach. Everyone should have his own Bible. Whether we show our gratitude to Jehovah by our words or by our actions, we should regularly read our Bible."
16, 17. (a) What does Jehovah want us to do? (b) How can we show that we value it?
16 The New World Translation is available in more and more languages. But Satan continues to try to deceive people and prevent them from understanding God's Word, so we must trust that Jehovah helps his faithful ones to discern truth from falsehood. (Read Isaiah 30:21.) Daily, we can prove that "the direction of the righteous is what is pleasing to Jehovah, but the counsel of the wicked leads to ruin."—Isa. 11:9.
17 Let us use all the provisions Jehovah makes available to us. One provision is the Bible itself, which is now available in many languages. Appreciate it and read it daily, applying its principles to your life. And with great effort, let us continue to seek to understand it. Getting to know Jehovah better through his Word leads to greater love for him.—John 17:3.
^ See the article "How to Choose a Good Bible Translation" in The Watchtower of May 1, 2008.
^ For information about other translations, see the website www.jw.org.
^ See the article "The Divine Name in the Hebrew Scriptures," pages 156-161 of the reference edition of the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures.

"Mũkĩelekan'ya na ala meũtiĩwa matho kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo na wũmĩĩsyo."—AEVL. 6:12.
MBATHI: 3, 54
1, 2. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva wĩ vinya wakwatie Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake?
MWĨĨTU wa Yevitha aumie asembete akathaũe ĩthe. Eew'aa mũyo nũndũ wa ĩthe kuma kaũnĩ e mũima na asindĩte. Ĩndĩ ĩla ĩthe wamwonie, vandũ va kũtana eekie kũtembũa ngũa ila weekĩĩte syathokoanĩĩte kaũnĩ, na aĩa ayasya: "Ĩiaa, mwĩĩtu wakwa! nĩwantheesya mũno." Ĩtina wa ũu, ndeto ila Yevitha wawetie nĩsyatumie maũndũ ma mwĩĩtu ũsu mavĩndũka vamwe na mĩvango ĩla ĩngĩ waĩ nayo ya kwĩkala ta aka ala angĩ. Ĩndĩ mwĩĩtu ũsu ate kwananga saa nĩwasũngĩie ĩthe nesa na amwĩkĩa vinya eanĩsye kĩla wamwathĩte Yeova. Ndeto syake syonanasya kana aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Nĩwaĩkĩĩte kana Yeova ndaĩ amũkũlya eke ũndũ wĩsĩ ndũmũuna. (Asi. 11:34-37) Ĩthe wa mwĩĩtu ũsu nĩweewie mũyo mũno nũndũ nĩweesĩ kana ĩla mwĩĩtu wake weetĩkĩlile kũmũkwata mbau nĩwatumie Yeova amenda.
2 Yevitha na mwĩĩtu ũsu wake waĩ na kĩkĩo kya Ngai mayaĩ na nzika kana Yeova ekaa maũndũ na nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte vyũ, o na ĩla maũndũ asu mekwoneka me metu vyũ. Nĩmeesĩ nesa vyũ kana kwendwa nĩ Ngai nĩ kwa vata vyũ kwĩ kĩla mũndũ ũtonya kwasya.
3. Nĩkĩ ngelekany'o ya Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake ĩtonya kũtũtethya mũno ũmũnthĩ?
3 Nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kana ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu vala ve Yeova. Ũw'o nĩ kana no nginya 'tũkitĩe ũla mũĩkĩĩo.' (Yuta 3) Nĩ kana tũmanye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ũu, ekai tũneenee matatwa ala Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake makĩlilye vinya. Nĩ kyaũ kyamatetheeisye maendeee kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vala ve Yeova?
NO TŨLŨMYE MŨĨKĨĨO O NA KAU NTHĨ ĨNO NĨ NTHŨKU
4, 5. (a) Yeova anengie Aisilaeli mwĩao wĩva ĩla malikile Nthĩ ya Watho? (b) Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Savuli 106, nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie mbaĩ ya Isilaeli nũndũ wa kũlea kwĩw'a?
4 Kĩla mũthenya Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake nĩmeeyoneaa ũthũku wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Yeova. Vakuvĩ myaka 300 ĩvinda ya Yevitha yĩte ĩviku, aaũmae moo meeaĩwe mamine mbaĩ syonthe ila syathaithaa ngai sya ũvũngũ, ila syatwĩe Nthĩ ĩsu ya Watho. (Kũt. 7:1-4) Na kwoou ĩla Aisilaeli maleile kũatĩĩa ũndũ meeĩtwe, nĩmambĩĩe kwĩkala ta Akanaani, na ũu watuma mambĩĩa kũthaitha ngai sya mũvw'anano na kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalo mũthũku vyũ.—Soma Savuli 106:34-39.
5 Kũlea kũmwĩw'a Yeova nĩkwatumie aeka kũmenda na kwoou aeka kũmasũvĩa. (Asi. 2:1-3, 11-15; Sav. 106:40-43) Waĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya mũno kwa mĩsyĩ ĩla yaĩ na kĩkĩo kya Ngai kũendeea kwĩkala ĩlũmanĩtye nake ĩvindanĩ yĩu yũmũ. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana kwaĩ andũ maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yevitha, mwĩĩtu wake, Elikana, Aana, o na Samueli nĩmatataa vyũ mendwe nĩ Ngai.—1 Sam. 1:20-28; 2:26.
6. Andũ ma nthĩ ũmũnthĩ methĩawa mailyĩ ata, na twaĩlĩte kwĩka ata?
6 Twĩkalĩte nthĩ yĩ na andũ masũanĩaa o tondũ Akanaani masũanĩaa, na mekaa maũndũ o tamo. Mendete ũlaalai na ũng'endu, na monaa kwĩthĩwa na malĩ taw'o ũndũ ũla wa vata. Yeova nũtũnengete mokany'o matevithanĩtye o tondũ wanengete Aisilaeli, nĩ kana atũsũvĩane na maũndũ ta asu mawetwa. We wasisya maũndũ ala makwatie Aisilaeli ve kĩndũ ũkwĩmanyĩsya? (1 Ako. 10:6-11) No nginya tũtate tũikese kwĩthĩwa tũilyĩ ta Akanaani o na vanini. (Alo. 12:2) We nũtatĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito wĩke ũu?
NO TŨLŨMYE MŨĨKĨĨO O NA ĨLA ANGĨ MATUMA TŨKW'A NGOO
7. (a) Yevitha eekiwe ata nĩ andũ a make? (b) Yevitha eekie ata ĩla mamwĩkaĩlile?
7 Ĩvindanĩ ya Yevitha, Aisilaeli nĩmatw'ĩkĩthiw'e ngombo nĩ Avilisiti na Aamimoni nũndũ wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai. (Asi. 10:7, 8) Na eka ũu, ũ Yevitha no wathĩnaw'a nĩ ana-a-ĩthe na atongoi ma Isilaeli. Kwa ngelekany'o, kĩwĩu na kĩmena nĩsyatumie ana-a-ĩthe mamũlũngya na mamũvata ũtiĩwa ũla mĩao yaĩtye waĩle kũnengwa ĩkithathi. (Asi. 11:1-3) Yevitha ndaaĩtĩkĩla ngoo yake ĩvĩndũwe nĩ meko asu moo mathũku. Vandũ va kũmathatĩa na ailea kũthi kũtetheesya ĩla atumĩa ma mbaĩ ĩsu mamwĩkaĩlile, we nĩwaendie ametaana. (Asi. 11:4-11) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kyatumie Yevitha osa maũndũ ta mũndũ mũima kĩ-veva?
8, 9. (a) Mĩao ya Mose yaĩ na myolooto yĩva ĩla ĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yatetheeisye Yevitha? (b) Nĩ kyaũ Yevitha woonaa kĩ kya vata vyũ?
8 Yevitha aĩ ngũmbaũ nene ya kaũ na nĩweemanyĩasya ũndũ Ngai weekanaa na Aisilaeli kuma tene. Ũmanyi ũsu waĩ naw'o nĩwatumaa aelewa nesa nĩ kyaũ Yeova wonaa kyaĩle na nĩ kyaũ wonaa kĩtaĩle. (Asi. 11:12-27) Aekie ngoo yake na mesilya make matongoew'e nĩ myolooto ĩla yatw'ĩĩkĩte ĩla Mĩao ya Mose. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩweesĩ kana Yeova ndendete kwona mũndũ e ũthũ na ũngĩ, ĩndĩ endaa andũ onthe mekale mendene. Mĩao ya Mose nĩyasyokete ĩkaweta kana mũndũ ndaĩle kũeka angĩ manyamae, o na ethĩwa 'nĩmamũmenete.'—Soma Kuma 23:5; Alivai 19:17, 18.
9 O na ngewa sya andũ ala maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo no kwĩthĩwa syamũtetheeisye eke ũndũ weekie. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩweesĩ kana Yosevu nĩweew'ĩie tei ana-a-ĩthe o na kau "nĩmamũmenaa." (Mwa. 37:4; 45:4, 5) Nĩ laisi ũkethĩa kũvindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa andũ ta asu nĩkwamũtetheeisye oosa ĩtambya yĩla yaĩ yĩtonya kũmwendeesya Yeova. Kĩko kĩla ana-a-ĩthe mamwĩkie vate nzika nĩkyatumie ew'a woo, ĩndĩ kyu kĩyaatuma alea kũmũthũkũma Yeova na andũ make. (Asi. 11:9) Kũthi kaũnĩ akokitĩe ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova kwaĩ kwa vata mũno kwake kwĩ kũthokoana kũla wathokoanĩte na andũ angĩ. Nĩwatw'ĩte kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova vyũ, na kyu nĩkyaeteie andũ make ũseo o vamwe nake.—Aevl. 11:32, 33.
10. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana myolooto ya Ngai ĩtũtetheesye twĩkue ta Aklĩsto?
10 We nũkwĩtĩkĩlya ngelekany'o ya Yevitha ĩũtethye? Kwa ngelekany'o, no kwĩthĩwa ve ana-a-asa matumĩte ũkw'a ngoo kana makwĩkĩte maũndũ mathũku. Ethĩwa ũndũ ta ũsu nĩwĩkĩkĩte, ndwaĩle kũeka maũmbano kana kũeka kũmũthũkũma Yeova, o na ndwaĩle kũola kĩthito kĩla wĩthĩawa nakyo kĩkundinĩ. O naitũ twaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yevitha kwa kwĩtĩkĩla tũtongoew'e nĩ myolooto ya Ngai nĩ kana ĩtũtetheesye tũkĩlye vinya mathĩna ala matũkwata, na ĩitũtetheesya tũendeee kwĩthĩwa ngelekany'o nzeo kwa ala angĩ.—Alo. 12:20, 21; Ako. 3:13.
KWĨYUMYA KUMA NGOONĨ KWONANASYA TWĨ NA MŨĨKĨĨO
11, 12. Yevitha eevĩtie ata, na wĩvĩto wake woonanasya kyaũ?
11 Yevitha nĩweesĩ no nginya amwĩkwatye Ngai nĩ kana avote kwĩtaana Aisilaeli kuma mokonĩ ma Aamimoni. Nĩkyo kĩtumi wamwathie Yeova kana amũtetheesya asinde Aamimoni, akamũnenga ũla ũkamũthaũa aumĩte kaũnĩ ethĩwe "nthembo ya kũvĩvw'a." (Asi. 11:30, 31) Ĩndĩ we esaa kumya nthembo ĩsu ata?
12 Kumya mũndũ ethĩwe nthembo nĩ kĩndũ kĩmenetwe mũno nĩ Yeova. Kwoou vai nzika kana Yevitha ndavangĩte kũtwaa mũndũ kĩthembeonĩ amũthembe. (Kũt. 18:9, 10) Kwosana na Mĩao ya Mose, ĩla mũndũ waumya nthembo ya kũvĩvw'a aaĩlĩte kũmĩnenga Yeova yonthe. Kwoou veonekana kana ĩla Yevitha waisye akaumya ũla ũkamũthaũa ethĩwe nthembo ya kũvĩvw'a, endaa amũnengane kwa Ngai nĩ kana amũthũkũmae ĩvinda yonthe. Ũu nĩ kwasya mũndũ ũsu esaa kũthũkũma ĩeemanĩ ya Yeova nginya ĩla ũkakw'a. Yeova nĩweetĩkĩlile ndeto isu sya Yevitha na amũtetheesya nginya akũna ala amaitha ma Isilaeli na amakĩlya vinya vyũ. (Asi. 11:32, 33) Ĩndĩ nũũ ũla wesie kũnenganwe ta "nthembo ya kũvĩvw'a"?
13, 14. Ndeto sya Yevitha ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Asili 11:35 syĩonany'a kyaũ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wake?
13 Kwalilikana ngewa ĩla yĩ mwambĩĩonĩ wa ĩsomo yĩĩ. We nũũlilikana kana ĩla Yevitha waumie kaũnĩ no mwĩĩtu wake ũla wasyaĩtwe e weka wookie kũmũthaũa? Yu ĩtatwa yaĩ vau. We Yevitha nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto wake na ainengane mwĩĩtu wake athũkũmae ĩeemanĩ nginya ĩla ũkakw'a?
14 O nayo ĩvindanĩ yĩu myolooto ya Ngai nĩyamũtetheeisye Yevitha eke ũtwi ũla waĩlĩte. Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa alilikanile ila ndeto syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Kuma 23:19, ila syaĩtye kana andũ ma Ngai maĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa meyũmbanĩtye ngoonĩ kũmũnenga kĩla kĩseo. O na ĩngĩ Mĩao ya Mose yoonanĩtye kana mũndũ eevĩta aĩ no nginya eanĩsye wĩvĩto wake. Yaĩtye ũũ: "Yĩla mũndũ mũũme ũkevĩtĩa Yeova wĩvĩto . . . , ndakaeke ndeto yake; akeke kwĩanana na w'onthe ũla wumaa kanyw'anĩ wake." (Mot. 30:2) Yaĩ no nginya Yevitha eanĩsye wĩvĩto wake o tondũ Aana weekie. Lilikana kana Aana nũtonya kwĩthĩwa atwĩe ĩvinda yĩmwe nake. Ĩndĩ Yevitha no weesĩ kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto wake kwaĩ kũalyũle vyũ thayũ wake na wa mwĩĩtu wake. Nũndũ ndaĩ na mwana ũngĩ, mwĩĩtu wake no we waĩ wĩkwatyo wake wa kũtuma ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩikole, na ate vo ũtiĩwa wa Yevitha mbaĩnĩ ya Isilaeli waĩ wae. (Asi. 11:34) O na ũu wĩ o vo, ĩandĩko ya Asili 11:35 yĩminĩĩe na ndeto ii sya Yevitha: "Nĩnamwathamĩsye Yeova kanyw'a wakwa, na nditonya kũalyũka." Kwĩyumya kũu weeyumisye kwoonanisye aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo na kĩu nĩkyatumie endwa nĩ Ngai na aathimwa. Keka nue nĩwĩka take?
15. Aingĩ maitũ tweevĩtie ata, na tũtonya kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku ata?
15 Ĩla tweeyumisye tũmũthũkũme Yeova tweevĩtie twasya tũkekaa kwenda kwake o na kweethĩwa kũilyĩ ata. Tũyĩvĩta no tweesĩ kana tũyĩsa kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto ũsu ethĩwa tũyĩleete. Ĩndĩ ĩla tweewa nĩtwĩke maũndũ tũtendete, wendi ũsu witũ wa kwĩyumya nũmanyĩkaa ethĩwa wĩ o vo. Ĩla tweeyumya twĩke maũndũ ala Ngai ũkwenda twĩke o na ethĩwa twĩĩw'a tũtekwenda, twonanasya kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa nĩtũtonya kwĩw'a ta twaũmĩa nũndũ wa kwĩyumya, moathimo ala tũkwataa mayĩsa kũelekanw'a na woo ũsu o na ethĩwa wĩana ata. (Mal. 3:10) Ĩndĩ kwaekai twone we mwĩĩtu wa Yevitha eekie ata.
16. Mwĩĩtu wa Yevitha eekie ata ĩla wamanyie ũndũ ĩthe weevĩtie? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 5.)
16 Ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa mwĩĩtu wa Yevitha kwĩtĩkĩlana na kĩla kĩkamũkwata nũndũ wa wĩvĩto wa ĩthe. Wĩvĩto wa ĩthe waĩ kĩvathũkany'o na wĩvĩto wa Aana, nũndũ we Aana anenganĩte mwana wake Samueli athũkũme yĩla ĩeemanĩ e Mũnasali. (1 Sam. 1:11) Mũnasali aĩ atonya kũtwaana na akethĩwa na mũsyĩ. Ĩndĩ mwĩĩtu wa Yevitha anenganĩtwe ta "nthembo ya kũvĩvw'a," na kwoou ndaĩ esa kũtwawa na kũmesya mũsyĩ. (Asi. 11:37-40) Mwĩĩtu ũsu ethĩwa atwaiwe nĩ mũndũũme ũla mũseo vyũ nthĩ ĩsu nũndũ ĩthe aĩ ngũmbaũ ya kaũ na mũtongoi mbaĩnĩ ya Isilaeli. Ĩndĩ yu nũndũ wa wĩvĩto wa ĩthe aĩ no nginya atw'ĩke mũthũkũmi yĩla ĩeemanĩ. Kwoou we eekie ata? Ũsũngĩo wake woonanisye kana endete kwĩka kwenda kwa Yeova mbee wa kwĩka kwenda kwake. Aisye: "Nau, nĩwamwathamĩsye Yeova kanyw'a waku; mbĩka kwĩanana na ũndũ ũnaumie kanyw'anĩ waku." (Asi. 11:36) O na kau nĩwesaa kwĩw'a mũyo kwona e mũtwae na e na syana, nĩwatwie kũekana na mĩvango ta ĩsu nĩ kana amũthũkũme Yeova. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twonany'e nĩtwĩleete o ũndũ mwĩĩtu ũsu weeleete?
17. (a) Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ta ũla waĩ na Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake? (b) Ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Aevelania 6:10-12 itonya kũũtetheesya ata wĩyumye vyũ?
17 Ve Aklĩsto aingĩ ma mũika ala kavindanĩ kaa matw'ĩte kuma ngoonĩ kwamba kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate na syana nĩ kana mamũthũkũme Yeova ũndũ matonya. Namo ala akũangũ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa maolangaa ĩvinda yĩla matũmĩaa na syana syoo kana esũkũũe nĩ kana mayĩtũmĩe kwaka myako ĩkonetye maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ, kana mathi Sukulu ya Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ na maitũmwa isionĩ ila syĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Namo angĩ nĩmambaa kũũngamya maũndũ moo nĩ kana methĩwe vo ĩvindanĩ ya kambeini ila syĩkawa ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Kwĩyumya kwa mũthemba ũsu nĩkũtumaa Yeova atana mũno, na we ndesa kũlwa nĩ wĩa witũ na kũmwenda kũla tũmwendete. (Soma Aevelania 6:10-12.) We nũkwona ta ve maũndũ ũtonya kwamba kũeka nĩ kana wongelange ĩvinda yĩla ũmũthũkũmaa Yeova?
KĨLA TWEEMANYĨSYA
18, 19. Ngewa ya Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake yatũmanyĩsya kyaũ, na tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yoo ata?
18 O na kau Yevitha nĩwakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna maingĩ, nĩweetĩkĩlile Yeova amũtongoesye maũndũnĩ onthe ala weekaa. Ndaaĩtĩkĩla kwaw'a nĩ andũ. Na o na kau angĩ nĩmatumie akw'a ngoo, kyu kĩyaatuma aeka kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Kwĩyumya kwake na kwa mwĩĩtu wake kwaĩ ũathimo nũndũ Yeova nĩwamatũmĩie ũthaithinĩ wa w'o. Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake nĩmaatĩĩie myolooto ya Ngai o na kau ĩvinda yoo andũ mayalũnganaa nayo.
19 Mbivilia ĩtũthangaaĩtye 'twĩyĩelekany'e na ala matiĩwe matho kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo na wũmĩĩsyo.' (Aevl. 6:12) Kwoou ekai tũtw'e kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yevitha na mwĩĩtu wake nũndũ ngelekany'o ĩsu yoo nĩyĩĩkĩĩthĩtye ũndũ ũũ wa vata: Kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nĩkũtumaa twendwa nĩ Ngai.

translation:
"Put on the complete suit of armor from God so that you may be able to stand firm against the wicked schemes and tactics of the Devil."—EPH. 6:12.
PAGE 3, 54
1, 2. What challenges did Eve face, and what can we learn from her experience?
Eve's husband failed to give her proper support and direction. She was deceived because she did not fully appreciate the value of God's law and gave consideration to the serpent's suggestions. When she saw that the fruit looked delicious and would make her wise, she took some and ate it and then offered it to her husband, saying: "Come, eat also." As a result, both she and Adam disobeyed God and began to experience imperfection and its consequences. But Eve's mistake highlights an important principle: We should not associate with those who might lead us astray or adopt their thinking, and we should always seek Jehovah's guidance when making decisions. Otherwise, we may find ourselves in a difficult situation and regret our choices. It is vital that we remember that Jehovah cares for us and wants to help us succeed. (Ps. 11:34-37) Your own life proves this, does it not? You have seen how often Jehovah has helped you when you were facing difficulties. So trust in him completely and do not doubt his love for you.
2 Eve and her husband had faith in God, yet they allowed themselves to be influenced by Satan's lies and doubts about God's purpose and ways. They foolishly thought that they could determine for themselves what is right and wrong. This shows us that even faithful ones can be misled if they do not remain vigilant and rely on God's strength.
3. How can Eve's experience teach us something valuable?
3 We need to recognize that resisting the influence of Satan requires effort and determination. That is why we must 'put on the complete suit of armor.' (Judg. 3) Only by understanding what we are up against can we imitate the example of Eve and her husband in avoiding temptation. But how can we strengthen our resolve to resist Satan's influence?
DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE ENEMY AND HIS METHODS
4, 5. (a) Why did Jehovah allow Israel to be tested in the wilderness? (b) According to Psalm 106, what mistakes did Israel make while in the wilderness?
4 Throughout their journey, Eve and her husband repeatedly demonstrated a lack of trust in Jehovah. For some 300 years after Eve's fall, humans generally lived in wickedness, practicing idolatry and rejecting God's authority. (Gen. 7:1-4) Because the Israelites failed to maintain loyalty, they were permitted to settle in Canaan, which led them to associate with those who worshiped false gods and engage in immoral practices.—Read Psalm 106:34-39.
5 Disloyalty to Jehovah resulted in plagues and hardships. (Ex. 2:1-3, 11-15; Ps. 106:40-43) However, God was merciful to those who showed genuine repentance and continued to seek his favor. The Bible shows that many individuals exercised faith. For instance, Eve, her husband, Hannah, and Samuel pleased God greatly.—1 Sam. 1:20-28; 2:26.
6. What lessons can we learn from their experiences, and how can we apply them?
6 We can be loyal despite opposition and temptation. Like the ancient Israelites, we face challenges and trials. Let us examine our hearts and conduct, and determine whether we are allowing ourselves to be influenced by bad associations. Jehovah remembers our faithfulness, just as he remembered Israel, and he will help us resist wrongdoing. Why did the mistakes of the Israelites serve as a warning to us? (1 Cor. 10:6-11) How can we avoid making similar errors? (Prov. 12:2) Will we heed this counsel?
DO NOT LET PAST ERRORS AND OTHER FACTORS WEAKEN OUR RESOLVE
7. (a) What qualities did Eve display? (b) What lessons does Eve's example teach us?
7 Because of Eve's disobedience, the Israelites were repeatedly defeated by the Philistines and Ammonites, who sought to turn them away from God. (Judg. 10:7, 8) And yet, Jehovah continued to deliver them from their oppressors. However, Jehovah also allowed them to experience suffering because of their wickedness. For instance, famine and pestilence afflicted those who practiced idolatry and immorality, causing many to die. (Judg. 11:1-3) Eve regretted her error deeply, but she still benefited from Jehovah's mercy. Those who humbly acknowledge their mistakes and seek forgiveness will find relief. (Judg. 11:4-11) What can motivate us to remain loyal to Jehovah despite difficulties?
8, 9. (a) What request did Moses make that demonstrated his humility? (b) Why did Jehovah answer Moses' request?
8 Moses was a very mild man and exceedingly humble. He showed concern for God's relationship with Israel. This attitude enabled him to understand why Jehovah does what he does and why he does not do certain things. (Judg. 11:12-27) He appreciated his own imperfections and recognized that his qualities were due to Jehovah's spirit. For example, he asked whether Jehovah would be patient with a people who were stubborn and rebellious. Moses' request proved that a person can appeal to Jehovah even when others view him as unreasonable or overly sensitive.—Read Numbers 23:5; Leviticus 19:17, 18.
9 And often people react badly to expressions that they do not like. For instance, we might ask whether Joseph became upset because his brothers said he was "trying to become ruler over them." (Gen. 37:4; 45:4, 5) It is vital that we endeavor to discern the motive behind people's words so that we do not respond in a way that could cause them to turn away from Jehovah. Each time someone speaks harshly, let us try to determine whether his words are meant to hurt us, realizing that this could lead him to blaspheme Jehovah and His people. (Judg. 11:9) To some extent, we should overlook offenses committed against us, especially if those offenses are minor. We want to show appreciation for Jehovah by being willing to forgive others, and this will help our brothers.—Prov. 11:32, 33.
10. Can we tell how God's spirit can help us to be mild like Christ?
10 How can we imitate the example of Jesus in this regard? For instance, when people misuse their tongues or say thoughtless things, let us remember that they may be under duress, and instead of reacting in anger or feeling offended, let us look for an opportunity to comfort them or to help them appreciate why what they said was wrong. By imitating Jesus' example, we can demonstrate that we are guided by God's spirit and that we are determined to continue showing mildness toward others.—Phil. 12:20, 21; Acts 3:13.
TO SHOW PRACTICAL WISDOM IN OUR SPEECH
11, 12. What did Jesus do on one occasion, and what lesson does his example teach us?
11 Jesus once rebuked Peter for opposing God when he tried to dissuade Him from going to Jerusalem to suffer. This shows why we should trust in Jehovah and support His will, even if it means facing opposition. He corrected Peter, reminding him that his thinking reflected "what originates with men," not with God. (Matt. 11:30, 31) But how can we discern what such "thinking originating with men" is?
12 Discerning what constitutes human wisdom requires spiritual insight from Jehovah. It takes courage to correct someone who seems confident in his own wisdom. (Prov. 18:9, 10) In Moses' Law, anyone who stubbornly refused to acknowledge Jehovah was considered deserving of death. It is evident that Jesus rightly discerned that Peter's thinking originated with men, and he gently reproved him so that he could realign himself with God's will. Such correction can help individuals strengthen their faith in Jehovah and avoid making serious mistakes. Jehovah appreciated Peter's sincere love and supported him despite his imperfections and errors. (Matt. 11:32, 33) So, what can help us to avoid displaying "thinking originating with men"?
13, 14. What does the account at Genesis 11:35 reveal about the way humans think?
13 Consider how this story illustrates our inclination toward independent thought. Do we tend to believe that our ideas are superior to those found in God's Word? The truth is, we are inclined to rely on our own reasoning and to disregard divine guidance. Does Jesus encourage us to conform to worldly standards or to align ourselves with God's thoughts?
14 However, God's purpose allows individuals like Eve to make choices. It is important to remember what is stated at Proverbs 23:19, but realize that God's loyal servants are willing to accept correction in order to please Him. Also, the Mosaic Law acknowledged that a person could act unwisely. It said: "A foolish man will become wise when he listens… so that he may acquire skill to discern what is good." (Proverbs 30:2) And because Eve acted unwisely, Adam also fell. Consider whether Adam would have been able to remain faithful had Eve not made her choice. Eve's desire to be wise led her to disregard God's warning, and she influenced her husband to do the same. This resulted in great suffering for herself and her family, and ultimately affected all Israelites. (Acts 11:34) But more than that, the account at Genesis 11:35 shows the effect Eve's decision had on her: "I have acquired a male child from Jehovah, and yet I am distressed." Realizing her error, she expressed regret over her independence and the consequences that followed. What can we learn from this?
15 Often we do not see the full picture, and we may wonder why things happen.
15 Yet, if we trust in Jehovah, we can be confident that He will guide us in His way and help us to avoid wrongdoing. We need to recognize that our desire to be independent can lead us astray. If we allow ourselves to be motivated by pride, we may pursue a course that does not align with God's will. If we do not heed God's guidance, we may find ourselves facing difficulties, and we may feel frustrated and disappointed. (Malachi 3:10) So let us examine how Eve's example affects us.
16 How did Eve's example affect those who came after her? (See accompanying article "Learning From Bible Examples.")
16 One way Eve's example has affected people is through their struggle with temptation. The temptation faced by Eve is similar to the temptation faced by Hannah, who vowed to dedicate her son Samuel to Jehovah. (1 Samuel 1:11) Hannah was deeply moved by her prayers. Eve, however, chose to disobey, and this led to suffering and hardship. (Proverbs 11:37-40) This woman, whose name is not mentioned, was a mother in Israel, and she showed great faith. But because of her vow, she continued to pray earnestly. How did she show her confidence in Jehovah? She said: "O Lord, as I have sworn to you, so I will make good my vow to you." (Proverbs 11:36) And even though she continued to pray, she remained confident that Jehovah would fulfill his promise. Can we learn something from this woman's example?
17. (a) How can we benefit from considering the example of Eve and her husband? (b) How can the counsel found in Hebrews 6:10-12 help us to remain steadfast?
17 Many Christians find that they face challenges when trying to stay busy in spiritual activities, especially when they want to please Jehovah. Some also experience difficulties because of pressures from family members or friends who do not value spiritual things, or because of demands made on their time by secular work, school, or other obligations. Others may be distracted by personal interests. However, remembering the importance of imitating Christ's example can help us overcome such obstacles. By maintaining our hope, we encourage Jehovah to support us, and he will give us strength to continue serving him faithfully. (Read Hebrews 6:10-12.) So how can we ensure that we do not neglect spiritual activities?
EVERYONE AGREES
18, 19. What does the example of Eve and her husband teach us, and what can we learn from it?
18 Although Eve was faced with many temptations, she trusted that Jehovah would direct her steps. She showed faith by speaking about what she had learned. And although others might use their free will improperly, this does not excuse us from making choices that displease God. The loyalty of Eve and her husband demonstrated Jehovah's willingness to forgive those who sincerely repent. Eve and her husband respected God's law, even though people around them did not.
19 The Bible encourages us to "put on the complete suit of armor from God." (Heb. 6:12) In effect, we can learn from the example of Eve and her husband so that we too can strengthen ourselves in this way: Being loyal to God means being loved by Him.

text:
"Syĩtwa yaku yĩtaĩwe."—MT. 6:9.
1. Ĩla tũũtavany'a tũtonya kũtũmĩa ata mboya ĩla ĩwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 6:9-13?
ANDŨ aingĩ nĩmatonya kwinĩlĩĩla Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi mateũsisya vandũ. Naitũ ĩla tũũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, mavinda maingĩ nĩtũweteaa ala twakomana namo ĩũlũ wa mboya ĩsu nĩ kana tũmatetheesye maelewe kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ silikalĩ ĩkaete moalyũku manene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Kana nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũtũmĩaa mũsoa wa mbee mboyanĩ ĩsu nĩ kana twony'e andũ kana Ngai e ĩsyĩtwa, na kana ĩsyĩtwa yĩu nĩyaĩle kũtaĩwa, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ĩsyĩtwa yĩu yaĩle 'kwoswa ta ĩtheu.'—Mt. 6:9, maelesyo ma kwongeleela ma NWT.
2. Twĩsĩ ata kana Yesũ ndendaa twĩkae kwinĩlĩĩlaa Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi ĩla twenda kũvoya?
2 Ĩndĩ we Yesũ endaa andũ mekae kwinĩlĩĩla mboya ĩsu o tondũ andũ aingĩ ma ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto mekaa? Aiee. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o na atanamba kũmanyĩsya andũ mboya ĩsu aisye: "Mũkĩvoya mũikatindĩe ndeto." (Mt. 6:7) O na ĩvinda yĩngĩ ĩla amanyĩw'a make mendie kũmanyĩw'a kũvoya, nĩwatũngĩlĩile mboya ĩsu ĩndĩ atũmĩĩte ndeto syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. (Luka 11:1-4) Kwoou kĩla Yesũ wendaa nĩ kũtũtetheesya tũmanye twaĩle kũvoya ĩũlũ wa kyaũ, na nĩ maũndũ meva twaĩle kwambĩĩa namo. Vate nzika, mboya ĩsu nĩtũmanyĩasya mũno ũndũ twaĩle kũvoya.
3. Nĩ makũlyo meva tũtonya kwĩkũlya ĩvindanĩ yĩla tũũneenea ĩla Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi?
3 Nthĩnĩ wa ĩsomo yĩĩ na yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩtũũneenea kĩla kĩ Mboyanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi. Ĩvindanĩ yĩla tũũneenea mboya ĩsu ĩkũlye atĩĩ, 'Mboya ĩno ĩtonya kũndethya ata naĩlangye mboya syakwa? Na ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ, nyie nĩnĩkalaa kwosana na mboya ĩsu?'
"ASA WAITŨ ŨLA WĨ ĨTUNĨ"
4. Ndeto "Asa waitũ" itũlilikanasya kyaũ, na nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Yeova nĩ "Asa" wa Aklĩsto ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ?
4 Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi yambĩĩe na ndeto ii, "Asa waitũ," ĩndĩ ti "Asa wakwa." Nũndũ wa ũu, ndeto isu "Asa waitũ" itũlilikanasya kana twĩ na "ana-a-asa" aingĩ matwendete. (1 Vet. 2:17) Ĩsu nĩ ndaĩa nene ta kĩ! Nũndũ Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, nĩmatw'ĩtwe ana ma Ngai. Na kwoou asu nomo matonya nesa vyũ kwĩta Yeova "Asa." (Alo. 8:15-17) O namo Aklĩsto ma w'o ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ no mamwĩte Yeova "Asa." Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nĩwe ũmanengete thayũ na no we wĩanĩasya nesa mavata moo. Ĩndĩ asu me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ makatw'ĩka syana sya Ngai nesa vyũ ĩla makavetewa naĩ na mayĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku ĩvindanĩ ya ũla mũtiani wa mũthya.—Alo. 8:21; Ũvu. 20:7, 8.
5, 6. Nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wĩva mũseo asyai matonya kũnenga syana syoo, na kĩla mwana aĩle kũtũmĩa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 20.)
5 Ĩla asyai mamanyĩsya syana syoo ũndũ itonya kũvoya na maitetheesya imwone Yeova ta Ĩthe wasyo wa ĩtunĩ na ũsyendete, methĩawa mainenga mũthĩnzĩo mũseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩthĩawa e mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko nthĩ ya South Africa aĩtye ũũ: "Kuma mũthenya ũla eĩtu makwa masyaiwe, nambĩĩe kũvoya namo kĩla wĩoo ate o ĩla nesa kwĩthĩwa nde kw'o. Mavinda maingĩ eĩtu asu makwa masasya kana mayĩsa kũlilikana kĩla nawetaa ĩla ngũvoya namo. Ĩndĩ nĩmalilikanaa ũndũ kweethĩawa kũilyĩ ĩla tũũvoya, na nĩmalilikanaa maũndũ ta ndaĩa ĩla twanengae Asa witũ, Yeova, ĩla tũũmũvoya, na ũndũ meew'aa mauĩtye na mate kũthĩnĩka. Na ĩndĩ ĩla mamanyie kũneena oou, nĩnamathangaaisye mambĩĩe kũvoya na wasya nĩ kana nĩw'e ũndũ meũtavya Yeova kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ na kĩla meũsũanĩa. Noonaa ũsu wĩ mwanya mũseo wa kũmanya ngoo syoo. Nũndũ wa ũu, naĩ nĩtonya kũmatetheesya nesa mamanye ũndũ matonya kũlikya mboyanĩ syoo maũndũ amwe ma vata mawetetwe ĩla Mboyanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi nĩ kana wĩthĩe matw'a kũvoya mevoya ũndũ vaĩle."
6 Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, eĩtu asu nĩmesie kwĩana me na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. Yu nĩ atwae na mekalanasya nesa na aũme moo. O na ĩngĩ, eĩtu asu na aũme moo mamũthũkũmaa Ngai me athũkũmi ma ĩvinda yonthe. Vai mũthĩnzĩo mũnene asyai matonya kũnenga syana syoo ũvĩtũkĩte kũitetheesya syĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kana kĩla mwana nĩwe waĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova ĩendeee kwĩthĩwa yĩ ndũmu. Nĩ kana eke ũu, ũndũ ũmwe waĩle kwĩka nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kwenda ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai na kũyĩnenga ndaĩa nene kwĩ kĩndũ kĩngĩ o na kĩva.—Sav. 5:11, 12; 91:14.
"SYĨTWA YAKU YĨTAĨWE"
7. Nĩ ndaĩa yĩva andũ ma Ngai me nayo, na ndaĩa ĩsu manengetwe yaĩlĩte kũtuma meka ata?
7 Nĩ ndaĩa nene mũno kwĩthĩwa twĩsĩ ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, na kwĩthĩwa twĩ 'andũ kwondũ wa ĩsyĩtwa yake.' (Meko 15:14; Isa. 43:10) Nĩkyo kĩtumi tũmũvoyaa Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ tũkĩmwĩa: "Syĩtwa yaku yĩtaĩwe." Kũmũtavya Yeova ũu nĩkũtonya kũũsukuma ũmwĩe aũtetheesye ndũkese kwĩka kĩndũ kana kwasya ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma ĩsyĩtwa yake ĩtheu yĩvũthw'a. Tũikwenda twĩkale ta andũ amwe ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa ala mwĩkalĩle woo ũtosanaa na kĩla meũtavya andũ ala angĩ. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wamo: "Syĩtwa ya Ngai yĩumawa Andũnĩ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ nũndũ wenyu."—Alo. 2:21-24.
8, 9. Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ Yeova ũathimaa ala mendaa mũno kwona ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩitaĩwa.
8 Nĩtũtataa mũno kwĩka maũndũ matonya kũtuma ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩtaĩwa. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wa Norway ũla wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũũme atataĩĩe. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu atiiwe na kamwana ka myaka ĩlĩ. Easya ũũ: "Ĩvinda yĩu navonie thĩna mwingĩ mũno. Kĩla mũthenya navoyaa vakuvĩ kĩla ĩsaa nĩkwate vinya ndikese kũvũavũana na ũndũ ũsu ũituma nĩka ũtwi ũtaĩlĩte kana nĩthĩwa nde mũĩkĩĩku, na nũndũ wa ũu ngĩmũnenga Satani mwanya wa kũmũvũthya Yeova. Nendaa kũtaĩa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova, na nĩnendaa mwanawa eĩsa kwona ĩthe Nthĩ Nzaũ."—Nth. 27:11.
9 We Yeova nĩweethukĩĩisye mboya ta isu sya kuma ngoonĩ? Ĩĩ. Mbee, mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩweekĩiwe vinya mũno nũndũ wa kũtindany'a na Aklĩsto ala angĩ. O na ĩngĩ ĩtina wa myaka ĩtano nĩwatwaiwe nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Nake mwanae, ũla yu wĩ na myaka 20, nĩ mũvatise. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu easya atĩĩ: "Nĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ mũemewa nũndetheetye kũmũea."
10. Nĩ kyaũ kyaĩle kwĩkwa nĩ kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩtaĩwe nesa vyũ?
10 Nĩ kyaũ kyaĩle kwĩkwa nĩ kana ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai yĩtaĩwe nesa vyũ na yĩivetangĩwa kĩko kyonthe kĩla yaailĩĩlwa? Nĩ kana kĩu kĩkĩke, no nginya Yeova avetange onthe ala maleaa na ngũlũ ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. (Soma Esekieli 38:22, 23.) Ĩtina wa ũu nĩw'o andũ makambĩĩa kũvetewa naĩ kavola kwa kavola. Mwa twĩkũlasya nĩ ĩndĩĩ ĩvinda yĩkavika wĩthĩe alaĩka onthe vamwe na andũ nĩmekũtuma ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩtaĩwa! Ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o ĩndĩ Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ ũkethĩwa "syonthe nthĩnĩ wa syonthe."—1 Ako. 15:28.
"ŨSUMBĨ WAKU WŨKE"
11, 12. Aklĩsto ma w'o matetheeiw'e kũelewa kyaũ mwakanĩ wa 1876?
11 Yesũ atanamba kwambata ĩtunĩ, atũmwa make mamũkũlilye atĩĩ: "Mwĩaĩi, ũkatũngĩa Isilaeli ũsumbĩ ĩvinda yĩĩ twĩ nayo?" Ũsungĩo wa Yesũ woonanisye kana mayaĩ maneanĩĩa kũtavw'a ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wĩambĩĩa kũsumbĩka. Eeie amanyĩw'a make nĩmatũnge ilĩko syoo wĩanĩ wa vata ũla maaĩle kũtethya, naw'o waĩ kũtavany'a. (Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 1:6-8.) Ĩndĩ o na amatavĩtye oou, nĩwamamanyĩisye maendeee kweteela mũno Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Kyu nĩkyo kĩtumi kuma ĩvinda yĩu ya atũmwa, Aklĩsto methĩĩtwe maivoya Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wũke.
12 Vatiele kavinda kanini Yesũ ambĩĩe kũsumbĩka ĩtunĩ, Yeova nĩwatetheeisye andũ make maelewe nĩ mwaka wĩva Yesũ wĩambĩĩa kũsumbĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa 1876, ve kĩlungu kĩmwe kyaandĩkiwe nĩ Charles Taze Russell na kyaumĩthw'a ĩkasetinĩ yĩtawa Bible Examiner. Kĩlungu kyu kyaĩ na kyongo, "Mavinda ma Mbaĩ Ingĩ: Makathela Ĩndĩĩ?," na nĩkyaeleisye ũndũ mwaka wa 1914 ne wa vata. Kĩlungu kyu nĩkyoonanisye kana ala "mavinda mũonza" mawetetwe wathaninĩ wa Ndanieli nĩmakonanĩtye na "mavinda ma Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ" ala Yesũ wawetie. *—Nda. 4:16; Luka 21:24.
13. Nĩ kyaũ kyeekĩkie mwakanĩ wa 1914, na maũndũ ala maendeee kũũ nthĩ kuma ĩvinda yĩu maĩkĩĩthasya kyaũ?
13 Mwakanĩ wa 1914, nthĩ sya Europe nĩsyambĩĩe kũkita, na kaũ ũsu nĩwesie kũnyaĩĩka nthĩ yonthe. Kaũ ũsu ũyĩsa kũthela mwakanĩ wa 1918, andũ makwatĩtwe nĩ yũa ĩvyũ mũno na makasyoka makakwatwa nĩ ndetema nthũku mũno ĩla yooaie andũ aingĩ kwĩ ala mooaĩtwe nĩ ũ kaũ. Maũndũ asu meekĩkie moonanisye kana "wonan'yo" ũla Yesũ waisye kana ũkatetheesya andũ mamanye nĩwatw'ĩkĩthw'a Mũsumbĩ ĩtunĩ nĩwambĩĩa kwĩanĩa. (Mt. 24:3-8; Luka 21:10, 11) Ve maũndũ maingĩ maĩkĩĩthasya kana Mwĩaĩi Yesũ Klĩsto 'anengiwe ngovia ya ũsumbĩ' mwakanĩ wa 1914. Mwakanĩ ũsu nĩw'o 'waumaalile aikĩlany'a, na nĩ kana akĩlany'e.' (Ũvu. 6:2) Nĩwatheisye ĩtunĩ ĩla wokitie na Satani na ndaimoni syake na amekya kũũ nthĩ. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu andũ nĩmakwatĩtwe nĩ kĩla kĩwetetwe ndetonĩ ii mbeveee: "Woo nĩ wanthĩ na wa ũkanga: nũndũ ndevili nĩwamũtheeea inyw'ĩ, e na ũthilĩku mũnene, akĩmanya kana e na kavinda o kanini."—Ũvu. 12:7-12.
14. (a) Nĩkĩ o na ũmũnthĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũvoya Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wũke? (b) Tũnengetwe kĩanda kĩva kya mwanya?
14 Wathani ũla ũandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo 12:7-12 nũeleetye nĩkĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wasumbĩka kwambĩĩe mothũku ala mathĩnĩtye andũ mũno kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ. Ĩvinda yĩu Yesũ, ũla nĩwe Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, nĩw'o wambĩĩe kũsumbĩka katĩ wa amaitha make. Na kwoou twĩendeea kũvoya Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wũke nginya ĩla Yesũ ũkasinda amaitha make vyũ na aimina ũthũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ kavindanĩ kaa tweteele kĩu, twaĩlĩte kũendeea kwĩkala kwosana na mboya isu tũvoyaa. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Nĩ kwa kũtethya wĩa wa kũtavany'a, nũndũ nũkonetye mũno kwĩanĩa kwa ũla "wonan'yo." Yesũ athanie ũũ: "Ũvoo ũũ mũseo wa ũsumbĩ ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe; na ĩndĩ mũminũkĩlyo ũkyũka."—Mt. 24:14.
"KWENDA KWAKU KWĨKE KŨŨ NTHĨ"
15, 16. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva tũtonya kwĩkala kwosana na kĩlungu kĩĩ kya Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi, "Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ"?
15 Myaka ta 6,000 mĩvĩtu, kwenda kwa Ngai nĩkweekawa vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nesa vyũ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova amina kũmbĩa mũndũ syĩndũ nzeo na vandũ vaseo wasyaisye kĩla kĩndũ na asya "kyaĩ kĩseo mũno." (Mwa. 1:31) Ĩtina wa ũu Satani nĩwaleanile na Ngai, na kuma ĩvinda yĩu no andũ anini mekĩte kwenda kwa Ngai vaa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ ũmũnthĩ kwĩ Ngũsĩ ta milioni nyanya. Ngũsĩ isu iyĩkaa o kũvoya kwenda kwa Ngai kwĩkwe kũũ nthĩ, ĩndĩ nitataa mũno syĩkale kwosana na mboya ĩsu ivoyaa. Syĩkaa ũu kwa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũla ũmwendeeasya Ngai, na kwa kwĩkĩa kĩthito wĩanĩ wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a.
16 Kwa ngelekany'o, mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wavatisiwe mwaka wa 1948 na waĩ misonalĩ Africa aisye atĩĩ: "Nyie nĩnĩvoyaa kwosana na ndeto isu syĩ Mboyanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi ["Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ"]. Nĩvoyaa kana andũ ala mailyĩ ta malondu moneke vala maĩ na maitetheew'a mamũmanye Yeova matanamba kũselewa. O na ĩla ngwenda kũtavya mũndũ ũvoo, nĩnĩvoyaa nĩkwate ũĩ nĩ kana nĩtonye kũkiita ngoo yake. O na ĩngĩ, nĩnĩvoyaa Yeova aathime kĩthito kitũ kya kũmasũvĩa ala mailyĩ ta malondu na mambĩĩe kũmanyĩw'a ũw'o." Kwoou ti ũsengy'o kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu wĩ na myaka 80 nĩwonete mosyao maseo ũtavany'anĩ, na kana aitetheanĩsya na angĩ nũtetheesye andũ aingĩ makatw'ĩka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Vate nzika, no ũlilikane andũ angĩ ala meyumĩtye na ngenda meke kwenda kwa Ngai o na kau me o na mathĩna ma ũkũũ.—Soma Savuli 110:3.
17. We wĩw'aa ata wasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova ũkeka nĩ kana asũngĩe kĩlungu kĩĩ kya Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi, "Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ"?
17 Twĩendeea kũvoya kwenda kwa Ngai kwĩkwe kũũ nthĩ nginya ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkavetanga amaitha maw'o kũũ nthĩ. Ũu wathela, tũkeeyonea kwenda kwa Ngai kũyĩkwa nesa vyũ kwĩ tene ĩla andũ mbilioni mbingĩ methayũũkw'a mekale nthĩ nzaũ. Yesũ aisye ũũ: "Mũikaseng'e kwondũ wa ũu: nũndũ saa nĩwũkĩte, yĩla onthe ala me mbũanĩ makew'a wasya [wakwa], namo makauma." (Yoa. 5:28, 29) Tũkew'a mũyo mũno ethĩwa tũkeethĩwa twĩ thayũ ĩvinda yĩu tũthokye endwa maitũ ala makathayũũkw'a! Ĩvinda yĩu Ngai "akavyaĩa methoi onthe methonĩ [maitũ]." (Ũvu. 21:4) Aingĩ methayũũkw'a nĩ ala "mate alũngalu," ala makwie matemanyĩĩtye ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai na Mwana wake. Ĩkeethĩwa ndaĩa nene mũno kũmanyĩsya asu methayũũkw'a ĩũlũ wa kwenda kwa Ngai na kĩeleelo kyake, na nũndũ wa ũu ũyĩthĩa nĩtwamatetheesya methĩwe matonya kũkwata "thayũ ũtathela."—Meko 24:15; Yoa. 17:3.
18. Mavata ala manene ma andũ nĩ meva?
18 Kũikethĩwa na mũuo na wĩw'ano kũũ nthĩ nginya ĩla Yeova ũkathesya ĩsyĩtwa yake aitũmĩa Ũsumbĩ wake. Kwoou ĩla Ngai wĩsũngĩa nesa maũndũ ma mbee atatũ ala me ĩla Mboyanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi, akeethĩwa eanĩsya mavata ala manene ma andũ. Ĩndĩ ve maũndũ angĩ ana me nthĩnĩ wa ĩla Mboya ya Mwĩaĩi ala monanĩtye maũndũ angĩ ma vata twendaa kwĩanĩw'a. Maũndũ asu nĩmaneeneetwe ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe.
