translation:
"When you pray, say this."—Matt. 6:9.
1. But why should we be careful to use only the words that are recorded in Matthew 6:9-13?
Many people think it is right to explain God's Word to others. But why should we go from house to house, spending much time, when our message may not touch their hearts, or when they may not believe that God's Kingdom is something real and close? Or should we try to impress people with fine speeches, so that they will think we are wise, or that God is important? Or should we simply tell them what God wants us to say, and if our prayer is not answered, or if we are told to stop, should we say our prayer was "said in vain"?—Matt. 6:9, footnotes explaining the New World Translation.
2. What if Jesus taught us to pray in order that we might have opportunity to preach?
Yes, Jesus taught his disciples to pray so that they would have an excuse to preach to many people, especially those who were not Christians. Why? Because he wanted to help them learn how to preach: "When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites." (Matt. 6:7) And because many people needed to learn how to pray, he gave them a model prayer to use so that they would not stumble. (Luke 11:1-4) So Jesus taught us to learn how to pray properly, and he showed us things we should include in our prayers. Therefore, the model prayer helps us know what to pray about.
3. What reasons do we have for being willing to use the model prayer when we teach about God's Word?
The third lesson and the one that follows will help us understand this. The question is, 'Can this prayer really help me to express my own thoughts in my own words? And if I do, will you still approve of my prayer?'
"TEACH US TO PRAY"
4. The expression "Our Father" teaches us something important, and why can we confidently call Jehovah "Father," unlike some others who claim to be children of God?
God's Word explains this regarding the expression "Our Father," not "My Father." For this reason, the expression "Our Father" shows that we are among many "children" of God. (1 Pet. 2:17) That is very encouraging! Since Christ has been given authority to intercede for us, we can approach God as sons. And so we can rightly call Jehovah "Father." (Rev. 8:15-17) Also, since Christ has been given authority to intercede for others, we can call Jehovah "Father." Why? Because he is the one who leads the way, and we imitate him in expressing sincere devotion. He gives those who seek God as sons the privilege of approaching God through his Son, just as they would approach a loving father.—Rev. 8:21; Acts 20:7, 8.
5, 6. What benefits does a young person gain from practicing regularly, and how can parents encourage their children to do so? (See accompanying article on page 20.)
A young person will strengthen his faith and develop the ability to remain loyal to Jehovah when faced with trials and temptations, if he practices regularly. For example, a young man in South Africa said: "When I was growing up, my parents encouraged me to talk about my feelings and to share what was troubling me. Many young people feel that their parents do not really listen to them. But I felt comfortable talking to my parents, and I knew they understood how I felt. So I continued to practice speaking honestly, and I continued to tell them things that were bothering me. And I learned to appreciate the value of being able to confide in someone. It helped me to stay close to Jehovah."
Furthermore, we can strengthen our relationship with Jehovah by spending time with him. Yes, he wants to get to know us personally. Also, we show appreciation to God by thanking him for everything he does for us. A strong desire to maintain a close relationship with Jehovah will help us to overcome difficulties. We might also be reminded of the importance of continuing to cultivate our personal relationship with Jehovah so that it does not weaken. This could involve making an effort to learn more about God's qualities and to imitate his love.—Ps. 5:11, 12; 91:14.
"HIS LOYAL LOVE IS EVERLASTING"
What reasons do God's servants have for rejoicing, and why is this good news?
It is comforting to know that God cares about us, and that he considers us 'his people.' (Acts 15:14; Isa. 43:10) That is why we refer to our loving Father as follows: "His loyal love is everlasting." By supporting Jehovah, we demonstrate that we trust in his ability to fulfill his purpose, no matter what obstacles may arise. We want to be like the faithful angels who remain united in their support of God and his people. The apostle Paul wrote: "God's Kingdom…is among you."—Col. 2:21-24.
8, 9. How can we show that we appreciate what Jehovah has done for us and continues to do?
8 We can strengthen our faith by thinking about things that prove God's loyal love is everlasting. Consider the example of a sister in Norway who was raised by an unbelieving father. This sister became a dedicated Christian while still a young girl. She explains: "I felt very insecure. Every day I worried whether my parents would accept me if I took a stand, or if they would think I was foolish, and because of this, I often prayed to Jehovah for help to overcome Satan's influence. I wanted to honor Jehovah, and I wanted my family to see how important spiritual things were to me."—Prov. 27:11.
9 Why does Jehovah allow us to face trials? Yes, it is often to strengthen our faith and draw us closer to him. This sister also explained that she benefited greatly from associating with fellow Christians. And within five years, her husband joined the congregation. Her son, now 20 years old, is baptized. This sister says: "I am so grateful for the encouragement I received from others."
10. What will we discuss next regarding honoring God's name?
10 What will we discuss next regarding honoring God's name and making sure it continues to be glorified throughout eternity? If we do, we can be confident that Jehovah will support us and use his great power. (Read Ezekiel 38:22, 23.) At that time, people will learn to fear Jehovah more and more. Let us therefore zealously continue proclaiming God's name, knowing that we are joining those whom Jehovah has sent to proclaim it! This is what the apostle Paul meant when he called our ministry "good news of peace."—1 Cor. 15:28.
"YOUR LOYALTY WILL BE TESTED"
11, 12. What did faithful Christians realize in 1876?
11 Jesus asked questions to get his disciples thinking, and they asked him: "Lord, are you going to restore the kingdom to Israel now?" Jesus' answer showed that they needed to focus on supporting God's Kingdom. They realized that they should not try to set a specific date for its establishment, nor should they be discouraged if things did not happen as quickly as they expected. (Read Acts 1:6-8.) So they continued to preach the good news with boldness. That is why this ministry of the apostles came to be known as "the good news of God's Kingdom."
12 While encouraging them to preach the good news, Jehovah helped his people understand what was involved in fulfilling Jesus' prophecy. For example, in 1876, an article was written by Charles Taze Russell and published in a small journal called Bible Examiner. The article was titled, "The Times of the Gentiles: When Do They End?," and it explained how the year 1914 would be significant. This article connected the "times of the Gentiles" mentioned in Daniel's prophecy with the "times of the nations" that Jesus spoke about. *—Dan. 4:16; Luke 21:24.
13 What did Christians observe in 1914, and what events have continued to unfold since then?
13 In 1914, war broke out in Europe, and soon much of the world became embroiled in conflict. That war lasted until 1918, and millions of young men lost their lives, while many more were left maimed or traumatized. These events corresponded to the "wars" Jesus foretold as signs that would identify the time when he would begin to exercise authority as King. (Matt. 24:3-8; Luke 21:10, 11) Many important developments occurred in 1914 that showed that Jesus Christ had been "made king." That year marked the beginning of "the conclusion of the system of things," and it continues to this day. (Rev. 6:2) It also signaled increased activity by Satan and his demons. As the end has drawn near, people have experienced intense trouble, as described in this vision: "Woe to those on the earth because of the blast of the trumpet blasts of the seven angels!"—Rev. 12:7-12.
14. (a) What is involved in supporting God's Kingdom? (b) What questions will we answer?
14 The account at Revelation 12:7-12 shows why God's Kingdom began to triumph over the enemy and what this means for faithful Christians. In that vision, Jesus, who is the King of God's Kingdom, is depicted as taking action to strengthen his loyal followers. And we want to support God's Kingdom by being like Jesus in our zealous ministry. To remain steadfast, we need to be aware of the tactics the enemy uses to discourage us. How can we do that? By paying attention to warnings about "wars." Jesus said: "This good news of the kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all nations." (Matt. 24:14).
"THE END IS APPROACHING"
15, 16. How can we stay close to God's organization, "the end"?
15 For some 6,000 years, mankind has been gradually drifting away from God's purpose. That is why Jehovah allowed imperfection to enter so that humans could prove their loyalty and demonstrate what "the heart" of man is really like. (Gen. 1:31) But Satan rebelled against God, and he has led millions of people to turn away from God's way. Today, billions live without knowing God's standards. So we must be careful not to drift away from the worship of God, and we must stay close to God's organization. We can do this by remaining humble, by continuing to seek God's guidance, and by being determined to help others learn the truth.
16 For example, a missionary who was sent to Africa in 1948 said: "I want to remain loyal to the Messianic Kingdom ["God's Kingdom"]. I want to remain loyal even if others ridicule me or persecute me because of my faith in Jehovah. And even if someone tries to force me to abandon the truth, I want to remain steadfast and refuse to compromise my integrity. Moreover, I want Jehovah to use me to encourage others to remain faithful despite difficulties and trials." He continued serving faithfully until he was over 80 years old, and his fine example helped many others to get involved in Jehovah's service. Consider this, and strengthen others who may be getting discouraged in their worship of God—whether they are young or older.—Read Psalm 110:3.
17 What, then, can we do to avoid drifting away from Jehovah and His Messianic Kingdom, "God's Kingdom"?
17 Let us continue to show our appreciation for God's Kingdom by actively supporting the work of proclaiming it. To do so, remember that billions of people have never had a real opportunity to learn about it. Jesus said: "The hour is coming when all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out…to everlasting life." (John 5:28, 29) How happy we can be to know that Jehovah has made provisions for resurrecting millions who lived in the past! Jehovah "will wipe out every tear from their eyes." (Revelation 21:4) Many of those resurrected ones will be "sheep," who will appreciate learning about Jehovah God and his Son. So let us zealously share the good news of God's Kingdom and its blessings with everyone we meet, so that they too may have the opportunity to gain "everlasting life."—Mark 24:15; John 17:3.
18 What great blessings await mankind?
18 We will discuss this under the heading 'God's Purpose Revealed,' as Jehovah lovingly reveals his purposes through his Word. This is why God is using his organization to help sincere people understand what the Bible teaches about these great blessings awaiting mankind. In addition, there are many other things we can learn from the Bible that will help us to live lives pleasing to him. These matters will be considered in the following chapters.

text:
"Kĩwĩu kya nyũmba yaku kĩkandya."—YOA. 2:17.
MBATHI: 13, 21
1, 2. (a) Athũkũmi ma Yeova mamũthaithĩaa va ĩvinda ya tene? (b) Yesũ aĩ na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa ĩkalũ ya Ngai yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme? (c) Kĩeleelo kya ĩsomo yĩĩ nĩ kĩva?
KUMA tene andũ ma Ngai nĩmethĩawa na kũndũ kwĩsĩkĩwe kũla mamũthaithĩaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, no kwĩthĩwa Aveli aakĩie Ngai kĩthembeo nĩ kana amumĩsye nthembo. (Mwa. 4:3, 4) O na Noa, Avalaamu, Isaka, Yakovo, na Mose nĩmaakĩie Ngai ithembeo. (Mwa. 8:20; 12:7; 26:25; 35:1; Kuma 17:15) Namo Aisilaeli nĩmaseũvisye ĩeema maatĩĩe mũtalatala ũla Yeova wamanete. (Kuma 25:8) O na nĩmesie kwaka ĩkalũ ya kũmũthaithĩa Yeova. (1 Asu. 8:27, 29) O na ĩngĩ, ĩla Ayuti mesie kuma ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni, mambĩĩe kũthaithĩaa masinakokenĩ. (Mko. 6:2; Yoa. 18:20; Meko 15:21) Nayo ĩvinda ya atũmwa, Aklĩsto nĩmoombanĩaa mĩsyĩ kwa ana-a-asa ala angĩ. (Meko 12:12; 1 Ako. 16:19) Na ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ, andũ ma Yeova nĩmombanĩaa Nyũmbanĩ sya Ũsumbĩ nĩ kana mamanyĩw'e na maimũthaitha Yeova. Na kũvikĩĩa yu kwĩ Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ ngili mĩongo yĩana ũna nthĩ yonthe.
2 Yesũ nĩwendete mũno ĩkalũ ya Yeova yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme na nĩwayĩnengete ndaĩa. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ũmwe wa ala maandĩkie mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo woonanisye kana wathani ũũ nĩwamũkonetye: "Kĩwĩu kya nyũmba yaku nĩkĩndĩte." (Sav. 69:9; Yoa. 2:17) Ũmũnthĩ vai Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ o na yĩva yaĩlĩtwe vyũ nĩ kwĩtwa "nyũmba ya Yeova" ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ ĩkalũ yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme yeetawa. (2 Mav. 5:13; 33:4) O na vailyĩ ũu, Mbivilia yĩ na myolooto ĩtwonasya ũndũ kũla tũthaithĩaa ũmũnthĩ kwaĩlĩte kũtũmĩwa na kũnengwa ndaĩa. Kwoou kĩeleelo kya ĩsomo yĩĩ nĩ kũneenea myolooto ĩmwe katĩ wa ĩsu nĩ kana twone ũndũ ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmanye ũndũ twaĩle kwĩkuaa ĩla twĩ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, na tũyona ũndũ ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tumasye mĩvothi kwondũ wa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ, na ũndũ tũtonya kũisũvĩa. *
NĨTŨNENGAE NDAĨA ŨTHAITHI WA W'O
3-5. Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ yĩthĩawa na vata mwaũ? Kĩu kyaĩle kũtũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na woni wĩva ĩũlũ wa maũmbano ala mekĩawa vau?
3 Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ nĩvo andũ ma ũtũi mũna matonya kũkomanĩa nĩ kana mamũthaithe Yeova. Maũmbano ma kĩla kyumwa ala mekĩawa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ nĩ mũthĩnzĩo ũmwe Yeova ũtũnengete nĩ kana tũlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yitũ vamwe nake. Ĩla twathi maũmbanonĩ asu nĩtwĩkĩawa vinya na tũkatavw'a ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka maũndũ. Kwoou ala onthe maendaa maũmbanonĩ no ũndũ ũmwe na methĩawa mathoketw'e nĩ Yeova na Mwana wake. Ĩndĩ o na kau mavinda onthe nĩtwĩthĩawa tũthoketw'e tũye "mesanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi," tũyaĩle kwĩsa kwona ũsu ta ũndũ mũnini.—1 Ako. 10:21.
4 Yeova onaa mavinda asu tũmbanaa nĩ kana tũmũthaithe na tũyĩkĩana vinya me ma vata mũno, na nĩkyo kĩtumi wamũveveee mũtũmwa Vaulo atũthangaasye tũendeee kũmbana vamwe tũte kũeka. (Soma Aevelania 10:24, 25.) Kwoou-ĩ, nĩtwĩthĩwa tũimũnenga Yeova ndaĩa ethĩwa tũkatĩĩaa maũmbano ma Kĩklĩsto vate kĩtumi kĩ va kĩĩ? Ĩla tweeyũmbanĩsya maũmbano nesa na twaumya maelesyo na ngoo yonthe, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea, na kana nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ wa maũmbano asu.—Sav. 22:22.
5 Mwĩkalĩle witũ ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ na woni witũ ĩũlũ wa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ waĩle kwonany'a kana nĩtũmũnengete Yeova ndaĩa ĩla yaĩle. Kana we tyo ũkwĩtĩkĩla kana ethĩwa nũnengete ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai ndaĩa, yĩla yĩthĩawa yĩandĩkĩtwe kĩvwaũnĩ kya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ, nĩwaĩle kwĩthĩwa ũnengete ndaĩa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ na maũmbano maitũ?—Sianĩsya na 1 Asumbĩ 8:17.
6. Andũ amwe maĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa Nyũmba sitũ sya Ũsumbĩ na ĩũlũ wa ala mombanĩaa vo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 27.)
6 Mavinda maingĩ andũ mate Ngũsĩ nĩmonaa ndaĩa ĩla tũnengete vala tũthaithĩaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ ũmwe kuma nthĩ ya Turkey aisye atĩĩ: "Neewie nenda mũno ũndũ Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ yaĩ ntheu na ũndũ maũndũ na syĩndũ syavangĩtwe nesa. Ala maĩ vo meekĩĩte ngũa nesa, maĩ atanu, na mangethisye nesa mũno. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumie nĩtana mũno." Mũndũ ũsu nĩwambĩĩe kũendaa maũmbanonĩ ateũtĩĩa, na ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ nĩwavatisiwe. O na ĩngĩ mũsyĩnĩ ũmwe nthĩ ya Indonesia kĩkundi kĩmwe nĩkyathokisye anene ma silikalĩ ma kwoo na atũi moke meloele Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ ĩtanamba kũvathwa kwondũ wa kũmũthaithaa Yeova. O na mũnene wa mũsyĩ ũsu (mayor) nĩwaendie vau. Nĩwendeeiw'e mũno nĩ mwakĩle wayo, ũndũ yaakĩtwe yĩ ndũmu, na ũndũ kawanza kala kaĩ vau kaanakavĩtw'e. Mũnene ũsu aisye ũũ: "Ũtheu wa nyũmba ĩno wĩonany'a nesa vyũ kana mwĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu."
7, 8. Ala onthe maendaa maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto maĩle kũlilikana maũndũ meva ma vata?
7 Mwĩkĩĩle witũ wa ngũa, mwĩkalĩle witũ, na kwĩyanakavya kwitũ kwaĩle kwonany'a kana nĩtũnengete ndaĩa Ngai ũla ũtũthokasya maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto. Na ethĩwa nĩtũnengete Ngai ndaĩa ĩsu, tũikavĩtaa mĩvaka. Nĩkwĩsĩte kwoneka kana amwe nĩ ta mekĩĩaa andũ mĩao mingĩ mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩtaĩle kwĩkwa ĩla twĩ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, namo angĩ ĩla mathi vau nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa melekeleelye mũno ta me mũsyĩ. Nĩ w'o kana Yeova nĩwendaa athũkũmi make na aeni ala matũthokea mew'e me eanĩe me vau. Ĩndĩ ti ũseo kũvũthĩĩsya maũmbano maitũ kwa kũendaa vau na ngũa sya mũsyĩ, kana kwĩka maũndũ angĩ maũmbano maendeee, ta kũtũma mesengyi, kũea ngewa, na kũya na kũnyw'a syĩndũ. Namo asyai maĩle kũmanyĩsya syana syoo kana iyaĩle kũsembasemba na kũthaũka syavika Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ.—Mũta. 3:1.
8 Ĩvinda yĩmwe ĩla Yesũ woonie andũ maiete viasala ĩkalũnĩ ya Ngai, nĩwathatie mũno na amalũngya. (Yoa. 2:13-17) O ta ũu, Nyũmba sitũ sya Ũsumbĩ nĩ kũndũ kwa kũthaithĩa Yeova na kũmanyĩw'a ĩũlũ wake. Kwoou viasala syonthe itakonetye ũthaithi witũ syaĩle kũkũnĩwa kũndũ kũngĩ na ti vau.—Sianĩsya na Neemia 13:7, 8.
NĨTŨTETHEEASYA KWAKA NYŨMBA SYA ŨSUMBĨ
9, 10. (a) Kwĩkawa ata nĩ kana Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ syakwe, na kĩu kĩtetheesye ata? (b) Nĩ mũvango wĩva wĩthĩĩtwe ũitetheesya mũno ikundi ila itona mbesa sya kwĩyakĩa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ?
9 Andũ ma Yeova nĩmatataa ũndũ matonya make Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ ite na maũndũ maingĩ, o na nĩmatataa maumye mĩvothi kwondũ wasyo. Wĩa w'onthe wa kũsola ũndũ Nyũmba isu sya Ũsumbĩ syĩkwakwa na wa kũsyaka na kũitũngĩĩa, ũtethaw'a nĩ andũ meyumĩtye mate kũĩvwa. Kĩu kĩtetheesye ata? Kuma Ĩtukũ 1, Mwei wa 11, 1999, Nyũmba mbanake sya Ũsumbĩ mbee wa 28,000 nĩsyakĩwe ikundi nthĩ yonthe. Ũu nĩ kwasya kana kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 15 mĩvĩtu, Nyũmba ta itano sya Ũsumbĩ nĩsyakawa kĩla mũthenya.
10 Andũ ma Yeova nĩmatetheeasya nĩ kana Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ syakwe kũla ite kw'o. Mũvango ũũ wosanĩte na mwolooto wa Maandĩko ũla wonanĩtye kana ala me na mbingĩ no matetheesye ala manyivĩwe, nĩ kana onthe 'meanany'e.' (Soma 2 Akolintho 8:13-15.) Nũndũ wa ũu, Nyũmba mbanake sya Ũsumbĩ nĩsyakĩwe ikundi ila itaĩ syona mbesa sya kwĩyakĩa.
11. Ana-a-asa amwe maasya ata mamina kwakĩwa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ? Ndeto syoo itumaa wĩw'a ata?
11 Kĩkundi kĩmwe kĩ nthĩ ya Costa Rica kyaakĩiwe Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ kyaandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ĩla twasisya Nyũmba yitũ ya Ũsumbĩ twonaa ta tũkũota. O na tũyonaa ta w'o. Aĩ na mwa nyũmba ĩsu yanakavĩte ũu yathelile na mĩthenya nyanya! Mwako ũsu wathelile nũndũ Yeova nĩwaũathimie, andũ ma Yeova nĩmeekĩte mĩvango mĩseo, na ana-a-asa maitũ nĩmatũkwatie mbau. Vandũ vau va kũthaithĩa nĩ mũthĩnzĩo mũseo vyũ na wa vata twanengiwe nĩ Yeova. Twĩ na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno nũndũ wa ũu." We tyo ũtanaa mũno ĩla weew'a ana-a-asa maweta ndeto ta isu sya kũtũnga mũvea ĩtina wa kwakĩwa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ? Na we tyo ũtanaa mũno wamanya kana ana-a-asa ngili mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe nĩmatanaa o ta ana-a-asa asu ma Costa Rica ĩla maakĩwa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ? Wĩa w'onthe ũkonetye kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ nĩ wĩa wa Yeova nũndũ mavinda maingĩ Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ yathela oou, andũ aingĩ me na ngoo ntheu na mekwenda kũmanya ĩũlũ wa Mũmbi witũ wĩ wendo nĩmambĩĩaa kũthi vo.—Sav. 127:1.
12. Ũtonya kũtetheesya ata myako ya Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ?
12 Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ nĩmatanaa mũno nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa nĩmakwatĩte mwanya wa kũtetheesya myako ya Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ o na twĩthĩwe nĩtũtonya kũthi kwaka Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ kana tũitonya, ithyonthe no tũtetheesye wĩa ũsu kwa kumya mĩvothi. Andũ aingĩ maĩ na kĩthito kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa w'o ĩvinda ya tene nĩmaumisye mĩvothi ya kwaka myako ĩkonetye ũthaithi wa Yeova, naitũ ũmũnthĩ no twĩke oou, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu tũimũtaĩa Yeova.—Kuma 25:2; 2 Ako. 9:7.
NĨTŨTHEASYA NYŨMBA YITŨ YA ŨSUMBĨ
13, 14. Nĩ myolooto yĩva yĩ Maandĩkonĩ ĩtũtetheeasya kũmanya kana nĩtwaĩle kũthesya Nyũmba yitũ ya Ũsumbĩ na kũmĩvanga nesa?
13 Ngai ũla tũthaithaa ti wa kĩthokoany'o. Nũndũ wa ũu, twamina kwakĩwa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ nĩtwaĩle kũmĩthesya na kũmĩvanga nesa yĩkale ũndũ Ngai ũsu tũthaithaa wendaa. (Soma 1 Akolintho 14:33, 40.) Mbivilia nĩwetanĩasya ũthaithi witũ na ũtheu witũ wa kĩ-mwĩĩ. (Ũvu. 19:8) Kwoou ethĩwa andũ nĩmekwenda metĩkĩlwe nĩ Yeova, no nginya mekale me atheu kĩ-mwĩĩ.
14 Twaatĩĩa myolooto ĩsu, tũkathokasya andũ maũmbanonĩ maitũ twĩ eanĩe nũndũ nĩtwĩsĩ mooka nĩmeĩthĩa kana ũtheu wa nyũmba yitũ nĩwosanĩte na ũvoo mũseo ũla tũtavanasya. O na nĩmakonaa kana tũthaithaa Ngai mũtheu, ũla o mĩtũkĩ ũkilyĩ anathesya nthĩ ĩno na aimĩtw'ĩkĩthya nzaũ.—Isa. 6:1-3; Ũvu. 11:18.
15, 16. (a) Nĩkĩ mavinda amwe ti laisi kũthesya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ, ĩndĩ nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmĩthesya? (b) Nĩ mĩvango yĩva yĩkĩtwe ya kũthesya vala mũthaithĩaa, na kĩla ũmwe atonya kũtanĩa kwĩka ata?
15 Andũ amwe nĩmendete ũtheu mũno kwĩ angĩ. Kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩtumaa andũ methĩwa na kĩvathũkany'o kĩu nĩ mũeele ũla maeetwe. O na ĩngĩ, angĩ mekalaa kũndũ kwĩ ndaka kana kĩtoo, nakw'o kũndũ kũngĩ kwĩ malelũ mathũku. Namo amwe kũkwata kĩw'ũ na savunĩ nĩ thĩna. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa kwitũ kũilyĩ ata na andũ nĩ atheu kana ti atheu, twaĩle kũthesya Nyũmba yitũ ya Ũsumbĩ na kũmĩvanga nesa nũndũ yĩtanĩaw'a na Yeova, na vau nĩvo tũmũthaithĩaa.—Kũt. 23:14.
16 Tũitonya kwasya tũkatheasya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ ĩla mwanya waumĩla. Kwoou kĩla nzama ya atumĩa nĩyaĩle kũandĩka mũvango wa kũthesya vala kĩkundi kĩthaithĩaa na ĩimantha syĩndũ ianĩte sya kũvathesya na kũvekalya vailyĩ nesa vyũ. Ĩndĩ ve mawĩa amwe maĩle kũtethw'a ĩtina wa kĩla ũmbano, namo angĩ no matethw'e ĩtina wa kavinda. Nũndũ wa ũu, nũseo vethĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na mawĩa asu maiũngamĩwa nesa nĩ kana maũndũ amwe maikatiwe mate meke. Kĩla ũmwe kĩkundinĩ no atanĩe kũkwata mbau mĩvango ya ũtheu.
NĨTŨSŨVĨAA NYŨMBA YITŨ YA ŨSUMBĨ
17, 18. (a) Nĩ ngelekany'o syĩva syĩ Maandĩkonĩ syĩkwonany'a kana nĩtwaĩle kũsũvĩaa kũla tũthaithĩaa? (b) Nĩkĩ no nginya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ ĩsũvĩwe?
17 Ũndũ ũngĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova mekaa nĩ kũtata mũno masũvĩe kũla mathaithĩaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Mũsumbĩ Yeoasi wasumbĩkĩte Yuta, nĩweeaĩe athembi matũmĩe mĩvothi ĩla yaumĩtw'e kwondũ wa nyũmba ya Yeova nĩ kana 'matũngĩĩe kũndũ kũvũthũku kwa nyũmba, o vala voonekie ũomboku.' (2 Asu. 12:4, 5) Ĩtina wa myaka mbee wa 200 o nake Mũsumbĩ Yosia nĩwatũmĩie mĩvothi ĩla yaumĩtw'e kwondũ wa ĩkalũ nĩ kana kũla kwaanangĩkĩte kũseũvw'e.—Soma 2 Mavinda 34:9-11.
18 Kamitii imwe sya Movisi ma Ũvonge niwetete kana andũ ma nthĩ imwe syĩ ungu wa movisi moo ma ũvonge mayĩthĩawa makwatĩĩe mũno kũsũvĩa myako kana mĩio ndĩkanangĩke. No kwĩthĩwa aingĩ me nthĩ isu matethĩawa na ũtũĩka wa kũsũvĩa myako kana mĩio mĩna, kana mate na mbesa sya kũtethya wĩa ũsu. Ĩndĩ ũw'o nĩ kana tũkaema kũsũvĩa Nyũmba yitũ ya Ũsumbĩ, yanangĩka mĩtũkĩ mũno na ũndũ ũsu nĩũtuma twoswa naĩ ũtũinĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla kĩkundi kyatata ũndũ kĩtonya kĩsũvĩe Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ, ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova nĩyĩtaĩawa na ũndũ ũsu nũsũvĩaa mbesa ila syumĩtw'e nĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala angĩ.
19. Ũtwi waku nĩ wĩva ĩũlũ wa kũndũ kũla tũmũthaithĩaa Yeova?
19 Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ nĩ mwako wĩthĩawa ũvathĩtwe kwondũ wa kũmũthaithĩa Yeova. Kwoou tũyĩsa kwasya vyũ nyũmba ĩsu nĩ ya mũndũ mũna kana kĩkundi kĩna, o na ethĩwa yĩandĩkĩthĩtw'e ata silikalĩnĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, myolooto ĩla Aklĩsto maatĩĩaa nĩmatetheeasya mathũkũme na ngwatanĩo nĩ kana mekalye nyũmba ĩsu kwosana na kĩeleelo kĩla yaakĩwe. Kwoou, onthe kĩkundinĩ nĩmatonya kwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kĩu kwa kũnenga vala mathaithĩaa ndaĩa ĩla ĩvaĩlĩte, kwa kumya mĩvothi ya kwaka nyũmba ingĩ, na kwa kwĩyumya matũmĩe ĩvinda yoo na vinya woo kũsũvĩa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ na kũithesya. Na o tondũ Yesũ wailyĩ, tweeka maũndũ asu tũkeethĩawa tũyonany'a kana twĩ na kĩwĩu, kana kĩthito, kwondũ wa vandũ vala tũmũthaithĩaa Yeova.—Yoa. 2:17.
^ kal. 2 O na kau ĩsomo yĩĩ yĩneenee Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ, myolooto ĩla yĩ vo no ĩkonetye Nyũmba sya Maũmbano Manene vamwe na myako ĩngĩ ĩla ĩtũmĩawa kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa w'o.

translation:
"The wisdom of the home is ruinous."—PROV. 2:17.
NOTES: 13, 21
1, 2. (a) What important qualities did Jehovah look for when choosing a wife for Isaac? (b) What desire did Jesus express regarding his future presence in God's Kingdom in Jerusalem? (c) What is the point of this lesson?
TRUE worshipers of God have always been willing to make sacrifices. For example, Abel offered God a sacrifice that was pleasing to Him. (Gen. 4:3, 4) Also, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Moses were men who pleased God. (Gen. 8:20; 12:7; 26:25; 35:1; Ex. 17:15) And the Israelites showed their faith by obeying God's commands. (Ex. 25:8) They also expressed their desire to dwell in God's tabernacle. (1 Chron. 8:27, 29) Moreover, individuals like Ruth chose to associate with true worshippers, even under difficult circumstances. (Ruth 1:16; Prov. 18:20; Acts 15:21) Today, spirit-guided Christians zealously share the good news with others. (Acts 12:12; 1 Cor. 16:19) And they willingly support the work of the Kingdom Hall, often making personal sacrifices to do so. The Kingdom Hall may be humble, but it is a place where people can learn about Jehovah.
2 Jesus traveled extensively to preach the good news throughout Judea and Galilee. This is why one of the psalmist's expressions moved him deeply: "The zeal for your house has consumed me." (Ps. 69:9; John 2:17) In ancient times, both the Temple and the Tabernacle were referred to as "the house of Jehovah," and this expression came to be associated with Jerusalem itself. (2 Ki. 5:13; 33:4) However, the Bible and history show us that genuine worship involves more than just being connected to a physical location. The purpose of our study today is to examine how we can demonstrate our zeal for the spiritual activity centered around the Kingdom Hall, how we can show our appreciation for the privileges we enjoy there, and how we can continue to improve. *
LET US EXAMINE THIS QUESTION OF ZEAL
3-5. What motivated those who built the temple? How does this help us to appreciate what those who volunteer their time and resources contribute?
3 The temple was a place where people could come to express their devotion to Jehovah. The gatherings at the Kingdom Hall are an important way for Jehovah to remind us of his love for us and to strengthen our bond with one another. But if we attend meetings regularly without making real progress, we may find ourselves going through motions without truly benefiting. It is vital that we remember that Jehovah and his Son approve of those who make sacrifices to support the work of the Kingdom Hall. Indeed, those who actively assist in maintaining the hall are considered "ministers of the sanctuary," showing their dedication to something sacred.—1 Cor. 10:21.
4 Jehovah appreciates that we associate with one another and worship him together, and this is why he inspired Paul to encourage us to continue meeting together for encouragement. (Read Hebrews 10:24, 25.) So, how can we show that we value Jehovah and want to attend Christian meetings regularly? By avoiding being overly concerned about personal matters and by prioritizing our attendance at meetings, we demonstrate that we are genuinely interested in pleasing Jehovah.—Prov. 22:22.
5 Consider this: If we attend meetings at the Kingdom Hall, does that necessarily mean that we are strengthening our relationship with Jehovah? Perhaps we feel that we are already devoted to God, yet we still benefit from the reminders and instruction provided at the Kingdom Hall. Does this not indicate that attending meetings can help us remain devoted to the Kingdom Hall and our fellow worshippers?—Compare 1 Thessalonians 8:17.
6 Some may wonder, 'What if I am unable to contribute financially to the upkeep of the Kingdom Hall or participate fully in the meetings?' (See the accompanying article, "Questions From Readers.")
6 Many people appreciate the effort that congregations make to maintain places of worship. For example, a brother in Turkey wrote: "I was very impressed when I saw how clean and well-maintained the Kingdom Hall was, despite the fact that there were few resources available. The local brothers worked hard to make it appealing, and they took pride in their work. This motivated me to get involved." That brother began attending meetings more regularly, and his interest grew. Also, a mayor in Indonesia visited one of the Kingdom Halls during a renovation project and was amazed at the dedication shown by the brothers and sisters in maintaining a place where people could worship Jehovah. He even sent workers to assist them, and he commented: "The condition of this building is much better than many others in town." The mayor added: "It shows that you really care for this place."
7, 8. What benefits do those who regularly attend Christian meetings experience?
7 By being regular, diligent, and zealous in our worship of God, we show that we value the congregation and the privilege of meeting together as Christians. And by valuing God, we strengthen our faith. It is encouraging to see that some have made adjustments to their schedules so that they can attend meetings at the Kingdom Hall, even though it may require sacrifices. Others have found ways to support the work of the congregation in other ways. It pleases Jehovah to see his worshippers supporting one another and showing appreciation for the spiritual provisions made available to them. However, we should not feel obligated to participate in social activities outside of meetings, such as meals, outings, or refreshments. But we can be hospitable and invite others to our homes, while still respecting their personal choices.—Matt. 3:1.
8 On one occasion, Jesus drove out those who were doing business in the temple, because they were defiling it. (John 2:13-17) Today, the Kingdom Hall is a place to honor Jehovah and learn about his will. Let us therefore keep it clean and free from distractions so that we can fully concentrate on spiritual matters.—Compare with Nehemiah 13:7, 8.
LET US KEEP THE KINGDOM HALL CLEAN
9, 10. (a) What does it mean to keep the Kingdom Hall clean, and why is this important? (b) What practical steps can we take to show respect for the Kingdom Hall?
9 Jehovah's people appreciate a clean and well-maintained Kingdom Hall, and they also value its peaceful atmosphere. Everyone wants the Kingdom Hall to be a pleasant place to worship and to preach, and this is especially true for visitors. Why is this important? On November 11, 1999, some 28,000 Kingdom Halls were cleaned simultaneously. This took place during a 15-minute period, and five Kingdom Halls were cleaned every minute.
10 Jehovah's people are willing to keep the Kingdom Hall clean. This willingness is motivated by their understanding of Bible principles that teach that generosity should be proportional to what one has means. (Read 2 Corinthians 8:13-15.) As a result, Kingdom Halls are often cleaned quickly and efficiently.
11. What further assistance may some Kingdom Hall custodians need? What can motivate us to offer such help?
11 One congregation in Costa Rica wrote to the branch office saying: "We really enjoyed cleaning our Kingdom Hall; it was so satisfying. And we realized how much more it could be done! Our hall had never been so bright! We feel that Jehovah has blessed our efforts, and Jehovah's people have shown appreciation, and our brothers and sisters have encouraged us. Many others have expressed their gratitude, and we feel very grateful to Jehovah. We have great joy because of this." How can you show similar joy when assisting with the cleaning of the Kingdom Hall? And how can you find out whether there is a greater need for volunteers in your congregation or in another congregation in your area? Above all, remember that those who build the Kingdom Hall are building for Jehovah, and many people will come to know about God's love through them.—Ps. 127:1.
12 Should we pay attention to the appearance of the Kingdom Hall?
12 Many brothers and sisters enjoy contributing to maintaining the beauty of the Kingdom Hall. However, we should not become overly concerned about its appearance, but rather focus on keeping it clean. Many appreciate the effort put into making the hall attractive, and they are reminded of the importance of honoring Jehovah, and in turn, they are motivated to worship Him.—Prov. 25:2; 2 Cor. 9:7.
LET US KEEP OUR KINGDOM HALL CLEAN
13, 14. What Scriptural principles can help us determine whether we are zealous about keeping our Kingdom Hall clean and well-maintained?
13 God values neatness. Therefore, we want to maintain the Kingdom Hall so that it reflects our desire to honor God. (Read 1 Corinthians 14:33, 40.) Let us examine ourselves and our attitude toward cleanliness. (Prov. 19:8) We want to please Jehovah, and we want our conduct to be exemplary.
14 If we apply what we learn, we will likely find ways to encourage others to join us in ensuring that the appearance of our hall is pleasing and that it does not clash with the fine example we set. Also, we can discern whether we truly value God's standards, which require humility and reverence.—Isa. 6:1-3; Prov. 11:18.
15, 16. (a) What are some reasons why we might not feel qualified to clean the Kingdom Hall, and how can we overcome such feelings? (b) What practical steps can we take to contribute to cleaning, and what can each one do?
15 Some may feel inadequate because they lack experience. One reason people hesitate is fear of making mistakes. Others may live far away or have limited mobility. Still others may struggle with health problems. However, regardless of whether we feel capable or not, we should strive to care for our Kingdom Hall and show that we are devoted to Jehovah, and this is how we worship him.—Eccl. 23:14.
16 We can find ways to assist with cleaning even if we have limited time. Each congregation should arrange for a schedule of cleaning, and everyone can volunteer to do tasks that he feels able to handle. Some may be assigned specific duties during certain meetings, while others may be asked to help on an occasional basis. Thus, those who are able can work alongside others, and adjustments can be made to accommodate individual circumstances. Everyone should endeavor to adhere to the established schedule.
WE VALUE OUR KINGDOM HALL
17, 18. (a) How can we determine whether we are doing enough to support the Kingdom Hall? (b) What steps are taken when a Kingdom Hall needs to be renovated?
17 Jehovah appreciates it when his worshippers make earnest efforts to contribute. For example, when King Josiah repaired the temple in Judah, he directed men to remove "the corruptions" from the house of Jehovah and to 'repair the damage to the wall,' or even rebuild it. (2 Chron. 12:4, 5) After about 200 years, King Josiah sent men to repair the damage to the roof—perhaps due to neglect.—Read 2 Kings 34:9-11.
18 At times, circuit overseers have noted that some congregations need encouragement to put forth more effort in maintaining their meeting places. If this applies to us, we might ask ourselves, 'Are we willing to use our time and resources to improve the appearance of our hall, or are we simply waiting for others to do so?' If we love the House of God, we will be motivated to work hard and take pride in keeping it clean and well-maintained. And if a congregation consistently neglects the Kingdom Hall, Jehovah's name is dishonored, and this affects their spirituality. If a group repeatedly fails to care for the Kingdom Hall, they may lose the privilege of having one.
19. What question will we now answer to show how we can continue to support Jehovah?
19 The Kingdom Hall is a place where we gather to worship Jehovah. We should always view it as something sacred, not merely as a building owned by individuals or a congregation, nor as just a place where meetings are held. Because of this, zealous Christians are happy to spend their time and energy caring for the Hall, making needed repairs, and keeping it clean. They also willingly contribute financially to help maintain it and improve its appearance. And like Jesus instructed, we should not become overly concerned about material things, such as furniture or decorations, when supporting those who worship Jehovah.—John 2:17.
^ par. 2 Often, during visits to the Kingdom Hall, circuit overseers observe that little has been done to make improvements, while much money has been spent on large Assembly Halls and other facilities used for larger gatherings.

text:
"Eka mũndũ wa Ngai ũla ũnatũmĩte oke [atũmanyĩsye] ũndũ twĩĩkana na kana kala kesyawa."
MBATHI: 41, 6
1. Manoa eekie ata ĩla wamanyie kana nũkũmesya mwana?
MANOA na mũka mayaĩ na mwana na mayeeteele kũmesya ũmwe nũndũ Manoa nĩweesĩ nesa mũka ndasyaa. Nũndũ wa ũu Manoa nĩwaseng'ie mũno ĩla mũthenya ũmwe mũka wamũtavisye ũvoo mũseo mũno. Mũlaĩka wa Yeova aĩ anamũthokea na akamwĩa o mĩtũkĩ nũkũsyaa mwana. Vate nzika, Manoa nĩwatanie mũno o na kau nĩwamanyie kana yu nĩwakwata wĩa ũngĩ mũitango. Wĩa mwaũ? Ĩvinda yĩu matwĩe andũ maĩ athũku mũno, na no nginya ethĩwe aseng'aa matonya kũea ata mwana woo atw'ĩke mũthũkũmi wa Ngai. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Manoa "wamũvoyie Yeova," na amwĩa: "Nĩngũũvoya, eka mũndũ wa Ngai [mũlaĩka] ũla ũnatũmĩte oke ĩngĩ kwitũ, na aitũmanyĩsya ũndũ twĩĩkana na kana kala kesyawa."—Asi. 13:1-8.
2. Nĩ kyaũ waĩle kũmanyĩsya mwana waku, na ũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? (No ũtũmĩe ĩsandũkũ "Amanyĩw'a Maku Ala ma Vata Vyũ.")
2 Ethĩwa wĩ mũsyai nĩvatonyeka ũkaelewa nĩkĩ Manoa wamwĩsũvie Ngai. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o naku wĩ na kĩanda kĩito mũno kya kũtetheesya mwana waku amũmanye Yeova na aimwenda. * (Nth. 1:8) Asyai Aklĩsto nĩmatataa methĩwe na mũvango mũseo wa Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ ũla ũtonya kũtetheesya syana syoo iendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova na iimwenda mũnango. Vate nzika, Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ wĩ w'oka ndũtuma ũtetheesya mwana waku alũmye ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. (Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 6:6-9.) Kwoou ũtonya kwĩanĩsya ata kĩanda kĩu kya kũmanyĩsya mwana waku ũw'o? Ĩsomo yĩĩ na yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩmeũtũmanyĩsya ũndũ asyai matonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. O na vala Yesũ ndaĩ na syana, asyai nĩmatonya kũtetheka mũno maatĩĩa nzĩa yake ya kũmanyĩsya. Yesũ amanyĩasya amanyĩw'a make kwa nzĩa yoonanisye nĩwamendete, aĩ na wĩnyivyo, na ũmanyi. Ekai tũneenee maũndũ asu me atatũ.
ENDA MWANA WAKU
3. Yesũ oonanasya ata kana nĩwendete amanyĩw'a make?
3 Yesũ ndeew'aa vinya wa kwĩa amanyĩw'a make kana nũmendete. (Soma Yoana 15:9.) O na ĩngĩ, nĩwamonisye kana nĩwamendete nũndũ aĩ ndũũ namo na nĩwatindanasya namo mũno. (Mko. 6:31, 32; Yoa. 2:2; 21:12, 13) Yesũ ndaĩ mũndũ ũtathekaa na amanyĩw'a make. Nũndũ wa maũndũ ta asu, amanyĩw'a nĩmeesĩ nesa ki kana nĩwamendete vyũ. Ĩndĩ we ũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya Yesũ?
4. Ũtonya ata kũtetheesya syana syaku imanye kana nũsyendete? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 3.)
4 Asyai, tavasyai syana syenyu kana nĩmũsyendete na kĩla ĩvinda mũisyonasya kana nĩmwonaa syĩ sya vata mũno. (Nth. 4:3; Tito 2:4) Mwana-a-asa wĩkalaa Australia wĩtawa Samuel aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ĩla naĩ kamwana kanini Tata nĩwanzomeaa Ĩvuku Yakwa ya Ngewa sya Mbivilia kĩla wĩoo. Nĩwanzũngĩaa makũlyo makwa, akangumbatĩa, akamumunya, na aimbĩa nĩnĩkome nesa. Naseng'ie mũno ĩla nesie kũmanya kana Tata aeewe mũsyĩ andũ matamanyĩĩte kũkumbatĩana na kũmumunyana! Ĩndĩ o na aeetwe oou, atataa ũndũ ũtonya ambony'e kana nũmbendete. Kyu kyatumie nĩtuma ndũũ nake, na neew'aa nĩ mwĩanĩe na nĩ mũsũvĩĩku." Ethĩwa wĩ mũsyai, o naku no ũtume syana syaku syĩw'a ta mwana-a-asa ũsu waitavya ndeto ta, "Nĩngwendete." Ony'a syana syaku ũndũ ũsyendete. Eaa ngewa nasyo, ĩsaa vamwe nasyo, o na thaũkaa nasyo.
5, 6. (a) Yesũ ekanaa ata na ala ũmendete? (b) Elesya ũndũ kũkany'a mwana nesa kũtonya kũmũtetheesya ekale e mwĩanĩe na aimanya nĩwendetwe.
5 Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Ala nĩmendaa, nĩnĩmakanasya na kũmakũna." * (Ũvu. 3:19) O na kau amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ matindĩaa kũkusanĩsya nũũ waĩ mũnene katĩ woo, Yesũ ndaamekĩsya ngoo. Ĩndĩ ĩla maema kũatĩĩa ũndũ wamatavya, ndeekaa o kũvindya. We nĩwamanthaa ĩvinda ĩseo na vandũ vaseo nĩ kana amalũnge auĩtye na kwa nzĩa ĩkwonany'a nũmendete.—Mko. 9:33-37.
6 Ĩla mũsyai wakany'a syana onanasya kana nũsyendete. Mavinda amwe kũelesya mwana ũseo kana ũthũku wa ũndũ mũna kwĩthĩawa kũtoetye. Ĩndĩ ve mavinda mwana ũtonya kũema kũatĩĩa kĩla ũmũtavĩtye. (Nth. 22:15) Vekala ũu atĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Mantha ĩvinda yaĩlĩte na vandũ vaseo nĩ kana ũkany'e mwana waku nesa na ũuĩtye. No wĩke ũu kwa kũmwony'a nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte, kũmũmanyĩsya, na kũmwony'a mavĩtyo make. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wa South Africa wĩtawa Elaine aĩtye ũũ: "Asyai makwa mayavĩndũkangaa ĩla meũngany'a." Aendeee kwasya: "Ĩla navĩtya na maimbĩa nĩmeũmbosea ĩtambya, mayaemaa kwĩka ũu. Ĩndĩ mayaaĩsa kũngany'a mũthenya o na ũmwe mathatĩte kana matandavĩtye nĩkĩ meũngany'a. Nũndũ wa ũu, nekalaa nĩ mwĩanĩe. Nĩneesĩ kĩla ndaaĩlĩte kwĩka na kĩla naaĩlĩte kwĩka."
ĨTHĨWA NA WĨNYIVYO
7, 8. (a) Yesũ oonanisye ata kana nĩweenyivasya ĩla ũkũvoya? (b) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva mboya syaku itonya kũmanyĩsya syana syaku kũmwĩkwatya Ngai?
7 Yesũ atanamba kũkwatwa nĩ kana akoawe avoyie atĩĩ: "Nau, Asa, maũndũ onthe nĩmatonyeka kwaku; mbĩtĩthya kĩkombe kĩĩ: ĩndĩ ti ũndũ ngwenda nyie, ĩndĩ ũndũ ũkwenda we." (Mko. 14:36) Kwasũanĩa ũndũ amanyĩw'a make meewie ĩla moonie aivoya mboya ĩsu, kana ĩla mesie kũmanya kana nĩwavoyie ũu. Vate nzika, amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ nĩmeemanyĩisye kana ethĩwa Yesũ nĩweenyivisye ũu eesũva Ĩthe wake amũtetheesye nake aĩ Mwana wa Ngai ũte na naĩ, o namo nĩmaaĩlĩte kwĩka ũu.
8 We mũsyai, syana syaku syĩmanyĩasya kyaũ ĩla syeew'a mboya yaku? Nĩ w'o kana kĩeleelo kyaku ĩla ũũmũvoya Yeova ti o kũmanyĩsya syana syaku kĩndũ. Ĩndĩ ĩla wavoya wĩnyivĩtye syĩ vo, nimanyaa kũmwĩkwatya Yeova. Ana, kuma Brazil, aĩtye ũũ: "Ĩla mathĩna mesa kumĩla, ta kwa ngelekany'o ĩla sũsũ na ũmau mawaa, asyai makwa nĩmamũvoyaa Yeova amanenge vinya momĩanĩsye na ũndũ ũsu na aimanenga ũĩ wa kwĩka motwi maseo. O na ĩla kwaia vyũ nĩmamwĩkwatasya Yeova amatetheesye. Nũndũ wa ũu nĩneemanyĩisye kũmwĩkwatasya Yeova." Kwoou ĩla ũũvoya na syana syaku, ndũkeanĩawe nĩ kũivoyea. Voyaa Yeova nĩ kana o naku aũtetheesye. Kwa ngelekany'o, no ũmũkũlye aũnenge ũkũmbaũ wa kũneena na mũnene waku wĩanĩ nĩ kana ũkwate mwanya wa kũthi ũmbanonĩ mũnene, aũnenge ũkũmbaũ wa kũtavya mũtũi waku ũvoo mũseo, kana aũtetheesye maũndũnĩ angĩ. Wamwĩkwatya Ngai wĩnyivĩtye syana syaku ikeemanyĩsya kwĩka o taku.
9. (a) Nĩ nzĩa syĩva Yesũ watũmĩie kũmanyĩsya atũmwa make kũthũkũma ala angĩ menyivĩtye? (b) Syana syaku syĩmanyĩasya kyaũ syoona wĩyumĩtye kũthũkũma angĩ?
9 Yesũ nĩwamanyĩisye amanyĩw'a make ũndũ matonya kũthũkũma ala angĩ menyivĩtye. Amamanyĩisye ũu kwĩsĩla ndeto syake na meko make. (Soma Luka 22:27.) Amanyĩisye atũmwa make kana maaĩle kwĩyumya na ngoo yonthe ĩla meũmũthũkũma Yeova na meũtetheesya Aklĩsto ala angĩ. O naku weenyivya na weeyumya na ngoo yonthe, syana syaku no syĩmanyĩsye kĩu atũmwa meemanyĩisye. Debbie, ũla wĩ na syana ilĩ, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndyaaĩsa kwĩw'a kĩwĩu aĩ nũndũ mũemewa nĩwatũmĩaa ĩvinda na angĩ nĩ kana eanĩsye kĩanda kyake e mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi." O na easya, "Nĩneesĩ kana ĩla ithyĩ tũkamwenda ndakatwaĩa." (1 Tim. 3:4, 5) Nake mũũme wake, Pranas, ongelete kwasya atĩĩ: "Ĩtina syana sitũ nĩsyendie mũno kwĩyumya itetheesye maũndũ maũmbanonĩ manene na maũndũnĩ angĩ makonetye Ũsumbĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu nĩsyaendeeie nesa, syatuma ndũũ na Aklĩsto ala angĩ, na weethĩa syĩenda o kũtindany'a namo!" Ũmũnthĩ mũsyĩ ũsu w'onthe nĩwĩyumĩtye ũmũthũkũme Yeova kwa kũlika ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe. Woonany'a kana nĩwĩnyivĩtye na nĩwĩyumĩtye ũthũkũme angĩ, nĩ laisi syana syaku ikemanyĩsya kũthũkũma angĩ.
ĨTHĨWA NA ŨMANYI
10. Yesũ oonanisye ata kana aĩ na ũmanyi ĩla ĩkomano yamũatĩĩie?
10 Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana aĩ na ũmanyi nũndũ ndeanĩawa nĩ kĩla woona, ĩndĩ nĩwendaa kũmanya nĩkĩ andũ mekwĩka ũndũ mũna. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe aitavany'a Kalilii ve andũ mamwĩthukĩĩisye na mekala ta me na wendi wa kũmũatĩĩa. (Yoa. 6:22-24) Ĩndĩ nũndũ Yesũ aĩ atonya kũsoma ngoo syoo, nĩwamanyie kana andũ asu mendaa kũya mũno mbee wa kĩla wamanyĩasya. (Yoa. 2:25) Kwoou nĩwamanyie thĩna woo waĩ va, amalũnga auĩtye, na amaelesya ũndũ matonya kwĩka.—Soma Yoana 6:25-27.
11. (a) Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ kwĩthĩwa na ũmanyi kũtonya kũũtetheesya ũmanye ethĩwa mwana waku nũtanĩaa kũtavany'a. (b) Ũtonya kwĩka ata ũtetheesye mwana waku atanĩe mũno kũtavany'a?
11 O na kau ndũtonya kũsoma ngoo ya mwana waku, no wonany'e wĩ na ũmanyi kwa kũtata ũmanye ũndũ mwana waku wĩw'aa ĩũlũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Asyai aingĩ ĩla mathi kũtavany'a na syana syoo nĩmatilĩlaa ũtavany'a mavinda kwa mavinda nĩ kana syana syoo ithyũmũe na iiya kaĩndũ. Ĩndĩ ĩla weeka ũu ndũkeanĩawe nĩ kĩla wene na kwoou nũseo ũkekũlya-ĩ, 'Mwanawa ew'aa mũyo ĩla tũendeee na kũtavany'a kana nĩ ĩla twathyũmũa?' Wamanya kana syana syaku iyĩw'aa mũyo mũno ĩla iũtavany'a, nũseo mũkavanga ĩmwe nasyo kĩla itonya kwĩka. Iaĩe maũndũ mana syĩke ĩla ũũtavany'a nasyo nĩ kana syĩw'e no syeeka ũndũ.
12. (a) Yesũ atũmĩie ũmanyi ata nĩ kana atetheesye aatĩĩi make maikese kwĩlikya mwĩkalonĩ mũthũku? (b) Nĩkĩ ũtao ũla Yesũ wanengie amanyĩw'a make wamaĩle vyũ?
12 Ũndũ ũngĩ ũkwonany'a kana Yesũ aĩ na ũmanyi nĩ kana nĩwatavasya andũ kĩla kĩtonya kũmalikya naĩnĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, aatĩĩi make nĩmeesĩ kana kũlaalaa nĩ naĩ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩwamatavisye kĩla kĩtonya kũmalikya ũlaalainĩ. Ameie: "Kĩla mũndũ ũsyaasya mũndũ mũka na kũmwĩw'ĩa mũmeo nĩweka ũlaalai nake ngoonĩ yake. Na ethĩwa itho yaku ya ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwa aũme nĩyĩũkũlulutĩkya, yumye, ũyĩkye kũasa naku." (Mt. 5:27-29) Ũtao ũsu nĩwamaĩle vyũ Aklĩsto ala matwĩe nthĩ ila syasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Lomi. Nũndũ wa kĩ? Nũndũ mũsomi ũmwe wa maũndũ ma tene aisye kana ĩvindanĩ yĩu mũndũ athi kwĩloela mathaũ "itho yoonaa maũndũ mavuku na kũtũ kũkew'a maũndũ mathe, [na] mathaũ ala me kĩko ki nĩmo mauĩaw'a ngemi nĩ andũ aingĩ." Nĩ w'o vyũ kana Yesũ aĩ ũmanyi mwingĩ na nĩwendete mũno amanyĩw'a make nũndũ nĩwamatavisye maũndũ ala matonya kũtuma melikya mwĩkalĩlenĩ mũthũku.
13, 14. Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũsũvĩe syana syaku iikese kwĩtanĩthya na maũndũ mathũku?
13 Weethĩwa na ũmanyi no ũtetheesye syana syaku syĩsũvĩe iikeke ũndũ ũtonya kũmũthatya Yeova. Matukũ aa ti ta tene nũndũ o na syana nini no ikomane na mavisa ma ũlaalai kana syĩndũ ingĩ syĩ na maũndũ mavuku. Kũneena ũla w'o, Aklĩsto ala me na syana nĩmaitavasya kana kwĩtanĩthya na maũndũ mavuku nĩ kũthũku. Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa na ũmanyi no kũũtetheesye kũmanya nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩsa kũtuma mwana waku enda kũsisya mavisa ma ũlaalai. Ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũkusya mwanawa ende kũsisya mavisa ma ũlaalai? We mwanawa nĩwĩsĩ mavisa ma ũlaalai me mũisyo wĩva? Twĩ ndũũ ũkethĩa no oke kũngũlya ũtao esa kwĩw'a ta ũkwenda kũsisya mavisa asu?' O na ethĩwa mwana waku anyivĩte ata, no ũmũtavye atĩĩ: "Ũkesa kũkomana na kĩsese kĩ na maũndũ mathavu na ũyĩw'a ta ũkwenda kũsisya maũndũ asu, mwa wĩũka ũndavye. Ndũkaaĩw'e nthoni. Nĩenda ũkũtetheesya."
14 O na ĩngĩ kwĩthĩwa na ũmanyi kũkaũtetheeasya we mwene ũnyuvae nesa kĩla ũkwĩtanĩthya nakyo. Ũla mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Pranas awetete ũũ: "Syana syendeeaw'a mũno nĩ mbathi, sinema, kana mavuku ala asyai mendete. No ũtũe ũwetaa maũndũ maingĩ, ĩndĩ syana syaku ikasiasya o ũndũ ũkwĩka na iyĩka o taku." Syana syaku syoona ũinyuva nesa kĩla ũkwĩtanĩthya nakyo, no laisi ikenda kwĩka oou.—Alo. 2:21-24.
NGAI WA W'O AKAKWĨTHUKĨĨSYA
15, 16. (a) Nĩkĩ ndwĩ na nzika kana Ngai no aũtetheesye kũmanyĩsya syana syaku? (b) Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩeleetye ũndũ wĩva?
15 Kwaendie ata ĩla Manoa weesũvanie atetheew'e kũea mwanae? Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte ũũ: "Na Ngai eethukĩĩsya wasya wa Manoa." (Asi. 13:9) No ta ũu inyw'ĩ asyai, Yeova akamwĩthukĩĩasya. Akasũngĩaa mboya syenyu na aimũtetheesya kũmanyĩsya syana syenyu. Na no mũvote kũmanyĩsya syana syenyu kwa nzĩa ĩkwonany'a nĩmũsyendete, mwĩ na wĩnyivyo, na mwĩ na ũmanyi.
16 O ũndũ Yeova ũtetheeasya asyai nĩ kana mamanyĩsye nesa syana syoo ila nini, now'o ũtonya kũmatetheesya mamanyĩsye nesa syana ila ineananga. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩeleetye ũndũ we mũsyai ũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ala maũndũnĩ atatũ nĩ kana ũtetheesye syana ta isu imũthũkũme Yeova.
^ kal. 2 Ĩsomo yĩĩ yĩneeneete ũndũ asyai matonya kũtetheesya syana ila itavikĩtye myaka 12 imũthũkũme Yeova.
^ kal. 5 Ndeto ya kĩthyomo kya tene ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "kũkũna" ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu no ĩalyũlĩtwe kũndũ kũngĩ Mbivilianĩ ta "kũsilĩla," "kũtaa," "kũmanyĩsya," "kũkany'a," na "kwony'a mavĩtyo." Vai vandũ Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana mũndũ aĩle kwĩka maũndũ asu athatĩte ĩndĩ aĩle kũmeka kwa nzĩa ya wendo.

translation:
"And a man of God came to him [Timnah] and said to him something concerning his wife and what she had done."
MBATHI: 41, 6
1. Did Manoah ever ask whether his wife was barren?
MANOA and his wife prayed earnestly about having a child, and Jehovah heard their prayer. But because of this, Manoah began to worry about what his wife had done. He feared that Jehovah would punish her for doing so. The angel of Jehovah appeared to him again and said to him about his wife: "Be careful, do not do anything rashly regarding your wife. Do not be anxious about having a son." Then Manoah pleaded with Jehovah, and he reminded him about his wife's request for a son. Why did he do that? Because he knew that many people were troubled by being unable to have children, and he wanted to show compassion to anyone who might be experiencing similar difficulties. That is why Manoah "kept begging Jehovah," and he said: "Please, O man of God [angel], send him again to us, and let him tell us something concerning our wife and what she had done."—Judg. 13:1-8.
2. What can help you to comfort your child, and how can you do so? (Use the box "Comforting Your Child.")
2 Often, children feel better when they understand why Manoah prayed to God. Why? Because he showed them that it is important to talk to God about your worries and desires. * (Prov. 1:8) Christian parents strive to teach their children to pray to Jehovah and to love him. However, sometimes the Worldly Organization does not allow parents to teach their children to pray to Jehovah and to love him. Therefore, the Worldly Organization encourages parents to teach their children to imitate the example of Jesus. (Read Paragraphing Information 6:6-9.) How can you find ways to teach your child to pray to Jehovah? Lessons and experiences can help you to teach them what Christians can do to show faith like Jesus'. And just as Jesus spent time with children, Christian parents can also spend time teaching them. Jesus taught his followers by using illustrations, and he spoke kindly and with understanding. Let us learn from those examples.
TEACH YOUR CHILD
3. Did Jesus ever ask whether his followers loved him?
3 Jesus asked his followers whether they loved him or not. (Read John 15:9.) Also, he showed them whether he loved them or not, so that they would continue to love him. (Luke 6:31, 32; John 2:2; 21:12, 13) Jesus is someone who loves his followers. In fact, he loves them so much that he was willing to die for them. So how can you show faith like Jesus'?
4. Can you think of ways to teach your children to love Jehovah? (See the suggestions in paragraph 3.)
4 Children, obey your parents in everything, because this pleases Jehovah. (Eph. 4:3; Titus 2:4) A young man from Australia named Samuel said: "When I was a little boy, my father always took me to the Kingdom Hall every week. I enjoyed those visits, hugging him, sitting on his lap, and hearing him pray. I remember thinking how wonderful it was that Father wanted me to feel close to Jehovah! But sometimes he was busy, and I wondered why he didn't have time to hug me or sit with me. However, I realized that he was doing it for my good." Parents, when you are busy, try to spend some quality time with your children, even if it means saying 'No' to other things. Show your children that you love them. And be an example for them, so that they will want to imitate your faith.
5, 6. (a) Did Jesus ever ask anyone whether they loved him? (b) Explain how teaching a child to love Jehovah can help him to obey and appreciate what Jehovah does for him.
5 Jesus said: "If anyone loves me, he will observe my commandments." *(John 14:15) And just as Jesus showed his great love for us, we should show our love for Jehovah. It is important to teach our children about Jehovah's love for them, so that they will want to please him. We can also share experiences with them and tell them stories that illustrate Bible principles.—Mark 9:33-37.
6 But parents need to be patient. Some children take longer to respond than others. It is important not to give up on a child, even if he seems stubborn. (Prov. 22:15) Remember Jesus' example. Often, people were slow to accept his message, yet he continued to help them. So continue to reason with your child, encourage him, and praise his efforts. A sister named Elaine from South Africa says: "I used to get discouraged easily." She adds: "But I realized that I needed to be more positive. I began to focus on what my children were doing right, rather than on their mistakes. As a result, things improved. I became more optimistic. I appreciated what each one was trying to do, and I praised them for their efforts."
TRAINING AND DISCIPLINE
7, 8. (a) What did Jesus say about loving someone? (b) How can parents help their children to love God?
7 Jesus explained how much he loved his Father when he said: "Father, if you are willing, please let this cup pass from me. Nevertheless, let your will be done, not mine." (Matt. 14:36) This shows that he recognized that knowing God's will and submitting to it could be difficult. However, Jesus trusted that Jehovah would support him. He knew that Jehovah understood his feelings and would help him.
8 So why should you ask Jehovah to give you strength? It is because you love him and want to please him. If you pray for strength, it means that you trust in Jehovah. For example, a sister in Brazil said: "When I was very young, my parents were poor and did not have much education, but they taught me to love Jehovah and to value what we had. And even though they had little money, they always found ways to show their gratitude to Jehovah." She added: "I learned to trust in Jehovah." Think about how you feel when you pray for strength. Praying to Jehovah can comfort you. Remember, too, that Jehovah can help you to speak courageously to others. Perhaps you find it hard to talk to your parents, but you know that you need to discuss something important with them. Or perhaps someone has hurt your feelings, and you want to tell him how you feel. Trust in God and ask for strength to say what is on your heart.
9. (a) How did Jesus teach his disciples to preach to people who spoke different languages? (b) What can you learn from this example about preaching to people who are different from you?
9 Jesus taught his disciples how to preach to people who spoke different languages by using simple language and gestures. He did this by means of his spirit and his organization. (Read Luke 22:27.) He taught his disciples to be willing to humble themselves and to put Jehovah first and Christ second in everything they do. And just as he taught them, you too can teach others. Debbie, a sister with children, said: "I try to speak in a way that those I meet will understand, and I always try to show respect for their culture." She added: "I realize that sometimes we need to adjust our approach." (1 Tim. 3:4, 5) Her husband, Pranas, explained: "It is important that we are willing to humble ourselves and to learn about the customs and traditions of others so that we can effectively share the good news. By doing so, we can strengthen our relationship with Christ and avoid offending others!" The most important thing is to humble yourself and to preach to people regardless of their background. Remember that if you are willing and humble enough to preach to others, you can help them to learn about God.
UNDERSTANDING AND SKILL
10. Did Jesus ever use illustrations or examples to help people understand what he was teaching?
10 Jesus often used illustrations and examples to help people grasp spiritual truths, because he knew that people learn best when things are made clear to them. For example, on one occasion, he used the illustration of leaven to help his listeners understand how wickedness spreads. (John 6:22-24) Also, he could read people's thoughts, so he knew whether they were genuinely interested in learning. (John 2:25) However, he did not simply reveal what he knew; rather, he asked questions and encouraged them to think for themselves.—Read John 6:25-27.
11. (a) How can you apply what you have learned about understanding and skill to help someone who is struggling to accept the truth? (b) What can you do to improve your ability to help others appreciate the truth?
11 If you want to help someone understand God's Word, try to put yourself in their position and see things from their viewpoint. Many people find it difficult to accept the truth because they have been taught certain ideas since childhood, and those ideas may be deeply ingrained. Remember that each person is different, and what works for one may not work for another. Ask yourself, "What questions does this person have?" and "What objections might he raise?" If you know what concerns your listener has, you will be better able to address them. Don't be afraid to admit that you don't know something.
12. (a) Did Jesus always explain everything fully, or did he sometimes challenge his disciples to think for themselves? (b) Why did Jesus ask his followers questions?
12 One way Jesus showed wisdom was by asking questions that helped people reason and apply Bible principles. For example, he often used illustrations that required thinking. Jesus encouraged people to examine their own hearts. He said: "Anyone who looks at a woman with lustful desire has already committed adultery with her in his heart. . . . If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away." (Matt. 5:27-29) This principle helps Christians avoid getting involved in situations that could lead to temptation. A researcher once wrote about how some people can become so preoccupied with minor details that they miss the bigger picture, saying: "They get lost in the trees and fail to see the forest, [and] then wonder why they are unable to navigate." Isn't it clear that Jesus had great insight and that he skillfully used questions to help people reason through matters and apply Bible principles?
13, 14. How can you show wisdom when helping your children learn spiritual lessons?
13 The key is to encourage them to think critically and to relate what they are learning to real life. Young ones may be distracted by things that seem more appealing. To help them focus, try to connect spiritual lessons to their interests. Like Jesus did, encourage your children to examine their own hearts. Help them understand that it is better to stop doing something wrong than to continue and risk stumbling. For instance, ask: "What can you do to avoid being influenced by bad associations? What if your friend encourages you to do something wrong? How can you respond?" Even if your child does not fully grasp the lesson, reassure him and say: "It's okay to admit that you don't understand. Let's talk about it further."
14 Encourage critical thinking by asking questions that make them reason for themselves. One young man named Pranas said: "I used to hang out with friends who were disrespectful, rebellious, or involved in questionable activities. But I realized that associating with them would lead to trouble." Your children will benefit from reasoning on matters themselves.—Prov. 2:21-24.
GOD WILL HELP YOU
15, 16. (a) Why should we trust that God will help us to teach our children? (b) What important lesson does the example of Manoah teach us?
15 Consider how Manoah pleaded with God to bless his wife and son. The Bible says: "Jehovah listened to [Manoah] and answered his request." (Judg. 13:9) Yes, Jehovah heard his prayer and helped him. He sent an angel to give Manoah guidance. So when you pray for help in teaching your children, remember that God cares for you and wants to help you succeed.
16 What Jehovah can do for us is to provide opportunities to teach our children, but he expects us to take advantage of those opportunities. This is what the example of Manoah teaches us—we need to be proactive in helping our children learn to love Jehovah.
^kal. 2 This lesson shows that it is possible to help children become dedicated to Jehovah even if they are older than 12 years.
^kal. 5 The expression "discipline" as it is used in this publication is similar to the terms used in the Bible such as "correction," "training," "instruction," "admonishment," and "reproof." Many Bible scholars believe that a person benefits when he considers why he has made mistakes and learns from them through loving correction.

text:
Nĩ ĩndĩĩ andũ ma Ngai maĩ ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene?
Kavinda keana ũna ĩtina wa mwaka wa 100 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa nĩw'o andũ ma Ngai malikile ũkombonĩ ũsu, na mesie kuma vo mwakanĩ wa 1919. Nĩkĩ maelesyo asu me kĩvathũkany'o na ala ma tene?
Twĩ na itumi mbingĩ sya kũĩkĩĩthya kana ũkombo ũsu wathelile mwaka wa 1919, ĩla Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta mombanĩw'e ĩngĩ kĩkundinĩ. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wambĩĩa kũsumbĩka mwakanĩ wa 1914, andũ ma Ngai nĩmatatiwe na mathew'a kwa kavinda ka myaka mĩvũthũ. * (Mal. 3:1-4) Na ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1919, Yesũ nĩwanyuvie ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" nĩ kana ĩnengae andũ ma Ngai ala maĩ manathew'a "lĩu ĩvinda yaw'o." (Mt. 24:45-47) Mwaka ũsu nĩw'o andũ ma Ngai mambĩĩe kũsyoka vala Ngai wendaa mekale. Mwaka ũsu now'o maumie ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. (Ũvu. 18:4) Ĩndĩ ũkombo ũsu wambĩĩie ĩndĩĩ?
Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ twĩthĩĩtwe tũielesya kana ũkombo ũsu wambĩĩie mwaka wa 1918, na kana kau nĩ kala kavinda kakuvĩ andũ ma Ngai maĩ ungu wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/03/1992 yaisye: "O tondũ andũ ma Ngai tene matw'ĩkĩthĩtw'e ngombo nĩ Mbaviloni kwa ĩvinda, now'o athũkũmi ma Yeova malikilw'e ũkombonĩ nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene mwaka wa 1918." Ĩndĩ ũkunĩkĩli wĩonany'a kana ũkombo ũsu wambĩĩe tene vyũ mwaka wa 1918 ũte mũviku.
Kwa ngelekany'o, ekai tũsũanĩe ĩũlũ wa wathani ũmwe ũla wathanie ĩũlũ wa ũkombo ũsu vamwe na kũthaw'a kwa andũ ma Ngai. Wathani ũsu wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Esekieli 37:1-14. Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩwetete Esekieli e woninĩ ayonw'a mwanda wusũĩte mavĩndĩ. Yeova nĩwamũeleisye Esekieli kana mavĩndĩ asu nĩ "nyũmba yonthe ya Isilaeli." Nũndũ wathani ũsu nĩwaaĩle kwĩanĩa ĩvinda ya kelĩ, no ũkonetye "Isilaeli ma Ngai." (Aka. 6:16; Meko 3:21) Ĩtina wa ũu Esekieli nĩwoonie mavĩndĩ asu meethĩwa thayũ na matw'ĩka nguthu nene mũno ya kaũ. Ĩsu nĩ nzĩa nzeo ta kĩ ya kũelesya ũndũ andũ ma Ngai maumie ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene mwakanĩ wa 1919! Ĩndĩ woni ũsu wĩtũtetheesya ata kũmanya ĩvinda yĩla andũ ma Ngai makuie me ũkombonĩ?
Ũndũ wa mbee, mavĩndĩ asu mawetetwe ta maĩ "momũ" kana "momũ mũno." (Esek. 37:2, 11) Kĩu kĩonany'a kana mavĩndĩ asu maĩ ma andũ makw'ĩte tene mũno. Ũndũ wa kelĩ, ũthayũũkyo wa andũ asu ti ũndũ weekiwe mĩtũkĩ ĩndĩ weekiwe kavola kwa kavola. Ata? Mwambĩĩonĩ kwaĩ kĩlonzo, kĩtetemo kya nthĩ, na "mavĩndĩ mathengeeanĩa, ĩvĩndĩ na ĩvĩndĩ yayo." Na ĩndĩ mavĩndĩ asu nĩmeekĩiwe "malangũ . . . na nyama." Ĩtina wa vau, mavĩndĩ, malangũ, na nyama nĩsyavw'ĩkiwe kĩkonde. Kĩu kyathela 'veva nĩwamalikile, na meethĩwa thayũ.' Mũthya Yeova nĩwatũngie andũ asu mathayũũkiw'e nthĩ yoo. Nĩ kana maũndũ asu onthe mekĩke yaĩ no nginya vakue ĩvinda.—Esek. 37:7-10, 14.
Mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yekalile ũkombonĩ ĩvinda ĩasa. Ũkombo ũsu wambĩĩe mwaka wa 740 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, ĩla ũsumbĩ wa mbaĩ ĩkũmi wa Isilaeli wasindiwe na andũ aingĩ ma ũsumbĩ ũsu matavwa. Na ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 607 Klĩsto ate mũsyae ndũa ya Yelusaleme nĩyaanangiwe, na ala maĩ ũsumbĩnĩ ũla ũngĩ wa mbaĩ ilĩ matavwa. Ũkombo ũsu w'onthe wathelile mwaka wa 537 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, ĩla Ayuti amwe masyokie Yelusaleme na maaka yĩla ĩkalũ ĩngĩ na mambĩĩsya ũthaithi wa w'o ĩngĩ.
Wasũanĩa maũndũ asu me Maandĩkonĩ, nũkwona kana andũ ma Ngai mekalile me ngombo sya Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mũno, ĩndĩ ti o kuma mwaka wa 1918 nginya 1919. Ĩvinda yĩu maĩ ũkombonĩ noyo ĩvinda yĩla ĩthaaa yeanie vamwe na nganũ, kana "ana ma ũsumbĩ." (Mt. 13:36-43) Ĩvinda yĩu ĩthaaa yeanie vamwe na nganũ nĩ yĩla ĩvinda Aklĩsto ma w'o maĩ avũthũ vyũ kwĩ ala makaĩĩte mũĩkĩĩo. Kwoou no twasye ĩvinda yĩu kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto no ta kyaĩ ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. Ũkombo ũsu wambĩĩe kavinda keana ũna ĩtina wa mwaka wa 100 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, na waendeea nginya ĩla ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva yatheiw'e mĩthenyanĩ ĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo.—Meko 20:29, 30; 2 Ath. 2:3, 6; 1 Yoa. 2:18, 19.
Ĩvinda yĩu yĩasavĩte ũu andũ ma Ngai maĩ ũkombonĩ wa kĩ-veva, atongoi ma ndĩni vamwe na ala maĩ siasanĩ nĩmavatie andũ Ndeto ya Ngai maikĩa kwasya ũkũmũ ũla maĩ naw'o. Mavinda amwe yaĩ ĩvĩtyo kũsoma Mbivilia na kĩthyomo kĩla kĩsĩkĩe nĩ aingĩ. Andũ amwe meekie ũu nĩmooveeiwe ituĩnĩ na mavĩvw'a. Ala mesa kwĩthĩwa na woni wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na momanyĩsyo ma atongoi ma ndĩni mooseawa ĩtambya yũmũ mũno, na kyu nĩkyasiĩĩaa kyeni kya ũla w'o kĩikanyaĩĩke.
Nao nata ĩũlũ wa kuma ũkombonĩ? Kyu kyeekĩkie ĩndĩĩ na ata? Andũ ma Ngai maumie ũkombonĩ ũsu kavola kwa kavola. O tondũ wathani waisye, vambie kũka "kĩtetemo kya nthĩ." Kĩu kyambĩĩe vatiele myaka maana meana ũna ĩvinda ya mũminũkĩlyo yambĩĩe. Myakanĩ ĩsu ve andũ amwe aĩkĩĩku mokitĩie ũthaithi wa w'o ũndũ matonya, o na kau momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni sya ũvũngũ nĩmo maĩ maingĩ. Amwe nĩmatatie kũalyũla Mbivilia ithyomonĩ sya andũ ala mate asomu mũno. Namo angĩ nĩmatavanisye ũw'o ũla meemanyĩĩtye Ndetonĩ ya Ngai.
Na ĩndĩ mũthyanĩ wa myaka ya 1800, Charles Taze Russell na atindany'a make nĩmeekĩie kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana matume ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ ũmanyĩka ĩngĩ. No twasye ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o ala mavĩndĩ mambĩĩe kũvw'ĩkwa nyama na kĩkonde. Ĩkaseti ya Zion's Watch Tower vamwe na mavuku angĩ nĩsyatetheeisye ala maĩ na ngoo nthalĩku mamanye ũw'o. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, syĩndũ ta ĩla "Photo-Drama of Creation" ya 1914 na ĩvuku yeetawa The Finished Mystery ya 1917 nĩsyalũlũmĩilye andũ ma Ngai. Tũineena kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o no twasye mwakanĩ wa 1919 nĩw'o ĩndĩ andũ ma Ngai manengiwe thayũ na matwawa nthĩ yoo ene. O ũndũ ĩvinda yĩvĩtĩte ũtialo wa Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta nũkwatĩtwe mbau nĩ ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ, na onthe nĩmatw'ĩkĩte "nguthu nene mũno ya kaũ."—Esek. 37:10; Nzek. 8:20-23. *
Maũndũ asu onthe meonany'a kana andũ ma Ngai malikile ũkombonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene ĩla andũ ala makaĩie ũla mũĩkĩĩo mongelekile myakanĩ ya 100 na kĩndũ Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa. Ĩvinda yĩu ya kĩvindu yailyĩ ĩvinda yĩla Aisilaeli matavĩtwe. Twĩ na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno nũndũ o na kau athũkũmi ma Ngai mekalĩte myaka mingĩ mũno maithĩnw'a kĩ-veva, ithyĩ twĩkalĩte ĩvinda yĩla 'ala oĩ makatisa,' na ĩvinda yĩla "aingĩ makeethesya" na "kũtheethw'a"!—Nda. 12:3, 10.
Ĩla Satani wamũtataa Yesũ nĩwĩthĩwa amũtwaie ĩkalũnĩ?
Kwa ũkuvĩ, tũyĩsa kwasya vyũ kana Yesũ nĩwaendie kũũngama ĩkalũnĩ kana eekie kwona woni. Ve mavinda mavuku maitũ monanasya nĩwaendie nginya ĩkalũnĩ na mavinda angĩ mayonany'a eekie kwona woni.
Kwamba kũvindĩĩsya kĩla Mbivilia ĩwetete. Ĩla mũtũmwa Mathayo waandĩkaa yĩla ĩvuku yake ya Ũvoo Mũseo aveveewe aandĩka ũũ: 'Na ĩndĩ ndevili amũtwaa [Yesũ] nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ndũa ntheu; na amwĩkalya mũthyanĩ wa ĩkalũ [kana, vala vatũlu vyũ].' (Mt. 4:5) Naw'o ũvoo ũla ũngĩ ta ũsu wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Luka waĩtye ũũ: 'Na amũtwaa Yelusaleme, amwĩkalya mũthyanĩ wa ĩkalũ.'—Luka 4:9.
Navu ĩtinanga mavuku maitũ manawetaa kana no kwĩthĩwa Yesũ ataathi ĩkalũnĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩsũngũ) ya 01/03/1961 yaisye ũũ: "Ti ũndũ wosanĩte na kĩlĩko kwasya atĩ syĩndũ syonthe ila iwetetwe ngewanĩ ya kũtatwa kwa Yesũ e weũnĩ syaĩ syĩndũ syĩ vo. Kũneena ũla w'o vai kĩĩma o na kĩmwe mũndũ waĩ atonya kũũngama ĩũlũ nĩ kana onw'e 'mosumbĩ onthe ma nthĩ, na ndaĩa syamo.' Kwoou no twasye kana Satani ndaatwaa Yesũ nginya alika 'nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ndũa ntheu' na amwĩkalya 'mũthyanĩ wa ĩkalũ.' Ndyaĩ lasima Satani amũtate me vau ĩkalũnĩ." Ĩndĩ ve makaseti amwe maumie ĩtina wa yĩu ala moonanisye kana ta keka Yesũ nĩweetĩkĩlanile na Satani na ayĩyĩkya ethĩwa eekie kwĩyũaa.
Andũ amwe maisye kana nũndũ Yesũ ndaĩ wa nyũmba ya Livai, ndaaĩle kwambata kĩalanĩ kya vala vatheu ĩkalũnĩ. Na kwoou matw'a kana Yesũ no ta weekie 'kũtwawa' ĩkalũnĩ e woninĩ, o tondũ ĩvinda ĩvĩtu mwathani Esekieli watwaiwe ĩkalũnĩ e woninĩ.—Esek. 8:3, 7-10; 11:1, 24; 37:1, 2.
Ĩndĩ ethĩwa Satani aimũtata Yesũ eekie kũmwony'a woni, kwasũanĩa makũlyo aa:
Ethĩwa waĩ woni, Yesũ aĩ atonya kwĩw'a ta watatwa eyĩkye?
Ethĩwa mavinda ala angĩ Satani wamũtatie Yesũ endaa eke ũndũ ta kũvĩndũa mavia matw'ĩke imũtũ kana kũmũtulĩlya ndu amũthaithe, tyo twasye kana o na ĩtatwanĩ yĩĩ Satani amũtwaie Yesũ ĩkalũnĩ nũndũ nĩweesĩ e vau no eyĩkye?
Ĩndĩ ethĩwa Yesũ nĩwaendie kũũngama mũthyanĩ wa ĩkalũ, kwasyoka ũsũanĩe makũlyo aa:
Ethĩwa Yesũ nĩwaendie kũũngama ĩũlũ wa vala vandũ vatheu, ndethĩwa atũlile ĩla Mĩao ya Mose?
Yesũ aumie weũnĩ ata esa kũvika Yelusaleme?
Ũkunĩkĩli mwingangĩ ũla twĩkĩte nũtũtetheesye kũkwata ũvoo ũtonya kũtũtetheesya kũsũngĩa makũlyo asu elĩ ma mũthya.
Mbee, Professor D. A. Carson awetete kana ndeto ya Kĩkiliki hi·e·ron', ĩla nĩyo ĩalyũlĩtwe "ĩkalũ" ngewanĩ ĩsu ya Yesũ yĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo na ya Luka, "no kwĩthĩwa yonanasya ũ mwako w'onthe ĩndĩ ti vala vandũ vatheu ve voka." Kwoou ti lasima Yesũ ethĩwe aendie kũũngama ĩũlũ wa vala vandũ vatheu. Kwa ngelekany'o, no kwĩthĩwa aendie kũũngamĩla kĩalanĩ kyaĩ ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya ĩkalũ welekele wumĩlonĩ wa syũa. Keka ve mũndũ weeyĩkĩasya vau atheea vuti ta 450 (mita 137) nginya nthĩ Ũsĩnĩ wa Kitiloni. Kĩala kĩu kyaĩ kĩtindimalu na kyaakĩĩwe ũkũta mũkuvĩ wĩlingĩlĩte ndeenĩ syakyo. Vau kĩalanĩ kĩu nĩvo vaĩ na vuti ila mbingĩ vyũ kũthi nthĩ. Mũsomi ũmwe wa tene weetawa Josephus aisye kana mũndũ ũũngama kĩalanĩ kĩu na aisisya nthĩ "akwatwa nĩ nthyũũa" nũndũ vaĩ vaasa. Nũndũ Yesũ ndaĩ wa nyũmba ya Livai, aĩ mwĩtĩkĩlye kũũngamĩla kĩalanĩ kĩu na ndaĩ esa kũtuma andũ malua nduuthĩ.
Ĩndĩ ethĩwa Yesũ aĩ weũnĩ-ĩ, vatonyeka ata akethĩwa atwaiwe nginya ĩkalũnĩ? Kwa ũkuvĩ ũsũngĩo nĩ kana tũyĩsĩ nesa. Ũvoo ũla ũeleetye matatwa ala Yesũ wakomanie namo ĩvinda yĩu nĩ mũkuvĩ, na kwoou ndũwetete atatiwe kwa ĩvinda yĩana ata kana aĩ ngalĩko yĩva ya weũ ũsu. Ĩndĩ o na kau kũthi Yelusaleme na maaũ umĩte weũnĩ ũsu kwaĩ kũtonya kũkua masaa maingĩ, tũitonya kwasya vyũ kana Yesũ ndaaĩka ũu. O na ĩngĩ ũvoo ũsu ndũwetete kana ĩvinda yĩu yonthe Yesũ aitatwa aĩ weũnĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩla ũvoo ũsu ũwetete nĩ kana Yesũ nĩwatwaiwe Yelusaleme.
Ĩndĩ nata ĩla Satani wamũtatie na "mosumbĩ onthe ma nthĩ"? Vate nzika, Satani oonisye Yesũ mosumbĩ asu woninĩ, kĩtumi nũndũ vai kĩĩma ũlĩsa ũkethĩa wĩ mũthya no wone mosumbĩ onthe. No kwĩthĩwa Satani atũmĩie mũthemba mũna wa woni, o tondũ ũtonya kwony'a mũndũ sinema ya mavisa ma kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ o na kau no kwĩthĩwa Satani amwonisye mosumbĩ asu woninĩ, kĩla wendaa nĩ Yesũ eke kĩko kĩkwonany'a 'nĩwamũthaitha.' (Mt. 4:8, 9) O ta ũu no twasye kana ĩla Satani watatie Yesũ eyĩkye kuma mũthyanĩ wa ĩkalũ endaa Yesũ eke kĩko kĩu kya kwĩyĩkya. Na keka nĩweeyĩkisye, thayũ wake wĩthĩwa waĩ mũisyonĩ. We ndũkwona ũndũ kĩko kĩu kyesaa kũtuma ĩtatwa yĩu yĩthĩwa na ũito kwĩ ta keka waĩ o woni?
Ũndũ ũmwe twaĩle kũweta nĩ ũla ũwetetwe mwambĩĩonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ: tũitonya kũelesya ngewa ĩno ũndũ ũmwe na tũilũma vau. Na kwoou tũitonya kwasya kana vaitonyeka Yesũ akethĩwa aendie Yelusaleme na aũngama mũthyanĩ wa ĩkalũ. Ĩndĩ kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana Ndevili atatie Yesũ eke maũndũ mathũku, na kĩla ĩvinda wamũtata Yesũ amũsũngĩaa ate na nzika o na vanini.
^ kal. 2 Sisya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/07/2013, ĩth. 16-18, kal. 5-8, 12.

Wathani ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Esekieli wathanĩte ũndũ andũ onthe ma Ngai maĩ mambĩĩe kũmũthaitha Yeova ĩngĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩasa mũno ya ũkombo. Ĩndĩ wathani ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo wonanĩtye kũnyuvwa kwa kĩkundi kĩnini kya ana-a-asa etĩkĩw'a mauta kĩtongosye ĩtina wa kavinda kanini ka kũsiĩĩwa.
