translation:
Are you among those of God who were in the fall of Babylon the Great?
Since the year 100 C.E., faithful Christians have been aware of this, and they have kept on watching, until 1919. Does this information seem strange to you?
We have many reasons to believe that the end came in 1919, but Christ was already ruling invisibly in heaven from an earlier time. Consider this: God's temple began being purified in 1914, and his people were afflicted by trials for many years. * (Mal. 3:1-4) And in 1919, Jesus rejoiced that the "faithful and discreet slave" was continuing to provide them with spiritual food "at the right time." (Matt. 24:45-47) That year marked a turning point for God's people, as they began to separate themselves from false religion. That year saw the beginning of the exposure of Babylon the Great. (Rev. 18:4) What does this end mean to you?
For many years we wondered whether the end would come in 1918, and whether that year would mark the beginning of the destruction of Babylon the Great. For example, the March 15, 1992, Swahili Kingdom News reported: "Because God's people knew that Babylon was falling, Jehovah's witnesses recognized the beginning of the destruction of Babylon the Great in 1918." How can you reconcile what you know with the fact that the end did not actually begin in 1918?
For instance, let us examine the illustration of the dry bones, which illustrates the restoration of God's people. That illustration is based on Ezekiel 37:1-14. In that vision, Ezekiel saw a valley filled with very dry bones. Jehovah caused Ezekiel to understand that those bones represented "the entire house of Israel." So the illustration helps us to understand the meaning of the expression "Israel of God." (Acts 6:16; Galatians 3:21) The point of Ezekiel's vision is that those dry bones will be brought back to life. We want to help God's people to remember the destruction of Babylon the Great in 1919! Do you wonder why God's people were so eager to see the fulfillment of this prophecy?
In effect, the bones mentioned were called "bones" or "very dry bones." (Ezekiel 37:2, 11) This indicates that they were human bones. To illustrate, the condition of the people was not something that could be repaired little by little. Was it not remarkable that Ezekiel described them as "many bones, exceedingly many"? And he said that there were "tendons . . . and flesh" upon the bones. Apparently, the bones, tendons, and flesh were arranged in their proper order. This showed 'that He is able to make alive, and bring back to life.' It is because Jehovah gives his people strength that they can recover. It is as though everything was put together again and then breath entered into them.—Ezekiel 37:7-10, 14.
The nation of Israel experienced exile for a long period of time. That exile began in 740 B.C.E. and lasted until the end of the tenth exile of Israel was completed by many nations. Also, from 607 B.C.E. onward, the city of Jerusalem was devastated, and the land experienced another long exile. That exile ended in 537 B.C.E., when some Jews returned to Jerusalem and rebuilt the wall, along with many other things, and restored worship.
Considering matters relating to the Scriptures, we see that God's people experienced captivity at the hand of Great Babylon for a long period of time, starting about the year 1918 C.E. and continuing into 1919. This recent period of exile is like a seed sown among weeds, or "sons of the kingdom." (Matt. 13:36-43) This seed sown among weeds is like Christ's brothers who are faithful ones. So we have seen this seed, a group of Christians, being separated from the spiritual wilderness of Great Babylon. That exile began shortly after the turn of the first century C.E., and it continues on until the large crowd of other sheep are gathered together.—Acts 20:29, 30; 2 Thess. 2:3, 6; 1 John 2:18, 19.
This has helped those of God's people who were in the spiritual wilderness to distinguish themselves from others who claim to be Jehovah's people but who are led astray. Some of them found it difficult to study the Bible and to give an honest witness. Others became discouraged because of opposition and false accusations made by opposers, and so they lost their zeal for the truth.
But what about the duration of the exile? Why did it continue for so long? God's people experience this exile little by little. But since you are awake, speak out "the secret thing." It means years of hardship and the exile of the loyal ones. These years have seen some individuals become hardened in their hearts toward this matter, or they have been influenced by the wrong teachings of opposers. Others have stopped studying the Bible and giving a witness to others. Yet still others have remained steadfast in their loyalty to Jehovah.
And during the 19th century, Charles Taze Russell and his associates began to shed light on this time of the end and to show how it was connected with Bible prophecy. So we see that this work is also among the many ways in which God is separating people like sheep and goats. The Watch Tower Society and its related publications have helped many to understand this matter. Such presentations as the "Photo-Drama of Creation" in 1914 and the book entitled The Finished Mystery in 1917 enlightened God's people. We recall that in 1919, many of God's people recovered their spiritual strength and zeal for service. And the fact that the remnant completed the work assigned to Christ of gathering His elect proved to be a powerful testimony, and it resulted in many becoming "one flock," a united people.—Ezek. 37:10; Zech. 8:20-23.
*
However, many others did not heed God's warning about Babylon the Great and continued to support her until she came to her ruin after 100 years, and Christ intervened to save His people. This history of unfaithfulness parallels that of ancient Israel. We too can benefit from remembering how God's faithful servants of old persevered through many trials, so that we might remain in the "last days," and in the time when "wickedness abounds" and people are "hardened"!—Matt. 12:3, 10.
How did Satan tempt Jesus to try to gain power?
Therefore, let us examine what happened when Jesus was tempted to seek glory and honor. Various accounts tell us that he was led to a high place and shown all the kingdoms of the world, and other accounts say that he was given a vision of future glory.
To understand this fully, we need to look closely at the Bible account. The apostle Matthew wrote that during his temptation, Jesus was taken "[to] a very high mountain; and the Devil brought him all the kingdoms of the world." (Matt. 4:5) Luke's account also says: "And he brought him up to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple."—Luke 4:9.*
However, some accounts make it appear as though Jesus saw the entire earth. For example, *The Watchtower* (Kenya) of March 1, 1961, stated: "It wasn't a vision of the whole earth, but a demonstration to show what would happen when Jesus exercised authority over all the earth. To put it another way, it was like someone saying, 'All these things I will give you if you prostrate yourself before me, and I will make them yours.' So we see that Satan took Jesus and showed him 'all the kingdoms of the world,' and set him 'on the pinnacle of the temple.' This demonstrated Satan's claim that he had power over all the kingdoms." There have been other publications that suggest that Jesus actually visualized himself ruling with Satan and that this was a test of his loyalty.
Some have suggested that Jesus was in Levi's house, looking at a panoramic view of all the kingdoms. And they reason that Jesus could not have been literally 'taken' to all the kingdoms, but that the vision resembled what Ezekiel saw when he was transported to various places.—Ezek. 8:3, 7-10; 11:1, 24; 37:1, 2.
So, the question arises: Did Satan really take Jesus to see all the kingdoms, or did he merely present a vivid illusion? The following questions may help us to understand this:
What purpose would it serve for Jesus to be able to see everything?
How does this account compare with others where Satan tempts Jesus to do something wrong, such as to perform a miracle to prove his identity, or to worship him, so that Satan can demonstrate his control over Jesus?
Why did Jesus need to visualize ruling over all the kingdoms, and how does this relate to the Mosaic Law?
Did Jesus actually go to Jerusalem during this time?
Let us examine further the points raised in order to determine whether we can arrive at a satisfactory understanding of this matter.
Moreover, Professor D.A. Carson notes that the Greek term hieron' refers to "the temple," which is used in both Matthew's and Luke's accounts of Jesus' temptation, "and to say that he was standing on the parapet overlooking the court of the Gentiles." This suggests that Jesus was shown a vision of ruling over all the kingdoms from the Temple mount. However, the distance from the top of the Temple mount to the Kidron Valley was approximately 450 feet (137 meters), making it difficult to see all the kingdoms. The view from that location was limited and obscured by hills. The historian Josephus also mentions someone who stood on the Temple mount and looked down, describing them as being "seized by dizziness." Therefore, Jesus, being a descendant of Levi, could have visualized ruling over all the kingdoms without physically going there to show people around.
Concerning whether Jesus was willing, they questioned even his willingness to be tempted. For this reason, it is important to remember that Jesus submitted himself to temptation, and it is noted that he was tested in every way, just as we are. Concerning his journey to Jerusalem and spending much time teaching, we can only speculate about what Jesus thought. And further, this reason is noted that all the temptations Jesus faced were internal. Regarding every reason, it is stated that Jesus was led to Jerusalem.
Regarding how Satan asked him, "All these kingdoms I will give you?" He replied, Satan deceived Jesus by showing him all the kingdoms, because there is always a price for true worship. But concerning Satan using false hope, it is important to realize that one should not trust anyone who offers something without considering its source. Concerning how Satan showed him all the kingdoms, each time it is said that Jesus firmly responded, 'It is Jehovah you must worship.' (Matt. 4:8, 9) And so we see that Satan tempted Jesus by appealing to his desire for power, and then he offered him a way to achieve it. And let us reflect, why would someone offer something for nothing unless they wanted to control you? We understand that such an offer could lead to our spiritual ruin and ultimately cause us to fail.
One thing we learn is what was pointed out in the recent public talk: we can appreciate this matter more fully when we remember past experiences. And so we can ask whether they truly love Jesus enough to allow him to go to Jerusalem and finish his work. Regarding how we feel, Satan tempts Jesus with difficult things, and each time he tries to make Jesus compromise, yet he remains steadfast.

That understanding of Ezekiel helped people to worship Jehovah properly during the final part of the harvest work. And that understanding of Revelation helped to appreciate the great crowd of other sheep being cleansed and sanctified.

text:
"Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe; ũla ũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe."—2 AKO. 1:3, 4.
MBATHI: 38, 6
1, 2. Yeova atũkiakiasya ata mathĩnanĩ maitũ, na Ndeto yake ĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye ata?
MŨTHENYA ũmwe, mwanake tũũmũtw'ĩĩa ĩsyĩtwa Eduardo nĩwaneenie na mũtumĩa ũmwe ũtwaanĩte wĩtawa Stephen ĩũlũ wa kathĩna waĩ nako. Kathĩna kake kakonetye ndeto ii wasomete ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 7:28: "Ala [matwaana] maitĩa kwĩthĩwa na mathĩna mwĩĩnĩ." Akũlilye Stephen atĩĩ: "'Mathĩna' asu nĩ meva, na ngeeka ata mangwata ĩla nĩtwaana?" Stephen atanamba kũmũnenga ũsũngĩo amũkũlilye ambe kũsũanĩa ũndũ ũmwe mũtũmwa Vaulo waandĩkie. Vaulo aandĩkie kana Yeova nĩwe "Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe; ũla ũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe."—2 Ako. 1:3, 4.
2 Yeova nĩ Asa witũ ũtwendete, na nĩwe ũtũkiakiasya ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ. No kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kũlilikana mavinda Ngai waũtw'ĩĩkie na aũtongoesya atũmĩĩte Ndeto yake. Tũi na nzika atwendeaa ũseo o tondũ wĩthĩĩtwe ayĩka kuma tene.—Soma Yelemia 29:11, 12.
3. Twĩmantha ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo meva?
3 Nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kana ethĩwa mũndũ nĩwĩsĩ mathĩna make maumanĩte na kyaũ, ethĩawa e na vinya mwingangĩ wa kũmĩanĩsya namo. Ũu now'o vethĩawa vailyĩ ethĩwa mũsyĩ wĩ na mathĩna, kana ala matwaanĩte me na mathĩna. Kwoou-ĩ, nĩ maũndũ ta meva matonya kũtuma ala matwaanĩte methĩwa na "mathĩna mwĩĩnĩ"? Nĩ andũ meva mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ na ma ĩvinda yĩĩ tũĩ matonya kũtũtetheesya tũkwate ũkiakisyo ũla twĩ na vata naw'o? Kũsũanĩa ngewa yoo no kũtũnenge wũmĩĩsyo.
"MATHĨNA MWĨĨNĨ"
4, 5. Nĩ maũndũ ta meva maetae "mathĩna mwĩĩnĩ"?
4 Vaaya mwambĩĩonĩ Ngai aisye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ mũũme akatia ĩthe na nyinyia, na akalũman'ya na mũka wake: nao makeethĩwa mwĩĩ ũmwe." (Mwa. 2:24) Yeova awetie ndeto isu ĩla wanengie Atamu mũka wake, Eva. Ĩndĩ nũndũ twĩ ene naĩ, kũtwaana na kwĩka mũsyĩ nĩkwĩthĩawa kũtonya kumĩlya mathĩna mũsyĩ. (Alo. 3:23) Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ mũka atanatwawa ethĩawa e ungu wa ũkũmũ wa asyai, ĩndĩ atwawa ethĩawa mũno mũno ungu wa ũkũmũ wa mũũme. Ngai anengete mũndũũme kĩanda kya kwĩthĩwa e mũtwe wa mũka. (1 Ako. 11:3) Ũsu ti ũndũ mũnini kwa ala matwaanie o mĩtũkĩ. Kwosana na Ndeto ya Ngai, kĩveti kyaĩle kũmanya kana mũũme nĩwe waĩle kũkĩtavya ũndũ kĩkwĩka ĩndĩ ti asyai makyo. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ nĩ kana, ndũũ katĩ wa ala matwaanie na athoni, kana andũ ma mũsyĩ wa mũũme, no ĩlike thĩna na yĩu no yĩthĩwe yĩ ĩtatwa kwa asu matwaanie.
5 Thĩna ũngĩ ũlikaa ĩla kĩveti kyeea mũũme, "Nĩwĩsĩ nĩ mũito?" O na kau no matane nũndũ yu nĩmamanya nĩmeteele mwana, mailea kũthĩnĩka masũanĩa mathĩna ala matonya kũlika kĩveti kĩkaambĩĩa kũthĩnw'a nĩ ĩvu yĩu, kana ala matonya kũka mwana aminĩte kũsyawa. O na ĩngĩ, ngalama yĩthĩawa yongeleka kuma vu na kũendeea. Na eka ũu, mwana asyawa no nginya meke moalyũku. Kwa ngelekany'o, kĩveti nĩkĩtonya kũtũmĩa masaa ala maingĩ kĩisiany'a na mwana. Nũndũ wa ũu, aũme aingĩ monaa ta maeka kwendwa moona kĩveti kĩkwatene na mwana mũno kũte mo. Twathi ngalĩko ya mũndũũme, wĩthĩaa yu e na wĩa mũitango wa kwĩanĩsya. Wĩa wake wingĩvaa nũndũ ethĩawa akwata mwana waĩlĩte kũewa na kũsũvĩwa.
6-8. Ala matwaanĩte matonya kwĩw'a ata mesa kwĩthĩa maitonya kũkwata syana?
6 Ve thĩna ũngĩ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o ũlikaa mĩtwaanonĩ ĩmwe. Amwe nĩmendaa mũno kũkwata syana ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa nĩvaemelile. Kĩveti kĩthĩnĩkaa mũno kyoona kĩtekũitava. Kũtwawa kana kũtwaana na kũsyaa syana ti w'o mũthya wa mathĩna, ĩndĩ kwenda mũno kwĩthĩwa na mwana na ũyĩthĩa vaitonyeka nĩ ũndũ ũmwe ũtonya kũtalwa ta "mathĩna mwĩĩnĩ." (Nth. 13:12) Ĩvindanĩ ya tene kĩveti kyeew'aa nthoni mbingĩ mũno kyamanya nĩ ngũngũ. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mũka wa Yakovo weetawa Lakeli. Kĩveti kĩu kyeew'aa thĩna mwingĩ mũno kyoona mwĩĩtu-a-inyia e na syana. (Mwa. 30:1, 2) Ũmũnthĩ amisonalĩ ala matũmĩtwe nthĩ ila andũ methĩawa na mĩsyĩ mĩnene makothaa kũkũlw'a nĩkĩ mate na syana. O na kau no matate kũelesya angĩ nesa nĩkĩ mate na syana, ti vinya kwĩw'a mayĩwa, "Mũikamake nĩtũũmũvoyea!"
7 O na kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wa nthĩ ya England waĩ na mea maingĩ ma kũkwata mwana. Ĩndĩ wendi ũsu ndwaaĩsa kwĩanĩw'a nũndũ ekalile nginya avikya ĩla myaka mũndũ mũka ũtesa kũsyaa. Aasya kana myaka ĩsu yavika, eewie akw'a ngoo vyũ nũndũ amanyie vau wavika ndakesa kũsyaa ate o e nthĩ nzaũ. Kwoou e na mũũme nĩmatwie kwosa mwana kũla kũnenganawe syana. Ĩndĩ o na mekĩte ũu easya: "Kĩu kĩyaambetea kyeva. Nĩneesĩ kana mwana wa kũnengwa ti ũndũ ũmwe na mwana nĩsyaĩe."
8 Mbivilia nĩwetete kana mũndũ mũka Mũklĩsto "akatangĩĩwa" nũndũ wa 'kũsyaa syana.' (1 Tim. 2:15) Ĩla ĩkwasya kũtangĩĩwa, ndĩkwasya kana kũsyaa syana kana kũea no kũtetheesye mũndũ ekwata thayũ ũtathela. Yĩweta kana ĩla mũndũ mũka wĩ na syana sya kũea, vamwe na mawĩa angĩ ma vau mũsyĩ, kĩu no kĩmũtetheesye ndakese ũkwatwa nĩ mũtuo wa kũsukana kana kwĩlikya maũndũnĩ meene. (1 Tim. 5:13) Ĩndĩ o na e na syana isu, no akwatwe nĩ mathĩna ala methĩawa mĩtwaanonĩ na mĩsyĩ.
9. Nĩkĩ kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũndũ ũtwaanĩte nake nĩ ĩtatwa ya mwanya?
9 Mavinda maingĩ ĩla tũũweta mathĩna ala maumĩlaa mũtwaanonĩ, ve thĩna ũmwe ũtokaa kĩlĩkonĩ mĩtũkĩ. Thĩna ũsu nĩ kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake. Vate nzika, yĩu nĩ ĩtatwa yĩmwe ya mwanya yĩkwatĩte andũ aingĩ. Twĩasya ũu nũndũ ũla watiwa nũtonya kwĩthĩwa o na ataasũanĩa kana akakw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũũme kana mũka nthĩ nzaũ ĩte mbiku. Ithyĩ Aklĩsto tũyĩthĩawa na nzika kana kũkeethĩwa na ũthayũũkyo o tondũ Yesũ wathanie. (Yoa. 5:28, 29) Wĩkwatyo ũsu ũtethasya ata ũla watiwa? Ũmũkiakiasya mũno. Ĩsu nĩ nzĩa ĩngĩ Asa witũ wĩ wendo ũtũmĩaa kwĩsĩla Ndeto yake nĩ kana atw'ĩĩke na aikiakisya ala me thĩnanĩ ta ũsu. Ekai yu tũneenee ngewa sya athũkũmi amwe ma Ngai twone ũndũ meewie amakiakisya, na ũndũ matethekie.
ŨKIAKISYO ĨVINDANĨ YA THĨNA
10. Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Aana thĩnanĩ wake? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 4.)
10 Aana nĩwakwatĩtwe nĩ thĩna ũmwe mũnene o na kau nĩwendetwe mũno nĩ mũũme, Elikana. Aana aĩ ngũngũ, ĩndĩ mwĩue, Venina, aĩ na syana. (Soma 1 Samueli 1:4-7.) "Kĩla mwaka" Aana nĩwavũthaw'a nĩ Venina. Ũndũ ũsu watumaa Aana athĩnĩka mũno na kwĩw'a woo. Ĩndĩ kĩla kyamũtethisye nĩ kũtavya Yeova thĩna wake. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "nĩwaendeeie kũvoya Mwĩai Ngai vandũ va ĩvinda ĩasa." We nĩweesilasya Yeova ta ũtonya kũmũnenga kĩla wendaa? Ndalea kwĩthĩwa aĩ na wĩkwatyo ũsu. Ĩndĩ o na kwĩthĩwe kwailyĩ ata, kĩveti kĩu kyamina kũvoya, "ũthyũ wakyo ndwaatuka ĩngĩ." (1 Sam. 1:12, 17, 18; The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Nĩweesĩ kana Yeova akamũtetheesya akwate mwana, kana ethĩwa ti ũu amũtw'ĩĩke na nzĩa ĩngĩ.
11. Mboya ĩtonya kũtũkiakisya ata?
11 Tũtesie kũvetewa naĩ na nthĩ ĩno ĩtongoew'e nĩ Satani ĩtesie kũvetwa, twĩendeea kũkomana na matatwa na mathĩna. (1 Yoa. 5:19) Ĩndĩ kũmanya kana Yeova nĩ "Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe" nĩkũtwĩkĩaa vinya. Kũvoya nĩ ũndũ ũmwe ũtũtetheeasya kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna ala twĩ namo. Aana nĩwamũtulũĩle Yeova ngoo yake. O ta ũu, ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ, ve ũndũ ũngĩ twaĩle kwĩka eka o kũmũwetea Yeova ũndũ tũkwĩw'a. Twaĩle kũmwĩsũva, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kũmũvoya na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo kingĩ tũimũelesya ũndũ tũkwĩw'a ngoonĩ.—Avi. 4:6, 7.
12. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Ana akwata ũtanu?
12 O na ethĩwa twĩ na kyeva kingĩ nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa tũtatonya kũkwata mwana, kana nũndũ wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũndũ tũtwaanĩte nake, no tũkwate ũkiakisyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvindanĩ ya Yesũ kwaĩ mwathani mũndũ mũka weetawa Ana wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũũme ĩtina wa kwĩkalany'a nake o kwa kavinda ka myaka mũonza. Mbivilia ndĩwetete kana aĩ na syana. Ĩndĩ nĩwetete kĩla Ana weekaa o na e na myaka 84. Ĩandĩko ya Luka 2:37 yaĩtye: "O na ndaumaa ĩkalũnĩ, akĩthaitha na kũtĩĩa kũya na kwĩsũvana ũtukũ na mũthenya." Ndeto isu sionany'a nesa vyũ kana kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩkwanengie Ana ũkiakisyo na ũtanu.
13. Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ anyanya ma w'o matonya kũkiakisya mũndũ andũ ma mũsyĩ maema kwĩka ũu.
13 No tũkwate atindany'a aseo na ma w'o katĩ wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ. (Nth. 18:24) Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Paula nũlilikanaa ũndũ weemakĩĩte ĩla inyia watiie ũw'o. Ĩvinda yĩu aĩ o na myaka ĩtano. Kũkĩlya vinya ĩtatwa yĩu kũyaĩ laisi. Ĩndĩ aendeangĩe nĩweekĩiwe vinya mũno nĩ vainia wĩtawa Ann meethĩawa kĩkundinĩ kĩmwe, ũla weeyumisye amũtetheesye aendeee nesa kĩ-veva. Paula easya: "O na kau ndyaileny'e ũndũ na Ann, nĩwandethisye mũno." Aendeee kwasya: "Ũseo ũsu wambĩkie nĩwandetheeisye nĩendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova." Kũvika ũmũnthĩ ũũ, Paula nĩ mũĩkĩĩku. O na nũtanaa nũndũ inyia wake nĩwasyokie kĩkundinĩ na yu me ĩmwe maimũthũkũma Yeova. O nake Ann e na ũtanu nũndũ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ta inyia wa Paula aimũtetheesya ekale e mũĩkĩĩku.
14. Ala mathĩnĩkĩaa angĩ makwataa moathimo meva?
14 Ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana ĩla twoony'a ala angĩ kana nĩtũũmathĩnĩkĩa, nĩtũekaa kũsũanĩa mũno mathĩna amwe twĩ namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, eĩtu-a-asa atwae na ala mate atwae nĩmesĩ nesa vyũ kana kũtavany'a nĩkũmaeteae ũtanu mwingĩ mũno nũndũ ĩla meĩka ũu methĩawa atethya ma wĩa vamwe na Ngai. Kĩeleelo kyoo kĩthĩawa kĩ kũmũtaĩa Ngai kwa kwĩka kwenda kwake. O na angĩ monaa ũtavany'a ta ndawa. Vate nzika, ithyonthe nĩtũtumaa kĩkundi kĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ĩla twathĩnĩkĩa angĩ kĩsionĩ kĩla tũtavanasya na ĩla twathĩnĩkĩa ala me kĩkundinĩ. (Avi. 2:4) Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwatwiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo ũndũnĩ ũsu. Athĩnĩkĩie Aklĩsto ala maĩ Thesalonika o tondũ "mũei," kana inyia wa syana, ũsũvĩaa syana syake. O na nĩwamathĩnĩkĩie o tondũ ĩthe wa syana ũthĩnĩkĩaa syana syake.—Soma 1 Athesalonika 2:7, 11, 12.
KŨKIAKISYA ANDŨ MA MŨSYĨ
15. Kĩanda kya kũmanyĩsya syana kĩnengetwe aaũ?
15 Ũndũ ũmwe waĩle kũsũanĩwa nĩ ũndũ mĩsyĩ yaĩle kũkiakiw'a na kũtetheew'a. Ve mavinda ala eũ kĩkundinĩ matonya kũkũlya Aklĩsto aima kĩ-veva mamatetheesye mamanye ũndũ matonya kũmanyĩsya syana syoo ũw'o, kana o makamakũlya maimanyĩsye Mbivilia nemo. Kwosana na Maandĩko, kĩanda kya kũmanyĩsya syana kĩnengetwe mũsyai. (Nth. 23:22; Aev. 6:1-4) Ĩndĩ mavinda amwe, wĩthĩaa asyai nĩmaĩle kũtetheew'a na nĩmatũngaa mũvea mũno angĩ meeka ũu. Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana mũsyai nĩwavetewa kĩanda kyake kya kũmanyĩsya syana. Mũsyai nĩwaĩle kũendeea kũea ngewa na syana syake kĩla ĩvinda.
16. Twaĩle kũlilikana kyaũ ĩla tũũtetheesya syana?
16 Ethĩwa mũsyai nĩwatw'a kana nũkwenda mũndũ ũngĩ emanyĩsye na syana syake, ũsu ũkũkũlw'a eke ũu ndaĩle kwĩyosea kĩanda kya mũsyai. Mavinda amwe ana-a-asa kana eĩtu-a-asa nĩmatonya kũkũlw'a memanyĩsye Mbivilia na syana sya asyai matendeeaw'a nĩ ũw'o. Ũla wakũlw'a eke ũu nĩwaĩle kũlilikana kana o na kũtw'ĩka nĩwe ũkũtetheesya mwana ũsu kĩ-veva, ti we mũsyai wake. Na atw'ĩka nũkwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na mwana ta ũsu, wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ akeka ũu me mũsyĩ kwa mwana ũsu, asyai ma mwana me vo kana ve Mũklĩsto ũngĩ mũima. Ethĩwa ti ũu maĩle kũsomea vandũ vaseo menekee nĩ andũ. Meeka ũu mainenga mũndũ o na ũmwe kĩtumi kya kũmasũanĩĩa naĩ. O na vailyĩ ũu, ve wĩkwatyo kana ĩvinda yĩkavika asyai asu meanĩsye kĩanda kĩla manengetwe nĩ Ngai kya kũsũvĩa syana syoo kĩ-veva.
17. Syana itonya kũkiakisya andũ ma mĩsyĩ yoo ata?
17 Syana ila syĩmanyĩasya kũmwenda Ngai wa w'o na kũatĩĩa ũtao wake nitonya kũkiakisya mĩsyĩ yoo. Itonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũnenga asyai masyo ndaĩa na kũmatetheesya vala ve na vata. O na ĩngĩ, syekala syĩ ndĩkĩĩku, no syĩkĩe vinya ala angĩ mũsyĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mbua ya ĩvinda ya Noa ĩtanamba kua, ve nzyawa ĩmwe ya Sethi yeetawa Lameki yamũthaithaa Yeova. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Lameki aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa mwanae, Noa: "Nĩwe ũkatũkiakisya wĩanĩ witũ na thĩnanĩ wa moko maitũ, kwondũ wa nthĩ ĩla Yeova waumanĩe." Wathani ũsu weanĩiw'e ĩla kĩumo kĩla kyaumanĩwe nthĩ kyavetiwe. (Mwa. 5:29; 8:21) O nasyo syana ila syĩtĩkĩlaa kũlũmany'a na ũthaithi wa w'o nitonya kũkiakisya andũ ma mũsyĩ, na ikamatetheesya momĩĩsye mathĩna ma ĩvinda yĩĩ na mũthya maivonoka mũisyo mũnene kwĩ ĩla mbua ya ĩvinda ya Noa.
18. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũkomĩĩsya twĩ na ũkũmbaũ ĩla twĩ matatwanĩ kana mathĩnanĩ?
18 Kũvoya, kũsũanĩa ngelekany'o sya andũ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ, na kũtindany'a na andũ ma Yeova nĩ maũndũ matumĩte andũ milioni mbingĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ makwata ũkiakisyo mathĩnanĩ moo. (Soma Savuli 145:18, 19.) Kũmanya kana Yeova nĩwe Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe nĩkũtũtetheeasya kũmĩĩsya twĩ na ũkũmbaũ mathĩna o na meva ala matonya kũtũkwata ũmũnthĩ na ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte.

translation:
"The God of all comfort; who comforts us in all our tribulation."—2 COR. 1:3, 4.
PARAGRAPH: 38, 6
1, 2. Jehovah comforts us even in all our tribulations, and does his purpose succeed even so?
A brother, whose name we will call Eduardo, once spoke with a ministerial servant named Stephen about a difficult situation he was facing. Stephen quoted him the scripture from 1 Corinthians 7:28: "But if a virgin should marry, she does well, yet she also does not sin." Stephen then asked: " 'Marry' means what to you, and how can it be possible when I am already engaged?" Stephen offered to help him research what Paul wrote. Paul wrote that Jehovah is "the God of all comfort; who comforts us in all our tribulation."—2 Cor. 1:3, 4.
2 Jehovah is our Father who supports us, and he comforts us in all our tribulations. It is good to remember this when we find it hard to cope and feel that God is listening to our prayers and answering them through his Word. Let us have confidence that he cares for us deeply.—Read Jeremiah 29:11, 12.
3. How can we strengthen our faith?
3 We may wonder if a person truly values his spirituality when he seems preoccupied with worldly things, or if he is being influenced by bad associations. It is often true that people get involved in worldly pursuits or become attached to material possessions. So, why is it sometimes hard to avoid becoming attached to "worldly concerns"? Are there Christians who struggle with similar temptations and how can we imitate their example to remain close to Jehovah? To find out, let us examine some examples.
"WORLDLY CONCERNS"
4, 5. What are some examples of "worldly concerns"?
4 Paul wrote under inspiration: "A married man is concerned about the affairs of this world—how to please his wife." (1 Cor. 7:33) Jehovah allows husbands and wives to enjoy their marriage. However, we need to be careful not to allow our desire for financial security to lead us to pursue worldly concerns excessively. (Prov. 23:23) For instance, a husband might feel pressured to provide his family with a certain standard of living, while a wife might want to maintain a similar lifestyle. God expects a husband to take the lead in providing spiritual guidance for his family. (Eph. 5:23) This does not mean that a Christian couple should disregard practical matters. Rather, they should seek direction from God's Word to determine what is truly important.
5 There may be times when a wife asks her husband, "Are you sure this is right?" Or a husband may wonder whether he is making the best decision for his children, perhaps because of pressure from others or because he fears what his friends will think. It is vital that a couple discuss such matters openly and honestly, and that they pray together for guidance. Furthermore, expenses can increase unexpectedly. And sometimes, a child may become ill and require medical attention. In such cases, a couple may have to spend considerable time dealing with the problem. Often, parents find that they have less time for personal pursuits. As a result, a husband and wife may need to adjust their priorities. A loving couple will support each other and work together to meet the needs of their family.
6-8. Why do some Christians find it difficult to say 'enough' when it comes to material possessions?
6 At times, a person may feel overwhelmed by his responsibilities. He may feel pressured to acquire more possessions simply to impress others. A home can easily become cluttered. Spending time and energy on acquiring possessions is not necessarily wrong, but it can lead to an unhealthy obsession with "things." (Prov. 13:12) The Bible shows that excessive materialism can cloud our judgment. For example, Jacob's wife Leah was very fond of ornamental pillows. She had many pillows, which likely took up a lot of space and required a great deal of care. (Gen. 30:1, 2) Some people accumulate so much stuff that they have difficulty enjoying life with their families. They may constantly worry about protecting their possessions, saying, "If only I had more!"
7 And some individuals in modern lands, like a woman in England, have become obsessed with having children. She kept getting pregnant, and eventually she had eleven children. As years passed, she realized that she could not adequately provide for them financially. She admitted that she regretted having so many children because it caused her family hardship. She said: "I wish I had never had so many children. Having a child is one thing, but raising a child is another."
8 The Bible warns that a Christian woman might be "led astray" by the desire to have children. (1 Tim. 2:15) But being led astray does not mean merely wanting to have children; it means letting that desire consume one's thoughts and lead to unwise decisions. A woman who has children should not neglect other important aspects of her life, such as spiritual activities and helping others, just to focus on motherhood. (1 Tim. 5:13) In fact, a woman may find satisfaction in other ways, serving Jehovah faithfully alongside her husband.
9 Is it wrong to want to please someone we love?
9 Many people feel obligated to please their parents. However, there is a limit to how much we should try to please them. We should not let our desire to please them override our conscience. It is important to remember that pleasing God should always come first. True Christians strive to please God and obey his commands, following the example of Jesus Christ. (John 5:28, 29) So, will doing so please everyone? Of course not. But this is what our loving Father wants us to do—to prioritize pleasing him above all others. Let us imitate those ancient ones who pleased God and proved faithful despite opposition.
CONSIDER THE EXAMPLE OF ANNA
10 What motivated Anna to pray to Jehovah? (See accompanying picture.)
10 Anna was deeply distressed because she was unable to have children, and her husband, Elkanah, loved her very much. Anna had rivals, and they often provoked her. (Read 1 Samuel 1:4-7.) Every year Anna would go with Elkanah. This situation made Anna weep and lose her appetite. She prayed to Jehovah each time she went. The Bible says she prayed with a broken heart, asking Jehovah to grant her a child. Will you endeavor to pour out your heart to Jehovah in prayer? Remember that he cares about your feelings. Even if it takes time for an answer, continue praying, saying, "Your favor is better than life." (1 Sam. 1:12, 17, 18; The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Trust that Jehovah will respond in due time, whether by granting you a child or providing comfort in another way.
11 How can we show gratitude?
11 Let us be reminded that this world, which is influenced by Satan, causes us to experience trials and difficulties. (1 John 5:19) Knowing that Jehovah is "the God of all comfort" strengthens us. Prayer is one way we can draw closer to him during difficult times. Anna told Jehovah her request. But even if we do not receive what we ask for, let us continue to love and worship Jehovah for what he does provide. Let us praise him, and through continued prayer, express our appreciation for his blessings.—Phil. 4:6, 7.
12 What motivated Anna to pray fervently?
12 Often we face challenges such as being unable to have a child, or being mistreated by others, and we feel discouraged. For example, Jesus' mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph when she learned she was pregnant, and she faced disapproval from some because of it. The Bible does not say whether she felt sad. However, it says that Anna was 84 years old. The account in Luke 2:37 states: "And she continued in the temple worshipping with fasting and prayers night and day." Such devotion shows how much Anna loved and trusted Jehovah.
13 Consider another example showing why it is important to remain loyal despite facing obstacles.
13 We should be kind to those who are struggling and show them compassion, especially our brothers and sisters. (Prov. 18:24) A sister named Paula experienced something similar. She had been serving Jehovah for five years when her husband left her. Because of this, she felt very lonely. But she kept busy in the ministry and met a brother named Ann who encouraged her to continue serving faithfully. Paula said: "When I spoke with Ann, I felt strengthened." She added: "This support helped me to continue worshiping Jehovah." To this day, Paula is still serving as a pioneer. And although she has never remarried, she continues to find comfort in her close friendship with fellow worshippers of Jehovah. Ann also benefited from their friendship, as she too became a pioneer thanks to Paula's encouragement.
14 What can help us stay steadfast when facing trials?
14 When we face difficulties, it is good to remember that others may be going through similar experiences. This can help us to feel less alone. For example, some Christians have lost loved ones and feel sad and discouraged, while others struggle with health problems or financial hardship. All of these situations can make it difficult to remain faithful to God. However, remembering that God understands how we feel can give us strength. And sometimes, simply talking about our problems can bring relief. So, let us always seek out the support of the congregation, relying on the loving counsel of elders and fellow worshippers. (Acts 2:4) The apostle Paul showed us a fine example. He commended the Thessalonian Christians because they were "comforting one another" and building up one another's faith. He also reminded them that he treated them like a father would his children.—Read 1 Thessalonians 2:7, 11, 12.
TO HELP OTHERS COPE
15 How can we comfort others?
15 One way to show love is to listen attentively and offer encouragement. Many people find it helpful to talk about their feelings, and Christians can provide a listening ear and offer practical advice. By doing so, we can help others to cope with their problems and strengthen their faith in Jehovah. In harmony with the Scriptures, comforting others is an important part of being a Christian. (Prov. 23:22; Heb. 6:1-4) Some individuals may be reluctant to open up, but we can assure them that we care and are willing to listen. It is important to respect their privacy and not pressure them to share more than they are comfortable with. We should strive to be available to offer comfort and support whenever possible.
16 What can we learn from Jesus' example regarding how we comfort others?
16 Jesus showed empathy and compassion when dealing with those who were grieving, and he took the time to listen to their concerns. He did not dismiss their feelings or minimize their pain. Many people responded favorably to his kindness and appreciated his willingness to share Bible-based counsel. His example teaches us that showing genuine concern and offering heartfelt sympathy can have a powerful impact on others. And when we encourage someone to turn to the Bible for comfort, we are helping them to find lasting hope, rather than simply offering temporary relief. But let us not impose our views on others or try to force them to accept our beliefs. Instead, let us allow God's Word to speak to their hearts and minds, trusting that the Holy Spirit will guide them to the truth. This does not mean that we should avoid sharing our faith with others. Rather, it means that we should approach them with humility and respect, recognizing that each person has the right to make their own decisions. Let us remember that our goal is to help others, not to judge them.
17 Can children teach adults something about showing empathy?
17 Children often demonstrate a natural ability to show empathy toward God and to appreciate his standards. They may be more willing to forgive others and to offer support to those in need. Furthermore, young ones are often very observant and sensitive to the emotions of others. For instance, the account of Noah's ark shows that Seth had a son named Lamech who foretold: "This one will become a source of comfort to us regarding our work and the toil of our hands because of the ground that Jehovah has cursed." That prophecy was fulfilled. (Gen. 5:29; 8:21) So, children can indeed teach adults something about showing empathy, and they can inspire us to imitate the compassionate qualities displayed by individuals like Noah and his family.
18 What can help us to express ourselves tactfully and respectfully, especially when discussing sensitive matters?
18 To a large extent, this involves following the example set by godly men such as David, and associating with Jehovah's people—millions of whom strive to speak kindly to others. (Read Psalm 145:18, 19.) Recognizing that Jehovah is the God of kindness will motivate us to be tactful and respectful in our speech and to approach others with genuine concern.

text:
"Moko maku matikaleele."
MBATHI: 54, 32
1, 2. (a) Nĩ mathĩna ta meva matũkwataa ũmũnthĩ, na matumaa twĩw'a ata? (b) Nĩ wĩkwatyo wĩva wa w'o tũnengetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Isaia 41:
MWĨĨTU-A-ASA ũmwe ũla nĩ vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda na ũtwaĩtwe nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi aĩtye atĩĩ: "O na kũtw'ĩka nĩnĩthĩawa na mũvango mũseo wa maũndũ ma kĩ-veva, nĩnĩthĩĩtwe ndyĩmakĩa mũno kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ. Ũndũ ũsu ũtumaa nĩkosa too, nĩthĩwa na mathĩna ma mwĩĩ, ũkatuma ndekalany'a na angĩ nesa, na mavinda angĩ nũtumaa nĩkw'a ngoo ũkethĩa nĩĩw'a ta nĩlika ĩimanĩ."
2 We no ũelewe ũndũ mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu wĩw'aa? Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani ĩvinyĩĩe andũ mũno, na kĩu nĩkĩtumĩte mambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa na ũyĩthĩa meĩw'a makuĩte makanoa. Ũndũ ũsu no ũelekanw'e na nanga ĩla ĩkwataa ĩsiwa ũkethĩa yĩithi mbee. (Nth. 12:25) Nĩ maũndũ meva matonya kũtuma wĩw'a ũu? Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa ũendeee kũmĩanĩsya na kĩkw'ũ kya mũndũ ũmwendete, ũkethĩwa wĩ na ũwau mũthũku, ũkethĩwa ũitata kũmanthĩa mũsyĩ waku ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ kwĩ na thĩna wa mbesa, kana o ũkethĩwa ũendeee kũkitana na ũvĩnganĩsya. Nũtonya kũthĩnĩka ngoonĩ nũndũ wa maũndũ asu nginya vinya waku ũkathela. O na ũu no ũtume wasya ũtanu ũla ũnaĩ naw'o mbeenĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana Ngai nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye kũũtetheesya.
3, 4. (a) Mbivilia ĩtũmĩaa ata ndeto "moko"? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma moko maitũ maleela?
3 Mavinda maingĩ Mbivilia ĩtũmĩaa mamutha ma mwĩĩ kwonany'a nguma syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kana meko me kĩvathũkany'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, kw'oko nĩkũwetetwe mavinda maingĩ vyũ Mbivilianĩ. Ĩla mũndũ weekĩwa kw'oko kwake vinya, kĩu no kyonany'e kana nĩwathangaaw'a, nĩwalũlũmĩlw'a, na nĩwakwata ũkũmbaũ wa kwosa ĩtambya ĩna. (1 Sam. 23:16; Esa. 1:6) O na no kyonany'e kana yu e na woni mũseo na wĩkwatyo kwondũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.
4 Mavinda amwe kwasya kw'oko kwa mũndũ nĩ kũleelu nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya mũndũ ũsu nũkw'ĩte ngoo, kana nde na wĩkwatyo. (2 Mav. 15:7; Aevl. 12:12) Mũndũ avika vau nĩ laisi akeyĩtũka. Ũtonya kumya va ũkũmbaũ ĩla wakwatwa nĩ maũndũ meũtuma ũthĩnĩka kĩlĩko, wĩw'a wĩ mũleelu mwĩĩ, ngoonĩ, kana kĩ-veva? Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũthuthya na kũkwĩkĩa vinya ũendeee kũmĩĩsya na ũyĩthĩwa na ũtanu?
"KW'OKO KWA YEOVA TI KŨKUVĨVYE, ŨNDŨ KŨTATONYA KŨTANGĨĨA"
5. (a) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtonya kũtũkwata ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ, ĩndĩ twaĩle kwĩkala tũlilikene ata? (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
5 Soma Nzevania 3:16, 17. Kũeka tũkwatwe nĩ wia kana tũkw'e ngoo nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kũeka moko maitũ maleele. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwĩka ũu, Asa waitũ, Yeova, atwĩkĩĩte vinya 'tũmwiĩe kwĩmakĩa kwitũ kw'onthe,' nũndũ nĩwe ũtũsũvĩaa. (1 Vet. 5:7) Lilikana ndeto ila Ngai watavisye Aisilaeli. Ameie kana kw'oko kwake "ti kũkuvĩvye, ũndũ kũtatonya kũtangĩĩa" athũkũmi asu make aĩkĩĩku. (Isa. 59:1) Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ nĩtũkwona mavinda atatũ Yeova woonanisye e wendi na ũtonyi wa kwĩkĩa vinya andũ make o na ĩla mekwona ta me thĩnanĩ mateyumya. Tata kũvindĩĩsya ũndũ maũndũ asu tũũneenea matonya kũkwĩkĩa vinya.
6, 7. Nĩ kyaũ kya vata tũkwĩmanyĩsya twasũanĩa ĩvinda yĩla Aisilaeli masindie Aamaleki?
6 Kavinda o kakuvĩ Aisilaeli mamina kumw'a ũkombonĩ wa Misili kwa nzĩa ya kyama, Aamaleki nĩmamavithũkĩie. Na nũndũ Yosua aĩ ngũmbaũ, Mose amwĩie natongoesye Aisilaeli kaũnĩ. Amina kũmwĩaĩa, oosie Aluni na Uulu mambata kalĩmanĩ kaĩ o vau vakuvĩ nĩ kana wĩthĩe nĩmene vala kaũ ũkũkitĩwa. Mose na aũme asu angĩ elĩ ko methĩwa makwatiwe nĩ wia na makavanga kũkĩĩa kalĩmanĩ kau? Aiee, ti w'o o na vanini!
7 Kĩu Mose weekie nĩkyo kyatumie masinda kaũ ũsu. Me vau kalĩmanĩ ookĩlilye moko make ĩũlũ akwete ĩla ndata ya ũla Ngai wa w'o na ekala ailyĩ ũu. Ĩvinda yonthe yĩla Mose wekalile ũu, Yeova nĩweekĩie moko ma Aisilaeli vinya wa kũkũna Aamaleki. Ĩndĩ ĩla moko ma Mose manoie na ambĩĩa kũmatheesya, Aamaleki nĩmo mambĩĩe kũkũna Aisilaeli. Aluni na Uulu moona ũu maendie na mĩtũkĩ "moosa ĩvia, mamwiĩa nthĩ, nake ayĩkalĩla; na Aluni na Uulu matw'ĩĩka moko make mokĩlĩtye na ĩũlũ, ũmwe ngalĩ ĩmwe, na [ũngĩ] ngalĩ ĩla ĩngĩ; na moko make matw'ĩĩkwa kũvika syũa yathũa." Kwoou Aisilaeli masindie kaũ ũsu nũndũ wa kũla kw'oko kwĩ vinya kwa Ngai.
8. (a) Asa eekie ata ĩla Aethiovia mookie kũkita Yuta? (b) Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũmwĩkwatye Ngai o ũndũ Asa wamwĩkwatisye?
8 Ĩvinda yĩla yĩngĩ Yeova woonanisye kw'oko kwake ti kũkuvĩvye nĩ ĩvindanĩ ya Mũsumbĩ Asa. Ve makaũ maingĩ mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Ĩndĩ katĩ wa makaũ asu onthe mũndũ ũla waathi kũkita e na asikalĩ aingĩ vyũ nĩ Nzela Mũethiovia. Aĩ na asikalĩ amanyĩsye 1,000,000. Na kwoou asikalĩ asu make maĩ vakuvĩ kũndũ kwĩlĩ kwa asikalĩ ma Asa. Wasũanĩa kĩu no wone ũndũ vaĩ laisi mũno Asa kwambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa na kũkwatwa nĩ wia, o na kũeka moko make maleele. Ĩndĩ kĩla Asa weekie nĩ kũmwĩkaĩla Yeova amwovosye. Ala mesene na ũvoo wa ita sya kaũ maĩ matonya kwasya kana Asa ndesa kũsinda Aethiovia o na akenda. Ĩndĩ "kwa Ngai maũndũ onthe nĩmatonyeka." (Mt. 19:26) Ngai nĩwoonanisye vinya wake mũnene na kwoou "akũnĩa Aethiovia mbee wa Asa," nĩkwĩthĩwa ngoo yake "yaĩ mbĩanĩu kwa Yeova mĩthenya yake yonthe."
9. (a) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtaatulya Neemia akaeka kũtũngĩĩa ngũta sya Yelusaleme? (b) Ngai asũngĩie mboya ya Neemia ata?
9 Ĩla Neemia waendie Yelusaleme eethĩie ndũa ĩsu ĩte na ngũta sya kũmĩsũvĩa na eethĩa Ayuti ala angĩ me atũlĩku ngoo mũno. We nũtonya kũsũanĩa ũndũ weewie? Kũtĩsw'a kũla Ayuti matĩsĩtw'e nĩ amaitha moo nĩkwatumĩte moko moo maleela, na kwoou maeka kũtũngĩĩa ngũta sya Yelusaleme. We Neemia eethĩa maũndũ mailyĩ ũu nĩwĩthĩwa o nake akwie ngoo na akaeka moko make maleele? Ekaĩ! O tondũ Mose, Asa, na athũkũmi angĩ aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova meekaa, kĩla ĩvinda Neemia nĩwamũvoyaa Yeova amũtetheesye. Na ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ndaaũlwa nĩ kwĩka ũu. O na kau no kwĩthĩwa Ayuti matalĩthasya kana maitonya kwĩyumya thĩnanĩ ũsu maĩ, Yeova nĩwamwĩthukĩĩsye Neemia na amũsũngĩa mboya yake. Nĩ kana Ngai alũlũmĩlye moko ma Ayuti, atũmĩie 'vinya wake mũnene' na 'kw'oko kwake kwĩ vinya.' (Soma Neemia 1:10; 2:17-20; 6:9.) We nũĩkĩĩaa kana Yeova no atũmĩe 'vinya wake mũnene' na 'kw'oko kwake kwĩ vinya' nĩ kana alũlũmĩlye athũkũmi make ũmũnthĩ?
YEOVA AKEEKĨA MOKO MAKU VINYA
10, 11. (a) Satani ekaa ata nĩ kana aleelye moko maitũ? (b) Yeova atũmĩaa kyaũ nĩ kana atũlũlũmĩlye na aitwĩkĩa vinya? (c) Maũndũ ala Ngai ũtũmanyĩasya maũtetheetye ata?
10 Nĩtwĩsĩ kana vai mũthenya Ndevili ũkaola kĩthito kyake kya kũũngamya mawĩa maitũ ma Kĩklĩsto. Atumaa silikalĩ, atongoi ma ndĩni, na angĩ ala makaĩĩte ũla mũĩkĩĩo makengana ĩũlũ witũ na matũtĩsya. Ekaa ũu e na kĩeleelo kĩva? Endaa aleelye moko maitũ wĩanĩ ũũ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ Yeova e wendi na e ũtonyi wa kũtwĩkĩa vinya, na nũndũ wa ũu nũtũnengae veva wake mũtheu nĩ kana ũtũlũlũmĩlye. (1 Mav. 29:12) Kwoou ve vata mũnene wa kũvoya Ngai atũnenge veva ũsu nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na vinya wa kũsinda matatwa onthe ala matonya kũtũkwata nũndũ wa Satani na nthĩ ĩno nthũku. (Sav. 18:39; 1 Ako. 10:13) O na nĩtwaĩle kũtũnga mũvea nũndũ twĩ na Ndeto ya Ngai, nayo ĩveveewe na veva wake mũtheu. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ nĩ lĩu wa kĩ-veva ũla tũkwataa kĩla mwei. Ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Nzekalia 8:9, 13 (soma) nĩ ndeto itonya kũtwĩkĩa vinya o na ũmũnthĩ. Ndeto isu syaneeniwe yĩla ĩvinda ĩkalũ ya Yelusaleme yatũngĩĩawa.
11 O na ĩngĩ, nĩtwĩkĩawa vinya nĩ maũndũ ala Ngai ũtũmanyĩasya maũmbanonĩ maitũ ma kĩkundi, maũmbanonĩ manene, na masukulunĩ ala twĩthĩawa namo. Maũndũ asu Ngai ũtũmanyĩasya no matũtetheesye tũmũthũkũme twĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo, twĩvangĩĩe kwĩanĩsya maũndũ mana ũthũkũminĩ wake, na tũyĩanĩsya ianda ila kĩla Mũklĩsto waĩle kwĩanĩsya. (Sav. 119:32) We nĩwĩthĩawa na mea ma kũtũmĩa nesa maũndũ ala Ngai ũtũmanyĩasya nĩ kana ũkwate vinya?
12. No nginya twĩke ata ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda kwĩkala twĩ na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova?
12 Yeova nĩwatetheeisye Aisilaeli masinda Aamaleki na Aethiovia, na anenga Neemia vamwe na ala waĩ namo vinya wa kũmina wĩa ũla maĩ naw'o. Ũu now'o Ngai ũkatũnengae vinya wa kũmĩĩsya ĩla andũ meũtũvĩnga, kana ĩla mate kwendeew'a, kana ĩla tũkwĩmakĩa nĩ kana tũvote kwĩanĩsya wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a. (1 Vet. 5:10) Yeova ndatũveteaa mathĩna maitũ kwa nzĩa ya kyama. Ĩndĩ no nginya tũtethye a vaitũ. Maũndũ amwe ithyĩ ene tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai kĩla mũthenya, kwĩyũmbanĩsya maũmbano na kũmathi tũteũkĩlĩĩla kyumwa o na kĩmwe, kwĩthĩwa na mũvango wa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na wa kwĩka ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ, na kũtata mavinda onthe tũmũvoye Yeova atũtetheesye. Tũikaaĩse kwenda maũndũ angĩ matwanangĩe nzĩa isu Yeova ũtũmĩaa kũtwĩkĩa vinya na kũtũthangaasya. Weew'a moko maku ta mambĩĩe kũleela ũndũnĩ o na ũmwe katĩ wa asu twaĩle kwĩka, mwĩsũve Ngai aũtetheesye. Weeka ũu ũkoona ũndũ veva wake 'ũkathũkũma nthĩnĩ waku, ũkũtonyethye kwĩthĩwa na wendi na vinya wa kwĩkaa' maũndũ asu. (Avi. 2:
LŨLŨMĨLYA MOKO ALA MALEELU
13, 14. (a) Mwana-a-asa ũmwe eekĩiwe vinya ata ĩtina wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũka? (b) Nĩ maũndũ ta meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkatw'ĩĩka ala angĩ?
13 Yeova nũtũtetheetye tũkethĩwa na ana-a-asa matwendete nthĩ yonthe na matonya kũtwĩkĩa vinya. Kwalilikana ndeto ii sya mũtũmwa Vaulo: "Ũkĩlyai moko ala maleelu, na maũũ ala monzu; na seũvĩsyai nyaĩĩ syenyu nzĩa ndũngalu." (Aevl. 12:
14 Yĩla ĩvinda Aisilaeli mokitaa na Aamaleki, Aluni na Uulu nĩmatw'ĩĩkie moko ma Mose. O naitũ no tũtw'ĩĩke ala angĩ kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Naaũ tũtonya kũtw'ĩĩka? Ala me na mathĩna ma ũkũũ kana o mathĩna angĩ ma mwĩĩ, ala meũvĩngwa nĩ andũ moo kana mekwona ta vate mũndũ ũkũũngana namo, kana ala makw'ĩĩwe. O na no twĩkĩe vinya amũika ala methĩwa maithing'ĩĩw'a meke maũndũ mataĩle, kana methĩwa maithing'ĩĩw'a maatĩanĩe na kĩla nthĩ ĩno ĩkĩtaa maendeeo, methĩwe nĩ maũndũnĩ ma kĩsomo, wĩa, kana o ũmanthi. (1 Ath. 3:
15. Ndeto syaku syeethĩwa syĩ nzeo itonya kũtethya ata Aklĩsto ala angĩ?
15 Ĩla Mũsumbĩ Asa wakwatie ũsindi wake, mwathani Asalia amwĩkĩie vinya vamwe na andũ ala angĩ akyasya: "Ĩthĩwai na vinya, na moko menyu matikaleele; nũndũ wĩa wenyu ũkatuvwa." (2 Mav. 15:7) Ndeto isu nĩsyatumie Asa eka moalyũku maingĩ nĩ kana atetheesye andũ mambĩĩe kũmũthaitha Yeova ĩngĩ. Ũu now'o ndeto syaku, syeethĩwa syĩ nzeo, itonya kwĩkĩa ala angĩ vinya. Na kĩu no kĩtume menda kwongelanga kĩthito kyoo kya kũmũthũkũma Yeova. (Nth. 15:23) Na ĩla wĩ maũmbanonĩ, ndũkaaĩse kwona ta ũtesa kwĩkĩa angĩ vinya ĩla wookĩlya kw'oko na waumya maelesyo maseo.
16. Atumĩa matonya kwĩka ata mekĩe vinya moko ma ala me kĩkundinĩ o tondũ Neemia weekie? Weta ũndũ Aklĩsto ala angĩ methĩwa maakũtethya.
16 Kwa vinya wa Yeova, Neemia na anyanyae nĩmalũlũmĩlye moko moo nĩ kana meanĩsye wĩa woo. Mĩthenya 52 ĩithela oou nĩmaminie kwaka ngũta sya Yelusaleme! (Nee. 2:18; 6:15, 16) Ĩndĩ Neemia ndaaĩka o kũũngamĩa wĩa ũsu. We mwene nĩweeyumisye atetheesya kwaka ngũta isu. (Nee. 5:
"MOKO MAKU MATIKALEELE"
17, 18. Nĩ kyaũ tũtesa kwĩthĩwa na nzika nakyo ĩla twĩ mathĩnanĩ kana twĩ na kĩũũyũ?
17 Kũthũkũma na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa twĩ na ngoo ĩmwe nĩkũtumaa twĩthĩwa na mũuo katĩ witũ. O na kwĩka ũu nĩkũtũtetheeasya tũkatuma ndũũ ĩtesa kũthela, na nĩkũlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ vamwe na ũ woo wa kwĩsa kwona moathimo ala tũkakwata tũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Kwĩkĩa vinya moko ma ala angĩ nĩkũmanengae vinya wa kwĩthĩwa me alũmu ĩla me mathĩnanĩ meũmatũla ngoo. O na kũtumaa maendeea kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo na woni mũseo. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana kũlũlũmĩlya ala angĩ nĩkũtũtethasya ithyĩ ene tũikelelũke maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva, na kũtumaa tũendeea kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu nthĩnĩ wa maũndũ ala Ngai ũtwathĩte. Ĩĩ nĩw'o ki, kwĩkĩa vinya moko ma ala angĩ kũtumaa o na moko maitũ makwata vinya.
18 Kũvindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa mavinda me kĩvathũkany'o ala Yeova watw'ĩĩkie na asũvĩa athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku, nĩkwaĩle kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo witũ nthĩnĩ wake. Kwoou ĩla wesa kwĩyĩthĩa thĩnanĩ, "moko maku matikaleele"! Ĩvindanĩ ta yĩu mũvoyae Yeova, na ũyĩeka kw'oko kwake kwĩ vinya kũũlũlũmĩlye na kũyĩũtongoesya nzĩanĩ ĩla ĩkatuma ũkwata moathimo ma Ũsumbĩ.

translation:
"A little dust will kill you."
MBATHI: 54, 32
1, 2. (a) Why is it important to be loyal, and what benefits does it bring? (b) How can we show loyalty like the one described in Isaiah 41:
A CERTAIN FARMER who owns every field and is respected as a leader of the community said: "It is good to work hard and honestly in farming, so that we may have enough food for many years. This also causes respect, because of good deeds, which makes me happy with others, and other fields help me get along well and feel satisfied with life."
2 Did you understand what this farmer meant? The desire to get rich is like Satan deceiving people, and he uses them to chase after worthless things. This is shown by the example of a man who borrowed money to buy something useless. (Matt. 12:25) Are there things that can make you fall into this trap? Things like wanting to compete with another person, wanting to be admired, wanting to live extravagantly, or wanting to continue arguing and being envious. Don't let such thoughts ruin your life. And this can cause you to suffer more than you need to. Remember that contentment is better than chasing after empty desires. It is good to trust in God and ask Him for guidance.
3, 4. (a) What does the expression "a little" mean? (b) What can cause a little thing to become serious?
3 Many Bible writers used mild expressions to show consideration, or to avoid causing offense. For instance, they often used mild language when giving warnings. But a person may disregard a warning, thinking it is insignificant, and then suffer the consequences. (1 Sam. 23:16; Isa. 1:6) Or he may think he can handle the situation himself.
4 Sometimes a small mistake on someone's part can lead to a bigger problem, or a small act of disobedience can have serious results. (2 Chron. 15:7; Heb. 12:12) A person who ignores warnings is foolish. You can tell whether a problem will become serious by considering the underlying causes, how much it affects you, or its potential consequences. Why is it important to recognize problems quickly and deal with them promptly?
"TO SEEK JEHOVAH IS TO PROTECT YOURSELF, AND YOU WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED"
5. (a) What can help us to identify situations where we might stumble, and why is it important to be realistic? (b) How can we improve our discernment?
5 Read Proverbs 3:16, 17. Whether we experience success or failure, and whether we are young or old, is not as important as maintaining integrity. Because faithful men like Asa trusted in Jehovah, he helped them 'to seek him diligently,' and he sustained them. (1 Chr. 5:7) Similarly, God assured ancient Israel that their "seeking would not be disappointed." (Isa. 59:1) This scripture shows us that Jehovah is concerned about our welfare and wants us to succeed. Let us examine what principles we can learn from this example to help us discern matters carefully.
6, 7. Why should we strive to improve our discernment regarding spiritual matters, just as the Israelites did when fighting Amalek?
6 When the Israelites were traveling from Egypt toward Canaan, the Amalekites attacked them unexpectedly. Despite Joshua leading the fight, Moses climbed to a hilltop and prayed to Jehovah. Meanwhile, Aaron and Hur supported his hands so they would not become weak. Did Moses and the others realize that their strength depended on Jehovah's backing and that they needed to continue praying? Yes, indeed!
7 Then Moses told Joshua to select men and go out to fight against Amalek. He said to him, "Choose some men and go out to fight against Amalek tomorrow. I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand." So Joshua did what Moses instructed, and he went out to fight against Amalek. And Aaron and Hur went up to support Moses' hands. As long as Moses kept raising his hands, Jehovah continued to help Israel defeat the Amalekites. But when Moses let his hands drop, the Amalekites began to gain the upper hand. Aaron and Hur realized this and quickly helped Moses raise his hands again, supporting them until sunset. This caused the Israelites to win the battle.
8. (a) How did Asa show faith when facing the Ethiopian army? (b) What can we learn from how Asa showed faith about how we can strengthen our relationship with Jehovah?
8 On another occasion, Jehovah demonstrated his power by helping King Asa of Judah defeat a huge Ethiopian army. The Bible says that there were 1,000,000 soldiers in the Ethiopian army. They marched toward Jerusalem and camped nearby. Asa and his people prayed to Jehovah, asking for his help, and they sacrificed animals. Because Asa trusted in Jehovah, he was able to defeat the Ethiopians. Some may wonder why Asa needed help despite being a righteous king. The Bible explains that "with man some things are impossible." (Matthew 19:26) Jehovah answered Asa's prayer and defeated the Ethiopians, and the Bible states that Asa "gave all his strength to Jehovah" throughout his life.
9. (a) What motivated Nehemiah to rebuild the wall of Jerusalem? (b) Did Jehovah support Nehemiah's efforts?
9 Nehemiah went to Jerusalem and found that the wall was broken down and the gates burned. He wanted to rebuild the wall, but he faced opposition from those who did not want him to succeed. Why should we be encouraged when facing obstacles? Because just as Jehovah helped Asa, he can also help us overcome challenges. Nehemiah did not give up, and he asked Jehovah for assistance. Like Moses, Asa, and other faithful men, Nehemiah knew that Jehovah hears prayers. And this account shows us how important it is to pray. Furthermore, even though the enemies tried to intimidate them and prevent them from rebuilding, Jehovah strengthened Nehemiah and supported his efforts. Does this mean that God always intervenes directly to solve our problems? Read Nehemiah 1:10; 2:17-20; 6:9. Do you think that Jehovah will use his powerful spirit and his organization to help his servants?
JEHOVAH ANSWERS PRAYERS
10, 11. (a) What does Satan try to make us believe about prayer? (b) How does Jehovah show that he listens to and answers prayers? (c) Are there things that God may allow to happen anyway?
10 Let us remember how devoted Nebuchadnezzar was when he acknowledged his Creator's authority. He humbly admitted his mistakes, and others who were loyal imitated his example and benefited. Why did he reach this conclusion? Because he saw what happened to those who opposed the true worship. Jehovah is willing and able to answer our prayers, and we can be sure that he hears them. (1 Chron. 29:12) So let us continue to thank God for helping us to overcome the temptation to give up when faced with difficulties, so that we will not fall victim to Satan's schemes. (Ps. 18:39; 1 Cor. 10:13) And let us strive to remain strong spiritually by means of God's Word, which is powerful and effective. Another thing that will help us stay strong is regular meditation. The scriptures at Ezekiel 8:9, 13 (read) teach us how to resist temptation and maintain our spirituality. These scriptures remind us of what happened when Jerusalem was despoiled.
11 Also, we benefit from seeing how God uses his organization, the congregations, large assemblies, and schools to strengthen us. By means of these things, God helps us to improve our spiritual understanding, to appreciate more fully his purposes, and to cooperate with fellow Christians. (Ps. 119:32) But how can you make good use of the provisions God makes available to help you stay strong?
12 Will you always endeavor to keep close to Jehovah?
12 Jehovah delivered Israel from the Amalekites and Ethiopians, and he encouraged Nehemiah and others like him to rebuild the wall. Today, God can encourage us to overcome obstacles, whether they seem insurmountable or whether we feel discouraged about cooperating. (1 Chron. 5:10) Jehovah supports us through his spirit. Let us therefore support one another. Some ways we can do so are by reading God's Word daily, attending meetings and sharing what we learn with others, keeping busy in the ministry and striving to apply Bible principles, and being diligent in observing the blessings Jehovah gives us. We should also be willing to consider new ways Jehovah uses to teach us and strengthen us. Perhaps you have qualities that could be used to help others, so offer your assistance willingly. Remember that God encourages those who encourage others. Like the psalmist, you may find it helpful to say, "I will certainly watch for you constantly; I will take delight in watching for you." (Ps. 2:
SOME WAYS TO ENCOURAGE OTHERS
13, 14. (a) How did one young man show initiative in helping a friend? (b) What practical things can we do to encourage others?
13 Jehovah empowers us to stand firm under trial and helps us to find ways to assist others. Consider Paul's counsel: "Be joyful with those rejoicing, and weep with those weeping." (Rom. 12:
14 When the Israelites fought against the Amalekites, Aaron and Hur supported Moses. Similarly, we can support others in various ways. Can we offer help to those who are sick or elderly, to those who are facing financial difficulties, to those who feel lonely or isolated, or to those who need spiritual strengthening? Also, we can show appreciation for those who work hard in the congregation, such as those who prepare meals for us, give us rides, or spend time teaching us, or for their efforts in maintaining the Kingdom Hall and grounds. (1 Thess. 3:
15. Why is your personal example a powerful way to encourage fellow Christians?
15 When King Asa relied on Jehovah, Azariah encouraged him and his army, saying: "Jehovah is with you when you go out to fight against the enemy." (2 Chron. 15:7) Asa's example shows us that sincere encouragement can strengthen others spiritually. Your fine example can also be a source of strength to others. And may this scripture move you to speak truthfully about what Jehovah has done for you. (Acts 15:23) Furthermore, remember to look for opportunities to commend others for their good qualities and accomplishments.
16. What practical steps did Nehemiah take to encourage his brothers, and how can Christians today imitate him?
16 Because of his love for Jehovah, Nehemiah and his companions worked diligently to rebuild the wall. In just 52 days they completed the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem! (Neh. 2:18; 6:15, 16) Nehemiah showed concern for his brothers. We too can demonstrate our concern for our brothers. (Neh. 5:
"YOUR LOYALTY IS WORTH MUCH"
17, 18. Why should we value loyalty, especially when we face difficulties or temptations?
17 Loyalty to Jehovah and to our spiritual brothers unites us and strengthens us. But failing to show loyalty can lead to discouragement and can weaken our faith and our zeal for God's service. It can also damage our relationships with others and cause us to feel isolated. Valuing loyalty means appreciating those who remain steadfast during difficult times and encouraging them. It also means avoiding gossip and remaining loyal to our brothers, even when others try to discourage us. Moreover, valuing loyalty helps us to avoid being influenced by negative thinking and encourages us to maintain a positive outlook, so that we can continue to serve Jehovah joyfully. That is why valuing loyalty benefits both the loyal person and those around him.
18 To demonstrate our love for Jehovah, we must listen to his warnings and heed the direction he gives through his organization. We need to be determined to say, "I will always remember this!" By doing so, we show that we trust Jehovah and that we are willing to let him guide us in applying Bible principles and in making decisions that will help us stay faithful and enjoy his blessing.

text:
"Umai nthĩnĩ wake, andũ makwa."—ŨVU. 18:4.
MBATHI: 10, 45
1. Nĩ kyaũ kyanengie andũ ma Ngai wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kuma Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene, na nĩ makũlyo meva tũũneenea?
ĨSOMONĨ ĩvĩtu nĩtũnoonie ũndũ Aklĩsto ala aĩkĩĩku mataviwe nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. Ĩndĩ ũseo nĩ kana mayaĩ matũae vo ĩvinda yonthe. Makatw'ĩka maĩ matũe mũtavonĩ wa ndĩni isu sya ũvũngũ vate mũndũ ũkesa kuma vo, mwĩao ũũ wa Ngai wĩthĩwa waĩ wa mana: "Umai nthĩnĩ wake, andũ makwa." (Soma Ũvuan'yo 18:4.) Yu twĩ na mea ma kũmanya nĩ ĩndĩĩ andũ ma Ngai maumie vyũ mũtavonĩ wa Mbaviloni! Ĩndĩ tũtanamba kũmanya kĩu, ekai twambe kũsũngĩa makũlyo aa: Mwaka wa 1914 ũte mũviku, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia moonaa ata Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene? Ĩvindanĩ ya Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe mo ana-a-asa maitũ mathũkũmie wĩa wa kũtavany'a na kĩthito kĩana ata? No twasye andũ ma Ngai mataviwe nĩ Mbaviloni ĩvindanĩ yĩu aĩ nũndũ nĩmaaĩle kũkanw'a na kũlũngwa?
"MBAVILONI NĨ MBALŨKU"
2. Kwosana na ũmanyi ũla Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maĩ naw'o, mo moonaa ata ndĩni sya ũvũngũ?
2 Myaka mĩongo ĩana ũna Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe ũtambĩĩe, Charles Taze Russell na anyanyae nĩmamanyie kana ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto iyamanyĩasya ũw'o wa Mbivilia. Nũndũ wa ũu, kwosana na ũmanyi ũla maĩ naw'o ĩvinda yĩu, nĩmatwie vyũ kana maikalikana na ndĩni ya ũvũngũ. Tene vyũ Mweinĩ wa 11, 1879, ĩkaseti ya Zion's Watch Tower yawetie ũtwi woo, ũla wosanĩte na Maandĩko, yĩteũvithany'a yasya atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa ĩkanisa o na yĩva yĩvangaa kana yo nĩ mwĩĩtu mũtheu wĩvaĩw'e Klĩsto, ĩndĩ yesa kũsiw'a yĩyĩthĩwa yĩkwatanĩtye na [nthĩ na] yĩkakwatwa mbau nĩ nthĩ (ĩla nyamũ), no nginya tũyĩvangĩle vala maandĩko mayĩvangĩle. Yo nĩ ĩkanisa ĩlwaya." Ĩlwaya yĩla yĩũwetwa nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene.—Soma Ũvuan'yo 17:1, 2.
3. Nĩ ĩtambya yĩva Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia moosie yĩkwonany'a kana nĩmamanyĩte vata wa kwĩvathana na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 26.)
3 Aũme na aka asu mamũkĩĩte Ngai nĩmeesĩ kĩla maaĩlĩte kwĩka. Nĩmeesĩ kana Ngai ndesa kũmaathima maendeea kwĩkwatany'a na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. Na nũndũ wa ũu, Amanyĩw'a aingĩ ma Mbivilia nĩmaandĩkie mavalũa meyumĩtye mũambanĩ wa kanisa ũla mathaithaa. O na aingĩ moo nĩmaendaa ne mo makasoma valũa woo mbee wa kanisa. Na kũla mavatwa maisomea ĩkanisa valũa woo, amwe nĩmatũmĩaa kĩla ũmwe kanisanĩ ũsu valũa ũsu. Mayendaa nongi kũendeea kwĩkwatany'a na ndĩni ya ũvũngũ! Mũndũ waĩ atata kwosa ĩtambya ta yĩu myakanĩ yĩ navu ĩtina ethĩwa ekaa kũawa. Ĩndĩ kũvikĩĩa mwaka wa 1870, silikalĩ mbingĩ nĩsyaekete kũkwata kanisa mbau tondũ syeekaa navu ĩtina. Na kwoou nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ta isu andũ maĩ na ũthasyo wa kũneenea maũndũ ma ndĩni, o na kũleana ũtheinĩ na atongoi ma kanisa mateũkĩa kwĩkwa ũndũ.
4. Ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe andũ ma Ngai maĩ na woni wĩva ĩũlũ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene?
4 O na kau Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmatavĩtye andũ moo ma mũsyĩ, anyanyae moo, na ala maĩ makanisanĩ moo ma tene ũndũ moonaa ndĩni sya ũvũngũ, nĩmamanyie kwĩka ũu kũitoetye. Nthĩ yonthe nĩyaaĩlĩte kũmanya kana Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene nĩ ĩlwaya maũndũnĩ ma ndĩni! Nũndũ wa ũu, katĩ wa Mwei wa 12, 1917 na myeinĩ ya mbee ya mwaka wa 1918, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia nĩmanyaĩĩkisye tulakiti 10,000,000 syaĩ na ũvoo ũũ: "Mbaviloni Nĩ Mbalũku." Tulakiti ĩsu yavuanĩtye vyũ makanisa ala meyĩtaa ma Kĩklĩsto, na mamĩnenganie na kĩthito kingĩ mũno o na kau maĩ o ngili nini ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Vate nzika, kĩu nĩkyatumie atongoi ma ndĩni mathata, ĩndĩ kũthata kwoo kũyaatuma Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maekana na wĩa ũsu wa vata. Nĩmatw'ĩte vyũ kũmwĩw'a "Ngai mbee wa kũmew'a andũ." (Meko 5:29) Kwoou yu tũtonya kwasya ata? Tũtonya kwasya kana ĩvindanĩ ya ũla kaũ wa mbee tiw'o Aklĩsto asu maendeee kũtavwa nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene, ĩndĩ nĩw'o maendeee kuma nthĩnĩ wayo na kũtetheesya andũ angĩ meke o tamo.
KĨTHITO KYA ANDŨ MA NGAI ĨVINDA YA KAŨ WA MBEE WA NTHĨ YONTHE
5. Twĩsĩ ata kana ana-a-asa maĩ na kĩthito kingĩ mũno ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe?
5 Navu ĩtina tũnaĩkĩĩaa kana ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe, Yeova nĩweew'ĩthiw'e woo nĩ andũ make nũndũ mayaĩ na kĩthito kya kũtavany'a. Na nũndũ wa ũu twasya kana Yeova nĩweetĩkĩlilye Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene ĩmatave kwa kavinda kanini. Ĩndĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aĩkĩĩku ala mathũkũmaa Ngai myakanĩ ya 1914-1918 nĩmesie kũweta nesa kana andũ ma Mwĩaĩi me ta kĩkundi nĩmeekie kyonthe kĩla maĩ matonya nĩ kana wĩa wa kũtavany'a ndũkaũngame. Ve ũkũsĩ mwĩanu wa kũĩkĩĩthya kĩu. Kũelewa nesanga kĩla Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia meekaa ĩvinda yĩu nĩkũtumĩte tũelewa nesanga maũndũ amwe maandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ.
6, 7. (a) Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia moonie mawetu meva ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe? (b) Nengane ngelekany'o ikwonany'a kĩthito kĩla Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maĩ nakyo.
6 Ũw'o nĩ kana Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ala maĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe (1914-1918) nĩmaumisye ũkũsĩ mũnene ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Ĩndĩ ũyaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwoo kwĩka ũu nũndũ wa itumi iana ũna. Ekai tũneenee itumi ilĩ katĩ wa isu. Kĩtumi kya mbee, wĩa ũla mũnene matethasya ĩvinda yĩu waĩ kũnengane mavuku. Kwoou ĩla yĩla ĩvuku yeetawa The Finished Mystery yakũniwe maluvuku nĩ silikalĩ mwambĩĩonĩ wa mwaka wa 1918, wĩa wa kũtavany'a nĩwaitavĩie ana-a-asa aingĩ. Mayeemanyĩĩtye kũtavany'a na Mbivilia yĩ yoka, na ĩvuku The Finished Mystery nĩ tayo yaneenaa vandũ voo. Kĩtumi kya kelĩ nĩ ĩla ndetema nthũku mũno (Spanish influenza) yaumĩlile mwakanĩ wa 1918. Ndetema ĩsu yatambĩte mũno vyũ ũkethĩa ti laisi kwa atavany'a kũthi kũndũ na kũndũ. Ĩndĩ o na kau kwaĩ mathĩna asu na angĩ maingĩ, Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia me ta kĩkundi matatie vyũ wĩa ndũkaũngame.
7 Mwakanĩ wa 1914 wĩ w'oka, kĩkundi kyu kĩnini kya Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia kyoonisye andũ mbee wa 9,000,000 ĩla sinema yeetawa "Photo-Drama of Creation." Nĩ kana maseũvye sinema ĩsu, matũmĩie visa na tũsinema tũkuvĩ na matũvulany'a na wasya. Sinema ĩsu yoonanisye maũndũ ala methĩĩtwe kuma mũndũ oombwa nginya mũthya wa ĩla Myaka Ngili. Myaka ĩsu ũsu waĩ ũndũ mũnene vyũ. Kwamba kũsũanĩa kĩu! Atĩ ũtalo wa andũ ala moonie sinema ĩsu mwakanĩ wa 1914 wĩ w'oka waĩ mũnene kwĩ ũtalo w'onthe wa atavany'a ala me nthĩ yonthe ũmũnthĩ! Livoti syonanasya kana mwakanĩ wa 1916 andũ 809,393 nĩmaendie maũmbanonĩ ma andũ onthe nthĩ ya Amelika, na mwakanĩ wa 1918 ala maendie maũmbanonĩ o ta asu mongelekile mavika 949,444. Mwa vai ngũĩ Amanyĩw'a asu ma Mbivilia maĩ kĩthito!
8. Ana-a-asa ala matongoesye ĩvinda ya ũla kaũ wa mbee meekie ata nĩ kana ala angĩ makwate lĩu wa kĩ-veva?
8 Ĩvinda ya ũla kaũ wa mbee wa nthĩ yonthe ala matongoetye meekie kĩla kyonthe maĩ matonya nĩ kana maendeee kũnenga ana-a-asa lĩu wa kĩ-veva o na kau nĩmanyaĩĩkĩte kũũ na kũũ. Lĩu ũsu wa kĩ-veva nĩwanengie ana-a-asa vinya wa kũendeesya wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Richard H. Barber nũmwe waĩ kw'o ĩvinda yĩu na aeleetye ũũ: "Nĩtwavotie kũtetheesya asyaĩĩsya ma kũthyũlũlũka meana ũna maendeee na wĩa woo na nĩtwavotie kũtũmĩaa ana-a-asa makaseti ma The Watch Tower. O na nĩtwamavikasya Canada o na kũtw'ĩka kũu maĩ makũne maluvuku. O na nĩnatanĩie kũtũmĩa ana-a-asa amwe tũvuku tũnini twaĩ tũtonya kwĩanĩa ngusunĩ twa The Finished Mystery nũndũ nĩmavenetwe ala maĩ namo mbeenĩ. Mwana-a-asa Rutherford nĩwatũkũlilye tũvangĩthye maũmbano manene taoninĩ imwe ngalĩko ya wumĩlonĩ wa sua ya Amelika, na tũitũma ana-a-asa makaumye maũvoo nĩ kana mekĩe ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa vinya mũno vyũ ũndũ vatonyeka."
VE MAŨNDŨ MAAĨLE KŨLŨNGWA
9. (a) Nĩkĩ andũ ma Ngai maaĩle kũkanw'a na kũlũngwa katĩ wa 1914 na 1919? (b) O na kau ve kũndũ Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maaĩle kũlũngwa, wĩthĩwa wĩ ũthũku kũsũanĩa ata?
9 Ti maũndũ onthe meekawa nĩ Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia katĩ katĩ wa 1914 na 1919 moosanĩte na myolooto ya Maandĩko. O na kau ana-a-asa asu mayaĩ na ũseleke ngoonĩ, mayamanyaa nĩ ĩndĩĩ maaĩle kwĩw'a silikalĩ na nĩ ĩndĩĩ mataaĩle kwĩka ũu. (Alo. 13:1) Kwoou me ta kĩkundi, mayaaĩvathana vyũ na kaũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mũsumbĩ wa nthĩ ya Amelika waumisye mũthenya wa Matukũ 30, Mwei wa 5, 1918, wĩthĩwe mũthenya wa kũvoyea mũuo, ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower nĩyeekĩie Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia vinya yamea o namo no meke oou. O na ana-a-asa amwe nĩmaumisye mbesa syoo itetheesye kaũnĩ na ve angĩ mate aingĩ maendie ũ kaũnĩ makuĩte mĩio ya kaũ. Ĩndĩ twĩthĩwa tũivĩtya tũkasya Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mataviwe nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene ĩvindanĩ yĩu aĩ nũndũ nĩmaaĩle kũkanw'a na kũlũngwa. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, nĩmeesĩ nesa kana nĩmaaĩle kwĩvathana vyũ na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ, na ĩvindanĩ ya Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe matielye o vanini metithũkany'e vyũ na Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene.—Soma Luka 12:47, 48.
10. Nĩ kyaũ Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maleile vyũ kwĩka?
10 O na kau Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mayaeleawa nesa ũla mwolooto wa kũema kwĩlikya kaũnĩ tondũ tũũeleetwe ũmũnthĩ, ve kĩndũ kĩmwe meesĩ nesa vyũ. Nĩmeesĩ Mbivilia nĩvatanĩte kũaana. Kwoou o na ala ana-a-asa moosie mĩio ya kaũ na malika ũla Kaũnĩ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe, nĩmaleile vyũ kũtũmĩa mĩio ĩsu kũaa andũ ala angĩ. Amwe ala maleile kũaana matwaiwe kũla kaũ waĩ mũvyũ vyũ nĩ kana makakw'ĩĩe kw'o.
11. Silikalĩ syeekie ata ĩla Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia maleile kũkita kaũnĩ?
11 Ndevili nĩwathatiw'e mũno nĩ ũtwi ũsu wa ana-a-asa, o na kau ti atĩ nĩmeevathanĩte vyũ na kaũ. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩwatumie 'sila ũte wa katĩ ũtw'ĩka mwĩao.' (Sav. 94:20, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Mũnene ũmwe wa Ita sya Amelika weetawa James Franklin Bell aineena na Mwana-a-asa J. F. Rutherford na Mwana-a-asa W. E. Van Amburgh nĩwamaumbũkie kana mũvĩa ũmwe wa mĩao (U.S. Department of Justice) nĩwatatĩte kũvĩtũkĩthya mwĩao mbungenĩ wa kana ala malea kũkita kaũnĩ nĩmoawe. Aineena ũu awetaa Amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia. Mũnene ũsu atavisye Mwana-a-asa Rutherford ũũ ew'ĩte woo: "Mwĩao ũsu ndũnavĩtũkĩthw'a nũndũ Wilson [mũsumbĩ wa Amelika] nũleile, ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ ũndũ tũtonya kũmũkwatya, na nĩtũũmũkwatya!"
12, 13. (a) Nĩkĩ ala ana-a-asa nyanya matw'ĩwe kwovwa ĩvinda ĩasa? (b) Kwovwa kwa ana-a-asa asu nĩkwatumie maeka kũmwĩw'a Yeova? Elesya.
12 Silikalĩ nĩyesie kwĩanĩsya kĩu yawetie. Amwe ma ana-a-asa ala makwatĩĩe Watch Tower Society nĩmeekĩiwe mbĩnĩ. Asu nĩ Mwana-a-asa Rutherford na Mwana-a-asa Van Amburgh, na angĩ thanthatũ. Saa sya kũtw'a sila syavika, ũla wasilaa ĩkoani yoo aisye: "Momanyĩsyo ma ndĩni ala andũ aa maendeesye no mathũkye maũndũ mũno o na kwĩ nguthu ya asikalĩ ma Germany . . . Andũ aa mekua anene ma mĩao Silikalĩnĩ na ala ma mũvĩa wa ita wa kũthiana maũndũ ta matesĩ wĩa woo, na masyokete makaneenea naĩ atavany'a onthe ma makanisa onthe. Maĩle kwosewa ĩtambya ĩvyũ mũno ya mĩao." (Kavuku Faith on the March, ka A. H. Macmillan, ĩth. 99) Ũu nĩw'o kwaendie. Ana-a-asa asu nyanya nĩmatw'ĩwe kwovwa ĩvinda ĩasa yelanĩ yĩmwe yĩ Atlanta, Georgia. Ĩndĩ ĩla kaũ wathelile nĩmathaiw'e na ĩkoani yoo yavutwa.
13 Aũme asu nyanya nĩmaũngamie na kĩla meesĩ kuma Maandĩkonĩ o na ĩla maĩ ove. Valũanĩ ũmwe maandĩkĩĩte mũsumbĩ wa Amelika maikũlya mew'ĩwe tei maisye ũũ: "Mwĩaĩi nũwetete kwenda kwake Maandĩkonĩ akasya, 'Ndũkoae,' na kwoou mũndũ o na wĩva wĩtanĩaw'a na [International Bible Students] Association na wĩyumĩsye Mwĩaĩi vyũ wĩsa kũema kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto wake wa kwĩkala e mũtheu ndaendeea kwendwa nĩ Ngai, o na kĩu kĩtuma esa kwanangwa vyũ. Kwoou andũ ta asu mayĩsa kũaana o mesĩ kĩla mekwĩka." Isu nĩ ndeto syaĩ ngito mũno. Vate nzika, ana-a-asa asu mayavangĩte kũtũla mwĩao wa Yeova o na vanini!
ĨVINDA YA KUMA MBAVILONI NĨYESIE KŨVIKA!
14. Elesya ũtũmĩĩte Maandĩko kĩla kyaendeeie kuma mwaka wa 1914 nginya 1919.
14 Ĩandĩko ya Malaki 3:1-3 nĩyĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla "ana ma Livai," ala nĩmo etĩkĩw'a mauta, maaĩle kũthew'a. Ĩvinda yĩu yaĩ kuma 1914 nginya mwambĩĩonĩ wa mwaka wa 1919. (Soma.) Ĩvindanĩ yĩu Yeova Ngai, ũla nĩwe wĩtĩtwe "Mwĩaĩi," e na Yesũ Klĩsto, ũla wĩtĩtwe "mũtũmwa wa ũtianĩo," nĩmookie ĩkalũnĩ ya kĩ-veva nĩ kana mathiane ala mathũkũmaa vo. Ĩtina wa andũ ma Yeova kũkanw'a na kũthew'a nĩmeethĩiwe matonya kũnewa mawĩa maingangĩ. Mwakanĩ wa 1919, ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" nĩyanyuviwe nĩ kana ĩnengae andũ ma nyũmba ya mũĩkĩĩo lĩu wa kĩ-veva. (Mt. 24:45) Kũvikĩĩa vau andũ ma Ngai maĩ manaumanwa vyũ na Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, nũndũ wa mumo wa Yeova andũ make methĩĩtwe maikwata ũmanyi mwingangĩ wa kwenda kwake na nĩmaendeee kũmwenda mũnango tawe Ĩthe woo wa ĩtunĩ. Matũngaa mũvea ta kĩ nũndũ wa moathimo make! [1]
15. Kũmanya kana nĩtwathaiw'e kuma Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene kwaĩle kũtũtethya ata?
15 Ko tũtatanaa mũno nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩtwaumie mũtavonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene! O na kau Satani nĩwĩkĩĩte kĩthito kingĩ avete vyũ Ũklĩsto ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, nũemetwe vyũ. Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla ũthasyo ũsu Yeova ũtũnengete wĩthĩwe wĩ wa mana. (2 Ako. 6:1) Andũ aingĩ mũno me ngoo nzeo no movetwe nĩ ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. Andũ asu nĩmaĩle kũtetheew'a maume kũu. Na nithyĩ tũtonya kũmony'a nzĩa. Kwoou o ta ana-a-asa ala maĩ kw'o myaka yĩ navu ĩtina, nĩtwĩkei kyonthe kĩla tũtonya tũtetheesye andũ ta asu maume ndĩninĩ sya ũvũngũ!
^ [1] (kalungu ka 14) Kũtavwa kwa Ayuti nĩ Mbaviloni kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 70 nĩkũvw'anene kwa nzĩa mbingĩ na kĩla kyakĩtĩkĩie Aklĩsto ĩvinda yĩla andũ mambĩĩe kũkaĩa ũla mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o. Ĩndĩ vai kĩndũ kĩkwonany'a kana kũtavwa kwa Ayuti kwaĩ kyuu kya kĩla kyakwatie Aklĩsto. Nĩkĩ? Mbee, ĩvinda yĩla Ayuti mekalile Mbaviloni yĩyĩanene na ĩvinda yĩla Aklĩsto mataviwe nĩ Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. Kwoou tũyaĩle kwambĩĩa kũmantha syuu tũmaũndũnĩ tw'onthe tũla twakwatie Ayuti ĩvindanĩ yĩu maĩ atave tũyasya kana tũmaũndũ tũu nĩtũkonanĩtye na kĩla kyakwatie Aklĩsto myaka ĩana ũna mwaka wa 1919 ũte mũviku.
