translation:
"Be loyal to her until death, and many nations will be your friends."—PROVERBS 18:4.
NOTES: 10, 45
1. Why did faithful Christians allow themselves to be imprisoned by the great Babylon, and what lesson can we learn from this?
ISOMONIA helps us understand how Christ also underwent trials in the great Babylon. Indeed, they may experience similar trials throughout their lives. Let us examine some examples to see how Jehovah has supported his people: "Be loyal to her until death, and many nations will be your friends." (Read Proverbs 18:4.) Yes, we know that Jehovah's people need loyalty during times of trouble in Babylon! So let us now consider what we can learn from this: In 1914, did Bible Students recognize that the great Babylon had begun to collapse? Did the Governing Body give clear direction regarding our neutrality in world affairs? Can we assure Jehovah's people who are undergoing trials in Babylon that we will continue to support and encourage them?
"BABYLON IS FALLING"
2. As you research using Bible literature, what further information do you find?
2 For nearly two decades after the formation of the Governing Body, Charles Taze Russell and his associates realized that Christendom was part of Satan's organization. However, as you research further, you will find that they gradually came to associate it with political governments. On November 11, 1879, the journal Zion's Watch Tower published an article that explained the scriptures and stated: "The church is only a small body of those who have truly consecrated themselves to Christ, and who are willing to suffer reproach for [truth and] righteousness, and who earnestly desire to do the will of God. This is the church which is spiritual." That spiritual church is represented by the great Babylon.—Read Revelation 17:1, 2.
3. What questions do Bible Students ask themselves when considering whether to take sides in politics? (See accompanying box "Questions to Consider.")
3 Some may feel obligated to support certain political parties because they believe God supports them. They may reason that God wants them to influence world affairs. And yet, many Bible Students wrote letters expressing their loyalty to the Christian congregation. Moreover, many continued to study God's Word regularly and to share it with others in the congregation. They also encouraged each member of the congregation to conduct personal study. How important it is to remain neutral in politics! A person could easily become discouraged if he took a stand on political issues. Since the 1870's, many Christians have found it difficult to stay aloof from politics. But because of their love for truth and their desire to maintain integrity, they have striven to do so.
4. Why did members of the Governing Body allow Jehovah's people to be associated with worldly organizations, including the great Babylon?
4 Also, Bible Students realized that associating with imperfect humans, with their various viewpoints, and allowing themselves to be influenced by the opinions of men would compromise their neutrality. Therefore, on May 12, 1917, and throughout 1918, Bible Students distributed 10,000,000 copies of the tract "Babylon the Great Has Fallen." This tract awakened many nominal Christians and led them to investigate further. However, this action provoked opposition from those in power, and it resulted in severe persecution of Bible Students. We want to imitate the example of those who called upon "the God of comfort." (2 Corinthians 5:29) What can we learn from this? We can learn that the Governing Body allowed Christ's followers to be attacked by Great Babylon, knowing that they would continue to proclaim the truth and defend God's people.
THE FAITHFUL SLAVE'S NEUTRALITY IN WORLD WAR I
5 Did the brothers take a definite stand regarding World War I?
5 In view of the outbreak of World War I, Jehovah revealed to his people the principle of maintaining neutrality. And because of this, we know that Jehovah did not approve of Great Babylon's involvement in that devastating conflict. The experiences of conscientious objectors during World War I demonstrated that people of all nations were willing to sacrifice much rather than participate in warfare. So let us appreciate this important lesson. To understand this fully, Bible Students need to examine the scriptures carefully.
6, 7. (a) How did Bible Students view World War I? (b) Explain why maintaining Christian neutrality is so vital for Bible Students.
6 They realized that Bible Students had taken a firm stand against World War I (1914-1918), which brought them great difficulty. But they also understood that this experience was beneficial to them in a certain way. Let us consider some benefits. A major benefit was that it helped them to clarify their understanding. This led to the publication of the book *The Finished Mystery* in 1918, which strengthened their resolve to remain neutral. It helped faithful Christians to see the importance of being separate from the world. The Spanish flu epidemic of 1918 also played a role. That epidemic caused widespread death, proving how little humans can do when faced with serious problems. Despite these trials, Bible Students remained united and steadfast.
7 In 1914, the Bible Student organization released an eight-reel film called "Photo-Drama of Creation," reaching over 9,000,000 people. They also produced shorter films, using slides and motion pictures. This film presented basic Bible teachings in an interesting way, including the story of the Flood. That event was significant. Imagine how thrilled people were to see this film in 1914—it reached more people than any previous evangelizing effort! Reports show that in 1916, 809,393 people attended public demonstrations throughout the United States, and in 1918, nearly a million—949,444—attended such events. What a witness those Bible Students gave!
8 Did the experiences during World War I cause some loyal ones to question their course?
8 The experiences during that great war caused many loyal ones to feel deeply disturbed, yet they continued to preach, despite facing opposition. This opposition strengthened the determination of the brothers to proclaim the good news. Richard H. Barber wrote about his experience: "We resolved to make greater efforts to distribute literature and continue our work, and we resolved to use the colporteurs liberally. We sent them to Canada and provided them with funds. And I determined to send out some colporteurs in large territories so that they could cover more ground with 'The Finished Mystery.' Brother Rutherford encouraged us to hold large gatherings, sometimes renting entire halls in major American cities, and to send out colporteurs to visit homes and to reach people with the truth."
THE THINGS THAT NEED TO BE REMEMBERED
9. (a) Who were the faithful Christians who faced persecution between 1914 and 1919? (b) And how did Bible Students face persecution, showing their loyalty?
9 These loyal ones were Bible Students during 1914 and 1919 who stood firm with respect to the truth from the Scriptures. And how did they show courage and steadfastness, knowing that imprisonment was possible and that death was also possible? (Luke 13:1) As a group, they proved themselves courageous and showed great endurance. For example, the American branch office sent out a letter on May 30, 1918, informing the Bible Students about the urgent need, and the May 1 issue of The Watch Tower encouraged them to continue. And they showed courage when some were imprisoned for refusing to compromise and others were subjected to much abuse because of their stand. Indeed we see that those who remained loyal to the Bible Students were identified by "Babylon the Great" as being disloyal and deserving of persecution. In harmony with this, it is important that we be courageous and maintain our integrity, and let the organization of Jehovah's Witnesses help us to remain loyal to Babylon the Great.—Read Luke 12:47, 48.
10. Why did Bible Students refuse to compromise?
10 And why did the Bible Students refuse to compromise, even though they knew that doing so would mean avoiding trouble? They felt obligated to obey God. As Christians, they wanted to be neutral. As they saw it, Jehovah God of All Nations had commanded them to preach the good news to all people, and they refused to use their time to support war efforts instead of helping others. Some refused to participate at all, while others compromised to a certain extent.
11. What questions does this raise regarding the attitude of Bible Students?
11 They were deeply affected by the plight of fellow humans, yet they maintained neutrality. However, they applied the principle found at Proverbs 94:20, which says: "As for you, O Jehovah, do not rebuke me." One American judge named James Franklin Bell met with brothers J. F. Rutherford and W. E. Van Amburgh and was impressed by their integrity. He learned that an official from the U.S. Department of Justice had accused them of conspiring to obstruct justice because of their refusal to support war efforts. This judge became sympathetic to the Bible Students. That judge later told Brother Rutherford: "Your position is what President Wilson himself advocated when he said, 'I am trying to make this country too strong to be attacked, and I will make it so!'"
12, 13. (a) What reasons might motivate some humans to take sides in worldly conflicts? (b) How can taking sides distract humans from serving Jehovah? Yes.
12 It is understandable why someone would want to get involved. Some humans who supported the Watch Tower Society were imprisoned. These included Brothers Rutherford and Van Amburgh, along with others. At the time of their imprisonment, one official stated: "The information received from our representatives abroad shows that in Germany…these men have become prominent and influential, and they are using their influence to undermine the morale of the troops and to discourage enlistment. Their activities have caused considerable unrest." (Faith on the March, by A. H. Macmillan, p. 99) That is what happened. Those brothers were imprisoned in Atlanta, Georgia, and the case drew much attention.
13 Furthermore, those brothers made a full defense based on the scriptures and the facts of the case. One American newspaper reported something like this: "A witness testified in court, saying, 'I heard him,' and he identified himself as being associated with the [International Bible Students] Association and declared that his conscience would not allow him to take up arms in war because of his faith in God, and that this was the reason he objected. He said that other men felt the same way.'" This is a fine example. Truly, those brothers courageously defended Jehovah's name and his organization!
BABYLON THE GREAT HAS FALLEN!
14. The clergy used the Scriptures to justify getting involved in World War I, from 1914 to 1919.
14 Malachi 3:1-3 foretold the coming of a class of "sons of Levi," but they were defiled, unable to offer a proper sacrifice. That class appeared from 1914 onward until the end of 1919. (Read.) That class included Jehovah God, who is called "the Lord," and Jesus Christ, who is called "the messenger of the covenant," and they cleansed their temple, whether literally or spiritually. The loyalty and devotion of Jehovah's people have been strengthened by trials and persecution. In 1919, the "loyal slave" was restored and began to feed the household of faith. (Matt. 24:45) Recognizing this helped God's people to remain separate from Babylon the Great. From that time on, the faithful servants of Jehovah have had a greater understanding of his purpose and continue to support his King with wholehearted devotion. Let us be grateful for these faithful servants! [1]
15. How can we know if we are separated from Babylon the Great in order to maintain our integrity?
15 We must constantly examine ourselves to see if we are maintaining our separation from Babylon the Great! For Satan continues to exert influence over Christendom and its followers. Let us always remember to appreciate the provision that Jehovah makes for our spiritual nourishment. (2 Cor. 6:1) Many people today are deeply affected by commercialism. These ones may find it difficult to practice self-control. But with prayer, we can discern what is right. So let us take advantage of every opportunity to help others to exercise self-control and to resist the influence of commercialism!
^ [1] (paragraph 14) The desolation of Jerusalem by Babylon for 70 years illustrates in a powerful way how everything connected with false religion will be destroyed. It also shows why Christians must remain separate from the world. But how does the desolation of Jerusalem relate to everything connected with Christendom? Simply put, the period during which Jerusalem lay desolate under Babylon corresponds to the time when Christendom has been dominated by Babylon the Great. Therefore, we should strive to disassociate ourselves completely from all things connected with Jerusalem while she was desolate, and we should not associate with anything connected with Christendom since 1919.

text:
"Nzyokeai, . . . nakwa ngamũsyokea."—NZEK. 1:3.
MBATHI: 6, 20
1-3. (a) Kwailyĩ ata ĩvinda yĩla Nzekalia wambĩĩe kwathana? (b) Nĩkĩ Yeova weeie andũ make 'mamũsyokee'?
ĨVUKUNĨ ya Nzekalia nĩvaandĩkĩtwe mawoni ma kũsengy'a ala mwathani ũsu wooniw'e. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwooniw'e ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa yĩũlũkĩte, mũndũ mũka ũkunĩkĩwe kĩkavũnĩ, na aka elĩ me na nthwau ta sya ĩsaũ maũlũkĩte kĩsevenĩ. (Nzek. 5:1, 7-9) Nĩkĩ Yeova woonisye mwathani ũsu mawoni ta asu? Mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yailyĩ ata ĩvindanĩ yĩu? Nao mawoni asu ma Nzekalia matonya kũtũtethya ata ũmũnthĩ?
2 Mwaka wa 537 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, waĩ mwaka wa kũtana kwondũ wa andũ ma Yeova. Mwaka ũsu nĩw'o mathaiw'e ĩtina wa myaka 70 me atave nĩ ũsumbĩ wa Mbaviloni. Mavika Yelusaleme oou maĩ na ũthangaau mwingĩ wa kwaka ĩkalũ ĩngĩ na kwambĩĩa kũmũthaitha Yeova. Mwakanĩ wa 536 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, mũsingi wa ĩkalũ nĩwaakiwe. Ĩvinda yĩu andũ "mookĩlilye wasya mũnene, na kĩlonzo nĩkyeew'ĩkie kũasa." (Esa. 3:10-13) Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa mĩthenya o mĩvũthũ amaitha nĩmambĩĩe kũsiĩĩa mwako ũsu. Kĩu nĩkyooaie Aisilaeli ngoo. Kwoou nĩmakolile kwaka ĩkalũ na mathi kũsiany'a na nyũmba syoo na mĩũnda yoo. O na ĩtina wa myaka 16 kuma mũsingi wa ĩkalũ ya Yeova weekĩwa, ĩkalũ yĩyaĩ yaathela. Nũndũ wa ũu andũ ma Ngai maĩ na vata wa kũlilikanw'a kana maĩlĩte kũmũsyokea Yeova na maieka kũsembany'a mũno na maũndũ a moo. Yeova endaa mamũsyokee na mayambĩĩa ĩngĩ kũmũthaitha na ngoo ĩmwe mate na wia.
3 Nĩ kana Ngai alilikany'e andũ make ũndũ ũla mũnene watumie etĩkĩlya Mbaviloni ĩmathasye, atũmie mwathani Nzekalia aneene namo mwakanĩ wa 520 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. Ũalyũlo wa ĩsyĩtwa Nzekalia nĩ "Yeova Nĩwalilikana," na no kwĩthĩwa ũalyũlo ũsu wamalilikanilye ũndũ ũũ ũmwe wa vata na wa w'o. Wamalilikanilye kana o na kau mo ene nĩmoolĩtwe ũndũ Yeova wamatangĩĩte, Yeova ndaĩ aaũlwa nĩmo. (Soma Nzekalia 1:3, 4.) Nĩwamaĩkĩĩthisye kana nĩwesaa kũmatetheesya matũngĩĩe ũthaithi wa w'o, ĩndĩ nĩwasyokie amakany'a vate ngũĩ kana ndemetĩkĩla ethĩwa maimũthũkũma na ngoo mbĩanĩu. Ekai twone ũndũ woni wa thanthatũ na wa mũonza ũla Yeova woonisye Nzekalia wamaamũkisye masyoke wĩanĩ. O na nĩtũkwona ũndũ mawoni asu me elĩ matonya kũtũtetheesya ũmũnthĩ.
NGAI NŨSILĨLAA ALA MOYAA
4. Woni wa thanthatũ wa Nzekalia waĩ ĩũlũ wa kyaũ? Nĩkĩ ĩvuku yĩu wooniw'e yaandĩkĩtwe ngalĩko syelĩ? (Sisya visa wa 1 ĩthangũnĩ ya 21.)
4 Kĩlungu kya 5 kya ĩvuku ya Nzekalia kyambĩĩe na woni ũmwe wa ũsengy'o. (Soma Nzekalia 5:1, 2.) Nzekalia ooniw'e ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa yĩũlũkĩte. Ĩvuku yĩu yaĩ na ũasa wa vuti ta 30 (mita 9) na ũthanthau wa vuti ta 15 (mita 4.5)! Ĩvuku yĩu yaĩ ĩkũnzũe yeteele o kũsomwa. Yaandĩkĩtwe ngalĩko syelĩ ũvoo wa ũsilĩlo. (Nzek. 5:3) Nĩkwĩthĩwa ĩvinda yĩu ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa yaandĩkawa o ngalĩko ĩmwe tũ, no nginya yĩu ya Nzekalia yĩthĩwe yaandĩkĩtwe ũvoo mũito na ũte wa ngũĩ nũndũ yaandĩkĩtwe ngalĩko syelĩ.
5, 6. Yeova osaa ũng'ei ata o na ethĩwa nĩ wa mũthemba wĩva?
5 Soma Nzekalia 5:3, 4. O na kau kĩla mũndũ akaumya ũtalo mbee wa Yeova, ala metanĩaw'a na ĩsyĩtwa yake makaumya ũtalo mũnenange. Ala mamwendete Ngai nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana ũng'ei o na wĩva 'nũvũthasya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai woo.' (Nth. 30:8, 9, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) O na mũndũ akatw'ĩka eonaa e na kĩtumi kĩseũvĩte ata ayũya, twaĩle kũmanya kana ũla wũyaa onanasya ĩtomo yake nĩyo ya vata kwĩ Ngai na kana nĩwendete malĩ mũno vyũ. Ethĩawa aivũthya mwĩao wa Ngai. Ndonaa Yeova e wa vata, o na ndonaa ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩ ya vata.
6 Nĩwoona kana ĩandĩko ya Nzekalia 5:3, 4 yaĩtye "kĩumo . . . kĩkalika nyũmbanĩ ya kĩng'ei, . . . na kĩkekala katĩ wa nyũmba yake, na kĩkamĩmina"? Vai mũndũ ũsiĩĩa ũsilĩlo wa Yeova na ituĩ kana ivulĩ. Vai mũthũkũmi o na ũmwe wake wĩka ũthũku evithĩte na aiema kũmumĩlya nĩ kana amũsilĩle. O na mũndũ akoya na aivitha silikalĩ, anene make wĩanĩ, atumĩa ma kĩkundi, kana asyai, ndesa kũvitha Ngai, nũndũ Ngai ũsu aĩtye kana akaĩkĩĩthya ũng'ei w'onthe nĩwaumĩlw'a methonĩ. (Aevl. 4:13) Twĩw'aa twĩ eanĩe ta kĩ kwĩthĩwa tũtumĩte ndũũ na andũ meũtata ũndũ matonya methĩwe na mĩendele mĩseo "maũndũnĩ onthe"!—Aevl. 13:18.
7. Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũikakwatwe nĩ ũsilĩlo ũla wĩ yĩla ĩvukunĩ ya kũkũnzwa yĩũlũkĩte?
7 Vai ũng'ei o na ũmwe Yeova wendete. Twonaa yĩ ndaĩa nene kwĩkala kwosana na myolooto ya Yeova ya mwĩkalĩle nĩ kana tũikese kũtuma angĩ mavũthya ĩsyĩtwa yake. Tweeka ũu no kwĩthĩwa tũtakakwatwa nĩ ũsilĩlo ũla Yeova ũkaetee ala matũlaa mĩao yake na ngũlũ.
KWĨANĨSYA WĨVĨTO WITŨ "KĨLA MŨTHENYA"
8-10. (a) Kwĩvĩta nĩ kwĩka ata? (b) Nĩ wĩvĩto wĩva Mũsumbĩ Nzetekia ũtaaĩanĩsya?
8 Ũvoo ũla ũatĩĩe yĩla ĩvukunĩ ya kũkũnzwa wĩ na ũkany'o kwa ũla 'wĩvĩtaa ũvũngũ na syĩtwa ya Ngai.' (Nzek. 5:4) Mũndũ eevĩta ethĩawa eeyĩava kana kĩndũ kĩna nĩ kya w'o, kana akeyĩava nũkwĩka kana ndakeka ũndũ mũna.
9 Ti ũndũ mũnini kwĩvĩta na ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova. Kĩu twĩkyona nesa twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mũsumbĩ wa mũthya ũla wasumbĩkie Yelusaleme. Nzetekia nĩweevĩtie na ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova asya kana akamwĩw'aa na kũmũthũkũma mũsumbĩ wa Mbaviloni. Ĩndĩ Nzetekia ndaaĩanĩsya kĩu weeyĩavie. Nũndũ wa ũu Yeova amũsilĩle na ndeto ii: "O tondũ nyie . . . nĩ thayũ, kwa w'o mũndũ ũsu [Nzetekia] akakw'ĩĩa Mbavilonĩ, nthĩ ya mũsumbĩ ũla wamũtw'ĩkĩthisye mũsumbĩ, ĩndĩ mũndũ ũsu avũthĩĩsya wĩvĩto wake na aananga ũtianĩo wake."—Esek. 17:16, BCK.
10 Nũndũ Mũsumbĩ Nzetekia nĩweevĩtĩte na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, Yeova endaa eanĩsye wĩvĩto ũsu. (2 Mav. 36:13) Ĩndĩ Nzetekia ndaaĩanĩsya wĩvĩto wake nũndũ aendie kũmantha ũtethyo Misili nongi kana nĩwuma ungu wa Mbaviloni. Kĩu kĩyaamũtethya.—Esek. 17:11-15, 17, 18.
11, 12. (a) Nĩ wĩvĩto wĩva wa vata vyũ twaaĩvĩta? (b) Twaĩle kwĩkaa ata kĩla mũthenya twasũanĩa wĩvĩto ũla tweevĩtie wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova?
11 Nĩtwoona kana Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa ethukĩĩsye ĩla tũkwĩvĩta. Ndosaa mawĩvĩto ala twĩvĩtĩte ta ũndũ mũnini, na kwoou no nginya tũmeanĩsye ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda atwende. (Sav. 76:11) Vai wĩvĩto wa vata ta ũla mũndũ wĩvĩtaa ĩla ũkwĩyumya amũthũkũmae Yeova. Ĩla ũkwĩvĩta wĩvĩto ũsu ũmũvoyaa Yeova ũkamwĩa kana ũkamũthũkũmaa mavinda onthe kwĩ kwiũ na kwĩ kweũ.
12 Tũtonya ata kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto ũsu tweevĩtĩe Yeova? Ĩtambya yĩla twosaa ĩla twakomana na matatwa manene na manini nĩyaĩle kwonany'a kana nĩtũtw'ĩte kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto witũ wa kũmũtaĩaa Yeova "kĩla mũthenya." (Sav. 61:8) Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũ mũthũkũmaa ĩmwe kana mũsomaa ĩmwe nũtonya kũũvũĩa ngũĩ nthũku. We no wone ũsu ta mwanya wa kwonany'a kana 'nũtanĩaa nzĩa sya Yeova' na ũitila ngũĩ sya mũthemba ũsu? (Nth. 23:26) Kana ethĩwa mũsyĩ kwitũ ti onthe Ngũsĩ, nĩtũmũvoyaa Yeova atũtetheesye tũendeee kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle wa Kĩklĩsto o na ethĩwa vai ũngĩ vau mũsyĩ wĩ na wendi ta witũ? Nĩtũmũvoyaa Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ kĩla mũthenya nĩ kana tũmũtũngĩe mũvea nũndũ wa kũtũtongoesya na kũtwenda? Kĩla mũthenya nĩtũmanthaa ĩvinda ya kũsoma Mbivilia? Maũndũ asu tyo mo tũtonya kwasya twamwathie Yeova ĩla tweeyumisye tũmũthũkũme? No nginya twĩthĩwe twĩ ewi nĩ kana twĩanĩsye wĩvĩto ũsu twamwĩvĩtĩe Yeova. Kũmũthaitha Yeova na ngoo yonthe kwonanasya kana nĩtũmwendete na nĩtweeyumisye vyũ tũtw'ĩke make. Tũithaithaa no kwĩthĩwa nĩkũthaithawa. Tũmũthaithaa Yeova nũndũ nĩtwendete kũmũthaitha. Tweanĩsya kĩla twamwathie tũilea kwona ũseo nũndũ athĩte ala mamũthũkũmaa me aĩkĩĩku ĩvinda ĩseo mũno.—Kũt. 10:12, 13.
13. Woni wa thanthatũ wa Nzekalia wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
13 Woni wa thanthatũ ũla Nzekalia wooniw'e nĩwatũtetheesya twamanya kana ala mamwendete Yeova maĩlĩte kwĩvathana na ũng'ei w'onthe vala wavika na nĩmaĩlĩte kwĩanĩsya kĩla meevĩta. Na nĩtwoona kana Yeova ndaaĩkĩsya Aisilaeli ngoo o na kau mekalaa maimũvĩtĩsya. Nĩwaeleawa kana maĩ na ĩvinda yetu nũndũ mathyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ amaitha. Yeova nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo mũno kwitũ nũndũ nĩwĩanĩasya kĩla wathana, na kwoou no atũtetheesye o naitũ twĩanĩsye kĩla tweevĩta. Ũtethyo ũmwe ũtũnengete nĩ kũtwatha kana o mĩtũkĩ nũkũvetanga ũthũku w'onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Woni wa mũonza ũla Nzekalia wooniw'e nũũtũĩkĩĩthya kana Yeova akeanĩsya watho ũsu.
ŨTHŨKU 'NĨWĨKALĨTW'E VANDŨ VAW'O'
14, 15. (a) Nzekalia ooniw'e kyaũ woninĩ wake wa mũonza? (Sisya visa wa 2 ĩthangũnĩ ya 21.) (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩelekanĩtw'e na ũla mũndũ mũka wĩ kĩla kĩkavũnĩ kĩtĩtwe eva, na nĩkĩ ũkunĩkĩwe vau?
14 Nzekalia amina kwonw'a yĩla ĩvuku ya kũkũnzwa yĩũlũkĩte, eeiwe nĩ mũlaĩka 'okĩlye metho make.' Ookĩlya metho ooniw'e kyaũ? Ooniw'e woni wa mũonza na woninĩ ũsu vaĩ kĩkavũ kĩtĩtwe "eva" kyumĩte kĩthi. (Soma Nzekalia 5:5-8.) Kĩkavũ kĩu kĩyaĩ kĩnini ĩndĩ kĩyaĩ kĩnene mũno na kyaĩ na ngunĩko ya "ĩvulũ." Ngunĩko yakunũwa Nzekalia oonie "mũndũ mũka wĩkalĩte katĩ wa eva." Mũlaĩka amũtavisye kana mũndũ mũka ũsu wĩ kĩkavũnĩ kĩu nĩ "Ũthũku." Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Nzekalia watelemile ĩla woonie mũndũ mũka ũsu aitata kwĩkusũũkya aume vau wavingĩwe! Mũlaĩka ũsu o na ndaananga saa. Atũngie mũndũ mũka ũsu kĩkavũnĩ nthĩnĩ na akĩkunĩka vyũ na ngunĩko ngito mũno. Woni ũsu wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
15 Wĩtũmanyĩsya kana Yeova ndatonya kũmĩĩsya ũthũku o na ũmwe katĩ wa andũ make. Oona ũndũ ũthũku aũsiĩĩaa na ayosa ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ mũno aũvete. (1 Ako. 5:13) Tũi na nzika na kĩu nũndũ ũla mũlaĩka oosie ĩla ngunĩko ya ĩvulũ na mĩtũkĩ akunĩka ĩngĩ kĩla kĩkavũ.
16. (a) Nzekalia oonie kĩla kĩkavũ kyeekanwa nakyo ata? (Sisya visa wa 3 ĩthangũnĩ ya 21.) (b) Ala aka elĩ me na nthwau matwaie kĩkavũ kĩu va?
16 Ĩtina wa Nzekalia kwonw'a kĩkavũ, asyokie oonw'a aka elĩ me na nthwau syĩ na vinya ta sya ĩsaũ. (Soma Nzekalia 5:9-11.) Aka asu elĩ maĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũla mũndũ mũka wakunĩkĩwe kĩkavũnĩ. Aka asu matheeie na nthwau syoo moosa kĩla kĩkavũ kĩ na "Ũthũku" na maũlũka nakyo. Makĩtwaie va? Matwaie kĩkavũ kĩu kĩ na Ũthũku "nthĩ ya Sinali," kana Mbaviloni. Nĩkĩ matwaie kĩkavũ kĩu Mbaviloni?
17, 18. (a) Nĩkĩ "Ũthũku" weeiwe 'vandũ vaw'o' nĩ Sinali? (b) Twaĩlĩte kwĩka ũtwi wĩva ĩũlũ wa ũthũku?
17 Aisilaeli ala matwĩe ĩvinda ya Nzekalia nĩmakwatisye nĩkĩ nthĩ ya Sinali yaĩ vandũ vaseo va kũtwaa Ũthũku. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu Nzekalia na Ayuti ala angĩ nĩmeesĩ ũndũ Sinali, kana Mbaviloni, yausũĩte ũthũku. Nĩkwĩthĩwa kũu nĩkw'o meanĩe, no nginya wĩthĩe me kũu meekĩaa kĩthito kingĩ kĩla mũthenya maikese kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũvuku ũla waĩ nthĩ ĩsu ya andũ matamwĩsĩ Ngai, na maitata maikese kũthaitha mĩvw'anano tamo. Vate nzika, woni ũsu nĩwamekĩie vinya nũndũ wamaĩkĩĩthisye kana Yeova ndaketĩkĩla ũthaithi wake ũvukw'e!
18 Ĩndĩ woni ũsu nĩwalilikanilye Ayuti kana maĩ na kĩanda kya kũtata ũndũ matonya maikavukye ũthaithi wa w'o. Ũthũku ndwĩsa kwĩtĩkĩlw'a ũlike na ũitũa katĩ wa andũ ma Yeova. Ũseũvyo wa Ngai nĩ mũtheu na Ngai witũ wĩ wendo atũsũvĩaa twĩ vau, na kwoou twĩ na kĩanda kya kũtata ũndũ tũtonya tũwĩkalye wĩ mũtheu. Ithyĩ nĩtwĩthĩawa na wendi wa kwĩkalya ũseũvyo wa Yeova wĩ mũtheu? Ũthũku o na wĩva ndwĩsa kũekwa katĩ wa andũ ma Yeova.
ANDŨ ALA METHEETYE NĨMAMŨTAĨAA YEOVA
19. Ala mawoni ma ũsengy'a Nzekalia wooniw'e metũtethya ata?
19 Woni wa thanthatũ na wa mũonza wa Nzekalia wĩ na ũkany'o ũte wa ngũĩ kwondũ wa ala me mũtuo wa kwĩka kĩla kĩtaĩle. Mawoni asu metũlilikany'a kana Yeova ndesa kũmĩĩsya ũthũku. Ala mamũthaithaa na ngoo ntheu no nginya mamene ũthũku na ngoo yonthe. O na Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ atũmĩĩte mĩsoa ĩsu kũtũĩkĩĩthya ũndũ ũmwe wa vata. Ũndũ ũsu nĩ kana tweekĩa kĩthito twĩthĩwe na mwĩkalĩle ũla waĩle, Ngai akatũsũvĩaa na tũikekalaa na wia wa kũkwatwa nĩ kĩla kĩumo kĩthũku. Vandũ va ũu akatanĩaa kũtũathima. Kĩthito kĩla tweekĩa twĩyĩkalye twĩ atheu o na kau nthĩ yusĩe ũthũku, kĩikaleaa kwĩthĩwa na mosyao maseo. Ndũkaye nzika o na vanini kana kwa vinya wa Yeova no tũsinde! Ĩndĩ twĩsĩ ata kana ũthaithi wa w'o ndwĩsa kũthela o na kau nthĩ ĩno yusĩe andũ matekaa kwenda kwa Ngai? Na twĩsĩ ata kana Yeova nũkũendeea kũsũvĩa ũseũvyo wake kavindanĩ kaa tweteele ũla thĩna mũnene? Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩneeneete makũlyo asu.

translation:
"Keep on seeking, . . . and keep on asking."—NZek. 1:3.
THURSDAY: 6, 20
1-3. (a) Why did Ezekiel need to be strong despite what he faced? (b) How does Jehovah view his faithful servants as "searchers"?
Ezekiel's vision was written so that people could understand its meaning when the appointed time came. For example, we can understand the vision about boiling a pot, a man with a writing stylus, and a scroll as being related to Jerusalem's destruction. (Nz. 5:1, 7-9) How did Jehovah show them what would happen? What lessons did ancient Israel learn from those visions? And how can Ezekiel's warnings help us today?
2 In 537 B.C.E., an important year arrived for Jehovah's people. That year marked the end of 70 years of exile in Babylon. The Jews returned to Jerusalem and began rebuilding the city and especially worshiping Jehovah again. In 536 B.C.E., the foundation of the temple was laid. However, many people were "joyful, yet the heart of the masses did not feel relief." (Isa. 3:10-13) Because of their past mistakes, they had reasons to be cautious. This saddened loyal Israelites. They saw how slowly the building progressed and how little interest some showed in separating themselves from the surrounding nations. After 16 years, the foundation of Jehovah's temple was completed, but the temple itself remained unfinished. Many of God's people felt discouraged and wondered whether they would ever finish worshiping Jehovah acceptably and restoring true worship. Jehovah encouraged searchers and gave them further support to continue worshiping him loyally and zealously.
3 But God used the great power he possessed to inspire Zerubbabel to take the lead in 520 B.C.E. The name Zerubbabel means "Jehovah Is a Restorer," and this name appropriately described what he accomplished—restoring something that had been destroyed. He restored confidence in the fact that Jehovah could fulfill his purpose, and Jehovah proved himself able to do so. (Read Zechariah 1:3, 4.) It reminded them that even when things seemed impossible, they should not give up hope or listen to discouraging voices. Let us examine what lessons we can learn from the example Zerubbabel set and how Jehovah supported him. And let us see how those lessons can help us remain courageous.
GOD INSPIRED HIM WITH SPIRIT
4 What questions will Zechariah answer? What vision did he receive, and what does it teach us? (Consider paragraph 21.)
4 In the fifth vision, Zechariah saw something that represented a new challenge. (Read Zechariah 5:1, 2.) Zechariah received a vision of a flying scroll. This scroll was about 30 feet [9 m] long and 15 feet [4.5 m] wide! The scroll was open, meaning it was ready to be read. It was written on both sides, indicating its importance. (Ze. 5:3) It is said that this flying scroll was like a measuring line, and the spirit of Zerubbabel was measured with it, showing that he was being assessed.
5, 6. What does Jehovah look for, and why is this important?
5 Read Zechariah 5:3, 4. And just as everyone wants to know whether they have Jehovah's approval, so too they want to know whether his servant has his approval. But how can we show God that we are eager to "honor his name"? (Prov. 30:8, 9, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) And if someone makes a mistake despite having good intentions, we need to determine whether his error is due to a lack of love for God and whether he disrespects sacred things. His actions reveal what is in his heart. Jehovah values loyalty, and he values his name.
6 Does Zechariah 5:3, 4's description of "a basket…standing between two baskets, and another basket upon it" mean that some people do not fully support Jehovah's organization and its work? Does a supervisor and his companion act dishonestly and exploit others? And if someone steals and repents, confesses his sins, makes restitution, or pleads for forgiveness, does this mean that God overlooks all his wrongdoing and excuses him?—Acts 4:13. We should be careful not to use our authority over fellow believers to take advantage of them and to practice "oppression"!—Acts 13:18.
7. Should we worry about being influenced by disloyal individuals who may try to mislead us?
7 How can we be sure that Jehovah supports us? We see it when we strive to cooperate with Jehovah's righteous standards and when we endeavor to honor his name. Let us therefore be determined not to let disloyalty influence us, but instead trust in Jehovah and adhere to his principles.
TO UNDERSTAND THE EXPRESSION "EVERY EFFORT"
8-10. (a) What does it mean to exert effort? (b) Why did ancient Israel fail to demonstrate genuine effort?
8 The expression "exerting effort" refers to striving zealously to please God. (Zeph. 5:4) A person exerts effort when he works hard at something, perseveres despite difficulties, or diligently seeks improvement.
9 It is vital to exert effort in serving Jehovah. To illustrate this, consider the example of the builders who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls. Zechariah exerted effort in supporting Jehovah's work and in encouraging the builders to finish the wall despite opposition from Babylonians. So Zechariah demonstrated genuine effort. Therefore, Jehovah gave him this promise: "This is what Jehovah has said to you, 'Because they have acted contrary to me…that man [Zechariah] will go to Babylon.'"—Ezek. 17:16, CEB.
10 Because King Zedekiah exerted effort against Jehovah, Jehovah allowed his efforts to come to nothing. (2 Kings 36:13) Zedekiah demonstrated his lack of effort by turning away from seeking guidance from the prophet Jeremiah and by making an alliance with Babylon. This proved disastrous.—Ezek. 17:11-15, 17, 18.
11, 12. (a) What reasons might we have for slacking off in our service? (b) How can we make sure that we continue to exert ourselves in order to honor Jehovah?
11 We should examine ourselves to see whether Jehovah is pleased with our efforts. Often, we may feel that we are exerting effort, yet we may not be accomplishing much. (Ps. 76:11) However, exertion of effort involves doing what pleases Jehovah. If you exert yourself, Jehovah will notice and will bless your efforts, enabling you to accomplish more than you could on your own.
12 Should we hesitate to ask Jehovah to help us exert ourselves? It is understandable if we struggle when facing great difficulties and feel unable to continue to exert ourselves in honoring Jehovah "day after day." (Ps. 61:8) For example, a faithful Christian or a zealous publisher may sometimes feel overwhelmed. Do you ever feel that way—that you are unable to 'give attention to Jehovah' and that your hope is dwindling? (Prov. 23:26) Or perhaps circumstances prevent you from attending meetings regularly or from participating fully in the ministry? Do you imitate Asa, who sought Jehovah's help each day, so that he could be strengthened and encouraged? Day after day, do we take time to read the Bible? Are there things we can stop doing so that we can show Jehovah how grateful we are for his blessings? By continuing to exert ourselves in our service to Jehovah, we demonstrate our love for him and prove that we are determined to remain loyal. We can also find refreshment by exerting ourselves. The more we seek Jehovah, the more we will desire to seek him. As we exert ourselves, we will experience the joy of seeing others appreciate the truth.—Acts 10:12, 13.
13 What did Nehemiah's prayer teach them?
13 Nehemiah's earnest prayer taught them to acknowledge their sins and to pray for Jehovah's continued favor despite all the opposition they faced and despite their inability to carry out their work. They realized that Jehovah had shown mercy to Israel in times past and had delivered them from enemies. They understood that their present distress was due to their own unfaithfulness. Jehovah is always willing to listen to us and to strengthen us as we exert ourselves in our ministry. One way he strengthens us is by helping us to see how our efforts benefit others. Nehemiah's courageous stand teaches us that Jehovah supports those who support him.
THE IMPORTANCE OF 'EXERTING YOURSELF'
14, 15. (a) What question did Nehemiah ask himself when facing opposition? (See accompanying picture on page 21.) (b) How does this relate to what each of us may feel when we meet apathy, and why should we not be discouraged?
14 Nehemiah admitted feeling deeply distressed, saying that he became like "one exhausted." What caused him to become exhausted? He felt overwhelmed because the opposers kept saying, "Let us rebuild the wall." (Read Nehemiah 5:5-8.) This expression likely referred to a plot to attack them. The term "wall" here seems to symbolize their strength. The opposers were trying to weaken Nehemiah by making him feel helpless. He refused to let such feelings paralyze him. Instead, he strengthened himself. Let us imitate his example and not give up when we encounter apathy or opposition. Strengthen yourself and continue preaching zealously! Help your brothers and sisters to remain courageous and steadfast. What will help us to do so?
15 We can be confident that Jehovah empowers those who trust in Him to face trials. True discouragement comes from Satan, who tries to make us feel inadequate and useless. (1 Cor. 5:13) So, whenever we find ourselves becoming disheartened, let us remember that Satan is behind our negative feelings and resolve to fight them.
16. (a) What question did Nehemiah ask himself regarding the wall? (See accompanying picture on page 21.) (b) Why were some particularly disturbed by the rebuilding of the wall?
16 When Nehemiah considered the condition of the wall, he carefully examined the breaches and observed how easily enemies could enter through them. (Read Nehemiah 5:9-11.) These breaches represented vulnerabilities that would allow an enemy to exploit weaknesses. Some were especially troubled by the rebuilding of the wall because they associated it with "trouble" and saw it as a threat to their interests. Why were they disturbed by the rebuilding of the wall? They viewed Babylon—or "Great Babylon"—as representing their security and prosperity. Were they right to view the rebuilding of the wall as a threat to Babylon?
17, 18. (a) How was "Babylon" actually "the chiefs of the people" in Nehemiah's time? (b) How can we discern the source of discouragement?
17 The Israelites who opposed Nehemiah's work identified Babylon with those who sought to prevent God's people from rebuilding. In their eyes, Babylon—or Great Babylon—represented everything that hindered the worship of Jehovah. It is important to recognize that this opposition came from individuals who benefited from keeping God's people weak and discouraged, and who wanted to disrupt their spiritual progress. Therefore, when we experience discouragement, let us remember that Jehovah strengthens those who put their faith in Him!
18 So, if we find ourselves feeling defeated, let us examine whether our feelings stem from external pressures or from our own imperfections. Discouragement arises when we allow ourselves to focus on what we cannot accomplish rather than on what we can. God's purpose will prevail, and our loving Father wants to help us succeed. But do we allow ourselves to benefit from Jehovah's strength and support? Discouragement and negativity have no place among God's people.
PEOPLE WHO PLEASED JEHOVAH
19. How did Nehemiah's contemporaries respond to his efforts?
19 Some were supportive and others were hostile toward Nehemiah, yet he remained steadfast in his determination to rebuild the wall. These men recognized that Jehovah was able to frustrate the schemes of his enemies. Those who feared God and loved righteousness continued to pursue their work despite the obstacles. For example, King Asa of Judah led his people in seeking God's help. This reminds us that when we face trials, we can rely on Jehovah to strengthen us and protect us from all harm. Others conspired against them. Every time we make a decision, let us ask ourselves whether it will please God or whether it will hinder His work. Let us always seek Jehovah's guidance and favor so that we may succeed! Are we willing to give up personal interests and ambitions in order to advance God's Kingdom? And are we confident that Jehovah will continue to bless our efforts to uphold his standards? This lesson is very meaningful and practical.

text:
"Ĩvia, wĩa wake nĩ mwĩanĩu; nũndũ nzĩa syake syonthe nĩ ndũngalu."—KŨT. 32:4.
MBATHI: 2, 11
1. Avalaamu oonanisye ata nĩwaĩkĩĩte vyũ kana Yeova asilaa katĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
AVALAAMU akũlilye atĩĩ: "Mũsili wa nthĩ yonthe ndakeka ũlũngalu?" (Mwa. 18:25) Aikũlya ĩkũlyo yĩu aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova nũkũsilĩla ndũa ya Sotomo na Ngomola ũndũ vaĩlĩte vyũ. Avalaamu aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana Yeova ndesa "kũaa alũngalu vamwe na ala athũku." Nĩweesĩ kana yĩsilya ta yĩu yaĩ "kũasa" na mosũanĩo ma Yeova. Ĩtina wa myaka 400 ũu, Yeova aeleisye ũndũ we mwene ũilyĩ asya: "Ĩvia, wĩa wake nĩ mwĩanĩu; nũndũ nzĩa syake syonthe nĩ ndũngalu: Ngai wa kĩthito na ũte na naĩ, nake nĩ wa w'o na mũlũngalu."—Kũt. 31:19; 32:4.
2. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Yeova ndesa kwelelũkya sila wa katĩ?
2 Nĩkĩ Avalaamu ũtaĩ na nzika kana ĩvinda yonthe Yeova asilaa katĩ? Nĩkwĩthĩwa vai ũngĩ mũlũngalu vyũ na wĩ ũsili wa katĩ ta Yeova. O na nthĩnĩ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania, mavinda maingĩ ndeto ĩla ialyũlĩtwe "ũsili wa katĩ" na ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "ũlũngalu" ikothaa kũatĩanĩa. Kwa ũkuvĩ, vala ve sila wa katĩ no nginya vethĩwe ũlũngalu. Kwoou nũndũ Yeova nĩwe mũlũngalu vyũ, ĩvinda yonthe asilaa katĩ. O na ĩngĩ, Ndeto yake yaĩtye kana "nĩwendete ũlũngalu na ũsili wa katĩ."—Sav. 33:5.
3. Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ andũ ũmũnthĩ mathĩnaw'a vate kĩtumi.
3 Kũmanya kana Yeova asilaa katĩ ĩvinda yonthe nĩkũkiakiasya ala me ngoo nzeo nũndũ nthĩ ĩno yusũĩte ũsili ũte wa katĩ. Nĩkwĩthĩwa nthĩ ĩilyĩ ũu, andũ amwe nĩmesaa kũthĩnw'a mũno nũndũ wa mavĩtyo matekĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, amwe nĩmekaw'a yela nũndũ wa kwilĩĩlwa mavĩtyo mataaĩka na mayovwa myaka mingĩ. Mesaa kũtetheka ĩla ĩkoani yoo yasilwa ĩngĩ na ũkunĩkĩli wa mwanya ta ũla wa DNA woonany'a kana mayaĩ mavĩtyo. O na kau syovo ta isu nitumaa mũndũ athĩna na ayĩw'a woo mũno, ve kũthĩnw'a kũngĩ kũtonya kũtuma Aklĩsto mew'a ta matomĩĩsya.
KĨKUNDINĨ
4. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtonya kũtuma mũĩkĩĩo wa Mũklĩsto ũtatĩka?
4 Aklĩsto nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana andũ ala mate kĩkundinĩ no mamathĩny'e o na vate kĩtumi. Ĩndĩ mũĩkĩĩo witũ nũtatĩkaa ĩla tweew'a ta tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle nĩ Mũklĩsto ũngĩ kĩkundinĩ, kana ĩla twoona ũsili wa katĩ ta ũtanaatĩĩwa. We wĩka ata ũkesilya nĩ ta ve ũndũ ũtaĩle ũendeee nthĩnĩ wa kĩkundi, kana wĩka ata ũkesilya mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa nũkwĩkĩte ũndũ ũtaĩle? Ũu no ũtume ũlulutĩka?
5. Nĩkĩ Mũklĩsto ũtaĩle kũseng'a oona, kana eekwa, ũndũ ũtaĩle kĩkundinĩ?
5 Nũndũ ithyonthe twĩ ene naĩ na mavinda maingĩ nĩtũvĩtasya, nĩtwĩthĩawa twĩsĩ kana nĩvatonyeka tũkekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle kĩkundinĩ kana ethĩwa ti ũu, ithyĩ ene tũkeka Aklĩsto ala angĩ ũndũ ũtaĩle. (1 Yoa. 1:8) O na kau ũsu ti thĩna wĩthĩawa mavinda maingĩ, Aklĩsto ala aĩkĩĩku maiseng'aa na mayĩtĩkĩlaa kũlulutĩka ĩla moona thĩna ta ũsu. Kwoou ti ũsengy'o kwona Yeova atũnengete motao nthĩnĩ wa Ndeto yake, ala matonya kũtũtetheesya tũendeee kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku o na ĩla tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle nĩ angĩ kĩkundinĩ.—Sav. 55:12-14.
6, 7. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtaĩle mwana-a-asa ũmwe weekiwe nthĩnĩ wa kĩkundi, na nĩ kyaũ kyamũtetheeisye omĩanĩsye na thĩna ũsu?
6 Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Willi Diehl. Mwana-a-asa Diehl athũkũmie e mũĩkĩĩku Mbetheli ya Bern, Switzerland, kuma mwaka wa 1931. Mwakanĩ wa 1946 nĩweetiwe kĩlasi kya nyanya kya Sukulu ya Ngileati, ĩla yaĩ New York, Amelika. Auma sukulu ekalangile na atw'ĩkĩthw'a mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko nthĩ ya Switzerland. Ngewanĩ yake Mwana-a-asa Diehl aeleetye ũũ: "Twĩ Mwei wa 5, mwaka wa 1949, nĩnaeleisye ovisi wa Bern kana nĩnĩvangie kũtwaana." Ovisi wa Bern wamũsũngĩie ata? Wamwĩie atĩĩ: "Ndwĩtiĩwa kĩanda o na kĩmwe eka o kwĩthĩwa wĩ vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda." Mwana-a-asa Diehl aendeee kũelesya ũũ: "Ndyaanengwa ĩngĩ mwanya wa kumya maũvoo . . . Aingĩ nĩmaekie kũtũkethya, na matũkuaa ta twĩ atenge."
7 Mwana-a-asa Diehl eekie ata thĩna ũsu wamũkwata? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩtweesĩ kana Maandĩko maivatanĩte kũtwaana, na kwoou twaendeeie kũmũvoya Yeova na kũmwĩkwatya." Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, ala matumĩte Mwana-a-asa Diehl athĩna ũu nĩmatetheeiw'e mavĩndũa mawoni moo mathũku ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano, na ĩndĩ Mwana-a-asa Diehl atũngĩwa ianda ila waĩ nasyo. Yeova nĩwamũathimie mũno nũndũ wa kũendeea kwĩkala e mũĩkĩĩku. * Nũseo tũkekũlya ũũ: 'Nyie ngekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle ta ũsu no nĩendeee kwĩthĩwa na woni mũseo o ta mwana-a-asa ũsu? No nũmĩĩsye na ndyeteela Yeova alũnge maũndũ, kana nambĩĩa kwĩyũkitĩa?'—Nth. 11:2; soma Mika 7:7.
8. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma twona ithyĩ ene kana mũndũ ũngĩ ta wĩkĩtwe ũndũ ũtaĩle ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa ti w'o vailyĩ?
8 Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, mavinda angĩ nũtonya kwona ta wĩkĩtwe ũndũ ũtaĩle kana mũndũ ũngĩ kĩkundinĩ ta wĩkĩtwe ũndũ ũtaĩle, ĩndĩ wesa kũatĩĩa ũyĩthĩa ũu ti w'o vailyĩ. Ti vinya kwĩthĩwa na mawoni ta asu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ no kwĩthĩwa tũtanaelewa nesa kĩla kĩendeeie, kana o tũkethĩwa tũtesĩ maũndũ onthe ala makonetye ũndũ ũla wĩkiwe. Ĩndĩ o na twĩthĩwe nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kĩla kĩendeeie kana tũyĩsĩ, twaĩle kũmũvoya Yeova na kũmwĩkwatya, na tũyĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku. Kwĩka ũu no kũtũtetheesye 'tũikamũnyungunyĩsye Yeova.'—Soma Nthimo 19:3.
9. Nĩ ngewa syĩva tũũneenea nthĩnĩ wa ĩsomo yĩĩ na yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
9 Ekai twĩlilikany'e ngewa itatũ syĩ Mbivilianĩ ikwonany'a ũndũ athũkũmi amwe ma Yeova meekiwe maũndũ mataĩle nĩ athaithi ala angĩ. Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩneenea ngewa ya Yosevu, ũla waĩ nzũkũũkũ ya Avalaamu. Ngewanĩ ĩsu nĩtũkwona ũndũ wathĩniw'e nĩ ana-a-ĩthe. Nayo ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩtũkwona ũndũ Yeova weekanie na Mũsumbĩ Aavu wa Isilaeli, vamwe na kĩla kyaendeeie ĩla mũtũmwa Vetelo waĩ ndũanĩ ya Silia yeetawa Andiokia. Ĩla tũendeee kũneenea ngewa isu, sisya maũndũ ma vata ala matonya kũũtetheesya ndũkalulutĩke na matonya kũũtetheesya ũsũvĩe ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova, na mũno mũno ethĩwa nũkwona ta wĩkĩtwe ũndũ ũtaĩle.
ŨNDŨ YOSEVU WATHĨNIW'E MANA
10, 11. (a) Yosevu athĩniw'e ata vate kĩtumi? (b) Yosevu akwatie mwanya wa kwĩka ata e kolokolonĩ?
10 Yosevu aĩ mũthũkũmi mũĩkĩĩku wa Yeova. Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwathĩniw'e mana nĩ andũ, na kũthũkya ũvoo amwe mamũthĩnisye nĩ ana-a-ĩthe. Yosevu angĩe kũvikya myaka 20, ana-a-ĩthe nĩmamwosie mamũthoosya ta ngombo. Ala mamũthooie mamũtwaie Misili. (Mwa. 37:23-28; 42:21) E kũu ũeninĩ nĩwesie kwilĩĩlwa mavĩtyo ũtekĩte. Atw'ĩkie atĩ endaa kũkwata kĩveti kyeene na vinya, na nũndũ wa ũu ekw'a kolokolonĩ o na ataũngamĩtw'e kotinĩ etetee. (Mwa. 39:17-20) Yosevu ekalile e ngombo na e mũvungwa kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ta 13. Nĩ maũndũ meva me ngewanĩ ĩsu ya Yosevu matonya kũtũtetheesya ĩla tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle nĩ mũndũ kĩkundinĩ?
11 Yosevu nĩwesie kũkwata mwanya wa kũelesya mũvungwa moovetwe ĩmwe thĩna wake. Mũvungwa ũsu atanamba kwovwa eethĩawa e mũnene wa anengani ma mbinyu ma mũsumbĩ. Maendeee o na kyovo kyoo, mũthenya ũmwe mũnengani ũsu wa mbinyu nĩwaotie, na Yosevu amũalyũlĩla ĩ ndoto avuanĩw'e nĩ Ngai. Yosevu aeleisye mũvungwa ũsu kana nũkũtũngwa ĩngĩ wĩanĩ ũla watethasya nyũmbanĩ ya ũsumbĩ ya Valao. Ĩla Yosevu waeleasya ũalyũlo wa ndoto ĩsu nĩw'o wakwatie mwanya wa kũelesya mathĩna make. Ve maũndũ ma vata tũkwĩmanyĩsya twasũanĩa kĩla Yosevu watavisye mũvungwa ũsu vamwe na kĩla ũtaatinda aimũelesya ĩũlũ wa mathĩna make.—Mwa. 40:5-13.
12, 13. (a) Ndeto ila Yosevu watavisye mũnengani wa mbinyu sionany'a ata kana ndaneenaa ta mũndũ wĩkĩte kwĩtĩkĩla athĩnw'e avindĩtye? (b) Nĩ maũndũ meva Yosevu ũtaatinda aiweta ĩla waeleasya ũla mũnengani wa mbinyu kĩla kyamũkwatĩte?
12 Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 40:14, 15. Nĩwoona kana Yosevu aĩtye eekie 'kũywa'? Kĩu kĩonany'a kana eekiwe ũndũ ũtaĩle. O na nĩwawetie kana eekĩte kwilĩĩlwa mavĩtyo ala matumĩte ovwa. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi weeie mũnengani wa mbinyu elilikana amũwete kwĩ Valao. Endaa ata aimwĩa ũu? Aeleisye kana eekaa ũu nĩ kana 'eumw'a nyũmbanĩ ĩsu.'
13 We Yosevu aneenaa ta mũndũ wĩkĩte kwĩtĩkĩla athĩnw'e avindĩtye? Aiee, ti w'o. Nĩweesĩ nesa kana ve maũndũ kauta weekĩtwe mataĩle. Nĩkyo kĩtumi waeleisye ũla mũnengani wa mbinyu ũw'o wa maũndũ ala mamũkwatĩte, ayĩkwatya kana nũtonya kũmũtetheesya. Ĩndĩ vai vandũ Maandĩko mawetete kana Yosevu aatavya mũndũ, o na ũ Valao mwene, kana ana-a-ĩthe nĩmo mamũyie. O na ĩla ana-a-ĩthe mookie Misili na meew'ana nake, Valao amanengie ũtũo na amea matanĩe "ũseo wa nthĩ yonthe" ya Misili.—Mwa. 45:16-20.
14. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũikese kũneenea angĩ naĩ o na ethĩwa nĩtweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle?
14 Ĩla Mũklĩsto woona ta wĩkĩtwe ũndũ ũtaĩle, nĩwaĩle kwĩsũvĩa ndakese kũnyaĩĩkya nzukũ. Ti ũthũku kwĩtya ũtethyo kũla kwĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi kana kũneena namo ethĩwa nĩtwamanya kana ve ũmwe nthĩnĩ wa kĩkundi wĩkĩte naĩ ngito. (Ali. 5:1) Ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ no tũmine thĩna ũla twĩ naw'o na mwana-a-asa tũteũtavya angĩ, o na atumĩa, ethĩwa ĩvĩtyo yĩla yĩkĩtwe ti naĩ ngito. (Soma Mathayo 5:23, 24; 18:15.) Ekai tũatĩĩae myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩla thĩna ta ũsu waumĩla. Tweeka ũu, mavinda angĩ nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩa kaĩ o na vai ũndũ mũthũku twĩĩkĩtwe, no ithyĩ tũnesilasya ũu! O na tũkatanaa mũno nũndũ tũikethĩwa tũnathũkĩĩsya maũndũ kwa kwanangĩa angĩ ĩsyĩtwa. Lilikana kana, wĩthĩwe wĩ mũvĩtĩsye kana ndwĩ mũvĩtĩsye, kũneenea angĩ naĩ kũyĩsa kwaĩlya maũndũ. Twaendeea kwĩthĩwa twĩ aĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova na kwa ana-a-asa maitũ, tũikeka ũndũ ta ũsu. Mũandĩki wa Savuli nũwetete mũndũ "ũla ũendaa na mĩendele myaĩlu." Aĩtye kana "nĩ ũla ũtasukanaa na ũĩmĩ wake, kana kwĩka mũnyanyae naĩ, kana kwĩtĩkĩla ndeto sya kĩvũthya ĩũlũ wa mũtũi wake."—Sav. 15:2, 3; Yak. 3:5.
NGWATANĨO YAKU NA YEOVA NĨYO YA VATA VYŨ
15. Yosevu aathimiwe ata nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na Yeova?
15 Ve ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata mũnango tũkwĩmanyĩsya twasũanĩa ngwatanĩo ĩla Yosevu waĩ nayo na Yeova. Myakanĩ ĩsu yonthe 13 Yosevu wathĩnie, nĩwatataa kwona maũndũ ũndũ Yeova ũmonaa. (Mwa. 45:5-8) Ndaamũtũla Yeova mũtĩ nongi nũndũ wa kĩla kyamũkwatĩte. O na kau ndaĩ olwa nĩ mathĩna ala woonete, ndaaĩtĩkĩla kwoveea ũthatu ngoonĩ. Na ũndũ ũla mũnene nĩ kana ndaaeka mawonzu ma ala angĩ na mavĩtyo ala mamwĩkĩte mamwanangĩe ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova. Kwoou nũndũ Yosevu nĩwaendeeie kwĩkala e mũĩkĩĩku, nĩweeyoneie kw'oko kwa Yeova kũilũnga maũndũ, na nĩwoonie aimũathima vamwe na mũsyĩ woo.
16. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmũthengeea Yeova mũnango ĩla tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle nĩ mũndũ kĩkundinĩ?
16 O naitũ nĩtwaĩle kũsũvĩaa ngwatanĩo yitũ vamwe na Yeova na tũimyonaa yĩ ya vata. Mawonzu ala ana-a-asa methĩawa namo mayaĩle kũtuma twananga ngwatanĩo yitũ vamwe na Ngai ũla tũmwendete na tũmũthaithaa. (Alo. 8:38, 39) Vandũ va ũu, ĩla tweekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle nĩ mũndũ kĩkundinĩ, ekai tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ya Yosevu. Twaĩle kũendeea kũmũthengeea Yeova na kwona maũndũ ũndũ we ũmonaa. Na ethĩwa nĩtwatata a vaitũ kũatĩĩa myolooto ĩla yĩ Maandĩkonĩ nĩ kana tũlũnge maũndũ na nĩvaemela, twaĩle kũekea Yeova ũndũ ũsu tũĩkĩĩte vyũ kana akalũnga maũndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩla ũkwona yaĩle na kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle.
MWĨKWATYE "MŨSILI WA NTHĨ YONTHE"
17. Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũmũĩkĩĩte ũla "Mũsili wa nthĩ yonthe"?
17 Nthĩ ĩno nthũku ĩtesie kũvetwa, tũiema kwona ithyĩ ene kana angĩ mayĩkwa maũndũ mataĩle. Mavinda amwe ithyĩ ene nĩtũtonya kũsũanĩa nĩtwĩkĩtwe ũndũ ũtaĩle kĩkundinĩ kana tũkona mũnyanyae witũ ta weekwa ũndũ ũtaĩle. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka kĩkundinĩ o na kau wĩkĩkaa mavinda mavũthũ mũno. Ĩndĩ ndwaĩle kũeka ũndũ ũsu ũtume ũlulutĩka. (Sav. 119:165) Vandũ va kũlulutĩka, twaĩlĩte kũendeea kũmũthũkũma Ngai twĩ aĩkĩĩku na tũimũvoya tũmwĩkwatĩtye. O na ĩngĩ, twaĩle kũmanya kana ĩla ũndũ mũna weekĩka, nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũtesĩ nesa maũndũ onthe ala makonetye ũndũ ũsu wĩkiwe. Na ĩndĩ tũikolwe kana nũndũ twĩ ene naĩ, no kwĩthĩwa ne ithyĩ twĩkie kwona maũndũ kwa nzĩa ĩla ĩtaĩlĩte. O tondũ twoona ngewanĩ ya Yosevu, vai vata wa kũneenea angĩ naĩ ĩla thĩna waumĩla nũndũ kwĩka ũu kwĩkaa kwimbya maũndũ. Ũndũ wa mũthya nĩ kana ti ũseo kwĩyũkitĩa ĩndĩ nũseo tũtw'e vyũ kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku, na tũyeteela Yeova twĩ na wũmĩĩsyo twĩsĩ kana nũkũlũnga maũndũ. Tweeka ũu, Yeova ndakaema kũtana na kũtũathima o tondũ waathimie Yosevu. Vate nzika, ĩvinda yonthe Yeova, ũla nĩwe "Mũsili wa nthĩ yonthe," akeekaa ũla waĩle, nũndũ "nzĩa syake syonthe nĩ ndũngalu."—Mwa. 18:25; Kũt. 32:4.
18. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
18 Ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩtũũneenea ngewa ingĩ ilĩ syĩ Mbivilianĩ sya andũ meekiwe maũndũ mataĩle nĩ athaithi angĩ ma Yeova. Kũneenea ngewa isu nĩkũũtwony'a ũndũ kwĩnyivya na kwĩthĩwa twĩyũmbanĩtye tũekee angĩ kũtũtetheeasya twĩthĩwe na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũsili wa katĩ.
^ kal. 7 No ũsome ngewa ĩno ya Willi Diehl, "Yehova Ni Mungu Wangu Nitakayemtumaini," ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 01/11/1991.

translation:
"Indeed, His ways are wonderful; and His works are all equitable."—Ps. 32:4.
FOOTNOTES: 2, 11
1. Would Balaam have been willing to act wickedly if Jehovah had not led him? (Consider what this teaches us.)
BALAAM said: "Is it possible I should certainly do wickedness?" (Num. 22:25) He spoke this way because he was eager to please Jehovah and thought that Jehovah would not lead him to do something harmful. Balaam was eager to know what Jehovah considered to be "goodness" with respect to Sodom and Gomorrah. He was willing to "search" for Jehovah's direction. Some 400 years later, Jehovah revealed the reason why He allowed those cities to be destroyed: "Indeed, His ways are wonderful; and His works are all equitable: the God of faithfulness, with whom there is no injustice, is righteous and upright."—Deut. 31:19; 32:4.
2. How can we show that we trust Jehovah to guide us?
2 Did Balaam really believe that everything Jehovah does is right? It is evident that he valued Jehovah's guidance. Also, in the Greek Scriptures, many verses that were originally written using the expression "righteousness" are now rendered "equity." Therefore, value Jehovah's guidance and view his direction as equitable. Remember that Jehovah is very equitable, so everything he does is right. Moreover, his Word shows that "justice and equity are the foundation of his throne."—Ps. 33:5.
3. Briefly explain how people benefit when they use wisdom.
3 To understand whether Jehovah does what is right, we need to examine the evidence and consider how this affects our lives. It is important to remember that some people have been misled because of false teachings. For example, some have been led to believe that evolution explains the origin of life and that the earth is millions of years old. They may feel that scientific discoveries disprove the Bible, especially when findings from DNA research seem to contradict Biblical accounts. But such views can cause a person to lose faith and abandon his worship.
SECTION
4. What is one way to strengthen your confidence in the Christian ministry?
4 Christians have found it helpful to meditate on scriptures that support the ministry and to use them effectively. If our confidence weakens when someone raises objections or questions about our beliefs, or if we feel inadequate to explain things clearly, should we stop sharing the good news? Or should we ask an older Christian for help and guidance? Doing so will help us remain steadfast.
5. How can a Christian deal with feelings of inadequacy while engaging in the ministry?
5 All of us make mistakes and say wrong things at times, but we can learn from those experiences. If we confess our errors and seek forgiveness, Jehovah will help us overcome our shortcomings. (1 John 1:8) And even if we feel that we lack the ability to express ourselves well, fellow Christians who are experienced ministers can offer encouragement and practical advice. Pray to Jehovah to guide you as you apply his principles, which can help you speak confidently and address concerns raised by others.—Ps. 55:12-14.
6, 7. What happened to one young brother when he was assigned to a congregation, and what lesson can we learn from his experience?
6 Consider the example of Willi Diehl. Brother Diehl served at Bethel in Bern, Switzerland, starting in 1931. In 1946, he attended the 23rd class of Gilead School in New York, United States. After graduating, he returned to Switzerland to serve as a missionary. Brother Diehl later wrote: "On May 2, 1949, I received a letter from the Bern office stating that I was being appointed to a congregation." How did the Bern office respond to his request? They told him: "We are assigning you a territory and giving you one day each week to work it." Brother Diehl continued: "I felt very discouraged because of this limited opportunity . . . Many were more capable than I was, and they could accomplish much more."
7 Did Brother Diehl allow this situation to discourage him? He said: "I prayed about it, asking whether the Scriptures supported such an arrangement, and we decided to continue to Jehovah and to trust in him." As a result of his faith, Brother Diehl found ways to make his ministry fruitful, and eventually he was appointed an elder in that congregation. Jehovah blessed his efforts to remain in the full-time ministry. * So, let us ask ourselves: 'When faced with a seemingly unfavorable assignment, do we become discouraged, or do we pray to Jehovah for guidance and strength?'—Phil. 11:2; read Micah 7:7.
8. Why is it important for us to be positive, even when someone treats us unfairly or does not appreciate our efforts?
8 To illustrate this, consider how encouraging it can be when someone appreciates our efforts or when someone shows kindness to us, especially when we feel unappreciated. It feels good to be treated with respect. Why is that? Because we all want to be understood and valued, or we want our efforts to produce something worthwhile. And when we feel appreciated or encouraged, we are more likely to love Jehovah and trust in him, and we will maintain our zeal. This attitude helps us to 'strengthen our hearts toward Jehovah.'—Read Proverbs 19:3.
9. How can we benefit from personal study and meetings?
9 Let us examine three examples showing how Jehovah has blessed faithful ones who have faced difficulties. One example is the story of Joseph, a descendant of Abraham. Another example teaches us about what happened to his father. Also, let us look at how Jehovah dealt with Moses, the prophet of Israel, and also what happened during Paul's ministry while he was in Syria and Cilicia. As we continue to learn from these examples, may we find ways to strengthen our faith and deepen our relationship with Jehovah, so that we may always appreciate what he does for us.
THE STORY OF JOSEPH SHOWS US HOW
10, 11. (a) What trials did Joseph face? (b) How did Joseph turn his difficult situation into an opportunity?
10 Joseph was a devoted servant of Jehovah. He experienced hardship because of what people did to him, and this caused him great suffering. Joseph was only 17 years old when his brothers sold him into slavery. They took him to Egypt. (Gen. 37:23-28; 42:21) But despite everything, he remained loyal. His brothers accused him falsely, and they conspired against him to put him in prison. (Gen. 39:17-20) Joseph spent about 13 years in prison and in bondage. What lessons can we learn from Joseph's experience that will help us remain faithful when facing difficulties?
11 Joseph had the opportunity to interpret dreams for two of his fellow prisoners. One of them was the chief cupbearer, and the other was the chief baker. The cupbearer told him about a dream he had, and Joseph explained to him that the dream meant he would be restored to his position. Joseph told the cupbearer that God revealed this meaning to him in a dream. Joseph interpreted the dream for the baker, but he told him that his dream foretold bad news—that he would be impaled. However, Joseph reminded the cupbearer that it was God who could fulfill the interpretation of the dreams.—Gen. 40:5-13.
12, 13. (a) Why did Joseph bother interpreting the dreams of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, especially since it seemed that neither man appreciated what Joseph did for them? (b) What lessons can we learn from Joseph's willingness to explain the meaning of the dreams even though the cupbearer forgot about him?
12 Read Genesis 40:14, 15. Notice how Joseph mentioned "drinking." What does this suggest? It suggests that drinking something was involved. And it reminds us that sometimes things may seem insignificant. This is why the chief cupbearer eventually remembered Joseph when Pharaoh was troubled. Did anyone else remember Joseph? He was remembered because he said that the dream signified 'release.'
13 Did Joseph resent the fact that the chief cupbearer forgot about him? No, he did not. He understood that there were circumstances beyond his control. That is why he continued to trust that God would fulfill the meaning of the dream, even if he had to wait a long time for it to happen. In fact, the Bible shows that Joseph did not blame either the man or Pharaoh when they finally remembered him. And when Pharaoh sent messengers to get Joseph and his brothers, Pharaoh generously gave them provisions and said, "The best of all Egypt" would be theirs.—Gen. 45:16-20.
14. What can motivate us to remain optimistic and patient even when things don't turn out as expected?
14 If a Christian finds himself facing difficulties, he will strive to maintain a positive outlook. It is unwise to become discouraged or to dwell on negative thoughts, especially if we know that our brothers and sisters are supporting us. (Phil. 5:1) Often, though, we need to remind ourselves that we are not alone in experiencing trials, and others have faced similar challenges. (Read Matthew 5:23, 24; 18:15.) Let us learn from the example of the Ethiopian eunuch who wanted to worship God. He took the initiative, and despite obstacles, he persevered! And we should not hesitate to seek help from others when we feel overwhelmed. But we must also be willing to take steps to resolve matters peacefully and avoid unnecessary conflict. Remember, whether you are giving advice or receiving it, always speak kindly and respectfully. We want to please Jehovah and our fellow humans, so let us conduct ourselves appropriately. The psalmist described someone who "walks uprightly." He said that such a person is one "who does not practice deceit, nor does he speak falsely, nor does he deceive his companion."—Ps. 15:2, 3; Jas. 3:5.
THE IMPORTANCE OF LOYALTY TO JEHOVAH
15. What motivated Joseph to remain loyal to Jehovah even when facing difficult circumstances?
15 We can strengthen our loyalty to Jehovah by considering how Joseph demonstrated it. Throughout his entire life—for 13 years—Joseph remained confident in what Jehovah saw. (Gen. 45:5-8) He trusted that Jehovah knew what was best. And even when things were difficult, he did not blame God. Instead, he continued to put his trust in Jehovah, knowing that Jehovah would support him. Furthermore, he refused to allow worldly concerns to distract him from his relationship with Jehovah. Like Joseph, we can stay close to Jehovah, seeking his guidance, and showing confidence in his promises.
16. How can we show loyalty to Jehovah when facing a difficulty that involves another imperfect human?
16 Often, we can demonstrate our loyalty to Jehovah by being forgiving. The experiences of others can teach us to be more tolerant and to maintain our loyalty to the God we worship and serve. (Acts 8:38, 39) In such situations, let us imitate Joseph's example. Let us continue to seek Jehovah's direction and to trust in his judgment. Also, let us remember that the Bible teaches us to be reasonable and understanding. So, instead of becoming discouraged, let us ask Jehovah for help to deal with the situation in a way that will please him.
CONSIDER "THE WHOLE TRIBE"
17. Why should we try to understand what is meant by "the whole tribe"?
17 This expression reminds us that problems often affect many people. We need to see things from their perspective and recognize that they too may be facing difficulties. It helps us to be more compassionate and considerate. Such an attitude can prevent misunderstandings. (Proverbs 119:165) Those who are peaceable want to honor God and show love for their brothers. They also realize that there may be times when they need to forgive others, even if they have been wronged. And if we are willing to do so, we can avoid causing trouble and maintain good relationships. As illustrated by Joseph's experience, sometimes it takes time and patience to resolve matters. However, it is important to remain loyal to Jehovah and to trust in his guidance. Jehovah has shown that he cares about us and is willing to help us, just as he helped Joseph. Therefore, we can confidently say that Jehovah, who is "the Whole Tribe," always acts in our best interests.—Matthew 18:25; Revelation 32:4.
18 What can strengthen our faith?
18 Our faith can be strengthened by meditating on examples of faithful ones recorded in the Bible, such as those who pleased Jehovah. Meditating on these examples will help us to imitate them and to appreciate how Jehovah supports those who serve him loyally.

text:
ĨVINDA yĩmwe Yosevu aũngamĩte mũũndanĩ syũa yĩithũa. Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa asyaĩĩsye mĩtĩ ya ndende, na mĩtĩ ĩngĩ ya matunda, ithima syĩ na mĩtĩ ĩla ĩmeaa kĩw'ũnĩ, na o vu vakuvĩ na mũsyĩ wake, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa eene nyũmba ya Valao. Kwasũanĩa Yosevu ayĩw'a wasya wa kamwana kake Manase kainyangilya kamũinae ka ko Evalaimu. Nokwĩthĩwa asũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ kĩveti kyake kyathekaa kyoona tũmwana tu tũithaũka. Kũsũanĩa maũndũ asu no nginya kwĩthĩwe kwatumie ew'a mũyo. Nĩweesĩ kana aĩ mũathime mũno.
Yosevu eetie kana kake ka mbee Manase nũndũ ĩsyĩtwa yĩu yonanasya kũlwa. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 41:51) Moathimo ala Yosevu wakwatĩte kuma kwa Ngai nĩmaolangĩte woo ũla waumanaa na mosũanĩo ĩũlũ wa mũsyĩ kwoo, ana-a-ĩthe, na ĩthe wake. Kĩmena kya ana-a-ĩthe nĩkyatumĩte thayũ wake ũalyũka. Nĩmamũthĩnisye, o na nĩmendaa kũmũaa, na ĩndĩ mamũthoosya ta ngombo kwa akũni ma viasala. Kuma ĩvinda yu maũndũ maendeeie maalyũkĩte. Kwa myaka kauta nĩwoomĩĩisye kwĩthĩwa e ngombo, na kwĩthĩwa e mũvungwa, o na ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwooviwe na mĩnyololo. Ĩndĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana, ĩvinda yĩĩ aĩ wa kelĩ kwa Valao ũsumbĩnĩ wĩ vinya wa Misili! *
Kwa myaka mingĩ Yosevu nĩwoonete maũndũ mayĩanĩa o tondũ Yeova wathanĩte. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ twaĩ ĩla myaka mũonza ya ngetha mbingĩ o tondũ kwathanĩtwe, na Yosevu nĩwe waũngamĩe wĩa wa kũmbany'a lĩu. Aĩ na tũmwana twĩlĩ tũla wasyaĩwe nĩ mũka wake Asenathi. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, mavinda maingĩ nĩwasũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa andũ make ala maĩ kĩlomita mbingĩ kuma Misili. Mũno mũno asũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa mũinae Mbenyamini na ĩthe wake Yakovo. Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa eekũlasya kana no aima. O na ĩngĩ, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa eekũlasya kana ana-a-ĩthe nĩmaalyũkile na mambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa na tei na kana nĩ vaĩ vatonyeka makesa kwĩkalany'a na mũuo.
Ethĩwa ve ĩvinda mũsyĩ wenyu ũtaaĩthĩwa wĩ na mũuo nũndũ wa kĩwĩu, kũkosa ũĩkĩĩku, kana kĩmena, nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa maũndũ ta asu nĩ amwe katĩ wa ala mamũkwatie Yosevu. Tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na mũĩkĩĩo ũla Yosevu waĩ naw'o aisũvĩa andũ ma mũsyĩ wake?
"ENDAI KWA YOSEVU"
Yosevu aĩ na wĩa mwingĩ na nũndũ wa ũu myaka nĩyavĩtie na mĩtũkĩ. Ĩtina wa mwaka wa mũonza wa ngetha mbingĩ maũndũ nĩmaalyũkile o tondũ Yeova woonanĩtye kwĩsĩla ndoto ya Valao. Lĩu ũyaasyaa. Kavinda kanini ĩtina wa ũu, nthĩ ila syaĩ vakuvĩ na Misili nĩsyakwatiwe nĩ yũa. Ĩndĩ o tondũ Mbivilia yonanĩtye, "nthĩ yonthe ya Misili kwaĩ lĩu." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 41:54) Vate nzika, ndoto ĩla Yosevu watetheeiw'e nĩ Yeova kũalyũla o vamwe na ngelekany'o yake ya kũvanga maũndũ nesa, nĩyatethisye andũ ma Misili.
Nĩvatonyeka Amisili makethĩwa matũngĩaa Yosevu mũvea mũno, na makamũkatha nũndũ wa ũmanyi wake wa kũvanga maũndũ. Yosevu ndaĩ enda andũ mamũkumye, ĩndĩ endaa mamũkumye Ngai wake, Yeova. Ĩla twatũmĩa inengo ila twĩ nasyo kũmũthũkũma Ngai, nĩvatonyeka akatũnenga vinya tũkaitũmĩa kwa nzĩa nene vyũ, o na tũte kũsũanĩaa.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, o namo Amisili nĩmambĩĩie kũkwatwa nĩ yũa. Ĩla Amisili mamwĩkaĩla Valao mayenda lĩu ameaa atĩĩ: "Endai kwa Yosevu; o ũndũ wĩmũtavya, wĩkei." Kwoou, Yosevu nĩwambĩĩie kumya lĩu ũla waiĩte makũmbĩnĩ, namo andũ nĩmaendaa kwake makathooa lĩu ũla mekwenda.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 41:55, 56.
Ĩndĩ nthĩ ila syaĩ vakuvĩ na Misili iyaĩ na lĩu. Andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Yosevu ala maĩ Kanaani, kĩlomita mbingĩ mũno kuma Misili maĩ na nzaa mũno. Yakovo, ũla yu waĩ mũkũũ, ĩla weewie kana Misili kwaĩ lĩu mwingĩ, nĩwatũmie ana make kw'o nĩ kana makathooe lĩu.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 42:1, 2.
Yakovo atũmie ana make ĩkũmi ĩndĩ mayaathi na mwana wake ũla waĩ wa ĩtina, Mbenyamini. Yakovo nĩwalilikene nesa ĩvinda yĩla watũmie Yosevu akasisye akũũe. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda ya mũthya kwona mwana ũsu wake. Akũũe asu make maeteie ĩthe ĩkoti ya mwanae yĩla wamũtumĩe. Mamũtwaĩie yusĩe nthakame na yĩĩtembũkangu. Makengie mũtumĩa ũsu kana mwanae Yosevu nũĩwe nĩ nyamũ nthũku ya kĩthekanĩ.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 37:31-35.
"YOSEVU ALILIKANA"
Ĩtina wa kũthi mũendo mũasa, ana ma Yakovo nĩmavikie Misili. Ĩla mawetie kana mendaa kũthooa lĩu, matũmiwe kwa mũnene ũmwe wa Misili weetawa Nzevenathivanea. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 41:45) Yo ĩla mamwonie nĩmamanyie kana nĩwe Yosevu? Aiee. Moonie o mũnene wa Misili ũla mendaa amatetheesye. Na nĩ kana monany'e ndaĩa kwake meekie o ũndũ kweekawa: 'Makunamisye mothyũ moo melekele nthĩ.'—Mwambĩlĩlyo 42:5, 6.
We Yosevu nĩwamanyie ana-a-ĩthe? Ĩĩ, amamanyie vu kwa vu! Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana, ĩla woonie mamũkumanĩe nĩwalilikanile ĩvinda yĩla waĩ kamwana. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Yosevu alilikana ndeto ila waotie" ila Yeova wamwonisye ĩla waĩ kamwana. Ndoto isu syoonanĩtye kana ĩvinda yĩmwe ana-a-ĩthe makamũkumanĩa. Na ũu nĩw'o meekie! (Mwambĩlĩlyo 37:2, 5-9; 42:7, 9) Yosevu esaa kwĩka ata? Esaa kũmakumbatĩa? Kana esaa kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya?
Yosevu nĩweesĩ kana ndaaĩle kũatĩĩa ũndũ ngoo yake yendaa. Yeova nĩwe watongoesye maũndũ asu onthe. Maũndũ asu makonetye kĩeleelo kyake. Nĩwathanĩte kana akatw'ĩkĩthya nzyawa sya Yakovo mbaĩ yĩ vinya. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 35:11, 12) Takethĩwa ĩvinda yĩu ana-a-ĩthe ma Yosevu mayaĩ na tei, nĩmeeyendete, kana maĩ athũku methĩwa meeyĩeteie mũisyo mũnene! Nake Yosevu takethĩwa nĩweekie maũndũ ate kũsũanĩa, aĩ atonya kũũmĩsya angĩ ala mataĩ vo, o na nĩwaĩ atonya kũũmĩsya ĩthe wake na Mbenyamini. We o na nĩweesĩ kana maĩ thayũ? Yosevu nĩwavangie kũlea kũmatavya nĩwe ũũ nĩ kana amanye kana ana-a-ĩthe nĩmaĩ maalyũkile. Na ĩndĩ aĩ atonya kũmanya kĩla Yeova wendaa eke.
Nĩvatonyeka ũkaema kwĩsa kũkwatwa nĩ maũndũ ta asu. Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ mĩsyĩ mingĩ nĩyĩthĩawa na ngananĩo na mĩtilĩkangano. Ĩla twakwatwa nĩ maũndũ ta asu, nĩtũtonya kũatĩĩa ngoo sitũ na tũyĩka maũndũ kwa nzĩa ĩla ĩtaĩle. Ĩndĩ wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yosevu, na kũtata kũelewa ũndũ Ngai ũkwenda twĩke maũndũ. (Nthimo 14:12) Lilikana kana o ũndũ kwĩthĩwa na mũuo na andũ ma mũsyĩ ne ũndũ wa vata, now'o kwĩthĩwa na mũuo na Yeova na Mwana wake ne ũndũ wa vata mũno vyũ.—Mathayo 10:37.
"NĨMŨŨTATWA"
Yosevu nĩwavangie kũtata ana-a-ĩthe kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, nĩ kana amanye kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ syoo. Ambĩĩie kwa kũneena namo e mũkalĩ vyũ, na amea kana maĩ athiani. Aneenie namo atũmĩĩte mũndũ wa kũmũalyũlĩla. Nĩ kana metetee nĩmamũtavisye ĩũlũ wa mũsyĩ woo. O na nĩmamũtavisye ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata kana maĩ na mũinae ũla mamũtiĩte mũsyĩ. Yosevu nĩwatatie ũndũ ũtonya ndakonany'e kana ũndũ ũsu nĩwamũtany'a. Yosevu nĩwamanyie kana mũinae aĩ thayũ! Na ũu watuma amanya ĩtambya yĩla waaĩle kwosa. Ameie atĩĩ: "Nĩmũũtatwa na ũndũ ũũ," na ongeleela kũmatavya kana no nginya one mũinae woo. Ĩtina nĩweetĩkĩlile masyoke mũsyĩ kwoo makaete mũinae ũsu ĩndĩ yaĩ lasima ũmwe woo atiwe.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 42:9-20.
Ĩla ana-a-ĩthe mambĩĩie kũneena ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu matesĩ kana Yosevu nũkũelewa ũndũ mekwasya, nĩmeetũlile mũtĩ nũndũ wa naĩ ĩla maĩ meekie myaka 20 mĩvĩtu. Maisye atĩĩ: "Nĩ w'o twĩ avĩtan'ya ũndũ wa mwana-a-asa waitũ, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩtwoonie thĩna wa ngoo yake, yĩla watwĩsũvie o na tũtyaaĩthukĩĩsya; kwondũ wa ũu thĩna ũũ nĩwatũkwata." Yosevu nĩwaeleiwe ũndũ masasya na ũu watuma ethyũũa maikone methoi make. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 42:21-24) Ĩndĩ nĩweesĩ kana kwĩlila kwa w'o kwonanaw'a na maũndũ maingĩ, ĩndĩ ti o ũndũ mũndũ ũkwĩw'a ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũna weekie. Na kwoou nĩwaendeeie kũmatata.
Nĩwametĩkĩlilye menũka ĩndĩ Simeoni atiwa e mwove. O na nĩwavangie mbesa ila maĩ nasyo syĩkĩwe makunianĩ ma lĩu ũla makuĩte. Ĩla mavikie mũsyĩ nĩmamwĩsũvie mũno ĩthe woo Yakovo ametĩkĩlye masyoke na Mbenyamini Misili. Ĩla mavikie Misili nĩmatavisye mũthũkũmi wa Yosevu ĩũlũ wa mbesa ila meethĩie makunianĩ moo, na masya nĩmekũĩva mbesa isu syonthe. Ũndũ ũsu mendaa kwĩka waĩ mũseo, ĩndĩ Yosevu nĩwendaa kũmanya nesa kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ syoo. Nĩwamekĩĩie mboka ĩndĩ ate kũmonethya kana nĩweewie mũyo nũndũ wa kũmwona Mbenyamini. Amina kwĩka ũu, nĩwametĩkĩlilye menũka na amanenga lĩu makue, ĩndĩ kĩkombe kyake kya vetha kyavithwa ĩkunianĩ ya Mbenyamini.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 42:26–44:2.
Yosevu nĩwakwatie mwanya mũseo wa kũmanya ũndũ ana-a-ĩthe mailyĩ. Nĩwaumisye mwĩao ana-a-ĩthe maatĩĩwa, makwatwa na meewa nĩmoyĩte kĩkombe. Ĩla kyeethĩiwe ĩkunianĩ ya Mbenyamini, onthe nĩmatũngiwe kwa Yosevu. Yu ĩndĩ Yosevu aĩ na mwanya mũseo wa kũmanya kana ana-a-ĩthe maĩ maalyũkile. Yuta nĩwe waneenie kwondũ woo. Nĩweesũvanie nginya asya onthe me 11 no matw'ĩkĩthw'e ngombo Misili. Ĩndĩ Yosevu aisye no Mbenyamini e weka ũkũtw'ĩka ngombo na ala angĩ mayĩnũka.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 44:2-17.
Ũndũ ũsu watumie Yuta aweta ndeto ii ĩũlũ wa Mbenyamini e na tei mwingĩ: "Atiele e weka wa inyia wake; na ĩthe wake nũmwendete." No nginya ndeto isu ikethĩwa syakiitie Yosevu mũno nũndũ nĩwe waĩ mwana ũla mũkũũ wa kĩveti kya Yakovo kĩla wendete vyũ kyeetawa Lakeli. Kĩveti kyu kyakwie kĩisyaa Mbenyamini. Vate nzika, Yosevu na ĩthe wake nĩmalilikanaa maũndũ maseo ĩũlũ wa Lakeli. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumaa Yosevu enda Mbenyamini mũno.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 35:18-20; 44:20.
Yuta nĩwaendeeie kũmwĩsũva Yosevu ndakatw'ĩkĩthye Mbenyamini ngombo. O na nĩweeyumisye atw'ĩke ngombo vandũ va Mbenyamini. Na ĩndĩ aminĩĩa kwa kũweta ndeto ii syaĩ na kyeva kingĩ: "Nũndũ ngatonya ata kwambata kwa ĩthe wakwa, ethĩwa kĩmwana kĩti vamwe nakwa? ndikese kwona ũthũku ũla wĩmũkwata asa wakwa"! (Mwambĩlĩlyo 44:18-34) Ndeto isu syoonanisye kana Yuta aĩ aalyũkile vyũ. O vamwe na kwonany'a kana nĩweelilĩte, oonanisye kana aĩ na tei na ndeeyendete.
Yosevu nĩwaemiwe nĩ kwĩyũmĩĩsya kũvĩtũka vau. Ndaĩ atonya kũsiĩĩa ũndũ weew'aa ngoonĩ. Nĩwaumaalilye athũkũmi make onthe, na aĩa na wasya mũnene nginya wasya wake weew'ĩka nyũmbanĩ kwa Valao. Na ĩndĩ amatavya nĩwe ũũ. Ameie: "Ninyie Yosevu mwana-a-ĩthe wenyu." Na ĩtina wa ũu amakumbatĩa ana-a-ĩthe ala mbikĩa ya vau maĩ matelemile vyũ, na amaekea. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 45:1-15) Kwa kwĩka ũu, oonanisye ũndũ Yeova ũilyĩ, nũndũ nũekeaa vyũ. (Savuli 86:5) Ithyĩ nĩtũekeaa angĩ o ta Yosevu?
"WĨ O THAYŨ"!
Ĩla Valao weewie kĩla kyaendeeie nyũmbanĩ kwa Yosevu, nĩwamwĩie athamĩĩsye ĩthe wake ũla waĩ mũkũũ Misili vamwe na mũsyĩ wake w'onthe. Vayaavĩta ĩvinda ĩasa Yosevu atakomanĩte na ĩthe wake ũla wamwendete mũno. Yakovo aĩie na asya atĩĩ: "Yu ĩndĩ nĩkw'e, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩnakwona ũthyũ waku, kana wĩ o thayũ."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 45:16-28; 46:29, 30.
Yakovo ekalile myaka ĩngĩ 17 ĩtina wa kũthi Misili. Ekalile thayũ ĩvinda ĩasa nginya esa kwathana moathimo ala ana make 12 maĩ makwate. Anengie Yosevu mwana wake wa 11 ũtiĩwa kũndũ kwĩlĩ ũla mũno mũno wanengawa ĩkithathi. Mbaĩ ilĩ sya Isilaeli syaĩ syumane nake. Nao nata ĩũlũ wa Yuta mwana wake wa kana ũla weelilile vyũ mbee wa ana-a-ĩthe? Aathimiwe mũno nũndũ Masia aĩ aume nzyawanĩ yake!—Mwambĩlĩlyo, kĩlungu kya 48 na 49.
Ĩla Yakovo wakwie e na myaka 147, ana-a-ĩthe ma Yosevu nĩmakwatiwe nĩ wia, mayona Yosevu ta ũtonya kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya nũndũ aĩ na ũtonyi mwingĩ. Ĩndĩ Yosevu nĩwamaĩkĩĩthisye nesa kana ndaĩ na mũvango wa kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya. Kuma tene aĩ atwie ũu nũndũ Yeova nĩwe watongoesye maũndũ nĩ kana mũsyĩ woo ũthamĩĩe Misili, na kwoou ana-a-ĩthe mayaaĩle kũthĩnĩka nũndũ wa kĩla kyeekĩkie. Na ĩndĩ amakũlya ĩkũlyo yĩĩ ya vata: "Nyie nĩ vandũ va Ngai?" (Mwambĩlĩlyo 15:13; 45:7, 8; 50:15-21) Yosevu nĩweesĩ kana Yeova nĩwe Mũsili ũla mũseo. Na kwoou ndaĩ atonya kwĩyĩĩvanĩsya kwa ana-a-ĩthe ala Yeova waĩ amaekeie.—Aevelania 10:30.
We ve mavinda wĩw'aa vinya kũekea ala angĩ? Nũtonya kwĩw'a wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya, ethĩwa mũndũ akũvĩtĩsya na ngũlũ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ĩla twaekea vyũ ala meelila kuma ngoonĩ, nĩtwĩw'aa twĩ eanĩe na ũndũ ũsu nũminaa mathĩna maingĩ. Na tũkeethĩawa tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ya Yosevu na Ĩthe wake wĩ tei, Yeova.
