translation:
"I have taken delight in doing Your will, O my God."—PS. 40:8.
PAGE: 51, 48
1, 2. (a) What does it mean to be zealous in serving Jehovah? (b) Why might a Christian feel inadequate to serve, and what can help him?
DO YOU ever feel unqualified to serve? If so, you are not alone. It is normal to feel apprehensive when faced with a new assignment. But remember this important lesson: zeal does not come from within ourselves. We are appointed to serve because Jehovah has chosen us and has equipped us to accomplish his purpose. Consider how Jehovah views your service, and then think about practical steps you can take to overcome your hesitancy and become more effective in your ministry.
2 Have you ever wondered why you were assigned to a particular territory or why you were paired with a certain publisher? Or perhaps you have questioned whether you should accept a specific meeting or share in a certain activity? Even if you do not understand the reasons, trust that there is wisdom in such arrangements. Use the tools available to you—such as the Meeting Workbook and the Service Group Worksheet—to prepare thoroughly for your ministry. And remember, prayerful consideration of (1) your strengths, (2) your weaknesses, and (3) your goals can help you make progress.
YOUR STRENGTHS
3, 4. How did Timothy show courage in proclaiming the good news?
3 Prayerfully consider how you can strengthen your faith by asking yourself questions like these: 'Do I truly believe that God exists?' 'Is it possible to be both a Christian and live according to worldly principles or to disregard Bible standards?' 'Do I believe that rejecting God's laws will ultimately lead to unhappiness?' The answer to these questions will reveal your heart condition. Many people find it helpful to meditate on Paul's inspired words: "Continue making earnest supplication in your prayers, always keeping vigilant and giving thanks." (Col. 4:2) Did Christians in ancient times sometimes struggle with doubts?
4 Consider the example of a brother named Apollos. Timothy was well-versed in the Scriptures. However, he needed help to discern what was true. So Paul encouraged him: "Keep holding fast to the pattern of healthful words you heard from me." (2 Tim. 3:14, 15) The expression "healthful words" refers to sound doctrine—truth that builds up spiritual health. Timothy had discernment, but he still needed guidance. We too may at times feel uncertain about certain matters, yet we can benefit from seeking counsel from those who have spiritual insight.—Read 1 Thessalonians 5:21.
5, 6. What does it mean to "test everything"?
5 How so? To test whether something aligns with God's Word. For instance, when faced with a new teaching, ask yourself: 'Does this teaching build me up spiritually? Does it motivate me to draw closer to Jehovah?' Your conscience, along with prayerful consideration of God's view, will guide you.
6 To "test everything," you need to be willing to examine carefully how it affects your relationship with Jehovah and your brothers and sisters. Think about the questions they might ask: 'Is this in harmony with what the Bible says? Does it please Jehovah? Will it strengthen my faith?' By being thoughtful, you can protect your heart from error and maintain a close relationship with God.
7-9. Why does the brochure "Apollos Helps Us Reason" encourage us to reason? Explain.
7 Reasoning and careful thought help you to identify false teachings, defend your beliefs, and strengthen your relationship with Jehovah. (Proverbs 17:11) There are many ways to reason effectively. Many people have found helpful the publications Questions Big and Small—Answers From the Bible and Is There a Creator Who Cares About You. Another resource is the website jw.org/kam, which features the brochure "Apollos Helps Us Reason." This brochure offers practical advice. Look for the article titled LEARN FROM THE BIBLE. The brochure also provides sample conversations and shows how Bible principles can be applied to everyday life.
8 To improve your ability to reason, study the Bible regularly and practice applying what you learn. Ask yourself, 'Can I explain this clearly and convincingly?' The brochure discusses how to use scripture to reason on various topics, and it includes space to write down your thoughts. By practicing, you will become more confident in expressing your beliefs. The brochure "Apollos Helps Us Reason" has helped many people to strengthen their faith. If you have access to the Internet, why not explore the website jw.org to find articles and videos that can help you to reason on different subjects?
9 Strengthening your faith may require effort, especially if you have been misled. One sister wrote: "I used to fear being questioned, but now I enjoy discussing the Bible and sharing what I believe. With each passing day, my faith grows stronger."
IMPORTANT POINTS
10. How can a Christian respond when faced with questions that challenge his beliefs?
10 The Bible says: "Faith without works is dead." (Jas. 2:17) So, having faith also means demonstrating it through your actions. Do your actions align with your beliefs? Consider what the Bible says about 'making supplication for one another, so that you may be healed.'—Read 2 Corinthians 3:11.
11. What does it mean to 'make supplication for one another'? Explain.
11 Even if you have been taught to 'make supplication for one another,' do not stop praying for yourself. Should we continue doing so indefinitely? For example, think about a person who has been sick for a long time. Would you question whether his 'request' has moved God to help him? (Eph. 5:14) Do not hesitate to ask for help when you need it, or to seek advice from others when facing a difficult situation. But how well do you apply your own counsel? Are you willing to accept correction, or do you feel offended when someone points out your mistakes? (1 Cor. 4:3, 4) To put it simply, everyone needs help. And a humble person will allow Jehovah to use others to strengthen his resolve and encourage him. A person who loves Jehovah will humbly accept help from others and will see this as an expression of love for him.
12. Mention some ways to "[make supplication to God]." Will you try to imitate them in your life?
12 So what about "[making supplication to God]"? Some ways include spending time alone in prayer, and also speaking to God during family worship. Others involve expressing our feelings openly to trusted friends, and seeking their support. A person who loves Jehovah desires to do more than just pay lip service. Like ancient King David, he pours out his heart to God, saying: "I have longed to come to you, O my God; I have earnestly sought you."—Ps. 40:8.
13, 14. What can motivate us to 'make supplication to God' regularly? Can you identify some personal goals?
13 See pages 308 and 309 of the book Questions Young People Ask—Answers That Work, Volume 2, for suggestions on how to make your prayers more meaningful. Some practical goals might be to ask yourself questions like: "What really troubles me?" "How can I show Jehovah that I appreciate him?" "What specific things can I improve?" These goals can help you write down your thoughts and feelings, as well as what you want to thank Jehovah for, what you struggle with, and what you would like to change.
14 Many find that setting aside time each day to read their Bible helps them to pray. One young woman named Tilda says: "I set aside specific times for prayer. I go over my schedule repeatedly, and after about a year, I have become better at praying." And a young man named Patrick has had a similar experience. He says: "Writing down my prayers helps me focus and remember what I have prayed about."
15 Remember that everyone needs time to develop the habit of praying.
15 One important goal you may have is this: "How can I continue to strengthen my relationship with Jehovah, especially when facing difficulties?" A true Christian will rely on Jehovah and trust in Him. Continue to strengthen your relationship with Jehovah by associating with others and by focusing on spiritual matters. Your love for God will grow stronger, and you will feel closer to Him, and you will continue to progress spiritually.
TO BE CONTINUED
16, 17. (a) What can motivate someone to become a dedicated Christian? (b) How can we help someone appreciate the value of dedicating himself to Jehovah?
16 A man once asked Jesus: "Which is the greatest commandment?" Jesus replied: "'You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.' " (Matt. 22:35-37) Jesus' answer shows that the primary motivation for becoming a dedicated Christian is to love Jehovah with all your heart. One way to show our love for Jehovah is to appreciate the great gift he has given us—the ransom sacrifice of his Son. (Read 2 Corinthians 5:14, 15; 1 John 4:9, 19.) Appreciating the ransom and what it means can move us to want to dedicate ourselves to Jehovah.
17 If someone is hesitant about making a dedication, perhaps you could reason on this: Would a reasonable person risk his life to save a friend? Of course! He would carefully weigh the risks, and he would be willing to make sacrifices. Similarly, those who understand the value of the ransom will be motivated to dedicate themselves to Jehovah. Let us not take this privilege lightly! Otherwise, we might miss out on many blessings now and in the future. Those who are saved will forever be grateful for what Jehovah and Jesus Christ have done for them. They will always remember the price paid for their salvation and will continue to express their gratitude.
18, 19. (a) Why is it important to remain zealous in our service to Jehovah? (b) What can help us to stay spiritually strong?
18 How can we remain zealous? One way is to focus on what Jehovah does for us. By meditating on Jehovah's goodness and expressing our appreciation, we strengthen our love for him. Consider whether you are putting forth effort to draw closer to Jehovah and to maintain a close relationship with him. If you find yourself drifting away, ask yourself why. Is it because you are preoccupied with material things? No! Remember that Jehovah cares for you, and he wants you to "make the most of your time." (Eph. 5:16) Staying spiritually strong involves focusing on what matters most—appreciating Jehovah and remaining dedicated to him. Many people have found that regularly thinking about the reasons why they appreciate Jehovah helps them to stay motivated. For example, a young man named David, who became an active publisher at age 13, said: "Even though I was encouraged by my parents, I realized that dedicating myself was something I wanted to do personally, especially because I deeply appreciated what Jehovah had done for me, so I continued to pray earnestly about it."
19 Satan tries to exploit any weakness we have, and this includes our desire for possessions! Satan uses materialism to tempt people to put spiritual things last. But how does he succeed in doing so? Satan subtly influences people to believe that having more things will make them happy, and he appeals to their selfish desires. Does he ever offer a quick solution? Yes, Satan often presents temptations as harmless ways to get ahead, but his motives are far from pure.—Prov. 21:10.
20 Can a Christian allow himself to become attached to material things? (See also the section "How to Keep Your Goals Spiritual.")
20 To remain close to Jehovah, we need to cultivate the right attitude toward material possessions. Are you willing to examine your own attitude? If so, be honest with yourself. If you find that your heart is becoming attached to worldly things, take steps to refocus on spiritual matters. The apostle Paul wrote: "Our conduct should be modest." (Phil. 3:16) By being content with what we have, we can keep our hearts focused on pleasing Jehovah and serving him.

text:
"Mũtaĩei Yeova; nũndũ nĩ ũseo kũmũkumya Ngai waitũ; nũndũ nĩkwendeeasya, na ndaĩa nĩ nzeo."—SAV. 147:1.
MBATHI: 9, 152
1-3. (a) Savuli ya 147 ĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yaandĩkiwe ĩndĩĩ? (b) Nĩ maũndũ meva tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya twasoma Savuli ya 147?
MŨNDŨ weanĩsya nesa ũndũ eĩnengetwe kana wĩ na nguma nzeo mũno ya Kĩklĩsto nĩwaĩle kũkathwa. Ethĩwa nĩtũkathaa andũ, ti mbee mũno Yeova Ngai? Twĩ na itumi nzeo vyũ sya kũmũtaĩa. No tũmũtaĩe nũndũ wa vinya wake, ũla ũtonya kwoneka syĩndũnĩ ila woombie. O na no tũmũtaĩe nũndũ wa maũndũ maseo ala wĩkĩte andũ, kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwaumisye Mwana wake ethĩwe nthembo ya wovosyo.
2 Mũandĩki wa Savuli ya 147 nĩweewie aĩle kũmũtaĩa Yeova. O na ĩngĩ nĩwathokisye angĩ mamũtaĩe Ngai vamwe nake.—Soma Savuli 147:1, 7, 12.
3 Tũyĩsĩ savuli ĩsu yaandĩkiwe nũũ, kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana mũandĩki wayo nũtonya kwĩthĩwa atwĩe vakuvĩ na ĩvinda yĩla Aisilaeli ala matavĩtwe makatwawa Mbaviloni matũngiwe Yelusaleme nĩ Yeova. (Sav. 147:2) No nginya kũtũngwa kwa andũ ma Ngai vala maĩ matonya kũmũthaithĩa ũndũ wendaa kwĩthĩwe kwatumie mũandĩki ũsu wa Savuli amũtaĩa Yeova. Ĩndĩ eka kĩu, nĩwasyokie aweta itumi ingĩ sya kũmũtaĩa. Itumi isu nĩ syĩva? Naku wĩ na itumi syĩva sya kwasya "Aleluya" thayũnĩ waku?—Sav. 147:1; Ũvu. 19:1.
YEOVA NŨVOASYA ALA MATŨLĨKĨTE NGOO
4. Aisilaeli ala matavĩtwe makatwawa Mbaviloni meewie ata ĩla mathaiw'e nĩ Mũsumbĩ Kulusi, na nĩkĩ?
4 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Aisilaeli meew'aa me Mbaviloni. Ala mamaumĩtye kwoo makamatwaa kũu mamavũthasya maimea atĩĩ: "Twinĩei wathi ũmwe wa Saioni." Ndũa ya Yelusaleme yaĩ ĩnaanangwa, navo nĩvo matanĩaa vyũ kũmũthaithĩa Yeova. (Sav. 137:1-3, 6) Kwoou Ayuti asu mayeew'aa matonya kwina. Meew'aa me atũlĩku ngoo na maĩ na vata wa kũkiakiw'a na kwĩkĩwa vinya. Ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwesie kũmovosya atũmĩĩte mũsumbĩ wa Velisia weetawa Kulusi, o ũndũ wathanĩte. Mũsumbĩ ũsu avalũkilye Mbaviloni na atangaasa atĩĩ: "Yeova . . . nũmbĩaĩĩte nĩmwakĩe nyũmba Yelusaleme . . . O ũla wĩ katĩ wenyu wa andũ make onthe, Yeova Ngai wake nĩethĩwe vamwe nake, nake nĩambate." (2 Mav. 36:23) Ũndũ ũsu wakiakĩisye Aisilaeli ala mekalaa Mbaviloni ta kĩ!
5. Mũandĩki wa Savuli aandĩkie ata ĩũlũ wa ũtonyi wa Yeova wa kũvosya?
5 Yeova ndaakiakisya o mbaĩ yonthe ya Isilaeli, ĩndĩ nĩwathĩnĩkĩie o na mũndũ ũmwe ũmwe. Ũmũnthĩ ũũ, ekaa oou. Mũandĩki wa Savuli aandĩkie ũũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai: "Nũvoasya ala matũlĩkile ngoo, na kwova mawũkite moo." (Sav. 147:3) Nĩ w'o, Yeova nũthĩnĩkĩaa ala me na mathĩna, methĩwe nĩ awau kana mekĩte kũtũlĩka ngoo. Ũmũnthĩ Yeova nĩwendete mũno kũtũkiakisya na kũtũtetheesya tũusye ngoonĩ. (Sav. 34:18; Isa. 57:15) Nũtũnengae ũĩ na vinya wa kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna o na meva ala matonya kũtũkwata.—Yak. 1:5.
6. Kĩla mũandĩki wa Savuli ũwetete nthĩnĩ wa Savuli 147:4 kĩtonya kũtũtethya ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 17.)
6 Mũandĩki ũsu wa Savuli nũsyokete akaweta ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ ila syĩ matunĩ. Atũtavĩtye kana Yeova "nũtalaa ndata ũndũ syĩana" na "nũsyĩtaa syonthe na masyĩtwa masyo." (Sav. 147:4) Wasũanĩa mũsoa ũsu no wone ta waeka kũneenea kĩla ũkũneeneaa na ambĩĩa kũelesya ĩũlũ wa ndata sya matunĩ. Ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Mũandĩki ũsu wa Savuli aĩ atonya kwona ndata na metho make, ĩndĩ ndaĩ amanya ũtalo wasyo. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu kũvika ũmũnthĩ, ndata ila tũmanyĩte kana syĩ vo nĩ mbingĩ mũno. Andũ amwe masũanĩaa kana kĩkundi kya ndata na syĩndũ ingĩ ila syĩ vamwe na nthĩ yitũ (Milky Way galaxy) kĩ na ndata mbilioni mbingĩ. Na nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa kwĩ ikundi ta isu mbilioni ngili mbingĩ. Ithyĩ tũkakũlw'a twasya ndata iitalĩka! Ĩndĩ we Mũmbi nũnengete kĩla ĩmwe ĩsyĩtwa. Ũu nĩ kwasya kana Yeova nĩwĩsĩ kĩla ndata nesa vyũ. (1 Ako. 15:41) Nao nata syũmbe syake ila syĩ kũũ nthĩ? Ngai ũsu wĩsĩ kĩla ndata vala yĩĩ o na ethĩwa nĩ ĩndĩĩ, nũkwĩsĩ nesa. Nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ nesa vyũ vala ũĩ, akamanya nesa vyũ ũndũ ũkwĩw'a, na nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ nesa vyũ kĩla wĩ na vata nakyo ĩvinda o na yĩva!
7, 8. (a) Nĩ kyaũ Yeova wĩsĩ ĩũlũ witũ? (b) Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ Yeova wĩthĩawa na tei ĩla ũkũtethya andũ make o na kũtw'ĩka me na naĩ.
7 Yeova nũkũthĩnĩkĩaa we mwene. Na ti ũu wĩ w'oka, ĩndĩ e vinya na e tei na kwoou no aũtetheesye ĩla wĩ thĩnanĩ. (Soma Savuli 147:5.) Nũtonya kwĩw'a ta ũkuĩte mũno ũndũ ũtatonya, na thĩna ũla wĩ naw'o ta ũvĩtũkĩte vinya waku. Ĩndĩ ndũkolwe kana Ngai nũeleawa ũtonyi waku na 'nũlilikanaa kana wĩ kĩtoo.' (Sav. 103:14) Nũndũ twĩ andũ me na naĩ, nĩtũvĩtasya. O na twĩthĩaa tũsyokeleile ĩvĩtyo o yĩla yĩla ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũthĩnĩkaa mũno twesa kwĩthĩa tũneenie ndeto itaĩle, twĩ na mĩmeo ĩtaĩle, kana twesa kwĩthĩa nĩtũkwĩw'ĩa angĩ kĩwĩu nĩ syĩndũ ila me nasyo. O na kũtw'ĩka Yeova ndathĩnaw'a nĩ naĩ ta isu, nũtũeleawa nesa vyũ o na kwĩ ũndũ tũtonya kũmanya!—Isa. 40:28.
8 No kwĩthĩwa ve ĩvinda waĩ na thĩna na woona kw'oko kwa Yeova kwĩ vinya kwaũtethya wasinda thĩna ũsu. (Isa. 41:10, 13) Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe vainia wĩtawa Kyoko. Eewie atũlĩka ngoo mũno ĩvinda watũmiwe akatavany'e kĩsionĩ kĩngĩ. Yeova oonanisye ata kana nĩwaeleiwe mathĩna make? Kĩkundinĩ kĩla Kyoko waendie nĩweethĩie andũ mekũelewa ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Eewie Yeova ta wamwĩa atĩĩ: "Nĩngwendete, ti aĩ no kwĩthĩwa wĩ vainia, ĩndĩ nũndũ wĩ mwĩĩtu wakwa na nĩwĩyumĩtye ũnthũkũme. Nĩenda ũtanĩe thayũ waku wĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ syakwa!" Nao a vaku, Mwene Vinya W'onthe akwonetye ata kana "ũmanyi wake ndũthimĩka"?
YEOVA NĨWĨANĨASYA MAVATA MAITŨ
9, 10. Yeova ambaa kũtũtethya ata? Nengane ngelekany'o.
9 Ithyonthe nĩtwĩthĩwa na vata wa syĩndũ ta lĩu, ngũa, na vandũ va kwĩkala. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtonya kũthĩnĩka ũyona ta ũtekwata lĩu ũkwĩanĩtye. Ĩndĩ Yeova oombie nthĩ ĩtonya kũsyaa lĩu mwingĩ kĩla ĩvinda, o na kwondũ wa tũswii twa ngũngũũ tũla tũkayaa tũyenda lĩu! (Soma Savuli 147:8, 9.) Ethĩwa Yeova nũĩthasya ngũngũũ, ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana akaũmanthĩaa syĩndũ ila wĩ na vata nasyo.—Sav. 37:25.
10 Ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ Yeova ũtũtethasya naw'o nĩ kũtũtw'ĩĩka kĩ-veva. Atũnengae "mũuo wa Ngai, ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe." (Avi. 4:6, 7) Ngelekany'o nzeo nĩ ya Mutsuo na mũka. Mwakanĩ wa 2011, ĩla nthĩ ya Japan yakũniwe nĩ kĩuutani kyookie na kĩw'ũ kingĩ kuma ũkanganĩ (tsunami), nĩmoonie Yeova amatethya mũno. Mauniwe nĩ kũlĩsa kĩalanĩ kya nyũmba yoo. Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũsu maaisye vakuvĩ kĩla kĩndũ, o na nyũmba yoo yaanangĩkie mũno. Ũtukũ ũsu mekalile kalumunĩ kaĩ ngolovanĩ yoo ya kelĩ. Kaĩ kĩvindu na mbevo mbingĩ mũno. Kwakya oou, nĩmamanthie kĩndũ kĩtonya kũmekĩa vinya kĩ-veva. Ĩvuku yĩla moonie no Kitabu cha Mwaka cha Mashahidi wa Yehova cha 2006. Kyongo kĩla Mutsuo woonie mayĩvua oou nĩ, "Tsunami Mbaya Sana Kuwahi Kurekodiwa" (Iuutani Ila Nthũku Vyũ sya Tsunami Syaalekotiwa Mavukunĩ). Kyongo kĩu kyaneeneaa kĩthingitho kya nthĩ kyakũnie kĩthama kya Sumatra mwakanĩ wa 2004. Kĩthingitho kĩu kyaetie tsunami ĩla nthũku vyũ katĩ wa tsunami syonthe ila syaaoneka na ikalekotiwa mavukunĩ. Mutsuo na mũka masomie maĩĩte ngewa ila iandĩkĩtwe vau ĩũlũ wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala makwatiwe nĩ mũisyo ũsu. Kũsoma ngewa isu kwatumie mamanya kana Ngai nũmendete nũndũ nĩwamekĩie vinya kĩ-veva ĩvindanĩ yĩu maĩ na vata. O na ĩngĩ Yeova nĩwamanengie syĩndũ ila maĩ na vata nasyo. Nĩmakwatie ũtethyo kuma kwa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa. Ĩndĩ kĩla kyamekĩie vinya vyũ nĩ kũthokewa nĩ ana-a-asa ala matũmĩtwe nĩ ũseũvyo wa Ngai. Mutsuo aĩtye, "Neewie Yeova ta waĩ ũtee wa kĩla ũmwe witũ aitũtetheesya. Mwa tweewie twakiakiw'a ata we!" Kwoou nzĩa ĩla ya vata vyũ Ngai wambaa kũtũtethya nayo nĩ kũtũtw'ĩĩka kĩ-veva. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩwĩanĩasya mavata ala angĩ maitũ.
EKA NGAI AŨTETHYE
11. Ala mekwenda kũtethw'a nĩ Yeova maĩle kwĩka ata?
11 Kĩla ĩvinda Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa eyũmbanĩtye kwosa ĩtambya nĩ kana 'aũngamye ala auu.' (Sav. 147:6a) Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana atũtethye? No nginya twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo nake. Naw'o ũuu nĩ wa vata nĩ kana kĩu kĩtonyeke. (Nzev. 2:3) Ala auu mekalaa meteele Ngai alũnge maũndũ na aimaminĩa thĩna ũla methĩwa naw'o. Yeova nĩwendete ala mekaa ũu.
12, 13. (a) Twaĩle kwĩvathana na kyaũ ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda Ngai atũtethye? (b) Yeova endeeaw'a naaũ?
12 Nao nata ĩũlũ wa ala athũku? Mbivilia yaĩtye Ngai "nũmatheeasya nthĩ ala athũku." (Sav. 147:6b) Isu ti ndeto sya ngũĩ! Nĩ kana tũtetheke nĩ ũseo wa Yeova wĩ wendo na nĩ kana ndakatwosee ĩtambya, no nginya tũmene kĩla ũmenete. (Sav. 97:10) Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtwaĩle kũmena ũlaalai. Ũu nĩ kwasya kana nĩtwaĩle kwĩvathana na kyonthe kĩla kĩtonya kwĩsa kũtũlikya naĩnĩ ĩsu, na kĩmwe nĩ mavisa na ngewa sya ũlaalai. (Sav. 119:37; Mt. 5:28) O na kũtw'ĩka kũkitana na maũndũ asu ti laisi, kũathimwa nĩ Yeova kũyĩsa kwĩanana na kĩla tũtonya kwĩyĩima.
13 Tũyaĩle kwĩkwatya vinya witũ ĩla twĩ kaũnĩ ũsu, ĩndĩ twaĩle kũmwĩkwatya Yeova. We Yeova nĩwĩsa kwendeew'a nithyĩ ethĩwa tũkeekwatasya "vinya wa mbalasi," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, syĩndũ ila andũ mekwatasya nĩ kana imatethye? Aiee, ndesa kwendeew'a nithyĩ. O na eka ũu, tũyaĩle kwĩkwatya "maũũ ma mũndũ," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kwĩka maũndũ kwa nzĩa ĩkwonany'a ithyĩ no twĩtangĩĩe kana mũndũ ũngĩ akatũtangĩĩa. (Sav. 147:10) Vandũ va kwĩka ũu, nĩtwaĩle kũmũvoya Yeova tũimwĩkaĩla atũtetheesye. Yeova ndailyĩ ta atai ma nthĩ ĩno. We ndanoaw'a nĩ mboya sitũ o na tũkatw'ĩka twĩmũvoya ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye, "Yeova nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ ala mamũkĩaa, ala mekwatasya ũseo wake wĩ wendo." (Sav. 147:11) No twĩthwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana nũndũ e ũseo wĩ wendo, ndakatũtia na akatũtetheeasya tũkĩlye vinya mĩmeo yitũ mĩthũku.
14. Mũandĩki wa Savuli eekĩiwe vinya nĩ kũmanya ũndũ wĩva?
14 Yeova nũtũnengete kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũĩkĩĩa vyũ kana nũkatetheeasya andũ make ĩla me na vata. Mũandĩki wa Savuli nĩwainie ĩũlũ wa Yeova aisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kwakwa ĩngĩ kwa Yelusaleme. Ainie atĩĩ: "Nũsyĩkĩĩte vinya ivingi sya mbingĩlo syaku; nũathimĩte syana syaku ila syĩ nthĩnĩ waku. Nũtumaa mũuo mĩvakanĩ yaku." (Sav. 147:13, 14) Kũmanya kana Ngai nĩwesaa kũlũlũmĩĩlya mbingĩlo sya ndũa ĩsu nĩ kana asũvĩe athaithi make, nĩkweekĩie mũandĩki wa Savuli vinya mũno.
15-17. (a) Mavinda amwe tũtonya kwĩw'a ata, ĩndĩ Yeova atũmĩaa Ndeto yake ata kũtũtetheesya? (b) Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ 'ndeto ya Ngai ĩsembaa mĩtũkĩ mũno.'
15 Nũtonya kũkwatwa nĩ mawetu ũkambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa. Vakesa kwĩkala ũu, lilikana kana Yeova no aũnenge ũĩ wa kũng'ang'ana na mawetu asu. Mũandĩki wa Savuli awetie ũũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai: "Nũetae mwĩao wake ĩũlũ wa nthĩ; ndeto yake nĩsembaa mĩtũkĩ mũno." Asyokete akasya kana Yeova 'nũnenganae ĩa, nũnyaĩĩkasya ĩmwe, na nĩwĩkasya manzĩ make momĩtw'e nĩ mbevo me tũlungu,' na ĩndĩ akakũlya atĩĩ: "Nũũ ũtonya kũũngama mbee wa mbevo yake?" Ongeleele kwasya: "Nũetae ndeto yake, natw'o tũitweka." (Sav. 147:15-18) Ngai witũ nĩ mũĩ mũno na e vinya mwingĩ mũno. E ũtonyi ĩũlũ wa mbua ya mavia na ĩa na kwoou nũtonya kũũtetheesya ũsinde thĩna o na wĩva ũla ũtonya kũkomana naw'o.
16 Ũmũnthĩ Yeova atũtongoeasya atũmĩĩte Ndeto yake, Mbivilia. Na ĩla Mbivilia ĩkwasya "ndeto yake nĩsembaa mĩtũkĩ mũno," yĩtũtavya kana nũtwonasya nzĩa mĩtũkĩ ĩla twĩ na vata. Sũanĩa ũndũ ũtethekaa ĩla ũũsoma Mbivilia, ĩla ũũsoma mavuku ma "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ," ĩla ũkwĩloela JW Broadcasting, ĩla ũũsoma maũvoo nthĩnĩ wa jw.org, ĩla ũũneena na atumĩa, na ĩla ũkwĩka maũndũ vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ. (Mt. 24:45) O naku tyo wonete kana Yeova nũkwonasya nzĩa ĩla waĩle kwĩsĩla ateũselewa?
17 Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Simone nĩwĩyoneete vinya wa Ndeto ya Ngai. Navu ĩtina eew'aa ayĩmena mũno nginya avika vandũ weethĩa eona ta ũte vata methonĩ ma Ngai. Ĩndĩ mavinda ala weew'aa atũlĩkĩte ngoo vyũ avoyaa na kĩthito mũno aimwĩkaĩla Yeova amũtetheesye. O na nĩwatũmĩaa ĩvinda yingĩ aisoma Mbivilia. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndi ĩndĩ naaĩsa kwĩkala ngew'a Yeova ta wandekie nĩweka na aeka kũnenga vinya." Kyu nĩkĩmũtetheesye atate ũndũ ũtonya ethĩawe na woni ũla waĩle.
18. Nĩkĩ ũtonya kwasya kana wĩ mũathime nĩ Ngai, na wĩ na itumi syĩva sya kũkĩlya wasya ũkyasya, "Mũtaĩei Yeova"?
18 Mũandĩki wa Savuli nĩwamanyie kana andũ ma Ngai ma tene maĩ aathime mũno. No mo me oka maĩ mbaĩ ĩla Ngai wanengie "ndeto" yake na "myamũlo yake na motw'ĩo make." (Soma Savuli 147:19, 20.) Ũmũnthĩ twĩ aathime mũno, nũndũ vai angĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ eka ithyĩ metanĩaw'a na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Nĩtũtanĩaa kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova nũndũ nĩtwamũmanyie na nĩtwĩtĩkĩlaa Ndeto yake ĩthũkũme nthĩnĩ witũ. O ta mũandĩki wa Savuli ya 147, we ndũkwona wĩ na itumi mbingĩ nzeo mũno sya kũkĩlya wasya ũkyasya, "Mũtaĩei Yeova," na ũyĩkĩa angĩ vinya meke o taku?

translation:
"Praise Jehovah; it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting."—PSA. 147:1.
FOOTNOTE: 9, 152
1-3. (a) According to Psalm 147, what reason does it give for praising God? (b) What are some things we can think about as we read Psalm 147?
A humble person appreciates being able to serve Christ loyally. But why should we praise Jehovah God? We have so many reasons to praise him. Let us praise him for his wonderful works, which may seem small but are actually great. And let us praise him for his powerful acts on behalf of people, such as when he sent his Son as a ransom.
2 The writer of Psalm 147 was eager to praise Jehovah. And he encouraged others to join him in praising God.—Read Psalm 147:1, 7, 12.
3 As we read this psalm, remember that the writer likely lived at a time when the Israelites were returning from exile in Babylon and rebuilding Jerusalem with Jehovah's help. (Ps. 147:2) So the experiences of God's people then could move the psalmist to praise Jehovah. Also, he had other reasons to praise him. What were those reasons? Think about how you feel when you say "Praise Jah!"—Ps. 147:1; Rev. 19:1.
JEHOVAH RESTORES AND STRENGTHENS
4. What did the exiles who returned from Babylon experience, and why?
4 Consider what the Israelites experienced when they were exiled to Babylon. While there, they remembered Zion and mourned, saying: "Let us sing one of the songs of Zion." The ruins of Jerusalem reminded them of their need to honor Jehovah. (Ps. 137:1-3, 6) But they also had hope. They knew that Jehovah was able to restore them and provide them with food and water. God showed his willingness to use Cyrus, king of Persia, to fulfill his purpose. This king decreed that the temple in Babylon should be rebuilt and said: "Jehovah, the God of heaven, has commissioned me to build him a house in Jerusalem…and you yourselves are to set free the people, so that each one may go to his own city and his own property, and you, O Jehovah, are to be praised." (2 Chron. 36:23) How happy this news made the Israelites who were living in Babylon!
5. What motivated the psalmist to write about Jehovah's restorative power?
5 Jehovah is willing to help all of Israel, even individuals. He understands our feelings and cares for us personally. The psalmist wrote about God's ability: "He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds." (Ps. 147:3) Yes, Jehovah comforts those who are grieving, and he strengthens those who are weak and helps them to recover. Jehovah is always ready to support and encourage us. (Ps. 34:18; Isa. 57:15) Let us therefore pray confidently and ask for wisdom from God, especially when we face difficulties.—Jas. 1:5.
6. Why can the psalmist confidently say that Psalm 147:4 applies to us today? (See accompanying article, page 17.)
6 This psalm writer also expressed confidence in God's power to accomplish his purpose. He assured us that Jehovah "pays attention to the humble ones" and "gives strength to the powerless." (Ps. 147:4) Consider how this applies to us as we strive to expand our ministry and teach others about God's Word. Think about this: This psalm writer could see only what his physical eyes allowed him to see, yet he knew God's potential. Today, we have learned much more about the universe than people did in ancient times. Some estimate that there are billions of stars in our Milky Way galaxy alone. And there may be billions of galaxies like ours! It is truly amazing to contemplate the vastness of creation! Yet, our Creator knows each star by name. This shows that Jehovah is aware of every detail of his creation. (1 Cor. 15:41) But does he care about individual humans? Our God knows every person intimately, and he cares deeply for us. He is aware of our needs and challenges, and he is eager to help us succeed, now and forever!
7, 8. (a) How does Jehovah show that he values our life? (b) Explain why it is comforting to know that Jehovah is moved by our feelings and desires.
7 Jehovah personally values each of us. He doesn't want to see anyone suffer needlessly, and he delights when we use our free will wisely. (Read Psalm 147:5.) He can foresee the future, but he allows us to make choices, and he respects those choices. He understands that God is compassionate and forgiving, and that he "does not deal with us according to our sins." (Ps. 103:14) So, despite our imperfections, he loves us. And he wants us to experience joy and satisfaction in life. For example, he appreciates it when we put effort into improving our skills, whether it is in our secular work or in spiritual activities. And he encourages us to trust in him completely, knowing that he will support us and give us the strength to do what is right.—Is. 40:28.
8 Do not be afraid of facing difficulties, knowing that Jehovah is with you and that he cares about your well-being. (Is. 41:10, 13) Consider the example of a sister named Kyoko. She was assigned to preach in a territory where people were very hostile. At first, she felt overwhelmed and discouraged. But Jehovah strengthened her, and she continued preaching. Did Jehovah overlook her fear? It encouraged Kyoko to remember that Jehovah knows how we feel and that he will help us. She told herself: "Jehovah, please do not let me become fearful, but help me to remain courageous because I am your servant and I want to please you." And so, the Almighty God helped her to overcome her fear.—Isaiah 41:10.
JEHOVAH STRENGTHENS US
9, 10. Does Jehovah always answer our prayers immediately? Explain.
9 We often face problems that seem overwhelming, such as sickness, accidents, and unkind people. For example, you might try hard to find work, but still struggle to make ends meet. However, Jehovah can help us cope with difficult situations, and he can also use his spirit to strengthen us so that we can endure trials! (Read Psalm 147:8, 9.) Remember that Jehovah cares for us, and he is willing to help us even when things seem hopeless.—Ps. 37:25.
10 Another way that Jehovah supports us is by giving us comfort. He has been described as "the God of all comfort." (2 Cor. 4:6, 7) Recently, this was true for Mitsuo and his wife. In 2011, when an earthquake and resulting huge wave (tsunami) struck Japan, they saw that Jehovah truly helps. They lost their home. But thankfully, everyone in their family survived, and their house was spared. That night they huddled together in their car. It was cold and dark. Later, they learned about a book called the 2006 Yearbooks of Jehovah's Witnesses. The article that Mitsuo read was titled "The Worst Tsunami Ever Recorded." This article discussed the devastating tsunami that hit Sumatra in 2004. That disaster caused the deadliest tsunami in recorded history, surpassing all previous tsunamis. Mitsuo and his wife realized how fortunate they were to have survived. Reading that article helped them understand that God cares for us deeply and protects us. And they also understood that Jehovah can help us cope with difficulties. They appreciated the comfort found in God's Word. Mitsuo said, "We felt so grateful that Jehovah heard our prayers. We really feel blessed!" So, like those who experienced God's support, we too can be comforted. And as we continue to live, we will likely face more challenges.
KEEP TRUSTING JEHOVAH
11. What will help us to trust in Jehovah always?
11 Every day, Jehovah shows his care for us in countless ways, even by helping us with our daily needs. (Ps. 147:6a) How can we show that we trust him? By being thankful and appreciating what he does for us. This demonstrates our faith. (Prov. 2:3) But faith also means believing that God will fulfill his promises. Jehovah wants us to trust in him.
12, 13. (a) What can we do to please Jehovah when he helps us? (b) What does Jehovah expect of us?
12 Are you facing trials right now? The Bible says that God "supports the crushed ones." (Ps. 147:6b) We should never give up! When we speak to Jehovah in prayer with sincerity and express our gratitude, he will listen. (Ps. 97:10) For example, we can strive to obey him fully. That means avoiding things that displease him and making changes in our lives when necessary, as well as examining our thoughts and actions. (Ps. 119:37; Matt. 5:28) And by striving to maintain a close relationship with him, we demonstrate our love for Jehovah and our desire to please him.
13 We need to be careful about what influences us, and we need to be especially careful to focus on pleasing Jehovah. Does Jehovah want us to avoid "wicked associations," or, rather, people who do not share our values? Yes, he does. So too, we need to be careful about "worldly desires," which could lead us to do things that are wrong or that others might disapprove of. (Ps. 147:10) If we do this, we will make Jehovah happy, and he will continue to help us. Jehovah knows what is best for us. He cares deeply for us, and the more we get to know him, the more we will appreciate his guidance. The Bible states, "Jehovah takes pleasure in those who fear him, those who hope in his loving-kindness." (Ps. 147:11) So let us remain confident and trust in his loving-kindness, knowing that he will support and guide us through difficult times.
14 What motivated the psalmist to write what he did?
14 Jehovah can use his spirit to strengthen us and to help us encourage others. The psalmist was inspired by Jehovah to describe the restoration of Jerusalem. He wrote: "I firmly established my gates; I protected my people from disaster. He sent out his word with great speed." (Ps. 147:13, 14) Seeing how God was able to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem quickly demonstrated his power, and this encouraged the psalmist.
15-17. (a) What are some ways we can show that we value Jehovah's direction? (b) How does the expression 'God's word is alive' apply to us?
15 We can be moved by what we read to take action. Consider this: Does Jehovah really care about our struggles? The psalmist expressed his confidence in God: "He gives strength to the weary; his word is very reliable." He then explained how Jehovah 'fastens shut the gate, so no wicked person can escape,' and added: "Can you scrutinize his works? They are beyond your full understanding!" He asked: "Let us pay attention to his word and let us prove ourselves trustworthy." (Ps. 147:15-18) Our God is powerful and has shown his power in many ways. He can deliver us from difficult situations and protect us from danger, and he can help us cope with problems.
16 Jehovah encourages us to use his Word, the Bible. And since the Bible says that "his word is very reliable," we can trust that it will guide us correctly. To benefit fully, regularly read the Bible, study publications like "Questions Young People Ask—Answers That Work," watch JW Broadcasting, visit jw.org, speak to publishers, and associate with fellow Christians. (Matt. 24:45) But how will you know that Jehovah is guiding you when there are so many options available?
17 A faithful man named Simon came to appreciate the value of God's Word. Because of his sincere desire to please God, he was willing to learn from others. He also realized that Jehovah responds to those who seek him diligently. So he asked for more help in reading the Bible. He said: "I want to become someone who belongs to Jehovah so that I can continue to serve him faithfully." This motivated him to find out what he could do to improve.
18. How can you show that you are determined to please God, and how can you then ask, "Where should I look?"
18 The psalmist David knew that God's people need guidance. He prayed that God would remember his "word" and his "loving-kindness and judgments." (Read Psalm 147:19, 20.) When we pray for guidance, we demonstrate our confidence in God's willingness to help us. We strengthen our relationship with Jehovah when we value and apply his Word in our lives. So, like the psalmist in Psalm 147, may we always feel moved to ask, "Where should I look?" and be eager to receive direction.

text:
"Kiakian'yai, na kĩla mũndũ akyaka ũla ũngĩ." —1 ATH. 5:11.
MBATHI: 53, 28
1, 2. Nĩkĩ nũseo tũneenee ũndũ tũtonya kũkiakisya ala makw'ĩĩwe? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MWĨĨTU-A-ASA ũmwe wĩtawa Susi aisye atĩĩ: "Twekalile vandũ va mwaka ta ũmwe ũu tũyĩw'a kyeva kingĩ mũno ĩtina wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ kĩmwana kitũ." Nake Mũklĩsto ũngĩ aĩtye kana mũka akwie atataĩĩe na kuma vau eew'aa 'mwĩĩ wake ũyalya ũndũ ũtaĩ aelesya.' Ũthũku nĩ kana ve andũ angĩ aingĩ matatalĩka makwatĩtwe nĩ kyeva ta kĩu. Aingĩ me kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa mataasũanĩa kana endwa moo nĩmesa kũkw'a Ali–Maketoni ĩte mbiku. Wĩthĩwe wĩmũkw'ĩĩe kana nĩwĩsĩ mũndũ mũna mũkw'ĩĩe, nũtonya kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Ala me na kyeva matonya kũtetheew'a ata momĩanĩsye na woo ngoonĩ syoo?'
2 Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa waaĩw'a andũ mayasya thĩna ũthelaa na ĩvinda. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Woo wĩ ngoonĩ ya mũndũ nũtonya kũthela na ĩvinda vate ũndũ ũkwĩkwa? Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũũme aisye ũũ: "Nĩsĩte kwĩthĩa nĩ kavaa kwasya kana kĩla kĩtetheeasya mũndũ kũvoa nĩ ũndũ ũkũtũmĩa ĩvinda yĩla wĩ nayo." O tondũ kĩtau kĩsaa ũvoa o kavola kyaiitwa nesa, kyeva kĩla kĩthĩawa ngoonĩ no kĩoleke ĩtina wa ĩvinda ethĩwa nĩkĩũthĩnĩkĩwa nesa. Kyo nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya ala makw'ĩĩwe nĩ kana kyeva kyoo kĩoleke?
YEOVA NĨWE "NGAI WA ŨKIAKISYO W'ONTHE"
3, 4. Ĩla mũndũ wĩ na kyeva, nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Yeova nũeleawa kana mũndũ ũsu nĩwaĩle kũkiakiw'a?
3 Vate nzika, ũla ũtũkiakiasya vyũ nĩ Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ, Yeova, nũndũ e tei. (Soma 2 Akolintho 1:3, 4.) Vai ũngĩ ũeleawa nesa ũndũ tũkwĩw'a ta Yeova. Aĩkĩĩthisye andũ make amea atĩĩ: "Nyie, o nyie; ninyie ũla ũkũkiakiasya."—Isa. 51:12; Sav. 119:50, 52, 76.
4 O nake Ĩthe witũ wa matei mololo nĩwakw'ĩĩwe nĩ endwa make ta Avalaamu, Isaka, Yakovo, Mose, na Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti. (Mot. 12:6-8; Mt. 22:31, 32; Meko 13:22) Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana Yeova ethĩawa na mea maingĩ, kana nĩweteele mũno mũthenya ũla ũkamathayũũkya. (Yovu 14:14, 15) Mathayũũkw'a makekalaa me atanu na me na mĩĩ mĩseo. O na ĩngĩ lilikana kana ve ĩvinda Mwana wa Ngai mwendwa, ũla waĩ "ũtanu wake kĩla mũthenya," wakwie kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo mũno. (Nth. 8:22, 30) Vai mũndũ ũtonya kũelesya nesa woo ũla Yeova weewie ĩvinda yĩu.—Yoa. 5:20; 10:17.
5, 6. Yeova atonya kũtũkiakisya kwa nzĩa yĩva?
5 No twĩkale tũte na nzika o na vanini kana Yeova akatũtetheeasya. Kwoou ĩla twĩ na kyeva tũyaĩle kũemwa nĩ kũmũvoya nĩ kana tũmũtulũĩle ngoo sitũ. Kũmanya kana Yeova nũeleawa kyeva kĩla twĩthĩawa nakyo na nũtũkiakiasya nesa, nĩkũtwĩkĩaa vinya mũno. Ĩndĩ we atũkiakiasya ata?
6 Ũndũ ũmwe Ngai ũtwĩkĩaa vinya naw'o nĩ kwĩsĩla "ũkiakisyonĩ wa Veva Mũtheu." (Meko 9:31) Vinya ũsu Ngai ũtũmĩaa kwĩka maũndũ wĩthĩawa ũtonya kũtũkiakisya mũno. Yesũ atwathie kana Asa witũ akeethĩawa eyũmbanĩtye "kũmanenga Veva Mũtheu ala mamwĩtasya." (Luka 11:13) Ũla Susi twĩĩ tũnamũweta aisye atĩĩ: "Ve mavinda maingĩ mũno tweekaa kũtulya ndu tũkamwĩsũva Yeova atũkiakisye. Kĩla ĩvinda tweeka ũu, mũuo wa Ngai nĩwasũvĩaa ngoo sitũ na mosũanĩo maitũ."—Soma Avilivi 4:6, 7.
YESŨ NĨ MŨTHEMBI MŨNENE WĨ TEI MWINGĨ
7, 8. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana Yesũ akatũkiakiasya?
7 Tei wa Yeova nĩwoonekie nesa kwĩsĩla Mwana wake, Yesũ. Ũndũ ũsu woonekie nesa vyũ ndetonĩ ila Yesũ waneenaa na maũndũnĩ ala weekaa e kũũ nthĩ. (Yoa. 5:19) Yesũ atũmiwe oke kũkiakisya ala "me na ngoo ndũlĩku" na "onthe ala mametaa." (Isa. 61:1, 2; Luka 4:17-21) Kwoou nĩweesĩkĩe ta mũndũ wĩ tei mwingĩ, mũndũ waeleawa ĩla angĩ meũthĩna na waĩ na wendi mwingĩ ngoonĩ wa kũmavetea thĩna woo.—Aevl. 2:17.
8 Tũi na nzika kana ĩla Yesũ waĩ wa mũika nĩwakw'ĩĩwe nĩ andũ amwe ma mũsyĩ na anyanyae. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yosevu, ũla waeie Yesũ, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa akwie Yesũ e o wa mũika. * Kwasũanĩa ũndũ kĩu kĩthĩwa kyamũitavĩie! No kwĩthĩwa aĩ na myaka ĩkũmi na kĩndũ kana akethĩwa no ĩndĩ waĩ anavikya myaka 20. E mũnini ũu nĩwalasimĩkie kũmĩanĩsya na kyeva kyake na kya inyia na ala angĩ masyaanĩw'e.
9. Yesũ oonanisye ata kana e tei ĩla Lasalo wakwie?
9 Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ, nĩwaeleawa vyũ ũndũ andũ mekwĩw'a na nĩwamew'ĩaa tei. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ĩla mũnyanyae, Lasalo, wakwie. O na kũtw'ĩka Yesũ nĩweesĩ nũkũmũthayũũkya, nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kyeva kingĩ mũno oona ũndũ Meli na Matha maemeewe nĩ kyeva. Kĩndũ kyu kyamũtinie na kyamũũmĩsya ngoonĩ nginya etĩkya methoi.—Yoa. 11:33-36.
10. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yesũ nũtwĩw'ĩaa tei ũmũnthĩ?
10 O tondũ twoona, Yesũ aĩ tei na nĩwakiakiasya angĩ. Kũmanya ũu kũtonya kũtũtethya ata ũmũnthĩ? Maandĩko matũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana "Yesũ Klĩsto no ũndũ ũmwe ĩoo na ũmũnthĩ, ĩĩ, o na kũvika tene na tene." (Aevl. 13:8) Na nũndũ e "Mũnene wa thayũ" nũeleawa nesa ũndũ mũndũ wĩ na kyeva wĩw'aa, "nũtonya kũmatetheesya ala matatawa." (Meko 3:15; Aevl. 2:10, 18) Kwoou tũikethĩwe na nzika kana kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, Klĩsto nũthĩnĩkaa oona angĩ me na thĩna, nũeleawa kyeva kĩla me nakyo, na nũmanengae ũtethyo "ĩvinda ya vata."—Soma Aevelania 4:15, 16.
"ŨKIAKISYO WA MAANDĨKO"
11. Nĩ maandĩko meva wĩw'aa maiũkiakisya mũno?
11 Ĩandĩko yĩla yĩeleetye ũndũ Yesũ weewie thĩna mwingĩ ĩla Lasalo wakwie nĩ yĩmwe katĩ wa maandĩko ala matũkiakiasya mũno Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. Na ũsu ti ũsengy'o "nũndũ maũndũ o na meva ala mambie kũandĩkwa, nĩmaandĩkiwe nũndũ wa kũtũmanyĩasya, nĩ kana ũndũ wa wũmĩĩsyo na ũkiakisyo wa maandĩko twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo." (Alo. 15:4) Ethĩwa wĩ na kyeva, o naku no ũkiakiw'e nĩ maandĩko ta aa maatĩĩe:
"Yeova e vakuvĩ na ala matũlĩkĩte ngoo, na nũtangĩĩaa ala mekwĩlila vevanĩ."—Sav. 34:18, 19.
"Mosũanĩonĩ makwa maingĩ nthĩnĩ wakwa mokiakisyo maku [Yeova] matan'ya ngoo yakwa."—Sav. 94:19.
"Na yu Mwĩaĩi waitũ Yesũ Klĩsto mwene, na Ngai Asa waitũ ũla watwendie na kũtũnenga ũkiakisyo ũtathela na wĩkwatyo mũseo kwondũ wa mumo, nakiakisye ngoo syenyu na kwilũlũmĩlya."—2 Ath. 2:16, 17. *
KĨKUNDI NĨKĨTŨKIAKIASYA MŨNO
12. Nĩ ũndũ ũmwe wĩva wa vata tũtonya kwĩka tũkakiakisya angĩ?
12 Vandũ vangĩ Aklĩsto ala me na kyeva matonya kũkwata ũkiakisyo nĩ kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. (Soma 1 Athesalonika 5:11.) Ũtonya kwĩkĩa vinya ata na kũkiakisya ala me na "veva mũtũlĩku"? (Nth. 17:22) Ĩkalaa ũlilikene kana ve "ĩvinda ya kũvindya, na ĩvinda ya kũneena." (Mũta. 3:7) Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Dalene wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũũme aeleetye atĩĩ: "Ala makw'ĩĩwe nĩmendaa kũelesya kĩla meũsũanĩa na ũndũ mekwĩw'a ngoonĩ. Kwoou kĩla kya vata vyũ ũtonya kũtethya mũndũ ũkw'ĩĩwe nakyo nĩ kũmwĩthukĩĩsya ũte kũmũtilĩĩla." Nake mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũngĩ wĩtawa Junia, ũla waĩ na mwana-a-inyia weeyũaie, awetete ũũ: "O na kau nũtonya kũema kũelewa nesa kyeva kĩla me nakyo, kĩla kya vata nĩ we mwene wĩthĩwe ũyenda kũelewa ũndũ mekwĩw'a."
13. Twaĩle kũlilikana kyaũ ĩũlũ wa kyeva?
13 O na ĩngĩ nũseo ũkekalaa ũlilikene kana andũ maivw'ananaa, na kwoou kyeva kya andũ kĩyĩthĩawa kĩvw'anene na mayĩyĩeleasya ũndũ ũmwe. Mavinda amwe no mũndũ mwene ũeleawa nesa vyũ woo ũla wĩ ngoonĩ yake na ũyĩthĩa ti laisi kũtavya angĩ ũndũ ũkwĩw'a. Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ngoo nĩyĩsĩ ũũ wayo e yo; na mũeni ndelikasya ũtanunĩ wayo." (Nth. 14:10) O na mũndũ akaelesya ata ũndũ ũkwĩw'a, ti laisi mavinda onthe ala angĩ makaelewa kĩla ũkũmatavya.
14. Tũtonya kumya va ndeto sya kũtavya ala makw'ĩĩwe?
14 Nũndũ wa ũu, ti laisi kũmanya ũndũ ũtonya kũtavya mũndũ ũemeewe nĩ kyeva, na nengĩ ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũkũeleeka. O na vailyĩ ũu, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "ũĩmĩ wa ũla mũĩ nũvoasya." (Nth. 12:18) Aingĩ nĩmakwatĩte ndeto itonya kũmatetheesya makiakisye angĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩla mbulosua yĩtawa Mtu Fulani Umpendaye Anapokufa. * Ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ kĩndũ kĩla kya vata vyũ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ 'kũĩa na ala mekũĩa.' (Alo. 12:15) Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Gaby wakw'ĩĩwe nĩ mũũme aĩtye: "Kĩla yu nĩkothaa kwĩka nonany'e ũndũ ngwĩw'a no kũĩa. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi nĩw'aa nausya ĩla anyanyawa maĩa nakwa. Mavindanĩ ta asu ndyĩw'aa ta nĩekanĩw'e na kyeva kyakwa nĩ weka."
15. Tũtonya kũkiakisya mũndũ ata ethĩwa nĩtwaemwa nĩ kũmũtavya ũndũ twenene? (O na ĩngĩ sisya kasandũkũ "Ndeto Nzeo Syaĩ na Ũkiakisyo.")
15 Ũkaemwa nĩ kũtavya mũndũ ũndũ mwenene, no ũmũtũmĩe kaati ya kũmũkiakisya, e-mail, mesengyi ya simũ, kana o valũa. No ũandĩke ĩandĩko wĩw'aa yĩtonya kũkiakisya mũndũ, ũkaandĩka ũndũ mũseo wĩsĩ ĩũlũ wa ũla ũkwie kana nguma yake nzeo, kana o ũkaandĩka kĩndũ watanĩie kwĩka nake. Junia aĩtye: "Ĩla nakwata mesengyi nguvĩ ya kũmbĩkĩa vinya kana ĩla nathokw'a nĩ Mũklĩsto ũngĩ tũtũmĩe ĩvinda ĩmwe, nĩw'aa natetheka ũndũ ndaeleekya. Ĩla angĩ meeka ũu matumaa nĩmanya nĩnendetwe na nĩngũthĩnĩkĩwa."
16. Nĩ nzĩa ĩngĩ yĩva nzeo mũno ya kũkiakisya mũndũ?
16 Ndũkaaĩse kwona mboya ila tũvoyaa vamwe na Mũklĩsto ũkw'ĩĩwe kana kwondũ wake ta itatethasya. Nũtonya kwĩw'a vinya kũvoya nesa ĩvindanĩ ta yĩu o naku ũkwĩw'a wĩmũitavĩe ngoonĩ, ĩndĩ mboya ila ũtonya kũvoya nake, o na ethĩwa wĩvoya ũĩĩte na ũte kũneena nesa, nitonya kũmũkiakisya mũno. Dalene aĩtye: "Mavinda amwe ĩla eĩtu-a-asa mooka kũngiakisya nĩmakũlasya ethĩwa no mende kũvoya. Mayambĩĩa kũvoya maneenaa maiemwa, ĩndĩ kĩla ĩvinda o ũndũ maendeea na mboya now'o wasya woo ũkwataa vinya, na mũthya mavoyaa mboya ĩkũkiita ngoo vyũ. Mũĩkĩĩo woo mũlũmu, wendo woo, na kũnthĩnĩkĩa kũla manthĩnĩkĩaa nĩkũlũlũmĩlĩtye mũĩkĩĩo wakwa."
ENDEEA KŨMAKIAKISYA
17-19. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũendeea kũkiakisya ala makw'ĩĩwe?
17 Ĩvinda yĩla mũndũ ũmwe ũtonya kwĩkala na kyeva no yĩthĩwe yĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ya ũla ũngĩ. Kwoou tata ũtũmĩe ĩvinda ĩasanga na ũsu ũkw'ĩĩwe. Vandũ va kwĩkala nake mĩthenya o ĩla andũ ma mũsyĩ na anyanyae me vo, endeea kwĩthĩwa vakuvĩ nake myei yĩana ũna ĩtina wa ala angĩ kũsyoka maũndũnĩ moo. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Mũnyanya nĩwendanaa ĩndĩ yonthe; na mwana-a-ĩthe asyaiwe kwondũ wa kũthĩnũkasya." (Nth. 17:17) Twĩ Aklĩsto nĩtwaĩle kũendeea kũkiakisya mũndũ o na ethĩwa kyeva kyake kĩkua ĩvinda yĩana ata.—Soma 1 Athesalonika 3:7.
18 Lilikana kana mũndũ no ambĩĩe kwĩw'a kyeva ĩngĩ nũndũ wa maũndũ ũkũmakonany'a na mwendwa wake ta mũthenya woo wa alũsi, wathi mũna, visa, maũndũ mana meekaa, o na mũnyungo mũna, wasya mũna, kana ĩvinda ĩna ya mwaka. Mũndũ akw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũũme kana mũka, maũndũ maingĩ ala wĩkaa ya mbee e weka, ta kwa ngelekany'o, kũthi ũmbanonĩ mũnene kana ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, nĩmatonya kũmũetee kyeva kingĩ. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe aisye: "No neesĩ kana mwaka wa mbee ĩtina wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũka wakwa ngathĩnĩka mũno mũthenya ũla twatwaanie wavika, na ũu now'o vailyĩ. Ĩndĩ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa amwe nĩmavangĩthisye kyathĩ kĩnini vamwe na ala nĩ ndũũ namo vyũ nĩ kana mũthenya ũsu ndikatinde nĩ nyioka."
19 Ĩndĩ manya kana ala makw'ĩĩwe nĩmaĩle kwĩkĩwa vinya kĩla ĩvinda na ti o ĩla kwĩ maũndũ ma mwanya. Junia aeleetye atĩĩ: "Mavinda maingĩ ĩla andũ matethya ũla ũkw'ĩĩwe na matinda nake ĩla kũte ũndũ mũna wa mwanya, kĩu nĩkĩtethasya mũno. Kwĩka kaũndũ mwĩ ĩmwe mavinda ta asu vate ũndũ mũnene mũvangĩĩe nĩ kwa vata mũno na nĩkũtonya kũkiakisya mũno." Nĩ w'o kana tũitonya kũmina vyũ kyeva kĩla mũndũ wĩ nakyo nũndũ wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mwendwa wake, na tũitonya kusũsya mwanya ũla ũnatiiwe, ĩndĩ no tũtate o vala tũtonya tũkamũkiakisya kwa kwĩka maũndũ mana ma vata tũmũtetheesye. (1 Yoa. 3:18) Gaby aĩtye: "Nĩnĩtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mũno na atumĩa nũndũ nĩmandetheeisye ĩvindanĩ yĩu yonthe yetu. Mandetheetye vyũ ngew'a Yeova ta ũngwete na moko make."
20. Nĩkĩ mawatho ma Yeova matũkiakiasya mũno?
20 Tũkiakiaw'a mũno twamanya kana Yeova, Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe, akaveta kyeva kyonthe na aithyũmũsya andũ vyũ ĩla ndeto ii ikeanĩa: "Onthe ala me mbũanĩ makew'a wasya wake [Klĩsto], namo makauma"! (Yoa. 5:28, 29) Ngai athanĩte kana 'akamelya kĩkw'ũ tene na tene; na Mwĩaĩi Yeova akavyaĩa methoi mothyũnĩ onthe.' (Isa. 25:8) Ĩla ũndũ ũsu ũkekĩka, tũikasyoka ĩngĩ 'kũĩa na ala mekũĩa,' vandũ va ũu tũkeekaa 'kũtana vamwe na ala meũtana'!—Alo. 12:15.
^ kal. 8 Yosevu awetetwe ya mwĩso ĩla Yesũ waĩ na myaka 12. Yosevu ti mũwete ĩvindanĩ yĩla Yesũ weekie kyama kyake kya mbee kya kũvĩndũa kĩw'ũ kĩtw'ĩke mbinyu. O na vai ĩvinda yĩngĩ ũwetetwe ĩtina wa vau. Na ĩla Yesũ waĩ mũtĩnĩ wa mathĩna, anengie mũtũmwa Yoana wĩa wa kũmũsũvĩa Meli. Keka Yosevu aĩ thayũ, Yesũ ndethĩwa aaĩka ũu.—Yoa. 19:26, 27.
^ kal. 11 Maandĩko angĩ makiakĩĩtye andũ aingĩ nĩ ta Savuli 20:1, 2; 31:7; 38:8, 9, 15; 55:22; 121:1, 2; Isaia 57:15; 66:13; Avilivi 4:13; na 1 Vetelo 5:7.
^ kal. 14 O na ĩngĩ no ũsisye kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, "Wafariji Waliofiwa Kama Yesu Alivyofanya," ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/11/2010.

translation:
"Be industrious, and each person will reap what he sows." —1 THESS. 5:11.
NOTES: 53, 28
1, 2. Why is it important for us to be diligent in our ministry, especially when people show little interest? (Consider practical examples.)
ONE sister named Susi explains: "We spent almost a year visiting one family, and finally the mother allowed us to give her daughter a publication." Another Christian said that his wife was upset because he kept spending time helping others, feeling that he was neglecting his own family. However, she realized that he was showing love for their neighbor. Often many people are troubled by problems. Many who profess to be Christians find it difficult to live up to their claims, and some may even feel hypocritical. So if someone expresses doubts about your faith, you can reason with him by asking: "Is it possible that I am not the only one struggling with this?"
2 We should also be patient with those who are discouraged or facing difficulties. One reason why this is important is: Can we understand what causes a person to become discouraged or lose hope? A housewife explained: "I used to think that if something bothered a person, they could just stop thinking about it." But often a problem continues to bother a person until it is resolved. Therefore, it is helpful to listen carefully and try to understand how another feels. But does that mean we should excuse wrong behavior?
JEHOVAH IS "THE GOD OF ALL COMFORT"
3, 4. If a person has a problem, how can we know whether Jehovah understands how that person feels?
3 Of course, our loving Father, Jehovah, cares for us deeply. (Read 2 Corinthians 1:3, 4.) He fully appreciates the challenges we face. He assured his servants of this when he said: "O you people, yes, you; you are the ones whom I comfort." —Isa. 51:12; Ps. 119:50, 52, 76.
4 Our faithful God has comforted imperfect humans like Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, and King David. (Gen. 12:6-8; Matt. 22:31, 32; Mark 13:22) God's promise assures us that Jehovah will continue to show compassion, and that he will provide comfort during times of distress. (Job 14:14, 15) His comfort can come in many ways. And sometimes it comes through his Son, the beloved Messiah, who "has experienced everything" we go through. (Prov. 8:22, 30) So a person can find comfort knowing that Jehovah knows how he feels.—John 5:20; 10:17.
5, 6. How can Jehovah comfort us in practical ways?
5 Let us now consider some specific ways in which Jehovah comforts us. Often, when we are grieving, we need someone to listen to us and sympathize with us. Knowing that Jehovah understands how we feel and that he cares for us can bring us great relief. But who provides such comfort?
6 One way God comforts us is through "gifts in men." (Eph. 4:8) He uses people to help us cope with difficult situations. Jesus taught his followers to ask their Father for "holy spirit." (Luke 11:13) Thus, we can pray confidently, saying: "Jehovah, please send your spirit to comfort us. Help us to express our feelings so that you may comfort us." With each expression of our feelings, God's spirit can work on our hearts.—Read Proverbs 4:6, 7.
JESUS IS A GREAT COMFORTER
7, 8. Why can we be confident that Jesus will comfort us?
7 Jehovah's greatest gift is his Son, Jesus. The fact that Jehovah sent his Son shows just how much he values us. (John 3:16) Jesus understands our problems because he personally experienced suffering while on earth. (Heb. 5:19) Jesus was sent to proclaim good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, and to declare liberty to captives. (Isa. 61:1, 2; Luke 4:17-21) Therefore, he is uniquely qualified to comfort those who are distressed.—Acts 2:17.
8 We can be sure that Jesus cares for us deeply, even though he is surrounded by imperfect humans. For example, Joseph, who was a friend of Jesus, was able to comfort Jesus when he was grieving. *Think about what this means! It would have been easy to feel sorry for oneself when facing difficulties. But Joseph focused on supporting his friend.
9. How did Jesus respond when Lazarus died?
9 When Jesus was on earth, he showed empathy for others and shared their grief. Consider the example of Lazarus, a friend of Jesus, who died. Although Jesus knew that he could resurrect Lazarus, he allowed himself to become visibly moved when Martha and Mary expressed their sorrow. His reaction demonstrated genuine compassion.—John 11:33-36.
10. Why can we be confident that Jesus will continue to comfort us?
10 To a large extent, Jesus feels our pain and understands our struggles. Does this understanding help us in any way? The Scriptures assure us that "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever." (Hebrews 13:8) And the prophecy regarding the "Seed of the woman" assures us that she will experience relief from suffering.—Matthew 3:15; Acts 2:10, 18. So, even though we may face trials, Christ remains sympathetic, understands our feelings, and offers practical support.—Read Hebrews 4:15, 16.
"UNDERSTANDING THE SCRIPTURES"
11. What scriptures show that God is compassionate?
11 One scripture that shows how much Jesus cares about us is Psalm 30, which is part of the inspired writings. But it does not say, "everything that has happened or will happen is recorded in the Bible so that we can understand it, or that everything is predetermined and the scriptures reveal it to us." (Acts 15:4) Rather, they teach us what God does:
"Jehovah draws near to those broken at heart, and saves those crushed in spirit."—Psalm 34:18, 19.
"The loyal love of Jehovah is toward those who fear him, and his loving-kindness extends to all who observe his commandments."—Psalm 94:19.
"And may our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father, who loved us and gave us comfort beyond what words can express, comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word."—2 Thessalonians 2:16, 17. *
WHAT HELPS US TO UNDERSTAND MORE
12. What is one thing we can do to deepen our understanding?
12 Many Christians find that meditating on the Scriptures helps them to appreciate them more fully. (Read 1 Thessalonians 5:11.) Can you also meditate on what others have said when explaining the Scriptures? (Acts 17:22) Consider using "the gift of discernment" and "the gift of speaking." (1 Corinthians 3:7) A sister named Delaine explained: "I try to think about what each verse means to me personally. I ask myself, 'How can this help me to be a better person?' " Another sister, Junia, who is raising a young family, says: "I often reflect on what I learn from the meetings and then think about how it applies to my life."
13. How can we benefit from meditation?
13 And if you regularly meditate on spiritual things, you will feel closer to Jehovah, and your love for his people will grow stronger. The Bible shows that a thoughtful person considers the consequences of his actions and is careful not to rush into things. God's Word states: "The heart of the prudent knows the proper time to act." (Proverbs 14:10) So even if you are busy, take the time to meditate on what you learn.
14. What steps can we take to make our meditations meaningful?
14 To begin with, remember that meditating means thinking deeply about something, and it requires effort. Also, the Bible says that "wisdom calls out in the street." (Proverbs 12:18) Many find it helpful to use scriptures when they meditate, such as those found in books like "When Someone You Love Dies." * Often, much comfort can be gained from simply repeating key thoughts to yourself—'thinking them over and over.' (Acts 12:15) For example, Gaby, a sister, said: "Whenever I feel sad, I try to think about positive things and repeat them to myself. That helps me cope with my feelings and stay calm. Thinking about Jehovah and knowing that he cares for me comforts me."
15. How can we help others who are grieving? (See also the box "Practical Suggestions for Comforting Others.")
15 When comforting someone, don't just tell them what to do; instead, offer practical help, such as sending an email, a text message, or a card. And when writing a note to comfort someone, mention specific qualities you admire in that person or share a fond memory you have of him or her. June recalls: "I received a lovely letter from a friend who told me how much she appreciated our friendship and how she remembered a happy time we had together. It really encouraged me and helped me feel loved."
16. What more can we do to comfort others?
16 Sometimes simply listening is the best way to comfort a fellow Christian or visit him or her at home. We can also offer to help with chores or errands, or we can simply spend time with them. However, be careful not to give unsolicited advice. Instead, let them know you care and are willing to listen. Delaine says: "Sometimes people just need to vent their feelings without being judged or criticized. Let them express themselves freely, and then offer support and encouragement. Remember that showing empathy—understanding and sharing their feelings—can be very comforting. Your kindness, your love, and your willingness to listen will mean a great deal to them."
KEEP COMFORTING OTHERS
17-19. How can we continue to comfort those around us?
17 One way to show genuine concern is to remember that each person has unique experiences and faces different challenges. So avoid making generalizations or comparisons. Instead, try to understand what they are going through. Many find comfort in knowing that others care about them deeply and sincerely. The Bible states: "A true companion loves at all times, and is a brother born for adversity." (Prov. 17:17) As Christians, we want to continue to comfort those who are struggling emotionally.—Read 1 Thessalonians 3:7.
18 Consider how you would feel if someone were to offer unsolicited advice regarding a personal matter, especially when you are already feeling vulnerable, upset, or overwhelmed—perhaps because of financial difficulties, health problems, or a recent loss. A person may be comforted by a friend or family member, but often such help is insufficient, and they need more than just sympathy or encouragement; they need practical assistance. One young man said: "I didn't need anyone to tell me what I should have done differently during the difficult time we went through, and that doesn't help now. My parents and other relatives did a lot to support us, but sometimes I felt like I needed something more concrete."
19 But many people find it hard to accept help, perhaps fearing that it comes with strings attached or that it will compromise their independence. June explains: "Many times people who are going through trials don't want others to get involved in their private affairs, and they become defensive. It can be hard to persuade them to let you help, and it's easy to offend them." So how can we show genuine concern for those who are struggling without overstepping boundaries, and how can we offer practical help without making them feel indebted? (1 John 3:18) Gabe says: "I try to appeal to Jehovah's love for people and remind myself that he wants me to comfort my brothers and sisters. I try to do things that will genuinely help them, rather than just saying nice words."
20 What motivates Jehovah to extend such kindness to us?
20 We appreciate his kindness when we realize that Jehovah, the God of all comfort, has the power to undo all the effects of sin and suffering and promises to do so: "All those in the memorial tombs will come out." (John 5:28, 29) God assures us that he will 'swallow up death forever; and the Lord Jehovah will wipe away tears from all faces.' (Isaiah 25:8) In view of this hope, we can now endure 'affliction along with affliction,' and those who persecute us can experience 'affliction for affliction!'—Acts 12:15.
^ ch. 8 Joseph was betrothed while Jesus was about 12 years old. Joseph did not consummate their marriage until Jesus reached the age of maturity. And it was during this time that Jesus performed his first miracle. And since Jesus was a carpenter, he likely worked with his adoptive father, Joseph.—John 19:26, 27.
^ ch. 11 Many scriptures encourage Christians, such as 2 Samuel 20:1, 2; 31:7; 38:8, 9, 15; 55:22; 121:1, 2; Isaiah 57:15; 66:13; Proverbs 4:13; and 1 Peter 5:7.
^ ch. 14 Also, you may find helpful the article "Comfort Those Who Mourn as Jesus Did," in The Watchtower of November 1, 2010.

text:
"Nzĩa nĩ ĩno, endaai nayo."—ISA. 30:21.
MBATHI: 32, 48
1, 2. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kyatangĩĩie andũ aingĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtetheeasya andũ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ mekale me asũvĩĩku?
NDETO ii nĩsyatangĩĩie andũ matatalĩka: "ŨNGAMA, SISYA, ĨTHUKĨĨSYE." Ndeto isu syaandĩkĩtwe ivwaũnĩ nene myaka mbee wa 100 mĩvĩtu, na syaambĩtwe kũla kwĩ makutano ma leli na lelũ ngalĩko ya North America. Nĩkĩ ivwaũ isu syaambĩtwe? Syaambĩtwe nĩ kana ngalĩ iikese kũkĩlanĩlya leli ve ngalĩ ya mwaki yũkĩte, na iikongwa. Kũatĩĩa ndeto isu nĩkwatangĩĩie mathayũ ma andũ.
2 Ve ũndũ Yeova wĩkaa mũseango vyũ kwĩ kwamba ivwaũ. We no ta wĩkaa kũũngama mbee wa andũ make akamoneleelya nzĩa ya thayũ ũtathela nĩ kana mevathane na mĩisyo. O na eka ũu, nĩwĩkaa ũndũ mũĩthi mũseo wĩkaa. Onasya malondu make nzĩa ĩla yaĩle, na aimanenga ũkany'o maikese kũatĩĩa tũsĩla tũte tũseo.—Soma Isaia 30:20, 21.
YEOVA ETHĨĨTWE AITONGOESYA ANDŨ MAKE KUMA TENE
3. Andũ onthe malikile mũisyonĩ wa kĩkw'ũ ata?
3 Kuma tene Yeova ethĩĩtwe ayony'a andũ make nzĩa na kũmatavya nesa maũndũ ala maĩlĩte kwĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova nĩwatavisye nesa ala maĩ mũũndanĩ wa Eteni kĩla maaĩle kwĩka na kĩla mataaĩle kwĩka. Mĩao ĩsu yaĩ ĩtonya kũtetheesya andũ mekale tene na tene me atanu. (Mwa. 2:15-17) Keka Atamu na Eva nĩmeewie kĩla wamatavisye, mayĩthwa maaĩlikya mũisyonĩ ũla malikile wa kwĩkala na mathĩna maingĩ na ĩtina kũkw'a mate na wĩkwatyo. Ĩndĩ vandũ va Eva eke ũndũ weeĩtwe, aatĩĩe ũtao weesilasya enengwa nĩ nyamũ ya kĩthekanĩ. Atamu nake eethukĩĩisye wasya wa mũndũ o take. Onthe mavũthisye ũtao wa Ĩthe woo, o na kau nĩwamendete. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, andũ onthe malikile mũisyonĩ wa kĩkw'ũ.
4. (a) Nĩkĩ Ngai wongeleeile andũ mĩao ĩtina wa ĩla mbua ya ĩvinda ya Noa? (b) Ĩla maũndũ mavĩndũkie nĩ kyaũ kyamanyĩkie nesa ĩũlũ wa Ngai?
4 Ĩvindanĩ ya Noa, Ngai nĩwanenganie mĩao nĩ kana ĩtangĩĩe andũ. Ĩtina wa ĩla mbua ya ĩvinda ya Noa, Yeova nĩwavatanie kũya nthakame. Nĩkĩ weekie ũu? Nũndũ kwaĩ moalyũku meekĩkie. Moalyũku meva? Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, Yeova nĩwanenganie mwanya wa kũya nyama, na kwoou yaĩ no nginya amanenge mĩao ĩkonetye kyu. Ameie atĩĩ: "Nyama ĩ na thayũ wayo, nĩw'o nthakame yayo, mũtikaye." (Mwa. 9:1-4) Maũndũ mamina kũvĩndũka kwa nzĩa ĩsu, nĩkwoonekie nesa ũndũ Ngai wonaa thayũ nũndũ ũ thayũ nĩ wake. Nũndũ nĩwe Mũmbi na nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ, no we e weka waĩlĩte kũtũnenga mĩao ĩũlũ wa thayũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwaisye kana vai mũndũ wĩ na ũkũmũ wa kũaa ũla ũngĩ. Ngai onaa thayũ na nthakame syĩ ntheu, na kwoou akasilĩla onthe ala matũlaa mĩao yake ĩũlũ wa thayũ na nthakame.—Mwa. 9:5, 6.
5. Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ, na nĩkĩ?
5 Ekai tũsisye maũndũ amwe, ala meũtwony'a ũndũ Ngai wĩthĩĩtwe ayony'a andũ make nzĩa kuma tene. Kĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩkĩũtwĩkĩa vinya tũtw'e vyũ kũatĩĩa nzĩa ĩla Yeova ũtwonasya nũndũ nĩyo yĩtũlikya nthĩ nzaũ.
MBAĨ NZAŨ NĨYANENGIWE MĨAO MYEŨ
6. Nĩkĩ andũ ma Ngai maaĩlĩte kũatĩĩa ĩla mĩao watũmie Mose amanenge, na maaĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni wĩva?
6 Ĩvinda ya Mose vaĩ vata mũnene wa mĩao ya kwony'a andũ nesa ũndũ maaĩle kwĩkala na ũndũ maaĩle kũthaitha. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o na ĩvindanĩ yĩu maũndũ maĩ mavĩndũku. Nzyawa sya Yakovo syekalĩte Misili mbee wa myaka 200 isumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Amisili. Namo Amisili mathaithaa akw'ũ, matũmĩaa mĩvw'anano, na maĩ na mĩĩkĩĩo na syĩthĩo itataĩaa Ngai. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩla andũ ma Ngai maumie ũkombonĩ Misili, vaumĩlile vata wa mĩao myeũ. Kuma vau andũ ma Ngai nĩmaekie kũtw'ĩka ngombo, na matw'ĩka andũ athasye maĩle kũatĩĩa ĩla Mĩao ya Yeova yĩ yoka. Mavuku amwe maasyaa kana ndeto ya Kĩevelania ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "mĩao" yumanĩte na ndeto ĩngĩ ĩtonya kũelew'a ta "oneleelya, tongoesya, manyĩsya." Kwoou Mĩao ya Mose yaĩ ta kĩsiĩĩi kĩla kyasũvĩie Aisilaeli maikavukw'e nĩ mĩkalĩle mĩthũku na meko mathũku ma mothaithi ma mbaĩ ingĩ. Ĩla mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yethukĩĩsya Ngai, nĩwamĩathimaa. Ĩndĩ yalea kũmwĩthukĩĩsya, yakwatawa nĩ mathĩna manene mũno.—Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 28:1, 2, 15.
7. (a) Elesya nĩkĩ Yeova wanengie andũ make mĩao. (b) Mĩao yatw'ĩkie mũmanyĩsya wa mbaĩ ya Isilaeli ata?
7 Vaĩ na vata wa mĩao nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩngĩ. Mĩao ĩsu nĩyaeleetye ũndũ ũngĩ waĩ wĩkĩke, ũla wosanĩte na kwenda kwa Yeova. Ũndũ ũsu waĩ kũka kwa Masia, ũla nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto. Mĩao ĩsu nĩyatetheeisye Aisilaeli mamanya nesa kana mo nĩ andũ me na naĩ. O na nĩyamatetheeisye mamanya kana me na vata wa kwovow'a na nthembo ĩte na naĩ, ĩla ĩtonya kũvw'ĩka vyũ naĩ syoo. (Aka. 3:19; Aevl. 10:1-10) Ũndũ ũngĩ ĩla Mĩao yeekaa nĩ kũsũvĩa ũko ũla wesie kumĩlya Masia, na ĩndĩ ĩla Masia wesie kumĩla nĩyatetheeisye Aisilaeli kũmũmanya. Kwa nzĩa ĩsu, ĩla Mĩao no ta yaĩ mũsũvĩi, kana "mũmanyĩsya," ũla wamatongoesye nginya vala ve Klĩsto.—Aka. 3:23, 24.
8. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũtongoew'a nĩ myolooto ĩla ĩtw'ĩĩkĩte Mĩao ya Mose?
8 O na ithyĩ Aklĩsto no tũtetheke nĩ maũndũ ala me nthĩnĩ wa ĩla Mĩao yanengiwe mbaĩ ya Isilaeli. Kwa nzĩa yĩva? Nĩ kwa kwamba kũũngama na kũsisya myolooto ĩla ĩtw'ĩĩkĩte mĩao ĩsu. O na kau tũi ungu wa mĩao ĩsu, mingĩ yayo no tũmĩkwatye ĩtũtongoesye nesa thayũnĩ witũ kĩla mũthenya, o na no tũmĩkwatye ĩtũtongoesye ĩla tũũthaitha Ngai witũ mũtheu, Yeova. Aandĩkĩthisye mĩao ĩsu Mbivilianĩ nĩ kana tũmanyĩw'e nĩyo, tũtongoew'e nĩ myolooto ĩla ĩmĩtw'ĩĩkĩte, na tũyona ũseo wa kũatĩĩa mwĩkalĩle ũla waĩle Aklĩsto. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩthukĩĩsye ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Nĩmwĩw'ĩte kana nĩkwaneeniwe, Ndũkalaalae: Ĩndĩ nyie nĩngũmwĩa, kana kĩla mũndũ ũsyaasya mũndũ mũka na kũmwĩw'ĩa mũmeo nĩweka ũlaalai nake ngoonĩ yake." Kwoou ti ũlaalai w'oka twaĩle kwĩvathana naw'o, ĩndĩ nĩtwaĩle kwĩvathana na mĩmeo ya kwĩka ũlaalai.—Mt. 5:27, 28.
9. Maũndũ mavĩndũkie ata weethĩa Ngai no anenganaa mĩao ĩngĩ?
9 Ĩla Yesũ watw'ĩkie Masia, Yeova nĩwaumisye mĩao ĩngĩ myeũ na atetheesya andũ maelewe kĩeleelo kyake nesanga. Kĩtumi kya kwĩka ũu nũndũ o ta tene, maũndũ nĩmavĩndũkie ĩngĩ. Mwakanĩ wa 33 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, Yeova nĩwaekie kũathima mbaĩ ya Isilaeli na vandũ vayo ambĩĩa kũathima kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto.
MĨAO KWONDŨ WA MBAĨ NZAŨ YA KĨ-VEVA
10. Nĩkĩ kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kyanengiwe mĩao myeũ, na yaĩ kĩvathũkany'o kĩva na ĩla yanengetwe Aisilaeli?
10 Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, andũ ma Ngai ala matw'ĩkie Aklĩsto nĩmanengiwe mĩao myeũ ya ũthaithi na mwĩkalĩle, kana maelew'a ũndũ maĩ matonya kũtũmĩa ĩla yaĩ vo nesanga. Athũkũmi asu meeyumĩtye mamũthũkũme Ngai maĩ manalika ũtianĩonĩ mweũ. Mĩao ya Mose yanengetwe mbaĩ ĩmwe tũ, ĩla nĩ mbaĩ ya Isilaeli. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, andũ ala matw'ĩkie Isilaeli ma kĩ-veva maumĩte mbaĩnĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na maeetwe na mĩeele yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Vate nzika, "Ngai ti mwendeesya wa andũ; ĩndĩ mbaĩnĩ syonthe ũla ũmũkĩaa we, na kwĩka ũlũngalu, nĩwĩtĩkalawa nĩwe." (Meko 10:34, 35) Mĩao ya Mose yaandĩkĩtwe ĩvianĩ, na nĩyo yatongoesye mbaĩ ya Isilaeli ĩla yaĩ Nthĩ ya Watho. Ĩndĩ Isilaeli ma kĩ-veva maaĩle kũatĩĩa "mwĩao wa Klĩsto" ũla ũtw'ĩĩkĩtwe nĩ myolooto ĩandĩkĩtwe ngoonĩ. "Mwĩao wa Klĩsto" waĩ kwondũ wa Aklĩsto onthe o na ethĩwa me va, na waĩ ũmatethye onthe.—Aka. 6:2.
11. Nĩ maũndũ meva elĩ me nthĩnĩ wa ũla "mwĩao wa Klĩsto"?
11 Isilaeli ma kĩ-veva nĩmatethekie mũno nũndũ Ngai nĩwamatongoesye aitũmĩa Mwana wake. Kavinda kanini ũla ũtianĩo mweũ ũtanambĩĩw'a, Yesũ anenganie mĩao ĩlĩ ya vata. Mwĩao ũmwe wakonetye wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Naw'o ũla ũngĩ wakonetye mwĩkalĩle wa aatĩĩi make na ũndũ maaĩle kũkua Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Mĩao ĩsu yanengiwe Aklĩsto onthe, na kwoou athaithi onthe ma w'o ũmũnthĩ nĩmaĩle kũmĩatĩĩa, methĩwe me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ kana nĩ wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ.
12. Nĩ moalyũku meva meekiwe wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a?
12 Kwasũanĩa ũla wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo Yesũ wanengie aatĩĩi make. Wĩa ũsu wesaa kũtethw'a kĩsionĩ kĩnenange na kwa nzĩa yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ata? Mbeenĩ andũ ma mbaĩ ingĩ meeyĩete kwa Aisilaeli nĩw'o mathokaw'a mamũthũkũme Yeova. (1 Asu. 8:41-43) Ĩndĩ maũndũ nĩmavĩndũkie Yesũ amina kũnengane ũla mwĩao wĩ nthĩnĩ wa Mathayo 28:19, 20. (Soma.) Amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ manengiwe mwĩao meewa "endai" kwa andũ onthe. Mũthenya wa Vendekosito ya mwaka wa 33, nĩkwoonekie kyeni kĩnini kana Yeova nĩwaĩ anavĩndũa nzĩa ĩla yatũmĩawa kũtavany'a. Endaa yu andũ kĩla vandũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ matavw'e ũvoo mũseo. Veva wake mũtheu nĩwanengie Aklĩsto ta 120 ma kĩkundi kĩu kyeũ ũtonyi wa kũneena na ithyomo, maineena na Ayuti na andũ ma mbaĩ ingĩ ala malikĩte ũthaithinĩ wa Kĩyuti. (Meko 2:4-11) Ĩtina wa vau ũvoo nĩwambĩĩe kũtavw'a Asamalia. Na mwakanĩ wa 36 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, o namo Andũ-ma-mbaĩ-ingĩ mate aĩke nĩmambĩĩe kũtavw'a ũvoo. Kwa ũkuvĩ no twasye kana kĩsio kĩla kyatavanaw'a kya Ayuti kyaĩ kĩnini ta ndia, ĩndĩ ĩla ũvoo wambĩĩe kũtavanw'a nthĩ yonthe kyaneneva ta ũkanga.
13, 14. (a) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva wĩ nthĩnĩ wa ũla "mwĩao mweũ" Yesũ wanenganie? (b) Ngelekany'o ya Yesũ yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
13 Ekai yu tũneenee ũndũ twaĩle kũkua Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Yesũ nĩwanenganie "mwĩao mweũ." (Soma Yoana 13:34, 35.) Mwĩao ũsu ndwĩkĩte o kũweta kana twaĩle kwendana tũ, ĩndĩ wonanĩtye kana twaĩle kwĩthĩwa twĩyũmbanĩtye kũkw'a kwondũ wa ana-a-asa maitũ. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtaawetwa Mĩaonĩ ya Mose.—Mt. 22:39; 1 Yoa. 3:16.
14 Yesũ nĩwatũtiĩe ngelekany'o ĩla nzeo vyũ ũndũnĩ ũsu. Nĩweeyumĩtye vyũ kwondũ wa amanyĩw'a make. Mũndũ wendete angĩ mũno wĩana ũu no nginya ethĩwe eyũmbanĩtye kũkw'a kwondũ woo, na Yesũ nĩweeyũmbanĩsye kwĩka ũu. Na oou now'o wendaa amanyĩw'a make methĩwe meyũmbanĩtye kwĩka kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ. Kwoou twaĩle kwĩkalaa twĩyũmbanĩtye kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna, o na kũkw'a kwondũ wa ana-a-asa maitũ.—1 Ath. 2:8.
MĨAO KWONDŨ WA ĨVINDA YĨĨ NA YĨLA YŨKĨTE
15, 16. Twonete moalyũku meva, na Ngai atũtongoeasya ata?
15 Yesũ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ainenga andũ make lĩu wa kĩ-veva ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩlĩte, na mũno mũno kuma ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" yanyuviwe. (Mt. 24:45-47) Lĩu ũsu andũ ma Ngai methĩĩtwe mainengwa nũmatetheeasya kũmanya ũndũ mekwĩka ĩla maũndũ mavĩndũka.
16 Tũtwĩe matukũ ala Mbivilia ĩmetĩte 'mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo,' na mbee witũ kĩla tweteele nĩ thĩna mũnene ũtaaoneka o na ĩndĩĩ. (2 Tim. 3:1; Mko. 13:19) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana Satani na ndaimoni syake nĩmekiw'e kuma ĩtunĩ nginya kũũ nthĩ, na nũndũ wa ũu kũũ nthĩ kwĩthĩĩtwe na mathĩna maingĩ vyũ. (Ũvu. 12:9, 12) Na ĩndĩ ve wĩa tũnengetwe tũũtethye ũndũ ũtaaĩsa kũtethw'a o na ĩndĩĩ. Wĩa ũsu nĩ wa kũtavya andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe ũvoo mũseo!
17, 18. Twaĩle kwĩka ata ĩla twanengwa mĩao?
17 Ĩla tũũtavany'a, nĩtwaĩle kũtũmĩa syĩndũ ila tũnengetwe nĩ ũseũvyo wa Ngai. We nĩwĩthĩawa na wendi wa kwĩka ũu? Ĩla twamanyĩw'a maũmbanonĩ ũndũ tũtonya kũtũmĩa syĩndũ isu nesa vyũ, we nũatĩĩaa ũndũ tweewa? We nĩwonaa ũsu ta Ngai ũendeee kũtũtongoesya?
18 Nĩ kana Ngai aendeee kũtũathima, nĩtwaĩle kwĩthukĩĩsya mĩao yonthe ĩla tũnengawe kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. Tweethĩwa twĩ ewi oyu tũĩ tũikaemwa nĩ kũatĩĩa mĩao ĩla tũkanengwa ĩvindanĩ ya ũla "thĩna mũnene," ĩla nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani ĩkethĩwa ĩyanangwa. (Mt. 24:21) Na ĩndĩ ũu wathela, tũkanengwa mĩao ĩngĩ ĩtũtetheesye kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ, vala Satani ũtakethĩwa vo atongoesye andũ naĩ.
19, 20. Nĩ mavuku meva makavuanw'a, na kũkeethĩwa ata mavuanw'a?
19 Mbaĩ ya Isilaeli nĩyanengiwe mĩao myeũ ĩvindanĩ ya Mose, na ĩtina wa ĩvinda o nakyo kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto nĩkyanengiwe ũla "mwĩao wa Klĩsto." O ta ũu, Mbivilia nĩtũtavasya kana ve mavuku meũ makavuanw'a nĩ kana tũmanye mĩao ĩla tũkaatĩĩa nthĩ nzaũ. (Soma Ũvuan'yo 20:12.) Nĩ laisi mũno ũkethĩa mavuku asu meũ makaweta kĩla Yeova ũkenda andũ meanĩsye ĩvinda yĩu. Kwĩmanyĩsya mavuku asu kũkatetheesya andũ onthe, vamwe na ala makathayũũkw'a, kũmanya kwenda kwa Ngai. Vate nzika, mavuku asu makatũmanyĩsya mũnango ũndũ Yeova wonaa maũndũ. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu ũmanyi ũla twĩ naw'o na ũendeee kwongeleka wa Ndeto mbeveee ya Ngai vamwe na maũndũ ala makavuanw'a ala mavukunĩ meũ, ikatetheesya ala makethĩwa Nthĩ Nzaũ mekalany'e nesa mendanĩte, manenganĩte ndaĩa, na mate kũvũthany'a. (Isa. 26:9) Kwavindĩĩsya ũndũ andũ makamanyĩw'a mũno wĩana matongoew'e nĩ Mũsumbĩ, Yesũ Klĩsto!
20 Ala makaatĩĩa "maũndũ ala maandĩkĩtwe mavukunĩ asu" makakwata thayũ ũtathela. Yeova akaandĩka nthĩnĩ wa yĩla "ĩvuku ya thayũ" masyĩtwa ma ala makekala me aĩkĩĩku ĩvindanĩ ya yĩla ĩtatwa ya mũthya, na masyĩtwa asu maikavutwa. O naitũ no tũandĩkwe ĩvukunĩ yĩu! Kwoou, kĩla ĩvinda ŨNGAMA nĩ kana wĩmanyĩsye Ndeto ya Ngai, SISYA ũmĩelewe, na ĨTHUKĨĨSYE kwa kwĩtĩkĩla Ngai aũtongoesye ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ. Weeka ũu no wĩkale na wĩkwatyo wa kũvonoka ũla thĩna mũnene na wa kũtanĩa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai witũ wĩ wendo na ũĩ mwingĩ, Yeova, tene na tene.—Mũta. 3:11; Alo. 11:33.
