translation:
"This is the way, walk in it."—ISA. 30:21.
NOTES: 32, 48
1, 2. (a) What has comforted many people? (Consider the highlighted verse.) (b) What makes God's servants stay strong despite facing great difficulties?
THIS reminder comforts many troubled people: "BE BRAVE, TAKE HEART, BE STRONG." This reminder was first used over 100 years ago and has been featured at large gatherings throughout North America. Why has this reminder been so effective? It is because it appeals to people's desire to be courageous and hopeful. More importantly, this reminder comes from God.
2 Jehovah wants us to be courageous. He does not want us to become discouraged when faced with challenges, even if they seem overwhelming. Also, he wants us to remember that he is powerful and can help us. So, meditate on his promises, and confidently trust in him.—Read Isaiah 30:20, 21.
JEHOVAH ENCOURAGES HIS SERVANTS
3. What questions will we answer?
3 From time to time, Jehovah encourages his people by means of timely reminders. For example, Jehovah reminded ancient Israel about his promise to give them a homeland. He did so repeatedly and clearly. His Law contained specific provisions to help his people remain loyal. (Deut. 2:15-17) However, Adam and Eve disobeyed, and as a result, mankind lost the prospect of living forever in paradise. Sadly, Eve's descendants also suffered, and they have inherited a tendency toward imperfection. Adam's mistake led to suffering and death. Over time, wickedness increased. Eventually, the earth became filled with violence. Therefore, mankind lost the prospect of living forever.
4. (a) How did God encourage people during the time of Noah's Flood? (b) What lesson can we learn from how God dealt with those who survived the Flood?
4 During the Flood of Noah, God encouraged people by preserving Noah and his family. After the floodwaters receded, Jehovah made a covenant with Noah. Why did he do this? To show his loving-kindness. He said: "This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between myself and all flesh that is upon the earth." (Gen. 9:1-4) The fact that God remembered mankind shows us that he cares about humans and their future. He is the Creator and has the right to direct human affairs, and he will hold humans accountable for their actions. For instance, he allows each person to choose whether or not to worship him. God cares about humans and their lives, and he wants them to use their life to honor him.—Gen. 9:5, 6.
5 What will we discuss now, and why?
5 Let us consider some examples that illustrate how God views people. As we do so, we will better understand why Jehovah feels deeply moved when people turn to him.
AFTER THE FLOOD GOD ENCOURAGED PEOPLE
6 Why did God encourage the people who lived during the time of Moses, and what lesson can we learn from this?
6 The account of Moses shows that God cares about the way people respond to his message and whether they choose to obey him. But why? Because he understands their feelings. Jacob's ancestor Shem lived in Egypt for 200 years, and then the Egyptians mistreated them, oppressed them, and made life difficult for them. This is why God's people were forced to live in Egypt for a long time, and they longed to be free. However, God's people began to forget God, and they forgot what Jehovah had done for them. Some scholars say that the Hebrew word rendered "people" can also be understood as "families, clans, tribes." The Law of Moses was given to help the Israelites remember their history and to remind them of God's requirements. The book of Exodus explains that the Israelites became discouraged because of the hard work and the harsh treatment they received.—Read Exodus 28:1, 2, 15.
7. (a) How does Jehovah feel about his people? (b) How did the Law help the Israelites to remember God?
7 They also remembered God through the Law. The Law helped them to understand important truths about worshipping Jehovah. These truths pointed forward to the Messiah, who is Jesus Christ. The Law reminded the Israelites of their past mistakes, as well as the mistakes of others, and it showed them how to avoid repeating those mistakes. (Acts 3:19; Heb. 10:1-10) Another purpose of the Law was to reveal the standard that the Messiah would fulfill, and how the Messiah would help the Israelites to know God. In this way, the Law acted as a tutor, or "instructor," leading people to Christ.—Acts 3:23, 24.
8. Why should we be interested in the Law of Moses?
8 But now Christians are not judged according to the Law that was given to Israel. Why is that? Because they have come to appreciate the law that is within their hearts. And so, while we may study the Law, most of it does not apply to us today. Instead, it helps us to better love and worship our God, Jehovah. By writing his laws in our hearts, we can understand them and benefit from them, and we can see how much Christ valued them. For example, consider these words of Jesus: "You heard that it was said, 'Do not commit adultery.' But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with desire has already committed adultery with her in his heart." This shows that simply avoiding the act of adultery is not enough; we must also avoid having improper thoughts.—Matt. 5:27, 28.
9. What more will we learn about why God allows laws?
9 Since Jesus is the Messiah, Jehovah has revealed more laws and helped people to understand his purpose. Because of this, there are more things to learn. In 33 C.E., after Christ's death, Jehovah began to gather a new nation of Israel and invited people to join the Christian congregation.
LAWS RELATING TO THE NEW NATION
10. How did the Christian congregation receive more laws, and how does this differ from what happened with ancient Israel?
10 Through the apostles, God showed Christians more laws about worship and conduct, or he helped them to apply existing laws in a way that pleased him. Loyal ones joyfully obeyed God's commands. The Law given to Moses was one law for only the Israelites. However, like this, other nations who became part of ancient Israel also received laws that applied to them. They said, "God is not partial; rather, in every nation the man who fears him and does righteousness is acceptable to him." (Acts 10:34, 35) The Law given to Moses was written down, and it governed ancient Israel until the time of the Messiah. Ancient Israel needed to be reminded of "Christ's Law" that was written through inspired writings. "Christ's Law" refers to everything Christ taught and the principles he emphasized.—Gal. 6:2.
11. What matters will help us to understand what "Christ's Law" is?
11 Ancient Israel proved their loyalty to God when he sent his Son. As the perfect human, Jesus fulfilled the Law perfectly. This one law covers all those who want to imitate his example. One aspect of this law involves avoiding wrongdoing. Another aspect involves maintaining good standing with God and doing his will. All things were made through Christ, and all things exist for his glory, so we should strive to honor him in our thoughts and actions.—Col. 1:16.
12. What important points should we remember regarding wrongdoing?
12 Jesus showed what wrongdoing involves when he taught his disciples. Those who deliberately sin are rejecting God's forgiveness. But does that mean they have committed everlasting sin? No! Many imperfect humans have stumbled while serving Jehovah, yet he has forgiven them. (1 Sam. 8:41-43) We can be sure that Jesus authorized his followers to preach the good news to all people, as stated at Matthew 28:19, 20. (Read.) His command to go and make disciples means that all nations should hear about him. On Pentecost of 33 C.E., about 120 disciples gathered together in Jerusalem, including some women and many others who had become believers. (Acts 2:4-11) From there, they began preaching the good news in Jerusalem. By 36 C.E., Christians were sending out preachers, and soon many others joined them in proclaiming the good news. Because of opposition, the first Christian congregation in Jerusalem faced a serious challenge, but they continued to preach the good news despite persecution.
13, 14. (a) What is involved in obeying Jesus' command to love one another? (b) How does Jesus' example affect us?
13 Let us examine more closely what Christ told his disciples. Jesus commanded them to "love one another." (Read John 13:34, 35.) This love is demonstrated by our willingness to sacrifice ourselves for fellow believers, showing genuine concern for their welfare. It is a selfless love—like God's love for mankind.—Matt. 22:39; 1 John 3:16.
14 Jesus set a perfect example of this kind of love. He willingly sacrificed himself for his disciples. A loving person is moved to help those in need, and Jesus showed the depth of his love by giving his life. We too can show love by being willing to put the interests of others ahead of our own, even risking our lives for our brothers and sisters.—1 Thess. 2:8.
LOVE FOR FELLOW HUMANS AND ALL PEOPLE
15, 16. Why should we be zealous in our ministry, and how does God view such zeal?
15 Jesus foretold that his followers would be diligent in proclaiming the good news until the end of the system of things, and he used the illustration of the "faithful and discreet slave." (Matt. 24:45-47) In that time, God's people have been strengthened to discern what is happening in connection with world events.
16 We are living in the "last days," when the Bible foretold there would be a marked increase in wickedness and lawlessness. (2 Tim. 3:1; Mark 13:19) This is also the time when Satan and his demons are exerting greater influence on humanity, and this increased activity is contributing to much distress. (Rev. 12:9, 12) So we should not be surprised if we encounter opposition or persecution. Rather, let us use every opportunity to warn people about the coming destruction!
17, 18. How can we show love in our ministry?
17 As we preach, we should strive to appeal to people's hearts, letting God's spirit guide us. Are you motivated by a desire to help others? If we recognize that people desperately need spiritual guidance, will we not be eager to share the good news with them? Do we trust that God will continue to bless our efforts?
18 If God continues to empower us, we should zealously pursue every opportunity to witness to the truth about Christ. Let us not become complacent, fearing that we might offend some by taking a firm stand on what is right, especially in view of the fact that Satan is actively deceiving people. (Matt. 24:21) And when this great tribulation arrives, we will be glad that we took such a stand, for Satan will be restrained from misleading mankind.
19, 20. What important questions should we ask ourselves, and why?
19 The Israelites were given laws through Moses, and similarly, the Christian congregation has been given the "law of Christ." However, the Bible does not specify exactly how each individual law applies today. So, to determine what is right, we need to study the scriptures and pray for guidance. (Read Exodus 20:12.) It is vital that we seek Jehovah's direction so that we can apply his laws correctly. By carefully considering the principles behind those laws, we can help others—even those who may disagree with us—to understand God's viewpoint. In this way, the laws help us to show respect for Jehovah and to appreciate his standards. Furthermore, understanding the underlying principles enables us to cope with new situations and to make wise decisions in harmony with God's Word, avoiding extremism, being reasonable, and remaining humble. (Isa. 26:9) How grateful we are that God has provided his Son, Jesus Christ, to enlighten our minds!
20 Those who say, "Let us observe 'laws that are written in the heart'" have a good intention. Jehovah wrote his laws on faithful hearts, making them eager to do his will and causing them to hate wickedness. Let us strive to have such a heart! Therefore, when studying the Bible, always seek God's direction, APPLY what you learn, and MEDITATE on how to please God in every aspect of your life. This will help you remain steadfast in your determination to live according to God's will and to express your love for him more fully, Jehovah, forever.—Prov. 3:11; Ps. 11:33.

text:
"Tũikendane na ndeto, kana na ũĩmĩ; ĩndĩ twendane na kwĩka, na twendane w'o."—1 YOA. 3:18.
MBATHI: 3, 50
1. Nĩ wendo wĩva wa vata vyũ, na nĩkĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
WENDO ũla ũtongoeaw'a nĩ myolooto mĩlũngalu (a·gaʹpe) nĩ mũthĩnzĩo twĩthĩawa tũnengetwe nĩ Yeova. Nĩwe Mwambĩlĩĩlya waw'o. (1 Yoa. 4:7) Vai wendo ũvĩtũkĩte wa a·gaʹpe. Mũndũ wĩ wendo ũsu nũthangaaĩaa ala angĩ, ĩndĩ mũno mũno kĩla kyonanasya kana mũndũ e wendo ũsu nĩ kwĩyumya na kwĩyĩima maũndũ make nĩ kana eke angĩ ũseo. Kwosana na ĩvuku yĩmwe, wendo wa a·gaʹpe "ũmanyĩkaa no ũndũ wa maũndũ ala wendo ũsu ũtumaa mũndũ eka." Ĩla twendwa kana twenda angĩ kuma ngoonĩ, nĩtwĩw'aa twĩ atanu na twĩ na kĩtumi kya kwĩkala thayũ.
2, 3. Yeova onanĩtye ata kana e wendo wa w'o?
2 Yeova nĩwoonanisye nĩwendete andũ o na atombĩte Atamu na Eva. Ndaaũmba nthĩ yĩthĩwe o kĩndũ kya kũkwatĩĩa thayũ, ĩndĩ amyũmbie yĩ nzeo andũ matanĩae vyũ kwĩkala vo tene na tene. Kĩla kyatumie Yeova eka ũu nĩ kana endaa andũ maunĩke, ĩndĩ ti we mwene. Ũndũ ũngĩ weekie oonany'a wendo wa w'o nĩ kũmanenga wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzeo ĩla wamaseũvĩsye.
3 Ĩvinda yĩla Yeova woonanisye wendo wa w'o nesa vyũ nĩ ĩtina wa Atamu na Eva kũvĩtya. Eekie mũvango nĩ kana syana ila Atamu na Eva mesyaa syovow'e o na kũtw'ĩka mo maĩ manatw'ĩka alei. Ĩla weekie ũu oonanisye ndaĩ na nzika kana amwe ma ũsyao woo makamwĩw'aa na kũmwenda. (Mwa. 3:15; 1 Yoa. 4:10) O na ũndũ wa kwendeesya nĩ kana, kuma ndatĩka ĩla Yeova wathanie kana akatũma Mũtangĩĩi, methonĩ make nthembo ya wovosyo yeanene na ĩla yumĩtw'e. Na ĩndĩ ĩtina wa myaka ta 4,000, Yeova nĩweeyumisye kwa nzĩa nene mũno anengane Mwana wake mũsyawa weka akw'e kwondũ wa andũ. (Yoa. 3:16) Tũtũngaa mũvea ta kĩ nũndũ wa wendo wa Yeova ũte maela!
4. Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana andũ me na naĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa na wendo wa w'o?
4 O naitũ no twonany'e wendo wa w'o nũndũ tũmbĩtwe na mũvw'ano wa Ngai. Ti laisi kwĩthĩwa na wendo wa w'o nũndũ wa naĩ ĩla twatiĩwe, ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana tũitonya kwĩka ũu. Kwa ngelekany'o, Aveli nĩwoonanisye kana nĩwendete Ngai vyũ ĩla wamumĩisye kĩla kĩseo katĩ wa ila waĩ nasyo. (Mwa. 4:3, 4) Nake Noa oonanisye kana nĩwendete andũ vyũ kwa kũmatavya ũvoo kuma kwa Ngai kwa myaka mingĩ o na kũtw'ĩka vai ũmwe wamwĩthukĩĩasya. (2 Vet. 2:5) O nake Avalaamu nĩwoonanisye kana vai kĩndũ kĩngĩ wendete kwĩ ũndũ wamwendete Ngai ĩla weetĩkĩlile kumya mwana wake, Isaka. (Yak. 2:21) Kwoou, nĩtwaĩle kwĩka o ta aũme asu aĩkĩĩku twonany'e wendo o na ethĩwa ti laisi kwĩka ũu.
WENDO WA W'O NA WENDO ŨTE WA W'O
5. Nĩ maũndũ meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a twĩ na wendo wa w'o?
5 Mbivilia yaĩtye kana wendo wa w'o ndwonanaw'a "na ndeto, kana na ũĩmĩ," ĩndĩ ĩtwĩĩte "twendane na kwĩka, na twendane w'o." (1 Yoa. 3:18) Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ kwasya tũyaĩle kũtavya ala angĩ kana nĩtũmendete? Ti w'o o na vanini! (1 Ath. 4:18) Ndeto isu sionany'a kana tũyaĩle o kwĩa mũndũ nĩtũmwendete naitũ nĩtwene e na vata ũkwenda kũtetheew'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa Mũklĩsto ũla ũngĩ nde na lĩu, ngũa, kana vandũ ũkoma, tũyaĩle o kũmwĩa twĩmwendea ũseo tũteũmũtethya. (Yak. 2:15, 16) O ta ũu, ethĩwa nĩtwendete Yeova na mũtũi, tũikekaa o kũvoya Ngai "atũme akethi ngethanĩ," ĩndĩ tũkeekĩaa kĩthito kyonthe kĩla tũtonya tũtavany'e ũvoo mũseo.—Mt. 9:38.
6, 7. (a) "Wendo ũte na wangangan'yo" nĩ wendo ũilyĩ ata? (b) Nengane ngelekany'o sya wendo ũte wa w'o.
6 Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie atĩĩ: 'Twendane na kwĩka, na w'o.' Kwoou no nginya wendo witũ "ndũkethĩwe na wangangan'yo" kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, waĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩ wendo "ũte na wangangan'yo." (Alo. 12:9; 2 Ako. 6:6) Ũu nĩ kwasya kana tũyaĩle kwony'a ala angĩ atĩ twĩ na wendo wa w'o naitũ ti w'o tũilyĩ ngoonĩ. Kwĩka ũu no ũndũ ũmwe na kwĩkĩa kĩndũ ũthyũ tũvithe nithyĩ aaũ. Ĩndĩ nĩtũtonya kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Vo ve wendo wĩthĩawa na wangangany'o?' Kwa w'o, vai kĩndũ ta kĩu. Wendo ta ũsu nĩ wendo ũtesa kũtethya o na vanini.
7 Ekai tũsũanĩe ngelekany'o imwe sya wendo ũte wa w'o. Ĩla Satani waneenaa na Eva mũũndanĩ wa Eteni, eetusaa eĩka kũmũtethya, ĩndĩ we endaa kwĩyĩuna, na ũsu waĩ wangangany'o mũthei. (Mwa. 3:4, 5) Ĩvindanĩ ya Ndaviti, ve mũndũ weetawa Aithoveli weetusaa mũnyanyae ĩndĩ ĩtina esa kwonany'a kana ũnyanya wake na mũsumbĩ ndwaĩ wa w'o. Ĩla Aithoveli wamanyie kana no aunĩke avũnyanĩa Ndaviti, nĩweekie ũu. (2 Sam. 15:31) Ũmũnthĩ akaĩi ma mũĩkĩĩo na angĩ ala maetae mũaanĩko kĩkundinĩ matũmĩaa "ndeto syoo nduu na sya kwendeesya" nĩ kana monethye andũ nĩmamendete, ĩndĩ kĩeleelo kyoo kĩthĩawa ne kwĩyĩuna mo ene.—Alo. 16:17, 18.
8. Twaĩle kwĩkũlya ata?
8 Nĩ ũndũ wĩ nthoni mũno mũndũ kwoneka ta wĩthĩawa na wendo na kaĩ nĩ mwangangany'a. Mũndũ wa mũthemba ũsu ethĩawa ateyumĩtye kuma ngoonĩ ũndũ Ngai wendaa. Mwangangany'a ta ũsu no akenge andũ ĩndĩ ndakenga Yeova. O na Yesũ aisye kana ũla ũkethĩwa na wangangany'o akavũwa "mũno." (Mt. 24:51) Kwa w'o, athũkũmi ma Yeova mayĩsa kwenda kwĩthĩwa na wangangany'a. Ĩndĩ nũseo kwĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Kĩla ĩvinda nyie nĩnĩthĩawa na wendo wa w'o ndekwenda kwĩyĩuna mwene kana ndeũkengana?' Ekai tũneenee maũndũ kenda tũtonya kwĩka twonany'e twĩ na wendo "ũte na wangangan'yo."
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA 'KWENDANA NA KWĨKA, NA KWENDANA W'O'
9. Wendo wa w'o ũtumaa twĩka ata?
9 Tanĩaa kwĩka maũndũ ũte na kĩeleelo kya kũmanyĩka. Vatonyeka twaĩle kwĩkaa ana-a-asa maitũ maũndũ maseo na "kĩmbithĩ" kana tũtenekee nĩ andũ. (Soma Mathayo 6:1-4.) Anania na Savaila nĩmaemiwe nĩ kwĩka ũu. Nũndũ moonie mataumya mũvothi woo kĩmbithĩnĩ, mawetie kĩla mekumya o na mongela mautĩĩo na wangangany'o woo watuma mavonea naĩ. (Meko 5:1-10) Vandũ va ũu, wendo wa w'o ũkatumaa tũtanĩa kwĩka ana-a-asa maitũ maũndũ maseo o na ethĩwa ala angĩ maimanya. Kwa ngelekany'o, ana-a-asa ala matetheeasya Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye kũseũvya lĩu wa kĩ-veva matethasya wĩa ũsu kĩmbithĩnĩ na mayĩsaa kũweta kana nĩmo maseũvĩtye kĩndũ kĩna.
10. Tũtonya ata kũnenga ala angĩ ndaĩa?
10 Ĩthĩwa wendete kũnenga ala angĩ ndaĩa. (Soma Alomi 12:10.) Yesũ nĩwatũtiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo ya kũnenga ala angĩ ndaĩa ĩla watethisye wĩa woonekaa ũte wa kũtethw'a nĩ mũndũ take. (Yoa. 13:3-5, 12-15) Nĩtwaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito mũno nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na wĩnyivyo ta wa Yesũ na tũitetheesya ala angĩ. O namo atũmwa mayaaelewa nesa nĩkĩ Yesũ weekie ũu nginya ĩla mesie kũtũmĩwa veva mũtheu. (Yoa. 13:7) O naitũ no tũnenge ala angĩ ndaĩa kwa kũema kwona ta twĩ aseo kwĩ mo nũndũ wa kĩsomo kitũ, malĩ ĩla twĩ nayo, kana nũndũ wa ianda sitũ ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova. (Alo. 12:3) O na tũyaĩlĩte kwĩw'ĩa ala angĩ kĩwĩu makathwa, vandũ va ũu twaĩle kũtana vamwe namo o na ethĩwa twĩona o naitũ twĩĩaĩle kũkathwa nũndũ wa kĩla kĩanĩiw'e.
11. Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kũkatha ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ?
11 Katha ana-a-asa kuma ngoonĩ. Twaĩle kũtũmĩa nesa myanya ĩla twakwata tũkathe ala angĩ nũndũ ndeto sya kũkatha nĩ "nzeo sya kwaka." (Aev. 4:29) Ĩndĩ no nginya twĩke ũu kuma ngoonĩ. Tũkaema kũkatha ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ nĩ kwĩsa kwĩthĩa tũyĩka kũvaka mũndũ mauta kana ũkethĩa tũikwenda kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kitũ kya kũmũnenga ũtao mũna twaĩle kwĩthĩwa tũimũnenga. (Nth. 29:5) Ũkakatha mũndũ na ũisyoka ũimumany'a mwataanĩsya, ũtw'ĩka mwangangany'a. Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwatataa ndakeke ũu, na kwoou we nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ya mũndũ wendete angĩ ate na wangangany'o nũndũ amakathaa ũndũ vaĩlĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwakathie Aklĩsto ma Kolintho nũndũ wa maũndũ mana meekĩte maseo. (1 Ako. 11:2) Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ asisya mwĩkalĩle woo oonie mataĩle kũkathwa, na amaelesya nesa nĩkĩ ũtemakatha.—1 Ako. 11:20-22.
12. Ĩla tũũthokya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa, tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana wendo witũ nĩ wa w'o?
12 Ĩthĩawa wĩ mũthokya wa aeni. Yeova nũtwĩaĩe twonasye ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ ũlau. (Soma 1 Yoana 3:17.) Ĩndĩ twaĩle kwĩka ũu twĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo na tũte na kĩima o na vanini. No twĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Nyie nĩthokasya o anyanyawa, kana andũ ala me nguma, kana ala nĩsĩ no mandethye? Kana nĩnĩmanthaa ũndũ ndonya kwony'a ũlau ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa o na ndamesĩ nesa kana matatonya kũndĩva kĩla nameka?' (Luka 14:12-14) Kana nata mwana-a-asa akakwatwa nĩ thĩna nũndũ wa kwĩka mĩvango ĩte mĩseo, kana akalea kũtũtũngĩa mũvea twamũthokya kwitũ? Mavindanĩ ta asu twaĩlĩte kũatĩĩa ũtao ũũ: "Mũkĩthokan'ya ene kwa ene mũtekũnyungunyĩsya." (1 Vet. 4:9) Waatĩĩa ũtao ũsu, ũkakwata ũtanu ũla mũndũ ũkwataa anengane na kĩeleelo kĩseo.—Meko 20:35.
13. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma mavinda angĩ wĩthĩa ti laisi kũtetheesya amwe onzu? (b) Nĩ maũndũ ta meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkatw'ĩĩka ala onzu?
13 Tw'ĩĩka ala onzu. Mbivilia ĩtũnengete mwĩao ũũ: "Tw'ĩĩkaai ala onzu, ũmĩanĩasyai na andũ onthe." Mwĩao ũsu no ũtũtetheesye kũmanya wendo witũ nĩ wa w'o kana ti wa w'o. (1 Ath. 5:14) O na kau ana-a-asa aingĩ onzu nĩmesaa kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, amwe moo no nginya tũendeee kũmatetheesya o kavola twĩ na wũmĩĩsyo. No tũmatetheesye kwa kũea ngewa namo ĩũlũ wa maandĩko mana ma kwaka, tũkeka mĩvango namo ya kũthi ũtavany'a, kana o tũkamantha ĩvinda ya kũmethukĩĩsya. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana tũyaĩle o kũvanga kana Mũklĩsto mũna nĩ mũlũmu kana nĩ mwonzu. Twaĩle kũmanya kana kĩla ũmwe witũ e ngalĩko ĩla wĩthĩawa e mũlũmu na e ngalĩko ĩla wĩthĩawa e mwonzu. O nake mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩweesĩ kana aĩ na mawonzu a make. (2 Ako. 12:9, 10) Kwoou vai Mũklĩsto ũtatw'ĩĩka ũla ũngĩ.
14. Twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa twĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũikanange mũuo ũla twĩ na w'o?
14 Ĩthĩwa na mũuo na ala angĩ. Twĩkaa kyonthe kĩla tũtonya tũikanange mũuo ũla twĩ naw'o na ana-a-asa maitũ, o na ethĩwa ve mavinda tũkwona ta matanatũelewa kana ta matũkua naĩ. (Soma Alomi 12:17, 18.) Ethĩwa nĩtwavĩtĩsya mũndũ, kũmwĩtya ũekeo no kũusye ngoo yake, ĩndĩ no nginya twĩke ũu kuma ngoonĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, vandũ va kwĩa mwana-a-asa, "Vole nũndũ wa ũu ũkwĩw'a," nũseo ũkonany'a nũũkwatya nũmũvĩtĩisye kwa kũmwĩa, "Vole nũndũ ndeto syakwa nikũũmĩisye." Mũuo wĩthĩawa wĩ wa vata mũno mũno mũtwaanonĩ. Mũndũ na mũka mayaĩlĩte kwonethya andũ nĩmendene, na kaĩ me mũsyĩ maineenanasya, matũmĩaa ndeto mbai, kana nĩmokitaa.
15. Nata tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a kana twaekea mũndũ kũma ngoonĩ?
15 Ĩthĩawa wĩyũmbanĩtye kũekea. Twaekea mũndũ tũiatĩanĩaa na ĩvĩtyo yĩla watwĩka na nĩtũvetaa ũthatu ũla twĩĩ naw'o. Ethĩwa nĩtwĩyũmbanĩtye 'kũmĩanĩsya ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo; tũkĩthing'ĩĩsya kũsũvĩa wĩw'ano ũmwe wa veva wovanonĩ wa mũuo,' tũikaemawa nĩ kũekea ala matũvĩtĩsya matesĩ kana nĩmatũvĩtĩsya. (Aev. 4:2, 3) Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda tũekee mũndũ kuma ngoonĩ, no nginya tũsisye mũno tũikatinde tũisũanĩa ĩvĩtyo yĩla ũtwĩkie nũndũ wendo "ndũtalĩlaa ũthũku." (1 Ako. 13:4, 5) Kwĩkalya ũthatu ngoonĩ kana kwĩkala twĩ ũthũ na mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa no kũtume twĩsa kwananga vyũ ngwatanĩo yitũ nake, o na no kwĩse kũtuma twananga ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova vyũ. (Mt. 6:14, 15) O na ĩngĩ no tũvoyee ala matũvĩtĩsya nĩ kana twonany'e nĩtwamaekea kuma ngoonĩ.—Luka 6:27, 28.
16. Twaĩle kwosa ata ianda ila twanengwa ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova?
16 Ndũkamanthe kwĩyĩuna. Mũndũ akwata ianda ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova, aĩlĩte kũitũmĩa kwa nzĩa ĩkũtuma ala angĩ mamanya kana nũmendete kuma ngoonĩ. Ata? Ndaĩlĩte kũsyona ta nzĩa ya "kwĩuna mwene," ĩndĩ aĩle 'kũmantha kũuna angĩ.' (1 Ako. 10:24) Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla twĩ na maũmbano manene, ana-a-asa ala manyuvĩtwe ta athokany'a nĩmo methĩawa ma mbee kũvika kũla kũkwĩkalwa. Athokany'a aingĩ mayosaa kĩanda kĩu manengetwe ta mwanya wa kũkwata ivĩla ila nzeo vyũ kwondũ woo na andũ moo, ĩndĩ manyuvaa ivĩla ila ite nzeo mũno na syĩ vakuvĩ na vala maaĩwe. Meeyĩima moseo kwa nzĩa ĩsu, methĩawa mayonany'a kana nĩmendete ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ. Wĩona ta ũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ĩsu yoo ata?
17. Wendo wa w'o ũtonya kũtetheesya mũndũ ata ethĩwa nĩweeka naĩ ngito?
17 Umbũla naĩ ĩla wĩthĩwa wĩkĩte na ũiekana nayo vyũ. Aklĩsto amwe meeka naĩ ngito matataa kũmĩvitha nĩ kana maikevake nthoni kana maikasonokye angĩ. (Nth. 28:13) Ĩndĩ mũndũ ũkũvitha naĩ nde wendo nũndũ ethĩawa ayĩyĩũmĩsya na ayĩũmĩsya ala angĩ. Kwĩka ũu kũsiĩĩaa veva wa Ngai ũilika nesa kĩkundinĩ, o na no kwanange mũuo ũla wĩ kĩkundinĩ. (Aev. 4:30) Kwoou ethĩwa Mũklĩsto nĩweeka naĩ ngito na e na wendo wa w'o, kĩu kĩkatuma athi kũneena na atumĩa nĩ kana mamũtetheesye.—Yak. 5:14, 15.
18. Wendo wa w'o nĩ wa vata mũno wĩana ata?
18 Wendo nĩw'o nguma ĩla ya vata vyũ kwĩ syonthe. (1 Ako. 13:13) Nĩw'o ũtumaa andũ mamanya kana twĩ aatĩĩi ma Yesũ, na kana twĩthĩawa tũyĩyĩelekany'a na ũla umanĩte na wendo ũsu, nake nĩ Yeova. (Aev. 5:1, 2) Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "[Ethĩwa] ndi na wendo, nyie ti kĩndũ." (1 Ako. 13:2) Kwoou "tũikendane na ndeto" tũ, ĩndĩ ekai tũendeee 'kwendana na kwĩka, na kwendana w'o.'

translation:
"Let us walk together in affection, even with tenderness; let us walk together in speech, and let us walk together in action."—1 JOHN 3:18.
FOOTNOTE: 3, 50
1. What kind of love is most important, and why? (Consider the preceding verses.)
THE love that pleases God is selfless love (a·gaʹpe), which is an expression of our appreciation for what Jehovah has done for us. He is its source. (1 John 4:7) This is different from self-seeking love. A person showing this kind of love does not simply feel kindly toward others, but consistently acts in their best interests, even if it means sacrificing his own comfort or convenience. As one writer put it, a·gaʹpe "is marked not by what it feels, but by what it does." But if we truly love both Jehovah and our neighbor, we will strive to show it in practical ways.
2, 3. How does Jehovah demonstrate his love for us?
2 Jehovah demonstrated his love for imperfect humans by sending his Son, Adam, and Eve. Despite knowing they would misuse their free will, he allowed them to live forever. Everything Jehovah did afterward to undo the effects of their rebellion was motivated by love—not by compulsion. The fact that Jehovah patiently worked to restore obedient mankind shows how much he values life.
3 One way Jehovah showed his love was by providing a ransom through Jesus Christ's sacrifice. He foresaw that Adam and Eve would sin and that their offspring would need redemption. So he made arrangements for a perfect human life to be given as a ransom. (Gen. 3:15; 1 John 4:10) And to accomplish this, he sent his Son to earth, knowing that it would mean suffering and death. After nearly 4,000 years, Jehovah fulfilled his promise by sending his only-begotten Son to die for humankind. (John 3:16) Truly, we have reason to marvel at the depth of Jehovah's love!
4 What can motivate us to show love despite imperfections in others?
4 We can demonstrate our love because we appreciate God's love for us. It is not easy to show love when someone has wronged us, but we should strive to do so. For example, Abel demonstrated his love for God despite being mistreated by his brother Cain. (Gen. 4:3, 4) Noah also showed love for people by warning them about the coming flood for many years and building an ark to save those who believed. (2 Pet. 2:5) Abraham demonstrated faith and love by being willing to sacrifice his beloved son Isaac. (Jas. 2:21) Therefore, let us endeavor to imitate those faithful men and show love regardless of how others treat us.
LOVE FOR GOD AND LOVE FOR PEOPLE
5 How can we show that we truly love God?
5 The Bible says that love for God means "loving one another," and that loving one another means "loving him." (1 John 3:18) Does this mean that we should simply feel affection for all our brothers and sisters? Not at all! (1 Thess. 4:18) True love moves us to help our brothers and sisters when they are in need. For instance, if a Christian brother or sister is sick, poor, or distressed, we should be moved to assist them practically. (Jas. 2:15, 16) And since we love Jehovah and want to please him, we respond to his heartfelt plea for more workers, readily volunteering to share the good news with others.—Matt. 9:38.
6, 7. (a) What is "unearned kindness"? (b) Give examples of unearned kindness shown by people.
6 The apostle John wrote: "Love one another." But what kind of love are we talking about—a general feeling of goodwill, or something deeper? The expression "unearned kindness" helps us understand that this is a love that is deeply felt. (Rev. 12:9; 2 Cor. 6:6) So does this mean that we should show unearned kindness to everyone, regardless of whether they deserve it? No. Unearned kindness involves extending ourselves to those who are already showing love. It prompts us to ask ourselves: 'How can I show unearned kindness to my brothers?' To illustrate, consider this point: Love is often expressed through actions rather than just feelings.
7 Let's examine an example of such love. Satan deceived Eve by appealing to her desire for knowledge forbidden by God, leading her to disobey him, and ultimately causing her to turn away from true worship. (Gen. 3:4, 5) In David's case, Ahithophel, a trusted counselor, betrayed him, revealing his secret plans to Absalom. However, Ahithophel realized he had gone too far and regretted betraying David, so he ended his own life. (2 Sam. 15:31) Therefore, we should be cautious about making assumptions based on outward appearances, because people may hide their true motives. The proverb says that "a heart knows its own bitterness," and only Jehovah can truly read hearts.—Rev. 16:17, 18.
8 Should we always try to forgive?
8 It is often difficult to forgive someone who has deeply hurt us. But a humble person will recognize that he too makes mistakes and needs God's forgiveness. Forgiving others is essential if we want to remain close to Jehovah. And Jesus said that those who show mercy will receive mercy. (Matt. 24:51) So, let us strive to imitate Jehovah's willingness to forgive. Ask yourself, 'Am I willing to extend forgiveness to others, even if they don't ask for it?' Let us carefully consider how we can demonstrate "love, though imperfectly."
HOW TO SHOW 'FORGIVENESS AND MERCY'
9 What does our love for God motivate us to do?
9 We should be quick to forgive. Sometimes people do wrong things because they are under pressure or influenced by others. (Read Matthew 6:1-4.) Ananias and Sapphira were motivated to lie by pride. However, if you practice forgiving, you will avoid becoming bitter and resentful. (Acts 5:1-10) By doing so, you will also be more inclined to forgive others and to maintain good relationships. For example, some Christians who had been harmed by a disfellowshipped relative found comfort in helping him spiritually, even though they still felt hurt. They realized that showing mercy was important.
10 How can we help those who have wronged us?
10 It is loving to help those who have wronged us. (Read Romans 12:10.) Jesus gave an excellent example of how to help those who have wronged us when he washed the feet of his disciples. (John 13:3-5, 12-15) We can imitate his humility by being willing to forgive others. And we can show them kindness, remembering that Jesus expects us to extend mercy to others. (John 13:7) Also, we can help those who have wronged us by speaking kindly to them, even if we feel hurt or embarrassed, or if their actions have caused us serious problems. (Rom. 12:3) And we should be ready to assist them in practical ways, knowing that our efforts may please Jehovah.
11 What can we do to remain forgiving?
11 Forgive generously. We need to use self-control when someone wrongs us, realizing that holding on to resentment is "harmful." (Eph. 4:29) But how can we do this? We can choose to forgive generously by focusing on what good qualities the person has or by thinking about the circumstances that led him to act the way he did. (Prov. 29:5) When you forgive someone, you will likely feel much better. The apostle Paul understood this, and he encouraged Christians to be generous toward those who wrong them. For instance, he commended the Corinthians for restoring a repentant Christian. (1 Cor. 11:2) However, some find it difficult to forgive, and they may wonder if forgiveness is really appropriate.—1 Cor. 11:20-22.
12 How can we deal with feelings of anger and bitterness, especially if the wrong done to us was very serious?
12 Consider the example of Asaph. Jehovah helped him to see things from a spiritual perspective. (Read 1 John 3:17) But we also need to examine our own heart and motives. We might ask ourselves: 'Am I being unreasonable, or am I letting personal pride influence me? Or am I simply feeling sorry for myself because of the wrong done to me, and am I finding it hard to show compassion?' (Luke 14:12-14) What if a fellow believer repeatedly does something hurtful, or fails to live up to our expectations? Should we stop associating with him? Instead, let us apply the principle found in these words: "Continue putting up with one another." (Col. 4:9) Applying this principle will help you maintain a positive outlook.—Acts 20:35.
13 (a) Why might it be difficult to forgive others? (b) What practical steps can we take to improve our ability to forgive?
13 Let us work on forgiving others. The Bible gives us this counsel: "Keep on forgiving one another." This counsel does not mean that we should excuse serious wrongdoing, nor does it say whether what they did was right or wrong. (1 Thess. 5:14) Often, fellow believers hurt us unintentionally, and sometimes we may continue to feel upset about it. So we strive to be understanding by considering the circumstances, avoiding exaggeration, and not dwelling on past offenses. Also, we remember that even a faithful Christian is imperfect. We recognize that each one of us has weaknesses and makes mistakes. For example, the apostle Paul himself had imperfections. (2 Cor. 12:9, 10) Therefore, Christians do not expect perfection from one another.
14 How can we cultivate empathy so that we are more willing to forgive?
14 Show kindness and compassion. Always try to put yourself in their place and understand how they feel, and do not let personal prejudices or misunderstandings prevent you from doing so. (Read Romans 12:17, 18.) Try to see things from their perspective, and avoid judging them harshly. For instance, when someone offends you, instead of saying, "You really hurt me," you might say, "I felt hurt when you did that." A person who is truly humble will listen carefully. People often react negatively when they feel criticized, but they are more likely to respond favorably when approached with gentleness.
15 What can we do if we find it difficult to forgive someone?
15 Forgiveness takes effort. We forgive others when we show them the same mercy that we hope to receive. Try to 'treat others as you would like to be treated,' being willing to overlook offenses, even serious ones. (Eph. 4:2, 3) We should strive to forgive others generously and completely, and avoid dwelling on past wrongs. (1 Cor. 13:4, 5) To maintain peace in our families or congregations, and to avoid letting resentment damage our relationship with Jehovah, we must be quick to forgive. (Matt. 6:14, 15) And we should also be ready to ask for forgiveness when we have wronged others.—Luke 6:27, 28.
16 How can we prove that we value God's favor above everything else?
16 Consider this question. A person who truly values God's favor will use it to help others, rather than seeking personal gain or prominence. Does that make sense? He will be motivated to show practical wisdom, "seeking not his own advantage." (1 Cor. 10:24) For example, imagine a large gathering where children are present. The parents might take turns watching over the children so that everyone can relax. They might willingly sacrifice some of their time and energy to benefit others, knowing that doing so will create a more pleasant atmosphere for all. In a similar way, mature Christians are often willing to put aside their own interests to help others spiritually. Do you see how such selflessness demonstrates genuine love?
17 What can motivate us to forgive, even when it is difficult?
17 Understanding why we need forgiveness helps. Some Christians have found it challenging to forgive others, especially when they have been deeply hurt or wronged. (Matt. 18:13) However, remembering that we ourselves need God's forgiveness can move our heart to extend forgiveness to others. By showing mercy, we imitate Jehovah, who is always ready to forgive those who repent. (Eph. 4:30) When a fellow Christian asks for forgiveness, and we respond with lovingkindness, it strengthens our relationship and encourages him.—Jas. 5:14, 15.
18 Is love simply an emotion?
18 Love is much more than just a feeling. (1 Cor. 13:13) It motivates people to show concern for one another, to support each other, and to live in harmony with God's standards, ultimately pleasing Jehovah. (Eph. 5:1, 2) Paul wrote: "Love never fails." (1 Cor. 13:2) So let us continue to "earnestly strive" to cultivate love, striving "to be peaceable with all men" and to demonstrate love in everything we do.

text:
"Mũndũ o na wĩva ndakamũvute mũthĩnzĩo wenyu."—AKO. 2:18.
MBATHI: 32, 55
1, 2. (a) Athũkũmi ma Ngai me na mea ma kũkwata mũthĩnzĩo wĩva? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkalae tũsyaĩĩsye ũla mũthĩnzĩo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
AKLĨSTO etĩkĩw'a mauta me na wĩkwatyo wa vata o ta ũla mũtũmwa Vaulo waĩ naw'o wa kũkwata 'mũthĩnzĩo ũla weetĩwe ĩũlũ nĩ Ngai.' (Avi. 3:14) Meteele na mea kũsumbĩka vamwe na Yesũ Klĩsto Ũsumbĩnĩ wake wa ĩtunĩ na kũtetheanĩsya nake wĩanĩ wa kũvetea andũ naĩ. (Ũvu. 20:6) Aklĩsto asu mathĩtwe nĩ Ngai mũthĩnzĩo wa vata mũno maĩlĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito maũkwate! Namo malondu angĩ mathĩtwe mũthĩnzĩo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ũsu. Me na wĩkwatyo mũseo ta kĩ wa kwĩkala tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yĩ nzaũ!—2 Vet. 3:13.
2 Nĩ kana Vaulo atetheesye Aklĩsto ala angĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta mekale me aĩkĩĩku na maikakose mũthĩnzĩo ũla mathĩtwe, amatavisye ndeto ii: "Mosũanĩo menyu malũme maũndũnĩ ala me ĩũlũ." (Ako. 3:2) Maaĩlĩte kwĩkalaa malilikene wĩkwatyo woo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. (Ako. 1:4, 5) Athũkũmi ma Yeova mekala mavindĩĩsye moathimo ala we wathĩte andũ make, makeethĩawa matonya kwĩkala masyaĩĩsye ũla mũthĩnzĩo ũmathĩte, wĩthĩwe nĩ wa kũthi ĩtunĩ kana nĩ wa kũtanĩa thayũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ.—1 Ako. 9:24.
3. Vaulo akanisye Aklĩsto ĩũlũ wa kyaũ?
3 Vaulo nĩwasyokie aweta maũndũ ala matonya kwĩsa kũvata Aklĩsto mũthĩnzĩo woo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla waandĩkĩaa kĩkundi kya Kolosai nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa Aklĩsto ma ũvũngũ ala makwatĩĩaa ĩla Mĩao mũno vandũ va kũmwĩtĩkĩla Klĩsto mayona kũu takw'o kũmwendeesya Ngai. (Ako. 2:16-18) O na ĩngĩ, Vaulo nĩwawetie maũndũ amwe me kw'o nginya ũmũnthĩ, ala matonya kũtũsiĩĩa tũikese kũkwata ũla mũthĩnzĩo. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũeleetye ũndũ Aklĩsto matonya kwĩsiĩanĩa na mĩmeo mĩthũku, na ũndũ matonya kũmina mathĩna ala maumĩla mũsyĩ kana o katĩ woo. Motao ala wumĩtye ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu nĩ ma vata mũno kwitũ ũmũnthĩ. Kwondũ wa ũu, ekai tũsisye mokany'o amwe Vaulo waandĩkĩie Akolosai.
ŨAA MĨMEO MĨTHŨKU
4. Nĩkĩ mĩmeo mĩthũku ĩtonya kũtuma tũtakwata ũla mũthĩnzĩo?
4 Vaulo amina kũlilikany'a ana-a-asa make ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo mũseo ũla maĩ naw'o aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ũaai mamutha menyu ala me kũũ nthĩ: ũlaalai, na ũvuku, na mĩmeo mĩthũku, na kwenda maũndũ mathũku, na ĩtomo." (Ako. 3:5) Mĩmeo mĩthũku nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yĩ na vinya mũno ũkethĩa no ĩtume twananga ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova na tũyasya wĩkwatyo witũ. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe wakwatiwe nĩ mĩmeo mĩthũku na yamwelelũkya aisye ũũ asyoka kĩkundinĩ: "Nakusiw'e nĩ mĩmeo yaĩ vinya mũno, na ndikaasalukya maũndũ maĩ mathũkie."
5. Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũkesũvĩa ĩla twĩ mũisyonĩ?
5 Nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩsũvĩa mũno mũno ĩla twakomana na maũndũ matonya kũtuma tũemwa nĩ kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Yeova ĩũlũ wa mwĩkalĩle. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũseo andũ mambĩĩa kwĩvaany'a oou makeyĩkĩĩa mĩvaka mĩseo maũndũnĩ ta kũkwatana, kũkũnana kisi, kana kwĩthĩwa me oka kũndũ matonya kũtatĩka meke maũndũ mataĩle. (Nth. 22:3) O na ve mavinda Mũklĩsto ũtonya kũtatĩka eke maũndũ mataĩle, ta kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla wathi savalĩ ya kĩ-wĩa kana ĩla ũkũthũkũma na mũndũ ũngĩ ũte mũka kana mũũme. (Nth. 2:10-12, 16) Ũkesa kwĩthĩa wĩ vandũ ũtonya kũlika mũisyonĩ, weta ũtheinĩ kana wĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, na ũyĩkua ta mũndũ wĩ ndaĩa, ũte kũlwa kana ngũĩ mbingĩ na mũndũ ũte mũkau kana mũemeu nĩtonya kwĩsa kũũlikya thĩnanĩ. Mavinda angĩ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa twĩ mũisyonĩ wa kwĩka maũndũ mataĩle nĩ ĩla tũkwĩw'a tũkw'ĩte ngoo kana tũkwĩw'a ta twĩ ithyoka. Mavindanĩ ta asu nĩtũtonya kwĩkũlya keka nĩtwona o mũndũ ũtuma twĩw'a twĩ ma vata. O na nĩtũtonya kũvinyĩĩwa nginya ũkethĩa twĩĩtĩkĩla mũndũ o na wĩva atũkiakisye o na ethĩwa aumĩte va. Wesa kwĩw'a vavikwa vau, mwĩkaĩle Yeova na andũ make nĩ kana ũtetheew'e ndũkese kwĩka ũndũ ũtonya kũũvata ũla mũthĩnzĩo.—Soma Savuli 34:18; Nthimo 13:20.
6. Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kũlilikana ĩla tũũnyuva syĩndũ sya kwĩtanĩthya?
6 Nĩ kana tũae mĩmeo mĩthũku no nginya twĩvathane na maũndũ ma kwĩtanĩthya ala makumasya mĩkalĩle mĩthũku. Maũndũ maingĩ ma kwĩtanĩthya ũmũnthĩ matũlilikanasya mĩkanĩlye ĩla yaĩ na andũ ma Sotomo na Ngomola. (Yuta 7) Ala maseũvasya syĩndũ sya kwĩtanĩthya maseũvasya syĩndũ ikwonany'a ũlaalai tate ũndũ mũnene na ta ũte ũthũku o na ũmwe. Kwoou tũyaĩle kwĩtĩkĩla o kĩndũ kyonthe kĩla twakomana nakyo kya kwĩtanĩthya. Twaĩle kũnyuva syĩndũ sya kwĩtanĩthya ila itatonya kũtũsiĩĩa tũikaendeee kũsyaĩĩsya ũla mũthĩnzĩo.—Nth. 4:23.
"ĨVW'ĨKEI" WENDO NA ŨSEO
7. Nĩ mathĩna meva matonya kumĩla kĩkundinĩ?
7 Vai mũndũ ũlea kana nĩ ũathimo mũnene kwĩthĩwa kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. Maũmbanonĩ nĩtwĩmanyĩasya Ndeto ya Ngai na tũkekĩana vinya na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa matwendete. Kĩu kĩtũtetheeasya kwĩkala tũsyaĩĩsye ũla mũthĩnzĩo. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, mavinda angĩ no tũeme kũeleanwa na mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa na kĩu kĩiete mathĩna. Mathĩna ta asu makaumĩla na tũimaeka, nĩkwĩsa kwĩthĩa twoveee ũthatu ngoonĩ.—Soma 1 Vetelo 3:8, 9.
8, 9. (a) Nĩ nguma syĩva itonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkwata ũla mũthĩnzĩo? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũendeee kwĩkalany'a na mũuo o na ethĩwa Mũklĩsto ũngĩ nĩwatũthatya?
8 Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũikekale na ũthatu ngoonĩ na ũyĩsa kũtũvata ũla mũthĩnzĩo? Vaulo eeie Akolosai atĩĩ: "Tondũ mwĩ anyuve ma Ngai, atheu na endwa, ĩvw'ĩkei ngoo yĩ na ĩnee ya kwĩw'anĩa tei [kana, kwĩkana ũseo], wĩnyivyo, ũuu, wũmĩĩsyo; kũmĩĩasya ũmwe kwa ũla ũngĩ, na kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene, ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva e na ũndũ na ũngĩ; o tondu Mwĩaĩi wamũekeie, inyw'ĩ nenyu ĩkaai o ta ũu: na mbee wa maũndũ aa onthe ĩvw'ĩkei wendo, naw'o nĩ wovano wa wĩanĩu."—Ako. 3:12-14.
9 Ethĩwa nĩtwendete kwĩka ũseo na nĩtwendanĩte, tũikaemawa nĩ kũekeanaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa nĩtũkwĩw'a twaũmĩw'a nĩ kĩndũ Mũklĩsto ũngĩ weeka kana ndeto waneena, no tũsũanĩe mavinda ala ithyĩ ene twaaneena tũkavĩtya kana tũkeka kĩndũ kĩte kĩseo. Ithyĩ tyo tũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa wendo na ũseo wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala mataatinda maatĩanĩe na mavĩtyo maitũ? (Soma Mũtavan'ya 7:21, 22.) Na kĩla kĩtumaa tũtũnga mũvea mũnango nĩ ũseo ũla Klĩsto wonetye athaithi ma w'o kwa kũmombany'a vamwe mekale me ngwatanĩo. (Ako. 3:15) Ithyonthe twendete Ngai ũmwe, tũtavanasya ũvoo ũvw'anene, na tũkomanaa na mathĩna maingĩ mavw'anene. No tũlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo ya kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto na tũyĩkalaa tũsyaĩĩsye ũla mũthĩnzĩo ethĩwa tũkeethĩawa twendene na tũkeekaa ala angĩ ũseo kwa kũmaekea kuma ngoonĩ.
10, 11. (a) Nĩkĩ kĩwĩu ti kĩseo? (b) Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana kĩwĩu kĩikese kũtũvata ũla mũthĩnzĩo?
10 Ve ngelekany'o sya andũ mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ itũlilikanasya kana kĩwĩu no kĩtume tũtakwata ũla mũthĩnzĩo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Kaini wambĩĩe kwĩw'ĩa mwana-a-inyia Aveli kĩwĩu, nĩwesie kũmũaa. Namo Kola, Ndathani, na Avilamu nĩmambĩĩe kwĩw'ĩa Mose kĩwĩu na mũthya malika kũmũvĩnga. O nake Mũsumbĩ Saulo nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩwĩu nũndũ wa kwona Ndaviti aikwata nguma na kwoou enda kũmũaa. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Vala ve kĩwĩu na ngananĩo, nĩvo ve kĩthokoo na kĩla wĩa mũthũku."—Yak. 3:16.
11 Ethĩwa twĩ wendo na nĩtwendete kwĩka angĩ ũseo, ti laisi tũkwatwe nĩ kĩwĩu. Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye: "Wendo nĩwũmĩĩasya, na nĩwĩkaa moseo; wendo ndwĩ na kĩwĩu." (1 Ako. 13:4) Twenda tũikese kũlikwa nĩ kĩwĩu ngoonĩ sitũ, no nginya tũtate kwonaa maũndũ ũndũ Ngai ũmonaa. Ũu nĩ kwasya twaĩle kũmanya kana ithyonthe twĩ mamutha ma mwĩĩ ũmwe, ũla nĩw'o kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto. Kũmanya ũu kũkatũtetheeasya twĩkae o ũndũ ndeto ii mbeveee itũtavĩtye: "Ethĩwa . . . mutha ũmwe nũũtaĩwa, aa angĩ onthe nĩmatanaa vamwe naw'o." (1 Ako. 12:16-18, 26) Na kwoou angĩ makwata ũathimo, tũkatanaa vamwe namo vandũ va kũmew'ĩa kĩwĩu. Kwa twose ngelekany'o ya mwana wa Mũsumbĩ Saulo weetawa Yonathani. Yonathani ndaaĩw'ĩa Ndaviti kĩwĩu ĩla wanyuviwe etw'ĩka mũsumbĩ. Vandũ va ũu, eekie kũmwĩkĩa vinya. (1 Sam. 23:16-18) Ithyĩ tyo twaĩle kwĩka angĩ ũseo na tũimenda ũndũ Yonathani wendete Ndaviti?
MŨSYĨ WENYU ŨKASINDA MŨTHĨNZĨO?
12. Nĩ ũtao wĩva wĩ Maandĩkonĩ waatĩĩwa ũtonya kũtetheesya mĩsyĩ yitũ yĩsinda ũla mũthĩnzĩo?
12 Kũatĩĩa myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ no kũtetheesye mũsyĩ w'onthe kwĩkala na mũuo na ũtanu, na ĩtina mũsyĩ ũsu ũisinda ũla mũthĩnzĩo. Vaulo anengie Aklĩsto ala maĩ Kolosai ũtao wĩva ĩũlũ wa mĩsyĩ? Aisye: "Iveti, ĩnyivĩsyei aũme menyu, ũndũ waĩle nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi. Aũme, endai iveti syenyu, na mũikasyĩw'ĩe woo. Syana, mew'ei asyai menyu maũndũnĩ onthe, nũndũ ũu nĩwendeeasya nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi. Aasa, mũikathatye syana syenyu, itikakw'e ngoo." (Ako. 3:18-21) We no ũlee kana kũatĩĩa ũtao ũsu mũveveee no kũtethye aũme, iveti, na syana ũmũnthĩ?
13. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũtwaĩtwe nĩ mũndũũme ũte mwĩtĩkĩli atonya kũmũtetheesya ata emanyĩsye ũw'o?
13 Nata ethĩwa ũtwaĩtwe nĩ mũndũ ũte mwĩtĩkĩli na ndwĩw'aa aiũkua nesa? We nũkwona kũtinda ũitetany'a nake ta kũtethya? O na ethĩwa ĩteta yaku nĩyatuma eka ũndũ ũkwendaa, we wĩona ĩteta yĩu ta yĩtuma emanyĩsya ũw'o? Ve vinya. Kĩla kĩtonya kũũtethya nĩ kwĩnyivĩsya ũkũmũ wa mũemeu. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtonya kũtuma mũsyĩ wenyu wĩthĩwa na mũuo, ũetee Yeova ndaĩa, o na kũkatuma mũemeu emanyĩsya ũw'o, na mũthya inyw'elĩ mũikwata ũla mũthĩnzĩo.—Soma 1 Vetelo 3:1, 2.
14. Mwana-a-asa aĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa ndekwona ainengwa ndaĩa nĩ mũka wake ũte mwĩtĩkĩli?
14 Nata ethĩwa mũka waku ti mwĩtĩkĩli na wonaa ateũkũnenga ndaĩa? We wĩona kũmũkũnĩa kelele nĩ kana amanye nũũ mũtwe wa mũsyĩ ta kwĩsa kũtuma aũnenga ndaĩa? Eka mwa! Ngai endaa ũũngamĩe mũsyĩ waku wĩ na wendo o tondũ Yesũ ũũngamĩaa kĩkundi. (Aev. 5:23) Yesũ nĩwendete kĩkundi na akĩtongoeasya na wũmĩĩsyo. (Luka 9:46-48) Mwana-a-asa aatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ, no atetheesye mũka emanyĩsye ũw'o.
15. Mũndũũme Mũklĩsto atonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩwendete mũka?
15 Aũme meĩtwe atĩĩ: "Endai iveti syenyu, na mũikasyĩw'ĩe woo." (Ako. 3:19) Mũndũũme wendete kĩveti kyake na ũkĩnengete ndaĩa nũkĩthukĩĩasya nesa ĩla kĩkumya mawoni na aikĩĩkĩĩthya kana mawoni makyo nĩ ma vata. (1 Vet. 3:7) O na kau ti mavinda onthe ũtonya kwĩka ũndũ kĩveti kĩkwenda, no eke motwi maseango akĩkũlya woni wakyo. (Nth. 15:22) Mũndũũme wendete kĩveti kyake ndakĩlasimĩthasya kĩmũnenge ndaĩa, ĩndĩ nĩwĩkaa maũndũ matonya kũtuma kyenda kũmũnenga ndaĩa. Ethĩwa mwana-a-asa nĩwendete syana syake vamwe na kĩveti kyake, ti vinya mũsyĩ wake ũkamũthũkũma Yeova na ũtanu, na ũyĩsa kũsinda ũla mũthĩnzĩo wa thayũ.
AMŨIKA MŨIKETĨKĨLE KĨNDŨ O NA KĨVA KĨMŨVATE ŨLA MŨTHĨNZĨO!
16, 17. Amũika, mũtonya kwĩka ata mũikew'ĩe asyai menyu woo mũno?
16 Nata ethĩwa wĩ wa mũika na wĩw'aa asyai maku mateũkũelewa na maikwĩkĩĩa mĩao mingĩ? Nũtonya kwĩw'a ũithĩnĩka nginya ũkambĩĩa kwĩkũlya kana kũthaitha Yeova ve vandũ kwĩsa kũũvikya. Ĩndĩ ũkaelya kũeka kũmũthũkũma Yeova nũndũ wa ũndũ ũkwĩw'a, wĩsa kwĩthĩa kaĩ vai vandũ wĩsa kũthĩnĩkĩwa nesa ta mokonĩ ma asyai maku Aklĩsto na nthĩnĩ wa kĩkundi!
17 Ũkekala na asyai mateũkũlũnga mũthenya o na ũmwe, we ndwĩkũlya kana kwa w'o nĩmaũnganaa naku? (Aevl. 12:8) Ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa kĩla kĩtumaa wĩw'a woo nĩ ũndũ asyai maku maũkanasya. Vandũ va kũtinda ũsũanĩĩte mũno ũndũ maumasya ũkany'o, sũanĩa kĩla kĩtumaa meka ũndũ mekaa kana maneena ũndũ maneenaa. Kwoou ĩkalaa ũuĩtye na ũitata ũndũ ũtonya wĩsiĩĩe ĩla ũũkanw'a. Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye: "Ũla ũsũvĩaa ndeto syake e na ũĩ; na ũla wĩ na veva mũuu nĩ mũndũ wĩ na ũmanyi." (Nth. 17:27) Wĩona ata ũkekĩa kĩthito ũtw'ĩke mũndũ mũima ũtonya kwosa ũkany'o auĩtye na ayĩtĩkĩla kũũatĩĩa ate kũsũanĩa mũno ũndũ waumw'a? (Nth. 1:8) Nũathimo mũnene kwĩthĩwa na asyai mamwendete Yeova kuma ngoonĩ. Asyai asu methĩawa mayenda kũũtetheesya wĩkwata ũla mũthĩnzĩo wa thayũ.
18. Nĩkĩ ũtw'ĩte vyũ kwĩkalaa ũsyaĩĩsye ũla mũthĩnzĩo?
18 Wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o ndwĩ maela, wĩthĩwe nĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa kũkwata thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a ĩtunĩ kana thayũ wa tene na tene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ. Ũsu nĩ wĩkwatyo twaĩle kwĩkala tũiũvindĩĩsya. Nĩ watho wa w'o vyũ twathĩtwe nĩ Mũmbi mwene. Ngai aĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Nthĩ ĩsu Nzaũ: "Ĩkausũw'a nĩ kũmũmanya Yeova." (Isa. 11:9) Onthe ala makatũa nthĩ ĩsu makeethĩwa me andũ mamanyĩĩtw'e nĩ Ngai. Ũsu nĩ mũthĩnzĩo waĩle kũtata ũndũ ũtonya ndũkaaũkose o na vanini. Kwoou ĩkalaa ũivindĩĩsya kĩla Yeova ũtwathĩte, na ndũkaaĩtĩkĩle kĩndũ o na kĩva kĩũvate ũla mũthĩnzĩo!

translation:
"A person who loves me will keep my commands."—JOHN 14:15.
PAGE 32, 55
1, 2. (a) What reasons does God give for keeping his commands? (b) Why is it important that we strive to obey them fully? (Consider the illustration.)
CHRIST was an example of obedience, and he encouraged others to be obedient to God's Law. (Phil. 3:14) We too can show our love for Jesus Christ by supporting his Kingdom and zealously proclaiming the good news. (Matt. 20:6) Christ earnestly prayed to God for strength to remain obedient! And we can ask for help to keep our resolutions and to stay loyal to Jehovah.—2 Pet. 3:13.
2 Paul continued to support Christ, even though he himself had once persecuted Christians, saying: "Let your reasonableness become known to everyone." (Acts 3:2) He wanted to live in harmony with God's will. (Acts 1:4, 5) The servants of Jehovah are motivated by their love for him to help people learn about his requirements, whether they relate to worship or to righteous living.—1 Acts 9:24.
3. How did Paul support Christ?
3 Paul readily used examples to illustrate how to apply Christian principles. For instance, in writing to the congregation at Colossae, he showed how Christ's teachings were superior to human traditions and philosophies that led people away from Christ and toward false worship. (Colossians 2:16-18) Also, Paul gave practical advice on everyday matters, which could help them maintain spiritual stability. For example, he explained how to deal with disagreements among family members and how to avoid getting involved in frivolous lawsuits. These things helped them appreciate the value of maintaining good relationships. In view of this, let us examine some of the counsel Paul wrote to the Colossians.
CONSIDER EVERYDAY MATTERS
4. What everyday matters can hinder our spirituality?
4 Paul mentioned some common weaknesses that can affect our thinking, and he warned against them, saying: "Put away from yourselves all uncleanness, and also wicked ways, and improper conduct, and abusive speech." (Acts 3:5) Improper conduct can gradually erode our relationship with Jehovah and cause us to lose sight of what is important. One young man who was influenced by bad association later admitted: "I began to enjoy doing wrong, and I started to disregard moral standards."
5. How can we avoid being influenced by negative influences?
5 It is vital that we be discerning about the company we keep so that we do not stumble and feel that we have failed to meet Jehovah's high standard. For example, perhaps you know people who spend their time engaging in questionable activities, such as getting involved with harmful companions, practicing violence, or indulging in immoral entertainment. (Prov. 22:3) And even Christians may face temptations to engage in wrongdoing, whether it involves lying or associating with someone who has a bad reputation. (Prov. 2:10-12, 16) If you find yourself drawn to negative influences, seek help from an elder or a mature Christian, and ask him to pray for you. Do not try to deal with temptation on your own. We can also protect ourselves from negative influences by avoiding situations where we might be exposed to wrongdoing or by limiting our contact with those who practice it. But sometimes, despite our best efforts, we may still find ourselves struggling. In such cases, we need to rely on God's strength and continue to fight. We can also benefit from speaking to someone who can help us analyze the situation and offer practical advice. Remember that Jehovah and his organization are always ready to assist us.—Read Psalm 34:18; Proverbs 13:20.
6. How can we remain spiritually strong?
6 We will strengthen our spirituality if we regularly examine ourselves and address any problems we see. Many spiritual problems arise because of association with worldly people. (Jude 7) However, examining ourselves should involve more than just identifying serious sins. We should also look for subtle ways in which worldly thinking might affect us. We need to examine everything we encounter in connection with worldly things. We should examine ourselves regularly, but this should not discourage us from continuing to progress.—Prov. 4:23.
"BE VIGILANT" REGARDING BAD ASSOCIATIONS
7. What questions should we ask ourselves?
7 Ask yourself whether you feel comfortable being around certain individuals. Often, we are influenced by those who do not value Bible principles and who associate with immoral people. This can weaken our spirituality. So, when possible, limit your contact with such people. Also, be cautious about getting too involved with family members or friends who have questionable standards. If they persist in bad habits, it may be wise to distance yourself from them.—Read 1 Peter 3:8, 9.
8, 9. (a) What principle can help us maintain our spirituality? (b) Why is it important to continue associating with Christians who encourage us?
8 Can we ever completely avoid having some association with imperfect people? The apostle Paul wrote: "Since you are God's chosen people, holy and beloved, cultivate brotherly affection, tender mercies, humility, mild temper, patience, gladly forgiving one another, and above all, love, which is the bond of perfection." (Col. 3:12-14.)
9 To maintain peace, we need to be considerate and kind. For example, when a fellow Christian makes a mistake or says something hurtful, we should try to overlook it rather than dwell on it. How can we show empathy and understanding toward others, especially those who have been deeply hurt? (Read Matthew 7:21, 22.) And remember that our ability to empathize stems from Christ's example of self-sacrifice. (Col. 3:15) Above all, let us imitate God, being generous and ready to forgive, just as he generously forgave us. Let us strengthen ourselves in the love of the Christian congregation and remain united in pursuing righteousness, so that we may continue to please Jehovah and enjoy closer fellowship with one another.
10, 11. (a) What is empathy? (b) Can empathy help us to maintain spiritual health?
10 Consider the experience of some ancient men. They illustrate how empathy can affect our spiritual health. For instance, Cain was consumed by envy when his brother Abel received approval from God, which led him to murder Abel. Also, Korah, Dathan, and Abiram were motivated by envy when they rebelled against Moses. Similarly, King Saul was tormented by jealousy toward David, leading him to seek David's death. That is why the Bible warns: "Jealousy is the fury of mankind."—Jas. 3:16.
11 Let us cultivate love and avoid becoming envious of others. The Bible says: "Love is patient and kind. Love does not become jealous." (1 Cor. 13:4) We want to please Jehovah, so we should not allow ourselves to be controlled by envy, nor should we try to imitate those who give way to it. This will help us to understand whether we truly belong to the Christian congregation. Understanding this can strengthen our resolve to heed the counsel found in the Scriptures: "Be devoted to one another in brotherly affection." (1 Cor. 12:16-18, 26) And if others show animosity toward us, we should strive to maintain peace with them. A fine example of loyalty is seen in Jonathan, the son of King Saul. Jonathan loved David deeply and risked his own life to protect him. People appreciated his loyalty. (1 Sam. 23:16-18) How then can we cultivate such loyalty and show love like Jonathan did?
DO YOU VALUE LOYALTY?
12. Is it wise to carefully examine the reasons why our brothers may seem disloyal?
12 To illustrate, consider the experience of the traveling overseer Apollos and how he helped a congregation to deal with disunity. He took time to listen to both sides and to offer encouragement. Paul asked the Christians in Colossae about their spiritual condition, saying: "I want you to know how much I am concerned for you, and how hard I work in my prayers for you. I want you to stand firm in your faith, and not be moved from the hope held out in the good news." (Col. 3:18-21) Think about whether taking such steps—listening, offering encouragement, and praying—would help you to better understand the situation.
13. What qualities in a true friend enable him to remain loyal even when there is disagreement?
13 Does a true friend always agree with everything you say or do? No, a true friend will speak honestly, even if it means pointing out your faults. But does honesty necessarily mean being unkind? Or can tactfulness help to convey the truth in a way that is easier to accept? Of course. The key to speaking truthfully is to show genuine concern for the person. In fact, loyalty often means helping your friend to maintain his dignity, so that Jehovah will be glorified, and others will respond favorably to the message.—Read 1 Peter 3:1, 2.
14. How can a wife show confidence in her husband even if she disagrees with him?
14 Does a wife need to publicly correct her husband or embarrass him in front of others? Instead, she can thoughtfully consider whether she can support him privately, while still maintaining her integrity. Would it be possible to discuss her concerns with him in a calm and respectful manner? Certainly! Let us imitate Jesus' example in dealing with the congregation. (Eph. 5:23) Jesus spoke to the disciples with dignity and mildness. (Luke 9:46-48) A wife can imitate Jesus' approach and help her husband to maintain his dignity.
15. Can a Christian elder sometimes offer counsel without being asked?
15 Some elders have said: "Go through your own homes and strengthen yourselves." (Acts. 3:19) An elder who goes to his brothers and sisters to encourage them may notice problems that they themselves haven't recognized, such as a negative attitude or a tendency to associate with bad company. (1 Pet. 3:7) And even if he doesn't see a problem, his visit might give them something positive to think about. (Prov. 15:22) An elder who visits his brothers and sisters shows that he cares for them, which can help them to avoid problems and remain loyal. When a wife supports her husband and they both seek guidance from Jehovah, they are more likely to find solutions that honor God.
REMEMBER TO BE DISCREET AND TO CONSIDER THE CONSEQUENCES!
16, 17. Why should we carefully consider how our words might affect others?
16 Think of the effect your words have on others—how they react and what they remember. Are there times when you could unintentionally discourage someone or cause him to stumble spiritually? If you speak thoughtlessly, you might hinder someone's progress in serving Jehovah. But if you choose your words carefully, you can build up fellow Christians and strengthen their faith!
17 Do you regularly spend time thinking about how your words affect others? (Prov. 12:8) If so, you will likely avoid saying things that could be hurtful. People often respond negatively to harsh comments, so strive to speak kindly and thoughtfully. Always try to put yourself in the other person's place. God's Word says: "The heart of the discerning one discerns his speech, and he makes discernment of ears attentive." (Prov. 17:27) Have you ever felt hurt because someone said something unkind or discouraging? Did it make you question whether you were doing the right thing? (Prov. 1:8) It is important to be considerate of those who are trying to please Jehovah. They need our encouragement and support.
18 Then, how can we make sure our words are encouraging?
18 To encourage others, we need to show genuine interest in them, appreciate their efforts, and help them see their value. We should also remind them of God's love and promises. By doing so, we can strengthen their faith and resolve. This pleases our Creator. God said through Isaiah: "By knowing Jehovah, people come to know him." (Isa. 11:9) Therefore, when we take the time to get to know others and learn what is important to them, we are showing that we care. So let us endeavor to encourage one another, always remembering that our words have power!

text:
"Ũtanu wakwa waĩ na ana ma andũ."—NTH. 8:31.
1, 2. Nĩ ũndũ ũmwe wĩva wonanasya kana Yesũ nĩwendete andũ mũno?
ŨĨ WA Yeova woonekie nesa vyũ ĩla woombie Mwana wake mũsyawa wa mbee. Mwana ũsu awetetwe ta we ũĩ na akasyoka akewa aĩ "mũthũkũmi mũnene" wa Ĩthe. Kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla weew'aa na ũndũ weew'aa e mwĩanĩe ĩla Ĩthe "walũmilye matu" na 'atw'a myambĩlĩlyo ya nthĩ.' O na kau Mwana mũsyawa wa mbee wa Ngai nĩwendie syĩndũ isu syoombiwe, "ũtanu [wake] waĩ na ana ma andũ." (Nth. 8:22-31) Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩonany'a kana Yesũ ambĩĩe kũtanĩthw'a nĩ andũ, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ambĩĩe kwenda andũ, tene o na ataaĩsa kũka kũũ nthĩ.
2 Ĩtina, Mwana Mũsyawa wa Mbee wa Ngai nĩwoonanisye kana nĩwendete Ĩthe na nũlũmanĩtye vyũ nake, na kana nĩwendete "ana ma andũ," ĩla kwa ngenda yake 'watiie ũla w'onthe' waĩ naw'o na oosa mũvw'ano wa andũ. Eekie ũu nĩ kana anengane "thayũ wake wĩthĩwe wovosyo kwondũ wa aingĩ." (Avi. 2:5-8, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language; Mt. 20:28) Vate nzika nĩwendete andũ mũno. Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ, Ngai nĩwamũnengie vinya wa kwĩka syama syoonanisye ũndũ wendete andũ. Syama isu Yesũ weekie syoonanisye maũndũ maseo vyũ ala makilyĩ maneekĩka nthĩ yonthe.
3. Twĩneenea kyaũ?
3 O na ĩngĩ, ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ 'nĩwatavanisye ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai.' (Luka 4:43) Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩw'o ũkathesya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ĩthe wake na ũivetea andũ mathĩna onthe tene na tene. Kwoou ti ũsengy'o kana ĩla waendaa kũũ na kũũ aitavany'a, nĩweekie maũndũ maingĩ moonany'a kana nĩwathĩnĩkĩaa andũ vyũ kuma ngoonĩ. Kũmanya ũu kũtonya kũtũtethya ata? Nĩ kwa vata nũndũ maũndũ ala weekie matumaa twĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo na tweteela ĩvinda yũkĩte twĩ eanĩe. Ekai ĩndĩ tũneenee syama inya katĩ wa ila Yesũ weekie.
'VINYA WA KŨVOSYA WAĨ VAMWE NAKE'
4. Elesya kĩla kyeekĩkie ĩla Yesũ wakomanie na mũndũ waĩ na ũwau wa mangũ.
4 Ve ĩvinda Yesũ watavanasya kĩsionĩ kya Kalilii na vaĩ vavĩtu ĩvinda kuma ambĩĩa kũtavany'a kũũ nthĩ. E ndũanĩ ĩmwe kũu Kalilii, nĩwakomanie na mũndũ wa kũmakĩwa. (Mko. 1:39, 40) Mũndũ ũsu aĩ na ũwau mũthũku wa mangũ. Luka, ũla waĩ ndakĩtalĩ, aandĩkie mũndũ ũsu 'oombĩtwe nĩ mangũ' nĩ kana onany'e ũndũ mũndũ ũsu wawaĩte mũno wĩana. (Luka 5:12) Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Na [mũndũ ũsu] amwona Yesũ, eevalũkya nthĩ na ũthyũ, amwĩsũva, akyasya, Mwĩaĩi, ethĩwa nũkwenda, nũtonya kũnthesya." Mũndũ ũsu ndaĩ na nzika kana Yesũ nĩwaĩ na ũtonyi wa kũmũvosya, ĩndĩ kĩla wendaa kũmanya nĩ, We Yesũ aĩ na wendi wa kwĩka ũu? Yesũ esaa kwĩka ata ĩla weesũviwe nĩ mũndũ ũsu? Asũanĩaa ata aũngye vau asyaĩĩsye mũndũ ũsu waanangĩtwe mũno wĩana ũu nĩ ũwau? We Yesũ nĩwesaa kwĩka ta Avalisi ala mateew'ĩaa tei andũ ala mawaĩte ũwau ũsu? Keka nue wĩthĩwa weekie ata?
5. Nĩkĩ ĩla Yesũ wavoasya ũla mũndũ waĩ na mangũ waisye, "Nĩngwenda"?
5 Kwosana na Mĩao ya Mose, mũndũ ũsu waĩ mũwau mangũ aaĩle kwĩthĩwa aisye na wasya mũnene, "Mũvuku, mũvuku," ĩndĩ veoneka ndaaĩka ũu. Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaatinda aimũkũlya isu. Kĩlĩko kyake kyaĩ mũndũnĩ ũsu vamwe na thĩna ũla waĩ naw'o. (Ali. 13:43-46) O na kau tũyĩsĩ nesa kĩla Yesũ wasũanĩaa, nĩtwĩsĩ kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ yake. Nũndũ wa tei wake, eekie ũndũ o na andũ mataĩ masũanĩa kana nũtonyeka. Amũkiitie, na aneena na ũkũmbaũ ĩndĩ e na tei, amwĩa, "Nĩngwenda; ĩthĩwa mũtheu." Ĩtina wa ũu Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Na oyu mangũ mavoa." (Luka 5:13) Vate nzika vinya wa Yeova nĩwoonekie ĩvinda yĩu. Vinya ũsu nĩw'o watetheeisye Yesũ kwĩka kyama kĩu na kwonany'a ũndũ wendete andũ mũno wĩana.—Luka 5:17.
6. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtwendeeasya mũno ĩũlũ wa syama ila Yesũ weekie, na syama isu syĩtwony'a kyaũ?
6 Vinya wa Ngai nĩwatetheeisye Yesũ Klĩsto eke syama mbingĩ sya ũsengy'a. Eka kũvosya ala maĩ na mangũ, nĩwavoisye andũ me na mowau ma mĩthemba yonthe na kĩla wonzu. Mbivilia ĩtwĩaa atĩĩ: "Mũvaka yĩla ĩkomano yaseng'a, yoona ala mataaneena maineena, na ala au mamutha me aima, na ila syonze iikinya, na ililinda ikyona." (Mt. 15:31) Ũmũnthĩ mavinda amwe ĩla matakĩtalĩ meũthĩnza mũndũ ũwaĩte mamutha mana, mekaa kũmumya mamutha asu mawau makamwĩkĩa angĩ nĩ kana avoe. Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaĩ na vata wa kwĩka ta matakĩtalĩ asu, eekaa kũvosya mamutha ala mawau! Na ũndũ wa ũsengy'o nĩ kana avoasya andũ vau kwa vau, na mavinda angĩ o na me vaasa nake. (Yoa. 4:46-54) Maũndũ asu manenevete ũu meekiwe nĩ Yesũ metwony'a kyaũ? Metwony'a kana nũndũ Yesũ yu nĩ Mũsumbĩ ĩtunĩ, e na vinya na wendi wa kũvetangĩa andũ mowau tene na tene. Ĩla tweemanyĩsya ũndũ Yesũ weekaa andũ maũndũ maseo, nĩtwĩthĩawa na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu kana ĩvinda ya nthĩ nzaũ wathani ũũ wĩ Mbivilianĩ ũkeanĩa: "Akeew'ĩa tei ngya na athĩni." (Sav. 72:13) Nĩ w'o vyũ, ĩvinda yĩu Yesũ akeka kwosana na wendi ũla wĩ ngoonĩ yake atetheesye ala onthe me na mathĩna.
"ŨKĨLA, NOKYOSA ŨKOMO WAKU ŨTHI"
7, 8. Elesya maũndũ ala maendeee Yesũ ayĩsa kwĩthĩana na mũndũ mũwau ndianĩ ya Vethesita.
7 Nĩvavĩtie myei mĩvũthũ kuma Yesũ akomanĩa na ũla mũndũ wawaĩte mangũ kĩsionĩ kya Kalilii. Auma Kalilii aendie Yutia akatavany'e na kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Andũ ala Yesũ watavisye ũvoo na ameka maũndũ maseo mailea kwĩthĩwa mavikie makili meana ũndũ mũna. Andũ nĩmeene nesa kana aĩ na wendi wa kũtavya ngya ũvoo mũseo, kũtavany'a ũthasyo kwa ala atave, na kwova ala me na ngoo ndũlĩku.—Isa. 61:1, 2; Luka 4:18-21.
8 Ĩla mwei wa Nisani wavikie, Yesũ nĩwaendie Yelusaleme kwondũ wa Vasaka o tondũ Ĩthe weeaĩte. Ndũa ĩsu yausũĩte andũ mokĩte kũkwata Vasaka. O vau ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya ĩkalũ vaĩ ndia yeetawa Vethesita. Vau ndianĩ ĩsu nĩvo Yesũ weethĩanĩie na mũndũ mũwau.
9, 10. (a) Nĩkĩ andũ maendaa ndianĩ ya Vethesita? (b) Yesũ eekie ata ĩla waendie ndianĩ ĩsu, na kĩu kĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
9 Ndianĩ ya Vethesita voombanĩaa andũ aingĩ awau na onzu. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumaa mathi vau? Nũndũ wa itumi itesĩkĩe, maĩkĩĩaa kana mũndũ mũwau alika ndianĩ ĩsu ĩla kĩw'ũ kyakwaithangw'a, ve kyama kyeekĩkaa akavoa. Kwoou kwasũanĩa ũndũ vandũ vau vavĩtũkanaa andũ meew'aa makw'ĩte ngoo, me na kĩũũyũ kingĩ, na makilyĩ kwĩyĩĩtũka. Ĩndĩ we Yesũ aendete vau kĩ na ndaĩ mũwau, o na ndaĩ na naĩ? Aendie vau nũndũ nĩwendete andũ. E vau nĩw'o woonie mũndũ wawaĩte kuma o nake mwene ate mũsyae.—Soma Yoana 5:5-9.
10 Kwa kũna visa wone ũndũ mũndũ ũsu wakw'ĩte ngoo Yesũ aimũkũlya ethĩwa nũkwenda kũvoa. Asũngĩie ĩkũlyo ya Yesũ o na atekwananga ndatĩka. Amwĩie nĩwendaa mũno kũvoa, ĩndĩ ndoonaa ta ũkesa kũkwata mwanya ũsu nũndũ ndaĩ na mũndũ ũmũtethya kũlika ndianĩ kĩla ĩvinda yesa kũkwaithangw'a. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Yesũ weeie mũndũ ũsu eke ũndũ wa kũsengy'a. Amwĩie nĩ ose ũkomo wake na aithi. Nĩwaĩkĩĩie ndeto sya Yesũ, oosa ũkomo wake, na ambĩĩa kũthi. Kyama kĩu nĩkĩtwĩkĩaa vinya mũno nũndũ kĩtwonasya maũndũ ala Yesũ ũkeka nthĩ nzaũ. O na ĩngĩ kyama kyu kĩtwonasya ũndũ Yesũ wĩany'a tei. Nĩwamanthaa ala me na thĩna amatethye. Kwoou ngelekany'o yake yaĩle kũtwĩkĩa vinya tũkamanthaa isionĩ sitũ andũ ala makw'ĩte ngoo nũndũ wa maũndũ mathũku ma nthĩ ĩno.
"NŨŨ ŨLA WANGIITA NGŨA SYAKWA?"
11. Ĩandĩko ya Maliko 5:25-34 yonanĩtye ata kana Yesũ nĩweew'ĩaa awau tei?
11 Soma Maliko 5:25-34. Ve mũndũ mũka ũmwe wekalĩte myaka 12 e na ũwau wĩ nthoni mũno. Ũwau ũsu wamwanangĩĩte maũndũ maingĩ nginya o na ũkamwanangĩa ũthaithi. Mũndũ mũka ũsu aendeee naĩ o na kau 'nĩwanyamaĩtw'e mũno nĩ aiiti aingĩ, na nĩwaanangĩte syonthe ila waĩ nasyo.' Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe nĩwavangie kwĩka kaũndũ kake avoe. Avangie kwĩsĩla vakuvĩ na Yesũ. Kwoou nĩwalikĩile nguthunĩ ya andũ na akiita ngũa sya Yesũ. (Ali. 15:19, 25) Yesũ nĩweewie vinya waoleka, na akũlya ũla wamũkiita nũũ. Ĩla mũndũ mũka ũsu weewie ũu, 'nĩwakĩie na atetema,' na athi vala ũĩ, "avalũka nthĩ mbee wake, na amũtavya w'o w'onthe." Ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩwamanyie kana Ĩthe wake, Yeova, nĩwavosya mũndũ mũka ũsu, na nũndũ wa ũu amũneenisye na tei amwĩa: "Mwĩĩtu, mũĩkĩĩo waku nĩwakũvosya; thi na ũvoo, wĩthĩwe wĩ mũima, ũte na ũthĩn'yo waku."
12. (a) Kũvikĩa vau ũtonya kwasya Yesũ ailyĩ ata? (b) Yesũ atũtiĩe ngelekany'o yĩva?
12 Tei ũla Yesũ ũĩ nĩ mwingĩ mũno! O na e ngoo ya kũtethya ala meũthĩnw'a nĩ mowau. Ĩndĩ we Satani endaa twone ta twĩ andũ mate vala maĩ na ta vate mũndũ ũtwendete. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, ĩla Yesũ weekie syama oonanisye nesa ki kana nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa vyũ na nĩwendaa kũtũvetea mathĩna. Twaĩle kwĩw'a mũyo mũno nũndũ twĩ na Mũsumbĩ na Mũthembi Mũnene ũla ũtwĩw'ĩaa tei! (Aevl. 4:15) Ti laisi kũelewa ũndũ ala me na mowau mathũku mew'aa, na mũno mũno ethĩwa tũyaakwatwa nĩ ũwau ta ũsu. Ĩndĩ lilikana kana we Yesũ nĩweew'ĩaa tei ala awau o na kau ndaawaa sua o na ũmwe. Nĩtũtatei ũndũ tũtonya tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ĩsu ya Yesũ.—1 Vet. 3:8.
"YESŨ AĨA"
13. Kyama kĩla Yesũ weekie kya kũthayũũkya Lasalo kyoonanisye we ailyĩ ata?
13 Yesũ nĩwathĩnĩkaa oona ala angĩ maithĩna. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla woonie ala angĩ maiĩa ĩla mũnyanyae Lasalo wakw'ĩte, Yesũ 'nĩweewie woo vevanĩ' na "aũũya." Akwatiwe nĩ kyeva kĩu o na kau nĩweesĩ akilyĩ anathayũũkya Lasalo. (Soma Yoana 11:33-36.) Yesũ ndaakĩa kwonany'a kyeva kĩla waĩ nakyo. O na ala masyaĩĩsye nĩmoonie nesa kana Yesũ nĩwendete Lasalo na mũsyĩ ũsu. Ũndũ ũsu Yesũ weekie wa kũtũmĩa vinya ũla wanengetwe nĩ Ngai amũthayũũkye mũnyanyae woonanisye e tei mwingĩ mũno.—Yoa. 11:43, 44.
14, 15. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana Yeova e na wendi mwingĩ wa kũvetea andũ mathĩna? (b) Ngai akatũmĩa kĩlilikano kyake ata ĩvindanĩ ya ũthayũũkyo?
14 Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yesũ nĩwe "mũvw'ano ki wa mũvw'anĩle [wa Mũmbi]." (Aevl. 1:3) Kwoou ĩla weekie syama, nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana we na Ĩthe me na wendi wa kũvetanga mathĩna ala maaetwe nĩ mowau na kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ ti atĩ wendi ũsu woo nĩwathelile ĩla mathayũũkisye andũ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ wawetie ndeto ii: "Saa nĩwũkĩte, yĩla onthe ala me mbũanĩ . . . makauma."—Yoa. 5:28, 29.
15 Ĩvindanĩ ya ũthayũũkyo, Ngai nũkatũmĩa kĩlilikano kyake. Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe, ũla nĩwe woombie nthĩ yonthe, nũtonya kũlilikana maũndũ onthe ĩũlũ wa endwa maitũ ala makwie. Ũu nĩ kwasya no alilikane tũmaũndũ twoo twa mũsyawa vamwe na tũla meekie kwĩmanyĩsya. (Isa. 40:26) Na eka kũtw'ĩka kana Ngai nũtonya kũlilikana, we na Mwana wake methĩawa na wendi wa kũlilikana maũndũ onthe ĩũlũ wa andũ asu. Kũthayũũkw'a kwa Lasalo na ala angĩ mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ kwonanasya kĩla kĩkekĩka nthĩ nzaũ.
SYAMA SYA YESŨ ITONYA KŨŨMANYĨSYA KYAŨ?
16. Aklĩsto ala mekalaa me aĩkĩĩku makanewa kĩanda kĩva ĩvinda yũkĩte?
16 Twekala twĩ aĩkĩĩku, nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kwona kyama kĩnene vyũ kũte syama syonthe ila syaaĩkĩka, nakyo nĩ kũvonoka ũla thĩna mũnene. Na ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni, tũkoona syama ingĩ mbingĩ ila ikatuma andũ methĩwa na ũima wa mwĩĩ. (Isa. 33:24; 35:5, 6; Ũvu. 21:4) Kwa kũna visa andũ mayĩkya mĩwanĩ, ndata, tũsululu twa ala onzu mamutha, tũmasinĩ twa matũ, na syĩndũ ingĩ ta isu. Yeova akeethĩwa na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũnenga ala makavonoka Ali–Maketoni ũima wa mwĩĩ. Kĩtumi kĩva? Onthe ala makavonoka makethĩwa na wĩa wa kũtethya. Na nũndũ makeethĩwa na ũima wa mwĩĩ, makethĩwa matonya kũtethya na kĩthito wĩa wa kũseũvya nthĩ ĩno Ngai watũnengie ta mũthĩnzĩo yĩkale ũndũ mũũnda wa Eteni wailyĩ.—Sav. 115:16.
17, 18. (a) Kĩeleelo kĩnene kya syama sya Yesũ kyaĩ kyaũ? (b) Nĩkĩ waĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito wĩlika nthĩ nzaũ ĩla Ngai ũtwathĩte?
17 Syama ila Yesũ weekie tene sya kũvosya andũ nĩsyĩkĩaa vinya yĩla "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ" ũmũnthĩ yĩlũlũmĩlye wĩkwatyo wayo wa kwĩsa kũvetewa mowau onthe. (Ũvu. 7:9) O na ĩngĩ syama isu nĩsyoonanisye ũndũ Mwana ũsu mũsyawa wa mbee wa Ngai wĩw'aa ngoonĩ, na syoonany'a ũndũ wendete andũ. (Yoa. 10:11; 15:12, 13) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana tei wa Yesũ nũtwonasya nesa ũndũ Yeova ũthĩnĩkĩaa kĩla ũmwe wa athũkũmi make.—Yoa. 5:19.
18 Ũmũnthĩ andũ onthe nĩmalumaa nũndũ wa woo na nĩmakusaa. (Alo. 8:22) Ithyonthe twĩ na vata wa kũlika nthĩ nzaũ vala vatakethĩwa thĩna o na ũmwe wa mwĩĩ o tondũ Ngai ũtwathĩte. Ĩandĩko ya Malaki 4:2 nĩyĩtũnengae kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũĩkĩĩa kana ala makavow'a 'makatũva ta tũsaũ twa kĩtũũnĩ' nũndũ wa ũtanu ũla makethĩwa naw'o maminĩte kumw'a ũkombonĩ wa naĩ. Ethĩwa nĩtũtũngĩaa Ngai mũvea na twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana akeanĩsya mawatho make, tũkeethĩawa tũtonya kwĩka maũndũ onthe ala ũtwĩaĩe nĩ kana twĩvota kũlika nthĩ nzaũ. Nĩtwĩkĩawa vinya mũno twamanya kana syama ila Yesũ weekie ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ syoonanisye ũndũ andũ makavetewa mathĩna moo onthe tene na tene ĩvindanĩ ya ũsumbĩki wa Masia!
