translation:
"My strength is made perfect in weakness."—2 COR. 12:9.
1, 2. What is one reason why Jesus continued to associate with people?
JEHOVAH showed his love for us by sending his beloved Son. That Son willingly came to earth and eventually became known as "a man of sorrows" and acquainted with suffering. In view of the immense value of what was sacrificed and the suffering involved, the Bible says that he "poured out his soul unto death" and was counted with the "transgressors." But God's beloved Son did not simply endure this; he said, "My strength is made perfect in weakness." (Isa. 53:10-12) This scripture shows that Jesus knew he would be weakened, yet he continued to preach, and he also kept on going from place to place.
2 Moreover, God's beloved Son demonstrated that he was willing to serve mankind and that he was willing to serve "the sons of men," by means of his ministry which covered 'all the nations' and brought comfort to people. It is therefore fitting that he spoke of giving "his life as a ransom for many." (Ps. 45:6-8, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language; Matt. 20:28) He willingly served people. But Jesus knew that God would empower him to accomplish what needed to be done. And Jesus accomplished so much during his earthly service, far more than anyone could have expected.
3. What will we now examine?
3 Indeed, but Jesus himself said that 'I must proclaim the good news of the Kingdom of God.' (Luke 4:43) Jesus understood that this Kingdom is what would solve the problems of the earth and benefit all people. So do not wonder why he went from place to place, proclaiming things and comforting people. Understanding this helps us appreciate how much he did for us. Is this not something worth thinking about? Because it shows how much he has done for us and how much we should value his sacrifice. Let us see what we can learn from Jesus' example.
'HIS LIFE AS A RANSOM FOR MANY'
4. Consider each instance where Jesus associated with someone and helped them.
4 Remember when Jesus cured Peter's mother-in-law of fever and she got up and began serving others? And just like Peter, she immediately told everyone about her cure. (Mark 1:39, 40) This woman had a severe fever. Luke, the doctor, writes that she was 'gripped by a high fever,' meaning she was very sick. (Luke 5:12) The Bible says: "And immediately he healed her, and she rose and began to serve him." This woman realized that Jesus had the power to heal her, so she showed her gratitude by getting up and serving him. Do you think she wondered, 'Why does Jesus have time to help me?' Did Jesus take time to help people because they asked him to? Perhaps she thought about whether her recovery was due to his compassion. Does Jesus still take time to help those who need him today? Can we be sure that Jesus will respond to our prayers?
5. Was it because Jesus felt sorry for the man afflicted with fever that he said, "I want to"?
5 In contrast to Moses' Law, this man with a fever did not need to offer a sacrifice and say, "Be cleansed, be cleansed," in order to get well. Instead, Jesus healed him right away. His healing of this man encouraged others who were sick. (Acts 13:43-46) So let us remember that whenever Jesus shows compassion, we can trust in his love. But sometimes things happen that we don't understand, and we may feel discouraged. Encourage yourself, and remember that God cares for us, and tell him, "I want to; please make me healthy." The Bible says: "And immediately the fever left him." (Luke 5:13) Let Jehovah's servants see your faith. Your faith is what moved Jesus to heal you and to show kindness to others.—Luke 5:17.
6. What can we learn from the fact that Jesus took the time to help people, and how can this encourage us?
6 God's spirit empowered Jesus to perform many miracles. He traveled throughout Galilee, doing good and curing people of all kinds of sickness and ailment. The Bible tells us: "He sent forth his word and healed them, and delivered them from their distresses." (Matt. 15:31) Often, large crowds gathered around him, and those suffering from various diseases would come to him, hoping he would cure them. Jesus was willing to use his power to heal many people! And he often helped individuals personally, showing concern for each one. (John 4:46-54) What great blessings we receive because of what Jesus did! Because Jesus is the Messiah, he has the authority and the desire to relieve people of their suffering. But if we want Jesus to help us, we must have faith in him and appreciate the value of his teachings. The Bible reminds us: "He will have pity on the afflicted and the poor." (Ps. 72:13) That is why Jesus felt such compassion for people and used his power to help everyone.—Matthew 14:14.
"ALWAYS REMEMBER YOUR OWN NEEDS"
7, 8. How did Jesus show consideration for individuals while continuing his ministry?
7 It is reported that Jesus once showed kindness to a woman who had a daughter possessed by a demon. This woman came from Canaanite territory and pleaded with Jesus for help. Jesus had already ministered to many Jews, and they were receiving wonderful benefits. The people needed reassurance that Jehovah would also care for others, and that his love extended to all nationalities.—Isa. 61:1, 2; Luke 4:18-21.
8 However, during Nisan, Jesus went up to Jerusalem toward Passover time. News about him spread, and large crowds began to flock to him. Many people wanted to see him and learn from him. They followed him along the road leading to Bethany. It was in this area that Jesus performed another miracle for an individual.
9, 10. (a) Why did people go to Bethany? (b) On what occasions did Jesus visit Bethany, and what does this teach us? (See accompanying picture.)
9 Bethany was a place frequented by many people because of its pleasant surroundings. What caused them to come there? Perhaps they felt refreshed when visiting this peaceful location, away from the hustle and bustle of city life. Also, they may have associated Bethany with Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, whom Jesus loved. Jesus visited them on several occasions, showing that he cared for individuals. Did he visit them only when invited, or did he seek them out? He sought them out because he loved people. He saw their needs and responded accordingly.—Read John 5:5-9.
10 To show how much God loves us, Jesus humbled himself and came to earth. He set an example of humility for us to follow. He willingly submitted to death, demonstrating his love for us, so that we might have the opportunity to gain eternal life. This is why Jesus healed that man—to illustrate what he would do for us. He showed compassion for him and relieved his suffering. Let us imitate Jesus' example, showing compassion for others and helping those in need. Just as Jesus did, let us be willing to go out of our way to help people, even if it requires effort on our part. We can learn much from Jesus' actions and teachings. And we will better understand what Jesus does for us. Let us reflect on his words and apply them in our lives. It is important to remember that Jesus cares about us deeply.
"HOW CAN I SHOW LOVE?"
11. How does the account in Mark 5:25-34 demonstrate that Jesus shows genuine concern for people?
11 Read Mark 5:25-34. A certain woman had been suffering from a bleeding condition for twelve years. She had sought treatment from many doctors, but her condition only worsened. This woman heard about Jesus and believed she could be healed if she touched him, even just his garment. One day, she managed to push through the crowd and touch his cloak. Immediately, the flow of blood stopped. But Jesus noticed that power had gone out from him. He asked, "Who touched me?" His disciples were surprised because a large crowd was pressing against him. But a woman came forward trembling and confessed, "I touched your garment." Jesus told her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace." Jesus knew that Jehovah, his Father, had empowered this woman, and he wanted to acknowledge her faith: "Daughter, your faith saved you; go, and be well."
12. (a) What motivated Jesus to heal the woman? (b) What lesson can we learn from Jesus' response?
12 Truly, Jesus showed great compassion! And his desire to help people moved him deeply. But Satan tries to make us believe that people are worthless and that no one cares for us. Despite this, Jesus always took the time to show kindness and willingness to help others. Let us imitate his example and demonstrate genuine love for our brothers and sisters! (Eph. 4:15) We should not dismiss anyone as unimportant, but rather remember that each person is valuable. Consider how Jesus responded when a rich man approached him and asked what he needed to do to gain everlasting life. He did not turn him away, but spoke to him kindly.—1 Pet. 3:8.
"JESUS HEALS"
13. Why did Jesus emphasize Lazarus' resurrection when speaking to Martha?
13 Jesus demonstrated deep feeling and sympathy. By doing so, he showed Martha that he understood her grief over the loss of Lazarus. Jesus "became perturbed" and was "deeply moved." His reaction revealed his strong affection for Lazarus. (Read John 11:33-36.) Jesus was not afraid to express his emotions. And he wants us to know that he feels for us when we grieve. This shows that Jesus has the power to comfort those who mourn and can restore them to life.—John 11:43, 44.
14, 15. (a) What reasons does Jehovah have for wanting to help mankind? (b) How does God use his power in connection with resurrections?
14 The Bible reveals that Jesus is "God's expression [of love]." (Heb. 1:3) As we have seen, this means that he is eager to use his authority to help people who are suffering and distressed. It is not surprising, then, that he would be willing to resurrect those whom God loves. This is why Jesus could make such a bold statement: "The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear my voice . . . and come out."—John 5:28, 29.
15 In connection with resurrections, God uses his power. The Almighty God, who created everything, is fully capable of remembering the personality of each deceased person. He can recreate them exactly as they were. (Isa. 40:26) Moreover, God knows what is best for each individual and whether a resurrection would truly benefit him. With confidence, we can trust that God will exercise his power wisely, along with his Son. The resurrection of Lazarus and others mentioned in the Bible demonstrates this clearly.
WHAT POWER DOES JESUS HAVE TO COMFORT PEOPLE?
16. Why did early Christians boldly proclaim the good news despite facing opposition?
16 Because they trusted in Jehovah, they were able to overcome great fear and continue preaching the good news, despite intense opposition. And as illustrated by the experience of Alice—Maconie, they saw many people respond favorably to the message, which brought them joy. (Isa. 33:24; 35:5, 6; Rev. 21:4) Imagine the relief felt by those who had been blind, lame, paralyzed, or afflicted with other serious ailments. Jehovah deserves credit for empowering Alice—Maconie to bring comfort to people in distress. Why? Because all those who recover are motivated to praise God. And those who regain their health are moved to express gratitude to Him.—Ps. 115:16.
17, 18. (a) What is a key aspect of Jesus' comforting work? (b) How can we show appreciation for what God has done for us?
17 Jesus showed his compassion for people by willingly giving his life "as a ransom for many." (Matt. 20:28) Also, his example demonstrates the extent to which the Son of God was willing to humble himself and go forth zealously in the ministry. (John 10:11; 15:12, 13) To this extent, Jesus imitated Jehovah's love for mankind.—John 5:19.
18 However, most people are self-seeking and stumble. (Acts 8:22) Still, we can be grateful for the opportunity to learn from our mistakes, knowing that God trains us. The prophecy in Malachi 4:2 foretold that those who would turn away from wickedness would experience 'wings like those of eagles,' meaning they would have the strength to overcome obstacles. Let us therefore continue to pray to God earnestly and maintain a strong desire to do his will, so that we may always find joy in serving him and feel confident that we are pleasing him. We will then appreciate why Jesus willingly gave his life and demonstrated such great love for people, even though it meant enduring much suffering in connection with the fulfillment of the Messianic prophecies!

text:
"Nũũ kwenyu, akyenda kwaka nyũmba yĩ mũnyoolo ũtambaa kwĩkala nthĩ na kũtala mbesa sya kũmyakĩthya, nĩ kana amanye ethĩwa e nasyo sya kũmĩmina?"—LUKA 14:28.
MBATHI: 6, 34
Masomo aa elĩ maatĩanĩe maandĩkĩwe amũika ala mavangĩte kũvatiswa
1, 2. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa andũ ma Ngai matana ũmũnthĩ? (b) Atumĩa vamwe na asyai Aklĩsto matonya kũtetheesya amũika ata maelewe ũito wa kũvatiswa?
MŨTHENYA ũmwe mũtumĩa ũmwe wa kĩkundi aineena na kamwana ka myaka 12 ketawa Christopher akeie atĩĩ: "Ũisyawa no ngwene, na ethĩwa nĩwatw'a kũvatiswa nĩneew'a mũyo mũno. Ĩndĩ kwaeka ngũkũlye, 'Nĩkĩ ũkwenda kwosa ĩtambya yĩu?'" Yĩu yaĩ ĩkũlyo ĩseo mũno. Ithyonthe nĩtũtanaa mũno kĩla mwaka ĩla twoona andũ aingĩ ma mũika nthĩ yonthe maivatiswa. (Mũta. 12:1) O na vailyĩ ũu, asyai Aklĩsto na atumĩa ma kĩkundi nĩmendaa matiwe mate na nzika kana amũika ta asu meeka ũtwi ũsu na ngenda na mawĩka me na kĩtumi kĩseo.
2 Ndeto ya Ngai yonanĩtye kana ĩla mũndũ weeyumya na ĩndĩ avatiswa ethĩawa ambĩĩsya kyalo kya Ũklĩsto. Kyalo kĩu kĩtumaa aathimwa nĩ Yeova na ĩvindanĩ o yĩu kĩtumaa ambĩĩa kũtatwa nĩ Satani. (Nth. 10:22; 1 Vet. 5:8) Kwoou asyai Aklĩsto nĩmosaa ĩvinda mamanyĩsye syana syoo nĩ maũndũ meva mũmanyĩw'a wa Klĩsto waĩle kwĩanĩsya. Namo atumĩa ma kĩkundi nĩmatetheeasya o nesa amũika ala mate na asyai Aklĩsto kwĩka masavu nĩ kana mamanye ethĩwa nĩmeyũmbanĩsye kũtw'ĩka amanyĩw'a ma Klĩsto. (Soma Luka 14:27-30.) Nĩ kana mũndũ ambĩĩsye mwako na aiũmina nesa, nĩwaĩle kwĩyũmbany'a. O ta ũu, mũndũ nĩwaĩle kwĩyũmbany'a nesa nĩ kana amũthũkũme Yeova e mũĩkĩĩku "kũvika mũminũkĩlyo." (Mt. 24:13) Ĩndĩ amũika maĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana malũmany'e vyũ na ũtwi woo wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova nginya kĩkw'ũ? Ekai twone.
3. (a) Ndeto ila syaneeniwe nĩ Yesũ na Vetelo itũtetheeasya ata twone ũito wa ũvatiso? (Mt. 28:19, 20; 1 Vet. 3:21) (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva, na nĩkĩ?
3 We wĩ mũndũ wa mũika ũvangĩte kũvatiswa? Ethĩwa wĩ ũmwe, wĩkĩte nesa mũno! Nĩ ũathimo mũnene kũvatiswa ũtw'ĩke ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Na eka ũu, nĩ lasima kĩla Mũklĩsto avatiswe, na yĩu nĩ ĩtambya ya vata ethĩwa mũndũ nũkwenda etangĩĩwa. (Mt. 28:19, 20; 1 Vet. 3:21) Na nũndũ ndwenda kũema kwĩanĩsya wĩvĩto ũla ũkevĩtĩa Yeova, no nginya wĩthĩwe ũyenda kwamba kwĩyũmbany'a. Kwoou nũseo ũsũanĩe makũlyo atatũ ala matonya kũũtethya ũmanye ethĩwa nĩwĩyũmbanĩsye kũvatiswa. Makũlyo asu nĩ: (1) Nyie nĩnĩanĩĩe kwĩka ũtwi ũsu? (2) Wendi ũsu umĩte ngoonĩ? (3) Nyie nĩnĩeleawa ũito wa kũmwĩyumĩsya Yeova? Ekai tũneenee makũlyo asu.
WE NĨWĨANĨĨE KŨVATISWA?
4, 5. (a) Nĩkĩ ti ala maneananga me oka maĩle kũvatiswa? (b) Mũklĩsto ũneananga ethĩawa ailyĩ ata?
4 Vai vandũ Mbivilia ĩwetete kana ala maĩle kũvatiswa no ala akũangũ kana ala mavikĩĩe ũkũũ ũtonya kũtuma metĩkĩlw'a nĩ silikalĩ kwĩka maũndũ amwe. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩvuku ya Nthimo 20:11 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "O na kana nĩkemanyĩthanasya kwondũ wa meko mako, ethĩwa wĩa wako nĩ mũtheu na ethĩwa nĩ mũlũngalu."Kwosana na ĩandĩko yĩu, o na mũndũ wa mũika mũnini nũtonya kũvathũkany'a ũla ũseo na nũtonya kwĩyumya amũthũkũme Mũmbi wake. Kwoou ethĩwa mũndũ wa mũika nĩwonanĩtye kana nĩ mũima, na ethĩwa nĩwosete ĩtambya akeyumya amũthũkũme Yeova, ĩtambya yĩla yĩngĩ ya vata waĩle kwosa nĩ kũvatiswa.—Nth. 20:7.
5 Mũndũ ũneana ethĩawa ailyĩ ata? Nĩ kana ũmanye mũndũ nĩwĩanĩte ndũsiasya mwĩĩ wake wĩ w'oka. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa andũ ala aima: "Ilĩko syoo nimanyĩĩtw'e kũvathũkan'ya ũseo na ũthũku." (Aevl. 5:14) Kwoou mũndũ ũneana nĩ ũla wĩsĩ kĩla Yeova wonaa kĩ kĩseo na ethĩawa atw'ĩte vyũ kũkĩatĩĩa kuma ngoonĩ. Kĩu kĩtumaa mũndũ ta ũsu ethĩwa atakengeka oou mĩtũkĩ eke ũla ũthũku, na ti nginya alilikanw'e kwĩka ũla ũseo. Nũndũ wa ũu, tũyĩthĩwa tũivĩtya tũkasya kana mũndũ wa mũika avatiswa no akwate mĩao ya Ngai o na ĩla ũte vakuvĩ na asyai make kana andũ angĩ aima.—Sianĩsya na Avilivi 2:12.
6, 7. (a) Nĩ mathĩna meva Ndanieli woonie ĩla watwaiwe Mbaviloni? (b) Ndanieli oonanisye ata kana nĩweanĩte?
6 Andũ ma mũika no methĩwe me aima kwa nzĩa ĩsu? Kwaeka tũsũanĩe ĩũlũ wa ũla Ndanieli ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Nũtonya kwĩthĩwa aĩ kĩvĩsĩ kya myaka ĩkũmi na kĩndũ ĩla wataananiw'e na asyai make na atwawa Mbaviloni. Kũu akwĩthĩie andũ maĩ na woni wĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ ĩũlũ wa ũla ũseo na ũla ũthũku. Ve ũndũ ũngĩ wamũthĩnasya. Ĩla wavikie kũu ambĩĩie kũnengwa ndaĩa ũtaĩ aanengwa. O na aĩ ũmwe wa ila imwana syanyuvĩtwe nesa iũngamae mbee wa mũsumbĩ! (Nda. 1:3-5, 13) No twasye kana ve moseo Ndanieli wakwatie Mbaviloni ũtaĩ amona kwoo Isilaeli.
7 Ĩndĩ we Ndanieli eekie ata? We nĩwakengiwe nĩ ũseo w'onthe ũla woonie Mbaviloni? We nĩweetĩkĩlilye Mbaviloni ĩmũvĩndũe kana yonzye mũĩkĩĩo wake? Aiee, ndaatata! Mbivilia yaasya kana ĩla Ndanieli waĩ Mbaviloni "nĩwetw'ĩĩe ngoonĩ yake kana ndakevukya" na kĩndũ o na kĩva kyumanĩte na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ. (Nda. 1:8) Nĩ w'o vyũ, Ndanieli nĩwoonanisye kana nĩweanĩte vyũ!
8. Ngewa ya Ndanieli yĩũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
8 Ngewa ya Ndanieli yĩũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Mbee, ethĩwa mũndũ wa mũika nĩwĩanĩte, ndethĩawa na nzika na mũĩkĩĩo wake. Ndavĩndũkangaa na kĩla kĩ vakuvĩ ta kĩmbu. Ndatw'ĩkaa mũnyanyae wa Ngai ĩla wĩ Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ na athi sukulu aitw'ĩka mũnyanyae wa andũ ma nthĩ. Vandũ va kũluutangwa kũũ na kũũ, ekalaa e mũlũmu o na ĩla mũĩkĩĩo wake watatwa.—Soma Aeveso 4:14, 15.
9, 10. (a) Mũndũ wa mũika atonya kũtetheka ata asũanĩa ũndũ weekie ĩla wĩla kũkwatwa nĩ matatwa? (b) Mũndũ onanasya kyaũ ĩla wavatiswa?
9 Nĩ w'o kana vai mũndũ ũte naĩ, na nĩkyo kĩtumi andũ ma mũika, o na vamwe na ala mate ma mũika, mekalaa maivĩtya. (Mũta. 7:20) Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, ĩla ũendeee kwĩka mĩvango ya kũvatiswa, nũseo ũkeyĩosya we mwene ũmanye ethĩwa nũtw'ĩte vyũ kũlũmany'a na mĩao ya Yeova kana ve vandũ ũtialĩtye. Ũtonya kũmanya ata ethĩwa nũtw'ĩte vyũ? Ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Ndonya kwasya ata nasisya ũndũ nĩthĩĩtwe ngĩkwata mĩao ya Ngai?' Kwasũanĩa ũndũ weekie ĩla wĩla kũkwatwa nĩ matatwa. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwonanĩtye kana wĩ na kĩlĩko kĩtoetye kũvathũkany'a ũseo na ũthũku? Nao nata ũkanengwa ndaĩa ya mwanya nĩ mũndũ wa nthĩ ĩno o tondũ Ndanieli wanengiwe? We no 'ũmanye kwenda kwa Mwĩaĩi ũndũ kũilyĩ' o na ĩla watatĩka wĩke ũndũ ũtosanĩte na kwenda kwake?—Aev. 5:17.
10 Nĩkĩ tũkwasya nĩwĩyĩosye na makũlyo ta asu? Nũndũ maseũvĩtw'e maũtetheesye wĩthĩwe na woni ũla waĩlĩte ĩũlũ wa ũvatiso. O tondũ twonie mbeenĩ, wavatiswa wĩthĩawa woonany'a kana nũminĩte kwĩvĩta mbee wa Yeova mwene. Wĩthĩawa ũmwathĩte kana ũkamwendaa na kũmũthũkũmaa tene na tene na ngoo yaku yonthe. (Mko. 12:30) Na kwoou mũndũ w'onthe ũla wamina kũvatiswa nĩwaĩlĩte kũĩkĩĩthya kana nĩweanĩsya wĩvĩto wake.—Soma Mũtavan'ya 5:4, 5.
WENDI ŨSU UMĨTE NGOONĨ?
11, 12. (a) Mũndũ ũvangĩte kũvatiswa aĩle kwamba kũĩkĩĩthya ata? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na woni ũla waĩle ĩũlũ wa mũvango wa Yeova wa ũvatiso?
11 Mbivilia yaĩtye kana andũ ma Yeova, o na vamwe na ala ma mũika, "nĩmeĩthembaa na ngoo ya kwenda" mathũkũme wĩa wake. (Sav. 110:3) Kwoou mũndũ ũla ũvangĩte kwosa ĩtambya ya kũvatiswa nĩwaĩle kwamba kũĩkĩĩthya kana wendi ũsu umĩte ngoonĩ. Nĩ kana ũĩkĩĩthye ũu nĩwaĩlĩte kwamba kwĩyĩosya we mwene. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ no kwĩthĩwa wĩ na ũathimo ũmwe amwe matawona. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa ũeetwe nĩ asyai Ngũsĩ.
12 O ũndũ myaka ĩvĩtĩte no kwĩthĩwa wonete andũ aingĩ maivatiswa. Amwe moo nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa ne ala mwĩ ma ĩika yĩmwe kana makethĩwa ne ala mũsyaanĩw'e. Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, waĩle kwĩsũvĩa mũno ndũkeke ata? Ĩsũvĩe ndũkone ũvatiso ta kĩthĩo amũika onthe maĩle kũatĩĩa mavikya myaka mĩna. Kwoou-ĩ, ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na woni ũla waĩle ĩũlũ wa mũvango ũsu wa Yeova wa ũvatiso? Ĩkalaa ũyosa ĩvinda ũsũanĩe nĩkĩ ũvatiso nĩ wa vata mũno. No ũkwate itumi imwe nzeo mũno ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ na yĩla yĩatĩĩe.
13. Ũtonya kũmanya ata kana ũtwi waku wa kũvatiswa umĩte ngoonĩ?
13 Ve nzĩa sya kũmanya ethĩwa ũtwi waku wa kũvatiswa umĩte ngoonĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa nũkwenda vyũ kũmũthũkũma Yeova kuma ngoonĩ, mboya syaku nitonya kwonany'a ũu nesa. Kwekũlye-ĩ, 'Nĩvoyaa mavinda meana ata? Nyie nĩnĩtavasya Yeova maũndũ makwa ndeũvithany'a?' Makũlyo asu nĩmatonya kũũtetheesya ũmanye ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova ĩseũvĩte ata. (Sav. 25:4) Nzĩa ĩmwe ya vata Yeova ũtũmĩaa kũsũngĩa mboya sitũ nĩ kũtũtetheesya tũtũnge kĩlĩko kitũ Ndetonĩ yake. Kwoou ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kwonany'a kana nĩtũkwenda kũmũthengeea Yeova na kũmũthũkũma kuma ngoonĩ nĩ kwĩkĩa kĩthito twĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia. (Yos. 1:8) Kwoou nũseo ũkekũlya ĩkũlyo yĩĩ yĩngĩ: 'Nyie nĩnĩmanyĩasya Mbivilia ndeũtĩĩa?' Na ethĩwa mũsyĩ kwenyu nĩmwĩthĩawa na Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ, ĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nyie nĩnĩũkwataa mbau na ngenda?' Mosũngĩo maku nĩmeũkũtetheesya ũmanye ethĩwa wendi waku wa kũvatiswa umĩte ngoonĩ.
ŨITO WA KWĨYUMYA
14. Elesya kĩvathũkany'o kĩla kĩ vo katĩ wa kwĩyumya na kũvatiswa.
14 Amwe nĩmolanĩalw'a nĩ kĩvathũkany'o kĩla kĩ vo katĩ wa kwĩyumya na kũvatiswa. Kwa ngelekany'o, amũika amwe maasya nĩmeeyumisye mamũthũkũme Yeova ĩndĩ mayĩyũmbanĩtye kũvatiswa. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩwosanĩte na kĩlĩko? Ĩla mũndũ weeyumya amũthũkũme Yeova amwathaa kana akamũthũkũmaa nginya tene na tene. Na ĩla mũndũ ũkũvatiswa ethĩawa ayonany'a ũtheinĩ kana nĩwĩyumĩtye amũthũkũme Yeova. Kwoou kũvatiswa nĩ kwonany'a ũtheinĩ kana nũmũvoyete Yeova kĩmbithĩnĩ ũkamwĩa nĩweeyumya ũmũthũkũme. Ũtanamba kũvatiswa amba kũmanya nesa ũito wa ĩtambya yĩu ya kwĩyumya.
15. Elesya ĩtambya ya kwĩyumya.
15 Kwa ũkuvĩ, ĩla weeyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova wĩthĩawa weeka kwĩlea vyũ. Ũmwathaa Yeova kana ũkeekaa kwenda kwake mbee wa maũndũ ala angĩ onthe thayũnĩ waku. (Soma Mathayo 16:24.) Ethĩwa ĩla twatha mũndũ kĩndũ tũyaĩle kwĩsa kũvatũnga ngũĩ, ti mbee mũno ĩla twamwatha Yeova Ngai ũndũ mũna? (Mt. 5:33) Ĩndĩ ũtonya kwonany'a ata nĩwĩleete na kana yu wĩ wa Yeova?—Alo. 14:8.
16, 17. (a) Kwĩlea nĩ kwĩka ata? Nengane ngelekany'o. (b) Ĩla mũndũ weeyumya ethĩawa no ta wasya ata?
16 Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno. Twasye mũnyanyau nĩwaũnenge mũthĩnzĩo wa ngalĩ. Na ĩndĩ aiũnenga valũa wa ngalĩ ĩsu na aikwĩa: "Mesya ngalĩ nĩ ĩsu." Ĩndĩ wĩona ata akasyoka akakwĩa atĩĩ: "Ninyie ngekalaa na i mbungũo. Na ninyie ngatwaaa ĩ ngalĩ, tuuwe." We wona mũthĩnzĩo ũsu ata? O na ũsu waũnenga ĩ ngalĩ ũmwosa ata?
17 Yu kwasyoka ũsũanĩe. Twasye mũndũ nĩweeyumya amũthũkũme Yeova, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ amwĩa, "Nĩnaũnenga thayũ wakwa. Nyie nĩ waku." Yeova enda mũndũ ta ũsu eanĩsye wĩvĩto wake. Ĩndĩ nata mũndũ ũsu akambĩĩa kwĩka maũndũ mathũku evithĩte, ta kwa ngelekany'o, akambĩĩa kwĩvaany'a na mũndũ ũte Ngũsĩ? Nata aketĩkĩla kũandĩkwa wĩa ũũtuma ateyumya na ngoo yonthe ũtavany'anĩ kana ũũtuma ambĩĩa kũtĩĩa maũmbano? We ndũkwona kana ũsu no ũndũ ũmwe na kũnenga mũndũ ngalĩ na ũiema na i mbungũo? Kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova no ũndũ ũmwe na kũmwĩa atĩĩ: "Ngekalaa kwondũ waku ĩndĩ ti kwondũ wakwa. Ĩla nesa kũkomana na ũndũ mũna na ngĩsaanĩw'a nĩĩka kwenda kwaku-ĩ kana nĩĩka kwenda kwakwa, ĩvinda yonthe nganyuvaa kwĩka ũndũ we ũkwenda." Mũndũ eeka ũu ethĩawa e na woni ta ũla wa Yesũ. Ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ aisye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ ndyaatheea kuma ĩtunĩ nĩke kwenda kwakwa, ĩndĩ no kwenda kwa ũla wandũmie."—Yoa. 6:38.
18, 19. (a) Maelesyo ma Rose na Christopher meonany'a ata kana kũvatiswa nĩ ĩtambya yĩtumaa mũndũ aathimwa mũno? (b) We wĩ na woni wĩva ĩũlũ wa ũvatiso?
18 Vate nzika, ĩtambya ya ũvatiso ti ĩtambya ya kũvũĩwa ngũĩ nĩ mũndũ o na wĩva. Ĩndĩ nĩ ũathimo mũnene vyũ kwĩthĩwa wĩyumĩtye ũmũthũkũme Yeova na kũvatiswa. Amũika ala mendete Yeova na ala mesĩ ũito wa kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme, maikĩaa kũvatiswa na mayĩsaa kwĩlila nũndũ wa ũtwi ũla meeka. Kelĩtu kamwe kavatise ketawa Rose kaisye: "Nĩnendete Yeova na vai kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩndanĩthasya ate o kũmũthũkũma. Katĩ wa motwi onthe ala naaĩka, ũtwi wa kũvatiswa nĩw'o neekie ndeũsyoka ĩtina."
19 Nao nata Christopher ũla ũwetetwe mwambĩĩonĩ wa ĩsomo yĩĩ? O na kau avatisiwe e na myaka 12, nĩwasyokie kwĩlila? Christopher alilikana ĩla weeyumisye na esa kũvatiswa ew'aa mũyo mũno. Atw'ĩkie vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda e na myaka 17 na atw'ĩka mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi e na myaka 18. Ũmũnthĩ athũkũmaa Mbetheli. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũtwi ũla neekie wa kũvatiswa nĩw'o waaĩlĩte. Wĩa ũla nĩthũkũmaa kwondũ wa Yeova na ũseũvyo wake ũtumaa nĩw'a nĩ mwĩanĩe vyũ." Ethĩwa nũvangĩte kũvatiswa, ũtonya kwĩyũmbany'a ata? Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩũneenea ĩkũlyo yĩu.

translation:
"So none of you can build a house when he begins it and does not first sit down and count the cost whether he has enough to finish it?—LUKE 14:28.
FOOTNOTES: 6, 34
Lessons from ancient writings to help us imitate them
1, 2. (a) What causes some of God's people to stumble? (b) How can we, like loyal Christians, show that we understand the importance of counting the cost?
A BROTHER who is an elder in a congregation shared this experience with his 12-year-old son named Christopher: "Imagine you want something very much, but you know that getting it will require a lot of effort. Wouldn't you ask yourself, 'Can I really afford to get this?' " His son understood right away. Every year they see many people start projects that they do not finish. (Prov. 12:1) And often, loyal Christians and elders in congregations face similar situations when helping others, wondering if those ones are willing to put forth the necessary effort and make the required sacrifices.
2 God's Word warns us that if someone dedicates himself but does not fully count the cost, he may bring reproach on Christ's name. That name is sanctified because of Jehovah, and defending it means resisting Satan. (Prov. 10:22; 1 Pet. 5:8) So loyal Christians carefully examine matters so that their efforts will honor Christ and not bring shame to his name. Elders in congregations also try to help others appreciate the seriousness of becoming disciples of Christ. They encourage them to think about what is involved and to be sure they are willing to make the necessary sacrifices. (Read Luke 14:27-30.) If someone makes a dedication without understanding what it involves, he may later fall away. But even if he does not fall away, he may find it difficult to remain dedicated if he does not keep Jehovah foremost in his thinking—if he does not "keep his eye on the prize." (Matt. 24:13) Are there things you could do to strengthen your determination to keep Jehovah foremost? Let us see.
3. (a) How do Jesus' command and Peter's counsel help us understand the importance of baptism? (Matt. 28:19, 20; 1 Pet. 3:21) (b) What will we discuss, and why?
3 Would you like to get baptized? If so, rejoice! Getting baptized is an important step toward showing loyalty to Jehovah God. And rightly so, it is essential that all Christians get baptized, as baptism demonstrates a person's willingness to live in obedience to God. (Matt. 28:19, 20; 1 Pet. 3:21) But before you take this vital step, you want to be certain that you are doing so out of love for Jehovah, and that you are determined to remain faithful. Therefore, thoughtfully consider the following questions to help you determine whether you are ready for baptism. These questions are: (1) Do I truly believe what I am learning? (2) Am I living in harmony with my beliefs? (3) Do I understand what it means to dedicate myself to Jehovah? Let us consider those questions.
ARE YOU READY FOR BAPTISM?
4, 5. (a) What can help us decide if we are ready for baptism? (b) Can a Christian ever feel completely prepared?
4 Many Bible accounts show that people got baptized because they wanted to demonstrate their dedication to God, and others were moved to do so by what they learned. This explains why 2 Timothy 20:11 says: "And if anyone does not work, let him not eat." In line with this principle, a conscientious person will not rush into baptism unless he is convinced that he can live up to his dedication. So a person should examine himself carefully to see if he is sincere, and he should make sure that he is motivated by genuine desire to please his Creator. Otherwise, a person may baptize himself prematurely, and then he may find it difficult to continue pleasing Jehovah, which would be a sad outcome.—Prov. 20:7.
5 Does a young one need help in this regard? Yes, for a child may not fully appreciate what dedication means. The Bible states about all mankind: "The understanding of a boy is not reliable." (Prov. 5:14) A young one needs help from parents who love Jehovah and who teach him what dedication involves and why it is important. This will help the young one to avoid making a vow thoughtlessly, and it will prevent him from regretting it later. For this reason, we should encourage a young person to wait until he has a personal relationship with God and understands what is involved before he gets baptized.—Compare Proverbs 2:12.
6, 7. (a) What reasons did Daniel give for being faithful while in Babylon? (b) Did Daniel ever feel doubtful?
6 How do people today show faith in similar ways? Let us examine the case of Daniel when he was taken captive to Babylon. He had been in Babylon for some years when his captors asked him and his companions to eat food prepared according to their custom and drink wine. But he decided to stick to what was right in the eyes of Jehovah and refused to defile himself. It took courage on his part. Imagine telling a king that you would not eat certain foods! (Dan. 1:3-5, 13) Yet, Daniel knew that faithfulness to Jehovah meant more than just physical comfort.
7 What qualities did Daniel display? Was he influenced by the environment around him in Babylon? Did Babylon cause him to forget his identity? Not at all! The Bible says that Daniel "purposed in his heart that he would not pollute himself with the royal delicacies or with the wine they drank." (Dan. 1:8) So, Daniel proved that he could be faithful despite his circumstances!
8. What does Daniel's example teach us?
8 What does Daniel's example teach us? Often, young people feel pressured to conform, to go along with the crowd. They may fear being different. But remember that true friends will respect your principles. Like the students at the Watch Tower Bible School of Gilead, you can stand up for what is right.—Read Ephesians 4:14, 15.
9, 10. (a) Can a young person remain firm when faced with pressure to do wrong? (b) What helps someone to succeed?
9 It takes courage to be different, and that is why young people—and even some older ones—often give in to peer pressure. (Prov. 7:20) However, if you continue to meditate on the scriptures and strengthen your faith, you will find it easier to resist negative influences and to associate with those who love Jehovah. How can you build such strength? Ask yourself, "Am I willing to sacrifice my own desires in order to please God?" Resist doing what is wrong. For instance, ask yourself, "Do I have something valuable to offer others, or am I easily influenced?" And do not let the fear of disapproval prevent you from taking a stand, just as Daniel did. Rather, strive "to walk worthily of the calling" you have received.—Eph. 5:17.
10 But how can we remain courageous? By regularly reviewing our dedications and remembering the joy we experienced when we first got baptized. And because we love Jehovah, we want to show that we are determined to live according to his standards. We want to please him always, walking in his ways and obeying him fully. (Ps. 12:30) Also, remember that everyone who wants to remain dedicated needs help at times.—Read Proverbs 5:4, 5.
WHY COURAGE IS NEEDED
11, 12. (a) What pressures might cause someone to compromise? (b) How can we strengthen ourselves spiritually so that we can adhere to Jehovah's standard of conduct?
11 The Bible says that some of Jehovah's people, and even others, "voluntarily offered themselves on the day of battle." (Ps. 110:3) Similarly, you may feel pressured to compromise or give up entirely. Perhaps you fear what others will think of you. Why is this? Because we are influenced by the world around us. For example, you might be tempted to imitate bad examples.
12 Or perhaps years have passed since you got baptized. You may find yourself associating mostly with those who do not value spiritual things or with those who are worldly. Is this dangerous? Yes, it can weaken your resolve. So examine yourself: Does your dedication still mean something to you? Ask yourself whether you truly appreciate Jehovah's high standard of conduct. Consider also whether you would be willing to make sacrifices for your faith. Remember, maintaining zeal requires effort and constant vigilance.
13. How can you tell if your courage is waning?
13 Here are some signs that your courage is waning. For instance, if you hesitate to speak about Jehovah when an opportunity arises, you may be losing your zeal. Also, ask yourself, 'Am I really interested in spiritual activities?' If you find yourself questioning your relationship with Jehovah, meditate on Psalm 25:4: "Show me your ways, O Jehovah; teach me your paths." One way to strengthen our love for Jehovah is to pray earnestly for his guidance. Furthermore, regularly reading and meditating on God's Word can help us maintain our zeal. (Josh. 1:8) Therefore, ask yourself these questions: 'How well do I know the Bible?' And if you feel inadequate, ask yourself, 'What can I do to improve?' By honestly examining ourselves, we can determine if our courage is waning.
A CALL TO VIGILANCE
14. Let us always remember the connection between vigilance and remaining dedicated.
14 Some may wonder why it is so important to remain vigilant and dedicated. For example, a brother might have stopped speaking about Jehovah because he has become discouraged due to opposition. Does this indicate a problem? Yes, because a dedicated person will continue to speak about Jehovah, even if he faces difficulties. And a dedicated person who feels discouraged will seek strength from Jehovah. Remaining dedicated means continuing to seek strength from Jehovah and speaking about him, even when you feel discouraged. It also means being determined to make progress in your personal study of the Bible.
15. Let us examine what dedication involves.
15 In effect, if you are dedicated to Jehovah, you are willing to sacrifice much. You will put Jehovah first, even ahead of your own interests and those of others. (Read Matthew 16:24.) So, should we not be willing to sacrifice whatever it takes to please Jehovah God?—Matt. 5:33. Ask yourself, 'Does my conduct show that I value Jehovah's approval?'—Prov. 14:8.
16, 17. (a) What does it mean to dedicate oneself? Explain. (b) Why is it vital for a dedicated person to remain active?
16 Consider this illustration. Imagine a man who owns a beautiful garden. He diligently tends to his garden and protects it from weeds. Then someone comes along and says: "This garden belongs to me." The owner might reply: "You can take the garden, but you will never take my heart." Do you see the point? Similarly, we can lose our possessions, but we should never lose our dedication to Jehovah.
17 You may face trials. Imagine a man who loves Jehovah deeply, or perhaps he has told Him, "I dedicate myself to you. You are mine." Jehovah accepts that man's dedication and gives him evidence of its acceptance. But what if that man later starts thinking about bad things, or because of some trial, he begins to feel distant from Jehovah? Will you help him to remember his dedication and encourage him to strengthen his relationship with Jehovah? To be loving and compassionate like Jehovah means being willing to say: "Your heart belongs to me, but I want to help you to overcome whatever difficulties you are facing so that you can continue serving me, whether you go forward or backward, always remembering the love you have for me." A person who feels this way shows that he truly follows the example of Jesus. But why did Jesus say: "I came down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of the One who sent me"?—John 6:38.
18, 19. (a) How did the experiences of Rose and Christopher show that trials can test our determination? (b) What can help you to remain determined during trials?
18 Remember, a trial is not a punishment from God. Rather, it is an opportunity to demonstrate the depth of your love for Jehovah and your determination to serve him. By helping others to stay close to Jehovah and encouraging them to remain dedicated, you can help them to pass through their trials and maintain their faith. For example, Rose once said: "I love Jehovah, and nothing else matters more than pleasing him. Of all the qualities a person can develop, determination is the most important."
19 And what about Christopher, whom we mentioned earlier? Although he was baptized when he was 12 years old, did he find it easy to remain determined? Christopher admits that he struggled at times, but he wanted to remain faithful. He served as a ministerial servant while still in his teens and then pioneered at age 18. Eventually, he joined Bethel. He says: "The best way to remain determined is to focus on serving Jehovah and to appreciate the privilege of being in his service." So, how can you strengthen your determination? The lesson we will now discuss will be very helpful.

text:
NDEVOLA ekisye metho oona asikalĩ aingĩ mamũthyũlũlũkĩte ngalĩ syonthe ĩũlũ wa Kĩĩma kya Tavoli. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwamwendeeisye mũno nũndũ nĩwoonie ũndũ maĩ na ũkũmbaũ na mũĩkĩĩo. Kwakya kũu, nĩwasũanĩie ĩũlũ wa ũkũmbaũ woo, na mũĩkĩĩo wa Mbalaka mũtongoi woo. O na kau maĩ aũme 10,000, ũkũmbaũ na mũĩkĩĩo woo nĩwesaa kũtatwa mũno mũthenya ũsu. Maendete kũkita na amaitha maĩ na vinya kũmakĩla, nũndũ maĩ na mĩio myai ya kaũ kwĩ ĩla yoo. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, mookĩte kaũnĩ nũndũ nĩmeekĩiwe vinya mũno nĩ Ndevola.
Kwasũanĩa Ndevola na Mbalaka maũngye vandũ ve kaseve vau kĩĩmanĩ ĩũlũ masyaĩĩsye kũũya nthĩ. Kĩĩma kya Tavoli kyailyĩ mbĩla, ĩndĩ vaaya mũthya vaĩ veananu. Wĩ ĩũlũ waĩ ũtonya kwona nthĩ ndindimalu ya Esdraelon (Plain of Esdraelon), ĩla yĩ vuti 1,300 (mita 400) kuma kĩĩmanĩ ĩũlũ, na yĩ ngalĩ ya ĩtheo ya ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa. Ũsĩ wa Kisoni watheelele ũiĩnĩ, ũvaasene na Kĩĩma kya Kameli ũkathi kũlika Ũkanganĩ Mũnene. Nĩvatonyeka kwakya kũu ũsĩ ũsu ũkethĩwa waĩ mũng'alu, ĩndĩ wasisya kũũya ũiĩnĩ, ve kĩndũ kyoonekaa kĩikena. Ita sya Sisela syaendeee kũthengeea, na ũtisu wa mĩio yoo ya kaũ ya kũtĩsya nĩwoonekaa. Ĩsu yaĩ mĩio ĩla mĩseo vyũ ya ita sya Sisela ĩla yaĩ makasya ma kaũ 900, ala matonya kwĩthĩwa mathinĩkĩtwe mbyũ ndeenĩ sya ndĩa. Sisela avangĩte kũwaa Aisilaeli aingĩ na mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka!
Ndevola nĩweesĩ kana Mbalaka na ita syake nĩmeeteele amatavye ũndũ maĩle kwĩka. No we waĩ mũndũ mũka vau e weka? Eew'aa ata nũndũ wa kĩanda kĩu kĩito waĩ nakyo? Yo nĩweekũlasya eĩka ata vau? Vate nzika ndaaĩka ũu. Yeova, Ngai wake, nĩwamwĩĩte ambĩĩe kaũ ũsu na nĩwamũvuanĩisye kana mũndũ mũka nĩwe ũkaũmina. (Asili 4:9) Ngelekany'o ya Ndevola na aũme asu ma kaũ maĩ na ũkũmbaũ yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo?
"ENDA ŨTHENGEEE KĨĨMANĨ KYA TAVOLI"
Mbivilia ĩmũwetete Ndevola ya mbee ta "mwathani mũndũ mũka." Ti ũndũ weekĩkaa mũno aka kwĩthĩwa me athani ta Ndevola, ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, tiwe ũwetetwe e weka Mbivilianĩ ta mwathani mũndũ mũka. * Ve wĩa ũngĩ Ndevola waĩ naw'o. Nĩweew'anĩthasya andũ kwa kũmanenga motao ma Yeova ĩũlũ wa ũndũ matonya kũmina mathĩna maumĩla.—Asili 4:4, 5.
Ndevola ekalaa nthĩ yĩ iĩma ya Evalaimu, katĩ katĩ wa Mbethieli na Lama. E kũu ekalaa ungu wa mũtende, aisilany'a andũ ma Yeova kwosana na ũndũ Yeova wamwĩaĩaa. Wĩa ũsu wake ndwaĩ laisi, ĩndĩ ndaaĩtĩkĩla ũndũ ũsu ũmũtũle ngoo. Vaĩ vata mũnene mũno wa mũndũ wa kũtethya wĩa ũsu. O na nĩwaveveewe kũtunga wathi ũla waĩ na maũndũ mawetete ũndũ Aisilaeli mataĩ aĩkĩĩku. Aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩmanyuvie ngai ingĩ; na ĩndĩ kwaĩ kaũ i mbingĩlonĩ." (Asili 5:8) Nũndũ Aisilaeli nĩmamũtiie Yeova na mathaitha ngai ingĩ, nĩwamaekie mathĩnw'e nĩ amaitha moo. Mũsumbĩ wa Kanaani weetawa Yavini nĩwamasumbĩkĩte Aisilaeli na akamavinyĩĩa mũno atũmĩĩte mũnene wa ita weetawa Sisela.
Aisilaeli meew'a Sisela awetwa matelemaa na makakwatwa nĩ wia mũno. Ndĩni na syĩthĩo sya Akanaani syaĩ nthũku mũno nũndũ nĩmathembaa syana, na kweethĩawa na malwaya ĩkalũnĩ. Kweethĩawa kũilyĩ ata Aisilaeli masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ mũnene wa ita sya Kanaani na asikalĩ make? Wathi ũla Ndevola watungie wonanasya kana ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi andũ kũtembea na kwĩkala nthĩ ĩsu. (Asili 5:6, 7) No tũsũanĩe Aisilaeli mayĩvitha mĩtĩnĩ mĩnene na iĩmanĩ, maikĩa kũĩma na kwĩkala kũndũ kũte kwiĩĩe na ngũta, maikĩa kũtembea lelũnĩ nĩ kana maikavithũkĩwe, na syana syoo iikoswe, na iveti syoo iikwatwa na vinya. *
Aisilaeli meethĩiwe me thĩnanĩ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 20 nginya ĩla Yeova woonie kana nĩmatw'ĩte kũalyũla mwĩkalĩle woo mũthũku, na o tondũ ndeto ii mbeveee sya Ndevola na Mbalaka syaĩtye, "Mũvaka yĩla nyie Ndevola nookĩlile, nookĩla nĩ inyia nthĩnĩ wa Isilaeli." Tũyĩsĩ kana Ndevola, kĩveti kya Lavitothi kyaĩ na syana, ĩndĩ ĩla Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ookĩlile ta inyia, ndeto ĩsu ĩtũmĩkĩte kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova wanengie Ndevola wĩa wa kũsũvĩa Aisilaeli o ũndũ kĩveti kĩsũvĩaa syana syakyo. Nĩwamũnengie Ndevola wĩa wa kũneena na Mũsili Mbalaka, ũla waĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, na aimũtavya kana aĩle kũthi kũkita na Sisela.—Asili 4:3, 6, 7; 5:7.
Yeova atũmĩie mwathani Ndevola aneene na Mbalaka na aimwĩa, "Enda ũthengeee kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli." Mbalaka aaĩle kũmbany'a aũme 10,000 kuma mbaĩnĩ ilĩ sya Isilaeli. Ndevola nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa watho wa Ngai kana Aisilaeli makasinda Sisela e na makasya make 900 ma kaũ! Vate nzika watho ũsu nĩwamũseng'isye Mbalaka mũno. Aisilaeli mayaĩ na aũme amanyĩsye ma kaũ na mĩio ya kaũ mĩseo. O na vailyĩ ũu, Mbalaka nĩweetĩkĩlile kũthi kaũnĩ. Aisye ethi kaũnĩ ethĩwa mwathani Ndevola nũkũendany'a vamwe nake Kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli.—Asili 4:6-8; 5:6-8.
Andũ amwe monaa Mbalaka ta ũtaĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nũndũ endaa Ndevola athi nake kaũnĩ, ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o. Twĩasya ũu nũndũ ndaavoya Ngai amwongele mĩio ya kaũ. Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, nũndũ aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, oonie wĩ ũndũ wa vata ethĩwe na mũthũkũmi wa Yeova nĩ kana amwĩkĩe vinya vamwe na aũme make ma kaũ. (Aevelania 11:32, 33) Yeova nĩwamũnengie Mbalaka kĩla wavoyie. Nĩweetĩkĩlile Ndevola aendany'e nake o ũndũ wamũkũlĩtye. O na vailyĩ ũu, aveveeiwe nĩ Yeova na athana kana mũndũ mũka nĩwe ũkakumw'a mamina kũsinda kaũ ũsu. (Asili 4:9) Ngai aĩ atwie kana Sisela akooawa nĩ mũndũ mũka!
Ũmũnthĩ aka nĩmoneawa, makanyamaw'a, na makavũthw'a mũno. Mavinda maingĩ mainengawe ndaĩa o tondũ Ngai wendaa manengwe. Methonĩ ma Ngai aka na aũme nĩ ũndũ ũmwe. (Alomi 2:11; Akalatia 3:28) Ngelekany'o ya Ndevola yĩtũlilikany'a kana Ngai nũnengae aka ianda syĩ mwanya, na akamony'a kana nũmaĩkĩĩte na nĩwendeeaw'a nĩmo. Kwoou tũyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ta andũ ma nthĩ ala mosaa aka ta andũ mate vata.
"NTHĨ NĨYATETEMIE, MATU NAMO MAVALŨKA"
Mbalaka nĩwoombanisye ita syake. Oombanisye aũme 10,000 ala maĩ ngũmbaũ na maĩ matonya kũkita na ita nthũku sya Sisela. Mbalaka amatongoesye kwambata Kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli, aĩ na ũtanu kwĩthĩwa na mũndũ ũkũmekĩa vinya. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Na Ndevola ambata vamwe nake." (Asili 4:10) Kwavindĩĩsya ũndũ asikalĩ asu makwatie vinya nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa vamwe na mũndũ mũka ũsu ngũmbaũ mambatĩte Kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli, eeyũmbanĩtye kwĩlikya mũisyonĩ nũndũ nĩwamũĩkĩĩaa Yeova Ngai!
Ĩla Sisela wamanyie kana Aisilaeli nĩmeeyũmbanĩtye kũkita nake nĩwoosie ĩtambya ya mĩtũkĩ, na asumbĩ kauta ma Kanaani makwatana na ita sya Mũsumbĩ Yavini ũla ũtonya kwĩthĩwa nowe waĩ vinya vyũ katĩ woo. Na ĩndĩ makasya maingĩ ma kaũ ma Sisela matetemya nthĩ nginya kĩla ũmwe ũla waĩ ũiĩnĩ ũsu amanya kana nĩmokĩte. Akanaani masũanĩaa kana meĩka kũtuta Aisilaeli na mĩtũkĩ mũno nũndũ ita sya Aisilaeli iyaĩ na vinya.—Asili 4:12, 13; 5:19.
Mbalaka na Ndevola mesaa kwĩka ata nũndũ amaitha moo nĩmathengeee? Yesaa kwĩthĩwa yĩ kavaa kwoo maũngama ivaũũkonĩ sya Kĩĩma kya Tavoli nũndũ makasya ma kaũ ma ita sya Kanaani mendaa vandũ vatindimalu nĩ kenda methĩwe matonya kũkita nesa. Ĩndĩ Mbalaka esaa kũkita kwĩanana na ũndũ Yeova wesaa kwasya, na kwoou eeteela ew'e Ndevola easya ata. Na ĩndĩ ĩvinda yavika na Ndevola asya: "Ũkĩla; nũndũ ũũ nĩ mũthenya ũla Yeova ũnenganĩte Sisela kw'okonĩ kwaku; Yeova ndaumaalĩte akũtongoesye?" Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩendeee kwasya: "Mbalaka atheea kuma Kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli, e na andũ ngili ĩkũmi mamũatĩĩe."—Asili 4:14. *
Ita sya Isilaeli syasembie itheeete, syelekele ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe vala vaĩ ita isu syaũtĩsya sya Kanaani. Yo Yeova nĩwaumaalile na atongoesya ita sya Aisilaeli o ũndũ Ndevola waĩtye? Ĩĩ, nĩweekie ũu na mĩtũkĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nthĩ nĩyatetemie, matu namo mavalũka." Ita sya Sisela na makasya make ma kaũ nĩsyathokoaniw'e. Na mbua nene mũno yaua nginya nthĩ ĩsu yausũa kĩw'ũ! Ĩla ũu weethĩiwe makasya manene ma ita sya Kanaani nĩmamatw'ĩkĩie mũio vandũ va kũmatethya. Makwamie ndakanĩ weethĩa vai vandũ mathi.—Asili 4:14,15; 5:4.
Mbalaka na aũme make mayaatelemw'a nĩ mbua ĩsu nũndũ nĩmeesĩ vala yaumĩte. Masembie melekele vala vaĩ ita isu sya Kanaani. Na nũndũ Aisilaeli mokitaa kwondũ wa Yeova, mayaatia mũsikalĩ o na ũmwe wa ita sya Sisela e thayũ. Ũsĩ wa Kisoni wausũie kĩw'ũ vyũ na kyakua simba sya asikalĩ ma Sisela kyathi kũmainda nthĩnĩ wa Ũkanga Mũnene.—Asili 4:16; 5:21.
Ũmũnthĩ Yeova ndatũmaa athũkũmi make makokite na andũ, ĩndĩ nũmatavĩtye kana nĩmaĩle kũkita kaũ wa kĩ-veva. (Mathayo 26:52; 2 Akolintho 10:4) Tũkitaa kaũ ũsu ĩla tweekĩa kĩthito kũmwĩw'a Yeova. No nginya twĩthĩwe na ũkũmbaũ nũndũ ala me ngalĩ ya Yeova nĩmavĩngawa mũno. Yeova ndaalyũka nũndũ o na ũmũnthĩ nũmatetheeasya athũkũmi make ala mamũĩkĩĩa na mamwĩkwatasya o ta Ndevola, Mbalaka, na asikalĩ ma Isilaeli.
"AKAATHIMWA KŨVĨTŨKA AKA"
Sisela, ũla waĩ mũmaitha mũnene wathĩnasya andũ ma Ngai mũno nĩwatolokile! Atiie aũme make makw'ĩĩe vau mũtondonĩ na asemba avĩtũka asikalĩ ma Isilaeli matamwene nginya athi kũla waĩ atonya ũkwata vandũ va kwĩvitha. Asembeile ũiĩnĩ e na wia mwingĩ mũno ayona asikalĩ ma Isilaeli ta matonya kũmwona. Eelekeile ĩeemanĩ ya Eeveli, ũla waĩ Mũkeni, na ĩtina esa kwĩvathana na andũ make ala maĩ aĩthi, na eew'ana na Mũsumbĩ Yavini atũe kĩsionĩ kyake.—Asili 4:11, 17.
Sisela nĩwavikie ĩeemanĩ ya Eeveli anoete vyũ. Avika eethĩie Eeveli ate mũsyĩ, ĩndĩ mũka Yaeli nĩwe waĩ vo. Sisela asũanĩaa kana Yaeli nde ũndũ emwĩka nũndũ mũũme aĩ ndũũ na Mũsumbĩ Yavini. No kwĩthĩwa asũanĩaa kana kĩveti kĩyĩsa kwĩka, kana kũsũanĩa ũndũ wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na mũũme. Sisela ndamwĩsĩ Yaeli nesa! Vate nzika, Yaeli nĩweeyoneete ũndũ Akanaani mavinyĩĩe Aisilaeli, na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa amanyie kana aĩ na ũtwi waaĩle kwĩka. Aĩ na maũndũ elĩ waĩ atonya kũnyuva kwĩka, kũtetheesya mũndũ ũsu mũthũku, kana anyuve kwosa ĩtambya ngalĩ ya Yeova, na aimina mũmaitha wa andũ Make. Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Esaa kwĩka ata? Kwa w'o mũndũ mũka aĩ atonya kũsinda mũndũũme ũsu waĩ na vinya na wamanyĩĩtw'e kũkita?
Yaeli aaĩle kwĩka masavu na mĩtũkĩ. Nĩwamwonisye Sisela vandũ athũmũe. Sisela amwĩie ndakatavye mũndũ o na ũmwe kana e vau. Ĩla wakomie, Yaeli amũvw'ĩkie nesa, na ĩla wamwĩtisye kĩw'ũ amũnenga ĩia ĩkamu. Ĩtina wa kavinda kanini, Sisela akomie ta mũkw'ũ. Yaeli oosie kĩiva na kyambo kya ĩeema, ila syatũmĩawa nĩ aka ala maĩ na ũtũĩka wa kwamba maeema. Ĩla Yaeli wathengeeie mũtwe wa Sisela, aĩ na wĩa mũmũ wa kũwaa mũmaitha wa Yeova. Takeka Yaeli nĩwateeteie o vanini ũu, ethĩwa oonie naĩ. Yo no ethĩwe asũanĩie ĩũlũ wa andũ ma Yeova na ũndũ mũndũũme ũsu watwĩe amathĩnĩtye kwa myaka mingĩ? Kana nũtonya kwĩthĩwa asũanĩie ĩũlũ wa ũseo wa kũkwata mbau mũvango wa Yeova? Mbivilia ndĩeleetye ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu. Kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwooaie Sisela!—Asili 4:18-21; 5:24-27.
Ĩtina Mbalaka nĩwaendie kwa Yaeli aimantha nthũ yake. Ĩla Yaeli wamwonisye kimba kya Sisela kĩathĩĩwe kyambo mũtwe nĩvo wamanyie kana wathani wa Ndevola nĩweanĩa. Mũndũ mũka aĩ ooaa ngũmbaũ ĩsu ya kaũ yeetawa Sisela! Ala mavũthĩĩasya Ndeto ya Ngai ũmũnthĩ mamwĩtaa Yaeli masyĩtwa mathũku na ma kĩvũthya, ĩndĩ Mbalaka na Ndevola nĩmo mamwĩsĩ nesa. Nĩmaveveeiwe nĩ Ngai mamũkumye Yaeli wathinĩ woo. Maisye atĩĩ: 'Nĩ mũathime kũvĩtũka aka,' nũndũ wa ĩtambya yĩu woosie yĩkwonany'a aĩ na ũkũmbaũ. (Asili 4:22; 5:24) Ndevola ndaĩ na kĩwĩu. Ndaaĩw'a wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũmũkumya Yaeli, ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla waĩ wa vata kwake nĩ kana ndeto sya Yeova nĩsyeanĩie.
Mũsumbĩ Yavini nĩwaminiwe vinya vyũ ĩla Sisela wooaiwe. Akanaani mayaĩ matonya kũnyamasya Aisilaeli ĩngĩ. Na kwondũ wa ũu, kweethĩwa na mũuo kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 40. (Asili 4:24; 5:31) Ũsu waĩ ũathimo mũnene kwa Ndevola, Mbalaka, na Yaeli ĩtina wa kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova Ngai! Tweethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu ta wa Ndevola, na tũimũthũkũma Yeova twĩ na ũkũmbaũ vamwe na kwĩkĩa angĩ vinya meke ũu, Yeova akatũtetheesya tũsinde mathĩna na tũyĩthĩwa na mũuo wa tene na tene.
^ kal. 7 Miliamu, Ilikia, na mũka wa Isaia maĩ aka athani.—Kuma 15:20; 2 Asumbĩ 22:14; Isaia 8:3.
^ kal. 9 Wathi wa Ndevola wonanasya kana mavinda maingĩ Sisela aendaa kaũnĩ na aisyoka na mũtavo. Katĩ wa kĩla kyeethĩawa mũtavonĩ ũsu nĩ eĩtu, na mavinda maingĩ mũsikalĩ ũmwe eethĩawa na mwĩĩtu ũmwe kana elĩ. (Asili 5:30) Ndeto "mwĩĩtu" ĩla ĩtũmĩĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩĩ yĩonany'a "ĩvu yĩla yĩkuaa mwana." Ũu wĩtũlilikany'a kana eĩtu asu mendekaa kwondũ wa kũkomwa namo. Ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ũkethĩa kũkwata aka na vinya waĩ ũndũ weekĩkaa kĩla ĩvinda.
^ kal. 17 Kaũ ũsu ũeleetw'e mavinda elĩ Mbivilianĩ. Mbee ũeleetw'e ĩvukunĩ ya Asili kĩlungu kya 4, na ũkaelew'a ĩngĩ wathinĩ wa Ndevola na Mbalaka ũla ũandĩkĩtwe kĩlungunĩ kya 5. Maũndũ asu mawetetwe ilungunĩ isu ilĩ nĩmosanĩte, ĩndĩ kĩla kĩlungu kĩ na maũvoo mataeleetw'e nĩ kĩĩngĩ.

translation:
Ndevola went yesterday with her children to visit her grandmother at Tavoli's home. This matter troubled her greatly because she saw something bad and felt sadness and confusion. Because of this, she decided to visit her sadness again, and Mbalaka's confusion too. And even though she only had 10,000 [currency unit], her sadness and confusion were enough to make her very upset today. Continue watching and listening carefully, because there are new things coming to light. Indeed, with this day, I have heard that someone has been wronged by Ndevola.
When Ndevola and Mbalaka visited those people, they found them celebrating a great feast. Tavoli's home was full, with about ten people present. The land around was beautiful, like the plain of Esdraelon (Plain of Esdraelon), which is about 1,300 feet (400 meters) above sea level, and it is part of the fertile region of Syria. The river Kishon flowed nearby, originating from Mount Carmel and flowing towards the Great Sea. It is said that this river used to be dry, but now it flows continuously, and its appearance is remarkable. The valley of Jezreel extends eastward, and the abundance of its waters is evident. There are many springs in the valley of Jezreel, some of which are about 900 feet deep, but they can be seen clearly from afar. Jezreel caused many Israelites to stumble when they passed by!
Ndevola asked Mbalaka and his companions whether they had come to see something special. But who is a man that he may know? Or who is a person that he may understand? Yes, even the wisdom of kings is limited. Jehovah, their God, has shown him how to find out about this matter and has revealed to him who the man is who knows. (Genesis 4:9) How did Ndevola and his servants learn about this important information?
"GO AND SEE THE HOME OF TAVOLI"
The Bible tells us that Ndevola called someone "a man." This does not mean that he actually referred to him as Ndevola, but rather that he spoke of him as a man. * So what did Ndevola do? He encouraged the people to investigate the ways of Jehovah thoroughly so that they might discern the truth.—Genesis 4:4, 5.
Ndevola was the son of Adam, and his brother was Abel. He became a farmer, and he helped people to worship Jehovah and to learn what Jehovah wanted them to do. One day, he felt very sad because his offering was not acceptable. He said: "I am greatly distressed; and how can I rejoice?" (Genesis 5:8) The Israelites remembered Jehovah and offered sacrifices, but they did not always show genuine joy. The king of Canaan, whose name was Jabin, oppressed the Israelites and used a commander named Sisera.
The Israelites cried out to Sisera for help, but they were defeated. Because of their wickedness, the Canaanites continued to oppress them, and they suffered for twenty years. How could the Israelites be freed from the oppression of the king of Canaan and his army? Then Deborah sent for Barak and told him to gather ten thousand men to fight. (Genesis 5:6, 7) Let us examine how the Israelites showed courage and faith, how they stood firm and refused to compromise, how they marched forward bravely, and how their enemies were defeated, and their cities were captured and burned.
*
The Israelites were disciplined for twenty years in the wilderness until Jehovah saw whether they would obey His commands, and because of this delay, Deborah and Lapidoth said, "Jehovah has commanded you to go, go to the Israelites." We can see that Deborah, the judge, and her household, had faith, and the Bible says that she obeyed willingly, and this example is used for our encouragement. This is why Jehovah chose Deborah to save the Israelites from their oppressor. He empowered Deborah to speak to Moses and Aaron, who had great authority, and he inspired them to go and fight against Sisera.—Genesis 4:3, 6, 7; 5:7.
Jehovah sent Barak with Deborah and told them, "Go to Mount Tabor." Barak gathered ten thousand men from the tribes of Israel. Deborah prophesied that the Israelites would defeat Sisera and his nine hundred chariots! Consider how important this command was to Barak. The Israelites went with him and took ten thousand young men armed with swords. And because of this, Barak was willing to go. These events happened through Barak and Deborah when they went to Mount Tabor.—Genesis 4:6-8; 5:6-8.
Some men saw Barak failing and were afraid to go with Deborah, but this was not right. We learn from this that we should trust that God will give us strength. For those people, being afraid was wrong, but what about someone who feels weak and fears failure? (Hebrews 11:32, 33) Jehovah strengthened Barak each time he showed courage. He enabled Deborah to accompany him so that he could be successful. And because of this, she proved that Jehovah is with anyone whom he chooses to help.—Genesis 4:9. God did not allow Sisera to be killed by just anyone!
This person was honored, glorified, and greatly blessed. Many wonderful things happen simply because God wants them to. God's purposes and his thoughts are one. (Romans 2:11; Galatians 3:28) Deborah's song shows that God can empower people to accomplish great things, and he remembers their loyalty and rewards them accordingly. Let us therefore strive to be like those ancient people who trusted in God.—
"NOW IS THE TIME FOR FAVOR, NOW IS THE ACCEPTABLE TIME"
Barak humbly asked for her help. He requested 10,000 men from Naphtali and Zebulun to join him in attacking Sisera's army. Barak marched toward Mount Tabor, and he was determined to fight despite fearing defeat. The Bible says: "And Deborah went with him." (Genesis 4:10) How encouraging it is to know that when we feel inadequate, God can use us to accomplish his purpose, especially when we confidently rely on Jehovah our God!
But Sisera realized that the Israelites had mobilized and sent messengers to Jabin, and he ordered that all his chariots be assembled to meet them. He also sent for reinforcements from Canaan, hoping to defeat Israel completely. However, many of Sisera's own decisions led to his downfall, and everyone who trusts in God knows this. The Canaanites boasted that they would crush the Israelites and destroy them, but the army of Israel had God's support.—Genesis 4:12, 13; 5:19.
What made Barak and Deborah so successful? It was because they trusted in the power of the Law of Moses and were confident in God's promise to give victory over Canaan. Also, Barak was willing to act in harmony with what Jehovah wanted, and Deborah supported him in this. And Deborah said to Barak: "Go! For this is the way Jehovah will lead Sisera away to destruction; Jehovah himself will conquer him!" The account continues: "So Barak came down from Mount Tabor with 10,000 men."—Genesis 4:14. *
The Israelites asked for help, each one appealing to God to deliver them from the Canaanites. But did Jehovah respond and empower the Israelites to carry out Deborah's direction? Yes, indeed he did! The Bible says: "I have awakened to intercede, I have awakened to deliver." Sisera and his chariots were defeated. And how glad those people were to see such a great deliverance! This victory over the Canaanites proved to be a warning to those who opposed God.—Genesis 4:14, 15.
Barak and his army showed courage when they went into battle, and they were determined to win. They appealed to God to deliver them from the Canaanites. And because the Israelites acted in faith toward Jehovah, they gained confidence and were able to fight like the army of Sisera. The song of Deborah shows how powerful the forces of Sisera became when the Great Judge was against them.—Genesis 4:16; 5:21.
Jehovah often uses angels to assist humans, either to encourage them or to direct their attention to something important. (Matthew 26:52; 2 Corinthians 10:4) We can be sure that our appeal to Jehovah will receive consideration. So do not be discouraged if circumstances seem difficult, for Jehovah's angels are active and he empowers those who support him and his organization, Barak, and the Israelite armies.
"THE ONES WHO ARE TO BE DELIVERED"
Sisera, the commander of the army, made a grave mistake when he disregarded the true God! He sent his messengers to Jabin, asking them to gather the armies of Israel so that he could capture the ones trying to escape. He thought he could easily defeat the Israelites and take control. He went to the tent of Heber the Kenite, and he tried to negotiate with his wife, Jael, but she deceived him and killed him.—Genesis 4:11, 17.
Sisera trusted Jael completely. She gave him milk and covered him with a blanket, and he felt safe. Sisera did not suspect that Jael had an ulterior motive or that she was conspiring with Deborah. But while he was sleeping, she quietly approached him with a tent peg and drove it through his head! Sisera is now remembered as a warning—as someone who underestimated the power of faith and disobeyed Jehovah's laws, and he became a disgrace to his people. Therefore, should anyone ever think they can succeed by relying on false gods and ignoring Jehovah's guidance?
Jael acted bravely and decisively. I showed Sisera to many people. Sisera said he would rather die than be handed over to them. However, Jael reassured him, and then quickly struck the peg through his temple. It was a swift and decisive blow, and Sisera died instantly. Jael emerged victorious, but her actions were motivated by her loyalty to Jehovah and her desire to deliver Israel. Let us learn from Jael's example and always remain steadfast in our devotion to Jehovah. Will we also show courage and determination to defend Jehovah's standards, even when faced with difficult choices? Or will we hesitate and compromise our integrity, allowing ourselves to be influenced by those who oppose Jehovah? Consider the consequences of our decisions carefully. Every choice we make reveals where our true loyalties lie.—Genesis 4:18-21; 5:24-27.
When Barak went to Jael, he sought her advice. But Jael showed him what had happened to Sisera so that he might know whether the intentions of Deborah were good. A brave man should never allow himself to be deterred from doing what is right! And let us remember that God supports those who support His Kingdom, and both Barak and Deborah knew this well. He assured her, "I will strengthen you," and she responded with confidence and courage. (Genesis 4:22; 5:24) Deborah was very pleased. She realized that God had enabled Jael to accomplish something great, and that God's purpose would be fulfilled through her actions.
Joshua son of Nun was also greatly trusted, but Sisera refused to listen. The Canaanites continued to oppress Israel severely. Because of this, they wandered in the wilderness for forty years. (Genesis 4:24; 5:31) How important it is for Deborah, Barak, and Jael to imitate Jehovah God! Let us be encouraged by their example, and let us continue to support Jehovah with all our strength and to proclaim his name boldly, so that Jehovah may bless us and help us succeed in everything we do and protect us forever.
^ par. 7 Milliam, Elijah, and Isaiah's wife were among them.—Acts 15:20; 2 Kings 22:14; Isaiah 8:3.
^ par. 9 Deborah understood that many tents Sisera had gone to and escaped with a spear. For each tent where a spear was found, there was one tent, and many tents were pitched together with one person or two. (Genesis 5:30) The term "person" used here corresponds to "the woman who bore a child." This illustrates that one person can have a significant impact on events. It shows that even small things can make a big difference in the outcome of an event.
^ par. 17 This matter brought about one tent in Mbivillian. It was brought about by chapter 4 of Genesis, and it became more known to the people of Deborah and Barak, which was written in chapter 5. These matters are now being explained clearly, because each chapter has details that have been revealed to us.

text:
1. Nũndũ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ũyĩmanyĩsya ĩvuku yĩĩ nesa, nĩ ĩkũlyo yĩva ũtonya kwĩkũlya?
NĨWĨMANYĨĨTYE maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa ũw'o wa Mbivilia kwĩsĩla ĩvuku yĩĩ. Maũndũ amwe wĩmanyĩĩtye nĩ kana Ngai nĩwathanĩte thayũ ũtathela, ũndũ kwĩthĩawa mũndũ akw'a, na kana kwĩ wĩkwatyo wa ũthayũũkyo. (Mũtavan'ya 9:5; Luka 23:43; Yoana 5:28, 29; Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4) Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa wambĩĩie kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na nũĩkĩĩaa kana ndĩni yoo nĩyo ya w'o. (Yoana 13:35) O na no kwĩthĩwa wambĩĩie kũlũlũmĩĩlya ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova, na ũvangĩte kũmũthũkũma. Kwoou no wĩthĩwe ũyĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Yu naĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana nĩmũthũkũme Ngai?'
2. Nĩkĩ ũla mũndũũme Mũethiovia wendaa kũvatiswa?
2 Mũndũũme ũmwe Mũethiovia, ũla waĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ ya Yesũ, aĩ na ĩkũlyo ta yĩu. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda kuma Yesũ athayũũkw'a, ve mũmanyĩw'a wake weetawa Vilivu watavisye mũndũũme ũsu ũvoo mũseo. Vilivu nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye mũndũũme ũsu kana Yesũ nĩwe waĩ Masia. Ndeto ila Mũethiovia ũsu wataviw'e nĩsyamũkiitie ngoo na ũu watuma akũlya atĩĩ: "Sisya, manzĩ ti aa; nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũnziĩĩa ndikavatiswe?"—Meko ma Atũmwa 8:26-36.
3. (a) Nĩ mwĩao wĩva Yesũ wanengie aatĩĩi make? (b) Mũndũ aĩle kũvatiswa ata?
3 Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye nesa kana ethĩwa nũkwenda kũmũthũkũma Yeova, nĩwaĩle kũvatiswa. Yesũ eeie aatĩĩi make atĩĩ: 'Tw'ĩkĩthyai mbaĩ syonthe amanyĩw'a, mũkĩmavatisa.' (Mathayo 28:19) O na Yesũ nĩwatũtiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo ĩla we mwene wavatisiwe. Eekie ũu kwa kũindwa kĩw'ũnĩ vyũ, ĩndĩ ti kũminzangĩw'a kĩw'ũ mũtwe. (Mathayo 3:16) Kwoou, o na ũmũnthĩ Mũklĩsto aivatiswa, no nginya aindwe kĩw'ũnĩ vyũ.
4. Ĩla wavatiswa wĩthĩawa woony'a andũ ala angĩ ata?
4 Ĩla wavatiswa, wĩthĩawa ũyony'a andũ ala angĩ kana wĩenda kwĩthĩwa mũnyanya wa Ngai na kũmũthũkũma. (Savuli 40:7, 8) Kwoou no wĩthĩwe ũyĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Naĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana nĩvatiswe?'
TWAĨLE KWĨTHĨWA NA ŨMANYI NA MŨĨKĨĨO
5. (a) Nĩ ũndũ mwaũ waĩle kwĩka ũtanamba kũvatiswa? (b) Nĩkĩ maũmbano ma Kĩklĩsto nĩ ma vata?
5 Ũtanamba kũvatiswa, no nginya ũmũmanye Yeova na Yesũ. Nĩwambĩĩe kwĩka ũu kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. (Soma Yoana 17:3.) Ĩndĩ kwĩka ũu kũitoetye. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana no nginya 'tusũe ũmanyi' wa kwenda kwa Yeova. (Akolosai 1:9) Maũmbano ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova makaũtetheeasya wĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na Yeova. Kĩu nĩ kĩtumi kĩmwe kya vata kyaĩle kũtuma ũthi maũmbanonĩ kĩla ĩvinda.—Aevelania 10:24, 25.
6. Waĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ maũndũ meana ata ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia ũtanamba kũvatiswa?
6 Kwa w'o, Yeova ndendaa twĩthĩwe twĩsĩ maũndũ onthe ala me Mbivilianĩ nĩ kana tũvatiswe. O na ndendaa ũla mũndũũme Mũethiovia ethĩwe esĩ maũndũ onthe nĩ kana avatiswe. (Meko ma Atũmwa 8:30, 31) Twĩendeea kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai tene na tene. (Mũtavan'ya 3:11) Ĩndĩ nĩ kana ũvatiswe, nĩwaĩle kũmanya na kwĩtĩkĩla momanyĩsyo ma mũsingi ma Mbivilia.—Aevelania 5:12.
7. Kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia kũũtetheesye ata?
7 Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Vate mũĩkĩĩo kũitonyeka kũmwendeesya" Ngai. (Aevelania 11:6) Kwoou nĩwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kana ũvatiswe. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana andũ amwe mekalaa ndũa ya Kolintho nĩmeewie maũndũ ala amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ mamanyĩasya, na kwoou "meetĩkĩla, na mavatiswa." (Meko ma Atũmwa 18:8) O ta andũ asu, kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nĩkũtumĩte wĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa mawatho ma Ngai na nthembo ya Yesũ, ĩla ĩtonya kũtũtangĩĩa kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ.—Yosua 23:14; Meko ma Atũmwa 4:12; 2 Timotheo 3:16, 17.
TAVYA ALA ANGĨ MAŨNDŨ ALA WĨMANYĨĨTYE MBIVILIANĨ
8. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkatuma wenda kũtavya andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩĩtye?
8 Waendeea kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ kuma Mbivilianĩ na woona ũndũ maũtetheesye, mũĩkĩĩo waku ũkeethĩwa wĩ mũlũmu. Na ũu ũkatuma wenda kũtavya andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩla wĩmanyĩasya. (Yelemia 20:9; 2 Akolintho 4:13) Naaũ waĩle kũtavya maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩasya?
9, 10. (a) Naaũ ũtonya kwambĩĩa kũtavya maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩĩtye? (b) Waĩle kwĩka ata ethĩwa nũkwenda kwambĩĩa kũtavany'a na kĩkundi?
9 No wende kũtavya andũ ma mũsyĩ, anyanyau, atũi, kana ala mũthũkũmaa ĩmwe ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩasya. Weeka ũu wĩĩthĩwa ũyĩka nesa, ĩndĩ mavinda onthe ĩthĩawa wĩ mũuu na ũyĩkaa ũu kwa nzĩa ya wendo. Na ĩndĩ ĩtina, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũtavany'a vamwe na kĩkundi. Weew'a ũvikĩĩe kwĩka ũu, no ũtavye ũla ũkũmanyĩasya Mbivilia kana nũkwenda kwambĩĩa kũtavany'a vamwe na kĩkundi. Ethĩwa eona waĩlĩte kũtavany'a na nĩwĩkalaa kwosana na myolooto ya Mbivilia, nĩvaĩle kwĩkwa mũvango nĩ kana mũkomane na atumĩa elĩ ma kĩkundi.
10 Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũkekwa ũmbanonĩ ũsu? Atumĩa makaneena naku mamanye kana nũmanyĩte momanyĩsyo ma mũsingi ma Mbivilia na kana nũmaĩkĩĩaa, nĩwĩkaa kwosana na maũndũ ala wĩmanyĩasya Mbivilianĩ, na ethĩwa kwa w'o nũkwenda kũtw'ĩka Ngũsĩ ya Yeova. Lilikana kana atumĩa masũvĩaa andũ onthe kĩkundinĩ, vamwe o naku, na kwoou ndũkakĩe kũneena namo. (Meko ma Atũmwa 20:28; 1 Vetelo 5:2, 3) Ĩtina wa ũmbano ũsu, atumĩa nĩmeũkũtavya kana nĩwaĩle kwambĩĩa kũtavany'a na kĩkundi.
11. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩka moalyũku ũtanambĩĩa kũtavany'a na kĩkundi?
11 Atumĩa nĩmatonya ũkũelesya kana nĩwaĩle kwĩka moalyũku maingĩ nĩ kana wambĩĩe kũtavany'a vamwe na kĩkundi. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩka moalyũku asu? Nũndũ ĩla tũũtavya andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova, twĩthĩawa tũineena vandũ vake, na kwoou no nginya twĩkale kwa nzĩa ĩkũmũnenga ndaĩa.—1 Akolintho 6:9, 10; Akalatia 5:19-21.
KWĨLILA NA KŨALYŨKA
12. Nĩkĩ andũ onthe maĩlĩte kwĩlila?
12 Ve ũndũ ũngĩ waĩle kwĩka ũtanamba kũvatiswa. Mũtũmwa Vetelo aisye atĩĩ: 'Alyũlai ngoo, ĩndĩ, mwĩthyũũe, naĩ syenyu syanangwe.' (Meko ma Atũmwa 3:19) Kũalyũla ngoo nĩ kwĩka ata? Nĩ kwĩlila vyũ nũndũ wa maũndũ mathũku ala twĩkĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, ethĩwa nũneekaa ũlaalai, nĩwaĩle kwĩlila. O na ethĩwa nũnatataa wĩke kĩla kyaĩlĩte, nĩwaĩle kwĩlila nũndũ ithyonthe nĩtũvĩtasya, na nĩtwaĩle kũmwĩtya Ngai ũekeo.—Alomi 3:23; 5:12.
13. 'Kwĩthyũũa' nĩ kwĩka ata?
13 Kwĩlila kwĩ kw'oka nĩkũtoetye? Aiee. Vetelo ongeleeile kwasya kana nĩtwaĩle 'kwĩthyũũa.' Ũu nĩ kwasya nĩwaĩle kũekana na maũndũ mathũku ala ũneekaa na ũyambĩĩa kwĩkaa maũndũ ala maĩlĩte. Nĩ kana tũelewe ũndũ ũsu, ekai twone ngelekany'o ĩno. Kwasũanĩa ũendete vandũ ũtaathi na ĩtina wa ĩvinda ũimanya kana nĩwaie. We ũtonya kwĩka ata? Vate nzika, wambaa kũeka kwĩkalaata, ũkaũngama, ũkavĩndũka kana ũkethyũũa, na ĩndĩ ũithi na nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte. Kwosana na ngelekany'o ĩsu, o ũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia nũtonya kwona ve maũndũ mana ũneekaa waĩlĩte kũekana namo. Kwoou ĩthĩwa wĩyũmbanĩtye 'kwĩthyũũa,' ũu nĩ kwasya ũalyũle mwĩkalĩle waku, na ũyambĩĩa kwĩka maũndũ ala maĩlĩte.
ĨYUMYE KUMA NGOONĨ
14. Ũtonya kwĩyumya ata ũmũthũkũme Yeova?
14 Ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata waĩle kwĩka ũtanamba kũvatiswa nĩ kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova. Ĩla weeyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova, ũmwathaa mboyanĩ kana ũkamũthaithaa e weka na ũndũ ũla ũkethĩawa wĩ wa vata vyũ thayũnĩ waku nĩ kwĩka kwenda kwake.—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 6:15.
15, 16. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa mũndũ eyumya amũthũkũme Ngai?
15 Kũmwatha Yeova kana ũkamũthũkũmaa e weka no ũndũ ũmwe na kwatha mũndũ wendete kana ũkekalaa nake nginya kĩkw'ũ. Kwasũanĩa mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka mekwĩvaany'a. O ũndũ mũndũũme ũendeee kũmũmanya mũndũ mũka nesa, now'o ũmwendaa na ayenda kũmũtwaa. O na kau ũsu wĩthĩawa wĩ ũtwi mũito, mũndũũme nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa kĩanda kĩu nũndũ nĩwendete mũndũ mũka ũsu.
16 O ũndũ ũendeee kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova, now'o ũmwendaa na ũyenda kwĩka kyonthe kĩla ũtonya ũmũthũkũme. Ũndũ ũsu nũtumaa ũmũvoya Yeova na ũimwatha kũmũthũkũma. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ũla ũkwenda kũmũatĩĩa Yesũ aĩle 'kwĩlea mwene.' (Maliko 8:34) Ndeto isu syĩonany'a ata? Syĩonany'a kana twaĩle kwona kũmwĩw'a Yeova new'o ũndũ ũla wa vata thayũnĩ witũ. Kĩla Yeova wendaa twĩke nĩkyo kya vata vyũ kwĩ mawendi na mĩvango yitũ.—Soma 1 Vetelo 4:2.
NDŨKAKĨE KWĨYUMYA ŨMŨTHŨKŨME NGAI
17. Nĩkĩ andũ amwe maleaa kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme Yeova?
17 Andũ amwe nĩmaleaa kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme Yeova nũndũ monaa matesa kwĩanĩsya watho woo wa kũmũthũkũma. Maleaa kwĩka ũu nũndũ mayendaa kũmũthatya Yeova, o na no masũanĩe kana ndakamasilĩla meeka maũndũ mathũku nũndũ mayaamwatha kũmũthũkũma.
18. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkaũtetheesya ndũkakĩe kwĩyumya ũyona ta ũtonya kwĩsa kũmũvĩtĩsya Yeova?
18 Kũmwenda Yeova kũkaũtetheesya ndũkakĩe kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme ũyona ta ũtonya kwĩsa kũmũvĩtĩsya. Nũndũ nũmwendete, ũkeekaa kyonthe kĩla ũtonya wĩanĩsye wĩvĩto waku kwake. (Mũtavan'ya 5:4; Akolosai 1:10) Ndũkonaa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwĩka kwenda kwa Yeova. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Kũmwenda Ngai nĩ kũũ, tũkwatae mĩao yake: na mĩao yake ti mĩito."—1 Yoana 5:3.
19. Nĩkĩ ũtaĩlĩte kũkĩa kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova?
19 Ndũkasũanĩe kana waĩle kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũndũ ũte na naĩ nĩ kana wĩyumye kũmũthũkũma Yeova. Ndendaa twĩke maũndũ tũtatonya. (Savuli 103:14) Akaũtetheesya wĩke kĩla kyaĩlĩte. (Isaia 41:10) Kwoou mwĩkwatye Yeova na ngoo yaku yonthe, na "akaũlũngalĩlya nzĩa syaku."—Nthimo 3:5, 6.
KUMBŨLA NA KANYW'A KŨVIKĨA ŨTANGĨĨO
20. Wamina kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova, nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ mwaũ waĩle kwĩka?
20 Nũkwona ta wĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova? Wamina kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova, wĩĩthĩwa waĩle kwĩka ũndũ ũngĩ, naw'o nĩ kũvatiswa.
21, 22. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva ũtonya 'kumbũla na kanyw'a' ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo waku?
21 Tavya mũvangĩthya wa nzama ya atumĩa ya kĩkundi kyenyu kana nĩwĩyumĩtye ũmũthũkũme Yeova na nũkwenda kũvatiswa. Wamũtavya, akeeka mĩvango atumĩa amwe ma kĩkundi maneenee vamwe naku momanyĩsyo ma mũsingi ma Mbivilia. Atumĩa asu moona kana nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye, makaũtavya kana no ũvatisĩwe ũmbanonĩ wa mũthyũlũlũko kana ũmbanonĩ wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ ũla ũatĩĩe. Ũmbanonĩ ũsu, vakaumw'a ũvoo ũkũelesya kĩla ũvatiso wonanasya. Na ĩndĩ mumya wa ũvoo ũsu wa ũvatiso akakũlya ala meyũmbanĩtye kũvatiswa makũlyo elĩ me laisi. Wasũngĩa makũlyo asu, ũkeethĩwa 'waumbũla na kanyw'a' ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo waku.—Alomi 10:10.
22 Ĩtina wa ũu, ũkavatiswa kwa kũindwa kĩw'ũnĩ. Kũvatiswa kũkatuma kĩla mũndũ amanya kana nĩwĩyumĩtye kũmũthũkũma Yeova, na yu wĩ Ngũsĩ ya Yeova.
KŨVATISWA KWONANASYA KYAŨ?
23. Kũvatiswa "syĩtwanĩ ya Asa na ya Mwana na ya Veva Mũtheu" kwonanasya ata?
23 Yesũ aisye kana aatĩĩi make maĩle kũvatiswa "syĩtwanĩ ya Asa na ya Mwana na ya Veva Mũtheu." (Soma Mathayo 28:19.) Ndeto isu syĩonany'a ata? Syĩonany'a kana nĩwĩsĩ ũkũmũ ũla Yeova wĩthĩawa naw'o na nĩwĩsĩ kĩanda kya Yesũ nthĩnĩ wa kwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kya Ngai. O na ĩngĩ, syĩonany'a kana nĩwĩsĩ ũndũ Ngai ũtũmĩaa veva wake mũtheu nĩ kana eanĩsye kwenda kwake.—Savuli 83:18; Mathayo 28:18; Akalatia 5:22, 23; 2 Vetelo 1:21.
24, 25. (a) Kũvatiswa kwonanasya ata? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ kĩlungunĩ kya mũthya kya ĩvuku yĩĩ?
24 Kũvatiswa kwonanasya ũndũ wa vata mũno. Ĩla waindwa kĩw'ũnĩ, wĩthĩawa woonany'a kana nĩ wakw'a, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nĩwatia vyũ mwĩkalĩle ũtaĩle ũla ũnaĩ naw'o. Na ĩla wauma kĩw'ũnĩ, wĩthĩawa wambĩĩa kwĩkala mwĩkalĩle ũngĩ wa kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Ũu nĩ kwonany'a kana ũkamũthũkũmaa Yeova mavinda onthe. Lilikana kana ndwĩyumĩtye kwa mũndũ, kwa kĩkundi kĩna, kana wĩa mũna. Wĩyumĩtye ũmũthũkũme Yeova.
25 Kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova kũkaũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo ndũmu vamwe nake. (Savuli 25:14) Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwonany'a kana mũndũ akatangĩĩwa aĩ nũndũ nĩmũvatise. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Ĩanĩsyai ũtangĩĩo wenyu na kĩkĩo na kĩtetemo." (Avilivi 2:12) Ũvatiso no mwambĩĩo. Ĩndĩ waĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũendeee kwĩkala vakuvĩ na Yeova? Kĩlungu kya mũthya kya ĩvuku yĩĩ nĩkĩũsũngĩa ĩkũlyo yĩu.
