translation:
1. Should a person be baptized before he fully understands what it means, just to get rid of fear and anxiety?
WE LEARN many things from the example of Jesus Christ recorded in the Bible about baptism. We learn that God can resurrect people to everlasting life, that a person may deserve punishment, and that there is a ransom price for sins. (Matthew 9:5; Luke 23:43; John 5:28, 29; Revelation 21:3, 4) We also learn how important it is to show love for Jehovah and to prove whether we are on his side. (John 13:35) And we learn how important it is to have a good relationship with Jehovah and to please him. So if someone asks you, "What if I want to get baptized, but I am still learning?"
2. Why should a Ethiopian official ask to be baptized?
2 There was an Ethiopian official who had come to Jerusalem to worship. He was reading a portion of the Scriptures when Philip approached him. After explaining those scriptures to the official, Philip baptized him. The Ethiopian then said that Jesus was the Messiah. But before the Ethiopian could be baptized, he asked: "Is there anything preventing me from getting baptized?"—Acts 8:26-36.
3. (a) How did Jesus commission his followers? (b) Can a person be baptized without understanding?
3 The Bible shows us clearly that our desire to please Jehovah should motivate us to get baptized. Jesus gave his followers this command: "Go therefore and make disciples of people of all nations, baptizing them." (Matthew 28:19) However, Jesus did not authorize anyone to baptize others unless they first learned about him. It would be illogical to baptize someone who does not understand what it means. (Matthew 3:16) Therefore, a true Christian will not allow himself to be baptized until he has learned about the truth.
4. What should a newly baptized one look forward to?
4 A newly baptized one should look forward to drawing closer to God and pleasing Him. (Psalm 40:7, 8) He may also wonder, 'What more can I do now that I have been baptized?'
WE MUST BE BAPTIZED WITH ACCURATE KNOWLEDGE AND A PURPOSE
5. (a) What is essential before getting baptized? (b) What are Christian meetings for?
5 Before getting baptized, it is vital that you know Jehovah and Jesus. Learn how to do so by studying the Bible. (Read John 17:3.) This requires effort. The Bible says that we need to "keep growing in the knowledge" of Jehovah. (Colossians 1:9) Meetings of Jehovah's Witnesses help you strengthen your faith and your relationship with Jehovah. They are one way that Christians can encourage one another regularly.—Hebrews 10:24, 25.
6. Are there other important things we can do to prepare for baptism?
6 Yes, Jehovah wants us to learn as much as possible from the Bible, even after we get baptized. And he wants each individual to examine himself to see if he is truly making progress. (Acts 8:30, 31) We should continue to study God's Word diligently. (Proverbs 3:11) So even if you have already been baptized, strive to grow in accurate knowledge of basic Bible teachings.—Hebrews 5:12.
7. How does studying the Bible benefit us?
7 The Bible states: "Without faith it is impossible to please [God]." (Hebrews 11:6) Therefore, you need faith even after you get baptized. The Bible tells us that some in Corinth began believing but did not fully appreciate the meaning of Jesus' teachings, and they were told to "hold firmly to the faith." (Acts 18:8) Thus, studying the Bible helps us exercise faith and conform our lives to God's standards and the example of Jesus, which will lead to salvation.—Joshua 23:14; Acts 4:12; 2 Timothy 3:16, 17.
OTHER WAYS TO INCREASE YOUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIBLE
8. What can motivate you to help others increase their understanding?
8 As you learn more from the Bible and see how practical it is, your desire to help others will likely intensify. This can motivate you to assist them in learning. (Jeremiah 20:9; 2 Corinthians 4:13) But how can you effectively share what you are learning?
9, 10. (a) How can you prepare to share what you are learning? (b) Is it wise to offer to study with someone without first speaking to the congregation?
9 Do not hesitate to approach people who seem interested, thoughtful, humble, or who have expressed some curiosity about spiritual things. Consider this: A warm welcome makes a good impression, and a kind attitude shows genuine interest. Also, sometimes it may be best to invite someone to join a group study rather than offering individual assistance. However, if you feel qualified to teach someone the Bible or to invite him to a group study, do so. It is important to remember that our goal is to help people come to know Jehovah and to associate with the congregation, not to simply fulfill a quota.
10 Is this something we should always do? Elders should encourage and strengthen their brothers, and they should refresh their understanding of basic Bible teachings and how to apply them, and they should remain occupied with things that build up others spiritually, and also they should continue to seek God's guidance. But if elders mistreat fellow worshipers, causing them distress, or if they try to dominate others in a group study, they will bring reproach upon themselves and possibly damage their reputation. (Acts 20:28; 1 Peter 5:2, 3) In such cases, elders may need to apologize or ask forgiveness from those they have wronged.
11 What, then, can we do to avoid causing distress to fellow worshipers?
11 Elders should be careful not to overstep their authority or to misuse their position to control others or to force them to participate in a group study. What, then, can we do to avoid overstepping our authority? As we endeavor to help people learn about Jehovah, we want to show respect for his sheep, and we must never allow ourselves to become arrogant or self-righteous.—1 Corinthians 6:9, 10; Galatians 5:19-21.
TO BE CONCERNED AND HELPFUL
12 Why should we be concerned about others?
12 We should be deeply moved by their plight. The apostle Peter urged us: "Repent, therefore, and turn around, so that your sins may be wiped out." (Acts 3:19) To repent means to feel remorseful, does it not? It means being sorry for wrong actions and making changes. For example, if someone has been unkind, he may feel regret and express repentance. Or if someone has repeatedly engaged in wrongdoing, he may feel sorrow because his conduct has displeased God.—Romans 3:23; 5:12.
13 What does it mean to 'turn around'?
13 Is turning around simply a matter of saying you are sorry? No. Peter explained that it involves more than just saying "I am turning around." It means changing our course, abandoning bad habits, and starting to do what is right. If we understand this, let us examine ourselves closely. Consider a driver who has taken a wrong route—does he merely say, "I am turning around"? No, he turns the steering wheel, makes a U-turn, and then proceeds in the correct direction. Similarly, to truly turn around, we must make earnest efforts to align our lives with Bible principles and see what changes we need to make. When someone uses the expression "turning around," it means he has changed his attitude and is determined to do what is right.
KEEP REMINDING YOURSELF
14 Can you strengthen your faith in Jehovah?
14 One way to strengthen your faith is to focus on strengthening your relationship with Jehovah. The more you come to know and love Jehovah, the more confident you will be when facing trials and temptations.—See box "How to Strengthen Your Faith."
15, 16 What motivates a person to turn back to God?
15 Loving Jehovah and wanting to please him is one reason why a person might turn back to God, even after making serious mistakes. But a person may also be motivated by a desire to maintain good relationships with others. People generally want to be accepted and loved. So a person may try to improve his relationship with another individual so that the other one will continue to associate with him. However, if such a person does not genuinely change his heart, his efforts may be superficial. He may only pretend to have turned over a new leaf.
16 But if you truly strive to imitate Jehovah, you will want to live in harmony with all that he teaches. This will help you to appreciate Jehovah more fully and to love him deeply. It will move you to take action, just as Jesus urged his followers to "disown themselves." (Mark 8:34) Why is this important? Because our love for Jehovah is often tested by the trials and difficulties we face in life. When Jehovah asks us to make sacrifices, it is because he loves us and wants what is best for us.—Read 1 Peter 4:2.
TO KEEP YOUR FAITH STRONG
17 Why do some find it hard to stay close to Jehovah?
17 Some find it hard to stay close to Jehovah because they feel unworthy to approach him. They may believe that their past mistakes disqualify them from receiving his favor. They may fear that Jehovah is displeased with them, or they may feel overwhelmed by guilt and regret.
18 What can help you to remain loyal despite feeling unworthy and doubting your value in Jehovah's eyes?
18 Loving Jehovah can help you to remain loyal despite feeling unworthy and doubting your value in his eyes. The more you come to know and love him, the more you will appreciate his standards and ways.—Proverbs 5:4; Colossians 1:10. Remember that Jehovah values your efforts. The apostle John wrote: "This is the love that God expresses toward us, that he gives us his Son."—1 John 5:3.
19 How can you strengthen your determination to stay close to Jehovah?
19 Do not be discouraged if you sometimes struggle with feelings of inadequacy. Jehovah understands our imperfections. (Psalm 103:14) Focus on what you *can* do. (Isaiah 41:10) Lean heavily on Jehovah and trust in him completely, and "he will bring it about."—Proverbs 3:5, 6.
REMEMBER AND APPLY WHAT YOU LEARN
20 Why is it vital to keep your faith strong?
20 Are you determined to keep your faith strong? Keeping your faith strong will enable you to overcome obstacles and maintain your joy, and it will also mean survival.
21, 22. What does it mean to 'remember and apply' what you learn?
21 Do not hesitate to ask experienced elders in your congregation for help if you are struggling to stay motivated. They can suggest practical steps you can take, such as reviewing Bible principles with them. Elders can discern if you are being overly critical of yourself, and they can encourage you to accept loving discipline or to seek assistance from qualified counselors. Such counsel can help you address underlying issues and make progress. Also, remember that regular self-examination can reveal areas where you need to improve. By taking those steps, you will demonstrate that you are 'remembering and applying' what you learn.—Romans 10:10.
22 In this way, you will continue to grow spiritually. Being disciplined helps each individual determine whether he is truly devoted to Jehovah and is pleasing to God.
WHAT DOES REGULAR SELF-EXAMINATION INVOLVE?
23 Does regular self-examination involve asking ourselves, "Am I measuring up to the standard set by the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit"?
23 Jesus showed that we should strive to measure up to the standard set by the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. (Read Matthew 28:19.) But how can we do so? We can do so by recognizing that Jehovah cares about our efforts and that Jesus' example shows us how to reflect God's personality. Furthermore, we can be confident that God uses imperfect humans who sincerely want to please him.—Psalm 83:18; Matthew 28:18; Colossians 5:22, 23; 2 Peter 1:21.
24, 25. (a) What does regular self-examination involve? (b) What can motivate us to examine ourselves honestly?
24 Regular self-examination involves honest evaluation. If you find yourself falling short, acknowledge it and perhaps discuss it with someone you trust. And if you are doing well, use that as motivation to continue serving God zealously. This will show that you are deeply appreciative of Jehovah. Consider whether your feelings, your conduct, or your associations are affecting your spirituality. Strive to remain devoted to Jehovah.
25 To stay devoted to Jehovah requires effort and reliance on his help. (Psalm 25:14) It means being willing to correct our thinking and actions. The apostle Paul wrote: "Carefully observe your way and your conduct." (Philippians 2:12) Baptism is an important step. But what more can you do to maintain a close relationship with Jehovah? Honest self-examination can help you strengthen your faith.

text:
"Yeova akeethĩwa katĩ wakwa naku, na katĩ wa ũsyao wakwa na ũsyao waku, tene na tene."—1 SAM. 20:42.
MBATHI: 43, 31
1, 2. Nĩkĩ ndũũ ya Yonathani na Ndaviti nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo vyũ ya andũ malũmanĩtye vamwe?
ĨLA Ndaviti wooaie yĩla ĩmũndũ yeetawa Ngoliathu, no nginya Yonathani ethĩwe aseng'iw'e mũno nĩ ũndũ ũsu, nũndũ Ndaviti aĩ o kamwana. Ĩtina wa ũndũ ũsu, Ndaviti nĩwatwaiwe vala ve Saulo mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli, aũngama mbee wake "e na mũtwe wa ũla Mũvilisiti kw'okonĩ kwake." (1 Sam. 17:57) No kwĩthĩwa Yonathani eewie amwenda nũndũ wa ũkũmbaũ wake. Vayaĩ nzika kana Ngai aĩ vamwe na Ndaviti, na nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, "ngoo ya Yonathani yakwatana na ngoo ya Ndaviti." O na "matianĩe ũtianĩo nĩkwĩthĩwa [Yonathani] nĩwamwendie [Ndaviti] o tondũ wĩyendete mwene." (1 Sam. 18:1-3) Kuma mũthenya ũsu nginya ĩla wesie kũkw'a, ekalile alũmanĩtye na Ndaviti.
2 Yonathani nĩwaendeeie kũlũmany'a na Ndaviti, o na kau Ngai nĩwamũnyuvĩte Ndaviti etw'ĩka mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli ĩtina wa Saulo. Nĩkyo kĩtumi wambĩĩe kũthĩnĩka ĩla wamanyie kana Saulo nũkwenda kũaa Ndaviti. Na kwoou nĩwaumisye kyalo athi nginya vandũ vetawa Olesi weũnĩ wa Yutia nĩ kana ekĩe mũnyanyae vinya. Ĩla wavikie kũu Ndaviti waĩ, nĩwoosie mwanya eekĩa "kw'oko kwake vinya nthĩnĩ wa Ngai." Amwĩie atĩĩ: "Ndũkakĩe; . . . ũkeethĩwa mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli, nakwa ngeethĩwa nĩ wa kelĩ ũsumbĩnĩ."—1 Sam. 23:16, 17.
3. Nĩ kyaũ Yonathani woonaa kĩ kya vata vyũ kwĩ kũlũmany'a na Ndaviti, na twĩsĩ ũu ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 21.)
3 Kaingĩ nĩtwendete andũ ala mekalaa malũmanĩtye na anyanyae moo. Ĩndĩ o na kau nĩtũmwendete Yonathani nũndũ nĩwalũmanĩtye na Ndaviti, ve ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata vyũ ũla waĩle kũtuma tũmwenda, naw'o nĩ kũlũmany'a kũla walũmanĩtye na Ngai. We wĩona nĩkĩ Yonathani wamwendete Ndaviti vandũ va kũmwona ta nthũ? Vate nzika, ve ũndũ Yonathani woonaa wĩ wa vata mũno kwĩ kwĩyĩuna we mwene. Lilikana kana nĩwoosie mwanya aneena na Ndaviti na "amwĩkĩa kw'oko kwake vinya nthĩnĩ wa Ngai." Kwoou ũndũ ũla Yonathani woonaa wĩ wa vata vyũ nĩ kũlũmany'a na Ngai. Na kĩu nĩkyo kyatumie ekala alũmanĩtye na Ndaviti. Aũme asu me elĩ nĩmeanĩisye ũtianĩo ũũ matianĩie: "Yeova akeethĩwa katĩ wakwa naku, na katĩ wa ũsyao wakwa na ũsyao waku, tene na tene."—1 Sam. 20:42.
4. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtwĩkalya twĩ atanu vyũ na twĩ eanĩe? (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
4 Ta twĩ Aklĩsto, tũyĩkaa o kwĩw'a mũyo twoona angĩ malũmanĩtye na anyanyae moo. Ithyĩ ene nĩtwĩkĩaa kĩthito tũlũmany'e na andũ maitũ ma mũsyĩ, anyanyae maitũ, na Aklĩsto ala angĩ. (1 Ath. 2:10, 11) Ĩndĩ nũũ ũla twaĩle kũlũmany'a nake mbee vyũ? Vai ũngĩ eka ũla watũnengie thayũ! (Ũvu. 4:11) Tweeka ũu, tũkeethĩawa twĩ eanĩe na twĩ atanu vyũ. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana twonany'e nĩtũlũmanĩtye vyũ na Ngai, tũyaĩle kũmũtia ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna metu. Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ nĩtũkwĩmanyĩsya ũndũ ngelekany'o ya Yonathani ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkale tũlũmanĩtye na Yeova maũndũnĩ aa ana: (1) ĩla twoona tũtaĩle kũnenga ndaĩa mũndũ mũna wĩ na ũkũmũ, (2) ĩla twatuanĩwa nũũ ũla tũũlũmany'a nake, (3) ĩla tũtanaeleeka nesa kana twooswa naĩ, na (4) ĩla weethĩa no nginya twĩyĩime nĩ kana twĩanĩsye wĩvĩto witũ.
ETHĨWA NĨTŨKWONA TŨTAĨLE KŨNENGA NDAĨA MŨNDŨ MŨNA WĨ NA ŨKŨMŨ
5. Nĩkĩ Aisilaeli meew'aa kũlũmany'a na Ngai kwĩ vinya ĩla Saulo wasumbĩkĩte?
5 Saulo, ĩthe wa Yonathani, etĩkĩw'e mauta nĩ Ngai atw'ĩke mũsumbĩ, ĩndĩ ĩla waekie kũmwĩw'a, Ngai nĩwamũleile. (1 Sam. 15:17-23) Nũndũ Ngai ndaamũvena ũsumbĩ mũthenya ũla wamũleile, mwĩkalĩle wake mũthũku nĩwatumie ala wasumbĩkĩte na anyanyae malika thĩnanĩ. Thĩna waĩ ũũ: meĩkala malũmanĩtye na Ngai ata, nake ũla wĩ "kĩvĩlanĩ kya ũsumbĩ kya Yeova" nũtiĩte nzĩa?—1 Mav. 29:23.
6. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtwonasya kana Yonathani nĩwalũmanĩtye vyũ na Yeova?
6 Ĩvinda ya mbee ĩla Saulo waleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai, mwanae Yonathani nĩwoonanisye kana we alũmanĩtye na Yeova. (1 Sam. 13:13, 14) Mwathani Samueli aĩ anaweta ũũ: "Yeova ndakamatia andũ make nũndũ wa syĩtwa yake ĩnene." (1 Sam. 12:22) Yonathani oonanisye nĩwaĩkĩĩe ndeto isu ĩla ita sya Avilisiti syookie kũkita na Aisilaeli syĩ na makasya 30,000 ma kaũ. Ĩvinda yĩu Saulo aĩ na o aũme 600, na ate o we na Yonathani, vai ũngĩ waĩ na mĩio ya kaũ! Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, Yonathani nĩwaendie vala Avilisiti asu mambĩte kambi ate na mũndũ ũngĩ eka mwanake ũla wamũkuĩaa mĩio ya kaũ. Eeie mwanake ũsu atĩĩ: "Vati kĩsiĩĩi kwa Yeova kũtangĩĩa na aingĩ kana na avũthũ." Me elĩ mooaie Avilisiti ta 20. Na ĩndĩ "nthĩ yatetema: o ta ũu kwaĩ kĩtetemo kĩnene mũno" kuma kwa Ngai. Avilisiti moona ũu, mavũavũanie nginya mambĩĩa kũaana. Vate nzika, mũĩkĩĩo wa Yonathani nĩwatumie Aisilaeli masinda.—1 Sam. 13:5, 15, 22; 14:1, 2, 6, 14, 15, 20.
7. Yonathani oonaa ĩthe ata?
7 O na kau ngwatanĩo ya Saulo na Yeova nĩyaendeeie kwanangĩka, Yonathani nĩwaendeeie kũmũkwata ĩthe kw'oko ĩla veethĩwa vata. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwaendaa nake kaũnĩ makokitĩe andũ ma Ngai.—1 Sam. 31:1, 2.
8, 9. Nĩkĩ kũnenga ndaĩa ala me na ũkũmũ kwonanasya kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Ngai?
8 O naitũ twaĩle kwĩka ta Yonathani. No twonany'e kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Yeova kwa kwĩnyivĩsya silikalĩ ĩla vaĩlĩte, nũndũ ũu nĩw'o Ngai wendaa twĩke. Twaĩle kwĩka ũu o na ethĩwa twĩona ve amwe nthĩnĩ wa silikalĩ tũtaĩle kũmanenga ndaĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũnene mũna wa silikalĩ no ethĩwe e mũlũsani, ĩndĩ tũilea kũmũnenga ndaĩa nũndũ nĩtwĩaĩwe twĩnyivĩsye ũndũ vaĩle "ala me na ũkũmũ" silikalĩnĩ. (Soma Alomi 13:1, 2.) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ithyonthe no twonany'e kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Yeova kwa kũmanenga ndaĩa onthe ala ũmanengete ũkũmũ.—1 Ako. 11:3; Aevl. 13:17.
9 Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Olga [1] kuma La Paz, Bolivia, nĩwalũmanilye na Ngai kwa kũnenga mũũme ndaĩa, o na kau maũndũ maĩ metu. Kwa myaka mingĩ, mũũme nĩwamwonethasya ũtheinĩ kana ndatanaa kwona atw'ĩkĩte Ngũsĩ. Nĩwamũtavasya ndeto nthũku, akamũumanga, akamũvindĩsya, na nĩwamwĩaa nũkwosa syana na aimũtia. Ĩndĩ Olga ndaaĩvanĩsya. Nĩwatatie kwĩka kyonthe kĩla ũtonya ethĩwe e kĩveti kĩseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwamũuĩaa, akamũvũĩa ngũa, na akatetheesya andũ ma mũsyĩ ũsu watwaĩtwe. (Alo. 12:17) O na ĩla vatonyeka, nĩwaendanasya na mũũme ĩla kwa aa mũũme kwĩ syathĩ sya mũsyĩ kana ĩla mũũme ũkũthi kũkethya anyanyae. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩla mũũme waendaa taoni ĩngĩ akathike ĩthe, Olga nĩwoombanisye syana vamwe na syĩndũ syonthe ila syendekaa kwondũ wa kyalo kĩu. Na ĩla mavikie, ekalile mũomonĩ wa ĩkanisa eteele mũũme nginya ĩla maminie kĩla maendeesye. Ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ, ngoo ya mũũme nĩyambĩĩe kwololoa nũndũ wa wũmĩĩsyo wake na ndaĩa ĩla wamũnengete. Ũmũnthĩ mũũme ũsu nĩwe ũmũtwaaa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, o na nũmwĩkĩaa vinya athi ũmbano, na mavinda amwe nũendanasya nake.—1 Vet. 3:1.
ĨLA TWATUANĨWA NŨŨ ŨLA TŨŨLŨMANY'A NAKE
10. Yonathani amanyie ata ũla waaĩle kũlũmany'a nake?
10 Nũndũ Saulo nĩwatw'ĩte vyũ kũmũaa Ndaviti, Yonathani nĩwasaanĩiw'e elũmany'a naũ. O na kau Yonathani nĩwatianĩĩte ũtianĩo na Ndaviti, no wendaa kwĩnyivĩsya ĩthe. Ĩndĩ nĩweesĩ kana Ngai aĩ vamwe na Ndaviti na ti Saulo. Kwoou Yonathani nĩwatwie kũlũmany'a na Ndaviti mbee wa ũndũ walũmanĩtye na Saulo. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩvinda yĩmwe weeie Ndaviti nĩevithe, na ĩndĩ aneena maũndũ maseo ĩũlũ wa Ndaviti kũla kwĩ ĩthe, Saulo.—Soma 1 Samueli 19:1-6.
11, 12. Kũmwenda Ngai kũtũtetheeasya ata tũtw'e kũlũmany'a nake?
11 Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Alice kuma Australia nĩwatwie kũlũmany'a na Ngai, na kĩu nĩkyamũtetheeisye kũtw'a elũmany'a na andũ ala angĩ mũno wĩana ata. Ĩla weemanyĩasya Mbivilia nĩwatavasya andũ make ma mũsyĩ maũndũ maseo ala weemanyĩasya. Ĩndĩ nĩvavikie vandũ amatavya kana maiya Kĩlisimasi ndakaĩsaa namo. Mwambĩĩonĩ ĩla wamatavisye nĩkĩ ũtekwatĩanĩa namo ũndũnĩ ũsu, mayoonekaa maithĩnĩka mũno, ĩndĩ nĩmesie kũmũthilĩkĩla vyũ. Moonaa Alice ta ũkwenda kũmavatha. Ũ Alice easya atĩĩ: "Mũthya Mami esie kũmbĩa ndi mwana wake. Natelemile na neew'a naũmĩa mũno nũndũ nĩnendete andũ maitũ ma mũsyĩ vyũ. Ĩndĩ nĩnatwie kana Yeova na Mwana wake nĩmo mekũtw'ĩka ma vata vyũ ngoonĩ yakwa. Na kwoou nĩnavatisiwe ũmbanonĩ mũnene ũla waatĩĩe."—Mt. 10:37.
12 Tũkaema kwĩsũvĩa twĩsa kwĩthĩa tũlũmanĩtye mũno na nthĩ yitũ, sukulu ĩla tũsomeaa, kana timũ ya mathaũ, na kĩndũ kĩu nĩũtuma tũeka kũlũmany'a na Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Henry nĩwendete kũthaũka ĩthaũ ya chess. Sukulu yoo nĩyeesĩkĩe kana nĩyo ĩsindaa masindanonĩ ma ĩthaũ yĩu, na kwoou nĩwendaa eyumye vyũ ũndũ vatonyeka. Ĩndĩ esie kwasya: "O kavola kwa kavola nĩnambĩĩe kũlũmany'a na sukulu mũno kũte ũndũ nalũmanĩtye na Ngai. Kĩla mũthya wa kyumwa naendaa kũthaũka chess vandũ va kwĩka maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ. Kwoou nĩnatwie kuma timũnĩ ĩsu ya chess."—Mt. 6:33.
13. Kũlũmany'a na Ngai kũtũtetheeasya ata kũmina mathĩna ma mũsyĩ?
13 Mavinda amwe mũndũ no atuanĩwe elũmany'a na mũndũ wĩva wa mũsyĩ mũno kũte ũla ũngĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Ken aĩtye ũũ: "Nũndũ inyia wakwa nĩ mũkũũ, nĩnendie kwĩkalanga ngĩmwona, na o na nĩnendie okae kwĩkalanga naitũ mavinda kwa mavinda. Ĩndĩ inyia wakwa na kĩveti kyakwa mayeew'anaa. Nambie kwaĩwa nĩ nthĩ, nũndũ nakilasya neeka ũndũ nendeesye ũmwe ngatia ũla ũngĩ aũmĩĩte. Nĩvo ĩndĩ nesie kũmanya kana maũndũ mekala ũu, kĩveti kyakwa nĩkyo naaĩle kũlũmany'a nakyo mũno. Kwoou nĩnaĩsanie na mũtwe na namanya ũndũ naĩ ndonya kwĩka nĩ kana kĩveti kyakwa kĩw'e kĩ kĩanĩe." Nĩkwĩthĩwa Ken nĩwalũmanĩtye na Ngai na nĩwanengete Ndeto yake ndaĩa, nĩwakwatie ũkũmbaũ wa kũtavya kĩveti kyake nĩkĩ kyaaĩle kũkua inyia wake nesa. O na nĩwakwatie ũkũmbaũ wa kũelesya inyia wake nĩkĩ waaĩle kũnenga kĩveti kyake ndaĩa.—Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:24; 1 Akolintho 13:4, 5.
ĨLA TŨTANAELEEKA NESA KANA TWOOSWA NAĨ
14. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Saulo wakuie Yonathani naĩ?
14 Ĩla mũndũ mũna wĩ na ũkũmũ watũelewa naĩ, no wĩthĩwe wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũlũmany'a na Yeova. No kwĩthĩwa Yonathani akwatiwe nĩ thĩna ta ũsu. Mũsumbĩ Saulo, ũla waĩ mwĩtĩkĩsye mauta nĩ Ngai, nĩweesĩ kana mwanae aĩ ndũũ na Ndaviti, ĩndĩ ndakwatasya nĩkĩ. O na ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩwathatie mũno nginya amũtavya Yonathani ndeto syĩ nthoni mbee wa andũ. Ĩndĩ Yonathani ndaaĩkũlĩlya. Na vai mũthenya waaeka kũlũmany'a na Ngai kana Ndaviti, ũla wesaa kũtw'ĩka mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli.—1 Sam. 20:30-41.
15. Twaĩle kwĩka ata tũkesa kũkuwa naĩ nĩ mwana-a-asa?
15 Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwona ikundinĩ sya andũ ma Yeova kũte ũsili wa katĩ. Ĩndĩ ala matongoesye nĩ andũ me naĩ na mavinda amwe nĩmatonya kũtũelewa naĩ. (1 Sam. 1:13-17) Kwoou o na tũkaelya kwĩsa kũeleeka naĩ kana tũkoswa naĩ, nĩtwĩkalei tũlũmanĩtye na Yeova.
ĨLA WEETHĨA NO NGINYA TWĨYĨIME NĨ KANA TWĨANĨSYE WĨVĨTO WITŨ
16. Nĩ mavinda ta meva ũtonya kwĩthĩa no nginya twĩyĩime nĩ kana tũendeee kũlũmany'a na Ngai?
16 Saulo eekĩaa vinya Yonathani ekĩe kĩthito eosa ũsumbĩ nowe. (1 Sam. 20:31) Ĩndĩ nũndũ Yonathani nĩwalũmanĩtye na Ngai, nĩweesĩ kavaa akatuma ndũũ na Ndaviti vandũ va kwĩyosea ũsumbĩ. O naitũ no tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ĩsu ya Yonathani ya kwĩyĩima maũndũ ethĩwa tũkekalaa tũlilikene kana Yeova endete mũndũ "ũla wĩanĩasya wĩvĩto wake o na ethĩwa vailyĩ ata." (Sav. 15:4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Yonathani 'nĩweanĩisye wĩvĩto' ũla weevĩtĩe Ndaviti. O ta ũu naitũ no nginya tũkeanĩasya maũndũ ala twĩvĩtĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũtonya kũandĩkana na mũndũ maũndũ ma viasala, ĩndĩ maũndũ maialyũka ũyĩthĩa nĩ vinya kwĩanĩsya ũndũ twĩĩw'anĩte. Ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Ngai na nĩtũnengete Mbivilia ndaĩa, no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito twĩanĩsye wĩvĩto witũ. Nao nata mũtwaano witũ ũkalika mathĩna tũtaasũanĩa kana nĩtwĩsa kũmona? Nũndũ nĩtwendete Ngai, tũkekala tũlũmanĩtye na ũla tũtwaanĩte nake.—Soma Malaki 2:13-16.
17. Ĩsomo yĩĩ yaũtetheesya ata?
17 Ĩla twasũanĩa ũndũ Yonathani walũmanĩtye na Ngai, tyo twĩw'aa twenda kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake? Tũikaaende kwĩkaa mawendi maitũ mbee. Na ĩndĩ o tondũ Yonathani weekaa, nĩtwonany'e vyũ kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Yeova kwa kũlũmany'a na andũ make, o na ala matũvĩtĩsya. Twalũmany'a na Yeova o na ĩla maũndũ metu, nĩtũtanĩthasya ngoo yake, na kĩu nĩkĩtumaa twĩkala twĩ eanĩe vyũ. (Nth. 27:11) O na ĩngĩ, twekala tũlũmanĩtye na Yeova tũkoonaa ũndũ waĩlasya maũndũ onthe kwondũ wa ala mamwendete. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩeleetye maũndũ ma vata ala tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya twasisya andũ angĩ matwĩe ĩvinda ya Ndaviti. Amwe ma asu nĩmalũmanĩtye na Ngai na angĩ mayalũmanĩtye nake.

translation:
"Jehovah remembers both your kindness and my kindness to you, forever and ever."—1 SAM. 20:42.
FOOTNOTE: 43, 31
1, 2. How does the friendship between Jonathan and David stand out among human friendships?
WHEN David killed the Philistine named Goliath, young Jonathan showed his loyalty when he made a covenant with David, although David was a commoner. Because of this covenant, David was spared by Saul, the king of Israel, who wanted to kill him, and David became his "son." (1 Sam. 17:57) And Jonathan readily gave David his princely robe. This indicated that God was with David, and because of his loving-kindness, "the soul of Jonathan stuck to the soul of David." Also, "Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself." (1 Sam. 18:1-3) Over time, Jonathan continued to show his loyalty to David.
2 Jonathan sought to help David, and God supported David in becoming king of Israel in place of Saul. That is why he tried to find out what Saul intended to do to David. On one occasion, he warned David about Saul's plan to kill him while the men stationed at Ramah were unaware. But David learned that Jonathan had protected him, so he said that Jonathan was like an angel of God. He said: "It is good; . . . you will become king over Israel, and I will be second to you."—1 Sam. 23:16, 17.
3. What motivated Jonathan to continue helping David, and what can we learn from this? (See paragraph 21.)
3 Often we are influenced by others when making decisions. For example, we may have been influenced by Jonathan to support David, but the main reason we should want to do so is because we want to support those who support God. Do you think Jonathan wanted to see how David would act toward him? Certainly, but Jonathan's primary motivation was his desire to honor God. And that is why he helped David. He also expressed his confidence in Jehovah by saying: "Jehovah is my witness, and your father's witness, that between me and you there is a sworn covenant."—1 Sam. 20:42.
4. (a) Why is it important for us to examine our motives? (b) What will help us to do so?
4 As Christians, we strive to live in harmony with God's principles. We show love to our brothers and sisters, our families, and fellow humans. (1 Thess. 2:10, 11) But how can we make sure our motive is pure? By being honest with ourselves! (Prov. 4:11) Remember, we are accountable to God for our motives. If we honestly examine our hearts, we will be able to correct any wrong tendencies. This lesson will help us learn from Jonathan's example how to strengthen our relationship with Jehovah: (1) show genuine interest in someone and appreciate his qualities, (2) be convinced of what is right, (3) be willing to take risks, and (4) be ready to forgive if we are wronged.
LET US EXAMINE OURSELVES TO SEE IF WE ARE INTERESTED IN SOMEONE AND APPRECIATE HIS QUALITIES
5. Why did the Israelites often fail to support God despite their initial willingness?
5 Saul, Jonathan's father, was initially favored by God because he was courageous, but when he disobeyed God, God rejected him. (1 Sam. 15:17-23) However, God showed him mercy and explained why he rejected him—because he did not fully obey God's command. This shows us that maintaining a good standing with God requires more than just having good intentions; it means doing what He says is "God's way." —1 Chron. 29:23.
6. What shows that Jonathan was loyal to Jehovah?
6 After Saul displeased God, his son Jonathan wondered whether he too had displeased Jehovah. (1 Sam. 13:13, 14) The prophet Samuel explained: "Jehovah has firmly chosen your king." (1 Sam. 12:22) Jonathan realized this when he saw that his father intended to offer a sacrifice contrary to Jehovah's law. At that time, there were about 30,000 Israelite foot soldiers and 600 men with Saul and Jonathan! Yet, Jonathan went to the Philistine camp, accompanied only by his armor bearer. His armor bearer said: "There is no restraint with Jehovah to save by many or by few." Jonathan proved his faith by saying to his armor bearer: "Go and see what the Philistines are doing," and then he added: "It may be that Jehovah will act for us." The lot fell favorably for them, indicating Jehovah's approval. The Philistines heard this and became anxious. As a result, Jonathan saved Israel.—1 Sam. 13:5, 15, 22; 14:1, 2, 6, 14, 15, 20.
7. Did Jonathan show courage?
7 Because Saul was displeased with Jehovah, Jonathan showed courage to find out what Jehovah wanted him to do. For example, he went with his armor bearer to spy on the Philistines.—1 Sam. 31:1, 2.
8, 9. How can we know if our conscience is properly trained so that we please God?
8 We should imitate Jonathan. We should examine ourselves to see if we are pleasing Jehovah by carefully considering Bible principles, because God wants us to do so. We should do this especially when we face a difficult decision. For instance, a young brother might feel pressured to engage in wrongdoing, but if he has trained his conscience, he will remember the principle that "bad associations spoil good habits." (Read Romans 13:1, 2.) This is just one way we can examine ourselves to see if we are pleasing Jehovah by making decisions that honor Him.—1 Ac. 11:3; Heb. 13:17.
9 One sister named Olga [1] from La Paz, Bolivia, pleased God by listening to her conscience, even when it was difficult. For many years, her husband mistreated her physically and emotionally. She endured insults, beatings, and verbal abuse, and she felt helpless. Olga prayed earnestly. She decided to do whatever was necessary to maintain her integrity. For example, she rebuked him, refused to cook for him, and stopped associating with his relatives. (Rom. 12:17) And despite the difficulties, she continued to support her husband in some ways, such as helping him to care for his family. In time, her husband changed. Olga realized that she had been able to endure everything because she had kept her heart focused on Jehovah. For example, when her husband came home drunk and started causing trouble, Olga would calmly reason with him and encourage him to think about the consequences of his actions. (Prov. 12:17) Also, she often spoke kindly to him and helped him to see how his behavior affected others. Eventually, her husband enrolled in a rehabilitation program, and Olga supported him throughout his recovery. After many years, her husband expressed gratitude for her patience and love. This sister now serves as an elder in the congregation, and she uses her experience to help others.—1 Pet. 3:1.
HOW WE CAN REMAIN LOYAL TO JEHOVAH
10 How did Jonathan show that he was loyal to David?
10 Although Saul tried hard to kill David, Jonathan remained loyal to him. And Jonathan made a covenant with David, and he went to great lengths to protect him. He believed that God was with David and not with Saul. So Jonathan risked his life to warn David of Saul's schemes. That is why David was able to escape, and because of Jonathan's loyalty, David was able to survive Saul's attempts to kill him.—Read 1 Samuel 19:1-6.
11, 12. How does loving God motivate us to be loyal to him?
11 A sister named Alice from Australia decided to remain loyal to Jehovah, and she found that it helped her to be loyal to other Christians too. But when she began studying the Bible with others, they often raised objections. She says: "I used to feel bad when people rejected my efforts, especially around Christmas time. However, I realized that if I wanted to please Jehovah, I needed to put his standards first, even if it meant being unpopular. Because of this, Alice continued preaching. Alice explains: "My mother always taught me to love Jehovah and his Son. I grew up knowing that being different from others was important. And I learned that Jehovah and his Son are the ones who give us real value in life." And so she has been strengthened by that conviction.—Matt. 10:37.
12 We can show our loyalty to Jehovah by prioritizing spiritual activities—personal study, school, congregation meetings—and by making sure those activities help us draw closer to him. For example, a brother named Henry enjoyed playing chess. His school allowed him to compete in chess tournaments, and he became quite good at it. He admits: "I started to think that my identity was wrapped up in being good at chess. I would spend hours practicing, and I felt that my success depended on my ability to win. But then I realized: 'I am becoming more focused on chess than on pleasing Jehovah.' I began to use my chess skills to preach to people at school, sharing what I had learned from the Bible. And I joined a chess club so that I could meet new people and share the truth with them."—Matt. 6:33.
13 How does remaining loyal to Jehovah benefit us greatly?
13 Sometimes we may be tempted to become overly attached to someone who serves Jehovah. For instance, a brother named Ken said: "My father was very strict, and I wanted to please him, and I also wanted to impress my friends. I thought that if I did well in sports, my father would be proud of me. I always tried to excel, and I often put a lot of pressure on myself. I felt that my value came from what I accomplished. So I constantly sought approval from others, and I wondered if they were pleased with me. I realized that I needed to focus on pleasing Jehovah first and foremost. Then I began to appreciate that my relationship with Jehovah was more important than anyone else's opinion. I learned to rely on his guidance and to seek his approval rather than trying to earn the approval of others."—Ken remained loyal to Jehovah and continued to support his parents, but he made sure that his priority was to please Jehovah. And he learned to value himself based on Jehovah's standards.—Read Proverbs 2:24; 1 Corinthians 13:4, 5.
ARE WE STAYING LOYAL OR BEING SWAYED?
14 Why did Saul try to harm Jonathan?
14 But a person who has true understanding will not let the opinions of others influence his loyalty to Jehovah. It seems that Jonathan was deeply affected by his father's attitude. Saul, who had been chosen by God, became jealous because his son showed affection for David. He feared that David might take over the kingdom. And he allowed his jealousy to motivate him to mistreat Jonathan cruelly. Jonathan remained loyal. Yet, despite his efforts to reason with Saul and with David, Saul refused to listen to anyone.—1 Sam. 20:30-41.
15 How can we make sure that we remain loyal?
15 It is vital to cultivate strong love for our brothers and sisters. We can learn from examples of those who have shown loyalty under difficult circumstances. (1 Sam. 1:13-17) Also, whether we feel encouraged or discouraged, we should continue to strengthen our relationship with Jehovah.
BUT TEST YOURSELF TO SEE IF YOU ARE HOLDING FAST
16 What questions can help us determine if we are remaining loyal and continuing to serve Jehovah?
16 Saul made a vow that would affect Jonathan severely. (1 Sam. 20:31) However, because Jonathan was loyal to Jehovah, he felt compelled to warn David and help him escape. Let us examine the example of Jonathan and ask ourselves if we would be willing to risk our comfort and security to stand up for what is right, even if it meant displeasing people. (Ps. 15:4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Jonathan 'held fast' to his loyalty to David. Similarly, we need to examine our own conduct. For instance, we may avoid associating with someone who is practicing serious sin, yet we may still enjoy listening to stories about his exploits. But if we are loyal to Jehovah and carefully study the Bible, we will be able to maintain integrity and hold fast to our loyalty. So let us not allow our personal feelings to cause us to compromise.—Read Malachi 2:13-16.
17 What lesson can we learn from this?
17 If we appreciate how Jonathan showed loyalty to Jehovah, will we not strive to imitate his example? We should regularly review our priorities. And just as Jonathan did, we want to please Jehovah by being loyal to His organization and by supporting his faithful servants. Our loyalty to Jehovah and our willingness to uphold his standards will bring us joy. (Prov. 27:11) Moreover, if we remain loyal to Jehovah, we will be able to discern what is truly important and will not be unduly influenced by the opinions of others. This lesson teaches us that we can benefit greatly by learning from the example of David and those who supported him. Some individuals are loyal to God, while others are disloyal to Him.

text:
"Mũĩkĩĩe Yeova, na ũkĩka ũseo; . . . na ũiĩsaa kĩthito kyake."—SAV. 37:3.
MBATHI: 49, 18
1. Yeova atũmbie twĩ na ũtonyi wa kwĩka maũndũ meva ma ũsengy'a?
YEOVA oomba mũndũ amũnengie ũtonyi wa kwĩka maũndũ ma ũsengy'o. Atũnengie kĩlĩko kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũmanye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ, na tũimanya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩvangĩĩa maũndũ. (Nth. 2:11) Nĩwatũnengie ũtonyi wa kwĩanĩsya mĩvango ĩla tweeka, na kwoou no twĩkĩe kĩthito tũkeanĩsya maũndũ maseo ala twĩvangĩĩe. (Avi. 2:13) O na atũmbie twĩ na wasya wa ngoo ũtũtetheesye kũvathũkany'a ũseo na ũthũku. Wasya ũsu nũtũsiĩĩaa tũikese kwĩlikya ũthũkunĩ, na ĩla twavĩtya nũtũtetheeasya tũkelũnga.—Alo. 2:15.
2. We Yeova endaa tũtũmĩe ũtonyi witũ ata?
2 Yeova endaa tũtũmĩe nesa ũtonyi w'onthe ũla watũnengie. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ nũtwendete na we mwene nĩwĩsĩ kana twatũmĩa ũtonyi witũ nesa twĩkalaa twĩ eanĩe. O na nũkindĩlĩĩle Ndetonĩ yake kana nũseo tũkatũmĩaa ũtonyi witũ nesa. Kwa ngelekany'o, Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩevelania tũsomaa kana "mosũanĩo ma ala athingu maelete wingĩnĩ wa syĩndũ," na kana "o ũla kw'oko kwaku kwona wa kwĩka, ĩka na vinya waku." (Nth. 21:5; Mũta. 9:10) Namo Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto matwĩĩte kana "o ũndũ twĩĩthĩwa na ũthei, twĩkei andũ onthe nesa," na makasyoka makatwĩa o "ũndũ kĩla mũndũ wosie mũthĩnzĩo, thũkũmanai ene kwa ene." (Aka. 6:10; 1 Vet. 4:10) Kwoou vai nzika kana Yeova endaa twĩke kyonthe kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana twĩtethye na tũitethya ala angĩ.
3. Nĩ maũndũ meva mũndũ ũteka?
3 O na kau Yeova nĩwendaa tũtũmĩe ũtonyi ũla watũmbie naw'o, nĩwĩsĩ ve maũndũ tũteka. Nĩwĩsĩ kana tũyĩsa kwĩvetea mawonzu maitũ, naĩ, na kĩkw'ũ. O na nĩwĩsĩ tũyĩsa kũtw'ĩĩa ala angĩ kĩla mekwĩka, nũndũ kĩla mũndũ e ũthasyo wa kũnyuva kĩla ũkwenda. (1 Asu. 8:46) O na twĩthĩwe na ũmanyi kana ũĩ wĩana ata, kĩla ĩvinda tũkeethĩawa tũilyĩ o ta syana twaelekanw'a na Yeova.—Isa. 55:9.
4. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
4 Kĩla ĩvinda o na kwĩthĩwe nĩ ĩndĩĩ, twaĩlĩte kũmwĩkwatasya Yeova atũtongoesye, na aitũtw'ĩĩka na kũtũtetheesya kũla tũtetonya. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, ĩla ve na thĩna twaĩlĩte kwĩkaa kyonthe kĩla tũtonya twĩtetheesye na tũitetheesya angĩ. (Soma Savuli 37:3.) Kwa ũkuvĩ twaĩlĩte kwĩka maũndũ aa elĩ: 'Kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova, na kwĩka ũseo.' Twĩ na kĩu, ekai twone twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ twasũanĩa ngewa ya Noa, Ndaviti, na athũkũmi angĩ ma Ngai. Asu onthe nĩmamũĩkĩĩe Yeova na nĩmeekie kĩla maĩ matonya. O tondũ tũũsoma twone, andũ asu nĩmasyaasya makamanya kĩla mataĩ matonya kwĩka na kĩla maĩ matonya kwĩka, na ĩndĩ mamanya mayosa ĩtambya yĩla yaĩlĩte.
ĨLA ŨTHŨKU WAINGĨVA
5. Elesya ũndũ ũmwe Noa wakomanie naw'o.
5 Nthĩ ĩla Noa watwĩe "yausũĩte ũng'endu" na mĩkalĩle mĩthũku. (Mwa. 6:4, 9-13) Nĩweesĩ kana ĩvinda yĩkavika Yeova anange nthĩ ĩsu nthũku. Ĩndĩ o na Noa esĩ oou, ndalea kwĩthĩwa athĩnĩkaa vyũ oona andũ mayĩka maũndũ asu matoosanĩte na kwenda kwa Ngai. Ĩla kwaendie ũu, Noa nĩwamanyie kana ve maũndũ amwe waĩ atonya kwĩka na angĩ waĩ atatonya kwĩka.
6, 7. (a) Nĩ kyaũ Noa ũtaĩ atonya kwĩka? (b) Ngewa ya Noa ĩtũkonetye ata?
6 Kĩla Noa ũtaĩ atonya kwĩka: O na kau Noa aĩ mũĩkĩĩku wĩanĩ wake wa kũtavya andũ ũtũmane wa Yeova, ndaĩ atonya kũlasimĩthya ala athũku metĩkĩlane na ndeto sya Yeova, na ndaĩ esa kũkalaatanga mbua ĩla yathanĩtwe. Kwoou kĩla waĩ atonya kwĩka no kũmwĩkwatya Yeova eanĩsye watho wake wa kũvetanga ala athũku, na ayĩkala ate na nzika kana Yeova akoosa ĩtambya yĩu ĩvindanĩ o yĩla yaĩlĩte.—Mwa. 6:17.
7 O naitũ tũtwĩe nthĩ yusũĩte ũthũku, na nĩtwĩsĩ kana Yeova aĩtye ndakalea kũmyananga. (1 Yoa. 2:17) Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kana tũyĩsa kũlasimĩthya andũ metĩkĩle ũla 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ.' Na vai ũndũ twĩka tũkakalaatanga ũla "thĩna mũnene." (Mt. 24:14, 21) Kwoou twĩ na vata wa kwĩkala na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu o ta Noa, tũte na nzika kana o mĩtũkĩ Ngai nũkwosa ĩtambya. (Sav. 37:10, 11) Nĩtwĩsĩ nesa ki kana Yeova oona ĩvinda nĩyavika ya kwananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku, ndakaeka mũthenya o na ũmwe ũvĩtũke.—Ava. 2:3.
8. Elesya ũndũ Noa watatie mũno eke kĩla waĩ atonya kwĩka. (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 7.)
8 Kĩla Noa waĩ atonya kwĩka: Noa ndaakw'a ngoo nũndũ wa kĩla ũtaĩ atonya kwĩka, vandũ va ũu atatie mũno eke kĩla waĩ atonya kwĩka. Noa nĩwatavisye andũ ũkany'o ũla wanengetwe, na aĩ mũĩkĩĩku wĩanĩ ũsu e ta "mũtavan'ya wa ũlũngalu." (2 Vet. 2:5) Nĩtwĩsĩ kwĩka ũu nĩkwatumie ekala e na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Na eka wĩa wa kũtavany'a, nĩwatũmĩie vinya ũla waĩ naw'o vamwe na kĩlĩko kyake nĩ kana ake ngalawa ĩla Ngai wamwĩĩte nĩ ake.—Soma Aevelania 11:7.
9. Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Noa ata?
9 O ta Noa, nĩtũtataa 'kũthangaa mũno wĩanĩ wa Mwĩaĩi.' (1 Ako. 15:58) Maũndũ amwe twĩkaa wĩanĩ ũsu nĩ ta kwaka na kũtũngĩĩa kũla tũthaithĩaa, kwĩyumya tũtetheesye maũmbanonĩ manene, kana kũtethya mawĩa ala tũaĩwe ovisinĩ wa ũvonge kana ovisinĩ wa ũalyũli. Na ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ twĩkaa nĩ kũthangaaĩa wĩa wa kũtavany'a, twĩsĩ kana wĩa ũsu nũtumaa twĩkala tũte na nzika na wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩthĩĩtwe e mũĩkĩĩku aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩla watavya angĩ moathimo ala Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkatũetee, nĩw'o ũmanyaa kana vai wĩkwatyo me naw'o o na ũmwe. Mo monaa vai kĩndũ kĩkesa kũmataanany'a na mathĩna moo." Kwoou nĩ w'o kana kũtavany'a nĩkũlũlũmĩlasya wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o wa ĩvinda yũkĩte, vamwe na ũtwi witũ wa kũendeea kũsemba ũkĩlany'onĩ wa thayũ tũte kũnoa.—1 Ako. 9:24.
ĨLA TWEEKA NAĨ
10. Elesya maũndũ ala mamũkwatie Ndaviti.
10 Yeova aisye kana Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti aĩ "mũndũ wendeeasya ngoo [yake]." (Meko 13:22) Ndaviti aĩ mũndũ mũĩkĩĩku. Ĩndĩ o na e mũĩkĩĩku oou, ve mavinda weekie naĩ ngito. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩweekie ũlaalai na Mbathi-sieva. Kũthũkya maũndũ nĩwavangie Ulia, mũũme wa Mbathi-sieva, oaĩwe kaũnĩ nĩ kana naĩ ĩsu ndĩkaumĩle. O na Ndaviti anengie Ulia valũa ũla woonanĩtye ũndũ we mwene waĩle kũawa ekuĩe! (2 Sam. 11:1-21) Ĩndĩ kũvitha kwake kwaĩ kwa mana nũndũ naĩ isu syake nĩsyaumbũkie. (Mko. 4:22) Ndaviti eekie ata ĩla kwaendie ũu?
11, 12. (a) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva Ndaviti ũtaĩ atonya kwĩka amina kũvĩtya? (b) Ĩla tweelila nũndũ wa naĩ twĩkĩte, nĩ ũndũ wĩva tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova nũkũtwĩka?
11 Kĩla Ndaviti ũtaĩ atonya kwĩka: Ndaviti ndaĩ atonya kũtũnga maũndũ na ĩtina akatw'ĩka ndekĩte naĩ. Na vai ũndũ waĩ eka ndakakwatwe nĩ mathĩna ala maetiwe nĩ naĩ syake. O na mathĩna amwe mamũnyamaisye nginya ĩla wesie kũkw'a. (2 Sam. 12:10-12, 14) Kwoou aĩ na vata wa mũĩkĩĩo. Aĩ no nginya aĩkĩĩe kana nũndũ nĩwaĩ aneelila vyũ, Yeova nĩwesaa kũmũekea na aimũtetheesya omĩĩsye mathĩna asu mamũkwatie nũndũ wa naĩ syake.
12 Ithyonthe nĩtũvĩtasya nũndũ twĩ andũ me naĩ. Mavĩtyo amwe twĩkaa nĩ maito kũte angĩ. Na mavinda angĩ vai ũndũ twĩka tũkavuta naĩ ĩla twĩkĩte. Wĩthĩaa no nginya tũmĩanĩsye na mathĩna ala makaetwe nĩ naĩ ĩsu. (Aka. 6:7) Ĩndĩ nĩtũĩkĩĩaa Ngai vyũ tũkamanya kana tweelila, akatũkwata mbau ĩvindanĩ ya mathĩna o na ethĩwa no ithyĩ twĩyĩetee mathĩna asu.—Soma Isaia 1:18, 19; Meko ma Atũmwa 3:19.
13. Ndaviti eekie ata atũngĩĩa ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova?
13 Kĩla Ndaviti waĩ atonya kwĩka: Ndaviti nĩwendaa kũtũngĩĩa ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova na kwoou nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlilye amũtetheesye kwĩka ũu. Ũndũ ũmwe weekie oonany'a nĩweetĩkĩlĩtye Yeova amũtetheesye waĩ kwĩtĩkĩla kũlũngwa nĩ mwathani wake, Nathani. (2 Sam. 12:13) O na ĩngĩ Ndaviti nĩwavoyie aumbũla naĩ syake na amũtavya Yeova ĩũlũ wa wendi ũla waĩ naw'o wa kuma ngoonĩ wa kũtũngĩĩa ngwatanĩo ĩla waĩ nayo vamwe nake. (Sav. 51:1-17) Ndaviti ndaaeka mĩlilo ĩmũnyite wĩthĩe ndasonga. Ĩndĩ naĩ syake nĩsyatumie evũnya kũtũ. Ndaasyoka kwĩka naĩ ngito ta isu ĩngĩ. Ĩtina wa myaka mingĩ nĩwakwie e mũĩkĩĩku, na Yeova ndakolwa o na vanini nĩ ũĩkĩĩku ũsu wa Ndaviti.—Aevl. 11:32-34.
14. Ngelekany'o ya Ndaviti yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
14 Ngelekany'o ya Ndaviti yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Twĩĩmanyĩsya kana ĩla tweeka naĩ ngito nĩtwaĩle kwĩlila kuma ngoonĩ na tũyĩtya Yeova ũekeo. No nginya tũmumbũlĩle naĩ sitũ. (1 Yoa. 1:9) O na ĩngĩ nĩtwaĩle kũmona atumĩa nĩ kana matũtetheesye kũtũngĩĩa ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova. (Soma Yakovo 5:14-16.) Ĩla tweetĩkĩla Yeova atũtetheesye, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana nũkũtũekea o tondũ ũtwathĩte. Ĩtina wa ũu nũseo tũkatata tũikasyokee mavĩtyo maitũ, na nũseo tũkaendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova, na tũiendeea kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.—Aevl. 12:12, 13.
MAWETU ANGĨ
15. Ngelekany'o ya Aana yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
15 No kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa athũkũmi angĩ ma Yeova ma tene ala mamwĩkwatisye vyũ na meeka kĩla maĩ matonya ĩla makwatiwe nĩ mawetu. Kwa ngelekany'o, Aana ndaĩ atonya kwĩminĩa thĩna ũla waĩ naw'o wa kwĩthĩwa atakwata mwana. Ĩndĩ aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova nũkũmũkiakisya, na kwoou nĩwaendeeie kũthaithĩa yĩla ĩeemanĩ na kũmũtulũĩla Yeova kyonthe kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ yake. (1 Sam. 1:9-11) Ĩsu nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ta kĩ! Ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna ma mwĩĩ kana o mawetu angĩ tũte na vinya wa kũmamina, nĩtwaĩle kũmwiĩa Yeova kwĩmakĩa kwitũ kw'onthe, twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana akatũsũvĩa. (1 Vet. 5:6, 7) O na nĩtwaĩle kwĩka kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana tũtetheke nĩ maũmbano maitũ na syĩndũ ingĩ ila ũseũvyo wa Yeova ũtũnengae.—Aevl. 10:24, 25.
16. Ngelekany'o ya Samueli ĩtonya kũmanyĩsya asyai kyaũ?
16 Nao nata ethĩwa asyai nĩ aĩkĩĩku ĩndĩ syana syoo nĩsyatiie ũla w'o? Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Samueli. Ĩla imwana syake syatw'ĩkie andũ aima ndaĩ atonya kũilasimĩthya iendeee kũatĩĩa maũndũ malũngalu ala waimanyĩĩtye. (1 Sam. 8:1-3) Aĩ no nginya aie ũndũ ũsu mokonĩ ma Yeova. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, Samueli aĩ atonya kũendeea kwĩkala e mũĩkĩĩku na aimũtanĩthya Ĩthe wake wa ĩtunĩ, Yeova. (Nth. 27:11) O na ũmũnthĩ asyai amwe Aklĩsto nĩmakwatawa nĩ ũndũ ta ũsu. Asyai asu nĩmethĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo kana o ta ũla ĩthe wa mwana kĩmaamai, Yeova nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye kũmathokya eki ma naĩ ĩla meelila mamũsyokee. (Luka 15:20) Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu asyai asu nĩmekĩaa kĩthito mekale malũmanĩtye na Yeova, me na wĩkwatyo wa kana ngelekany'o yoo nĩkũtetheesya syana syoo isyoke ĩĩthyanĩ.
17. Nĩkĩ ngelekany'o ya ĩla ndiwa ngya ĩkũtwĩkĩa vinya?
17 O na ĩngĩ kwasũanĩa ĩla ndiwa ngya ya ĩvinda ya Yesũ. (Soma Luka 21:1-4.) Mũndũ mũka ũsu ndaĩ esa kwĩka ũndũ akamina ũlũsani ũla watwaĩĩaw'a ĩkalũnĩ. (Mt. 21:12, 13) Na no kwĩthĩwa vate ũndũ waĩ eka akamina ũkya ũla waĩ naw'o. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, nĩwaumisye na ngoo ya kwenda "tũwela twĩlĩ," tũla nĩtw'o twaĩ 'wĩkwatyo w'onthe wa thayũ ũla waĩ naw'o.' Mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwoonanisye kana nĩwamũĩkĩĩe Yeova na ngoo yake yonthe esĩ kana eeka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva mbee, akamwĩanĩĩsya mavata make ma kĩ-mwĩĩ. Mũĩkĩĩo ũsu wake nĩwatumie akwata mbau mũvango wa ũthaithi wa w'o ũla waĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ yĩu. O naitũ twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana twamantha Ũsumbĩ mbee, Yeova akaĩkĩĩthasya nĩtwakwata kĩla twĩ na vata nakyo.—Mt. 6:33.
18. Nengane ngelekany'o ya mũthũkũmi ũmwe wa Yeova waĩ na woni waĩlĩte.
18 O ta ũu, athaithi aingĩ ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ nĩmonanĩtye kana nĩmamũĩkĩĩe Yeova kwa kwĩka kĩla matonya vandũ va kũtindĩanĩa na kĩla matatonya. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Malcolm, ũla walũmanilye na Yeova nginya ĩla wakwie mwakanĩ wa 2015. Myakanĩ ĩla wathũkũmie Yeova e na kĩveti kyake, maĩ na mavinda ma kũtheka na mavinda ma kũĩa. Malcolm aisye ũũ: "Mavinda angĩ thayũ ũũ ti wa kwĩkwatw'a, na ndũmanyaa ũnĩ kwĩthi ata, na eka ũu, maũndũ nĩmesaa kweta vyũ. Ĩndĩ Yeova nũathimaa ala mamwĩkwatasya." Kwoou we mwana-a-asa ũsu anenganie ũtao wĩva? Aisye ũũ: "Voya ũkwate mosyao maingĩ ũndũ ũtonya na wĩthĩwe na kĩthito kingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova. Ĩkaa maũndũ ala ũtonya na ndũkatindĩanĩe na ala ũtatonya." *
19. (a) Nĩkĩ ĩandĩko yitũ ya mwaka wa 2017 nĩ ĩandĩko yaĩlĩte vyũ? (b) We mwene ũtonya kũtũmĩa ata ĩandĩko ya mwaka wa 2017?
19 Nũndũ mĩthenya ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo ĩendeee "kwongeleka kũthũka," no nginya twĩkalae tweteele kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna maingangĩ. (2 Tim. 3:1, 13) Kwoou twĩ na vata mũnene vyũ kwĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva wa kwĩkĩa kĩthito tũikaminwe vinya nĩ mathĩna ta asu. Twĩ na vata wa kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana tũmũĩkĩĩe Yeova mũnango na tũyĩkaa kĩla tũtonya. Kwoou ĩandĩko yĩĩ yĩnyuvĩtwe kwondũ wa mwaka wa 2017 nĩ ĩandĩko yaĩlĩte vyũ: "Mũĩkĩĩe Yeova, na ũkĩka ũseo."—Sav. 37:3.
Ĩandĩko yitũ ya 2017: "Mũĩkĩĩe Yeova, na Ũkĩka Ũseo."

translation:
"Praise Jehovah, and exalt him; . . . and show forth his loving-kindness."—PS. 37:3.
FOOTNOTE: 49, 18
1. Does Jehovah comfort us with the assurance that he cares for our concerns?
JEHOVAH wants people to be assured that he cares for their concerns. He assures us that he will help us to discern what is important and what is not, and to appreciate what we have. (Phil. 2:11) He helps us to be content with the standards that we have, and to know that we can trust him to provide what we need. (Prov. 2:13) And he comforts us with the hope that he will help us to cope with sorrow and adversity. This hope enables us to remain courageous, and when we stumble, he helps us to get back on our feet.—Hos. 2:15.
2. How does Jehovah empower us to use our discernment?
2 Jehovah empowers us by giving us holy spirit. Why? Because his spirit helps us to make good decisions and to use our discernment effectively. And because we value his guidance, we are more likely to use our discernment wisely. For example, the Bible tells us that "senseless ones meet with ruin," and that "one who is quick to anger acts foolishly." (Prov. 21:5; Matt. 9:10) Also, the Christian Greek Scriptures state that "whatever things we ask in prayer, let us be content with them," and they urge us to "be generous and ready to share."—Acts 6:10; 1 Pet. 4:10. Thus, we can see that Jehovah wants us to use all the discernment we have and to speak and act thoughtfully.
3. What matters most to a person?
3 And since Jehovah desires that we use the discernment he gives us, it means that what matters to him is not what we possess. It does not mean that we should disregard our needs, of course, nor should we be materialistic. But it does mean that we should not become overly concerned about acquiring possessions, letting such concerns overshadow our spirituality. (1 Tim. 8:46) And even though we may gain knowledge, we must remember that true wisdom comes from Jehovah.—Isa. 55:9.
4. What will help us to succeed?
4 Every day, and especially when faced with difficulties, we need to strengthen our faith in Jehovah, who guides us and comforts us so that we can cope. Difficulties often come unexpectedly, but they give us an opportunity to demonstrate our loyalty and devotion. (Read Psalm 37:3.) To do this, we must always keep in mind the principle: "Trust in Jehovah, and do what is right." Let us learn lessons from faithful men like Noah, David, and others whom God approved. Timothy also trusted in Jehovah and conducted himself well. So let us continue to study and imitate those who have shown exemplary faith and zeal.
LET US BE PRACTICAL
5. Consider one example of how Noah showed his faith.
5 Indeed, Noah preached about "righteousness" for many years. (Gen. 6:4, 9-13) He did so despite knowing that people would reject his message. Like Noah, we too may encounter people who do not want to listen to us or who oppose God's standards. But Noah knew which things were pleasing to God and which were displeasing.
6, 7. (a) What helped Noah to remain steadfast? (b) How does Noah's example benefit us?
6 Noah remained steadfast because he was a devoted worshiper of Jehovah, and he strove to live according to God's righteous standards. He kept himself separate from the wicked people around him and obeyed God's commands. This helped him to maintain a good relationship with Jehovah and to be confident that God would fulfill his promises.—Gen. 6:17.
7 We also face a world that does not value righteousness, and we know that Jehovah allows this state of affairs to continue. (1 John 2:17) So we strive to live according to God's standards and to proclaim the good news of the Kingdom, even though others may view our work as foolish. (Matt. 24:14, 21) By doing so, we show that we are determined to remain loyal to God, and we can be assured that he will support us.—Ps. 37:10, 11. We are also reminded that Jehovah has set a time limit for allowing wickedness to flourish, and he will soon take action.—Acts 2:3.
8 Consider what Noah accomplished through his faithfulness. (See accompanying box on page 7.)
8 Noah was faithful despite everything that people said and did. He warned them about the coming flood, but they paid no attention. Noah preached to those who were ungodly, and he became "an heir of righteousness." (2 Pet. 2:5) Let us imitate him in being courageous and steadfast. And like Noah, let us use the time we have left to warn others and to help them find refuge in Jehovah.—Read Hebrews 11:7.
9 How can we strengthen our faith like Noah's?
9 Like Noah, we can show that we 'are walking with God.' (1 John 15:58) There are times when this means facing ridicule, enduring opposition, or resisting temptations. But whatever trials we face, we can be confident that Jehovah will give us strength to endure—the strength we need. A sister once said: "When I felt overwhelmed because of the pressures from Satan, I prayed earnestly to Jehovah, and I realized that I was not alone. I could see how his spirit helped me to cope." Truly, prayer strengthens us to remain steadfast and to continue preaching the good news.—1 Cor. 9:24.
LET US KEEP SPEAKING
10 What lessons can we learn from David?
10 Jehovah described King David as a man who was agreeable to His heart. (Acts 13:22) David was imperfect. Despite being a king, he made serious mistakes. For example, he committed adultery with Bathsheba. Because of his actions, things became very complicated. He also showed a lack of consideration for Uriah, Bathsheba's husband. (2 Sam. 11:1-21) As a result of his sin, David experienced much suffering. (Ps. 32:3, 4) How did David respond?
11, 12. (a) Why did David eventually regain Jehovah's approval? (b) What can we learn from this regarding our own imperfections and Jehovah's forgiveness?
11 David came to recognize: 'I have sinned against Jehovah.' And he understood that his sin was grievous in Jehovah's eyes. But he also realized that Jehovah was willing to show him mercy. (2 Sam. 12:10-12, 14) This demonstrates that even imperfect people can be forgiven. However, Jehovah expects them to acknowledge their wrongdoing and express genuine repentance.
12 Often, we too struggle with imperfections. We may find it difficult to forgive others. And sometimes we may feel overwhelmed when thinking about our own mistakes. But remember that Jehovah is understanding. He knows that we are imperfect and that we will make errors. (Gal. 6:7) So let us humbly appeal to God for forgiveness, and strive to avoid repeating those mistakes.—Read Isaiah 1:18, 19; Acts 3:19.
13. In what ways did David restore his relationship with Jehovah?
13 David came to realize: 'David earnestly desired to restore his relationship with Jehovah,' and Jehovah responded favorably to his repentance. One way Jehovah showed this was by sending Nathan to reprove him. (2 Sam. 12:13) Also, David prayed sincerely to Jehovah and begged Him to forgive his serious sin. (Ps. 51:1-17) David expressed deep regret and sorrow. He determined to live differently from then on. Over many years, he continued to serve Jehovah faithfully, and Jehovah remembered his past sins no longer.—Heb. 11:32-34.
14. What lessons does David's example teach us?
14 What lessons does David's example teach us? It teaches us that when we make mistakes, we should confess them to Jehovah and ask for forgiveness. And we should also be honest with others. (1 John 1:9) Furthermore, it reminds us that it is possible to maintain a good relationship with Jehovah even after making serious errors. (Read James 5:14-16.) If we trust that Jehovah will forgive us, we can face trials with courage and confidence, knowing that He supports us. Because of this, we can continue to improve our conduct, keep strengthening our love for Jehovah, and strive to please Him always.—Heb. 12:12, 13.
OUR HOPE
15. What lessons does Hannah's example teach us?
15 To remain spiritually strong, we need to imitate those faithful servants of Jehovah who faced difficulties but remained loyal. For instance, Hannah earnestly prayed for a son. She had faith that Jehovah would answer her prayers, and she continued to pray until He granted her request. (1 Sam. 1:9-11) This is a fine example for us! But what if we are struggling with emotional problems or feel overwhelmed by our burdens? We can pour out our heart to Jehovah in prayer, trusting that He will comfort us. (1 Pet. 5:6, 7) Also, we can be sure that Jehovah will help us cope with any challenges we may encounter as we endeavor to live according to His standards.—Heb. 10:24, 25.
16. What lessons can we learn from Samuel's example?
16 How did Samuel show faith when he was young? Consider Samuel's example. Although his mother dedicated him to Jehovah, she allowed him to grow up with her and continue serving at the tabernacle. (1 Sam. 8:1-3) He knew that everything belonged to Jehovah. And yet, Samuel continued to serve loyally at the tent of meeting, Jehovah's place of worship. (Prov. 27:11) Today, too, Christians face similar situations. Some may have a close relationship with their children and want to provide them with the best possible upbringing. Jehovah understands this desire and appreciates parents who lovingly train their children. (Luke 15:20) However, they must always put their relationship with Jehovah first and not allow family concerns to hinder their spiritual progress.
17. Why is it important to meditate on examples of faith?
17 By meditating on examples of faith, we can strengthen our own faith. For instance, consider Jesus' example. (Read Luke 21:1-4.) That man did not hesitate to expose wrongdoing, even when it meant facing opposition. (Matt. 21:12, 13) And he was willing to speak out about what he saw was right. So, like him, we should be zealous in proclaiming the good news and 'always ready to give a defense of the hope you have.' A faithful Christian will align his life with Jehovah's will and wholeheartedly support God's Kingdom, even if it means making sacrifices. His loyalty will move Jehovah to bless his efforts. We also need to prioritize spiritual pursuits, even if it means simplifying our lives.—Matt. 6:33.
18. What can we learn from the example of one of Jehovah's servants who remained loyal despite trials?
18 Indeed, many of Jehovah's servants have demonstrated courage and loyalty to Jehovah by enduring hardships and difficulties. For example, consider young brother Malcolm, who dedicated his life to Jehovah while still in his teens in 2015. Throughout his ministry, he faced challenges involving his health, family, and friends. Malcolm said: "I realized that my problems were nothing compared to what I could face, and because of this, I began to appreciate things more. With Jehovah's help, I felt able to cope." How did this young man maintain his zeal? He explained: "I focused on the many blessings I had and kept busy in the ministry. This helped me to stay positive and deal with my difficulties." *
19. (a) Why is the 2017 Yearbook particularly encouraging? (b) How can you benefit from reading the 2017 Yearbook?
19 As faithful Christians continue "to progress in faith," we need to remain vigilant so as not to be influenced by worldly thinking. (2 Tim. 3:1, 13) How can we strengthen our resolve to reject false teachings and uphold Bible principles? By remembering that our loyalty to Jehovah is tested when we face trials and difficulties. We can strengthen our resolve by focusing on how we can show our appreciation to Jehovah and by keeping active in spiritual activities. The 2017 Yearbook highlighted this point: "Be loyal to Jehovah, and keep seeking him."—Ps. 37:3.
The 2017 Yearbook: "Be Loyal to Jehovah, and Keep Seeking Him."

text:
"Mũĩkĩĩo nĩ . . . kĩla kĩĩkĩĩthasya maũndũ ala matonekaa." —AEVL. 11:1.
MBATHI: 54, 43
1. Twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wa Kĩklĩsto?
MŨĨKĨĨO wa Kĩklĩsto nĩ wa vata mũno. Ĩndĩ ti andũ onthe me mũĩkĩĩo ũsu. (2 Ath. 3:2) O na vailyĩ ũu, Yeova nũnengete kĩla ũmwe wa athaithi make 'kĩthimo kĩna kya mũĩkĩĩo.' (Alo. 12:3, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language; Aka. 5:22) Na kwoou, onthe ala me mũĩkĩĩo nĩmaĩle kũtũnga mũvea mũno.
2, 3. (a) Mũndũ wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ethĩawa atonya kũkwata moathimo meva? (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva?
2 Yesũ Klĩsto aisye kana Ĩthe wake wa ĩtunĩ nũkusasya andũ mamũthengeee kwĩsĩla vala ve Mwana wake. (Yoa. 6:44, 65) Mũndũ ambĩĩa kũmũĩkĩĩa Yesũ nĩwĩthĩawa atonya kũekewa naĩ syake. Ũu naw'o ũmũnengae mwanya wa kũtanĩa ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova tene na tene. (Alo. 6:23) Tweekie ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe twaĩlwe nĩ kũkwata ũathimo ũsu ũseũvĩte ũu? Nũndũ twĩ ene naĩ, kĩla kĩtwaĩle no kĩkw'ũ. (Sav. 103:10) Ĩndĩ ĩla Yeova watũsyaisye oonie kana nĩtũtonya kwĩka maũndũ maseo. Na kwoou nũndũ wa mumo wake, nĩwavingũie ngoo sitũ nĩ kana twĩw'e ũla ũvoo mũseo. Kuma vau nĩtwaambĩĩe kwonany'a kana nĩtũmũĩkĩĩe Yesũ, twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela.—Soma 1 Yoana 4:9, 10.
3 Ĩndĩ sũanĩa makũlyo aa: W'o mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kyaũ? Kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo no kwĩka kũmanya moathimo ala Ngai ũtwathĩte? Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ, twaĩle kwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo witũ kwa nzĩa syĩva?
'ĨTĨKĨLA NGOONĨ YAKU'
4. Elesya nĩkĩ mũndũ wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ti ũla wĩkĩte o kũelewa kĩeleelo kya Ngai.
4 Mũndũ wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nĩwĩthĩawa aeleetwe nĩ kĩeleelo kya Ngai, ĩndĩ ti ũu w'oka. Mũndũ ta ũsu ethĩawa na mea maingĩ mũno ma kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai. Kũĩkĩĩa nzĩa ĩla Ngai ũtũmĩaa nĩ kana etũtangĩĩa nĩkũtumaa mũndũ wĩ mũĩkĩĩo atavya angĩ ũvoo mũseo. Nĩkyo kĩtumi mũtũmwa Vaulo waeleisye ũndũ ũsu kwa nzĩa ĩno: 'Ethĩwa ũkamumbũla Yesũ na kanyw'a waku kana nĩwe Mwĩaĩi, na ũkeetĩkĩla ngoonĩ yaku kana Ngai nĩwamũthayũũkisye kũmumya akw'ũnĩ, ũkatangĩĩwa: Nũndũ mũndũ nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa na ngoo kũvikĩa ũlũngalu; na nĩwumbũlaa na kanyw'a kũvikĩa ũtangĩĩo.'—Alo. 10:9, 10; 2 Ako. 4:13.
5. Nĩkĩ mũĩkĩĩo nĩ wa vata mũno, na tũtonya kwĩka ata wĩkale wĩ mũlũmu? Nengane ngelekany'o.
5 Nĩtwĩsĩ nesa kana tũte na mũĩkĩĩo na tũtosete matambya ma kũũlũlũmĩlya, tũyĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla twathĩtwe nĩ Ngai. No tũelekany'e mũĩkĩĩo na mũtĩ mũvande. Mũtĩ nĩwaĩle kũng'ithw'a nĩ kana wĩane. Mũtĩ mũvande ndũtũaa vandũ vamwe ta mũtĩ wa kũseũvw'a. Wang'ithw'a nesa nũsanzamũkaa na ũyĩana, ĩndĩ ũkaa kĩw'ũ wĩka kũvoova. O na mũtĩ wĩĩendeee o nesa ũkaema kũng'ithw'a nesa, ũendeea naĩ nginya ũkesa kũma. Ũu now'o mũĩkĩĩo witũ ũilyĩ. Ũkaema kũsiw'a nesa wambĩĩa kwonza na mũthya ũikw'a. (Luka 22:32; Aevl. 3:12) Ĩndĩ tũkasũvĩa mũĩkĩĩo witũ ũndũ vaĩle, wĩkala wĩ mũlũmu, ũkaendeea 'kwĩana,' na ithyĩ ene twĩthĩwa twĩ "aima mũĩkĩĩonĩ."—2 Ath. 1:3; Tito 2:2.
ŨNDŨ MBIVILIA ĨELEETYE MŨĨKĨĨO
6. Ĩandĩko ya Aevelania 11:1 yĩeleetye mũĩkĩĩo kwa nzĩa syĩva ilĩ?
6 Mbivilia nĩeleetye mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kyaũ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Aevelania 11:1. (Soma.) Mũĩkĩĩo ũkonetye maũndũ aa elĩ ala tũtamba kũmona: (1) "Maũndũ ala mekwatĩtw'e." Asu nĩ maũndũ ma ĩvinda yũkĩte ala twathĩtwe ĩndĩ matanamba kwĩanĩa, ta kũminwa kwa ũthũku w'onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ na kwona ĩla nthĩ nzaũ twathĩtwe. (2) "Maũndũ ala matonekaa." Maũndũ asu nĩ ta kũmanya kana Yeova Ngai, Yesũ Klĩsto, na alaĩka me kw'o o na kau tũyaamona. O na ĩngĩ nĩ vamwe na kũmanya kana Ũsumbĩ wa ĩtunĩ wĩ vo. (Aevl. 11:3) Tũtonya kwonany'a ata twĩ na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu na kana nĩtũĩkĩĩe maũndũ asu matonekaa maneenewe Ndetonĩ ya Ngai? Tũtonya kwĩka ũu kwĩsĩla ndeto na meko maitũ. Tweeka ũu now'o tũtonya kwasya twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o.
7. Maũndũ ala Noa weekie metũtetheesya ata tũelewe mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kyaũ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 26.)
7 Ĩandĩko ya Aevelania 11:7 nĩyonanĩtye mũĩkĩĩo ũla Noa waĩ naw'o. Yaĩtye kana Ngai nĩwamũkanisye ĩũlũ wa 'ũvoo wa maũndũ ala matanamba kwoneka, [na nũndũ] wa kũmũkĩa Ngai, nĩwaseũvisye ngalawa avĩtye nyũmba yake.' Kwoou Noa nĩwoonanisye mũĩkĩĩo wake kwa kwaka ngalawa ĩsu yaĩ nene mũno. Vate nzika, no nginya atũi make methĩwe mamũkũlilye nĩkĩ ũkwaka kĩndũ kĩu kĩnenevete ũu. We Noa nĩwĩthĩwa eekie kũvindya kana akamea makwatye maũndũ a moo? Ekaĩ! Vandũ va ũu, mũĩkĩĩo wake nĩwatumie amatavya ũvoo e na ũkũmbaũ na akany'a andũ asu ĩũlũ wa ũsilĩlo ũla Ngai wavangĩte kũmaetee. O na nĩvatonyeka Noa akethĩwa atavisye andũ asu ndeto ila Yeova Ngai wamũtavĩtye. Yeova amwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Mũminũkĩlyo wa mĩĩ yonthe nĩwooka mbee wakwa; nũndũ nthĩ nĩyusũĩtwe nĩ ũng'endu kwondũ woo . . . Nĩngũete kĩw'ũ kingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, kyanange mĩĩ yonthe, yĩ na mĩvevo ya thayũ nthĩnĩ wayo, ungu wa ĩtu, kyonthe kĩla kĩ kũũ nthĩ kĩkakw'a." O na ĩngĩ vai nzika kana Noa nĩwamaeleisye kĩla maaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana matangĩĩwe. Nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa amatavisye ũndũ ũũ Ngai wamwĩĩte no nginya eke: "Ũkalika ngalawanĩ." Kwa nzĩa ĩsu, Noa nĩwoonanisye mũĩkĩĩo wake ĩngĩ kwa kwĩthĩwa e "mũtavan'ya wa ũlũngalu."—Mwa. 6:13, 17, 18; 2 Vet. 2:5.
8. Mũmanyĩw'a Yakovo aveveewe aelesya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o wa Kĩklĩsto?
8 Nĩvatonyeka Yakovo akethĩwa aandĩkie valũa wake ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ Vaulo amina kũandĩkĩa Aevelania valũa amaeleetye mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kyaũ. O ta Vaulo, Yakovo nĩwaeleisye kana Mũklĩsto wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ũla wa w'o no nginya awonany'e na meko, ĩndĩ ti o kwĩthĩwa aĩkĩĩe maũndũ. Aisye atĩĩ: "Mbon'ya mũĩkĩĩo waku ute na meko, nakwa nĩngũkwon'ya mũĩkĩĩo wakwa na meko makwa." (Yak. 2:18) Yakovo nĩwasyokie aelesya kana mũndũ wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo wĩ na meko e kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na mũndũ wĩkaa kũĩkĩĩa ũndũ mũna. O nasyo ndaimoni niĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai e kw'o ĩndĩ ũsu ti w'o ũla mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ syo syĩkaa maũndũ maleanĩte vyũ na kĩeleelo kya Ngai. (Yak. 2:19, 20) Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, Yakovo nĩwaneenie ĩũlũ wa Avalaamu, ũla waĩ na mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o. Akũlilye ũũ: "Avalaamu, ĩthe waitũ, ndaatalĩlwa ũlũngalu ũndũ wa meko, yĩla wathembie Isaka mwana wake kĩthembeonĩ? Nũkwona ũndũ mũĩkĩĩo watethanisye na meko make, na kwondũ wa meko mũĩkĩĩo nĩweanĩw'e." Na nĩ kana Yakovo akindĩlĩĩle kana mũĩkĩĩo waĩle kwonanw'a na meko, ongeleeile ndeto ii: "Mwĩĩ ũte na veva nĩ mũkw'ũ, no ta ũu mũĩkĩĩo ũte na meko nĩ mũkw'ũ."—Yak. 2:21-23, 26.
9, 10. Mũtũmwa Yoana atũtetheesye ata tũelewe vata wa kwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo witũ?
9 Myaka mbee wa 30 kuma vau, mũtũmwa Yoana nĩwaandĩkie yĩla Ĩvuku ya Ũvoo Mũseo na valũa ingĩ itatũ. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, We nĩweetĩkĩlanile na kĩla aandĩki ala angĩ ma Mbivilia maveveewe kũelesya ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o wa Kĩklĩsto? Mavukunĩ ala Yoana waandĩkie atũmĩie ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla mavinda amwe ĩalyũlawa "kwĩtĩkĩla" kana "kwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo," na atũmĩie ndeto ĩsu mavinda maingĩ mũno kwĩ mũandĩki ũngĩ o na wĩva wa Mbivilia.
10 Kwa ngelekany'o, Yoana aeleisye atĩĩ: "Ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa ũ Mwana e na thayũ ũtathela; ĩndĩ ũla ũtamwĩtĩkĩlaa [kana "ũtamwĩw'aa," NWT] Mwana ndakona thayũ, ĩndĩ ũthatu wa Ngai wĩkalaa ĩũlũ wake." (Yoa. 3:36) Kwoou Mũklĩsto wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o no nginya ew'e mĩao ya Yesũ. O na mavinda maingĩ Yoana aiandĩka nĩwawetaa ndeto sya Yesũ ila syonanĩtye kana Mũklĩsto no nginya aendeee kwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo ate kũeka.—Yoa. 3:16; 6:29, 40; 11:25, 26; 14:1, 12.
11. Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa kũmanya ũla w'o?
11 Nĩtũtũngaa mũvea mũno nĩkwĩthĩwa Yeova nĩwatũmĩie veva wake mũtheu nĩ kana atũvuanĩsye ũla w'o na nĩ kana atũtetheesye twonany'e twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa ũla ũvoo mũseo. (Soma Luka 10:21.) Tũikaaĩse kũlwa tũeke kũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa kũtũkusya kwake kwĩsĩla vala ve Mwana wake, ũla nĩwe "mwambĩlĩlya na mwĩanĩsya wa mũĩkĩĩo witũ." (Aevl. 12:2) Nĩ kana twonany'e nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mumo ũsu twooniw'e, twaĩle kũendeea kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo witũ kwa kũvoya na kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai.—Aev. 6:18; 1 Vet. 2:2.
12. Tũtonya kwonany'a mũĩkĩĩo witũ ata?
12 Nĩtwaĩle kũendeea kwonany'a kana nĩtũĩkĩĩaa mawatho ma Yeova. Ĩndĩ no nginya twĩke maũndũ mekwoneka nesa vyũ nĩ andũ ala angĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, no nginya tũendeee kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai na kũendeeaa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a. O na ĩngĩ no nginya tũendeee kwĩka "andũ onthe nesa, ĩndĩ mũno ala ma nyũmba ya mũĩkĩĩo." (Aka. 6:10) O na eka ũu, twaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito 'tumye mũndũ ũla wa tene na meko make,' na kwĩsũvĩana na ũndũ w'onthe ũla ũtonya kwonzya ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova.—Ako. 3:5, 8-10.
KŨMŨĨKĨĨA NGAI NĨ KĨLUNGU KĨMWE KYA WAMBĨLĨLYO WITŨ
13. "Kũĩkĩĩa Ngai" nĩ kwa vata ata, na kũelekanĩtw'e na kyaũ, na nĩkĩ?
13 Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Vate mũĩkĩĩo kũitonyeka kũmwendeesya [Ngai]; nũndũ ũla wũkaa kwa Ngai mũvaka etĩkĩle kana e vo, na ĩngĩ nũmanengae ĩtuvi ala mamũmanthaa." (Aevl. 11:6) Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye kana "kũĩkĩĩa Ngai" nĩ ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala Aklĩsto ma w'o maĩle kwĩka. Maũndũ asu nĩmo maelekanĩtw'e na "wambĩlĩlyo" wa mwako. (Aevl. 6:1) No nginya Aklĩsto 'mekĩe mũĩkĩĩonĩ woo' nguma ingĩ sya vata nĩ kana maendeee 'kwĩyĩkalya ene wendonĩ wa Ngai.'—Soma 2 Vetelo 1:5-7; Yuta 20, 21.
14, 15. Ũtonya kwasya ata waelekany'a mũĩkĩĩo na wendo?
14 Aandĩki ma Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto mawetete mũĩkĩĩo mavinda maingĩ mũno kwonany'a kana nĩ wa vata. Vai nguma ĩngĩ ya Kĩklĩsto ĩwetetwe mavinda maingĩvĩte ũu. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ kwonany'a kana mũĩkĩĩo nĩw'o nguma ĩla ya vata vyũ ya Kĩklĩsto?
15 Vaulo aelekanilye mũĩkĩĩo na wendo na aandĩka atĩĩ: "O na ngethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo w'onthe, o na wa kũthamya iĩma, na ndi na wendo, nyie ti kĩndũ." (1 Ako. 13:2) Nake Yesũ nĩwakindĩlĩĩle vata wa kũmwenda Ngai mũno vyũ ĩla wasũngĩaa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ: "Mĩaonĩ, mwĩao ũla mũnene nĩ wĩva?" (Mt. 22:35-40) Wendo ũkuĩte nguma mbingĩ sya vata sya Kĩklĩsto, na mũĩkĩĩo nũmwe wa isu. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "wendo . . . nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa maũndũ onthe." Ũu nĩ kwasya kana mũndũ wĩ wendo nũĩkĩĩaa maũndũ ala Ngai ũwetete Ndetonĩ yake ya w'o.—1 Ako. 13:4, 7.
16, 17. Mũĩkĩĩo na wendo iwetanĩw'e ata Maandĩkonĩ? Kĩla kĩnene nĩ kĩva, na nĩkĩ?
16 Nũndũ mũĩkĩĩo na wendo nĩ nguma sya vata mũno, mavinda maingĩ aandĩki ma Mbivilia nĩmakothaa kũiwetanĩsya vamwe. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũtũmwa Vaulo eekĩie ana-a-asa make vinya 'mekĩe ngao ya kĩthũi ya mũĩkĩĩo na wendo.' (1 Ath. 5:8) Nake Vetelo aandĩkie: 'Ũla mũmwendaa [Yesũ] o na kau mũiaamwona; o na mũtiũmwona yu, ĩndĩ mũkĩmwĩtĩkĩla.' (1 Vet. 1:8) Yakovo nake akũlilye ana-a-asa make etĩkĩw'a mauta atĩĩ: 'Ngai ndaamanyuva ala ngya ma kũũ nthĩ methĩwe athwii mũĩkĩĩonĩ, na atiĩwa ma ũsumbĩ ũla wamathie ala mamwendaa?' (Yak. 2:5) Yoana aandĩkie: 'Na mwĩao wake [Ngai] nĩ ũũ, kana twĩtĩkĩle syĩtwa ya Mwana wake Yesũ Klĩsto, na kwendana.'—1 Yoa. 3:23.
17 O na kau mũĩkĩĩo nĩ wa vata, ĩvinda yũkĩte tũikethĩwa ĩngĩ na vata wa kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa mawatho ma Ngai nĩkwĩthĩwa wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o ũkeethĩwa ũneanĩa. Ĩndĩ vai ĩvinda yĩkavika tũeke kwenda Ngai na mũtũi. Kwoou nĩkyo kĩtumi Vaulo waisye atĩĩ: "Ĩndĩ yu kwĩkalĩte mũĩkĩĩo, na wĩkwatyo, na wendo, asu atatũ; na mũnene wa asu nĩ wendo."—1 Ako. 13:13.
ŨNDŨ TWONANĨTYE NESA VYŨ KANA TWĨ NA MŨĨKĨĨO
18, 19. Ũmũnthĩ twonanĩtye ata nesa vyũ kana twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, na nũũ ũla waĩlĩte kwosa nguma nũndũ wa ũu?
18 Ũmũnthĩ andũ ma Yeova nĩmethĩĩtwe mayonany'a nĩmaĩkĩĩte vyũ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nũsumbĩkĩte. Kĩu kĩtumĩte kwĩthĩwa na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa mbee wa milioni nyanya ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, ala mekalaa na mũuo na ngwatanĩo ikundinĩ syoo. Nĩmonanasya ũsyao wa veva wa Ngai kwa nzĩa nene mũno. (Aka. 5:22, 23) Ũsu nĩ wonany'o mũnene ta kĩ wa Aklĩsto me mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o na wendo wa w'o!
19 Vai mũndũ wĩsa kwasya kana ũu w'onthe wĩanĩĩte nũndũ wake. Ngai e weka no we ũtonya kwĩanĩsya kĩu. Wĩa ũsu wa ũsengy'a nũetae "syĩtwa kwa Yeova, wonan'yo wa tene na tene ũla ũtakavetwa." (Isa. 55:13) Kwa w'o, 'kũtangĩĩwa kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo' nĩ "mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai." (Aev. 2:8) Yeova nũkũendeea kũtetheesya andũ aingĩ mamesye mũĩkĩĩo vala ũĩ nginya ĩla nthĩ yonthe ĩkausũa andũ mate naĩ, alũngalu, na atanu, na kĩu kĩikalea kũtuma ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩtaĩwa tene na tene. Ekai ĩndĩ tũtw'e kũendeea kwonany'a kana nĩtũĩkĩĩaa mawatho ma Yeova!
