translation:
"And in those days, . . . truly, he sent them out to proclaim the good news of God."
1-3. Is this why there is such eagerness among Jehovah's Witnesses to finish their ministry so they can have "all nations"?
JESUS CHRIST commissioned his followers extensively. He told them: "Go . . . and make disciples of all nations." It is vital to finish "this important work of witnessing . . . before the end comes for all nations."—Matt. 24:14; 28:19.
2 Jesus' followers continue and will continue to finish their ministry. Today we live in times when it may seem impossible to reach everyone because of the large population. Why? Because of the increase, many people. Also, Jesus himself, who was God's Son, was impaled. And because of the third reason, people "were amazed, and greatly astonished." (Acts 4:13) Today we are able to finish our ministry through modern means, and also through classes in schools, but they do not teach about spiritual things. This is why many people are amazed at what they see. And like the nation of Israel of old, will we be associated with the Kingdom of God that will bring peace to the earth?
3 Furthermore, Jesus foretold that his followers would be betrayed by family members and some would kill them. (Luke 21:16, 17) And he foretold that they would be hated, persecuted, and falsely accused, and that the earth would experience great earthquakes. (Matt. 24:10-12) And so it has happened to all people, making it difficult to finish even "preaching the good news." (Acts 1:8) But let us remember that this is something that needs to be done to reach those around us.
4 Will the finishing of this ministry happen during our lifetime?
4 And since the ministry can only continue if we remain faithful, it will involve supporting the work in Jerusalem and Samaria and to the most distant part of the earth. The ministry will also involve facing many difficulties, including about 30 years when they were trying to fulfill "all the Scriptures," and then the need to 'strengthen their hands and encourage their hearts.' (Acts 1:6, 23) Consider this example: Once the apostle Paul was in Cyprus and met a certain sorcerer named Elymas who opposed him. Scripture says: "[Elymas] was opposing us and hindering the ways of the Lord."—Read Acts 13:6-12.
5 (a) What did Jesus foretell regarding his followers? (b) How have some individuals shown their opposition to God's purposes through the way they have treated his apostles?
5 Jesus' followers have been given a powerful ministry. Jesus promised that he would be with them always, even to the end of the age. (Matt. 28:20) Also, they continued to strengthen themselves by doing certain things that helped them to maintain their zeal for the ministry. One source stated: "From time to time they visited various congregations and cities to encourage the church and [. . .] By the year 100 C.E., Christians . . . began to claim that God had inspired the writings of Christ."—Evangelism in the Early Church.
6 Let us discuss (a) what is involved; (b) what has already been accomplished.
6 The Bible shows that God allowed certain things to happen so that his angelic organization could continue to function effectively. So we can be sure that Jehovah wants his people to remain united against Satan's opposition. What is involved is continuing to support the work of the angelic organization. And this lesson will help us to appreciate how much progress has been made in maintaining our unity since ancient times.
THE ROMAN PEACE
7 What was the Pax Romana, and why was it important?
7 There were some events during the Roman Peace that affected Christians in the first century. For example, the period came to be called Pax Romana, or The Roman Peace. The Roman Peace brought relative peace to many people throughout the empire. But it also saw the fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy. (Matt. 24:6) In fact, the end of the Roman Peace coincided with Jerusalem's destruction in 70 C.E., and it marked the beginning of widespread trouble for the Christian congregation. For nearly 200 years after Jesus' death, the world enjoyed a time of relative peace. One historian wrote: "The whole world was enjoying a most peaceful rest, and everywhere there was prosperity."
8 How did Christians in the first century view the existing political order?
8 A scholar of the second century named Origen explained what they believed. He wrote: "Christians are accused of being responsible for all the misfortunes that come upon the world… because they refuse to participate in the customs which others observe.… They are blamed for floods, droughts, famines, and earthquakes, and for everything else that happens contrary to expectation." However, he pointed out that the Roman Empire itself was built on bloodshed, asking: "Is it not evident that Jesus wished his followers to live peacefully among men?" And yet, despite the fact that the Roman Empire brought relative peace, it was still an imperfect system—one that would eventually disappear.—Read Romans 12:18-21.
TO KEEP NEUTRALITY
9, 10. Why should we remain neutral toward worldly governments?
9 Christians strive to be obedient to God's law, but they do not seek political power. Rome often used force to maintain order, but it did not succeed in winning the hearts of its people. It is possible that some citizens appreciated the stability it provided, but many were dissatisfied, and Paul wisely avoided taking sides. The roads built by the Romans stretched for over 400,000 miles (over 640,000 kilometers) throughout the empire, facilitating trade and military movements. These roads were well-maintained, durable, and safe.
10 On those roads, travelers could find lodging and substantial meals. They covered about 17,000 miles (about 27,000 kilometers). And there were also approximately 400 seaports. Those ports were busy because of extensive sea travel. Because of this, Christians could travel throughout the Roman world. Also, like Paul, others needed documents to cross borders—such as passports and visas. A person who broke the law or caused trouble could face imprisonment or further punishment. So it was important to respect local customs and laws so as not to cause problems. This would help avoid unnecessary difficulties when traveling. Also, like Paul, one might be arrested and imprisoned on false charges, as happened to him, and face other trials, as the Scriptures show us that prisoners were sometimes unjustly held in prison.—2 Cor. 11:25, 26.
QUESTION
11. Do you know what the Kingdom of God is?
11 Every language has its own way of expressing things, but the common language spoken in the first century was called Koine. That language enabled Christians to communicate effectively with people from various backgrounds. Why is this important? The Roman Empire facilitated travel, and Governor Alexander the Great helped spread the Koine language, making it easier for many people to understand the good news. Thus, God could reach people from all nations, and this contributed to the fulfillment of his purpose. Moreover, in the first century, copies of the Greek Scriptures were made available in Egypt. These earlier manuscripts are known as the Septuagint and have proven valuable. Early Christians used them extensively. This language is why all Christians use it to write most of the Bible. Its value lies in the fact that it can be understood by an educated person anywhere in the biblical world.
12. (a) What is a codex, and what advantage did it offer over loose scrolls? (b) Which earlier codices were used by Christians?
12 Christians used codices—manuscripts bound together—to make the scriptures more portable and durable. They used both longer rolls and these newer books. It is like someone wanting to read something and being able to find it quickly, and having the writings organized neatly. For example, the Gospel of Matthew was originally written on a single scroll. Later, collections of such scrolls were bound together and called codices. These books were also more convenient to store. Because they were compact, a traveler could carry more material. And it was easier to locate a specific passage. So, it is not surprising that early Christians began using codices; one writing says: "Christians used codices from about AD 100, and there is evidence that they started using them even earlier in the late first century [after Christ]."
THE WORD OF GOD
13, 14. (a) Why did Paul defend himself before Felix, the Roman governor? (b) How did the accusations against Paul affect his witness to Christ?
13 The Word of God is powerful and effective, and Governor Felix had heard much about it. Paul defended himself before Felix on several occasions. On one occasion, when Paul was brought before him for trial, he addressed the governor, saying: "I practice righteousness toward God constantly, and so I have not missed an opportunity to speak to you." This made Felix uneasy. But because Paul spoke about faith and justice, and about the Kingdom of God, Felix listened to him, though he said: "Go away now, and at some other time I will hear you," hoping Paul would bribe him.—Acts 22:25-29.
14 Paul also defended himself before officials in Philippi while speaking about the good news of the Kingdom. (Acts 16:35-40) And on another occasion in Ephesus, a silversmith defended the gods of the city when Paul spoke about the true God. (Acts 19:35-41) And in Caesarea, Paul defended himself before Caesar and used this opportunity to preach the good news. (Acts 25:8-12) Thus, the accusations against Paul served to give him opportunities to bear witness to Christ "to make known the glorious good news."—Phil. 1:7.
IMPORTANT POINTS TO REMEMBER
15. What important points should we remember regarding our defense?
15 We should remember the great power of the Kingdom and the fact that people need to hear the good news so they can be saved. Do we remember this? For many years, Athens and Babylon challenged the truth. However, over time, Athens became a ruin and Babylon fell. In the 4th century C.E., about 127 years after the death of Christ, the Roman Empire controlled most of the known world. (Est. 9:30) But Jesus foretold that the good news would be preached throughout the entire inhabited earth of Africa, as well as Europe, Asia Minor, and Mesopotamia. Some estimate that the Kingdom, which included some 60,000,000 people, had only one disciple for every 14 inhabitants. Nevertheless, because the good news spread widely, it made an impact.—Matt. 23:15.
16, 17. (a) How did the preaching work affect those who opposed the good news? (b) What questions will we now answer regarding how we can defend ourselves?
16 Because the good news was being proclaimed, many opponents of the good news misrepresented the Scriptures. For example, they claimed that God was partial, and that their traditions were superior to his law. Many Greek writings also contained much false information about the Messiah. (Luke 24:44) So the Jews and others who opposed the good news needed to understand that the Greek Scriptures were inspired by God, and Paul used this knowledge when reasoning with them. This is why Paul often engaged in discussions with Greeks to show them what the Scriptures say.—Read Acts 17:1, 2.
17 The Jews were zealous for their tradition. They often gathered in synagogues or public places to discuss religious matters. And many of these gatherings resulted in people becoming disciples of Christ.
JEHOVAH IS THE ONE WHO EMPOWERS US
18, 19. (a) What things did angels do to empower the apostles? (b) What things can we do to demonstrate our confidence in Jehovah?
18 Let us consider some things that empowered those ancient servants. These included Roman peace, a common language, good roads, and the spread of the good news. These things helped to spread the knowledge about Jesus as the one whom God had appointed.
19 About 400 years after Christ's death, the philosopher Plato wrote: "It is difficult to discover the creator and the nature of the universe, and even if discovered, it is difficult to explain them to everyone." But Jesus said: "What is impossible with men is possible with God." (Luke 18:27) The Creator of all things wants people to know him and to understand spiritual matters. Also, Jesus gave his followers the instruction: 'Go and make disciples of all nations.' (Matt. 28:19) We are therefore privileged to learn about Jehovah God and to share what we learn with others. This lesson shows how we can strengthen our faith.

text:
1, 2. (a) Yo kũmanya ĩsyĩtwa ya mũndũ wĩ nguma kwonanasya nũmwĩsĩ nesa vyũ? Elesya. (b) Andũ maĩkĩĩaa kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ?
KWĨ andũ aingĩ me nguma ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. No wĩthĩwe wĩsĩ ĩsyĩtwa ya mũndũ wĩ nguma mũno. Ĩndĩ kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ ĩsyĩtwa yake kũyonanasya kana nũmwĩsĩ nesa. O na kũyonanasya kana nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kaũndũ ĩũlũ wake na ũndũ ũilyĩ.
2 No wĩthĩwe weewie ĩũlũ wa Yesũ Klĩsto o na kau aĩ kũũ nthĩ myaka ta 2,000 mĩvĩtu. Ĩndĩ andũ aingĩ mayĩsĩ ũndũ Yesũ wailyĩ. Amwe maasyaa kana Yesũ aĩ mũndũ mũseo, angĩ maasyaa aĩ mwathani, na angĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana Yesũ nĩ Ngai. We wĩona ata?—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 12.
3. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũmũmanya Yeova Ngai na Yesũ Klĩsto?
3 Nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno vyũ kũmanya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: 'Na thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto.' (Yoana 17:3) Wamanya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Yeova na Yesũ, ũkekala nthĩ nzaũ tene na tene. (Yoana 14:6) O na ĩngĩ, kũmanya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Yesũ kũkaũtetheesya nũndũ Yesũ nĩwatũtiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo ya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩkalany'a na andũ na kũmeka maũndũ maseo. (Yoana 13:34, 35) Kĩlungunĩ kya 1 nĩtũneemanyĩisye ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Yu ekai twone kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa Yesũ.
NĨTWAMWONA MASIA!
4. Masyĩtwa "Masia" na "Klĩsto" monanasya ata?
4 Myaka mingĩ Yesũ atambĩte kũsyawa, Yeova nĩwathanĩte Mbivilianĩ akamũtũma Masia, kana Klĩsto, kũũ nthĩ. "Masia" nĩ ĩsyĩtwa ya kĩthyomo kya Kĩevelania, nayo ĩsyĩtwa "Klĩsto" nĩ ya kĩthyomo kya Kĩkiliki. Masyĩtwa asu elĩ ma ũnene meonany'a mũndũ ũla Ngai waĩ etĩkĩsye mauta na aimũnenga kĩanda kya vata mũno. Masia nĩwe ũkatuma mawatho onthe ma Ngai meanĩa. O na ĩngĩ, Yesũ no aũtetheesye ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ atanamba kũsyawa, andũ aingĩ meekũlasya-ĩ, 'Nũũ ũkatw'ĩka Masia?'
5. Mo amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ nĩmeesĩ kana nĩwe waĩ Masia?
5 Amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ mayaĩ na nzika kana nĩwe Masia ũla wathanĩtwe. (Yoana 1:41) Kwa ngelekany'o, Simoni Vetelo eeie Yesũ atĩĩ: "We nue Klĩsto." (Mathayo 16:16) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũĩkĩĩthya kana Yesũ nĩwe waĩ Masia?
6. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Yeova watetheeisye andũ ala maĩ na ngoo nzeo mamũmanye Masia?
6 Myaka mingĩ Yesũ atanamba kũsyawa, athani ma Ngai nĩmaandĩkie maũndũ maingĩ ala maaĩle kũtetheesya andũ mamũmanye Masia. Maũndũ asu mesaa kũmatetheesya ata? Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩĩ. Twasye nĩwatũmwa ũlatye mũndũ ũtaamwona kĩwanzanĩ kya ngalĩ kĩ na andũ aingĩ mũno. Waelew'a nesa ũndũ mũndũ ũsu ũilyĩ, nĩ laisi ũkamũmanya. O ta ũu, Yeova nĩwatũmĩie athani make matũelesye maũndũ ala Masia waĩ eke na maũndũ ala maĩ mamũkwate. Kwĩanĩa kwa mawathani asu onthe nĩkũtetheeasya andũ ala me na ngoo nzeo mamanye kana Yesũ nĩwe Masia.
7. Nĩ mawathani meva elĩ maĩkĩĩthasya kana Yesũ nĩwe Masia?
7 Ekai twone mawathani elĩ ĩũlũ wa Masia. Mbee, myaka 700 Yesũ atanamba kũsyawa, Mika nĩwathanie kana Masia akasyaĩwa taoninĩ nini ya Mbethi-leemu. (Mika 5:2) Yesũ esie kũsyaĩwa taoninĩ ĩsu! (Mathayo 2:1, 3-9) Kelĩ, Ndanieli nĩwathanie kana Masia aĩ aumĩle mwakanĩ wa 29 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa. (Ndanieli 9:25) Mawathani asu elĩ no amwe katĩ wa mawathani maingĩ ala maĩkĩĩthasya nesa kana Yesũ nĩwe Masia.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 13.
8, 9. Nĩ kyaũ kyeethĩiwe Yesũ aivatiswa kĩtũĩkĩĩthasya kana nĩwe Masia?
8 Yeova nũĩkĩĩthĩtye nesa vyũ kana Yesũ nĩwe Masia. Ngai nĩwamwathie Yoana Mũvatisi wonany'o nĩ kana eĩthĩwa atonya kũmanya nũũ ũla waĩ Masia. Ĩla Yesũ waendie kũla kwĩ Yoana akavatiswe Ũsĩnĩ wa Yolotani mwakanĩ wa 29 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, Yoana nĩwoonie wonany'o ũsu. Mbivilia nĩtũeleetye ũndũ kweethĩiwe. Yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Na Yesũ, avatiswa, ambata oyu kuma manzĩnĩ: na sisya, matu mamũvingũkĩa, na oona Veva wa Ngai aitheea ta ĩvũĩ, na aimũvũĩla; na sisya, wasya wauma matunĩ, ũkyasya, Ũũ nĩwe Mwana wakwa mwendwa, ũla nendeeaw'a nĩwe." (Mathayo 3:16, 17) Ĩla Yoana woonie ũndũ ũsu na eew'a ndeto isu, nĩwamanyie kana Yesũ nĩwe waĩ Masia. (Yoana 1:32-34) Mũthenyanĩ ũsu, ĩla Yeova wamwĩtĩkĩsye Yesũ veva wake, Yesũ nĩwatw'ĩkie Masia. Nĩwe Ngai wanyuvĩte ethĩwe Mũtongoi na Mũsumbĩ.—Isaia 55:4.
9 Maũndũ ala mathanĩtwe, ndeto ila Yeova waneenie, na wonany'o ũla Yeova wanenganie Yesũ aivatiswa, nĩsyaĩkĩĩthisye kana Yesũ nĩwe waĩ Masia. Ĩndĩ Yesũ aumĩte va, na aĩ na ndaĩa syĩva? Ekai twone kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya.
YESŨ AUMIE VA?
10. Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa vala Yesũ wekalaa atanoka kũũ nthĩ?
10 Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kana Yesũ ekalaa ĩtunĩ myaka mingĩ atanoka kũũ nthĩ. Mika aisye kana Masia aĩ wa "kuma ĩvinda ya tene." (Mika 5:2) Na ve mavinda maingĩ Yesũ waisye kana ekalaa ĩtunĩ atanamba kũsyawa kũũ nthĩ. (Soma Yoana 3:13; 6:38, 62; 17:4, 5.) O na atokĩte kũũ nthĩ, Yesũ aĩ na ngwatanĩo ndũmu mũno na Yeova.
11. Nĩkĩ Yeova wonaa Yesũ e wa vata mũno?
11 Yeova amwonaa Yesũ e wa vata mũno. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Ngai amũmbie mbee wa syũmbe ila ingĩ syonthe. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ wĩtĩtwe "mũsyawa ũla wĩ mbee wa syũmbe syonthe." * (Akolosai 1:15) O na ĩngĩ, Yesũ ethĩawa e wa vata mũno kwa Yeova nũndũ nĩwe e weka woombiwe ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe nĩ Yeova. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi wĩtĩtwe "Mwana wake e ũmwe." (Yoana 3:16) O na ĩngĩ, Yesũ e weka nĩwe watũmĩiwe nĩ Yeova kũmba syĩndũ ila ingĩ syonthe. (Akolosai 1:16) Na no Yesũ e weka wĩtĩtwe "ĩla Ndeto," nũndũ nĩwe Yeova watũmĩaa kũtavya alaĩka na andũ ũndũ ũkwenda.—Yoana 1:14.
12. Twĩsĩ ata kana Yesũ na Ngai mayĩanene?
12 Andũ amwe maĩkĩĩaa kana Yesũ na Ngai nĩmeanene. Ĩndĩ ũu ti w'o Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya. Mbivilia yaasyaa kana Yesũ nĩwoombiwe, na ũu wĩonany'a e mwambĩlĩlyo. Ĩndĩ Yeova, ũla woombie syĩndũ syonthe, nde mwambĩlĩlyo. (Savuli 90:2) O nake Yesũ ndaasũanĩa kwĩthĩwa eanene na Ngai nũndũ we mwene nĩ Mwana wa Ngai. Mbivilia nĩtũmanyĩĩtye nesa kana Asa nĩ mũnene kwĩ Mwana. (Soma Yoana 14:28; 1 Akolintho 11:3.) Yeova e weka nĩwe "Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 17:1) Nĩwe mũnene vyũ na wĩ vinya mwingĩ mũno ĩtunĩ na kũũ nthĩ.—Soma Maelesyo ma Mũthya namba 14.
13. Nĩkĩ Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yesũ nĩwe "mũvw'ano wa Ngai ũtonekaa"?
13 Yeova na Mwana wake, Yesũ, nĩmathũkũmie ĩmwe kwa myaka mbilioni mbingĩ nthĩ na matu itanamba kũmbwa. No nginya methĩwe mendanĩte mũno vyũ! (Yoana 3:35; 14:31) Yesũ e ndaĩa nzeo ta ila sya Ĩthe wake na nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩmwĩtĩte "mũvw'ano wa Ngai ũtonekaa."—Akolosai 1:15.
14. Vatonyekie ata Mwana wa Ngai mwendwa asyawa ta mũndũ?
14 Mwana wa Ngai mwendwa ndaalasimĩthw'a kuma ĩtunĩ, ĩndĩ eekie ũu na ngenda na asyawa kũũ nthĩ ta mũndũ. Ũu watonyekie ata? Kwa nzĩa ya kyama, Yeova athamisye thayũ wa Mwana wake kuma ĩtunĩ na awĩkĩa ĩvunĩ ya mũndũ mũka weetawa Meli ũla ũtaĩ aakoma na mũndũũme. Nũndũ wa ũu, vayaĩ vata wa Meli akome na mũndũũme nĩ kana Yesũ asyawe. Kwoou Meli asyaie mwana ũte na naĩ, na amwĩta Yesũ.—Luka 1:30-35.
YESŨ AĨ NA NDAĨA SYĨVA?
15. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva ũtonya kũmũmanya Yeova mũnango?
15 No wĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ, ũndũ wekalaa e kũũ nthĩ, na ndaĩa syake nzeo kwa kũsoma ĩvuku ya Mathayo, Maliko, Luka, na Yoana. Mavuku asu ma Mbivilia metawa Mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo. Nũndũ Yesũ ailyĩ o ta Ĩthe wake, maũndũ ala ũũsoma nĩmeũkũtetheesya ũmũmanye Yeova mũnango. Na nĩkyo kĩtumi Yesũ waisye atĩĩ: "Ũla wambonie nĩwamwonie Asa."—Yoana 14:9.
16. Nĩ maũndũ meva Yesũ wamanyĩasya? Momanyĩsyo ma Yesũ maumĩte va?
16 Andũ aingĩ mamwĩtaa Yesũ "Mũmanyĩsya." (Yoana 1:38; 13:13) Ũndũ ũmwe wa vata Yesũ wamanyĩasya nĩ "ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ." Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩ kyaũ? Nĩ silikalĩ ya Ngai ĩla ĩkasumbĩka vaa nthĩ kuma ĩtunĩ na ĩietee andũ ala mamwĩw'aa Ngai moathimo maingĩ. (Mathayo 4:23) Maũndũ onthe ala Yesũ wamanyĩasya maumĩte kwa Yeova. Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Ũmanyĩsyo wakwa ti wakwa, ĩndĩ nĩ wa ũla wandũmie." (Yoana 7:16) Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana Yeova endaa andũ mew'e ũvoo mũseo wa kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkasumbĩka ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
17. Yesũ amanyĩasya andũ va? Nĩkĩ waĩ na kĩthito kingĩ kya kũmanyĩsya andũ ala angĩ?
17 Yesũ amanyĩasya andũ va? Amamanyĩasya kĩla vandũ weethĩana namo. Nĩwamamanyĩasya ndũanĩ, sokonĩ, masinakokenĩ, na mĩsyĩnĩ yoo. Yesũ ndeeteelaa andũ moke vala ũĩ, ĩndĩ mavinda maingĩ aendaa vala maĩ. (Maliko 6:56; Luka 19:5, 6) Yesũ aĩ na kĩthito kingĩ na nĩwatũmĩaa ĩvinda na vinya mwingĩ aimanyĩsya andũ. Nĩkĩ weekaa ũu? Nũndũ nĩweesĩ kana Ngai endaa eke ũu, na nĩwamwĩw'aa Ĩthe wake mavinda onthe. (Yoana 8:28, 29) O na ĩngĩ, Yesũ atavanasya nũndũ nĩweew'ĩaa andũ tei. (Soma Mathayo 9:35, 36.) Nĩwoonaa atongoi ma ndĩni mate kũmanyĩsya ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai na Ũsumbĩ wake. Kwoou endaa kũtetheesya andũ aingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka mew'e ũvoo mũseo.
18. Nĩ ndaĩa syĩva sya Yesũ ikwendeeasya mũno?
18 Yesũ nĩwendete andũ na nĩwamathĩnĩkĩaa. Nĩwamew'ĩaa tei na maĩ na ũthasyo wa kũneena nake. O na syana nĩsyendete kwĩthĩwa vakuvĩ nake. (Maliko 10:13-16) Mavinda onthe nĩwendete sila wa katĩ na nĩwamenete ũlũsani. (Mathayo 21:12, 13) Ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ aka matũmĩawa naĩ na nĩmavũthĩtw'e. Ĩndĩ we mavinda onthe nĩwanengae aka ndaĩa. (Yoana 4:9, 27) Kwa w'o Yesũ aĩ na wĩnyivyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda wathambisye amanyĩw'a make maaũ, ũndũ ũla wakothaa kwĩkwa nĩ athũkũmi.—Yoana 13:2-5, 12-17.
19. Nĩ ngelekany'o yĩva ĩkwonany'a kana Yesũ nĩweesĩ mavata ma andũ na nĩwendaa kũmatetheesya?
19 Yesũ nĩweesĩ mavata ma andũ na nĩwendaa kũmatethya. Oonanisye ũu nesa ĩla watũmĩie vinya wa Ngai kũvosya andũ kwa nzĩa ya kyama. (Mathayo 14:14) Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũũme ũmwe wawaĩte mangũ ookie vala ve Yesũ na amwĩa atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa nũkwenda, nũtonya kũnthesya." Yesũ nĩwakiitiwe ngoo mũno ĩla woonie ũndũ mũndũũme ũsu ũkũthĩna. Nĩwamwĩw'ĩie tei na enda kũmũvosya. Na kwoou Yesũ nĩwatambũũkisye kw'oko kwake, amũkiita, na amwĩa atĩĩ: "Nĩngwenda; ĩthĩwa mũtheu." Na mũndũ ũsu waĩ mũwau avoa. (Maliko 1:40-42) Kwasũanĩa ũndũ mũndũũme ũsu weewie!
MAVINDA ONTHE EETHĨAWA E MŨĨKĨĨKU KWA ĨTHE WAKE
20, 21. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Yesũ weethĩiwe e ngelekany'o nzeo ya mũndũ wamwĩwie Ngai vyũ?
20 Yesũ nĩwe ngelekany'o ĩla nzeo ya mũndũ wamwĩwie Ngai vyũ. Aĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ĩthe wake o na akwatwa nĩ maũndũ mailyĩ ata, kana o na eekwa maũndũ mathũku nĩ amaitha make. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ ndaaĩka naĩ ĩla Satani wamũtatie. (Mathayo 4:1-11) Andũ amwe ma mũsyĩ wa Yesũ mayaĩkĩĩaa kana nĩwe Masia na maasyaa kana "e na ndũũka," ĩndĩ nĩwaendeeie kũtethya wĩa wa Ngai. (Maliko 3:21) O na ĩla amaitha make mamũthĩnasya, Yesũ nĩweethĩiwe e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai na ndaatata kũmaũmĩsya.—1 Vetelo 2:21-23.
21 O na ĩla Yesũ wathĩnaw'a nginya ooawa kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo, nĩwaendeeie kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Yeova. (Soma Avilivi 2:8.) Kwasũanĩa mathĩna ala woomĩĩisye mũthenya ũla wakwie. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwakwatiwe, ngũsĩ sya ũvũngũ syasya nũmũumĩte Ngai, asili mataĩ aseo masya nũvĩtĩtye, andũ mamũthekeea, na asikalĩ mamũvũa na mamũathĩĩa mũtĩnĩ. Yesũ akilyĩ kũkw'a aneenie asya: "Nĩwathela." (Yoana 19:30) Mĩthenya ĩtatũ ĩtina wa Yesũ kũkw'a, Yeova nĩwamũthayũũkisye na amũnenga mwĩĩ wa veva. (1 Vetelo 3:18) Ĩtina wa syumwa nini Yesũ nĩwasyokie ĩtunĩ, na "ekala nthĩ ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwa aũme kwa Ngai" eteele Ngai emũtw'ĩkĩthya Mũsumbĩ.—Aevelania 10:12, 13.
22. Nũndũ Yesũ aĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ĩthe wake, twĩ na mwanya wa kwĩsa kũkwata kyaũ?
22 Nũndũ Yesũ nĩwaendeeie kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ĩthe wake, twĩ na mwanya wa kwĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nzaũ o tondũ Yeova wendaa. Kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩatĩĩe, nĩtũũneenea ũndũ kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kĩtonya kũtuma twĩkala tene na tene.
^ kal. 11 Yeova etawa Asa nũndũ nĩwe Mũmbi. (Isaia 64:8) Nake Yesũ etawa Mwana wa Ngai nũndũ oombiwe nĩ Yeova. O namo alaĩka vamwe na Atamu metawa syana sya Ngai.—Yovu 1:6; Luka 3:38.

translation:
1, 2. (a) Why is it important to know what people believe? Explain. (b) What do many people believe about Jesus?
FOR many people, religion is an important part of life. But few really know what people believe. It is often difficult to understand what their beliefs mean or why they hold them. And understanding what they believe can help us relate to them better.
2 Few people today truly know the story of Jesus Christ and how it affects their lives. For almost 2,000 years, many people have wondered what Jesus did. Some think Jesus was just a man, others think he was a myth, and still others believe Jesus is God. What do you think?—Read Matthew chapter 12.
3. Is it vital to get to know Jehovah God and Jesus Christ?
3 It is very important to learn about Jesus. How can we do this? The Bible says: "And this means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and his Son, Jesus Christ." (John 17:3) Knowing about Jehovah and Jesus will make you strong forever. (John 14:6) Also, learning about Jesus will help you show love like Jesus showed love, so you can live peacefully with others and do good things. (John 13:34, 35) Paragraph 1 has helped us learn about God. Let us see what the Bible teaches about Jesus.
LET US LEARN MORE!
4. What do the terms "Messiah" and "Christ" mean?
4 Many years before Jesus came to earth, Jehovah told people through the prophets that he would send a Messiah, or Christ, to earth. "Messiah" is a Hebrew word, and "Christ" is a Greek word. Both words mean "the one whom God appoints." The Messiah is the one who will carry out God's purpose. And also, Jesus showed a fine example. Before Jesus died, many people asked, 'Will you be the Messiah?'
5. Why did Jesus perform miracles?
5 Jesus performed miracles to prove that he was the Messiah that God had sent. (John 1:41) For example, Simon Peter once told Jesus: "You are the Christ." (Matthew 16:16) Is there a way to know for sure that Jesus is the Messiah?
6. Why did Jehovah allow people to remain in darkness for so long before sending the Messiah?
6 Many years before Jesus began his ministry, God allowed many prophecies to be recorded that would help people identify the Messiah. What do those prophecies accomplish? Consider this illustration. Imagine someone trying to find a specific person in a large crowd. It helps to have some information about what that person looks like. In the same way, Jehovah gave us the prophecies so we could recognize the Messiah when he arrived. To understand those prophecies, we need God's help. Through those prophecies, we learn about the qualities of the Messiah and about what he would do. The fulfillment of those prophecies helps people to know that Jesus is the Messiah.
7. What prophecies help us to identify Jesus as the Messiah?
7 Let's examine some of the prophecies fulfilled by the Messiah. About 700 years before Jesus began his ministry, Micah prophesied that the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem. (Micah 5:2) Jesus was indeed born in Bethlehem! (Matthew 2:1, 3-9) Also, Daniel prophesied that the Messiah would begin his public service 29 years after the start of his ministry. (Daniel 9:25) These are just a few of the many prophecies that confirm that Jesus is the Messiah.—Read The Watchtower Study article number 13.
8, 9. Why is it important that Jesus fulfilled prophecy to prove he is the Messiah?
8 Jehovah has used prophecies to show that Jesus is the Messiah. God inspired John the Baptist to declare that he would identify the one whom God had appointed as the Messiah. But when Jesus came to John, he was baptized by him in the Jordan River in 29 C.E., John received further evidence. The Bible tells us what happened. It says: "And Jesus, after being baptized, immediately came up out of the water; and behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit descending like a dove and coming upon him; and listen, a voice from the heavens said: 'This is my Son, the beloved one, whom I have approved.' " (Matthew 3:16, 17) So John knew beyond any doubt that Jesus was the Messiah. (John 1:32-34) Furthermore, Jehovah announced that Jesus was his Son, confirming that Jesus is the Messiah. He is the God-appointed Leader and Savior.—Isaiah 55:4.
9 Many things have been foretold, but how does knowing that Jehovah fulfills his prophecies help us strengthen our faith that Jesus is the Messiah? We will see this as we continue examining what the Bible teaches.
IS JESUS GOD'S SON?
10. Does the Bible indicate that Jesus existed eternally?
10 The Bible indicates that Jesus existed for an unlimited time. Micah prophesied that the Messiah would be from "time indefinite." (Micah 5:2) And Jesus himself spoke of existing in heaven before coming to earth. (Read John 3:13; 6:38, 62; 17:4, 5.) However, while in heaven, Jesus maintained a close relationship with Jehovah.
11. How did Jehovah view Jesus before his birth?
11 Jehovah viewed Jesus as his beloved Son. Why? Because God assigned him a special role in carrying out God's purpose. That is why Jesus is called "the firstborn of all creation." * (Colossians 1:15) Also, Jesus was deeply loved by Jehovah because he was the one who would be sent forth to redeem mankind. This is why he is called "his only-begotten Son." (John 3:16) Moreover, Jesus was the one Jehovah used to create everything else. (Colossians 1:16) And so Jesus is appropriately called "The Word," because Jehovah used him to express his thoughts and purposes to humankind.—John 1:14.
12. Is there a contradiction between Jesus being God's son and God being supreme?
12 Some people believe there is a contradiction. But this is not what the Bible teaches. The Bible shows that Jesus is subordinate, and this does not diminish Jehovah's greatness. To Jehovah, the Creator of all things, subordination is fitting. (Psalm 90:2) Furthermore, Jesus willingly submitted to being under God because he is God's Son. The Bible clearly shows that a son is inferior to a father. (Read John 14:28; 1 Corinthians 11:3.) Jehovah is the ultimate "God Almighty." (Revelation 17:1) He is superior in power and possesses far more authority than anyone else, including his Son.—Read Proverbs 8:31-36.
13. What does the Bible say about Jesus being "God's image"?
13 Jehovah and his Son, Jesus, have been closely united for billions of years and will remain so forever. What a wonderful thought! (John 3:35; 14:31) Jesus perfectly reflects Jehovah's qualities, which is why the Bible calls him "the image of the invisible God."—Colossians 1:15.
14. Would God's beloved Son ever become imperfect like a human?
14 God's beloved Son voluntarily humbled himself to live on earth, and he experienced difficulties and imperfections common to humans. Why did he do this? Because Jehovah allowed his Son to come to earth in order to demonstrate loyalty and to experience what humans go through. In this way, Jesus could sympathize with our weaknesses. The account of Melchizedek illustrates this—Melchizedek was a priest who associated with imperfect humans. Similarly, Jesus became imperfect when he came to earth.—Luke 1:30-35.
DOES JESUS HAVE A BEGINNING?
15. How can you get to know Jehovah better?
15 By learning more about Jesus, his role in God's purpose, and his deep love for mankind by reading the books of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. These four Bible books are called the Gospel accounts. Also, Jesus' teachings reveal much about his Father. As you study these accounts, you will come to know Jehovah better. That is why Jesus said: "Whoever has seen me has seen the Father also."—John 14:9.
16. What important truths does Jesus reveal? What benefits do you gain from knowing Jesus?
16 Many call Jesus "The Revealer." (John 1:38; 13:13) One aspect of Jesus' revealing work is "God's good news." But what is "good news"? It is the message about God's Kingdom, which will soon bring relief to humankind and allow people to worship God under righteous conditions. (Matthew 4:23) All the things Jesus reveals honor Jehovah. Jesus said: "My teaching is not my own, but comes from the One who sent me." (John 7:16) Jesus was able to accurately represent Jehovah and make known God's good news to people everywhere.
17. To whom does Jesus reveal God? Does he have another important way to reveal God to others?
17 Jesus reveals God to whom? He reveals it to all those who respond to him. He reveals it to rich ones, poor ones, sick ones, and healthy ones. Jesus went out of his way to help people, and many crowds followed him. (Mark 6:56; Luke 19:5, 6) Jesus had a strong desire, and he used much time and energy to reveal God to people. Why did he feel this way? Because he knew that God wanted people to know about Him and His Kingdom and to benefit from them. (John 8:28, 29) Also, Jesus showed compassion because he cared for people deeply. (Read Matthew 9:35, 36.) This moved him to teach them more fully about God and His Kingdom. Soon people would see the benefits of God's good news.
18. What is one reason why Jesus continued to travel around?
18 Jesus traveled among the people and felt sorry for them. He taught them readily and with kindness. And often he helped them solve their problems. (Mark 10:13-16) Many people traveled from far away to hear him. (Matthew 21:12, 13) The woman at the well was surprised when Jesus asked her for water, and she offered to draw water for him. In fact, many people were willing to do things for him gladly. (John 4:9, 27) That is why Jesus had many friends. For example, when he washed his disciples' feet, he showed how much he valued them—even though they were humble.—John 13:2-5, 12-17.
19. What lesson can we learn from the fact that Jesus knew people's needs and wanted to help them?
19 Jesus knew people's needs and wanted to help them. He used his power from God to relieve suffering. (Matthew 14:14) For instance, a leper once approached Jesus and begged him: "If you want to, you can heal me." Jesus was moved by this man's faith, so he healed him and sent him away. Then Jesus told him to tell no one about it, but the man went out and spread the good news. (Mark 1:40-42) How happy that man must have been!
MANY PEOPLE WERE HEALED BECAUSE OF THEIR FAITH
20, 21. Why did Jesus perform miracles, and what does this teach us about what pleases Jehovah?
20 Jesus performed miracles because he pleased Jehovah. He may have felt compassion for someone who was sick or afflicted, or he may have seen their faith. For example, Jesus allowed Satan to tempt him. (Matthew 4:1-11) Some of John the Baptist's disciples wondered whether Jesus was the Messiah or not, and they reported this to John. (Mark 3:21) But despite the opposition, Jesus continued to please Jehovah and set an example for us.—1 Peter 2:21-23.
21 Because Jesus willingly offered himself as a sacrifice, we can be forgiven and brought close to Jehovah. (Read Psalm 2:8.) Consider how much courage it took for him to do so. For instance, he was arrested, falsely accused of blasphemy, beaten, mocked, and nailed to a torture stake. Yet, Jesus calmly said: "I am finished." (John 19:30) After three days, Jehovah resurrected Jesus and glorified him in heaven. (1 Peter 3:18) This shows that Jesus completely honored Jehovah, and "to stand in God's favor" means that God approves of us.—Hebrews 10:12, 13.
22. So, why did Jesus please his Father, and what can we learn from this?
22 Since Jesus pleased his Father, we too can find ways to please Jehovah. By regularly thinking about Jesus' example, we can strengthen our determination to remain loyal.
^ par. 11 Jehovah showed Asa who He is, the Creator. (Isaiah 64:8) Likewise, Jesus proved that he is God's Son because Jehovah declared him to be. Adam and his descendants were also sons of God.—Job 1:6; Luke 3:38.

text:
"Na kwondũ wa ũthũku kwingĩva, wendo wa aingĩ ũkavoa." —MT. 24:12.
MBATHI: 23, 24
1, 2. (a) Ndeto ila Yesũ wawetie ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 24:12 syeanĩie kwa aaũ ĩvinda ya mbee? (b) Ĩvuku ya Meko ma Atũmwa yonanĩtye ata kana Aklĩsto ala aingĩ mayaaeka wendo woo ũkavoa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
KĨNDŨ kĩmwe Yesũ wawetie kĩkonany'a "wĩanĩu wa ĩvinda yĩĩ" nĩ kana "wendo wa aingĩ ũkavoa." (Mt. 24:3, 12) Ndeto isu syeanĩie ĩvinda ya mbee kwa Ayuti ala maĩ ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa nũndũ nĩmaekie kũmwenda Ngai ũndũ mamwendete tene o na kũtw'ĩka maasyaa mo nĩ andũ make.
2 Ĩndĩ kĩvathũkany'o na Ayuti asu, Aklĩsto aingĩ ala maĩ kw'o ĩvinda yĩu maendeeie kwĩthĩwa na kĩthito kya "kũtavan'ya ũvoo mũseo wa Yesũ," na kwonany'a kana nĩmamwendete Ngai, nĩmendete Aklĩsto ala angĩ, o na nĩmendete ala mate etĩkĩli. (Meko 2:44-47; 5:42) O na vailyĩ oou, ve aatĩĩi amwe ma Yesũ ma ĩvinda yĩu ya atũmwa maekie wendo woo wavoa.
3. Nĩ ũndũ ta wĩva wĩthĩwa watumie wendo wa Aklĩsto amwe ũvoa?
3 Yesũ Klĩsto amina kũthayũũkw'a nĩwaneenie na Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa ala maĩ ndũanĩ ya Eveso amea atĩĩ: "Nĩ na ũndũ naku, nũndũ nũtiĩte wendo waku wa mbee." (Ũvu. 2:4) Nĩ ũndũ ta wĩva wĩthĩwa watumie amatavya ndeto isu? No kwĩthĩwa amanyĩw'a asu ma Klĩsto maĩ manambĩĩa kũatĩĩa kĩla moonaa kĩyĩkwa nĩ andũ ma nthĩ ĩno ala meekaa maũndũ matongoew'e nĩ mĩmeo yoo. (Aev. 2:2, 3) O tondũ kũilyĩ isionĩ mbingĩ ũmũnthĩ, ndũa ya Eveso yausũĩte andũ maĩ na mĩkalĩle mĩthũku mũno. Ndũa ya Eveso yaĩ na andũ aingĩ athwii na ma kĩlasi, na mendete mũno kwĩtanĩthya. Andũ asu moonaa kĩu kĩ kya vata kwĩ ũndũ ũngĩ o na wĩva. Motanu ma nthĩ matumĩte andũ maeka kwendana w'o kuma ngoonĩ. Na eka ũu, andũ aingĩ meelikasya naĩnĩ ngito na angĩ matũlaa mĩao ya Ngai na ngũlũ mateenda kũtavw'a.
4. (a) Wendo wa aingĩ ũvoete ata ũmũnthĩ? (b) Wendo witũ ũtonya kũtatĩka maũndũnĩ meva atatũ?
4 Ũla wathani wa Yesũ nĩwĩanĩĩte o na ũmũnthĩ. Mũthenya kũthi ũla ũngĩ andũ nĩmaekete kũmwenda Ngai ũndũ mamwendete tene. Andũ milioni mbingĩ mũno nĩmaekete kũmwĩkwatya, na vandũ vake mekwatasya ngwatanĩo sya andũ imaminĩe mathĩna. Nũndũ wa ũu, wendo wa ala matamũthaithaa Yeova Ngai ũendeee kũvoa. Ĩndĩ o tondũ twoona ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩkundi kyaĩ ndũanĩ ya Eveso, ti vinya Aklĩsto ma w'o ũmũnthĩ makelekeleelya nũndũ wa kwĩw'a me eanĩe vyũ, na nũndũ wa ũu maieka wendo woo ũvoe. Ekai yu tũvindĩĩsye ũndũ wendo witũ ũtonya kũtatĩka maũndũnĩ aa atatũ: (1) Kũmwenda Yeova, (2) kwenda ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, (3) na kũmenda ana-a-asa.
KŨMWENDA YEOVA
5. Nĩkĩ no nginya tũmwende Ngai?
5 Yesũ atanamba kũweta kana wendo wa aingĩ ũkavoa, aĩ anaweta ĩũlũ wa wendo ũla wa vata vyũ andũ maĩle kwĩthĩwa naw'o. Awetete atĩĩ: "Mwende Mwĩaĩi Ngai waku na ngoo yaku yonthe, na thayũ waku w'onthe, na kĩlĩko kyaku kyonthe. Ũu nĩw'o mwĩao ũla mũnene na wa mbee." (Mt. 22:37, 38) Kũmwenda Yeova na ngoo yonthe nĩkũtũnengae vinya wa kũatĩĩa mĩao yake, vinya wa kũmĩĩsya, na wa kũmena ũla ũthũku. (Soma Savuli 97:10.) Ĩndĩ Satani na andũ ma nthĩ ĩno yake matataa ũndũ matonya nĩ kana mone tũekete kũmwenda Ngai.
6. Ala maeka kũmwenda Ngai makwatawa nĩ kyaũ?
6 Andũ ma nthĩ ĩno mendaa kĩla kĩtaĩle kwendwa. Vandũ va mamwende Mũmbi, methĩawa "makĩyenda ene." (2 Tim. 3:2) Andũ ma nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Satani maatĩanĩaa na "wendi wa mwĩĩ na wendi wa metho na wĩyĩan'yo wa thayũ." (1 Yoa. 2:16) Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwakanisye Aklĩsto ala angĩ maikese kwĩka maũndũ ma mwĩĩ. Ameie atĩĩ: "Kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ; . . . nĩkwĩthĩwa kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ nĩ ũmaitha na Ngai." (Alo. 8:6, 7) Vai nzika o na imwe kana ala mate na ũndũ ũngĩ kĩlĩkonĩ eka o kũatĩanĩa na malĩ kana kwĩanĩsya wendi woo wa kwĩka ũlaalai matiawa makw'ĩte ngoo na maũmĩĩte mũno.—1 Ako. 6:18; 1 Tim. 6:9, 10.
7. Weta mathĩna ala aatĩĩi ma Klĩsto makomanaa namo ũmũnthĩ.
7 O na kwĩ nthĩ imwe syĩ andũ maasya kũi Ngai, syĩ andũ mate na mũĩkĩĩo nake, na angĩ maĩkĩĩaa syĩndũ syeekie kwĩyumĩlya. Andũ asu mawetaa mawoni moo ũtheinĩ, na mawoni asu matumaa ala angĩ maeka kũmwenda Ngai na kũmũĩkĩĩa. O na matumĩte andũ aingĩ maĩkĩĩa kana no nginya mũndũ ũĩkĩĩaa kwĩ Mũmbi ethĩwe e mũtumanu kana ethĩwe akosete ũmanyi. Na eka ũu, andũ makumasya andũ ma saenzi mũno. Kĩu kĩtumaa matesa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Mũmbi witũ. (Alo. 1:25) Tũkethukĩĩsya mawoni ta asu ti vinya tũkambĩĩa kũmũtia Yeova, na ti vinya wendo witũ ũkambĩĩa kũvoa.—Aevl. 3:12.
8. (a) Nĩ maũndũ ta meva matumaa athũkũmi ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ makw'a ngoo? (b) Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 136 yĩtũĩkĩĩthasya ata?
8 O na ĩngĩ, tũkakw'a ngoo na tũyĩyĩtũka, mũĩkĩĩo witũ no ũleele na tũieka kũmwenda Ngai ũndũ tũnamwendete. Nĩkwĩthĩwa nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Satani, mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtũkomanaa na maũndũ matonya kũtũtũla ngoo. (1 Yoa. 5:19) Kwa ngelekany'o, no kwĩthĩwa tũithĩnw'a nĩ ũkũũ, mathĩna ma mwĩĩ, kana kũthelelwa. Kana tũkethĩwa tũyĩmakĩa twoona tũte kwĩanĩsya maũndũ maingĩ ũndũ tũkwenda, kana tũkethĩwa tũtũlĩkĩte ngoo nũndũ wa kwona tũvĩngĩĩsĩkĩte maũndũ makalea kũthi ũndũ twĩĩkwatĩtye. Ĩndĩ mũthenya o na ũmwe, tũikaaĩse kũeka maũndũ ta asu kana mawoni ta asu matume twona Yeova ta watũmenie. Kĩla twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kũvindĩĩsya ũndũ Yeova ũtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana mavinda onthe nũtwendete. Ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 136:23 atwĩkĩĩte vinya na ndeto ii: "Ũla watũlilikanile tũte ndaĩa; nũndũ ũseo wake wĩ wendo nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene." Ũseo wĩ wendo wa Yeova ndũnyivaa o na ĩndĩĩ. Kwoou twĩkale twĩsĩ kana nĩwĩthukĩĩasya "mawĩsũvano" maitũ na nũtũtetheeasya.—Sav. 116:1; 136:24-26.
9. Vaulo aumisye va vinya wa kũendeea kũmwenda Ngai?
9 O ta mũandĩki wa Savuli ĩsu, kĩla kyanengie Vaulo vinya nĩ kũvindĩĩsya ũtethyo ũla Yeova wamũnengae kĩla ĩvinda. Aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Mwĩaĩi nĩ mũtetheesya wakwa; ndikakĩa: Mũndũ akambĩka ata?" (Aevl. 13:6) Vaulo aĩ na vinya wa kũmĩanĩsya na mathĩna ala mamũkwata nũndũ ndaĩ na nzika kana Yeova nũmwendete. Ndaaeka mathĩna mamũae ngoo. Na twĩsĩ ũu nũndũ o na ĩla waĩ mwove nĩwaandĩkie mavalũa meana ũna e na kĩeleelo kya kwĩkĩa ana-a-asa vinya. (Aev. 4:1; Avi. 1:7; Vil. 1) Vaulo ndaaĩsa kũeka kũmwenda Ngai o na atw'ĩke e ĩtatwanĩ yetete ata. We aumisye va vinya ũsu? Amwĩkwatasya "Ngai wa ũkiakisyo w'onthe; ũla ũtũkiakiasya mathĩnanĩ maitũ onthe." (2 Ako. 1:3, 4) Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Vaulo ata nĩ kana tũendeee kũmwenda Yeova o ũndũ tũmwendete?
10. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũikaaĩse kũeka kũmwenda Yeova?
10 Vaulo nĩwawetie kĩndũ kĩmwe kya vata kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũendeee kũmwenda Yeova. Ĩvinda yĩmwe aandĩkĩie athaithi ala angĩ atĩĩ: "Voyaai mũtekũeka." O na asyokie aandĩka: "Mũkĩkala na ũlũmu mboyanĩ." (1 Ath. 5:17; Alo. 12:12) Tũyĩsa kwĩthĩwa anyanyae ma Ngai ethĩwa tũivoyaa. (Sav. 86:3) Ĩla twamantha ĩvinda ĩseo tũmũtulũĩle Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ, nĩtũmũthengeeaa nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe "ũla wĩw'aa mboya." (Sav. 65:2) Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ĩla twesa kwona Yeova asũngĩa mboya sitũ, twĩw'aa twamwenda mũnango. O na kĩu kĩtumaa twĩthĩa kaĩ "Yeova e vakuvĩ na onthe ala mamwĩkaĩlaa"! (Sav. 145:18) Kwĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana Yeova nũtwendete na nũtũtw'ĩĩkaa kũtumaa tũmĩanĩsya na maũndũ onthe ala matonya kũtata mũĩkĩĩo witũ.
KWENDA ŨW'O ŨLA WĨ MBIVILIANĨ
11, 12. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twende mũno ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ?
11 Ithyĩ Aklĩsto nĩtwendete ũla w'o. Vai vangĩ tũtonya kũkwata ũw'o eka Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. Mũthenya ũmwe Yesũ aivoya Ĩthe wake amwĩie, "Ndeto yaku nĩyo w'o." (Yoa. 17:17) Kwoou nĩ kana twende ũla w'o, no nginya tũkwate ũmanyi wa w'o wa Ndeto ya Ngai. (Ako. 1:10) Ĩndĩ kũkwata ũmanyi ũsu kũitoetye. Kwasisya ũndũ mũandĩki wa Savuli ya 119 ũtũtetheesye kũelewa ũndũ mũndũ wendete ũla w'o wĩthĩawa ailyĩ. (Soma Savuli 119:97-100.) We nĩwosaa ĩvinda sua yĩikaathũa ũkasũanĩa, kana ũkavindĩĩsya, Maandĩko ala wasoma? Twavindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ tũtethekaa nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩtwĩw'aa twawenda mũnango.
12 Mũandĩki wa Savuli ĩsu asyokie asya atĩĩ: "A! Ndeto syaku syĩ mũyo kaakaanĩ wakwa! Ĩĩ, mũyo kwĩ ũkĩ wa nzũkĩ kanyw'anĩ wakwa!" (Sav. 119:103) O ta ũu, o naitũ no tũtanĩe lĩu wĩ mũyo umĩte Mbivilianĩ ũla tũnengawe nĩ ũseũvyo wa Ngai. Twaũeka wĩkalange kaakaanĩ witũ kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o, tũkeethĩawa tũtonya kũlilikana "ndeto syĩ mũyo" sya ũla w'o na tũkeethĩawa tũtonya kũitũmĩa ĩla tũũtetheesya angĩ.—Mũta. 12:10.
13. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Yelemia enda ũw'o ũla wĩ Maandĩkonĩ, na ũndũ ũsu wamũtetheeisye ata?
13 Mwathani Yelemia nĩwendete ũw'o ũla wĩ Maandĩkonĩ. Kwoona ũndũ ndeto sya Ngai syamũtethisye. Aisye: "Ndeto syaku nĩsyoonekie, nakwa naiya; na ndeto syaku kwakwa syaĩ mũyo na ũtanu wa ngoo yakwa: nũndũ nĩtanĩaw'a na syĩtwa yaku, ame Yeova, Ngai wa nguthu." (Yel. 15:16) Yelemia nĩwaĩe na athaumya ndeto sya Ngai kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o. Eekie ũu kwa kũivindĩĩsya. Kĩu kyamũtetheeisye weethĩa nũkwona wĩ ũndũ wa vata vyũ kwĩtanĩw'a na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Kwoou ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Ithyĩ nĩtwendete ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ vyũ nginya ũkethĩa nĩtũkwona wĩ ũndũ wa vata kwĩtanĩw'a na ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai na kũtavany'a Ũsumbĩ wake ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo?
14. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twende mũnango ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ?
14 Eka o kũsoma Mbivilia na mavuku maitũ, nĩ kyaũ kĩngĩ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twende mũno ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ? Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya nĩ kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi tũteũtĩĩa. Kĩla kyumwa maũmbanonĩ asu nĩtwĩmanyĩasya Mbivilia tũtũmĩĩte ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya. Ĩsu nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe nene ĩtũmĩawa kũtũmanyĩsya. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana tũelewe nesa ĩsomo ya Mũsyaĩĩsya yĩla yĩũsomwa kĩkundinĩ, nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa tũyĩseũvĩtye nesa. Nzĩa ĩmwe nzeo ya kũseũvya nĩ kũsoma maandĩko onthe ala manenganĩtwe. Matukũ aa no tumye ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya kĩsesenĩ kya jw.org, kana tũkayĩsoma nthĩnĩ wa JW Library na ithyomo mbingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ve mĩthemba ya ĩkaseti yĩu tũtonya kumya Indanetinĩ ũkethĩa ĩla tũũyĩsoma tũitũmĩa syĩndũ ta simũ, nĩ laisi mũno kũsisya maandĩko ala manenganĩtwe nthĩnĩ wa kĩla ĩsomo. Ĩndĩ o na twĩthĩwe twĩsoma mũthemba wĩva wa ĩkaseti yĩu, kũsoma maandĩko ala manenganĩtwe na kũmavindĩĩsya kũkatumaa twenda ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ mũnango.—Soma Savuli 1:2.
KŨMENDA ANA-A-ASA
15, 16. (a) Nĩ mwĩao wĩva ũwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Yoana 13:34, 35 twaĩle kũũatĩĩa? (b) Kũmenda ana-a-asa maitũ kũkonanĩtye ata na kũmwenda Ngai na kwenda ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ?
15 Ũtukũ wa mũthya Yesũ e kũũ nthĩ eeie amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "Nĩngũmũnenga mwĩao mweũ, atĩ mwendane inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ; o ũndũ namwendie, nenyu mwĩthĩwe mũkyendana o w'o. Na kwondũ wa ũu andũ onthe makamanya kana mwĩ amanyĩw'a makwa, ethĩwa mwĩthĩwa na wendo ĩnyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ."—Yoa. 13:34, 35.
16 Kũmenda ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ nĩkũkonanĩtye na kũmwenda Yeova. Ethĩwa nĩtũmwendete Yeova tũilea kũmenda ana-a-asa maitũ. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie ũũ: "Ũla ũtamwendaa mwana-a-ĩthe ũla wonaa, ndatonya kũmwenda Ngai ũla ũtaamwona." (1 Yoa. 4:20) Na eka ũu, tũyĩsa kũmwenda Yeova na ana-a-asa maitũ ethĩwa tũyendete ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ twenda ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, ũkatũsukumaa tũatĩĩe ũla mwĩao tũnengetwe wa kũmwenda Ngai na kũmenda ana-a-asa maitũ.—1 Vet. 1:22; 1 Yoa. 4:21.
17. Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkony'a ala angĩ kana nĩtũmendete?
17 Soma 1 Athesalonika 4:9, 10. Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkony'a ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ kana nĩtũmendete? No kwĩthĩwa ve mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa mũkũũ wĩ na vata wa kũtwawa maũmbanonĩ ma Kĩklĩsto. O na no kwĩthĩwa ve mwĩĩtu-a-asa ndiwa wĩ na nyũmba yaĩlĩte kũseũvw'a kũndũ kwĩ na thĩna. (Yak. 1:27) Nĩtwaĩle kũmethukĩĩsya, tũkamekĩa vinya, na kũmakiakisya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa onthe ala methĩwa makw'ĩte ngoo kana makomanĩte na ĩtatwa ya mũthemba ũngĩ, methĩwe nĩ akũũ kana nĩ ma mũika. (Nth. 12:25; Ako. 4:11) Twonanasya kana nĩtwendete ana-a-asa maitũ na ngoo yonthe ĩla twatata mũno ndeto sitũ na meko maitũ syonany'e kana nĩtũthĩnĩkĩaa mũno "ala ma nyũmba ya mũĩkĩĩo."—Aka. 6:10.
18. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkatũtetheeasya ĩla twavĩtũũkana na Aklĩsto ala angĩ?
18 Mbivilia yathanie kana "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo" ya nthĩ ĩno nthũku, andũ makeethĩwa makĩyenda na makeethĩwa na ĩtomo. (2 Tim. 3:1, 2) Ĩndĩ ithyĩ ta twĩ Aklĩsto no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito tũikaaeke kũmwenda Ngai, kwenda ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, na kwendana ithyĩ ene. Kũneena ũla w'o, mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtũtonya kũvĩtũũkana na Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla vathi ũu, onthe kĩkundinĩ nĩmaathimĩkaa mũno ĩla maeka wendo ũmatongoesye mamine mathĩna ala methĩwa vo. (Aev. 4:32; Ako. 3:14) Kwoou mwa tũikaaeke wendo witũ ũvoe! Vandũ va ũu, nĩtũendeee kũmwenda Yeova, Ndeto yake, na ana-a-asa maitũ kuma ngoonĩ.

translation:
"And because of the increase of lawlessness, the love of many will grow cold." —Matt. 24:12.
HEADINGS: 23, 24
1, 2. (a) What does Jesus' reference to Matthew 24:12 mean to faithful Christians today? (b) How did the experience of the first-century Christians show that Christ's presence and the increasing wickedness would go hand in hand? (Consider parallel accounts.)
ONE thing Jesus foretold was "the start of distressing pains" and "the love of many will grow cold." (Matt. 24:3, 12) Why should this be evident to Jehovah's Witnesses today as they observe the condition of people in general and see how little interest many have in spiritual things?
2 As they associate with people generally, Christians often find that many have no real appreciation for the importance of living according to Bible principles, nor do they value worship of God or obedience to Him. They may also be indifferent to Christian witnesses and their message.
3. Does this mean that a Christian should become discouraged when witnessing to others?
3 Jesus Christ himself emphasized the need for endurance, saying to the congregation at Ephesus: "I know your works, your patient endurance." (Rev. 2:4) Does this suggest that we can simply expect people to respond favorably to our ministry? No. We should remember that Christians live in a world where Satan has blinded people so that they cannot see the truth. (2 Cor. 4:4; Acts 26:18) However, just as the Ephesian Christians were commended for their endurance, we too can remain steadfast despite opposition. The world is filled with people who are preoccupied with material pursuits and who give little thought to spiritual matters. In fact, many are deeply engrossed in selfish interests and are unwilling to listen to good news. Often people are influenced by family traditions and personal preferences. Thus, it takes courage to stand up for what is right and to speak truthfully.
4. (a) To what extent will the love of many cool off? (b) How can our love remain strong despite trying circumstances?
4 Jesus' example encourages us to be courageous. By following his example, we can show genuine love for God, even when faced with difficulties. Millions have come to appreciate Jehovah and to worship him acceptably. Yet, many others reject the message and persecute those who proclaim it. Nevertheless, the love of those who truly value Jehovah continues to grow stronger. Let us examine how the first-century Christians in Ephesus demonstrated endurance, and let us learn from their example how we can strengthen our own love: (1) Love Jehovah, (2) imitate the example set by the faithful ones, and (3) meditate on Bible principles.
LOVING JEHOVAH
5. Why should we love God?
5 Jesus explained that the greatest commandment is to love God with all one's heart, soul, mind, and strength. He said: "You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.' This is the greatest and first commandment." (Matt. 22:37, 38) Loving Jehovah with our whole heart means being willing to obey his commands, to please him, and to defend his name. (Read Psalm 97:10.) Satan and his demons try to hinder us from loving God.
6. What benefits result from loving God?
6 People today often seek satisfaction in things other than worship. They may say they "love pleasure." (2 Tim. 3:2) These people are influenced by Satan and are drawn to "the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the showy display of one's life." (1 John 2:16) The apostle Paul warned Christians against getting involved in worldly pursuits. He wrote: "The ardent desire for riches is a root of all sorts of injurious things;" and "pursuing the desire for riches leads to ruin and destruction."—1 Cor. 6:18; 1 Tim. 6:9, 10.
7. Explain how Christians can maintain their spirituality.
7 But remember that some people may appear to be serving God, yet they have ulterior motives, and their actions do not please him. Such ones may preach fine words, but their hearts do not move them to love God and obey him. Also, many people become discouraged when they face difficulties, and they stop seeking God and obeying him. Many others may simply lose interest in spiritual things. However, most people are influenced by their environment. This can make it difficult to appreciate God's standards.—Prov. 1:25. Let us examine why we want to serve Jehovah, and why our love for him motivates us to act.—Eph. 3:12.
8. (a) What reasons might someone have for being interested in Jehovah's service? (b) How does Psalm 136 encourage us?
8 Moreover, we should always remain vigilant, because our devotion could weaken and we might start to love God less than we once did. This is because Satan constantly presents temptations to lead us astray.—1 John 5:19. For example, we may be troubled by worries, bad habits, or pressure from others. Or we may feel inclined to focus on too many activities, which makes us busy, or we may become discouraged because we see so much wickedness around us and wonder if things will ever improve. In any case, we must resist influences that cause us to forget about Jehovah or to take his blessings for granted. Psalm 136:23 reminds us of this with these words: "He delivered us from our enemies; and he showed mercy toward us, for his loving-kindness is everlasting." Jehovah's loving-kindness is truly remarkable. So let us not allow ourselves to become complacent or to think that "things just happen," but rather let us give him credit.—Ps. 116:1; 136:24-26.
9 What helped Paul to stay steadfast in his devotion to God?
9 As the psalmist David did, Paul often remembered the benefits that Jehovah had shown him throughout his life. He wrote: "I shall remember your acts of kindness, O Jehovah; I will recount your wonderful works." (Acts 13:6) Paul was encouraged by thinking about the good things Jehovah had done for him. He also realized that his fellow Christians were facing similar challenges. And like him, they needed encouragement. That is why he wrote letters filled with practical advice and heartfelt expressions of affection. (Acts 4:1; Titus 1:7; Philem. 1) Paul wanted to strengthen their devotion to God and to assure them that they were not alone. What can we learn from his example? Let us imitate his way of viewing Jehovah as "the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our tribulation."—2 Cor. 1:3, 4. Will we continue to serve Jehovah faithfully if we want to please him?
10 Why is it important for us to remind ourselves to stay devoted to Jehovah?
10 Paul pointed out something that can help us to remain steadfast in our service to Jehovah. On one occasion, he instructed fellow believers: "Pray constantly." And he added: "Do not be anxious about anything." (1 Thess. 5:17; Phil. 12:12) By regularly pouring out our heart to God in prayer, we show that we trust in him. (Ps. 86:3) Also, when we meditate on what Jesus Christ sacrificed for us, we are reminded of how much Jehovah loves us. (Ps. 65:2) And knowing that Jehovah cares for us deeply motivates us to love him in return. Furthermore, remembering that Jehovah answers our prayers encourages us to keep serving him zealously. It moves us to exclaim: "Jehovah is near everyone calling upon him!" (Ps. 145:18) Constant prayer reminds us that Jehovah supports us and helps us to cope with all the difficulties we face.
KEEP ON LOOKING TO THE EXAMPLE OF PAUL
11, 12. How can we benefit from looking to the example of Paul?
11 The apostle Paul encouraged us to do so. He often spoke of being subject to God's will. Once, Jesus quoted a scripture and said: "This is the force of my words." (John 17:17) So, if we want to live according to God's will, we need to understand what that will is. (Acts 1:10) Gaining such understanding requires effort. Consider the account of Psalm 119, which shows how someone meditated on God's Word to gain insight into his will. (Read Psalm 119:97-100.) Do you take time to ponder over what you read in the Bible? Meditating on scriptures can help us to appreciate more fully how the example of Paul encourages us to serve Jehovah zealously.
12 The psalmist wrote: "Oh, how I love your law! It is my meditation all day long." (Ps. 119:103) Indeed, we too can develop a deep love for Jehovah's Law. We can make it our constant companion, meditating on "your law" and applying it in our lives—thereby showing that we value it.—Matt. 12:10.
13 What motivated Jeremiah to do this regarding God's Word, and what can we learn from his example?
13 Jeremiah eagerly sought God's Word. He found delight in it. He said: "Your words were found, and I ate them, and your speech became to me the joy of my heart." (Jer. 15:16) Jeremiah savored and treasured God's words. This should motivate us to reflect on how much our spiritual well-being depends on God's Word. Consider this point: How can we show that we cherish God's Word and uphold its integrity?—See also paragraph 14.
14 What can help us to treasure God's Word?
14 Besides reading the Bible regularly, what else can help us to treasure God's Word? Another way is to attend congregation meetings. At each meeting, we benefit from a demonstration involving the publisher's edition of the Bible. It is a fine tool to aid our understanding. Also, if we understand a scripture read at a meeting, we can make a note of it. One excellent way to review is to read the scriptures along with the material being discussed. Many have found it helpful to use the jw.org website or the JW Library app to access various publications. With the help of these tools, we can often find scriptures while traveling without carrying a large bag, making it easier to review the material being discussed at each meeting. And if we are assigned to read a portion of the Bible during a meeting, reading the scriptures along with the material and meditating on them will help us to prepare for the meeting.—Read Psalm 1:2.
KEEPING LOVE ACTIVE
15, 16. (a) How can we show obedience to Jesus' command recorded at John 13:34, 35? (b) How does loving our brothers and sisters relate to loving God and keeping his commandments?
15 On the night of his death, Jesus told his disciples: "I am giving you a new commandment, that you love one another; just as I have loved you, you also should love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another."—John 13:34, 35.
16 Loving our brothers and sisters is closely linked to loving Jehovah. In fact, we demonstrate our love for Jehovah when we show love for our brothers and sisters. The apostle John wrote: "Whoever claims to love God yet hates his brother is a liar. For whoever loves God also loves his brother." (1 John 4:20) So, we show our love for Jehovah and our brothers and sisters when we keep active in the Christian ministry. Why? Because the ministry helps us to express our love for God and for our brothers and sisters.—1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 4:21.
17. What are some ways we can show ourselves approved to God?
17 Read 1 Thessalonians 4:9, 10. What are some ways we can show ourselves approved to God, especially when dealing with our brothers and sisters? It may involve showing affection for a spiritual brother or sister who is experiencing difficulties. Or it may involve being hospitable to those who need a place to stay. (James 1:27) We can be thoughtful, encouraging, and generous toward all our brothers and sisters, whether they are rich or poor, influential or humble. (Proverbs 12:25; Acts 4:11) Let us examine ourselves to see if we are treating our brothers and sisters with genuine warmth and kindness, or if we are becoming "aloof from the household of faith."—Acts 6:10.
18. What can help us to remain close to Christ and other Christians?
18 The Bible describes the difficult times we live in as the "last days," a time when people will be self-centered and materialistic. (2 Timothy 3:1, 2) To remain close to Christ, we must continue to prioritize worshipping Jehovah, living according to the principles found in the Bible, and pursuing spiritual growth. In this way, step by step, we can remain close to Christ. If we do so, we will likely find that our love for others becomes more heartfelt and sincere. (Ephesians 4:32; Acts 3:14) May we all strive to do so! Brothers and sisters, let us continue to worship Jehovah, his Son, and our fellow worshippers zealously.

text:
"Keka Yeova wakaa nyũmba, matethya wĩa mana ala mamyaka."
1-3. Andũ matwaanĩte makwatawa nĩ mathĩna meva? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MWANA-A-ASA ũmwe wĩkalanĩtye nesa na kĩveti kyake kwa myaka 38 aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũkekĩa kĩthito vyũ kuma ngoonĩ na ũyonany'a kana nũkwenda mũtwaano waku ũendeee nesa, Yeova ndalea ũkũathima." Vate nzika, nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka mũndũ na mũka makatanĩa kwĩkalany'a vamwe na kũtethany'a mavindanĩ ma thĩna.—Nth. 18:22.
2 Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, andũ matwaanĩte mailea kũkwatwa nĩ "mathĩna mwĩĩnĩ." (1 Ako. 7:28) Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ kũkomana na tũmathĩna tũla tumĩlaa kĩla mũthenya kũilea kũmaitavĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na ethĩwa mũtwaano ũseũvĩte ata, andũ ti eanĩu na nũndũ wa ũu mavinda angĩ no maee ngewa makavĩtũũkana, kana ũmwe akaũmĩsya ũla ũngĩ ngoonĩ, kana o akamũelewa naĩ. (Yak. 3:2, 5, 8) Na ĩndĩ ve angĩ methĩawa makwatene mũno wĩanĩ na me na syana sya kũea. Namo angĩ methĩawa makuĩte maũndũ maingĩ ilĩkonĩ na manoete mũno nginya ũkethĩa mai na ĩvinda ya kũtinda vamwe malũlũmĩlye mũtwaano. Mathĩna ma mbesa, mathĩna ma mwĩĩ, kana o mathĩna angĩ nĩmatonya kũthi maolete ndaĩa ĩla manenganĩte na wendo ũla maĩ naw'o. Na eka ũu, mũtwaano ũkwoneka wĩ o mũseo nũtonya kwanangwa vyũ nĩ "mawĩa ma mwĩĩ," ta ũlaalai, mĩmeo mĩthũku, ũmaitha, ĩteta, kĩwĩu, mothilĩku, na ngananĩo.—Aka. 5:19-21.
3 Kũthũkya ũvoo, andũ aingĩ 'mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo' nĩmeyendete na me na mawoni matosanĩte na ma Ngai, na kyu nĩkyanangaa mũtwaano. (2 Tim. 3:1-4) Na ĩndĩ kũmina ũvoo, ve mũmaitha mwai ũsyĩmanĩte mũno na mĩtwaano na ndekwenda kũmĩnenga nzeve o na vanini. Nĩkyo kĩtumi mũtũmwa Vetelo ũkũtũtaa atĩĩ: "Mũvinganĩsya wenyu ndevili angangaa kũũ na kũũ ta mũnyambũ ũkũluma, aimantha mũndũ aye."—1 Vet. 5:8; Ũvu. 12:12.
4. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma andũ matwaanĩte methĩwa na mũtwaano mũlũmu na maitanĩa kwĩkalany'a vamwe?
4 Mwana-a-asa ũmwe kuma Japan easya: "Ve ĩvinda yĩmwe naĩ mũthelele vyũ. Na nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu ndyaeaa ngewa nesa na kĩveti kyakwa, o nakyo nĩkyambĩĩe kũthĩnĩka mũno kĩlĩkonĩ. Na o mĩtũkĩ nĩkĩnasyokie kĩnakwatwa nĩ mathĩna manene ma mwĩĩ. Maũndũ asu onthe matumaa mavinda angĩ tũvĩtũũkana." Nĩ w'o kana vai ũndũ andũ meka maikakwatwe nĩ mathĩna amwe, ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana maitonya kũmasinda. Ala matwaanĩte mamũthokya Yeova mũtwaanonĩ woo, no methĩwe na mũtwaano mũlũmu na makatanĩa kwĩkalany'a vamwe. (Soma Savuli 127:1.) Kwoou, ekai twone maũndũ atano ala matonya kũtuma andũ matwaanĩte methĩwa na mũtwaano mũlũmu. Na ĩndĩ tũyona ũndũ wendo ũtonya kũtuma ala matwaanĩte maatĩĩa maũndũ asu nesa. Maũndũ asu atano no tũmaelekany'e na mavali ma kwaka, naw'o wendo no tũũelekany'e na simiti wa kũmakwatany'a.
MŨTHOKYEI YEOVA MŨTWAANONĨ WENYU
5, 6. Mũndũ na mũka matonya ata kũmũthokya Yeova mũtwaanonĩ woo?
5 Kĩtuĩ kya mũtwaano mũseo nĩ kĩĩ: kwĩnyivĩsya na kwĩkala wĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ũla wambĩĩisye mũtwaano. (Soma Mũtavan'ya 4:12.) Mũndũ na mũka nĩmatonya kũmũthokya Yeova mũtwaanonĩ woo kwa kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla ũtũnengete nũndũ nũtwendete. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa athaithi ma Ngai ma tene: "Matũ maku makeew'a ndeto ĩtina waku, ĩkyasya, Nzĩa nĩ ĩno, endaai nayo; yĩla mwĩathũka kw'oko kwa aũme, na yĩla mwĩathũka kw'oko kwa aka." (Isa. 30:20, 21) Ũmũnthĩ andũ matwaanĩte nĩmatonya 'kwĩw'a' ndeto ya Yeova masoma Mbivilia vamwe. (Sav. 1:1-3) Ũndũ ũngĩ matonya kwĩka malũlũmĩlye mũtwaano woo nĩ kwĩka Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ kwa nzĩa matonya kũtanĩa na kwĩkĩwa vinya. O nakw'o kũvoya vamwe kĩla mũthenya nĩ kwa vata vyũ nĩ kana mũtwaano woo wĩthĩwe na vinya ũndũ ũtanangwa nĩ nthĩ ĩno ya Satani.
6 Gerhard kuma Germany easya atĩĩ: "Ĩla twaasya ũtanu nũndũ wa kũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ ũndũ kana kũlea kũeleanwa, ũtao ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai nũtũtetheeasya tũekeanĩe na tũyĩthwa na wũmĩĩsyo. Mũtwaano ndwĩsa kwaĩla maũndũ asu mate vo." Mũndũ na mũka matata vyũ kũmũthokya Ngai mũtwaanonĩ woo kwa kũmũthũkũma vamwe, ngwatanĩo yoo nake nĩlũlũmĩlaa, na ndũũ yoo ĩikamĩĩa na mayĩkalany'a na ũtanu.
AŨME, TŨMĨAI ŨKŨMŨ WENYU KWA NZĨA YA WENDO
7. Aũme maĩlĩte kũtũmĩa ũkũmũ woo ata?
7 Mũndũũme atũmĩa ũkũmũ wake nesa, kĩu nĩkĩtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũtwaano wake na kĩituma ekalany'a nesa na mũka. Mbivilia yaasya: "Mũtwe wa kĩla mũndũ mũũme nĩ Klĩsto; na mũtwe wa mũndũ mũka nĩ mũũme." (1 Ako. 11:3) Mĩsoa ĩla ĩthengeanĩe na mũsoa ũsu nĩeleetye ũndũ aũme maĩle kũtũmĩa ũkũmũ woo. Maĩle kũũtũmĩa o ũndũ Klĩsto ũtũmĩaa ũkũmũ wake ĩũlũ wa mũndũũme. Yesũ ndeekaa maũndũ na kĩthũi na ndaĩ mũmũ. Ĩndĩ aĩ tei, aĩ mũuu, aĩ na wĩnyivyo ngoonĩ, nĩwendete andũ, na nĩwamaeleawa.—Mt. 11:28-30.
8. Mwana-a-asa atonya kwĩka ata ethĩwa nũkwenda mũka amũnenge ndaĩa na aimwenda?
8 Vai vata aũme Aklĩsto makatindaa kwĩyĩtĩsya ndaĩa kuma kwa iveti syoo. Vandũ va ũu meĩtwe ũũ: "Ĩkalai na iveti syenyu kwĩanana na ũmanyi [kana, kũisũanĩa kana kũsielewa, kwosana na maelesyo ma kwongeleela ma NWT]." Aũme nĩmaĩle kũnenga iveti syoo "ndaĩa, ta mũio ũte na vinya." (1 Vet. 3:7) Methĩwe me vandũ me elĩ kana me na andũ angĩ, nĩmaĩle kwonany'a kana iveti syoo nĩ sya vata mũno. Ata? Kwa kũtũmĩa ndeto syĩ ndaĩa na kũsyĩka maũndũ kwa nzĩa yĩ na ĩnee. (Nth. 31:28) Ĩla mwana-a-asa watũmĩa ũkũmũ wake kwa nzĩa ĩsu, mũka nũmwendaa mũno na aimũne ndaĩa, nake Ngai aimaathima.
IVETI, ĨNYIVĨSYEI AŨME MENYU
9. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva kĩveti kĩtonya kwonany'a kana nĩkĩnyivasya?
9 Kũmwenda Yeova kuma ngoonĩ nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa myolooto yake nĩkũtũtetheeasya twĩnyivye ungu wa kw'oko kwake kwĩ vinya. (1 Vet. 5:6) Kwoou nzĩa ĩmwe ya vata kĩveti kyonanasya kana nĩkĩnengete ũkũmũ wa Yeova ndaĩa nĩ kwa kũkwatĩanĩa na mũũme maũndũnĩ ma mũsyĩ. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Iveti, ĩnyivĩsyei aũme menyu, ũndũ waĩle nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi." (Ako. 3:18) Nĩ w'o kana kĩveti kĩyĩsa kwĩtĩkĩlana na motwi onthe ala mũũme wĩkaa. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa kĩveti nĩkĩnyivasya, kĩkaatĩĩaa na ngenda motwi ma mũũme ethĩwa nĩmosanĩte na mĩao ya Ngai.—1 Vet. 3:1.
10. Nĩ ũseo mwaũ wĩthĩawa mũsyĩ ĩla kĩveti kyenyivya nũndũ nĩkyendete mũũme?
10 Kĩveti nĩkĩnengetwe kĩanda kya mwanya kya kwĩthĩwa 'mũtindany'a' wa mũũme. (Mal. 2:14) Nĩkyo kĩtumi kĩtetheeasya mũũme ĩla ũkwĩka motwi kwa kũelesya mawoni makyo na kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ, ĩndĩ kĩyĩka ũu kĩ na ndaĩa na kĩnyivĩtye. Nake mũndũũme mũĩ nũteaa kũtũ nesa ĩla mũka ũkwĩyĩelesya. (Nth. 31:10-31) Ĩla kĩveti kyenyivya nũndũ nĩkyendete mũũme, mũsyĩ ũsu nũmeasya ũtanu, mũuo, na ngwatanĩo, na elĩ mekalaa me eanĩe nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩmesĩ memwendeesya Ngai.—Aev. 5:22.
ENDEEAI KŨEKEANĨA ENE KWA ENE
11. Nĩkĩ kũekeanĩa nĩ kwa vata?
11 Kũekeanĩa nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata mũno ũtonya kũtuma mũtwaano wĩkala wĩ mũlũmu. Mũtwaano nũlũlũmĩlaa ĩla ala matwaanĩte 'moomĩanĩsya ũmwe kwa ũla ũngĩ, na maekeanĩa ene kwa ene.' (Ako. 3:13) Ĩndĩ nĩwanangĩkaa ĩla mũndũ waia mavĩtyo ala waaĩkwa ngoonĩ, na ĩndĩ ĩla wesa kũvĩtĩw'a aimatũmĩa kũkũna ũla ũngĩ. O tondũ myalĩka yĩ ngũtanĩ ĩtonya kwananga mwako, now'o kũkundĩka ngoo na kwoveea ũthatu kwanangaa ngoo na kũituma wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũekeanĩa. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, mũtwaano nũlũlũmĩlaa ĩla mũndũ na mũka maekeanĩa o ũndũ Yeova ũmaekeaa.—Mika 7:18, 19.
12. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva wendo 'ũvw'ĩkaa wingĩ wa naĩ'?
12 Wendo wa w'o "ndũtalĩlaa ũthũku." Ĩndĩ "nũvw'ĩkaa wingĩ wa naĩ." (1 Ako. 13:4, 5; soma 1 Vetelo 4:8.) Ũu nĩ kwasya kana mũndũ wendete ũla ũngĩ ndatalaa mavinda ala ũkũmũekea. Ĩla mũtũmwa Vetelo wakũlilye Yesũ aĩle kũekea mũndũ mavinda meana ata, Yesũ amũsũngĩie atĩĩ: "Kũvika mũonza kũndũ mĩongo mũonza." (Mt. 18:21, 22) Kĩla Yesũ wawetaa nĩ kana vai mũthya wa mavinda ala Mũklĩsto waĩle kũekea angĩ.—Nth. 10:12. *
13. Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ndũkaatw'ĩke mũndũ ũtaekeaa?
13 Mwĩĩtu-a-asa Annette easya ũũ: "Andũ matwaanĩte malea kwĩthĩwa na kĩmanyĩo kya kũekeanĩa, ũthatu nĩwĩanaa ngoonĩ syoo na maieka kũĩkĩĩana, na kyu nĩkyanangaa mũtwaano. Mwaekeanĩa, mũtwaano wenyu ũendeeaa kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũlũmu na ndũũ yenyu nĩseũvĩĩaa." Nĩ kana ndũkaatw'ĩke mũndũ ũtaekeaa, tata wĩthĩwe mũndũ ũtũngaa mũvea na wonaa maũndũ ala mekwĩkwa nĩ ala angĩ me ma vata. Manyĩa kũkathaa mũemeu kana mũkau. (Ako. 3:15) Weeka ũu ũkeethĩawa ũtonya kũekea ũla ũngĩ aũvĩtĩsya. Na nũndũ wa ũu ũkakwata mũuo wa kĩlĩko, mũkeethĩwa na ngwatanĩo, na Ngai akamũathima.—Alo. 14:19.
ATĨĨAI ŨLA MWOLOOTO WĨ NGUMA
14, 15. Ũla mwolooto wĩ nguma nĩw'o wĩva, na ũtonya kũtũmĩwa ata mũtwaanonĩ?
14 Ndũlea kwĩthĩwa wendete kũnengwa ndaĩa. Nĩwĩw'aa mũyo ĩla andũ makwĩthukĩĩsya na matata ũkũelewa. Ĩndĩ waaĩw'a mũndũ ayasya, "Nĩmwĩka ũndũ wambĩka nũndũ mũsyĩ wa ũtukũ ũtũngĩlawa vala wesĩla"? Ĩla mũndũ wasya ũu mavinda amwe no ũmũelewe, ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩtwĩĩte atĩĩ: 'Ndũkasye, Ngamwĩka o tondũ ũmbĩkĩte.' (Nth. 24:29) O na eka ũu, Yesũ mwene nĩwawetie nzĩa nzeo ya kũmina mathĩna. Mwolooto ũla wanenganie wĩ nguma mũno, na nĩw'o ũũ: "Ũndũ ũla mũkwenda kwĩkwa nĩ andũ, o ta ũu mekei o w'o." (Luka 6:31) Vau Yesũ oonanasya kana twaĩle kũkua andũ o ũndũ ithyĩ ene twendaa matũkue, ĩndĩ ti kũĩvanĩsya ũthũku na ũthũku. Kwoou kwosana na mũsoa ũsu, kĩla ũmwe nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano aĩle kwĩka ũla ũngĩ kĩla ũtonya kwenda ekwe.
15 Andũ matwaanĩte nĩmatonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũtwaano woo ethĩwa kĩla ũmwe akekĩa kĩthito aelewe ũndũ ũla ũngĩ ũkwĩw'a na aianĩsya vata wake. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe kuma South Africa easya atĩĩ: "Nĩtũtatĩte mũno kũatĩĩa ũla mwolooto wĩ nguma." Aendeee kwasya ũũ: "Nĩ w'o ve mavinda twĩw'aa woo, ĩndĩ nĩtwĩkĩaa kĩthito kĩla ũmwe eke ũla ũngĩ o tondũ ũtonya kwenda ekwe, na ũu nĩ kwasya kana nĩtũnenganae ndaĩa na kĩla ũmwe nũtataa one ũla ũngĩ e wa vata."
16. Nĩ maũndũ meva andũ matwaanĩte mataĩle kwĩkana?
16 Ethĩwa nĩwĩsĩ mũemeu kana mũkau e wonzu mũna ndũkawumaalye, kana ethĩwa nĩwĩsĩ kaũndũ kake kasaanĩtye ndũkatindĩae kũkaweta, o na ethĩwa wĩĩka kũmũvũĩa ngũĩ. Lilikana kana mũtwaano ti kĩng'ang'a kya masindano, ũkethĩaa atĩ mwĩsisya nũũ wĩ vinya, kana nũũ wĩ wasya mũtũlu, na nũũ wĩsĩ kũneena naĩ vyũ. Kwa w'o, ithyonthe nĩtũvĩtasya na mavinda angĩ nĩtũũmĩasya ala angĩ. Ĩndĩ vai kĩndũ kyaĩle kũtuma ala matwaanĩte makavana kana ũmwe akatavya ũla ũngĩ naĩ, o na ndaĩle kũmũluuta kana kũmũkũna.—Soma Nthimo 17:27; 31:26.
17. Aũme matonya ata kũatĩĩa ũla mwolooto wĩ nguma?
17 O na kau kũndũ kũmwe ala mathĩnasya kana makavũa aka moo monekaa nemo aũme, Mbivilia ĩtwĩaa atĩĩ: 'Mũmĩĩsya wa kũthata e kavaa kwĩ ũla wĩ na ũtonyi; na ũla ũsumbĩkaa veva wake, e kavaa kwĩ ũla ũkwataa ndũa.' (Nth. 16:32) No nginya mũndũ ethĩwe na ũkũmbaũ mwingĩ vyũ ethĩwa nũkwenda asumbĩke veva wake na aiatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya mũndũũme ũla mũseo vyũ waaĩkala kũũ nthĩ, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto. Ũla ũtavasya mũka ndeto nthũku kana akamũkũna, ndesa kũtalwa ta mũndũũme, na mũndũ wa mũthemba ũsu nĩwanangaa ũnyanya wake na Yeova. Mũandĩki wa Savuli, Ndaviti, ũla waĩ ngũmbaũ yĩ vinya, aisye atĩĩ: "Thataai, ĩndĩ mũikeke naĩ; yĩla mũkomete mokomonĩ menyu, neenany'ai kĩla mũndũ na ngoo yake, na ĩthĩwai mũvindĩtye."—Sav. 4:4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
"ĨVW'ĨKEI WENDO"
18. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũendeee kũlũlũmĩlya wendo wenyu?
18 Soma 1 Akolintho 13:4-7. Wendo nĩw'o kĩndũ kĩla kya vata vyũ nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Ĩvw'ĩkei ngoo yĩ na ĩnee ya kwĩw'anĩa tei, wĩnyivyo, ũuu, wũmĩĩsyo. Na mbee wa maũndũ aa onthe ĩvw'ĩkei wendo, naw'o nĩ wovano wa wĩanĩu." (Ako. 3:12, 14) Mwendana na ngoo ntheu tondũ Klĩsto ũtwendete, mũtwaano wenyu ndũkathingithĩka. Wendo ta ũsu no ũelekanw'e na simiti ũla ũkwatanasya mavali nyũmba ĩyakwa. Mũtwaano wa mũthemba ũsu wĩthĩawa wĩ mũlũmu ũkethĩa ndũthingithw'a nĩ maũndũ ta mwĩkalo mũsaanu wa mũemeu kana mũkau, mathĩna manene ma mwĩĩ, thĩna mwingĩ wa mbesa, na mathĩna metu ala maumanaa na athoni kana andũ ma mũsyĩ ũla kĩveti kĩtwaĩtwe.
19, 20. (a) Ala matwaanĩte matonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana malũlũmĩlye mũtwaano woo na mayĩkalany'a na ũtanu? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
19 No nginya andũ matwaanĩte methĩwe mendene vyũ, malũmanĩtye, na mayĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana mũtwaano waĩle. Vandũ va kũtaanĩsya ĩla mathĩna maumĩla, ala matwaanĩte maĩlĩte kũtata ũndũ matonya methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na ndũmu ĩndĩ ti o kwĩkalany'a nĩkwĩthĩwa atĩ vai ũndũ ũngĩ vekwa. Aklĩsto ala mamwĩyumĩsye Yeova vyũ na masũvĩanaa methĩawa mendene na makamwenda Yeova, na nũndũ "wendo ndũnyivaa o na ĩndĩĩ," ĩla mathĩna maumĩla nĩmamaminaa.—1 Ako. 13:8; Mt. 19:5, 6; Aevl. 13:4.
20 Kwĩthĩwa na mũtwaano mũlũmu na kwĩkalany'a mwĩ na ũtanu ti ũndũ wĩ laisi nũndũ twĩkalĩte "mavinda ma mũisyo." (2 Tim. 3:1) Ĩndĩ kwa vinya wa Yeova, ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka. O na vailyĩ ũu, no nginya ala matwaanĩte maendeee kũkitana na mĩkalĩle mĩthũku ĩla ĩtambĩte mũno ũmũnthĩ. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩũtetheesya aũme na aka mamanye ũndũ matonya kũsũvĩa mũtwaano woo ndũkanangwe nĩ mĩkalĩle mĩthũku ĩla yĩ kw'o.
^ kal. 12 O na kau andũ matwaanĩte nĩmatataa maekeanĩe na maimina thĩna ũla wĩ katĩ woo, ĩla ũmwe weeka ũlaalai Mbivilia nĩyĩtĩkĩlĩtye ũla ũte na ĩvĩtyo atw'e ethĩwa nũkũekea ũla ũngĩ kana nũkũthasya mũtwaano. (Mt. 19:9) Sisya Ũvoo wa Kwongeleela" Woni wa Mbivilia Ĩũlũ wa Kũthasya Mũtwaano na Kũtaanĩsya" ĩthangũnĩ ya 219-221, ĩvukunĩ 'Wendo wa Ngai.'
