translation:
"When Jehovah builds a house, the foundations will be strong and lasting for years."
1-3. What reasons do faithful ones have for being encouraged? (Consider practical examples.)
ONE young man served loyally with zeal for 38 years, then he said: "To feel approved and to continue serving Jehovah faithfully, I need to keep reminding myself of the importance of remaining loyal."—Prov. 18:22.
2 Indeed, we live in times when faithful ones are often tested by "difficult times." (1 Thess. 7:28) Why is this so? Because we are surrounded by imperfect humans who make mistakes daily. For example, a husband may say something thoughtless, causing his wife to feel hurt, or someone might offend us intentionally or unintentionally. (Jas. 3:2, 5, 8) Also, many people are struggling with problems related to finances or raising children. Furthermore, some individuals are easily influenced by negative thoughts and can become discouraged or resentful. But such difficult times—whether they involve spouses, family members, or others—can sometimes lead to positive results, helping us to show love and compassion. And in this regard, a husband should recognize that his marriage can be strengthened if he does not allow himself to be overwhelmed by "irritating habits," such as nagging, selfishness, laziness, talkativeness, stubbornness, and jealousy.—Col. 5:19-21.
3 Sadly, many people today 'have an appearance of devotion but disown the power of it,' and their conduct dishonors God. (2 Tim. 3:1-4) And because of this, some Christians find it hard to maintain peace with fellow believers and avoid getting involved in disputes. This is why the apostle Peter urges us: "Be vigilant, because your adversary the Devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour."—1 Pet. 5:8; Rev. 12:12.
4 What then can help us to deal with difficult people and challenging situations in a peaceful way?
4 A young woman in Japan once said: "I used to get very upset when my parents criticized me. I felt hurt and angry, and I often argued with them. But gradually I realized that much of my frustration came from unreasonable expectations. I learned that sometimes we need to forgive others and let go of things." Is it possible that many problems arise simply because people have unrealistic expectations? However, if we trust in Jehovah and seek his guidance, we will be able to cope with difficult people and challenging situations. (Read Psalm 127:1.) Let us now consider five practical suggestions that can help us to deal with difficult people peacefully. And later we will discuss another important principle that can help us to maintain unity.
HOW TO DEAL WITH DIFFICULT PEOPLE
5, 6. What can a husband and wife do to honor Jehovah in their dealings with each other?
5 One key to a successful marriage is this: Be considerate and kind toward your mate. (Read Ephesians 4:12.) Husbands and wives can honor Jehovah by being willing to compromise and by showing empathy. The following example illustrates how godly principles can be applied: A father told his children: "Choose what is right, do not merely say, 'It is good.' Go and do it; turn away from evil and do good." (Isa. 30:20, 21) Similarly, Christian husbands and wives can benefit from regularly reading God's Word together. (Ps. 1:1-3) Another way to strengthen your marriage is to take time to meditate on spiritual matters and to pray together. Also, remember that resisting temptation and remaining faithful to Jehovah requires effort, and Satan will try to undermine your relationship.
6 Gerhard from Germany explains: "When we were going through a difficult time, or when we had problems communicating, knowing that God's law required us to love one another helped us to persevere and to accept each other's imperfections." A husband and wife show their love for God by supporting each other in their spirituality, and they find that their bond becomes stronger and more satisfying.
FAMILIES, SHOW LOVE FOR ONE ANOTHER
7. Are family heads doing so?
7 Family heads need to show love for their families, because this helps them to maintain a strong family bond and to have a peaceful home. The Bible says: "The head of every man is Christ; the head of a woman is the man." (1 Cor. 11:3) Problems arise when family members do not respect the authority of the head of the household. Christ set an excellent example for family heads to imitate. He was understanding and compassionate, and he showed genuine concern for people, patiently teaching and helping them.—Matt. 11:28-30.
8. Can a young person sometimes feel that his parents are unreasonable?
8 At times young Christians may feel that their parents are being unfair. They should remember the principle: "Honor your father and your mother" (that is, show them respect and appreciation, and be willing to learn from their wise counsel—see the footnote on NWT). Parents should also try to be reasonable and avoid making demands that are unrealistic. (Prov. 31:28) But if a young person shows love for his family, his parents will likely appreciate him and will be more understanding.
WIVES, RESPECT YOUR HUSBANDS
9. How can a wife show that she respects her husband?
9 Showing Jehovah loyalty by supporting his arrangements helps wives to demonstrate deep love for him. (1 Pet. 5:6) One way a wife can show that she respects her husband is by cooperating with him and avoiding conflicts over minor matters. The Bible says: "Wives, be subject to your husbands, so that those who do not obey the Word may be won over by your conduct."—1 Pet. 3:1.
10. What if a Christian wife feels that her husband is wrong about something?
10 A wife should remember that she is a helper to her husband. (Prov. 31:10) This means that she should support him, listen to his advice, and avoid contradicting him, especially in public. However, a thoughtful wife will also try to reason with her husband privately. She can then appeal to his conscience and help him see things from God's viewpoint.—1 Pet. 3:1.
ENDAVOR TO BE CONSIDERATE OF ONE ANOTHER
11. Why is being considerate important?
11 Being considerate is an essential quality that helps maintain peace in the family. Peace is disturbed when family members "speak against each other," or find fault with one another. (Acts 3:13) It is wise to be patient with those who make mistakes, and to be willing to forgive them. Otherwise, small disagreements could easily escalate into major conflicts. So, instead of dwelling on what others have done wrong, focus on showing love and extending kindness, and strive to overlook offenses. In this way, peace is preserved in the family.—Micah 7:18, 19.
12. How can we show that we 'are ready to forgive generously'?
12 Love is "patient and kind." It "does not keep account of a wrong." (1 Cor. 13:4, 5; read 1 Peter 4:8.) This means that a loving person does not constantly bring up past mistakes. For example, the apostle Peter asked Jesus how often he should forgive someone. Jesus told him: "Not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!" (Matt. 18:21, 22) Jesus showed that Christians should be willing to forgive others freely.—Luke 10:12. *
13. What can you do to help someone who has wronged you?
13 A sister named Annette explained: "Sometimes people find it hard to apologize because they fear that an apology will be seen as an admission of guilt, and they don't want to lose face. But when you apologize, you show humility. Your humility can help the other person feel less defensive." If you can forgive someone who has wronged you, you will experience the joy of being relieved from a heavy burden and your relationship will improve. Remember to be reasonable and understanding. (Acts 3:15) This principle can also help you to forgive yourself. And if you have been hurt by someone, pray to God about it.—Ps. 14:19.
SHOW LOVE BY YOUR ACTIONS
14, 15. How can we show love by our actions, and why is this important?
14 People often respond well to kindness. It takes effort to understand others and their difficulties. Have you ever wondered what motivates someone to say, "I don't care what happens tonight, I just want to get even"? That person may be hurting deeply inside, so the Bible advises us: "Before you retaliate, listen carefully." (Prov. 24:29) Also, Jesus showed remarkable empathy toward those he met. The Golden Rule expresses this same principle: "Always treat others as you would like them to treat you." (Luke 6:31) So Jesus taught us that we should try to see things from another person's viewpoint before judging them. In effect, put yourself in their place. Everyone appreciates it when someone tries to understand his feelings.
15 Many people find it difficult to forgive others, especially when they feel wronged or hurt. A young man in South Africa explained: "It wasn't easy to let go of my anger." He continued: "But I realized that holding on to resentment only hurts myself, and I wanted to be able to move forward. This helped me to start forgiving others and to stop dwelling on past wrongs."
16. Why do many people struggle to forgive?
16 Sometimes forgiveness seems impossible when someone has deeply wounded us, or sometimes forgiveness seems unfair when the wrongdoer shows no remorse, or sometimes we simply don't want to forgive. However, remember that unforgiveness can lead to bitterness, causing emotional pain, physical illness, and strained relationships. Therefore, we should strive to forgive, and seek help from others if needed. In fact, often we harm ourselves and others more by refusing to forgive than by extending forgiveness—Read Proverbs 17:27; 31:26.
17. What can help us to forgive others?
17 And if our heart is inclined to excuse or justify wrongdoing because it seems minor, the Bible reminds us: "He who is quick to anger will stir up strife, but he who is slow to anger is better." (Prov. 16:32) Often a person burdened with much guilt feels unworthy of forgiveness and may be afraid to approach God, but Jesus Christ assures him that God is willing to forgive anyone who sincerely repents. Those who refuse to accept forgiveness deprive themselves of peace and risk damaging their relationship with Jehovah. The psalmist David, who himself made serious mistakes, wrote: "Watch over my mouth, and let me not fall prey to evil, nor indulge in wickedness." —Ps. 4:4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
"SHOW KINDNESS"
18. Why is it important to continue showing kindness?
18 Read 1 Corinthians 13:4-7. Love is essential for maintaining unity. The Bible says: "Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful." (1 Cor. 13:4, 5) Be considerate of others, and remember that Christians are united by love. Your marriage will be stronger if you show each other kindness, just as cement holds bricks together. A family can overcome difficulties such as financial problems, illness, loss of employment, or disagreements with relatives if they show kindness and understanding.
19, 20. (a) What questions might arise when we try to maintain unity and when faced with challenges? (b) What will help us to remain steadfast?
19 Many married couples face trials, pressures, and misunderstandings. Sometimes, it seems impossible to maintain their unity. But those who are determined to make their marriage work will seek ways to resolve conflicts peacefully and lovingly. True Christians value their relationship with Jehovah and want to please him, so they strive to apply the principle that "love never fails."—1 Cor. 13:8; Matt. 19:5, 6; Eph. 13:4.
20 Maintaining marital unity and facing challenges require effort. We need to avoid being "lovers of ourselves." (2 Tim. 3:1) By putting Jehovah first, we demonstrate our reasonableness. And if we do so, we will continue to strengthen our marriage despite the difficulties we encounter. This lesson highlights the importance of regularly examining ourselves and identifying areas where we can improve our conduct toward our mate.
^ kal. 12 Often, married couples struggle because they have different backgrounds or personalities. One partner may be more talkative than the other, or they may have differing views on how to raise their children or handle finances. (Matt. 19:9) See the publication *Reasoning From the Scriptures*, pages 219-221, under the heading "The Bible's View of Divorce and Separation."

text:
"Yesũ aendeea akyũĩva na akĩana, e mwaĩlu kwa Ngai na kwa andũ."—LUKA 2:52.
MBATHI: 41, 11
1, 2. (a) Nĩ maũndũ meva mathĩnasya asyai ĩla syana syoo syĩ na myaka katĩ wa 13 na 19? (b) Nĩ maũndũ meva Aklĩsto ma mũika matonya kwĩanĩsya?
ASYAI Aklĩsto mew'aa mũyo mũno ĩla mwana woo wavatiswa. * Kwa ngelekany'o, syana inya sya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Berenice syavatisiwe itavikĩtye myaka 14. Easya atĩĩ: "Tweewie mũyo mwingĩ mũno. Twatũngie mũvea mũno nũndũ syana sitũ nĩsyendie kũmũthũkũma Yeova. O na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩtweesĩ kana syana isu ikakwatwa nĩ mawetu maingĩ o iendeee kwĩana." No kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kũmũelewa Berenice ethĩwa wĩ na syana syĩ na myaka katĩ wa 13 na 19 kana ikilyĩ kũvika vau.
2 Mũsomi ũmwe nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩte kana syana syĩ katĩ wa myaka 13 na 19 nithĩnasya asyai na syo mbene nikwatawa nĩ mathĩna. Ĩndĩ asyokete akasya ũũ: "Kwasya mwana nĩ wa mũika ti kwasya kana 'e na mbũsũ' na kana e na 'wana.' Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu akiitawa ngoo mĩtũkĩ nĩ maũndũ, ethĩawa e na wendi wa kũtindany'a na anyanyae, na ethĩawa e na ũĩ wa kwĩka maũndũ." Kwoou ĩvindanĩ yĩu amũika no matume ndũũ ngamu na Yeova, makeka motwi ta kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme Yeova na maiatĩĩa mĩao yake, na makevangĩĩa maũndũ ala makeanĩsya ũthũkũminĩ wake. Amũika no matũmĩe ĩvinda yĩu kwĩana kĩ-veva o tondũ Yesũ weekie ĩla waĩ wa mũika. (Soma Luka 2:52.) Ĩndĩ ĩla syana syĩ myakanĩ ĩsu we mũsyai waĩlĩte kwĩka ata? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Yesũ woonanisye kana e na wendo, wĩnyivyo, na ũmanyi ĩla watw'ĩkie mũndũ mũima. Maũndũ asu matonya kũũtetheesya ata ũmanyĩsye mwana waku amũthũkũme Yeova?
ENDA MWANA WAKU
3. Nĩkĩ Yesũ waĩ atonya kwĩta atũmwa make anyanyae?
3 Yesũ aĩ ndũũ mũno na amanyĩw'a make na nĩwalũmanĩtye namo. (Soma Yoana 15:15.) Ĩvindanĩ ya andũ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ, mũndũ ndatavasya ngombo syake maũndũ make ma kĩ-nthĩnĩ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ aĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Aĩ vwana wa amanyĩw'a make aĩkĩĩku, na aĩ mũnyanyae woo. Atindanasya namo, akamaelesya ũndũ ũkwĩw'a, na nĩwamethukĩĩasya nesa ĩla meũmũelesya kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ syoo. (Mko. 6:30-32) Kũea ngewa ta kũu nĩkw'o kwatumie Yesũ atuma ndũũ ngamu na atũmwa make na kwatuma amatetheesya meyũmbany'e kwondũ wa ianda ila syaĩ mbee woo ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai.
4. Ũtonya ata kũtuma ndũũ na mwana waku na ũyĩthĩa no ũkũnengete ndaĩa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
4 Mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Michael wĩ na syana ilĩ aĩtye atĩĩ: "O na kau ithyĩ asyai tũyĩsa kwĩanana na syana sitũ, no twĩthĩwe anyanyae masyo." Andũ me ndũũ makothaa kũtinda ĩmwe mũno. Nũndũ wa ũu, sũanĩa mũno na ũivoya nĩ kana ũsisye kana no ũolange masaa ala ũtũmĩaa wĩanĩ na maũndũnĩ angĩ nĩ kenda ũkwate mwanya mwingangĩ wa kũtindany'a na syana syaku. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana andũ me ndũũ methĩawa mendete maũndũ mavw'anene. Kwoou tata mũno ũtanĩe maũndũ ala mwana waku ũtanĩaa ta mbathi, sinema, kana mathaũ. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Ilaria wa Italy aĩtye ũũ: "Asyai makwa nĩmendie mũno kũmanya mbathi ila neethukĩĩasya. O na eka ũu, ĩthe-akwa nĩwatw'ĩkie mũnyanyawa ũla mũnene, na neew'aa nĩ mwĩanĩe ĩla ngũmũelesya tũmaũndũ twakwa twa kĩ-nthĩnĩ." Kũtuma ndũũ na syana syaku na kũitetheesya syĩthĩwe syĩ "ndũũ" na Yeova kũyĩsa kũtuma iũvũthya. (Sav. 25:14, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Vandũ va ũu, wĩthĩawa ũyonany'a kana nũsyendete na nũinengete ndaĩa, na ũu ũtumaa ieka kũũkĩa. Vekala ũu syĩthĩawa itonya kũkũelesya kĩla kĩkũithĩny'a.
5. Yesũ atetheeisye amanyĩw'a make ata nĩ kana makwate ũtanu ũla mũndũ ũkwataa nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na maũndũ maingĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova?
5 Yesũ nĩwendaa amanyĩw'a make na anyanyae makwate ũtanu ũla mũndũ ũkwataa nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na maũndũ maingĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩwendaa mũno methĩwe na kĩthito maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Nĩkyo kĩtumi wamekĩie vinya meyumye vyũ kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a. O na nĩwamathie kana akeethĩwa vamwe namo nĩ kana meanĩsye wĩa ũsu.—Mt. 28:19, 20.
6, 7. Nĩkĩ asyai ala mendete syana syoo maĩkĩĩthasya syĩ na mũvango wa kwĩka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva vate kũtĩĩa?
6 Nĩwendaa syana syaku syĩthĩwe syĩ na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na Yeova. O nake Yeova endaa ũee syana syaku "na mosilĩlo na motao" make. (Aev. 6:4) Kwoou ĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩla ũnengetwe nĩ Ngai kwa kwĩthĩwa na mũvango mũseo wa kũmanyĩsya syana syaku kĩla ĩvinda. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwĩkĩaa syana syaku vinya ithi sukulu nũndũ nĩwĩsĩ kana kĩsomo nĩ kya vata na nĩwendaa syĩthĩwe na wendi wa kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ meũ. O ta ũu asyai ala mendete syana syoo nĩmasyĩkĩaa vinya syĩmanyĩsye "motao ma Mwĩaĩi" ĩla syĩ maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi, maũmbanonĩ manene, na ũthaithinĩ wa mũsyĩ. Na nũndũ kũmanyĩw'a nĩ Yeova nĩ kwa vata, nĩwaĩlĩte kũtataa nĩ kana syana syaku syende mũno maũndũ ma kĩ-veva na iimanya kana no Yeova ũtonya kũimanyĩsya syĩthĩwe na ũĩ. (Nth. 24:14) O tondũ Yesũ watetheeisye amanyĩw'a make, waĩlĩte kũtata ũtetheesye syana syaku nĩ kana iendeee nesa ũtavany'anĩ. Ũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũitetheesya syende mũno kũmanyĩsya angĩ Ndeto ya Ngai na kwa kũitetheesya itavanasye iteũtĩĩa.
7 Kwĩthĩwa na mũvango mũseo wa maũndũ ma kĩ-veva kĩla ĩvinda kũtonya kũtetheesya syana ata? Mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Erin kuma South Africa aĩtye atĩĩ: "Twĩ syana nĩtweeminyaminyaa na tũkateta tũilea kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia, kũthi maũmbanonĩ, na kũtavany'a. Mavinda angĩ ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya vamwe vau mũsyĩ tweekanasya mĩthũmbi nĩ kana tũikaendeee kwĩmanyĩsya. Ĩndĩ asyai maitũ mayaaĩtĩkĩla tũmoae ngoo." Aendeee kwasya: "Ũndũ ũsu wandetheeisye nĩmanyĩsye kwĩthĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo. Matukũ aa ĩla mĩvango yakwa ya kwĩka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva yaanangĩka, nĩnĩtataa nĩmĩtũngĩĩe mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka. Keka asyai makwa mayaaĩthĩwa me alũmu mĩvangonĩ ya maũndũ ma kĩ-veva ndikwona ta nĩthĩwa na wendi ũsu. Keka nĩmaekie tũmoae ngoo, nĩnĩsĩ ki kana ũmũnthĩ nĩthĩwa nonaa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kũtĩĩa maũmbano na kũkĩlĩla maũndũ angĩ ma kĩ-veva."
MWONY'E NA MEKO ŨNDŨ ŨTONYA KWĨNYIVYA
8. (a) Yesũ oonanisye ata kana nĩweenyivĩtye? (b) Wĩnyivyo wa Yesũ watumie amanyĩw'a make meka ata?
8 O na kau Yesũ ndaĩ na naĩ, wĩnyivyo nĩwatumaa etĩkĩla kana kwĩ maũndũ amwe ũtatonya na kana nĩweethĩawa amwĩkwatĩtye Yeova. (Soma Yoana 5:19.) Ĩndĩ w'o wĩnyivyo wa Yesũ nĩwatumie amanyĩw'a make maeka kũmũnenga ndaĩa? Aiee. Eka ũu, amanyĩw'a make mamũĩkĩĩaa mũnango moona ũndũ wamwĩkwatĩtye Yeova. Ĩtinanĩ nĩmesie kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo o ta Yesũ.—Meko 3:12, 13, 16.
9. Kwĩtya ũekeo na kwĩtĩkĩla kana ve maũndũ amwe ũtatonya kũtonya kũtetheesya syana syaku ata?
9 Ve maũndũ maingĩ mũno tũtatonya, na kĩvathũkany'o na Yesũ, twĩ andũ me na naĩ na nĩtũvĩtasya. Kwoou ĩtĩkĩlaa kana ve maũndũ amwe ũtatonya, na ũyĩtĩkĩlaa mavĩtyo maku. (1 Yoa. 1:8) Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩ mũnene wĩva ũtonya kũnenga ndaĩa mũno? Nĩ ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa avĩtya kana nĩ ũla ũtetasya ũekeo? No ta ũu, ĩla mwana waku weew'a ũyĩtya ũekeo nũkũnengae ndaĩa mũnango. Mwana ũsu no emanyĩsye kana o nake nĩwaĩlĩte kwĩtĩkĩla ĩla wavĩtya. Mũndũ mũka ũmwe ũaĩsye syana itatũ wĩtawa Rosemary aĩtye ũũ: "Ithyĩ nĩtweetĩkĩlaa mavĩtyo na ũndũ ũsu nĩwatumaa syana sitũ itũelesya mathĩna masyo iteũkĩa. Na nũndũ nĩtweesĩ kana tũitonya maũndũ onthe, nĩtwamanyĩisye syana sitũ kũla itonya kumya ũtethyo ĩla syĩ na mathĩna. Ĩla syatwĩtya ũtethyo, nĩtwaitavasya ĩvuku yĩla itonya kũsoma yĩ na myolooto ya Mbivilia na tũivoya nasyo."
10. Yesũ oonanasya ata kana aĩ na wĩnyivyo atw'a kwĩaĩa aatĩĩi make?
10 Yesũ aĩ atonya kwĩaĩa amanyĩw'a make ũndũ ũkwenda. Ĩndĩ ĩla wameaĩa meke ũndũ nĩwamanengae kĩtumi kya kwĩka ũu. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla wameie mambe kũmantha Ũsumbĩ na ũlũngalu wa Ngai mbee, ongelile kũmea atĩĩ: "Na isu syonthe nĩmũkongeleelwa." Na ĩla waisye, "Mũikasilĩle," asyokie amanenga kĩtumi kĩĩ: "Nĩ kana mũikasilĩlwe. Nũndũ ũsilĩlo ũla mũsilĩlaa, now'o mũkasilĩlwa."—Mt. 6:31–7:2.
11. Nĩkĩ vatonyeka mũsyai waĩle kũnenga mwana wake kĩtumi kya mwĩao mũna kana ũtwi mũna?
11 Tavasya mwana waku kĩtumi kya kũmũnenga mwĩao mũna kana kwĩka ũtwi mũna ĩla woona vaĩlĩte. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mwana amanya kĩeleelo kyaku ethĩawa atonya kũkwĩw'a na ngenda. Barry aeete syana inya na aĩtye ũũ: "Wanenga syana syaku kĩtumi kya ũndũ mũna nikũĩkĩĩaa nũndũ imanyaa kana ndwĩkaa motwi ũtasũanĩĩte kana ũte na kĩtumi kĩseo, ĩndĩ ũmekaa ũtũmĩĩte kĩlĩko." Manya kana mwana ethĩawa aendeee kwĩana atw'ĩke mũndũ mũima ũtũmĩaa kĩlĩko. Barry aeleetye ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu akasya atĩĩ: "Syana syaĩlĩte kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩka motwi itũmĩĩte kĩlĩko ĩndĩ ti kĩla syeew'a ngoo yaitavya." (Sav. 119:34) Ĩla weenyivya na wanenga mwana waku itumi sya kwĩka ũndũ mũna, amanyaa kana o naku nũkũelewa kana nũendeee kwĩana, nake nĩwĩmanyĩasya kwĩyĩkĩa motwi atũmĩĩte kĩlĩko.
ĨTHĨWA NA ŨMANYI, NA ŨIELEWA MWANA WAKU
12. Yesũ atũmĩie ũmanyi ata amũtetheesye Vetelo?
12 Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana e na ũmanyi na nĩwaeleawa ũtethyo ũla amanyĩw'a make mekwenda. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũtũmwa Vetelo ndaĩ na kĩeleelo kĩthũku ĩla weeie Yesũ nĩ aeke maũndũ ala mesaa kũmũkwata methĩwe me kũasa nake nĩ kana ndakese kũawa. Ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana ũneeni ũsu wa Vetelo woonanasya ndasũanĩaa kĩla kyaĩlĩte. Nĩ kana Yesũ amũtetheesye na aitetheesya amanyĩw'a ala angĩ, nĩwamũkanisye ateũvithany'a kĩndũ, na aweta ũthũku wa kũlea kwĩyumya vamwe na moathimo ala mũndũ ũkwataa eethĩwa na veva wa kwĩyumya. (Mt. 16:21-27) Vetelo nĩwakwatisye kĩla Yesũ wamũmanyĩisye.—1 Vet. 2:20, 21.
13, 14. (a) Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva matonya kũũtetheesya ũmanye kana mũĩkĩĩo wa mwana waku nĩwambĩĩe kũleela? (b) Ũtonya kũtũmĩa ũmanyi ata nĩ kana ũelewe mwana waku na ũimũtetheesya?
13 Voya Yeova akũnenge ũmanyi nĩ kana ũelewe vala ũtonya kũtetheesya mwana waku. (Sav. 32:8) Kwa ngelekany'o, ũtonya kũmanya ata kana mũĩkĩĩo wa mwana waku nũtinie kũleela? Nũtonya kwona ambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa ate mũtanu, ambĩĩe kũneenea naĩ ana-a-asa ala angĩ, kana e na kĩmbithĩ kingĩ ũtanaĩ nakyo. Wesa kwona mwana waku ailyĩ ũu, ndũkese kũsũanĩa mĩtũkĩ kana e na mwĩkalo mũthũku, na kana nĩwĩkĩte naĩ ngito. * O na ũu wĩ o vo, ndwaĩlĩte kũvũthĩĩsya maũndũ ta asu. Na ĩla mwana waku watina kũvitha tũmaũndũ twake ndũkasũanĩe atĩ ũsu no ũndũ ũvĩtĩte.
14 No ũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ya Yesũ kwa kũkũlya mwana waku makũlyo o nesa na wĩ na ndaĩa. O tondũ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩtanga kĩw'ũ nũndũ wa kũkĩkusya kĩthimanĩ na mĩtũkĩ, now'o kũkũlya mwana makũlyo ũteũmũnenga nzeve na kũmũlasimĩthya asũngĩe kũtonya kũtuma atakũtavya maũndũ nesa. (Soma Nthimo 20:5.) Ilaria, ũla ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ, aĩtye ũũ: "Ĩvinda yĩla naĩ wa mũika neew'aa nũlanĩlw'e nĩatĩĩa ũla w'o-ĩ, kana ngatindaa na ala nzomaa namo. Mosũanĩo asu mathokoanisye ngoo yakwa nginya asyai makwa mamanya. Mũthenya ũmwe kwĩ wĩoo nĩmandavisye kana nĩmonete ndi mwĩanĩe na mangũlya nĩ kyaũ kĩũnthĩny'a. Nambĩĩe kũĩa, namaelesya thĩna wakwa, na namea mandetheesye. Nĩvo ĩndĩ mangumbatĩie na mambĩa nĩmangelewa na nĩmeũndetheesya." Asyai ma Ilaria nĩmambĩĩe mĩtũkĩ kũmũtetheesya atume ndũũ na andũ angĩ aseo kĩkundinĩ.
15. Elesya ũndũ Yesũ watũmĩaa ũmanyi e na angĩ.
15 O na ĩngĩ, Yesũ nĩwatũmĩaa ũmanyi ũkethĩa no amanye kũla amanyĩw'a make mekwenda kũtetheew'a na kũla maendeee nesa. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mũndũũme ũmwe weetawa Nathanaeli weewie kana Yesũ aumĩte Nasaleti aisye atĩĩ: "Nasaleti nĩvatonya kuma kĩndũ kĩseo?" (Yoa. 1:46) Keka nue weewie Nathanaeli ayasya ũu ũmwosa ata? Ũmwosa ta mũndũ ũtesaa kwona ũseo wa ala angĩ? Kana ũmwosa ta mũndũ wĩ kĩmena? Kana nĩ mũndũ ũte na mũĩkĩĩo? Yesũ aĩ na ũmanyi na nĩkyo kĩtumi woonie ũseo wa Nathanaeli. Yesũ amwĩtie, "Mũisilaeli ki, ũte [ũseleke]!" (Yoa. 1:47) Yesũ aĩ atonya kũsoma ngoo sya andũ na nĩwatũmĩaa ũtonyi ũsu amanthe ũseo wa angĩ.
16. Ũtonya kũtetheesya mwana waku ata ethĩwe na nguma nzeo?
16 O na kau ndũtonya kũsoma ngoo, Ngai no akũtetheesye wĩthĩwe na ũmanyi. We ũkatũmĩa ũmanyi ũla Ngai ũkũnete nĩ kana wone ũseo wa mwana waku? Vai mũndũ wendaa kwĩtwa "mũndũ wa itai." Ndwaĩlĩte kwĩta mwana waku "mbaa matũ" kana "nema kũvya," o na ndwaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa ũu kĩlĩkonĩ. O na ethĩwa mwana waku nũkũemwa nĩ maũndũ amwe, mũtavye kana nĩwĩsĩ ũtonyi wake na wendi wake wa kwĩka ũla ũseo. Na woona kũndũ wĩkĩte nesa mũkathe. Vatonyeka, mũnenge ũthasyo wa kwĩka maũndũ amwe ala ũtanamwĩtĩkĩlasya kwĩka nĩ kana ũmũtetheesye emanyĩsye kwĩthĩwa na nguma nzeo. Ũu nĩw'o Yesũ weekanaa na amanyĩw'a make. Mwaka ũmwe na nusu ĩtina wa Yesũ kũkomana na Nathanaeli (no we weetawa Valitholomayo), nĩwamũnyuvie atw'ĩka mũtũmwa, na Nathanaeli eethĩwa e Mũklĩsto wĩ kĩthito. (Luka 6:13, 14; Meko 1:13, 14) Wakatha mwana waku na wamũthangaasya, akeew'aa e Mũklĩsto ũtonya kũtũmĩwa nĩ Yeova ĩndĩ ti mũndũ ũteanĩsya ũla waĩlĩte.
ŨKATANA MŨNO WAMANYĨSYA MWANA WAKU
17, 18. Kũmanyĩsya mwana waku amũthũkũme Yeova ũte kũnoa kũetae ũathimo wĩva?
17 Ĩvinda yĩĩ ũendeee kũea syana syaku, mavinda amwe no wĩw'e ta mũtũmwa Vaulo. We aĩ na syana mbingĩ sya kĩ-veva, na kĩu nĩkyatumie akwatwa nĩ "thĩna mwingĩ na kũũũya kwa ngoo" nũndũ wa 'wendo mwingĩ' ũla waĩ naw'o kwondũ wa syana imwe syake ila syaĩ Kolintho. (2 Ako. 2:4; 1 Ako. 4:15) Victor aeie imwana ilĩ na mwĩĩtu ũmwe na aĩtye ũũ: "Ĩla syana sitũ syaĩ na ũkũũ wa katĩ wa myaka 13 na 19 maũndũ maĩ vinya. Ĩndĩ ũseo ũla twakwatie waĩ mwingĩ kũvĩta mathĩna ala twaĩ namo. Yeova nĩwatũtetheeisye tũtume ndũũ ngamu na syana sitũ."
18 Ĩkĩa kĩthito mũno ũte kũnoa nĩ kana ũtetheesye syana syaku imũthũkũme Yeova. Waendeea kwony'a syana syaku ũndũ ũsyendete mũno wĩana, ũkakwata ũtanu mwingĩ woona iyĩtĩkĩla ũla w'o na iiendeea 'kũendaa nthĩnĩ wa ũla w'o.'—3 Yoa. 4.

translation:
"Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man."—LUKE 2:52.
FOOTNOTE: 41, 11
1, 2. (a) What challenges do young people often face between the ages of 13 and 19? (b) What helped Christians maintain their spirituality during their teenage years?
CHRISTIAN youths today face a similar challenge—that of growing up. * For example, a young woman named Bernice was baptized when she was 14 years old. She says: "It was a very difficult time. We had to work hard to stay spiritual so that we could continue to please Jehovah. And even then, we sometimes felt overwhelmed and wanted to give up." It can be challenging to understand why Bernice and other young people between the ages of 13 and 19 feel this way.
2 One researcher has observed that teenagers often experience emotional turmoil and may struggle with identity issues. He explains: "Adolescence is not simply a matter of becoming older; it is also a matter of becoming an individual. During this period, they grapple with questions about who they are, what they want out of life, and what their values are." This emotional turmoil can distract them from serving Jehovah, making it harder to meditate on spiritual things and apply Bible principles. It can also lead them to experiment and make poor choices. But how can they overcome these challenges and remain close to Jehovah? (Read Luke 2:52.) What lessons can we learn from Jesus' example regarding his growth and development? What practical steps can parents take to help their children remain spiritual?
HELP YOUR CHILD
3. How did Jesus set an example for his followers?
3 Jesus was very busy, yet he made time for his friends and strengthened them spiritually. (Read John 15:15.) In modern times, many people feel overwhelmed and have difficulty managing their responsibilities. However, Jesus never felt too busy to care for others. He valued his friendships, and he spent time encouraging them, listening to their concerns, and helping them cope with difficulties. (Mark 6:30-32) So, like Jesus, we can prioritize spending quality time with our children and helping them strengthen their faith in God.
4. How can you encourage your child to share his feelings and confide in you? (See suggestions in paragraph 8.)
4 One young man named Michael said: "I wish my parents had taken more time to get to know me and my siblings individually." Many young people feel this way. Therefore, make an effort to spend individual time with each of your children, even if it means setting aside just a few minutes each day to talk and listen attentively. It may be that young people hide important things from their parents. A father once admitted: "I did not realize how much my son was struggling until he started getting into trouble—skipping school, experimenting with drugs, or associating with bad company." A young woman named Ilaria from Italy says: "Sometimes I was afraid to tell my parents about my problems because I thought they would not understand. But eventually, I realized that talking to them helped me deal with my anxieties." Spending time with your children and confiding in Jehovah will help you provide effective guidance. (Ps. 25:14, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Often, young people want to feel accepted and loved unconditionally, and knowing that you are willing to listen will reassure them. Be available to help your children when they need you.
5 Did Jesus show his disciples that he valued their individuality, even though they made mistakes and were imperfect?
5 Jesus valued his disciples and appreciated their willingness to learn about God's Kingdom. He also encouraged them to use their gifts effectively. That is why he took the time to train them thoroughly. And he patiently associated with them, even when they disappointed him.—Matt. 28:19, 20.
6, 7. What can parents do to encourage their children to share their feelings and concerns openly?
6 I value my children and want them to feel comfortable talking to Jehovah. I want Jehovah to view them as "wise and understanding." (Prov. 6:4) Therefore, I try to create an atmosphere where each child feels loved and accepted. For example, I listen to my children attentively when they come home from school, and I ask them questions about what they learned. But sometimes parents may find it difficult to help their children express "their thoughts" because of busy schedules, large families, and the pressures of daily life. However, if we remember that Jehovah values our children, we will be motivated to take the time to listen to them and understand their needs. (Prov. 24:14) So, just as Jesus showed his disciples appreciation, we can show our children that we appreciate their efforts and encourage them to continue progressing spiritually. We can do this by praising them for applying Bible principles and by helping them overcome challenges.
7 Can family worship help us to appreciate our children? A sister named Erin from South Africa says: "We made sure that we always included our children when preparing for Bible studies, meetings, and field service. Often, when we discussed material with them, they would have insights that helped us to improve our preparation. It was encouraging." She adds: "This taught me to value their contributions. There were times when my own schedule was very full, but I made an effort to set aside time so that they could share their thoughts. Seeing how much my children appreciated this encouraged me to continue making time for them, even when things were busy. It reminded me that spending time together strengthens family bonds and helps everyone to cope with problems."
QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
8. (a) What did Jesus notice about his followers? (b) How did Jesus use what he knew about his disciples?
8 Yes, Jesus knew what his disciples were thinking and feeling, and he used this knowledge to help them, even when they didn't ask for help. (Read John 5:19.) But did Jesus use what he knew about his disciples to manipulate them? No. Instead, he used his understanding to strengthen their faith in Jehovah. Note how Jesus showed appreciation for his disciples.—Lesson 3:12, 13, 16.
9. How can we show that we value our children's contributions?
9 There are many ways we can do so, and by following Jesus' example, we will be more sensitive and considerate. So value your children's contributions, and praise their efforts. (1 John 1:8) For instance, would it be helpful to point out their mistakes? It is better to encourage them than to criticize them. In fact, a loving parent will try to focus on what his child does right. A young person may not always realize how much effort you put into helping him. A sister named Rosemary said: "Sometimes I don't appreciate the things my parents do until later. And even when we make mistakes, they help us learn from them. When they correct us, we feel motivated to improve and study the Bible more diligently."
10. Did Jesus ever reveal information that his disciples did not need to know?
10 Jesus knew how to share information appropriately. The reason he revealed certain things was to help them grow spiritually. For example, if you have prayed earnestly about something, you might feel confident enough to say: "I am convinced this is the right course." But if you are unsure, you could pray: "Help me to see what is best."—Matt. 6:31–7:2.
11. Why does a loving father discipline his son?
11 Loving parents discipline their children because they want what is best for them. Why? Because a child who understands why he is being corrected can learn from his mistakes. Barry shared an experience and said: "Parents discipline their children for a good reason—to teach them what is right and wrong, so they will develop a conscience. A child who feels loved is more likely to respond positively." Remember that a well-adjusted child will continue to listen to reasonable guidance. Barry explained the importance of this principle by saying: "Children need to be taught to respect authority, but only when that authority is deserved." (Prov. 119:34) So if you lovingly correct your child, remember that he may need time to think about it and decide what to do, or he may need further explanation to understand why.
SHOW LOVE AND UNDERSTANDING, AND BE PATIENT WITH YOUR CHILD
12. How did Jesus show wisdom when dealing with Peter?
12 Jesus knew Peter's heart and understood his imperfections. For example, when Peter rebuked Jesus for telling him how his death would take place, Jesus kindly yet firmly corrected him. Jesus recognized that Peter was influenced by Satan, who wanted to discourage him from carrying out Jehovah's will. Jesus gently reminded Peter of this influence and helped him see things from God's viewpoint, showing him the importance of remaining loyal despite facing difficulties and trials. (Matt. 16:21-27) Peter accepted Jesus' correction.—1 Pet. 2:20, 21.
13, 14. (a) What are some ways you can determine whether your child is responding to discipline in a positive way? (b) How can wisdom help you to deal with your child and correct him effectively?
13 Ask Jehovah to give you insight and understanding so that you can discern how best to discipline your child. (Ps. 32:8) For instance, can you identify the underlying reason why your child misbehaves? Can you observe his reactions—his facial expressions, tone of voice, and body language—to get clues about what he is feeling? Observe whether he shows remorse, admits his mistake, and tries to make amends. * And remember, sometimes children may not express their feelings verbally. If your child seems troubled, try to find out what is bothering him and listen patiently.
14 Do not imitate the world's way of disciplining children by using harsh methods that instill fear and resentment. A parent who wants to train his child in righteousness should not use punishment that is excessive or abusive, which could lead to the child becoming rebellious and unable to learn from his mistakes. (Read Proverbs 20:5.) One mother, who was interviewed, said: "I used to yell and scream at my children, and they would just shut down or become defiant. But I realized that yelling only made things worse. So I started listening to them more carefully, and I tried to understand their perspective. It took time, but eventually we were able to communicate better." She added: "I learned to control my temper, to be patient, and to show my children love. That is when I began to see positive results." This mother found that by being gentle and loving, she could help her children learn and cooperate.
15 Teach your child what Jesus taught.
15 Moreover, Jesus helped people to know themselves. For example, when he met Nathaniel, he told him: "Nathaniel, you are an Israelite indeed!" (John 1:46) Why did Jesus say this to Nathaniel? Was it because Nathaniel looked different from others? Or was it because he was a kind person? Or was it because he had a good reputation? Jesus knew Nathaniel's heart, and that is why he could tell him about himself. Jesus said to him: "You are truly an Israelite!" (John 1:47) Jesus could read people's hearts, and he used this ability to help them.
16 How can you help your child to develop self-control?
16 Also, if you want to understand your child, ask God to give you insight. Then use that insight to help your child. But do not label your child as "bad" or "stubborn," and do not scold him unnecessarily. Instead, try to understand what motivates his behavior and why he does certain things. And remember that children need encouragement. Help them to learn from their mistakes, and teach them how to make good choices. This is what Jesus did with his disciples. About a year and a half after meeting Nathaniel (who was also called Bartholomew), Jesus appointed twelve apostles, and Nathaniel became a minister of Christ. (Luke 6:13, 14; Mark 1:13, 14) Encourage your child to become a minister of Christ, so that he may be used by Jehovah to help others.
TRAIN YOUR CHILD TO THINK FOR HIMSELF
17, 18. How can you train your child to love Jehovah and to make wise decisions?
17 As your children grow up, they will face challenges, some of which may seem difficult. The apostle Paul had many young brothers and sisters who were struggling with "much pressure and anxiety" because of their 'deep affection' for them. (2 Cor. 2:4; 1 Cor. 4:15) A father named Victor said about his son: "My son went through a difficult time between the ages of 13 and 19. During that period, we often felt helpless. Jehovah helped us to stay close to our son."
18 To help your child develop a love for Jehovah, take the time to listen to him and find out what he is thinking. Then show genuine interest in his thoughts and feelings, and encourage him to 'think deeply' about matters.—3 John 4.

text:
"Itindo nthũkũ nĩsyanangaa mwĩkalĩle mũseo."—1 AKO. 15:33.
MBATHI: 25, 20
1. Ĩvinda yĩĩ tũtwĩe nĩ yĩva?
ĨVINDA yĩĩ tũtwĩe nĩ yathe vyũ. Yambĩĩe mwaka wa 1914, na Mbivilia yaasya kana nĩyo 'mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo.' Mĩthenya ĩsu no ĩsyokete ĩketwa "mavinda ma mũisyo," na maũndũ ala me kw'o nĩ mathũku vyũ maelekanw'a na ala maĩ kw'o mwaka ũsu wa vata ũte mũviku. (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Na eka ũu, maũndũ mayĩĩsa kũleela nũndũ Mbivilia nĩyathanie kana "andũ athe na akengani makaendeea na kwongeleka kũthũka."—2 Tim. 3:13.
2. Andũ ma nthĩ ĩno metanĩthasya na maũndũ mailyĩ ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
2 Ĩla andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ mekwenda kwĩtanĩthya, meloelaa kana makeka maũndũ ala Mbivilia ĩmatalaa nĩ ma ũng'endu, ũlaalai, ũwe, kana matosanĩte na kwenda kwa Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, mavinda maingĩ Indaneti, ivĩndĩ sya televiseni, sinema, mavuku ma mbano, na makaseti mawetaa na makonany'a maũndũ ma ũng'endu na ũlaalai tate maũndũ mathũku. Na ĩndĩ o na mĩkalĩle ĩmwe ĩtaĩ yĩtĩkĩlwa andũnĩ, yu nĩyĩtĩkĩlĩtw'e nĩ silikalĩ imwe. Ĩndĩ o na yeetĩkĩlw'a nĩ andũ, ũu ti kwasya kana Ngai nũmĩtĩkĩlĩte.—Soma Alomi 1:28-32.
3. Mavinda maingĩ ala maatĩĩaa myolooto ĩla yĩ Maandĩkonĩ monekaa ata?
3 Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa mayeetĩkĩlaa kwĩtanĩthya na maũndũ mathavu. Na nũndũ mayeekaa ũu na maĩ na mwĩkalĩle ũla Ngai wendaa, nĩmaneeneawa naĩ na makathĩnw'a. Mũtũmwa Vetelo nĩwawetie ũndũ ũsu asya: "Monaa nĩ ũseng'yo inyw'ĩ [Aklĩsto] kũlea kũsemba vamwe nao kũendeeaa naĩnĩ isũ vate kwĩsiĩĩa, makĩmũneenea naĩ." (1 Vet. 4:4) Ũu nĩw'o kũilyĩ ũmũnthĩ. Andũ ma nthĩ ĩno monaa ala maatĩĩaa myolooto ya Ngai masaanĩtye. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana Mbivilia nĩyawetie kana "onthe ala mendaa kwĩkalya thayũ woo kũmũkĩa Ngai nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ makathĩnw'a."—2 Tim. 3:12.
"ITINDO NTHŨKŨ NĨSYANANGAA MWĨKALĨLE MŨSEO"
4. Maandĩko matũkanĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩno?
4 Maandĩko nĩmakanĩtye ala mendaa kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai makamea maikende nthĩ ĩno na maũndũ ala me kw'o. (Soma 1 Yoana 2:15, 16.) Maũndũ ala makonetye ndĩni, siasa, viasala, na vamwe na nzĩa ila nthĩ ĩno ĩtũmĩaa kũnyaĩĩkya maũvoo, methĩawa matongoew'e nĩ "ngai ya nthĩ ĩno," nayo nĩ Satani ũla Ndevili. (2 Ako. 4:4; 1 Yoa. 5:19) Kwoou nũndũ twĩ Aklĩsto, nĩtwaĩlĩte kwĩsũvĩana mũno na itindo nthũku. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũkanĩtye ũũ: "Mũikakengeke: Itindo nthũkũ nĩsyanangaa mwĩkalĩle mũseo."—1 Ako. 15:33.
5, 6. Naaũ tũtaĩle kũtuma ndũũ namo, na nĩkĩ?
5 Ethĩwa tũikwenda kwananga mwĩkalĩle witũ, tũyaĩle kũtuma ndũũ na ala mekaa mothũku. O na tũyaĩle kũtuma ndũũ na ala meyĩtaa athaithi ma Yeova ĩndĩ matũlaa mĩao yake na ngũlũ. Ngũsĩ ta isu syeeka naĩ ngito na syaema kwĩlila, nĩtũtilaa kĩtindo kitũ nasyo.—Alo. 16:17, 18.
6 Twatuma ndũũ na ala mataatĩĩaa mĩao ya Ngai, no laisi o naitũ tũkambĩĩa kwĩka tamo nĩ kana matwende. Ta kwa ngelekany'o, twatuma ndũũ na ilaalai, no laisi o naitũ tũkalika ũlaalainĩ. Aklĩsto amwe avatise nĩmalikile thĩnanĩ ta ũsu, na amwe moo nĩmatengiwe nũndũ mayaaĩlila. (1 Ako. 5:11-13) Makaema kwĩsa kũmũsyokea Yeova, mesa kũvika vala Vetelo wawetie.—Soma 2 Vetelo 2:20-22.
7. Twaĩle kũtuma ndũũ naaũ?
7 O na kau nĩtũkuaa nesa andũ ala mataatĩĩaa mĩao ya Ngai, mayaĩle kũtw'ĩka kĩtindo kitũ, o na tũyaĩle kũtuma ndũũ namo. Kwondũ wa ũu ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũte mũtwae kana ũtatwaanĩte ndaĩle kwĩvaany'a na mũndũ ũteyumĩtye amũthũkũme Ngai na ũte mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai, kana ũtaatĩĩaa myolooto yake. Kwĩkala wĩ mũĩkĩĩku nĩ kwa vata vyũ kwĩ kũmantha kwendwa nĩ andũ mataatĩĩaa mĩao ya Yeova. Kwoou twaĩlĩte kũtuma ndũũ na ala mekaa kwenda kwa Ngai. Yesũ aisye: "O ũla wĩkaa kwenda kwa Ngai, ũsu nĩwe mwana-a-ia, na mwĩĩtu-a-ia, na mwaitũ."—Mko. 3:35.
8. Itindo nthũku syaanangie ata mbaĩ ya Isilaeli?
8 Ana ma Isilaeli nĩmoonie thĩna ũla ũkwataa ala meekwatany'a na itindo nthũku. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ũndũ Yeova wamatavisye me kyalonĩ kya kũthi Nthĩ ya Watho ĩtina wa kũmaumya ũkombonĩ wa Amisili. Ameie: "Ndũkakunamĩe ngai syoo, o na kwithũkũma, o na kwĩka kũatĩĩa meko masyo: ĩndĩ ũkaing'uthũlange vyũ, na kũtũlanga ituĩ syasyo ilungu. Nenyu mũkathũkũmae Yeova Ngai wenyu." (Kuma 23:24, 25) Ĩndĩ mũthya aingĩ moo mayaatĩĩa mĩao ya Ngai. (Sav. 106:35-39) Nũndũ mayaaĩkala me aĩkĩĩku, Yesũ esie kũmea atĩĩ: "Sisyai, nyũmba yenyu nĩtiĩtwe yĩ nthei." (Mt. 23:38) Yeova nĩwakolile mbaĩ ya Isilaeli, na ũathimo ũla wesaa kũmĩnenga anenga kĩkundi kĩla kyaĩ kĩnambĩĩw'a kya Kĩklĩsto.—Meko 2:1-4.
NYUVA NA ŨĨ SYĨNDŨ ILA ŨŨSOMA NA KWĨLOELA
9. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana syĩndũ sya kwĩtanĩthya vamwe na ila inyaĩĩkasya maũvoo nitonya kwĩthĩwa na mũisyo?
9 Syĩndũ mbingĩ ila iseũvĩtw'e nĩ nthĩ ĩno sya kwĩtanĩthya na kũnyaĩĩkya maũvoo no syanange ngwatanĩo yitũ na Ngai. Syĩndũ isu iyĩthĩawa iseũvĩtw'e itũtetheesye tũmũĩkĩĩe Yeova mũnango vamwe na maũndũ ala ũtwathĩte. Ĩndĩ syĩthĩawa syosanĩte na nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani vamwe na mĩvango yake. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa twĩ metho mũno tũikese kwenda kĩndũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũkwatwa nĩ 'mawendi ma nthĩ.'—Tito 2:12.
10. Syĩndũ ila nthũku sya kwĩloela na kũsoma ikeekanwa nasyo ata?
10 Syĩndũ syonthe nthũku sya kũsoma na kwĩloela ikilyĩ inavetwa. Nũndũ syumanĩte na nthĩ ĩno ya Satani, ikavetwa ĩla nthĩ ĩno ĩkethĩwa ĩyanangwa. Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye ũũ: "Nthĩ nĩnĩũvĩta, na wendi wayo: ĩndĩ ũla wĩkaa kwenda kwa Ngai ekalaa tene na tene." (1 Yoa. 2:17) Mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli awetie ũndũ ta ũsu asya atĩĩ: "Eki ma naĩ makavetwa; ĩndĩ ala mamweteelaa Yeova, asu makatiĩwa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ ala auu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makeetan'ya mũuonĩ mwingĩ." Makekala ĩvinda yĩana ata? Mũandĩki ũsu aisye: "Ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makatũa vo kũvika tene na tene."—Sav. 37:9, 11, 29.
11. Ngai ekĩte ata nĩ kana andũ make makwate lĩu mũseo wa kĩ-veva?
11 Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo andũ ma Yeova maseũvasya syĩndũ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ila nthĩ ĩseũvasya. Ata? Syĩndũ isu maseũvasya syĩkĩaa andũ vinya methĩwe na mwĩkalĩle mũseo ũla ũkatuma makwata thayũ ũtathela. Yesũ amũvoyie Yeova asya: "Thayũ ũtathela nĩw'o ũũ, nĩ kana makũmanye we Ngai ũla wa w'o weka, na ũla wamũtũmie, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto." (Yoa. 17:3) Nĩkyo kĩtumi Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ ũtũmĩaa andũ make ũmũnthĩ kũtũnenga lĩu mwingĩ wa kĩ-veva ũtonya kũtwĩkĩa vinya. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũtanaa mũno nũndũ twĩ na makaseti, mbulosua, mavuku, vitio, o na twĩ na ũvoo wĩ Kĩsesenĩ kitũ, na maũndũ asu onthe matwĩkĩaa vinya tũkwate mbau ũthaithi wa w'o! O na ĩngĩ andũ make nĩmavangĩte maũmbano ma kĩla kyumwa kwondũ wa ikundi mbee wa 110,000 nthĩ yonthe. Ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ asu ma kĩkundi na maũmbanonĩ manene, nĩtũmanyĩaw'a maũndũ mosanĩte na Mbivilia, ala matumaa tũmũĩkĩĩa Ngai mũnango vamwe na mawatho make.—Aevl. 10:24, 25.
KŨTWAANA O "NTHĨNĨ WA MWĨAĨI"
12. Ĩla Mbivilia yaweta ĩũlũ wa kũtwaana "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi" yĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a ata?
12 Nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwa Aklĩsto ala mate atwae kana matatwaanĩte masisye maikekwatany'e na itindo nthũku ĩla mekũmantha mũndũ wa kũtwaana nake. Ndeto ya Ngai ĩnenganĩte ũtao ũũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu: "Mũtikovanĩw'e ĩsoki yĩmwe na ala mate etĩkĩli: nũndũ ũlũngalu na ũthũku wĩ mũamba mwaũ? kana kyeni kĩ na mũamba mwaũ na kĩvindu?" (2 Ako. 6:14) Mbivilia nĩtaĩte Aklĩsto ala meũmantha mũndũ ĩkamea nĩmatwaane o "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nĩmatwaane na mũthũkũmi wa Yeova wĩyumĩtye amũthũkũme na akavatiswa, na wĩkalaa kwosana na momanyĩsyo ma Maandĩko. (1 Ako. 7:39) Ĩla Mũklĩsto watwaana na Mũklĩsto ũngĩ ethĩawa akwata mũtindany'a wĩyumĩtye amũthũkũme Yeova na ũtonya kũmũtetheesya aendeee kwĩkala e mũĩkĩĩku.
13. Nĩ mwĩao wĩva Ngai wanengie Aisilaeli ũkonetye mũtwaano?
13 Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ kĩla kĩtonya kũtethya athũkũmi make, na nũndũ wa ũu kuma tene atwĩe atũtũngĩlĩĩlaa mwĩao wake ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa mwĩao wĩ laisi kũeleeka ũla wanengie Mose atavye Aisilaeli. Kwosana na mwĩao ũsu, Yeova akanisye Aisilaeli maikekwatany'e na mbaĩ ila syamathyũlũlũkĩte nũndũ iyamũthaithaa. Ameie: "Ndũkaatwaanĩe nao; mwĩĩtu waku ndũkaamũne mwana wake, kana mwĩĩtu wake ndũkaamũtwaĩe mwana waku. Nũndũ akamwathũkya mwana waku aeke kũmbikĩla, nĩ kana mathũkũme ngai ingĩ: na kwondũ wa ũu ũthatu wa Yeova ũkakwakanĩa, na akakwananga mĩtũkĩ."—Kũt. 7:3, 4.
14, 15. Nĩ kyaũ kyamũkwatie Solomoni ĩla watũlile mwĩao wa Yeova?
14 Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Solomoni, mwana wa Ndaviti. Ambĩĩa kũsumbĩka oou nĩwamũvoyie Ngai amũnenge ũĩ, nake Ngai nĩwamũnengie ũĩ mwingĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, Mũsumbĩ Solomoni nĩwesie kũmanyĩka ta mũsumbĩ mũĩ wa nthĩ nthwii. Na ũu nĩ w'o nũndũ o na yĩla ũla mũndũ mũka ũtonya kwĩthĩwa asumbĩkĩte vandũ veetawa Sieva wamũthokeie Solomoni, amwĩie: "Ndyaaĩtĩkila i ndeto, kũvika nĩnooka, na metho makwa nĩmawonete: Na, sisya, ndyaatavw'a nyunzu; ũĩ waku na kũathimĩka kwaku nĩkũvĩtũkĩte nguma ĩla neewie." (1 Asu. 10:7) Ĩndĩ kĩla kyesie kũmũkwata Solomoni nĩ ngelekany'o ya kĩla kĩtonya kũkwata mũndũ atũla mwĩao ũla Ngai ũtũnengete wa kũtwaana nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi tũ.—Mũta. 4:13.
15 O na kau Solomoni nĩweekĩtwe maũndũ maingĩ maseo nĩ Ngai, nĩwavũthisye mwĩao wake na atwaa iveti itamũthaithaa, ila syaĩ sya mbaĩ ila syamathyũlũlũkĩte. Solomoni "nĩwendete aka aingĩ" na mũthya esie kũmesya iveti 700 na ingĩ sya ndũsyo 300. Vesie kũthi ata? Ĩla Solomoni wesie kũtumĩa, iveti isu syake 'syathyũũie ngoo yake ĩatĩĩe ngai ingĩ, na eeka ũla Yeova wonaa wĩ ũthũku.' (1 Asu. 11:1-6) Nũndũ Solomoni eekwatanisye na kĩtindo kĩthũku, ũĩ ũla waĩ naw'o ndwaamũtethya, na kyu nĩkyatumie aeka kũmũthaitha Yeova. Ũsu nĩ ũkany'o mũseo ta kĩ kwa Aklĩsto ala me na yĩsilya ya kũtwaana na mũndũ ũtamwendete Yeova!
16. Nĩ ũtao wĩva wĩ Maandĩkonĩ ũtonya kũtethya Mũklĩsto ũtwaanĩte na mũndũ ũte Ngũsĩ?
16 Nata ĩndĩ mũndũ mũka ũtwaĩtwe nĩ mũndũ ũte Ngũsĩ akambĩĩa kũmũthaitha Ngai? Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte ĩkasya: "Inyw'ĩ iveti, ĩnyivĩsyei aũme menyu; nĩ kana ethĩwa ve amwe mate ewi ma ĩla ndeto, matonye kwonw'a nĩ mwĩkalĩle wa iveti syoo vate ĩla ndeto." (1 Vet. 3:1) Ndeto isu itavĩtw'e aka Aklĩsto, ĩndĩ no itethye mũndũũme ũla wambĩĩa kũmũthũkũma Yeova atwaĩte mũndũ mũka ũte Ngũsĩ. Kwoou ũtao ũsu wa Mbivilia wĩkwĩa atĩĩ: Ĩkalany'a nesa na ũla ũngĩ, na ũiatĩĩa myolooto ĩla Ngai ũnengete ala matwaanĩte. Andũ aingĩ mate Ngũsĩ nĩmesĩte kwĩtĩkĩla ũw'o nũndũ nĩmonete ala matwaanĩte namo maivĩndũka mamina kwambĩĩa kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai.
TINDANY'A NA ALA MAMWENDETE YEOVA
17, 18. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Noa na ala Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa matananganĩw'a na andũ ma ĩvinda yoo?
17 Kĩtindo kĩthũku kyanangaa mwĩkalĩle mũseo, nakyo kĩtindo kĩseo kĩtumaa twĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Kwosana na ũu, sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Noa. O na kau atwĩe ĩvinda yaĩ na andũ athũku, ndaatuma ndũũ namo. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩu: "Na Yeova oona kana ũthũku wa mũndũ waĩ mũnene kũũ nthĩ, na kĩla kĩsũanĩo kya malilikano ma ngoo yake kyaĩ kyathe vyũ mavinda onthe." (Mwa. 6:5) Nũndũ wa ũu, Ngai nĩwatwie kusya mbua mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe nĩ kana anange vyũ nthĩ ĩsu ya ĩvinda yĩu. Ĩndĩ "Noa aĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu, na mwĩanĩu nzyawanĩ sya ĩvinda yake: Noa aendanasya na Ngai."—Mwa. 6:7-9.
18 Vate nzika Noa ndatindanasya na andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai. We na andũ ala angĩ make mũonza nĩmeeyumĩtye vyũ matethye mawĩa ala Ngai wamanengete, na ũmwe wa mawĩa asu waĩ kwaka ngalawa. O na ĩngĩ Noa aĩ "mũtavan'ya wa ũlũngalu." (2 Vet. 2:5) Noa ndaĩ na ũthei wa kwĩka maũndũ angĩ eka ala Ngai wendaa nũndũ atũmĩaa ĩvinda yake kũtavany'a, kwaka ngalawa, na kĩtindo kyake kyaĩ kya andũ make. Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩwavonokie e na andũ make ĩla Ngai wauisye ĩla mbua. Ithyonthe twesie kũsyawa nũndũ Noa, mũka, anae, na aka-a-mwana make maĩ aĩkĩĩku, na kĩu nĩ kĩndũ kyaĩle kũtuma tũtana mũno. O namo Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa maĩ aĩkĩĩku na maĩ ewi na mayaaĩkwatany'a na andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai. Nũndũ wa ũu, mayaanangwa ĩla ndũa ya Yelusaleme yaanangiwe mwakanĩ wa 70.—Luka 21:20-22.
19. No nginya twĩke ata ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda kũmũthũkũma Ngai twĩ aĩkĩĩku?
19 Nĩkwĩthĩwa twĩ athaithi ma Yeova, nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Noa na andũ make, vamwe na ya ala Aklĩsto maĩ ewi ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa. No nginya twĩvathane vyũ na nthĩ ĩno nthũku na tũimantha kĩtindo vala ve ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maitũ aĩkĩĩku, ala yu nĩ milioni mbingĩ. Kũtindany'a na ala me na ũĩ wa Ngai kũkatũtetheesya 'tũũngame twĩ alũmu mũĩkĩĩonĩ' ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ yathe. (1 Ako. 16:13; Nth. 13:20) Na ĩndĩ eka ũndũ ũsu, kwasũanĩa moathimo ala tũkakwata ĩvinda yũkĩte! Ĩla nthĩ nzaũ Yeova ũtwathĩte yĩ vakuvĩ mũno. Kwoou tweesũvĩana na itindo nthũku ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kũvonoka ĩla nthĩ ĩno ĩkethĩwa ĩyanangwa, na tũilika nthĩ ĩsu nzaũ yĩ na ũlũngalu.

translation:
"A wise person listens to counsel." – 1 PROVERBS 15:33.
PAGE: 25, 20
1. What is one thing we live in?
We live in challenging times. Since 1914, the Bible has shown that we are living in the 'time of the end.' These last days are often called "critical times," and many problems around the world are connected to what is happening this year. (2 Timothy 3:1-5) Also, people are becoming more and more dishonest, which makes it harder to trust others.—2 Timothy 3:13.
2. How do people today show that they care little for truth? (Consider some examples.)
Many people prefer to be entertained rather than to think about what the Bible teaches is right, moral, true, or pleasing to God. For example, much material on the Internet, television programs, movies, music, books, and magazines focuses on violence and immorality. And sometimes even games are designed to appeal to people's bad qualities, making those qualities seem normal. This does not mean that God approves of how people behave.—Read Romans 1:28-32.
3. What serious question does this raise regarding the Scriptures?
3 Jesus' followers were encouraged to be interested in important things. And when we allow our heart to be moved by what God values, we will be strengthened by his spirit. The apostle Peter wrote: "Be clearheaded [Christians], so that you may pray effectively and also continue united in love." (1 Pet. 4:7) That is how to live meaningfully. People who appreciate God's standards want to live in harmony with them. And they realize that the Bible shows us "what everyone needs to know in order to approve themselves to God as qualified workers."—2 Tim. 3:12.
"EVERYDAY LIFE IS FULL OF CHOICES"
4. What practical question does this raise?
4 The Scriptures show that people want to please God and conform their lives to his requirements and his ways. (Read 1 John 2:15, 16.) However, worldly desires, materialism, and other influences can make it difficult to discern the truth, and "the god of this system" blinds people.—2 Cor. 4:4; 1 John 5:19. As we follow Christ, we need to be vigilant against everyday life's influence. This is why God's Word urges us: "Keep on making appeal: Everyday life is full of choices."—1 Cor. 15:33.
5, 6. How can we maintain spiritual strength, and why?
5 If we want to remain loyal to Jehovah, we must regularly examine ourselves and make sure we are keeping busy doing what is spiritually beneficial. We should also associate with those who are zealous in serving Jehovah and supporting his organization. By being diligent and persistent, we can strengthen our faith.—Ps. 16:17, 18.
6 We strengthen our faith by associating with others who love God, and we encourage them by sharing with them when we can. Also, we strengthen our faith by associating with exemplary Christians, and we benefit from their example. Some Christians have faced severe trials, while others have been tested in various ways. (1 Pet. 5:11-13) Above all, strive to deepen your love for Jehovah and to imitate the zeal of Jesus.—Read 2 Timothy 2:20-22.
7. Why should we examine ourselves?
7 We should examine ourselves so that we can identify areas where we need to improve and so that we can ask Jehovah to help us. If someone claims to love God but does not live according to his standards or does not appreciate his teachings, he is deceiving himself. Being honest with yourself will help you to avoid being misled by those who do not love Jehovah. As we examine ourselves, we can pray for assistance in remaining loyal to God. Jesus said: "Everyone who practices doing God's will is my brother and sister and mother."—Mark 3:35.
8. Does everyday life pose a threat to spiritual Israelites?
8 The spiritual Israelites face a similar threat. For instance, Jehovah allowed the nation of Israel to be taken captive by Babylon because they had become unfaithful. He warned them: "I will certainly give you advice and guidance, but you must also pay attention and turn away from what is bad. If you do this, I will make your enemies few, and those who hate you will be insignificant." (Josh. 23:24, 25) Many people today disregard God's standards. (Ps. 106:35-39) Because of their unfaithfulness, Jesus said: "Your house is left desolate." (Matt. 23:38) Jehovah rejected the nation of Israel, and the time came when he turned to gather a new people—the Christian congregation.—Acts 2:1-4.
KEEP READING AND MEDITATING
9. How can we deal with feelings of discouragement or sadness, especially when facing difficult circumstances?
9 Many find comfort in prayer and by meditating on Bible principles. This can strengthen our relationship with God. Such feelings often indicate that we need to draw closer to Jehovah and examine our thinking. However, such feelings may also be caused by Satan and his influence. So, to a large extent, we can protect ourselves from being overwhelmed by 'the anxieties of life' by taking deliberate steps.—Titus 2:12.
10. Why is regular reading and meditation important?
10 All spiritual progress depends on regular reading and meditation. By resisting Satan's influence, we can avoid being misled. God's promise is: "The world is passing away, and so is its desire, but whoever does the will of God remains forever." (1 John 2:17) One writer once said: "Good things are temporary; but those who love Jehovah will remain secure. Those who hate security, and delight in wickedness, will be cut off." Are these words still true today? That same writer added: "But the meek will possess the earth, and they will find exquisite delight in abundance of peace."—Ps. 37:9, 11, 29.
11. What does God allow to happen, and why does he permit bad things to occur?
11 Many faithful Christians have wondered why bad things happen to Jehovah's people. Why does God allow such suffering? Spiritual progress depends on our remaining close to God and avoiding what displeases him. Jesus explained this to Jehovah when he prayed: "This means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and your Son Jesus Christ." (John 17:3) This is why Asaph, a Levite, helped his brothers understand much about God's purpose. For example, we may enjoy music, books, art, sports, and even beautiful scenery, but these things can become distractions if we let them take first place in our lives! And many of his people were moved to attend assemblies—some 110,000 in total—in various countries. Whether at smaller gatherings or larger ones, we benefit from learning more about the Bible and drawing closer to God and his worship.—Heb. 10:24, 25.
TO KEEP "THE SPIRITUALITY"
12 But what does the Bible mean when it speaks of keeping "the spirituality"?
12 It involves being loyal to Christ and maintaining spiritual qualities that help us remain separate from the world. God's standard requires us to ask ourselves questions like these: "Is my association with others affecting my spirituality? Am I spending too much time with those who do not share my faith, or am I getting involved in worldly pursuits?" (2 Cor. 6:14) The Bible directs Christians to associate with those who will strengthen their spirituality, or, in other words, with fellow worshippers of Jehovah who encourage them and help them live by Bible principles. (1 Cor. 7:39) However, a Christian may associate with non-Christians as long as he maintains a strong desire to please Jehovah and avoids being influenced by negative influences.
13 How did God view Israel's marriages?
13 Jehovah was deeply concerned about the loyalty of his people, and he provided guidance regarding marriage. For example, consider how he dealt with Moses when he married an Israelite woman. In harmony with his purpose, Jehovah forbade the Israelites from marrying individuals from nations that worshipped false gods. He said: "You must not intermarry with them. Should you become attached to their daughters, they will turn your heart away to their gods. And should you take their sons as wives, their sons will turn your hearts away to other gods."—Deut. 7:3, 4.
14, 15 What mistake did Solomon make that displeased Jehovah?
14 Let us consider the case of Solomon, David's son. He asked God to grant him wisdom, and God granted him abundant wisdom. Because of this, King Solomon became renowned as the wisest man. But this is why what happened next was so serious. A man disguised himself as a servant and approached King Solomon, asking: "Please give me one girl as a slave, so that I may test her. Perhaps she will bear me a son, and then I will have a heir." (1 Ki. 10:7) This request was similar to the way anyone who is loyal to Jehovah would approach him to ask for something—to use it to promote true worship.—Matt. 4:13.
15 Now, Solomon received many gifts from God, he valued his relationship with Him, and he built an impressive temple. However, he also had 700 wives and 300 concubines. What was the result? Well, Solomon allowed them to turn his heart away from Jehovah, and they led him to worship other gods. (1 Ki. 11:1-6) So Solomon associated with people who did not love Jehovah, and that is why he eventually turned against Jehovah. This should serve as a warning to all Christians today about associating with those who do not love Jehovah!
16. How can we tell whether a Christian is associating with someone disloyal to Jehovah?
16 Consider this example: A man invites a disloyal person to his home and says to him: "Come, eat some bread and drink some wine; let us enjoy ourselves while I explain things to you." (Pr. 3:1) That disloyal person may not openly encourage the man to abandon Jehovah, but simply being around a disloyal person can influence him negatively. The Bible warns us: "Do not be misled by bad associations, for 'bad company corrupts good morals.'" Many people have been influenced by disloyal ones and have gradually drifted away from Jehovah.
KEEP YOURSELF FREE FROM THOSE WHO DO NOT LOVE JEHOVAH
17, 18. What lessons can we learn from Noah and from Christians in the first century regarding association with wicked people?
17 A strong odor can affect one's sense of smell, and a foul odor can make one feel sick. Similarly, consider the case of Noah. He associated with violent and wicked people, and this troubled his heart. The Bible describes the wickedness of the world at that time: "The earth was also corrupt in God's eyes, and the land was filled with violence." (Gen. 6:5) Because of this, God decided to destroy the entire earth except for Noah and his family. The Bible states: "Noah was a righteous man, blameless among his contemporaries; Noah walked with God."—Gen. 6:7-9.
18 But Noah preached to those people, warning them to turn back to God. However, they paid no attention to his warnings, ignoring what God said, and they continued their violent ways. So Noah became "a herald of righteousness." (2 Pet. 2:5) Noah had faith that God would fulfill his purpose of preserving life through him, despite the opposition he faced from his neighbors. Therefore, he saved eight souls—his family—when God brought the flood. Today we learn a lesson from Noah, his wife, his sons, and his daughters-in-law, who were all saved, because it shows us how important it is to remain loyal to God. Also, Christ spoke about the flood when addressing his disciples and others who were turning away from God. He foretold the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 C.E.—Luke 21:20-22.
19 Then why should we strive to please God now?
19 Because we want to be like those whom Jehovah approves, such as Noah and his household, and also like faithful Christians during the time of the apostles. Why should we associate with our brothers and sisters, millions of whom there are worldwide? By associating with those who love God, we can strengthen our resolve to be "steadfast in the faith" and continue serving him faithfully. (1 Cor. 16:13; Heb. 13:20) And remember, we need to support our brothers so that they can preach the good news! For Jehovah has given us this privilege. As we see the fulfillment of Bible prophecies, let us prove ourselves ready to escape the coming great tribulation, and let us use our time wisely.

text:
"Ĩkalai na mũuo inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ."—MKO. 9:50.
MBATHI: 39, 35
1, 2. Ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩlyo yĩwetete mathĩna meva maĩ andũnĩ, na nĩkĩ kĩu nĩkĩtũkonetye?
WAASŨANĨA ĩũlũ wa andũ maemaniwe mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ? Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa amwe mawetetwe ilungunĩ sya mbee vyũ sya ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩlyo. Ilungu isu niwetete ĩũlũ wa ĩla Kaini wooaie Aveli (Mwa. 4:3-8), ĩla Lameki wooaie mwanake ũmwe wamũkũnie (Mwa. 4:23), ĩla aĩthi ma Avalaamu (Avalamu) na Loto matetanisye (Mwa. 13:5-7), ĩla Akali wamenie Sala (Salai), nake Sala amũthatĩa Avalaamu (Mwa. 16:3-6), na ĩla Isumaeli wokitaa kĩla mũndũ nake akokitwa nĩ kĩla mũndũ.—Mwa. 16:12.
2 Nĩkĩ Mbivilia ĩwetete mavinda ta asu andũ maemaniwe? Kĩtumi kĩmwe nĩ kana ngewa ta isu nitũtetheeasya kũmanya nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩkala na mũuo ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ. O na Mbivilia nĩsyokete ĩkatũtavya kĩla tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana twĩkale na mũuo. Kũsoma ngewa ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ nĩkũtũtethasya nĩkwĩthĩwa iwetete andũ taitũ makwatiwe nĩ mathĩna o ta ala matũkwataa. Kũsoma ĩũlũ wa kĩthito kĩla meekĩie no kũtũtetheesye o naitũ twĩke tamo ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna mana. Na vate nzika kĩu no kĩtũtetheesye kũmanya kĩla twaĩle kwĩka ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna ta ala mamakwatie, na kĩla tũtaĩle kwĩka.—Alo. 15:4.
3. Nĩ maũndũ meva tũkwona ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ nĩtũkwona nĩkĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova maĩle kwĩw'ana ethĩwa nĩmaemanwa, na ũndũ matonya kwĩka ũu. O na ĩngĩ nĩtũkwona myolooto ya Maandĩko ĩla ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ethĩwa ve na thĩna. Nĩtũũsyoka twone ũndũ myolooto ĩsu ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkalany'e nesa na atũi maitũ na tũyĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova Ngai.
NĨKĨ ATHŨKŨMI MA NGAI MAĨLE KWĨW'ANA ĨLA MAEMANWA
4. Nĩ woni wĩva walikile andũnĩ, na kyu kĩtumĩte kwĩthĩwa kũilyĩ ata?
4 Satani nĩwe mũno mũno waĩle kũtũlwa mũtĩ nũndũ wa ithokoo ila syĩ andũnĩ. Aineena na Eva mũũndanĩ wa Eteni woni wake waĩ kana kĩla mũndũ aĩle kwĩtw'ĩĩa ũla ũseo na ũla ũthũku, atekwenda kũmanya nake Ngai easya ata. (Mwa. 3:1-5) Ũmũnthĩ vai mũndũ ũtene thĩna ũla walikile nũndũ wa woni ũsu wake. Nthĩ yusĩe andũ matendete kwĩaĩwa. Kĩu kĩtumĩte andũ methĩwa na mĩtũlyo, mona me aseo kwĩ ala angĩ, na methĩwa na kĩmena. Ũla wĩtĩkĩlaa kũtutya andũ ta asu ma nthĩ, no ũndũ ũmwe na wĩthĩawa ayĩtĩkĩlana na ũla woni wa Satani wa kana mũndũ aĩle kwĩka ũndũ ũkwenda atekwenda kũmanya ala angĩ meĩw'a ata. Mwĩkalĩle ta ũsu nĩw'o wĩsaa kũtuma andũ mathokoana. Ĩndĩ nũseo tũkamanya kana "mũndũ mũthatu nĩwũkĩlasya ĩteta, na mũndũ mũthilĩku nĩwusũĩte mavĩtyo."—Nth. 29:22.
5. Yesũ amanyĩisye andũ maũndũ meva matonya kũmatetheesya mew'ane na ala maemanwa namo?
5 Kĩvathũkany'o na Satani, Yesũ amanyĩisye andũ kũmanthaa mũuo o na ethĩwa meona meeka ũu nĩmo mekwasya. Nthĩnĩ wa ũla Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ, nĩwanenganie ũtao mũseo mũno ũtonya kũtetheesya andũ mamanye kĩla maĩle kwĩka ĩla maemanwa kana vaumĩla ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma maemanwa. Kwa ngelekany'o, eekĩie vinya amanyĩw'a make methĩwe me andũ auu, andũ mekaa mũuo, andũ mesiĩaa maikathate, mendete kwĩw'ana mĩtũkĩ ĩla maemanwa, na mendete amaitha moo.—Mt. 5:5, 9, 22, 25, 44.
6, 7. (a) Nĩkĩ waemanwa na mũndũ waĩle kwosa ĩtambya ya mĩtũkĩ wĩw'ane nake? (b) Athũkũmi onthe ma Yeova maĩle kwĩkũlya makũlyo meva?
6 Nĩtwĩkĩaa kĩthito mũno tũmũthũkũme Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũmũvoyaa, tũkathi maũmbanonĩ na ũtavany'a, na tũkeka maũndũ angĩ makonetye ũthaithi witũ. Ĩndĩ maũndũ asu onthe no ma mana ethĩwa tũyĩtĩkĩla kwĩw'ana na ala twaemanwa namo. (Mko. 11:25) Ngai ndesa kũtũtala ta anyanyae ethĩwa tũyendaa kũekea ala matũvĩtĩsya.—Soma Luka 11:4; Aeveso 4:32.
7 Kĩla Mũklĩsto aĩlĩte kwĩkala nthĩ akasũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa kũekea ala angĩ na kwĩkalany'a namo nesa, na ayĩthiana we mwene amanye ũndũ ũilyĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, we nũekeaa Aklĩsto ala angĩ na ngenda? Nĩwendete kũtindany'a namo o na kau no kwĩthĩwa ve ĩvinda maũvĩtĩisye? Yeova endaa athũkũmi make memanyĩsye kũekea. Kwoou, ethĩwa nũkwĩw'a wasya waku wa ngoo ũikwĩa kana ve vandũ waĩle kũlũnga, mũvoye Yeova aũtetheesye kwĩlũnga! Asa witũ ndaema ũkwĩthukĩĩsya oona ũimũvoya aũtetheesye, na ndaema kũũsũngĩa.—1 Yoa. 5:14, 15.
NO ŨVĨTĨW'E NA ŨKOLWA NŨU?
8, 9. Twaĩle kwĩka ata twavĩtĩw'a?
8 Nũndũ twĩ andũ me na naĩ, twaĩle kwĩkalaa twĩsĩ kana mũndũ no atũtavye ndeto ĩkatũthatya kana akeka kĩko kĩkatũthatya. O na ũkeka ata, andũ maiema kũvĩtya. (Mũta. 7:20; Mt. 18:7) We ũkavĩtĩw'a wĩka ata? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ĩvinda yĩmwe kwaendie. Ĩvinda yĩu ve Ngũsĩ syoombanĩte vandũ syĩtanĩthye, na syĩ vau ve ana-a-asa elĩ makethiw'e nĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa mũna, ĩndĩ ũmwe woo oona mũkethelye ũsu ũte mũseo. Matiwa me oka, mwana-a-asa ũla wathatiw'e nĩ mũkethelye wa mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩwambĩĩe kũmumany'a. Ĩndĩ mwana-a-asa ũla ũngĩ nĩwamũlilikanilye kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu alũmanĩtye na Yeova e mathĩnanĩ kwa myaka 40, na kwoou ndaĩ na nzika kana amakethisye ũu ate na ũthũku. Mwana-a-asa ũla wathatĩte ambie kũsũanĩa ndeto isu, na ĩndĩ asya, "Waweta w'o." Ngewa isu syatheleile vau.
9 Ũndũ ũsu wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? No uwe ũtonya kũtw'a wĩĩka ata ĩla vaumĩla ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma ũemanwa na angĩ. Mũndũ wendete angĩ ndatindaa aatĩanĩe na tũmavĩtyo tũnini. (Soma Nthimo 10:12; 1 Vetelo 4:8.) Yeova aasyaa kana nĩ "ndaĩa" kwaku ĩla 'waekea ĩvĩtyo.' (Nth. 19:11; Mũta. 7:9) Kwoou kĩla waĩle kwamba kwĩkũlya ĩla woona ta ve mũndũ waũkua naĩ nĩ kĩĩ: 'No nĩekane na ĩvĩtyo yĩu? Nĩ lasima nĩtinde nĩatĩanĩe na ũla wambĩtĩsya?'
10. (a) Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe ambie kwĩka ata ĩla wamanyie kana nũkũneenewa naĩ? (b) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva wĩ Maandĩkonĩ watetheeisye mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu ekale auĩtye?
10 Ĩla wamanya angĩ nĩmeũkũneenea naĩ ti laisi ũkosa ũsu ta ũndũ mũnini. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya vainia ũmwe tũũmũtw'ĩĩa ĩsyĩtwa Lucy. Ve ĩvinda andũ maneenaa naĩ ĩũlũ wa mũtavanĩlye wake na ũndũ ũtũmĩaa ĩvinda. Ngewa isu nĩsyambie kũthatya Lucy, na kwoou athi kwona ana-a-asa amwe aima. Aeleetye kĩla kyaendeeie akasya: "Manengie ũtao umĩte Maandĩkonĩ na ũtao ũsu nĩwandetheeisye nĩthĩwe na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa kĩla ala angĩ mawetaa, na ngĩmanya kana ũla naĩle kũsũanĩa mũno nĩ Yeova." Lucy nĩweekĩiwe vinya nĩ kũsoma ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 6:1-4. (Soma.) Ĩandĩko yĩu yamũlilikanilye kana kĩla waĩle kũthĩnĩkĩa nĩ kũmũtanĩthya Yeova. Aisye: "O na angĩ maneenea naĩ ũtavany'a wakwa, nĩkalaa nĩ mũtanu nũndũ nĩnĩsĩ nĩtatĩte ũndũ ndonya nĩmũtanĩthye Yeova." Ĩla Lucy weekĩie kyu kĩlĩkonĩ, nĩwatwie kũlwa nĩ ũndũ andũ mamũneeneaa naĩ.
NATA ETHĨWA NĨ ĨVĨTYO ŨTAEKANA NAYO?
11, 12. (a) Mũklĩsto aĩle kwĩka ata ĩla woona mwana-a-asa 'e ũndũ nake'? (b) Tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ twasũanĩa ũndũ Avalaamu weekie ĩvinda vaumĩlile thĩna? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 3.)
11 Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Maũndũnĩ maingĩ ithyonthe nĩtũlulutĩkaa." (Yak. 3:2) Kwoou twasye nĩwamanya kana ve mwana-a-asa wĩw'ĩthiw'e woo nĩ kĩndũ ũneenie kana wĩkie. Waĩle kwĩka ata vathi ũu? Yesũ aisye ũũ: "Ethĩwa . . . nũũnengane mũthĩnzĩo waku kĩthembeonĩ, na ũkĩlilikanĩla vu kana mwana-a-au e ũndũ naku, tia mũthĩnzĩo waku vu mbee wa kĩthembeo, noithi, wambe kwĩw'ana na mwana-a-au na ĩndĩ ũkyũka ũnengane mũthĩnzĩo waku." (Mt. 5:23, 24) Kwosana na ũtao ũsu wa Yesũ, waĩle kũthi ũneene na mwana-a-asa ũsu. Ĩndĩ nĩwoona waĩle kũthi kũmwona wĩ na kĩeleelo kĩva? Ti kya kwony'a mwana-a-asa ũsu kana o nake ve vandũ ũvĩtĩtye, ĩndĩ nĩ kwĩtĩkĩla ĩvĩtyo ĩ yaku na kwĩw'ana nake. Kwĩw'ana na athaithi ala angĩ nĩkw'o kwa vata vyũ kwĩ ũndũ ũngĩ o na wĩva.
12 Ĩla ngewa ya Avalaamu na Loto ĩeleetw'e Maandĩkonĩ nĩ ngewa nzeo yonanĩtye ũndũ maminie nesa thĩna waĩ ũtonya kũete mũaanĩko. Avalaamu na Loto maĩ na ndĩthya sya indo na no kwĩthĩwa aĩthi moo matetanĩasya kĩsesi kĩla maĩthasya. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Avalaamu nĩwendaa kũmina ithokoo isu, anengie Loto mwanya wa mbee anyuve vala ũkwenda kũtũa na andũ make. (Mwa. 13:1, 2, 5-9) Ĩsu nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ta kĩ! Avalaamu amanthaa kwĩka mũuo, ĩndĩ ti kwĩyĩuna. Ve kĩndũ waaisye nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa ate na ĩtomo? Ndaakwata wasyo o na ũmwe. O na akililye ataanĩsya na Loto oou, Yeova amwatha moathimo maingĩ. (Mwa. 13:14-17) Ngai ndakaeka athũkũmi make makwate wasyo tene na tene ethĩwa nĩwoona maatĩĩa myolooto yake na maeka wendo ũmatongoesye mew'ane ĩla maemanwa. [1]
13. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũmwe eekie ata ĩla wataviw'e naĩ, na ngelekany'o yake ĩtonya kũtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
13 Kwaekai yu tũneenee ũndũ ũneekĩkie o mĩtũkĩ. Ve mũthenya mũsyaĩĩsya ũmwe wa mũvĩa mũna wa ũmbano mũnene wakũnĩie mwana-a-asa ũngĩ simũ nĩ kana amũkũlye ethĩwa no ende kwĩyumya atetheesye wĩa ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Ĩndĩ mwana-a-asa ũsu amũtavisye naĩ na atila ĩ simũ. Mwana-a-asa ũsu aĩ na kyũa nũndũ wa thĩna walikĩte aithũkũma na mũsyaĩĩsya ũla ũngĩ waĩ mbee wa ũũ. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu mweũ ndaathatw'a nĩ mũneenele ũsu ũte mũseo ĩndĩ ndaĩ aekana na ũndũ ũsu. Ekalangile na ĩtina wa ĩsaa yĩmwe akũna simũ ĩngĩ atavya mwana-a-asa ũsu no ende makomane mamine thĩna ũsu. Makomanĩie Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ĩtina wa kyumwa kĩmwe. Mambie kũvoya na ĩndĩ maneena vandũ va ĩsaa yĩmwe. Mwana-a-asa ũsu weew'aa e mũvĩtĩsye nĩweeyĩeleisye. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu nĩwamwĩthukĩĩsye e na tei, amũnenga ũtao wa Maandĩko, na ĩndĩ mataanĩsya ve mũuo. Mwana-a-asa ũsu nĩwesie kũthũkũma ũla ũmbanonĩ mũnene, na yu nũmũtũngĩaa ũla mũsyaĩĩsya mũvea nũndũ wa kũneena nake auĩtye na e na tei.
NĨ ĨNDĨĨ WAĨLE KŨTAVYA ATUMĨA?
14, 15. (a) Nĩ ĩndĩĩ ũtao ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 18:15-17 waĩle kũatĩĩwa? (b) Nĩ matambya meva atatũ Yesũ wawetie, na kĩeleelo kitũ kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa kĩ kĩva ĩla tũũmaatĩĩa?
14 Ĩla Aklĩsto elĩ mathokoana, mavinda maingĩ wĩthĩaa ũsu nĩ thĩna matonya kũmina me oka, na nengĩ ũu nĩw'o vaĩle kwĩthĩwa vailyĩ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩwawetie kana ve vandũ vatonya kũvikwa ũkethĩa thĩna ũsu no ũtavaw'a kĩkundi. (Soma Mathayo 18:15-17.) Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu ya tene vaendaa ata mũndũ ũla ũvĩtĩtye alea kwĩthukĩĩsya ũla ũngĩ, alea kwĩthukĩĩsya ngũsĩ ila syĩsĩ ũndũ ũsu, na ailea kwĩthukĩĩsya kĩkundi? Mũndũ ũsu aaĩle kwoswa ta "Mũndũ-wa-mbaĩ-ingĩ na ta mumya wa koti." Ũmũnthĩ mũndũ wa ũko ũsu ekaa kũtengwa. Nĩkwĩthĩwa ĩtambya yĩu ti ĩtambya ya ngũĩ, no nginya "naĩ" ĩla ĩwetetwe vau ĩkethĩwa yaĩ nene, ĩndĩ ti o kũvĩtũũkana kũla andũ mavĩtũũkanaa. No nginya naĩ ĩsu yĩthĩwe (1) yaĩ ĩtonya kũneenewa nĩ andũ asu me elĩ na mayĩw'ana, na (2) yaĩ ngito ũkethĩa ũla ũmĩkĩte no atengwe malea kũeleanwa. Naĩ ĩsu nĩ ta ũvenani kana o ũneeni ũtonya kwanangĩa mũndũ ĩsyĩtwa. Ĩla naĩ ta isu syeekwa, now'o matambya ala atatũ Yesũ wawetie maĩle kũatĩĩwa. Naĩ ta ii iyaatalĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu: ũlaalai, aũme kũkoma na aũme kana aka kũkoma na aka, kũkaĩa mũĩkĩĩo, kana kũthaitha mĩvw'anano. Naĩ isu na ingĩ ngito no nginya ineenewe nĩ atumĩa ma kĩkundi.
15 Yesũ ainengane ũla ũtao wake endaa kwonany'a kana wendo nĩw'o waĩle kũtũtongoesya ĩla tũũlũnga mwana-a-asa ũvĩtĩtye. (Mt. 18:12-14) Awetie kana ĩtambya ya mbee nĩ kũneena na mwana-a-asa ũsu ũteũlikya andũ angĩ. O na no kwĩthĩwa waĩle kũneena nake ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ. Ĩtambya yĩu yaemela yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩ kũthi kũmwona wĩ na ngũsĩ ila syĩsĩ kĩla kĩendeee, kana wĩ na andũ angĩ matonya kũĩkĩĩthya kana kwa w'o vau ve ĩvĩtyo. Andũ asu makũtetheesya kũmina thĩna wenyu, no ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya "nĩwamwona mwana-a-au." Waĩle kwĩsa kũtavya atumĩa naĩ ĩsu ethĩwa nũtatĩte ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ kũtetheesya ũla ũkũvĩtĩsye na akaema.
16. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana kũatĩĩa ũla ũtao wa Yesũ nĩkũtethasya na nĩkwonanasya kana nĩtwendete angĩ?
16 Nĩ mavinda mavũthũ wĩthĩaa no nginya ana-a-asa maatĩĩe matambya onthe atatũ ala me ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 18:15-17. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũũtwĩkĩa vinya nũndũ wĩonany'a kana kaingĩ thĩna ũminawa tene vatanesa kũvikwa vala mũndũ waĩle kũtengwa. Mavinda maingĩ ũla ũvĩtĩtye nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa ĩvĩtyo yake na ayĩlũnga. Vathi ũu ũla ũvĩtĩw'e nũtonya kwona vate kĩtumi kyaĩlu kya kũatĩanĩa na ũla ũmũvĩtĩsye na nũtonya kũtw'a kũmũekea. Ĩndĩ o na maũndũ methĩwe mailyĩ ata, ndeto sya Yesũ syĩonany'a kana kĩkundi kĩyaĩle kũlikĩlĩĩla ana-a-asa maemanĩtwe ĩvinda yĩte ĩviku. Atumĩa maĩle kwĩsa kũlikĩlĩĩla ethĩwa matambya ala elĩ ma mbee nĩmaminĩte kwoswa, na ethĩwa ve na ũkũsĩ mwĩanu ũkũĩkĩĩthya kĩla kĩnaendeeie.
17. Tũkatanĩa moathimo meva tweekĩa kĩthito 'tũmanthe mũuo'?
17 O na twekala ata nthĩ ĩno ya Satani, tũilea kwĩsa kũvĩtĩsya angĩ nũndũ twĩ na naĩ. Ndeto ila mũmanyĩw'a Yakovo wawetie nĩ sya w'o. Aisye: "Ethĩwa mũndũ ndalulutĩkaa ndetonĩ, ũsu nĩ mũndũ mwĩanĩu, ũtonya kũvota o na mwĩĩ wake w'onthe." (Yak. 3:2) Twenda kwĩw'ana ĩla twaemanwa, no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito 'tũmanthe mũuo, na kũũatĩĩa.' (Sav. 34:14) Ethĩwa twĩ andũ ma mũuo, tũkekalanasya nesa na athaithi ala angĩ na tũkatumaa kĩkundi kĩkala kĩ ngwatanĩo. (Sav. 133:1-3) Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana tũkethĩawa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, nũndũ we nĩ "Ngai wa mũuo." (Alo. 15:33) Ala makwataa moathimo ta asu no ala maekaa wendo ũmatongoesye mew'ane ĩla maemanwa na angĩ.
