translation:
"Be discreet as to how much you reveal to others."—MATT. 9:50.
NOTES: 39, 35
1, 2. Why did Jehovah allow wickedness to develop among humans, and what does this teach us about his patience?
WHY do people often conceal their wrongdoings? Consider why someone might hide a sin like Cain murdering Abel (Gen. 4:3-8), Lamech boasting of killing a man (Gen. 4:23), or the disputes between Abram (Abraham) and Lot (Gen. 13:5-7), Jacob deceiving Esau (Gen. 27:1-46), Sarah mistreating Hagar (Gen. 16:3-6), and Ishmael becoming rebellious and aggressive toward everyone.—Gen. 16:12.
2 Does the Bible give examples of people concealing wrongdoing? One reason is that it helps us understand how easy it is for us to be imperfect. And the Bible shows that concealing something can make us feel we have more control over a situation. Reading about how people in ancient times concealed things can help us appreciate that we are not unique in our tendency to hide faults or mistakes. Studying such accounts can also help us learn from them and avoid making similar errors. It can strengthen our resolve to speak truthfully and to seek forgiveness when we err.—Prov. 15:4.
3. What will we discuss in this section?
3 We will discuss how Jehovah allows imperfection to manifest itself among humans, and why he does so. Also, we will see how a study of the Scriptures can help us view matters realistically. We will examine why it is important that we be honest with ourselves and with others, and why we should strive to maintain integrity with God.
WHY GOD ALLOWS IMPERFECTION TO MANIFEST ITSELF
4. Why did God allow humans to experience temptation, and what is the purpose of allowing it?
4 Satan is the main instigator who leads people astray through temptation. He misled Eve, Adam's wife, leading her—and eventually all mankind—to desire independence from God and to want to determine good and bad for themselves. (Gen. 3:1-5) Every human inherits this inclination toward independence. That is why people often try to justify their wrong actions. Temptation gives people opportunities to choose between right and wrong, and it reveals their true character. The one who yields to temptation demonstrates his lack of appreciation for God's standards, and he aligns himself with Satan, who wants people to reject God's guidance. By remaining faithful, however, a person proves his loyalty to God and strengthens his relationship with Him. So, God allows temptation to test people and expose their hearts.—Prov. 29:22.
5. How did Jesus show people how they could deal with imperfections and remain loyal to God?
5 By his example, Jesus showed people how to resist Satan and overcome temptation. He demonstrated that we can maintain integrity even when faced with difficult trials. In harmony with God's will, Jesus firmly rejected Satan's attempts to tempt him to compromise his principles. For instance, Jesus rebuked those who harbored resentment, those who lusted, those who committed adultery, those who swore falsely, and those who sought revenge.—Matt. 5:5, 9, 22, 25, 44.
6, 7. (a) What does it mean to be imperfect and still please God? (b) What qualities of Jehovah help us to cope with our imperfections?
6 We can still have a close relationship with God despite being imperfect. For example, we may stumble, make mistakes, and struggle with undesirable tendencies. But if we sincerely repent and strive to do what is right, God will forgive us. (Mark 11:25) God understands that we are not perfect and that we need time to learn to apply Bible principles.—Read Luke 11:4; Ephesians 4:32.
7 Every Christian should endeavor to show kindness to others and associate with them, while at the same time maintaining high standards. This requires self-control and discernment. For example, how can we show genuine interest in fellow Christians and strengthen their faith? Should we quickly become intimate with someone, or should we take time to get to know them well? Jehovah appreciates our efforts to exercise good judgment. So, if a brother or sister feels drawn to someone, is it wise to pursue a romantic relationship without first seeking Jehovah's guidance? Our prayers can help us to discern whether such a relationship would be pleasing to Him, and we can ask for His blessing.—1 John 5:14, 15.
DO IMPERFECTIONS EXCUSE US?
8, 9. Why is it important for us to acknowledge our imperfections?
8 As imperfect humans, we may sometimes say or do things that hurt others, either intentionally or unintentionally. But even when this happens, there is always room for improvement. (Proverbs 7:20; Matthew 18:7) What if you offend someone? The way you handle the situation will reveal much about your spirituality. Satan delights in causing division among God's people, and he uses our imperfections to tempt us to react badly. However, a mature Christian will strive to repair any damage done and will humbly apologize. Consider a young man who has wronged a fellow believer. He might approach him and say, "I am sorry." Such an attitude pleases Jehovah.
9 What can help us to avoid causing offense? Do not be quick to take offense yourself, but try to show understanding toward others. People often respond positively to kindness. (Read Proverbs 10:12; 1 Peter 4:8) Jehovah understands that we are "prone to error," yet he expects us to 'make efforts.' (Proverbs 19:11; Matthew 7:9) Often, simply taking the initiative to listen can prevent a misunderstanding from escalating. Ask yourself, "Could I have misunderstood what was said? Should I try to discuss the matter calmly with the person who offended me?"
10. (a) How does a mature Christian respond when he realizes he has offended someone? (b) What Scriptural principles can help a Christian to maintain good relationships?
10 Realizing you may have offended someone is never easy. Consider the experience of a sister named Lucy. She felt hurt because of something her husband said and how he said it. Instead of reacting in anger, she decided to talk to him about it. She told him: "I feel bad when you criticize my cooking and speak to me in a harsh tone, and I wonder if you would be willing to work on this." Lucy then took the time to read Matthew 6:1-4. (Read.) This scripture helped her see that practicing humility is vital to maintaining a loving relationship with Jehovah. She realized: "Even if others say unkind things, I can remain calm and not let my feelings get the better of me so that I will continue to please Jehovah." As a result of applying what she learned, Lucy found it easier to cope with difficult situations.
DO EFFORTS TO MAKE PEACE PLEASE JEHOVAH?
11, 12. (a) How can a Christian tell if he has wronged someone? (b) What can we learn from Abraham's example about making peace? (See footnote 3.)
11 The Bible says: "A soft answer turns away rage." (Jas. 3:2) But how can we know if we have offended someone, whether intentionally or unintentionally? Jesus gave this advice: "If, therefore, you are presenting your gift at the altar, and there you remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there at the altar and go reconcile yourself with your brother. Then come and offer your gift." (Matt. 5:23, 24) Following Jesus' counsel, make an effort to approach the person you may have offended. Ask yourself, 'How would I feel if someone spoke to me in a similar way?' If you sense that you have hurt his feelings, apologize sincerely and try to resolve the issue. Approaching others with a humble spirit can often lead to positive results.
12 The account of Abram (Abraham) and Lot teaches us a valuable lesson about avoiding disputes and maintaining peace. Both men were wealthy and had many possessions, which led to quarrels among their herdsmen. Abram generously allowed Lot to choose the best land for himself. (Gen. 13:1, 2, 5-9) This illustrates a fine principle! Abram showed humility, and he did not insist on getting his own way. What does this teach us about dealing with disagreements? Jehovah richly blessed Abram because of his peaceful attitude. (Gen. 13:14-17) God expects all Christians to show consideration for others and to put love for them above personal interests, so that they will glorify his name. [1]
13. How can we improve our ability to maintain peace, and what will help us to do so?
13 Consider a situation that troubles your heart. Perhaps you feel slighted by someone. Before reacting, ask yourself: 'Is this issue really worth damaging my relationship with this person?' Often, it is not. A child may offend us unintentionally, yet we get upset with him. That child may then become discouraged and withdraw. But if we respond calmly, we can reason with him and help him to understand why his actions were wrong. We can then strengthen our bond with that child. Remember, a calm response often disarms another person and opens the way for a peaceful resolution. Think of the example of a parent who patiently explains things to a child. By doing so, the parent helps the child to learn and grow. And the child feels loved and appreciated.
WHY SHOULD WE STRIVE TO MAINTAIN PEACE?
14, 15. (a) How does Matthew 18:15-17 teach us how to resolve disputes? (b) What steps did Jesus outline, and what important principle is highlighted in those steps?
14 If a fellow Christian wrongs you, often it is best to try to solve the problem yourself first, if possible. However, Jesus showed that there are times when it is necessary to get help from others in the congregation. (Read Matthew 18:15-17.) Does this scripture show that we should go to another person to complain about someone who has wronged us, to seek his opinion on the matter, or to ask him to intervene? Such a course might lead someone to be labeled as "a gossip" or "one who goes around talking." It is vital that such a one remain isolated. This step is not meant to involve a committee, nor does the expression "you" refer to going to more than one person. Rather, it means (1) going to someone whom you trust and who is mature, and (2) going to someone who can offer practical assistance and is willing to listen. This approach avoids causing unnecessary embarrassment. But if this step is ignored, then the steps that Jesus outlined become especially important. The scripture highlights these points: Go by yourselves, or take one or two with you, so that every matter may be established by the evidence of two or three witnesses. And if he will not listen to them, tell it to the congregation. This also shows that it is important to have support from members of the congregation.
15 Jesus illustrated what we should do if a brother or sister offends us by telling the parable of the lost sheep. (Matt. 18:12-14) He taught that it is important to search for that erring one, just as a shepherd searches for a lost sheep. We should be willing to speak to him again and again. That effort demonstrates our desire to restore him to spiritual health, whether he responds positively or whether others may try to help him. Christians should make an effort to reason with those who wrong them, and they should remember the words "I once felt like that too." Be willing to use the Scriptures and to continue speaking to him repeatedly, helping him to see his error.
16. How, then, can we apply Jesus' teaching regarding how to deal with offenses, and how can we show love toward our brothers?
16 This is a vital point, and we find further guidance in Matthew 18:15-17. It shows us the importance of taking steps to help a brother or sister who has stumbled so that he does not become permanently alienated. Often, such a one needs encouragement and loving attention. But when someone stubbornly refuses to listen, it may be necessary to involve others in an attempt to help him, and we may need to ask for assistance. However, Jesus stressed the importance of dealing with the matter privately whenever possible, rather than publicly exposing the fault before the congregation. The disciples were willing to forgive seventy times seven, showing their readiness to extend forgiveness generously.
17. What practical steps can we take to determine 'whether we have caused offense'?
17 We should also be alert to Satan's influence, which might lead us to stumble without realizing it. James' warning is relevant here. He wrote: "If anyone does not stumble in speech, he is a perfect man, able also to bridle his whole body." (Jas. 3:2) Let us examine ourselves honestly, and then apply the principle: 'Keep watch over my mouth, and do not let my lips speak foolishly.' (Ps. 34:14) As spiritual people, we strive to maintain peace and unity among our brothers, and we work together harmoniously. (Ps. 133:1-3) And in this way, we show that we value our close relationship with Jehovah, whom the psalmist calls "the God of peace." (Isa. 15:33) So let us carefully consider how our words affect others, and let us avoid saying anything that could cause pain or division.

MBATHI: 1, 48
1, 2. Yeova atũmĩaa ata syĩndũ ila ũmbĩte kwonany'a nĩ mũlau?
YEOVA nĩ Ngai mũlau. Nĩwe ũtũnengete kyonthe kĩla twĩ nakyo. Thaavu na vetha nĩ syake vamwe na syĩndũ ila ingĩ sya vata syoombiwe, na nũitũmĩaa nĩ kana atũtetheesye tũendeee kwĩkala thayũ. (Sav. 104:13-15; Akai 2:8) Mbivilianĩ ve ngewa mbingĩ syonanĩtye kana ve mavinda Yeova weekie syama atetheesya andũ make atũmĩĩte syĩndũ ila woombie.
2 Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova nĩwanengie mbaĩ ya Isilaeli mana na kĩw'ũ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 40 ĩla maĩ weũnĩ. (Kuma 16:35) Na kwa kĩtumi kĩu "vai kĩndũ kyaamaĩa." (Nee. 9:20, 21, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Nake mwathani Elisa nĩwatũmĩiwe nĩ Yeova kwĩka kyama kĩla kyatumie mauta manini ma kĩveti ndiwa maingĩva mũno. Mũthĩnzĩo ũsu Ngai wakĩnengie nĩwakĩtetheeisye kũĩva makoani ala kyataĩtwe na kyakwata mbesa itoetye kũkĩĩthya vamwe na syana syakyo. (2 Asu. 4:1-7) O nake Yesũ nĩwatetheeiw'e nĩ Yeova eeka kyama andũ makwata lĩu o na mbesa ĩla vaĩ vata.—Mt. 15:35-38; 17:27.
3. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Yeova e na malĩ mbingĩ ũtonya kũtũmĩa atetheesye syũmbe syake kũũ nthĩ. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu nũthoketye athũkũmi make matũmĩe kĩla me nakyo kũtetheesya wĩa ũseũvyonĩ wake. (Kuma 36:3-7; soma Nthimo 3:9.) Yo nĩkĩ Yeova wendaa tũmũolele syĩndũ sya vata ila ũtũnete? Mo athũkũmi ma Yeova ma tene matũmĩie syĩndũ syoo ata kũtetheesya wĩa wake? W'o ũseũvyo witũ ũtũmĩaa ata mĩvothi ĩla yumaw'a ũmũnthĩ? Makũlyo asu nĩmo tũũsũngĩa ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ.
NĨKĨ TŨMŨNENGAE YEOVA SYĨNDŨ ILA ŨTŨNENGETE?
4. Twĩthĩawa tũyony'a Yeova kyaũ ĩla twatetheesya wĩa wake?
4 Tũmũnengae Yeova nũndũ nĩtũmwendete na nĩtwendaa kũmũtũngĩa mũvea. Twasũanĩa maũndũ ala Yeova ũtwĩkĩte twĩw'aa ngoo sitũ syakiitwa mũno. Ve kĩndũ Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti wawetie ĩla waneeneaa syĩndũ ila syendekaa kwondũ wa wĩa ũla wavangĩtwe wa kwaka ĩkalũ. Awetie kana kyonthe kĩla twĩ nakyo kyumaa kwa Yeova na kyonthe kĩla tũtonya kũmũnenga no kĩla ũtũnengete.—Soma 1 Mavinda 29:11-14.
5. Maandĩko monanĩtye ata kana kũnengane na ũlau nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya vata ya kũmũthaitha Yeova?
5 O na ĩngĩ kũmũnenga Yeova kĩla twĩ nakyo nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũmũthaitha. Woninĩ ũla mũtũmwa Yoana wooniw'e nĩweewie athũkũmi ma Yeova ĩtunĩ mayasya: "Nĩwaĩle we, Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Ngai waitũ, kwosa ndaĩa na nguma na vinya: nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwoombie syĩndũ syonthe, na kwondũ wa kwenda kwaku syaĩ kw'o, na ĩngĩ syoombwa." (Ũvu. 4:11) O naku ndũkwĩtĩkĩla kana nĩtwaĩle kũmũnenga Yeova nguma na ndaĩa yonthe kwa kũmũnenga kĩla kĩseo twĩ nakyo? Ĩvinda yĩmwe Mose nĩwataviw'e nĩ Yeova eaĩe mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yũmbanae katatũ kwa mwaka. Meeĩtwe ĩla ĩvinda ya kũmbana yavika "matikokae mbee wa Yeova na moko mathei" nũndũ kũmũnenga Yeova kĩla me nakyo kwaĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũmũthaitha. (Kũt. 16:16) O ta ũu, ũmũnthĩ nĩtwaĩle kumya kĩla twĩ nakyo na ũlau tũtetheesye wĩa ũla kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Yeova kya kũũ nthĩ kĩtwaĩĩsye, na tũyonany'a nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa wĩa ũsu. Kwĩka ũu nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya vata vyũ ya kũmũthaitha Yeova.
6. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana kũnengane nĩkũtũunaa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 17.)
6 Kũnengane nĩ kũseo. O na kau nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo twanewa, tũunĩkaa mũno ĩla twanengane na ũlau. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Mũthũkũmi ananw'a kuma e kana, mũminũkĩlyo akatw'ĩka mũndũ ũte mũvea." (Nth. 29:21, NWT) Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwana wathooea asyai mũthĩnzĩo atũmĩĩte o tũsilingi tũla mamũnengae. We wĩona asyai asu ta mew'a ata? Kana kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwanake kana mwĩĩtu ũtonya kwĩthĩwa aendeee kũkũna ũvainia e mũsyĩ, na aitw'a kũtetheesya asyai make na mbesa sya kũũngamĩa ngalama imwe sya vau mũsyĩ. O na kau no kwĩthĩwa asyai ma syana isu mateeĩkwatĩtye syana isu syĩke ũu, mayamba kũlea mĩthĩnzĩo yasyo nũndũ ĩla mwana weeka ũu ethĩawa ayonany'a nũkũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa moseo ala mũsyai ũmwĩkĩte. O ta ũu, Yeova nĩwĩsĩ kana kũmũnenga syĩndũ sitũ sya vata nĩkũtũunaa.
ŨNDŨ ATHŨKŨMI MA TENE MA NGAI MAMŨNENGAE SYĨNDŨ SYOO
7, 8. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana athũkũmi ma Yeova ma tene nĩmatũtiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo kwa kumya mĩvothi (a) kwondũ wa mawĩa mana mavangĩĩwe? (b) kwondũ wa kũtwaĩĩsya mbee wĩa wake?
7 Maandĩko nĩmaeleetye ngewa sya andũ maumisye syĩndũ ila maĩ nasyo nĩ kana makwate mbau wĩa wa Ngai. Ve mavinda athũkũmi ma Yeova maumisye mĩvothi ya kũtetheesya mawĩa mana mavangĩĩwe. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mose nĩwakũlilye andũ maumye mĩvothi kwondũ wa kwakwa kwa ĩeema ya kũmbanĩa, o tondũ Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti weekie ĩla woombanasya mĩvothi kwondũ wa mwako wa ĩkalũ. (Kuma 35:5; 1 Mav. 29:5-9) Nayo ĩvindanĩ ya Mũsumbĩ Yoasi athembi matũmĩie mbesa ila syoombaniw'e kũtũngĩĩa nyũmba ya Yeova. (2 Asu. 12:4, 5) O na kĩkundinĩ kya mbee kya Kĩklĩsto mĩvothi nĩyatethisye. Ana-a-asa makililye matavw'a vata ũla waĩ vo nũndũ wa yũa, "kĩla mũndũ kwĩanana na ũtonyi wake, masũanĩa, matw'a kũmatwaĩa ũtethyo ana-a-ĩthe moo ala matwĩe Yutia."—Meko 11:27-30.
8 Nao mavinda angĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova nĩmaumasya mĩvothi matetheesye ala matongoesye wĩanĩ wa Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvindanĩ ya Mĩao ya Mose, Alivai mayaanengwa ũtiĩwa ta mbaĩ ila ĩngĩ sya Isilaeli. Na kwoou Aisilaeli mamanengae kĩlungu kya ĩkũmi nĩ kana matũngĩanĩe kĩlĩko kyoo ũthũkũminĩ ũla manengetwe ĩeemanĩ ya kũmbanĩa. (Mot. 18:21) O ta ũu, Yesũ na atũmwa make nĩmatethekie mũno nĩ ũlau wa aka ala 'mamatetheeasya na isamũ syoo.'—Luka 8:1-3.
9. Ĩvindanĩ ya tene andũ maumasya mĩvothi va?
9 Tene andũ makwataa syĩndũ na mbesa ila maumasya ta mĩvothi kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Aisilaeli maumasya mĩvothi kwondũ wa mwako wa ĩeema ya kũmbanĩa me weũnĩ, nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa manenganie syĩndũ imwe maumĩtye Misili. (Kuma 3:21, 22; 35:22-24) Nayo ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, Aklĩsto amwe nĩmathooisye syĩndũ syoo, ta mĩũnda kana nyũmba, na manenga atũmwa i mbesa ta mũvothi. Namo atũmwa makwata mbesa isu nĩmaaĩaa ala me na vata wa kũtetheew'a. (Meko 4:34, 35) Angĩ namo nĩmaiaa mbesa imwe ũtee nĩ kana masyumye itetheesye wĩa wa Ngai. (1 Ako. 16:2) Kwa nzĩa ĩsu andũ onthe, kuma ũla ngya vyũ nginya ũla mũthwii mũno, nĩmaĩ matonya kumya mĩvothi.—Luka 21:1-4.
TŨNENGAE NGAI SYĨNDŨ SITŨ ATA ŨMŨNTHĨ?
10, 11. (a) O ta athũkũmi ma Yeova ma tene, tũtonya ata kũnengane syĩndũ sitũ na ũlau? (b) We wĩw'aa ata wasũanĩa kĩanda kĩla ũnengetwe kya kũtetheesya wĩa wa Ũsumbĩ?
10 Ũmũnthĩ o naitũ no tũkũlw'e tumye mĩvothi kwondũ wa wĩa mũna wa mwanya. Kwa ngelekany'o, kĩkundi kyenyu nĩkĩtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũvango wa kwaka Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ. Kana nĩvatonyeka Nyũmba yenyu ya Ũsumbĩ ĩkethĩwa yĩ na kũndũ kũkwenda kũtũngĩĩwa. O na nĩtũtonya kũtavw'a kana ve mĩvothi ĩkwendeka ĩtetheesye kũtũngĩĩa ovisi witũ wa ũvonge kũla kwĩ na thĩna, kana ĩtũmĩke ũmbanonĩ mũnene ũvangĩĩwe, kana o ĩtetheesye ana-a-asa me vandũ makwatiwe nĩ mũisyo. O na ĩngĩ nĩtumasya mĩvothi ya kũtetheesya ala mathũkũmaa ovisinĩ witũ mũnene na movisinĩ ma ũvonge isionĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Na ti ũu wĩ w'oka, mĩvothi yitũ nĩtũmĩawa kũtetheesya amisonalĩ, mavainia ma mwanya, na asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana no kwĩthĩwa kĩkundinĩ kyenyu veekiwe ũtwi wa kũtũmaa mbesa iana ũna nĩ kana itũmĩwe ũla mũvangonĩ wa kwakĩa ana-a-asa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ na Nyũmba sya Maũmbano Manene isionĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
11 Kĩla ũmwe no aumye kĩndũ akatetheesya wĩa ũla Yeova ũendeee kũtethya mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo. Mĩvothi mingĩ ĩla tumasya yĩthĩawa yĩ ya kĩmbithĩ. Kwoou tũyendaa ala angĩ mamanye mbesa ila tweekĩa ĩsandũkũnĩ ya mĩvothi Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, kana ila twaumya ta mũvothi tũtũmĩĩte jw.org. No twone kamũvothi kala tumasya ta katatethya mũno. Ĩndĩ manya kana mĩvothi mingĩ ĩla tũkwataa yĩthĩawa yumanĩte na tũmĩthĩnzĩo tũnini tũnini tũla tumĩtw'e, na ti mĩthĩnzĩo o ĩla mĩnene yumĩtw'e no andũ ma kũtala. O na kau ana-a-asa amwe mekalaa isionĩ syĩ na thĩna wa mbesa, mailyĩ ta andũ ma Masetonia, ala o na nthĩnĩ wa "ũkya woo mũnene" meesũvanie mũno manengwe mwanya wa kũnengane na kwenda kwa ngoo syoo.—2 Ako. 8:1-4.
12. Ũseũvyo witũ wĩkaa ata nĩ kana ũĩkĩĩthye mĩvothi ĩla yaumw'a nĩyatũmĩka nesa?
12 Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye nĩvoyaa mũno ĩtetheew'e yĩthĩwe yĩ ndĩkĩĩku na yĩ na ũĩ nĩ kana ĩvangĩĩe ũndũ mbesa ila syakwatĩkana ũseũvyonĩ ikũtũmĩwa nesa. (Mt. 24:45) Mbesa ila syakwatĩkana ivangĩĩawa kwosana na mavata ala me vo na iitũmĩwa o vatanĩ ũla syavangĩĩwa. (Luka 14:28) Ĩvindanĩ ya tene aũme aĩkĩĩku ala mekalaa na mĩvothi ĩla yaumw'a nĩmeethĩawa na mũvango mũseo wa kũĩkĩĩthya kana mĩvothi ĩsu ndĩnatũmĩwa ũndũnĩ ũngĩ eka o vatanĩ ũla ĩkumĩaw'a. Ũmwe woo aĩ Esala, ũla wavothewe syĩndũ nĩ mũsumbĩ wa Velisia asyoke nasyo Yelusaleme. Anengiwe thaavu, vetha, na syĩndũ ingĩ ila ũmũnthĩ itonya kwĩthĩwa syĩ na lato wa mbee wa ndola milioni 100 sya Amelika. Esala oosie syĩndũ isu ta mũthĩnzĩo wanengwa Yeova, na kwoou nĩweekie mĩvango myalany'e nesa nĩ kana aĩkĩĩthye malĩ ĩsu nĩyasũvĩĩka nesa me kyalonĩ kyoo nũndũ mesaa kwĩsĩla kũndũ kũthũku na kwĩ amaitha. (Esa. 8:24-34) Nake mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwoombanisye mĩvothi ya kũtetheesya ana-a-asa ma Yutia ala maĩ na thĩna. Nĩweekie mĩvango aĩkĩĩthye nesa kana ala meũtwaa mĩvothi ĩsu nĩmamĩtũmĩa nesa kwĩanĩsya "maũndũ ala maĩlu, ti mbee wa Ngai weka, ĩndĩ o na mbee wa andũ." (Soma 2 Akolintho 8:18-21.) O tondũ Esala na Vaulo meekie, ũmũnthĩ ũseũvyo witũ nĩwĩthĩawa na mĩtalatala mĩseo ĩkonetye ũndũ mĩvothi ĩkũtũmĩwa na nĩatĩĩawa nesa vateũtũngwa ngũĩ.
13. Nĩkĩ ũseũvyo wĩkĩte moalyũku mana myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ?
13 Nĩ kana mwene mũsyĩ na andũ make methĩwe matonya kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme Yeova mũnango, no mavange kũolanga ngalama syoo wĩthĩe nĩmaeka kũtũmĩa mbesa mbingĩ kwĩ ila makwataa, kana makeka kũolanga syĩndũ imwe me nasyo. Ũu now'o ũseũvyo wa Yeova wĩkaa. Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ nĩkwĩthĩĩtwe kũyambĩĩw'a tũmaũndũ twingĩ tũseo. Nũndũ wa ũu, mavinda amwe wĩthĩaa mbesa ila ikumw'a nĩ nini kwĩ ila siũtũmĩka. Kwoou o ta ũla mwene mũsyĩ na andũ make, ũseũvyo nũmanthaa ũndũ ũtonya kũolanga ngalama na ũimantha nzĩa ingĩ syĩ laisi sya kũtethya wĩa ũla wĩ vo nĩ kana mĩvothi ĩla mumasya na ũlau yĩthĩwe ĩtonya kwĩanĩsya mavata maingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka.
ŨNDŨ MĨVOTHI YAKU ĨTETHASYA
14-16. (a) Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva meanĩĩtw'e na mĩvothi ĩla umasya? (b) Maũndũ asu maũtetheetye ata we mwene?
14 Andũ aingĩ mamũthũkũmĩte Yeova kwa ĩvinda ĩasa maasya kana vai ĩvinda ũseũvyo wa Yeova waatũnenga syĩndũ mbingĩ sya kũtũtetheesya kĩ-veva ta ũndũ ũtũnengete ũmũnthĩ. Kwasũanĩa we! Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ nĩtũnaseũvĩiw'e kĩsese kya jw.org, na JW Broadcasting yambĩĩw'a. O na eka ũu, Biblia Takatifu—Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya yu nĩtumbĩthĩtw'e na ithyomo ingĩ mbingĩ. Na ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa ũndũ katĩ wa mwaka wa 2014 na 2015 iwanza imwe nene syĩ taoninĩ 14 nene ĩũlũ wa nthĩ syausũĩte andũ moombanĩte kwondũ wa Ũmbano Mũnene wa Nthĩ Mbingĩ, ũla waĩ na kyongo, "Endeeai Kũmantha Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai Mbee!" Ala maĩ maũmbanonĩ asu matanie mũno!
15 Aingĩ nĩmatũngĩte mũvea nũndũ wa mĩthĩnzĩo mingĩ ĩla ũseũvyo wa Yeova ũtũnengete. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mũka matũmĩtwe nthĩ ĩmwe ya Asia maandĩkie ũũ maiweta JW Broadcasting: "Tũtũmĩtwe taoninĩ ĩmwe nini. Na nũndũ wa ũu mavinda angĩ twĩw'aa twĩ kũasa mũno na andũ ala angĩ, na nĩ laisi tũkolwa kana ve maũndũ maingĩ mũno meanĩĩtw'e wĩanĩ wa Yeova. Ĩndĩ ĩla tweeloela JW Broadcasting nĩtũlilikanaa kana twĩ na ana-a-asa nthĩ yonthe. Ana-a-asa ala me kĩsionĩ kĩĩ mew'aa mũyo mũno meeloela JW Broadcasting. Nĩtũkothaa kwĩw'a maiweta kana meeloela vitio isu syumaa kĩla mwei mew'aa menda mũno ana-a-asa ma Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye. Yu nĩmew'aa wĩ ũndũ mũnene kũwetanĩw'a na ũseũvyo wa Ngai kwĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva."
16 Yu tũũneena, nthĩ yonthe twĩ na Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ vakuvĩ 2,500 iendeee kwakwa kana kwĩkwa moalyũku manene. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma kĩkundi kĩmwe kya nthĩ ya Honduras nĩmaandĩkie valũa ĩla mambĩĩe kũtũmĩa Nyũmba yoo ya Ũsumbĩ. Maisye: "Twĩ na ũtanu kwĩthĩwa twĩ amwe ma athaithi ma Yeova, na nĩtũtanĩaa ngwatanĩo ĩla twĩ nayo ya ana-a-asa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe nũndũ maũndũ asu nĩmo meanĩĩtye wĩkwatyo witũ wa kwĩthĩwa na Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ vaa kĩsionĩ." O ta ũu ve aingĩ maeleasya ũtanu woo ĩtina wa kũkwata Mbivilia na mavuku angĩ maalyũlĩtwe na ithyomo syoo, ĩtina wa kũtetheew'a ĩvinda ya thĩna, kana ĩtina wa kwona moathimo ma kũtavany'a taoninĩ nene na kũla kwĩthĩawa andũ aingĩ isionĩ syoo.
17. Twasũanĩa ũndũ ũseũvyo witũ ũthũkũmaa, nĩkĩ tũĩkĩĩaa vyũ kana Yeova e vamwe naitũ?
17 Ala mate Ngũsĩ maikwatasya ũndũ wĩa witũ ũtonya kũtw'ĩka ũtwaĩĩaw'a na mĩvothi ya ngenda. Ve ĩvinda mũũngamĩi wa kambunĩ ĩmwe nene watembeie ovisinĩ ũmwe wa kũtumbĩthya mavuku maitũ. Aseng'ie mũno ĩla wamanyie kana wĩa ũsu ũtethaw'a nĩ andũ mekĩte kwĩyumya, na kana ũtwaĩĩaw'a na mĩvothi ya ngenda, na kana tũi ĩndĩ twĩsaa kũsangĩthya mbesa. Aisye kana ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtatonyeka. Na nĩ w'o! Nĩtwĩsĩ kana ũu ũtonyekete nũndũ Yeova e vamwe naitũ.—Yovu 42:2.
ŨNDŨ TŨATHIMĨKAA TWAMŨNENGA YEOVA
18. (a) Tũkwataa moathimo meva twakwata mbau wĩa wa Ũsumbĩ? (b) Tũtonya kũtetheesya ata syana sitũ na ala eũ makwate mbau wĩa ũsu?
18 Yeova nũtũnengete kĩanda kĩ mwanya kya kũtetheesya wĩa mũnene ũla ũendeee ũmũnthĩ. Na nũtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana akatũathima twakwata mbau wĩa ũsu wa Ũsumbĩ. (Mal. 3:10) Yeova nũmwathĩte ũla ũnenganae na ũlau kana maũndũ make mailea kũthi nesa. (Soma Nthimo 11:24, 25.) O na ĩngĩ kũnengane nĩkũtumaa twĩthĩwa na ũtanu nũndũ "kwĩ mũyo kũnengane kwĩ kwosa." (Meko 20:35) Kwoou kwa ndeto na kwa ngelekany'o sitũ nzeo, nĩtwaĩle kũmanyĩsya syana sitũ na ala eũ mamanye ũndũ matonya kũtetheesya wĩa ũsu, nĩ kana o namo methĩwe matonya kũtanĩa moathimo maingĩ.
19. Ĩsomo yĩĩ yakwĩkĩa vinya ata?
19 Kyonthe kĩla twĩ nakyo tũnengetwe nĩ Yeova. Ĩla twamũnenga kĩla twĩ nakyo twonanasya kana nĩtũmwendete na kana nĩtũũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa maũndũ ala ũtwĩkĩte. (1 Mav. 29:17) Ĩla mĩvothi ya kwaka ĩkalũ yaumaw'a, 'andũ nĩmatanie, nũndũ nĩmanenganie na kwenda kwa ngoo, nũndũ nĩmamumĩsye Yeova makyenda na ngoo mbĩanĩu.' (1 Mav. 29:9) O ta ũu, twaendeea kũmũnenga Yeova o kĩla ũtũnengete, tũkakwataa ũtanu na tũkekalaa twĩ eanĩe.

translation:
"My God, we praise you for your kindness, and we proclaim your truthfulness." – 1 CHR. 29:13.
NOTES: 1, 48
1, 2. Does Jehovah use imperfect people despite their flaws because he is loving?
JEHOVAH is a loving God. He cares deeply about us. The plants and animals are his creations, and although some cause problems, he continues to use them to accomplish his purpose and to allow us to continue living. (Ps. 104:13-15; Acts 2:8) Many people wonder why Jehovah would use imperfect humans to accomplish his will.
2 For example, Jehovah was patient with Israel for 40 years while they wandered in the wilderness. (Num. 16:35) And he used the expression "human foolishness." (Neh. 9:20, 21, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Also, Elijah was used by Jehovah to perform miracles, such as providing abundant food during a severe famine. However, God also allowed him to experience feelings of fear and discouragement, which led him to flee for his life. (1 Ki. 4:1-7) Similarly, Jesus was used by Jehovah to feed thousands of people who were hungry.—Matt. 15:35-38; 17:27.
3. What will we now consider?
3 Jehovah has many ways of using his spirit to help us. Indeed, he often uses imperfect humans to accomplish his will. (Num. 36:3-7; see Proverbs 3:9.) But does Jehovah expect us to wait for extraordinary things to happen before we show our appreciation for what he does? Do Jehovah's servants need spectacular displays to motivate them to serve him? Or should our love for him move us to act without needing a miracle? Let us examine this further.
WHY SHOULD WE APPRECIATE WHAT JEHOVAH DOES FOR US?
4. How can we show Jehovah that we appreciate what he does for us?
4 We can show Jehovah that we love him by being obedient and eager to please him. We should be grateful for the blessings Jehovah gives us, realizing that we deserve none of them. King David showed his gratitude when he acknowledged that everything came from Jehovah and that everything belonged to Jehovah.—Read 1 Chronicles 29:11-14.
5. Can the scriptures help us to avoid feeling entitled and to continue appreciating Jehovah?
5 Showing appreciation for Jehovah is also a way to honor him. The apostle John wrote about how deeply moved he was when he saw visions of Jehovah: "I fell prostrate before the angel who was showing me these things and began worshiping him. But he said to me: 'Get up! Worship God only!'" (Rev. 4:11) Should we not feel similarly motivated to express our gratitude to Jehovah for all that he does for us? Moses demonstrated great appreciation when Jehovah assigned the Israelites three annual festivals. These festivals reminded them that they were to give thanks to Jehovah "for his loving-kindness and for his wonderful works."—Ex. 16:16. So, when we take time to reflect on all that Jehovah does for us and meditate on his beautiful qualities, we strengthen our love for him and are more eager to please him. This is another way to honor Jehovah.
6. How can we know whether we are truly appreciative? (See the accompanying article, "Staying Appreciative.")
6 Being appreciative involves action. While we may have good intentions, we need to show our appreciation through what we do. The Bible says: "A slave is not above his master. If he is given authority, the whole household will fall into disorder." (Prov. 29:21, NWT) Just imagine a son who constantly asks his parents for money but never uses it responsibly. Would you not be disappointed? Or imagine a husband who repeatedly promises his wife something but always puts off fulfilling his promise, causing her frustration and disappointment. Similarly, if we claim to appreciate Jehovah but do not act in harmony with that appreciation, our words will sound empty. It is important to demonstrate our gratitude by using our resources to support God's work and by zealously proclaiming the good news. Jehovah values genuine expressions of appreciation.
WAYS TO SHOW APPRECIATION FOR GOD
7, 8. How can we show that we value the privilege of (a) sharing in the ministry and (b) being part of God's family?
7 The Scriptures show us examples of people who demonstrated their appreciation for God's blessings. They did so by actively engaging in activities pleasing to Him. For example, Moses encouraged the Israelites to contribute toward the construction of the tabernacle, and King David made generous donations toward the building of the temple. (Ex. 35:5; 1 Chron. 29:5-9) Also, King Joash authorized the use of funds that had been set aside for the repair of the house of Jehovah. (2 Kings 12:4, 5) And early Christians readily used their means to help others. They willingly shared whatever they had, saying: "Each one should give what his heart prompts him—generously, without grudging, because God loves a cheerful giver."—Acts 11:27-30.
8 Furthermore, there are numerous examples of people who showed their gratitude to Jehovah by supporting those engaged in spiritual activities. For instance, during the time of Moses, the Levites were appointed to care for the tabernacle on behalf of all Israel. And the Israelites voluntarily contributed a tenth of their income to support those serving at the tabernacle. (Num. 18:21) Similarly, Jesus and his apostles were supported by women who provided for them out of their own resources.—Luke 8:1-3.
9. What motivates people to be generous?
9 People are motivated by various factors to be generous, but true generosity stems from love. For example, the Israelites willingly contributed toward the construction of the tabernacle because they loved Jehovah and appreciated the opportunity to serve him. (Ex. 3:21, 22; 35:22-24) Also, the apostles, including Christ, used their personal possessions, such as money or homes, to help fellow believers. And the apostles readily shared what little they had with others so that the good news could be preached. (Acts 4:34, 35) Some also share their belongings freely, knowing that this pleases God. (1 Cor. 16:2) In fact, some have sold all their possessions to devote themselves fully to the ministry.—Luke 21:1-4.
WHAT CAN WE OFFER TO GOD?
10, 11. (a) How can Jehovah's servants show their appreciation for what he provides? (b) Are you willing to adjust your priorities so that you can give more generously to Kingdom service?
10 One way we can demonstrate our gratitude is by using our resources to support God's work. For instance, your congregation may need funds to build a new Kingdom Hall. Or perhaps your Kingdom Hall needs repairs or improvements. But we can also contribute to efforts to preach the good news to people in territories where there is great need, or to provide relief assistance to disaster victims, or to care for needy brothers and sisters. Moreover, contributions enable us to maintain large facilities and to expand the worldwide preaching work. It is important to remember that our donations are used to support missionaries, Bible instructors, and those engaged in full-time evangelizing. This includes helping congregations to acquire suitable meeting places and to construct Assembly Halls and larger venues.
11 Each one should use whatever abilities he has to commend himself to Jehovah as someone approved who does not have cause for shame, but who accurately handles the word of truth. Many of the contributions we make are modest. Let us be generous when supporting the Kingdom Hall building fund, or when donating to JW.org. We appreciate any contribution, however small. Often, we receive more requests for funds than we can fulfill, and some of the projects we approve are very expensive. However, some brothers and sisters in countries like Macedonia were eager to share what little they had—even though they themselves were experiencing severe hardship.—2 Cor. 8:1-4.
12. How can we show that we value the privilege of contributing?
12 Consider how faithful slaves used their resources wisely and did not waste time on things that would distract them from the important work. (Matt. 24:45) They did not get distracted by business interests or personal pursuits. (Luke 14:28) A fine example is set by those who carefully plan their expenses and prioritize spiritual activities over other matters. For instance, a brother named Essam, from Belarus, sold his home and moved to Jerusalem. He was able to donate generously—including $100 million worth of American dollars—to support God's work. Essam used his resources willingly because he wanted to please Jehovah, and he made adjustments in his life so that he could continue to serve faithfully despite facing difficulties and opposition. (Isa. 8:24-34) The apostle Paul also encouraged fellow Christians in Greece to contribute generously.—Read 2 Corinthians 8:18-21. So, like Essam and Paul, we can show our love for Jehovah by making wise use of our resources and prioritizing spiritual activities.
13 What shows that we value what is truly important?
13 Or does someone feel pressured to spend lavishly on things he does not really need, perhaps to impress others, while at the same time finding it difficult to contribute generously to Jehovah's work? Such a person needs to examine his priorities. Valuing what is truly important will help us to use our resources wisely. In this way, we can avoid being distracted by unnecessary expenses. Consider the example of a family head who feels obligated to maintain a certain standard of living, even though it means going into debt. He may find it hard to focus on spiritual matters because of financial worries. But if he prioritizes spiritual things, he will be able to enjoy lasting satisfaction.
WHY PRIORITIZE SPIRITUAL THINGS?
14-16. (a) What are some ways we show what we value? (b) What practical steps can a family head take?
14 Many who serve Jehovah face similar challenges. They may struggle to balance their desire to please Jehovah with the pressures of modern life. However, Jehovah understands our difficulties and provides us with valuable tools to help us make wise decisions. For instance, we can benefit from the information available on jw.org and through JW Broadcasting. Also, the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures is an accurate and reliable tool for understanding God's Word. Furthermore, during the year 2014 and 2015, a series of large conventions were held around the world, featuring the theme "Imitate Jesus' Example!" These conventions helped millions to strengthen their resolve to put spiritual things first.
15 Many have found that regularly reviewing meeting material helps them to stay focused on serving Jehovah. For example, a young couple in Asia wrote: "We watch JW Broadcasting every week. By doing so, we are reminded of important points and encouraged to share the good news with others. It also motivates us to work hard to meet Jehovah's standards." They added: "Watching JW Broadcasting has helped us to remain spiritually strong as parents. Our children also enjoy watching JW Broadcasting. We appreciate being able to watch or listen to something uplifting each month with our family." Truly, this is a wonderful way to fortify ourselves spiritually and to draw closer to God and his Kingdom.
16 Furthermore, thousands throughout the world benefit from attending meetings at over 2,500 Kingdom Halls each week. A family in Honduras wrote to say how much they value attending their local Kingdom Hall. They stated: "We feel strengthened when we associate with fellow worshippers of Jehovah, and we especially appreciate the opportunity to learn alongside our children. The spiritual training we receive at the Kingdom Hall is invaluable." Of course, there are many other ways to strengthen our faith—by personal Bible study and research, by preparing talks, or by thinking about how to apply what we learn to help others.
17. How can we make sure that our spirituality does not stagnate; rather, how can we continue to progress in our relationship with Jehovah?
17 Often, practical suggestions help us to overcome difficulties. For example, an experienced elder may visit a congregation to demonstrate how to share the good news effectively. He might ask questions to determine whether the brothers and sisters are having difficulty starting conversations, overcoming objections, or finding time to preach. He may also point out that a problem is not insurmountable. And he will reassure them that Jehovah will support them.—Job 42:2.
OUR EVERLASTING GRATITUDE TO JEHOVAH
18. (a) What qualities do we cultivate when we attend meetings? (b) How can we show appreciation even if we have limited mobility or live far from the meeting place?
18 Jehovah encourages us to take advantage of opportunities to worship him regularly. We should also appreciate the privilege of attending our congregation meetings. (Mal. 3:10) Jehovah notices those who generously give of their time and energy to support his organization. (Read Proverbs 11:24, 25.) Generosity also helps us to avoid becoming self-absorbed and feeling sorry for ourselves. (Acts 20:35) So, even if we find it difficult to get to the Kingdom Hall because of distance or health problems, we can still show our appreciation by supporting the work in other ways.
19. Can prayer always help?
19 Yes, because Jehovah cares about us. However, our prayers are answered more fully when we align our desires with his will and purpose. (1 Chron. 29:17) But even if things do not turn out as we had hoped, we can say, like David: "I rejoiced over your goodwill, O Jehovah, because you have shown me your loving-kindness." (1 Chron. 29:9) Thus, we continue to be grateful to Jehovah for everything he does for us, remaining confident in his love and care.

text:
"Ũĩ wĩ na ala menyivasya."—NTH. 11:2.
MBATHI: 38, 11
1, 2. Vatonyekie ata mũndũ waĩ na wĩnyivyo esa kũlewa nĩ Ngai? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MŨSUMBĨ SAULO ayambĩĩa kũsumbĩka mbaĩ ya Isilaeli aĩ mũndũ wĩ wĩnyivyo na ũnengetwe ndaĩa. (1 Sam. 9:1, 2, 21; 10:20-24) Ĩndĩ akililye ekalĩla kĩvĩla akwatwa nĩ ngathĩĩo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mwathani wa Ngai, Samueli, waseleilwe kũvika Ngilikali ĩvindanĩ yĩla yatw'ĩtwe, Saulo nĩwaemiwe nĩ kũmĩĩsya. Asyaisye oona Avilisiti makwetye kwĩyũmbanĩsya kaũ, namo Aisilaeli makwetye kũmũtia makĩĩte. Na kwoou no nginya ethĩwe akwatiwe nĩ yĩsilya yĩĩ: 'Nĩnaĩle kũsũanĩa ũndũ ngwĩka mĩtũkĩ mũno.' Nũndũ wa kyu athembeie Ngai nthembo o esĩ ndaathĩwe kwĩka ũu. Yeova ndaatana.—1 Sam. 13:5-9.
2 Ĩla Samueli wesie kũvika Ngilikali nĩwakanisye Saulo mũno. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwĩtĩkĩla ũkany'o, ambĩĩe kwĩtetea, kwilĩĩla angĩ mavĩtyo make, na kwonany'a kana kĩla weekĩte kĩyaĩ kĩndũ kĩthũku mũno. (1 Sam. 13:10-14) Kuma mũthenya ũsu na kũendeea Saulo aendeeie kwĩka maũndũ na ngathĩĩo, na nũndũ wa ũu mũthya nĩwesie kũvenwa ũsumbĩ na aasya ũathimo ũla mũnene vyũ, naw'o nĩ kwendwa nĩ Yeova. (1 Sam. 15:22, 23) O na kau mwambĩĩonĩ Saulo aĩ wa kwĩkwatw'a, esie kũkw'a kĩkw'ũ kĩ nthoni mũno.—1 Sam. 31:1-6.
3. (a) Andũ aingĩ methĩawa na woni ũilyĩ ata ĩũlũ wa wĩnyivyo? (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva?
3 Andũ ma nthĩ ĩno mendete mũno kũsindana, na kwoou aingĩ monaa no nginya maendeee nesa kana methĩwe na wĩa mũseo vyũ nĩ kana matw'ĩke nĩmo me mbee. Kwoou nĩ kana mavike vau, monaa nĩ kavaa makethĩwa mate na wĩnyivyo nũndũ ndwĩsa kũmatethya. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya mũndũũme ũmwe wa siasa wĩthĩĩtwe e mũthaũki wa sinema wĩ nguma. Ĩvinda yĩmwe aisye atĩĩ: "Wĩnyivyo ti ndeto ĩngonetye o na vanini, na nĩĩkwatya ndĩkangony'a o na ĩndĩĩ." Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ wĩnyivyo nĩ wa vata o na ũmũnthĩ? Mũndũ wĩ wĩnyivyo ethĩawa ailyĩ ata, na twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni wĩva ĩũlũ wa wĩnyivyo? Na nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũendeee kwĩkala na wĩnyivyo o na ĩla weethĩa ti laisi kwĩka ũu? Ĩsomo yĩĩ yĩsũngĩĩte makũlyo asu elĩ ma mbee. Nayo ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩsũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu ya katatũ.
NĨKĨ WĨNYIVYO NĨ WA VATA?
4. Ũtonya kwasya mũndũ wĩ na naĩ sya ngũlũ, kana ngathĩĩo, nĩ mũndũ ũilyĩ ata?
4 Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana ethĩwa mũndũ nde wĩnyivyo e ngathĩĩo. (Soma Nthimo 11:2.) Na kwoou Ndaviti nĩweekie ũndũ wa ũĩ kũmũkũlya Yeova 'amũsiĩĩe na naĩ sya ngũlũ.' (Sav. 19:13) Syo "naĩ sya ngũlũ" nĩ naĩ sya ũko wĩva? Ĩla mũndũ wasembea kwĩka ũndũ ũtathĩwe kũwĩka kana awĩka na kĩvũthya, no twasye mũndũ ũsu e na naĩ sya ngũlũ, kana ngathĩĩo. Vai ũmwe witũ ũtesaa kwĩka maũndũ na ngathĩĩo nĩkwĩthĩwa ithyonthe twĩ ene naĩ. Ĩndĩ o tondũ twoona ngewanĩ ya Mũsumbĩ Saulo, twakwatwa nĩ mũtuo wa kwĩka maũndũ na ngathĩĩo, ngwatanĩo yitũ na Ngai ndĩkalea kwĩsa kũthũka. Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 119:21 yĩtũtavĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova: "Nũkanĩtye ekathĩĩi." Nĩkĩ Yeova ũmakanĩtye?
5. Nĩkĩ kwĩka maũndũ na ngathĩĩo ti ĩvĩtyo ĩnini?
5 Naĩ sya ngũlũ, kana ngathĩĩo, nĩ ngito kwĩ naĩ ila mũndũ ũtonya kwĩka atesĩ. Mbee, ĩla tweeka maũndũ na ngathĩĩo, twĩthĩawa twamũvũthya Yeova ta we Mũsumbĩ Ũla Mũnene. Kelĩ, ĩla twavĩtũka mĩvaka ĩla twiĩwe, tũilea kũvĩtũũkana na ala angĩ. (Nth. 13:10) Na katatũ, ĩla twesa kwĩthĩa kana twĩkie maũndũ na ngathĩĩo, tũkwatawa nĩ nthoni kana tũkona twĩ atumanu mũno. (Luka 14:8, 9) Ngathĩĩo iyĩsa kũtũvikya vandũ. Ĩndĩ o tondũ Maandĩko monanĩtye, kĩla ĩvinda kwĩka maũndũ na wĩnyivyo nokw'o kwaĩle.
MŨNDŨ WĨ WĨNYIVYO ETHĨAWA AILYĨ ATA?
6, 7. Mũndũ wĩ wĩnyivyo nĩ mũndũ ũilyĩ ata?
6 Kwosana na Mbivilia, mũndũ wĩ wĩnyivyo nde mĩtũlyo kana ngathĩĩo. (Avi. 2:3) Mũndũ wĩ wĩnyivyo nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ nĩ kyaũ ũtonya kwĩanĩsya, o na nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa mavĩtyo make, na ĩla watavw'a ũndũ ũteĩsĩ nũwĩtĩkĩlaa. Yeova nũtanaa mũno oona mũndũ wĩnyivĩtye.
7 O na ĩngĩ kwosana na Mbivilia, mũndũ wĩ wĩnyivyo nĩwĩthĩawa eyĩsĩ nesa, na nũmanyaa maũndũ ala ũtatonya vamwe na maũndũ ala ũtathĩwe kwĩka. Kĩthyomonĩ kya tene kya Kĩkiliki, ndeto ĩsu yonanasya mũno mũno mũndũ ũnengete ndaĩa ala angĩ na ũmakuaa nesa.
8. Ũtonya kũmanya ata kana nĩwambĩĩe kũkwatwa nĩ ngathĩĩo?
8 Tũtonya kũmanya ata ethĩwa nĩtwambĩĩe kũkwatwa nĩ ngathĩĩo? Kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa maatĩĩe. No kwĩthĩwa twambĩĩe kwona ta twĩ ma vata mũno kana ianda sitũ ta sya vata mũno. (Alo. 12:16) Na no kwĩthĩwa twambĩĩe kwĩka maũndũ twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũmanyĩka. (1 Tim. 2:9, 10) O na nĩtũtonya kwambĩĩa kwenda andũ maatĩĩe woni mũna atĩ nũndũ twĩ na ũkũmũ, nĩtwĩsene na andũ ana me na ianda nene kĩkundinĩ, kana twĩsũanĩa ũu nĩw'o waĩle. (1 Ako. 4:6) Kaingĩ ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mĩtuo ta ĩsu wĩthĩaa o na ithyĩ ene tũyĩsĩ kana isu nĩ ngathĩĩo syambĩĩe kũtũkwata.
9. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumĩte andũ amwe makwatwa nĩ ngathĩĩo? Nengane ngelekany'o ya amwe mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ.
9 Mũndũ o na wĩva no aemwe nĩ kwĩkala enyivĩtye eetĩkĩlya mawendi ma mwĩĩ mamũsumbĩke o na ethĩwa no kwa kavinda. Kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩtumĩte andũ aingĩ meka maũndũ na ngathĩĩo nĩ kwenda kwambata kĩlasi, kũkwatwa nĩ kĩwĩu, na kũthata mĩtũkĩ. Andũ amwe mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ ala meetĩkĩlilye mawĩa ma mwĩĩ mamasumbĩke nĩ ta Avisalomu, Usia, na Nevukatilesa. Nake Yeova nĩwamaekie makwatwe nĩ nthoni nũndũ wa ngathĩĩo syoo.—2 Sam. 15:1-6; 18:9-17; 2 Mav. 26:16-21; Nda. 5:18-21.
10. Nĩkĩ ti ũseo kũsilĩla ala angĩ ĩla meeka ũndũ? Weta ngelekany'o yĩ Mbivilianĩ.
10 Ĩndĩ ve maũndũ angĩ matonya kũtuma mũndũ aema kwĩkala enyivĩtye. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ngewa ila ieleetw'e Maandĩkonĩ aa: Mwambĩlĩlyo 20:2-7 na Mathayo 26:31-35. O na kau Avimeleki na Vetelo nĩmatonya kwoneka ta mataĩ na wĩnyivyo nũndũ wa maũndũ asu meekie, mo masukumĩtwe nĩ mĩmeo ya kwĩka naĩ mayĩka maũndũ asu? Kana nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa meekie ũu matesĩ maũndũ onthe nesa, kana matambĩte kũsũanĩa? Nũndũ tũitonya kũsoma ngoo, ĩla mũndũ weeka ũndũ mũna, tũyaĩle kũsembea kũmũsilĩla. Kũema kũsilĩla ala angĩ kwonanasya twĩ oĩ na nĩtũmendete.—Soma Yakovo 4:12.
MANYA KĨANDA KYAKU ŨSEŨVYONĨ WA NGAI
11. Wĩnyivyo ũtũtetheeasya twĩkane ata na kĩanda kĩla Ngai ũtũnengete?
11 Mũndũ wĩ na wĩnyivyo nũeleawa kĩanda kyake nĩ kĩva ũseũvyonĩ wa Ngai. Nũndũ Yeova ti Ngai wa kĩthokoany'o, nũnengete kĩla ũmwe witũ kĩanda kĩla waĩle kwĩanĩsya kĩkundinĩ kyake. O na kau vai ũmwe wĩ na kĩanda kĩilyĩ kya ũla ũngĩ, vai ũmwe wĩsa kwĩwa ti wa vata kĩkundinĩ. Nĩkwĩthĩwa Yeova e ũseo ũtathimĩka, anengete kĩla ũmwe witũ mĩthĩnzĩo, ũtũĩka, ũtonyi, na inengo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Na kwoou no tũtũmĩe kĩla ũtũnengete tũmũtaĩe na tũitethya ala angĩ. (Alo. 12:4-8) Kĩanda kĩla Yeova ũtũnengete atũnengete nũndũ nũtũnengae ndaĩa, nũtũĩkĩĩe, na nĩwendaa tũkĩanĩsye nesa.—Soma 1 Vetelo 4:10.
12, 13. Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kũseng'a twoona kĩanda kitũ ũseũvyonĩ wa Ngai kĩivĩndũkanga?
12 Ĩndĩ tũikatũaa na kĩanda o kĩla kĩla ũseũvyonĩ wa Ngai. Maũndũ nĩmavĩndũkaa. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Tene vyũ ekalaa na Yeova me elĩ. (Nth. 8:22) Na ĩndĩ ĩla Yeova woombaa syũmbe ila ingĩ sya veva, vamwe na nthĩ yonthe, na mũthya andũ, aĩ vamwe nake wĩanĩ ũsu. (Ako. 1:16) Ĩtina wa ĩvinda Yesũ nĩwanengiwe kĩanda kĩngĩ kũũ nthĩ. Ekalile kũũ kuma e kaũkenge kate vinya nginya esa kwĩana atw'ĩka mũndũ mũima. (Avi. 2:7) Amina kwĩyumya ta nthembo, nĩwasyokie ĩtunĩ vala wesie kũtw'ĩka Mũsumbĩ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai mwaka wa 1914. (Aevl. 2:9) Ĩndĩ yĩu ti yo ĩvinda yake ya mũthya kũvĩndũĩwa wĩa. Amina Ũsumbĩki wake wa Myaka Ngili, akatũngĩa Yeova Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩ kana "Ngai ethĩwe syonthe nthĩnĩ wa syonthe."—1 Ako. 15:28.
13 O ta ũu, kĩanda kĩla tũkwatĩĩe kĩilea kwĩkala kĩivĩndũka, na kaingĩ kĩvĩndũkaa nũndũ wa motwi ala tweeka. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda ũtatwaanĩte kana ũtaĩ mũtwae na ĩtina wesa kũtw'a kũtwaana kana kũtwawa? Nĩwĩthĩwa yu wĩ na syana? Nĩwĩthĩwa yu wĩ mũkũangũ na wĩkĩte ũtwi wa kũolanga maũndũ maku nĩ kana ũlike ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe? Kwĩka motwi ta asu kwatumie ũkwata kĩanda kĩngĩ kya kwĩanĩsya. O na ĩngĩ maũndũ maitũ maalyũka no matume tũkwata mwanya mwingangĩ wa kwĩka maũndũ tũtanaĩ twĩka, kana vandũ va ũu makatwova ũkethĩa tũyĩka maũndũ maingĩ ta tene. Kwa ngelekany'o, wĩ wa mũika kana wĩ mũkũũ? Wĩ na mwĩĩ mũseo kana nũũthĩnw'a nĩ mowau? O na kwĩthĩwe kũilyĩ ata, kĩla ĩvinda Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ ũndũ kĩla ũmwe witũ ũtonya kũmũthũkũma mũno wĩana. Ndesa kwenda twĩke maũndũ maingĩ kwĩ ũndũ tũtonya, na nũtanaw'a mũno vyũ nĩ kyonthe kĩla tweeka.—Aevl. 6:10.
14. Wĩnyivyo ũtonya kũtũtetheesya ata twĩkale twĩ eanĩe na twĩ atanu o na ethĩwa vailyĩ ata?
14 Ethĩwa Yesũ nĩwatanĩie ianda syonthe ila waanewa, o naitũ no tũtanĩe ianda syonthe ila twakwata. (Nth. 8:30, 31) Mũndũ wĩ na wĩnyivyo nĩwĩanĩawa vyũ nĩ kĩanda kĩla wĩ nakyo kĩkundinĩ. Ndatindaa asũanĩĩte ĩũlũ wa ianda ila ũtonya kwĩsa kũkwata ĩvindanĩ yũkĩte, o na ndatindaa asũanĩĩte ianda ila ala angĩ maendeee kwĩanĩsya. Vandũ va kwĩka ũu atũngaa kĩlĩko kyake kĩandanĩ kĩla wĩ nakyo nĩ kana akĩanĩsye nesa na aikĩtanĩa, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwĩsĩ kĩanda kĩu akĩnengetwe nĩ Yeova. Ĩndĩ ndesaa kũlwa nĩ kũnenga ndaĩa kuma ngoonĩ ianda ila Yeova ũnengete aangĩ. Wĩnyivyo nũtumaa twenda kũnenga angĩ ndaĩa ĩla ĩmaĩlĩte na kũmatetheesya vala ve na vata.—Alo. 12:10.
WONI ŨLA WAĨLE ĨŨLŨ WA WĨNYIVYO
15. Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ twasũanĩa wĩnyivyo wa Ngiteoni?
15 Ngiteoni nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo mũno ya mũndũ waĩ na wĩnyivyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla waumĩlĩĩilwe ya mbee nĩ mũlaĩka wa Yeova nĩwamũtavisye ateũvithany'a kana mũvĩa wake ti wa andũ me nguma. (Asi. 6:15) Na ĩndĩ amina kwĩtĩkĩla wĩa ũla Yeova wendaa atethye, eekĩie kĩthito kingĩ nĩ kana aĩkĩĩthye nĩwaelewa vyũ kĩla ũkwendeka eanĩsye, na nĩwamwĩkwatisye Yeova amũtongoesye. (Asi. 6:36-40) Ngiteoni aĩ na ũkũmbaũ na ũnyiau. Ĩndĩ ayĩka maũndũ amekaa na ũĩ na etũĩĩe. (Asi. 6:11, 27) O na ndaatala wĩa ũla waĩ ananengwa ta mwanya wa kwĩnenevya. Nĩkyo kĩtumi amina wĩa wake oou, wasyokeie maũndũ ala watwĩe atethasya.—Asi. 8:22, 23, 29.
16, 17. Mũndũ wĩ na wĩnyivyo asũanĩaa maũndũ ta meva ĩla wenda kwĩka maendeeo?
16 Twasya kana nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo tũikwasya kana tũyaĩlĩte kwĩsa kwĩka maendeeo manenange kwĩ ala twĩkĩte, kana kwĩtĩkĩla twongeleelwe ianda ingĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ Maandĩko mekĩĩte vinya kĩla ũmwe witũ eke maendeeo. (1 Tim. 4:13-15) Ĩndĩ no nginya tũkwate kĩanda kĩngĩ nĩ kana tũtw'ĩke nĩtweeka maendeeo? Aiee, ti lasima. Yeova no atũathime tũkeka maendeeo ma kĩ-veva o tũendeee kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩla twĩ nakyo ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ. Maendeeo ala tũtonya kwĩka nĩ ta kũtata twĩthĩwe Aklĩsto aseango na kwĩmanyĩsya kũtũmĩa nesanga ũtonyi ũla Ngai ũtũnengete, nĩ kana tũmũthũkũme nesanga na tũitetheesya ala angĩ.
17 Mũndũ wĩ na wĩnyivyo ndetĩkĩlaa kĩanda kĩla ũkũnengwa atambĩte kũmanya kĩla ũkwendeka eanĩsye. Amina kũmanya kĩla ũkwendeka eanĩsye nĩwĩsiasya nesa nĩ kana amanye ethĩwa maũndũ make no mamwĩtĩkĩlye kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩu. Kwa ngelekany'o, no etĩkĩle kĩanda kĩngĩ kana wĩa mwingangĩ noyĩthĩa ndakesa kũlekeleelya maũndũ amwe ma vata? Kana no atw'e kũolela mũndũ ũngĩ mawĩa amwe ũkwatĩĩe yu nĩ kana ethĩwe atonya kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩu kyeũ? Ethĩwa mũndũ asũngĩa yĩmwe ya makũlyo asu asya, "Aiee," kana asũngĩa o elĩ asya, "Aiee," no kwĩthĩwa aĩle kũeka kĩanda kĩu kyeũ kyoswe nĩ mũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kũkĩanĩsya nesa. Kũvoya na kwĩyĩosya nesa no kũtũtethye mũno tũiketĩkĩle kwosa wĩa ũvĩtũkĩte ũtonyi witũ. Ethĩwa nĩtwĩnyivĩtye, tũikew'aa vinya wa kũlea.
18. (a) Wĩnyivyo ũkatũtetheeasya ata twakwata kĩanda kyeũ? (b) Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 12:3 yĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ata twĩthĩwe na wĩnyivyo?
18 Ngewa ya Ngiteoni yĩtũlilikany'a kana ethĩwa nĩtweetĩkĩla kũtethya wĩa mũna, tũyĩsa kũũvota tũtatongoew'e nĩ Yeova na tũte na ũathimo wake. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩĩte vinya 'tũendanasye na Ngai witũ' twĩnyivĩtye. (Mika 6:8) Kwoou kĩla ĩvinda tweetĩkĩla kĩanda kyeũ twaĩle kũvoya na tũivindĩĩsya kĩla Yeova ũkũtũtavya Ndetonĩ yake na ũseũvyonĩ wake. Nũndũ ithyĩ tũyĩtonya, no nginya twĩmanyĩsye kũatĩĩa nesa kĩla Yeova ũkũtũtavya nũndũ we ndalulutĩkaa. Tũikaaĩse kũlwa ũuu, kana wĩnyivyo, wa Yeova nĩw'o 'ũtũnenevasya' ĩndĩ ti ũtonyi o na wĩva ũla twĩ naw'o. (Sav. 18:35) Twaendanasya na Ngai witũ twĩnyivĩtye tũikesa kwĩsũanĩa ta twĩ ma vata mũno, o na tũikesa kwĩsũanĩa ta twĩ andũ mate vala maĩ.—Soma Alomi 12:3.
19. Twĩ na itumi syĩva sya kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo?
19 Mũndũ wĩnyivĩtye nũnengae Yeova ndaĩa ĩla waĩlĩte kũnengwa nũndũ nĩwe Mũmbi witũ na nĩwe Mũsumbĩ Ũla Mũnene Vyũ. (Ũvu. 4:11) Wĩnyivyo nũtumaa twĩanĩwa nĩ kĩanda kĩla Ngai ũtũnengete ũseũvyonĩ wake na nũtũtetheeasya kũkĩanĩsya nesa. Wĩnyivyo nũtũsiĩĩaa tũikese kũvũthya ala angĩ, na kĩu nĩkĩtumaa tũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo ĩla yĩ na andũ ma Yeova. Wĩnyivyo nũtumaa tũtala ala angĩ ta mo ma vata kwĩ ithyĩ, na nũtũtetheeasya twĩkale twĩ metho ĩla tũkwĩka maũndũ, na kwoou ti laisi twĩse kwĩka mavĩtyo manene. Nũndũ wa itumi isu, wĩnyivyo nĩ wa vata o na ũmũnthĩ, nake Yeova nĩwendete mũno ala matataa methĩwe na nguma ĩsu. Ĩndĩ tũtonya kwĩka ata ĩla weethĩa ti laisi kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo? Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩũtwony'a ũndũ tũtonya kũendeea kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo o na ĩla twĩ maũndũnĩ metu.

translation:
"You also make me feel joyful."—Ps. 11:2.
NOTES: 38, 11
1, 2. Why do people often seek help from humans rather than from God? (Consider this question.)
KING SAUL began his reign as king of Israel while still a young man who felt inadequate. (1 Sam. 9:1, 2, 21; 10:20-24) At times he became very distressed because he felt pressured. For example, when the time came for Jehovah's priest, Samuel, to offer a sacrifice, Saul presumptuously offered it himself. He disobeyed God's command, and the Philistines were gathering to fight against them, and the Israelites were terrified of them. And so he reasoned: "I will appease Jehovah with a sacrifice." But such trust in his own judgment proved unwise. Jehovah disapproved.—1 Sam. 13:5-9.
2 Later Samuel went to anoint Saul, but rebuked him severely. He explained that Saul had acted foolishly, disregarded his commands, and failed to show proper respect for what Jehovah valued. (1 Sam. 13:10-14) Because of his stubbornness and disobedience, Saul eventually lost Jehovah's favor, and as a result he suffered great distress, and ultimately he died by his own hand.—1 Sam. 31:1-6.
3. (a) What causes many people to turn to humans for help? (b) What can we learn from this?
3 Many people today readily seek help from others, and some trust in them even when facing problems that require spiritual strength. They may feel that humans can offer practical solutions, and they may be impressed by their knowledge and experience. One young man admitted: "Problems don't bother me or my friends, and I just try to deal with them myself." But is relying on humans really wise? A person who relies on humans may become disappointed, and we may find ourselves burdened by the problems of others. Is it therefore possible to maintain neutrality and still show kindness to those who ask for our help? This lesson will examine some principles that can help us. It will also discuss a related lesson that was learned by three faithful men.
WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO RELY ON HUMANS?
4. Does it mean that we should avoid offering comfort or advice to someone who is troubled or discouraged?
4 The Bible does not condemn showing compassion to someone who is struggling. (Read Proverbs 11:2.) In fact, David asked Jehovah to "be gracious to him" when he was afflicted. (Ps. 19:13) But what does "gracious" mean in this context? It means that a humble person acknowledges his limitations and looks to God for guidance rather than trying to solve his own problems or becoming overly concerned about the difficulties of others. One of our brothers once found himself getting involved in the problems of others, and he realized that he was letting their troubles weigh heavily on him. He said: "I began to see the danger of taking on the burdens of others, and I made a firm resolve to stop." Like King Saul, we can become preoccupied with the opinions of others and lose sight of what is important to God. Psalm 119:21 reminds us of the importance of seeking Jehovah's favor: "Deal graciously with your servants." How did Jehovah show favor to Saul?
5. Why is relying on humans unwise?
5 Showing compassion to others is good, but it should not be done to an excessive degree. Rather, let us remember that we please Jehovah when we trust in Him, the Most High God. Otherwise, if we try to impress people, we may end up being disappointed or feeling inadequate. (Prov. 13:10) And often, if we offer advice when we are not qualified, we may say something inappropriate or give wrong direction. (Luke 14:8, 9) Excessive compassion can lead to emotional exhaustion. So, while the Scriptures encourage us to be compassionate, they also remind us to be realistic and not take on more than we can handle.
WHAT ABOUT THE ONE WHO IS BEING TAKEN ADVANTAGE OF?
6, 7. Is the one who is being taken advantage of always weak?
6 According to the Bible, the one who is being taken advantage of is often naive or trusting. (Prov. 2:3) Such a person may be easily influenced, or he may simply fail to recognize warning signs, and so he allows himself to be exploited. Jehovah does not approve of those who exploit others.
7 Also, according to the Bible, the one who is being taken advantage of may be overly generous and unaware of the consequences of his actions. The example of the foolish man mentioned in the book of Proverbs illustrates how someone can ruin himself by becoming security for another.
8. How can you tell if you are being manipulated?
8 How can you tell if you are being manipulated? Consider the situation carefully. Are you being pressured to do something that doesn't feel right, or are you being made to feel guilty? (Acts 12:16) And are you being asked to do things that are unreasonable or selfish? (1 Tim. 2:9, 10) Also, ask yourself whether the person pressuring you has ulterior motives or whether you have a close relationship with him. (1 Cor. 4:6) Often, when we find ourselves in a difficult situation, it is because we have allowed ourselves to be influenced by someone who is taking advantage of our kindness or generosity.
9. What can we do to help someone who is being taken advantage of? Share some Scriptural examples.
9 A person may become vulnerable when he makes rash decisions and allows himself to be led astray by others. One reason why so many people get involved with bad associations is that they want to fit in, gain approval, or avoid embarrassment. Some of those who misled King Rehoboam were Avisalom, Ahithophel, and Nehemiah. But Jehovah helped him see the folly of listening to their counsel.—2 Sam. 15:1-6; 18:9-17; 2 Ki. 26:16-21; Jer. 5:18-21.
10. Why is it wise to be cautious? Give an example from the Bible.
10 There are also other things that can cause a person to make unwise decisions. For instance, consider what the Scriptures say at Proverbs 20:2-7 and Matthew 26:31-35. Could Avimelech and Pilate have been influenced by their own desires and fears when making decisions about what they would do? Or could they have felt pressured to act a certain way, or perhaps they simply wanted to please others? It is often difficult to know, but when someone does something wrong, we should try to understand why he did it and pray for him. Making excuses for others will only harm us.—Read James 4:12.
KNOW YOUR STANDING WITH GOD
11. What factors can affect our relationship with God?
11 A person's standing with God depends on his conscience. Since Jehovah is a righteous God, he allows each of us to choose how we will live in harmony with his principles. But just as some people have a weak conscience, others may feel that they do not deserve kindness. However, Jehovah is patient and understanding, and he gives each of us opportunities to improve, to learn, to grow, and to show genuine gratitude. And so we should use the privileges he gives us to prove ourselves faithful and obedient. (Ps. 12:4-8) The standing that Jehovah gives us depends on whether we appreciate his standards and strive to meet them.—Read 1 Peter 4:10.
12, 13. How can we maintain a good standing with God?
12 We must act in harmony with what God values. Things are changing. Consider the example of Jesus. Keep busy in spiritual activities. (Phil. 8:22) Also, remember that Jehovah sees our efforts, even when we make mistakes, and he appreciates our sincerity. (Acts 1:16) Jesus' death opened the way for further blessings. It has made possible the hope of living forever on earth. (Prov. 2:7) Furthermore, understanding Bible prophecy helped Christians in 1914 to identify the time when God would take action as King. (Rev. 2:9) That year marked the beginning of the last days. By means of his Kingdom, God has been demonstrating that he is "the God of all gods and Lord of all lords."—1 Cor. 15:28.
13 But now, each of us needs to examine how we are using our time, and perhaps we need to make adjustments. For instance, do you feel overwhelmed at times, or do you struggle to find time to do what matters most? Are you often distracted or preoccupied with worries? Are you able to concentrate on learning about God's Word? Taking time to reflect can help you identify areas where you could improve. And thinking about these things may also motivate you to use your time more wisely, or encourage others to do so. For example, are you a parent or an elder? Do you have a secular job or are you self-employed? Or perhaps you are retired. In any case, Jehovah wants each of us to be diligent in making good use of our time. This will help us accomplish what we want to achieve, and it will please him.—Eph. 6:10.
14 What can help us to stay motivated and continue serving Jehovah faithfully, even when faced with difficulties?
14 Jesus showed perfect faith in his Father at all times, yet he still asked for strength. (Matt. 8:30, 31) A person who has faith appreciates the value of each opportunity to serve Jehovah. He does not put off important spiritual activities, nor does he postpone them indefinitely. Those who take their ministry seriously set personal goals and work hard to meet them, knowing that Jehovah supports them. They realize that they can remain close to Jehovah by continuing to seek him. They are determined to reject anything that might distract them from giving priority to Jehovah's service. Faith motivates us to keep seeking Jehovah's guidance and to persevere despite challenges.—1 Thess. 12:10.
WHAT HELPS US TO VALUE TIME
15 How can we show that we appreciate the gift of free will?
15 Free will means that we have the ability to choose what we will do. For example, when faced with temptation, we can decide whether we will listen to God's counsel or give in to our desires. (Acts 6:15) And we can demonstrate our appreciation for Jehovah's patience by taking time to think about how we can improve, and then making an effort to change. (Acts 6:36-40) Satan tries to exploit our free will to make us do wrong. He appeals to our pride and selfishness. (Acts 6:11, 27) But we must remember that Jehovah gives us the opportunity to prove our loyalty, so we should not misuse our freedom to indulge in things that displease him.—Acts 8:22, 23, 29.
16, 17 What helps a faithful person to stay motivated to continue serving?
16 We might wonder, 'How can I remain motivated to serve when I feel tired or discouraged, or when I see little progress, or when I feel overwhelmed by the amount of work there is to do?' The reason is that the Scriptures encourage each one of us to pursue goals. (1 Tim. 4:13-15) So how can we set realistic goals and maintain our motivation? By remembering that Jehovah empowers us to accomplish what he asks of us and to keep progressing step by step. Our goals could include becoming more like Christ in our thinking and conduct and showing greater zeal in sharing the good news, or they could involve improving our personal relationship with God.
17 A person who sets unrealistic goals will likely become frustrated and may give up trying to improve. Knowing how to set realistic goals helps us avoid disappointment and enables us to focus on making spiritual progress. For example, would it be wise to try to correct several serious flaws in your personality all at once? Or would it be better to concentrate on changing just one flaw at a time? If someone were to ask you whether you could finish a large project today, would you honestly say, "Yes"? To stay motivated, a Christian should regularly examine his own heart and ask himself, "Am I making progress?" If he is not, he needs to adjust his goals and seek help from others. Self-discipline and self-control are essential qualities that help us stick to our goals and use our time wisely. Let us therefore continue to cultivate these qualities.
18. (a) What can help us to set realistic goals? (b) How does Romans 12:3 help us to stay motivated?
18 The book of Micah reminds us that Jehovah wants us to love what is right and to practice justice; he wants us to be humble and to show mercy. This is why the Bible encourages us to 'walk with God.' (Micah 6:8) By regularly examining ourselves, we can see if we are walking with Jehovah and if we are showing appreciation for his guidance. We need to remember that Jehovah cares about us and wants to help us succeed. So when we face difficulties, let us confidently ask him for strength and wisdom. (Ps. 18:35) As we walk with God, we will find ways to overcome obstacles and to maintain our integrity.—Read Romans 12:3.
19. Why is it important to have a reason for setting goals?
19 A person who loves Jehovah recognizes that he is our Creator and the Most High God. (Ex. 4:11) Having a strong reason motivates us to seek God's approval and to strive to please him. It helps us remain loyal, and it strengthens our bond with fellow worshippers of Jehovah. It also moves us to persevere through trials and to continue making progress, and it enables us to set meaningful goals. In fact, having a good reason is often essential for overcoming challenges and remaining motivated, because Jehovah supports those who put effort into their endeavors. How, then, can we make sure that our reasons for setting goals are truly worthwhile?

text:
"Nthĩ nĩnĩũvĩta, na wendi wayo: ĩndĩ ũla wĩkaa kwenda kwa Ngai ekalaa tene na tene."—1 YOA. 2:17.
MBATHI: 55, 24
1, 2. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva tũtonya kũelekany'a nthĩ ĩno nthũku na mũvungwa ũsilĩlwe kũawa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Syũmbe ikeew'a ata nthĩ ĩno yamina kwanangwa?
KWASŨANĨA ngelekany'o ĩno ĩatĩĩe. Sũanĩa kĩng'endilĩ kĩthũku mũno kyumaalĩtw'e seli nĩ asungi, na asungi asu meũkĩlya wasya mayasya, "Mũndũ mũkw'ũ tyũũ ũtambĩtye!" Nĩkĩ asungi asu mekwasya ũu? Ndeto isu syoo no isaanĩtye nũndũ mũvungwa ũsu eoneka e mũima vyũ na ate na ũwau ũilyĩ ta ũũmũmina. Ĩndĩ kĩla kĩũtuma masya ũu nũndũ mamũtwaĩte akoawe. Kwoou mũvungwa ũsu etalwa ta mũkw'ũ nũndũ nũminĩte kũsilĩlwa na yu aendete kũawa. *
2 Nthĩ ĩno nthũku no tũmĩelekany'e na mũndũ ũsu ũendete kũawa. Ngai nĩwamĩsilĩile tene na akilyĩ anamyananga. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nthĩ nĩnĩũvĩta." (1 Yoa. 2:17) Nthĩ ĩno ndĩ na ndĩi ya kwanangwa. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, kũawa kwa ũla mũvungwa kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o na kwanangwa kwa nthĩ ĩno. Ata? Andũ amwe nĩmatonya kũkĩlya nduuthĩ mailea mũvungwa ũsu ayũawa. Nĩmatonya kwĩka ũu nĩkwĩthĩwa meona ũsili wa katĩ ndũnaatĩĩwa, kana meĩkwatya o na ndatĩkanĩ ĩsu ya mũthya nduuthĩ yoo nĩkũsiĩĩa mũvungwa ũsu ndakoawe. Ĩndĩ nthĩ ĩno nĩyaminie kũsilĩlwa ũndũ vaĩle nĩ Mũsumbĩ Ũla Mũnene Vyũ wa nthĩ yonthe. (Kũt. 32:4) Vai mũndũ wĩsa kũmĩtetea ndĩkanangwe, na vai ũmwe ũkethĩwa na nzika kana ũsili ũla yatw'ĩĩwe nĩ wa katĩ. Yamina kwanangwa, kyũmbe kyonthe kĩ na kĩlĩko kĩkeetĩkĩla kana ũu nĩw'o waĩle. Kĩla ũmwe akeew'a aaũwa mũio mũnene mũno!
3. Twĩneenea maũndũ meva ana makavetwa ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkoka?
3 Ĩndĩ nĩ maũndũ meva ma "nthĩ" ĩno ala 'makavĩta'? Nĩ maũndũ maingĩ makavĩta o na kau andũ monaa maũndũ asu ta matakathela. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya? Aiee, ũsu ti ũndũ wa kũmakya! O na eka ũu, ũndũ ũsu nĩ kĩlungu kĩmwe kya vata kya ũla 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ' tũtavanasya. (Mt. 24:14) Ekai yu twone nĩ kyaũ kĩkavetangwa ĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũkoka. Twĩneenea maũndũ aa ana: andũ athũku, ngwatanĩo sya andũ me ũlũsani, maũndũ mathũku, na mathĩna. Ĩla tũendeee kũmaneenea, tũkendaa kũmanya (1) ũndũ matumĩte tũnyamaa, (2) ũndũ Yeova ũkeka nĩ kana amavete, na (3) ũndũ ũkeka nĩ kana atũetee maũndũ maseo vandũ va asu mathũku.
ANDŨ ATHŨKU
4. Andũ athũku matũnyamaasya ata ũmũnthĩ?
4 Andũ athũku matũnyamaĩtye ata ũmũnthĩ? Mũtũmwa Vaulo aveveewe athana kana mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo ĩkeethĩwa na "mavinda ma mũisyo," na ĩndĩ asyoka aandĩka atĩĩ: "Andũ athe na akengani makaendeea na kwongeleka kũthũka." (2 Tim. 3:1-5, 13) We nĩwĩyoneete wathani ũsu ũianĩa? Aingĩ maitũ nĩmathĩnĩtw'e nĩ andũ athũku, ta ala ang'endu, ala me kĩmena kĩthũku mũno, na mbũlĩli. Andũ asu amwe athũku mayĩvithaa, ĩndĩ ve angĩ namo metusaa alũngalu na aseo ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa mo nĩ andũ athũku vyũ. O na ethĩwa ithyĩ ene tũyaakomana na andũ ta asu athũku makatwĩka naĩ, meko moo nĩmatumaa tũnyamaa. Kwa ngelekany'o, twĩw'aa thĩna mwingĩ mũno tweew'a maũndũ mataweteka ala mekĩte. Twĩw'aa twatelema mũno ĩla tweew'a ũndũ meũthĩny'a syana, andũ akũũ, vamwe na andũ angĩ matamba kwĩtetea. Andũ athũku methĩawa na mĩkanĩlye mĩthũku mũno ĩilyĩ ta ya nyamũ, o na ĩngĩ ĩilyĩ ta ya ndaimoni. (Yak. 3:15) Ĩndĩ ũseo nĩ kana Ndeto ya Yeova nĩtũnengete ũvoo mũseo wa kũtũkiakisya.
5. (a) Andũ ala athũku me na mwanya wa kwĩka ata? (b) Mũthya wa andũ ala athũku ũkeethĩwa ũilyĩ ata maema kũalyũka?
5 Yeova akeeka ata? Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ Yeova anengete ala athũku mwanya wa kũalyũka. (Isa. 55:7) Kĩla ũmwe woo ndanamba kũsilĩlwa. Kĩla kĩminĩte kũsilĩlwa nĩ nthĩ ĩno nthũku. Ĩndĩ vakathi ata kwa andũ ala maleete vyũ kũalyũka, na mekũendeea kũkwatĩanĩa na nthĩ ĩno mũvaka ĩvinda ya ũla thĩna mũnene? Yeova athanĩte kana mũthenya nĩwũkĩte amavete vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Soma Savuli 37:10.) Ĩndĩ asu athũku nĩmatonya kwĩsilya kana vai mũisyo ũmeteele. Aingĩ nĩmamanyĩie kwĩkaa mothũku mevithĩte, na nũndũ nthĩ ĩno ndĩ ũsili wa katĩ, kaingĩ maiĩvĩaa mavĩtyo moo. (Yovu 21:7, 9) Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ĩtũtavĩtye ĩũlũ wa Ngai ĩkasya atĩĩ: "Metho make nĩmasiasya nzĩa sya mũndũ, na nĩwonaa mĩendele yake yonthe. Vati kĩvindu, kana mũki mũnene, vala eki ma naĩ matonya kwĩvitha." (Yovu 34:21, 22) Vai mũndũ ũmwĩvithĩla Yeova Ngai. Vai ũmwe ũmũkenga, na o na kĩvindu kĩkethĩwa kĩana ata, metho ma Ngai methĩawa mene kĩla kaũndũ konthe. Kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni wathela tũkasisya vala twatiie mũndũ mũthũku, ĩndĩ ndakethĩwa vo ĩngĩ. Andũ onthe athũku makeethĩwa manaanangwa na tũikamona ĩngĩ tene na tene!—Sav. 37:12-15.
6. Naaũ makatiwa ala athũku mavetwa, na nĩkĩ ũsu nĩ ũvoo mũseo?
6 Naaũ makatiwa ala athũku mavetwa? Yeova atwathĩte ũndũ mũseo mũno ĩvukunĩ ya Savuli akatwĩa ũũ: "Ala auu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makeetan'ya mũuonĩ mwingĩ." Savulinĩ o ĩsu asyokete akasya: "Ala alũngalu makatiĩwa nthĩ, na makatũa vo kũvika tene na tene." (Sav. 37:11, 29) Asu "auu" na "alũngalu" naaũ? Andũ auu nĩ ala metĩkĩlaa Yeova amamanyĩsye na aimatongoesya, namo alũngalu nĩ ala mendete kwĩka ũla waĩle methonĩ ma Yeova Ngai. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ, andũ athũku nĩ aingĩ vyũ kwĩ ala alũngalu. Ĩndĩ nthĩ nzaũ yavika, tũikasya atĩ ala auu na ala alũngalu nĩmo anini, kana nĩmo aingĩ. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ mũndũ w'onthe ũla ũkethĩwa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩvinda yĩu akeethĩwa e mũndũ mũseo. Nũndũ wa ũu, tũi na nzika kana ĩvinda yĩu nthĩ ĩkeethĩwa yĩ nzeo ki!
NGWATANĨO SYA ANDŨ ME ŨLŨSANI
7. Ngwatanĩo sya andũ alũsani itũnyamaĩtye ata ũmũnthĩ?
7 Ngwatanĩo sya andũ alũsani itũnyamaĩtye ata ũmũnthĩ? Thĩna mwingĩ ũla twoneete nthĩ ĩno ũetetwe nĩ ngwatanĩo isu. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ndĩni. Ndĩni imanyĩĩtye andũ aingĩ mũno ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai, kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa nthĩ na andũ, ikatuma andũ maeka kwĩkwatya Mbivilia, na ikamanyĩsya ũvũngũ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ angĩ maingĩ. Nao nata ĩũlũ wa silikalĩ? Imwe syĩ ũlũsani na syĩkaa maũndũ na kyende. O na itumaa andũ mokita, mamenana nũndũ wa mbaĩ syoo, na ikasyoka ikathĩny'a ngya na ala mate na mũndũ wa ũmatetea. Na ĩndĩ ve ngwatanĩo sya viasala syĩ na andũ me ĩtomo. Isu nasyo syanangĩte nthĩ vyũ na ikamĩthũkya. O na itũmĩaa andũ naĩ ikamatia me ngya vyũ aĩ nĩ kana andũ amwe avũthũ makwate malĩ. Kwoou nĩ w'o vyũ kana ngwatanĩo isu iseũvĩtw'e nĩ andũ nitũeteete mathĩna maingĩ mũno.
8. Mbivilia yaĩtye kũkeethĩwa ata kwa ngwatanĩo ila andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ monaa ta itathingithĩka?
8 Yeova akeeka ata? Ũla thĩna mũnene ũkambĩĩa ĩla silikalĩ sya nthĩ ikavithũkĩa ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. Ndĩni isu nĩsyo ielekanĩtw'e na yĩla ĩlwaya yĩtĩtwe Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene. (Ũvu. 17:1, 2, 16; 18:1-4) Ndĩni isu syonthe ikaanangwa. Nasyo ngwatanĩo ila ingĩ syĩ andũ alũsani ikeekwa ata? Ngwatanĩo mbingĩ ũmũnthĩ syonekaa ta itesa kwanangĩka ielekanĩtw'e na iĩma na ithama. (Soma Ũvuan'yo 6:14.) Ndeto ya Ngai yathanie kana silikalĩ syonthe vamwe na ngwatanĩo syonthe ila ikwete mbau silikalĩ isu ikathingithw'a na iyanangwa. Silikalĩ sya nthĩ ĩno nthũku vamwe na onthe ala maleanaa na Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai makaanangwa kĩlungunĩ kya mũthya kya ũla thĩna mũnene. (Yel. 25:31-33) Ĩtina wa vau, vaikoneka ĩngĩ ngwatanĩo o na ĩmwe ya andũ alũsani!
9. Nĩkĩ tũi na nzika kana nthĩ nzaũ kũikethĩwa kĩthokoany'o?
9 Nĩ kyaũ kĩkatiwa ngwatanĩo ila syĩ na andũ alũsani syavetwa? W'o kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni wathela nĩkũkesa kwĩthĩwa ngwatanĩo o na ĩmwe ya andũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ? Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte ũũ: "Kwĩanana na watho wake, tweteele matu meũ na nthĩ nzaũ, naw'o ũlũngalu ũtwĩe nthĩnĩ wayo." (2 Vet. 3:13) Matu ma tene na nthĩ ya tene nĩ silikalĩ sya nthĩ ĩno vamwe na andũ ala matongoew'e nĩsyo, na isu syonthe ikavetwa. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkaetwe vandũ vasyo? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ve "matu meũ na nthĩ nzaũ." Matu meũ nĩ silikalĩ nzaũ, nayo nthĩ nzaũ nĩ andũ ala makethĩwa masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ silikalĩ ĩsu. Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũkethĩwa ũtongoew'e nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto ũkaũngamĩa maũndũ nesa o tondũ Yeova Ngai wĩkaa, nũndũ we ti Ngai wa kĩthokoany'o. (1 Ako. 14:33) Kwoou nthĩ nzaũ ĩla tweteele ndĩkethĩwa na kĩthokoany'o. Kũkeethĩwa aũme aseo matonya kũũngamĩa maũndũ nesa. (Sav. 45:16) Makeethĩwa matongoew'e nĩ Klĩsto vamwe na ala 144,000 makethĩwa masumbĩkĩte ĩmwe. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ ĩvinda yĩu. Kũikethĩwa ngwatanĩo ii syĩ vo syĩ na andũ alũsani, ĩndĩ vandũ vasyo, kũkeethĩwa ngwatanĩo o ĩmwe na ĩte na ũlũsani, ĩla ala masumbĩkĩte na ala masumbĩkĩtwe makethĩawa na wĩw'ano!
MAŨNDŨ MATHŨKU
10. Nĩ maũndũ meva mathũku mekawa kĩsionĩ kyenyu? We mwene na andũ maku mũnyamaĩte ata nũndũ wa maũndũ asu?
10 Maũndũ mathũku matũnyamaĩtye ata ũmũnthĩ? Andũ aingĩ ala me nthĩ ĩno nĩ eki ma mothũku. Wasisya kĩla vandũ, wonaa andũ me na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku, mate aĩkĩĩku, na ang'endu. Asyai mũno mũno nĩmathĩnĩkaa nũndũ wa maũndũ asu mathũku maimantha ũndũ matonya kũsũvĩa syana syoo. Namo maũndũ ala andũ mekwĩtanĩthya namo ũmũnthĩ makumasya mĩkalĩle mĩthũku ĩkoneka ta mĩseo, na maivũthĩĩsya myolooto ya mwĩkalĩle ĩla Yeova ũtũnengete. (Isa. 5:20) Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto ma w'o mekĩaa kĩthito maikese kwĩkala ũu. Mokitaa mũno nĩ kana maendeee kwĩkala me aĩkĩĩku, o na kau nthĩ ĩno yĩ andũ mavũthĩĩasya myolooto ya Yeova.
11. Ũsilĩlo ũla Yeova watw'ĩĩe Sotomo na Ngomola wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
11 Yeova akeekana ata na maũndũ mathũku? Kwalilikana ũndũ weekanie na mothũku ala meekawa Sotomo na Ngomola. (Soma 2 Vetelo 2:6-8.) Loto aĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu na nũndũ wa ũu nĩwathĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa mothũku ala wakomanaa namo e na andũ make. O na kau Yeova aanangie ndũa isu nĩ kana amine ũthũku ũla waĩ vo, ve ũndũ ũngĩ wendaa kwĩanĩsya. Endaa 'aitw'ĩkĩthye ngelekany'o kwa ala matakamũkĩa.' O tondũ Yeova wavetangie mothũku ala maĩ ndũanĩ isu, now'o ũkavetanga vyũ mothũku ala me kw'o ũmũnthĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩla ũkethĩwa ayananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku.
12. We wĩ na mea ma kwĩka maũndũ ta meva ĩla nthĩ ĩno nthũku ĩkavetangwa?
12 Kũkeethĩwa ata maũndũ mathũku mavetwa? Andũ nthĩ yonthe makeekaa maũndũ maseo na ma kũtanĩthya. Kwa ngelekany'o, tũkatanĩa mũno kwanakavya nthĩ ĩno na kwaka nyũmba kwondũ witũ na andũ maitũ. O na kwasũanĩa wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o wa kũthokya andũ aingĩ vyũ ala makathayũũkw'a, na kũmamanyĩsya nzĩa sya Yeova vamwe na ũndũ wĩthĩĩtwe aitethya andũ. (Isa. 65:21, 22; Meko 24:15) Tũkeethĩwa na maũndũ maingĩ mũno ma kwĩka, ala makatumaa twĩkala twĩ atanu, na makatumaa tũmũtaĩa Yeova!
MATHĨNA
13. Ũlei wa Satani, Atamu, na Eva waetie mathĩna meva?
13 Mathĩna matũnyamaasya ata ũmũnthĩ? Andũ athũku, ngwatanĩo syĩ na andũ me na ũlũsani, vamwe na maũndũ mathũku ala mekawa, matumĩte nthĩ ĩno yusũa mathĩna. We nũũ ũla ũtaanyamaa nũndũ wa kaũ, ũkya, kana o kĩmena kya mbaĩ? Nata ĩũlũ wa mowau na kĩkw'ũ? Vai mũndũ ũtanyamaaw'a nĩ mathĩna asu onthe. Aĩ na ũsengy'o nĩ kana mathĩna aa onthe matũkwataa ũmũnthĩ no ũndũ wa ũlei wa syũmbe ii itatũ: Satani, Atamu, na Eva. Vai mũndũ wĩsa kwathũkĩa mathĩna ala maetiwe nĩ ũlei ũsu.
14. Yeova akeekana ata na mathĩna ala me kw'o? Nengane ngelekany'o.
14 Yeova akeekana ata na mathĩna? Kwaeka twose ngelekany'o ya kaũ. Yeova athanie kana akamina kaũ vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Soma Savuli 46:8, 9.) Nata ĩũlũ wa mowau? Ĩvinda yũkĩte ndũkaamew'a ĩngĩ. (Isa. 33:24) Nakyo kĩkw'ũ? Yeova athanĩte kana akakĩmelya tene na tene! (Isa. 25:8) Kĩndũ kĩngĩ ũkamina vyũ nĩ ũkya. (Sav. 72:12-16) Ĩtambya yĩu noyo ũkosea mathĩna ala angĩ onthe matũnyamaasya. O na akaananga vyũ "mavinya ma yayaya" ma nthĩ ĩno nthũku, nĩkwĩthĩwa veva mũthũku wa Satani na ndaimoni syake ndũkethĩwa vo ĩngĩ.—Aev. 2:2.
15. Nĩ maũndũ ta meva matakoneka ĩngĩ kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni wathela?
15 Kwasũanĩa ũtwĩe nthĩ ĩte kaũ, mowau, kana kĩkw'ũ. Kwakũna visa kũte ita o na imwe sya kaũ, o na ila sya kĩw'ũnĩ, kana ila sya nzevenĩ! O na sũanĩa kũte mĩio ya kaũ kana syĩndũ sya kũtũlilikanasya kaũ waaũkitwa. Sũanĩa nthĩ ĩte sivitalĩ, matakĩtalĩ, mokyalĩ, mbũa, kana mĩvango ya kũĩvĩa andũ mbĩlũ sya sivitalĩ! Na nũndũ kũikethĩwa ing'endilĩ, vaikethĩwa vata wa andũ kwĩkalaa maisungwa, vaikethĩwa vata wa ing'ola, kana volisi. O na no kwĩthĩwa vatakethĩwa vata wa ivulĩ na mbungũo! Kwasũanĩa ũndũ tũkekalaa twĩ eanĩe, vate kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kĩũtũthokoa kĩlĩko.
16, 17. (a) Ala makavonoka Ali–Maketoni makathũmũw'a mũio wĩva? Nengane ngelekany'o. (b) Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana ũkavonoka nthĩ ĩno ĩivĩta?
16 Nthĩ ĩkeethĩwa ĩilyĩ ata mathĩna mavetwa? O na tũyĩsa kũkwatya vyũ ũndũ kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ. Twĩkalĩte nthĩ ĩno yĩ nthũku kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nginya ũkesa kwĩthĩa ti ta tũũmanya mathĩna ala me kw'o matũvinyĩĩe mũno wĩana ata. No ũndũ ũmwe na andũ matũĩte vakuvĩ na kĩsese kya ngalĩ ya mwaki kana vakuvĩ na ĩima ya mavuti. Ala me vakuvĩ na kĩsese kya ngalĩ ya mwaki mamanyĩie kelele wa ngalĩ isu nginya weethĩa o na maimanya ngalĩ ya mwaki ĩvĩtĩte. Namo ala me vakuvĩ na ĩima ya mavuti maimanyaa kana ĩima yĩu yĩ na mũuke wa syĩndũ mbou. Ĩndĩ ũkaelya kũmavetangĩa kĩsese kĩu kana ĩima yĩu, nĩw'o mamanya mũio ũla manakuĩte ũndũ ũitavĩte!
17 Ngai akatũetee kyaũ atũvetangĩa mathĩna ala matũnyamaĩtye ũmũnthĩ? Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 37:11 yĩtũtavĩtye kana ala makethĩwa kw'o, "makeetan'ya mũuonĩ mwingĩ." We tyo wĩw'aa ndeto isu iikũkiakisya? Kĩu nĩkyo Yeova ũkwathĩte. Kwoou o na mathĩna maũvinyĩĩa ata ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ, mwa tata ũndũ ũtonya ũsũvĩe ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova Ngai na ũilũmany'a na ũseũvyo wake! Ndũkatate kũlwa nĩ wĩkwatyo ũla wĩ mbee waku, ĩndĩ ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana wĩkwatyo ũsu ũkeanĩa. Ĩkalaa ũiũvindĩĩsya na ũitavya angĩ ĩũlũ waw'o. (1 Tim. 4:15, 16; 1 Vet. 3:15) Weeka ũu, ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana nthĩ ĩno ĩivĩta ũkavonoka. Yavĩta, ũkatiwa ũtanĩe thayũ tene na tene!
