translation:
"This is what is eternal, and life everlasting: to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent." – 1 JOHN 17:3.
PARAGRAPH: 55, 24
1, 2. (a) Why do we find it so difficult to make spiritual progress and remain steadfast? (Consider practical examples.) (b) What benefits will result from making spiritual progress?
LET US CONSIDER this illustration. Imagine a man who has been imprisoned for years. The prisoners often pass the time by shouting, "If I were free!" But does that prisoner actually become free? No, his situation does not improve at all, and he remains in prison. Similarly, dwelling on regrets over past mistakes will not undo them. Instead, such thinking can rob you of joy and prevent you from moving forward. Every time you dwell on those mistakes, you feel worse. So why allow yourself to be tormented by something you cannot change? *
2 This important truth applies also to our relationship with God. God has shown us great love and forgiveness. The Bible says: "This is what is eternal." (1 John 2:17) This truth has real value. For us, continuing to seek forgiveness for sins is closely linked to appreciating this truth. Otherwise, some might feel unworthy because of their past sins. They might think they need to earn back God's favor, or they might fear that their past sins will always haunt them. However, this truth assures us that our sins can be completely forgiven through faith in Jesus Christ. (Ps. 32:4) A person may struggle with feelings of guilt, and another may be troubled by circumstances beyond his control. Yet, they can experience relief, knowing that there is hope regardless of their situation. Everyone deserves this peace of mind!
3. How can we strengthen our faith in Jehovah's promises?
3 What does this "truth" refer to, and why are "faithful" ones mentioned? There are many faithful people who have faced difficult trials. Is this something to expect? No, this is not something to expect! But still, this is one aspect of the sign of "the end of the system of things" that we should recognize. (Matt. 24:14) Let us see how this is being fulfilled in connection with Jehovah's Kingdom. We can identify these features: distressing times, conflicts between nations, famines, and earthquakes. As we continue to pay attention, we will come to understand (1) why we must remain humble, (2) what Jehovah expects of us, and (3) what he expects us to do to help others facing difficulties.
DISTRESSING TIMES
4. Why are distressing times affecting so many people?
4 Are distressing times affecting anyone at all? The apostle Paul foretold that in the last days, Christians would be surrounded by "critical times," and he wrote: "Wicked men and impostors will advance from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived." (2 Tim. 3:1-5, 13) How true that is today! Many people feel insecure, fearful, and distrustful. Some wicked people are brazen, while others are subtle and deceptive. However, we should not associate with wicked people, because their wickedness can influence us. For example, we often hear about terrible events that cause us distress. We often find ourselves feeling sorry for those who suffer, including young people, some of whom are misled and influenced by bad associations. But even when we try to avoid them, we may be affected by their wickedness. This can make it more difficult for us to remain humble. Furthermore, wicked people are often motivated by selfish desires and demons. (Jas. 3:15) So let us strengthen our determination to live up to the standard set by Jehovah's Organization.
5. (a) Who are among those who are causing trouble? (b) What is the outcome for those who give in to wickedness?
5 Does Jehovah care? Let us see how Jehovah views those who cause trouble. (Isa. 55:7) Everyone deserves to be forgiven. Every mistake deserves forgiveness because it is human. But what about those who repeatedly cause trouble, and continue to practice wickedness despite knowing the serious consequences? Jehovah is patient, but there is a limit to his patience. (Read Psalm 37:10.) Some wicked people prosper, seemingly getting away with their wrongdoing. Many become arrogant and boastful, and they do not realize that they are only living for a short time. (Job 21:7, 9) The Bible reveals God's purpose as follows: "My eyes have seen everything mankind does, and I watch over all their activities. There is no wisdom, no insight, no trickery that can succeed against Jehovah." (Job 34:21, 22) Someone may try to deceive Jehovah God. Another may deny him, and even if things seem to go well for them temporarily, God's eyes observe everything thoroughly. The case of Ali–MacIntyre shows us that we should not imitate a wicked person, because he suffered greatly. All such wicked people will be brought to ruin, more and more!—Ps. 37:12-15.
6 Are the righteous troubled, and if so, why?
6 Are the righteous troubled? Jehovah has assured us of this truth through the words of Psalm 37, which says: "Those who are upright will reside forever, and their hope will be abundant." Psalm 37 also states: "The righteous will inherit the earth, and they will find exquisite delight." (Ps. 37:11, 29) What do "upright" and "righteous" mean? Upright people are those who love Jehovah and obey him, while righteous people are those who reject the ways of the world and live according to Jehovah God's standards. It is true that many righteous people experience difficulties like those of the unrighteous. But why is this so? Because everyone experiences the effects of imperfect humanity and the troubles that come with it. For this reason, we should not lose heart when trials come our way!
EXAMPLES OF PEOPLE IN THE WORLD
7 Do examples of people in the world ever encourage us?
7 Do examples of people in the world ever encourage us? Often, much of what we see is discouraging because of the examples around us. Consider the influence of bad association. Bad associations can lead many people away from Jehovah, causing them to disregard his law and his people, leading them to neglect the Bible, and making them unaware of many important things. And what about the influence of schools? They often promote worldly values and lifestyles, leading people to become materialistic, selfish, and disrespectful. Also, there are examples of crime and violence among people. We too may be affected by these things and become discouraged. But they can also motivate people to do good, even if some people make mistakes along the way. So it is good to have such examples, even though these examples sometimes cause more harm than good.
8 Does the Bible give encouragement, but do many people still get discouraged despite its reliability?
8 Does Jehovah allow this? The reason why so much wickedness exists in the world is because Satan has been given power. This is the same great dragon that was thrown down from heaven and is referred to as Babylon the Great. (Rev. 17:1, 2, 16; 18:1-4) This system of things is condemned. So will other governments also be allowed to exist? Many governments today seem unable to solve problems and are corrupt. (Read Revelation 6:14.) God's purpose is to eliminate all wickedness and all governments except for the Kingdom government which will not be destroyed. The world's religions, together with all other forms of false worship, will be destroyed along with wicked people who oppose God's sovereignty. (Jer. 25:31-33) Therefore, take warning, you rulers and people of the world!
9 Should we therefore be selective about whom we associate with?
9 Is it wise to associate with those who are disloyal and unfaithful? Was the example of Allie-MacIntyre helpful in showing how dangerous it can be to associate with disloyal people? The Bible urges us: "Associate with those who have a reputation for righteousness, and become companions of those zealous for goodness." (2 Tim. 3:13) Those who are righteous and faithful are like a spiritual family, and we should associate with them. Why should we be careful about our associations? The Bible warns against "companionship" that is bad. Our companions influence us, and bad associates can lead us astray spiritually. This sovereignty is exercised by Jesus Christ, who carries out Jehovah God's will, though he himself is not God Almighty. (1 Cor. 14:33) Choose loyal friends who will help us to remain faithful. Being surrounded by such fine examples will strengthen our resolve. (Ps. 45:16) Be careful about associating with those who are disloyal—those who are part of the 144,000 who are faithful—and with others who are imperfect but striving to be faithful, so that you may not be influenced by their imperfections!
IMPORTANT POINTS
10 Are there things that make you feel uncomfortable? Do you sometimes find yourself disturbed by certain practices?
10 Do some things bother your conscience? Many people today disregard what is right and wrong. They mock those who try to live by moral standards, and they ridicule those who speak out against wrongdoing. But we must not allow ourselves to become accustomed to wickedness, lest we lose our sensitivity to what is right and wrong. Also, we must not imitate those who promote immoral behavior, because this would offend Jehovah. (Isa. 5:20) Christians must avoid being influenced by those who reject Bible principles. Otherwise, they may gradually lower their own standards and begin to tolerate what Jehovah disapproves.
11 How does Jehovah view Sodom and Gomorrah?
11 Does Jehovah condone wicked practices? Consider what happened to Sodom and Gomorrah. (Read 2 Peter 2:6-8.) It is clear that anyone who engages in such practices deeply offends Jehovah. However, Jehovah is patient, and he gives people time to repent. He wants "the righteous ones to escape." Therefore, Jehovah destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, but he rescued Lot and his family.
12 What can you do to protect yourself from harmful influences?
12 Are there ever justifiable reasons for engaging in wicked practices? People everywhere are influenced by wrong ideas and bad associations. For example, we may be tempted to associate with those who engage in harmful activities or to spend too much time with our neighbors. But remember that associating with bad company can lead us astray, and that sharing Bible truths with others can save lives. (Isa. 65:21, 22; Matt. 24:15) We are grateful for the many blessings we enjoy, which help us remain faithful and strengthen our love for Jehovah!
HEADINGS
13 What mistakes did Satan, Adam, and Eve make?
13 Did humans originate wickedness? Wicked people, along with imperfect humans and spirit creatures, have contributed to human suffering. Would you deliberately choose to lie, steal, or commit adultery? Would you practice idolatry or witchcraft? Anyone who does so is following the example set by three originators of wickedness: Satan, Adam, and Eve. Avoid imitating those who made those serious mistakes.
14 Does Jehovah allow wickedness to exist? Let us examine this closely.
14 Does Jehovah allow wickedness? Let us consider some important points. Jehovah does not cause or approve of wickedness. (Read Psalm 46:8, 9.) Why does he permit it? Because he allows humans free will. (Isa. 33:24) But what about injustice? Jehovah will correct matters eventually! (Isa. 25:8) He will also bring relief to those who are oppressed. (Ps. 72:12-16) Continue to trust in Jehovah and avoid getting involved in any form of wickedness. Also, beware of "the deceptive practices" of this world, which are promoted by Satan and his demons.—Rev. 2:2.
15 What further questions might arise regarding the case of Allis-Mackenzie?
15 Perhaps you wonder why such things happen, or what the reason is. It may involve obtaining visas to travel abroad, or perhaps it involves illegal immigration, or even human trafficking! And you may be tempted to get involved in fraudulent schemes or activities that exploit others. Avoid questionable business dealings, false advertising, extortion, bribery, or exploiting vulnerable people! And do not become involved in smuggling, whether it involves transporting drugs, weapons, or counterfeit goods. Be careful not to associate with criminals, because they often lead to trouble.
16, 17. (a) What motivated Allis-Mackenzie's accomplices? Let us examine this closely. (b) How can you protect yourself from being influenced by wicked individuals or situations?
16 Is it right to benefit from another's wrongdoing? We should always strive to avoid profiting from dishonest practices. Let us remember that some people may appear successful while secretly engaging in unethical conduct. Some may prosper through fraud or deceit. But those who profit from dishonesty will eventually face consequences. Others may succeed through hard work and diligence. They earn an honest living and maintain integrity. Therefore, do not envy those who engage in dishonest practices or take advantage of others; instead, focus on maintaining your own moral standards!
17 Will God allow the wicked to continue prospering indefinitely? Psalm 37:11 assures us that "the meek will possess the earth." So why worry about the success of the wicked? Jehovah allows it. However, even their apparent prosperity is temporary. Instead, concentrate on strengthening your relationship with Jehovah God and adhering to his principles! Do not be discouraged by the successes of others, whether they flaunt their wealth or subtly boast. Remain occupied with spiritual activities and let your good works speak for themselves. (1 Tim. 4:15, 16; 1 Pet. 3:15) By doing so, you will find contentment and avoid being consumed by envy. Remember, continued meditation on this matter will help you remain steadfast!

text:
"Ĩndĩ we, Isilaeli, mũthũkũmi wakwa, Yakovo ũla nĩnyuvĩte, ũsyao wa mũnyanyawa Avalaamu."—ISA. 41:8.
MBATHI: 51, 22
1, 2. (a) Twĩsĩ ata kana no vatonyeke mũndũ akatw'ĩka mũnyanyae wa Ngai? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
KUMA twĩ tũũkenge nginya tũkakw'e, kĩndũ kĩla twĩthĩawa na vata mũno nakyo nĩ kwendwa. Andũ onthe nĩmethĩawa na vata mũnene wa kwendwa. Nĩtwĩthĩawa na mea ma kũtuma ndũũ na kwĩthĩwa twĩsene na angĩ. Ĩndĩ ve ũla twĩ na vata mũnene vyũ wa kwendwa nĩwe, nake nĩ Yeova. Andũ aingĩ monaa mũndũ atatonya kũtw'ĩka mũnyanyae wa Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe, nũndũ we nĩ veva na ekalaa ĩtunĩ. Ithyĩ nĩtwĩthĩawa na nzika ta isu? Aiee, ithyĩ tũyĩthĩawa na nzika!
2 Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana ve andũ maĩ anyanyae ma Ngai. Kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa andũ asu no kũtũtetheesye mũno, nũndũ vai kĩndũ kya vata thayũnĩ ta kwĩthĩwa anyanyae ma Ngai. Mũndũ ũmwe ũla waĩ mũnyanyae mũnene wa Ngai eetawa Avalaamu. (Soma Yakovo 2:23.) We Avalaamu atw'ĩkie mũnyanyae wa Yeova ata? Kĩndũ kĩmwe kya vata vyũ kĩla kyatumie matuma ndũũ nĩ mũĩkĩĩo ũla Avalaamu waĩ naw'o. O na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩmwĩtaa Avalaamu "ĩthe wa onthe ala metĩkĩlaa [kana, methĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo]." (Alo. 4:11) Kwoou ekai yu tũneenee ũndũ mũĩkĩĩo wa Avalaamu watumie ethĩwa mũnyanyae wa Ngai. Tũineenea ũndũ ũsu, kĩla ũmwe witũ no ekũlye atĩĩ, 'Ndonya kwĩka ata nĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Avalaamu nĩ kana nĩlũlũmĩlye ũnyanya wakwa vamwe na Yeova?'
AVALAAMU ATW'ĨKIE MŨNYANYAE WA YEOVA ATA?
3, 4. (a) Nĩ ĩndĩĩ mũĩkĩĩo wa Avalaamu ũtonya kwĩthĩwa waatatwa kwĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva? Elesya. (b) Nĩkĩ Avalaamu weeyũmbanĩtye kũthemba Isaka?
3 Kwakũna visa mũtumĩa mũkũũ ang'atĩte kĩĩma. E kyalonĩ kyetu vyũ ũtaakĩthi na ũtakakĩthi ĩngĩ thayũnĩ wake. Ti atĩ kyalo kĩu kĩ na vinya aĩ nũndũ nĩ mũkũũ. Mũtumĩa ũsu nĩ Avalaamu, na o na kau e na myaka ta 125, e o na vinya. [1] Aumĩtwe ĩtina nĩ mwanake wĩ na myaka ta 25. Mwanake ũsu nĩ mwanae, Isaka, na akuĩte mũio wa ngũ. Nake Avalaamu akuĩte kavyũ na syĩndũ ingĩ sya kũmũtetheesya kwakany'a mwaki. Kyalo kĩu kyonthe nĩ kya kĩ? Yeova aĩ amũkũlĩtye Avalaamu athembe mwana wake ũsyaĩte!—Mwa. 22:1-8.
4 No kwĩthĩwa vate ĩvinda yĩngĩ mũĩkĩĩo wa Avalaamu waatatwa ta ĩvinda yĩu. Andũ amwe maasyaa kana ũndũ ũsu Ngai wakũlilye Avalaamu eke woonanisye kana nde tei, namo angĩ masasya kana Avalaamu amwĩwie Ngai atatũmĩĩte kĩlĩko na ndamwendete mwana wake. Masasya ũu nũndũ mo ene mayĩthĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo na maiwĩsĩ nesa. (1 Ako. 2:14-16) Ĩndĩ Avalaamu nĩweesĩ kĩla ũkwĩka ĩla watwie kũmwĩw'a Ngai. Amwĩwie nũndũ aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo ũsu, nĩweesĩ nesa ki kana Ĩthe wake wa ĩtunĩ, Yeova, ndesa kwĩa athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku meke ũndũ ũtonya kũmaũmĩsya tene na tene. Avalaamu nĩweesĩ kana amwĩw'a Yeova, ndakalea kũmũathima vamwe na mwana wake Isaka. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumĩte Avalaamu ethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ũlũmĩte ũu? Nĩ ũmanyi ũla waĩ naw'o na maũndũ ala weeyoneete.
5. Avalaamu atonya kwĩthĩwa amũmanyangie Yeova ata, na ũmanyi ũsu wamũtetheeisye ata?
5 Ũmanyi. Avalaamu nĩwamwĩsĩ Yeova o na kau eanĩe ndũanĩ ya Ulu ĩla yaĩ nthĩ ya Akalitei, vala andũ aingĩ mathaithaa mĩvw'anano. Kwoou no tũseng'e-ĩ, amũmanyie Yeova ata na ĩthe, Tela, aĩ mũthaithi wa mĩvw'anano? (Yos. 24:2) Mbivilia ndĩwetaa ũtheinĩ ũndũ ũsu, ĩndĩ nĩyonanĩtye kana Avalaamu aĩ wa nzyawa ya kenda kuma kwa mwana wa Noa weetawa Semu, ũla waĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Semu aikw'a Avalaamu aĩ na myaka ta 150. Tũyĩsa kũweta vyũ tũkasya kana Avalaamu emanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Yeova kuma kũla kwĩ Semu. Ĩndĩ no twasye kana Semu nĩwamanyĩisye andũ make maũndũ ala weesĩ ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Na kwoou veoneka o nake Avalaamu nĩwesie kũmanya maũndũ asu na mamũkiita ngoo. Nũndũ wa ũmanyi ũsu, nĩwambĩĩe kũmwenda Ngai na alũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo wake.
6, 7. Maũndũ ala Avalaamu weeyoneie malũlũmĩilye mũĩkĩĩo wake ata?
6 Maũndũ ala weeyoneete. Nĩ kana Avalaamu ese kũtw'ĩka nĩweyonea maũndũ matonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo wake, eekie ata? Andũ amwe maasya kana mosũanĩo nĩmo matumaa mũndũ ethĩwa na woni mũna ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũna, naw'o woni ũsu nĩw'o ũtumaa osa ĩtambya ĩna. Maũndũ ala Avalaamu weemanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Ngai nĩmatumie ew'a aĩle kũmũkĩa na kũmũtaĩa "Yeova, Ngai Ũla Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe, mwene wa ĩtu na nthĩ." (Mwa. 14:22) Kyu Avalaamu weew'aa kĩtĩtwe nĩ Mbivilia "kũmũkĩa Ngai." Kĩkĩo ta kĩu nĩ kya vata nĩ kana mũndũ ethĩwe mũnyanyae wa Ngai. (Aevl. 5:7; Sav. 25:14) Kĩkĩo kyu nĩkyo kyatumie Avalaamu osa ĩtambya yĩla woosie.
7 O na kau Avalaamu na mũka wake Sala maĩ akũũ, Ngai ameie maume ndũanĩ ya Ulu mathi nthĩ ya ũeninĩ. Mesaa kwĩkala maeemanĩ nginya makakw'e. Avalaamu aĩ mwĩwi na nũndũ wa ũu Yeova nĩwambĩĩe kũmũathima na kũmũsũvĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda yĩmwe Avalaamu woonaa nũkũawa na aivenwa mũka nũndũ aĩ mwanake mũno. O na kau aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũkĩa, we ndaaĩtĩkĩla ũndũ ũsu ũtume aeka kũmwĩw'a Yeova. Kwoou Yeova nĩwalikĩlĩĩle na amũsũvĩa Avalaamu na Sala kwa nzĩa ya kyama. Na ti ĩvinda yĩu yĩ yoka weekie ũu. (Mwa. 12:10-20; 20:2-7, 10-12, 17, 18) Maũndũ asu Avalaamu weeyonee na metho make nĩmalũlũmĩilye mũĩkĩĩo wake.
8. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twongeleele ũmanyi na tũyĩyonea maũndũ angĩ ala matonya kũtũtetheesya tũlũlũmĩlye ũnyanya witũ na Yeova?
8 Nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ithyĩ tũkethĩwa anyanyae ma Yeova? Ĩĩ, vyũ! Ũmanyi ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ na ũvoo ĩũlũ wa andũ angĩ ala maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo nitonya kũtũtethya. Avalaamu aĩ na kaũmanyi kanini twasianĩsya na ũĩ mwingĩ ũla tũkwataa Mbivilianĩ ũmũnthĩ. (Nda. 12:4; Alo. 11:33) Maũndũ asu me Ndetonĩ ya Ngai nĩmatonya kũtũtetheesya tũmũmanye nesa "mwene wa ĩtu na nthĩ," na maitũtetheesya tũmũkĩe na kũmwenda. Ĩla twamwĩw'a Ngai nũndũ wa kũmũkĩa na kũmwenda, nĩtwĩyoneaa ithyĩ ene ũndũ kũmwĩw'a Ngai kũtethasya. Nĩtwonaa ũndũ motao make matũsũvĩaa na ũndũ ũtũathimaa na aitwĩkĩa vinya. Nĩtwĩyoneaa kana kũmũthũkũma Ngai na ngoo yonthe kũtumaa twĩkala twĩ eanĩe, twĩ na mũuo, na twĩ atanu. (Sav. 34:8; Nth. 10:22) O ũndũ twaendeea kũmanya Ngai na kwona aitũathima, now'o mũĩkĩĩo witũ ũlũlũmĩlaa na ndũũ yitũ vamwe na Yeova ĩyĩthĩwa yĩ ndũmangu.
ŨNDŨ AVALAAMU WAENDEEIE KWĨTHĨWA MŨNYANYAE WA NGAI
9, 10. (a) Andũ me ndũũ maĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana ndũũ yoo ĩendeee kũlũlũmĩla? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana Avalaamu nĩwoonaa ndũũ yake na Yeova yĩ ya vata na kana nĩwaendeeie kũmĩlũlũmĩlya?
9 Andũ matuma ndũũ, ndũũ ĩsu nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kĩndũ kya vata mũno. (Soma Nthimo 17:17.) Ĩndĩ ndũũ ndwĩsa kũmĩelekany'a na kĩndũ ũtonya kũthooa na ũikĩlekya vandũ kĩũlũkĩlawe nĩ kĩtoo. Ndũũ no ta ũndũ ũmwe na ĩlaa yanake, yĩla yaĩle kũng'ithw'a na kũsũvĩwa nĩ kana yĩane na yĩisanzamũka. Avalaamu nĩwoonaa ndũũ yake na Yeova yĩ ya vata na nĩwaendeeaa kũmĩlũlũmĩlya. Eekaa ũu ata?
10 Vai mũthenya Avalaamu waasũanĩa kana ĩvinda yĩla weethĩĩtwe e mwĩwi na aimũkĩa Ngai nĩyeanĩtye. Ĩla wakwatie kyalo kya kũthi Kanaani e na mũsyĩ wake no waendeeie kũeka Yeova amũtongoesye ĩla ũkwĩka motwi, methĩwe nĩ manene kana nĩ manini. Kwa ngelekany'o, vatiele mwaka ũmwe Isaka asyawe, ĩla Avalaamu waĩ na myaka 99, Yeova amwĩie kana aũme onthe ma nyũmba yake maĩle kwaĩkwa. We Avalaamu aaya nzika na mwĩao ũsu wa Yeova kana akamantha kĩtumi kya kwĩlingya? Aiee, ndaaĩka ũu, ĩndĩ nĩwamwĩkwatisye Ngai na eeka ũu wamwĩaĩe o "mũthenya ũsu."—Mwa. 17:10-14, 23.
11. Nĩkĩ Avalaamu wathĩnĩkie ĩla wamanyie kana ndũa ya Sotomo na Ngomola nikwanangwa, na Yeova amũtetheeisye ata?
11 Nũndũ Avalaamu aĩ na kĩmanyĩo kya kũmwĩw'aa Yeova o na maũndũnĩ ala monekaa ta manini, ndũũ yoo nĩyaendeeie kũlũlũmĩla. Ndakĩaa kũmũelesya Yeova kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ yake, na ĩla wĩ na makũlyo meũmũya mũtwe nĩwamũkũlasya amũtetheesye. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla wamanyie kana Ngai nĩwavangĩte kwananga ndũa ya Sotomo na Ngomola, nĩweewie athĩnĩka mũno nũndũ oonaa ala alũngalu ta matonya kwananganĩw'a na ala athũku. Nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa asũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa Loto (mwana wa mwana-a-inyia) na mũsyĩ wake, nũndũ mekalaa ndũanĩ ya Sotomo. Avalaamu amũkũlilye Ngai makũlyo ala waĩ namo enyivĩtye mũno na amũĩkĩĩe vyũ, esĩ nĩwe "Mũsili wa nthĩ yonthe." Nake Yeova nĩwoomĩĩisye Avalaamu na amũmanyĩsya kana we nĩ Ngai wĩ tei mwingĩ o na ĩla watw'a kũsilĩla andũ, na kana nũsomaa ngoo aimantha ala alũngalu nĩ kenda amatangĩĩe.—Mwa. 18:22-33.
12, 13. (a) Maũndũ ala Avalaamu weemanyĩĩtye na weeyoneete mesie kũmũtethya ata? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana Avalaamu nĩwamũĩkĩĩte Yeova?
12 Vate nzika, maũndũ onthe ala Avalaamu weemanyĩĩtye na weeyoneete nĩmamũtetheetye akaendeea kwĩkala e mũnyanyae wa Yeova. Kwoou ĩla Yeova wesie kũmũkũlya Avalaamu athembe mwana wake, Isaka, o na kau ũndũ ũsu waĩ vinya mũno, Avalaamu nĩwasũanĩie ũndũ wamwĩsĩ Mũnyanyae ũsu wa ĩtunĩ. Kwaekai tũkũne visa ĩngĩ mũtumĩa ũsu mũĩkĩĩku ang'atĩte kĩla kĩĩma kyaĩ nthĩ ya Molia. We Avalaamu nĩwĩthĩwa eesilasya kana Yeova no aalyũke akatw'ĩka Ngai ũte tei? Avalaamu ndaĩ aelya kũsũanĩa ũu! Twĩsĩ ata?
13 Avalaamu atanamba kũtaanĩsya na athũkũmi ala waĩ namo ameie atĩĩ: 'Inyw'ĩ ĩkalai vaa na ĩng'oi, nakwa na mwana nĩtũũthi kũya; na tũkathaitha, na kũmũsyokea ĩngĩ.' (Mwa. 22:5) We Avalaamu endaa kwasya ata? We eekaa kũmakenga ĩla wameie nũkwĩsa kũsyoka na Isaka na no weesĩ aendete kũmũthemba? Aiee. Mbivilia nĩtũtetheeasya tũkaelewa kĩla Avalaamu wasũanĩaa. (Soma Aevelania 11:19.) Avalaamu 'atalaa kana Ngai nũtonya kũmũthayũũkya [Isaka] o na kũmumya akw'ũnĩ.' Kĩu kĩonany'a kana Avalaamu nĩwaĩkĩĩaa kana akw'ũ no mathayũũkw'e. Aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu nũndũ nĩweesĩ kana, o na kau we na mũka maĩ akũũ, Yeova nĩwatũngĩĩie ũtonyi woo wa kũsyaa. (Aevl. 11:11, 12, 18) Avalaamu nĩweesĩ ki kana vai ũndũ ũmũema Yeova. Kwoou nĩweesĩ nesa kana o na kweekĩka ata mũthenya ũsu waendete kũthemba mwanae, ndalea kũmũtũngĩwa nĩ kana maũndũ onthe ala Yeova wathanĩte makeanĩa. Mwa o na Avalaamu ndaĩ alea kwĩtwa "ĩthe wa onthe ala metĩkĩlaa"!
14. Nĩ maũndũ ta meva wĩw'aa me vinya kwĩanĩsya ĩla ũũmũthũkũma Yeova, na kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Avalaamu kũtonya kũũtethya ata?
14 Nao nata ithyĩ? Nĩ w'o kana Ngai ndatũkũlasya twĩke ũndũ ta ũsu wamũkũlilye Avalaamu eke. Ĩndĩ nĩwendaa tũmwĩw'e o na ĩla tũkwĩw'a mĩao ĩmwe ũtũnengete yĩ vinya, kana o na ĩla tũtekũelewa nĩkĩ ũtũnengete mĩao mĩna. Katĩ wa maũndũ ala Ngai ũtwĩaa nĩtwĩke, ve ũmwe we wĩw'aa wĩ vinya? Kwa amwe, nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa nĩ kũtavany'a. No kwĩthĩwa me nthoni ũkethĩa nĩmekũemwa nĩ kũtavya mũndũ matamwĩsĩ ũvoo mũseo. Namo angĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa makĩaa kwoneka me kĩvathũkany'o na andũ ala angĩ, ta ĩla me sukulu kana ĩla me wĩanĩ. (Kuma 23:2; 1 Ath. 2:2) Mavinda amwe ĩla wasũanĩa ũndũ mũna mũito Yeova ũkwenda wĩke, nĩwĩw'aa ta ũng'atĩte kĩĩma kya Molia ta Avalaamu? Ethĩwa nĩwĩw'aa ũu, ngelekany'o ya Avalaamu na mũĩkĩĩo wake nitonya ũkwĩkĩa vinya. Ĩla twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa aũme na aka ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku, nĩtwĩkĩawa vinya twĩke tamo na tũimũthengeea Mũnyanyae witũ, Yeova.—Aevl. 12:1, 2.
NDŨŨ ĨLA ĨETAE MOATHIMO
15. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Avalaamu ndaaĩlila nũndũ wa kũmwĩw'a Yeova kĩla ĩvinda?
15 We wĩona Avalaamu ta waaĩsa kwĩlila nũndũ wa kũmwĩw'a Yeova kĩla ĩvinda? Kwoona ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye ĩũlũ wa matukũ ma mũthya ma Avalaamu. Yaĩtye: "Na Avalaamu aumwa nĩ veva, akw'a ũkũunĩ mũseo, e mũtumĩu mũno, na wa myaka mingĩ." (Mwa. 25:8) O na ĩla Avalaamu wakusaa e na myaka 175, aĩ mwĩanĩe vyũ asisya ũndũ watũmĩĩte thayũ wake nesa. Thayũnĩ wake w'onthe kĩla kyaĩ kya vata kyaĩ ũnyanya wake na Yeova Ngai. Ĩndĩ ĩla Mbivilia yasya kana Avalaamu akwie "e mũtumĩu mũno, na wa myaka mingĩ," ndeto isu iyaĩle kũtuma tũsũanĩa kana Avalaamu nĩweanĩtye kwĩkala thayũ na ndaĩ na mea ma kwĩkala thayũ ĩngĩ ĩvinda yũkĩte.
16. Nĩ maũndũ meva Avalaamu ũkatanĩa Nthĩ Nzaũ?
16 Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Avalaamu: "Nĩweteelaa onw'e ndũa ĩla yĩ na myambĩlĩlyo, na mwambĩlĩlya na mwaki wayo nĩ Ngai." (Aevl. 11:10) Ndũa ĩsu nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, na Avalaamu aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana mũthenya ũmwe akamyona ĩsumbĩkĩte nthĩ. Na nĩ w'o, akoona ũu! We wĩona Avalaamu ta ũkatana ata ĩla ũkeyĩthĩa Nthĩ Nzaũ, vala ũkakwata mwanya wa kũendeea kũlũlũmĩlya ndũũ yake vamwe na Yeova? No nginya ethĩwe akakiitwa ngoo mũno ĩla ũkamanya kana mũĩkĩĩo wake nĩwatetheeisye athũkũmi angĩ ma Yeova o na myaka mingĩ ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kyake! O na ĩvinda yĩu akamanya kana nthembo ĩla wesaa kumya Kĩĩmanĩ kya Molia yaĩ "ngelekan'yo" ya ũndũ ũngĩ mũnene waĩ mbee. (Aevl. 11:19) O na ĩngĩ, akamanya kaĩ woo ũla weewie ĩla weeyũmbanasya kũmũthemba Isaka nũtetheetye andũ aingĩ mũno aĩkĩĩku maelewe ũndũ Yeova mwene weewie ĩla wamumisye Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, atw'ĩke nthembo ya wovosyo! (Yoa. 3:16) Ngelekany'o ya Avalaamu nĩtũtetheesye ithyonthe tũkaelewa mũnango ũndũ nthembo ya wovosyo ne ya vata. Nthembo ĩsu nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ Yeova waaĩka akonany'a nũtwendete!
17. We watw'a kwĩka ata, na ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩneeneete kyaũ?
17 Kĩla ũmwe witũ natw'e kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Avalaamu. O ũndũ twaendeea kũmũmanya Yeova nesanga now'o tũmwĩw'aa mũnango, na nũndũ wa ũu tũkoonaa aitũathima vyũ na kũtũsũvĩa. (Soma Aevelania 6:10-12.) Ekai ĩndĩ tũmũtw'e Yeova Mũnyanyae witũ tene na tene! Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩeleetye athũkũmi angĩ atatũ ma Ngai ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku na maĩ anyanyae.
^ [1] (kalungu ka 3) Mũtumĩa ũũ mbeenĩ eetawa Avalamu nake mũka eetawa Salai, ĩndĩ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩtũmĩa masyĩtwa ala Yeova wesie kũmanenga ĩtina, namo nĩ Avalaamu na Sala.

translation:
"But you, Israel, are my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend." – ISA. 41:8.
PARAGRAPH: 51, 22
1, 2. (a) Why is it important for us to show appreciation for God's love? (b) What will we discuss in this section?
ALTHOUGH we often take things for granted, everything we have is a gift from Jehovah. Many people are ungrateful for the blessings they enjoy. We are prone to being preoccupied with our own problems and desires. But the One who gives us countless blessings is Jehovah. Most people do not recognize Jehovah as the loving God, the Sovereign Lord, and they live selfishly. So why are we so grateful? Yes, we are grateful because of what we know!
2 The Bible shows that there are those who demonstrate genuine appreciation for God's love. To help us imitate their example, let us consider how showing appreciation can strengthen our relationship with God. One man who showed great appreciation for God was Abraham. (Read James 2:23.) Did Abraham appreciate Jehovah's love? One way his loyalty demonstrated this was through his willingness to sacrifice Isaac, his son. And that is why the Bible calls Abraham "a friend of Jehovah" [or, "a man loyal to Jehovah."] (Acts 4:11) Let us examine Abraham's example to see how it can motivate us to show appreciation for God's love. Let each of us ask himself, 'Can I show the kind of loyalty that Abraham did, and thus prove my devotion to Jehovah?'
DID ABRAHAM SHOW APPRECIATION FOR JEHOVAH'S LOVE?
3, 4. (a) How did Abraham show that he was willing to go to great lengths to please Jehovah? Explain. (b) Why did Abraham hesitate to offer Isaac?
3 At times, people face difficult trials. It may seem as though they have more than they can handle. But often such trials reveal what is truly in a person's heart. This was true of Abraham, who was about 125 years old and still vigorous. [1] He had just become a father to a son when the son was 25 years old. That son was Isaac, whom Abraham loved dearly. Yet, Abraham was willing to risk losing him as an offering. What does this all mean? Jehovah asked Abraham to show his faith by sacrificing his beloved son!—Gen. 22:1-8.
4 Now, imagine how Abraham felt when he realized what God was asking him to do. Some might wonder why God would test Abraham in this way, and why He would ask him to do something so drastic as offering up his only son. Such questions are understandable and deserve consideration. (1 Cor. 2:14-16) For Abraham, it was a severe test of his loyalty to God. He loved his son deeply. His loyalty, however, was rooted in his profound love for Jehovah, and his desire to please Him in every way. Abraham knew that Jehovah is loving and compassionate, and that He would never ask anyone to do something unreasonable. Abraham was willing to trust Jehovah, even if it meant parting with his son Isaac. Why did Abraham respond to this severe trial with such loyalty? The answer lies in what he knew about Jehovah.
5 Did Abraham fully understand why Jehovah allowed this, and did that knowledge strengthen his faith?
5 Indeed. Abraham had confidence in Jehovah, even though he did not know the full extent of Jehovah's purpose, just as many others have shown faith without knowing everything. Consider this: Would you have trusted Jehovah, even if you had been like Terah, Abraham's father, who was likely associated with idolatry? (Josh. 24:2) The Bible indicates that Abraham was a descendant of Shem, Noah's son, which means he came from a family that valued true worship. Shem lived to be 150 years old, and Abraham was born while Shem was still alive. It is reasonable to believe that Abraham learned about Jehovah from Shem. Furthermore, it seems that Shem passed on his knowledge to his descendants. Thus, Abraham likely grew up knowing about Jehovah and appreciating His qualities. This knowledge strengthened his resolve to obey God and live according to His will.
6, 7. What shows that Abraham appreciated Jehovah's promise?
6 He showed that he did. Did Abraham simply pay lip service to what he believed, or did he truly appreciate Jehovah's promise? Some people may say that circumstances can cause a person to act in a certain way, and that such action does not necessarily reflect what is in their heart. However, Abraham demonstrated his faith in God by using Jehovah's name when speaking to others and acknowledging Him as "Jehovah, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth." (Gen. 14:22) That is why the Bible calls him "a friend of God." This title highlights the close relationship that a faithful worshiper has with God. (Isa. 5:7; Ps. 25:14) This friendship motivated Abraham to continue walking with Jehovah.
7 Now, Abraham and his wife Sarah were advanced in years, yet God assured them they would have a son, a sign of His favor. It may seem impossible at times. Abraham trusted in Jehovah's power to fulfill His promise. For example, consider how Abraham responded when he was told that they would have a child in their old age. Despite this seeming impossibility, he continued to hold fast to his faith in Jehovah. Jehovah remembered Abraham and Sarah favorably and granted them their request. And this blessing proved to be lasting. (Gen. 12:10-20; 20:2-7, 10-12, 17, 18) What Abraham did demonstrates the depth of his faith.
8 Then, how can we imitate Abraham, strengthening our own faith and appreciating more fully the wonderful things Jehovah does for us?
8 Is it possible for us to become more convinced of Jehovah's love? Yes, indeed! The knowledge found in the Bible and the experiences of others can help us to strengthen our faith. Abraham had great faith, similar to what many of us experience when we learn about Jehovah. (Prov. 12:4; Acts 11:33) The teachings from God's Word can help us to appreciate more deeply what "the gift" means, and motivate us to speak about Him and worship Him. If we love God and desire to know and worship Him, we will find that knowing God brings satisfaction. We will see benefits in our lives and feel secure, peaceful, and content. (Ps. 34:8; Prov. 10:22) So, as we come to know God and appreciate what He does for us, our faith grows stronger and our bond with Jehovah becomes closer.
WHAT ABRAHAM DID TO REMAIN CLOSE TO GOD
9, 10. (a) What situations might test whether someone truly has faith? (b) How did Abraham show that he valued his relationship with Jehovah and was determined to strengthen it?
9 Often, people's faith is tested when they face difficulties. (Read Proverbs 17:17.) Sometimes a problem seems impossible to solve, and it may cause anxiety and distress. Such problems may be like obstacles that hinder our progress or make us feel discouraged. But Abraham valued his relationship with Jehovah and was determined to strengthen it. How did he do this?
10 Remember how Abraham readily responded when God asked him to leave his homeland and go to a place he would later designate. He packed up his family and went to Canaan, without knowing exactly where he was going, though it meant traveling a great distance. Later, Jehovah promised Abraham that his offspring would become a great nation, even though Abraham was 99 years old and Sarah was barren. Did Abraham question Jehovah's ability to fulfill this promise? No, he continued to have confidence in God and showed his faith by obeying what God told him—"walking before Him."—Gen. 17:10-14, 23.
11. Did Abraham ever wonder why Sodom and Gomorrah were being destroyed, and did Jehovah reassure him?
11 Indeed, Abraham was deeply concerned about the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, and he felt compelled to plead with Jehovah. He knew that Jehovah was just and compassionate, so he reasoned that He would not destroy the righteous along with the wicked. Abraham expressed his willingness to help Jehovah find even a small number of righteous people in those cities, saying, "Please do not wipe them out." (Lot's son) and his family who lived in Sodom. Abraham appealed to Jehovah based on His justice, reminding Him that He would be willing to spare the cities if even a few righteous ones could be found there. Jehovah assured Abraham that He would spare the cities if Abraham could find at least ten righteous men. This demonstrates Jehovah's willingness to listen to sincere appeals and to show mercy.—Gen. 18:22-33.
12, 13. (a) What questions did Abraham ask, and why was it appropriate for him to ask them? (b) What shows that Abraham trusted Jehovah?
12 Of course, Abraham asked these questions because he wanted to understand what Jehovah expected of him and how he could remain loyal to Him. He knew that Jehovah had promised to make a great nation through his son Isaac, and he wondered how this promise could come true if Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed. Abraham showed his faith by being willing to offer up his beloved son Isaac as a sacrifice, demonstrating that he trusted in Jehovah's promises. Like us, Abraham wanted to know whether Jehovah would act in harmony with His own principles. Did Abraham ever doubt that Jehovah was able to fulfill His purpose? Certainly not!
13 Abraham did not hesitate to express his concern about the righteous people who might be harmed along with the wicked ones, saying: "Please do not wipe out the righteous with the wicked. What if there should be fifty righteous people in the city? Would you really destroy it?" (Gen. 18:25) Why did Abraham ask this question? Was he trying to test Jehovah, wondering if He would actually carry out His threat? No. Rather, his words show that he understood Abraham's deep desire to see justice prevail. (Read Hebrews 11:19.) Abraham "reasoned that God was able to raise Isaac from the dead." This shows that Abraham believed that nothing is too difficult for God. And because of his faith, Jehovah rewarded him with the prospect of resurrection. (Heb. 11:11, 12, 18) Abraham firmly believed that Jehovah is good. He also realized that even though it may seem unreasonable to ask someone to sacrifice his son, Jehovah has reasons for doing things that we may not fully understand. That is why Abraham is rightly called "a friend of Jehovah!"
14 What lessons can we learn from Abraham's example regarding our relationship with Jehovah and our willingness to trust in Him?
14 But how is that possible? It is because God allows us to experience trials that prove our loyalty, just as He did with Abraham. We may find ourselves facing difficulties, or we may struggle to understand why certain things happen. However, God gives us strength to endure them. But what if we feel inadequate or fear that we will fail? Remember that others have felt the same way. Some may be afraid to speak publicly, while others may worry about being rejected by their peers at school or in the workplace. (Prov. 23:2; 1 Thess. 2:2) Many young people who want to serve Jehovah wholeheartedly wonder if they have the courage to face challenges like those faced by Abraham. If so, remember that Abraham's faith grew stronger over time. As we learn more about Jehovah and His purposes, we become more confident in our ability to remain loyal to Him.—Heb. 12:1, 2.
WHY THIS IS IMPORTANT
15. Can we be sure that Abraham always remained faithful to Jehovah throughout his life?
15 Do you think Abraham always found it easy to remain faithful to Jehovah throughout his life? The Bible tells us about a period in Abraham's life when he showed imperfection. It says: "Now Abraham became old, advanced in age, and Jehovah had blessed him in everything." (Gen. 25:8) Even though Abraham lived to be 175 years old, he still made mistakes. Throughout his life, his greatest desire was to please Jehovah God. So, when the Bible says that Abraham "became old, advanced in age," this reminds us that even faithful men can grow weak physically and emotionally as they get older.
16. What questions did Nicodemus ask Jesus?
16 The Bible reports what Nicodemus asked Abraham: "Teacher, we know that you came from God as a teacher; no one can perform the signs you do unless God is with him." (John 3:2) Nicodemus was a Jewish religious leader, and Abraham recognized that he was sincere in wanting to learn more about God. But despite that, Nicodemus was confused. Do you think Abraham would have been quick to judge Nicodemus, or would he have taken time to help him understand things better? Of course, he would have been patient! And he would have rejoiced when Nicodemus finally understood that God's love for mankind led Him to send His Son, Jesus Christ, to give his life as a ransom! (John 3:16) Abraham's example teaches us to be patient and understanding so that others may come to appreciate the wonderful gift of salvation.
God's promise to Abraham has great meaning for us today!
17. What can we learn from this, and what lesson does it teach us?
17 Like everyone else, we can benefit from having faith like Abraham's. As we get to know Jehovah better, we will love and appreciate Him more, and this will motivate us to obey Him. (Read Ephesians 6:10-12.) Let us always remember that Jehovah is our loving Father! This lesson reminds us that God cares for those who seek Him sincerely.
^ [1] (paragraph 3) This man named Abraham and his wife named Sarai, in this account we are referring to, Jehovah showed His willingness to fulfill his promise, and it was Abraham and Sarah.

text:
"Meli . . . ekala nthĩ maũũnĩ ma Yesũ, akĩthukĩĩsya ndeto syake. Ĩndĩ Matha athĩniw'e nĩ wĩa."—LUKA 10:39, 40.
MBATHI: 40, 55
1, 2. Nĩkĩ Yesũ wamwendete Matha, na twĩsĩ ata kana Matha aĩ mũndũ wĩ na naĩ?
ĨLA wasũanĩa Matha ũla ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ, we wonaa aĩ mũndũ mũka wa mũthemba mwaũ? O na kau no we mũndũ mũka ũla Mbivilia ĩwetete ĩsyĩtwa yake ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe na ĩkaweta kana Yesũ nĩwamwendete, Yesũ nĩwendete na akanenga ndaĩa aka angĩ ta inyia-ake, na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia wa Matha ũla weetawa Meli. (Yoa. 11:5; 19:25-27) Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ Yesũ wamwendete Matha?
2 Yesũ endete Matha nũndũ aĩ mũlau na aĩ na kĩthito. O na ĩngĩ, aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu mũno. Nĩwaĩkĩĩaa vyũ kĩla Yesũ wamanyĩasya. Na ndaĩ na nzika o na vanini kana Yesũ nĩwe waĩ Masia ũla wathanĩtwe. (Yoa. 11:21-27) O na vailyĩ ũu, Matha aĩ mũndũ waĩ na naĩ o taitũ. Ĩvinda yĩmwe ĩla mathoketye Yesũ kwoo, oonie aĩle kũtavya Yesũ akany'e mwĩĩtu-a-inyia Meli nũndũ oonaa avĩtĩtye. Amwĩie atĩĩ: "Mwĩaĩi, ndũkwona ũndũ mwĩĩtu-a-ia ũndekanĩsye na wĩa nĩtethye nĩ nyioka? mwĩe andetheesye." (Soma Luka 10:38-42.) Ngewa ĩsu yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
MATHA NĨWAVĨNGĨĨSIWE NĨ MAŨNDŨ
3, 4. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Meli wanyuvie "kĩlungu kĩseo," na Matha eemanyĩisye kyaũ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 18.)
3 Nũndũ Yesũ nĩwatanĩie kũthokw'a nĩ Matha na Meli, nĩwatwie kũtũmĩa ĩvinda yĩu amamanyĩsye maũndũ ma vata. Meli nĩwoonie nĩ ũseo atũmĩe mwanya ũsu nesa akwate ũmanyi kuma kwĩ Mwalimũ Mũnene na kwoou ekala nthĩ "maũũnĩ ma Yesũ, akĩthukĩĩsya ndeto syake." Matha aaĩlĩte kwĩka oou na vate nzika Yesũ ethĩwa amũkathie mũno.
4 Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwĩka ũu, Matha akwatanie mũno ayĩua lĩu mũseo na kwĩka maũndũ angĩ nĩ kana Yesũ ethĩwe e mwĩanĩe. Ĩndĩ wĩa ũsu w'onthe watumie athĩnĩka mũno nginya amũthatĩa Meli. Yesũ nĩwamanyie kana Matha nĩweekwatanĩtye na maũndũ maingĩ mũno na kwoou amwĩa atĩĩ: "Matha, Matha, nũkwĩnyamasya na kwĩthĩn'ya na maũndũ maingĩ." Na ĩndĩ amwĩa vayaĩ vata wa kũua malĩu maingĩ. Ĩtina wa ũu, Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana Meli ndavĩtĩtye ĩla wamũkathie akyasya atĩĩ: "Meli nũnyuvie kĩlungu kĩseo, kĩla ũtakavenwa." Ĩtina wa ĩvinda yĩte yĩasa, no kwĩthĩwa Meli oolilwe nĩ kĩla waĩye mũthenya ũsu wa mwanya, ĩndĩ ndaĩ olwa nĩ ũndũ Yesũ wamũkathie na maũndũ ma vata mũno ala weemanyĩisye mũthenya ũsu wamwĩthukĩĩisye Yesũ nesa vyũ. Ĩtina wa myaka mbee wa 60, mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Yesũ nĩwamwendete Matha, na mwĩĩtu-a-inyia." (Yoa. 11:5) Vate nzika, ndeto isu mbeveee syĩtũĩkĩĩthya kana Matha nĩweetĩkĩlile kũlũngwa nĩ Yesũ na eekĩa kĩthito amũthũkũme Yeova e mũĩkĩĩku nginya ĩla wakwie.
5. Maũndũ mailyĩ ata ũmũnthĩ masianĩw'a na ũndũ mailyĩ ĩvindanĩ ya tene, na kĩu kĩtuma twĩkũlya ĩkũlyo yĩva?
5 Ũmũnthĩ kwĩ syĩndũ mbingĩ mũno ila itonya kũtũvĩngĩĩsa tũimũthũkũma Yeova kwĩ ila syaĩ kw'o ĩvinda ya tene. Myaka mbee wa 60 mĩthelu, kĩkundi kĩmwe kya amanyĩw'a ma sukulu ĩmwe yĩ Amelika kyeeiwe atĩĩ: "Vaiĩ ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva andũ maaĩsa kũtanĩa kwĩthĩwa na nzĩa syĩ laisi sya kũneena, masinĩ syĩ mĩtũkĩ sya kũtumbĩthya mavuku, makaseti me mavisa maingĩ, letiũ, sinema, televiseni. . . . Kĩla mũthenya nĩkũseũvaw'a syĩndũ nzaũ itonya kũtũvĩngĩĩsa. O mĩtũkĩ, andũ aingĩ manasũanĩaa kana ĩvinda yĩĩ yitũ nĩ 'Ĩvinda ya Kwĩthĩwa na Ũmanyi' ĩndĩ yĩsĩte kũtw'ĩka 'Ĩvinda ya Kũvĩngĩĩswa.'" Nayo ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩsũngũ) ya 15/09/1958 yaisye atĩĩ: "Syĩndũ ila itonya kũvĩngĩĩsa andũ nitonya kũendeea kwongeleka o ũndũ mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno ũthengeee." Ndeto isu nĩ sya w'o ki! Na kĩndũ kĩu kĩtumaa twĩkũlya ĩkũlyo yĩĩ ya vata mũno: O ta Meli, tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũtũnge ilĩko sitũ maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva na tũyĩkala tũteũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ maũndũ mate ma lasima?
KWĨTETHYA NA SYĨNDŨ SYA NTHĨ ĨNDĨ TŨTEŨSYĨKWATYA MŨNO
6. Andũ ma Yeova matũmĩĩte tekinolongyia ata?
6 Kĩla ĩvinda, kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Ngai kya kũũ nthĩ nĩkĩtũmĩaa tekinolongyia nesa nĩ kana kĩendeesye ũthaithi wa w'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũseũvyo wa Yeova nĩwatũmĩie visa na tũsinema tũkuvĩ kũseũvya sinema yaĩ na mavisa me na langi. * Andũ milioni mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩmakiakĩiw'e nĩ sinema ĩsu Kaũ wa Mbee wa Nthĩ Yonthe ũtanamba kũkitwa o na ĩla kaũ ũsu waendeee. Sinema ĩsu ĩithela nĩyaeleisye ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Yesũ Klĩsto ũla ũkethĩwa na mũuo. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, ũseũvyo wa Yeova nĩwatũmĩie letiũ kũtangaasa ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ na weew'ĩka nĩ andũ milioni mbingĩ nthĩ yonthe. Ũmũnthĩ, kombiũta na Indaneti nitũmĩkĩte mũno kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo mũseo. Kĩu nĩkĩtumĩte ũvoo ũsu ũvikĩa andũ ala mekalaa ithamanĩ syĩ kũndũ kũasa na ũkavika itulu syonthe sya nthĩ.
7. (a) Kũtũmĩa syĩndũ sya nthĩ ĩno mũno kũtonya kũtũlikya mũisyonĩ wĩva? (b) Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kwĩsũvĩana mũno nakyo? (Sisya maelesyo ma kwongeleela.)
7 Mbivilia nĩtũkanĩtye kana kũtũmĩa mũno syĩndũ sya nthĩ ĩno nĩkũtonya kũtũlikya mũisyonĩ. (Soma 1 Akolintho 7:29-31.) Nĩ laisi mũno Mũklĩsto akasya ĩvinda yingĩ mũno ayĩka maũndũ mate mathũku. Maũndũ asu nĩ ta kwĩka maũndũ ala wendete ĩla ũthyũmũĩte, kũsoma mavuku nĩ kana wĩtanĩthye, kwĩloela televiseni, kũthi kũndũ nĩ kana wĩloele wũmbi, kũsisya syĩndũ matukanĩ, na kũmantha syĩndũ ila syumĩte mĩtũkĩ ta simũ kana syĩndũ ingĩ ite sya lasima. Maũndũ angĩ matonya kũtũkwata mũno na kũtwanangĩa ĩvinda nĩ kũtũmĩa isese sya kũea ngewa Indanetinĩ, kũtũmanĩa mesengyi na valũa ũitũmĩa simũ kana kombiũta, kwenda kũmanya maũvoo ma mathaũ na maũvoo angĩ kĩla ĩvinda. * (Mũta. 3:1, 6) Tũkaema kũola ĩvinda yĩla tũtũmĩaa maũndũnĩ mate ma lasima, nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kwĩthĩa twaekie ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ naw'o nĩ ũthaithi witũ.—Soma Aeveso 5:15-17.
8. Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kwĩsũvĩa mũno tũikende syĩndũ sya nthĩ?
8 Satani aseũvĩtye nthĩ ĩno yake ayenda tũmyende nĩ kana ĩtũvĩngĩĩse. Ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa kwailyĩ ũu na ũmũnthĩ nĩ kũthũku mũnango. (2 Tim. 4:10) Kwoou nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa ũtao ũũ: 'Mũikende syĩndũ sya nthĩ.' Ũu wĩonany'a kana kĩla ĩvinda nĩtwaĩle kwĩkaa moalyũku nĩ kana twĩkale kwosana na ũtao ũsu. Tweeka ũu tũkamũthũkũmaa Yeova tũteũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ syĩndũ ingĩ na tũiendeea kwĩthĩwa na "wendo wa Asa." Ũu ũkatuma wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai na tũyĩtĩkĩlwa nĩwe tene na tene.—1 Yoa. 2:15-17.
ĨTHĨWA NA ITHO YĨSYAĨTYE MAŨNDŨ ALA MA VATA
9. Yesũ eeie amanyĩw'a make methĩwe na itho yĩilyĩ ata, na we mwene aiie ngelekany'o yĩva?
9 Ndeto nzeo ila Yesũ wamũtavisye Matha aimũtaa syoosanĩte nesa vyũ na kĩla wamanyĩasya na ũndũ we mwene wekalaa. Eekĩie amanyĩw'a make vinya methĩwe na itho "ĩseo," kana itho yĩsyaĩtye maũndũ ala ma vata, nĩ kana methĩwe matonya kũmantha Ũsumbĩ mateũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ kĩndũ. (Soma Mathayo 6:22, 33.) Yesũ ndaĩ na syĩndũ mbingĩ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ; o na ndaĩ na nyũmba kana mũũnda.—Luka 9:58; 19:33-35.
10. Yesũ atũtiĩe ngelekany'o yĩva nzeo?
10 Ve maũndũ maingĩ maĩ matonya kũvĩngĩĩsa Yesũ ĩla watavanasya ĩndĩ ndaaĩtĩkĩla mamũvĩngĩĩse. Kwa ngelekany'o, vatathelete ĩvinda yĩasa kuma ambĩĩa kũtavany'a, nĩwamanyĩisye andũ ndũanĩ ya Kavelinaumi na eeka syama na nũndũ wa ũu andũ ma kũu nĩmamwĩsũvie ndakathi. Ĩndĩ we Yesũ eekie ata ĩla andũ matatie kũmwĩsũva ndakathi? Ameie atĩĩ: "Mũvaka nĩtavan'ye ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ndũanĩ ila ingĩ nasyo: nũndũ natũmiwe nũndũ wa ũu." (Luka 4:42-44) Yesũ aneenie w'o nũndũ aendie kĩla vandũ nthĩ ya Valestina aitavany'a na kũmanyĩsya. O na kau aĩ mũndũ ũte naĩ, nĩweethĩawa na mavata ta ma andũ ala angĩ na mavinda amwe nĩwanoaa mũno nũndũ wa kwĩyumya vyũ ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai.—Luka 8:23; Yoa. 4:6.
11. Yesũ eeie ata ũla mũndũ waĩ na ĩkoani ya mũsyĩ, na aumisye ũkany'o wĩva?
11 Ĩvinda yĩngĩ Yesũ akililye aimanyĩsya aatĩĩi make ũndũ matonya kwĩka mavĩngwa, mũndũ ũmwe ookĩla asya: "Mũmanyĩsya, mũtavye mwana-a-ia andaĩe ũtiĩwa." Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaaĩtĩkĩla kwĩlikya ĩkoaninĩ yĩu. Vandũ va ũu, asũngĩie mũndũ ũsu atĩĩ: "Mũndũ we, nũũ ũla ũndw'ĩte mũsili kana mũaan'ya ĩũlũ wenyu?" Aminana na mũndũ ũsu, aendeeie kũmanyĩsya andũ ala mamwĩthukĩĩsye na amakany'a kana masembany'a na syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ, no mavĩngĩĩsĩke makaeka kũmũthũkũma Ngai.—Luka 12:13-15.
12, 13. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Akiliki amwe menda kũmwona Yesũ mĩthenya mĩvũthũ atanamba kũawa? (b) Yesũ eekie ata nĩ kana ndakavĩngĩĩswe nĩ ũndũ ũsu?
12 Kyumwa kya mũthya Yesũ atanamba kũawa kyaĩ kyetu mũno. (Mt. 26:38; Yoa. 12:27) Aĩ na wĩa mwingĩ mũno wa kũtethya na nĩweesĩ akilyĩ anathĩnw'a mũno na ayũawa naĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwasũanĩa kĩla kyeethĩiwe mũthenya wa Wakyumwa matukũ 9, mwei wa Nisani, mwaka wa 33. O tondũ kwathanĩtwe, mũthenya ũsu Yesũ nĩwalikile Yelusaleme ekalĩle kang'oli na makomano mamũkatha makyasya nĩwe "Mũsumbĩ ũla wũkĩte syĩtwanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi." (Luka 19:38) Ũnĩ ũsu Yesũ nĩwalikile ĩkalũnĩ na akuthũa ateũkĩa atandĩthya me ĩtomo ala matũmĩaa nyũmba ya Ngai kũvena Ayuti ala angĩ mbesa syoo.—Luka 19:45, 46.
13 Akiliki amwe ala maĩ katĩ wa ĩkomano yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme nĩmendeeiw'e mũno nĩ maũndũ asu Yesũ weekie nginya mamũtũma Vilivu mayenda monane nake. Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaaĩtĩkĩla kũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ andũ asu nũndũ nĩweesĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata waĩ mbee wake waĩ kwĩyumya ethĩwe nthembo. Ndendaa kwĩmanthĩa nguma andũnĩ nĩ kana ndakoawe nĩ amaitha ma Ngai. Kwoou amina kũelesya kana aĩ vakuvĩ kũawa, eeie Andalea na Vilivu atĩĩ: "Ũla wendaa thayũ wake nũnũkũwasya; na ũla ũmenaa thayũ wake e kũũ nthĩ akoosũvĩa kũvika thayũ ũtathela." Vandũ va kwĩanĩsya wendi wa Akiliki asu, Yesũ oonanisye kana mũndũ aĩle kwĩthĩwa eyũmbanĩtye kumya thayũ wake na asyoka asya: "Ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva akanthũkũma, akataĩwa nĩ Asa." Vate nzika, Vilivu nĩwatavisye Akiliki asu mendaa kwonana na Yesũ ũvoo ũsu wa vata.—Yoa. 12:20-26.
14. O na kũtw'ĩka Yesũ oonaa wĩa wa kũtavany'a wĩ wa vata vyũ, nĩ kyaũ kĩkwonany'a kana ndasũanĩaa wĩa ĩvinda yonthe?
14 O na kũtw'ĩka Yesũ ndaaĩtĩkĩla ũndũ o na wĩva ũmũvĩngĩĩse ayĩanĩsya wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, ũu ti kwonany'a kana asũanĩaa o wĩa ũsu ĩvinda yonthe. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda wathokiw'e alũsinĩ na e kũu nĩwatumie andũ mamĩtanĩa mũno ĩla weekie kyama avĩndũa kĩw'ũ kyatw'ĩka mbinyu. (Yoa. 2:2, 6-10) O na ĩngĩ nĩweetĩkĩlaa kũthokw'a lĩunĩ wa wĩoo nĩ anyanya make na andũ angĩ ala mendeeaw'a nĩ ũvoo mũseo. (Luka 5:29; Yoa. 12:2) Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana kĩla ĩvinda Yesũ nĩwamanthaa ĩvinda ya kũvoya, ya kũvindĩĩsya maũndũ e weka, na ya kũthyũmũa.—Mt. 14:23; Mko. 1:35; 6:31, 32.
"NĨTWIE ŨTEE KĨLA KĨŨTŨVATA KŨTHI KYONTHE"
15. Mũtũmwa Vaulo anenganie ũtao wĩva, na nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva watũtiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo?
15 Mũtũmwa Vaulo aelekanilye thayũ wa Mũklĩsto ũla wĩyumĩtye amũthũkũme Yeova na mathaũ ma kũsemba, na ĩndĩ asya atĩĩ: "Nĩtwie ũtee kĩla kĩũtũvata kũthi kyonthe." (Soma Aevelania 12:1.) Vaulo mwene nĩweekie ũu nũndũ nĩwakolile kĩanda kĩla waĩ nakyo ndĩninĩ ya Ayuti, kĩla kyesaa kũtuma athua na ethĩwa na nguma. Nĩweeyumĩtye kwĩka "maũndũ ala maseo mbee" na nĩkyo kĩtumi watavanisye ũvoo mũseo na kĩthito kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o ta Silia, Asia Nini, Masetonia, na Yutia. Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ aiweta ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo ũla waĩ naw'o wa kũthi ĩtunĩ: "Ngyũlwa nĩ maũndũ ala me ĩtina, na ngĩkoota nĩvĩkĩe maũndũ ala me mbee, nĩngwĩthing'ĩĩsya kũthi nĩvikĩe ngoolu kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo." (Avi. 1:10; 3:8, 13, 14) Na nũndũ Vaulo ndatwaanĩte, nĩwatũmĩie ĩvinda yake nesa na 'amũthũkũma Mwĩaĩi ateũvũavũanw'a.'—1 Ako. 7:32-35.
16, 17. Twĩthĩwe nĩtũtwaanĩte kana tũitwaanĩte, nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Vaulo? Elesya ũndũ weekĩkie.
16 O ta Vaulo, athũkũmi amwe ma Ngai nĩmatw'ĩte kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae nĩ kana meke maũndũ maingangĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa Ũsumbĩ nũndũ mayĩthĩawa me akwatanu mũno maũndũnĩ ma mũsyĩ. (Mt. 19:11, 12) Mavinda maingĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai ala matwaanĩte na ala atwae methĩawa makwatene mũno na maũndũ ma mũsyĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩla ũmwe ethĩwe nũtwaanĩte kana ndatwaanĩte, nũtonya 'kwia ũtee kĩla kĩũmũvata kũthi kyonthe' na aimũthũkũma Ngai ateũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ maũndũ maingĩ. Nĩ kana twĩke ũu, no nginya tũekane na maũndũ amwe ala matwanangĩaa ĩvinda na tũyĩka mũvango wa kwongela ĩvinda yĩla tũtũmĩaa ũthũkũminĩ wa Ngai.
17 Kwasũanĩa Mark na kĩveti kyake Claire, ala maumĩte nthĩ ya Wales. Elĩ nĩmoosie ũvainia ĩla maminie sukulu na maendeea na ũthũkũmi ũsu ĩtina wa kũtwaana. Mark easya: "Nĩ kana tũtw'ĩke athũkũmi ma nthĩ yonthe, nĩtwatee nyũmba yitũ ya lumu itatũ sya kũkoma na twatia wĩa witũ ũla twatethasya masaa manini kwa kyumwa." Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 20 mĩvĩtu, nĩmaendete nthĩ mbingĩ sya Africa nĩ kana matetheesye ana-a-asa kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ. Mavinda amwe meethĩawa me athelele ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwamasũvĩaa. Claire easya: "Twĩw'aa twĩ eanĩe vyũ nũndũ nĩtũtũmĩaa ĩvinda yitũ kĩla mũthenya ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova. Nĩtũtumĩte ndũũ na andũ aingĩ na vai kĩndũ tũte nakyo. Tũitonya kũelekany'a syĩndũ nini ila twatiie na ũtanu ũla tũkwataa nũndũ wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova ĩvinda yonthe." Aingĩ ala me ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe nĩmonete ũu. *
18. Nĩ makũlyo meva twaĩle kwĩkũlya?
18 Nao nata we? Ũtonya kwĩka ata wamanya kana yu ndwĩ na kĩthito kĩla weethĩawa nakyo maũndũnĩ ma Ũsumbĩ nũndũ wa kũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ maũndũ mate ma vata? No kwĩthĩwa kĩla kĩtonya kũũtethya no kwaĩlangya mũvango ũla wĩ naw'o wa kũsoma na kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Kĩlungu kĩla kĩatĩĩe nĩkĩkũelesya ũndũ ũsu.

^ kal. 17 O na ĩngĩ soma ngewa ya Hadyn na Melody Sanderson ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/03/2006 kĩlungunĩ kĩla kĩ na kyongo "Kujua Yaliyo Sawa na Kuyatenda." Nĩmatiie viasala wamaeteae ũtandĩthyo mwingĩ nthĩ ya Australia na malika ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe. Soma kĩla kyeekĩkie ĩla matheleilwe maithũkũma me amisonalĩ nthĩ ya India.

translation:
"Mary . . . sat at the Lord's feet, listening attentively to his word."—LUKE 10:39, 40.
NOTES: 40, 55
1, 2. Why did Jesus visit Martha, and what does it show about how Martha was as a person?
INDEED, Martha was a woman who lived in Bethany, wasn't she a sister of Lazarus and Miriam? Or perhaps you know her as the sister of Lazarus whom the Bible mentions individually when stating that Jesus visited him, Jesus visited and comforted her because of her brother's death, and the friend of Martha who is called Mary. (John 11:5; 19:25-27) So why did Jesus visit Martha?
2 Jesus went to Martha's house, and he found her busy and preoccupied. However, she was also deeply troubled. It seems that she wanted to know what Jesus was saying. And she wondered whether Jesus was the Messiah who had been foretold. (John 11:21-27) But apparently, Martha was not alone. One occasion that moved Jesus greatly was when he saw her weeping, and he learned that she had lost her brother Lazarus. He said: "Martha, don't you realize that I have come so that you may believe in me?" (Read Luke 10:38-42.) What can we learn from this?
MARTHA WAS PRIVILEGED TO HEAR
3, 4. Why did Mary choose "the good portion," and what did Martha come to appreciate? (See accompanying article on page 18.)
3 When Jesus chose to associate with both Martha and Mary, he took the opportunity to teach them important lessons. Mary realized that it was best to use that time wisely to learn from the great Teacher and to sit at his feet "listening attentively to his word." Martha failed to see this and thought Jesus should help her with her work.
4 In contrast to Martha, Mary devoted herself fully to listening to Jesus and learning from him, rather than being concerned about many things. She used that time well, and Jesus praised her for it, saying: "Martha, Martha, you are anxious and worried about many things, but only one thing is necessary." And he showed her that there were more important matters to attend to. Furthermore, Jesus knew that Mary was very fond of their brother Lazarus and told her: "Mary, Lazarus is seriously ill." Later, when he arrived, he found that Mary was already grieving, and he appreciated how quickly she responded when she heard that Jesus was coming to her. After about 60 years, the apostle John wrote: "Jesus loved Martha and her sister." (John 11:5) This shows that Martha came to benefit from her association with Jesus and that she proved to be a faithful woman who cherished Jehovah and continued to serve him zealously.
However, why do so many people today find it difficult to focus on what is most important in life?
5 What reasons cause many people to become preoccupied with material possessions and worldly pursuits, and what can help us to avoid doing so?
For years, many have found it hard to concentrate on spiritual things, yet they want to serve Jehovah. In recent decades, one group of American schoolteachers stated: "More and more distractions compete for our attention—newspapers, magazines, numerous gadgets, cassettes, videos, television… . Every day brings something new that makes it harder to concentrate. And often, people wonder whether this world is 'a world of distraction' or 'a world of enlightenment.'" The Watchtower magazine (English) of September 15, 1958, said: "Things that distract people can also lead them to continue progressing and to make further advancement." Isn't that true! And what causes so many of us to get caught up in unimportant things: Is it not because we allow ourselves to be influenced by the fast pace of life and remain absorbed in trivial matters?
TO COPE WITH THE DISTRACTIONS OF THIS WORLD
6. Do Jehovah's Witnesses use technology at all?
6 Every day, the global work of proclaiming God's Kingdom uses technology to some extent. For example, Jehovah's Witnesses use videos and dramas to present Bible accounts vividly. * Millions worldwide benefit from the video "The Greatest Man Who Ever Lived," which has been dubbed into many languages and continues to be popular. This video portrays the life of Jesus Christ as described in the Gospels. Furthermore, Jehovah's Witnesses use websites to share information about the Bible and reach millions globally. Increasingly, the Internet is used effectively to find information. This helps us to share the good news with people in remote areas and to spread the truth throughout the earth.
7. (a) How can using worldly things hinder our spirituality? (b) What can we do to stay focused on spiritual matters? (See accompanying article.)
7 The Bible warns us that using worldly things can hinder our spirituality. (Read 1 Corinthians 7:29-31.) It is wise for a Christian to spend less time on nonessential activities. These include pursuing hobbies, reading magazines or novels, watching television, spending excessive time socializing, getting involved in questionable pursuits, and indulging in frivolous pastimes. Other things that can consume our time and distract us are surfing the Internet, sending messages and emails, playing computer games, and attending numerous social events. * (Prov. 3:1, 6) By simplifying our lives and avoiding unnecessary activities, we can focus on what is truly important—our worship of Jehovah.—Read Ephesians 5:15-17.
8. Why should we simplify our lives?
8 Satan tries to influence people to pursue worldly interests and become distracted. The desire for wealth and possessions can lead to discontentment. (2 Tim. 4:10) We need to heed the advice: "Simplify your life." This means that each day we should examine whether we are prioritizing spiritual matters. Let us always put Jehovah first and avoid being influenced by materialistic desires, so that we will not be misled by "the love of money."—1 John 2:15-17.
KEEP YOUR SPIRITUALITY STRONG
9. What did Jesus know about his Father's timing, and how did he remain loyal?
9 In fact, Jesus entrusted Martha with information about his resurrection, yet he did not reveal everything to her. He knew that his Father had a specific time for him to be glorified. (Read Matthew 6:22, 33.) Jesus was concerned about pleasing his Father; he did not worry about having a home or possessions.—Luke 9:58; 19:33-35.
10. How did Jesus show that he trusted his Father's timing?
10 There were many things Jesus could have done to speed up the fulfillment of God's purpose. For example, he could have used his power to free people from sicknesses and disabilities, and he could have exposed the wickedness of the Jewish rulers and their supporters. But he asked himself, 'Will people truly come to worship God because of these miracles?' He replied: "I must go on preaching the good news of God's Kingdom to other cities too, because that is what I was sent to do." (Luke 4:42-44) Jesus understood that he needed to reach as many people as possible with the truth. And he continued traveling and teaching, even though some people opposed him and tried to hinder his work.—Luke 8:23; John 4:6.
11. Did Jesus ever get tired, and how did he deal with it?
11 On one occasion, Jesus spent much time teaching and healing, and when a man approached him and said, "Teacher, please help my son who is possessed," Jesus responded favorably. The crowd pressed around him, and someone said: "Who among you has a father or mother whom you would want to see healed?" Then he went on to teach them about the importance of putting God first.—Luke 12:13-15.
12, 13. (a) What motivated some Christians to eagerly seek out Jesus despite facing opposition? (b) Did Jesus feel frustrated when his ministry was interrupted?
12 Jesus deeply appreciated our need for comfort. (Matt. 26:38; John 12:27) He also knew that he had a vital work to accomplish and that his death was imminent. For example, on Nisan 9, 33 C.E., the day before the Passover, he entered Jerusalem riding on a donkey, and people joyfully greeted him as "the King who comes in Jehovah's name." (Luke 19:38) On that day, Jesus went directly to the temple and began driving out those who were turning it into a place of business, showing his zeal for God's house.—Luke 19:45, 46.
13 While among the crowds near the gate of Jerusalem, he was approached by some Greeks who had come up to worship during the festival. They asked Jesus to speak to them. But Jesus said that the hour had not yet come when he would be glorified. He explained that unless a grain of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains just a single grain. However, if it dies, it produces much fruit. This illustrated that his sacrificial death would bring blessings to mankind. He added: "If anyone desires to be a disciple of mine, let him disown himself and take up his torture stake and follow me." To help his disciples understand this, Jesus said: "The hour has come for the Son of man to be glorified." (John 12:20-26)
14. So why did Jesus say that he was distressed about having to face death, and what does this teach us about how we can cope with difficulties?
14 So why did Jesus explain that he was dreading the prospect of facing death, and what does this teach us about how we can cope with difficulties? For example, think of those who have been deeply disappointed because they were wrongly accused. They often feel helpless and frustrated, like being trapped in a tight place. (John 2:2, 6-10) We too can strengthen our faith by meditating on examples of faithful men and women who endured trials. (Luke 5:29; John 12:2) In fact, Jesus frequently withdrew to solitary places to pray, to recover, and to refresh himself.—Matt. 14:23; Mark 1:35; 6:31, 32.
"LET US MAKE THE MOST OF EVERY OPPORTUNITY"
15. What practical lesson did the apostle Paul emphasize, and why is it important for us to heed his counsel today?
15 The apostle Paul zealously defended the Christian ministry, encouraging others to preach and to serve Jehovah, and he said: "Let us make the most of every opportunity." (Read Hebrews 12:1.) Paul personally made great efforts to reach people throughout the Roman Empire, traveling extensively despite hardships and dangers. He was determined to declare "the good news" and used every available means to spread the truth to such places as Syria, Asia Minor, Macedonia, and Greece. Paul wrote that he was willing to endure "toilsome things" and that he continued to strive for "greater things," so that he might be approved to God. (Acts 1:10; 3:8, 13, 14) And just as Paul persevered, we can use our time wisely and 'be zealous in our ministry.'—1 Cor. 7:32-35.
16, 17. Whether we are able to devote much time to the ministry or only a limited amount of time, how can we imitate Paul's example?
Let us see.
16 Like Paul, some dedicated servants of God choose to remain unmarried or they may forgo marriage so that they can give more attention to their ministry. (Matt. 19:11, 12) Many dedicated servants of God who are married also find ways to balance family life with full-time service. Regardless of whether one is single or married, he can strive 'to make the most of every opportunity' and show appreciation to God through increased activity. If we do so, we will likely identify specific areas where we can expand our ministry and align our activities with God's priorities.
17 Consider Mark and his wife Claire, who live in Wales. They both grew up in families who valued education and supported their pursuit of spiritual goals. Mark explains: "If we had focused on pursuing careers throughout our lives, we would have been limited to just one way of serving and would have missed out on many blessings." For over 20 years, they served as missionaries in Africa, helping people learn about God's Kingdom. Some of those experiences deeply touched their hearts and strengthened their love for Jehovah. Claire says: "We realize how much we benefit from using our time to support Jehovah's work. We enjoy associating with many fine people and feel satisfied with what we accomplish. We don't need extravagant things; we are happy with the peace of mind that comes from knowing that we are pleasing Jehovah fully." Many others share this view. *
18 What can we do to improve?
18 And how about you? Are you willing to examine yourself honestly and identify areas where you could make improvements spiritually? Don't hesitate to seek help when needed and take advantage of opportunities to read and study the Bible regularly. Are you willing to do that? Every small effort will be beneficial.

text:
"Ti ma nthĩ."—YOA. 17:16.
MBATHI: 18, 54
1, 2. (a) Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata Aklĩsto mekale malũmanĩtye na Ngai, na kĩu kĩtonya kũtũtethya ata ĩla kwaumĩla ngusanĩsyo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Andũ aingĩ malũmanasya na maũndũ meva, ĩndĩ kĩu kĩtonya kũmaetee mathĩna meva?
KWĨTHĨWE kwĩ kaũ kana kũi kaũ, Aklĩsto ma w'o nĩmakomanaa na maũndũ mana ũkethĩa no manyuvaa melũmany'a na Ngai kana nĩ nthĩ ĩno. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ onthe ala meyumĩtye mamũthũkũme Yeova nĩmamwathie kana makalũmanasya nake, makamwenda, na kũmwĩw'a. (1 Yoa. 5:3) Kwondũ wa ũu nĩtwĩthĩawa na wendi wa kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Ngai o na twĩthwe twĩ va, kana twĩthĩwe twaeiwe ata, twasyaĩwe va, kana syĩthĩo sya kwitũ iilyĩ ata. Kũlũmany'a na Yeova na Ũsumbĩ wake nĩ kwa vata kwĩ kũlũmany'a na ũndũ ũngĩ o na wĩva. (Mt. 6:33) Kwoou Mũklĩsto ũlũmanĩtye na Yeova na Ũsumbĩ wake ndesa kwĩkwatany'a na moteti na ngusanĩsyo sya nthĩ ĩno.—Isa. 2:4; soma Yoana 17:11, 15, 16.
2 Andũ mate Ngũsĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa malũmanasya mũno na nthĩ yoo, mbaĩ yoo, syĩthĩo ila syĩ kwoo, kana timũ ĩla ĩthaũkĩaa nthĩ yoo. Thĩna nĩ kana kũlũmany'a na maũndũ asu nĩkũetete masindano na ngusanĩsyo, na mavinda angĩ nĩkũtumĩte andũ moaana kana o na makoaa mbaĩ nima. Ĩla kwaumĩla mathĩna ta asu, andũ nĩmatonya kwenda kũmamina maitũmĩa nzĩa syoo, methĩwe meĩka kũseũvĩĩsya maũndũ kana metia mamanangĩĩa. Na nũndũ ithyĩ twĩ andũ o ta ala angĩ, nzĩa ila meũtũmĩa nitonya kũtũtethya kana o ikatũetee mathĩna. O na ĩngĩ nũndũ Ngai oombie mũndũ e na ũtonyi wa kũvathũkany'a ũseo na ũthũku, mavinda angĩ nĩtũtonya kũthatw'a nĩ ũtwi ũla weekwa nĩ silikalĩ. (Mwa. 1:27; Kũt. 32:4) Kwoou-ĩ, twĩkaa ata ĩla twakomana na maũndũ ta asu? Nĩ laisi mũno tũkelikya maũndũnĩ asu na nũndũ wa ũu tũyĩyĩthĩa ngusanĩsyonĩ.
3, 4. (a) Nĩkĩ Aklĩsto matelikasya ngusanĩsyonĩ sya nthĩ? (b) Twĩneenea maũndũ meva ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Ĩla kwaumĩla ngusanĩsyo ũndũnĩ mũna, silikalĩ sya nthĩ nitonya kũingĩĩsya ala isumbĩkĩte melikye ngusanĩsyonĩ isu. Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto ma w'o mayĩsa kwĩka ũu. Tũyĩlikasya siasanĩ sya nthĩ ĩno, o na tũitũmĩaa mĩio ya kaũ. (Mt. 26:52) O na tũyĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla tũsesengwe nĩ mũndũ o na wĩva twambĩĩe kwona ta ve vandũ vamwe va nthĩ ĩno ya Satani vaseo kwĩ kũla kũngĩ. (2 Ako. 2:11) Nũndũ tũi ma nthĩ, tũyĩlikasya ngusanĩsyonĩ ila syaumĩla kũũ.—Soma Yoana 15:18, 19.
4 Amwe maitũ no kwĩthĩwa tene twaĩ na woni ũtaĩle ĩũlũ wa andũ ala angĩ, na nũndũ twĩ andũ me na naĩ no kwĩthĩwa o nayu twĩ na woni ũsu, o na kau no tũendeee kũtata tũũvetange. (Yel. 17:9; Aev. 4:22-24) Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, ĩsomo yĩĩ nĩyĩneeneete myolooto mĩna ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũekane vyũ na woni ta ũsu. Nĩtũũmanya ũndũ tũtonya kũmanyĩsya ilĩko sitũ na mawasya maitũ ma ngoo nĩ kana tũlũmany'e na Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai.
KĨLA KĨTUMAA TŨTELIKYA MAŨNDŨNĨ MA NTHĨ ĨNO
5, 6. O na kau nthĩ ĩla Yesũ watwĩe yaĩ na andũ aingĩ me kĩvathũkany'o, we ekalaa ata na nĩkĩ?
5 Ũkesa kũkwatwa nĩ ũndũ mũna na ũyaĩwa nĩ kĩla ũkwĩka, nũseo ũkekũlya-ĩ, 'Keka nĩ Yesũ wakwatwa nĩ ũndũ ũũ, we eka ata?' Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mbee nthĩ ĩla Yesũ watwĩe yaĩ na isio syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwaĩ Yutia, Kalilii, Samalia, na kũngĩ. Na Mbivilia nĩwetete kana andũ ala matwĩe isionĩ isu mayeew'anaa. (Yoa. 4:9) O na kwaĩ kĩvũthya katĩ wa Avalisi na Asatukai (Meko 23:6-9), katĩ wa aumya ma koti na andũ ala angĩ (Mt. 9:11), na katĩ wa ala masomethetw'e ĩla Mĩao na ala matasomethetw'e. (Yoa. 7:49) Na ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu, nthĩ ya Isilaeli yasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Alomi, na Aisilaeli mayendaa kũmona. Ĩndĩ o na kau Yesũ nĩwateteaa ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai na nĩweetĩkĩlaa kana ũtangĩĩo wumaa kwa Ayuti, ndaaĩsa kwĩkĩa vinya amanyĩw'a make mambĩĩe kwona ta aseo kwĩ ala angĩ. (Yoa. 4:22) Amekĩaa vinya mende andũ onthe ta atũi moo.—Luka 10:27.
6 Nĩkĩ Yesũ ũtaaĩkĩa andũ vinya melikye ngusanĩsyonĩ ila Ayuti maĩ nasyo? Nũndũ we na Ĩthe mayĩlikasya ngusanĩsyonĩ sya nthĩ ĩno. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ĩla Yeova woombie ala andũ elĩ ma mbee aitũmĩa Mwana wake, kĩeleelo kyake kyaĩ andũ asu masyaane mausũsye nthĩ yonthe. (Mwa. 1:27, 28) Na aimomba, amombie kwa nzĩa matonya kũsyaa andũ ma ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Nũndũ wa ũu, Yeova na Yesũ mayĩsaa kwona ta ve ũko ũmwe wa andũ mũseo kwĩ ũla ũngĩ, kana ta ve nthĩ na kĩthyomo kĩmwe kĩseo kwĩ kĩla kĩngĩ. (Meko 10:34, 35; Ũvu. 7:9, 13, 14) No nginya naitũ tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yoo ĩte maela.—Mt. 5:43-48.
7, 8. (a) Aklĩsto maĩle kwĩlikya ũndũnĩ wĩva? (b) Aklĩsto maĩle kwĩthĩwa mesĩ ata ĩũlũ wa mathĩna ma andũ?
7 Ĩndĩ nĩtwaĩle kwĩlikya ũndũnĩ ũmwe, naw'o ũkonetye ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova. Kwaumĩlile ngusanĩsyo ya mbee ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu mũũndanĩ wa Eteni ĩla Satani woonanisye atĩ Yeova ti tawe waĩle kũsumbĩka andũ. Kwoou yu no nginya kĩla mũndũ etw'ĩĩe nũũ ũla wonaa ta wĩkaa maũndũ nesa katĩ wa Ngai na Satani. Nũndũ wa ũu, ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ, We nũtw'ĩte kuma ngoonĩ kũlũmany'a na Yeova kwa kũatĩĩa mĩao yake na myolooto yake vandũ va kwĩka ũndũ ũkwenda? We nũĩkĩĩaa kana vai kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩkavetea andũ mathĩna eka Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai? Kana wonaa mũndũ e na ũtonyi wa kwĩtongoesya?—Mwa. 3:4, 5.
8 Ũndũ wasũngĩa makũlyo asu no kũũtetheesye kũmanya ũndũ ũtonya kũsũngĩa ĩla andũ maũkũlya woni waku ĩũlũ wa kĩndũ kĩ na ngusanĩsyo. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũũ: Kuma tene andũ ma siasa, andũ ala mateteaa andũ na syĩndũ, vamwe na ala mendaa kũete moalyũku kũũ nthĩ nĩmatatĩte mũno kũmina ngusanĩsyo katĩ wa andũ. No kwĩthĩwa mekaa ũu na ngoo ntheu na mate na kĩeleelo kĩthũku. Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto nĩmesĩ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wĩ w'oka now'o ũtonya kũveta mathĩna, na now'o ũtonya kũatĩĩa nesa vyũ ũsili wa katĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, kĩndũ kyonthe kĩ na ngusanĩsyo twaĩle kũkĩekanĩsya na Yeova. Na nengĩ vakatw'ĩka ĩla kwaumĩla ngusanĩsyo kĩla Mũklĩsto akendaa maũndũ mekwe kwosana na kĩla ũkwona kĩ kĩseo, we tyo ũkwona kana ikundi iaanĩka mĩtũkĩ mũno?
9. Nĩ thĩna wĩva waĩ kĩkundinĩ kya Kolintho kĩla kyaĩ ĩvinda ya atũmwa, na mũtũmwa Vaulo akĩnengie ũtao wĩva?
9 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Aklĩsto amwe ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa meekie ĩla vaumĩlile ngusanĩsyo kĩkundinĩ kyoo kya Kolintho. Amwe kĩkundinĩ kyu maasya: "Nyie nĩ wa Vaulo; nakwa nĩ wa Avolo; nakwa nĩ wa Keva; nakwa nĩ wa Klĩsto." O na methĩwe maneenaw'a ũu nĩ kyaũ, Vaulo ndaaendeew'a nĩ kĩla kyaumĩlilw'e nĩ ũndũ ũsu. Amakũlilye ũũ: "Klĩsto nĩ mũaan'ye?" Kyo nĩ kyaũ kyaĩ kĩtonya kũmatethya maekane na mosũanĩo asu maĩ matonya kũete ngusanĩsyo? Vaulo amekĩie vinya kwa kũmea atĩĩ: "Yu nĩmwĩsũva, ana-a-asa, syĩtwanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi waitũ Yesũ Klĩsto, nĩ kana inyw'onthe mũneene ũndũ o ũmwe, na nĩ kana kũikethĩwe ũtilĩkangano katĩ wenyu; ĩndĩ nĩ kana mũlũmanw'e vamwe kĩsũanĩonĩ kĩmwe na mũĩkĩanĩonĩ ũmwe." O ta ũu kũyaĩle kwĩthĩwa mũtilĩkangano o na ũmwe nthĩnĩ wa kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto.—1 Ako. 1:10-13; soma Alomi 16:17, 18.
10. Mũtũmwa Vaulo anenganie ngelekany'o yĩva nĩ kana ony'e Aklĩsto kana mayaĩle kwĩlikya ngusanĩsyonĩ sya nthĩ ĩno?
10 Vaulo eekĩie vinya Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta masũanĩe mũno wĩkalo woo wa ĩtunĩ vandũ va kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma kũũ nthĩ. (Avi. 3:17-20) * Maaĩle kwĩkua ta atũmwa kwondũ wa Klĩsto. Mũndũ ũla watũmwa nĩ silikalĩ ya nthĩ yake akekale nthĩ ĩngĩ vandũ vayo ndelikasya siasanĩ na mathĩnanĩ ma nthĩ ĩsu watũmwa. Ekalaa alũmanĩtye na silikalĩ ya kwoo. (2 Ako. 5:20) O namo Aklĩsto ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ me ungu wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, na kwoou mayaĩle kwĩlikya ngusanĩsyonĩ sya nthĩ ĩno.
ĨMANYĨSYE KWĨKALAA ŨLŨMANĨTYE NA YEOVA
11, 12. (a) Nĩ vandũ vailyĩ ata Mũklĩsto ũtonya kũsyaĩwa ũkethĩa ti laisi akekala alũmanĩtye na Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai? (b) Mũklĩsto ũmwe akwatiwe nĩ thĩna wĩva, na eekie ata?
11 Wathi kũndũ kwingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩwĩthĩaa andũ mekalaa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu. Mekalaa ũu nũndũ nĩ ma wumo ũmwe, kĩthĩo kĩmwe, na kĩthyomo kĩmwe. Namo nĩmatanĩaa ũndũ ũsu mũno. No nginya Aklĩsto ala masyaĩwe kũndũ ta kũu mamanyĩsye ilĩko syoo na mawasya moo ma ngoo kwĩka ũtwi ũla waĩlĩte ĩla kwaumĩla kĩndũ kĩ na ngusanĩsyo. Matonya kwĩka ũu ata?
12 Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya Mirjeta, * ũla wasyaĩwe kĩsionĩ kya nthĩ ĩla tene yeetawa Yugoslavia. Eanie esĩ kana andũ ma Serbia nĩ nthũ. Ĩndĩ ĩla wamanyie kana Yeova ndendeeasya mbaĩ ĩmwe kwĩ ĩngĩ na kana Satani nĩwe wendaa andũ mamene mbaĩ ila ingĩ, nĩweekĩie kĩthito avete mosũanĩo ala waĩ namo. Ĩndĩ o na ekĩte oou, ĩla mbaĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o kũu kwoo syambĩĩe kũkita, kĩmena kĩla waĩ nakyo tene nĩkyookĩlile na weethĩa nũkũemwa nĩ kũtavya andũ ma Serbia ũvoo mũseo. Ĩndĩ Mirjeta nĩweesĩ kana ndatonya kwĩkala mana eteele mawoni asu waĩ namo mathele oou atekĩte ũndũ. Nũndũ wa ũu nĩwamwĩkaĩlile Yeova amũtetheesye asinde thĩna ũsu, na aimũtetheesya ongelange ĩvinda yĩla watũmĩaa kũmũthũkũma na nĩ kana atw'ĩke vainia. Mirjeta easya ũũ: "Nĩsĩte kwĩthĩa kana kũtũnga kĩlĩko kyakwa ũtavany'anĩ nĩw'o ũtethyo mũnene kwakwa. Ĩla ngũtavany'a nĩnĩtataa nĩthĩwe na nguma ta sya Yeova, na nũndũ wa ũu nĩnonete mosũanĩo ala naĩ namo maithela."
13. (a) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva watumaa mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe ekala ate mwĩanĩe, na eekie ata? (b) Maũndũ ala mamũkwatie Zoila metũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
13 Sũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩngĩ ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Zoila, ũla wasyaĩwe Mexico. Nĩwathamie kũu na yu ombanaa kĩkundi kĩ Europe. Ĩndĩ esie kwĩthĩa kana kĩkundinĩ kĩu vaĩ ana-a-asa amwe masyaĩwe nthĩ imwe sya Latin America maĩ na mũneenele ũte mũseo na wĩ na kĩvũthya ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩla wasyaĩwe, vamwe na syĩthĩo ila syĩ kwoo na mwinĩle woo. Keka nue Zoila wĩka ata? Mũneenele wa ana-a-asa asu nĩwatumaa Zoila ekala ate mwĩanĩe, na nĩtũkũelewa nĩkĩ. Ĩndĩ ũseo nĩ kana Zoila nĩwamũvoyie Yeova amũtetheesye ndakathate ngoonĩ. O ta mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu, tũyĩsa kũlea kana amwe maitũ me na thĩna ta ũsu maendeee kũtata maũkĩlye vinya. Naitũ tũyenda kwĩsa kũweta kĩndũ kana kwĩka ũndũ ũtonya kũete mũaanĩko, kana ũtonya kũtuma andũ amwe moneka ta aseo kwĩ ala angĩ, twĩthĩwe twĩ na ana-a-asa kana twĩ na andũ angĩ.—Alo. 14:19; 2 Ako. 6:3.
14. Nĩ kana Mũklĩsto onae andũ ũndũ Yeova ũmonaa, atonya kũmanyĩsya ata kĩlĩko kyake na wasya wake wa ngoo?
14 Kwasũanĩa makũlyo aa: No kwĩthĩwa vala wumĩte na andũ ala wĩanĩte namo monaa kĩsio kyoo kana nthĩ yoo yĩ nzeo kwĩ ila ingĩ? No kwĩthĩwa we mwene wĩw'aa ũu ngoonĩ? Aklĩsto mayaĩle kwĩsa kwona ta ve kĩsio kana nthĩ ĩmwe nzeo kwĩ ĩla ĩngĩ. Ĩndĩ nata ũkethĩa kana wĩ na woni ũte mũseo ĩũlũ wa andũ ma nthĩ ĩngĩ, kĩthyomo kĩngĩ, ũko ũngĩ, kana ala mataatĩĩaa syĩthĩo ila syĩ kwenyu? Ũkethĩa ũilyĩ ũu, nũseo ũkasũanĩa mũno ũndũ Yeova wonaa ala mamenete andũ mate ma kwoo. O na ĩla ũkwĩmanyĩsya wĩ weka kana mwĩ na ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ, no ũtetheke mũno weeka ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa woni wa Yeova maũndũnĩ asu. Na ĩndĩ mũthya no ũmũvoye Yeova aũtetheesye wĩthĩwe na woni ta wake.—Soma Alomi 12:2.
15, 16. (a) Twalũmany'a na Ngai, andũ ala angĩ makeekanaa naitũ ata? (b) Asyai matonya kũtetheesya ata syana syoo ĩla syathĩnw'a nũndũ wa kũlũmany'a na Ngai?
15 Vai ĩvinda athũkũmi ma Yeova mateyĩthĩĩla thĩnanĩ ũtonya kũtuma mawasya moo ma ngoo mamasukuma meke kĩvathũkany'o na andũ ala angĩ. Mavindanĩ ta asu nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa me sukulu, kana me na anyanyae moo, atũi, andũ ma mũsyĩ, kana andũ angĩ. (1 Vet. 2:19) Ĩndĩ o na kwĩthĩwe kũilyĩ ata, no nginya twĩke kĩvathũkany'o na andũ ala angĩ. Tweeka ũu, tũyaĩle kũseng'a twoona andũ ma nthĩ maitũmena nũndũ Yesũ nĩwawetie kana nthĩ ĩkatũmena. Aingĩ matũmenaa mayĩsĩ nĩkĩ ithyĩ twonaa wĩ ũndũ mũnene kũlũmany'a na Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai vandũ va kũlũmany'a na silikalĩ sya nthĩ. Ĩndĩ ithyĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kana kũlũmany'a na Ũsumbĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwitũ.
16 Nĩ kana tũlũmany'e na Yeova, no nginya twĩthĩwe twĩ alũmu vyũ ĩla twatelemw'a. (Nda. 3:16-18) O na kau vai mũndũ ũtakwatwa nĩ wia wa andũ, amũika mũno mũno nĩmatonya kũemwa nĩ kwĩka maũndũ mataatĩĩe mwĩmbĩsĩ. Kwoou ethĩwa wĩ na syana iũthĩnw'a nũndũ wa kũlea kũkũnĩa kĩvendela saluti kana kũlea kwĩlikya sikũkũnĩ sya nthĩ, osa ĩtambya na mĩtũkĩ ũitetheesye. Ĩka Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũitetheesya ielewe nĩkĩ iũkwata thĩna ũsu. Weeka ũu nitonya kũsinda thĩna ũsu ite na wia. Itetheesye imanye ũndũ itonya kwĩyĩelesya nesa, na kwa nzĩa yĩ na ndaĩa. (Alo. 1:16) Na nĩ kana ũitetheesye mũnango, no wose ĩtambya ya kũneena na alimũ masyo ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu ethĩwa ve vata wa kwĩka ũu.
TANĨAA KYONTHE KĨLA YEOVA WOOMBIE!
17. Nĩ woni wĩva tũtaĩle kwĩthĩwa naw'o, na nĩkĩ?
17 Mavinda angĩ nĩtwĩw'aa tũyendeew'a nĩ ũndũ nthĩ ĩla tũeewe ĩilyĩ, syĩthĩo sya kwitũ, kĩthyomo kitũ, kana o lĩu ũla wendetwe kwitũ. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũeleeka. Ĩndĩ no nginya tũtate ũndũ tũtonya tũikethĩwe na woni ta wa andũ ala maasya, "Kakwa no ko kaseo." Yeova oombie syĩndũ mbingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nĩ kana tũitanĩe. (Sav. 104:24; Ũvu. 4:11) Kwoou ve vata mwaũ wa kwonaa kĩsũanĩo kyaku takyo kĩseo kwĩ kya ala angĩ?
18. Nĩkĩ nũseo tũkethĩwa na woni ta wa Yeova ĩũlũ wa andũ ala angĩ?
18 Ngai endaa andũ ma mĩthemba yonthe mamanye ũla w'o na mayĩsa kũtanĩa thayũ ũtathela. (Yoa. 3:16; 1 Tim. 2:3, 4) Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩtũtethekaa mũno na tũkasũvĩa ngwatanĩo yitũ ya Kĩklĩsto tweethĩwa na wendi wa kwĩthukĩĩsya mawoni ma andũ ala angĩ. O na ĩngĩ twenda kwĩkala tũlũmanĩtye na Yeova, no nginya tũtate vyũ tũikelikye ngananĩonĩ sya andũ ma nthĩ. Katĩ wa andũ ma Yeova vai mwanya wa mũndũ ũkũmena ala angĩ. Kwondũ wa ũu nĩtũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ nũtũtetheesye ũkethĩa tũi na ngusanĩsyo, mĩtũlyo, na masindano ta andũ ma nthĩ ĩno ya Satani. Nĩtũtatei ĩndĩ twĩthĩwe na woni mũseo ta ũla waĩ na mũandĩki ũũ wa Savuli waisye atĩĩ: "Sisyai, ũndũ ũseo ũnenevete na ũndũ ũseũvĩte ana-a-asa mekalan'ya vamwe me ũmwe!"—Sav. 133:1.
