translation:
"These are my words."—JOHN 17:16.
NOTES: 18, 54
1, 2. (a) Why is it important for Christians to remain separated from the world, and how can this help us to avoid being influenced by bad associations? (Consider the example mentioned.) (b) Many people struggle with wrong desires. How can we resist them?
TO stay close to God, Christians must distance themselves from things that could weaken their spirituality or lead them away from Jehovah. But why? Because the more we associate with Jehovah and his worship, the more we love him, obey him, and appreciate him. (1 John 5:3) So, whether we feel tempted to compromise our standards, or whether we are already involved in wrongdoing, or even if we are simply enjoying questionable entertainment, cultivating our relationship with Jehovah and giving him first place in our lives will help us to make right decisions. (Matt. 6:33) A Christian who loves Jehovah and his Kingdom will want to avoid getting mixed up in the problems and conflicts of this world.—Isa. 2:4; read John 17:11, 15, 16.
2 People may be tempted to become involved in worldly affairs because of ambition, fear, curiosity, or just habit. However, pursuing such interests can lead to stress and conflict, and often involves competing with others or compromising principles. While some may seem harmless, certain pursuits can easily consume our time and energy, distracting us from spiritual activities. Moreover, even seemingly innocent forms of entertainment can influence our thinking and desires. And while we may feel that we can handle worldly influences, they can still affect us negatively. Furthermore, God wants each person to use his faculty of reason and exercise discernment. Often, we can protect ourselves by setting clear boundaries. (Gen. 1:27; Prov. 32:4) So, how can we maintain our neutrality? By making a conscious effort to separate ourselves from the world and focusing on spiritual matters.
3, 4. (a) Why did Jesus condemn the world? (b) What practical steps can we take?
3 While maintaining neutrality, it is important to remember that the world's standards can subtly influence our thinking and compromise our spirituality. Jesus Christ was able to remain detached. We should examine our values carefully and avoid unnecessary involvement. (Matt. 26:52) Also, we should be careful not to let others pressure us into doing things that violate Bible principles. (2 Cor. 2:11) Therefore, we need to be selective about what we allow into our minds.—Read John 15:18, 19.
4 Some people may find it difficult to resist temptation because of their upbringing or personality. And even those who have made progress may occasionally stumble. But we must continue striving to improve. (Jer. 17:9; Eph. 4:22-24) The more we study the Bible, the better equipped we will be to discern right from wrong. We will also come to appreciate Jehovah's view of things and strengthen our resolve to live according to His standards.
EVERY TRANSLATION HELPS US TO MAINTAIN NEUTRALITY
5, 6. What questions might arise when we see Jesus associating with imperfect people, and why?
5 It is easy to judge others, especially when they do something we disapprove of. So you might ask yourself, "If Jesus associated with such people, would I do the same?" Why? Because Jesus willingly associated with all sorts of people. For example, he spoke with Zacchaeus, Nicodemus, Samaritans, and many others. The Bible shows that he showed kindness to many who were considered outcasts. (John 4:9) He also conversed with Pharisees and Sadducees (Acts 23:6-9), tax collectors and sinners (Matt. 9:11), and those who had been demonized (Luke 7:49). Furthermore, the nation of Israel was once favored by God, yet its people often proved unfaithful. In fact, Jesus went out of his way to preach the good news to Samaritans and demonstrated genuine interest in their worship, despite the prejudice against them. (John 4:22) He treated everyone with dignity.—Luke 10:27.
6 So why did Jesus show compassion to people whom most Jews despised? One reason is that Jehovah loves all mankind and sent his Son to be a ransom for everyone. (Gen. 1:27, 28) And he wants us to reflect his love by showing compassion to all people, regardless of their background. Therefore, both Jehovah and Jesus can see beyond our imperfections and appreciate what we are trying to do, even if we don't always succeed. (Acts 10:34, 35; Rev. 7:9, 13, 14) Let us therefore imitate their attitude.—Matt. 5:43-48.
7, 8. (a) What should Christians strive to avoid? (b) How can Christians show impartiality in everyday life?
7 One way we can avoid taking sides is by remembering that doing so would offend Jehovah greatly. By remaining neutral, we show that we support God's side, unlike Satan, who tries to turn people against Jehovah. This will help each one of us to maintain a clear conscience and to take a firm stand on the issue between God and Satan. In this regard, ask yourself: 'Am I determined to strengthen my relationship with Jehovah by obeying his commands and following his principles?' Or 'Do I allow personal preferences to influence my decisions and cloud my judgment?'—Gen. 3:4, 5.
8 The more seriously we view neutrality, the easier it will be to remain neutral when faced with difficult situations. Consider this example: There are nations that are divided, some citizens supporting one side and others another, and still others refusing to participate because they feel it is wrong. It takes courage to stick to your convictions despite pressure from family and friends. As Christians, we know that God's Kingdom is the only solution to mankind's problems, and that it will soon resolve matters justly. Therefore, everything involving politics should motivate us to draw closer to Jehovah. And if we do so, will we not appreciate the value of maintaining our neutrality and avoiding involvement in worldly affairs?—Rom. 13:1.
9 What valuable counsel does Paul give regarding Christian neutrality in his first letter to the Corinthians, and how did he himself act in harmony with that counsel?
9 Paul explains that Christians should maintain their neutrality in order to please God. However, some were saying: "We belong to Paul"; "I belong to Apollos"; "I belong to Cephas"; "I belong to Christ." But Paul showed that such divisions were unwise, stating that he himself was simply a servant who had been entrusted with delivering God's message. He asked: "Did Christ get divided?" This question highlights the absurdity of dividing oneself along human lines and failing to maintain unity. Paul firmly stated: "God is not a God of confusion, but a God of peace." He urged them to all speak in agreement and to be united in thought.—1 Cor. 1:10-13; read Rom. 16:17, 18.
10 How did the apostle Paul demonstrate the importance of remaining neutral, and what can we learn from his example?
10 Paul clearly showed that Christians should not align themselves with any particular leader or party within the congregation. (Acts 3:17-20) * They should instead support Christ's brothers. The one sent forth by Christ represents his person and will accomplish his work, while those supporting him show loyalty to Christ. He is united with the one who sent him. (2 Cor. 5:20) Moreover, Christ has the backing of Jehovah God, and thus supporting Christ means supporting God's organization.
MAINTAINING LOYALTY TO JEHOVAH
11, 12. (a) What quality does a true Christian need to cultivate in order to remain loyal to Jehovah's organization? (b) One Christian faced a difficult situation, and how did she respond?
11 In many lands today, people are being influenced by strong nationalistic sentiments. They feel a sense of unity, belonging, and purpose. But this can be dangerous. So let Christians be careful not to become overly involved in politics and to avoid taking sides. How can they do this?
12 Consider the example of Mirjana, * who grew up in what was then Yugoslavia. She explains that many Serbs felt strongly about their nation. They believed that Jehovah allowed them to conquer others and that Satan led those who opposed them. This belief caused much hatred and violence. She adds: "I realized that I could easily get caught up in that spirit of nationalism, and I saw how it blinded people, making them cruel and unforgiving. It made me determined not to allow myself to be carried away by such feelings." Mirjana understood that she needed to remain neutral and that pleasing Jehovah required her to love all people, regardless of their nationality. She said: "I want to make it clear that I do not support any kind of hatred or revenge. My only desire is to serve Jehovah and to live according to his principles."
13. (a) What can cause a young person to feel nationalistic, and what can happen as a result? (b) What experiences helped Zoila to appreciate this?
13 Let us consider another example, that of a young woman named Zoila, who grew up in Mexico. She moved to Europe with her parents. At first, she found it difficult to adjust because the congregation there included brothers and sisters from various parts of Latin America, and they had different customs and ways of doing things. But gradually, she came to appreciate the unity among God's people. Zoila recalls: "It helped me to realize that my own background wasn't the most important thing. I learned to value our international brotherhood." She also realized that Zoila had prayed to Jehovah for help to overcome her nationalistic feelings. Like many young people, we may find it challenging to resist pressure from family or friends to adopt nationalistic views. So we need to cultivate a strong desire to please Jehovah and to see people as he does—with love and compassion.—Prov. 14:19; 2 Cor. 6:3.
14. How can a Christian show that he respects Jehovah's view of people?
14 Consider this scenario: You are assigned to work alongside people from a different culture. Do you focus on their differences or on what you have in common? Do you try to understand their perspective? Christians should strive to see others as Jehovah sees them. It is natural to be curious about the customs and traditions of people from other lands, but do not let such curiosity lead to prejudice or discrimination against anyone. Instead, let us imitate the example set by Jesus and his apostles.—Read Proverbs 12:2.
15, 16. (a) How can we broaden our understanding of people? (b) What benefits can come from striving to understand others?
15 Jehovah has created a wide variety of people, and he wants us to reach out to them with the good news. We may encounter people from different backgrounds at school, at work, through our neighbors, in our congregations, or elsewhere. (1 Pet. 2:19) But even if we have had negative experiences, we should continue to seek opportunities to get to know others. By doing so, we demonstrate love for our brothers and sisters, and we please Jehovah. Many people are deeply affected by their upbringing and find it difficult to accept new ideas. However, when they sense genuine interest and respect, they are more likely to listen. For some, coming to appreciate Bible truth may require overcoming deeply ingrained prejudices. So, let us remember that broadening our understanding of people is an important way to show love.
16 If we love Jehovah, we will want to share his message with those around us. (Ps. 3:16-18) Often, people who seem unfriendly are simply struggling with personal problems. They may be burdened by worries or facing difficult circumstances. Therefore, let us try to understand their perspective and offer encouragement. Instead of being quick to judge, let us patiently help them see how Bible principles can address their concerns. The Holy Spirit can empower us to speak in a way that touches their heart. By showing genuine concern, we can build trust and open the way for meaningful conversations. (Prov. 1:16) And if someone rejects our message, we can still maintain a respectful attitude and leave a positive impression.
LET US ALL PRAISE JEHOVAH TOGETHER!
17. Why should we make an effort to get to know others, and how can we do so?
17 Many people are willing to listen when we show a sincere interest in them—their joys, their challenges, their families, or their work. Showing such interest demonstrates that we value them as individuals. We can then ask questions about their beliefs and respectfully explain why we believe what we do. Jehovah appreciates our efforts to reach out to others, even if they initially appear uninterested. (Ps. 104:24; Eccl. 4:11) How can we show empathy and understanding toward those who have different viewpoints?
18. What motivates us to share the good news with others?
18 God loves all mankind and wants everyone to gain life everlasting. (John 3:16; 1 Tim. 2:3, 4) Therefore, we strive to imitate Christ's example and preach the good news so that people everywhere may have an opportunity to learn about Jehovah's Kingdom. And as we remain close to Jehovah, we will be moved to help others appreciate the hope that we have. Jehovah values those who use their time and energy to defend the truth against the influence of Satan and his world. So let us continue to support one another in this important work, just as the psalmist wrote: "How good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity!"—Ps. 133:1.

text:
"Kĩla mũndũ wenyu nakyende kĩveti kyake o ũndũ wĩyendete mwene; na kĩveti nĩkĩmũkĩe mũũme."—AEV. 5:33.
MBATHI: 36, 3
1. O na kau ala meũtwaana nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa na ũtanu, nĩ kyaũ maĩle kwĩthĩwa mesĩ kana nĩkĩtonya kũmakwata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
ĨLA mũtwawa waumĩla mũthenya wa alũsi na mũtwaani amwona, ũtanu ũla wĩthĩawa vo nĩ mwingĩ mũno. Wendo woo ĩvinda ya kwĩvaany'a wĩthĩawa waingĩvie ũkethĩa yu nĩmeyũmbanĩtye kwĩvĩta mekalany'e me aĩkĩĩku. O na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩmaĩle kwĩka moalyũku nĩ kana mekalany'e nesa mamina kũtwaana. Ndeto ya Ngai nĩnenganĩte ũtao mũseo kwa onthe ala mekwenda kũtwaana, nũndũ Mwambĩlĩlya wa mũtwaano endaa kĩla ũmwe ethĩwe na ũtanu na mũtwaano woo ũyĩthĩwa wĩ mũseo. (Nth. 18:22) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, Maandĩko nĩmonanĩtye nesa kana andũ ala matwaana "maitĩa kwĩthĩwa na mathĩna mwĩĩnĩ." (1 Ako. 7:28) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũmatetheesya maikaemeewe nĩ mathĩna asu? Na nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma mũtwaano wĩthĩwa wĩ mũseo?
2. Ala matwaanĩte maĩle kwĩthĩwa na mĩthemba yĩva ya wendo?
2 Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye vata wa kwĩthĩwa na wendo. Ala matwaanĩte nĩmaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wendo mũuu (Kĩkiliki, phi·liʹa). Wendo ũla wĩthĩawa katĩ wa mũndũũme na mũndũ mũka (eʹros) nũtumaa mũtwaano wĩthĩwa na ũtanu, naw'o wendo katĩ wa andũ ma mũsyĩ (stor·geʹ) nĩ wa vata mũno ĩla mesa kwĩthĩwa na syana. Ĩndĩ wendo ũla wĩthĩawa ũtongoew'e nĩ myolooto (a·gaʹpe) nĩw'o ũtumaa mũtwaano wĩthĩwa wĩ mũseo. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa wendo ũsu: "Kĩla mũndũ wenyu nakyende kĩveti kyake o ũndũ wĩyendete mwene; na kĩveti nĩkĩmũkĩe mũũme."—Aev. 5:33.
MAŨNDŨ ALA KĨLA ŨMWE WAĨLE KWĨANĨSYA NTHĨNĨ WA MŨTWAANO
3. Andũ ala matwaanĩte maĩle kwĩthĩwa mendanĩte ata?
3 Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Aũme, endai iveti syenyu, o ũndũ Klĩsto wendie ĩkanisa, na enengane mwene kwondũ wayo." (Aev. 5:25) Nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ĩsu ya Yesũ kwa kwendana o tondũ we watwendie. (Soma Yoana 13:34, 35; 15:12, 13.) Kwoou, ala matwaanĩte nĩmaĩle kwendana mũno ũkethĩa kĩla ũmwe no akw'e kwondũ wa ũla ũngĩ. Ĩla mathĩna maito maumĩla mũtwaanonĩ andũ nĩmatonya kwĩw'a ta mate na wendo ũsu. O na ũu wĩ o vo, wendo ũla wĩtawa a·gaʹpe "nũvw'ĩkaa maũndũ onthe, nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa maũndũ onthe, nĩwĩkwatasya maũndũ onthe, nĩwũmĩĩasya maũndũ onthe." O na ĩngĩ, "wendo ndũnyivaa o na ĩndĩĩ." (1 Ako. 13:7, 8) Ĩla andũ matwaanĩte na mamũkĩaa Ngai malilikana kana nĩmeevĩtie kwendana na kwĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku mũtwaanonĩ woo, ũu no ũmatetheesye kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Yeova ĩla mekũkitana na mathĩna ala maumĩla.
4, 5. (a) Nĩ maũndũ meva maĩle kwĩanĩw'a nĩ mũndũũme ũla ũtwaanĩte? (b) Kĩveti kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa ũkũmũ wa mũũme? (c) Nĩ moalyũku meva mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mũka meethĩie no mekaa?
4 Vaulo nĩwaeleisye ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala kĩla ũmwe waĩle kwĩanĩsya mũtwaanonĩ. Aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Inyw'ĩ iveti, ĩnyivĩsyei aũme menyu ta mwĩnyivĩsye Mwĩaĩi. Nũndũ mũndũ mũũme nĩ mũtwe wa kĩveti, o tondũ Klĩsto nake nĩ mũtwe wa ĩkanisa." (Aev. 5:22, 23) Mũvango ũsu ndwonanasya kana kĩveti ti kya vata mũtwaanonĩ. Ĩndĩ ũkĩtetheeasya kwĩanĩsya ũndũ ũla Ngai wendaa iveti sianĩsye. Ngai aisye ũũ: "Ti ũseo mũndũ [Atamu] ethĩwe e weka; nĩngũmũmbĩa mũtetheesya ũmwaĩle." (Mwa. 2:18) Mũndũũme Mũklĩsto ũtwaanĩte aĩle kũtũmĩa ũkũmũ wake kwa nzĩa ya wendo o tondũ Klĩsto, ũla nĩ "mũtwe wa ĩkanisa," wĩkaa. Eeka ũu kĩveti kĩkeew'aa kĩ kĩanĩe na kĩikew'aa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kũmũnenga ndaĩa, kũmũkwata mbau, na kũmwĩnyivĩsya.
5 Mũndũ mũka ũmwe wĩtawa Cathy [1] aisye kana yaĩ no nginya eke moalyũku mana ĩtina wa kũtwawa. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩla ndaĩ mũtwae namanyĩĩte kwĩthĩnĩkĩa na neekaa maũndũ kwosana na ũndũ nĩvangĩĩe. Kwoou natwawa yaĩ no nginya nĩmanyĩsye kũmwĩthukĩĩasya mũemewa. Ũsu ndwĩthĩĩtwe wĩ ũndũ laisi, ĩndĩ nũndũ wa kwĩka maũndũ kwosana na myolooto ya Yeova nĩtwendene mũno." Nake mũũme wake, Fred, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kuma tene ndwaĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwakwa kwĩka motwi. Kwoou ĩla natwaanie waĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwĩka motwi kwondũ wa andũ elĩ. Ĩndĩ ve maũndũ mandetheesye ũndũnĩ ũsu, namo nĩ kũmũvoya Yeova andongoesye na kwĩthukĩĩsya mawoni ma kĩveti kyakwa. Yu twĩkaa maũndũ twĩ na ngwatanĩo vyũ!"
6. Ĩla mathĩna maumĩla mũtwaanonĩ, wendo ũtonya ata kwĩthĩwa "wovano wa wĩanĩu"?
6 Nĩ kana mũtwaano wĩthĩwe wĩ mũlũmu, ala matwaanĩte nĩmaĩle kũmanya kana kĩla ũmwe woo nĩwĩkaa mavĩtyo. Kwoou nĩ ũndũ wa vata "kũmĩĩasya ũmwe kwa ũla ũngĩ, na kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene." O tondũ twoona, elĩ nĩmatonya kũvĩtya. Ĩndĩ ĩla ũu weethĩwa, no matũmĩe mwanya ũsu kwĩmanyĩsya kumana na mavĩtyo moo, kũekeanĩa, na maieka wendo katĩ woo wĩthĩwe "wovano wa wĩanĩu." (Ako. 3:13, 14) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana "wendo nĩwũmĩĩasya, na nĩwĩkaa moseo; . . . na ndũtalĩlaa ũthũku." (1 Ako. 13:4, 5) Ethĩwa nĩmaema kũeleanwa nĩmaĩle kũmina ũndũ ũsu mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka. Kwoou Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte nĩmaĩle kũtata kũmina thĩna o na wĩva katĩ woo mũthenya ũtanathela. (Aev. 4:26, 27) Kwasya, "Nĩ vole nĩngũvĩtĩsye," nĩ ũndũ wendaa mũndũ ethĩwe na wĩnyivyo na ũkũmbaũ. Ĩndĩ kwĩka ũu nĩkũtetheeasya mũno kũmina mathĩna na kũtuma andũ ala matwaanĩte mendana mũno.
WENDO NA ŨUU NĨ SYA VATA MŨNO
7, 8. (a) Mbivilia ĩnengete andũ ala matwaanĩte ũtao wĩva ĩũlũ wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ? (b) Nĩkĩ andũ ala matwaanĩte maĩle kwĩkalany'a kwa wendo na ũuu?
7 Mbivilia nĩnenganĩte ũtao mũseo ũla ũtonya kũtethya ala matwaanĩte methĩwe na woni waĩle ĩũlũ wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. (Soma 1 Akolintho 7:3-5.) Nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũndũ na mũka kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mavata ma ngoonĩ ma kĩla ũmwe. Ethĩwa mũndũũme ndekalanasya na kĩveti kyake kwa wendo na kwa ũuu, nĩvatonyeka kĩveti kĩu kĩkaemwa nĩ kũtanĩa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. Aũme ala matwaanĩte meĩtwe mekalanasye na iveti syoo "kwĩanana na ũmanyi." (1 Vet. 3:7) Kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ ti ũndũ waĩle kũlasimĩthw'a mũndũ ĩndĩ nĩ ũndũ mũndũ waĩle kwĩka kwa ngenda. Mavinda maingĩ wendi wa mũndũũme wa kwenda kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ wũkĩlaa mĩtũkĩ kũte wa mũndũ mũka. Ĩndĩ nũseo ĩvinda yĩla mũndũ na mũka matw'a kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ yĩkethĩwa ne ĩvinda yĩla elĩ me na wendi ũsu.
8 Mbivilia ndĩwetete ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala mũndũ na mũka matonya kwĩka nĩ kana monany'e wendo mbee wa matanamba kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ na ĩla meũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ. Ĩndĩ nĩwetete maũndũ makonanĩtye na kwonany'a wendo ũsu. (Wa. 1:2; 2:6) Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte nĩmaĩle kwĩkalany'a kwa wendo na ũuu.
9. Nĩkĩ ti ũseo kwendeew'a nĩ mũndũ ũtatwaanĩte nake?
9 Ethĩwa nĩtũmwendete Ngai na tũkamwenda mũtũi witũ mũno, tũiketĩkĩlya ũndũ o na ũmwe ũtume mũtwaano wanangĩka. Mĩtwaano ĩmwe nĩyĩthĩĩtwe na thĩna kana o na ĩkanangĩka nũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa ala matwaanĩte e na kĩmanyĩo kya kwĩloela mavisa ma ũlaalai. Kwĩthĩwa ũyendeew'a nĩ mavisa ta asu kana kwendeew'a nĩ mũndũ ũtatwaanĩte nake nĩ maũndũ waĩle kwĩvathana namo vyũ. O na nĩwaĩle kwĩvathana vyũ na kũthaũkĩa mũndũ ũtatwaanĩte nake, nũndũ ũu wonanasya ndwendete ũla ũtwaanĩte nake. Kũmanya kana Ngai nĩwĩsĩ mosũanĩo maitũ na meko maitũ no kũtume tũtata ũndũ tũtonya tũmwendeesye na tũyĩkala twĩ atheu methonĩ make.—Soma Mathayo 5:27, 28; Aevelania 4:13.
ĨLA VEETHĨWA MATHĨNA NTHĨNĨ WA MŨTWAANO
10, 11. (a) Kũthasya mũtwaano kwongelekete ata? (b) Mbivilia yaĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa kũtaanĩsya? (c) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya ala matwaanĩte maikasembee kũtaanĩsya?
10 Ethĩwa mũtwaano nĩwaendeea kwĩthĩwa na mathĩna maito, kĩu no kĩtume ũmwe wa asu matwaanĩte kana o elĩ matw'a kũtaanĩsya kana kũthasya mũtwaano. Nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ imwe, mbee wa nusu ya andũ ala matwaana nĩmathaasya mũtwaano woo. Ũndũ ũsu ndwĩthĩawa mũno kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. Ĩndĩ mĩtwaano ya andũ ma Ngai nĩyĩsĩte kũlika mathĩna maingĩ na ũsu ti ũndũ waĩle kũvũthĩĩw'a.
11 Mbivilia ĩnenganĩte ũtao ũũ: "Mũndũ mũka ndakamũlee mũũme, (ĩndĩ ethĩwa nũnũũthi, nĩeyĩkalye ate mũtwae, kana ethĩwa ti ũu, ew'ane na mũũme wake;) na mũũme ndakamũlee mũka wake." (1 Ako. 7:10, 11) Kũtaanĩsya kũyaĩle kwoswa ta ũndũ wa ngũĩ. O na kau kũtaanĩsya nĩkũtonya kwoneka ta kũtonya kũmina mathĩna ala maumĩla, mavinda maingĩ ũu ũtumaa mathĩna mongeleka. Yesũ amina kũweta kana Ngai aisye mũndũũme akatia ĩthe na nyinyia na ailũmany'a na mũka, asyokie asya: "Ala Ngai ũlũmanĩtye ĩndĩ, mũndũ ndakaamataan'ye." (Mt. 19:3-6; Mwa. 2:24) Ũndũ ũsu wonanasya kana mũndũ na mũka mayaĩle kũtaanĩsya nũndũ makeka ũu methĩwa 'mataanany'a ala Ngai ũlũmanĩtye.' Yeova onaa ala matwaanĩte maĩle kwĩkalany'a thayũnĩ woo w'onthe. (1 Ako. 7:39) Kũmanya kana ala matwaanĩte makaumya ũtalo mbee wa Ngai nĩkwaĩle kũtuma mekĩa kĩthito kũmina mĩtũkĩ mathĩna ala maumĩla nĩ kenda maũndũ maikese kũthũkĩĩa.
12. Nĩ thĩna ta wĩva ũtonya kũtuma mũndũ enda kũtaanĩsya na mũũme kana mũka?
12 Mũtwaano nũtonya kũlika thĩna ethĩwa ala matwaanĩte meekwatĩtye kana mũtwaano woo ndũkaaĩthĩwa na mathĩna. Ethĩwa andũ nĩmatwaana na meethĩa mũtwaano woo ndwĩ na ũtanu ũla meekwatasya makeethĩwa naw'o, nĩmatonya kũkw'a ngoo, kana ũmwe woo akona ta weekie kũkengwa, o na nĩmatonya kũthatanĩa. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana, nũndũ vai mũndũ wĩw'aa ta ũla ũngĩ na tũeetwe kĩvathũkany'o, mathĩna nĩmatonya kũlika. O na mathĩna no maumĩle nũndũ wa mĩtũmĩĩle ya mbesa, athoni na andũ ma kwa mũũme, kana nzĩa ila matonya kũtũmĩa kũea syana syoo. Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto aingĩ nĩmaĩlĩte kũkathwa nĩkwĩthĩwa mo nĩmakwatĩanĩaa na makamina mathĩna onthe ta asu nũndũ wa kũmwĩkwatya Ngai amatongoesye.
13. Nĩ itumi syĩva nzeo itonya kũtuma ala matwaanĩte mataanĩsya?
13 Mavinda amwe ala matwaanĩte no methĩwe na itumi nzeo sya kũtaanĩsya. Maũndũ amwe maito matonya kũtuma andũ mataanĩsya nĩ ta aa: ethĩwa mũndũũme nĩwalea na ngũlũ kwĩanĩsya mavata ma andũ make, ethĩwa ve ũmwe ũkũũmĩw'a mũno kĩ-mwĩĩ, kana ethĩwa ve ũmwe wĩ mũisyonĩ vyũ kĩ-veva. Aklĩsto ala me na thĩna mũnene mũtwaanonĩ woo nĩmaĩle kwona atumĩa mamatetheesye. Atumĩa nĩ ana-a-asa me na ũmanyi na kwoou no matetheesye ala matwaanĩte makamanya kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya kũmina mathĩna nĩ kũmũvoya Yeova atũnenge veva wake, atũtetheesye tũatĩĩe ũtao wa Mbivilia, na aitũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na ũla ũsyao wa veva.—Aka. 5:22, 23. [2]
14. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva Mbivilia ĩtavĩtye Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte na andũ mate Ngũsĩ?
14 Kwĩ Aklĩsto amwe methĩawa matwaanĩte na andũ mate athũkũmi ma Yeova. Mbivilia nĩnengete Aklĩsto ta asu itumi nzeo sya kũendeea kwĩkalany'a na ala matwaanĩte namo. (Soma 1 Akolintho 7:12-14.) Mbee, nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa atwaanĩte na mũndũ mwĩtĩkĩli, ũla ũte mwĩtĩkĩli "nũvathĩkĩte," kana nũtheetw'e, ethĩwe nĩwĩsĩ ũu kana ndesĩ. Kelĩ, syana ila masyaĩte, Ngai aitalaa ta "ntheu" na kwoou nũtonya kũisũvĩa. Vaulo akũlilye: "Wĩsĩ ata we, kĩveti, kana ũkatangĩĩa mũemeu? kana wĩsĩ ata we, mũũme, kana ũkatangĩĩa mũkau?" (1 Ako. 7:16) Vakuvĩ kĩla kĩkundi wathi nĩwĩthĩaa Mũklĩsto watetheeisye mũka kana mũũme 'atangĩĩwa.'
15, 16. (a) Mbivilia ĩtaĩte ata Aklĩsto ala matwaĩtwe nĩ aũme matamũthũkũmaa Ngai? (b) Mũklĩsto aĩlĩte kwĩka ata "ethĩwa ũla ũtetĩkĩlĩte nũnũũthi"?
15 Mũtũmwa Vetelo nũtaĩte aka Aklĩsto akamea nĩmenyivĩsye aũme moo, "nĩ kana ethĩwa ve amwe mate ewi ma ĩla ndeto, matonye kwonw'a nĩ mwĩkalĩle wa iveti syoo vate ĩla ndeto; makyona mwĩkalĩle wenyu mũtheu wĩ na w'ĩa." Kĩveti kyeethĩwa na "veva wa wĩnyivyo na wa ũuu, ũla wĩ vata mũno mbee wa Ngai," no kĩtetheesye mũũme nesa vyũ akambĩĩa kũmũthaitha Yeova kũte ũndũ kĩkwĩsaa kũmũtetheesya takeka kĩtindĩaa kũmũtavya ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wa Kĩklĩsto.—1 Vet. 3:1-4.
16 Ĩndĩ vaĩle kũthi ata ũla ũte Ngũsĩ atw'a we nũkũtaanĩsya na mũka kana mũũme? Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte ũũ: "Ethĩwa ũla ũtetĩkĩlĩte nũnũũthi, nathi: mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtũ-a-asa ti ngombo maũndũnĩ mailyĩ ũu: ĩndĩ Ngai nũtwĩtĩte twĩkalae na mũuo." (1 Ako. 7:15) Mbivilia ndĩkwasya kana vathi ũu ũla Mũklĩsto no atwaane na ũngĩ. Kĩla ĩkũweta nĩ kana Mũklĩsto ndaĩle kũlasimĩthya ũla ũte mwĩtĩkĩli ekale ethĩwa nĩwenda kũthi. Nĩkĩ kĩtumi? Nũndũ kũtaanĩsya no kũmaetee mũuo. O na Mũklĩsto ũla watiwa no ekale ekwatĩtye kana mũthenya ũmwe mũka kana mũũme akamũsyokea e na wendi wa kũlũlũmĩĩlya mũtwaano woo. Na no kwĩthĩwa mũthenya ũmwe akatw'ĩka Ngũsĩ.
KĨLA KYAĨLE KWĨTHĨWA KĨ KYA VATA VYŨ MŨTWAANONĨ
17. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ala matwaanĩte maĩle kũeka wĩthĩwe new'o wa vata vyũ?
17 Tũtwĩe mũthyanĩ vyũ wa 'mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo,' ĩla yĩ na "mavinda ma mũisyo." (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Ĩndĩ tweethĩwa na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na Yeova, tũkeethĩawa tũtonya kũsinda matatwa ma nthĩ ĩno. Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: 'Ĩvinda nĩ ĩkuvĩvye mũno.' Na ĩndĩ asya: 'Kuma yu, ala me na aka nĩmethĩwe ta mataĩ; na ala metethasya na syĩndũ sya nthĩ, nĩmethĩwe ta matasyĩkwatasya mũno.' (1 Ako. 7:29-31) Ĩla Vaulo waisye ũu ndatavasya andũ kana maĩle kũeka kũũngana na ala matwaanĩte namo. Ĩndĩ ameaa kana nĩkwĩthĩwa ĩvinda nĩ ĩkuvĩvye mũno, maaĩlĩte kũeka ũthaithi wa Yeova wĩthĩwe new'o ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ.—Mt. 6:33.
18. Nĩkĩ no twasye kana Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte no mekale me atanu na mũtwaano woo ũiendeea nesa?
18 Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte no mekale me atanu na no maendeee nesa o na kũtw'ĩka ĩvinda yĩĩ tũĩ nĩ ĩthũku na mĩtwaano mingĩ nĩyanangĩkĩte. Vate nzika, "ala Ngai ũlũmanĩtye" no maendeee kwĩkala malũmanĩtye ethĩwa nĩmekũendeea kwĩthĩwa me ngwatanĩo na andũ ma Yeova, nĩmekũatĩĩa ũtao wa Maandĩko, na ethĩwa nĩmekũeka veva mũtheu wa Yeova ũmatongoesye.—Mko. 10:9.

"Every one of you should go back to his own home, and each one stay there; do not go out."—AEV. 5:33.
MBATHI: 36, 3
1. And so when someone is being reproved, will it help to be angry, or is it better to be calm or will it help to accept [correction]? (Consider the following points.)
IF a loving elder and a companion observe anger, that anger shows itself to be very bad. Such love encourages one to calmly accept reproof because he feels convinced about its correctness. And if this is true, it is better to listen carefully than to stubbornly refuse correction. God's purpose is to help everyone who wants to accept correction, and Jehovah lovingly gives each one opportunity to respond to reproof calmly. (Prov. 18:22) Indeed, as we have seen, the Scriptures show that others also "become mild when they are reproved." (1 Cor. 7:28) Is it possible to become mild despite our feelings? And is it possible to make reproof helpful?
2. Can companions find it difficult to be reproved?
2 The Bible shows the value of being reproved. Companions can find it difficult to be reproved with love (Greek, phi·liʹa). Love shown between husband and wife (eʹros) often leads to jealousy, and also the love among family members (stor·geʹ) is often limited to those closely related. But the love shown selflessly (a·gaʹpe) is what makes reproof helpful. The apostle Paul gave this principle of love: "Every one of you should go back to his own home, and each one stay there; do not go out."—AEV. 5:33.
OTHER THINGS EACH ONE CAN DO TO IMPROVE COMPANIONSHIP
3. Can companions sometimes feel resentful?
3 Paul wrote: "Husbands, continue loving your wives, just as Christ loved the congregation and gave himself up for it." (AEV. 5:25) We can show our appreciation for Jesus' example by loving one another. (Read John 13:34, 35; 15:12, 13.) Also, companions can strengthen their love for one another by thinking about the good qualities of the other. However, imperfections may cause companions to become irritated with one another, and without this love they might say things that hurt. But this kind of love, called a·gaʹpe, "is patient and kind. It does not become jealous, it does not brag, it does not act unbecomingly. It does not seek its own advantage." And further, "love never fails." (1 Cor. 13:7, 8) But companions who appreciate God may find it easier to forgive and to be reproved when necessary, because they want to please Jehovah and live up to his high standards.
4, 5. (a) What practical steps can companions take? (b) How can a wife support her husband as head of the family? (c) What lesson did one married couple learn?
4 Paul explained what each companion should do to strengthen their love. He wrote: "Let each one of you also individually love his wife as he loves himself. For a husband is head of his wife, just as Christ is head of the congregation." (AEV. 5:22, 23) This arrangement does not mean that the husband is superior. Rather, it shows that we should respect the way God has organized matters. God said: "It is not good that the man [Adam] should be alone. I will make someone suitable to be a helper for him." (Gen. 2:18) A Christian husband should use his authority for the benefit of his wife, because Christ, who is "head of the congregation," did so. In this way, the wife feels secure, protected, and cherished.
5 One wife named Cathy [1] admitted that she used to feel insecure. She said: "I often felt inadequate and compared myself unfavorably with others. I was afraid that my husband would find fault with me. But I realized that if I wanted to please Jehovah, I needed to focus on my own strengths." Her husband, Fred, said: "I too had to make changes. I used to be quick to criticize. But I learned that when I am considerate of others, it makes me more appealing. I now try to appreciate the things she does well, and I trust that Jehovah will help us both to live up to our responsibilities." They have found that working together brings them closer.
6. So how can companions show that they value one another?
6 Sometimes a companion may feel hurt, but it is important to determine whether the offense was intentional. It is helpful to remember the principle of "looking beyond the offense and being forgiving." Of course, this is not always easy. If you are offended, use the time to reflect on the situation, to empathize, and to strengthen the love you share. This will help you avoid letting resentment build up—what has been called "a weed in the garden." (Acts 3:13, 14) Love "is patient and kind; . . . it does not keep account of a wrong." (1 Cor. 13:4, 5) It is wise to discuss matters calmly rather than allowing anger to fester. Christians should also strive to resolve conflicts quickly so that they do not become deeply rooted. (Eph. 4:26, 27) The expression "I am sorry" can be very meaningful to someone who feels wronged and upset. By apologizing, you can contribute to maintaining peace and helping those around you to remain united.
LOVE AND FORGIVENESS ARE ESSENTIAL
7, 8. (a) How do Bible principles help married couples deal with disagreements? (b) Why is it vital for married couples to be loving and forgiving?
7 The Bible offers practical guidance for resolving marital disputes peacefully. (Read 1 Corinthians 7:3-5.) It is beneficial for a husband and wife to allow each other personal space and freedom. However, when a husband or wife acts unkindly or unreasonably, it is essential to address the issue with love and forgiveness, avoiding letting the disagreement escalate. Some married couples have found it helpful to apply the principle of "sexual relations." (1 Pet. 3:7) Sexual intimacy is not simply a physical act; it is an emotional bond. Many husbands and wives find that regular expressions of affection help them maintain their closeness. In fact, a couple's intimate moments can often serve as a reminder of the love they share.
8 The Bible encourages each individual to examine his or her own conduct and determine whether he or she is contributing to the problem or needs to make adjustments in order to maintain peace in the marriage. It also encourages us to reflect on our own attitude. (Phil. 1:2; 2:6) Christian married couples should strive to be loving and forgiving.
9. What if a person is unmarried?
9 We can show love for God by obeying him and by expressing love for our neighbor, which will help us to avoid being influenced by bad associations. Bad associations can lead to immoral thoughts or actions, and they may cause us to disregard Scriptural principles. However, if we associate with those who have questionable standards, we may find ourselves compromising our integrity. Associating with such people can weaken our devotion to God. To know what God expects of us and how we can please him, we must study his Word and pray regularly.—Read Matthew 5:27, 28; Hebrews 4:13.
HOW TO DEAL WITH BAD ASSOCIATIONS
10, 11. (a) How can we strengthen our resolve to resist bad influences? (b) What can help us to stay spiritually strong? (c) Why is it important to protect our association with fellow Christians?
10 Showing love for our brothers and sisters moves us to want to help them, whether it means encouraging them to maintain their spirituality or helping them to overcome bad habits. In some cases, nearly half of all those who were once associated with Jehovah's Witnesses have fallen away. This shows how vital it is for Christians to be selective about their associates. The majority of God's people realize that bad associations are more dangerous than ever.
11 The Bible gives this warning: "A companion of fools will become foolish himself, (and he will suffer rebuke from others, or he will be ruined, or his marriage will be dissolved); but as for a wise man, he will be refreshed when he associates with the righteous." (Proverbs 13:20, 21) Dissociating can sometimes be difficult, but it is often necessary to protect oneself from harmful influences. Jesus correctly pointed out that God created man and woman and instituted marriage, saying: "What therefore God has yoked together, let no man put asunder." (Matthew 19:3-6; Genesis 2:24) This principle shows that a husband and wife should not think of separating unless there is a valid Scriptural reason—that is, unless they are following 'God's arrangement.' Jehovah cares deeply for all his loyal servants. (1 Corinthians 7:39) Knowing what pleases God helps us to avoid making decisions that could lead to serious problems and regrets.
12 What can help us to make the right decision regarding association with a disfellowshipped person?
12 A Christian should carefully consider whether the reasons for associating with a disfellowshipped person are Scriptural. Some may feel obligated to maintain a relationship because of family ties or past associations, but such feelings should not outweigh their loyalty to God. They may find themselves being influenced negatively, or one of them may stumble, or it may lead to separation. It is important to remember that if we deliberately associate with someone who is practicing sin, we risk becoming defiled ourselves. Also, our example might influence others, perhaps even members of our own families, to disregard spiritual principles. Many Christians have found it helpful to pray earnestly about the matter and to seek counsel from mature elders.
13 What further considerations can help Christians to remain neutral?
13 There are some who may be tempted to take sides in disputes. Some things that can cause people to become partial include personal affection for those involved, a desire to appear impartial, or a feeling of sympathy. Christians who have a strong conscience will strive to avoid taking sides. They will rely on accurate information and will weigh matters according to God's standards. To remain neutral requires courage and faith in Jehovah's guidance.—Prov. 29:25. [2]
14 How does the Bible equip Christians to deal with relatives and friends who are non-Witnesses?
14 Some Christians live with family members who are not yet serving Jehovah. The Bible gives Christians practical counsel on how to maintain peace with their household. (Read 1 Corinthians 7:12-14.) However, if a Christian finds himself in a situation where his relative—whether a husband or wife—is "unbelieving," or disapproving, he should carefully consider whether to continue in that relationship. In any case, let us remember that God allows for imperfections and that humans are often influenced by imperfect reasoning. Paul asked: "Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek a divorce; are you bound to a husband? Do not seek a separation." (1 Cor. 7:16) In each case, the individual Christian must decide whether he can continue to please God while remaining in that marriage.
15, 16. (a) What Scriptural principles can help Christians to stay neutral when relatives pressure them to take sides? (b) How can a Christian respond to a relative who says, "You are taking sides!"
?
15 The apostle Peter wrote to Christians, encouraging them to be ready to give a reason for their hope, saying: "Always be prepared to make a defense to anyone asking for a reason concerning your hope, but do so with gentleness and respect." To remain neutral, avoid getting involved in arguments or expressing disrespectful opinions. Instead, show genuine interest in others and kindly explain why you believe what you do. Remember that "the fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom," and this will help you to speak tactfully and respectfully. Paul advised: "Whether slave or free, let each one remain in the condition in which God has called him." (1 Pet. 3:1-4.)
16 Does this mean that we should never associate with people who have different views than ours? The Bible gives us guidance on this matter: "If possible, so far as it depends on you, be peaceable with all men." (Rom. 12:18) This does not mean that we should compromise our beliefs. However, we can still show kindness and consideration toward those who disagree with us. Why? Because we want to win their hearts. And when a Christian is accused unjustly by someone, he should not react angrily or seek revenge. Rather, he should trust in Jehovah to vindicate him.
KEEP YOUR HEART MOTIVATED
17 What can help you to stay motivated in your ministry?
17 We need to be aware of the "signs of the times," which include "difficult times." (2 Tim. 3:1-5) As we draw closer to Jehovah, we become more determined to overcome the obstacles we face. Paul wrote: "The world is passing away." And he added: "Let those who make use of the world not get too absorbed in it." (1 Cor. 7:29-31) But Paul did not advise Christians to isolate themselves from everyone. He encouraged them to focus on what truly matters—pleasing Jehovah—rather than getting caught up in worldly pursuits.—Matt. 6:33.
18 So how can we show that we value our relationship with Christ and that his teachings are important to us?
18 Showing that we value our relationship with Christ means making his priorities our own and being busy with the ministry. Let us, like those who said, "God is generous," continue to be generous in supporting Jehovah's work, in upholding Bible standards, and in zealously proclaiming the good news.—Mark 10:9.

text:
"Yeova, Yeova, Ngai wĩ tei na mũseo [kana, wĩ ĩnee]."—KUMA 34:6.
MBATHI: 142, 12
1. Yeova eemanyĩthisye kwa Mose ata, na nĩkĩ kĩu nĩ kya vata kwitũ?
ĨVINDA yĩmwe Ngai nĩweemanyĩthisye kwĩ Mose kwa kũmũtavya ĩsyĩtwa yake na nguma syake. Nguma sya mbee ila wamũtavisye syaĩ tei na ũseo, kana ĩnee. (Soma Kuma 34:5-7.) Keka Yeova nĩwendaa, nguma ila wĩthĩwa aneeneie mũno nĩ vinya wake na ũĩ wake. Ĩndĩ nĩkwĩthĩwa ĩvinda yĩu Mose endaa Yeova amũĩkĩĩthye kana e vamwe nake, Yeova amũweteie nguma ila syaĩ itonya kũmũtetheesya aelewe kana e na wendi wa kũtetheesya athaithi make. (Kuma 33:13) Kwasũanĩa! Ngai ambie kũweta nguma isu iseũvĩte ũu atanamba kũweta ila ingĩ. We tyo ũkwĩw'a kĩu kĩikwĩkĩa vinya? Ĩsomo yĩĩ yĩneenea nguma ya ĩnee. Mũndũ wĩ nguma ĩsu e tei na nũthĩnĩkaa amanya kana ũla ũngĩ e na thĩna kana nũitavĩwe, na nĩwendaa mũno kũmũolangĩla thĩna ũsu.
2, 3. (a) Twĩsĩ ata kana mũndũ asyaawa e na ũtonyi wa kwĩw'ĩa angĩ ĩnee? (b) Nĩkĩ waĩlĩte kwĩmanyĩsya mũnango ĩũlũ wa nguma ya ĩnee?
2 Ngai oombie andũ na mũvw'ano wake. Kwoou nũndũ Yeova e ĩnee, andũ onthe masyaawa me na wendi wa kwona ala angĩ maendeee nesa. O na mavinda maingĩ ala matesĩ Ngai ũsu wa w'o no monanasya ĩnee. (Mwa. 1:27) Twasoma Mbivilia nĩtwĩthĩaa ngewa sya andũ meew'ĩie angĩ ĩnee. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ngewa ya ala malwaya elĩ matwaĩe Solomoni ĩkoani atw'e nũũ inyia wa kana kala makananĩaa nũndũ kĩla ũmwe aasya kana kau nĩ kake. Ĩla Solomoni waisye kana kau katilanĩlw'e katĩ, kĩveti kĩla kyakasyaĩte kyeewie kĩtomĩĩsya. Ĩnee yĩla kyaĩ nayo yatumie kyona o na nĩ kavaa kana kau koswe nĩ kĩveti kĩla kĩngĩ kwĩ koawe. (1 Asu. 3:23-27) O na no ũlilikane ĩvinda yĩla mwĩĩtu wa Valao woovoisye Mose ĩla waĩ kaũkenge. O na kau nĩweesĩ kaũkenge kau kaaĩle kũawa nũndũ kaĩ ka mũndũ mũka Mũevelania, akililye akona "akew'ĩa ĩnee" na nũndũ wa ũu akosa nĩ kana akaee ta kake ũsyaĩte.—Kuma 2:5, 6.
3 Nĩkĩ waĩlĩte kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa nguma ya ĩnee? Kĩtumi nũndũ Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩĩte vinya twĩyĩelekany'e na Yeova. (Aev. 5:1) Ĩndĩ o na kau twoombiwe tũtonya kwĩw'ĩa angĩ ĩnee, naĩ ĩla twatiĩwe nĩ Atamu ĩtumaa tũkotha kwĩyenda mũno kwĩ ala angĩ. Ve mavinda twĩsaa kwĩthĩa ti laisi kũtw'a twĩtethya ala angĩ kana twĩĩtethya ithyĩ ene. Andũ amwe mekalaa maithĩnany'a na ũndũ ũsu kĩla ĩvinda. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũũtetheesya wendae mũno kwona ala angĩ maendeee nesa? Ũndũ wa mbee, osa ĩvinda ũsisye ũndũ Yeova wonanĩtye kana e ĩnee na ũndũ angĩ maatĩĩe ngelekany'o yake. Kelĩ, sũanĩa ũndũ ũtonya kwĩyĩelekany'a na Ngai na ũisũanĩa moseo ma kwĩka ũu.
YEOVA NĨWE NGELEKANY'O ĨLA NZEO VYŨ
4. (a) Nĩkĩ Yeova watũmie alaĩka ndũanĩ ya Sotomo? (b) Ngewa ya Loto na eĩtu make yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
4 Ve ngewa mbingĩ syĩ Mbivilianĩ iĩkĩĩthĩtye kana Yeova nĩ Ngai wĩ ĩnee. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Ngai woonanisye e ĩnee ĩvinda ya Loto. Loto aĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu, na nũndũ wa ũu "anyamaĩtw'e" mũno nĩ mwĩkalĩle mũthũku na ũte nthoni wa andũ ma Sotomo na Ngomola. Mwĩkalĩle ũsu watumie Ngai atw'a kwananga andũ asu vyũ. (2 Vet. 2:7, 8) Ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwatũmie alaĩka mavonokye Loto. Mathi nĩmakalaatile Loto na andũ make maume ndũanĩ isu itanamba kwanangwa. "Ĩndĩ [Loto] ekalanga; na ala [alaĩka] mamũkwata kw'oko, na kw'oko kwa mũka wake, na kw'oko kwa eĩtu make elĩ, kwondũ wa Yeova kũmwĩw'ĩa tei: na mamumaalya, mamwia ũtee wa ndũa." (Mwa. 19:16) Ngewa ĩsu yĩtũtetheesya kwona nesa kana Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa ene vyũ mathĩna ala athũkũmi make makomanaa namo.—Isa. 63:7-9; Yak. 5:11; 2 Vet. 2:9.
5. Ĩandĩko ta 1 Yoana 3:17 yĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ata twĩthĩwe na ĩnee?
5 O na kau Yeova nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ũndũnĩ ũsu, nũsyokete akamanyĩsya andũ make ũndũ o namo matonya kwĩthĩwa na ĩnee. Kwasũanĩa ũla mwĩao wanengie Aisilaeli wakonetye kwosea mũndũ ngũa na ũyĩkala nayo ta ngwatĩlĩlyo nginya ĩla ũkaĩva kĩla wamũkovethya. (Soma Kuma 22:26, 27.) Mũndũ ũte tei aĩ atonya kũema kũtũngĩa mwene ngũa yake, na nũndũ wa ũu aituma akoma ate na kĩndũ kya kwĩvw'ĩka. Ĩndĩ Yeova eeie andũ make mevathane na mwĩkalĩle ta ũsu ũte tei. Andũ make maaĩle kwĩthĩwa andũ me ĩnee. Mwolooto ũla wĩ mwĩaonĩ ũsu no ũtũtethye? Ĩĩ, no ũtũtethye. Nũũ katĩ witũ wenda kũekea mwana-a-asa mbevo kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o e na ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka akamũtetheesya?—Ako. 3:12; Yak. 2:15, 16; soma 1 Yoana 3:17.
6. Kĩthetheesyo kĩla Yeova waĩ nakyo kya kũtetheesya Isilaeli melile kĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
6 Yeova nĩweew'ĩaa andũ make Isilaeli ĩnee o na kũtw'ĩka nĩmamũvĩtĩasya. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Yeova, Ngai wa aaĩthe moo, atũmanaa kwoo na kanyw'a wa atũmwa make, akyũkĩla tene na akĩtũmana, nĩkwĩthĩwa amew'ĩaa andũ make ĩnee, o na ũtũo wake." (2 Mav. 36:15) O ta ũu, o naitũ tyo twaĩle kwĩw'ĩa ĩnee ala matamwĩsĩ Ngai ĩndĩ matonya kwĩlila na maitw'ĩka anyanyae? Yeova ndendaa mũndũ o na ũmwe eanangwa ĩvindanĩ ya ũsilĩlo. (2 Vet. 3:9) Kwoou ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ Ngai weteele kwananga ala athũku, tũikaeke kũtavya andũ ĩtambya yĩla ũkwenda mose nĩ kana amew'ĩe ĩnee.
7, 8. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie mũndũ ũmwe na mũsyĩ wake maĩkĩĩa kana Yeova nĩwamew'ĩie ĩnee?
7 Ũmũnthĩ kwĩ athũkũmi aingĩ ma Ngai matonya kũĩkĩĩthya kana nũmonetye ĩnee. Kwasũanĩa kĩla kyakwatie kamwana kamwe tũũkatw'ĩĩa ĩsyĩtwa Milan, vamwe na andũ ala angĩ moo. Mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1990, ĩla kaĩ na myaka 12, nthĩ yoo ya Bosnia nĩyalikile kaũ wa mbaĩ. Mũthenya ũmwe Milan e na kĩvĩsĩ kĩinae, asyai make, vamwe na Ngũsĩ ingĩ kauta nĩmakũisye kyalo kya kũthi nthĩ ya Serbia. Maendete Serbia kwondũ wa ũmbano mũnene, na asyai ma Milan mavatisĩawa ku ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Ĩndĩ mavika mũvakanĩ, asikalĩ nĩmaumisye Milan e na mũinae vamwe na asyai moo mbasinĩ nũndũ maĩ ma mbaĩ yĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na maekana na Ngũsĩ ila ingĩ iendeee na kyalo. Ĩtina wa kwĩkala namo mĩthenya ĩlĩ, mũnene wa asikalĩ asu nĩwaneenie na mũnene wake nĩ kana amanye ũndũ ũkwĩkana namo. Mũnene wa asikalĩ asu aneenaa aũngye o vau vakuvĩ namo na kwoou nĩmeewie ũndũ wasũngĩiwe. Eeiwe: "Mosei na mũimaathanga!"
8 Ĩla mũnene ũsu wa asikalĩ waendie aneene na asikalĩ make, aũme elĩ nĩmookie vala ve Milan na ala angĩ na mamasukĩĩsya kana mo nĩ Ngũsĩ. Ana-a-asa asu mameie kana ala maĩ namo mbasinĩ nĩmo mamatavisye kĩla kĩnaendeeie. Na kwoou meeie Milan na mũinae malike kakalĩnĩ nĩ kana mamakĩlye mũvakanĩ nũndũ asikalĩ ala maĩ vau mayasiasya mavalũa ma syana. Ana-a-asa asu masyokie meea asyai moo mevĩlĩle navu ĩtina wa kambi na maikĩla nĩ kana makomane ngalĩko ĩsu ĩngĩ ya mũvaka. Milan oolanĩlw'e nĩ nthĩ weethĩa ndesĩ aĩle kũtheka kana aĩle kũĩa. Asyai make makũlilye ana-a-asa asu: "Mwĩĩsilya metwathũkĩa tũthi oou matũsyaĩĩsye?" Ĩla matambisye mathi asikalĩ asu nĩmamasyaĩĩsye, ĩndĩ mailyĩ ta meene vathei. Mũthya syana isu na asyai masyo nĩmakomanĩie ngalĩko ĩsu ĩngĩ ya mũvaka. Makomana nĩmaendeeie na kĩla kyalo kyoo mũvaka ũmbanonĩ mũnene mate na nzika kana Yeova nĩwasũngĩie mboya ila mamũvoyete na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo. Nĩtwĩsĩ kana Mbivilianĩ ve mavinda Yeova ũtaaĩka kyama asũvĩe athũkũmi make. (Meko 7:58-60) Ĩndĩ Milan easya ũũ asũanĩa ĩvinda yĩu: "Nyie noonie asikalĩ asu meekie kũvw'ĩkwa metho nĩ alaĩka na Yeova atũvonokya."—Sav. 97:10.
9. Yesũ eekie ata oona ũndũ makomano ala mamũatĩĩaa manyamaĩte? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
9 O na ĩngĩ no twĩmanyĩsye o kĩndũ twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Yesũ. Nĩweew'ĩie makomano ĩnee nĩkwĩthĩwa "nĩmanyamaaw'a na kũnyaĩĩkw'a ta malondu mate na mũĩthi." Eekie ata oona ũndũ meũnyamaw'a? Akililye amona "ambĩlĩlya kũmamanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ." (Mt. 9:36; soma Maliko 6:34.) Aĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na Avalisi nũndũ mo mayaũnganaa na andũ ta asu. (Mt. 12:9-14; 23:4; Yoa. 7:49) We nĩwĩthĩawa na wendi ta ũsu wa Yesũ wa kũtetheesya ala me na nzaa ya kĩ-veva?
10, 11. Nĩ kĩla ĩvinda twaĩlĩte kwĩw'ĩa angĩ ĩnee? Elesya.
10 Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana nĩ kĩla ĩvinda twaĩlĩte kwĩw'ĩa angĩ ĩnee. Ngewanĩ ila sya Mbivilia twaneenea, Ngai ndaavĩtya ĩla weew'ĩie andũ asu ĩnee. Ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Mũsumbĩ Saulo. Ĩvinda yĩmwe eekie ũndũ waleanĩte na mwĩao wa Yeova aisũanĩa nĩ ĩnee ũkwonany'a. Yĩu nĩ yĩla ĩvinda waleile kũaa mũmaitha wa andũ ma Ngai weetawa Akaki vamwe na indo ila nzeo. Nũndũ wa ũu, Yeova nĩwamũleile ndakaendeee kwĩthĩwa mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli. (1 Sam. 15:3, 9, 15) Vate nzika, Yeova nĩwe Mũsili mũlũngalu. Nũtonya kũsoma ngoo sya andũ, na nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ nĩ ĩndĩĩ mataĩle kwĩw'ĩwa ĩnee. (Iĩo 2:17; Esek. 5:11) Kwoou mũthenya nĩwũkĩte ĩla ũkaete ũsilĩlo ĩũlũ wa onthe ala maleaa kũmwĩw'a. (2 Ath. 1:6-10) Yĩu yĩikethĩwa ĩvinda ya kũmew'ĩa ĩnee onthe ala ũkethĩwa anamatw'ĩĩa sila akasya nĩ athũku. Ĩndĩ kwosa ĩtambya ya kũmananga kũkeethĩwa ne nzĩa nzeo vyũ ya kwonany'a kana nũkũmew'ĩa ĩnee ala ũkamatangĩĩa nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩ alũngalu.
11 Ti kĩanda kitũ kũtw'a sila naaũ makanangwa na naaũ makaekwa thayũ. Vandũ va ũu, twaĩle kwĩka kyonthe kĩla tũtonya ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũmatetheesye. Kwoou nĩ nzĩa syĩva nzeo sya kwonany'a kana nĩtwĩw'ĩaa ala angĩ ĩnee? Kwaekai twone nzĩa iana ũna.
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KWONANY'A TWĨ NA ĨNEE
12. Ũtonya kwĩka ata ũkonany'a nĩwĩw'ĩaa ala angĩ ĩnee?
12 Kĩla mũthenya mantha ũndũ ũtonya kũtetheesya ala angĩ. Tũyĩsa kwasya nĩtũatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ethĩwa tũyĩw'ĩaa ĩnee atũi maitũ na ana-a-asa maitũ. (Yoa. 13:34, 35; 1 Vet. 3:8) Amwe maeleasya nguma ya ĩnee makasya nĩ "kũnyamaa vamwe na ũla ũkũthĩna." Mũndũ wĩ ĩnee nĩwĩthĩawa na mea ma kũolanga mathĩna ma andũ angĩ, ta kwa kũmatetheesya ĩla me thĩnanĩ. Kwoou manthaa ũndũ ũtonya kũtetheesya ala meũthĩna. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve mũndũ wĩsĩ wĩ na vata wa kũtetheew'a kwĩka kaũndũ mũsyĩ kwake kana wĩthĩwa ayenda kũtũmana vandũ?—Mt. 7:12.
13. Andũ ma Ngai mekaa ata ĩvinda ya mĩisyo?
13 Ĩyumye ũtetheesye ĩvinda ya mĩisyo. Andũ aingĩ moona kũnyamaa kwa ala makwatĩtwe nĩ mũisyo, nĩmendaa kwosa ĩtambya mamatetheesye. Andũ ma Yeova nĩmesĩkĩe ta andũ matetheeasya mũno ĩvindanĩ ya mĩisyo. (1 Vet. 2:17) Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wa Japan watwĩe vandũ vakũniwe mũno nĩ kĩla kĩthingitho kya nthĩ na kĩuutani kĩthũku kya mwaka wa 2011. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu aasya kana 'eekĩiwe vinya mũno na akiakiw'a' nĩ kwona kĩthito kya onthe ala maumie isionĩ ingĩ kũu Japan na mũingo nĩ kana moke mamatetheesye kũtũngĩĩa nyũmba ila syaanangĩkĩte. Aandĩkie ũũ: "Kĩndũ kĩu kyatumie nĩmanya kana Yeova nũtũthĩnĩkĩaa. Nĩnamanyie kana o nasyo Ngũsĩ nithĩnĩkĩaa Ngũsĩ ila ingĩ. Na ve ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ mavoyaa kwondũ witũ."
14. Ũtonya kũtetheesya ata ala awau na ala akũũ?
14 Tetheesya ala awau na ala akũũ. Tũkilasya twoona andũ mainyamaa nũndũ wa ĩla naĩ ya Atamu tũkew'a twenda kũmony'a ĩnee. Tweteele mũno kwona ĩvinda yĩla kũtakethĩwa mowau na ũkũũ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi tũvoyaa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũke. Ĩndĩ ũitw'ĩka nĩwooka, nĩtũendeee kũtata ũndũ tũtonya tũtetheesye ala meũthĩna. Kwasũanĩa kĩla mũandĩki ũmwe waandĩkie ĩũlũ wa inyia. Inyia aĩ mũkũũ na aĩ na ũwau wĩtawa Alzheimer's na kwoou mũthenya ũmwe nĩweethokoanisye atanavika kyoonĩ. Akililye aitata kwĩvangũlanga kĩko kĩu ngengele ya mũomonĩ yakũnwa. Ala maĩ mũomonĩ maĩ Ngũsĩ ilĩ syakothaa kũmũthokea. Eĩtu-a-asa asu nĩmamũkũlilye ethĩwa ve vandũ matonya kũmũtetheesya. Kĩveti kĩu kyameie: "Ĩĩ ve vamwe, o na kau nĩngwĩw'a nthoni kũmũtavya." Eĩtu-a-asa asu nĩmakĩtetheeisye kwĩthesya. Mamina nĩmakĩuĩie kyai na mekala nthĩ maee ngewa nakyo. Mwana ũsu wa kĩveti kĩu atanie ta kĩ! Aandĩkie: "Mwa Ngũsĩ nĩ sya kumĩw'a ngovia!" Aisye: "Syĩkaa kĩla itavanasya." We nĩwĩw'ĩaa ĩnee ala awau na akũũ na nĩwĩkaa kyonthe kĩla we mwene ũtonya nĩ kana maeke kũnyamaa mũno?—Avi. 2:3, 4.
15. Wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũtetheeasya ala angĩ ata?
15 Tetheesya andũ mamũmanye Yeova. Nĩkwĩthĩwa andũ me na mathĩna maingĩ meũtuma memakĩa, nĩtwĩthĩawa na wendi wa kũmatetheesya methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. Nzĩa nzeo ya kwĩka ũu nĩ kũmamanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai na kũmaelesya moathimo ala Ũsumbĩ wake ũkaetee andũ. Nzĩa ĩngĩ nĩ kũmatetheesya mone ũndũ matonya kũunĩka maatĩĩa myolooto ya Ngai. (Isa. 48:17, 18) Nũndũ kũtavany'a nĩkũmũtaĩaa Yeova na nĩ nzĩa nzeo ya kwonany'a kana nĩtwĩw'ĩaa angĩ ĩnee, wĩona ata ũkongelanga ĩvinda yĩla ũtũmĩaa wĩanĩ ũsu?—1 Tim. 2:3, 4.
KWĨTHĨWA NA ĨNEE NO KŨŨTETHYE WE MWENE!
16. Mũndũ wĩ ĩnee atethekaa ata we mwene?
16 Ala masomeete ilĩko sya andũ maasya kana kwĩw'ĩa angĩ ĩnee nĩkũũsũvĩaa ndũkethĩwe na mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ na nĩkũtumaa wĩkalany'a na ala angĩ nesa. Ĩla watetheesya angĩ maeke kũnyamaa mũno nĩwongelangaa ũtanu ũla wĩ naw'o, nũsũvĩĩkaa ndũkakw'e ngoo nũndũ wa mathĩna, nĩwĩthĩawa na mawoni maseo, na ti laisi ũkona vai mũndũ ũkũũngana naku. Kwoou nĩ w'o ki, kwĩthĩwa na ĩnee no kũũtethye we mwene! (Aev. 4:31, 32) Aklĩsto ala matetheeasya ala angĩ nũndũ nĩmamendete, mekalaa na wasya mũseo wa ngoo nũndũ nĩmesĩ meatĩĩa myolooto ĩla Ngai wendaa tũatĩĩe. Kwĩthĩwa na ĩnee nĩkũtũtetheeasya kũea syana sitũ nesanga, kwĩkalany'a nesa na ala tũtwaanĩte namo, na nĩkũtumaa ala twĩ ndũũ namo matanĩa mũnango ũnyanya witũ. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ala me nguma ya ĩnee nĩmakothaa kũtetheew'a na kũtw'ĩĩkwa ĩla me thĩnanĩ.—Soma Mathayo 5:7; Luka 6:38.
17. Nĩkĩ we ũkwenda kwĩthĩwa na nguma ya ĩnee?
17 O na kau nũtethekaa woony'a ala angĩ ĩnee, kĩu kĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ne kyo kĩtumi kyaku kĩnene kya kwĩkĩa kĩthito wĩthĩwe na nguma ĩsu. Waĩle kwĩka ũu nũndũ wĩenda kwĩyĩelekany'a na Yeova na kũmũtaĩa, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe Ngai wa wendo na ĩnee. (Nth. 14:31) Yeova nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo mũno kwitũ. Ekai tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yake kwa kũtata ũndũ tũtonya twĩthĩwe na nguma ya ĩnee nĩ kana tũlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yitũ na ana-a-asa maitũ na tũyĩkalanasya nesa na atũi maitũ.—Aka. 6:10; 1 Yoa. 4:16.

translation:
"Jehovah, Jehovah, the God of tender mercy [yes, he is]"—CUM 34:6.
PAGE: 142, 12
1. How did Jehovah show his forgiveness to Moses, and what does this teach us?
ONE way God showed his forgiveness to Moses was by allowing him to ask for help in carrying out his work and in dealing with his people. His people were stubborn, yet he forgave them again and again. (Read CUM 34:5-7.) Let Jehovah lead, and his people will always follow his direction and his guidance. It is like Moses asked Jehovah to go with him and with his people, and Jehovah promised to give him help so that he could understand and also have the desire to carry out his purpose. (CUM 33:13) How wonderful! God promises to give help to those who seek it, and he will continue to give help more and more. So why should we be afraid to ask for help? This lesson teaches us about forgiveness. A person who has been forgiven may forget or think that he is no longer worthy, but God continues to remember and forgive him.
2, 3. (a) What can help us to remain humble? (b) What will motivate us to forgive others?
2 God asks people to show compassion. He knows that humans are imperfect, and he wants them to be kind to one another. People often make mistakes, but God still loves them. (Gen. 1:27) By reading the Bible, we learn how God views people. For example, the wise words of Solomon show us that everyone makes mistakes. But Solomon learned from his mistakes, and each time he made a mistake, he tried to correct it. And when he corrected it, he became wiser. (1 Ki. 3:23-27) Also, remember the case of Pharaoh, who opposed Moses and refused to let God's people go. Pharaoh thought he could get away with it, but eventually he realized his error and regretted his decision.—CUM 2:5, 6.
3 How can we cultivate compassion? We can do so by letting the Bible teach us what Jehovah feels. (Ps. 5:1) So, although we may have been raised to think certain ways, we can allow Adam's ransom to help us view others kindly. The choices we make should not cause us to judge others harshly or to mistreat them. Some people find it difficult to show compassion consistently. Is it possible to train yourself to be more compassionate toward others? Yes, it is. Focus on what Jehovah values and on what he has taught through his Word. Regularly meditate on how to imitate God and strive to apply what you learn.
JEHOVAH IS THE BEST EXAMPLE
4. (a) Why did Jehovah forgive Solomon? (b) What does Lot's example teach us?
4 Many scriptures demonstrate that Jehovah is the true God. Consider what God allowed to happen to Lot. Lot was a righteous man, yet because of his bad association he "became tormented" by the wicked conduct of Sodom and Gomorrah. This conduct caused him to distressingly use God to deliver himself from those men. (2 Pet. 2:7, 8) God forgave Lot despite his weakness. However, Lot's wife did not heed the warning and looked back longingly. "And she became a pillar of salt," because she disobeyed Jehovah's command. (Gen. 19:16) Her example shows us that Jehovah is deeply moved when loyal ones disregard his warnings.—Isa. 63:7-9; Jas. 5:11; 2 Pet. 2:9.
5. How can 1 John 3:17 help us to be more compassionate?
5 But if Jehovah is so understanding toward imperfections, why does he allow suffering among his people? To illustrate this, consider how Israelite parents would discipline their child when he did something wrong, but still love him. (Read Proverbs 22:26, 27.) A loving parent does not spoil his child, and neither does Jehovah. He allows his people to experience the consequences of their choices. So they learn to hate wickedness. Therefore, if you see a brother stumble, do you think that means he has lost Jehovah's favor?—Acts 3:12; Jas. 2:15, 16; read 1 John 3:17.
6. What lesson regarding compassion does Lot's wife's fate teach us?
6 Jehovah showed compassion to the Israelites despite their stubbornness. The Bible says: "Jehovah the God of their forefathers sent warning by his messengers time after time, sending them warnings by his servants the prophets, yet they paid no attention, and they refused to listen." (2 Ki. 36:15) So, should we expect that God will overlook our imperfections and forgive our mistakes? Jehovah desires a person who humbly acknowledges his errors. (2 Chron. 3:9) Because God is righteous, we can be sure that he will always act justly, even if we do not understand his ways.
7, 8. What might move a Christian and his mate to seek help if they are struggling to maintain their marriage?
7 Often, Christians find it difficult to admit they need help in their marriage. It is like trying to repair a damaged car tire yourself, rather than taking it to a trained mechanic, such as Milan. In the 1990's, a 12-year-old boy in Bosnia became a refugee because of war. One day Milan and his parents, along with many others, were forced to flee their home in Serbia. Upon arriving in Serbia, they found themselves in a large refugee camp, and Milan's parents struggled to cope with the conditions there. Seeing their distress, some fellow refugees helped Milan and his parents find food and shelter, and they also encouraged them to remain faithful to God. After spending some time in the camp, the director of the camp noticed how well Milan and his parents were doing and spoke to his father, asking if he knew what was helping them. The director then said: "Moses and the priest!"
8 But this director of the camp continued to observe Milan and his family, and he began to notice that Milan and others were sharing with those around them and showing kindness to everyone, including strangers. He saw how they used whatever little they had to help others, and he realized that they were different from most people in the camp. This director asked his wife: "What makes these people so generous?" But she replied that it was due to their faith. These young ones and their parents showed compassion to others, and they always tried to share what they had with those in need. They understood that Jehovah had rescued them and provided for them. We too can imitate the example of the ancient Israelites who trusted in Jehovah and obeyed His commands. (Ps. 7:58-60) So Milan learned an important lesson: "You too should encourage others to love Jehovah and to show loyalty to Him." – Ps. 97:10.
9 Did Jesus ever show similar compassion towards people? (See accompanying article on page 8.)
9 And more importantly, let us strive to understand Jesus' thinking. He said that his motive was "to preach the good news to the poor." Did he really mean that? He felt sorry for people because "they were harassed and helpless like sheep without a shepherd." (Matt. 9:36; see Mark 6:34) He also healed people on the Sabbath despite opposition from religious leaders. (Matt. 12:9-14; 23:4; John 7:49) Are you willing to follow the example set by Jesus in showing compassion to others?
10, 11. What can we learn from their example? Let's discuss.
10 This does not mean that we should try to imitate them in every detail. However, when we study the Bible, God helps us to feel what they felt. Consider the case of Saul. On one occasion, he deeply regretted disobeying Jehovah's command. He realized that obedience was more important than offering sacrifices. Later, Jehovah reminded him to continue serving as Israel's king. (1 Sam. 15:3, 9, 15) Of course, Jehovah is discerning. He reads hearts, and he knows whether our motives are sincere. (Prov. 2:17; Ezek. 5:11) So, be determined to cultivate love and to show genuine concern for those who need help. (2 Thess. 1:6-10) Remember that a person may be experiencing hidden difficulties, so avoid being quick to judge. Instead, endeavor to discern their needs and offer assistance, always striving to please Jehovah.
11 It is not enough simply to say that we love others. We must also demonstrate our love through our actions. Like Jesus, we can show kindness to everyone, and we can use our words to encourage them. But how can we know if our efforts to show love are truly appreciated? Let us examine some examples.
WHAT HELPS US TO DISCERN HOW OTHERS FEEL
12. How can we determine whether our expressions of love are pleasing to others?
12 Often, people find it difficult to express their feelings. We must remember that we want to imitate Jesus, who showed love for others while also respecting their dignity. One way to do this is by showing "consideration for those around us." A loving person will be sensitive to the feelings of others, rather than trying to force his own opinions on them. What, then, can help us to discern how to show love effectively? For example, if someone seems reluctant to accept your help, could it be because he feels proud or because he fears burdening you?—Matt. 7:12.
13. Do God's servants always agree on everything?
13 Sometimes, disagreements arise. Many people find it hard to accept criticism, and they may become defensive when someone points out their flaws. Jehovah's Witnesses strive to be considerate of others, even when addressing serious errors. (1 Pet. 2:17) Consider the experience of a sister in Japan who visited many people affected by the earthquake and tsunami of 2011. This sister noticed that some were feeling overwhelmed and discouraged. She learned that 'being patient and understanding' helped her to see the needs of others more clearly, especially in Japan where many people tend to hide their emotions. She wrote: "This experience helped me realize how much Jehovah cares for us. I realized that God cares for us deeply. And many brothers and sisters throughout the land felt moved to assist our brothers."
14. Can we show love to those who are different from us?
14 Show love to those who are different from us. As we saw earlier, Adam and Eve disobeyed God and suffered the consequences. We need to make an effort to understand why people act the way they do. That is why we try to view matters from their perspective. This helps us to please God. If we remain humble, we will continue to improve in showing love to those around us. For example, consider a brother who wrote about his own experience. His mother was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and gradually lost her memory. He found it difficult to communicate with her, like talking to a stranger. But he remembered that God loves his mother. So he continued to care for her. One elder commented: "If we are willing, we can always find ways to help them." This brother persevered in caring for his mother. He often told her stories about the past. His son said: "I am so grateful for what you have done!" He added: "It takes patience." So be willing to show love to those who are different from you, and remember that each person has reasons for acting the way they do.—Prov. 2:3, 4.
15. How can we show love to others?
15 Show love to those who know Jehovah. It is comforting to know that many people are making progress in learning the truth, and we want to encourage them with our loving words and genuine interest in spiritual things. One important way to do this is to teach people about God and help them appreciate his purposes. Another way is to show love by helping them overcome obstacles to living according to God's standards. (Isa. 48:17, 18) To show love, we must get to know Jehovah ourselves. And when we pray for others, do we really mean it?—1 Tim. 2:3, 4.
SHOW LOVE AND BE LOYAL!
16. What does it mean to be loyal?
16 Loyalty means supporting Jehovah's organization and upholding the principles found in his Word, and it moves us to associate with those who are zealous in serving him. But being loyal does not mean blindly following someone, regardless of what he does, or excusing serious sins. Rather, loyalty is based on sound reasoning and a deep appreciation for God's laws, and it involves having a sincere desire to please Him. (Eph. 4:31, 32) Christians show their loyalty by continuing to learn from God's Word and by striving to apply its teachings in their lives. Being loyal helps us remain united, strengthens our bond with fellow believers, and enables us to witness effectively to others. Also, when brothers make mistakes, being loyal means helping them correct their errors and encouraging them.—Read Matthew 5:7; Luke 6:38.
17. How will you show loyalty?
17 One way to demonstrate loyalty is to support faithful brothers who are taking the lead, recognizing that this is an important aspect of maintaining Christian unity. By doing so, you show that you value cooperation with Jehovah and that you appreciate him as the God of love and righteousness. (Prov. 14:31) Jehovah deeply values loyalty. Let us therefore show our loyalty to him by diligently applying the principles found in his Word, by rejecting false teachings, and by remaining united with our spiritual brothers and sisters.—Acts 6:10; 1 John 4:16.

text:
KWAKŨNA visa Leveka aisisya nthĩ yĩ na maliko maingĩ ĩa-mawĩoo. Vavĩtĩte syumwa siana ũndũ mũna nayu nũmanyĩĩte kũkuwa nĩ ngamĩle. Aĩ anatia na kĩlomita mbingĩ nthĩ ĩla wasyaĩwe yeetawa Aalani, ĩla yaĩ ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ. Nĩvatonyeka akaema kwĩsa kwona andũ ma mũsyĩ wake ĩngĩ. No nginya akethĩwa asũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte, na mũno mũno yu wĩ vakuvĩ kũvika.
Maĩ manatia kĩsio kĩnene kya nthĩ ya Kanaani na yu mesĩle malelũ mathũku ma nthĩ ya ngalĩ ya Ĩtheo yeetawa Nengevu. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:62) Maendete, nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Leveka oonaa malondu. Nthĩ ĩsu nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yaĩ nũmũ ũkethĩa nĩ vinya andũ kũĩma, ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, yaĩ na ũĩthyo wĩanĩtye kwondũ wa ndĩthya. Mũtumĩa ũla waendanĩtye na Leveka nĩweesĩ nesa kũndũ ku mesĩle. Aĩ na mea ma kũtavya vwana wake ũvoo mũseo wa kana Leveka nũkwĩthĩwa e kĩveti kya Isaka! No nginya Leveka akethĩwa aseng'aa ũndũ ũkekalaa nthĩ ĩno. Na no nginya akethĩwa aseng'aa ũndũ Isaka, ũla ũkũmũtwaa, ũilyĩ nũndũ mayaĩ maaonana. O na ĩngĩ, no nginya akethĩwa eekũlasya makũlyo ta aa: We nũkwendeew'a ninyie ĩla ũkũmbona? Nakwa nĩngwendeew'a nĩwe ĩla ngũmwona?
Nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ mbingĩ andũ monaa mĩtwaano ĩsu ya kũvangĩĩwa ũla wĩtwaana nake ĩsaanĩtye. Ĩndĩ isionĩ ingĩ andũ nĩmavangĩĩawa ũla metwaana nake na ũsu ti ũndũ wa kũsengy'a kwoo. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa umĩte va, no wĩtĩkĩle kana Leveka aendete vandũ ũtesĩ. Kwa w'o ki, aĩ mũndũ mũka waĩ na ũkũmbaũ na mũĩkĩĩo. O naitũ nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa ta isu ĩla maũndũ maalyũka. Ve ndaĩa ingĩ nzeo na sya vata Leveka waĩ nasyo syĩkwonany'a kana aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo.
"NĨNGŨTAVĨA NGAMĨLE SYAKU NASYO"
Ũalyũku ũla mũnene wamũkwatie Leveka wambĩĩie na kĩndũ wamanyĩĩte kwĩka. Eanĩie kĩsionĩ kyeetawa Aalani kana vakuvĩ nakyo. Kĩsio kĩu kyaĩ ndũanĩ ya Mesovotamia. Asyai make maĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ekali aingĩ ma ku Aalani nũndũ mayathaithaa ngai ya mwei yeetawa Sin, ĩndĩ maĩ athaithi ma Yeova Ngai.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:50.
Leveka aĩ mwĩĩtu mwanake, ĩndĩ aĩ na ndaĩa ingĩ nzeo. Aĩ na kĩthito na aĩ na mwĩkalĩle mũseo. Mũsyĩ kwoo maĩ athwii nũndũ maĩ na athũkũmi, ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, Leveka ndananaw'a. Nĩwamanyĩĩtw'e kũthũkũma na kĩthito. O ta aka aingĩ ma ĩvinda yĩu, Leveka eethĩawa na wĩa mũito wa kũtethya, kwa ngelekany'o, kũutĩa andũ ma mũsyĩ kĩw'ũ. Ĩa-mawĩoo aendaa kĩthimanĩ kũuta kĩw'ũ akuĩte kĩtete kana kĩkuu.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:11, 15, 16.
Mũthenya ũmwe ĩa-mawĩoo amina kusũsya kĩkuu kyake kĩw'ũ nĩwoonie mũtumĩa ũmwe asembete moke ũkomana. Ĩla mũtumĩa ũsu wavikie vala ũĩ amwĩie atĩĩ: "Nenga nĩnyw'e, nĩngũũvoya, tũmanzĩ kuma kĩtetenĩ kyaku." Mũtumĩa ũsu aneenie na Leveka enyivĩtye na e na ndaĩa. Leveka nĩwamanyie kana mũtumĩa ũsu aumĩte vaasa. Kwoou, atheesya kĩkuu nthĩ na mĩtũkĩ na eekĩa mũtumĩa ũsu kĩw'ũ kingĩ anyw'a alaũka. Leveka nĩwoonie ngamĩle ĩkũmi ila mũtumĩa ũsu waĩ nasyo itindiĩte o vu vakuvĩ, na iyaĩ inesa kũnyw'a kĩw'ũ nũndũ mũvalatĩ ndwaĩ na kĩw'ũ. Nĩwoonie mũtumĩa ũsu amũketee na amanya kana nĩwaĩle kũmwony'a ũlau ũndũ vatonyeka. Amina kũmũnenga kĩw'ũ amwĩie atĩĩ: "Nĩngũtavĩa ngamĩle syaku nasyo, mũvaka ilaũke."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:17-19.
Ĩla Leveka waisye nũkũtavĩla ngamĩle kĩw'ũ ndendaa o kũinenga kalw'ũ kanini, ĩndĩ aisye kana eing'ithya nginya ilaũke. Ngamĩle yĩ na waũni no ĩnyw'e kĩw'ũ kya lita 95! Ngamĩle isu syĩ ĩkũmi ikethĩwa syaĩ na waũni ũu, Leveka ethĩwa atethisye wĩa mwingĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ veonekana kana ngamĩle isu iyaĩ na waũni mwingĩ mũno. * Ĩndĩ no twĩkũlye-ĩ, Leveka nĩweesĩ kana syĩnyw'a kĩw'ũ kingĩvĩte ũu atanamba kwasya nũkũing'ithya? Aiee. Nĩweeyũmbanĩtye na nĩwendaa kũtethya wĩa ũsu mwingĩ nĩ kana onany'e ũlau kwa mũtumĩa ũsu ũtamwĩsĩ. Mũtumĩa ũsu nĩweetĩkĩlile Leveka ang'ithye ngamĩle. Na ĩndĩ amũsyaĩĩsya aisyokanĩsya ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ kĩthimanĩ, aendeee kũtavĩĩa kĩw'ũ mũvalatĩnĩ.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:20, 21.
Ngelekany'o ya Leveka no ĩtũtetheesye mũno ũmũnthĩ. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũilyĩ, andũ nĩmeyendete mũno. O tondũ kwathanĩtwe, andũ 'nĩmeyendete ene,' o na mayendaa kwĩyumya matethye ala angĩ. (2 Timotheo 3:1-5) Aklĩsto ala mekwenda kũkitana na mwĩkalĩle ũsu wa kwĩyenda nĩmaĩle kũsũanĩa mũno ngelekany'o ĩsu ya Leveka aisyokanĩsya ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ kĩthimanĩ.
No nginya Leveka ethĩwe oonie ũndũ mũtumĩa ũsu wamũketeee. Mũtumĩa ũsu ndamũsyaĩtye e na ũthũku, ĩndĩ eekĩte kũseng'a na kũtanĩthw'a nĩ Leveka. Ĩla Leveka waminie kũng'ithya ngamĩle, mũtumĩa ũsu amũnengie ngome na itang'a sya thaavu! Na ĩndĩ amwĩa: "Wĩ mwĩĩtu waũ, we? nĩngũkwĩsũva, ndavya. Ve ũthei nyũmbanĩ ya au wa ũtũkomya?" Mũtumĩa ũsu nĩwatanie mũno ĩla Leveka wamũtavisye ĩũlũ wa andũ moo. O na nĩvatonyeka Leveka e mũtanu akethĩwa amwĩie: "Twĩ na ũa o na ũĩthyo mwĩanĩu, na ũthei wa kũmũkomya." Kwa w'o, ũsu waĩ ũlau mũnene nũndũ mũtumĩa ũsu aĩ na andũ angĩ ala maendete ĩmwe. Na ĩndĩ Leveka asemba mbee wa ũla mũtumĩa akatavye inyia wake kĩla kyaendeea.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:22-28, 32.
Vate nzika, Leveka nĩwamanyĩĩtw'e kũthokasya aeni. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ andũ nĩmaekete kũthokya aeni, na nĩkyo kĩtumi twaĩlĩte kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Leveka ya kũthokany'a. Kũmũĩkĩĩa Ngai nĩkũtumaa twĩthĩwa twĩ athokya ma aeni. Yeova nĩ mũthokya wa aeni nũndũ ethĩawa e mũlau kwa andũ onthe, na kwoou endaa o naitũ twĩke oou. Nĩtũmwendeeasya Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ ĩla twamathokya andũ onthe, o na ala mate na ũtonyi.—Mathayo 5:44-46; 1 Vetelo 4:9.
"ŨKAMŨTWAĨE MWANA WAKWA MŨKA"
Mũtumĩa ũsu waĩ kĩthimanĩ aĩ ũũ? Aĩ mũthũkũmi wa Avalaamu. Avalaamu asyaanĩw'e na ũmae wa Leveka. Kwoou nĩwathokiw'e mũsyĩ kwa Mbethueli, ĩthe wa Leveka. Nĩvatonyeka mũthũkũmi ũsu akethĩwa eetawa Elieseli. * Ĩla wavikie kwa Mbethueli nĩwathokiw'e aye lĩu, ĩndĩ aisye ndeya lĩu nginya ĩla ũkatavany'a kĩtumi kyake kya kũka kũu. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:31-33) No tũkũne visa ũndũ waneenaa e mũtanu nũndũ nĩwoonie vinya na moathimo ma Yeova Ngai kyalonĩ kyake. Aathimĩtwe kwa nzĩa yĩva?
Kwakũna visa Mbethueli ĩthe wa Leveka, na Lavani mwana-a-inyia, mamwĩthukĩĩsye nesa Elieseli aimatavya ũndũ maũndũ mailyĩ. Amatavisye kana Yeova nũathimĩte Avalaamu mũno e nthĩ ya Kanaani na kana me na mwana wĩtawa Isaka, ũla waaĩle kũtiĩwa malĩ yonthe. Avalaamu nĩwanengete mũthũkũmi wake wĩa wa vata wa kũmanthĩa mwana wake, Isaka, kĩveti kuma andũnĩ make ma mũsyĩ ala mekalaa Aalani.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:34-38.
Avalaamu nĩweeie Elieseli evĩte kana ndakamũmanthĩa Isaka kĩveti kuma akanĩ ma Kanaani. Nĩkĩ wamwĩie ũu? Nũndũ andũ ma Kanaani mayamũnengete Yeova Ngai ndaĩa na mayamũthaithaa. Na Avalaamu nĩweesĩ kana ĩvinda ya Yeova yeanĩa akaananga andũ asu nũndũ wa mothũku moo. Avalaamu ndendaa Isaka mwana wake ethĩwe ailyĩ ta andũ asu kwa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku. O na nĩweesĩ kana mwana wake Isaka aĩ na kĩanda kya vata mũno nthĩnĩ wa kwĩanĩsya mawatho ma Ngai.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 15:16; 17:19; 24:2-4.
Elieseli nĩwaendeeie kũmatavya ala mamũthokisye kana ĩla ũvikie kĩthimanĩ kĩla kĩ vakuvĩ na Aalani, nũmũvoyie Yeova Ngai. Elieseli amũvoyie Yeova amũnyuvĩe Isaka kĩveti atwae. Eekie ũu ata? Amũkũlilye Yeova aĩkĩĩthye kana mwĩĩtu ũla ũkwenda atwawe nĩ Isaka nĩwe ũkũka kĩthimanĩ, na mwĩĩtu ũsu amwĩtya kĩw'ũ kya kũnyw'a emũnenga anyw'e na aisyoka ang'ithye ngamĩle. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:12-14) Nũũ weekie maũndũ asu Elieseli wakũlilye Yeova mekĩke? Nĩ Leveka! Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Leveka wĩthĩwa eewie kethĩwa nĩweewie ngewa ĩsu Elieseli watavasya andũ ma mũsyĩ wake!
Mbethueli na Lavani nĩmendeeiw'e nĩ ndeto sya Elieseli. Maisye atĩĩ: "Ũndũ ũũ wumĩte kwa Yeova." O tondũ meekaa kuma tene, nĩmeekie ũtianĩo wa mũtwaano, na Leveka anenganwe kwĩthĩwa e kĩveti kya Isaka. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:50-54) Mo maũndũ asu meonany'a kana Leveka ndaaĩtĩkĩlw'a aumye mawoni make ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu?
Syumwa siana ũndũ mũna Elieseli aĩ anamũkũlya Avalaamu ũndũ kũkethĩwa "mũndũ mũka" ũsu alea kũkany'a nake. Nake Avalaamu amũsũngĩa amwĩa: "Malea ũkũnenga, ũkaekewa wĩvĩto wakwa." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:39, 41) Mbethueli na andũ ma mũsyĩ wake nĩmendaa kwĩw'a mawoni ma Leveka. Elieseli atanie mũno ĩla maũndũ maendie nesa nginya akũlya kana no aendany'e na Leveka Kanaani mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe. Ĩndĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ wa Leveka mendaa mekalange nake kwa ĩvinda ya mĩthenya ĩkũmi. Ĩtina mesie kwasya atĩĩ: "Nĩtũkwĩta mwĩĩtu, tũmũkũlye ũndũ ũnũkwasya."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:57.
Leveka aĩ na ũtwi mũito wa kwĩka. Aaĩle kwasya ata? Esaa kũneena ta ũkwenda kũendeea kwĩkalany'a na asyai aimesũva ndakathi kũndũ kũasa na ũtakwĩsĩ? Kana esaa kwona wĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya mũno kwĩthĩwa na kĩanda nthĩnĩ wa ũndũ ũsu watongoew'e nĩ Yeova? Ũsũngĩo wake nĩwoonanisye ũndũ weew'aa ĩũlũ wa ũalyũku ũsu weekĩkie thayũnĩ wake atataĩĩe. Asũngĩie atĩĩ: "Nĩngũthi."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:58.
Leveka aĩ na ndaĩa nzeo mũno. Ũmũnthĩ syĩthĩo sitũ ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano no syĩthĩwe syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, ĩndĩ no twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ kuma kwa Leveka. Ũndũ ũla Leveka woonaa wĩ wa vata mũno kwake waĩ kwĩka kwenda kwa Yeova Ngai, ĩndĩ ti kwenda kwake. Ndeto ya Ngai ũmũnthĩ nĩtũnengae motao maseo ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano. Nĩyonanĩtye ũla twaĩle kũnyuva kũtwaana nake na ũndũ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa e mũũme kana kĩveti kĩseo. (2 Akolintho 6:14, 15; Aeveso 5:28-33) Kwoou, nĩ ũseo kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Leveka na kwĩka maũndũ kwosana na kwenda kwa Ngai.
"MŨNDŨ ŨYA NŨŨ?"
Mbethueli na mũsyĩ wake nĩmamũathimie Leveka. Na ĩndĩ Leveka, na Ndevola, ũla waĩ mũsũvĩi wake kuma e kana kanini, na aka angĩ maĩ athũkũmi nĩmaendanisye na Elieseli na aũme make. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:59-61; 35:8) Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩnini maĩ vaasa na Aalani. Savalĩ ĩsu yaĩ ndaasa nũndũ yaĩ ya maili vakuvĩ 500 (kĩlomita 800), na yakuie syumwa ta itatũ. Nokwĩthĩwa savalĩ ĩsu ĩtaĩ laisi. Leveka nĩwoonete ngamĩle mavinda maingĩ mũno, ĩndĩ tũyĩsa kwasya kana nĩwamanyĩĩte kũkuawa nĩ ngamĩle. Mbivilia yonanĩtye kana mũsyĩ wa Leveka waĩthasya indo, ĩndĩ ndyonanĩtye kana maĩ andũ ma viasala ala maendaa kũndũ kũasa na ngamĩle. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 29:10) Mavinda maingĩ andũ ala matakuawa nĩ ngamĩle mew'aa mate eanĩe o na ĩla yamakua kwa kavinda kanini!
Leveka ndaasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala watiie ĩtina, ĩndĩ nĩwendaa Elieseli amũtavye maũndũ maingĩ mũno ĩũlũ wa Isaka na mũsyĩ woo. Kwasũanĩa mũtumĩa ũsu aiea ngewa na Leveka mailyĩ vandũ mayota mwaki ĩa-mawĩoo, aimũtavya ĩũlũ wa watho ũla Yeova wamwathĩte Avalaamu. Kwĩsĩla ũsyao wa Avalaamu, Ngai esaa kũnyuva mũndũ ũla ũkaete moathimo kwa andũ onthe. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Leveka watanie ĩla wamanyie kana Yeova akeanĩsya watho wake kwĩsĩla Isaka, ũla wesaa kũmũtwaa, o na ĩngĩ kwĩsĩla we mwene!—Mwambĩlĩlyo 22:15-18.
Na ĩndĩ, mũthenya ũla tũwetie vaaya mwambĩĩonĩ wavika. Andũ asu mesĩlĩte nthĩ ya Nengevu ĩa-mawĩoo, Leveka nĩwoonie mũndũũme aitembeanga kĩsesinĩ. Mũndũũme ũsu akwetye kũsũanĩa. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "[Leveka] auma ngamĩlenĩ," nokwĩthĩwa o na ataaeteela ngamĩle ĩtulye ndu. Na ĩndĩ amũkũlya mũthũkũmi atĩĩ: "Mũndũ ũya nũũ ũnũkũtambũka kĩsesinĩ atũthaũĩte?" Ĩla Leveka wamanyie kana nĩ Isaka, eevw'ĩkie mũtwe na suka wake. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:62-65) Nĩkĩ weekie ũu? Nokwĩthĩwa eekie ũu nĩ kana onany'e ndaĩa kwa Isaka, ũla waĩ amũtwae. Andũ amwe ũmũnthĩ no mone wĩnyivyo ũsu waĩ na Leveka ũte wa vata ĩvinda yĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ũw'o nĩ kana aũme na aka no memanyĩsye ũndũ wa vata kumana na ngelekany'o ya Leveka ya wĩnyivyo, nũndũ vai mũndũ ũtenda kwĩthĩwa na ndaĩa ĩsu.
Isaka aĩ na myaka vakuvĩ 40, na aĩ na kyeva nũndũ wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ inyia wake, Sala, ũla waĩ na myaka ta ĩtatũ kuma akw'a. Ũu wĩonany'a kana Isaka aĩ mũndũũme wĩ tei na wĩ ngoo nzeo. Kwoou waĩ ũathimo mũnene kwa mũndũũme wĩ na ndaĩa isu kũkwata kĩveti kĩ kĩthito, kĩlau, na kĩnyivĩtye! Maũndũ meethĩiwe mailyĩ ata ĩla Isaka na Leveka moonanie? Mbivilia yaĩtye nesa kana Isaka 'nĩwamwendie' Leveka.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 24:67; 26:8.
O naitũ no twendeew'e nĩ Leveka nũndũ wa ndaĩa nzeo ila waĩ nasyo, o na kau nĩvavĩtĩte myaka vakuvĩ 3,900 kuma akw'a. Tũtonya kwĩyĩelekany'a nake kwa kwĩthĩwa na ũkũmbaũ, kĩthito, ũlau, na wĩnyivyo. Ekai ithyonthe twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Leveka!
^ kal. 10 Leveka ayambĩĩa kũng'ithya ngamĩle kwaĩ ĩa-mawĩoo. Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩyonanĩtye kana Leveka nĩwekalile kĩthimanĩ masaa maingĩ. O na yĩyonanĩtye kana aisyokethya eethĩie andũ ma mũsyĩ makomie, na yĩyaĩtye kana ve mũndũ watũmiwe akasisye nĩkĩ wĩkalile mũno kĩthimanĩ.
^ kal. 15 Elieseli ndawetetwe ĩsyĩtwa yake ngewanĩ ĩno, ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa no we mũthũkũmi ũla watũmĩtwe. Ve ĩvinda Avalaamu wendaa kũtiĩa Elieseli ũtiĩwa wake w'onthe. Esaa kwĩka ũu aema kwĩthĩwa na mwana ũmũtiĩa malĩ yake, na kwoou vate nzika, Elieseli nĩwe waĩ mũthũkũmi ũla mũkũũ na waĩkĩĩwe nĩ Avalaamu. Na kwa w'o, mũthũkũmi ũla ũwetetwe ngewanĩ ĩno ailyĩ ũu vaeleetw'e.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 15:2; 24:2-4.
