translation:
There are visas for Leveka who wants things and many beautiful flowers. People gather together and remember to be happy. He went with many kilometers until he reached a place called Aalani, which is near the forest. They continued to look around to see his other people. But now he is being asked to clear a large piece of land quickly, and this work will take them a while to finish.
He remembered a great story about the land of Canaan and how he crossed many rivers of the land belonging to God named Nengevu. (Joshua 24:62) Afterwards, they continued to ask Leveka for more help. This time it can't be done because asking people to stop is difficult, whether it's good or bad, and it requires a lot of patience. The messenger who goes with Leveka needs to hurry to cross over. And there are plans to send his son soon to learn from Leveka so he can be trained at Isaac's school! But now Leveka is being asked to investigate something about this land. And now he is being asked to investigate Isaac, who is leading him, and he doesn't understand what they are saying. And also, now he is being asked to explain why he did that: "Will you go where I show you?" And "Will I go with you where you lead me?"
Concerning this matter, people see different opinions on how to deal with the situation, and each opinion seems important. However, many people are misled by their own opinions, and this is not a way to seek truth. Whether or not it is right, don't force Leveka to go among the people against his will. Because of this, someone might have pride and arrogance. So let us try to find out what happened with the past events. Let us look at those things again and see if Leveka was wronged or if he had arrogance.
"I WILL NOT CHANGE MY MIND"
The great leader who sent Leveka told him something he understood well. He mentioned a place called Alani or its surroundings. That place was part of Mesopotamia. It is said that water flows through many canals in Alani, and they worship a god named Sin, and they also worship the God Jehovah.—Joshua 24:50.
Leveka had a servant, and he had many concerns. He had authority and he had a good reputation. But because of these things and because of his wealth, Leveka became arrogant. I understand that he wanted to be powerful and authoritative. And so, like many rulers, Leveka began to oppress people, for example, by forcing them to work. The officials went to enforce the work, causing distress and hardship.—Joshua 24:11, 15, 16.
One official went to force a certain man to work, and he saw a messenger standing nearby. But the messenger rebuked him, saying: "I am your God, I will help you, let us go together to your master." The messenger spoke, and Leveka heard and had many concerns. Leveka understood that the messenger was testing him. Then, he sent messengers to find out what the messenger was doing there. Leveka saw ten spies, but the messenger did not reveal himself to them, and they continued to cause distress and hardship. He saw the messenger speak to him and know whether he would show him respect. The official went to force him to work and said: "I will not spare your life, but I will take you away."—Joshua 24:17-19.
But Leveka refused to spare his life because of forcing him to work, and he considered whether he would punish him. His life was worth only about 95 liters of water! Ten more lives were valued like this, and Leveka thought much about it. And it appeared that those ten lives were also worth much. * And now we ask ourselves, could Leveka have known that if he caused him further harm, he would be punished? Yes. He was very afraid and wanted to say much to the messenger who did not recognize him. The messenger was pleased that Leveka punished the spies. And although he continued to test him again and again, he kept causing trouble.—Joshua 24:20, 21.
The example of Leveka should teach us a lesson. In the last days, people are proving themselves unreasonable. Because they are self-centered, people "are unreasonable," and they do not want to understand good advice. (2 Timothy 3:1-5) Christians must associate with those who are reasonable so that they can continue to live in harmony with the example of Leveka, who continued to test them again and again.
But Leveka did not allow this important matter to pass unnoticed. This matter involves life and death, and it is vital to seek guidance from Leveka. But Leveka wants us to be convinced, so this matter will strengthen our faith and make us more determined! And he asks: "Who are you, really? I will answer you, I assure you. Do you think your house is unique?" This matter proves that Leveka cares about the welfare of his people. And he has shown Leveka five times what he meant: "Come, both now and in the future, and let us discuss your case." Therefore, your case is very serious because this matter affects others as well. And Leveka shows how important it is for each person to examine his own heart.—Proverbs 24:22-28, 32.
Indeed, Leveka knows how to discern hearts. Many people try to discern hearts, and that is why we can trust Leveka's ability to discern. To fear God means to be motivated to discern what is right. Jehovah is the One who discerns hearts, and he sees the value of everyone, and he wants us to imitate him. Let us show love for all our brothers, even those who cause us trouble.—Matthew 5:44-46; 1 Peter 4:9.
"SEND YOUR SON TO ME"
What was this important matter? It involved Abraham. Abraham was visited by an angel of Leveka. He was sent to Bethuel's house, the sister of Leveka. Then he asked the servant to go and find a wife for Isaac. * But when he arrived at Bethuel's house, he was given hospitality, and he explained his mission and purpose. (Proverbs 24:31-33) So let us learn something from this incident, which demonstrates the activity and purposes of Jehovah God. What lessons can we draw?
Bethuel's sister, Leveka, and her son Laban, were very hospitable to Eliezer and offered him food and water. They inquired whether Jehovah had directed Abraham to send him to seek a wife for his son Isaac, so that he could settle him among his relatives in their land.—Proverbs 24:34-38.
Abraham sent Eliezer to find a wife for Isaac among the daughters of Canaan. Why did he do so? Because the Canaanites did not worship Jehovah God and they did not obey him. And Abraham wanted his son to associate only with those who feared Jehovah and who would uphold true worship. Abraham desired that his son Isaac have a wife from among his own relatives, so that his descendants would remain loyal to Jehovah.—Genesis 15:16; 17:19; 24:2-4.
Eliezer went to Mesopotamia and prayed that he might meet a woman who was willing to give water to him and his camels, thus showing kindness to Jehovah God. He prayed to Jehovah to let the young woman whom he asked for water come forward willingly. He said, 'Let it be the one who offers water to my camels and also gives me something to drink.' (Genesis 24:12-14) But how would Eliezer know which woman Jehovah had chosen? It was Rebekah! As soon as she heard about Eliezer's request, she quickly ran down and offered water to him and his camels!
Bethuel and Laban were impressed by Eliezer's manner. They said, "This matter has come from Jehovah." So they agreed to the proposal, and Rebekah consented to become Isaac's wife. (Genesis 24:50-54) But what shows that Rebekah was truly willing and happy to marry Isaac?
It was customary for Eliezer to present valuable gifts to Abraham's relatives when asking for a wife for Isaac. And Abraham gave him instructions: "You will ask for a woman from among my relatives." (Genesis 24:39, 41) Bethuel and his family readily accepted Rebekah's gifts. Eliezer was anxious to continue his journey and take Rebekah back to Canaan, so he hurried on. The members of Rebekah's family delayed him for ten days. Then they said, "We should wait until she is old enough; then she can go with you."—Genesis 24:57.
Rebekah was faced with a difficult decision. Did she hesitate at all? Perhaps she wondered whether leaving her family and homeland to go to a land she did not know would be wise? Or perhaps she considered whether this arrangement was really approved by Jehovah? Her feelings were expressed in just one word: "I will go."—Genesis 24:58.
Rebekah showed great faith. It is not always easy to make important decisions, and we often need much information before making them. But Rebekah realized that what mattered most was pleasing Jehovah God, not simply doing what she wanted. God's standards require us to put spiritual matters first in our lives. Let us remember that true happiness comes from being in harmony with God's will and from living according to His principles. (2 Corinthians 6:14, 15; Ephesians 5:28-33) So, it is vital to imitate Rebekah's faith and to seek guidance from God.
"WHO IS THAT MAN?"
Betuel and his servant greeted Rebekah. And along with Rebekah, and Deborah, her nurse, they brought many gifts and provisions to Eliezer and his men. (Genesis 24:59-61; 35:8) They traveled a great distance to Canaan. The journey was about 500 miles (800 kilometers), and it took three days. However, this journey was not difficult. Rebekah saw many fine things, but we can be sure that she was more interested in learning about God. The Bible shows that Rebekah's servant may have had concerns, but I am convinced that the people who were traveling with them were eager to learn about God. (Genesis 29:10) Many people who did not fear God perished because of their greed, and they met a tragic end like that of a foolish man!
Rebekah understood the importance of what was happening, and she wanted Eliezer to help Isaac greatly, just as she helped her own husband. She sent her servant with Rebekah and many young women with her supplies, so that he could help her fulfill the purpose that Jehovah had given Abraham. By means of Abraham's faith, God showed that he approves of someone who is devoted to him and to others. Because of this, Rebekah realized that Jehovah would fulfill his purpose through Isaac, whom he promised to bless, or perhaps even through herself!—Genesis 22:15-18.
And so, when the time came for them to leave, they went along with the messengers. Some people from Nahor's family, Rebekah saw a man who was showing kindness. This man was willing to work hard. The Bible says: "[Rebekah] offered to give him water," and she quickly gave him something to eat. Then she said: "May I please have some water?" And she added: "Is there room enough for me to stay overnight?" But Rebekah knew that it was Isaac, she lowered her head and covered her face. (Genesis 24:62-65) Why did she do that? It was because she heard about Isaac, whom he was going to marry. Some men with her were amazed at how quickly she responded to Rebekah's request. So she thought that maybe she and her companions should be allowed to stay overnight, and then they could continue their journey.
Isaac was forty years old, and he had been troubled because his father, Abraham, wanted him to marry. It shows that Isaac was a kind and considerate man. How wonderful it is for a man to show love, kindness, and consideration! What lessons can we learn from the example of Isaac and Rebekah? The Bible says that Isaac 'was comforting' Rebekah.—Genesis 24:67; 26:8.
So let us think about Rebekah and her fine qualities, and also remember that she was only three thousand nine hundred years old at the time. We can imitate her by showing love, kindness, consideration, and hospitality. May we always be comforted by the example of Rebekah!
^ par. 10 Rebekah hurried to unload the gifts for the messengers. The account shows that Rebekah was very busy for many hours. It also shows that she willingly helped others, and it states that she was a generous person who was happy to help those who were tired.
^ par. 15 Elisha was given a special assignment on this occasion, and he proved himself faithful to the messenger who sent him. He went to meet Abraham to offer him his service. See how similar this is to a son offering his father his services, and how pleased the father is, Elisha became the chief servant and was honored by Abraham. And so, the servant who was given this assignment did what was appropriate.—Genesis 15:2; 24:2-4.

text:
"Anenga ĩmwe mbesa sya talendi itano, na ĩngĩ sya talendi ilĩ, na ĩngĩ sya talendi ĩmwe."
1, 2. Nĩkĩ Yesũ wanenganie ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi?
NTHĨNĨ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi, Yesũ nĩwonanĩtye nesa ũndũ mũna aatĩĩi make etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩle kwĩanĩsya. Nĩtwaĩle kũelewa ngelekany'o ĩsu nũndũ nĩkonetye Aklĩsto onthe ma w'o, methĩwe me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala ĩtunĩ kana nĩ wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ.
2 Yesũ anenganie ngelekany'o ĩsu ĩvinda yĩla wasũngĩaa amanyĩw'a make ĩkũlyo yĩĩ mamũkũlilye: "Wonan'yo nĩ wĩva wa kũka kwaku [kana, kũsumbĩka kwaku wĩ mũsumbĩ ũtenekee], na wa wĩanĩu wa ĩvinda yĩĩ?" (Mt. 24:3) Kwoou ngelekany'o ĩsu ĩanĩaa ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ yitũ na nĩ ĩmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala monanasya kana Yesũ nĩ Mũsumbĩ.
3. Ngelekany'o ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo kĩlungunĩ kya 24 na kya 25 itũmanyĩasya kyaũ?
3 Ngelekany'o ya talendi nĩ ĩmwe katĩ wa ngelekany'o inya ikonanĩtye, ila iandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo 24:45 nginya 25:46. Ila ingĩ itatũ nĩ ĩla ngelekany'o ya ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ, ya eĩtu ĩkũmi, na ya malondu na mbũi. O nasyo isu itatũ ainenganie ĩla wasũngĩaa ĩkũlyo ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩkonany'a kana nũsumbĩkĩte e mũsumbĩ ũtenekee. Nthĩnĩ wa ngelekany'o syonthe inya, Yesũ nĩwonanĩtye nguma ila itonya kũtuma aatĩĩi make ma w'o methĩwa me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo. Aumisye ngelekany'o ya ngombo yĩ na kĩthito, ya eĩtu, na ya talendi kwondũ wa aatĩĩi make etĩkĩw'a mauta. Mbee, nthĩnĩ wa ngelekany'o ya ngombo yĩ na kĩthito, Yesũ onanĩtye kana no nginya kĩkundi kĩnini kya etĩkĩw'a mauta kĩla kĩnengetwe kĩanda kya kũĩthya ala ma nyũmba yake mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo kĩthĩwe na kĩthito na ũĩ. Kelĩ, nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya eĩtu, Yesũ akindĩlĩle kana aatĩĩi make onthe etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩle kwĩkala meyũmbanĩtye na me metho, mesĩ kana Yesũ nĩwũkĩte, o na ethĩwa mayĩsĩ mũthenya kana saa. Mũthya, nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi Yesũ onanĩtye kana etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩle kwĩanĩsya ianda syoo sya Kĩklĩsto me athangaau. Ĩndĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi, Yesũ aneenete na ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. Akindĩlĩle kana maĩle kwĩthĩwa me aĩkĩĩku na maikwata mbau vyũ etĩkĩw'a mauta ala me kũũ nthĩ, ala nĩmo ana-a-asa ma Yesũ. * Ekai yu tũneenee ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi.
VWANA NĨWANENGIE NGOMBO SYAKE ŨTHWII WAKE
4, 5. Vwana ũla ũwetetwe ĩla ngelekany'onĩ nũũ, na talendi ĩmwe ĩana ata?
4 Soma Mathayo 25:14-30. Kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mavuku maitũ methĩĩtwe maielesya kana vwana ũla ũwetetwe ngelekany'onĩ ĩsu nĩ Yesũ, na kana aendie nthĩ ĩngĩ ĩla waendie ĩtunĩ mwaka wa 33. Nthĩnĩ wa ngelekany'o ĩngĩ, Yesũ nĩwawetie kĩeleelo kyake kya kũthi nthĩ ĩngĩ, nakyo nĩ 'kũnengwa ũsumbĩ.' (Luka 19:12) Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaatw'ĩka Mũsumbĩ avika ĩtunĩ o ũu. * Vandũ va ũu aendie "ekala nthĩ ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwa aũme kwa Ngai; [na] kuma ĩvinda yĩu [eeteela] amaitha make matwiwe kavĩla ka nyaĩĩ syake."—Aevl. 10:12, 13.
5 Vwana ũla ũwetetwe ngelekany'onĩ ĩsu aĩ na talendi nyanya, nasyo syaĩ ũthwii mwingĩ mũno ĩvindanĩ yĩu. * Atanamba kũthi nthĩ ĩngĩ anengie ngombo syake talendi isu, na endaa iitandĩthye amina kũthi. O ta vwana ũsu, Yesũ aĩ na kĩndũ kya vata mũno atanamba kũthi ĩtunĩ. Kĩndũ kyaũ? Ũsũngĩo ũkonetye wĩa ũla watethasya e kũũ nthĩ.
6, 7. Talendi nĩ kyaũ?
6 Yesũ oonaa wĩa wake wa kũtavany'a na kũmanyĩsya wĩ wa vata mũno. (Soma Luka 4:43.) Aitethya wĩa ũsu no ta ũndũ ũmwe na waseũvasya mũũnda weesĩ nesa ũkasyaa mũno. Mbeenĩ eethĩĩtwe atavĩtye amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "Ũngalalyai metho menyu, mũsisye mĩũnda, kana nĩ mĩathĩku kũvika ũkethwa." (Yoa. 4:35-38) Aiweta ndeto isu nĩweesĩ kana andũ angĩ aingĩ me na ngoo nthalĩku makatw'ĩka amanyĩw'a make. Nũndũ wa ũu, Yesũ ndaĩ esa kũthi atavangĩthĩtye maũndũ, o tondũ mũĩmi mũseo wĩ na mũũnda mũathĩku ũtesa kũthi atavangĩthĩtye ũndũ ũkakethwa. Nĩkyo kĩtumi amina kũthayũũkw'a oou na atanamba kũthi ĩtunĩ wanengie amanyĩw'a make wĩa mũna maaĩle kũwosa kwa ũito akĩmea atĩĩ: "Endai ĩndĩ mũkatw'ĩkĩthye [andũ] amanyĩw'a." (Mt. 28:18-20) Ĩla wamanengie wĩa ũsu wa kũtavany'a, no ũndũ ũmwe na wamanengie ũthwii wa mwanya.—2 Ako. 4:7.
7 Kwoou tũtonya kwasya ata? Ĩla Yesũ wanengie aatĩĩi make wĩa wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a, no ũndũ ũmwe na wamanengie "ũthwii wake," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, talendi syake. (Mt. 25:14) O kwa ũkuvĩ, talendi nĩ kĩanda kya kũtavany'a na kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a.
8. O na kau vwana ndaanenga ngombo syake talendi ianene, endaa syĩke ata?
8 Ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi yonanĩtye kana vwana anengie ngombo ĩmwe yake talendi itano, ĩngĩ ilĩ, na ĩla ĩngĩ talendi ĩmwe. (Mt. 25:15) O na kau vwana ndaanenga ngombo syake talendi ianene, endaa i ngombo syonthe itandĩthye talendi isu na ũthangaau. O ta ũu, Yesũ endaa aatĩĩi make etĩkĩw'a mauta meke kĩla kyonthe matonya wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. (Mt. 22:37; Ako. 3:23) Kwambĩĩa Vendekosito ya mwaka wa 33, aatĩĩi ma Klĩsto nĩmambĩĩe kũtandĩthya talendi syoo. Ũthangaau woo wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a na kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a nũeleetw'e nesa Mbivilianĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku ya Meko ma Atũmwa. *—Meko 6:7; 12:24; 19:20.
KŨTANDĨTHYA ILA TALENDI ĨVINDANĨ YĨĨ YA MŨMINŨKĨLYO
9. (a) Ila ngombo ilĩ nthangaau syeekanie na ila talendi ata, na ũu wĩonany'a kyaũ? (b) "Malondu angĩ" me na kĩanda kĩva?
9 Ĩvindanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo na mũno mũno kwambĩĩa mwaka wa 1919, etĩkĩw'a mauta ala aĩkĩĩku, kana ngombo sya Klĩsto, nĩmethĩĩtwe maitandĩthya talendi sya Vwana wasyo. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩmathũkũmĩthĩtye kĩla me nakyo ũndũ matonya o ta ila ngombo ilĩ. Ĩndĩ vai vata wa kwambĩĩa kwatatĩthya nũũ wakwatie talendi itano kana nũũ wakwatie ilĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ngelekany'o ĩsu yonanĩtye kana ngombo isu syatandĩthisye kĩla syanengetwe syakwata kũndũ kwĩlĩ, na kwoou nĩsyeaneny'e ũthangaau. Namo ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ me na kĩanda kĩva? Me na kĩanda kya vata mũno! Ĩla ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya malondu na mbũi ĩtũmanyĩasya kana ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ nĩmaĩlĩte kũlũmany'a na ana-a-asa ma Yesũ, etĩkĩw'a mauta, wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a na wa kũmanyĩsya. Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, ikundi isu ilĩ ithũkũmaa syĩ vamwe ta "ĩĩthya yĩmwe," iithũkũma na kĩthito wĩa wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a.—Yoa. 10:16.
10. Nĩ wonany'o ũmwe wĩva wa vata wa kana Yesũ nũsumbĩkĩte e mũsumbĩ ũtenekee?
10 Vwana e na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwenda amanyĩw'a make mathũkũmĩthye talendi nesa. O tondũ vawetetwe mwambĩĩonĩ, amanyĩw'a aĩkĩĩku ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa nĩmongelile ũthwii wa Vwana woo. Nao nata ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi ĩendeee kwĩanĩa? Athũkũmi ma Yesũ aĩkĩĩku na athangaau nĩmathũkũmĩte mũno wĩa wa kũtavany'a na wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a mbee wa ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva. Kĩthito kyoo, vamwe na ngwatanĩo yoo nĩkĩtumaa andũ aingĩ matw'ĩka amanyĩw'a namo makambĩĩa kũtavany'a. Wĩa ũsu matethetye vamwe na mosyao maseo ala makwatĩte ũtumĩte kũtavany'a kwĩthĩwa kwĩ wonany'o ũmwe wa vata wa kana Yesũ nũsumbĩkĩte e mũsumbĩ ũtenekee. No nginya kyu kĩthĩwe kĩtumĩte Vwana woo ew'a mũyo mũno!
NĨ ĨNDĨĨ VWANA ŨKOKA KWĨKA MASAVU?
11. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Yesũ akoka kwĩka masavu ĩvindanĩ ya ũla thĩna mũnene?
11 Yesũ akoka kwĩka masavu na ngombo syake thĩna ũla mũnene ũkilyĩ kũthela. Thĩna ũsu wĩ vakuvĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ tũkwasya kana akoka kwĩka masavu ĩvinda yĩu? Yesũ nũwetete ĩũlũ wa kũka kwake mavinda maingĩ nthĩnĩ wa wathani wake ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo kĩlungu kya 24 na kya 25. Ĩla wawetaa ĩũlũ wa ũsilĩlo wa ĩvinda ya ũla thĩna mũnene, aisye kana andũ "makoona Mwana wa mũndũ okĩte ĩũlũ wa mathweo ma ĩtu." Nĩkyo kĩtumi weesũvie aatĩĩi make ala makethĩwa mĩthenyanĩ ĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo mekale me metho. Ameie atĩĩ: "Mũtyĩsĩ mũthenya ũla Mwĩaĩi wenyu wĩũka," na "saa ũla mũtataĩĩe nĩw'o wĩũka ũla Mwana wa mũndũ." (Mt. 24:30, 42, 44) Kwoou ĩla Yesũ waisye kana 'vwana wa ngombo isu nĩwookie, na atalana nasyo,' awetaa ĩvinda yĩla we ũkoka kũsilĩla andũ na kwananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku. *—Mt. 25:19.
12, 13. (a) Vwana atavisye ila ngombo ilĩ sya mbee ata, na nĩkĩ? (b) Nĩ ĩndĩĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta makekĩwa ũsiĩlo wa mũthya? (Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Nĩmanenganae Ĩsavu Yoo Ĩvindanĩ ya Kũkw'a.") (c) Ala makaiwa ngalĩ ya malondu makanengwa ĩtuvi yĩva?
12 Ĩla ngelekany'o yonanĩtye kana ĩla vwana wookie eethĩie ila ngombo ilĩ sya mbee itandĩthĩtye na kĩthito ila talendi wainengete. Ĩla yanengiwe itano yakwatie ingĩ itano, na ĩla yanengiwe ilĩ yakwatie ingĩ ilĩ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ vwana watavisye kĩla ĩmwe ya ngombo isu ilĩ ũũ: "Nĩwĩkĩte nesa, ngombo nzeo na ĩla yĩ na kĩthito: Waĩ na kĩthito ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ mbũthũ, ngakwia ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ nyingĩ." (Mt. 25:21, 23) Kwoou tweteele kyaũ ĩla Vwana, ũla nĩwe Yesũ, ũkoka kũsilĩla andũ na kwananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku?
13 Ngombo sya mbee ilĩ nĩ aatĩĩi ma Yesũ etĩkĩw'a mauta ala me kĩthito, na makeethĩwa mekĩĩtwe ũsiĩlo woo wa mũthya thĩna ũla mũnene ũtanamba kwambĩĩa. (Ũvu. 7:1-3) Na ĩndĩ kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni ũtanamba kũkitwa, Yesũ akamanenga ĩtuvi yĩla mathĩtwe ya kũthi ĩtunĩ. Nata ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ na makethĩwa makwatie ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto mbau wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a? Asu makethĩwa manasilĩlwa makaiwa ngalĩ ya malondu, na nĩmo makanewa mwanya wa kwĩkala vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai.—Mt. 25:34.
NGOMBO NTHŨKU NA NDULU
14, 15. We Yesũ oonanasya kana aingĩ ma etĩkĩw'a mauta makeethĩwa me athũku na me atulu? Elesya.
14 Nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o, ngombo ĩla ya katatũ yenzĩie nthĩ talendi yayo vandũ va kũmĩtandĩthya kana kũmĩia vengi ĩkwate ũsyao. Ngombo ĩsu yaĩ nthũku nũndũ nĩyaleile na ngũlũ kwĩka ũndũ vwana wayo wendaa. Kwoou vwana wayo aĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũmĩta ngombo "nthũku na ndulu." Nũndũ wa ũu, nĩwamĩvenie ĩ talendi na anenga ngombo ĩla yaĩ na talendi ĩkũmi. Ĩtina wa kĩu ngombo ĩsu nthũku nĩyekiw'e "kĩvindunĩ nza." Vau nĩvo yeethĩiwe na "kĩĩo na kũvevetan'ya maeo."—Mt. 25:24-30; Luka 19:22, 23.
15 Nũndũ ngombo ĩmwe katĩ wa ila itatũ yeekie kwĩnzĩa nthĩ talendi yayo, we Yesũ nĩwĩthĩwa endaa kwonany'a kana mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta ũmwe katĩ wa kĩla etĩkĩw'a mauta atatũ akeethĩwa e mũthũku na mũtulu? Aiee. Nĩkĩ? Kwasũanĩa ũvoo ũla ũthyũlũlũkĩte ngelekany'o ĩsu. Nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ, Yesũ nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa ngombo ĩmwe nthũku ĩkavũa ila ingĩ. Ĩndĩ vau Yesũ ndathanaa kana vakaumĩla kĩkundi kĩna kĩthũku kya etĩkĩw'a mauta. Vandũ va ũu, eekaa kũkany'a ĩla ngombo yĩ na kĩthito ndĩkese kwĩthĩwa ĩilyĩ ta ngombo ĩsu nthũku. O ta ũu, nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya eĩtu, Yesũ ndoonanasya kana nusu ya etĩkĩw'a mauta ĩkeethĩwa ĩilyĩ ta ala eĩtu atano atumanu. Vandũ va ũu, akanasya ana-a-asa make ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩtonya kwĩsa kũmakwata maema kwĩkala me metho na meyũmbanĩtye. * Kwoou kwosana na ngelekany'o isu, no twasye kana ĩla Yesũ wanenganie ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi ndendaa kwonany'a kana mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo aingĩ ma ana-a-asa make etĩkĩw'a mauta makeethĩwa me athũku na me atulu. Vandũ va ũu Yesũ akanasya aatĩĩi make etĩkĩw'a mauta mekale me metho, kana kwa nzĩa ĩngĩ 'matethye wĩa' na talendi syoo, na maitata maikethĩwe na mawoni kana meko mailyĩ ma ĩla ngombo nthũku.—Mt. 25:16.
16. (a) Ngelekany'o ya talendi yĩtũmanyĩsya maũndũ meva? (b) Ĩsomo yĩĩ yatũtetheesya ata kũelewa nesanga ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi? (Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Ũndũ Twaĩle Kũelewa Ĩla Ngelekany'o ya Talendi.")
16 Ngelekany'o ya talendi yĩtũmanyĩsya maũndũ meva elĩ? Ũndũ wa mbee, Vwana, ũla nĩwe Klĩsto, nũnengete etĩkĩw'a mauta, kana ngombo syake, kĩndũ we mwene wonaa kĩ kya vata mũno, nakyo nĩ wĩa wa kũtavany'a na kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a. Ũndũ wa kelĩ, Klĩsto endaa ithyonthe twĩthĩwe twĩ athangaau ĩla twĩ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Naitũ tweethĩwa twĩ athangaau wĩanĩ ũsu, na twekala twĩ metho, twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, na twĩ aĩkĩĩku, nĩtwĩkalei twĩsĩ kana Vwana ndakalea kũtũnenga ĩtuvi.—Mt. 25:21, 23, 34.

Na ĩndĩ ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi nĩeleetw'e ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/10/1995, ĩthangũnĩ ya 23-28, na ĩkasyoka ĩkaelew'a ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe ĩkasetinĩ yĩĩ.

translation:
"He gave to one five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent."
1, 2. Why did Jesus tell the illustration of the talents?
THE purpose of the illustration of the talents is that Jesus wanted us to understand something important about our ministry—how we use what we have been entrusted with. It will help us to appreciate this illustration if we consider what it means to be faithful or unfaithful.
2 Jesus told this illustration to answer a question his disciples asked him: "When will these things happen, and what will be the sign of your presence?" (Matt. 24:3) This illustration shows us that those events will come unexpectedly, and it is one way to recognize when Jesus is present.
3. What does the illustrations found in Matthew chapters 24 and 25 teach us?
3 The illustration of the talents is one of several illustrations that Jesus used, but it is recorded in Matthew 24:45 onward and 25:46. Other illustrations include that of the slave and the steward, that of the ten virgins, and that of the sheep and the goats. All three illustrations show how important it is for his followers to be diligent and ready when the master returns. Because of these illustrations, Jesus wanted to impress upon his disciples the importance of using their privileges wisely. He used the illustrations of the slave and the steward, of the virgins, and of the talents to remind them of their responsibility. Therefore, because of the illustrations of the slave and the steward, Jesus showed that a large group of responsible people would be rewarded for being loyal to their master's interests and for being diligent. Also, because of the illustration of the virgins, Jesus indicated that his faithful ones should always be prepared to meet him, even if he comes at an unexpected hour. Moreover, because of the illustration of the talents, Jesus showed that responsible people would be rewarded for making progress in spreading the good news. And because of the illustration of the sheep and the goats, Jesus distinguished between those who would be blessed and those who would be cursed. * Let us now examine the illustration of the talents.
THE SLAVE IS REWARDED FOR HIS FAITHFULNESS
4, 5. What does the illustration teach about the responsibilities of slaves, and what about the talent itself?
4 Read Matthew 25:14-30. In view of what happened when the master went away on a journey, what lesson can we learn from the fact that the slave was entrusted with the possessions? And how did this relate to Jesus, and to the time when he went up to heaven in 33 C.E.? Because of another illustration, Jesus showed his disciples what it means to 'be appointed over possessions.' (Luke 19:12) But Jesus did not actually appoint anyone to be such a steward during that time. * Those people will go into "the place where his master went; and they will receive their reward." – Rev. 10:12, 13.
5 The slave entrusted with the possessions had talents, and also a great deal of responsibility. * He gave an account of what he had done with his talents, and he proved himself faithful. But Jesus had something more to say about what he would do with the faithful one. What was it? He would give him authority over cities.
6, 7. What are talents?
6 Jesus continued to teach and to declare good news. (Read Luke 4:43.) He said that he had to preach the good news of the Kingdom because that was why he was sent out. However, many did not accept his message, so he used illustrations to help them understand. For example, he said: "Four months from now there will be a harvest, and look! The field is already white for harvesting." (John 4:35-38) He kept traveling and teaching others, while many others were busy doing nothing. Therefore, Jesus did not hesitate to spend time teaching people, even though some may have thought that he should be spending his time doing something more important. This is why he commissioned his followers to continue preaching, telling them: "Go and make disciples of all nations." (Matt. 28:18-20) So, like those men, we too have something to be zealous about.—2 Cor. 4:7.
7 What can we learn from this? Well, Jesus entrusted his disciples with the work of making more disciples, and also what is called his "authority," or, literally, his talents. (Matt. 25:14) And so, a talent represents something to be developed and used to make more disciples.
8 But how would each slave respond to receiving a large amount of his master's talents, and what does this mean?
8 In fact, one slave received five talents, another two, and still another one. (Matt. 25:15) But how would each slave respond to receiving a large amount of his master's talents, and what does this mean? Also, Jesus told his disciples to love God with their whole heart and soul and mind. (Matt. 22:37; Acts 3:23) Beginning in the year 33 C.E., his disciples began to develop their talents. Their zeal for developing and using their talents to make more disciples was highlighted in the book of Acts. *—Acts 6:7; 12:24; 19:20.
DEVELOPING YOUR INDIVIDUAL TALENTS
9. (a) How does zeal relate to our talents, and what does this mean? (b) Where does the expression "spiritual gifts" come from?
9 Since 1919, faithful Christians have been experiencing an increase in spiritual understanding, and zeal has played a vital role, just like zeal did in Christ's time, in helping us make good use of our talents. Brothers and sisters who have increased their spiritual activity often find that they can accomplish more than they could before. Why is this? Because when we put zeal behind our efforts, we see things more clearly and we are motivated to work harder. But what about those who feel limited in what they can do? Should they be discouraged if they only have one or two talents? No, because Jehovah values zeal, regardless of how many talents we have. Jesus' illustration regarding spiritual gifts shows that Jehovah appreciates those who use whatever talents they have diligently. This is why zealous brothers and sisters are able to accomplish so much in the ministry, and why they enjoy doing it. The further advance of true worship, including the uniting of all others, depends on our willingness to preach and to teach.—John 10:16.
10. How does the example of Jesus show that he is willing to give help to his followers?
10 The Son sent out his disciples to preach, and they used the talents they had effectively. Although imperfect, these preachers were instruments for conveying God's message. And does the further advance of true worship depend on our using our talents zealously? Yes, Jesus' apostles and other first-century servants worked hard to spread the good news. Their zeal, along with God's spirit, moved people to respond favorably. However, some may feel that they lack the ability to preach effectively. They might think that they do not have the necessary talents. What can such ones do? How can they imitate the example of Jesus in being willing to ask for help? Let us now examine what happened when Jesus sent out his disciples. It truly demonstrates the great value that the Son places on zeal!
WHY SHOULD THE SON BE GLORIFIED?
11. What reason do we have for believing that Jesus is able to provide strength for us in the ministry?
11 Jesus can provide strength through his spirit and through a strong desire to please Jehovah. He feels deeply about this. But how can we be sure that he will provide strength for us individually? Jesus gave ample evidence of his power to strengthen others during his earthly ministry, as recorded in the Gospels of Matthew chapters 24 and 25. He foretold events that would occur in connection with the destruction of the Jewish temple system, and he showed that people would say, "Look! The Son of man is coming with the clouds!" This is why faithful Christians today pay attention to the signs of the times. He said: "When you see all these things, know that the kingdom of God is near," and "that hour you do not know. The Son of man will come at an unexpected time." (Matt. 24:30, 42, 44) So, just as Jesus indicated that 'the faithful slave is discreet and gives them food at the proper time,' he also shows that he will empower his servants to proclaim the good news and to withstand opposition.—Matt. 25:19.
12, 13. (a) What did the master do with the talents, and why? (b) Why is it important to use our gifts fully? (See the box "How Can You Make Good Use of Your Gifts?") (c) What questions will we now answer?
12 The master entrusted five talents to one slave, two to another, and one to still another. He then went on a journey. Upon returning, he settled accounts with them. Those who had made more gained more, and those who had made less lost what they had. This illustrates what each of us should do with the abilities we have been given: "Use what you have been entrusted with, until I return." (Matt. 25:21, 23) How, then, does Jesus empower his servants to proclaim the good news and to withstand opposition?
13 The slave with one talent was afraid that Jesus would entrust him with more than he could handle, so he hid it. (Rev. 7:1-3) Similarly, some Christians may fear being assigned responsibilities they feel unqualified for. But how can they overcome this fear and continue to serve Christ faithfully? Are there ways to gain experience and develop skills so that they can contribute more to God's work?—Matt. 25:34.
THE JUDGING OF THE NATIONS
14, 15. What will Jesus determine when judging the nations, and what will be the result? Let us see.
14 In illustration, imagine three slaves each entrusted with a certain amount of money—say, five talents. Two of them use their talents to make a profit, while the third hides his. This slave is fearful and does nothing with what he has been given. Because of this, his master calls him "wicked and lazy." He had the ability to invest the talent, but he did not. That is why the master takes away the talent from him and gives it to the slave who had ten talents. Thus, the slave who was lazy is called "worthless." This illustrates the principle that those who misuse what they have been entrusted with will lose it.—Matt. 25:24-30; Luke 19:22, 23.
15 Now, if one of these three slaves were to say, 'I am afraid I might lose the talent,' would Jesus approve of such an attitude? No. Why not? Consider the example we discussed earlier. In illustration, Jesus showed that a slave who was afraid lost even what little he had. So, if someone fears losing what he has been entrusted with, he should not be given more responsibility. Otherwise, in illustration, Jesus would take away even what little he has and give it to others who can handle greater responsibility. Those people will then increase their possessions. Therefore, let us examine how we use what we have been entrusted with so that we may prove ourselves faithful and discreet. * As we reflect on this illustration, let us see whether we are like the slave who hid his talent because he feared his master. Let us also examine our hearts to see whether we are using our talents to the full extent, and whether we are making spiritual progress.—Matt. 25:16.
16. (a) What does the illustration of the talents teach us? (b) What lesson can we learn from understanding the meaning of the illustration of the talents? (See the box "What We Can Learn From the Illustration of the Talents.")
16 What further does the illustration of the talents teach us? In effect, Christ, through his faithful slaves, entrusts us with possessions, or our ministry, and expects us to use what we have been given to help others. Furthermore, Christ expects all of us to make good use of the privileges we have received, and if we do so zealously, diligently, and loyally, we will be approved by the Master.—Matt. 25:21, 23, 34.
^ kal. 3 The Ministry School publication of July 1, 2013, pages 27-28, paragraphs 8-10, shows how boldness and courage are needed. And the lesson from that publication also showed how to apply it. Also, the illustration of the lost sheep was featured in the Ministry School (Swahili) publication of October 15, 1995, pages 23-28, and then the point of the lesson was explained in connection with that publication.
^ kal. 4 See the box "How the Illustration of the Talents Relates to the Last Days."
^ kal. 5 According to Jesus, one talent was equal to six thousand [denarii]. A skilled worker could earn one denarius per day, so he would need about 20 years to earn one talent.
^ kal. 8 Because of Satan's influence, the weeds were sown among the wheat, and they continued to grow for many years. This illustrates how the faithful slaves help others to learn about Christ. Moreover, those who do not appreciate spiritual things are often influenced by weeds. (Matt. 13:24-30, 36-43) See the Ministry School publication of July 1, 2013, pages 15-19.
^ kal. 11 See the Ministry School publication of July 1, 2013, pages 13-14, paragraphs 14-18.

text:
"Kuma kwake mwĩĩ w'onthe, [nũkomanĩtw'e] nesa na kũkwatanw'a."—AEV. 4:16.
MBATHI: 53, 16
1. Nĩ kyaũ kyambĩĩe kwoneka mawĩanĩ ma Ngai kuma tene?
NGWATANĨO yambĩĩe kwoneka tene kuma o ĩla syĩndũ syoombawa. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mwana mũsyawa wa mbee wa Ngai, ũla ũwetetwe tawe ũĩ, aisye atĩĩ: "Naĩ vakuvĩ nake [Yeova], mũthũkũmi mũnene; na naĩ ũtanu wake kĩla mũthenya." (Nth. 8:30) Ĩvindanĩ ya wũmbi Mwana nĩwathũkũmie na Ĩthe me ngwatanĩo. Ve angĩ maĩ na ngwatanĩo ta ĩsu maitethya wĩa wa Ngai. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii: Noa ayaka ngalawa amyakie e ngwatanĩo na angĩ. Na ĩla andũ ma Ngai maĩ kyalonĩ mesĩle weũnĩ meethĩawa na ngwatanĩo mayamba yĩla ĩeema na maiyambũa nĩ kana mathame. O na ĩvinda yĩla kwaĩ ĩkalũ andũ maĩ no nginya methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nĩ kana makũne wathi nesa na mayina na mawasya mekwosana nesa maimũtaĩa Yeova. Mawĩa asu onthe mayaĩ mesa kũendeea vate ngwatanĩo.—Mwa. 6:14-16, 22; Mot. 4:4-32; 1 Mav. 25:1-8.
2. (a) Kĩla kĩkundi kya mbee kya Kĩklĩsto kyeesĩkĩe na nguma yĩva? (b) Nĩ makũlyo meva tũũneenea?
2 O na kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto kya ĩvinda ya atũmwa kyaĩ na ngwatanĩo ta ĩsu kĩtongoew'e nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aisye kana Aklĩsto asu onthe etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩ "mwĩĩ ũmwe" o na kũtw'ĩka kwaĩ "ivathũkan'yo sya mĩthĩnzĩo," kwaĩ na "ivathũkan'yo sya mothũkũmi," na "ivathũkan'yo sya kwĩka [kana, mawĩa]." (Soma 1 Akolintho 12:4-6, 12.) Ĩndĩ nata ũmũnthĩ? Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo? Na tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo kĩkundinĩ na mũsyĩ?
ĨTHĨWAI NA NGWATANĨO WĨANĨ WA KŨTAVANY'A
3. Mũtũmwa Yoana ooniw'e woni wĩva?
3 Mũminũkĩlyonĩ wa ĩvinda ya atũmwa, mũtũmwa Yoana nĩwooniw'e woni wa alaĩka mũonza, na kĩla mũlaĩka nĩwavuvie soo. Ĩla mũlaĩka wa katano wavuvie soo wake, Yoana oonie "ndata" yauma ĩtunĩ yavalũka nthĩ. "Ndata" ĩsu yaĩ na ũvungũo yavungũie ĩima yĩte kĩtulu naw'o. Ĩima yavingũwa, vatoie syũki yingĩ na vu syũkinĩ vaumĩla ngie itatalĩka. Ĩndĩ vandũ va ngie isu syanange nthĩ, syaendie kũla kwĩ "ala mate na ũsiĩlo wa Ngai itulyanĩ syoo." (Ũvu. 9:1-4) Yoana nĩweesĩ ũndũ ngie itonya kwananga vandũ. Ũu nĩw'o syaanangie nthĩ ya Misili ĩvinda ya Mose. (Kuma 10:12-15) Nũndũ ũmũnthĩ Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩmatavanasya ũvoo mũito wa ũsilĩlo wa Yeova, nĩmo maelekanĩtw'e na ngie ila Yoana woonie. Aklĩsto asu makwetwe mbau nĩ angĩ milioni mbingĩ ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. Nũndũ nĩtwĩthĩĩtwe na ngwatanĩo wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a, ti ũsengy'o kwona andũ aingĩ matiĩte ndĩni sya ũvũngũ makaeka kũtongoew'a nĩ Satani!
4. Nĩ wĩa wĩva andũ ma Ngai maĩle kwĩka, na nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũmatethya mawĩanĩsye?
4 Andũ ma Yeova me na wĩa mwingĩ mũno wa kũtavany'a ũla 'ũvoo mũseo' nthĩ yonthe mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno ũtanamba kũvika. (Mt. 24:14; 28:19, 20) Ũndũ ũmwe twĩkaa wĩanĩ ũsu nĩ kũthokya "ũla wĩ na waũni" oke anyw'e "manzĩ ma thayũ mana." (Ũvu. 22:17) Nĩkwĩthĩwa ithyonthe twĩ kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto, tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩanĩsye ũndũ ũsu nesa? Kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtethya no kwĩkala 'tũkomanĩtw'e nesa na tũkwatanĩtw'e,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kwĩkala twĩ na ngwatanĩo.—Aev. 4:16.
5, 6. Elesya ũndũ twĩthĩawa na ngwatanĩo wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo.
5 Nĩ kana tũvote kũtavya andũ aingĩ vyũ ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ, no nginya wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũtethw'e na mũvango. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi tũnengawe myolooto ya kũtethya wĩa ũsu. Myolooto ĩla ĩnengawe ikundi syonthe nthĩ yonthe nĩtũtetheeasya tũtethye wĩa na ngwatanĩo. Kĩla ĩvinda twamina ũmbano wa ũtavany'a nĩtumaalaa tũthi tũkatavye andũ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Tũmatavasya ũvoo ũsu kwa kũmaelesya kĩla kĩ Mbivilianĩ na kwa kũmanenga mavuku milioni mbingĩ me na ũvoo wa Mbivilia. We nĩwĩkĩaa kĩthito ũkwatane na ala angĩ ĩla tweewa kwĩ kambeini ya mwanya ya kũtavany'a? Ethĩwa nĩwĩkaa ũu, wĩthĩawa wĩ ngwatanĩo na angĩ milioni mbingĩ mũitavany'a ũla ũtũmane wĩ na 'mũlaĩka ũũlũkĩle ĩtunĩ katĩ,' o tondũ vawetetwe ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo 14:6.
6 Mũyo ũla twĩw'aa nĩ mwingĩ mũno ĩla twasoma ĩvukunĩ ya Kitabu cha Mwaka livoti ya wĩa ũla tũtethetye nthĩ yonthe. O na ĩngĩ, kwasũanĩa ngwatanĩo ĩla twĩthĩawa nayo ĩla tũũnyaĩĩkya tũvalũa twa kũthokya andũ maũmbanonĩ manene ma mwanya, ma mĩthenya ĩtatũ, na ma nthĩ mbingĩ. Maũmbanonĩ asu nĩtwĩthukĩĩasya maũvoo maseo mosanĩte na Maandĩko, o na nĩkwĩthĩawa ndulama na mawonany'o. Kaingĩ maũndũ asu methĩawa maũmbanonĩ asu matũtetheeasya kwona kana Ngai endaa tũmũthũkũme na vinya witũ w'onthe. Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtũkwatanĩtye vamwe nĩ kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mumo wa Ngai na ĩngĩ twendaa kwĩanĩsya mwĩao wa Yesũ, kĩla mwaka nĩtũmbanaa kwondũ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, na tũkomanaa matukũ 14 ma mwei wa Nisani syũa yamina kũthũa. (1 Ako. 11:23-26) Na ti Ngũsĩ syoka syaĩlĩte kũthi ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Syumwa siana ũna itiele nĩ kana tũlilikane kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, tũthokasya andũ aingĩ kĩsionĩ kĩnene ũndũ vatonyeka nĩ kana twĩthĩwe vamwe namo ũmbanonĩ ũsu.
7. Kũthũkũma twĩ ngwatanĩo kũtethetye ata?
7 Ngie ĩmwe ndĩ ĩndĩ yĩsa kwananga vandũ vanene. O ta ũu kĩthito kya mũndũ ũmwe no kĩeme kũtethya vanene. Ĩndĩ kũthũkũma twĩ ngwatanĩo nĩkũtumĩte tũtetheesya andũ milioni mbingĩ mamanye kana kwĩ Ngai wĩtawa Yeova, ũla waĩlĩte nguma na ndaĩa syonthe! O na ũu wĩ o vo, kũtavany'a ti kw'o kwĩ kw'oka kũtumaa andũ ma Ngai mekala me ngwatanĩo.
ĨTHĨWAI NA NGWATANĨO KĨKUNDINĨ
8, 9. (a) Nĩ ngelekany'o yĩva Vaulo watũmĩie amanyĩsye Aklĩsto kwĩkalaa me ngwatanĩo? (b) Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo kĩkundinĩ?
8 Valũanĩ ũla Vaulo waandĩkĩe Aeveso nĩwawetie ũndũ kĩkundi kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mĩvango, na aweta vata wa onthe 'kwĩana maũndũnĩ onthe.' (Soma Aeveso 4:15, 16.) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya kĩla ũmwe witũ avike vau? Nĩ kana Vaulo onany'e ngwatanĩo ĩla yĩthĩawa kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto kĩtongoew'e nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto, atũmĩie ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩ wa mũndũ. Mũtũmwa ũsu awetie kana mwĩĩ wĩthĩawa wĩ na ngwatanĩo "nũndũ wa ũtethyo wa kĩla ũleenyũ." Kĩla ũmwe witũ ethĩwe nĩ mũkũũ kana nĩ wa mũika, e na vinya kana nĩ mwonzu, atonya kũtethya kĩkundi ata kĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo na kĩiendeea nesa kĩ-veva?
9 Kĩndũ kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya vyũ nĩ kĩĩ: kwĩnyivĩsya na kũnenga ndaĩa ala Yesũ ũnyuvĩte matongoesye kĩkundi, namo nĩ atumĩa. (Aevl. 13:7, 17) Mavinda amwe no twĩw'e ũndũ ũsu ũte mũvũthũ kwĩanĩsya. Ĩndĩ no tũmũkũlye Ngai atũtetheesye, na tũyĩka ũu tũte na nzika kana nũkũtũtethya. Veva wake mũtheu no ũtũnenge vinya wa kũkwata mbau mĩvango ĩla yĩ kĩkundinĩ na ngoo yonthe. Kwoou ĩla twesa kwĩw'a tũiemwa nĩ kũatĩĩa mwolooto mũna, nũseo tũkasũanĩa ũndũ kwĩnyivya tũkwatĩanĩe na ala angĩ kũtonya kũete ngwatanĩo kĩkundinĩ. O na eka ũu, kũkwatĩanĩa na ala angĩ maũndũnĩ ta asu no kũtume ithyonthe twendana mũno.
10. Nĩ kĩthito kĩva atetheesya ma kĩkundi mekĩaa nĩ kana kĩkundi kĩkale kĩ ngwatanĩo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 13.)
10 Nĩtũtanaa mũno kwona kĩthito kĩla atetheesya ma kĩkundi mekĩaa nĩ kana kĩkundi kĩkale kĩ ngwatanĩo. Ana-a-asa asu, o na methĩwe me na myaka ĩana ata, meyumasya vyũ mathũkũme ala angĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩmatetheeasya atumĩa kwa kũĩkĩĩthya kana onthe kĩkundinĩ nĩmakwata mavuku ma kũtavany'a. O na ĩngĩ nĩmatheasya na makasũvĩa Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ, na no mo mathokasya aeni ala mooka ũmbanonĩ. Tweethĩwa twĩ ngwatanĩo na ana-a-asa asu tũkatumaa mĩvango ĩla yĩ kĩkundinĩ ĩendeea o ũndũ ĩvangĩtwe.—Sianĩsya na Meko ma Atũmwa 6:3-6.
11. Nĩ kyaũ andũ ma mũika matonya kwĩka nĩ kana matetheesye kĩkundi kĩkale kĩ ngwatanĩo?
11 Kwĩ ana-a-asa aingĩ aima me na myaka maikwatĩĩa mawĩa kĩkundinĩ. Na kwoou nũndũ maendeee na kũkũa, no kwĩthĩwa ve maũndũ amwe matatonya kwĩka, na nũndũ wa kĩtumi kĩu ũyĩthĩa moalyũku no mekiwe. Mavindanĩ ta asu ana-a-asa ma mũika methĩawa me ũtethyo mũnene vyũ. O na kau mai na ũmanyi mwingĩ, makamanyĩw'a no makwatĩĩe maũndũ maitango kĩkundinĩ. Wĩthĩawa wĩ ũseo ta kĩ kwona atetheesya ma kĩkundi mayĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana matw'ĩke atumĩa! (1 Tim. 3:1, 10) O na ve atumĩa amwe ma mũika mekĩte maendeeo nginya makalika wĩanĩ wa kũthyũlũlũka, makĩthũkũma ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ikundinĩ mbingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Ĩndĩ tyo tũtanaa kwona wĩa ũla amũika matethasya na ngoo ya kwenda?—Soma Savuli 110:3; Mũtavan'ya 12:1.
ĨTHĨWAI NA NGWATANĨO MŨSYĨ
12, 13. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya mĩsyĩ yĩkale yĩ ngwatanĩo?
12 Ekai ngewa ĩno ya ngwatanĩo tũmyamaangye twone ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo mũsyĩ. Aingĩ nĩmethĩĩte kana kwĩka Ũthaithi wa Mũsyĩ nesa kĩla kyumwa nĩkũlũlũmĩlasya ngwatanĩo katĩ wa asyai na syana. Mavinda asu methĩawa me maseo mũno na mausĩe maũndũ ma kĩ-veva, kwoou nĩmatetheeasya mũsyĩ wĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo. O na ĩngĩ kwĩyũmbanĩsya ũndũ mũtonya kũthi kũtavany'a no kũmũtetheesye inyw'onthe mwĩthĩwe mũtonya kũtavany'a nesa. O na mavinda maingĩ wĩthĩaa ĩla kĩla ũmwe weew'a ũla ũngĩ aielesya kĩla wemanyĩsya Ndetonĩ ya Ngai, na ĩla inyw'onthe mwoona kana mwendete Ngai ũla ũmwe na kana mwendaa kwĩka kwenda kwake, kyu kĩtumaa mwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo.
13 Ala matwaanĩte matonya kwĩka ata mekale na ngwatanĩo nĩ kana Yeova ataĩwe? Ethĩwa mũndũ na mũka nĩ athũkũmi aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova, no methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na kĩu nĩkĩmaeteae ũtanu mwingĩ mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ aa nĩmoonanasya wendo mĩtwaanonĩ yoo: Avalaamu na Sala, Isaka na Leveka, na Elikana na Aana. O naitũ twaĩlĩte kũtata twĩke o tamo. (Mwa. 26:8; 1 Sam. 1:5, 8; 1 Vet. 3:5, 6) Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtũthengeanĩasya na aũme maitũ kana na iveti sitũ, na kũituma twĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ.—Soma Mũtavan'ya 4:12.
14. Ethĩwa mũemeu kana kĩveti kyaku ti mũthũkũmi wa Yeova, ũtonya kwĩka ata mũtwaano wenyu wĩkale wĩ mũlũmu?
14 Aklĩsto mayaĩlĩte kwovanĩw'a ĩsoki yĩmwe na andũ mate etĩkĩli. (2 Ako. 6:14) Ĩndĩ nata ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala matwaanĩte na andũ mate Ngũsĩ? Amwe meemanyĩisye ũw'o me atwae kana matwaanĩte, na kwoou yu aũme kana aka moo ti Ngũsĩ. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia no kũtetheesye mĩsyĩ ta ĩsu ĩkethĩwa na ngwatanĩo. Nĩ kana kyu kĩthĩwe, ũla Ngũsĩ no atate ũndũ ũtonya akwatĩanĩe na ũla ũngĩ maũndũnĩ ĩndĩ aisisya ndakatũle mĩao ya Yeova. Kwĩka ũu no kwĩthĩwe kwĩ vinya ĩndĩ sũanĩa ũathimo ũla wĩ vo. Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kũtuma vethĩwa ve vinya kũatĩĩa myolooto ya Mbivilia nĩ ĩla ũla ũtwaanĩte nake watia kĩkundi. Ũndũ ta ũsu nĩwamũkwatie mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Mary. Mũũme etawa David na nĩmamũthũkũmaa Yeova ĩmwe, ĩndĩ myaka ta 25 mĩvĩtu David nĩwaekie kũthi maũmbanonĩ. Mary we ndaaeka kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi na maũmbanonĩ manene. O na nĩwatataa vyũ aatĩĩe myolooto ya Mbivilia mũsyĩ, ta kũmanyĩsya syana syoo thanthatũ. Ĩla syana syeanie na syauma mũsyĩ, eew'aa ũu ta wĩ weka. Ĩndĩ Mary ailangye, David nĩwambĩĩe kũsoma makaseti ala wamũtiĩaa. Mũthya nĩwesie kwambĩĩa kũthi Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, na avika eethĩaa mwĩsũkũũe wa myaka thanthatũ amũkwatĩie kĩvĩla. David aelya kũtĩĩa kamwĩsũkũũe kakomana nake kamwĩaa, "Ũmau, keka tyo ũkie ũmbanonĩ ũmũnthĩ." Ũmũnthĩ ũũ David atanĩaa kũmũthũkũma Yeova mũno, na ũtanu ũla Mary wĩ naw'o nĩ mwingĩ nũndũ yu memũthũkũma Yeova me ĩmwe.
15. Ala akũangũ matonya kũtetheesya ata ala manatwaanie mĩtũkĩ?
15 Twasũanĩa ũndũ Satani ũvangĩte kwananga mĩsyĩ, ve vata mũnene wa athũkũmi onthe ma Ngai kũtata methĩwe na ngwatanĩo ndũmu mĩtwaanonĩ yoo. O na mwĩthĩwe mwatwaanie ĩndĩĩ, ĩkala nthĩ ũsũanĩe kĩla we mwene ũtonya kũweta kana kwĩka nĩ kana ũlũlũmĩlye mũtwaano wenyu. Ala akũangũ no matetheesye ala aninangi kĩkundinĩ nĩ kana o namo malũlũmĩlye mĩtwaano yoo. Mavinda kwa mavinda no mũthokye asu aninangi ĩla mwĩ na ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ. Ĩla mwĩ namo vau no methĩe kaĩ wendo na ngwatanĩo nĩ maũndũ ma vata o na andũ matw'ĩke matwaanie ĩndĩĩ!—Tito 2:3-7.
"TWAMBATE KĨĨMANĨ KYA YEOVA"
16, 17. Andũ ma Ngai me na mea ma kwona ĩvinda yĩva?
16 Kwakũna visa Aisilaeli maimũtaĩa Yeova ĩvindanĩ ya sikũkũ me ĩkalũnĩ yake Yelusaleme. Nĩ kana mavike kũu meethĩawa mambie kwĩyũmbany'a, na ĩndĩ makwatya kyalo nĩmatethanasya nzĩanĩ nĩ kana ĩndĩ mese kũvika ĩkalũnĩ mathaithe me ĩmwe. Maũndũ asu onthe mendaa ngwatanĩo. (Luka 2:41-44) O naitũ twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa twĩ kĩmwe na twĩ ngwatanĩo nũndũ twĩ kyalonĩ kya kũthi nthĩ nzaũ. Nĩ kana tũvote kwĩka ũu twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na kĩthito kingĩ kĩte kũoleka. We nũkwona ta waĩle kũsũanĩa ũndũ ũsu mũnango?
17 Kwatata kũsũanĩa moathimo ala tweteele! O na kau nthĩ ĩno yusĩe andũ mate ngwatanĩo na mate mũuo, ithyĩ twĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ namo. Ithyĩ nĩtwene nesa kĩla Isaia na Mika mathanie kĩianĩa. Mathanie kana andũ ma Ngai makambata "kĩĩmanĩ kya Yeova" me ngwatanĩo. (Isa. 2:2-4; soma Mika 4:2-4.) Vate nzika, 'mĩthenyanĩ ĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo' ũthaithi witũ nĩw'o mũseo vyũ. Ĩndĩ ũtanu ũla mwingĩ vyũ tũkaũkwata ĩla twĩvika ĩvinda yĩla andũ onthe makekalaa 'makomanĩtw'e nesa' na me na ngwatanĩo!

translation:
"But from his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace."—John 1:16.
FOOTNOTE: 53, 16
1. What is one way to show appreciation for what God has done for us?
APPRECIATION can be shown by being generous. For example, God's beloved Son, who was perfect, said: "And I will give them eternal life, and they will never perish." (John 8:30) The Son demonstrated his gratitude by means of his ministry and sacrifice. We too can express our appreciation by supporting God's work. Consider this illustration: Noah built an ark to show his appreciation for God's warning. And God's people today often use their time and resources to proclaim the good news. But sometimes people feel that they do not have enough to share. However, they can still demonstrate their gratitude by remaining loyal to Jehovah and by using whatever they have to support the preaching work.—Matt. 6:14-16, 22; 1 Tim. 4:4-32; 1 Chron. 25:1-8.
2. (a) What quality does each congregation of Christians need? (b) What questions will we answer?
2 Moreover, each Christian congregation needs generosity to succeed. The apostle Paul wrote that Christ gave certain ones "as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelizers, some as shepherds and teachers." (Read 1 Corinthians 12:4-6, 12.) Why is this important? Because we need to recognize that spiritual gifts are given for the common good. And we need to realize that spiritual gifts are not always spectacular or dramatic.
SHOW GENEROSITY FOR THE COMMON GOOD
3. What did the apostle John see in vision?
3 The faithful apostle John saw visions of angels, and each angel had a distinct message. But when he saw five angels, John said he heard "a voice from heaven" saying: "The secret of God will be finished up." That secret involved making God's name known throughout the earth. As that work progressed, more and more people turned to God, and their faith strengthened. How do we feel about sharing in that work? Are we eager to help others learn about Jehovah's purpose? We should be! For just as John was able to discern the meaning of his vision, so too can we understand the significance of what is happening today. Christ has already begun to gather his chosen people—millions of imperfect humans who desire to live forever. So if we are generous in supporting the work, we will not allow Satan to deceive many and lead them away from the truth!
4. How do God's people show generosity, and why is it vital that we maintain a positive view?
4 Jehovah's Witnesses generously give of their time and energy to proclaim the good news of God's Kingdom, and they continue doing so despite opposition. (Matt. 24:14; 28:19, 20) One way we can support this work is by being loyal to "the faithful and discreet slave," which provides spiritual food at the right time. (Rev. 22:17) By uniting with the Christian congregation, we can remain steadfast, even if we face difficulties. Should we ever question whether our efforts are worthwhile, let us remember that we are part of something bigger than ourselves—a worldwide brotherhood.—Eph. 4:16.
5, 6. What helps us to be generous in supporting the work?
5 Even though we may want to help many people learn about God's Word, we need to be realistic about what we can accomplish. It is important that we set reasonable goals. Reasonable goals will help us stay motivated and make progress. Every time we participate in the ministry, we have the opportunity to help others learn about God's Word. We can expand our ministry by making use of the tools available to us, such as the Bible and publications based on the Bible. Are you thinking about ways to cooperate with others in the full-time ministry? If so, you are joining millions of others who are sharing the good news with "angels" who are interested in hearing it, as foretold in Revelation 14:6.
6 The joy we experience is much greater than what is described in the Yearbook regarding those whom we teach. And more than that, we appreciate the encouragement we receive from seeing people overcome big challenges, make significant changes, and achieve many things. These experiences strengthen our faith and remind us of the importance of adhering to Scriptural principles, while also being practical and discerning. Many times, these experiences move us to thank God for using us to help others. Another thing that unites us is the commemoration of Jesus' death. By regularly meditating on the meaning of Jesus' sacrifice and striving to imitate his example, each year we remember the commemoration of Jesus' death, and we observe the 14 days of Nisan leading up to it. (1 Cor. 11:23-26) And this is not the only way to show our appreciation for the memorial. It is satisfying to know that when we commemorate Jesus' death, we help many people understand the significance of this event and encourage them to associate with us in this worship.
7. Should we be zealous in our ministry?
7 One sister said she was shy about approaching people. But she realized that her shyness should not prevent her from speaking boldly. Being zealous in our ministry means helping millions of people learn about Jehovah, the true God, who is loving and kind! And even if they reject us, continuing to preach does not mean we are failing to fulfill our assignment from God.
LET US BE ZEALOUS IN OUR MINISTRY
8, 9. (a) How did Paul illustrate the importance of zeal in the ministry? (b) What can we do to remain zealous in our ministry?
8 The apostle Paul wrote to Ephesians and encouraged them to make progress in living a life worthy of their calling and to "make the most of [their] time." (Read Ephesians 4:15, 16.) Is it possible for each of us to improve in our ministry? Paul recognized that zeal in the ministry is influenced by a person's personality. He used the illustration of a man who is eager to fight a battle. That missionary showed that a person who is zealous "does not boast beyond what is proper." Each of us has different strengths and weaknesses, but can we all strive to be more zealous in our ministry and continue to put forth effort?
9 One thing that can help us to be more zealous is this: To imitate Jesus' example in being willing to associate with people and to minister to them. (Acts 13:7, 17) Some may find this difficult. Let us pray to God to help us to be more zealous, and let us ask Him to help us overcome our shyness or fear. However, we should not allow our personal feelings to prevent us from associating with others and sharing the good news. We need to remember that our desire to please Jehovah is stronger than our reluctance to speak to others. And also, associating with others will often help us to feel more comfortable and confident in speaking about the truth.
10. What can motivate us to be more zealous in the ministry, and how can we determine whether we are making progress?
(See accompanying article "How to Improve Your Zeal.")
10 We can stay motivated by setting goals for ourselves and then working hard to achieve them. For example, we might set a goal to spend a certain amount of time each week witnessing or to start a Bible study with someone. Also, we can benefit from observing experienced ministers and imitating their fine qualities. Furthermore, we can seek assistance from the elders and ask them for suggestions on how to improve our ministry. By regularly reviewing our progress, we can see where we are doing well and where we need to make adjustments.—Compare Acts 6:3-6.
11. Why might some find it difficult to share in the ministry, and what can they do about it?
11 Many young ones find it challenging to overcome their shyness and get involved in the ministry. As they grow older, they may also face new challenges, and they may feel inadequate at times. However, such brothers and sisters can be encouraged by seeing others who have successfully faced similar difficulties. With training and practice, they can become more effective witnesses. And those who have more experience can help them by giving encouragement and practical advice. So do not give up when you encounter obstacles in your efforts to preach the good news! (1 Tim. 3:1, 10) But some mature Christians may find it increasingly difficult to maintain their zeal. They may feel tired or discouraged, and they may struggle to motivate themselves to continue putting spiritual things first. If this happens, let us examine ourselves and ask: 'What can I do to rekindle my zeal?'—Read Psalm 110:3; Hebrews 12:1.
MAINTAIN YOUR ZEAL
12, 13. What can help us to stay zealous in the ministry?
12 One reason why we might lose our zeal is because we focus too much on the negative aspects of the ministry. Many have found that thinking about Jehovah's qualities helps them to view the ministry in a positive light. Seeing how Jehovah lovingly cares for people, including imperfect humans, can strengthen our desire to share his message. Also, remembering that preaching is a privilege that allows us to defend Jehovah's name and purposes can motivate us. Furthermore, many find that setting personal goals helps them to stay focused and productive. For example, they may aim to spend a certain amount of time each week witnessing or to start a Bible study.
And when we see others progressing spiritually and appreciating God's Word, it encourages us to continue persevering.
13 But what if you feel discouraged despite your efforts to remain zealous in the ministry? Does this mean that Jehovah has abandoned you? No! A husband and wife can be exemplary servants of Jehovah, yet still experience discouragement at times. Consider the examples of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Elkanah and Hannah. We can learn from their experiences. (Gen. 26:8; 1 Sam. 1:5, 8; 1 Chron. 3:5, 6) By regularly examining ourselves and making adjustments where needed, we can maintain our zeal and please Jehovah.—Read Proverbs 4:12.
14 How then can a Christian family cultivate love and unity so that none of its members become disheartened?
14 Christians strive to associate closely with one another. (2 Cor. 6:14) Are there young ones in your family who find it difficult to get along with others? Perhaps they need help to develop social skills. It is important to teach them Bible principles and to encourage them to apply those principles in their dealings with others. If they make mistakes, gently correct them, helping them understand how their actions affect others and how to please Jehovah. This will also help them to avoid getting involved in bad associations that could lead to spiritual decline. The example of a sister named Mary illustrates this point. For about 25 years, she helped her father, David, in the full-time ministry. Mary also engaged in much public speaking, both at congregation meetings and larger assemblies. She diligently studied the Bible, striving to improve her understanding of God's Word. However, she began associating with companions who did not value spiritual things. As a result, she gradually lost her zeal. Seeing this, Mary's father encouraged her to read material that would strengthen her faith. He invited her to attend the Kingdom Hall and arranged for her to spend time with mature Christians. David realized that good associations can have a positive influence, and he told her, "Daughter, let us see if you can regain your former enthusiasm." With his encouragement, Mary resumed serving Jehovah wholeheartedly, and soon her own zeal returned.
15. What can parents do to help their children choose good associates?
15 We must remember that Satan promotes wickedness and tries to mislead people, including young ones, so that they may disobey God. Therefore, be vigilant and help your children to discern what is right and wrong. Encourage them to think independently and to reason on matters themselves. Parents should set a fine example by choosing their own associates carefully. They should also help their children to identify and avoid harmful influences. Regularly discuss the importance of choosing friends wisely and emphasize that true friendship is based on shared love for God and obedience to His laws.—Titus 2:3-7.
"LET US HOLD FAST TO THE HOPE"
16, 17. How did ancient Israelites show their appreciation for spiritual provisions?
16 The Israelites traveled to Jerusalem each year to celebrate festivals at the temple. They made sacrifices and offered prayers, and they took time to associate with fellow worshippers. All of this strengthened their faith. (Luke 2:41-44) Today, too, we benefit from associating with our brothers and sisters and sharing in the ministry. By doing so, we reinforce our determination to remain faithful. But what if we find it difficult to maintain our zeal? Should we give up? Consider how you feel when you have been helped by others. Do you not want to encourage those who are struggling spiritually?—Titus 2:3-7.
17 To encourage one another, let us take the initiative! Let us visit our brothers and sisters, especially those who are sick or discouraged. This will strengthen them. Indeed, just as Isaiah and Micah foretold, God's people are clinging to "the hope of Jehovah." (Isa. 2:2-4; read Micah 4:2-4) So let us be determined to continue "exerting ourselves vigorously" in this regard. May we always remember that the majority of people today are living in "the last days," and they need our help and encouragement!

text:
"Mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kĩla kĩmanyĩthasya vyũ maũndũ ala mekwatĩtw'e."—AEVL. 11:1.
MBATHI: 54, 55
1, 2. (a) Ve kĩvathũkany'o kyaũ katĩ wa wĩkwatyo ũla Aklĩsto ma w'o me naw'o na wĩkwatyo wa andũ ma nthĩ ĩno ya Satani? (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva ma vata?
AKLĨSTO ma w'o methĩawa na wĩkwatyo mũseo ta kĩ! Ithyonthe, twĩthĩwe twĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta kana twĩ "malondu angĩ," twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kwona Yeova aianĩsya kĩla kĩeleelo kyake na kwona ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩithew'a. (Yoa. 10:16; Mt. 6:9, 10) Vai maũndũ angĩ maseo ta asu mũndũ o na wĩva ũtonya kũmeteela na mea maingĩ. O na ĩngĩ twĩ na mea ma kwona ũla watho wa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela ũianĩa, twĩthĩwe tũkaũkwata ĩtunĩ kana nĩ kũũ nthĩ. (2 Vet. 3:13) Ĩndĩ tũtanamba kũvika vau, twĩ na mea ma kwona ũndũ Ngai ũkũendeea kũtongoesya na kũtw'ĩĩka andũ make.
2 O namo ala makwete mbau nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani me o wĩkwatyo ũla methĩawa naw'o, ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa na nzika kana ũkeanĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ milioni mbingĩ ala mothaa kalata nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũsinda, ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa me o na nzika kana ũu no ũtonyeke. Ĩndĩ Mũklĩsto wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo wa w'o ethĩawa 'amanyĩthĩtw'e vyũ,' kana ate na nzika na wĩkwatyo wake wa Kĩklĩsto. (Aevl. 11:1) Ĩndĩ no kwĩthĩwa ũyĩkũlya-ĩ, 'Ndonya kwĩka ata nĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu vyũ nthĩnĩ wa wĩkwatyo ũla nĩ naw'o? Na nĩ moathimo meva ndonya kũkwata nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu nthĩnĩ wa wĩkwatyo ũsu?'
3. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa Aklĩsto methĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ũla methĩawa naw'o?
3 Mũĩkĩĩo ti kĩndũ andũ masyaawa nakyo kana kĩndũ kĩkaa kwĩyĩete. Mũklĩsto ethĩawa na mũĩkĩĩo ĩla weetĩkĩlya veva mũtheu wa Ngai ũthũkũme ngoonĩ yake. (Aka. 5:22) Mbivilia ndĩwetete kana Yeova e mũĩkĩĩo na kana nĩwĩthĩawa na vata wa kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo. Nũndũ Yeova nĩ mwene vinya w'onthe na nĩ mũĩ mũno, vai kĩndũ kĩtonya kũmũsiĩĩa aianĩsya kĩeleelo kyake. Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ kana mawatho make makeanĩa. Ethĩawa esĩ ũu nesa vyũ nginya o na ũkethĩa kwake mawatho asu no ta maminĩte kwĩanĩa. Nĩkyo kĩtumi waĩtye, "Nĩ kwĩke," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, mawatho asu nĩmeanĩĩte. (Soma Ũvuan'yo 21:3-6.) Nũndũ Yeova nĩ "Ngai wĩ kĩthito," ndalea kwĩanĩsya mawatho make, na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumaa Aklĩsto methĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ũla methĩawa naw'o.—Kũt. 7:9.
ATHŨKŨMI MA NGAI ALA MAĨ NA MŨĨKĨĨO
4. Ala aũme na aka maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu ĩvindanĩ ya tene Ũklĩsto ũtanambĩĩa maĩ na wĩkwatyo wĩva?
4 Ĩvuku ya Aevelania kĩlungu kya 11 nĩyĩwetete masyĩtwa ma aũme na aka 16 ala maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Mũandĩki wa ĩvuku yĩu aveveewe kũandĩka ĩũlũ wa andũ asu na angĩ aingĩ, ala "makũsĩĩwe kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo woo." (Aevl. 11:39) Asu onthe 'nĩmamanyĩthĩtw'e vyũ' kana Yeova akaumĩlya "ũsyao" ũla wathanĩtwe nĩ kana wanange amaitha make na ũianĩsya kĩla kĩeleelo kyake. (Mwa. 3:15) Andũ asu aĩkĩĩku makwie Yesũ Klĩsto, ũla nĩwe ũla "ũsyao" wathanĩtwe, atanamba kũvingũa nzĩa ya kũthi ĩtunĩ. (Aka. 3:16) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, makathayũũkw'a matanĩe thayũ nthĩ nzaũ tene na tene nĩkwĩthĩwa mawatho ma Yeova mailea kwĩanĩa.—Sav. 37:11; Isa. 26:19; Osea 13:14.
5, 6. Avalaamu na ala angĩ ma mũsyĩ wake maĩ na wĩkwatyo wĩva, na nĩ kyaũ kyamatetheeisye mekala me na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 21.)
5 Ĩvuku ya Aevelania 11:13 yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa andũ amwe maĩ kw'o Ũklĩsto ũtanambĩĩa: "Asu onthe nĩmakwie mũĩkĩĩonĩ, matosete matho, ĩndĩ mamonete me kũasa na kũmatanĩa." Avalaamu aĩ ũmwe wa andũ asu. We Avalaamu nĩwekalaa aisũanĩa ũndũ kũkethĩwa kũseũvĩte andũ masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ ũla "ũsyao" wathaniwe? Yesũ nĩwasũngĩie ĩkũlyo yĩu nesa ĩla weeie ala mamũvĩngaa atĩĩ: "Ĩthe wenyu, Avalaamu, nĩwatanie nũndũ wa kwona mũthenya wakwa; na nĩwawonie, na atana." (Yoa. 8:56) O nake Sala, Isaka, Yakovo, na angĩ aingĩ nĩmekalaa maisũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo woo wa kwĩsa kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Ũsumbĩ, 'ũla mwambĩlĩlya na mwaki waw'o nĩ Ngai.'—Aevl. 11:8-11.
6 Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Avalaamu na ala angĩ ma mũsyĩ wake maendeea kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu? Nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa memanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Ngai kwa kwĩthukĩĩsya andũ me mũĩkĩĩo ala maĩ akũangũ kwĩ mo, kana Ngai akethĩwa aneenaa namo kwĩsĩla alaĩka, woni, kana ndoto. O na ĩngĩ, no kwĩthĩwa masomaa mavuku ma tene ala maĩ matonya kwĩkwatw'a. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ, mayaaũlwa nĩ maũndũ ala meemanyĩĩtye. Vandũ va ũu, nĩmendaa mũno kwona mawatho ma Ngai maianĩa na nĩmendete mĩao yake, o na nĩmavindĩĩasya maũndũ asu. Nĩkwĩthĩwa aũme na aka asu mayaĩ na nzika na wĩkwatyo woo, nĩmeeyũmbanĩtye kũmĩĩsya mathĩna onthe nĩ kana maendeee kwĩkala malũmanĩtye na Ngai.
7. Nĩ kyaũ Yeova ũtũnengete nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, na no nginya twĩke ata?
7 Nĩkwĩthĩwa Yeova nĩ mũseo, nũtũnengete Ndeto yake, Mbivilia, nĩ kana ĩtũtetheesye kwĩkala twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Nĩ kana 'tũathimwe' na 'tũyaĩla' maũndũnĩ maitũ, no nginya tũtate vyũ tũsomae Ndeto ya Ngai kĩla mũthenya. (Sav. 1:1-3; soma Meko ma Atũmwa 17:11.) Na ĩndĩ o ta ala athaithi ma Yeova maĩ kw'o Ũklĩsto ũtanambĩĩa, nĩtwaĩle kũvindĩĩasya mawatho ma Ngai na kwĩw'a mĩao yake. O na ĩngĩ, Yeova nũtũathimĩte na lĩu mwingĩ wa kĩ-veva kuma kwa ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ." (Mt. 24:45) Kwoou twaendeea kũtanĩa kũsoma na kũvindĩĩsya maũndũ ala Yeova ũtũmanyĩasya kwĩsĩla syĩndũ ila ũtũnengete, tũkeethĩwa ta ala andũ ma tene maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, ala 'mamanyĩthĩtw'e vyũ' kana wĩkwatyo woo ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ waĩ wa w'o.
8. Mboya ĩtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo witũ ata?
8 Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kyatetheeisye mũno andũ asu mekale me na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu nĩ mboya. Mũĩkĩĩo woo nĩwalũlũmĩlaa mũno ĩla moona Ngai aisũngĩa mboya syoo. (Nee. 1:4, 11; Sav. 34:4, 15, 17; Nda. 9:19-21) O naitũ no tũmũtulũĩle Yeova mavata maitũ, twĩsĩ nesa kana nũkũtwĩthukĩĩsya na aitũlũlũmĩlya tũendeee kũmĩĩsya twĩ atanu. Na ĩndĩ ĩla mboya sitũ syasũngĩwa, mũĩkĩĩo witũ nũendeeaa kũlũlũmĩla. (Soma 1 Yoana 5:14, 15.) Nũndũ mũĩkĩĩo nĩ kĩlungu kĩmwe kya ũsyao wa veva, nĩtwaĩle kũendeea 'kũvoya' Ngai atũnenge veva wake mũtheu, o tondũ Yesũ watũthuthisye twĩkae.—Luka 11:9, 13.
9. O vamwe na kũvoya kwondũ wa mavata maitũ, naaũ angĩ twaĩle kũmavoyeaa?
9 Ĩndĩ tũyaĩle o kũvoyaa kwondũ wa mavata maitũ me moka. Kĩla mũthenya no tũmũtũngĩae Yeova mũvea na tũkamũkatha nũndũ wa 'mawĩa make ma ũsengy'a,' namo nĩ "maingĩ mũno." (Sav. 40:5) O na ĩngĩ ĩla tũũvoya nĩtwaĩle 'kũmalilikanaa ala ove, ta twovetwe vamwe nao.' O na eka ũu, nĩtwaĩle kũvoyaa kwondũ wa ana-a-asa nthĩ yonthe, na mũno mũno 'ala me na ũtongoi ĩũlũ witũ.' Tũtanaa ta kĩ ĩla Yeova wasũngĩa mboya sitũ vamwe na sya ana-a-asa nthĩ yonthe!—Aevl. 13:3, 7.
MAYAAĨTĨKĨLA KWĨKA MAŨNDŨ MALEANĨTE NA MŨĨKĨĨO WOO
10. Nĩ athũkũmi ta meva ma Ngai maleile kwĩka maũndũ maleanĩte na mũĩkĩĩo woo, na nĩ kyaũ kyamanengie vinya wa kwĩka ũu?
10 Ĩvukunĩ ya Aevelania kĩlungu kya 11 mũtũmwa Vaulo nũeleetye mathĩna makwatie athũkũmi aingĩ ma Ngai, o na kau ndaaweta masyĩtwa moo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũtũmwa ũsu nũwetete aka maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ala makw'ĩĩwe nĩ syana syoo ĩndĩ ĩtina syesa kũthayũũkw'a. Na ĩndĩ aweta angĩ ala mathĩniw'e mũno "matekwĩtĩkĩla kũthaw'a; nĩ kana mone ũthayũũkyo [mũseango]." (Aevl. 11:35) O na kau tũyĩsa kũmanya nesa naaũ Vaulo wasũanĩaa, athũkũmi amwe ma Ngai ta Navothi na Nzekalia nĩmakimangiwe na mavia nginya makw'a nũndũ wa kũmwĩw'a Ngai na kwĩka kwenda kwake. (1 Asu. 21:3, 15; 2 Mav. 24:20, 21) Nake Ndanieli na ala anyanyae make maĩ o matonya 'kwĩtĩkĩla kũthaw'a' vandũ va kũlũmany'a na Yeova. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwĩka ũu, mũĩkĩĩo ũla maĩ naw'o nthĩnĩ wa ũtonyi wa Ngai watumie meka maũndũ tũtonya kwasya no ũndũ ũmwe na 'kũtumya makanyw'a ma mĩnyambũ,' na 'kũvosya vinya wa mwaki.'—Aevl. 11:33, 34; Nda. 3:16-18, 20, 28; 6:13, 16, 21-23.
11. Nĩ matatwa meva athani amwe makomanie namo nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo woo?
11 Namo angĩ ta mwathani Mikaia na Yelemia makwatiwe nĩ "matatwa ma kũvũthw'a . . . na kwĩkĩwa kolokolonĩ" nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo woo. Na ĩndĩ ve angĩ ta Eliya "mangangie maweũnĩ na iĩmanĩ na ngunganĩ, na maimanĩ ma nthĩ." Asu onthe moomĩĩisye nũndũ 'nĩmamanyĩthĩtw'e vyũ kĩla meekwatĩtye,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, mayaĩ na nzika na kĩla meekwatĩtye.—Aevl. 11:1, 36-38; 1 Asu. 18:13; 22:24-27; Yel. 20:1, 2; 28:10, 11; 32:2.
12. Nũũ ũla watũtiĩe ngelekany'o ĩla nzeo vyũ ya kũmĩĩsya matatwa, na nĩ kyaũ kyamũtetheeisye?
12 Vaulo amina kũelesya ĩũlũ wa aũme na aka asu maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, nĩwasyokie aelesya ĩũlũ wa Yesũ Klĩsto ũla nĩwe ngelekany'o ĩla nzeo vyũ. Ĩandĩko ya Aevelania 12:2 yaĩtye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Yesũ: "Ũla kwondũ wa ũtanu ũla waiiwe mbee wake oomĩĩsya ĩla ngelan'yo, aivũthya nthoni, na nĩwekalile nthĩ ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwa aũme kwa kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya Ngai." Kwoou, nĩw'o ki kana nĩtwaĩle 'kũsũanĩa mũno' ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya mũĩkĩĩo ĩla waĩ mathĩnanĩ momũ vyũ. (Soma Aevelania 12:3.) O ta Yesũ, Aklĩsto ma mbee ala mooaiwe kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo woo, ta ũla mũmanyĩw'a weetawa Andiva, nĩmaleile kwĩka maũndũ matoosanĩte na mũĩkĩĩo woo. (Ũvu. 2:13) Aklĩsto asu maĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kũthayũũkw'a na kũthi ĩtunĩ. Ũthayũũkyo ũsu woo nĩ mũseo vyũ o na kũkĩla ũla "ũthayũũkyo [mũseango]" athũkũmi ma tene ma Ngai meekwatĩtye. (Aevl. 11:35) Ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ ĩtina wa Ũsumbĩ kwambĩĩa kũsumbĩka mwakanĩ wa 1914, etĩkĩw'a mauta onthe ala makwie me aĩkĩĩku nĩmathayũũkiw'e na mĩĩ ya veva na mathi ĩtunĩ nĩ kana mesumbĩka andũ me vamwe na Yesũ.—Ũvu. 20:4.
ATHŨKŨMI MA NGAI ALA METHĨĨTWE NA MŨĨKĨĨO MŨLŨMU
13, 14. Rudolf Graichen akwatiwe nĩ mathĩna meva, na nĩ kyaũ kyamũnengie vinya wa kũmĩĩsya?
13 Athũkũmi ma Ngai milioni mbingĩ ũmũnthĩ nĩmaatĩĩaa ngelekany'o nzeo ya Yesũ kwa kwĩthĩwa me na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte, na mate kwĩtĩkĩlya matatwa monzye mũĩkĩĩo woo. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩmwe ya mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Rudolf Graichen, ũla wasyaĩwe Germany mwaka wa 1925. Mwana-a-asa ũsu nũwetete mavisa ma ngewa syĩ Mbivilianĩ ala mambĩtwe ngũtanĩ sya nyũmba yoo. Rudolf aandĩkie ũũ: "Ĩvisa yĩmwe yaĩ na nzũi na kalondu, katena na ngo, na kasaũ na mũnyambũ syĩkalanĩtye nesa na itongoew'e nĩ kamwana. . . . Ndyaaũlwa nĩ visa ta isu o na vanini." (Isa. 11:6-9) Rudolf aminie myaka aithĩnw'a mũno nĩ asikalĩ meetawa Gestapo ma kyama kya Nazi, na ĩtina nĩ asikalĩ ma Stasi ma East Germany. Ĩndĩ o na kau nĩwathĩniw'e ũu, aendeeie kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu ĩũlũ wa ĩla nthĩ nzaũ weeteele.
14 Rudolf nĩwakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna angĩ maito mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla inyia woovetwe kambinĩ ya mathĩna ya Ravensbrück nĩwakwatiwe nĩ ndetema ya typhus na akw'a. O na ĩngĩ nĩwoonie mũĩkĩĩo wa ĩthe ũyonza nginya esa kũkaĩa mũĩkĩĩo wake kwa kwĩkĩa saii valũa ũkwasya kana we ti ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩndĩ ĩla Rudolf wathaiw'e, nĩwatanĩie kũkwata kĩanda kya kũthũkũma e mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko na ĩtina nĩwathokiw'e Sukulu ya Ngileati. Amina sukulu nĩwatũmiwe ta misonalĩ nthĩ ya Chile, na e kũu nĩwasyokeie wĩa wake wa kũthyũlũlũka. Ĩndĩ mathĩna ma Rudolf mayaathelela vau. Mwaka ũmwe ĩtina wa kũtwaana na misonalĩ weetawa Patsy, nĩmakw'ĩĩwe nĩ kana koo ka kelĩtu. Ekalangĩte nĩwasyokie akw'ĩĩwa nĩ mũka wake Patsy, ũla waĩ na myaka 43. Rudolf nĩwoomĩĩisye mathĩna asu onthe. Ĩla ngewa yake yakwatĩkanie ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya Kĩswaili ya Ĩtukũ 1, Mwei wa 8, 1997, ĩthangũnĩ ya 20-25, athũkũmaa ta vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda na mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi, o na kũtw'ĩka aĩ mũkũũ na aĩ na mathĩna ma mwĩĩ. [1]
15. Weta Ngũsĩ imwe sya Yeova syĩthĩĩtwe iyũmĩĩsya mathĩna iteũkw'a ngoo.
15 Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nitanaa mũno nũndũ wa wĩkwatyo ũla syĩ naw'o o na kwĩthĩwa nithĩnaw'a mũno na kũnyamaw'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ nĩmovetwe nthĩ ya Eritrea, ya Singapore, na ya South Korea, na aingĩ moo movetwe nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa ila ndeto sya Yesũ syaasya kana mũndũ ndaĩle kũkwatĩa ũngĩ ũvyũ. (Mt. 26:52) Amwe moo nĩ Isaac, Negede, na Paulos. Me atatũ methĩĩtwe kyovonĩ nthĩ ya Eritrea kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 20. O na kau ana-a-asa asu nĩmanyamaĩtw'e mũno na makaimwa ũthasyo wa kũsũvĩa asyai moo na wa kũtwaana, nĩmekalĩte me aĩkĩĩku. Wasisya visa woo nthĩnĩ wa kĩsese kitũ kya jw.org, wĩmona me atanu, kwonany'a kana methĩĩtwe me na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. O na asikalĩ ala mamasungaa nĩmesĩte kũmanenga ndaĩa.
16. Kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kũtonya kũũtethya ata?
16 Athũkũmi aingĩ ma Yeova mayaaĩsa kwovwa yela kana kũnyamaw'a ta ana-a-asa asu. Ĩndĩ mũĩkĩĩo woo nũtatawa kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Amwe nĩmonete thĩna mwingĩ nũndũ wa ũkya, kana makethĩwa mathĩnĩte mũno nũndũ wa kaũ kũlika nthĩ yoo, kana o makethĩwa makwatĩtwe nĩ mĩisyo ta ithingitho sya nthĩ. Angĩ mekĩte ta Mose na ala atumĩa angĩ aĩkĩĩku ma tene kwa kũtia moseo na nguma sya nthĩ ĩno nĩ kana mamũthũkũme Yeova. Nĩmang'ang'anĩte mũno maikese kũtatĩka mambĩĩe kũsembany'a na syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ na kũmantha kwĩyĩuna. Ĩndĩ kyo nĩ kyaũ kĩmatetheeasya kwosa ĩtambya yĩu? Kĩtumi nũndũ nĩmamwendete Yeova na me na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu kana ndakalea kwĩanĩsya watho wake wa kũvetanga ũsili ũte wa katĩ, vamwe na kũathima athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku na thayũ ũtathela me nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ yĩ ũlũngalu.—Soma Savuli 37:5, 7, 9, 29.
17. Ũtw'ĩte kwĩka ata, na twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
17 Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ nĩtwoona ũndũ kũvindĩĩsya mawatho ma Ngai na kũvoyaa tũteũtĩĩa kũtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo witũ. Mũĩkĩĩo ũsu nĩw'o "kĩla kĩmanyĩthasya vyũ maũndũ ala mekwatĩtw'e." Na kwoou tweethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu tũkeethĩwa tũtonya kũmĩĩsya matatwa na kwĩkala tũlilikene wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o wa Kĩklĩsto, tũte na nzika kana ũkeanĩa. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩeleetye mũĩkĩĩo kwa nzĩa mbaamu mũnango na kĩu nĩkyo kĩneenewe ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe.
^ [1] (kalungu ka 14) O na ĩngĩ sisya kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, "Licha ya Majaribu, Tumaini Langu Halijafifia," ĩkasetinĩ ya Amkeni! ya 22/04/2002, kĩla kĩeleetye ngewa ya Andrej Hanák kuma Slovakia.
