translation:
"Son, be obedient to your father, and do not despise your mother when she is old." —Prov. 23:22.
PARAGRAPH 23, 22
1, 2. Why did Daniel remain faithful to God despite intense pressure, and how can we imitate Daniel's example?
THE account of Daniel illustrates how young people faced challenges in ancient Babylon and remained loyal to Jehovah despite opposition from powerful people. Daniel and his three companions were taken captive to Babylon along with other Jews from noble families. (Dan. 1:6, 8, 12; 3:16-18) Daniel and his companions resolutely determined to honor Jehovah no matter what happened. And they succeeded! An angel told Daniel that he was a man "highly esteemed."—Dan. 10:11, 19.
2 The potter has the ability to shape clay according to his will, and he can correct mistakes. Similarly, Jehovah is the Great Potter, and He has the right to mold us to suit His purpose. (Read Jeremiah 18:6.) In fact, God desires to mold each of us. So, instead of resisting correction, let us accept it willingly and cooperate. By doing so, we show that we are willing to be molded into the kind of person Jehovah wants us to be. Let us consider four questions that will help us to determine whether we are allowing ourselves to be molded by God: (1) What specific steps can we take to avoid bad associations that could lead us to fear displeasing God? (2) Can we identify habits that need improvement so that we can become more zealous in serving Jehovah? (3) How can Christian elders demonstrate their faith in God's guidance?
AVOID BAD ASSOCIATIONS
3. What are some things that can cause us to fear displeasing God? We will now discuss this.
3 Proverbs 4:23 says: "Safeguard your heart [or, mind] diligently, for out of it are the sources of life." What are some things that can cause us to fear displeasing God, yet we may find it difficult to distance ourselves from them? These include materialism, a craving for power, and stubborn pride. Such things can lead a person to act dishonestly or to be influenced by negative people. (Prov. 5:1, 20; Heb. 3:13, 18, 19) One man who was ensnared by materialism was King Uzziah of Judah. (Read 2 Kings 26:3-5, 16-21.) It is said that Uzziah "did what was right in Jehovah's eyes" and "kept seeking Jehovah," yet "when he became strong, his heart got haughty." And because of his pride, he suffered consequences! He even dared to enter the temple to offer incense, something only priests were authorized to do. But did he learn a lesson? Pride led him to ruin! What does this teach us? God will not tolerate anyone who becomes arrogant and ignores His standards.—Prov. 16:18.
4, 5. What can we do to avoid being overtaken by materialism? We will now discuss this.
4 If we want to avoid being overtaken by materialism, we must remind ourselves that 'the love of money is a root of all sorts of injurious things,' and that we should be content with our way of life. (1 Tim. 6:10; Prov. 29:1) Consider the experience of a brother named Jim, whose work involved associating with people who were wealthy and who often discussed business matters. Jim said: "I began to enjoy their company and I found myself wanting to imitate their lifestyle." Over time, he started to feel dissatisfied with his own situation and wanted to join their circle. Jim explained: "I thought, 'If I had what they have, I could really do some good.'" Jim worked hard for ten years. Eventually, he realized: "I still wasn't satisfied, and I realized that I was letting materialism control my thinking and distract me from spiritual pursuits."
His experience showed him that pursuing material possessions would never bring true contentment.—Read Ecclesiastes 7:6.
5 Jim's experience shows us that materialism can lead us to neglect spiritual activities and cause us to stumble. (Jer. 17:9) Jim learned this lesson, saying: "I made a decision to focus on spiritual things rather than material wealth." Are you facing a similar challenge as a Christian? Or are you already struggling with materialism? If so, examine yourself closely. Are you allowing materialism to influence you? Or are you determined to continue putting Jehovah first in your life and to keep seeking to please Him?—Read Psalm 119:165; Colossians 3:13.
6 What can help us to resist the influence of materialism?
6 A person who appreciates what he has and is grateful for it will find satisfaction. This helps him to live in harmony with God's will. However, some find it difficult to be content with what they have. For example, a young man might feel envious when he sees others enjoying certain privileges. (Prov. 8:11) But another young man may struggle with the temptation to spend his money foolishly, thinking: "I deserve to enjoy myself." That temptation can damage his relationship with Jehovah. It is important to remember that true happiness comes from knowing and loving Jehovah. Let us always strive to maintain our love for Jehovah. Should we allow ourselves to become preoccupied with material possessions or should we defend our spirituality against those who do not value spiritual things, we can remain content and use our resources to support God's work.
7, 8. (a) What did the Israelites learn about being satisfied and avoiding greed? (b) What lessons can we draw from their example?
7 The Israelites remembered their deliverance from Egypt and realized that Jehovah had provided for them. They learned that being satisfied was essential to avoid greed. Today, we too can learn much from how God dealt with them. Consider how they reacted during their journey through the wilderness. They repeatedly complained and tested God, showing a lack of faith! They even murmured against Moses. And on one occasion, they became restless and longed for the delicacies they had enjoyed in Egypt. Those who truly loved Jehovah remained loyal and encouraged others to trust in Him. And despite their murmurings, Jehovah continued to care for them. He asked: "Will this people try me forever?" (Num. 14:1-4, 11; Ps. 78:40, 41) Their history shows us the dangers of craving worldly possessions and being dissatisfied.
8 But how can we make sure that our desire for material things does not lead us astray? We need to keep spiritual matters first in our life. To do so, we must thoroughly understand what our Creator requires of us. For example, let us examine Jesus' words recorded in Matthew 6:33. It reads: "Seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness." Ask yourself: 'Are my interests and desires aligned with those of the Kingdom of God? Am I willing to sacrifice comforts or pleasures if necessary? Should I be concerned about accumulating wealth or possessions?' Reflect on whether your attitude reveals genuine love for God and a desire to please Him.
9 So, how can we cultivate the quality of contentment and remain focused on spiritual things, and how can we avoid becoming greedy?
9 Consider another illustration. Imagine a loyal servant of Jehovah who is asked to do something that he finds unpleasant—perhaps dealing with difficult people, facing opposition, or being transferred to another assignment. He might ask himself: 'Can I endure this?' We should strive to respond like that servant, willingly accepting assignments, even if they require effort, so that we can continue to give priority to our spiritual pursuits! This is why the Bible gives us this counsel: "Set your mind on things above, not on earthly things." (Col. 3:2) Every decision we make should reflect our dedication to God's law.
LET US EXAMINE OUR HEARTS
10 How, then, can we determine if we have become overly attached to materialistic things?
10 God values his Word, his organization, and the privilege of preaching. He allows trials to test whether we will remain devoted. Therefore, to avoid becoming too attached to material possessions, read the Bible daily and meditate on its contents, allowing it to help you stay devoted to Jehovah. Jehovah showed his disapproval when the Israelites repeatedly broke his Law and neglected to study it daily. (Deut. 17:18, 19) Similarly today, some may excuse themselves from reading the Scriptures and meditating on them because of their secular work or other commitments. But the Beroeans were exemplary because they carefully examined the Scriptures daily to see whether what Paul taught was accurate. (Acts 17:11) So let us each resolve to read God's Word daily and apply what we learn. (1 Tim. 4:15) Doing so will help us remain spiritually strong and avoid getting distracted by materialism.
11, 12. How can Jehovah help us to remain part of the Christian congregation, even if we feel inclined to associate with those who do not share our beliefs? Let us consider an illustration.
11 Jehovah helps us to remain part of the Christian congregation even if we feel inclined to associate with those who do not share our beliefs. A brother named Jim told about an experience he had when a coworker expressed interest in learning more about the truth. Jim said: "Every day this coworker would come to me and ask questions, and I would try to answer him as best I could. Because of this, he began to appreciate the time I took to explain things to him." After several months, the coworker invited Jim to his home. Jim said: "The congregation showed kindness and warmth, and he really appreciated that. I told him that if he wanted to learn more, I would be happy to arrange for him to meet with others. Over time, I saw how he strengthened his relationship with God, especially with his wife and children, who were very supportive. One thing that impressed me greatly was his reading of the publications 'Jehovah Is Not to Blame' and 'Serve Jehovah Faithfully,' which appeared in The Watchtower of November 15, 1992."
12 Brother Jim continued to encourage the man to attend meetings with the congregation. As a result, he helped many people, including some who were initially skeptical, to take a firm stand. He admitted and explained: "I am so grateful to Jehovah for giving me the opportunity to preach the good news! I rejoice to see how people respond favorably to the truth. And I rejoice to see how they strengthen their determination to live according to Bible principles."—1 Cor. 10:12.
13 What can help us to be courageous in offering assistance to others? Why is such courage important?
13 Also, what can help us to be courageous in associating with fellow Christians? Such courage means being willing to offer assistance despite opposition and persecution from those who oppose God's standards. (Acts 5:22, 23) Practice will increase your courage. And remember, associating with mature Christians can strengthen our resolve, and their example can motivate us to be courageous. For instance, in recent years an Australian brother was disfellowshipped because he associated with someone who had been disfellowshipped. Because of this, the brother felt deeply saddened and wrote a letter expressing his regret. One paragraph of his letter read: "Because of my association with those who are disloyal, I want to demonstrate my loyalty by showing that I am sincere and by distancing myself from his influence. I hope to continue worthy of the support of the brothers and to cooperate with them." You can see that this brother realized that his actions could affect his standing with Jehovah and his relationship with his brothers. Isn't it wise to learn from his experience and to be cautious about whom we associate with and how we spend our time?
LET GOD'S PRINCIPLES GUIDE YOU
14. How can you determine whether a certain association is appropriate?
14 Many associations are neutral, and they may not involve worship. (Matt. 18:1-4) However, some associations may lead to compromising Bible principles and may cause you to stumble. (2 Tim. 3:14, 15) If an association seems questionable, carefully weigh its effects on your spirituality, and then make a decision based on your conscience. But if an association clearly leads to wrongdoing, avoid it completely, as such associations can have a damaging effect, similar to that of bad companions. And always remember that pleasing Jehovah is more important than pleasing men.
15, 16. What should parents do if their child associates with someone who does not share Bible principles?
15 Also, what if your Christian son or daughter begins associating with someone who has questionable standards? This could be a serious matter that requires prompt attention. A brother from South Africa said: "When my teenage son started keeping company with a young man who had a bad influence, I felt helpless. I was very worried!" What did he do? He took his son aside and discussed God's Word with him. (Read 1 Corinthians 5:11, 13.) His son responded positively, saying: "We realized that the Bible condemns this type of behavior, and we understood that we would risk displeasing God if we continued to associate with this young man. We also realized that Jehovah cares about us and will help us if we trust in Him." So they stopped associating with that young man, and the son gradually overcame the negative influence.
16 But what if your son or daughter does not respond so readily? One father explained: "I tried reasoning with her, but she seemed determined to continue doing what she wanted." And another parent said: "I prayed earnestly to Jehovah, asking for guidance on how to deal with the situation." It can be heartbreaking when your own child seems bent on a course that you know is wrong! Remember, however, that pleasing God should always be our priority—even more than our personal feelings.—Prov. 3:5, 6; 28:26.
17 How, then, can we help our children to maintain their love for Jehovah and to avoid bad associations?
17 Consider Isaiah's words regarding his people, who were feeling helpless and discouraged: "O Jehovah, you are our Father; you are the Potter, and we are the clay." This heartfelt expression moved Jehovah to say: "I will certainly give attention, O Jehovah, and I will remember your kindnesses forever; I will never cease to show my loyal love to you." (Isa. 64:8, 9) So let us humbly ask Jehovah to help us train our children in his ways and to strengthen their love for him daily, just as Daniel did. And realize that when Jehovah sees our sincere efforts to teach them his principles, his laws, and his loving-kindness, he may well use one of his angels to assist us.—Ps. 8:21.

text:
"O ũndũ mwamwĩkie ũmwe wa ana-a-asa aa makwa, o na ala anini, mwambĩkie nyie."—MT. 25:40.
1, 2. (a) Nĩ ngelekany'o syĩva Yesũ watavisye ala anyanyae? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Nĩ kyaũ tũkwenda kũmanya ĩũlũ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi?
KAVINDA keana ũna nĩkavĩtie kuma ala amanyĩw'a me ndũũ mũno na Yesũ, ala nĩ Vetelo, Andalea, Yakovo, na Yoana, mooka vala ũĩ maneene nake. Aineena namo nĩwamatavisye ĩla ngelekany'o ya ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ, ya ala eĩtu ĩkũmi, na ya ila talendi. Ĩndĩ aiminĩĩa ngewa yake nĩwamatavisye ngelekany'o ĩngĩ ĩmwe. Nthĩnĩ wa ngelekany'o ĩsu nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla "Mwana wa mũndũ" ũkasilĩla "mbaĩ syonthe." No nginya amanyĩw'a asu methĩwe mendeeiw'e mũno nĩ ngelekany'o ĩsu! Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ngelekany'onĩ ĩsu Yesũ nĩwaeleisye mũno ĩũlũ wa ikundi ilĩ sya andũ. Kĩkundi kya mbee akĩelekanilye na malondu na kĩla kĩngĩ akĩelekany'a na mbũi. Na ĩndĩ asyoka amatavya ĩũlũ wa kĩkundi kĩngĩ kya vata kĩla wakĩtie "ana-a-asa" ma "Mũsumbĩ."—Soma Mathayo 25:31-46.
2 Kuma tene andũ ma Yeova nĩmendeeaw'a mũno nĩ ngelekany'o ĩsu, na me na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũmyenda nũndũ nthĩnĩ wayo Yesũ nĩwaeleisye ũndũ ũkonetye thayũ wa andũ. Nĩwoonanisye nĩkĩ amwe makakwata thayũ ũtathela na nĩkĩ angĩ makanangwa tene na tene. Na kwoou no nginya tũelewe maũndũ ala Yesũ wamanyĩisye na tũimaatĩĩa nĩ kana twĩĩsa kũkwata thayũ. Ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, ekai tũmanye atĩĩ: Yeova atũtetheesye ata kũelewa ngelekany'o ĩsu? Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ngelekany'o ĩsu nĩkindĩlĩle vata wa kũtavany'a? Mo naaũ manengetwe wĩa wa kũtavany'a? Na nĩkĩ yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya kũlũmany'a vyũ na "Mũsumbĩ" na ala ũmetĩte 'ana-a-asa makwa'?
YEOVA ATŨTETHEESYE ATA KŨELEWA NGELEKANY'O ĨSU?
3, 4. (a) Nĩ maũndũ meva ma vata twaĩle kũmanya nĩ kana tũelewe nesa ĩla ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi? (b) Ĩkaseti ya Zion's Watch Tower yaeleisye ngelekany'o ĩsu ata mwakanĩ wa 1881?
3 Nĩ kana tũelewe nesa ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi, no nginya tũkwatye maũndũ aa atatũ mawetetwe vau: mbee, naaũ ala mawetetwe, kelĩ, nĩ ĩndĩĩ andũ makasilĩlwa, na katatũ, nĩ kyaũ kĩkatuma amwe maiwa ngalĩko ya malondu na ala angĩ ngalĩko ya mbũi.
4 Mwakanĩ wa 1881, ĩkaseti ya Zion's Watch Tower yaisye kana Yesũ nĩwe "Mwana wa mũndũ" na no we "Mũsumbĩ." Yasyokie yaelesya kana "ana-a-asa" ma Mũsumbĩ nĩ ala makasumbĩka na Klĩsto ĩtunĩ, o vamwe na onthe ala makethĩwa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩtina wa kũvetewa naĩ. Masũanĩaa kana wĩa wa kũvathany'a malondu na mbũi ũkatethw'a ĩvindanĩ ya Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Klĩsto. Na moonaa kana andũ ala makaiwa ngalĩ ya malondu nĩ ala makethĩwa maatĩĩe mwĩao wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa kwendana.
5. Ũmanyi witũ wakenũkangie ata mwakanĩ wa 1923?
5 Mwakanĩ wa 1923, Yeova nĩwatetheeisye andũ make maelewe ngelekany'o ĩsu nesanga. Ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower ya 15/10/1923, nĩyeetĩkĩlile kana Yesũ nĩwe "Mwana wa mũndũ." Ĩndĩ nĩyasyokie yanengane itumi nzeo kuma Maandĩkonĩ, ila syoonanisye naaũ ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto na naaũ malondu. Yaisye kana ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto nĩ ala makasumbĩka nake ĩtunĩ, namo malondu nĩ ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Klĩsto. Nao nĩ ĩndĩĩ malondu makavathanw'a na mbũi? Ĩkaseti yĩu yawetie kana nũndũ ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto makethĩwa masumbĩkĩte nake ĩtunĩ ĩvinda ya Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili, maikethĩwa matonya kũtetheew'a kana matatonya kũtetheew'a nĩ ala makethĩwa kũũ nthĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Kwoou yoonany'a kana malondu makavathanw'a na mbũi Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili ũtanambĩĩa. Nao nĩ kyaũ kĩkatuma mũndũ aiwa ngalĩ ya malondu? Ĩkaseti yĩu yaeleisye kana ala makaiwa ngalĩ ya malondu nĩ ala meetĩkĩlile kana Yesũ nĩ Mwĩaĩi woo na meekwatya Ũsumbĩ ũmaetee moseo.
6. Mwakanĩ wa 1995, twatetheeiw'e ata kũelewa nesanga ĩla ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi?
6 Nũndũ wa ũmanyi ũsu, andũ ma Yeova mambĩĩe kwona kana ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo nĩw'o andũ maendeee kũsilĩlwa na kũiwa ngalĩ ya malondu kana ya mbũi, kwosana na ũndũ mekwosa ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1995, nĩtwaeleiw'e ũndũ ũsu nesanga. Ilungu ilĩ ila syaĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/10/1995, nĩsyoonanisye ũndũ ndeto sya Yesũ ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo 24:29-31 (soma) ivw'anene na ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo 25:31, 32. (Soma.) * Kwondũ wa ũu yavikĩie ũtwi wĩva? Kĩlungu kya mbee katĩ wa isu ilĩ kyaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũsilĩlo wa malondu na mbũi nĩ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte." Ĩndĩ nĩ ĩvinda yũkĩte ĩndĩĩ? "Ũkeethĩwa ĩtina wa ũla 'thĩna' ũwetetwe nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku ya Mathayo 24:29, 30 kwambĩĩa na ĩtina wa Mwana wa mũndũ 'kũka na ũtheu mũtisu.' . . . Na nũndũ nthĩ ĩno nthũku ĩkeethĩwa ĩkilyĩ kwanangwa, Yesũ akasilĩla andũ na aimosea ĩtambya."
7. Ũmũnthĩ tũeleawa ata ĩla ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi?
7 Ũmũnthĩ nĩtũeleawa nesa ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi. Naaũ ala mawetetwe nthĩnĩ wa ngelekany'o ĩsu? Mbee, Yesũ nĩwe "Mwana wa mũndũ," na no we Mũsumbĩ. Namo ala metĩtwe 'ana-a-asa makwa' nĩ aũme na aka ala metĩkĩw'e mauta mesumbĩka na Klĩsto ĩtunĩ. (Alo. 8:16, 17) Na ĩndĩ "malondu" na "mbũi" nĩ andũ kuma mbaĩnĩ syonthe. Asu ti etĩkĩw'a mauta. Nao nĩ ĩndĩĩ andũ makasilĩlwa? Andũ makasilĩlwa thĩna mũnene ũkilyĩ kũthela. Na nĩ kyaũ kĩkatuma andũ matalwa ta malondu kana mbũi? Makasilĩlwa kwosana na ũndũ mekaa ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto ala matiele kũũ nthĩ. Nĩkwĩthĩwa mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ ĩno nĩmũthengeeu vyũ, nĩtũtũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ Yeova nĩwĩthĩĩtwe aitũtetheesya kũelewa ngelekany'o ĩsu na ingĩ ikonanĩtye nayo, ila iandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo kĩlungu kya 24 na kya 25!
NGELEKANY'O ĨSU ĨKINDĨLĨLE ATA VATA WA KŨTAVANY'A?
8, 9. Nĩkĩ ala maelekanĩtw'e na malondu metĩtwe "alũngalu"?
8 Nthĩnĩ wa ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi, Yesũ ndawetete wĩa wa kũtavany'a ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe. Nĩkĩ ĩndĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ngelekany'o ĩsu nĩkindĩlĩle vata wa kũtavany'a?
9 Mbee vyũ, lilikana kana vau Yesũ amanyĩasya aitũmĩa ngelekany'o. Vate nzika ndawetaa ĩũlũ wa kũvathany'a malondu na mbũi mbene. O ta ũu ndaasya kana kĩla ũmwe wa ala makaiwa ngalĩ ya malondu no nginya asũvĩe ũmwe wa ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto, amũnenge lĩu, amũmanthĩe ngũa, kana athi akamwone e kolokolonĩ. Ĩndĩ aneeneaa ũndũ ala maelekanĩtw'e na malondu maĩle kwosa ana-a-asa make. Etĩte ala mailyĩ ta malondu "alũngalu" nũndũ nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana Klĩsto e na ana-a-asa make etĩkĩw'a mauta kũũ nthĩ. O na ĩngĩ ametĩte ũu nũndũ nĩmalũmanĩtye na etĩkĩw'a mauta mĩthenyanĩ ĩno mĩthũku ya mũminũkĩlyo.—Mt. 10:40-42; 25:40, 46; 2 Tim. 3:1-5.
10. Malondu matetheeasya ata ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto?
10 Kelĩ, sũanĩa kĩla Yesũ waneeneaa ayĩsa kũweta ngelekany'o ĩsu. Aneeneaa wonany'o wa kwĩthĩwa kwake e mũsumbĩ ũtenekee na wa mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ ĩno. (Mt. 24:3) Ayambĩĩa kũnengana ũvoo ũsu nĩwawetie kana ũndũ ũmwe wa vata ũla ũkonany'a we nĩwambĩĩe kũsumbĩka na kana twĩ ĩvindanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo nĩ kana ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ "ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe." (Mt. 24:14) Na atanamba kũmanenga ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi, aĩ anamanenga ĩla ngelekany'o ya talendi. Ĩsomo ĩvĩtu nĩyĩeleetye kana Yesũ anenganie ngelekany'o ĩsu nĩ kenda atetheesye etĩkĩw'a mauta, ala nomo "ana-a-asa" make, mamanye kana no nginya matavany'e na kĩthito. Ĩndĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta ala matiele kũũ nthĩ ĩvinda yĩĩ Yesũ ũsumbĩkĩte no anini na me na wĩa mwingĩ mũno wa kũtavya "mbaĩ syonthe" ũvoo mũseo mũminũkĩlyo ũtavikĩte. O na ũu wĩ o vo, ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi yonanĩtye kana etĩkĩw'a mauta me na andũ ma kũmatetheesya. Kwoou ũndũ ũmwe wa vata ũla malondu matonya kwĩka nĩ kana matetheesye ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto nĩ kũlũmany'a namo wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Ĩndĩ matonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana monany'e nĩmalũmanĩtye namo? No kwa kumya mĩvothi na kũmekĩa vinya, kana ve maũndũ angĩ mendekaa?
NAAŨ ALA MAĨLE KŨTAVANY'A?
11. Mũndũ atonya kwĩkũlya ĩkũlyo yĩva, na nĩkĩ?
11 Ũmũnthĩ aingĩ ma amanyĩwa ma Yesũ milioni nyanya ti etĩkĩw'a mauta. Mayaanengwa talendi ila Yesũ wanengie ngombo syake etĩkĩw'a mauta. (Mt. 25:14-18) Kwoou ĩkũlyo nĩ, 'Mo ala mate etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩmanengetwe wĩa ũsu wa kũtavany'a?' Kwasũanĩa itumi ila ikwonany'a kana ũsũngĩo nĩ ĩĩ.
12. Ndeto sya Yesũ ila iandĩkĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo 28:19, 20 itũmanyĩasya kyaũ?
12 Yesũ nĩweaĩe amanyĩw'a make onthe matavany'e. Amina kũthayũũkw'a, eeie aatĩĩi make matw'ĩkĩthye andũ amanyĩw'a, maimamanyĩsya kũkwata "maũndũ onthe" ala wameaĩe. Ũmwe wa maũndũ ala wameaĩe meke nĩ kũtavany'a. (Soma Mathayo 28:19, 20.) Kwoou amanyĩw'a onthe ma Klĩsto nĩmaĩle kũtavany'a, methĩwe me na wĩkwatyo wa kũsumbĩka me ĩtunĩ kana nĩ wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ.—Meko 10:42.
13. Woni ũla woonekie nĩ Yoana wĩonany'a kyaũ, na nĩkĩ?
13 Ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo yonanasya kana wĩa wa kũtavany'a waĩ ũtethw'e nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta vamwe na andũ angĩ. Yesũ nĩwoonisye mũtũmwa Yoana woni wa "mũtwawa" aithokya andũ 'mose manzĩ ma thayũ mana.' Mũtwawa ũsu nĩwe ala etĩkĩw'a mauta 144,000 ala makasumbĩka na Klĩsto ĩtunĩ. (Ũvu. 14:1, 3; 22:17) Namo manzĩ ala mawetetwe vau nĩ nthembo ya Klĩsto ya wovosyo ĩla ĩkatethya andũ maume ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. (Mt. 20:28; Yoa. 3:16; 1 Yoa. 4:9, 10) Wovosyo ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno nthĩnĩ wa ũvoo ũla tũtavanasya. Nũndũ wa ũu etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩmatongoeasya wĩanĩ wa kũtetheesya andũ mamanye ĩũlũ wa wovosyo na maitetheka nĩw'o. (1 Ako. 1:23) Ĩndĩ woninĩ ũsu, Yoana nĩwoonie angĩ mate kĩkundinĩ kya mũtwawa. O namo meawa nĩmasye, "Ũka." Meewa ũu, nĩmetĩkĩlaa na maithokya angĩ mose manzĩ ma thayũ. Kĩkundi kĩu kya kelĩ nĩ ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. Kwoou woni ũsu wa Yoana nĩwonanĩtye nesa kana onthe ala metĩkĩlaa mamina kwĩwa, "Ũka," o namo me na kĩanda kya kũtavany'a.
14. Twaĩle kwĩka ata nĩ kana twonany'e nĩtũatĩĩaa "mwĩao wa Klĩsto"?
14 No nginya ala onthe me ungu wa "mwĩao wa Klĩsto" matavany'e. (Aka. 6:2) Yeova nde mĩao kũndũ kwĩlĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, eeie Aisilaeli atĩĩ: "Kũkeethĩwa mwĩao ũmwe wa ũla ũsyaawa kwenyu, na wa mũeni ũla wĩkalaa ũeni kwenyu." (Kuma 12:49; Ali. 24:22) Ũmũnthĩ Aklĩsto mai ungu wa Mĩao ya Mose. Ĩndĩ ithyonthe twĩ ungu wa "mwĩao wa Klĩsto," twĩthĩwe twĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta kana tũi etĩkĩw'a mauta. Maũndũ ala Yesũ wamanyĩisye me nthĩnĩ wa mwĩao ũsu. Ũndũ ũla mũnene katĩ wa maũndũ ala Yesũ wamanyĩisye nĩ kana aatĩĩi make maĩle kwendana. (Yoa. 13:35; Yak. 2:8) Na nzĩa ĩla nene twonanasya nĩtwendete Ngai, Klĩsto, na atũi maitũ nĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ.—Yoa. 15:10; Meko 1:8.
15. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana mwĩao ũla Yesũ wanenganie nĩwaĩle kũatĩĩwa nĩ aatĩĩi make onthe?
15 Kĩla Yesũ watavasya kakundi kanini ka andũ no kĩkony'e andũ aingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na kau Yesũ atianĩe ũtianĩo na amanyĩw'a make 11 kwondũ wa Ũsumbĩ, ũtianĩo ũsu nũkonetye ala 144,000 onthe. (Luka 22:29, 30; Ũvu. 5:10; 7:4-8) O ta ũu, ĩtina wa Yesũ kũthayũũkw'a nĩwaumĩlĩile amanyĩw'a mate aingĩ mũno na amanenga mwĩao wa kũtavany'a. (Meko 10:40-42; 1 Ako. 15:6) Ĩndĩ amanyĩw'a make onthe ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa nĩmakwatisye kana mwĩao ũsu nũmakonetye, o na ala mataamwĩw'a na matũ moo ayasya ũu. (Meko 8:4; 1 Vet. 1:8) Ũu now'o vailyĩ ũmũnthĩ. Yesũ ndaaneena na mũndũ o na ũmwe katĩ wa atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ milioni nyanya. Ĩndĩ onthe nĩmesĩ kana no nginya mamũĩkĩĩe Klĩsto na mayonany'a mũĩkĩĩo woo kwa kũtavany'a.—Yak. 2:18.
YĨĨ NĨYO ĨVINDA YA KŨLŨMANY'A VYŨ NA ANA-A-ASA MA KLĨSTO
16-18. Ala makaelekanw'a na malondu matonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩmalũmanĩtye na ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto? Nĩkĩ yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya kwĩka ũu?
16 Satani aendeee kũkita ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto ala matiele kũũ nthĩ, na eendeea kũmokita vyũ o ũndũ "kavinda o kanini" kala wĩ nako kekũendeea na kũthela. (Ũvu. 12:9, 12, 17) Ĩndĩ o na kau no mathĩnaw'a mũno, mo nĩmatongoesye wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ũkethĩa ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ nĩmew'ĩte ũvoo mũseo mbee wa ĩvinda yĩngĩ o na yĩva. Ũu wĩonany'a kana vate nzika Yesũ e vamwe namo amatongoesye.—Mt. 28:20.
17 Ala makaelekanw'a na malondu monaa ne ndaĩa nene kwĩthĩwa matonya kũkwata mbau ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a na maũndũnĩ angĩ ma vata. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩmaumasya mĩvothi, makatetheesya kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ, Nyũmba sya Maũmbano Manene, na ovisi sya ũvonge, o na ĩvinda yonthe nĩmew'aa ala manyuvĩtwe nĩ "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" matongoesye maũndũnĩ.—Mt. 24:45-47; Aevl. 13:17.
18 O mĩtũkĩ alaĩka nĩmeũlekya ila iseve sya wanangĩko sya ũla thĩna mũnene. Makeka ũu ĩtina wa ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto ala makethĩwa matiele vaa nthĩ kwĩkĩwa ũsiĩlo woo wa mũthya. (Ũvu. 7:1-3) Na ĩndĩ Ali–Maketoni ĩtanambĩĩa, etĩkĩw'a mauta makatwawa ĩtunĩ. (Mt. 13:41-43) Kwoou ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda twĩĩsa kwiwa ngalĩko ya malondu, yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya kũlũmany'a vyũ na ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto.
^ kal. 6 Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa ngelekany'o ĩsu, sisya ilungu ii, "Utasimamaje Mbele ya Kiti cha Hukumu?" na "Kuna Wakati Ujao Gani kwa Kondoo na Mbuzi?" ila syĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 15/10/1995.

translation:
"And truly I say to you, whatever you did to one of these brothers of mine, however insignificant, you did it to me."—Matt. 25:40.
1, 2. (a) How does Jesus show his love for his brothers? (Consider what he already did.) (b) Why should we want to understand the meaning of the illustration of sheep and goats?
CONSIDER how happy Jesus was when he was with his friends—Philip, Andrew, James, and John—who were very loyal to him. He also showed his love for others by giving them important assignments, such as those involving ten cities and their districts, and those involving talents. He gave another assignment to one of his faithful ones. But why did he give this assignment called "Son of Man" to search "everywhere"? It seems that his friends were eager to know the meaning of this assignment! Why? Because Jesus explained the meaning of this assignment to his disciples. This assignment involved two groups of people—sheep representing righteous people and goats representing wicked people. And he said that he would separate one group from the other, saying "the sheep from the goats."—Read Matthew 25:31-46.
2 We, as Jehovah's people, are eager to learn about this assignment, and we need to understand why Jesus explained it so that we can be ready for the day he searches. Some may feel that they have already shown loyalty and some may feel that they still need to improve. So let us examine what Jesus taught and see whether we are showing loyalty. Let us ask ourselves these questions: Does Jehovah expect us to fully understand this assignment? Are we afraid to ask if we do not understand it? Or are there reasons why we might hesitate to identify who are "the sheep" and who are "the goats"?
DOES JEHOVAH EXPECT US TO FULLY UNDERSTAND THIS ASSIGNMENT?
3, 4. (a) What things can help us determine whether we really understand the meaning of the illustration of sheep and goats? (b) Did the Watch Tower Society explain this assignment as early as 1881?
3 To truly understand the illustration of sheep and goats, we should consider these points: first, what does the illustration teach; second, what is the background; third, how did it help some Christians to discern between true worshipers and others who were only pretending to worship.
4 In 1881, the Watch Tower Society showed that Jesus is both "the Son of Man" and "the Shepherd." It helped readers to understand that the "sheep" are those who follow Christ loyally, while others who do not show such devotion are like the goats. This understanding was connected to the time of the Harvest of the Christian Age. And it showed that those who are identified as sheep are those whom God approves as worthy of everlasting life.
5. How was our understanding clarified in 1923?
5 In 1923, Jehovah directed his people to a clearer understanding of this illustration. The October 15, 1923, issue of The Watch Tower explained that Jesus is "the Son of Man." It admitted that earlier publications had been unclear regarding the Scriptures, but they harmonized with the idea that Christ has sheep and also goats. It stated that Christ's sheep are those who loyally follow him, whereas the goats are those who oppose his followers and are disfellowshipped because of their unfaithfulness. So, do the sheep and the goats represent the same ones throughout the entire Harvest period? That issue explained that those who are approved as sheep during the Harvest period are those who prove themselves faithful and obedient, unlike those who become unfaithful. It further explained that the sheep and the goats are distinguished by the Harvest period itself. Why would someone be identified as a goat? That publication explained that those who are identified as goats are those who have come to believe that Jesus is their Savior and have accepted the good news.
6 In 1995, we came to understand something more about this illustration.
6 In view of what we know, Jehovah's Witnesses realized that the distinction between sheep and goats could continue to apply to individuals as they progress and are identified as either sheep or goats, depending on their course. This is in harmony with the principle found in the Bible. In 1995, we were helped to see this point clearly. For example, an article in The Preacher (Swahili) of October 15, 1995, showed how Matthew 24:29-31 (read) parallels Matthew 25:31, 32. (Read.) * What does this comparison highlight? A key thought expressed in that discussion is: "The separating of sheep from goats is a feature of the final conclusion." But what is this final conclusion? "It will take place when 'the sign' described at Matthew 24:29, 30—that is, when the Son of man 'comes with power and great glory'—begins to manifest itself. . . . And as this momentous time draws near, Jesus will conclude judging mankind and rendering a decision."
7 Can we now better understand the distinction between sheep and goats?
7 We can now better understand the distinction between sheep and goats. But does this mean that the distinction has already begun to be made? Yes, Jesus is the "Son of man," and he is also the Judge. Those who are called "sheep" are those who have faith and who appreciate Christ's ransom sacrifice. (Rev. 8:16, 17) And "goats" include all others. They do not exercise faith. So, why are people being separated? People are being separated because of their response to the good news about Christ and their willingness to side with his brothers. It is comforting to remember that Jehovah helps us to understand this important illustration and its connection to the prophecies recorded in Matthew chapters 24 and 25!
THIS ILLUSTRATION – DOES IT APPLY TO ALL PEOPLE?
8, 9. How do those represented by the "sheep" respond to bad association?
8 In the illustration of the sheep and goats, Jesus will separate people individually. How then can we know whether this illustration applies to a final separation?
9 Indeed, consider how Jesus sends out his disciples to preach. He directs them to associate with people who are responsive to the good news. He does not tell them to go looking for everyone who is associated with bad company, but rather to look for those who show some appreciation for the message about Christ and his Kingdom. He tells them to seek out those who are willing to listen, to learn, or to express curiosity. This shows that those represented by the "sheep" are more than just anyone who happens to be associated with good people. Rather, they are those who demonstrate faith in Christ and his Kingdom. And this is what makes them different from those who are unfaithful and who reject the truth.—Matt. 10:40-42; 25:40, 46; 2 Tim. 3:1-5.
10. Do sheep imitate the ways of Christians?
10 Certainly, Jesus expects all of us to reflect his qualities. He wants us to show the same love and compassion that he displayed toward mankind. (Matt. 24:3) He instructs us to continue preaching the good news until the end of the world, and he assures us that when we are persecuted for our faith, he will support us. Also, he foretold that the sign of his presence would include the work of proclaiming the "good news of the kingdom." (Matt. 24:14) And just as he taught his disciples to distinguish between the illustration of the sheep and goats and the illustration of the talents, so we too should understand that Jesus judges people based on their actions, especially their treatment of others—his brothers. The fact that the judgment involves "all nations" indicates that it will be a thorough investigation of each individual's heart and motives. It also means that the illustration of the sheep and goats applies to all people, including those who claim to be Christians but may not actually practice true worship. So, the distinction between the sheep and the goats depends on how individuals respond to the message and how they treat Jesus and his followers. What, then, determines whether someone is considered among the sheep or the goats? Is it simply outward appearance, or is it something deeper?
WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO BE SHEEP OR GOATS?
11. How can a person demonstrate that he is on the side of the sheep, and why?
11 Many of Jesus' followers today are like the wise virgins who made ready oil for their lamps. They use their talents to promote God's Kingdom. (Matt. 25:14-18) Therefore, the question arises, 'How can we prove ourselves worthy of being among those who will survive?' By diligently using what we have been entrusted with.
12. What does Jesus' command recorded at Matthew 28:19, 20 instruct us to do?
12 Jesus has given all his followers a commission. He commands them to go and make disciples of people of all nations, teaching them to observe "all things" he has commanded. One of the things he has commanded is to preach the good news. (Read Matthew 28:19, 20.) Thus, all Christians should zealously participate in the ministry, whether it is by actively sharing the good news in public or by supporting those who do.—Acts 10:42.
13. Who was John, and what did he see in vision?
13 The book of Revelation shows that those who will be sheeps will associate closely with others who are also seeking salvation. Jesus revealed to the apostle John a vision of "a great crowd" who were standing before God's throne and worshiping him. This great crowd represents the 144,000 anointed ones who will reign with Christ in heaven. (Rev. 14:1, 3; 22:17) And the remaining sheep are represented by countless others who exercise faith in Jesus and obey him. (Matt. 20:28; John 3:16; 1 John 4:9, 10) Salvation is something precious, and it is right that we desire to know more about God's purpose and how we can attain life everlasting. (1 Cor. 1:23) In this connection, John saw other things that were symbolic of the great crowd. He said: "I looked, and I heard a voice of many multitudes." He then described them as worshiping God. This large group of people are those who will live forever on earth. So John's vision assures us that there is a hope for those who respond favorably to the good news, saying, "Come." It means that they will live forever on earth.
14. Will we show that we are truly "Christians" by our actions?
14 Not everyone who claims to be a "Christian" is a true Christian. (Acts 6:2) Jehovah is the one who judges what is in the heart. For example, ancient Israelites said: "We are the offspring of Abraham," but they did not demonstrate genuine faith. (Rom. 12:49; Luke 24:22) Just as Christians are disciples of Christ, they should imitate his qualities. Therefore, when we speak of being "Christians," we should live according to Bible principles. Jesus taught his followers important lessons about what it means to be a Christian. One key point he emphasized was the importance of love. (John 13:35; James 2:8) To please God, Christ, and our fellow humans, we must practice this vital quality of love.—John 15:10; Mark 1:8.
15. How can we determine whether Jesus' teachings harmonize with what we believe and practice?
15 Jesus gathered a large group of disciples, and his teachings had a profound effect on many people. For instance, during his ministry on earth, Jesus assigned 11 faithful apostles to preach the good news, and their ministry eventually reached 144,000 others. (Luke 22:29, 30; Rev. 5:10; 7:4-8) However, Jesus also wanted his followers to help many more people come to know the truth and become disciples. (Mark 10:40-42; 1 Cor. 15:6) His loyal apostles played an integral part in spreading the good news, and countless others joined them in proclaiming the message. (Mark 8:4; 1 Peter 1:8) This demonstrates how effective their ministry was. Jesus associated himself with both men and women, and he showed kindness to millions of imperfect humans. It is therefore essential that we identify ourselves as Christians and prove our dedication by making disciples.—James 2:18.
WHY THIS UNDERSTANDING IS IMPORTANT FOR DISCIPLES OF CHRIST
16-18. Why is it important for us to examine ourselves to see if we are truly following Christ? What will help us to do so?
16 Satan continues to deceive those who claim to be disciples of Christ, subtly leading them astray and causing them to stumble. (Rev. 12:9, 12, 17) He does this by presenting error as something "small," hoping that they will gradually accept it and compromise. But if we remain vigilant and steadfast, we can resist his efforts and maintain our integrity. (Rev. 12:11) We need to remember that Jesus promised to be with his followers always.—Matt. 28:20.
17 How can we avoid being misled by false teachings and remaining firm in our faith? For example, we might be tempted to engage in questionable practices, such as attending worldly entertainment, visiting places of worship that promote false doctrines, or associating with individuals who have harmful influences. All of these things can weaken our spiritual strength and cause us to compromise our standards.—Matt. 24:45-47; Heb. 13:17.
18 Many people today are influenced by materialistic pursuits and the desire for prominence. However, true Christians strive to remain humble and prioritize spiritual values. (Prov. 7:1-3) And just as wheat is separated from weeds, so too will genuine Christians be distinguished from those who are insincere. (Matt. 13:41-43) Therefore, let us continue to examine ourselves and strengthen our association with fellow believers, so that we may discern truth from falsehood.
^ Oct. 6 If you obtain an extra copy of this publication, refer to the article "Will You Stand Firm Before God's Judgment Seat?" and "What Future Time Is Set for Sheep and Goats?" which appeared in The Watchtower of October 15, 1995.

text:
"Endai . . . mũkatw'ĩkĩthye mbaĩ syonthe amanyĩw'a, mũkĩmavatisa . . . mũkĩmamanyĩsya kũkwata maũndũ onthe o na meva ala namwĩaĩe."—MT. 28:19, 20.
MBATHI: 141, 17
1, 2. Nĩ makũlyo meva tũtonya kũkũlya maumanĩte na ndeto ila Yesũ wawetie ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 24:14?
NĨ ANDŨ anini mũno matonya kũlea kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyĩsĩkĩe mũno nũndũ wa wĩa woo wa kũtavany'a. Ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ o na ethĩwa andũ nĩmeĩtĩkĩlana naitũ kana nĩmeũtũvĩnga vyũ. O naku no kwĩthĩwa ũkomanĩte na andũ ũitavany'a makakwĩa kana o na kau maikwĩtĩkĩlana naku, nĩmanengete ndaĩa wĩa ũla tũtethasya. O tondũ twĩsĩ, Yesũ athanie kana ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ ũkatavanw'a nthĩ yonthe. (Mt. 24:14) Ĩndĩ twĩsĩ ata kana wĩa ũla tũtethasya wĩanĩsya wathani wa Yesũ? Tũkasya kana vai angĩ matethasya wĩa ũsu eka ithyĩ, twĩthĩwa tũyĩtũlya?
2 Ndĩni mbingĩ syonaa kana syo nitavanasya ũvoo ũla Yesũ waisye nũtavanw'e. Ĩndĩ kĩla andũ ma ndĩni isu mekaa no kumĩsya ala mathaithaa namo ũkũsĩ, kũtavany'a makanisanĩ, kana kũtavany'a isesenĩ sya maũvoo ta Indaneti na televiseni. Namo angĩ mawetaa ũtethyo ũla ndĩni syoo inenganĩte kana kĩthito kĩla syĩkĩĩte maũndũnĩ ma ũiiti na kĩsomo. Mo maũndũ asu andũ ma ndĩni mawetaa nĩmo Yesũ weeaĩe amanyĩw'a make meke?
3. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 28:19, 20, no nginya aatĩĩi ma Yesũ meke maũndũ meva ana?
3 Mo amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ mekalaa mana meteele andũ moke kũla maĩ? Vaitonyeka! Yesũ amina kũthayũũkw'a atavisye amanyĩw'a make maana meana ũna ndeto ii: 'Endai ĩndĩ mũkatw'ĩkĩthye mbaĩ syonthe amanyĩw'a, mũkĩmavatisa: mũkĩmamanyĩsya kũkwata maũndũ onthe o na meva ala namwĩaĩe.' (Mt. 28:19, 20) Ndeto isu syĩonany'a ve maũndũ ana maĩle kwĩkwa. Maũndũ asu nĩ kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a, kũmavatisa, na kũmamanyĩsya. Ĩndĩ tũtanesa kwĩka maũndũ asu twaĩle kwamba kwĩka ata? Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Endai"! Mũsomi ũmwe wa Mbivilia aielesya ndeto ĩsu aisye ũũ: "Etĩkĩli onthe nĩmatavĩtw'e 'endai,' methĩwe mekĩlanĩlya lelũ kana meinga ũkanga."—Mt. 10:7; Luka 10:3.
4. Kũtw'ĩka "atei ma andũ" kũkonetye kyaũ?
4 We Yesũ endaa ndeto isu syake ianĩw'e nĩ kĩla mũndũ e weka, kana endaa ianĩw'e nĩ kĩkundi kĩ na ngwatanĩo kĩitavany'a ũvoo mũseo? Nũndũ mũndũ ũmwe ndaĩ atonya kũthi kwa andũ ma "mbaĩ syonthe," wĩa ũsu waĩ no nginya ũthũkũmwe nĩ kĩkundi kya andũ aingĩ me ngwatanĩo. Yesũ nĩwoonanisye ũu ĩla wathokisye amanyĩw'a make amatw'ĩkĩthye "atei ma andũ." (Soma Mathayo 4:18-22.) Kũtea kũla Yesũ wawetaa vaa ti kũla mũndũ ũendaa kũtea makũyũ e weka aitũmĩa ndoano na ayĩkala nthĩ eteele ĩkũyũ yĩse kũka kũũma kasama kala wĩkĩĩte. Vandũ va ũu, Yesũ awetaa andũ meũtea makũyũ maitũmĩa neti, na wĩa ũsu wendaa mũndũ atũmĩe vinya mwingĩ na athũkũme e ngwatanĩo na angĩ.—Luka 5:1-11.
5. Twaĩle kũmantha mosũngĩo ma makũlyo meva ana, na nĩkĩ?
5 Nĩ kana tũmanye ala matavanasya ũvoo mũseo ũmũnthĩ kwosana na wathani wa Yesũ, twaĩle kũmantha mosũngĩo ma makũlyo aa ana:
Nĩ ũvoo wĩva waĩle kũtavanw'a?
Kĩeleelo kya kũthũkũma wĩa ũsu kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa kĩva?
Nĩ nzĩa syĩva syaĩle kũtũmĩwa?
Wĩa ũsu waĩle kũtethw'a kĩsio kĩana ata na kwa ĩvinda yĩana ata?
Kũmanya mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu nĩkũũtũtetheesya tũmanye naaũ matethasya wĩa ũũ wa kwovosya mathayũ, o na nĩkũũtũtetheesya tũlũlũmĩlye ũtwi witũ wa kũendeea kũtethya wĩa ũsu twĩ aĩkĩĩku.—1 Tim. 4:16.
NĨ ŨVOO WĨVA WAĨLE KŨTAVANW'A?
6. Nĩkĩ ũtonya kwasya ũte na nzika kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyo itavanasya ũvoo ũla Yesũ waisye ũtavanw'e?
6 Soma Luka 4:43. Yesũ atavanasya "ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ," na endaa amanyĩw'a make meke o take. Nĩ kĩkundi kĩva kya andũ kĩtavasya "mbaĩ syonthe" ũvoo ũsu? Vai kĩkundi kĩngĩ eka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. O na amwe matũvĩngaa nĩmesĩ ũu. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũthembi ũmwe wĩthĩawa misonalĩ kũndũ atavisye Ngũsĩ ĩmwe kana we ekalĩte kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na nĩwakũlĩtye Ngũsĩ mbingĩ nthĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ũvoo ũla itavanasya. Asũngĩiwe ata? Mũthembi ũsu aisye ũũ: "Onthe maĩ atumanu nũndũ manengae o ũsũngĩo ũũ ũmwe: 'Ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ.'" Ngũsĩ isu iyaanengane ũsũngĩo ũvw'anene aĩ nũndũ nĩ 'ndumanu,' ĩndĩ nũndũ syĩ ngwatanĩo o ũndũ Aklĩsto ma w'o maĩle kwĩthĩwa mailyĩ. (1 Ako. 1:10) Ũsũngĩo wasyo wosanĩte na ũvoo ũla wĩthĩawa ũneenewe ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya Yĩtavanasya Ũsumbĩ wa Yeova. Ĩkaseti yĩĩ yĩkwatĩkanaa kwa ithyomo 254, na kĩla ĩvinda yatw'a kumw'a no ta yĩtumbĩthaw'a kovi vakuvĩ milioni 59. Vai ĩkaseti yĩngĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yĩtumbĩthaw'a mũno wĩana ũu.
7. Twĩsĩ ata kana atongoi ma ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto maitavanasya ũvoo ũla Yesũ waisye ũtavanw'e?
7 Atongoi ma ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto maitavanasya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Na ĩla mesa kũweta ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ maũwetaa ũu ta kĩndũ kĩthĩawa ngoonĩ ya Mũklĩsto. (Luka 17:21) Maitetheeasya andũ maelewe kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ silikalĩ yĩ ĩtunĩ ĩtongoew'e nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto, na kana nĩyo ĩkamina mathĩna onthe ma andũ, na kana o mĩtũkĩ ĩkilyĩ ĩnavetanga ũthũku ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Ũvu. 19:11-21) Vandũ va ũu monaa nĩ kavaa makamũlilikana Yesũ ĩvindanĩ ya sikũkũ ya Kĩlisimasi na ya Isita. O na ti ta mesĩ kĩla Yesũ ũkeka ĩla ũkethĩwa Mũsumbĩ wa nthĩ. Yu nũndũ mayĩsĩ ũvoo ũla maĩle kũtavany'a, we wĩona ta ũsengy'o tũkasya kana o na mayĩsĩ ũvoo ũsu waĩle kũtavanw'a na kĩeleelo kĩva?
KĨELEELO KYA KŨTHŨKŨMA WĨA ŨSU KYAĨLE KWĨTHĨWA KĨVA?
8. Nĩ maũndũ meva mũndũ ũtonya kwĩka akonany'a e na kĩeleelo kĩthũku kya kũtavany'a?
8 Kĩeleelo kya kũtethya wĩa wa kũtavany'a kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa kĩ kĩva? Kĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ne kwosany'a mbesa na kwaka myako mĩnene myanakavye. Ĩndĩ Yesũ eeie amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "Nĩmwosete mana, nenganai mana." (Mt. 10:8) Ndeto ya Ngai ndyaĩlĩte kũtandĩthw'a. (2 Ako. 2:17) Ala meũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ mayaĩlĩte kũtavany'a me na kĩeleelo kya kwĩyĩuna. (Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 20:33-35.) O na kau ũtao ũsu wĩ ũtheinĩ, makanisa maingĩ maiũatĩĩaa. Vandũ va ũu, mosanasya mbesa nĩ kana iũngamĩe ngalama sya makanisa moo. Methĩawa na ngalama sya kũĩva atongoi moo, vamwe na athũkũmi angĩ aingĩ ki ala mathũkũmaa kw'o. O na mavinda maingĩ wĩthĩaa atongoi asu ma ndĩni nĩmeyũmbanĩsye malĩ mbingĩ mũno.—Ũvu. 17:4, 5.
9. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itavanasya na kĩeleelo kĩseo?
9 Nasyo Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩsĩkĩe ata? Wĩa ũla itethasya ũũngamĩwe nĩ mĩvothi ĩla andũ maumasya na ngenda. (2 Ako. 9:7) Na ĩla me Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ kana me maũmbanonĩ manene, vai mbesa ikolanaw'a. Ĩndĩ mwaka mũthelu, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova inatũmĩie masaa vakuvĩ mbilioni ilĩ iitavany'a ũvoo mũseo na iimanyĩsya andũ mbee wa milioni kenda Mbivilia kĩla mwei vate ndĩvi. Ũndũ wa ũsengy'o nĩ kana, eka kũtw'ĩka matavanasya mate kũĩvwa, mo ene nĩmo maũngamĩaa ngalama syoo ĩla meũtavany'a! Mũsomi ũmwe aisye ũũ aiweta wĩa ũla Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itethasya: "Kĩeleelo kyoo nĩ kũtavany'a na kũmanyĩsya. . . . Na nũndũ mai atongoi, maikwataa ngalama mbingĩ." Kwoou-ĩ, kĩeleelo kitũ kya kũtethya wĩa ũũ nĩ kĩva? Kwa ũkuvĩ, ithyĩ tũthũkũmaa wĩa ũũ na ngenda nũndũ nĩtwendete Yeova na nĩtwendete atũi maitũ. Kwĩyumya kũu kwitũ kwosanĩte na wathani ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 110:3. (Soma.)
NĨ NZĨA SYĨVA SYAĨLE KŨTŨMĨWA?
10. Yesũ na amanyĩw'a make matũmĩaa nzĩa syĩva kũtavany'a?
10 Yesũ na amanyĩw'a make matũmĩaa nzĩa syĩva kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo? Maendaa kw'onthe kũla matonya kwĩthĩa andũ, ta masokonĩ, malelũnĩ, na mĩsyĩ. Nĩmatavanasya nyũmba na nyũmba maimantha ala mekwendeew'a. (Mt. 10:11; Luka 8:1; Meko 5:42; 20:20) Kũtavany'a na mũvango ũseũvĩte ũu kwoonanasya mayaĩ na kyende.
11, 12. Wasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩ kĩvathũkany'o kyaũ na ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto?
11 Syo ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto nĩsyĩkaa ũu? Athaithi ma mbingĩ syasyo maekeie atongoi masyo wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Na vandũ va kwĩthĩwa "atei ma andũ," atongoi ma ndĩni isu syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto methĩawa masyaĩtye mũno masũvĩe andũ ala maminĩte kũmakwatya. Nĩ w'o kana mavinda amwe atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmesaa kwĩkĩa vinya aatĩĩi moo matavany'e. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwambĩĩonĩ wa mwaka wa 2001, Pope John Paul II aandĩkie ũũ valũanĩ: "Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩana ũna, nĩnĩthĩĩtwe ndineena ĩũlũ wa ũla mũtavanĩlye mweũ. Na yu nĩngwenda kũtũngĩlĩĩla ũu . . . No nginya tũamũkye veva ũla Vaulo waĩ naw'o ĩla waisye: 'Woo nĩ wakwa, ethĩwa ndiũtavany'a Ũvoo Mũseo.'" Vovu ũsu aendeeie kwasya kana wĩa ũsu "ndwaĩle kũekewa o ala 'mesene naw'o' ĩndĩ nĩ wa Andũ ma Ngai onthe." Ĩndĩ nĩ andũ meana ata maatĩĩe ndeto syake?
12 Nasyo Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩkĩte ata? Nosyo syĩ syoka itavanasya kana Yesũ ethĩĩtwe e Mũsumbĩ kuma mwaka wa 1914. O tondũ Yesũ waisye, syonaa wĩa wa kũtavany'a wĩ wa vata mũno. (Mko. 13:10) Ĩvuku yĩmwe yaĩtye: "Ngũsĩ sya Yeova siĩte wĩa wa kũtavany'a mbee wa maũndũ onthe." (Pillars of Faith—American Congregations and Their Partners) Mũandĩki wa ĩvuku yĩu aandĩkie ũũ aiweta maũndũ amwe maneeniwe nĩ Ngũsĩ ĩmwe ya Yeova: "Ĩla syakomana na mũndũ wĩ na nzaa, ũkwĩw'a wii, kana mũwau, nitataa imũtetheesye, . . . ĩndĩ iyũlawa kana wĩa wasyo mũnene nĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno na vata wa ũtangĩĩo." Ngũsĩ sya Yeova niendeee kũtavany'a ũvoo ũsu iitũmĩa nzĩa ila syatũmĩawa nĩ Yesũ na amanyĩw'a make.
WĨA ŨSU WAĨLE KŨTETHW'A KĨSIO KĨANA ATA NA KWA ĨVINDA YĨANA ATA?
13. Wĩa wa kũtavany'a waĩle kũtethw'a kĩsio kĩana ata?
13 Yesũ nĩwawetie ũvoo mũseo waĩle kũtavanw'a kĩsio kĩana ata. Aisye kana ũkatavanw'a 'nthĩ yonthe.' (Mt. 24:14) O na eeie aatĩĩi make matw'ĩkĩthye andũ ma 'mbaĩ syonthe' amanyĩw'a. (Mt. 28:19, 20) Ndeto isu syonthe syĩonany'a kana wĩa ũsu waĩle kũtethw'a nthĩ yonthe.
14, 15. Twĩsĩ ata kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyo ianĩĩtye ũla wathani wa Yesũ ũkonetye kĩsio kĩla kyaĩlĩte kũtavanw'a? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
14 Ekai tũsũanĩe maũndũ mana nĩ kana tũelewe ũndũ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ianĩĩtye ũla wathani wa Yesũ ũkonetye kĩsio kĩla kyaĩlĩte kũtavanw'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, nthĩ ya Amelika yĩ na atongoi ta 600,000 ma ndĩni syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, nasyo Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nthĩ ĩsu nĩ ta 1,200,000. Nthĩ yonthe Ĩkanisa ya Roman Catholic yĩ na athembi mavĩtũkĩte 400,000 o vanini. Yu wĩ na kyu kĩlĩkonĩ, kwasũanĩa Ngũsĩ ila itavanasya ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ iitũmĩa Mbivilia. Nthĩ yonthe Ngũsĩ ta milioni nyanya nĩsyĩyumĩtye kũtavany'a nthĩ 240. Ũsu nĩ wĩa wa ũsengy'o mũno ũendeee kwĩanĩw'a, na kyu nĩkĩtumaa Yeova akwata nguma na ngatho.—Sav. 34:1; 51:15.
15 Ithyĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova twĩthĩawa na wendi mwingĩ mũno wa kũtavya andũ aingĩ ũndũ vatonyeka ũvoo mũseo mũthya ũtanavika. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, vai angĩ matethasya wĩa ta ũla tũtethasya wa kũalyũla na kumĩthya mavuku. Mavuku milioni mbingĩ vamwe na makaseti, tulakiti, valũa sya kũthokya andũ maũmbanonĩ manene, na sya kũthokya andũ moke kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ inyaĩĩkaw'a mana. Tumĩthĩtye mavuku ma mĩthemba mingĩ kwa ithyomo mbee wa 700. Nayo Biblia Takatifu—Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya ĩtumbĩthĩtw'e kovi mbee wa milioni 200 na kwa ithyomo mbee wa 130. Mwaka mũthelu wĩ w'oka tũnatumbĩthisye mavuku ta mbilioni inya na nusu. Nakyo kĩla kĩsese kitũ kya Indaneti kĩ na maũvoo ma ithyomo mbee wa 750. Ve atavany'a angĩ we wĩsĩ matethetye wĩa ta ũsu?
16. Twĩsĩ ata kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syĩ na veva wa Ngai?
16 Wĩa wa kũtavany'a waĩle kũtethw'a ĩvinda yĩana ata? Yesũ aisye kana wĩa ũũ ũkatethw'a nginya mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, "na ĩndĩ mũminũkĩlyo ũkyũka." Nĩ ndĩni yĩva yĩthĩĩtwe ĩitavany'a ũvoo mũseo o na mĩthenyanĩ ĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo? Andũ amwe tũkomanaa namo tũitavany'a no matwĩe: "Ithyĩ nithyĩ twĩ na veva mũtheu, ĩndĩ inyw'ĩ ninyw'ĩ mũtavanasya ũvoo." Ĩndĩ we ndũkwona kana kũmĩĩsya kwitũ wĩanĩ ũũ kwonanasya kana twĩ na veva wa Ngai? (Meko 1:8; 1 Vet. 4:14) Mavinda kwa mavinda ndĩni imwe nitataa kwĩka ũndũ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova itindaa iyĩka, ĩndĩ niemetwe. Namo angĩ matw'ĩkaa amisonalĩ, ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kavinda maikola na mayĩnũka. O na kau amwe namo nĩmatataa kũthi maitavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, mo methĩawa maitavany'a ĩũlũ wa kyaũ? Ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu wĩonany'a kana mayĩthĩawa maitethya wĩa ũla Klĩsto wambĩĩisye.
NAAŨ ALA VATE NZIKA MATAVANASYA ŨLA ŨVOO MŨSEO?
17, 18. (a) Nĩkĩ tũte na nzika kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyo itavanasya ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa tũendeea kũtavany'a?
17 Kwoou ũtonya kwasya naaũ ala vate nzika matavanasya ũla ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ? Tũte na nzika o na vanini tũtonya kũsũngĩa tũkasya: "Nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova." Nĩkĩ tũte na nzika? Nũndũ nithyĩ tũtavanasya ũvoo ũla Yesũ waisye ũtavanw'e, naw'o nĩ ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. Na ĩla tũũthi tũimantha andũ tũmatavye ũvoo twĩthĩawa tũitũmĩa nzĩa ila syaĩle. Tũtavanasya twĩ na kĩeleelo kĩseo, nakyo nĩ wendo ti kũmantha mbesa. Nithyĩ tũtavanĩtye kĩsio kĩnene, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩtũtatĩte tũvikĩsye andũ ma mbaĩ syonthe na ithyomo syonthe ũvoo mũseo. Na ĩndĩ twĩendeea kũtavany'a tũteũnoa nginya ĩla mũthya ũkavika.
18 Nĩtũseng'aa mũno nũndũ wa kĩla andũ ma Ngai maendeee kwĩanĩsya ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ twĩkalĩte. Ĩndĩ nĩ kyaũ kĩtetheesye andũ ma Ngai meanĩsye maũndũ asu onthe? Valũa ũla mũtũmwa Vaulo waandĩkĩe Avilivi nũsũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu. Amaandĩkĩe ũũ: "Nĩndonya maũndũ onthe nthĩnĩ wake ũla ũndonyethasya." (Avi. 4:13) Ekai ithyonthe tũendeee kũthũkũma na vinya ũla Ĩthe witũ wĩ wendo ũtũnengae, na nĩtũendeei kũtata ũndũ tũtonya twĩanĩsye ũthũkũmi witũ.—2 Tim. 4:5.

translation:
"Go . . . and make disciples of people of all nations, baptizing them . . . teaching them to observe all things I have commanded you."—Matt. 28:19, 20.
FOOTNOTE: 141, 17
1, 2. What reasons do we have to be confident that the good news will be preached to people of all nations before Christ's presence ends, and what does Matthew 24:14 indicate?
IT IS people who determine whether Jehovah's Kingdom will come or not. This means that the fulfillment depends on our activity and effort. But how can we show confidence that we are actively participating, and how can we maintain that confidence? If we become discouraged because of opposition or because few seem interested in the message, we need to remember what Jesus foretold about the sign of his presence. (Matt. 24:14) And so, what should we do to strengthen our faith and continue preaching? We may wonder if there are certain territories where the work is especially difficult, and if we should concentrate our efforts there.
2 Why are many convinced that the work Jesus commissioned will be completed? Many feel that they personally have a responsibility to do everything they can to preach the good news, despite obstacles such as persecution, restrictions, or negative influences from the Internet and television. They also realize that some people may be preoccupied with their own problems and interests and may not give attention to spiritual matters. So, what can those individuals do to imitate Jesus' example and zeal?
3. According to Matthew 28:19, 20, what commission did Jesus give his followers?
3 What does Jesus' commission mean for us today? It means that we should actively share the good news with as many people as possible. He urged his disciples to go and make disciples of people of all nations, teaching them to observe all things he had commanded. (Matt. 28:19, 20) This instruction has great significance for us today. It involves going to people, making disciples, and teaching them. How can we effectively carry out this assignment? Jesus said: "Go!" One Bible scholar explained this command as follows: "The force of 'go' implies constant activity or progress."—Matt. 10:7; Luke 10:3.
4. What does it mean to "go to all people"?
4 Does Jesus want each individual to personally seek out people, or does he want us to work in groups to reach those who are responsive? While one person may be able to speak to "all people," it is often more practical to associate with a group of interested individuals. Jesus demonstrated this principle when he commissioned his disciples to "go to all people." (Read Matthew 4:18-22.) As Jesus traveled from town to town, he did not simply look for isolated individuals; rather, he focused on reaching communities. And as he did so, Jesus drew people who were eager to learn, and they responded favorably to his message.—Luke 5:1-11.
5. What further questions might arise, and why?
5 If we want to imitate the example of Jesus and his apostles, we might ask ourselves these questions:
Are we willing to adjust our routines?
What steps can we take to improve our ability to communicate?
How can we use our time wisely?
Are we willing to go where people are, even if it means going to unfamiliar places?
Thinking about these questions will help us examine ourselves and determine whether we are truly zealous in sharing the good news, or whether we need to make adjustments in how we conduct our ministry.—1 Tim. 4:16.
ARE WE WILLING TO ADJUST OUR ROUTINES?
6. Why might you hesitate to start new conversations, and what confidence does Jehovah give us?
6 Read Luke 4:43. Jesus continued to preach "the good news of the Kingdom," and he did not neglect his brothers. Is this group of people who were eager to hear "everything" the good news similar to a group associated with Jehovah today? Yes, and there are many such groups. For example, one elder visited a family who asked him about one publication or another, and he brought them several publications, which led to more interest and eventually a Bible study. Was this wrong? This elder said: "I realized that I had been focusing on just one thought: 'The good news of the Kingdom.'" That publication sparked their interest, and they wanted to learn more, so it was wise of him to share other publications with them. (1 Pet. 1:10) Your zeal should be in harmony with Jehovah's desire to have people know the truth about His Kingdom. This magazine reaches people in over 250 languages, and each issue is distributed to nearly 59 million people. There are also other publications that can help people find out more about the truth.
7. Should we try to force people to accept the message of the Kingdom, like Jesus did when he preached it?
7 We should let people freely choose whether to accept the message of God's Kingdom. And we should remember that the Kingdom message will ultimately triumph because it has the backing of Christ. (Luke 17:21) Help people understand that God's Kingdom is a real government ruled by Jesus Christ, that it will solve mankind's problems, and that it will bring lasting peace. (Rev. 19:11-21) People often associate Jesus with Christmas and Easter. But don't forget that Jesus proclaimed the Kingdom during his ministry. So when you share the good news, ask yourself, 'Am I being respectful and considerate?'
QUESTIONS TO HELP YOU STAY RESPECTFUL AND CONSIDERATE
8. What things can a person do to show respect and consideration when sharing the good news?
8 How can we be respectful and considerate when sharing the good news? By being generous and giving willingly. Jesus encouraged his followers: "You received without cost; give without cost." (Matt. 10:8) God wants us to be liberal. (2 Cor. 2:17) Therefore, our preaching work should be done with generosity. (Read Acts 20:33-35.) However, some brothers may feel they cannot afford to contribute much financially. Congregations have learned to be understanding. Some brothers generously donate their time and energy, while others contribute what little money they have. Many congregations also receive donations from those who appreciate the help they receive.—Rev. 17:4, 5.
9. How can we know that Jehovah's organization supports our efforts to be respectful?
9 Does Jehovah's organization truly care about us? It shows its concern by how it deals with problems. (2 Cor. 9:7) And whether it involves the Kingdom Hall or large conventions, expenses are carefully managed. For example, last year, Jehovah's organization used billions of hours to share the good news and helped millions learn about the Bible each month. What this demonstrates is that, despite the need to cover so many expenses, funds are used wisely! One student once wrote to say that Jehovah's organization "is concerned with spreading the truth… and uses its resources effectively." So, what is the purpose behind this careful management? To show our appreciation to Jehovah and to support his people. Meditating on this can strengthen our faith, as shown by Psalm 110:3. (Read.)
HOW IS THE ORGANIZATION SUPPORTED?
10. How did Jesus and his disciples support themselves while traveling and preaching?
10 Did Jesus and his disciples support themselves during their extensive travels? They often worked secular jobs to pay for food, lodging, and clothing. They preached from house to house and visited homes. (Matt. 10:11; Luke 8:1; Mark 5:42; 20:20) This practical approach made their ministry more effective and sustainable.
11, 12. Why does Jehovah's organization provide financial assistance to congregations when needed, yet also encourage Christians to be generous?
11 Why does Christian generosity matter? Because many brothers need help to continue preaching. And people who are touched by the message, known as "interested ones," may need material things to progress spiritually and accept the truth. It is possible that some interested persons will respond favorably only if they receive assistance. For example, in a 2001 article, Pope John Paul II wrote: "For nearly two decades, I have been reflecting on the importance of evangelization. And I want to contribute to this… Let us embrace the words of Paul which still resonate today: 'Woe to me if I do not preach the good news!'" That sentiment reflects a desire to share the good news with others, regardless of whether they seem "worthy" or "unworthy." Does that mean that we should give aid to anyone who asks, no matter what their background?
12 Does Jehovah's organization support such generosity? Some say that it did not begin until Jesus began ruling in heaven in 1914. However, Jesus commanded his followers to be generous. (Matt. 13:10) One publication states: "Jehovah's Witnesses do not engage in general philanthropy." (Pillars of Faith—American Congregations and Their Partners) The author of that book writes about how one of Jehovah's organizations responded to a request from a man who had problems with alcohol: "If a man comes to us with a problem, whether it is drink, gambling, or marital difficulties, we try to help him… but we do not provide financial assistance unless it is to relieve extreme distress and prevent starvation." Jehovah's organization continues to show generosity, but it uses funds differently than Jesus and his disciples did.
DO WE NEED TO ASK QUESTIONS OR INVESTIGATE THOROUGHLY?
13 Should we ask questions or investigate thoroughly?
13 Jesus authorized his followers to preach the good news thoroughly. He told them to go to "all nations." (Matt. 24:14) And he instructed them to make disciples of people of "all ethnies." (Matt. 28:19, 20) So all of us should endeavor to reach all people.
14, 15. Why can we be sure that Jehovah's organization is supporting the fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy regarding the preaching work? (See accompanying article, page 8.)
14 Let us examine some facts so that we may understand how Jehovah's organization is supporting the fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy regarding the preaching work. For example, the United States has about 600,000 congregations, while Jehovah's organization worldwide has about 1,200,000. The entire Roman Catholic Church has approximately 400,000 priests. Therefore, there is good reason to believe that Jehovah is using his organization to proclaim the Bible's message. In fact, over 240 countries have been reached with the good news. This is a sign of continuing progress, and it shows why Jehovah is blessing his people.—Ps. 34:1; 51:15.
15 As Jehovah's Witnesses continue to reach out to many people, they are helping them to find solutions to their problems and to learn about God's Kingdom. To accomplish this, they use various methods, such as public meetings and home Bible studies. Millions of publications, including books, magazines, brochures, and tracts, are used to help people learn about God and to appreciate Jesus' teachings. We distribute hundreds of millions of these publications each year. Also, the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures has been printed over 200 million copies and in over 130 languages. Last year alone we printed billions of pages. And the Internet provides access to information on over 750 websites. Who are doing this important work?
16. Do Jehovah's Witnesses claim to be inspired by God?
16 Are those who preach willing to share good news with others? Jesus asked his followers whether they would continue preaching despite opposition, saying: "Go make disciples." What can motivate us to continue sharing the good news even when facing difficulties? Some of us reason like this: "We want to show our gratitude, so we will continue to preach." But does this reasoning reveal that we are motivated by divine direction? (Acts 1:8; 1 Cor. 4:14) One way to determine what motivates Jehovah's Witnesses is to examine their conduct closely, especially when faced with challenges. And some may wonder why we visit homes from house to house, and why we speak to people wherever they gather. The example set by early Christians shows us how to imitate Christ's ministry.
WHY ARE PEOPLE WILLING TO SHARE THIS GOOD NEWS?
17, 18. (a) Why are we confident that Jehovah supports our efforts to share the good news? (b) What moves us to preach?
17 How do you know that people are willing to share the good news? We are confident because often they readily state: "It is Jehovah who is making me do this." Are they being honest? Yes, because they are continuing to share the message that Jesus sent them out to proclaim—the good news of God's Kingdom. And as they help others learn about this message, they use the Scriptures to teach them. They preach with sincere zeal, and this stems from love for their neighbor. By showing such great appreciation, they demonstrate that they are determined to reach people everywhere with the good news. And as they continue to preach, they strengthen their own faith.
18 We should be encouraged knowing that all of God's servants are united in this work. But what can motivate God's servants to accomplish so much? Consider the example of the apostle Paul when he wrote to the Philippians. He wrote: "I am able to do all things through him who strengthens me." (Phil. 4:13) So let us always strive to remain close to Jehovah in prayer, asking him to give us strength, and let us diligently fulfill the ministry that we have been assigned.—2 Tim. 4:5.

text:
"Navoye na mũĩkĩĩo, ate nzika nongi."
MBATHI: 54, 42
1. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Kaini eka ũtwi mũthũku, na kwaendie ata?
ĨVINDA ĩna ĩvĩtu Kaini aĩ na ũtwi ũũ wa kwĩka: Aĩ no nginya anyuve esumbĩka ũthatu ũla waĩ ngoonĩ, kana eũeka ũsumbĩke meko make. Ĩndĩ ndaĩ aema kũketha ũsyao wa ũtwi ũla wesaa kwĩka o na wĩthĩwe nĩ wĩva. Nĩtwĩsĩ kana ũtwi ũla weekie waĩ ũtwi mũthũku. Ũtwi ũla weekie watumie oaa mwana-a-inyia Aveli, o na kau aĩ mũndũ mũĩkĩĩku. O na ũtwi ũsu nĩwatumie ananga ngwatanĩo yake na Mũmbi wake.—Mwa. 4:3-16.
2. Kwĩka motwi maseo nĩ kwa vata ata?
2 Ve motwi o naitũ twaĩle kwĩka. Ti kĩla ũtwi twĩkaa ũtonya kũtuma twasya thayũ witũ. Ĩndĩ motwi maingĩ twĩkaa nĩmatonya kũvĩndũa maũndũ maitũ vyũ. Na tũkeka motwi maseo no twĩkale o nesa twĩ na mũuo, tũte kũkwatwa nĩ mathĩna maingĩ, kana tũte kũkwatwa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtũtũla ngoo.—Nth. 14:8.
3. (a) Twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo wĩva nĩ kana twĩke motwi maseo? (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva?
3 Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkae motwi maseo? No nginya tũmũĩkĩĩe Ngai na tũitata tũikethĩwe na nzika o na vanini kana we e wendi na ũtonyi wa kũtũtetheesya kwĩka motwi maseo. O na ĩngĩ no nginya twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu Ndetonĩ ya Yeova na nthĩnĩ wa nzĩa yake ya kwĩka maũndũ, na tũyĩkwatasya ũtao wake mũveveee. (Soma Yakovo 1:5-8.) O ũndũ twaendeea kũmũthengeea na kwenda Ndeto yake mũno, now'o tũmanyaa kana we atwendeaa ũseo. Na tweeka ũu, ũkeethĩaa tũtanamba kwĩka ũtwi, twĩamba kwĩkũlya Ndeto yake yĩasya ata. Ĩndĩ tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana twĩkae motwi maseango? Na no nginya tũatĩĩe ũtwi ũla tweeka tũte kũũvĩndũa o na maũndũ mathi ata?
TŨYĨSA KWĨKALA TŨTE KWĨKA MOTWI
4. Nĩ ũtwi wĩva Atamu waĩ no nginya eke, na ũtwi ũla weekie waetie kyaũ?
4 Kuma ĩla andũ moombiwe, methĩĩtwe maikomana na maũndũ maito ũkethĩa no mekaa motwi. Kwa ngelekany'o, Atamu aĩ no nginya atw'e eĩthukĩĩsya Eva kana eĩthukĩĩsya Mũmbi wake. Ĩndĩ we wonaa ata ũtwi ũla weekie? Eekie ũtwi mũthũku mũno nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa woni wa mũka. Kĩu kyatumie asya wĩkalo mũseo mũũndanĩ wa Eteni vamwe na thayũ wake. Na ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mwambĩĩo wa mathĩna. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ ũũ nĩtũthĩnaa mũno nũndũ wa ũtwi ũsu mũthũku wa Atamu.
5. Twaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa kwĩka motwi?
5 Andũ amwe no masye kwĩthĩwa kwĩ kũseo mũnango keka twĩkalaa tũte kwĩka motwi. We nĩwĩthĩawa na woni ta ũsu? Lilikana kana Yeova ndaaũmba andũ mailyĩ masinĩ, matatonya kũsũanĩa na kwĩka motwi. Ũu ti w'o nũndũ o na Mbivilia nĩtũmanyĩasya kwĩka motwi maseo. Kwoou ĩla Yeova ũkũtwĩa kana nĩtwaĩle kwĩka motwi, ethĩawa ayenda kũtũtethya. Kwaekai twone maũndũ amwe meũtũĩkĩĩthya ndeto isu.
6, 7. Aisilaeli ma tene maĩ na ũtwi wĩva wa kwĩka, na nĩkĩ maemiwe nĩ kũwĩka nesa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 13.)
6 Ĩla mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yavikie Nthĩ ya Watho, yaĩ na ũtwi ũũ ũmwe wa vata yaaĩle kwĩka: Yĩthaitha Yeova, kana nĩ ngai ingĩ. (Soma Yosua 24:15.) Ithyĩ tũkakũlw'a twasya ũsu nĩ ũtwi ũte vinya. Ĩndĩ kwĩka ũtwi mũseo ũndũnĩ ũsu kwesaa kũtuma makwata thayũ, na kwĩka ũtwi mũthũku kwesaa kũmaetee kĩkw'ũ. O na mesĩ oou, ĩvindanĩ ya Asili matindĩaa kwĩka motwi mathũku. Mamũtiaa Yeova na mayambĩĩa kũthaitha ngai sya ũvũngũ. (Asi. 2:3, 11-23) Kwasyoka ũsũanĩe ĩvinda yĩngĩ andũ asu ma Ngai maĩ na ũtwi wa kwĩka. Mwathani Eliya amanengie maũndũ aa elĩ manyuve ũmwe: Kũmũthũkũma Yeova kana kũthũkũma Mbaali. (1 Asu. 18:21) Eliya nĩwamakanisye nũndũ wa kũemwa nĩ kwĩka ũtwi. No wasye ũsu waĩ ũtwi wĩ laisi nũndũ kĩla ĩvinda kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩkũtũunaa. Kana no wasye vai mũndũ ũkũsũanĩa nesa ũtonya kwendeew'a nĩ Mbaali, kana ũtonya kũmĩthaitha. Ĩndĩ Aisilaeli asu 'maendaa makĩthua katĩ wa ngalĩ ilĩ.' Ĩndĩ Eliya amekĩie vinya meke ũtwi wa ũĩ. Ameie nĩmanyuve kũmũthaitha Yeova, nũndũ ũsu nĩw'o ũthaithi ũla waĩlĩte vyũ.
7 Nĩkĩ Aisilaeli asu maemetwe nĩ kwĩka ũtwi mũseo? Mbee vyũ, mũĩkĩĩo woo vala ve Yeova waĩ ũnonza vyũ na makaeka kũmwĩthukĩĩsya. Na mayemanyĩĩtye mũno ĩũlũ wa Yeova na ĩũlũ wa ũĩ ũla wumaa kwake, o na mayamwĩkwatasya. Keka nĩmoosete ũmanyi wa w'o na makaũatĩĩa, methĩwa meekaa motwi maseo. (Sav. 25:12) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana nĩmeetĩkĩlile kwaw'a nĩ andũ angĩ na kwĩkĩwa motwi nĩ andũ angĩ. Andũ ala maĩ nthĩ ĩsu ya watho mayaĩ athaithi ma Yeova, na kwoou nĩmatumie mambĩĩa kũsũanĩa o tamo, na kyu kyatuma mambĩĩa kwĩka o tamo. Kuma tene Yeova nĩwamakanĩtye akamea ũndũ ta ũsu nũtonya kwĩkĩka.—Kuma 23:2.
MO ANDŨ ANGĨ NĨMAĨLE KŨTWĨKĨA MOTWI?
8. Nĩ ĩsomo yĩva ya vata ĩũlũ wa kwĩka ũtwi tũkwĩmanyĩsya twasisya ũndũ Aisilaeli meekie?
8 Ngelekany'o isu syawetwa vau ĩũlũ syatũmanyĩsya ũndũ mũna wa vata. Nĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩla ũmwe witũ eyĩkĩe motwi. Na mũndũ enda kwĩka motwi maseo na maĩlĩte, no nginya atũmĩe ũmanyi wa Maandĩko. Ĩandĩko ya Akalatia 6:5 yĩtũlilikanasya ũũ: "Kĩla mũndũ akakua mũio wake mwene." Ũu nĩ kwasya kana tũyaĩlĩte kũkuĩthya mũndũ ũngĩ mũio witũ wa kwĩka motwi. Vandũ va ũu, kĩla ũmwe nĩwaĩle kwĩmanyĩsya kĩla Ngai wonaa kĩ kĩseo na aikĩka.
9. Nĩkĩ nĩ mũisyo mũnene mũno kũeka angĩ matwĩkĩe motwi?
9 Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma mũndũ aeka angĩ mamwĩkĩe motwi? Mũndũ nũtonya kũkusw'a nĩ andũ angĩ nginya akesa kwĩka ũtwi ũte mũseo. (Nth. 1:10, 15) Ĩndĩ o na tũkathing'ĩĩw'a mũno ata nĩ andũ angĩ, ithyĩ ene twaĩle kũatĩĩa wasya witũ wa ngoo ũla ũmanyĩĩtw'e nĩ Mbivilia. Mavinda maingĩ kũeka angĩ matwĩkĩe motwi no ta ũndũ ũmwe na kwĩtĩkĩla 'kũendany'a namo,' kana kũmaatĩĩa. Tweeka ũu twĩthĩwa o tweeka ũtwi, ĩndĩ ũtonya kũtũlikya thĩnanĩ mũnene mũno.
10. Vaulo akanisye Akalatia ĩũlũ wa ũndũ wĩva?
10 Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwaandĩkĩie Akalatia amatavya ũthũku wa kũeka angĩ mamekĩe motwi. (Soma Akalatia 4:17.) Ana-a-asa amwe kĩkundinĩ kĩu mendaa kwĩkĩa ala angĩ motwi nĩ kana mamakusye maeke kũatĩĩa atũmwa. Nĩkĩ meekaa ũu? Kĩtumi kĩmwe nĩ kana meemanthĩaa nguma. Mayaĩ na wĩnyivyo na mayanengete ndaĩa ũthasyo ũla ana-a-asa ala angĩ maĩ naw'o wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi nemo ene.
11. Tũtonya kũtetheesya angĩ ata ĩla mekwĩka motwi?
11 Vaulo aĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ũndũnĩ ũsu wa kũnenga ndaĩa ũthasyo wa ana-a-asa wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi. (2 Akolintho 1:24.) Ũmũnthĩ ĩla atumĩa mekũnenga ana-a-asa motao ĩũlũ wa ũtwi mũna mekwenda kwĩka, nĩmaĩle kũatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ĩsu. Nĩmatanaa mũno kũneenea motao maumĩte Mbivilianĩ vamwe na ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ. Ĩndĩ o na mayĩka ũu, methĩawa me metho maikalikĩlĩĩle ũthasyo ũla ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa me naw'o wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi. Na ũu nĩw'o waĩle nũndũ ethĩwa ve thĩna ũkaumĩla ĩtina, ũkakwata ana-a-asa asu kana eĩtu-a-asa na ti atumĩa asu. Ũndũ ũla wa vata tũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩ atĩĩ: No tũtetheesye ala angĩ, na tũimony'a myolooto ya Maandĩko na motao ala maĩlĩte. Ĩndĩ nĩmo me na kĩanda kya kwĩyĩkĩa motwi. Meeka ũtwi ũla waĩlĩte, nĩmakwataa moathimo. Kwa w'o, tũyaĩle kwĩsa kũsũanĩa atĩ twĩ na mwanya wa kwĩkĩa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa motwi.
NDŨKETĨKĨLE NGOO YAKŨ ĨŨTONGOESYE KWĨKA MOTWI
12, 13. Nĩkĩ ti ũseo kwĩka ũtwi ĩla tũthatĩte kana ĩla tũkw'ĩte ngoo?
12 Andũ nĩmakothaa kũtũmĩa kyuo kĩĩ: Ĩka kĩla ngoo yaku ĩkwenda. Ĩndĩ kwĩka ũu nĩkũtonya kũlikya mũndũ thĩnanĩ. O na no twasye mũndũ akeka ũu ethĩwa athi ũtee na Maandĩko. Mbivilia nĩtũkanĩtye ĩkatũtavya tũiketĩkĩle kwĩka ũtwi tũatĩĩe ngoo sitũ nũndũ twĩ andũ me na naĩ. (Nth. 28:26) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ve ngewa syĩ Mbivilianĩ syonanĩtye andũ makwatiwe nĩ maũndũ mathũku nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa ngoo syoo. Thĩna ũla mũnene wa kũatĩĩa ngoo nĩ kana twĩ andũ me na naĩ, na kwoou ngoo sitũ "nĩ ngengani kũvĩtũka syĩndũ syonthe, na nĩ nthũku ki." (Yel. 3:17; 13:10; 17:9; 1 Asu. 11:9) Kwoou maũndũ mekala ata tũketĩkĩla kũtongoew'a nĩ ngoo sitũ?
13 Ngoo ya Mũklĩsto nĩ ya vata nũndũ nĩtũnengetwe mwĩao wa kũmwenda Yeova na ngoo yitũ yonthe na tũimwenda mũtũi o tondũ twĩyendete. (Mt. 22:37-39) Ĩndĩ maandĩko ala mekĩĩtwe kalungunĩ ka 12 nĩmoonany'a mũisyo ũla ũtonya kumĩla ethĩwa tũkeekaa motwi tũtongoew'e nĩ ngoo sitũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kumĩla ũkeka ũtwi ĩla ũthatĩte? Ethĩwa waaĩka ũu nĩwĩsĩ ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu. (Nth. 14:17; 29:22) Kwasũanĩa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ yĩngĩ: We nũkwona mũndũ ta wĩka ũtwi mũseo ĩla ũkw'ĩte ngoo? (Mot. 32:6-12; Nth. 24:10) Ĩkalaa ũlilikene kana Ndeto ya Ngai nĩtwonetye kana 'kũthũkũma ĩla mĩao ya Ngai' nĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ. (Alo. 7:25) Vate nzika, tũkaeka ngoo sitũ itũsumbĩke ĩla tũkwĩka motwi maito no tũkengeke mũno.
NĨ ĨNDĨĨ ŨTONYA KŨVĨNDŨA ŨTWI WAKU?
14. Twĩsĩ ata kana ti ũthũku kũvĩndũa motwi amwe?
14 Twĩ na vata wa kwĩka motwi maseo. Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana tũyaĩle kũsenzya ũtwi twamina kũwĩka. Ve mavinda ũtonya kwĩthĩa nũseo tũkasũanĩa ĩngĩ ũtwi tũminĩte kũwĩka, na vatonyeka tũyĩũvĩndũa. Kwasisya ũndũ Yeova weekanie na andũ ma Nineva ĩvinda ya Yona. Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Na Ngai oona mawĩa moo, kana nĩmeethyũũie kuma mũendelenĩ woo mũthũku; na Ngai eetũnga aeka ũthũku ũla waĩtye akameka; na ndaawĩka." (Yona 3:10) Ĩla Yeova woonie kana andũ ma Nineva nĩmeelila na methyũũa, nĩwavĩndũie ũtwi wake. Kwĩka ũu kwoonanisye kana nĩwĩnyivĩtye, e tei, na ndomaa vamwe ĩla weeka ũtwi. O na ĩngĩ, Ngai ndatusaa ũndũ ũkwĩka asukumĩtwe nĩ ũthilĩku wa kavinda o tondũ andũ aingĩ mekaa.
15. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũvĩndũa ũtwi witũ?
15 Ve mavinda tũtonya kwĩthĩa nũseo tũkasũanĩa ĩngĩ ũtwi mũna twĩkĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, no twĩke ũu ĩla maũndũ maitũ mavĩndũka. O nake Yeova ve mavinda wavĩndũie ũtwi wake ĩla woonie maũndũ mavĩndũka. (1 Asu. 21:20, 21, 27-29; 2 Asu. 20:1-5) O na ĩngĩ nĩtũtonya kũkwata ũvoo tũteĩ naw'o na tũyĩthĩa nĩtwaĩle kũvĩndũa ũtwi witũ. Ngelekany'o ĩmwe ya ũndũ ũsu nĩ ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti. Ve ĩvinda wataviw'e ũvoo ũte wa w'o ĩũlũ wa mwĩsũkũũe wa Saulo weetawa Mevivosethi. Ĩndĩ ĩla Ndaviti wesie kũmanya ũw'o nesa, nĩwavĩndũie ũtwi wake. (2 Sam. 16:3, 4; 19:24-29) Nĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ o naitũ tũkekaa ũu mavinda amwe.
16. (a) Nĩ maũndũ amwe meva matonya kũtũtethya twĩke ũtwi mũseo? (b) Nĩkĩ mavinda amwe twaĩle kũsũanĩa ĩngĩ ũtwi mũna twĩkĩte, na twaĩle kwĩka ata twamina kũsũanĩa?
16 Ndeto ya Ngai nĩtũtaĩte ĩkatwĩa tũikasembee kwĩka ũtwi ĩla twakomana na ũndũ mũito. (Nth. 21:5) Ĩla twoosa ĩvinda tũosye nesa maũndũ onthe ala makonanĩtye na ũndũ ũla twĩ naw'o, nĩ laisi mũno tũkeka ũtwi mũseo. (1 Ath. 5:21) Mwene mũsyĩ nĩwaĩle kũmantha ĩvinda akeka ũkunĩkĩli Maandĩkonĩ na mavukunĩ maitũ atanamba kwĩka ũtwi mũna. O na nĩwaĩle kwĩthukĩĩsya mawoni ma ala angĩ vau mũsyĩ. Lilikana kana Ngai eeie Avalaamu nĩethukĩĩsye wasya wa mũka. (Mwa. 21:9-12) Atumĩa o namo nĩmaĩle kũmantha ĩvinda ya kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli. Na mavinda amwe nĩmatonya kũkwata ũvoo mateĩ naw'o ũkonetye ũtwi meĩ maneeka. Vekala ũu, ethĩwa mo nĩ andũ menyivĩtye na matomaa vamwe, maikaleaa kũvĩndũa ũtwi ũsu maikĩa kwasya ndaĩa yoo. Maĩle kwĩthĩwa meyũmbanĩtye kwona maũndũ kwa nzĩa ĩngĩ, na kũvĩndũa motwi amwe mekĩte ĩla makwata kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩka ũu. Nũseo o naitũ tũkaatĩĩa ngelekany'o yoo ũndũnĩ ũsu. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtumaa kĩkundi kĩkala na mũuo na kĩte na kĩthokoany'o.—Meko 6:1-4.
ĨKA KĨLA WATW'A
17. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩke motwi maseo?
17 Motwi amwe methĩawa me maito kwĩ angĩ. Motwi ala maito nĩmendaa mũndũ avoye na aimasũanĩa mũno, na ũu no ũkue ĩvinda. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũtwi ũmwe mũito Aklĩsto amwe makomanaa naw'o nĩ kũnyuva ethĩwa nĩmeũtwaana kana maitwaana, na ethĩwa nĩmeũtwaana, nũũ ũla meũtwaa. Na ũtwi ũngĩ mũito na ũtonya kũetee mũndũ moathimo maingĩ nĩ kũtw'a esakũa ũthũkũmi wĩva wa ĩvinda yonthe na eĩka ũu ĩndĩĩ. Ĩla tũkwĩka motwi ta asu nũseo tũkaĩkĩĩa vyũ kana Yeova nĩwe ũtonya kũtũnenga ũtao ũla mũseo. (Nth. 1:5) Kwoou nĩ ũndũ wa vata mavindanĩ ta asu tũkasoma Mbivilia nũndũ nĩyo ĩtonya kũtũnenga ũtao ũla mũseo vyũ na tũimũvoya Yeova atũtetheesye. O na ĩngĩ, tũyaĩle kũlwa kana Yeova nũtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na nguma itonya kũtuma twĩka motwi mosanĩte na kwenda kwake. Kwoou ĩla wĩ na motwi ma vata waĩle kwĩka, ĩkũlasye makũlyo ta aa: 'W'o ũtwi ũla ngwĩka nũkwonany'a kana nĩnĩmwendete Yeova? Nũũtuma mũsyĩ witũ wĩthĩwa na ũtanu na mũuo? Na nũkwonany'a kana nĩ wũmĩĩsyo na tei?'
18. Nĩkĩ Yeova wendaa twĩyĩkĩe motwi ne ithyĩ ene?
18 Yeova ndatũlasimĩthasya tũmwende kana tũmũthũkũme. Ũsu nĩ ũtwi twaĩle kwĩyĩkĩa ithyĩ ene. Nũndũ nũtũnengete ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa, we nũnengae ndaĩa kĩanda kĩla twĩ nakyo kya 'kwĩnyuvĩa' ithyĩ ene ethĩwa nĩtũũmũthũkũma kana tũimũthũkũma. (Yos. 24:15; Mũta. 5:4) Ĩndĩ we nĩwendaa twĩanĩsye motwi ala tweeka tũtongoew'e nĩ Ndeto yake. Tweethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo nthĩnĩ wa nzĩa ya Yeova ya kwĩka maũndũ na twaĩkĩĩa myolooto ĩla ũtũnete, tũkeekaa motwi maseo. Kĩu kĩkoonanasya twĩ alũmu nzĩanĩ sitũ syonthe.—Yak. 1:5-8; 4:8.
