translation:
"I am satisfied with little, but righteousness is better."
MBATHI: 54, 42
1. Is this why Cain was very angry, and why his countenance fell?
IVINDA had several reasons why Cain was angry and his face fell: He was jealous because Abel's sacrifice was more acceptable than his, or he thought his sacrifice was rejected. But there was another reason—he was influenced by Satan who made him believe God was unjust. We can see from this that jealousy can lead to anger. The person who became like Cain was a son of the serpent Abel, and he did not love his brother. And this man used his envy to fight against his Creator.—Gen. 4:3-16.
2. Why should we listen carefully?
2 We listen so that we may learn. It is not always easy to listen, because sometimes we want to say our own things. But often we find it easier to understand others when we listen to them. And if we listen carefully, we will be happier and more peaceful, and we will avoid many problems, or we will avoid difficult situations.—Prov. 14:8.
3. (a) How can we be affected by jealousy, and how does listening carefully help us? (b) What benefits do we gain?
3 Is it possible for jealousy to affect us negatively? Yes, we can ask God for help and pray that he strengthen us to deal with feelings of envy and bitterness, or we can try to overcome the temptation to become jealous. And also we are helped by learning about Jehovah's organization and the principles of listening to others, and we imitate his example perfectly. (Read James 1:5-8.) And the more we strive to please him and walk in his direction, the more we realize that he cares for us. And if we do this, we will continue to improve in listening, and we will enjoy following his advice greatly. But can we ever listen too much? And can we ever ignore what we hear and disregard important things?—
LET US CONTINUE TO IMPROVE IN LISTENING
4. What question did Adam ask, and what answer did he receive?
4 Many people today, especially young ones, find it difficult to listen to advice. For instance, Adam was tempted by Eve or tempted by his Creator. Did he listen to anyone? He listened to his wife, which led to disastrous consequences for himself and for all mankind. And that is why it is an example for us to learn from Adam's mistake.
5. How can we be helped to listen better?
5 Some people may struggle to listen because they think it means being weak. Are you struggling with this? Remember that Jehovah created humans imperfect, prone to making mistakes and getting envious. This is why the Bible teaches us how to listen to others. Know that Jehovah wants us to succeed in listening, and he promises to help us. Consider some examples that show how we can apply what we have learned.
6, 7. The Israelites had a problem with listening, and what were the results? (See footnote 13.)
6 But the people of Israel turned to the God of Worth, yet they listened with only one ear: Choose Jehovah, or another god. (Read Joshua 24:15.) Today we can show our loyalty with one ear. It is important to listen carefully to advice that will help us make good decisions, and to listen carelessly to advice that will lead us astray. And indeed, the account of Elijah shows how important it is to listen carefully. They provoked Jehovah and boasted about choosing the gods of the nations. (Acts 2:3, 11-23) Because of this, many people turned away from the God of their forefathers with one ear. Elijah challenged the people to a contest: To honor Jehovah or to honor Baal. (1 Kings 18:21) Elijah showed his faith by listening carefully. He knew that if he honored Jehovah, it would be successful. Or he knew that anyone who tried to please Baal would fail. Indeed, the Israelites were "walking between two opinions." Indeed, Elijah proved his loyalty with one ear. He firmly chose to honor Jehovah, and that choice brought success.
7 Did the Israelites really listen carefully? Yes, because Jehovah saw their indecision and was moved to pity them. And he reminded them of his covenant and his promise to bless them, and he encouraged them. So let us examine ourselves and see if we are listening carefully. (Proverbs 25:12) Sometimes we may feel pressured by others and listen carelessly to others. These people do not fear the God of Worth, and often they try to influence others to turn aside, and sometimes they succeed in influencing others to turn aside. Remember that Jehovah sees what we choose and knows whether we are able to listen carefully.—Psalm 23:2.
WHAT IF OTHERS TRY TO MAKE US LISTEN CARELESSLY?
8. What lesson from the past should motivate us to listen carefully?
8 Consider how important it is to be motivated to listen carefully. It is each one of us who listens carelessly. And if someone listens carelessly and does wrong, then let him use the knowledge of the Scriptures. Colossians 6:5 reminds us: "Each man will carry his own load." This means that we should not try to excuse another person's carelessness. Instead, each one should be motivated to please God and listen carefully.
9. Why is this an important quality to cultivate?
9 Is there something that can cause a person to make others listen carelessly? A person can be influenced by others so that he stops listening carefully. (Proverbs 1:10, 15) But even if others influence us, we must always remember our personal responsibility to learn from the Bible. Many reasons why others make others listen carelessly are pride and stubbornness. Let us avoid this by being careful and avoiding becoming careless.
10. What did Paul advise the Corinthians about this matter?
10 The apostle Paul wrote to the Corinthians about the importance of making others listen carefully. (Read 1 Corinthians 4:17.) He encouraged them to appoint mature men who could help others listen carefully and correct those who were doing wrong. Why did he do this? One reason is that they believed lies. Also, their thoughts and words were causing harm to others.
11. How can we motivate others to listen carefully?
11 Paul wisely used encouragement when helping people to listen carefully. (2 Corinthians 1:24.) When someone uses encouragement to help others listen carefully, it is more likely that they will respond positively. It is important to imitate the good examples of our brothers and sisters. If you see this happening, praise them for helping others listen carefully and for correcting them. This will strengthen their resolve to continue helping others and correcting them. We should remember this principle: Let us encourage one another, and let us pay attention to the teachings of the Scriptures and to good examples. This will help us to improve our ability to help others listen carefully. By doing so, we will show that we value the opportunity to help others and correct them.
LET US BE THANKFUL FOR THE PRIVILEGE OF HELPING OTHERS LISTEN
12, 13. What if we try to help someone listen carefully, but they refuse to accept our counsel?
12 Many people have expressed this concern: 'My efforts seem to be in vain.' Trying to help someone can be frustrating. But we should not give up on a person just because he does not want to listen to Bible principles. The Bible encourages us to keep trying to help others listen carefully, even if it seems difficult. (Prov. 28:26) Sometimes, our brothers may encounter individuals who are deeply troubled and unwilling to accept counsel. In such cases, we can still offer encouragement, saying, "I am concerned about you, and I know this is troubling." (Jer. 3:17; 13:10; 17:9; 1 Thess. 11:9) What can we do to remain motivated to help others listen carefully?
13 A Christian's love is demonstrated by his desire to please Jehovah and to use his whole heart in serving Him faithfully. (Matt. 22:37-39) So, the scriptures at 1 Corinthians 12 remind us of the importance of listening carefully so that we can benefit from what we hear. For example, how can we show that we are eager to listen? By giving attention to those speaking to us. This shows respect. (Prov. 14:17; 29:22) Consider these questions: Would you want someone to listen when you share your thoughts? (Deut. 32:6-12; Prov. 24:10) It is vital that we remember that upholding 'God's standards' is important. (Acts 7:25) Therefore, let us strive to listen attentively so that we can apply what we learn and continue to grow spiritually.
HOW CAN YOU IMPROVE YOUR LISTENING SKILLS?
14. Is there something you could personally work on to become a better listener?
14 We all have opportunities to improve our listening skills. It is not always easy to concentrate while others are speaking. However, we can make an effort to focus more intently on what they are saying, and then we will be able to respond appropriately. Remember how Jehovah dealt with the people of Nineveh through Jonah. The Bible says: "And God saw their works, that they had turned back from their evil way; and God felt regret over the calamity that He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it." (Jonah 3:10) Because Jehovah saw that the people of Nineveh had repented and were sincere, he listened to their plea. Showing consideration like this is pleasing to him, and it encourages others to speak openly. Moreover, God wants us to be considerate because many people are troubled.
15. What can help us to become better listeners?
15 We can make an effort to focus more intently when others are speaking. For example, we should listen when problems trouble us. Just as Jehovah listened to his people when they faced difficulties. (1 Sam. 21:20, 21, 27-29; 2 Sam. 20:1-5) Also, we can try to identify ourselves with those who are speaking and show genuine interest in what they are saying. An excellent example of this is David's reaction to Shimei's abusive words during Absalom's revolt against King Saul, which was called Mephibosheth. Although David knew Shimei's accusations were unjust, he showed consideration. (2 Sam. 16:3, 4; 19:24-29) This is something we can all strive for.
16. (a) What are some things that can distract us when we try to listen carefully? (b) What can we do to focus more intently when others are speaking, and what if we find it difficult to concentrate?
16 God's Word urges us to be quick to listen and slow to speak when dealing with important matters. (Jas. 1:19) If we value our relationship with Jehovah, we will make an effort to give careful attention to what others say, especially when it involves spiritual matters. (1 Thess. 5:21) However, sometimes it may be hard to concentrate. Perhaps we are preoccupied with worries or concerns. Or we may simply feel tired. Remember how Abraham listened to Sarah, despite her being unreasonable at times. (Gen. 21:9-12) It is often possible to improve our listening skills. But there are times when distractions are unavoidable—perhaps because of noise or interruptions from others—and it becomes difficult to focus. In such cases, we might try to view the situation from another perspective and concentrate on just one aspect of what is being said. Then we can later discuss the matter further. By doing so, we demonstrate respect for others and maintain unity within the congregation.—Acts 6:1-4.
BE A GOOD LISTENER
17. What can help us to become better listeners?
17 One way is to practice active listening. Active listeners give the speaker their full attention and show genuine interest, and this makes the speaker feel valued. For example, when a fellow Christian mentions something he is struggling with, we may respond with empathy and encouragement, and our words can be comforting. Also, another way to listen attentively is to try to understand what the speaker is saying and how he feels, and then share his feelings. And when we listen carefully and show sincere concern, we demonstrate that we care about him and his problems. But let us remember that we can only truly benefit if we apply what we learn from Jehovah and allow him to guide us. (Prov. 1:5) This is why it is important for us to read the Bible regularly so that we can learn from it and appreciate how much Jehovah loves us. Moreover, we should pray to Jehovah asking him to help us to become better listeners and to use our ears to hear his direction. This will help us to be more considerate and responsive to his guidance. So if you find yourself having difficulty listening, ask yourself questions like: "Am I really trying my best to understand what Jehovah wants me to know? Am I letting my emotions and prejudices affect my judgment? And am I being humble?"
18. How can Jehovah help us to be good listeners?
18 Jehovah empowers us to listen and to make choices. It is up to us to decide whether we will pay attention. However, if we want to improve, we need to take deliberate steps. We must strive to grasp the meaning of what is said, rather than simply hearing the words. (Josh. 24:15; Matt. 5:4) Furthermore, we must endeavor to align our thinking with God's thoughts. By meditating on Jehovah's standards and appreciating the wisdom they contain, we can train ourselves to be good listeners. Doing so will bring us closer to Jehovah.—Jas. 1:5-8; 4:8.

text:
"Maũndũ asu nĩwamavithie andũ oĩ na ala me na ũmanyi, na wavuanĩsye twana tũnini."
1. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie Yesũ "atana nthĩnĩ wa Veva Mũtheu"? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
KWA kũna visa Yesũ Klĩsto 'atanĩte nthĩnĩ wa veva mũtheu.' No kwĩthĩwa wasũanĩa aitheka na metho make mayonany'a ũtanu ũla waĩ naw'o. Kyo nĩ kyaũ kyatumie ethĩwa na ũtanu ũsu? Eethĩĩtwe atũmĩte amanyĩw'a 70 katĩ wa ala waĩ namo mathi makatavany'e ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Aimatũma nĩwendaa kwĩsa kwona ũndũ mekwĩanĩsya wĩa ũsu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu kwaĩ na amaitha aingĩ na me vinya ma ũvoo mũseo. Amwe mamo maĩ aandĩki na Avalisi na maĩ asomu mũno na maĩ maũĩ. Nĩmatumie andũ aingĩ mavũthya Yesũ nũndũ mamwonaa e o vundi wa mbwaũ. O na nĩmavũthĩtye amanyĩw'a make nũndũ mamonaa ta andũ "matamanyĩĩtw'e, na mate na ũmanyi." (Meko 4:13; Mko. 6:3) Ĩndĩ amanyĩw'a asu masyokie me atanu mũno. Nĩmatavanĩtye o na kau mavĩngĩtwe nginya makavĩngwa nĩ ndaimoni! Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie methĩwa me atanu na me na ũkũmbaũ?—Soma Luka 10:1, 17-21.
2. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa syĩva amanyĩw'a ma Yesũ mailyĩ ta syana? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye aatĩĩi ma Klĩsto makwatye ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ?
2 Yesũ atavisye Yeova atĩĩ: "Nĩngũũtũngĩa mũvea, we Asa, Mwĩaĩi wa ĩtu na nthĩ, nĩkwĩthĩwa maũndũ asu nĩwamavithie ala me na ũĩ na ũmanyi, na watũvuanisye twana: ĩĩ, Asa, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩw'o wendeesye kwaku." (Mt. 11:25, 26) Ũu ti kwasya kana Yesũ oonanasya amanyĩw'a make maĩ o syana. Vandũ va ũu nĩweesĩ kana moonekaa mailyĩ syana maelekanw'a na andũ ala maĩ na ũmanyi na asomu na meeyonaa me oĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ o na eka kyu, Yesũ nĩweeĩte amanyĩw'a make methĩwe andũ menyivĩtye na matonya kũmanyĩw'a ta syana nini. (Mt. 18:1-4) Matethekie ata nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa menyivĩtye? Yeova nĩwamatetheeisye na veva mũtheu nĩ kana maelewe ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, namo ala meeyonaa me oĩ na mamathekeeaa matiiwe kĩvindunĩ nũndũ wa ngũlũ syoo, na nũndũ matongoew'e nĩ Satani.
3. Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Kwoou tũyaĩle kũsaanĩw'a ĩla twasoma kana Yesũ aĩ mũtanu. Eewie mũyo nũndũ wa kwona ũndũ Yeova wavuanisye momanyĩsyo maito ma Mbivilia kwa andũ ma mĩthemba yonthe ala maĩ na wĩnyivyo, ateũsisya kĩsomo kyoo kana inengo syoo. Nĩweewie mũyo nũndũ Ĩthe wake nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ nzĩa ĩsu ya kũmanyĩsya. We Yeova nĩwaalyũkile, na onanasya ata kana o na yu nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ nzĩa ĩsu ya kũmanyĩsya? Ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo asu nũtonya kũtuma o naitũ tũtana o tondũ Yesũ watanie.
KŨTETHEESYA KĨLA MŨNDŨ AELEWE NĨ MOMANYĨSYO MAITO
4. Nĩ kwa nzĩa syĩva ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya yĩla yĩ na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi yĩthĩĩtwe yĩilyĩ ta mũthĩnzĩo?
4 Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ ũseũvyo wa Yeova wĩthĩĩtwe ũitũmanyĩsya mũno mũno kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi na ĩkũeleeka. Kwasũanĩa maũndũ aa atatũ. Ũndũ wa mbee nĩ kwambĩĩa kũtumbĩthw'a kwa ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya yĩ na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi. * Ĩkaseti yĩu yĩthĩĩtwe ta mũthĩnzĩo kwa ala matesĩ kĩthyomo kĩna nesa na ala matesĩ kũkĩsoma nesa. Andũ ala me mĩsyĩ nĩmesĩte kwĩthĩa kana syana syoo nieleawa ĩkaseti yĩu nesa. Na ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno nũndũ ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya nĩyo nzĩa ĩla nene ya kũtũĩthya kĩ-veva. O na aingĩ nĩmaandĩkĩte valũa maitũnga mũvea kuma ngoonĩ nũndũ wa ĩkaseti yĩu yĩ na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe aandĩkie kana we nĩwaemawa nĩ kumya maelesyo ĩvinda ya Ĩsomo ya Mũsyaĩĩsya. Aisye, "Nekalaa vau o ta ĩvisa." Ĩndĩ yu ti ta tene! Ĩla wambĩĩe kũsoma ĩkaseti yĩla yĩ na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi aandĩkie ũũ: "Yu nĩnumasya maelesyo mavinda maingĩ, o na ndyĩw'aa ndikĩa! Nĩngũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea vamwe nenyu."
5. Nĩ moseo amwe meva me nthĩnĩ wa Biblia Takatifu—Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya ĩla yĩkĩtwe moalyũku?
5 Ũndũ wa kelĩ nĩ kumĩthw'a kwa Biblia Takatifu—Tafsiri ya Ulimwengu Mpya kwa kĩthyomo kya Kĩsũngũ. Mbivilia ĩsu yĩkĩtwe moalyũku yaumiw'e Matukũ 5, Mwei wa 10, 2013. * Maandĩko maingĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩsu me na ndeto nini ĩndĩ nieleetye maũndũ nesa na kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩandĩko ya Yovu 10:1 tene yĩnaĩ na ndeto 27 ĩndĩ yu yĩnatheeie nginya ndeto 19, nayo ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 8:6 yĩnaĩ na ndeto 20 ĩndĩ yu yĩnatheeie nginya ndeto 13. Mĩsoa ĩsu yelĩ nĩeleekaa nesanga Mbivilianĩ ĩsu nzaũ. O na mwana-a-asa ũmwe mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta wĩthĩĩtwe e mũĩkĩĩku kwa myaka mingĩ anaisye ũũ: "Nĩnasomie ĩvuku ya Yovu Mbivilianĩ ĩla nzaũ na nĩneew'a ta ĩndĩ nayĩelewa ĩvinda ya mbee!" Andũ aingĩ nĩmaĩtye take.
6. We wĩw'aa ata nũndũ wa kũelewa nesanga ĩandĩko ya Mathayo 24:45-47?
6 Ũndũ wa katatũ, kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũmanyi witũ ũendeee kũkenũka. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtwatanie mũno ĩla ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/07/2013 yatũeleisye nesanga ĩũlũ wa ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ." (Mt. 24:45-47) Ĩkaseti yĩu yaeleisye kana ngombo yĩ na kĩthito nĩyo Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye, namo ala ma "nyũmba [ya vwana]" nĩ onthe ala maĩthaw'a kĩ-veva, methĩwe nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta kana nĩ "malondu angĩ." (Yoa. 10:16) Twĩw'aa mũyo ta kĩ ĩla twamanyĩw'a maũndũ ta asu na twasyoka twamamanyĩsya ala eũ! Ve maũndũ angĩ mekwonany'a kana Yeova nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ nzĩa ya kũmanyĩsya ĩla yĩ laisi na ĩkũeleeka?
KŨELESYA NGEWA SYA MBIVILIA KWA NZĨA YĨ LAISI NA ĨKŨELEEKA
7, 8. Nengane ngelekany'o sya ngewa imwe syĩ Mbivilianĩ itonya kũelew'a ta wathani.
7 Ethwa wĩthĩĩtwe ũimũthũkũma Yeova kwa myaka mingĩ, no kwĩthwa wonete ũndũ kũendeee kwĩthĩwa na ũalyũku ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mavuku maitũ maeleasya ngewa mbingĩ ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ. Ũalyũku wĩva? Navu ĩtina mavuku maitũ moosaa ngewa yĩ Mbivilianĩ makamĩsianĩsya na ũndũ mũna wesie kwĩkĩka kana ũkesa kwĩkĩka na maisisya ũndũ ngewa ĩsu na ũndũ ũsu syosanĩte. Ngewa ĩsu ya Mbivilia yatalawa tayo kyuu kana wathani, naw'o ũndũ ũsu ũitalwa taw'o kĩla kya w'o. Mo Maandĩko nĩmatũnengete kĩtumi kya kũelesya ngewa sya Mbivilia kwa nzĩa ĩsu? Ĩĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa "kyama kya mwathani Yona." (Soma Mathayo 12:39, 40.) Aeleisye kana ngewa ya Yona ĩla waĩ ĩvunĩ ya ĩkũyũ yaĩ wathani wa ũndũ we mwene ũkekala mbũanĩ, o ũndũ yĩla ĩvu ya ĩkũyũ yĩthĩwa yatw'ĩkie mbũa ya Yona ta keka Yeova ndaamũsũvĩa ndakakw'e.
8 Mbivilia yĩ na ngewa ingĩ mbeveee itonya kũelew'a ta wathani. Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwawetie imwe syasyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũamba ũla waĩ vo katĩ wa Avalaamu, Akali, na Sala no ũelew'e ta wathani ũkwonany'a mũamba ũla waĩ vo katĩ wa Yeova na mbaĩ ya Isilaeli, na ũla wĩ vo yu katĩ wa Yeova na kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wake kya ĩtunĩ. (Aka. 4:22-26) O ta ũu, maũndũ ta yĩla ĩeema na ĩkalũ, Mũthenya wa Wĩw'anĩthyo, mũthembi mũnene, na maũndũ angĩ makonetye ĩla Mĩao ya Mose maĩ "kyuu kya syĩndũ nzeo ila ikoka." (Aevl. 9:23-25; 10:1) Ĩla tweemanyĩsya ngewa ta isu sya Mbivilia, nĩtwĩw'aa twaakwa mũĩkĩĩo na tũisyenda mũno. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ kwasya kana kĩla mũndũ ũwetetwe Mbivilianĩ, kana o kĩndũ o na kĩva kĩwetetwe vamwe na maũndũ onthe ala maaĩkĩka, nĩ wathani ũkonetye mũndũ mũna kana kĩndũ kĩna?
9. Tene mavuku maitũ maeleasya ata ngewa ya Navothi?
9 Tene ũu nĩw'o mavuku maitũ makothaa kũelesya ngewa sya Mbivilia. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Navothi. Yeseveli, ũla waĩ mũka wa Mũsumbĩ Aavu na mũndũ mũka mwathe, nĩweekie mĩvango Navothi asikatwe mana na ayũawa vate kĩtumi nĩ kana mũũme ose mũũnda wake wa mĩsavivũ. (1 Asu. 21:1-16) Mwakanĩ wa 1932, ngewa ĩsu ya Navothi yaeleiw'e ta wathani. Kwatw'ĩkie Aavu na Yeseveli maelekanĩtye Satani na ũseũvyo wake, nake Navothi aelekanasya Yesũ, na ĩndĩ nakyo kĩkw'ũ kya Navothi kyaĩ wonany'o wa kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa myaka ĩana ũndũ mũna, ĩvuku "Let Your Name Be Sanctified," yĩla yaumĩthiw'e mwaka wa 1961, yaelekanilye Navothi na etĩkĩw'a mauta, na yaelekany'a Yeseveli na ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto. Kwoou kwosana na ĩvuku yĩu, kũthĩnw'a kwa Navothi nĩ Yeseveli kwaelekanilw'e na kũthĩnw'a kwa etĩkĩw'a mauta mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo. Kwa myaka mingĩ andũ ma Ngai moonaa nzĩa ĩsu ya kũelesya ngewa sya Mbivilia ĩyaka mũĩkĩĩo. Nĩkĩ ĩndĩ kwĩthĩĩtwe na ũalyũku?
10. (a) Ngombo yĩ na kĩthito ĩtũmĩaa ũĩ ata ĩla ĩkũelesya ngewa imwe syĩ Mbivilianĩ? (b) Matukũ aa mavuku maitũ makothete kũelesya ngewa ata?
10 O ũndũ myaka ĩvĩtĩte, now'o Yeova ũtetheetye ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" ĩendeee kũĩva. Nũndũ wa ũĩ ũsu, yĩthĩawa yĩsũvĩĩte mũno yatw'a kũelesya ngewa yĩ Mbivilianĩ ndĩkamĩelesye ta wathani vate na kĩtumi kĩseo kya Maandĩko. O na ĩngĩ, nĩvesĩte kũmanyĩka kana andũ aingĩ maieleawa nesa ngewa sya Mbivilia syaelew'a tondũ syaeleaw'a tene. Maũndũ ta nũũ ũelekanĩtye ũũ na nĩkĩ, nĩmatonya kũlanĩlya andũ, na me vinya kũlilikanwa kana kũtũmĩwa. Na ĩndĩ thĩna ũla mũnene vyũ nĩ kana, kũmanthĩthya wathani ngewanĩ sya Mbivilia nĩkũtonya kũtuma andũ matakwatya nesa ũndũ matonya kũtũmĩa ũvoo ũla wĩ ngewanĩ ĩsu, kana ũyĩthĩa kĩla mũndũ ũtonya kũsoma vau kĩkamũtethya thayũnĩ wake nĩkyaa vyũ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ũmũnthĩ mavuku maitũ mũno mũno maeleasya ngewa sya Mbivilia kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi vyũ. Nũndũ wa ũu nĩtũeleawa nĩ kĩla tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya ngewanĩ ĩsu kĩkaka mũĩkĩĩo witũ, kĩkatũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na wũmĩĩsyo, twĩyumye vyũ tũmũthũkũme Ngai, na tũielewa maũndũ angĩ ma vata. *
11. (a) Yu tũeleawa ata ngewa ya Navothi, na nĩkĩ ngewa yake nĩtũkonetye? (b) Nĩkĩ matukũ aa mavuku maitũ maikothete kũelesya ngewa sya Mbivilia ta syuu? (Sisya "Makũlyo Kuma kwa Asomi Maitũ" ĩkasetinĩ yĩĩ.)
11 Kwoou yu tũeleawa ata ngewa ya Navothi? Tũmĩeleawa nesanga na kwa nzĩa yĩ laisangi. We ndaakw'a nĩ kana ngewa yake yĩĩsa kwoswa ta wathani ũkonetye Yesũ kana etĩkĩw'a mauta, ĩndĩ akwie nũndũ aĩ mũĩkĩĩku nginya ndatĩka ya mũthya. Alũmanisye na Mĩao ya Yeova o na ĩla anene mamũthĩnisye naĩ mũno vate ũndũ wĩkĩte. (Mot. 36:7; 1 Asu. 21:3) Nũndũ wa ũu, ngelekany'o yake nĩtũkonetye vyũ nĩkwĩthĩwa kĩla ũmwe witũ no athĩnw'e nũndũ wa kũlũmany'a na mĩao ya Yeova. (Soma 2 Timotheo 3:12.) Ti ũndũ wĩ vinya kwa Aklĩsto onthe kũkwatya mĩtũkĩ, kũlilikana, na kũtũmĩa ĩsomo ta yĩu yĩtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo woo.
12. (a) Nata tũtaĩle kũtw'a ĩũlũ wa ngewa ila syĩ Mbivilianĩ? (b) Nĩkĩ no tũelewe o na maũndũ ala maito? (Sisya maelesyo ma kwongeleela.)
12 Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Maũndũ asu no matume twasya kana ngewa sya Mbivilia ieleasya o ũndũ tũtonya kwĩkala na vai ũndũ ũngĩ mbee wa vau? Aiee. Ũmũnthĩ mavuku maitũ mũno mũno nĩmatonya kũtũmanyĩsya ũndũ ngewa ĩmwe ĩkũtũlilikany'a ĩũlũ wa ĩngĩ, kana makamĩtũmĩa ta ngelekany'o ya ũndũ mũna. Ĩndĩ ti laisi ũkethĩa maielesya ngewa mbingĩ sya Mbivilia ta wathani na ũyĩthĩa atĩ vai ũndũ ũngĩ ielew'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, no twasye kana ngewa ya Navothi ĩtũlilikanasya ĩũlũ wa ũĩkĩĩku wa Klĩsto na wa etĩkĩw'a mauta nũndũ ekalile e mũĩkĩĩku nginya ndatĩka ya mũthya o na kau nĩwathĩnaw'a. Ĩndĩ ngewa ĩsu ya Navothi no ĩtũlilikanasya ũĩkĩĩku wa ala "malondu angĩ" ma Mwĩaĩi. Ngai endete nzĩa ta ĩsu yĩ laisi na ĩkũeleeka ya kũmanyĩsya. *
KŨELESYA NGELEKANY'O SYA YESŨ KWA NZĨA YĨ LAISANGI
13. Nĩ maũndũ meva mekwonany'a kana matukũ aa tũeleasya ngelekany'o sya Yesũ kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi na ĩkũeleeka nesa?
13 Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwe Mwalimũ ũla mũnene waaĩkala kũũ nthĩ. Nĩwendete mũno kũtũmĩa ngelekany'o aimanyĩsya andũ. (Mt. 13:34) Ngelekany'o itumaa mũndũ akũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ na kyu kĩituma kĩlĩko kyake kyambĩĩa kũthũkũma. Nũndũ wa ũu kĩla wemanyĩsya nĩkĩkiitaa ngoo yake. Mo mavuku maitũ nĩmethĩwa matinĩte kũelesya ngelekany'o sya Yesũ kwa nzĩa yĩ laisi na ĩkũeleeka? Ũsũngĩo nĩ ĩĩ! Kwa ngelekany'o, tyo tweewie mũyo ĩla ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/07/2008 yatũeleisye nesanga ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya ĩlawa, ya mbeke ya kalatali, na ya kĩtei kya makũyũ? Yu nĩtũeleetwe nesa kana ngelekany'o isu ikonetye Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai na ũndũ ũtetheetye andũ aingĩ ki maumanwe na nthĩ ĩĩ nthũku na maitw'ĩka aatĩĩi ma w'o ma Klĩsto.
14. (a) Tene tũnaeleasya ata ĩla ngelekany'o ya Mũsamalia mũseo? (b) Ngelekany'o ĩsu tũmĩeleawa ata matukũ aa?
14 Nao nata ngelekany'o imwe sya Yesũ ila syĩ na ũvoo mwingĩ? Imwe syasyo syĩ na ũvoo wĩvithanĩtye na no ielew'e ta wathani, nasyo ingĩ iwetete maũndũ tũtonya kũtũmĩa. Thĩna nĩ, tũtonya kũivathũkany'a ata? O ũndũ myaka ĩvĩtĩte, now'o tũmanyĩte ũndũ tũtonya kũivathũkany'a. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ tene tũnaeleasya ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya ũla Mũsamalia mũseo. (Luka 10:30-37) Mwakanĩ wa 1924, ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower yaisye kana Mũsamalia ũsu nĩ Yesũ, naw'o lelũ ũla waumĩte Yelusaleme ũtheeete Yeliko no ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ mũndũ ũendeee naĩ kuma ĩla waleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai e mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. Ing'ei ila syaĩ lelũnĩ ũsu nasyo syaelekanilw'e na maviasala manene na atandĩthya me ĩtomo, nake mũthembi na Mũlivai matw'ĩka nĩ ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto. Ĩndĩ matukũ aa mavuku maitũ matũmĩaa ngelekany'o ĩsu kũlilikany'a Aklĩsto onthe kana mayaĩle kwĩthĩwa na kyende ĩla meũtetheesya ala me na vata, na mũno mũno maũndũnĩ ma kĩ-veva. Mwa tyo nginya twĩthĩwe tũtanaa mũno ĩla twoona Yeova aitũmanyĩsya kwa nzĩa tũtonya kũelewa?
15. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩneeneete kyaũ?
15 Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩeleetye ngelekany'o ĩngĩ ya Yesũ, nayo nĩ ĩla ya eĩtu ĩkũmi. (Mt. 25:1-13) Yesũ endaa aatĩĩi make ma ĩvinda ya mũminũkĩlyo maelewe ata ngelekany'o ĩsu yĩ na ũvoo wa vata? We nĩwĩthĩwa endaa maelewe kana kĩla mũndũ ũwetetwe vau, kana syĩndũ, kana maũndũ ala meekĩkie ĩ ngewanĩ nĩ wathani wĩ na ũvoo wĩvithanĩtye? Kana endaa ngelekany'o ĩsu ĩmamanyĩsye ũndũ matonya kwĩkala mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo? No tũũmanya.
^ kal. 4 Ĩkaseti yĩla yĩ na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi yambĩĩe kumĩthw'a kwa kĩthyomo kya Kĩsũngũ Mwei wa 7, 2011. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, ĩkaseti yĩu yĩ na kĩthyomo kĩ laisi nĩyumĩthĩtw'e kwa ithyomo ingĩ ite mbingĩ.
^ kal. 5 Mĩvango nĩendeee kwĩkwa nĩ kana Mbivilia ĩsu yĩkĩtwe moalyũku yumĩthw'e kwa ithyomo ingĩ.
^ kal. 10 Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvuku Igeni Imani Yao nĩyĩeleetye mũno ĩũlũ wa andũ 14 mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kũelesya ngewa syoo ta wathani, yĩeleetye mũno mũno ũndũ tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o syoo.
^ kal. 12 Vate nzika, Ndeto ya Ngai nĩyĩthĩawa na maũndũ matonya kwoneka "me vinya kũmanya," ta amwe maandĩkiwe nĩ Vaulo. O na ũu wĩ o vo, onthe ala maandĩkie Mbivilia manengetwe veva mũtheu. Veva ũsu now'o ũtetheeasya Aklĩsto ma w'o ũmũnthĩ maelewe ũw'o ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ, o na "maũndũ maliku ma Ngai."—2 Vet. 3:16, 17; 1 Ako. 2:10.

translation:
"The demons fear those who have power over them and know [God], and they obey them greatly."
1. Why did Jesus ask, "What name shall I call Beelzebub by?" (Consider what this means.)
BECAUSE Jesus Christ said, 'I will not call Beelzebub by name.' It is not right to give credit to someone evil with the glory that belongs to God. So why should we give glory to evil? Indeed, he sent seventy disciples among his followers and gave them authority to drive out unclean spirits from people. They reported back joyfully saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name." He replied, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Look, I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and to overcome all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you. However, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven." He sent many more to proclaim Jesus so that people would see him as a dog. And he taught them about his authority so that they would not say, "We have power, and we know [God]." (Luke 4:13; Mark 6:3) Now some of those disciples were very successful. But they became proud and thought they were better than others! Why should we be careful not to become proud?—Read Luke 10:1, 17-21.
2. (a) What reason did Jesus give for sending out his disciples two by two? (b) Why did Christians in the first century feel compassion for people?
2 Jesus prayed to Jehovah, saying: "I publicly praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent people, but have revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, because that is what pleased you. All things have been handed over to me by my Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him." (Matt. 11:25, 26) This shows that Jesus did not simply send out his disciples without a good reason. Those disciples were humble and willing to learn, unlike many wise and intelligent people who think they already know everything. In fact, Jesus told his disciples to become like little children in order to understand spiritual matters. (Matt. 18:1-4) What does it mean to become like little children? Jehovah feels compassion for imperfect humans, just as he felt compassion for Beelzebub, and he wants to help people who are deceived by Satan and who need guidance.
3. What will we now consider?
3 Let us examine how Jesus showed humility. It is important that we appreciate how Jehovah has used the Bible to teach people throughout history, and let us be grateful for this valuable lesson. It is also important that we remember that God's Kingdom is the only hope for mankind. Does Jehovah expect us to show humility when teaching others about the truth? Of course! He wants us to imitate Jesus in our ministry.
TO HELP PEOPLE UNDERSTAND THE TRUTH
4. What reason did the Watch Tower Society give for publishing a simplified version of the book *Reasoning From the Scriptures*?
4 Many of Jehovah's servants find it easier to learn by means of simple language and illustrations. Consider the following points. One way to help them is to use the simplified version of the book *Reasoning From the Scriptures*. *This revised edition is especially helpful to those who have limited education and those who are new to the truth.* Some publishers have found that some individuals respond better to the simplified edition than to the regular edition. So it is good to offer the simplified edition whenever possible. Also, many write letters expressing their appreciation for the simplified edition. For example, one sister wrote: "I was able to understand the information more clearly." Isn't that encouraging! So continue to offer the simplified edition and write to the branch office, saying: "I appreciate the additional information, and I will use it!"
5. Is the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures available in several languages?
5 It is now available in Swahili. This Bible was released on May 10, 2013. *Many scriptures in this new Bible have footnotes that explain things more clearly and provide further insight. For instance, Job 10:1 now has 27 footnotes instead of 19, and Psalm 8:6 now has 20 footnotes instead of 13.* This new Bible is very appealing to many people. And one young man who had been studying for many years said: "I read the book of Job in the new Bible and I felt like I understood it better than ever before!" Many others feel the same way.
6. Will you be able to explain Matthew 24:45-47?
6 Third, continue to make our understanding of God's Word progress. For example, the July 1, 2013, issue of The Watchtower explained the illustration of "a faithful slave and a wicked slave." (Matt. 24:45-47) That article explained that the faithful slave is the one whom Jehovah appointed, and the "households" are those who support the faithful slave, whether they are "shepherds" or "other sheep." (John 10:16) Let us always remember what we have learned and strive to apply it! Are there other ways that Jehovah is helping us to understand his purpose more fully?
HELPING PEOPLE TO UNDERSTAND THE BIBLE MORE FULLY
7, 8. How can we help others to benefit from the new Bible?
7 Even though someone has been studying the Bible with Jehovah for years, he may still need help to grasp the meaning of certain scriptures found in the new Bible. Why is this so? Because people's backgrounds vary, and their way of thinking differs. So, when we discuss Bible teachings with them, we should try to relate them to things they already know or believe, and show how these teachings affect their lives. The new Bible will help sincere ones to see the truth, and it will also help those who are skeptical. But how can we use the Scriptures to help people understand the Bible more fully? Yes, by using illustrations. For instance, Jesus spoke of "the sign of Jonah." (Read Matthew 12:39, 40.) He explained that the account of Jonah illustrates that just as Jonah was in the belly of a large fish for three days, so too would he be in the heart of the earth for three days, and then be resurrected.
8 The Bible contains many illustrations that can help us understand difficult points. The apostle Paul used several illustrations. For example, he compared the covenant between Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to the covenant between Jehovah and the nation of Israel, and the covenant between Jehovah and his loyal servants. (Gal. 4:22-26) Also, he used events such as the Flood, the ten plagues, and Joshua's conquest of Canaan to illustrate important truths. (Heb. 9:23-25; 10:1) By understanding these illustrations in the Bible, we can strengthen our faith and make progress. In fact, whenever a person becomes a Christian, or something happens that affects him personally, does it not often lead him to think about things more deeply?
9. Then let us examine what happened in the case of Naboth?
9 This is how we can benefit from studying Bible illustrations. Let us consider the illustration of Naboth. Jezebel, the wife of King Ahab and a wicked woman, arranged for Naboth to be falsely accused and put to death so that Ahab could take possession of his vineyard. (1 Ki. 21:1-16) In 1932, the illustration of Naboth was explained in detail. It showed how Ahab and Jezebel represented Satan and his organization, how Naboth represented Jesus, and how the desire for Naboth's vineyard symbolized the desire for Jesus' life. Later, in 1961, the drama "Let Your Name Be Sanctified" featured Naboth being unjustly condemned and Jezebel representing false religion. In harmony with this drama, Naboth's condemnation and Jezebel's wickedness were shown to be a foretype of the condemnation and wickedness of false religion. For many years, God's people have seen how the illustration of Naboth helps them to understand spiritual things. But should we stop there?
10. (a) What questions will help us to get the most out of an illustration in the Bible? (b) What benefits can come from considering illustrations?
10 Over the years, Jehovah has been using the expression "illustrations and pictures" more and more. As time goes on, we are motivated to use illustrations in our ministry, and we can share them with others along with a scripture support. Also, we need to determine whether many people understand the point of the Bible's illustrations because they may not fully grasp it. The way we present things and how we speak can affect people, and it may be helpful to observe their reaction or listen to their comments. And sometimes, a large part of the reason why people do not appreciate the Bible's illustrations is that they do not apply to their lives, or they do not take the time to read them carefully and meditate on them personally. That is why it is important for us to regularly consider the Bible's illustrations ourselves. By doing so, we can make sure that we understand them clearly, we can be moved emotionally, we can show appreciation to God, and we can learn further truths. *
11. (a) What lesson do we learn from Naboth's example, and what principle does his case highlight? (b) Why do people today find it difficult to appreciate Bible illustrations at times? (See "Suggestions for Meeting Questions.")
11 How do we learn from Naboth's example? We learn from his experience through the illustration. He was willing to stand up for what he believed was right, even though it meant facing opposition from powerful people. His story shows us that it takes courage to remain faithful to Jehovah, even when it means making sacrifices. (Prov. 36:7; 1 Kings 21:3) Therefore, his example highlights the importance of each of us being determined to know and obey Jehovah's laws. (Read 2 Timothy 3:12.) It is vital for all Christians to avoid getting involved in disputes, becoming resentful, and misapplying scriptures to justify their own selfish desires.
12. (a) How can we improve our use of illustrations in the ministry? (b) What will help us to benefit from illustrations ourselves? (See suggestions for elaboration.)
12 In effect, should we ask ourselves whether a Bible illustration helps us to understand something more clearly or simply adds confusion? No. Often, our experiences enable us to see how one illustration may complement another, or how certain features of an illustration apply to a particular situation. However, do not hesitate to research further if an illustration seems unclear or raises questions. For instance, considering Naboth's case helped us to understand the loyalty of Christ's followers and those who were persecuted because they remained faithful despite facing danger and hardship. But Naboth's case also helps us to understand the meaning of the expression "good name." God values a good name and wants us to protect it. *
UNDERSTANDING JESUS' ILLUSTRATIONS THROUGH THE ILLUSTRATION
13. What things will help us to benefit fully from Jesus' illustrations?
13 Jesus Christ is the greatest Teacher who ever lived. He often used illustrations to teach people. (Matt. 13:34) Illustrations can help a person to remember important points and motivate him to investigate them further. The key to understanding an illustration is to identify its main point. So why have many of us found it difficult to understand Jesus' illustrations? One reason is this! For example, the article "The Watchtower" of July 15, 2008, helped us to appreciate Jesus' illustration of the sheep, the goats, and the sheepfold. Did it also help us to understand what the illustration means for us today and how it affects our relationship with Jehovah and our ministry?
14. (a) What can help us to benefit from the illustrations used by the Samaritan woman? (b) What illustrations have particularly moved you?
14 And does Jesus use only one illustration at a time? Sometimes he uses several illustrations, and they may be closely related, yet each one highlights different aspects of the truth, and we can apply them in various ways. Therefore, can we always grasp their meaning right away? Often, it takes years to fully appreciate what an illustration means. For instance, what can help us to understand Jesus' illustration of the Good Samaritan? (Luke 10:30-37) In 1924, The Watch Tower explained that the Samaritan represents Jesus, and the man going up from Jerusalem to Jericho represents those who turn away from God and get involved in worldly affairs. However, this explanation was later shown to be incorrect, and faithful Christians realized that it did not harmonize with other scriptures. Today, many of us use that illustration to remind ourselves that we should show kindness to others, regardless of their background, and to zealously preach the good news. But how can we make sure that we truly understand what Jehovah wants us to learn from an illustration?
15 What important lesson does this illustrate?
15 This illustrates another important lesson taught by Jesus—that of the ten virgins. (Matt. 25:1-13) Did Jesus tell this story simply to teach us about the importance of being prepared? Or does it also teach us that each individual will be judged according to his own works, whether good, bad, or mediocre? Or does this story reveal something about what we can do to remain close to Jehovah? We do not know.
^ par. 4 This article is based on the Kingdom Ministry School talk "Using Illustrations Effectively," given on March 7, 2011. As mentioned there, this article is also based on information found in other publications.
^ par. 5 Questions often arise as to whether our understanding of Bible accounts is accurate.
^ par. 10 For example, the book Imitate Faith showed that 14 individuals are highlighted in the Bible. It helped many to see that these individuals provide practical lessons that we can imitate.
^ par. 12 Note this point, God's Word is full of things that may seem "difficult to understand," as Paul himself admitted. But despite this, most of the Bible has been understood by sincere Christians throughout history. They have used it to strengthen their faith and to help others understand God's purpose.—2 Pet. 3:16, 17; 1 Cor. 2:10.

Ĩvinda yĩmwe ngĩneena na Izak Marais simũnĩ namũkũlilye: "We nũũkwatya nĩ na myaka yĩana?" Nake Izak anzũngĩie ambĩa: "Nĩsĩ ũkũũ waku nesa vyũ." Simũ ĩsu angũnĩĩte nĩ Colorado nake aĩ Patterson, New York. Ekai nĩmũelesye kĩla kyatumie tũkũlany'a makũlyo asu.
NASYAĨWE Wichita, Kansas, Amelika, kwĩ Matukũ 10, Mwei wa 12, 1936, na ninyie mũkũũ kwitũ. Tũsyaĩtwe twĩ ana, na asyai makwa, William na Jean, maĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova me kĩthito. Ĩvinda yĩu Tata nĩwe watethasya wĩa ũla ũmũnthĩ ũtethaw'a nĩ mũvangĩthya wa nzama ya atumĩa (aĩ company servant). Mami nake amanyĩiw'e Mbivilia nĩ inyia, Emma Wagner. Ve andũ angĩ aingĩ Emma wamanyĩisye ũw'o, na ũmwe woo nĩ Gertrude Steele, ũla wesie kũtũmwa ta misonalĩ ngalĩko ya Puerto Rico na akũtavany'a myaka mingĩ. * Kwoou vaĩ andũ aingĩ mũno naĩ nĩtonya kwĩyĩelekany'a namo.
AMWE ALA MANDIĨE NGELEKANY'O NZEO
Nĩ wa myaka ĩtano, nĩngũlilikana Wathanthatũ ũmwe ĩ ya wĩoo tũũngye vandũ kasĩlanĩ nĩ na ĩthe wakwa. Sua ũsu Tata anenganae makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na Consolation (yu yĩtawa Amkeni!). Ĩvinda yĩu nthĩ yatolonganĩtw'e mũno vyũ nĩ ũla Kaũ wa Kelĩ wa Nthĩ Yonthe. Tũũngamangĩte o vu kasĩlanĩ ndakĩtalĩ ũmwe wanyw'ĩte nĩwookie na ambĩĩa kũumanga Tata nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwaleete kũlika kaũnĩ. Ndakĩtalĩ ũsu aisye kana Tata aĩ na wia, na eekaa ũkengana nĩ kana ndakalike kaũnĩ. Ookie aũngama Tata mbee na amwĩa: "Kĩw'ĩla ngũngũũ kĩĩ ndũngũne!" Natelemile mũno ĩndĩ Tata nĩwe wanzeng'isye. O na kau andũ nĩmoombĩĩie vau twaĩ, we aendeeie kũmanenga makaseti. Twĩkalangĩte ve mũsikalĩ wavĩtĩile vau, na nĩvo ĩndĩ ũla ndakĩtalĩ watũlilye wasya amũkũlya: "Nĩũkũlya vai ũndũ wĩkana na kĩw'ĩla ngũngũũ kĩĩ?" Mũsikalĩ amũsyaisye oou oona nũnyw'ĩte na kwoou amwĩa: "Kwenũka we ũkambe ũmĩlũkwa!" Mũsikalĩ ũsu na ndakĩtalĩ makwatie nzĩa mathi. Mwa nĩtanaa mũno nalilikana ũkũmbaũ ũla Yeova wanengie ĩthe-akwa! Tata aĩ na inyosi ilĩ ku Wichita, na ũsengy'o ũmwe wamwenzaa nĩ ndakĩtalĩ ũsu!
Nĩ na myaka nyanya asyai makwa nĩmatee nyũmba yoo na nduka syoo, maseũvya kasũmba matonya kũthama nako, na ĩndĩ twathamĩĩa Colorado nũndũ kwaĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Twaendie kwĩkala taoninĩ ya Grand Junction, na vau nĩvo asyai makwa makũnĩie ũvainia, na nĩvo makwatie kĩvalũa vandũ vaĩ mĩũnda na indo sya kũĩthya. Kwa vinya wa Yeova na ĩngĩ nũndũ wa kĩthito kyoo, nĩvambĩĩiw'e kĩkundi. Kwĩ Matukũ 20, Mwei wa 6, 1948, o ku taoninĩ ĩsu nĩw'o Tata wambatisĩie kalũsĩnĩ kamwe kaumĩte kĩĩmanĩ. Naĩ na angĩ ala maĩ maneetĩkĩla ũw'o, na ũmwe woo aĩ Billie Nichols na mũka. Ĩtina Billie Nichols na mwanae nĩmesie kũtw'ĩka asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko.
Ithyĩ twakothaa kũtuma ndũũ mũno na aingĩ ala mendete wĩa wa Ũsumbĩ na nĩtwaeaa ngewa mũno namo sya kĩ-veva. Mũsyĩ ũmwe twatumie ndũũ naw'o nĩ ũla wa Steele (Don na Earlene, Dave na Julia, na Si na Martha), na ngelekany'o yoo nĩyandethisye mũno. Asu nĩmatumie nona ũndũ kwamba kũmantha Ũsumbĩ kũtumaa mũndũ akwata ũtanu wa w'o.
KŨTHAMA ĨNGĨ
Nĩ wa myaka 19 Bud Hasty, ũla waĩ mũnyanyae witũ, nĩwangũlilye kana no nĩthi nake tũkakũne ũvainia ngalĩko ya ĩtheo ya Amelika. Mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko atwĩie no tũthamĩĩe taoninĩ ya Ruston, Louisiana, vala vaĩ na Ngũsĩ mbingĩ syavoete. Tweeiwe kĩla kyumwa nĩtwĩke maũmbano onthe tũteũkũlya nĩ meana mekũka. Nĩtwakwatie vandũ vaseo va kũmbanĩa na twavaseũvya. Nĩtwambĩĩe kwĩka maũmbano onthe ĩndĩ kwa ĩvinda yĩana ũna vai ũngĩ wookaa ate o ithyĩ twĩ elĩ. Natwaĩĩasya kĩlungu kĩmwe nake Bud aisũngĩa makũlyo onthe na ĩndĩ namina kĩlungu kyakwa ayoseleela kĩu kĩngĩ nakwa ngĩsũngĩa makũlyo onthe. Ethĩwa kĩlungu kĩ na wonany'o ithyelĩ twaendaa vu mbee ivĩla ikatiwa syĩ nthei! Ĩtina mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe mũkũũ nĩwambĩĩe kũka maũmbanonĩ. Mũthya amanyĩw'a amwe ma Mbivilia vamwe na Ngũsĩ imwe ila syavoete nĩmatinie kũka, na vatathelete kavinda keana ũndũ kĩkundi kyakwata mwaki.
Sua ũmwe nĩ na Bud nĩtwakomanie na vasita wa Church of Christ na atũwetea maandĩko o na ndaĩ naamasoma. Neewie o natelema vanini na kĩu nĩkyatumie nzũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wakwa. Naminie kyumwa ngĩsoma nginya ũtukũ wa mbiti nĩ kana ngwate mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ma vasita ũsu. Kĩu kyatumie nenda ũw'o kuma ngoonĩ, na weethĩa nĩkũlya ngakomana na vasita ũngĩ ta ũsu ĩndĩĩ!
Ĩtina wa kavinda, mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko nĩwangũlilye nĩthi ngatetheesye kĩkundi kyaĩ taoninĩ ya El Dorado, Arkansas. Nĩ vau nĩnaendie Colorado mavinda meana ũna nĩtĩtwe nĩ ĩla kamitii yalikasya andũ itanĩ sya kaũ. Nĩngũlilikana ĩvinda yĩmwe neetiwe nĩ kamitii ĩsu na twavanga nĩ na mavainia angĩ tũthi ku tũtũmĩĩte kakalĩ kakwa. Ĩndĩ twakililye tũivika Texas twakwata akisitendi ĩla yatiie yaananga kakalĩ kakwa vyũ. Nĩtweetie mwana-a-asa mũna na ĩla wookie atũtwaie kwake na esa kũtũtwaa ũmbano. Twĩ ũmbanonĩ kwatangaasiwe kana ve thĩna ũtũkwatie na kwoou ana-a-asa nĩmatũsangĩie mbesa. O na mwana-a-asa ũsu watwosie nĩwathooisye kakalĩ kau ndola 25.
Twauma kwa mwana-a-asa ũsu nĩtwakwatie ngalĩ ĩtonya kũtũvikya Wichita. Taoninĩ ĩsu vekalaa vainia ũmwe mũnyanyae witũ, E. F. McCartney, ũla twakothaa kũmwĩta Doc. Aĩ na mavatha elĩ ma ivĩsĩ, Frank na Francis, ala kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ twĩ ndũũ vyũ. Maĩ na kakalĩ kakũũ na makandeeie ndola 25, o ta ila nakwatie nathoosya kala kangĩ. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kwona nesa Yeova aimbĩanĩĩsya vata wakwa nũndũ wa kũmantha Ũsumbĩ mbee. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu naĩ kwa McCartney nĩmambonanisye na mwĩĩtu ũmwe mũseo na mwanake wĩtawa Bethel Crane. Bethel aĩ kĩthito o ta inyia, Ruth, ũla wakũnie ũvainia na kĩthito ngalĩko ya Wellington, Kansas, nginya o na e na myaka 90 na kĩndũ. Mwaka ũmwe ndwaathela kuma nakomana na Bethel, na kwoou twatwaanie mwakanĩ wa 1958 na twakũna ũvainia nake taoninĩ ya El Dorado.
KŨKWATA IANDA SYA MWANYA
Twasũanĩa ala maĩ ngelekany'o nzeo kwitũ ĩla tweanaa, nĩtwatwie kwĩyumya tũmũthũkũme Yeova ũndũnĩ w'onthe ũseũvyo wake watũthokya twĩke. Na kwoou nĩtweetĩkĩlile kũtũmwa ta mavainia ma mwanya vandũ vetawa Walnut Ridge, Arkansas. Na ĩndĩ mwakanĩ wa 1962 twatanie ta kĩ ĩla twakwatie valũa wa kũthi kĩlasi kya 37 kya Ngileati! O na nĩtwatanie kũmanya kana twĩĩthĩwa kĩlasi kĩmwe na Don Steele. Twamina masomo asu nĩ na Bethel twatũmiwe Ilovi, Kenya. Twaumie New York twĩw'ĩte thĩna mwingĩ mũno ĩndĩ ĩla twakinyie kĩwanzanĩ kya ndeke Ilovi na tweethĩa ana-a-asa vau matũthaũĩte, twatanie mũno.
Ĩtina wa kavinda kateana ũndũ nĩtwendie Kenya mũno na nĩtwatanĩaa kũtavany'a kũu. Amanyĩw'a maitũ ma mbee kwĩka maendeeo nĩ Chris na Mary Kanaiya. O na ũmũnthĩ me ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe nthĩ ya Kenya. Ĩtina wa mwaka ũmwe Kenya, nĩtwakũlilw'e tũthamĩĩe Kampala, Uganda. Nithyĩ twaĩ amisonalĩ ma mbee Uganda. Twatanĩie mũno myaka ĩsu nũndũ vaĩ aingĩ maĩ na mea ma kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia ala ĩtina mesie kũvatiswa. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa kwĩkala myaka ĩtatũ na nusu Africa, nĩtwasyokie Amelika nĩ kana tũkaeee mwana witũ kũu asyawa. Sua ũla twaumie Africa tweewie thĩna mwingĩ mũno o na kũte ũla tweewie tũithama New York. Twaĩ tũnenda mũno andũ ma Africa na kwoou twaumie twĩkwatĩtye kana mũthenya ũmwe tũkasyoka.
NĨTWESIE KŨNENGWA KĨANDA KĨNGĨ
Twaendie kũtũa ivaũũkonĩ sya iĩma ngalĩko ya ũthũĩlonĩ wa syũa wa Colorado, na vau no vo asyai makwa matũaa. Twekalangile o vanini na mwĩĩtu witũ mũkũũ, Kimberly, asyawa. Myei 17 ĩithela nĩtwakwatie Stephany. Kĩanda kĩu twakwatie kya kũea tũyaakyosa na ngũĩ, na nũndũ wa ũu nĩtwatwie kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ tũmanyĩsye twĩlĩtu tu twitũ ũw'o. Ithyĩ nĩtwendaa mũno twĩyĩelekany'e na ala twoonaa me ngelekany'o nzeo ngalĩkonĩ ĩsu. Nĩtwasũanĩie mũno na twamanya kana o na kau ngelekany'o nzeo no itetheesye syana mũno, ũsu ti ũĩkĩĩthyo wa kana syana isu ikaendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova syeana. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũinawa wa mwanake na wa mwĩĩtu nĩmakolile ũla w'o. Ĩndĩ nĩkalaa nĩkwatĩtye kana o mũthenya ũmwe makalilikana andũ ala mamatiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo.
Nĩtwatanĩaa mũno kũea syana sitũ na kĩla ĩvinda nĩtwatataa kwĩka maũndũ twĩ ĩmwe. Twekalaa taoni ya Aspen, Colorado, kũla andũ mendete kũthi kũsiũũka ĩanĩ. Kwoou mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtwaendaa kũsiũũka ĩanĩ. Mavinda ta asu ma kwĩtanĩthya nĩmatũnengae mwanya mũseo wa kũea ngewa na eĩtu maitũ, ta ĩla twalĩsa kakalĩ ka kũtwambatya kĩĩmanĩ nĩ kana tũkasiũũke. O na ĩngĩ nĩtwaendaa kũtembea kũndũ na tũyamba maeema, na mavinda ta asu nĩtwaeaa ngewa nzeo tũyota mwaki. O na kau twĩlĩtu twitũ twaĩ tũnini, twakothaa kũkũlya makũlyo ta "Ngeeka ata ĩla ngeana?" na "Ngatwawa nĩ mũndũ ũilyĩ ata?" Nĩtwatataa mũno kũmanyĩsya syana sitũ kwenda myolooto ya Yeova. Twasyĩkĩaa vinya syĩthĩwe na mũvango wa kũlika ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe, na nĩtwasyonasya ũseo wa kũtwawa nĩ mũndũ wĩ na mũvango o ta ũsu. O na ĩngĩ nĩtwaitetheeasya syone ũseo wa mũndũ kũtwawa aneananga. Twakothaa kũsyĩa, "Amba kũtanĩa kwĩkala ũte mũtwae nginya ĩla wĩvikya myaka 23 ũu."
Nĩtwendie kwĩka o ũndũ asyai maitũ meekaa ĩla tweanaa, na kwoou nĩtwatataa mũno twĩ ta mũsyĩ tũthi maũmbanonĩ na ũtavany'a tũteũtĩĩa. O na nĩtweekaa mĩvango nĩ kana amwe me ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe makomele kwitũ. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana nĩtwendete mũno kũnenga syana sitũ ngewa syĩ mũyo sya ĩla twaĩ amisonalĩ. Nĩtwamanengaa wĩkwatyo wa kana mũthenya ũmwe nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kũthi kũtembea Africa twĩ ana. Yĩsilya yĩu yamatanĩthasya mũno.
Tũyakĩlĩĩlaa mũvango witũ wa kwĩmanyĩsya ta mũsyĩ, na mavindanĩ ta asu nĩtweethĩawa na mawonany'o ma ũndũ eĩtu maitũ matonya kwĩka makwatwa nĩ maũndũ mana me sukulu. Ĩla tũkwĩka mawonany'o asu eĩtu maitũ nĩmo meetw'ĩkĩthasya Ngũsĩ na maisũngĩa makũlyo ala twamakũlya. Meew'aa mũyo mũno ĩla tũkwĩka ũu na kĩu nĩkyamanengie ũkũmbaũ. Ĩndĩ maendeee kwĩana mavinda angĩ nĩmanyungunyĩasya mamanya ĩvinda ya kwĩmanyĩsya nĩyavika. Sua ũmwe neewie woo mũno nginya namea tũisoma kwoou nĩmathi makekale na ku wĩĩ kwoo. Matelemile mũno na mambĩĩa kũĩa mayasya nĩnĩeke masome. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o twamanyie kaĩ nĩtwamatetheetye makambĩĩa kwenda maũndũ ma kĩ-veva! O ũndũ myaka yasongie now'o maendeeie kũtanĩa kwĩmanyĩsya, naitũ nĩtwamaekaa makeyĩelesya vyũ. Ĩndĩ ve o mavinda maasyaa kana maikwĩtĩkĩlana na maũndũ amwe mekwĩmanyĩsya na kĩu nĩkyatumaa tũthĩnĩka. Ĩndĩ no kyatumaa tũmanya kĩla mavindĩĩsye ngoonĩ. Vekala ũu twasũanĩaa vamwe namo na mũthya mayĩsa kwĩtĩkĩlana na kĩla Yeova ũwetete na mayĩanĩwa.
MOALYŨKU ANGĨ ALA TWEEKIE
Syana sitũ syeanie mĩtũkĩ mũno o na tũte kũmanya. Myolooto ĩla twakwataa ũseũvyonĩ wa Ngai nĩyatũtetheeisye kũea syana sitũ kwa nzĩa itonya kũmwenda Yeova. Twatanie ta kĩ ĩla eĩtu maitũ moosie ũvainia ĩtina wa kũmina sekondalĩ, na matata kwĩthĩwa na ũmanyi ũtonya kũmatetheesya kwĩmanthĩa ilovia! O na nĩmathamĩĩe Cleveland, Tennessee, me na eĩtu-a-asa angĩ elĩ nũndũ kũu kwaĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Tweewie thĩna tũimalekya mathi ĩndĩ ũtanu witũ waĩ kwona maitũmĩa thayũ woo ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe. Mathi nĩnoosie ũvainia ĩngĩ nĩ na Bethel na kĩu nĩkyatumie tũkwata ianda ingĩ nzeo mũno. Nĩnatw'ĩkĩthiw'e mũsyaĩĩsya wa mũthyũlũlũko wa kũtetheesya na nĩnanengiwe wĩa wa kũvanga maũmbano manene.
Ĩndĩ eĩtu maitũ matanamba kũthamĩĩa Tennessee, mambie kũtembea London, England, na me ku nĩmesĩile ovisinĩ wa ũvonge. Vau nĩvo Stephany wakomanie na mwanake ũmwe wathũkũmaa Mbetheli kũu wĩtawa Paul Norton. Ĩvinda yĩu Stephany aĩ na myaka 19. Ĩla makũsyokie ĩngĩ ndembea, Kimberly nake nĩwakomanie na mwana-a-asa wathũkũmaa na Paul wĩtawa Brian Llewellyn. Paul na Stephany nĩmatwaanie ĩndĩ maitwaana Stephany nĩwavikĩtye myaka 23. Namo Brian na Kimberly matwaanie mwaka ũla waatĩĩe, Kimberly e na myaka 25. Kwoou nĩw'o nĩmambie kũtanĩa kwĩkala mate atwae nginya mavĩtũkya myaka 23. Ithyĩ naitũ tũyaĩ na nzika na aũme ala manyuvie mamatwae.
Eĩtu maitũ matwĩaa kana ngelekany'o yitũ na ya asyai maitũ nĩyamatetheeisye kũatĩĩa mwĩao wa Yesũ wa 'kwamba kũmantha Ũsumbĩ,' o na ĩla me na thĩna wa mbesa. (Mt. 6:33) Kwĩ Mwei wa 4, 1998, Paul na Stephany nĩmathokiw'e kĩlasinĩ kya 105 kya Sukulu ya Ngileati, na makĩmina matũmiwe Malawi, Africa. Ĩvindanĩ o yĩu Brian na Kimberly manengiwe valũa wa kũthũkũma Mbetheli ya London na ĩtina matũmwa Mbetheli ya Malawi. Twatanie mũno vyũ nũndũ nĩtweesĩ kana vai nzĩa ĩngĩ nzeo ta ĩsu amũika matonya kũtũmĩa thayũ woo.
KĨANDA KĨNGĨ KYA MWANYA VYŨ
Twĩ Mwei wa 1, 2001, nĩw'o nakũnĩwe ĩla simũ nĩwetie mwambĩĩonĩ. Mwana-a-asa Marais, ũla waũngamĩe Mũvĩa wa Kũtetheesya Maũndũ ma Ũalyũli, nĩwangeleisye kana ana-a-asa nĩmavangĩte vethĩwe na koosi ya kũmanyĩsya aalyũli ĩũlũ wa nthĩ Kĩsũngũ. Na o na kau naĩ na myaka 64 nĩmanzũanĩaa mũno nĩtw'ĩke ũmwe wa amanyĩsya ma koosi ĩsu. Ĩndĩ nyie na kĩveti kyakwa Bethel nĩtwavoyie kwondũ wa ũndũ ũsu na twaneena na aa-inyia maitũ matũtetheesye kwĩka ũtwi. Twaneena namo mayaalea tũithi o na kau maĩ akũũ na twesaa kwĩthĩwa twĩ vaasa namo ũndũ tũtamatetheesya. Kwoou nĩnaneenie na Mwana-a-asa Marais namwĩa kana nĩtũũtanĩa mũno kwĩyumya twĩanĩsye kĩanda kĩu kya mwanya.
Ĩvindanĩ yĩu inyia wakwa nĩweethĩiwe na kanza. Namũtavisye kana nĩtũũtĩsya savalĩ yitũ nĩ kana tũtetheesye mwĩĩtu-a-mwaitũ, Linda, kũmũsũvĩa. Ĩndĩ Mami ambĩie: "Ndwaĩlĩte kwĩka ũu. Nĩka kũwaa ĩ ya mũno mũkaema kũthi." O nake Linda aĩ o na woni ta wa Mami. Nĩtweewie tweekĩwa vinya mũno twoona kwĩyumya kũla Mami na Linda meeyumisye nĩ kana matũkwate mbau, o na vamwe na ũtethyo ũla ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa kĩsionĩ kitũ matũnengie. Mũthenya ũla waatĩĩe ĩtina wa twathi Watchtower Educational Center, taoninĩ ya Patterson, Linda nĩwatũkũnĩie simũ na atwĩa Mami nũkwie. Ĩndĩ nĩtweeyumisye vyũ wĩanĩ ũla twathĩĩwe kũtethya nũndũ nĩtweesĩ ũu now'o Mami wenda twĩke takeka e thayũ.
Ĩla twaminie masomo, vandũ va mbee vala twatũmiwe nĩ ovisinĩ wa ũvonge wa nthĩ ya Malawi, vala eĩtu maitũ na aũme moo matũmĩtwe. Twatanie mũno kũkomana namo ĩngĩ! Twauma vau nĩtwasyokie twatũmwa tũkamanyĩsye aalyũli nthĩ ya Zimbabwe na mũthya twaminĩĩa na Zambia. Ĩtina wa kũmanyĩsya myaka ĩtatũ na nusu, nĩtwakũlilw'e tũsyoke Malawi tũkaandĩke maũndũ ala ana-a-asa moonete maithĩnw'a nũndũ wa kũlea kũlika siasanĩ. *
Kwa ĩvinda yĩngĩ mwakanĩ wa 2005 nĩtwathĩnĩkie mũno ĩla twatw'ĩkie nĩtũũsyoka mũsyĩ Basalt, Colorado. Kũu nokw'o tũĩ nĩ na Bethel tũendeee na ũvainia. Twĩ mwakanĩ wa 2006, Brian na Kimberly nĩmathamĩĩe nyũmbanĩ ĩvakene na yitũ nĩ kana maeee eĩtu moo vau. Eĩtu asu nĩ Mackenzie na Elizabeth. Ĩndĩ Paul na Stephany me o Malawi, na Paul ethĩawa nthĩnĩ wa Kamitii ya Ovisi wa Ũvonge. Nĩthengeee myaka 80 na nĩnĩtanaa mũno kwona anake ala nĩthũkũmĩte namo myakanĩ ĩsu makwatĩĩe ianda ila neethĩawa nasyo. Yu twĩ na ũtanu mwingĩ mũno, na mũno mũno ũtanu ũsu tũũkwatĩte nũndũ wa ala maĩ ngelekany'o nzeo kwitũ, na ala twatwie kwĩyĩelekany'a namo nĩ kana syana sitũ na esũkũũa matetheke.
