translation:
One day I was talking with Isaac Maris when he asked me: "Are you afraid of growing old?" Isaac answered me saying: "I don't think about such things." Then I went to Colorado and then to Patterson, New York. It was exciting to use those means to help people.
I WAS BORN in Wichita, Kansas, America, on October 10, 1936, and I am proud of my upbringing. We were raised with two children, and our parents, William and Jean, were devoted servants of Jehovah. My father was the one who pioneered this full-time ministry (a company servant). My mother learned about the Bible from her sister, Emma Wagner. She helped many others learn about it, and one of them was Gertrude Steele, who served as a missionary in Puerto Rico for many years. * Many more brothers and sisters also benefited from their example.
OTHER INTERESTING ARTICLES
When I was five years old, I remember one of the brothers taking us to his home. He would play recordings of The Watchtower and Consolation (now called Awake!). That brother was named Carl Klein. We enjoyed listening to those recordings very much, and one time he told me to ask Father why he was so happy. He said that Father always had a smile, and he wondered why. He told Father, "Tell me what makes you so happy!" Father replied to him: "It is because I know the truth!" I realized then that Father was the one who influenced me. And many brothers encouraged us to read, and one brother especially encouraged Father to bring recordings to listen to. We listened to those recordings often, and that is why one brother asked me: "Why are you so interested in knowing the truth?" That brother impressed me greatly, and he said: "You should tell others about it!" That brother and I became good friends. Now I realize how important the work of Jehovah is! Father had a business in Wichita, and one of his customers was a brother!
I was quite young when we moved from our house to another house, and we traveled a lot, and in 1947 we moved to Colorado to be near my maternal grandfather. We went to live in Grand Junction, and they were very kind to us, and they helped us find people who could help us with things. Through the Witnesses and their publications, I was invited to a congregation. On March 20, 1948, in that town, Father baptized me as a symbol of my dedication. I had many fine examples, and one of them was Billie Nichols and his wife. Billie Nichols and his family helped us to become more zealous in the ministry.
Later we began sending letters to many others along with our support to the missionary work, and we received encouraging letters back. One family we wrote to was the Steeles (Don and Earlene, Dave and Julia, and Si and Martha), and their response was very appreciative. He also sent money to help send someone to the missionary work.
MORE TRAVELING
When I was 19 years old, Bud Hasty, a friend of our family, suggested that we might go to America to preach. The missionary encouraged us to move to Ruston, Louisiana, where several of his relatives lived. Every week we held meetings so that we could learn how to improve. We met many good people and enjoyed being with them. We organized meetings regularly in a small hall, and sometimes there were so many people that we had to stand. And we appreciated the opportunity that Bud gave us to travel extensively and often, and I remember one trip he took us on where we drove all night! A certain elderly man told me about the meetings. He knew some scriptures and had a relative who was a Witness, but they did not allow him to attend because the congregation did not have enough space.
One day, Bud and I went with a member of the Church of Christ and he showed us scriptures and asked us questions. It seemed like I didn't understand anything, and I wished I had studied more. I remember one time when I stayed up late reading until I fell asleep from exhaustion. That helped me to be able to speak better, and I was grateful to be able to talk to that brother again!
After leaving that place, the missionary suggested that we move to El Dorado, Arkansas. Then we traveled to Colorado for a few days and I didn't like the cold weather very much. I remembered a hall where we used to meet with many people, and we would gather with others to help each other. After we left there, we went to Texas and found a building that looked just like the one we had left behind. I met a young man there whose parents invited us to their home and offered us food. We continued holding meetings, hoping that we would find someone who would accept us and that those young people would be interested. And that young man later helped us by giving us $25.
We left with that young man and traveled towards Wichita. In that town, there was an old friend of ours named E. F. McCartney, whom we called Doc. He also had two sons, Frank and Francis, who were kind to us. With his help and our own efforts, we managed to get some money, about $25. This was the first time I ever earned money working for Jehovah, trying to preach the good news. Through McCartney, I met another kind man and his wife, Bethel Crane. Bethel had a daughter named Ruth, who lived with her family in Wellington, Kansas, and she was over 90 years old. One year later, I visited him and we got married in 1958 and moved to live in El Dorado.
GETTING A PLACE TO STAY
We looked around for a place to stay, but since we didn't have much money, we decided to try to please Jehovah so that he would provide for us. And then we received an invitation to serve at the branch office in Walnut Ridge, Arkansas. And in the summer of 1962, we were accepted into class 37 of Gilead! We were happy to learn that we would be classmates with Don Steele. After finishing our studies with Bethel, we were assigned to Illovo, Kenya. We left New York with many blessings, and when we arrived in Illovo, we enjoyed helping the children there, and we were very happy.
During those wonderful years, we traveled extensively throughout Kenya, and we were able to encourage others. We became acquainted with Chris and Mary Kanaiya, who were very kind to us. They also introduced us to many other brothers and sisters throughout Kenya. After spending one year in Kenya, we were transferred to Kampala, Uganda. While in Uganda, we had many interesting experiences. We spent several years happily working with people and helping them to understand the Bible, and we were grateful for the opportunity to witness. After serving in Africa for two and a half years, we returned to America, hoping to see our son again. Since we lived in Africa, we experienced many blessings, and we learned lessons that helped us when we returned to New York. We missed the friends we had made in Africa, but we knew that we could always remember them.
WE ARE LOOKING FORWARD TO ANOTHER ASSIGNMENT
We moved to a beautiful area near Boulder, Colorado, where there was a need for more publishers. We enjoyed living there, and we often visited our older brother, Kimberly, who lived nearby. On December 17th, we welcomed Stephany. This assignment gave us the opportunity to work closely with the congregation, and through this experience, we got to know many fine individuals. We continued to travel frequently, and we saw how people responded to the good news. We realized that many people were willing to learn, but some needed more time to make a decision. However, we trusted that Jehovah would help them. In addition to the joy of seeing people progress spiritually, we also appreciated the support of our family and friends. It was encouraging to see how they supported our ministry and shared our enthusiasm for the truth.
We made it a point to spend time with our children and each week we planned activities together. We lived near Aspen, Colorado, where many tourists came to ski. Day after day, we took advantage of opportunities to speak to people about spiritual things, knowing that sometimes just a small seed could be planted. And often we found ourselves walking around town and helping others, and on those days we would enjoy sharing the good news with them. Our children often asked questions like, "Why does everyone need to hear?" and "Are we the only ones doing this?" We continued to encourage our children to participate in Jehovah's service. We benefited from the privilege of attending meetings at the Kingdom Hall throughout the year, and we cherished the opportunity to associate with fellow believers and strengthen our resolve. And often we were touched by the kindness shown to us by others. We learned to say, "Please don't feel obligated to donate anything if you have been benefiting from this information for over 23 years."
We wondered how we could use what we had to help others, and we realized that we could make a greater impact by being organized and efficient. And we set goals to continue making progress throughout the year. This helped us to stay motivated and to focus on reaching out to more people with the good news. We appreciated the support of friends who encouraged us to travel to Africa with them. That experience was very rewarding.
We also considered our responsibility to be an example to others, and we were inspired by the way young ones at school applied what they learned. But we wanted to be better examples ourselves so that we could influence others positively. It's important to remember that our actions speak louder than words. So let us strive to live in harmony with our beliefs. Let us continue to share the truth with others, and may our efforts bring glory to God. We have learned that it takes courage to stand up for what is right, even when it is difficult. And we know that Jehovah will strengthen us as we face challenges.
MORE THINGS THAT WE LEARNED
Sometimes we feel inadequate, but we can find comfort in knowing that God loves us and wants to help us become more like his Son. We should not be discouraged if we make mistakes, but rather learn from them and keep striving to serve Jehovah faithfully. We appreciate the support we receive from fellow believers, and we are grateful for the opportunity to share the good news with others. We trust that Jehovah will guide us and give us strength as we continue to preach the Kingdom message. We realize that some people may oppose us or misunderstand our teachings, but this should not deter us from sharing the truth. Rather, it should motivate us to pray for understanding and wisdom. Let us work together to encourage one another and to remain united in our service to Jehovah.
I am writing from Cleveland, Tennessee, along with many friends who send their warm greetings. We are very busy helping to prepare for the international convention. We are thankful for the privilege of serving at Bethel and for the opportunity to have a greater share in the ministry. I was recently assigned to assist with the construction project, and I am enjoying working alongside experienced builders.
Some of our family members who live in Tennessee joined us on a trip to London, England, and I had the pleasure of meeting several interesting people there. One of them was Stephanie, who works with her husband, Paul Norton, at Bethel. Stephanie is 19 years old. But there were also other surprises; Kimberly, her sister, works with her son and Paul named Brian Llewellyn. Paul and Stephanie have been married for 23 years. And Brian and Kimberly got married last year, Kimberly being 25 years old. So it's true that I went to visit to see how they were doing after 23 years. It's nice to see families thriving and happy in their marriage.
Our family has always tried to put spiritual things first, like Jesus taught us—'to seek first the Kingdom,'—but sometimes we struggle to do so. (Matt. 6:33) On April 4, 1998, Paul and Stephanie graduated from the 105th class of Gilead School, and they were then appointed to Malawi, Africa. At that time, Brian and Kimberly were invited to serve at Bethel in London and later sent to Bethel in Malawi. We appreciate your prayers and encouragement, and we hope that you will continue to support us in this work.
ANOTHER INTERESTING EXPERIENCE
On May 1, 2001, I had an interesting experience. Brother Marais, who served as a pioneer special, asked if his children could benefit from a course on effective teaching for publishers. He was 64 years old, yet he volunteered to take the course with them. My wife and I appreciated how eager he was to improve his teaching skills. We also enjoyed spending time with his family and helping them to apply what they learned. I remember talking to Brother Marais and realizing how much we can accomplish when we cooperate in this important work.
His recent visit reminded me of a difficult situation we faced some years ago. We were concerned about whether we would be able to help our sister, Linda, spiritually. Her mother told me: "Please don't give up on her. She has the potential to make progress." So my wife and I continued to pray for Linda, and we were thrilled to see her respond favorably, along with others in her family and some of our friends. The day she completed her training at the Watchtower Educational Center, near Patterson, Linda thanked us for introducing her to Mother and encouraging her. I was so happy to see her determination to put what she had learned into practice, and Mother was very pleased too.
After completing our assignment, we received an invitation to serve as volunteers at the branch office in Malawi, where there was a great need for assistance. We accepted gladly, and we looked forward to it eagerly! We realized that this meant we would have to travel through Zimbabwe and then on to Zambia. After serving for three and a half years, we returned to Malawi and assisted in compiling material to help congregations strengthen their organizational routines.—*
In the spring of 2005, we received another exciting assignment—to move to Basalt, Colorado. There we joined the Bethel family and enjoyed full-time service. In 2006, Brian and Kimberly welcomed us warmly into their home, and we appreciated their hospitality. Their children are Mackenzie and Elizabeth. Meanwhile, Paul and Stephany remained in Malawi, and Paul served as a member of the Branch Committee. He reached the age of 80 and continues to enjoy good health, and he often recalls those years with fondness. We cherish many fond memories, and we especially appreciate the love and support that brothers and sisters showed us during those challenging times, and we continue to value the friendships we formed with them.

text:
"[Meaĩe] mekae nesa, . . . nĩ kana makwate ũla thayũ wa tene na tene, naw'o nĩ thayũ wa w'o."—1 TIM. 6:18, 19.
MBATHI: 43, 40
1, 2. (a) We wĩ na mea ma kwona moathimo meva ma kĩ-mwĩĩ ĩla twĩvika Nthĩ Nzaũ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩkatũtanĩthya mũno vyũ ĩla tũkalika nthĩ nzaũ?
"THAYŨ WA W'O." Aingĩ maitũ ĩla tweew'a ndeto isu tũlilikanaa wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o wa kwĩsa kwĩkala Nthĩ Nzaũ. O na mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwoonanisye kana "thayũ wa tene na tene" na "thayũ wa w'o" nikonanĩtye. (Soma 1 Timotheo 6:12, 19.) Tweteele ĩvinda yĩla tũkekala tũteũkw'a, twĩ atanu vyũ, na twĩ eanĩe vyũ. O na tũitonya kũsũanĩa ũndũ tũkew'aa kĩla mũthenya tũiamũka tũkethĩa vate kĩndũ kĩũtũthĩny'a kĩlĩkonĩ kana ngoonĩ, kana tũte na ũwau o na ũmwe. (Isa. 35:5, 6) Kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla tũkew'aa tũitindany'a na andũ ma mũsyĩ na anyanyae maitũ, o na vamwe na ala makathayũũkw'a! (Yoa. 5:28, 29; Meko 24:15) O na nĩtũkakwata mwanya wa kwongela ũmanyi witũ maũndũnĩ ma saenzi, mbathi, myako, kana o maũndũ angĩ.
2 O na kau nĩtweteele kwona maũndũ asu maseũvĩte ũu, kĩla kĩkatũtanĩthya mũno vyũ nĩ maũndũ ala makonetye ũthaithi wa Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, twĩ kũu tũkeew'a mũyo ta kĩ twalilikana kana Yeova nũtheetye ĩsyĩtwa yake na akatetea ũsumbĩki wake mũnene! (Mt. 6:9, 10) Nata ĩla tũkona kĩeleelo kya Yeova kwondũ wa nthĩ na andũ kĩendeee kwĩanĩa? Ũndũ ũsu ũkatuma tũtana mũno. Na ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa ũndũ tũtakew'a vinya wa kũmũthengeea Yeova ĩvinda yĩu tũkethĩwa tũivetewa naĩ o kavola kwa kavola nginya naĩ ĩsu yĩse kũthela vyũ!—Sav. 73:28; Yak. 4:8.
3. Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kwĩyũmbanĩsya?
3 No twĩse kũkwata moathimo asu nũndũ Yesũ aisye atĩĩ: "Kwa Ngai maũndũ onthe nĩmatonyeka." (Mt. 19:25, 26) Ĩndĩ ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda twĩĩkala nthĩ nzaũ na tũiendeea kwĩkala twĩ thayũ o na ĩtina wa Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Klĩsto, no nginya twose ĩtambya oyu ya 'kũlũmya' ũla thayũ wa tene na tene. Twaĩle kwĩkala twĩsĩ kana mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno nthũku ũkilyĩ ũnavika, na kwoou no nginya twose ĩtambya yu tũĩ nĩ kana twĩyũmbanĩsye kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ. Ĩndĩ tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata twĩ nthĩ ĩno ĩthũkĩte ũu?
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KWĨYŨMBANY'A
4. Tũmĩa ngelekany'o ũelesye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩyũmbanĩsya kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ.
4 Tũtonya kwĩyũmbanĩsya ata kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ ya Ngai? Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Twasye nũvangĩte kũthamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ. Ũtonya kwĩyũmbanĩsya ũndũ ũsu ata? No kwĩthĩwa ũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya andũ ala mekalaa kũu. O na ĩngĩ kwĩmanyĩsya syĩthĩo syoo no kũũtethye. O na no ũtw'e kũsama malĩu amwe ma kũu. Kwa ũkuvĩ, wambĩĩa kwĩkala ta wavikie kw'o. Nĩkĩ ũtonya kũtata kwĩka maũndũ asu? Nũndũ nĩmo ũkethĩa nthĩ ĩla ũkwenda kũthamĩĩa. O ta ũu, twaĩle kwĩyũmbanĩsya kwĩsa kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ kwa kũtata ũndũ tũtonya twĩkale ũndũ tũkwĩkwatya andũ ta makethĩwa mayĩkala me kũu. Ekai ĩndĩ twone maũndũ amwe tũtonya kwĩka twĩyũmbanĩsye kwĩsa kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ.
5, 6. Kwĩmanyĩsya kũatĩĩaa myolooto ĩla tũnengawe kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma Yeova kũtũmbanasya ata kwondũ wa kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ?
5 Nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ vai mũndũ ũkethĩwa aileana na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai. Kũkethĩwa kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o mũno na ũmũnthĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩno ĩtongoew'e nĩ Satani andũ mendete kwĩsumbĩka. Andũ amwe nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa mendete kwĩtongoesya na kwĩka kĩla monaa takyo kĩseo, ĩndĩ kw'o kwĩka ũu kũtumĩte maũndũ methĩwa mailyĩ ata? Nũndũ andũ mayendaa kũtongoew'a nĩ Ngai, ũndũ ũsu nũtumĩte kwĩthĩwa na mathĩna, kyeva, na mĩisyo. (Yel. 10:23) Mwa twĩ na mea maingĩ ma kwĩsa kwona ĩvinda yĩla andũ onthe makethĩwa menyivĩsye ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova!
6 Ũkethĩwa wĩ ũndũ mũseo mũno kũtongoew'a nĩ Yeova mĩvangonĩ ĩla ĩkethĩwa vo ya kwanakavĩĩsya nthĩ nzaũ, kũmanyĩsya ala makethĩwa manathayũũkw'a, na kwĩka kyonthe kĩla Yeova ũkenda twĩke. Ĩndĩ nata tũkesa kwĩwa tũthũkũme wĩa tũtawendete? No tũatĩĩe ũndũ tweewa twĩnyivĩtye na tũitata ũndũ tũtonya twĩanĩsye wĩa ũla tũnengetwe twĩ atanu? Aingĩ maitũ matonya kũsũngĩa ĩĩ! Ĩndĩ ethĩwa ũu nĩ w'o, ũmũnthĩ nĩtũatĩĩaa myolooto ĩla tũnengawe kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma Yeova? Ethĩwa nĩtwĩkaa ũu, nĩtũendeee kwĩyũmbany'a kwondũ wa kwĩkala tene na tene tũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Yeova.
7, 8. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩmanyĩsya kũatĩĩa ũndũ tweewa twĩke? (b) Aklĩsto amwe mekĩte moalyũku meva? (c) Nĩ ũndũ mwaũ twĩsĩ ĩũlũ wa wĩa kana kũndũ kũla tũkekala nthĩ nzaũ?
7 Kũatĩĩa myolooto ĩla tũnengawe kĩkundinĩ kya andũ ma Yeova ti kw'o kwĩ kw'oka kũtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩyũmbanĩsye kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ. Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kũtũtetheesya nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kwĩanĩwa na kwĩthĩwa twĩ na ngwatanĩo nzeo na ala angĩ. Ethĩwa ũmũnthĩ twanengwa wĩa ũngĩ nĩ ala matongoesye nĩtwĩw'aa twĩ eanĩe na twĩ atanu, nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kwĩthĩwa tũilyĩ oou ĩla twĩlika nthĩ nzaũ. (Soma Aevelania 13:17.) Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Aisilaeli malikile Nthĩ ya Watho, maaĩawa itheka kwa nzĩa ya kũkũna kula. (Mot. 26:52-56; Yos. 14:1, 2) O ta ũu, tũyĩsĩ vala kĩla ũmwe ũkanengwa ekale ĩla twĩvika nthĩ nzaũ. Ĩndĩ o na tũtw'ĩke tũkekala va, tũkeethĩwa twĩ atanu na twĩ eanĩe twaendeea kũmũthũkũma Yeova na kũatĩĩa ũndũ tũkwĩwa.
8 Nĩ ũndũ mũseo ta kĩ kwĩsa kwĩthĩwa tũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai! Nũndũ wa ũu twaĩlĩte kũtanĩa mũno kũatĩĩa ũndũ kĩkundi kya andũ ma Yeova kĩũtwĩa ũmũnthĩ na kwĩanĩsya wĩa ũla twanengwa. Nao nata ĩla kweethĩwa na moalyũku o ũndũ ĩvinda yĩvĩtĩte? Kwa ngelekany'o, athũkũmi amwe ma Mbetheli ya Amelika nĩmanengiwe ũthũkũmi ũngĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe, na ũmũnthĩ nĩmatanĩaa moathimo ala makwatĩte. Namo angĩ ala maĩ asyaĩĩsya ma kũthyũlũlũka matw'ĩkĩthiw'e mavainia ma mwanya nũndũ wa ũkũũ kana o maũndũ angĩ. Kũkesa kũthi ũu, twaĩle kũmũthũkũma Ngai twĩ eanĩe, tũimũvoya atũtetheesye, na tũyĩka kyonthe kĩla tũtonya. Tweeka ũu tũkeethĩwa twĩ atanu na tũkakwata moathimo maingĩ o na kau tũtwĩe ĩvindanĩ ĩthũku. (Soma Nthimo 10:22.) Nao nata ĩvinda yũkĩte? Nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũsũanĩaa kũla tũkenda kũtũa twalika nthĩ nzaũ, ĩndĩ noĩthwa tũkesa kwĩwa twĩkale vandũ vangĩ. Ĩndĩ o na kwesa kwĩthĩwa kũilyĩ ata, kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana o na ethĩwa tũkamũthũkũma Yeova twĩ va kana o na ethĩwa tũkanengwa wĩa mwaũ, tũkeew'a twĩ eanĩe, twĩ atanu, na tũkatũngaa mũvea.—Nee. 8:10.
9, 10. (a) Nĩ maũndũnĩ ta meva ũkethĩa no nginya twĩthĩwe na wũmĩĩsyo? (b) Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana twĩ na wũmĩĩsyo?
9 Ĩla twĩlika nthĩ nzaũ, no kwĩthĩwa ve mavinda ũkethĩa no nginya twĩthĩwe na wũmĩĩsyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, no twĩse kwona andũ amwe me na ũtanu nũndũ anyanyae moo na andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmathayũũkw'a. Ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa ithyĩ no tweteelaa nginya ĩla ala maitũ makathayũũkw'a. Vakesa kwĩkala ũu nĩtũtana na ala angĩ o tũendeee kweteela? (Alo. 12:15) Ũmũnthĩ tweemanyĩsya kweteela moathimo ala Yeova ũtwathĩte tũteũkw'a ngoo, ũu ũkatũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na wũmĩĩsyo ĩvindanĩ yĩu.—Mũta. 7:8.
10 Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩyũmbany'e kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kweteela ĩla vaumĩla ũalyũku momanyĩsyonĩ maitũ. Ithyĩ twĩkaa ata ĩla vaumĩla ũalyũku momanyĩsyonĩ maitũ? Nĩtwĩmanyĩasya ũvoo ũsu na kĩthito na tũkethĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo ethĩwa tũinaũelewa? Ethĩwa nĩtwĩkaa ũu, ĩla twĩvika nthĩ nzaũ tũikaemwa nĩ kũmĩĩsya na kũmweteela Yeova atũtetheesye tũelewe kwenda kwake.—Nth. 4:18; Yoa. 16:12.
11. Yeova atũmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa kwĩkalany'a na andũ, na ũu ũkatũtetheesya ata twĩ nthĩ nzaũ?
11 Kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩyũmbanĩsye kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kũekea. Ĩvindanĩ ya Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Klĩsto, nĩvatonyeka ĩvinda yĩkavĩta ala alũngalu na mate alũngalu mayĩsa kũvetewa naĩ vyũ. (Meko 24:15) Kwoou ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ, Tũkekalany'a na andũ ala angĩ nesa ĩvindanĩ yĩu? Tweemanyĩsya kũekea ala angĩ na kwĩkalany'a namo nesa, tũikaemwa nĩ kwĩka oou ĩvindanĩ yĩla yũkĩte.—Soma Akolosai 3:12-14.
12. Elesya ũndũ mwĩkalo witũ ũmũnthĩ ũkonanĩtye na wĩkwatyo witũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.
12 Ĩla twĩlika nthĩ nzaũ, ti lasima tũkakwataa kĩndũ kĩla tũkwenda ĩvinda yĩla tũũkyenda. Kwoou o na kau Yeova akatũathimaa nũndũ wa kwĩnyivĩsya ũsumbĩki wake, no nginya ĩvinda yĩu twĩĩmanyĩsya kũtũngaa mũvea na kwĩanĩwa nĩ kĩla twĩ nakyo. Kwĩthĩwa na nguma ila Yeova ũtũmanyĩasya ũmũnthĩ nĩkũkatũtetheesya ĩvinda yĩu. Kwondũ wa ũu, tweemanyĩsya kwĩkalaa ta andũ meteele kwĩsa kũtũa nthĩ nzaũ, nĩtwĩthĩawa na nguma ila ikatũtetheesya kwĩkala tene na tene. O na ĩngĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ now'o tũlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ nthĩnĩ wa maũndũ ala matũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana kwĩ 'nthĩ yũkĩte.' (Aevl. 2:5; 11:1) Na ĩndĩ nĩtwĩkaa maũndũ mekwonany'a kana twĩ na mea mũno ma kwĩsa kwona nthĩ yusĩe ũlũngalu. Kwoou nĩ w'o vyũ, tũendeee kwĩyũmbanĩsya ĩvinda yĩla tũkekala tene na tene nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ ĩla Ngai ũtwathĩte.
TŨNGA KĨLĨKO KYAKU ŨTHŨKŨMINĨ WA YEOVA
13. Nĩ maũndũ meva makethĩwa me ma vata vyũ ĩla twĩvika nthĩ nzaũ?
13 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana twĩyũmbanĩsye kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ. O na kau nĩtwathĩtwe lĩu mwingĩ na syĩndũ mbingĩ ĩla twĩlika nthĩ nzaũ, kĩndũ kĩla kĩkatũtanĩthya mũno vyũ nĩ kwona tũyĩanĩĩw'a mavata maitũ ma kĩ-veva. (Mt. 5:3) Kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩkw'o kũkethĩwa ũndũ ũla wa vata, na tũkatanĩa mũno kwĩka ũu. (Sav. 37:4) Kwoou twoona kũmũthũkũma Yeova new'o ũndũ ũla wa vata ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ, tũkeethĩawa tũyĩyũmbanĩsya kũtanĩa ũla thayũ wa w'o ĩvinda yũkĩte.—Soma Mathayo 6:19-21.
14. Nĩ mĩvango yĩva ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova ĩtonya kũtetheesya andũ ma mũika meyũmbanĩsye kwĩkala tene na tene?
14 Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũtanĩe mũnango kũmũthũkũma Yeova ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ? Kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya nĩ kwĩvangĩĩa kwĩka maũndũ mana ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova. We wĩ mũndũ wa mũika ũsũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova na ngoo yonthe? Wĩona ata ũkasoma maũvoo amwe maeleetye mĩthemba yĩ kĩvathũkany'o ya ũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe na ũyĩvangĩĩa ũla ũkwenda kwĩanĩsya? * O na no ũneene na amwe methĩĩtwe ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe kwa myaka mingĩ. Weeyumya vyũ ũmũthũkũme Ngai, no ũkwate ũmanyi wa vata ũla ũkaũtetheesya ũmũthũkũme wĩ nthĩ nzaũ.
15. Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ matonya kwĩanĩsya maũndũ meva ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova?
15 Nũndũ twĩ atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ, nĩ maũndũ meva ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova tũtonya kũvanga kwĩanĩsya? No twĩvangĩĩe twĩthĩwe na ũtũĩka mũna ũtavany'anĩ. Kana no twĩkĩe kĩthito tũelewe mũnango myolooto mĩna ya Mbivilia na ũndũ ĩtonya kũtũmĩwa. O na no twĩkĩe kĩthito twĩke maendeeo maũndũnĩ ta kũsoma, kumya ũvoo, na kumya maelesyo ũmbanonĩ. O naku ndũema kũsũanĩa maũndũ angĩ ũtonya kwĩka. Kwoou kĩla twaĩle kũmanya nĩ atĩĩ: Kwĩvangĩĩa maũndũ mana ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova nĩkwongelaa wendi witũ wa kũmũthũkũma, na ũu ũitũtetheesya kwĩyũmbany'a ũndũ tũkekala nthĩ nzaũ.
O NA ŨMŨNTHĨ NĨTŨATHIMAWA!
16. Nĩkĩ kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mũseo vyũ?
16 Nũndũ tũtũmĩaa ĩvinda yitũ tũyĩyũmbanĩsya ũndũ tũkekala nthĩ nzaũ, ũu nĩ kwasya kana tũyĩkalaa nesa ũmũnthĩ? Aiee! Kũmũthũkũma Yeova nĩkyo kĩndũ kĩla kĩtumaa mũndũ ew'a e mwĩanĩe mũno. Tũimũthũkũmaa Yeova aĩ nũndũ nĩtũũlasimĩthw'a tũmũthũkũme nĩ kana twĩvonoka ũla thĩna mũnene. Ĩndĩ tũmbĩtwe twĩ na wendi wa kũmũthũkũma na ĩla tweeka ũu nĩtũtanaa mũno. Kũtongoew'a nĩ Yeova na kwendwa nĩwe nĩ syĩndũ sya vata mũno kwĩ kwasya ngwatanĩo yitũ nake. (Soma Savuli 63:1-3.) Kwoou ti lasima tweteele nginya ĩla tũkalika nthĩ nzaũ nĩ kana tũkwate moathimo ala tũkwataa nũndũ wa kũmũthũkũma Yeova na ngoo yonthe. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o na ũmũnthĩ nĩtũathimawa! O na amwe maitũ methĩĩtwe maikwata moathimo asu kwa myaka mingĩ, na kwosana na ũndũ twĩyoneete nĩtwĩsĩ nesa ki kana kũmũthũkũma Yeova nokw'o kũtonya kũtuma twĩkala twĩ eanĩe.—Sav. 1:1-3; Isa. 58:13, 14.
17. Kwĩtanĩthya na kwĩka tũmaũndũ tũla twendete nĩkw'o kũkethĩwa kwa vata vyũ Nthĩ Nzaũ?
17 Nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzaũ andũ makatanĩa kwĩtanĩthya na kwĩka tũmaũndũ tũla mendete ĩvindanĩ yĩla yaĩle. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nũndũ takeka Yeova ndendaa twĩanĩsye wendi ũsu, ndethĩwa aatũmba naw'o. (Mũta. 2:24) Kwoou Yeova 'akeanĩĩsya kwenda kwa kĩla kĩndũ kĩ thayũ' ũndũnĩ ũsu na maũndũnĩ angĩ. (Sav. 145:16) Kwĩtanĩthya na kũthyũmũa nĩ maũndũ ma vata, ĩndĩ tũtanĩaa mũno maũndũ asu ethĩwa twĩamba kwĩka kwenda kwa Yeova mbee. Ũu now'o kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ twĩ Nthĩ Nzaũ. Kwoou nĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ mũno ũkethĩa nĩtweemanyĩsya kwĩtanĩthya ĩvinda yĩla yaĩle na tũyĩendeea kũmantha Ũsumbĩ mbee na kũsũanĩa mũno moathimo ala Yeova ũtũnengete yu.—Mt. 6:33.
18. Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtwĩyũmbanĩsye kwĩkala Nthĩ Nzaũ tene na tene?
18 Nthĩnĩ wa Nthĩ Nzaũ tũkeethĩwa na ũtanu mwingĩ tũtaawona ĩvinda o na yĩva. Ekai ĩndĩ twonany'e vyũ twĩ na wendi wa kũkwata ũla thayũ wa w'o kwa kwĩyũmbanĩsya thayũ ũsu ũmũnthĩ. Na ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kwĩthĩwa na nguma ila Yeova ũtũmanyĩasya, na kũtanĩa mũno wĩa ũla tũnengetwe wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ twĩ na kĩthito. O na ekai kũmũthaitha Yeova kwĩthĩwe ne kw'o ũndũ ũla ũtũeteae ũtanu mwingĩ vyũ. Na mũthya nũndũ nĩtũĩkĩĩte vyũ mawatho ma Yeova, ekai tũtw'e kwĩkala ta andũ meteele kwĩsa kũtũa nthĩ nzaũ!
^ kal. 14 Sisya ĩvuku Maswali Ambayo Vijana Huuliza—Majibu Yafanyayo Kazi, Ĩvu. 2, ĩth. 311-318.

translation:
"[Teaching] is good, . . . for they have an aim to be wealthy and to be generous, and they are generous."—1 TIM. 6:18, 19.
NOTES: 43, 40
1, 2. (a) How can we show that we value the things God considers important? (Consider the examples.) (b) What motivates people to pursue wealth?
"GENEROSITY." Many people today are determined to become rich and often think about how to acquire wealth. The apostle Paul contrasted "wealth" and "generosity" to help them see the difference. (Read 1 Timothy 6:12, 19.) Let us examine what generosity involves, what benefits it brings, and why it is so important. And let us consider how we can demonstrate generosity daily, whether by helping someone who is sick or disabled, or by sharing what we have with others. (Isa. 35:5, 6) Demonstrating such generosity strengthens our empathy for fellow humans, including those who may be suffering or grieving, and even those who seem to have everything! (John 5:28, 29; Luke 24:15) And it gives us opportunities to speak about our faith to scientists, doctors, neighbors, or anyone else.
2 But how can we show generosity in practical ways, especially when doing so might require effort on our part? One way is to remember that whatever we give up pales in comparison to what Jehovah has given us and continues to defend his great name! (Matt. 6:9, 10) How, then, can we cultivate an appreciation for Jehovah's generosity toward us and toward others? This will motivate us to use our resources to honor him, knowing that he notices and values our efforts.—Ps. 73:28; Jas. 4:8.
3 What will help us to be generous?
3 We need to have the right attitude, the one Jesus described when he said: "With God nothing is impossible." (Matt. 19:25, 26) Realistically, we may face challenges and find it difficult to remain generous, especially during times of economic hardship. However, we should never allow ourselves to become preoccupied with material possessions or to feel that we cannot afford to be generous. Can we strengthen our resolve to be generous despite such difficulties?
HOW WE CAN BE GENEROUS
4. Let us now examine some specific ways we can be generous.
4 Can we be generous even when facing financial constraints? Consider this illustration: A person wants to help others, but feels unable to do so. Can you be generous in some way anyway? Perhaps you can offer encouragement to others. Or you might share what little you have. For example, you could offer to help someone with a chore. Ask yourself, 'What can I do?' If you are willing to put forth effort, you will find ways to help others. So, let us strive to be generous in whatever way we can, even if it means making sacrifices. Here are some things we can do to cultivate generosity.
5, 6. How can we show appreciation for Jehovah's organization and its efforts to assist us spiritually?
5 Spiritual wealth is truly a precious gift from God. Appreciating it brings joy and satisfaction. Why? Because spiritual wealth is not affected by Satan and his wicked system. Some people may feel they deserve good things because of their hard work and abilities, but does that entitle them to special favor from God? No, true Christians understand that blessings come from God, through Jesus Christ, and are earned through obedience. (Jer. 10:23) Let us therefore continue to value the privilege of enjoying Jehovah's generous provision!
6 Genuine appreciation motivates us to remain loyal to Jehovah, to make known His name, to correct those who misrepresent Him, and to obey all that Jehovah asks of us. But how can we show that we appreciate what He provides? We should not take our privileges for granted, but rather cherish them and use them zealously to serve others. How much more so should this be true when considering the loving support provided by our brothers! Indeed, this is vital, for it helps us maintain a positive attitude and strengthens our bond with fellow worshippers of Jehovah. So let us always strive to deepen our love for one another and continue to seek ways to prove ourselves worthy of Jehovah's continued blessing.
7, 8. (a) How can we demonstrate our gratitude for what we have? (b) What practical steps did some Christians take? (c) What will help us to stay focused on what matters most?
7 Demonstrating genuine appreciation for the loving support of our brothers does not mean simply being thankful for their assistance. It also means cooperating fully with them and showing consideration for their feelings. For example, when we are assigned to work alongside others, we can readily offer encouragement and support, helping them to remain zealous in the ministry. (Read Hebrews 13:17.) The Israelites, for instance, were willing to share the burdens of those who had fallen behind during their journey. (Num. 26:52-56; Josh. 14:1, 2) Similarly, each of us should be ready to assist our brothers whenever possible. Thus, we can continue to enjoy a close relationship with Jehovah and strengthen our determination to please Him and express our gratitude for his provisions.
8 How wonderful it is to benefit from God's provision! By appreciating what we receive from the worldwide brotherhood of Jehovah's Witnesses, we strengthen our bonds with one another and show our gratitude for the privileges we have. But what about when we face difficulties or trials? Consider the American Bethelites, who were given an assignment that involved extensive traveling. They maintained a positive attitude despite the challenges they faced. And there are many others who willingly accept assignments that require them to go to remote areas or deal with difficult circumstances. To help us maintain this spirit, let us always remember to thank God for His blessings, appreciate His care for us, and focus on what we can do. We can then continue to enjoy a close relationship with Him and experience abundant joy and satisfaction.—Ps. 10:22. But what if trials seem overwhelming? We can be confident that as we draw near to God, He will give us strength to endure until we reach our goal. So let us never hesitate to seek His guidance and support, whether through prayer or by asking experienced elders for advice. Let us also remember that a cheerful disposition can be contagious.—Neh. 8:10.
9, 10. (a) What can help us to remain positive when facing trials? (b) Can we ever be certain that our trials will end?
9 When we are experiencing trials, it is important to focus on the good things in life and to be grateful for the blessings we have received. For example, we may notice kind acts from brothers and sisters, even those who are having their own problems. It is helpful to dwell on such examples and to imitate their positive attitude. Should we simply wait passively for things to improve, or should we actively strive to maintain a positive outlook? (Prov. 12:15) The more we express appreciation for the spiritual provisions Jehovah makes, the better equipped we will be to cope with trials.—Matt. 7:8.
10 One way to strengthen our resolve to remain positive is to focus on what we can do to help others. How can we show concern for those who are struggling spiritually? We can demonstrate empathy and offer encouragement, while also reminding them of the hope we have. By doing so, we will not only comfort them but also strengthen our own faith.—Phil. 4:18; John 16:12.
11. Does Jehovah expect us to isolate ourselves from others when facing difficulties, and how can he help us to avoid this trap?
11 Another factor that can help us to remain positive is to continue associating with others. In the Yearbooks of Jehovah's Witnesses, there are often accounts of individuals who benefited greatly from the support of their friends. The question might arise, 'Should we associate with just anyone?' We can seek out those who are exemplary and associate closely with them, being careful about the company we keep.—Read Colossians 3:12-14.
12. Consider how our choice of associates affects us and our spiritual health.
12 When we remain positive, we are more likely to maintain a good routine and pursue activities that please Jehovah. This, in turn, helps us to stay busy and productive. With Jehovah's help, we can cultivate a positive outlook and find joy in serving him. Furthermore, we can strive to be kind and considerate toward others, which will further enhance our happiness. And if we encounter situations that discourage us, we can remind ourselves of the blessings we already enjoy and focus on "the things that are unseen."—2 Cor. 4:18; 11:1. Also, we should not dwell on negative experiences or allow ourselves to become overly concerned about minor imperfections. Rather, let us continue to apply ourselves zealously to the ministry, confident that God will bless our efforts.
STRENGTHEN YOUR RESOLVE TO REMAIN POSITIVE
13. What practical steps can we take to stay positive?
13 One way to strengthen our resolve is to meditate on the reasons why we want to remain positive. We may also benefit from spending time with those who have a positive attitude, and we can learn from their example. (Prov. 13:20) Showing appreciation for what we have can also help us to focus on the good things in life. (Matt. 5:3) To honor Jehovah is to appreciate his gifts, and we can show our gratitude by doing so. (Ps. 37:4) By continuing to honor Jehovah and appreciating his gifts, we can cultivate a spirit of contentment and avoid becoming preoccupied with material possessions.—Read Matthew 6:19-21.
14. How can the principles found in God's Word help those who struggle to stay positive?
14 How can Bible principles help us to maintain a positive outlook? One thing that can help us is to focus on what the Bible says about how to view life. Are you making a conscious effort to put Jehovah first in your life? Do you regularly read and meditate on scriptures that highlight the importance of spiritual values and apply them to your daily living? * Many have found that years of studying the Bible has strengthened their faith. By worshipping God and gaining knowledge of his Word, you will be able to make decisions that will help you to stay positive.
15. What benefits does true worship offer?
15 Does true worship offer practical benefits? Yes, true worship helps us to find meaning in life. But we need to be diligent and not give up. Or we may lose our zeal and fail to appreciate the full value of Bible teachings. And we need to be determined to continue reading, meditating, and applying information from the Bible. Also, we need to remember that there are things that can hinder us. The important thing to remember is this: Focusing on what the Bible teaches strengthens our desire to worship Jehovah, and this helps us to avoid being discouraged and to remain positive.
LET US BE DETERMINED!
16. Why is worshipping Jehovah so vital?
16 How can we show that we are determined to remain positive, even when facing difficulties? It is not by simply pretending to be happy. Worshipping Jehovah is the most important thing a person can do to be truly satisfied. We worship Jehovah because we love him and want to please him, even if we experience great trials. If we stay close to him through prayer and study, we will always have good reason to rejoice. Being approved by Jehovah and having his friendship is far more valuable than anything else we might possess. (Read Psalm 63:1-3.) So let us never take for granted the privilege of worshipping Jehovah and enjoying his favor. Why? Because we are determined! And some of our brothers and sisters have remained faithful for many years, and they have found that worshipping Jehovah continues to help them to remain joyful.—Ps. 1:1-3; Isa. 58:13, 14.
17. How can we make sure that our efforts to do what is right are not in vain?
17 To remain steadfast and continue doing what is right, we need to focus on the reasons why we serve God. Why should we do this? Because Jehovah wants us to enjoy life, and he helps us to do so. (Eccl. 2:24) Moreover, Jehovah "pays attention to the desire of each creature." (Ps. 145:16) Remaining steadfast and praying regularly are vital things, and they remind us to trust in Jehovah completely. This is also how we show appreciation for everything that Jehovah does for us. So it is wise to remember that remaining steadfast requires effort and that we must keep seeking God's guidance.—Matt. 6:33.
18. What can we do to strengthen our determination to remain loyal to Jehovah forever?
18 We can strengthen our determination to remain loyal to Jehovah by focusing on the blessings we already have and those we will receive in the future. It is good to reflect on the ways in which Jehovah has blessed us and to appreciate his generosity. And we can be sure that Jehovah will support us, help us to make progress, and enable us to live up to our dedication. Also, when we meditate on Jehovah's qualities, we will be more determined to remain faithful despite difficulties. But most importantly, let us imitate the faith of young people who are zealous in their service!
^ kal. 14 See the book Questions Young People Ask—Answers That Work, vol. 2, pp. 311-318.

text:
"Mũkĩmwiĩa [Yeova] kwĩmakĩa kwenyu kw'onthe, nũndũ nĩwe ũmũsũvĩaa."—1 VET. 5:7.
MBATHI: 23, 38
1, 2. (a) Nĩkĩ tũtaĩle kũseng'a ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mawĩmakĩo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
MAVINDA aa tũtwĩe me mathĩna maingĩ mũno. Satani, ũla nĩwe Ndevili, nĩ mũthilĩku mũno na "angangaa kũũ na kũũ ta mũnyambũ ũkũluma, aimantha mũndũ aye." (1 Vet. 5:8; Ũvu. 12:17) Kwoou, ithyĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai tũyaĩle kũseng'a ĩla twakwatwa nĩ mathĩna na twambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa. O na athũkũmi aĩkĩĩku ma tene ta Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti no mesaa 'kũthĩnany'a na mosũanĩo moo.' (Sav. 13:2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) O na syoka ũlilikane kana Mũtũmwa Vaulo 'nĩwaũũyĩaa makanisa onthe.' (2 Ako. 11:28) Ĩndĩ ithyĩ tũtonya kwĩka ata ĩla twaemeewa nĩ mawĩmakĩo?
2 Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ nĩwatethisye athũkũmi make ma tene, na o naitũ nũtũtethasya tũusye ĩla twĩmakĩĩte nũndũ wa thĩna twĩ naw'o. Nĩkyo Mbivilia ĩtwĩkĩĩte vinya ĩkatwĩa: "Mũkĩmwiĩa kwĩmakĩa kwenyu kw'onthe, nũndũ nĩwe ũmũsũvĩaa." (1 Vet. 5:7) Ĩndĩ we ũtonya kũmwiĩa Ngai kwĩmakĩa kwaku ata? Ethĩwa nĩtũkwĩmakĩa, ekai twone maũndũ ana matonya kũtũtetheesya. Ũndũ wa mbee nĩ kũmwonoesya Yeova ngoo yaku, wa kelĩ nĩ kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai na kũmĩvindĩĩsya, wa katatũ nĩ kũmũvoya Yeova aũne veva mũtheu, na wa kana nĩ kũtavya mũndũ ũmũĩkĩĩe thĩna waku. Ĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ asu me ana, sisya nĩ kyaũ ũtonya kwosa vo kĩkaũtethya.
"MWAŨĨE YEOVA MŨIO WAKU"
3. Mboya ĩtonya kũũtetheesya ata 'ũmwaũĩe Yeova mũio waku'?
3 Ũndũ wa mbee tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kũmũvoya Yeova na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo. Ĩla weeyĩthĩa ũndũnĩ ũtonya kũtuma wĩmakĩa, wĩkala na kĩũũyũ, na kwĩw'a ũte mwĩanĩe, mũtulũĩle Ĩthe waku wa ĩtunĩ ngoo yaku nũndũ nũtwendete. Mũandĩki wa Savuli, Ndaviti, amwĩsũvie Yeova amwĩa: "Tea matũ wĩw'e mboya yakwa, ame Ngai." Na ĩndĩ Savulinĩ o ĩsu asyokie asya: "Mwaũĩe Yeova mũio waku, nake akakũtw'ĩĩka." (Sav. 55:1, 22) Ethĩwa nĩwĩkĩte kyonthe kĩla ũtonya ũmine thĩna mũna, mboya nĩyo ĩtonya kũũtethya mũno kwĩ kwĩmakĩa. Ĩndĩ mboya ĩtonya kũũtetheesya ata ndũkaemeewe nĩ woo na mosũanĩo maingĩ?—Sav. 94:18, 19.
4. Nĩkĩ mboya nĩ ya vata mũno ĩla tũkwĩmakĩa?
4 Soma Avilivi 4:6, 7. Yeova nũtonya kũtũsũngĩa ĩla twathetheesya kũmwĩsũva na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo kuma ngoonĩ atũtetheesye. Atũsũngĩaa ata? Atũsũngĩaa kwa kũtũtetheesya tũusye na kĩu kĩtumaa ilĩko sitũ na ngoo sitũ ithyũmũa. Andũ aingĩ no makũsĩĩe kana nĩmeyoneete ũndũ ũsu. Andũ ta asu maĩ na thĩna watumaa memakĩa mũno na mekala na wia mwingĩ, ĩndĩ Ngai nĩwamanengie mũuo mwingĩ mataĩ mesa kũwumya vandũ vangĩ. Yeova nũtonya kũũtetheesya kwa nzĩa o ta ĩsu. "Mũuo wa Ngai" nũtonya kũkĩlya vinya thĩna o na wĩva ũla ũtonya kũũkwata. Kwoou ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana Yeova e tei na ndaema kwĩanĩsya watho ũũ wake: "Ndũkateve, nũndũ nyie nĩ Ngai waku; ngakwĩkĩa vinya; ĩĩ, ngakũtethya."—Isa. 41:10.
NDETO YA NGAI NO ĨTŨNENGE MŨUO WA KĨLĨKO
5. Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ata twĩthĩwe na mũuo wa kĩlĩko?
5 Ũndũ wa kelĩ tũtonya kwĩka tũkakwata mũuo wa kĩlĩko nĩ kũsoma Mbivilia na kũvindĩĩsya kĩla twasoma. Nĩkĩ ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa vata? Mbivilia yĩ na ũtao mũseo mũno ũtonya ũkũtethya ndũkemakĩe, kana ethĩwa nĩwĩmakĩĩte ũtao ũsu no ũũtethye ũolange mesilya kana ũmanye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ũmine mesilya ala meũtuma wĩmakĩa. Ndũkese kũlwa kana kĩla kĩtumaa Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũtethya na ĩtũnenga vinya nĩ kana ũĩ ũla wĩ vo wumĩte kwa Mũmbi mwene. Ũkakwata vinya mwingĩ mũno ethĩwa kĩla mũthenya ũkasũanĩaa woni wa Ngai na ũkavindĩĩasya ũndũ ũtonya kũtũmĩa nesa ũtao ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Yeova oonanisye nesa kana kũsoma Ndeto yake nĩkũtumaa mũndũ ethĩwa na "vinya na ũkũmbaũ mũnene" na ekala 'ateũkĩa na kũteva.'—Yos. 1:7-9.
6. Ndeto sya Yesũ itonya kũũtetheesya ata?
6 Ndetonĩ ya Ngai ve ndeto sya kũkiakisya syaneeniwe nĩ Yesũ. Ndeto syake na momanyĩsyo make nĩmeekĩaa ethukĩĩsya make vinya. Makomano nĩmaendaa vala ũĩ nũndũ nĩwathũmũasya ngoo ila syaĩ na kĩũũyũ, akalũlũmĩlya ala onzu, na akakiakisya ala makw'ĩte ngoo. (Soma Mathayo 11:28-30.) Nũndũ nĩwendete andũ nĩwathĩnĩkĩaa mavata moo ma kĩ-veva, ma kĩ-mwĩĩ, na ma ngoonĩ. (Mko. 6:30-32) O na ũmũnthĩ Yesũ no ũtũtw'ĩĩkaa o tondũ wathanie. Atũtw'ĩĩkaa o tondũ watw'ĩĩkaa atũmwa make ala waendanasya namo. Ĩndĩ ti nginya wĩthĩwe vala Yesũ ũĩ nĩ kana aũtethye. O na kau yu nĩ Mũsumbĩ ĩtunĩ, e tei o ũla waĩ naw'o na kũvika yu nũtwĩw'ĩaa tei. Kwoou nũndũ Yesũ e tei, ĩla wesa kwambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa lilikana kana nũtonya 'kũũtetheesya' na ekaa ũu "ĩvinda [yĩu wĩ na] vata." Vate nzika, ndeto sya Yesũ nitonya kũũtetheesya ũmĩanĩsye na thĩna na nitonya kũũnenga wĩkwatyo na ũkũmbaũ.—Aevl. 2:17, 18; 4:16.
VEVA WA NGAI NŨTUMAA TWĨTHĨWA NA NGUMA NZEO
7. Ũkatethekaa ata ĩla Ngai waũsũngĩa wamwĩtya veva mũtheu?
7 Yesũ nĩwatwathie kana Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ ndakaema kũnenga veva mũtheu ala mamwĩtasya. (Luka 11:10-13) Na kwoou kĩu nĩkyo kĩndũ kya katatũ na kya vata mũno kĩla kĩtũtetheeasya tũikemakĩe mũno. Veva mũtheu ũtũtetheeasya kwĩthĩwa na ũla ũsyao wa veva. Ũsyao ũsu nĩ nguma nzeo ila itũtetheeasya twĩyĩelekany'e na ũla Ngai mwene vinya w'onthe. (Soma Akalatia 5:22, 23; Ako. 3:10) O ũndũ waendeea kũtata wĩthĩwe na ũsyao ũsu wa veva, now'o ngwatanĩo yaku na ala angĩ yĩendeeaa kũlũlũmĩla. Naku weethĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na ala angĩ, ti laisi kwĩsa kwĩthĩa wĩ na mathĩna namo ũndũ wambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa. Kwamba kũsũanĩa kwa ũkuvĩ ũndũ ũsyao wa veva ũtonya kũũtetheesya.
8-12. Ũsyao wa veva ũtonya kũũtetheesya ata?
8 "Wendo, ũtanu, mũuo." Wanenga ala angĩ ndaĩa nũtonya kwĩthĩa kana o naku mwene nĩwavũthĩwa nĩ ũito ũla wĩ naw'o ngoonĩ. Vaendaa ũu ata? Kwĩthĩwa na wendano wa ana-a-asa, wendo mũuu, na kũnenga ala angĩ ndaĩa nĩkũtonya kũkwathũkanĩsya na mathĩna matonya kũtuma wambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa.—Alo. 12:10.
9 "Wũmĩĩsyo, kwĩka angĩ nesa, ũseo." Wenda kwĩkalany'a nesa na angĩ nĩwaĩle kũatĩĩa mwĩao ũũ: "Mwĩthĩwe mũkyaĩlan'ya ene kwa ene, mũkĩw'anĩa tei, mũkĩekanĩa inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ." (Aev. 4:32) Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtonya kũkwathũkanĩsya na mathĩna matonya kũtuma wambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa. O na ĩngĩ kwĩthĩwa na nguma isu nĩũkũtetheesya ũmanye ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ĩla mathĩna mesa kumĩla nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa twĩ andũ me na naĩ.
10 "Kĩthito [kana, mũĩkĩĩo]." Kwĩmakĩa kwingĩ ũmũnthĩ kũetawe nĩ kũthelelwa kana wendi wa mbesa na malĩ. (Nth. 18:11) Ĩndĩ ethĩwa twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova no atũsũvĩe, tũikathĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa maũndũ asu. Ũu ũtonyeka ata? Mũtũmwa Vaulo atwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Ĩanĩwai nĩ syĩndũ ila mwĩ nasyo." Kwĩka ũu nĩkũtũtetheeasya tũikemakĩe mũno. Vaulo asyokie asya: "We mwene [Ngai] nĩwaisye, Ndikakũnyivĩa o na ata, na ndikakũtia o na ĩndĩĩ. Kwondũ wa ũu nĩtũkwasya na ũnyiau, Mwĩaĩi nĩ mũtetheesya wakwa; ndikakĩa: Mũndũ akambĩka ata?"—Aevl. 13:5, 6.
11 "Ũuu, wĩting'o." Sũanĩa ũndũ ũtonya kũtetheka mũno wĩana weethĩwa na nguma isu. Nguma isu nitonya kũũtethya ndũkaneene ndeto kana wĩke ũndũ ũsyoke ũkũetee mathĩna we mwene. O na ũkatetheka mũno weevathana na "ũũ, na ũthilĩku, na ũthatu, na ĩteta, na moumano."—Aev. 4:31.
12 Ethĩwa ndwĩnyivĩtye, ve vinya mũno kũĩkĩĩa "kw'oko kwa Ngai kwĩ na vinya" na ve vinya 'ũmwiĩe kwĩmakĩa kwaku kw'onthe.' (1 Vet. 5:6, 7) Ĩndĩ weethĩwa na wĩnyivyo ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kwendwa nĩ Ngai na kũtetheew'a nĩwe. (Mika 6:8) Kwĩkala twĩsĩ nesa kĩla tũtonya kwĩanĩsya na kĩla tũtatonya kwĩanĩsya na vinya witũ kana ilĩko sitũ, na kũmanya kĩla tũtonya kũmĩĩsya na kĩla tũtatonya kũmĩĩsya, kũkatũtetheeasya tũikaemeewe nĩ mawĩmakĩo nũndũ kĩla ĩvinda tũkeethĩawa tũmwĩkwatĩtye Ngai.
"MŨIKEMAKĨE"
13. Yesũ endaa kwasya ata ĩla waisye: "Mũikemakĩe"?
13 Ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 6:34 (soma), Yesũ atũnengie ũtao ũũ wa vata mũno: "Mũikemakĩe." Ĩndĩ ũtao ũsu nũtonya kwoneka ta wĩ vinya kũatĩĩa. We Yesũ endaa kwasya ata ĩla waisye: "Mũikemakĩe"? Ndethĩwa asasya atĩ mũthũkũmi wa Ngai ndakesa kwĩmakĩa thayũnĩ wake w'onthe. Lilikana kana nĩtwoona ve mavinda Ndaviti na Vaulo meemakĩaa. Ĩndĩ Yesũ atetheeasya amanyĩw'a make makwatye kana kwĩmakĩa vate kĩtumi kĩseo kana kwĩmakĩa mũno kũiminaa mathĩna. Kĩla mũthenya wĩ mathĩna maw'o, na kwoou Mũklĩsto ndaĩle kwĩnosya na mesilya ma maũndũ mavĩtie, kana ma maũndũ mataaĩsa kũvika, nake no ũkuĩte mathĩna ma ũmũnthĩ. Ũtao ũsu wa Yesũ ũtonya kũũtetheesya ata ndũkeyĩũmĩsye na mawĩmakĩo maingĩ?
14. Ũtonya kwĩka ata ndũkaũmĩw'e nĩ mesilya ma maũndũ weekie tene?
14 Mavinda amwe mũndũ nũtonya kwĩmakĩa nũndũ wa maũndũ weekie tene. Nũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩyĩandũa nũndũ wa ũndũ weekie ĩvinda ĩvĩtu, o na no ethĩwe awĩkie myaka mingĩ mĩvĩtu. Mavinda amwe Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti eew'aa mavĩtyo make ta "mang'okele mũtwenĩ" wake. Aisye: "Nĩlumĩte kwondũ wa kũlea kũusya kwa ngoo yakwa." (Sav. 38:3, 4, 8, 18) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva wa ũĩ Ndaviti waaĩle kwĩka? We eekie ata? Nĩweethĩiwe na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana Yeova nũkũmwĩw'ĩa tei na aimũekea. Aisye ũũ ate na nzika nongi: "Kũathimwa nĩ mũndũ ũla ũekewe ĩvĩtyo yake."—Soma Savuli 32:1-3, 5.
15. (a) Nĩkĩ ũtaĩle kwĩmakĩa mũno nũndũ wa mathĩna ma ũmũnthĩ? (b) Ũtonya kwĩka ata ndũkemakĩe mũno? (Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Nzĩa Imwe sya Kũolanga Mawĩmakĩo.")
15 Ve mavinda ũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa nũndũ wa mathĩna ma ũmũnthĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Ndaviti aiandĩka Savuli ya 55 nĩwathĩnĩkaa ayona ta ũtonya kũawa. (Sav. 55:2-5) Ĩndĩ ndaaĩtĩkĩlya thĩna ũsu waĩ naw'o ngoonĩ ũtume aeka kũmwĩkwatya Yeova. Ndaviti nĩwavoyie Ngai mũno amũtetheesye thĩnanĩ ũsu waĩ naw'o, ĩndĩ ndaaekela vau. Nĩwoosie matambya ala waĩ atonya kwosa akĩlye vinya thĩna ũla watumaa athĩnĩka. (2 Sam. 15:30-34) Ve kĩndũ ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya vau. Vandũ va kwĩtĩkĩlya mawĩmakĩo maũkĩlye vinya, ĩkĩa kĩthito kĩla ũtonya ũkĩlye vinya thĩna ũla wĩ naw'o na ĩndĩ ũiekea Yeova maũndũ onthe amathĩnĩkĩe, na ũyĩka ũu ũte nzika nake.
16. Kũvindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũalyũlo wa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai kũtonya kũlũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo waku ata?
16 Mũklĩsto nũtonya kwambĩĩa kwĩmakĩa vate kĩtumi kĩseo ethĩwa esũanĩa mathĩna ala ũkwona ta matonya ũmũkwata ũnĩ. Ĩndĩ vai vata wa kwĩmakĩa nũndũ wa maũndũ o na ũtamesĩ. Nĩkĩ ũtaĩle kwĩka ũu? Nũndũ mavinda maingĩ maũndũ nĩmatonya kũema kwĩthĩwa me mathũku tondũ tũnamasũanĩaa. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana vai ũndũ ũthonokete vinya wa Ngai ũla ũtwĩĩte tũmwiĩe kwĩmakĩa kwitũ kw'onthe. Ũalyũlo wa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai ũsu nĩ, "Nũtw'ĩkĩthasya." (Kuma 3:14, NWT) Ũalyũlo ũsu ũtũĩkĩĩthasya kana Ngai e ũtonyi wa kũĩkĩĩthya kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa athũkũmi make nĩkyeanĩw'a. Kwoou, ĩkala ũte na nzika o na imwe kana Ngai nũtonya kũathima ala mamũthũkũmaa me aĩkĩĩku na akamatetheesya ĩla me na mawĩmakĩo, methĩwe meĩmakĩa nũndũ wa maũndũ mavĩtu, maũndũ ma ũmũnthĩ, kana meĩmakĩa nũndũ wa ũnĩ.
NEENA NA MŨNDŨ ŨMŨĨKĨĨE
17, 18. Kũneena na angĩ kũtonya kũũtetheesya ata ndũkemakĩe mũno?
17 Ũndũ wa kana ũtonya kũũtetheesya ndũkemakĩe mũno nĩ kũmantha mũndũ ũmũĩkĩĩe ũmũelesye kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ. Mũndũ ũsu no ethĩwe ne ũla ũtwaanĩte nake, kana mũnyanyau mwĩ ndũũ mũno, kana o mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi, na no aũtetheesye wĩkuũe nesa thĩna ũla ũũtuma wĩmakĩa. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Kĩmako ngoonĩ ya mũndũ nĩkĩminamasya; ĩndĩ ndeto nzeo nĩmĩtanasya." (Nth. 12:25) Wamantha mũndũ ũmũtavye kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ ũteũmũvithany'a kĩndũ, kĩu no kĩũtetheesye mũno ũelewe thĩna waku nesanga, na ũimanya ĩtambya yĩla ũtonya kwosa. Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Vala vate ũtao, maũndũ ala masũanĩĩtwe kwĩkwa nĩmanangĩkaa; ĩndĩ vala ve wingĩ wa atai nĩmalũlũmĩlaw'a."—Nth. 15:22.
18 O na ĩngĩ, kĩla kyumwa ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi, Yeova nũtũtetheeasya tũmanye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka ethĩwa twĩ thĩnanĩ ũũtuma twĩmakĩa. Ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ asu nĩtũkomanaa na Aklĩsto endwa, ala matwendete na methĩawa na wendi wa kũthangaany'a. (Aevl. 10:24, 25) Ĩla 'twakiakiany'a' na ana-a-asa nĩtũkwataa vinya, na ũyĩthĩa ti laisi tũemeewe nĩ mathĩna o na meva ala matonya kũtuma twĩmakĩa.—Alo. 1:12.
NGWATANĨO YAKU NA NGAI NĨYO ŨTETHYO ŨLA MŨNENE
19. Nĩkĩ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana ngwatanĩo yaku na Ngai no ĩũnenge vinya?
19 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ mũtumĩa ũmwe wa kĩkundi kuma nthĩ ya Canada weemanyĩisye nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ waĩlĩte kũmwaũĩa Yeova thĩna wake. Mũtumĩa ũsu nĩ mwalimũ wa sukulu na nĩ mũtai wa syana na wĩa ũsu ũmũĩsaa mũtwe mũno. O na ĩngĩ ethĩĩtwe ayũmĩanĩsya na ũwau ũtumaa emakĩa mũno. Nĩ kyaũ kĩmũtethetye? Aeleetye akasya, "Mbee wa ũndũ o na wĩva, nĩnonete kana kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yakwa na Yeova nĩkũnengae vinya ũla mũnene vyũ wa kũmĩanĩsya na mawĩmakĩo makwa. Ũtethyo ũla anyanyawa ma w'o na ana-a-asa manengae ĩvinda ya thĩna nĩ wa vata. Nĩnĩeleasya kĩveti kyakwa maũndũ ala me ngoonĩ ndeũkĩvitha. O na ndiwetekya ũndũ atumĩa ala angĩ na mũsyaĩĩsya witũ wa mũthyũlũlũko mandetheetye kwonaa maũndũ kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana nĩnamanthie ũiiti, neeka moalyũku ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ndũmĩaa ĩvinda yakwa, na namantha mwanya wa kũthyũmũaa na kwĩka masoesi. Na kwoou kavola kwa kavola nĩnĩekete kwĩmakĩa ũndũ nemakĩaa tene. Ĩla nakwatwa nĩ maũndũ mathonokete ũmanyi wakwa, nĩmaiaa mokonĩ ma Yeova."
20. (a) Tũtonya kũmwiĩa Ngai mawĩmakĩo maitũ ata? (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
20 Kwa ũkuvĩ, nĩtwamanya vata wa kũmwiĩa Ngai kwĩmakĩa kwitũ kwa kũmũvoya kuma ngoonĩ na kwa kũsomaa Ndeto yake na kũmĩvindĩĩsya. O na nĩtwoona vata wa kwĩthĩwa na ũsyao wa veva wa Ngai, vata wa kũelesya ala tũmaĩkĩĩte kĩla kĩũtũmakya, na vata wa kũthi maũmbanonĩ maitũ ala matumaa twĩkĩwa vinya nĩ Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩũtũmanyĩsya ũndũ Yeova ũtwĩkĩĩte vinya kwa kũtwatha ĩtuvi.—Aevl. 11:6.

translation:
"Jehovah [Yeova] cares for all of you, so be anxious for nothing."—1 PET. 5:7.
FOOTNOTES: 23, 38
1, 2. (a) Why should we care when we face trials? (Consider the example mentioned.) (b) What will help us to remain steadfast?
SATAN provides us with many challenges. Satan, who is the Devil, is very active and "walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour," (1 Pet. 5:8; Rev. 12:17) Of course, God's loyal servants want to care when they face challenges and to trust in Jehovah. And some faithful ones, like King David, at times felt 'weakened because of the reproach.' (Ps. 13:2, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) And once Paul the apostle was 'greatly distressed.' (2 Cor. 11:28) So, can we care even when we are overwhelmed by anxiety?
2 Our loving Father does comfort his loyal servants, and often we need to care about what troubles us and talk about it. The Bible tells us why: "Cares for all of you, so be anxious for nothing." (1 Pet. 5:7) How can you care for Jehovah about something that worries you? Well, caring means that we allow him to carry our burden, and this includes reading God's Word and meditating on it, praying regularly to Jehovah, and also speaking to a mature Christian friend. We will discuss more about this shortly, but first let us see how we can identify what causes our anxiety.
"TELL JEHOVAH YOUR ANXIETY"
3 How can you practically 'tell Jehovah your anxiety'?
3 One way we can do this is by talking to Jehovah in prayer. But sometimes it may be hard to put into words what bothers you, yet when you pray, remember that Jehovah understands your feelings. King David told Jehovah in prayer: "Pour out your heart before him; God is your refuge." And David himself prayed: "Tell Jehovah your anxiety, and he will sustain you." (Ps. 55:1, 22) So whatever you are going through, do not hesitate to tell Jehovah everything that concerns you, because prayer can help you cope with problems. What practical steps can you take to deal with anxiety?—Ps. 94:18, 19.
4 Why is prayer such an effective way to cope with anxiety?
4 Read Proverbs 4:6, 7. Jehovah can help us to cope when we confide in him and ask for his guidance. How does he help us? He helps us by reminding us of truths from his Word that reassure us. Many people have found comfort in doing so. Some individuals who were once very anxious now find they can face life with more confidence, and they feel closer to God. Jehovah can also help us in unexpected ways. The expression "God's peace" refers to inner tranquility and a sense of security. It is something that surpasses anything this world can offer. Consider how Jehovah has helped others in similar situations: "Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not look around anxiously, for I am your God."—Isa. 41:10.
GOD'S PURPOSE AND FINDING INNER PEACE
5 Can God's purpose help us to cope with anxiety?
5 One way we can strengthen our faith and find inner peace is by reading the Bible regularly and meditating on what we read. But is this practical? The Bible offers sound advice that can help us deal with problems, or it shows us how others successfully faced similar challenges. By applying those principles, we can learn to think calmly and make wise decisions. Remember that everything God allows to happen ultimately serves a loving purpose. As you apply what you learn from God's Word, you will gain greater appreciation for his qualities and be able to trust in him more fully. Jehovah wants us to benefit from reading his Word, helping us to experience "peace and great prosperity" and to remain 'courageous and strong.'—Josh. 1:7-9.
6 Can Jesus' example help us to cope?
6 God's Law reflects Jesus' personality. His laws and teachings reveal his love. He invites everyone who is tired and burdened to come to him, and he refreshes and strengthens them. (Read Matthew 11:28-30.) He understands the pressures people face—emotional distress, financial worries, and health concerns. (Mark 6:30-32) And like Jesus, we can show empathy when others are struggling. We can empathize because we have been sent out as messengers to comfort others. In fact, we should strive to imitate Jesus in all that he did. It may seem difficult to live up to his standard, but remember that Jehovah is patient, and he will help us if we ask him. So don't give up trying to become more like Jesus. Instead, focus on making small improvements, knowing that you can 'keep progressing' and experiencing "everlasting life."—Acts 2:17, 18; 4:16.
GOD'S LOVE MOTIVATES US TO HELP OTHERS
7. What motivates Jehovah to extend loving-kindness to imperfect humans?
7 Jesus showed that Jehovah wants to forgive our sins and help us improve. (Luke 11:10-13) And that is why it is so important that we forgive others. Forgiveness helps us maintain peace with those around us. Loving-kindness moves us to be considerate and compassionate, reflecting Jehovah's own feelings toward us. (Read Titus 3:4, 5; Acts 3:10) But what if someone has deeply hurt you? It is understandable to feel angry and resentful. However, holding onto such negative emotions will only cause you further pain. By forgiving, you can experience inner healing. Remember that extending loving-kindness does not mean condoning wrong behavior.
8-12. How can loving-kindness be expressed?
8 "Love, patience, thoughtfulness." These qualities enable us to deal with others kindly, even when they may not deserve it. Why is this important? Because love, patience, and thoughtfulness help us to avoid getting carried away by anger and resentment.—Col. 3:10.
9 "Generosity, quick to assist, forgiving." Be willing to share what you have with others and say things like: "I am happy to help you," "I will gladly do that," and "I appreciate your kindness." (Eph. 4:32) Generosity helps us to avoid getting carried away by selfishness and greed. Also, remember that being humble allows us to recognize our own imperfections and to be more understanding toward others.
10 "Caution [or, discernment]." A wise person is careful about his health and possessions. (Prov. 18:11) If we trust in Jehovah and ask him for guidance, we can make good decisions in all aspects of life. Does this mean that we will never face problems? The apostle Paul wrote: "Never think you are too self-sufficient." Being cautious helps us to remain realistic. Paul also said: "If God is for us, who will be against us? He did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for all of us. If he has done this for us, will he not generously give us everything else along with him?"—Rom. 8:5, 6.
11 "Truly, earnestly." Strive to cultivate qualities that please God. Those qualities can protect you from harmful influences and help you resist temptation. And strive to get rid of "every sort of wicked bitterness, and anger, and rage, and clamoring, and abusive speech."—Eph. 4:31.
12 Be humble, so that you may continue to seek "God's wisdom and understanding" and continue to "apply your heart to the knowledge of your Creator." (1 Pet. 5:6, 7) If we are humble, God will guide us and bless us. (Micah 6:8) Let us always examine ourselves to see what we are doing right and what we are doing wrong, and let us learn from our mistakes, so that we can continue to draw close to God and please him.—"MAKE DISCERMENT YOUR PRIORITY"
13. Jesus asked: "Make discernment your priority?"
13 According to Matthew 6:34 (read), Jesus gave us this important advice: "Make discernment your priority." But how can we show that we really value discernment? Jesus asked: "Make discernment your priority?" It means that a true Christian puts Jehovah's standards first in his life. Consider how David and Paul showed discernment. Jesus wants us to use our powers of discernment to support the Kingdom work and to avoid being influenced by false teachings. Every day we face decisions, and as Christians we want to make wise choices and remain neutral. This advice from Jesus can help us to stay strong despite many trials?—"MAKE DISCERMENT YOUR PRIORITY"
14. Can you think of ways to apply this counsel in your life?
14 Sometimes a person may struggle to make good decisions. He may be tempted to compromise on what he knows is right, or he may have been making mistakes for years. For example, King David expressed his feelings saying: "My wounds are festering." He said: "I am helpless because of my guilt." (Ps. 38:3, 4, 8, 18) What caused David to feel this way? Was he forgiven? He was comforted knowing that Jehovah would not abandon him and would heal him. He also admitted frankly: "The burden of my sin weighs heavily upon me."—Read Psalm 32:1-3, 5.
15. (a) How can you make discernment a priority in your life? (b) Can you think of ways to improve your discernment? (See the box "Some Ways to Improve Discernment.")
15 Often we need to make decisions about moral matters. For instance, David wrote Psalm 55 when he was deeply troubled because he felt betrayed. (Ps. 55:2-5) But instead of letting those negative emotions drive him away from Jehovah, David poured out his heart to God, and he confessed his errors. David learned to trust in Jehovah, and he sought guidance from Him. He also meditated on examples of faithful men who had faced similar trials. (2 Sam. 15:30-34) This helped him to cope. People who make poor choices often focus on their own desires, ignoring Bible principles and failing to give Jehovah credit for everything good, and they end up following a course that displeases him.
16. Why is it important to understand the purpose of God's law?
16 A Christian needs to make decisions about many things, and sometimes it may be difficult to know what is right. But if we want to please God, we will seek his guidance and pray for wisdom. How can we do this? Many times, the best way to find answers is to meditate on Scriptural principles. The purpose of God's Law is, "To show people what is righteous." (Rom. 3:14, NWT) That purpose is fulfilled when God helps us to apply his standards in our lives. Of course, we still have free will, and God allows us to choose whether or not to obey him. However, if we allow God to guide us, we will avoid making foolish decisions that could lead to regret and disappointment, and we will maintain a close relationship with him.
NEED TO BE LOYAL
17, 18. What can help us to remain loyal when facing difficulties?
17 One way to remain loyal is to confide in a mature Christian who can listen to your concerns without judging you. This person might be an elder, a friend, or a member of the congregation, and he should be willing to offer practical advice. The Bible says: "The heart of the righteous meditates, so as to discern and understand." (Prov. 12:25) Confide in someone you trust, share your thoughts openly, and ask for help in understanding how to apply Bible principles. The Bible also states: "The plans of diligent ones come to fruition; but there is haste only for those lacking discernment."—Prov. 15:22.
18 Furthermore, during our congregation meetings, Jehovah helps us to learn things we need to know to stay spiritually strong and motivated. These meetings give us the opportunity to associate with fellow Christians, and they provide encouragement and practical suggestions. (Heb. 10:24, 25) By 'encouraging one another,' we strengthen our faith, and this helps us to overcome difficulties and remain motivated.—Acts 1:12.
OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH JEHOVAH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE
19. How can loyalty to God be strengthened by our personal relationship with Him?
19 A brother in Canada shared an experience that illustrates this point. This brother is a schoolteacher and has children. He was facing a serious problem. Also, his wife was very worried about the situation. What helped him? He said: "The value of my spirituality, I realized, depends on how much my relationship with Jehovah means to me—how important it is to me to please Him. The joy that comes from serving with my family is great. I have learned to appreciate what I have and not focus on what I lack. And I have come to see that others also face problems, so I try to be understanding. Sometimes I may feel overwhelmed, but I always take time to examine my heart and make adjustments. And little by little, I find that I am able to cope with the situation. But when I rely on my own understanding, I often fail. So I pray to Jehovah for guidance."
20. (a) How can we show appreciation for God's provisions? (b) What will help us to maintain our zeal?
20 We show our appreciation for God by using what He provides, both in connection with our ministry and in our personal study. And we stay zealous by being moved by the spirit of living creatures, by appreciating all the privileges we have, and by associating with fellow Christians. The lesson is that Jehovah values us highly and wants to bless us.—Prov. 11:6.

text:
'Nĩvo ĩndĩ mũkavathũkany'a katĩ wa ala alũngalu na ala athũku.'—MAL. 3:18.
MBATHI: 29, 53
1, 2. Andũ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ makwatĩtwe nĩ thĩna wĩva? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MATAKĨTALĨ aingĩ me wĩanĩ mavulanaa na andũ me na mowau matonya kũkwatanw'a. Masũvĩaa andũ asu awau nũndũ methĩawa mayenda kũmatetheesya. Ĩndĩ mayĩka oou nĩmaĩle kwĩsũvĩa nĩ kana maikakwatwe nĩ mowau asu maendeee kũiita. O ta matakĩtalĩ asu, aingĩ maitũ twĩkalanasya na tũkathũkũma na andũ me na mawoni na mĩkalĩle ĩleanĩte na kwenda kwa Ngai. Ti laisi kwĩkalany'a na andũ asu.
2 Mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo andũ me mĩkalĩle mĩthũku vyũ. Nthĩnĩ wa valũa wa kelĩ ũla mũtũmwa Vaulo waandĩkĩe Timotheo, nũeleetye ũndũ andũ ala mavathanĩtw'e na Ngai mekalaa. Mĩkalĩle ĩsu yĩendeea kũthũkĩĩa o ũndũ ĩvinda yĩvĩtĩte. (Soma 2 Timotheo 3:1-5, 13.) O na kũtw'ĩka nĩtũtonya kũsengw'a nĩ ũndũ andũ maendeee kũthũka, nĩ laisi mũno tũkesa kwĩthĩa tũkwatiwe nĩ mĩtuo yoo na mawoni moo. (Nth. 13:20) Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ nĩtũkwona ũndũ nguma ila andũ asu methĩawa nasyo ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na sya ala mamũthũkũmaa Ngai. O na nĩtũkwona ũndũ tũtonya kwĩsũvĩa tũikakwatw'e nĩ mĩtuo mĩthũku ĩla tũendeee kũtetheesya andũ methĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Ngai.
3. Naaũ me nguma ila iwetetwe nthĩnĩ wa 2 Timotheo 3:2-5?
3 Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie kana "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo kũkeethĩwa mavinda ma mũisyo." Ĩtina wa ũu asyokie aandĩka nguma 19 nthũku ila andũ makethĩwa nasyo ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ. Nguma isu waandĩkie no ũndũ ũmwe na ila syĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Alomi 1:29-31, o na kau nguma imwe katĩ wa isu waandĩkie aiandĩkĩa Timotheo iiwetetwe vandũ vangĩ nthĩnĩ wa Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto. Vaulo ayambĩĩa kũandĩka nguma isu nthũku ambĩĩe na ndeto ii: "Nũndũ andũ makeethĩwa . . . " Ũu ti kwasya kana nguma isu syĩthĩawa na andũ onthe. Aklĩsto me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ.—Soma Malaki 3:18.
ITHYĨ TWĨKUAA ATA?
4. Ũtonya kwasya andũ ala me mĩyimbyo methĩawa mailyĩ ata?
4 Ĩtina wa Vaulo kũandĩka kana andũ makeethĩwa meyendete mo ene na mendete mbesa, asyokie aandĩka kana makeethĩwa makĩkathĩĩa, kwĩtaĩa, na me na mĩyimbyo. Mavinda maingĩ andũ ala me na nguma isu methĩawa na mĩyono nũndũ wa ũtonyi woo, wanake woo, malĩ ĩla me nayo, kana kĩvĩla manengetwe. Andũ me nguma isu mendete kũkumw'a na kwoswa ta ma vata mũno. Mũsomi ũmwe aandĩkie ndeto ii ĩũlũ wa mũndũ wĩ mĩyimbyo mingĩ: "Ngoonĩ kwake ethĩawa na kathembeo kala ũkumanĩaa ayĩthaitha we mwene." Namo andũ amwe maasya kana mĩyimbyo ĩthũkĩte ũkethĩa o na ala me mĩyimbyo nĩmamenete kwona angĩ me nayo.
5. Athũkũmi amwe aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova makwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo ata?
5 Yeova nũmenete vyũ mĩyimbyo. Nũmenete "metho me mĩtũlyo." (Nth. 6:16, 17) Mĩyimbyo, kana mĩtũlyo, nĩsiĩĩaa mũndũ aimũthengeea Ngai. (Sav. 10:4) O na Ndevili mwene esĩkĩe na mĩtũlyo. (1 Tim. 3:6) Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũmwe mũthũku nĩ kana athũkũmi amwe aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova nĩmakwatĩtwe nĩ mĩtũlyo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũla mũsumbĩ wa Yuta weetawa Usia nĩwaminie myaka mingĩ e mũĩkĩĩku. Ĩndĩ Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Yĩla waĩ na vinya, ngoo yake yeetũlya, kwondũ wa ũu eeka naĩ mũno, na amũvĩtanĩsya Yeova Ngai wake; nũndũ alikile ĩkalũnĩ ya Yeova atoeesye ũvani kĩthembeonĩ kya kũtoeesya ũvanĩ." O nake Mũsumbĩ Esekia nĩwakwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo, ĩndĩ o kwa kavinda.—2 Mav. 26:16; 32:25, 26.
6. Nĩ kyaũ kyaĩ kĩtonya kũtuma Ndaviti akwatwa nĩ mĩtũlyo, ĩndĩ nĩkĩ wekalile enyivĩtye?
6 Andũ amwe mameasya mĩtũlyo nũndũ wa wanake woo, nguma, ũtũĩka ũla me naw'o wa kũkũna wathi, vinya ũla me naw'o, kana nũndũ wa ũnene manengetwe vandũ. Maũndũ asu onthe Ndaviti aĩ namo ĩndĩ ekalaa enyivĩtye mavinda onthe. Ĩla wooaie Ngoliathu na anengwa mwĩĩtu wa Mũsumbĩ Saulo amũtwae, akũlilye atĩĩ: "Nyie nĩ ũũ, na thayũ wakwa nĩ kyaũ, kana mũvĩa wa asa wakwa nthĩnĩ wa Isilaeli, kana nĩtw'ĩke mũthoni wa mũsumbĩ?" (1 Sam. 18:18) Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Ndaviti ekale enyivĩtye? Ndaviti aĩ na nguma nzeo, ũtonyi mwingĩ, na ianda nũndũ Ngai 'nĩweenyivisye' amũtetheesye. (Sav. 113:5-8) Ndaviti nĩweesĩ kana vai kĩndũ kĩseo waĩ nakyo ũtanengetwe nĩ Yeova.—Sianĩsya na 1 Akolintho 4:7.
7. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkalae twĩnyivĩtye?
7 Andũ ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ nĩmatataa mũno methĩwe na wĩnyivyo o ta Ndaviti. Vai mũndũ mũnene kwĩ Yeova ĩndĩ we nĩwĩthĩawa e mũuu, kana enyivĩtye. Kũmanya ũu nĩkũtũtanĩthasya mũno. (Sav. 18:35) O na kũtumaa tũtata mũno kũatĩĩa ũtao ũũ: "Ĩvw'ĩkei ngoo yĩ na ĩnee ya kwĩw'anĩa tei, wĩnyivyo, ũuu, wũmĩĩsyo." (Ako. 3:12) Na eka ũu, nĩtwĩsĩ kana "wendo ndwĩtũlasya, o na ndwĩkathĩĩaa." (1 Ako. 13:4) Andũ moona twĩ na wĩnyivyo nĩmatonya kwenda kũmũthengeea Yeova. O tondũ aũme matonya kũkusw'a nĩ mwĩkalĩle mũseo wa iveti syoo o na vate ndeto, now'o angĩ matonya kwendeew'a nĩ kũmũthũkũma Ngai moona wĩnyivyo ũla andũ make methĩawa naw'o.—1 Vet. 3:1.
TWĨKALANASYA ATA NA ALA ANGĨ?
8. (a) Andũ amwe monaa ata mũtuo wa syana kũema kwĩw'a asyai? (b) Maandĩko matavĩtye syana syĩke ata?
8 Vaulo nĩwaeleisye ũndũ andũ ma mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo makekalanasya. Aandĩkie kana mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo syana iikew'aa asyai. Mavinda amwe kũema kwĩw'a asyai kũyonekaa ta thĩna, na syĩndũ ta mavuku, sinema, na televiseni nitumĩte syana syona ũsu tate mũtuo mũthũku. Ĩndĩ mũtuo ũsu nĩwanangaa mĩsyĩ na nĩtwĩsĩ kana vate mĩsyĩ vai andũ. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ andũ methĩĩtwe mesĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ma nthĩ ya tene ya Ũkiliki maĩ na mwĩao waĩtye kana mũndũ akũna mũsyai wake nĩwavenawa ũthasyo wa kwĩka maũndũ ta andũ ala angĩ, na kwosana na mĩao ya Alomi, mũndũ akũna ĩthe oosawa ũndũ ũmwe na mũndũ woaa ũngĩ. Namo Maandĩko ma Kĩevelania na Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto nĩmanengete syana mwĩao wa kũtaĩa asyai moo.—Kuma 20:12; Aev. 6:1-3.
9. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya syana imew'e asyai?
9 Syana no syĩsũvĩe iikakwatwe nĩ mũtuo wa kũema kwĩw'a asyai masyo kwa kũsũanĩa moseo ala asyai masyĩkĩte. Kũmanya kana Ngai, ũla nĩwe Ĩthe witũ ithyonthe, nĩwendaa twĩthĩwe twĩ ewi, nĩkũtonya kũitetheesya itũngae mũvea mũno nũndũ wa moseo asu. Syana syeemanyĩsya kũneenaa nesa ĩũlũ wa asyai masyo, no itetheesye syana ila ingĩ ikethĩwa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ wa asyai masyo. Ĩndĩ ethĩwa asyai mai na wendo waĩle kwondũ wa syana syoo, nũtonya kwĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwa syana kũmew'a kuma ngoonĩ. Nasyo syana syamanya kana asyai nĩmasyendete vyũ, nĩsyĩw'aa syeekĩwa vinya imatanĩthye o na ĩla syatatwa ieme kũmew'a. Mwanake wĩtawa Austin aĩtye atĩĩ: "O na kũtw'ĩka ve mavinda neew'aa nditatĩka nĩke maũndũ nĩvatĩtwe, asyai makwa nĩmambĩkĩĩaa mĩao ĩtambinyĩĩe, makangelesya nĩkĩ mambĩkĩĩe mĩao ĩmwe, na nĩmaneenanasya nakwa nesa. Kĩu kyandetheeisye nĩthĩwe nĩ mwĩwi. Nĩnoonaa kana nĩmanthĩnĩkĩaa, na kĩu kyatumaa nenda kũmatanĩthya."
10, 11. (a) Nĩ nguma syĩva ite nzeo syonanasya kana andũ mayendanĩte? (b) Aklĩsto maĩle kwenda ala angĩ mũno wĩana ata?
10 Ve nguma ingĩ ite nzeo Vaulo waandĩkie syonanasya kana andũ mayendanĩte. Ĩtina wa kũweta kana andũ makeethĩwa "matew'aa asyai" aatĩĩisye kũweta kana makeethĩwa mate mũvea. Ũu nũkũeleeka nũndũ andũ matatũngaa mũvea mayonaa ũseo ũla mekĩtwe nĩ andũ angĩ. O na ĩngĩ nĩwawetie kana andũ makeethĩwa mate atheu, kana mate aĩkĩĩku. Makeethĩwa mate na wĩw'ano, na ũu nĩ kwasya kana makeethĩwa matendete kũmantha mũuo na ala angĩ. Aisye angĩ makeethĩwa aumani na akaĩi, maineena maũndũ mate maseo na matonya kũthatya andũ ala angĩ na Ngai. Na ĩndĩ angĩ meeiwe makeethĩwa me ailĩanĩli. Asu nĩ andũ ala maneenaa maũndũ matonya kwanangĩa ala angĩ ĩsyĩtwa yoo. *
11 Ũmũnthĩ ala mamũthaithaa Yeova me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na andũ aingĩ ma nthĩ nũndũ mo nĩmendete ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ. Ĩvinda yonthe vethĩĩtwe vailyĩ ũu. Yesũ aisye kana kũmwenda mũtũi nĩw'o mwĩao wa kelĩ kwa ũnene nthĩnĩ wa ĩla Mĩao ya Mose. Wendo ũsu nĩ mũthemba ũmwe wa a·gaʹpe. Mwĩao ũla mũnene kũthonoka mwĩao ũsu no ũla wa kũmwenda Ngai. (Mt. 22:38, 39) Yesũ asyokie asya kana nguma ĩla ĩkatuma Aklĩsto ma w'o mamanyĩka nĩ kwendana. (Soma Yoana 13:34, 35.) O na aisye Aklĩsto maaĩle kwenda o na amaitha moo nĩ kana meanĩsye mwĩao ũsu.—Mt. 5:43, 44.
12. Yesũ oonisye ala angĩ ata kana nĩwamendete?
12 Yesũ nĩwoonanisye kana nĩwendete angĩ mũno. Aendaa ndũa na ndũa atavĩtye andũ ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Avoisye ililinda, ala mathuaa, ala mawaĩte mangũ, na ala maĩ au matũ. O na nĩwathayũũkisye akw'ũ. (Luka 7:22) Na eka ũu, aumisye thayũ wake mwene kwondũ wa andũ o na kũtw'ĩka aingĩ nĩmamũmenete. Yesũ aatĩĩie ngelekany'o ya Ĩthe ya kwenda ala angĩ ateũvĩtya o na vanini. O ta Yesũ, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe nĩsyonasya andũ onthe kana nimendete.
13. Kwenda ala angĩ kũmatetheeasya ata mamũthengeee Yeova?
13 Twenda ala angĩ nĩtũtumaa mamũthengeea Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũũme ũmwe nthĩ ya Thailand nĩweendeeiw'e mũno ĩla waendie ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa mĩthenya ĩtatũ na oona ũndũ ana-a-asa mendanĩte. Ĩla wenũkie nĩwakũlilye amanyĩaw'e Mbivilia kelĩ kwa kyumwa. Atavisye andũ make onthe ma mũsyĩ ũvoo, na myei thanthatũ ĩithela kuma ĩla waendie ũla ũmbanonĩ, nĩwaumisye ũvoo wake wa mbee wa kũsoma Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ. No twĩkũlye makũlyo aa nĩ kenda tũmanye ethĩwa nĩtwendete ala angĩ ũndũ vaĩle: 'Nyie nĩnĩtataa ũndũ ndonya nĩtetheesye ala angĩ mũsyĩ, kĩkundinĩ, na ũtavany'a? Nĩnĩtataa kwona ala angĩ ũndũ Yeova ũmonaa?'
NZŨI NA TŨTENA TWA MALONDU
14, 15. Nĩ nguma syĩva iilyĩ sya nyamũ andũ aingĩ me nasyo, ĩndĩ amwe maalyũkĩte ata?
14 Nguma ingĩ andũ me nasyo mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo ninengae Aklĩsto itumi ingi sya kwĩvathana namo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ala matamũkĩaa Ngai nĩ andũ matendete ũseo. Mbivilia ingĩ imetaa "andũ mamenete ũseo" kana andũ "me ũthũ na ũseo w'onthe." Nĩ andũ mate na wĩting'o na ai. Angĩ nĩ andũ me na ngũlũ, kana mekaa maũndũ mate kũsũanĩa na mateũmaka.
15 Andũ aingĩ maĩ na nguma ta isu iilyĩ sya nyamũ mbai, ĩndĩ nĩmavĩndũkĩte na makaseũva. Kũalyũka kũu kũseũvĩte ũu nĩkwathaniwe Mbivilianĩ. (Soma Isaia 11:6, 7.) Wathani ũsu ũwetete ĩũlũ wa nyamũ sya kĩtheka ta nzũi na mĩnyambũ syĩkalĩte na mũuo na nyamũ sya mũsyĩ ta tũtena twa malondu na tũsaũ. Wasisya nũkwona kana wathani ũsu waisye vakeethĩwa mũuo ta ũsu "nũndũ nthĩ ĩkausũw'a nĩ kũmũmanya Yeova." (Isa. 11:9) Nũndũ nyamũ iyĩsa kũmũmanya Yeova, wathani ũsu wawetie kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o ĩũlũ wa andũ makavĩndũka vyũ mĩkalĩlenĩ yoo.
16. Mbivilia ĩtetheesye andũ ata meke moalyũku thayũnĩ woo?
16 Ve aingĩ tene mailyĩ ta nzũi mbai ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ mekalaa na mũuo na ala angĩ. No ũsome ngewa sya amwe moo kĩlungunĩ kĩthĩawa na kyongo, "Mbivilia Nĩalyũlaa Andũ," kĩla kĩthĩawa jw.org. Ala mamwĩsĩ Yeova na mamũthũkũmaa mayĩilyĩ ta ala meĩtwe me na mũvw'ano wa kĩkĩo kwa Ngai, ĩndĩ nĩmakaĩĩte vinya wakyo. Asu metusaa nĩmamũthaithaa Ngai ĩndĩ mwĩkalĩle woo nũleaa. Vandũ va ũu, ala tene maĩ ta nyamũ mbai mũno 'nĩmevw'ĩkĩte mũndũ mweũ, ũla wombiwe na mũvw'ano wa Ngai nthĩnĩ wa ũlũngalu na ũtheu wa w'o.' (Aev. 4:23, 24) O ũndũ andũ memanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai, now'o monaa vata wa kũalyũka maatĩĩe myolooto yake. Kuma vau nĩmaekaa kũĩkĩĩa maũndũ mataĩle, makavĩndũa mawoni moo, na mwĩkalĩle woo. Ti laisi kwĩka moalyũku ta asu, ĩndĩ ala mamekaa methĩawa matetheew'e nĩ veva wa Ngai nũndũ nĩmendaa kwĩka kwenda kwake kuma ngoonĩ.
"ĨVATHANE NA ASU NAO"
17. Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũikatutye ala me nguma ite nzeo?
17 Kĩvathũkany'o kya ala mamũthũkũmaa Ngai na ala matamũthũkũmaa nĩkĩendeee kwoneka nesa. Ithyĩ ala tũmũthũkũmaa Ngai no nginya twĩkale twĩ metho tũikatutye ala mate alũngalu. Nĩtũtataa kwĩthĩwa twĩ oĩ tũatĩĩe ũtao ũla ũtwĩĩte nĩtwĩvathane na ala me ĩla mĩtuo ĩeleetw'e nthĩnĩ wa 2 Timotheo 3:2-5. Nĩtwĩsĩ kana vai ũndũ twĩsa kwĩka tũkatw'ĩka tũivulana vyũ na andũ onthe me nguma nthũku. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ andũ asu nomo ala tũthũkũmaa namo, tũsomaa namo, na twĩkalaa namo mũsyĩ. Ĩndĩ ti lasima tũkasũanĩa tamo kana tũkeka maũndũ tamo. Kĩla kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya nĩ kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kũmantha kĩtindo kya ala matw'ĩte vyũ kũmũthũkũma Yeova.
18. Mwĩkalĩle witũ na ũneeni witũ ũtonya kũtetheesya ata ala mekwenda kũmũmanya Yeova?
18 Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana nĩtwaĩle kũtata tũtetheesye angĩ mamũmanye Yeova. Tũmĩaa nesa myanya ĩla yaumĩla ya kumya ũkũsĩ, na ũimũvoya Yeova aũtetheesye kũmanya kĩla waĩle kũweta na ĩvinda yĩla waĩle kũkĩweta. Nũseo tũkatavasya ala angĩ kana twĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Tweeka ũu mwĩkalĩle witũ mũseo ũkamũtaĩaa Ngai na ti ithyĩ ene. Nĩtũmanyĩĩtw'e "tũlee maũndũ onthe mate ma kũmũkĩa Ngai na mawendi onthe ma nthĩ, twĩkalasye mathayũ maitũ na kĩlĩko kĩanĩu na ũlũngalu na kũmũkĩa Ngai ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ." (Tito 2:11-14) Tweekua nesa ũndũ Ngai wendaa, ala matũsyaĩĩsye maikalea kwona kĩu. O na amwe moo nĩmatonya kwasya: "Nĩtũkũthi nenyu, nũndũ nĩtwĩw'ĩte kana Ngai e vamwe nenyu."—Nzek. 8:23.
^ kal. 10 Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "mũilĩanĩli [mũsukani]" kana "mũvinganĩsya" nĩ di·aʹbo·los. Ndeto ĩsu ĩtũmĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ ta ĩsyĩtwa ya Satani, kĩla kyũmbe kĩthũku kilĩĩlaa Ngai ũvũngũ.
