translation:
"That is what Jehovah says, 'You people will see the difference between the righteous and the wicked.'"—MAL. 3:18.
PAGE: 29, 53
1, 2. What reasons do God's servants have for being hopeful? (Consider practical examples.)
Many Christians find it difficult to deal with those who do not value spirituality. It pains them to see people wasting their lives pursuing empty goals. Sometimes it may seem as though such ones get ahead while those who serve God fall behind. But Christians, most of us struggle with feelings of discouragement when dealing with people who have worldly priorities and materialistic interests and who disregard God's standards. Do not become discouraged with such people.
2 This increasing wickedness should not surprise true Christians. Long ago the apostle Paul wrote to Timothy, describing how people would behave in the last days. Today, we see his words coming true. (Read 2 Timothy 3:1-5, 13.) And as conditions worsen, we can be sure that people will become more self-centered and less considerate. (Prov. 13:20) This scripture shows us why so many people today act the way they do, but it also reminds us that this does not excuse the behavior of those who claim to be Christians. And it helps us understand why we may sometimes feel frustrated when dealing with selfish people who show little concern for God's standards.
3 What are some of the things described at 2 Timothy 3:2-5?
3 The apostle Paul wrote that people would be "lovers of themselves." He said that this would be especially noticeable in the last days. He listed 19 traits that such people would display. Some of these traits are mentioned elsewhere in the Bible—for example, at Romans 1:29-31. But he also included some traits that were new at that time. Paul began listing these traits by saying: "People will be . . ." This indicates that not everyone would exhibit all of these traits. True Christians are discerning.—Read Malachi 3:18.
WHAT CAN WE DO ABOUT IT?
4 Can we avoid associating with all imperfect people?
4 When Paul wrote about people being "lovers of themselves," he also mentioned that they would be disobedient to parents, reckless, and without self-control. Many people today display some of these traits, whether because of their upbringing, their environment, bad associations, or simply a desire for excitement. People who exhibit these traits may be difficult to deal with and may cause trouble. One writer described the attitude of a young person with many negative qualities: "He seems to think that the world owes him something." And some people excuse bad behavior by saying that it is just part of youthfulness.
5 Are some elders in Jehovah's organization making mistakes?
5 Jehovah hates wickedness. He hates "the work of wickedness." (Ps. 95:10, 11) Wickedness, or wrongdoing, can lead a person to disrespect God. (Ps. 10:4) And the Devil himself is associated with wickedness. (1 Tim. 3:6) So it is not surprising that some elders occasionally make mistakes. For example, Elder Uziah of Judah was stubborn for many years. The Bible says: "Because he acted presumptuously, he incurred guilt, and Jehovah struck him with leprosy throughout his whole body, and he became leprous until the day of his death." Also, King Hezekiah made a mistake—but he admitted it.—2 Ki. 26:16; 32:25, 26.
6 What caused David to stumble into sin, and what lesson can we learn from this?
6 Some people commit sins because of their desires, such as the desire for power, the desire for praise, or the desire for wealth. These desires led David to act unwisely. However, Goliath taunted Israel and challenged them, saying: "Give me a man to fight with me! Why have you come down against me? Am I a dog that you should send me to fetch a stick?" (1 Sam. 17:43) What motivated David to accept the challenge? David had great faith, courage, and confidence in Jehovah, who 'supported' him. (Ps. 113:5-8) David knew that Jehovah could help him.—Compare 1 Corinthians 4:7.
7 What can help us avoid stumbling into sin?
7 Those whom Jehovah loves discipline those he loves, just as he disciplined David. A person pleasing to Jehovah is humble, not proud. Remembering this will help us. (Ps. 18:35) It also helps us to be modest when considering our accomplishments: "Let everyone carefully examine himself, and then let him eat of the bread and drink from the cup." (1 Cor. 11:28) And remember that "love does not boast, nor does it get puffed up."—1 Cor. 13:4. Many people find it difficult to express love, but they can show love by being considerate and kind, and they can demonstrate love by avoiding bad association.—1 Pet. 3:1.
ARE WE BEING MODEST?
8. (a) How do some people react when they receive commendation? (b) What Scriptural principles can help us remain modest?
8 Paul explained why Christians should be modest. He wrote that Christian privileges should not cause them to become arrogant. Some forms of entertainment can contribute to arrogance, such as movies, videos, and television programs that glorify violence. Such entertainment can desensitize us to wrongdoing and may lead us to imitate bad behavior. This is especially true because entertainment often portrays immoral conduct as appealing and exciting, and it may even encourage viewers to disregard God's standards. For example, people in some parts of Hawaii have been known to invite others to witness their immoral activity, and they openly discuss their affairs. However, the Bible and Christian principles teach us to avoid improper associations.—Acts 20:12; Eph. 6:1-3.
9. What can we do to remain modest?
9 We can cultivate modesty by avoiding situations that might tempt us to become arrogant. Remembering that God, who is the ultimate authority, wants us to live in dignity, can help us to maintain a balanced view of ourselves. Modesty also involves being careful about how we speak and act, and avoiding boasting or drawing undue attention to ourselves. It is important to show genuine interest in others and to treat them with kindness and respect. Also, if we realize that our privileges could affect others negatively, we should be willing to adjust our conduct. A young man named Austin said: "I noticed that when I watched violent videos, I began to feel numb to the suffering of others. The characters in those videos were committing terrible acts, and I started to think that such things weren't so bad. That attitude made me want to experiment with violence myself."
10, 11. (a) What question does modesty help us to answer regarding our relationship with others? (b) Can Christians reasonably expect to have a perfect understanding of themselves?
10 This is another quality that helps us to assess our relationship with others. Paul's writings reveal what questions modesty helps us to ask regarding our relationship with others. The desire to know whether people are "approved" is linked to the desire to know whether they are approved by God. This shows that we should not base our opinion of others on what others think of them. Rather, we should try to determine whether people are approved by God, regardless of their background or circumstances. People who are modest do not boast about their accomplishments, nor do they look down on others. They recognize that all abilities come from God, and this helps them to avoid becoming proud or critical. Others may be materialistic and selfish, focusing on their own interests and disregarding the feelings of others and God. But some individuals remain humble. These are the ones who continue to appreciate what they have and who are less likely to cause trouble. *
11 Those who love Jehovah deeply value his friendship and want to please him in everything they do. They strive to imitate his example in all aspects of their lives. Jesus showed what it means to prioritize loving God when he emphasized the greatest commandment found in Deuteronomy 6. That command is an expression of brotherly love. Loving God supremely surpasses any other form of love, including self-love. (Matt. 22:38, 39) Jesus also taught that the new commandment he gave to Christians was closely related to showing love. (Read John 13:34, 35.) And Christians can show love, even toward those who mistreat them—in fact, this is what demonstrates their love.—Matt. 5:43, 44.
12. What did Jesus teach his followers about forgiving others?
12 Jesus taught his followers to be generous in extending forgiveness. He went from house to house, kindly helping people learn about God's Kingdom. He associated with the sick, the poor, the despised, and even tax collectors. And he forgave their sins. (Luke 7:22) Moreover, he used his authority to forgive sins and empowered others to do the same. Jesus set the perfect example of how to extend forgiveness to everyone, regardless of their past. Truly, Jehovah's Son, Jesus, demonstrated exceptional compassion toward all people.
13. Does showing love to others ever tire out Jehovah?
13 We show our love for others by zealously proclaiming the good news. For instance, a brother in Thailand moved his family to a remote village so that they could help more people learn the truth. The villagers were initially suspicious, but he persevered in sharing Bible knowledge with them. He helped many people, and eventually the entire village welcomed him and his family, allowing him to conduct regular Bible studies. So let us be encouraged to continue showing love, knowing that we can ask ourselves this question: "Can I really get tired of doing what Jehovah approves of and delights in? Can I become weary of showing love?"
REASONS FOR BEING ENCOURAGED
14, 15. Why are many people responsive to the message, and what does this mean for us?
14 Many people respond favorably to the good news because they yearn for genuine worship. They may feel empty inside despite having material possessions. The Bible refers to them as "spiritual people" or people who are "longing for spiritual things." These are the ones who appreciate our message and are receptive to it.
15 Many people have a deep need for peace and justice, and they are disillusioned with the world. They are looking for answers that the Bible provides. (Read Isaiah 11:6, 7.) This shows that there is still much work to be done to bring peace and righteousness to mankind. Consider whether your ministry has helped someone to experience the fulfillment described in the scripture: "The result of righteousness will be peace." (Isa. 11:9) If so, you have contributed to helping someone come to know Jehovah.
16. What further encouragement does the Bible offer us?
16 Many find comfort in knowing that God cares about them personally. You can find more information on this topic in the publication "The Bible—What It Teaches," available at jw.org. Those who love Jehovah and want to strengthen their relationship with him will be grateful for your efforts. Let us continue to help people approach God and learn his ways. For some, this may mean overcoming deeply ingrained beliefs and prejudices. However, they may eventually say, "I have come to appreciate how reasonable and satisfying God's standards are." (Eph. 4:23, 24) As people gain an understanding of God's purposes, they often make significant changes in their lives.
"ASSOCIATE WITH THEM"
17. How can we show empathy toward those who are struggling?
17 We need to remember that both those who love God and those who do not often face difficulties. While we strive to please God, we should also try to empathize with those around us. We must avoid being quick to judge others, especially when they behave in ways that seem unreasonable to us. Why? Because many people have been hurt or mistreated. Like Paul, we recognize that we once lived among them and shared their way of life. (2 Tim. 3:2-5) So we understand that simply telling someone what is right may not move his heart. Instead, we take the time to get to know them, associate with them, and share our lives with them. But we must not compromise our principles or overlook serious wrongdoing. The best way to encourage ourselves is to deepen our own appreciation for Jehovah by studying the Bible and imitating the example of those who zealously serve him.
18. What can we do to help those who are seeking to know Jehovah?
18 One way is to be patient and understanding toward those who are learning about Jehovah. We use practical wisdom, recognizing that each person has a different background and experiences. We trust that Jehovah will help us to speak in a way that appeals to their heart and helps them to see the truth. Therefore, we do not hesitate to offer assistance to others, knowing that this pleases Jehovah. Let us maintain this attitude, always striving to commend God and not just talk about Him. We remember the words: "Let us train our conscience so that we may reject things disapproved by God and wicked practices, and let us live with soundness of mind and righteousness and godly devotion." (Titus 2:11-14) We are confident that God cares about those who seek him, and he wants to help them. And we can be sure that some may respond like the psalmist did: "I will declare your name to my brothers; in the congregation I will praise you." —Ps. 22:22.
^ par. 10 The Greek word rendered "demonized" or "possessed" is diaʹbolos. This term is used in the Bible to identify Satan, the Devil, as the invisible force behind such activity.

text:
KWAKŨNA visa wone Ndaviti aivĩtũkana na asikalĩ me na wia ma ita sya Isilaeli mavalũkanganĩtye na masembete na kĩvũvũ maumĩte kĩwanzanĩ kya kaũ. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumĩte asikalĩ asu methĩwa na wia mwingĩ ũu? No nginya Ndaviti ethĩwe eew'aa asikalĩ ma Isilaeli maitindĩa kũweta ĩsyĩtwa ya mũndũ ũmwe me na wia. Mũndũũme ũsu aũngamĩte mwandanĩ na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa aĩ mũnene kwĩ mũndũ o na wĩva Ndaviti waĩ aaona.
Mũndũũme ũsu eetawa Ngoliathu, na ĩla Ndaviti woonie ũndũ ũnenevete nĩwamanyie nĩkĩ asikalĩ asu mamũkĩaa. O na atekĩĩte ngũa sya kaũ, nĩvatonyeka Ngoliathu akethĩwa aĩ mũnene kwĩ aũme elĩ anene makwatanĩtw'e. Ĩndĩ mũthenyanĩ ũsu, Ngoliathu nĩweekĩĩte ngũa sya kaũ na aĩ na mĩio myai ya kaũ, aĩ mũndũ wĩ vinya mwingĩ mũno na nĩweesĩ kaũ. Ngoliathu nĩwatolekelaa asikalĩ ma Isilaeli mũno ayenda o ũmwe oke mokite. Kwasũanĩa ĩwasya yake ĩnene na ĩito ĩyĩw'ĩka iĩmanĩ akwete kũumanga ita sya Isilaeli na mũsumbĩ woo, Saulo. Endaa o mũsikalĩ ũmwe oke kũkita nake nĩ kana amũsinda, kaũ ũsu ũthele!—1 Samueli 17:4-10.
Aisilaeli vamwe na mũsumbĩ woo Saulo, maĩ na wia mwingĩ mũno. Ndaviti nĩwamanyie kana ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩĩtwe ũendeee mbee wa mwei ũmwe. Ita sya Isilaeli na sya Avilisiti syekalĩte ĩvinda yĩu yonthe itaaĩsa kũkita, ĩndĩ Ngoliathu nowe waumĩlaa kĩla mũthenya nĩ kana aendeee kũumanga Aisilaeli. Ũndũ ũsu nĩwaũmĩisye Ndaviti mũno. Waĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya mũno kwona mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli, vamwe na asikalĩ make, na akũũe atatũ ma Ndaviti me na wia! Methonĩ ma Ndaviti, Ngoliathu ndaumangaa ita sya Isilaeli syĩ syoka, ĩndĩ nĩwaumangaa Yeova, Ngai wa Isilaeli! Ĩndĩ nũndũ Ndaviti aĩ o mũndũ wa mũika, esaa kwĩka ata? Na tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ kumana na mũĩkĩĩo wa Ndaviti?—1 Samueli 17:11-14.
"MWĨTĨKĨSYE MAUTA: NŨNDŨ ŨŨ NĨWE"
Ekai twone maũndũ meekĩkĩte myei mingĩ mĩvĩtu. Mũthenya ũmwe ĩa mawĩoo Ndaviti aĩthasya malondu ma ĩthe wake iĩmanĩ syaĩ vakuvĩ na Mbethelemu. Ndaviti aĩ o kamwana ka mũika kanake, ke na ũthyũ mũseo, na kombe nesa. Mavinda amwe ĩla kũuĩtye Ndaviti eethĩawa aithaũka mbeve. Nũndũ Ndaviti nĩwendeeaw'a nĩ wũmbi wa Ngai na nĩwaendeeie kũmanya kũinga mbeve nesa, atũmĩaa masaa maingĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kũinga mbeve. Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũsu ĩa mawĩoo, Ndaviti nĩwatũmaniwe nĩ ĩthe wake ayenda kũmwona na mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka.—1 Samueli 16:12.
Eethĩie ĩthe wake, Yese, aineena na mũtumĩa waĩ mũkũũ mũno. Mũtumĩa ũsu aĩ mwathani Samueli. Yeova nĩwamũtũmĩte aketĩkĩsye mwana ũmwe katĩ wa syana sya Yese mauta nĩ kana eĩthĩwa e mũsumbĩ ũla ũatĩĩe kũsumbĩka Isilaeli. Samueli aĩ anoona akũũe mũonza ma Ndaviti, ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwamwonisye Samueli kana vai ũmwe woo ũnyuvĩte. Ĩla Ndaviti wavikie, Yeova nĩwamũtavisye Samueli ndeto ii: "Mwĩtĩkĩsye mauta: nũndũ ũũ nĩwe." Samueli e mbee wa ana-a-inyia ma Ndaviti, nĩwaumisye ũvya wa mauta na amwĩtĩkĩsya Ndaviti. Kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu Ndaviti wetĩkĩiw'e mauta, maũndũ make mambĩĩie kwĩthĩwa me kĩvathũkany'o nũndũ o na Mbivilia yaĩtye kana 'veva wa Yeova nĩwookie na vinya mũnene ĩũlũ wa Ndaviti kuma mũthenya ũsu na kũendeea.'—1 Samueli 16:1, 5-11, 13.
We Ndaviti nĩwambĩĩie kwĩmanthĩa nguma ĩtina wa kũmanya kana nĩwe ũkasumbĩka Isilaeli? Aiee, aĩ mwĩanĩe na nĩwavangie kweteela nginya ĩla veva wa Yeova ũkamũtongoesya kũmanya nĩ ĩndĩĩ ũkethĩwa e mũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu weeteele, nĩwaendeeie kũtethya wĩa wake wa ndĩthya ũla waĩ wa kĩlasi kya nthĩ. Ndaviti nĩweeyumĩtye vyũ kũtethya wĩa ũsu ate na wia. Ndĩthya ya ĩthe wake nĩyavithũkĩiwe mavinda elĩ, ĩvindanĩ yĩmwe yavithũkĩiwe nĩ mũnyambũ, na ĩvindanĩ ya kelĩ yavithũkĩiwe nĩ nduva. Ndaviti ndaaĩka kũlũngĩlĩĩlya nyamũ isu kĩthekanĩ. Ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, ambĩaa kũkita nasyo ate kwananga saa nĩ kana asũvĩe ndĩthya ya ĩthe wake. Mavindanĩ asu onthe, nĩwooaie nyamũ isu mbai e weka!—1 Samueli 17:34-36; Isaia 31:4.
Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, Ndaviti nĩwatũmaniwe ĩngĩ. Mũsumbĩ Saulo nĩweew'ĩte nguma syake. O na kau Saulo aĩ ngũmbaũ ya kaũ, Yeova nĩwamũkolete nũndũ wa kũema kwĩw'a mĩao yake. Yeova nĩwavetete veva wake nthĩnĩ wa Saulo, na kĩu kĩkatuma ethĩwa na veva ũngĩ mũthũku ũla watumaa ethĩwa e mũthilĩku, e na nzika, na e mũng'endu. Ĩla Saulo weethĩwa na veva ũsu mũthũku, ũndũ ũla wamũtetheeasya kwĩw'a nesa nĩ kũingĩwa mbeve. Amwe ma athũkũmi ma Saulo nĩmeew'ĩte kana Ndaviti nĩ mũingi mũseo wa mbeve na nĩ mũndũ wa kaũ. Kwoou Ndaviti nĩwatũmaniwe, na ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, eethĩwa e ũmwe katĩ wa ala mainĩaa mũsumbĩ na makuaa mĩio yake ya kaũ.—1 Samueli 15:26-29; 16:14-23.
Andũ ma mũika no memanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ kumana na mũĩkĩĩo wa Ndaviti. Ũndũ ũmwe tũkwĩmanyĩsya nĩ kana Ndaviti eetanĩthasya na maũndũ matonya kũmũtetheesya kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana Ndaviti nĩwaendeeie kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ matonya kũmũtethya na matonya kũtuma akwata wĩa. Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla mũnene vyũ nĩ kana Ndaviti nĩweetĩkĩlile kũtongoew'a nĩ veva wa Yeova. Ĩsu nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo mũno vyũ kwitũ na nĩtwaĩle kũmĩatĩĩa!—Mũtavan'ya 12:1.
"VAIKETHĨWE MŨNDŨ ŨKW'A NGOO NŨNDŨ WAKE"
O aendeee na kũthũkũma kwa Saulo, ve mavinda Ndaviti wasyokaa mũsyĩ kũĩthya malondu, na mavindanĩ amwe nĩweekaa ũu kwa ĩvinda ĩasa. Ĩvindanĩ yĩmwe katĩ wa mavinda asu, Ndaviti nĩwatũmiwe nĩ ĩthe wake, Yese, nĩ kana akasisye akũũe atatũ ala maĩ itanĩ sya kaũ sya Saulo. Ndaviti nĩwamwĩthukĩĩisye ĩthe na kwoou athi elekele Mwandanĩ wa Ela kwona ana-a-inyia amakuĩe lĩu. Ĩla wavikie kũu, Ndaviti nĩwasaanĩiw'e mũno kwona ita isu ilĩ sya kaũ ite kũkita o tondũ vaeleiw'e mwambĩĩonĩ wa kĩlungu kĩĩ. Ita isu sya asikalĩ syeekĩte kũsiany'a, amwe maũngamĩte mũingo ũmwe na ala angĩ maũngamĩte mũingo ũla ũngĩ wa kĩĩma.—1 Samueli 17:1-3, 15-19.
Ndaviti ndaaendeew'a nĩ ũndũ ũsu na ndaĩ etĩkĩla ũendeee. Vaĩ vatonyeka ata ita sya Yeova Ngai ikakĩa kũkita na mũndũ ũtamũthaithaa Yeova? Methonĩ ma Ndaviti, Ngoliathu ndaumaa mũndũ, ĩndĩ avũthasya Yeova. Na kwoou Ndaviti nĩwambĩĩie kũneena na asikalĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũtonya kũkita na Ngoliathu na akamũsinda. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ, mũkũũe wa Ndaviti ũla weetawa Eliavu nĩweewie ndeto syake. Ĩla Eliavu weewie ndeto sya Ndaviti, nĩwathatie na amũtavya maũndũ mathũku kwa kũmwĩa kana eeũkĩte vau kwĩloela kaũ. Ĩndĩ Ndaviti amũsũngĩie na amũkũlya atĩĩ: "Neka ata yu? Vati kĩtumi?" Na ĩndĩ Ndaviti aendeea kũneena na ũkũmbaũ ĩũlũ wa kũkita na Ngoliathu, nginya ndeto isu syesa kũmũvikĩa Saulo. Mũsumbĩ Saulo nĩwaisye Ndaviti aetwe mbee wake.—1 Samueli 17:23-31.
Ndaviti nĩwamũtavisye Saulo ndeto ii sya kwĩkĩa vinya ĩũlũ wa Ngoliathu, aisye atĩĩ: "Vaikethĩwe mũndũ ũkw'a ngoo nũndũ wake." Saulo na asikalĩ make mayoonaa ta mesa kũkita na Ngoliathu na makamũsinda. Thĩna woo nũtonya kwĩthĩwa walikile ĩla mambĩĩie kwĩyĩelekany'a na ĩmũndũ yĩu ĩnene, na meesianĩsya nayo mayĩthĩa o na maiyĩvika kĩthũi. Masũanĩaa kana Ngoliathu emakũna amamine na ndatĩka ĩmwe. Ĩndĩ Ndaviti ndasũanĩaa tamo. O tondũ tũkwĩmanyĩsya, Ndaviti oonie ũndũ ũsu kwa nzĩa yĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na nĩkyo kĩtumi wavangie kũkita na Ngoliathu.—1 Samueli 17:32.
Ĩndĩ Saulo amwĩie Ndaviti atĩĩ: "Ndũtonya kũthi kũkita na Mũvilisiti ũũ; nũndũ wĩ o kĩmwana, nake nĩ mũndũ wa kaũ kuma wana wake." Kwa w'o Ndaviti aĩ o kamwana? Aiee, ĩndĩ asianĩw'a na asikalĩ ala angĩ, aĩ mũnini, na oonekaa ailyĩ o kamwana. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu, Ndaviti nĩweesĩkĩe ta mũndũ wa kaũ na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa aĩ na myaka vakuvĩ 20.—1 Samueli 16:18; 17:33.
Nĩ kana Ndaviti aĩkĩĩthye Saulo kana nũkũthi kũkita na Ngoliathu, nĩwamũeleisye ũndũ wooaie mũnyambũ na nduva. Ndaviti eekaa o kwĩkathĩĩa? Aiee. Ndaviti nĩweesĩ kĩla kyatumie oaa mũnyambũ ũsu na nduva. Aisye atĩĩ: "Yeova ũla wambonokisye kuma kĩthunĩ kya mũnyambũ, na kuma kĩthunĩ kya nduva, akambonokya nume kw'okonĩ kwa Mũvilisiti ũũ." Ĩtina Saulo nĩwesie kwĩtĩkĩla na amwĩa Ndaviti atĩĩ: "Thi, na Yeova akeethĩwa vamwe naku."—1 Samueli 17:37.
We no wende kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Ndaviti? Ethĩwa no wende, manya kana mũĩkĩĩo wa Ndaviti ndwaĩ o kĩndũ weekaa kũsũanĩa. Kĩla kyamũtetheeisye amũĩkĩĩe Ngai nĩ ũmanyi na ũndũ woonete Yeova aimũtethya. Nĩweesĩ kana Yeova nũsũvĩaa andũ make na nĩwĩanĩasya kĩla waweta. Ethĩwa nũkwenda kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ta ũsu wa Ndaviti, endeea kũmũmanya Ngai kwa kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Ethĩwa tũkeekaa maũndũ ala tweemanyĩsya Mbivilianĩ, mosyao maseo ala tũkonaa makalũlũmĩĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ.—Aevelania 11:1.
"YEOVA NŨKŨŨNENGANE KW'OKONĨ KWAKWA"
Mbeenĩ, Saulo nĩwamũnengie Ndaviti ngũa syake sya kaũ ekĩe. Syendaa kwĩkala ila sya Ngoliathu syaseũvĩtw'e na kĩaa na syaĩ na kakoti kaseũvĩtw'e na kĩaa. Ndaviti nĩwatatie kũthi ekĩĩte ngũa isu sya kaũ ngito na nene, ĩndĩ eethĩa ndatonyana nasyo. Ndaĩ mũsikalĩ na kwoou ndamanyĩĩte kwĩkĩaa ngũa sya kaũ. Mũno mũno ndaĩ ekĩa ngũa sya kaũ ila syeekĩawa nĩ Saulo, ũla nĩwe waĩ mũasa vyũ mbaĩnĩ ya Isilaeli! (1 Samueli 9:2) Nĩwaumisye ngũa isu sya kaũ, na eekĩa ngũa sya ndĩthya ila wamanyĩĩte kwĩkĩa.—1 Samueli 17:38-40.
Ndaviti oosie ndata ĩla watũmĩaa ndĩthya, ekya kamũvuko kake kĩtuo, na akua kĩkũtha. Mũndũ nũtonya kũvũthĩĩsya kĩkũtha, ĩndĩ kyeethĩawa kĩ mũio mũthũku mũno wa kaũ. Kĩkũtha kyeethĩawa na kamũvuko kanini katonya kwĩanĩa ĩvia na mĩkwa ĩlĩ ya kĩthuma, na weethĩawa wĩ mũio mũseo wa mũndũ wa ndĩthya. Mũndũ enda kwĩkya ĩvia na kĩkũtha, eekĩaa ĩvia kamũvukonĩ kakyo, na aivyũlya kĩkũtha na vinya na ĩndĩ aĩlekya mũkwa ũmwe athimĩte vala ũkwendaa kũatha. Kĩkũtha kyaĩ mũio mũthũku mũno wa kaũ, na nĩkyo kĩtumi mavinda amwe ita sya kaũ syeethĩawa na ikundi sya asikalĩ ma kũkita matũmĩĩte ikũtha.
Nũndũ Ndaviti nĩweeyũmbanĩtye nesa, nĩwaendie kũkita na Ngoliathu. No tũsũanĩe Ndaviti aivoya aendeee na kũmbany'a mavia atano matendeu nesa kuma kalũsĩnĩ kaĩ kang'alu kĩw'ũ. Na ĩndĩ Ndaviti athi vala mokitĩaa asembete vandũ va kũthi ekalaatĩte!
Ĩla Ngoliathu woonie Ndaviti asũanĩie kyaũ? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Na amwona Ndaviti, amũmonda; nũndũ aĩ o kĩmwana, na mũtune, na vamwe na ũu aĩ na ũthyũ mũseo." Ngoliathu amũtolekeile Ndaviti na asya: "Nyie nĩ ngitĩ, kana ũmbũkĩe na ndata?" Nĩvatonyeka Ngoliathu akethĩwa oonie ndata ya Ndaviti na akavũthĩĩsya kĩkũtha kĩla wakwete. Nĩwamũumanĩie Ndaviti kwa ngai sya Avilisiti, na amwĩa kana athi vala ũĩ enengane mwĩĩ wake kwa nyũnyi sya yayaya na nyamũ sya kĩthekanĩ.—1 Samueli 17:41-44.
Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, ndeto ila Ndaviti wamũtavisye Ngoliathu syonanasya aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Kwakũna visa mwanake ũsu aitavya Ngoliathu ndeto ii: "We wĩmbũkĩa na ũvyũ, na ĩtumo, na katumo: ĩndĩ nyie nĩkũkĩa na syĩtwa ya Yeova wa nguthu, Ngai wa ita sya Isilaeli, ũla ũvũthĩĩsye." Ndaviti nĩweesĩ kana mĩio ya kaũ ti yo ya vata. Ngoliathu nĩwamũvũthisye Yeova Ngai, nake Yeova ndaĩ aema kũĩvanĩsya. O tondũ Ndaviti wawetie, 'kaũ waĩ wa Yeova.'—1 Samueli 17:45-47.
Ndaviti nĩwoonie ũndũ Ngoliathu wanenevete na mĩio ya kaũ ĩla waĩ nayo. Ĩndĩ Ndaviti ndaaĩtĩkĩla ũndũ ũsu ũmũsiĩĩe kwĩka ũndũ wavangĩte. Ndaaĩthĩwa na wia ta Saulo na asikalĩ make. O na ndaaĩsianĩsya na Ngoliathu, ĩndĩ vandũ va ũu, asianĩisye Ngoliathu na Yeova. Ngoliathu aĩ na ũasa wa vuti kenda na nusu (mita 2.9), ĩndĩ tũimũsianĩsya na Ngai Mwene Vinya W'onthe, Ngoliathu aĩ o kaindo kanini vyũ. Mũndũ ũsu woonekaa nĩ andũ anenevete ũu, aĩ o kasamũ kanini mũno methonĩ ma Yeova, na kwoou Yeova nĩweeyũmbanĩtye kũmwananga vyũ!
Ndaviti aendete kũkita na Ngoliathu oosie mavia kamũvukonĩ kake na asemba elekele kũla kwĩ Ngoliathu. Nĩweekĩie ĩvia kĩkũthanĩ kyake na akĩvyũlya na vinya wake w'onthe. Ngoliathu nĩwathengeeie vala ve Ndaviti, na nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa aĩ ĩtina wa mũsikalĩ ũla wakuĩte ngao yake ya kaũ. Nĩvatonyeka ũasa wa Ngoliathu ũkethĩwa wamwanangĩie maũndũ nũndũ mũkui wa ngao ndaĩ atonya kũsiĩĩa mũtwe wa Ngoliathu nũndũ aĩ mũasa mũno. Na nũndũ wa ũu, Ndaviti avangie kũmũatha mũtwe.—1 Samueli 17:41.
Ĩla Ndaviti wavyũlilye kĩkũtha eew'a kyakwata mwaki, nĩwalekilye ĩvia yĩkakime Ngoliathu. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ kwakilĩtye asikalĩ meteele mone kĩla kĩkwĩthĩwa nũndũ ĩvia yĩu yekiwe yĩthimĩte Ngoliathu kyongo. Yeova nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana Ndaviti ndeĩkya ĩvia yĩngĩ. Ĩvia yĩu yakimie vala Ndaviti wathimĩte, yaendie kũkima kĩtulyanĩ kya Ngoliathu yalika nthĩnĩ. Ĩmũndũ yĩu yanenevete ũu yaendie kũkima nthĩ na ũthyũ. Nĩvatonyeka mũsikalĩ ũla wamũkuĩe ngao akethĩwa asembie akĩĩte. Ndaviti nĩwaendie vala ve Ngoliathu, na oosa ũvyũ ũla waĩ wa Ngoliathu, na amũtila mũtwe naw'o.—1 Samueli 17:48-51.
Ĩtina wa ũndũ ũsu, Saulo na asikalĩ make nĩmeewie makwata ũkũmbaũ. Asikalĩ asu ma Saulo nĩmauisye ngemi na mamasembany'a Avilisiti. Kweethĩiwe ũndũ Ndaviti wamũtavĩtye Ngoliathu, amwĩie atĩĩ: 'Yeova nũkũmũnengane mokonĩ maitũ.'—1 Samueli 17:47, 52, 53.
Ũmũnthĩ, athũkũmi ma Yeova mayũkitaa nũndũ ĩvinda ya kwĩyũkitĩa nĩyathelile. (Mathayo 26:52) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu ta wa Ndaviti. O ta Ndaviti, nĩtwaĩle kũmanya kana Yeova nĩ Ngai wĩ na ũtonyi wa kũtũtethya, na nowe e weka twaĩle kũthũkũma na kũmũkĩa. Mavinda amwe nĩtũtonya kwĩw'a mathĩna ala twĩ namo me maito mũno, ĩndĩ mathĩna asu ti kĩndũ twamasianĩsya na vinya wa Yeova. Twanyuva kũmũthũkũma Yeova na twamũĩkĩĩa o tondũ Ndaviti wamũĩkĩĩe, vai ũndũ o na ũmwe ũkethĩwa ũtonya kũtũtelemya. Vai thĩna o na ũmwe ũtonya kũema Yeova!

translation:
There was a Philistine who was named Goliath, from Gath, who challenged Israel; he stood and shouted, "Give me a man to fight with!" When Saul and all Israel heard this, they were dismayed and terrified. Now David was the son of Jesse, an Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah, who had three sons: Eliab the firstborn, then Abinadab, and finally David was the youngest. While his father was tending sheep, David was taking care of them. One day while David was tending the flock, a lion and a bear came and attacked the flock, and David struck them down. Why did Saul send soldiers to fight with the Philistine? Did Saul think the soldiers would be able to defeat him? No, David was chosen from among all the Israelites to go against the Philistine. This man was strong and courageous, and when David arrived to see Goliath, he was already preparing for battle.
This man was called Goliath, and when David saw the size of the giant, he was afraid, knowing that all the soldiers were afraid of him. He mocked David, saying, "Am I a dog that you come against me with sticks?" Goliath threatened the army of Israel, challenging anyone to fight him alone, boasting about his strength and skill. He said, "I defy the armies of Israel today! Give me a man to fight with." His spear was like a weaver's beam, and its point weighed six hundred shekels. A young man carried his shield. —1 Samuel 17:4-10.
The Israelites and Saul gathered together, greatly distressed. David learned that this challenge continued for forty days. The armies of Israel and Philistia were lined up facing each other, and Goliath came forward daily to issue his challenge, hoping to intimidate the Israelites. This troubled David deeply. He asked why no one dared to face the commander of Israel's army, along with his soldiers, and offered himself to fight Goliath! David declared, "Goliath will not overpower Israel; I will strike him down, so that everyone will know that God belongs to Israel!" But some questioned whether David, being just a youth, could possibly succeed. And we wonder what motivated David?—1 Samuel 17:11-14.
"CHOOSE YOUR BATTLE: YOU ARE ENOUGH"
Let us now consider many interesting points. One day, while tending his father's sheep near Bethlehem, David was visited by Samuel. David was a young shepherd boy, handsome and impressive, and he played the harp skillfully. Some animals would bother David while he was caring for them, causing him distress. However, David proved to be a courageous shepherd who protected his flock from danger, spending much time learning how to defend them. On that particular day, David was sent by his father to visit his brothers and find out how they were doing.—1 Samuel 16:12.
When his brothers arrived, Jesse sent someone with a donkey and some food to them. This man was an attendant of Samuel. Jehovah had commissioned him to go and anoint one of Jesse's sons because there was no one among them suitable to become king over Israel. Samuel saw and considered the outward appearance of each of Jesse's sons, but Jehovah showed Samuel that none of them was the chosen one. But when David came, Jehovah said to Samuel: "This is the one; anoint him." Samuel filled the horn with oil and anointed David. From that day forward, David was anointed, and the spirit of Jehovah departed from Saul and troubled him greatly, and it was reported that 'a spirit from Jehovah left Saul and tormented him severely'.—1 Samuel 16:1, 5-11, 13.
Did David realize how great an honor it was to be appointed king over Israel? No, he did not know, but he trusted that Jehovah would guide him to understand what was right in this situation. From what we have learned, he continued to care for his father's sheep, just like a young shepherd boy. David proved himself faithful in small matters, and also in greater ones. The lions and bears that attacked his father's flock were overpowered by him. He demonstrated courage when facing those wild animals, and he never hesitated to defend his father's sheep.—1 Samuel 17:34-36; Isaiah 31:4.
Because of his bravery, David was sent on another mission. King Saul asked him to play the harp. But because Saul was troubled by a spirit from God, Jehovah helped him to see the value of having someone who could soothe him with music. Jehovah removed the distressing spirit from Saul, and whenever it returned, David would play until the man felt relieved, calm, and peaceful. Saul appreciated David greatly, and he made him his armor bearer.—1 Samuel 15:26-29; 16:14-23.
People often learn many things about others through observation. One thing we observe is whether David pleased God by being obedient and loyal to Jehovah. Another thing is whether David tried to find out what pleased God and strove to do what was right. And most importantly, we observe whether David allowed himself to be guided by Jehovah's spirit. Let us therefore carefully examine this matter and strive to imitate him!—Proverbs 12:1.
"APPOINT A STRONG MAN TO TAKE HIS PLACE"
As Saul continued his persecution of David, he sent messengers to arrest him, but they could not find him. Some messengers went to one place, and others stayed in another location. One day among those messengers, David was informed by his father, Jesse, that Saul had asked for him to come to him. David then sent his brother to inquire from Eliab where he was going. But he heard, David was reassured to know that Saul intended only to have him come to him to appoint him as a musician to soothe him. Saul's request did not seem serious, and he went along with his brothers to see what would happen.—1 Samuel 17:1-3, 15-19.
David went with them and continued on his way. While they were there, Goliath came out from the Philistine army to challenge Israel. He was a giant man who defied the God of Israel. And David heard about Goliath, he considered Goliath an ordinary man, but he trusted in Jehovah. And David inquired from his brothers how he could face Goliath and defeat him. The eldest brother of David, whose name was Eliab, became angry with him. But Eliab was angry with David, he rebuked him and accused him of coming to see the battle just to boast. However, David explained to him and said: "What have I done? Is it not right?" And David continued to speak with the entire army about facing Goliath, so the report reached Saul. King Saul sent for David and took him as his attendant.—1 Samuel 17:23-31.
David told Saul that he would go and fight Goliath, and he said: "Someone skilled in warfare should be chosen to fight against him." Saul and his soldiers were afraid to fight Goliath and they defeated him. It is important to remember that courage does not mean being fearless, but rather overcoming fear and doing what is right despite it. Consider how Goliath had armor and a spear. David considered this carefully. Therefore, David showed confidence because he knew that Jehovah would help him overcome Goliath.—1 Samuel 17:32.
Saul told David: "You are too young to go and fight against this Philistine; you are only a boy, and he is a seasoned warrior." Was David really a boy? No, although he was among older soldiers, he was a grown man, and he appeared strong and capable. In fact, David was already considered a mature man and was known to be brave and courageous, and he was over 20 years old.—1 Samuel 16:18; 17:33.
If David had asked Saul for permission to fight Goliath, he would have been relying on his own strength and ability. What did David rely on? He relied on Jehovah's strength and ability. He said: "Jehovah who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Then Saul allowed him to go and told David: "Go, and may Jehovah be with you."—1 Samuel 17:37.
What can we learn from David's example? We can learn that trusting in Jehovah is essential. David's trust was based on his knowledge of what Jehovah could do. We can also be confident that Jehovah will support his people and strengthen them in everything they do. So let us imitate David's trust, and get to know God better by studying the Bible. Let us continue to study the Bible regularly, so that we can develop our faith.—Hebrews 11:1.
"JEHOVAH WILL FIGHT FOR YOU"
However, Saul tried to clothe David with his own armor. It was heavy and uncomfortable, like Goliath's armor, and David found it awkward and restrictive. David rejected it, preferring to fight with what he knew well. But first he practiced using his sling and stones until he became skilled with it. Then he went to meet Goliath, but without Saul's approval, which was wrong because Saul was the leader of Israel! (1 Samuel 9:2) He confidently faced Goliath, and he went to meet him knowing that Jehovah would help him.—1 Samuel 17:38-40.
David took off the clothes that he had put on to go and face Goliath, and he ran toward him quickly and bravely. A man should not try to be brave in someone else's clothes, but rather in his own proper clothing. Someone who puts on another person's clothes feels restricted and uncomfortable, and he will not be able to move freely or fight effectively. A man who goes to fight wearing someone else's clothes will feel clumsy and awkward, and he may stumble and fall while trying to run. The clothes fit him properly, and they gave him the confidence to defeat Goliath, along with the support of the soldiers who were with him.
So David prepared himself and went to fight Goliath. Let us now see how David managed to overcome the giant with just five smooth stones that he picked up from the stream. And so David stood ready to fight, surprising everyone who came to watch the battle!
But what did Goliath say when he saw David preparing to fight? He scoffed and said: "Are you the one who has come to challenge me? You are just a boy, inexperienced in warfare, and you have no weapons!" Goliath threatened David and asked: "Am I a dog that you come against me with sticks?" Goliath underestimated David and was unaware of the power that God would give him to win the battle. David trusted in the God of Israel, and he knew that God would help him defeat his enemy with courage and strength.—1 Samuel 17:41-44.
To this day, the story of David defeating Goliath remains an inspiration. There is a lesson here for young people: do not underestimate yourself, because with God's help you can overcome any obstacle. David said to Goliath: "You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the Lord Almighty, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied." David knew that his strength did not come from himself, but from God. Goliath blasphemed the God of Israel, and God would not allow his name to be dishonored. That is why David succeeded, 'because the victory belonged to the Lord.'—1 Samuel 17:45-47.
David noticed how Goliath had been boasting about his strength and skill. David realized that he needed to rely on God to help him succeed. He was encouraged by King Saul and his soldiers. And when he confronted Goliath, he reminded Goliath and everyone present that he was fighting Goliath in the name of the Lord. Goliath was a mighty warrior, over nine feet tall (2.9 meters), but when compared to the greatness of our God, Goliath was nothing more than a small obstacle. This giant looked down on everyone, but he underestimated the power of the Lord, and the Lord was able to empower David to defeat him!
David went forward to meet Goliath, choosing five smooth stones from a stream and putting them in his shepherd's bag. Goliath sneered at David, and he rushed forward to attack David with his sword and shield. But David stood firm and skillfully slung a stone from his sling, hitting Goliath right between the eyes. The weight of the stone caused Goliath to fall to the ground, and David ran up and cut off Goliath's head with his own sword, preventing Goliath from being able to lift his head.—1 Samuel 17:41.
However, David did not need to use all five stones; just one was enough to subdue Goliath. It demonstrated to the Philistine army how little their champion meant to God, and showed that the Lord could save through anyone. The Lord showed that David was worthy to use the weapon he had chosen. The stone David threw struck Goliath in the forehead, causing him to fall to the ground unconscious. David ran to Goliath, stood over him, took Goliath's sword, and killed him with it.—1 Samuel 17:48-51.
As a result, Saul and his men returned to Jerusalem victorious. Saul's soldiers praised David and celebrated his victory over Goliath. They acknowledged that David had saved them.—1 Samuel 17:47, 52, 53.
Truly, the examples of Jehovah's faithful servants show us what courage can accomplish. (Matthew 26:52) Like David, we too may face challenges that seem overwhelming. But like David, we can be confident that Jehovah is our God and that He will strengthen us, and with His help we can remain courageous and loyal. There are times when we may feel inadequate to meet certain trials, but we should remember that our strength comes from Jehovah. We rejoice in getting to know Jehovah better and in trusting Him, as David trusted Him, because we realize that He has the power to help us overcome any obstacle. Yes, let us always strive to please Jehovah!

text:
"Kĩla kũnengwa kũseo na kĩla kũnengwa kwĩthĩanu nĩkumaa . . . kwa Ĩthe [witũ]."—YAK. 1:17.
MBATHI: 148, 5
1. Nĩ moathimo meva tũkakwata nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo?
NTHEMBO ya wovosyo ya Yesũ Klĩsto nĩtumaa tũkwata moathimo maingĩ mũno. Mũvango wa wovosyo nĩw'o ũkatonyethya nzyawa syonthe sya Atamu ila syendete ũlũngalu kwĩthĩwa syĩ ngwatanĩo na syũmbe ila ingĩ sya Ngai. Wovosyo ũsu now'o ũtumaa twĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũtanĩa thayũ tene na tene. Ĩndĩ ve ũndũ ũngĩ nthembo ya wovosyo ĩla Klĩsto waumisye ĩanĩasya kĩvathũkany'o na kũnenga ala ewi wĩkwatyo mũseo. Ũtwi ũla Yesũ weekie wa kũlũmany'a na ũsumbĩki wa Yeova na kũnengane thayũ wake na ngenda nĩwĩanĩasya maũndũ ma vata mũno makonetye kĩla ũmwe, ethĩwe e ĩtunĩ kana e kũũ nthĩ.—Aevl. 1:9.
2. (a) Mboya ĩla Yesũ wamanyĩisye amanyĩw'a make yĩ na maũndũ meva ma vata mũno makonetye kĩla ũmwe, ethĩwe e ĩtunĩ kana e kũũ nthĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.) (b) Twĩenda kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
2 Ĩvinda yĩmwe vatiele myaka ĩlĩ Yesũ akw'e na ainengane thayũ wake ta nthembo ya wovosyo, amanyĩisye amanyĩw'a make kũvoyaa atĩĩ: 'Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ, syĩtwa yaku yĩtaĩwe. Ũsumbĩ waku wũke. Kwenda kwaku kwĩke kũũ nthĩ o ta kũya ĩtunĩ.' (Mt. 6:9, 10) Ekai twone ũndũ nthembo ya wovosyo ĩkonanĩtye na kũtaĩwa, kana kũthew'a, kwa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, ũndũ ĩkonanĩtye na Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, vamwe na kwĩanĩw'a kwa kĩeleelo kya Ngai. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũũtuma twenda kũtũnga mũvea mũnango kwondũ wa nthembo ĩsu.
"SYĨTWA YAKU YĨTAĨWE"
3. Ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩtumaa tũmanya kyaũ ĩũlũ wake, na Satani amwanangĩie ĩsyĩtwa yĩu ata?
3 Kĩndũ kĩla kya mbee Yesũ wawetie ĩla mboyanĩ ya Mwĩaĩi nĩ kũtaĩwa, kana kũthew'a, kwa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. Ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩ yoka yĩtumaa twona ũnene wake w'onthe, vamwe na ũlũngalu na ũtheu wake. Nĩkyo kĩtumi o na ĩvindanĩ yĩngĩ Yesũ aimũvoya Yeova wamwĩtie "Asa Mũtheu." (Yoa. 17:11) Kwoou nĩkwĩthĩwa Yeova nĩ mũtheu, myolooto yonthe na mĩao yonthe ĩla ũtũnengae nĩ mĩtheu. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, Satani atũmĩie ũseleke mũũndanĩ wa Eteni nĩ kana atume syũmbe sya Ngai syĩthĩwa na nzika kana we Ngai nĩwaĩlĩte kũtw'ĩĩa andũ kĩla kĩseo na kĩla kĩthũku. Ĩla Satani wakenganie ĩũlũ wa Ngai, amwanangĩie ĩsyĩtwa yake ĩtheu.—Mwa. 3:1-5.
4. Yesũ atetheeisye ata kũthew'a kwa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai?
4 Yesũ aĩ kĩvathũkany'o nũndũ we nĩwendete ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova mũno. (Yoa. 17:25, 26) Na kwoou nĩwatatie a vake kũthesya ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai. (Soma Savuli 40:8-10.) Yesũ ekalile e mũĩkĩĩku na ateũvĩtya o na ĩmwe, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu nĩwoonanisye kana myolooto ya Yeova nĩ myaĩlu, na kana kĩla ũtwĩaa nĩtwĩke nĩ kwondũ wa ũseo witũ. O na ĩla Satani wamũtatie na kĩkw'ũ kĩ woo mũno, aendeeie kwĩkala alũmanĩtye na Ĩthe wake wa ĩtunĩ. Kĩu kyaĩkĩĩthisye kana mũndũ ũte na naĩ no aatĩĩe mĩao yonthe ya Ngai ateũtũla mwĩao o na ũmwe.
5. Nata tũtonya kwĩka tũkatetheesya kũthew'a kwa ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai?
5 Nata naitũ? Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtwendete ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova? Nĩ kwa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũla waĩle. Yeova endaa twĩkale twĩ atheu. (Soma 1 Vetelo 1:15, 16.) Kwoou no nginya tũmũthaithae Yeova e weka na tũitataa mũno vyũ tũmwĩw'e na ngoo yitũ yonthe. O na twathĩnw'a ata, twĩkaa ũndũ w'onthe ũla tũtonya tũatĩĩe myolooto na mĩao yake. Tweethĩwa na meko maseo, kyeni kitũ kĩkakenaa mbee wa andũ, na kĩu kĩkatumaa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩtaĩwa. (Mt. 5:14-16) Twekala ũu, ala angĩ makaĩkĩĩa kana mĩao ya Yeova nĩ mĩseo, na kana maũndũ ala Satani wawetie nĩ ma ũvũngũ. Ĩndĩ nũndũ vai mũndũ ũtavĩtya, ĩla twesa kwĩka mavĩtyo nĩtwĩlilei kuma ngoonĩ na tũiekana vyũ na maũndũ ala manangĩaa Yeova ĩsyĩtwa.—Sav. 79:9.
6. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa Yeova atwona twĩ alũngalu o na kũtw'ĩka twĩ ene naĩ?
6 Yeova atũmĩaa ĩla nthembo ya Klĩsto kũekea naĩ sya ala monanasya kana nĩmetĩkĩlĩte nthembo ĩsu. Na ala meeyumya mamũthũkũmae nũmetĩkĩlasya methĩwe athaithi make. Yeova nũmatalĩlaa ũlũngalu Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ta ana make, namo ala "malondu angĩ" nũmatalĩlaa ũlũngalu ta anyanyae make. (Yoa. 10:16; Alo. 5:1, 2; Yak. 2:21-25) Kwoou o na yu tũĩ, nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo Asa witũ nũtwonaa twĩ alũngalu methonĩ make, na nĩtũkwataa mwanya wa kũtetheesya kũthesya ĩsyĩtwa yake.
"ŨSUMBĨ WAKU WŨKE"
7. Nthembo ya wovosyo ĩtumĩte twĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kũkwata moathimo meva?
7 Kĩndũ kya kelĩ kĩla Yesũ wawetie ĩla mboyanĩ nĩ kĩĩ: "Ũsumbĩ waku wũke." Nthembo ya wovosyo ĩkonanĩtye ata na Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai? Nthembo ĩsu nĩyo ĩtumĩte ala 144,000 methĩwa matonya kũthayũũkw'a na kũthi ĩtunĩ nĩ kana metw'ĩka asumbĩ na athembi vamwe na Klĩsto. (Ũvu. 5:9, 10; 14:1) Asu nĩmo makasumbĩka Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ngai me vamwe na Yesũ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ngili. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu Yesũ vamwe na asu 144,000 makaetee andũ ala ewi moathimo ala maumanaa na nthembo ya wovosyo. Nthĩ ĩkathew'a yĩkale ũndũ mũũnda wa Eteni wailyĩ na andũ onthe aĩkĩĩku makavetewa naĩ vyũ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ ala me ĩtunĩ na ala makethĩwa kũũ nthĩ makethĩwa me ngwatanĩo ta andũ ma mũsyĩ ũmwe. (Ũvu. 5:13; 20:6) Yesũ akatumba mũtwe wa ĩla nzoka na aivetanga vyũ mathĩna onthe ala maaetwe nĩ Satani.—Mwa. 3:15.
8. (a) Yesũ eekie ata nĩ kana atetheesye amanyĩw'a make mone vata wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwonany'a kana nĩtũkwete mbau Ũsumbĩ?
8 Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ nĩwatetheeisye amanyĩw'a make mone vata wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, akililye amina kũvatiswa oou ambĩĩa kũthi kũndũ na kũndũ akĩtavany'a "ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai." (Luka 4:43) Na ĩla watavasya amanyĩw'a make ndeto sya mũthya atanamba kũsyoka ĩtunĩ, ameaĩe matw'ĩke ngũsĩ syake "kũvika itulu sya nthĩ." (Meko 1:6-8) Wĩa ũsu wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ nĩwatumie andũ kĩla vandũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ makwata mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa wovosyo na kwĩtĩkĩla Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũmasumbĩke. Ĩla twatetheesya ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto ala me kũũ nthĩ kwĩanĩsya mwĩao wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nthĩ yonthe, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtũkwete mbau Ũsumbĩ ũsu.—Mt. 24:14; 25:40.
"KWENDA KWAKU KWĨKE"
9. Nĩkĩ tũi na nzika kana Yeova akeanĩsya kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa andũ?
9 We Yesũ endaa kwasya ata ĩla wawetie ũndũ ũũ wa katatũ: "Kwenda kwaku kwĩke"? Yeova nĩwe Mũmbi. Ĩla waweta nũkwĩka ũndũ, kwake ũndũ ũsu wĩthĩawa no ta wĩanĩĩte. (Isa. 55:11) Ndesa kũeka Satani amwanangĩe kĩeleelo kyake kwondũ wa andũ. Kuma mwambĩĩonĩ waĩ wendi wa Yeova nthĩ ĩno yusũw'e nĩ nzyawa sya Atamu na Eva ite na naĩ. (Mwa. 1:28) Takeka Atamu na Eva makwie mate mwana, kĩeleelo kĩu kya Ngai kwondũ wa nthĩ kĩyĩsa kwĩanĩa. Nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩtina wa Atamu na Eva kwĩka naĩ Yeova wamaekie methĩwe na syana. Ĩndĩ nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo, Ngai nũnengete ala metĩkĩlaa nthembo ĩsu wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũvetewa naĩ na kwĩkala tene na tene. Yeova nĩwendete andũ, na wendi wake nĩ kwona ala ewi maitanĩa kwĩkala ũndũ we wamendeaa.
10. Nthembo ya wovosyo ĩtethasya ata ala makwie?
10 Ĩndĩ nata ĩũlũ wa andũ aingĩ vyũ matatalĩka ala makwie matakwatĩte mwanya wa kũmũmanya Yeova na kũmũthũkũma? Nthembo ya wovosyo nĩtumĩte ala akw'ũ methĩwa matonya kũthayũũkw'a. Nĩkwĩthĩwa Asa witũ nĩwendete andũ, akamathayũũkya na aimanenga mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa kĩeleelo kyake na wa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. (Meko 24:15) Yeova ndatanaw'a nĩ kwona andũ maikw'a. Endaa mekale thayũ. Na nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe Mbuluti ya thayũ, nĩwe ũtw'ĩkaa Ĩthe wa onthe ala mathayũũkw'a. (Sav. 36:9) Kwoou Yesũ ndaavĩtya ĩla watũmanyĩisye kũvoyaa atĩĩ: 'Asa waitũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ.' (Mt. 6:9) Yeova nũmũnengete kĩanda kya mwanya mũno wĩanĩ ũsu wa kũthayũũkya akw'ũ. (Yoa. 6:40, 44) Yesũ aisye: "Ninyie ũthayũũkyo, na ninyie thayũ." Akeanĩsya kĩanda kĩu ĩla nthĩ ĩkatw'ĩkĩthw'a nzaũ.—Yoa. 11:25.
11. Kwenda kwa Ngai nĩ kwĩva kwondũ wa yĩla "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ"?
11 Yeova ndaavathũla andũ amwe akasya asu nĩmo me oka ũkamony'a ũlau wake. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Kĩtumi nũndũ Yesũ aisye: 'O ũla wĩkaa kwenda kwa Ngai, ũsu nĩwe mwana-a-ia, na mwĩĩtu-a-ia, na mwaitũ.' (Mko. 3:35) Kwenda kwa Ngai nĩ kwona "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ" matatalĩka kuma andũnĩ ma kĩla mũthemba, na mbaĩ, na ithyomo yĩyĩtĩkĩla kũmũthaitha. Ala mekaa kwenda kwa Ngai na monanasya kana nĩmetĩkĩlĩte nthembo ya wovosyo ĩla Klĩsto waumisye, no methĩwe amwe katĩ wa ala manĩĩasya mayasya, "Ũtangĩĩo nĩ wa Ngai waitũ ũla wĩkalĩle kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ, na wa kala Katena."—Ũvu. 7:9, 10.
12. Elesya ũndũ mboya ya Mwĩaĩi ĩtũtetheeasya kũelewa kĩeleelo kya Yeova kwondũ wa andũ ala ewi.
12 Ĩla mboya ya Mwĩaĩi nĩyatũtetheesya kũmanya kĩeleelo kya Yeova kwondũ wa andũ ala ewi nĩ kĩva. Mbee, o tondũ mboya ĩsu yonanĩtye, no nginya twĩke kyonthe kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana tũthesye ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova na tũimũetee ndaĩa. (Isa. 8:13) Nthembo ya Yesũ ĩkatuma tũkwata ũtangĩĩo, na ũtangĩĩo ũsu ũkaetee ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova nguma na ndaĩa. Ũsu ti ũsengy'o nũndũ o na ũalyũlo wa ĩsyĩtwa ya Yesũ mwene nĩ "Yeova Nĩ Mũtangĩĩi." Kelĩ, Yeova akatũmĩa Ũsumbĩ wake kũetee ala ewi moathimo ala wathanĩte nũndũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo. Na ĩndĩ katatũ, mboya ya Mwĩaĩi ĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye vyũ kana vai kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kĩsa kũsiĩĩa Ngai aianĩsya kwenda kwake.—Sav. 135:6; Isa. 46:9, 10.
ONANY'A NŨTŨNGAA MŨVEA NŨNDŨ WA NTHEMBO YA WOVOSYO
13. Ũvatiso witũ wonanasya kyaũ?
13 Ũndũ ũmwe wa vata tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a kana nĩtũtũngaa mũvea kwondũ wa nthembo ya wovosyo nĩ kwĩyumya tũmũthũkũme Yeova nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo ũla twĩ naw'o nthĩnĩ wa nthembo ĩsu, na ĩndĩ tũivatiswa. Ĩla twavatiswa twĩthĩawa twoonany'a kana "twĩ ma Mwĩaĩi," Yeova. (Alo. 14:8) O na twĩthĩawa no ũndũ ũmwe na twamũkũlya Ngai atũnenge wasya mũseo wa ngoo. (1 Vet. 3:21) Nake Yeova nũtwĩthukĩĩasya na aitũthesya atũmĩĩte ĩla nthakame Klĩsto wetĩkisye. Tũyĩthĩawa na nzika kana akatũnenga kyonthe kĩla ũtwathĩte.—Alo. 8:32.
14. Nĩkĩ tũnengetwe mwĩao wa kwenda mũtũi?
14 Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a nĩtũtũngaa mũvea kwondũ wa wovosyo? Nĩkwĩthĩwa vai ũndũ Yeova wĩkaa atatongoew'e nĩ wendo, wendi wake nĩ kwona athaithi make onthe mesĩkĩe vyũ na nguma ya wendo. (1 Yoa. 4:8-11) Ĩla twenda atũi maitũ, twonanasya kana nĩtũkwenda kũtw'ĩka 'ana ma Ĩthe witũ ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ.' (Mt. 5:43-48) Mwĩao wa kũmwenda mũtũi nĩw'o ũatĩĩe mwĩao ũla mũnene vyũ wa kũmwenda Yeova. (Mt. 22:37-40) Kwoou kĩndũ kĩmwe kya vata tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a kana nĩtwendete mũtũi witũ nĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai o tondũ twĩaĩwe. Ĩla twenda andũ ala angĩ twĩthĩawa twaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Ngai. Wendo wa Ngai 'wĩanĩaw'a nthĩnĩ waitũ' ĩla twaatĩĩa mwĩao ũla ũtũnengete wa kwenda angĩ, na mũno mũno ana-a-asa maitũ.—1 Yoa. 4:12, 20.
NTHEMBO YA WOVOSYO NĨTŨETEAE "MAVINDA MA ŨVUŨKYO" KUMA KWA YEOVA
15. (a) Yeova atũathimĩte ata ũmũnthĩ? (b) Akatũathima ata ĩvinda yũkĩte?
15 Ĩla twoonany'a kana nĩtwĩtĩkĩlĩte ĩla nthembo ya wovosyo, twĩthĩawa twakwata mwanya wa kũekewa naĩ sitũ vyũ. Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana naĩ sitũ no "syanangwe." (Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 3:19-21.) O tondũ twonie mwambĩĩonĩ, nũndũ wa ĩla nthembo ya wovosyo Yeova nĩwosete athũkũmi make etĩkĩw'a mauta ta ana make. (Alo. 8:15-17) Nao nata ala "malondu angĩ"? No ũndũ ũmwe na ũandĩkĩte valũa wa kwĩsa kũtwosa tũtw'ĩke ana make na valũanĩ ũsu akaandĩka ĩsyĩtwa yitũ. Ĩndĩ Yeova akeekĩa valũa ũsu saii yake ĩla wĩtũvetea naĩ vyũ na tũivĩta ũla mũtiani wa mũthya. Eekĩa saii ĩsu nĩw'o ũkatwosa ta syana syake sya kũũ nthĩ. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũkatanĩa mũno kwĩka. (Alo. 8:20, 21; Ũvu. 20:7-9) Yeova endete syana syake mũno na wendo ũsu ndũkesa kũnyiva o na ĩndĩĩ. Namo moathimo ala twathĩtwe nũndũ wa wovosyo maikesa kũthela. (Aevl. 9:12) Na vai ĩvinda mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa wovosyo ũkethĩwa ũtatethya. Vai mũndũ o na wĩva kana kĩndũ o na kĩva kĩtonya kũtũvena mũthĩnzĩo ũsu.
16. Nthembo ya wovosyo ĩtũthaasya ata?
16 Vai ũndũ Ndevili ũtonya kwĩka akasiĩĩa ala maalyũla ngoo vyũ kwĩsa kwĩkala me ngwatanĩo na ana ala angĩ ma Yeova. Yesũ ookie kũũ nthĩ na akw'a "o ĩmwe tũ." Kwoou nthembo ĩla waumisye ndĩkaumw'a ĩngĩ. (Aevl. 9:24-26) Ĩvetaa vyũ kĩumo kĩla twatiĩwe nĩ Atamu. Na nũndũ wayo, tũi ngombo ĩngĩ sya nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Satani na tũyĩthĩawa na wia wa kĩkw'ũ.—Aevl. 2:14, 15.
17. Wendo ũla Yeova ũkwendete naw'o ũtumaa wĩw'a ata?
17 Mawatho ma Ngai nĩmakwĩkwatw'a vyũ. O tondũ mĩao na mĩvaka ĩla Yeova weekĩie wũmbinĩ wake yĩthĩawa yĩ ya kwĩkwatw'a vyũ, we ndakesa kũtũsonokya. Yeova ndaalyũkaa. (Mal. 3:6) Na eka kũtw'ĩka Yeova nũtũnengete thayũ, ethĩĩtwe e mũseo mũno kwitũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtwendete. Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩtwĩsĩ na [nĩtwĩtĩkĩlĩte] wendo ũla Ngai wĩ naw'o nthĩnĩ waitũ. Ngai nĩ wendo." (1 Yoa. 4:16) Nthĩ yonthe ĩkatw'ĩkĩthw'a nzaũ na tũkeetany'a mũuonĩ mwingĩ, na kĩla mũndũ ũkethĩwa kw'o akaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Ngai ya kwenda angĩ. Ekai ithyonthe twĩ vamwe na athaithi ala angĩ aĩkĩĩku ma Ngai me ĩtunĩ tũkĩlasye mawasya tũyasya: "Ũathimo, na ndaĩa, na ũĩ, na mũvea, na nguma, na vinya, na ũtonyĩ, nĩ ma Ngai waitũ, kũvika tene na tene. Ameni."—Ũvu. 7:12.

translation:
"Every good gift and every perfect present is from above, coming down from the Father of lights."—JAK. 1:17.
MBATHI: 148, 5
1. Is it encouraging to understand the value of the ransom?
The ransom of Jesus Christ enables us to have many encouragements. The benefit of the ransom is that it cancels out the entire debt Adam passed on to his descendants, except for continuing to live with the prospect of eternal life and a close relationship with God. This ransom now enables us to approach and obtain forgiveness for past sins time and time again. Indeed, because the ransom exercised by Christ was accepted, it provides a basis for faith and encouragement. Jesus' loyalty to Jehovah and his willingness to carry out His will provide a fine example for us, showing how we can be loyal and face trials.—Heb. 1:9.
2. (a) How did Jesus show his loyalty to Jehovah and his willingness to carry out His will, providing a fine example for us? (Consider the points mentioned.) (b) What can we learn from this example?
At one point during his earthly ministry, Jesus taught his disciples, saying: "When praying, this is what you should say: 'Our Father in the heavens, sanctified be your name. Let your kingdom come. Let your will take place, as in heaven, so also on earth.'" (Matt. 6:9, 10) As we reflect on this, we see that the ransom is connected with the sanctification, or vindication, of God's name, it is connected with God's Kingdom, and it is connected with the doing of God's will. In fact, this helps us appreciate the importance of supporting the work of the Kingdom.
"LET YOUR WILL TAKE PLACE"
3. Why does Jehovah's sovereignty matter to us, and why does Satan challenge that sovereignty?
3 Every aspect of Jesus' life demonstrated reverence for God's sovereignty. Jehovah's sovereignty is what enables us to see His greatness, His justice, and His love. This is why Jesus confidently called Jehovah "Father." (John 17:11) To honor Jehovah as Father means recognizing Him as supreme over all things. And just as Satan tried to turn Eve away from trusting in God, he uses lies and deception to lead people astray and to make God's laws seem unreasonable. Satan opposes God's rule and challenges His right to govern.—Gen. 3:1-5.
4. How did Jesus demonstrate reverence for God's sovereignty?
4 Jesus showed deep appreciation for Jehovah's sovereignty. (John 17:25, 26) And he taught his followers to revere God's sovereignty. (Read Psalm 40:8-10.) Jesus was an example, and by imitating him, we can show that we trust in Jehovah's promise that He will fulfill His purpose, and that everything happens for our good. But Satan continues to challenge this confidence, trying to make people believe that God does not care about them.
5. What can we do to remain reverent toward God's sovereignty?
5 Why should we? Should we be confident that Jehovah's sovereignty will prevail? Because of what it means to us. Jehovah wants us to live. (Read 1 Peter 1:15, 16) So let us continue to praise Jehovah and to devote ourselves whole soul to Him. And even if difficulties come, let us maintain our confidence in His promises. Let us shine brightly, being a light to others, and let this bring glory to Jehovah's name. (Matt. 5:14-16) In this way, we will prove that Jehovah's laws are righteous, and that Satan's accusations are false. Indeed, though imperfect, we can demonstrate our devotion by zealously defending Jehovah's sovereignty.—Ps. 79:9.
6. What reasons does Jehovah give us to trust in Him and to defend His sovereignty?
6 Jehovah gives us his gift through Christ to help us overcome all obstacles, even if we feel inadequate. And he strengthens faithful ones to accomplish their ministry. Jehovah has gathered together the flock of Christ so that they may receive care from shepherds, and also "other sheep" have been gathered together. (John 10:16; Acts 5:1, 2; James 2:21-25) Therefore, brothers, if the gift of shepherd Asa helps us to trust in him, then we can take advantage of the opportunity to promote his sovereignty.
"YOUR OWN PERSONALITY"
7. How can the gift of a shepherd help us to cope with difficult people?
7 One important quality Jesus demonstrated was this: "Your own personality." Does the gift of God allow for individuality? This gift empowers 144,000 spirit-anointed ones to stand out and to prove themselves loyal, even when faced with opposition and trials alongside Christ. (Revelation 5:9, 10; 14:1) They are also used to demonstrate God's personality along with Jesus over a period of thousands of years. During this time, Jesus and the 144,000 anointed ones will comfort all those who are experiencing distress because of the gift of a shepherd. It will be like a healing balm to those who have been wounded by Satan and his demons. (Revelation 5:13; 20:6) Jesus crushed the head of the serpent and destroyed the demons that had afflicted all mankind.—Genesis 3:15.
8. (a) How does Jesus show that he respects the personalities of his followers? (b) Why is it important for us to maintain our own personality?
8 Jesus showed respect for the personalities of his followers. For example, he readily allowed them to accompany him so that they could learn from him and he encouraged them to use "their voice" in proclaiming the good news. (Luke 4:43) And as he sent out his disciples to preach, he did not stifle their initiative but rather urged them to "keep on walking until [they] reach[ed] the land." (Mark 1:6-8) By allowing them freedom of expression, he helped people everywhere understand the message of life and appreciate the greatness of God's love. If we imitate the example of Christ in respecting the personalities of our brothers and sisters, we will help them feel more confident in using their voice to proclaim the good news—Matthew 24:14; 25:40.
"YOUR KINGDOM COME"
9. What can we be sure Jehovah will accomplish regarding his purpose?
9 Jesus asked a question that highlights this important point: "Your kingdom come?" Jehovah is the Originator. But he allows things to take time, because his purpose includes having people who want to serve him willingly. (Isaiah 55:11) However, Satan has tried to discredit that purpose. He misled Adam and Eve into doubting Jehovah's intentions. (Genesis 1:28) As Adam and Eve had children, God's purpose concerning mankind began to unfold. This is why the family of Adam and Eve was able to populate the earth. Jehovah wants people to live forever, and his desire is that they enjoy life to the fullest. Jehovah cares about people, and his dealings show that he wants what is best for us.
10. What does the Kingdom offer those who support it?
10 In fact, many people find it difficult to see how supporting the Kingdom can benefit them personally. The Kingdom will help people overcome their problems. For example, Asaph, a Levite, once felt discouraged, but he regained his joy by focusing on God's purpose and appreciating its benefits. (Psalm 73:15) Jehovah understands that people need help. He provides comfort. And he is the Source of comfort, the One who gives hope to those who are struggling. (Psalm 36:9) Jesus taught his disciples to pray: "Our Father in the heavens, sanctified be your name." (Matthew 6:9) Jehovah will grant opportunities for those who sincerely desire to know him better. (John 6:40, 44) Jesus said: "You practice making yourselves dead, and those who make themselves dead are dead." He was referring to the resurrection.—John 11:25.
11. How does God's kingdom differ from "the great crowd"?
11 Jehovah has chosen some people to rule with Christ in heaven. Why does he choose them? Jesus explained this when he said: "Whoever wishes to go to God must be a son and a spirit." (Mark 3:35) Going to God means being part of "the great crowd," which includes imperfect humans who hope to live forever on earth. But those who go to God also show loyalty by supporting the Kingdom and zealously proclaiming the good news, just like the faithful Christians of the first century did, saying: "The salvation comes from our God, who sits upon the throne, and from the Lamb."—Revelation 7:9, 10.
12. What practical steps can elders take to help others understand Jehovah's purpose?
12 The way elders support their brothers helps others to understand Jehovah's purpose. In fact, the reason elders are appointed is so that they can discern what is right and teach others about Jehovah's will. So let us always appreciate the fine example set by elders and cooperate fully with them as they endeavor to uphold Jehovah's standards. (Isaiah 8:13) By following the direction of the elders, we demonstrate respect for Jehovah's organization and show that we value his guidance. We should never forget that the name of Jehovah is connected to the name of Jesus Christ—"Jehovah Is Exalted." Therefore, Jehovah uses his Spirit to strengthen all those who loyally support the Kingdom work. And because of this, the way elders shepherd their flock often results in people coming closer to God and appreciating his purposes.—Psalm 135:6; Isaiah 46:9, 10.
REMEMBER THE IMPORTANCE OF THE KINGDOM WORK
13. What will we discuss?
13 One important aspect of our ministry that shows whether we are zealous and active in supporting the Kingdom work is our willingness to share good news about Jehovah, especially when we have opportunities to speak about our faith and explain our beliefs. When we do so, we are showing that we are on the side of Jehovah. Also, when we are baptized, we declare that we belong to Jehovah. (Acts 14:8) Furthermore, we show that we trust that God will fulfill his promises. (1 Peter 3:21) Because Jehovah cares for us, he strengthens us and uses us in connection with the sacrifice of Christ. We want to be courageous and speak boldly.—Acts 8:32.
14. How can we improve our speaking skills?
14 What helps us to be zealous and active in supporting the Kingdom work? It is because we know that Jehovah loves us deeply, and his love is shown by his concern for all those who obey him. (1 John 4:8-11) So when we treat others kindly, we demonstrate that we are treating them as 'brothers and sisters,' pleasing Jehovah. (Matthew 5:43-48) The best way to show kindness to others is to love Jehovah more than anyone else. (Matthew 22:37-40) Another reason why we are zealous and active in supporting the Kingdom work is that we want to honor God's name and teach others about it. When we treat others kindly, we reflect God's qualities. God's love 'motivates us' to treat others kindly, and this pleases him greatly.—1 John 4:12, 20.
THE KINGDOM WORK IS A PRIVILEGE FROM JEHOVAH
15. (a) How does Jehovah view our ministry? (b) What privilege does he give us in connection with our ministry?
15 But if we realize that we are privileged to share in the Kingdom work, we will feel motivated to take advantage of every opportunity to witness. God's law shows us that we can have confidence, even if we feel inadequate. (Read Acts 3:19-21.) And although we may be imperfect, Jehovah accepts us as his ministers and uses us to reach people's hearts. (Revelation 8:15-17) What about "other sheep"? Well, one important way we show our love for Jehovah and our brothers is by helping them to preach and to strengthen their faith. Jehovah values our willingness to support his faithful servants and appreciates our efforts. He sees our value and knows how much effort it takes to endure. Our willingness is what matters most. (Revelation 8:20, 21; Revelation 20:7-9) Jehovah supports his loyal friends generously and lovingly. That is why experienced ministers encourage us to continue in the ministry. (Hebrews 9:12) And even if a difficult situation arises, we can remain confident that Jehovah will help us to cope. Anyone who wants to serve Jehovah can find a way to overcome obstacles.
16. Does the Kingdom work bring joy?
16 Yes, because Nebuchadnezzar was willing to acknowledge that Jehovah is the One who empowers his people to accomplish great things. Jesus also felt this way when he said: "I am among you." The Kingdom work is a unifying activity. (Hebrews 9:24-26) It reminds us of what Adam had originally. And since Satan has blinded people and led them astray, we need to use discernment.—Hebrews 2:14, 15.
17. How does Jehovah's love move us to action?
17 God's love motivates us greatly. Because Jehovah gave his Son to die for obedient humans, we want to show our gratitude. Jehovah is reliable. (Malachi 3:6) And as we learn more about Jehovah, we will be more determined to please him. For example, let us demonstrate our love by obeying his commands. The Bible says: "We have come to know and believe the love that God has for us. God is love." (1 John 4:16) All those who appreciate this truth will zealously share the good news, and each individual will desire to live up to God's standard of loving others. In fact, we can unite with faithful angels in proclaiming God's qualities: "Worthy is the Lamb…to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing."—Revelation 7:12.

text:
"Ala mavikĩlaa Veva malilikanaa maũndũ ma Veva."—ALO. 8:5.
MBATHI: 22, 52
1, 2. Nĩkĩ kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi nĩ kya vata mũno kwa Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta?
NĨWĨTHĨWA waasoma ĩandĩko ya Alomi 8:15-17 ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa weekie ũu. Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩeleetye ũndũ Aklĩsto mamanyaa kana mo nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. Mamanyaa ũu nũndũ veva mũtheu nũkũsĩaa vamwe na maveva moo. Naw'o mũsoa wa mbee kĩlungunĩ kĩu ũneenete ĩũlũ wa "ala me nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ." Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Kyo kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi kĩneenete ĩũlũ wa etĩkĩw'a mauta me oka? Kana kĩlungu kĩu no kĩneenete ĩũlũ wa Aklĩsto ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ?
2 Kĩlungu kĩu kyaandĩkĩwe mũno mũno Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta. Asu makwataa "Veva" ta ala 'meteelaa kũtuwa ana, nakw'o nĩ wovosyo wa mĩĩ yoo.' (Alo. 8:23) Kwoou methĩawa meteele kwĩkala ĩtunĩ me ana ma Ngai. Ũu ũtonyekaa nũndũ nĩmavatisiwe, na Ngai nĩwatũmĩie nthembo ya wovosyo amaekea naĩ syoo, na amatalĩla kwĩthĩwa alũngalu nĩ kana matw'ĩke ana make.—Alo. 3:23-26; 4:25; 8:30.
3. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi nĩ kya vata kwa ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ?
3 Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi no kya vata kwa ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ nũndũ o namo Ngai no amose ta alũngalu. Ndeto ila Vaulo waandĩkie ilungunĩ sya mbee sya valũa ũsu wa Alomi nĩsyonanĩtye ũndũ ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o, kĩlungunĩ kya 4 Vaulo nĩwaeleisye ĩũlũ wa Avalaamu. Mũndũũme ũsu mũĩkĩĩku aĩ kw'o ĩvindanĩ ya tene o na Yeova ataanenga Aisilaeli ĩla Mĩao, o na Yesũ ataakw'a kwondũ wa naĩ sitũ. Ĩndĩ Yeova nĩwoonie mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu wa Avalaamu na amwosa ta mũlũngalu. (Soma Alomi 4:20-22.) Kwa nzĩa o ta ĩsu, nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo woo, Yeova nũtonya kũmosa ta alũngalu Aklĩsto ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ tene na tene. Na kwoou Aklĩsto asu nĩmatonya kũtetheka nĩ ũtao ũla wĩ kĩlungunĩ kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi, ũla umĩtw'e kwondũ wa ala alũngalu.
4. Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 8:21 yaĩle kũtũtetheesya tũvindĩĩsye ĩkũlyo yĩva?
4 Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 8:21 nĩyonanĩtye kana vate ndĩi tũkalika nthĩ nzaũ. Mũsoa ũsu wathanĩte kana "syũmbe nasyo ikathaw'a kuma ũkombonĩ wa wanangĩko, [ilike] ũthasyonĩ wa ũtaĩo wa syana sya Ngai." Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Tũkeethĩwa vo, na tũkakwata mũthĩnzĩo ũsu? We mwene wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ki kana ũkeethĩwa vo? Kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi kĩ na ũtao mũseo ũtonya kũũtetheesya wĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu.
"KŨLILIKANA KWA MWĨĨ"
5. Ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 8:4-13, Vaulo aneneete ũndũ wĩva wa vata?
5 Soma Alomi 8:4-13. Kĩlungu kya 8 kya ĩvuku ya Alomi nĩkĩeleetye kĩvathũkany'o kya ala mavikĩlaa 'maũndũ ma mwĩĩ' na ala mavikĩlaa 'maũndũ ma veva.' Andũ amwe no masũanĩe kana kĩlungu kĩu kĩeleetye kĩvathũkany'o kya andũ ala matesĩ ũw'o na ala mawĩsĩ, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, Aklĩsto na ala mate Aklĩsto. Ĩndĩ valũanĩ ũsu Vaulo aneenaa na 'ala me Lomi, endwa ma Ngai, ala meetiwe methĩwe atheu.' (Alo. 1:7) Kwoou kĩlungunĩ kyu Vaulo oonanasya kĩvathũkany'o kya Aklĩsto ala maatĩĩaa maũndũ ma mwĩĩ na Aklĩsto ala maatĩĩaa maũndũ ma veva. Kĩvathũkany'o kyu nĩ kĩva?
6, 7. (a) Mbivilia ĩtũmĩĩte ndeto "mwĩĩ" kwa nzĩa ta syĩva? (b) Ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 8:4-13, Vaulo aneeneaa kyaũ ĩla watũmĩie ndeto "mwĩĩ"?
6 Kwamba kũsũanĩa ndeto "mwĩĩ" ĩla yatũmĩiwe nĩ Vaulo. Aitũmĩa ndeto ĩsu oonanasya kyaũ? Ndeto "mwĩĩ" ĩtũmĩĩtwe Mbivilianĩ kwa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Mavinda amwe ĩla yatũmĩwa yĩthĩawa ĩyonany'a mwĩĩ ũũ witũ wa nyama. (Alo. 2:28; 1 Ako. 15:39, 50) O na mavinda angĩ no yonany'e andũ maileny'e ũndũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yesũ aĩ "wa ũsyao wa Ndaviti kwondũ wa mwĩĩ," na Vaulo atalaa Ayuti ta 'mbaĩ yake kwa mwĩĩ.'—Alo. 1:3; 9:3.
7 Ĩndĩ maũndũ ala Vaulo waandĩkie kĩlungunĩ kya 7 no matũtetheesye tũkaelewa kĩla waneeneaa ĩla watũmĩie ndeto "mwĩĩ" ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 8:4-13. Kĩlungunĩ kyu kya 7 oonanisye kana kwĩkala "maũndũnĩ ma mwĩĩ" nĩkwakonanĩtye na "mĩmeo ya naĩ" ĩla ĩvindanĩ yĩu 'yeekaa mamuthanĩ moo.' (Alo. 7:5) Ũndũ ũsu no ũtũtetheesye tũkaelewa kĩla Vaulo woonanasya ĩla wawetie "ala mavikĩlaa mwĩĩ" na asya kana asu "malilikanaa maũndũ ma mwĩĩ." Aneeneaa andũ ala masumbĩkĩtwe kana mendaa mũno kwĩanĩsya mawendi ma mĩĩ yoo yĩ na naĩ. Aingĩ moo nĩ andũ maatĩĩaa mĩmeo yoo na mawendi moo, methĩwe nĩ mawendi ma kũlaalaa kana nĩ mawendi o angĩ.
8. Nĩkĩ waĩ ũndũ mwaĩlu kũkany'a o na Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ĩũlũ wa 'kũvikĩla mwĩĩ'?
8 Ĩndĩ no ũseng'e nĩkĩ Vaulo woonie vata wa kũtavya Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ĩũlũ wa mũisyo wa 'kũvikĩla mwĩĩ.' W'o mũisyo ta ũsu no ũmakwate Aklĩsto ũmũnthĩ, o na kũtw'ĩka Ngai nũmetĩkĩlĩte matw'ĩke anyanyae na nũmosaa ta alũngalu? Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana vai Mũklĩsto ũtambĩĩa kũatĩĩa mawendi ma mwĩĩ wake wĩ na naĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Vaulo aandĩkie kana ana-a-asa amwe ma Lomi maĩ ngombo sya "mavu moo ene," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, maĩ ngombo sya mawendi moo ene, methĩwe nĩ mawendi ma ũlaalai kana nĩ ĩtomo ya kũya, kũnyw'a, kana o ya maũndũ angĩ. O na amwe ma ana-a-asa asu "nĩmakengaa andũ ala mate na ũthũku." (Alo. 16:17, 18; Avi. 3:18, 19; Yuta 4, 8, 12) O na ĩngĩ lilikana ve mwana-a-asa wa Kolintho wekalĩte na "mũka wa ĩthe" kwa ĩvinda. (1 Ako. 5:1) Maũndũ asu nĩmeũtuma tũelewa nĩkĩ Ngai watũmĩie Vaulo kũkany'a Aklĩsto ĩũlũ wa "kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ."—Alo. 8:5, 6.
9. Nĩ maũndũ meva tũtonya kwasya kana ti mo maneenewe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 8:6?
9 Ũkany'o ũsu nũtwaĩlĩte o na ũmũnthĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o na Mũklĩsto ũmũthũkũmĩte Ngai kwa myaka mingĩ no ambĩĩe kũtũnga kĩlĩko kyake maũndũnĩ ma mwĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩla tũkwasya ũu tũikũneenea Mũklĩsto ũla mavinda kwa mavinda ũsũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa kyaũya, kũkwata wĩa, kwĩtanĩthya, kana wĩsaa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa wendo ũla wĩthĩawa katĩ wa mũndũũme na mũka. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ asu nĩ maũndũ mekawa nĩ vakuvĩ athũkũmi onthe ma Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ nĩwatanĩaa kyaũya, na nĩwaĩthisye andũ angĩ. O na ĩngĩ, nĩweesĩ vata wa kwĩtanĩthya. Nake Vaulo nĩwaandĩkie ĩũlũ wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ nthĩnĩ wa mũtwaano.
10. Ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 8:5, 6, ndeto "kũlilikana," yonanasya kyaũ?
10 Kwoou ĩla Vaulo wawetie ndeto ii, 'kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ,' aneenaa ĩũlũ wa kyaũ? Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla Vaulo watũmĩie vau yonanasya "kũsũanĩa ũndũ mũna mũno kana kwĩkĩa ũndũ mũna ngoonĩ, na kũtũmĩa ũtonyi witũ wa kũsũanĩa tũvange maũndũ kĩlĩkonĩ kĩeleelo kĩnene kĩ kũmeanĩsya." Ala malilikanaa maũndũ ma mwĩĩ mũno mũno metĩkĩlasya mĩĩ yoo yĩ na naĩ ĩmatongoesye ĩla mekwĩka maũndũ. Mũsomi ũmwe nĩwaeleisye ĩũlũ wa ndeto ĩsu ĩtũmĩĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Alomi 8:5 asya kana yonanasya "andũ ala methĩawa o malilikene maũndũ ma mwĩĩ. Andũ ta asu mendete mũno vyũ maũndũ ma mwĩĩ, matindĩaa kũmaneenea, na nĩmamekaa na kũmakumya."
11. Nĩ maũndũ meva twaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa ĩla tũkwĩkũlya ĩkũlyo yĩĩ, 'Nĩ kyaũ twendete mũno kwĩka?'
11 Waĩ ũndũ wa vata Aklĩsto ma Lomi meyĩosye mamanye ilĩko syoo syalũmĩte maũndũnĩ meva. Mo no methĩwe mendete mũno kana masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ "maũndũ ma mwĩĩ"? O naitũ twĩ na vata wa kwĩyĩosya. Nĩ maũndũ meva twendete mũno, na nĩ kyaũ tũneeneaa mavinda maingĩ? Nĩ ũndũ wĩva twonaa wĩ wa vata? Amwe meyĩosya no methĩe kaĩ kĩla mendete mũno nĩ kũsama mbinyu syĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kwanakavya nyũmba syoo, kũmantha mĩsono myeũ ya ngũa, kwĩka mĩvango ya viasala, kũthi kũtembea kũndũ, na maũndũ angĩ ta asu. Maũndũ asu ti mathũku nũndũ nĩ maũndũ andũ mekaa kĩla mũthenya. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yĩmwe Yesũ nĩwaseũvisye mbinyu, na ve ĩvinda Vaulo weeie Timotheo anyusae "mbinyu nini." (1 Tim. 5:23; Yoa. 2:3-11) Ĩndĩ mo Yesũ na Vaulo 'matindĩaa kũneenea, na kũkumya' ũnywi wa mbinyu? Ũsu nĩw'o ũndũ ũla mendete mũno na 'matindĩaa kũneenea'? Aiee. Nata naitũ? Nĩ kyaũ twendete mũno kwĩka?
12, 13. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwosa kwa ũito maũndũ ala tũsũanĩaa kwĩka?
12 Kwĩyĩosya nĩ kwa vata mũno. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ: 'Kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ.' (Alo. 8:6) Kwoou vate nzika, ũsu ti ũndũ wa kũvũĩwa ngũĩ nũndũ no ũtume mũndũ akw'a kĩ-veva ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ na ĩvindanĩ yĩla yũkĩte ayũka kwanangwa. Ĩndĩ Vaulo ndoonanasya kana mũndũ ambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa na 'kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ' ndatetheka na mũthya wake no kwanangwa. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nũndũ nĩvatonyeka mũndũ akaalyũka. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ũla mũndũũme wa Kolintho waatĩĩie maũndũ ma "mwĩĩ" na ĩtina esa kũtengwa. Ĩndĩ aĩ o atonya kũalyũka, na nĩ w'o nĩwaalyũkile. Nĩwaekie kũatĩĩa maũndũ ma mwĩĩ na asyoka nzĩanĩ ĩla yaĩlĩte.—2 Ako. 2:6-8.
13 Ethĩwa nĩvatonyekie mũndũ ũsu aalyũka, o na ũmũnthĩ nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka Mũklĩsto akaalyũka, na mũno mũno ethĩwa ndalikĩte maũndũnĩ ma mwĩĩ mũno ta mũndũũme ũsu wa Kolintho. Kwa w'o, ũkany'o ũsu Vaulo waumisye ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩtonya kũkwata mũndũ ũla wĩthĩawa na "kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ," nĩwaĩle kũthuthya Aklĩsto makeka moalyũku ala maĩlĩte!
"KŨLILIKANA KWA VEVA"
14, 15. (a) Vaulo atũthangaaĩtye tũlilikanae kyaũ? (b) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ndeto ii, "kũlilikana kwa Veva," itonanasya?
14 Mũtũmwa Vaulo amina kumya ũkany'o ĩũlũ wa "kũlilikana kwa mwĩĩ" nĩwawetie ndeto ii nzeo: "Kũlilikana kwa Veva nĩ thayũ na mũuo." Ũsu nĩ mũthĩnzĩo mũseo ta kĩ kwa ala methĩawa na kũlilikana kwa veva! Mathĩtwe thayũ na mũuo. Tũtonya ata kũkwata mũthĩnzĩo ũsu?
15 Ndeto ii, "kũlilikana kwa Veva," iyonanasya aĩ mũndũ aĩle kwĩkala ta ũtwĩe nthĩ yake e weka. O na iyonanasya kana mũndũ ndaĩle kũsũanĩa maũndũ angĩ eka o ĩũlũ wa Mbivilia, ngwatanĩo yake na Ngai, na wĩkwatyo wake wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Lilikana kana Vaulo na angĩ ma ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa ala mamwendeeasya Ngai, nĩmeekaa maũndũ o ala mekawa kĩla mũthenya. Nĩmaĩsaa na kũnyw'a. O na angĩ moo maĩ na mĩsyĩ na nĩmathũkũmaa nĩ kana meanĩsye mavata moo.—Mko. 6:3; 1 Ath. 2:9.
16. O na kau Vaulo nĩweekaa maũndũ maingĩ mekawa o kĩla mũthenya, nĩ kyaũ kyaĩ kya vata kwake?
16 Ĩndĩ athũkũmi asu ma Ngai mayaaĩtĩkĩlya maũndũ asu ma kĩla mũthenya matw'ĩke nĩmo ma vata kwoo. Mbivilia nĩwetete kana Vaulo nĩwathũkũmaa wĩa wa kũseũvya maeema. Ĩndĩ ĩsyokete ĩkonany'a kana ũndũ ũla waĩ wa vata kwake na wawĩkaa ate kũtĩĩa waĩ kũtavany'a na kũmanyĩsya andũ. (Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 18:2-4; 20:20, 21, 34, 35.) Ũndũ ũsu now'o wathuthisye ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ma Lomi mekae. Kwoou vate nzika, kĩla kyaĩ kya vata mũno kwa Vaulo kyaĩ maũndũ ma kĩ-veva. Ana-a-asa ma Lomi nĩmaaĩle kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake na ũu now'o o naitũ twaĩle kwĩka.—Alo. 15:15, 16.
17. "Kũlilikana kwa Veva" kũtonya kũtũetee moathimo meva?
17 Tũtonya kũtetheka ata twaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Vaulo? Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 8:6 nĩyĩsũngĩĩte ĩkũlyo yĩu nesa. Yaĩtye: "Kũlilikana kwa Veva nĩ thayũ na mũuo." Ũu nĩ kwasya kana twaĩle kũeka ilĩko sitũ itongoew'e na iisumbĩkwa nĩ veva mũtheu, na kũieka isũanĩe maũndũ mosanĩte na kwenda kwa Ngai na mosũanĩo make. No twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo vyũ kana tweetĩkĩla kũsumbĩkwa nĩ "Veva" tũkekalaa nesa na twĩ eanĩe. Na ĩtinanĩ tũkakwata thayũ ũtathela, twĩthwe tũkathi ĩtunĩ kana tũkekala kũũ nthĩ.
18. "Kũlilikana kwa Veva" kũtũeteae mũuo ata?
18 Kwaekai twambe kwona nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva 'kũlilikana kwa veva nĩ mũuo.' Andũ aingĩ nĩmathĩnĩkaa mũno maimantha mũuo wa kĩlĩko. Ĩndĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩu methĩawa maiũmantha ithyĩ twĩthĩawa tũiũtanĩa. Kĩndũ kĩmwe kyonanasya kana twĩ na mũuo ũsu nĩ kĩĩ: Nĩtũtataa kĩla tũtonya twĩthĩwe na mũuo mĩsyĩnĩ yitũ na ikundinĩ sitũ. Nũseo tũkekala twĩsĩ kana ithyĩ ene vamwe na ana-a-asa ala angĩ twĩ andũ me na naĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, mavinda kwa mavinda mathĩna nĩmatonya kumĩla. Ĩla kweethĩwa ũu nĩtũthuthĩtw'e tũatĩĩe ũtao ũũ wa Yesũ: 'Ĩw'ana na mwana-a-au.' (Mt. 5:24) Wĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩw'ana ĩla twalilikana kana o nake mwana-a-asa kana mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu tũvĩtanĩsye amũthũkũmaa ũla "Ngai wa mũuo."—Alo. 15:33; 16:20.
19. Nĩ mũuo wĩva wa mwanya tũtonya kũtanĩa?
19 Na ĩndĩ ve mũuo wa mũthemba ũngĩ ũtatonya kũthimĩka. Nĩ mũuo wĩva? "Kũlilikana kwa Veva" nĩkũtumaa tũtanĩa mũuo vamwe na Mũmbi witũ. Isaia aandĩkie atĩĩ: "[We Yeova] ũkamwĩkalya e mũuonĩ mwĩanĩu we ũla kĩlilikano kyake kĩlũlũmĩle kwaku we; nũndũ nũkũĩkĩĩaa." Ndeto isu nĩsyeanĩie ĩvindanĩ ya Isaia, ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ niendeee kwĩanĩa kwa nzĩa nenange.—Isa. 26:3; soma Alomi 5:1.
20. Nĩkĩ ũũtũnga mũvea nũndũ wa ũtao ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Alomi kĩlungu kya 8?
20 Kwoou twĩthĩwe twĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta kana twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala nthĩ nzaũ tene na tene, nĩtwaĩle kwonany'a mũvea witũ kwondũ wa ũtao mũveveee ũla wĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩvuku ya Alomi kĩlungu kya 8. Tũtũngaa mũvea ta kĩ nũndũ wa ũtao ũsu ũtwĩkĩĩte vinya tũiketĩkĩlye thayũ witũ ũsumbĩkwe nĩ maũndũ ma "mwĩĩ"! Vandũ va kũsumbĩkwa nĩ mwĩĩ, nĩtwonaa ũĩ wa kwĩkala kwosana na ndeto ii mbeveee: "Kũlilikana kwa Veva nĩ thayũ na mũuo." Ũathimo wa kwĩka ũu nĩ thayũ wa tene na tene, nũndũ Vaulo aandĩkie: "Ĩtuvi ya naĩ nĩ kĩkw'ũ; ĩndĩ mũthĩnzĩo wa Ngai nĩ thayũ ũtathela nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ Mwĩaĩi waitũ."—Alo. 6:23.
