translation:
"If anyone makes distinctions between foods, let him know that God accepts them."—ROM. 14:3.
BAPTISM: 22, 52
1, 2. What question regarding baptism did we consider in the previous article?
DID you read Romans 8:15-17 in connection with the spirit you receive when you become a Christian? Reflect on this. That scripture shows what the spirit enables Christians to do. It enables us to feel love for our brothers and sisters. Also, the expression "the spirit of sonship" indicates what relationship we have with God. So, does Romans chapter 8 teach that baptism is essential for salvation? Or does that chapter show that Christians already have a loving relationship with God because of their faith?
2 This scripture was specifically written to Christians who had been baptized. Paul speaks of "life" as something they had already received, and also of the hope of future glory. (Rom. 8:23) They were showing themselves obedient to God by getting baptized. This is illustrated by the fact that they had already been sanctified, God had given them his holy spirit, and he was using them to proclaim the good news, while others may have opposed them.—Rom. 3:23-26; 4:25; 8:30.
3. Why then should we ask whether Romans chapter 8 applies to those already in a loving relationship with God?
3 Yes, indeed, Romans chapter 8 does apply to those already in a loving relationship with God because God has promised us glory. However, Paul wrote this scripture to a congregation of local believers so that they might understand this matter. For example, in Romans chapter 4, Paul explains Abraham's faith. He shows how Abraham trusted in God's promise that through him nations would be blessed, and Jesus would come as his descendant. God showed Abraham great kindness and blessed him richly. (Read Genesis 4:20-22.) So, just as in Abraham's case, God can bless faithful Christians with a loving relationship with him now and forever. And through Christ, they can benefit from the fulfillment of the promise made in Romans chapter 8, which points forward to future glory.
4. What does Romans 8:21 help us to appreciate about why we suffer?
4 Romans 8:21 assures us that our suffering is not meaningless. It says that "the whole creation keeps on groaning together until now [like] expectant waiting for the manifestation of the sons of God." This means: We are hoping, and we have a reason for hope, don't we? Do you personally have hope that you are hoping? Romans chapter 8 offers a powerful reason to remain hopeful despite your trials.
"LOOKING FORWARD TO IT"
5. According to Romans 8:4-13, what did Paul emphasize regarding what we have?
5 Read Romans 8:4-13. Romans chapter 8 highlights the contrast between those who live according to 'the ways of the flesh' and those who live according to 'the ways of the spirit.' Some wonder whether this contrast applies only to other people—those who are clearly wicked and those who are righteous—or also, in some way, to Christians themselves. In reality, Paul was addressing 'those from Rome, called ones, beloved by God, holy ones.' (Rom. 1:7) Therefore, Paul explained the contrast between Christians who walk according to the ways of the flesh and Christians who walk according to the ways of the spirit. What is the basis for this contrast?
6, 7. (a) How does the Bible define "flesh"? (b) According to Romans 8:4-13, what did Paul explain about the term "flesh"?
6 The meaning of the term "flesh" as used by Paul is important. What does he mean when he uses this term? The term "flesh" in the Bible does not refer simply to our physical bodies. It often refers to our imperfect human nature. (Rom. 2:28; 1 Cor. 15:39, 50) And sometimes it refers to bad tendencies within us. For example, the Bible says that Jesus was "of the seed of David according to the flesh," and Paul spoke of his "pride in connection with the flesh."—Rom. 1:3; 9:3.
7 In order to understand what Paul wrote in chapter 7 and how it helps us to understand the struggle each one of us faces when we use the term "flesh," read carefully Romans 8:4-13. Chapter 7 explains that being "in the flesh" is connected with being under the control of "the law of sin" which leads to 'death'. (Rom. 7:5) This helps us to understand why Paul speaks of "weakness in the flesh" and of not being able to make "the things of the spirit" happen. People who are controlled by their sinful desires may find it difficult to live up to God's standards. Many such people have strong desires and habits, whether they be desires for material possessions or other desires.
8 So, why is understanding what the "flesh" means vital for Christians?
8 The reason is because Paul wants Christians to understand the importance of overcoming the power of the "flesh". That power can lead a Christian away from God and cause him to stumble and fall. The key is that a Christian must strive to resist the desires of his own flesh. For example, Paul writes that some of the works of the "flesh" are "sexual immorality", or, more broadly, works of the desires of the flesh, whether they be desires for pleasure or something else. And some of those works are "getting drunk" and "wild parties". (Rom. 16:17, 18; Titus 3:18, 19; Jude 4, 8, 12) And others are like the Corinthian Christian who was living in "adultery". (1 Cor. 5:1) These things show us why God used Paul to warn Christians about "the manifestation of the flesh."—Rom. 8:5, 6.
9 What points should we focus on when reading Romans 8:6?
9 This desire leads both to sin and to death. Why? Because a Christian who loves God for many years may still be tempted to do things that please his own flesh. The point is that we need to constantly fight against the temptation to indulge in pleasures such as food, drink, entertainment, or satisfying our desire for affection between husband and wife. Why? Because this desire is what causes people to become disobedient to God. For example, Jesus enjoyed food, and he showed kindness to others. And yet, he could resist the temptation to overindulge. Likewise, Paul wrote about the importance of maintaining self-control in matters of marriage.
10 How does Romans 8:5, 6 define "manifestation"?
10 What did Paul mean when he used the expression "manifestation of the spirit"? The Greek text that Paul used defines "manifestation" as "making something known or revealing something hidden, and using our spiritual gift to make important matters understandable." So manifestations are things that are clearly seen and felt, and they can help us understand deeper truths. One scholar explained that this verse from Romans 8:5 uses the term "manifestations" to refer to those who truly love God. Those who do not live according to God's will often misunderstand, and they remain confused and frustrated.
11 What are some things we should avoid so that we can ask with confidence, "What shall we do to inherit eternal life?"
11 Why do some Christians find it difficult to apply Bible principles in their lives? Perhaps they feel that doing so would be "manifestations of the spirit"? Or maybe they simply lack the desire to try. But what are some practical things we can do, and why are they important? What kind of example did Jesus set? Some may think that living a Christian life means giving up certain pleasures, such as fine food, beautiful homes, stylish clothes, exciting travel, and so on. However, these things are not wrong in themselves; they are things people enjoy in everyday life. For instance, Jesus once turned water into wine, and Paul encouraged Timothy to use wine moderately "for your health." (1 Tim. 5:23; John 2:3-11) Did Jesus and Paul encourage moderation in all things? Yes, they did. So what does it mean to "be moderate" in our desires? Why is it important?
12, 13 How can we ensure that our efforts to imitate Christ are genuine?
12 Being sincere comes from the heart. Why? Because Paul wrote: "Whatever makes you happy is what you should do." (Rom. 14:6) Of course, this does not mean that we should indulge in something that could harm us spiritually or cause a brother to stumble. Paul was concerned that a Christian might excuse improper conduct by saying he was exercising his "right to choose." Was Paul suggesting that a Christian should deliberately seek out ways to test his limits? No. The point is, we need to examine our motives. For example, a Corinthian Christian began boasting about his "rights" and was causing division in the congregation. He needed to adjust his thinking, and he eventually did. He stopped focusing on his rights and started considering others.—2 Cor. 2:6-8.
13 If we notice that a brother is acting improperly, or if we ourselves struggle with a temptation, we should quickly address the matter, just as Paul did with the Corinthian Christian. Otherwise, we risk allowing harmful spiritual weeds to take root!
"MODERATION IN ALL THINGS"
14, 15. (a) What principle did Paul emphasize regarding moderation? (b) How does the expression "moderation in all things" apply?
14 The apostle Paul explained the importance of moderation by stating: "Moderation in all things." This is excellent advice for anyone struggling with moderation! It means avoiding extremes. Can we always easily apply this principle?
15 The expression "moderation in all things" applies to a Christian who wants to live in harmony with God's will. It also applies to someone who needs to be reasonable in his study of the Bible, his relationship with God, and his use of material possessions. Consider how Paul and other faithful apostles conducted themselves while traveling and preaching—they were moderate in their habits. They worked hard, yet they also took time to rest. And they appreciated hospitality without becoming overly demanding.—Matt. 6:3; 1 Thess. 2:9.
16 But even though Paul often made concessions to accommodate others, what was the main focus of his activity?
16 Despite making concessions to accommodate others, Paul's primary concern was to please God. The Bible shows that Paul was diligent in proclaiming the good news. He was willing to endure hardships so that he could continue to preach and teach people. (Read Acts 18:2-4; 20:20, 21, 34, 35.) His example encourages us today. Like Paul, we can make our ministry our priority. People responded favorably to Paul's earnestness. Those in Lystra tried to offer sacrifices to him because they saw that he had special qualities.—Acts 14:15, 16.
17 How can "moderation in all things" help us maintain spiritual health?
17 What can we learn from Paul's example regarding moderation? Philippians 4:5 reminds us of this important principle. It states: "Let your reasonableness become known to all men." This means that we should avoid extremes and strive to be balanced in our thinking and conduct, aligning ourselves with God's standards. If we are influenced by worldly thinking or allow ourselves to be overcome by "reasonableness," we will likely stumble. But if we cultivate self-control, we will remain stable and steadfast.—Prov. 19:14.
18 In what ways can "moderation in all things" benefit us?
18 Let us examine how this applies to the expression 'moderation in all things.' Many people believe that moderation is a virtue. However, sometimes they find it difficult to practice what they preach. One reason why we may struggle to maintain balance is because we are often influenced by strong emotions and desires. Therefore, we need to be vigilant so that we do not become like those who indulge in excessive pleasures and associate with immoral individuals. In view of this, let us carefully examine our habits. But to achieve this, we must imitate Jesus' example: "Become reconciled to your brother." (Matt. 5:24) If we want to enjoy peace, we must first resolve conflicts with our brothers or sisters before offering gifts at God's altar.—Ps. 15:33; 16:20.
19 How can we show discernment when deciding what entertainments to pursue?
19 And how can we avoid being distracted from spiritual pursuits? The expression "moderation in all things" encourages us to seek balance in our relationship with our Creator. Isaiah wrote: "[Jehovah] will swallow up death forever, and the Lord Jehovah will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the reproach of his people he will take away out of all the earth." So let us heed Isaiah's counsel, striving to remain loyal to Jehovah.—Isa. 26:3; read Rom. 5:1.
20 What can help us to apply the principles found in the eighth chapter of Romans?
20 Whether we are experiencing trials or enjoying relative peace, it is vital that we maintain our zeal in connection with the practical application of the principles found in the eighth chapter of Romans. We can do so by regularly reviewing this important chapter and meditating on its meaning. Those who are zealous in their service will find themselves saying, like the apostle Paul: "Christian conduct is what I am eager to practice!" This earnest desire will strengthen them, and Paul wrote: "The wages the gift God gives is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord."—Rom. 6:23.

text:
"Nzama ya Yeova yĩ na ala mamũkĩaa.12"—SAV. 25:14.
MBATHI: 27, 21
1-3. (a) Nĩkĩ tũte na nzika kana no tũtw'ĩke anyanyae ma Ngai? (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa aaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
KWĨ kũndũ kũtatũ Mbivilianĩ kũwetete kana Avalaamu aĩ mũnyanyae wa Ngai. (2 Mav. 20:7; Isa. 41:8; Yak. 2:23) Vai mũndũ ũngĩ ũwetetwe ĩmwe kwa ĩmwe Mbivilianĩ akewa aĩ mũnyanyae wa Ngai eka Avalaamu. Nũndũ wa ũu, no twasye atĩ Avalaamu e weka no we mũndũ ũla waatuma ndũũ na Yeova? Tũyĩsa kwasya ũu nĩkwĩthĩwa Mbivilia o ĩsu noyo ĩwetete kana vai mũndũ ũtatw'ĩka mũnyanyae wa Ngai.
2 Ndeto ya Ngai nĩwetete andũ aingĩ mũno, aka o na aũme, ala maĩ aĩkĩĩku na mamũkĩaa Yeova. Andũ asu nĩmamũĩkĩĩe na nĩmatw'ĩkie anyanyae. (Soma Savuli 25:14.) Kwa ngelekany'o, mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa 'mũumbĩ mũnene wa ngũsĩ.' No nginya asu onthe wawetie methĩwe maĩ anyanyae ma Ngai. (Aevl. 12:1) Asu onthe maĩ andũ aseo na ma mĩthemba yĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
3 Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩsũanĩa vamwe ĩũlũ wa anyanyae atatũ ma Yeova mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ. Twĩĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa andũ aa: (1) Luthi, ũla waĩ kĩveti ndiwa kuma Moavi na waĩ mũĩkĩĩku. (2) Esekia, ũla waĩ mũsumbĩ mũlũngalu wa Yuta. Na (3) Meli, ũla waĩ inyia wa Yesũ na waĩ na wĩnyivyo. Kũsũanĩa ũndũ kĩla ũmwe woo watatie ethĩwe mũnyanyae wa Ngai kũtonya kũtũtetheesya ata?
WENDO WA LUTHI NDWAANYIVA
4, 5. Nĩ ũtwi wĩva mũito Luthi waaĩlĩte kwĩka, na nĩkĩ ũtwi ũsu waĩ mũito? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 13.)
4 Kwamba kũkũna visa wone aka atatũ ndiwa me kyalonĩ. Mesĩle ndiĩnĩ sya Moavi ngũa syoo ikũnĩtwe nĩ kĩseve kĩla kĩ kw'o. Aka asu ndiwa nĩ Naomi na aka-a-mwana elĩ, ala nĩ Luthi na Oliva. Nayu maendangĩte Oliva aitw'a kũsyoka mũsyĩ kũla ũsyaĩwe o kũu Moavi. Ĩndĩ Naomi nũtw'ĩte vyũ kũthi nginya avike Isilaeli, kũla waumie. Ĩla Oliva wakwata nzĩa asyoka kwoo, Naomi atianĩw'a na Luthi, na o nake e na ũtwi wa kwĩka. No kwĩthĩwa ataakomana na ũndũ ũngĩ ũitavĩte ũu. No anyuvaa ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa aa elĩ: kũsyoka kwa andũ moo kũu Moavi kana kũlũmany'a na inyia wa mũũme, Naomi, na maiendany'a Mbethi-leemu.—Lu. 1:1-8, 14.
5 Waĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi mũno kwa Luthi kwasya kana nũndũ inyia na andũ angĩ ma mũsyĩ me kũu Moavi, no mamwose makekala nake. Na nengĩ ũsu waĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka nũndũ Moavi kwaĩ mũsyĩ vyũ. Syĩthĩo sya kũu nĩsyo weanĩte nasyo, kĩthyomo kya kũu nĩkyo weanĩte esĩ, na andũ ma kũu nĩmo maĩ andũ make ki. Naomi ndaĩ esa kũmwatha kana mavika Mbethi-leemu akatanĩa maũndũ ta asu. Nĩkyo kĩtumi weeie Luthi natiwe kũu Moavi. Ndaĩ esa kũĩkĩĩthya aka-a-mwana asu make kana akamamanthĩa aũme na mĩsyĩ. Ĩndĩ Luthi esĩ oou, we eekie ata? Aĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na Oliva, nũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Oliva 'asyokie kwa andũ make, na kwa ngai yake.' (Lu. 1:9-15) We Luthi nĩwĩthĩwa aĩ na mea ma kũsyokea ngai sya andũ make? Ũsũngĩo nĩ aiee.
6. (a) Luthi eekie ũtwi wĩva mũseo? (b) Nĩkĩ Mboasi waisye kana Luthi no ta ũmanthĩte wĩvitho nthwaunĩ sya Yeova?
6 No kwĩthĩwa Luthi amanyĩĩtw'e ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ Naomi kana akamanyĩw'a nĩ mũũme atanamba kũkw'a. Nĩweesĩ kana Yeova ndailyĩ ta ngai sya Moavi. Na nĩweesĩ kana Ngai ũla waaĩle kwenda na kũmũthaitha nĩ Yeova. Ĩndĩ kũmanya ũu kwĩ kw'oka kũyaĩ kũmũtethya. Luthi aĩ no nginya eke ũtwi ũla waĩle. Kwoou we nĩwatwie kũmũthaitha Yeova? Ĩĩ, nĩweekie ũtwi ũsu mũseo. Eeie Naomi atĩĩ: "Andũ maku makeethĩwa andũ makwa, na Ngai waku Ngai wakwa." (Lu. 1:16) Nĩtwĩw'aa twakiitwa ngoo twasũanĩa ũndũ Luthi wamwendete Naomi. Ĩndĩ amwendete Yeova mbee wa ũu. Nĩkyo kĩtumi o na ĩvinda yĩmwe mũndũ weetawa Mboasi wamũkathie Luthi nũndũ wa kũmantha wĩvitho nthwaunĩ sya Yeova. (Soma Luthi 2:12.) Ngelekany'o ĩsu Mboasi watũmĩie no ĩtũlilikany'e ĩũlũ wa kaswii kevithĩte nthwaunĩ sya ĩthe wako. (Sav. 36:7; 91:1-4) Yeova asũvĩie Luthi oou. Yeova nĩwamũathimie nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wake, nake Luthi ndaaĩsa kwĩlila nũndũ wa ũtwi ũla weekie.
7. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya ala makĩaa kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme Yeova?
7 O na kau andũ aingĩ nĩmemanyĩasya ĩũlũ wa Yeova, nĩmakĩaa kũmantha wĩvitho kwake. Nĩmakĩaa kwĩyumya mamũthũkũme na maivatiswa. Ethĩwa we nũkĩaa kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova, waaĩsa kwĩkũlya nĩkĩ ũkĩaa? Kĩla mũndũ wĩ thayũ e ngai ĩla ũthaithaa. (Yos. 24:15) Nĩkĩ we ũtatw'a kũthaitha Ngai ũla ũmwe waĩle kũthaithwa? Nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ ĩtonya kwonany'a nũmũĩkĩĩe Yeova nĩ kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme. Akaũtetheesya wĩanĩsye wĩvĩto waku na wũmĩĩsye mathĩna o na meva ala ũtonya kũkomana namo. Ũu now'o Ngai wamũtetheeisye Luthi.
"ALŨMANĨTYE NA YEOVA" O NA KAU MŨSYĨ WOO NDWAĨ MŨSEO
8. Elesya ũndũ Esekia waeiwe.
8 Esekia aĩ kĩvathũkany'o na Luthi nũndũ we aĩ wa mbaĩ yavathĩtwe ĩmũthũkũmae Yeova. Ĩndĩ ti Aisilaeli onthe mamũthaithaa Yeova ũndũ vaĩle. Mũsumbĩ Aasu, ũla waĩ ĩthe wa Esekia, aĩ ũmwe wa asu. Aasu aĩ mũndũ mũthũku mũno nũndũ nĩwatumie andũ ma Yuta matw'ĩka athaithi ma mĩvw'anano, o na nĩwavukisye ĩkalũ ya Yeova, yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme. O na nĩ kyeva kũvindĩĩsya ũndũ Esekia waeiwe, nũndũ ana-a-inya amwe makwie na thĩna mwingĩ maivĩvw'a me thayũ mathembewe ngai ya ũvũngũ.—2 Asu. 16:2-4, 10-17; 2 Mav. 28:1-3.
9, 10. (a) Nĩkĩ Esekia waĩ atonya kwĩana akundĩkĩte ngoo? (b) Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kũmũthatĩa Ngai? (c) Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kũsũanĩa kana no nginya twĩĩka ũndũ tweethĩie mũsyĩ kwĩkawa?
9 Esekia aĩ o atonya kwĩana e mũndũ ũkundĩkĩte ngoo na ũthatĩe Ngai. Amwe monaa ta me na kĩtumi kĩseo kya 'kũmũnyungunyĩsya Yeova' kana kũthatĩa ũseũvyo wake, o na kau maũndũ ala makomanĩte namo ti maito ta ala Esekia wakomanie namo. (Nth. 19:3) Namo angĩ maasya kana nũndũ mĩsyĩ ĩla meanĩie ti mĩseo, maikesa kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle mũseo, na no kwĩthwa makavĩtũũkany'a matambya o ala asyai moo mavĩtũũkanisye. (Esek. 18:2, 3) We wĩona mawoni asu ta ma w'o?
10 Kwosana na ngewa ya Esekia, ũsũngĩo nĩ: Aiee, ũu ti w'o o na vanini! Vai mũndũ wĩsa kũũngama akanengane kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũmũthatĩa Yeova, nũndũ Yeova tiwe ũtumaa andũ mathĩnĩa nthĩ ĩno. (Yovu 34:10) Kũneena ũla w'o, asyai no matume syana syoo iana syĩ nzeo kana ikeana syĩ nthũku. (Nth. 22:6; Ako. 3:21) Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana ethĩwa mwana asyaĩwe mũsyĩ mũthũku, no nginya etw'ĩka mũndũ mũthũku. Ũu ti w'o nũndũ Yeova anengete kĩla ũmwe witũ mũthĩnzĩo wa mwanya, naw'o nĩ ũtonyi wa kũnyuva kĩla ũkwenda kwĩka na ũndũ ũkwenda kwĩana ailyĩ. (Kũt. 30:19) We Esekia atũmĩie mũthĩnzĩo ũsu ata?
11. Nĩkĩ Esekia eana watw'ĩkie ũmwe wa asumbĩ ala aseo vyũ ma Yuta?
11 Ĩthe wa Esekia aĩ ũmwe wa asumbĩ ala athũku vyũ ma Yuta, ĩndĩ Esekia eana, atw'ĩkie ũmwe wa asumbĩ ala aseo vyũ ma nthĩ ĩsu. (Soma 2 Asumbĩ 18:5, 6.) Ĩthe wa Esekia amũtiĩe ngelekany'o nthũku vyũ, ĩndĩ vaĩ andũ angĩ aseo waĩ atonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o syoo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvinda yake kwaĩ mwathani Isaia, Mika, na Osea. Kwasũanĩa Mũsumbĩ Esekia aivindĩĩsya mũno mawathani ala aũme asu aĩkĩĩku maumasya, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu ayĩeka motao ma Yeova malike ngoonĩ yake. Nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu, nĩwatwie kũlũnga maũndũ ala ĩthe weekĩte. Na kwoou nĩwoosie ĩtambya ya kũthesya ĩkalũ, kũthemba nthembo kwondũ wa naĩ sya Aisilaeli, na kũvanga kambeini nene ya kwananga mĩvw'anano yonthe ĩla yathaithawa. (2 Mav. 29:1-11, 18-24; 31:1) O na ĩla Esekia wesa kũkomana na maũndũ maito, eekaa maũndũ e na ũkũmbaũ na mũĩkĩĩo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Senakelivu mũsumbĩ wa Asuli wavangie kũvithũkĩa Yelusaleme, Esekia amwĩkwatisye Ngai amatangĩĩe, na ndeto syake na ngelekany'o yake nĩsyatumie andũ mosa vinya. (2 Mav. 32:7, 8) Na ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩmwe ĩla Esekia wakwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo na alũngwa, nĩweelilile enyivĩtye. (2 Mav. 32:24-26) Kwoou no twasye vyũ kana Esekia ndaaeka mũeele ũla waeiwe naw'o ũmwanangĩe thayũ wake. Vandũ va ũu, aekie thayũ wake wonany'e kana we aĩ mũnyanyae wa Yeova na aĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ĩtonya kũatĩĩwa.
12. O ta Esekia, aingĩ ũmũnthĩ mekĩte ata nĩ kana matw'ĩke anyanyae ma Yeova?
12 Nũndũ nthĩ ĩno tũtwĩe andũ nĩ ang'endu mũno na mayendanĩte, syana mbingĩ ieawa nĩ asyai matasyendete na mataisũvĩaa. (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Ĩndĩ o na kau Aklĩsto aingĩ ũmũnthĩ maeetwe oou, nĩmosete ĩtambya makatw'ĩka anyanyae ma Yeova. O tondũ ngewa ya Esekia yonanĩtye, o namo nĩmaĩkĩĩthĩtye kana ti lasima thayũ wa mũndũ wanangwe nĩ ũndũ ũeetwe. Yeova nũtũnengete mwanya wa kwĩnyuvĩa ũndũ tũkwenda kwĩka, na nĩ ndaĩa nene kwitũ kũtũmĩa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nesa nĩ kana tũlũmany'e nake na tũimũetea ngatho na nguma, o tondũ Esekia weekie.
AISYE: "SISYA, NYIE NĨ NGOMBO YA MWĨAĨI"!
13, 14. Nĩkĩ no twasye kana wĩa ũla Meli wanengiwe ndwaĩ mũvũthũ? Meli asũngĩie Kavilieli ata?
13 Ĩtina wa myaka maana maingĩ kuma ĩvinda yĩu ya Esekia, ve mwĩĩtu Mũyuti kuma Nasaleti watw'ĩkie mũnyanyae mũnene wa Yeova. Vai mũndũ ũngĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ waanengwa wĩa ũilyĩ ta ũla mwĩĩtu ũsu wanengiwe. Wĩa ũla wanengiwe waĩ kũitava Mwana mũsyawa weka wa Ngai, na ĩndĩ esa kũmũsyaa aimũea! Kwasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova waĩkĩĩte mwĩĩtu ũsu wa Eli weetawa Meli mũno wĩana nginya amũnenga kĩanda kĩnenevete ũu. Ĩndĩ we wĩona Meli ta weewie ata mũthenya ũla wanengiwe wĩa ũsu?
14 Kĩla mũndũ ũtonya kũsũanĩa mũno nĩ ũndũ wĩa ũsu Meli wanengiwe waseũvĩte, ĩndĩ ayũlwa kana ve maũndũ mana matonya kwĩthĩwa mamũthĩnasya. Lilikana kana Kavilieli amũtavisye kana akaitava o na atakomete na mũndũũme. Mũlaĩka ũsu wa Ngai ndaatavya Meli atĩ nũkwĩtwaa newe mwene akatavye andũ ma mũsyĩ na atũi kĩla kĩtumĩte aitava. Kwoou no kwĩthĩwa Meli eekũlasya mo andũ memwosa ata. Na no kwĩthĩwa athĩnĩkaa asũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mũndũũme ũla wamwĩvaĩtye. Esaa kũmũĩkĩĩthya Yosevu ata kana ndaakoma na mũndũũme o na kau aĩ mũito? Na eka ũu, kĩanda kĩu wanengiwe kya kũea, kũsũvĩa, na kũmanyĩsya Mwana mũsyawa weka wa Ũla wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe kĩyaĩ kĩanda kya ngũĩ! Mwa o na tũyĩsa kũmanya maũndũ onthe ala Meli weew'aa maimũthokoa kĩlĩko Kavilieli amina kũneena nake! Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ ũsũngĩo ũla wanengie Kavilieli. Amũsũngĩie amwĩa: "Sisya, nyie nĩ ngombo ya Mwĩaĩi [Yeova]; nĩwĩthĩwe kwakwa o ta ndeto syaku."—Luka 1:26-38.
15. Nĩkĩ no twasye Meli aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu mũno?
15 Meli aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu mũno, kana ti w'o? Mũndũ mũka ngombo eethĩawa eyumĩtye eke ũndũ vwana wake ũkwenda. Kwoou ĩla waisye we nĩ ngombo ya Yeova, aisye ũu nũndũ aiĩte maũndũ onthe mokonĩ make, na nĩweeyumĩtye eke ũndũ we ũkwenda. Nĩweeyumĩtye amũthũkũme vyũ o na ethĩwa emwĩa eke ata. Ĩndĩ kyo nĩ kyaũ kyatumĩte ethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo ta ũsu? Vai mũndũ ũsyaawa na mũĩkĩĩo. Nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo, no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito na tũitetheew'a nĩ Ngai. (Aka. 5:22; Aev. 2:8) We Meli aaĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana alũlũmĩlye mũĩkĩĩo wake? Ĩĩ, na ve kĩtumi kya kwasya ũu. Kwaekai twone ũndũ weethukĩĩasya vamwe na ndeto syake.
16. Twĩsĩ ata kana Meli nĩweethukĩĩasya nesa ĩla angĩ meũneena?
16 Ũndũ Meli weethukĩĩasya. Mbivilia ĩtũnengete ũtao ũũ: "Kĩla mũndũ nĩethĩwe mwĩwi wa mĩtũkĩ, na kũlea kũneena mĩtũkĩ." (Yak. 1:19) We Meli nĩweethukĩĩasya nesa ĩla angĩ meũneena? Ũsũngĩo nĩ ĩĩ. Ĩvuku ya Luka nĩyĩwetete mavinda elĩ Meli weethukĩĩisye nesa maũndũ maito ala mawetawa, na ĩtina amantha ĩvinda amavindĩĩsye. Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩ ĩla Yesũ wasyaiwe, ĩla aĩthi maendie kũla kwĩ Meli na mamũtavya ũvoo ũla matavĩtw'e nĩ mũlaĩka. Na ĩvinda yĩngĩ nĩ yĩla Yesũ waĩ kĩmwana kya myaka 12. Ĩvinda yĩu atavisye Meli ũndũ wamũsengy'a. Mavinda asu elĩ, Meli nĩweethukĩĩisye kĩla wataviw'e, akĩkĩa kĩlĩkonĩ, na akĩvindĩĩsya mũno.—Soma Luka 2:16-19, 49, 51.
17. Nĩ kyaũ tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya twasũanĩa ndeto ila Meli waneenaa?
17 Ndeto sya Meli. Ndeto mbingĩ ila Meli waneenie iyaandĩkwa Mbivilianĩ. Ũneeni wake ũla mũasa vyũ wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Luka 1:46-55. Ndeto isu syĩ nthĩnĩ wa ĩandĩko yĩu syonanĩtye kana Meli nĩwasomete Maandĩko nesa. Ndeto isu syĩthĩawa iilyĩ ta imwe syĩ ĩla mboyanĩ ya Aana, inyia wa mwathani Samueli. (1 Sam. 2:1-10) No kwĩthĩwa ũneeninĩ ũsu Meli awetie ndeto syĩ kũndũ ta 20 Maandĩkonĩ. Maũndũ asu metũĩkĩĩthya kana Meli ndakĩaa kũneenea maũndũ ala weemanyĩĩtye Maandĩkonĩ. Nĩweekĩĩte ngoonĩ maũndũ onthe ala wamanyĩĩtw'e nĩ ũla Mũnyanyae mũnene, Yeova Ngai, na nĩwamaweteaa andũ angĩ.
18. Tũtonya kwĩka ata twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Meli?
18 O naitũ mavinda amwe Yeova no atũnenge wĩa tũtonya kwona wĩ vinya mũno. Ĩndĩ o tondũ Meli weekie, nĩtwĩnyivasye na tũyia maũndũ onthe mokonĩ ma Yeova, tũte na nzika kana nũkũtũtetheesya. No twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Meli ethĩwa tũkethukĩĩasya nesa ĩla tũũmanyĩw'a ĩũlũ wa Yeova na ieleelo syake, ethĩwa tũkavindĩĩasya kĩla tweemanyĩsya, na ethĩwa tũkatanĩaa kũtavya angĩ kĩla tweemanyĩsya.—Sav. 77:11, 12; Luka 8:18; Alo. 10:15.
19. Nĩ kyaũ twĩsĩ tũkakwata ethĩwa tũkaendeeaa kwĩyĩelekany'a na andũ ala maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu?
19 Nũũ ũtonya kwasya kana Luthi, Esekia, na Meli mayaĩ anyanyae ma Yeova o tondũ Avalaamu waĩ mũnyanyae wa Yeova? Asu onthe vamwe na ala angĩ mawetetwe ũla 'mũumbĩnĩ mũnene wa ngũsĩ,' na vamwe na angĩ methĩĩtwe me aĩkĩĩku o na kuma ĩvinda ya tene, nĩmakwatie ĩla ndaĩa nene ya kwĩthĩwa me anyanyae ma Ngai. Tũikaaeke kwĩyĩelekany'a na andũ ta asu. (Aevl. 6:11, 12) Twaendeea kwĩka ũu, no twĩkale tũte na nzika kana ĩtuvi yĩla tũkakwata nĩ ĩnene, nayo nĩ kwĩthĩwa anyanyae ma Yeova tene na tene!

translation:
"Jehovah's people have always been loyal."—PS. 25:14.
FOOTNOTE: 27, 21
1-3. (a) Why should we be zealous in our ministry, and why should we trust in God? (b) What will help us to remain zealous?
WHEN faced with difficult situations, both Hezekiah and Abraham put their faith in God. (2 Ki. 20:7; Isa. 41:8; Jas. 2:23) Like those men, each of us can demonstrate our faith in God like Abraham. But how did Abraham show that he was a friend of Jehovah? Let us examine what the Bible says about his example so that we too may strengthen our faith in God.
2 God has favored many people, young and old, who have shown loyalty to Him. These ones proved they were willing to trust in Him. (Read Psalm 25:14.) For instance, the apostle Paul spoke of "an outstanding minister" of the good news. Did others also recognize this man's zeal for God? (Acts 12:1) Yes, they did, and many people benefited from his efforts.
3 We will now consider the examples of three faithful men whom the Bible mentions: (1) Lot, who lived near Moab and remained righteous. (2) Hezekiah, who defended Judah. And (3) Melchizedek, who was a priest of Jesus and brought out provisions. By examining their experiences, can we learn ways to show our loyalty to God and avoid being discouraged?
LOT ESCAPES DESTRUCTION
4, 5. What challenge did Lot face, and what challenge do we face? (See accompanying picture on page 13.)
4 It is good to remember this about those ancient ones. The people of Moab were descended from Lot's daughter, and they caused trouble for Israel throughout their history. But Lot also had a family: his wife Naomi and her two daughters-in-law, Orpah and Ruth. Orpah and Ruth urged Naomi to stay in Moab, but she decided to return to Israel. However, Ruth chose to go with Naomi, and Naomi welcomed her. So they both went back, but it involved some difficulty. One problem was that the law said that Moabites could not marry Israelites, so Naomi worried about what would happen to them. Also, Naomi knew that life in Israel might be hard for Ruth. Nevertheless, Naomi allowed Ruth to accompany her to Bethlehem.—Ru. 1:1-8, 14.
5 What did Ruth have to give up to associate with Jehovah's people? She gave up her home and relatives in Moab, and she faced uncertainty about the future. And she willingly gave up her former way of life. It meant giving up her homeland and her gods, and associating with a new group of people who worshiped Jehovah. Naomi knew that Ruth would face difficulties in Bethlehem, but she didn't try to stop her. This is why Ruth went with Naomi to Moab. She was willing to care for Naomi's son and raise him as her own. So how did Ruth feel about going to Bethlehem? Did she hesitate? She discussed the matter with Naomi, and the Bible says that Orpah "kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her," saying, 'Do not urge me to leave you or to turn back from following you. For wherever you go, I will go; and wherever you lodge, I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.' (Ru. 1:9-15) Was Ruth motivated by selfish reasons when she decided to go with Naomi? Certainly not.
6. (a) What decision did Ruth make that pleased Naomi? (b) Why did Boaz commend Ruth for showing faith in Jehovah?
6 Ruth showed that she trusted in Jehovah when she chose to associate with Naomi and when she demonstrated loyalty to her. He also recognized that Jehovah had brought her to Moab. And he realized that God was able to reward her faithfulness. Knowing this helped her to remain loyal. Ruth made a deliberate choice to trust in Jehovah. How can we imitate her example? Yes, we too should make a deliberate choice to trust in Jehovah. Naomi said: "Your people will be my people, and your God my God." (Ru. 1:16) We can learn much from the way Ruth treated Naomi. She remained loyal to Jehovah in doing so. That is why a man named Boaz praised Ruth for showing faith in Jehovah. (Read Ruth 2:12.) Let us like Boaz show appreciation for those who demonstrate faith in Jehovah. (Ps. 36:7; 91:1-4) Jehovah blessed Ruth abundantly. Jehovah rewarded her loyalty, and Ruth experienced the fulfillment of her hope.
7. What can we learn from Ruth's example about being courageous in serving Jehovah?
7 Many people have come to know Jehovah, but they find it difficult to show their devotion to him. They may fear disapproval or persecution. If you want to show courage in serving Jehovah, what can you do? Each person has a personal relationship with God. (Jos. 24:15) Will you allow yourself to be influenced by others and stop worshipping God? If you value your close relationship with Jehovah, you will not let fear prevent you from expressing your faith. Be willing to defend your beliefs and stand up for what is right, even if it means facing opposition. This is what God did for Ruth.
"REMAIN LOYAL TO JEHOVAH" AND LIKE RUTH MAKE A DELIBERATE CHOICE
8. Consider the example of Ezekiel.
8 Ezekiel prayed to Jehovah about his vision because he felt unworthy to serve Jehovah. The Israelites had repeatedly broken their covenant with Jehovah. High Priest Ahaz, who was related to Ezekiel, was wicked. Ahaz sent men to Babylon to learn about idolatry, and he made an altar to Baal, which he placed in Jerusalem. But Ezekiel showed courage when he condemned Ahaz's actions, and he boldly spoke against false worship.—2 Ki. 16:2-4, 10-17; 2 Chron. 28:1-3.
9, 10. (a) How did Ezekiel demonstrate courage? (b) How can we show courage in our worship of God? (c) How can we remain loyal when faced with pressure to compromise our integrity?
9 Ezekiel demonstrated courage by speaking out against wickedness and denouncing false worship. Some may feel that using the expression "to provoke Jehovah" or showing zeal is extreme, but they should remember that Ezekiel also used strong language. (Prov. 19:3) However, we must always be tactful and considerate, and avoid making accusations that are harsh or unkind.—Ezek. 18:2, 3. What lessons can we learn from this?
10 In harmony with what was said about Ezekiel, ask yourself: 'Would I say that, or would I not?' No true Christian wants to misuse the name of God when trying to persuade someone to worship Jehovah, knowing that Jehovah does not send people to destruction without good reason. (Job 34:10) Therefore, let us not make rash judgments or pronounce severe decrees. (Prov. 22:6; Acts 3:21) It would be wrong to condemn anyone harshly, and we should not allow ourselves to become bitter. It would not be right to think that Jehovah takes pleasure in the pain of his creatures, because he delights in seeing them live and progress.—Ps. 30:19. So how did Ezekiel show tactfulness?
11. Did Ezekiel ever speak kindly to some of the older men of Judah?
11 Ezekiel spoke kindly to some of the older men of Judah, and he showed respect for their position. (Read 2 Kings 18:5, 6.) Ezekiel also took pains to explain matters thoroughly so that those men could understand. For example, he consulted prophets like Isaiah, Micah, and Hosea. King Hezekiah appreciated the counsel of these wise men, and he sought to obey Jehovah's commands fully. Because of this, he led the people in making important changes. And he courageously carried out a cleansing of the temple, restored true worship, and removed the idolatrous objects that had defiled it. (2 Ki. 29:1-11, 18-24; 31:1) But Hezekiah also made mistakes, and he learned from them. For instance, when Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against Jerusalem, Hezekiah prayed to God for help, and his prayer and his humble attitude moved God to deliver his people. (2 Ki. 32:7, 8) And when Hezekiah became sick and was near death, he earnestly begged for recovery. (2 Ki. 32:24-26) Today, too, we can learn much from Hezekiah's example. We can be grateful for the privilege of having spiritual men among us who lovingly shepherd us and teach us what the Bible says.
12. So, how did Hezekiah show that he valued the advice of godly men?
12 In our time, we need to be discerning and cautious, recognizing that there are many who present themselves as teachers but are actually misleading others. (2 Timothy 3:1-5) However, genuine Christians value the advice of godly men. Like Hezekiah, they realize that listening to such counsel can save them from error. Jehovah gives us the opportunity to benefit from the wisdom of others, and he wants us to use it wisely, accepting reproof and correction, just as Hezekiah did.
"YOU ARE THE SALT OF THE EARTH!"
13, 14. What lessons can we draw from Melchizedek's experience? Did Melchizedek ever fight battles?
13 Many years later, during the time of Jehosaphat, a man named Jahaziel prophesied about Jehovah's help. This reminds us that God often uses imperfect humans to convey his message. Those whom God appoints are like his Son, and we should support them! Consider how Jehovah used the man Eli to train Samuel, a young Levite. Do you see parallels between Samuel and Melchizedek?
14 Everyone who wants to please God must support those whom God appoints, even if they have flaws or make mistakes. It is similar to how Jehosaphat listened to Micaiah, despite his unpopular prophecies. God's angel strengthened Melchizedek so he could lead his people and deliver them from their enemies. But Melchizedek also needed encouragement from others. He benefited from the support of those who appreciated him. Was Melchizedek able to encourage others too? And did he remain humble, recognizing his dependence on God? Like Joseph, did he avoid becoming arrogant? Furthermore, this appointment of Melchizedek illustrates the importance of proclaiming God's unique Son, the Only-Begotten One, and teaching people about his Kingdom! Let us strive to learn more about Melchizedek, because Samuel's confidence in Jehosaphat is an example for us! So let us examine what happened when Jehosaphat appointed Melchizedek. He encouraged him, saying: "You are God's champion; be strong and courageous."—Luke 1:26-38.
15. What then can we learn from Melchizedek's example?
15 Does Melchizedek's example teach us something important? A person who is favored by God often feels inadequate. Just as you feel like God's champion, you may feel unworthy, yet God has chosen you and will empower you to accomplish his purpose. He empowers you to succeed, even though you may feel incapable. Is this not why God uses imperfect people? A person needs faith to accept God's assignment. If we are assigned a task, we should rely on God's strength and work hard. (Acts 5:22; Eph. 2:8) Did Melchizedek show faith when he accepted his assignment? Yes, and he had good reason to do so. Let us consider how his faith affected others.
16. How can we imitate Melchizedek in showing appreciation for others?
16 Melchizedek showed appreciation. The Bible highlights this quality by saying: "Every generous gift comes from above, along with every perfect present." (Jas. 1:19) Did Melchizedek show appreciation when he welcomed Abraham? Absolutely. Luke's account shows that Melchizedek generously provided Abraham with provisions and comfort after his victories, and he expressed his gratitude. One instance is when Jesus was born, when he went to visit Melchizedek and brought gifts with him through an angel. And another time is when Jesus was 12 years old. That event helped Melchizedek understand what was happening. In those instances, Melchizedek appreciated everyone he met, listened carefully, and expressed his gratitude.—Read Luke 2:16-19, 49, 51.
17. Why should we strive to be hospitable like Melchizedek was?
17 Melchizedek's hospitality. Much of Melchizedek's hospitality is recorded in the Bible. His expression of joy is found in Luke 1:46-55. This song reveals something about why Melchizedek valued the Scriptures. This song is similar to Hannah's prayer, the mother of the prophet Samuel. (1 Sam. 2:1-10) It is evident that Melchizedek often expressed his feelings in songs, which were included in over 20 scriptures. These things demonstrate that Melchizedek deeply cherished and understood the Scriptures. He always remembered the great Creator, Jehovah God, and he wanted others to know him.
18. How can we imitate the example of Melchizedek's hospitality?
18 We can show our love for Jehovah by doing what we can to help others spiritually. Like Melchizedek did, we can be generous and share the good news about Jehovah with others, whether they are rich or poor. By imitating Melchizedek's example, we will also come to appreciate more fully Jehovah's purpose and requirements, and we will be moved to tell others about them, and we will unite in helping others learn about them.—Ps. 77:11, 12; Luke 8:18; Prov. 10:15.
19. What can we do to continue to associate with those who have a positive influence?
19 Why should we imitate faithful men like Abraham, Hezekiah, and Melchizedek, who were close friends of Jehovah? They showed faith despite facing trials, and others saw their loyalty to 'the Most High God.' Because of their fine example, some were encouraged to worship the true God. Let us imitate such men. (Heb. 6:11, 12) Let us strive to remain loyal to Jehovah always, even when we face difficulties, and let our friendship with Jehovah grow stronger and stronger!

text:
"Sisyai, ũndũ ũseo ũnenevete na ũndũ ũseũvĩte ana-a-asa mekalan'ya vamwe me ũmwe!"—SAV. 133:1.
MBATHI: 149, 30
1, 2. Nĩ ũmbano wĩva mwakanĩ ũũ wa 2018 ũkalũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ kwa nzĩa ya mwanya, na nĩkĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MATUKŨ 31, Mwei wa 3, 2018, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova na andũ angĩ aingĩ mendeeaw'a nĩ ũw'o makeethĩwa na ũmbano wa kũlilikana Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi ũla wĩkawa kĩla mwaka. Syũa yĩithũa mũthenya ũsu nĩw'o andũ milioni mbingĩ makombana malilikane kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto. Kĩla mwaka ũmbano ũsu nũlũlũmĩlasya ngwatanĩo ya andũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ kwa nzĩa ya mwanya kwĩ ũmbano ũngĩ o na wĩva.
2 Mũthenya ũsu ũitw'ĩka nĩwathela, no nginya wĩthĩe Yeova na Yesũ nĩmatanaa mũno moona andũ milioni mbingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ maendeee kũmbana kwondũ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Mbivilia yathanie kana "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ, yĩla mũndũ o na wĩva ũtatonya ũyĩtalĩkya, kuma andũnĩ ma kĩla mũthemba na mbaĩ na ngo na ithyomo," yĩkasya ũũ na wasya mũnene: "Ũtangĩĩo nĩ wa Ngai waitũ ũla wĩkalĩle kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ, na wa kala Katena." (Ũvu. 7:9, 10) Nĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya mũno kwona andũ maingĩvĩte ũu maietee Yeova na Yesũ ndaĩa nene kwa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ!
3. Twĩsũngĩa makũlyo meva ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩsũngĩa makũlyo aa ana: (1) Kĩla ũmwe witũ atonya kwĩyũmbanĩsya na kũtetheka ata nĩ ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? (2) Ũmbano ũsu ũlũlũmĩlasya ngwatanĩo ya andũ ma Ngai ata? (3) Kĩla ũmwe witũ atonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana alũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo ĩsu? (4) Ve ĩvinda tũkombana ya mũthya tũlilikane kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? Ethĩwa nĩ w'o, nĩ ĩndĩĩ?
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KWĨYŨMBANĨSYA NA KŨTETHEKA NĨ ŨMBANO ŨSU
4. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũtata ũndũ vatonyeka tũikatĩe ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ?
4 Kwasũanĩa nĩkĩ ũmbano ũsu nĩ wa vata mũno. Lilikana kana kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũmũthaitha Yeova. Kwoou vate nzika, Yeova na Yesũ nĩmonaa andũ ala mekĩaa kĩthito maikatĩe ũmbano ũsu wa mwanya. O naitũ nĩtwendaa mone kana tũilea kũthi kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ ate o tũkwatiwe nĩ thĩna mũnene tũtesa kũwathũkĩa. Ĩla twoonany'a na meko maitũ kana nĩtwonaa maũmbano me ma vata mũno, twĩthĩawa tũyongeleela Yeova kĩtumi kya kũekana na masyĩtwa maitũ nthĩnĩ wa "ĩvuku ya ũlilikan'yo." Yĩu no yo yĩla 'ĩvuku ya thayũ' yĩandĩkawa masyĩtwa ma ala maĩle kwĩsa kũnengwa thayũ ũtathela.—Mal. 3:16; Ũvu. 20:15.
5. Tũtonya kũtũmĩa ata mĩthenya ĩla yĩthĩawa ĩtiele ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ ũtanavika 'twĩthime ethĩwa twĩ o ũla mũĩkĩĩonĩ'?
5 Mĩthenyanĩ ĩla yĩthĩawa ĩtiele ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ ũvike, nĩtwaĩle kũmantha ĩvinda ya kũvoya na kũvindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova. (Soma 2 Akolintho 13:5.) Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata? Nĩ kwa 'kwĩthima ethĩwa twĩ o ũla mũĩkĩĩonĩ.' Nĩ kana twĩthime, nũseo tũkekũlya makũlyo ta aa: 'Nyie nĩnĩĩkĩĩaa vyũ kana vai ũseũvyo ũngĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ wĩkaa kwenda kwa Yeova eka ũũ witũ? Nĩnĩtataa ũndũ ndonya nĩtavany'e na ndimanyĩsya angĩ ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ? Meko makwa nĩmonanasya kana ndi na nzika twĩkalĩte mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, na kana mũthya wa ũsumbĩki wa Satani wĩ vakuvĩ? Nĩnĩendeee kũmwĩkwatya Yeova na Yesũ o ũndũ namekwatĩtye ĩla neeyumisye nĩmũthũkũme Yeova Ngai?' (Mt. 24:14; 2 Tim. 3:1; Aevl. 3:14) Kũvindĩĩsya makũlyo asu no kũtũtetheesye tũmanye mũĩkĩĩo witũ ũilyĩ ata.
6. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩkatuma tũkwata thayũ ũtathela? (b) Mũtumĩa ũmwe ekaa ata kĩla mwaka eyũmbanĩsye kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? Ũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake ata?
6 Soma na ũivindĩĩsya maũvoo ala methĩawa maeleetye ũndũ ũmbano ũsu ne wa vata. (Soma Yoana 3:16; 17:3.) Tũyĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela tũtesie kwosa ĩvinda 'tũmũmanye' Yeova, na tũisyoka 'tũmwĩtĩkĩle' Mwana wake mũsyawa weka, Yesũ. Kwoou nĩ kenda wĩyũmbany'e, wĩona ata ũkamantha maũvoo kauta matonya kũũtetheesya ũlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yaku vamwe na Yeova na Yesũ? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩthĩĩtwe e mũtumĩa kwa ĩvinda ĩasa wĩkaa. Kwa myaka mingĩ ethĩĩtwe ayũmbany'a ilungu sya Mũsyaĩĩsya ila ineeneete mũno mũno kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, vamwe na maũndũ ala Yeova na Yesũ mekĩte makonany'a kana nĩmatwendete. Vatiele syumwa nini ũmbano ũsu ũvike, osaa ilungu isu akaisoma ĩngĩ na aivindĩĩsya vata wa kũthi ũmbanonĩ ũsu. O na nĩwĩsaa kwĩkala akamantha kĩlungu kĩmwe kana o ilĩ akongeleela ila wĩthĩawa ombanĩtye. Mũtumĩa ũsu esĩte kwĩthĩa nĩwĩmanyĩasya maũndũ meũ kĩla mwaka nũndũ wa kũsyokeleela ilungu isu, vamwe na kũsoma na kũvindĩĩsya ilungu sya Mbivilia ila twĩthĩawa tũaĩwe tũsome ĩvindanĩ yĩu. Na ũndũ ũla wa vata nĩ kana kĩla mwaka ew'aa amwenda Yeova na Yesũ mũnango. Kwĩthĩwa na mũvango ta ũsu no kũũtetheesye wende Yeova na Yesũ mũnango na ũimatũngĩaa mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kĩla mekĩte. Kĩu no kĩtume ũtetheka vyũ nĩ ũmbano ũsu.
ŨMBANO ŨSU NŨLŨLŨMĨLASYA NGWATANĨO YITŨ
7. (a) Yesũ avoyie ĩũlũ wa kyaũ ũtukũ ũla wambĩĩisye Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi? (b) Twĩsĩ ata kana Yeova nũsũngĩĩte mboya ya Yesũ?
7 Ũtukũ ũla Yesũ wambĩĩisye Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi, avoyeie aatĩĩi make methĩwe na ngwatanĩo o tondũ we na Ĩthe me ngwatanĩo. (Soma Yoana 17:20, 21.) Yeova nĩwasũngĩie mboya ĩsu Mwana wake mwendwa wavoyie, na nũndũ wa ũu ũmũnthĩ kwĩ andũ milioni mbingĩ maĩkĩĩaa kana nĩwatũmie Mwana wake. Vai ũmbano ũngĩ wa andũ ma Ngai wonanasya nesa ngwatanĩo ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ta ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Ũmbano ũsu wĩkawa kũndũ kwingĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩ andũ ma nthĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o na langi syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kũndũ kũmwe ndwĩsa kwĩw'a atĩ andũ ma ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nĩmombanie vamwe mathaithe, o na moombana, andũ amwe monaa kĩndũ kyu kĩsaanĩtye mũno. Ĩndĩ Yeova na Yesũ moona ngwatanĩo ĩsu matanaa mũno!
8. Yeova anengie Esekieli ũtũmane wĩva ũkonetye ngwatanĩo?
8 Ithyĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova tũiseng'aa twoona ngwatanĩo ĩla twĩthĩawa nayo. Na kĩtumi nũndũ o na Yeova nĩwathanie tũkeethĩwa na ngwatanĩo ĩsu. Kwasũanĩa ũtũmane ũla wanengie mwathani Esekieli. Amwĩie akwatany'e mĩtĩ ĩlĩ, ũmwe waandĩkĩtwe "kwa Yuta" na ũla ũngĩ waandĩkĩtwe "kwa Yosevu." (Soma Esekieli 37:15-17.) Kĩlungu kya "Makũlyo Kuma kwa Asomi Maitũ" kya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya Mwei wa 7, 2016, kyaeleisye ũtũmane ũsu ũũ: "Yeova amũnengie Esekieli ũvoo wa wĩkwatyo, ũla wathanĩte ĩũlũ wa ngwatanĩo ĩla ĩkethĩwa vo mbaĩnĩ ya Isilaeli ĩtina wa kũsyoka Nthĩ ya Watho. O na ĩngĩ, ũvoo ũsu nĩwathanĩte ĩũlũ wa ngwatanĩo ĩla ĩkethĩwa andũnĩ ma Ngai. Ngwatanĩo ĩsu yaĩ yambĩĩe mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo."
9. Kĩla mwaka ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ twonaa ata ngwatanĩo ĩla Esekieli wathanie?
9 Kuma mwaka wa 1919 na kũendeea, Yeova nĩwambĩĩe kũvanga o kavola etĩkĩw'a mauta nesa ĩngĩ na amombany'a. Kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o nĩmo ũla mũtĩ waandĩkĩtwe "kwa Yuta." Na ĩndĩ tũendeangĩe, ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ nĩmaendeeie kwongeleka na makwatana na etĩkĩw'a mauta. Asu me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ nĩmo maelekanĩtw'e na ũla mũtĩ waandĩkĩtwe "kwa Yosevu." Ikundi isu syelĩ syakwatanw'a syatw'ĩkie "ĩĩthya yĩmwe." (Yoa. 10:16; Nzek. 8:23) Yeova athanie kana akakwatany'a mĩtĩ ĩsu ĩlĩ ĩtw'ĩke mũtĩ ũmwe kw'okonĩ kwake. (Esek. 37:19) Ũmũnthĩ ikundi isu syelĩ ithũkũmaa syĩ ngwatanĩo itongoew'e nĩ Mũsumbĩ ũmwe, nake nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto. Ũsu nĩwe wathaninĩ wa Esekieli wĩtĩtwe nĩ Ngai "mũthũkũmi wakwa Ndaviti." (Esek. 37:24, 25) Kĩla mwaka, ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto nĩtwonaa ngwatanĩo ĩsu ya mwanya yawetiwe nĩ Esekieli nũndũ etĩkĩw'a mauta na "malondu angĩ" nĩmombanaa vamwe ũmbanonĩ ũsu. Ĩndĩ kĩla ũmwe witũ atonya kũsũvĩa ata ngwatanĩo ĩsu na aimĩlũlũmĩlya?
ŨNDŨ KĨLA ŨMWE ŨTONYA KŨLŨLŨMĨLYA NGWATANĨO YITŨ
10. Tũtonya ata kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo ya andũ ma Ngai?
10 Nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo ya andũ ma Ngai nĩ kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo. Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ nĩweekĩie vinya amanyĩw'a make mekalae menyivĩtye. (Mt. 23:12) Tweethĩwa na ngoo syĩnyivĩtye tũiketũlasya ta andũ ma nthĩ. Ĩndĩ wĩnyivyo ũkatumaa twĩnyivĩsya ala matongoesye, na veva ũsu nũtumaa kĩkundi kĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo. Na kĩla kya vata nĩ kana tũkamwendeeasya Ngai nũndũ "nũsiĩĩaa ala mekwĩnenevya, ĩndĩ amanengae mumo ala menyivasya."—1 Vet. 5:5.
11. Nĩkĩ kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mũkate na mbinyu kũtonya kũtũtetheesya tũlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yitũ?
11 Nzĩa ya kelĩ nĩ kũvindĩĩsya kĩla kyonanaw'a nĩ mũkate na mbinyu ĩla ĩtũmĩawa ĩvinda ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ. Ĩla ũendeee kwĩyũmbanĩsya mũthenya ũsu vindĩĩsya mũno nĩkĩ kũtũmĩawa mũkate ũte ĩlawa na mbinyu ndune, na nũseo ũkavindĩĩsya maũndũ asu mũno mũno ũtukũ ũsu wa mwanya. (1 Ako. 11:23-25) Mũkate ũsu wonanasya mwĩĩ ũte na naĩ ũla Yesũ waumisye ta nthembo, nayo mbinyu yonanasya ĩla nthakame yake yetĩkie. Ĩndĩ kũelewa maũndũ asu kwĩ kw'oka kũitoetye. Lilikana kana nthembo ya wovosyo ya Klĩsto ĩtumaa twona ũndũ Yeova na Yesũ matwendie mũno kũte mũndũ ũngĩ o na wĩva. Yeova oonanisye nũtwendete kwa kũtũnenga Mwana wake, nake Yesũ oonanisye kana nũtwendete kwa kwĩtĩkĩla na ngenda akw'e kwondũ witũ. Kũsũanĩa kĩu kwaĩlĩte kũtuma o naitũ tũmenda. Na nũndũ kĩla ũmwe witũ nũmwendete Yeova, wendo ũsu ũilyĩ mũkwa ũtwovanĩtye vamwe ũla ũlũlũmĩlasya ngwatanĩo ĩla twĩthĩawa nayo.
12. Nthĩnĩ wa ĩla ngelekany'o ya mũsumbĩ wendie ũtalo kwa ngombo syake, Yesũ oonanisye ata kana Yeova endaa tũekee ala angĩ?
12 Nzĩa ya katatũ ya kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ nĩ kũekea angĩ kuma ngoonĩ. Twaekea ala matũvĩtĩsya, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a nĩtũtũngaa mũvea twalilikana naĩ ila tũekeawa nũndũ wa nthembo ya Klĩsto. Kwasoma na ũivindĩĩsya ngelekany'o ĩla Yesũ wanenganie ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 18:23-34. Ĩkũlye-ĩ: 'Nyie nĩnendaa kũatĩĩa kĩla Yesũ wamanyĩisye? Nĩnĩmomĩĩasya Aklĩsto ala angĩ na nĩnĩmaeleawa? Nĩnĩthĩawa nĩyũmbanĩtye kũekea ala mambĩtĩsya?' Nĩ w'o kana kĩla ĩvĩtyo yĩ ũito wayo, na ve ĩvĩtyo ĩna ũtonya kwĩkwa ũkethĩa ta mũndũ wĩĩw'a ũiemwa vyũ nĩ kũekea ũla waũvĩtĩsya. Ĩndĩ ngelekany'o ĩsu ĩtũmanyĩasya kĩla Yeova wendaa twĩke. (Soma Mathayo 18:35.) Yesũ endaa tũkwatye nesa kana Yeova ndesa kũtũekea ethĩwa tũiekeaa ana-a-asa maitũ ĩla ve na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũmaekea. Vate nzika, ũsu nĩ ũndũ twaĩle kũũvindĩĩsya mũno. Kwoou nĩ kana tũsũvĩe na tũilũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ, twaĩlĩte kũekea angĩ o tondũ Yesũ watũmanyĩisye.
13. Kũmantha mũuo kũlũlũmĩlasya ata ngwatanĩo yitũ?
13 Kũekea angĩ kwonanasya kana twĩ andũ mendete kũmantha mũuo. Kwalilikana ũla ũtao mũtũmwa Vaulo wanenganie ĩla waisye kana twaĩlĩte 'kwĩthing'ĩĩsya tũsũvĩe wĩw'ano ũmwe wa veva wovanonĩ wa mũuo.' (Aev. 4:3) Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, na mũno mũno ũtukũ ũla tũkeka ũmbano ũsu, sũanĩa mũno ũndũ ũkuaa andũ ala angĩ. Ĩkũlye atĩĩ: 'Ala angĩ nĩmene nesa kana nyie ndyoveeaa ũthatu ngoonĩ? Andũ no masye kana nĩndataa vyũ nĩw'ane na ala angĩ na ngĩsũvĩa ngwatanĩo yitũ?' Asu nĩ makũlyo maito, na yĩĩ nĩ ĩvinda ĩseo ya kũmasũanĩa.
14. Tũtonya kwonany'a ata 'nĩtũmĩanĩasya ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo'?
14 Nzĩa ya kana ya kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yitũ nĩ kwenda ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa o tondũ Yeova ũmendete nũndũ we nĩ wendo. (1 Yoa. 4:8) Yĩsilya yĩĩ yĩyaĩlĩte kwĩsa kũlika kĩlĩkonĩ kitũ: 'Ngeekaa o kũmĩanĩsya namo, ĩndĩ ti lasima nĩthĩwe nĩ vata namo'! Yĩsilya yĩu yĩyosanĩte na ũtao ũũ wa Vaulo: "Mũkyũmĩanĩsya inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo." (Aev. 4:2) Vaulo ndaatwĩa twĩke o 'kũmĩanĩsya ithyĩ kwa ithyĩ.' Atwĩie tũmĩanĩsye "nthĩnĩ wa wendo." Asu nĩ maũndũ elĩ me kĩvathũkany'o. Ikundinĩ sitũ kwĩ andũ ma mĩthemba mingĩ na onthe Yeova nũmakusĩtye kwake. (Yoa. 6:44) Na nũndũ Yeova nũmakusĩtye, no nginya ethĩwe onete kana nĩ andũ matonya kwendeka. Kwoou nithyĩ aaũ twasye atĩ tũyĩsa kwenda Mũklĩsto mũna? Tũyaĩlĩte o na vanini kwĩsa kwĩthĩwa tũtendete ala angĩ o tondũ Yeova wendaa tũmende!—1 Yoa. 4:20, 21.
NĨ ĨNDĨĨ TŨKEKA ŨMBANO WA MŨTHYA WA KŨLILIKANA KĨKW'Ũ KYA YESŨ?
15. Twĩsĩ ata kana mũthenya ũmwe tũkalilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ tũtakeka ũu ĩngĩ?
15 Mũthenya ũmwe tũkalilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ tũtakeka ũu ĩngĩ. Twĩsĩ ata? Valũanĩ wa mbee ũla Vaulo waandĩkĩie Akolintho, eĩte Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta kana kwa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ kĩla mwaka methĩawa 'mayonany'a kĩkw'ũ kya Mwĩaĩi kũvika yĩla wĩũka.' (1 Ako. 11:26) Vaulo aitũmĩa ndeto 'kũka' awetaa o 'kũka' kũla Yesũ wawetie wathaninĩ wake wa mũthenya wa mũminũkĩlyo. Wathaninĩ ũsu awetie ĩũlũ wa ũla thĩna mũnene tweteele asya: 'Kũkooneka wonany'o wa Mwana wa mũndũ ĩtunĩ: na ĩndĩ mbaĩ syonthe sya nthĩ ikameta, na makoona Mwana wa mũndũ okĩte ĩũlũ wa mathweo ma ĩtu na vinya na ũtheu mũnene mũtisu. Nake [Yesũ] akatũma alaĩka make na wasya mũnene wa soo, nao makoombany'a ala anyuve make kuma ngalĩ inya sya iseve, kuma itulunĩ sya matu kũvika itulunĩ ila ingĩ syamo.' (Mt. 24:29-31) Ĩla Yesũ waisye alaĩka "makoomban'ya ala anyuve make," awetaa ĩvinda yĩla Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ala makethĩwa matiele kũũ nthĩ makakwata ĩtuvi yoo ya kũthi ĩtunĩ. Ũndũ ũsu ũkeekĩka kĩlungu kya mbee kya ũla thĩna mũnene kyavĩta na kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni ũtambĩĩe. Ĩtina wa ũu nĩvo ĩndĩ ala 144,000 makakwatĩanĩa na Yesũ kaũnĩ wa kũmina asumbĩ ma nthĩ. (Ũvu. 17:12-14) Ĩla tũkathi ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ na ĩtina wa vau ũ Yesũ 'ayũka' kũmbany'a etĩkĩw'a mauta mathi ĩtunĩ, nĩw'o tũkethĩwa tweeka ũmbano ũsu ya mũthya.
16. Nĩkĩ we ũtw'ĩte kwĩka kyonthe kĩla ũtonya ndũkatĩĩe ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ mwaka ũũ?
16 Kĩla ũmwe witũ naĩkĩĩthye kana akatetheka nĩ kũthi ũmbanonĩ wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ Matukũ 31, Mwei wa 3, 2018. Na mwa nĩtũmũvoye Yeova atũtetheesye kwĩka kyonthe kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana tũlũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo ya andũ make! (Soma Savuli 133:1.) Tũikolwe kana mũthenya ũmwe tũkeeka ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ ya mũthya. Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũsu ũte mũviku, nĩtũtatei vyũ ũndũ tũtonya tũikaatĩe ũmbano wa kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ, na nĩtũendeee kwona ngwatanĩo ĩla twĩthĩawa nayo ĩvindanĩ ya ũmbano ũsu yĩ ya mwanya.
