translation:
Jehovah answers the righteous ones; and he delivers them from all their distresses."—PS. 34:22.
PAGE: 49, 32
1. How many of us have wondered why so many righteous people experience trials?
A brother named Paul once said: "Let your reasonableness become known to all men." (Phil. 4:5) Many righteous people wonder why God allows things to happen to them when Paul himself experienced such difficulties. However, we should remember that sometimes we need trials to prove our faith and to show Jehovah that we truly love him and want to please him. Some Christians find comfort in knowing that others have gone through similar experiences and have remained faithful to God despite their trials.
2. (a) What does Psalm 34:22 teach us about how God views the troubles of his people? (b) What will we discuss in this article? (See the box "Why Does God Allow Trials?")
We can be sure that the Scriptures teach us that Jehovah cares about those who lovingly serve him and wants to help them during times of trouble. (Read Psalm 34:22.) Can we trust that Jehovah hears our prayers and will assist us? It may be helpful to examine the example of ancient Israel to learn some important lessons. We will see that the pattern of trials began with Moses, which occurred during the spring of 33 C.E., and continued throughout that period. The point is that Moses was closely united with Jehovah. This pattern of trials helps us understand what Jehovah expects of us, namely, to remain loyal, to endure, and to pray. Let us therefore carefully consider each situation we face and how it affects us.
"WHY DOES GOD ALLOW TRIALS?"
3. What question did most of the Israelites ask after experiencing trials?
3 Jehovah knows what is best for each individual. In the case of Israel, most of the people who experienced trials felt they were being punished because of their sins and shortcomings. That person was called "the afflicted one." (Deut. 35:19) Consequently, the guilty ones confessed their sins and sought forgiveness. These trials proved the integrity of Job, and God said: "You have tried my servant Job: and my servant [Job] has remained upright."—Deut. 35:33, 34.
4. How could an Israelite benefit from enduring trials?
4 And how can an Israelite benefit from enduring trials? Or perhaps you feel that trials are not beneficial, that person was shown to be loyal through his trials. (Gen. 9:5) Indeed, we may learn valuable lessons when undergoing trials, which can strengthen our faith and help us to appreciate more fully the meaning of life. Let us therefore view trials as opportunities to demonstrate our loyalty.—Deut. 35:15, 28.
5. How does the way trials affect us help us to know Jehovah better?
5 Jehovah allows trials to affect us so that we may get to know him better, not just to punish us. Joshua stated: "Come and hear, O Israel, this day." Those trials 'were a test.' (Josh. 20:1, 2, 7, 8) Therefore, Jehovah provides tests to reveal the condition of our heart, and we should take advantage of them to learn about ourselves. Does that test help us to understand Jehovah's ways better? And does that test help us to appreciate the importance of remaining loyal to Jehovah during trials?
'HE DOES NOT DESIRE THEIR DEATH'
6, 7. (a) What factors determine whether a man benefits from a trial? Explain. (See accompanying article on page 8.) (b) Why is it important for a man to benefit from a trial?
6 A man who endures trials can benefit only if he "does not desire their death" but has a sincere desire to please God. His actions during those trials will show his true attitude. (Josh. 20:4) For example, his actions during trials may reveal whether he values his relationship with Jehovah above everything else. (Read Deuteronomy 35:24, 25.) Such actions can help him to see whether he is truly devoted to Jehovah or is influenced by selfish desires, and thus he will grow spiritually.
7 How should a person feel about trials? It is vital that trials move us to examine our hearts, just as the Israelites of old examined theirs when they faced trials, and to ask ourselves whether our loyalty is to Jehovah. One Bible student wrote that a person facing trials might say, "I have come to my wit's end." He explained: "The weight of the world seemed to be upon his head because of his determination to live up to what God expected of him." To examine our hearts regarding trials, we must honestly assess how we react to them and make adjustments accordingly. We must strive to view trials as opportunities to demonstrate our faith and to draw closer to Jehovah, rather than as something negative.
8, 9. How can a Christian maintain a positive outlook when facing trials?
8 A true Christian will always look for ways to strengthen his relationship with Jehovah. But how can they do so? Well, the Scriptures show that Jehovah allows trials to test people. (Jas. 5:14-16) Therefore, this opportunity to help someone who is experiencing difficulties can remind us of God's love and give us a sense of purpose. (Act. 6:1; Heb. 12:11) Furthermore, missionaries often find comfort in knowing that their ministry helps others, and they appreciate being able to share good news with those who are receptive, or even with those who are initially resistant. Jehovah gives his servants "insight." (Isa. 32:1, 2) So, reflect on whether this counsel has helped you to see things from God's perspective.
9 Many of God's servants have found that regularly sharing with others has strengthened their faith and brought them joy. For example, a young man named Daniel faced trials and felt compelled to speak to people about his beliefs. He said: "I realized that when I am downcast, talking to others about what I believe lifts my spirits. Every time I talk, I feel closer to Jehovah, and my understanding deepens. And even when people reject me, I know that I have done my best to express my faith." Because of this, Daniel continued to share his faith with others. He also learned some valuable lessons, saying: "I discovered that I enjoyed speaking to people. The more I spoke, the easier it became, and I began to pray earnestly to Jehovah to help me say something meaningful." This experience gave Daniel a greater appreciation for the importance of preaching and teaching.
"ANOTHER WAY TO SHOW LOVE"
10. What can we do to encourage brothers and sisters who may be struggling?
10 A brother or sister who is going through a difficult time may appreciate our encouragement. But how can we offer such encouragement? (Read Joshua 20:4.) You might notice a brother or sister who seems discouraged. Perhaps he feels overwhelmed by his circumstances or is facing a serious problem. In such cases, simply showing genuine concern can mean a lot. For instance, he might be battling an illness, dealing with financial difficulties, or grieving the loss of a loved one, and he needs our support and practical assistance to cope. * (Prov. 35:25) However, there are times when just listening is the most helpful thing we can do. And if that brother or sister continues to struggle, we can assure him that we will remember him in our prayers and offer our ongoing support.
11. How can a Christian maintain zeal and continue to preach, even if he does not always feel like it?
11 Of course, a person may lack enthusiasm at times. But this does not mean that God has abandoned him. He may be struggling with feelings of inadequacy or be burdened by personal problems. This is where self-discipline comes in. He can schedule specific times for preaching and make himself go out, even though he doesn't feel like it. The apostle Paul wrote to the Christians in Colossae about the importance of diligence. He urged them: "Continue applying yourselves diligently to prayer, being watchful with thanksgiving, praying also for us, that God may open to us a door to speak the sacred secret of the Christ." (2 Cor. 7:10, 11) If we want to remain close to Jehovah, we must cultivate good habits and persevere, even when we don't feel like it, trusting that he will bless our efforts.
12. What can a Christian do if he finds it hard to stay spiritually awake?
12 There are several reasons why a Christian might struggle to stay spiritually awake. Perhaps he is preoccupied with worldly concerns or feels overwhelmed by his responsibilities. (Matt. 18:8, 9) Consider some practical steps you can take to strengthen your relationship with Jehovah. Is there something you could eliminate from your life to free up time and energy? Could you reduce your involvement in entertainment, such as television, Internet browsing, and other activities that can distract you from spiritual pursuits? Examine whether you have allowed yourself to become overly concerned with material possessions, which can hinder your zeal for serving Jehovah. Seek things that please Jehovah. And seek things that help you remain zealous in knowing Jehovah and walking with Him in "loving-kindness."—Isa. 54:7, 8.
'BE VIGILANT CONCERNING YOUR PRIVILEGE'
13. How can we show that we appreciate our privilege of declaring God's Word, even when we face difficulties?
13 A Christian should be eager to declare God's Word, despite obstacles. Jehovah views this as "the privilege of declaring" His Word. (Josh. 20:2, 3) Jehovah understands that each individual has limitations and may feel inadequate to meet certain challenges in connection with declaring God's Word. He does not expect us to be perfect, but he does encourage us to make an earnest effort. A person who is determined will find ways to overcome obstacles. Declaring God's Word is an expression of our love for Jehovah and a means of showing our gratitude for his undeserved kindness. Moreover, it protects us from being influenced by Satan. Others who share in declaring God's Word will also strengthen your resolve, encourage you, and help you maintain your zeal!
14. What can a Christian do to improve his ability to teach others?
14 We can benefit from the examples of faithful men of God who persevered and continued to practice, becoming skilled in their work. Also, we can imitate those who love Jehovah and are willing to work hard to become proficient in their ministry. Be confident in this: If you ask Jehovah for help, He will help you, and He will give you opportunities to improve! For example, young Daniel purposed in his heart to understand the meaning of visions. He prayed earnestly to Jehovah and asked Him to explain them, saying: "Please give me insight. I want to understand the meaning of these things. The meaning of these matters is too difficult for me." But Jehovah answered him, saying: "Go on, because you are beloved. Pay attention to the words, and understand the matter." Daniel understood the vision and remembered it. A Christian should be eager to declare God's Word, and he will find ways to express himself effectively when speaking to people. So, Jehovah can help us to speak appropriately, so that we can be convincing and avoid causing others to stumble or misrepresent Him.—Read Psalm 103:8-12.
15, 16. How can we show that Jesus is the Messiah and High Priest that God appointed, even if someone questions our faith?
15 We have a strong reason for doing so, and it is this: Every Israelite should be convinced that Jehovah exists. Paul was willing to suffer much persecution because he wanted to walk in loyalty to Jehovah, and he boldly said: "I esteem the reproach of Christ as something valuable." (Acts 7:25) So, like Paul, we too will continue to bear witness faithfully and courageously, showing that we believe God has honored his promise regarding salvation through Jesus. The evidence of God's favor toward Jesus is that He raised him from the dead, giving us hope for everlasting life. (Rev. 9:13, 14) And furthermore, the High Priest "does not offer himself repeatedly, otherwise he would have ceased to exist; but with one sacrifice he made perfect those who are being sanctified forever." (Rev. 7:24, 25) Therefore, every priest stands daily ministering and offering the same sacrifices again and again, which never take away sins. But this priest offered one sacrifice for sins perpetually, then sat down at the right hand of God, waiting from that time onward until his enemies are placed as a footstool for his feet. Is not this High Priest, Jesus, greater than those who were priests according to the Law? We have a strong reason for believing this, namely, that we "have beheld with our own eyes" [or, "have personally seen," NWT] His manifestation.—Rev. 4:15, 16.
16 So let us continue to approach Jehovah with confidence, because of the sacrifice Jesus made. Let us also remember that the sacrificial value benefits many people. For us, the fact that this sacrifice benefits us personally is what matters. (Acts 2:20, 21) Be confident that the sacrificial value applies to you personally. And realize that this sacrifice is what makes personal forgiveness possible and gives you a good standing with God. Jesus' sacrifice is how Jehovah demonstrates His love for you.
17. Will you continue to approach Jehovah with confidence?
17 One reason why we can be confident is that Jehovah cares about us deeply. Your feelings are important to Him. Also, He uses his active forces to help us, and we appreciate that help very much, and we trust that Jehovah will always support us. So, will you continue to approach Jehovah with confidence? Many have found it helpful to meditate on the qualities of Jehovah! (Ps. 91:1, 2) Read scriptures that strengthen your conviction that your feelings are important to Jehovah, so that you may remain close to him.
^ kal. 10 The ten commandments from Exodus show that a person who does not obey and appreciates the privilege of living may find it difficult to remain in a right relationship with God.

text:
"Nũndũ andũ nĩmeenenganie na ngoo ya kwenda, mũtaĩei Yeova."—ASI. 5:2.
MBATHI: 150, 10
1, 2. (a) Elivasi na Mbilitati maisye ata ĩũlũ wa kĩthito kitũ kya kũmũthũkũma Ngai? (b) Yeova oonanisye ata woni wake ĩũlũ wa kĩthito kitũ?
ELIVASI MŨTEMANI akũlilye Yovu atĩĩ: "Mũndũ nũtonya kũmũuna Ngai? Vate ndĩi ũla mũĩ nĩwĩunaa mwene. Nĩ ũndũ wa kwendeesya Mwene Vinya W'onthe, atĩ wĩ mũlũngalu? Kana nĩ ũtandĩthyo wake, atĩ nĩwĩanĩasya mĩendele yaku?" (Yovu 22:1-3) We waamantha ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo ta asu? Vai nzika kana ĩla Elivasi wakũlilye Yovu makũlyo asu, we eesĩ ũsũngĩo wamo nĩ aiee. O na ve mũnyanyae ũmwe wa Elivasi weetawa Mbilitati Mũsui waisye kana vai mũndũ wĩsa kwĩthĩwa e mũlũngalu kwa Ngai.—Soma Yovu 25:4.
2 Andũ asu mavangaa mekiakisya Yovu, ĩndĩ maisye atĩ o na tweekĩa kĩthito ata tũmũthũkũme Yeova twĩ aĩkĩĩku, we ndesa kwona ũu ta ũndũ. O na maisye atĩ tũi kavaa kwĩ lungulu kana kĩinyũ. (Yovu 4:19; 25:6) Wasoma ndeto sya Elivasi na Mbilitati ũteũsũanĩa no wambe kwona ta maĩ andũ meenyivĩtye. (Yovu 22:29) Na kĩtumi nũndũ ũkasisya kũũ nthĩ wĩ mũthyanĩ wa kĩĩma kana wĩ ndekenĩ, ndwona ta ve kĩndũ kĩ maana andũ maendeesye vaa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ, Ĩla Yeova wasisya kũũ nthĩ e ku ĩũlũ ĩtunĩ, we onaa kĩthito kĩla twĩ nakyo kwondũ wa Ũsumbĩ kĩte maana? Yeova nĩwanenganie ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu ĩla wakanisye Elivasi, Mbilitati, na Nzovali nũndũ wa kũneena ũvũngũ na ĩtina wa kũmakany'a aweta kana nũtanĩthĩtw'e nĩ Yovu. O na amwĩtie, "mũthũkũmi wakwa." (Yovu 42:7, 8) Kwoou vate nzika, "mũndũ nũtonya kũmũuna Ngai."
"ŨMŨNENGAE KYAŨ?"
3. Eliu akũlilye ata ĩũlũ wa kĩthito kitũ kya kũmũthũkũma Yeova, na endaa kwasya ata aikũlya ĩkũlyo yĩu?
3 Yeova ndaamũkany'a Eliu ĩla wakũlilye ũũ: "Ethĩwa wĩ mũlũngalu, ũmũnengae [Ngai] kyaũ? Kana nake osaa kyaũ kw'okonĩ kwaku?" (Yovu 35:7) We Eliu aikũlya ĩkũlyo yĩu endaa kwonany'a kĩthito kitũ kya kũmũthũkũma Ngai nĩ kya mana? Aiee. Endaa kwasya kana Yeova ndethĩawa ekwetye ũthaithi witũ. Yeova nĩwĩtoetye. Vai ũndũ twĩka tũkatw'ĩka nĩtwamũthusya kana nĩtwamwongelanga ũkũmũ. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, ũ Ngai nĩwe ũtwaĩlasya, akatũnenga inengo, na vinya wa kwĩka maũndũ, na nĩwonaa ũndũ tũũitũmĩa.
4. Yeova osaa ata ũseo ũla tweeka angĩ?
4 Ĩla tweeka athũkũmi ala angĩ ma Yeova maũndũ maseo, Yeova atalaa asu ta maũndũ twamwĩka e we mwene. Ĩandĩko ya Nthimo 19:17 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũla wĩw'ĩaa ngya tei akovethasya Yeova, na wĩko wake mũseo akamũĩva ĩngĩ." Yo ĩandĩko yĩu yĩenda kũtwĩa kana Yeova nĩwonaa kaũseo konthe kala ngya yeekwa? Kana no twasye ĩla ithyĩ andũ tweeka angĩ ũndũ mũseo, we Mũmbi wa nthĩ yonthe osaa ũsu ta ũndũ twamũkovethya, na waĩlĩte kũtũĩva kwa kũtwĩka ũseo kana kũtũathima? Ũsũngĩo nĩ ĩĩ, na Mwana wa Ngai nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kĩu.—Soma Luka 14:13, 14.
5. Yu twĩmantha ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo meva?
5 Ĩvinda yĩmwe Yeova nĩwatũmie mwathani Isaia akaneene vandũ vake. Kĩu kyoonanisye ũndũ Yeova ũtanĩaa kũthũkũma vamwe na andũ ala aĩkĩĩku ĩla ũkwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kyake. (Isa. 6:8-10) Isaia nĩweetĩkĩlile na ngoo yonthe kwĩka kĩla Yeova wendaa. Ũmũnthĩ andũ ngili mbingĩ me na veva ta ũsu wa Isaia. Ĩla Yeova wamanenga ianda ite laisi ũthũkũminĩ wake mamwĩaa kuma ngoonĩ, "Ninyioo; ndũma nyie." Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, mũndũ no ekũlye atĩĩ: 'Kyo kĩla nyie nĩkaa nĩ kya vata? O na kau Yeova nũnengete mwanya wa kwĩnengane ũthũkũminĩ wake, nĩ lasima nĩnengane na ngoo yonthe? Nĩnenganĩte na ndenenganĩte, we nũlea kwĩka kyonthe kĩla kĩkwendeka nĩ kana Ndeto yake ĩanĩe?' Nĩ kana tũkwate ũsũngĩo wa makũlyo asu, kwaekai tũsũanĩe vamwe maũndũ ala meekĩkie ĩvinda ya Ndevola na Mbalaka.
NĨMALEELETE NŨNDŨ WA WIA, ĨNDĨ NGAI AMEKĨA VINYA
6. Elesya kĩvathũkany'o kĩla kyaĩ vo katĩ wa ita sya Aisilaeli na sya Yavini.
6 Kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 20, Mũsumbĩ Yavini wa Kanaani "nĩwathĩnasya ana ma Isilaeli na vinya." Myakanĩ ĩsu ana asu ma Isilaeli o na nĩmakĩaa kumaalũka. Na twalika maũndũnĩ ma ita, ita sya Isilaeli syaĩ vathei syaelekanw'a na sya Kanaani nĩkwĩthĩwa Akanaani maĩ na makasya 900 ma iaa, namo Aisilaeli mayaĩ na mĩio ya kwĩsiĩĩa kana kwĩyũkitĩa.—Asi. 4:1-3, 13; 5:6-8. *
7, 8. (a) Nĩ mwĩao wĩva wa mbee Yeova wanengie Mbalaka? (b) Elesya ũndũ Aisilaeli masindie ita sya Yavini. (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 28.)
7 Ĩndĩ o na kau Aisilaeli mayaĩ na mĩio ya kaũ, Yeova atũmie mwathani Ndevola anenge Mbalaka mwĩao ũũ: "Enda ũthengeee kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli, na ũkĩthi na andũ ngili ĩkũmi ma ana ma Navitali na ma ana ma Nzevuluni . . . Nakwa ngakũthengeesya Sisela ũsĩnĩ wa Kisoni, kavuteni wa ita sya Yavini, vamwe na makasya make ma kaũ na nguthu yake; na ngamũnengane kw'okonĩ kwaku."—Asi. 4:4-7.
8 Mbalaka nĩwanyaĩĩkisye ũvoo ũsu. Namo ala meenenganie na ngoo ya kwenda mamina kwĩw'a ũvoo ũsu nĩmoombanie Kĩĩmanĩ kya Tavoli. Moombana, Mbalaka ndaaananga ndatĩka ĩndĩ nĩweekie kĩla Yeova wamwĩaĩe. (Soma Asili 4:14-16.) Matheea Taanaki malike kaũnĩ, mbua nene nĩyambĩĩe kwĩtĩka na yatuma kĩsio kĩu kĩtw'ĩka kya ndaka nthei. Mbalaka akũkanisye ita sya Sisela mũvaka kĩsionĩ kya Alosethi, mũendo wa maili 15 (kĩlomita 24) kuma Taanaki. Matavikĩte Alosethi vavikie vandũ Sisela oona yĩla ĩkasya yake yĩteũmũtethya, na kwoou ayĩtia na akũka na maaũ nginya Nzaananimu. Kũu Nzaananimu aendie kũmantha wĩvitho ĩeemanĩ ya kĩveti kya Eeveli ũla Mũkeni kyeetawa Yaeli. Alika ĩeemanĩ akomie too nĩ mĩnoo ĩla waĩ nayo nũndũ wa kĩtuu kya kaũ. Ĩla wakomie anengie Yaeli mwanya mũseo mũno wa kũmũaa. (Asi. 4:17-21) Nũndũ wa ũkũmbaũ wa Yaeli na ũtwi wake wa mĩtũkĩ, nthũ ĩsu ya Isilaeli yaminĩiwe vau! *
ANDŨ MAĨ NA NGOO YA KWĨNENGANE NA ANGĨ MATAĨ NAYO
9. Ĩandĩko ya Asili 5:20, 21 yongeleele ũvoo wĩva ĩũlũ wa kaũ ũla Aisilaeli mokitie na Sisela?
9 Nũseo tũkemanyĩsya kĩlungu kya 4 kĩatĩanĩe na kya 5 ĩvukunĩ yĩu ya Asili nũndũ kĩla kĩmwe kĩ na ũvoo ũtonya kũtũtetheesya kũelewa kĩla kĩngĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩandĩko ya Asili 5:20, 21 yaĩtye: "Ndata nĩsyokitie syĩ ĩtunĩ, syĩ nzĩanĩ syasyo syamũkita Sisela. Ũsĩ wa Kisoni wamatwaa vyũ." Yo ĩandĩko yĩu yĩasya kana alaĩka nĩmatetheeisye Aisilaeli, kana yĩasya mũthenya ũsu ve tũlungu twa mavia twetĩkie kuma ndatanĩ? Mbivilia ndĩtũtavĩtye. Ĩndĩ ate o twasye Ngai nĩwe watetheeisye Aisilaeli mũthenya ũsu, nĩ kyaũ kĩngĩ kĩsa kũtuma mbua ĩtoetye kũkolya kĩsio kĩu nginya ĩkwamye makasya 900 ma kaũ yĩtĩka vau vaĩ kaũ na saanĩ o ila ve vata? Wasoma ĩandĩko ya Asili 4:14, 15, nũkwĩthĩa Yeova anengetwe nguma katatũ nũndũ wa ũsindi ũsu. Vai mũndũũme o na ũmwe katĩ wa ala aũme 10,000 ma Isilaeli waĩ ekũna kĩthũi akasya nĩwe waete ũsindi ũsu.
10, 11. Melosi yaumanĩiwe nĩkĩ?
10 Ĩndĩ ve ndeto sya ũsengy'a syĩ ũla wathinĩ Ndevola na Mbalaka mamũtaĩe Yeova naw'o nũndũ wa ũsindi ũla wamanengie. Wathinĩ ũsu meina mayasya: "Umanĩai Melosi, asya ũu mũlaĩka wa Yeova, Maumanĩei na wai ala matwĩe vo, nũndũ matyaaũka kũmũtetheesya Yeova, kũmũtetheesya Yeova kwa ala me vinya mũno."—Asi. 5:23.
11 Kĩumo kĩla kyakwatie Melosi nĩ ta kyaĩ kĩthũku mũno nginya ũkethĩa o na ũmũnthĩ ti laisi kũmanya vala Melosi yaĩ. Yo no yĩthĩwe yaĩ ndũa yaĩ na andũ maleile kwĩnengane matetheesye ũla kaũnĩ? Kana ethĩwa yaĩ ndũa yaĩ nzĩanĩ ĩla Sisela wasembele akĩĩte, ekali mayo nĩmethĩwa maleile kũtũmĩa mwanya ũsu makamũsiĩĩa? Na eka ũu, mo no methĩwe mataaĩw'a kana Yeova nĩwakũlĩtye andũ menengane? Ũu ndũtonyeka nũndũ andũ 10,000 kuma kĩsionĩ kĩu kyoo nĩmeenenganie na ngoo ya kwenda mathi kũkita na Akanaani. O na ĩngĩ, kwasũanĩa ekali ma Melosi monete ĩla ngũmbaũ yaĩ nthũ ĩsembele vau kwoo yĩ yoka ĩthelile vinya vyũ! Ũsu waĩ mwanya mũseo wa kũkwata mbau mũvango wa Yeova na maiathimwa. Ĩndĩ vandũ va matũmĩe mwanya ũsu nesa monany'e kana me vamwe na Yeova, meekie kũekana na ngũmbaũ ĩsu ĩvĩte oou mana. Vate nzika, ekali ma Melosi maĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na Yaeli, ũla woosie ĩtambya yĩla yaaĩlĩte o tondũ mĩsoa ĩla ĩatĩĩe yonanĩtye.—Asi. 5:24-27.
12. Ĩandĩko ya Asili 5:9, 10 yĩwetete ikundi syĩva ilĩ sya andũ maĩ kĩvathũkany'o, na kĩu kĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
12 Ve kĩvathũkany'o kĩngĩ tũkwona ĩandĩkonĩ ya Asili 5:9, 10. Ala meeyumisye mathi na Mbalaka maĩ na woni wĩ kĩvathũkany'o mũno na wa ala meekie kwĩlingya. Mĩsoanĩ ĩsu Ndevola na Mbalaka makathie "makavana ma Isilaeli, ala meenenganie na ngoo ya kwenda katĩ wa andũ." Makavana asu maĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ala 'makuawa nĩ mang'oi meũ,' ala meetalaa ta andũ ma vata mũno mataĩle kũthi kaũnĩ. O na maĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ala 'mekalĩlaa mĩkeka yĩ thooa mũnene,' ala mendete kwĩkala mana vate ũndũ mekwĩka. Ala meenenganie mathi na Mbalaka kũkita ivaũũkonĩ sya kĩĩma kya Tavoli na mwandanĩ wa Kisoni maĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ala angĩ 'maendaa na nzĩa,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ala matendaa kwĩnosya. Onthe ala matw'ĩte kwĩkala mana metanĩthye vandũ va kwĩnengane maaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa mũno. Maaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa mwanya ũsu maĩ naw'o wa kũkwata mbau mũvango wa Yeova na maeka wavĩta oou. O na ala ũmũnthĩ mate na wendi wa kũmũthũkũma Ngai na ngoo yonthe maĩlĩte kũsũanĩa mũno.
13. Andũ ma mbaĩ ya Leuveni, Ndani, na Aseli maĩ kĩvathũkany'o ata na andũ ma mbaĩ ya Nzevuluni na Navitali?
13 Ala meenenganie mathi kaũnĩ nĩmeeyoneie nesa ũndũ Yeova ũteteaa ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. Maĩ na ũvoo matonya kũtavya angĩ 'makĩwetanga meko malũngalu ma Yeova.' (Asi. 5:11) Kĩvathũkany'o na asu, ĩandĩko ya Asili 5:15-17 yĩwetete kana andũ ma mbaĩ ya Leuveni, Ndani, na Aseli mayaalũngana na wĩa ũla Yeova wendaa ũtethw'e ĩndĩ mathĩnĩkĩaa mũno malĩ yoo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mĩsoa ĩsu nĩwetete ĩũlũ wa ndĩthya syoo, ngalawa, na syoko sya ũkanga (ilĩndĩ). Andũ ma mbaĩ ya Nzevuluni na Navitali mayailyĩ ta andũ ma mbaĩ isu itatũ nũndũ mo malikilye "mathayũ moo mũisyonĩ kũvika kĩkw'ũ" nĩ kana matonye kũkwatĩanĩa na Ndevola na Mbalaka. (Asi. 5:18) Kĩvathũkany'o kĩla kyaĩ vo katĩ wa mbaĩ ila syeenenganie na ila itaaĩnengane nĩkĩũtũmanyĩsya ũndũ wa vata mũno.
"MŨTAĨEI YEOVA"
14. Ũmũnthĩ tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũkwete mbau ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova?
14 Ũmũnthĩ tũikũlaw'a twĩnengane kaũnĩ, ĩndĩ twĩ na mwanya mũseo wa kwonany'a twĩ ngũmbaũ syĩ kĩthito wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Vai ĩvinda ũseũvyo wa Yeova waaĩsa kwenda andũ menengane ta ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ. Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa milioni siana ũna, methĩwe nĩ andũ aima kana nĩ ma mũika, nĩmenenganĩte na ngoo ya kwenda makalika ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe ta ũvainia, ũthũkũmi wa Mbetheli, wĩa wa myako ya Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ, kana o makenengane matetheesye wĩa maũmbanonĩ manene. Yu eka asu, kwasũanĩa ũndũ atumĩa ala me Kamitiinĩ sya Maũndũ ma Sivitalĩ, kana ala mavangĩthasya maũmbano manene, methĩawa na wĩa ũitavĩte. Ndũkethĩwe na nzika kana Yeova nũtanĩthaw'a mũno nĩ veva waku wa kwĩnengane, na ndakolwa nue o na ĩndĩĩ.—Aevl. 6:10.
15. Tũtonya kũmanya ata ethĩwa wendi witũ wa kwĩnengane wĩanĩ wa Yeova nũolekete?
15 Kĩla ũmwe witũ aĩlĩte kwĩkũlya ũũ: 'Nyie nendete kũthũmũa na kũekea ala angĩ wĩa ũla mwingĩ? Nyie nĩnĩekete wendi wa malĩ ũmbate kwĩnengane? Nyie nĩ na mũĩkĩĩo na ũkũmbaũ wa kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Mbalaka, Ndevola, Yaeli, na ala andũ 10,000 kwa kwĩka kyonthe kĩla nĩtonya nĩ kana nĩmũthũkũme Yeova? Na ethĩwa nĩ na mũvango wa kũthamĩĩa taoni ĩngĩ kana o nthĩ ĩngĩ ngamanthe mbesa, nĩnĩvoyete na ngasũanĩa mũno ũndũ vatonya kwĩthĩwa vailyĩ kwa andũ makwa na kĩkundi kĩla nĩthĩawa?' *
16. O na kau Yeova ti mũnyivĩe nĩ kĩndũ o na kĩmwe, nĩ kyaũ tũtonya kũmũnenga?
16 Nĩ ndaĩa nene mũno kwona Yeova atũnengete mwanya wa kũkwata mbau ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. Kuma ĩla Ndevili wakengie andũ ma mbee ethĩawa ayenda twĩtĩkĩle atũsumbĩke, ĩndĩ wakwata mbau ũsumbĩki wa Yeova wĩthĩawa wamwony'a Satani nesa vyũ kana ndwĩ nake o na vanini. Yeova atanaa mũno oona ũyĩnengane nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa wĩ na mũĩkĩĩo na wĩenda kũlũmany'a nake. (Nth. 23:15, 16) Atũmĩaa kĩthito kĩu kyaku kũmũsũngĩa Satani, ũla ũmũvũthasya. (Nth. 27:11) Kwoou ĩla wamwĩw'a Yeova, no ũndũ ũmwe na wĩthĩawa wamũnenga kĩndũ wonaa kĩ kya vata vyũ. Ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũmũtanĩthasya mũno.
17. Ĩandĩko ya Asili 5:31 yonanĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yũkĩte?
17 O mĩtũkĩ nthĩ ĩno ĩkatiwa o ala metĩkĩlaa ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova wĩ w'oka. Twĩ na wendi mwingĩ ta kĩ wa kwona mũthenya ũsu ũivika! Twĩ na wendi ta ũla Ndevola na Mbalaka maĩ naw'o ĩla mainie: "Amaitha maku onthe nĩmathele ũu, ame Yeova; ĩndĩ ala mamwendaa nĩmethĩwe ta syũa yĩkyuma na vinya wayo mũnene." (Asi. 5:31) Yeova akeanĩsya wendi ũsu ĩla ũkananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani. Kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni wambĩĩa tũikakũlw'a twĩnengane tũtetheesye kaũnĩ ũsu. Yĩu yĩkeethĩwa ĩvinda ya kũatĩĩa ndeto ii: "Ũngamai, mwone ũtangĩĩo wa Yeova." (2 Mav. 20:17) Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu yĩte ĩviku, twĩ na myanya mingĩ ya kũkwata mbau ũsumbĩki wa Yeova twĩ na ũkũmbaũ na kĩthito.
18. Weenengane na ngoo ya kwenda ũkatumaa ala angĩ meka ata?
18 "Nũndũ andũ nĩmeenenganie na ngoo ya kwenda, mũtaĩei Yeova." Ũu nĩw'o Ndevola na Mbalaka mambĩĩe wathi woo wa ũsindi. Wathi ũsu mayawinĩaa kyũmbe kĩngĩ o na kĩva ĩndĩ mainĩaa Ũla wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe. (Asi. 5:1, 2) O ta ũu ũmũnthĩ, eka kwĩnengane kwaku na ngoo ya kwenda kũtume ala angĩ 'mamũtaĩa Yeova'!
^ kal. 6 Makasya asu meethĩawa na mbyũ ndaasa, mbũĩ, na syĩ ngoto. Mbyũ isu sya kĩaa syeethĩawa ithinĩkĩtwe ĩkasyanĩ yĩu, na mũno mũno ndĩanĩ katĩ. We nũũ waĩ athengeea ĩkasya ta yĩu yĩthũngĩlĩte mbyũ kĩla ngalĩko?
^ kal. 8 Ngewa ĩsu ĩany'a mũyo ũu yĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/08/2015, ĩth. 12-15.
^ kal. 15 Sisya kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, "Kwĩmakĩa Nũndũ wa Mbesa," ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/07/2015.

translation:
"Truly the sons of men are prone to error when going, let us pray to Jehovah."—Ps. 5:2.
HEADLINE: 150, 10
1, 2. (a) How did Elihu and Bildad show they were prejudiced against justifying God? (b) In what way has Jehovah shown that his own sons are prejudiced?
ELIPHAS THE TEMANITE said to Job: "Is mankind able to benefit God? It is for his own good that he benefits. Or will he benefit the Mighty One, so that it may be worth while to him? Or will he take delight in your correction, so that he may answer you?" (Job 22:1-3) What is the force of these questions? Perhaps you feel that Elihu spoke to Job in this way because he was prejudiced—but know that there is also a sense in which Bildad the Shuhite showed the same prejudice toward God.—Read Job 25:4.
2 These men accused Job of making excuses, saying that he could not justify himself even if he tried to prove his integrity, and that it was useless to struggle or strive. (Job 4:19; 25:6) As you read their statements, note how they reflected the thought that humans are insignificant. (Job 22:29) And why is it that people often think little of themselves or underestimate their abilities? Because they do not appreciate what others have done for them. They reason, 'If Jehovah allows things like this to happen, does it really matter whether we try to live up to his standards?' Jehovah recognized the force of this reasoning when he rebuked Elihu, Bildad, and Zophar for speaking without knowledge and for trying to prove themselves right rather than defending Job. He then told them, "My devoted one." (Job 42:7, 8) How appropriate that he should say, "Is mankind able to benefit God?"
"WHO IS THIS WHO DARKENS COUNSEL?"
3. How did Elihu show that he was prejudiced against justifying Jehovah, and what result did this have?
3 Jehovah reproved Elihu because he was prejudiced, asking: "Do you contend against me? Or will you accuse me?" (Job 35:7) But did Elihu realize the force of his prejudice and stop trying to justify himself before God? No. He continued to argue that it was right to defend God's ways. Is it reasonable to think that Jehovah would be pleased with such an attitude? Of course not. Let us remember that we can approach Jehovah only through Christ, and that he gives us forgiveness and the opportunity to correct our mistakes. With this in mind, let us examine ourselves and see if we are not doing something similar. For God is the One who forgives us, grants us mercy, and shows us kindness.
4. What does Jehovah allow to test our faith?
4 Although we may feel that Jehovah is testing us severely, Jehovah allows only what we can endure. The proverb at Proverbs 19:17 says: "The one giving to the poor lends to Jehovah, and he will repay him." So, does this scripture teach us that Jehovah is willing to help those who give generously? Yes, it does. Then why do we sometimes feel that we have little when we try to be generous? Because the Creator of all things knows what we need, and he wants to train us to trust in him rather than seeking wealth or power. The answer is this: His Son showed us how.—Read Luke 14:13, 14.
5. Why should we be modest in our expectations?
5 Once, Jehovah sent Isaiah to warn his people. This commission illustrated how eager Jehovah is to use others to accomplish his purpose. (Isa. 6:8-10) Isaiah readily responded to whatever Jehovah asked of him. Many faithful men and women today respond like Isaiah did. But Jehovah often waits until we are ready to say, "Here I am!" Before and after doing so, a person might ask himself: 'Why am I being used? Does Jehovah really want me to take on more responsibility, or am I simply trying to prove my zeal? Am I willing to do everything possible to fulfill his will?' If we are modest in our expectations, we will be able to cooperate with others in harmony with the example set by Joshua and Caleb.
LET US REVIEW THIS MATERIAL
6. Explain what is meant by the expression "the ten tribes."
6 For 20 years, Deborah, a prophetess, judged Israel and Canaan. During those years the Israelites were oppressed. And as time passed, the Israelites began to intermarry with the Canaanites, and about 900 years elapsed from the time they entered the Promised Land until the Assyrians exiled them, causing them to forget or reject Jehovah.—Josh. 4:1-3, 13; 5:6-8. *
7, 8. (a) How does Jehovah show consideration for his servants? (b) Explain why the Israelites failed to conquer Canaan. (See accompanying box "Important Dates.")
7 Now that the Israelites had enjoyed peace for some time, Jehovah sent Joshua to lead Caleb in this assignment: "Go through the land, examine it, and see whether the report about it is accurate. . . . Also, bring back a sample of the fruit of the land, along with its produce; and go up to the mountainous region, and see what kind of place it is." (Josh. 4:4-7)
8 Caleb accepted this commission willingly. So all the older men among the tribes went to investigate the mountainous region, and their report regarding the area was favorable. They reported to Joshua, saying: "Jehovah has surely given us this land." (Read Joshua 4:14-16.) Later, when Joshua was old, he divided the land among the nine and a half tribes. However, Hebron remained under Caleb's control because he followed Jehovah fully. The Bible says that Caleb silenced any opposition by courageously sending his daughter Achsah away as a reward. Caleb gave Achsah the spring of En Rogel. She then asked him for more land, and he gave her upper and lower springs. From En Rogel she traveled south to the oak tree of Elon, which was located near Hebron. There she set up a tent. This spring became known as En Rogel, meaning "Spring of the Young Goat," and is still called that today. It is said that Achsah's spirit was courageous. (Josh. 4:17-21) Because of the boldness of Caleb and his daughter Achsah, the tribe of Judah was strengthened! *
PEOPLE AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP WITH OTHERS
9. What does Genesis 5:20, 21 reveal about how the ancient Israelites viewed life?
9 We will now examine chapters 4 and 5 of Genesis, noting that each chapter provides insight that can help us understand things better. For example, Genesis 5:20, 21 states: "After Seth had fathered Enosh, he lived 807 years and then died." Does this account mean that people at that time actually lived to be over 800 years old, or does it convey something else? Let us reason together. It is reasonable to conclude that God caused the patriarchs to live longer during that period, perhaps so they could oversee the rebuilding of mankind after the Flood. Did you ever wonder why the Bible mentions such great ages? Read Genesis 4:14, 15, and see how Jehovah views wickedness. Imagine someone who murdered another person—perhaps 10,000 Israelites—would he be considered righteous?
10, 11. What lesson can we learn from Melchizedek?
10 The fact that Noah prayed to Jehovah and received an answer shows that Jehovah was concerned about righteousness. That incident illustrates what the Bible says: "Bless Melchizedek, priest of the Most High God, who met Abraham and blessed him, and to whom Abraham gave a tenth."—Gen. 14:18–20.
11 Why did Melchizedek not reveal his genealogy? Was it not because he wanted people to focus on Jehovah? Or was it because he knew that Jehovah would choose someone from among mankind? This is illustrated by the account of the 10,000 men who went to war against Canaan. Also, remember how Melchizedek acted when Sodom was destroyed; he showed that he valued life greatly! So make good use of this opportunity to show your appreciation for Jehovah and his Kingdom. Those who take advantage of this opportunity will be able to associate closely with Jehovah's organization and enjoy lasting peace. However, some may feel that they are not qualified to serve alongside Melchizedek, like Jael, who courageously killed Sisera. But let us remember that Melchizedek appreciated her actions.—Gen. 5:23.
12 What does Genesis 5:9, 10 tell us about those whom God approves, and what lesson can we learn from this?
12 Let us examine Genesis 5:9, 10 again. But remember that Noah and his family were approved, while others did not gain deliverance. Why did Noah and his family find favor with Jehovah and with Noah? The scriptures say regarding the princes of Israel, "But they allied themselves with the people to go among the nations." Those princes found fault with others, saying, 'These men are troublesome,' but they failed to act in harmony with those who were loyal. And they found fault with others, saying, 'They have very large houses,' but they did not bother to live in an upright way. But they allied themselves with Noah to witness the judgment of the table and the writing of Cush regarding their conduct, and they said, 'They walk with boldness,' or in some other way, but they failed to heed. Therefore, they failed to live in an upright way, because they associated with disloyal people. Disloyalty leads to ruin, just as it led to the loss of God's approval and the destruction that followed. And anyone who associates with the wicked shows that he has no desire to please God and all that disloyalty involves.
13. How about the men of Reuben, Gad, and Asher—did they associate with the men of Naphtali and Zebulun?
13 But they allied themselves with them, realizing that Jehovah would vindicate his great name. They also took care not to say, 'Let us make covenants with the families of Jehovah.' (Gen. 5:11) It says further, the scripture in Genesis 5:15-17 shows that the men of Reuben, Gad, and Asher would join those whom Jehovah wanted to save from the flood. For example, it says that they had boats, barges, and ships for transportation (cargo). The men of Naphtali and Zebulun were like those three tribes in that they 'were eager to come forward' or took care to cooperate with Noah and his family. (Gen. 5:18) This shows that there was a difference between the tribes that cooperated and those that did not, and this is why the loyal ones were saved.
"SHOW APPRECIATION FOR JEHOVAH"
14. How can we show appreciation for Jehovah's great loving-kindness?
14 We will be motivated to do so when we realize that we have an opportunity to demonstrate our loyalty. Seeing how Jehovah has used millions of imperfect humans, both young and old, to proclaim the good news throughout the earth, including at Bethel homes, Kingdom Halls, and large assemblies, moves us to act. Yes, some send donations, while others serve as Kamiteens, or they help organize large events, and still others get involved in various ways. Strengthened by faith, they know that Jehovah appreciates their efforts, and they rejoice because of it.—Eph. 6:10.
15. What practical steps can we take to show our appreciation for Jehovah's loving-kindness?
15 Each one of us should ask himself: "Am I willing to share generously with others?" "Am I eager to support the work of making disciples?" "Do I imitate the courage of Barak, Deborah, Jael, and the 10,000 who were willing to fight for Jehovah?" "And am I determined to use my time and resources to help those who may be facing difficulties, whether spiritual or material?" *
16. Why does Jehovah value our willingness more than the amount we give?
16 We deeply appreciate what Jehovah has done to provide his Son as a ransom. However, just as David showed his loyalty when he offered to build God a temple, we can demonstrate our loyalty by being zealous in supporting Jehovah's organization and by exposing Satan and his wicked system. Jehovah is pleased when we show that we are determined to remain loyal to him and to cooperate with his direction. (Prov. 23:15, 16) He uses our zeal to strengthen us in resisting Satan, who tries to discourage us. (Prov. 27:11) The more we love Jehovah, the more we will enjoy using our resources to promote his interests. This will bring us great satisfaction.
17. What did Genesis 5:31 reveal about the extent of Noah's family?
17 Let us always remember the great value of Jehovah's gift of life. And let us make good use of the time we have left to preach the good news! Remember what David and Solomon said: "O Jehovah, how precious is your loving-kindness! That is why the sons of men find refuge in the shadow of your wings." (Ps. 5:31) Jehovah values our efforts to expose the wickedness of Satan. A man named Alistair MacIntyre once said that people often need to be reminded of basic truths. Here is another scripture that reminds us of an important truth: "Pray now, O Jehovah, remember me and show my strength." (2 Ki. 20:17) By praying for strength, we can continue to support Jehovah's organization with zeal and courage.
18. How can we show our appreciation for the Kingdom?
18 "And people of all nations will stream to him," David and Solomon foretold regarding the Kingdom. These words were fulfilled to some extent when Jesus was on earth. (Ps. 5:1, 2) But they will be fully realized when the Kingdom takes action to subdue all opposition and establish God's rulership. So, let us continue to proclaim the good news of the Kingdom and to urge others to 'seek Jehovah!'

ENOKO nĩwekalĩte ĩvinda yĩasa. Nĩtũtonya kũsũanĩa kana nĩ vinya mũndũ kwĩkala ĩvinda yĩasa mũno, ĩndĩ Enoko ekalile myaka 365, ũu nĩ kwasya kana nĩ kũndũ kũna kwa myaka mingĩ ĩla andũ mekalaa ĩvindanĩ ya ũmũnthĩ! Ĩndĩ kwosana na ũndũ andũ mekalaa myaka mingĩ ĩvindanĩ yake, Enoko ekalile ĩvinda ĩkuvĩ mũno. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu, myaka mbee wa 5,000 mĩvĩtu, andũ nĩmekalaa myaka mingĩ mũno vyũ kwĩ ũmũnthĩ. Atamu, ũla nĩwe mũndũũme wa mbee, aĩ na myaka mbee wa maana thanthatũ Enoko aisyawa, na nĩwaendeeie kwĩkala myaka ĩngĩ maana atatũ! O na ve nzyawa imwe sya Atamu syekalile myaka mingĩ kwĩ ĩsu ya Atamu. Kwoou Enoko e na myaka 365, nĩvatonyeka akethĩwa aĩ mũndũũme wĩ na vinya na weteele kwĩkala myaka mingĩ. Ĩndĩ ũw'o nĩ kana ndaaĩkala myaka yingĩvĩte ũu.
Nĩvatonyeka Enoko akethĩwa aĩ vakuvĩ kũawa. Kwakũna visa Enoko atolokete amaitha make, na alilikene ũndũ andũ ala wauma kũtavya ũvoo kuma kwa Ngai mavĩnga ndeto syake. Andũ asu moonekaa me na woo mwingĩ na nĩmamũmenete. Mayaaendeew'a nĩ ũvoo wake, o na nĩmamenete Ngai wa Enoko. Mayaĩ matonya kũkita na Ngai wa Enoko, ũla nĩwe Yeova, ĩndĩ maĩ na ũtonyi wa kũvithũkĩa Enoko! Nĩvatonyeka Enoko akethĩwa eekũlasya kana akesa kwona andũ make ĩngĩ. We nĩwĩthĩwa asũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa kĩveti kyake na eĩtu make, kana mwana wake ũla weetawa Methusela, kana mwĩsũkũũe ũla weetawa Lameki? (Mwambĩlĩlyo 5:21-23, 25) Ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mũminũkĩlyo wake?
No twasye kana Enoko ndawetetwe mũno Mbivilianĩ. Awetetwe o kwa ũkuvĩ kũndũ kũtatũ Mbivilianĩ. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 5:21-24; Aevelania 11:5; Yuta 14, 15) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, mĩsoa ĩsu yĩ Mbivilianĩ yĩ na ũvoo wĩanĩtye kũtũtetheesya kũmanya ũndũ Enoko waĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. We nĩwĩanĩasya mavata ma mũsyĩ waku? Kana waaĩsa kwĩyĩthĩa waĩle kwĩka ũtwi mũito wa kwĩka kĩla kyaĩle? Ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, no wĩmanyĩsye maũndũ maingĩ kũmana na mũĩkĩĩo wa Enoko.
"ENOKO AENDANASYA NA NGAI"
Andũ maĩ na mwĩkalĩle mũthũku mũno ĩvindanĩ ya Enoko. Ĩsu yaĩ nzyawa ya mũonza kuma kwa Atamu. Vate nzika, ĩvindanĩ yĩu andũ mayaĩ na mathĩna maingĩ ma mwĩĩ nũndũ vayaĩ ĩvinda yĩasa kuma Atamu na Eva mavĩtya. Na kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi andũ mekalaa myaka mingĩ mũno. Ĩndĩ maĩ na thĩna mũnene wa kĩ-veva na mwĩkalĩle woo waĩ mũthũku. Kwaĩ na ũng'endu mwingĩ mũno. Ũng'endu waĩ wambĩĩie nzyawanĩ ya kelĩ ya Atamu, ĩla Kaini wooaie mwana-a-inyia Aveli. O na veonekana kana ve nzyawa ĩmwe ya Kaini yaĩ na mĩtũlyo mũno nũndũ yaĩ na ũng'endu mwingĩ kwĩ ũ Kaini! Nzyawanĩ ya katatũ kuma Atamu, ve maũndũ angĩ mathũku mambĩĩie kwĩkĩka. Andũ nĩmambĩĩie kwĩkaĩla ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova, ĩndĩ mayatũmĩaa ĩsyĩtwa yĩu nĩ kwĩthĩwa nĩmayĩnengete ndaĩa. Nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa matũmĩaa naĩ ĩsyĩtwa ĩtheu ya Ngai.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:8, 23-26.
Nĩvatonyeka ũthaithi ũsu wa ũvũngũ ũkethĩwa waendeee mũno ĩvindanĩ ya Enoko. Kwoou Enoko aendeee kwĩana nĩwaaĩle kwĩka ũtwi mũito. Nĩwaaĩle kwĩka maũndũ ala meekawa nĩ andũ ala angĩ? Kana aaĩle kũmũmantha Ngai wa w'o, Yeova, ũla woombie matu na nthĩ? No nginya Enoko akethĩwa eekĩiwe vinya mũno ĩla weemanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Aveli ũla wooaiwe nũndũ wa kũmũthaitha Yeova kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩle. Enoko nĩwatwie kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Aveli. Ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩlyo 5:22 yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Enoko aendanasya na Ngai." Ndeto isu sya kwendeesya syĩonany'a kana Enoko aĩ mũndũ wamũkĩaa Ngai o na kau athyũlũlũkĩtwe nĩ andũ matamũkĩaa Ngai. Na nĩwe mũndũ wa mbee kũwetwa Mbivilianĩ kana aendanasya na Ngai.
Mũsoa o ũsu nĩwonanĩtye kana Enoko nĩwaendeeie kũendany'a na Yeova ĩtina wa kũsyaa Methusela. Kwoou Enoko aĩ na mũsyĩ e na myaka 65. Aĩ na kĩveti, o na kau ĩsyĩtwa yakyo yĩiwetetwe Mbivilianĩ, na aĩ na "ana na eĩtu," o na kau maiwetetwe maĩ meana. Ethĩwa mũndũũme nũkwenda kũendany'a na Ngai o aendeee kũea na kũsũvĩa mũsyĩ wake, no nginya atate vyũ kũũsũvĩa kwosana na kwenda kwa Ngai. Enoko nĩweesĩ kana Yeova endaa ethĩwe e mũĩkĩĩku vyũ kwa kĩveti kyake. (Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:24) Na vate nzika nĩweekĩie kĩthito kũmanyĩsya syana syake ĩũlũ wa Yeova Ngai. Kweethĩiwe ata nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu?
Mbivilia ĩeleetye o maũndũ manini ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu. Mbivilia ndĩwetete ũndũ o na ũmwe ĩũlũ wa mũĩkĩĩo wa Methusela, ũla waĩ mwana wa Enoko. Methusela nĩwe wekalile ĩvinda ĩasa katĩ wa andũ ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ, na akwie mwakanĩ ũla ĩla mbua ya kĩw'ũ kingĩ yauie ĩvindanĩ ya Noa. Methusela nĩwe waĩ ĩthe wa Lameki, na Lameki aĩ na myaka mbee wa ĩana ũmae wake Enoko aikw'a. Lameki aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Yeova nĩwamũveveeie Lameki athane ĩũlũ wa mwana wake Noa, na wathani ũsu nĩweanĩie ĩtina wa mbua ya kĩw'ũ kingĩ. O ta ũmae wake wa tene Enoko, Noa awetiwe ta mũndũ waendanasya na Ngai. Noa ndaamwona Enoko. Ĩndĩ Enoko nĩwatiĩie Noa ũtiĩwa wa vata vyũ. Nĩvatonyeka Noa akethĩwa eemanyĩisye maũndũ ma vata vyũ ĩũlũ wa Enoko kuma kwa ĩthe wake Lameki, kana kuma kwa ũmae Methusela, kana kuma kwa ĩthe wa Enoko ũla weetawa Yaleti, ũla wakwie Noa e na myaka 366.—Mwambĩlĩlyo 5:25-29; 6:9; 9:1.
Kwasũanĩa kĩvathũkany'o katĩ wa Enoko na Atamu. O na kau Atamu aĩ mũndũ ũte na naĩ, nĩwamũvĩtĩisye Yeova na atiĩa nzyawa syake mathĩna na atuma itw'ĩka alei o take. Nake Enoko, o na kau aĩ na naĩ, nĩwaendanasya na Ngai na atiĩie nzyawa syake ngelekany'o nzeo kwa kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Atamu akwie Enoko e na myaka 308. Nzyawa sya Atamu syaĩ na kyeva nũndũ wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ ũmae woo ũla weeyendete mũno? Mbivilia ndĩwetete. Ĩndĩ kĩla twĩsĩ nĩ kana Enoko "aendanasya na Ngai."—Mwambĩlĩlyo 5:24.
Ethĩwa nue ũmanthĩaa andũ ma mũsyĩ waku, ve maũndũ ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kumana na mũĩkĩĩo wa Enoko. O na kau nĩ ũndũ wa vata kũmanthĩa andũ ma mũsyĩ waku, vai ũndũ wa vata mũno ta kũmasũvĩa kĩ-veva. (1 Timotheo 5:8) Ũtonya kwĩanĩsya vata wa kĩ-veva wa mũsyĩ waku kwĩsĩla ndeto na meko maku. O ta Enoko, wanyuva kũendanasya na Ngai kwa kwĩtĩkĩla ũtongoew'e nĩ myolooto ĩla yĩ Mbivilianĩ, ũkeethĩwa ũtonya kũtiĩa andũ ma mũsyĩ waku ngelekany'o nzeo matonya kũatĩĩa.
ENOKO 'NĨWATHANIE' ĨŨLŨ WOO
Nĩvatonyeka Enoko akethĩwa ataĩ na ũtanu nũndũ ekalĩte nthĩ ĩtaĩ na andũ me na mũĩkĩĩo. Ĩndĩ we Yeova Ngai nĩwoonaa mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu wa Enoko? Ĩĩ, nĩwawonaa nũndũ ĩvinda nĩyavikie Yeova aneena na mũthũkũmi ũsu wake mũĩkĩĩku. Ngai nĩwamũtavisye Enoko ũvoo ũla wendaa andũ ma ĩvinda yake maũmanye. Kwoou nĩwamũnyuvie Enoko ethĩwe mwathani, na nĩwe wa mbee wathani wake kũvuanw'a Mbivilianĩ. Ndeto isu nĩ sya w'o nũndũ Yuta, ũla wasyaanĩw'e na Yesũ, nĩwaveveewe kũandĩka wathani ũla Enoko waĩ athanie myaka maana maingĩ mĩvĩtu. *
Nĩ maũndũ meva Enoko wathanie? Athanie atĩĩ: "Sisyai, Mwĩai nĩwokie vamwe na atheu make, nguthu ĩtatalĩka, kũmasilĩla andũ onthe, na kũmaĩkĩĩthya onthe ala matamũkĩaa Ngai ũndũ wa meko moo onthe ma kũlea kũmũkĩaa Ngai ala meekie, na nũndũ wa ndeto syoo syonthe nyũmũ ila asu athe matamũkĩaa Ngai mamũneeneete." (Yuta 14, 15) Ũndũ ũmwe ĩandĩko yĩu yoonany'a nĩ kana Enoko athanie ũndũ ũsu ta waĩ weekĩkie ĩvindanĩ ĩvĩtu, na Ngai ta waĩ eanĩsye maũndũ ala me wathaninĩ ũsu. Nzĩa ĩsu ya kwathana yatũmĩiwe nĩ Enoko nĩyesie kũtũmĩwa nĩ athani angĩ. Ũu nĩ kwasya, athani asu mathanaa maũndũ mataĩ na nzika kana makeanĩa na nĩkyo kĩtumi mamawetaa ta maĩ meanĩie!—Isaia 46:10.
Waĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi Enoko kumya wathani ũsu kwa kũtavya andũ onthe ala maaĩle kũwĩw'a? Wathani ũsu waĩ na ndeto ngito mũno nũndũ ũwetete ndeto "matamũkĩaa Ngai" mavinda elĩ, na ũkaweta kana andũ asu maĩ na meko ma kũlea "kũmũkĩaa Ngai," kwonany'a ũndũ andũ asu mailyĩ, na ũndũ ndeto syoo syoonanasya kana mayamũkĩaa Ngai. Kwoou wathani ũsu waumasya ũkany'o kwa andũ onthe mamanye kana nthĩ yaendeee na kũthũkĩĩa kuma ĩla mũndũ walũngilw'e mũũndanĩ wa Eteni. Nthĩ ĩsu yeeteele wanangĩko mũnene ĩla Yeova waĩ oke na "atheu make," ala nĩ nguthu nene ya alaĩka mokĩte kwondũ wa kũete wanangĩko ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Enoko nĩwaumisye ũkany'o ũsu ateũkĩa, na eekaa ũu e weka! Nĩvatonyeka Lameki e mũnini akethĩwa oonie ũndũ ũsu na endeew'a mũno nĩ ũkũmbaũ wa ũmae wake. Na ethĩwa vailyĩ ũu, no tũelewe nĩkĩ Lameki wendeeiw'e nĩ ũndũ Enoko waĩ na ũkũmbaũ.
Mũĩkĩĩo wa Enoko no ũtũtetheesye kũmanya kana twĩ na woni ta wa Ngai kwelekela maũndũ ma nthĩ ĩno. O tondũ Enoko waumisye ũkany'o ĩũlũ wa ũsilĩlo wa andũ ala matamũkĩaa Ngai, now'o o naitũ ũmũnthĩ tũkanasya andũ ĩũlũ wa ũsilĩlo ũla wũkĩte. Kwosana na ũndũ Enoko wathanĩte, ĩvindanĩ ya Noa Yeova nĩwaetie mbua nene nĩ kana anange andũ ala matamũkĩaa. Ĩndĩ wanangĩko ũsu weethĩiwe waĩ kyuu kya wanangĩko mũnene ũla wũkĩte. (Mathayo 24:38, 39; 2 Vetelo 2:4-6) O tondũ Ngai vamwe na alaĩka make atheu meeyũmbanĩtye kwananga andũ ala matamũkĩaa, now'o ũvangĩte kwĩsa kwananga andũ ala athũku. Kĩla ũmwe waitũ nĩwaĩle kũlilikanaa ũkany'o ũla Enoko waumisye na aitavya andũ ala angĩ ĩũlũ waw'o. Andũ maitũ ma mũsyĩ na anyanya maitũ no mevathane naitũ. O na mavinda angĩ nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũyĩw'a ta tũtendetwe. Ĩndĩ Yeova ndaaĩsa kũmũtia Enoko, na ndesa kũmatia athũkũmi make ala aĩkĩĩku ĩvindanĩ ya ũmũnthĩ!
"NĨWAMBATIW'E NDAKONE KĨKW'Ũ"
Mũminũkĩlyo wa Enoko wailyĩ ata? No twasye kana ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kũelewa ũndũ Enoko wakwie tondũ tũtonya kũelewa nesa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ wekalaa ĩla waĩ thayũ, ĩndĩ kũmanya ũndũ wakwie nĩ ũndũ ũtonya kũtwendeesya. Ĩvuku ya Mwambĩlĩlyo yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Enoko aendanasya na Ngai: na ndaĩ vo; nũndũ Ngai nĩwamwosie." (Mwambĩlĩlyo 5:24) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Ngai wamwosie Enoko? Mbivilia imwe ialyũlĩte ndeto ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Aevelania 11:5 kwa kwasya kana Ngai nĩwamwambatisye Enoko ĩtunĩ. Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũsu ti wa w'o. Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye kana Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwe waĩ wa mbee kũthayũũkw'a na kwambata ĩtunĩ.—Yoana 3:13.
O na ĩngĩ, ve Mbivilia imwe ialyũlĩte ĩandĩko yu ya Aevelania 11:5 ikonany'a kana Enoko 'nĩwathamiw'e' nĩ kana "ndakone kĩkw'ũ." Ndeto isu twaĩle kũsielewa ata? Nĩvatonyeka Yeova akethĩwa eekie kyama nĩ kana Enoko akw'e kĩkw'ũ kĩte woo vandũ va ese kũawa nĩ andũ ala mavangĩte kũmũaa kwa nzĩa nthũku. Ĩndĩ mbee, Enoko ambie 'kũkũsĩĩwa kana nĩwamwendeeasya Ngai.' Ũu weethĩiwe ata? Nĩvatonyeka Enoko atanamba kũkw'a akethĩwa ooniw'e woni nĩ Ngai, na woni ũsu no wĩthĩwe woonanasya nthĩ ĩno yĩ nzaũ. Enoko nĩwakwie ĩtina wa kwonw'a woni ũsu ũla wamũĩkĩĩthisye kana nĩwamwendeeasya Yeova. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aielesya ĩũlũ wa Enoko o vamwe na aũme na aka angĩ maĩ aĩkĩĩku aisye atĩĩ: "Asu onthe nĩmakwie mũĩkĩĩonĩ." (Aevelania 11:13) Nĩvatonyeka amaitha ma Enoko makethĩwa mamanthie mwĩĩ wake, ĩndĩ 'mayaawona' nũndũ no kwĩthĩwa Yeova aũvetangie nĩ kana asiĩĩe amaitha make maikawanange kana maikaũvukye kwa kũũtũmĩa nĩ kana maendeesye ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ. *
Tũlilikene maũndũ asu tweemanyĩsya Maandĩkonĩ, ekai tũsũanĩe ũndũ Enoko ũtonya kwĩthĩwa akwie. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ ũtonya kwĩthĩwa new'o weethĩiwe. Kwakũna visa wone Enoko atolokete amaitha make, na e mũnou mũno. Andũ ala mamũvĩngaa nĩmamũmanthaa me na ũthilĩku mwingĩ nũndũ wa ũvoo wa ũsilĩlo ũla wamatavĩtye. Enoko nĩwoonie vandũ ũtonya kwĩvitha athyũmũe o vanini, ĩndĩ nĩweesĩ kana ndesa kwĩvitha andũ asu kwa ĩvinda yĩasa. Yu Enoko aĩ vakuvĩ kũawa naĩ. Athyũmũĩte vau, nĩwamũvoyie Ngai wake. Na ĩndĩ ambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa na mũuo mwingĩ. Enoko nĩwooniw'e woni nginya wesa kwĩthĩa eona ta maũndũ maendeee kwĩkĩka saanĩ isu, na woni ũsu watuma asũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ mokĩte.
Kwasũanĩa Enoko ayona woni wa nthĩ ĩngĩ nzeo na yĩ kĩvathũkany'o mũno na nthĩ ĩla ũtwĩe. Oonie nthĩ ĩsu yĩ mbanake o ta ũndũ mũũnda wa Eteni waanakavĩte, ĩndĩ nthĩ ĩsu ndyaĩ na akelũvi ma kũsiĩĩa andũ maikamĩlike. Nthĩ ĩsu yausĩe aũme na aka me na mĩĩ mĩseo na me na vinya mwingĩ. O na mekalanasya na mũuo. Nthĩ ĩsu ndyaĩ na kĩmena kana andũ meũthĩny'a angĩ nũndũ wa ũthaithi woo tondũ kwailyĩ ĩvinda yake. Enoko nĩwoonie kana Yeova nĩwamwendete na nĩwendeeaw'a nĩwe. Ndaĩ na nzika kana akalika nthĩ ĩla woonie woninĩ ũsu. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu waendeeie kwĩthĩwa na mũuo, Enoko nĩwakomie too mũito ũte ndoto.
O na yu e o toonĩ ũsu, ũu nĩ kwasya kana nĩ mũkw'ũ, ĩndĩ Yeova Ngai nũmũlilikene! O tondũ Yesũ wathanie, mũthenya ũkavika ĩla onthe ala me kĩlilikanonĩ kya Ngai makew'a wasya wa Klĩsto na mayuma mbũanĩ, nĩ kana malike nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ nzeo na yĩ mũuo.—Yoana 5:28, 29.
We no wende wĩĩthĩwa nthĩnĩ wa nthĩ ĩsu? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũkatana wakomana na Enoko. Kwasũanĩa maũndũ maseo ala ũkemanyĩsya kuma kwake! Akeethĩwa atonya kũtũtavya maũndũ ala twasũanĩaa wĩthĩwa ooniw'e nĩ Yeova atanamba kũkw'a kana maĩ ma w'o. Ĩndĩ yu ve ũndũ wa vata mũno twaĩle kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wake. Ĩtina wa kũneenea ĩũlũ wa Enoko, Vaulo aendeeie kwasya atĩĩ: "Vate mũĩkĩĩo kũitonyeka kũmwendeesya" Ngai. (Aevelania 11:6) Ũu wĩonany'a kana twĩ na kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩyĩelekany'a na Enoko, ũla waĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu vyũ!
^ kal. 14 Asomi amwe ma Mbivilia maasya kana ndeto ila Yuta waandĩkie syaumĩte ĩvukunĩ yaĩ na maũndũ mate ma w'o yĩla yeetawa Ĩvuku ya Enoko (Book of Enoch), ĩndĩ o na kau ĩvuku yĩu yĩwetanĩaw'a na Enoko, yĩyĩsĩkĩe mwambĩlĩĩlyo wayo. Ĩvuku yĩu nĩyĩwetete nesa ĩũlũ wa wathani wa Enoko, ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka wathani ũsu wĩ ĩvukunĩ yĩu ũkethĩwa waumĩtw'e mavukunĩ maĩ maandĩkiwe ĩvinda ya tene o na kau yu tũyĩsa kũmona, kana ũkethĩwa waumĩtw'e ngewanĩ sya tene. Yuta nũtonya kwĩthĩwa atũmĩie mavuku asu ma tene kana akethĩwa eemanyĩisye ĩũlũ wa Enoko kuma kwa Yesũ, ũla wekalaa ĩtunĩ na kwoou no nginya ethĩwe oonaa maũndũ ala Enoko weekaa.
^ kal. 20 O ta Enoko, nĩvatonyeka Ngai akethĩwa aĩkĩĩthisye kana mwĩĩ wa Mose na wa Yesũ ndwaĩ ũtonya kwoneka nĩ mũndũ nĩ kana ndũkatũmĩwe naĩ.—Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 34:5, 6; Luka 24:3-6; Yuta 9.
