translation:
Enoch was walking with God. We don't fear to say or is it possible someone to walk with God like this, because Enoch lived for 365 years, which is little compared to the many years people live in the world! Because compared to how many years people live in their lives, Enoch lived a very short life. In his lifetime, about 5,000 generations, people have lived many years on earth. Adam, who was the first man, had about eighty years when Enoch was born, and he continued to live another ninety years! And there were others born of Adam who lived many years during the time of Adam. Now Enoch was 365 years old, we don't know why someone would want and be able to live many years. Because of this, maybe I will live more years than this.
We don't know why Enoch was taken away. During his time, Enoch found favor with God, and he pleased God by living righteously according to His will. People saw him as having much wisdom and they respected him. He continued in his righteousness, and he honored God of Enoch. They may not understand God of Enoch, who is Jehovah, so they don't understand the reason for honoring Enoch! We don't know why Enoch was taken to show him to his people. Who is the one who tells us about his family and his things, or his son whose name is Methuselah, or his grandson whose name is Lamech? (Genesis 5:21-23, 25) This is what we learn from his history?
But let's see if Enoch was transferred to heaven. He was transferred because of his righteous life to heaven. (Genesis 5:21-24; Hebrews 11:5; Jude 14, 15) So now this story of heaven has a purpose to help us understand what Enoch did and his excellent example. Who will examine the details of this matter? Or will you listen carefully to hear every little thing? If you study this well, you will understand many things related to the example of Enoch.
"ENOCH WALKED WITH GOD"
Many people know about the account of Enoch. It happened shortly after Adam. Later on, the account says that people began to multiply greatly and they populated the earth like Adam and Eve had commanded. And that is why people lived for so many years then. But there was also a great sin and people knew about it. There was much wickedness then. This wickedness reminded me of the sin of Cain when he killed his brother Abel. And it appeared that there was only one righteous man, Cain, who had much wickedness! The third generation from Adam experienced many bad things. People began to disregard the name of Jehovah, and instead of honoring His name, they honored false gods. They stopped obeying God's commandments and laws.—Genesis 4:8, 23-26.
They continued to practice this wicked course until the time of Enoch. Now Enoch continued to walk with God, keeping his heart upright. Did he care what others thought of him? Or did he fear men, Jehovah, who sees everything and knows our thoughts? Well, let us see how Enoch proved his faith by speaking out against the wickedness that existed because of Abel's murder. Enoch dared to prophesy concerning the judgment that would come upon those wicked ones. Genesis 5:22 states: "Enoch walked with God." What does it mean to walk with someone? Does it mean that Enoch was a perfect man or that he was better than other imperfect men? He is the first person to be resurrected to heaven because he walked with God.
This question arises: Did Enoch continue walking with Jehovah during the lifetime of Methuselah? Now Enoch was 65 years old when he had Methuselah. He became a father, and Methuselah was later taken to heaven, and he also had "sons and daughters," who were born after he went to heaven. Anyone desiring to walk with God must continue to learn about Him and to apply what he learns, and he will find strength to remain loyal to God. Enoch knew that Jehovah could bring about His purpose through his son. (Genesis 2:24) And so he took courage to testify to his sons about Jehovah God. Will he do anything to speak the truth?
The Bible reveals important things regarding this matter. The Bible tells us about something concerning the genealogy of Methuselah, the son of Enoch. Methuselah became the oldest man among those called people, and he lived 969 years, which was before the flood of Noah's time. Methuselah was the father of Lamech, and Lamech was 182 years old when his son Enoch was born. Lamech had a prophecy. Jehovah foretold to Lamech about his son Noah, and this prophecy showed that there would be relief from the flood. But like his ancestor Enoch, Noah proved to be a righteous man who walked with God. Noah saw Enoch. Indeed, Enoch instructed Noah on matters relating to future events. It seems Noah received information from Enoch through his father Lamech, or through his grandfather Methuselah, or through the father of Enoch who was named Jared, who lived to be 969 years old.—Genesis 5:25-29; 6:9; 9:1.
Considering the differences between Enoch and Adam. And though Adam was a perfect man, he disobeyed Jehovah and risked his life by eating from the forbidden tree. Unlike Adam, Enoch pleased God and risked his life by walking in righteousness. Adam lived to be 930 years old. Did Adam's life show any evidence of being approved because of his long life? The Bible does not say so. In fact, it says that Enoch "walked with God."—Genesis 5:24.
However, some may find it difficult to reconcile what is said with the genealogy of Enoch. Though it is a matter of future events, it is not a matter of certainty. (1 Timothy 5:8) It can be hard to understand future events involving relatives and friends. Like Enoch, enjoying walking with God requires making sacrifices, which may make it difficult to help others.
ENOCH 'WALKED' IN THIS WAY
It is remarkable that Enoch is mentioned along with men who had a reputation for integrity. Is this because Jehovah approved of Enoch's integrity? Yes, because He saw that Enoch kept himself separate from the wickedness of his time. God foretold to Enoch that disaster would come upon those wicked people. Therefore, He rescued Enoch from that fate, and He made him an example for all faithful ones to follow. Today, we have a similar hope through Jesus Christ, who has given us the opportunity to write about Enoch's experience after many years. *
What lessons can we learn from Enoch's example? He taught that "Jehovah will deliver his loyal ones and rescue them from all distress, to gather together those who know his name and cause them to dwell near him, so that they may seek Jehovah and find him, and those who seek him will be blessed." (Jude 14, 15) This teaching shows that Enoch understood that Jehovah would fulfill His purpose toward those who love Him, and that He would bless those who seek Him sincerely. The way Enoch spoke about the future proves that he was used by God to convey messages, just like other prophets were. It is no surprise, then, that his words were accurate and that his prophecy came true!—Isaiah 46:10.
Why did Enoch feel compelled to speak out against the wicked people of his time? His warning contained the expression "those who know God's name" repeatedly, and it showed that people needed to strive to "seek Jehovah," which meant living in harmony with what pleases Jehovah. However, most people did not heed this warning, nor did they show genuine desire to know God. So his warning proved to be effective only among those who accepted his message and continued to put faith in Jehovah. This is similar to how it was with Noah, whom God warned about a great flood. Jehovah foretold that He had "his own people," and this was a reason why He decided to bring a devastating flood upon the earth. Enoch realized the importance of this message, and he acted accordingly! We see that Lamech, his great-grandson, also spoke about this matter and expressed confidence in God's promise. And because he did so, we understand that Lamech was influenced by what Enoch said and believed.
The prophecy of Enoch helps us to discern whether we too are pleasing Jehovah by the way we live our lives. Because Enoch spoke out against the wickedness of the people who claimed to worship God, we can learn from his example and warn others about the dangers of wickedness. In line with what Enoch prophesied, Jehovah provided a means of escape for Noah and his family when He brought a flood to destroy those who were wicked. The fulfillment of this prophecy demonstrates the magnitude of Jehovah's concern for those who love Him. (Matthew 24:38, 39; 2 Peter 2:4-6) Since God associates with his angels in carrying out judgment on those who are wicked, we should be encouraged to share in denouncing the conduct of the ungodly. Each one of us needs to remember the warning that Enoch gave and to warn those who are inclined to walk in wickedness. Our brothers and sisters, along with interested ones, will appreciate our efforts. And let us always trust that Jehovah will help us to do what is right.
"I HAVE CONFIDENCE IN THIS PROMISE"
What does Enoch's prophecy mean to you? Perhaps you wonder how Enoch could have such confidence in foretelling future events, especially since we find it difficult to understand matters relating to the distant future. However, knowing what happened to Enoch can encourage us to put our trust in Jehovah. The book of Genesis states: "Enoch walked with God; and he was gone, because God took him." (Genesis 5:24) How did God take Enoch? A Bible commentary sheds light on this by referring to Hebrews 11:5, which explains that God transferred Enoch to another realm. But that is not what the Bible says. The Bible indicates that Jesus Christ is the one who will bring about the resurrection of those who are faithful.—John 3:13.
Furthermore, a Bible commentary refers to the scripture in Hebrews 11:5 stating that Enoch 'was taken away,' meaning he "met his end." So, how can we understand this? It seems reasonable that Jehovah approved of Enoch's integrity and transported him to a safe place among angels. In effect, Enoch experienced a preview of the resurrection. Did Enoch die? It seems that Enoch did not experience death, but was brought up to be with God, and this hope is now available to others. Enoch lived looking forward to being with Jehovah. The apostle Paul spoke of Enoch along with others who demonstrated faith, saying: "All these died in faith."—Hebrews 11:13. Does this mean that Enoch's life lost its value, or that his accomplishments were meaningless because they were not fully realized during his lifetime? It seems that Jehovah appreciates the faith of individuals and values their efforts, even if the full outcome of their endeavors is not seen until later. *
Let us examine what the scriptures reveal about Enoch so that we may better understand why he was transported. Understanding this matter can be encouraging. Like Enoch, we too can maintain our integrity despite difficulties. But remember that Enoch's case is unique, and it does not set a precedent. Others may face trials and hardships, and they will need courage and endurance. Enoch proved to be an example to those who would live later, showing them that it is possible to please God even when facing opposition. Because Enoch walked with God, he had a close relationship with Him. And he continued to serve faithfully despite obstacles. Enoch showed us that we can remain steadfast even when things seem impossible, and that our faithfulness can inspire others.
Understanding Enoch's experience helps us appreciate how much Jehovah values loyalty. He did not promise anyone else such a transfer. It illustrates the principle that Jehovah supports those who support him. This is similar to what happened to Adam when he disobeyed God, resulting in suffering and death for mankind. This situation has caused pain and sorrow throughout history. Yet, Jehovah remains compassionate. And he continues to offer hope. Enoch demonstrated that Jehovah cares for those who love him and that He responds to their prayers. We can also find comfort knowing that Jehovah remembers those who are loyal to Him. The prospect of resurrection offers great encouragement.
And so, let us take heart from this, for it shows that Jehovah is merciful! Since Jesus died, the opportunity for eternal life is available to all who exercise faith in God and demonstrate obedience to Christ and share in proclaiming the good news—John 5:28, 29.
How can we show our appreciation for what Enoch did? By learning more about his example! By meditating on the things he experienced, we can be motivated to remain faithful to Jehovah despite difficulties. For he assures us that he will remember those who seek him. To have a closer relationship with Jehovah, Paul wrote: "Without faith it is impossible to please God." (Hebrews 11:6) Let us therefore strengthen our faith and imitate Enoch's exemplary loyalty!
^ par. 14 Some Bible students also study other ancient writings such as the Testament of Judah which was written around the same time as Enoch's book (Book of Enoch), though it is not included in the canon of Scripture, this book is closely linked to Enoch, and provides further insight into his life. This book sheds light on Enoch's righteous conduct, and helps us understand how he remained loyal during difficult times, and shows us how we too can remain steadfast when facing trials today. Judah could use these ancient books to help others understand Enoch's loyalty to Jesus, showing that he lived in harmony with God's will and taught people important truths that Enoch revealed.
^ par. 20 Like Enoch, let us strive to please God and demonstrate our faith like Moses and Jesus did—by proving ourselves obedient to Him.—Numbers 34:5, 6; Luke 24:3-6; Jude 9.

text:
"Mũtyĩsĩ mũthenya ũla Mwĩaĩi wenyu wĩũka."—MT. 24:42.
MBATHI: 136, 54
1. Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a vata wa kũmanya twĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩva na nĩ kyaũ kĩendeee? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
KWASŨANĨA ĩvinda ya ũmbano mũnene. Mwene kĩvĩla aendaa mbee na aithokya kĩla mũndũ kwondũ wa wini ũla ũkilyĩ kwambĩĩa. Ala methukĩĩsye nĩmamanyaa yĩu nĩyo ĩvinda ya kwĩkala nthĩ makilĩtye. Kwondũ wa kĩ? Nĩ kwondũ wa kũtanĩa kwĩthukĩĩsya mbathi nzeo ikũnĩtwe nĩ kĩkundi kya kũkũna wathi kya Watchtower, na mũno mũno kũmbany'a kĩlĩko na ngoo nĩ kana methukĩĩsye maũvoo ala maatĩĩe. Nao nata vesa kwĩthĩwa ve andũ amwe mavĩngĩĩsĩkie kĩlĩko na makwetye kũtangatanga maendeee kũea ngewa na anyanyae matesĩ kana ũmbano ũkilyĩ kwambĩĩa? Methĩawa mate metho makamanya nĩ saa siana ata na nĩ kyaũ kĩendeee. Kwa ngelekany'o, mayĩthĩawa mesĩ mwene kĩvĩla e mbee, wini nĩwambĩĩe, na andũ nĩmekalile nthĩ. Ngelekany'o ĩsu nĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũelewe nesa ũndũ ĩvinda yĩla yĩtialĩte ne ĩnini vekĩke ũndũ mũnene, na ũndũ ũsu wĩenda ithyonthe twĩthĩwe twĩ metho. Ũndũ ũsu mũnene ũkilyĩ kwĩkĩka nĩ wĩva?
2. Nĩkĩ Yesũ weeie amanyĩw'a make ũũ, "Syaĩĩsyai"?
2 Ĩla Yesũ Klĩsto waneenaa ĩũlũ wa "wĩanĩu wa ĩvinda yĩĩ," eeie amanyĩw'a make ũũ: "Ĩsũvĩei, syaĩĩsyai, na voyai: nũndũ mũtyĩsĩ ĩvinda yĩu nĩ ĩndĩĩ." Ĩtina wa ũu Yesũ amatavisye ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ ndeto ĩĩ: "Syaĩĩsyai." (Mt. 24:3; soma Maliko 13:32-37.) O naw'o ũvoo ũla wĩ ĩvukunĩ ya Mathayo ũvw'anene na ũsu wĩonany'a kana Yesũ nĩwakanisye aatĩĩi make aimea: 'Syaĩĩsyai ĩndĩ; nũndũ mũtyĩsĩ mũthenya ũla Mwĩaĩi wenyu wĩũka. Ĩkalai mwĩyũmbanĩtye; nũndũ saa ũla mũtataĩĩe nĩw'o wĩũka ũla Mwana wa mũndũ.' Nĩwasyokie ĩngĩ amea: 'Syaĩĩsyai ĩndĩ, nũndũ mũtyĩsĩ mũthenya kana saa.'—Mt. 24:42-44; 25:13.
3. Nĩkĩ twosaa ũkany'o wa Yesũ na ũito?
3 Ithyĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩtwosaa kwa ũito ũkany'o ũsu wa Yesũ. Nĩtwĩsĩ kana twĩ mũniinĩonĩ wa "ĩvinda ya mũminũkĩlyo," na kana kavinda kala katiele ũla "thĩna mũnene" wambĩĩe nĩ kanini mũno! (Nda. 12:4; Mt. 24:21) Kĩla vandũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ nĩtwonete makaũ mathũku, tũkona maũndũ ma ũlaalai na ũng'endu mayingĩva, ũkengani wa ndĩni, ũnyivu wa lĩu, mowau mathũku, na ithingitho sya nthĩ. O na nĩtwĩsĩ kana andũ ma Yeova kĩla vandũ nĩmaendeee kũtethya wĩa mũnene wa kũtavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ. (Mt. 24:7, 11, 12, 14; Luka 21:11) Na ĩndĩ nĩtweteele mũno kwona ũndũ kũka kwa Mwĩaĩi kũkethĩwa ũathimo kwitũ, na ũndũ kũkeanĩsya kĩeleelo kya Ngai.—Mko. 13:26, 27.
MŨTHENYA NŨTHENGEEE MŨNO!
4. (a) Twĩsĩ ata kana Yesũ yu nĩwĩsĩ ĩla kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni ũkokitwa? (b) O na kau tũyĩsĩ nĩ ĩndĩĩ ũla thĩna mũnene ũkambĩĩa, nĩ kyaũ tũte na nzika nakyo?
4 Nĩtwĩsĩ kana kĩla ũmbano mũnene wĩ saa ila wĩthĩawa ũvangĩĩwe kwambĩĩa. Ĩndĩ o na tũkatata ata tũyĩsa kũmanya ũla thĩna mũnene ũkambĩĩa mũthenya wĩva na saa wĩva. O na eka i saa na mũthenya, tũyĩsa kũmanya ũkambĩĩa mwaka wĩva. Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ aisye: "Mũthenya ũsu na saa ũsu vai ũmwe wĩsĩ, o na alaĩka ma ĩtunĩ, o na Mwana, ĩndĩ no Asa weka." (Mt. 24:36) Ĩndĩ yu tũĩ Klĩsto nũnengetwe ũkũmũ ĩtunĩ wa kũkita nthĩ ĩno ya Satani. (Ũvu. 19:11-16) Kwoou no twasye kana yu Yesũ nĩwĩsĩ kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni ũkethĩwa ĩndĩĩ. Ĩndĩ ithyĩ tũyĩsĩ. Kwoou kĩla twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kũendeea kũsyaĩĩsya nginya ĩla thĩna ũsu ũkavika. Vai mũthenya o na ũmwe Yeova waaĩthĩwa atesĩ ĩvinda yĩu yĩkavika ĩndĩĩ. Nĩwatwie nĩ ĩndĩĩ mũthya ũkavika. Nayu nũendeee kũtala ĩvinda yĩla yĩtialĩte thĩna mũnene ũyĩsa kwambĩĩa, naw'o "ndũkekala." (Soma Avakuki 2:1-3.) Twĩsĩ ata kana ndũkaselewa?
5. Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a kana kĩla ĩvinda mawathani ala Yeova wathanaa meanĩaa ĩvindanĩ o yĩla ũvangĩĩe.
5 Kĩla ĩvinda mawathani ala Yeova wathanaa meanĩaa ĩvindanĩ o yĩla ũvangĩĩe! Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya ĩvinda yĩla waumisye Aisilaeli ũkombonĩ nthĩ ya Misili. Ĩvinda yĩmwe ve ũndũ Mose waisye aiweta ĩũlũ wa matukũ 14 ma mwei wa Nisani, mwaka wa 1513 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. Aisye: 'Myaka ĩsu maana ana na mĩongo ĩtatũ yathela, mũthenya o ũsu kweethĩwa atĩ nguthu syonthe sya Yeova syauma nthĩ ya Misili.' (Kuma 12:40-42) Myaka ĩsu "maana ana na mĩongo ĩtatũ" yambĩĩe kũtalwa ĩla ũtianĩo ũla Yeova watianĩie na Avalaamu wambĩĩe kwĩanĩa mwakanĩ wa 1943 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. (Aka. 3:17, 18) Ĩvinda ĩna matianĩa ũtianĩo ũsu, Yeova atavisye Avalaamu ndeto ii: "Manya vyũ kana ũsyao waku ũkeethĩwa mũeni nthĩ ĩte yoo, na makamathũkũma; na makamathĩn'ya myaka maana ana." (Mwa. 15:13; Meko 7:6) Myaka ĩsu "maana ana" no kwĩthĩwa yambĩĩe mwakanĩ wa 1913 Klĩsto ate mũsyae, yĩla ĩvinda Isaka waaĩw'e na Isumaeli amũvũĩa ngũĩ, na no kwĩthĩwa yathelile yĩla Aisilaeli maumie nthĩ ya Misili mwakanĩ wa 1513 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. (Mwa. 21:8-10; Aka. 4:22-29) Yeova nĩwatwie nesa ĩvinda yĩla ũkatangĩĩa andũ make, myaka maana ana kĩu kĩtanethĩwa!
6. Nĩkĩ tũi na nzika kana Yeova akavonokya andũ make?
6 Yosua aĩ ũmwe katĩ wa ala maumiw'e ũkombonĩ Misili, na kwoou alilikanilye mbaĩ ya Isilaeli ũndũ ũũ: "Inyw'ĩ nĩmwĩsĩ ngoonĩ syenyu syonthe na mathayũnĩ menyu onthe, kũtyaalea kwĩanĩw'a ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ onthe maseo ala Yeova Ngai wenyu waneenie ũndũ wenyu; onthe nĩmeanĩw'e kwenyu, kũtyaalea kwĩanĩw'a ũndũ ũmwe katĩ wamo." (Yos. 23:2, 14) O naitũ no twĩkale tũte na nzika kana watho ũla Yeova ũtwathĩte wa kũtũvonokya ũla thĩna mũnene ndũkatĩa kwĩanĩa. Ĩndĩ twenda kũvonoka mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno, no nginya tũendeee kũsyaĩĩsya.
NO NGINYA TŨSYAĨĨSYE NĨ KANA TWĨVONOKA
7, 8. (a) Mũsungi aĩ na wĩa wĩva ĩvindanĩ ya tene, na kĩu kĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩkĩka asungi makoma me wĩanĩ? Nengane ngelekany'o.
7 Kũsisya ũndũ kwailyĩ ĩvinda ya tene no kũtũmanyĩsye kĩndũ ĩũlũ wa vata wa kũsyaĩĩsya. Ĩvinda yĩu ya tene ndũa ila nene ta Yelusaleme syeethĩawa syakĩĩwe ũkũta mũtũlu kũithyũlũlũka. Ngũta isu nĩsyasũvĩaa ndũa ndĩkavithũkĩwe laisi, na syaĩ ndũlu ũkethĩa mũndũ no aũngame ĩũlũ akona nthĩ ĩla ĩthyũlũlũkĩte ndũa ĩsu. Kwĩthĩwe nĩ ũtukũ kana nĩ mũthenya, asungi meethĩawa ku ngũtanĩ ĩũlũ vamwe na mĩvĩanĩ ya ũlikĩla. Wĩa woo waĩ kũtavya ala me ndũanĩ mũisyo ũla moona ũtonya kũmavikĩa. (Isa. 62:6) Asungi asu maema kwĩkala masyaĩĩsye na me metho wĩanĩ woo, maĩ matonya kũtuma andũ aingĩ ndũanĩ ĩsu makw'a.—Esek. 33:6.
8 Mũsomi ũmwe Mũyuti weetawa Josephus aisye kana mwakanĩ wa 70 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa, ita sya Lomi syatavie Mwako Mũtũlu wa Antonia ũla wakwatene na ũkũta wa Yelusaleme nũndũ asungi ala maĩ mũvĩanĩ wa kũlika mwakonĩ ũsu maĩ too. Ita isu syamina kũlikĩla mũvĩanĩ ũsu syavĩtie ĩmwe ĩkalũnĩ na syayĩkwatya mwaki. Kĩko kĩu nĩkyo kyaminĩĩie ĩvinda ya thĩna mwingĩ ũla ũtaĩ waaoneka ĩngĩ ndũanĩ ĩsu ya Yelusaleme na ũtaĩ waakwata ĩngĩ mbaĩ ya Ayuti.
9. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ matesĩ?
9 Nthĩ mbingĩ ũmũnthĩ iiaa asikalĩ mĩvakanĩ nĩ kana masunge, o na nĩsyĩthĩawa na masinĩ sya matukũ aa sya kũsisya mĩisyo ĩla ĩtonya kumĩla. Wĩa wa asungi asu na masinĩ isu nĩ kũsisya kĩndũ o na kĩva kana mũndũ o na wĩva ndakese kũlika nthĩ yoo ate mwĩtĩkĩlye, na kũsiĩĩa amaitha ala matonya kũlika nthĩ yoo maete thĩna mũnene nthĩ ĩsu. Ĩndĩ mĩisyo ĩla masinĩ isu na asungi asu matonya kwona no ĩla ĩetawe nĩ andũ kana silikalĩ sya andũ. Ĩndĩ mayĩsĩ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nũsumbĩkĩte ĩtunĩ, na mayĩsĩ maũndũ ala ũendeee kwĩka ũtongoew'e nĩ Klĩsto. O na mayĩsĩ maũndũ ala Ũsumbĩ ũsu ũkilyĩ kwĩka ĩvindanĩ yĩla mbaĩ syonthe ikethĩwa iisilĩlwa. (Isa. 9:6, 7; 56:10; Nda. 2:44) Ĩndĩ ithyĩ twekala twĩ metho na tũsyaĩĩsye, ĩla mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo ũkavika ũkatwĩthĩa twĩyũmbanĩtye.—Sav. 130:6.
ĨSŨVĨE NDŨKAAĨSE KWELELŨKW'A ŨEKE KŨSYAĨĨSYA
10, 11. (a) Twaĩle kwĩsũvĩa tũikeke ata, na nĩkĩ? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩkũĩkĩĩthasya kana Ndevili nũtumĩte andũ mavũthĩĩsya wathani wa Mbivilia?
10 Kwavindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa mũsungi wĩkalile asalukĩtye ũtukũ mũima. Atielye o kavinda kanini amine saa syake sya wĩa nĩw'o ũtonya kwĩw'a anoete na ũyĩthĩa nĩ laisi kũkoma. Ũndũ ũmwe na ũu, o ũndũ tũthengeee mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno, now'o ve vinya kwĩkala tũsyaĩĩsye. Wĩthĩwa wĩ ũthũku ta kĩ tũkaemwa nĩ kũsyaĩĩsya! Ekai twone maũndũ atatũ ala twaema kwĩsũvĩa matonya kũtuma tũemwa nĩ kũsyaĩĩsya na kwĩkala twĩ metho.
11 Ndevili aendeee kũkenga andũ maleele kĩ-veva. Kavinda kakuvĩ Yesũ atanamba kũkw'a, nĩwakanisye amanyĩw'a make mavinda atatũ ĩũlũ wa ũla "mũnene wa nthĩ ĩno." (Yoa. 12:31; 14:30; 16:11) Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana Ndevili akaasya mosũanĩo ma andũ nĩ kana maikose kwa ũito mawathani ma Ngai ala monanĩtye nesa kana ĩvinda yĩla yĩtiele nĩ ĩkuvĩ mũno. (Nzev. 1:14) Satani atũmĩaa ndĩni sya ũvũngũ kwasya mosũanĩo ma andũ. We ĩla ũkũea ngewa na andũ angĩ wĩw'aa maiea ngewa iilyĩ ata? We tyo wonete kana Ndevili 'nĩwaĩtye mosũanĩo ma ala matetĩkĩlaa' makaeka kũĩkĩĩa kana mũthya wa nthĩ ĩno nĩwũkĩte, na kana Klĩsto nĩwe yu ũsumbĩkĩte Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ngai? (2 Ako. 4:3-6) Nĩ keana we wĩw'ĩte mũndũ aikwĩa, "Ndikwenda kũtavw'a ũvoo"? Kaingĩ ĩla twatata kũmatavya vala nthĩ ĩno ĩelete mayĩthĩawa makwetye ũu witũ.
12. Nĩkĩ no nginya twĩsũvĩe Ndevili ndakatũkenge?
12 O na kau angĩ mayendeeaw'a nĩ kĩla tũũmatavya, ndũkaeke kĩu kĩũtũle ngoo kana kĩũtulye ũeke kwĩkala ũsyaĩĩsye. We nĩwĩsĩ nesa kĩla tweteele. Vaulo eeie Aklĩsto ala angĩ atĩĩ: "Inyw'ĩ ene nĩmwĩsĩ vyũ kana mũthenya wa Mwĩaĩi [nĩwũkĩte]." Na ĩndĩ ongela kũmea: "O ũndũ kĩng'ei kyũkaa ũtukũ." (Soma 1 Athesalonika 5:1-6.) Yesũ atũnengie ũtao ũũ: "Ĩkalai mwĩyũmbanĩtye: nĩkwĩthĩwa Mwana wa mũndũ akooka saa ũla mũtataĩĩe." (Luka 12:39, 40) O mĩtũkĩ Satani akilyĩ anakenga andũ mambĩĩe kwona "kwĩ mũuo na vai mũisyo." Akamasya mambĩĩe kwona maũndũ maendeee nesa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Nata naitũ? Twekala "tũsyaĩĩsye na kwĩthĩwa na wĩting'o," ti lasima mũthenya wa ũsilĩlo 'wĩtũvikĩa ta kĩng'ei.' Nũndũ wa ũu no nginya kĩla mũthenya tũsomae Ndeto ya Ngai na tũivindĩĩsya kĩla we ũkũtũtavya.
13. Veva wa nthĩ ũtumĩte andũ methĩwa mailyĩ ata, na nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũikalikwe nĩw'o?
13 Veva wa nthĩ ĩno ũendeee kũtuma andũ makoma kĩ-veva. Andũ amwe methĩawa makwatanĩtw'e mũno nĩ tũmaũndũ twoo twa kĩla mũthenya nginya ũkethĩa maikwona "me na ũkya wa kĩ-veva." (Mat. 5:3, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Melikĩtye vyũ maũndũnĩ ma nthĩ ala matumaa mũndũ ethĩwa na "wendi wa mwĩĩ na wendi wa metho." (1 Yoa. 2:16) O na ĩngĩ maũndũ ma kwĩtanĩthya ala me kw'o matumĩte andũ matw'ĩka "endi ma motanu," na kĩla mwaka maũndũ asu maendeeaa kwongeleka. (2 Tim. 3:4) Kwondũ wa kĩtumi kyu Vaulo eeie Aklĩsto kana mayaĩle kwĩsa "kũlilikana kwĩka mawendi" ma mwĩĩ nũndũ nĩmo matumaa mũndũ akoma kĩ-veva.—Alo. 13:11-14.
14. Nĩ ũkany'o wĩva wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Luka 21:34, 35?
14 Vandũ va kwĩtĩkĩla tũtongoew'e nĩ veva wa nthĩ, twĩtĩkĩlaa kũtongoew'a nĩ veva wa Yeova, ũla nĩw'o we mwene ũtũnengete ũtũtetheesye tũelewe nesa maũndũ ala tweteele kwona. [1] (1 Ako. 2:12) Ĩndĩ nĩtwĩsĩ kana ti maũndũ ala manene matumaa mũndũ akoma kĩ-veva. Tũmaũndũ tũla twĩkaa kĩla mũthenya notw'o tũtonya kũtuma tũkoma twatwĩtĩkĩlya tũlikĩlĩĩle ũthũkũmi witũ. (Soma Luka 21:34, 35.) Angĩ no matũthekeee moona tũyĩkala tũsyaĩĩsye, ĩndĩ kyu ti kĩtumi kya kũtuma tũeka kũsyaĩĩsya. (2 Vet. 3:3-7) Vandũ va ũu twaĩle kũendaa maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi tũteũtĩĩa nĩ kana twĩthĩawe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Vau nĩvo vethĩawa veva wa Ngai.
15. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva wakwatie Vetelo, Yakovo, na Yoana, na nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva ũndũ ũsu ũtonya kũtũkwata?
15 Nũndũ twĩ ene naĩ, ũu nĩũtuma tũemwa nĩ kũsyaĩĩsya. Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana andũ me mũtuo wa kwenda kwĩka ũndũ mwĩĩ ũkwenda. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa kĩla kyeekĩkie ũtukũ wa mũthya Yesũ atanamba kũawa. Nĩ kana ekale e mũĩkĩĩku, nĩwatwie kũmũvoya Asa wake amũnenge vinya. Na kwoou nĩwakũlilye Vetelo, Yakovo, na Yoana maendeee "kũsyaĩĩsya" ĩla we mwene ũkũvoya. Ĩndĩ asu me atatũ mayakwatasya ũito wa ũndũ ũla wakilyĩ kwĩkĩka. Vandũ va kũsyaĩĩsya kwondũ wa Vwana woo, meekie ũndũ mĩĩ yoo yendaa na makoma. Ĩndĩ kĩvathũkany'o namo, Yesũ aendeeie kũsyaĩĩsya na kũvoya Asa wake na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo, o na kũtw'ĩka o nake aĩ na mĩnoo. Anyanyae make atatũ maaĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa meekie oou.—Mko. 14:32-41.
16. Kwosana na ĩandĩko ya Luka 21:36, nĩ ũndũ wĩva Yesũ waisye twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kana tũendeee "kũsyaĩĩsya"?
16 Nĩ kana tũendeee "kũsyaĩĩsya," no nginya twĩthĩwe na kĩeleelo kĩseo. Ĩndĩ ti ũu w'oka. Mĩthenya mĩvũthũ mbee wa ũndũ ũsu weekĩkie mũũndanĩ wa Ngesemanii, Yesũ eeie ala amanyĩw'a atatũ nĩmamwĩkaĩle Yeova mboyanĩ. (Soma Luka 21:36.) Kwoou o naitũ twenda twĩkale tũsyaĩĩsye, no nginya tũendeee kũsyaĩĩsya kũvoyanĩ.—1 Vet. 4:7.
ENDEEAI KŨSYAĨĨSYA
17. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kenda twĩkale twĩsĩ kana nĩtwĩyũmbanĩsye maũndũ ala mokĩte?
17 Nĩkwĩthĩwa Yesũ aisye kana mũthya ũkooka 'saa ũla tũtataĩĩe,' yĩĩ tiyo ĩvinda ya kwombosya kĩ-veva, na tiyo ĩvinda ya kwĩka ũndũ mĩĩ yitũ ĩkwenda kana kũatĩanĩa na syĩndũ ila Satani na nthĩ yake maseũvĩtye, nĩkwĩthĩwa isu no ndoto. (Mt. 24:44) Ngai na Klĩsto nĩmatũtavĩtye Mbivilianĩ moathimo ala matũvangĩĩe tũkwate o mĩtũkĩ, vamwe na ũndũ tũtonya kwĩkala tũsyaĩĩsye. Kwoou no nginya tũtate tũendeee kwĩkala twĩ alũmu kĩ-veva, tũsũvĩe ngwatanĩo yitũ na Yeova, na twĩke maũndũ ma Ũsumbĩ mbee. Na no nginya tũendeee kwĩkala twĩ metho tũmanye ĩvinda yĩla tũĩ nĩ ĩvinda yĩkũ na nĩ maũndũ meva maendeee, nĩ kana kĩla kyũkĩte kĩikatũkitye tũteyũmbanĩtye. (Ũvu. 22:20) Kwĩka ũu no kũtangĩĩe mathayũ maitũ!

translation:
"Be vigilant at all times, because you do not know on what day your Lord will come." – MT. 24:42.
MBATHI: 136, 54
1. Why is it important for us to be watchful, and what does this involve? (Discuss practical ways.)
CONSIDER the importance of spiritual alertness. The Master encourages each one of us to pay attention to the time when his coming draws near. But how can we show that we are alert and ready? It is by being zealous in our ministry, just like the faithful slave and his companions, and by constantly strengthening ourselves spiritually through study and prayer. Also, I have noticed some brothers getting discouraged because of difficulties they encounter while preaching, or because the work seems slow. Are such feelings normal? Yes, they are, but we should not allow them to paralyze us. For example, perhaps some of us feel tired after serving as the master, someone tells us, and people seem uninterested. However, let us remember that the vital issue is whether we are doing our best, and that Jehovah appreciates our efforts. This important matter involves what?
2. What did Jesus mean when he said, "Keep on the watch?"
2 Jesus Christ used the expression "watchfulness" to emphasize this very point, saying: "Keep on the watch, keep praying, and keep yourselves prepared, because you do not know when my Lord will come." He repeatedly stressed this idea, Jesus, emphasizing: "Keep on the watch." (Matt. 24:3; see also Mark 13:32-37.) And so the account in Matthew chapter 24 shows that Jesus was warning his followers about the need to be watchful, saying: 'Keep on the watch, because you do not know the day my God appoints. Be ready, because you do not know the hour the Son of Man will come.' He further emphasized: 'Keep on the watch, because you do not know the exact time.'—Matt. 24:42-44; 25:13.
3. How can we imitate Jesus' exhortation?
3 We should imitate Jehovah's servants in being watchful. We realize that we are living in "the time of the end," and that events are unfolding in such a way that they fulfill the prophecy of "great tribulation"! (Dan. 12:4; Matt. 24:21) In all lands people are experiencing anxieties, wars, famines, earthquakes, floods, and other disasters. And we realize that Jehovah's people continue to bear witness to the Kingdom despite increasing opposition. (Matt. 24:7, 11, 12, 14; Luke 21:11) Also, we are moved to show our faith by remaining steadfast in our loyalty to God and by making known His purpose.—Mark 13:26, 27.
BE EVER SO WATCHFUL!
4. (a) What did Jesus mean when he spoke of the faithful slave? (b) But what should we do personally regarding this important feature, and why?
4 We realize that each major event will be distinctive. So we should try to discern the meaning of the features of "the time of the end" as they develop. However, along with the features and the time, we should also try to discern the year. But Jesus himself said: "Concerning that day and hour nobody knows, neither the angels of heaven nor the Son, but only the Father." (Matt. 24:36) Therefore, let us trust Christ to reveal the proper time to take action against this wicked system of Satan. (Rev. 19:11-16) That is why Jesus meant the faithful slave to be aware of the signs. Let us therefore always strive to become more zealous in proclaiming the good news. May the time come when Jehovah deems it right to intervene. It will be a welcome relief. Let us continue to watch for the fulfillment of the prophecies concerning "great tribulation," and also "keep on the watch."—(Read Habakkuk 2:1-3.) What can help us to do so?
5. Consider how the illustration of the heart shows that Jehovah values individuals who cherish their relationship with him.
5 How Jehovah values individuals who cherish their relationship with him! To illustrate this, think of how Jehovah dealt with Israel during the Exodus from Egypt. At a specific time, he told Moses to celebrate the Passover on the evening of Nisan 14, 1513 B.C.E. He said: "This day should serve you as a memorial throughout your generations. You must observe it as a festival to Jehovah, throughout your generations." (Ex. 12:40-42) Those "generations" amounted to 1,943 years, pointing forward to 1913 C.E., when the modern witness work began. (Gen. 3:17, 18) In connection with those "generations," Jehovah made this promise to Abraham: "Know for certain that your offspring will reside as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and they will be enslaved and afflicted for 400 years." (Gen. 15:13; Acts 7:6) Those "400 years" came to their fulfillment in 1913 C.E., which marked the time Isaac and Ishmael were about to reach adulthood, and it also pointed to the time the Israelites would leave Egypt in 1513 B.C.E. (Gen. 21:8-10; Acts 4:22-29) Jehovah has shown his faithfulness regarding the timeline he gave to his people, and those 400 years have proven to be significant!
6. Does it bother us that Jehovah allows his people to experience trials?
6 Joshua was one of the leaders who led the Israelites out of Egypt, and he exhorted them: "Keep yourselves zealous and very devoted to carrying out all the words of the law that Moses my God commanded you; do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left. . . ." (Josh. 23:2, 14) So we can be sure that Jehovah's purpose in allowing trials is for our good, and that his love for us is great. If we want to remain close to Jehovah, we must continue to prove ourselves loyal.
DO NOT GIVE UP ON LOYALTY
7, 8. (a) What motivated some in ancient times, and what does this teach us? (b) Why might some faithful ones become discouraged, and how can we encourage them? Consider an example.
7 Remaining steadfast during trials teaches us much about loyalty. In ancient times, Jerusalem was often under attack, and its inhabitants had to defend it courageously. Today too, many Christians face opposition and persecution. They may feel overwhelmed at times, yet they continue to preach the good news despite the difficulties. Whether it is late at night or early in the morning, faithful ones often go from house to house with their publications. Those who support them provide practical help and encouragement. (Isa. 62:6) Loyal ones are happy to be supported by fellow believers, and such support can help them reach more people.—Ezek. 33:6.
8 A historian named Josephus, who lived in the first century C.E., wrote that in 70 C.E. Roman soldiers led by Titus invaded Jerusalem and surrounded the city. He said that the Romans were relentless in their efforts to conquer the city, and they used various tactics. This account helps us understand why Jerusalem experienced so much suffering and destruction.
9. Why do many people find it difficult to remain loyal?
9 Many people find it difficult to remain loyal because they are tempted by selfish desires, or they are influenced by false teachings. Those who are disloyal often rationalize their actions, telling themselves that what they are doing is not really wrong, and they try to justify their choices. They may also be motivated by fear or by a desire for personal gain. But such excuses do not eliminate the consequences of disloyalty. Disloyal acts can damage relationships and trust. And disloyalty to God can lead to spiritual ruin. (Isa. 9:6, 7; 56:10; Dan. 2:44) So let us examine ourselves carefully and pray earnestly, that we may avoid being misled.—Ps. 130:6.
LET US EXAMINE OURSELVES TO SEE IF WE ARE LOYAL
10, 11. (a) How can we show our loyalty, and why? (b) What motivates Satan to tempt people to become disloyal to Jehovah?
10 Consider the example of a faithful watchman who diligently guards his city during the night. He remains alert despite the darkness and the discomfort, knowing that lives depend on his vigilance. Similarly, we need to stay awake spiritually, so that we do not succumb to temptation. We want to continue showing our loyalty! Let us see some ways in which we can strengthen our resolve to remain loyal and upright.
11 The Devil continues to deceive people subtly. Jesus' example shows us how to respond—by rejecting false accusations and remaining firm in the truth, even when facing opposition. (John 12:31; 14:30; 16:11) Jesus knew that the Devil would try to mislead people, just as he did with Adam and Eve, making them question God's standards. (Genesis 1:14) Satan uses deceptive arguments to mislead people. So, will you be cautious about associating with those who promote worldly thinking? Will you recognize that the Devil 'misrepresents the words of God,' twisting the truth to suit his purposes, and that Christ is the one who perfectly embodies God's wisdom? (2 Corinthians 4:3-6) Before someone asks you, "Where are you going?" think carefully about whether this course will lead you astray.
12 How, then, can we remain steadfast in our faith?
12 And many Christians find that regular personal study helps them stay alert, so they can discern what is true and reject what is false. It is vital that we stay vigilant. Paul wrote to fellow Christians: "The night has come where you should awaken." He urged them to "put on the armor of righteousness." (Read 1 Thessalonians 5:1-6.) Jesus warned us: "Keep yourselves ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour that you do not expect." (Luke 12:39, 40) Often, Satan deceives people by appealing to their desire for "pleasure and self-indulgence." He leads them to believe that certain things are harmless, even though they contradict Bible principles. Why is that? Because we tend to become "complacent and distracted," failing to appreciate the urgency of our time. Therefore, let us regularly read God's Word and meditate on its meaning, always being prepared to defend our faith.
13 What subtle methods does the Devil use to influence people, and how can we avoid being misled?
13 The Devil continues to use deceptive methods to mislead people. Some Christians have been influenced by worldly thinking, which causes them to view certain practices as acceptable—even desirable. (Matt. 5:3, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) They are attracted to "the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes." (1 John 2:16) Also, many things that are presented as harmless entertainment actually lead people to embrace "false teachings," and each year such harmful influences increase. (2 Tim. 3:4) This is why Paul warned against "an intense desire for selfish interests"—because this can cause someone to be deceived.—Acts 13:11-14.
14 Why is it important to heed the warning found at Luke 21:34, 35?
14 We want to remain faithful during the time of great tribulation, so we need to remain faithful to Jehovah, who gives us the power to understand what is happening and to cope with difficult circumstances. [1] (1 Pet. 2:12) It is vital that we recognize how serious the matters are that can lead someone to be deceived. Let us regularly examine ourselves to see if we are remaining spiritually strong. (Read Luke 21:34, 35.) If we become complacent, we may find it hard to stay awake spiritually. (2 Peter 3:3-7) Those who take part in the Christian ministry should zealously preach and teach, whether others accept their message or not. These are the ones whom God approves.
15 What lesson did Peter, James, and John learn, and how does this affect us today?
15 They were deeply moved, and this helped them to appreciate the importance of staying awake spiritually. Jesus knew that his disciples would face trials, and he prepared them for this. For example, on the night of his death, he warned them about what was going to happen. He also told them to watch out for distractions that could weaken their faith. And just like Peter, James, and John benefited from being willing to stay awake spiritually, we too will benefit if we remain alert. But some may find it hard to concentrate when they are tired. Those who are determined to remain loyal to God's Son will make an effort to stay awake and keep serving him faithfully. If we do so, Jesus will continue to help us to stay awake and to strengthen our faith, and he will give us the support we need.—Mark 14:32-41.
16 According to Luke 21:36, what did Jesus urge his followers to do in order to 'stay awake'?
16 To 'stay awake,' we must pray earnestly for strength. It is not enough simply to want to. On the evening of Nisan 14, while in the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus repeatedly prayed to Jehovah for help. (Read Luke 21:36.) So let us always be diligent in praying to stay awake, and let us continue to pray for strength.—1 Pet. 4:7.
KEEP STAYING AWAKE
17 What can we do to ensure that we remain spiritually awake and do not become distracted?
17 Jesus warned his disciples that they might not recognize the sign saying "the beginning of pangues," because of their being troubled by everyday affairs and because of Satan's influence. (Matt. 24:44) God and Christ assure us that they will protect their loyal servants from falling into spiritual darkness, helping some to recover if they do drift away. So let us continue to strive to remain fully occupied with the ministry, strengthening our relationship with Jehovah, and applying Bible principles in our lives. And let us continue to be quick to discern what is important and what is urgent, so that nothing unexpected takes us by surprise. (Rev. 22:20) Let this urge us on!

text:
"Vala ve ũthwii wenyu, nĩvo vethĩawa ngoo syenyu nasyo."—LUKA 12:34.
MBATHI: 153, 9
1, 2. (a) Nĩ maũndũ meva atatũ Yeova ũtũnengete ta ũthwii wa kĩ-veva? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
YEOVA nĩwe mũthwii ũla mũnene vyũ kwĩ onthe. (1 Mav. 29:11, 12) Na nũndũ nĩ Asa mũlau, nũolelaa ũthwii wake onthe ala mesĩ vata waw'o. Tũtũngaa mũvea ta kĩ nũndũ Yeova nũtũnengete ũthwii wa kĩ-veva! Ũthwii ũsu nĩ ta (1) Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, (2) ũthũkũmi witũ, na (3) ũw'o wa vata ũla twĩmanyĩĩtye Ndetonĩ yake. Thĩna nĩ kana tũkaema kwĩsũvĩa, nĩkwĩsa kwĩthĩa twaekie kwona vata wa ũthwii ũsu, na tũyĩsa kũwĩkya ĩtheka. Kwoou nĩ kana tũlũmye ũthwii ũsu, nĩtwaĩle kwĩkalaa tũyĩlilikany'a nĩkĩ nĩ wa vata, na tũyĩĩkĩĩthya kĩla ĩvinda kana nĩtũwendete. Yesũ aisye: "Vala ve ũthwii wenyu, nĩvo vethĩawa ngoo syenyu nasyo."—Luka 12:34.
2 Ekai tũneenee ũndũ tũtonya kũendeea kwenda Ũsumbĩ, ũthũkũmi witũ, na ũw'o, na ĩndĩ tũyona ũndũ tũtonya kwonany'a kana nĩtwonaa syĩ sya vata. Ĩla tũkwĩthĩwa tũyĩka ũu, vindĩĩsya ũndũ we mwene ũtonya kwenda mũno ũthwii ũsu wa kĩ-veva.
ŨSUMBĨ WA NGAI NO TA LŨLŨ WA THOOA MŨNENE
3. Ũla mũtandĩthya ũwetetwe ngelekany'onĩ ya Yesũ eeyũmbanĩtye kwĩka ata akwate ũla lũlũ wa thooa mũnene? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 9.)
3 Soma Mathayo 13:45, 46. Yesũ nĩwanenganie ngelekany'o ya mũtandĩthya wamanthaa malũlũ. Mũtandĩthya ũsu ndaema kwĩthĩwa akũnĩte viasala ya kũthooa na kũthoosya malũlũ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka kauta. Ĩndĩ mũthenya ũmwe nĩwesie kwona lũlũ ũmwe wa thooa mũnene kũte malũlũ onthe ala waakwata. Ngoo yake yatanie mũno. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana athooe lũlũ ũsu, yaĩ lasima athoosye kyonthe kĩla waĩ nakyo. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ we woonaa lũlũ ũsu wĩ wa vata!
4. Tũkeekaa ata ethĩwa nĩtwendete Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai mũno o tondũ ũla mũtandĩthya wendete ũla lũlũ?
4 Ngelekany'o ĩsu yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ ta lũlũ ũsu wa thooa mũnene. Ethĩwa nĩtũwendete o tondũ mũtandĩthya wendete ũla lũlũ, tũkeethĩawa twĩyũmbanĩtye kũtia kĩla kĩndũ nĩ kana twĩtĩkĩle kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Ũsumbĩ ũsu na tũyĩkalaa ungu waw'o mavinda onthe. (Soma Maliko 10:28-30.) Kwaeka twone andũ elĩ meekie ũu.
5. Sakayo oonanisye ata kana nĩweeyumĩtye vyũ akwate Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai?
5 Sakayo aĩ mũnene wa aumya ma koti na athuĩtw'e nĩ kũvenana mbesa na nzĩa ya ũkengani. (Luka 19:1-9) O na kũtw'ĩka ndaĩ mũndũ mũlũngalu, ĩla weewie Yesũ aitavany'a ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ oonie ũsu ne w'o ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ na oosa ĩtambya vau kwa vau. Aisye: "Sisya, Mwĩaĩi, nyunzu ya syĩndũ syakwa nĩngũnenga ngya; na ethĩwa nĩnĩvenete mũndũ kĩndũ na nzĩa ya ũkengani, nĩngũmũtũngĩa kũndũ kũna." Akolile malĩ ĩsu wakwatĩte na nzĩa ya ũvenani e mũthalĩku ngoonĩ na aekana na ĩtomo ya syĩndũ.
6. Nĩ moalyũku meva Rose weekie nĩ kana etĩkĩle kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, na eekie ũu nĩkĩ?
6 Mũndũ mũka ũmwe tũũmũtw'ĩĩa ĩsyĩtwa Rose nĩwavikĩiwe nĩ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ myaka yĩ navu ĩtina. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu atumĩte ndũũ na mũndũ mũka ũngĩ ũndũ mũndũũme ũtumaa ndũũ na mũndũ mũka. O na aĩ ndongoi ya kyama kĩmwe kĩteteaa mĩtwaano na ndũũ sya aũme kwa aũme na aka kwa aka. Ĩndĩ ĩla Rose weemanyĩisye Mbivilia, nĩwamanyie kana ũw'o ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai nĩ wa vata kwĩ ũndũ ũngĩ o na wĩva. O na vailyĩ ũu, nĩwamanyie kana nĩwaaĩle kwĩka moalyũku manene. (1 Ako. 6:9, 10) Nũndũ wa kũmwenda Yeova, nĩwaumie kyamanĩ kĩu na ataanĩsya na mũndũ mũka ũsu maĩ ndũũ. Rose avatisiwe mwaka wa 2009, na mwaka ũla waatĩĩe nĩwatw'ĩkie vainia wa kĩla ĩvinda. Nĩwamwendie Yeova na enda Ũsumbĩ wake kwĩ mĩmeo o na yĩva ya mwĩĩ.—Mko. 12:29, 30.
7. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũikaaĩse kũeka kwenda Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai na ngoo yonthe?
7 Aingĩ maitũ nĩtwĩkĩte moalyũku manene nĩ kana twĩthĩwe tũtonya kũsumbĩkwa nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. (Alo. 12:2) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, ĩvinda ya kũthyũmũa ti ĩviku. No nginya twĩkalae twĩsũvĩĩte tũikese kwelelũkw'a nĩ maũndũ ta wendi wa malĩ na mĩmeo mĩthũku ya ũlaalai, nũndũ asu nĩ maũndũ mekalaa maitũvĩngĩĩsa tũeke kwenda Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. (Nth. 4:23; Mt. 5:27-29) Yeova nũtũnengete ũthwii ũngĩ wa vata mũno nĩ kana atũtetheesye tũendeee kwenda Ũsumbĩ wake na ngoo yonthe.
ŨTHŨKŨMI WITŨ NŨTANGĨĨAA MATHAYŨ
8. (a) Nĩkĩ mũtũmwa Vaulo waisye kana ũthũkũmi witũ nĩ ta 'ũthwii mĩionĩ ya mũthanga'? (b) Vaulo oonanisye ata kana nĩwoonaa ũthũkũmi wake wĩ wa vata?
8 Lilikana kana Yesũ nĩwatũnengie wĩa wa kũtavany'a na kũmanyĩsya angĩ ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. (Mt. 28:19, 20) Mũtũmwa Vaulo nĩweesĩ nesa kana ũthũkũmi ũsu nĩ wa vata mũno. Aisye kana ũthũkũmi wa ũtianĩo mweũ nĩ ta 'ũthwii mĩionĩ ya mũthanga.' (2 Ako. 4:7; 1 Tim. 1:12) O na kau tũilyĩ ta mĩio ya mũthanga nĩkwĩthĩwa twĩ ene naĩ, ũvoo ũla tũtavanasya no ũtume ithyĩ na ala matwĩthukĩĩasya tũka kũkwata thayũ ũtathela. Vaulo nĩweesĩ kĩu nesa, na kwoou nĩwatatie kũtũmĩa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ũtavany'anĩ wake. Aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩkaa maũndũ aa onthe kwondũ wa ũla ũvoo mũseo, nĩ kana nĩthĩwe nĩ mwosi ũmwe waw'o vamwe na angĩ." (1 Ako. 9:23) Vate nzika, Vaulo nĩweekĩie kĩthito kingĩ atw'ĩkĩthye andũ amanyĩw'a nũndũ nĩwendete ũthũkũmi ũsu. (Soma Alomi 1:14, 15; 2 Timotheo 4:2.) Kĩu nĩkyamũtetheeisye omĩĩsya kũnyamaw'a. (1 Ath. 2:2) Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtwendete ũthũkũmi witũ o ta Vaulo?
9. Nĩ maũndũ meva tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a nĩtwonaa ũthũkũmi witũ wĩ wa vata?
9 Ũndũ ũmwe Vaulo weekaa akonany'a nũkwona ũthũkũmi wĩ wa vata nĩ kũtũmĩa nesa mwanya ũla wakwata aneene na angĩ. O naitũ twĩkaa o ta atũmwa na ala Aklĩsto ma mbee kwa kũtavany'a ĩla twĩ maũndũnĩ maitũ, kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ, na nyũmba na nyũmba. (Meko 5:42; 20:20) Ethĩwa maũndũ maitũ nĩmeũtwĩtĩkĩlya, nĩtwongelangaa ũthũkũmi witũ, twasye kwa kũtw'ĩka mavainia atetheesya kana mavainia ma kĩla ĩvinda. Ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩngĩ, kũthamĩĩa kĩsionĩ kĩngĩ kĩ nthĩ yitũ, kana o kũthamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ.—Meko 16:9, 10.
10. Irene aathimiwe ata nũndũ wa kĩthito kyake kya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo?
10 Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũte mũtwae wĩkalaa Amelika wĩtawa Irene. Aĩ na wendi mwingĩ mũno wa kũtavya andũ maneenaa kĩthyomo kya Russian ala mathamĩĩe nthĩ yoo. Ayambĩĩa kwĩka ũu mwakanĩ wa 1993 kakundi ka kĩthyomo kya Russian, kala kaĩ New York City, kaĩ na atavany'a o ta 20. Irene athũkũmĩte na kĩthito kingĩ aimantha andũ ma kĩthyomo kĩu kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ta 20. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Kũvika o na yu ndineenaa kĩthyomo kya Russian nesa vyũ." Ĩndĩ Yeova nũathimĩte kĩthito kyake na kya ala angĩ mailyĩ take. Ũmũnthĩ ũũ New York City ve ikundi thanthatũ sya kĩthyomo kya Russian. Andũ 15 katĩ wa ala Irene wĩmanyĩĩtye namo nĩmavatisĩtwe. Amwe nĩ athũkũmi ma Mbetheli, mavainia, na atumĩa. Irene aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nasũanĩa maũndũ ala angĩ naĩ nĩka, vai ũmwe nonaa waĩ wĩsa kũtuma nĩthĩwa na ũtanu wingĩvĩte ũu." Ĩĩ nĩ w'o vyũ, Irene nĩwonaa ũthũkũmi wake wĩ wa vata!
11. Kũtavany'a tũte kũeka o na ĩla tũũthĩnw'a kũetae moseo meva?
11 Ethĩwa nĩtwonaa ũthũkũmi witũ wĩ wa vata, tũikaeka kũtavany'a o na twanyamaw'a. Ũu now'o Vaulo weekie. (Meko 14:19-22) Myakanĩ ya 1930 na mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1940, ana-a-asa maitũ nthĩ ya Amelika nĩmathĩniw'e mũno. Ĩndĩ o na mathĩnĩtw'e oou, meekie ta Vaulo nũndũ maũngamie na ũlũmu na maendeea kũtavany'a. Ana-a-asa asu nĩmasilile makoani maingĩ mũno kotinĩ nĩ kana matetee wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a. Mwakanĩ wa 1943, Mwana-a-asa Nathan H. Knorr nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa ĩkoani yĩmwe masilĩle Kotinĩ Ũla Mũnene Vyũ wa Amelika na masinda. Aisye: "Tũsindaa makoani aa nũndũ wa kĩthito kyenyu. Keka we mũtavany'a ndwaaendeea kwĩkĩa kĩthito ũtavany'anĩ, vai makoani methĩwa maisilĩlwa Kotinĩ Ũla Mũnene Vyũ; ĩndĩ nũndũ inyw'ĩ atavany'a, inyw'ĩ ana-a-asa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe, mwĩ na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo kingĩ na mũyĩtĩkĩla kũnoa, nĩtũvotete kũsinda ala meũtũnyamasya. Kĩthito kĩla andũ ma Mwĩaĩi mekĩaa maũngame na ũlũmu nĩkyo kĩsaa kũtuma ũtwi ta ũsu wĩkwa." Nũndũ ana-a-asa nthĩ ingĩ nĩmaũngamĩte na ũlũmu o tondũ asu maũngamie, nĩmasindĩte makoani maingĩ. Vate nzika, twenda ũthũkũmi witũ, tũikaaeka kũthĩnw'a kũtũvate kũtavany'a.
12. We ũtw'ĩte kwĩka ata ũthũkũminĩ waku?
12 Ethĩwa twonaa ũtavany'a witũ ta ũthwii wa vata mũno kuma kũla kwĩ Yeova, tũikeanĩawa tũ nĩ kũtavany'a aĩ no kana tusũsye masaa. Vandũ va ũu, tũkeekaa kyonthe kĩla tũtonya nĩ kana tũendeee "kũkũsĩĩa [vyũ] ũla ũvoo mũseo." (Meko 20:24; 2 Tim. 4:5) Ĩndĩ twaĩle kũmanyĩsya ala angĩ kyaũ? Ekai tũsũanĩe ũthwii ũngĩ tũnengetwe nĩ Ngai.
ŨW'O WA VATA ŨLA TWĨMANYĨĨTYE
13, 14. 'Kyũmbanĩsyo' kĩla Yesũ wawetie nthĩnĩ wa Mathayo 13:52 nĩ kya kyaũ, na tũkyusũĩĩasya ata?
13 Ũw'o wa vata ũla twĩmanyĩĩtye nĩ ũthwii ũngĩ wa katatũ tũnengetwe nĩ Ngai. Yeova nĩwe Ngai wa w'o. (2 Sam. 7:28; Sav. 31:5) Na nũndũ nĩ Asa mũlau, nũmanyĩasya ala mamũkĩaa ũla ũw'o. Kuma ĩla twamanyie ũw'o, nĩtwĩthĩĩtwe tũyũmbany'a maũndũ ala tweemanyĩsya Ndetonĩ yake, Mbivilia, mavukunĩ maitũ, maũmbanonĩ manene, na maũmbanonĩ ala twĩkaa kĩla kyumwa. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu kũvika yu, nĩtwĩseũvĩsye kĩla Yesũ weetie 'kyũmbanĩsyo' kya momanyĩsyo ma tene na meũ. (Soma Mathayo 13:52.) Yeova akatũtetheesya twongeleele momanyĩsyo angĩ meũ na ma vata "kyũmbanĩsyonĩ" kitũ ethĩwa tũkaendeea kũmantha ũw'o ũsu o ũndũ tũtonya kũmantha ũthwii mũvithe. (Soma Nthimo 2:4-7.) Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata?
14 No nginya twĩthĩwe na kĩmanyĩo kya kwĩmanyĩsya nesa na tũyĩka ũkunĩkĩli nesa Ndetonĩ ya Ngai na mavukunĩ maitũ. Kwĩka ũu kũkatũtetheesya tũmanye ũw'o 'mweũ,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, tũmanye momanyĩsyo amwe nesanga kũte ũndũ tũnatwĩe tũmesĩ. (Yos. 1:8, 9; Sav. 1:2, 3) Kyava ya mbee vyũ ya ĩkaseti yĩĩ ĩla yatumbĩthiw'e Mwei wa 7, 1879, yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Ũw'o thayũnĩ witũ nĩ ta kalaa kanini kanake kathyũlũlũkĩtwe kakew'a kũvw'ĩkwa vyũ nĩ ĩia yĩ na vinya, yĩla no ũndũ ũmwe na ũvũngũ ũla ũendeee kwongeleka. Kwoou nĩ kana ũũkwate no nginya ũũmanthe mũno. . . . Na nĩ kana ũũlũmye, no nginya wĩkĩe kĩthito ũũmanthe. Ndũkeanĩwe no kaũw'o kamwe kala weemanyĩsya. . . . Endeea kũmantha, na endeea kũmbany'a tũlaa twingangĩ." No nginya tũendeee kwongeleela kyũmbanĩsyonĩ kitũ ũthwii wa momanyĩsyo ma w'o.
15. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ũw'o ũmwe nĩ 'mũkũũ,' na nĩ ũw'o wĩva we mwene ũtanĩaa kwĩthĩwa wĩsĩ?
15 Nĩtwamanyie ũw'o wa vata mũno ĩla twambĩĩe kũlikana na andũ ma Ngai. No twasye ũw'o ũsu twamanyie ĩvinda yĩu nĩ 'mũkũũ,' nĩkwĩthĩwa twaũmanyie na twawenda ĩla twambĩĩe kyalo kĩĩ kya Ũklĩsto. Ũw'o ũsu twamanyie ĩvinda yĩu nĩ ta wĩva? Nĩtwamanyie kana Yeova nĩwe Mũmbi witũ na nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ, na twamanya kana e na kĩeleelo kwondũ wa andũ. O na nĩtwamanyie kana Ngai nĩwatwendie na atũnenga nthembo ya wovosyo ya Mwana wake nĩ kana tũtangĩĩwe kuma naĩnĩ na kĩkw'ũnĩ. Ũw'o ũngĩ twamanyie nĩ kana Ũsumbĩ wake ũkamina thĩna w'onthe, na kana twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene kwĩ mũuo na ũtanu tũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ ũsu.—Yoa. 3:16; Ũvu. 4:11; 21:3, 4.
16. Twaĩle kwĩka ata ĩla twaelew'a ũw'o mũna nesanga?
16 Mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtũtonya kũelew'a wathani mũna wa Mbivilia nesanga kana kĩlungu kĩna kya Maandĩko nesanga kwĩ ũndũ tũneesĩ. Ĩla twesa kũelew'a maũndũ nesanga, nĩtwaĩle kũmantha ĩvinda twĩmanyĩsye ũvoo ũsu nesa na tũiũvindĩĩsya. (Meko 17:11; 1 Tim. 4:15) Tũyaĩle o kũtata kũelewa ũmanyĩsyo ũla mũnene wĩkiwe ũalyũku wĩ w'oka, ĩndĩ nũseo tũkakwatya o na tũvathũkany'o tũnini tũla twĩ vo katĩ wa ũndũ tũnaeleawa ũndũ mũna na ũndũ yu tũkũũelewa. Tweeka ũu, tũkeethĩawa twĩsĩ vyũ nĩtwongela ũw'o mweũ kyũmbanĩsyonĩ kitũ. Kwĩkĩa kĩthito kĩu nĩ kwa vata nĩkĩ?
17, 18. Veva mũtheu ũtonya kũtũtethya ata?
17 Yesũ amanyĩisye kana veva wa Ngai no ũtũlilikany'e maũndũ ala twĩmanyĩĩtye. (Yoa. 14:25, 26) Ũndũ ũsu ũtonya kũtũtethya ata ĩla tũũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo? Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũmwe mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Peter woonie. Mwakanĩ wa 1970 aĩ na myaka 19 na no ĩndĩ waĩ anambĩĩa kũthũkũma Mbetheli ya Britain. Mũthenya ũmwe aitavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba nĩwakomanie na mũndũ ũmwe waĩthĩtye kĩng'ee, ũla waĩ na myaka ta 50. Peter akũlilye mũndũ ũsu ethĩwa no ende kũelewa Mbivilia. Mũndũ ũsu ekalile ta waseng'a na ĩndĩ amwĩa we aumĩte mũsyĩ wa atongoi ma Kĩyuti. Nĩvo ĩndĩ mũtongoi ũsu wakũlilye Peter ĩkũlyo nĩ kana amũtate. Amũkũlilye atĩĩ: "Yu kamwana kwa ndavye-ĩ, yo ĩvuku ya Ndanieli yaandĩkiwe na kĩthyomo kĩva?" Peter amũsũngĩie amwĩa: "Kĩlungu kĩmwe kya ĩvuku yĩu kyaandĩkiwe na Kĩalamu." Peter aĩtye: "Mũtongoi ũsu aseng'ie mũno eethĩa nĩneesĩ ũsũngĩo. Ĩndĩ ninyie naseng'ie ĩ ya mũno! Namanyangie ũsungĩo ata? Nenũka nasyaisye makaseti ma Mũsyaĩĩsya na ma Amkeni! ala maĩ manauma myeinĩ yĩ navu ĩtina, na neethĩa kĩlungu kyaeleetye kana ĩvuku ya Ndanieli yaandĩkiwe na Kĩalamu." Ĩĩ nĩ w'o, veva mũtheu no ũtũlilikany'e maũndũ ala tũsomete na tũkaia nesa kyũmbanĩsyonĩ kitũ.—Luka 12:11, 12; 21:13-15.
18 Ethĩwa nĩtwonaa ũĩ ũla wumaa kwa Yeova wĩ wa vata, ngoo sitũ ikatũsukumaa tusũsye kyũmbanĩsyonĩ kitũ ũw'o mweũ na ũla mũkũũ. Na ũndũ twaendeea kwenda ũĩ ũla wumaa kwa Yeova na kwona wĩ wa vata, now'o tũkakwataa kyonthe kĩla kĩkwendeka nĩ kana tũmanyĩsye angĩ ũndũ vaĩle.
SŨVĨA ŨTHWII WAKU
19. Nĩkĩ twaĩlĩte kũsũvĩa ũthwii witũ wa kĩ-veva?
19 Satani na andũ ma nthĩ yake mekalaa maimantha ũndũ matonya kũtwĩka tũkaeka kwona ũthwii wa kĩ-veva ũla twaneenea ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ wĩ wa vata, kana tũkaeka kũwenda. Vai mũndũ ũtavalũkw'a nĩ Satani. Nĩ laisi mũno tũkakengeka twathwa wĩa mũseo, kana twambĩĩa kũsũanĩa ũndũ tũtonya kwambata kĩlasi, kana o twambĩĩa kwĩyonany'a nũndũ wa malĩ ĩla twĩ nayo. Mũtũmwa Yoana atũlilikanĩtye kana nthĩ ĩno nĩnĩũvĩta na wendi wayo. (1 Yoa. 2:15-17) Kwoou no nginya twĩkĩe kĩthito nĩ kana tũikaeke kwenda ũthwii witũ wa kĩ-veva na kwona wĩ wa vata.
20. Ũtw'ĩte kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũsũvĩe ũthwii waku wa kĩ-veva?
20 Ĩkalaa wĩyũmbanĩtye kũtia kyonthe kĩla kĩtonya kũtuma ũeka kwenda Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai na ngoo yonthe. Endeea kũtavany'a na kĩthito na ndũkaaĩse kũsũanĩa ũthũkũmi witũ ta ũte wa vata. Endeea kwĩmanyĩsya ũw'o ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai na kĩthito. Weeka ũu, ũkeethĩawa ũyũmbany'a "ũthwii . . . ĩtunĩ . . . vala kĩng'ei kĩtathengeaa, o na lungulu ũtananga. Nũndũ vala ve ũthwii wenyu, nĩvo vethĩawa ngoo syenyu nasyo."—Luka 12:33, 34.
