translation:
"Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also."—LUKE 12:34.
PAGE 153, 9
1, 2. (a) What are some ways Jehovah shows us that he values our spiritual wealth? (b) What will we discuss in this section?
JEHOVAH is the most generous Giver. (1 Chron. 29:11, 12) And just as a loving master appreciates his possessions, Jehovah values our spiritual wealth. We can be sure that Jehovah values our spiritual wealth because of (1) His love, (2) his loyalty, and (3) his concern for those who honor his name. So even if we face difficulties, we can remain confident knowing that Jehovah sees our efforts, and he will remember them. When we focus on our spiritual wealth, we will be more motivated to please Jehovah, and we will find joy in serving him each day. Jesus said: "Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also."—Luke 12:34.
2 How can we make sure that we continue to value spiritual things—love, loyalty, and concern—and how will this help us to see what is truly valuable? But to stay focused on these things, we need to examine ourselves regularly to see what we really value.
GOD'S LOVE IS LIKE A GREAT TREASURE
3. What lesson does the illustration of Jesus' parable about the hidden treasure teach us about valuing spiritual treasures? (See paragraph 9.)
3 Read Matthew 13:45, 46. Jesus used an illustration about a man who found a hidden treasure. The man sold everything he had to buy the field where the treasure was buried. He was willing to give up everything to get that treasure. Similarly, we may come to realize that spiritual treasures are far more valuable than anything else we possess. The treasure represented something precious. If someone offered you such a treasure, would you not do everything possible to obtain it?
4. How can we show that we value God's Love when faced with decisions?
4 This illustration teaches us something important. God's Kingdom is like that great treasure. When we face a decision, we should be willing to sacrifice anything so that we can serve Jehovah faithfully and remain loyal to his organization.—Read Mark 10:28-30. Let us consider some examples of people who did just that.
5. Did Zacchaeus realize the value of God's love?
5 Zacchaeus was a wealthy tax collector who was disliked because of his dishonest practices. (Luke 19:1-9) However, when Jesus came to Jericho, Zacchaeus was eager to see him. Jesus showed him that he valued Zacchaeus as a person, and this moved Zacchaeus to say: "Look! Half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore four times over." He proved that he was willing to make changes in his life and abandon his former way of living.
6. How did Rose feel when she learned about God's Kingdom, and what did she decide to do?
6 A sister named Rose had been studying the Bible for several years. She enjoyed sharing what she was learning with another sister, and that sister shared it with others. She also realized that her marriage was causing problems, and she began to separate from her husband. But after Rose studied the Bible more, she understood that God's Kingdom is something precious, and that it will last forever. And she realized that she wanted to devote herself fully to serving Jehovah. (1 Cor. 6:9, 10) Because she loved Jehovah, she was willing to make sacrifices and separate from her husband. Rose was baptized in 2009, and in that year she made the decision to put spiritual things first. She continued to serve Jehovah and remained faithful until her death.—Matt. 12:29, 30.
7. What can we learn from these examples about putting God's Kingdom first in our lives?
7 Many of us want to please Jehovah, but we may find it difficult to put God's Kingdom first. (Luke 12:2) However, remember that time is limited. So let us be determined to focus on what is truly important, such as preaching and teaching others, rather than getting caught up in material possessions and worldly pursuits. These things can distract us from putting God's Kingdom first. (Prov. 4:23; Matt. 5:27-29) Jehovah will strengthen us and help us to continue putting his Kingdom first in our lives.
LESSONS FOR US TODAY
8. (a) Why did Paul say that our bodies are "temples" of holy spirit? (b) Did Paul ever feel that his body was an obstacle to his ministry?
8 Remember that Jesus commanded us to make disciples and teach them everything he taught. (Matt. 28:19, 20) The apostle Paul understood this well. He said that our bodies are "temples" of holy spirit. (2 Cor. 4:7; 1 Tim. 1:12) But sometimes our physical limitations can hinder us from doing as much as we would like, and this can discourage us. Paul felt this way too, but he was determined to overcome those obstacles. He said: "I take delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in distresses for the sake of Christ." (1 Cor. 9:23) In fact, Paul often disciplined his body so that he could serve more effectively. (Read Philippians 1:14, 15; 2 Timothy 4:2.) This shows us the importance of self-discipline. (1 Thess. 2:2) We need to ask ourselves whether we are putting our bodies to good use, just as Paul did.
9. What things can help us to put our bodies to good use?
9 One thing Paul did to put his body to good use was to spend time with people. And like him and other Christians, we can show our faith by going house to house. (Acts 5:42; 20:20) While we may face difficulties, we should focus on what we *can* do, rather than dwelling on our limitations. Another thing we can do is be flexible, being willing to try different approaches or methods.—Acts 16:9, 10.
10. How did Irene benefit from thinking about her ministry?
10 Consider the experience of Irene, an American sister who learned Russian so she could help others. She had a strong desire to share the good news with Russian-speaking people. In 1993, she began attending a Russian-language congregation in New York City, and soon she was spending 20 hours a week in the ministry. Irene realized that she enjoyed helping people learn about Jehovah. She said: "I found that I really enjoyed teaching people Russian." Jehovah blessed her efforts and those of others. There were several Russian-language congregations in New York City. Some 15 of Irene's friends joined them and got baptized. These included Bethelites, pioneers, and regular publishers. Irene commented: "I often think about those experiences, and I am grateful for the opportunity I had." Truly, Irene put her body to good use!
11. How can we make sure that we continue to find joy in our ministry?
11 We can maintain our joy by continuing to associate closely with others and being zealous. This is what Paul did. (Acts 14:19-22) During the 1930s and 1940s, our brothers in America faced much opposition. Despite this opposition, they continued to preach, imitating Paul's example. Many of our brothers traveled to numerous territories, sometimes facing difficult conditions. In 1943, Nathan H. Knorr, a brother, visited one such territory—the United States branch office's circuit. He said: "We appreciate your loyalty and your willingness to endure hardship in order to proclaim the good news. Continue to travel and strengthen your fellow believers; and when you come to circuits where there is little activity, encourage the brothers and sisters to work harder and to be more courageous. The suffering experienced by God's people is what motivates us to push forward." Because of their loyalty despite difficulties, many brothers traveled extensively. So, let us imitate their zeal and determination to keep preaching.
12. How can we show that we value our ministry?
12 We show our appreciation for our ministry by making it a priority in our lives, giving it first place, even if it requires sacrificing time. Like those in the first century, let us each resolve to continue "to finish the ministry" that was entrusted to us. (Acts 20:24; 2 Timothy 4:5) But how can we remain motivated? By remembering why we are dedicated to Jehovah.
THE JOY OF SHARING WHAT WE LEARN
13, 14. What is the 'new things' Jesus referred to in Matthew 13:52, and how can we make them new to us?
13 The joy of sharing what we learn is closely linked to our dedication to Jehovah. Jehovah is the God of joy. (2 Samuel 7:28; Psalm 31:5) And as Asaph did, we can find joy in thinking about his purposes. Once we understand his purposes, we will be more eager to share what we learn from the Bible, our publications, our experiences, important events, and everyday occurrences. From time to time, we can reflect on what Jesus called "new things"—deeper understanding of truths we already know. (Read Matthew 13:52.) Jehovah can help us to increase our knowledge and to view "new things" as exciting so that we continue to appreciate his Word. (Read Proverbs 2:4-7.) Can we do this?
14 Of course, we benefit when we meditate on what we learn and apply it in our lives, making God's Word and our ministry a priority. Doing so helps us to enjoy the Word "more," or perhaps, to gain a greater appreciation for the truths we have learned. (Joshua 1:8, 9; Psalm 1:2, 3) A brother wrote in a letter dated July 7, 1879: "The Word is a vast treasure, constantly revealing its riches with increasing splendor. It may seem difficult at times…but even if you stumble, do not give up trying to understand it. Keep seeking, and keep digging for precious gems." Let us continue to seek out exciting new aspects of Bible truth.
15 But how can we tell whether something is truly "important," and how can we determine if a teaching comes from God?
15 We need to compare what we are taught with what the Bible says. Then we will be able to see if a teaching is "important" and if it agrees with what we already know about Christ. Does this teaching originate with God? We need to remember that Jehovah is our Creator and Sustainer, and we should appreciate his view of things. And we need to realize that God loved us enough to send his Son as a ransom. This understanding will help us to accept the Kingdom message and to live in harmony with God's laws.—John 3:16; Revelation 4:11; 21:3, 4.
16 What, then, can we do to make sure that we really believe what we learn?
16 Step by step, we can strengthen our belief by carefully examining the Bible and seeing how its teachings fit together. But simply knowing facts is not enough; we must also apply what we learn and share it with others. (Acts 17:11; 1 Timothy 4:15) We should not hesitate to ask questions about important matters, and we should not be afraid to admit when we do not fully understand something. In fact, doing so will help us to think critically and to distinguish between what is true and what is false. To put it another way, we need to use discernment when evaluating information. Why is this so vital?
17, 18. What reasons do we have for being discerning?
17 Jesus showed that God's spirit helps us to understand things that were previously unclear. (John 14:25, 26) So why is it vital for us to be discerning? Consider the experience of a young man named Peter. In the 1970's, when he was 19 years old, he was invited to serve at Bethel in Britain. One day, while visiting from house to house, he met a man who was about 50 years old. The man listened to Peter's explanation of the Bible and became interested. This man was a former judge who had retired from the Kentucky courts. It was because of his background that he challenged Peter, asking him: "Young man, do you mean to tell me that the book of Daniel was written in Aramaic?" Peter replied: "One passage in that book was written in Chaldean." The judge then said: "I would like to examine that passage myself." He added: "Did you ever wonder why I asked that question? I have examined those passages and found them to be accurate!" He concluded: "You youngsters have done your homework!"—Luke 12:11, 12; 21:13-15.
18 Therefore, we should always remember that Jehovah's spirit enables us to discern matters thoroughly, both small and great. And as we continue to seek Jehovah's guidance and to prove ourselves faithful, we will be able to cope with whatever challenges arise.—Proverbs 3:5, 6.
QUESTIONS FOR REVIEW
19. Why is it important for us to review our ministry?
19 Satan and his angels constantly try to deceive us into becoming discouraged about our ministry or into giving up. Satan is the master deceiver. He may tempt us to become self-sufficient, to feel that we can handle things on our own, or to compromise Bible principles. The apostle John warned us about this tendency. (1 John 2:15-17) So let us regularly examine ourselves to see whether we are maintaining zeal in our ministry and proving ourselves faithful.
20. What can help us to stay motivated in our ministry?
20 It is vital to reject everything that could lead you to give up serving God and to abandon all your activities. Continue to be diligent and make determined efforts to overcome selfishness and prove yourself worthy of Jehovah's favor. Keep meditating on the example of Jesus Christ and be zealous. In this way, you will remain "ready…with your loins girded and your lamps burning," and you will be happy when your Master arrives.—Luke 12:33, 34.

text:
"[Makwie] matosete matho, ĩndĩ mamonete me kũasa na kũmatanĩa."
1. Ũtonyi ũla twĩ naw'o wa kũkũna visa wa maũndũ tũtaaona ũtũtethasya ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
NGAI atũnengie mũthĩnzĩo wa vata mũno ĩla watũmbaa. Mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nĩ ũtonyi wa kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ ũkethĩa no ta twene syĩndũ o na kau tũyaasyona na metho. Ũndũ ũsu ũtumaa twĩthĩwa tũtonya kũvangĩĩa maũndũ nesa, na twĩthĩwa na mea ma kwona maũndũ maseo ala me mbee. Yeova mwene nũtonya kwona ũndũ ĩvinda yũkĩte yĩkethĩwa yĩilyĩ, na mavinda maingĩ nũtũtavasya Maandĩkonĩ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ mana o na mataaĩsa kwĩkĩka. O na kau ithyĩ tũitonya kwona na metho maitũ maũndũ asu makekĩka, nĩtũtonya kũkũna visa wamo ilĩkonĩ sitũ. Ĩla twatũmĩa ũtonyi ũsu witũ kwa nzĩa ĩsu twĩthĩawa tũilũlũmĩlya mũĩkĩĩo witũ.—2 Ako. 4:18.
2, 3. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kũsũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ matonyeka? (b) Twĩsũngĩa makũlyo meva?
2 Mavinda angĩ no twambĩĩe kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ wa kĩndũ o na kĩtesa kwĩkĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, sũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kamwĩlĩtu keũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ kakuĩtwe nĩ kĩmbalutw'a. Kũu no kũkenga kĩlĩko. Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩla Aana woosie mwanya wa kũsũanĩa ũndũ kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ mũthenya ũla ũkatwaa mwanae, Samueli, ĩeemanĩ ya kũmbanĩa akamũthũkũmae Ngai, ndeekaa kũkenga kĩlĩko kyake. Ndakengaa kĩlĩko kyake nũndũ ũsu nĩ ũndũ watw'ĩte kwĩka, na kũkũna visa ĩũlũ wa mũthenya ũsu nĩkwamũtetheeisye alũmany'e na ũtwi wake. (1 Sam. 1:22) O ta ũu, ĩla twakũna visa wa kĩla Ngai ũtwathĩte kwĩka, twĩthĩawa tũisũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ matatĩa kwĩkĩka.—2 Vet. 1:19-21.
3 Vate nzika, andũ aingĩ aĩkĩĩku ala mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ nĩmakũnaa visa ilĩkonĩ syoo ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala Ngai wamathĩte. Kwĩka ũu kwamatethasya ata? Na tũtonya kũtetheka ata twoosa ĩvinda ya kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ maseo ala Ngai wathĩte ala mamwĩw'aa?
NĨMEEKĨIWE VINYA NĨ KWĨKALA MENE KĨLA MATHĨTWE
4. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumaa Aveli ethĩwa atonya kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yaĩ mbee?
4 Aveli nĩwe waĩ mũndũ wa mbee kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku. We nĩwĩthĩwa ekalaa ene ũndũ o na ũmwe katĩ wa maũndũ ala Yeova wathanĩte? Tũitonya kwasya kana Aveli nĩweesĩ nesa vyũ ũndũ watho ũla Ngai waumisye ĩũlũ wa ĩla nzoka ũkeanĩa. Ngai athanie atĩĩ: "Ngeekĩa ũmaitha katĩ wenyu we na mũndũ mũka, na katĩ wa ũsyao waku na ũsyao wake: Akatumba mũtwe waku, naku ũkatumba kĩtiinyo kyake." (Mwa. 3:14, 15) Ĩndĩ nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Aveli nĩwavindĩĩsye mũno watho ũsu, na akwatya kana ve mũndũ 'ũkatumbwa kĩtiinyo' nĩ kana andũ makaaĩsa kũvetewa naĩ, na mayĩkala o tondũ Atamu na Eva mailyĩ matanamba kũvĩtya. O na Aveli akethĩwa akũnaa visa ũilyĩ ata ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yaĩ mbee wake, aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ũsu nũndũ wa watho ũla Yeova waumĩtye na nĩkyo kĩtumi Yeova weetĩkĩlile nthembo yake.—Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 4:3-5; Aevelania 11:4.
5. Enoko atonya kwĩthĩwa atethekaa ata nũndũ wa kwĩkalaa aikũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yaĩ mbee?
5 Mũndũ ũngĩ mũĩkĩĩku aĩ Enoko, o na kau atũaa na andũ matamũkĩaa Ngai na maneeneaa ũ Ngai ndeto nthũku. Yeova nĩwamũveveee Enoko athana kana akatheea "vamwe na atheu make, nguthu ĩtatalĩka, kũmasilĩla andũ onthe, na kũmaĩkĩĩthya onthe ala matamũkĩaa Ngai ũndũ wa meko moo onthe ma kũlea kũmũkĩaa Ngai ala meekie, na nũndũ wa ndeto syoo syonthe nyũmũ ila asu athe matamũkĩaa Ngai mamũneeneete." (Yuta 14, 15) Nũndũ Enoko aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo, aĩ atonya kũkũnaa visa wa ũndũ nthĩ ĩtonya kwĩthĩwa ĩilyĩ ĩte na andũ matamũkĩaa Ngai.—Soma Aevelania 11:5, 6.
6. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva Noa wĩthĩwa aendeeie kũsũanĩa ĩtina wa ĩla mbua ya ĩvinda yake?
6 O nake Noa aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo na nĩkyo kĩtumi ũtaanangwa na ĩla mbua ya ĩvinda yake. (Aevl. 11:7) Mbua ĩsu yathela, mũĩkĩĩo ũsu now'o watumie aumya nthembo sya nyamũ. (Mwa. 8:20) O ta Aveli, vate nzika Noa aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo wa kana ĩvinda yĩmwe andũ makathaw'a maume ũkombonĩ wa naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. Noa ndaaeka kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo na wĩkwatyo ũsu o na ĩla myaka yavĩtie na esa kwĩthĩwa nĩ yĩla ĩvinda ĩthũku Nimiloti wambĩĩe kũvĩndũa andũ maleane na Yeova. (Mwa. 10:8-12) Nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ũkethĩa nĩweekĩawa vinya mũno nĩ kũsũanĩa ĩvinda yĩla mbaa andũ makavetewa asumbĩki athũku vamwe na naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. O naitũ no twĩkale twene ĩvinda yĩu ĩseo yĩ mbee witũ. Yĩi vaasa!—Alo. 6:23.
NO TA MEENE MAŨNDŨ ALA MATHĨTWE MAIANĨA
7. Nĩ maũndũ meva maĩ mbee ala Avalaamu, Isaka, na Yakovo mekalaa mene?
7 Avalaamu, Isaka, na Yakovo nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa makũnaa visa ilĩkonĩ syoo makona ĩvinda ĩseo mbee woo nũndũ Ngai nĩwamathĩte kana kwĩsĩla ũsyao woo, mbaĩ syonthe ikaathimĩka. (Mwa. 22:18; 26:4; 28:14) Mathĩtwe kana ũsyao woo ũkaingĩva na ũitũa ĩla Nthĩ ya Watho Ngai ũkaũnenga. (Mwa. 15:5-7) Nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo woo, no ta meene ũsyao woo ũtwĩe nthĩ ĩsu mathĩtwe. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ kuma ĩla andũ malikile naĩnĩ, Yeova ekalaa ayĩĩkĩĩthya athũkũmi make ala aĩkĩĩku kana moathimo ala maaiw'e nĩ Atamu mayaaa tene na tene.
8. Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeasya Avalaamu ethĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu?
8 Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Avalaamu eekaa maũndũ manene ma mũĩkĩĩo nũndũ nĩwakũnaa visa wa maũndũ ala Ngai wathanĩte. Maandĩko nĩmawetete kana o na kau Avalaamu na andũ angĩ mamũthũkũmĩte Ngai me aĩkĩĩku makwie "matosete matho," ĩla maĩ thayũ "mamonete me kũasa na kũmatanĩa." (Soma Aevelania 11:8-13.) Ve maũndũ maingĩ mũno matumaa Avalaamu aĩkĩĩa kana maũndũ ala weeteele mayaĩ maema kũka nginya ũkethĩa we no ta wamene o na kũtw'ĩka ndaĩ aamavakya itho.
9. Avalaamu atethekie ata nũndũ wa kũĩkĩĩa mawatho ma Ngai?
9 Nũndũ Avalaamu nĩwaĩkĩĩe mawatho onthe ma Ngai, aĩ na vinya wa kwĩka ũndũ w'onthe ũla Ngai wamũkũlasya eke. Nĩkyo kĩtumi weetĩkĩlile kũtia ndũa ya Ulu na alea vyũ kwaka mũsyĩ ndũanĩ ila syaĩ Kanaani. O ta ndũa ya Ulu, ndũa isu sya Kanaani iyaĩ syĩsa kwĩkala tene na tene nũndũ ala maisumbĩkĩte mayamũthaithaa Yeova. (Yos. 24:2) Myaka yonthe ĩla Avalaamu wekalile e thayũ kuma auma Ulu, "nĩweteelaa onw'e ndũa ĩla yĩ na myambĩlĩlyo, na mwambĩlĩlya na mwaki wayo nĩ Ngai." (Aevl. 11:10) Avalaamu nĩwakũnaa visa akona atwĩe kũndũ kũtakanangwa kũsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Yeova. Aveli, Enoko, Noa, vamwe na Avalaamu na andũ angĩ tamo mayaĩ na nzika kana akw'ũ makathayũũkw'a, na nĩmeeteele mũno kwĩsa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Ũsumbĩ ũsu nĩw'o "ndũa ĩla yĩ na myambĩlĩlyo." Kũvindĩĩsya moathimo ta asu nĩkwatumie mamũĩkĩĩa Yeova mũnango.—Soma Aevelania 11:15, 16.
10. Wĩkwatyo ũla Sala waĩ naw'o wamũtethisye ata?
10 Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mũka wa Avalaamu, ũla weetawa Sala. O na kau aivikya myaka 90 ndaĩ aasyaa, wĩkwatyo ũla waĩ naw'o nĩwatumaa ethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana no ũkasyaa. Ũu no ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya kana nĩwakũnaa visa akona Yeova aathimĩte syana syake o tondũ wathanĩte. (Aevl. 11:11, 12) Nĩ kyaũ kyatumaa ethĩwa na wĩkwatyo ũsu? Yeova athĩte mũũme atĩĩ: "Ngamũathima, na ĩngĩ ngakũnenga mwana kuma kwake: ĩĩ, ngamũathima, nake akeethĩwa inyia wa mbaĩ; asumbĩ ma andũ makauma kwake." (Mwa. 17:16) Kwoou ĩla Sala wasyaie Isaka, aĩ atonya kũkũna visa ate na nzika akona moathimo ala angĩ Ngai wathĩte Avalaamu maianĩa. O naitũ twĩ na ũtonyi ta ũsu wa kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ tũkona maũndũ ala Ngai ũtwathĩte. Maũndũ asu maikalea kwĩanĩa!
NĨWASYAĨĨSYE ĨTUVI YĨLA YĨKANENGANWE
11, 12. Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Mose amwende Yeova?
11 Mũndũ ũngĩ wamũĩkĩĩe Yeova nĩ Mose, na nĩwamwendete mũno. Ĩndĩ e mũnini ekalaa Misili kwa Valao, na nũndũ wa ũu yaĩ laisi mũno akakwatwa nĩ wendi wa malĩ na monene. Ũseo nĩ kana atanamba kũthi kwa Valao, asyai make nĩmamũmanyĩĩtye ĩũlũ wa Yeova na kĩeleelo kyake kya kumya Aevelania ũkombonĩ na kũmanenga ĩla Nthĩ ya Watho. (Mwa. 13:14, 15; Kuma 2:5-10) Ethĩwa Mose nĩwakothaa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa moathimo ala Ngai wathĩte andũ make, we wĩona nĩ kyaũ wesaa kwenda ngoonĩ yake? Nĩ monene-ĩ, kana nĩ Yeova?
12 Maandĩko matwĩĩte ũũ: "Kwondũ wa mũĩkĩĩo Mose, yĩla waĩ aneana, nĩwaleile kwĩtwa mwana wa mwĩĩtu wa Valao; akĩnyuva kavaa kũthĩnw'a vamwe na andũ ma Ngai, kwĩ kũtana maũndũnĩ ma naĩ ĩvinda; aitala kũvũthw'a kwa Klĩsto nĩ ũthwii mwingĩ kũvĩta ũthwii wa Misili, nũndũ nĩwasyaisye ĩtuvi yĩla yĩkanenganwe."—Aevl. 11:24-26.
13. Mose atethekie ata nũndũ wa kũvindĩĩsya mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩla Ngai wathanĩte?
13 O ũndũ Mose watũmĩie ĩvinda yĩana aivindĩĩsya mũno kĩla Yeova wathĩte Aisilaeli, now'o wamũĩkĩĩe mũnango na amwenda mũnango. Mose nũtonya kwĩthĩwa akũnaa visa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla Yeova ũkaumya andũ ũkombonĩ wa kĩkw'ũ, o tondũ athaithi ala angĩ ma Ngai meekaa. (Yovu 14:14, 15; Aevl. 11:17-19) Kĩu nĩkyatumie amanya ũndũ Ngai weew'ĩaa tei Aevelania vamwe na andũ ala angĩ onthe, na nũndũ wa ũu nĩwamwendie mũnango. Kũmwenda Ngai na kũmũĩkĩĩa nĩkw'o kwamwĩkĩie vinya ĩvinda yonthe yĩla waĩ thayũ. (Kũt. 6:4, 5) O na ĩla Valao wamwĩie aũngama mbee wake nũkũawa, mũĩkĩĩo ũla waĩ naw'o na ũndũ wamwendete Ngai nĩsyatumie ethĩwa na ũkũmbaũ. O na no kwĩthĩwa visa ũla wakũnaa kĩlĩkonĩ wa ĩvinda ĩseo yĩla yaĩ mbee wake wamũtetheeisye kwĩthĩwa na ũkũmbaũ ũsu.—Kuma 10:28, 29.
VINDĨĨSYA MAŨNDŨ ALA ŨSUMBĨ WA NGAI ŨKEANĨSYA
14. Nĩ mosũanĩo meva mũndũ ũtonya kwĩkenga kĩlĩko namo?
14 Andũ aingĩ ũmũnthĩ makengaa ilĩko syoo kwa kũkũna visa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ matakesa kwĩkĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na kau ũmũnthĩ myaka yitũ yusĩe "thĩna na kĩĩo," andũ amwe maotaa matw'ĩkĩte athwii mũno na mate na thĩna o na ũmwe, o na kũtw'ĩka oyu mai na syĩndũ mbingĩ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ. (Sav. 90:10, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) O na kau Mbivilia yaĩtye kana vai kĩndũ kĩngĩ kĩkatethya andũ eka Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, andũ ma ũko ũsu makũnaa visa masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ silikalĩ ya mũndũ kũte thĩna o na ũmwe. (Nda. 2:44) Monaa Ngai ndakaaĩsa kwananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku. Ĩndĩ kĩla Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya kĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na kyu maĩkĩĩaa. (Nzev. 1:18; 1 Yoa. 2:15-17) Wĩkwatyo ta ũsu wa andũ asu mavũthasya kĩeleelo kya Yeova no wa mana nũndũ methĩawa maikenga ilĩko syoo.
15. (a) Nĩ ũtethyo mwaũ Aklĩsto makwataa ĩla makũna visa ĩũlũ wa mũthenya ũla wĩkwatyo woo ũkeanĩa? (b) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva we weteele mũno kwona ũianĩa?
15 Kĩvathũkany'o na andũ asu, Aklĩsto nĩmew'aa makwata vinya ĩla makũna visa wa mũthenya ũla wĩkwatyo woo ũkeanĩw'a, wĩthĩwe nĩ wa kũthi ĩtunĩ kana nĩ wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. We nũkũnaa visa ũkona ũitanĩa moathimo ala Ngai wathanĩte? Vate nzika kũsũanĩa kĩla wĩĩka Ngai eanĩsya wĩkwatyo waku nĩkũtonya kũũtanĩthya mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, no kwĩthĩwa ũkũnaa visa ũkona ũilyĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene. Kwasũanĩa wĩ na andũ angĩ mũendeee kũthesya nthĩ ĩno yĩkale ũndũ mũũnda wa Eteni wailyĩ. Atũi maku onthe mamwendete Yeova o ũndũ ũmwendete. Ndwĩ na thĩna o na ũmwe wa mwĩĩ, wĩ na vinya, na maũndũ onthe ala wĩkwatĩtye kwĩsa kwona nĩ maseo. Andũ ala maũngamĩe wĩa wenyu wa kũthesya nthĩ maiũmũtulya nũndũ nĩmamwendete vyũ. Naku wĩĩw'a mũyo ũitũmĩa inengo syaku na ũtũĩka waku nũndũ kyonthe kĩla ũkwĩka nĩkĩũtethya ala angĩ na nĩkĩũmũtaĩa Ngai. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũũtũmĩa ĩvinda ũkatetheesya ala mathayũũkw'a mamũmanye Yeova. (Yoa. 17:3; Meko 24:15) Ethĩwa nũsũanĩaa maũndũ asu onthe, ndwĩthĩawa ũiota. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ kũkũna visa wa maũndũ asu maseũvĩte ũu nĩkwosanĩte na kĩla Maandĩko mawetete ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.—Isa. 11:9; 25:8; 33:24; 35:5-7; 65:22.
NĨKĨ WAĨLE KŨNEENEA WĨKWATYO WAKU?
16, 17. Kũneenea wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o kũtonya kũtũtethya ata?
16 Kũea ngewa na Aklĩsto ala angĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩla tũkenda kwĩka ĩla Yeova ũkethĩwa aianĩsya mawatho make nĩkũtũtetheeasya ithyonthe kũkũna visa mũseango vyũ wa ĩvinda yĩu. O na kau vai ũmwe witũ ũtonya kũweta nesa vyũ ũndũ ũkethĩwa ailyĩ e nthĩ nzaũ, kũea ngewa ĩũlũ wa kĩla tũkwona ta kĩkekĩka nĩkũtumaa tũthangaany'a, na nĩkũtũnengae mwanya wa kwonany'a nĩtũĩkĩĩe kana Ngai akeanĩsya maũndũ ala wathanĩte. O tondũ mũtũmwa Vaulo 'wathangaanisye' vamwe na ana-a-asa ala maĩ Lomi ĩla wamathokeie, kũea ngewa ta isu nĩkũtumaa tũthangaany'a tũendeee kũmũthũkũma Yeova ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ yĩ na mathĩna.—Alo. 1:11, 12, BCK.
17 Kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yũkĩte nĩkũtonya kũtũtethya ũkethĩa tũikwĩsilya mũno ĩũlũ wa mathĩna ala twĩ namo. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya ĩvinda yĩmwe mũtũmwa Vetelo weemakĩe mũno. Ĩvinda yĩu amũkũlilye Yesũ atĩĩ: "Sisya, ithyĩ nĩtũtiĩte syonthe na twakũatĩĩa; tũkosa kyaũ ĩndĩ?" Nĩ kana Yesũ atetheesye Vetelo vamwe na ala angĩ makũne visa ilĩkonĩ syoo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ĩvinda yũkĩte yĩkethĩwa yĩilyĩ, asungĩie ĩkũlyo yĩu asya: "Nĩ w'o nĩngũmwĩa, kana inyw'ĩ mũmbikĩlĩte, yĩla Mwana wa mũndũ ũkekalĩla kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya ũtheu wake mũtisu kũalyũkwanĩ kweũ, inyw'ĩ nenyu nĩmũkekalĩla ivĩla sya ũsumbĩ ĩkũmi na ilĩ, mũkĩsilĩla mbai ĩkũmi na ilĩ sya Isilaeli. Na kĩla mũndũ ũla ũtiĩte nyũmba, kana ana-a-inyia, kana eĩtu-a-inyia, kana ĩthe, kana nyinyia, kana syana, kana mĩũnda, kwondũ wa syĩtwa yakwa, akoosaa vandũ va kĩmwe, ĩana, na akatiĩwa thayũ ũtathela." (Mt. 19:27-29) Nũndũ wa maũndũ asu Yesũ wamatavisye, Vetelo vamwe na amanyĩw'a ala angĩ maĩ matonya kũkũna visa ĩũlũ wa wĩa ũla makethĩwa makwatĩĩe nthĩnĩ wa silikalĩ ĩla ĩkasumbĩka nthĩ na ĩietee andũ ala ewi moathimo maseo vyũ.
18. Tũtethekaa ata twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ Ngai ũkeanĩsya mawatho make?
18 Kuma tene athũkũmi ma Yeova ala me kũũ nthĩ nĩmatethekaa mavindĩĩsya mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩla Yeova wathanĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, maũndũ ala Aveli weesĩ ĩũlũ wa kĩeleelo kya Ngai nĩmatoetye kũmũtetheesya akũne visa wa ĩvinda ĩseo yĩla yaĩ mbee wake. O na nĩmamũtetheeisye kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo na wĩkwatyo mũlũmu. Nake Avalaamu eekie maũndũ manene ma mũĩkĩĩo nũndũ no ta weene Ngai aianĩsya wathani wake ĩũlũ wa ũla "ũsyao." (Mwa. 3:15) O ta ũu, Mose aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo na aendeeie kũmwenda Yeova nũndũ "nĩwasyaisye ĩtuvi yĩla yĩkanenganwe." (Aevl. 11:26) Naitũ no tũmwende Ngai mũnango na tũyĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmangu twakũna visa maũndũ ala wathanĩte maianĩa. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩneeneete ũndũ tũtonya kũtũmĩa nesa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu tũnengetwe nĩ Ngai.

translation:
"[Makwie] let your eyes be straight, lest you stumble because of sin and destruction."
1. Will the discernment we have help us to avoid bad association? (Consider good examples.)
GOD helps us to cope with trials that come upon us. This discernment is the ability to associate with the right people so that we can benefit from what they say and do. It helps us to be cautious about getting involved in things that are not pleasing to God, and it helps us to avoid being influenced by those who do not love him. Jehovah helps us to see what is hidden in people's hearts, and many times he guides us to the Scriptures which warn us about wicked people and their ways. And sometimes we can see with our own eyes how wrong certain people are, and then we can avoid associating with them. But we must use this discernment of ours in order to remain loyal to our dedication.—2 Cor. 4:18.
2, 3. (a) How can we improve our discernment? (b) What will motivate us?
2 Many of us want to have discernment regarding something or someone. For example, improving discernment may involve studying diligently. However, it takes effort. In fact, Hannah prayed earnestly when she vowed to dedicate her son Samuel to God, showing that she put effort into it. Putting effort into it helped her to trust in God, and having discernment during that time strengthened her faith. (1 Sam. 1:22) So, if we want to please God and obey his commands, we must strive to improve our discernment regarding difficult matters.—2 Pet. 1:19-21.
3 Often, many Christians find it hard to discern what God approves of. Does this cause trouble? And can we learn to appreciate the value of discerning what God approves of from others?
THIS IS WRITTEN TO HELP YOU STAY STRONG
4 What caused Abel to be approved and able to have discernment regarding the offering he made?
4 Abel was a righteous man who was pleasing to God. Was he approved because he did what God commanded? Can we learn whether Abel understood the significance of God's prophecy about the serpent's offspring? God foretold: "I will put enmity between you and the woman and between your offspring and her offspring." (Gen. 3:14, 15) Therefore, Abel likely realized that his death would be part of fulfilling that prophecy, and he did not fear those who might try to harm him, just as Adam and Eve did not become paralyzed with fear. Also, Abel was approved because he had faith, even though he knew that the offspring of the serpent would oppose Jehovah's purpose.—Read Genesis 4:3-5; Hebrews 11:4.
5 How could Enoch be approved despite living among wicked people?
5 A righteous man like Enoch walked with God and pleased Him greatly. Jehovah showed Enoch a vision of "the future," including the destruction of wicked people and the vindication of those who worshiped God loyally, as well as the fulfillment of God's purposes toward those who loved Him. (Jude 14, 15) Because Enoch had this vision, he was able to maintain faith despite being surrounded by wickedness.—Read Hebrews 11:5, 6.
6 Why was Noah approved so that he could build an ark to survive the flood?
6 Noah had faith, and that is why he was warned about the coming flood. (Heb. 11:7) Today, faith can motivate us to preach the good news. (Gen. 8:20) But unlike Abel, Noah did not just have faith that his family would be saved; he acted on his faith. Noah demonstrated his faith by building the ark, and because of his faith, his family survived when the great flood came and wiped out those who were disloyal to Jehovah. (Gen. 10:8-12) It is important to remember that we show our faith by taking practical steps to live in harmony with God's will. So let us continue to walk with God faithfully.—Acts 6:23.
DO NOT MISS OTHER IMPORTANT POINTS
7 What examples of faith did Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob display?
7 Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob showed their faith by being willing to move to a land that God promised them, even though they did not know where they were going. (Gen. 22:18; 26:4; 28:14) They trusted that God would fulfill his promise to bless them. (Gen. 15:5-7) Because of their faith, they received a blessing from God, and they continued to trust in him. Like them, Jehovah helps his faithful servants to endure trials and difficulties, and he remembers their loyalty.
8 What strengthened Abraham's faith greatly?
8 Abraham was strengthened because he remembered God's promises and what God had done for him. The Scriptures tell us that Abraham did not become discouraged when he grew old and childless, but he continued to believe that God could fulfill his promise. He saw God's power as being able to "make dead ones alive," rather than just seeing the situation as hopeless. (Read Hebrews 11:8-13.) Many things helped Abraham to remain faithful, including his understanding of what God had done for him and his confidence in God's ability to fulfill his promises.
9 Did Abraham ever doubt God's promises?
9 Abraham did have moments of weakness, but he never lost faith in God's promise to bless him greatly. This is why he was willing to travel from Ur to an unknown land, even though it meant leaving behind his relatives and friends in Haran. Like the land of Ur, the land of Canaan appeared to be unproductive and difficult to live in, yet it was the land that Jehovah had promised to give them. (Josh. 24:2) Throughout his life while living in Canaan, Abraham felt secure knowing that "the city he was expecting had foundations, and its designer and builder was God." (Heb. 11:10) Abraham knew that God would honor those who seek to glorify Him. Abel, Enoch, Noah, along with Abraham and others like them showed faith and courage, and they were counted righteous because of their faith. That faith is what "has good recommendation with God." To encourage us, let us remember how our forefathers remained faithful to Jehovah.—Read Hebrews 11:15, 16.
10 How can you show that you trust in God's promise?
10 Sarah, Abraham's wife, also demonstrated her faith. Although she was nearly 90 years old when Isaac was born, she firmly believed that God could fulfill His promise, despite the fact that she was barren. She realized that God is able to do what He promises. (Heb. 11:11, 12) What helped her to maintain that belief? Jehovah assured her: "I will certainly return to you at the appointed time next year, and Sarah will then have a son." (Gen. 18:16) Because of this assurance, Sarah gave birth to Isaac, and she came to have even greater faith in God's power. So, let us learn from her example and strengthen our own faith in what God has promised us. The blessings are well worth waiting for!
SHOWING YOUR APPRECIATION
11, 12. Why did Moses remain loyal to Jehovah?
11 Another man who showed loyalty to Jehovah was Moses. He chose to associate himself with God's people rather than enjoy a life of luxury as the grandson of Pharaoh. He refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, preferring to suffer mistreatment with God's people and to look forward to the reward—the Kingdom. (Ex. 13:14, 15; Heb. 2:5-10) Moses was willing to endure hardship because he valued God's favor more than anything else. But how was he able to do so? It was because he kept his focus on Jehovah.
12 The Scriptures tell us: "By faith Moses, when grown up, refused to be known as the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing to be mistreated along with God's people rather than to enjoy the temporary pleasure of sin. He considered reproach for Christ to be greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward."—Heb. 11:24-26.
13. Did Moses ever doubt God's ability to deliver his people?
13 Why did Moses trust that Jehovah would fulfill what he promised to Israel, despite the fact that Pharaoh opposed him? Moses knew that Jehovah could use His power to save them from Pharaoh's oppression, just as He had done in the past. (Job 14:14, 15; Heb. 11:17-19) This helped him appreciate what God could do for others and encouraged him to remain loyal. To show loyalty to God and to have confidence in Him means to put your trust in Him completely. (Deut. 6:4, 5) And like Pharaoh, those who oppose God will eventually fail, while those who remain faithful will receive blessings. Also, remember that the reproaches you experience because of your faith can strengthen your resolve and deepen your love for God.—Heb. 10:28, 29.
WHAT ELSE DOES GOD REWARD LOYALTY WITH?
14. What is one way a person can demonstrate that he does not value material things?
14 Many people often value possessions more than life itself, especially when they become attached to their comforts and luxuries. For example, some may spend years of their lives working hard "to get ahead," and others may accumulate wealth only to find themselves burdened with worry and anxiety. (Ps. 90:10, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Moreover, the Bible shows that pursuing riches can distract people from spiritual pursuits, causing them to forget God. (Prov. 2:44) However, God understands our desire for security. The Bible does not condemn us for wanting to provide for ourselves and our families, but it warns us against letting materialism control our lives. (Eccl. 1:18; 1 John 2:15-17) Therefore, be careful not to let the pursuit of worldly things hinder your zeal for serving Jehovah and learning about his purposes.
15. (a) How do Christians view the fulfillment of the promise that God made regarding the Kingdom? (b) What can help you stay focused on what is truly important?
15 By associating with fellow believers, Christians develop a balanced view of the importance of the Kingdom and avoid becoming overly concerned with material possessions or social status. Do you ever wonder whether God values your efforts? Rest assured that God appreciates those who diligently pursue his will. For instance, he notices when you use your resources to support his work. Consider how valuable it is to have a good reputation among your neighbors. Showing kindness to others demonstrates your love for Jehovah and your appreciation for what he has done for you. With time and effort, you can cultivate qualities that please him and make your life meaningful. Others will notice your fine conduct and be moved to learn about Jehovah. Remember that everything you have—your abilities, your health, and your possessions—is a gift from God. Use these blessings wisely to honor him and to share the good news with others. For example, use your knowledge to help others come to know Jehovah. (John 17:3; Mark 24:15) Be willing to discuss spiritual matters with others, and do so tactfully. Why? Because focusing on spiritual things helps us appreciate the meaning of life and aligns our thinking with God's thoughts as expressed in his Word.—Isa. 11:9; 25:8; 33:24; 35:5-7; 65:22.
WHY SHOULD YOU VALUE YOUR RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD?
16, 17. What reasons do we have for wanting to strengthen our relationship with God?
16 Like Jesus, we want to please our Father, Jehovah, and show that we appreciate his loving provision. But sometimes we may struggle to maintain zeal, especially when faced with difficulties. Like Jesus, we need to pray regularly to remain close to God and to ask for his guidance. Also, we should reflect on the ways in which God has blessed us, which will motivate us to keep serving him wholeheartedly. Paul "kept his eye fixed" on fellow Christians in Lystra, and this helped them stay spiritually strong. Similarly, we can encourage one another to continue pursuing Jehovah with all their heart.—Acts 1:11, 12, footnote.
17 We can also strengthen our faith by remembering past experiences where God helped us. Consider the example of Peter. Jesus asked his disciples: "Who do people say I am?" Then he asked them: "But who do *you* say I am?" After Peter answered, Jesus commended him. However, Peter later denied Jesus three times. Despite this failure, Jesus restored Peter and gave him an important assignment. Jesus said: "Simon, look! Satan has sought to sift you people like wheat, but I made intercession for you, so that your faith might not give out. Also, you, once you have recovered, strengthen your brothers." (Luke 22:31-32) Jesus knew that Peter would face trials, but he prayed for him. Later, Jesus showed Peter great compassion and entrusted him with a vital role in caring for the flock. This illustrates how much value Jesus placed on his relationship with Peter.
(Matt. 19:27-29) In view of all these things Jesus had done, Peter and the other disciples were willing to leave everything behind to follow him, knowing that they would receive a far greater reward.
18. Can we truly trust that God will fulfill his promises?
18 There are numerous examples in the Bible showing that Jehovah keeps his promises. For instance, the account of Abel demonstrates how seriously God views obedience. Abel's offering was acceptable to God because of his faithful worship. But Cain became jealous and killed Abel. Yet, God promised to avenge Abel's death. (Gen. 4:8) And he did. Moses also faced a difficult choice when he decided to side with Jehovah rather than enjoy "the temporary pleasure of sin." (Heb. 11:25) Therefore, let us continue to put our trust in God and remain loyal to him, confident that he will honor our dedication. The lesson here is clear: We can be sure that God will help us to endure trials and remain steadfast in our service to him.

text:
"Nĩtũkũthi nenyu, nũndũ nĩtwĩw'ĩte kana Ngai e vamwe nenyu."—NZEK. 8:23.
MBATHI: 32, 31
1, 2. (a) Yeova athanie ũndũ wĩva ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yitũ? (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
YEOVA nĩwaumisye wathani ũkonetye ĩvinda yĩĩ tũtwĩe. Athanie ũũ: "Mĩthenya ĩsu kũkeethĩwa, atĩ andũ ĩkũmi, kuma ithyomonĩ syonthe sya i mbaĩ, makakwata, ĩĩ, makakwata mũthya wa ngũa ya mũndũ Mũyuti, makyasya, Nĩtũkũthi nenyu, nũndũ nĩtwĩw'ĩte kana Ngai e vamwe nenyu." (Nzek. 8:23) O ta andũ asu ĩkũmi, Aklĩsto ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ nĩmosete ĩtambya "makakwata mũthya wa ngũa ya mũndũ Mũyuti." Nĩmatanĩaa kũthũkũma vamwe na Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta, kana "Isilaeli ma Ngai," nũndũ nĩmesĩ kana Yeova nũmaathimĩte.—Aka. 6:16.
2 O nake Yesũ nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa ngwatanĩo ĩla andũ ma Ngai methĩawa nayo. Awetie kana aatĩĩi make nĩ ikundi ilĩ. Kĩkundi kya mbee akĩtie "ĩĩthya ĩnini" na kya kelĩ akĩta "malondu angĩ." Ĩndĩ aisye kana ikundi isu syelĩ ikeethĩwa "ĩĩthya yĩmwe" yĩtongoew'e nĩ "mũĩthi ũmwe." (Luka 12:32; Yoa. 10:16) Nĩkwĩthĩwa ikundi nĩ ilĩ, no twende kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo aa: (1) Nĩ lasima malondu angĩ mamanye masyĩtwa ma etĩkĩw'a mauta onthe ala me kw'o ũmũnthĩ? (2) Etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩle kwĩkua ata? (3) We waĩle kwĩka ata wamanya Mũklĩsto wĩ kĩkundinĩ kyenyu nĩwambĩĩe kũya kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? (4) Nĩtwaĩle kũthĩnĩka twoona ũtalo wa ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ũyongeleka? Ekai tũsũanĩe vamwe mosũngĩo ma makũlyo asu me ana.
VE VATA WA KŨMANYA MASYĨTWA MA ETĨKĨW'A MAUTA ONTHE?
3. Nĩkĩ vaitonyeka tũkamanya nũũ ũkatalwa yĩla ĩsavunĩ ya 144,000?
3 Nĩ lasima malondu angĩ mamanye masyĩtwa ma etĩkĩw'a mauta onthe ala me kw'o ũmũnthĩ? Ũsũngĩo nĩ aiee. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ mũndũ akwata wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, ethĩawa eeka o kũthokw'a ĩndĩ ũu ti kwonany'a kana no nginya ethi ĩtunĩ. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi Satani ũkĩlasya "athani ma ũvũngũ . . . nĩ kana masye, o na anyuve, ethĩwa ũu nũtonyeka." (Mt. 24:24) Ate o Yeova esie kũtw'a kana Mũklĩsto mũna mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta nĩwaĩle kũkwata mũthĩnzĩo wake wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, vai mũndũ o na ũmwe ũtonya kũmũtw'ĩĩa. Kavinda kakuvĩ Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta atanamba kũkw'a e mũĩkĩĩku, Yeova nũmũtw'ĩĩaa kũthi ĩtunĩ na aimwĩkĩa ũsiĩlo wa mũthya. Akeekana oou na ala makethĩwa thayũ kavinda kakuvĩ 'ũla thĩna mũnene' ũtambĩĩe. (Ũvu. 2:10; 7:3, 14) Kwoou wĩthĩwa wĩ o wĩa wa mana kwambĩĩa kũtatĩthya nũũ katĩ wa athũkũmi ma Ngai ũkatalwa yĩla ĩsavunĩ ya 144,000. [1]
4. Ethĩwa vaitonyeka tũkamanya masyĩtwa ma Aklĩsto onthe etĩkĩw'a mauta ala me kũũ nthĩ, vatonyeka ata 'tũkathi namo'?
4 Ethĩwa vaitonyeka tũkamanya masyĩtwa ma Aklĩsto onthe etĩkĩw'a mauta ala me kũũ nthĩ, vatonyeka ata malondu angĩ 'makathi namo'? Kwoona ũndũ wathani wa Nzekalia waĩtye ĩũlũ wa ala andũ ĩkũmi. Waĩtye kana andũ asu ĩkũmi 'makakwata mũthya wa ngũa ya mũndũ Mũyuti, makyasya, Nĩtũkũthi nenyu, nũndũ nĩtwĩw'ĩte kana Ngai e vamwe nenyu.' O na kau wathani ũsu ũwetete Mũyuti ũmwe, ũsyokete ũkatũmĩa ndeto "nenyu" kwonany'a Mũyuti ũsu ti mũndũ ũmwe. Kwoou no nginya Mũyuti ũsu ũwetetwe ethĩwe ne kĩkundi kya andũ na ti mũndũ ũmwe! Nũndũ wa ũu vai vata wa kũmanya kĩla Mũyuti, kana kĩla mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta, nĩ kana tũatĩanĩe nake. Vandũ va ũu twaĩle kũmanya kana asu nĩ kĩkundi na tũimakwata mbau me kĩkundi. O na vai vandũ Maandĩko matwĩkĩaa vinya tũatĩĩe mũndũ nũndũ Yesũ nĩwe Mũtongoi witũ.—Mt. 23:10.
ETĨKĨW'A MAUTA MAĨLE KWĨKUA ATA?
5. Nĩ ũkany'o wĩva etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩle kũsũanĩa mũno, na nĩkĩ maĩlĩte kwĩka ũu?
5 Aklĩsto onthe ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ maĩle kũsũanĩa kwa ũito ũkany'o ũla ũwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya 1 Akolintho 11:27-29. (Soma.) Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩtũtetheesya kũelewa ata? Yĩtũtetheesya kũelewa kana ethĩwa Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta ndasũvĩĩte ngwatanĩo yake vamwe na Yeova, ethĩwa aiya kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ũndũ vataĩle. (Aevl. 6:4-6; 10:26-29) Ũkany'o ũsu nũtetheeasya Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta malilikane kana mayambĩte kũkwata ĩtuvi yĩla mathĩtwe. Maĩlĩte kwĩthing'ĩĩsya kũthi 'mavikĩe ngoolu kwondũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũla meetĩwe ĩũlũ nĩ Ngai nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ.'—Avi. 3:13-16.
6. Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta maĩle kwĩkua ata?
6 Vaulo nĩwaveveeiwe aandĩkĩe Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ndeto ii: "Nĩngũmwĩsũva mũendae o ũndũ waĩle wĩtano ũla mweetiwe naw'o." Maĩlĩte kwĩka ũu ata? Vaulo aendeeie kwasya ũũ: "[Mũendae] na wĩnyivyo w'onthe na ũuu, na wũmĩĩsyo, mũkyũmĩanĩsya inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ nthĩnĩ wa wendo; mũkĩthing'ĩĩsya kũsũvĩa wĩw'ano ũmwe wa Veva wovanonĩ wa mũuo." (Aev. 4:1-3) Veva wa Yeova ũtetheeasya mũndũ ethĩwe na wĩnyivyo na ti ngathĩĩo. (Ako. 3:12) Nũndũ Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta methĩawa menyivĩtye, nĩmetĩkĩlaa kana ti lasima methĩwe manengetwe veva mwingangĩ kũthonoka ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. Mayonaa ta mesĩ maũndũ andũ angĩ matesa kũmanya kana ta mavuanĩw'e maũndũ mana, o na maitataa kwonethya andũ kana mo nĩ ta ma vata mbee wa ala angĩ. O na mayĩsa kwĩa mũndũ nambĩĩe kũya kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ nĩkwĩthĩwa atĩ meĩsilya nĩ ta mwĩtĩkĩsye mauta. Ĩndĩ nũndũ me na wĩnyivyo, nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana Yeova nĩwe ũnyuvaa nũũ ũkũmwĩtĩkĩsya mauta.
7, 8. Nĩ ũndũ mwaũ Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta mataĩle kwĩkwatya mekwe, na nĩkĩ?
7 O na kau nĩ ndaĩa ya mwanya kũthi ĩtunĩ, Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta mayĩthĩawa meteele kũnengwa ndaĩa ya mwanya nĩ ala angĩ. (Aev. 1:18, 19; soma Avilivi 2:2, 3.) Veva wa Yeova wakũsĩĩie kĩla ũmwe e weka. Andũ mayaatangaasĩwa kana Mũklĩsto mũna nĩwetĩkĩw'a mauta. Kwoou maiseng'aa moona andũ amwe mate kwĩtĩkĩla mĩtũkĩ kana mo nĩmetĩkĩw'e mauta. Vandũ va kũseng'a, nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana Maandĩko nĩmatũkanĩtye tũiketĩkĩle mĩtũkĩ ĩla mũndũ wasya atĩ Ngai nũmũnyuvĩte akwatĩĩe kĩanda kĩna kya mwanya. (Ũvu. 2:2) O na ĩla makomana na mũndũ ya mbee mayendaa kũmũtavya kana mo nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ti laisi wĩthĩe maitavya mũndũ kana mo nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩkwĩthĩwa mayendaa kwĩtũlya. O na mayĩkũnaa kĩthũi nũndũ wa ĩtuvi yĩla mathĩtwe.—1 Ako. 1:28, 29; soma 1 Akolintho 4:6-8.
8 O na ĩngĩ, Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta mayĩkuaa ta me kĩkundinĩ kya mwanya. Maimanthaa ala angĩ mekwasya me na wĩkwatyo ta ũsu woo nĩ kana methĩwe na ngwatanĩo ya mwanya kana maseũvye kĩkundi kyoo kya kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. (Aka. 1:15-17) Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ kwĩka ũu nĩkũtonya kũete mũaanĩko ikundinĩ na methĩwa maileana na veva mũtheu, nũndũ veva ũetae mũuo na ngwatanĩo.—Soma Alomi 16:17, 18.
WE WAĨLE KWĨKA ATA?
9. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa twĩ metho ũndũ tũkwosa ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? (Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Wendo 'Ndwĩkaa Ũndũ Ũtaĩle.'")
9 Waĩle kwosa ata Mũklĩsto ũĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ? Yesũ eeie amanyĩw'a make atĩĩ: "Inyw'onthe mwĩ ana ma ĩthe ũmwe." Ongeleeile kwasya atĩĩ: "O ũla ũkenenevya [akanyivw'a]; na o ũla ũkenyivya akanenevw'a." (Mt. 23:8-12) Kwoou ti ũndũ waĩle kũnenevya mũndũ o na ethĩwa nĩ mwana-a-asa wa Klĩsto. O na kau Mbivilia nĩtwĩkĩaa vinya twĩyĩelekany'e na mũĩkĩĩo wa atumĩa Aklĩsto, vai vandũ ĩtwĩaa nĩtũnenevye mũndũ o na wĩva wĩthĩe nĩ tawe mũtongoi witũ. (Aevl. 13:7) Nĩ w'o vyũ, Maandĩko nĩmawetete kana Aklĩsto amwe nĩmaĩle "kũnengwa ndaĩa nene." Ĩndĩ mayaĩle kũnengwa ndaĩa ĩsu nĩkwĩthĩwa atĩ nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta, ĩndĩ nũndũ "masilaa nesa" na "matethasya wĩa wa ĩla ndeto na wa kũmanyĩsya." (1 Tim. 5:17) Kwoou Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta no mew'e mate eanĩe ethĩwa andũ angĩ makamakathaa mũno ũndũ vataĩle kana makamosaa ta ma vata mũno ũndũ vataĩle. Kũthũkya ũvoo, no tũtume wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwa Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta kwĩkala menyivĩtye ethĩwa tũkamosaa ta ma vata mũno ũndũ vataĩle. (Alo. 12:3) Vai ũmwe witũ wenda kũlulutĩkya mwana-a-asa o na ũmwe wa Klĩsto!—Luka 17:2.
10. Ũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nũnengete etĩkĩw'a mauta ndaĩa?
10 Tũtonya kwonany'a ata nĩtũmanengete Aklĩsto ala Yeova ũnyuvĩte kũmetĩkĩsya mauta ndaĩa ĩla ĩmaĩlĩte? Nĩ kwa kũlea kũmakũlangya tũmakũlyo ĩũlũ wa ũndũ metĩkĩw'e mauta. Kwa kwĩka ũu nĩtwĩvathanaa na kwĩlikya maũndũnĩ matatũkonetye. (1 Ath. 4:11; 2 Ath. 3:11) Tũyaĩle kũsũanĩa kana ethĩwa mũndũ nĩ mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta, asyai make, mũka (mũũme), kana andũ make ma mũsyĩ o namo maĩle kwĩthĩwa me etĩkĩw'a mauta. Ĩla Yeova ũkũnyuva ũla ũkũmwĩtĩkĩsya mauta, ndasiasya ũndũ andũ maileny'e. (1 Ath. 2:12) O na tũyaĩle kũtindĩa kũkũlya kĩveti kana mũũme wa mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta ũndũ wĩw'aa asũanĩa kana akekala Nthĩ Nzaũ ate nake. Vandũ va kũkũlya makũlyo matonya kũũmĩsya andũ angĩ, ithyonthe nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana Yeova akakũnzũa ũvĩ wake na "kwĩanĩsya kwenda kwa kĩla kĩndũ kĩ thayũ."—Sav. 145:16.
11. Twĩsũvĩanaa na mũisyo wĩva ĩla tweevathana na kĩtei kya 'kwendeesya andũ'?
11 Kũkua Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte nĩkũtũsũvĩaa tũikakwatwe nĩ mũisyo ũtonya kũtũkwata tũteũmanya. Maandĩko matwĩĩte kana "ana-a-asa ma ũvũngũ" nĩmatonya kũlika kĩkundinĩ. (Aka. 2:4, 5; 1 Yoa. 2:19) Ana-a-asa asu ma ũvũngũ nĩmatonya kũvanga kana mo nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. O na eka ũu, Aklĩsto amwe etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩmatonya kũtia ũla mũĩkĩĩo. (Mt. 25:10-12; 2 Vet. 2:20, 21) Tweesũvĩa tũikalike kĩteinĩ kya 'kwendeesya andũ,' tũikakusw'a nĩ andũ ta asu tũtie ũla w'o, o na mũĩkĩĩo witũ ndũkonza atĩ nũndũ nĩtwoona Mũklĩsto wĩ nguma kana wĩthĩĩtwe e mũĩkĩĩku kwa ĩvinda ĩasa amũtia Yeova.—Yuta 16.
NĨTWAĨLE KŨTHĨNĨKA NŨNDŨ WA ŨTALO WA ALA MAĨSAA KĨMŨTŨ NA KŨNYW'A MBINYU?
12, 13. Nĩkĩ tũyaĩle kũthĩnĩka nũndũ wa ũtalo wa ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Yesũ?
12 Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ, ũtalo wa ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya kũlilikana kĩkw'ũ kya Klĩsto wĩthĩĩtwe ũyongeleka. Ĩndĩ wasianĩsya na myaka mingĩ yĩ navu ĩtina, ũtalo ũsu ũneekaa kũoleka. Kĩu nĩkyaĩle kũtuma tũthĩnĩka? Aiee. Ekai tũsũanĩe maũndũ amwe twaĩle kũlilikana.
13 "Mwĩaĩi [Yeova] nũmesĩ ala make." (2 Tim. 2:19) Kĩvathũkany'o na Yeova, ala meũtala ala maya kĩmũtũ na manyw'a mbinyu maitonya kũmanya vyũ naaũ ala anyuve. Amwe ala matalawa mekaa o kwĩsilya mo nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. O na amwe ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ĩtina nĩmesie kũeka. Namo angĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa na mathĩna ma kĩlĩko na ma ngoonĩ ala matumaa masũanĩa kana makasumbĩka vamwe na Klĩsto ĩtunĩ. Kwoou ũtalo wa ala maĩsaa kĩmũtũ na kũnyw'a mbinyu ti w'o ũtalo wa etĩkĩw'a mauta ala matiele kũũ nthĩ.
14. Mbivilia yaĩtye ata ĩũlũ wa ũtalo wa etĩkĩw'a mauta ala makethĩwa matiele ĩla thĩna mũnene ũkethĩwa ũyambĩĩa?
14 Etĩkĩw'a mauta makethĩwa kũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa nthĩ ĩla Yesũ ũkoka kũmombany'a mathi ĩtunĩ. Mbivilia nĩwetete ĩvinda yĩu ĩkasya kana Yesũ "akatũma alaĩka make na wasya mũnene wa soo, nao makoomban'ya ala anyuve make kuma ngalĩ inya sya iseve, kuma itulunĩ sya matu kũvika itulunĩ ila ingĩ syamo." (Mt. 24:31) Maandĩko nĩmawetie kana no etĩkĩw'a mauta avũthũ makethĩwa matiele kũũ nthĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo. (Ũvu. 12:17) Ĩndĩ Mbivilia ndĩwetete nĩmeana makethĩwa matiele ĩvinda yĩla thĩna mũnene ũkethĩwa ũyambĩĩa.
15, 16. Nĩ ũndũ mwaũ twaĩle kũmanya ĩũlũ wa ala 144,000 Yeova ũnyuvĩte?
15 Yeova nĩwe ũtusaa nĩ ĩndĩĩ ũkũnyuva Aklĩsto amwe matw'ĩke etĩkĩw'a mauta. (Alo. 8:28-30) Yeova ambĩĩie kũnyuva etĩkĩw'a mauta ĩtina wa Yesũ kũkw'a na kũthayũũka, na veonekana Aklĩsto onthe ma w'o ala maĩ ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa maĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu ya atũmwa kũvika mwambĩĩonĩ wa ĩvinda ya mũminũkĩlyo, andũ aingĩ ala maasyaa nĩ aatĩĩi ma Klĩsto maĩ Aklĩsto ma ũvũngũ, na nĩmo Yesũ wamaelekanilye na "ĩthaaa." Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, ĩvindanĩ yĩu Yeova nĩwaendeeie kwĩtĩkĩsya Aklĩsto amwe aĩkĩĩku mauta, na asu nĩmo Yesũ wamaelekanilye na "nganũ." (Mt. 13:24-30) O na ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo Yeova no ũendeee kũnyuva ala makeanĩsya yĩla ĩsavu ya etĩkĩw'a mauta 144,000. [2] Ethĩwa Yeova akatw'a kũnyuva amwe mũthyanĩ wa ĩvinda yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, ithyĩ twĩ aaũ twambĩĩe kwĩthĩwa na nzika ĩũlũ wa ũĩ wake? (Isa. 45:9; Nda. 4:35; soma Alomi 9:11, 16.) [3] Twaĩle kwĩthĩwa twĩ metho tũikeke ta ala athũkũmi manyungunyĩisye vwana woo ĩla moonie ũndũ weekana na ala mambĩĩe kũthũkũma saa 11.—Soma Mathayo 20:8-15.
16 Ti onthe me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ methĩawa me amwe ma ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ." (Mt. 24:45-47) O tondũ kweethĩawa ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, ũmũnthĩ Yeova na Yesũ matũmĩaa andũ avũthũ kũĩthya aingĩ. O na ĩngĩ, ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa no Aklĩsto avũthũ etĩkĩw'a mauta matũmĩiwe kũandĩka Maandĩko ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto. O ta ũu ũmũnthĩ, no Aklĩsto avũthũ etĩkĩw'a mauta manyuvĩtwe manengane "lĩu ĩvinda yaw'o."
17. Elesya kĩla weemanyĩsya ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ.
17 Maũndũ asu twaneenea matũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Matũmanyĩsya kana Yeova nĩwathĩte andũ mĩthĩnzĩo kũndũ kwĩlĩ. Ala maelekanĩtw'e na ũla Mũyuti amathĩte mũthĩnzĩo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, na ala maelekanĩtw'e na ala andũ ĩkũmi amathĩte thayũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. Ĩndĩ Yeova endaa onthe meanĩsye o maũndũ ala amwe, methĩwe me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ kana nĩ wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. No nginya onthe methĩwe na wĩnyivyo. No nginya onthe methĩwe na ngwatanĩo. No nginya ikundi isu syelĩ syĩkĩe kĩthito nĩ kana kwĩthĩwe na mũuo ikundinĩ. Kwoou o ũndũ mũthya ũthengeee, ekai ithyonthe tũtw'e kũthũkũma twĩ ĩĩthya yĩmwe yĩtongoew'e nĩ Klĩsto.
^ [1] (kalungu ka 3) Ĩandĩko ya Savuli 87:5, 6 yonanĩtye kana nĩvatonyeka ĩvinda yũkĩte tũkesa kũmanya masyĩtwa ma onthe ala makethĩwa maendie ĩtunĩ makasumbĩke na Yesũ.—Alo. 8:19.
^ [2] (kalungu ka 15) O na kau ĩandĩko ya Meko ma Atũmwa 2:33 yonanĩtye kana andũ metĩkĩaw'a veva mũtheu kwĩsĩla vala ve Yesũ, Yeova nĩwe ũtusaa naaũ ũkũnyuva.
^ [3] (kalungu ka 15) Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ, sisya kĩlungu kĩĩ "Makũlyo Kuma kwa Asomi Maitũ" ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 01/05/2007, ĩth. 30-31.
