translation:
"I speak to you, and also I will teach you who God is among you."—EZRA 8:23.
HEADLINE: 32, 31
1, 2. (a) What has Jehovah shown us about the importance of accurate knowledge? (b) What benefits do we experience from sound reasoning? (See accompanying article.)
JEHOVAH has kindly provided us with accurate knowledge. He showed this by saying: "While they were making preparations, I strengthened their hands, and I encouraged them, and I spoke to them, saying, 'I speak to you, and also I will teach you who God is among you.' " (Ezra 8:23) So those ten men, Christians along with others, appreciated the encouragement to "strengthen their hands" and to be able to say, "I speak to you, and also I will teach you who God is among you." It motivates us to associate with fellow Christians who are zealous in their ministry, or "Israel of God," knowing that Jehovah is supporting them.—Acts 6:16.
2 Jesus illustrated the importance of associating with God's people. He explained that his sheep belong to "one flock." This flock consists of "a great crowd" and "other sheep." He indicated that this flock is united as "one fold" and has "one shepherd." (Luke 12:32; John 10:16) Because there is unity within the flock, let us examine some questions: (1) Are other sheep actively identifying zealous ministers who are associated with the anointed ones? (2) Can the anointed ones benefit from further growth? (3) Will you take the initiative to get to know individual Kingdom proclaimers and share encouraging experiences with them? (4) Can we all strive to show appreciation for the spiritual maturity of our brothers and sisters? Let us now discuss these questions more fully.
LET US EXAMINE HOW TO IDENTIFY ZEALOUS MINISTERS
3. How can we determine whether someone is counted among the 144,000?
3 Are other sheep actively identifying zealous ministers who are associated with the anointed ones? The answer is yes. Why? Because an individual may have a modest station in life, yet he may be loyal and diligent in his service. That is why Satan misleads people by saying that "the Christ . . . will not come, or if he does come, he will not succeed." (Matt. 24:24) But Jehovah allows faithful Christians to identify those whom he has appointed to take the lead, so that no one deceives them. Remember that the faithful and discreet slave does not claim to be infallible, but Jehovah supports him in guiding the people and protects them from false teachings. It is therefore fitting that we imitate those who "carry on vigorously," as described at Revelation 2:10; 7:3, 14. By doing so, we demonstrate that we are determined to remain loyal during the time when the 144,000 are being sealed. [1]
4. How can we determine whether all other Christians are identified as belonging to the other sheep, and how can we 'keep on the watch'?
4 How can we determine whether all other Christians are identified as belonging to the other sheep, and how can we determine whether some are 'keeping on the watch'? Consider the case of Zechariah, who saw a vision of ten thousand foot soldiers. He saw that there were also ten thousand who 'were carrying a weapon of silver.' And just as Zechariah understood that this vision did not refer to only one man, neither should we understand the expression "you" as referring to only one person! Rather, "you" refers to a group of people, not to one individual! Therefore, we need to recognize each Christian, or each member of the anointed ones, individually. We should realize that they are part of a group and that we belong to that group. Also, the Scriptures teach us to address individuals directly, rather than speaking about them generally—as Jesus did.—Matt. 23:10.
ARE THE ANOINTED ONES STILL NEEDED?
5. Is it proper for the anointed ones to seek prominence, and why not?
5 All other Christians regularly commemorate the death of Jesus by partaking of the bread and wine at the Memorial, thus showing their appreciation for his sacrifice. But does this mean that they are seeking prominence? No, because an anointed Christian who maintains a close relationship with Jehovah continues to give priority to spiritual things and to partake of the bread and wine. (Eph. 6:4-6; 10:26-29) Such a one understands that the anointed ones are united and are working together toward a common goal. They strive to imitate the example set by Paul, who said: "Keep yourselves free from idolatry."—Acts 3:13-16.
6. Are the anointed ones still needed?
6 Paul wrote the following to the anointed Christians: "I commend you because you remember my instructions as I delivered them to you." Can we say the same about ourselves? Paul went on to urge them: "[Continue] making appeal to God through him, and with all the holy people, cultivate brotherly love; be mindful of hospitality." (Eph. 4:1-3) Jehovah's servants show love for others and are hospitable. (Acts 3:12) So even though there are fewer anointed Christians now than in times past, they continue to play an important role in helping us to remain steadfast and to strengthen our faith. Many of our brothers and sisters appreciate their help in understanding Bible truths and in refuting false teachings. And some may feel encouraged when they see a fellow believer partaking in the bread and wine at the Memorial, knowing that he too is loyal to Jehovah. In fact, those who have a close relationship with Jehovah will always seek to demonstrate their loyalty.
7, 8. Why do anointed Christians continue to serve, and what can we learn from them?
7 And just as a loving shepherd tends his sheep, anointed Christians continue to shepherd God's flock. (Eph. 1:18, 19; read Proverbs 2:2, 3.) Jehovah empowers each one of them to do so. Some may wonder whether Jesus Christ is still the only Shepherd. However, we can observe how certain elders lovingly care for the congregation. Loyal shepherds realize that the Scriptures teach us to support those who work hard among us and preside over us. (1 Thess. 5:12) And when dealing with someone who has stumbled, they strive to restore him, realizing that it pleases God to forgive repentant ones. It is therefore wise to cooperate with such restoration efforts rather than being quick to judge.—1 Acts 1:28, 29; read 1 Corinthians 4:6-8.
8 Moreover, anointed Christians demonstrate practical wisdom in their ministry. They often spend time preparing and thoughtfully choose publications to offer people. (Acts 1:15-17) Why? Because they want to help others come to an accurate knowledge of Bible truth and appreciate Jehovah. So let us imitate their fine example and zealously share in the ministry.—Read Romans 16:17, 18.
WHAT CAN WE DO TO IMITATE THEM?
9. How can we show that we value the privilege of associating with anointed Christians and learning from their exemplary faith?
(Consider the box "The Question 'What Does This Mean?'")
9 To what extent should a Christian associate with and learn from an anointed one? Jesus himself said: "Call no man Father." He explained this by saying: "Neither be called leaders; for there is only One Leader, namely, God." (Matt. 23:8-12) It is therefore appropriate to respect anointed brothers as spiritual men appointed by Christ, but we should not idolize them or become overly dependent on them. (Heb. 13:7) In fact, the Scriptures show that even apostles did not want to be viewed as being "above" their fellow believers. Rather, they wanted to be "fellow workers" and "helpers for your joy."—1 Tim. 5:17. It is because anointed Christians have been given special privileges that they are able to help many others spiritually, and it is vital that we support them in their efforts to do so. (Acts 12:3) Let each of us strive to encourage an anointed brother and a member of Christ's household!—Luke 17:2.
10. How can we determine whether someone is truly anointed?
10 Can we really know whether Jehovah is blessing a Christian to serve as an anointed one? We can do so by observing his conduct and seeing whether it aligns with Bible principles. By doing so, we will avoid being misled and becoming involved in something harmful. (1 Thess. 4:11; 2 Thess. 3:11) We should also consider whether the person lives modestly, works hard, and cares for his family. Jehovah values such qualities, and he does not approve of those who take advantage of others. (1 Thess. 2:12) And we should be cautious about giving financial assistance to anyone claiming to be anointed, especially if he seems unwilling to work or support himself. Those who are genuinely needy will appreciate any help we give, and we can be confident that Jehovah will bless our generosity and "satisfy the desire of every living thing."—Ps. 145:16.
11. How do we harmonize our view with the principle of 'making disciples'?
11 As Christians, we want to be guided by a modest spirit when considering whether someone is anointed. The scriptures warn us against "false prophets." (Acts 2:4, 5; 1 John 2:19) False prophets may claim to be anointed. But even genuine anointed Christians can sometimes make mistakes. (Matt. 25:10-12; 2 Pet. 2:20, 21) So we need to be careful about applying the label 'disciples,' avoiding being influenced by those who promote themselves, and remembering that our loyalty belongs to Christ and that we want to please Jehovah.—Judah 16.
SHOULD WE BE CONCERNED ABOUT THE LOYALTY OF OTHERS OR BE CONTENT AND TRUSTFUL?
12, 13. Why should we be concerned about the loyalty of others and be content and trustful in imitation of Jesus?
12 Over time, the loyalty of others and their contentment have been tested more and more, especially as we get closer to the conclusion. This trend will likely continue. What can help us remain steadfast? Let us examine some things we can do to maintain our loyalty.
13 "Jehovah knows those who belong to him." (2 Tim. 2:19) Put your confidence in Jehovah, and he will help you discern who is truly loyal and who is not. Some who appear loyal may actually be disfellowshipped. And some who are loyal and contented may stumble. However, we do not want to be influenced by the opinions of imperfect people who might cause division or discourage us from associating with fellow Christians. Therefore, the loyalty of others and their contentment is not the issue; rather, it is our own loyalty to God that matters.
14. How can we avoid being misled by false prophets who present themselves as belonging to the anointed class?
14 False prophets try to deceive us by misrepresenting what the Bible says about the anointed class, just as Satan tried to mislead Jesus. The Bible foretold that Jesus would gather his elect ones and send them off to a great gathering place, "like a man calling his domestics together," and they would separate the righteous from the wicked. (Matt. 24:31) The Scriptures also indicate that false prophets will attempt to imitate this arrangement. (Rev. 12:17) So the Bible warns us to be wary of anyone claiming to be part of the anointed class.
15, 16. What can we learn from the account of the 144,000 whom Jehovah has chosen?
15 Jehovah shows us what the anointed ones are like by means of illustrations. (Prov. 8:28-30) Jehovah used illustrations to show that Jesus would gather and cleanse the anointed ones, and he revealed that Christ would have loyal followers who would prove their faith during a time of trial. And just as weeds grow among the wheat until the harvest, many imitators will appear among the anointed ones, and Jesus will distinguish them with the expression "I do not know you." But Jehovah continues to identify the true anointed ones, and Jesus will say to them, "I approve you." (Matt. 13:24-30) Also, Jehovah keeps examining those making the claim to be among the 144,000 anointed ones. [2] How does Jehovah help us to discern who are truly part of the anointed class, and why should we be interested in this? (Isa. 45:9; Jer. 4:35; read Romans 9:11, 16.) [3] We need to be discerning so that we do not associate with those who misrepresent themselves, especially when they offer us something that seems too good to be true—like offering us more than a fair wage for an hour's work.—Read Matthew 20:8-15.
16 This is why we must be diligent in examining ourselves. (Matt. 24:45-47) Otherwise, we may find ourselves among those whom Jehovah and Jesus use others to correct. Moreover, the faithful slaves and Christ use the Scriptures to write accurate Christian publications. And because of this, the faithful slaves carefully examine "each publication."
17. The church understands each teaching.
17 What reasons do we have to be diligent in examining things? Because Jehovah has allowed many people to stumble, and also because the majority make mistakes when trying to understand the scriptures, and also because many people ten times over make errors in their thinking. For Jehovah sees whether we truly appreciate these things, whether they relate to understanding the scriptures or to remaining loyal. But let us not be careless. Let us not be negligent. Let us not allow our heart to become hardened, or to be misled by some influence. As time goes on, let us always strive to improve our discernment so that we can distinguish what is right from what is wrong, according to Christ's teachings.
^ [1] (paragraph 3) Psalm 87:5, 6 shows that we should remember that we need to know the names of all our brothers who are associated with Jesus.—Rev. 8:19.
^ [2] (paragraph 15) Also, Acts 2:33 shows that those who respond favorably will receive holy spirit from Jehovah, and he will prove them worthy.—Prov. 16:9.
^ [3] (paragraph 15) If you would like more information, see the article "Questions From Readers" in The Watchtower (Swahili) of 01/05/2007, pages 30-31.

text:
"Ndi na ũtanu ũngĩ mũnene ũvĩtũkĩte ũũ, ngĩw'a ũvoo wa syana syakwa ũndũ iendaa nthĩnĩ wa ũla w'o."—3 YOA. 4.
MBATHI: 41, 11
1, 2. (a) Nĩ thĩna wĩva syana ila syĩ ũeninĩ ikomanaa naw'o? (b) Twĩneenea makũlyo meva ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
JOSHUA aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩ mũnini natũmĩaa kĩthyomo kya asyai makwa ĩla twĩ mũsyĩ na ĩla twĩ maũmbanonĩ." Aendeee kwasya: "Ĩndĩ ĩla naendie sukulu nĩnambĩĩie kwenda kĩthyomo kya kũla twathamĩĩe. Vatavĩtĩte myaka mingĩ nambĩĩe kũtũmĩa kĩthyomo kĩu kĩ kyoka. Nũndũ wa ũu vai kĩndũ nakwatasya maũmbanonĩ, o na ndyeew'aa ndyenda kũatĩĩa syĩthĩo sya asyai makwa." Ti Joshua e weka ũkwatĩtwe nĩ thĩna ũsu.
2 Ũmũnthĩ andũ mbee wa 240,000,000 mekalaa kũndũ mataasyaĩwa. Ethĩwa wĩ mũsyai wĩkalaa ũeninĩ, ũtonya kũtetheesya ata syana syaku nesa vyũ syĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo ndũmu na Yeova, na 'iiendaa nthĩnĩ wa ũla w'o'? (3 Yoa. 4) Namo ala angĩ matonya kũtetheesya ata?
INYW'Ĩ ASYAI, ĨTHĨWAI NGELEKANY'O NZEO
3, 4. (a) Asyai matonya ata kwĩthĩwa me ngelekany'o nzeo? (b) Nĩ kyaũ asyai mataĩle kwĩkwatya syana imeke?
3 Asyai, ngelekany'o yenyu nĩ ya vata mũno ethĩwa nĩmũkwenda syana syenyu ikinyĩle nzĩanĩ ya thayũ. Syana syenyu syoona 'mũyamba kũmantha Ũsumbĩ,' ikeemanyĩsya kũmwĩkwatasya Yeova eanĩasye mavata masyo ma kĩla mũthenya. (Mt. 6:33, 34) Kwoou mũikasembany'e na malĩ. Mũiketĩkĩle syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ imũvate kwĩka maũndũ ma kĩ-veva. Ĩvathanei na makoani. Ĩkĩai kĩthito mũmwendeesye Yeova kwa kwĩmanthĩa "ũthwii ĩtunĩ" vandũ va kũmantha "ndaĩa ya andũ."—Soma Maliko 10:21, 22; Yoa. 12:43.
4 Mũikakwatane mũno nginya mwaĩwe nĩ mwanya wa kwĩthĩwa na syana syenyu. Ekai imanye kana kĩla kĩtonya kũmũtanĩthya nĩ kĩthito kyasyo kya kũmwendeesya Yeova mbee, ĩndĩ ti ndaĩa ya andũ kana malĩ ĩla itonya kwĩmanthĩa kana ikamũmanthĩa. Andũ aingĩ masũanĩaa kana syana nĩsyo syaĩle kũmantha malĩ nĩ kana ithũmũsye asyai. Mũklĩsto ndaĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni ta ũsu o na vanini. Nũseo mũkalilikana kana "syana ityaĩlwe nĩ kũmbanĩsya asyai, ĩndĩ asyai nĩmaĩlwe nĩ kũmbanĩsya syana."—2 Ako. 12:14.
ŨNDŨ ASYAI MŨTONYA KWĨKA ETHĨWA VE THĨNA WA KĨTHYOMO
5. Nĩkĩ asyai maĩle kũneenaa na syana syoo ĩũlũ wa Yeova?
5 O tondũ Mbivilia yathanie, andũ "kuma ithyomonĩ syonthe sya i mbaĩ" nĩmaendeee kũlika ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova. (Nzek. 8:23) Ĩndĩ thĩna wa kĩthyomo no ũtume vethĩwa ve vinya kũmanyĩsya syana syenyu ũw'o. Syana syenyu nĩsyo amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ala ma vata vyũ mũtonya kwĩthĩwa namo, nasyo 'syamũmanya' Yeova ikeethĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene. (Yoa. 17:3) Kwoou nĩ kana syana syaku syĩkĩe ndeto sya Yeova ngoonĩ, "ineenae ndeto isu" kĩla ĩvinda mwanya waumĩla.—Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 6:6, 7.
6. Syana syenyu itonya kũtetheka ata syeemanyĩsya kĩthyomo kyenyu? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 8.)
6 Nĩvatonyeka syana syenyu ikemanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya kũla mũthamĩĩe ĩla syĩ sukulu, kana ikemanyĩsya kuma kwa ala siũtindany'a namo kĩsionĩ. Ĩndĩ ikeemanyĩsya kĩthyomo kyenyu ethĩwa mũkakĩtũmĩaa mavinda maingĩ ĩla mũkũea ngewa nasyo. Syana syenyu nitonya kũneena nenyu mũkaeleanwa nesa ethĩwa nĩsyĩsĩ kĩthyomo ĩ kyenyu. O na eka ũu, kũmanyĩsya syana kĩthyomo kyenyu no kũitethye maũndũnĩ angĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, syana syeemanyĩsya kĩthyomo kyenyu vamwe na kĩthyomo kya kĩsio kĩla mũthamĩĩe niamũkaa kĩlĩko ikoĩvanga, na nĩsyĩthĩawa itonya kũeleanwa nesa na andũ ala angĩ. O na ĩngĩ, ũu no ũitetheesye kwongelanga ũthũkũmi wasyo. Kwasũanĩa ndeto sya Carolina, ũla asyai make nĩ ekali ma ũeninĩ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩndanĩaa mũno kwĩthĩwa kĩkundinĩ kĩtũmĩaa kĩthyomo kya asyai makwa." O na easya: "Ũndũ ũngĩ ũndanĩthasya nĩ kũtetheesya isionĩ ila syĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a."
7. Mũtonya kwĩka ata ethĩwa mũsyĩ ve na thĩna wa kĩthyomo?
7 O na ũu wĩ o vo, o ũndũ syana sya asyai ala me ũeninĩ iendeee kũmanyĩa kĩthyomo na syĩthĩo ila syeethĩa kũla asyai mathamĩĩa, now'o imwe itonya kũlwa kana ikasya mea ma kũtũmĩa kĩthyomo kya asyai masyo. Inyw'ĩ asyai, ethĩwa syana syenyu syĩ na thĩna ta ũsu, mwĩona ata mũkatata kwĩmanyĩsya ne inyw'ĩ kĩthyomo kĩla kĩtũmĩawa kũla mũĩ? Ethĩwa nĩmũkũeleanwa na syana syenyu ĩla mũkũea ngewa, mũkeethĩwa mũtonya kũitetheesya nesanga syĩthĩwe Aklĩsto aseo. O na mũkeethĩwa mũtonya kũitethya ethĩwa nĩmũkũelewa nesa syĩndũ ila syĩkwĩtanĩthya nasyo, ethĩwa nĩmũkũelewa inengetwe wĩa ũilyĩ ata sukulu, na ethĩwa nĩmũtonya kũea ngewa na alimũ masyo. Nĩ w'o kana kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩeni nĩkwendaa ĩvinda, kĩthito kingĩ, na nĩkwendaa wĩnyivyo. Ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa mwanau awaĩte matũ na aieka kwĩw'a, we ndwĩkĩa kĩthito wĩmanyĩsye kĩthyomo kya ala matew'aa nongi kana nũea ngewa nake? Kĩthito kĩu nokyo waĩle kwĩkĩa ethĩwa mwana waku aeleawa nesa kĩthyomo kĩngĩ we mũsyai ũtakĩsĩ nesa, kana ti w'o? *
8. Ũtonya kũtetheesya ata syana syaku ethĩwa ndwĩsĩ nesa kĩthyomo kĩla itũmĩaa?
8 Vate nzika, asyai amwe nĩmatonya kũemwa nĩ kwĩmanyĩsya nesa kĩthyomo kya kũla mathamĩĩe. Na kĩu no kĩtume wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wĩ vinya kwa asyai kũtetheesya syana syĩthĩwe na ũmanyi mwingĩ wa "maandĩko matheu." (2 Tim. 3:15) Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ kwaku, ndũkakw'e ngoo. Nũtonya kũtetheesya syana syaku imũmanye Yeova na iimwenda. Shan nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi na aĩtye ũũ: "Inyia witũ ndeesĩ nesa kĩthyomo kĩla twaeleawa nĩ na eĩtu-a-mwaitũ, naitũ tũyaneenaa nesa kĩthyomo kĩla kyake. Ĩndĩ kwona Mami ayĩmanyĩsya, aivoya, na aitata ũndũ ũtonya atongoesye ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ kĩla kyumwa, kwatumie tũmanya kana kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno."
9. Asyai matonya kũtetheesya ata syana ila itonya kwĩthĩwa na vata wa kwĩmanyĩsya na ithyomo ilĩ?
9 Syana imwe nitonya kũtetheka syamanyĩw'a ĩũlũ wa Yeova na kĩthyomo kĩla kya asyai masyo vamwe na kĩthyomo kĩla kĩtũmĩawa sukulu. Nĩ kana asyai amwe meanĩsye kĩu, matũmĩaa mavuku, vitio, na syĩndũ ingĩ ilekotiĩtwe sya ithyomo isu syelĩ. Vate nzika, ve vata wa asyai ala mekalaa ũeninĩ matũmĩe ĩvinda yingangĩ na mayĩkĩa kĩthito kingangĩ nĩ kana matetheesye syana syoo syĩthĩwe na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe na Yeova.
MWAĨLE KŨNYUVA KĨKUNDI KYA KĨTHYOMO KĨVA?
10. (a) Nũũ ũla waĩle kũtw'a kĩkundi kĩla mwaĩle kũthi? (b) Aĩle kwamba kwĩka ata ataneka ũtwi?
10 Ethĩwa "ekali ma ũeninĩ" mai vakuvĩ na Ngũsĩ ingĩ ineenaa kĩthyomo kyoo, maĩle kũthi maũmbano kĩkundinĩ kĩla kĩ vakuvĩ. (Sav. 146:9) Ĩndĩ twasye ve o kĩkundi kĩ ũkuvĩnĩ kĩtũmĩaa kĩthyomo kĩla inyw'ĩ asyai mwasyaiwe nakyo, ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Mũtonya kũtethekea kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kĩva? Mwene mũsyĩ aĩlĩte kwamba kũsũanĩa mũno na aivoya, na ĩndĩ aioany'a na mũka na syana atanamba kwĩka ũtwi. (1 Ako. 11:3) Nĩ maũndũ ta meva mwene mũsyĩ waĩle kũsũanĩa? Nĩ myolooto yĩva ĩtonya kũmũtetheesya? Eka twone ĩmwe.
11, 12. (a) Kĩthyomo kĩtonya ata kũtuma mwana atetheka nĩ maũmbano? (b) Nĩkĩ syana imwe itemanyĩasya kĩthyomo kya asyai masyo?
11 No nginya asyai masũanĩe nesa mavata ma syana syoo. O na vatw'ĩke vai thĩna wa kĩthyomo, mwana ndesa kũlũmya ũla w'o no ũndũ wa masaa manini ala ũmanyĩĩaw'a maũmbanonĩ kĩla kyumwa. Ĩndĩ kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Syana syathi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩthyomo ikũelewa nesa, nĩvatonyeka maũndũ ala syeew'a makalika ngoonĩ vyũ o na kwĩ ũndũ asyai meũsũanĩa. Ĩndĩ iyĩsa kũtetheka ũu ethĩwa iikũelewa nesa kĩthyomo kĩla kĩũtũmĩwa. (Soma 1 Akolintho 14:9, 11.) Na ti lasima kĩthyomo kĩla mwana wasyaiwe nakyo kĩkaendeea kwĩthĩwa nekyo kĩthyomo kĩla wĩsĩ na wendete. O na syana imwe no syumasye maelesyo, maũvoo, kana o ikekaa mawonany'o na kĩthyomo kya asyai masyo, ĩndĩ ũyĩthĩa kĩla iũweta o na kĩyumĩte ngoonĩ.
12 Ũndũ ũngĩ mwaĩle kũmanya nĩ kana ve maũndũ angĩ matonya kũkiita ngoo ya mwana ĩndĩ ti kĩthyomo kĩ kyoka. Ũla mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Joshua ũwetiwe mwambĩĩonĩ nĩweeyoneie ũndũ ũsu. Mwĩĩtu masyaanĩw'e wĩtawa Esther aĩtye atĩĩ: "Syana syonaa kĩthyomo kya asyai masyo o ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ syonaa syĩthĩo syoo, na ndĩni yoo." Syana ikethĩwa itendete kũatĩĩa syĩthĩo sya asyai masyo, nitonya kũlea kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kyoo, o na kwĩtĩkĩlana na mũĩkĩĩo woo. Kwoou mo asyai ala me ũeninĩ maĩle kwĩka ata?
13, 14. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie asyai amwe mekalaa ũeninĩ mathamĩĩa kĩkundi kya kĩthyomo kya kũu me na syana syoo? (b) Asyai asu meekaa ata nĩ kana malũlũmĩĩlye ngwatanĩo yoo na Yeova?
13 Asyai Aklĩsto mathĩnĩkĩaa mũno mavata ma kĩ-veva ma syana syoo vandũ va kũmantha kwĩuna ene. (1 Ako. 10:24) Samuel, ũla nĩwe ĩthe wa Joshua na Esther, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa nĩtwasyaisye syana sitũ nesa tũmanye nĩ kĩthyomo kĩva kĩtonya kũitethya iendeee nesa kĩ-veva, na ĩndĩ twavoya tũnengwe ũĩ. Ũsũngĩo ũla twakwatie waĩ kĩvathũkany'o na wendi witũ. Ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩtwoonie kana iitethekaa nĩ maũmbano ma kĩthyomo kitũ, nĩtwathamĩĩie kĩkundinĩ kĩngĩ kya kĩthyomo kya kũu. Nĩtwaendaa vamwe nasyo maũmbanonĩ na ũtavany'a tũte kũtĩĩa. O na nĩtwathokasya anyanyae maitũ kũu tũkaĩsanĩa na tũkai ndembea. Kwĩka maũndũ asu onthe nĩkwatetheeisye syana sitũ syamanyana na ana-a-asa na syeethĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, weethĩa syĩmwona ta Ngai wasyo, Ĩthe wasyo, na Mũnyanyae wasyo. Twatalile ũsu taw'o ũndũ ũla wesaa kũitethya mũno o na kwĩ kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kitũ."
14 Samuel ongeleele kwasya: "Nĩ kana nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa tũendeee kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, nĩtwasyokaa tũkathi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩthyomo kitũ. Tweethĩawa tũkwatene na twanoaa mũno. Ĩndĩ nĩtũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ nĩwaathimie kĩthito kitũ na kwĩyumya kwitũ. Yu syana sitũ syonthe syĩ itatũ syĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe."
KĨLA AMŨIKA MATONYA KWĨKA
15. Nĩkĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Kristina woonie ve vata wa kũthamĩĩa kĩkundi kya kĩthyomo kya kũla maĩ?
15 Syana syamina kwĩana no syĩthĩe itonya o kũmũthũkũma Yeova nesa syĩ kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kĩla syĩkũelewa nesa vyũ. Ikeka ũtwi ta ũsu, asyai mayaĩle kũsũanĩa kana nĩmo itekwenda. Kwasũanĩa ngewa ya Kristina. Aĩtye: "O na kau nĩneesĩ o vanini kĩthyomo kya asyai makwa, neew'aa kĩthyomo kĩla kyatũmĩawa maũmbanonĩ kĩ vinya vyũ." Aendeee kwasya: "Ĩvinda yĩmwe nĩ na myaka 12 nĩnaendie ũmbanonĩ mũnene wa kĩthyomo kĩla twatũmĩaa sukulu. Yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kũelewa kana kĩla kyamanyĩaw'a nĩkyo ũw'o. O na ĩvinda yĩngĩ neewie maũndũ maalyũka nĩ ĩla nambĩĩe kũvoya na kĩthyomo kĩla twatũmĩaa sukulu. Kuma vau naĩ ndonya kũneena na Yeova kuma ngoonĩ!" (Meko 2:11, 41) Kristina aima nĩwaneeneie ũndũ ũsu na asyai make, na atw'a kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kyatũmĩaa kĩthyomo kya kĩsio kĩla maĩ. Aĩtye: "Kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova na kĩthyomo kĩla natũmĩaa sukulu nĩkwatumie nĩka maendeeo." O na vatavĩtĩte ĩvinda ĩasa, Kristina nĩwoosie ũvainia wa kĩla ĩvinda na nũtanĩaa mũno ũthũkũmi ũsu.
16. Nĩkĩ mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Nadia ũtanaa nũndũ wa kũendeea kwĩkala kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kya asyai make?
16 Andũ ma mũika, nĩmũkwona ta ve vata wa kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kĩtũmĩaa kĩthyomo kya kĩsio kĩla mũĩ? Ethĩwa wĩona ũu, kwekũlye nĩ kyaũ kĩũtuma wenda kũthama. Wĩenda kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kĩu kĩngĩ nũndũ wa ngwatanĩo yaku na Yeova? (Yak. 4:8) Kana wĩthĩwa ũyenda kũthama nũndũ ndũkwenda kũtinda ũisungwa kana ndũkwenda kwĩnosya? Nadia, ũla yu ũthũkũmaa Mbetheli, aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩ na syana ila tũsyaanĩw'e twakililye twavĩtũkya myaka 13, twambĩĩa kwenda kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kya kĩthyomo kya kĩsio kĩla twaĩ." Ĩndĩ asyai make nĩmeesĩ kana kũthamĩĩa kĩkundinĩ kĩu kũyaĩ kũtethya syana isu ilũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yasyo vamwe na Yeova. Nadia easya: "Yu nĩtũtũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ wa kĩthito kĩla asyai maitũ meekĩie nĩ kana matũmanyĩsye kĩthyomo kyoo, na nũndũ mayaaĩtĩkĩla tume kĩkundinĩ kĩu kya kĩthyomo kyoo. Ũndũ ũsu nũtũtethetye mũno thayũnĩ na ũkatũvingũĩa myanya mingĩ ya kũtetheesya angĩ mamũmanye Yeova."
ŨNDŨ ALA ANGĨ MATONYA KŨTETHEESYA
17. (a) Yeova anengete aaũ kĩanda kya kũea syana? (b) Asyai matonya kumya ũtethyo va ĩla mekũmanyĩsya syana syoo ũw'o?
17 Yeova anengete asyai kĩanda kya kũea syana na kũimanyĩsya ũla w'o, ĩndĩ ti aa-ũmae kana aa-ũsũe kana andũ angĩ. (Soma Nthimo 1:8; 31:10, 27, 28.) Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, asyai ala matesĩ kĩthyomo kĩla syana ieleawa nesa nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa na vata wa kũtetheew'a nĩ kana mavikie ngoo syasyo. Kũkũlya ũtethyo ta ũsu ti kwonany'a kana maikwenda kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩla manengetwe, ĩndĩ no matale kwĩka ũu ta nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũea syana syoo "na mosilĩlo na motao ma Mwĩaĩi." (Aev. 6:4) Kwa ngelekany'o, asyai nĩmatonya kũkũlya atumĩa motao ĩũlũ wa kũtongoesya ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ, o na no mamakũlye mamatetheesye kũmanthĩa syana syoo atindany'a aseo.
18, 19. (a) Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala aima kĩ-veva matonya kũtetheesya amũika ata? (b) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva asyai mataĩle kũeka kwĩka?
18 Kwa ngelekany'o, mavinda kwa mavinda asyai no mathokye Aklĩsto angĩ na mĩsyĩ yoo methĩwe namo ĩla mekwĩka ũthaithi woo wa mũsyĩ. O na ĩngĩ, kĩtindo kya amũika vamwe na Aklĩsto aima kĩ-veva nĩkĩmatetheeasya mũno makeka maendeeo, ta kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mathi ĩmwe ũtavany'a, kana ĩla me ĩmwe mayĩtanĩthya. (Nth. 27:17) Ũla mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Shan ũwetiwe navu ĩtina aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ndyamba kũlwa nĩ ana-a-asa ala mandetheeisye. Neemanyĩasya maũndũ maingĩ mũno ĩla meũndetheesya kwĩyũmbanĩsya maũvoo ala nanengwa. Na nĩnatanĩaa mũno kĩtindo kyoo ĩla tũkwĩka o maũndũ maitũ."
19 Ala manyuvwa nĩ asyai matetheesye syana syoo maĩle kũitetheesya inenge asyai masyo ndaĩa kĩla ĩvinda, ĩndĩ mayaĩle kumany'a asyai asu kana kwĩyosea kĩanda kyoo. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana, ĩla me na syana isu mayaĩle kwĩka maũndũ matonya kũtuma angĩ kĩkundinĩ kana nza wa kĩkundi mambĩĩa kwĩkũlya makũlyo. (1 Vet. 2:12) Asyai mayaĩle kũekea angĩ vyũ kĩanda kyoo kya kũmanyĩsya syana ũla w'o. No nginya mekalae mesĩ kĩla syana syoo iũmanyĩw'a nĩ ala meũmatetheesya, na o namo ene mayaĩlĩte kũeka kũimanyĩsya.
20. Asyai matonya kũtetheesya ata syana syoo syĩthĩwe athũkũmi aseo ma Yeova?
20 Inyw'ĩ asyai, voyai Yeova amũtetheesye na mũitata vala mũtonya. (Soma 2 Mavinda 15:7.) Ambai kũsisya kĩla kĩtonya kũtuma syana syenyu syĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova mũtanamba kũsũanĩa wendi wenyu ene. Ĩkai kyonthe kĩla mũtonya nĩ kana mũĩkĩĩthye Ndeto ya Ngai nĩyalika ngoonĩ ya syana syenyu. Mũikaaĩse kũsũanĩa o na ĩmwe kana mwana wenyu ndatw'ĩka mũthũkũmi mũseo wa Yeova. Syana syenyu syaatĩĩa Ndeto ya Ngai na ngelekany'o yenyu nzeo, mũkeethĩwa mũtonya kwasya o tondũ mũtũmwa Yoana waisye ĩũlũ wa syana syake sya kĩ-veva. Aisye: "Ndi na ũtanu ũngĩ mũnene ũvĩtũkĩte ũũ, ngĩw'a ũvoo wa syana syakwa ũndũ iendaa nthĩnĩ wa ũla w'o."—3 Yoa. 4.
^ kal. 7 Sisya kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, "Unaweza Kujifunza Lugha Nyingine!," ĩkasetinĩ ya Amkeni! ya Mwei wa 3, 2007, ĩth. 10-12.

translation:
"And I saw another great throne, white; and He who sat on it had a rainbow around the throne."—3 JOHN 4.
BATHI: 41, 11
1, 2. (a) What can help young ones to remain loyal despite peer pressure? (b) What benefits do we gain from meditating on Bible verses?
JOSHUA said: "It helped me to use the scriptures when talking to my friends, both those who are friendly and those who are not." He continued: "When I went to school, I would make it a point to use the scriptures. After many years, I still make it a habit to use them. Because of this practice, I have been able to maintain friendships, and I am also able to defend my beliefs to my friends." Truly, Joshua has found a valuable way to stay strong.
2 Nearly 240,000,000 people attend schools worldwide. However, many young people find it difficult to remain loyal to God despite pressure from their peers, and how does Jehovah view such loyalty—as 'walking in the truth'? (3 John 4) And what can help young ones to resist negative influences?
SHOW LOYALTY BY YOUR ACTIONS
3, 4. (a) How can young ones show loyalty by their actions? (b) Why should young ones be careful about the company they keep?
3 Young ones, your example is powerful. By prioritizing spiritual activities, you demonstrate to others that you value Jehovah. Your willingness to 'seek first the Kingdom,' shows that you are serious about pleasing Jehovah and living according to his standards. (Matt. 6:33, 34) Be selective about your associations. Avoid bad habits and questionable entertainment. Stay busy in meaningful activities. Share your faith with others. Demonstrate your love for Jehovah by striving to apply "the wisdom from above," rather than "the wisdom of the world."—Read Mark 10:21, 22; John 12:43.
4 Make good use of opportunities to discuss spiritual things with your family. Help them see that putting Jehovah first is more important than material possessions or hobbies. Many young people realize that money and pleasure cannot bring lasting happiness. A Christian should be willing to give up personal interests to please Jehovah and to support his parents. So do not hesitate to say, "My friendship with Jehovah is more important than my friendship with anyone else."—2 Cor. 12:14.
WHAT YOUNG PEOPLE CAN DO TO REMAIN SPIRITUALLY STRONG
5 How can young ones maintain their zeal for serving Jehovah?
5 The Bible encourages us to associate with those who "love righteousness." (Ps. 8:23) Good friends will help you stay focused on spiritual pursuits. Your peers may not understand why you prioritize Bible study and meetings, but they can learn to respect your decisions. Strive to know Jehovah better and strengthen your relationship with him through prayer and meditation. (John 17:3) Be determined to live by Jehovah's standards, saying, "I want to obey God's laws" at all times.—Read Proverbs 6:6, 7.
6 Can your family be helped to appreciate your spirituality? (See paragraph 8.)
6 Perhaps you can help your family see the value of attending school regularly or being honest and trustworthy. By setting a fine example, you can influence them for good. Young ones often enjoy talking about what they are learning with their parents. Also, sharing your faith with your family can lead to positive results. For instance, when young people discuss their beliefs with their classmates, it can spark interest and open the way for further discussion. It also gives you an opportunity to practice expressing yourself clearly. As an example, a young woman named Carolina said: "I made it a point to talk about my faith with my relatives." And she added: "What really touched me was seeing how much my grandmother appreciated it."
7 What if you face opposition from others?
7 But even if you do, remember that many young people who come from families where the Bible is not valued still manage to maintain their own faith, and some may even be motivated to learn more. Consider this: If your classmates don't have anyone at home to support their education, would you offer to study with them? It is important to set a fine example for your younger siblings, encouraging them to live up to Christian standards. And encourage them to speak honestly, even when it means going against the crowd, and to take pride in their accomplishments. Don't think that sharing your knowledge will cause problems; rather, it will bring benefits. I once met a brother who visited his aunt and uncle, and he wondered whether he should share what he had learned with them. He asked himself: "Would it be helpful for my aunt to understand something new, or would it just upset her?" *
8 Can you help your family members appreciate the value of Bible study?
8 Of course, some parents want their children to succeed academically. They feel that a good education will give their children opportunities they themselves did not have. However, they may also worry about their children being influenced by bad associations and exposed to "worldly wisdom." (2 Timothy 3:15) This is understandable. So how can you help your family members to know Jehovah and to walk with him? One elder explained: "We try to teach our children that what we learn from the Bible is valuable, and we discuss it openly with them. We also encourage our wife to research, investigate, and find ways to apply what she learns to everyday life, so that we can all grow in our understanding of Jehovah's will."
9 Can young ones help their parents appreciate the value of learning, even if their parents are not interested in spiritual things?
9 Some young people can share what they are learning about Jehovah and his requirements with their parents, as well as what they are taught at school. Perhaps they could use illustrations, examples, and other practical aids to explain important principles. Of course, parents who are not Jehovah's Witnesses may still be skeptical. But when young ones show genuine interest and demonstrate that their faith strengthens their desire to please Jehovah, it may move their parents to examine matters more closely.
WHERE CAN YOU FIND HELP TO IMPROVE YOUR STUDY SKILLS?
10. (a) What resources are available to help us improve our study skills? (b) How can we benefit from these resources?
10 The brochure "Study Skills" offers practical suggestions, and many congregations organize classes on this topic. (Prov. 146:9) We want to help each student to make good use of the tools available to him, so ask yourself: 'Can I share what I am learning with others?' A parent might be willing to listen if his child shows that he is applying Bible principles in his life and that these principles have helped him to become a more responsible person. (1 Cor. 11:3) What obstacles might prevent a parent from listening? What specific assistance can you offer? Let us now consider some ways to help.
11, 12. (a) What can motivate a young person to study diligently? (b) What can young ones do to show their parents that they value Bible teachings?
11 Often young people respond well when given encouragement. Also, we can point out the benefits of studying—that it will help them to succeed in school and prepare them for life. But a parent may need to see that the young person is actually putting what he learns into practice. For example, a young person who studies Bible principles regularly will likely demonstrate improved conduct and will be able to explain those principles clearly. So encourage the student to apply what he is learning. (Read 1 Corinthians 14:9, 11.) And remember that each student learns differently. Some students learn best by reading material over and over, while others benefit from discussions or demonstrations. If a young one seems unsure about how to apply Bible teachings, help him to relate them to everyday situations.
12 One way to determine this is to observe whether the young person is willing to obey his parents, for obedience is often an indication of spiritual maturity. A young brother named Joshua found this to be true. A sister named Esther said: "When young people respect their parents and listen to their counsel, it shows that they value God's standards." A student who strives to please his parents is more likely to be receptive to Bible instruction and to cooperate with Jehovah. But what if a young person does not seem interested in spiritual things?
13, 14. (a) What might cause some young people to resist parental guidance and the direction of God's organization? (b) How can parents strengthen their relationship with Jehovah?
13 Many Christian youths face strong peer pressure. (1 Cor. 15:33) Samuel, Joshua's and Esther's father, observed: "I have noticed that when young people do not know how to respond to situations, they tend to look to their peers for guidance. It is important for us to help them see that submitting to godly principles will benefit them. We need to reason with them and show them why our advice is loving. And we should pray that they will make good decisions. By doing so, we demonstrate that we trust in Jehovah and want what is best for our children. We also show that we are willing to work alongside them to help them apply Bible principles. Furthermore, we can reassure them that we love them unconditionally and that our desire is to see them develop a close relationship with Jehovah, recognizing him as their God, their Father, and their Friend. Let us continue to do everything we can to help our children grow spiritually and to remain loyal to Jehovah."
14 Samuel went on to say: "I am confident that if we continue to seek Jehovah's guidance, we will be able to help our children navigate the challenges they face. We need to spend time with them and get to know them well. Then we can support them and encourage them. But most importantly, we must teach them to love Jehovah and to appreciate his standards. May all of us strive to raise our children to become mature Christians who will serve Jehovah whole-souled."
WHAT WILL HELP THEM TO STAND FIRM
15. What helped young Kristina to resist pressure from her peers to join a worldly group?
15 Young people often find it hard to resist peer pressure, especially when it comes to things they do not fully understand. However, if you train your heart, you may be able to cope. Consider Kristina's experience. She says: "At first I was afraid to associate with those who were not interested in spiritual things, because I feared that their bad influence would affect me." She continues: "One girl was 12 years old and she began bringing worldly literature to school. That is how I learned about some of the things that young people do. And many others started talking about exciting things that they did at school. But I remembered what I had been taught about keeping company with good associates." (Proverbs 2:11, 41) Kristina spoke to her parents about this, and they encouraged her to choose good friends. She says: "By learning to love Jehovah and by remembering what I had been taught at school, I was able to stay firm." And even though she was very young, Kristina showed discernment and made wise decisions.
16. What helped a young sister named Nadia to stick to her resolve to maintain her spirituality?
16 Brothers and sisters, how can we strengthen our resolve to remain spiritual? Think about this: Is there something that tempts you to compromise? Are you willing to strengthen your relationship with Jehovah? (James 4:8) Or do you feel inclined to give in to temptation or to become self-sufficient? Nadia, who serves at Bethel, explains: "I had a strong desire to please my parents, but when I was about 13 years old, we felt compelled to start associating with those who were not interested in spiritual things." Her parents realized that associating with such ones could hinder her close relationship with Jehovah. Nadia adds: "We quickly noticed that we were losing interest in spiritual activities and that we were becoming more concerned with what others thought of us. This caused us to realize how important it is to choose our companions carefully and to avoid those who might lead us astray from Jehovah."
OTHER WAYS TO STAY STRONG
17. (a) How does Jehovah view raising children? (b) What practical help is available to parents who want to raise their children spiritually?
17 Jehovah encourages parents to bring up their children in discipline and mental adjustment, regardless of whether they are sons or daughters or others. (Read Proverbs 1:8; 31:10, 27, 28.) Also, remember that even experienced parents may need help in teaching their children sound principles and coping with challenges. It is wise to seek counsel and not assume that you already know everything. In fact, being willing to learn is one way to show respect for "the instruction and the discipline of wisdom." (Proverbs 6:4) For example, parents may find it helpful to use tools to teach their children about Bible history, and they may also benefit from discussing ways to train their children to be obedient.
18, 19. (a) What qualities in both parents and children contribute to a peaceful home? (b) Why is it vital for parents to set boundaries?
18 For instance, often children respond well when parents lovingly correct them and give them reasons for doing so. Moreover, a key factor in maintaining peace is treating each child as an individual—recognizing that some may be more sensitive than others, or that some may have certain weaknesses. (Proverbs 27:17) The experience of a sister named Shannon illustrates this point: "I struggled with my teenage children. I tried to understand what was bothering them. And I made an effort to appreciate their good qualities."
19 Many parents find that consistent discipline is effective, while others feel that a more flexible approach works better. Either way, it is important to help children learn self-control and to teach them how to deal with peer pressure. It is also vital to avoid being overly strict or lenient. (1 Corinthians 2:12) Parents should strive to create a loving atmosphere in which children feel safe to express themselves, knowing they will be listened to and understood.
20. What can parents do to help their children remain loyal to Jehovah?
20 Pray to Jehovah for guidance and strength. (Read 2 Chronicles 15:7.) By consistently setting a good example and encouraging your children to put Jehovah first, you can help them develop a strong relationship with him. Remember that every opportunity to teach your children about God's law is valuable. Strive to discuss spiritual matters with them regularly, both at home and elsewhere. Your children will appreciate your genuine interest in their spiritual well-being, and they will likely imitate your faith, just as John the Baptist imitated his father Zechariah's faith. He said: "I owe this great privilege to my father."—3 John 4.
^ par. 7 See the article "You Can Learn Another Language!," The Watchtower of March 2007, pages 10-12.

text:
"Ninyie Yeova Ngai waku, ũla ũkũmanyĩasya kwaĩla."—ISA. 48:17.
MBATHI: 20, 37
1, 2. (a) Ngũsĩ sya Yeova imyosaa Mbivilia ata? (b) Nĩ mĩsoa yĩva we wendete?
ITHYĨ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩtwendete Mbivilia. Nĩyo ĩnenganae ũtao wa kwĩkwatw'a na nĩtũkiakiasya na ĩkatũnenga wĩkwatyo. (Alo. 15:4) Ithyĩ tũimyosaa Mbivilia ta ĩvuku yusũĩte mawoni ma andũ, ĩndĩ "o ũndũ ĩtilyĩ w'o, ndeto ya Ngai."—1 Ath. 2:13.
2 Vate nzika, ithyonthe twĩ mĩsoa ĩla twendete. Amwe mendete mũno ala Mavuku ma Ũvoo Mũseo, nĩkwĩthĩwa maeleetye nesa ũndũ Yesũ ũilyĩ nginya makatuma twona nesa vyũ ũndũ Yeova ũseũvĩte. (Yoa. 14:9) Namo angĩ mendete mavuku ala maneeneete wathani. Kwa ngelekany'o, amwe nĩmendete ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo nũndũ yĩwetete "maũndũ ala matatĩa kwĩkĩka mĩtũkĩ." (Ũvu. 1:1) Na ĩndĩ we nũũ ũtaakiakiw'a nĩ ĩvuku ya Savuli, kana nũũ ũtaatethw'a nĩ ĩvuku ya Nthimo? Nĩ w'o vyũ, vai mũndũ ũtatethw'a nĩ Mbivilia.
3, 4. (a) Twĩthĩawa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa mavuku maitũ? (b) Nĩ maũvoo meva tũkwataa methĩawa maandĩkĩwe andũ ma mũthemba mũna?
3 Kwenda Mbivilia nĩkũtumaa twenda mavuku maitũ, nũndũ methĩawa na ũvoo wumĩte ĩ Mbivilianĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo ĩla tũũsoma maũvoo ala me mavukunĩ, mbulosuanĩ, makasetinĩ, na tũvukunĩ tũngĩ. Nĩtwĩthĩawa twĩsĩ kana syĩndũ isu Yeova ũtũnengete nĩsyo itumaa twĩkala metho kĩ-veva, tũkwata lĩu ũla twĩ na vata naw'o, na twĩkala twĩ "aima mũĩkĩĩonĩ."—Tito 2:2.
4 Eka maũvoo ala methĩawa maandĩkĩwe Ngũsĩ sya Yeova syonthe, nĩtũkwataa maũvoo angĩ o maumanĩte na Mbivilia ĩndĩ maandĩkĩwe andũ ma mũthemba mũna. Kwa ngelekany'o, maũvoo amwe methĩawa maandĩkĩwe mũno mũno amũika, namo angĩ methĩawa maandĩkĩwe asyai moo. Naw'o ũvoo mwingĩ ũla ũtumbĩthĩtw'e kana wĩkĩĩtwe kĩsesenĩ kitũ mũno mũno wĩthĩawa ũandĩkĩwe ala mate Ngũsĩ. Lĩu ũsu wingĩvĩte ũu wa kĩ-veva ũtũlilikanasya kana Yeova nĩwĩanĩĩtye ũla watho wake wathanie kana "akavokea ngo syonthe sya andũ mboka ya syĩndũ nou."—Isa. 25:6.
5. Yeova ew'aa mũyo oona tũyĩka ata?
5 Nĩ laisi mũno ũkethĩa aingĩ maitũ twĩkũlasya takeka twĩ na ĩvinda yingĩ ya kũsoma Mbivilia vamwe na mavuku ala angĩ maitũ. Ĩndĩ vai nzika kana Yeova nĩwĩw'aa mũyo oona kĩthito kĩla twĩ nakyo kya 'kũtangĩĩa ĩvinda' yitũ nĩ kana tũkwate mwanya wa kũsoma Mbivilia kĩla mũthenya na kwĩmanyĩsya. (Aev. 5:15, 16) O na vailyĩ oou, no kwĩthĩwa ve maũvoo amwe tũtũmĩaa kavinda kanini tũimasoma namo angĩ tũitũmĩa ĩvinda yingĩ. Ĩndĩ kĩu no kĩtũlikye mũisyonĩ tũteũmanya. Mũisyo wĩva?
6. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtuma tũvĩtwa nĩ ũndũ wĩĩ ũtonya kũtũtethya ũvoonĩ mũna?
6 Mũisyo ũla ũtonya kũtũkwata nĩ ũũ: Tũkambĩĩa kwona maũvoo mana maitũkonetye, nĩ laisi tũkavĩtwa nĩ maũndũ matonya kũtũtethya. Kwa ngelekany'o, nata ũkasoma Mbivilianĩ vandũ vawetete maũndũ mataakũkwata? Kana nata ũkakwata ĩvuku na ũyĩthĩa mũno mũno yĩandĩkĩwe andũ angĩ eka we? Mavindanĩ ta asu we ũsomaa maũvoo asu ũsembethetye kana wĩkaa kũvanga ndwĩmasoma o na vanini? Tũkethĩwa twĩkaa ũu, twĩthĩwa tũyĩvata ũvoo ũtonya kũtũtethya vyũ. Kwoou kyo nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũikese kwĩlikya mũisyonĩ ũsu? Kĩndũ kĩla kya mbee vyũ nĩ kũmanya kana Ngai nĩwe wĩthĩawa aumanĩte na lĩu w'onthe wa kĩ-veva ũla tũkwataa. Ngai mwene atũmie mwathani Isaia awete ndeto ii: "Ninyie Yeova Ngai waku, ũla ũkũmanyĩasya kwaĩla." (Isa. 48:17) Kwondũ wa ũu, ĩsomo yĩĩ yĩneeneete maũndũ atatũ matonya kũtũtetheesya tũtetheke ĩla tũũsoma kĩlungu o na kĩva kya Mbivilia kana mũthemba o na wĩva wa maũvoo ala tũkwataa.
MAŨNDŨ MANA MATONYA KŨŨTETHEESYA ĨLA ŨŨSOMA MBIVILIA
7. Nĩkĩ ĩla tũũsoma Mbivilia twaĩle kũmĩsoma twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kwĩmanyĩsya kĩndũ?
7 Soma wĩ na kĩeleelo kya kwĩmanyĩsya kĩndũ. Mbivilia ĩwetete nesa ĩkasya kana 'kĩla Ũandĩko nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai, naw'o nĩwaĩle.' (2 Tim. 3:16) Nĩ w'o kana ilungu imwe sya Mbivilia syaandĩkĩwe mũndũ mũna kana kĩkundi kĩna kya andũ. Kyu nĩkyo kĩtumi ĩla tũũsoma Maandĩko twaĩle kũmasoma twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kwĩmanyĩsya kĩndũ. Mwana-a-asa ũmwe aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩla ngũsoma Mbivilia nĩlilikanasya kana ve maũndũ maingĩ ndonya kwĩmanyĩsya kĩlungunĩ kĩna." Ongelile kwasya: "Kwĩlilikany'a ũu kũtumaa nenda kũsisya nĩ ĩsomo yĩva yĩvithanĩtye kĩlungunĩ kĩu." Kwoou nũseo tũtanambĩĩa kũsoma Ndeto ya Ngai tũkamũvoya atũtetheesye tũsome twĩ na kĩeleelo kya kwĩmanyĩsya kĩndũ, na aitũnenga ũĩ wa kwona kĩla we ũkwenda twĩmanyĩsye.—Esa. 7:10; soma Yakovo 1:5.
8, 9. (a) Nĩ makũlyo ta meva tũtonya kwĩkũlya ĩla tũkwetye kũsoma Mbivilia? (b) Twĩmanyĩasya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova ĩla twasoma nguma ila waĩtye no nginya atumĩa ma kĩkundi methĩwe nasyo?
8 Ĩkũlye makũlyo. Ĩla ũendeee kũsoma kĩlungu kĩna kya Mbivilia, ambaa kwosa ĩvinda ũkekũlya makũlyo ta aa: 'Ũvoo ũũ wĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova? Ndonya kũtũmĩa ũvoo ũũ ata? Ndonya kũtetheesya angĩ ata ngĩtũmĩa ũvoo ũũ?' Ĩla twekũlya makũlyo ta asu, tũilea kwĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ kĩlungunĩ kĩla tũũsoma. Kwaekai twone ngelekany'o ĩmwe. Maandĩko nĩmawetete nguma ila mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi waĩle kwĩthĩwa nasyo. (Soma 1 Timotheo 3:2-7.) Nĩkwĩthĩwa aingĩ maitũ tũi atumĩa, nĩvatonyeka ĩla twavika ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu twonaa ta yĩtesa kũtũtethya mũno. Ĩndĩ kwaekai twone mosũngĩo amwe tũtonya kũkwata twekũlya makũlyo aa maatĩĩe. Kwĩka ũu nĩkũũtũtetheesya twone kana kwĩthĩwa na nguma ila iwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu no kũtũune ithyonthe maũndũnĩ maingĩ.
9 Ũvoo ũũ wĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa Yeova? Ĩla Yeova wawetie nguma ila syĩ ĩandĩkonĩ yĩu, oonanisye kana nũandũaa maũndũ maingangĩ kuma kwa ala manengetwe ianda. Endaa mekale me ngelekany'o nzeo kwa ala angĩ, na nũkamasilĩla kwosana na ũndũ makuaa kĩkundi, nĩkwĩthĩwa 'akĩthooete na nthakame ya Mwana wake.' (Meko 20:28, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana Yeova endaa twĩkale twĩ eanĩe ĩla maendeee kũtũsũvĩa. (Isa. 32:1, 2) Kwoou wasũanĩa maũndũ asu onthe, nũkwona kana kũsoma ĩũlũ wa nguma ila Yeova wendaa atumĩa ma kĩkundi methĩwe nasyo kũtumaa tũlilikana ũndũ we mwene ũtwendete mũno wĩana.
10, 11. (a) Kũsoma nguma ila Maandĩko maĩtye no nginya atumĩa ma kĩkundi methĩwe nasyo kũtonya kũtũtethya ata? (b) Tũtonya kũtetheesya angĩ ata tũitũmĩa ũvoo ũsu?
10 Ndonya kũtũmĩa ũvoo ũũ ata? Ĩvinda kwa ĩvinda mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi nĩwaĩle kwĩthiana aitũmĩa yĩla ĩandĩko nĩ kana amanye ethĩwa ve nguma imwe ũte nasyo waĩlĩte kwĩkĩa kĩthito ethĩwe nasyo. O nake mwana-a-asa ũla 'ũkwenda wĩa wa mũsyaĩĩsya' nĩwaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa ĩandĩko yĩu, nĩkwĩthĩwa o nake aĩlĩte kũtata ũndũ ũtonya ethĩwe na nguma isu. (1 Tim. 3:1) Na eka ũu, vai Mũklĩsto ũtemanyĩsya kĩndũ asoma mĩsoa ĩsu nũndũ mbingĩ sya nguma ila iwetetwe vau no itũtetheesye maũndũnĩ ala Yeova wendaa kĩla Mũklĩsto eke. Kwa ngelekany'o, ithyonthe nĩtwaĩle kwĩthĩwa na ũuu na kĩlĩko. (Yak. 3:17; 1 Vet. 4:7) Na ĩndĩ ĩla twoona atumĩa maitata methĩwe "ngelekan'yo sya yĩla ĩĩthya," nĩtwĩmanyĩasya kĩndũ kuma kwoo na tũkatata 'twĩyĩelekany'e na mũĩkĩĩo woo.'—1 Vet. 5:3; Aevl. 13:7.
11 Ndonya kũtetheesya angĩ ata ngĩtũmĩa ũvoo ũũ? No tũtũmĩe ĩla mĩsoa ĩwetete nguma ila atumĩa maĩle kwĩthĩwa nasyo nĩ kana tũtetheesye ala mekwendeew'a kana amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia mone ũndũ atumĩa ala me ikundinĩ sya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova me kĩvathũkany'o na atongoi ma makanisa ala meyĩtaa ma Kĩklĩsto. O na ĩngĩ ĩla tũũsoma mĩsoa ĩsu no tũlilikane kĩthito kĩla atumĩa kĩkundinĩ kitũ mekĩaa nĩ kana matũtetheesye. Na twasũanĩa ũndũ meyumasya mũno wĩana kwondũ witũ, nĩtwĩkĩawa vinya twongelange ndaĩa ĩla tũnengae "ala mathĩnĩaa wĩa" katĩ witũ. (1 Ath. 5:12) Tweekĩa kĩthito kingĩ tũnenge ndaĩa atumĩa ta asu, nĩtũtumaa methĩwa na ũtanu mwingangĩ.—Aevl. 13:17.
12, 13. (a) Tũtonya kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ta wĩva tũitũmĩa syĩndũ ila tũtonya kũkwata sya kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli? (b) Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũndũ kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli kũtonya kũtuma twĩmanyĩsya kĩndũ mũndũ ũtamanya atekĩte ũkunĩkĩli.
12 Ĩka ũkunĩkĩli. No tũtũmĩe syĩndũ sya kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ila tũtonya kũkwata nĩ kana tũmanthe mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ta aa:
Nũũ waandĩkie kĩlungu kĩĩ kya Maandĩko?
Kyaandĩkĩwe va na ĩndĩĩ?
Nĩ maũndũ meva manene meekĩkie ĩvinda yĩla ĩvuku yĩĩ ya Mbivilia yaandĩkawa?
Kũkwata mosũngĩo ma makũlyo ta asu no kũtume twĩmanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ mũndũ ũtamanya atekĩte ũkunĩkĩli.
13 Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩandĩko ya Esekieli 14:13, 14 yaĩtye ũũ: "Yĩla nthĩ ĩkambĩtanĩsya kwondũ wa kwĩka naĩ, nakwa ngamĩtambũũkĩsya kw'oko kwakwa, na kũtũla ndata ya kĩmũtũ kyayo, na kũmĩetee yũa, na kũveta kwayo mũndũ na nyamũ; o na ethĩwa andũ aa atatũ, Noa, na Ndanieli, na Yovu, me kw'o, makavonokya no mathayũ moo ene kwondũ wa ũlũngalu woo, easya ũu Mwĩaĩi Yeova." Weeka ũkunĩkĩli nũkwĩthĩa kana mĩsoa ĩsu ya ĩvuku ya Esekieli nĩ ta yaandĩkiwe mwakanĩ wa 612 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. O na kũtw'ĩka ĩvinda yĩu Esekieli waandĩkaa ndeto isu Noa na Yovu maminĩte myaka mingĩ me akw'ũ, Ngai no walilikene ũndũ mekalĩte me aĩkĩĩku. Nake Ndanieli aĩ thayũ ĩvinda yĩu. O na kau no kwĩthĩwa aĩ na myaka ta 20, Yeova aisye aĩ mũlũngalu tondũ Noa na Yovu maĩ alũngalu. Nĩ kyaũ tũkwĩmanyĩsya vau? Twĩĩmanyĩsya kana Yeova nĩwonaa kĩthito kĩla athaithi make mekĩaa nĩ kana mekale me aĩkĩĩku, na nĩwonaa kĩ kya vata o na ethĩwa athaithi asu nĩ ma mũika.—Sav. 148:12-14.
TŨMĨA NESA MAŨVOO ME KĨVATHŨKANY'O ALA TŨSEŨVĨAW'A
14. Maũvoo ala maandĩkĩwe amũika mamatethasya ata, na maũvoo asu matonya kũtethya andũ angĩ ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 23.)
14 Nĩtwoona kana vai kĩlungu o na kĩmwe kya Ndeto ya Ngai kĩtatũtethya. O ta ũu lĩu w'onthe wa kĩ-veva ũla ũseũvaw'a no ũtũtethye. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii imwe. Ũvoo ũla ũandĩkĩawa andũ ma mũika. Myakanĩ ya mĩtũkĩ, amũika methĩĩtwe maiandĩkĩwa maũvoo maingĩ. [1] Maũvoo amwe katĩ wa asu methĩawa maandĩkĩtwe matetheesye amũika kũkĩlya vinya mathĩna ala mamakwataa me sukulu, kana ala makomanaa namo matambĩte kũvikya myaka 20. Maũvoo ta asu matonya kũtethya kĩla ũmwe witũ ata? Ĩla twamasoma, matũlilikanasya thĩna ũla amũika ala mamũthũkũmaa Yeova me aĩkĩĩku makomanaa naw'o. Kyu kĩtumaa tũmanya nesa ũndũ tũtonya kũmatetheesya na kũmekĩa vinya.
15. Nĩkĩ nũseo Aklĩsto ala aima makendeew'a nĩ maũvoo ala methĩawa maandĩkĩwe amũika?
15 Mathĩna maingĩ ala methĩawa maneenewe maũvoonĩ ma andũ ma mũika maikwataa andũ ma mũika me oka. Kwa ngelekany'o, kĩla ũmwe witũ no nginya atetee mũĩkĩĩo wake, emanyĩsye kũsumbĩka ngoo yake, ekĩe kĩthito ndakalikw'e naĩnĩ nĩ ala me ĩika nake, na aisisya kĩtindo kyake vamwe na maũndũ ala wĩtanĩthasya namo. Maũndũ asu na angĩ maingĩ nĩmethĩawa maũvoonĩ ala maandĩkĩwe amũika. Kwoou Aklĩsto ala aima nĩmaĩle kwona ta mekwĩtũnga ĩtina ĩla mekũsoma maũvoo ala maandĩkĩwe amũika? Mayaĩle kwona ũu o na vanini! Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o na kau maũvoo asu maandĩkĩtwe mendeesye amũika, kĩla kĩandĩkĩtwe vau kĩthĩawa kyumĩte Maandĩkonĩ. Na nũndũ myolooto ĩla yĩ Maandĩkonĩ ndĩsaa kũvĩtwa nĩ ĩvinda, kĩla ũmwe witũ no atethw'e nĩ syĩndũ ta isu Yeova ũtũnengete.
16. Maũvoo ala maandĩkawa matetheeasya andũ ma mũika ũndũnĩ ũngĩ wĩva?
16 O na kau maũvoo ala makonetye amũika nĩmamatetheeasya kũkĩlya vinya mathĩna, maũvoo asu no mamatetheeasya meane kĩ-veva na maimũthengeea Yeova. (Soma Mũtavan'ya 12:1, 13.) O namo Aklĩsto ala aima no matetheke oou. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya ĩkaseti ya Amkeni! ya Mwei wa 4, 2009. Ĩkaseti yĩu yaĩ na kĩlungu kĩ na kyongo, "Vijana Huuliza . . . Ninaweza Kufanya Nini ili Nifurahie Kusoma Biblia?" Kĩlungu kĩu nĩkyawetete maũndũ mana matonya kũtetheesya amũika, na kyaĩ na kasandũkũ ũtonya kũtila na ũikalikya Mbivilianĩ yaku nĩ kana ũkekalaa ũikatũmĩa. Mo andũ ala aima nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa matethetw'e nĩ kĩlungu kĩu? Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩ na mũsyĩ aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Neew'aa kũsoma Mbivilia kwĩ vinya mũno. [Ĩndĩ] neekĩie maũndũ ala nemanyĩisye kĩlungunĩ kĩĩ ngoonĩ yakwa, na nĩnĩendeee kũtũmĩa nesa kasandũkũ kala tweeĩtwe tũtile. Matukũ aa nĩnĩtanĩaa mũno kũsoma Mbivilia. Nĩnonete nesa ũndũ mavuku ala me Mbivilianĩ makwatĩanĩe na makalikana nesa tondũ kĩtambaa kĩlikanaa nesa na ĩlaa yĩla yĩtumĩĩwe vo. Ndyaatanĩa kũsoma Mbivilia tondũ nĩtanĩaa ũmũnthĩ."
17, 18. Kũsoma ũvoo ũla wĩthĩawa mũno mũno ũandĩkĩwe andũ mate Ngũsĩ kũtonya kũtũtethya ata? Nengane ngelekany'o.
17 Ũvoo ũla ũkonetye ala mate Ngũsĩ. Kuma mwaka wa 2008, nĩtwĩthĩĩtwe tũitanĩa kũtũmĩa ĩkaseti ya kwĩmanyĩsya ya Mũsyaĩĩsya, yĩla mũno mũno yĩthĩawa yĩandĩkĩwe Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Ĩndĩ nata makaseti ala methĩawa maandĩkĩwe mũno mũno andũ mate Ngũsĩ? Asu o namo no matũtethye? Ĩĩ. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno. Twasye ve mũndũ wathokya Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ na ũyona ooka ũvoo wa andũ onthe ũtambĩĩe. Ndũema kwĩw'a mũyo. Na ĩla mumya wa ũvoo ũendeee kumya ũvoo wake nĩ laisi ũkambĩĩa kũsũanĩa mũeni ũsu waku. Wĩthĩwa ũitata ũelewe ũvoo ũsu ũndũ we ũkũũelewa. Nũndũ wa ũu, ũvoo ũsu ũithela kĩla kĩũneeneawa ũkyosa nesa o na kwĩ ũndũ ũnakyosaa.
18 Ũu now'o tũtonya kũtetheka ĩla tũũsoma maũvoo ala maandĩkĩwe mũno mũno andũ mate Ngũsĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩkaseti ya andũ onthe ya Mũsyaĩĩsya yĩeleasya Maandĩko yĩtũmĩĩte ndeto itonya kũeleeka nĩ ala mate Ngũsĩ. Ũu now'o Maandĩko maeleaw'a ilungunĩ mbingĩ ila syĩ Kĩsesenĩ kya jw.org, ta ila ilungu syĩ na kyongo, "Mosũngĩo ma Makũlyo ma Mbivilia" na "Makũlyo Makũlaw'a Mavinda Maingĩ." Kũsoma ilungu ta isu nĩkũtumaa twenda mũnango momanyĩsyo ala tũtwĩe twĩsĩ. Na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana kũisoma nĩkũtumaa tũmanya nzĩa mbingĩ sya kũelesya kĩla tũĩkĩĩaa ĩla tũũtavany'a. Ũu now'o ĩkaseti ya Amkeni! yĩtũtethasya nũndũ kĩla ĩvinda nĩyĩlũlũmĩlasya mũĩkĩĩo witũ wa kana kwĩ Ngai wa w'o, na nĩyĩtũtetheeasya kũmanya ũndũ tũtonya kũtetea mũĩkĩĩo witũ.—Soma 1 Vetelo 3:15.
19. Nĩ kyaũ tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a kana nĩtũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wa syĩndũ ila ũtũnengae?
19 Vate nzika, Yeova nũtũnengete syĩndũ mbingĩ mũno sya kũtũtetheesya tũmine "ũkya wa kĩ-veva." (Mat. 5:3, BCK) Kwoou nĩtũendeei kũtũmĩa nesa syĩndũ syonthe ila Yeova ũtũnengete. Tweeka ũu tũkoonanasya kana nĩtũmũtũngĩaa mũvea nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe ũtũmanyĩasya kwaĩla.—Isa. 48:17.
^ [1] (kalungu ka 14) Maũvoo amwe nĩ ta ala me ĩvukunĩ Maswali Ambayo Vijana Huuliza—Majibu Yafanyayo Kazi, Ĩvuku ya 1 na ya 2, na ala me kĩlungunĩ "Makũlyo ma Andũ ma Mũika," kĩla yu kyonekaa Indanetinĩ ve voka.
