translation:
"You, Jehovah God, are the One who teaches what is beneficial."—ISA. 48:17.
PARAGRAPH: 20, 37
1, 2. (a) How does Jehovah use the Bible today? (b) What benefits do we receive from it?
TRUE Jehovah uses the Bible to teach us. It shows us how to live and helps us to make right decisions and avoid wrongdoing. (Prov. 15:4) True, we benefit from the Bible because it gives insight into people's hearts, helping us to understand "the thought of his heart."—1 Thess. 2:13.
2 However, sometimes it is not easy to apply what we learn. Some may find it difficult to see how Jesus' example can help them deal with specific problems, or how Jehovah feels about certain things. (John 14:9) Others may struggle with understanding scriptures that seem complicated. For instance, some may find the account of the Flood hard to grasp. (Gen. 1:1) And perhaps you have wondered about the account of Saul, or you have difficulty understanding the account of Naomi? That is understandable, for the Bible is a deep book.
3, 4. (a) How can we deepen our appreciation for God's Word? (b) What practical steps can we take to benefit others through our ministry?
3 Studying the Bible can help us deepen our appreciation for God's Word and improve our spirituality. For example, we can look for practical wisdom in the accounts of people, places, and events, and we can meditate on what we read. This will help us to see how Jehovah guides us, strengthen our faith, increase our love for him, and remain "sound in mind."—Titus 2:2.
4 In addition to studying the entire Bible, we can focus on specific scriptures that are particularly helpful in our ministry. For instance, some scriptures may be especially suited to addressing certain concerns, while others may be more effective when dealing with different types of people. Also, much valuable information can be found in publications that explain Bible teachings clearly. The comfort this provides can assure us that Jehovah cares about his worshipers and will fulfill his purpose.—Isa. 25:6.
5. Does Jehovah want us to be happy?
5 It would be wise for all of us to make time for personal study of the Bible along with regular family reading. This will help us to see how Jehovah wants us to find joy in applying what we learn from 'the sacred secret' and in making time each day to read the Bible and meditate on it. (Eph. 5:15, 16) And remember, we can use the time we spend traveling to listen to spiritual material. How does this benefit us?
6. What can help us to remain motivated despite facing difficulties?
6 One way to stay motivated is to focus on the good things happening around us rather than letting minor annoyances discourage us. For example, when you read the Bible, do you concentrate on the positive teachings? Or when you face a challenge, do you dwell on the negative aspects of the situation? Consider whether you are using your time wisely or wasting it on unproductive activities. If we do this, we will be more determined to overcome obstacles. But what can help us to stay focused and avoid discouragement? The key is to remember that our God cares about us and understands our limitations. Our loving Father, through Isaiah, assures us: "O Jehovah, you are my God; I will exalt you." (Isa. 48:17) Therefore, let us regularly examine ourselves to see if we are allowing minor problems to prevent us from enjoying our Bible reading or from being grateful for the blessings we have received.
WHAT CAN HELP US TO REMAIN MOTIVATED WHILE STUDYING THE BIBLE
7. How does studying the Bible help us to remain motivated?
7 Study with a purpose—to learn something. The Bible teaches that "all Scripture is inspired of God and beneficial," and it is able to equip us. (2 Tim. 3:16) However, some parts of the Bible may seem difficult to understand or irrelevant. That is why it is important to study the Scriptures with a desire to learn something. A young man once said: "When I read the Bible, I often find many things that are hard to grasp." He added: "But thinking about those things helps me to make the lessons more meaningful." So let us ask God to help us understand his Word so that we can apply it to our lives, and let him guide us as we seek to learn more.—Isa. 7:10; see James 1:5.
8, 9. (a) What questions should we ask ourselves to determine if we need to improve our reading habits? (b) How can we show appreciation for Jehovah's organization while still maintaining personal initiative?
8 Consider these questions. If you continue to read portions of the Bible, ask yourself: 'What am I learning from this? Is this helping me to draw closer to Jehovah? Can I use this information in my ministry?' By asking such questions, we will be motivated to learn more as we read. Let us look at an example. The Scriptures say that overseers should be exemplary. (Read 1 Timothy 3:2-7.) Many brothers appreciate having qualified men appointed, but they may wonder if they can personally imitate those qualities. If we feel that way, we can strive to cultivate those qualities ourselves rather than simply waiting for others to demonstrate them. This will help us to benefit fully from the Scriptural guidance and to avoid being misled by false teachings.
9 What does it mean to "shepherd God's flock"? Jehovah has given his organization the responsibility to shepherd his people, guiding them and protecting them from harmful influences. Elders work hard to care for the congregation, and they are referred to as "overseers" of God's flock. (Acts 20:28, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) And they also endeavor to comfort and strengthen us. (Isa. 32:1, 2) So, when you encounter difficult situations, remember that Jehovah uses the organization to provide assistance through capable elders who can offer practical advice.
10, 11. (a) How can reading exemplary scriptures and attending meetings help us to imitate those qualities? (b) What can we do to apply what we learn?
10 Why imitate such fine examples? From time to time, congregation ministers visit brothers and sisters who may be facing challenges, and they share encouraging thoughts based on the Scriptures. A loving parent teaches his child 'to observe what is right,' helping him to understand principles and to discern truth. (1 Tim. 3:1) Also, a mature Christian strives to read regularly and to meditate deeply on God's Word so that he can give appropriate counsel. For example, he will often use illustrations and comparisons. (Jas. 3:17; 1 Pet. 4:7) And when we see outstanding ministers who are "examples to the flock," we benefit from their conduct and strive 'to imitate their faith.'—1 Pet. 5:3; Heb. 13:7.
11 But how can we imitate such fine examples? We can do so by carefully observing those who shepherd us well and by striving to apply the advice found in God's Word. We can also learn from the exemplary zeal of Jehovah's Witnesses in the ministry and from the fine organization of the Christian congregations. As we read the accounts of faithful men, we can identify qualities worthy of imitation and endeavor to manifest them in our own life. By doing so, we will be moved to speak kindly to others, avoiding "harsh words." (1 Thess. 5:12) We show appreciation for ministers who work hard among us, supporting them generously.—Heb. 13:17.
12, 13. (a) How can we determine whether we are making progress in imitating good examples? (b) Explain why it is important to practice discerning spiritual things so that we can help someone who is struggling spiritually.
12 Practice discernment. We can examine ourselves to see whether we are making progress in practicing discernment by asking ourselves questions like these:
Do I diligently study the Scriptures?
Am I quick to listen?
What major events in Bible history impress me?
By considering such questions, we can better understand spiritual matters and help others who may be struggling spiritually.
13 For example, Ezekiel 14:13, 14 states: "And should there come a land where they dwell, I will set my face against that land, and I will bring upon it disaster, and I will cut off from it man and beast; and should those men come—Noah, Daniel, and Job—they would deliver neither son nor daughter. They would deliver only themselves by their righteousness. As for Jehovah, he is righteous!" Such expressions show that the book of Ezekiel was written well after 612 B.C.E., and possibly later. And the fact that Ezekiel mentions Noah and Job by name indicates that many years had passed since their time, and God remembered what they had done. But Daniel lived during that time. And he was about 20 years old when Jehovah revealed to him things that were to happen to Noah and Job in the future. Why then do we mention them? We mention them to show that Jehovah remembers every faithful servant, whether ancient or modern, and he remembers what they have done and what those loyal ones will do.—Ps. 148:12-14.
USE THESE QUESTIONS TO HELP YOU REMEMBER
14. Are questions often asked in publications, and why are some questions easier to answer than others? (See paragraph 23.)
14 Let us see whether a question or a point raised in God's Word is difficult to understand. Often the entire context helps us to understand. Consider the example we just discussed. This scripture was written to encourage people who are loyal. It applies especially to those who have been serving faithfully for many years. [1] Some questions found in our publications may be easy to answer because they deal with information that we learned in school, or that we have heard repeatedly. Can most people answer every question right away? No, but by doing research, we can learn more about those loyal servants of Jehovah and how they acted, which helps us to know what we can do to be successful and to apply what we learn.
15. What helped early Christians to remember the questions that were asked?
15 In many cases, those who were assigned questions encouraged those present to think about them. For instance, each of us might review his own assignment, prepare an outline, practice presenting his talk, and then ask himself whether he has covered the main points clearly. He should also consider how his presentation will affect the audience. Many other things help us to remember questions that are asked in our publications. So early Christians could readily recall what they had learned from studying those questions. Why is this important? Because when we study questions that are asked in our publications, we are reminded of scriptures. And since the Scriptures are inspired by God, they can guide us to the truth, helping each of us to please Jehovah.
16. From where do questions that help faithful people come?
16 Often, questions found in our publications encourage us to do more research, but some questions simply help us to strengthen our love for Jehovah. (Read Proverbs 12:1, 13.) Also, Christ encourages us to do so. See the article "Awake!" of April 4, 2009. That article included a box entitled "Young People Ask . . . What Can I Do to Enjoy Reading the Bible More?" That box offered practical suggestions on how to make reading the Bible more enjoyable, and it also mentioned tools that can help you locate scriptures quickly. How can young people benefit from that box? One sister wrote: "I used to find it hard to enjoy reading the Bible. [But] I applied the suggestions in that box to my personal routine, and I have continued to use those tools ever since. Now I look forward to reading the Bible. I appreciate that the information in the Bible is relevant and up-to-date, and that it helps us to understand life. I enjoy reading the Bible because I feel closer to Jehovah."
17, 18. Why is doing thorough research sometimes necessary when studying? Consider the example.
17 The need for thorough research. In 2008, we were encouraged to use the research tool available on JW.ORG, which is a valuable resource for all of Jehovah's Witnesses. But what about other research tools? Are they helpful? Yes. Let's examine this. Imagine a brother who was assigned to give a talk at the Kingdom Hall and he needed information on a certain topic. He spent hours researching, and finally he found what he was looking for. However, he still did not fully grasp the meaning. So he asked an elder to help him understand. With the elder's assistance, he was able to see how the information applied to his talk.
This shows us that even though we may find information, we may still need help understanding it.
18 Now why is it important that we do thorough research when studying material prepared by others? For instance, the public talk from the Watch Tower Society uses scriptures to support its points, and these scriptures are often taken out of context. Also, articles on the website jw.org, such as the article "Bible Teachings" and "Sound Advice," can be very helpful, but they should also be read carefully. Reading these articles can help us expand our knowledge and strengthen our faith. And it can also help us appreciate the value of accurate information. Furthermore, the *Awake!* magazine helps us understand current events in light of God's Word, and it encourages us to defend our beliefs.—Read 1 Peter 3:15.
19. How then can we make sure that we are representing Jehovah accurately and not misrepresenting him?
19 Remember, Jehovah has given us much guidance on how to distinguish "the spirit of the truth." (Matt. 5:3, footnote) So let us rely on Jehovah to help us discern what is true. We will show that we trust him by seeking his guidance.—Isa. 48:17.
[1] (paragraph 14) Further information can be found in the books *Questions Young People Ask—Answers That Work*, Volumes 1 and 2, and in the article "Help From God's Word," which is available online at www.jw.org.

text:
"Ngai wa mũuo . . . namwĩanĩsye kĩla ũndũnĩ ũseo mwĩkae kwenda kwake."—AEVL. 13:20, 21.
MBATHI: 136, 14
1. Yesũ endete wĩa wa kũtavany'a mũno wĩana ata? Elesya.
YESŨ nĩwendete kũneena ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. Ũkasisya ũvoo ũla ũandĩkĩtwe Mbivilianĩ, wĩthĩa aneenie ĩũlũ wa Ũsumbĩ mũno vyũ kũte kĩndũ kĩngĩ o na kĩva. Aũwetie mbee wa mavinda 100 ĩla watavanasya kũũ nthĩ. Vate nzika, Yesũ nĩwendete Ũsumbĩ ũsu mũno.—Soma Mathayo 12:34.
2. Nĩ andũ meana ata matonya kwĩthĩwa maĩ vo ĩla mwĩao ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Mathayo 28:19, 20 wanenganiwe, na nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu?
2 Kavinda kakuvĩ Yesũ amina kũthayũũkw'a, nĩwoombanie na andũ mbee wa 500 mendeeaw'a nĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ. (1 Ako. 15:6) No kwĩthĩwa ĩvinda yĩu new'o wanenganie ũla mwĩao wa kũtavya andũ ma "mbaĩ syonthe" ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ, o na kau ĩvinda yĩu kũtethya wĩa ũsu kũyaĩ laisi. * Asyokie athana kana wĩa ũsu wingĩvĩte ũu waĩ ũtethw'e kũvika "wĩanĩu wa ĩvinda yĩĩ," na ũu nĩw'o vethĩĩtwe vailyĩ. Nĩ laisi mũno ũkethĩa o naku nũendeee kũtetheesya kwĩanĩsya wathani ũsu.—Mt. 28:19, 20.
3. Tũmbanĩtw'e maũndũnĩ meva atatũ nĩ kana twĩanĩsye ũla ũtũmane wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo?
3 Yesũ amina kũnenga aatĩĩi make mwĩao ũsu wa kũtavany'a asyokie amatha atĩĩ: "Nyie nĩ vamwe nenyu." (Mt. 28:20) Kwoou we mwene nĩwesaa kũũngamĩa wĩa ũũ wingĩvĩte ũu wa kũtavany'a. Nake Ngai witũ nũtũmbanĩtye "kĩla ũndũnĩ ũseo" nĩ kana twĩanĩsye ũtũmane ũsu. (Aevl. 13:20, 21) Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩneenea ũndũ tũmbanĩtw'e maũndũnĩ atatũ. Twĩneenea (1) mĩio ĩla tũnengetwe, (2) nzĩa ila tũtũmĩĩte, na (3) ũndũ tũmanyĩĩtw'e. Mbee, kwasũanĩa mĩio ĩla twĩthĩĩtwe tũitũmĩa ĩvindanĩ ya myaka 100 mĩvĩtu.
MŨSUMBĨ NŨNENGETE ATHŨKŨMI MAKE MĨIO YA KŨTAVANY'A
4. Mĩio yĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩla tũtũmĩĩte wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ĩtũtetheetye ata?
4 Yesũ aisye kana ĩla "ndeto ya ũsumbĩ" no ũndũ ũmwe na mbeũ ĩvuĩwe kũndũ kwĩ na mĩthanga yĩ kĩvathũkany'o. (Mt. 13:18, 19) Mũĩmi no atũmĩe mĩio yĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩla ũkũseũvya mũũnda wake nĩ kana avuĩe mbeũ. Ũndũ ũmwe na ũu, Mũsumbĩ witũ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe aitũnenga mĩio tũtonya kũtũmĩa tũtetheesye andũ aingĩ metĩkĩle ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Mĩio ĩmwe twamĩtũmĩie kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ta ĩkũmi kana o vandũ vau, nayo ĩngĩ nĩtũmĩtũmĩaa o na ũmũnthĩ. Ĩndĩ mĩio ĩsu yonthe nĩtũtetheesye kwongela ũtũĩka witũ wa kũtavany'a.
5. Nĩ kyaũ kyeetawa kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ, na yatũmĩawa ata?
5 Mũio ũmwe watetheeisye aingĩ mamanyĩe kũtavany'a nĩ kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ. Kaati ĩsu yambĩĩe kũtũmĩwa mwakanĩ wa 1933. Kaati ĩsu yaĩ na ũasa wa inzi ta itano na waamu wa inzi ta itatũ (sendimita 12.7 kwa sendimita 7.6), na yaĩ na ũvoo mũkuvĩ wa Mbivilia. Mavinda kwa mavinda ũvoo ũla wĩ kaatinĩ ĩsu nĩwasenzaw'a. Kũtavany'a nayo kwaĩ laisi vyũ! Mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa C. W. Erlenmeyer atũmĩie kaati ĩsu ya mbee e na myaka ta ĩkũmi. Aeleetye ũũ: "Ndeto ila aingĩ matũmĩaa maitavany'a na kaati ĩsu syaĩ, 'No wende kũsoma kaati ĩno?' Mwene nyũmba amina kũsoma kaati ĩsu twamũnengae mavuku na tũikwata nzĩa tũithi."
6. Nĩ ũndũnĩ wĩva kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ yatetheeasya?
6 Kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ nĩyatethasya maũndũnĩ angĩ maingĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na kũtw'ĩka atavany'a amwe maĩ na wendi mwingĩ mũno wa kũtavany'a, maĩ nthoni na mayeethĩawa mesĩ kĩla matonya kũtavya mwene nyũmba. Angĩ namo maĩ andũ ma ngewa. Nũndũ wa ũu mavinda maingĩ mayatavanasya na ũĩ nũndũ matũmĩaa ndatĩka nini ila me nasyo mamwonoeesye mwene nyũmba kĩla kyonthe mesĩ! Vandũ va wĩa ũsu w'onthe, kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ nĩyo yaneenaa vandũ va mũtavany'a.
7. Atavany'a amwe makomanaa na mathĩna meva maitavany'a na kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ?
7 Kũtavany'a na kaati ĩsu kwaĩ na mathĩna makw'o. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wĩthĩĩtwe e Ngũsĩ kwa ĩvinda ĩasa wĩtawa Grace A. Estep aĩtye ũũ: "Mavinda amwe twakũlaw'a, 'Kwani yaĩtye ata? Wĩtuma ũtandavya ũndũ yaĩtye nĩkĩ?'" Thĩna ũngĩ nĩ kana andũ amwe mayaĩ matonya kũsoma kĩla kĩandĩkĩtwe. Angĩ namo moonaa ta manengwa ĩ kaati mamesye, na kwoou mamyosaa na maivinga mũomo. Na ĩndĩ mũtavany'a esa kũkomana na mũndũ ũte kwenda kwĩw'a, mũndũ ũsu aĩ atonya kũmĩtembũanga. Ĩndĩ o na kau kwaĩ mathĩna ta asu, kaati ĩsu nĩyatumie ana-a-asa maitũ mamanya ũndũ matonya kũneena na andũ na ũndũ matonya kwĩyĩelesya nesa kana mo nĩ atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ.
8. Elesya ũndũ kĩla kĩnanda kĩvũthũ kyatũmĩawa. (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 26.)
8 Mũio ũngĩ watũmĩawa myakanĩ ya 1930 na mwambĩĩonĩ wa myakanĩ ya 1940 waĩ kĩnanda kĩvũthũ. Ana-a-asa amwe meetaa kĩnanda kĩu Aluni nũndũ vandũ va maneene ne mo ĩla mekũtavany'a, nĩkyo kyakothaa kũneena. (Soma Kuma 4:14-16.) Mwene nyũmba ametĩkĩlya, mamwĩkĩĩaa ũvoo wa Mbivilia wa ndatĩka inya na nusu ethukĩĩsye na ĩndĩ maimũnenga mavuku. O na mavinda angĩ andũ onthe ma mũsyĩ maĩ matonya kũmbana methukĩĩsye ũvoo wa Mbivilia kĩnandanĩ kĩu! Mwakanĩ wa 1934, Watch Tower Society nĩyaumisye inanda mbũthangũ syaseũvĩtw'e mũno mũno itũmĩwe wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Ĩtina maũvoo asu mesie kũvika 92.
9. Kĩnanda kyatetheeisye ata?
9 Ĩvinda yĩmwe mũndũ ũmwe wĩtawa Hillary Goslin nĩweethukĩĩisye ũmwe wa maũvoo asu kĩnandanĩ kĩu. Wathela eetisye mũtavany'a ũla waĩ nakyo mwanya akĩtũmĩe kwa ĩvinda ya kyumwa kĩmwe nĩ kana ekĩĩe atũi make ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩla mũtavany'a ũsu wesie kũsyoka, eethĩie eteelwe nĩ andũ meana ũna mekwendeew'a. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda amwe moo nĩmeeyumisye mamũthũkũme Yeova, na eĩtu elĩ ma Hillary nĩmesie kũthi Sukulu ya Ngileati na matw'ĩka amisonalĩ. Kĩnanda kĩu nĩkyatetheeisye aingĩ mamanyĩe wĩa wa kũtavany'a o tondũ ĩla kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ yeekie. Ĩndĩ ĩtina Mũsumbĩ witũ nĩwesie kũtũmĩa Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi nĩ kana amanyĩsye atavany'a kũtũmĩa ndeto syoo ĩla meũtavany'a.
NĨTŨTŨMĨĨTE NZĨA ILA TŨTONYA NĨ KANA TŨVIKĨE ANDŨ
10, 11. Mathangũ ma maũvoo na letiũ syatũmĩiwe ata kũnyaĩĩkya ũw'o wa Mbivilia, na nĩkĩ nzĩa isu syaĩ nzeo?
10 Mũsumbĩ nũtetheesye andũ ma Ngai makatũmĩa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o nĩ kana mavikĩsye andũ aingĩ vyũ ũndũ vatonyeka ũvoo mũseo. Kũtũmĩa nzĩa isu kwatetheeisye mũno mũno ĩvinda yĩla 'akethi maĩ avũthũ.' (Soma Mathayo 9:37.) Kwa ngelekany'o, mwambĩĩonĩ wa myaka ya 1900 mathangũ ma maũvoo nĩmatũmĩawa kũvikĩsya andũ aingĩ ũvoo kũndũ kũla andũ ma Yeova mataĩ aingĩ. Kĩla kyumwa Charles Taze Russell atũmĩaa telegraph kũtũma ũvoo mũna wa Mbivilia kambunĩnĩ ila syũmbanasya maũvoo. Nasyo kambunĩ isu syakwata ũvoo ũsu syasyokaa ikatũmĩa nzĩa o ĩsu kũtũmĩa aandĩki ma mathangũ ma maũvoo ala maĩ Amelika, Canada, na Europe. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa kana kũvika mwaka wa 1913, mathangũ ma maũvoo 2,000 nĩmavikĩisye andũ 15,000,000 maũvoo ma Mwana-a-asa Russell!
11 Ve nzĩa ĩngĩ nzeo ya kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo mũseo ĩla yambĩĩiw'e ĩtina wa kĩkw'ũ kya Mwana-a-asa Russell. Nzĩa yĩva? Matukũ 16, Mwei wa 4, 1922, Joseph F. Rutherford nĩwaumisye ũvoo ũmwe katĩ wa maũvoo ala ma mbee waumisye isesenĩ sya letiũ. Eethukĩĩw'e nĩ andũ ta 50,000. Na ĩndĩ Matukũ 24, Mwei wa 2, 1924, Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyavingũie kĩsese kya letiũ kĩla kyeetawa WBBR. Ĩkaseti ya The Watch Tower (Mũsyaĩĩsya) ya 01/12/1924 yaisye ũũ yĩiweta ĩũlũ wa nzĩa ĩsu ya kũtavya andũ ũvoo mũseo: "Katĩ wa nzĩa syonthe ila twĩthĩĩtwe tũitũmĩa kũnyaĩĩkya ũla w'o, tũi na nzika kana kũtũmĩa letiũ nĩyo nzĩa ĩla nzeo vyũ na ĩtethĩawa na ngalama mbingĩ." Letiũ nĩyatetheeisye kũvikĩsya andũ aingĩ ũvoo mũseo kũla kwaĩ na atavany'a anini o tondũ mathangũ ma maũvoo matetheeisye.
12. (a) Katĩ wa kũla kwĩthĩawa andũ aingĩ nĩ va we wendete kũtavanĩlya? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya ethĩwa nĩtũkĩaa kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ?
12 Matukũ aa twĩkĩawa vinya mũno tũtavany'e kũla kwĩthĩawa andũ aingĩ. Kũu nĩ kũndũ ta iwanzanĩ sya mbasi na sya ngalĩ ya mwaki, kũla ngalĩ iũngamaw'a, sokonĩ, vamwe na kũla andũ mathyũmũĩlaa. Ethĩwa nũkĩaa kũtavany'a kũndũ kũmwe ta kũu, voya na ũisũanĩa mũno ndeto ii sya mwana-a-asa wĩthĩĩtwe e mũsyaĩĩsya wa kũthyũlũlũka kwa ĩvinda ĩasa wĩtawa Angelo Manera, Jr. Aisye atĩĩ: "Twoonw'a nzĩa nzaũ ya kũtavany'a twamyosaa ta nzĩa ĩngĩ ya kũmũthũkũma Yeova, o ta nzĩa ĩngĩ ya kũmwony'a kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye nake, na ta nzĩa ĩngĩ ya kũtata ũĩkĩĩku witũ, na nĩtwendaa mũno kũmũĩkĩĩthya Yeova kana nĩtũkwenda kũmũthũkũma ũndũ we ũkwenda o na ethĩwa nata." Twatũmĩa nzĩa nzaũ ya kũtavany'a, ta kwa ngelekany'o nzĩa ĩla twĩw'aa tũte eanie tũimĩtũmĩa, nĩtũmũĩkĩĩaa Yeova mũnango na tũitw'ĩka atavany'a aseango.—Soma 2 Akolintho 12:9, 10.
13. Kĩsese kitũ kya jw.org kĩtetheesye ata wĩanĩ witũ wa kũtavany'a? Nĩ maũndũ meva we mwene wonete ĩla ũkũelesya andũ kĩsese kĩu?
13 Atavany'a aingĩ nĩmatanĩĩte kũelesya andũ ĩũlũ wa kĩsese kitũ kya jw.org, vala matonya kũsoma na kumya mavuku ma kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na ithyomo mbee wa 700. Kĩla mũthenya andũ mbee wa 1,600,000 nĩmalikaa kĩsesenĩ kĩu. O ũndũ letiũ yatetheeisye ĩvinda ya tene, now'o kĩsese kitũ kĩtumĩte ũvoo mũseo ũvikĩa andũ aingĩ o na ala mekalaa kũasa na taoni.
KŨMANYĨSYA ATAVANY'A MA ŨVOO MŨSEO
14. Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ maaĩlĩte kũmanyĩw'a kwĩka ata, na nĩ sukulu yĩva ĩmatetheesye matw'ĩke alimũ aseo?
14 Twaneenea o mĩio mĩnini na nzĩa nini ila itũmĩĩtwe kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo mũseo. Nao nata ũndũ twĩthĩĩtwe tũimanyĩw'a? Kũmanyĩw'a kwĩthĩĩtwe kwĩ kwa vata nũndũ mũtavany'a aĩ atonya kwĩkĩĩa mũndũ ũvoo kĩnandanĩ na mũndũ ũsu ethukĩĩsya aileana naw'o, kana o akanenga mũndũ ĩla kaati ya kumya ũkũsĩ na ayendeew'a. Kwoou atavany'a nĩmaaĩle kũmanya ũndũ matonya kũtũmĩa ũĩ ĩla andũ maleana na ũvoo woo, na ũndũ matonya kũmanyĩsya nesa ala maĩ na ngoo nzeo. Nũndũ wa ũu Nathan H. Knorr nĩwatongoew'e nĩ veva mũtheu oona vata ũsu wa kũmanyĩsya atavany'a ũndũ matonya kũtũmĩa mũthĩnzĩo woo wa kũneena ũtavany'anĩ. Nĩ kyaũ kyeekiwe? Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi nĩyambĩĩiw'e mwaka wa 1943. Sukulu ĩsu nĩtũtetheesye tũkatw'ĩka alimũ aseo.
15. (a) Kwaendaa ata ĩla amwe mekumya ũvoo Sukulunĩ ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi? (b) Watho wa Yeova ũla ũandĩkĩtwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Savuli 32:8 wĩanĩĩte ata ngalĩkonĩ ĩ yaku?
15 Andũ aingĩ nĩmekalangile mayĩsa kũmanyĩa kũneena me mbee wa andũ aingĩ. Mwana-a-asa Julio S. Ramu nũlilikanaa ũvoo wake wa mbee ũla waumisye sukulunĩ ĩsu mwakanĩ wa 1944. Ũvoo ũsu waneeneaa kyaũ? Waĩ ĩũlũ wa mũndũ weetawa Ndoeki, nake awetetwe o nthĩnĩ wa mĩsoa ĩtano tũ ya Mbivilia! Mwana-a-asa ũsu aĩtye atĩĩ: "Mau makwa mathĩlĩĩte ũkethĩa nĩmeũtinana, namo moko na ngambu syatetemete vyũ." O na asyokie asya kana ũvoo wake w'onthe waaĩle kuma maandĩkonĩ asu atano me moka. Aminĩie kwasya: "Naumisye ũvoo wakwa na ndatĩka itatũ. O na kau yĩu nĩyo yaĩ ĩvinda yakwa ya mbee kumya ũvoo nĩũngye mbee wa andũ, nawumisye nginya namina." O nasyo syana no syalikile sukulunĩ ĩsu o na vala imwe nĩsyeew'aa vinya kumya ũvoo kĩkundinĩ. Ũla mwana-a-asa wĩtawa Angelo Manera nũlilikanaa ũndũ kamwana kamwe kanini kaumisye ũvoo wako wa mbee. Aĩtye: "Kaĩ na wia mwingĩ mũno nginya kambĩĩa kũĩa ĩla kambĩĩe kumya ũvoo wako. Ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩkeeyumĩtye kũwumya vyũ, kawumisye kaĩĩte nginya wathela." We waaĩsa kũemwa nĩ kumya maelesyo maũmbanonĩ nũndũ wa kwĩw'a nthoni kana nũndũ wa thĩna o ũngĩ waku? Voya Yeova aũtetheesye ũkĩlye thĩna ũsu vinya. Akaũtetheesya o ũndũ watetheeisye asu maĩ Sukulunĩ ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi.—Soma Savuli 32:8.
16. Sukulu ya Ngileati yatetheeisye ata (a) ĩvinda yĩ navu ĩtina na (b) kuma mwaka wa 2011?
16 Andũ ma Yeova me sukulu ingĩ eka Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Kĩtheokulasi. Sukulu ya Ngileati nĩtetheetye amisonalĩ mũno vamwe na angĩ. Mwalimũ ũmwe wa sukulu ĩsu aisye kana kĩeleelo kĩmwe kyayo nĩ "kũtetheesya amanyĩw'a mende mũno wĩa wa kũtavany'a." Kuma Sukulu ya Ngileati yambĩĩw'a mwaka wa 1943, ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa mbee wa 8,500 nĩmamanyĩĩtw'e nĩ sukulu ĩsu. Amisonalĩ ala mesĩlĩte Sukulu ya Ngileati nĩmatũmĩtwe nthĩ vakuvĩ 170 syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Kuma mwaka wa 2011, ala metawa sukulunĩ ĩsu nĩ ala methĩawa ũthũkũminĩ wa ĩvinda yonthe wa mwanya. Asu nĩ ta mavainia ma mwanya, asyaĩĩsya ma kũthyũlũlũka, athũkũmi ma Mbetheli, kana amisonalĩ ala mataaĩsĩla Sukulu ya Ngileati.
17. Sukulu ya Ngileati ĩtethetye mũno wĩana ata?
17 Sukulu ya Ngileati ĩtethetye mũno wĩana ata? Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno. Mwei wa 8, 1949, Japan yaĩ na atavany'a ma kũu matavika ĩkũmi. Mwaka ũsu ũyũka kũthela kwaĩ amisonalĩ 13 mesĩlĩte Sukulu ya Ngileati na nĩmaĩ na kĩthito wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Ũmũnthĩ nthĩ ĩsu ya Japan yĩ atavany'a ta 216,000, na vakuvĩ nusu yoo nĩ mavainia!
18. Weta sukulu ingĩ ila itetheesye Ngũsĩ ila isomeete vo iane kĩ-veva.
18 Ve sukulu ingĩ ta Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Ũsumbĩ, Sukulu ya Mavainia, Sukulu ya Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ, Sukulu ya Asyaĩĩsya ma Mũthyũlũlũko na Iveti Syoo, na Sukulu ya Ala me Kamitiinĩ ya Ovisi wa Ũvonge na Iveti Syoo. Sukulu isu nitethetye mũno vyũ ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa malũlũmĩlye mũĩkĩĩo woo na mayongela ũtũĩka woo wa kũtavany'a. Vate nzika, Mũsumbĩ nũendeee kũmanyĩsya andũ make!
19. Nĩ ndeto syĩva syawetiwe nĩ Charles Taze Russell ĩũlũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a syoonany'a kana nĩweene vaasa? Ndeto syake ianĩĩte ata?
19 Yu nĩvavĩtĩte myaka mbee wa 100 kuma Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wasumbĩka. Mũsumbĩ witũ, Yesũ Klĩsto, no ũendeee kũtũmanyĩsya. Mwakanĩ wa 1916, kavinda kanini Charles Taze Russell atanamba kũkw'a, nĩwawetie ndeto syoonany'a kana nĩweene vaasa. Atavisye mũnyanyae ũmwe ndeto ii ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũvoo mũseo ũkatavanw'a: "Wĩa nũendeee kwongeleka na mĩtũkĩ, na wĩendeea kwongeleka, nũndũ 'ũvoo mũseo wa ũsumbĩ' ũkatavanw'a kĩla vandũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ." (Ĩvuku yĩtawa Faith on the March, ya A. H. Macmillan, ĩth. 69) Mwana-a-asa ũsu aneenie ndeto sya w'o ki! Naitũ twĩtũnga mũvea mũno nũndũ Ngai witũ wa mũuo nũendeee kũtũmbany'a nĩ kana tũtethye wĩa ũsu ũseũvĩte ũu! Vate nzika, nũtwĩanĩsye "kĩla ũndũnĩ ũseo" nĩ kana twĩke kwenda kwake!
^ kal. 2 Ve kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũĩkĩĩa kana aingĩ ala maĩ vo ĩvinda yĩu nĩmesie kũtw'ĩka Aklĩsto. Kĩtumi kĩva? Valũanĩ ũla Vaulo waandĩkĩie Akolintho awetie kana ala maĩ vo maĩ 'ana-a-asa maana atano.' O na asyokie ongela vinya ũndũ ũsu ĩla waisye atĩĩ: "Aingĩ moo me o kw'o kũvika o na yu, ĩndĩ amwe nĩmakomete." Kwoou ũndũ ũsu wĩtwony'a kana Vaulo na Aklĩsto angĩ ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa nĩmeesene na aingĩ ma ala meewie na matũ moo ene Yesũ ainengana mwĩao ũsu.

translation:
"The God of love… has shown compassion for every soul so that they may go to his place." – AEVL 13:20, 21.
FOOTNOTE: 136, 14
1. Did Jesus ever speak in riddles at all? Yes.
JESUS used to speak in illustrations about the Kingdom of God. As he explained what was written in the Prophets, he would use illustrations to make the truth clear and memorable. He once said that 100 measures of wheat were scattered and then gathered up. Because of this, Jesus often spoke about the Kingdom like this.—Read Matthew 12:34.
2. Are there people who might be tempted to misuse the commission found in Matthew 28:19, 20, and if so, how can we avoid doing so?
2 One reason why Jesus commanded his followers to baptize is that he wanted them to associate themselves with the Kingdom. (1 Cor. 15:6) But some might misuse this commission to force people to become disciples of the Kingdom, or they might feel pressured to do so. * Some brothers may even feel obligated to fulfill a quota of "so many" disciples, and they may pressure others to get baptized quickly. It is important to remember that the command is to make disciples, not just to baptize them—Matt. 28:19, 20.
3. What lessons can we learn from the examples discussed above regarding how to show compassion?
3 Jesus showed compassion by telling his disciples: "I am with you always." (Matt. 28:20) This assurance helped them to be courageous in their ministry. Our God assures us that he will support us in "every good work" we undertake. (Heb. 13:20, 21) Let us examine three things that contribute to our ability to show compassion. We need (1) empathy, (2) practical help, and (3) understanding. For example, consider the effort required to learn a language so that we can preach to people for over 100 years.
THE KINGDOM IS WORTH SACRIFICING FOR
4. Are there sacrifices involved in our ministry, and if so, what kind?
4 Jesus used the illustration of the "treasure" and the pearl to illustrate something valuable being acquired at the cost of possessions. (Matt. 13:18, 19) A dedicated Christian may sacrifice personal comfort in order to serve Jehovah more fully. Similarly, our Kingdom Ministry involves sacrificing time to teach others about the Kingdom and help them to understand its blessings. Some of us have been doing this for decades, while others have done so for only a short time. All of these efforts help us to proclaim the good news of the Kingdom.
5. What is needed to remain zealous, and how can we get it?
5 One way to remain zealous is to remember the experiences of those who were zealous in the past. One experience was related in 1933. It involved a hall measuring 5 meters by 7.6 meters (12.7 feet by 7.6 feet), and it had a prominent display of Bibles. The hall itself became known as "the hall." Truly, zeal pays off! A young man named C. W. Erlenmeyer used that hall for ten years. He wrote: "The treasure that most people sought in that hall was, 'Will you read this?' The householder would readily read it, and we would take hold of their interest."
6. What benefits result from remaining zealous?
6 Remaining zealous brings many blessings. For example, it helps us to be effective witnesses, spending much time in the ministry, bringing back some who have left, and helping others each month to become householders. Also, more people come to see us. Because of this, many blessings result, and it makes our service more enjoyable! To all people, remaining zealous is what attracts people to the truth.
7. How can we compare our activity to that of those zealous ones who used the hall?
7 By being zealous in another way and using different methods. One sister in America named Grace A. Estep wrote: "We often asked ourselves, 'How can we make our ministry more appealing?'". Another reason is that some people find it hard to read everything that is printed. Also, they enjoy seeing pictures and illustrations. And if a witness meets someone who is going on a trip, that person might be able to place literature. So, like them, let us use various ways to help people learn about God's Word and understand it so that they too will become Jehovah's Witnesses.
8. Review each point thoroughly. (See chart on page 26.)
8 This method was used in the 1930's and became popular in the 1940's. Some children learned it from their parents, and this helped them to speak effectively. (Read Matthew 4:14-16.) The householder was pleased, and he invited the Bible students back the next week. He also showed his neighbors what he had learned. So many people were eager to have the Bible explained to them! In 1934, the Watch Tower Society introduced a new publication specifically designed for witnessing work. It contained up to 92 questions.
9. What did this accomplish?
9 One brother named Hillary Goslin used this question book in his ministry. He found that it helped him start conversations and gave him opportunities to share the good news. But as time went on, he realized that this approach was not always effective, because people often answered without really thinking. However, this experience motivated him and others to improve their presentation of the truth. Eventually, Hillary attended Gilead School and received further training. This method proved helpful to many publishers, although some found it difficult to remember all the questions. Also, our organization sent some to the Kingdom University and they gained more skills in teaching.
LET US CONSIDER HOW TO MAKE OUR PRESENTATION INTERESTING
10, 11. How can we use questions effectively when sharing the Bible, and why is this important?
10 Our Creator wants us to help others learn about God and become his friends. To do so, we need to be tactful and show genuine interest in people. Using questions skillfully can help us reach the hearts of those who are seeking the truth. (Read Matthew 9:37.) For example, during the 1900s, questions were used to help many people come into contact with Jehovah's Witnesses. Brother Charles Taze Russell used the telegraph to send Bible texts along with questions to fellow workers. These texts would then be used to start conversations. Soon, thousands of volunteers began using this method to spread the good news throughout America, Canada, and Europe. By 1913, over 2,000 volunteers had reached 15,000,000 people with the message of God's Kingdom!
11 Another effective way to arouse interest is through public demonstrations. How did this begin? On April 16, 1922, Joseph F. Rutherford organized a demonstration in Cedar Point, Ohio, and authorized the use of radio broadcasts. Some 50,000 people attended. Then on February 24, 1924, Jehovah's Witnesses launched a radio station called WBBR. The Watchtower magazine of December 1, 1924, explained the purpose of using this new tool: "Of all the means we have employed, none has been more effective in reaching the masses than the radio, because it carries the message directly into their homes." Radio broadcasting helped reach many more people than was possible otherwise, and it proved to be very economical.
12. (a) What will motivate you to reach out to more people? (b) Why is it important to remain confident when trying to reach out to more people?
12 Today, we have many opportunities to reach out to more people. This includes door-to-door ministry, informal witnessing, street work, conventions, and reaching out to people online. However, remaining confident can sometimes be challenging, especially like young brother Angelo Manera, Jr., who wrote: "At first, I was afraid to speak about my faith, fearing what others might think, whether they would ridicule me, or whether I would say something wrong. But I wanted to honor Jehovah and share his Word." We can make good use of our initial efforts to preach, and we can also improve our skills over time, thus honoring Jehovah and showing our gratitude for his provision.—Read 2 Corinthians 12:9, 10.
13. What valuable resource does JW.ORG offer to help us in our preaching work? What specific features of this website may be helpful?
13 Many publishers find JW.ORG to be a valuable tool in their preaching work, offering access to over 700 Bible-based articles and videos. On average, some 1,600,000 people visit the site each month. And because the site is available in so many languages, it helps reach millions of people around the world.
HELP PUBLISHERS IMPROVE THEIR SKILLS
14. How can experienced publishers assist others, and what training school has proven effective?
14 We need to be patient and understanding when helping our brothers and sisters improve their skills. But how can we offer assistance? By working alongside them, an experienced publisher can observe a brother or sister while he preaches and then offer constructive suggestions. Experienced publishers can also help others learn how to use this tool effectively, and they can share practical tips on how to prepare and conduct studies. In 1943, Nathan H. Knorr suggested starting a school to train publishers to make better use of their time. What was the result? The Watchtower Bible School of Gilead was established in 1943. That school has helped thousands of publishers become more effective.
15. (a) What questions did we answer regarding the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead? (b) What spiritual insight does Psalm 32:8 provide?
15 Many people were eager to improve their ministry. Young Julio S. Ramirez volunteered to attend that school in 1944. What motivated him? He said: "I wanted to serve Jehovah fully." He traveled from his home in the Dominican Republic to the United States! He wrote: "The journey was difficult, but I was determined to succeed." He added: "I dedicated my life to Jehovah and promised to do everything I could to preach the good news." Others also made sacrifices to attend the school. One young man named Angelo Manera recalled what happened when he was a boy: "My parents had very little money, but they encouraged me to pursue my goal. They sold some of their belongings so that I could afford to go, and they told me: 'We will manage.'" He continued: "I attended the school and graduated, and I have always been grateful for their support." Are you willing to make sacrifices—perhaps giving up something valuable or working extra hard—to accomplish your goals? Trust in Jehovah, and he will help you.—Read Psalm 32:8.
16. What did the Gilead School teach its students to do (a) effectively and (b) in 2011?
16 Jehovah's people value the training they receive at the Kingdom Ministry School. The Gilead School has trained many capable men and women. One school instructor described one of its aims as "to train zealous preachers who are not afraid to work hard." Since the Gilead School was established in 1943, over 8,500 graduates have benefited from its instruction. Graduates often serve where there is greater need, and some 170 countries have been served by Gilead-trained missionaries. In 2011, those graduating from the school were assigned to full-time service in various lands. These included circuit overseers, traveling overseers, Bethel families, or missionaries serving where the need is great.
17. What important quality does the Gilead School cultivate?
17 Does the Gilead School cultivate an important quality? Consider this example. On August 8, 1949, Japan had ten major islands devastated by war. That year, 13 graduates of the Gilead School arrived in Japan and demonstrated outstanding courage. By then, there were some 216,000 Witnesses in Japan, and half of them were active publishers!
18. Mention other schools that have equipped ministers to expand the good news.
18 Other schools include the Pioneer Service School, the Missionary School, the Kingdom Evangelizers School, the Public Speaking School, and the Schools for Ministerial Training in regional centers. These schools have trained many, and their graduates have greatly expanded the work of preaching. So continue to support our brothers!
19. Did Charles Taze Russell originate the practice of giving ministerial training, and if so, did he see his efforts bear fruit? What evidence shows that he did?
19 It has been over 100 years since the Watch Tower Society began its operations. Our Leader, Jesus Christ, continues to instruct us. In 1916, Charles Taze Russell appointed a committee to prepare a discourse, and he presented a talk that contained this thought: "As the people continue to grow in numbers, and continue to increase, the 'harvest work' will be completed within a short time." (Faith on the March, by A. H. Macmillan, p. 69) This publisher saw the fulfillment of that prophecy! Let us therefore rejoice knowing that our God continues to bless us despite our imperfections! So let us cooperate with "every good endeavor" so that we can walk in his ways!
^kal. 2 This reason is why some others also believe that the purpose of this organization is to teach about Christ. What is the reason? Paul wrote to the Corinthians and said that there were 'some who missed the occasion.' And he continued to explain this matter by saying: "Many of you I have met personally, and I found you imperfect." This thing shows that Paul and Christ both knew that the messengers had imperfections and many others had flaws in the things that Jesus taught them.

text:
"Maũndũ asu . . . maandĩkiwe kwondũ wa ũtũtaa ithyĩ, ala tũvikĩwe nĩ mũminũkĩlyo wa mavĩnda."
MBATHI: 11, 29
1, 2. Twĩneenea ngelekany'o sya ala asumbĩ ana ma Yuta nĩkĩ?
ŨKONA mũndũ esĩle kasĩlanĩ kana na aitiũũka aivalũka nthĩ, we ũkinyĩla vo wĩyĩelele? Vate nzika, ndwĩka ũu! Kũsũanĩa mavĩtyo ala meekwa nĩ andũ angĩ no kũtume twĩkala twĩsũvĩĩte tũikamasyokee. Kyalo kitũ kya Kĩklĩsto kĩilyĩ oou. No twĩmanyĩsye maũndũ ma vata twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mavĩtyo ala meekiwe nĩ andũ amwe mawetetwe Mbivilianĩ.
2 Ala asumbĩ ana ma Yuta mawetetwe ĩsomonĩ ĩvĩtu mamũthũkũmaa Yeova na ngoo mbĩanĩu. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, no meekie mavĩtyo manene. Ngewa yoo yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ, na tũtonya kwĩsũvĩa ata tũikasyokee mavĩtyo asu moo? Kũvindĩĩsya ĩũlũ wa andũ asu no kũtume tũtetheka nĩ maũndũ ala maandĩkiwe tene kwondũ wa kũtũmanyĩsya.—Soma Alomi 15:4.
KWĨKWATYA ŨMANYI WA MŨNDŨ NĨ MŨISYO
3-5. (a) Nĩ thĩna wĩva wakwatie Asa o na kau nĩwamũthũkũmaa Yeova na ngoo mbĩanĩu? (b) Nĩ maũndũ meva methĩwa matumie Asa ekwatya ũmanyi wa andũ ĩla wavithũkĩiwe nĩ Mbaasa?
3 Ekai twambe kũneena ĩũlũ wa Asa, na tũyona ũndũ Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtonya kũtũtethya. Asa nĩwamwĩkwatisye Yeova ĩla wavithũkĩiwe nĩ ita milioni ĩmwe sya Ethiovia. Ĩndĩ ndaaĩka ũu ĩla woonie ũla mũsumbĩ wa Isilaeli weetawa Mbaasa ambĩĩa kwĩyũmbany'a amũkite. Ĩvinda yĩu Mbaasa ambĩĩe kwaka ĩla ndũa ya Lama yaĩ vakuvĩ vyũ na mũvaka wa ũsumbĩ wa Asa nĩ kana amĩlũlũmĩlye. (2 Mav. 16:1-3) Asa oona ũu eekwatisye ũĩ wake mwene na athi kwa Mũsumbĩ Mbeni-aatati wa Silia na amũĩva nĩ kana avithũkĩe Mbaasa. Kamũvango kau ka Asa nĩkamũtethisye? Mbivilia ĩsũngĩĩte ũũ: "Yĩla Mbaasa wewie ũu, aeka kwaka Lama, na aũngamya wĩa wake." (2 Mav. 16:5) Kwoou we Asa amanyie nĩwatetheka!
4 Ĩndĩ we Yeova oonie ata mũvango ũsu wa Asa? Ngai atũmie Aanani akamũkany'e nũndũ wa kũlea kũmwĩkwatya. (Soma 2 Mavinda 16:7-9.) Aanani amũtavisye ũũ: "Kuma yu ũkeethĩwa na makaũ." Kwoou o na kau Mbaasa nĩwatũngĩthiw'e aekana na mũvango wake, kuma ĩvinda yĩu Asa na andũ make mambĩĩe kũkitwa nĩ amaitha nginya mũthyanĩ wa ũsumbĩki wake.
5 O tondũ ĩsomo ĩvĩtu yĩwetete, ĩla Ngai wathianie ngoo ya Asa, oonie kana yaĩ mbĩanĩu. (1 Asu. 15:14) Ngai asisya Asa oonaa mũndũ wĩyumĩtye ũndũ ũtonya eanĩsye kwenda kwake. O na vailyĩ ũu, aĩ no nginya akethe mosyao ma ũtwi wake mũthũku. Ĩvinda yĩu Asa wavithũkĩiwe nĩ Mbaasa eekwatisye ũmanyi wake mwene na amwĩkwatya Mbeni-aatati vandũ va kũmwĩkwatya Yeova. Nĩkĩ weekie ũu? We nĩwĩthĩwa asũanĩie kana kũtata kũtũmĩa ũĩ wake nĩ kana ew'ane na amaitha make, kana kwĩkwatya ũtethyo wa ita sya kaũ kwaĩ kũtonya kũmũtethya kũte kũmwĩkwatya Ngai? Nĩwĩthĩwa asũanĩie ũu wasũanĩie nũndũ wa kũnengwa ũtao mũthũku nĩ andũ angĩ?
6. Ngewa ya Asa yĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ? Nengane ngelekany'o.
6 We nũkũeka ngewa ĩsu ya Asa ĩũtethye ũsũanĩe ũndũ wĩkaa motwi? Nĩ laisi mũno kwona ve vata wa kũmwĩkwatya Yeova ĩla twakwatwa nĩ maũndũ maito. Ĩndĩ twĩkaa ata twakomana na tũmathĩna tũla tũngĩ tũkomanaa natw'o kĩla mũthenya? Nĩtwĩkwatasya ũmanyi witũ kwa kũtata kũmina mathĩna asu ũndũ ithyĩ ene twĩsĩ? Kana twonanasya nĩtũmwĩkwatĩtye Yeova atũtetheesye kũmina mathĩna maitũ kwa kũmantha myolooto ya Mbivilia na tũitata kũmĩatĩĩa? Kwa ngelekany'o, andũ ma mũsyĩ nĩmatonya kũũvĩnga nũndũ wa kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma kĩkundi kana o ũmbanonĩ mũna mũnene. No ũmũvoye Yeova aũtongoesye na aiũtetheesya ũmanye nesa ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka. Kana nata ũkesa kwĩthĩa ũte wĩanĩ, na ndũkwona ũikwata wĩa ũngĩ mĩtũkĩ? Ĩla wesa kũkomana na mũndũ ũtonya kũkũandĩka, no ũmũtavye kana kĩla kyumwa ũkendaa mwanya wa kũthi maũmbanonĩ ma katĩ katĩ wa kyumwa? O na ũkakwatwa nĩ thĩna wĩva, nũseo ũkalilikanaa ndeto ii sya mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli: "Mwiĩe Yeova nzĩa yaku; mũĩkĩĩe we, nake akeeka."—Sav. 37:5.
VE ŨTHŨKU MWAŨ WA KŨNYUVA KĨTINDO KĨTHŨKU?
7, 8. Nĩ mavĩtyo meva Yeosavati weekie, na kwaendie ata? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 23.)
7 Nata ĩũlũ wa mwana wa Asa ũla weetawa Yeosavati? Aĩ na nguma mbingĩ mũno nzeo. Na nũndũ wa kũmwĩkwatya Ngai, Yeosavati nĩweekie maũndũ maingĩ maseo. Ĩndĩ o nake no weekie motwi mathũku. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwavangie mwanae atwae mwĩĩtu wa Mũsumbĩ Aavu, ũla waĩ mũsumbĩki mũthũku wa ila mbaĩ ĩkũmi sya Isilaeli. Na ĩvinda yĩngĩ nĩwoosanie na Aavu o ũsu mathi kũkita na Asilia, o na kau nĩmakanĩtw'e nĩ mwathani Mikaia. Kaũnĩ ũsu Yeosavati avĩtĩie o vanini kũawa. Kuma vau asyokie Yelusaleme. (2 Mav. 18:1-32) Nĩvo ĩndĩ mwathani Yeu wamũkũlilye: "Nĩwaĩle kũtethya athũku, na kũmenda ala mamũmenaa Yeova?"—Soma 2 Mavinda 19:1-3.
8 We Yeosavati nĩweemanyĩisye kĩndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu? O na kau nĩwaendeeie kwonany'a kana aĩ na kĩthito kya kũmwendeesya Ngai, eoneka ti ta waaĩmanyĩsya kĩndũ ĩvindanĩ yĩu wavoneie kĩtoo aendete kũtetheesya Aavu kaũnĩ. O na ndeto sya Yeu ti ta syaamũtethya. Asyokie eekwatany'a na mũsumbĩ ũngĩ waĩ mũmaitha wa Ngai. Mũsumbĩ ũsu aĩ mwana wa Aavu weetawa Aasia. Yeosavati na Aasia maseũvisye meli me ngwatanĩo, ĩndĩ iyaamatethya nũndũ syatũlĩkangile vyũ o na mataitũmĩĩte.—2 Mav. 20:35-37.
9. Ve ũthũku mwaũ wa kũnyuva kĩtindo kĩthũku?
9 Ngewa ĩsu ya Yeosavati nĩyaĩle kũtuma twĩthiana ithyĩ ene. Twaĩle kwĩthiana ũndũnĩ wĩva? Yeosavati aĩ mũsumbĩ mũseo maũndũnĩ maingĩ. Eekaa ũla Yeova wonaa wĩ ũseo, na 'nĩwamũmanthie na ngoo yake yonthe.' (2 Mav. 22:9) Ĩndĩ ũu w'onthe ndwaĩ ũmũsũvĩa ndakakwatwe nĩ mathĩna nũndũ wa itindo nthũku. Kwalilikana nthimo ĩno ĩveveewe nĩ Ngai: "Endaa na andũ oĩ, ũkeethĩwa mũĩ; ĩndĩ ũla ũtindanasya na ndia akathĩna." (Nth. 13:20) Twĩtetheka ata? Nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũyenda kũtetheesya ala mekwendeew'a memanyĩsye ũw'o. Ĩndĩ lilikana kana ĩla Yeosavati weekwatanisye na Aavu esaa kũvoaĩwa. O ta ũu, kũlikana mũno na andũ ala matamũthũkũmaa Yeova nĩkũtonya kũtũetee mathĩna.
10. (a) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũkonetye kũtwaana kana kũtwawa tũkwĩmanyĩsya ngewanĩ ya Yeosavati? (b) Twaĩle kwĩkala tũlilikene kyaũ?
10 Nĩ ũndũ mwaũ ũtonya kũtũtethya ngewanĩ ĩsu ya Yeosavati? Mũklĩsto nũtonya kwambĩĩa kwenda kwĩvaany'a na mũndũ ũtamwendete Yeova, aisũanĩa atĩ ndesa kũkwata Mũklĩsto ũngĩ ũmwaĩlĩte. Kana Mũklĩsto nũtonya kwambĩĩa kũthing'ĩĩw'a nĩ andũ ma mũsyĩ amanthe mũndũ ndakese kũkũa ate na mũsyĩ. Ti ũu wĩ w'oka. Angĩ nĩmatonya kwĩw'a ta mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe waisye atĩĩ: "Tũmbĩtwe twĩ na wendi wa kwendwa na kwĩthĩwa na mũtindany'a." Mũklĩsto avika vau aĩle kwĩka ata? Kũsũanĩa kĩla kyamũkwatie Yeosavati no kũmũtethye. Mavinda maingĩ Yeosavati nĩweekwatasya Ngai amũtongoesye. (2 Mav. 18:4-6) Ĩndĩ kwaendie ata ĩla Yeosavati woosanie na Aavu, nake ndamwendete Yeova? Yeosavati aĩle kwĩthĩwa alilikanile kana Yeova amanthaa ala ngoo yoo ĩmwelekele yĩ mbĩanĩu. O na ũmũnthĩ ũũ metho ma Ngai "maendaa kũũ na kũũ nthĩ yonthe," na nĩwĩyũmbanĩtye 'kwĩyonany'a e vinya' kwondũ witũ. (2 Mav. 16:9) Nũeleawa thĩna witũ na nũtwendete. We mwene nũĩkĩĩaa kana Ngai akakũmanthĩa mũtindany'a mũseo ũkwendete na ũkwaĩle? Ĩthĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo kana mũthenya ũkavika eke ũu!
NDŨKAEKE NGOO YAKU ĨKWATWE NĨ MĨTŨLYO
11, 12. (a) Nĩ kyaũ Esekia weekie kyoonany'a kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ yake? (b) Nĩkĩ Ngai wamũekeie Esekia?
11 Kĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya ngewanĩ ya Esekia kĩkonetye ngoo. Ĩvinda yĩmwe ũla ũthianaa ngoo nĩwavuanisye kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ ya Esekia. (Soma 2 Mavinda 32:31.) Ĩla Esekia waĩ mũwau mũno, Ngai nĩwamũnengie wonany'o nĩ kana amanye nũkũvoa. Atumie muunyĩ ũsyoka na ĩtina. Ĩtina wa vau, nĩvatonyeka anene ala maĩ mbee ũsumbĩnĩ wa Mbaviloni makethĩwa matũmie andũ makamũkũlye ĩũlũ wa wonany'o ũsu. (2 Asu. 20:8-13; 2 Mav. 32:24) Ĩvinda yĩu Ngai 'nĩwamũekie' onany'e kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ yake. Na kwoou ĩla Ambaviloni asu mookie amonisye "nyũmba yonthe yĩ na syĩndũ syake syĩ vata mũno." Ũndũ ũsu wa ũtumanu woonanisye 'w'onthe ũla waĩ ngoonĩ yake.'
12 Mbivilia ndĩtũtavĩtye kĩla kyatumie ngoo ya Esekia ĩkwatwa nĩ mĩtũlyo. Nĩwĩthĩwa akwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo nũndũ nĩwasindie Aasuli kana nũndũ nĩwavoiw'e nĩ Ngai na kyama? Kana nĩwĩthĩwa akwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo nũndũ wa "ũthwii na ndaĩa mbingĩ mũno" ila waĩ nasyo? O na vakethĩwa vailyĩ ata, Esekia nĩwakwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo, na nũndũ wa ũu "ndaaĩka . . . kwĩanana na ũseo ũla wekiwe." Ũsu ko ũtaĩ ũndũ wa kũmakya mũno! Ndaamwendeesya Ngai o na kau navu ĩtina amwĩsũvĩte aimwĩa kana nĩwamũthũkũmĩte na ngoo yonthe. Ũseo nĩ kana ĩtina 'Esekia nĩweenyivisye,' na nũndũ wa ũu ũthilĩku wa Ngai ndwaamũkĩa we na andũ make.—2 Mav. 32:25-27; Sav. 138:6.
13, 14. (a) Nĩ ĩndĩĩ Yeova ũtonya 'kũtũeka atũtate'? (b) Twaĩle kwĩka ata twakathwa nũndũ wa ũndũ mũna tweanĩsya?
13 Kũsoma ngewa ya Esekia na kũmĩsũanĩa kũtonya kũtũtetheesya ata? Lilikana kana mĩtũlyo ya Esekia yoonekie nesa ĩtina wa Yeova kũsinda Senakelivu, na ĩtina wa kũmũvosya ũwau waĩ mũthũku mũno. Nao nata ithyĩ? Ĩla tweanĩsya ũndũ mũna wa vata, nĩvatonyeka Yeova akethĩwa 'aitũeka atũtate' nĩ kana kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ yitũ kyumĩle nesa? Kwa ngelekany'o, mwana-a-asa nũtonya kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingĩ aseũvye ũvoo nĩ kana awumye mbee wa ĩkomano ĩnene. Amina kũwumya nũtonya kũkathwa mũno nĩ andũ aingĩ. Akathwa ũu aĩle kwĩka ata?
14 Ĩla twakathwa nĩtwaĩle kũatĩĩa ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Mweeka maũndũ onthe ala mwĩaĩwe, aasyai, Twĩ ngombo ite ũtandĩthyo; nĩtwĩkĩte maũndũ ala twaĩlĩtwe nĩ kwĩka." (Luka 17:10) Vaa ve kĩndũ tũkwĩmanyĩsya ũndũnĩ ũsu wakwatie Esekia. Oonanisye kana aĩ na mĩtũlyo nũndũ "ndaaĩka . . . kwĩanana na ũseo ũla wekiwe." Kũsũanĩa maũndũ ala Yeova ũtwĩkĩte kũkatũtetheeasya tũikethĩwe na mĩtũlyo. Kĩu kĩkatumaa tũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea. Twaĩle kwĩka ũu nũndũ nĩwe ũtũnengete Maandĩko Matheu na veva wake mũtheu nĩ kana atũtetheesye ta twĩ andũ make.
NDŨKEKE ŨTWI ŨSEMBETE
15, 16. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva Yosia weekie watuma Yeova aema kũmũsũvĩa na watuma we mwene akw'a?
15 Mũthya vyũ twĩneenea Mũsumbĩ Yosia. Nĩ ũkany'o wĩva tũkwataa twasũanĩa kĩla kyamũkwatie o na kau aĩ mũsumbĩ mũseo? Kwasũanĩa kĩla kyatumie asindwa na akw'a. (Soma 2 Mavinda 35:20-22.) Mbivilia yaĩtye kana Yosia 'aumaalile okite' na Mũsumbĩ Neko wa Misili, o na kau Neko nĩwamũtavisye kana ndookĩte kũkita nake. Ĩsyokete ĩkasya kana ndeto isu sya Neko "syaumĩte kanyw'anĩ wa Ngai." Nĩkĩ ĩndĩ Yosia waumaalile akokite na Neko? Mbivilia ndĩwetete.
16 Kwoou Yosia esaa kũmanya ata kana ndeto sya Neko syaumĩte kũla kwĩ Yeova? Aĩle kwĩthĩwa akũlilye Yelemia nũndũ aĩ ũmwe wa ala athani aĩkĩĩku. (2 Mav. 35:23, 25) Ĩndĩ vai vandũ vonanĩtye kana nĩweekie ũu. Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana we Neko aendete Kalikemisi akokite "na nyũmba" ĩngĩ, ĩndĩ ndookĩte kũkita na Yelusaleme. Na eka ũu, kaũ ũsu ndwakonetye ĩsyĩtwa ya Ngai, nũndũ Neko ndaauma Yeova na ndaauma andũ make. Kwoou Yosia nĩwavĩtisye ĩla waendie kũkita na Neko. Ve ũndũ ũkwona vau tũtonya kũtũmĩa? Ĩla twĩ thĩnanĩ nũseo kũsisya tũmanye Yeova we eenda twose ĩtambya yĩva.
17. Tũkesa kũkwatwa nĩ thĩna mũna, tũtonya kwĩka ata tũikasyokee ĩvĩtyo ta yĩla Yosia weekie?
17 Tũkesa kũkwatwa nĩ ũndũ na ũyĩthĩa no nginya twĩke ũtwi, nũseo tũkamba kũsũanĩa nĩ myolooto yĩva yĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩtonya kũtũtetheesya, na tũisũanĩa ũndũ tũtonya kũmĩtũmĩa. O na mavinda amwe nũseo kũkũlya atumĩa ũtao. Nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa tũsũanĩĩte mũno maũndũ ala twĩsĩ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu, na nĩtũtonya kwĩthĩwa twĩkĩte ũkunĩkĩli mavukunĩ maitũ. Ĩndĩ atumĩa no matũtetheesye kwa kũtwony'a myolooto ĩngĩ ya Mbivilia twaĩlĩte kũsũanĩa. Ekai twose ngelekany'o ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũtwaĩtwe nĩ mũndũũme ũte Ngũsĩ. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩwĩsĩ kana nĩwaĩlĩte kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo. (Meko 4:20) Ĩndĩ twasye mũthenya ũmwe mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu avangĩte kũthi kũtavany'a mũũme nĩwamwĩa eenda matinde vau mũsyĩ. Mũũme nũtonya kũmwĩa mela kũtindany'a ĩmwe tene na no ende meke kaũndũ kana me vamwe. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu atonya kwĩka ata? No asũanĩe mĩsoa mĩna Mbivilianĩ ĩkonetye ũndũ ũsu, ta mũsoa ũla waĩtye twaĩle kũmwĩw'a Ngai na ũla ũngĩ ũtũtavĩtye kana nĩtwaĩle kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a. (Mt. 28:19, 20; Meko 5:29) Ĩndĩ vamwe na ũu, nĩwaĩle kũlilikana kana kĩveti nĩkyaĩle kũmwĩnyivĩsya mũũme na kana nũseo kũmĩĩsya angĩ. (Aev. 5:22-24; Avi. 4:5) We mũũme nũmũvataa vyũ aithi kũtavany'a, kana no mũthenya ũsu ũmwe ũkũmũkũlya eke ũndũ ũngĩ? Nũseo tũkethĩwa na wũmĩĩsyo nĩ kana twĩanĩsye kwenda kwa Ngai na tũitata twĩthĩwe na wasya mũseo wa ngoo.
MŨTHŨKŨME YEOVA NA NGOO MBĨANĨU NAKE AKAKŨATHIMA
18. Ngewa sya asumbĩ ana ala mawetwa ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ syĩkũtetheesya ata?
18 Nũndũ twĩ andũ me na naĩ, nĩtũtonya kwĩka mavĩtyo o ta ala meekiwe nĩ asumbĩ asu twaweta. Nĩtũtonya (1) kwĩkwatya ũmanyi wa andũ o na tũteũmanya, (2) kwĩkwatany'a na itindo nthũku, (3) kũkwatwa nĩ mĩtũlyo, kana (4) kwĩka motwi tũtambĩte kũsũanĩa kwenda kwa Ngai nĩ kwĩva. Yeova e ũseo mwingĩ mũno, na kwoou nĩwonaa ũseo ũla wĩ nthĩnĩ witũ o tondũ woonie ũseo wa asumbĩ asu ana. O na ĩngĩ Yeova nĩwonaa ũndũ tũmwendete mũno wĩana, na ũndũ twendete kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingangĩ tũmwendeesye vyũ. Kwoou nĩ kana tũikeke mavĩtyo manene, nũtũtavĩtye maũndũ mana meekiwe nĩ andũ ĩvinda ĩvĩtu nĩ kana methĩwe ũkany'o kwitũ. Ekai ĩndĩ tũvindĩĩsye ngewa isu syĩ Mbivilianĩ na tũitũngĩaa Yeova mũvea nũndũ wasyo!
