translation:
"Jehovah proved to be generous toward me in his loving-kindness; and according to your abundance he has made my mouth full."—PSA. 3:19.
CHAPTERS 15, 16
1, 2. (a) What are some ways people show appreciation to God? (b) What will we discuss in this section?
TO SHOW appreciation, what can we do? Some may say: "I would like to show appreciation to God, but I don't know how. It seems that everything is already done for us." What is the reason for such thinking? Where does this thought come from?
2 This section will help us understand why Jehovah is a deserving God, and why it is important to express our gratitude. Also, it will help us see how we can demonstrate our appreciation for what Jehovah does for us. (1 Cor. 14:33, 40) The Bible shows us examples of how people expressed their appreciation for Jehovah's loving-kindness, so that others could learn how to avoid being selfish. And when we imitate those faithful men and women in showing appreciation for Jehovah, we strengthen the entire congregation, making it closer, more united, and more devoted.
JEHOVAH IS A GENEROUS GOD
3. Why is it important to remember that Jehovah is a generous God?
3 We need to appreciate why God is a generous God. The Bible says: "Jehovah is near to all those calling upon him; to all those calling upon him sincerely he answers." (Ps. 145:19) Let us say, "How wonderful are your works, [God]!" and "How great are your deeds!" (Job 26:14) Considering everything that has been created—the stars, the planets, and countless other things—helps us realize how much God cares about his creation. (Ps. 8:3, 4) For example, there are billions of stars, and they all shine brightly. But the amazing thing is that the light from those stars travels vast distances to reach us, and yet we can still see them! So let us be grateful for all the things we see, which help us to appreciate that Jehovah, "the One who made the eyes," and also gave us the ability to see and enjoy beauty.—Ps. 136:1, 5-9.
4. What have scientists discovered that demonstrates generosity on a large scale?
4 Scientists have helped us learn many things about the universe and our planet. They have also shown us things that make life easier in many ways. But despite all this, they have discovered that generosity on a large scale exists. For instance, people study the stars and learn about the wonders of the universe, and they share this knowledge with others, animals, and plants. Also, people have invented many tools that allow us to live more comfortably. (Eccl. 3:11) People have developed many useful tools, but sometimes they lead to problems. Why is this? One reason is that many scientists and inventors do not honor God or do not think about whether what they invent is pleasing to him. However, Jehovah continues to provide the resources needed for humans to develop new inventions.
5. How can we show that we appreciate what God provides for us?
5 In response, Jehovah provides opportunities to use what he gives us, and he expects us to use them wisely. People who study medicine or engineering, including those who design vehicles, airplanes, and computers, often face decisions about how to use their skills. For example, engineers might be able to design something that will help someone get water easily, or they might design something that will harm another person. Consider this illustration. A doctor could help one person recover from an illness, or he could help another person end his life. This is similar to the case of Cain and Abel. Cain used his opportunity to harm his brother Abel, and the result was tragic. So always remember that Jehovah expects us to use our opportunities wisely. For example, a carpenter might build a house or destroy it—it depends on what he chooses to do!
GOD VALUES OUR DECISIONS
6. How can we show that we appreciate what Jehovah provides for us?
6 One way is to use it gratefully. Let us examine whether Jehovah wants us to use what he provides for good purposes. And if there are things that seem unimportant, let us consult the Bible for guidance. By respecting God's standards and principles, we can remain loyal and please him fully.
7. Why is the Bible a reliable source of guidance?
7 The Bible is not like the books of philosophy and other Christian publications that have been altered over time. Rather, the Bible is a reliable source of guidance. It comes from God, and it was written by inspired men. Every book in the Bible has a theme that harmonizes with the overall message of the Bible. There is one main thought running through the entire Bible. That thought is connected to the promise found in Genesis 3:15, which foretold the coming of the Messiah, Jesus Christ.—Read Genesis 3:15; Matthew 6:10; Acts 11:15.
8. How did ancient Israel show gratitude?
8 The Israelites of old demonstrated their gratitude for what God provided them. For example, when they built the tabernacle, they voluntarily contributed materials for its construction. (Exodus 38:8) Also, the Israelites made regular contributions to support the Levites and those engaged in priestly service. King David organized divisions of Levites and singers to serve regularly. (1 Chronicles 23:1-6; 24:1-3) Furthermore, the rest of the Israelites willingly gave offerings, and Jehovah accepted them with appreciation.—Deuteronomy 11:26, 27; 28:1-14.
9. Why is the Christian congregation a spiritual refuge?
9 The Christian congregation is a spiritual refuge, and it provides an opportunity to learn about God's standards. Many who come to us are imperfect people. (Mark 6:1-6) In fact, some of the first Christians were former tax collectors. (Mark 15:6) However, such ones endeavored to conform to God's standards, and they proved to be valuable members of the congregation. Those appointed as overseers should be exemplary men who demonstrate love for God and his standards.—1 Timothy 3:1-13; Titus 1:5-9. Should we expect perfection from anyone in the congregation?
10. What qualities should those appointed as overseers display? (See also paragraph 9.)
10 Read Mark 16:4, 5. Former tax collectors became part of the Christian congregation and preached the good news "to everyone in Jerusalem." They did not allow their past to prevent them from doing what Jehovah wanted of them. How can we imitate their example and show confidence in God's forgiveness?
WHAT IF WE HAVE A DIFFICULT PAST?
11. Why should we not think that our past disqualifies us from serving Jehovah?
11 Should former criminals or those who have been involved in immoral conduct feel that they cannot be forgiven by God? The Bible shows that Jehovah is willing to forgive anyone who repents. (Prov. 30:16; Heb. 13:7, 17) So, if someone has wronged you, remember that Jehovah forgives people who express remorse and make amends. As Christians, we want to please God and be obedient to his commands, even if it means humbling ourselves and apologizing to others. (Read 3 John 9, 10.) Therefore, let us ask ourselves, 'Are we imitating Christ by being willing to associate with those who are trying to remain loyal to Jehovah? Are we showing genuine love and compassion toward those who have made mistakes?'
12. What practical steps can we take to help others overcome a difficult past?
12 To find out what we can do, let us consider an example from Zambia. The November 15, 2014 issue of *The Watchtower*—Study Edition* reported on the experience of a congregation in Zambia. It highlighted the case of a former criminal who was making progress spiritually. The article explained how the elders helped him to deal with feelings of guilt and shame related to his past. In addition, on January 1, 2014, some publishers were assigned to assist individuals who had a criminal record. The publisher assigned to work with such ones took time to get to know them and their circumstances. Often, these individuals were reluctant to share details about their past because they feared rejection. However, when they felt accepted, they began to open up. Sometimes, they did not even reveal their true identity to family members. (1 Tim. 3:4, 5) For this reason, both the publisher and the elders need to carefully examine whether Scriptural qualifications apply to those who wish to serve as ministerial servants or elders.—1 Tim. 3:1-10, 12, 13; 1 Pet. 5:1-3.
13. How then can we show discernment regarding those whom we associate with?
13 I have decided not to associate with certain Christians who do not live up to what they profess. They boast about their love for God yet practice wickedness, and they make light of truth and righteousness. (1 Tim. 6:3) Apparently, Paul felt similarly about some people, for he said they were "inflated with pride, blinded, and self-willed." But he kindly warned them, hoping they would come to their senses and return to their spiritual moorings. What can we learn from this? Paul advised: "Admonish them; at the same time, be patient with each one." If we do so, we may help them to see the error of their ways and to correct their conduct. (2 Thess. 3:11-15) However, there is a limit. If someone deliberately rejects correction and continues on a wrong course, we may need to disassociate ourselves from him, just as Paul did with Hymenaeus and Philetus. (1 Tim. 1:20) So, how do you feel when faced with such a situation? If you find yourself getting emotionally involved, perhaps you should prayerfully seek Jehovah's guidance and ask him to help you maintain neutrality and avoid taking sides. Remember, our goal is to please Jehovah and to uphold his standards, and that will ultimately benefit us. [1]
KEEP LOYAL TO THE CHRISTIAN CONGREGATION—IN DOCTRINE, SPIRITUALLY, AND IN UNITY
14. Can we remain loyal to the congregation if it becomes divided?
14 Yes, we can remain loyal to the congregation even if it becomes divided by adhering to the standard of God's Word. Consider the case of the first-century Corinthian congregation. Paul rebuked them for their divisions, saying they were "pneumatic," or worldly-minded. (1 Cor. 1:1, 2) It seems that some were aligning themselves with particular individuals, creating factions. Paul strongly opposed this spirit, warning against following men rather than Christ. He told them to unite in thought and purpose. (1 Cor. 3:4-7, 5:1, 5-7, 12) Let us take note of the way Paul dealt with those who caused division. He was willing to oppose even Satan himself or his demons to protect the unity of the congregation. He urged fellow Christians to "stand firm" and not allow themselves to be misled. (1 Cor. 5:1, 5-7, 12) How can we show loyalty to the congregation and help others to remain loyal to it, especially when facing pressure from those who are spiritually sick?
15. How can we remain loyal to the congregation spiritually?
15 We should learn from what happened in Corinth. Some there practiced gross immorality. And Paul asked this rhetorical question: "Is it proper for a Christian to go to court before unbelievers?" (1 Cor. 6:1-8) Such matters should be settled among Christians themselves. However, some engaged in lawsuits, defrauding one another, and associating with immoral people. Others continued practicing gross immorality, ignoring the counsel of God's organization. This could lead someone to practice conduct that would bring reproach on God's name or dishonor the congregation. [2] Therefore, we need to examine our own hearts and make sure that we are applying Jesus' teachings. (Read Matthew 5:23, 24; 18:15-17.) To this end, we must help fellow believers to maintain spiritual health.
16. Why do Jehovah's people strive to maintain unity?
16 Jehovah's organization teaches us the importance of unity. The psalmist wrote: "How good and how pleasant it is when brothers dwell together in unity!" (Ps. 133:1) Ancient Israel enjoyed peace and prosperity when they were united and cooperated. God desires his people to live in harmony, saying: "I will gather them like sheep." (Micah 2:12) Moreover, Nehemiah reminded the Jews: "This is what I mean: that you should fear Jehovah and serve him with all sincerity, turning away from idols [or, "from disunity," according to the NWT footnotes]." (Neh. 3:9) Let us always appreciate the privilege of honoring Jehovah through our unity!
17. What can we do to show that we value Christian unity?
17 Congregations can help maintain unity by extending kindness to individuals who may be experiencing difficulties or who need encouragement. Paul showed that God can use imperfect people, and he was willing to overlook minor imperfections. (Phil. 15:3) For example, Paul knew about the divisions in the Corinthian congregation, and he wrote a letter to address those problems. Also, the fact that Paul wrote a second letter to the Corinthians shows that a congregation can improve its unity if it is willing to listen to counsel. However, if a Christian repeatedly causes division and refuses to repent, loving-kindness does not require us to associate with such a person.—Acts 6:1.
18. (a) How did the Governing Body respond when there was division among the apostles? (b) What lesson can we learn from this?
18 We can learn from how the Governing Body dealt with the division among the apostles and in the Corinthian and other congregations—with patience, mildness, and loving-kindness. (1 Cor. 1:10; Eph. 4:11-13; 1 Pet. 3:8) And because they were united in their thinking, they could accomplish much more than they could individually. That is why the apostle Paul said that their ministry would not be "frustrated." (Acts 1:23) Therefore, when Christians demonstrate the fruit of the spirit and work together harmoniously, people everywhere will better appreciate the truth about Jehovah. The lesson that we can learn is that if we want to fully understand Jehovah's purpose, we must give diligent attention to the Bible and meditate on what we learn.—Ps. 71:15, 16.

text:
"Ĩthĩwa wĩ mũthangaau kũsoma, kũtaa, na kũmanyĩsya." —1 TIM. 4:13.
MBATHI: 45, 42
1, 2. (a) Ĩandĩko ya Isaia 60:22 yĩanĩĩte ata ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo? (b) Kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Yeova kya kũũ nthĩ kĩ na mavata meva ũmũnthĩ?
MBIVILIA yathanie ũũ: "Ũla mũnini akatw'ĩka ngili, na ũla mũnini akeethĩwa mbaĩ yĩ vinya." (Isa. 60:22) Wathani ũsu nũendeee kwĩanĩa mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Mwakanĩ wa ũthũkũmi wa 2015, kũnaĩ na atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ 8,220,105 me kĩthito nthĩ yonthe! Kalungu ka mũthya ka wathani ũsu nĩkaĩle kũkiita kĩla Mũklĩsto nũndũ Yeova aĩtye ũũ: "Nyie, Yeova, ngakalaata ũndũ ũsu ĩvinda yaw'o." Ĩla ndeleva wambĩĩa kũsembethya ngalĩ, ala makuĩtwe maileaa kũmanya ngalĩ ĩsu nĩsembete. O ta ũu ithyĩ nĩtũmanyĩte kana wĩa wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a nĩwambĩĩe kũkalaatwa. Ĩndĩ we a vaku wĩkĩte ata nĩ kana ũtetheesye wĩa ũsu? Nĩwĩkĩte ũndũ ũtonya nĩ kana wĩthĩwe mũtavany'a wĩ kĩthito? Ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ nĩmaendeee kũkũlya matw'ĩke mavainia ma kĩla ĩvinda kana mavainia atetheesya. Ithyĩ tyo twĩw'aa mũyo ĩla andũ aingĩ meeyumya kũthi kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ vata mũnene wa atavany'a kana meeyumya kũtetheesya o wĩa ũngĩ ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova?
2 O na ũu wĩ o vo, nĩtwonete kana ve vata mũnene wa atavany'a aingangĩ ma Ũsumbĩ. Kĩla mwaka ikundi ta 2,000 nĩsyambĩĩaw'a. Vakatw'ĩkĩka kĩla kĩkundi kyambĩĩw'a kyaĩle kwĩthĩwa na atumĩa 5, vethĩwa vayendeka atetheesya ma kĩkundi 10,000 matw'ĩkae atumĩa kĩla mwaka. Ũu nĩ kwonany'a kana ana-a-asa ngili mbingĩ methĩwa mayendeka meke maendeeo nĩ kana matw'ĩke atetheesya ma kĩkundi. O na mbee wa ũu, twĩthĩwe twĩ ana-a-asa kana twĩ eĩtu-a-asa, nĩtwaĩle 'kũthangaaa mũno mavinda onthe wĩanĩ wa Mwĩaĩi.'—1 Ako. 15:58.
KĨLA KYENDEKAA NĨ KANA TWĨKE MAENDEEO
3, 4. Nĩ kyaũ kyendekaa ngalĩkonĩ ĩ yaku nĩ kana wĩke maendeeo?
3 Soma 1 Timotheo 3:1. Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "eenda" yonanasya kũtata kwĩtũlĩĩlya ũvikĩle kĩndũ kĩ ĩũlangũ wa vala ũtonya kũvikĩla. Mũtũmwa Vaulo atũmĩie ndeto ĩsu ayonany'a kana kwĩka maendeeo ma kĩ-veva nĩkwendaa kĩthito. Kwasũanĩa mwana-a-asa ũkwendeew'a nĩ kwĩka maendeeo kĩkundinĩ kyoo. No ethĩwe yu ate mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi ĩndĩ aimanya kana nĩwaĩle kũtata ethĩwe na nguma nzeango sya Kĩklĩsto. Na kwoou mbee vyũ aitw'a kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana atw'ĩke mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi. Na ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda nũtonya kwambĩĩa kwendeew'a nĩ kũtw'ĩka mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Kwa ũkuvĩ, no nginya mwana-a-asa ũsu ekĩe kĩthito kingĩ eanĩsye nguma ila syendekaa nĩ kana avikĩĩe ianda isu syonthe.
4 O ta ũu, ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa ala me na mea ma kũtw'ĩka mavainia, kũthũkũma Mbetheli, kana kũtetheesya kwaka Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ, nĩmaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩ kana meanĩsye mĩvango yoo. Kwoou ekai twone ũndũ Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtwĩkĩĩte vinya ithyonthe twĩke maendeeo ũthaithinĩ wa w'o.
TATA MŨNO WĨKE MAENDEEO MANENANGE
5. Andũ ma mũika matonya kũtũmĩa vinya woo ata ũthũkũminĩ wa Ũsumbĩ?
5 Andũ ma mũika me vinya wa kwĩka maũndũ maingĩ ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova. (Soma Nthimo 20:29.) Ana-a-asa amwe ma mũika mathũkũmaa Mbetheli nĩmatetheeasya wĩa wa kũtumbĩthya na kũkwatany'a Mbivilia na mavuku angĩ. Namo ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ ma mũika nĩmatetheeasya wĩa wa kwaka na kũtũngĩĩa Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ. Eka ũu, ĩla mĩisyo yaumĩla andũ ma mũika nĩmatetheanĩasya na ana-a-asa angĩ me na ũmanyi kũnengane ũtethyo ũla ũkwendeka. Na mavainia aingĩ ma mũika nĩmatetheeasya kũtavya ũvoo mũseo andũ ala maneenaa kĩthyomo kya kĩsio kĩla maĩ, kana o angĩ maneenaa kĩthyomo kĩngĩ kĩeni.
6-8. (a) Mũndũ ũmwe wa mũika avĩndũie ata woni wake ĩũlũ wa ũthũkũmi wa Ngai, na kweethĩiwe ata? (b) Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana 'ũsame ũsisye kana Yeova nĩ mũseo'?
6 Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩwa wonaa ve vata mũnene wa kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Ngai na ngoo yonthe. Ĩndĩ nata ũkethĩwa wĩw'aa tondũ mwana-a-asa ũmwe wĩtawa Aaron weew'aa navu ĩtina? O na kũtw'ĩka aeiwe nĩ asyai Ngũsĩ, ĩvinda yĩmwe aisye atĩĩ: "Ve ĩvinda new'aa kũthi maũmbano na ũtavany'a kwĩ ũtulu." Ĩvindanĩ yĩu aĩ na mea ma kũmũthũkũma Ngai na ũtanu ĩndĩ asaanĩaw'a nĩkĩ ũte na ũtanu ũsu. Kwoou nĩ ĩtambya yĩva woosie?
7 Aaron nĩweekie mũvango mũseo wa kũsomaa Mbivilia, kwĩyũmbanĩsya maũmbano, na kũsũngĩa ĩla wĩ maũmbanonĩ. O na nĩwambĩĩe kũvoyaa ateũtĩĩa. Ĩla wambĩĩe kũmwenda Yeova mũno, nĩw'o wambĩĩe kwĩka maendeeo ma kĩ-veva. Kuma ĩvindanĩ yĩu Aaron nũtanĩĩte kũtavany'a e vainia, kũthũkũma na angĩ wĩanĩ wa kũnengane ũtethyo ĩla kwaumĩla mĩisyo, na kũtavany'a nthĩ ĩngĩ. Yu Aaron athũkũmaa Mbetheli na nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Ew'aa ata nũndũ wa maũndũ ala yu wĩanĩĩtye? Aĩtye atĩĩ: "'Nĩnĩsamĩte ngona kana Yeova nĩ mũseo.' Nũndũ nũngathimĩte mũno, nĩw'aa ve ũndũ naĩle kũmwĩka na nũndũ wa ũu nĩnĩmũthũkũmaa mũnango. Kĩu nĩkĩndeteae moathimo maingangĩ."
8 Mũandĩki wa Savuli aisye atĩĩ: "Ala mamũmanthaa Yeova matikaĩwa nĩ kĩndũ kĩseo o na kĩva." (Soma Savuli 34:8-10.) Vate nzika, Yeova ndasonokasya ala mamũthũkũmaa na kĩthito. Ĩla tweeka kyonthe kĩla tũtonya ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova, twĩthĩawa 'tũisama tũsisye kana nĩ mũseo.' Na ĩla twamũthaitha Ngai na ngoo yonthe, nĩtũkwataa ũtanu ũte maela.
ĨYŨMĨĨSYE VYŨ NA NDŨKANOE
9, 10. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata twĩthĩwe na veva wa 'kweteela'?
9 Ĩvindanĩ yĩla ũendeee kwĩkĩa kĩthito wĩanĩsye mĩvango yaku, nũseo ũkethĩwa na veva wa 'kweteela.' (Mika 7:7) Kĩla ĩvinda Yeova nũtetheeasya athũkũmi make aĩkĩĩku, o na kau nũtonya kũeka ĩvinda yĩvĩte matakwata ianda ila mekwenda, kana akaeka mekale nginya ĩla maũndũ moo meseũva. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla wamwathie Avalaamu mwana, yaĩ no nginya Avalaamu ethĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo na wũmĩĩsyo. (Aevl. 6:12-15) O na kau Avalaamu nĩweeteelile myaka mingĩ Isaka ayĩsa kũsyawa, ndaakw'a ngoo nake Yeova ndaamũsonokya.—Mwa. 15:3, 4; 21:5.
10 Kũmĩĩsya kũi laisi. (Nth. 13:12) Tũkatindĩa kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa ianda ila twendaa tũnengwe, no tũkw'e ngoo vyũ. Vandũ va ũu, nũseo tũkatũmĩa ĩvinda yitũ kũtata kwĩthĩwa Aklĩsto aseango me na nguma ila itonya kũtũtetheesya tũvikĩĩe kĩanda kĩna kĩkundinĩ. Ekai twone maũndũ atatũ matonya kũtũtetheesya twĩke ũu.
11. Nĩ nguma syĩva tũtonya kwĩkĩa kĩthito twĩthĩwe nasyo, na nĩkĩ nĩ sya vata?
11 Tata wĩthĩwe na nguma ila syaĩle. Ĩla twasoma Ndeto ya Ngai na twamĩsũanĩa, nĩtũkwataa ũĩ, ũmanyi, kĩlĩko, na nĩtũmanyaa kũsila katĩ. Nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno ala matongoetye ũthaithinĩ wa w'o makethĩwa na nguma ta isu. (Nth. 1:1-4; Tito 1:7-9) O na ĩngĩ ĩla tũũsoma mavuku maitũ, nĩtũmanyaa woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa maũndũ me kĩvathũkany'o. Kĩla mũthenya nĩtũkomanaa na maũndũ makonetye kwĩtanĩthya, mĩkĩĩle ya ngũa na kwĩyanakavya, mĩtũmĩĩle ya mbesa, na kwĩkalany'a na andũ angĩ. Ĩndĩ twaatĩĩa kĩla tũkwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilianĩ, twĩthĩawa tũtonya kwĩka motwi meũmwendeesya Yeova.
12. Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana no twĩkwatw'e kĩkundinĩ?
12 Onany'a kana wĩ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩkwatw'a. Twĩthĩwe twĩ ana-a-asa kana twĩ eĩtu-a-asa, no nginya twĩke ũndũ tũtonya twĩanĩsye kĩanda kĩla twanewa ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Neemia waĩ ngavana nĩwoonie ve na vata wa kũnyuva amwe andũnĩ ma Ngai nĩ kana amanenge mawĩa mana. Ĩndĩ anyuvie aaũ? Anyuvie ala mamũkĩaa Ngai, maĩ kĩthito, na maĩ ma kwĩkwatw'a. (Nee. 7:2; 13:12, 13) O na ũmũnthĩ "veendwa asũvĩinĩ, mũndũ oneke e kĩthito." (1 Ako. 4:2) Kĩthito kitũ kya kwĩka maũndũ maseo kĩilea kwoneka.—Soma 1 Timotheo 5:25.
13. Ũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya Yosevu ĩla angĩ makwĩka ũndũ ũtaĩle?
13 Eka Yeova aũtetheesye. Ũtonya kwĩka ata ĩla angĩ makwĩka ũndũ ũtaĩle? Nũtonya kwosa ĩtambya na mĩtũkĩ nĩ kana waĩlye maũndũ. Ĩndĩ mavinda amwe kwĩtetea mũno kwĩkaa kwananga maũndũ. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya Yosevu. Ana-a-ĩthe nĩmamũthĩnisye mũno ĩndĩ we ndaaĩkalya ũthatu ngoonĩ yake. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda Yosevu nĩwailĩĩlwe ũvũngũ na oovwa vate kĩtumi. Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ oou, nĩwamwĩkwatisye Yeova amũtongoesye ĩvindanĩ yĩu waĩ na thĩna. Kweethĩiwe ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye "ndeto ya Yeova nĩyamũtatie," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nĩyamũtetheeisye atw'ĩka mũndũ mũseango. (Sav. 105:19) Ĩla matatwa asu mesie kũthela, Yosevu aĩ atonya kũnewa kĩanda kya mwanya. (Mwa. 41:37-44; 45:4-8) Ĩla wakwatwa nĩ maũndũ metu voyaa Ngai aũnenge ũĩ na vinya, na ĩla ũũneena na kwĩka maũndũ tata kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũuu. Vate nzika, Yeova akaũtetheesya.—Soma 1 Vetelo 5:10.
ĨKA MAENDEEO WĨANĨ WA KŨTAVANY'A
14, 15. (a) Nĩkĩ ve vata wa kũsisya nesa ũndũ tũtavanasya? (b) Ũtonya kwĩka ata ĩla maũndũ kĩsionĩ kyenyu mavĩndũka? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 20 na ĩsandũkũ yĩla yĩ na kyongo, "We no Wende Kũtata Nzĩa Ĩngĩ ya Kũtavany'a?")
14 Vaulo athangaaisye Timotheo na ndeto ii: "Ĩthĩwa wĩ mũthangaau kũsoma, kũtaa, na kũmanyĩsya. Ĩsũvĩe mwene, vamwe na momanyĩsyo maku." (1 Tim. 4:13, 16) Vaulo aiandĩka ndeto isu Timotheo aĩ akwatie ũmanyi wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. Ĩndĩ ũtavany'a wake wesaa kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũseango 'asũvĩa' momanyĩsyo make, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, asisya nesa ũndũ wamanyĩasya. Andũ no mamwĩthukĩĩasya ĩndĩ ndaaĩle kwĩanĩwa nĩ ũu. Nĩ kana aendeee kũmakiita ngoo, aaĩle kũvĩndũa nzĩa syake sya kũtavany'a syosane na mavata ma andũ ala ũkũtavya. O ta ũu, ithyĩ atavany'a ma ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ nĩtwaĩle kwĩka ũu.
15 Mavinda maingĩ ĩla tũũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba tũyĩthĩaa ene. O na isionĩ ingĩ tũyĩtĩkĩlaw'a kũlika nyũmbanĩ imwe. Ethĩwa maũndũ asu nĩmethĩawa kĩsionĩ kyenyu, wĩona ata ũkatata kũtũmĩa nzĩa ingĩ sya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo?
16. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũkwate mosyao maseo ĩla tũũtavany'a kũla kwĩthĩawa andũ aingĩ?
16 Kũtavany'a kũla kwĩthĩawa andũ aingĩ nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe nzeo vyũ ya kũnyaĩĩkya ũvoo mũseo. Aingĩ ma Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmakwatĩte mosyao maseo kwa kũtavany'a kũndũ ta kũu. Nĩmamanthaa ĩvinda ya kũtavany'a isesenĩ sya ngalĩ ya mwaki, iwanzanĩ sya ngalĩ, masokonĩ, kũla kũthũmũĩlaa andũ, na kũndũ kũngĩ ta kũu kwĩ andũ aingĩ. Mũtavany'a no atũmĩe kĩlĩko akamanya ethĩwa eambĩĩsya ũneenany'a na mũndũ ũngĩ kwa kũweta ũvoo mũna ũwetiwe mĩvĩanĩ ya maũvoo, kũweta ũndũ mũseo ĩũlũ wa syana syake, kana eĩka o kũmũkũlya ĩkũlyo ĩũlũ wa wĩa wake. Ĩvindanĩ yĩu maendeee kũea ngewa, mũtavany'a ũsu no awete ũndũ ũkonetye Maandĩko na aimũkũlya woni wake. Mavinda maingĩ ũsũngĩo ũla ũkũnengwa nũtumaa maendeea kũneenea Mbivilia mũnango.
17, 18. (a) Ũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana wĩthĩwe na ũkũmbaũ wa kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ wingĩ wa andũ? (b) Kũsũanĩa wendi ũla Ndaviti waĩ naw'o wa kũmũtaĩa Yeova kũtonya kũũtetheesya ata ĩla wĩ ũtavany'a?
17 Ethĩwa nũemawa nĩ kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ, ndũkakw'e ngoo. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ya vainia ũmwe umĩte New York City wĩtawa Eddie. Eddie nĩwakĩaa kũneena na andũ vandũ ve wingĩ. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩvinda, nĩwakwatie ũkũmbaũ. Nĩ kyaũ kyamũtetheeisye? Aĩtye ũũ: "Ĩla ngwĩka ũthaithi wa mũsyĩ nĩ na kĩveti kyakwa, nĩtũmanthaa ũndũ tũtonya kũtũmĩa nzĩa syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ĩla tũũsũngĩa ala matũvĩnga na angĩ me na mawoni me kĩvathũkany'o. O na nĩtũkũlasya atavany'a angĩ ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka." Yu Eddie nĩwĩthĩawa na mea ma kũtavany'a kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ.
18 O ũndũ ũendeee kũkwata ũmanyi na ũkũmbaũ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo, now'o angĩ makona maendeeo maku. (Soma 1 Timotheo 4:15.) O na eka ũu, ũkamũtaĩa Ĩthe witũ wa ĩtunĩ o tondũ Ndaviti weekie. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ngamũtaĩaa Yeova mavinda onthe: ndaĩa syake ikeethĩwa kanyw'anĩ wakwa mavinda onthe. Thayũ wakwa ũkekathĩĩaa nthĩnĩ wa Yeova: ala auu makeew'a ũu, na makatana." (Sav. 34:1, 2) Na nĩvatonyeka nũndũ wa kĩthito kyaku kya kũtavany'a, ala auu maketĩkĩla ũthaithi wa w'o na maitana kũthaitha vamwe naku.
MŨTAĨE NGAI KWA KWĨKA MAENDEEO MA KĨ-VEVA
19. Nĩkĩ mũthũkũmi mũĩkĩĩku wa Yeova waĩle kwĩthĩwa e mũtanu o na ethĩwa nũkwatĩtwe nĩ maũndũ momũ?
19 Ndaviti ainie ayasya: "Mawĩa maku onthe makakũtũngĩaa mũvea, ame Yeova; na atheu maku makakũtaĩaa. Makawetaa ndaĩa ya ũsumbĩ waku, na kũneenaa ũndũ wa vinya waku; nĩ kana mamanyĩthye ana ma andũ meko make me ũtonyi, na ndaĩa ya ũnene wa ũsumbĩ wake." (Sav. 145:10-12) Ndeto isu syake syĩonany'a woni wa athũkũmi onthe aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova. Ĩndĩ nata ũkethĩa ũwau kana ũkũũ nũtumĩte ũolanga kĩthito kyaku kya kũtavany'a? Lilikanaa kana ĩla watavya ala maendeee kũũsũvĩa na ala angĩ me vakuvĩ naku ũvoo mũseo, wĩthĩawa ũimũkumya Ngai witũ mũnene. Na ethĩwa wovetwe nũndũ wa mũĩkĩĩo waku, no kwĩthĩwa ĩla vaumĩla mwanya ũtavasya angĩ ũla w'o, na kĩu nĩkĩmũtanĩthasya Yeova. (Nth. 27:11) O na ĩngĩ, Yeova nũtanaa mũno ĩla twalũmany'a na mĩvango yitũ ya kũmũthaitha o na ethĩwa amwe ma mũsyĩ witũ ti Ngũsĩ. (1 Vet. 3:1-4) Kwoou o na ũkethĩwa mathĩnanĩ manenevete ata, nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka ũkamũkumya Yeova na ũyĩka maendeeo.
20, 21. Ethĩwa nũnengetwe ianda mbingangĩ ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova, ũtonya ata kwĩthĩwa ũathimo kwa ala angĩ?
20 Nĩ w'o vyũ kana Yeova akakũathimaa waendeea kwĩka maendeeo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ũkavĩndũa mĩvango yaku o vanini, no ũkwate mwanya mũnenange wa kũtavya ala mate na wĩkwatyo ĩũlũ wa ũw'o wa vata kuma kwa Ngai. O na ĩngĩ kĩthito kyaku kya kwĩka maendeeo na kwĩyumya kwaku ũmũthũkũme Ngai nĩkũtonya kũetee ana-a-asa ala angĩ moathimo maingĩ. Na nũndũ wa kũthũkũma kĩkundinĩ wĩnyivĩtye, ala angĩ mamwendete Yeova makakwenda mũno na mayĩũkwata mbau.
21 Twĩthĩwe tũthũkũmĩte Yeova kwa myaka mingĩ kana o kwa ĩvinda ya myei mĩvũthũ, ithyonthe no twĩke maendeeo ũthaithinĩ wa w'o. Ĩndĩ ala mamũthũkũmĩte Yeova ĩvinda ĩasa matonya ata kũtetheesya ala eũ meke maendeeo? Ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩyo yĩneenewe ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe.

translation:
"Let your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt." —1 TIM. 4:13.
MBATHI: 45, 42
1, 2. (a) What does Isaiah 60:22 indicate about the quality of a minister's speaking? (b) Why is the emphasis on the importance of good communication timely today?
MBIVILIA explained: "The great One has made us strong, and the great One has glorified us." (Isa. 60:22) Consider how this applies to our ministry. How can we make it effective? In 2015, some 8,220,105 people attended Kingdom Hall meetings worldwide! The encouraging thought is that each Christian can please Jehovah by praying: "Jehovah, give me skill to speak effectively." But simply praying is not enough; we need to work at improving our ability to communicate. Do you sometimes wonder what makes an excellent speaker? Or do you feel that you lack the ability to express yourself clearly? Many find that practicing helps them become better communicators. Also, young ones often benefit from observing experienced speakers. Is there someone you admire for his speaking ability? Think about what makes him so effective. And if you have opportunities to practice speaking, take advantage of them. Do you ever ask yourself, 'Am I doing my best?' Or, 'Could I improve?'
Brothers and sisters often continue to refine their communication skills, whether they are giving talks or engaging in informal conversations. Does this show that they are taking the important matter of public speaking seriously, wanting to honor Jehovah?
2 Of course, we want to be skilled speakers, but more importantly, we want to share the good news. Every year, over 2,000 new ones get baptized. They join thousands who are already actively sharing the good news, and some 10,000 are appointed as ministerial servants each year. This shows that brothers and sisters are eager to expand their ministry and that many are qualifying to do more in the preaching work. Moreover, when we help others learn about Bible truth, we are fulfilling the command to 'make disciples of people of all nations.'—1 Cor. 15:58.
EVERY EFFORT COUNTS
3, 4. What will help you to make your effort count?
3 Read 1 Timothy 3:1. The Greek word rendered "managing" conveys the thought of being diligent in caring for something valuable. The apostle Paul used this word to emphasize that being busy in God's service is commendable. So, being zealous in our ministry is like managing something precious. And just as a loving parent takes care of his child, so too does a mature Christian take the initiative to improve his own skillfulness. He also helps others to become better teachers of God's Word. In fact, he may even invite them to practice giving talks and offer constructive suggestions.
4 Thus, both brothers and sisters can find ways to improve their ability to communicate effectively, whether it is by studying examples of excellent speakers, such as Bethelites, or by practicing their presentations. But remember, the most important thing is that our efforts are motivated by love for Jehovah and a desire to please him.
TAKE THE INITIATIVE TO IMPROVE YOUR MINISTRY
5. Why should we constantly strive to improve our speaking skills?
5 Some Christians may feel shy about speaking publicly, especially when witnessing. (Read Proverbs 29:25.) However, some brothers who were once reluctant to speak up have found that serving at Bethel has helped them overcome their fear and become more confident in presenting Bible discourses. Also, many brothers and sisters benefit from preparing and delivering talks at the Kingdom Hall. By doing so, they gain experience and learn how to express themselves clearly. Furthermore, observing experienced speakers can help us identify areas where we can improve. Many fine speakers make an effort to vary their tone and pace, and some use illustrations to explain points more vividly.
6-8. (a) How might a congregation member show initiative regarding spiritual matters, and what could result? (b) What can we do to determine if we are truly "approved workers"?
6 We can demonstrate our zeal by striving to please God in all aspects of our lives. But what if someone feels inadequate? Consider the example of young Aaron. He was hesitant to speak when Moses appointed him to assist. Yet, Moses encouraged him, saying: "You will be my mouth, and I will be your God." Aaron accepted this responsibility, and he proved capable. So, too, we can pray earnestly for God's assistance and trust that he will empower us to speak effectively. To what extent does prayer help us?
7 Aaron took the initiative to study the Bible, prepare his talks, and practice his delivery. And he asked for feedback on how he could improve. He also made it a priority to meditate on Jehovah's name and to reflect on the reasons why worship is important. Furthermore, Aaron did not become discouraged when facing opposition, but he persevered despite difficulties and challenges. Yes, Aaron became a successful proclaimer, and he was respected within the congregation. Did he ever feel unqualified? He admitted: "I am inexperienced, and Jehovah is great." However, he continued to serve willingly, knowing that Jehovah would support him. This is what strengthened his confidence.
8 The psalmist David wrote: "Taste and see that Jehovah is good; happy is the man who takes refuge in him." (Read Psalm 34:8-10.) As we experience Jehovah's goodness firsthand, we develop greater faith. Therefore, let us continue to apply what we learn from the Scriptures, striving to 'taste and see' that Jehovah truly is good. And as we praise God wholeheartedly, we will enjoy peace of mind.
WHY WE NEED ENCOURAGEMENT
9, 10. What is involved in extending encouragement to others?
9 Often, when someone is struggling to maintain spiritual strength, they need practical help and encouragement from others—what the Bible calls "restoration." (Micah 7:7) At times, Jehovah uses fellow Christians to comfort those who are disheartened, and sometimes he allows them to face trials that teach endurance and strengthen their resolve. For example, Abraham grieved over the loss of his son, yet he remained faithful despite intense sorrow and disappointment. (Heb. 6:12-15) And although Abraham waited many years for Isaac to be born, he never lost confidence that Jehovah would fulfill his promise.—Gen. 15:3, 4; 21:5.
10 Hope deferred makes the heart sick. (Prov. 13:12) We can often brighten someone's day by expressing our appreciation and offering words of encouragement. By doing so, we show that we care about our brothers and sisters and want to help them remain close to Christ and active in the ministry, enabling them to find joy and satisfaction in serving Jehovah. Let us look for ways to encourage others.
11. Why do we need encouragement, and what does this reveal about Jehovah?
11 We all experience moments of discouragement. As we read God's Word and meditate on its contents, we gain wisdom, insight, and understanding, and we learn how to conduct ourselves properly. It is vital that we associate with those who are spiritually mature and are an example of faith. (Prov. 1:1-4; Titus 1:7-9) Also, as we examine our own lives, we become aware of areas where we need improvement—such as overcoming bad habits, resisting temptation, dealing with financial pressures, and getting along with others. When we humbly seek Jehovah's guidance, we can find the strength to overcome these challenges.
12. How can we show empathy, even when we have not faced similar difficulties?
12 Empathy involves trying to understand another person's feelings. Although we may not have gone through the exact same experiences, we can still offer support and encouragement, knowing that they are striving to please Jehovah. For instance, Nehemiah was deeply moved when he learned about the distress of his brothers and sisters and their opposition from enemies. What motivated him to help them? His love for God, his loyalty, and his desire to see his people prosper. (Neh. 7:2; 13:12, 13) And remember the principle: "Become imitators of those who exhibit fine qualities." (1 Cor. 4:2) Fine qualities include being willing to assist others in need.—Read 1 Timothy 5:25.
13. How might the example of Joseph encourage us when facing difficult circumstances?
13 Trust in Jehovah will help you. Can you be sure that he understands what you are going through? He can discern our thoughts and feelings. Sometimes, though, we may need to put forth effort to explain how we feel. Consider the example of Joseph. He patiently endured much mistreatment, yet he remained faithful to Jehovah. The account of Joseph shows that even when things seem hopeless, Jehovah can use powerful means to intervene. Did he forget his loyal friends? No, he remembered them and arranged for them to be rescued. This demonstrates that Jehovah remembers those who are loyal to him and will act on their behalf. Was this not fulfilled when the Bible says, "Jehovah delivered [Joseph] from confinement"? Or, in some translations, "Jehovah loosened his bonds"? (Ps. 105:19) After three years in prison, Joseph was able to give an accurate interpretation of dreams. (Gen. 41:37-44; 45:4-8) If you are struggling with problems, pray to God and ask for his guidance, and if you continue to seek his direction, you will find peace. Remember, Jehovah cares for you.—Read 1 Peter 5:10.
KEEP APPLYING YOURSELF TO BE SYMPATHETIC
14, 15. (a) What helps us to show sympathy toward others? (b) How can you be sure that your counsel is timely and appropriate? (See the article "How to Show Sympathy That Comforts," on jw.org.)
14 Paul encouraged Timothy with these words: "Keep practicing reading aloud, exhorting, and teaching. Do not neglect your gift, but cultivate it along with your discernment." (1 Tim. 4:13, 16) Paul wrote these words to Timothy because he wanted him to develop his ability to teach effectively. To improve in this area, we must strive to be discerning—to accurately assess whether someone needs encouragement or correction. People respond favorably when they sense that we genuinely care about them. They may be more willing to accept our advice if we continue to show kindness and compassion and if we take their feelings into consideration. Otherwise, our efforts to teach them may be unsuccessful.
15 Many times we visit people in their homes. But sometimes we find it difficult to reach certain individuals. If you have faced such challenges, does that mean you should give up trying to help those people spiritually?
16. How can we be sure that we are using our time wisely when we try to reach many people?
16 Reaching many people is one way to show zeal. Many of Jehovah's Witnesses have found it rewarding to share the good news with others whenever possible. This includes visiting people who are interested, return visits, conducting Bible studies, helping people to attend meetings, and assisting them to progress spiritually. When someone uses his time well, he shows that he values the privilege of helping others learn about God and His Kingdom, and he cares about their spiritual welfare. He also demonstrates that he is willing to sacrifice his own interests and activities to benefit others. Such activity continues to be pleasing, and it helps us to remain zealous in proclaiming the good news. Often, the effort we put forth results in more people being reached with the message from the Bible.
17, 18. (a) How can we be sure that we are not discouraged if we feel overwhelmed by the thought of reaching many people? (b) What lesson can we learn from David's example regarding how to maintain our zeal?
17 Showing zeal means reaching many people, but this is not always easy. Consider the experience of a brother named Eddie who lives in New York City and enjoys speaking to many people. At times, he feels overwhelmed. What has helped him to stay motivated? He says: "When I feel tired, I remind myself that my strength comes from Jehovah, and I pray for help to find ways to make my ministry effective despite the challenges I face. And I try to focus on the joy of making disciples." So Eddie remains zealous in reaching many people.
18 But how can you continue to be enthusiastic about your ministry and remain spiritually strong? Take time to meditate on what you learn. (Read 1 Timothy 4:15.) Also, regularly review your personal study of the Bible, just as David did. He said: "I will speak of all Your wonderful works; I will rejoice greatly over You. All those who seek You will exult and be joyful in You. May those who love Your salvation say continually, 'Jehovah is great!'" (Ps. 34:1, 2) By focusing on the privilege of being in the ministry, you will maintain your enthusiasm and enjoy sharing the good news with others.
SHOW ZEAL BY KEEPING BUSY
19. Why does a dedicated servant of Jehovah want to be busy in the ministry and showing zeal?
19 David wrote: "All my bones will declare Your greatness, O Jehovah; and there is none like You. I will proclaim Your wonderful works. And I will recount all Your benefits; I will extol Your praise, even to the generation and beyond." (Ps. 145:10-12) This is how all zealous servants of Jehovah feel. Do you sometimes wonder whether your efforts in the ministry really matter? If so, remember that even small acts of diligence please Jehovah. And when you use your time wisely, you show respect for Jehovah. (Prov. 27:11) Moreover, Jehovah understands that we are limited and that our circumstances may prevent us from doing as much as we would like. (1 Pet. 3:1-4) So, continue to do the best you can, and let your zeal move you to keep busy.
20, 21. How can we remain diligent in declaring Jehovah's name, even when facing difficulties?
20 It is true that Jehovah appreciates our willingness to keep busy. For example, you might be limited by your health or have little free time. But you can still find ways to serve Jehovah and make good use of whatever time you have. Also, your determination to keep busy and your sincere desire to honor God can help you overcome obstacles. And by remaining spiritually strong, you will encourage others to stay active in Jehovah's service.
21 Whether we have served Jehovah for many years or for only a short time, we should always keep busy. If some have served Jehovah faithfully for decades, why can they still not become complacent? The answer lies in the principle found in the proverb.

text:
"Mwende mũtũi waku o tondũ wĩyendete."—MT. 22:39.
MBATHI: 25, 36
1, 2. Maandĩko monanĩtye ata kana wendo nĩ wa vata mũno?
WENDO nĩw'o nguma ĩla nene Yeova Ngai wĩsĩkĩe nayo. (1 Yoa. 4:16) Yeova ambie kũmba Yesũ mbee, na kwoou Yesũ ekalanilye nake ĩtunĩ myaka ĩte ĩsavu na eemanyĩsya ũndũ Yeova wendete angĩ. (Ako. 1:15) Ĩvinda yĩla Yesũ wĩkalĩte ĩtunĩ, vamwe na ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ, nĩwonanĩtye nesa kana nũeleawa vyũ kana Yeova Ngai nĩwendete angĩ mũno, o na nũatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ĩsu yake. Kĩu kĩtumaa twĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana ĩvinda yonthe Yeova na Yesũ makasumbĩkaa kwa nzĩa ĩkwonany'a kana nĩmendete angĩ.
2 Ĩla Yesũ wakũlilw'e mwĩao ũla mũnene nĩ wĩva, asũngĩie atĩĩ: "Mwende Mwĩaĩi Ngai waku na ngoo yaku yonthe, na thayũ waku w'onthe, na kĩlĩko kyaku kyonthe. Ũu nĩw'o mwĩao ũla mũnene na wa mbee. Na wa kelĩ ũvw'anene naw'o, nĩw'o ũũ, Mwende mũtũi waku o tondũ wĩyendete."—Mt. 22:37-39.
3. Nũũ ũla tũtonya kũmwĩta "mũtũi"?
3 Wasisya nesa nũkwona kana Yesũ amina kũweta ĩũlũ wa kwenda Yeova awetie kana mwĩao wa kelĩ nĩ kwenda mũtũi. Ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a kana nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũno kwenda andũ onthe. Ĩndĩ nũũ ũla tũtonya kũmwĩta "mũtũi"? Ethĩwa nũtwaanĩte kana wĩ mũtwae, mũtũi ũla wĩ vakuvĩ naku vyũ nũsu ũtwaanĩte nake. Angĩ tũtonya kũmeta atũi nĩ ala me kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto, namo nĩ ala angĩ mathaithaa ũla Ngai wa w'o. Na ĩndĩ atũi angĩ maitũ nĩ ala tũkomanaa namo ĩla tũũtavany'a. Ala mamũthaithaa Yeova na maatĩĩaa momanyĩsyo ma Mwana wake matonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩmendete atũi moo?
ENDA ŨLA ŨTWAANĨTE NAKE
4. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya mũtwaano ũendeee nesa o na kau andũ me na naĩ?
4 Yeova nĩwe wambĩlĩĩlye mũtwaano ĩla woombie Atamu na Eva na amatw'ĩkĩthya mũndũ na mũka. Endaa mekalany'e ĩmwe tene na tene me atanu na maisyaana mausũsye nthĩ. (Mwa. 1:27, 28) Ĩndĩ ĩla maleile kũmwĩw'a Yeova, mũtwaano woo nĩwaanangĩkie na matuma naĩ na kĩkw'ũ ikwata andũ onthe. (Alo. 5:12) Ũseo nĩ kana Maandĩko nĩmatũtavĩtye ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka nĩ kana mĩtwaano yitũ ĩendeee nesa. Ũtao ũla Maandĩko matũnengete ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano nĩw'o mũseo vyũ nũndũ maumĩte kũla kwĩ Yeova, ũla nĩwe Mwambĩlĩlya wa mũtwaano.—Soma 2 Timotheo 3:16, 17.
5. Nĩkĩ ala matwaanĩte maĩle kwendana mũno?
5 Ndeto ya Ngai yonanĩtye kana no nginya andũ me ndũũ methĩwe mendanĩte mũno nĩ kenda matanĩe ngwatanĩo yoo. Ũu now'o vailyĩ mũtwaanonĩ. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkĩe kĩkundi kĩmwe atĩĩ: "Wendo nĩwũmĩĩasya, na nĩwĩkaa moseo; wendo ndwĩ na kĩwĩu; wendo ndwĩtũlasya, o na ndwĩkathĩĩaa, o na ndwĩkaa ũndũ ũtaĩle, o na ndwĩmanthĩaa syĩndũ, o na ndũthataa, na ndũtalĩlaa ũthũku; ndũtanĩaa ũndũnĩ ũte ũlũngalu, ĩndĩ ũtanaa vamwe na ũla w'o; nũvw'ĩkaa maũndũ onthe, nĩwĩtĩkĩlaa maũndũ onthe, nĩwĩkwatasya maũndũ onthe, nĩwũmĩĩasya maũndũ onthe. Wendo ndũnyivaa o na ĩndĩĩ." (1 Ako. 13:4-8) Kũsũanĩa ndeto isu mbeveee na kũsiatĩĩa kũilea kwongela ũtanu mũtwaanonĩ.
6, 7. (a) Mbivilia yonanĩtye mũndũ aĩle kũtũmĩa ũkũmũ ata? (b) Mwana-a-asa aĩle kwĩkalany'a na mũka ata?
6 Kwosana na ũndũ Ngai ũvangĩthĩtye maũndũ, kĩla ũndũnĩ vethĩawa ve na ũla wĩ na ũkũmũ. Nũndũ wa ũu, wendo nĩ wa vata mũno. Vaulo aisye atĩĩ: "Nĩenda mũmanye, kana mũtwe wa kĩla mũndũ mũũme nĩ Klĩsto; na mũtwe wa mũndũ mũka nĩ mũũme; na mũtwe wa Klĩsto nĩ Ngai." (1 Ako. 11:3) Ĩndĩ ũla wĩ na ũkũmũ ndaĩle kũũngamĩa ala angĩ na kĩthũi. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova nĩwe mũtwe wa Klĩsto na we amũũngamĩaa nesa, ate kwĩyenda, na nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu Yesũ nũmũnengete ndaĩa. Nĩwĩw'aa mũyo nĩ ũndũ Ngai ũmũũngamĩaa nũndũ ve ĩvinda yĩmwe waisye: "Nĩnĩmwendete Asa." (Yoa. 14:31) Yesũ ndaĩ esa kwasya ũu keka Yeova nĩwamũkandĩaa kana akamũũngamĩa na kĩthũi.
7 O na kau mũndũũme nĩwe mũtwe wa kĩveti kyake, Mbivilia ĩmwĩĩte kana aĩle 'kũkĩnenga ndaĩa.' (1 Vet. 3:7) Nzĩa ĩmwe aũme matonya kũnenga iveti syoo ndaĩa nĩ kwa kũsũanĩa mavata masyo na kũieka syĩnyuvĩe kĩla syĩkwenda mavinda amwe. O na Ndeto ya Ngai yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Aũme, endai iveti syenyu, o ũndũ Klĩsto wendie ĩkanisa, na enengane mwene kwondũ wayo." (Aev. 5:25) Kwosana na ĩandĩko yĩu, Yesũ nĩwaumisye thayũ wake kwondũ wa aatĩĩi make. Mũndũũme aatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ kwa kũũngamĩa mũka na wendo, wĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi mũnango kwa mũka kũmwenda, kũmũnenga ndaĩa, na kũmwĩnyivĩsya.—Soma Tito 2:3-5.
MENDE AKLĨSTO ALA ANGĨ
8. Kĩla mũthaithi wa Yeova aĩle kwona ũla ũngĩ ata?
8 Nthĩ yonthe kwĩthĩawa na andũ milioni mbingĩ mamũthaithaa Yeova na makatavany'a ĩũlũ wa ĩsyĩtwa yake na kĩeleelo kyake. Kwoou kĩla mũthaithi wa Yeova aĩle kwona ũla ũngĩ ata? Ndeto ya Ngai ĩsũngĩĩte atĩĩ: "Twĩkei andũ onthe nesa, ĩndĩ mũno ala ma nyũmba ya mũĩkĩĩo." (Aka. 6:10; soma Alomi 12:10.) Mũtũmwa Vetelo aandĩkie ũũ: "Nũndũ nĩmũtheetye ngoo syenyu kwondũ wa kwĩw'a kwenyu kwa ũla w'o kũvika kwenda ana-a-asa kũte wangangan'yo, endanai na wendo mũvyũ kuma ngoonĩ." O na ĩngĩ, Vetelo atavisye Aklĩsto ala angĩ atĩĩ: "Na mbee wa maũndũ onthe ĩthĩwai mũkyendana mũno na wendo mũvyũ inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ."—1 Vet. 1:22; 4:8.
9, 10. Nĩkĩ andũ ma Ngai methĩawa na ngwatanĩo?
9 Nũndũ nĩtwendanĩte mũno ithyĩ ene, vai andũ angĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe mailyĩ taitũ. O na eka ũu, nũndũ nĩtũmwendete Yeova na nĩtũatĩĩaa mĩao yake, nũtũtetheeasya aitũmĩa vinya ũla mũnene vyũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, naw'o nĩ veva wake mũtheu. Ũsu nĩw'o vinya ũla ũtũmĩaa kwĩka maũndũ. Veva ũsu nĩw'o ũtumĩte twĩthĩwa twĩ na ngwatanĩo nzeo vyũ na ana-a-asa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe.—Soma 1 Yoana 4:20, 21.
10 Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ aiweta nĩkĩ Aklĩsto maĩle kwendana: "Ĩvw'ĩkei ngoo yĩ na ĩnee ya kwĩw'anĩa tei, wĩnyivyo, ũuu, wũmĩĩsyo; kũmĩĩasya ũmwe kwa ũla ũngĩ, na kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene, ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva e na ũndũ na ũngĩ; o tondu Mwĩaĩi wamũekeie, inyw'ĩ nenyu ĩkaai o ta ũu: na mbee wa maũndũ aa onthe ĩvw'ĩkei wendo, naw'o nĩ wovano wa wĩanĩu." (Ako. 3:12-14) Nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ wendo, ũla nĩ "wovano wa wĩanĩu," nĩwonekaa nesa athũkũminĩ ma Yeova o na ethĩwa maumĩte mbaĩnĩ yĩva kana maeetwe ata.
11. Wendo na ngwatanĩo itumaa ata athũkũmi ma Yeova mamanyĩka?
11 Wendo wa kuma ngoonĩ na ngwatanĩo nĩsyo itumaa andũ mamanya kana athũkũmi ma Yeova nĩmo methĩawa na ndĩni ĩla ya w'o. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ Yesũ aisye ũũ: "Kwondũ wa ũu andũ onthe makamanya kana mwĩ amanyĩw'a makwa, ethĩwa mwĩthĩwa na wendo ĩnyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ." (Yoa. 13:34, 35) Nake mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkie ũũ: "Ũndũnĩ ũũ syana sya Ngai nikwonanw'a, o na syana sya ndevili: o mũndũ ũla ũtekaa ũlũngalu ti wa Ngai, o na ũla ũtamwendaa mwana-a-ĩthe. Nũndũ ũtũmane ũla mweewie kuma mwambĩlĩlyonĩ nĩ ũũ, twendane ene kwa ene." (1 Yoa. 3:10, 11) Kwendana kũla twendene kũtumaa twĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo ĩtoneka vangĩ, na kĩu kĩtumaa andũ mamanya kana Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩmo aatĩĩi ma w'o ma Klĩsto na nĩmo Ngai ũtũmĩaa kwĩanĩsya kĩeleelo kyake. Kĩeleelo kĩla meanĩasya nĩ kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe.—Mt. 24:14.
"ĨKOMANO ĨNENE YA ANDŨ" NĨYĨENDEEE KŨMBANW'A
12, 13. Yĩla "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ" yĩendeee kwĩka ata, na ala me ĩkomanonĩ yĩu makilyĩ manoona kyaũ?
12 Athũkũmi aingĩ ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ nĩ amwe ma "ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ . . . kuma andũnĩ ma kĩla mũthemba na mbaĩ na ngo na ithyomo." Athũkũmi asu ma Ngai "maũngeme mbee wa kĩla kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ [kya Ngai] na mbee wa kala Katena [Yesũ Klĩsto]." Athũkũmi asu ma Ngai nĩ meva? Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Nĩo ala maumĩte thĩnanĩ ũla mũnene, na nĩmathambisye ngũa syoo, na maitw'ĩkĩthya nzaũ nthakamenĩ ya kala Katena," nũndũ nĩmaĩkĩĩaa nthembo ya Yesũ ya wovosyo. Ala me 'ĩkomanonĩ yĩu ĩnene' maendeee kwongeleka na nĩmamwendete Yeova na Mwana wake, o na "nĩmamũthũkũmaa [Ngai] mũthenya na ũtukũ."—Ũvu. 7:9, 14, 15.
13 Ngai akilyĩ anaananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku ĩvindanĩ ya ũla "thĩna mũnene." (Mt. 24:21; soma Yelemia 25:32, 33.) Ĩndĩ nũndũ Yeova nĩwendete athũkũmi make, akamasũvĩa me kĩkundi na aimalikya nthĩ nzaũ. Na ĩndĩ o tondũ kwathaniwe myaka ta 2,000 mĩvĩtu, Ngai "akavyaĩa methoi onthe methonĩ moo; na kĩkw'ũ kĩikethĩwa vo ĩngĩ; o na kũikethĩwa ĩngĩ kũmeta, kana kũĩa, kana woo." We wĩ na mea ma kwĩkala Nthĩ Nzaũ ĩtina wa 'maũndũ ma mbee kũvĩta'?—Ũvu. 21:4.
14. Yu yĩla ĩkomano ĩnene yĩ na andũ meana ata?
14 Mwakanĩ wa 1914, ĩla mĩthenya ya mũminũkĩlyo yambĩĩe, kwaĩ athũkũmi ma Yeova o ngili mbũthũ nthĩ yonthe. Kĩkundi kĩnini kya etĩkĩw'a mauta kĩla kyaĩ kw'o ĩvinda yĩu nĩkyatavanisye ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ na kĩthito. Kyeekie ũu nũndũ nĩkyendete atũi na nũndũ nĩkyatetheeiw'e nĩ veva mũtheu wa Ngai. Nũndũ wa kĩtumi kyu, ũmũnthĩ ve kĩkundi kĩngĩ kya ĩkomano ĩnene ya andũ kĩla kĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ kĩendeee kũmbanw'a. Ngũsĩ sya Yeova nĩsyongelekete ikavika ta 8,000,000 na syĩthĩawa ikundinĩ mbee wa 115,400 ila syĩ nthĩ yonthe, na niendeee kwongeleka. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwakanĩ wa ũthũkũmi wa 2014, mbee wa andũ 275,500 nĩmavatisiwe matw'ĩka Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, na ũu nĩ ũndũ ũmwe na kwasya andũ ta 5,300 nĩmavatisawa kĩla kyumwa.
15. Elesya ũndũ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ ũnyaĩĩkĩte matukũ aa.
15 Ũndũ wa kũsengy'a ũmũnthĩ nĩ kana andũ aingĩ mũno vyũ nĩmew'ĩte ũvoo mũseo. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mavuku maitũ yu maumĩthaw'a kwa ithyomo mbee wa 700. Nayo ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya nĩyo ĩkaseti yĩla yĩnyaĩĩkaw'a mũno ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe. Yĩtumbĩthaw'a kovi mbee wa 52,000,000 kĩla mwei, na yumĩthaw'a kwa ithyomo 247. Nayo ĩvuku, Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata?, yĩla tũtũmĩaa kũmanyĩsya andũ Mbivilia nĩyĩtumbĩthĩtw'e mbee wa kovi 200,000,000 kwa ithyomo mbee wa 250.
16. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtumĩte athũkũmi ma Yeova ala me vaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ maendeea nesa?
16 Athũkũmi ma Yeova mongelekete ũmũnthĩ mũno wĩana ũu nũndũ nĩmamũĩkĩĩe Ngai na nĩmetĩkĩlĩte kana Mbivilia nĩyo Ndeto yake mbeveee. (1 Ath. 2:13) Ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla mũnene nĩ kana Yeova nũmaathimĩte mũno o na kũtw'ĩka nĩmamenetwe mũno na nĩmavĩngawa mũno nĩ Satani, ũla nĩwe "ngai ya nthĩ ĩno."—2 Ako. 4:4.
MENDAE ALA ANGĨ ĨNDĨ YONTHE
17, 18. Athũkũmi ma Ngai maĩle kũkua ata ala mate Ngũsĩ?
17 Athũkũmi ma Yeova maĩle kwona ata ala matamũthaithaa Ngai ũla ũmwe wa w'o? Ĩla tũũtavany'a andũ amwe nĩmatwĩthukĩĩasya na angĩ maitwĩthukĩĩasya. Ĩndĩ o na makeka ata, Ndeto ya Ngai nĩwetete ũndũ athũkũmi make maĩle kwĩka. Yaĩtye ũũ: "Ndeto syenyu syĩthĩwe na mumo mavinda onthe, isamae mũnyũ, nĩ kana mũmanye ũndũ mwaĩlwe nĩ ũsũngĩa kĩla mũndũ." (Ako. 4:6) Kwoou nũndũ nĩtwendete atũi maitũ, ĩla tũũsũngĩa mũndũ watũkũlya ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo ũla twĩ naw'o, twaĩle kwĩka ũu twĩ "na ũuu na w'ĩa."—1 Vet. 3:15.
18 O na ethĩwa tweethĩa mũndũ ũthatĩte na aitũneeny'a naĩ, nũseo tũkonany'a kana nĩtwendete atũi maitũ. Tweeka ũu twĩthĩawa tũiatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "aumwa, ndaaĩumĩa; athĩnw'a, ndaakanda; ĩndĩ eeyia mwene kwa ũla [Yeova] ũsilaa w'o." (1 Vet. 2:23) Twĩthĩwe twĩ na Ngũsĩ ila ingĩ kana twĩ na andũ angĩ, nĩtwonanasya kana nĩtwĩnyivĩtye kwa kũatĩĩa ũtao ũũ: "Mũikaĩvanĩsye ũthũku kwa ũthũku, kana mwaumwa mũkeyĩumĩa; vandũ va kwĩka ũu maathimaei ala meũmwĩka naĩ."—1 Vet. 3:8, 9, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
19. Nĩ mwolooto wĩva Yesũ wanenganie ũtũtetheesye kũmanya ũndũ twaĩle kũkua ala matũvĩngaa?
19 Ĩla andũ ma Yeova mekala menyivĩtye, monanasya kana nĩmaatĩĩaa mwolooto ũmwe wa vata wanenganiwe nĩ Yesũ. Ĩvinda ya ũla Ũtavany'a wa Kĩĩmanĩ aisye ũũ: "Nĩmwĩw'ĩte kana nĩkwaneeniwe, Mwende mũtũi waku, na mũmene mũmaitha waku: Ĩndĩ nyie nĩngũmwĩa, Mendei amaitha menyu, na mavoyeaei ala mamũthĩnasya; nĩ kana mwĩthĩwe ana ma Ĩthe wenyu ũla wĩ ĩtunĩ; nĩkwĩthĩwa we nũmaumĩasya syũa yake athũku na aseo, na kũmauĩsya mbua ala mekaa ũlũngalu na ala matekaa ũlũngalu." (Mt. 5:43-45) Kwoou, nũndũ twĩ athũkũmi ma Ngai, no nginya twĩmanyĩsye 'kũmenda amaitha maitũ,' o na methĩwe matwosaa ata.
20. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana andũ onthe nthĩ nzaũ makeethĩwa mendete Ngai na atũi? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 21.)
20 No nginya kĩla ĩvinda maũndũ ala andũ ma Yeova mekwĩka vamwe na mawoni moo monany'e kana nĩmamwendete Yeova na mũtũi. Kwa ngelekany'o, o na ethĩwa andũ amwe nĩmalea ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ, nĩtwonanasya kana nĩtũmendete kwa kũmatetheesya ĩla makwatwa nĩ vata. Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Mũĩkethĩwe mwi thiĩ na mũndũ wa kĩndũ o na kĩva kyonthe, ate o kwendana inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ: nũndũ ũla ũmwendaa ũngĩ nĩwĩanĩsye ĩla mĩao. Kwondũ wa ũu, Ndũkalaalae, Ndũkoae, Ndũkoye, Ndũkakĩw'ĩe kĩndũ kya ũngĩ ĩtomo, na ethĩwa kwĩ mwĩao ũngĩ, ũtalanĩlwe ndetonĩ ĩno, Mwende ũngĩ ũndũ wĩyendete mwene. Wendo ndwĩkaa naĩ kwa ũngĩ; kwondũ wa ũu wendo nĩ wĩanĩsyo wa ĩla mĩao." (Alo. 13:8-10) Nĩkwĩthĩwa twĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova, nĩtwonanasya kana twĩ na wendo wa w'o o na kau tũtwĩe nthĩ nthũku vyũ ĩtongoew'e nĩ Satani na yusĩe andũ ang'endu na mate ngwatanĩo. (1 Yoa. 5:19) Vate nzika, ĩla twĩvika nthĩ nzaũ, kĩla mũndũ akeethĩawa endete ũla ũngĩ nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu Satani na ndaimoni syake na andũ ala ang'endu makeethĩwa mavetangiwe. We ndũkwona ũkeethĩwa wĩ ũndũ mũseo mũno kwona andũ onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ mendete Ngai na atũi moo?
