translation:
"Love your neighbor as yourself."—Matt. 22:39.
NOTES: 25, 36
1, 2. Why does the Bible mention love even though it may seem obvious?
LOVE is a powerful force that Jehovah God feels deeply. (1 John 4:16) Jehovah showed his love by sending Jesus, and Jesus demonstrated his love for Jehovah by faithfully doing Jehovah's will for over 30 years. (Acts 1:15) Because Jesus was faithful, as well as because of what he did for us, we can be sure that Jehovah loves us, and we can trust that he will fulfill his promises. This helps us to cope with trials and to endure throughout our life, knowing that Jehovah and Jesus support us.
2 Jesus was asked what the greatest commandment was, and he replied: "You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind. This is the greatest and first commandment. The second is like it: 'You must love your neighbor as yourself.'"—Matt. 22:37-39.
3. What does it mean to "love"?
3 To understand what Jesus meant when he said to love Jehovah with your whole heart, consider how Jesus proved his love for Jehovah by obeying his command to preach. This principle applies to loving others. But what does it mean to love our neighbor? Think about what it means to love someone—it is showing genuine affection for them. We show love by being considerate and kind, and by treating others as we would like to be treated. Those who imitate Christ's love and those who fear God will often demonstrate love toward others. And those whom Jehovah loves will also show love to others. Can we truly love people if we do not know what is important to them?
SHOWING LOVE IN PRACTICE
4. How can we show love to others, even if they are unkind to us?
4 Jehovah instituted marriage between Adam and Eve, and he blessed them and told them to become fruitful and multiply. Marriage was originally intended to be a happy arrangement between one man and one woman. (Gen. 1:27, 28) However, when humans disobeyed Jehovah, marriage became imperfect and brought problems. (Eccl. 5:12) Therefore, the Bible gives guidance on how we can make our marriages successful. The advice found in the Bible can help couples to strengthen their love for Jehovah, the Originator of marriage.—Read 2 Timothy 3:16, 17.
5. What will help us to show love effectively?
5 God's love motivates us to be kind and considerate toward others, even those who may mistreat us. This is what true love does. The apostle Paul wrote to a congregation: "Love is patient and kind; love does not envy; love does not boast, it is not proud, it does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs, it does not delight in evil but rejoices with the truth, it always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always perseveres. Love never fails." (1 Cor. 13:4-8) To demonstrate genuine love, we need to practice empathy and understanding.
6, 7. (a) How does love affect the way we deal with faults? (b) Can a husband and wife ever have a perfect relationship?
6 In harmony with how God deals with us, each of us has imperfections and makes mistakes. However, love is forgiving. Paul explained: "I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is her husband, and the head of Christ is God." (1 Cor. 11:3) Because of this arrangement, each person has responsibilities. For example, Jehovah is the Head of Christ and directs him perfectly, yet allows him freedom, and because of Jesus' loyalty, Jehovah deeply appreciates him. It shows respect when we acknowledge that God directs things, and he has shown this respect to us by saying: "I have loved you just as the Father loves me." (John 14:31) Jesus demonstrated this by always seeking to please Jehovah and submitting to his direction.
7 And just as a husband is the head of his household, the Bible explains that husbands should 'love their wives tenderly.' (1 Pet. 3:7) One way they can show this love is by being considerate of their wife's feelings and making her happiness a priority. Also, God's Word says: "Husbands, continue loving your wives, just as Christ loved the congregation and gave himself up for it." (Eph. 5:25) Following this principle, Jesus set an excellent example for his followers. Husbands can imitate Jesus' example by directing their families with love, showing consideration for their needs, cherishing them, and providing for them.—Read Titus 2:3-5.
FOLLOW CHRIST'S EXAMPLE
8. What quality does each servant of Jehovah need to cultivate?
8 All over the earth there are millions of dedicated servants of Jehovah who zealously proclaim God's Kingdom and His message. What quality does each servant of Jehovah need to cultivate? God's Word urges us: "Be affectionate to one another, having brotherly affection." (Rom. 12:10; read Colossians 12:10.) The apostle Peter wrote: "Above all things, have intense love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins." And further, Peter encouraged fellow Christians: "Continue to love one another warmly from a sincere heart."—1 Pet. 1:22; 4:8.
9, 10. How do God's people show hospitality?
9 Since we deeply love one another, visitors often feel welcome among us. Moreover, since we love Jehovah and appreciate his commands, we are eager to use our resources to help others spiritually, and we are happy to share what we have. This is how we demonstrate our gratitude. Sharing what we have enables us to be hospitable to visitors and to provide them with necessities.—Read 1 John 4:20, 21.
10 Paul wrote this advice to fellow Christians regarding their conduct: "Put on the qualities of compassion, kindness, humility, mildness of temper, patience. Bear with one another, and forgive one another freely if anyone has a cause for complaint against another, just as Jehovah also forgave you freely; and above all things have love, which is the bond of completeness." (Col. 3:12-14) We show such love when "the bond of completeness" is evident in our unity and peaceable association with fellow believers.
11. How does love and hospitality make Jehovah's name known?
11 Love and hospitality are vital in helping people learn whether Jehovah's worship is genuine and from God. Why? Jesus said: "By this everyone will know that you are my disciples—if you have love for one another." (John 13:34, 35) The apostle John wrote: "The love God shows is this: that he sent his only-begotten Son into the world, so that those who believe might have life through him. By this the love of God was manifested in our case, that God sent his only-begotten Son into the world. Beloved ones, if God loved us so much, we also ought to love one another." (1 John 3:10, 11) Loving one another makes our brotherhood strong, and this helps people recognize that Jehovah's organization is supported by God and Christ and that God is using it to proclaim his Kingdom. This Kingdom will bring lasting peace to all the earth.—Matt. 24:14.
"A GREAT CROWD" CONTINUES TO GATHER
12, 13. How is "a great crowd" continuing to gather, and what questions will we answer?
12 Many of Jehovah's Witnesses are part of "a great crowd…out of all nations and tribes and peoples and tongues." These others are "sheep" who hear Jesus' voice but are not among the "other sheep." What indicates that they are sheep? Revelation chapter 7 describes them as saying: "Salvation we owe to the One sitting on the throne and to the Lamb," thus expressing their faith in Jesus' ransom sacrifice. This 'great crowd' continues to increase as more and more people come to love Jehovah and his Son, and "they continue to serve Him day and night."—Rev. 7:9, 14, 15.
13 God will soon take action to defend His name and kingdom against those who oppose "the great tribulation." (Matt. 24:21; read Jeremiah 25:32, 33.) But first, Jehovah will direct attention to his witnesses, separating them from the wicked and rescuing them. And after nearly 2,000 years, God "will gather his chosen ones from the four winds…and he will place them upon the land of Israel." Are you determined to be among those who will survive 'the things that are destined to happen'?—Rev. 21:4.
14. What does the great crowd accomplish along with other dedicated ones?
14 In 1914, the end of the times of the Gentiles began, and Jehovah's witnesses zealously proclaimed God's Kingdom throughout the earth. A large number of honesthearted people have been drawn to this spiritual food, and they have joined in defending the sovereignty of God and proclaiming his truth. This is why a growing number of others are joining the great crowd of people who want to live forever and continue supporting God's Kingdom. Jehovah's organization has grown to include over 8,000,000 publishers, and there are now more than 115,400 congregations worldwide, and it continues to grow. For example, in the year 2014, 275,500 people were baptized as Jehovah's Witnesses, and this meant that about 5,300 people got baptized each day.
15. Explain how the work of preaching is being accomplished today.
15 The preaching work is largely done by individuals. Why is this effective? Because our publications are printed in over 700 languages. Also, the magazine The Watchtower is published in nearly 247 languages and reaches an audience of over 52,000,000 each month. And the book What Does the Bible Really Teach?, which we use to help people learn from the Bible, has been printed 200,000,000 copies in 250 languages.
16. Why should we trust in Jehovah's promises that things will get better?
16 Jehovah's witnesses are confident because they know that God fulfills his promises and that the Bible is his inspired Word. (1 Thess. 2:13) Above all, we can be confident because Jehovah loves us and gives us holy spirit so that we may remain faithful and he can deliver us from Satan, who is "the god of this system of things."—2 Cor. 4:4.
OTHER QUESTIONS TO CONSIDER
17, 18. How can God's servants continue to grow spiritually?
17 Can Jehovah's Witnesses ever become complacent about spiritual matters? No, we need to reason with ourselves and examine others. But even if we do, God's standard remains the same. It says: "Your speech should always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to respond to each one." (Col. 4:6) Therefore, while we endeavor to help those who are seeking the truth, we also need to 'prove ourselves worthy of approval'—that is, "with respect to all."—1 Pet. 3:15.
18 And when someone treats us unfairly or speaks abusively, we should continue to show kindness and consideration. Let us imitate Jesus' example. The scripture states that he "when reviled, he did not retaliate; when suffering, he did not threaten, but continued entrusting himself to the One who judges justly." (1 Pet. 2:23) Whether we are dealing with believers or unbelievers, let us strive to maintain this attitude: "Be united in thought, feeling sympathetic, brotherly, tenderhearted, and humble in spirit."—1 Pet. 3:8, 9, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
19 What can we learn from Jesus' example about knowing what we need to grow spiritually?
19 But Jehovah's people are discerning, so they appreciate when others show practical wisdom like that demonstrated by Jesus. The Watchtower magazine said: "Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, pray for those who mistreat you: For if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same. But love your enemy, and do good, and lend without expecting anything back; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because he is kind to the unthankful and wicked. Be compassionate, just as your Father is compassionate." (Matt. 5:43-45) Truly, if we are children of God, we should endeavor to 'love our enemies,' even though it may be difficult.
20 How can we tell whether people genuinely want to please God and their fellow humans? (See paragraph 21.)
20 And why does each instance of showing love by Jehovah's people strengthen their bond with Jehovah and with one another? For example, even if some have been hurt by former associates, we can still strive to show them kindness, remembering how Jesus forgave those who wronged him. The apostle Paul wrote: "Owe nothing to anyone except to love one another, for the one who loves his fellow man has fulfilled the law. 'Do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, but whatever other command there may be—it is summed up in this rule: Love your neighbor as yourself.' Love works no evil to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law." (Rom. 13:8-10) As servants of Jehovah, we realize that love for one another and for all mankind helps us counteract Satan's influence and the bad effects he has on people. (1 John 5:19) So, as we get closer to the time of trouble, everyone will clearly show what they are—whether they are on the side of Jehovah and his people or on the side of Satan and his demons and those influenced by them. Who will prove to be truly loving, and how will this affect the way people view God and his worshipers?

text:
"Mwĩvw'ĩke mũndũ mweũ, ũla wombiwe na mũvw'ano wa Ngai."—AEV. 4:24.
MBATHI: 43, 27
1, 2. (a) Nĩkĩ vai mũndũ ũtevw'ĩka ũla mũndũ mweũ? (b) Nĩ nguma syĩva sya ũla mũndũ mweũ iwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akolosai 3:10-14?
KĨTHYOMONĨ kya mbee kĩla Mbivilia yaandĩkiwe nakyo, ndeto "mũndũ mweũ" itũmĩĩtwe kelĩ. (Aev. 4:24; Ako. 3:10) Mũndũ ũsu mweũ nĩ ũla 'ũmbĩtwe na mũvw'ano wa Ngai.' Vai mũndũ ũtevw'ĩka mũndũ ũsu mweũ. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ Yeova oombie andũ na kĩtũtya kyake na kwoou no twĩthĩwe na nguma ta syake.—Mwa. 1:26, 27; Aev. 5:1.
2 Ĩndĩ nũndũ wa naĩ ĩla twatiĩwe nĩ asyai maitũ, nĩtũthĩnaw'a nĩ mawendi mathũku. O na no kwĩthĩwa tũkwatĩtwe nĩ mĩtuo mĩna mĩthũku nũndũ wa vala twĩanĩe. Ĩndĩ nũndũ Yeova e tei, no atũtetheesye tũkethĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũla wendaa twĩthĩwe naw'o. Nĩ kana tũtw'e vyũ kwĩthĩwa na mwĩkalĩle ũsu, twĩneenea nguma siana ũna sya ũla mũndũ mweũ mũtũmwa Vaulo waveveewe kũandĩka ĩũlũ wake. (Soma Akolosai 3:10-14.) O na nĩtũkwona ũndũ tũtonya kwonany'a nguma isu ũthũkũminĩ witũ.
"INYW'ONTHE MWĨ ŨMWE"
3. Nĩ nguma ĩmwe yĩva yĩthĩawa na ũla wĩvw'ĩkĩte mũndũ mweũ?
3 Vaulo amina kũtwĩkĩa vinya twĩvw'ĩke ũla mũndũ mweũ, nĩwawetie nguma ĩmwe yonanasya nesa vyũ kana nĩtwĩvw'ĩkĩte mũndũ mweũ. Aeleisye kana mũndũ wa ũko ũsu nde kyende. Aisye kana nthĩnĩ wa mũndũ ũsu nĩ vandũ "vatatonyeka kwĩthĩwa Mũkiliki kana Mũyuti, kwaĩkwa kana kũlea kwaĩkwa, ũla ũte na ũmanyi kana Mũsithiani, ngombo kana ũla ũte ngombo." * Nĩkĩ kĩkundinĩ vayaĩlĩte kũlika kĩvathũkany'o kya ngo, nthĩ, kana kĩlasi? Ũsũngĩo nĩ kana aatĩĩi ma w'o ma Klĩsto maĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa 'me ũmwe.'—Ako. 3:11; Aka. 3:28.
4. (a) Athũkũmi ma Yeova maĩlĩte kũkua ala angĩ ata? (b) Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtonya kwananga ngwatanĩo ya Aklĩsto?
4 Twevw'ĩka mũndũ mweũ twĩthĩawa tũtonya kũnenga ndaĩa athaithi ala angĩ vamwe na ala mate Ngũsĩ, tũteũkũlya ũko woo kana kĩlasi kyoo. (Alo. 2:11) Ĩndĩ kwĩ nthĩ imwe kĩu kĩthĩawa kĩ vinya mũno. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa South Africa. O na ũmũnthĩ kwĩ Ngũsĩ mbingĩ mũno nthĩ ĩsu syĩkalaa kũndũ kũla tene kwavathĩtwe kwondũ wa andũ ma ũko mũna. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwĩ taoni ila tene syavathĩtwe kwondũ wa asũngũ, ingĩ kwondũ wa andũ aiũ, na ingĩ kwondũ wa nzyawa ila andũ aiũ masyaie na andũ ma ngo ingĩ. Kwoou nĩ kana Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye yĩkĩe vinya ana-a-asa asu 'maneneve ngoonĩ syoo,' nĩyavĩtũkĩthisye mũvango wa mwanya kwĩ Mwei wa 10, 2013. Mũvango ũsu waĩ wa kũtetheesya ana-a-asa ma ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o mamanyane nesa. (2 Ako. 6:13) Mũvango ũsu wailyĩ ata?
5, 6. (a) Nĩ mũvango wĩva weekiwe nthĩ ĩmwe nĩ kana andũ ma Ngai malũlũmĩlye ngwatanĩo yoo? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 22.) (b) Nĩ moseo meva monekete nũndũ wa mũvango ũsu?
5 Mũvango waĩ kana ana-a-asa ma ikundi ilĩ sya ithyomo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o kana ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o makoosaa wikendi imwe makatindany'a vamwe. Kĩu kyamanengae mwanya wa kũtavany'a vamwe, kũthi ĩmwe maũmbanonĩ, na kũthokany'a mĩsyĩ kwoo. Ikundi maana maingĩ niatĩĩe mũvango ũsu na ovisi wa ũvonge nũkwatĩte livoti nzeo mũno o na kuma kwa andũ mate Ngũsĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũtavany'a ũmwe wa ndĩni aisye ũũ: "Nyie ndi Ngũsĩ, ĩndĩ nĩmwĩa wĩa wenyu wa kũtavany'a nĩ mũvange nesa, na mwĩ ngwatanĩo o na kũtw'ĩka mwĩ ma ngo syĩ kĩvathũkany'o." Mũvango ũsu ũtethetye ata Ngũsĩ ila syĩ kũu?
6 Mũvango ũsu ũyambĩĩa, mwĩĩtu-a-asa wa mbaĩ ya Xhosa wĩtawa Noma nĩwakĩaa kũthokya kwake ana-a-asa asũngũ ma kĩkundi kya Kĩsũngũ nũndũ nde nyũmba nzeo. Ĩndĩ ĩla watavanisye na ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa asũngũ na mamũthokya kwoo, aisye ũũ aseng'ete mũno: "Kaĩ asu no andũ taitũ!" Kwoou ĩla kĩkundi kyake kya kĩthyomo kya Xhosa kyavikĩiwe nĩ kyathĩ kya kũthokya ana-a-asa ala me kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩsũngũ, nĩwauie lĩu na athokya amwe. Ũmwe wathokisye nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi mũsũngũ. Noma aisye atĩĩ: "Kĩla kyanzeng'isye nĩ kwona ateũmakw'a nĩ kwĩkalĩla kĩleti." Mũvango ũsu ũendeee South Africa nũtumĩte ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa aingĩ matuma ndũũ na Aklĩsto angĩ aingangĩ. O na nũtumĩte matw'a kũendeea kũmanya Aklĩsto angĩ ma mbaĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o.
"NGOO YĨ NA ĨNEE YA KWĨW'ANĨA TEI"
7. Ve vata mwaũ wa kwĩw'ĩaa ala angĩ ĩnee kĩla ĩvinda?
7 Twĩendeea kũkomana na matatwa nginya ĩla nthĩ ĩno ya Satani yĩvetwa. Aingĩ maitũ nĩtwaĩawa nĩ wĩa tũthũkũma, nĩtũwaaa mowau manene, tũkathĩnw'a, tũkakwatwa nĩ mĩisyo ta ithingitho sya nthĩ, tũkasya malĩ nũndũ wa ing'endilĩ, kana tũkakwatwa nĩ mathĩna o angĩ me kĩvathũkany'o. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana tũtethany'e mathĩnanĩ asu, no nginya twĩw'ĩanĩe ĩnee kuma ngoonĩ. Ĩnee yĩu nĩyo yĩkatumaa twĩka ala angĩ maũndũ mekwonany'a kana nĩtũũmew'ĩa tei. (Aev. 4:32) Nguma isu ilĩ sya mũndũ mweũ ikatũtetheeasya twĩyĩelekany'e na Ngai na tũikiakisya ala angĩ.—2 Ako. 1:3, 4.
8. Ve moseo ta meva ma kwĩw'ĩa onthe kĩkundinĩ ĩnee na tei? Nengane ngelekany'o.
8 Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũkonany'a kana nĩtũkwĩw'ĩa tei mũnango ala maumĩte nthĩ ingĩ kana ala me na mathĩna kĩkundinĩ kitũ? Ũndũ ũla mũseo nĩ kũtuma ndũũ namo na kũmatetheesya mone kana nĩ ma vata kĩkundinĩ. (1 Ako. 12:22, 25) Ekai twone ngewa ya Dannykarl, ũla wathamĩĩe Japan aumĩte Philippines. Vala wakwatie wĩa ndakuawa ũndũ ala angĩ ma kũu makuawa. Ĩndĩ ekalangĩte nĩwaendie ũmbanonĩ ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Dannykarl easya: "Vakuvĩ onthe ala maĩ ũmbanonĩ ũsu maĩ andũ ma nthĩ ĩsu ya Japan, ĩndĩ manthokisye nesa mũno ta tweesene kuma tene." Ana-a-asa asu nĩmaendeeie kũmwĩka nesa, na kĩu nĩkyamũnengie vinya wa kwĩka maendeeo. Dannykarl nĩwesie kũvatiswa na ũmũnthĩ nĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi. Atumĩa ala angĩ monaa wĩ ũathimo mũnene mũno kwĩthĩwa na Dannykarl na mũka, Jennifer, kĩkundinĩ kĩu. Maasya ũũ ĩũlũ woo: "Asu nĩ mavainia mateyũmbĩlĩĩle maũndũ maingĩ na nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ya andũ mambĩte kũmantha Ũsumbĩ."—Luka 12:31.
9, 10. Nengane ngelekany'o syĩkwonany'a ũseo wa kwĩw'ĩa ala tũkwĩthĩa ũtavany'a ĩnee.
9 Wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ nũtũnengae mwanya mũseo wa kwĩka "andũ onthe nesa." (Aka. 6:10) Ngũsĩ mbingĩ nĩsyĩw'ĩaa ĩnee ala mathamĩĩe nthĩ yoo, na nũndũ wa ũu nitataa mũno kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kyoo. (1 Ako. 9:23) Moathimo ala Ngũsĩ isu ikwatĩte nĩ maingĩ mũno. Kwa ngelekany'o, vainia wĩtawa Tiffany wa nthĩ ya Australia nĩweemanyĩisye kĩthyomo kya Kĩswaili nĩ kana atetheesye kĩkundi kya Kĩswaili kĩ taoninĩ ya kũu yĩtawa Brisbane. Kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kĩu kwaĩ vinya, ĩndĩ moathimo ala Tiffany ũkwatĩte nĩ maingĩ. Easya: "Ethĩwa nĩwĩkũlasya wĩĩka ata ũtanĩe ũtavany'a, enda ũtetheesye kĩkundi kya kĩthyomo kĩeni. Wĩw'aa ta wathi kũtembea kũndũ kũngĩ wĩ o vala ũĩ. Kwĩka ũu kũtumaa wĩyonea na metho a maku ngwatanĩo ya ũsengy'o ĩla twĩthĩawa nayo nthĩ yonthe."
10 Kwasũanĩa ĩngĩ ĩũlũ wa mwana-a-asa ũmwe wa Japan, vamwe na mũka na mwĩĩtu woo, Sakiko. Mwĩĩtu ũsu woo easya: "Myakanĩ ya 1990 twakothaa kũkomana na andũ maumĩte Brazil ĩla tũũtavany'a. Matwĩthukĩĩasya nesa mũno o na angĩ nĩmaĩaa ĩla twamony'a maandĩko ta Ũvuan'yo 21:3, 4, kana Savuli 37:10, 11, 29 Mbivilianĩ ya kĩthyomo kyoo kya Portuguese." Ĩndĩ Sakiko na asyai make mayaaĩanĩwa nĩ kĩu. Sakiko easya: "Kwona nzaa ĩla maĩ nayo ya kĩ-veva kwatumie twenda kwĩmanyĩsya kĩthyomo kya Portuguese twĩ ta mũsyĩ." Ĩtina wa ĩvinda nĩmatetheeisye kwambĩĩsya kĩkundi kya kĩthyomo kya Portuguese. Myakanĩ ĩla yaatĩĩe nĩmatetheeisye aingĩ ala mathamĩĩe kũu matw'ĩka athũkũmi ma Yeova. Sakiko easya atĩĩ: "Kwĩmanyĩsya Portuguese kũyaĩ ngũĩ, ĩndĩ moathimo ala twakwatie nĩ maingĩ kwĩ kĩthito kĩla tweekĩie. Tũmũtũngĩaa Yeova mũvea mwingĩ."—Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 10:34, 35.
"ĨVW'ĨKEI . . . WĨNYIVYO"
11, 12. (a) Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩthĩwa na kĩeleelo kĩseo ĩla tũkwĩkĩa kĩthito twĩvw'ĩke mũndũ mweũ? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩkale twĩnyivĩtye?
11 Tũyaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito twĩvw'ĩke mũndũ mweũ aĩ nĩ kana tũtaĩwe nĩ andũ. Twaĩle kwĩka ũu nĩ kana tũmũtaĩe Yeova. Lilikana kana kĩla kyatumie mũlaĩka ũmwe avalũka nĩ kũkwatwa nĩ mĩtũlyo. (Sianĩsya na Esekieli 28:17.) Kwoou we wĩona mũndũ wĩ na naĩ ta ũtonya kũvalũkw'a mĩtũkĩ ata nĩ mĩtũlyo na ngathĩĩo? Ĩndĩ o na vailyĩ ũu, nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka tũkevw'ĩka wĩnyivyo. Kwoou nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya?
12 Twenda kwĩkala twĩnyivĩtye, no nginya kĩla mũthenya tũmanthe ĩvinda ya kũvindĩĩsya kĩla twasoma Ndetonĩ ya Ngai. (Kũt. 17:18-20) Na mũno mũno twaĩlĩte kũvindĩĩsya maũndũ ala Yesũ wamanyĩisye na ũndũ we mwene weenyivĩtye. (Mt. 20:28) O na athambisye maaũ ma atũmwa make nĩ wĩnyivyo ũla waĩ naw'o. (Yoa. 13:12-17) Ũndũ ũngĩ twaĩle kwĩka nĩ kũvoya Ngai kĩla ĩndĩ atũnenge veva wake nĩ kana ũtũnenge vinya wa kũvetanga wendi wa kwĩtũlya ĩũlũ wa ala angĩ.—Aka. 6:3, 4; Avi. 2:3.
13. Ve moathimo meva ma kwĩthĩwa twĩ na wĩnyivyo?
13 Soma Nthimo 22:4. Yeova endaa athũkũmi make onthe methĩwe na wĩnyivyo, na ve moathimo maingĩ mokanasya naw'o. Twekala twĩnyivĩtye, kĩkundi nĩkĩthĩawa na ngwatanĩo ndũmangu na mũuo mwingangĩ. O na ĩngĩ twatata twĩthĩwe twĩnyivĩtye vyũ, Ngai ndakalea kũtwony'a ũseo wake ũtathimĩka. Mũtũmwa Vetelo aisye atĩĩ: "Inyw'onthe ĩvotoei wĩnyivyo, mũtethan'ye inyw'ĩ kwa inyw'ĩ: nĩkwĩthĩwa Ngai nũsiĩĩaa ala mekwĩnenevya, ĩndĩ amanengae mumo [kana, "ũseo ũtathimĩka," NWT] ala menyivasya."—1 Vet. 5:5.
"ĨVW'ĨKEI . . . ŨUU, WŨMĨĨSYO"
14. Nũũ wĩthĩĩtwe e ngelekany'o ĩla nzeo vyũ ya ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo?
14 Ũmũnthĩ andũ ala auu na me wũmĩĩsyo maitalawa ta ngũmbaũ. Ĩndĩ woni ũsu ti wa w'o o na vanini. Nguma isu ilĩ nĩ nzeo mũno na syumanĩte na Ngai ũla mwene vinya w'onthe. Vai ũngĩ wĩthĩĩtwe na ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo ta wa Yeova Ngai. (2 Vet. 3:9) Nũũlilikana ũndũ wasũngĩie makũlyo ma Avalaamu na Loto atũmĩĩte alaĩka? (Mwa. 18:22-33; 19:18-21) Na eka ũu, Yeova oomĩanĩisye na mbaĩ ya Isilaeli kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 1,500 o na kũtw'ĩka ndyamwĩw'aa.—Esek. 33:11.
15. Yesũ oonanisye ata kana aĩ na ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo?
15 Yesũ aĩ "mũuu." (Mt. 11:29) Amanyĩw'a make maĩ na mawonzu mana ĩndĩ nĩwamomĩĩisye mũno. Na ĩvinda yonthe waĩ kũũ nthĩ aitavany'a, nĩwoomĩĩisye o na kau nĩwaneeneawa naĩ nĩ atongoi ma ndĩni. Aendeeie kũmĩĩsya na kwĩkala auĩtye kũvika ĩla wooaiwe. O na kũtw'ĩka e mũtĩnĩ wa mathĩna aĩ na kyalya kingĩ mũno, akũlilye Asa wake aekee ala mamũaie. Aisye kĩtumi nũndũ "matimanya ũndũ mekwĩka." (Luka 23:34) Ĩsu nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ta kĩ ya mũndũ waĩ na ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo o na e ĩtatwanĩ yetete ata!—Soma 1 Vetelo 2:21-23.
16. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a twĩ na ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo?
16 Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana twĩ auu na twĩ wũmĩĩsyo? Vaulo nĩwawetie ũndũ ũmwe ĩla waandĩkĩe ana-a-asa make ndeto ii: "[Endeeai] kũmĩĩasya ũmwe kwa ũla ũngĩ, na kũekeanĩa ene kwa ene, ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva e na ũndũ na ũngĩ; o tondu Mwĩaĩi wamũekeie, inyw'ĩ nenyu ĩkaai o ta ũu." (Ako. 3:13) Tũyĩsa kũatĩĩa mwĩao ũsu ethĩwa tũi auu na tũi wũmĩĩsyo. Ĩndĩ kũekea ala angĩ nĩkũlũlũmĩlasya ngwatanĩo ya kĩkundi na nĩkũmĩsũvĩaa ndĩkanangĩke.
17. Nĩkĩ ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo nĩ nguma sya vata?
17 Mũndũ ũkwĩtwa Mũklĩsto no nginya evw'ĩke ũuu na wũmĩĩsyo. No nginya twĩke ũu ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda twĩtangĩĩwa. (Mt. 5:5; Yak. 1:21) Na ũndũ ũla mũnene nĩ kana nguma isu nitumaa tũmũetee Yeova ndaĩa na ikatuma tũtetheesya angĩ meke oou.—Aka. 6:1; 2 Tim. 2:24, 25.
"ĨVW'ĨKEI WENDO"
18. Kwenda ala angĩ kũkonanĩtye ata na kwĩthĩwa tũte kyende?
18 Nguma isu syonthe twaneenea nikonanĩtye mũno na wendo. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũmanyĩw'a Yakovo nĩwakanisye ana-a-asa make nũndũ wa kũkua ala athwii nesa kwĩ ngya. Awetie kana mwĩkalĩle ta ũsu nũvĩtũũkene na mwĩao ũũ ũkĩlĩte ĩla ĩngĩ yonthe: "Mwende ũngĩ o tondũ wĩyendete mwene." Na ĩndĩ asya: "Ethĩwa mwĩendeesya andũ, nĩmũkwĩka naĩ." (Yak. 2:8, 9) Ĩndĩ wendo nũtũtetheeasya tũikavathũle andũ nũndũ wa kĩsomo kyoo, ũko woo, kana kĩlasi kyoo. Kũneena ũla w'o, tũyĩsa kwĩtw'ĩkĩthya atĩ twĩ andũ mate kyende. No nginya twĩthĩwe tũilyĩ ũu kuma ngoonĩ.
19. Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata twĩvw'ĩke wendo?
19 O na ĩngĩ wendo "nĩwũmĩĩasya, na nĩwĩkaa moseo," na "ndwĩkathĩĩaa." (1 Ako. 13:4) No nginya twĩthĩwe na wũmĩĩsyo, wĩnyivyo, na twende kwĩka angĩ ũseo nĩ kana tũvote kũendeea kũtavya atũi maitũ ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ. (Mt. 28:19) O na nguma isu nitumaa twĩkalany'a nesa mũno na Aklĩsto onthe kĩkundinĩ. Ũathimo nĩ wĩva wa kwĩthĩwa na wendo ta ũsu? Ũtumaa ikundi syĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo na nũndũ wa ũu Yeova nũtaĩawa. O na ĩngĩ kĩu nĩkĩtumaa andũ angĩ mendeew'a nĩ ũw'o. Nĩkyo kĩtumi Mbivilia ĩminĩĩe kũelesya ĩũlũ wa ũla mũndũ mweũ na ndeto ii itakananĩw'a: "Mbee wa maũndũ aa onthe ĩvw'ĩkei wendo, naw'o nĩ wovano wa wĩanĩu."—Ako. 3:14.
ENDEEAI KWĨKĨA KĨTHITO "MŨTW'ĨKĨTHW'E EŨ"
20. (a) Twaĩlĩte kwĩkũlya makũlyo meva, na nĩkĩ? (b) Nĩ ĩvinda yĩva tweteele na mea?
20 Kĩla ũmwe witũ aĩlĩte kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva ndonya kwĩka ngaumya mũndũ ũla wa tene na kũmwĩkya vaasa vyũ?' Nĩtwaĩle kũthetheesya kũmũvoya Ngai atũtetheesye, na nĩtwaĩle kwĩkĩa kĩthito tũekane na mawoni kana mwĩkalĩle ũla ũtonya kũtũvata Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. (Aka. 5:19-21) O na nũseo twĩkũlye-ĩ, 'Nĩnĩendeeaa kwĩkĩa kĩthito nĩtw'ĩkĩthw'e mweũ vevanĩ wa kĩlĩko kyakwa?' (Aev. 4:23, 24) Twĩendeea kwĩkĩa kĩthito kya kwĩvw'ĩka mũndũ mweũ tũteũmumya nginya ĩla ũkethĩa tũiũthĩnw'a nĩ naĩ. Kwatata kũsũanĩa ũndũ tũkatanĩa kwĩkalany'a na andũ mevw'ĩkĩte mũndũ mweũ vate vandũ matialĩtye o na vamwe!
^ kal. 3 Ĩvindanĩ ya tene, Asithiani moonekaa me ang'endu mũno na kwoou nĩmamenetwe.

translation:
"Become new persons, being renewed in the power of your mind."—Eph. 4:24.
HEADLINE: 43, 27
1, 2. (a) What does it mean to become a new person? (b) How does the description of a new person at Colossians 3:10-14 help us understand what it means?
THE Bible often uses the expression "new person." (Eph. 4:24; Col. 3:10) This new person is someone who is 'being made new in the power of God's Spirit.' What does it mean to become this new person? Why? Because Jehovah loves us and wants us to reflect His qualities and to be happy doing so.—Gen. 1:26, 27; Eph. 5:1.
2 We have inherited imperfection from our first parents, and we find ourselves drawn to bad habits. And we may struggle with negative tendencies because of the world around us. But because Jehovah cares for us, he helps us to make changes and to cultivate a personality that pleases him. Even if we find it hard to change, we can benefit from considering the advice Paul gave in his letter. (Read Colossians 3:10-14.) And we will see how practical that advice is when we examine some specific areas of our lives.
"PUT ON THE NEW PERSONALITY"
3. What is involved in putting on the new personality?
3 Paul explained that putting on the new personality means letting go of the old personality and becoming a new person. He emphasized that the old personality includes such things as lying, stealing, and immorality. He also said that the new personality includes qualities like kindness, humility, patience, and love. * Why is it important to work at removing those undesirable traits, attitudes, or habits? The reason is that Christians want to be united with Christ and reflect his qualities.—Col. 3:11; Eph. 3:28.
4. (a) How can Jehovah help us to improve? (b) What can motivate us to overcome our weaknesses?
4 As we put on the new personality, we strive to reject bad associations and worldly desires, and we avoid places where we might be tempted. (Prov. 2:11) This may require effort. Consider the example of South Africa. There, many people live in areas where crime is rampant. However, some have made changes in their lives so that they associate with honest and upright individuals rather than with criminals, and they avoid dangerous places. It seems that God allows Satan to test people, giving them opportunities to prove whether they will remain loyal. For instance, on October 10, 2013, he permitted a severe storm to hit the Philippines, causing widespread devastation. That disaster revealed who truly valued human life. (2 Cor. 6:13) Did that event teach you something?
5, 6. (a) What lesson does this situation illustrate regarding how God views loyalty? (See accompanying article, "Staying Neutral.") (b) What questions should we ask ourselves about our own loyalty?
5 The fact that imperfect humans sometimes make wrong choices does not mean that God approves of wrongdoing. Rather, it shows that he gives people time to demonstrate their loyalty, allowing them to make a decision. This provides an opportunity to show love for others, to preach, and to defend the truth. Many people throughout the world have demonstrated their loyalty, and they are enjoying a good standing with God. For example, a young man once said: "I am a Witness, and my reason for preaching is because I want to show my loyalty, and I want to help others learn about the truth." Does such loyalty please Jehovah?
6 This incident illustrates how Noma, a young woman from the Xhosa tribe, felt when she learned that her parents were associating with a group called the Sungu, who lived nearby. She was deeply disturbed by what she saw her parents doing with these people, and she exclaimed: "What will become of our people!" Her parents' association with this Sungu group, which was known for its practice of initiating youths into secret societies, caused her great distress. One of those initiates was the leader of the Sungu group. Noma later stated: "All I could think about was seeing the destruction and being left alone." This incident spread throughout South Africa, affecting many people and leading some to turn away from Christ. It also led to efforts to learn more about Christ from other tribes.
"THE REASON FOR BEING DIFFERENT"
7. Why do we often feel awkward or out of place?
7 We need to cope with challenges because this world is influenced by Satan. Many of us are tempted by things we see, desire large possessions, get angry, are trapped by harmful habits, waste money on unnecessary things, or are caught up in immoral practices. Sometimes we even argue with others, and we may find ourselves feeling different than everyone else. This difference can cause us to stumble or make wrong decisions. (Eph. 4:32) But such feelings can motivate us to draw closer to God and avoid bad associations.—2 Cor. 1:3, 4.
8. What steps can we take to remain distinct and separate? Consider the examples.
8 How can we stay distinct, even when we are tempted to conform to worldly standards or associate with those who have poor moral standards? The key is to spend time meditating and praying regularly.—1 Cor. 12:22, 25. Let's look at the experience of Dannykarl, who served in Japan and the Philippines. He was assigned to help congregations in remote areas. He found that serving in one congregation of Jehovah's Witnesses was very satisfying. Dannykarl said: "I really appreciated being able to assist fellow believers in that part of Japan, and I felt encouraged to continue serving." Others also responded favorably to his assistance, and they were strengthened by his encouragement. Dannykarl was appointed as an elder in the congregation. Elders in other congregations often commended Dannykarl and his wife, Jennifer, for their zeal. They learned this lesson from their experience: "We should not be overly concerned about material possessions, but rather focus on what is important to God."—Luke 12:31.
9, 10. How can we show that we value spiritual things and make them our priority?
9 To prioritize spiritual pursuits, we need to 'seek first the Kingdom.' (Matt. 6:10) Many find it challenging to do so, especially when faced with pressures from the world around them. (1 Cor. 9:23) However, there are benefits to making spiritual activities a priority. For example, a sister named Tiffany from Australia learned Swahili and began assisting the Swahili-speaking congregation in her city, Brisbane. Prioritizing this activity brought her great joy, and she experienced many blessings. She says: "If you feel drawn to serve where there is greater need, don't hesitate—offer your help to the local congregation. You will be surprised how much you benefit and how grateful people will be for your support. Doing so will help you to strengthen your relationship with Jehovah and appreciate the brotherhood more fully."
10 Consider the experience of Sakiko, a mother in Japan, along with her husband and daughter. Her husband said: "In the 1990's, we came into contact with brothers from Brazil who needed assistance. We were deeply moved by what they were doing, and we remembered scriptures like Proverbs 21:3, 4, and Psalm 37:10, 11, 29, which speak about helping others." Both Sakiko and her family felt motivated to assist. Sakiko explains: "Because I had some knowledge of Portuguese, we offered to help them learn Portuguese." As a result, she was able to assist in forming a Portuguese-language congregation. Over the years, she has helped many become dedicated worshippers of Jehovah. Sakiko adds: "Learning Portuguese has been very rewarding, and the friendships we have made have strengthened our faith. We have come to love Jehovah even more."—Read Acts 10:34, 35.
"SPEAK . . . THE TRUTH"
11, 12. (a) How can we show appreciation for the fine example set by those who zealously share the good news? (b) What can motivate us to be courageous?
11 We can show appreciation when we support those who zealously share the good news, whether they are pioneers or others. We can do so especially because we know that each one faces challenges and opposition. (Compare Ezekiel 28:17.) Have you ever noticed someone who despite feeling shy or apprehensive, courageously speaks to others? If so, you likely admired his boldness. What can motivate us to be courageous?
12 We want to remain courageous, and to help us, let us regularly meditate on the scriptures found in God's Word. (Prov. 17:18-20) And let us strive to imitate Jesus' attitude and spirit. (Matt. 20:28) He also set an example for his followers to be humble. (John 13:12-17) One way we can do this is by being grateful to God for everything he has done and continues to do for us—for his undeserved kindness and loving provision.—Acts 6:3, 4; Phil. 2:3.
13. What questions will we now answer?
13 Read Proverbs 22:4. Jehovah values humility, and many blessings come to those who are humble. We want to remain courageous, but often we struggle because of pride and a strong desire for recognition. However, if we continue to cultivate humility, God will bless us with his favor. The apostle Peter wrote: "All of you become humble under God's mighty hand, so that he may exalt you at the proper time; cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you."—1 Pet. 5:5.
"BE . . . SLOW TO SPEAK"
14. Why should we be slow to speak?
14 Many people speak impulsively and say things they later regret. They often cause problems and hurt others. But wisdom is found when we carefully consider our words and how they affect others. It shows respect for God, who has given us the ability to communicate. So strive to be slow to speak and thoughtful in what you say to honor Jehovah God. (2 Tim. 3:9) How did Abraham and Lot set an example in this regard? (Gen. 18:22-33; 19:18-21) And remember, Jehovah showed patience with the nation of Israel for about 1,500 years, giving them opportunity to repent.—Ezek. 33:11.
15. Did Jesus show that he was slow to speak?
15 Jesus was "mild-tempered." (Matt. 11:29) He knew his value and did not get upset over trivial matters. Throughout his ministry, he spoke calmly and thoughtfully, always showing consideration for others. He continued to practice self-control, even when deeply moved. He also demonstrated remarkable empathy, as seen when he comforted his father David. He even said, "They do not know what they are doing." (Luke 23:34) We can imitate his example by being considerate in our speech and avoiding harshness.—Read 1 Peter 2:21-23.
16. What can help us to be slow to speak?
16 Can we learn to be slow to speak? Paul gave some practical advice to fellow Christians in a letter, saying: "[Continue] making earnest efforts to promote peace with all men, and to build up one another, each one encouraging the other; because there is something good in unity and harmony."—Acts 3:13. Let us strive to apply this counsel in our daily life. Being quick to listen helps us avoid misunderstandings and promotes goodwill.
17. Why is mildness a strength?
17 A true Christian is known for his mildness. It shows that we are teachable and willing to correct our thinking. (Matt. 5:5; Jas. 1:21) And more importantly, mildness moves us to please Jehovah and strengthens our desire to live according to his will.—Acts 6:1; 2 Tim. 2:24, 25.
"PRACTICE KINDNESS"
18. How can we show kindness in our dealings with others?
18 We should always endeavor to be kind in our dealings with others. For example, James reminded his brothers to be impartial when helping those in need. He warned them not to favor one person over another, stating: "Treat everyone kindly." And he added: "Because judgment is without mercy to anyone who has shown no mercy." (Jas. 2:8, 9) Kindness motivates us to help our brothers and sisters spiritually, whether during the Kingdom Ministry School or in the congregation. To do so, let us try to put ourselves in their place. We want to be treated with consideration, and they do too.
19. What benefits does practicing kindness bring?
19 Moreover, kindness "makes people agreeable," "is mild," and "is easily controlled." (1 Ac. 13:4) When we show kindness, compassion, and empathy, we will be more inclined to obey the command to go and make disciples of all peoples. (Mt. 28:19) Also, this will move us to associate closely with all Christians out of love. Is it satisfying to experience such kindness yourself? It can strengthen our relationship with Jehovah and encourage us to show kindness to others. And it may lead others to appreciate the truth. That is why the Bible emphasizes the importance of each individual's response to the good news, saying: "The man who shows favor to the poor lends to Jehovah himself."—Ac. 3:14.
KEEP PRACTICING KINDNESS
20. (a) What practical steps can we take, and why? (b) What questions will help us to show empathy?
20 Each of us can ask himself: 'What can I do to show genuine interest in my brothers and sisters and to comfort them?' We can strive to imitate God's empathy toward us, and we can practice showing empathy so that we do not become complacent or feel that we already fully understand God's ways. (Ac. 5:19-21) Also, we might ask ourselves, 'How can I practice showing empathy so that I am moved to help my brothers and sisters?' (Ephesians 4:23, 24) We should endeavor to show empathy when comforting someone, especially when he is going through a difficult time. Do not hesitate to spend time with those who have been wronged or who are suffering!

text:
"Ĩthĩwai mũkĩelekan'ya na Ngai, ta twana twendetwe." —AEV. 5:1.
1. Nĩ ũtonyi wĩva ũtonya kũtũtetheesya tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ĩla Ngai ũtwiĩe?
YEOVA atũmbie tũtonya kũelewa ũndũ ala angĩ mekwĩw'a. O na kau tũitonya kũkwatya vyũ, no tũtate kũelewa ũndũ mũndũ wĩw'aa akwatwa nĩ ũndũ mũna o na ethĩwa ndwaatũkwata kana tũyaawĩka. (Soma Aeveso 5:1, 2.) Tũtonya kũtũmĩa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nesa ata? Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũikatũmĩe mũthĩnzĩo ũsu kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kũtũetee mathĩna?
2. Yeova ew'aa ata ĩla tũũthĩna?
2 Vate nzika, nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ Ngai nĩwathanĩte kana etĩkĩw'a mauta ala aĩkĩĩku makathi ĩtunĩ na mainengwa thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a, na kana "malondu angĩ" ma Yesũ ala mekalĩte me aĩkĩĩku makanewa thayũ wa tene na tene vaa nthĩ. (Yoa. 10:16; 17:3; 1 Ako. 15:53) Na nĩtwĩsĩ kana onthe ala makakwata thayũ ũtatonya kũkw'a ĩtunĩ, na ala makakwata thayũ wa tene na tene vaa nthĩ maikakwatwa nĩ mathĩna ala matũkwataa ũmũnthĩ. Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ Yeova nĩwĩthĩawa esĩ ũndũ twĩw'aa ĩla tũũthĩna o tondũ weesĩ ũndũ Aisilaeli meew'aa ĩla mathĩnaw'a me ngombo Misili. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "thĩnanĩ woo w'onthe nake nĩwathĩnaw'a." (Isa. 63:9) Myaka mingĩ ĩtina wa ũu, ve ĩvinda Ayuti makwatiwe nĩ wia nũndũ wa amaitha ala mamasiĩĩaa mayaka ĩkalũ, ĩndĩ Ngai amea atĩĩ, "Ũla ũkũkiitaa akiitaa kyũma kya itho [yakwa]." (Nzek. 2:8) O tondũ mũndũ mũka wĩthĩawa endete mwana wake, now'o Yeova wendete andũ make na nũndũ wa ũu nũmatethasya. (Isa. 49:15) Kwa ndeto ingĩ, Yeova nũeleawa ũndũ ala angĩ mekwĩw'a, na o naitũ nũtũnengete ũtonyi ũsu.—Sav. 103:13, 14.
ŨNDŨ YESŨ WOONANISYE NĨWENDETE ANDŨ O TONDŨ NGAI ŨMENDETE
3. Nĩ kyaũ kyonanasya kana Yesũ aĩ tei?
3 Yesũ nĩwaeleawa ũndũ ala angĩ mekwĩw'a, o na nĩwaeleawa ala mathĩnaw'a nĩ maũndũ mataamũkwata. Kwa ngelekany'o, atongoi ma ndĩni nĩmamakengaa na kũmombĩĩa mĩao yoo meseũvĩsye, na andũ aingĩ nĩmamakĩĩte mũno. (Mt. 23:4; Mko. 7:1-5; Yoa. 7:13) Yesũ ndamakĩaa o na ndaĩ akengeka, ĩndĩ nĩwaeleawa ũndũ ala mathĩnaw'a nĩ atongoi asu meew'aa. Nĩkyo Mbivilia yaĩtye atĩĩ: "Na amona makomano, amew'ĩa tei nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩmanyamaaw'a na kũnyaĩĩkw'a ta malondu mate na mũĩthi." (Mt. 9:36) Yesũ nĩwendete andũ na nĩwamew'ĩaa tei o ta Ĩthe.—Sav. 103:8.
4. Yesũ eekaa ata ĩla woona andũ meũthĩna?
4 Nũndũ Yesũ nĩwendete andũ, ĩla woona maithĩna nĩwamatetheeasya. Kwĩka ũu kwoonanisye kana nĩwendete andũ vyũ o tondũ Ĩthe wake wamendete. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũthenya ũmwe Yesũ nĩwendaa kũthũmũa e na amanyĩw'a make vandũ vauĩtye nũndũ matindĩte maitavany'a. Ĩndĩ nĩwoonie andũ mamweteele, amew'ĩa tei, na oosa ĩvinda ambĩlĩlya "kũmamanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ."—Mko. 6:30, 31, 34.
ŨNDŨ TŨTONYA KWENDA ALA ANGĨ O TONDŨ YEOVA ŨMENDETE
5, 6. Nĩ kana twende atũi maitũ o tondũ Ngai ũmendete, twaĩle kũmosa ata? Nengane ngelekany'o. (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 24.)
5 Twonanasya kana nĩtwendete atũi maitũ o tondũ Ngai ũmendete twekalany'a namo nesa. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno: Twasye ve mwanake ũmwe Mũklĩsto wĩtawa Alan ũkũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwana-a-asa mũna mũkũũ ũtatonya kũsoma nesa nũndũ nĩwaaie metho. O na mwana-a-asa ũsu mũkũũ nũemawa nĩ kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba. Kavindanĩ kau Alan ũkũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa mwana-a-asa ũsu aililikana ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Ũndũ ũla mũkwenda kwĩkwa nĩ andũ, o ta ũu mekei o w'o." (Luka 6:31) Alan ayĩkũlya, 'Nĩ ũndũ wĩva ngwenda kwĩkwa nĩ andũ?' Ayĩsũngĩa atĩĩ kuma ngoonĩ, 'Nĩenda makũne mũvĩla nakwa!' Ĩndĩ ũla mwana-a-asa mũkũũ ndatonya kũkũna mũvĩla. Ĩla Yesũ wawetie ndeto ila syĩ mũsoanĩ ũsu no ũndũ ũmwe na watwĩaa nĩtwĩkũlye atĩĩ, 'Ndonya kwenda mũtũi wakwa ambĩke ata keka nĩ na thĩna ta ũla wake?'
6 We Alan ti mũkũũ ĩndĩ nũtonya kũsũanĩa ũndũ we ũtonya kwĩw'a keka nĩ mũkũũ. Kwoou aimantha ĩvinda ya kũelewa ũla mwana-a-asa mũkũũ na kũmwĩthukĩĩasya nesa ĩla ũkũneena. O aendeee o ũu, Alan aielewa ũndũ mũndũ mũkũũ wĩw'aa ĩla waemwa nĩ kũsoma Mbivilia nesa na kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba. Alan amina kũmanya ũndũ ũla mwana-a-asa mũkũũ ũthĩnĩkaa, yu aimanya ũtethyo ũla ũtonya kũmũnenga na ayĩthĩwa na wendi wa kũmũtethya. O naitũ no twĩke ta Alan. Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda twende ala angĩ o tondũ Ngai ũmendete, twaĩlĩte kwĩyosa ta ithyĩ twĩ na thĩna ũla twoona mwana-a-asa e naw'o.—1 Ako. 12:26.
7. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana ũkethĩa no tũũkwatya thĩna ũla andũ aangĩ me naw'o?
7 Ti laisi mavinda onthe kũmanya nesa vyũ mathĩna ala mũndũ wĩ namo. Andũ aingĩ nĩmakwatawa nĩ mathĩna o na mataatũkwata. Amwe nĩ onzu nũndũ wa kũũmĩa moomĩie, kũwaa, kana ũkũũ. Angĩ namo nĩmathĩnĩkaa mũno nũndũ wa kwĩkala makw'ĩte ngoo, me na kĩũũyũ kingĩ, kana me na kyeva kya kwĩthĩwa meekiwe naĩ navu tene. Namo angĩ maumĩte mĩsyĩ ĩtathaithaa vamwe kana mĩsyĩ yĩ mũsyai ũmwe. Kĩla mũndũ e thĩna ũ wake, na mavinda maingĩ thĩna ũsu twĩthĩawa ithyĩ ene tũtaakwatwa nĩw'o. Ĩla maũndũ meethĩwa mailyĩ ũu-ĩ, tũtonya kwenda ala angĩ ata o tondũ Ngai ũmendete? Nĩ kwa kwĩthukĩĩsya nesa ĩla mũndũ ũkũneena nĩ kana tũmanye ũndũ ũkwĩw'a, o na ethĩwa tũielewa vyũ. Ũu ũkatuma tũmũnenga ũtethyo ũla ũkwenda na kwa nzĩa ĩsu tũyonany'a nĩtũmwendete o tondũ Yeova ũmwendete. O na kau kĩla mũndũ ethĩawa na thĩna wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na wa ũla ũngĩ, no tũtetheesye ala angĩ makakwatya ũndũ Yeova wĩw'aa oona thĩna woo kana o tũkamatetheesya kwa nzĩa ingĩ.—Soma Alomi 12:15; 1 Vetelo 3:8.
ĨTHĨWA NA ĨNEE O TA YA YEOVA
8. Nĩ kyaũ kyatetheeisye Yesũ ethĩwe na ĩnee?
8 Mwana wa Ngai aisye atĩĩ: "Ũla Wĩ Ĩũlũ wa Onthe . . . nĩwe mũseo kwa ala mate mũvea na ala athũku." (Luka 6:35) O nake Yesũ aĩ na ĩnee ta ya Ngai. Nĩ kyaũ kyatumaa Yesũ ethĩwa ailyĩ ũu? Nĩwasũanĩaa mũno ũndũ kĩla ũkũweta na kĩla ũkwĩka kĩtonya kũtuma ala angĩ mew'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve mũndũ mũka ũmwe weesĩkĩe ta mwĩki wa naĩ. Mũthenya ũmwe nĩwookie vala ve Yesũ na ambĩĩa kũĩa etĩkĩsye methoi maũũnĩ ma Yesũ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ nĩwoonie kana mũndũ mũka ũsu nũkwĩlila na amanya kana amũneeny'a naĩ etuma akw'a ngoo mũno. Kwoou vandũ va kwĩka ũu, eekie kũmũkatha na amũekea. O na ĩla Mũvalisi waĩ vau wendie kwonany'a kana ti ta ũneeka nesa, Yesũ amũsũngĩie o kwa ĩnee.—Luka 7:36-48.
9. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩthĩwe twĩ na ĩnee ta Ngai? Nengane ngelekany'o.
9 Tũtonya kwĩka ata tũkonany'a kana twĩ ĩnee ta Ngai? Mũtũmwa Vaulo aandĩkie ũũ: "Ngombo ya Mwĩaĩi ndyaĩlwe nĩ ũkandanĩa, ĩndĩ nĩyaĩle kwĩthĩwa ĩ nduu kwa andũ onthe." (2 Tim. 2:24) Mũndũ mũuu nũmanyaa ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka ndakaũmĩsye ala angĩ ĩla maũndũ menda kwĩkala ta matonya kũthũka. Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũtonya kwĩka maũndũnĩ aa maatĩĩe: Twasye wĩ wĩanĩ na mũnene waku ndaũngamĩe wĩa wake nesa. Ũtonya kwĩka ata? Kana nũtonya kwona mwana-a-asa ooka ũmbanonĩ nake e na myei ũtavakinya. Ũtonya kũmwĩa ata? Kana ĩvinda yĩmwe ũitavany'a nũtonya kũkomana na mwene nyũmba na aikwĩa, "Ndi na mwanya, nĩngwatene." We no ũmũelewe? Kana twasye wĩ mũsyĩ na ũikũlw'a nĩ kĩveti kyaku kana mũemeu atĩĩ: "Watumie ũtandavya kĩla ũnavangĩĩe Wathanthatũ nĩkĩ?" We no ũmũsũngĩe na ĩnee? Tweeyosa ta ithyĩ twĩ na thĩna ũla wĩ na andũ asu, na twasũanĩa ũndũ ndeto sitũ itonya kũtuma mew'a, nĩtũtonya kũneena na kwĩka maũndũ mekwonany'a twĩ na ĩnee o ta Yeova.—Soma Nthimo 15:28.
TŨMĨA ŨĨ O TONDŨ NGAI WĨKAA
10, 11. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũtũmĩe ũĩ o tondũ Yeova wĩkaa? Nengane ngelekany'o.
10 Nũndũ twĩ na ũtonyi wa kũelewa ũndũ mũndũ ũtonya kwĩw'a akwatĩtwe nĩ ũndũ ũtaatũkwata, nĩtũtonya kũtũmĩa ũĩ maũndũnĩ o tondũ Yeova wĩkaa, na nũndũ wa ũu ũyĩthĩa no tũmanye kĩla kĩtonya kwĩkĩka tweeka ũndũ mũna. Nguma ya ũĩ nĩ ĩmwe katĩ wa nguma sya Yeova ila nene, na akenda kũmanya maũndũ ala mekwĩkĩka mũndũ eeka maũndũ mana, no amanye. Ithyĩ tũyamba kũmanya maũndũ ala makekĩka ĩvinda yũkĩte, ĩndĩ nĩtwaĩle kũsũanĩa kĩla kĩtonya kwĩkĩka tweeka ũndũ mũna. Aisilaeli mayaasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa kĩla kyaĩ kĩtonya kũmakwata malea kũmwĩw'a Ngai. O na kau Ngai nĩwamekĩte maũndũ maingĩ, Mose nĩweesĩ kana Aisilaeli makamũvĩtĩsya Yeova. Mũthenya ũmwe Mose ainie wathi wĩ na ndeto ii ethukĩĩw'e nĩ nguthu yonthe ya Aisilaeli: "Nĩ mbaĩ ĩtataĩkaa, na ndĩ ũmanyi nthĩnĩ wayo. A! Kethĩwa nĩ oĩ, na makamanya ũũ, na makasũanĩa mũminũkĩlyo woo!"—Kũt. 31:29, 30; 32:28, 29.
11 Ethĩwa nĩtũkwenda tũkekaa maũndũ kwa ũĩ o tondũ Ngai wĩkaa, nũseo tũkasũanĩa nĩ maũndũ meva matonya kwĩkĩka tweeka ũndũ mũna. O na mavinda angĩ no tũkũne visa wa maũndũ asu kĩlĩkonĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o ethĩwa nĩtũkwĩvaany'a, nĩtwaĩle kũlilikana kana wĩthĩawa wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisi mũno kwĩlikya mwĩkalĩlenĩ wa ũlaalai. Tũikaatate kũvangĩĩa maũndũ kana kwĩka ũndũ ũtonya kũtuma twananga ũnyanya wa mwanya ũla twĩ naw'o vamwe na Yeova! Vandũ va ũu twaĩlĩte kwĩka maũndũ kwosana na ndeto ii Ngai waveveee: "Mũndũ wĩ kĩlĩko nĩwonaa ũthũku, na kwĩvitha; ĩndĩ ala mate ũmanyi nĩmaendeeaa, na kũthĩna."—Nth. 22:3.
NDŨKETĨKĨLE KŨSŨANĨA MAŨNDŨ MATHŨKU
12. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva kũsũanĩa kũtonya kũtwananga?
12 Mũndũ mũĩ nĩwĩsĩ kana kũsũanĩa maũndũ no kũelekanw'e na mwaki. Ĩla mwaki watũmĩwa nesa, no ũtethye. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũtũtethasya ĩla tũkũua. Ĩndĩ mwaki ũthũkaa ĩla walea kũsianw'a naw'o na wavĩvya nyũmba vamwe na ala me nthĩnĩ. O ta ũu kũsũanĩa no kũtũtetheesye mũno ethĩwa twĩsũanĩa maũndũ matonya kũtuma tũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yeova. Ĩndĩ kũsũanĩa kũthũkaa ĩla twasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa maũndũ matonya kũtuma twambĩĩa kwĩthĩwa na mawendi mavuku. Kwa ngelekany'o, twamanyĩa kũsũanĩa maũndũ mathũku nĩtũtonya kwĩsa kwĩka maũndũ asu. Vate nzika, kũsũanĩaa maũndũ mathũku nĩkũtonya kwananga vyũ ũnyanya witũ na Yeova!—Soma Yakovo 1:14, 15.
13. Eva atonya kwĩthĩwa akũnaa visa ũilyĩ ata asũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla yaĩ mbee wake?
13 Kwasũanĩa kĩla kyatumie mũndũ mũka wa mbee, Eva, akwatwa nĩ wendi wa kũya ũla ũsyao "wa mũtĩ wa kũmanyĩthya ũseo na ũthũku." (Mwa. 2:16, 17) Nzoka yamwĩie atĩĩ: "Mũikakw'a nongi: nũndũ Ngai nĩwĩsĩ kana mũthenya ũla mũkaya waw'o, nĩvo mũkasalukw'a metho, nenyu mũkeethĩwa ta Ngai, mũkĩmanya ũseo na ũthũku." Ĩla Eva "wonie kana mũtĩ nĩ mũseo wa ũya, na nĩ wa kwendeesya methonĩ," eekie ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye: "Atw'a ũsyao waw'o, aya; na ĩngĩ anenga mũũme, nake aya." (Mwa. 3:1-6) Kwosana na Eva, nĩ ta vaĩ kĩndũ kĩseo ndetonĩ ila Satani wamũtavisye. Kĩndũ kĩva? Eva amanyie yu ndakatavaw'a ũla ũseo na ũla ũthũku, ĩndĩ akeetw'ĩĩaa ne we mwene. Kũsũanĩa kwa mũthemba ũsu kwaetie thĩna ũtaaoneka. Ata? Ĩla mũũme wake, Atamu, wavĩtisye, "naĩ yalikile kũũ nthĩ, na kĩkw'ũ kwondũ wa naĩ."—Alo. 5:12.
14. Mbivilia ĩtũtetheeasya ata twĩvetangane na ũlaalai?
14 Naĩ ĩla Eva weekie mũũndanĩ wa Eteni ndyaĩ ũlaalai. Ĩndĩ Yesũ nũtũkanĩtye ĩũlũ wa kũsũanĩa tũyĩka maũndũ makonetye ũlaalai. Aisye: "Kĩla mũndũ ũsyaasya mũndũ mũka na kũmwĩw'ĩa mũmeo nĩweka ũlaalai nake ngoonĩ yake." (Mt. 5:28) O nake Vaulo aumisye ũkany'o ũũ: "[Ekai] kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũkwĩanĩsya mawendi ma mwĩĩ."—Alo. 13:14, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
15. Nĩ ũthwii wĩva ũla twaĩle kwĩmanthĩa, na nĩkĩ?
15 Kũsũanĩa kũngĩ kũthũku nĩ kũla mũndũ ũkũnaa visa athuĩte vyũ na ũyĩthĩa ndakesa kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Ngai. Ĩndĩ ũw'o nĩ kana o na ethĩwa mũndũ nĩ mũthwii, malĩ yake ndĩmũsũvĩa nũndũ yĩthĩawa ĩilyĩ o 'ta wako mũtulu ũsũanĩonĩ wake.' (Nth. 18:11) Yesũ nĩwanenganie ngelekany'o ĩmwe nĩ kana onany'e kĩla kĩkwataa mũndũ "ũla wĩyũmbanĩasya isamũ, na ti mũthwii kwa Ngai." (Luka 12:16-21) Nake Yeova nĩwĩw'aa mũyo mũno ĩla tweeka maũndũ meũmwendeesya. (Nth. 27:11) Naitũ nĩtũtanaa ĩla watwĩtĩkĩla nũndũ wa kwĩyiĩa "ũthwii ĩtunĩ." (Mt. 6:20) Kĩu nĩkĩtumaa twĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, nayo nĩyo ũthwii ũla wa vata vyũ tũtonya kwĩmanthĩa.
NDŨKEMAKĨE
16. Nĩ ũndũ ũmwe mwaũ ũtonya kũtũtetheesya tũikemakĩe mũno?
16 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ tũtonya kũtindaa twĩmakĩe mũno wĩana twatw'ĩka kĩthito kitũ kyonthe kĩkeethĩawa kĩ kya kwĩyiĩa "ũthwii kũũ nthĩ." (Mt. 6:19) Yesũ nĩwanenganie ngelekany'o oonany'a kana "kwĩmakĩa kwa nthĩ, na ũkengani wa ũthwii," nitonya kũnyita ĩla ndeto ya Ũsumbĩ. (Mt. 13:18, 19, 22) Andũ amwe, methĩwe masũanĩaa ĩũlũ wa mbesa kana maisũanĩaa ĩũlũ wasyo, matindaa mathĩnĩkĩte ĩũlũ wa maũndũ mathũku ala monaa ta mesa kũmakwata. Ĩndĩ kwĩmakĩa mũno nĩkũtonya kũtũetee mowau na kũkananga ũnyanya witũ na Ngai. Kwoou nĩtũmwĩkwatyei Yeova na tũililikana kana "kĩmako ngoonĩ ya mũndũ nĩkĩminamasya; ĩndĩ ndeto nzeo nĩmĩtanasya." (Nth. 12:25) Ĩla twatavw'a ndeto nzeo sya kwĩkĩa vinya nĩ mũndũ ũtwĩsĩ nesa, nĩtwĩw'aa twatana mũno. Kwoou ethĩwa ve ũndũ ũũtuma twĩmakĩa, no tũneene na asyai maitũ, ũla tũtwaanĩte nake, kana o mũnyanyae witũ tũmũĩkĩĩe. Ethĩwa ũla tũũneena nake ethĩawa na woni ũilyĩ wa Ngai, nũtonya kũtũtetheesya tũkaeka kwĩmakĩa mũno.
17. Yeova atũtetheeasya ata tũikemakĩe mũno?
17 Vai mũndũ ũtũeleawa nesa ĩla tũkwĩmakĩa, ate o Yeova. Vaulo aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Mũikemakĩe kwa ũndũ o na wĩva; ĩndĩ kĩla ũndũnĩ mavata menyu nĩmatavanw'e kwa Ngai na kũvoya na kwĩsũva vamwe na kũtũnga mũvea. Na mũuo wa Ngai, ũla ũvĩtũkĩte ũmanyi w'onthe, ũkasũvĩaa ngoo syenyu na mosũanĩo menyu nthĩnĩ wa Klĩsto Yesũ." (Avi. 4:6, 7) Kwoou ĩla wĩmakĩĩte mũno sũanĩa ala tũnengetwe nĩ Yeova matũtetheesye tũendeee kwĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo nake. Nũtũnengete ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa, atumĩa ma kĩkundi, ngombo yĩ na kĩthito, alaĩka, Yesũ, o na ũ Yeova mwene nĩwĩyumĩtye atũtethye.
18. Kũsũanĩa kũtonya kũtũtethya ata?
18 O tondũ twoona, kũsũanĩa nĩkũtonya kũtũtetheesya twĩthĩwe na nguma ta sya Ngai, kwa ngelekany'o, wendo. (1 Yoa. 4:8) Tũkekalaa na ũtanu twenda ala angĩ kuma ngoonĩ, twasũanĩa kĩla kĩtonya kwĩkĩka nũndũ wa meko maitũ, na twatata tũikemakĩe mũno ũndũ vataĩle. Kwoou ekai tũtw'e vyũ kũtũmĩa nesa ũtonyi ũla Ngai ũtũnengete wa kũkũna visa kĩlĩkonĩ tũkona maũndũ ala ũtwathĩte, na nĩtũatĩĩei ngelekany'o yake ya wendo, ĩnee, ũĩ, na ũtanu.—Alo. 12:12.

translation:
"Be imitators of God, as beloved children." —Eph. 5:1.
1. Is it not beneficial for us to strive to please God in everything we do?
JEHOVAH helps us to be able to understand things that are difficult. And so we can learn to deal with situations, and we will be able to understand what a person feels when he is experiencing something good or bad, or when we make mistakes. (Read Ephesians 5:1, 2.) Can we use this quality now? Can we practice using this quality so that it may help us to become better people?
2. Does Jehovah care about how we feel?
2 Indeed, we know that God understands our feelings because He created humans and knows their weaknesses, and also because "Jesus felt sympathy" for imperfect humans. (John 10:16; 17:3; Heb. 4:15) And we realize that others who have experienced similar difficulties understand our feelings, and those who have always been successful may not understand what we are going through. In fact, Jehovah showed his empathy when the Israelites were slaves in Egypt. The Bible says that "He remembered His covenant." (Ps. 63:9) Many years later, the people of Judah were taken captive because of their sins, but God promised: "I will certainly remember them." (Zeph. 2:8) And just as a loving father cares for his child, Jehovah cares for his people and shows compassion. (Isa. 49:15) Furthermore, Jehovah understands our imperfections, and He is willing to forgive us.—Ps. 103:13, 14.
THE SYMPATHY JESUS SHOWED IS AN EXAMPLE OF GOD'S SYMPATHY
3. What evidence shows that Jesus was sympathetic?
3 Jesus understood how people felt, and he understood their struggles. For example, he rebuked the religious leaders for making life difficult for people, and many people benefited from his help. (Matt. 23:4; Mark 7:1-5; John 7:13) Jesus himself felt pain and became tired, so he understood what others were experiencing. This is why the Bible says: "Seeing the crowds, he felt pity for them, because they were harassed and abandoned like sheep without a shepherd." (Matt. 9:36) Jesus cared for people and did not hesitate to help them.—Ps. 103:8.
4. Did Jesus ever show sympathy toward people who were suffering?
4 While Jesus showed sympathy toward people, he often did something more than just feel sorry for them. Consider how he responded when he saw people who were troubled. For instance, on one occasion Jesus went out looking for people who were sad and comforted them. He noticed people were deeply moved, he felt pity for them, and he took the initiative to give them "more than enough."—Mark 6:30, 31, 34.
A REASON TO KEEP GOING WHEN WE FEEL DOWN
5, 6. Why can we be confident that God understands our feelings, and what can this help us to do? Let us examine some scriptures. (See also paragraph 24.)
5 We can be sure that God understands our feelings because he cares about us personally. Consider this example: A Christian named Alan was helping his nephew, who had difficulty reading well enough to pass his classes. And this nephew was also getting into trouble going from house to house. Alan helped his nephew by applying a principle that Jesus taught: "The way you want people to do to you, do the same to them." (Luke 6:31) Alan asked himself, 'Is this really the best way to help my nephew?' He then realized, 'I need to put myself in his place!' This helped the nephew to improve. But Jesus showed compassion in an even greater way, and he taught us to ask ourselves, 'How would I like to be treated if I were in this person's situation?'
6 So Alan realized that he needed to understand what his nephew was experiencing and show him empathy. And so, Alan came to realize that older people often struggle with learning to read the Bible and going from house to house. Alan understood why his nephew felt the way he did, and he knew how to encourage him. Let us imitate Alan. Let us always remember that God cares about us, and let us try to see things from the perspective of others—especially young ones.—1 Cor. 12:26.
7 Can we be certain that when we show kindness, others will respond kindly toward us?
7 It is true that sometimes people do not appreciate our efforts. Many are troubled and preoccupied with their own problems. Some are weighed down by worries, grief, or old age. Others may be facing difficulties because of illness, poverty, or feeling overlooked. Still others may have had bad experiences. Everyone has his own challenges, and there are many reasons why someone might not react positively to our ministry. But does this mean we should stop trying to help others simply because they don't respond favorably? Not at all! We can still show empathy and understanding, and we can strive to discern why they feel the way they do. This can help us to approach them tactfully and to continue witnessing to Jehovah. Also, each of us should be sensitive to the feelings of those around us and avoid saying or doing anything that might discourage them from serving Jehovah. And let us endeavor to put ourselves in their place and to view matters from their standpoint.—Read Romans 12:15; 1 Peter 3:8.
SHOWING COMPASSION AND EMPATHY
8. How did Jesus demonstrate compassion and empathy?
8 The Son of God said: "The lawless ones will never inherit the kingdom of God…but you continue loving your enemies." (Luke 6:35) Thus, Jesus showed compassion and empathy toward everyone. What motivated Jesus to be so compassionate? He understood that everyone deserves an opportunity to hear the good news. For example, imagine a man who is deaf. It would take effort to communicate with him. Yet, Jesus took the time to speak to such individuals and to help them understand his message. Jesus could see beyond their outward appearance and recognize whether they were sincere and willing to listen. So he treated them with kindness and consideration. And when his servants encountered similar situations, Jesus encouraged them to be patient and understanding.—Luke 7:36-48.
9. What can we do to show compassion and empathy? Consider the examples.
9 Can we show compassion even if we disagree with someone's views? The apostle Paul wrote: "With mildness let your attitude be known to all men." (2 Tim. 2:24) A wise person realizes that people often act the way they do because of their background and circumstances. Think about how difficult it might be to reason with someone who has strong prejudices. Let us consider some practical suggestions: Suppose we visit a brother who is going through a difficult time. Would we try to encourage him? Could we perhaps offer to help him with some chores? Or suppose we meet a sister who seems sad and withdrawn. Would we ask her what is troubling her? Imagine a homeowner who is annoyed because someone keeps interrupting him. Does he say, "I don't have time for this"? Do you understand? Similarly, if someone treats us unkindly, should we respond in kind? We need to remember that our words can either build up or tear down others, and we want to use our tongue to encourage others.—Read Proverbs 15:28.
USE YOUR TIME TO PRAISE GOD
10, 11. Why is it important for us to use our time to praise God? Consider an illustration.
10 Often, when we are busy, we find it hard to concentrate on spiritual matters. As a result, we may neglect to spend time praising God, and we may forget what is truly important. Our thinking becomes clouded, and we struggle to see things clearly. Prayer is like a vital link between us and Jehovah, and it helps us to maintain a close relationship with Him. It allows us to share our thoughts and feelings with Him, and He listens. By praying regularly, we can learn to discern what is right and wrong. The Israelites had to remind themselves constantly to obey God. Although God knew their hearts, Moses urged them to keep remembering His laws. On one occasion, Moses warned the entire nation of Israel: "Beware, lest you forget Jehovah your God. . . . Otherwise, you will certainly ruin yourselves, just as the nations that are ahead of you were ruined!"—Deut. 31:29, 30; 32:28, 29.
11 Therefore, let us make it a priority to spend time praising God, and let us be determined to focus on what is spiritually beneficial. We also need to be aware of distractions. At times, we may become preoccupied with trivial matters. However, if we remain vigilant, we can avoid being misled by false reasoning or becoming overly concerned about material possessions. Let us not allow ourselves to get carried away by selfish desires that could damage our friendship with Jehovah! Those who value their relationship with Jehovah will strive to heed this warning from God: "The person who is rich in wisdom is better than the one who is strong, and the one who has knowledge is more powerful than the one who has strength."—Prov. 22:3.
REMEMBER TO BE VIGILANT
12. What will help us to stay focused on what is important?
12 A person can easily become distracted or discouraged. But temptation is something we can cope with. For example, we might feel tired. Yet, we can still persevere. Temptation can come when we are feeling vulnerable, perhaps because of problems at home or difficulties at work. But resisting temptation will strengthen our determination to serve Jehovah faithfully. Being vigilant means recognizing that we are prone to making mistakes and striving to avoid situations that could lead us astray. It also means being willing to examine our thoughts and actions carefully so that we don't fall prey to worldly influences. By being vigilant, we can maintain our close bond with Jehovah!—Read James 1:14, 15.
13. How can we benefit from thinking ahead and considering potential pitfalls?
13 To help her husband make a decision, Eve was influenced by Satan, who presented a subtle lie about "the tree of knowledge of good and bad." (Gen. 2:16, 17) The serpent told her: "God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened and you will become like God, knowing what is good and what is bad." But did Eve simply want to know what was good and what was bad? The account reveals: "She took some of its fruit and ate; and she gave some to her husband, and he ate." (Gen. 3:1-6) Like Eve, we too may be misled if we allow Satan to influence us. Why? Because Eve desired to gain wisdom independently of God. What happened? Eve disregarded the clear distinction between good and bad, and she encouraged her husband to do the same. Her lack of self-control had disastrous consequences. Did her husband Adam show similar weakness? He "accepted from her hand and ate."—Rom. 5:12.
14. How does the Bible help us to remain steadfast?
14 Eve's mistake shows us the danger of yielding to temptation. Jesus showed us how to resist temptation when he taught us to avoid situations that could lead to wrongdoing. He said: "Anyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart." (Matt. 5:28) And Paul warned us: "[Keep] resisting temptation in the face of wicked desires."—Rom. 13:14, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language.
15. What can we learn from this, and why?
15 Resisting temptation requires each person to recognize their own weaknesses and to pray earnestly for God's help. In fact, a person may feel weak, but Jehovah will strengthen him so that he does not give in to temptation and say, "I am unable to endure temptation." (Prov. 18:11) Jesus demonstrated the importance of being honest with oneself about what motivates a person to be "greedy," and not pleasing to God. (Luke 12:16-21) Moreover, Jehovah gives us discernment so that we can make wise decisions. (Prov. 27:11) So let us strive to focus on "the things above." (Matt. 6:20) This will help us remain close to Jehovah, and this is the way to find lasting satisfaction.
CONSIDER THIS
16. What is one thing we can do to strengthen our resolve?
16 To resist temptation, we need to avoid storing up "treasure on earth." (Matt. 6:19) Jesus explained that those who are preoccupied with "riches and glory" may fail to understand the meaning of the parable. (Matt. 13:18, 19, 22) Some people, because they worry about material possessions or about what others think, may become overly concerned with accumulating wealth. But storing up such treasures can distract us from cultivating our relationship with God. We should rather trust in Jehovah and remember that "concern for a person makes him act foolishly; but reliance on Jehovah means success." (Prov. 12:25) If we allow anxiety to control our thinking, we will weaken our resolve. We may then start to rationalize our wrong desires, or we may feel overwhelmed by our problems. However, when we rely on Jehovah, we gain peace of mind and strength to resist temptation.
17. How does Jehovah help us to resist temptation?
17 Jehovah understands our imperfections and cares about how we cope with temptation. He assures us: "Keep making appeals to God for wisdom, and he will give it to you generously. . . . If you ask, he will give to you." (James 1:5, 6) So when we face temptation, we can pray to Jehovah for help to remain firm in our dedication and to make wise decisions. With God's spirit, which is powerful beyond measure, he can strengthen us and help us to overcome trials through Christ Jesus. (Phil. 4:6, 7) Thus, if we earnestly seek Jehovah's guidance, he will help us to continue walking in his ways and maintain our integrity. We can also benefit from the support of fellow Christians—congregations, groups, assemblies, conventions, and publications—as well as from Jesus himself, and especially from Jehovah, who delights to help us.
18. What more can help us to resist temptation?
18 Importantly, love is a strong motive for resisting temptation and remaining loyal to God, for example, love. (1 John 4:8) As we cultivate love in our heart, we will be motivated to please Jehovah and to avoid doing anything that would displease him, and we will strive to live in harmony with his laws. This will help us to appreciate more fully the value of God's gift of free will and to show appreciation for his loving provisions—yes, his mercy, his kindness, and his patience.—Acts 12:12.

text:
"Ũu ũkeethĩwa, ethĩwa mũkeew'aa na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo wasya wa Yeova Ngai wenyu."—NZEK. 6:15.
MBATHI: 17, 136
1, 2. Nzekalia aimina kwonw'a woni wake wa mũonza Ayuti ala maĩ Yelusaleme maendeee ata?
MWATHANI Nzekalia amina kwonw'a woni wake wa mũonza nĩwatiiwe na maũndũ maingĩ ma kũsũanĩa. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yeova nĩwamũĩkĩĩthĩtye kana ndaema kwosea andũ mate aĩkĩĩku ĩtambya nũndũ wa meko moo mathũku. Vai nzika kana watho ũsu nĩweekĩie Nzekalia vinya. Ĩndĩ kũvikĩa vau, maũndũ maendeee o ta tene. Andũ maendeee o kwĩthĩwa mate aĩkĩĩku na no meekaa maũndũ angĩ mathũku, naw'o mwako wa ĩkalũ ya Yeova waĩ vaasa mũno vyũ na kũthela. Nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie Ayuti moolwa na mĩtũkĩ wĩa ũla manengetwe nĩ Ngai? Masyokie nthĩ yoo nĩ kana o masembany'e na maũndũ ala moo ene?
2 Nzekalia nĩweesĩ kana Ayuti ala masyokie Yelusaleme maĩ andũ me mũĩkĩĩo. Asu nĩmo "Ngai waamũkisye maveva moo" matia mĩsyĩ yoo ĩla mekalaa me eanĩe na viasala syoo nzeo. (Esa. 1:2, 3, 5) Matiie nthĩ ĩla meesĩ mathi kũndũ aingĩ moo mataĩ maaona. Keka mayoonaa kwaka ĩngĩ ĩkalũ ya Yeova kwĩ kwa vata, mayĩthĩwa maakwatya kyalo kyũmĩte ũu kya maili ta 1,000 (kĩlomita 1,600) mesĩle nthĩ yĩ iĩma na weũ wĩ mavia.
3, 4. Ayuti ala masyokie makomanie na mathĩna meva?
3 Kyalo kĩu kyoo kĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kyailyĩ ata? No nginya Ayuti asu methĩwe matũmĩie ĩvinda yingĩ maisũanĩa ũndũ kũla maendete kũtũa kwailyĩ. Nĩmeew'ĩte ngewa sya ũndũ navu tene ndũa ya Yelusaleme yaanakavĩte. Ala akũũ vyũ maĩ kyalonĩ kĩu nĩmeeyoneete ũseo wa ĩkalũ yĩla yaĩ vo. (Esa. 3:12) Keka waĩ kyalonĩ kĩu namo wĩthĩwa weewie ata woona Yelusaleme ya mbee? Nĩwĩthĩwa watelemile woona masũmba maombokangu mavw'ĩkĩtwe nĩ ĩia kĩla vandũ? We woona ũndũ ngũta isu syaombokangĩte na ũndũ syaĩ na mavũthi manene kũla kwaĩ mbingĩlo na kũla myako mĩtũlu ya mũnyoolo yaakĩtwe, nĩwĩthĩwa waambĩĩe kũsũanĩa ũndũ ngũta isu syaĩ kĩvathũkany'o na ũvai wa Mbaviloni, ũla waĩ wa ngũta ilĩ syakanĩw'e vamwe? Ĩndĩ Ayuti nĩmoosie vinya. Nĩmeeyoneete Yeova aimatangĩĩa kyalonĩ kĩu kyonthe kya kwĩnũka. Kĩndũ kya mbee kĩla meekie mavika oou kyaĩ kwaka kĩthembeo vala vaakĩtwe ĩkalũ tene, na ĩndĩ mambĩĩa kumĩsya Yeova nthembo kĩla mũthenya. (Esa. 3:1, 2) Mũndũ asisya ũthangaau ũla maĩ naw'o mavika oou aĩ atonya kwasya vai kĩndũ o na kĩva kĩkamatũla ngoo.
4 Eka wĩa wa kwaka ĩkalũ, Aisilaeli asu maĩ na wĩa ũngĩ wa kwaka ĩngĩ ndũa syoo. Nĩmaaĩle kwĩyakĩa nyũmba, mavande mĩũnda, na maimantha kyaũya. (Esa. 2:70) Wĩa ũla maĩ naw'o ko ũtaĩ mwingĩ! Na wingĩvĩte oou waingĩvĩte, amaitha nĩmookĩlile na vinya mambĩĩa kũmavĩnga. O na vala nĩmaũngamie na ĩvĩndĩ ya mũongo kwa ĩvinda, myaka 15 ĩithela nĩ ta maĩ manaminwa vinya nĩ ala mamavĩngaa. (Esa. 4:1-4) Ĩndĩ yu kĩla kyamaminie vyũ nĩ kĩla kyamakwatie mwakanĩ wa 522 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. Mwakanĩ ũsu mũsumbĩ wa Velisia nĩwaũngamisye vyũ wĩa wa kwaka Yelusaleme. Mũndũ aĩ atonya kwasya yu ndũa ĩsu nĩyathela vyũ.—Esa. 4:21-24.
5. Yeova atetheeisye andũ make ata masyokee wĩa?
5 Yeova nĩweesĩ kĩla kyesaa kũtethya andũ make. Oonisye Nzekalia woni wa mũthya nĩ kana aĩkĩĩthye Ayuti kana nũmendete na kana nĩwoonaa kĩla meekĩte kĩ kya vata. O na woni ũsu nĩwesaa kũmaĩkĩĩthya kana nũkũmasũvĩa masyokea wĩa wake. Amatavisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa wĩa ũsu wa kwaka ĩkalũ ĩngĩ: "Ũu ũkeethĩwa, ethĩwa mũkeew'aa na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo wasya wa Yeova Ngai wenyu."—Nzek. 6:15.
ITA SYA ALAĨKA
6. (a) Nĩ kyaũ Nzekalia woonie mbee woninĩ wake wa nyanya? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 26.) (b) Nĩkĩ mbalasi isu syaĩ sya malangi me kĩvathũkany'o?
6 Woni wa mũthya katĩ wa mawoni nyanya ala Nzekalia wooniw'e nũtonya kwĩthĩwa new'o walũlũmĩilye mũĩkĩĩo woo vyũ. (Soma Nzekalia 6:1-3.) Kwasũanĩa kĩla Nzekalia woonie. Oonie makasya ana mailyĩ ta ma kaũ mokĩte "kuma katĩ wa iĩma ilĩ . . . sya ũthuku." Mbalasi ila syakusĩtye makasya asu syaĩ na malangi me kĩvathũkany'o. Kwoou vayaĩ vinya kũvathũkany'a atwai ma mbalasi isu. Nzekalia asyona akũlilye atĩĩ: "Ii nĩ myaũ?" (Nzek. 6:4) O naitũ no twende kũmanya nĩsyo myaũ nũndũ ũsu nĩ woni ũtũkonetye.
Ũmũnthĩ Yeova no ũtũmĩaa alaĩka kũlũlũmĩlya na kũsũvĩa andũ make
7, 8. (a) Ila iĩma ilĩ syonanasya kyaũ? (b) Nĩkĩ iĩma isu syũmbĩtwe na ũthuku?
7 Ve mavinda Mbivilia ĩtũmĩaa iĩma ĩineenea mosumbĩ kana silikalĩ. Iĩma ila Nzekalia ũeleetye no ũndũ ũmwe na ila iwetetwe wathaninĩ wa Ndanieli. Kĩĩma kĩmwe nĩ ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova wa tene na tene. Nakyo kĩĩma kĩla kĩngĩ nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Masia wĩ mokonĩ ma Yesũ. (Nda. 2:35, 45) Kuma Yesũ asumbĩka mwaka wa 1914, iĩma isu nĩsyĩthĩĩtwe iithũkũma syĩ vamwe na iianĩsya ũndũ wa vata mũno ũkonetye kĩeleelo kya Ngai ĩũlũ wa nthĩ.
8 Nĩkĩ ĩima isu syũmbĩtwe na ũthuku? O ta thaavu, kyũma kya ũthuku nĩ kyũma kya thooa mũnene. Yeova eeie andũ make nĩmatũmĩe kyũma kĩu kĩtisatisaa mayaka yĩla ĩeema ya kũmbanĩa, na no wamatavisye meke oou ĩla maakaa ĩkalũ yĩla yaĩ Yelusaleme. (Kuma 27:1-3; 1 Asu. 7:13-16) Kwoou ngelekany'o ĩsu ya iĩma sya ũthuku nĩyaĩle vyũ nũndũ kĩu kĩtũlilikanasya kana ũsumbĩki ũla mũnene vyũ wa Yeova na Ũsumbĩ wa Masia nĩ mosumbĩ ma vata mũno, na makaetee andũ mũuo na moathimo maingĩ mũno.
9. Ala matwaĩte makasya naaũ, na manengiwe wĩa wĩva?
9 Yu ekai tũneenee ĩngĩ ala makasya. Makasya asu na ala mamatwaĩte moonanasya kyaũ? Ala matwaĩte makasya asu nĩ alaĩka. Nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa maĩ nguthu kana ikundi syĩ kĩvathũkany'o sya alaĩka. (Soma Nzekalia 6:5-8.) Nguthu isu syaumĩte "vala iũngamaa mbee wa Mwĩaĩi wa nthĩ yonthe" na syanengetwe wĩa wa mwanya. Syanengetwe wĩa wĩva? Makasya asu na ala mamatwaĩte matũmĩtwe isionĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o. Matũmĩtwe makasũvĩe andũ ma Yeova, na mũno mũno maaĩlĩte kũmasũvĩana na "nthĩ ya ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ," ĩla nĩ Mbaviloni. Yeova aĩ aĩkĩĩthye kana Mbaviloni ndĩkatava andũ make ĩngĩ. No nginya woni ũsu wĩthĩwe wakiakĩisye mũno ala maakaa ĩkalũ ĩvindanĩ ya Nzekalia. Mayesaa kũthĩnĩka mayona ta mesa kũvĩngĩĩswa nĩ amaitha ĩngĩ.
10. Andũ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ makiakiaw'a ata nĩ wathani wa Nzekalia ĩũlũ wa ala makasya na atwai mamo?
10 O tondũ kwailyĩ ĩvindanĩ ya Nzekalia, ũmũnthĩ Yeova wa nguthu no ũtũmĩaa alaĩka kũlũlũmĩlya na kũsũvĩa andũ make. (Mal. 3:6; Aevl. 1:7, 14) Kuma mwaka wa 1919, ĩla Isilaeli ma kĩ-veva mathaiw'e kuma mũtavonĩ wa ngelekany'o wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene, vai mũndũ wĩthĩĩtwe atonya kũũngamya wĩa wa Yeova. (Ũvu. 18:4) Nũndũ nĩtũsũvĩawa nĩ alaĩka, tũyaĩle kwĩthĩwa na wia tũyona ũseũvyo wa Yeova ta ũtonya kwĩsa kũtavwa ĩngĩ nĩ ndĩni sya ũvũngũ. (Sav. 34:7) Vandũ va ũu, no twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo kana athũkũmi ma Ngai ĩũlũ wa nthĩ yonthe meendeea kũsonga na mbee kĩ-veva. Kũvindĩĩsya nesa woni wa Nzekalia nĩkũtumaa twĩthĩwa tũte na nzika kana twĩ asũvĩe vyũ nĩ ila iĩma ilĩ.
11. Nĩkĩ tũtaĩle kũkwatwa nĩ wia twasũanĩa ĩvinda yĩla andũ ma Ngai mevithũkĩwa?
11 O mĩtũkĩ mũno vyũ ngwatanĩo sya siasa sya nthĩ ĩno ya Satani ikoombana vamwe syĩ na kĩeleelo kya kũmina andũ ma Ngai. (Esek. 38:2, 10-12; Nda. 11:40, 44, 45; Ũvu. 19:19) Wathani wa Esekieli ũeleetye kana ngwatanĩo isu ikooka ta ĩthweo ivw'ĩke nthĩ, na ikookĩla ĩũlũ witũ syĩ na ũthilĩku mwingĩ ikuĩtwe nĩ mbalasi. (Esek. 38:15, 16) * Nĩtwaĩle kũkĩa? Tũyaĩle kũkĩa o na vanini! Twĩ na nguthu nene yĩ na makasya ma kaũ. Ĩla tũkavika vau ĩvindanĩ ya ũla thĩna mũnene, alaĩka ma Yeova wa nguthu makoombana nĩ kana masũvĩe andũ ma Ngai na mayananga ala mavĩngaa ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. (2 Ath. 1:7, 8) Ũsu ũkeethĩwa wĩ mũthenya mũnene ta kĩ! Ĩndĩ ũla ũkatongoesya ita isu sya Yeova sya ĩtunĩ nũũ?
YEOVA AINENGA ŨKŨMŨ ŨLA ŨMŨTW'ĨTE MŨSUMBĨ NA MŨTHEMBI
12, 13. (a) Nzekalia eeiwe nĩeke ata? (b) Twĩsĩ ata kana ũla mũndũ weetiwe Ũvonge nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto?
12 Kũvikĩa vau Nzekalia oonetw'e mawoni nyanya na amonetw'e e weka. Ĩndĩ yu eeiwe eke ũndũ ũngĩ kĩla mũndũ ene nĩ kana ekĩe vinya ala maendeee kwaka ĩngĩ ĩkalũ. Ũndũ ũsu waĩ wathani. (Soma Nzekalia 6:9-12.) Nzekalia eeiwe nĩose vetha na thaavu kuma kwa andũ atatũ maĩ manavika maumĩte Mbaviloni na ayĩitũmĩa kũseũvya ngovia nzeo mũno ya ũsumbĩ. Andũ asu maĩ Elitai, Toviya, na Yetaia. (Nzek. 6:11) We Nzekalia eeiwe nĩekĩe Ngavana Nzeluvaveli ũla waĩ wa mbaĩ ya Yuta na waĩ nzyawa ya Ndaviti ngovia ĩsu? Aiee. No nginya ala masyaĩĩsye makethĩwa maseng'ie ĩla weekĩie Mũthembi Mũnene Yosua ngovia ĩsu.
13 Ĩkũlyo nĩ, Ĩla Mũthembi Mũnene Yosua weekĩiwe ngovia ĩsu nĩwatw'ĩkie mũsumbĩ? Aiee. Kĩtumi nũndũ Yosua ndaĩ wa nzyawa ya Ndaviti ĩla yaumaa asumbĩ, na nũndũ wa ũu ndaaĩlĩte kũtw'ĩka mũsumbĩ. Kwoou kwĩka ũu kwaĩ wathani wa ũla Ngai ũkanyuva atw'ĩke mũsumbĩ na mũthembi tene na tene. Ũla mũthembi mũnene watw'ĩkĩthiw'e mũsumbĩ eetiwe Ũvonge. Maandĩko monanĩtye nesa kana ũsu wĩtĩtwe Ũvonge nĩ Yesũ Klĩsto.—Isa. 11:1; Mt. 2:23. *
14. Nĩ wĩa wĩva Yesũ ũtethasya e Mũsumbĩ na Mũthembi Mũnene?
14 Yesũ e Mũsumbĩ na Mũthembi Mũnene nĩwe mũtongoi wa nguthu sya Yeova sya ĩtunĩ. O na nũtethasya wĩa wake na kĩthito nĩ kana andũ ma Ngai mekale me asũvĩĩku o na kau matwĩe nthĩ yusĩe andũ ang'endu. (Yel. 23:5, 6) O mĩtũkĩ Klĩsto nũkũtongosya kaũnĩ wa kwananga mbaĩ nĩ kana atetee andũ ma Yeova na aikwata mbau ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai. (Ũvu. 17:12-14; 19:11, 14, 15) Ĩndĩ Ũvonge atanamba kũete ũsilĩlo, ve wĩa ũngĩ mũnene waĩle kwamba kwĩanĩsya.
NĨWANENGIWE WĨA WA KWAKA ĨKALŨ
15, 16. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva ũmũnthĩ andũ ma Ngai mombanĩtw'e ĩngĩ na makathew'a, na nũũ ũla wĩkĩte ũu? (b) Kũkeethĩwa moseo meva mũthyanĩ wa ũla Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Klĩsto?
15 Ve wĩa ũngĩ Yesũ wanengiwe eka kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩ na Mũthembi Mũnene. Eeiwe "akaaka ĩkalũ ya Yeova." (Soma Nzekalia 6:13.) Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ tũĩ, wĩa wa kwaka ũla Yesũ ũtethetye nĩ vamwe na kumya athaithi ma w'o mũtavonĩ wa Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene, na kũmbany'a ĩngĩ kĩkundi kya Kĩklĩsto. Maũndũ asu amekie mwaka wa 1919. O na nĩwanyuvie "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" nĩ kana ĩvangĩthasye wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũla ũtethaw'a nĩ kĩlungu kya yĩla ĩkalũ ya kĩ-veva kya kũũ nthĩ. (Mt. 24:45) O na ĩngĩ Yesũ nĩwĩthĩĩtwe e mũthangaau mũno wĩanĩ wa kũthesya andũ ma Ngai na kũmatetheesya mamũthũkũme Yeova ũndũ wendaa.—Mal. 3:1-3.
16 Ĩvindanĩ ya ũla Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili, Yesũ na ala asumbĩ na athembi 144,000 makasumbĩka vamwe nake, makavetea andũ aĩkĩĩku naĩ vyũ. Ĩla kĩu kĩkeanĩw'a, no athaithi ma w'o ma Ngai me oka makatiwa kũũ nthĩ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ kũtakethĩwa ũthaithi ũngĩ kũũ nthĩ eka o ũthaithi ũla wa w'o!
KWATA KW'OKO WĨA ŨLA ŨENDEEE WA KWAKA
17. Yeova asyokie aĩkĩĩthya Ayuti kyaũ, na ndeto syake syamatethisye ata?
17 W'o ũvoo wa Nzekalia watetheeisye Ayuti ata ĩvindanĩ yĩu? Yeova nĩwamaĩkĩĩthisye kana makekalaa na mũuo na akamasũvĩaa maendeea kũtethya wĩa wake. Ĩla wamaĩkĩĩthisye kana ĩkalũ yĩkaakwa, no nginya methĩwe mausũiwe nĩ wĩkwatyo ngoonĩ syoo. Ĩndĩ mesaa kũtethya wĩa wingĩvĩte ũu ata na nĩw'o manyivĩte? Ndeto ila Nzekalia wasyokie amatavya nĩsyavetangie wia kana nzika ila methĩwa maĩ nasyo. Ngai nĩwawetie kana andũ angĩ aingĩ aĩkĩĩku o ta Elitai, Toviya, na Yetaia "makooka na makyaka ĩkalũnĩ ya Yeova." (Soma Nzekalia 6:15.) Kwoou nũndũ kũvikĩa vau nĩmamanyie kana Ngai nũkũmatetheesya, mayaananga saa. Malikile wĩanĩ maendeea na mwako o na kau mũsumbĩ wa Velisia nĩwaĩ anaumya mwĩao wa kũũngamya wĩa ũsu. O na vayaavĩta ĩvinda ĩasa Yeova ataumĩtye kĩsiĩĩi kĩu kĩnene kyeekĩĩtwe nĩ mũsumbĩ ũsu. Ĩtina wa ũu ĩkalũ nĩyathelile mwakanĩ wa 515 Klĩsto ate mũsyae. (Esa. 6:22; Nzek. 4:6, 7) Ĩndĩ ndeto isu Yeova waneenie syoonanisye kana ve maũndũ maseo mũnango maĩlĩte kwĩanĩa ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ yitũ.
18. Ĩandĩko ya Nzekalia 6:15 yĩanĩaa ata ũmũnthĩ?
18 Ũmũnthĩ andũ milioni mbingĩ nĩmaendeee kũlika ũthaithinĩ wa w'o, na nĩmew'aa ngoo syoo iimasukuma maumĩsye Yeova 'syĩndũ syoo' ila nzeo vyũ nĩ kana makwate mbau wĩa wa kwaka yĩla ĩkalũ yake ĩnene ya kĩ-veva. Syĩndũ isu nĩ ta ĩvinda yoo, vinya woo, na malĩ yoo. (Nth. 3:9) Tũtonya kũmanya ata nesa vyũ kana Yeova nũtanaa oona tũilũmany'a nake? Lilikana kana Elitai, Toviya, na Yetaia nĩmaetie syĩndũ ila syatũmĩiwe nĩ Nzekalia kũseũvya ĩla ngovia ya ũsumbĩ. Ngovia ĩsu yatw'ĩkie "ũlilikan'yo" wa ũndũ meeyumisye nĩ kana makwate mbau ũthaithi wa w'o. (Nzek. 6:14) O ta ũu, wĩa ũla tũtethasya vamwe na wendo ũla twĩthĩawa naw'o kwondũ wa Yeova nĩ syĩndũ itakola. (Aevl. 6:10) Yeova akaililikanaa kĩla ĩvinda.
19. Ala mawoni Nzekalia wooniw'e maĩlĩte kũtũtethya ata ũmũnthĩ?
19 Wĩa ũla ũtethetw'e kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa w'o ũtũĩkĩĩthasya kana Yeova nũtũathimĩte na Klĩsto e vamwe naitũ atũtongoesye. Ũsu nĩ ũĩkĩĩthyo mũlũmu na tũwene na metho maitũ. Twĩ ũseũvyonĩ mũlũmu ũtakanangĩka tene na tene na ũtũsũvĩaa. Ũndũ w'onthe wosanĩte na kĩeleelo kya Yeova kwondũ wa ũthaithi wa w'o "ũkeethĩwa," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ũkeanĩa. Tanĩa kĩanda kyaku andũnĩ ma Yeova na 'ũyĩw'aa na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo wasya wa Yeova Ngai waku.' Weeka ũu ũkekalaa ũsũvĩonĩ wa Mũsumbĩ na Mũthembi Mũnene vamwe na ala atwai ma ala makasya ma kaũ ma ĩtunĩ. Ĩka kyonthe kĩla ũtonya ũkwate mbau ũthaithi wa w'o. Weeka ũu, ĩthĩwa ũte na nzika kana Yeova wa nguthu akaũsũvĩaa ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ yĩtiele nthĩ ĩno ĩtanamba kũthela, o na kũvika tene na tene!
