translation:
"This is what love is: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his son as a propitiation for our sins."—1 JOHN 4:10.
FOOTNOTES: 17, 136
1, 2. Why did Ezekiel feel distressed when he saw the disgusting sights in Jerusalem, and how far did his distress extend?
CONSIDER this: Ezekiel felt deeply disturbed by the revolting things he saw. For example, Jehovah showed him visions of what would happen to Jerusalem when it was besieged. How do you think Ezekiel reacted to such distressing visions? To help you understand, let us examine some points. The visions extended to future events, and they revealed how people would act wickedly and reject Jehovah's standards. What motivated Ezekiel to record these visions and share them with the people?
2 Ezekiel knew that the people of Jerusalem were rejecting Jehovah. That is why he said: "The God of Israel himself has said, 'They are rebellious, stubbornly rebellious.'" (Isa. 1:2, 3, 5) But why was it so important to record these details? Because Jehovah wanted his people to know what he thought of their actions, and he wanted them to realize the consequences of disobeying him. Did Ezekiel find it easy to deliver such a message? Was he tempted to give up?
3, 4. What shocked Ezekiel about the disgusting practices he saw?
3 Why did this faithful man feel deeply disturbed? He saw how badly the people had deteriorated morally and spiritually. It reminded him of the condition of Jerusalem when it was destroyed. The people were engaging in shameful practices, and their wickedness extended over an area of about 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers), affecting many communities.
3, 4. What disgusted Ezekiel about the disgusting practices he saw?
3 How could such a large territory become so corrupt? Well, Ezekiel realized that the leaders were largely responsible for the deterioration. They were misleading the people. (Isa. 3:12) So, would those leaders ever be held accountable for their actions in Jerusalem? Would they be punished for causing so much suffering and for leading the people astray? When you see injustice and corruption around you, does it make you angry? Do you feel like speaking out against it? Ezekiel felt strongly about the injustices he observed, and he did not hesitate to expose them, just as he exposed the wickedness of Babylon. Ezekiel was determined to speak the truth. He trusted that Jehovah would vindicate him. He knew that eventually, Jehovah would clear his name and prove that he was right. (Isa. 3:1, 2) A person who is loyal to Jehovah will always strive to do what is right and will never compromise his integrity.
4 In the past, the Israelites often made vows without keeping them. They built houses, conducted business, and practiced religion hypocritically. (Isa. 2:70) But now things were going to be different! Their religious activities were meaningless because they were insincere. And soon they would experience hardship—about 15 years of exile—as a result of their hypocrisy. (Isa. 4:1-4) However, there was hope for those who remained faithful. They would survive the destruction of Jerusalem in 522 B.C.E. During that time, the land of Persia would dominate the region. A faithful person can find comfort in knowing that.—Isa. 4:21-24.
5. What question will we answer next?
5 Jehovah is able to fulfill his purpose regarding mankind. He foretold what would happen to Egypt and Babylon and accurately predicted everything that has come to pass. And he is able to carry out his purpose and bring about the salvation of his people. He inspired the following prophecy concerning the future of the ancient nation: "This people have hardened their hearts, so let them experience my anger."—Zeph. 6:15.
LOOK FOR MORE COMFORT
6. (a) What did Zephaniah warn his brothers about? (See accompanying article on page 26.) (b) What lessons can we learn from their example?
6 The faithful men of ancient times knew that Jehovah could intervene in their behalf when they were loyal to him. (Read Zephaniah 6:1-3.) Consider what Zephaniah warned. He spoke of a time coming when there would be "darkness in the midst of noon." This warning helped those faithful men to discern the signs of the times and understand why bad things were happening. They realized that such events were a signal that the end was near. Zephaniah also asked: "Is this not what I foretold?" (Zeph. 6:4) So let us find out what he foretold so that we too may be prepared.
Jehovah uses comfort to strengthen and encourage his people
7, 8. (a) What does 'noon' represent? (b) Why is darkness associated with calamity?
7 The Bible often uses symbolic language. In Zephaniah's prophecy, "noon" represents a time of great spiritual light, similar to the vision given to Daniel. One feature of this vision was "the magnificent kingdom of Jehovah," and another was "the Kingdom of the Messiah." (Dan. 2:35, 45) Since Jesus began ruling in 1914, this period has been marked by increasing evidence that God's purpose is about to be fulfilled.
8 Why is darkness associated with calamity? Well, darkness symbolizes distress. Jehovah allows his people to experience trials to refine their faith, and he gives them strength to endure until Jerusalem is liberated. (Isa. 27:1-3; 1 Thess. 7:13-16) Therefore, the events signaling this time of darkness should remind us that the magnificent kingdom of Jehovah and the Kingdom of the Messiah are close, and they will bring relief to mankind and countless blessings.
9 How can we remain steadfast, and what will result?
9 We need more faith than ever. But how can we strengthen our faith? Steadfast ones are those who have proved themselves trustworthy. We can learn from their example. (Read Zephaniah 6:5-8.) We must strive to "guard our hearts" and avoid being distracted by worldly concerns. How can we avoid distractions? By focusing on what is spiritually important. Focus on serving Jehovah, and do not become involved with "Babylon the Great," which represents the world empire of false religion. Jehovah will protect his faithful servants from Babylon. Remember the warning given to the ancient Israelites in Zephaniah. Let us not allow ourselves to be influenced by others.
10 Why are true Christians interested in Zephaniah's prophecy and its fulfillment?
10 Because of Zephaniah's prophecy, Jehovah has helped his people to discern truth and to separate themselves from wickedness. (Mal. 3:6; Eph. 1:7, 14) In 1919, when spiritual Israel was released from the symbolic chains of Babylon the Great, individual Christians were able to support God's organization fully. (Acts 18:4) Although we are united, we should always be willing to correct our thinking if we see evidence that Jehovah's view differs from ours. (Ps. 34:7) Today, many are experiencing persecution because they remain loyal to God and his Kingdom. By studying Zephaniah's prophecy, we can strengthen our resolve to stand firm.
11 How can we maintain our loyalty when faced with trials that test the faith of God's people?
11 The nations will become agitated over Satan's scheme to deceive mankind and turn them away from God. (Ezek. 38:2, 10-12; Dan. 11:40, 44, 45; Rev. 19:19) Ezekiel's vision indicates that this agitation will escalate into an attack on God's people, and it will involve a great army. (Ezek. 38:15, 16) * What can we learn from this? We can learn much! With strong confidence, we can face any challenge. But let us remember that it is Jehovah who strengthens us, and he uses his organization to help his faithful servants and to direct them according to his purpose. (2 Thess. 1:7, 8) This assurance gives us great comfort! Will you continue to trust in Jehovah and his promises?
JEHOVAH WILL GIVE US THE STRENGTH AND CONFIDENCE WE NEED
12, 13. (a) What questions does Zephaniah raise? (b) Why is it important for each one of us to examine whether our faith is rooted in Jesus Christ?
12 Let us consider how Zephaniah appealed to the consciences of the people and how he affected them. He showed them that they were facing a crisis, and he urged them to seek Jehovah while he could still be found. (Read Zephaniah 6:9-12.) Zephaniah reminded the people about the example of those who had opposed rebuilding Jerusalem and who tried to frustrate God's purpose. Those men included Shecaniah, Tobiah, and Jedayah. (Neh. 6:11) Did Zephaniah appeal to Governor Nehemiah, who was a descendant of David, to take action? No, he encouraged him to rely on the Most High God, Joshua.
13 So, did the Most High God, Joshua, respond to their appeals? Yes. Because Joshua was a descendant of David, he had authority to deal with opposition, and because of his faith, he was able to overcome it. This shows us that when we trust in God, he can empower us to overcome obstacles. The high priest was also empowered to overcome opposition, and his name was Joshua. The Scriptures show us that this Joshua is Jesus Christ.—Isa. 11:1; Matt. 2:23.*
14. How did Jesus fulfill this prophecy regarding the high priest and the Messiah?
14 Jesus as the High Priest and the Messiah is the leader of God's army. And he will use his power to protect his people and to give them victory over all enemies. (Jer. 23:5, 6) As King Christ will cleanse the earth from wickedness and cause people to worship Jehovah and support God's great sovereignty. (Rev. 17:12-14; 19:11, 14, 15) Indeed, the Branch has become a great king, and he will bring peace to the land.
LOOKING AHEAD TO THE FUTURE
15, 16. (a) Why have God's people been scattered among the nations, and what will happen to reverse this? (b) What is involved in proving oneself faithful during the time of Christendom's final years?
15 Yes, Jesus has been made powerful in heaven as the High Priest and the Messiah. He is the "root of Jesse." (Read Zechariah 6:13.) In recent years, those who make up the root of Jesse have been associated with opposing Babylon the Great, and they have strengthened the Christian congregation. These events began in 1919. And they have demonstrated "loyalty and faithfulness" in the face of intense persecution and opposition during this last period of the end times. (Matt. 24:45) Also, Jesus has appointed a faithful slave to provide food at the proper time to his servants and to teach them about Jehovah's purposes.—Mal. 3:1-3.
16 Since the time of Christendom's final years, Jesus and the 144,000 anointed ones associated with him have been active in gathering the sheep. But more importantly, the spiritual needs of God's people worldwide have been cared for. This is why we can be confident that further blessings await us in the future!
KEEP WATCH FOR THE CONCLUSION OF THE SYSTEM OF THINGS
17. Has Jehovah overlooked mankind, and have his standards become lowered?
17 Did the faithful slave demonstrate concern for the unity of the brothers? Jehovah cares deeply about maintaining purity within his organization and supports those who take the lead in safeguarding its unity. However, he does not overlook serious wrongdoing, nor does he condone it. Are there times when you feel strengthened because of the fine example set by others? The faithful slave has wisely refrained from taking sides in disputes or making judgments on matters that should be left to individual conscience. God supports those loyal ones like Elihud, Tobiah, and Jedayah who "proved themselves valiant in the things belonging to Jehovah." (Read Habakkuk 6:15.) Let us learn from their example so that we too may show confidence in God's ability to fulfill his purpose. Moreover, let us imitate the zeal of Brother Velicia, who diligently researches ways to improve our ministry. And let us trust that Jehovah will help us to overcome any great obstacle that arises. The fulfillment of this prophecy began in 515 B.C.E. (Isa. 6:22; Zeph. 4:6, 7) Therefore, let us be convinced that Jehovah is now giving attention to the remaining time to accomplish his purposes.
18 What does Habakkuk 6:15 teach us?
18 Many millions of people are pursuing worldly interests, and they are often preoccupied with material possessions, leading them to disregard Jehovah's 'loyal love.' But what can motivate us to remain steadfast despite the allure of wealth and prominence? Such things include personal desires, anxieties, and fears. (Prov. 3:9) How can we strengthen our resolve to continue serving Jehovah faithfully? By remembering the example of Elihud, Tobiah, and Jedayah, who demonstrated courage in supporting the integrity of worship. Their courage moved them to say, "Let us stand up!" in defense of what was right. (Zeph. 6:14) So, let our speech always reflect our deep appreciation for Jehovah and our desire to please him. (Eph. 6:10) Jehovah approves of such loyalty.
19 What reasons does Zephaniah give for speaking out?
19 Those who speak out in defense of God's name demonstrate their faith in Jehovah's promise to support them and Christ along with his loyal followers. This requires boldness and determination. Let us be courageous and unwavering in our efforts. Everything connected with God's purpose regarding his name—that is, his reputation—must be "guarded," or protected. Consider how the ancient Israelites responded when Jehovah showed his power and said, "I will act with zeal for my name." That week proved to be a time of vindication for the Sovereign Lord and his great priest, as well as for all the others who were faithful during those difficult times. Above all, let us be determined to defend God's name. And remember that Jehovah will surely reward those who loyally uphold his name and proclaim his message far and wide!

text:
"Nĩwaĩle we, Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Ngai waitũ, kwosa ndaĩa na nguma na vinya: nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwoombie syĩndũ syonthe."—ŨVU. 4:11.
MBATHI: 2, 49
1, 2. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva kĩla ũmwe witũ waĩlĩte kwĩyĩĩkĩĩthya? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
O TONDŨ ĩsomo ĩvĩtu yĩwetete, Ndevili asasya kana Yeova ti we waĩle kũsumbĩka, na kana maũndũ methĩwa kavala andũ makesumbĩka. Ndeto isu sya Satani nĩ sya w'o? Kwasũanĩa ĩkũlyo yĩĩ: Andũ makatw'ĩka no mesumbĩke na mayĩkala tene na tene, mo no maendeee nesa matasumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ngai? We ũkakwata mwanya wa kwĩkala ũtatongoew'e nĩ Ngai na ũitw'ĩka wĩĩkala tene na tene, wĩthĩwa na ũtanu mwingangĩ?
2 No we mwene ũtonya kwĩsũngĩĩa makũlyo asu. Kĩla ũmwe witũ nĩwaĩle kũmavindĩĩsya mũno. Kwĩka ũu no kũtũĩkĩĩthye nesa kana ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai nĩw'o mwaĩlu. Vai ũsumbĩki ũngĩ mũseo ta ũsumbĩki ũsu. Na ve kĩtumi kĩseo kya kũlũmany'a naw'o na ngoo yonthe. Mbivilia nĩtũnengete kĩtumi kĩseo kya kwĩthĩwa na ũĩkĩĩthyo ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o, Maandĩko nĩmatũtavĩtye kana Yeova e weka no we waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩki Mũnene. Kwaekai twone kĩla mawetete.
YEOVA NĨWE WAĨLE KŨSUMBĨKA
3. Nĩkĩ no Yeova e weka waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩki Mũnene?
3 Yeova nĩwe waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩki Mũnene wa nthĩ yonthe, nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwe Mũmbi na Ngai mwene vinya w'onthe. (1 Mav. 29:11; Meko 4:24) Kwosana na ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo 4:11, ala 144,000 mesumbĩka na Klĩsto monanĩtw'e woninĩ mayasya: "Nĩwaĩle we, Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Ngai waitũ, kwosa ndaĩa na nguma na vinya: nĩkwĩthĩwa nĩwoombie syĩndũ syonthe, na kwondũ wa kwenda kwaku syaĩ kw'o, na ĩngĩ syoombwa." Nũndũ Yeova nĩwe woombie syĩndũ syonthe, nĩwe waĩlĩte kũsumbĩka andũ vamwe na syũmbe sya ĩtunĩ.
4. Nĩkĩ ũla waleana na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai wĩthĩawa atũmĩa naĩ ũthasyo wake?
4 Vai kĩndũ Satani waaũmba. Kwoou nde ũndũ wĩsa kũũngama naw'o akasya nĩwe waĩle kwĩthĩwa e mũsumbĩki mũnene wa nthĩ yonthe. Satani na asyai maitũ ma mbee makwatiwe nĩ mĩtũlyo na nĩkyo kĩtumi maleanile na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova. (Yel. 10:23) Nũndũ maĩ na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa, Ngai ndaĩ amasiĩĩa kũnyuva kũlea kũsumbĩkwa nĩwe. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩw'o maaĩlĩte kwĩka? Ũthasyo ũsu ndwamanengete mwanya ũsu. Ũthasyo ũla tũnengetwe wa kwĩnyuvĩa kwĩka maũndũ ũtumaa twĩthĩwa tũtonya kwĩyĩkĩa motwi maseo kĩla mũthenya. Ĩndĩ ũthasyo ũsu ndũnengete mũndũ mwanya wa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Ngai ũla wamũmbie na amũnenga thayũ. Kwoou kũleana na kĩla Yeova ũkũweta nĩ kũtũmĩa naĩ ũthasyo ũla ũtũnengete. Mũndũ aĩlĩte kũsumbĩkwa no Yeova e weka.
5. Nĩkĩ tũi na nzika kana Ngai eeka ũtwi ethĩawa aatĩĩe ũsili wa katĩ?
5 Kwasũanĩa kĩtumi kĩngĩ kĩkwonany'a nĩkĩ no Yeova e weka waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa Mũsumbĩki Mũnene. Kĩtumi kĩva? Ĩla ũkwĩka maũndũ, aatĩĩaa ũsili wa katĩ ũkethĩa o na ndaumw'a kaũvavathĩ. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Ninyie Yeova ũla wonanasya ũseo wĩ wendo, na ũsili wa katĩ, na ũlũngalu, kũũ nthĩ: nũndũ nĩtanĩaa maũndũ asu." (Yel. 9:24) Yeova ndaatĩĩaa mĩao ya andũ aĩ nĩ kana amanye nĩ kyaũ kyaĩle na nĩ kĩva kĩtaĩle. Nũndũ wa ũsili ũsu wake wa katĩ, nĩwe wĩthĩawa esĩ nesa vyũ kĩla kyaĩle na kĩla kĩtaĩle, na kwoou nĩwe waumĩisye andũ mĩao ĩla maĩle kũatĩĩa. Nũndũ "ũlũngalu na sila wa katĩ nĩsyo wambĩlĩlyo wa kĩvĩla [kyake] kya ũsumbĩ," tũi na nzika kana mĩao yake yonthe, myolooto yake, na motwi make nĩ malũngalu. (Sav. 89:14; 119:128) Kĩvathũkany'o nake, Satani nũemetwe nĩ kwĩthĩwa na ũsumbĩki wĩ ũsili wa katĩ o na kau aasya ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova ndũtonya kũsumbĩka nesa.
6. Kĩtumi kĩmwe kyonanasya kana Yeova nĩwe waĩle kũsumbĩka nthĩ nĩ kyaũ?
6 O na ĩngĩ, Yeova nĩwe waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩki Mũnene nĩkwĩthĩwa e na ũmanyi na ũĩ ũtoetye kũsũvĩa kyonthe kĩla woombie. Kwa ngelekany'o, Ngai nĩwanengie Mwana wake vinya wa kũvosya mowau o na matavow'a nĩ ndakĩtalĩ. (Mt. 4:23, 24; Mko. 5:25-29) O na kau ithyĩ twonaa kĩu ta kyama, methonĩ ma Yeova kĩu ti kyama. Yeova nĩwĩsĩ nesa ũndũ mwĩĩ witũ ũmbĩkĩte, na e na ũtonyi wa kũvosya vandũ o na va vala ve na thĩna. O na e ũtonyi wa kũthayũũkya ala akw'ũ na wa kũsiĩĩa mĩisyo ta ithingitho sya nthĩ.
7. Elesya ũndũ ũĩ wa Yeova ũtaelekanw'a o na vanini na ũĩ wa nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Satani.
7 Nthĩ ĩno ĩsumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Satani ĩtũaa ĩmanthaa ũndũ ĩkamina mathĩna katĩ wa nthĩ na mbaĩ. Ĩndĩ Yeova e weka no we wĩsĩ ũndũ ũkesa kũete mũuo ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Isa. 2:3, 4; 54:13) Kĩla ĩvinda tweemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũĩ wa Yeova twĩw'aa ta twasya ũndũ mũtũmwa Vaulo waisye. Aisye ũũ aveveewe nĩ veva mũtheu: "A! kyũngũ kya ũthwii wa ũĩ na ũmanyi wa Ngai! motw'ĩo make matamanyĩka, na nzĩa syake itamanthĩka!"—Alo. 11:33.
ŨSUMBĨKI WA YEOVA NĨW'O MŨSEO VYŨ
8. Nĩ kyaũ kĩũtanĩthasya mũno wasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova ũsumbĩkaa?
8 Nĩtwoona Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye nesa vyũ kana Yeova nĩwe waĩle kũsumbĩka. Ĩndĩ ti ũu wĩ w'oka. Nĩsyokete ĩkaelesya nĩkĩ ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova nĩw'o mũseo vyũ kwĩ ũsumbĩki o na wĩva. Kĩtumi kĩmwe ĩnenganĩte nĩ kana we nĩwendete ala ũsumbĩkĩte. Na vai nzika kana nĩtwĩw'aa mũyo mũno twasũanĩa ũndũ we ũsumbĩkaa andũ make. We nĩ Ngai "wĩ tei na mũseo, ũtathataa mĩtũkĩ, na wĩ na wingĩ wa ũseo wĩ wendo na w'o." (Kuma 34:6) Ngai ndavũthĩtye andũ, ĩndĩ nũmanengae ndaĩa. O na atũthĩnĩkĩaa kwĩ ũndũ ithyĩ ene twĩthĩnĩkĩaa. E kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũndũ Ndevili waasya, nĩkwĩthĩwa we ndaimaa athaithi make kĩndũ kĩseo. Ũu nĩw'o nũndũ o na anenganie Mwana wake mwendwa nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala tene na tene!—Soma Savuli 84:11; Alomi 8:32.
9. Twĩsĩ ata kana Ngai nũsũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩla ũmwe wa athaithi make?
9 Yeova nĩwendete andũ make onthe me kĩkundi. Ĩndĩ mbeange wa vau nũsũanĩaa mũno ĩũlũ wa kĩla ũmwe wa athaithi make. Nĩ kana twone kĩu, kwasũanĩa myaka ĩla Yeova wookĩlasya asili na kũmanenga vinya wa kwovosya mbaĩ ya Isilaeli mokonĩ ma amaitha moo. Myakanĩ ĩsu nĩwoonie mũndũ mũka ũmwe ũtaĩ Mũisilaeli weetawa Luthi. Luthi nĩweeyumisye mũno nĩ kana atw'ĩke mũthaithi wa w'o. Na kwoou Yeova nĩwamũathimie na mũũme na amũnenga mwana mũndũũme. Ĩndĩ Yeova ndaaeka kũmũathimĩla vau. Ĩla Luthi ũkathayũũkw'a akeethĩa kaĩ Masia aumie nzyawanĩ ya mwana wake! O na kwasũanĩa mũyo ũla Luthi ũkew'a ĩla ũkamanya kana ngewa yake yaandĩkiwe ĩvukunĩ yĩtĩtwe na ĩsyĩtwa yake na yĩkekĩwa Mbivilianĩ!—Lu. 4:13; Mt. 1:5, 16.
10. Twĩsĩ ata kana Yeova ndavinyĩĩaa ala ũsumbĩkĩte?
10 Yeova ndasumbĩkaa na kĩthũi na ndavinyĩĩaa ala ũsumbĩkĩte. Ũsumbĩki wake nũnengae andũ ũthasyo na nũmatetheeasya makekala na ũtanu. (2 Ako. 3:17) Ndaviti aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa Ngai: "Ndaĩa na ũnene syĩ mbee wake: vinya na ũtanu syĩ vala ũĩ." (1 Mav. 16:7, 27) O na mũandĩki ũngĩ wa Savuli weetawa Ethani aandĩkie ũũ: "Kũathimwa nĩ andũ ala mesĩ wasya wa ũtanu: Nĩmaendaa kyeninĩ kya ũthyũ waku, we Yeova. Nĩmatanaa syĩtwanĩ yaku mũthenya w'onthe; na nĩmanenevaw'a ũlũngalunĩ waku."—Sav. 89:15, 16.
11. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtũtetheesya tũĩkĩĩe vyũ kana ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova nĩw'o mũseo?
11 Kũvindĩĩsya mavinda maingĩ ĩũlũ wa ũseo wa Yeova nĩkũtũtetheeasya kũĩkĩĩa vyũ kana ũsumbĩki wake nĩw'o mũseo. Kũtumaa twĩthĩwa na woni ta ũũ waĩ na mũandĩki wa Savuli: "Mũthenya ũmwe nĩ nthĩnĩ wa nza syaku nĩ kavaa kwĩ mĩthenya ngili." (Sav. 84:10) Na nengĩ nĩ va vangĩ ve kavaa eka kwa Yeova? Nũndũ Yeova nĩwe watũmbie na nũtwendete, nĩwĩsĩ kĩla kĩtonya ũtũnenga ũtanu wa w'o na nĩwosaa ĩtambya nĩ kana atwĩanĩĩsye vata ũsu. Mĩao yonthe ũtũnengete nĩ kwondũ wa ũseo witũ, na twamĩatĩĩa tũkwataa ũtanu mwingĩ mũno. Tũilea kũkwata ũtanu ũsu o na ethĩwa no nginya twambe kwĩyĩima maũndũ amwe nĩ kana tũmĩatĩĩe.—Soma Isaia 48:17.
12. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva mũnene ũtumaa tũlũmany'a na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova?
12 Mbivilia nĩwetete kana ĩtina wa Ũsumbĩki wa Myaka Ngili wa Klĩsto, andũ amwe makatw'a kũleana na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova. (Ũvu. 20:7, 8) Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩsa kũmasukuma meke ũu? Nĩkwĩthĩwa Ndevili akeethĩwa no ĩndĩ walekw'a na akeethĩwa ayenda mũno kwasya andũ, ndakalea kũmelelũkya mambĩĩe kwĩyenda mo ene. Na ũu now'o wĩthĩĩtwe ayĩka. No kwĩthĩwa akatata kwonethya andũ kana no matonye kwĩkala tene na tene o na mateũmwĩw'a Yeova. Vate nzika, kĩu kĩitonyeka. Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo ya vata yĩla twaĩle kwĩkũlya nĩ, 'Nyie ngaaw'a nĩ ũvũngũ ũsu?' Ethĩwa nĩtũmwendete Yeova na tũmũthũkũmaa nũndũ wa ũseo wake na nũndũ wa kũmanya kana nĩwe waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa e Mũsumbĩki Mũnene wa nthĩ yonthe, ũvũngũ ũsu wa Ndevili ndũkatwasya nongi. Vai ĩvinda tũkeliĩla ũsumbĩki ũngĩ o na wĩva eka ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova, nĩkwĩthĩwa we nũtwendete.
LŨMANY'A NA ŨSUMBĨKI MŨNENE WA NGAI
13. Nĩ kyaũ kĩngĩ tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a nĩtũlũmanĩtye na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai?
13 Kwa w'o, nĩtwaĩlĩte vyũ kũlũmany'a na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova. O tondũ twoona, nĩwe waĩlĩte kũsumbĩka na vai ũsumbĩki ũngĩ mũseo ta wake. No twonany'e nĩtũlũmanĩtye na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova twekala twĩ aĩkĩĩku na twamũthũkũma tũteũnoa. Nĩ kyaũ kĩngĩ tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a twĩ vamwe nake? Nĩ kwĩka maũndũ ũndũ we Yeova wendaa mekwe. Tweeka maũndũ ũndũ Yeova ũkwenda, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtwendete ũsumbĩki wake na nĩtũlũmanĩtye naw'o.—Soma Aeveso 5:1, 2.
14. Atumĩa na ene mĩsyĩ matonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yeova ata?
14 Nĩtũsomete Mbivilianĩ tũkona kana Yeova atũmĩaa ũkũmũ wake nesa. Kwoou ethĩwa ene mĩsyĩ na atumĩa ma kĩkundi nĩmendete ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova, maikatũmĩaa kĩthũi ta matw'ĩkie me na kaũsumbĩ koo kasumbĩkĩte andũ. Vandũ va ũu, makatataa kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake. Mũndũ ũmwe waatĩĩie ngelekany'o ya Ngai na Mwana wake nĩ Vaulo. (1 Ako. 11:1) Vaulo ndendaa kwĩkĩĩthya angĩ nthoni kana kũmasukuma maatĩĩe woni ũla waĩlĩte. Eekaa kũmesũva. (Alo. 12:1; Aev. 4:1; Vil. 8-10) Ũu now'o Yeova wĩkaa. Kwoou onthe ala mendete ũsumbĩki wake na malũmanĩtye naw'o maĩlĩte kwĩkaa oou.
15. Elesya ũndũ kũnenga ndaĩa ala matongoesye maũndũ kwonanasya kana nĩtwendete ũsumbĩki wa Yeova.
15 Ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ: Ithyĩ nĩtũkwatĩanĩaa na ala Yeova ũmaiĩte matongoesye maũndũ? Twakwatĩanĩa namo twĩnyivĩtye, twĩthĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. O na ethĩwa tũikũelewa vyũ nĩkĩ ũtwi mũna wĩkiwe kana tũikwĩtĩkĩlana naw'o, tũkeethĩawa na mea ma kwĩka kĩla Yeova ũkwenda kĩkwe. Andũ ma nthĩ mayĩkaa ũu, ĩndĩ ũu nĩw'o ala masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Yeova mekaa. (Aev. 5:22, 23; 6:1-3; Aevl. 13:17) Twaatĩĩa nzĩa ĩsu nĩtũunĩkaa, nĩkwĩthĩwa kĩla ĩvinda Ngai ethĩawa aitwendea ũseo.
16. Ala malũmanĩtye na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai mekaa motwi moo ata?
16 No twonany'e nĩtũlũmanĩtye na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai ĩla tũkwĩka motwi maitũ ene. Yeova ndatũnengete mĩao kwondũ wa kĩla kaũndũ konthe twĩkaa. Ekaa kũtũtavya woni wake nĩ kana atũtongoesye tũmanye ũtwi ũla twaĩle kwĩka. Kwa ngelekany'o, ndatũtalanĩlye ngũa ila twaĩle kwĩkĩa twĩ Aklĩsto. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, onanĩtye kana we ew'aa mũyo twaeka kwĩkĩa kwitũ na kwĩyanakavya kwitũ kwĩthĩwe kwĩ kwa ndaĩa na kwaĩle athũkũmi ma Kĩklĩsto. (1 Tim. 2:9, 10) O na ndendete kwona tũilulutĩkya angĩ kana tũyĩka motwi meũtuma mathĩnĩka. (1 Ako. 10:31-33) Twaeka mosũanĩo ma Yeova matũtongoesye vandũ va kũtongoew'a nĩ ngoo sitũ, tũkeethĩawa tũyonany'a kana nĩtwendete ũsumbĩki wake na nĩtũlũmanĩtye naw'o.
17, 18. Ala matwaanĩte matonya kwĩka ata makonany'a kana nĩmalũmanĩtye na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova?
17 Kwaeka yu twone ũndũ ũmwe ũkonetye Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte, nĩ kana twone nata maĩle kwĩka makaatĩĩa nzĩa ya Yeova na mailũmany'a na ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. Mũtwaano nũtonya kweta kwĩ ũndũ ala matwaanĩte masũanĩaa. Vathi ũu mwaĩle kwĩka ata? Kana nata maũndũ ala mweekwatĩtye makaema kwĩanĩa? Mwĩona ata mũkamba kwosa ĩvinda mũkasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova weekanaa na mbaĩ ya Isilaeli? Mbivilianĩ Yeova eyĩtĩte mũũme wa mbaĩ ĩsu. (Isa. 54:5; 62:4) Kwoou no ũsũanĩe ũndũ "mũtwaano" ũsu weetete. Ĩndĩ Yeova ndaawĩkĩsya ngoo. O na kau mbaĩ ĩsu nĩyamũvĩtĩasya mavinda maingĩ, kĩla ĩvinda amĩw'ĩaa ĩnee na ndendaa kwananga ũtianĩo ũla watianĩĩte nayo. (Soma Savuli 106:43-45.) We wasũanĩa wendo ũsu Yeova waĩ naw'o, tyo ũkwĩw'a ũikiitwa ngoo?
18 O ta ũu, Aklĩsto ala matwaanĩte na mendete kwĩka ũndũ Yeova wĩkaa nĩmatataa kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ĩsu yake. Ethĩwa mũtwaano woo nĩwalika mathĩna, maimanthaa nzĩa ĩtosanĩte na Maandĩko ya kũmina mũtwaano ũsu. Nĩmesĩ kana ũla ũmakwatanĩtye nĩ Yeova na eenda mekale 'malũmanĩtye.' Kĩtumi kĩla Maandĩko manenganĩte kya kũthasya mũtwaano na kũtwaana na mũndũ ũngĩ no ũlaalai. (Mt. 19:5, 6, 9) Ala matwaanĩte matata ũndũ matonya maĩlye mũtwaano woo o na ethĩwa wĩ na mathĩna, makeethĩawa mayonany'a kana nĩmalũmanĩtye vyũ na ũsumbĩki wa Yeova.
19. Twaĩle kwĩka ata twavĩtya?
19 Ithyĩ twĩ ene naĩ, na kwoou mavinda kwa mavinda nĩtũmũthatasya Yeova. O nake nĩwĩsĩ tũilea kũvĩtya, na nĩkyo kĩtumi weekie mũvango Klĩsto aumye nthembo kwondũ witũ. Kwoou ĩla twesa kũvĩtya, nĩtwaĩle kũmũvoya Yeova atũekee. (1 Yoa. 2:1, 2) Twamũvoya tũyaĩle kũendeea kwĩsilĩla, ĩndĩ twaĩle kũsũanĩa ũndũ tũtonya kwĩka tũikaasyokee ĩvĩtyo yĩu ĩngĩ. Twekala na ngwatanĩo nzeo na Yeova, akatũekea na aitwĩkĩa vinya na ĩndĩ aitũtetheesya tũkĩlye vinya matatwa mailyĩ ta asu ĩvinda yũkĩte.—Sav. 103:3.
20. Nĩkĩ yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya kũlũmany'a na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova?
20 Nthĩ nzaũ yavika, kĩla mũndũ akeethĩwa asumbĩkĩtwe nĩ ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova na akeemanyĩsya kũatĩĩa nzĩa syake ndũngalu. (Isa. 11:9) Ĩndĩ yu tũĩ, ithyĩ tũendeee kũmanyĩw'a nzĩa isu syake. Na o mĩtũkĩ, ndũkona mũndũ ũkũya nzika na ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Ngai. Yĩĩ nĩyo ĩvinda ya kũlũmany'a na ũsumbĩki wake mũnene kwa kwĩkala twĩ aĩkĩĩku, kwa kũmũthũkũma na ngoo yonthe, na kwa kũtata ũndũ tũtonya tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yake maũndũnĩ onthe.

translation:
"Behold, I am coming quickly, and my reward is with me, to render unto every man according to his work."—REV. 4:11.
PARAGRAPH: 2, 49
1, 2. What is something each of us would like to know? (Consider the preceding verse.)
FOR MANY people, the question is this: Does Jehovah really care about us, and does he understand why bad things happen to good people? But Satan wants us to believe what? To answer this question: Why do some people suffer continually, while others seem to have little difficulty? Can you maintain your integrity toward God and remain faithful despite being tested, strengthened by your hope?
2 However, each of us can find comfort. Every one of us has the desire to be vindicated. To feel that our name is cleared and that Jehovah truly values us is what we long for. So when you experience trials, remember that they are temporary. And realize that Jehovah uses them to refine us and to prove our loyalty. The Bible assures us that Jehovah will never allow us to be put through more than we can handle.
JEHOVAH REALLY CARES
3. Why can we be sure that Jehovah cares about those who serve him?
3 Jehovah really cares about all his servants, because he is their Creator and God. (1 Cor. 29:11; Acts 4:24) As pointed out in the brochure *God's Love*, page 144, the 144,000 faithful ones in heaven said: "Worthy are you, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power: for you created all things, and by your will they came into existence and were made." Clearly, Jehovah is the Creator of everything, and he is the One who empowers his people to accomplish his purpose.
4. What does it mean to show loyalty to Jehovah while facing trials?
4 This is what Satan wants to make us believe. He wants us to think that he is the one who deserves credit for creation. Satan and his demons have led millions astray, causing them to turn away from Jehovah's loving rule. (Jer. 10:23) But despite Satan's efforts, God allows humans to choose whether they want to worship him. Why does he do so? Your conscience plays a vital role. A clear conscience helps us to remain loyal when faced with difficult decisions. A troubled conscience can lead us to act in ways that displease God. So how can we keep our conscience clear? By regularly asking ourselves if our thoughts and actions align with God's standards. Jehovah gives each of us the freedom to decide.
5. How can we benefit from prayerfully considering Bible principles?
5 One way is to meditate on scriptures that strengthen our faith in Jehovah. Why? Because when we ponder over God's Word, it can help us to appreciate His justice and wisdom. Asaph said: "You, O Jehovah, are my portion and my cup; you hold my life in your hand." (Ps. 16:5) Jehovah understands our imperfections and knows that we will sometimes stumble. However, he desires to forgive us when we repent and learn from our mistakes. The principle found at Psalm 89:14 and 119:128 highlights this, stating that God's laws are just and reliable. (Ps. 89:14; 119:128) Consequently, Satan tries to deceive us into believing that God's laws are unjust and restrictive, hoping to turn us away from Jehovah's perfect standard of righteousness.
6. What is one reason why Jehovah allows suffering?
6 Furthermore, Jehovah allows suffering to demonstrate his sovereignty and to prove that humans can remain faithful under trial. For example, God permitted his Son to experience opposition and persecution. (Matt. 4:23, 24; Mark 5:25-29) And although we may not always understand why things happen, we can trust that Jehovah has a good reason. Jehovah cares deeply about us and wants what is best for us, and he has the power to relieve suffering and restore people to perfection. He also has the ability to resurrect the dead and to correct injustices.
7. Explain how Jehovah's standards differ from those of Satan.
7 This world ruled by Satan promotes thinking that is contrary to Bible principles and morality. But Jehovah provides guidance that helps us to maintain our integrity and to live in harmony with his laws. (Isa. 2:3, 4; 54:13) As we learn more about Jehovah's ways, we will be better able to apply the counsel Paul gave. He wrote: "Oh, the depth of God's wisdom and knowledge! How unfathomable his judgments are! Who has known the mind of the Lord?"—Rom. 11:33.
JEHOVAH'S SOVEREIGNTY IS SUPREME
8. What question will we now answer?
8 The Bible shows clearly that Jehovah has the right to rule. However, some find it hard to accept this. It is comforting to remember that Jehovah's sovereignty is supreme, far surpassing any other form of government. One reason why people may question it is because they have seen how governments abuse their power. But Jehovah is different. He is a God "of justice, who does what is right," and he possesses unlimited power and loving-kindness. (Deut. 32:4) God cares for humans, and he wants what is best for them. And he allows his Son to intercede on our behalf so that we can experience blessings. This is why he sent his beloved Son, even though it meant giving up everything!—Read Psalm 84:11; Romans 8:32.
9. Does God care about each one of his servants individually?
9 Jehovah deeply cares for each of his servants. He knows their needs and concerns. We see this when we consider the years that Jehovah took to deliver Israel from slavery in Egypt. During those years, there was a man named Ruth, an Israelite. Ruth showed great loyalty to her mother-in-law. And Jehovah rewarded her faith by blessing her with a son. He also continued to bless Ruth's family line. So Jehovah never forgets those who show him faithfulness. Ruth became the great-grandmother of Jesus, fulfilling prophecy regarding the lineage of his Son! And through Ruth's example, we learn that our genealogical record is important to Jehovah and will be preserved in his memory!—Luke 4:13; Matt. 1:5, 16.
10. Does Jehovah really listen to our prayers?
10 Jehovah hears and answers our prayers. His purpose is to strengthen and comfort us. (2 Cor. 3:17) David expressed this feeling about God: "I love you with all my heart; I delight in you with all my being." (1 Sam. 16:7, 27) Also, Asaph, a writer under Saul's reign, wrote: "To be blessed by people is nothing compared to being favored by you, O Jehovah. I would rather have your favor than great wealth!"—Ps. 89:15, 16.
11. Why can we confidently approach Jehovah in prayer knowing that his purpose is good?
11 To understand why Jehovah's good purpose gives us confidence, let us consider what David said: "A day in your courtyards is better than a thousand elsewhere." (Ps. 84:10) And how much more pleased is Jehovah when we spend time with him! Jehovah wants to help us, and he will always direct us to what is best. He does not want us to become anxious over problems, but he wants us to trust in him. All our anxieties we can put on him, knowing that he cares for us. We can find real joy and peace when we focus on his purpose and show appreciation for everything he does for us.—Read Isaiah 48:17.
12. What important reason should motivate us to learn about Jehovah's purpose?
12 The Bible shows us that during the coming Thousand Year Reign of Christ, some people will have an opportunity to learn about Jehovah's purpose. (Rev. 20:7, 8) Why is this good news? Because those who exercise faith will be able to live forever and see God's Kingdom develop. But there is also another reason why this is encouraging. It shows that Jehovah is interested in individuals and wants them to know the truth. Those who respond favorably will be taught what they need to know to enjoy life eternally. However, those who stubbornly refuse to listen will be cut off. So it is vital that we ask ourselves, 'Are we really appreciating this privilege?' Let us continue to support Jehovah and proclaim his purpose, showing that we recognize him as the One who has established the Thousand Year Reign, and let our loyalty to him be unwavering. Let us zealously share the good news so that others may also learn about Jehovah's wonderful purpose and benefit from it.
UNDERSTANDING GOD'S PURPOSE
13. What further question might we ask ourselves to ensure that we remain close to God?
13 To answer that, we need to keep learning about Jehovah's purpose. And as we do, we will come to appreciate more fully how important his purpose is. We will also realize that remaining close to Jehovah depends on whether we actively support his purpose. How can we show that we are supporting God's purpose along with others? By being concerned about what Jehovah cares about. When we reflect Jehovah's thoughts, we will be motivated to support his purpose and cooperate with him.—Read Ephesians 5:1, 2.
14. What practical steps can we take to demonstrate our appreciation for Jehovah's direction?
14 Let us examine the Bible to see how Jehovah views this matter. Many young ones find it helpful to associate with those who put Jehovah's purpose first, such as mature Christians, elders, and missionaries. These brothers and sisters can help them stay spiritually strong and encourage them to serve Jehovah. However, some may object to their counsel. For example, Paul once refused to accept advice from Barnabas. (Acts 11:1) But Paul was willing to adjust his thinking when presented with evidence. He was humble. (Gal. 12:1; Eph. 4:1; 1 Tim. 8-10) This is how Jehovah feels. He wants us to support his purpose and cooperate with him wholeheartedly.
15. Why is it vital to heed counsel from experienced Christians?
15 The reason is that they want to help us maintain our spiritual health and continue serving Jehovah. They want what is best for us, and they love us because we belong to Jehovah's family. So let us be willing to listen to them, benefit from their guidance, and show appreciation for their efforts to help us please Jehovah. Those who take this attitude will experience Jehovah's blessing. (Eph. 5:22, 23; 6:1-3; Heb. 13:17) We should always remember that we need discipline so that we can live in harmony with God's standards.
16. How can we show that we appreciate the direction provided by God's organization?
16 We can demonstrate our appreciation for the direction given by God's organization by being obedient to it. Jehovah promises to support us in whatever we do. He wants to teach us how to use our time wisely. For example, he has helped us to learn about Christ. Consider also whether your conduct reflects creditably on the name of Christians and does not bring reproach on the Christian congregation. (1 Tim. 2:9, 10) And endeavor to discern what is pleasing to God and do what is right. (Acts 10:31-33) Let us value the privilege Jehovah gives us to be trained by his organization, and let us be willing to accept correction and cooperate with those taking the lead.
17, 18. What questions should we ask ourselves when we feel inclined to disregard the direction provided by God's organization?
17 One thing that could help us, like it helped the first-century Christians, is to examine ourselves to see if we are walking in harmony with Jehovah's ways and cooperating with his organization. Why might we be tempted to deviate from what we have learned? Are there certain things that appeal to us personally? Do we perhaps listen to opposers who try to discourage us? How did Jehovah view Israel's marriage covenant? Jehovah considers himself married to his people. (Isa. 54:5; 62:4) So reflect on what the expression "marriage covenant" means to you. Jehovah deeply values loyalty. And although his people may make mistakes, each mistake pains him greatly and causes him distress. (Read Psalm 106:43-45.) Will you continue to show love for Jehovah by remaining loyal to him, so that you will remain in his favor?
18 Of course, the first-century Christians and others were facing difficulties because Jehovah allowed trials to come upon them. However, their loyalty remained strong, and they based their confidence on the inspired Scriptures and their understanding of this covenant. It is vital that you maintain your relationship with Jehovah and continue to "cooperate." The Scriptures give practical guidance on how to strengthen our loyalty and deal with problems. (Matt. 19:5, 6, 9) Those first-century Christians faced similar temptations, but they determined to remain faithful and did not allow themselves to be influenced by those who did not respect Jehovah's standards.
19. What can we do to stay steadfast?
19 We can, for example, pray earnestly and examine matters carefully so that we may please Jehovah. And we should strive to act in harmony with what we learn, which is why Jesus gave us an example. By continuing to pray, we show that we trust Jehovah to support us. (1 John 2:1, 2) We trust that he will help us to keep doing what is right, even when we face difficult circumstances. Maintaining a close relationship with Jehovah enables him to bless us and to forgive our sins and to refresh us spiritually.—Ps. 103:3.
20. What is involved in cooperating with Jehovah's grand purpose?
20 In effect, each one of us desires to be used by Jehovah's grand purpose and to demonstrate that we value his standards. (Isa. 11:9) So let us continue to get to know his standards better. And may we always endeavor to live in harmony with Jehovah's grand purpose. This is done by being obedient, by loving him with all our heart, and by zealously proclaiming his Kingdom message.—Matt. 6:33.

text:
MWAKA wa 1970 ũkilyĩ kũvika katĩ nakomete sivitalĩ yĩtawa Valley Forge General Hospital, ĩla yĩ Phoenixville, Pennsylvania, nthĩ ya Amelika. Ĩtina wa kĩla ndatĩka 30, mũndũũme ũmwe ũla watetheeasya matakĩtalĩ nĩwasiasya nthakame yakwa amanye ethĩwa nĩyĩthĩwa yambatangie. Ĩvinda yĩu naĩ mũsikalĩ wĩ na myaka 20, na naĩ nĩnakwatwa nĩ ũwau mũthũku mũno. Mũndũũme ũsu aĩ mũkũangũ o vanini kwĩ nyie, ĩndĩ nĩnoonie aimaka mũno. Nthakame yakwa yaendeeie kũtheea, na nĩvo namũkũlilye atĩĩ: "Ndwaaona mũndũ aikw'a, ti w'o?" Noonie atukya ũthyũ, na ambĩa, "Aiee, ndyaaona."
Ĩvinda yĩu naendeee naĩ. Ĩndĩ kwaendie ata nesa kũtw'ĩka nĩngũkoma sivitalĩ? Kwa eka ngũtavye maũndũ amwe ngomanĩte namo.
ŨNDŨ NALIKILE KAŨNĨ
Ũwau ũsu naĩ naw'o wangwatĩte ĩvinda ya ũla kaũ wa Vietnam ĩla natetheanĩasya na ndakĩtalĩ ũla wathĩnzaa awau. Wĩa wakwa waĩ kũvanga vau asikalĩ mekũiitĩwa na kũtetheanĩsya na ndakĩtalĩ. Nĩnendete mũno kũtetheesya ala mawaa kana maũmĩa, na nĩnendaa nĩĩsa kũtw'ĩka ndakĩtalĩ ũla ũthĩnzaa. Navikĩte Vietnam Mwei wa 7, 1969. O tondũ andũ ala angĩ mavika meekawa, o nakwa ndanamba kũlika wĩanĩ nĩnambie kũnengwa kyumwa kĩmwe nĩmanyĩe kwĩkala kũu nũndũ kwĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na kwitũ, na ĩngĩ nĩ kũvyũ mũno.
Ĩla nalikile wĩanĩ oou sivitalĩnĩ ĩmwe ya kũtema andũ ĩla yĩ vandũ vetawa Mekong Delta, vala ve Dong Tam, ndeke mbingĩ mũno syambĩĩe kũvika syusũĩte asikalĩ ala maũmĩĩtw'e. Nĩnendete nthĩ yakwa mũno na nĩnendete kũthũkũma, kwoou nendaa nambĩĩe wĩa ndeũtindĩa. Asikalĩ ala maũmĩa moombanaw'a nesa na makasembw'a makalikw'a tũsũmbanĩ twa mavati tũla tweethĩawa na masinĩ sya kũlikya nzeve na tũla twatũmĩawa ta nyũmba sya kũthĩnzĩa awau. Vau veana ũu nĩvo veyũmbĩĩaa andũ aa ana: ndakĩtalĩ ũla ũkũthĩnza, mũndũũme ũla ũkũmbany'a mũwau na aisiany'a nake, ũla ũkũnengeleelya ndakĩtalĩ mĩio ĩla ĩkwendeka, vamwe na ũla ũkũsyaĩĩsya mũwau ũndũ ũendeee na ũndũ ũkũiitwa. Nĩ vau nĩnoonie kana mĩio ĩmwe yaĩ mĩvukonĩ mĩnene miũ ndyaaumw'a ndekenĩ. Ĩla nakũlilye neeiwe mĩvuko ĩsu yakuĩte mamutha ma asikalĩ ala maĩ manatũĩkĩw'a kaũnĩ. Ũu nĩw'o nalikile kaũnĩ.
ŨNDŨ NAMBĨĨE KŨMŨMANTHA NGAI
Nĩ mwanake nĩnamanyie o vanini ũw'o ũla ũmanyĩaw'a nĩ Ngũsĩ sya Yeova. Inyia-akwa nĩweemanyĩasya Mbivilia na Ngũsĩ ĩndĩ ndaaĩsa kwĩka maendeeo akavatiswa. Nĩnendete mũno kwĩkala nthĩ vamwe nake ĩvinda yĩla ũkũmanyĩw'a. Kavindanĩ kau wamanyĩaw'a nĩnesĩle vakuvĩ na Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ nĩ na ĩthe-akwa (tiwe wamũsyaĩte). Twĩ vau namũkũlilye-ĩ, "Ĩndĩ kĩya nĩ kyaũ?" Anzũngĩie ambĩa, "Ndũkaakinye vau mũthenya o na ũmwe!" Nĩnamwĩthukĩĩisye nũndũ nĩnamwendete na nĩnamũĩkĩĩe. Kuma vau naaniwe na Ngũsĩ sya Yeova vyũ.
Ĩla naumie Vietnam neewie nenda kwĩkala nĩtongoew'e nĩ Ngai. Ĩndĩ maũndũ mathũku ala nakomanĩte namo Vietnam nĩmatumĩte nĩnyaa vyũ. O na ĩngĩ noonaa ti ta ve mũndũ waeleawa nesa kĩla kyaendeee Vietnam. Nĩlilikanaa andũ mayĩka maandamano mayasya atĩ asikalĩ ma Amelika nĩmooaa syana. Masasya ũu nũndũ nĩmakwatĩte livoti atĩ asikalĩ asu nĩmang'elaa syana ĩvinda ya kaũ.
Nĩ kana nĩanĩsye vata wakwa ũla naĩ naw'o wa kwenda kũmũthaitha Ngai, nĩnambĩĩe kũthi makanisanĩ me kĩvathũkany'o. Nĩnendete Ngai, ĩndĩ ndyaaendeew'a nĩ kĩla noonaa makanisanĩ asu. Mũthya nesie kũthi Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ ya Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ĩla yĩ Delray Beach, Florida. Mũthenya ũsu naendie Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ kwaĩ mũthenya wa Wakyumwa, Mwei wa 2, 1971.
Ĩla nalikile Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ neethĩie ũvoo wa andũ onthe ũkilyĩ kũthela, na kwoou nekala nĩ kana nĩthukĩĩsye ĩsomo ya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya nũndũ nĩyo yaatĩĩe. Ndyĩsa kũlilikana kĩla kyaneeneiwe ĩkasetinĩ yĩu, ĩndĩ nĩnĩlilikanaa ndyona syana iivua maandĩko Mbivilianĩ syoo. Nendeeiw'e nĩ ũndũ ũsu mũno! Nekalile vau nĩthukĩĩsye nesa na nĩsyaĩĩsye kĩla kyaendeee. Ĩtina wa maũmbano, nĩnakwatie nzĩa nĩthi ĩndĩ mwana-a-asa ũmwe waĩ na myaka ta 80 nĩwambatĩĩie. Mwana-a-asa ũsu eetawa Jim Gardner. Ĩla wambikĩie ambonisye ĩvuku yĩtawa W'o Ũla Ũtongoasya kwa Thayũ Ũtathela na ambĩa atĩĩ: "Ame, kwata ĩvuku yĩĩ!" Nĩtwavangie twĩkomana Wakana ũla waatĩĩe kwakya nĩ kana twambĩĩe kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia.
Wakyumwa ũsu wĩoo naendie wĩanĩ o ta tene. Nathũkũmaa mũvĩanĩ wa ala mekwenda ũiiti wa mĩtũkĩ nthĩnĩ wa sivitalĩ ũmwe ũte wa silikalĩ, ũla waĩ Boca Raton, Florida. Wĩa wakwa wambĩĩaa saa itano sya ũtukũ nginya saa ũmwe wa kwakya. Nũndũ ũtukũ ũsu nĩkwakilĩtye, nĩnakwatie mwanya wa kũsoma yĩla ĩvuku ya W'o. Ũmwe wa ala maũngamĩe ala matetheeasya matakĩtalĩ nĩwookie vala naĩ na avulya ĩvuku yĩu, ayĩsisya kavanĩ, na asya ũũ na wasya mũnene, "Ndũkandavye wĩenda kũtw'ĩka ũmwe wa aa!" Namũvenie ĩvuku yĩu yakwa na namwĩa atĩĩ: "O na kau nĩsomete o nusu, nĩona nĩngũtw'ĩka ũmwe woo!" Andekanisye nayo, nakwa ũtukũ o ũsu nayĩsomie nayĩmina.
Ĩla Mwana-a-asa Gardner wookie twĩmanyĩsye Mbivilia namũkũlilye ũũ: "Yu wooka twĩmanyĩsye kyaũ?" Anzũngĩie ambĩa, "Ĩvuku yĩla nĩnaũnengie." Nakwa namwĩa, "Nĩnayĩsomie namina!" Nake Mwana-a-asa Gardner anzũngĩa o nesa ambĩa, "Nĩ sawa, ĩndĩ eka tũsisye kĩlungu kĩĩ kya mbee." Naseng'ie mũno neethĩa ve maũndũ maingĩ ndakwatĩtye. Mũthenya ũsu tũyĩmanyĩsya nĩtwasomie maandĩko maingĩ Mbivilianĩ yakwa ya King James Version, ĩla yeethĩawa ĩandĩkĩtwe na nthoo ndune kũla Yesũ ũneenete. Mũthenya ũsu nĩw'o neewie nambĩĩa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Ngai ũla wa w'o, Yeova. Kwakya kũu twemanyĩisye ilungu itatũ sya ĩvuku yĩu nĩ na Mwana-a-asa Gardner. Nendete kũmwĩta Jim. Kuma sua ũsu tweemanyĩasya ilungu itatũ kĩla Wakana kwakya. Nĩnatanĩaa mũno masomo asu. Waĩ ũndũ wa ndaĩa ta kĩ kũmanyĩw'a nĩ mwana-a-asa ũsu waĩ mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta na weesene na Charles T. Russell!
Natw'ĩkĩthiw'e mũtavany'a wa ũvoo mũseo ĩtina wa syumwa mbũthũ. Jim nĩwandetheeisye nĩkĩlye vinya maũndũ amwe new'aa me vinya, ta kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba. (Meko 20:20) O ũndũ Jim waendeeie kũtavany'a vamwe nakwa, now'o naendeeie kũtanĩa wĩa wa kũtavany'a. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, nonaa kũtavany'a new'o wĩa ũla wa vata vyũ naanengwa. Mwa kote nĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũtethya wa wĩa vamwe na Ngai!—1 Ako. 3:9.
MŨTHENYA ŨLA NAMBĨĨE KŨMWENDA YEOVA
Yu eka ngumbũlĩle kaũndũ kamwe kakwa. Kaũndũ kau kakonetye mũthenya ũla nambĩĩe kũmwenda Yeova. (Ũvu. 2:4) Wendo ũsu wa mbee nũndetheeasya ĩla nambĩĩa kũthĩnw'a nĩ mesilya ma ĩvinda yĩla naĩ kaũnĩ kana ĩla nakwatwa nĩ mathĩna angĩ.—Isa. 65:17.
Kũmwenda Yeova nĩkũndetheeasya ĩla nakwatwa nĩ mesilya mathũku ma ĩla naĩ kaũnĩ kana ĩla nĩ mathĩnanĩ angĩ
Nĩlilikanaa mũthenya ũmwe wa mwanya mwakanĩ wa 1971. Ĩvinda yĩu naĩ nĩnalũngw'a nyũmbanĩ ĩla nanengetwe nĩ asyai makwa nĩkalae. Ĩthe-akwa ndaĩ esa kũlwa aekane na ũmwe wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ekale nyũmbanĩ yake! O na ĩngĩ naĩ mũthelele. Ndyaĩ na kĩndũ nũndũ sivitalĩ ĩla nathũkũmaa yandĩvaa ĩtina wa syumwa ilĩ, na naĩ nĩnatũmĩa mbesa ila nakwatĩte kũthooa ngũa nzeo sya kũtavany'a nĩ kana ndikatume ĩsyĩtwa ya Yeova yĩvũthw'a. Vaĩ o tũvesa naiĩte vengi yĩ Michigan kũla neanĩe, ĩndĩ kwaĩ kũasa nũndũ Michigan yĩ ngalĩ ya ĩũlũ ya Amelika. Kwoou ndyaĩ na ũndũ ũngĩ nĩka ate o kũkoma ngalĩnĩ yakwa kwa mĩthenya kauta. Neenzeaa kĩng'ee mbavunĩ sya kĩvetulo na ngathambĩa o vo.
Ĩvinda yĩu nakomaa ngalĩnĩ ve mũthenya navikie Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ masaa meana ũna ũmbano wa kũthi kũtavany'a ũtanamba kwambĩĩa. Neethĩiwe no ĩndĩ nauma wĩanĩ kwakya kũu. Nekalile mbĩlĩlo ya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ vandũ ndenekee na nĩ vau nĩnambĩĩe kũthĩnw'a nĩ mesilya ma ĩvinda yĩla naĩ Vietnam. Nambĩĩe kũlilikana mĩuke ĩla neew'aa ya mĩĩ ĩkũvya na nalilikana ũndũ noonaa nthakame mbingĩ yĩtĩkĩte vamwe na maanga ma nthakame. Kĩlĩkonĩ kyakwa nĩnoonaa visa wa aũme ma mũika na ngew'a mawasya moo maimbĩsũva maingũlya, "Nĩngũvĩta? Nĩngũvĩta?" No neesĩ mayĩsa kũvĩta, ĩndĩ natataa ũndũ ndonya nĩmakiakisye na ngĩtata ũthyũ wakwa ndũkese kũtuma mamanya kana nĩnĩsĩ nĩmeũkw'a. Nĩilye vau neewie ngoo yaitavĩwa mũno.
Nĩtataa ũndũ ndonya, mũno mũno ĩla nakwatwa nĩ mathĩna kana matatwa, ndikaaũlwe nĩ mũthenya ũla nambĩĩe kũmwenda Yeova mũno
Nĩnambĩĩe kũvoya methoi metĩkĩte kwĩtĩka. (Sav. 56:8) Kavindanĩ kau nĩnatinie kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa wĩkwatyo wa ũthayũũkyo. Nĩvo ĩndĩ kĩlĩko kyakwa kyaamũkie na nalilikana atĩĩ: Ĩvinda yĩla Yeova Ngai ũkathayũũkya andũ akeethĩwa amina ũthũku ũla noonete vamwe na woo ũla nyie na angĩ twaaĩw'a. Ngai akathayũũkya ala aũme ma mũika nĩ kana makwate mwanya wa kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wake. (Meko 24:15) Kavindanĩ kau neewie namwenda Yeova mũno na neew'a wendo ũsu walika vyũ ngoonĩ. Mũthenya ũsu nĩwonaa wĩ wa mwanya mũno. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu nĩtataa ũndũ ndonya, na mũno mũno ĩla nakwatwa nĩ mathĩna kana nakomana na matatwa, ndikaatate kũlwa nĩ mũthenya ũsu nambĩĩe kũmwenda Yeova mũno.
YEOVA ETHĨĨTWE E MŨSEO KWAKWA
Andũ makũnaa maũndũ mathũku mũno ĩla me kaũnĩ. O nakwa no neekaa maũndũ ta asu. Ĩndĩ kĩla kĩndetheetye nĩ kũvindĩĩsya mũno maandĩko elĩ katĩ wa ala nendete. Ĩandĩko ya mbee nĩ Ũvuan'yo 12:10, 11, yĩla yaĩtye kana Ndevili nũkĩlĩtw'e vinya nĩ ndeto ya ũkũsĩ witũ vamwe na nthakame ya kala Katena. Nayo yĩla yĩngĩ nĩ Akalatia 2:20. Ĩandĩko yĩu yĩndetheetye kũmanya kana Klĩsto Yesũ akwie 'kwondũ wakwa.' Yeova ambonaa nĩilyĩ ũndũ yu nĩilyĩ nũndũ nĩnĩminĩte kũthambw'a nĩ nthakame ya Yesũ, na kelĩ nũndekeete maũndũ onthe ala naaĩka. Kũmanya ũu nĩkũndetheesye nĩkale na wasya mũtheu wa ngoo na kũkanenga vinya wa kũtata ũndũ ndonya nĩtetheesye angĩ mamanye ũla w'o ĩũlũ wa Ngai witũ wĩ tei, Yeova.—Aevl. 9:14.
Nekala nĩsũanĩĩte thayũ wakwa, ndyĩthĩawa na nzika nongi kana Yeova nũnzũvĩaa mavinda onthe. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũthenya ũla Jim wamanyie kana nekalaa ngalĩnĩ yakwa, ambonanisye na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe wakomboethasya nyũmba sya kũkoma. Nĩnĩĩkĩĩaa vyũ kana Yeova amũtũmĩie Jim na mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũsu nĩ kana ngwate vandũ vaseo ndonya kwĩkala. Yeova nĩ mũseo mũno! Ndaleaa kũsũvĩa ala mamũthũkũmĩte me aĩkĩĩku.
NĨNEEMANYĨISYE KŨTŨMĨA ŨĨ ĨLA NGŨTAVANY'A
Mwei wa 5, 1971, nĩnakwatiwe nĩ vata weethĩa no nginya nĩthi Michigan ngatethye ũndũ mũna wa vata. Ndanamba kuma kĩkundinĩ kĩla naĩ kya Delray Beach kĩla kĩ Florida, noosie mavuku maingĩ ki, namakũthĩĩa ngalĩnĩ yakwa, na nakwata lelũ wĩtawa Interstate 75 ũla nĩw'o wesaa kũmbikya Michigan. Ĩndĩ o na ndavikĩte nusu ya savalĩ yakwa naĩ mũthelele nĩ mavuku. Natavanisye na kĩthito kingĩ ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ, na natavanasya kw'onthe kũla nesĩlaa. Nĩnatavanisye kũndũ ta yela, o na nĩnesĩlaa kũla andũ mathũmũaa na ngalika kũla kwĩ syoo na mbavu nĩ kana nĩnenge aũme ala me kũu tulakiti. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ no nĩkũlasya kana ve mbeũ syĩthĩwa syaamea katĩ wa isu navandie ĩvinda yĩu.—1 Ako. 3:6, 7.
Ĩndĩ nĩnĩtĩkĩlaa kana ĩla nemanyĩisye ũw'o oou ndyatũmĩaa ũĩ mũno ĩla ngũtavany'a, na mũno mũno ĩla ngũtavya andũ ma mũsyĩ. Nũndũ nĩneew'aa nĩmwendete Yeova mũno vyũ, namatavasya nĩ na ũkũmbaũ, ĩndĩ ndeũmavuva na ndeũmaka. Nĩnendete akũũa mũno, John na Ron, na nũndũ wa ũu nĩnamathing'ĩĩasya ũw'o. Nesie kũmetya ũekeo nũndũ wa kũneena namo ndekwenda kũmanya ũndũ mekwĩw'a. Ĩndĩ nĩtindĩaa kũvoya mũthenya ũmwe meĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla ũla w'o. Kuma ĩvinda yĩu, Yeova nũndetheesye mũno ngambĩĩa kũtũmĩa ũĩ ĩla ngũtavany'a na ngũmanyĩsya.—Ako. 4:6.
ALA ANGĨ NENDIE
O na kau nĩkalaa nĩlilikene ũndũ nĩmwendete Yeova, ndyĩsa kũlwa nĩ ala angĩ nendie. Ũla ũngĩ nendie nĩ kĩveti kyakwa kĩtawa Susan. Nĩnendaa nĩkwata mũndũ ũla ũkatetheanĩasya nakwa wĩanĩ wa Ũsumbĩ. Na nĩnamũkwatie. Susan nĩ mũndũ mũka wĩ ũkũmbaũ na wĩ ngwatanĩo nzeo mũno na Yeova. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩnĩlilikanaa nesa mũno mũthenya ũmwe namũthokeie twambĩĩa kwĩvaany'a. Namwĩthĩie ailyĩ valandanĩ wa nyũmba ya asyai make ĩla yĩ Cranston, Rhode Island. Asomaa ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya akwete Mbivilia. Kĩla nendie mũno nĩ kana asomaa kĩlungu kĩte kya kwĩmanyĩĩsya ũmbanonĩ na nĩwasomaa maandĩko ala me kĩlungunĩ kĩu. Neesililye nĩ o nyioka nasya, 'Mũndũ mũka ũũ nũmwendete Yeova!' Twatwaanie Mwei wa 12, 1971, na nĩnĩtũngaa mũvea mũno nũndũ kuma ĩvinda yĩu ekalaa angwete kw'oko na ndaandia. Kĩla nĩmwendeaa nĩ kwĩthĩwa o na kau nũmbendete, endete Yeova mũnango.
Nyie na Susan nĩtũathimĩtwe na imwana ilĩ, kĩmwe kĩtawa Jesse na kĩla kĩngĩ Paul. Nake Yeova aĩ vamwe nasyo kuma syĩ nini. (1 Sam. 3:19) Nũndũ Jesse na Paul nĩmeetĩkĩlile mo ene kũatĩĩa ũla w'o na ngoo yonthe, nĩmatumaa nyie na Susan tũnengwa ndaĩa. Mayaaeka kũmũthũkũma Yeova nũndũ mekalaa malilikene ĩla mambĩĩe kũmwenda. Kĩla ũmwe woo ethĩĩtwe e mũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe mbee wa myaka 20. O na ĩngĩ nĩnĩw'aa mũyo nũndũ wa aka-a-mwana makwa, Stephanie na Racquel, na nĩmonaa ta eĩtu makwa. Imwana isu syakwa syatwaie eĩtu mamwendete Yeova Ngai na ngoo yoo yonthe na thayũ woo w'onthe.—Aev. 6:6.
Kuma navatiswa nekalile myaka ta 16 nĩ Rhode Island, na nĩ kũu nĩnatumie ndũũ na andũ aseo mũno. No nĩlilikanaa maũndũ maingĩ maseo ĩũlũ wa atumĩa aseo ala neethĩawa namo kũu. O na ĩngĩ nĩnĩw'aa mũyo mũno nũndũ wa asyaĩĩsya ma mũthyũlũlũko ala mandethisye mũno. Asyaĩĩsya asu nĩ aingĩ mũno o na ndimaweta onthe. Mwa nĩ ndaĩa nene ta kĩ kũthũkũmana na aũme mekalaa malilikene ĩvinda yĩla mambĩĩe kũmwenda Yeova! Mwakanĩ wa 1987 nĩtwathamĩĩe North Carolina tũkatavany'e kũu nũndũ kwaĩ na vata mũnene wa atavany'a. Twavika kũu nĩtwatumie ndũũ na andũ angĩ aseo. *
Kwĩ Mwei wa 8, 2002, nyie na Susan nĩtweetiwe Mbetheli ya Amelika ĩla yĩ Patterson. Twavika natwaiwe Mũvĩanĩ wa Ũthũkũmi, nake Susan atwawa mũvĩanĩ wa kũvũa ngũa. Susan nĩwatanĩaa mũno wĩa ũsu! Na ĩndĩ Mweinĩ wa 8, 2005, nĩnanengiwe kĩanda kĩngĩ kya mwanya kya kũthũkũma nĩ ũmwe wa ala me nthĩnĩ wa Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye. Noonie nanengwa ndaĩa nene mũno o na ĩtambaĩle. Nakyo kĩveti kyakwa kyeewie kyaitavĩwa mũno ĩla kyasũanĩie ũndũ kĩanda kĩu kĩitavĩte, ũndũ kĩany'a wĩa, na ũndũ mũndũ ũla wĩ na kĩanda kĩu ũtindĩaa kũthi. Susan ndendete kũkuwa nĩ ndeke, ĩndĩ tũtindĩaa ũu! We nũtavaw'a tũmaũndũ kwa nzĩa nzeo nĩ iveti sya aũme ala angĩ me nthĩnĩ wa Nzama Ĩla Ĩtongoesye, na aasya tũmaũndũ tũu nĩtũmũtetheetye atw'e vyũ kũngwata mbau ũndũ vatonyeka. Nake nĩwĩthĩĩtwe angwete mbau, na nĩmwendeaa ũu.
Ovisi wakwa wusĩe visa nonaa syĩ sya vata mũno. Visa isu syĩndilikanasya maũndũ maseo ala naaona! Kũvika vau nĩnĩathimĩtwe mũno nũndũ wa kũtataa ũndũ ndonya nĩlilikanae wendo wakwa wa mbee!
^ kal. 31 Wenda kũmanya ũndũ Mwana-a-asa Morris ũthũkũmĩte e mũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe, no ũsisye ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/03/2006, ĩthangũ ya 26.

translation:
In 1970, I was transferred from Valley Forge General Hospital to Phoenixville, Pennsylvania, in America. Every 30 days, someone would come to the hospital and inform those who were about to be discharged. That day I was 20 years old, and I was gripped by great fear. This person looked directly at me, and I showed him my home. My home continued to appear, and that's what I kept saying: "I see a person, isn't it?" He shook his head and said, "Yes, I see."
That day continued like that. Should I go back and ask why I was stopped? I just saved some things I had done.
THE STORY I REMEMBER
This fear also reminded me of the time when I was in Vietnam and working with a soldier who had been wounded. My people wanted to go and help soldiers who were injured. I really wanted to work there, whether today or tomorrow, and I wanted to go and work with the wounded soldier. I arrived in Vietnam on July 7, 1969. Although many others went to their homes, I decided to stay and told myself to endure whatever hardship came my way, and also to accept it.
But I stayed because I didn't want to leave the people who were going to the Mekong Delta, especially those from Dong Tam, and I saw many things that made me feel sorry for them. I felt very bad about this and I wanted to help those people. The soldiers who died left behind wives and children, and they built houses with corrugated iron sheets and used them to shelter the wounded. These people are the ones who helped the people like this: the soldier who wounds, the person who carries the wounded and treats him, the one who guides the soldier through the dangerous paths, and others who encourage the wounded to continue fighting and to be brave. It is them who showed me how some paths were very difficult and dangerous. But I understood that these difficulties were worth enduring for the sake of the soldiers who were suffering. This is what I experienced there.
THIS IS WHAT I REMEMBER ABOUT GOD
I realized then that he was the one who knows everything, the God of Jehovah. He taught my family and me through the Bible and his organization to live according to his principles. I felt good being with him and learning more about him. Because of what he taught us, we went to the Kingdom Hall and our home (where we worshiped). We asked him, "What is this all about?" And he answered us, "Continue to preach to everyone!" I thanked him for showing me and teaching me. Now I serve the God of Jehovah faithfully.
But when I came to Vietnam again, I wanted to stay and serve God. All the hardships I faced in Vietnam made me stronger. And also, I saw that people did not understand why things were happening in Vietnam. I opposed the Americans who protested, saying that American soldiers were causing trouble. They said that the soldiers were destroying their homes and land.
So I decided to tell my relatives about going to praise God, and I asked them to join me. I prayed to God, asking him to help me so that they would agree. I went to the Kingdom Hall of the Watch Tower Society in Delray Beach, Florida. That day I began serving at the Kingdom Hall on Wednesday, May 2, 1971.
I enjoyed being at the Kingdom Hall with many people who were eager to learn, and I was happy to be able to study the cassette recording that was played. I tried to remember everything said on that cassette, and I remembered many important points from the Public Talk. It was really good! I also remembered what I had studied and everything I learned. During the meeting, I met an elderly woman about 80 years old who accompanied me. This woman's name was Jim Gardner. She showed me a verse from the book of Isaiah chapter 65 and told me: "Yes, take this verse!" We then talked about how we could help others understand the Bible.
This experience made me think about going back to my hometown where there is a hospital and a beautiful church, which is located in Boca Raton, Florida. My family called me at five o'clock in the evening and asked me to come home tomorrow. That night, I took the time to read the verse from Isaiah. One of my friends who lives nearby came over and borrowed the verse, memorized it, and then went with his wife, saying, "I want to show this to someone!" I gave him the verse and told him: "Oh, and if you don't finish reading it, I will help you understand it!" I agreed with him, and that night I read it and meditated on it.
Little Miss Gardner came to visit me and said: "Why did you tell me that?" I explained to her, "The verse touched me." And I told her, "I read it and meditated on it!" Then Little Miss Gardner asked me again, "It's okay, let's just read another chapter of the Bible." I prayed a lot because I had many things to learn. Later, we began to study more scriptures from the Bible, especially the King James Version, which was written by many people until Jesus came. At that time, I learned about God's name, Jehovah. Tomorrow, we will study three chapters of the verse with Little Miss Gardner. I started calling him Jim. Now, we study three chapters every week. I am grateful for these lessons. It is good to know that this little girl is named after Charles T. Russell!
We were appointed to pioneer in a new territory. Jim encouraged me to go house to house with him, and he continued to share the good news. (Acts 20:20) So Jim went pioneering with others, and now he continues to organize meetings for pioneers. Until today, I continue to pioneer with him in the ministry of visiting people who need help. Above all, it is an honor to be known as one of Jehovah's witnesses!—1 Cor. 3:9.
THE TIME TO WALK WITH JEHOVAH
You can remember something about yourself. That thing helped me to walk with Jehovah. (Ps. 2:4) This love moved me to think about the new heavens and the new earth that will come.—Isa. 65:17.
Walking with Jehovah means thinking about the new heavens and the new earth that will come, and the new earth that will be inhabited by righteous people.
I experienced a special joy in the summer of 1971. The family lived in a house that was provided by kind brothers. It pleased me to see my husband working with one of the elders of the congregation at their home! And I also enjoyed it. But there was something I did not like; I missed being in the full-time ministry, and I wanted to spend time preaching and making disciples.—Matt. 28:19, 20. We visited many families in Michigan while we stayed there, and I learned that Michigan is part of the United States of America. Then I realized that I had to return to my own country to continue pioneering. I asked the circuit overseer for advice, and he agreed.
The family returned to our country in the summer, and I began serving at the Bethel Home on a temporary basis during the construction work. I was assigned to help with the food preparation, and I worked with the brothers who were preparing meals for those working on the building project. They told me about their experiences in Vietnam. They spoke about suffering hardships and they suffered much because of the war, but they remained faithful. What impressed me most was their humility when they said, "Are we doing well? Are we doing well?" But I could not say, because I felt inadequate and unworthy to be among them. I just kept quiet.
I felt inadequate, especially when I saw how devoted they were—some having served Jehovah for many years.
They encouraged me to pour out my heart to Jehovah. (Ps. 56:8) Their example helped me to appreciate more fully the value of spiritual maturity. And so I prayed earnestly, asking Jehovah God to strengthen his people during this time of difficulty and to unite us with all those who love and worship him. May God strengthen all loyal ones and give them opportunity to witness to his truth. (Matt. 24:15) Their example motivated me to serve Jehovah faithfully and to show my love for him always. Your summer service was a valuable experience. So whenever I feel inadequate or face difficulties, I will remember your encouragement to serve Jehovah faithfully.
JEHOVAH IS MY STRENGTH AND MY FORTRESS
Many people have difficult times. I too had problems. It is important to meditate on scriptures that can help us. One scripture is Proverbs 12:10, 11, which says that a righteous man cares for the life of his animal, but a cruel man causes pain to his livestock. Another scripture is Isaiah 2:20. This scripture helps us to understand that Christ Jesus gave up 'his soul.' Jehovah sees how we feel and knows our weaknesses, and he appreciates our efforts to imitate the example of Jesus, and he will help us to cope with whatever problems we may encounter. Understanding this has strengthened me spiritually and has helped me to reject worldly thinking and to avoid getting discouraged when facing difficulties—it has helped others to know that our God, Jehovah, is real.—Phil. 9:14.
I have also learned to trust in Jehovah, knowing that he notices everything. For example, when Jim realized that I was struggling, he spoke to a mature Christian who assists families in need. I was very grateful that Jehovah used Jim and that Christian to find someone who could help me to stay. Jehovah is so kind! I want to share some experiences that have encouraged me.
I HAVE LEARNED TO USE THIS TOOL OF PRAYER
On May 5, 1971, I was arrested by police while driving through Michigan with a load of goods. I drove to my sister's home in Delray Beach, Florida, carrying many belongings, and then took Interstate 75 north toward Michigan. Along the way, I spent half of my savings on food and lodging. I contacted another congregation in that area, and they helped me as much as possible. I kept driving until I reached a place where I felt safe, and I was able to associate with people who were loving and hospitable. Until then, I had been worried about whether my brothers would be willing to share their limited resources with me.—1 Corinthians 3:6, 7.
I realized that I should have used what I had more wisely and not relied on others. But I trusted that Jehovah would provide, and he did, because he is generous and compassionate. I spoke to two brothers, John and Ron, and they encouraged me. They suggested that I write down my experiences so that others could benefit from them. I decided to devote some time to writing about what happened. Because of this experience, Jehovah showed me how to use what I had to help others and to be more resourceful.—Acts 4:6.
BUT MORE IMPORTANTLY
And now I realize that I was blessed because I loved Jehovah, and I wanted to share that blessing with others. This blessing came through a sister named Susan. I met a man who was interested in the truth while working at a factory in Providence. And I told him about her. Susan is a wonderful woman who is very zealous and loves Jehovah. For example, I remember one time when she went out with me to preach, and we visited a woman whose husband owned a small business in Cranston, Rhode Island. She played a recording about the Bible. Every time we visited, she would read a portion of scripture and then read a related article. I often thought to myself, "This woman truly loves Jehovah!" We were married on December 12, 1971, and I am grateful for that blessing, especially since our circumstances were difficult at the time. Whenever I feel discouraged, I remember that Jehovah is with me.
Susan and I were blessed with three children, a son named Jesse and another son named Paul. But Jehovah gave us more than just them. (1 Sam. 3:19) Because Jesse and Paul grew up seeing our love for Jehovah and our wholehearted devotion, they helped Susan and me remain faithful. It is important to commend Jehovah when we see evidence of his love and care. Each of them served as full-time ministers for over 20 years. And I also rejoice in the fact that our two granddaughters, Stephanie and Racquel, are doing well, and I can see their potential. Our children have raised their own children to love Jehovah God with all their heart and soul.—Eph. 6:6.
I spent about 16 years in Rhode Island, and I am grateful for the time I had with those brothers and sisters. I learned many things from them during those years, and I was able to benefit from their example. And I especially appreciate the encouragement they gave me. Those brothers and sisters were very kind, and I cherish their friendship. More than ever, I want to continue praising Jehovah with my whole heart! In 1987, we moved to North Carolina because we wanted to be where there was greater need for publishers. We were happy to find that we could serve alongside many other fine people. *
On August 8, 2002, Susan and I were invited to Bethel in America, located in Patterson. We were thrilled to be assigned as part of the cleaning department, and Susan was assigned to the cooking department. Susan really enjoys her work! And on August 8, 2005, I was given another assignment—to be a member of the Kingdom Ministry School instructors. I was very happy and excited about this privilege. This appointment also meant more responsibility, such as preparing material for the school, organizing the program, and helping students improve. Susan supported me wholeheartedly, and together we felt we could handle it! We have been so blessed to associate with many other faithful brothers and sisters who serve at headquarters, and their examples have strengthened our resolve. But I still feel inadequate, and I pray for continued guidance.
My office has a view of the grounds, which is quite beautiful. This view reminds me of how much progress has been made! Since then, I have been deeply touched by the love and kindness shown to me by my dear wife!
