text:
"Yĩla mwoosie . . . ĩla ndeto ya ũtũmane wa Ngai, mũtyaamyosa ta ndeto ya andũ, ĩndĩ o ũndũ ĩtilyĩ w'o, ndeto ya Ngai."—1 ATH. 2:13.
MBATHI: 37, 11
1-3. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kyaendeeie katĩ wa Euotia na Sinitike? Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana thĩna ta ũsu ndũkaumĩle? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
ATHŨKŨMI ma Yeova nĩmanengete yĩla Ĩvuku yake ĩtheu ndaĩa nene mũno. Na nĩkwĩthĩwa twĩ ene naĩ nĩtwĩkalaa tũinengwa ũtao wa Maandĩko. Twĩkaa ata twatawa? Kwaekai twambe kwona ngewa ya Euotia na Sinitike, ala maĩ Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa. Ve thĩna mũnene waumĩlile katĩ wa aka asu. Thĩna wĩva? Mbivilia ndĩtũtavĩtye. Ĩndĩ kwaekai twĩke kũsũanĩa kĩla kĩtonya kwĩthĩwa kyeekĩkie.
2 Eka twasye Euotia nũtonya kwĩthĩwa athokisye ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa kwake maĩsanĩe na maitana kwĩthwa vamwe. Sinitike ti ũmwe waĩ mũthokye ĩndĩ nĩwesie kwĩw'a andũ maiea ngewa sya ũndũ matanĩie kwĩthwa na Euotia. No kwĩthĩwa Sinitike asũanĩie ũũ kĩlĩkonĩ eew'a ngewa isu: 'O na ndikũĩkĩĩa Euotia ndaneenthokya! Nasyaa twĩ ndũũ ĩtathela.' Kyu nĩkyaũmĩisye Sinitike mũno na ambĩĩa kwona Euotia ta ũtamwendete na ta wambĩĩe kũmũvatha. Nũndũ wa ũu, Sinitike nĩwavangĩthisye kyathĩ kyake na athokya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa o ala mathoketw'e nĩ Euotia, ĩndĩ ndaamũthokya ũ Euotia! Thĩna ũla waĩ katĩ wa Euotia na Sinitike waĩ ũtonya kwananga vyũ mũuo ũla waĩ kĩkundinĩ. O na kaũ Mbivilia ndĩtũtavĩtye thĩna ũsu watumie kũthi ata, eĩtu-a-asa asu elĩ nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa meetĩkĩlile ũtao ũla mũtũmwa Vaulo wamanengie.—Avi. 4:2, 3.
3 Ikundinĩ sya andũ ma Yeova ũmũnthĩ no kwĩsaa kumĩla thĩna ta ũsu. Ĩndĩ twaatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai, Mbivilia, nĩtũtonya kũema kwĩsa kũvika vau, kana ethĩwa ve thĩna waumĩla no tũũmine. Na ethĩwa nĩtũnengae yĩla Ĩvuku ya Yeova ndaĩa nene, tũkeekaa ũndũ yĩũtũtavya.—Sav. 27:11.
ŨNDŨ ĨVUKU YA NGAI YĨTŨTETHEEASYA TŨSUMBĨKE NGOO SITŨ
4, 5. Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtũnengete ũtao wĩva ĩũlũ wa kũsumbĩka ngoo sitũ?
4 Ti laisi kũsumbĩka ngoo sitũ ĩla twavĩtĩw'a kana twakuwa ũndũ vataĩle. Na maũndũ methĩawa me metangu ethĩwa twĩkuwa naĩ nũndũ wa mbaĩ yitũ, kana nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa twĩ ma langi wĩ kĩvathũkany'o, kana twĩ na wũmbo wĩ kĩvathũkany'o na wa ala angĩ. Na ĩndĩ maũndũ metaa ĩ ya mũno ethĩwa ũla watũkua naĩ nĩ Mũklĩsto ũngĩ! Kwoou vo ve ũtao wĩ Ndetonĩ ya Ngai ũtonya kũtũtethya twesa kwĩkwa ũu?
5 Kuma ĩla Yeova woombie andũ kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ nũsyaasya ũndũ mekalanasya. Nĩwĩthĩawa ene kĩla kĩendeee ngoonĩ sitũ vamwe na meko maitũ. Ĩla twĩw'ĩte woo kana twathata nĩtũtonya kwĩka maũndũ kana tũkaweta ndeto na ĩtina tũyambĩĩa kwĩlila. Na kwoou wĩthĩwa wĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ tũkaatĩĩa ũtao ũla wĩ Mbivilianĩ. Ĩtwĩĩte nĩtũvete ũthilĩku ngoonĩ na tũitata tũikathatae mĩtũkĩ. (Soma Nthimo 16:32; Mũtavan'ya 7:9.) Vai nzika kana kĩla ũmwe witũ e kĩthito kĩla waĩlĩte kwĩkĩa nĩ kana ndakathatae mĩtũkĩ ĩndĩ ethĩawe na mĩtũkĩ ya kũekea. Methonĩ ma Yeova na Yesũ kũekea angĩ mavĩtyo moo ti ũndũ mũnini. (Mt. 6:14, 15) We weesisya nũkwona wĩ na vata wa kwĩkĩa kĩthito kingangĩ kya kũsumbĩka ngoo yaku na kũekea ala angĩ?
6. Nĩkĩ twaĩle kwĩsũvĩa mũno tũikaie ũthatu ngoonĩ?
6 Mũndũ aemwa nĩ kũsumbĩka ngoo yake nũtonya kwĩkala athatĩe ũngĩ, kana o na akambĩĩa kũmũmena. Mũndũ ekala ũu angĩ no maemwe nĩ kũtindany'a nake. O na no atume angĩ kĩkundinĩ methĩwa na kĩmena ta kyu. Mũndũ ta ũsu nũtonya kũtata kũvithany'a ũthatu wake kana kĩmena kĩla wĩ nakyo, ĩndĩ ĩtina ũthũku ũsu wĩ ngoonĩ yake "ũkoonanw'a ũtheinĩ mbee wa ũmbano." (Nth. 26:24-26) Atumĩa no matetheesye andũ ta asu mamanye kana Ngai ndendaa kwona ũseũvyo wake wĩ na andũ maiĩte ũthatu ngoonĩ, me na kĩmena, kana ũthũ. Yĩla Ĩvuku ya Yeova yĩwetete ũndũ ũsu nesa vyũ. (Ali. 19:17, 18; Alo. 3:11-18) We nũatĩĩaa kĩu yĩwetete?
LILIKANAA ŨNDŨ YEOVA ŨTŨTONGOEASYA
7, 8. (a) Yeova atongoeasya ata kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wake kya kũũ nthĩ? (b) Nĩ maũndũ ta meva Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtwĩaĩe, na nĩkĩ twaĩle kũmaatĩĩa?
7 Nĩ kana Yeova anenge ala me kĩlungunĩ kya ũseũvyo wake kya kũũ nthĩ lĩu wa kĩ-veva, atũmĩaa "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito na mbũĩ" ĩla yĩthĩawa ĩtongoew'e nĩ Klĩsto, nake nĩwe "mũtwe wa ĩkanisa." (Mt. 24:45-47; Aev. 5:23) Ngombo ĩsu nĩatĩĩaa ndeto ya Ngai mbeveee na nĩmĩnengete ndaĩa nene o tondũ nzama ĩla ĩtongoesye ya ĩvinda ya atũmwa yeekaa. (Soma 1 Athesalonika 2:13.) Kwoou nĩ myolooto ta yĩva yĩ Mbivilianĩ ĩtonya kũtũtethya?
8 Mbee, Mbivilia nĩtũnengete mwĩao wa kũmbana na angĩ tũte kũtĩĩa. (Aevl. 10:24, 25) Nĩsyokete ĩkatwĩa nĩtũtate twĩthĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ũmwe. (1 Ako. 1:10) O na ĩngĩ, Ndeto ya Ngai ĩtwĩaa kana twaĩle kwamba kũmantha Ũsumbĩ. (Mt. 6:33) O na Maandĩko nĩmonanĩtye ĩngĩ na ĩngĩ kana nĩtwaĩle kũtavany'a nyũmba na nyũmba, kũla kwĩ andũ aingĩ, na ĩla twĩ maũndũnĩ maitũ. (Mt. 28:19, 20; Meko 5:42; 17:17; 20:20) Na eka ũu, Ĩvuku yĩu ya Ngai yĩaĩe atumĩa Aklĩsto yĩkamea nĩmekalye ikundi syĩ ntheu. (1 Ako. 5:1-5, 13; 1 Tim. 5:19-21) Na ĩndĩ Yeova ndendaa athũkũmi make mekale na kĩko kana methĩwe na mesilya na mwĩkalĩle ũla ũmenete.—2 Ako. 7:1.
9. Nũũ ũla ũnyuvĩtwe atũtetheesye kũelewa Ndeto ya Ngai?
9 Andũ amwe monaa no mamĩelewe Mbivilia o na mate atetheesye. Ĩndĩ vai ũngĩ Yesũ ũnyuvĩte anenge aatĩĩi make lĩu wa kĩ-veva eka ĩla "ngombo yĩ na kĩthito." Kuma mwaka wa 1919, Yesũ Klĩsto ethĩĩtwe aitũmĩa ngombo ĩsu kũtetheesya aatĩĩi make maelewe nesa yĩla Ĩvuku ya Ngai na maiatĩĩa motao mayo. Kũatĩĩa kĩla Mbivilia ĩtũtavĩtye kũtumaa ikundi syĩkala syĩ ntheu, syĩ na mũuo, na syĩ na ngwatanĩo. Kwoou nũseo kĩla ũmwe witũ akekũlya atĩĩ: 'Nyie nĩnĩthĩawa nĩlũmanĩtye na Yesũ kwa kũatĩĩa myolooto ĩla yanenganwe nĩ ĩla ngombo yĩ na kĩthito?'
ĨKASYA YA YEOVA YĨSEMBETE MŨNO!
10. Ĩvuku ya Esekieli yĩeleetye kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Yeova kya ĩtunĩ ata?
10 Ndeto ya Yeova nĩtũtavĩtye kĩla kĩthĩawa kĩendeee kĩlungunĩ kya ũseũvyo wake kya ĩtunĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, mwathani Esekieli nĩwooniw'e woninĩ kĩlungu kĩu kya ũseũvyo wa Ngai kya ĩtunĩ. Woninĩ ũsu kĩlungu kĩu kyaelekanilw'e na ĩkasya yĩ ĩtunĩ. (Esek. 1:4-28) Yeova nĩwe ũtwaĩte ĩkasya yĩu, na yĩendaa kĩla vandũ veva wake wayĩsukuma yĩthi. Ĩla kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Ngai kya ĩtunĩ kĩla kĩelekanĩtw'e na ĩkasya kyasonga, o nakyo kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Ngai kya kũũ nthĩ nĩkĩsongaa. Na vate nzika, ĩkasya yĩu nĩyĩsembete mũno! Kwamba kũsũanĩa moalyũku ala meethĩĩtwe ũseũvyonĩ kwa ĩvinda ya myaka ĩkũmi mĩvĩtu, na ndũkatate kũlwa kana Yeova nĩwe ũtumĩte mekwa. Na nĩkwĩthĩwa yu Klĩsto na alaĩka makilyĩ manaananga nthĩ ĩno nthũku, ĩkasya ya Yeova yĩsembete vyũ nĩ kana yĩtume ũsumbĩki mũnene wa Yeova ũtetewa na yĩituma ĩsyĩtwa yake yĩthew'a!
11, 12. Nĩ maũndũ ta meva ũseũvyo wa Yeova wĩthĩĩtwe ũyĩka?
11 Kwaekai twone maũndũ ala kĩlungu kya ũseũvyo wa Ngai kya kũũ nthĩ kĩthĩĩtwe kĩyĩka mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo. Myako. Ve ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa maana maingĩ ala methĩĩtwe mayaka ũla ovisi mũnene wa Ngũsĩ sya Yeova ũkwakwa Warwick, New York, Amelika. Eka asu ve angĩ ngili mbingĩ nthĩ yonthe methĩĩtwe maitetheesya maũndũnĩ makonetye myako ya Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ na movisi ma ũvonge, na mathũkũmanaa na mũvĩa wĩtawa Idara ya Ulimwenguni Pote ya Usanifu-Majengo na Ujenzi. Tũtanaa mũno ta kĩ nũndũ wa ana-a-asa na eĩtũ-a-asa ta asu meyumĩtye meanĩsye wĩa ũsu mate kũnoa! O na ndũkolwe kana atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ nthĩ yonthe nĩmaumasya mĩvothi kwosana na ũtonyi woo nĩ kana matetheesye wĩa ũsu. Nake Yeova nũmaathimaa mũno nũndũ nĩmalũmanĩtye nake na mekaa ũu menyivĩtye.—Luka 21:1-4.
12 Kũmanyĩw'a. Kwasũanĩa sukulu ila ivangĩtwe nĩ kana itũmanyĩsye kwenda kwa Ngai. (Isa. 2:2, 3) Nĩtũvangĩwe Sukulu ya Mavainia, Sukulu ya Atavany'a ma Ũsumbĩ, Sukulu ya Ngileati, Sukulu ya Athũkũmi Eũ ma Mbetheli, Sukulu ya Asyaĩĩsya ma Mũthyũlũlũko na Iveti Syoo, Sukulu ya Atumĩa ma Kĩkundi, Sukulu ya Ũthũkũmi wa Ũsumbĩ, na Sukulu ya Ala me Kamitiinĩ ya Ovisi wa Ũvonge na Iveti Syoo. Kĩu kĩtwony'a nesa vyũ kana Yeova nĩwendete kũmanyĩsya andũ make! O na kĩsesenĩ kitũ kya jw.org, no ũkwate mavuku ma ithyomo mbingĩ syĩ kĩvathũkany'o ma kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia. Kĩsese kyu kĩ na ilungu iseũvĩtw'e kwondũ wa syana, ala me na mĩsyĩ, vamwe na kĩlungu kya maũvoo ma maũndũ ala maumĩla. We nũtũmĩaa kĩsese kĩu ũtavany'anĩ na ũthaithinĩ wenyu wa mũsyĩ?
LŨMANY'A NA YEOVA NA ŨIKWATA MBAU ŨSEŨVYO WAKE
13. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva athaithi ala aĩkĩĩku ma Yeova maĩlĩte kwĩka?
13 Nĩ ndaĩa nene vyũ kwona twĩ ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova, kana ti w'o? Na kwoou nũndũ nĩtwĩsĩ mĩao ya Ngai na myolooto yake, nĩtwaĩlĩte kwĩka ũla waĩle na tũilũmany'a na ũsumbĩki wake mũnene. Nĩkwĩthĩwa andũ ma nthĩ ĩno maendeee kũlolomelya ũthũkunĩ, no nginya 'tũmene ũthũku' o tondũ Yeova ũũmenete. (Sav. 97:10) Tũyĩsa kwĩtĩkĩla kwĩkwatany'a na andũ matamwĩsĩ Ngai na tũyĩsa kwasya "ũthũku [nĩ] ũseo, na ũseo [nĩ] ũthũku." (Isa. 5:20) Nũndũ wendi witũ nĩ kũmwendeesya Ngai, twĩkĩaa kĩthito kingĩ mũno twĩkalye mĩĩ yitũ na mĩkalĩle yitũ yĩ mĩtheu, na twĩvathane na ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ. (1 Ako. 6:9-11) Nĩtũmwendete Yeova na nĩtũmwĩkwatĩtye. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩtumi tũtw'ĩte kũlũmany'a nake kwa kũatĩĩa ĩla myolooto ĩwetetwe nesa Ĩvukunĩ yake. Na tũtataa ũndũ tũtonya tũmĩatĩĩe kĩla vandũ, twĩthwe twĩ mũsyĩ, kĩkundinĩ, wĩanĩ, kana twĩ sukulu. (Nth. 15:3) Ĩndĩ kwaekai twone maũndũ angĩ tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Ngai.
14. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva asyai Aklĩsto matonya kwĩka makonany'a nĩmalũmanĩtye na Ngai?
14 Kũea. Ũndũ ũmwe asyai Aklĩsto matonya kwĩka makonany'a nĩmalũmanĩtye na Yeova nĩ kũea syana syoo kwosana na Ndeto yake. Ĩla asyai mendete Ngai mekũea syana syoo, maiatĩĩaa ũndũ vataĩle syĩthĩo sya kũla mekalaa. Na kĩtumi nũndũ veva wa nthĩ ĩno ndwaĩlĩte kwĩsa kwĩtĩkĩlw'a ũlike mũsyĩnĩ wa Ngũsĩ. (Aev. 2:2) Ta kwa ngelekany'o, yĩĩ nĩ yĩsilya yĩtaĩle kwĩsa kũlika kĩlĩkonĩ kya mwana-a-asa, 'Kũũ kwitũ aka nĩmo mamanyĩasya syana.' Mbivilia nĩwetete nesa ĩkasya: "Inyw'ĩ aaĩthe, . . . ieei [syana syenyu] na mosilĩlo na motao ma Mwĩaĩi." (Aev. 6:4) Iveti na aũme ala me kĩkĩo kya Ngai nĩmendaa mũno syana syoo itutye Samueli, nũndũ Yeova aĩ vamwe nake akĩana.—1 Sam. 3:19.
15. Ethĩwa twĩ na ũtwi mũnene tũkwenda kwĩka, tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Yeova?
15 Kwĩka motwi. Nzĩa ĩmwe tũtonya kwonany'a nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Ngai ĩla tũkwĩka motwi manene nĩ kũmantha ũtao Ndetonĩ yake na ũseũvyonĩ wake. Nĩ kana ũmanye vata wa kwĩka ũu, kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩno ya kaũndũ katonya kũkiita andũ aingĩ. Kaũndũ kau kakonetye asyai. Ĩla asyai amwe mathamĩĩa kũngĩ na makwata mwana me kũu, nĩmethĩawa na kĩthĩo kya kwĩnũkya mwana ũsu akasũvĩwe nĩ andũ angĩ ma mũsyĩ nĩ kana mo makwate mwanya wa kũendeea kũthũkũma na kũseũvya mbesa me ku maĩ. Tũikũlea kana ũsu nĩ ũtwi mũndũ ũtekĩwa nĩ ũngĩ, ĩndĩ nũseo tũkalilikana kana tũkaumya ũtalo kwa Ngai nũndũ wa motwi onthe ala twĩkĩte. (Soma Alomi 14:12.) Kwoou, we nũkwona ta ũndũ wa ũĩ kwĩka ũtwi mũnene ũkonetye mũsyĩ waku kana wĩa waku ũtambĩte kũsisya woni wa Mbivilia? Aiee, ti ũndũ wa ũĩ! Ithyĩ ene tũitonya kũtongoesya matambya maitũ, na kwoou twĩ na vata wa kũtongoew'a nĩ Asa witũ wa ĩtunĩ.—Yel. 10:23.
16. Ĩla mũndũ mũka ũmwe wakwatie mwana aaĩlĩte kwĩka ũtwi wĩva, na nĩ kyaũ kyamũtetheeisye kwĩka ũtwi mũseo?
16 Ve mũndũ mũka ũmwe wasyaie kavĩsĩ e nthĩ ya nza na atw'a nũkũkenũkya vala ve asyai ma mũũme makakaee. Ĩndĩ akasyaa oou, nĩwambĩĩe kũmanyĩw'a Mbivilia nĩ Ngũsĩ. Nĩweekie maendeeo na amanya kana Ngai amũnengete we mwene, na ti mũndũ ũngĩ, wĩa wa kũea mwana wake atw'ĩke mũthaithi wa Yeova. (Sav. 127:3; Nth. 22:6) Mũndũ mũka ũsu nĩwoosie ĩvinda amũtulũĩla Yeova ngoo yake, o tondũ Maandĩko matwĩkĩĩte vinya twĩke. (Sav. 62:7, 8) Nĩwatavisye ũla wamũmanyĩasya Mbivilia thĩna ũla wamũthokoaa ateũmũvitha kĩndũ, o na nĩwaneenie na angĩ kĩkundinĩ. Andũ ala angĩ ma mũsyĩ na anyanyae nĩmamwingĩĩisye mũno enũkye mwana, ĩndĩ we nĩweetw'ĩĩe ngoonĩ kana ũu ndwaĩle. Mũũme nĩwatanie mũno kwona ũndũ kĩkundi kyatetheeisye mũka na mwana woo nginya atw'a kwĩmanyĩsya Mbivilia na kũendany'a namo maũmbanonĩ. We mũndũ mũka ũsu no asye Yeova nĩwasũngĩie mboya ĩla wamũvoyie kuma ngoonĩ? Vai nzika kana no asũngĩe akasya, "Ĩĩ."
17. Nĩ maũndũ meva twĩthĩĩtwe tũyĩwa nĩtwĩke ĩla tũũmanyĩsya amanyĩw'a maitũ ma Mbivilia?
17 Kwĩka ũndũ twatavw'a. Ũndũ ũmwe wa vata vyũ tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a nĩtũlũmanĩtye na Ngai nĩ kwĩka kĩla twatavw'a nĩ ũseũvyo wake. Kwasũanĩa maũndũ ala twĩthĩĩtwe tũyĩwa nĩtwĩke ĩla tũũmanyĩsya amanyĩw'a maitũ ma Mbivilia. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩtũtavĩtw'e kana twambĩĩa kũmanyĩsya mũndũ ĩvuku Mbivilia Yo Ĩmanyĩasya Ata?, nũseo kĩla ĩvinda twamina kũsoma tũlungu tũla tũũsoma tũkosa ndatĩka nini nĩ kana tũtetheesye mũmanyĩw'a ũsu aelewe ũseũvyo wa Yeova nesanga. No tũtũmĩe vitio ĩĩ, Nĩ Kyaũ Kĩendeeaa Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ?, na mbulosua Naaũ Mekaa Kwenda kwa Yeova Ũmũnthĩ? Na ĩndĩ twamina kũsoma ĩvuku Mbivilia Ĩmanyĩasya na mũmanyĩw'a wĩkĩte maendeeo, twĩĩtwe kana twaĩle kũsoma nake ĩvuku "Ĩyĩkalyei Ene Wendonĩ wa Ngai" o na ethĩwa kũvika vau nĩ mũvatise. Kĩtumi kya ũseũvyo kũnengane mwolooto ũsu nĩ kana wĩenda ala meũmanyĩw'a 'malũlũmĩlw'e mũĩkĩĩonĩ woo.' (Ako. 2:7) We nĩwĩkaa maũndũ asu tũtavĩtw'e nĩ ũseũvyo wa Yeova?
18, 19. Nĩ maũndũ ta meva maĩle kũtuma tũmũtũngĩa Yeova mũvea?
18 Nĩ maũndũ maingĩ Yeova ũtwĩkĩte ala maĩle kũtuma tũmũtũngĩa mũvea! Mbee, nĩwe ũtũnengete thayũ ũũ twĩ naw'o, na kethĩwa ti vake tũyĩthĩwa vo, o na tũyĩthĩwa tũithi. (Meko 17:27, 28) Nũtũnengete mũthĩnzĩo wa vata vyũ, naw'o nĩ yĩla ĩvuku yake, Mbivilia. O tondũ ala Aklĩsto ma Thesalonika moosie ndeto ya Ngai na mamĩtĩkĩla, o naitũ nĩtũtanaa kwĩtĩkĩla Mbivilia ta ũtũmane Ngai ũtũandĩkĩe.—1 Ath. 2:13.
19 Kwa ũtethyo wa Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia, nĩtũkwatĩte mwanya wa kũmũthengeea Yeova, nake nĩwosete ĩtambya ya kũtũthengeea. (Yak. 4:8) Nĩ ndaĩa nene mũno kwona Asa witũ atwĩtĩkĩlĩtye twĩthĩwe ũseũvyonĩ wake. Asu nĩ moathimo matumaa tũtana ta kĩ! Ũtanu ta ũsu nĩw'o mũandĩki ũmwe wa Savuli waĩ naw'o ĩla wainie Savuli ĩno: "Mũtũngĩei Yeova mũvea; nũndũ nĩ mũseo; nũndũ ũseo wake wĩ wendo nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene." (Sav. 136:1) Kĩsyokeo kĩĩ, "ũseo wake wĩ wendo nĩwĩkalaa tene na tene," kyonekaa mavinda 26 nthĩnĩ wa Savuli ĩsu ya 136. Twekala tũlũmanĩtye na Yeova na ũseũvyo wake, ndeto isu iseũvĩte ũu ikeanĩa ngalĩkonĩ ĩ yitũ nĩkwĩthĩwa tũkekala tene na tene!

translation:
"Be joyful, my brothers and sisters… rejoice in the hope of God's Kingdom, which is also a hope for mankind, because the hope of God is near." – 1 THESS. 2:13.
PARAGRAPH: 37, 11
1-3. Why is it important to be united as Christians? Why should we care about maintaining our unity? (Consider the example mentioned.)
THE servants of Jehovah want to imitate his love fully. And we can show that we are doing so by living according to the principles found in the Bible. But how can we do this? Let us examine the example of Euphemia and Synetiche, and see what lessons we can learn from their experience. They had a serious disagreement, but they were willing to humble themselves. What helped them? We will discuss this further and see why it is vital for us to resolve disagreements quickly.
2 As we saw earlier, Euphemia was upset because Synetiche did not appreciate her contributions and those of her family. Synetiche, however, felt that she was being unfairly treated by Euphemia. She expressed her feelings to others, saying: "I am determined to side with Euphemia!" Then she and her family stopped associating with Euphemia altogether. Because of this, Synetiche began to feel regretful and asked Euphemia to forgive her. Eventually, Synetiche humbled herself and apologized to Euphemia and her family, and Euphemia forgave her. Thus, Euphemia and Synetiche restored their friendship. This shows us that when there is disunity among Christians, it can cause great pain. However, if we are humble and willing to forgive, we can maintain peace, just as the apostle Paul encouraged us to do.—Phil. 4:2, 3.
3 The love among Jehovah's people motivates them to be united. By studying God's Word, the Bible, we learn how to resolve differences and maintain unity, even when faced with difficult situations. And as we meditate on Psalm 27:11, we will be more determined to remain loyal to Jehovah's organization.—Ps. 27:11.
WHY BIBLE PRINCIPLES HELP US TO REMAIN UNITED
4, 5. How does God's Word help us to remain united?
4 It is easy to become discouraged or resentful when we feel wronged. We may also struggle with pride, envy, or jealousy. Or we may be offended by something someone says or does. But remember that even fellow Christians are imperfect! So how can we apply Bible principles to maintain our unity?
5 Jehovah expects us to forgive others readily and to seek reconciliation. He wants us to be considerate of others and to work at maintaining good relationships. When we are humble and willing to admit our mistakes, it is easier to apologize and make amends. And how grateful we can be for the guidance found in the Bible! (Read Proverbs 16:32; Titus 7:9.) Remember that each of us has weaknesses and makes mistakes. Jehovah and Jesus are very forgiving. (Matt. 6:14, 15) Will you strive to show the same spirit of forgiveness toward others?
6. What can we do to strengthen our loyalty?
6 A loyal person is determined to remain faithful despite difficulties, or even when tempted to give up. Such a person is often tested. But he uses his influence for good and does not misuse authority. A disloyal person may find it hard to resist temptation or to maintain integrity, especially when faced with pressure from others to compromise his standards. (Prov. 26:24-26) He might also try to justify wrong conduct or excuse himself, saying that God does not notice his lack of loyalty or his wrongdoing. However, Jehovah's organization helps us to stay strong. (Ps. 19:17, 18; Amos 3:11-18) How does it do so?
RESPECT GOD'S ORGANIZATION
7, 8. (a) In what ways does Jehovah support his organization? (b) What benefits come from valuing God's direction, and how can we show that we appreciate it?
7 Even though Jehovah could directly intervene in matters affecting his people, he chooses to use "a faithful and discreet slave" to provide spiritual food, and this slave is Christ, who is the "head of the congregation." (Matt. 24:45-47; Rev. 5:23) This slave provides guidance based on God's Word and applies it practically, often through publications and meetings of the Watch Tower Society. (Read 1 Thessalonians 2:13.) So why is it important to benefit from the information provided by the Governing Body?
8 Indeed, the Bible encourages us to associate with one another to encourage one another. (Heb. 10:24, 25) We need to be united in our beliefs. (1 Cor. 1:10) Also, God's Word teaches us to put the Kingdom first. (Matt. 6:33) And the Scriptures show us more and more how to preach from house to house, to many people, and to care for our brothers. (Matt. 28:19, 20; Mark 5:42; 17:17; 20:20) Furthermore, God's spirit empowers anointed Christians to accomplish much. (1 Cor. 5:1-5, 13; 1 Tim. 5:19-21) And Jehovah wants his elders to shepherd and strengthen his sheep and to correct those who stray.—2 Cor. 7:1.
9. What will help us to understand God's Word?
9 Some find it helpful to study the Bible and to discuss what they learn. For example, Jesus often used illustrations to explain things, and he called them "seed" and "soil." Since 1919, Jesus Christ has been using his faithful servants to help people understand the seed of God's Word and its meaning. To ensure that the Bible continues to reach people in their own language, clearly, accurately, and attractively. This is why each of us should ask himself: 'Am I keeping in step with Jesus by supporting the work of spreading the seed of truth?'
LET JEHOVAH BLESS YOU!
10. How does Ezekiel's vision illustrate Jehovah's sovereignty over nations?
10 Jehovah allows nations to continue existing so that his sovereignty can be vindicated. For instance, Ezekiel was given a striking vision illustrating God's sovereignty over nations. That vision showed a majestic chariot. (Ezek. 1:4-28) Jehovah designed that chariot, and he directs all his creatures to carry out his will. The description of God's sovereignty over nations is similar to the description of God's Kingdom in heaven. In fact, the chariot itself beautifully illustrates Jehovah's sovereignty! Think about how remarkable it is that after nearly 2,600 years, we can still recognize that Jehovah is the One who inspired Daniel to write about it. And it is thrilling to know that Christ and his angels are actively involved in demonstrating Jehovah's sovereignty and in fulfilling his purpose!
11, 12. What questions will we answer?
11 Let us now examine what the description of God's Kingdom in heaven reveals. Consider, for example, the work done by our brothers and sisters at the world headquarters in Warwick, New York, USA. They oversee the construction of numerous Kingdom Halls and offices, and they cooperate with architects and engineers from around the globe. We are truly impressed by the ingenuity displayed by our brothers and sisters in this work! But even more impressive is the fact that throughout the entire building process, they demonstrate faith and trust in Jehovah. And Jehovah blesses their efforts, helping them to accomplish much.—Luke 21:1-4.
12 Remember this. Attending school can help us to walk in God's ways. (Isa. 2:2, 3) We benefit from the School for Ministerial Servants, the School for Elders, Gilead School, the School for Kingdom Evangelizers, the School for Asian Missionaries, the Bethel Home School, the School for Group Servants, the School for Pioneering, and the School for Overseers and Circuit Supervisors. How grateful we are that Jehovah provides training for his people! Also, take advantage of JW.ORG, where you will find a wealth of information to help you teach others about the Bible. This website also has articles and videos on various topics that may be of interest to you. Will you use this resource to strengthen your own spirituality?
GET TO KNOW JEHOVAH AND APPRECIATE HIS KINGDOM
13 What are some reasons why Jehovah deserves our love?
13 Do we truly want to show our appreciation for Jehovah, or not? And when we learn about God's qualities and purposes, we become more determined to live in harmony with him and to support his great sovereignty. Those who continue to practice wickedness will face destruction, but let us say, "Let us examine our ways" so that Jehovah does not have to discipline us. (Ps. 97:10) Let us avoid associating with those who do not honor God and let us refrain from saying, "What is right is wrong, and what is wrong is right." (Isa. 5:20) Our main goal should be to please God, so let us prioritize our time and energy, and let us avoid unwholesome associations. (1 Cor. 6:9-11) Let us love Jehovah and let us remain loyal to him. That is why we strive to imitate him by showing kindness to everyone, whether they are family members, friends, coworkers, or classmates. (Prov. 15:3) Often, we can tell how someone feels by observing their actions. Are they honest and sincere, or do they deceive us?
14 What helps Christians to maintain good relationships while also having a good standing with God?
14 Yes. One way Christians can maintain good relationships while also having a good standing with Jehovah is by being moderate in their speech. If someone loves God and wants to be moderate, he will try to avoid using harsh language. And this will help him to avoid causing offense to others. (Eph. 2:2) So, like a loving parent, we may need to correct our children, saying, "This is the way you should speak." The Bible gives this advice: "Slaves, be obedient…to your masters, with sincerity of heart." (Eph. 6:4) Parents who train their children according to God's principles often find that their children respond well, just as Samuel did, and Jehovah supports them.—1 Sam. 3:19.
15 How can we listen attentively and make sure that we understand what others are saying, even if we disagree with them?
15 Listen carefully. We can make sure that we understand what others are saying even if we disagree with God by listening attentively and showing respect for their views. If you know how to listen well, you can often calm down difficult situations. This skill is valuable. But some people find it hard to listen because they are quick to judge. They may feel that they already know what the other person is going to say, so they interrupt and do not give the person a chance to explain fully. We realize that such a person is not truly listening, and we may become frustrated when we see that he does not care about our feelings. (Read Proverbs 14:12.) Really, would you want to use your ability to listen attentively only to those who share your own opinions or beliefs? Of course not! It is important for us to endeavor to understand the thoughts of others, and we can ask our Father, Jehovah, for help in doing so.—Jer. 10:23.
16 But what if someone repeatedly says something offensive, and it seems impossible to reason with him?
16 Suppose a man constantly makes inappropriate comments, and it is very difficult to reason with him. What should you do? He might be influenced by bad associates. Help him to learn Bible principles by being patient and kind. Encourage him to trust that Jehovah will support him, and not rely on another person, especially when raising his children. Teach them to love Jehovah. (Prov. 127:3; Prov. 22:6) Such a man needs to be reminded that Jehovah cares for him, and that the Scriptures offer practical guidance. (Ps. 62:7, 8) Be willing to help him understand the Bible and to apply its teachings in his life, and also be an example to others. Many people need encouragement to raise their children properly, and you can show them kindness and consideration. A parent should always try to discern what is best for his child and teach him to appreciate the value of learning from the Bible and following righteous standards. Does this man really worship Jehovah, or is he simply paying lip service to Him? Perhaps he will admit, "I am."
17. Are there specific things we can do to make our efforts to teach Bible truths more effective?
17 Let us consider what hinders us. One reason why people may reject our message is because they feel that we are imposing our views on them, rather than helping them to draw their own conclusions. To illustrate this point, are there specific things we can do to make our efforts to teach Bible truths more effective? For example, when someone asks, "Is the Bible really God's Word?", do we simply tell him that it is, or do we help him to examine the evidence for himself? When we encourage others to read the Bible, do we just give them a Bible and expect them to understand its meaning without assistance? Or do we offer to study with them, helping them to grasp Jehovah's viewpoint? Also, have we used publications such as *What Does the Bible Really Say?*, and brochures like *God's Love*, in our ministry? And when we invite people to read the brochure *The Bible—God's Word or Man's?*, do we offer to study with them or simply leave it with them? The reason why some find it difficult to accept the truth is because they have been influenced by false teachings. (Acts 2:7) So how can we counteract those false teachings and help people to see the truth?
18, 19. What practical steps can we take to strengthen our faith?
18 There are many ways Jehovah helps us to strengthen our faith! For instance, he encourages us to meditate regularly on his Word, and he provides us with spiritual food through his organization. (Ps. 1:2) By meditating on Bible texts, we can come to appreciate their depth and meaning. Also, we should continue to study the Bible systematically, so that we can better understand God's purposes.—1 Thess. 2:13.
19 According to God's Word, the Bible, we draw close to Jehovah when we approach him in prayer, and he wants us to pray to him. (Jas. 4:8) I especially enjoy remembering how my father used to encourage us to pray to him. He often quoted this scripture to us: "Keep showing gratitude to Jehovah; for his loving-kindness is everlasting." (Ps. 136:1) In fact, the expression "his loving-kindness is everlasting" appears 26 times in Psalm 136. Let us remain close to Jehovah and be grateful for his loving-kindness, so that we too can experience his steadfast love forever!

text:
"Ĩmanthĩei anyanya na ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu."—LUKA 16:9.
MBATHI: 32, 154
1, 2. Nĩkĩ nthĩ ĩno ya Satani ĩkũendeea kwĩthĩwa na andũ amwe ngya?
ĨVINDA yĩĩ nĩ yũmũ na maũndũ nĩ metu mũno. Andũ ma mũika mamanthĩte wĩa makaĩwa nĩ nthĩ. Aingĩ mathamĩĩaa nthĩ ila nthwii o na ethĩwa kwĩka ũu kwĩmalikya mũisyonĩ. Ũkya wĩ kĩla vandũ, o na nginya nthĩ ila nthwii. Ala makwete maendeee kũthua, naw'o ũkya wa ala mate kĩndũ ũendeee kwongeleka. Livoti sya mĩtũkĩ syonanĩtye kana kĩlungu kĩmwe katĩ wa ĩana kya andũ ala athwii ĩũlũ wa nthĩ me na malĩ ĩanene na ya andũ ala angĩ onthe ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. O na kau vai ũw'o mũlũmu ĩũlũ wa livoti ta isu, vai mũndũ ũlea kana nthĩ ĩno yĩ na andũ mbilioni mbingĩ mũno mavinyĩĩwe nĩ ũkya, na ĩvindanĩ o yĩu ve angĩ me na ũthwii mwingĩ ũtoetye kũtũmĩwa nĩ nzyawa na nzyawa. Yesũ nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu ĩla waisye atĩĩ: "Ngya mwĩ nasyo mavinda onthe." (Mko. 14:7) Ĩndĩ nĩkĩ nthĩ ĩilyĩ ũu?
2 Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai ũtesie kũvika, maũndũ nthĩ ĩno meendeea kwĩthĩwa mailyĩ oou. Maũndũ ma siasa, ndĩni ila syĩ kw'o, na maũndũ ma viasala, ala nĩmo maelekanĩtw'e na "atandĩthya" ala mawetetwe nthĩnĩ wa Ũvuan'yo 18:3, nĩ kĩlungu kya nthĩ ĩno ya Satani. O na kau andũ ma Ngai mayĩlikasya o na vanini maũndũnĩ ma siasa kana ndĩninĩ sya ũvũngũ, aingĩ maitonya kwĩkala matekwĩlikya viasalanĩ sya nthĩ ĩno ya Satani.
3. Twĩneenea makũlyo meva?
3 Ithyĩ Aklĩsto nĩtwaĩle kwĩthiana tũmanye twĩ na woni wĩva ĩũlũ wa ũmanthi wa malĩ. No twĩkũlye makũlyo ta aa: 'Ndonya kũtũmĩa malĩ yakwa ata nĩ kana nonany'e nĩ mũĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai? Ndonya ata kwĩyĩkĩĩa mĩvaka maũndũnĩ ma viasala? Ve ngelekany'o syĩva syonanĩtye kana andũ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ nĩmamwĩkwatĩtye vyũ o na kau matwĩe ĩvindanĩ yũmũ?'
NGELEKANY'O YA MŨSYAĨĨSYA ŨTAĨ MŨLŨNGALU
4, 5. (a) Ũla mũsyaĩĩsya wawetiwe nĩ Yesũ akwatiwe nĩ kyaũ? (b) Yesũ anengie aatĩĩi make ũtao wĩva?
4 Soma Luka 16:1-9. Ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ĩũlũ wa ũla mũsyaĩĩsya ũtaĩ mũlũngalu nĩyaĩlĩte kũtuma tũsũanĩa mũno. Mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu atw'ĩkie nĩwaĩtye syĩndũ, ĩndĩ nĩwatũmĩie "ũĩ" 'eemanthĩa anyanya' ma kũmũtetheesya akesa kũtw'ĩka nĩwavutwa. * Yesũ ainengane ngelekany'o ĩsu ndendaa kwĩkĩa vinya amanyĩw'a make matũmĩe nzĩa ĩte ya ũlũngalu kwĩmanthĩa syĩndũ. Nĩkyo kĩtumi waisye mwĩkalĩle wa mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu nĩ wa "ana ma nthĩ ĩno." Ĩndĩ atũmĩie ngelekany'o ĩsu amamanyĩsye kĩndũ kya vata.
5 O tondũ kwailyĩ kwa mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu, Yesũ nĩweesĩ kana aatĩĩi make aingĩ makeethĩwa na ĩvinda yetu me nthĩ ĩno nthũku maimantha kĩndũ kya kũmekalya. Nũndũ wa ũu, amekĩie vinya amea: "Ĩmanthĩei anyanya na ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu; nĩ kana yĩla wĩthela, [Yeova na Yesũ] mamwose inyw'ĩ mawĩkalonĩ ma tene na tene." Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ũtao ũsu wa Yesũ?
6. Twĩsĩ ata kana viasala sya ũmũnthĩ iyaĩ kĩeleelonĩ kya Ngai?
6 O na kũtw'ĩka Yesũ ndaaelesya nĩkĩ waisye kana ũthwii ũsu nĩ ũthwii "ũte wa ũlũngalu," Mbivilia nĩyonanĩtye nesa vyũ kana kĩyaĩ kĩeleelo kya Ngai andũ makũnae viasala ila ikũnawa na ĩtomo. Yeova nĩwanengie Atamu na Eva syĩndũ ila maĩ na vata nasyo me mũũndanĩ wa Eteni ateũmathimĩa. (Mwa. 2:15, 16) Nayo ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, veva mũtheu nĩwatetheeisye kĩkundi kya etĩkĩw'a mauta weethĩa "vai ũmwe waasya kĩndũ o na kĩmwe kya ila waĩ nasyo nĩ kyake mwene; ĩndĩ maĩ na mũamba wa syĩndũ syonthe." (Meko 4:32) O na mwathani Isaia nĩwawetie ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩla andũ onthe makatanĩaa mũno ũsyao wa nthĩ. (Isa. 25:6-9; 65:21, 22) Ĩndĩ kavindanĩ kaa tũĩ, no nginya aatĩĩi ma Yesũ matũmĩe "ũĩ" nĩ kana makwate syĩndũ ila me na vata nasyo matũmĩĩte "ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu" wa nthĩ ĩno, na kavindanĩ o kau maitata mũno mamwendeesye Ngai.
KŨTŨMĨA NA ŨĨ ŨTHWII ŨTE WA ŨLŨNGALU
7. Nĩ ũtao wĩva wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Luka 16:10-13?
7 Soma Luka 16:10-13. Ũla mũsyaĩĩsya wawetiwe nĩ Yesũ amanthie anyanya kwondũ wa kwĩyĩuna. Ĩndĩ ĩla Yesũ weekĩie vinya aatĩĩi make memanthĩe anyanya ĩtunĩ, ndameaa nĩmeke ũu atĩ nĩ kana meyĩune. Mĩsoa ĩla ĩatĩĩe ngelekany'o ĩsu wanenganie yonanĩtye kana ũndũ tũũtũmĩa "ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu" no kwonany'e twĩ aĩkĩĩku kwa Ngai kana tũi aĩkĩĩku. Yesũ endaa kũtũtetheesya tũkwatye kana no twonany'e 'twĩ na kĩthito,' kana twĩ aĩkĩĩku, twatũmĩa na ũĩ malĩ ĩla twakwata. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu ata?
8, 9. Weta Aklĩsto amwe monanĩtye nĩ aĩkĩĩku mĩtũmĩĩlenĩ yoo ya ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu.
8 Ũndũ ũmwe tũtonya kwĩka tũkonany'a twĩ aĩkĩĩku na malĩ ĩla twĩ nayo nĩ kumya mĩvothi kwondũ wa wĩa wa kũtavany'a ũla Yesũ waisye ũkatethw'a. (Mt. 24:14) Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ii iatĩĩe. Kamwĩlĩtu kamwe ka India kaĩ na kasandũkũ kanini keekĩaa mbesa. O na kaleaa kũthooa twĩndũ twa kũthaũka nĩ kana kakwate mbesa sya kwĩkĩa vau kasandũkũnĩ. Kasandũkũ kausũa kanenganie mbesa ila syaĩ vo itetheesye wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Ve mwana-a-asa ũmwe o nake wĩkalaa India wĩ mũũnda wa mĩnathi. Nũndũ ovisi wa ũalyũli wa Malayalam nĩwĩthĩawa na vata wa nathi, mwana-a-asa ũsu nĩwatwaie nathi mbingĩ ovisinĩ ũsu ta mũvothi wake nũndũ oonaa kĩu kĩtethya mũno kwĩ mbesa ila ũtonya kumya. Kwĩka ũu nĩ kũtũmĩa ũĩ. O ta ũu, ana-a-asa ma Greece nĩmakothaa kumya mĩvothi ya mauta ma mosyao ma mĩthata, matulu ma ĩia (cheese), na malĩu angĩ matonya kũtũmĩwa nĩ athũkũmi ma Mbetheli ya kũu.
9 Ve mwana-a-asa wa Sri Lanka waumie kũu athamĩĩa nthĩ ĩngĩ. Ĩndĩ nũnenganĩte mwanya mũsyĩ wake ũtũmĩwe kũmbanĩa maũmbano ma kĩkundi na maũmbano manene. O na nĩwĩtĩkĩlĩtye athũkũmi ma ĩvinda yonthe mekalae vo. Mwana-a-asa ũsu eyĩimĩte mbesa mbingĩ nĩ kana mũsyĩ wake ũtũmĩwe ũu, ĩndĩ ũsu nĩ ũtethyo mũnene kwa atavany'a ala me kĩsionĩ kĩu nĩkwĩthĩwa mo mai ũkwati mwingĩ. Nthĩ ĩmwe wĩa witũ wa kũtavany'a ũsiĩĩwe, ana-a-asa nĩmanenganĩte mĩsyĩ yoo ĩtũmĩwe ta Nyũmba sya Ũsumbĩ. Nũndũ wa ũu, mavainia aingĩ vamwe na angĩ mate na ũkwati nĩmakwatĩte vandũ matonya kũmbanĩa mate kũĩvĩa.
10. Tũkwataa moathimo ta meva tweethĩwa twĩ alau?
10 Ngelekany'o isu twaneenea syoonany'a kana andũ ma Ngai methĩawa na "kĩthito ũndũnĩ ũnini mũno," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, methĩawa me aĩkĩĩku mĩtũmĩĩlenĩ yoo ya malĩ o na kau ti ya vata mũno yasianĩw'a na ũthwii wa kĩ-veva. (Luka 16:10) Anyanyae asu ma Yeova mew'aa ata masũanĩa ũndũ maumasya malĩ yoo ĩtũmĩwe? Nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũkwata ũthwii ũla "wa w'o" nĩ kwĩthĩwa wĩ mũlau. (Luka 16:11) Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe umasya mĩvothi kĩla ĩvinda kwondũ wa wĩa wa Ũsumbĩ nũwetete ũathimo ũmwe ũkwatĩte. Aĩtye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ nĩnĩthĩĩtwe nĩ mũlau na malĩ yakwa, nĩtethekete kwa nzĩa o na nyie mwene ndatonya kũelesya. Nĩthĩĩte kana o ũndũ naolela angĩ malĩ yakwa, now'o nĩthĩawa na woni mũseo ĩũlũ woo. Kĩvathũkany'o na tene, yu nĩnĩekeaa angĩ mũnango, ngamomĩĩsya, ndikusaa ngoo maũndũ maema kũthi ũndũ ngũsũanĩaa, na nĩnĩthĩawa nĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩtĩkĩla ũtao." Aingĩ nĩmethĩĩte kana kwĩthĩwa me alau nĩkũmatetheeasya kũlũlũmĩlya ngwatanĩo yoo na Yeova.—Sav. 112:5; Nth. 22:9.
11. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva kũnengane malĩ yitũ kwonanasya kana twĩ na "ũĩ"? (b) Nĩ kyaũ andũ ma Ngai maendeee kwĩka ũmũnthĩ? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 7.)
11 O na ĩngĩ nĩtwonanasya twĩ na "ũĩ" ĩla twatũmĩa ũthwii ũla twĩ naw'o nĩ kana tũtetheesye angĩ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Ala me na malĩ ĩndĩ matatonya kũtw'ĩka athũkũmi ma ĩvinda yonthe kana kũthamĩĩa kũla kwĩ na vata wa atavany'a, nĩmatanaa kũmanya kana mĩvothi ĩla maumya nĩtetheeasya angĩ wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. (Nth. 19:17) Nũndũ wa mĩvothi ĩla yumaw'a, nthĩ ila syĩ ũkya mwingĩ ĩndĩ syĩ andũ aingĩ mekwendeew'a nĩ ũw'o nikwataa mavuku na ikatetheew'a wĩanĩ wa kũtavany'a. Kwa ngelekany'o, kwa myaka mingĩ ana-a-asa ala me nthĩ imwe ta Congo, Madagascar, na Rwanda mayaĩ matonya kũmanthĩa mĩsyĩ yoo lĩu, na ĩvindanĩ o yĩu maithooa Mbivilia. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ mavinda amwe thooa wa Mbivilia ĩmwe wĩthĩawa wĩanene na mũsaala wa kyumwa kana mwei ũmwe. Ĩndĩ ũmũnthĩ, ũseũvyo wa Yeova nũvotete kũũngamĩa wĩa wa kũalyũla na kũtumbĩthya Mbivilia kwondũ wa kĩla ũmwe nthĩnĩ wa mũsyĩ vamwe na amanyĩw'a ma Mbivilia ala me na waũni wa kũmanya ũw'o. Kĩu kĩtonyekete nũndũ wa mĩvothi ĩla yumaw'a nĩ aingĩ na nũndũ 'kusũa kwa amwe nĩkũtethetye kũnyivĩwa kwa angĩ.' (Soma 2 Akolintho 8:13-15.) Kwoou vai ũmwe ũtatw'ĩka mũnyanyae wa Yeova, ethĩwe nĩ ũla umĩtye malĩ yake kana nĩ ũla ũtethekete nĩ kĩla angĩ maumĩtye.
KŨTATA TŨIKALIKANE VYŨ NA "MAŨNDŨ MA THAYŨ ŨŨ"
12. Avalaamu oonanisye ata kana nĩwamwĩkwatĩtye Ngai?
12 Ũndũ ũngĩ tũtonya kwĩka tũkatw'ĩka anyanyae ma Yeova nĩ kũtata tũmanthe ũla ũthwii "wa w'o" vandũ va kwĩlikya mũno ũmanthinĩ. Kwasũanĩa ĩũlũ wa Avalaamu. Aĩ mũndũ wĩ mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu na nĩweekie ũndũ Ngai wamwĩie. Nĩwatiie ndũa nthwii ya Ulu nĩ kana athi kwĩkalaa maeemanĩ na aiendeea kũlũlũmĩĩlya ngwatanĩo yake na Yeova. (Aevl. 11:8-10) Kĩla ĩvinda amwĩkwatasya Ngai nũndũ nĩweesĩ nĩwe ũtonya kũnengane ũthwii ũla wa w'o, na ndaaenda kwĩmanthĩa malĩ kwa nzĩa ĩtonya kwonany'a ti ta ũmwĩkwatĩtye. (Mwa. 14:22, 23) Yesũ nĩwendaa aatĩĩi make methĩwe na mũĩkĩĩo ta ũsu, nĩkyo kĩtumi weeie mwanake ũmwe mũthwii atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa nũkwenda kwĩthĩwa mwĩanĩu, thi, ũkathoosye ila wĩ nasyo, ũnenge ngya, naku ũkethĩwa na ũthwii ĩtunĩ: na ĩndĩ ũkyũka ũngatĩĩe." (Mt. 19:21) Mwanake ũsu ndaĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ta wa Avalaamu, ĩndĩ ve angĩ monanĩtye kana nĩmamwĩkwatĩtye Ngai na ngoo yonthe.
13. (a) Nĩ ũtao wĩva Vaulo wanengie Timotheo? (b) Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ũtao wa Vaulo?
13 O nake Timotheo aĩ mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu. Vaulo amina kũmwĩta "mũsikalĩ mũseo wa Klĩsto Yesũ" amwĩie ũũ: "Vai mũsikalĩ e kaũnĩ ũvĩndanĩw'a [kana, ũlikana] na maũndũ ma thayũ ũũ; nĩ kana amwendeesye ũla wamũandĩkie ethĩwe mũsikalĩ." (2 Tim. 2:3, 4) Aatĩĩi ma Yesũ ũmũnthĩ, ala nĩ vamwe na athũkũmi ma ĩvinda yonthe mbee wa milioni ĩmwe, nĩmatataa kũatĩĩa ũtao ũsu wa Vaulo ũndũ matonya. Mayĩtĩkĩlaa kũthing'ĩĩw'a maatĩanĩe na syĩndũ ila syĩthĩawa matangasonĩ ma viasala na mayĩtĩkĩlaa kũlikana vyũ na nthĩ ĩno. Vandũ va ũu, mekalaa malilikene mwolooto ũũ: "Ũla ũkovaa nĩ mũthũkũmi wa ũla ũkovethasya." (Nth. 22:7) Vai kĩndũ kĩtanĩthasya Satani ta kwona tũitũmĩa ĩvinda yitũ yonthe na vinya witũ tũithũkũma nthĩ ĩno yake. Ve motwi amwe tũtonya kwĩka tũkatiwa na makoani tũtonya kũmina myaka tũitw'ĩka nĩtwamaĩva. Kwosa mũkovo mũnene wa nyũmba, kusũsya mĩkovo ya sukulu ĩkũkua ĩvinda ĩasa kũĩvĩa, kũĩvĩa ngalĩ sya mbesa mbingĩ, kana kwĩkĩa alũsi nene no kũtũtie na thĩna mwingĩ mũno wa mbesa. Twonanasya twĩ na ũĩ ĩla twatata tũikasembany'e na syĩndũ kana twatata kũolanga makoani na ngalama. Kwĩka ũu kũtũnengae mwanya wa kũmũthũkũma Ngai vandũ va kũthũkũma nthĩ ĩno.—1 Tim. 6:10.
14. Twaĩle kwĩkalaa tũtw'ĩte kwĩka ata? Nengane ngelekany'o.
14 Nĩ kana tũikasembany'e na malĩ, no nginya tũmanye nĩ ũndũ wĩva waĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa wĩ wa vata. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ya mwana-a-asa ũmwe na mũka ala maĩ na viasala mũnene mũno. Ĩndĩ nũndũ maĩ na mea ma kũsyokea ũthũkũmi wa ĩvinda yonthe, nĩmathooisye viasala ũsu, vamwe na ĩsiwa yoo, na syĩndũ ingĩ maĩ nasyo. Mamina ũu nĩmaendie kũtetheesya wĩa wa kwaka ovisi mũnene ũla wĩ Warwick, New York. Ũathimo ũmwe mũnene makwatĩte nũndũ wa kwĩka ũu nĩ kũthũkũma Mbetheli me vamwe na mwĩĩtu woo na mũũme. O na ve ĩvinda mathũkũmangie syumwa iana ũna me na asyai ma mwana-a-asa ũsu ala o namo meeyumĩtye matetheesye wĩa ku Warwick. Ngelekany'o ĩngĩ nĩ ya mwĩĩtu-a-asa vainia wa Colorado, Amelika. Ve ĩvinda wakwatie wĩa vengi akathũkũmaa masaa manini kwa kyumwa. Athũkũmie wĩa wake nesa vyũ nginya ala angĩ mawenda na mamũkũlya athũkũmae vau kĩla mũthenya na maimwambatĩsya mũsaala wake kũndũ kũtatũ. Ĩndĩ nũndũ nĩweesĩ kana eetĩkĩla mũvango ũsu ũthũkũmi wake nũũthi nthĩ, nĩwaleile o na kau mũsaala waĩ mũseo. Asu no Aklĩsto anini twaweta. Ve athũkũmi angĩ aingĩ ma Yeova meyumĩtye o tamo. Kĩthito ta kĩu kya kũmantha Ũsumbĩ mbee kyonanasya kana nĩtwonaa ngwatanĩo yitũ na Ngai vamwe na ũthwii wa kĩ-veva ne mo maũndũ ala ma vata vyũ o na kwĩ malĩ ĩla tũtonya kũkwata nthĩ ĩno.
ĨLA ŨTHWII WĨTHELA
15. Nĩ ũthwii wĩva ũtumaa twĩkala twĩ eanĩe vyũ?
15 Ti lasima Ngai anenge mũndũ ũthwii nĩ kana amũĩkĩĩthye nũmũathimĩte. Yeova aathimaa ala methĩĩtwe me "athwii ma kwĩkaa nesa." (Soma 1 Timotheo 6:17-19.) Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla mwĩĩtu-a-asa wĩtawa Lucia * wamanyie kana nthĩ ya Albania yĩ na vata wa atavany'a, nĩwaumie Italy na athamĩĩa kũu mwakanĩ wa 1993. Lucia ndeesĩ akaumasya mbesa va, ĩndĩ nĩwamwĩkwatĩtye Yeova. Nĩweemanyĩisye kĩthyomo kya Albanian, na kuma ĩvinda yĩu nũtetheetye andũ mbee wa 60 makavikĩĩa kũvatiswa. O na kau andũ aingĩ ma Ngai maitavanasya isionĩ syĩ andũ maingĩvĩte ũu mekwendeew'a nĩ ũw'o, kĩndũ o na kĩva kĩla tweeka tũtetheesye angĩ makwate nzĩa ĩla ĩelete thayũnĩ na maiendeea kũkinyĩla vo, nĩ kĩndũ ithyĩ vamwe namo kĩtakaatũla tene na tene.—Mt. 6:20.
16. (a) Viasala sya nthĩ ĩno ielekele va? (b) Kũmanya kĩla kyũkĩte kwaĩle kũtuma twĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa malĩ?
16 Yesũ aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu: 'Yĩla wĩthela.' Ndaasya: 'Ethĩwa ũkathela.' (Luka 16:9) Ĩvindanĩ yĩĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo, vengi imwe nithelelwe na nthĩ imwe nikwatĩtwe nĩ thĩna wa mbesa. Ĩndĩ ũsu ti thĩna twasũanĩa kĩla kĩkilyĩ kũkwata nthĩ yonthe o mĩtũkĩ. Maũndũ onthe ala me nthĩ ĩno ya Satani makathela, methĩwe makonetye siasa, ndĩni, kana viasala. Mwathani Esekieli na mwathani Nzevania mathanie kana syĩndũ ila syĩthĩĩtwe iitũmĩwa viasalanĩ kuma tene, ta vetha na thaavu, ikavika vandũ wĩthĩe iitethya. (Esek. 7:19; Nzev. 1:18) We wĩw'a ata ũkesa kwĩthĩa nũkũie, na wasisya ĩtina kĩla wasembanisye mũno nakyo nĩ "ũthwii ũla ũte wa ũlũngalu" ĩndĩ ti ũla ũthwii wa w'o? No kwĩthĩwa ũkew'a ta mũndũ wanangĩte myaka yake yonthe aithũkũmĩa kĩvunda kya mbesa na mũthya ayĩsa kwĩthĩa mbesa isu ti sya w'o. (Nth. 18:11) Vate ndĩi, ũthwii wa nthĩ ĩno ũkathela. Kwoou osa ĩvinda yĩĩ ũũtũmĩe nesa nĩ kana 'wĩmanthĩe anyanya' ĩtunĩ. Ũndũ w'onthe ũla tweeka nĩ kana tũkwate mbau wĩa wa Ũsumbĩ wa Yeova ũtumaa twĩthĩwa na ngwatanĩo nzeo vamwe nake.
17, 18. Anyanyae ma Ngai meteele ĩvinda yĩilyĩ ata?
17 Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai wooka, vai mũndũ ũkakomboaa nyũmba kana kwosa mũkovo, lĩu ndũkatesawa na ũkethĩawa kw'o kwa wingĩ, na kũikethĩawa mbĩlũ sya sivitalĩ. Nthĩ ĩkeethĩawa na syĩndũ nzeo vyũ, na andũ ma Yeova makaitanĩaa. Thaavu, vetha, na mavia angĩ ma thooa mũnene makatũmĩawa ta wanake vandũ va kũtũmĩwa kũkũnĩthya vaita. Mbwaũ sya mĩtĩ ĩla mĩseo vyũ, mavia ala maseo, na syũma ila ndũmu vyũ ikanenganawe mana kĩla ũmwe eyakĩe mũsyĩ mwanake. Andũ makatethanasya nũndũ nĩmeũtanĩa kwĩka ũu ĩndĩ ti kwĩthĩwa meenda mbesa. Kĩla mũthenya tũkatanĩaa kũolanĩla kĩla tũkwatie.
18 Ĩvinda yũkĩte, ala memanthĩaa anyanya ĩtunĩ makatanĩa maũndũ angĩ maingĩ mũno eka asu twaweta. Ũtanu wa athaithi ma Yeova ndũkethĩwa ũthimĩka ĩla makew'a ndeto ii sya Yesũ: "Ũkai inyw'ĩ mũathimĩtwe nĩ Asa wakwa, osai ũsumbĩ ũla mwaseũvĩw'e kuma mwambĩlĩlyo wa nthĩ."—Mt. 25:34.
^ kal. 4 Yesũ ndaaweta ethĩwa ndeto ila mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu waneeneiwe syaĩ sya w'o. Ndeto ya Kĩkiliki ĩla ĩalyũlĩtwe "avinganĩw'a" nthĩnĩ wa Luka 16:1 nĩtonya kwonany'a kana mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu eekie kwilĩĩlwa ũvũngũ. Ĩndĩ Yesũ ndaneeneaa kĩla kyaĩ kĩtonya kũtuma mũsyaĩĩsya ũsu alũngw'a. Aneeneaa ĩtambya yĩla woosie.
^ kal. 15 Ngewa ya Lucia Moussanett yĩ ĩkasetinĩ ya Amkeni! ya 22/06/2003, ĩth. 18-22.

translation:
"Be practical in handling wealth, using it to make friends, so that when it fails you may be welcomed into everlasting life."—LUKE 16:9.
PAGE 32, 154
1, 2. Why does Satan lead some people astray by means of money?
LIFE is precious, and possessions can be useful. Many people work hard to acquire material things. Some value them greatly, yet money alone cannot bring lasting happiness. As time goes on, everyone realizes that money has its limitations. Moreover, the more one accumulates, the more he worries about losing it. Consider the plight of millions who suffer because of financial hardship, or those who lose everything they have worked for. Often, such ones feel helpless and hopeless. But Jesus showed the seriousness of this attitude when he said: "No slave can serve two masters." (Matt. 6:24) What is involved in being a slave to money?
2 Jesus knew that the Kingdom of God would last forever, but material things are temporary. Things we desire, though pleasant, are fleeting, and things we dread often come to pass. However, those who allow themselves to be controlled by "the anxiety" mentioned at Matthew 6:31, are coming under the influence of Satan. And if God's servants become preoccupied with acquiring riches or with pursuing pleasure, they may easily fall prey to the influence of Satan.
3. How can we remain balanced?
3 True Christians want to please Jehovah and live according to his standards. So they ask themselves questions like these: 'Am I willing to use my resources to support God's work, even if it means making sacrifices? Am I willing to avoid questionable business practices?' They realize that Jehovah blesses those who put spiritual interests first.—Prov. 10:22.
CONSIDER THIS EXAMPLE
4, 5. (a) What illustration did Jesus use to show how important it is to be loyal? (b) What principle did Jesus emphasize in that illustration?
4 Read Luke 16:1-9. The illustration Jesus used about the shrewd manager helps us understand this important point. The manager was facing dismissal, so he cleverly reduced the debts owed to his master in order to gain favor. * Jesus showed that we can learn from the example of this dishonest man and use our resources wisely to promote spiritual interests. That is why some have been called "sons of this age." He also taught us a lesson about priorities.
5 In addition to the illustration, Jesus said that his disciples should focus on what is truly important—seeking God's Kingdom. He explained: "Keep looking for the Kingdom first, and everything else you need will be added." (Matt. 6:33) How can we imitate Jesus' example?
6. Does concern for material possessions prove that someone has lost sight of God's standards?
6 To help us appreciate what Jesus meant when he spoke of "everything else you need," the Bible shows how God views material things and true riches. Jehovah forgave Adam and Eve their sin, but they still suffered the consequences of disobeying Him. (Gen. 2:15, 16) And the angels who abandoned their proper position rebelled against God and desired independence. (Heb. 10:38) Also, Isaiah foretold a time when people would feast on abundant provisions. (Isa. 25:6-9; 65:21, 22) So, when we hear Jesus say that God provides "everything else you need," it means that He will supply us with what is necessary to live according to His will, and when we put those things first, God blesses our efforts.
USING RESOURCES TO SEEK GOD'S KINGDOM
7. What does Luke 16:10-13 teach us?
7 Read Luke 16:10-13. This illustration used by Jesus highlights the importance of being loyal to spiritual pursuits. The principle Jesus illustrated is that if we give priority to spiritual matters, we can trust that God will provide for our needs. We should not be overly concerned about "everything else you need," but rather focus on pleasing God and seeking his Kingdom. Jesus wants us to learn to use whatever resources we have wisely, so that we may use them for good. But how can we do this?
8, 9. How can a Christian show that he values spiritual wealth?
8 One way we can show that we value spiritual wealth is by using what we have to preach the good news, thus supporting those engaged in the work of proclaiming God's Kingdom, just as Jesus foretold they would be supported. (Matt. 24:14) Consider an example. In India, a woman had a large box full of saris. Yet, she was willing to part with some of them to help others obtain literature. That box represented her possessions, but she realized that helping others was more important. The box still contained possessions, but they were used to support the preaching work. A young man in India once told a missionary that his family owned several acres of land. However, because of their faith, they donated a portion of their land to help fund the building of a Kingdom Hall.
To illustrate further, young people in Greece often forgo buying expensive clothes, shoes, and snacks so that they can contribute financially to the work done by Jehovah's Witnesses.
9 A young person in Sri Lanka sacrificed personal pleasures to serve as a pioneer. He used his time to organize meetings and larger assemblies. And he was happy to assist traveling overseers in whatever way possible. This young man realized that such sacrifices brought him great joy, and he felt that this was a worthwhile use of his life. Another instance involved young people who, instead of spending their money on entertainment, contributed it to the funds for the construction of a new Kingdom Hall. As a result, they felt a sense of accomplishment and satisfaction. Some congregations have found that when young people make donations, they are more motivated to participate actively in the ministry.
10 How can we demonstrate that we appreciate the privileges we have?
10 Do not underestimate the importance of being honest and trustworthy, whether dealing with large sums or small amounts, because "the little along with the much" will be judged according to its value. (Luke 16:10) Should loyal servants of Jehovah be concerned about losing material possessions? It is wise to remember that those who prove themselves worthy of trust with "true riches" will be rewarded generously. (Luke 16:11) One manager recklessly squandered his master's property, but he reasoned: "What am I going to do, since my master is taking away the stewardship from me?" He decided to reduce the amount owed by others so that they might welcome him into their homes. "And the owner commended the unjust steward because he had acted shrewdly." However, let us always strive to please Jehovah and maintain a good standing with him.—Prov. 112:5; Matt. 22:9.
11. (a) Why should we be careful about how we use our money and possessions? (b) What can God's people continue to do to show their appreciation?—See accompanying article, page 7.
11 We should be careful about how we use our money because it can easily lead us astray. But even if we are determined to remain loyal, we may still find ourselves facing temptations. However, Jehovah understands our imperfections and does not expect us to be perfect. (Prov. 19:17) In view of the world's problems, it is vital that each of us take steps to protect himself from being influenced by materialism. For example, for many years brothers in countries like Congo, Madagascar, and Rwanda have found it difficult to resist the temptation to pursue wealth, and some have become involved in questionable business dealings. Why? Because they saw others getting rich quickly through such means. It is important to remember that true riches come from Jehovah and that he supports those who zealously preach and teach the Bible. He also appreciates the generosity of those who willingly share what they have with others. The principle illustrated by the apostle Paul applies today: "What is collected will not result in distress, for it will relieve the distress of others." (Read 2 Corinthians 8:13-15.) So let us not allow a love of money to weaken our loyalty to Jehovah, whether it is our own money or the contributions of others.
DO NOT BE DISTRACTED BY "IMPORTANT THINGS"
12. Did Abraham ever question God's direction?
12 One way we show our loyalty to Jehovah is by not letting "important things" prevent us from giving priority to his service. Consider the example of Abraham. He was a wealthy man, yet he was willing to give up everything when God asked him to do so. He realized that maintaining a close relationship with Jehovah was more important than material possessions. (Heb. 11:8-10) Whenever we put God first, we demonstrate that we value his approval and are willing to make sacrifices to please him. (Gen. 14:22, 23) Jesus told his followers that it is difficult for a rich man to enter the Kingdom. That is why he said to one young man: "If you want to be perfect, go sell your belongings and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come be my follower." (Matt. 19:21) This young man turned away saddened, because he was very fond of his wealth. Like this young man and like Abraham, we too may face a choice between material things and our loyalty to God.
13. (a) What advice did Paul give Timothy? (b) How can we apply Paul's advice?
13 For Timothy was distressed. Paul kindly called him "a faithful minister of Christ Jesus" and wrote to him: "Continue putting your trust in what you have learned and believed, knowing from whom you learned it. And continue doing so, because you know who taught you." (2 Tim. 2:3, 4) Considering that Jesus himself had only a small group of about 120 followers—perhaps around a million in total—it may be difficult to imitate Paul's example today. However, we can strive to share our faith with others, even if we feel inadequate or fear rejection. People of this sort often remember this saying: "The one who perseveres is the one who succeeds." (Prov. 22:7) Satan does everything he can to prevent us from using our time and energy to proclaim God's Word. So let us each resolve to remain firm in our determination, despite difficulties and setbacks. To avoid being distracted by worldly pursuits, such as accumulating wealth, pursuing higher education, or seeking personal pleasure, we need to set priorities. We should recognize that we may face challenges and temptations regarding money and possessions. Avoiding this will help us to focus on pleasing God and those who worship Him.—1 Tim. 6:10.
14 How, then, can we stay active in this work? Let us discuss some practical suggestions.
14 It is good to cooperate with others, and it is important to know what is involved in making spiritual progress. Consider the example of one full-time minister and his wife who faced a serious challenge. They spent months traveling throughout the entire country, often walking long distances, sometimes without food or shelter, and facing many other hardships. This couple felt compelled to go to visit the large estate of Mr. Warwick in New York. One significant factor that motivated them to undertake this journey was their desire to help Bethel members and those associated with them. And they walked for months, enduring hardship, so that they could return to Warwick. Another example involves a young pioneer from Colorado, America. He walked for miles each day, spending hours at a time preaching. He walked to see his family, but he also went out regularly and used his income to pay for his travel expenses. In fact, he was willing to walk for days on end if necessary, and he gladly sacrificed his personal comfort. He and Alistair were very determined. Many other servants of Jehovah have shown similar determination. The thought of pleasing Jehovah and strengthening our relationship with God and enjoying eternal life motivates us to overcome obstacles and to make sacrifices—to put spiritual things first.
BUT WHAT ABOUT…?
15 What can motivate us to stay spiritually active?
15 Jehovah knows that each person has different circumstances. Jehovah provides comfort through his Word, saying: "Those who desire to live comfortably will come to grief." (Read 1 Timothy 6:17-19.) For example, Sister Lucia from Albania realized that her country was facing political turmoil, so she moved to Italy in 1993. Despite her difficulties, Lucia continued to serve Jehovah. She learned the Albanian language and helped over 60 people learn about the Bible. And like many other faithful Christians, she found that when she puts spiritual things first, she experiences joy and satisfaction.—Matt. 6:20.
16. (a) How does this scripture encourage us? (b) Why is it important to be realistic about what we can accomplish?
16 Jesus used the illustration of the shrewd manager to teach us the importance of making good use of our resources: "Use practical wisdom." He also said: "Earnestly seek the kingdom." (Luke 16:9) In reality, most of us have limited time and energy. So we need to prioritize what is truly important. The temptations offered by Satan's world—such as wealth, pleasure, or fame—can lead us astray. Consider Ezekiel and Zephaniah, who foretold that people would misuse their resources and pursue empty desires, resulting in ruin. (Ezek. 7:19; Zeph. 1:18) Are you careful about how you spend your time and energy? Or do you find yourself constantly striving for more material possessions? Is that really what makes you happy?—Prov. 18:11. Remember, the pursuit of wealth is temporary. Instead, focus on using your life to support God's Kingdom and enjoy lasting happiness.
17, 18. What qualities does God value, and why?
17 God values humility. A humble person may be willing to leave his comfortable home or give up a secure job to serve Jehovah, knowing that doing so will please Him. Humility leads to obedience and a closer relationship with God. Those who are obedient receive blessings from God, and they are united with fellow worshippers. Generosity, hospitality, and selflessness are also pleasing to God. Like the trees in Eden, humans can demonstrate generosity by sharing what they have with others. People should be generous, not expecting something in return, but because they want to help those in need. They should be willing to share whatever they have, even if it means sacrificing some comfort themselves.
18 As we have seen, God appreciates genuine devotion. But what else do we need to do to show our love for him? One way is to imitate the example set by Jesus: "Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."—Matt. 25:34.
^ par. 4 Jesus set this example when he willingly gave up his heavenly privileges to come to earth. The Greek expression used at Luke 16:1, which is often rendered "manager," could also be understood as someone who has been entrusted with possessions. Jesus was willing to use everything he had to accomplish God's purpose. He was willing to make sacrifices.
^ par. 15 In an article in Awake! of June 22, 2003, pages 18-22, Lucia Moussanett shared her experience.

text:
"Vala ve Veva wa Mwĩaĩi [Yeova], nĩvo ve ũthasyo."—2 AKO. 3:17.
MBATHI: 31, 32
1, 2. (a) Andũ methĩawa na mawoni meva me kĩvathũkany'o ĩũlũ wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa? (b) Mbivilia ĩmanyĩasya ata ĩũlũ wa ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa, na twĩneenea makũlyo meva?
VE ĨVINDA mũndũ mũka ũmwe waĩ na ũtwi wa kwĩka ũmũkonetye we mwene. Mũndũ mũka ũsu eeie mũnyanyae atĩĩ: "Eka kwangangya kĩlĩko kyakwa; ndavye kĩla ngwĩka. Kĩu nĩkyo kĩ laisi." Vandũ va mũndũ mũka ũsu atũmĩe mũthĩnzĩo mũna ũnengetwe nĩ Mũmbi wake, oonie ne kavaa akatavw'a ũndũ ũkwĩka. Mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nĩ ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Nata naku? Nĩwendete kwĩyĩkĩa motwi, kana wonaa nĩ kavaa ala angĩ makakũamũĩa kĩla ũkwĩka? We wonaa ata mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa?
2 Andũ matwĩe maneeneaa ũndũ ũsu kwa ĩvinda ya myaka maana maingĩ. Amwe masasya atĩ vai kĩndũ kĩtawa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa aĩ nũndũ Ngai nĩwe ũtũvangĩaa maũndũ maitũ onthe. Namo angĩ masasya atĩ nĩ kana twĩthĩwe na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa kĩla tũkwĩka, no nginya twĩkale tũte na mwĩao o na ũmwe ũtwovete. Ĩndĩ nĩ kana tũelewe ũndũ ũsu nesa, no nginya tũsũanĩe ũndũ Ndeto ya Ngai, Mbivilia, yaĩtye. Nĩkĩ? Kĩtumi nũndũ Mbivilia nĩwetete kana Yeova atũmbie twĩ na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, atũmbie twĩ na ũtonyi wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi maseo na no tũmeke tũte kũsiĩĩwa. (Soma Yosua 24:15.) O na ĩngĩ, Mbivilia nĩsũngĩĩte makũlyo ta aa: Twaĩle kũtũmĩa ata ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi? W'o ũthasyo ũsu witũ wĩ mĩvaka? Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva motwi ala twĩkaa monanasya ũndũ tũmwendete Yeova mũno wĩana? Tũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nĩtũũnenga ndaĩa motwi ma ala angĩ?
TWĨĨMANYĨSYA KYAŨ TWASŨANĨA ĨŨLŨ WA YEOVA NA YESŨ?
3. Yeova atwiĩe ngelekany'o yĩva ya kũtũmĩa ũthasyo?
3 Yeova no we e weka wĩ na ũthasyo wa kwĩka kyonthe kĩla ũkwenda ate kwovwa nĩ mwĩao o na ũmwe, ĩndĩ ũndũ ũtũmĩaa ũthasyo wake nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo kwitũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, nĩwatwie kũnyuva mbaĩ ya Isilaeli yĩthĩwe "mbaĩ yake mwene." (Kũt. 7:6-8) Ũsu ti ũtwi weekie kĩthũlũmũkĩlo. Yeova eekie ũtwi ũsu nĩ kana eanĩsye watho ũla wathĩte mũnyanyae Avalaamu myaka maana maingĩ mbee wa vau. (Mwa. 22:15-18) Na kwongela kĩu, mavinda onthe Yeova atũmĩaa ũthasyo wake atongoew'e nĩ nguma ĩla wĩsĩkĩe nayo ya wendo na ya ũlũngalu. Twonaa ũu nesa twasisya ũndũ Yeova wakanasya Aisilaeli, o na kau matindĩaa kũtia ũthaithi wa w'o. Ĩla Aisilaeli meelila kuma ngoonĩ, Yeova nĩwamonasya na ngenda kana nũmendete na nĩwamew'ĩaa tei. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ngavosya kũsyoka na ĩtina kwoo, ngamenda mũno [kana, "ngamenda na ngenda," NWT]." (Osea 14:4) Ĩsu nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ta kĩ! Yeova atũmĩie ũthasyo wake kũtetheesya ala angĩ.
4, 5. (a) Nũũ waĩ wa mbee kũnengwa nĩ Ngai mũthĩnzĩo wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa, na aũtũmĩie ata? (b) Nĩ ĩkũlyo yĩva kĩla ũmwe waitũ waĩlĩte kwĩkũlya?
4 Nũndũ wa nguma ya Yeova ya wendo, ĩla wambĩĩie kũmba syĩndũ nĩwatwie kũnenga alaĩka na andũ ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ũla waĩ wa mbee kũkwata mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nĩ Mwana wake mũsyawa wa mbee, nake nĩ "mũvw'ano wa Ngai ũtonekaa." (Ako. 1:15) Yesũ atanamba kũka kũũ nthĩ nĩwatw'ĩte kũlũmany'a na Ĩthe wake, ĩndĩ ti kũkwata mbau ũlei ũla Satani wambĩlĩlye. Na ĩla wesie kũka kũũ nthĩ nĩwatũmĩie ũthasyo wake nesa nũndũ nĩwaleanile na motato ma ũla Mũmaitha mũnene. (Mt. 4:10) O na ũtukũ wa atanamba kũawa, Yesũ avoyie na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo mũno na aĩkĩĩthya Ĩthe wake ĩngĩ kana nĩwatw'ĩte kwĩka kwenda kwake. Aisye atĩĩ: "Asa, ethĩwa nũkwenda, mbathũkĩsya kĩkombe kĩĩ: ĩndĩ ti ũndũ ngwenda nyie, ĩndĩ nĩwĩkĩke ũla ũkwenda we." (Luka 22:42) Nĩtwĩkei o ta Yesũ na tũitũmĩa ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa tũmũtaĩe Yeova na tũyĩka kwenda kwake! Ĩndĩ w'o ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka?
5 Ĩĩ nĩ w'o nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka tũkaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ nũndũ o naitũ tũmbĩtwe na mũvw'ano na kĩtutya kya Ngai. (Mwa. 1:26) Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ithyĩ twĩ na mĩvaka twiĩwe. Tũi na ũthasyo ta wa Yeova nĩkwĩthĩwa we nde mwĩao o na ũmwe ũmwovete. Ndeto ya Ngai ĩeleetye kana ũthasyo witũ wĩ mĩvaka na kana no nginya tũtate tũikakĩle mĩvaka ĩsu mĩseo Yeova ũtwiĩe. Kwa ngelekany'o, iveti syĩĩtwe nĩsyĩnyivĩsye aũme masyo, nasyo syana syĩĩtwe imenyivĩsye asyai masyo. (Aev. 5:22; 6:1) Yo mĩvaka ĩsu twiĩwe yaĩle kũtũsukuma tũtũmĩe ũthasyo witũ ata? Ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩ wa vata nũndũ ũndũ tũũtũmĩa ũthasyo witũ no kũtume twĩsa kũkwata thayũ ũtathela kana tũkaũkosa.
ALA MATŨMĨIE ŨTHASYO WOO NESA NA ALA MAŨTŨMĨIE NAĨ
6. Nengane ngelekany'o ĩkwonany'a ũseo wa kwĩkĩĩwa mĩvaka.
6 Nĩkwĩthĩwa ũthasyo witũ wĩ mĩvaka, ũu nĩ kwonany'a ũsu ti ũthasyo wa w'o? Aiee, ti w'o! Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya ũu? Kĩtumi nũndũ mĩvaka ĩsu twiĩwe nĩ ũsũvĩo kwitũ. Kwoosa ngelekany'o ĩno: Twasye nũkwenda kũthi taoninĩ ĩmwe yĩ vaasa. O na kau wĩ na ũthasyo wa kũthi kũu ũtwaĩte ngalĩ, we nĩwĩw'a wĩ mwĩanĩe wĩsĩle malelũnĩ andũ mataatĩĩaa mĩao ya lelũ, na kĩla mũndũ wĩtw'ĩĩaa esemba mũno wĩana ata kana eĩsĩla ngalĩko yĩva ya lelũ? Vate nzika, ndwĩw'a wĩ mwĩanĩe! Kwoou no nginya twiĩwe mĩvaka nĩ kana ithyonthe tũtanĩe moseo ala maetawe nĩ ũthasyo wa w'o. Nĩ kana tũelewe mũnango nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa ũĩ kũtũmĩa ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa tũte kũkĩla mĩvaka ĩla twiĩwe nĩ Yeova, ekai twone ngelekany'o imwe sya andũ me Mbivilianĩ.
7. (a) Nĩ kĩvathũkany'o kĩmwe kĩva kyaĩ katĩ wa Atamu na nyamũ? (b) Weta ũndũ ũmwe ũkwonany'a ũndũ Atamu watũmĩie ũthasyo wake wa kwĩnyuvĩa.
7 Ĩla Ngai woombie mũndũ wa mbee, Atamu, nĩwamũnengie mũthĩnzĩo wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa o tondũ wanengete alaĩka ĩtunĩ. Mũthĩnzĩo ũsu nĩw'o watumie Atamu ethĩwa e kĩvathũkany'o na nyamũ nũndũ syo iyaanengwa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o ĩmwe ĩkwonany'a ũndũ Atamu watũmĩie ũthasyo wake ũndũ vaĩle. Nyamũ syoombiwe mũndũ atanamba kũmbwa. Ĩndĩ Yeova aiie kĩanda kya kũitw'ĩĩa masyĩtwa nginya ĩla wesie kũmba mũndũ wa mbee nĩ kana mũndũ ũsu atanĩe kwĩanĩsya kĩanda kĩu. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Ngai woosie nyamũ "atwaĩa mũndũ one ũndũ wĩsyĩta." Na ĩla Atamu wasyaisye kĩla nyamũ nesa na amĩnenga ĩsyĩtwa yĩmyaĩle, Yeova ndaaũka akavĩndũa masyĩtwa ala wanyuvĩte. Kũvika o na ũmũnthĩ, "o ũndũ [Atamu] wetie kĩla kyũmbe kĩ thayũ, noyo syĩtwa yakyo."—Mwa. 2:19.
8. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Atamu watũmĩie naĩ ũthasyo wake wa kwĩnyuvĩa? Ũndũ ũsu ũtumĩte kwĩthĩwa kũilyĩ ata?
8 Ũndũ wa kũmakya nĩ kana Atamu ndaaĩanĩwa nĩ kĩanda kĩla wanengetwe nĩ Ngai kya kũĩma na kũseũvya nthĩ yonthe yĩkale mũũnda wa Eteni, o na kau nĩwanengetwe ũthasyo mwingĩ vyũ wa kũtethya wĩa ũsu. Ngai amwĩĩte atĩĩ: "Ongelekai, mwingĩve, musũsye nthĩ, na kũmĩkĩlya vinya; na ĩthĩwai na ũsumbĩko ĩũlũ wa makũyũ . . . , nyũnyi . . . , na ĩũlũ wa kĩla kĩndũ kĩ thayũ kĩendaa ĩũlũ wa nthĩ." (Mwa. 1:28) Vandũ va kwĩanĩwa, anyuvie kũkĩla mĩvaka ĩla weekĩĩwe nĩ Ngai kwa kũya yĩla ĩtunda wavatĩtwe. Atũmĩie ũthasyo wake wa kwĩnyuvĩa naĩ vyũ na kĩu kĩtumĩte ũsyao wake ũlika thĩnanĩ mwingĩ mũno kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mingĩ mũno. (Alo. 5:12) Kwona kĩla kyeekĩkie nũndũ wa ũtwi wa Atamu kwaĩle kũtuma tũtũmĩa nesa ũthasyo ũla tũnengetwe tũteũthonoka mĩvaka ĩla twĩkĩĩwe nĩ Yeova.
9. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva Yeova waekie andũ make, Isilaeli, menyuvĩe? Mbaĩ ĩsu yanyuvie kwĩka ata?
9 Nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa Atamu na Eva mayaamwĩw'a Ngai, nĩmatiĩe nzyawa syoo naĩ na kĩkw'ũ. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, nzyawa isu iyaavenwa ũthasyo wasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ũndũ ũsu tũwonaa nesa twasisya ũndũ Ngai wakuie mbaĩ ya Isilaeli. Yeova atũmie mũthũkũmi wake Mose atavye Aisilaeli kana nũmanengete ũthasyo wa kwĩtĩkĩla kana kũlea kĩanda kya kũtw'ĩka andũ make mwene. (Kuma 19:3-6) Mo matavw'a ũu meekie ata? Nĩmenyuvĩie mate kũlasimĩthw'a kwĩka maũndũ ala Ngai wendaa meke nĩ kana matw'ĩke andũ make mwene. Onthe maisye ũũ na wasya ũmwe: "Onthe ala Yeova ũneenete tũkeeka." (Kuma 19:8) Ĩndĩ ũsengy'o, ĩtina wa ĩvinda mbaĩ ĩsu nĩyatũmĩie ũthasyo wayo naĩ na yalea kwĩanĩsya kĩla yamwathĩte Yeova. Ekai ngelekany'o ĩsu yoo ĩte nzeo ĩtũmanyĩsye kĩndũ, na ekai kĩla ĩvinda tũtũmĩae nesa mũthĩnzĩo witũ wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa kwa kũendeea kũlũmany'a na Yeova na kũatĩĩaa mĩao yake mĩlũngalu.—1 Ako. 10:11.
10. Nĩ ngelekany'o syĩva syonanĩtye kana nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka andũ me na naĩ makatũmĩa ũthasyo woo kwa nzĩa ĩkũmũtaĩa Ngai? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 12.)
10 Ĩvuku ya Aevelania kĩlungu kya 11 nĩyĩwetete masyĩtwa ma athũkũmi ma Ngai 16, ala manyuvie kũtũmĩa ũthasyo woo mate kũkĩla mĩvaka ĩla Yeova ũtwiĩe. Na nũndũ wa ũu, nĩmakwatie moathimo maingĩ na meethĩwa na wĩkwatyo mũseo wa ĩvinda yũkĩte. Kwa ngelekany'o, nũndũ Noa aĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, nĩwanyuvie kũatĩĩa mũtalatala ũla Ngai wamũnengete wa kwaka ĩla ngalawa nĩ kana atangĩĩe andũ make na nzyawa syake. (Aevl. 11:7) O namo Avalaamu na Sala nĩmaatĩĩie na ngenda kĩla Ngai wamatavisye na mathi nthĩ ĩla wamathĩte. O na ĩla mambĩĩe kyalo kya kũthi nthĩ ya watho, maĩ o na "ũthei wa kũalũka" mathi ndũanĩ nthwii ĩla maumĩte ya Ulu. Ĩndĩ vandũ va kwĩka ũu, nĩmaendeeie kũsyaĩĩsya wĩkwatyo ũla maĩ naw'o wa kũkwata "matho" ma Ngai. Nĩmendaa mũno kũlika "nthĩ nzeo mbee." (Aevl. 11:8, 13, 15, 16) Ngelekany'o ĩngĩ nĩ ya Mose. Atiie mothwii ma Misili, "akĩnyuva kavaa kũthĩnw'a vamwe na andũ ma Ngai, kwĩ kũtana maũndũnĩ ma naĩ ĩvinda." (Aevl. 11:24-26) Nĩtwonany'ei twĩ na mũĩkĩĩo ta andũ asu maĩ kw'o tene kwa kũtũmĩa nesa mũthĩnzĩo witũ wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Tũtonya kwĩka ũu kwa kũũtũmĩa kwĩka kwenda kwa Ngai.
11. (a) Kwĩthĩwa na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa kũtumaa tũkwata ũathimo ũmwe wĩva mũnene? (b) Nĩ kyaũ kĩkwĩkĩaa vinya ũtũmĩe nesa ũthasyo waku wa kwĩnyuvĩa?
11 O na kau no woneke wĩ ũndũ wĩ laisangi kwĩa mũndũ ũngĩ atũtw'ĩĩe kĩla tũkwĩka, kĩu nĩũtuma tũkosa ũathimo ũmwe mũseo tũkwataa nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Ũathimo ũsu nũwetetwe ĩandĩkonĩ ya Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 30:19, 20. (Soma.) Mũsoa wa 19 ũwetete ĩũlũ wa kĩndũ Ngai weeie Aisilaeli menyuvĩe. Naw'o mũsoa wa 20 wonanĩtye kana Yeova nĩwamanengie mwanya mũseo wa kũmwony'a kĩla kyaĩ ngoonĩ syoo. O naitũ no twĩnyuvĩe kũmũthaitha Yeova. Vai kĩtumi kĩngĩ kĩnene kya kũtũmĩa ũthasyo witũ nesa kwĩ kwony'a Ngai kana nĩtũmwendete, vamwe na kũmũkumya na kũmũtaĩa!
NDŨKATŨMĨE NAĨ ŨTHASYO WAKU WA KWĨNYUVĨA
12. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva tũtaĩle kwĩsa kwĩka?
12 Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ. We ũkesa kũnenga mũnyanyau mũthĩnzĩo wa vata mũno, wĩona ta wĩw'a ata ũmanyĩte atĩ anoosie mũthĩnzĩo ũsu awĩkya takatakanĩ, kana o na kũthũkya ũvoo, anaũmĩisye mũndũ ũngĩ naw'o? Wĩ na kĩu kĩlĩkonĩ kwasũanĩa ũndũ Yeova ũtonya kwĩthĩwa ew'aa oona ũndũ andũ aingĩ matũmĩaa naĩ ũthasyo woo ĩla mekwĩka motwi, kana o na ũndũ maũtũmĩaa kũũmĩsya angĩ. Vate nzika, kũilyĩ o tondũ Mbivilia yathanie kana "mĩthenyanĩ ya mũminũkĩlyo" andũ makeethĩwa "mate mũvea." (2 Tim. 3:1, 2) Mwa tũikaaĩse kũtũmĩa naĩ kana kũwosa ũndũ vataĩle mũthĩnzĩo ũũ wa vata Yeova ũtũnengete! Ĩndĩ tũtonya kwĩka ata tũikese kũtũmĩa naĩ mũthĩnzĩo witũ wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa?
13. Nĩ ũndũ ũmwe wĩva ũtonya kwonany'a tũikũtũmĩa ũthasyo witũ naĩ?
13 Ithyonthe twĩ na ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa atindany'a maitũ, ũndũ tũkwĩkĩa ngũa kana kwĩyanakavya, na nĩ syĩndũ syĩva tũkwĩtanĩthya nasyo. Ĩndĩ o na ũu wĩ o vo, ũthasyo witũ no ũtw'ĩke "ũthei wa kũvw'ĩka ũthũku" ethĩwa tũkanyuva kũtw'ĩka ngombo sya mĩmeo yitũ kana ethĩwa tũkalikana na maũndũ mathũku ala nthĩ ĩno yendete. (Soma 1 Vetelo 2:16.) Vandũ va kũtũmĩa ũthasyo witũ ta "ũthei wa kwendeesya mwĩĩ," nĩtũnyuvei kwĩkaa motwi ala matonya kũtũtetheesya tũatĩĩe ũtao ũũ: "Ĩkai maũndũ onthe kwa kũtaĩa Ngai."—Aka. 5:13; 1 Ako. 10:31.
14. Kũmwĩkwatya Yeova kũkonanĩtye ata na ũndũ tũtũmĩaa ũthasyo witũ wa kwĩnyuvĩa?
14 Nzĩa ĩngĩ ya kwĩsũvĩa tũikese kũtũmĩa mũthĩnzĩo witũ wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa naĩ nĩ kũmũĩkĩĩa Yeova na tũimũeka atũtongoesye tũikese kũkĩla mĩvaka ĩla ũtwiĩe. Yeova e weka nĩwe 'ũtũmanyĩasya kwaĩla, ũla ũtũtongoeasya nzĩanĩ ĩla twaĩle kũthi nayo.' (Isa. 48:17) No nginya twĩnyivye na tũyĩtĩkĩlana na ũw'o wa ndeto ii mbeveee: "Nzĩa ya mũndũ ndĩ nthĩnĩ wake mwene; kũtongoesya matambya make kũti nthĩnĩ wa mũndũ ũla ũendaa." (Yel. 10:23) Kwoou ekai tũtate tũikaaĩse kũkwatw'a nĩ kĩtei kya kwĩkwatya ũĩ witũ ene o ta Atamu na ala Aisilaeli maleile kũmwĩw'a Ngai. Vandũ va ũu, tũtatei tũatĩĩe ũtao ũũ: "Ĩkĩĩa Yeova na ngoo yaku yonthe."—Nth. 3:5.
NENGA NDAĨA ŨTHASYO WA ALA ANGĨ
15. Mwolooto ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akalatia 6:5 wĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
15 Mũvaka ũmwe Yeova ũtwiĩe nĩ kana no nginya tũnenge ndaĩa ũthasyo wa ala angĩ wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi. Nĩkĩ? Nĩkwĩthĩwa vai Aklĩsto elĩ matonya kwĩka motwi mavw'anene vyũ kĩla ĩvinda nũndũ ithyonthe twĩ na mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa. Na ũndũ ũsu nĩ wa w'o o na maũndũnĩ ala makonetye mwĩkalĩle witũ na ũthaithi witũ. Kwalilikana mwolooto ũla wĩ ĩandĩkonĩ ya Akalatia 6:5. (Soma.) Kũmanya kana kĩla Mũklĩsto "akakua mũio wake mwene" nĩkũtũtetheeasya tũnenge ndaĩa ũthasyo ũla angĩ me naw'o wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi.
16, 17. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa watw'ĩkie thĩna kĩkundinĩ kya Kolintho? (b) Vaulo eekie ata amine thĩna ũsu, na kĩu kĩtũmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa ũthasyo wa ala angĩ?
16 Kwasũanĩa ngelekany'o yĩ Mbivilianĩ yonanĩtye nĩkĩ no nginya tũnenge ndaĩa ũthasyo wa ana-a-asa wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi maũndũnĩ makonetye wasya wa ngoo. Ĩvinda yĩmwe Aklĩsto ma Kolintho maĩ na ngusanĩsyo ĩũlũ wa kũya nyama imwe syatesawa sokonĩ, ila itonya kwĩthĩwa mbeenĩ syathembewe ngai sya mĩvw'anano. Amwe maasyaa ũũ: 'Nũndũ mĩvw'anano ti kĩndũ, no tũye nyama isu twĩ na wasya mũseo wa ngoo.' Ĩndĩ Aklĩsto ala mbeenĩ mathaithaa mĩvw'anano ĩsu moonaa kũya nyama isu ne ũndũ ũmwe na kũthaitha. (1 Ako. 8:4, 7) Ũsu waĩ ũndũ mũito mũno na waĩ ũtonya kũete mũaanĩko kĩkundinĩ. We Vaulo atetheeisye Aklĩsto asu ma Kolintho ata mamanye woni wa Ngai ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu?
17 Ũndũ wa mbee ũla Vaulo weekie nĩ kũlilikany'a kĩkundi kyonthe kana lĩu ndwĩsa kũmatetheesya mamũthengeee Ngai mũnango. (1 Ako. 8:8) Ũndũ wa kelĩ ũla weekie nĩ kũmakany'a maiketĩkĩlye 'kũthaw'a ku kwoo' kũtw'ĩke "ũlulutĩkyo kwa ala [maĩ] onzu." (1 Ako. 8:9) Na ĩndĩ ĩtina nĩwamataie ala maĩ na wasya wa ngoo ũte na vinya mũno maikamasilĩle ala mekwona maĩle kũya nyama isu. (1 Ako. 10:25, 29, 30) Ũndũnĩ ũsu mũito wakonetye ũthaithi, kĩla Mũklĩsto aaĩle kwĩyĩkĩa ũtwi atongoew'e nĩ wasya wake wa ngoo. Kwoou o naitũ tyo twaĩle kũnenga ndaĩa ũthasyo ũla ana-a-asa maitũ me naw'o wa kwĩyĩkĩa motwi o na maũndũnĩ ala manini?—1 Ako. 10:32, 33.
18. Ũtonya kwonany'a ata kana nũtũmĩaa nesa mũthĩnzĩo waku wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa?
18 Yeova nũtũnengete mũthĩnzĩo wa ũthasyo wa kwĩnyuvĩa, na ũsu nĩw'o ũthasyo wa w'o ũla tũtonya kũkwata. (2 Ako. 3:17) Nĩtwonaa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wĩ wa vata vyũ nũndũ nũtũnengae mwanya wa kwĩka motwi ala matumaa Yeova amanya ũndũ tũmwendete mũno wĩana. Ekai tũendeee kwonany'a nĩtũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu wa vata kwa kũũtũmĩa kwa nzĩa ĩkũmũtaĩa Ngai na kwa kũnenga ndaĩa motwi ala angĩ mekaa matũmĩĩte mũthĩnzĩo ũsu.
