translation:
"Value also Jehovah [Yeova], for he is trustworthy."—2 COR. 3:17.
POINTS: 31, 32
1, 2. (a) What questions move many people to seek trustworthiness? (b) How can our own need for trustworthiness be illustrated, and what benefits can result?
IMAGINE a man who has lost something valuable to him. That man might say: "I will search everywhere for it; I will not rest until I find it. This is what matters most." People like this man use effort because they appreciate what their Creator has given them, and they want to recover what was lost. This effort is trustworthiness. But why? Is it simply a matter of remembering, or does it involve a deep desire to find what was lost? Do you value such effort on your part?
2 For years, many people have experienced this personally. Some feel that trustworthiness depends entirely on God giving us things. Others believe that we are born with trustworthiness and that we simply need to develop it. Either way, it is important that we understand this matter well, so that we may appreciate God's purpose, the Bible, more fully. Why? Because the Bible shows that Jehovah helps us to be trustworthy, or, for that matter, helps us to remember things easily and to avoid being misled. (Read Joshua 24:15.) Moreover, the Bible raises questions such as: Have we ever used our own initiative to be trustworthy? Where does such initiative come from? Is it because we truly want to please Jehovah and show him appreciation? Are we willing to examine ourselves honestly?
LET US EXAMINE HOW WE APPRECIATE JEHOVAH AND JESUS
3 What reasons does Jehovah give for helping us?
3 Jehovah consistently gives reasons why he helps us to succeed in everything we do, whether it is something small or something significant. He wants us to know that his help is generous. For example, he referred to the nation of Israel as "his own possession." (Deut. 7:6-8) This was not merely a formality. Jehovah showed his affection for them when he made a covenant with faithful Abraham many years ago. (Gen. 22:15-18) Furthermore, all the help Jehovah has given us is motivated by his love and loyalty. We can see this when we reflect on how Jehovah dealt with ancient Israel, and how he repeatedly demonstrated his faithfulness. However, Israel often failed to respond appreciatively, and Jehovah expressed his disappointment. They said: "I will charm her; I will win her heart." (Hosea 14:4) We too should be very appreciative! Let Jehovah motivate us to be generous.
4, 5. (a) How can we show our appreciation for God's generosity, and what does he expect of us? (b) What benefit is there in being generous?
4 As servants of Jehovah, let us explain how we can show appreciation for those who generously share with others. Our appreciation for this quality is demonstrated by our love for his Son, who is "the exact likeness of [God's] invisible qualities." (Col. 1:15) Jesus showed his gratitude to his Father by zealously proclaiming the Kingdom message, so that people could learn about God's will and be freed from Satan's influence. And he continued to use his power to help people, just as the great Creator had done. (Matt. 4:10) Furthermore, on the night before his death, Jesus earnestly prayed to God and strengthened himself to carry out God's will. He said: "Father, if you are willing, please take away this cup from me; nevertheless, let your will, not mine, take place." (Luke 22:42) Let us imitate Jesus and zealously proclaim the good news, thus honoring Jehovah and supporting his worship! Is that not something truly worthwhile?
5 This is something worthwhile because we are made in God's image and likeness, and we have a desire to reflect His personality. (Gen. 1:26) So, let us continue to cultivate Christian qualities. By being loyal to Jehovah, we demonstrate our love for him and prove ourselves obedient. God's spirit can empower us to develop Christian qualities and help us apply what we learn from the Bible to our lives. For example, husbands should lovingly care for their wives, and wives should respectfully respond to their husbands. (Eph. 5:22; 6:1) How can we make sure that we continue to use our powers to serve Jehovah? One way is to remember that using our powers properly helps us avoid becoming self-sufficient or independent.
ALWAYS USE YOUR POWERS FOR GOOD AND HELP OTHERS DO THE SAME
6 Appreciate the privilege of cultivating Christian qualities.
6 Is developing Christian qualities a selfish pursuit, or does it benefit others? Of course, it benefits others! How can we show this? Because Christian qualities are attractive to people. Consider this illustration: Suppose someone wants to visit a beautiful garden. Would he be pleased to see weeds growing everywhere, or would he want to see well-maintained plants and flowers? Similarly, people are drawn to those who display lovable qualities, and they appreciate individuals who are considerate and kind. Therefore, my brothers, let us always cultivate Christian qualities so that others may see our good works and give glory to our Father in heaven. Let us understand that it is a privilege to use our powers to express our appreciation to Jehovah, just as did some ancient Christians.
7. (a) What is one lesson we can learn from Adam's mistake? (b) Explain how Adam misused his power of free will.
7 God created perfect man, Adam, and gave him the precious gift of free will, but Adam misused it when he disobeyed God's command. This misuse led Adam to make a wrong decision and forfeit his free will. To illustrate how Adam misused his free will, consider this example: A person is given a valuable possession. But because of selfishness, he abuses it. Jehovah allows each individual to choose whether to obey Him or disobey Him, but a disobedient person forfeits his privileges. And since God loves mankind, He has allowed humans to have "opportunity for repentance." Also, Adam lost all perfection and became imperfect, and Jehovah kindly provided a way for humans to regain what Adam had lost.—Gen. 2:19.
8. Why did Adam misuse his free will? Does this teach us something about life?
8 One reason why Adam misused his free will is that he was influenced by Satan's challenge to God's right to rule and by his desire to be independent. God commanded him: "Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and subdue it, and dominate over the fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens . . . , and over all living creatures that move on the earth." (Gen. 1:28) Humans, therefore, should appreciate the privilege of living under God's rule and use their free will to support what God approves. Adam misused his free will, and this resulted in much suffering for himself and his descendants for many years.—Acts 5:12. Seeing this regarding Adam helps us to better understand why we need to use our free will wisely, so that we can live up to the standards set by Jehovah.
9. What opportunity did Jehovah give ancient Israel, and does this teach us something?
9 After Adam and Eve disobeyed God, they experienced consequences, including death. However, even then, humans were given an opportunity to exercise free will. We see this when we consider how God dealt with ancient Israel. Jehovah sent his servant Moses to offer the Israelites a covenant based on obedience or disobedience. (Ex. 19:3-6) But what did they do? They showed that they were willing to do everything that God asked them to do and to obey his laws.—Ex. 19:8. So today, let us learn from their example and always strive to do what pleases Jehovah. Let us also remember that each decision we make affects our relationship with Jehovah and our ability to carry out his will.—1 Cor. 10:11.
10. How can we show that we value our freedom of choice and use it to honor God? (Consider the points in paragraph 12.)
10 On November 11, 1922, the Watch Tower Society released 16 volumes of Gods standard books, but we were encouraged to use them to help people learn about Jehovah's will. And because of this, we gained much comfort and encouragement and strengthened our confidence in the truth. For example, Noah had a strong conviction, so he was happy to preach the warning message that God gave him regarding the flood that would come upon the wicked world. (Gen. 11:7) Also, Abraham and Sarah obeyed God's command and showed faith in what He promised. They even went to a foreign land, and they had "a tent as an inheritance," like strangers residing in the land. Those who imitate them continue to seek their own inheritance, which is God's approval. I want to be like those who say, "I am a stranger and a temporary resident." (Gen. 11:8, 13, 15, 16) Another example is Moses. He told the Israelites, "Keep yourselves separate from the other peoples and from their gods, so that you may not become involved in their worship." (Gen. 11:24-26) We can see from these examples that people have always had to make choices about using their freedom of choice properly. We can show that we appreciate this freedom by making decisions that please God.
11. (a) How does appreciating our freedom of choice help us to maintain spiritual strength? (b) What can happen if we misuse our freedom of choice?
11 But remember that if someone tries to influence us to do something wrong, it could cause us to lose spiritual strength if we allow ourselves to be influenced by that person's thinking. This strength is mentioned at Hebrews 30:19, 20. (Read.) Verse 19 speaks of the hope that God gave ancient Israel. And verse 20 reminds us that Jehovah has the right to hold us accountable for how we respond to what we know is right. So let us continue to honor Jehovah. It is a great privilege to use our freedom of choice to get to know God better and to love and worship Him!
LET US USE OUR FREEDOM OF CHOICE WISELY
12. What will we discuss?
12 Consider this. Have you ever met someone who seems very persuasive, and you noticed that he doesn't really care whether his words are true or false, or perhaps he is trying to deceive you, and yet he influences others? Is there something about the way Jehovah views things that makes it easy for many people to be misled by deceptive teachings, or is it because they want to be? The Bible shows that in the last days, people would be "deceitful" and "easily led astray." (2 Tim. 3:1, 2) Let us examine ourselves to see if we are allowing ourselves to be influenced by those who misrepresent Jehovah's standards! Otherwise, how can we maintain our freedom of choice?
13. What is one way we can protect our freedom of choice?
13 We all enjoy freedom of choice, and we often use it when deciding what to eat or how to spend our time, and it is important that we continue to value it. But whether we realize it or not, our choices affect us by giving us "a taste of the consequences" – either helping us appreciate the good things in life or leading us into difficult situations. (Read 1 Peter 2:16.) Those who misuse their freedom of choice call it "an excuse for wrongdoing," so let us listen carefully and avoid being influenced to think that we should live according to the principle: "Let us do bad things in order to glorify God."—Acts 5:13; 1 Cor. 10:31.
14. How does loving Jehovah help us to safeguard our freedom of choice?
14 One way to show love for Jehovah is to use our freedom of choice to honor him and ask him to guide us so that we can make wise decisions. Jehovah is willing to 'give insight' and 'instruct' us in the right path. (Isa. 48:17) So let us be determined to cooperate with his guidance and remember this important truth: "The direction of a man's heart belongs to himself alone; directing his steps is up to the man who makes them." (Jer. 10:23) Let us strive to imitate those who showed great loyalty, such as Adam and the Israelites who obeyed God. Let us resolve to live according to the principle: "Love Jehovah with all your heart."—Deut. 3:5.
QUESTIONS FOR REVIEW AND FURTHER STUDY
15. What does Paul's statement at Colossians 6:5 teach us?
15 Sometimes Jehovah allows us to face trials so that we may demonstrate our loyalty. Why? Because faithful Christians prove their faith time and again, showing that they value their relationship with Jehovah. This also affects others around us and strengthens our confidence in Jehovah. Read Paul's statement at Colossians 6:5. (Read.) Determining whether each Christian "is carrying his own load" helps us to show consideration for the needs of others and support them spiritually.
16, 17. (a) How did the freedom of choice affect the Corinthians? (b) What example did Paul give, and what does this illustrate about the freedom of choice of others?
16 Consider how the Bible explains that humans were created with free will, allowing them to choose between right and wrong. At one time, some Christians in Corinth were struggling with the issue of eating meat offered to idols, but they felt free to eat it if they did not believe the idol was real. Some reasoned: 'An idol is nothing, so we can eat the meat without violating our conscience.' However, those Christians realized that their freedom could cause others to stumble. (1 Cor. 8:4, 7) So they voluntarily restricted their freedom out of love for their brothers. Did Paul expect those Christians in Corinth to know everything about God regarding this matter?
17 What Paul emphasized was the importance of considering the entire congregation and avoiding causing anyone to stumble. (1 Cor. 8:8) He also warned against taking advantage of "the liberty" we have to do things that might make "weak ones" stumble. (1 Cor. 8:9) And he reminded them that when they use their freedom, they should be careful not to offend others who may have a different conscience. (1 Cor. 10:25, 29, 30) This principle highlights the need for discernment; each Christian needs to examine his own conscience carefully. How can we apply this principle when dealing with matters that others find objectionable?—1 Cor. 10:32, 33.
18 Can you think of situations where showing consideration would be wise?
18 Jehovah gives us the guidance we need to show consideration, and this is what helps us to please him. (2 Cor. 3:17) We realize that this guidance is valuable because it helps us to speak in a way that will move people to respond favorably to God's message. Let us continue to look for ways to demonstrate our appreciation for this guidance by using it to give a fine witness and by speaking in a considerate way to those around us.

text:
"Klĩsto nake nĩwathĩniw'e kwondũ wenyu, aimũtiĩa ngelekan'yo, nĩ kana mũatĩĩae nyaĩĩ syake."
1. Nĩkĩ kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ kũtonya kũtuma tũmũthengeea Yeova mũnango?
MAVINDA maingĩ nĩtũtataa kwĩyĩelekany'a na andũ ala twonaa me na nguma nzeo na mekaa maũndũ ala twendete. Katĩ wa andũ ala maaĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ, Yesũ Klĩsto nĩwe waĩ ngelekany'o nzeo vyũ ĩla twaĩle kũatĩĩa. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya ũu? Nũndũ Yesũ mwene aisye atĩĩ: "Ũla wambonie nĩwamwonie Asa." (Yoa. 14:9) Yesũ atutĩtye Ĩthe wake vyũ, kwoou ĩla tweemanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yesũ wĩthĩaa no ta tũkwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa Yeova. Nũndũ wa ũu, ĩla twaatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ nĩtũmũthengeeaa Yeova mũnango, ũla nĩwe mũnene vyũ nthĩ yonthe. Nĩ ũathimo mũnene ta kĩ kũatĩĩaa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ na kwĩka maũndũ ala weekaa!
2, 3. (a) Nĩkĩ Yeova watũnengie ũvoo ũeleetye nesa vyũ ũndũ Mwana wake ũilyĩ, na endaa twĩke ata? (b) Twĩneenea kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ na yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
2 Ĩndĩ tũtonya ata kũmanya ũndũ Yesũ ũilyĩ? Ũseo nĩ kana twĩ na ũvoo mũveveee ũandĩkĩtwe ũla ũeleetye nesa vyũ ũndũ Yesũ ũilyĩ. Yeova nĩwatũnengie ũvoo ũsu waandĩkiwe Maandĩkonĩ ma Kĩkiliki ma Kĩklĩsto nũndũ nĩwendaa tũmanye nesa ũndũ Mwana wake ũilyĩ nĩ kana tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o yake. (Soma 1 Vetelo 2:21.) Nthĩnĩ wa Mbivilia, ngelekany'o ĩla Yesũ watũtiĩe ĩelekanĩtw'e na "nyaĩĩ" kana makinya. Kwa ndeto ingĩ, Yeova etwĩa tũmume Yesũ ĩtina na tũikinyĩla o vala wakinyĩle. Nũndũ Yesũ ndaĩ na naĩ, kwa w'o atũtiĩe ngelekany'o nzeo vyũ. Ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana Yeova endaa tũatĩĩe nyaĩĩ sya Yesũ tũteũvĩtya o na vanini. Vandũ va ũu, endaa tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ya Mwana wake nesa vyũ ũndũ tũtonya, o na kau twĩ andũ me na naĩ.
3 Kwoou, ekai yu tũneenee nguma imwe nzeo sya Yesũ. Ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ twĩneenea nguma yake ya wĩnyivyo na ya tei, na ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩneeneete nguma yake ya ũkũmbaũ na ya ũmanyi. Ĩla tũũneenea kĩla nguma tũkasũngĩaa makũlyo aa atatũ: Nguma ĩsu yonanasya kyaũ? Yesũ oonanisye nguma ĩsu ata? Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o yake ata?
YESŨ E WĨNYIVYO
4. Ũtonya kwasya wĩnyivyo nĩ kyaũ?
4 Wĩnyivyo nĩ kyaũ? Nũndũ andũ ũmũnthĩ me mĩtũlyo, amwe nĩmatonya kwĩsilya wĩnyivyo wonanasya kana mũndũ e na wonzu mũna, na kana ndethĩawa eyĩkĩĩe. Ĩndĩ ũu nĩ w'o? Aiee. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, wĩnyivyo wendaa mũndũ ethĩwe e na ũkũmbaũ na e na vinya. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yaĩtye kana wĩnyivyo nĩ "mũndũ kwĩthĩwa ate na mĩtũlyo na ngũlũ." Wĩnyivyo ũkonanĩtye na kwĩthĩwa twĩ na woni ũla waĩlĩte ĩũlũ witũ. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩeleetye ndeto sya Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "wĩnyivyo nĩ kũmanya ũndũ twĩ anini methonĩ ma Ngai." Kwoou ethĩwa nĩtwĩnyivasya, tũyaĩlĩte kwonaa twĩ ma vata mũno kwĩ andũ ala angĩ. (Alo. 12:3; Avi. 2:3) Vate nzika, ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwa andũ me na naĩ kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo. Ĩndĩ nĩtũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya ũndũ tũtonya kwĩthĩwa na wĩnyivyo twasũanĩa ũnene wa Ngai na twaatĩĩa nyaĩĩ sya Mwana wake.
5, 6. (a) Mikaeli ũla mũlaĩka mũnene nũũ? (b) Mikaeli oonanisye ata kana aĩ na wĩnyivyo?
5 Yesũ oonanisye ata kana aĩ na wĩnyivyo? Kwa ĩvinda ĩasa nĩwĩthĩĩtwe ayonany'a nguma ĩsu, ethĩwe nĩ ĩla waĩ kũũ nthĩ e mũndũ ũte na naĩ kana nĩ e ĩtunĩ e kyũmbe kĩ vinya kya veva. Ekai twone ngelekany'o imwe sya ũndũ wĩkĩte ũu.
6 Ũndũ wonaa maũndũ. Mũandĩki wa Mbivilia wĩtawa Yuta nũeleetye ngelekany'o ĩmwe ya ũndũ weekĩkie Yesũ atanoka kũũ nthĩ. (Soma Yuta 9.) Yesũ, ũla wĩtĩtwe Mikaeli, mũlaĩka ũla mũnene, 'nĩwakandanĩe na Ndevili' na 'akananĩa' nake. Makananĩaa "mwĩĩ wa Mose." Lilikana kana ĩtina wa Mose kũkw'a Yeova nĩwathikie mwĩĩ wake vandũ vatesĩkĩe. (Kũt. 34:5, 6) Nĩvatonyeka Ndevili akethĩwa endaa kũtũmĩa mwĩĩ wa Mose kũendeesya ũthaithi wa ũvũngũ. O na ethĩwa Ndevili aĩ na kĩeleelo kĩva, Mikaeli nĩwamũsiĩie e na ũkũmbaũ. Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩeleetye kana ndeto sya Kĩkiliki ila ialyũlĩtwe, "wakandanĩe" na "ũkananĩa" no "itũmĩkaa kwonany'a andũ me na ĩkoani" na no syonany'e "kana Mikaeli 'nĩwoonanisye kana Ndevili ndaaĩle' kwosa mwĩĩ wa Mose." Ĩndĩ Mũlaĩka ũsu Mũnene nĩwamanyie kana wĩa wa kũmũsilĩla ndwaĩ wake. Kwondũ wa ũu, nĩwaekeie Yeova, Mũsili Ũla Mũnene, ĩkoani yĩu. Kwĩka ũu kwoonanisye kana Mikaeli ndaaosa ũkũmũ ũte wake o na kau nĩwathatĩtw'e. Ĩsu nĩ ngelekany'o nzeo ta kĩ ya wĩnyivyo!
7. Ũneeni wa Yesũ na meko make syoonanisye ata kana e wĩnyivyo?
7 Ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ, nĩwaneenaa na akeka maũndũ kwa nzĩa yoonanasya kana aĩ na wĩnyivyo wa w'o. Ũndũ waneenaa. Yesũ ndaaenda anengwe ndaĩa ĩtamwaĩle. Vandũ va ũu, endaa nguma syonthe imũsyokee Ĩthe wake. (Mko. 10:17, 18; Yoa. 7:16) Ĩla waneenaa na amanyĩw'a make, ndamavũthasya kana akatuma mona ta mate ma vata. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, nĩwamanengae ndaĩa kwa kũmakatha nũndũ wa nguma syoo nzeo, na kwa kũmony'a kana nĩwamaĩkĩĩe. (Luka 22:31, 32; Yoa. 1:47) Ũndũ weekaa maũndũ. Yesũ anyuvie kwĩkala ate na mathĩmbĩĩĩ maingĩ ma syĩndũ sya kĩ-mwĩĩ. (Mt. 8:20) Nĩwatethasya na ngenda mawĩa ala moonekaa me ma kĩlasi kya nthĩ vyũ. (Yoa. 13:3-15) O na ĩngĩ nĩwoonanisye ngelekany'o nzeo vyũ ya wĩnyivyo kwa kwĩthĩwa e mwĩwi. (Soma Avilivi 2:5-8.) Yesũ ndaaĩka ta andũ me ngũlũ ala monaa kwĩw'a kũte kwa vata, vandũ va ũu eenyivisye eeka kĩla Ngai wendaa, "atw'ĩka mwĩwi, o na kũvika kĩkw'ũ." Vate nzika maũndũ asu meonany'a kana Yesũ, Mwana wa mũndũ, aĩ na "wĩnyivyo ngoonĩ"!—Mt. 11:29.
ATĨĨA NGELEKANY'O YA YESŨ YA WĨNYIVYO
8, 9. Tũtonya ata kwonany'a wĩnyivyo?
8 Tũtonya ata kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya wĩnyivyo? Ũndũ twonaa maũndũ. Wĩnyivyo nũtũsiĩĩaa tũikeyosee kĩvĩla kĩte kitũ. Twamanya kana tũi na ũkũmũ wa kũsilĩla ala angĩ, tũikethĩawa andũ ma kumany'a ala angĩ nũndũ wa mavĩtyo moo kana kwĩkala tũteũmaĩkĩĩa. (Luka 6:37; Yak. 4:12) Wĩnyivyo nũtũtetheeasya tũikethĩwe twĩ na "ũlũngalu mũvĩtũku" na kwoou tũyambĩĩa kũvũthya ala mate na ũtonyi mũna kana ianda ila twĩ nasyo. (Mũta. 7:16) Atumĩa ma kĩkundi ala methĩawa na wĩnyivyo mayonaa me ma kĩlasi kũte Aklĩsto ala angĩ. Vandũ va ũu, aĩthi asu 'matalaa ala angĩ ta aseo kwĩ mo ene' na nĩmekuaa ta ala anini.—Avi. 2:3; Luka 9:48.
9 Kwasũanĩa mwana-a-asa wĩtawa W. J. Thorn, ũla waĩ mũsyaĩĩsya wa kũthyũlũlũka kwambĩĩa mwaka wa 1894. Ĩtina wa kũthũkũma wĩa ũsu kwa myaka mingĩ nĩwathokiw'e akathũkũme Mũũndanĩ wa Ũsumbĩ ũla wĩ ngalĩko ya ĩũlũ ya New York, na anengwa wĩa wa kũthũkũma nyũmbanĩ ya ngũkũ. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ĩla nesa kwambĩĩa kwona ta nĩ wa vata mũno, nĩvindĩĩasya na ndyĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'We na wĩ o katolo kate va kaĩ, wĩĩkathĩĩa nĩ kyaũ yu?'" (Soma Isaia 40:12-15.) Mwa ũsu ko te mũndũ weenyivĩtye!
10. Ũneeni na meko maitũ itonya kwonany'a ata kana twĩ na wĩnyivyo?
10 Ũndũ tũneenaa. Ethĩwa nĩtwĩthĩawa twĩ na wĩnyivyo ngoonĩ, ũndũ ũsu ũkatũtetheesya tũneenae nesa na andũ ala angĩ. (Luka 6:45) Ĩla tũũneena namo tũkatataa ũndũ tũtonya tũikekathĩĩe nũndũ wa maũndũ ala twĩanĩĩtye kana maendeeo ala twĩkĩte. (Nth. 27:2) Vandũ va kwĩka ũu, nũseo tũkasiasya ũseo wa ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa na tũimakatha nũndũ wa nguma syoo nzeo, ũtonyi woo, na maũndũ ala meanĩĩtye. (Nth. 15:23) Ũndũ twĩkaa maũndũ. Aklĩsto ala menyivĩtye mayendeeaw'a nĩ kwĩmanthĩa monene ma nthĩ ĩno. Monaa nĩ kavaa makekala mate na syĩndũ mbingĩ, na maithũkũma wĩa ũla wonekaa wĩ wa kĩlasi kya nthĩ mũno nĩ kana mamũthũkũme Yeova kwa nzĩa ĩla yaĩlĩte vyũ. (1 Tim. 6:6, 8) Na ĩndĩ nzĩa ĩla ya vata vyũ ya kwonany'a wĩnyivyo nĩ kwĩthĩwa twĩ ewi. Nĩ kana mũndũ ethĩwe e 'mwĩwi kwa ala me na ũtongoi' kĩkundinĩ, na aiatĩĩa myolooto ĩla tũkwataa ũseũvyonĩ wa Yeova, no nginya ethĩwe e na wĩnyivyo.—Aevl. 13:17.
YESŨ E TEI
11. Tei nĩ kyaũ? Elesya.
11 Tei nĩ kyaũ? Ndeto "tei" yonanasya "kũthĩnĩkĩa mũndũ kwa ĩnee, kana kũmwĩw'ĩa ĩnee." Kwĩw'ĩa mũndũ tei nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kũmwony'a kana nũmwendete. Maandĩko mawetaa kana Yeova na Yesũ nĩmatwĩw'ĩaa "ĩnee ĩnene," "matei," na "matei mololo." (Luka 1:78; 2 Ako. 1:3; Avi. 1:8) Ĩvuku yĩmwe yĩiweta ĩũlũ wa mwĩao ũla wĩ Maandĩkonĩ wa kwĩthĩwa na tei yaisye atĩĩ: "Mwĩao ũsu ndwĩthĩawa o ĩũlũ wa kwĩw'ĩa andũ ala me na thĩna tei. Nĩ mwĩao wa kũmathĩnĩkĩa ũndũ tũtonya, kwĩyosa ta uwe wĩ na thĩna ũsu me naw'o, na kwosa ĩtambya ya kũmatetheesya maendeee nesa mate na thĩna." Kwoou tei nĩ vinya ũtũsukumaa twose ĩtambya yĩla yaĩle. Mũndũ wĩ tei nĩwĩthĩnasya atetheesye ala angĩ mathĩnanĩ moo.
12. Nĩ kyaũ kĩkwonany'a kana Yesũ nĩweew'ĩaa andũ angĩ tei, na tei watumaa eka ata?
12 Nĩ kwa nzĩa syĩkũ Yesũ woonanisye tei? Meko make, na ũndũ weew'ĩaa andũ tei. Yesũ nĩweew'ĩaa andũ ala angĩ tei. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla woonie mũnyanyae ũla weetawa Meli vamwe na ala maĩ nake maiĩa nũndũ wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mwana-a-inyia wa Meli, Lasalo, 'Yesũ nĩwaĩie' ũtheinĩ. (Soma Yoana 11:32-35.) Na ĩndĩ athayũũkya Lasalo nũndũ wa tei o ta ũla watumie athayũũkya ũla mwanake wa kĩveti ndiwa. (Luka 7:11-15; Yoa. 11:38-44) Nũndũ wa ũndũ ũsu woonanisye tei, Yesũ nũtonya kwĩthĩwa atumie Lasalo ethĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩsa kũthi ĩtunĩ. O na ve ĩvinda yĩngĩ mbee wa vau, Yesũ 'weew'ĩie andũ tei' ĩla mookie vala waĩ. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩwasukumiwe nĩ tei na "ambĩlĩlya kũmamanyĩsya maũndũ maingĩ." (Mko. 6:34) No nginya wĩthĩe ũndũ ũsu watetheeisye mũno andũ ala maatĩĩe momanyĩsyo make. Maũndũ asu metũĩkĩĩthya nesa kana Yesũ ndeekaa o kwĩw'ĩa andũ tei, ĩndĩ nĩwoosaa ĩtambya ya kũmatetheesya.—Mt. 15:32-38; 20:29-34; Mko. 1:40-42.
13. Nĩ kwa nzĩa yĩva Yesũ woonanisye kana nĩwaneenaa na ala angĩ na tei? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 5.)
13 Ndeto syake sya tei. Nũndũ Yesũ aĩ na ngoo nzeo, nĩwaneenaa na andũ ala angĩ kwa nzĩa yoonanasya kana nĩwamew'ĩaa tei, na mũno mũno ala mooneawa. Ĩla mũtũmwa Mathayo waandĩkie ndeto kuma ĩvukunĩ ya Isaia, nĩwoonanisye kana syakonetye Yesũ. Aandĩkie: "Mũangi mũkanyange ndakatũla, na ũtambi ũtoaa syũki ndakavosya." (Isa. 42:3; Mt. 12:20) Yesũ aneenaa kwa nzĩa yeekĩaa vinya ala mailyĩ ta mũangi mũkanyange kana ũtambi wa taa ũkilyĩ kũvoa. Eekaa ũu kwa kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo ũla watumie andũ aingĩ methĩwa na wĩkwatyo, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu 'oova ala maĩ na ngoo ndũlĩku.' (Isa. 61:1) O na nĩwathokisye ala 'mathĩnĩaa wĩa na ala maĩ na mĩio mĩito,' na amaĩkĩĩthya kana mooka kwake 'makasyonea ngoo syoo ũthũmũo.' (Mt. 11:28-30) O na ĩngĩ Yesũ nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye amanyĩw'a make kana Ngai nĩwĩw'ĩaa kĩla ũmwe wa athaithi make tei, o na 'tũla tũnini,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, ala monekaa ta mate ma vata.—Mt. 18:12-14; Luka 12:6, 7.
ATĨĨA NGELEKANY'O YA YESŨ YA TEI
14. Tũtonya kwambĩĩa ata kwĩw'ĩa ala angĩ tei?
14 Tũtonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya Yesũ ya kwĩw'ĩa angĩ tei? Kwĩw'ĩa angĩ tei. Ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kwĩw'ĩa angĩ tei, ĩndĩ Mbivilia nĩtwĩkĩaa vinya tũtate ũndũ tũtonya twĩke ũu. Nũndũ kwĩthĩwa na "ngoo yĩ na ĩnee ya kwĩw'anĩa tei" nĩ nzĩa ĩmwe ya kwĩvw'ĩka mũndũ mweũ, Aklĩsto onthe maĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa nayo. (Soma Akolosai 3:9, 10, 12.) Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ atĩĩ, Tũtonya kwambĩĩa ata kwĩw'ĩa ala angĩ tei? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana twaĩle kũnenevya ngoo sitũ. (2 Ako. 6:11-13) Kwoou, ĩthukĩĩasye nesa ĩla mũndũ ũkũũtavya kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ na kĩla kĩũmũthĩny'a. (Yak. 1:19) Ĩkũlye atĩĩ, 'Keka ninyie nĩ thĩnanĩ ũsu nĩw'a ata? Nĩthĩwa ndyenda ũtethyo wĩva?'—1 Vet. 3:8.
15. Tũtonya kwĩka ata nĩ kana tũtetheesye andũ ala mailyĩ ta mũangi mũkanyange kana ũtambi ũũtoa syũki?
15 Meko maitũ ma tei. Tei nũtumaa twenda kũtetheesya andũ ala me na thĩna na mũno mũno ala mekwoneka mailyĩ ta mũangi mũkanyange kana ũtambi ũũtoa syũki. Tũtonya kũmatetheesya ata? Ĩandĩko ya Alomi 12:15 yaĩtye ũũ: "Ĩai na ala mekũĩa." Ala makw'ĩte ngoo nĩmatonya kwĩthĩwa me na vata wa kwĩw'ĩwa tei mũno kwĩ ala angĩ. Mwĩĩtu-a-asa ũmwe ũla wakiakiw'e nĩ Aklĩsto ala angĩ ĩtina wa kũkw'ĩĩwa nĩ mwĩĩtu wake easya atĩĩ: "Neewie mũyo mũno ĩla anyanyawa mookie na mambĩĩa kũĩa nakwa." O naitũ nĩtũtonya kwĩw'ĩa angĩ tei kwa kũmeka maũndũ ma tei. We nĩwĩsĩ mũndũ mũka ndiwa wĩthĩwa ayenda kũseũvĩw'a vandũ mũsyĩ kwake? We nĩwĩsĩ Mũklĩsto mũkũũ ũtonya kwĩthwa ayenda kũtwaawa ũmbanonĩ, ũtavany'anĩ, kana sivitalĩ? O na tũmaũndũ tũnini nĩtũtonya kũtetheesya mũno ala tũthaithaa namo. (1 Yoa. 3:17, 18) Na ĩndĩ nzĩa ĩla nene vyũ ya kwĩw'ĩa andũ tei nĩ kũmatavya ũvoo mũseo. Vai nzĩa ĩngĩ ĩvĩtũkĩte ĩsu ya kũtetheesya ala me na ngoo nthalĩku.
16. Tũtonya kũtũmĩa ndeto syĩkũ tũmekĩe vinya ala makw'ĩte ngoo?
16 Ndeto sitũ sya tei. Kwĩw'ĩa ala angĩ tei nĩkũtumaa 'tũmekĩa vinya ala me na ngoo mbũthũ.' (1 Ath. 5:14) Tũtonya kũtũmĩa ndeto syĩkũ tũmekĩe vinya? No twĩke ũu kwa kũmony'a kana nĩtũmathĩnĩkĩaa mũno. Nĩtũtonya kũmakatha kuma ngoonĩ nĩ kana tũmatetheesye mone nguma syoo nzeo na ũtonyi woo. O na no tũmalilikany'e kana Yeova nĩwe wamakusisye amaete kũla kwĩ Mwana wake, na kwoou no nginya methĩwe me ma vata kwake. (Yoa. 6:44) Nĩtũtonya kũmaĩkĩĩthya kana kwa w'o Yeova nũthĩnĩkĩaa athũkũmi make ala "matũlĩkĩte ngoo" na ala "mekwĩlila vevanĩ." (Sav. 34:18) Kwoou, ndeto sitũ sya tei nitonya kũtetheesya ala me na vata wa kũkiakiw'a.—Nth. 16:24.
17, 18. (a) Yeova endaa atumĩa ma kĩkundi masũvĩe malondu make ata? (b) Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩneeneete kyaũ?
17 Atumĩa ma kĩkundi, manyai kana Yeova endaa mũthĩnĩkĩe malondu make mwĩ na tei. (Meko 20:28, 29) Lilikanai kana nĩ kĩanda kyenyu kũmaĩthya, kũmathangaasya, na kũmathũmũsya. (Isa. 32:1, 2; 1 Vet. 5:2-4) Kwoou mũtumĩa wĩ tei ndatataa kwĩaĩa malondu kwa kũmekĩĩa mĩao ĩte vo, kana kũmony'a me na mavĩtyo nĩ kana amasukume meke maũndũ matatonya. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, atataa ũndũ ũtonya amatanĩthye, na ayĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo kana nũndũ malondu nĩmendete Yeova nĩmeũmũthũkũma vyũ ũndũ matonya.—Mt. 22:37.
18 Kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa wĩnyivyo na tei ũla Yesũ wĩthĩawa naw'o kũkatũsukuma tũkinyĩlae vala wakinyĩle. Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩneeneete nguma ingĩ ilĩ sya Yesũ, nasyo nĩ ũkũmbaũ na ũmanyi.

translation:
"Christ has been made subject to you by God, so that you may prove faithful, even though he was perfect."
1. Why should we be zealous to imitate Jesus' example in order to honor Jehovah?
MANY people find it difficult to associate with others because they have been hurt by those around them. Some have had bad experiences with relatives, while others have been disappointed by friends. In view of this, Jesus Christ is often the best example we can imitate. How can we do so? Jesus himself said: "If you have seen me, you have seen the Father also." (John 14:9) Jesus showed us what his Father is like, and through learning about Jesus, we come to know Jehovah better. Therefore, when we imitate Jesus' example, we are actually honoring Jehovah, who is the greatest Person in the universe. What a privilege it is to imitate Jesus and to reflect his qualities!
2, 3. (a) How did Jehovah show his love for his Son, and what can we learn from this? (b) What will help us to remain loyal when we face trials?
2 Why is it important for us to understand what Jesus experienced? Because understanding what Jesus went through helps us to appreciate why he is such a wonderful Example. Jehovah allowed his beloved Son to experience suffering, and he recorded an account of it in the Holy Scriptures so that we might learn to value the sacrifice his Son made. (Read 1 Peter 2:21.) The Bible shows that Jesus' example involves "suffering." More than that, Jehovah empowered Jesus to endure and gave him support. So Jesus could demonstrate perfect loyalty. It is therefore reasonable that Jehovah expects us to be loyal to Jesus, even when things are difficult. We must remember that showing loyalty to the Son is vital to our relationship with Jehovah and with fellow believers.
3 Now let us examine some specific examples of Jesus' loyalty. Let us consider how he acted under both favorable and unfavorable circumstances, and let us analyze how he demonstrated loyalty in times of comfort and times of difficulty. As we examine each example, ask yourself these questions: What lesson does this illustrate? Did Jesus show loyalty in this situation? How can we imitate his example?
JESUS AS AN EXAMPLE
4 What does it mean to be loyal?
4 What does loyalty mean? Often people claim to be loyal, yet they may be disloyal in their thoughts, words, or deeds. Why is this so? Because loyalty involves more than just feelings. True loyalty moves a person to act in accordance with what he believes. For instance, someone might say that loyalty means "being devoted to others despite difficulties." Loyalty requires us to remain devoted to our friends even when they disappoint us. Another definition states that loyalty is "understanding the truth about God." We often speak of being loyal when we see good qualities in others. (Prov. 12:3; Ps. 2:3) However, true loyalty goes beyond mere recognition of another's worthiness. It compels us to support those who demonstrate loyalty to God and to obey his commands.
5, 6. (a) Who is Michael the archangel? (b) In what way did Michael display loyalty?
5 Did Jesus display loyalty? On several occasions, he showed himself obedient to his Father, even when it meant facing difficult circumstances. Let us now examine some examples of his loyalty.
6 This will help you understand. The Bible writer Jude explains how Jesus was loyal to his Father. (Read Jude 9.) Jesus, who is Michael the archangel, "disputed with the Devil" and "condemned" him. That condemnation was like "the law of Moses." Just as obedience to Moses' Law demonstrated loyalty to Jehovah, so too did obedience to Jehovah's direction demonstrate loyalty to Him. (Ex. 34:5, 6) The Devil rebelled against God and tried to use the law of Moses to mislead people. But because the Devil had no legitimate basis for his claims, Michael powerfully refuted them. One ancient manuscript actually reads, "disputed" and "condemned," and also "used the law against people and their error," and also shows that "Michael 'disputed with the Devil and judged' according to the law of Moses." Indeed, this great Archangel knew how to defend his position in court. Because of this, give glory to Jehovah, the Most High Sovereign, and your support. In this way, show yourself loyal to Michael and support his righteous work. We can learn much from his example of loyalty!
7 What qualities of Jesus and his disciples show us what loyalty means?
7 But Jesus knew beforehand, he revealed it and explained matters in such a way as to test whether they had faith. He revealed it. Jesus went off alone to pray. And those people, went up to the temple together. (Mark 10:17, 18; John 7:16) But he revealed it and told them about his trials, so that when the time came, they might remember what he said about himself. (Luke 22:31, 32; John 1:47) He showed them things. Jesus was willing to be among many imperfect humans. (Matt. 8:20) He demonstrated his love for them by washing their feet. (John 13:3-15) Also, he foretold very clearly what trials they would face because of their faith. (Read Proverbs 2:5-8.) Jesus did not hide from those people, but allowed them to see his humility, and those people realized that God wants us to say, "I will be humble, and I will be obedient." They understood this lesson well, realizing that Jesus, the Son of Man, had "faithfulness" indeed!—Matt. 11:29.
THE IMPORTANCE OF JESUS' FAITHFULNESS
8, 9. How can we imitate faithfulness?
8 How can we show appreciation for Jesus' faithfulness? We should learn lessons. Faithfulness does not mean that we have no weaknesses at all. We realize that we have a tendency to stumble, we need to ask others who know us well for advice regarding our shortcomings. (Luke 6:37; James 4:12) Faithfulness does not excuse us from asking for help and being helped by "wise counsel" and allowing it to assist us in doing right with sincerity and honesty. (Proverbs 7:16) Let us learn from groups who demonstrate faithfulness in serving fellow Christians. Those people, should not 'look down on others because they are different' and become proud.—Acts 2:3; Luke 9:48.
9 Consider the example of Brother W. J. Thorn, who began his ministry in 1894. After years of struggling with poor health, he was assigned to serve in the Watch Tower Society's headquarters in Brooklyn, New York, and worked in the printing department. He said: "I felt so inadequate, yet I reasoned: 'If I am just a little drop of water, still I can join with others to form a great ocean.'" (Read Isaiah 40:12-15.) What a humble attitude!
10. What will help us to imitate faithfulness?
10 We need to be realistic. Often we feel inadequate, but this does not excuse us from doing our best to support God's organization and to cooperate with our brothers. (Luke 6:45) However, we should also be realistic about what we can accomplish and avoid taking on too much responsibility. (Prov. 27:2) For instance, we might limit our secular work so that we have more time for spiritual activities, such as preparing for meetings, engaging in the field ministry, and helping others. (Prov. 15:23) Let us be reasonable. Many faithful Christians find that maintaining neutrality is a real challenge, especially when faced with strong nationalistic sentiments or economic pressures. (1 Tim. 6:6, 8) And often the greatest test of our loyalty comes within our own family. It may be that someone feels that we are being 'disloyal to relatives' because we uphold Jehovah's standards, but we must remain loyal to Jehovah.—Acts 13:17.
JESUS IS THE ANSWER
11. What is the answer? Jesus.
11 What is the answer? The term "answer" conveys the idea of "responding to someone's needs or feelings." Responding to someone favorably is one way to show love or appreciation. The Scriptures show that Jehovah and Jesus respond to us in a loving way, using expressions like "loving-kindness," "mercy," and "great mercy." (Luke 1:78; 2 Cor. 1:3; Ps. 1:8) One publication explains how the expression "answer" applies to them by saying: "Their response is an expression of their deep love for people and their desire to help them. It is an expression of their willingness to forgive sins, to give comfort, and to restore those who turn to them." How does responding favorably benefit us? It strengthens our faith and encourages us to continue serving Jehovah.
12. Why does Jesus respond favorably to others, and why does he not always intervene directly?
12 Why did Jesus demonstrate such compassion? Perhaps because he understands what they are going through. Jesus responds favorably to people. For example, when he saw Martha and her sister Mary mourning over their brother Lazarus, he was deeply moved. (Read John 11:32-35.) And he felt sympathy for the widow at Nain when she mourned over her only son. (Luke 7:11-15; John 11:38-44) Because of his compassionate response, Jesus was willing to resurrect Lazarus and relieve his suffering. On another occasion, Jesus 'felt sorry' for the large crowds who were like sheep without a shepherd, and he taught them extensively. (Mark 6:34) As a result, many people benefited from his instruction. These examples show that Jesus cares about people and wants to help them, and they strengthen our faith.—Matt. 15:32-38; 20:29-34; Mark 1:40-42.
13 In what ways did Jesus show that he cared for others and had compassion? (Consider paragraph 5.)
13 His Father showed compassion. But Jesus also had deep feeling and showed compassion for people because he knew they were like sheep without a shepherd, and often they were misled. However, Matthew wrote down a statement from Isaiah which described how Jesus would be. He wrote: "The meek One I will fortify, and my servant I will exalt." (Is. 42:3; Matt. 12:20) Jesus acted in this way to fulfill what was said about the meek One and his servant who would bring good news. He did so to demonstrate God's purpose to use many people and to gather them together, and for the reason that he 'would not extinguish a smoldering wick.' (Is. 61:1) And he assured them that 'he would refresh those wearied ones,' and he proved that his yoke was 'easy and his burden light.' (Matt. 11:28-30) Also, Jesus showed his followers that God cares for each one of his creatures, and that 'even the smallest detail' is important to him—as shown by the value he placed on lost sheep.—Matt. 18:12-14; Luke 12:6, 7.
JESUS' EXAMPLE OF COMPASSION
14 Why should we try to imitate Jesus' compassion?
14 Why should we strive to show compassion like Jesus did? Because imitating Jesus' example is vital. If we do not show compassion, the Bible teaches us that we do not reflect the qualities we should have. For instance, being clothed with "tender affection" is one way to prove ourselves to be Christians who are truly clothed with the new personality. (Read Colossians 3:9, 10, 12.) Therefore, why should we try to imitate Jesus' compassion? The Bible says that we need to control our emotions. (2 Cor. 6:11-13) So, practice being quick to listen and slow to speak. (Jas. 1:19) Remember, 'Are you willing to forgive others?'—1 Pet. 3:8.
15 How can we show compassion toward those who are afflicted or troubled?
15 Let us consider some examples. It is not because we want to appear compassionate or righteous that we should feel sorry for others who are suffering. Can we show compassion? Romans 12:15 urges us to "rejoice with those rejoicing." Rejoicing with others means showing sympathy when they are happy. One Christian elder explained what he learned from his own experience: "I realized that I needed to share their joy." Of course, we can show compassion without necessarily agreeing with everything they do. But how can a loving person help someone who is making poor choices? And how can a true Christian avoid becoming judgmental, critical, or self-righteous? Often, we can help others by offering practical assistance. (1 John 3:17, 18) Also, remember that showing compassion does not mean condoning wrong behavior. There are times when we must take a firm stand against wrongdoing.
16 How can we use our resources to help those in need?
16 Our resources are limited. Showing compassion toward others does not require us to "give away all we have." (Acts 5:14) So how can we use our resources wisely? Well, we can examine ourselves to see if we are being generous. We can ask ourselves whether we are using our time and energy to help others. And we can remind ourselves that Jehovah has given his Son the greatest gift imaginable. (John 6:44) We can strengthen our faith in Jehovah by trusting that he will support us and guide us. (Ps. 34:18) Thus, our resources are sufficient to show compassion to those in need.—Prov. 16:24.
17, 18. (a) Does Jehovah expect us to be perfect in the way we extend help? (b) What lesson does the illustration highlight?
17 He does not expect perfection from us. Remember that Jehovah is patient and understanding. (Acts 20:28, 29) Be willing to listen, encourage, and comfort others. (Isa. 32:1, 2; 1 Pet. 5:2-4) As a loving shepherd, he doesn't demand that we solve all problems or know all the answers. Instead, he encourages us to seek his guidance and to rely on him for strength.—Matt. 22:37.
18 By imitating Jesus' example of showing compassion, we can touch people's hearts. The illustration highlights an important aspect of Jesus' ministry—his empathy and knowledge.

text:
"Maũndũ ala weewie kwakwa . . . , maie kwa andũ me na kĩthito."—2 TIM. 2:2.
1. (a) Athũkũmi ma Ngai kuma tene matũaa mesĩ kyaũ ĩũlũ wa kũmanyĩsya angĩ, na ũndũ ũsu ũkonanĩtye ata na ĩvinda yitũ? (b) Twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
KUMA tene athũkũmi ma Ngai nĩmethĩawa mesĩ kana kũmanyĩsya mũndũ nĩkũetae moseo. Kwa ngelekany'o, ve ĩvinda mũtumĩa ũmwe wa tene weetawa Avalamu 'waumisye andũ make ala wamamanyĩĩtye' mathi makamwĩtaane Loto, na andũ asu nĩmavotie kũmwĩtaana. (Mwa. 14:14-16) Ĩvindanĩ ya Mũsumbĩ Ndaviti, aini ma nyũmba ya Ngai 'nĩmamanyĩĩtw'e kũmwinĩa Yeova,' na ũu nĩwamũeteae ũ Yeova ngatho. (1 Mav. 25:7) Naitũ matukũ aa nĩtũkitaa na Satani na aatĩĩi make. (Aev. 6:11-13) O na ĩngĩ nĩtwĩkĩaa kĩthito kingĩ mũno nĩ kana tũtume Yeova akwata ngatho. (Aevl. 13:15, 16) Kwoou o ta athũkũmi ma Ngai ma ĩvinda ya tene, nĩtwaĩlĩte kũmanyĩw'a nĩ kana tũvote kwĩanĩsya maũndũ asu. Yeova anengete atumĩa wĩa wa kũmanyĩsya ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ. (2 Tim. 2:2) Atumĩa ala me na ũmanyi matũmĩaa nzĩa syĩva kũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa methĩwe matonya kũkwatĩĩa maũndũ kĩkundinĩ?
TETHEESYA MŨMANYĨW'A AMWENDE YEOVA MŨNANGO
2. Mũtumĩa atonya kũtw'a kwĩka ata atanamba kũmanyĩsya mũmanyĩw'a mawĩa mana, na nĩkĩ?
2 Ethĩwa wĩ mũtumĩa wa kĩkundi no tũkũelekany'e na mũĩmi. Mũĩmi atanamba kũvanda mũũnda wake, nũtonya kwona waĩle kwamba kwĩkĩwa vũũ nĩ kana wĩthĩwe wĩ mũnou. O ta ũu, ũtanamba kũmanyĩsya mwana-a-asa ũte na ũmanyi mwingĩ, no wone ve vata wa kũmwony'a maũndũ amwe ma kwaka me Maandĩkonĩ nĩ kana wĩthĩe nũtonya kũkwatya nesa ĩla ũkwĩsa kwĩthĩwa ũimũmanyĩsya.—1 Tim. 4:6.
3. (a) Mũtumĩa atonya kũtũmĩa ata ndeto sya Yesũ ila syĩ nthĩnĩ wa Maliko 12:29, 30 ĩla ũkũea ngewa na mũmanyĩw'a? (b) Mũmanyĩw'a atonya kũtetheka ata ĩla mũtumĩa wavoya vamwe nake?
3 Nĩ kana ũmanye ũvoo wa Ũsumbĩ ũalyũlĩte mesilya na meko ma mũmanyĩw'a mũno wĩana ata, no ũmũkũlye-ĩ, 'Ĩtina wa kwĩyumya ũmũthũkũme Yeova wĩkaa motwi mailyĩ ata?' Kũmũkũlya ũu nĩkũtonya kũmũnenga inywelĩ mwanya mũseo wa kũneenea ũndũ mũndũ ũtonya kũmũthũkũma Yeova na ngoo yonthe. (Soma Maliko 12:29, 30.) Mwamina kũea ngewa ta isu, nũtonya kũmũvoya Yeova anenge mũmanyĩw'a veva mũtheu nĩ kana veva ũsu ũmũtetheesye kũkwatya nesa kyonthe kĩla ũkwĩsa kũmũmanyĩsya. We wĩona mwana-a-asa ũsu ta ũtonya kwĩkĩwa vinya mũno wĩana ata eew'a ũivoya kuma ngoonĩ kwondũ wake?
4. (a) Weta ngewa imwe syĩ Mbivilianĩ ila itonya kũtetheesya mũmanyĩw'a eke maendeeo mĩtũkĩ. (b) Atumĩa methĩawa na kĩeleelo kĩva ĩla meũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa ala angĩ?
4 Wambĩĩa kũmanyĩsya mwana-a-asa oou, sũanĩa vamwe nake ngewa imwe syĩ Mbivilianĩ ila itonya kũmũtetheesya ethĩwe e na mea ma kũmanyĩw'a, atonya kwĩkwatw'a, na enyivĩtye. (1 Asu. 19:19-21; Nee. 7:2; 13:13; Meko 18:24-26) Nguma ta isu nĩ sya vata ĩla mwana-a-asa ũkũmanyĩw'a o tondũ vũũ wĩthĩawa wĩ wa vata mũũndanĩ. Nĩkĩ? Nitetheeasya mũndũ eke maendeeo mĩtũkĩ. Mũtumĩa wĩ France wĩtawa Jean-Claude easya ũũ: "Kĩeleelo kyakwa ĩla ngũmanyĩsya mũndũ nĩ kũmũtetheesya ende mũno maũndũ ma kĩ-veva. Nĩkalaa nĩmanthanĩte na kamwanya ka kwony'a mũmanyĩw'a maandĩko mana ala matonya 'kũsalukya metho' make mone 'maũndũ ma ũsengy'a' ala me Ndetonĩ ya Ngai." (Sav. 119:18) Nĩ nzĩa ingĩ syĩva ũtonya kũtũmĩa ũkekĩa mũmanyĩw'a vinya?
MŨTAVYE KĨLA ŨTONYA KWĨVANGĨĨA NA ŨIMŨELESYA NĨKĨ
5. (a) Ve vata mwaũ wa kũneena na mũmanyĩw'a ĩũlũ wa kĩla ũvangĩte kwĩanĩsya ũthũkũminĩ wa Yeova? (b) Nĩkĩ atumĩa maĩle kũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa ala me na myaka mĩnini? (Sisya maelesyo ma kwongeleela.)
5 No ũkũlye mũmanyĩw'a atĩĩ: 'Wĩ na mĩvango myaũ ĩkonetye kũmũthũkũma Yeova?' Ethĩwa nde na mũvango o na ũmwe kĩlĩkonĩ, no ũmũtetheesye evangĩĩe kwĩka ũndũ ũmwaĩle na ũtonya kwĩanĩsya. Mũtavye ũndũ mũna we mwene wevangĩĩie kwĩka, na ũimũelesya mũyo ũla weewie ĩla wesie kũwĩanĩsya. Ũimũtavya kĩu ndũkethĩwe ũtukĩtye ũthyũ. O na kau nzĩa ĩsu nĩtonya kwoneka ta nzĩa ĩte vala yĩĩ, no ĩtethye mũno. Mũtumĩa wĩtawa Victor, ũla wĩthĩawa e vainia nthĩ yĩ Africa, awetete atĩĩ: "Nĩ mũnini ve mũtumĩa mũna wangũlilye tũmakũlyo tũseo mũno ĩũlũ wa mĩvango yakwa. Tũkũlyo tu twatumie nambĩĩa kũsũanĩa mũno ĩũlũ wa ũthũkũmi wakwa." Atumĩa me na ũmanyi nĩmawetaa kana ve vata mũnene wa kwambĩĩa kũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa me o ma mũika kwa kũmaaĩa mawĩa kĩkundinĩ ala meanĩe myaka yoo. No mambĩĩe kũmanyĩw'a o na ethĩwa me na myaka mĩnini. Wambĩanĩa namo tene ũu, makekalaa malilikene kĩla mavangie kwĩanĩsya, o na meananga na mambĩĩa kũkomana na maũndũ me vinya.—Soma Savuli 71:5, 17. *
6. Nĩ ũndũ wĩva wa vata Yesũ weekaa ĩla ũkũmanyĩsya andũ?
6 Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kwĩka ũtetheesye mũmanyĩw'a ethĩwe na wendi wa kũthũkũma kĩkundinĩ nĩ kũmũelesya wĩa ũla ũtonya kũtethya vamwe na kĩtumi kya kũtethya wĩa ũsu. Wamũelesya itumi sya kũtethya wĩa ũla wamũnenga, ũkeethĩwa watutya ũla Mwalimũ Mũnene, nake nĩ Yesũ. Kwa ngelekany'o, Yesũ atanamba kũnenga atũmwa make wĩa wa kũtw'ĩkĩthya andũ amanyĩw'a, ambie kũmanenga kĩtumi kya kũtethya wĩa ũsu. Ambie kũmea: "Nĩnĩnengetwe ũkũmũ w'onthe ĩtunĩ na kũũ nthĩ." Na ĩndĩ asyoka amatavya atĩĩ: "Endai ĩndĩ mũkatw'ĩkĩthye mbaĩ syonthe amanyĩw'a." (Mt. 28:18, 19) Ũtonya ata kũatĩĩa nzĩa ĩsu ya Yesũ ya kũmanyĩsya?
7, 8. (a) Atumĩa matonya kũatĩĩa ata nzĩa ya Yesũ ya kũmanyĩsya? (b) Ve vata mwaũ wa kũkatha mũmanyĩw'a? (c) Nĩ maũndũ meva matonya kũtetheesya atumĩa ĩla meũmanyĩsya angĩ? (Sisya ĩsandũkũ "Ũndũ Ũtonya Kũmanyĩsya Angĩ.")
7 Ĩla wanenga mũmanyĩw'a wĩa mũna, tũmĩa Maandĩko ũmũelesye nĩkĩ wĩa ũsu nĩ wa vata. Weeka ũu, ũkeethĩwa wamũtetheesya amanye kwĩka maũndũ aatĩĩe myolooto ya Mbivilia ĩndĩ ti aatĩĩe mĩao. Kwa ngelekany'o, twasye nĩwanenga mwana-a-asa mũna wĩa wa kũtheasya kasĩla kala kalikĩte Nyũmbanĩ ya Ũsumbĩ, wĩthĩe o na mũndũ ndaũmĩa esĩle vo. No mũsũanĩe vamwe ĩandĩko ya Tito 2:10, na ũimũelesya ũndũ wĩa ta ũsu wa kũthesya Nyũmba ya Ũsumbĩ 'ũkanakavasya ũmanyĩsyo wa Ngai Mũtangĩĩi waitũ.' Ũndũ ũngĩ ũtonya kwĩka nĩ kũmũlilikany'a ĩũlũ wa andũ ala akũũ me kĩkundinĩ, na ũimũtetheesya one ũndũ kũkũna wĩa ũsu kũtonya kũmatetheesya. Kũneenea maũndũ ta asu ĩla ũũmũmanyĩsya nĩkũtonya kũmũtetheesya asũanĩe mũno mũno ũndũ wĩa ũsu ũũtethya andũ vandũ va kwonaa no mĩao ũkwĩanĩsya. Kĩu kĩkatuma atanĩa mũno kwona ũndũ wĩa wake ũũtethya ana-a-asa na eĩtu-a-asa kĩkundinĩ.
8 O na ĩngĩ ndũkolwe nĩ kũmũkatha nũndũ wa kĩthito kyake kya kũtũmĩa maũndũ ala ũũmũtavya. Ve vata mwaũ wa kwĩka ũu? O tondũ mũtĩ wang'ithw'a ũsanzamũkaa na ũiana, kũkatha mũmanyĩw'a kuma ngoonĩ nĩkũtumaa eka maendeeo.—Sianĩsya na Mathayo 3:17.
ŨNDŨ ŨNGĨ ŨETAE THĨNA
9. (a) Nĩ thĩna wĩva atumĩa ala mekalaa nthĩ ila nthwii makomanaa naw'o ĩla mekwenda kũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa? (b) Nĩkĩ ana-a-asa amwe ma mũika mataaĩsa kwona kũmũthũkũma Ngai kwĩ kwa vata mũno thayũnĩ woo?
9 Atumĩa ala mekalaa nthĩ ila nthwii nĩmakomanaa na ũndũ ũngĩ ũetae thĩna. Nĩmatonya kwaĩwa nĩ ũndũ meũtetheesya ana-a-asa ala me na myaka 20 na kĩndũ na 30 na kĩndũ methĩwe na wendi wa kũtetheesya mawĩa kĩkundinĩ. Twakũlilye atumĩa me na ũmanyi mwingĩ kuma nthĩ 20 sya Europe na sya Amelika ya Ĩũlũ nĩkĩ ana-a-asa amwe ma mũika matonya kwĩthĩwa maemawa nĩ kwĩtĩkĩla mawĩa kĩkundinĩ. O na kau nĩmanenganie mosũngĩo maingĩ, vakuvĩ kĩla ũmwe nĩwanenganie kĩtumi kĩĩ: Ana-a-asa asu ma mũika mayaaĩkĩwa vinya mevangĩĩe mĩvango ya kĩ-veva kuma me anini. O na vatw'ĩkĩkie kana o na kau ana-a-asa amwe ma mũika nĩmaĩ na mĩvango ya kĩ-veva, asyai moo mayaamekĩa vinya meanĩsye mĩvango ĩsu ĩndĩ mamekĩie vinya mevangĩĩe kũsoma mũno kana mamanthe mawĩa angĩ mathũkũme. Kwoou kũmũthũkũma Ngai kũyaaĩsa kwĩthĩwa kwĩ kwa vata mũno thayũnĩ woo.—Mt. 10:24.
10, 11. (a) Mũtumĩa atonya ata kũtetheesya mwana-a-asa ũilyĩ ta ũtakwetye ũu aalyũle mesilya make? (b) Mũtumĩa atonya kũtũmĩa maandĩko meva ĩla wĩ na mwana-a-asa wa mũthemba ũsu, na nĩkĩ? (Sisya maelesyo ma kwongeleela.)
10 Ethĩwa mwana-a-asa ailyĩ ta ũtakwetye ũu, ũyĩsa kũtw'ĩka nĩwamũvĩndũa no nginya wĩthĩwe na kĩthito kingĩ na wũmĩĩsyo mwingĩ mũno, ĩndĩ ũu ti kwasya kana ndatetheka. O tondũ mũĩmi ũlũngaa matina ma mĩtĩ yake o kavola kwa kavola, now'o o naku ũtonya kũtetheesya ana-a-asa amwe maalyũle mawoni moo nĩ kana wĩthĩe no metĩkĩle kũnengwa mawĩa kĩkundinĩ. Ĩndĩ ũtonya kwĩka ũu ata?
11 Mantha ĩvinda nĩ kana wĩthĩe nĩwatuma ndũũ na mwana-a-asa ũsu. Mũtetheesye aelewe kana nũkwendeka mũno kĩkundinĩ. Na mũendeee o ũu, no wĩse kwĩkala nthĩ nake mũkasũanĩa maandĩko mana nĩ kana ũmũtetheesye asũanĩe kĩla waĩle kwĩanĩsya yu nũndũ nĩweeyumisye amũthũkũme Yeova. (Mũta. 5:4; Isa. 6:8; Mt. 6:24, 33; Luka 9:57-62; 1 Ako. 15:58; 2 Ako. 5:15; 13:5) No ũmũkũlye-ĩ, 'Wamwathie Yeova ata ĩla weeyumisye ũmũthũkũme?' Tata kũmwĩkĩa vinya kwa kũmũkũlya atĩĩ: 'Wĩona Yeova ta weewie ata ĩla wavatisiwe?' (Nth. 27:11) 'Nake Satani eewie ata?' (1 Vet. 5:8) Ĩthĩawa wĩsĩ kana wanyuva maandĩko nesa nũtonya kũkiita mũno ngoo yake.—Soma Aevelania 4:12. *
INYW'Ĩ AMANYĨW'A, ĨTHĨWAI MWĨ AĨKĨĨKU
12, 13. (a) Elisa aĩ na woni ũilyĩ ata ĩla wamanyĩaw'a? (b) Yeova amũtuvie Elisa ata nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa e mũĩkĩĩku?
12 Nata nenyu ana-a-asa ma mũika? Lilikanai kana kĩkundi kĩ na vata nenyu mũno. Ĩndĩ nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũmutetheesya mwĩke maendeeo? Nĩ kana tũkwate ũsũngĩo, ekai tũsũanĩe ũndũ ũmwe weekĩkie ĩvindanĩ ya tene ũkonetye mũmanyĩw'a mũna.
13 Vakuvĩ myaka 3,000 mĩvĩtu, mwathani Eliya nĩwakũlilye mwanake ũmwe weetawa Elisa atw'ĩke mũthũkũmi wake. Elisa nĩweetĩkĩlile wĩa ũsu ateũtindĩa, na ambĩĩa kũtetheesya mwathani ũsu waĩ mũkũũ kwa kũthũkũma mawĩa ala mavũthaw'a nĩ andũ. Athũkũmie mawĩa asu e mũĩkĩĩku. (2 Asu. 3:11) Elisa nĩwekalile e mũmanyĩw'a vandũ va myaka ta thanthatũ, na ĩndĩ myaka ĩsu ĩithela nĩwamanyie kana Eliya akilyĩ anamina wĩa wake nthĩ ya Isilaeli. Kũvikĩĩa vau Elisa aĩ mũmanyĩsye nesa vyũ. Nĩvo ĩndĩ Eliya wamwĩie nĩ aeke kũendany'a nake, ĩndĩ Elisa amwĩa katatũ, "Ndikũtia." Atw'ĩte kwĩkala na mwalimũ wake ĩvinda yĩasa ũndũ vatonyeka. Nũndũ wa kwĩthĩwa aĩ mũĩkĩĩku, Yeova nĩwamũtuvie kwa kũmwĩtĩkĩlya amwone Eliya aithi na kĩlingi kwa nzĩa ya ũsengy'o.—2 Asu. 2:1-12.
14. (a) Amanyĩw'a matonya kũatĩĩa ata ngelekany'o ya Elisa? (b) Nĩkĩ nĩ ũndũ wa vata mũmanyĩw'a ethĩwe e mũĩkĩĩku?
14 Ũtonya ata kũatĩĩa ngelekany'o ya Elisa? Wanengwa mawĩa ĩtĩkĩla ũteũtindĩa, o na ethĩwa nĩ mawĩa ala mavũthĩtw'e. Tuma ndũũ na mwalimũ waku, na ũimũtavasya ũndũ ũtũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa kyonthe kĩla ũtethasya kwondũ waku. Ũndũ ũkwĩka wamanyĩw'a no ũtume mwalimũ waku aelewa nĩ ta ũũmwĩa atĩĩ, "Ndikũtia." Na ĩndĩ ũndũ ũla wa vata vyũ nĩ kana waĩlĩte kũtethya mawĩa onthe ala wanengwa wĩ mũĩkĩĩku. Nĩkĩ ũsu nĩ ũndũ wa vata? Nĩ wa vata nĩkwĩthĩwa atumĩa moona wĩ mũĩkĩĩku na wĩ wa kwĩkwatw'a, nĩmamanyaa kana Yeova nũkwenda ũnewe mawĩa maingangĩ kĩkundinĩ.—Sav. 101:6; soma 2 Timotheo 2:2.
MANENGE NDAĨA ĨLA ĨMAĨLE
15, 16. (a) Nĩ kwa nzĩa syĩva Elisa woonanisye kana nũnengete mwalimũ wake ndaĩa? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ ya 9.) (b) Nĩ kyaũ kyatumie athani ala angĩ mamwĩkwatya Elisa?
15 Ngewa ya Elisa nĩtũtetheeasya kũelewa ũndũ ana-a-asa matonya kũnenga atumĩa ala me na ũmanyi mwingĩ ndaĩa ĩla ĩmaĩle. Ngewa ĩsu nĩeleasya kana ĩtina wa Eliya na Elisa kũthi kwona kĩkundi kĩmwe kya athani kĩla kyaĩ Yeliko, nĩmaumie vu na mathi Ũsĩnĩ wa Yolotani. Ĩla mavikie vau Eliya eekie ata? Mbivilia yaĩtye ũũ: "Eliya oosa suka wake, na ookũnza, akũna manzĩ, na maaanĩka." Mamina kũinga makinyĩle nthĩ nyũmũ, 'nĩmaendangĩe makĩneenangany'a.' Kĩu kĩonany'a kana Elisa ndasũanĩaa kana kũvikĩĩa vu nĩweesĩ kĩla kĩndũ. Vandũ va ũu, Elisa aendeeie kwĩthukĩĩsya na kũsũanĩa mũno maũndũ onthe ala maneenawa nĩ Eliya nginya ĩla mesie kũtaanĩsya. Ĩtina wa ũu Eliya nĩwambatie na kĩlingi. Ĩla Elisa wesie kũsyokela Ũsĩnĩ wa Yolotani, nĩwakũnie kĩw'ũ na ũla suka wa Eliya, na asya, "Yeova aĩva, Ngai wa Eliya?" Eeka ũu, kĩw'ũ nĩkyaaanĩkie ĩngĩ.—2 Asu. 2:8-14.
16 We nĩwoona kana kyama kya mbee kya Elisa kĩvw'anene na kyama kya mũthya kya Eliya? Nĩkĩ tũkwendeew'a nĩ ũndũ ũsu? Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa Elisa ndaaĩsilya atĩ nũndũ nĩwe yu waĩ ĩũlũ, evĩndũany'a maũndũ ndatĩka ĩsu eke ũndũ ũkwenda. Vandũ va ũu, aendeeie kwĩka maũndũ o ũndũ Eliya weekaa, na kwa nzĩa ĩsu oonany'a kana nĩwanengete mwalimũ wake ndaĩa. Kĩu kyatumie athani ala angĩ mamwĩkwatya. (2 Asu. 2:15) Ĩtina wa vau Elisa nĩwaendeeie kũthũkũma e mwathani kwa ĩvinda ya myaka 60, na ĩvindanĩ yĩu yonthe Yeova nĩwamũnengie vinya wa kwĩka syama mbingĩ kũthonoka ila Eliya weekie. Ethĩwa we nũũmanyĩw'a, ũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ?
17. (a) Ala meũmanyĩw'a matonya ata kwĩthĩwa mailyĩ ta Elisa? (b) Yeova atonya kwĩsa kũtũmĩa amanyĩw'a ala aĩkĩĩku ata?
17 Wamina kũnengwa mawĩa mana kĩkundinĩ, ndũkatate kwona ta waĩle kũvĩndũa maũndũ vau kwa vau makekawa kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũndũ manatwĩe mekawa. Maũndũ kĩkundinĩ mavĩndũawa kwosana na mavata ma kĩkundi na kwosana na ũndũ ũseũvyo wa Yeova ũkwasya, ĩndĩ ti kwosana na wendi waku. Lilikana kana nũndũ Elisa eekaa maũndũ o tondũ Eliya weekaa, meko make nĩmatumie athani ala angĩ mamwĩkwatya na moonany'a kana nĩwanengete Eliya ndaĩa. O naku waendeea kwĩka maũndũ kwosana na ũndũ Mbivilia yaĩtye o tondũ ũmanyĩĩtw'e nĩ atumĩa ala me na ũmanyi, no ũtume Aklĩsto ala angĩ makwĩkwatya, na ũkonany'a kana nũnengete atumĩa asu ndaĩa. (Soma 1 Akolintho 4:17.) Ĩndĩ o ũndũ ũmanyi waku ũkũendeea kwongeleka, ũkekalaa ũkona moalyũku maĩle kwĩkwa kĩkundinĩ ala makatetheeasya kĩkundi kĩikatiwe ĩtina nĩ ũseũvyo wa Yeova, ũla wĩkalaa ũsongete. Na o tondũ Yeova weekanie na Elisa, weethĩwa wĩ mũmanyĩw'a mũĩkĩĩku, Yeova nũtonya kwĩsa kũtuma wĩka maũndũ manene mũno mbee wa ala mekĩtwe nĩ alimũ maku.—Yoa. 14:12.
18. Nĩkĩ kũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa ala angĩ kĩkundinĩ nĩ wĩa waĩle kũtethw'a na mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka?
18 Twĩĩkwatya maũndũ ala me ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ na yĩla ĩvĩtu nĩmeũtetheesya atumĩa mamanthe ĩvinda ya kũmanyĩsya ana-a-asa ala angĩ. O na twĩĩkwatya kana ana-a-asa ala maĩle nĩmekwĩtĩkĩla kuma ngoonĩ mamanyĩw'e na maitũmĩa kwa ũĩ maũndũ ala meũmanyĩw'a nĩ kana matetheesye wĩa wa kũsũvĩa ĩĩthya ya Yeova. Kwĩka ũu kũkalũlũmĩlya ikundi nthĩ yonthe, na kũkatũtetheesya ithyonthe twĩkale twĩ aĩkĩĩku ĩvindanĩ ya mwanya yĩla yĩ mbee witũ.
^ kal. 5 Ethĩwa mwana-a-asa mũnini nũkwoneka e o mũimu, enyivĩtye, na e na nguma ingĩ ila mwana-a-asa waĩle kwĩthĩwa nasyo nĩ kana aaĩwe ianda kĩkundinĩ, atumĩa no manengane ĩsyĩtwa yake nĩ kana atw'ĩkĩthw'e mũtetheesya wa kĩkundi o na ethĩwa ndavikĩtye myaka 20.—1 Tim. 3:8-10, 12; sisya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩsũngũ) ya 01/07/1989, ĩthangũ ya 29.
^ kal. 11 Ĩla mũkũea ngewa no ũtũmĩe maũndũ ala mawetetwe ĩkasetinĩ ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/04/2012, ĩthangũ ya 14-16, kalungu ka 8-13, na ĩvukunĩ "Ĩyĩkalyei Ene Wendonĩ wa Ngai," kĩlungu kya 16, kalungu ka 1-3.
