translation:
"Be loyal to what you know is right… , act honestly toward people." –2 TIM. 2:2.
1. (a) Why does God allow bad things to happen to good people, and how can we cope with such situations? (b) What will help us to remain loyal?
God allows trials so that people may prove their loyalty. For example, a man named Job was "tested" by Satan, and people criticized him because of his suffering. (Job. 14:14-16) King David prayed that his heart would be "loyal" to Jehovah, and he proved his loyalty to Jehovah repeatedly. (1 Chron. 25:7) But we live during the time when Satan and his demons are especially active. (Rev. 6:11-13) So we need more than ever to ask Jehovah for strength to remain loyal. (Eph. 13:15, 16) How can we benefit from the examples of faithful ones in the Bible, and how can we show that we are determined to be loyal? Jehovah provides spirit forces to help those who are loyal. (2 Tim. 2:2) How can spiritual men use their knowledge to help others become loyal and find joy in serving Jehovah?
SHOW LOYALTY TO JEHOVAH BY YOUR EXAMPLE
2. A spiritual man can set a fine example by always endeavoring to preach the good news, why is this so?
2 Let spiritual men work closely with elders. An elder should not neglect his own family, yet he can still see to it that his children receive proper training and that they grow spiritually. Also, he should endeavor to teach a young man who has potential, helping him to understand important truths from the Scriptures and showing him how to apply them practically.—1 Tim. 4:6.
3. (a) What can a spiritual man do to remind himself of Jesus' command recorded at Mark 12:29, 30 to love God with all his heart? (b) Can a spiritual man associate with those who are disfellowshipped?
3 If you want to show genuine love for Jehovah, ask yourself, "How can I demonstrate my love for Jehovah more fully?" Doing so will help you to identify areas where you can make progress in loving Jehovah with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength. (Read Mark 12:29, 30.) By regularly examining yourself, you can determine whether you are giving Jehovah first place in your life and whether you are making spiritual matters a priority. Do you feel that you could strengthen your relationship with Jehovah by doing more in the ministry?
4. (a) Give an example of how a Christian woman might support her husband when he faces difficulties. (b) How can spiritual men assist young ones in maintaining zeal?
4 When helping a young person, be tactful and considerate, and use the Bible to reason with him. (1 Tim. 19:19-21; Titus 2:6-8; 13:13; Acts 18:24-26) Remember that a young person's reaction may depend on his upbringing and personality. Why? Because each individual responds differently. Be patient and understanding. A brother named Jean-Claude in France said: "The key to helping someone is to appeal to his conscience and to help him see the value of applying God's principles to everyday situations. Only then will he truly appreciate the meaning of 'opening [his] eyes' to what is right and 'understanding the insight' from God's Word." (Ps. 119:18) What else can you do to help others appreciate the value of Bible study?
TO HELP OTHERS TO APPRECIATE AND APPLY WHAT THEY LEARN
5. (a) What is involved in expressing heartfelt appreciation for the good news? (b) What practical steps can spiritual men take to encourage young ones who have been serving for some time? (See suggestions under "Helping Others to Appreciate and Apply What They Learn.")
5 Sometimes, those studying the Bible ask themselves: 'Do I really want to please Jehovah?' If so, they need encouragement. Help them identify specific goals, and commend them when they make progress. Encourage them to share their faith with others, and show genuine interest in their efforts. Express your confidence in them, and remind them that Jehovah values sincere effort. Also, remember that sometimes people may appear unresponsive, yet they are actually giving the matter thought. A brother named Victor, who serves in West Africa, observed: "I have learned that it is important to focus on the positive aspects of a person's spirituality. We should commend them for their efforts to apply what they learn." Spiritual men often find it helpful to spend time with young ones, encouraging them to set realistic goals and to cope with challenges.—Read Psalm 71:5, 17. *
6. What helped Jesus to be an effective teacher?
6 One thing that made Jesus an effective teacher was his ability to empathize with people and understand their needs. He showed people why it was vital that they believe, and he used illustrations to help them grasp spiritual truths. For example, Jesus chose his apostles from among ordinary men, and then he trained them to teach others. He said: "All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth." And afterward he instructed them: "Go and make disciples of all nations." (Matt. 28:18, 19) Can you think of ways to imitate Jesus' example in teaching?
7, 8. (a) How can spiritual men imitate Jesus' example in teaching? (b) What can help them to be more effective teachers? (c) What qualities can encourage those being taught? (See the box "What Helps Make Teaching Effective.")
7 When someone shows interest, use the Scriptures to explain things clearly and show how Bible principles apply to his life. In this way, you can help him see that what you are saying is based on God's Word, not just your own opinion. For instance, suppose you are helping a young man who is struggling with pornography. Instead of simply telling him that it is wrong, you could read Titus 2:10 and explain how Christians should adorn the teaching of our great God by living a moral life. This will help him appreciate that following Bible principles benefits him personally and helps him maintain his dignity. By focusing on practical benefits, you can motivate him to take action and improve his life. It may also help him realize the harm that pornography does to individuals and families.
8 And another way to help them is to commend their efforts to make progress. But how can we do that? Often, a sincere compliment can encourage them to continue making spiritual advancement.—Compare Matthew 3:17.
ANOTHER IMPORTANT POINT
9. (a) What reasons might there be why some people seem interested at first but then stop coming to meetings? (b) How can parents help their children appreciate the value of honoring God?
9 People seem interested at first but then stop coming for various reasons. It may be because they are busy with their careers and have families and little time to devote to spiritual matters. We have learned from our experience with publishers in about 20 countries in Europe and in North America that some young people find it difficult to resist peer pressure. And even though many try hard, each one faces a challenge: Young people often feel pressured to conform to the standards of their peers. And sometimes, even when young people want to maintain high standards, they may face situations where they feel compelled to compromise their principles in order to fit in or to avoid being ridiculed. So we should remember that honoring God may require courage on the part of those who want to please him.—Matt. 10:24.
10, 11. (a) How can a publisher help a young person who feels torn between his desire to serve Jehovah and the influence of his friends? (b) What can a publisher do to assist a young person whose parents do not support his faith, and why? (See accompanying article.)
10 When a young person feels torn, reassure him that it is normal to struggle with conflicting desires and strong emotions, and that he is not weak or disloyal for feeling this way. After all, even mature Christians sometimes stumble and fall, yet they continue to strive to remain faithful. But how can you help a young person to resist peer pressure and not give in to temptation? How can you encourage him to stand firm for what is right?
11 Perhaps he needs to talk about his feelings. Help him to express himself openly and honestly. And then, listen carefully. Encourage him to meditate on scriptures that strengthen his resolve to serve Jehovah. (Ps. 5:4; Isa. 6:8; Matt. 6:24, 33; Luke 9:57-62; 1 Cor. 15:58; 2 Cor. 5:15; Col. 13:5) Then ask yourself, "Am I setting a good example?"—Read Hebrews 4:12. *
QUESTIONS FOR STUDY AND DISCUSSION
12, 13. (a) What quality did Elijah demonstrate when dealing with Ahab? (b) How does Jehovah empower us to be courageous?
12 Are there young ones in your family who need help? Consider how you can support them. What practical steps can you take to help them cope with difficulties? It may be helpful to spend time together discussing what is troubling them.
13 For over 3,000 years, people have remembered Elijah's faithful servant Elisha. Elisha was willing to work hard and diligently, and he asked Jehovah to give him the ability to perform miracles so that he could prove to the people that Jehovah is God. He performed miracles that glorified Jehovah. (2 Kings 3:11) Elisha served faithfully for many years, and eventually he learned that Elijah would soon leave Israel. Recognizing the value of Elijah's guidance, Elisha resolutely said, "I will not leave you." He continued to stay with his teacher despite the difficult circumstances. Because of his determination, Jehovah empowered him to witness Elijah being taken up into heaven in a miraculous way.—2 Kings 2:1-12.
14. (a) What qualities made Elisha a good student? (b) What can we learn from Elisha's example?
14 Should you strive to imitate Elisha's qualities? Many young ones face challenges, or they may experience difficulties. Spend time with your teacher, and ask him questions about things you do not understand. Your willingness to learn will encourage your teacher to feel that you appreciate his efforts. By showing such initiative, you demonstrate that you are determined to make progress. But is this the only benefit? It also shows that you respect those who are older and experienced, and it pleases Jehovah when you seek wise counsel.—Prov. 101:6; read 2 Timothy 2:2.
CONSIDER THE EXAMPLE
15, 16. (a) How did Elisha show that he valued his teacher's guidance? (See accompanying picture.) (b) Why were others impressed by Elisha's loyalty?
15 Elisha's example helps us to see how important it is to be willing to work hard and to have much zeal. This is especially true when trying to imitate Elijah and Elisha in their ministry. They traveled together as a group of ministers, going from place to place throughout the land of Israel. But what happened when Elijah was taken to heaven? The Bible says: "Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven." Some may wonder, 'What should I do?' The answer is: "Keep busy doing what is right." This shows that Elisha was determined to continue serving and learning everything he could. Like him, we too can become more zealous by associating with mature Christians and by imitating their faith. Elijah equipped him well. He passed on to Elisha his spirit and his power, and asked, "Is there anything I can do for you?" And Elisha replied, "Let me inherit two portions of your spirit."—2 Kings 2:8-14.
16 So, did Elisha prove to be as capable as Elijah? Let us examine this question. It seems that Elisha showed his willingness by continuing to serve even though Elijah was gone. Like him, we can also show our determination to carry on doing what Jehovah wants us to do. He continued to perform miracles like those Elijah had done, and people came to realize that he was a worthy successor. This encouraged the brothers. (2 Kings 2:15) After Elijah was taken away, Elisha traveled around among the groups of prophets for six years, and during all that time Jehovah helped him to accomplish many works of healing, just as he had helped Elijah. Think about it—what can you learn from this?
17. (a) What qualities did Elisha demonstrate by asking for a double portion of Elijah's spirit? (b) Can Jehovah help us to develop similar qualities?
17 We are often comforted when we see others showing genuine love, so imagine how comforting it is to know that faithful friends will continue serving alongside us even after loved ones have passed away. Genuine love moves us to support our brothers and sisters and to align ourselves with God's will. Just as Elisha proved to be as capable as Elijah, we too can encourage others and show that we appreciate them. And we can continue to seek guidance from the Bible and remember that God sends out qualified men to instruct us, just as he sent out apostles and later appointed overseers. (Read 1 Corinthians 4:17.) As your own faith grows stronger, you will be better able to comfort fellow believers who may be discouraged and to strengthen the congregation. By aligning yourself with God's organization, you will remain spiritually strong. And since Jehovah supported Elisha, we can be sure that he will empower faithful men today to perform great works for the benefit of his people.—John 14:12.
18 How can we show genuine love for our brothers and sisters, especially when they are experiencing difficulties?
18 We can imitate the example set by those whom we have already observed encouraging others. Also, we can try to understand what our brothers and sisters need and offer practical help. This demonstrates that we value their efforts to promote the Kingdom and that we want to assist them in upholding Jehovah's standards. To maintain this loving spirit throughout the congregation, let us always endeavor to speak kindly and thoughtfully to everyone we meet.
^ kal. 5 An elder should be compassionate and understanding, kind and gentle, and also reasonable. However, an elder should not become overly familiar with individuals or allow personal feelings to influence his decisions. He should avoid becoming involved in situations that could lead to gossip or compromise his integrity.—1 Tim. 3:8-10, 12; see The Ministry School book (Spanish), page 29, dated January 7, 1989.
^ kal. 11 For further information, please refer to the Spanish The Ministry School cassette recording of April 15, 2012, pages 14-16, paragraphs 8-13, and the article "How to Be a Fine Representative of God," paragraph 16, paragraphs 1-3.

text:
"Na Yeova Ngai asya, Ti ũseo mũndũ ethĩwe e weka; nĩngũmũmbĩa mũtetheesya."—MWA. 2:18.
MBATHI: 36, 11
1, 2. (a) Mũtwaano wambĩĩie ata? (b) Atamu na mũka matonya kwĩthĩwa maĩ na woni mwaũ ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MŨTWAANO ti ũndũ mweũ o na vanini andũnĩ. Kwĩmanyĩsya ĩũlũ wa ũndũ wambĩĩe na kĩeleelo kyaw'o no kũtũtetheesye twĩthĩwe na woni waĩlĩte ĩũlũ waw'o na tũiũtanĩa. Ngai amina kũmba mũndũ wa mbee, Atamu, nĩwamũeteie nyamũ syonthe nĩ kenda aitw'ĩĩe masyĩtwa. Ĩndĩ "kwondũ wa ũ mũndũ kũtyaaoneka mũtetheesya ũmwaĩle." Kwoou Ngai nĩwamũkomethisye Atamu na amumya wau ũmwe awũmba mũndũ mũka, na ĩndĩ amũetee ũ mũndũ mũka. (Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 2:20-24.) Kwoou Ngai nĩwe wambĩĩisye mũtwaano.
2 Yesũ nĩwawetie kana Yeova nĩwe waneenie ndeto ii: "Mũndũ akatia ĩthe na nyinyia, na akalũman'ya na mũka wake; na me elĩ makeethĩwa mwĩĩ ũmwe." (Mt. 19:4, 5) Ngai atũmĩie wau wa Atamu kũmba mũndũ mũka wa mbee, na ũu woonanisye kana andũ asu elĩ maaĩle kwĩthĩwa na mũtwaano mũlũmu. Kwoou vayaĩ mũvango wa kũthasya mũtwaano, o na vayaĩ mũvango wa mũndũũme kũtwaa iveti mbingĩ kana mũndũ mũka kũtwawa nĩ aũme aingĩ.
ŨNDŨ MŨTWAANO WĨANĨASYA KĨELEELO KYA YEOVA
3. Nĩ kyaũ kyaĩ kĩeleelo kĩnene kya mũtwaano?
3 Atamu nĩwendete mũka wake na amwĩtie Eva. Na nũndũ 'nĩwamwaĩle,' aĩ ethĩwe "mũtetheesya" wake na ũu wesaa kũtuma mekala na ũtanu maendeee kwĩanĩsya ianda syoo me andũ matwaanĩte. (Mwa. 2:18) Kĩeleelo kĩnene kya mũtwaano kyaĩ kusũsya andũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ. (Mwa. 1:28) Ana na eĩtu maĩ matie asyai moo, o na kau nĩmamendete mũno, na maitwaana na kwambĩĩsya mĩsyĩ yoo. Andũ maĩ mausũsye nthĩ ũndũ vaaĩle na maithanthasya wĩkalo woo kũvika nthĩ yonthe yĩthĩwe ĩilyĩ mũũnda wa Eteni.
4. Nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie mũtwaano wa mbee?
4 Mũtwaano wa mbee nĩwakwatiwe nĩ mathĩna nũndũ Atamu na Eva matũmĩie naĩ ũthasyo woo wa kwĩnyuvĩa kwa kũlea kũmwĩw'a Yeova. Satani, kana Ndevili, ũla wĩtĩtwe "nzoka ĩla ngũũ," nĩwakengie Eva aĩkĩĩa kana aya ũsyao wa "mũtĩ wa kũmanyĩthya ũseo na ũthũku" akeethĩwa na ũmanyi wa mwanya wa kũtw'a ũla ũseo na ũla ũthũku. Eva ndaakũlya mũũme woni wake ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu, na ũu woonanisye kana ndaamũnenga ndaĩa tawe waaĩle kũtongoesya mũsyĩ. Nake Atamu, vandũ va kũmwĩw'a Ngai, nĩweetĩkĩlile ĩtunda yĩla wanengiwe nĩ Eva.—Ũvu. 12:9; Mwa. 2:9, 16, 17; 3:1-6.
5. Tũtonya kwĩmanyĩsya kyaũ twasũanĩa ũndũ Atamu na Eva mamũsũngĩie Yeova?
5 Ĩla Ngai wambĩĩie kũsilĩla andũ asu elĩ, Atamu ailĩĩlile mũka mavĩtyo. Aisye atĩĩ: "Mũndũ mũka ũla wanengie ethĩwe nakwa, nĩwe ũnengie wa mũtĩ, na naya," nake Eva asya kana nzoka nĩyo ĩmũkengie. (Mwa. 3:12, 13) Matũmĩie itumi ite vala syĩĩ kwĩtetea! Ĩndĩ nũndũ mayaamwĩw'a Yeova, nĩwamasilĩile. Ũsu nĩ ũkany'o mũnene ta kĩ kwitũ! Kwoou nĩ kana mũtwaano wĩthĩwe wĩ mũseo, ala matwaanĩte nĩmaĩle kũmwĩw'a Yeova na kĩla ũmwe woo aimanya kana akaumya ũtalo kwondũ wa meko make.
6. Ũtonya kũelesya ata ĩandĩko ya Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:15?
6 Ĩtina wa Satani kwĩka ũndũ weekie mũũndanĩ wa Eteni, Yeova nĩwanengie andũ wĩkwatyo. Wĩkwatyo ũsu ũwetetwe nthĩnĩ wa wathani wa mbee wa Mbivilia. (Soma Mwambĩlĩlyo 3:15.) Kwosana na wathani ũsu, kyũmbe kĩu kya veva kyaĩ kĩse kũtumbwa (kwanangwa) nĩ "ũsyao" wa "mũndũ mũka." Kwĩsĩla wathani ũsu Yeova nĩwatumie andũ maelewa o vanini ngwatanĩo ya mwanya ĩla yĩthĩawa katĩ wake na syũmbe mbingĩ sya veva ila imũthũkũmaa ĩtunĩ. Ĩtina wa ĩvinda, Maandĩko nĩmavuanisye kana Ngai aĩ ese kũtũma ũmwe katĩ wa syũmbe syake sya veva nĩ kana 'etumba' Ndevili na aituma andũ ala ewi methĩwa na wĩkwatyo ũla asyai ma mbee maaisye. Wĩkwatyo ũsu nĩ kwĩkala ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene, kwosana na ũndũ Yeova wendaa kuma tene.—Yoa. 3:16.
7. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kyakwatie mĩtwaano kuma Atamu na Eva mavĩtya? (b) Mbivilia yaĩtye mũndũ na mũka maĩle kwĩkalany'a ata?
7 Ũlei wa Atamu na Eva nĩwaeteie mũtwaano woo mathĩna, o vamwe na mĩtwaano ĩla ĩngĩ yonthe. Kwa ngelekany'o, Eva na aka ala angĩ maĩ makwatawe nĩ woo ĩla me ĩvu, o na ĩvinda ya kũsyaa. Aka maĩ methĩwe na wendi mwingĩ kwelekela aũme moo, namo aũme maĩ masumbĩke iveti syoo, o na amwe mayithĩny'a o tondũ tũkwona mĩtwaanonĩ mingĩ ũmũnthĩ. (Mwa. 3:16) Mbivilia yaĩtye kana aũme maĩle kũtongoesya iveti syoo kwa nzĩa ya wendo. Nasyo iveti syaĩle kwĩnyivĩsya aũme masyo. (Aev. 5:33) Andũ ala matwaanĩte mekalany'a nesa, maũndũ ala matonya kũete mathĩna mũtwaanonĩ woo nĩmaolekaa kana makathela vyũ.
MŨTWAANO KUMA ĨVINDA YA ATAMU KŨVIKA ĨVINDA YA NOA
8. Ũtonya kũelesya kyaũ ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano kuma ĩvinda ya Atamu kũvika ĩvinda ya Noa?
8 Atamu na Eva matanamba kũkw'a nĩmasyaie anake na eĩtu. (Mwa. 5:4) Mwana woo wa mbee, Kaini, atwaie ũmwe katĩ wa eĩtu ma mũsyĩ woo. Ũmwe katĩ wa nzyawa sya Kaini ũla weetawa Lameki, nĩwe waĩ wa mbee Mbivilianĩ kũtwaa iveti ilĩ. (Mwa. 4:17, 19) Kuma ĩvinda ya Atamu kũvika ĩvinda ya Noa no andũ anini mawetetwe ta mamũthaithaa Yeova. Amwe moo maĩ Aveli, Enoko, na Noa na mũsyĩ wake. Mbivilia yaĩtye kana ĩvindanĩ ya Noa 'ana ma Ngai nĩmoonie kana eĩtu ma andũ maĩ aseo; na meetwaĩa aka, onthe ala manyuvie.' Mĩtwaano ĩsu yeethĩiwe katĩ wa aka na alaĩka asu meevw'ĩkĩte mĩĩ ya andũ nĩyatumie kũsyawa mamũndũ manene meetawa Nevilimu. O na eka ũu, "ũthũku wa mũndũ waĩ mũnene kũũ nthĩ na kĩla kĩsũanĩo kya malilikano ma ngoo yake kyaĩ kyathe vyũ mavinda onthe."—Mwa. 6:1-5.
9. Yeova eekanie ata na andũ athũku ĩvinda ya Noa, na ũndũ ũsu waĩle kũtũmanyĩsya kyaũ?
9 Yeova nĩwauisye mbua mbingĩ mũno ĩvinda ya Noa nĩ kenda anange athũku. Ĩvinda yĩu andũ maendeee o na maũndũ moo, ta kũtwaana, na nũndũ wa ũu mayaaosa kwa ũito kĩla "Noa, mũtavan'ya wa ũlũngalu," wamatavasya ĩũlũ wa wanangĩko ũla waĩ vakuvĩ. (2 Vet. 2:5) Yesũ aelekanilye maũndũ ala maĩ kw'o ĩvinda ya Noa na maũndũ ala tũkwona ũmũnthĩ. (Soma Mathayo 24:37-39.) Ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ nĩmaleaa kwĩthukĩĩsya ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai, ũla ũendeee kũtavanw'a nthĩ yonthe wĩthĩwe ũkũsĩ kwa mbaĩ syonthe nthĩ ĩno nthũku ĩtanamba kwanangwa. Kwoou tũyaĩlĩte kũeka maũndũ ta kũtwaana na kũea syana matume twambĩĩa kwona mũthenya wa Yeova ta wĩ vaasa.
MŨTWAANO KUMA ĨVINDA YA NOA KŨVIKA ĨVINDA YA YESŨ
10. (a) Mbaĩnĩ mbingĩ nĩ maũndũ meva ma ũlaalai meekawa nĩ andũ aingĩ? (b) Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya mũtwaano wa Avalaamu na Sala waĩ ngelekany'o nzeo?
10 Noa na ana make matwaĩte kĩla mũndũ kĩveti o kĩmwe. Ĩndĩ ĩtina wa ĩla mbua mbingĩ aũme aingĩ nĩmambĩĩie kũtwaa iveti mbingĩ. Mbaĩnĩ mbingĩ ũlaalai nĩweekawa nĩ andũ aingĩ o na nĩwalikĩtw'e ũthaithinĩ. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩla Avalamu (Avalaamu) na mũka wake Salai (Sala) mavikie Kanaani, nthĩ ĩla Ngai wameie mathi, meethĩie yusũĩte maũndũ mathũku ala matumaa mũtwaano ũtanengwa ndaĩa. Kwoou Yeova nĩwatwie kana ndũa ya Sotomo na ya Ngomola syaĩle kwanangwa nũndũ andũ ala mekalaa ndũanĩ isu nĩmeekaa maũndũ mavuku ma ũlaalai kana kũmetĩkĩlya maendeee. Avalaamu nĩwatongoesye mũsyĩ wake nesa, nake Sala nĩwaiie ngelekany'o nzeo ya kwĩnyivĩsya mũũme. (Soma 1 Vetelo 3:3-6.) O na Avalaamu nĩwaĩkĩĩthisye kana mwanae Isaka atwaa mũthaithi wa Yeova. O nake Isaka eekie oou kwondũ wa mwana wake Yakovo, ũla ana make mesie kũtw'ĩka mbaĩ 12 sya Isilaeli.
11. Mĩao ya Mose yasũvĩaa Aisilaeli ata?
11 Ĩtina wa ĩvinda Yeova nĩwatianĩie ũtianĩo na nzyawa sya Yakovo (Isilaeli). Ĩvinda yĩu, Mĩao ya Mose yaĩ na myolooto ĩla yatetheeasya andũ maũndũnĩ makonetye mũtwaano, ta kũtwaa iveti mbingĩ. Mĩao ĩsu nĩyasũvĩaa Aisilaeli kĩ-veva nũndũ nĩyamavatĩte kũtwaana na andũ matamũthaithaa Yeova. (Soma Kũtũngĩlĩlwa Kwa Mĩao 7:3, 4.) Ĩvinda yĩu vaumĩla mathĩna maito mũtwaanonĩ atumĩa nĩmo makothaa kũtetheesya ala me na mathĩna asu. Ethĩwa mũndũ ti mũĩkĩĩku mũtwaanonĩ, e na kĩwĩu, kana e na nzika ĩũlũ wa ũndũ mũna, maũndũ asu nĩmathĩnĩkĩawa kwa nzĩa yaĩlĩte. Kũthasya mũtwaano nĩkweetĩkĩlĩtw'e, ĩndĩ vaĩ mĩao yakonetye ũndũ ũsu. Kwa ngelekany'o, mũndũũme aĩ atonya kũnenga mũka valũa wa kũthasya mũtwaano ethĩwa nĩwoona e na "ũndũ ũtaĩle." (Kũt. 24:1) O na kau 'ũndũ ũsu ũtaĩle' ndũeleetw'e, no twasye kana ndwakonetye tũmaũndũ tũnini tũte vala tũĩ.—Ali. 19:18.
NDŨKEKE ŨLA ŨTWAANĨTE NAKE MAŨNDŨ MA ŨSELEKE
12, 13. (a) Aũme amwe ma ĩvinda ya Malaki meekanaa ata na iveti syoo? (b) Mũndũ mũvatise akosa kĩveti kyeene kana mũũme weene, vethĩwa ata?
12 Ĩvinda ya mwathani Malaki, Ayuti aingĩ nĩmatũmĩaa ũseleke nĩ kana mathasye mĩtwaano yoo. Manengae iveti syoo valũa wa kũthasya mũtwaano nũndũ wa kĩtumi o na kĩva kĩla maĩ matonya kũsũanĩa. Aũme ta asu malũngasya iveti syoo ila matwaie me ma mũika, na nĩvatonyeka makethĩwa meekaa ũu nĩ kana matwae ingĩ ite ngũũ kana itamũthaithaa Yeova. O na ĩla Yesũ waĩ kũũ nthĩ, aũme Ayuti nĩmatũmĩaa ũseleke kũthasya mĩtwaano yoo "kwondũ wa kĩla ũndũ" o na ethĩwa nĩ wĩva. (Mt. 19:3) Yeova Ngai nĩwamenete nzĩa ta ĩsu ya ũseleke ya kũthasya mũtwaano.—Soma Malaki 2:13-16.
13 Ũmũnthĩ andũ ma Yeova mayamba kwĩtĩkĩlya ũseleke ũendeee mũtwaanonĩ. Ĩndĩ nata mũndũ ũtwaanĩte kana mũtwae akosa kĩveti kana mũũme weene na amina kũthasya mũtwaano ũ wake aitwaana nake? Mũndũ ũsu akaema kwĩlila no atengwe nĩ kana kĩkundi kĩendeee kwĩthĩwa kĩ kĩtheu. (1 Ako. 5:11-13) Na nĩ kana ese kũtũngwa kĩkundinĩ no nginya ethĩwe na "ũsyao ũla waĩle ũalyũlo wa ngoo." (Luka 3:8; 2 Ako. 2:5-10) Vai ĩvinda yĩwetetwe yĩla yaĩle kũvĩta nĩ kana mũndũ ũla wĩkĩte ũndũ ta ũsu wa ũseleke atũngwe kĩkundinĩ, o na vala maũndũ asu ma ũseleke mekĩkaa o mavinda maũtala andũnĩ ma Ngai. O na ũu wĩ o vo ũndũ ta ũsu ndwaĩle kũvũthĩĩw'a. No vavĩte ĩvinda yĩasa, o ta mwaka kana o mbeange, mwĩki ũsu wa naĩ ayĩsa kwĩlila kuma ngoonĩ. Na o na ethĩwa nĩwatũngwa kĩkundinĩ no nginya eumya ũtalo "mbee wa kĩvĩla kya sila kya Ngai" onany'e nĩweelilile kuma ngoonĩ kana ndaaĩlila.—Alo. 14:10-12; sisya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩsũngũ) ya 15/11/1979, ĩth. 31-32.
MŨTWAANO WA KĨKLĨSTO
14. Mĩao yeanĩisye ũndũ wĩva?
14 Mĩao ya Mose yatongoeisye Aisilaeli kwa ĩvinda ya myaka mbee wa 1,500. Nĩyatetheeisye andũ ma Ngai malilikanae myolooto yake ĩla mekwĩka maũndũ ma mũsyĩ na angĩ maingĩ, na yamatongoesya kũvika ĩla Masia wookie. (Aka. 3:23, 24) Ĩla Mĩao ya Mose yaekie kũtũmĩwa Yesũ amina kũkw'a, Ngai nĩwambĩĩsye mũvango ũngĩ. (Aevl. 8:6) Mũvangonĩ ũsu, tũmaũndũ tũmwe twa ĩla Mĩao nĩtwaekie kũatĩĩwa.
15. (a) Nĩ mwolooto wĩva ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano waĩle kũatĩĩwa kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto? (b) Mũklĩsto aĩle kũsũanĩa maũndũ meva atanamba kũthasya mũtwaano?
15 Ĩla Yesũ wakũlilw'e ĩkũlyo nĩ Avalisi asũngĩie asya kana o na kau Mose nĩweetĩkĩlĩtye kũthasya mũtwaano, 'kũiailyĩ ũu kuma mwambĩlĩlyonĩ.' (Mt. 19:6-8) Kwoou Yesũ oonanisye kana mwolooto ũla Ngai wanenganie mũũndanĩ wa Eteni ĩũlũ wa mũtwaano waĩ ũendeee kũatĩĩwa kĩkundinĩ kya Kĩklĩsto. (1 Tim. 3:2, 12) Nũndũ andũ ala matwaanĩte nĩ "mwĩĩ ũmwe," nĩmaĩle kũlũmany'a vamwe na mayĩthĩwa na wendo katĩ woo, o vamwe na kũmwenda Ngai, nĩ kenda mũtwaano woo wĩthĩwe wĩ mũlũmu. Mũndũ ndatonya kũtwaana ĩngĩ ethĩwa athasya mũtwaano wake kwondũ wa itumi ingĩ eka ũlaalai. (Mt. 19:9) Veonekana kana mwathani Osea nĩwamũekeie mũka wake Ngomeli, ũla waĩ kĩlaalai. Kwoou mũndũ no atw'e kũmũekea mũndũ ũla ũtwaanĩte nake ethĩwa nĩweelila ĩtina wa kwĩka ũlaalai. O nake Yeova nĩwaekeie Aisilaeli meelila ĩtina wa kwĩka ũlaalai wa kĩ-veva. (Osea 3:1-5) Ũndũ ũngĩ nĩ kana ethĩwa mũndũ nĩwĩsĩ ũla matwaanĩte nĩwĩkĩte ũlaalai, na o vailyĩ oou aikoma nake, ũu wĩthĩawa ũyonany'a kana nĩwamũekea na nde na kĩtumi kya Maandĩko kya kũthasya mũtwaano woo.
16. Yesũ aisye ata ĩũlũ wa mũndũ kwĩkala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae?
16 Ĩtina wa Yesũ kwonany'a kana Aklĩsto ma w'o mayaĩle kũthasya mũtwaano kwondũ wa itumi ingĩ eka ũlaalai, nĩwasyokie aweta ĩũlũ wa "ala manengetwe" mũthĩnzĩo wa kwĩthĩwa matonya kwĩkala matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae. Asyokie asya kana 'ũla ũtonya kũwosa, nawose.' (Mt. 19:10-12) Andũ aingĩ nĩmatw'ĩte kũmũthũkũma Yeova matatwaanĩte kana mate atwae nĩ kana meke ũu mate kwelelũkw'a nĩ ũndũ. Nĩtwaĩle kũmakatha kwondũ wa ũtwi woo.
17. Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya Mũklĩsto atw'e kana nũkũtwaana (kana kũtwawa)?
17 Nĩ kyaũ kĩtonya kũtetheesya mũndũ atw'e kana nũkũtwaana (kana nũkũtwawa) kana ndeĩka ũu? Mũndũ nĩwaĩle kũtw'a ethĩwa nĩ ũndũ ũtonyeka kwake kwĩkala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae. Mũtũmwa Vaulo oonanisye kana nũseo mũndũ kwĩkala atatwaanĩte kana ate mũtwae. O na ũu wĩ o vo nĩwaisye atĩĩ: "Nũndũ wa molaalai, kĩla mũndũ nĩethĩwe na kĩveti kyake mwene, na kĩla mũndũ mũka nake nĩethĩwe na mũũme wake mwene." Asyokie asya atĩĩ: "Ethĩwa maitonya kwĩyũmĩĩsya, nĩmatwaane: nũndũ nĩ ũseo kũtwaana kwĩ kwakana mwaki." Kũtwaana kana kũtwawa nĩkũtonya kũtetheesya mũndũ ndakaeke wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ ũtume eka maũndũ mathũku ta kwĩkwatanga mamutha ma ũsyai, kana ũlaalai. O na ĩngĩ, ala meenda kũtwaana kana kũtwawa nĩmaĩle kũsũanĩa ĩũlũ wa ũkũũ woo nũndũ mũtũmwa ũsu aĩtye: "Ethĩwa mũndũ o na wĩva [eĩw'a atekala ũndũ vaĩle atatwaanĩte], na ethĩwa nĩwavĩta ũseo wa wana wake, na ethĩwa kwĩ vata wa ũu, nĩeke ũndũ ũnũkwenda; ndekwĩka naĩ; nĩmatwaane." (1 Ako. 7:2, 9, 36; 1 Tim. 4:1-3) Ĩndĩ mũndũ ndaĩle kũtwaana nũndũ wa wendi wa kũmanyana kĩ-mwĩĩ ũla ũtonya kwĩthĩwa naw'o e wa mũika. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ mũndũ ta ũsu nũtonya kwĩthĩwa ate mũimu ũndũ ũtonya kwĩanĩsya maũndũ ala maĩle kwĩanĩw'a nĩ mũndũ ũtwaanĩte kana mũtwae.
18, 19. (a) Andũ ala meũtwaana maĩle kwĩthĩwa mekĩte ata? (b) Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe yĩneenea kyaũ?
18 Mũklĩsto ũla ũkwenda kũtwaana aĩle kwĩthĩwa eyumĩtye amũthũkũme Yeova na amwendete na ngoo yonthe, na aĩlĩte kũtwaana na ũngĩ ũilyĩ oou. Maĩle kwĩthĩwa mendanĩte mũno ũkethĩa nĩmekwenda kwĩkalany'a vamwe matwaanĩte. Vate nzika, makakwata ũathimo nũndũ wa kũatĩĩa ũtao wa kũtwaana kana kũtwawa o "nthĩnĩ wa Mwĩaĩi." (1 Ako. 7:39) Mamina kũtwaana makeethĩa kana Mbivilia nĩyo ĩnenganĩte ũtao ũla waĩle vyũ ũla ũtonya kũmatetheesya mũtwaanonĩ.
19 Ĩsomo yĩla yĩatĩĩe nĩyĩũneenea Maandĩko matonya kũtetheesya andũ matwaanĩte methĩwe matonya kũkitana na mathĩna ala mekw'o 'mĩthenyanĩ ĩno ya mũminũkĩlyo,' o na kau aũme na aka aingĩ mekaa maũndũ matonya kwananga mũtwaano. (2 Tim. 3:1-5) Nthĩnĩ wa Ndeto yake, Yeova nũtũnengete ũtao ũla waĩle nĩ kenda mĩtwaano yitũ yĩthĩwe yĩ mĩseo na yĩ na ũtanu, o tũendeee kũkinyĩla nzĩanĩ ya thayũ ũtathela twĩ vamwe na andũ make.—Mt. 7:13, 14.

translation:
"And Jehovah God said, 'It is not good that the man should be alone.' I will make him a helper fit for him."—GEN. 2:18.
FOOTNOTE: 36, 11
1, 2. (a) What does marriage mean? (b) How can husbands and wives make their marriage happy and successful? (Consider practical examples.)
MARRIAGE is something precious to many people. Appreciating its meaning and purpose and treating each other with love and respect can help couples enjoy a fulfilling and lasting relationship. God cares about people, and he created Adam, the first man, knowing that he would need companionship. Indeed, "it is not good for the man to be alone." So God made woman to be a helper suited to him, and then he blessed them and told them to multiply. (Read Genesis 2:20-24.) Thus, God originated marriage.
2 Jesus showed that Jehovah is the originator of this arrangement when he said: "The man must stick to his wife, and the two will become one flesh." (Matt. 19:4, 5) God used Adam to illustrate that a woman is needed to be a companion, and this shows that people generally benefit from being married. However, there are reasons why some may choose to remain unmarried, such as wanting to devote themselves fully to serving God or because they have had bad experiences in past relationships.
WHY MARRIAGE IS IMPORTANT TO JEHOVAH
3. What is the primary purpose of marriage?
3 Adam named his wife Eve. And while she was "perfect," she was designed to be his "helper" and to complement him, allowing mankind to spread throughout the earth. (Gen. 2:18) The primary purpose of marriage is to populate the earth. (Gen. 1:28) Also, it provides security, comfort, and support. People who marry often find strength in times of difficulty and encouragement to pursue worthwhile goals. Mankind has benefited from marriage since the creation of the first human pair in the garden of Eden.
4. What does marriage involve?
4 Marriage involves a commitment between a man and a woman, and Adam and Eve demonstrated this when they chose to obey Jehovah's command to care for the beautiful garden. Satan, also called the Devil, is described as "a serpent," and he induced Eve to doubt whether God's prohibition regarding "the tree of the knowledge of good and bad" was truly motivated by God's love for them. Eve then disobeyed God, and this led her husband to disobey as well. Thus, Adam and Eve forfeited their perfect relationship with God.—Rev. 12:9; Gen. 2:9, 16, 17; 3:1-6.
5. How can we show appreciation for what Adam and Eve originally received from Jehovah?
5 Because God wants people to be happy, Adam expressed his delight in his wife. He said: "This time she is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh," and Eve realized that the serpent had misled her. (Gen. 3:12, 13) What a relief it is to have the truth! As loyal servants of Jehovah, we are deeply grateful. This is a great blessing indeed! For those who have been disfellowshipped, there is still hope, as each one can demonstrate repentance and prove himself worthy in God's eyes.
6. How can the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 give us comfort?
6 Satan's desire to ruin mankind originated when he tempted Eve, and Jehovah foretold how he would deal with such ones. That promise is found in the seed of the woman, which is explained throughout the Bible. (Read Genesis 3:15.) In connection with this promise, there is a symbolic head—the "serpent"—and a "seed" of the "woman." To fulfill this promise, Jehovah has allowed humans to understand what was involved in the dispute between his organization and the rebellious serpent, and to discern the meaning of the prophecies concerning the future. Furthermore, the Scriptures show that God did not send one of his angelic sons to become the promised Seed, but rather 'crushed' the Devil and sent his Son to earth to undo the damage caused by the serpent and his seed. This means continual warfare, but because of what Jehovah has done, there is hope.—John 3:16.
7. (a) What lesson does the experience of Adam and Eve teach us? (b) Does the Bible say that husbands should dominate their wives?
7 Adam and Eve experienced a loss of perfection, and they also lost other things. For example, Eve and her offspring were deprived of life in perfection, and of the prospect of living forever. Their offspring have inherited imperfection and weakness, and some are inclined to wrongdoing, so we see many problems arise among people. (Gen. 3:16) The Bible says that wives should submit to their husbands, but not in a way that violates love. Also, husbands should treat their wives with consideration. (Eph. 5:33) Other people who have been wronged can find comfort knowing that wrongs will be made right eventually, or they can take legal action.
THE LESSON FROM ADAM'S FALL TO THE FLOOD OF NOAH
8. How can you explain briefly the period from Adam's fall to the flood of Noah?
8 Adam and Eve began to have children. (Gen. 5:4) One of their sons, Cain, murdered his brother Abel. A descendant of Cain named Lamech boasted about killing a man. (Gen. 4:17, 19) From Adam's fall to the flood of Noah, many people turned away from Jehovah. Some, however, like Abel, Enoch, and Noah and his family, remained faithful. The Bible says that Noah was "righteous and perfect in his generations" and that he walked with God. It also says that "the earth came to be filled with wickedness." The bad deeds of those people caused great pain and suffering, leading to the destruction of the wicked world of that time. And regarding this, it said: "The human's wickedness became very great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all day long."—Gen. 6:1-5.
9. What did Jehovah decide to do with the people during the time of Noah, and what does this teach us?
9 Jehovah decided to bring a great flood during the time of Noah to rid the earth of wickedness. During that time, people continued to practice violence and immorality, and because of this, they were called "Noah's generation," who were corrupt and deserving of destruction. (2 Pet. 2:5) Jesus spoke of the events surrounding the flood of Noah and similar events we will see in the future. (Read Matthew 24:37-39.) In the future, many people will refuse to acknowledge God's warning, and just as in the days of Noah, the world will continue to pursue its own selfish desires until God intervenes. Let us therefore strive to avoid things such as violence and immorality so that we can show our appreciation for Jehovah's love and mercy.
LESSONS FROM THE FLOOD TO THE TIME OF JESUS
10. (a) What are some important lessons we can learn from the account of Noah? (b) How can we apply the example of Abraham and Sarah when we face challenges?
10 Noah and his family saved themselves and everyone on the ark. But most of the people living at that time refused to heed the warning about the coming flood. Many people today also disregard warnings and do not take them seriously. For instance, Abraham (Abram) and his wife Sarai (Sarah) traveled to Canaan, which God had shown them, but they struggled to have a child, and their faith was tested. However, Jehovah helped them, and they eventually had a son, Isaac, demonstrating that God keeps his promises. Just as Jehovah provided a ram instead of Isaac, he can help his faithful servants overcome difficulties. Abraham showed his willingness to obey God, and Sarah demonstrated her faith by believing in God's promise. (Read 1 Peter 3:3-6.) And Abraham taught his son Isaac to respect Jehovah. And Isaac passed on what he learned to his son Jacob, whose 12 sons became the forefathers of the nation of Israel.
11. How did Moses lead the Israelites out of Egypt?
11 God used his power to deliver Jacob (Israel) from slavery. The Law given through Moses contained many laws that protected people's rights and prevented injustice. These laws helped the Israelites maintain their loyalty to Jehovah. (Read Instructions Regarding Laws 7:3, 4.) These laws also promoted peace among families and discouraged revenge. If someone committed a crime, the punishment should fit the offense, and there should be evidence to support the accusation. Justice required fairness, and the laws helped ensure this. For example, a man might offer to pay compensation to a woman's father to settle a dispute, but only if she willingly agreed. (Ex. 24:1) And if the 'compensation' seemed inadequate, we can be sure that the matter would be investigated thoroughly.—Prov. 19:18.
REMEMBER WHAT YOU HAVE LEARNED AND APPLY IT
12, 13. (a) What are some ways that the priests in Malachi's time were failing to live up to their privileges? (b) Why might a person feel justified in divorcing his wife, or why might a husband want to divorce her?
12 In the days of the prophet Malachi, many priests were abusing their privilege of dissolving marriages. They were using the law to justify divorcing their wives for trivial reasons, perhaps because they wanted to marry someone younger or more appealing. But such divorces displeased Jehovah. Jesus later explained that the priests were misusing the law to dissolve marriages "for every sort of reason," and this was wrong. (Matt. 19:3) Jehovah hates any misuse of the privilege of dissolving marriage.—Read Malachi 2:13-16.
13 Christians today strive to use the principle of dissolving marriage properly. Should a Christian dismiss his wife or a wife dismiss her husband if one of them commits adultery and refuses to repent? Such a person shows that he does not value the marriage and may be disfellowshipped. (1 Cor. 5:11-13) And what about being influenced by worldly thinking and desiring something better—something that seems like "fruit from a tree of knowledge concerning good and bad"? (Luke 3:8; 2 Cor. 2:5-10) The scriptures show that if a person who has professed faith chooses to pursue such a course, he should be disfellowshipped, and his influence on God's people should be stopped. Otherwise, wickedness will spread. So if a scripture is misused, whether now or in the past, it can lead to serious consequences. It can cause those involved to stumble and fall spiritually. And if a person is disfellowshipped, he may find it difficult to recover. But if he repents, he may be restored, depending on his fruitage.—Acts 14:10-12; see also the November 15, 1979, Watchtower (Kenya), pages 31-32.
THE CHRISTIAN MARRIAGE
14. What will we discuss now?
14 The Mosaic Law was in effect for nearly 1,500 years. It provided God's people with a foretaste of what life would be like under Messiah's Kingdom, and it pointed forward to Jesus Christ. (Acts 3:23, 24) However, the Mosaic Law was superseded when Jesus came. God had purposed this. (Heb. 8:6) Therefore, some aspects of the Law no longer apply.
15. (a) Why is the principle of Christian marriage important? (b) How can a Christian demonstrate that he values marriage?
15 Jesus emphasized the original standard set by Adam. Moses allowed divorce because of the hardness of their hearts, saying: "It is for this reason that a man must leave his father and mother and adhere to his wife." (Matt. 19:6-8) Jesus showed that God's purpose is for marriage to last a lifetime. (1 Tim. 3:2, 12) Although some individuals may find it difficult to live together harmoniously, and despite imperfections and a lack of love on occasion, a loving and devoted couple should strive to make their marriage succeed. A person should not think about divorcing unless there is a valid Scriptural ground for doing so. (Matt. 19:9) As Hosea demonstrated toward his unfaithful wife, Gomer, a forgiving attitude can help a troubled marriage survive. And just as Jehovah forgave Israel despite their unfaithfulness, so too a husband may choose to forgive his erring mate. (Hosea 3:1-5) But if a person repeatedly commits adultery and refuses to repent, the situation is different, and the Bible provides grounds for dissolving the marriage.
16. Did Jesus say that a person is ever permitted to get divorced or remarried?
16 Jesus recognized that Christians may sometimes have to dissolve a marriage for valid Scriptural reasons. He made an exception for those who were part of the "uncircumcised heart" class—those who found it impossible to remain unmarried or chaste. He said that such ones could 'make themselves eunuchs.' (Matt. 19:10-12) Many people wrongly believe that being unmarried or chaste is undesirable. They feel that it is something to be ashamed of. It is important to weigh matters carefully in the light of Bible principles.
17. What can help a Christian to decide whether to stay married (or get divorced)?
17 What can help a person to decide whether to stay married (or get divorced) or not? A person should strive to remain faithful in his marriage, as this is pleasing to God. The apostle Paul acknowledged that a person might find it difficult to remain faithful. However, he also stated: "The wife does not have authority over her own body, but her husband does; and likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but his wife does." He further explained: "Do not deprive each other except by mutual consent, temporarily, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer, but then come together again." Divorce or separation should only be considered as a last resort when there is a serious problem that threatens spiritual well-being or life itself. Also, some may choose divorce or separation simply because they want to avoid dealing with problems. But the apostle wrote: "If a woman leaves her husband [even if she remains legally unmarried], let her keep on being unmarried, or else reconcile herself with him." (1 Cor. 7:2, 9, 36; 1 Tim. 4:1-3) A person should not seek divorce just because he feels dissatisfied or wants to marry someone else. Why not? Because a person who divorces often causes great pain and emotional distress, and a divorced or separated person may experience feelings of guilt and shame.
18, 19. (a) What factors can influence a Christian's decision regarding marriage? (b) What important principle should guide us?
18 A Christian who decides to separate should endeavor to please Jehovah and conduct himself properly throughout the process, and should not associate with those who practice immorality. It is vital to maintain neutrality and avoid taking sides. Remember, Christians must avoid becoming involved in "the world's legal disputes." (1 Cor. 7:39) Sound Bible principles, rather than secular laws, should guide our decisions regarding divorce or separation.
19 This important principle is rooted in God's Word, which helps people to deal with difficult situations and to resist "distressing times" and immoral influences. (2 Tim. 3:1-5) By means of his spirit, Jehovah can strengthen us to uphold righteous standards and to continue associating with fellow worshippers.—Matt. 7:13, 14.

text:
"Ũla Veva mwene [ũkũsĩĩaa] vamwe na maveva maitũ, kana ithyĩ twĩ syana sya Ngai."—ALO. 8:16.
MBATHI: 5, 14
1-3. Nĩ maũndũ meva matumaa Vendekosito yĩthĩwa yĩ ya mwanya, na maũndũ asu meanĩisye ata kĩla Maandĩko mathanĩte? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
MŨTHENYA ũmwe kwĩ Wakyumwa mwakanĩ wa 33 Klĩsto aminĩte kũsyawa kĩndũ ta saa itatũ sya kwakya, nĩkweekĩkie ũndũ wa mwanya ndũanĩ ya Yelusaleme. Mũthenya ũsu waĩ wa mwanya mũno mũno kwa andũ ala maĩ ndũanĩ ĩsu. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ũsu waĩ mũthenya wa sikũkũ ya Vendekosito na waĩ o mũthenya wa savato. Tũivika saa isu nthembo ila syakothaa kumw'a kwakya ĩkalũnĩ nĩsyaumĩtw'e. Yu saa isu andũ meew'ĩte mũyo mũno nũndũ mũthembi mũnene eeyũmbanĩasya kumya ĩla nthembo ya kũvyũlw'a ya imũtũ ilĩ syĩ ĩlawa, ila syauĩtwe na ũsyao wa mbee wa nganũ. (Ali. 23:15-20) Kumw'a kwa nthembo ĩsu kwoonanasya kana ngetha ya nganũ nĩyambĩĩa.
2 Maũndũ asu maendeee kwĩkĩka ĩkalũnĩ, ve ũndũ ũngĩ wa vata mũno vyũ wakilyĩ kwĩkĩka o ndũanĩ ĩsu vandũ nyũmbanĩ ya ĩũlũ. Nyũmbanĩ ĩsu vaĩ na Aklĩsto ta 120, ala moombanĩte "makĩvoya na kĩthing'ĩĩsyo." (Meko 1:13-15) Ũndũ ũla wakilyĩ kwĩkĩka vau maĩ wakonanĩtye mũno na maũndũ ala meekawa nĩ mũthembi mũnene kĩla mũthenya wa Vendekosito, na waĩ wĩanĩsyo wa wathani ũla mwathani Yoeli waumĩtye myaka ta 800 mĩvĩtu. (Yoe. 2:28-32; Meko 2:16-21) Kyo nĩ kyaũ kya vata kyaĩ kĩtonya kwĩkĩka?
3 Soma Meko ma Atũmwa 2:2-4. Veva mũtheu wa Ngai nĩwetĩkĩw'e nguthu ya Aklĩsto, ĩla yoombanĩte vau nyũmbanĩ ya ĩũlũ. (Meko 1:8) Aklĩsto asu nĩmambĩĩe kwathana, kana kumya ũkũsĩ, ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ma ũsengy'o ala meyoneete na kwĩw'a. O na vatathelete ĩvinda, nĩvoombanie nguthu nene, na mũtũmwa Vetelo nĩwambĩĩe kũmĩelesya kĩla kyaendeee. Na ĩndĩ atavya ethukĩĩsya asu make atĩĩ: 'Alyũlai ngoo, na mũivatiswa kĩla mũndũ syĩtwanĩ ya Yesũ Klĩsto, mwone ũekeo wa naĩ syenyu; na mũkoosa mũthĩnzĩo wa veva mũtheu.' Ĩla meewie ũu, andũ ta 3,000 nĩmeetĩkĩlile ũndũ Vetelo wameie na mavatiswa, na moosa ũla veva mũtheu mathĩtwe.—Meko 2:37, 38, 41.
4. (a) Nĩkĩ maũndũ ala meekĩkaa mũthenya wa Vendekosito nĩ ma vata kwitũ? (b) Nĩ ũndũ ũngĩ wĩva wa vata ũtonya kwĩthĩwa weekĩkie mũthenyanĩ o ta ũsu myaka mingĩ ĩtina? (Sisya maelesyo ma mũthya.)
4 Nĩkĩ Vendekosito ya mwaka wa 33 nĩ ya vata kwitũ? Ti nũndũ wa kĩla kyeekĩkie ĩkalũnĩ Yelusaleme. Vandũ va ũu, nĩ ya vata nũndũ Yesũ Klĩsto, ũla nĩwe Mũthembi Mũnene vyũ, nĩweanĩisye maũndũ ala maelekanaw'a nĩ kĩla kyeekĩkaa ĩkalũnĩ kĩla mũthenya wa Vendekosito. [1] Maũndũ meva? Mũthenya ũsu mũthembi mũnene nĩwaumĩasya Yeova imũtũ ilĩ ĩkalũnĩ. Imũtũ isu syekĩĩtwe ĩlawa syaelekanasya amanyĩw'a ala manyuvĩtwe kuma andũnĩ me na naĩ na maketĩkĩw'a mauta matw'ĩke ana ma Ngai. Kwondũ wa ũu nzĩa yeethĩiwe yavingũwa nĩ kana "mosyao ma mbee" kuma andũnĩ makwate mwanya wa kwĩsa kũthi ĩtunĩ, na maisumbĩka Ũsumbĩnĩ ũla ũkaetee andũ ala angĩ ewi moathimo matatalĩka. (Yak. 1:18; 1 Vet. 2:9) Kwoou twĩthĩwe twĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ kana wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ, maũndũ ala meekĩkie mũthenya ũsu nĩmatũkonetye mũno!
ŨNDŨ MŨKLĨSTO WĨTĨKĨAW'A MAUTA
5. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana Mũklĩsto ainyuvwa atw'ĩke mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta ndetĩkĩaw'a veva mũtheu ũndũ ũmwe kana ĩvinda yĩmwe na ũla ũngĩ?
5 Keka waĩ ũmwe wa amanyĩw'a ala mekalĩlwe mũtwe nĩ syĩndũ iilyĩ ta nĩ nĩmĩ sya mwaki, ndwĩsa kũlwa nĩ mũthenya ũsu. O na ndwĩthĩwa na nzika kana nĩwĩtĩkĩw'e veva mũtheu, na mũno mũno ethĩwa nĩwakwata mũthĩnzĩo wa kũneena na kĩthyomo ũtesĩ. (Meko 2:6-12) Ĩndĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta onthe metĩkĩaw'a na nzĩa ya ũsengy'o o tondũ ala amanyĩw'a ta 120 metĩkĩw'e? Aiee. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ o na ala angĩ maĩ Yelusaleme mũthenya ũsu mesie kwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta maivatiswa. (Meko 2:38) Na ĩla metĩkĩiw'e vai nĩmĩ sya mwaki syaaoneka mĩtwenĩ yoo. O na eka ũu, ti Aklĩsto onthe maitw'ĩka etĩkĩw'a mauta metĩkĩaw'a veva mũtheu ĩla meũvatiswa. Mo Asamalia metĩkĩw'e veva mũtheu kavinda kanini mamina kũvatiswa. (Meko 8:14-17) Ĩndĩ kwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta kwa Kolinelio na andũ make kwaĩ kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na ũndũ andũ meesĩ nũndũ metĩkĩw'e veva mũtheu o na mate avatise.—Meko 10:44-48.
6. Etĩkĩw'a mauta onthe methĩawa manengetwe kyaũ, na kĩmaĩkĩĩthasya ata?
6 Kwoou etĩkĩw'a mauta mayaaĩtĩkĩw'a veva mũtheu ũndũ ũmwe kana ĩvinda yĩmwe. Nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa amwe meetĩkĩlile vau kwa vau kana nĩmetĩkĩw'a mauta, namo angĩ noĩthwa makuie ĩvinda kwĩtĩkĩla kana nĩ etĩkĩw'a mauta. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa kĩla ũmwe etĩkĩw'e veva mũtheu ata, onthe methĩawa na kĩla mũtũmwa Vaulo wakĩeleisye na ndeto ii: 'Mwamwĩtĩkĩla, nĩmwekĩiwe ũsiĩlo, naw'o nĩ veva mũtheu ũla wathaniwe, nake nĩ ngwatĩlĩlyo ya ũtiĩwa witũ.' (Aev. 1:13, 14) Ĩla metĩkĩw'a veva mũtheu, veva ũsu wĩthĩawa ũtonya kũelekanw'a na ngwatĩlĩlyo, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kĩndũ kya kũmaĩkĩĩthya nĩ anyuve methi ĩtunĩ. Nũndũ wa ngwatĩlĩlyo ĩsu wakwata, Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta ndethĩawa na nzika kana nĩ mũnyuve.—Soma 2 Akolintho 1:21, 22; 5:5.
7. No nginya kĩla Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta eke ata nĩ kana ekwata mũthĩnzĩo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ?
7 Ĩndĩ ũu nĩkwonany'a kana Mũklĩsto akwata ngwatĩlĩlyo ĩsu ndatĩa kũthi ĩtunĩ? Aiee. Kĩla wĩthĩawa ate na nzika nakyo nĩ kana we nĩmũthokye. Ĩndĩ enda ekwata mũthĩnzĩo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ no nginya ekale e mũĩkĩĩku. Vetelo aisye ũũ ĩũlũ wa ũndũ ũsu: 'Kwondũ wa ũu, ana-a-asa, thangaai mũno mũlũlũmĩlye kwĩtwa kwenyu na kũnyuvwa kwenyu: nũndũ ethĩwa nĩmũkwĩka maũndũ asu, mũikalulutĩka o na ĩndĩĩ: Nũndũ o ũu mũkanengwa na ũlau kũlika ũsumbĩnĩ wa tene na tene wa Mwĩaĩi waitũ na Mũtangĩĩi Yesũ Klĩsto.' (2 Vet. 1:10, 11) Kwoou no nginya kĩla Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta atate ũndũ vatonyeka ekale e mũĩkĩĩku. Aema kwĩka ũu, wĩto ũla wakwatie wa kũthi ĩtunĩ ndũkamũtethya.—Aevl. 3:1; Ũvu. 2:10.
MŨNDŨ AMANYAA ATA?
8, 9. (a) Nĩkĩ andũ aingĩ monaa ve vinya mũno kũelewa ũndũ mũndũ wĩtĩkĩaw'a mauta? (b) Mũndũ amanyaa ata kana e na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ?
8 Ũmũnthĩ andũ aingĩ ma Ngai no mone ve vinya mũno kũelewa ũndũ mũndũ wĩtĩkĩaw'a veva mũtheu. Na nengĩ nĩ w'o ti laisi kũelewa nũndũ ũsu nĩ ũndũ ũtaamakwata. Kĩeleelo kya Ngai kĩyaĩ andũ mekale ĩtunĩ ĩndĩ kyaĩ mekale ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene. (Mwa. 1:28; Sav. 37:29) O na ũu wĩ o vo, Ngai nĩwĩkĩte mũvango wa mwanya mũno wa kũnyuva amwe metw'ĩka asumbĩ na athembi ĩtunĩ. Ĩla Ngai wanyuva ũmwe, mosũanĩo make na mawoni make nĩmavĩndũkaa mũno, na nĩwambĩĩaa kwĩthĩwa na mea ma kũthi ĩtunĩ.—Soma Aeveso 1:18.
9 Ĩndĩ mũndũ amanyaa ata kana e na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, nũnengetwe ĩla ngwatĩlĩlyo? Ũsũngĩo wĩ ndetonĩ ila Vaulo waandĩkĩe Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta ala maĩ Lomi, ala "meetiwe methĩwe atheu." Ameie: 'Mũiaaosa veva wa ũkombo ĩngĩ ũetae w'ĩa; ĩndĩ nĩmwoosie veva wa kũtuwa ana, kwondũ wa ũu nĩtwĩkaĩlaa, tũkyasya, Nau, Asa. Ũla Veva mwene akũsĩĩaa vamwe na maveva maitũ, kana ithyĩ twĩ syana sya Ngai.' (Alo. 1:7; 8:15, 16) Kwa ũkuvĩ, Ngai atũmĩaa veva mũtheu kũĩkĩĩthya mũndũ kana nũthoketw'e ĩtunĩ esumbĩka Ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ngai.—1 Ath. 2:12.
10. Ĩandĩko ya 1 Yoana 2:27 yĩthĩawa yĩyonany'a ata ĩla yĩkwasya kana etĩkĩw'a mauta mai na vata wa kũmanyĩw'a nĩ mũndũ ũngĩ?
10 Ala metĩtwe nĩ Ngai methi kũsumbĩka ĩtunĩ mayĩthĩawa me na vata wa kũkũsĩĩwa nĩ mũndũ. Mayĩthĩawa me na vata wa mũndũ ũngĩ amaĩkĩĩthye kĩla kĩkĩkie nthĩnĩ woo. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ ĩla Yeova wamina kũmanyuva, ndamatiaa me na nzika o na vanini ilĩkonĩ syoo na ngoonĩ syoo. Mũtũmwa Yoana aandĩkĩe Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta atĩĩ: "Mwĩ amenesye mauta [kana, etĩkĩsye mauta] kuma kwa ũla Mũtheu, na nĩmwĩsĩ maũndũ onthe." Aendeeie kwasya: "Nenyu, kũmenew'a mauta kũla mwanengiwe nĩwe nĩkwĩkalĩte nthĩnĩ wenyu na mũi na vata wa kũmanyĩw'a nĩ mũndũ; ĩndĩ nũndũ kũmenew'a mauta kũla kumaa kwake nĩkũmũmanyĩasya maũndũ onthe, na nĩ kwa w'o, na ti ũvũngũ, na o ũndũ kwamũmanyĩisye, ĩkalai nthĩnĩ wake." (1 Yoa. 2:20, 27) Etĩkĩw'a mauta nĩmendaa kũmanyĩw'a nĩ Yeova o ta andũ ala angĩ. Ĩndĩ mayĩthĩawa na vata wa kũmanyĩw'a, kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kũĩkĩĩthw'a nĩ mũndũ kana mo nĩ etĩkĩsye mauta. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ nĩmaĩkĩĩthĩtw'e ũu nĩ vinya ũla mũnene vyũ, naw'o nĩ ũla veva mũtheu wa Ngai!
ŨNDŨ 'MASYAAWA ĨNGĨ'
11, 12. Nĩ makũlyo meva Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta ũtonya kwĩkũlya, ĩndĩ nĩ ũndũ wĩva ũtesa kwĩthĩwa na nzika naw'o?
11 Ĩla veva mũtheu wakũsĩĩa Mũklĩsto kana nĩwetĩkĩw'a mauta, Mũklĩsto ũsu nũvĩndũkaa mũno. Yesũ aeleisye ũndũ ũsu asya kana kũu nĩ 'kũsyawa kuma ĩũlũ,' kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, kũsyawa ĩngĩ. [2] (Yoa. 3:3, 5) O na aendeeie kũelesya ũndũ ũsu atĩĩ: "Ndũkaseng'e nũndũ nakwĩa, Mũvaka mũsyawe kuma ĩũlũ. Kĩseve nĩkĩuutanaa o kũla kĩkwenda, naku nĩwĩw'aa wasya wakyo, ĩndĩ ndwĩsĩ kũla kyumaa, na kũla kĩendaa: nĩw'o wĩthĩawa ũla ũsyaĩtwe nĩ Veva." (Yoa. 3:7, 8) Nĩ w'o, ti ũndũ wĩ laisi kũelesya nesa mũndũ ũte mũnyuve ũndũ ala anyuve mew'aa.
12 No kwĩthĩwa andũ ala metĩkĩw'e mauta matonya kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Nĩkĩ ninyie nĩnyuviwe? Nĩkĩ vatananyuvwa mũndũ ũngĩ eka nyie?' O na no mone mo mataĩle kũnyuvwa. Ĩndĩ mayĩthĩawa na nzika kana nĩmanyuvĩtwe. Nĩmew'aa mũyo mwingĩ na nĩmatũngaa mũvea nũndũ wa mũthĩnzĩo ũsu. Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta mew'aa tondũ Vetelo weew'aa ĩla waveveewe kũandĩka ndeto ii: "Nakathwe Ngai, Ĩthe wa Mwĩaĩi waitũ Yesũ Klĩsto, ũla kwĩanana na tei wake mwingĩ watũsyaie ĩngĩ twĩthĩwe na wĩkwatyo wĩ thayũ kwondũ wa kũthayũũka kwa Yesũ Klĩsto kuma akw'ũnĩ, twĩthĩwe na ũtiĩwa ũtanangĩkaa, na ũtavukaa, na ũtathelaa, wiĩtwe ĩtunĩ kwondũ wenyu." (1 Vet. 1:3, 4) Ĩla etĩkĩw'a mauta masoma ndeto isu mayĩthĩawa na nzika nongi kana nĩmo meũtavw'a ndeto isu nĩ Ĩthe woo wa ĩtunĩ.
13. Ala metĩkĩw'a mauta maalyũkaa ata, na nĩ kyaũ kĩtumaa maalyũka?
13 Mũklĩsto mwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta atanamba kũkũsĩĩwa nĩ veva wa Ngai, aĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ. Nĩwaĩ na mea ma kwĩsa kwona ĩvinda yĩla Yeova ũkathesya nthĩ ĩno, na nĩwendaa kwona aiathimwa mũno vamwe na ala angĩ. O na nũtonya kwĩthĩwa akũnaa visa aithokya andũ ala make makwie maumĩte mbũanĩ. Nĩwendaa kwona ailyĩ vandũ wĩyakĩe we mwene na aiya matunda ma mĩtĩ wĩvandĩe. (Isa. 65:21-23) Nĩkĩ ĩndĩ mosũanĩo make mavĩndũkie? Ti atĩ eekie kwĩw'a akola wĩkwatyo ũsu. O na ti atĩ eekie kũvĩndũa mesilya nũndũ wa mathĩna maito waĩ namo ngoonĩ kana mathĩna angĩ maingĩ. Ndaakola kwĩthĩwa na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ aĩ nũndũ oonie kwĩkala kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ tene na tene ta kũtonya kwĩthĩwa na mĩnoo kana ũtulu, o na ti atĩ endaa akwate kamwanya ka kũmanya ĩtunĩ. Ĩndĩ aalyũkile nũndũ veva mũtheu wa Ngai nĩwamwĩtie, kana nĩwamũthokisye, na wasyoka waalyũla mosũanĩo make na wĩkwatyo wake.
14. Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta mew'aa ata ĩla me kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ?
14 Ĩndĩ ĩkũlyo nĩ, Nĩtwaĩle kwona etĩkĩw'a mauta ta mendaa mũno kũkw'a nĩ kana mathi ĩtunĩ? Vaulo aveveeiwe aandĩka atĩĩ: 'Tũendee kwĩkala ĩeemanĩ yĩĩ ya kũũ nthĩ, nĩtũlumaa tũyĩw'a twĩ avinyĩĩe. Ti atĩ twĩenda mwĩĩ ũũ twĩ naw'o wa kũũ nthĩ ũvetwe, ĩndĩ twĩenda ũvw'ĩkwe ũla wumaa ĩtunĩ, nĩ kana kĩla kĩkusaa kĩmelw'e nĩ thayũ.' (2 Ako. 5:4, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) Kwoou mayĩthĩawa manoetw'e nĩ kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ, ũkethĩa nĩ ta mekwenda makw'e mĩtũkĩ ũndũ vatonyeka. Kĩvathũkany'o na ũu, nĩmendaa mũno kũtũmĩa kĩla mũthenya me kũũ nthĩ kũmũthũkũma Yeova me vamwe na anyanyae moo na andũ ma mũsyĩ. Ĩndĩ o na ethĩwa makwetye ata, mayĩsaa kũlwa nĩ wĩkwatyo mũseo ki ũla me naw'o wa ĩvinda yũkĩte.—1 Ako. 15:53; 2 Vet. 1:4; 1 Yoa. 3:2, 3; Ũvu. 20:6.
WE WĨ NA WĨTO WA KŨTHI ĨTUNĨ?
15. Nĩ maũndũ meva matesa kwonany'a kana mũndũ nĩwĩtĩkĩw'e mauta?
15 No kwĩthĩwa wĩkũlasya kana wĩ ũmwe katĩ wa ala me na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. Ethĩwa nĩwonaa ta wĩ ũmwe mũnyuve, kwasũanĩa makũlyo aa ma vata. We nĩwĩthĩawa na kĩthito kingĩ mũno ũtavany'anĩ? We nĩwĩthĩawa na kĩthito kingĩ kya kwĩmanyĩsya Ndeto ya Ngai, na nĩwendete kwĩka ũkunĩkĩli ĩũlũ wa "maũndũ maliku ma Ngai"? (1 Ako. 2:10) Nĩwonete Yeova aikũathima kwa nzĩa ya mwanya ũtavany'anĩ? Nĩwĩw'aa wendete mũno kwĩka kwenda kwa Yeova? Nĩwĩw'aa wendete mũno vyũ kũtetheesya ala angĩ mamũthũkũme Yeova? Na nĩwĩyoneete Yeova aikũtetheesya maũndũnĩ mana? Ethĩwa wasũngĩa makũlyo asu wasya, "Ĩĩ," kw'o kũu nĩ kwonany'a kana wĩ na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ? Aiee, ti w'o. Nĩkĩ ti w'o? Nũndũ ala me na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ ti mo me oka methĩawa mailyĩ ũu. Veva wa Yeova ũtetheeasya ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ nthĩ tene na tene o ũndũ ũmwe na ũndũ ũtetheeasya ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. Na eka ũu, ethĩwa nĩwĩthĩawa na nzika kana wĩ na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ, ũndũ ũsu wĩonany'a kana ndwĩ na wĩto ũsu. Ala manyuvĩtwe nĩ Yeova mayĩthĩawa na nzika kana nũmanyuvĩte! Methĩawa mesĩ nesa ki!
16. Nĩkĩ tũtonya kwasya kana ti onthe maakwata veva mũtheu wa Ngai me na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ?
16 Maandĩko nĩmawetete aũme aingĩ maĩ na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu, ala veva mũtheu wathũkũmaa na vinya mũnene nthĩnĩ woo, o na kau mayaĩ na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. Ũmwe woo aĩ Yoana Mũvatisi. Yesũ nĩwamũkathie Yoana mũno ĩndĩ asyoka asya ndakethĩwa ũmwe katĩ wa ala makasumbĩka Ũsumbĩnĩ wa ĩtu. (Mt. 11:10, 11) O nake Ndaviti nĩwatongoew'e nĩ veva mũtheu. (1 Sam. 16:13) Veva mũtheu nĩwamũtetheeisye aelewa maũndũ maliku ĩũlũ wa Yeova, o na nĩwaveveeiwe aandĩka ilungu kauta sya Mbivilia. (Mko. 12:36) Ĩndĩ mũthenya wa Vendekosito, Vetelo aisye kana Ndaviti "ndaambata ĩtunĩ." (Meko 2:34) O na kau veva mũtheu nĩwathũkũmaa na vinya mũnene nthĩnĩ wa andũ asu, ndwaamakũsĩĩa kana nĩ anyuve methi ĩtunĩ. Ũu ndwaaonany'a kana ve vandũ matielye kana mayaaĩlĩte. Ĩndĩ woonanisye kana Yeova akamathayũũkya mekale nthĩ nzaũ.—Yoa. 5:28, 29; Meko 24:15.
17, 18. (a) Athũkũmi aingĩ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ me na wĩkwatyo wĩva? (b) Nĩ makũlyo meva masũngĩĩtwe ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe?
17 Athũkũmi aingĩ ma Ngai ũmũnthĩ mai na wĩto wa kũthi ĩtunĩ. Me na wĩkwatyo o ũla waĩ na Ndaviti, Yoana Mũvatisi, na aũme na aka aingĩ aĩkĩĩku ma tene. O ta Avalaamu, meteele mũno kwĩsa kwĩkala masumbĩkĩtwe nĩ Ũsumbĩ wa Ngai. (Aevl. 11:10) Namo ala yu matiele katĩ wa ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi kũsumbĩka ĩtunĩ nĩ avũthũ mũno. (Ũvu. 12:17) Ũu wĩonany'a kana aingĩ katĩ wa ala 144,000 manyuvĩtwe nĩmakwie me aĩkĩĩku.
18 Kwoou ala me na wĩkwatyo wa kwĩkala kũũ ĩũlũ wa nthĩ maĩle kwĩthĩwa na woni mwaũ moona Mũklĩsto ũkwasya e na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ? Nao woona ũmwe kĩkundinĩ kyenyu aiya kĩmũtũ na ainyw'a mbinyu ĩvindanĩ ya Kyaũya kya Wĩoo kya Mwĩaĩi, waĩle kwĩka ata? Nĩwaĩlĩte kũthĩnĩka woona ũtalo wa ala maasyaa me na wĩkwatyo wa kũthi ĩtunĩ ũendeee kwongeleka? Makũlyo asu nĩmasũngĩĩtwe ĩsomonĩ yĩla yĩatĩĩe.
^ [1] (kalungu ka 4) Vendekosito nĩtonya kwĩthĩwa yeethĩawa o mũthenya ũla Mose wanengeiwe Mĩao kĩĩmanĩ kya Sinai. (Kuma 19:1) Ethĩwa ũu nĩw'o vailyĩ, o tondũ Mose watũmĩiwe nĩ Yeova kũlikya mbaĩ ya Isilaeli ũtianĩonĩ wa Mĩao mũthenya ũsu, now'o Yesũ Klĩsto walikilye ĩla mbaĩ nzaũ, kana Isilaeli ma kĩ-veva, ũla ũtianĩonĩ mweũ o mũthenya ta ũsu.
^ [2] (kalungu ka 11) Nĩ kana ũkwate ũvoo mwingangĩ ĩũlũ wa kũsyawa ĩngĩ, sisya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 01/04/2009, ĩth. 3-11.

translation:
"Let Veva also be with the mature ones, along with the other older men, or perhaps we will look for God's approval."—1CO. 8:16.
PARAGRAPHS: 5, 14
1-3. What things motivate Christians to give priority to their ministry, and what does this have to do with understanding Bible prophecy? (Consider the points mentioned.)
ONE day in 33 C.E., a Christian was able to travel about three hours on foot from Jerusalem. That day was a busy day for people in those areas. Why? Because that day was a weekday and also the Sabbath. We take time now to examine why they were so busy traveling at that time. Today many people make similar efforts because of the important work of proclaiming the good news, but they are motivated by love for God. (Acts 23:15-20) The desire to accomplish this work and the urgency felt can be very strong.
2 These matters continue to stand out, but there is another factor that contributed to the busyness of people in those days. In those days there were about 120 disciples with Christ, but they were "constantly together in prayer." (Acts 1:13-15) This constant activity helped them to connect with one another and with other things that were important during that Pentecost season, and it fulfilled a prophecy Joel had made some 800 years earlier. (Joe. 2:28-32; Acts 2:16-21) So what lesson can we learn from this example?
3 Read Acts 2:2-4. The power of God was manifested on the day of Christ, but it affected those present in Jerusalem. (Acts 1:8) Christ has ascended to heaven, or gone away, so the things he taught will be accomplished and realized. And when they asked him, he told them to wait for the promised power, and the apostle Peter instructed them to be steadfast in everything. And now those who accepted his message said: "Brothers, what should we do?" He replied, "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit." But because of this, about 3,000 people responded to Peter's message and were baptized, and they received the gift of the Holy Spirit.—Acts 2:37, 38, 41.
4. (a) What things that happened on the day of Pentecost stand out to us? (b) What is one reason why it is important to remember that event even after many years have passed? (Consider the examples.)
4 Why is the celebration of the year 33 significant to us? It marks the fulfillment of prophecies in Jerusalem. Those people, through Jesus Christ, who is the High Priest, fulfilled the things foretold concerning everything that would happen on that day of Pentecost. [1] What does this mean? On that day, the high priest presented an offering to Jehovah representing the entire nation. This offering symbolized their desire to maintain a clean standing with God and to continue enjoying his favor. Because of this, it is referred to as "bread from firstfruits" among those who appreciate the opportunity to approach God, and it surpasses the value of sacrifices made by individuals facing difficult circumstances. (Jas. 1:18; 1 Pet. 2:9) How grateful we should be for the opportunity to approach God or remain loyal, the things that happened on that day are very important to us!
THE CHRISTIAN MINISTRY IS IMPORTANT
5. How can Christians show that they appreciate the importance of the ministry by participating in it regularly, either individually or with others?
5 Let one of the elders oversee the arrangement so that everyone has a share, especially those who may feel shy. And encourage them with zeal, and help them improve their ability to speak confidently and effectively. (1 Tim. 2:6-12) Were all 120 disciples present when the holy spirit was poured out? No. Why? Because they were also in Jerusalem on that day receiving the gift of the holy spirit. (Acts 2:38) And although they received it during that time, it did not appear to all at once. Also, it wasn't just the apostles who received the gift of the holy spirit on that occasion. For example, Samaria received the gift of the holy spirit after being baptized. (Acts 8:14-17) Furthermore, the gift of the holy spirit was given to Cornelius and his household, demonstrating that even Gentiles could receive the gift.—Acts 10:44-48.
6. Does the Christian ministry have great value, and how can we demonstrate our appreciation for it?
6 The Christian ministry has immense value, and there is only one way to show appreciation for it. By supporting the full-time ministers financially and by praying for them, while others may contribute by helping them find lodging or assisting them in the ministry. But each one should be zealous in supporting the ministry, remembering Paul's encouraging words: "I have made you a minister, and yet I myself am not imprisoned, and yet you have become fellow partakers of my good cheer." (Phil. 1:13, 14) While supporting the ministry, remember that the quality of our support depends on our sincerity, or, rather, on our heartfelt desire. Therefore, let us always strive to give generously, like the Christians in Corinth, who were eager to prove their love.—Read 2 Corinthians 1:21, 22; 5:5.
7. What should each Christian minister possess in order to be effective?
7 How can a Christian minister demonstrate his zeal for the ministry? Indeed. Every preacher needs faith, and he also needs courage. However, a minister's zeal for the ministry should motivate him to take the initiative. Consider this counsel: "For this very reason make progress in loving one another and in showing consideration for others, so that your love may increase more and more, just as we instruct you, and indeed you are doing. And may Jehovah himself grant that your love overflow toward one another and toward all people, so that you may strengthen one another, just as we are instructing you." (2 Thess. 1:10, 11) Let each Christian minister continue to take the initiative. Moreover, let the desire to be effective spur him on.—Eph. 3:1; Col. 2:10.
IS IT CLEAR?
8, 9. (a) Why do many people fail to appreciate the value of the Christian ministry? (b) Does a person need to be an evangelizer to have zeal for the ministry?
8 Many people do not fully appreciate the value of what ministers accomplish. And often they do not realize that understanding this matter is vital. God's Word shows that the ministry has been important since time immemorial. (Gen. 1:28; Ps. 37:29) Yet, despite this, God allows individuals to exercise their own free will in deciding whether to accept the good news. God respects our individuality, and his thoughts and ways are high, and he helps us to appreciate the importance of the ministry.—Read Ephesians 1:18.
9 If a person does not know how to respond to the ministry, or if he is busy, should we give up? An example is when Paul wrote to Christians in Rome about certain matters, saying: "I commend you to Phoebe, a minister." He said: 'Receive her as befits a Christian, and extend hospitality to her, so that she may have assistance from you in whatever she may need.' Thus, fellow Christians assisted Phoebe and others who were traveling while carrying out their ministry. (Rom. 1:7; 8:15, 16) In this way, God uses ministers to help people who are honest-hearted and who desire spiritual food—God's provision.—1 Thess. 2:12.
10. Does the scripture at 1 John 2:27 suggest that an anointed one might become spiritually weak or that a Christian minister might stumble?
10 We can trust that God will strengthen us in times of difficulty and assist those who are being strengthened by him. Difficulties and trials may affect anyone. Why is this so? Because Jehovah allows Satan to test us, and we are imperfect humans. The apostle John wrote to Christians, saying: "If anyone practices sin [or, stumbles], we have someone interceding for us with the Father." He then explained: "And not only that, but also if anyone continues practicing sins, we have someone interceding for us with the Father, and it is by means of his righteousness that we receive forgiveness for our sins, and he cleanses us from all unrighteousness." (1 John 2:20, 27) Intercession helps us to maintain our relationship with Jehovah and with other faithful ones. So difficulties and trials, or even stumbling, do not necessarily mean that a person has abandoned God. Why is this so? Because it is often during such times that we especially appreciate the help of God's spirit!
THE MATTER OF 'OTHER SHEEP'
11, 12. What qualities does a dedicated Christian need to cultivate in order to be able to shepherd "other sheep," and why is it important to do so?
11 When a spiritual man or a dedicated Christian feels the need to shepherd "other sheep," he should first examine himself thoroughly. Jesus illustrated this need when he said that one must be "born again," or, in effect, born from above. [2] (John 3:3, 5) And he further explained this by saying: "Unless a man undergoes a new birth, he cannot see God's kingdom." (John 3:7, 8) It is therefore vital that a man carefully examine himself to determine whether he truly desires to serve others selflessly.
12 Those who feel the need to shepherd "other sheep" might ask themselves: 'Am I qualified? Will people accept my help?' But they should not let fear prevent them from offering their assistance. They should not become discouraged or think they are unworthy. They have much encouragement from the inspired words found in this prayer: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has caused us to be reborn to a hope alive through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, to an inheritance incorruptible and undefiled and unfading, reserved in the heavens for you." (1 Peter 1:3, 4) Dedicated Christians find comfort in knowing that God's spirit will empower them to carry out this work effectively.
13 Why do some dedicated Christians remain inactive, and what can cause them to become inactive?
13 A Christian who becomes inactive may be feeling overwhelmed by worldly concerns or may simply lack spiritual strength. He may also wonder how Jehovah feels about him and whether he appreciates his efforts. However, such ones should remember that Jehovah delights in those who show genuine faith and who strive to live in harmony with his principles. He wants to see them enjoy life and reap the fruits of their obedience. (Isaiah 65:21-23) Should they give up easily when facing difficulties? Not at all! They should continue to apply themselves diligently and not allow minor setbacks to discourage them. Let each one examine his own heart and determine whether he is truly seeking to serve Jehovah wholeheartedly, without being influenced by selfish interests or fears. If he is inactive, let him seek Jehovah's guidance and humbly request his help to regain his zeal and activity.
14 What further encouragement does a Christian receive to assist others?
14 Indeed, we want to encourage fellow Christians who may be struggling spiritually. The apostle Paul wrote: "Let us pay attention to exhortation, and stimulate one another to love and fine works, not forsaking the gathering of ourselves together." (Hebrews 10:24, The Holy Bible in Current Kikamba Language) We can strengthen our brothers and sisters by reminding them of the importance of remaining close to Jehovah and by helping them to overcome obstacles. In this way, we can demonstrate our love for them and build them up in their faith.—1 Corinthians 15:33; 2 Thessalonians 1:4; 1 John 3:2, 3; Revelation 20:6.
WHAT IF YOU STRUGGLE YOURSELF?
15 What things might cause a person to become inactive?
15 It is often because of discouragement or feeling overwhelmed. Sometimes a brother or sister feels inadequate, perhaps because of past mistakes. Are you battling negative thoughts? Are you wrestling with feelings of guilt over some mistake you made? Have you asked Jehovah to help you forgive yourself and to restore your joy?—1 Corinthians 2:10. Does Jehovah comfort you through his spirit? Are you determined to continue walking with Jehovah? Are you willing to share with others so they too will come to know Jehovah? And do you trust that Jehovah will bless your efforts? If you have struggled for a long time, do not give up hope. Remember the example of the prodigal son—Luke 15:11-32. Jehovah lovingly welcomes back those who return to him, and he helps them to make spiritual progress. Moreover, if you struggle with staying active, remember that your feelings do not always reflect reality. Others may appreciate your contributions more than you realize! Jehovah strengthens those who are determined to remain close to him and supports those who strive to stay active. And in addition, if you feel discouraged, remember that your feelings do not define you. Other faithful ones also experience similar struggles! Let us be compassionate and understanding!
16. Should we hesitate to seek help from mature Christians?
16 The Bible shows that many loyal servants were encouraged by counsel from others, especially when facing difficult circumstances. One such person was John the Baptist. Jesus commended John for being courageous enough to speak boldly despite opposition.—Matthew 11:10, 11. Also, David benefited from Samuel's encouragement.—1 Samuel 16:13. Mature Christians can help us understand Jehovah's principles and can encourage us to apply what we learn from the Scriptures.—Mark 12:36. For instance, during Pentecost, Peter quoted Psalm 16, which David had written years earlier.—Acts 2:34. But mature Christians also face challenges and sometimes feel inadequate. They may wonder if they are truly helping others. This is understandable, as they are imperfect humans. However, remember that Jehovah sees things differently.—John 5:28, 29; Mark 24:15.
17, 18. (a) What qualities do God value in those who support others? (b) Why is it important to meditate on fine examples?
17 God values the loyalty of those who encourage others. Like David, John the Baptist, and many others, they demonstrate courage and faith. And like Abraham, they may be willing to endure trials because of their loyalty to God.—Hebrews 11:10. Many faithful ones have helped others to remain steadfast in times of difficulty.—Proverbs 12:17. It is evident that many of the 144,000 will experience great joy in this work.
18 How can you show appreciation for those who kindly assist you in maintaining spiritual strength? Would you enjoy having someone visit you regularly, perhaps bringing a comforting scripture? Is it wise to continue to look for ways to strengthen fellow worshipers?—Consider the benefits of meditating on fine examples.

This law foreshadowed what would take place later; for Moses acted as mediator of the Law given through an angel, now Jesus Christ has become mediator of a superior covenant, or the new Israel, which is spiritual.
