translation:
"Do not make false oaths in my name,"—Mt. 5:33.
NOTES: 18, 7
1. (a) Why did Eve and Hannah feel compelled to lie? (Consider their circumstances.) (b) What lessons can we learn from their examples?
EVE and Hannah were both under great pressure. Eve was deceived by a spirit creature, and Hannah vowed to dedicate her son Samuel to Jehovah, but Eli misinterpreted her actions, thinking she was drunk. Both Eve and Hannah made promises they later regretted. However, there is one thing they had in common: They sought to please God in some way, and each of them felt responsible for fulfilling their vow. Many people today face similar pressures, feeling obligated to fulfill vows they have made to others or to themselves. But what lessons can we draw from this: Is making a vow wrong? Can a person make a vow without intending to keep it, and then simply disregard it when it becomes inconvenient? What does the example of Eve and Hannah teach us?
2, 3. (a) Is making a vow wrong? (b) What scriptures show that lying to God is wrong?
2 According to the Bible, making a vow is a solemn act of devotion to God. A person should not make a vow to God unless he is sincere and willing to fulfill it. Otherwise, it is like offering something worthless to God or trying to bargain with Him. It may involve a promise to do something good or to refrain from doing something bad. A Christian will carefully consider whether he can honestly fulfill his vow, and he will pray for guidance. Does God really care about our vows? God values honesty very much, and He expects Christians to be truthful in all their dealings, so that they will not regret their words or actions. (Matt. 14:22, 23; Eph. 6:16, 17) What scriptures highlight the importance of keeping one's word?
3 Moses' Law stated: "If anyone makes a vow to Jehovah, whether it involves abstaining from something . . ., he must certainly pay what he vowed; he must be blameless in connection with it." (Deut. 30:2) Solomon also wrote: "If you make a vow to God, do not delay paying it, because He takes no pleasure in foolish ones." (Eccl. 5:4) And Jesus emphasized that vows should be sincere when he said: "Let your 'yes' mean yes, and your 'no' mean no," Jehovah.—Matt. 5:33.
4 (a) Why should we take vows seriously? (b) What lessons can we learn from the examples of Jephthah and Hannah?
4 One reason why a person might approach God is to ask Him to fulfill a vow. By taking vows seriously, we show our devotion to Jehovah and strengthen our relationship with Him. David wrote: "Who may dwell on Your holy hill? . . . The one who does not go about with false speech, nor practice deception . . . and who does not harm his companion." (Ps. 24:3, 4) Did Jephthah and Hannah take vows seriously? And did they always fulfill their vows completely?
UNDERSTANDING VOWS MADE TO GOD
5 What did Jephthah vow, and with what result?
5 Jephthah vowed to Jehovah that if He would give him victory over Ammon, he would offer up whatever came out of the door of his house to meet him as a burnt offering. (Judg. 10:7-9) It happened that Jephthah's daughter came out to meet him, and he fulfilled his vow: "I have made a vow to Jehovah, and I will do it. She will be dedicated to Jehovah." With what result? The daughters of Israel mourned for her year after year. Jephthah's vow caused great sorrow. So we should be careful when making a 'vow to Jehovah.' (Judg. 11:30-34) Does Jehovah want His people to suffer because of the vows they make?
6. (a) How can we avoid causing ourselves grief over vows that Jephthah made? Explain. (b) How do Proverbs 23:21, 23 and Psalm 15:4 help us understand the proper way to make a vow to God?
6 If a person makes a foolish vow, does that mean that Jehovah approves of it and wants him to carry it out no matter how harmful it may be? No, and the reason is that Jehovah does not delight in senseless sacrifices. But this does not excuse anyone from being careless about making vows. It is important for Jephthah and his household to carefully consider the matter. Let each one examine himself thoroughly. We see here that Jephthah regretted his rash vow and wished he had been more thoughtful. His daughter also felt bad about it, thinking she was going to die childless. Jephthah had two reasons for fulfilling his vow. First, he did not want to break his promise to Jehovah, and second, he feared the consequences if he did. Jephthah said: "I have opened my mouth to Jehovah, and I cannot take back my word." And his daughter replied: "Let me alone to do what I have vowed." (Judg. 11:35-39) These people were among those who stumbled badly because they failed to appreciate the importance of sanctifying God's holy name, and their example serves as a warning to us.—Read The Watchtower of December 23, 2018, pages 21, 23; Psalm 15:4.
7. (a) What mistakes did Hannah make, and why did she make them? Was her prayer answered? (b) In contrast with Hannah's vow, what lesson can we learn from Samuel's example? (See supporting scriptures.)
7 Hannah sincerely dedicated her son to Jehovah. She dedicated her son to Jehovah willingly and cheerfully, knowing that she would have to give him up when he reached the age of being trained, and she was determined to fulfill her vow. (1 Sam. 1:4-7, 10, 16) Hannah prayed to God earnestly, saying: "O Jehovah of armies, if you will please look upon the affliction of your handmaid, and remember me, and do not forget your handmaid, but will give to your handmaid a male child, then I shall dedicate him to Jehovah all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head." * (1 Sam. 1:11) Hannah's prayer was answered, and she gave birth to a son. This should encourage us! Let us always trust in what God has promised. Notice how this woman expressed her joy when giving her son to the temple, saying: "I requested him from Jehovah."—1 Sam. 1:20.
8. (a) What moved Hannah to dedicate her son? Explain. (b) What circumstances led David to write Psalm 61 while showing confidence like Hannah did?
8 After Hannah prayed to Samuel earnestly, she remembered her vow to God. At that time Samuel was about three years old. Hannah was deeply distressed because of the provocation of her rivals. And year after year Samuel went with his father to Shiloh, and would pray there, and they would offer sacrifices, and Hannah would go up too. She would say: "I have vowed this child to Jehovah; and Jehovah will certainly fulfill what I have vowed to him. Therefore, I also devote him forever to Jehovah; as long as he lives he shall be devoted to Jehovah." (1 Sam. 1:24-28) Thus, "young Samuel grew up in the temple of the Lord." (1 Sam. 2:21) Why is this important? It is important because Hannah continued to bring her son to the temple each year, so that she could see him when she went up to worship. She showed her love for him by visiting him, comforting him, and teaching him. These things show how much a mother cares for her child who continues to serve in the sanctuary. So, just as Hannah kept praying earnestly to God, let us continue to pray to Jehovah.—1 Sam. 2:1, 2; read Psalm 61:1, 5, 8.
9. What reasons do we have for persevering?
9 How can we know whether our prayers are pleasing to God, and what practical steps can we take? Are there times when we find it difficult to pray earnestly?
PRAYERS THAT MOVE JEHOVAH'S HEART
10. What specific ways can a Christian make his prayers effective, and why is it important to speak to Jehovah directly?
10 The way a Christian can make his prayers effective is by praying directly to Jehovah. How can we show that we appreciate this privilege? A person shows appreciation by speaking to Jehovah personally and confiding in him fully, regularly, and honestly. He does so because he loves Jehovah and wants to have a close relationship with him. This is what Jesus meant when he told his disciples: "Be sincere in your prayer." (Matt. 16:24) In effect, such a person says, 'I dedicate myself to you, Jehovah.' (Acts 14:8) Anyone who prays sincerely and confides in Jehovah will be able to cope with difficulties, just like David did. That faithful man wrote an honest account of his feelings, saying: "How can I repay Jehovah for all his goodness to me? I will offer a sacrifice to Jehovah; yes, I will pay my vow to Jehovah."—Ps. 116:12, 14.
11. Why should we be specific in our requests?
11 Do you confide in Jehovah and express your desires to him through prayer? If so, continue doing so! Remember that being specific in our requests does not mean that Jehovah will grant us everything we ask for, but rather that he may move us to take action and help us to see how his organization is using resources to assist those in need. For example, imagine that you learn about a brother who is facing a difficult situation, and you pray that Jehovah would comfort him. Your prayer might move you to offer practical assistance or to share encouraging scriptures with him. Then you might reason: "Yes, I will use my means to help others, and I will trust that Jehovah will bless my efforts and enable me to support his brothers." So confidently rely on Jehovah, knowing that he cares about you!
12. (a) What qualities do we value in friends? (b) Why can we be sure that we can confide in Jehovah?
12 Prayer is an important part of our worship. We engage in prayer because we want to strengthen our relationship with God and show our gratitude to him. But sometimes we may wonder, 'Will Jehovah always answer my prayers, especially when I am experiencing difficulties? Will I continue to trust in Jehovah even if things do not improve?' (Prov. 3:23) To remain steadfast, we should read God's Word daily, attend all meetings, and regularly examine ourselves to see if there are areas where we can make improvements. Or we might ask ourselves, 'Am I willing to adjust my life to align more closely with Bible principles?' The apostle Paul encouraged us to keep making progress in our spiritual growth, so that our love can increase along with knowledge, discernment, and moral uprightness.—Read 2 Corinthians 1:5-8.
13 Can a faithful Christian find satisfaction even when faced with trials?
13 There are ways we can maintain joy despite the trials we experience. A person shows his devotion to Jehovah when he continues to serve Jehovah even when facing challenges, rather than giving up simply because things are difficult, feeling that his efforts are futile. * However, those who have been tested often appreciate the encouragement they receive from others and their continued support in worshipping God. But how can we help them? We can offer practical assistance and express our confidence in Jehovah and His promises. (Ps. 14:12) Let us take time each day to remind ourselves and others, "Keep encouraging one another!" Like Jesus did, we can use our words to comfort others: "Strengthen your hearts and be courageous, for your reward will be great." (Rev. 2:4, 19) May we all strive to remain close to one another and to support one another in showing our love for Jehovah in all that we do.
OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH JEHOVAH
14 What is one way to strengthen our relationship with Jehovah, and what does this involve?
14 One way to strengthen our relationship with Jehovah is to meditate on His laws. Why is meditation important? Because meditating on God's laws helps us to value them more. Husbands and wives should regularly reflect on Bible principles together. Each one can benefit from doing so personally, thinking about how to apply them in his life, and praying for guidance. This will help him to feel that 'all the commandments are righteous and trustworthy.' Others may find it helpful to share ideas with fellow Christians, but always remember to put Jehovah first. Marriage mates should not allow disagreements to damage their love for one another. (Matt. 2:24; 1 Cor. 7:39) As Jesus said, "God is Love," and whether one is married, unmarried, or widowed, he should show love. So let marriage mates endeavor to avoid anything that would hinder their love for one another.—Mark 10:9.
15 Why might some Christians struggle to view marriage as something sacred, especially when others around them do not?
15 For this reason, many people today do not regard marriage as sacred. And those who live with someone without being married often feel free to end the relationship whenever they please. That is why the Bible warns against getting involved with those who do not appreciate the sanctity of marriage "with the world." (1 Cor. 7:28) However, many individuals genuinely want to honor their marriage. But sometimes difficulties arise, causing friction and disagreement. In such cases, it is wise for Christians to seek counsel. To maintain a good relationship with Jehovah and to receive His blessing, it is essential to be obedient to Him. (Acts 19:12; Num. 6:16-19) The apostle Paul asked: "Am I bound to a wife?" And he added: "I am not." (1 Cor. 7:27) Paul made this point to show that Jehovah blesses those who choose to remain faithful to Him.—Mal. 2:13-16.
16 What does the Bible say about dissolving a marriage and remarrying?
16 Jesus showed that while the Law permitted divorce, it was never God's purpose for a marriage to end. (Matt. 19:9; Heb. 13:4) But what about remarriage? The Bible gives clear guidance on this matter. (Read 1 Corinthians 7:10, 11.) The Bible provides reasons why a separation may be necessary. There are circumstances where a Christian may have valid grounds for dissolution. For example, one mate may commit adultery or abandon the family. Also, an unfaithful mate may find it difficult to continue living with his or her partner, and his or her spiritual routine with Jehovah may suffer. *
17 Can a Christian dissolve a marriage even if it causes great pain?
17 If they use worldly reasoning, they may feel justified in ending their marriage, but Christians should remember that God views marriage as sacred. Is it wise to risk damaging your relationship with God over a marital problem? Consider the account of a couple who were featured in the article "Making Your Marriage Work." Why did they seek help? Because they realized that their problems were affecting their spirituality. Some married couples have said: "We almost gave up on our marriage, but we decided to try to work things out." And one sister who had been married for 22 years says that her marriage improved considerably after they sought help. She explains: "We learned to communicate better, and we began to appreciate each other more. Our marriage has gotten so much stronger! May our marriage continue to flourish." Will you seek help if you face difficulties? Let us always prioritize pleasing Jehovah in our marriages. To do so, we must strive to maintain peace and unity in our families!
MAINTAINING FAMILY PEACE IS ESSENTIAL TO SPIRITUAL HEALTH
18, 19. (a) What questions do many Christians ask themselves? (b) How can maintaining family peace strengthen our faith?
18 Do you recall what happened to Rebekah and Abraham? Both Rebekah and Abraham demonstrated great faith when faced with difficult situations. Their faith was tested on several occasions, yet they continued to trust in God and his promises. Many Christians today also find themselves facing similar trials, and they want to show that their faith is genuine. But how can they do so? By upholding God's standards, even when it is difficult.—Acts 11:40; Ps. 110:3.
19 In 2017, some 67,000 volunteers assisted with the global activity of Kingdom Halls and Assembly Halls construction. Some traveled to Bethel, while others used their skills to help with local projects. Others served at schools connected to Bethel, doing maintenance work, landscaping, and renovations. And still others worked at large Assembly Halls or at Bible Schools. Often these volunteers were referred to as "pioneers of sacrifice and selflessness." These brothers and sisters willingly gave up comforts and conveniences to support the work. They were motivated by love and a desire to please Jehovah. Moreover, they often learned valuable lessons and developed stronger bonds with fellow believers. Those who did not have building experience found ways to contribute, and those who had experience appreciated the opportunity to use their skills to further the Kingdom work. This activity reminded us that maintaining family peace is essential to spiritual health.
20. What does it mean to 'value every day,' and why?
20 How can we show God appreciation for the privilege of being in his service? Is it just one thing, or several? Consider this: Are we willing to examine our own lives and see what adjustments we can make? (Prov. 20:25) It is vital to remember that loving Jehovah and serving him requires constant effort. (Matt. 5:6) By saying, "I will continually seek Jehovah; I will examine my actions each day," we demonstrate our determination.—Ps. 61:8.
^ par. 7 A Christian should always pray to God and ask his Son to forgive his sins. This shows humility and dependence on Jehovah's mercy.—Luke 6:2, 5, 8.
^ par. 13 We should be careful about accepting gifts from strangers, especially if there is an expectation of receiving something in return. It is wise to avoid situations where someone might feel obligated to reciprocate.—Prov. 23:6-9.
^ par. 16 See the article "How to Remain No Part of the World," pages 219-221.

text:
"Sisyai ĩũlũ, na ũkĩlyai mĩtwe yenyu; nũndũ wovosyo wenyu nĩ mũthengeeu."—LUKA 21:28.
MBATHI: 49, 43
1. Nĩ maũndũ meva meekĩkie mwakanĩ wa 66 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto? (Sisya visa ĩthangũnĩ yĩĩ.)
KWASŨANĨA keka waĩ Mũklĩsto mwakanĩ wa 66 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, na ũyĩthĩwa ũtũaa Yelusaleme. Twasye nĩwĩsĩ maũndũ maingĩ mũno ala maendeee vau ndũanĩ ĩsu. Mbee, nĩwĩsĩ mũnene ũmwe wa Lomi wĩtawa Florus nũnoosie talendi 17 sya kĩnandũ kya ĩkalũ, nakyo kyonekaa kĩ kĩtheu. Na ĩtina wa ũu, nĩwĩsĩ Ayuti nĩmanoosie ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ malua nduuthĩ na mambĩĩa kũaa asikalĩ ma Lomi ala manaĩ Yelusaleme, na ĩndĩ mavanga nĩmakwata wĩyathi kuma kwa Alomi. Ĩndĩ no wĩsĩ o ũndũ Lomi ĩnoosie ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ, na vatathelete myei ĩtatũ yatũma asikalĩ 30,000 moke vau matongoew'e nĩ mũnene wa Silia wĩtawa Cestius Gallus. Ndatĩka asikalĩ asu nĩmanavikie isionĩ ila ithyũlũlũkĩte Yelusaleme, na ĩla Ayuti ala manaluĩte nduuthĩ manoonie ũu masemba meevitha ĩkalũnĩ. Mũthya asikalĩ ma Lomi nĩmanambĩĩe kwĩnza ũkũta wa ĩkalũ. Nũndũ wa maũndũ asu, yu ndũa ĩsu yusũĩtwe nĩ wia. We wĩona ta wĩw'a ata wonete maũndũ asu mayĩkĩka?
2. Aklĩsto maaĩle kwosa ĩtambya yĩkũ mwakanĩ wa 66 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, na ũu watonyekie ata?
2 Vate nzika ndũlea kũlilikana ila ndeto sya Yesũ syaandĩkiwe nĩ Luka. Aandĩkie atĩĩ: "Yĩla mwĩona Yelusaleme yeelingĩlwa nĩ ita, manyai kana wanangĩko wayo wĩ vakuvĩ." (Luka 21:20) Ĩndĩ no kwĩthĩwa ũsyoka kwĩkũlya atĩĩ, 'Ndonya kũatĩĩa ata ũtao ũla Yesũ waumisye amina kũnengane ũkany'o ũsu?' Yesũ awetete ũũ: "Ĩvinda yĩu ala me Yutia makie mathi iĩmanĩ; na ala me nthĩnĩ wayo maume vo; na ala me ndee matikavote vo." (Luka 21:21) Nayu ũtonya kuma Yelusaleme ata na now'o asikalĩ mathyũlũlũkĩte ndũa ĩsu? Ĩndĩ ũendeee kũlanĩlw'a ũyona ũndũ wa ũsengy'o weekĩka. Ũndũ mwaũ? Ũyona ita sya Lomi syakwata nzĩa na kũthi! Kaĩ matukũ ma ita isu meeka 'kũkuvĩvw'a' o tondũ kwathanĩtwe. (Mt. 24:22) Yu mwanya nĩwesa kumĩla wa kũatĩĩa ũtao ũla Yesũ wanenganie. Nũndũ wa ũu, ũitw'a kwosa ĩtambya mĩtũkĩ na ũikĩĩa iĩmanĩ ila syĩ mũingo wa Ũsĩ wa Yolotani wĩ vamwe na Aklĩsto ala angĩ aĩkĩĩku me vau ndũanĩ nthĩnĩ na ndee syayo. * Wĩ kũu nĩw'o ũkwĩsa kũkwata livoti mwakanĩ wa 70 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto kana Lomi nĩyatũma ita syayo ithi ikanange ndũa ya Yelusaleme. Ĩndĩ ũseo we nĩwaatĩĩie mwĩao wa Yesũ.
3. O ta Aklĩsto ala maĩ ĩvinda ya atũmwa, Aklĩsto ala me kw'o yu makilyĩ manoona kyaũ, na twĩĩmanyĩsya kyaũ ĩsomonĩ yĩĩ?
3 Ĩtina wa kavinda kanini, kanini mũno, kĩla ũmwe witũ akilyĩ aneyĩthĩĩla thĩnanĩ ta ũsu wawetwa vau ĩũlũ. Ũkany'o ũla Yesũ wanengie Aklĩsto ma ĩvinda ya atũmwa ĩũlũ wa kwanangwa kwa Yelusaleme nũtũkonetye. Ainengane ũkany'o ũsu no wendaa kwonany'a ũndũ maũndũ makethĩwa mailyĩ ĩvindanĩ yĩla ũla "thĩna mũnene" ũkambĩĩa kĩthũlũmũko. (Mt. 24:3, 21, 29) Ũseo nĩ kana "ĩkomano ĩnene" ya andũ yĩkavonoka mũisyo ũsu ũkakwata nthĩ yonthe. (Soma Ũvuan'yo 7:9, 13, 14.) Mbivilia ĩtũtavĩtye kyaũ ĩũlũ wa maũndũ asu tweteele kwona? Nĩtwaĩle kwendeew'a mũno nĩ kũkwata ũsũngĩo wa ĩkũlyo yĩu nũndũ maũndũ asu makonetye mathayũ maitũ. Ekai yu tũsisye mũno ũndũ maũndũ asu tweteele makonetye kĩla ũmwe witũ.
ŨNDŨ ŨLA THĨNA MŨNENE ŨKAMBĨĨA
4. Ũla thĩna mũnene ũkambĩĩa ata?
4 Ũla thĩna mũnene ũkambĩĩa ata? Ĩkũlyo yĩu nĩyĩsũngĩĩtwe ĩvukunĩ ya Ũvuan'yo, vala vaeleetw'e ĩũlũ wa kwanangwa kwa "Mbaviloni ĩla nene." (Ũvu. 17:5-7) Ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ nĩsyo ielekanĩtw'e na ĩlwaya, nasyo nĩsyaĩlĩtwe vyũ nĩ ĩsyĩtwa yĩu! Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ atongoi ma ndĩni isu nĩmakũnĩte ũmalwaya na atongoi ma nthĩ ĩno nthũku. Vandũ va kũlũmany'a na Yesũ vamwe na Ũsumbĩ wake, atongoi asu ma ndĩni makwete mbau atongoi ma nthĩ na nĩmatũlaa myolooto ya Ngai no kana methĩwe na ũkũmũ maũndũnĩ ma siasa. Me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na etĩkĩw'a mauta nũndũ etĩkĩw'a mauta maivukĩtye ũthaithi woo, o na maelekanĩtw'e na mwĩĩtu mũtheu. (2 Ako. 11:2; Yak. 1:27; Ũvu. 14:4) Ĩndĩ we nũũ ũkananga asu maelekanĩtw'e na ĩlwaya? Yeova Ngai akeekĩa "kwenda kwake" ngoonĩ sya ala maelekanĩtw'e na ila "mbya ĩkũmi" sya ĩla "nyamũ ndune mũno." Mbya isu ĩkũmi nĩ silikalĩ syonthe ila ũmũnthĩ itw'ĩĩkĩte ĩla Ngwatanĩo ya Nthĩ (UN). Ngwatanĩo ĩsu ya Nthĩ nĩyo ĩelekanĩtw'e na ĩla "nyamũ ndune mũno."—Soma Ũvuan'yo 17:3, 16-18.
5, 6. Nĩkĩ tũkwasya kana ĩvinda yĩla Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene ĩkethĩwa ĩyanangwa aatĩĩi onthe mayo maikananganĩw'a nayo?
5 Ĩndĩ nĩtwaĩle kũtw'a kana o namo aatĩĩi onthe ma Mbaviloni Ĩla Nene makaanangwa ĩla ndĩni isu ikethĩwa iyanangwa? No twasye, aiee. Mwathani Nzekalia nĩwaveveewe aandĩka ĩũlũ wa ĩvinda yĩu. Aandĩkie ĩũlũ wa ngelekany'o ya mũndũ weekwatanĩtye na ndĩni sya ũvũngũ asya atĩĩ: "Akasya, Ndi mwathani nyie, nyie nĩ mũĩmi; nũndũ natw'ĩwe ngombo kuma wana wakwa. Na ũmwe akamwĩa, Mawũkite aa me itaanĩ syaku nĩ ma kyaũ? Nĩvo wĩsũngĩa, Aa nĩ ala nokitĩwe nyũmbanĩ ya anyanyawa." (Nzek. 13:4-6) Kwoou nĩvatonyeka ũkethĩa atongoi amwe ma ndĩni sya ũvũngũ makaikola na maikaĩa vyũ kana maaĩsa kwĩkwatany'a nasyo.
6 Mo andũ ma Ngai makeethĩwa maendeee ata? Yesũ aeleisye atĩĩ: 'Kethĩwa matukũ asu matyaakuvĩvw'a, kũivĩta mwĩĩ o na wĩva: ĩndĩ kwondũ wa ala anyuve matukũ asu makakuvĩvw'a.' (Mt. 24:22) O tondũ twoona, mwakanĩ wa 66 ĩtina wa kũsyawa kwa Klĩsto, matukũ ma thĩna ũla waĩ Yelusaleme na ndee syayo 'nĩmakuvĩviw'e.' Kĩu nĩkyatumie "ala anyuve," kana kwa ndeto ingĩ, Aklĩsto etĩkĩw'a mauta, makwata mwanya wa kuma kũu. O ta ũu, matukũ ma kĩlungu kya mbee kya ũla thĩna mũnene 'makakuvĩvw'a' kwondũ wa "ala anyuve." Ila silikalĩ ielekanĩtw'e na "mbya ĩkũmi" iiketĩkĩlw'a syanange vyũ andũ ma Ngai. Vandũ va ũu, kĩlungu kya mbee kya ũla thĩna mũnene kyathela kũkausya kwa kavinda.
ĨVINDA YA KŨTATWA NA KŨSILĨLWA
7, 8. Nĩ mwanya wĩva ũkaumĩla ndĩni sya ũvũngũ syamina kwanangwa, na andũ ma Ngai makoonany'a ata kana me kĩvathũkany'o na ala angĩ?
7 Nĩ kyaũ kĩkekĩka ndĩni syonthe sya ũvũngũ syamina kwanangwa? Yĩu yĩkethĩwa ne ĩvinda ya kwonany'a kĩla kĩ ngoonĩ sitũ. Andũ ala aingĩ makamantha wĩvitho ngwatanĩonĩ sya andũ, ila ielekanĩtw'e na 'mbai sya iĩma.' (Ũvu. 6:15-17) Ĩndĩ andũ ma Ngai makasemba kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o makevithe vala Yeova ũkethĩwa amaseũvĩsye. O na ĩngĩ lilikana kana ĩla matukũ ma thĩna 'makuvĩviw'e' ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa, yĩu yĩyaĩ ĩvinda ya kũalyũla nguthu nene ya Ayuti ĩtw'ĩke Aklĩsto. Ĩndĩ ĩvinda yĩu nĩw'o ala maĩ Aklĩsto maaĩle kwĩw'a na kwĩka ũndũ matavĩtw'e. O ta ũu, tũyaĩle kũsũanĩa kana ĩla ũla thĩna mũnene ũkamba kũtilĩĩlwa, andũ aingĩ makatw'ĩka Aklĩsto. Vandũ va ũu, Aklĩsto ma w'o makethĩwa makwata mwanya wa kwonany'a kana nĩmamwendete Yeova, vamwe na mwanya wa kũkwata mbau ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto.—Mt. 25:34-40.
8 O na kau tũyĩsĩ vyũ maũndũ ala makekĩka ĩvindanĩ yĩu ya kũtatwa, nĩtwĩsĩ kana vakavika vandũ wĩthĩe nĩ lasima twĩyĩime syĩndũ imwe. Kwa ngelekany'o, ĩvindanĩ ya atũmwa yaĩ no nginya Aklĩsto matie malĩ syoo na mayũmĩĩsya maũndũ mana nĩ kana mavonoke. (Mko. 13:15-18) Kwoou twaĩle kwĩkũlya atĩĩ: 'Nyie ngeethĩwa nĩyũmbanĩtye kwasya malĩ nĩ kana nĩendeee kwĩthĩwa nĩ mũĩkĩĩku? Nyie ngeethĩwa nĩyũmbanĩtye kwĩka kyonthe kĩla kĩkendeka nĩ kana nĩĩkĩĩthye nĩnĩlũmanĩtye na Yeova?' Kwasũanĩa ũndũ ũũ: Ĩvinda yĩu no ithyĩ tũkethĩwa tũatĩĩe ngelekany'o ya mwathani wa tene, Ndanieli, kwa kũendeea kũmũthaitha Ngai o na twakwatwa nĩ kyaũ.—Nda. 6:10, 11.
9, 10. (a) Andũ ma Ngai makatavany'a ũvoo wĩva ĩvindanĩ ya ũla thĩna mũnene? (b) Amaitha ma andũ ma Ngai makeka ata?
9 Yĩu yĩikethĩwa ĩvinda ya kũtavany'a 'ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ.' Ĩvinda ya kũtavany'a ũvoo mũseo wa Ũsumbĩ yĩkeethĩwa yathelile. Nĩkĩ? Nũndũ "mũminũkĩlyo" ũkeethĩwa ũnavika. (Mt. 24:14) Vate nzika ĩvinda yĩu andũ ma Ngai makatavany'a ĩũlũ wa ũsilĩlo mateũvuva andũ. No kwĩthĩwa makethĩwa maitavany'a kana kĩla kĩtiele kya nthĩ ĩno nthũku ya Satani kĩkilyĩ kĩnaanangwa. Mbivilia ĩelekanĩtye ũvoo ũsu makatavany'a na mbua ya mavia. Yaĩtye ũũ: "Na mbua nene ya mavia, kĩla ĩvia ũito wayo waĩ ta talendi ĩmwe, yamatheeea andũ kuma ĩtunĩ: na andũ mamũuma Ngai nũndũ wa ũthĩn'yo ũsu wa mbua ya mavia; nĩkwĩthĩwa ũthĩn'yo wayo nĩ mũnene mũno."—Ũvu. 16:21.
10 Ũvoo ũsu ndũkaema kũvikĩa amaitha maitũ. Esekieli nĩwaveveewe aandĩka kĩla Ngoki wa Makoki ũkeka, ũla nĩ mbaĩ ikethĩwa syĩ ngwatanĩo. Aisye atĩĩ: "Ũũ nĩw'o Mwĩaĩi Yeova ũnũkwasya: Kũkeethĩwa mũthenya ũsu, maũndũ makalika kĩlilikanonĩ kyaku, na ũkasũanĩa ũsũanĩo mũthũku: na ũkasya, Ngambata nthĩ yĩ tũmĩsyĩ tũte twiie; ngathi kwa ala mathũmũĩte, ala mekalaa meyelele, onthe mekalĩte mate na maũvai, na mate na ivingi kana mbingĩlo; nose mũtavo o na syĩndũ sya mbuta; nĩthyũũe kw'oko kwaku ĩũlũ wa kũndũ kũla kwaeketwe kũla yu kũtwĩwe nĩ andũ, na ĩũlũ wa andũ mombanĩtw'e kuma i mbaĩnĩ, ala me na indo na syĩndũ, ala matũaa nthĩ katĩ." (Esek. 38:10-12) Kwa nzĩa ya ngelekany'o, andũ ma Ngai nĩ ta makethĩwa matwĩe "nthĩ katĩ." Ũu nĩ kwasya kana makethĩwa me kĩvathũkany'o vyũ na andũ ala angĩ onthe. Nasyo mbaĩ isu syoona ũu, ikeew'a itomĩĩsya. Ikeethĩwa iyenda mũno kũvithũkĩa etĩkĩw'a mauta ma Yeova vamwe na ala mamakwete mbau.
11. (a) Nĩ kyaũ twaĩle kũlilikana ĩũlũ wa maũndũ ala makekĩka ĩvindanĩ ya ũla thĩna mũnene? (b) Andũ makeka ata ĩla makona mawonany'o matunĩ?
11 Ekai yu tũsisye kĩla kĩkaatĩĩa. Ĩla tũendeee kwĩka ũu nĩtũlilikanei kana Ndeto ya Ngai ndĩwetete nesa vyũ maũndũ makekĩka maatĩanĩe ata. No kwĩthĩwa maũndũ amwe makekĩka o ala angĩ maendeee. Ĩla Yesũ wathanaa ĩũlũ wa mũminũkĩlyo wa nthĩ ĩno nthũku aisye ũũ: "Kũkethĩwa mawonan'yo syũanĩ na mweinĩ na ndatanĩ; na kũũ nthĩ kũkethĩwa ũnyamao wa mbaĩ, ikĩsũanĩwa nũndũ wa kĩlitũko kya ũkanga na itulumo syaw'o; andũ nĩmakatw'ĩka nda nĩ w'ĩa, na ũndũ wa kweteela maũndũ ala mokĩte ĩũlũ wa nthĩ: nũndũ mavinya ma ĩtu nĩmakathingithangw'a. Ĩvinda yĩu nĩmakamwona Mwana wa mũndũ okĩte ĩthweonĩ na vinya na ũtheu mũnene mũtisu." (Luka 21:25-27; soma Maliko 13:24-26.) W'o wathani ũsu wĩonany'a kana kũkethĩwa na mawonany'o ma ũsengy'a na maũndũ angĩ ta asu matunĩ? Ekai tweteele twĩyonee kĩla kĩkekĩka. Ĩndĩ o na kũtw'ĩke kũkathi ata, nĩtwĩsĩ mawonany'o asu makatuma amaitha ma Ngai matelema na maitw'ĩka nda.
12, 13. (a) Nĩ kyaũ kĩkekĩka ĩla Yesũ ũkoka "na vinya na ũtheu mũnene mũtisu"? (b) Athũkũmi ma Ngai makeka ata ĩvinda yĩu?
12 Nĩ kyaũ kĩkekĩka ĩla Yesũ ũkoka "na vinya na ũtheu mũnene mũtisu"? Ala aĩkĩĩku makatuvwa ĩndĩ ala mate aĩkĩĩku makasilĩlwa. (Mt. 24:46, 47, 50, 51; 25:19, 28-30) Kwosana na ũndũ Mathayo waandĩkie, Yesũ aiminĩĩa kũweta wonany'o wa ĩvinda ya mũminũkĩlyo nĩwanenganie ngelekany'o ya malondu na mbũi. Aisye atĩĩ: "Yĩla Mwana wa mũndũ ũkoka ũtheunĩ wake mũtisu, na alaĩka onthe vamwe nake, nĩvo ũkekalĩla kĩvĩla kya ũsumbĩ kya ũtheu wake mũtisu: na mbee wake nikomban'wa mbaĩ syonthe: nake nũkamavathan'ya aa na aya, tondũ mũĩthi ũvathanasya malondu na mbũi; na nũkaia malondu ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwake kwa aũme, ĩndĩ mbũi ngalĩ ya kw'oko kwake kwa aka." (Mt. 25:31-33) Malondu na mbũi makakwata ũsilĩlo wĩva? Yesũ aminĩĩie ngelekany'o ĩsu na kũweta kana mbũi ikaanangwa tene na tene, "ĩndĩ ala alũngalu makalika thayũnĩ ũtathela."—Mt. 25:46.
13 Ala maelekanĩtw'e na mbũi makeeka ata ĩla memanya kana maitĩa kwanangwa tene na tene? Mbivilia yaĩtye kana 'makameta.' (Mt. 24:30) Ĩndĩ namo ana-a-asa ma Klĩsto vamwe na ala mamakwete mbau makeka ata ĩvinda yĩu? Nũndũ makethĩwa mamũĩkĩĩe vyũ Yeova Ngai na Mwana wake, Yesũ Klĩsto, makaatĩĩa mwĩao ũũ wa Yesũ: "Yĩla maũndũ asu makambĩlĩlya kwĩkĩka, sisyai ĩũlũ, na ũkĩlyai mĩtwe yenyu; nũndũ wovosyo wenyu nĩ mũthengeeu." (Luka 21:28) Vate nzika, tũkeethĩwa na mũĩkĩĩo mũlũmu vyũ kana nĩtũũtangĩĩwa.
MAKATISA ŨSUMBĨNĨ
14, 15. Nĩ kũmbanw'a kwĩva kũkekwa Ngoki wa Makoki ambĩĩa kũvithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai, na wĩa ũsu ũkatethw'a ata?
14 Nĩ kyaũ kĩkekĩka ĩla Ngoki wa Makoki ũkavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai? Mathayo na Maliko nĩmaandĩkie kĩla kĩkekĩka. Maĩtye: "Nĩvo [Mwana wa mũndũ] wĩtũma alaĩka momban'ye anyuve make kuma ngalĩ inya sya ĩseve, na kuma kĩtulu kya nthĩ kũvika kĩtulu kya ĩtu." (Mko. 13:27; Mt. 24:31) Kũmbany'a kũla kũwetetwe vau kũikonanĩtye na kwĩtĩkĩw'a mauta kwa Aklĩsto, o na kũikonanĩtye na kũsiĩlwa kwa mũthya kwa etĩkĩw'a mauta ala matiele kũũ nthĩ. (Mt. 13:37, 38) Etĩkĩw'a mauta makekĩwa ũsiĩlo ũsu wa mũthya ũla thĩna mũnene ũtanamba kwambĩĩa. (Ũvu. 7:1-4) Kwoou-ĩ, kũmbanw'a kũla Yesũ wawetie nĩ kwĩva? Yĩu nĩ ĩvinda yĩla ala matiele ma 144,000 makakwata ĩtuvi yoo ya kũthi ĩtunĩ. (1 Ath. 4:15-17; Ũvu. 14:1) Na makakwata ĩtuvi yoo ĩvinda ĩna Ngoki wa Makoki ambĩĩa kũvithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai. (Esek. 38:11) Nĩvo ĩndĩ ndeto ii sya Yesũ ikeanĩw'a: 'Ala alũngalu makatisa ta syũa ũsumbĩnĩ wa Ĩthe woo.'—Mt. 13:43. *
15 Mo etĩkĩw'a mauta 'makavulw'a' o tondũ andũ ma ndĩni maeleetwe ndeto ĩsu? Andũ aingĩ ma ndĩni ila syĩyĩtaa sya Kĩklĩsto maeleawa kana ndeto 'kũvulw'a' ĩkonanĩtye na kwambatw'a kwa Aklĩsto kuma vaa nthĩ me na mwĩĩ wa nyama. Na mesĩ kana ĩtina wa ũu Yesũ akasyoka e na mwĩĩ wa nyama nĩ kana asumbĩke nthĩ. Ĩndĩ mbee Mbivilia yaĩtye kana "wonan'yo wa Mwana wa mũndũ" ũkooneka ĩtunĩ, na ĩkasyoka ĩkasya kana Yesũ akoka "ĩũlũ wa mathweo ma ĩtu." (Mt. 24:30) Maũndũ asu me elĩ monanasya kana Yesũ mwene ndakoneka. O na ĩngĩ "nyama na nthakame ititonya kũtiĩwa ũsumbĩ wa Ngai." Kwoou no nginya ala makathi ĩtunĩ meamba 'kũalyũkw'a, kavinda kanini, kũveny'a na kũsalukya, ũivuvwa soo wa mũminũkĩlyo.' * (Soma 1 Akolintho 15:50-53.) Kwoou o na kau tũitũmĩa ndeto 'kũvulw'a' ũndũnĩ ũũ nũndũ ĩtũmĩawa naĩ, nĩtwĩsĩ kana etĩkĩw'a mauta ala aĩkĩĩku makethĩwa matiele makombanw'a vamwe ĩveny'a na ĩsalukya.
16, 17. Nĩ kyaũ kyaĩle kwĩkĩka mũtwaano wa kala Katena ũtanamba kwĩkwa ĩtunĩ?
16 Mĩvango ya mũthya ya mũtwaano wa kala Katena ĩkambĩĩa kwĩkwa onthe ma ala 144,000 mamina kũvika ĩtunĩ. (Ũvu. 19:9) Ĩndĩ ve ũndũ ũngĩ ũkekĩka mũthenya ũsu mũseo ũtanamba kũvika. Lilikana kana ĩla vakethĩwa vatiele kavinda kanini ala matiele ma ala 144,000 mathi ĩtunĩ, Ngoki akavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai. (Esek. 38:16) Kĩu kĩkatuma andũ ma Ngai meka ata? O na kau makeethĩwa mailyĩ ta mate na mũndũ wa kũmasũvĩa, makaatĩĩa ndeto ii syataviw'e Aisilaeli ĩvinda ya Mũsumbĩ Yeosavati: "Mũtikethĩwa na vata wa kũkita kaũnĩ ũũ: Ĩlũlũmĩlyei, ũngamai, mwone ũtangĩĩo wa Yeova ũla wĩ vamwe nenyu, inyw'ĩ Yuta na Yelusaleme; mũikakĩe, o na [mũikateve]." (2 Mav. 20:17) Ĩndĩ ũu tiw'o kũkethĩwa kũilyĩ ĩtunĩ. Nũndũ ĩvinda yĩu etĩkĩw'a mauta onthe makethĩwa ĩtunĩ, mo ala me kũu makeka ata? Ĩandĩko ya Ũvuan'yo 17:14 nĩyĩwetete ũndũ makeka ĩla Ngoki ũkavithũkĩa andũ ma Ngai. Yaĩtye kana amaitha ma andũ ma Ngai 'makokita na kala Katena ka ĩlondu, nake Katena akamakĩlya vinya, nĩkwĩthĩwa we nĩ Mwĩaĩi wa eaĩi na Mũsumbĩ wa asumbĩ; na ala me nake, ala meetiwe, anyuve na me na kĩthito, makakĩlya vinya.' Yesũ akoka kũtangĩĩa andũ ma Ngai e na ala 144,000 ũkasumbĩka namo ĩtunĩ.
17 Ĩtambya yĩu makosa yĩkaumĩlya kaũ wa Ali–Maketoni, ũla ũkatuma ĩsyĩtwa ĩtheu ya Yeova yĩtaĩwa. (Ũvu. 16:16) Ĩvinda yĩu onthe ala me na mũvw'ano wa mbũi makaanangwa tene na tene. Naw'o ũthũku w'onthe ũkavetangwa kũũ nthĩ, na ĩndĩ ĩkomano ĩnene yĩyĩinga kĩlungu kya mũthya kya ũla thĩna mũnene. Kũvikĩĩa vau mũtwaano wa kala Katena no wĩkwe nũndũ ũkeethĩwa ũnamina kwĩyũmbanĩw'a. Ũndũ ũsu mũseo na wa kũtanĩthya nĩw'o ũminĩĩe ĩvuku ya Ũvuan'yo! (Ũvu. 21:1-4) * Onthe ala makethĩwa thayũ kũũ nthĩ makatanĩa mũno kwĩtĩkĩlwa nĩ Ngai, na nĩmakatana mũno nĩ wendo ũla ũkamony'a. Mwa tũkatanĩa mũtwaano ũsu ta kĩ! Tyo twĩw'aa twĩ na mea ma kwona mũthenya ũsu?—Soma 2 Vetelo 3:13.
18. Nũndũ tweteele kwona maũndũ manene, twaĩle kũtw'a kwĩka ata?
18 Nũndũ nĩtweteele kwona maũndũ asu manenevete ũu, kĩla ũmwe witũ aĩlĩte kwĩthĩwa yu ayĩka ata? Mũtũmwa Vetelo nĩwaveveewe nĩ Ngai aandĩka atĩĩ: "Nĩkwĩthĩwa syĩndũ isu syonthe nikanyaĩĩkw'a ũu, inyw'ĩ mwaĩle kwĩthĩwa andũ mailyĩ ata mwĩkalĩlenĩ mũtheu wa thayũ na kũmũkĩa Ngai, mũkyeteela na kwenda mũno kũka kwa mũthenya wa Ngai . . . Kwondũ wa ũu, endwa, nĩkwĩthĩwa mweteele maũndũ asu, thangaai kana mwoneke mũuonĩ, mũte na ĩlanga na mũtekwilĩĩlĩka mbee wake." (2 Vet. 3:11, 12, 14) Kwoou ekai tũtw'e vyũ kwĩka ũndũ tũtonya tũikavukye ũthaithi witũ, na nĩtũtw'ei kũkwata mbau Mũsumbĩ wa Mũuo.
^ kal. 2 Sisya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya (Kĩswaili) ya 15/04/2012, ĩthangũ ya 25-26.
^ kal. 14 Sisya ĩkaseti ya Mũsyaĩĩsya ya 01/07/2013, ĩthangũ ya 19-20.
^ kal. 15 Mĩĩ ya etĩkĩw'a mauta ala makethĩwa me thayũ ĩvinda yĩu ndĩkatwawa ĩtunĩ. (1 Ako. 15:48, 49) No kwĩthĩwa mĩĩ ĩsu yoo ĩkekanwa nayo o ũndũ mwĩĩ wa Yesũ wekaniwe naw'o.
^ kal. 17 Savuli ya 45 o nayo nĩeleetye ũndũ maũndũ matonya kwĩsa kũatĩanĩa. Mũsumbĩ akamba kũkita, na ĩndĩ mũtwaano ũyĩkwa.

translation:
"When you see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near."—LUKE 21:28.
FOOTNOTES: 49, 43
1. Is it important to remember the year 66 C.E. when considering the fulfillment of Christ's prophecy? (Consider this point carefully.)
IN 66 C.E., while Christians were in Jerusalem awaiting the fulfillment of Christ's prophecy, a great commotion began to stir up trouble. We will now examine some events that led to the destruction of Jerusalem. For example, a certain Roman governor named Florus brazenly demanded 17 talents of silver from the temple treasury, which was an outrageous act. And at that time, a Syrian official named Gessius ordered soldiers to march through Jewish quarters and villages to collect taxes from the Jews and also from those in Jerusalem, and he caused disturbances. Furthermore, there was a dispute over who had the right to govern Judea, and the Romans arrested several prominent men. Then a Syrian official ordered soldiers to march through Jewish quarters, and he sent three legions—about 30,000 soldiers—under the command of a Syrian officer named Cestius Gallus. However, the soldiers were defeated and forced to retreat from Jerusalem, and the Syrians and their allies suffered heavy losses. Because of these events, war loomed on the horizon. Do you think that these events show us why it is important to remember the year 66 C.E.?
2. Did the Christians realize that the time for action was near in 66 C.E., and did they take any steps because of this?
2 However, some continued to hesitate, but Luke wrote down Jesus' prophecy. He wrote: "When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, know that her desolation is drawing near." (Luke 21:20) But how could they be sure that this would happen within their lifetime—that Jesus would not delay his return? Jesus gave this answer: "There will be signs in sun and moon and stars; and on earth nations will be in distress and sea and waves roaring." (Luke 21:21) So can we today recognize that Jerusalem is already being trampled on by the nations? If so, what should we do? We should pay attention to the fulfillment of the prophecy. What sign? The star of Bethlehem shone brightly and impressively! In those days the star showed 'the presence' of God's kingdom. (Matt. 24:22) Now is the time to be convinced that Jesus will fulfill his promise. Because of this, let us examine the scriptures carefully and give them serious consideration, along with the teachings of Christ and the other inspired men who were with him during his ministry. * You may wonder whether it is possible to determine the time in 70 C.E. when Bethlehem's star appeared or whether Bethlehem sent its star to signal the destruction of Jerusalem. If so, you will better understand Jesus' purpose.
3. Oh, but Christ, along with the angels, Christ himself made known a distinctive sign, and we have come to understand it from the scriptures, haven't we?
3 During the great tribulation, each one of us will find himself struggling to survive. The presence of Jesus will mean that Christ, along with the angels, will bring about the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the world. His presence will also signify the beginning of things that will be accomplished quickly, like the "great tribulation." (Matt. 24:3, 21, 29) This is why "the great crowd" will escape this system of things and survive. (Read Revelation 7:9, 13, 14.) How can we strengthen our faith during these times? It is by giving more thought to the meaning of the scriptures and by considering how they apply to us personally. Let us all do this, then, to strengthen our faith.
THE SIGN OF THE GREAT TRIBULATION
4. What does the sign of the great tribulation involve?
4 What does the sign of the great tribulation involve? The scriptures show that it is connected with the vision described in Revelation, where "Babylon the Great" is portrayed. (Rev. 17:5-7) All the nations have become drunk with her immorality, and she has become very rich! Why? Because the rulers of the world and the rulers of wealth have had relations with her. Those who know Jesus and his Kingdom, those rulers who remain faithful, do not get involved in the world's affairs and do not partake in its politics. They continue to uphold God's laws and standards. But others have become intoxicated with power and have become greedy, seeking their own glory and disregarding true worship. (2 Cor. 11:2; Jas. 1:27; Rev. 14:4) So, what should we avoid so that we don't become intoxicated with power? Jehovah God considers "his ways" separate from those who are intoxicated with the "ten horns" representing the "wild beast." These ten horns symbolize all the governments of the earth (United Nations). The United Nations represents the "wild beast."—Read Revelation 17:3, 16-18.
5, 6. Why can we be sure that the symbolic Babylon the Great will be completely destroyed when God acts?
5 How can we know whether the nations are becoming more and more involved in the affairs of Babylon the Great? Let us examine what Zechariah wrote. He wrote about a vision he had of a woman representing the nations and said: "This is what Jehovah showed me: 'Look! I am seeing a basket of ripe figs, and when I looked, the figs were good, very good. Then he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "Figs, ripe figs, very good."' " (Zech. 13:4-6) This shows that some rulers of the nations may cooperate with her and support her, or they may simply take advantage of her.
6 But will God allow his people to remain inactive? Jesus foretold: "As were the days of Noah, so the presence of the Son of man will be." (Matt. 24:22) As we have seen, the 66th week of Daniel's prophecy, which began in Jerusalem, was to be "cut off." This indicates that "the nations" would become active, and perhaps Christ's followers would have an opportunity to testify fully. However, those days of distress will also be a time when "the nations" will experience great tribulation. But this tribulation will serve as a refining fire for God's faithful people. Those who survive will be like refined gold, ready for use in God's service.
THE TIME TO ACT AND TO TEST
7, 8. What opportunity does God give the nations, and how do God's people feel about cooperating with others?
7 What is involved in giving the nations an opportunity? It means allowing them to demonstrate their loyalty to God. Many nations boast of their strength and independence from others, but they are actually under "the influence of the Devil." (Eph. 6:15-17) God's people, however, trust in Jehovah and know that he can save them. Also, they recognize that the days of "tribulation" may provide an opportunity to proclaim the good news more effectively, just as the persecution faced by Christians in the first century helped spread the message. Thus, this period allows Christ to separate the sheep from the goats. Therefore, let us endeavor to discern whether the present time of trouble is the fulfillment of Bible prophecy, and let many turn to Christ. In this way, Christ's loyal followers will show their devotion to Jehovah and prove worthy of receiving the blessings promised to Christ's brothers.—Matt. 25:34-40.
8 Moreover, as we observe events unfolding around us, let us ask ourselves whether those events indicate that we are living in the last days. For example, the first-century disciples foretold that there would be earthquakes and famines before the end. (Luke 13:15-18) We should therefore ask ourselves: 'Are we determined to remain faithful despite the difficulties we face? Are we determined to uphold all of God's standards and maintain our integrity toward Jehovah?' To help us appreciate this, remember how Daniel demonstrated his faith when confronted with a difficult situation.—Dan. 6:10, 11.
9, 10. (a) How do God's people view the nations? (b) What qualities do God's people possess?
9 They view the nations as forming 'the political system of Satan.' The political system of Satan is doomed. Why? Because "time of conclusion" has begun. (Matt. 24:14) Therefore, God's people recognize that they must separate themselves from the world and avoid being influenced by Satan's wicked ways. The Bible warns them to separate from false religion. It says: "And the great prostitute who sits upon many waters means the great city that has dominion over the kings of the earth."—Rev. 16:21.
10 This message touches our hearts. Ezekiel foretold that Gog of Magog would come up, like a storm. Isaiah said: "This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah says: 'Because you have said, "I will advance against the land of unwalled villages; I will come against the peaceful people who are dwelling without walls, both with livestock and with possessions, and against those who dwell in the wilderness, and against the people who are living confidently"; therefore, I will show my greatness and my holiness, and I will make myself known before many lands; and you will know that I am Jehovah.'" (Ezek. 38:10-12) In harmony with this prophecy, God's people do not become involved in "political affairs." This is because they want to remain neutral and not take sides with worldly powers. So let us also now heed this warning, and continue to support Jehovah's organization and his faithful brothers.
11. (a) What can we learn from the way the nations reacted when a great power invaded their land? (b) What qualities did those people display?
11 Let us examine each event carefully. But let us continue to look at this so that we may be prepared when signs from God become more frequent and noticeable. Do not be disturbed by some events, but let others continue. However, Jesus foretold a period of intense trouble during that generation, saying: "There will be signs in sun and moon and stars; and on earth distress of nations, perplexed over the roaring of the sea and the waves; men will become faint from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the world, because the powers of the heavens will be shaken." (Luke 21:25-27; read Mark 13:24-26.) How does what you see today compare with what was foretold about signs and other disturbances? Let us consider what each sign means. It is important for us to remember that these signs can cause God's faithful servants to feel anxious and fearful.
12, 13. (a) What is meant by Jesus' words "with great splendor"? (b) What do God's angels have to do with that event?
12 What is meant by Jesus' words "with great splendor"? They indicate something outstanding and impressive. (Matt. 24:46, 47, 50, 51; 25:19, 28-30) As Matthew wrote, Jesus meant that the presence of the Son of man would be conspicuous like a flash of lightning. He said: "Just as the lightning flashes from one part of the sky to another, so also will the Son of Man be in his day. And just as in the days of Noah, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the flood came and swept them all away, so too will the presence of the Son of Man be. Then two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left. Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and the other left." (Matt. 25:31-33) What do the sheep and the goats represent? Jesus explained that he would separate people based on how they treated the "least" of his brothers.—Matt. 25:46.
13 But what does it mean to be counted among those who are favorably viewed by the owner? It means being ready. (Matt. 24:30) So, should all Christians, along with those who associate with them, be watchful? Yes, because we need to strengthen our faith in Jehovah God and his Son, Jesus Christ, and imitate their example: "When these things begin to occur, straighten up and lift your heads, because your deliverance is getting near." (Luke 21:28) Therefore, let us remain alert and not be caught off guard.
KEEP WATCHFUL
14, 15. How can we show loyalty to the Faithful and Discreet Slave, and why is this important?
14 What does it mean to be loyal to the Faithful and Discreet Slave? Matthew and Mark tell us what will happen. They say: "That [the Son of Man] will send out his angels and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one extremity of the heavens to another." (Mark 13:27; Matt. 24:31) Gathering the chosen ones is closely connected with separating wheat from weeds, and with separating sheep from goats. (Matt. 13:37, 38) The separation of the wicked is like harvesting the weeds. (Rev. 7:1-4) In fact, the gathering that Jesus spoke about is the gathering of the 144,000 faithful Christians who will rule in heaven with him. (1 Thess. 4:15-17; Rev. 14:1) And they will be gathered to assist the Faithful and Discreet Slave in shepherding God's people. (Ezek. 38:11) This is why Jesus used the illustration of the wheat and the weeds, saying: "The weeds will be collected and burned."—Matt. 13:43. *
15 But how can the "wheat" be separated when imperfect humans are doing the separating? Many imperfect humans in Christendom misunderstand what the expression "to be separated" means, associating it with excommunication from Christ's organization. And they may think that if Jesus returns invisibly, it means he has already begun to separate people. The Bible shows that the "presence of the Son of Man" will be noticeable, and that then Jesus will begin to display his power. It says that he will appear "as lightning flashing from one end of the sky to the other." (Matt. 24:30) These events will clearly show that Jesus has returned. And more than that, "flesh and blood cannot inherit God's Kingdom." So how will those who are alive at that time experience "transformation," "being caught up," and "putting on incorruption"? * (Read 1 Corinthians 15:50-53.) Thus, the expression "to be separated" refers to something that will happen to them when they are resurrected. It will involve being transformed and putting on incorruption along with other faithful anointed ones.
16, 17. Why is it important to understand the meaning of the parable of the wheat?
16 The features of the parable of the wheat indicate that the separation will continue until all 144,000 faithful ones have been gathered. (Rev. 19:9) Therefore, there is still work for angels to do in this regard. Just as those who were approved proved themselves loyal during World War I, Jehovah will strengthen his people. (Ezek. 38:16) What will motivate Jehovah's people to take action? And why will those who prove faithful be reminded of the promise made to ancient Israel through Isaiah: "Do not fear the reproach of men, go forth and meet them; trust in Jehovah, you and Jerusalem; look forward, and let [them] become yours"? (2 Ki. 20:17) This is an encouragement to be courageous. As the time approaches for the final gathering of the "wheat," will all the faithful ones be able to remain steadfast? The account at Revelation 17:14 explains what will help Jehovah's people. It states that the armies of heaven will fight alongside the Lamb, and that those who are with him—those who have been appointed and chosen and faithful—will conquer. Jesus will lead Jehovah's people in conquering along with the 144,000 faithful ones.
17 That prophecy also involves errors that will cause the name of Ali-Maketoni to be dishonored. (Rev. 16:16) All the nations and their rulers will be thoroughly disturbed. Moreover, the great tribulation will bring about a time of distress such as has never occurred. In view of the coming trouble, how important it is that the wheat be separated! This is what the prophecy of Revelation urges us to remember! (Rev. 21:1-4) * All the faithful ones should strive to remain approved in God's eyes, and they can do so by maintaining loyalty. Let us resolve to support the wheat in this way! Why are we determined to do so?—Read 2 Peter 3:13.
18 So, since we see great things occurring, can we be sure that we will remain steadfast?
18 Since we see these great things taking place, can each one of us be confident that he will remain steadfast? The apostle Peter was inspired by God to write: "Seeing that all these things are going to dissolve, of what sort of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godly devotion, while you await and hasten the coming of the day of Jehovah… For this reason, give earnest thought to your means of proving yourselves approved to God, that you may continue to walk in his ways."—2 Pet. 3:11, 12, 14. How, then, can we make sure that we do not stumble, and how can we hold firmly to our shield, the Word of God?

text: NZIA YA UTANGIIO "Kila Uandiko niwaveveewe ni Ngai" Ndeto ya Ngai i thayu, na ni nthangaau, na ni mbui km uvyu ula mui ngali syeli. Aevelania 4:12. Ndeto yakma ikeethiwa iilyi ta uu ila yumaa kanyw'ani wakwa: ndikanzyokea mana, indi ikeanisya undu nendete, nayo ikaaila, unduni ula namitumie. Isaia 55:11. Uvuan'yo wa ndeto syaku nuetae kyeni. Savuli 119:130. Kutw'ikithw'a kwa nthi Mwambililyoni Ngai niwatw'ikithisye matu na nthi. Na Ngai oona kila kindu wombie, na, sisya, kyai kiseo muno. Mwambililyo 1:1, 31 Syindu syonthe nisyatw'ikithiw'e niwe; na ate vo vati kindu o na kimwe kyaatw'ikithw'a kati wa ila syatw'ikithiw'e. Yoana 1:3 Kutw'ikithw'a kwa mundu Na Ngai atw'ikithya mundu na muvw'ano wake, na muvw'ano wa Ngai amutw'ikithya; muume na muka amatw'ikithya. Na Ngai amaathima. Mwambililyo 1: 27, 28 Na Yeova Ngai oomba mundu na kitoo kya nthi, na amuvevea mithumu ya thayu manyiuuni make; na mundu atw'ika kyuu ki thayu. Na Yeova Ngai avanda muunda ngaliko ya wumiloni wa syua, nthini wa Eteni; na nikw'o wamwiie mundu ula wombie. Mwambililyo 2:7, 8 Na Yeova Ngai oosa mundu, na amwia muundani wa Eteni oseuvasye na kusuviaa. Na Yeova Ngai amwiaia mundu, akimwia, Wa kila muti wa muundani nutonya uya o undu ukwenda: indi wa muti wa kumanyithya useo na uthuku, ndukaye: nikwithiwa muthenya ula ukaya waw'o ndukatia ukw'a. Mwambililyo 2:15-17 Undu nai yookie Na indi nzoka yai nzeleke muno kwi nyamu o na yiva ya kithekani ila Yeova Ngai wombie. Na yamwia mundu muka atii, Ni w'o, Ngai niwaisye, Mutikaye ma miti yonthe ya muundani ? Na indi mundu muka eea nzoka, Mosyao ma miti ya muundani nitutonya uya: indi usyao wa muti ula wi kati wa muunda, Ngai niwaisye, Muikaye waw'o, o na muikakiite, muikese ukw'a. Na nzoka yamwia mundu muka, Muikakw'a nongi: nundu Ngai niwisi kana muthenya; ula mukaya waw'o, nivo mukasalukw'a metho, nenyu mukeethiwa ta Ngai, mukimanya useo na uthuku. Na yila mundu muka wonie kana muti ni museo wa uya, na ni wa kwendeesya methoni, na ni muti wa kwendwa kwa kuivya mundu, atw'a usyao waw'o na, aya; na ingi anenga muume, nake aya. Mwambililyo 3:1-6 Na Yeova Ngai eeta u mundu muume, amukulya . . . Nuite wa muti, ula nakwiaie ndukaye? Na mundu muume asungia, Mundu muka ula wanengie ethiwe nakwa, niwe unengie wa muti, na naya. Na Yeova Ngai akulya mundu muka, undu uu wikie nata ? Na mundu muka asungia, Nzoka ningengie, na naya. Na Yeova Ngai eea nzoka, Nundu niwikie uu, nuumaniwe, we, kwi indo syonthe, na kwi nyamu syonthe sya kithekani; ukaendaa na ivu, na ukaisaa kitoo mithenya yonthe ya thayu waku: na ngeekia umaitha kati wenyu we na mundu muka, na kati wa usyao waku na usyao wake: akatumba mutwe waku, naku ukatumba kitiinyo kyake. Amwia mundu muka, Ngaingivya muno woo waku wa kusyaa; wooni ukasyaa syana; na kwenda kwaku kukeethiwa kwa muemeu, nake akasumbika iulu waku. Na amwia Atamu, Nundu niweethukiisye wasya wa mukau, na ingi waya wa muti, ula nakwiaie, ngikwia, Ndukaaye waw'o: nthi niumaniwe nundu waku; ukaisaa wayo wooni matuku onthe ma thayu waku; miw'a nayo na thangila ikakumeesya; naku ukaisaa nyunyi sya muundani; yuutiani ya uthyu waku ukaisaa liu, kuvika yila ukasyoka muthangani; nundu nivo waumiw'e: nundu wi kitoo, na nukasyoka kitooni. Mwambililyo 3:9, 11-19 Na mukunga usu munene naw'o ni nzoka ila nguu, yitawa Ndevili, na ingi Satani, mukengani wa nthi yonthe. Uvuan'yo 12:9 Kwondu wa uu, nundu wa mundu umwe nai yalikile kuu nthi, na kikw'u kwondu wa nai; na kwa uu kikw'u kyavikia andu onthe, nikwithiwa onthe nimeekie nai. Alomi 5:12 Undu Ngai wonaa uthuku wa andu Ithyonthe ta malondu nitwaaite; nitweethyuuie kila umwe na kuatiia nzia yake mwene. Isaia 53:6 Yeova asyaiisye ana ma andu e ituni, Asisye ethiwa ve umwe ula wi na umanyi, Ula umumanthaa Ngai. Onthe nimathukite utee; onthe vamwe nimatw'ikite avuku; Vai umwe wikaa nesa, aiee, o na umwe. Savuli 14:2,3 0 tondu kuandikitwe, Kui mulungalu, aiee, o na umwe. . . . Na nzia ya muuo matyaamimanya: Kumukia Ngai kui methoni moo. . . . Nundu onthe nimeekie nai, na maivikiaa utaio wa Ngai. Alomi 3 :10, 17, 18, 23 Indi mothuku menyu nimamutaanitye inyw'i na Ngai wenyu, na nai syenyu nivithite uthyu wake kwenyu. Isaia 59:2 Wendo wa Ngai kwa andu Nundu Ngai niwendete nthi, niwanenganie Mwana wake e umwe, ni kana o ula umwitikilaa ndakae, indi ethiwe na thayu utathela. Yoana 3:16 Akimuvoya Ngai Yesu aisye: Na thayu utathela niw'o uu, ni kana makumanye we Ngai ula wa w'o weka, na ula wamutumie, nake ni Yesu Klisto. Yoana 17 :3 Unduni uu wendo wa Ngai niwonanitw'e kwitu, nundu Ngai niwamutumie Mwana wake kuu nthi, ula wasyaiwe e umwe, ni kana twithiwe na thayu kwondu wake. Uu niw'o wendo, ti ithyi twamwendie Ngai, indi niwe watwendie ithyi, na atuma Mwana wake ethiwe nthembo ya wiw'anithyo kwondu wa nai situ. 1 Yoana 4:9, 10 Kuka kwa Mwana wa Ngai kuu nthi Indi wianiu wa ivinda wooka, Ngai atuma Mwana wake. Akalatia 4:4 Ni ndeto ya kuikiiwa, na niyailwe ni kwitikilwa ni andu onthe, kana Klisto Yesu ookie kuu nthi kumatangiia andu athe. 1 Timotheo 1:15 Ai kuu nthi, na i nthi yatw'ikithiw'e niwe, na nthi ndiamwisi. Yoana 1:10 Kusyawa kwa Mwiaii Yesu Na kusyawa kwa Yesu Klisto kwailyi uu: Yila Meli inyia wake wevaitw'e ni Yosevu, matambite kutwaana, ooneka e na ivu ya Veva Mutheu. Na uu w'onthe utw'ikite, ni kana wianiw'e ula waneeniwe ni Mwiaii na kanyw'a wa mwathani, akyasya, Sisya, mwiitu akethiwa e ivu, na akasyaa kavisi, Nako syitwa yako makaketa Imanueli; na ualyulo wayo ni, Ngai vamwe naitu. Mathayo 1 :18, 22,23 Naku ukaketa syitwa yako YESU (Mutangiii); nundu mwe ukatangiia andu make kuma naini syoo. Mathayo 1:21 Mwiaii Yesu kuu nthi Uvoo wa Yesu wa Nasaleti, o undu Ngai wamwitikisye Veva Mutheu, o na vinya: ula waendaa aiika nesa, na aimavosya onthe ala manyamaaw'a ni ndevili; nikwithiwa Ngai ai vamwe nake. Meko ma Atumwa 10:38 Na Yesu anganga ndua syonthe na misyi, aimanyisya masinakokeni moo, na aitavan'ya uvoo museo wa usumbi, na aivosya mowau ma mithemba yonthe na kila wonzu. Mathayo 9:35 Na makomano manene mooka vala ui, me na syonze, na ililinda, na ala mataneenaa, na ala au mamutha, na angi aingi, mamaia mauuni ma Yesu; na amavosya. Mathayo 15:30 /12 Mwiaii Yesu niwathanie kikw'u na kuthayuuka ingi kwake Nundu amamanyiasya amanyiw'a make, na kumea, Mwana wa mundu nunukunenganwe mokoni ma andu, na makamuaa; na mamuaa, itina wa matuku atatu akathayuuka. Maliko 9:31 Yesu amea ... Nyie, ninyie muithi ula museo: muithi museo nunuuwia thayu wake nthi undu wa malondu. Kwondu wa uu Asa numbendete, nundu ningwia thayu wakwa nthi, ni kana niwose ingi. Vai mundu unuumbena thayu, indi no nyie nguwia nthi. Ni na ukumu wa kuwia nthi, na ni na ukumu wa kuwosa ingi. Mwiao uu noosie kwa Asa wakwa. Yoana 10:7,11,17, 18 Mwiaii Yesu niwakw'iie ngelan'yoni undu wa nai situ Na mavika vandu vetawa King'ala, mamwamba vo. ... Na Yesu asya, Asa, maekee; nikwithiwa matimanya undu mekwika. Luka 23:33,34 Niwavuthiw'e, na kulewa ni andu; ai mundu wa mawoo, na mumanyi wa thina. . . . Ni w'o, we niwakuie mathina maitu, na eeyaikya mawoo maitu; na uu w'onthe ithyi twamwona kwithiwa ni mukune, kukunwa ni Ngai, na kuthinw'a. Indi niwatonyiwe kwondu wa mavityo maitu, auauikw'a kwondu wa mothuku maitu.... naitu nituvoetw'e kwondu wa makunwa make. Ithyonthe ta malondu nitwaaite; nitweethyuuie kila umwe na kuatiia nzia yake mwene; nake Yeova amwaikisye uthuku witu ithyonthe. ... Niwavetiwe aume nthi ya ala me thayu kwondu wa ivityo ya andu makwa. ... Na nimamuseuvisye mbua vamwe na ala athuku, o na vamwe na ula muthwii kikw'uni kyake; o na kau we ndaaika ung'endu, o na vatyai ukengani kanyw'ani wake nongi. ... Nikwithiwa niwetikisye thayu wake kuvika akw'a, nake niwatalanilw'e na avitan'ya: indi niwakuie nai ya aingi, na amavoyea avitan'ya. Isaia 53:3-6, 8,9, 12 Klisto niwakwie kwondu wa nai situ kwianana na maandiko. 1 Akolintho 15:3 Mwiaii Yesu niwathayuukie kuma kwa akw'u Uu niw'o kuandikitwe, kana Klisto akanyamaw'a, na kuthayuuka muthenya wa katatu kuma akw'uni; na kana ualyulo wa ngoo na kuekewa nai kutavanw'e syitwani yake mbaini syonthe. Luka 24:46,47 Mundu usu Ngai niwamuthayuukisye muthenya wa katatu, na amumilya onanw'e, ti kwa andu onthe, indi kwa ngusi ila Ngai wambie unyuva. Meko ma Atumwa 10:40, 41 Indi yuyu Klisto niwathayuukiw'e kuma kwa akw'u, usyao wa mbee wa ala makomete. Nundu nikwithiwa kikw'u nikyookie kwondu wa mundu, kuthayuuka kwa akw'u nakw'o nikwookie kwondu wa mundu. Nundu o undu onthe makusaa nthini wa Atamu, o ta uu nthini wa Klisto onthe makeethiwa thayu. 1 Akolintho 15:20-23 Mwiaii Yesu niwasyokie ituni Niweyonanisye mwene kwamo na mawonan'yo maingi ma w'o, e thayu, itina wa kunyamaa kwake, akimaumilila ivinda ya mithenya miongo ina, na aineena maundu ma usumbi wa Ngai. ... Ambatw'a iulu masyaitye; na ithweo yamwosa auma methoni moo. Meko ma Atumwa 1:3,9 Na vate ngananio nzama ya kumukia Ngai ni nene; We ula wonaniw'e e na mwii, Atalilwa ulungalu vevani, Ooneka ni alaika, Atavanw'a kwa Andu-ma-mbai-ingi, Eetikilwa kuu nthi, Atwawa iulu utheuni mutisu. 1 Timotheo 3:16 Nzia ya Ngai ya utangiio Niika ata kana ndangiiwe? . . . Mwitikile Mwiaii Yesu, na nuutangiiwa. Meko ma Atumwa 16:30, 31 Alyulai ngoo indi, mwithyuue, nai syenyu syanangwe. Meko ma Atumwa 3:19 Alyulai ngoo, na muivatiswa kila mundu syitwani ya Yesu Klisto, mwone uekeo wa nai syenyu; na mukoosa muthinzio wa Veva Mutheu. Meko ma Atumwa 2:38 Ethiwa nitukumbula nai situ, we e kithito, na ni mulungalu wa utuekea nai situ, na kututhesya undu ute ulungalu w'onthe. 1 Yoana 1:9 Ethiwa ukamumbula Yesu na kanyw'a waku kana niwe Mwiaii, na ukeetikila ngooni yaku kana Ngai niwamuthayuukisye kumumya akw'uni, ukatangiiwa: nundu mundu niwitikilaa na ngoo kuvikia ulungalu; na niwumbulaa na kanyw'a kuvikia utangiio. Alomi 10:9, 10 Nundu nimutangiiitwe na mumo kwondu wa muikiio; naw'o ndumite kwa inyw'i ene, ni muthinzio wa Ngai. Aeveso 2:8 Nundu, O ula ukekaua syitwa ya Mwiaii, nukatangiiwa. Alomi 10:13 Mwiaii Yesu asya: Ula wukaa kwakwa ndikamwikya nza nongi. Yoana 6:37 Utangiio kwondu wa kikw'u kya Klisto Indi yu nthini wa Klisto Yesu inyw'i ala mwai kuasa nimuthengeew'e ni nthakame ya Klisto. Aeveso 2:13 Nthakame ya Yesu Mwana wake nitutheasya nai syonthe. 1 Yoana 1:7 Nikwithiwa kwai kwenda kuseo kwa Ithe ati wianiu w'onthe wikalae nthini wake (Klisto); na kwondu wake kusyiw'anithya syindu syonthe nake mwene, aetete muuo kwondu wa nthakame ya ngelan'yo yake. Akolosai 1 :19,20 Nimwoovoiw'e mume mwikalileni wenyu wa mana ... na muiaaovow'a na syindu ila syanangikaa, ta vetha kana thaavu; indi mwovoetw'e na nthakame yi vata muno, ... nayo ni nthakame ya Klisto. 1 Vetelo 1:18,19 Nthini wa Klisto twi na wovosyo witu kwondu wa nthakame yake, uekeo wa mavityo maitu, kwianana na uthwii wa mumo wake. Aeveso 1:7 Nundu thayu wa mwii wi nthakameni; ... nundu nthakame niyo yiw'anithasya mundu nundu yi thayu. Alivai 17:11 Na kwa uu ethiwa mundu o na wiva e nthini wa Klisto, ni kyumbe kyeu: maundu ala makuu ni mavitu; sisyai, nimatw'ikite meu. 2 Akolintho 5:17 Veva Mutheu Mwiaii Yesu asya: Nakwa ngamuvoya Asa, nake akamunenga Mutetheesya ungi, ethiwe nenyu mavinda onthe, nake niwe Veva wa w'o: ula nthi itatonya kumwosa; nundu ndimwonaa, o na ndimwisi: indi inyw'i nimumwisi; nundu ekalaa nenyu, na akeethiwa e nthini wenyu. Yoana 14:16,17 Indi ula Mutetheesya, nake ni Veva Mutheu, ula Asa wimutuma syitwani yakwa, akamumanyisya maundu onthe. Yoana 14:26 Na muikew'ithye Veva Mutheu wa Ngai woo, nake nthini wake mwikiitwe usiilo kuvika muthenya wa wovosyo. Aeveso 4:30 Kinyaai mutongoew'e ni Veva, na muikeanisya mimeo ya mwii. Akalatia 5:16 Nundu onthe ala matongoeaw'a ni Veva wa Ngai, asu ni o ana ma Ngai. Alomi 8:14 Indi usuwai ni Veva. Aeveso 5:18 Indi usyao wa Veva ni wendo, utanu, muuo, wumiisyo, kwika angi nesa, useo, kithito, uuu, witing'o. Akalatia 5:22,23 Kwikalaa na thayu mutheu Nundu uu niw'o ula wendetwe ni Ngai, naw'o ni kuvathwa kwenyu. 1 Athesalonika 4:3 Mwiaii Yesu avoyie: Mavathe methiwe atheu nthini wa ula w'o: ndeto yaku niyo w'o. Yoana 17:17 Twikale naini ni kana mumo wingive ? Aiee, kuikethiwe uu. Ithyi ala twakwie kwa nai, tukekala vo ingi ata ? Italei ene kwithiwa mwi akw'u kwa nai, indi mwi thayu kwa Ngai nthini wa Klisto Yesu. Alomi 6:1,2, 11 Indi yu nimuthaitw'e kuma naini, na mwatw'ika athukumi ma Ngai, mwi na usyao wenyu kuvika kuvathika, na muminukilyo ni thayu utathela. Alomi 6:22 Na Ngai wa muuo mwene namuvathan'ye mwithiwe atheu vyu; veva na ngoo na mwii syithiwe syi nima, itailiilika uthuku akyuka Mwiaii waitu Yesu Klisto. E na kithito ula umwitaa inyw'i, nake akeeka uu. 1 Athesalonika 5:23, 24 Kuvoya Mwiaii Yesu asya: O na wiva w'onthe ula mwivoya syitwani yakwa, ngawika, ni kana Asa ataiwe nthini wa Mwana. Ethiwa mukavoya undu o na wiva syitwani yakwa, ngawika. Yoana 14:13,14 Mukikala nthini wakwa, na ndeto syakwa ikikala nthini wenyu, voyai ula mukwenda w'onthe, na mukeekwa. Yoana 15:7 Maundu onthe o ala mukwitya mukivoya, itikilai kana nimuumosa na mukeethiwa mwi namo. Maliko 11:24 Mukivoya nthini wa Veva mavinda onthe na mboya syonthe na kwisuva. Aeveso 6:18 Voyaai mutekueka; tungaai muvea kila unduni: nundu uu niw'o Ngai wendaa nthini wa Klisto Yesu ngali i yenyu. 1 Athesalonika 5:17, l8 Uthukumi na wumiisyo Ethiwa mundu o na wiva nunukwenda kumbikila, nielee mwene, na kwiyaikya ngelan'yo yake, na akimbikila. Mathayo 16:24 Na Ngai nutonya kwingivya mumo w'onthe kwa inyw'i; ni kana inyw'i, mwianiwe vyu mavinda onthe maunduni onthe, mwingive kila wiani museo. 2 Akolintho 9:8 Ilulumuyei, muteuthingithika, mukithangaaa muno mavinda onthe wiani wa Mwiaii, nikwithiwa nimwisi kana kuthinia wia kwenyu ti kwa mana nthini wa Mwiaii. 1 Akolintho 15:58 Nikwithiwa nimunengetwe kwondu wa Klisto, ti kumwitikua kw'oka, indi o na kuthinw'a nakw'o kwondu wake. Avilivi 1: 29 Ethiwa mukathinw'a kwondu wa ulungalu, mwi aathime; na muikakie kutisya kwoo, o na muikauuye. 1 Vetelo 3:14 Ethiwa mwivuthw'a kwondu wa syitwa ya Klisto, mwi aathime; nikwithiwa Veva wa utaio, o Veva wa Ngai, ekalaa iulu wenyu. 1 Vetelo 4:14 Kuthaitha mivw'anano nikwavataniw'e ni Ngai Nyie ninyie Yeova Ngai waku ... Ndukethiwe na ngai ingi ate o nyie. Ndukeseuvisye muvw'anano mwasuvye, o na muvw'ano o na wiva wa kindu ki ituni iulu, kana kila ki kuu nthi, kana kila ki manzini itheo wa nthi: ndukamikunamie, o na ndukamithukume; nundu nyie Yeova Ngai waku ni Ngai wi kiwiu. Kuma 20:2-5 Nundu ngai syonthe sya ngo sya andu ni mivw'anano; Indi Yeova niwombie matu. Savuli 96:5 Nitwisi kana muvw'anano ti kindu kuu nthi, na ati kui Ngai ungi ate o umwe weka. 1 Akolintho 8:4 Kwi Ngai o umwe, nake niwe Asa, ula syindu syonthe syumaa kwake, na ithyi twi make; na kwi Mwiaii umwe, Yesu Klisto, na syindu syonthe ni kwondu wake, na ithyi twi kwondu wake. 1 Akolintho 8:6 Yesu wamwiie, Thi, Satani: nundu nikuandikitwe, Muthaithae Mwiaii Ngai waku, na muthukumae we, e weka. Mathayo 4:10 Uaai mamutha menyu ala me kuu nthi: ulaalai, na uvuku, na mimeo mithuku, na kwenda maundu mathuku, na itomo, nayo ni kuthaitha mivw'anano; kwondu wa maundu asu uthatu wa Ngai wukaa kwa ana ala matew'aa. Akolosai 3: 5, 6 Muisyo undu wa kulea utangiio wa Ngai Ithyi tukavonoka ata, twavuthya utangiio unenevete uu? Aevelania 2:3 Ula ukilasya akatiiwa maundu asu; nakwa ngeethiwa Ngai wake, nake akeethiwa mwana wakwa. Indi ala makiaa, na ala matetikilaa, na ala mathatasya, na oaani, na ilaalai, na aoi, na athaithi ma mivw'anano, na onthe ala maneenaa uvungu, kianda kyoo kikeethiwa iiani yila yakanaa mwaki na muviliti, nayo ni kikw'u kya keli. Uvuan'yo 21:7, 8 Ula witikuaa u Mwana e na thayu utathela; indi ula utamwitikilaa Mwana ndakona thayu, indi uthatu wa Ngai wikalaa iulu wake. Yoana 3:36 Nuu ula umwonetye kukia uthatu ula wukite ? Luka 3:7 Kutangiiwa kuma naini na kuma vinyani wa Satani Na Ngai wa muuo akamutumba Satani ungu wa nyaii syenyu mituki. Alomi 16:20 Mukimutungia Asa muvea ... ula watutangiie kuma vinyani wa kivindu, na kututhamya na kutulikya usumbini wa Mwana wake mwendwa. Akolosai 1:12,13 Kwondu wa uu Mwana wa Ngai niwonaniw'e, ni kana anange mawia ma ndevili. 1 Yoana 3:8 Mwiaii waitu Yesu Klisto, ula wenenganie mwene kwondu wa nai situ, ni kana atutangiie tume nthi ino nthuku ya ivinda yii, kwianana na kwenda kwa Ngai, Asa waitu: ndaia niyithiwe kwake tene na tene. Akalatia 1: 3-5 Ikiai miio yonthe ya kau ya Ngai, ni kana mutonye kusiiia maui ma Satani. Aeveso 6:11 Indi muvea niwithiwe kwa Ngai, ula utunengae kukilya kwondu wa Mwiaii waitu Yesu Klisto. 1 Akolintho 15:57 Kuka ingi kwa Klisto Ngooka ingi, na ngamwosa inyw'i mwithiwe kwakwa; ni kana vala nii, nenyu mwithiwe vo. Yoana 14:3 Yesu usu, ula woswa iulu ituni kuma vala mui, akooka o ta uu, o undu mwamwona aithi ituni. Meko ma Atumwa 1:11 Nikwithiwa Mwiaii mwene akatheea kuma ituni, na wasya mutulu, na wasya wa mulaika munene, na soo wa Ngai: na ala makwie nthini wa Klisto makathayuuka mbee; na indi itina ithyi ala twi thayu ala twatialile, tukavulw'a vamwe nao mathweoni, kumuthaua Mwiaii yayayani: na uu tukeethiwa vamwe na Mwiaii tene na tene. 1 Athesalonika 4:16,17 Nitwisi kana, yila wionanw'a, tukavw'anana nake; nundu tukamwona we o undu uilyi. 1 Yoana 3:2 Syaiisyai indi; nundu mutyisi muthenya ula Mwiaii wenyu wiuka . . . Nenyu ikalai mwiyumbanitye; nundu saa ula mutataiie niw'o wiuka ula Mwana wa mundu. Mathayo 24:42,44 Sisya, ngooka mituki; na ituvi yakwa yi vamwe nakwa, kumutuva kila mundu kwianana na wia wake undu uilyi. Uvuan'yo 22:12 Ameni: uka, Mwiaii Yesu. Uvuan'yo 22:20 KWA MUSOMI Ndeto ila iandikitwe kavukuni kaa na ndeto syumitw'e Mbiviliani, nayo ni Ndeto ya Ngai. Misoa nivangitwe kwianana na undu ula munene wayo. Nuikiithwa kwithiwa na Mbivilia yaku mwene, na kumisoma, nundu noyo uvuan'yo wa Ngai kwa andu onthe.
